guides.title: Diagnostic trouble codes: find the right Mustang diagnostic procedure
guides.summary: Use the reporting module, installed engine and fitted equipment to select the correct diagnostic chapter for a 2015 Mustang with a 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
guides.introduction: A trouble code is a useful lead, but it makes a lousy shopping list. Before the parts cannon gets another expensive round, I want to know which module reported the code and which diagnostic chapter belongs to it. This master index makes that connection. We’ll keep the code attached to its reporting module, sort the engine and equipment branches, and land at the right investigation.
guides.why: A diagnostic trouble code, or DTC, is a recorded fault identifier. The reporting module is the electronic controller associated with that result. This index connects module identifiers to the system chapters used to investigate their codes. Similar names can lead to different destinations, and the PCM and several infotainment entries require an engine or equipment choice before you can select the correct chapter.

when.summary: Use this guide when you already have a recorded trouble code and need to find its module-specific diagnostic procedure.
notes: Applies to the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
An equipment-specific entry applies only when the vehicle has that equipment.
A complaint description alone does not identify the reporting module.

prepare.title: Have the recorded result in front of you
prepare.detail: Keep the exact DTC and reporting module identifier together. Preserve the complete identifier: BCM and BCMB, for example, select different entries. If the result does not identify a module, resolve that before choosing a route.

prepare.title: Confirm the configuration needed for your branch
prepare.detail: For PCM results, establish whether the installed engine is 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L. For the infotainment entries with two destinations, establish whether the car has AM/FM/CD/SYNC or a touchscreen SYNC 2/SYNC 3 system.

prepare.title: Set the endpoint before reaching for tools
prepare.detail: This job ends with selecting the diagnostic chapter. Code retrieval, scan-tool commands, component access, connector checks, test limits, replacement and repair verification require that system’s diagnostic instructions. Obtain those instructions before physical testing or disassembly; no removal or unplugging is needed to use this index.

steps.title: Match the reporting module exactly
steps.body:
Start with the module name recorded alongside the DTC. Find that exact identifier in the routing rows below, using the [Master DTC Index](#/document/G1693178) or the [second Diagnostic Trouble Code Charts entry](#/document/G1693178-03ac7c67) as the reference.

I keep the code and module on the same note throughout this job. A familiar-looking acronym is not a reason to change the identifier or select a chapter by guesswork.

steps.title: For PCM results, select the installed engine
steps.body:
If the reporting module is PCM, use the engine-specific Electronic Engine Controls destination:

- 2.3L: [303-14A](#/document/G1692929).
- 3.7L: [303-14B](#/document/G1692931).
- 5.0L: [303-14C](#/document/G1692933).
- 5.2L: [303-14D](#/document/G1807235).

Check the engine before opening the chapter. The shared chapter title does not make these four routes interchangeable.

steps.title: For infotainment results, resolve the display branch and its exceptions
steps.body:
For APIM, ACM, DACMC, FCIM or GPSM, choose by fitted equipment: AM/FM/CD/SYNC goes to [Information and Entertainment System, 415-00A](#/document/G1692891); a touchscreen display goes to [Information and Entertainment System, 415-00B, SYNC 2/SYNC 3](#/document/G1702418).

Two entries have a fixed destination in this index: FCDIM goes to 415-00A, and DSP goes to 415-00B. Use those exact entries rather than giving every audio or display module the same branch. The alphabet soup has rules, damn it.

steps.title: Route body, entry, seat and convertible-top modules
steps.body:
Keep BCM and BCMB separate: use [Body Control Module](#/document/G1692965) for BCM and [Body Control Module B](#/document/G1704140) for BCMB.

DDM, PDM and RTM lead to [Locks, Latches and Entry Systems, 501-14](#/document/G1695898). DSM and SCME lead to [Front Seats, 501-10A](#/document/G1695509).

Moveable Roof Control Module A, MRCMA, and Moveable Roof Control Module B, MRCMB, both lead to Convertible Top, 501-18. That destination has no matching linked chapter here; obtain it before continuing with either roof-module result.

steps.title: Route chassis, steering and driving-assistance modules
steps.body:
Use the exact module row below to select among power steering, steering-wheel and column electrics, adaptive cruise control, collision warning, rear parking aid, blind-spot information and vehicle dynamic suspension. These are separate diagnostic destinations even where the systems sound related.

For an ABS Module result, the destination is Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) and Stability Control, 206-09. There is no matching linked chapter here for that branch; obtain section 206-09 before continuing.

steps.title: Route network, instrumentation and restraint-system modules
steps.body:
GWM goes to [Communications Network, 418-00](#/document/G1813071).

ICM and IPC both go to [Instrumentation, Message Center and Warning Chimes, 413-01](#/document/G1693940).

OCSM and RCM both go to [Airbag Supplemental Restraint System (SRS), 501-20B](#/document/G1696340). SRS is the restraint-system chapter, so keep either result attached to that destination.

steps.title: Check and record the diagnostic handoff
steps.body:
Compare the chosen chapter with the original module identifier. For PCM, check the engine again; for the split infotainment entries, check the fitted radio/display system. Also retain equipment qualifiers such as adaptive cruise control or rear parking aid.

Record the exact code, module, configuration and destination together. Then use that chapter’s diagnostic instructions for the next stage. We have given the investigation an address; we have not yet convicted a component.

watchFor.title: A module entry is not a replacement verdict
watchFor.body: Finding a module in the index tells you where to investigate its result. It does not establish that the module itself has failed.

watchFor.title: Similar identifiers select different routes
watchFor.body: BCM and BCMB have separate destinations. PSCM and SCCM also lead to different chapters. Read the full identifier before choosing.

watchFor.title: Infotainment exceptions matter
watchFor.body: APIM, ACM, DACMC, FCIM and GPSM have equipment-dependent routes. FCDIM is assigned to 415-00A and DSP to 415-00B in this index.

watchFor.title: An index listing does not establish fitted equipment
watchFor.body: The presence of an adaptive-cruise, convertible-top, blind-spot or suspension entry does not establish that the particular car has that system.

notes: Use the routing rows as module-to-chapter matches, not as interpretations of individual DTCs.
Keep the original code unchanged when recording the destination.

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is PCM and the installed engine is 2.3L.
diagnostics.meaning: The engine-control branch is 303-14A, Electronic Engine Controls — 2.3L EcoBoost.
diagnostics.next: Use [2.3L Electronic Engine Controls](#/document/G1692929) for the next diagnostic stage.

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is PCM and the installed engine is 3.7L.
diagnostics.meaning: The engine-control branch is 303-14B, Electronic Engine Controls — 3.7L Duratec.
diagnostics.next: Use [3.7L Electronic Engine Controls](#/document/G1692931) for the next diagnostic stage.

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is PCM and the installed engine is 5.0L.
diagnostics.meaning: The engine-control branch is 303-14C, Electronic Engine Controls — 5.0L 32V Ti-VCT.
diagnostics.next: Use [5.0L Electronic Engine Controls](#/document/G1692933) for the next diagnostic stage.

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is PCM and the installed engine is 5.2L.
diagnostics.meaning: The engine-control branch is 303-14D, Electronic Engine Controls — 5.2L 32V Ti-VCT.
diagnostics.next: Use [5.2L Electronic Engine Controls](#/document/G1807235) for the next diagnostic stage.

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is APIM, ACM, DACMC, FCIM or GPSM, and the vehicle has AM/FM/CD/SYNC.
diagnostics.meaning: These entries use the 415-00A infotainment branch for this equipment.
diagnostics.next: Use [Information and Entertainment System — vehicles with SYNC](#/document/G1692891).

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is APIM, ACM, DACMC, FCIM or GPSM, and the vehicle has a touchscreen display.
diagnostics.meaning: These entries use the 415-00B infotainment branch for SYNC 2/SYNC 3.
diagnostics.next: Use [Information and Entertainment System — vehicles with SYNC 2/SYNC 3](#/document/G1702418).

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is FCDIM.
diagnostics.meaning: This entry points directly to the 415-00A infotainment chapter.
diagnostics.next: Use [Information and Entertainment System — vehicles with SYNC](#/document/G1692891).

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is DSP.
diagnostics.meaning: This entry points directly to the 415-00B infotainment chapter.
diagnostics.next: Use [Information and Entertainment System — vehicles with SYNC 2/SYNC 3](#/document/G1702418).

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is BCM.
diagnostics.meaning: The destination is Body Control Module in section 419-10, Multifunction Electronic Modules.
diagnostics.next: Use [Body Control Module (BCM)](#/document/G1692965).

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is BCMB.
diagnostics.meaning: The destination is Body Control Module B in section 419-10, Multifunction Electronic Modules.
diagnostics.next: Use [Body Control Module B (BCMB)](#/document/G1704140).

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is DDM, PDM or RTM.
diagnostics.meaning: All three entries lead to section 501-14, Handles, Locks, Latches and Entry Systems.
diagnostics.next: Use [Locks, Latches and Entry Systems](#/document/G1695898), retaining the particular reporting module with the code.

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is DSM or SCME.
diagnostics.meaning: Both entries lead to section 501-10A, Front Seats.
diagnostics.next: Use [Front Seats](#/document/G1695509), retaining the particular reporting module with the code.

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is Moveable Roof Control Module A (MRCMA) or Moveable Roof Control Module B (MRCMB).
diagnostics.meaning: Both entries lead to Convertible Top, section 501-18.
diagnostics.next: Obtain the Convertible Top diagnostic chapter, section 501-18. Neither roof-module branch has a matching linked destination here.

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is ABS Module.
diagnostics.meaning: The destination is Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) and Stability Control, section 206-09.
diagnostics.next: Obtain the ABS and Stability Control diagnostic chapter, section 206-09. This branch has no matching linked destination here.

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is PSCM.
diagnostics.meaning: The destination is section 211-02, Power Steering.
diagnostics.next: Use [Power Steering](#/document/G1757488).

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is SCCM.
diagnostics.meaning: The destination is section 211-05, Steering Wheel and Column Electrical Components.
diagnostics.next: Use [Steering Wheel and Column Electrical Components](#/document/G1693269).

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is CCM.
diagnostics.meaning: The destination is section 419-03B, Cruise Control — vehicles with adaptive cruise control.
diagnostics.next: Use [Cruise Control](#/document/G1693153), preserving the adaptive-cruise equipment qualifier.

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is HUD.
diagnostics.meaning: The destination is section 419-03C, Collision Warning and Collision Avoidance System.
diagnostics.next: Use [Collision Warning and Collision Avoidance System](#/document/G1693174).

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is PAM.
diagnostics.meaning: The destination is section 413-13A, Parking Aid — vehicles with rear parking aid.
diagnostics.next: Use [Parking Aid](#/document/G1693946), preserving the rear-parking-aid equipment qualifier.

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is SODL or SODR.
diagnostics.meaning: Both entries lead to Blind Spot Information System in section 419-04, Side and Rear Vision.
diagnostics.next: Use [Blind Spot Information System](#/document/G1694004), retaining SODL or SODR exactly as recorded.

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is VDM.
diagnostics.meaning: The destination is section 204-05, Vehicle Dynamic Suspension.
diagnostics.next: Use [Vehicle Dynamic Suspension](#/document/G1694674).

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is GWM.
diagnostics.meaning: The destination is section 418-00, Module Communications Network.
diagnostics.next: Use [Communications Network](#/document/G1813071).

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is ICM or IPC.
diagnostics.meaning: Both entries lead to section 413-01, Instrumentation, Message Center and Warning Chimes.
diagnostics.next: Use [Instrumentation, Message Center and Warning Chimes](#/document/G1693940), retaining the exact reporting identifier.

diagnostics.finding: The reporting module is OCSM or RCM.
diagnostics.meaning: Both entries lead to section 501-20B, Supplemental Restraint System.
diagnostics.next: Use [Airbag Supplemental Restraint System (SRS)](#/document/G1696340), retaining the exact reporting identifier.

diagnostics.finding: The module identifier is missing, does not match an entry, or a required engine or infotainment configuration is unresolved.
diagnostics.meaning: The information needed to select a supported route is incomplete.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the reporting identifier or vehicle configuration before choosing a chapter. Do not substitute a similar acronym or select a route from the complaint alone.

verification.title: Confirm the module-to-chapter match
verification.body: Compare the recorded module identifier with its routing row and the selected destination. Check distinguishing letters, including BCM versus BCMB.

verification.title: Confirm the configuration branch
verification.body: For PCM, confirm the chosen chapter matches the installed engine. For APIM, ACM, DACMC, FCIM and GPSM, confirm the infotainment equipment branch. For FCDIM and DSP, retain their fixed index destinations.

verification.title: Keep a usable handoff record
verification.body: The completed record should contain the original DTC, reporting module, relevant configuration and destination title or section. For ABS Module, MRCMA or MRCMB, record the named chapter that must be obtained.

verification.title: Recognize what completion means
verification.body: These are checks of the route you selected. They do not test the vehicle or demonstrate a successful repair; those conclusions belong to the system-specific investigation.

applicability.equipment: Route selection depends on fitted equipment: AM/FM/CD/SYNC or touchscreen SYNC 2/SYNC 3, adaptive cruise control, rear parking aid, convertible top, blind-spot information and vehicle dynamic suspension, where applicable.

stepGroups.title: Identify the module and configuration
stepGroups.summary: Match the recorded identifier and resolve engine or infotainment branches.

stepGroups.title: Select the system destination
stepGroups.summary: Route body, chassis, assistance, network, instrument and restraint results.

stepGroups.title: Verify the diagnostic handoff
stepGroups.summary: Keep the code, module, configuration and selected chapter together.

guides.title: Inspect connector terminal fit and release damaged wire terminals
guides.summary: Check mating-terminal fit, identify the correct connector release geometry and use the specified tools to avoid damaging the terminals.
guides.introduction: An electrical connector’s plastic shell positions and retains the metal terminals that carry the circuit. The male and female terminals must fit correctly for a durable connection. This job checks that fit and provides a route to terminal removal when repair is needed; a connector fault does not establish that its attached module has failed.
guides.why: An unsuitable probe can distort a terminal during testing. A terminal guide can also add friction that masks weak mating contact. Removal requires equal care because different shells place their terminal-release tangs at different depths.

when.summary: When connector inspection is required during electrical diagnosis or a damaged terminal needs removal.
notes: Identify the actual connector shell and terminal position before choosing a release dimension.

prepare.title: Apply the relevant safety precautions
prepare.detail: Read Health and Safety Precautions and the applicable system warnings first. Disable remote start where fitted, prevent unauthorized starting and use the required protection. Follow system-specific isolation requirements; this general procedure does not authorize probing an airbag igniter.

prepare.title: Use the specified connection tools
prepare.detail: Use Rotunda Flex Probes NUD105-R025D or Terminal Probe Kit 29-011A when connecting test equipment or jumper wires. Have the correct mating terminal for fit assessment and a suitable terminal-removal tool that can be marked for insertion depth.

steps.title: Identify the connector arrangement
steps.body: Match the shell to the [terminal inspection and removal procedure](#/document/G1939867). One illustrated arrangement for the Audio Front Control Module, Body Control Module and Instrument Panel Cluster identifies an external terminal-release tang and a connector locking tab. Distinguish these features before attempting release.

steps.title: Assess the actual mating fit
steps.body: Use the mating terminal to check for normal separation force. Very low force indicates a damaged or poorly fitting terminal. The relevant check is terminal-to-terminal engagement, rather than how firmly the complete plastic connector seems to latch.

steps.title: Account for guide or retainer friction
steps.body: For small terminals, determine whether the terminal guide or retainer adds drag during insertion or withdrawal. If it does, remove it as required for an accurate fit check. Otherwise, its friction can make weak terminal engagement seem satisfactory.

steps.title: Select dimensions for the exact terminal position
steps.body: The shared Audio Front Control Module, Front Controls Interface Module, Gateway Module A and heating, ventilation and air-conditioning control-module arrangement distinguishes inner and outer terminals. The separate Body Control Module layouts also distinguish terminal widths and inner, outer or lower release positions. Use the matching illustration and table, rather than selecting a dimension from the module name alone.

steps.title: Match in-line and seat connectors separately
steps.body: The two body-harness in-line layouts have different release geometry. The body-harness/seat-harness and body-harness/seat-module arrangements also use different release depths, despite sharing a listed terminal width. Confirm which shell and cavity are present before preparing the tool.

steps.title: Mark the tool and follow the release operation
steps.body: The listed hard-shell dimension is measured from the connector’s front face to the terminal-release tang engagement point. Mark that distance on the removal tool before insertion. Follow the matching illustrated release operation and the linked repair demonstration for damaged terminal or connector replacement; the dimensions alone do not specify a universal release motion.

watchFor.title: A probe that changes the fault
watchFor.body: Avoid forcing an unsuitable test connection into the terminal. Use the specified probe equipment whenever test leads or jumpers are connected.

watchFor.title: Similar connector names
watchFor.body: Several entries share a module or harness name while describing different shells or terminal positions.

notes: The complete procedure retains the connector-specific widths and release-depth tables needed at the vehicle.

diagnostics.finding: Very low separation force between mating terminals
diagnostics.meaning: The terminal fit is compromised.
diagnostics.next: Identify the damaged terminal or connector and follow its replacement instructions.

diagnostics.finding: The terminal guide contributes insertion or removal drag
diagnostics.meaning: The apparent resistance does not accurately represent mating-terminal fit.
diagnostics.next: Remove the guide or retainer where necessary and repeat the assessment.

verification.title: Confirm terminal fit
verification.body: After any terminal repair, repeat the mating-terminal fit assessment without misleading guide or retainer drag.

verification.title: Record the finding
verification.body: Record the connector and cavity assessed, the fit finding and any terminal replacement. Keep this result separate from conclusions about the connected module.

procedures.purpose: Terminal fit assessment, connector-specific release dimensions and terminal-removal guidance.
Required general and applicable system-specific service precautions.

guides.title: Trace Mustang noise, vibration and harsh ride complaints
guides.summary: Use road tests, vibration measurements and listening checks to identify the system responsible before choosing a component repair.
guides.introduction: Noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) diagnosis connects what you hear or feel with the machinery producing it. Rotating components, suspension movement and body contact can create similar complaints. This investigation separates vehicle-speed, engine-speed, load-related and road-impact symptoms, then directs you to the appropriate component tests.
guides.why: The loudest or most strongly vibrating part may simply receive movement through another component. Replacing that receiving part can leave the cause untouched. Work from symptom to system, component and cause, using repeatable measurements and comparison with a known-good vehicle where helpful.

when.summary: Investigate a repeatable noise, vibration or harsh ride, particularly after a sudden change or previous repair.
notes: An unusual sensation is not automatically a defect; establish whether it differs from normal operation under comparable conditions.

prepare.title: Provide suitable testing capability
prepare.detail: Use a technician capable of controlled road testing, vibration analysis and engine load testing. Arrange a quiet, low-traffic route, a tachometer and wheel blocks for the stationary tests.

prepare.title: Choose measuring and listening equipment
prepare.detail: An MTS 4000/4100 analyzer compares measurements with vehicle computer data and entered vehicle specifications. An Electronic Vibration Analyzer (EVA) displays dominant frequencies and amplitudes. EngineEAR, ChassisEAR or a mechanic’s stethoscope helps localize noise.

prepare.title: Prepare calculations
prepare.detail: Have tire diameter, relevant vehicle specifications and the frequency worksheet available. Vibrate software can plot component speeds; its worksheet uses measured vibration and engine speeds to identify a likely component group.

steps.title: Describe and classify the concern
steps.body: Record when it began, whether onset was sudden or gradual, and any connection with repairs or unusual events. Reproduce it with the driver where possible. Classify it as noise, vibration or harshness; a combined noise-and-vibration complaint tied to vehicle speed follows the vibration path.

steps.title: Inspect before driving
steps.body: Correct anything compromising road-test safety. Check add-on items and potential wind-noise sources, turn off the radio and climate blower, and lower the antenna if possible. For harshness, compare operating conditions, check specified tire pressures and inspect modifications before suspecting damaged suspension parts.

steps.title: Establish a road-test baseline
steps.body: Begin with the Slow Acceleration Test, recording the speed and frequency at onset, greatest intensity and disappearance. Position the sensor where the vibration is felt. Steering-wheel vibration suggests the front; seat or floor vibration suggests the driveline, drive axle or rear wheels. Select the additional road tests below.

steps.title: Separate stationary engine-speed and loaded symptoms
steps.body: For the Neutral Engine Run-Up (NERU) Test, install a tachometer and raise engine speed from idle to approximately 4,000 RPM in NEUTRAL, recording the symptom. The Drive Engine Run-Up (DERU) Test applies to an automatic transmission: block all wheels, set the parking brake and firmly hold the service brake. Vary speed from idle to approximately 2,000 rpm in DRIVE, then repeat in REVERSE. Limit engine loading to 5 seconds. Reproduction directs attention to engine and transmission mounts.

steps.title: Isolate belt-driven accessories when justified
steps.body: For a definitely engine-speed-related complaint, follow the Engine Accessory Test. Block all wheels, set the parking brake and firmly apply the service brake. Remove the accessory belt or belts and reproduce the relevant engine speed, limiting belt-off running to one minute or less. Persistence excludes the belts and accessories; disappearance calls for reinstalling belts individually, as applicable, to isolate the source.

steps.title: Recreate a cold-start complaint
steps.body: For the Vehicle Cold Soak Procedure, match or document the original conditions. Leave the vehicle at or below the concern temperature for 6–8 hours. Inspect under the hood before starting and time the noise for up to 3 minutes. Listen around the vehicle, then narrow its location with EngineEAR or a stethoscope. Never probe moving parts.

steps.title: Compare frequencies and vibration orders
steps.body: Record EVA readings in average mode, allowing for its plus-or-minus 2 Hertz (Hz) range. Repeat measurements near the suspected source at the same road speed; matching frequency identifies a likely area. Use tire diameter, speed and the chart to calculate tire/wheel frequency, then the applicable axle-shaft and driveshaft frequencies. For engine-related symptoms, calculate engine, accessory and firing frequencies. Divide revolutions per minute (RPM) by 60 to obtain Hz. Order describes repetitions per revolution, so a second-order vibration occurs twice per revolution.

steps.title: Follow the causal system into component diagnosis
steps.body: Use the symptom charts in the linked procedure to select further testing. Front, rear or stationary noise may involve several systems; confirm the origin and transfer path before repair. Use engine- and equipment-matched procedures, then repeat the original road or system test.

watchFor.title: Load-test and belt-off limits
watchFor.body: Exceeding the DERU load duration can damage the transmission. Excessive running without accessory belts can seriously damage the engine.

watchFor.title: A receiving component can mislead you
watchFor.body: A loud component unrelated to the operating condition may be reacting to transmitted vibration. Trace its contact path before authorizing replacement.

notes: Apply only fitted-equipment branches. Front-wheel-drive run-up instructions, electric traction-motor checks and hybrid cooling-pump checks are not Mustang instructions here.
A reed tachometer measures frequency but not amplitude. A Sirometer finds frequency by adjusting a wire until it resonates. Analyzer strobe functions help isolate rotating sources.
For wind leaks, place the ultrasonic transmitter inside and sweep outside suspected seals. Squeak-and-rattle kit tapes, oil and grease address identified contact noises.

diagnostics.finding: Heavy Acceleration Test reproduces the concern
diagnostics.meaning: Reproduction during hard acceleration followed by lower-gear deceleration indicates a torque-related complaint.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the corresponding powertrain or mounting path.

diagnostics.finding: Neutral Coast Down Speed Test reproduces the concern
diagnostics.meaning: Coasting in NEUTRAL from above the symptom speed through it identifies a vehicle-speed-related concern and excludes the engine as its source.
diagnostics.next: Compare wheel and driveline frequencies.

diagnostics.finding: Steering Input Test changes the symptom
diagnostics.meaning: Sweeping turns in both directions alter loading; wheel bearings, hubs and tire tread wear become candidates.
diagnostics.next: Inspect these areas without treating the response as proof of one failed part.

diagnostics.finding: Brake Test reproduces noise or vibration
diagnostics.meaning: After warming the brakes with light decelerations, brake application may produce vibration at the steering wheel, seat or pedal, or noise that diminishes on release.
diagnostics.next: Use the complete test’s prescribed speeds and proceed to brake diagnosis if the relationship is confirmed.

diagnostics.finding: Road Test Over Bumps localizes a noise
diagnostics.meaning: Crossing roughness one wheel at a time distinguishes front from rear and left from right.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the corresponding suspension or body area.

diagnostics.finding: Measured vibration matches tire-speed orders
diagnostics.meaning: First order includes tires, wheels, bearings, driveshaft or brake discs; second order points to tires/wheels; third order includes tires/wheels or driveshaft.
diagnostics.next: Follow the matching chart. Imbalance alone produces first-order vibration.

diagnostics.finding: Measured vibration matches driveshaft or powertrain orders
diagnostics.meaning: First-order driveshaft vibration routes to the driveshaft, second to axle shafts and third to the drive axle. Engine and powertrain orders can involve the engine, mounts, transmission, exhaust or accessories.
diagnostics.next: Use the appropriate order chart to choose component testing rather than guessing from frequency alone.

diagnostics.finding: Amplitude is 0.06 Gs or less
diagnostics.meaning: That measured vibration is barely perceptible.
diagnostics.next: No corrective action is required for that vibration; assess any separate noise complaint independently.

verification.title: Repeat the original conditions
verification.body: After the confirmed repair, repeat the same road or system test to establish that the complaint is corrected or within an acceptable range.

verification.title: Retain comparable results
verification.body: Record before-and-after frequency, amplitude, sensor location, speed and operating conditions so improvement can be assessed objectively.

procedures.purpose: Complete NVH diagnosis: tools, road and stationary tests, cold-soak testing, frequency calculations and symptom-based routing.

guides.title: Diagnose suspension pull, uneven ride and noise
guides.summary: Check loading, tires and visible suspension condition, then use wheel exchanges, brake-drag screening and alignment measurements to narrow down a pull. Match noises to the driving conditions that produce them before choosing a repair.
guides.introduction:
A Mustang suspension has enough moving parts to form a percussion section. Unfortunately, a clunk does not come with a little label naming the guilty bastard. I’ll help you separate what happens over bumps, during turns and under braking, then work through the checks in a useful order.

This guide covers 2015 Mustangs with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines. Springs support the body, struts and shock absorbers control its movement, and suspension arms and joints keep the wheels located as they move. Tires, brakes and steering can create similar complaints, so we’ll give those their turn before condemning the suspension.
guides.why: The useful clue is often the load that produces the symptom. Bumps move suspension parts up and down; turning twists and flexes them; braking applies rearward and downward loads; acceleration loads the powertrain mounts. Following those clues, and changing one influence at a time during the pull test, gives a reason for the next action instead of an expensive parts lottery.

when.summary: Use this guide for a currently present pull, wander, uneven stance, abnormal tire wear, harsh ride, shimmy or repeatable suspension-related noise.
notes: A symptom description identifies possible causes; it does not prove that any listed component needs replacement.
Factory specifications do not apply to vehicles with aftermarket steering, suspension, wheel or tire equipment.
For an intermittent complaint, establish the conditions that reproduce it. Do not replace components through a diagnostic branch when its named concern is absent.

prepare.title: Know where this job ends
prepare.detail: I’ll cover preliminary inspection, wheel removal and refitting, and the drift/pull decision sequence. Component dismantling, joint or bearing wear measurements, ride-height measurement and alignment adjustment require their matching procedures and specifications. The linked repair destinations are the next stage of work. Before a tire exchange, establish that the fitted assemblies can occupy the proposed positions, including any size or directional restrictions; an incompatible arrangement needs matching tire/fitment guidance.

prepare.title: Gather tools and material for the checks you will perform
prepare.detail: Have a tire-pressure gauge, access to the Vehicle Certification (VC) label, suitable wheel-nut removal equipment and a torque wrench capable of 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). Wheel swapping and the brake-drag check require suitable lifting equipment. Have cleaning materials for the wheel bore and mounting surfaces, plus Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, for the wheel pilot interface. Alignment checking requires alignment equipment and its manufacturer's instructions. An electronic listening tool such as Chassis Ear is optional for noise isolation.

prepare.title: Arrange safe lifting
prepare.detail: Identify the lifting points by the triangles stamped into the body structure or frame. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; use floor stands. The emergency jack supplied with the car is intended for changing a deflated tire, not this workshop inspection. The wheel-removal procedure positions the vehicle in Neutral on a hoist. See [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631).

prepare.title: Review what changed before the complaint
prepare.detail: Check previous repairs and whether the steering, suspension, wheels or tires have been altered. An incorrectly completed repair can contribute to the present problem. Check relevant service information or bulletins when available. See [Diagnostic Methods](#/document/G1693185).

prepare.title: Keep electronic diagnosis on its own branch
prepare.detail: If the investigation moves into electronic steering diagnosis, use its matching diagnostic procedure. General prerequisites include correct battery and charging operation, battery state of charge above 70%, and checking related diagnostic trouble codes across the network modules. Address circuit faults before system or performance faults. Connector probing and scan-tool commands are outside the mechanical checks below.

steps.title: Identify the car and decode its spring application
steps.body:
Find the VIN on the metal tab at the upper left of the instrument panel, visible through the windshield. It is also on the VC label. VIN position 10 identifies model year: F means 2015. Position 8 identifies the engine: H is 2.3L, M is 3.7L, F is 5.0L and Z is 5.2L.

Open the left-hand door to locate the VC label in the door opening. Use its tire information for the pressure and size checks. Find the SPR field near the bottom of the label. Its spring code has two parts: the first identifies the front springs and the second identifies the rear springs. Decode each part separately using these mappings from [Identification Codes](#/document/G1663651).

Front spring codes:
AA → BR33-5310-A
BB → BR33-5310-B
CC → BR33-5310-C
FF → BR33-5310-F
GG → BR33-5310-G

Rear spring codes:
AA → BR33-5560-A
BB → BR33-5560-B
CC → BR33-5560-C
DD → BR33-5560-D
EE → BR33-5560-E
FF → BR33-5560-F
GG → BR33-5560-G
JJ → BR3V-5560-J
LL → BR3V-5560-L
MM → AR3V-5560-M
NN → AR33-5560-N

Record the front and rear spring identifications for comparison when checking whether the correct springs are fitted. The same two-letter code can identify different front and rear parts, so keep those lists straight. Ride height alone does not identify a spring.

Look for aftermarket changes to steering, suspension, wheels and tires. If present, the factory specifications used by this diagnostic route do not apply to that modified equipment.

steps.title: Check loading before blaming the suspension
steps.body:
Visually check for an unevenly loaded, incorrectly loaded or overloaded vehicle. Loading is a possible cause of pull, wander, excessive sway and a one-sided lean.

For the pull test, this is A1: if the vehicle is unevenly loaded, address that loading condition and explain its effect to the driver before continuing. If it is evenly loaded, proceed to the tire checks. I like this starting point: luggage is usually less expensive to move than suspension parts.

steps.title: Check cold tire pressures, sizes and visible condition
steps.body:
With the normal loads in the vehicle and the tires cold, measure the pressures and compare them with the VC label. Check that all tire sizes match the vehicle's specified fitment.

Look over the tires for damage and abnormal or uneven wear. Note whether wear is concentrated at the center ribs, both edges, or an inner or outer edge. These patterns help choose the tire-wear branch below, but they do not establish one cause on their own.

For pull-test step A2, adjust incorrect pressures to the label values and address tires needing replacement before continuing. When pressures and tire condition are acceptable, proceed to tire-force isolation. Detailed tire evaluation belongs with [Wheels and Tires](#/document/G1686502).

steps.title: Reproduce and describe the complaint on a smooth road
steps.body:
Road-test on a smooth road to verify the reported concern. Record whether it is a directional pull, wander, an off-center steering wheel, a ride-height concern, vibration or noise.

For a noise, record the event that brings it on: bumps, turning, braking, acceleration, driveway entries or dips. Distinguish a turning noise during normal steering movement from one occurring specifically at the full-left or full-right steering stop. That distinction changes the next decision.

Use the same description when you recheck the car later. 'Still sounds weird' gives the diagnosis very little to work with.

steps.title: Lift only at the designated points when underside access is needed
steps.body:
Before lifting, use a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Confirm that the jack or hoist is rated for the vehicle, including cargo and modifications. A jack alone is never a support for working underneath: use suitable stands at the designated points. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

For hoist-based wheel work, place the transmission in Neutral and position the vehicle on the hoist. Locate the stamped triangles before raising it. The lifting-point illustration identifies four positions along the sides of the body: behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels. Confirm the actual triangle markings on the car rather than estimating from a wheel opening.

Position adapters or forks so they do not interfere with suspension parts, mounting brackets or stabilizer mounting brackets. Avoid contact that could damage the axle or rear cover, steering linkage or exhaust. Never apply jack pressure to either bumper.

For a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving onto it. If a jack is used during workshop work, support the vehicle with floor stands before going underneath. See [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631).

steps.title: Expose the visible condition before choosing a repair
steps.body:
Remove excessive mud, dirt and road deposits from the chassis and underbody so they do not hide the parts you are checking.

Look over the front and rear suspension components and their fasteners; springs and their application; front struts; rear shock absorbers; bushings; steering components; and wheel hubs and bearings. The symptom branches below identify specific findings to pursue, including displaced spring seats, out-of-position stabilizer bushings and damaged mounts.

Correct an obvious cause, where possible, before continuing. A visible fault should lead to the appropriate repair or closer examination; an assembly that merely looks intact has not passed a joint, bearing or damper test.

For the front-suspension ball-joint branches—wander, sticky steering, front bump noise, turning noise, braking noise and clunk/pop/thump—have the ball joints inspected. A confirmed ball-joint fault calls for replacement of the affected control arm as necessary, using the applicable [Front Lower Arm](#/document/G1692532) or [Rear Lower Arm](#/document/G1692538) repair destination. These named lower-arm destinations belong to the front-suspension branches; they are not replacement instructions for rear-suspension toe-link or cross-axis joints.

This preliminary inspection does not call for unplugging wiring, removing brake calipers or dismantling a strut.

steps.title: Enter the pull test only after loading and tires are acceptable
steps.body:
For a currently present drift or pull, keep the order of [Suspension System Test A](#/document/G1686610): A1 loading, A2 tire pressures and condition, A3 tire-force isolation, A4 brake drag, then A5 alignment.

If you found uneven loading or a tire problem, correct that first and recheck the original complaint. Move to A3 when loading is even and tire pressures and condition are acceptable. Do not skip straight to an alignment adjustment because the steering wheel happens to be pointing at the scenery.

steps.title: Plan the A3 wheel exchange and record the original pull
steps.body:
Note which direction the car pulls before changing wheel positions. A3 exchanges the complete front wheel-and-tire assemblies from left to right; it does not call for removing tires from their wheels.

Confirm that the fitted assemblies permit that exchange. The later branch may call for front-to-rear rotation, so confirm compatibility for that exchange separately. If either required exchange is incompatible with the fitted arrangement, stop that swap branch and obtain applicable tire/fitment guidance.

Use the following removal and refitting actions for every wheel moved during this test. See [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Remove the wheel assemblies without heating seized nuts
steps.body:
With the vehicle in Neutral and correctly positioned and raised on the hoist, remove the five wheel nuts, then take the wheel-and-tire assembly off the hub. Repeat for the other wheel being exchanged and keep track of each assembly's original position.

Do not use heat to free a seized wheel nut. Heat can damage both the wheel and the wheel bearing. Resolve a seized attachment before continuing the exchange.

steps.title: Clean both mounting faces and the central pilot bore
steps.body:
Before refitting, remove corrosion, dirt and other foreign material from the wheel mounting face and the mating mounting surface on the hub and brake disc or drum, as fitted.

Clean the wheel's central pilot bore too. This is the hole that fits around the hub's central locating projection; wipe and clean this bore before applying lubricant. Cleaning only the flat face around it leaves part of the job unfinished.

Make sure any fasteners securing the brake rotor to the hub are secured and do not interfere with the wheel's mounting surface.

The wheel must seat correctly. Contamination or an interfering fastener can allow the wheel nuts to loosen and the wheel to detach while driving, causing loss of control and serious injury or death.

steps.title: Apply XL-2 only at the pilot interface
steps.body:
Apply a thin film of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, only where the cleaned wheel pilot bore meets the hub pilot.

Keep the lubricant off the flat wheel-to-brake-disc/drum mounting surfaces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and brake-disc friction surfaces. The wheel-stud and wheel-nut threads must be clean and dry for the stated torque.

steps.title: Position the exchanged wheels and start the nuts by hand
steps.body:
Place each wheel-and-tire assembly on its intended hub for this stage of the test. Install all five wheel nuts finger tight only at this stage.

Final wheel-nut tightening is performed with the vehicle resting on its tires.

steps.title: Lower onto the tires and tighten all five nuts in a star pattern
steps.body:
Before lowering, reapply the parking brake and restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground. Keep the vehicle restrained for the final wheel-nut tightening.

With the vehicle resting on its tires, tighten the wheel nuts in a star/cross pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), using clean, dry stud and nut threads.

To follow the illustrated sequence, view the wheel face with one nut at the top: tighten the top nut first, lower-left second, upper-right third, upper-left fourth and lower-right fifth. This crosses the wheel instead of proceeding around the circle.

Incorrect sequencing can produce excessive brake-disc runout—side-to-side deviation as the disc turns—which can contribute to brake roughness, shudder and vibration.

Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after wheel reinstallation. Wheels can loosen after initial tightening; this follow-up applies after any wheel moved during the diagnosis. Failure to retighten can result in serious injury.

steps.title: Road-test and interpret the A3 result
steps.body:
After crossing the front assemblies and completing wheel tightening, road-test to establish whether the vehicle still pulls and in which direction.

If the pull disappears, tire forces caused the complaint and the exchange has corrected it.

If the pull reverses direction, tire forces are responsible. Test A directs front-to-rear rotation of the wheel-and-tire assemblies. Make that exchange only with compatible fitment, using the same cleaning, lubricant restrictions and refitting actions above, then recheck the complaint.

If the pull remains in the same direction, continue to A4.

steps.title: Check all four wheels for brake drag at A4
steps.body:
Raise and support the vehicle using the designated lifting points and the precautions in step 5. Raise all four wheels fully clear of the ground and confirm the vehicle is securely supported. Keep the engine off. With the complete wheel-and-tire assemblies fitted and the transmission in Neutral, release the parking brake and fully release the service-brake pedal before spinning each assembly by hand. Check whether all four turn freely. The [brake-system check](#/document/G1721936) likewise checks wheel rotation with the brakes released; applied brakes would invalidate this check.

If any wheel does not spin freely, stop this sequence and move to [Brake System diagnosis](#/document/G1721936) to investigate brake drag. This screening result does not identify a particular caliper or bearing as faulty.

If all four wheels spin freely, continue to A5. Judge this check by free rotation; it does not establish a numerical spin-time or resistance limit.

Before lowering after this check, reapply the parking brake. Restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground, and keep the vehicle restrained afterward. Do not lower an unrestrained vehicle in Neutral.

steps.title: Check alignment at A5, then choose the correct destination
steps.body:
Use alignment equipment and its manufacturer's instructions to check wheel alignment against the correct vehicle specifications. Toe describes the direction the wheels point relative to one another; an alignment check is a measurement, not an invitation to turn adjusters by eye.

If alignment is outside specification, arrange the appropriate adjustment using the matching specifications and procedure. Test A names front toe adjustment as its repair destination.

If alignment is within specification, continue with [Power Steering diagnosis](#/document/G1757488) for the remaining drift, pull or wander. Retain the measured alignment results so the next decision rests on actual readings.

steps.title: Use the matching noise branch to localize the next inspection
steps.body:
For noise, vibration and harshness—usually shortened to NVH—use the diagnostic rows below to match the operating condition to possible sources. Check the indicated area for the named loose, displaced or damaged items before deciding on a repair.

An electronic listening tool such as Chassis Ear may help isolate the source. Use its manufacturer's attachment and operating instructions, choosing connection areas from the possible sources in the matching branch.

If the suspension is not the source, continue through [NVH diagnosis](#/document/G1663637) to identify the next likely system. A nearby exhaust, mount or brake can make a perfectly innocent suspension sound guilty.

steps.title: Close the check with a finding and a specific next action
steps.body:
After a correction, repeat the original driving condition and establish whether the complaint remains. Record what was found, what was changed and the result.

For pull diagnosis, retain the original pull direction, the result after the front-wheel exchange, any front-to-rear rotation, the four-wheel brake-drag result and the alignment readings reached in the sequence. For noise, record the triggering event and the component area actually implicated.

If the next action is a repair, identify the exact component and applicable engine or equipment branch. If wheels were reinstalled, include wheel-nut retightening within 160 km (100 mi) in the completion plan.

watchFor.title: An unsupported vehicle is a stop condition
watchFor.body: Use the designated lifting points. Never get beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Position hoist adapters to avoid interference with suspension, steering, exhaust and mounting brackets, and damage to the axle or rear cover.

watchFor.title: A clean mounting face and a lubricated pilot are different requirements
watchFor.body: Clean both mating mounting faces and the central wheel pilot bore. XL-2 belongs only at the pilot-bore/hub-pilot interface. Keep mounting faces, friction surfaces, studs and nuts free of anti-seize.

watchFor.title: A sound description is not a replacement order
watchFor.body: The same clunk, rattle or pull can come from several systems. Correct an obvious cause first, then use the matching component examination before replacing parts. A symptom chart does not establish a ball-joint movement limit, bearing-play limit or damper test.

watchFor.title: Carbon-fiber and alloy wheels need suitable tire machines
watchFor.body: If tire replacement becomes necessary, use a center-clamp tire changer such as Hunter Auto 34, Revolution, TC3900 or equivalent. Do not use a table-top machine that grips inside the wheel and rides on the front flange. Balancing equipment must avoid contact with the wheel face, as with a Hunter Road Force Touch GSP9700. Unsuitable equipment can damage the wheel.

watchFor.title: Hub destinations have strict applicability
watchFor.body: The general front-hub destination covers the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L. The separate SVT Performance Package front-hub destination covers the 5.2L with that equipment. Neither is a rear-bearing repair procedure. A 5.2L without confirmed SVT Performance Package applicability needs a matching front-hub repair procedure.

watchFor.title: Keep engine-specific referrals on their own engines
watchFor.body: The exhaust and front-subframe destinations linked here cover the 2.3L only. The left- and right-hand engine-mount destinations cover the 3.7L only. Other engines require matching procedures for those branches.

notes: Use the owner's literature for tire-rotation intervals.
The VC label's spring code identifies an application; a ride-height check measures the vehicle's stance. One does not substitute for the other.

For the front-suspension ball-joint branches, replace the affected control arm as necessary after confirming the joint fault. The Front Lower Arm and Rear Lower Arm destinations named there must not automatically be treated as instructions for rear-suspension control arms, toe-link joints or cross-axis joints.
Final wheel-nut torque is 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), in a star/cross pattern, with the vehicle resting on its tires and the stud and nut threads clean and dry.

diagnostics.finding: A1: The vehicle is unevenly loaded
diagnostics.meaning: Uneven loading is a possible cause of drift or pull and must be addressed before the remaining test.
diagnostics.next: Correct the loading condition, explain its effect to the driver and recheck the complaint. With loading even, move to A2.

diagnostics.finding: A2: Tire pressure or tire condition is unacceptable
diagnostics.meaning: Incorrect pressure or a tire needing replacement can influence the pull.
diagnostics.next: Adjust cold pressures to the VC label or arrange tire replacement as necessary. Use [Wheels and Tires](#/document/G1686502) for detailed tire evaluation. Continue to A3 when pressures and tire condition are acceptable.

diagnostics.finding: A3: Pull disappears after exchanging the front assemblies left to right
diagnostics.meaning: Tire forces caused the original pull, and the exchange has corrected the concern.
diagnostics.next: Record the result and complete the wheel-refitting checks and wheel-nut retightening within 160 km (100 mi).

diagnostics.finding: A3: Pull reverses direction after exchanging the front assemblies
diagnostics.meaning: The direction change identifies tire forces as the cause.
diagnostics.next: Rotate the wheel-and-tire assemblies front to rear where the fitted arrangement permits that exchange. Use the wheel cleaning and refitting steps, then recheck the complaint. If fitment prevents the exchange, obtain matching tire/fitment guidance.

diagnostics.finding: A3: Pull remains in the same direction after the front exchange
diagnostics.meaning: The test directs the investigation beyond tire-force isolation.
diagnostics.next: Proceed to A4 and spin all four wheel-and-tire assemblies by hand on the properly supported vehicle.

diagnostics.finding: A4: One or more wheels do not spin freely
diagnostics.meaning: The brake-drag branch must be investigated before continuing to alignment.
diagnostics.next: Use [Brake System diagnosis](#/document/G1721936). Do not identify a particular caliper or bearing as failed from this screening result alone.

diagnostics.finding: A4: All four wheels spin freely
diagnostics.meaning: The brake-drag screen permits the sequence to continue.
diagnostics.next: Proceed to the equipment-based alignment check at A5.

diagnostics.finding: A5: Alignment is outside specification
diagnostics.meaning: Incorrect alignment is a possible source of the pull.
diagnostics.next: Arrange the appropriate alignment correction using matching specifications and adjustment instructions. Test A identifies front toe adjustment as the repair destination. Recheck the original concern after correction.

diagnostics.finding: A5: Alignment is within specification but the pull remains
diagnostics.meaning: The sequence directs the investigation into the steering system.
diagnostics.next: Continue with [Power Steering diagnosis](#/document/G1757488) for drift, pull or wander.

diagnostics.finding: The vehicle wanders
diagnostics.meaning: Possible sources include incorrect loading, ball joints, damaged or missing front strut mount bearings, loose or damaged front wheel bearings, suspension or steering components, loose fasteners and excessive total front toe-out.
diagnostics.next: Correct loading first. Have the implicated joints, bearings and attachments evaluated before replacement or tightening to their component specifications. Inspect the ball joints; for a confirmed joint fault, install a new affected control arm as necessary through the applicable [Front Lower Arm](#/document/G1692532) or [Rear Lower Arm](#/document/G1692538) destination. Other repair destinations include [Front Strut and Spring Assembly](#/document/G1692536) and the applicable front hub: [2.3L/3.7L/5.0L](#/document/G1692537) or [5.2L with SVT Performance Package](#/document/G1692554). Check alignment for excessive total front toe-out and use [Power Steering](#/document/G1757488) when steering is implicated. If inspection confirms a damaged or missing front strut mount bearing, install a new bearing as necessary using the strut-assembly procedure. Confirmed loose, worn or damaged front wheel bearings require new bearings as necessary through the applicable hub procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The front bottoms out or rides low
diagnostics.meaning: Worn, damaged or incorrect springs and worn front struts are possible sources.
diagnostics.next: Use [Ride Height Measurement](#/document/G1686616) to establish the stance before deciding on springs. Compare the spring application with the separate front and rear code mappings in step 1. For a confirmed front spring or strut repair, continue to [Front Strut and Spring Assembly](#/document/G1692536).

diagnostics.finding: Tires have abnormal or uneven wear
diagnostics.meaning: Pressure can contribute to rapid center-rib or inner-and-outer-edge wear. Rotation history, high-speed cornering, excessive front or rear toe, excessive positive or negative camber, and suspension condition are also possible influences. Camber is the wheel's inward or outward tilt.
diagnostics.next: Set cold pressures from the VC label and check rotation history against the owner's literature. Use [Wheels and Tires](#/document/G1686502) for the wear investigation, and arrange alignment and suspension evaluation where indicated. Do not diagnose pressure or alignment solely from one wear pattern.

diagnostics.finding: Steering feels sticky or does not return readily
diagnostics.meaning: Damaged or worn front strut mount bearings, binding ball joints and steering components are possible sources.
diagnostics.next: Have the implicated parts evaluated. Confirmed strut-bearing repairs lead to [Front Strut and Spring Assembly](#/document/G1692536). Inspect the ball joints for binding; a confirmed ball-joint fault calls for a new affected control arm as necessary through the applicable [Front Lower Arm](#/document/G1692532) or [Rear Lower Arm](#/document/G1692538) destination. Continue steering investigation through [Power Steering](#/document/G1757488). If inspection confirms a damaged or worn front strut mount bearing, install a new bearing as necessary through the front strut-assembly procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The steering wheel is off-center
diagnostics.meaning: Unequal side-to-side front or rear toe settings and steering-component problems are possible sources.
diagnostics.next: Obtain an alignment check covering front and rear toe. Use the matching front or rear toe adjustment procedure for an out-of-specification result; continue with [Power Steering](#/document/G1757488) if steering components are implicated.

diagnostics.finding: The vehicle sways or rolls excessively
diagnostics.meaning: Possible sources include loading, loose wheel nuts, struts or shocks, loose stabilizer bracket-to-frame bolts, worn stabilizer bushings or links, a damaged bar, and worn springs. The stabilizer bar helps resist body roll.
diagnostics.next: Correct loading and address loose wheel nuts through the wheel-refitting steps. For confirmed component concerns, use [Front Strut and Spring Assembly](#/document/G1692536), [Rear Shock Absorber](#/document/G1686650), [Front Stabilizer Bar](#/document/G1692533), [Front Stabilizer Bar Bushing](#/document/G1692534), [Front Stabilizer Bar Link](#/document/G1692535), or [Rear Spring](#/document/G1686654), as applicable. Stabilizer bracket bolts require their own specification, not the wheel-nut torque. Replace confirmed worn stabilizer bushings or links, or the bar assembly, as necessary. A damaged or broken stabilizer bar requires a new bar or bar assembly. Replace confirmed worn springs as necessary. Use the matching linked procedure for installation; these decisions do not supply its dismantling or tightening instructions.

diagnostics.finding: The vehicle leans to one side
diagnostics.meaning: Uneven or excessive loading, front or rear suspension condition, and incorrect side-to-side ride height are possible sources.
diagnostics.next: Address loading, then use [Ride Height Measurement](#/document/G1686616) to establish whether the lean is outside specification. Evaluate the front and rear suspension for the cause before selecting replacement components.

diagnostics.finding: Front squeak, creak or rattle occurs mainly over bumps or rough roads
diagnostics.meaning: Vertical suspension movement can expose a loose strut top nut, jounce-bumper concern, displaced stabilizer bushings/isolators/locating pins, steering or tie-rod problems, brake-caliper concerns, lower-arm or ball-joint problems, hub concerns, exhaust or mount concerns, or subframe weld/insulator problems.
diagnostics.next: Look for the named displaced stabilizer parts and use the localized finding to choose a destination: [strut assembly](#/document/G1692536), [stabilizer bar](#/document/G1692533), [front stabilizer bushing](#/document/G1692534), [front stabilizer link](#/document/G1692535), [Power Steering](#/document/G1757488), [Brake System](#/document/G1721936), or the applicable front-hub procedure. Inspect ball joints; a confirmed joint fault calls for a new affected control arm as necessary through [Front Lower Arm](#/document/G1692532) or [Rear Lower Arm](#/document/G1692538), as applicable. A jounce bumper—the suspension travel cushion—may require lubrication or replacement after evaluation; the wheel-pilot lubricant is not a specification for that job. Engine-specific destinations are [2.3L Exhaust System](#/document/G1688077), [3.7L Engine Mount LH](#/document/G1681518), [3.7L Engine Mount RH](#/document/G1681519), and [2.3L Front Subframe](#/document/G1686629). Other engines need matching procedures.

diagnostics.finding: Rear squeak, creak or rattle occurs mainly over bumps or rough roads
diagnostics.meaning: Possible sources include loose or damaged rear shocks or shock bushings, damaged springs or spring mounts, worn or damaged stabilizer bushings or links, and worn or damaged lower control arms, toe-link ball joints or cross-axis joints.
diagnostics.next: Look for the named loose or damaged parts. Confirmed repairs lead to [Rear Shock Absorber](#/document/G1686650), [Rear Spring](#/document/G1686654), [Rear Stabilizer Bar Bushing](#/document/G1686652), or [Rear Stabilizer Bar Link](#/document/G1686653). Rear control-arm, toe-link and cross-axis-joint work needs matching rear-suspension instructions; the lower-arm destinations cited in the front-suspension branches are not substitutes. Inspect the rear lower control arms, toe-link ball joints and cross-axis joints for wear or damage; replace confirmed worn or damaged components as necessary using the matching rear-suspension procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The front crunches or ratchets while turning, away from the specific full-lock-stop condition
diagnostics.meaning: Twisting and flexing can load the strut top attachment and bearing, coil spring, strut brackets or seats, stabilizer bar, steering gear, tie-rod ends, hubs and lower-arm ball joints.
diagnostics.next: Localize the concern and evaluate those items. Use [Front Strut and Spring Assembly](#/document/G1692536), [Front Stabilizer Bar](#/document/G1692533), [Power Steering](#/document/G1757488), [Tie Rod End](#/document/G1686682), or the applicable front-hub destination for a confirmed finding. Inspect ball joints; replace the affected control arm as necessary for a confirmed joint fault using the applicable [Front Lower Arm](#/document/G1692532) or [Rear Lower Arm](#/document/G1692538) destination. A strut top nut must be tightened to its own specification.

diagnostics.finding: A crunch, clunk or grunt comes specifically from the steering stops at full left or right lock
diagnostics.meaning: This identified steering-stop condition is normal.
diagnostics.next: No repair is required for that condition. Keep noises occurring during other parts of steering travel in the separate turning-noise branch.

diagnostics.finding: Noise occurs while braking
diagnostics.meaning: Braking applies rearward and downward loads to the suspension and subframe. Possible sources include front brake calipers, hubs, lower arms/ball joints and powertrain mounts.
diagnostics.next: Continue with [Brake System](#/document/G1721936) for caliper concerns or the applicable front-hub destination for a localized hub finding. Inspect ball joints; a confirmed joint fault calls for a new affected control arm as necessary through the applicable [Front Lower Arm](#/document/G1692532) or [Rear Lower Arm](#/document/G1692538) destination. For mount concerns on the 3.7L, use [Engine Mount LH](#/document/G1681518) and [RH](#/document/G1681519). Mount investigation on another engine needs matching instructions.

diagnostics.finding: Noise occurs while accelerating
diagnostics.meaning: Powertrain torque and flex can load the mounts. Other possible areas are body structure, hubs, exhaust and subframe welds or insulators.
diagnostics.next: Examine the inner fender, bulkhead, seams and pinch welds when the noise is localized to body structure. Relevant component destinations are the applicable front hub, [3.7L Engine Mount LH](#/document/G1681518), [3.7L Engine Mount RH](#/document/G1681519), [2.3L Exhaust System](#/document/G1688077), and [2.3L Front Subframe](#/document/G1686629). Other engine configurations require matching mount, exhaust or subframe guidance.

diagnostics.finding: Noise occurs entering driveways or crossing dips and depressions
diagnostics.meaning: Body, subframe and suspension twisting can load body seams and welds, stabilizer links and subframe welds or insulators.
diagnostics.next: Localize the noise among the inner fender, bulkhead, seams, pinch welds, stabilizer links and subframe. Confirmed link repairs lead to [Front Stabilizer Bar Link](#/document/G1692535) or [Rear Stabilizer Bar Link](#/document/G1686653). The linked [Front Subframe](#/document/G1686629) destination covers the 2.3L only; body repairs and other subframe configurations need matching instructions.

diagnostics.finding: A clunk, pop, thump or thud sounds like parts striking or shifting under load
diagnostics.meaning: A clunk is often repeatable, rhythmic and metallic. Possible sources include loose fasteners, displaced or damaged bushings, worn or damaged struts/shocks, an out-of-position spring or spring seat, and worn or damaged ball joints.
diagnostics.next: Look specifically for loose nuts or bolts, displaced bushings, and a displaced or damaged spring or seat. Use the relevant repair procedure before tightening, repositioning or replacement. Confirmed damper repairs lead to [Front Strut and Spring Assembly](#/document/G1692536) or [Rear Shock Absorber](#/document/G1686650). Inspect ball joints; a confirmed fault in the front-suspension ball-joint branch calls for a new affected control arm as necessary through the applicable [Front Lower Arm](#/document/G1692532) or [Rear Lower Arm](#/document/G1692538) destination.

diagnostics.finding: A rapid, repetitive rattle occurs over rough or uneven surfaces at low speed
diagnostics.meaning: Possible sources include loose fasteners or brackets; loose or damaged struts, shocks or shock bushings; dust boots; jounce bumpers; damaged springs or mounts; worn control/radius-arm bushings; and worn stabilizer bushings or links.
diagnostics.next: Look for loose nuts and bolts and for the named out-of-position or damaged components. Tighten only to the applicable component specification. Arrange adjustment or replacement through the matching repair destination once the responsible area is identified.

diagnostics.finding: A whine, roar or groan generally occurs above 30 mph and becomes more noticeable with steering input
diagnostics.meaning: Loose or damaged front or rear wheel bearings are possible sources.
diagnostics.next: Arrange bearing evaluation rather than replacing a bearing from the sound alone. For a confirmed front repair, choose [2.3L/3.7L/5.0L Front Hub](#/document/G1692537) or [5.2L SVT Performance Package Front Hub](#/document/G1692554) only when applicable. Rear-bearing repairs need a matching rear procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The vehicle has shimmy
diagnostics.meaning: Loose wheel nuts, loose front suspension fasteners, loose front wheel bearings, and struts or shock absorbers are possible sources.
diagnostics.next: Address wheel attachments through the wheel-refitting steps. Have suspension attachments and bearings evaluated using their own specifications. Confirmed damper repairs lead to [Front Strut and Spring Assembly](#/document/G1692536) or [Rear Shock Absorber](#/document/G1686650); use the applicable front-hub destination for a confirmed bearing fault.

diagnostics.finding: Shimmy is most noticeable while coasting or decelerating and steering is also hard
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive positive caster is a possible source. Caster describes steering-axis tilt and is assessed through alignment measurement.
diagnostics.next: Arrange front-suspension and alignment evaluation. Repair or replace a component only after the responsible condition is established.

diagnostics.finding: The ride is rough or harsh
diagnostics.meaning: Incorrect tire pressure, struts or shocks, springs, and damaged suspension components are possible sources.
diagnostics.next: Check cold pressures against the VC label first. Use [Ride Height Measurement](#/document/G1686616) for the spring/stance branch. Confirmed repairs lead to [Front Strut and Spring Assembly](#/document/G1692536), [Rear Shock Absorber](#/document/G1686650), [Rear Spring](#/document/G1686654), or the matching procedure for another damaged component.

diagnostics.finding: The symptom remains, but the suspension is not identified as its source
diagnostics.meaning: Several vehicle systems can create similar noise, vibration or harshness.
diagnostics.next: Continue through [NVH diagnosis](#/document/G1663637) using a process of elimination. Preserve the triggering condition and the checks already completed so the investigation moves forward.

verification.title: Confirm every refitted wheel is ready for the road
verification.body: Before a road test, confirm that mating mounting faces and pilot bores were cleaned, XL-2 was confined to the pilot interface, and all five wheel nuts were finally tightened in the star/cross sequence to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) with the vehicle resting on its tires and threads clean and dry. This checks completion of the wheel work.

verification.title: Repeat the original condition after correction
verification.body: Recheck the same pull or noise condition that started the investigation. Record whether it disappeared, changed or remained. An unrelated quiet drive does not establish that a previously reproducible complaint is corrected.

verification.title: Keep measurements and branch results
verification.body: Retain pull directions before and after exchanges, wheel positions, brake-drag screening results, and any alignment or ride-height measurements obtained through the relevant procedures.

verification.title: Complete the wheel-nut follow-up
verification.body: Retighten wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after any wheel reinstallation. Initial tightening does not remove this requirement.

procedures.purpose: Primary preliminary inspection, suspension and NVH symptom branches, control-arm replacement decisions for confirmed ball-joint faults, and drift/pull Test A.
Diagnostic prerequisites, currently present concern requirement, previous-repair checks and electronic-diagnosis prerequisites.
VIN and VC-label locations, engine/year decoding, tire information and separate front/rear spring-code-to-part-number mappings.
Wheel removal and installation, pilot-bore cleaning and lubrication, clean/dry threads, five-nut tightening sequence, final torque and retightening interval.
Lifting-point identification, support warnings and hoist-positioning precautions.
