applicability.equipment: Factory steering, suspension, wheels and tires. Front-hub repair destinations distinguish 2.3L/3.7L/5.0L vehicles from 5.2L vehicles with the SVT Performance Package.

stepGroups.title: Establish the complaint and vehicle baseline
stepGroups.summary: Identify the configuration and spring application, check loading and tires, and reproduce the concern.

stepGroups.title: Gain safe access and inspect
stepGroups.summary: Position lifting equipment correctly and uncover visible causes.

stepGroups.title: Prepare the tire-force test
stepGroups.summary: Enter Test A in order and confirm that the required wheel exchanges are compatible.

stepGroups.title: Remove and refit the wheels
stepGroups.summary: Exchange assemblies with clean mounting surfaces, controlled pilot lubrication and correct tightening.

stepGroups.title: Interpret pull, brake and alignment results
stepGroups.summary: Use the pull direction and subsequent checks to select tire, brake or steering follow-up.

stepGroups.title: Localize noise and finish the diagnosis
stepGroups.summary: Choose the matching symptom branch and document the correction or next repair destination.

guides.title: Adjust front camber at the strut-to-spindle mounting
guides.summary: Correct measured front camber by modifying the upper strut mounting holes, fitting new service fasteners and completing alignment checks.
guides.introduction: Camber is the inward or outward lean of a wheel when viewed from the front. This procedure changes the relationship between the front strut and wheel spindle to permit correction. It involves controlled enlargement of the upper mounting hole and replacement of the original mounting hardware, followed by measurement on a wheel alignment system.
guides.why: The strut-to-spindle joint must both permit adjustment and securely retain the final setting. The hole modification, correct service bolts and final tightening sequence work together. Deburring and painting the worked area remove rough edges and protect exposed metal.

when.summary: When wheel-alignment measurements establish that front camber requires correction.
notes: Measure first; this procedure is justified by alignment results.

prepare.title: Alignment and workshop access
prepare.detail: Use a wheel alignment system according to its manufacturer's instructions. Arrange suitable vehicle lifting and support for wheel removal, mechanic's wire to support the spindle, a suitable grinding tool, deburring equipment and materials to clean and paint exposed metal.

prepare.title: Replacement hardware
prepare.detail: Obtain new service strut-to-spindle bolts and nuts for both sides and equipment capable of the specified final torque. Suspension fasteners must be the specified parts or equivalents of the same quality and design.

steps.title: Measure the starting camber
steps.body: Measure front camber using the alignment equipment and its manufacturer's instructions. Establish the required correction before disturbing either strut-to-spindle joint.

steps.title: Expose and support both joints
steps.body: Remove the wheels and tires using the wheel-and-tire procedure. On both sides, unclip the wheel-speed sensor harness and position it aside. Support the spindle with mechanic's wire before removing its attachment hardware.

steps.title: Remove and discard the original fasteners
steps.body: Note the orientation of the strut-to-spindle bolts and flag nuts, then remove and discard them on both sides. The replacement service bolts are smooth and smaller in diameter than the original splined bolts.

steps.title: Modify only the upper mounting hole
steps.body: Follow the component illustration: enlarge the upper strut-to-spindle mounting hole horizontally by 1.0 mm on each side. Preserve its height and leave the lower hole unchanged. Remove burrs, then clean and paint all exposed metal.

steps.title: Reassemble with adjustment still available
steps.body: Position each spindle and install two new service bolts and nuts per side, tightening only until snug. Reposition the wheel-speed sensor harnesses and reinstall the wheels and tires. Measure front camber again and correct the alignment before fully tightening the mounting fasteners.

steps.title: Secure and recheck the alignment
steps.body: On both sides, tighten the strut-to-spindle bolts and nuts to 250 Nm. Recheck alignment to verify the camber change, adjust front toe if necessary using its procedure, and road test the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Final tightening too early
watchFor.body: The bolts must remain snug until the alignment has been corrected. Fully tightening beforehand prevents the intended adjustment sequence.

watchFor.title: Incorrect hole modification or hardware
watchFor.body: Keep material removal within the illustrated upper-hole direction and amount. Do not reuse the discarded splined bolts or substitute lower-quality suspension fasteners.

notes: This is a workshop alignment and metal-modification task requiring accurate measurement and controlled grinding.

verification.title: Record the alignment result
verification.body: Record starting and final camber measurements. Confirm the final alignment was checked after tightening and that front toe was adjusted if required.

verification.title: Complete the road test
verification.body: Carry out the prescribed road test after the alignment and fastener work are complete.

procedures.purpose: Complete front-camber adjustment, upper-hole modification, fastener tightening and final alignment sequence.
Remove and reinstall the wheels and tires for access to the front strut-to-spindle joints.

guides.title: Adjust Front Toe at the Steering Tie Rods
guides.summary: Measure both front wheels, adjust the inner tie rods without twisting the steering boots, then recheck alignment and road test.
guides.introduction: Front toe describes how far the front wheels point inward or outward when viewed from above. The tie rods connect the steering gear to the wheels, and rotating their threaded adjustment changes each wheel’s direction. This job brings measured toe into specification while keeping the steering wheel straight ahead. It requires a wheel alignment system because the result must be measured accurately on both sides.
guides.why: The straight-ahead steering position and level working surface establish the conditions for a useful measurement. The outer tie rod jam nuts secure the adjustment. The steering gear bellows protect the moving linkage, so they must remain untwisted while the inner rods turn; otherwise the adjustment can leave the boots distorted.

when.summary: Adjust when an alignment measurement shows front toe outside the applicable specification.
notes: Measure both sides before deciding how much adjustment is needed.
Use the alignment equipment manufacturer’s instructions for setup and measurement.

prepare.title: Arrange measured alignment capability
prepare.detail: Use a wheel alignment system on a level surface. Have the applicable toe specification available rather than estimating wheel direction by eye.

prepare.title: Prepare access to both tie rods
prepare.detail: Provide access to the outer tie rod jam nuts, inner tie rods and steering gear boot clamps. Have suitable tools and a torque wrench for securing the adjustment.

steps.title: Establish the starting readings
steps.body: With the vehicle standing level and the steering wheel straight ahead, check front toe on both sides using the alignment system. Follow its manufacturer’s instructions so the readings provide a reliable starting point.

steps.title: Release the adjustment points
steps.body: Loosen the outer tie rod end jam nut on each side. Position the steering gear boot clamps aside as directed in the front toe procedure, allowing the rods to turn without winding up the bellows.

steps.title: Adjust while watching the readings
steps.body: Rotate the inner tie rods until the toe readings are within specification. Watch the bellows during rotation and prevent them from twisting. The illustrated adjustment points help distinguish the jam nut, boot clamp and rotating rod.

steps.title: Secure and remeasure
steps.body: Restore the boot clamps and secure the jam nuts to the specified 103 Nm. Recheck toe on both sides and adjust again if necessary; the final readings must confirm the secured setting.

steps.title: Complete the road test
steps.body: Road test the vehicle after the adjustment is secured and the measurements have been confirmed. Record any concern that remains rather than assuming an in-spec toe reading explains every steering complaint.

watchFor.title: Bellows winding around the rod
watchFor.body: A twisting boot means the adjustment is loading the bellows. Correct this before continuing to rotate the inner tie rod.

diagnostics.finding: One or both front toe readings are outside specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The measured wheel direction requires correction; the reading alone does not establish a failed steering component.
diagnostics.next: Adjust the inner tie rods, secure the adjustment and repeat the measurements.

verification.title: Record the final alignment result
verification.body: Record the final toe reading for each front wheel and confirm both are within the applicable specification.

verification.title: Confirm physical and driving completion
verification.body: Confirm the jam nuts are secured, the boot clamps are restored, the bellows are untwisted and the required road test is complete.

procedures.purpose: Complete front toe measurement and adjustment procedure, including both tie rods, boot precautions, fastening torque and road test.

guides.title: Adjust rear wheel camber
guides.summary: Measure rear camber, adjust the upper control arm position, and verify rear alignment before road testing.
guides.introduction: Camber is the inward or outward tilt of a wheel when viewed from behind the vehicle. It affects how the tire meets the road. This adjustment changes the upper control arm’s inboard mounting position to alter rear wheel camber. The work starts with an alignment measurement; the apparent angle of a parked wheel is not an adequate adjustment guide.
guides.why: The alignment equipment shows the effect of moving the arm, while the final fastening holds that setting in service. Suspension fasteners are safety-critical, so correct tightening and suitable replacement parts matter. Camber adjustment can also change rear toe, which is why the procedure continues beyond obtaining a satisfactory camber reading.

when.summary: When alignment measurements establish that rear camber requires adjustment.
notes: Use measured alignment results to decide whether adjustment is justified.

prepare.title: Set up alignment equipment
prepare.detail: Use a wheel alignment system and follow its manufacturer’s setup and measurement instructions. This job requires competence with alignment equipment.

prepare.title: Prepare for controlled fastening
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools to reach the upper control arm inboard nut and a torque wrench for final tightening.

steps.title: Measure the starting camber
steps.body: Follow the measurement stage in [Rear Camber Adjustment](#/document/G2361400). Establish the rear camber reading before disturbing the control arm so there is a measured starting point.

steps.title: Move the upper control arm
steps.body: Loosen the upper control arm inboard nut approximately 2 turns. Slide the arm inboard or outboard to adjust camber, using the alignment readings to establish the effect of the movement.

steps.title: Secure and recheck the setting
steps.body: Tighten the inboard nut to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). Recheck alignment to verify the camber change. If rear toe requires correction, continue with the Rear Toe Adjustment procedure in section 204-00.

steps.title: Complete the road test
steps.body: Road test the vehicle after fastening and alignment work are complete. This finishes the prescribed sequence after the stationary measurements have been verified.

watchFor.title: Unsuitable replacement fasteners
watchFor.body: If replacement is necessary, use the same or equivalent parts. Do not substitute a lesser-quality fastener or a different design.

watchFor.title: Camber corrected but toe overlooked
watchFor.body: A changed camber reading does not establish that the entire rear alignment is satisfactory; rear toe must also be assessed.

notes: The illustration identifies the sliding inboard attachment; the alignment equipment establishes the required adjustment.

diagnostics.finding: Rear toe requires correction after the camber adjustment.
diagnostics.meaning: Additional alignment work remains.
diagnostics.next: Complete Rear Toe Adjustment before the road test.

verification.title: Record the measured result
verification.body: Record starting and final camber readings and whether rear toe needed correction.

verification.title: Confirm completion
verification.body: Confirm specified nut tightening, the alignment recheck and completion of the road test.

procedures.purpose: Complete rear camber measurement, upper control arm adjustment, fastening, alignment recheck and road-test procedure.

guides.title: Adjust rear wheel toe and verify the alignment
guides.summary: Measure both rear toe settings, adjust the toe-link cams and complete any required camera alignment before road testing.
guides.introduction: Rear toe describes the direction each rear wheel points when viewed from above. Rotating the toe-link adjustment bolt changes that setting; tightening its nut secures the adjustment. This is a measured alignment operation, so the result comes from the wheel alignment system rather than the visible position of the cam.
guides.why: Tire condition, pressure and suspension wear must be checked before adjusting toe. Foreign material around the cam can prevent correct clamping, and tightening can disturb an otherwise correct setting. Vehicles equipped with Lane Departure Warning also require camera alignment so lane keeping alert and aid can function correctly.
searchTerms: lane keeping camera alignment after toe adjustment

when.summary: When alignment measurement shows rear toe needs adjustment, after checking tires and suspension.
notes: Incorrect tire wear calls for inspection and measurement; it does not by itself identify toe as the cause.

prepare.title: Arrange an alignment workstation
prepare.detail: Use a wheel alignment system, its manufacturer's instructions and a steering-wheel holding device. The vehicle must stand on a level surface, and the applicable toe specification must be available.

prepare.title: Check camera-alignment capability
prepare.detail: If Lane Departure Warning is fitted, have a compatible scan tool and the capability to complete the image processing module A (IPMA) camera alignment.

prepare.title: Prepare to inspect and clean
prepare.detail: Use hand force only when checking suspension relative movement. Have mild cleaning liquids available for the toe-link joint area.

steps.title: Check the conditions that affect measurement
steps.body: Check tire pressures, inspect the tires for incorrect wear or damage, and inspect the suspension for wear or damage. When assessing relative movement, use hand force only: tools can damage components and create movement that would not otherwise appear.

steps.title: Measure both rear wheels
steps.body: Hold the steering wheel straight ahead with the holding device. Following the alignment equipment manufacturer's instructions, measure rear toe on both sides before changing either setting.

steps.title: Clean the adjustment joints
steps.body: Follow [Rear Toe Adjustment](#/document/G2361401). Clean the general joint area using only mild liquids, preventing foreign material from entering the joint. Ensure the cam nut and bolt area is clean so it can clamp correctly.

steps.title: Adjust and secure the toe links
steps.body: On both sides, loosen the toe-link nut approximately one full turn and rotate the toe-link bolt to achieve the specified toe setting. Tighten the nut to 129 lb.ft (175 Nm), taking care not to disturb the setting.

steps.title: Recheck the secured settings
steps.body: Measure rear toe again on both sides and adjust as necessary. This confirms the settings after tightening, rather than relying on readings taken while the joints were loose.

steps.title: Complete calibration and road testing
steps.body: If Lane Departure Warning is fitted, connect the scan tool and perform IPMA camera alignment exactly as directed by the tool. Road test the vehicle after completing the applicable alignment work.

watchFor.title: Artificial suspension movement
watchFor.body: Do not use a lever or other equipment to produce movement during the relative-movement check.

watchFor.title: Toe changing during tightening
watchFor.body: A correct reading before tightening does not replace the required final recheck.

notes: The camera-alignment branch applies only to vehicles actually equipped with Lane Departure Warning.

diagnostics.finding: Tire or suspension wear or damage is found during the preliminary inspection.
diagnostics.meaning: The condition needs assessment before treating toe adjustment as the complete solution.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the inspection findings before finalizing the alignment.

diagnostics.finding: Rear toe is still outside specification after tightening.
diagnostics.meaning: The secured adjustment has not achieved the required setting.
diagnostics.next: Readjust and recheck both rear settings.

verification.title: Record the alignment result
verification.body: Record the final rear toe readings for both sides against the applicable specification.

verification.title: Confirm completion beyond the adjusters
verification.body: Record camera-alignment completion where required and the outcome of the road test.

procedures.purpose: Rear toe inspection, measurement and adjustment, with conditional IPMA camera alignment and final road test.

guides.title: Measure front and rear suspension ride height
guides.summary: Measure specified suspension reference points and calculate front and rear ride height from their differences.
guides.introduction: This ride-height check measures the vertical relationship between suspension mounting points. It does not use the wheel arch or bodywork as a reference. At the front, the reference points belong to the rear control arm within the front suspension; at the rear, they belong to the toe link. A surface gauge measures each point from the same level surface, and subtraction gives the required ride-height value.
guides.why: Using identified suspension points makes the result specific and repeatable. Correct tire pressure, a full fuel tank and a level surface establish the required measuring condition. The front and rear calculations use different numbered measurements, so keeping the readings clearly labelled matters as much as locating the points accurately.

when.summary: When front or rear suspension ride height needs to be established.
notes: This procedure obtains measurements; it does not specify an adjustment or an acceptable ride-height range.

prepare.title: Establish the measuring condition
prepare.detail: Position the vehicle on a flat, level surface, inflate the tires to the correct pressure and make sure the fuel tank is full.

prepare.title: Prepare the gauge and record
prepare.detail: Use a surface gauge. Keep separate labelled records for the front and rear reference-point measurements so their numbering cannot be confused.

steps.title: Identify the front reference points
steps.body: Use the illustration in the [ride-height procedure](#/document/G1686616) to locate the rear control arm ball-joint cap and inboard bolt within the front suspension. Measure to their centers, not to an adjacent edge or fastener surface.

steps.title: Record the front measurements
steps.body: With the surface gauge resting on the flat, level surface, measure from that surface to the center of the ball-joint cap and record this as measurement 2. Measure to the center of the control-arm inboard bolt and record this as measurement 3.

steps.title: Calculate front ride height
steps.body: Subtract measurement 2 from measurement 3. Record the result as front ride height, retaining both original readings so the calculation can be checked.

steps.title: Record the rear measurements
steps.body: Locate the rear toe link. Measure from the level surface to the center of its inboard cam bolt and record this as measurement 2. Measure to the center of its outboard bolt and record this as measurement 3.

steps.title: Calculate rear ride height
steps.body: Subtract measurement 3 from measurement 2. Record this separately as rear ride height; the numbered subtraction is the reverse of the front calculation.

watchFor.title: Confusing the front control arm with the rear axle
watchFor.body: The front measurement instruction names the rear control arm of the front suspension. The rear suspension measurement uses the toe link.

watchFor.title: Substituting convenient measuring points
watchFor.body: A wheel-arch height or a measurement to a bolt edge is not the reference-point measurement described here.

notes: Keep the same units throughout each pair of readings and its subtraction.

verification.title: Check the measuring conditions
verification.body: Confirm that the recorded readings were taken with the specified tire pressure, full fuel tank and flat, level measuring surface.

verification.title: Check the recorded results
verification.body: The front record must show measurement 3 minus measurement 2; the rear record must show measurement 2 minus measurement 3. These results alone do not establish whether a suspension component needs replacement.

procedures.purpose: Complete front and rear ride-height measuring procedure, including reference points and subtraction order.

guides.title: Overhaul and reinstall the front strut and spring assembly
guides.summary: Remove the front strut assembly, dismantle and rebuild it under controlled spring compression, then reinstall it with new specified fasteners and check front camber.
guides.introduction: The front coil spring supports the vehicle while the strut controls suspension movement and connects the assembly to the wheel spindle. The upper mount, bearing and spring seats keep these parts located as the suspension works. This job combines removal from the vehicle, bench disassembly and rebuilding, and final installation. The removal path also includes brake hardware and additional wiring where dynamic suspension or brake sensors are fitted.
guides.why: The compressed spring stores substantial energy, so its load must be controlled before the strut rod nut is removed. Component position, spring centering and bearing seating determine whether the rebuilt assembly sits correctly. Suspension fasteners are critical parts: use the specified quality, replace every fastener marked for discard and tighten each connection correctly. Front camber must be checked after installation.

when.summary: When repair requires replacement or internal servicing of a front strut, spring, mount or associated assembly component.
notes: Follow dynamic-suspension, brake-sensor and flexible-hose-bracket branches only where those items are fitted.

prepare.title: Arrange the required workshop capability
prepare.detail: This requires safe wheel and suspension access, a suitable spring compressor and vise, controlled handling of brake components, and front camber checking and adjustment capability.

prepare.title: Prepare holding and torque tools
prepare.detail: Have tools for the stabilizer-link ball stud and strut rod hex-holding features, plus torque equipment suitable for the specified connections. Do not use an impact wrench on the strut rod nut.

prepare.title: Obtain all required new fasteners
prepare.detail: Prepare a new strut rod nut, stabilizer-link upper nut, three upper mount nuts, two strut-to-spindle bolts and nuts, and two brake caliper anchor plate bolts.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and release the stabilizer link
steps.body: Follow [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507), then begin [assembly removal](#/document/G1692536). Hold the stabilizer-link ball stud with its hex feature while removing the upper nut. Discard the nut and separate the link; its low-friction joint can otherwise allow the stud to turn.

steps.title: Free the wiring and brake attachments
steps.body: Where fitted, remove the dynamic-suspension harness bracket bolt and move the bracket aside. Release the wheel-speed-sensor retainers and applicable suspension harness retainer. Disconnect the fitted brake and dynamic-suspension connectors, unclip the brake-sensor connector and wire retainers, and remove the flexible-hose bracket bolt where fitted. Remove and discard the caliper anchor plate bolts and position the caliper assembly aside.

steps.title: Remove the strut assembly from the vehicle
steps.body: Remove and discard the strut-to-wheel-spindle bolts and nuts; original bolts are splined and may need to be driven out. Separate the spindle from the strut. Remove and discard the upper mount nuts and remove the assembly.

steps.title: Control the spring load before dismantling
steps.body: Follow [bench disassembly and assembly](#/document/G1702517). Using the spring compressor and vise, compress the spring enough to relieve tension on the strut assembly. Note the position of the components before removal.

steps.title: Disassemble the unloaded strut
steps.body: Remove the cap. Use the hex-holding feature to prevent the rod turning while removing the strut rod nut, and discard the nut. Remove the upper mount, upper spring seat, spring, dust boot, jounce bumper and lower spring seat in the listed order.

steps.title: Rebuild and check component seating
steps.body: Reverse the disassembly sequence, restoring the recorded positions. Make sure the lower spring seat is properly installed, the spring is centered in it and the bearing sits evenly in the mount. With the spring controlled, hold the rod by its hex feature and tighten a new rod nut to 76 lb.ft (103 Nm). Install the cap and complete controlled release of the compressor.

steps.title: Install the assembly and brake hardware
steps.body: Fit the assembly with new upper mount nuts, then attach the spindle using new bolts and nuts. Reposition the caliper and install new anchor plate bolts. Use the distinct tightening specifications in the installation procedure for each connection. Refit the flexible-hose bracket where equipped.

steps.title: Restore the wiring, stabilizer link and wheel
steps.body: Restore the fitted brake-sensor clips and connectors, dynamic-suspension connector, wheel-speed and suspension-harness retainers, and dynamic-suspension bracket. Reconnect the stabilizer link with a new upper nut, using the hex-holding feature while tightening. Install the wheel and tire through its linked procedure.

steps.title: Check front camber
steps.body: Check front camber and adjust it if necessary using the Front Camber Adjustment procedure identified by the installation instructions.

watchFor.title: Spring load remaining on the rod nut
watchFor.body: Do not remove the rod nut until the compressor has relieved spring tension on the assembly.

watchFor.title: Reusing discarded hardware
watchFor.body: Keep the replacement-fastener list with the job through both bench work and vehicle installation.

notes: The bench illustrations show a typical assembly. Preserve the positions observed on the actual components.

diagnostics.finding: The mount bearing has unequal spacing around its sides.
diagnostics.meaning: The bearing does not meet the stated seating check.
diagnostics.next: Correct its seating before completing the assembly.

diagnostics.finding: The spring is not centered in the lower seat.
diagnostics.meaning: The spring and seat have not reached the required assembly position.
diagnostics.next: Correct their position while spring load remains controlled.

verification.title: Confirm bench assembly
verification.body: Check the recorded component positions, lower-seat installation, spring centering, bearing seating, new rod nut torque and fitted cap.

verification.title: Confirm vehicle attachments
verification.body: Verify all required new fasteners and their specified torques, together with the restored brake, hose and fitted wiring attachments.

verification.title: Record the alignment result
verification.body: Record the front camber check and whether adjustment was required; confirm the final result meets the applicable adjustment procedure.

procedures.purpose: Bench disassembly and assembly using a spring compressor and vise, including component seating and new strut rod nut installation.
Vehicle removal and installation, including equipment-dependent wiring, replacement fasteners, connection torques and final front camber check.
Wheel and tire removal before strut work and installation after suspension reassembly.

guides.title: Replace a front lower arm and complete suspension setup
guides.summary: Replace the front lower arm with new fasteners, tighten its bushing attachment at curb height, then check toe and calibrate dynamic suspension if fitted.
guides.introduction: The front lower arm connects the wheel assembly to the frame through an outboard ball joint and an inner bushing attachment. These joints allow suspension movement while locating the wheel. Replacement affects both the mechanical attachments and the finishing work: front toe must be checked, and dynamic suspension requires ride-height calibration when fitted.
guides.why: Tightening the inner bushing fastener with the suspension hanging can create incorrect clamp load and damage the bushing. Ball-joint separation also requires controlled tooling and movement to protect its seal. On dynamic-suspension vehicles, disconnecting the height-sensor bracket first protects the sensor from suspension movement during the repair.

when.summary: When a front lower arm requires replacement and toe checking and any required ride-height calibration can be completed.
notes: Identify the SVT or non-SVT fastening branch and whether dynamic suspension is fitted before starting.

prepare.title: Arrange supported access
prepare.detail: Have vehicle-support capability for wheel removal and vehicle/axle stands for supporting the suspension at curb height during final bushing tightening.

prepare.title: Prepare the specified separator and hardware
prepare.detail: Use lower-arm ball-joint separator 204-592. Obtain a new outboard nut and arm-to-frame bolt of the specified or equivalent quality and design, plus suitable torque tools.

prepare.title: Arrange the finishing work
prepare.detail: Have the capability to check and adjust front toe. Dynamic suspension additionally requires a scan tool capable of the Ride Height Calibration routine.

steps.title: Open access and protect the height sensor
steps.body: Remove the wheel and tire using the linked procedure. If dynamic suspension is fitted, remove the ride-height sensor arm bracket bolt and position the bracket aside before servicing the suspension components.

steps.title: Separate the outboard joint
steps.body: Remove and discard the lower-arm outboard nut. Separate the arm from the wheel spindle with separator 204-592. Do not place a separator fork or prying device between the joint and knuckle; any permitted pry-bar use is confined to the lower-arm body opening.

steps.title: Remove the arm
steps.body: Carefully allow the arm and wheel knuckle to reach their resting positions without damaging the ball-joint seal. Remove and discard the arm-to-frame bolt, then remove the lower arm.

steps.title: Fit the arm and secure the outboard joint
steps.body: Position the arm and install the new frame bolt only finger tight. Attach the arm to the spindle and install the new outboard nut. Tighten to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm) for non-SVT or 76 lb.ft (103 Nm) for SVT.

steps.title: Load the suspension before final tightening
steps.body: Support the suspension at curb height using vehicle/axle stands. With the suspension loaded, tighten the arm-to-frame bolt to 184 lb.ft (250 Nm). This loading requirement is essential to the bushing's correct clamping condition.

steps.title: Restore the sensor bracket and wheel
steps.body: If dynamic suspension is fitted, reposition the sensor arm bracket and tighten its bolt to 177 lb.in (20 Nm). Install the wheel and tire using the linked wheel procedure.

steps.title: Complete alignment and calibration
steps.body: Check front toe and adjust it if necessary using the referenced Front Toe Adjustment procedure. On dynamic-suspension vehicles, connect the scan tool and run Ride Height Calibration, following its directions.

watchFor.title: Joint-seal damage
watchFor.body: Incorrect separator placement or uncontrolled movement into the resting position can damage the ball-joint seal.

watchFor.title: Premature inner-bolt tightening
watchFor.body: Keep the new frame bolt finger tight until the suspension is supported at curb height.

watchFor.title: Connected height-sensor bracket
watchFor.body: On dynamic-suspension vehicles, leaving the bracket connected during suspension service can damage the sensor or system.

notes: The SVT nut-torque branch and the dynamic-suspension sensor branch are separate decisions; apply each according to the fitted configuration.

verification.title: Mechanical installation
verification.body: Confirm the discarded fasteners were renewed, the correct outboard-nut torque was used, and final frame-bolt tightening occurred with the suspension loaded.

verification.title: Record the toe result
verification.body: Record the front-toe check and whether adjustment was needed, including the final result when adjustment was performed.

verification.title: Record calibration when applicable
verification.body: For dynamic suspension, confirm bracket reconnection and record the scan tool's Ride Height Calibration completion result.

guides.title: Replace front stabilizer bar bushings on cars without the Performance Package
guides.summary: Replace the separately serviceable front stabilizer bushings with dry installation, rear-facing slits and new bracket bolts.
guides.introduction: The front stabilizer bar helps resist body roll by connecting the suspension movements on opposite sides. Its mounting bushings support and cushion the bar within retaining brackets. This job replaces those bushings where they are separately serviceable; Performance Package cars require replacement of the front stabilizer bar instead.
guides.why: Correct installation depends on more than fitting a bushing around the bar. The slit must face rearward, lubricant must not be applied because it can damage the bushing, and the bracket bolts must be renewed. Access also differs on the 5.0L engine because the rearward bracket bolt sits beneath the alternator.

when.summary: When a separately serviceable front stabilizer bar bushing requires replacement.
notes: Confirm the fitted suspension package before ordering bushings.
The 5.0L engine requires left front wheel removal for the specified bracket-bolt access.

prepare.title: Provide new bracket bolts
prepare.detail: The removed front stabilizer bushing bracket bolts are discarded. Have new bolts available for both sides before starting.

prepare.title: Prepare the correct access route
prepare.detail: Select the air-cleaner procedure for the fitted engine. For the 5.0L, arrange safe vehicle support and wheel removal using the wheel-and-tire procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare for controlled tightening
prepare.detail: Use suitable fastener tools and torque tools for the bushing brackets and coolant degas-bottle mountings. Keep lubricant away from the bar and bushings.

steps.title: Confirm that separate replacement applies
steps.body: Check whether the vehicle has the Performance Package. Its front stabilizer bushings are not separately serviceable; if fitted, take the complete-bar replacement route rather than continuing with separate bushings.

steps.title: Open access above the bar
steps.body: Remove the air cleaner using the procedure for the fitted engine. Remove the coolant degas-bottle bolts and position the bottle aside. These components are moved to provide access to the bushing brackets.

steps.title: Remove and discard the bracket bolts
steps.body: On engines other than the 5.0L, remove the bracket bolts on both sides. On the 5.0L, first remove the left front wheel and tire, then use the wheel opening for the rearward bracket bolt beneath the alternator. Discard the removed bracket bolts in either branch.

steps.title: Replace the bushings in the specified orientation
steps.body: Remove the brackets and bushings. Install each replacement bushing with its slit facing the rear of the vehicle, then refit its bracket. Do not lubricate either the stabilizer bar or the bushings.

steps.title: Secure the brackets and restore access components
steps.body: Install new bracket bolts on both sides and tighten to 76 lb.ft (103 Nm), using the wheel-opening route where required on the 5.0L. Reinstall that wheel and tire. Return the degas bottle and tighten its bolts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm), then reinstall the correct air cleaner.

watchFor.title: A Performance Package bushing being treated as separate
watchFor.body: Stop the separate-bushing operation if this equipment is fitted; the prescribed replacement is the front stabilizer bar.

watchFor.title: Lubricant or reversed slits
watchFor.body: Dry installation and rear-facing slits are explicit requirements, even if lubrication appears to make fitting easier.

notes: The 5.0L access restriction does not change the specified bracket-bolt torque.

diagnostics.finding: The vehicle is equipped with the Performance Package.
diagnostics.meaning: Its front stabilizer bushings cannot be serviced separately.
diagnostics.next: Plan front stabilizer bar replacement instead of this separate-bushing repair.

verification.title: Confirm the bushing installation
verification.body: Check rear-facing slits, dry bar-to-bushing contact and new bracket bolts tightened on both sides.

verification.title: Confirm access components are restored
verification.body: Check the degas-bottle mounting and air-cleaner installation, plus completion of wheel-and-tire installation on the 5.0L.

guides.title: Replace a front stabilizer bar link
guides.summary: Reach the link through the front wheel opening, replace its two attachment nuts, and tighten both joints while holding the ball studs against rotation.
guides.introduction:
I like a repair where the part count stays small. Two nuts, one link—easy, right? A spinning stud can turn that little promise into a pain in the ass. The trick is to hold the stud's hex feature while turning the nut, not enter a swearing contest with it.

The front stabilizer link connects the suspension strut to the bar that helps resist body roll. Its ball joints let that connection move as the suspension travels. I'll take you through wheel-off access, replacing the link and both nuts, then putting the wheel back properly.

This guide covers the documented 2015 Mustang applications: 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L.
guides.why: The link joins the strut bracket to the front stabilizer bar. Its joints deliberately have low friction, so a stud can turn with its nut unless you restrain it using the hex-holding feature. Both removed link nuts must be discarded. Correct replacement fasteners and tightening matter because these attachments are part of the suspension.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang front stabilizer bar link replacement

when.summary: Use this procedure after a front stabilizer bar link has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: The instructions cover one link and two new attachment nuts.
The wheel-off access route below includes wheel removal, installation and the required wheel-nut recheck.

prepare.title: Establish the replacement decision
prepare.detail: This is a replacement procedure, without a joint-play limit or a test for deciding whether the link is faulty. In particular, easy ball-stud movement alone does not establish wear: these joints are designed to move with low initial resistance.

prepare.title: Gather the link, nuts and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have the correct replacement link and two new attachment nuts. Suspension fasteners must be the same as, or equivalent to, the specified parts; do not substitute a lower-quality fastener or a different design. Prepare tools that fit the nuts and each stud's hex-holding feature, plus torque-wrench equipment suitable for 85 lb.ft (115 Nm) at the link and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) at the wheel.

prepare.title: Prepare lifting and wheel-cleaning equipment
prepare.detail: Use a suitable workshop hoist for the access route described here. Have cleaning materials and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, ready for wheel installation. The vehicle's emergency jack is for changing a deflated tire, not for this suspension job. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; floor stands are required when using a jack for support.

steps.title: Locate the lifting points and position the vehicle
steps.body:
Before lifting, use a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Confirm the jack or hoist is rated for the vehicle, including cargo and modifications. If using a jack, support the vehicle on suitable stands at the designated points before going underneath; a jack alone is not a support. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

Put the transmission in Neutral and position the vehicle on the hoist. Identify the approved lifting locations by the triangles stamped into the body or frame. The lifting illustration shows four locations along the sides of the underbody, one toward the front and one toward the rear on each side.

Position the hoist adapters at those marked locations. Check that the adapters and hoisting forks clear the suspension, steering linkage, exhaust, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, and cannot damage the axle or rear cover. Never lift against either bumper. If using a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving onto it.

Raise the vehicle using the hoist's operating procedure. Incorrect lifting locations can allow the vehicle to shift or fall. See [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631).

steps.title: Remove the front wheel for access
steps.body:
At the side being repaired, remove the five wheel nuts, then remove the wheel and tire assembly to open access to the strut and stabilizer link. Do not use heat to free a seized wheel nut: it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. If a nut cannot be removed without heat, stop this access step and arrange suitable wheel-nut service.

The wheel removal and installation details are also in [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Identify the link and both attachment points
steps.body:
Look through the wheel opening for the slender link running beside the strut. Its upper ball stud passes through a bracket on the strut; its lower ball stud attaches to the end of the curved stabilizer bar.

Locate the nut and the stud's hex-holding feature at each end before loosening anything. These are the two link fasteners to remove. The joint arrangement is shown with the [Front Stabilizer Bar Link procedure](#/document/G1692535).

steps.title: Remove and discard both link nuts
steps.body:
Engage a suitable tool with a ball stud's hex-holding feature to keep the stud stationary. While holding it, undo that joint's nut with the nut-removal tool. Repeat at the other end.

Discard both nuts. The joints have low breakaway torque—the small initial effort needed to start them moving—so a stud may rotate readily when it is not restrained. Use the hex feature instead of treating that rotation as proof of a bad joint.

steps.title: Withdraw the old link and position the replacement
steps.body:
With both nuts removed, withdraw the link's studs from the strut bracket and stabilizer-bar attachment, then remove the link.

Place the replacement link in the same arrangement, with its upper end at the strut bracket and its lower end at the stabilizer bar. Seat the studs in their corresponding mounting holes and fit a new nut at each end.

steps.title: Tighten both new link nuts
steps.body:
Hold each ball stud stationary using its hex-holding feature while tightening its nut to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). Apply that torque to both the upper and lower attachment nuts.

Before moving on, confirm that both ends are attached and both new nuts have received the specified torque with their studs restrained.

steps.title: Clean the wheel and hub mating surfaces
steps.body:
Before refitting the wheel, remove corrosion, dirt and other foreign material from the wheel's mounting face and the corresponding mounting surface at the hub and brake disc. Check that any fasteners securing the brake disc to the hub are secured and do not interfere with those mating surfaces.

These faces must meet properly. Contamination or an interfering fastener can allow the wheel nuts to loosen and the wheel to come off while driving.

Wipe the wheel’s central pilot bore clean before applying the specified lubricant at the pilot interface. [Wheel mounting preparation](#/document/G1686507)

steps.title: Lubricate only the wheel's centering interface
steps.body:
Apply a thin coat of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, only where the wheel's central pilot bore meets the hub pilot. The pilot is the raised center that locates the wheel; it is separate from the broad, flat mounting face.

Keep the lubricant off the wheel-to-brake-disc mounting faces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and brake-disc friction surfaces. The wheel-stud and wheel-nut threads must remain clean and dry for the specified tightening torque.

steps.title: Refit the wheel and finger-tighten its five nuts
steps.body: Position the wheel on the hub and install all five wheel nuts. Tighten them only finger tight at this stage. Check that the wheel sits against the cleaned mounting surface.

steps.title: Lower onto the tires and tighten in a star pattern
steps.body:
Before lowering, make sure the parking brake is applied. Restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground, and keep the vehicle restrained for final wheel-nut tightening. Do not lower an unrestrained vehicle in Neutral.

Lower the vehicle until it rests on its tires before final wheel-nut tightening. Tighten all five nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), working in a star or cross pattern.

For the illustrated five-nut layout, the sequence is top, lower left, upper right, upper left, then lower right. If the wheel is rotated, use the equivalent sequence across the center rather than working around adjacent nuts. The cross pattern helps avoid brake-disc runout, meaning uneven side-to-side disc movement that can contribute to brake roughness, shudder and vibration.

steps.title: Arrange the wheel-nut recheck
steps.body: Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after reinstalling the wheel. Use the same star pattern and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) torque with the vehicle resting on its tires and the threads clean and dry. Wheels can loosen after their initial tightening; this recheck is part of completing the job.

watchFor.title: A ball stud turning with its nut
watchFor.body: Keep the stud restrained with its hex-holding feature during both removal and installation. Low resistance to movement is an intentional feature of these joints.

watchFor.title: Reused or unsuitable suspension nuts
watchFor.body: Discard both removed link nuts. Fit two new nuts of the specified or equivalent quality and design, and tighten each to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm).

watchFor.title: Unsafe vehicle support
watchFor.body: Use the triangle-marked lifting locations. Never get underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack, and never use the emergency tire-changing jack to hoist the vehicle for this repair.

watchFor.title: Lubricant spreading beyond the hub pilot
watchFor.body: The anti-seize belongs only at the centering interface. Keep mounting faces, wheel fastener threads and braking surfaces free of it.

watchFor.title: Wheel tightening before the vehicle rests on its tires
watchFor.body: Leave the wheel nuts finger tight during initial installation. Perform final tightening on the tires, using the star pattern and clean, dry threads.

notes: The same link-nut torque applies to both attachment points: 85 lb.ft (115 Nm).
Removing the complete wheel for access does not require removing the tire from the wheel.

Tire changing and balancing are separate jobs. If you add either to this repair, check the wheel-specific machine restrictions in the linked Wheel and Tire procedure; complete-wheel removal needs neither machine.

diagnostics.finding: A ball stud rotates as its nut is loosened or tightened.
diagnostics.meaning: The ball joints are designed for low friction and low initial turning resistance. Rotation alone does not establish that the link has failed.
diagnostics.next: Restrain the stud using its hex-holding feature, then continue working the nut.

diagnostics.finding: A seized wheel nut prevents wheel removal.
diagnostics.meaning: The wheel-off access route cannot continue until the nut is removed safely; heating it risks wheel and bearing damage.
diagnostics.next: Stop wheel removal and arrange suitable wheel-nut service without applying heat.

diagnostics.finding: Debris, corrosion or a protruding brake-disc retaining fastener prevents flat wheel seating.
diagnostics.meaning: The wheel cannot make proper contact with its mounting surface, creating a risk of wheel-nut loosening.
diagnostics.next: Remove the contamination and ensure the retaining fastener is secured without interfering with the mating faces before installing the wheel.

verification.title: Confirm the link fastening
verification.body: Check that the replacement link connects the strut bracket to the stabilizer bar, both attachment nuts are new, and both were tightened to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm) while their studs were held stationary.

verification.title: Confirm the wheel installation
verification.body: Confirm clean, properly seated mounting faces, lubricant confined to the pilot interface, and all five wheel nuts tightened in a star pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) with the vehicle resting on its tires.

verification.title: Complete the follow-up tightening
verification.body: Record the wheel installation mileage and retighten its nuts within 160 km (100 mi). These fastening checks confirm assembly completion; they do not diagnose any original suspension complaint.

guides.title: Replace the front stabilizer bar
guides.summary: Release both stabilizer links, clear the engine-specific bracket access and replace the bar using new specified fasteners.
guides.introduction: The front stabilizer bar connects the left and right suspension through links and resists their relative movement, helping control body roll. Bushings and brackets locate the bar while allowing it to work. Removal involves both wheel openings and access around the air cleaner and coolant degas bottle, with a particular bracket-access route on the 5.0L engine.
guides.why: The link ball joints have deliberately low breakaway torque, so their studs can turn while a nut is being loosened or tightened. The hex-holding feature prevents this. Suspension fasteners are critical to the assembly's performance: the specified discarded nuts and bolts must be replaced, and replacements must not be of lesser quality or a substitute design.

when.summary: When the front stabilizer bar has been identified for replacement or must be removed for related work.
notes: Confirm the fitted engine before planning access to the rearward bushing-bracket bolt.

prepare.title: Provide wheel-off access
prepare.detail: Arrange the capability to raise and securely support the vehicle for wheel removal, following the wheel-and-tire procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Have tools for the link-stud hex-holding feature, suitable torque equipment, new lower link nuts and new stabilizer-bar bushing-bracket bolts for both sides.

prepare.title: Select the intake procedure
prepare.detail: Use the air-cleaner removal and installation procedure for the fitted engine. Plan space to position the degas bottle aside.

steps.title: Remove the wheels and tires
steps.body: Follow the [wheel-and-tire procedure](#/document/G1686507) to establish access on both sides. The wheel opening is also the required route for the obstructed bracket bolt on the 5.0L engine.

steps.title: Release both lower link connections
steps.body: Hold each ball stud using its hex feature while removing the lower stabilizer-link nut. Discard both nuts and position the links aside. Stud rotation by itself is not evidence that these low-friction joints have failed.

steps.title: Clear access above the bar
steps.body: Remove the air cleaner using the matching engine procedure. Remove the degas-bottle bolts and position the bottle aside to expose the working area.

steps.title: Remove the brackets and bar
steps.body: Follow the engine branch in the [stabilizer-bar procedure](#/document/G1692533). On engines other than the 5.0L, remove and discard the bushing-bracket bolts on both sides. On the 5.0L, move the fitted left-hand splash shield upward as needed and remove the rearward bolt beneath the alternator through the wheel opening. Discard the bracket bolts and remove the bar.

steps.title: Install the bar and new bracket bolts
steps.body: Position the bar and install new bushing-bracket bolts on both sides. Retain the wheel-opening access route for the 5.0L rearward bolt, moving the fitted shield as required. Tighten the bracket bolts to the specified value in the procedure.

steps.title: Restore access components and links
steps.body: Return the degas bottle and tighten its bolts to specification, then reinstall the correct air cleaner. Position both stabilizer links and install new lower nuts, again holding each stud by its hex feature while tightening. Finish by installing the wheels and tires using their procedure.

watchFor.title: Spinning link studs
watchFor.body: Use the hex-holding feature during both removal and installation; low joint friction makes stud rotation expected.

watchFor.title: Obstructed 5.0L bracket access
watchFor.body: The rearward bracket bolt beneath the alternator must be removed and installed through the wheel opening.

notes: The degas-bottle bolts, bracket bolts and link nuts have separate tightening specifications.

diagnostics.finding: A link ball stud rotates as its nut is turned.
diagnostics.meaning: The joint's low breakaway torque can allow this during service.
diagnostics.next: Hold the stud using the provided hex feature; do not diagnose joint failure from rotation alone.

verification.title: Check both sides
verification.body: Confirm new bracket bolts and lower link nuts are installed and tightened, with the air cleaner, degas bottle and wheels restored.

verification.title: Record fastening completion
verification.body: Record completion of the bracket, link, degas-bottle and wheel fastening requirements against their respective procedures.
