guides.title: Replace the front hub and bearing: 2015 5.2L Mustang with SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Remove the wheel, support the brake caliper aside, and remove the brake disc to replace the complete front hub-and-bearing assembly. Reassemble with new hub and caliper bolts, the correct tightening patterns, and the required brake and wheel checks.
guides.introduction: The front hub gets to spin all day while four bolts do the serious work of keeping it attached. I give those bolts considerably more respect than their modest head count might suggest. On this 2015 5.2L Mustang with the SVT Performance Package, the hub and bearing come off together after the wheel and front brake disc are out of the way. I’ll walk you through that access, keeping the hefty caliper supported and the three different tightening specifications straight.
guides.why: The hub carries the wheel studs and supports the wheel; the bearing lets that hub rotate while its mounting stays attached to the suspension. This repair replaces the complete hub-and-bearing assembly. Its attachment bolts are critical suspension fasteners: discard the removed bolts, use replacements of the same or equivalent quality and design, and tighten the new bolts in the specified cross pattern.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang 5.2L SVT Performance Package front hub replacement
front wheel bearing and hub assembly

when.summary: Use this replacement procedure after the need for a front hub-and-bearing assembly has been established on a 2015 5.2L Mustang fitted with the SVT Performance Package.
notes: The brake access and caliper torque here apply to the matching 5.2L SVT Performance Package brake configuration.
The broader engine coverage of the wheel and lifting procedures does not extend this hub repair to other engines or brake packages.

prepare.title: Confirm the repair and configuration
prepare.detail: Confirm the model year, 5.2L engine and SVT Performance Package before ordering parts. Have the need for hub replacement established before dismantling: this procedure provides no bearing play, noise or measured wear test.

prepare.title: Have the replacement assembly and disposable fasteners ready
prepare.detail: Obtain the correct complete front hub-and-bearing assembly, four new hub mounting bolts and two new brake caliper mounting bolts for the side being serviced. Both sets of removed bolts must be discarded. Use the same or equivalent fastener quality and design; lower-quality hardware or a substitute design is unacceptable.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and caliper support
prepare.detail: Have a suitable hoist and a caliper support hook or hanger, as illustrated in the brake procedure. Identify the stamped lifting-point triangles before raising the car. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; use floor stands when supporting a jacked vehicle. The emergency tire-changing jack is not suitable for this repair.

prepare.title: Gather fastening and cleaning equipment
prepare.detail: Have tools that fit the wheel nuts, caliper bolts and hub bolts, plus torque equipment suitable for 98 lb.ft (133 Nm), 136 lb.ft (185 Nm) and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). Have a wire brush, a cloth for wiping the wheel pilot bore, Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner – VOC Compliant or Motorcraft Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A or PM-4-B, and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2.

steps.title: Locate the lifting points and raise the car
steps.body:
Before lifting, use a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Confirm the jack or hoist is rated for the vehicle, including cargo and modifications. If using a jack, support the vehicle on suitable stands at the designated points before going underneath; a jack alone is not a support. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a suitable hoist. Find the triangles stamped into the body or frame at the designated lifting locations; the lifting illustration shows four locations along the sides, near the front and rear wheels.

Position the hoist adapters carefully so they do not damage the suspension, exhaust or steering linkage. On a two-column hoist, keep the lifting forks clear of suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, and avoid contact that could damage the axle or rear cover. Never apply jack pressure to either bumper. If using a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving onto it.

Incorrect lifting locations can allow the vehicle to shift or fall. Use the [lifting overview](#/document/G1663631) to identify the locations before lifting.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and tire assembly
steps.body:
Remove the five wheel nuts, then take the wheel and tire assembly off the hub. Do not use heat on a seized wheel nut: it can damage both the wheel and the wheel bearing.

Set the wheel aside for cleaning and reinstallation later. The [wheel and tire procedure](#/document/G1686507) also contains the mounting-surface and final-tightening requirements used below.

steps.title: Unbolt and support the brake caliper with its pads
steps.body:
Arrange the caliper hanger before removing the caliper. Remove the two caliper mounting bolts shown in the brake illustration and discard them.

Move the caliper and brake pads aside together and support the assembly with the hanger. Keep the brake hose connected and arrange the supported caliper so the hose does not carry its weight. Never allow the caliper to hang from the hose; that can damage it.

This clears the disc without disconnecting the hydraulic line. The caliper is heavy enough to deserve its own seat, not a dangling invitation to trouble. See the [SVT Performance Package brake disc procedure](#/document/G1716189).

steps.title: Remove the front brake disc
steps.body:
With the caliper clear, carefully draw the brake disc outward over the five wheel studs and remove it. Handle the disc with care and set it aside safely.

You can now see the hub flange—the round wheel-mounting face with the studs—and reach the hub attachment bolts from the rear of the suspension mounting.

steps.title: Remove the four hub bolts and the hub-and-bearing assembly
steps.body:
Locate the four hub mounting bolts around the rear of the hub. The rear-view illustration shows two upper and two lower bolt positions.

Remove all four bolts and discard them, then remove the complete front hub-and-bearing assembly from its mounting. Keep those old bolts away from the new installation hardware; looking perfectly respectable does not earn them another shift. Refer to the [hub-and-bearing procedure](#/document/G1692554).

steps.title: Position the replacement hub and start four new bolts
steps.body:
Position the replacement front hub-and-bearing assembly in its mounting and install four new hub bolts. Check that the assembly is correctly positioned and all four bolts have started before final tightening.

These are critical suspension fasteners. Use the correct replacement parts of the same or equivalent quality and design.

steps.title: Tighten the hub bolts in the illustrated cross pattern
steps.body:
Tighten all four new hub bolts to 98 lb.ft (133 Nm) in a cross pattern.

Viewed from behind the hub, as in the installation illustration, the numbered order is:

1. Upper right.
2. Lower left, diagonally opposite.
3. Lower right.
4. Upper left, diagonally opposite.

Use the rear-view orientation when identifying these positions. This torque belongs to the hub mounting bolts.

steps.title: Clean the brake disc mating surfaces
steps.body:
Before refitting the disc, clean its mating surfaces with a wire brush and Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner – VOC Compliant or Motorcraft Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A or PM-4-B.

The mating surfaces are the faces that seat against adjoining parts. Give the disc-to-hub seating area particular attention so the disc can sit properly against the replacement hub.

steps.title: Refit the brake disc
steps.body:
Carefully position the brake disc over the five studs and onto the hub. Check that it sits against the hub mating face before bringing the caliper back into position.

Keep handling deliberate; this is a sizeable disc, and the surrounding brake parts do not need an accidental introduction to its edge.

steps.title: Restore the caliper and pads using new bolts
steps.body:
Bring the supported caliper and brake pads back into their installed position around the disc. Install two new caliper mounting bolts and tighten them to 136 lb.ft (185 Nm).

Remove the temporary hanger after the caliper is secured. Check that the brake hose is free of the hanger and is no longer carrying the caliper’s weight. This restores the components moved aside in the [brake disc procedure](#/document/G1716189).

steps.title: Clean and check the wheel mounting faces
steps.body:
Remove corrosion, dirt and other foreign material from the wheel mounting surface and the corresponding hub and brake disc mounting surfaces. Look at the actual flat contact faces rather than judging cleanliness from the visible wheel face.

If any fasteners attach the rotor to the hub, make sure they are secured and do not interfere with the wheel mounting surfaces. Do not install the wheel over contamination or an obstruction: improper seating can allow the wheel nuts to loosen and the wheel to come off while driving, causing loss of control and serious injury or death.

steps.title: Wipe the wheel pilot bore clean, then lubricate only the pilot interface
steps.body:
Wipe the wheel pilot bore clean with a cloth before applying lubricant. The pilot bore is the wheel’s center opening; the hub pilot is the raised center that fits into it. Check that the bore is clean before proceeding.

Apply a thin coat of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, only at the interface between the wheel pilot bore and the hub pilot. The wheel illustration highlights this narrow central contact area.

Keep the lubricant off the flat wheel-to-disc mounting faces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and disc friction surfaces. Wheel stud and nut threads must remain clean and dry. This is a small, targeted application—the whole assembly does not need to be marinated.

steps.title: Fit the wheel and install the nuts finger tight
steps.body:
Position the wheel and tire assembly on the hub and install all five wheel nuts. Tighten them only finger tight at this stage.

Check that the wheel is positioned against its mounting face before lowering the vehicle for final tightening.

steps.title: Lower onto the tires and torque the wheel nuts in a star
steps.body:
Before lowering, make sure the parking brake is applied. Restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground, and keep the vehicle restrained for final wheel-nut tightening. Do not lower an unrestrained vehicle in Neutral.

With the vehicle resting on its tires, tighten the five wheel nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). This specification requires clean, dry stud and nut threads.

Follow the illustrated star pattern, viewed from outside the wheel:

1. Top.
2. Lower left.
3. Upper right.
4. Upper left.
5. Lower right.

Use the pattern rather than working around adjacent nuts. Uneven tightening can increase brake disc runout—the disc’s side-to-side wobble as it turns—and accelerate brake roughness, shudder and vibration.

steps.title: Apply the brake pedal and confirm reassembly
steps.body:
With the caliper, disc and wheel reinstalled, apply the brake pedal several times to verify correct brake system operation.

Before treating the job as finished, confirm that the caliper hanger has been removed, the caliper and hose are correctly positioned, and the hub bolts, caliper bolts and wheel nuts have each received their own specified torque. These are completion checks for the repair, not a new bearing diagnostic test. If correct brake operation cannot be verified, keep the vehicle out of service until the issue is resolved.

steps.title: Retighten the wheel nuts within 100 miles
steps.body:
Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after reinstalling the wheel. Use the same star pattern and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) specification, with the vehicle resting on its tires.

Wheels can loosen after initial tightening. This follow-up is a required part of finishing the job, not an optional favor to future you.

watchFor.title: Caliper weight on the brake hose
watchFor.body: Support the caliper while it is aside. The brake hose must never serve as its hanger.

watchFor.title: Mixing the three fastening specifications
watchFor.body: Hub bolts: four new bolts, cross pattern, 98 lb.ft (133 Nm). Caliper bolts: two new bolts, 136 lb.ft (185 Nm). Wheel nuts: five nuts, star pattern, 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), with clean, dry threads and the vehicle resting on its tires.

watchFor.title: Reusing discarded hardware
watchFor.body: Both the hub mounting bolts and caliper mounting bolts are discarded during removal. Keep them separate from the new bolts so they cannot drift back into the job.

watchFor.title: Anti-seize spreading beyond the pilot
watchFor.body: Wipe the wheel pilot bore clean first. Only the wheel center-bore-to-hub-pilot interface receives a thin coating of XL-2. Flat mounting faces, wheel fasteners and brake friction components must remain free of it.

watchFor.title: Lifting at a convenient-looking location
watchFor.body: Locate the stamped triangles and use the designated lifting points. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack, and do not use the emergency tire-changing jack for this repair.

notes: This procedure replaces the hub and bearing together; it does not describe dismantling or rebuilding the bearing internally.

Removing the tire from its wheel or balancing the wheel is not part of this hub replacement. If separate tire work is needed on carbon fiber or alloy wheels, use a center-clamp tire changer such as a Hunter Auto 34, Revolution, TC3900 or equivalent. Do not use a table-top machine that grips inside the wheel and rides on the front flange. Use a balancer that does not contact the wheel face, such as a Hunter Road Force Touch GSP9700; face-contact equipment can damage the wheel.

diagnostics.finding: A wheel nut is seized during removal.
diagnostics.meaning: Normal wheel removal is blocked; applying heat risks damage to the wheel and bearing.
diagnostics.next: Do not heat the nut. Resolve the seized fastener before continuing; a seized-nut removal method is not covered here.

diagnostics.finding: Corrosion, dirt or foreign material remains on a wheel mounting face.
diagnostics.meaning: The wheel may not seat correctly, which can allow its nuts to loosen.
diagnostics.next: Remove the contamination from both mating faces before installing the wheel. Check that any rotor-to-hub fasteners do not obstruct seating.

diagnostics.finding: The caliper is hanging from the brake hose while positioned aside.
diagnostics.meaning: The hose is carrying a load that can damage it.
diagnostics.next: Support the caliper with the hanger before continuing. If hose damage is suspected, resolve that concern before returning the vehicle to service.

diagnostics.finding: Correct brake operation cannot be verified after several pedal applications.
diagnostics.meaning: The brake reassembly completion check has not passed.
diagnostics.next: Do not return the vehicle to service. Further brake diagnosis is required; no pedal-travel limit or fault-isolation test is established by this replacement procedure.

verification.title: Hub installation
verification.body: Confirm that four new hub bolts were installed and tightened in the illustrated cross pattern to 98 lb.ft (133 Nm).

verification.title: Brake restoration
verification.body: Confirm that the disc mating surfaces were cleaned, the disc and caliper were restored, and two new caliper bolts were tightened to 136 lb.ft (185 Nm). The temporary hanger must be removed and the brake hose must not support the caliper.

verification.title: Wheel installation
verification.body: Confirm clean mounting faces, a wheel pilot bore wiped clean before lubrication, anti-seize confined to the pilot interface, and clean, dry wheel fastener threads. Verify final star-pattern tightening to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) with the vehicle resting on its tires.

verification.title: Brake operation
verification.body: Apply the brake pedal several times and verify correct brake system operation before returning the car to service.

verification.title: Wheel-nut follow-up
verification.body: Arrange and complete wheel-nut retightening within 160 km (100 mi) of wheel reinstallation.

procedures.purpose: Front hub-and-bearing assembly removal and installation, four discarded mounting bolts, replacement fastener requirements, and cross-pattern tightening to 98 lb.ft (133 Nm).
Matching 5.2L SVT Performance Package brake access: support the caliper and pads aside, replace its two mounting bolts, remove and clean the disc, restore the brakes, and check pedal operation.
Wheel removal and installation, mounting-face and pilot-bore cleaning, restricted XL-2 application, five-nut star sequence, 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) final torque, and retightening within 160 km (100 mi).
Stamped-triangle lifting locations, vehicle support requirements, and precautions for hoist positioning and underbody clearance.

stepGroups.title: Reach the hub
stepGroups.summary: Lift at the designated points, remove the wheel, support the caliper and remove the disc.

stepGroups.title: Replace the hub and bearing
stepGroups.summary: Discard the four old bolts, install the replacement assembly and torque new bolts in a cross pattern.

stepGroups.title: Restore the front brake
stepGroups.summary: Clean and refit the disc, then secure the caliper with new bolts.

stepGroups.title: Refit and tighten the wheel
stepGroups.summary: Clean the mounting faces and pilot bore, lubricate only the pilot interface and torque the nuts in a star.

stepGroups.title: Check operation and finish the follow-up
stepGroups.summary: Verify brake operation and assembly, then retighten the wheel nuts within 100 miles.

guides.title: Replace the front wheel bearing and hub
guides.summary: Replace the front hub and bearing assembly on a 2015 Mustang with a 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine, including brake access, new caliper mounting bolts for all three brake configurations, and correct hub and wheel tightening.
guides.introduction:
The front hub hides its biggest demand beneath a little grease cap: 251 lb.ft of properly measured commitment. Cute cap, serious nut. I’ll walk you from lifting the car through moving the brakes aside, replacing the hub assembly and putting everything back with the right parts and tightening sequence.

The hub is the round flange carrying the five wheel studs. Its bearing lets that flange—and the wheel and brake disc attached to it—turn on the stationary spindle. Here, the bearing and hub come off together as an assembly.
guides.why: The hub supports the wheel, and its central nut secures the assembly on the spindle. Correct retention matters, as does restoring the brakes and wheel mounting surfaces disturbed during access. Replace the removed hub nut, grease cap and both caliper mounting bolts. Critical suspension fasteners must retain the specified quality and design and receive the correct tightening torque.

when.summary: Use this procedure when removal or replacement of the front wheel bearing and hub assembly has already been justified.
notes: Choose the caliper branch by the brakes actually fitted to the car, rather than assuming the engine identifies the caliper.
The job removes and installs the hub and bearing together.

prepare.title: Establish the job before dismantling
prepare.detail: Confirm that assembly removal or replacement is needed. Bearing-condition diagnosis, internal bearing repair and seized cap or hub extraction require their own methods; this procedure provides no bearing acceptance limits or seized-part extraction technique.

prepare.title: Lay out the replacement parts
prepare.detail: Have the correct front bearing and hub assembly, a new wheel hub nut, a new wheel hub grease cap and two new caliper mounting bolts for the fitted caliper. Both mounting bolts must be discarded and replaced on the 2-, 4- and 6-piston caliper configurations. Replacement suspension fasteners must be the same or equivalent quality and design; do not substitute lower-quality or different-design parts.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting, caliper support and torque tools
prepare.detail: Provide suitable lifting equipment, floor stands if using a jack, and a caliper-support hook. Have tools that fit the actual fasteners and torque equipment capable of 251 lb.ft (340 Nm) for the hub nut, 85 lb.ft (115 Nm) for the caliper bolts and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) for the wheel nuts.

prepare.title: Gather cleaning materials
prepare.detail: Use a wire brush and Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner – VOC Compliant / Motorcraft Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A or PM-4-B, for the brake disc mating surfaces. Have Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, for the wheel pilot interface only.

prepare.title: Keep the access references handy
prepare.detail: The actions below incorporate [Brake Disc](#/document/G1693784), [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507) and [Jacking and Lifting – Overview](#/document/G1663631). Identify the stamped lifting-point triangles and the fitted caliper type before committing to disassembly.

steps.title: Locate the lifting points and raise the car safely
steps.body:
Before lifting, use a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Confirm the jack or hoist is rated for the vehicle, including cargo and modifications. If using a jack, support the vehicle on suitable stands at the designated points before going underneath; a jack alone is not a support. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

With the transmission in Neutral, position the vehicle on a suitable hoist. Locate the triangles stamped into the body or frame at the designated lifting points. There are four marked locations along the sides of the underside. Position the lifting equipment at those locations. See [Jacking and Lifting – Overview](#/document/G1663631).

Check that hoist adapters and forks clear the suspension, exhaust, steering linkage, mounting brackets, stabilizer brackets where fitted, axle and rear cover. Before driving onto a drive-on lift, check for underbody interference.

Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; use floor stands. Incorrect lifting contact can allow the vehicle to shift or fall, causing serious injury. The emergency tire-changing jack is not suitable for this repair. Never apply lifting pressure to either bumper.

steps.title: Remove the front wheel and tire assembly
steps.body:
Remove the five wheel nuts, then lift the wheel and tire assembly off the studs. This exposes the brake disc and caliper.

Do not use heat to release a seized wheel nut: it can damage both the wheel and the bearing. The tire stays on the wheel for this job. See [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Remove and discard both caliper mounting bolts
steps.body:
Identify whether the fitted front caliper has 2, 4 or 6 pistons—the hydraulic pistons that press the pads against the disc. Locate the two mounting bolts attaching the caliper assembly to the steering knuckle, behind the caliper.

For a 2-piston caliper: remove and discard both mounting bolts.

For a 4-piston caliper: remove and discard both mounting bolts.

For a 6-piston caliper: remove and discard both mounting bolts.

All three configurations require two new bolts during reassembly, tightened to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). Keep the caliper supported as you release it. See [Brake Disc](#/document/G1693784).

steps.title: Support the caliper and pads aside
steps.body:
Move the caliper and brake pads aside together, leaving the brake hose connected. Support the caliper with a hook so its weight is carried by the support, not the hose, and position it clear of the disc’s removal path.

Do not allow the caliper to hang from the brake hose; this can damage the hose. This is one place where letting something dangle is an expensive shortcut.

steps.title: Remove the brake disc to expose the hub
steps.body:
Withdraw the brake disc outward over the five wheel studs. Behind it is the hub flange, with a domed grease cap in its center and the brake shield remaining behind the hub.

The disc comes off before the hub cap and central nut. Keep the supported caliper clear while removing it.

steps.title: Remove and discard the central grease cap
steps.body:
Remove the domed grease cap from the circular recess at the center of the hub. Discard it; a new cap is required for assembly.

With the cap removed, the large central wheel hub nut is exposed. See [Front Wheel Bearing and Wheel Hub](#/document/G1692537).

steps.title: Remove and discard the wheel hub nut
steps.body:
Remove the central nut from the spindle and discard it. Keep it separate from the new nut so it cannot wander back into service during cleanup.

This central retaining nut is distinct from the five wheel nuts removed earlier.

steps.title: Withdraw the bearing and hub assembly
steps.body:
Withdraw the complete front bearing and hub assembly outward off the spindle. The flange and its five wheel studs come away together; the spindle and brake shield remain on the car.

Keep the work at assembly level rather than dismantling the bearing internally.

steps.title: Fit the replacement hub and tighten the new nut
steps.body:
Position the replacement front bearing and hub assembly over the spindle and install it in the location vacated by the old assembly.

Install a new wheel hub nut and tighten it to 251 lb.ft (340 Nm). Use the torque tool to establish that value. This is the hub retaining specification, not a wheel-nut setting, and it deserves more precision than a confident grunt.

steps.title: Install the new grease cap
steps.body: After tightening the hub nut, install the new grease cap into the center of the hub. Confirm that it is seated in its recess before covering the hub with the brake disc.

steps.title: Clean the mating faces and reinstall the brake disc
steps.body:
Use a wire brush and Motorcraft PM-4-A or PM-4-B brake parts cleaner to clean the brake disc mating surfaces—the faces where the disc seats against the hub. Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material that would prevent the parts from meeting properly.

Position the brake disc over the wheel studs and against the hub. Keep lubricant away from the disc friction surfaces and brake pads. See [Brake Disc](#/document/G1693784).

steps.title: Return the caliper and pads and install two new mounting bolts
steps.body:
Return the supported caliper and pads to their installed position around the disc. Keep the brake hose correctly routed as the caliper returns to its mounting.

Install two new caliper mounting bolts for whichever covered caliper is fitted: 2-, 4- or 6-piston. Do not reinstall the removed bolts.

Tighten both mounting bolts to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). Remove the support hook once the caliper is secured.

steps.title: Prepare the wheel mounting face and pilot
steps.body:
Clean corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel’s mounting face and the corresponding hub/brake-disc mounting face. Check that any fasteners securing the disc to the hub are secured and do not obstruct the wheel mounting surface. Contamination or interference here can allow the wheel nuts to loosen and the wheel to detach while driving, causing loss of control and serious injury or death.

Apply only a thin coat of Motorcraft XL-2 anti-seize at the interface between the wheel pilot bore and hub pilot. The pilot is the central locating fit: the wheel’s center hole fits around the hub’s raised center.

Do not spread anti-seize onto the flat wheel-to-disc mounting faces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads or brake disc friction surfaces. A little belongs at the pilot; enthusiastic smearing belongs nowhere near these brakes.

steps.title: Install the wheel and finger-tighten its nuts
steps.body:
Position the wheel and tire assembly over the five studs and onto the pilot. Install all five wheel nuts finger tight only at this stage.

Keep the wheel stud and wheel nut threads clean and dry. The final wheel-nut torque is specified for that condition.

steps.title: Lower onto the tires and torque the wheel nuts in a star
steps.body:
Before lowering, make sure the parking brake is applied. Restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground, and keep the vehicle restrained for final wheel-nut tightening. Do not lower an unrestrained vehicle in Neutral.

Lower the vehicle until it rests on its tires before final wheel-nut tightening.

Tighten all five wheel nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) in a star/cross pattern. With one nut at the top, the order is: top → lower left → upper right → upper left → lower right. Follow that crossing order rather than moving around the rim from one neighboring nut to the next.

The crossing pattern helps prevent excessive brake disc runout—sideways wobble as the disc turns—which can lead to brake roughness, shudder and vibration.

steps.title: Operate the brakes and arrange the wheel-nut recheck
steps.body:
Apply the brake pedal several times to verify correct brake system operation after reassembly. If correct operation is not restored, keep the vehicle out of service until the issue is resolved.

Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after wheel installation. Use the same 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) specification, clean and dry threads, star pattern and vehicle-resting-on-tires condition. Wheels can loosen after initial tightening, with a risk of serious injury; this follow-up is part of finishing the job.

watchFor.title: Caliper weight carried by the hose
watchFor.body: The caliper and pads must be supported while positioned aside. A hose carrying the caliper’s weight can be damaged.

watchFor.title: Discarded parts creeping back into the parts pile
watchFor.body: Always replace the hub nut, grease cap and both caliper mounting bolts. The two bolts are discard-on-removal parts on every covered caliper configuration: 2-, 4- and 6-piston.

watchFor.title: Confusing three different torque settings
watchFor.body: Hub nut: 251 lb.ft (340 Nm). Caliper mounting bolts for all three covered caliper types: 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). Wheel nuts: 150 lb.ft (204 Nm).

watchFor.title: Dirty wheel mounting faces
watchFor.body: Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material before wheel installation. Check for interfering disc-retaining fasteners where present. An improperly seated wheel can loosen and detach, causing loss of control and serious injury or death.

watchFor.title: Anti-seize outside the pilot interface
watchFor.body: XL-2 belongs only in a thin coat between the wheel pilot bore and hub pilot. Keep mounting faces, studs, nuts, pads and disc friction surfaces free of it.

watchFor.title: Incorrect lifting contact
watchFor.body: Use the triangle-marked lifting points and check equipment clearance before raising the car. Incorrect contact can damage components or allow the vehicle to shift or fall.

notes: This article applies to the 2015 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L central-nut front hub. The broader engine listings in the lifting and wheel references do not extend this hub procedure to the 5.2L.

Tire removal and wheel balancing are unnecessary for this hub replacement. If separate tire work is undertaken on carbon fiber or alloy wheels, use a center-clamp tire changer such as Hunter Auto 34, Revolution, TC3900 or equivalent. Do not use a table-top machine that grips inside the wheel and rides on its front flange. Use a balancer that avoids wheel-face contact, such as Hunter Road Force Touch GSP9700; unsuitable machines can damage the wheel.

diagnostics.finding: The fitted caliper has 2 pistons.
diagnostics.meaning: Use the 2-piston access configuration. Both caliper mounting bolts must be discarded when removed.
diagnostics.next: Remove and discard the two bolts, support the caliper and pads aside, then install two new mounting bolts during reassembly. Tighten both to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm).

diagnostics.finding: The fitted caliper has 4 or 6 pistons.
diagnostics.meaning: Use the matching caliper access configuration. Both caliper mounting bolts are discard-on-removal parts.
diagnostics.next: Discard the removed bolts and install two new bolts during reassembly. Tighten both to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm).

diagnostics.finding: Corrosion, dirt or foreign material remains between the wheel and its mounting face, or a disc-retaining fastener interferes with seating.
diagnostics.meaning: The wheel cannot be assumed to seat correctly; subsequent wheel-nut loosening is a safety risk.
diagnostics.next: Remove the contamination and correct the fastener interference before installing and tightening the wheel.

diagnostics.finding: The wheel stud or wheel nut threads are not clean and dry before final tightening.
diagnostics.meaning: The required thread condition for the 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) wheel-nut specification has not been met.
diagnostics.next: Restore clean, dry threads before final tightening. Keep XL-2 confined to the pilot interface.

diagnostics.finding: Repeated brake-pedal applications do not establish correct brake operation after reassembly.
diagnostics.meaning: The required brake completion check has failed.
diagnostics.next: Keep the vehicle out of service and resolve the brake issue before driving.

verification.title: Account for the hub retention parts
verification.body: Confirm installation of the replacement hub assembly, a new hub nut tightened to 251 lb.ft (340 Nm), and a new grease cap seated in the hub center.

verification.title: Confirm the caliper was secured with new bolts
verification.body: Confirm the disc, caliper and pads are back in position. Verify that two new caliper mounting bolts were installed and both received 85 lb.ft (115 Nm), whether the caliper has 2, 4 or 6 pistons. Check that the support hook is removed and the hose is not carrying caliper weight.

verification.title: Confirm wheel seating and tightening
verification.body: Verify clean mounting faces, anti-seize confined to the pilot interface, and all five wheel nuts tightened in a star pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) with clean, dry threads and the vehicle resting on its tires.

verification.title: Complete the brake operation check
verification.body: Apply the brake pedal several times and verify correct brake system operation before returning the vehicle to use.

verification.title: Complete the follow-up wheel-nut tightening
verification.body: Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) of reinstallation using the specified torque, thread condition and crossing sequence.

stepGroups.title: Lift the car and expose the hub
stepGroups.summary: Remove the wheel, discard both caliper mounting bolts, support the caliper assembly aside and withdraw the brake disc.

stepGroups.title: Replace and secure the hub
stepGroups.summary: Discard the old cap and nut, exchange the assembly and install its new retention parts.

stepGroups.title: Restore the brake assembly
stepGroups.summary: Clean and refit the disc, then secure the caliper with two new bolts at the specified torque.

stepGroups.title: Refit the wheel and complete the checks

guides.title: Replace the rear lower arm in the front suspension
guides.summary: Replace the front suspension’s rear lower arm using new mounting hardware, loaded-suspension tightening and the applicable calibration and toe checks.
guides.introduction: Here, rear lower arm means the rearward lower arm of the front suspension. It connects the frame to the front wheel spindle through a pivot and ball joint, helping locate the wheel while allowing suspension movement. Replacement requires controlled ball-joint separation, new specified fasteners and final tightening with the suspension at its normal resting height.
guides.why: The ball-joint seal can be damaged by the wrong separating tool or by allowing the released parts to fall into position. Tightening the frame pivot with the suspension hanging can produce incorrect clamp load and damage the bushing. Vehicles with dynamic suspension also need their height-sensor linkage protected and their ride height recalibrated after reassembly.
searchTerms: front suspension rear lower arm replacement
ride height calibration after lower arm replacement
front toe after suspension arm replacement

when.summary: When an established front-suspension repair requires removal or replacement of the rear lower arm.
notes: The height-sensor and scan-tool operations apply only to vehicles with dynamic suspension.

prepare.title: Gather the specified separator and support equipment
prepare.detail: Use lower-arm ball-joint separator 204-592, vehicle/axle stands and appropriate torque tools. Arrange wheel-removal access and the ability to support the suspension at curb height.

prepare.title: Obtain new critical fasteners
prepare.detail: Have a new arm-to-frame bolt and a new outboard nut. Suspension fasteners must meet the original or equivalent specification; inferior-quality or substitute-design hardware is unsuitable.

prepare.title: Plan the finishing work
prepare.detail: Arrange a front-toe check and adjustment capability. Dynamic-suspension vehicles also require a scan tool that can perform the Ride Height Calibration routine.

steps.title: Expose the arm and protect the height sensor
steps.body: Remove the wheel and tire using the linked procedure. On dynamic-suspension vehicles, remove the ride-height sensor arm bracket bolt and position the bracket aside before disturbing the suspension.

steps.title: Separate the outboard ball joint
steps.body: Remove and discard the outboard nut. Separate the arm from the wheel spindle with separator 204-592. Control the released components as they settle so the ball-joint seal is not damaged.

steps.title: Remove the frame connection
steps.body: Remove and discard the arm-to-frame bolt, then remove the arm. Both discarded fasteners must be replaced during installation.

steps.title: Fit the arm without locking the frame pivot
steps.body: Position the arm and install the new frame bolt finger tight only. Attach the arm to the wheel spindle, install the new outboard nut and tighten it to the specified torque.

steps.title: Load the suspension before tightening the pivot
steps.body: Support the suspension at curb height with vehicle/axle stands, then tighten the frame bolt as specified. This preserves the required bushing installation condition instead of clamping the pivot with the suspension hanging.

steps.title: Restore dynamic-suspension equipment where fitted
steps.body: Reposition the height-sensor arm bracket and tighten its bolt as specified. Connect the scan tool and complete Ride Height Calibration, following the tool’s directions.

steps.title: Refit the wheel and check front toe
steps.body: Install the wheel and tire using its procedure. Check front toe and adjust it if necessary using the Front Toe Adjustment procedure referenced in the arm instructions.

watchFor.title: Prying against the joint or seal
watchFor.body: Do not insert a pry tool or separator fork between the ball joint and wheel knuckle. Any permitted pry-bar use is through the lower arm’s body opening only.

watchFor.title: A connected height-sensor linkage during removal
watchFor.body: Leaving the sensor attached can damage the sensor or dynamic-suspension system as the arm moves.

notes: Curb height describes the suspension’s normal resting position, not the fully extended position produced by lifting the body.

verification.title: Confirm the fastening conditions
verification.body: Confirm that the outboard nut and frame bolt are new, and that the frame bolt received final tightening with the suspension loaded.

verification.title: Record the finishing results
verification.body: Record the front-toe check and any adjustment. Where dynamic suspension is fitted, also record successful completion of Ride Height Calibration.

procedures.purpose: Front suspension rear-lower-arm removal and installation, including the dynamic-suspension branch and final toe check.
Wheel-and-tire removal and installation for access to the front suspension arm.

guides.title: Replace an SVT Performance Package front wheel knuckle
guides.summary: Remove and refit the front wheel knuckle with new specified fasteners, then check camber and calibrate dynamic suspension if fitted.
guides.introduction: The front wheel knuckle carries the wheel hub and connects it to the strut, lower suspension arms and steering tie rod. Its position helps establish wheel geometry while allowing the wheel to steer. This job separates those connections, so correct joint handling, replacement fasteners and final suspension setup are central to a successful repair.
guides.why: Hammering or using a separator fork can damage the knuckle, ball joints or protective seals. Suspension fasteners are critical parts and must match the specified quality and design. A dynamic-suspension height sensor also needs protection during disassembly and calibration afterward.
searchTerms: SVT Performance Package front wheel knuckle

when.summary: When a confirmed repair requires removal or replacement of the front wheel knuckle.
notes: Identify whether dynamic suspension is fitted before beginning.

prepare.title: Arrange suspension-service capability
prepare.detail: Use appropriate vehicle lifting and support, a tie rod end remover, lower-arm ball-joint separator 204-592 and suitable torque equipment. Have access to the brake disc shield and front camber procedures called up by the knuckle procedure.

prepare.title: Obtain the required new fasteners
prepare.detail: Prepare a new tie rod end nut, front and rear lower-arm outboard nuts, and both strut-to-knuckle bolts and nuts. Use the same or equivalent quality and design.

prepare.title: Plan the dynamic-suspension branch
prepare.detail: If fitted, a scan tool capable of running Ride Height Calibration is needed to finish the job.

steps.title: Isolate power and clear the hub area
steps.body: Disconnect the battery ground cable using its procedure; the steering-service notice identifies a risk to the steering gear's internal power relay. Remove the SVT Performance Package front hub assembly and brake disc shield. Remove the wheel speed sensor bolt and position the sensor aside.

steps.title: Separate the steering connection
steps.body: Remove and discard the tie rod end nut. Use the tie rod end remover to separate the joint without striking the knuckle. Position the remover carefully so it does not damage the joint boot.

steps.title: Release the lower suspension arms
steps.body: If dynamic suspension is fitted, remove the height-sensor arm bracket bolt and move the bracket aside before disturbing the lower arms. Discard the front lower-arm outboard nut and separate its joint with tool 204-592, then repeat for the rear lower arm. Do not insert a pry tool or fork between a ball joint and knuckle; any pry-bar use is confined to the lower-arm body opening.

steps.title: Remove the knuckle
steps.body: Control the arms as they settle so their ball-joint seals are not damaged. Remove and discard both strut-to-knuckle bolts and nuts, then remove the knuckle.

steps.title: Rebuild the structural connections
steps.body: Position the knuckle and install new strut bolts and nuts. Reconnect the rear lower arm, followed by the front lower arm, using new outboard nuts. Tighten each connection to its specification in the [knuckle procedure](#/document/G1692539).

steps.title: Restore sensors, steering and hub components
steps.body: Refit the height-sensor arm bracket if equipped. Reconnect the tie rod with a new nut, reinstall the wheel speed sensor, then restore the brake disc shield and hub assembly. Reconnect the battery ground cable.

steps.title: Complete suspension setup
steps.body: Check front camber and adjust it if necessary using Front Camber Adjustment. For dynamic suspension, connect the scan tool and complete Ride Height Calibration following its directions.

watchFor.title: Seal damage during separation
watchFor.body: Care is needed both while applying the separator and while lowering the released arm into its resting position.

watchFor.title: Reused discarded hardware
watchFor.body: The specified nuts and strut fasteners must be replaced, even if they appear serviceable.

notes: The height-sensor disconnection and calibration requirements apply only when dynamic suspension is fitted.

verification.title: Verify mechanical completion
verification.body: Confirm all required new fasteners are installed and tightened, and that the sensor, shield and hub installation steps are complete.

verification.title: Record the setup results
verification.body: Record the front camber check and any adjustment. Where applicable, also record successful completion of Ride Height Calibration.

guides.title: Replace the front wheel spindle
guides.summary: Remove the front spindle from the hub, steering and suspension connections, then rebuild with new specified fasteners and check front camber.
guides.introduction: The front wheel spindle connects the wheel-bearing and hub assembly to the strut, lower suspension arms and steering tie rod. It supports the wheel while allowing the steering linkage to change its direction. Replacement therefore disturbs several structural joints, the wheel-speed sensor and the wheel's alignment. This is advanced suspension work requiring controlled joint separation and access to camber measurement and adjustment.
guides.why: The tapered steering and suspension joints must be separated without damaging the spindle or the protective joint boots. Several fasteners are discarded during removal and replaced during assembly. Their quality and tightening are critical to suspension performance. The battery disconnection also protects the steering gear's internal power relay during associated steering service.

when.summary: When the front spindle requires replacement or removal during a related suspension repair.
notes: This procedure is a removal and installation path; it does not establish that a particular driving symptom condemns the spindle.

prepare.title: Have the correct separation tools
prepare.detail: Use a tie rod end remover and lower-arm ball-joint separator 204-592. Arrange supported access through the linked hub-removal procedure.

prepare.title: Obtain the required new fasteners
prepare.detail: Have new tie-rod and front and rear lower-arm outboard nuts, plus two new strut-to-spindle bolts and nuts. Use specified or equivalent-quality parts without substituting a lesser design.

prepare.title: Arrange completion capability
prepare.detail: Have suitable torque tools and the capability to check and, if necessary, adjust front camber after assembly.

steps.title: Disconnect power and remove the hub components
steps.body: Disconnect the battery ground cable. Remove the front wheel bearing and hub assembly, then the brake disc shield, following the relevant linked procedures.

steps.title: Move the wheel-speed sensor clear
steps.body: Remove the front wheel-speed sensor bolt and position the sensor aside before separating the spindle from its steering and suspension joints.

steps.title: Separate the steering tie rod
steps.body: Remove and discard the tie-rod end nut. Use the tie rod end remover to release the joint. Position the tool carefully to protect the boot; do not hammer the tie rod out of the spindle.

steps.title: Release both lower arms
steps.body: Remove and discard the front lower-arm outboard nut and separate that joint with tool 204-592. Repeat for the rear lower arm at the same front wheel. Do not insert a pry tool or separator fork between either ball joint and the spindle. Any permitted pry-bar use is through the lower-arm body opening. Lower the released parts carefully to protect their seals.

steps.title: Remove and replace the spindle
steps.body: Remove and discard the two strut-to-spindle bolts and nuts, then remove the spindle. Position the replacement and install new strut fasteners. Reattach the rear lower arm, front lower arm and tie rod in that order, using new nuts and each joint's specified torque.

steps.title: Restore the sensor, shield and hub
steps.body: Position and secure the wheel-speed sensor, then install the brake disc shield and front bearing/hub assembly. Follow the spindle procedure and supporting articles for their individual tightening requirements. Reconnect the battery ground cable.

steps.title: Check front camber
steps.body: Measure front camber and adjust it if necessary using the Front Camber Adjustment procedure referenced by the spindle article. This completes the alignment check required after the structural connections have been disturbed.

watchFor.title: Boot or seal damage during separation
watchFor.body: Tool pressure in the wrong place, hammering or uncontrolled movement can damage parts that otherwise could remain in service.

watchFor.title: Reusing discarded fasteners
watchFor.body: The tie-rod nut, both lower-arm outboard nuts and both strut bolt-and-nut sets require replacement.

notes: The separately linked brake disc shield article covers 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications. For 5.2L work, use the applicable shield procedure referenced by the spindle article.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical completion
verification.body: Verify installation and specified tightening of the new structural fasteners, and restoration of the sensor, shield, hub and battery connection.

verification.title: Record the alignment result
verification.body: Record the final front-camber result and whether adjustment was required, using the applicable alignment specification.

procedures.purpose: Complete front spindle removal, installation, fastener requirements and final camber-check direction.
Disconnect and reconnect the battery ground cable.

guides.title: Replace a front wheel stud
guides.summary: Remove the front hub, press out the damaged stud, inspect the hub and bearing, then press in its replacement and reinstall the assembly.
guides.introduction: A wheel stud provides the threaded attachment that lets a wheel nut clamp the wheel against the hub. This repair replaces an individual stud using a hydraulic press after the wheel bearing and hub have been removed. The condition of that assembly determines whether a stud-only repair is appropriate.
guides.why: Pressing the stud transfers force through the hub. The assembly must be supported as illustrated, and the bearing and hub must be inspected after removal of the stud. A new stud cannot correct damage to the surrounding assembly.

when.summary: When a front wheel stud requires replacement.
notes: Choose the hub procedure that matches the vehicle's fitted equipment.

prepare.title: Provide hydraulic-press capability
prepare.detail: Have a hydraulic press and the capability to support the removed hub correctly during stud removal and installation.

prepare.title: Select the correct access procedure
prepare.detail: Use the standard front wheel bearing and hub procedure, or the separate SVT Performance Package procedure where fitted. These provide the vehicle removal and reinstallation details surrounding the bench work.

steps.title: Remove the wheel bearing and hub
steps.body: Follow the applicable linked hub procedure to remove the assembly from the vehicle. This brings the stud and hub to the press for the specified replacement method.

steps.title: Press the old stud out
steps.body: Use the hydraulic press and the removal arrangement illustrated in the wheel-stud procedure. The illustration shows the hub flange supported while the press acts along the stud. Keep that support relationship clear before applying force.

steps.title: Inspect the bearing and hub
steps.body: Inspect both components for damage after the stud is removed. Replace the damaged assembly as necessary before proceeding; the inspection is the decision point between replacing only the stud and carrying out a larger hub repair.

steps.title: Install the stud and return the hub to the vehicle
steps.body: Press the replacement stud into the wheel bearing and hub using the hydraulic press. Reinstall the assembly through the same equipment-specific hub procedure, completing its fastening and installation requirements.

watchFor.title: Incorrect hub procedure
watchFor.body: The SVT Performance Package has its own front-hub procedure. Confirm the fitted package before beginning removal.

notes: The specified replacement method uses a hydraulic press for both stud removal and installation.

diagnostics.finding: The wheel bearing or hub is damaged during the inspection.
diagnostics.meaning: Replacing the stud alone is insufficient.
diagnostics.next: Replace the damaged assembly as necessary before reinstallation.

verification.title: Confirm inspection and reassembly
verification.body: Confirm that the bearing and hub inspection has been completed, any necessary replacement addressed, and the stud pressed into the assembly.

verification.title: Complete the matching hub procedure
verification.body: Verify that hub installation is complete under the procedure for the fitted equipment.

procedures.purpose: Front wheel-stud press removal, bearing and hub inspection, and press installation.
Standard front wheel bearing and hub removal and installation.
Front wheel bearing and hub removal and installation for vehicles with the SVT Performance Package.

guides.title: Replace the rear lower arm vertical link
guides.summary: Replace the rear lower arm vertical link on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine, using two new bolts and tightening them with the suspension loaded.
guides.introduction: The rear lower arm vertical link looks like a tiny dumbbell with an unusually responsible job. It connects the lower arm to the wheel-knuckle area—the structure carrying the rear wheel hub—and helps maintain their relationship as the suspension moves. I’ll walk you through reaching it, replacing its two bolts and putting the wheel back correctly. The bolt count is pleasantly small; the attention they deserve is considerable.
guides.why: The Mustang’s independent rear suspension lets each rear wheel respond to road changes separately. This short upright link forms part of that suspension connection. Its fasteners must clamp correctly, and its bushings—the flexible joints at its attachments—must be tightened with the suspension loaded. Tightening with the suspension hanging can damage the bushings and produce incorrect clamp load. The upper and lower bolts also have different torque values.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang rear lower arm vertical link
lower arm vertical link bolt torque

when.summary: Use this procedure when replacement or removal of the rear lower arm vertical link has already been established as part of the repair.
notes: Applies to the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
A noise or handling complaint alone does not establish that this link needs replacing. This is a replacement procedure, without a link wear limit or a stand-alone diagnostic test.

prepare.title: Arrange safe lifting and a reliable curb-height position
prepare.detail: Have a suitable hoist and vehicle/axle stands ready. Curb height means the suspension’s normal position with the vehicle resting on its wheels. You must be able to establish and hold that position with the wheel removed; no numerical curb-height dimension or measurement method is given here. If you cannot establish it reliably, resolve that before releasing the link. The stand supporting the suspension does not replace safe support of the vehicle itself.

prepare.title: Obtain the link and two new attachment bolts
prepare.detail: Have the correct replacement link and both new lower arm vertical link bolts ready. Both removed bolts must be discarded. Suspension fasteners are critical parts: use the same or equivalent quality and design, never a lesser-quality substitute.

prepare.title: Prepare fastening tools and wheel lubricant
prepare.detail: Have tools suitable for the fitted fasteners and a torque wrench capable of 76 lb.ft (103 Nm), 129 lb.ft (175 Nm) and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). For wheel installation, have cleaning materials and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2. That lubricant is for the wheel pilot interface only; keep wheel stud and wheel nut threads clean and dry.

prepare.title: Review the access and fastening references
prepare.detail: The actions are included below. Keep the [Lower Arm Vertical Link procedure](#/document/G1686649), [Wheel and Tire procedure](#/document/G1686507) and [Jacking and Lifting overview](#/document/G1663631) available for their matching instructions.

steps.title: Identify the lifting points and check lift clearance
steps.body:
Before lifting, use a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Confirm the jack or hoist is rated for the vehicle, including cargo and modifications. If using a jack, support the vehicle on suitable stands at the designated points before going underneath; a jack alone is not a support. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

Locate the triangles stamped into the body or frame that identify the correct lifting points. The lifting illustration shows four positions along the sides of the underbody, ahead of the rear wheels and behind the front wheels. Use the actual stamped marks to locate them on the car.

Check that the hoist adapters and lifting arms clear the suspension, exhaust, steering linkage, mounting brackets and stabilizer brackets where fitted. Protect the axle and rear cover from contact. If using a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving onto it.

steps.title: Position and raise the vehicle safely
steps.body:
With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the Mustang on the hoist and raise it using the identified lifting points.

Never get underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; use floor stands when supporting a jacked vehicle. The emergency jack supplied with the car is intended for changing a deflated tire, not this repair. Never apply jack pressure to either bumper. Incorrect lifting or support can let the vehicle shift or fall and cause serious injury.

steps.title: Remove the rear wheel and tire assembly
steps.body:
Remove the five wheel nuts, then remove the wheel and tire assembly from the side being repaired. This exposes the vertical link and its two attachment bolts.

Do not use heat to release a seized wheel nut: heat can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. If a nut will not release, stop wheel removal until a suitable non-heat removal approach is established. The tire stays mounted on its wheel for this job.

steps.title: Locate the link and support the suspension at curb height
steps.body:
Find the short upright link beside the rear brake disc. It has a rounded attachment at each end, with one upper bolt and one lower bolt. The brake assembly and nearby lines remain installed.

Position a vehicle/axle stand beneath the rear lower-arm area shown in the support illustration, and support the suspension at curb height before loosening either link bolt. Confirm that the support is stable and that the suspension is held in its normal loaded position. Keep that support in place through link removal and tightening.

steps.title: Remove both bolts and lift out the link
steps.body: With the suspension supported, remove the upper and lower lower arm vertical link bolts, then remove the link from between its attachments. Discard both bolts immediately so neither finds its way back into the repair. Old bolts have a remarkable talent for looking useful at precisely the wrong moment.

steps.title: Position the replacement link and install two new bolts
steps.body:
Place the replacement link between its upper and lower attachments in the same position as the removed link. Install a new upper bolt and a new lower bolt.

Keep the suspension supported at curb height. Final tightening must take place with the suspension loaded, or with the vehicle’s weight resting on its wheels and tires. Do not torque these bushing attachments with the suspension hanging.

steps.title: Tighten the upper bolt, then the lower bolt
steps.body:
With the suspension still loaded at curb height, tighten in this order:

1. Upper lower arm vertical link bolt: 76 lb.ft (103 Nm).
2. Lower lower arm vertical link bolt: 129 lb.ft (175 Nm).

Check the bolt position before selecting the torque value. These two fasteners share a link, not a tightening specification.

steps.title: Clean the wheel mounting faces and central pilot bore
steps.body:
Before reinstalling the wheel, remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from its flat mounting face and the mating mounting surface on the hub or brake disc. Also clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the opening that fits over the hub’s raised center.

Check that any fasteners securing the brake disc to the hub are secure and do not interfere with the wheel seating flat. Contamination or interference at these mounting faces can allow wheel nuts to loosen and the wheel to come off, causing loss of control and serious injury or death.

steps.title: Lubricate only the wheel pilot interface
steps.body:
Apply a thin film of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, only where the wheel’s central pilot bore meets the hub pilot. The pilot is the raised center that locates the wheel.

Keep the lubricant off the flat wheel-to-brake-disc mounting faces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and brake disc friction surfaces. Check that wheel stud and wheel nut threads are clean and dry before assembly. I keep the lubricant’s territory small here: the center locating interface gets the film.

steps.title: Refit the wheel and finger-tighten the nuts
steps.body:
Before lowering, make sure the parking brake is applied. Restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground, and keep the vehicle restrained for final wheel-nut tightening. Do not lower an unrestrained vehicle in Neutral.

Position the wheel over the hub and install all five wheel nuts. Tighten them only finger tight at this stage.

Once the link bolts have been secured and the wheel is installed, clear the suspension-support stand as part of safely lowering the vehicle. Lower the Mustang until its weight rests on its tires before final wheel-nut tightening.

steps.title: Torque the wheel nuts in the five-position star pattern
steps.body:
With the vehicle resting on its tires and the wheel stud and wheel nut threads clean and dry, tighten all five wheel nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm).

Use the illustrated star sequence. Viewed from outside the wheel, with one nut at the top, the order is: top → lower left → upper right → upper left → lower right. If the wheel is rotated, follow the same crossing pattern around the five nuts.

Do not tighten around the wheel in a circle. Uneven tightening can cause brake disc runout—side-to-side variation as the disc rotates—which promotes brake roughness, shudder and vibration.

steps.title: Check completion and arrange wheel-nut retightening
steps.body:
Confirm that both link bolts are new and were tightened with the suspension loaded: upper 76 lb.ft (103 Nm), then lower 129 lb.ft (175 Nm). Confirm that all five wheel nuts received 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) in the star pattern with the car resting on its tires.

Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after reinstalling the wheel. Wheels can loosen after initial tightening; missing this follow-up can result in serious injury.

watchFor.title: Vehicle support and suspension support serve different jobs
watchFor.body: The hoist or vehicle stands support the car. The additional stand holds the rear suspension at curb height while the link is released and secured. Make sure both arrangements remain stable.

watchFor.title: Loaded tightening is part of the specification
watchFor.body: The correct torque with the suspension hanging is still an incorrect installation. The bushing fasteners require loaded suspension to avoid incorrect clamp load and bushing damage.

watchFor.title: Both removed link bolts are discarded
watchFor.body: Use two new bolts of the correct quality and design. Do not substitute a lower-grade fastener or reuse an old bolt because its appearance seems acceptable.

watchFor.title: Keep wheel lubricant away from friction and fastening surfaces
watchFor.body: XL-2 belongs only at the pilot bore-to-hub pilot interface. The mounting faces and brake friction surfaces must stay free of it, and the wheel stud and nut threads must be clean and dry for the stated torque.

notes: The [Rear Suspension overview](#/document/G1686641) describes the independent rear suspension layout. Its stabilizer bar and links control lean and sway; identify the short lower arm vertical link beside the brake disc before beginning.

If separate tire-changing or balancing work is added on alloy or carbon-fiber wheels, use a center-clamp tire changer such as Hunter Auto 34, Revolution, TC3900 or equivalent. Do not use a table-top machine that grips inside the wheel and rides on its front flange. Use a balancer that does not contact the wheel face, such as Hunter Road Force Touch GSP9700. Unsuitable machines can damage the wheel.

diagnostics.finding: A wheel nut is seized and will not release.
diagnostics.meaning: Wheel removal is blocked. Applying heat risks damage to the wheel and wheel bearing.
diagnostics.next: Stop at wheel removal and establish an appropriate non-heat removal approach before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: The suspension is hanging, or its curb-height support cannot be held securely.
diagnostics.meaning: The required condition for releasing and securing the link has not been established.
diagnostics.next: Correct the support arrangement before removing the bolts. Do not perform final bushing-fastener tightening until the suspension is loaded.

diagnostics.finding: Corrosion, debris or a protruding brake-disc attachment prevents the wheel from seating flat.
diagnostics.meaning: The wheel mounting interface is not ready for installation, and the wheel nuts may loosen if it is assembled this way.
diagnostics.next: Clean the mating surfaces and pilot bore, and secure any interfering disc attachment correctly before fitting the wheel.

diagnostics.finding: Anti-seize has reached the wheel studs, nuts or flat mounting faces.
diagnostics.meaning: The wheel is outside the required clean, dry fastening condition or has lubricant in a prohibited location.
diagnostics.next: Remove the misplaced lubricant and restore clean, dry threads and mounting faces before installation. Resolve any contamination of brake pads or disc friction surfaces before using the vehicle.

verification.title: Verify the link installation
verification.body: Check that the link occupies both attachment positions and that both bolts are new. Confirm the tightening record shows upper 76 lb.ft (103 Nm), followed by lower 129 lb.ft (175 Nm), with the suspension loaded.

verification.title: Verify wheel seating and fastening
verification.body: Confirm the wheel mounting faces and pilot bore were cleaned, lubricant was confined to the pilot interface, and all five nuts were torqued to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) in a star pattern with the vehicle resting on its tires.

verification.title: Complete the required follow-up
verification.body: Record the wheel installation mileage and retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi), using the clean, dry thread requirement and specified star pattern. These are installation completion checks, not a diagnostic test of the link.

guides.title: Replace the rear suspension lower arm
guides.summary: Replace the rear lower arm with controlled spring unloading, new specified fasteners, loaded-height tightening and final camber checks.
guides.introduction: The rear lower arm connects the chassis to the wheel knuckle and supports the coil spring and shock absorber. Together with the upper arm, it allows the wheel to move over road irregularities independently. Replacement therefore involves both wheel location and stored spring force; it is more involved than removing an unloaded suspension link.
guides.why: The spring must stay controlled as the arm is lowered. During assembly, its seats must align correctly, and the suspension bushing fasteners must receive their final tightening at loaded height. Tightening them with the suspension hanging can produce incorrect clamp load and damage the bushings.
searchTerms: rear control arm and bushing assembly

when.summary: When suspension assessment has established that the rear lower arm needs replacement.
notes: Dynamic suspension adds ride-height sensor bracket handling and scan-tool calibration.

prepare.title: Arrange secure support and controlled unloading
prepare.detail: Have vehicle/axle stands, suitable knuckle-retaining straps and the capability to support and lower the suspension safely while controlling the spring. Arrange rear-camber measurement and adjustment.

prepare.title: Obtain replacement hardware
prepare.detail: Replace the two lower shock bolts, vertical-link lower bolt, stabilizer-link lower nut, arm-to-knuckle bolt and both arm-to-frame bolts. Use the specified or equivalent-quality fasteners, suitable torque equipment and hand tools with the stabilizer stud's hex-holding feature.

prepare.title: Plan exhaust and equipment access
prepare.detail: Have the engine-matched muffler and tailpipe procedure for bolt clearance. Dynamic suspension also requires a scan tool capable of the Ride Height Calibration routine.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and support the suspension
steps.body: Follow the wheel-and-tire procedure, then use the stands to raise the suspension approximately 20mm from its rebound position. Maintain controlled support as the attached components are released.

steps.title: Disconnect the arm's outer attachments
steps.body: Remove and discard the lower shock bolts. If dynamic suspension is fitted, unbolt and move aside the ride-height sensor arm bracket. Discard the vertical-link lower bolt and move the link aside. Support the knuckle with retaining straps before disconnecting the stabilizer link and arm-to-knuckle joint, discarding their lower nut and bolt. Hold the stabilizer stud by its hex feature; do not use power tools.

steps.title: Clear the exhaust and release the spring
steps.body: Remove the muffler and tailpipe for rearward-bolt clearance. Remove and discard the forward arm-to-frame bolt, then lower the supported suspension to release spring compression. Prevent the spring from falling and place it aside when released. Remove and discard the rearward arm-to-frame bolt and remove the arm.

steps.title: Position the arm and spring
steps.body: Inspect and align the lower spring seat. Support and raise the replacement arm while holding the spring in place. Seat the spring correctly in both upper and lower seats, ensuring the upper seat sits properly on its mount. Install the new rearward and forward frame bolts finger-tight, recheck spring seating and reinstall the muffler and tailpipe.

steps.title: Reconnect the suspension attachments
steps.body: Position the knuckle, stabilizer link and vertical link with their new fasteners finger-tight. Refit the ride-height sensor bracket when equipped, and install the new lower shock bolts. Tighten the bracket and shock fasteners to their specified values in the lower-arm procedure.

steps.title: Finish tightening at curb height
steps.body: Support the suspension at curb height. Tighten the rearward frame bolt, arm-to-knuckle bolt, forward frame bolt and vertical-link lower bolt in the specified sequence and to their individual torques. Finish the new stabilizer-link lower nut at 85 lb.ft (115 Nm), holding the stud with the hex feature and using no power tools.

steps.title: Restore the wheel and suspension settings
steps.body: Install the wheel and tire using its procedure. Check rear camber and adjust if necessary. For dynamic suspension, connect the scan tool and complete Ride Height Calibration, following its directions.

watchFor.title: Uncontrolled spring movement
watchFor.body: Keep the spring supported during unloading and held in position during assembly. Take extra care whenever it remains compressed.

watchFor.title: Damage to stabilizer-link joints
watchFor.body: These low-friction ball joints can turn easily. Power tools can damage the joints and boots; use the hex-holding feature throughout nut removal and installation.

notes: Only the stabilizer link's lower connection needs releasing for this job; the complete link procedure supplies its final nut torque.
Use the applicable 5.2L exhaust procedure on that engine; the separate exhaust links below cover only their named engines.

verification.title: Check assembly completion
verification.body: Confirm both spring seats are correctly positioned, discarded hardware has been replaced and all specified fasteners—including the initially finger-tight stabilizer nut—have received final tightening.

verification.title: Record geometry and calibration
verification.body: Record the rear-camber check and any adjustment. Where dynamic suspension is fitted, also record successful completion of the Ride Height Calibration routine.
