guides.title: Replace a 2015 Mustang Rear Shock Absorber
guides.summary: Remove and refit a rear shock with the suspension supported, renew its mounting bolts, and handle the rod nut correctly when fitting a new shock. Includes dynamic-suspension wiring and complete wheel installation.
guides.introduction: The spring lets a rear wheel move over a bump; the shock helps stop it demanding an encore. I’ll walk you through reaching the shock through the rear wheel opening, supporting the suspension, and replacing the unit without turning its electrical lead into an accidental lifting strap. The important details are straightforward: four new mounting bolts, controlled rod-nut work when fitting a new shock, and a properly seated wheel afterward.
guides.why: The rear wheels can move independently over road imperfections. Each shock mounts to the lower suspension arm and works with the coil spring to control up-and-down movement. Supporting that arm keeps the suspension controlled while the shock is disconnected. Correct fasteners and tightening matter because these attachments secure a working suspension component, not decorative garage jewelry.

when.summary: For rear shock removal or replacement on a 2015 Mustang with a 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine, including dynamic suspension where fitted.
notes: Disconnect and reconnect the shock electrical connector only on vehicles with dynamic suspension.
Rod-nut and cap removal applies only when installing a new component; remove and refit the cap only if equipped.
Both suspension configurations use two lower mounting bolts and two upper mounting bolts per shock.

prepare.title: Establish the repair before dismantling
prepare.detail: Begin once the need to remove or replace the shock has been established. This procedure does not include a damper performance test or dynamic-suspension electrical diagnosis.

prepare.title: Have the replacement parts ready
prepare.detail: For each shock removed, obtain two new lower mounting bolts and two new upper mounting bolts. When installing a new shock, also obtain a new rod nut. Use the same or equivalent-quality suspension fasteners, with no lesser-quality or substitute design.

prepare.title: Arrange separate vehicle and suspension support
prepare.detail: Have a hoist or suitable workshop jack and vehicle stands rated for the vehicle’s weight, including cargo and modifications. Have an additional vehicle/axle stand to support the rear suspension while the shock is detached. The emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this repair. Review the [lifting points](#/document/G1663631) before raising the car.

prepare.title: Prepare hand tools and torque equipment
prepare.detail: Have suitable hand tools for the wheel nuts and shock fasteners, a tool that engages the shock rod’s hex-holding feature, and torque equipment covering 22–150 lb.ft (30–204 Nm). The rod must be held while its nut is removed and installed. Do not use power tools to remove that nut.

prepare.title: Prepare wheel-cleaning materials and protection
prepare.detail: Have cleaning cloths and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2. Read its material safety information before use. Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. Keep any cleaning solvents away from ignition sources.

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start and secure the work area
steps.body:
Before working around or underneath the car, disable remote start, if fitted, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup in the Central Display. Switch the ignition off and remove the key to prevent another person starting the engine.
For a jack-and-stand setup, position the car on a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block every wheel that will remain on the ground. These precautions must be in place before lifting. See [service safety precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Raise and securely support the vehicle
steps.body:
For hoist access, position the vehicle in Neutral and use a hoist with adequate capacity. Locate the triangles stamped into the body sheet metal or frame: they identify the correct lifting points. The [lifting overview](#/document/G1663631) shows the four locations along the sides of the underbody, ahead of the rear wheels and behind the front wheels.
Position the hoist adapters clear of suspension parts, brackets, exhaust, steering linkage, axle and rear cover. If using a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving onto it.
If using a workshop jack, lift only at the identified points and support the vehicle on floor stands before working underneath. Never rely on the jack alone, and never lift against either bumper. Vehicle support and the suspension support added later perform separate jobs.

steps.title: Remove the rear wheel and tire assembly
steps.body:
With the vehicle securely supported, remove the five wheel nuts and lift the wheel and tire assembly off the hub. Do not use heat on a seized wheel nut; it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. A nut that will not release without heat needs its removal problem resolved before continuing.
Set the wheel aside so its mounting surfaces remain protected. Removing the wheel opens access to the shock’s lower attachment and its upper body mount. The [wheel procedure](#/document/G1686507) covers removal and installation of the complete assembly; separating the tire from the wheel is unnecessary.

steps.title: Locate the shock and support the rear suspension
steps.body:
Through the wheel opening, identify the upright shock running from the lower suspension arm to the body above. The coil spring is a separate component nearby; the [rear suspension overview](#/document/G1686641) explains how they work together.
Place a vehicle/axle stand beneath the lower-arm area near the shock’s lower attachment, as shown in the [shock procedure](#/document/G1686650), and bring it into secure contact to support the suspension. Keep this support in place throughout shock removal and installation. Do not confuse supporting the arm with supporting the vehicle.

steps.title: Disconnect the electrical plug if dynamic suspension is fitted
steps.body:
On a dynamic-suspension shock, a short lead runs from the top of the shock to an electrical connector beside the upper mounting area. Locate that connection and disconnect it before removing either mounting attachment. Keep the separated lead clear of the shock’s removal path.
On a vehicle without dynamic suspension, skip this electrical step.

steps.title: Remove and discard the two lower mounting bolts
steps.body:
With the rear suspension still supported, locate the two bolts securing the shock’s lower mounting bracket to the lower arm. They sit on either side of the lower shock attachment.
Remove both bolts and discard them. The dynamic-suspension and other suspension illustrations show alternative versions of this attachment: remove the two bolts fitted to your car, not two sets of two. The old bolts do not get a second career.

steps.title: Remove the upper bolts and withdraw the shock
steps.body:
Support the shock itself while removing the two upper bolts, one at each end of the upper mounting bracket where it attaches to the body. Discard both bolts.
Remove the shock through the wheel opening, keeping it clear of the nearby wiring and brake hose. Leave the suspension stand in position. The upper bracket comes away with the shock; its central rod nut is dealt with off the vehicle only when installing a new component.

steps.title: For a new shock, release the upper mount from the old rod
steps.body:
Skip this step and the next if the removed shock is being refitted without new-component assembly work.
If a cap covers the rod nut at the center of the upper mount, remove it. Engage the rod’s hex-holding feature to prevent the rod turning, then remove the rod nut with hand tools. Do not use power tools for removal. Discard the nut.
Remove the upper mount released by the nut, retaining its orientation and the arrangement of the mounting pieces for assembly on the new shock.

steps.title: Assemble the new shock with a new rod nut
steps.body:
Fit the upper mount to the new shock in its retained arrangement. Hold the rod against rotation using its hex-holding feature and install a new rod nut.
Tighten the rod nut to 22 lb.ft (30 Nm) while keeping the rod restrained. Refit the rod-nut cap if equipped. I’d finish this small assembly now, while it is accessible, rather than rediscover it halfway into the wheel opening.

steps.title: Install the shock’s lower attachment with new bolts
steps.body:
Position the shock at its lower attachment and install two new lower mounting bolts. Use the attachment layout matching the fitted suspension.
Tighten both lower bolts to 35 lb.ft (48 Nm). This value applies to both illustrated lower-mount configurations. Keep the rear suspension supported.

steps.title: Compress the shock, locate the upper mount and tighten it
steps.body:
Compress the shock enough to bring its upper mounting bracket beneath the body’s alignment pins. Visually check that the bracket is aligned with both pins before installing the bolts.
Install two new upper mounting bolts and tighten both to 66 lb.ft (90 Nm). If the bracket does not line up, reposition the shock and mount before proceeding; do not use the bolts to drag a misplaced bracket into position.

steps.title: Reconnect dynamic-suspension wiring and check the installation
steps.body:
If dynamic suspension is fitted, reconnect the electrical plug beside the upper shock mount. Check that the connection is fully joined and that its lead is clear of the mounting joint and surrounding components.
Before removing suspension support, confirm that both lower bolts and both upper bolts are installed and tightened, the upper mount is located at the body alignment pins, and any rod-nut cap disturbed during replacement is back in place.

steps.title: Clean the wheel mounting faces and central pilot bore
steps.body:
Clean corrosion, dirt and other foreign material from the wheel’s flat mounting face and the mating hub/brake-disc mounting face. Also clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the center hole that locates the wheel on the hub’s raised pilot. Do not overlook that bore just because the flat face looks respectable.
Check that any fasteners securing the brake disc to the hub are secure and do not obstruct the wheel’s seating surfaces. Do not fit the wheel over contamination or an obstruction: incomplete seating can let the wheel nuts loosen and the wheel come off.

steps.title: Apply XL-2 only at the pilot interface
steps.body:
Apply a thin film of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, only where the clean wheel pilot bore meets the hub pilot.
Keep it off the flat wheel-to-brake-disc mounting surfaces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and brake-disc friction surfaces. The wheel nut torque is specified for clean, dry stud and nut threads; anti-seize is not permission to lubricate the whole damn neighborhood.

steps.title: Fit the wheel and start all five nuts by hand
steps.body:
Position the wheel and tire assembly on the hub and install all five wheel nuts. Tighten them only finger tight at this stage, as directed in the [wheel installation procedure](#/document/G1686507).
Check that the wheel sits against the cleaned mounting face before lowering.

steps.title: Remove the suspension support and lower the vehicle
steps.body:
Once the shock is fully secured and the wheel is installed, remove the separate rear-suspension stand. Check that tools and loose equipment are clear of the lowering path.
Before lowering, set the parking brake. Restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground, and keep the vehicle restrained afterward; do not lower an unrestrained vehicle in Neutral.
Lower the vehicle using the hoist or workshop lifting equipment. With a jack-and-stand setup, use the jack to take the vehicle’s weight before removing the vehicle stands, then lower it onto its tires. Do not put yourself underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Keep the vehicle secured against rolling throughout the transition.

steps.title: Tighten the wheel nuts on the ground in the star sequence
steps.body:
Perform final tightening with the vehicle resting on its tires. Tighten all five nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) in a star/cross pattern.
Viewed from the wheel face, the illustrated order is: 1, top; 2, lower left; 3, upper right; 4, upper left; 5, lower right. Use that crossing sequence rather than working around the circle. Incorrect sequencing can increase brake-disc runout—sideways variation as the disc rotates—and contribute to brake shudder and vibration.
The torque value requires clean, dry wheel stud and wheel nut threads.

steps.title: Complete the stationary checks and restore the vehicle
steps.body:
Confirm the wheel is seated and all five nuts have received final torque. Check that no vehicle or suspension stands, tools or loose parts remain beneath the car.
Secure the parked vehicle before removing the wheel chocks. Restore any settings changed for service, including remote start if it was previously enabled, only after the work area is clear and service is complete. These are assembly-completion checks, not a test proving the old shock caused a particular symptom.

steps.title: Retighten the wheel nuts within 100 miles
steps.body:
Arrange to retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after wheel installation. Use the same star pattern and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) specification, with the vehicle resting on its tires and clean, dry threads.
Do not skip this follow-up: a wheel can loosen after its initial tightening.

watchFor.title: Suspension support must remain effective
watchFor.body: Support the rear suspension before releasing the shock and keep that support in place until both attachments are secured. The stand beneath the suspension does not replace the hoist or stands supporting the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Two lower bolts, not four
watchFor.body: The two lower-mount illustrations represent configuration alternatives. Each shock uses two lower bolts, renewed during refitting, and both configurations tighten to 35 lb.ft (48 Nm).

watchFor.title: Discarded fasteners stay discarded
watchFor.body: Renew both upper bolts and both lower bolts whenever they are removed. Renew the rod nut when performing the new-component assembly steps. Suspension fastener quality and design must match the original or an equivalent.

watchFor.title: Hold the rod during nut work
watchFor.body: Use the rod’s hex-holding feature during removal and installation of its nut. Do not use power tools to remove the nut. Tighten the new rod nut to 22 lb.ft (30 Nm).

watchFor.title: Keep wheel lubricant away from threads and brakes
watchFor.body: XL-2 belongs only at the pilot-bore-to-hub-pilot interface. Clean mating faces, dry wheel fastener threads and uncontaminated brake friction surfaces are essential to correct wheel installation.

notes: This job removes the complete wheel and tire assembly; tire-changing and balancing machinery are not needed.
The shock, coil spring and stabilizer bar have different roles: the shock and spring control vertical movement, while the stabilizer bar and its links control suspension lean and sway.

diagnostics.finding: The shock has an electrical lead and connector beside its upper mounting area.
diagnostics.meaning: The dynamic-suspension electrical branch applies.
diagnostics.next: Disconnect the plug before releasing the shock mountings and reconnect it after the shock is secured.

diagnostics.finding: The original shock is being removed and refitted without installing a new component.
diagnostics.meaning: The new-component rod-nut and cap steps do not apply.
diagnostics.next: Leave that assembly intact. Renew the four mounting bolts during installation.

diagnostics.finding: A new shock is being installed and a cap covers the rod nut.
diagnostics.meaning: The cap must be removed to reach the rod nut and restored after assembly.
diagnostics.next: Remove the cap, hold the rod by its hex feature, remove the nut with hand tools and discard it. Assemble with a new nut at 22 lb.ft (30 Nm), then refit the cap.

diagnostics.finding: The upper mounting bracket does not align with the body pins.
diagnostics.meaning: The mount is not yet positioned for fastening.
diagnostics.next: Keep the suspension supported, compress and reposition the shock, and visually align the bracket beneath both pins before installing the new upper bolts.

diagnostics.finding: A wheel nut is seized.
diagnostics.meaning: Normal wheel removal cannot yet be completed.
diagnostics.next: Stop at wheel removal and resolve the seized fastener without applying heat, which can damage the wheel and bearing.

diagnostics.finding: Corrosion, debris or a protruding disc-retaining fastener prevents flat wheel seating.
diagnostics.meaning: The wheel cannot be safely clamped against its mating face.
diagnostics.next: Clean the wheel and hub/disc mounting surfaces and correct any retaining-fastener interference before installing the wheel.

verification.title: Shock fasteners and upper alignment
verification.body: Confirm two new lower bolts at 35 lb.ft (48 Nm), two new upper bolts at 66 lb.ft (90 Nm), and the upper mount located beneath the body alignment pins. For new-component assembly, confirm a new rod nut at 22 lb.ft (30 Nm) and the cap restored if equipped.

verification.title: Electrical connection where fitted
verification.body: Confirm the dynamic-suspension connector is rejoined and its lead is clear of the mounting joints and surrounding parts.

verification.title: Wheel seating and final tightening
verification.body: Confirm the flat mating faces and pilot bore were cleaned, XL-2 was confined to the pilot interface, and all five wheel nuts were tightened in the star sequence to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) with the car resting on its tires.

verification.title: Support removal and follow-up
verification.body: Confirm the vehicle is securely parked, all lifting and suspension supports are removed, service settings are restored as appropriate, and wheel-nut retightening is arranged within 160 km (100 mi).

procedures.purpose: Rear shock access, supported removal, configuration branches, upper-mount assembly, replacement fasteners and installation torques.
Wheel removal and installation, mounting-face and pilot-bore cleaning, XL-2 placement, wheel-nut sequence, torque and retightening requirement.
Rear suspension layout and the shock’s relationship to the lower arm, spring and independent wheel movement.
Triangle-marked lifting points, vehicle support requirements and lifting-equipment clearance precautions.
Remote-start prevention, ignition and key precautions, parking and chocking, lifting capacity and personal protection.

stepGroups.summary: Prevent startup, lift safely, remove the wheel and support the rear suspension.

stepGroups.title: Disconnect and remove the shock
stepGroups.summary: Handle dynamic-suspension wiring and discard the four mounting bolts.

stepGroups.title: Prepare a new shock
stepGroups.summary: Transfer the upper mount, hold the rod and tighten a new rod nut when replacing the component.

stepGroups.title: Secure and reconnect the shock
stepGroups.summary: Tighten the lower attachment, align the upper mount and restore any electrical connection.

stepGroups.title: Clean and reinstall the wheel
stepGroups.summary: Prepare the mating surfaces, lubricate only the pilot interface and tighten the wheel on the ground.

stepGroups.title: Finish and arrange the wheel-nut recheck
stepGroups.summary: Complete stationary checks, restore service settings and retighten within 100 miles.

guides.title: Replace the rear stabilizer bar bushings
guides.summary: Replace both rear stabilizer bar bushings on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine. Install the bushings dry with their slits facing forward, renew all four bracket bolts and tighten them to 52 lb.ft (70 Nm).
guides.introduction: The rear stabilizer bar helps keep the Mustang’s cornering enthusiasm from turning into excessive body lean. Its bushings have a quieter supporting role: they cradle the bar inside its mounting brackets. I’ll walk you through replacing both, including safe access and the optional wheel-removal branch. These bushings have one firm preference: keep the grease to yourself.
guides.why: The stabilizer bar and its links control suspension lean and sway, while the bushings support the bar at its brackets. This replacement depends on three small but important details: both bushing slits face the front of the car, the bar and bushings remain unlubricated, and the brackets receive new bolts tightened to the specified torque.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang rear stabilizer bar bushing replacement

when.summary: Use this procedure when both rear stabilizer bar bushings have been identified for replacement.
notes: The replacement covers the bushings on both sides.
Wheel removal is optional access work, not a required step in the bushing replacement.

prepare.title: Establish that replacement is the right job
prepare.detail: This article teaches replacement, not diagnosis of a suspension noise or handling complaint. There is no bushing wear limit or diagnostic test here to decide whether the bushings caused a complaint; establish that separately before choosing parts.

prepare.title: Gather parts and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Have two replacement rear stabilizer bar bushings, four new bushing-bracket bolts, suitable tools for the fitted fasteners and a torque wrench capable of 52 lb.ft (70 Nm). Each bracket has two bolts. The removed bolts must be discarded.

prepare.title: Arrange safe lifting
prepare.detail: Use a suitable hoist with the transmission in NEUTRAL. Locate the stamped triangles identifying the lifting points. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; a jack-supported vehicle requires floor stands. The vehicle’s emergency jack is for changing a deflated tire, not for this repair.

prepare.title: Keep assembly aids separate
prepare.detail: Do not lubricate the stabilizer bar or its bushings: lubrication can damage the bushings. Water may be applied to the brackets to help them fit.

prepare.title: If you choose to remove wheels
prepare.detail: Have cleaning materials, Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 and a torque wrench capable of 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). The anti-seize belongs only at the wheel’s central locating interface, never on the stabilizer bar or bushings. Wheel studs and nut threads must remain clean and dry.

steps.title: Position and lift the Mustang
steps.body:
Before lifting, use a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Confirm the jack or hoist is rated for the vehicle, including cargo and modifications. If using a jack, support the vehicle on suitable stands at the designated points before going underneath; a jack alone is not a support. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on the hoist. Locate the stamped triangles at the four lifting locations along the underside near the sides of the body, and use the lifting points identified by those marks. See [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631).

Before raising the car, check that the adapters and hoisting forks clear suspension parts, mounting brackets, stabilizer brackets, exhaust and steering linkage. Avoid contact that could damage the axle or rear cover. Never apply jack pressure to either bumper.

For a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving onto it. Raise the vehicle only after the equipment is correctly positioned. Incorrect lifting locations can allow the vehicle to shift or fall.

steps.title: Remove wheels only if you want additional access
steps.body:
The bushing procedure starts underneath the raised vehicle and does not require wheel removal. If you leave the wheels fitted, continue to the next step and skip the later wheel-refitting actions.

If you choose to remove a wheel, remove its five wheel nuts and take off the wheel. Do not use heat to release a seized nut; it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. The [Wheel and Tire procedure](#/document/G1686507) covers this optional branch.

steps.title: Find the two bushing brackets underneath the rear of the car
steps.body:
Locate the rear stabilizer bar and identify the two brackets wrapped over its bushings, one on each side. Each bushing surrounds the bar, and each bracket has two retaining bolts.

The [rear suspension overview](#/document/G1686641) explains the bar’s role in controlling lean and sway. For this job, the removal path is the bracket bolts, then the brackets, then the bushings; no electrical disconnection is part of that sequence.

steps.title: Remove both brackets and discard their bolts
steps.body:
On one side, remove the two rear stabilizer bar bushing-bracket bolts, then remove the bracket from over the bushing. Repeat on the other side.

Discard all four removed bolts and retain the brackets for installation. Keep the discarded hardware apart from the new bolts so it cannot wander back into service. The [bushing replacement procedure](#/document/G1686652) requires new bracket bolts.

steps.title: Remove both bushings from the bar
steps.body:
With both brackets removed, locate the slit in each bushing and open it sufficiently to remove the bushing from around the bar. Remove the bushing on each side.

The slit lets the bushing come off the bar without sliding it along the bar’s bends. Identify the front of the vehicle now; that is the direction both replacement slits must face.

steps.title: Fit the replacement bushings dry, with both slits facing forward
steps.body:
Place each replacement bushing around the bar at its bracket location through the bushing’s slit. Orient the slit toward the front of the vehicle on both sides.

Check the actual seam on each bushing before covering it with the bracket. Leave the stabilizer bar and bushings unlubricated. This is one of those occasions when reaching for grease creates a problem instead of solving one.

steps.title: Install both brackets with new bolts
steps.body:
Fit each retained bracket over its replacement bushing. If the bracket needs help fitting over the bushing, water may be applied to the bracket.

Install two new bracket bolts on each side. Tighten every rear stabilizer bar bushing-bracket bolt to 52 lb.ft (70 Nm). Complete both sides.

steps.title: Check the bushing installation while it is still accessible
steps.body:
Before lowering the vehicle, visually confirm that both bushings surround the bar at their bracket locations, both slits face forward and both brackets are fitted over the bushings. Confirm that all four bolts are new and have received 52 lb.ft (70 Nm).

These are assembly checks: they confirm the work you have just performed, rather than diagnose a suspension complaint.

steps.title: If wheels were removed, clean the mounting faces and central locating bore
steps.body:
Before refitting each removed wheel, remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel’s flat mounting face and the mating hub or brake-disc mounting face. Check that any rotor-to-hub retaining fasteners are secured and do not protrude into or obstruct the wheel’s mounting contact.

Also clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the center hole that locates on the raised hub pilot. The bore needs cleaning as well as the flat mounting face.

Apply a thin film of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 only at the interface between that pilot bore and the hub pilot. Keep it off the flat wheel-to-brake-disc/drum mounting surfaces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and brake-disc friction surfaces. Keep the stud and nut threads clean and dry. Dirt trapped between mounting faces can allow the wheel nuts to loosen in service.

steps.title: Refit removed wheels and complete final tightening on the tires
steps.body:
Before lowering, make sure the parking brake is applied. Restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground, and keep the vehicle restrained for final wheel-nut tightening. Do not lower an unrestrained vehicle in Neutral.

For each removed wheel, position it on the hub and install all five nuts finger tight only at this stage.

Once the underbody work is complete and the area is clear, lower the vehicle until it rests on its tires. Final-tighten the wheel nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) in a star/cross pattern.

Using the illustrated five-nut arrangement with one nut at the top, the sequence is: top, lower left, upper right, upper left, lower right. The sequence crosses the wheel rather than proceeding around its rim. This helps avoid brake-disc runout—uneven rotation that can contribute to brake roughness, shudder and vibration. The torque applies to clean, dry stud and nut threads.

steps.title: Finish and schedule the wheel-nut recheck if applicable
steps.body:
Before lowering, make sure the parking brake is applied. Restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground, and keep the vehicle restrained for final wheel-nut tightening. Do not lower an unrestrained vehicle in Neutral.

If the wheels stayed fitted, lower the vehicle after completing the bushing and bracket checks and clearing the work area.

If any wheel was removed and reinstalled, confirm its final tightening is complete and arrange to retighten its nuts within 160 km (100 mi). Wheels can loosen after initial installation, so that recheck is part of finishing the wheel work.

watchFor.title: Incorrect lifting-point or adapter placement
watchFor.body: Use the stamped triangles to identify the lifting points. Incorrect locations can allow the vehicle to shift or fall; misplaced adapters can also damage suspension parts or obstruct the stabilizer brackets you need to remove.

watchFor.title: Lubricant on the stabilizer bar or bushings
watchFor.body: Do not apply grease, anti-seize or other lubrication to these parts. It can damage the bushings. Water on the bracket is the permitted fitting aid.

watchFor.title: A slit turned away from the front
watchFor.body: Check both bushing seams before fitting the brackets. Each slit must face the front of the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Discarded bolts finding their way back
watchFor.body: Both brackets require new bolts: two per side, four total. Tighten each to 52 lb.ft (70 Nm).

watchFor.title: Wheel anti-seize spreading beyond the pilot
watchFor.body: If wheels were removed, confine XL-2 to a thin film at the pilot-bore/hub-pilot interface. The flat mounting faces, threads and brake friction surfaces must remain free of it.

notes: This procedure applies to the listed 2015 Mustang 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L applications.

Removing a wheel as an assembly does not require tire removal or balancing. If separate tire service is undertaken on carbon-fiber or alloy wheels, use a center-clamp tire changer such as Hunter Auto 34, Revolution, TC3900 or equivalent. Do not use a table-top machine that grips the wheel inside and rides on its front flange. A wheel balancer must not contact the wheel face; Hunter Road Force Touch GSP9700 is an example.

diagnostics.finding: A replacement bushing’s slit does not face the front of the car.
diagnostics.meaning: The bushing is incorrectly oriented for installation.
diagnostics.next: Reorient the bushing so its slit faces forward before fitting the bracket and completing bolt tightening.

diagnostics.finding: Only the removed bracket bolts are ready for reassembly.
diagnostics.meaning: The required replacement hardware is missing.
diagnostics.next: Obtain four new bracket bolts before completing installation. Discard the old bolts.

diagnostics.finding: A wheel nut is seized during optional wheel removal.
diagnostics.meaning: The optional access step cannot proceed normally.
diagnostics.next: Do not apply heat. Stop that removal branch and obtain an appropriate release method before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: Dirt, corrosion or an interfering rotor fastener prevents a removed wheel from sitting against its mounting face.
diagnostics.meaning: The wheel cannot make the required clean mounting contact, which risks loosening in service.
diagnostics.next: Remove contamination and make sure rotor-to-hub fasteners are secured clear of the contact faces before fitting the wheel.

verification.title: Both bushings and brackets complete
verification.body: Confirm both bushings are installed at their bracket locations, both slits face the front of the vehicle and both brackets are fitted.

verification.title: Replacement hardware torqued
verification.body: Confirm four new bracket bolts were installed and each was tightened to 52 lb.ft (70 Nm).

verification.title: Optional wheel work complete
verification.body: For every wheel removed, confirm clean mounting faces and pilot bore, XL-2 confined to the pilot interface, and final nut tightening to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) in a star pattern with the vehicle resting on its tires.

verification.title: Wheel-nut follow-up arranged
verification.body: If a wheel was reinstalled, retighten its nuts within 160 km (100 mi).

procedures.purpose: Replace both rear stabilizer bar bushings, orient the slits forward, renew the bracket bolts and tighten them to specification.
Explain the stabilizer bar and links’ role in controlling rear suspension lean and sway.
Identify lifting points and position lifting equipment without endangering the vehicle or damaging underbody components.
Cover optional wheel removal and installation, pilot-bore cleaning and lubrication, wheel-nut torque and sequence, and the subsequent retightening requirement.

applicability.equipment: 2015 Mustang with rear stabilizer bar; 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.

stepGroups.title: Lift and reach the brackets
stepGroups.summary: Position the vehicle safely, decide whether to remove wheels and identify both bushing brackets.

stepGroups.title: Remove brackets and bushings
stepGroups.summary: Discard the four bracket bolts, retain the brackets and remove both split bushings.

stepGroups.title: Fit and secure the replacements
stepGroups.summary: Install dry bushings facing forward, fit the brackets with new bolts and verify the assembly.

stepGroups.title: Refit optional wheels and finish
stepGroups.summary: Complete wheel preparation and tightening if needed, lower the car and arrange the wheel-nut recheck.

guides.title: Replace a rear stabilizer bar link
guides.summary: Reach the rear stabilizer link, hold its ball studs while removing the two nuts, and install the replacement with new nuts tightened to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). Includes optional wheel removal and refitting.
guides.introduction: Two nuts ought to make a short job. Give them a low-friction ball joint to spin, though, and suddenly the hardware wants to be a tiny merry-go-round. I’ll walk you through holding the studs, replacing the link and putting everything back securely. This guide applies to the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
guides.why: The rear stabilizer bar and its links help control how much the body leans or sways as the suspension moves. Each link transfers movement between the suspension and the bar, while its ball joints allow the connection to change angle. Those joints turn easily by design, so controlled hand-tool work matters: power tools can damage both the joints and their protective boots.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang rear stabilizer bar link replacement

when.summary: Use this procedure when a rear stabilizer bar link has already been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Body lean or sway alone does not establish that a link is defective.
Wheel removal is an optional way to improve access. If both link attachments are safely accessible with the wheel installed, skip the wheel removal and refitting actions.

prepare.title: Establish the repair before taking it apart
prepare.detail: This is a replacement procedure. It provides no measured joint-play limit or diagnostic test for deciding whether a link is faulty; have that decision established before starting.

prepare.title: Have the link and two new nuts ready
prepare.detail: Obtain the correct replacement rear stabilizer bar link and two new attaching nuts for the link being replaced. Both removed nuts must be discarded.

prepare.title: Arrange hand tools and controlled tightening
prepare.detail: Have hand tools that fit the link nuts, a tool matching the ball studs’ hex-holding feature, and a torque wrench suitable for 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). For wheel removal, also have suitable wheel-nut tools and a torque wrench capable of 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). Keep power tools away from the link nuts throughout removal and installation.

prepare.title: Provide safe lifting equipment
prepare.detail: Use a suitable workshop hoist and identify the triangle-marked lifting points before raising the car. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; floor stands are required when a jack is used. The vehicle’s emergency jack is intended only for changing a deflated tire and must not be used to lift the car for this repair.

prepare.title: Prepare for wheel refitting if removing it
prepare.detail: Have cleaning materials and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 ready. The lubricant belongs only at the wheel’s central locating bore and matching hub pilot. Wheel studs, wheel-nut threads and flat mounting faces must remain clean and dry.

steps.title: Position the car and identify the lifting points
steps.body:
Before lifting, use a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Confirm the jack or hoist is rated for the vehicle, including cargo and modifications. If using a jack, support the vehicle on suitable stands at the designated points before going underneath; a jack alone is not a support. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on the hoist. Locate the triangles stamped into the body or frame that identify the correct lifting points; the lifting illustration shows points along both sides near the front and rear wheel areas. Use those markings on the car to locate the points accurately.

Before driving onto a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance. For a two-column hoist, position the adapters and lifting arms so they clear suspension parts, mounting brackets, stabilizer mounting brackets, exhaust and steering linkage, and cannot damage the axle or rear cover. Never apply lifting pressure to either bumper. See [Jacking and Lifting - Overview](#/document/G1663631).

steps.title: Raise and securely support the vehicle
steps.body:
Raise the car using the correctly positioned lifting equipment. Confirm that it is securely supported before reaching into the rear suspension area. Incorrect lifting locations can allow the vehicle to shift or fall.

If using a workshop jack, support the vehicle on floor stands before working underneath it. A jack alone is not a safe support.

steps.title: Remove the wheel if needed for access
steps.body:
If wheel-off access will help you reach both link nuts, remove the five wheel nuts and take off the rear wheel on the side being repaired. Keep the tire mounted on the wheel; tire removal is unnecessary for this job.

Do not heat a seized wheel nut: heat can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. If a nut will not release, resolve that problem without heat before continuing with wheel removal. The wheel handling and refitting procedure is [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Identify the link and its two attachments
steps.body:
Find the short, roughly upright link beside the rear shock absorber, with the coil spring behind it. Its upper end connects to the stabilizer bar and its lower end attaches at the suspension bracket shown beside the shock. Identify the nut and ball-stud hex-holding feature at each end before loosening anything.

The two link nuts are the fasteners involved in this replacement. Leave the spring, shock absorber and surrounding lines in place. The [Rear Suspension - Overview](#/document/G1686641) explains the bar and links’ role in controlling lean and sway.

steps.title: Hold the studs, remove both nuts and take out the link
steps.body:
At one attachment, engage the ball stud’s hex-holding feature to prevent the stud from rotating. Use a hand tool to undo the nut while maintaining that hold. Repeat at the other attachment, supporting the link as its final nut comes off, then withdraw the link from its two mounting points.

Discard both nuts immediately. Do not use power tools to remove them: the ball joints and boots can be damaged. A stud that turns easily is consistent with the joint’s low-friction design; it is your cue to use the holding feature, not a verdict that the joint has failed. See [Rear Stabilizer Bar Link](#/document/G1686653).

steps.title: Position the replacement and tighten two new nuts
steps.body:
Place the replacement link into the same two attachment points, reversing the removal actions. Install a new nut at each end and start both by hand.

Use hand tools, controlling stud rotation through the hex-holding feature as needed. Tighten each of the two link nuts to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm) with a torque wrench. Power tools must not be used for installation either. This is where patience earns its keep; spinning the whole joint adds entertainment, not progress.

steps.title: Check the completed link installation
steps.body:
Before closing up the area, confirm that the replacement link occupies both original mounting points, both nuts are new, and each has received the specified torque. Look at both protective joint boots for damage caused during tool handling.

These are assembly checks, not a new test of joint condition. If a boot was damaged during the work, resolve that damage before considering the installation complete. If the wheel stayed installed, skip the wheel-refitting steps.

steps.title: Clean the wheel mounting faces and central bore
steps.body:
If you removed the wheel, clean corrosion, dirt and other foreign material from its flat mounting face and from the corresponding hub and brake-disc mounting surfaces. Check that any fasteners securing the brake disc to the hub are secure and do not stand in the way of the wheel seating flat.

Also clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the round opening that locates the wheel on the raised hub pilot—and the matching pilot interface. The central bore needs cleaning as well as the flat face.

Contamination trapped between the mounting faces can allow the wheel nuts to loosen and the wheel to come off while driving, with a risk of loss of control and serious injury or death.

steps.title: Apply a thin film only at the locating interface
steps.body:
Apply a thin coat of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 only where the wheel pilot bore meets the hub pilot.

Keep it off the flat wheel-to-brake-disc or drum mounting surfaces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and brake-disc friction surfaces. Clean away any misplaced lubricant before fitting the wheel. I keep this application small and deliberate: the center locator gets the film, and the rest stays clean.

steps.title: Refit the wheel and start all five nuts
steps.body:
Position the wheel on the hub, making sure it seats against the cleaned mounting surface. Install all five wheel nuts and tighten them only finger tight at this stage.

Keep the wheel-stud and wheel-nut threads clean and dry. The final torque value depends on that condition.

steps.title: Lower onto the tires and torque in a star pattern
steps.body:
Before lowering, make sure the parking brake is applied. Restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground, and keep the vehicle restrained for final wheel-nut tightening. Do not lower an unrestrained vehicle in Neutral.

Lower the vehicle so it rests on its tires before final wheel-nut tightening. Tighten all five wheel nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) in a star/cross pattern.

Viewed from outside the wheel as in the tightening illustration, the sequence is: top nut, lower-left nut, upper-right nut, upper-left nut, then lower-right nut. Move across the wheel between nuts rather than working around the circle.

The crossing sequence helps prevent brake-disc runout—side-to-side wobble as the disc rotates—which can accelerate brake roughness, shudder and vibration.

steps.title: Finish the job and arrange the wheel-nut recheck
steps.body:
Confirm that tools and removed hardware are clear of the work area and that the car is fully lowered before use.

If the wheel was removed, arrange to retighten its nuts within 160 km (100 mi) of reinstallation, using the same 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) torque and star pattern. Wheels can loosen after initial tightening; this follow-up is part of completing the wheel work.

watchFor.title: Power tools can damage the link
watchFor.body: Use hand tools for both removal and installation of the link nuts. Protect the ball joints and boots while engaging the stud-holding feature.

watchFor.title: The car must be supported at the correct points
watchFor.body: Find the stamped triangles before lifting. Never work underneath a car resting only on a jack, and do not use the emergency tire-changing jack for this repair.

watchFor.title: Wheel lubricant has a very small permitted area
watchFor.body: XL-2 belongs only at the pilot-bore-to-hub-pilot interface. Flat mounting faces, threaded wheel hardware and braking surfaces must stay free of it.

watchFor.title: Wheel torque and link torque are different
watchFor.body: Each link nut takes 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). Wheel nuts take 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), with clean, dry threads and the vehicle resting on its tires.

notes: The ball joints’ low breakaway torque means little force is needed to start them turning. That characteristic alone is not a reason to reject a link.
The wheel-off route adds access work; it does not require disturbing the spring, shock absorber or brake assembly.
The replacement procedure applies to all four listed engines. No separate engine-specific link tightening branch is needed.

diagnostics.finding: A ball stud rotates with its nut during removal.
diagnostics.meaning: The link uses low-friction ball joints, so stud rotation can be a normal handling issue.
diagnostics.next: Engage the stud’s hex-holding feature and continue undoing the nut with a hand tool. Do not switch to a power tool.

diagnostics.finding: The joint moves easily when handled.
diagnostics.meaning: Low breakaway torque is a design characteristic and does not establish that the joint is worn out.
diagnostics.next: Keep the replacement decision tied to the diagnosis established before this procedure.

diagnostics.finding: Dirt or corrosion remains between the wheel and its mounting surface.
diagnostics.meaning: The wheel may not seat securely, creating a risk that its nuts will loosen in service.
diagnostics.next: Remove the contamination before installing the wheel. Also check for brake-disc retaining hardware that interferes with the mating surfaces.

diagnostics.finding: Anti-seize reaches wheel threads, flat mounting faces or braking surfaces.
diagnostics.meaning: The lubricant is outside its permitted pilot-interface location, and the wheel torque specification requires clean, dry threads.
diagnostics.next: Remove the misplaced lubricant before refitting and tightening the wheel.

diagnostics.finding: A joint boot is damaged during removal or installation.
diagnostics.meaning: The protective boot has been compromised during the work.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the damaged component before completing the repair; tightening the nuts does not correct boot damage.

verification.title: Both link attachments are complete
verification.body: Confirm that the link is installed at both original attachment points, both attaching nuts are new, and each is tightened to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). Check the boots for tool damage.

verification.title: Any removed wheel is correctly refitted
verification.body: Confirm clean mounting faces and pilot bore, a thin XL-2 film confined to the pilot interface, and clean, dry wheel threads. All five nuts must be tightened in a star pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) with the vehicle resting on its tires.

verification.title: The follow-up is recorded
verification.body: If a wheel was reinstalled, record the need to retighten its nuts within 160 km (100 mi). These checks confirm assembly completion; they do not establish the cause of any remaining suspension complaint.

stepGroups.summary: Support the car, remove the wheel if useful and identify both link attachments.

stepGroups.title: Replace the link
stepGroups.summary: Hold the studs, discard the old nuts and torque the replacement hardware.

guides.title: Remove and replace the rear stabilizer bar
guides.summary: Remove the right rear wheel, disconnect both upper stabilizer links, and remove the bar and its brackets. Reassemble with four new bracket bolts and two new link nuts, then clean, refit and correctly torque the wheel.
guides.introduction: The rear stabilizer bar helps keep your Mustang’s cornering enthusiasm from turning into excessive body lean. It has a simple job, but its link nuts can turn that simplicity into a spinning-stud circus. I’ll walk you through holding those studs, releasing the bar and putting everything back with fresh hardware—including the wheel-fitting details that deserve just as much attention as the suspension bolts.
guides.why: The independent rear suspension lets each rear wheel react to road imperfections. The stabilizer bar and its links help control lean and sway between the two sides. Removing the bar means disconnecting both upper link joints and releasing its two mounting brackets. The links use low-friction ball joints, so their studs need to be held during nut removal and installation; power tools can damage the joints and their protective boots.
searchTerms: rear stabilizer link upper nut torque

when.summary: Use this procedure when an established repair requires rear stabilizer bar removal or replacement.
notes: The procedure applies to all four listed engine configurations.
Only the right rear wheel is removed for the specified access, but the upper stabilizer link connection must be released on both sides.

prepare.title: Establish the repair before dismantling
prepare.detail: Start with a confirmed reason to remove or replace the bar. This replacement procedure does not provide a test for condemning the bar or its links; unexplained handling concerns need diagnosis before parts are chosen.

prepare.title: Arrange safe lifting
prepare.detail: Plan to position the vehicle on a suitable hoist with the transmission in Neutral. Identify the triangle-marked lifting locations before raising it. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; floor stands are required when using jack support. The vehicle’s emergency tire-changing jack must not be used to lift it for this repair. Review the [lifting locations and precautions](#/document/G1663631).

prepare.title: Have replacement hardware ready
prepare.detail: Obtain four new stabilizer bar bracket bolts and two new upper stabilizer link nuts, plus the correct replacement bar if replacing it. Suspension fasteners are critical parts: use the same or equivalent quality and design, never lesser-quality or substitute-design hardware. All six removed suspension fasteners are discarded.

prepare.title: Gather hand tools, torque tools and cleaning materials
prepare.detail: Have hand tools that fit the link nuts and the ball studs’ hex-holding features, suitable torque-wrench arrangements for 52 lb.ft (70 Nm), 85 lb.ft (115 Nm) and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), and materials for cleaning the wheel and hub mating surfaces. Have Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, ready for the wheel’s central locating interface. Do not use power tools on the stabilizer link nuts.

steps.title: Locate the lifting points and raise the vehicle
steps.body:
Before lifting, use a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Confirm the jack or hoist is rated for the vehicle, including cargo and modifications. If using a jack, support the vehicle on suitable stands at the designated points before going underneath; a jack alone is not a support. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

Locate the triangles stamped into the body or frame at the designated lifting points. The lifting illustration shows a front and rear location along each side; use the actual stamped marks to identify them on the car.

With the transmission in Neutral, position the vehicle on the hoist. Place the adapters so they do not load or interfere with the suspension, exhaust, steering linkage, suspension mounting brackets or stabilizer brackets. On a two-column hoist, also keep the lifting arms clear of the axle and rear cover. Do not lift against either bumper. If using a drive-on lift, check for underbody interference before driving onto it.

Raise the vehicle using the correct locations and secure support. Incorrect lifting can let the vehicle shift or fall. Never go underneath while it is supported only by a jack. The [Jacking and Lifting overview](#/document/G1663631) provides the location reference.

steps.title: Remove the right rear wheel and tire
steps.body:
Remove the five right rear wheel nuts, then remove the wheel and tire assembly to open access to the rear suspension. Do not use heat on a seized wheel nut: it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. If a nut will not release, stop this removal sequence and have the seized fastening addressed before continuing.

Set the wheel aside for refitting. The [Wheel and Tire procedure](#/document/G1686507) covers this access operation; its cleaning and tightening requirements are included below.

steps.title: Identify both upper link connections and the two bar brackets
steps.body:
Find the bent stabilizer bar running across the rear underside. It is held by two brackets, with two bracket bolts on each side—four bolts altogether. The surrounding exhaust pipes help orient you, but they are not lifting or support points.

At each end, identify the slender stabilizer link and its upper connection to the bar. The close-up shows this connection beside the rear brake, shock absorber and coil spring. I’d identify both sides before undoing either; the left-hand connection still needs attention even though only the right wheel has come off. The [rear stabilizer bar procedure](#/document/G1686651) shows these attachments.

steps.title: Disconnect the upper stabilizer link joint on both sides
steps.body:
Use the hex-holding feature on the first link’s ball stud to prevent it from rotating while you undo the upper nut with hand tools. Remove and discard the nut, disengage the upper connection and move the link aside. Leave its lower connection attached.

Repeat on the other side, discarding that upper nut as well. Both links must be clear before the bar is removed.

Do not use power tools for either removal or installation of these nuts. The joints are designed to move with little initial resistance, so a stud turning with its nut is not, by itself, proof of failure. Hold the hex instead of inviting an impact wrench to make a damn nuisance worse.

steps.title: Remove the brackets and stabilizer bar
steps.body:
Keep the bar controlled while removing the four bracket bolts, two at each bracket. Discard all four bolts.

Remove the two brackets, then remove the stabilizer bar from its installed position, keeping it clear of the surrounding suspension and exhaust. Retain the brackets for reassembly. At this point both upper links are positioned aside and both bar mounts are released.

steps.title: Position the bar and tighten four new bracket bolts
steps.body:
Position the stabilizer bar and both mounting brackets in their installed locations. Install four new bracket bolts, two per bracket.

Tighten each bracket bolt to 52 lb.ft (70 Nm). Secure these bar mounts before reconnecting the links. Use the correct-quality replacement fasteners; this is no place for the miscellaneous-bolt tin.

steps.title: Reconnect both links with new upper nuts
steps.body:
Move each link back into position and engage its upper connection with the stabilizer bar. Install a new upper nut on each side.

Hold each ball stud using its hex-holding feature while tightening the nut to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). Use hand tools and a suitable torque-wrench arrangement; do not use power tools. Complete both sides before turning to the wheel.

steps.title: Clean the wheel and hub mounting faces
steps.body:
Before installing the right rear wheel, remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel’s flat mounting face and the corresponding hub/brake-disc mounting face. Check that any fasteners retaining the brake disc to the hub are secured and do not stand in the way of those mating faces.

These surfaces must allow the wheel to seat fully. Trapped material or an interfering fastener can let the wheel nuts loosen in service, potentially allowing the wheel to come off and causing loss of control.

steps.title: Clean the central pilot bore and apply a thin lubricant film
steps.body:
Clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the hole that locates over the raised center of the hub—as well as preparing the flat mounting face. The cleaning step includes this bore; do not simply wipe the broad face and call it done.

Apply a thin coat of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, only at the interface between that pilot bore and the hub pilot. Keep it off the flat wheel-to-brake-disc mounting surface, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and brake-disc friction surfaces. The wheel stud and nut threads must remain clean and dry for the specified tightening torque.

steps.title: Refit the wheel and finger-tighten its five nuts
steps.body:
Position the right rear wheel on the hub and install all five wheel nuts. At this stage tighten them only finger tight.

Make sure the wheel is seated against the cleaned mating face before proceeding to final tightening.

steps.title: Lower onto the tires and torque the wheel nuts in a star pattern
steps.body:
Before lowering, make sure the parking brake is applied. Restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground, and keep the vehicle restrained for final wheel-nut tightening. Do not lower an unrestrained vehicle in Neutral.

Lower the vehicle so it rests on its tires before final wheel-nut tightening.

Tighten all five nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), using a star/cross pattern. With one nut at the top as shown in the wheel illustration, the sequence is: top, lower left, upper right, upper left, lower right. Follow that crossing sequence around the actual wheel rather than tightening adjacent nuts in a circle.

The torque applies to clean, dry stud and nut threads. The crossing sequence helps prevent brake-disc runout—uneven sideways movement as the disc rotates—which can contribute to brake roughness, shudder and vibration.

steps.title: Check the completed assembly and arrange the wheel-nut recheck
steps.body:
Account for four new bracket bolts tightened to 52 lb.ft (70 Nm), two new upper link nuts tightened to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm), and five right rear wheel nuts tightened to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). Confirm that both links are reconnected and neither remains positioned aside.

Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after wheel installation, using the same torque and star pattern with the vehicle resting on its tires. Wheels can loosen after initial tightening; this follow-up is part of completing the job.

watchFor.title: Link joint and boot damage from power tools
watchFor.body: Do not use power tools on the upper link nuts in either direction. Hold the ball stud by its hex feature while working the nut with hand tools.

watchFor.title: Reusing discarded suspension hardware
watchFor.body: Both upper link nuts and all four bracket bolts require replacement. Correct torque does not make the discarded hardware suitable for reuse.

watchFor.title: Unsafe lifting or obstructed hoist adapters
watchFor.body: Use the triangle-marked lifting locations. Keep adapters and lifting arms clear of components and brackets, and never work beneath jack-only support. Lifting at an incorrect location can cause the vehicle to shift or fall.

watchFor.title: Lubricant reaching the wrong wheel surfaces
watchFor.body: XL-2 belongs only at the pilot bore-to-hub pilot interface. Keep flat mating faces, wheel fasteners and braking surfaces free of it.

watchFor.title: Wheel seating and final tightening
watchFor.body: Clean both mating faces, check for interfering disc-retaining fasteners, and perform final tightening on the tires in a star pattern. Incorrect wheel installation can allow the wheel to loosen or detach.

notes: The bar and links control rear suspension lean and sway; the springs and shock absorbers control vertical movement. See the [Rear Suspension overview](#/document/G1686641) for that component context.

No tire demounting or balancing is needed for this bar replacement. If separate tire work is undertaken on carbon-fiber or alloy wheels, use a center-clamp tire changer, such as Hunter Auto 34, Revolution, TC3900 or equivalent, and a balancer that does not contact the wheel face, such as Hunter Road Force Touch GSP9700. Tabletop changers that grip inside the wheel and ride on its front flange, and balancers contacting the wheel face, can damage the wheel.

diagnostics.finding: A link ball stud turns as its upper nut is loosened or tightened.
diagnostics.meaning: The link ball joints have low breakaway torque, meaning little force is needed to start them moving. Stud rotation alone does not establish a failed joint.
diagnostics.next: Hold the stud with its hex-holding feature and work the nut using hand tools. During assembly, use a new nut and tighten it to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm).

diagnostics.finding: A right rear wheel nut is seized.
diagnostics.meaning: Normal wheel removal cannot be completed, so access to the bar is interrupted.
diagnostics.next: Do not apply heat. Stop wheel removal and arrange appropriate seized-fastener repair before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: Corrosion, dirt or foreign material remains on a wheel or hub/brake-disc mating face.
diagnostics.meaning: The wheel may not seat securely, creating a risk of the nuts loosening after installation.
diagnostics.next: Remove the contamination before refitting the wheel. Also clean the central pilot bore before applying the thin XL-2 film at its locating interface.

diagnostics.finding: A brake-disc retaining fastener interferes with the wheel mounting face.
diagnostics.meaning: The wheel cannot sit properly against its mating surface.
diagnostics.next: Make sure the retaining fastener is secured and no longer interferes before installing the wheel.

verification.title: Bar and brackets secured
verification.body: Confirm the bar and both brackets are installed with four new bracket bolts, each tightened to 52 lb.ft (70 Nm).

verification.title: Both links restored
verification.body: Confirm both upper connections are engaged and secured with new nuts tightened to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm), with each stud held by its hex feature during tightening.

verification.title: Wheel installation complete
verification.body: Confirm the mating faces and pilot bore were cleaned, XL-2 was confined to the pilot interface, and all five wheel nuts were tightened to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) in a star pattern with the vehicle resting on its tires.

verification.title: Follow-up tightening scheduled
verification.body: Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) of installation. These assembly checks confirm completion of the replacement; they do not establish the cause of any pre-existing handling concern.

guides.title: Replace a rear coil spring
guides.summary: Remove the rear lower arm to release the spring safely, inspect its seats, and restore the suspension with new fasteners and required checks.
guides.introduction: The rear coil spring supports the vehicle through the lower arm and works with the shock absorber to control vertical movement. Replacing it involves the lower arm, several suspension connections and exhaust clearance. Correct spring seating and tightening at normal suspension height are central to the repair.
guides.why: A compressed spring stores substantial energy. Controlled support prevents sudden release, while tightening suspension bushings under load avoids incorrect clamp load and bushing damage.

when.summary: When a rear spring requires replacement or spring removal is needed to address a damaged upper seat.
notes: Dynamic suspension adds ride-height sensor handling and scan-tool calibration.

prepare.title: Support and access
prepare.detail: Arrange safe vehicle support, vehicle/axle stands, suitable knuckle retaining straps and torque tools. The muffler and tailpipe must be removed for rearward lower-arm bolt clearance.

prepare.title: Replacement hardware
prepare.detail: Obtain new lower shock bolts, vertical-link lower bolt, stabilizer-link lower nut, arm-to-knuckle bolt and both arm-to-frame bolts. Replacement suspension fasteners must be the same or equivalent quality and design.

prepare.title: Completion capability
prepare.detail: Provide rear-camber checking and adjustment capability. Vehicles with dynamic suspension also require a scan tool for Ride Height Calibration.

steps.title: Support the suspension
steps.body: Remove the wheel and tire, then support and raise the suspension approximately 20mm from rebound as directed in Lower Arm. Maintain control of the arm throughout release of spring compression.

steps.title: Disconnect the outer attachments
steps.body: Remove and discard the lower shock bolts. If dynamic suspension is fitted, move the ride-height sensor bracket aside. Disconnect the vertical link, support the knuckle with straps, then disconnect the stabilizer link and arm-to-knuckle connection, discarding their specified fasteners.

steps.title: Clear the arm and release the spring
steps.body: Remove the muffler and tailpipe using the applicable engine procedure, then remove and discard the forward arm-to-frame bolt. Carefully lower the supported suspension to release spring compression. Retain the spring so it cannot fall, remove it, then discard the rearward arm bolt and remove the arm.

steps.title: Inspect and position the seats
steps.body: Inspect the upper spring seat and replace it if damaged. Inspect the lower seat and confirm its alignment in the arm. Hold the spring in position as the supported arm is raised, ensuring the upper seat sits correctly on its mount and the coil locates in both seats.

steps.title: Reconnect with new hardware
steps.body: Install the rearward and forward arm bolts finger-tight, then restore the exhaust. Reconnect the knuckle, stabilizer link and vertical link with new fasteners, initially finger-tight. Refit the dynamic-suspension sensor bracket where applicable and install new lower shock bolts, tightening these attachments as specified.

steps.title: Tighten at the required height
steps.body: Support the suspension at curb height. Follow Lower Arm's final tightening sequence for the rearward arm bolt, knuckle bolt, forward arm bolt and vertical-link bolt. Tighten the stabilizer-link lower nut to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm), using its hex-holding feature to prevent stud rotation. Do not use power tools on link nuts.

steps.title: Complete alignment and calibration
steps.body: Reinstall the wheel and tire. Check rear camber and adjust if necessary. With dynamic suspension, connect the scan tool and complete Ride Height Calibration according to its directions.

watchFor.title: Spring slipping from its seat
watchFor.body: Hold the spring during arm installation and recheck its location before loading the suspension.

watchFor.title: Stabilizer-link damage
watchFor.body: Its low-friction ball joint may turn during nut removal or installation. Use the hex-holding feature; power tools can damage the joint and boot.

notes: The spring-release method is part of lower-arm removal; follow that complete sequence for support and fastener locations.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical completion
verification.body: Verify upper and lower spring seating, replacement of discarded hardware, and final tightening with the suspension supported at the specified height.

verification.title: Record geometry and calibration
verification.body: Record the rear-camber check and any adjustment. For dynamic suspension, record successful completion of Ride Height Calibration.

guides.title: Replace a rear toe link and recheck wheel alignment
guides.summary: Replace the rear toe link with new mounting hardware, tighten it at loaded suspension height and recheck rear toe.
guides.introduction: The toe link helps control the direction a rear wheel points when viewed from above. It connects the rear suspension frame to the wheel knuckle within the independent rear suspension. Removing the link disturbs both a structural attachment and an alignment setting. A complete replacement therefore includes preserving the adjustment references, renewing the specified hardware and measuring rear toe afterward.
guides.why: The cam-wheel marks provide a useful starting position during assembly, but they do not prove the final wheel alignment is correct. Suspension loading also matters: tightening the bushing fasteners with the suspension hanging can produce incorrect clamp load and damage the bushings. These requirements make the job more than a simple exchange of one link for another.

when.summary: When a rear toe link requires replacement and rear toe can be checked after installation.
notes: Arrange the alignment check as part of the repair.

prepare.title: Support the suspension at its working height
prepare.detail: Have suitable vehicle and suspension support so the wheel can be removed while the suspension is supported at curb height.

prepare.title: Provide new mounting hardware
prepare.detail: Obtain new toe link-to-frame and toe link-to-knuckle bolts and nuts. Use the same or equivalent quality and design; these suspension fasteners are critical parts.

prepare.title: Prepare marking, torque and alignment equipment
prepare.detail: Have a means of marking both cam wheels, torque equipment for the specified fasteners and the capability to measure and adjust rear toe.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and support the suspension
steps.body: Follow the Wheel and Tire procedure, then support the suspension at curb height. Establish this support before disturbing the toe link so the work follows the required suspension position.

steps.title: Mark both cam wheels
steps.body: Index-mark the inner and outer cam wheels shown in the toe-link procedure. Make the references clear enough to align during assembly before loosening the mounting hardware.

steps.title: Remove the link and discard its fasteners
steps.body: Remove the toe link-to-knuckle bolt and nut and the toe link-to-frame bolt and nut. Discard both sets of fasteners and remove the toe link.

steps.title: Install with the suspension loaded
steps.body: Position the toe link and align the removal reference marks. Install the new frame-side bolt and nut, followed by the new knuckle-side bolt and nut. Tighten each connection to 129 lb.ft (175 Nm), with the suspension loaded or the vehicle's weight resting on its wheels and tires.

steps.title: Restore the wheel and measure rear toe
steps.body: Install the wheel and tire through the linked procedure. Recheck rear toe and adjust as necessary using Rear Toe Adjustment in section 204-00, referenced by the toe-link procedure. Returning the cam marks to their earlier positions does not replace this measurement.

watchFor.title: Tightening at full suspension droop
watchFor.body: Do not finish tightening the bushing fasteners with the suspension hanging. The specified loaded condition protects clamp load and bushing condition.

watchFor.title: Hardware substitutions
watchFor.body: Do not reuse the discarded bolts and nuts or substitute fasteners of lesser quality or a different design.

notes: The rear suspension allows the wheels to move independently; the toe link's alignment role is distinct from the spring and shock absorber's control of vertical movement.

diagnostics.finding: Rear toe needs correction after the link is installed.
diagnostics.meaning: The reference marks provided an assembly position, but the measured alignment still requires adjustment.
diagnostics.next: Complete the rear toe adjustment using the applicable alignment specification.

verification.title: Confirm fastening conditions
verification.body: Check that both mounting connections received new hardware and were tightened with the suspension in the required loaded condition.

verification.title: Record the alignment result
verification.body: Record the final measured rear toe and any adjustment made against the applicable specification.

procedures.purpose: Rear toe link removal and installation, cam reference marks, new hardware, loaded tightening and rear toe recheck.
Wheel and tire removal and installation for toe-link access.

guides.title: Replace a rear suspension upper arm
guides.summary: Replace the rear upper arm with new attachment hardware, tighten it with the suspension loaded, and check rear camber.
guides.introduction: The rear upper arm connects the chassis to the wheel knuckle and works with the lower arm to locate the wheel as the suspension moves. Each rear wheel can respond independently to road irregularities. Replacing the upper arm disturbs these locating attachments, so the job includes controlled suspension support and a rear camber check.
guides.why: The bushings must be secured with the suspension loaded or the vehicle resting on its wheels. Tightening with the suspension hanging can produce incorrect clamp load and damage the bushings. Both attachment bolt-and-nut sets are discarded during removal, and their replacements must meet the specified quality and tightening requirements.

when.summary: When rear upper-arm replacement is required and loaded tightening plus a rear camber check can be completed.
notes: Have access to the Rear Camber Adjustment procedure in section 204-00 before beginning.

prepare.title: Provide controlled suspension support
prepare.detail: Have suitable vehicle lifting equipment, support for holding the suspension at curb height, and a torque wrench. Follow the wheel-and-tire procedure for access.

prepare.title: Obtain the required hardware
prepare.detail: Prepare a new upper-arm-to-knuckle bolt and nut and a new upper-arm-to-frame flag-bolt and nut. Use the same or equivalent quality and design, never a lesser substitute.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and support the suspension
steps.body: Follow [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507) to remove the wheel. Support the suspension at curb height before disturbing the upper-arm attachments.

steps.title: Remove the upper arm
steps.body: Follow [Upper Arm removal](#/document/G1686656). Remove and discard the upper-arm-to-wheel-knuckle bolt and nut first. Then remove and discard the frame flag-bolt and nut and remove the arm.

steps.title: Install with new fasteners
steps.body: Reverse removal using new attachment hardware. Tighten the bushing fasteners only with the suspension loaded or vehicle weight on the wheels. The knuckle attachment requires 76 lb.ft (103 Nm); the frame attachment requires 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). Keep these two specifications associated with their respective joints.

steps.title: Restore the wheel and check camber
steps.body: Complete wheel installation through its procedure. Check rear camber and adjust if necessary using Rear Camber Adjustment, section 204-00. This establishes whether wheel inclination needs correction after the arm has been replaced.

watchFor.title: Tightening at full droop
watchFor.body: Do not perform final bushing-fastener tightening with the suspension hanging unloaded.

watchFor.title: Old hardware returning to service
watchFor.body: Both removed bolt-and-nut sets must be discarded, including the frame flag-bolt.

notes: Curb-height support is a required working condition, not an instruction to estimate an arbitrary suspension position.

diagnostics.finding: Rear camber requires correction after installation.
diagnostics.meaning: Replacing the arm has not completed the wheel-alignment requirement.
diagnostics.next: Carry out the specified rear camber adjustment.

verification.title: Confirm attachment conditions
verification.body: Confirm new hardware was used and both attachments received their specified torque with the suspension loaded.

verification.title: Record the camber result
verification.body: Record the rear camber check and whether adjustment was necessary, including the final result if adjusted.

procedures.purpose: Rear upper-arm removal and installation, discarded hardware, loaded bushing tightening and required rear camber check.
Wheel-and-tire removal for rear upper-arm access and installation afterward.

guides.title: Replace the rear wheel bearing and hub
guides.summary: Replace the rear bearing-and-hub assembly using new mounting bolts and a new spindle nut tightened in the prescribed sequence.
guides.introduction: The rear hub carries the wheel, while its bearing lets the wheel rotate within the suspension knuckle. The halfshaft passes through the hub to transmit drive. This job removes the complete bearing-and-hub assembly after separating the halfshaft and removing the rear brake disc; it does not involve dismantling the bearing itself.
guides.why: The hub mounting bolts and spindle nut secure heavily loaded connections. Their replacement and tightening requirements are part of the repair, not optional finishing details. The spindle nut uses a staged tightening sequence that includes loosening, so simply tightening it to a single final torque would not reproduce the specified installation.

when.summary: When replacement of the rear bearing-and-hub assembly has been established as necessary.
notes: Use the rear brake-disc procedure appropriate to the fitted brakes, including the separate SVT Performance Package procedure where applicable.
The replacement procedure does not establish the cause of a wheel or suspension complaint.

prepare.title: Arrange wheel and brake access
prepare.detail: Be equipped to support the vehicle and complete the linked wheel-and-tire and rear brake-disc procedures before starting hub removal.

prepare.title: Have the specified remover and tightening equipment
prepare.detail: Use hub remover 205-D070 (D93P-1175-B) to press the halfshaft from the hub. Have torque and angle-measuring equipment suitable for the prescribed installation sequence.

prepare.title: Obtain replacement fasteners
prepare.detail: Have a new spindle nut and four new bearing-and-hub bolts ready. Suspension fasteners must be the same or equivalent quality and design.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and release the halfshaft
steps.body: Follow the wheel-and-tire procedure. Remove and discard the spindle nut, then use the specified remover to press the halfshaft from the hub. This separates the drive connection before the hub assembly is released.

steps.title: Remove the brake disc
