steps.body: Follow the applicable rear brake-disc procedure. The standard rear disc and SVT Performance Package disc have separate instructions; complete the correct access procedure before reaching the hub mounting bolts.

steps.title: Remove the bearing-and-hub assembly
steps.body: Remove and discard all four mounting bolts, then remove the assembly from the knuckle. The illustration identifies these bolts behind the hub and marks them for disposal.

steps.title: Mount the replacement hub
steps.body: Position the bearing-and-hub assembly and install four new bolts. Tighten them in a cross pattern to 98 lb.ft (133 Nm), then reinstall the brake disc using its applicable procedure.

steps.title: Complete the drive connection and wheel installation
steps.body: Apply the brake to prevent halfshaft rotation and install a new spindle nut. Tighten to 184 lb.ft (250 Nm), loosen 90°, tighten to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm), then tighten a further 30°. Complete every stage in order, then reinstall the wheel and tire.

watchFor.title: Reused retaining hardware
watchFor.body: The removed spindle nut and all four hub bolts are discarded parts. Do not return them to service.

watchFor.title: Incomplete spindle-nut sequence
watchFor.body: The loosening stage is intentional. A torque-only installation omits part of the specified fastening process.

notes: Although the specified tool is named a front wheel hub remover, this rear-hub procedure expressly calls for it.

verification.title: Confirm assembly completion
verification.body: Check that the hub has four new mounting bolts, the correct brake-disc installation is complete, and the wheel-and-tire procedure has been completed.

verification.title: Record the critical tightening
verification.body: Record completion of the cross-pattern hub tightening and every stage of the new spindle-nut sequence.

procedures.purpose: Rear wheel bearing-and-hub removal and installation, including the specified remover, discarded fasteners and staged spindle-nut tightening.
Wheel-and-tire removal for access and installation after hub replacement.
Standard rear brake-disc removal and installation for the listed 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications.
Rear brake-disc removal and installation for the listed 5.2L application with SVT Performance Package.

guides.title: Replace a rear wheel knuckle
guides.summary: Replace the rear wheel knuckle with new attachment fasteners, tighten the suspension at its loaded position and check rear toe.
guides.introduction: The rear wheel knuckle carries the wheel bearing and hub and connects them to the upper arm, lower arm and toe link. These connections locate the wheel while the independent rear suspension moves over the road. Replacing the knuckle requires separating those attachments, supporting the halfshaft and restoring the wheel's alignment afterward.
guides.why: Suspension fasteners carry loads that directly affect wheel control, so their quality and tightening matter. The bushing attachments must be tightened with the suspension loaded: tightening them while the suspension hangs can create incorrect clamp load and damage the bushings. A rear toe check confirms the wheel's direction after the connections have been disturbed.

when.summary: When an identified rear suspension repair requires wheel knuckle removal or replacement.
notes: Plan the job with the separate wheel bearing and hub, lower arm vertical link, and rear toe procedures available.

prepare.title: Provide controlled suspension support
prepare.detail: Arrange access and support that holds the suspension at curb height, plus separate support for the halfshaft. You must be able to maintain the loaded suspension position during bushing-fastener tightening.

prepare.title: Prepare new attachment hardware
prepare.detail: Have new knuckle-to-upper-arm and knuckle-to-toe-link bolts and nuts, and a new knuckle-to-lower-arm bolt. Use the same or equivalent quality and design, with torque equipment suitable for the specified values.

prepare.title: Arrange alignment capability
prepare.detail: Rear toe must be checked and adjusted if necessary after reassembly. Include that capability in the repair plan.

steps.title: Remove the hub and clear attached components
steps.body: Remove the [wheel bearing and hub](#/document/G1686657). Remove the wheel speed sensor bolt and position the sensor aside, then remove the parking brake cable bracket bolt and move the bracket aside.

steps.title: Support the suspension and halfshaft
steps.body: Support the suspension at curb height. Remove the [lower arm vertical link](#/document/G1686649), and support the halfshaft before releasing the knuckle attachments.

steps.title: Release the knuckle
steps.body: Following the [Wheel Knuckle procedure](#/document/G1686658), remove and discard the upper-arm bolt and nut, then the toe-link bolt and nut. Remove and discard the lower-arm bolt and remove the knuckle.

steps.title: Install and tighten the new attachments
steps.body: Position the knuckle and install the new lower-arm bolt, followed by the new toe-link bolt and nut and the new upper-arm bolt and nut. Tighten each to its own specification with the suspension loaded or the vehicle's weight on its wheels.

steps.title: Restore the sensor, cable bracket and hub
steps.body: Refit the parking brake cable bracket and wheel speed sensor, using their individual tightening specifications. Reinstall the lower arm vertical link, then the wheel bearing and hub through their linked procedures.

steps.title: Check rear toe
steps.body: Check rear toe and adjust it if necessary using the Rear Toe Adjustment procedure referenced by the knuckle article. Completing the mechanical assembly alone does not complete this repair.

watchFor.title: Fastener substitution or reuse
watchFor.body: The specified discarded knuckle attachment hardware must be replaced. Lesser-quality or substitute-design suspension fasteners are unsuitable.

watchFor.title: Tightening at full suspension droop
watchFor.body: Keep the required loaded position during bushing-fastener tightening to avoid incorrect clamp load and bushing damage.

notes: Keep the halfshaft supported while the knuckle is disconnected.

verification.title: Confirm the restored attachments
verification.body: Confirm that the specified new knuckle fasteners were used and tightened in the loaded position, and that the sensor and parking brake cable bracket are restored.

verification.title: Record the alignment result
verification.body: Record the rear toe check and any adjustment made, using the applicable alignment specifications.

procedures.purpose: Rear wheel knuckle removal and installation, replacement fasteners, loaded-position tightening and final rear toe check.
Rear wheel bearing and hub removal before knuckle work and installation afterward.
Lower arm vertical link removal and installation during knuckle access.

guides.title: Replace rear wheel studs with the hub removed
guides.summary: Remove the rear bearing and hub assembly, press out the affected stud, inspect the assembly and press in its replacement.
guides.introduction: Rear wheel studs provide the threaded attachment used by the wheel nuts to clamp the wheel to the hub. The studs are retained in the hub itself. This procedure replaces a stud using a hydraulic press after the wheel bearing and hub assembly has been removed from the vehicle.
guides.why: Stud replacement and hub condition are linked. After the old stud is pressed out, the bearing and hub must be inspected for damage; installing another stud does not resolve damage to the assembly that carries it. The job therefore includes a decision about whether the existing bearing and hub remain suitable for use.
searchTerms: press wheel stud out of rear hub

when.summary: When a rear wheel stud requires replacement and the bearing/hub assembly can be removed for press work.
notes: This procedure concerns rear wheel studs.
The required bearing-and-hub inspection determines whether stud replacement alone is sufficient.

prepare.title: Arrange hydraulic press capability
prepare.detail: Use a hydraulic press and the support arrangement shown in the [wheel stud procedure](#/document/G1686659). The operator must be able to position and support the removed assembly correctly.

prepare.title: Plan rear hub removal and installation
prepare.detail: Follow the complete [rear wheel bearing and hub procedure](#/document/G1686657) for vehicle access, support and attachment requirements. Have the capability to complete that work as well as the bench operation.

steps.title: Remove the bearing and hub assembly
steps.body: Complete the linked rear bearing-and-hub removal procedure. The stud work begins with this assembly removed; the illustrated press arrangement is for the removed assembly.

steps.title: Press out the affected stud
steps.body: Position the assembly as illustrated and use the hydraulic press to press the stud out. Follow the shown support and pressing direction without inventing fixture dimensions or a press-force specification.

steps.title: Inspect before proceeding
steps.body: Inspect the wheel bearing and wheel hub for damage. Replace them as necessary. Make this decision after stud removal and before installing the replacement stud.

steps.title: Press in the replacement and reinstall the hub
steps.body: Use the hydraulic press to install the replacement stud in the bearing and hub assembly. Then reinstall the assembly using the separate rear bearing-and-hub procedure.

watchFor.title: Damage to the bearing or hub
watchFor.body: A damaged assembly requires the replacement decision specified by the procedure; a new stud alone is not the completion criterion.

watchFor.title: An unsuitable press setup
watchFor.body: Use the illustrated support arrangement. Correct support is part of performing the specified press operation.

notes: Both stud removal and installation use the hydraulic press.
Complete hub reinstallation through its own procedure rather than inferring fastening details from the stud illustration.

diagnostics.finding: Bearing or hub damage is found after pressing out the stud.
diagnostics.meaning: The repair may require more than replacement of the stud.
diagnostics.next: Replace the bearing and hub as necessary before completing installation.

verification.title: Confirm both phases are complete
verification.body: Confirm the replacement stud has been pressed in and the bearing-and-hub assembly has been reinstalled through its complete procedure.

verification.title: Record the inspection decision
verification.body: Record whether the bearing and hub were retained after inspection or replaced because damage was found.

procedures.purpose: Rear wheel stud hydraulic-press removal, bearing/hub damage inspection and stud installation.
Required rear wheel bearing and hub removal before press work and installation afterward.

guides.title: Diagnose uneven tire wear, wheel shimmy and speed-related vibration
guides.summary: Use tread patterns, wheel inspection and radial-runout measurements to choose the appropriate tire, wheel, suspension or alignment correction.
guides.introduction: Tires carry the vehicle through a contact patch that should wear evenly across the tread and around its circumference. Uneven wear can reveal alignment or maintenance problems. Vibration needs a separate investigation: a wheel-and-tire assembly can be balanced yet vary in roundness or in the force it develops under load.
guides.why: Replacing a worn tire without addressing its cause can reproduce the same pattern. Radial runout is departure from a true circle; loaded Road Force measurement also accounts for the tire's radial stiffness. These checks answer different questions from a visual inspection or an unloaded dial-indicator reading.

when.summary: When tires wear unevenly, wheels wobble or shimmy, or vibration appears with vehicle speed.
notes: Do not begin tire/wheel vibration diagnosis on tires with less than 322 km (200 mi) of service; initial flat spotting may settle.
Visible damage and loose wheel nuts still require attention.

prepare.title: Arrange inspection and measurement equipment
prepare.detail: Use a digital tire-pressure gauge, tread-depth gauge, wheel-nut torque equipment, tire crayon, suitable lifting and wheel-removal capability, and a correctly adapted balancer. Runout testing needs either a Hunter Road Force balancer or a securely mounted dial indicator.

prepare.title: Protect the tires and wheels
prepare.detail: Ask whether tire sealant has been injected; it may be flammable. Carbon-fiber and alloy wheels require a center-clamp tire changer, a balancer that avoids wheel-face contact, and non-spade alignment equipment.

steps.title: Establish the complaint
steps.body: Verify the concern on a smooth road and identify whether it is wear, wobble or speed-related shake. If fitted, disable the Lane Keeping System for noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) testing. Use the [wheel-and-tire diagnostic sequence](#/document/G1686502); if this system is eliminated as the cause, continue broader NVH diagnosis.

steps.title: Inspect fitment, pressure and condition
steps.body: Check pressure against the vehicle label using a digital gauge. Replacement tires must match the recommended size, speed rating, load range and construction; wheel size and offset must match the original specification for those tires. Inspect tread, sidewalls, wheels and valve stems before interpreting a wear pattern.

steps.title: Measure the wear instead of judging by appearance alone
steps.body: Compare tread ribs and shoulders, including leading and trailing lug edges for heel/toe wear and measurements along diagonal patterns. The decisions in Tests A–D depend on whether the worn area remains above 1.6 mm. Follow the corresponding diagnostic entry below; normal wear is even, with no universal mileage expectation.

steps.title: Separate wobble from high-speed shake
steps.body: Test E, for wobble or shimmy, starts with wheel-nut torque. Tighten loose nuts to specification; otherwise inspect for bent wheels or damaged tires. Test F, for high-speed shake or vehicle vibration, begins with that damage inspection. Replace damaged parts and check alignment as directed. Without damage, correct pressure, rotate, inspect and repair suspension faults, and check alignment; Test F then proceeds to radial-runout measurement.

steps.title: Prepare each assembly for runout testing
steps.body: Mark every tire's original vehicle position on its inward sidewall, then remove the assemblies using the Wheel and Tire procedure. Set label pressure, remove foreign material and mount each assembly with the correct adapters. Incorrect mounting can introduce apparent runout or damage the wheel.

steps.title: Use the preferred loaded measurement
steps.body: Measure Road Force and temporarily mark the high spot and value. Above 9 kg (20 lb), continue to the separate Match Mounting procedure to optimize the assembly. At or below that value, permanently mark the high spot and result on the inward sidewall, balance the assembly and install it through Wheel-to-Hub Optimization.

steps.title: Use a dial indicator when appropriate
steps.body: Secure the indicator against the center tread rib; masking tape can smooth its measuring surface. Find the low spot, zero the gauge and rotate one complete revolution to confirm the zero returns. Rotate slowly and steadily, reading the overall maximum-to-minimum movement. Above 1.14 mm (0.045 in), temporarily mark the high spot and result and proceed to Match Mounting. At or below that limit, permanently mark them inward, balance and use Wheel-to-Hub Optimization for installation.

watchFor.title: Damage that changes the repair decision
watchFor.body: Replace wheels that are bent, cracked, dented, heavily corroded, leaking, have elongated hub-bolt holes or excessive runout. Inspect tires for cuts, bruises, abrasions, blisters and embedded objects. Replace damaged valve stems and fit a new stem whenever a new tire or wheel is installed.

watchFor.title: Unsafe powered testing
watchFor.body: Never use the engine to power the driveline unless every driven wheel is elevated clear of the ground.

watchFor.title: Machine and finish protection
watchFor.body: Turn off the balancer inflation station for tires at 60.0 psi (414 kPa) or above. Avoid abrasive wheel cleaners and sharp metal tools for removing adhesive weights; use designated removal tools.

notes: Unloaded dial-indicator runout can guide tire positioning on the wheel, but cannot accurately determine whether a tire should be removed from service.
Match Mounting and Wheel-to-Hub Optimization are separate follow-on procedures. A high measurement directs further optimization, not automatic tire replacement.

diagnostics.finding: The inner shoulder is worn more heavily than the outer shoulder — Test A.
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive toe out or negative camber, rotation history and high-speed cornering are possible contributors.
diagnostics.next: Above 1.6 mm, rotate and adjust toe to nominal +0.15 degrees, toe in, with caster and camber nominal. Otherwise replace the tire and set toe, caster and camber to nominal.

diagnostics.finding: The outer shoulder is worn more heavily than the inner shoulder — Test B.
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive toe in or positive camber, rotation history and high-speed cornering are possible contributors.
diagnostics.next: Above 1.6 mm, rotate and adjust toe to nominal -0.15 degrees, toe out, with caster and camber nominal. Otherwise replace the tire and set toe, caster and camber to nominal.

diagnostics.finding: Shoulder tread lugs have unequal leading and trailing edge heights — Test C.
diagnostics.meaning: This is heel/toe wear, also called feathering; toe error and rotation history are possible causes.
diagnostics.next: Above 1.6 mm, correct pressure, rotate, inspect and repair suspension faults, and check alignment. Otherwise replace the tire and adjust toe, caster and camber to nominal.

diagnostics.finding: Wear crosses the tread diagonally and continues around the tire — Test D.
diagnostics.meaning: Toe error and rotation history can contribute to diagonal wear.
diagnostics.next: The tire may remain in service above 1.6 mm if it causes no noise or vibration. Correct pressure, rotate, inspect and repair suspension faults, and check alignment. At or below the limit, replace the tire as well.

verification.title: Confirm the directed correction
verification.body: Check final pressure, wheel-nut torque and any required alignment correction. Verify whether the original smooth-road complaint remains; continue NVH diagnosis if the wheel-and-tire checks do not identify its cause.

verification.title: Preserve useful measurements
verification.body: Record tread readings, original wheel positions and runout or Road Force results. For assemblies within the applicable limit, retain the specified permanent inward-sidewall high-spot and measurement marks.

procedures.purpose: Preliminary inspection, wear Tests A–D, wobble Test E, vibration Test F, and loaded and dial-indicator runout methods.
Tire-sealant precautions, wheel-safe service equipment and finish protection.
Understanding and distinguishing noise, vibration and harshness symptoms.
Complaint verification, preliminary inspection and disciplined diagnostic decisions.

guides.title: Dismount and refit a tire while protecting the TPMS sensor
guides.summary: Remove the wheel, separate and refit the tire with the correct sensor clearances, renew valve hardware and restore the wheel attachment.
guides.introduction: The tire seals against the wheel at its beads, and the tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) sensor is attached to the valve stem inside the wheel. Tire service therefore involves both an air seal and a concealed electronic component. This guide follows wheel removal, tire disassembly, valve and sensor assembly, tire mounting and final wheel installation.
guides.why: A bead-breaking tool or displaced tire bead can strike the sensor. Pulling the valve stem without first separating the sensor can also damage it. At installation, clean wheel mounting faces and correctly tightened nuts are essential: contamination can let the wheel loosen, while an incorrect tightening pattern can contribute to brake-disc runout and vibration.

when.summary: When replacing a tire or wheel, or servicing a valve stem or TPMS sensor that requires tire dismounting.
notes: A new valve stem is required whenever a new tire or wheel is installed.
An undamaged original sensor can be reused; the procedure states that retaining it avoids TPMS training.

prepare.title: Check for injected tire sealant
prepare.detail: Before service, ask whether anyone has injected sealant into the tire. Some sealants may burn or explode when exposed to an ignition source.

prepare.title: Use compatible tire equipment
prepare.detail: Carbon-fiber and alloy wheels require a center-clamp tire changer. Do not use a tabletop machine that grips inside the wheel and rides on its front flange. A balancer must not contact the wheel face.

prepare.title: Gather valve and measurement equipment
prepare.detail: Have a digital tire-pressure gauge, suitable valve-stem tools, a wooden block, specified bead lubricant and torque equipment. Identify snap-in or bolt-on sensor hardware before disassembly.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and inflation capability
prepare.detail: Use the specified hoist points and check clearance around underbody components. Never work under a jack alone. The exceptional bead-seating sequence requires remote inflation equipment, protective equipment and, at its later stage, an OSHA-approved tire safety cage.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and release all air
steps.body: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, raise it using the lifting procedure and remove the wheel nuts and wheel. Do not heat a seized nut. Remove the valve core and fully deflate the tire before bead separation.

steps.title: Break the beads clear of the sensor
steps.body: Do not push either bead beyond the wheel's mid-plane. With a paddle separator at 3 o'clock, position the valve at 12 or 6 o'clock. With a roller separator, align the valve with the roller. These positions keep the operation clear of the sensor.

steps.title: Dismount both beads
steps.body: Index-mark the valve and wheel-weight positions on the tire. Set the valve at 11:30 and the machine arm at 12 o'clock to dismount the outer bead. Reset to the same relationship before dismounting the inner bead.

steps.title: Separate the valve and sensor
steps.body: Remove and discard the sensor-to-stem screw, then separate the sensor. For a snap-in stem, use the suitable remover and wooden block without damaging the wheel. For a bolt-on stem, discard the retaining nut and washer. Remove and discard the stem. Inspect any sensor intended for reuse and replace it if damaged.

steps.title: Assemble the appropriate valve arrangement
steps.body: Attach the new stem to the sensor before installing the assembly in the wheel, using a new screw and the specified tightening. Lubricate a snap-in stem with soapy water and pull it through parallel to the hole axis, using the installer and wooden block. For a bolt-on assembly, prevent sensor rotation while tightening the stem nut.

steps.title: Mount the tire in the specified positions
steps.body: Lubricate the beads with suitable fast-drying, corrosion-inhibiting bead lubricant. Position the bottom bead on the wheel before mounting. Align the valve and machine arm at 6 o'clock to mount the bottom bead; reposition to that same relationship for the top bead.

steps.title: Inflate and follow the seating decision
steps.body: Use the digital gauge and inflate to the pressure on the vehicle certification label at the driver door or pillar. If the beads do not seat, follow the linked staged procedure. Its above-sidewall-maximum sequence applies only after seating fails up to that maximum: relubricate, use a remote valve and gauge, wear eye and ear protection and stand at least 3.65 m (12 ft) away. The first stage stops at seating or 138 kPa (20 psi) above the sidewall maximum. If unsuccessful, deflate before the next stage. That stage requires an OSHA-approved safety cage and stops at seating or 276 kPa (40 psi) above the maximum. Never exceed that limit; replace the tire if seating still fails.

steps.title: Prepare the wheel mounting surfaces
steps.body: Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel and mating hub or brake mounting face. Ensure rotor-retaining fasteners cannot interfere. Apply a thin coat of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 only between the wheel pilot bore and hub pilot. Keep it off mounting faces, studs, nuts, pads and disc friction surfaces.

steps.title: Install and tighten the wheel
steps.body: Fit the wheel and finger-tighten the nuts. Perform final tightening with the vehicle resting on its tires, using clean, dry stud and nut threads. Tighten in a star/cross pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). Retighten within 160 km (100 mi) after reinstallation.

watchFor.title: Valve installation at an angle
watchFor.body: An angled pull can damage a snap-in stem and sensor. A bolt-on sensor must not rotate as its nut is tightened.

watchFor.title: Uncontrolled bead-seating pressure
watchFor.body: The exceptional pressure stages require the complete prescribed setup and limits; they are not ordinary inflation instructions.

notes: Use designated weight-removal tools; do not scrape adhesive weights off with a screwdriver or another sharp metal tool.
Do not clean aluminum wheels with steel wool, abrasive cleaners or strong detergents.
The no-training statement applies to reuse of the original sensor; it does not establish the setup requirements for a replacement sensor.

diagnostics.finding: A removed sensor is damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: It is unsuitable for reuse.
diagnostics.next: Install a replacement sensor rather than transferring the damaged unit.

diagnostics.finding: The beads remain unseated at the final permitted seating-pressure limit.
diagnostics.meaning: Further pressure increase is prohibited by the procedure.
diagnostics.next: Replace the tire.

verification.title: Confirm the final operating pressure
verification.body: Use the digital gauge to confirm the label-specified tire pressure. Elevated bead-seating pressure is not the operating-pressure target.

verification.title: Record pressure and wheel fastening
verification.body: Record the final tire pressure and wheel-nut torque, together with the required retightening within 160 km (100 mi).

procedures.purpose: Tire disassembly and assembly, sensor-specific valve service, machine positioning and the controlled bead-seating sequence.
Wheel removal and installation, mounting-face preparation, restricted anti-seize application and final wheel-nut tightening.
Vehicle lifting points and precautions for wheel removal.
Tire-sealant precautions, wheel-compatible equipment and finish-protection practices.

guides.title: Minimize wheel-to-hub runout on the 5.2L Mustang
guides.summary: Position the measured wheel-and-tire high spot at the bottom, then tighten the wheel under light suspension loading to use available hub clearance.
guides.introduction: A wheel can have a small amount of clearance around the hub before its nuts are fully tightened. This procedure uses that clearance to offset a known high spot in the wheel-and-tire assembly. Radial runout describes the assembly's high-and-low variation as it rotates. Road Force is also influenced by tire stiffness, so a small change in mounting position can affect the result.
guides.why: The prescribed position and loading work together. Placing the high spot at the bottom establishes the intended orientation, while slight ground contact loads the assembly before final tightening. Allowing the vehicle's full weight onto the tires at that stage breaks the specified method. This is a targeted mounting adjustment following identification of a high spot.

when.summary: When a radial-runout or Road Force high spot has been identified and wheel-to-hub optimization is appropriate.
notes: A vibration complaint alone does not identify the high spot or establish that this adjustment will resolve it.

prepare.title: Have a known high-spot location
prepare.detail: Use the identified radial-runout or Road Force high spot from wheel-and-tire assessment. The mounting procedure begins with that location already established.

prepare.title: Arrange controlled lifting and tightening
prepare.detail: Provide vehicle lifting capability that allows the tires to touch the ground without taking full vehicle weight, and torque equipment for the Mustang wheel installation procedure.

prepare.title: Protect the tire and wheel
prepare.detail: Before tire servicing, ask whether sealant has been injected; it may be flammable. If additional tire-machine work is needed on carbon-fiber or alloy wheels, use a center-clamp tire changer and a balancer that does not contact the wheel face.

steps.title: Prepare the wheel for positioning
steps.body: Use the [Mustang wheel and tire procedure](#/document/G1686507) for the required removal and handling. Keep the identified high spot recognizable when positioning the assembly on the vehicle.

steps.title: Place the high spot at the bottom
steps.body: Position the assembly with its radial-runout or Road Force high spot at the 6 o'clock position. Install the wheel nuts by hand until snug, as directed by the [optimization procedure](#/document/G1686504).

steps.title: Apply only slight loading
steps.body: Lower the vehicle until the tires contact the ground and the suspension is slightly loaded. Do not allow the full vehicle weight to rest on the tires while tightening the nuts.

steps.title: Complete wheel fastening
steps.body: Tighten the wheel nuts according to the Mustang Wheel and Tire procedure while maintaining the specified light loading. Use its fastening requirements for the fitted wheel.

watchFor.title: Wrong orientation or excessive loading
watchFor.body: Both the bottom-positioned high spot and slight suspension loading are required parts of the optimization.

notes: The shared procedure also references Super Duty wheel installation; that branch does not apply to this Mustang job.
The amount of improvement depends on available wheel-to-hub clearance and tire stiffness.

verification.title: Confirm the mounting conditions
verification.body: Confirm the identified high spot was at the bottom and final tightening occurred with only slight suspension loading.

verification.title: Confirm wheel installation completion
verification.body: Verify the wheel nuts were tightened according to the applicable Mustang wheel installation requirements.

procedures.purpose: Wheel-to-hub runout optimization through high-spot orientation and light loading.
Mustang wheel and tire removal, installation and wheel-nut fastening requirements.
Tire-sealant precautions and equipment requirements protecting carbon-fiber and alloy wheels.

guides.title: Match-mount a tire with the 180-degree runout test
guides.summary: Rotate the tire halfway around its wheel, remeasure the assembly and use the high-spot pattern to identify the supported correction.
guides.introduction: A tire and wheel can each contribute to radial runout—the assembly's out-of-round motion—and ride vibration. Match-mounting changes their relationship by rotating the tire on the rim. The 180-degree test can reduce combined runout or Road Force and, when it does not, help establish whether the remaining high spot follows the tire or wheel.
guides.why: Temporary flat spots can distort measurements. Two comparable measurements and clearly marked high spots are essential: a high reading alone cannot justify choosing a tire or wheel for replacement.

when.summary: When tire/wheel vibration is confirmed and assembly runout or Road Force needs correction.
notes: Do not diagnose tire/wheel vibration on tires with less than 200 mi (322 km).
Complete runout minimization before a tire warranty claim for out-of-specification Road Force or runout.

prepare.title: Use suitable tire-service equipment
prepare.detail: This requires tire mounting capability, a suitable tire machine, and a dial indicator or Hunter Road Force 9700 Series balancer. Road Force measurement is preferred. For carbon-fiber and alloy wheels, use a center-clamp changer and a balancer that does not contact the wheel face; tabletop changers are unsuitable.

prepare.title: Check sealant and sensor precautions
prepare.detail: Ask whether tire sealant has been injected before servicing the tire; it may ignite or explode near an ignition source. If a tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) is fitted, follow its tire dismounting precautions to avoid sensor damage.

steps.title: Confirm and condition the assembly
steps.body: Establish that the complaint is tire/wheel vibration through noise, vibration and harshness diagnosis. Drive 20 or more miles just before Road Force measurements to eliminate possible short-term flat-spotting.

steps.title: Select the correct matching method
steps.body: Hunter Gen I and II machines are for measurement only here; ignore their matching prompts and use the manual procedure. On Gen III, use Match Without Rim Runout if available, otherwise the manual method. Gen IV and V require Road Force → Procedures → 180 Matching; select it each time if it is not the default. Only Hunter software includes the Ford-approved automatic method; use the manual procedure with non-Hunter equipment.

steps.title: Establish the first reference
steps.body: Record the initial runout or Road Force measurement and mark its high spot on the tire. On the tire machine, mark the sidewall at the valve stem. Keep this position reference distinct from the high-spot mark.

steps.title: Move the tire halfway around the rim
steps.body: Separate the beads using the suitable tire machine. Apply suitable fast-drying, corrosion-inhibiting bead lubricant, then rotate the tire 180 degrees until its valve-stem reference mark is opposite the valve stem.

steps.title: Remeasure under the specified conditions
steps.body: Reinflate to the specified pressure and repeat the assembly measurement using the suitable indicator or balancer. Mark the second high spot. Compare the reading with the applicable specification and the mark with the original high spot.

steps.title: Apply the high-spot decisions
steps.body: Use the findings below to select the supported outcome. A wheel-following pattern requires a separate bare-wheel runout measurement before wheel replacement. If neither pattern fits, this test has not isolated the cause.

steps.title: Finish the supported correction
steps.body: After a within-specification result or the indicated component replacement, balance the assembly and install it using [Wheel to Hub Runout Minimization](#/document/G1686504). Permanently mark the final high spot and measurement values on the inward tire sidewall for future service.

watchFor.title: An alternative matching routine is selected
watchFor.body: Other machine routines may be available or set as defaults. Use only the approved routine for that generation or the manual procedure.

watchFor.title: Wheel-finish damage during balancing
watchFor.body: Use designated weight-removal tools. Do not pry adhesive weights off with a screwdriver or another sharp metallic instrument.

notes: Applicable assembly limits and inflation pressure must be obtained for the tire/wheel being serviced; the bare-wheel limit below is a separate decision threshold.

diagnostics.finding: The second assembly measurement is within specification.
diagnostics.meaning: Repositioning has resolved the measured runout or Road Force concern.
diagnostics.next: Balance the assembly and complete wheel-to-hub optimization.

diagnostics.finding: Both measurements exceed specification and the tire high-spot marks are within 101.6 mm (4 in) of each other.
diagnostics.meaning: The high spot followed the tire, supporting the tire as the cause.
diagnostics.next: Install a new tire, then complete balancing and wheel-to-hub optimization.

diagnostics.finding: The second measurement remains excessive and its high spot is within 101.6 mm (4 in) of the position opposite the first mark.
diagnostics.meaning: The high spot followed the wheel, making wheel runout the next check.
diagnostics.next: Dismount the tire and measure the wheel on a balancer. Replace the wheel only if runout exceeds 1.14 mm (0.0449 in), then finish balancing and installation.

diagnostics.finding: Neither high-spot pattern fits, or the suspected wheel passes its runout check.
diagnostics.meaning: The supported replacement criteria have not been met.
diagnostics.next: Continue diagnosis without declaring the cause isolated or replacing a component speculatively.

verification.title: Confirm the measured outcome
verification.body: Use the repeat reading to establish whether repositioning brought the assembly within specification. Confirm balancing and wheel-to-hub optimization are completed for the resolved branch.

verification.title: Preserve the measurement record
verification.body: Retain the first and second readings with their high-spot relationship, and check that the final high spot and values are permanently marked on the inward sidewall.

procedures.purpose: Equipment selection, complete 180-degree matching test and supported tire/wheel decisions.
Tire-service safety, wheel-compatible equipment and finish protection.
Wheel-to-hub optimization during installation after the supported correction.

guides.title: Diagnose TPMS warnings, missing pressure readings and sensor training faults
guides.summary: Separate low tire pressure from sensor, training, wiring, configuration and communication faults before replacing TPMS components.
guides.introduction: The tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) uses battery-powered sensors attached to the tire valve stems. Their radio messages reach the radio transceiver module (RTM), which passes information to the body control module (BCM) over a local interconnect network (LIN). The instrument panel cluster (IPC) displays pressures and warnings. Diagnosis establishes whether the tires need attention or that information path has failed.
guides.why: A warning does not identify a failed sensor. Low pressure, an untrained replacement, radio frequency interference (RFI), damaged connections and incorrect module configuration can produce overlapping symptoms. Following the relevant test prevents a communication problem from becoming an unnecessary parts replacement.
searchTerms: low tire pressure warning stays on

when.summary: When a pressure warning persists, readings disappear, sensors will not train or TPMS-related trouble codes are recorded.
notes: Replacement decisions require the relevant concern to be present during testing.

prepare.title: Diagnostic equipment and capability
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable diagnostic scan tool, digital tire pressure gauge and the equipment required by the sensor activation and calibration procedures. Electrical branches require a digital multimeter, correct terminal probe adapters and competence with isolated resistance and live voltage tests.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Review previous repairs and applicable Ford service information. Inspect aftermarket wheels, run-flat tires and electronic accessories, verify horn operation and identify whether the spare tire is fitted.

steps.title: Identify the exact warning
steps.body: Record the lamp behavior and message. A continuous warning with LOW TIRE PRESSURE follows Test E. A continuous warning without that message requires BCM and RTM diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Dashes in the pressure display call for sensor activation. An indicator that never operates or remains incorrectly illuminated also requires instrumentation diagnosis.

steps.title: Check communication before interpreting sensor faults
steps.body: Retrieve relevant module codes and follow the matching test below. A module that does not answer the scan tool requires communications-network diagnosis. Tests A and D check network communication and RTM self-test results before pursuing sensor training. Diagnose circuit faults before system or performance faults.

steps.title: Work through the low-pressure branch
steps.body: In Test E, verify B124D:02 by clearing it, cycling the ignition and activating the sensors. Restore the road wheel if the spare is fitted. Measure and record all tire pressures with the digital gauge, then correct low pressures to the vehicle certification label. To update the warning, drive for at least 2 minutes above 32.2 km/h (20 mph), or activate each sensor at least twice. Do not train sensors at this stage. If the warning remains, continue E through training and pressure-data comparison.

steps.title: Activate and train at the appropriate stage
steps.body: Activation wakes sensors; location calibration teaches their identities to the BCM. Sensors sleeping after more than 30 minutes stationary need activation. Follow the complete calibration procedure when the selected test requires training. Test G allows 2 minutes between sensor responses; two horn sounds and TIRE NOT TRAINED REPEAT require restarting the entire procedure.

steps.title: Complete connector and physical checks before module replacement
steps.body: At the selected test's connector-check stage, switch the ignition off. Replace damaged terminals or connectors, clean corroded module pins, and ensure connectors seat and latch. Retest after correcting the cause. Persistent A or B faults can require tire disassembly to confirm sensors are actually installed. Follow applicable service articles before a test-directed module replacement.

steps.title: Resolve configuration faults after module work
steps.body: RTM code U2100:00 requires scan-tool configuration. BCM code B1182:55 requires configuration, training all sensors and a successful BCM self-test. Location codes B1254:51, B1255:51, C1A56:51 and C1A58:51 identify unprogrammed right-rear, left-rear, left-front and right-front sensors respectively and require location training. For RTM U3000:04 or BCM U0559:56, review RTM service history: repeat programmable module installation (PMI) after recent incomplete or improper work; without recent service, the chart directs RTM replacement for failure to retain configuration.

watchFor.title: A spare cannot be trained
watchFor.body: A missing or inaccessible damaged road wheel can generate a sensor fault. Repair and refit that road wheel to restore operation.

watchFor.title: Interference can imitate component failure
watchFor.body: Ask which electronic devices were operating when the fault occurred. Disconnect aftermarket equipment where possible and perform interference testing away from other vehicles, motors and transmitters.

notes: Use engine-matched electronic-control diagnostics for powertrain faults. The linked 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L procedures are distinct; a 5.2L vehicle requires its appropriate engine-control procedure.
Sensor or module replacement is a separate repair phase. Use its complete procedure and carry out the required training or configuration afterward.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1182:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test A addresses loss of information from all sensors, including an RTM-to-BCM communication failure.
diagnostics.next: Check gateway module (GWM), RTM and BCM communication, then RTM codes and TPMS_STATUS. SYSTEM FAULT leads to training. If necessary, rotate the wheels at least one-fourth turn, leave doors open and restart at another wheel. Partial success identifies sensors requiring replacement; no success leads to BCM connector and sensor-presence checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B124D:02 is recorded with SENSOR FAULT status.
diagnostics.meaning: Test B addresses missing information from one, two or three sensors; SYSTEM FAULT redirects to A.
diagnostics.next: Record sensor identifiers before training. After successful training, compare identifiers without considering wheel position: changed identities reveal replacements that were not retrained. Otherwise repeat after rotating the wheels and starting elsewhere; persistent failures lead to sensor replacement or connector and sensor-presence checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1251:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test C addresses a low sensor battery detected during attempted training.
diagnostics.next: Train all sensors. Before replacing a nonresponsive sensor, rotate the wheels, repeat activation of that same sensor and attempt training with the doors open as directed. Replace only sensors that continue to fail.

diagnostics.finding: TPMS operation is intermittent and radio interference is suspected.
diagnostics.meaning: Test D distinguishes interference from missing sensors, wiring faults and module faults.
diagnostics.next: Check GWM/RTM communication, RTM codes and TPMS_STATUS. Train away from interference. If unsuccessful, rotate the wheels, open the doors and perform D5's known-good-sensor comparison. Successful training of all known-good sensors directs original-sensor replacement; follow the specified RTM branch if the comparison fails, then BCM checks if the concern persists.

diagnostics.finding: The warning remains on with LOW TIRE PRESSURE displayed.
diagnostics.meaning: Test E checks actual pressure, spare-wheel use and sensor pressure accuracy.
diagnostics.next: Follow the pressure-correction sequence above. If subsequent training fails, use G. If training succeeds, activate the sensors and compare scan-tool pressure values with the recorded gauge measurements; replace sensors reporting outside the specified tolerance.

diagnostics.finding: The BCM will not enter sensor training mode.
diagnostics.meaning: Test F checks the ignition, brake and vehicle-speed inputs needed for manual training.
diagnostics.next: Resolve BCM communication/data codes, check for the flashing start-stop switch indicator in RUN, perform the powertrain control module (PCM) key-on, engine-off self-test and check stoplamp operation. Diagnose failed inputs before BCM connector checks and any replacement decision.

diagnostics.finding: One or more sensors will not train and no DTCs are present.
diagnostics.meaning: Test G separates individual nonresponse from a broader reception problem.
diagnostics.next: If none train, use D. If some train, rotate the wheels at least one-fourth turn and repeat training. Replace sensors that still fail; successful retraining can indicate interference.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0146:00 is recorded in the RTM.
diagnostics.meaning: Test H addresses missing or invalid gateway messages.
diagnostics.next: Check GWM network response, clear the RTM code, cycle ignition and retest. If it returns, diagnose GWM codes and check other modules. After applicable bulletin checks, the same code elsewhere directs GWM replacement; an RTM-only occurrence directs RTM replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U1A00:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test I addresses interrupted LIN communication between the BCM and RTM.
diagnostics.next: Check network response and BCM codes, then RTM supply continuity, supply-to-ground isolation, ground continuity and LIN shorts/open circuits in order. Use the specified disconnected connectors and ignition states; only the short-to-voltage stage requires ignition on. Repair failed circuits, check the specified fuse where directed, then inspect RTM connections before considering replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0401:00 or U0401:82 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test J distinguishes invalid PCM vehicle-speed data from data that fails to refresh.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose U0146:00 first. Check GWM/PCM communication, clear codes, cycle ignition and drive for a minimum of 2 minutes above 24 km/h (15 mph). Persistent codes require GWM and PCM self-tests. After service-information checks, U0146:xx or U0447:xx in two or more modules directs GWM replacement; otherwise U0401 or U0401:xx beyond the RTM directs PCM replacement. Without corroboration, follow the intermittent-fault conclusion.

verification.title: Confirm the selected branch's endpoint
verification.body: Confirm each required training response by the horn. In E6, refreshed BCM pressure parameter identifications (PIDs) must match measured pressures within ±20.7 kPa (3 psi). Verify the warning and message have cleared where that is the test endpoint.

verification.title: Record the evidence
verification.body: Retain measured pressures, sensor identifiers, module codes and repeat-test results. Test B calls for all sensor identifiers on the applicable warranty claim. Clear codes where directed and complete required self-tests; a nonreturning communication code may represent an intermittent condition.

procedures.purpose: Complete TPMS symptom and DTC charts, Tests A–J, circuit measurements and decision branches.
Electrical diagnostic prerequisites, probe use and valid measurement methods.
Activate sensors to refresh transmitted pressure information.
Train sensor identities and wheel locations to the BCM.
Diagnose nonresponsive modules and gateway/network faults.
Follow up BCM codes requiring separate module diagnosis.
Diagnose incorrect warning-indicator operation.
Diagnose a failed start-stop switch input during Test F.
Diagnose stoplamp operation and brake-switch concerns during Test F.
Follow up PCM faults on the 2.3L engine.
Follow up PCM faults on the 3.7L engine.
Follow up PCM faults on the 5.0L engine.
Remove and install a road wheel when directed.
Dismount tires to check physical sensor installation.
Remove and install sensors after a supported failure finding.
Remove and install the RTM when its diagnostic branch requires replacement.
Remove and install the GWM after the communication tests justify replacement.

guides.title: Wake the TPMS sensors and refresh tire-pressure readings
guides.summary: Activate each tire-pressure sensor at least twice, work through the prescribed retries for an unresponsive sensor, and check the warning afterward.
guides.introduction: Your Mustang’s tire-pressure sensors get to take naps. The dashboard gets to complain about it. I’ll walk you around the car with the activation tool to wake each sensor and request fresh pressure information. This procedure applies to 2015 Mustangs with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
guides.why: Each battery-powered sensor is mounted to a tire valve stem and reports tire pressure by radio. A receiver, identified as the RTM, passes that information through a data link to the body control module, or BCM. The instrument cluster warns about low pressure or a system fault. While the car is stationary, the sensors can sleep to conserve their batteries and stop transmitting. Activation wakes them; it does not put air in the tires or prove that every part of the communication system is healthy.

when.summary: Use this procedure when sleeping sensors need to transmit current pressure information, including after a BCM reset has cleared stored readings.
notes: The TPMS indicator can report low tire pressure or a system fault. An illuminated indicator alone does not identify a failed sensor.
A BCM reset can leave pressure data at a factory default while the cluster displays dashes.

prepare.title: Have the activation tool ready
prepare.detail: Use Tire Pressure Monitor tool 204-D081A (204-D081). Have the customer activation tool available if possible; it is an alternative used later in the nonresponse sequence.

prepare.title: Check actual tire pressures first
prepare.detail: Have a tire-pressure gauge, a means of adjusting pressure and the correct inflation specification for the vehicle and fitted tires. Check and adjust actual pressures before judging the final warning state. The value 1033 kPa (149.96 psi) can be a BCM reset default; never use it as an inflation target.

prepare.title: Reach the sensors with the wheels fitted
prepare.detail: Locate the valve stem on each road wheel. You reach the sensor with the tool against the outside tire sidewall beside that stem; nothing needs to be removed, unplugged or positioned aside. Keep room available to move the vehicle safely if a sensor requires the wheel-rotation retry.

prepare.title: Know the endpoint
prepare.detail: This job covers sensor activation and its prescribed retries. If the warning remains after pressure adjustment and activation, or a sensor remains unresponsive, further TPMS diagnosis is required before choosing a repair. Fault-testing instructions and sensor replacement are separate work.

steps.title: Turn the ignition ON
steps.body: Turn the ignition switch to ON. Begin at the left-front tire—the front wheel on the vehicle’s left side. The [sensor activation procedure](#/document/G1686522) establishes this starting point.

steps.title: Place the tool beside the left-front valve stem
steps.body: Find the tire valve stem and hold tool 204-D081A (204-D081) against the tire sidewall at that location. The tool operates from outside the tire; leave the wheel fitted.

steps.title: Activate the left-front sensor at least twice
steps.body:
Press the tool’s test button to activate the sensor. Perform at least two activations at this wheel.

The tool may flash a green light and beep when a sensor responds. That feedback can sometimes be absent, and feedback that does appear does not prove the vehicle’s module received the transmission. I treat the beep as useful information, not a victory parade.

steps.title: Work through the retries if that sensor does not respond
steps.body:
Move the vehicle safely far enough to rotate the wheels at least one-fourth of a turn. Reposition the tool against the sidewall at the same tire’s valve stem and repeat the activation attempt.

If the sensor still does not respond, try activating that same sensor with the customer activation tool, if available.

If it still fails to respond or train, open the vehicle doors and attempt activation again. If the customer tool is unavailable, proceed from the wheel-rotation retry to the doors-open attempt. Keep track of the wheel involved; repeated silence is a reason to investigate, not a shopping list for sensors.

steps.title: Activate every remaining tire sensor
steps.body:
At each remaining tire, find its valve stem, place the activation tool against the adjacent sidewall and activate the sensor at least twice. Use the same nonresponse sequence wherever necessary.

Complete all remaining road wheels. The activation routine establishes left-front as the starting point but does not prescribe an order for the other wheels.

steps.title: Check the instrument cluster after completing the circuit
steps.body:
After actual tire pressures have been adjusted and every sensor has received its activation attempts, check the TPMS indicator and message display. Note whether the warning cleared and identify any wheel whose sensor remained unresponsive.

Review any displayed pressure information as well. A tool beep alone is not confirmation that the BCM received a fresh reading. These are completion observations, not additional fault tests.

watchFor.title: A reset default masquerading as a pressure reading
watchFor.body: After a BCM reset, pressure data identifiers—stored values often called DIDs—can revert to 1033 kPa (149.96 psi), with dashes displayed in the cluster. This is a factory default, not a measured tire pressure.

watchFor.title: Tool feedback with limited meaning
watchFor.body: A flashing green light and beep can indicate a sensor response to the tool. They do not establish that the vehicle received it. Conversely, absent feedback alone is not enough to condemn a sensor.

watchFor.title: An activation attempt cannot correct inflation
watchFor.body: The warning can remain because of low pressure or a system fault. Check actual inflation rather than trying to make the light disappear through repeated activation alone.

notes: The [TPMS overview](#/document/G1686515) explains the sensor-to-receiver-to-BCM communication path and why the cluster can warn about either low pressure or a fault.
Activation requires no wheel removal, tire dismounting or replacement parts.

diagnostics.finding: Pressure data show 1033 kPa (149.96 psi), and the cluster displays dashes after a BCM reset.
diagnostics.meaning: The reset may have cleared stored pressure information and restored the factory default.
diagnostics.next: Check actual tire pressures and perform the activation circuit to request current information. Do not inflate a tire to the reset value.

diagnostics.finding: A sensor does not respond to the specified activation tool.
diagnostics.meaning: The initial attempt has not produced a sensor response; this does not identify a failed component.
diagnostics.next: Move the vehicle to rotate the wheels at least one-fourth of a turn, then retry the same sensor.

diagnostics.finding: The same sensor remains unresponsive after the wheel-rotation retry.
diagnostics.meaning: Changing the wheel position has not resolved the nonresponse.
diagnostics.next: Try the customer activation tool if available. If the sensor still fails to respond or train, attempt activation with the vehicle doors open.

diagnostics.finding: A sensor remains unresponsive after the prescribed retries.
diagnostics.meaning: Normal communication has not been established through activation. The result alone does not establish which component needs repair.
diagnostics.next: Record the wheel position and have the TPMS fault diagnosed before replacing parts.

diagnostics.finding: The TPMS indicator remains illuminated after pressure adjustment and activation of every sensor.
diagnostics.meaning: The activation routine has not resolved the warning.
diagnostics.next: Continue with TPMS diagnosis and testing rather than assuming a particular sensor has failed.

verification.title: Confirm every wheel received attention
verification.body: Confirm that you started at the left-front tire, positioned the tool at each valve stem and activated every road-wheel sensor at least twice. Record any retries and any sensor that remained unresponsive.

verification.title: Record the vehicle’s result
verification.body: Record the TPMS indicator state, any remaining cluster message or dashes, and whether current pressure information is displayed. Judge the outcome from the vehicle’s indications as well as the activation attempts, not from tool feedback alone.

procedures.purpose: Ignition setting, activation-tool placement, minimum activation count, nonresponse retries and the endpoint for a persistent warning.
Sensor purpose, communication path and the distinction between low-pressure warnings and system faults.

applicability.equipment: Valve-stem-mounted TPMS sensors, tire-pressure warning indicator and instrument-cluster message display.

stepGroups.title: Wake the left-front sensor
stepGroups.summary: Set the ignition, position the tool and perform the first two activations.

stepGroups.title: Handle retries and finish the wheels
stepGroups.summary: Use the prescribed nonresponse sequence and activate the remaining sensors.

stepGroups.title: Check the vehicle’s response
stepGroups.summary: Review the warning and pressure display after completing activation.

guides.title: Calibrate TPMS sensor positions
guides.summary: Train the tire-pressure sensors in wheel order and verify that the body control module has accepted their locations.
guides.introduction: The tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) uses battery-operated sensors mounted at the tire valve stems. Their radio reports pass through a receiver to the body control module (BCM). Location calibration teaches the BCM which sensor belongs at each wheel; it does not itself correct low tire pressure or diagnose a failed sensor.
guides.why: The module learns positions in a fixed sequence, so the order and acknowledgement after each wheel matter. Training also has time limits. Moving on without recognition, or waiting too long between wheels, can leave the procedure unsuccessful even though some sensors were accepted.

when.summary: When sensor positions need to be learned, including after installation of a new body control module.
notes: A tire-pressure warning can indicate low pressure or a system fault; it does not establish a need for sensor replacement.

prepare.title: Have the activation tool ready
prepare.detail: Use tire-pressure monitor tool 204-D081A (204-D081). Manual entry into training mode still requires this tool to activate the wheel sensors.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic access
prepare.detail: Ford diagnostic equipment can enter training mode and read the updated sensor identifiers. It is also needed for the additional checks following BCM replacement.

steps.title: Choose scan-tool entry if available
steps.body: Follow [Sensor Location Calibration](#/document/G1686523). In the IDS interface, select Chassis > TPMS > Training Mode. In the FDRS interface, select Toolbox > BCM > BCM — TPMS Initialization. These are alternative entry paths.

steps.title: Use manual entry when needed
steps.body: With ignition OFF, press and release the brake pedal. Use the start/stop switch to cycle OFF to RUN 3 times, finishing in RUN. Press and release the brake pedal, switch ignition OFF, then repeat the 3 OFF-to-RUN cycles, again ending in RUN.

steps.title: Confirm training mode
steps.body: Successful entry produces one horn sound and a flashing TPMS indicator. If a message center is fitted, it displays TRAIN LF TIRE. Have the activation tool at hand before beginning the timed wheel sequence.

steps.title: Train the left-front sensor
steps.body: Within 2 minutes of the horn sounding, place the tool against the left-front tire sidewall at the valve stem. Press and release its test button. Keep it in place: activation can take up to 6 seconds. A brief horn sound confirms BCM recognition.

steps.title: Continue around the vehicle
steps.body: Train the right-front, right-rear and then left-rear sensor using the same placement and activation method. Begin each activation within 2 minutes of the preceding horn acknowledgement. Training finishes after the last tire is accepted.

steps.title: Document identifiers and complete any BCM follow-up
steps.body: Read the updated sensor identifiers from the BCM with the scan tool and document them on the applicable warranty claim. If training follows installation of a new BCM, clear diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) and run the BCM On-Demand Self-Test. This is required to clear B1182:55, exit manufacturing mode and check for other concerns.

watchFor.title: An unacknowledged sensor
watchFor.body: Allow the stated activation time with the tool held at the valve stem. Lack of acknowledgement alone does not prove sensor failure.

diagnostics.finding: The horn sounds twice when ignition is switched OFF after training.
diagnostics.meaning: The training procedure was unsuccessful.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the complete training sequence, observing wheel order and timing.

verification.title: Confirm completion
verification.body: Look for TIRE TRAINING COMPLETE where a message center is fitted. Without a message center, successful completion is confirmed by switching ignition OFF without a horn sound.

verification.title: Check the recorded result
verification.body: Confirm that the identifier record reflects the newly trained BCM entries. For a new BCM, also retain the result of the required On-Demand Self-Test.

procedures.purpose: Scan-tool or manual training-mode entry, sensor activation order, completion checks and new-BCM follow-up.

guides.title: Replace a tire-pressure sensor and train its wheel position
guides.summary: Replace or transfer the valve-mounted pressure sensor through controlled tire disassembly, then train a new sensor and verify recognition.
guides.introduction: The tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) sensor sits inside the wheel, attached to the valve stem, and transmits pressure information to the body control module (BCM). Access requires dismounting the tire; removing the road wheel alone does not expose the sensor.
guides.why: Tire-machine contact, excessive bead movement or pulling an attached valve stem can damage the sensor. Correct mechanical installation protects the assembly, while training lets the vehicle recognize a new sensor at its wheel position.
searchTerms: transfer tire pressure sensor to new wheel

when.summary: Diagnosis or visible damage justifies sensor replacement, or a wheel change requires transferring a serviceable sensor.
notes: An illuminated warning alone does not establish sensor failure.

prepare.title: Arrange tire-service capability
prepare.detail: You need wheel-removal and tire-machine skills, a suitable valve-stem remover/installer, wooden block, torque tools, digital tire-pressure gauge, TPMS tool 204-D081A (204-D081) and Ford diagnostic equipment.

prepare.title: Protect the wheel
prepare.detail: Carbon-fiber and alloy wheels require a center-clamp tire changer. Do not use tabletop machines that grip inside the wheel and ride on its front flange. Any balancing equipment must avoid wheel-face contact.

steps.title: Remove and fully deflate the assembly
steps.body: Follow the wheel removal procedure referenced by [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686509). Remove the valve core and release all air. Mark the valve-stem and wheel-weight positions on the tire. Leave the stem in place until the tire is dismounted and the sensor detached.

steps.title: Dismount without striking the sensor
steps.body: Keep the beads from moving beyond the wheel mid-plane. With a paddle separator, place the valve at 12 or 6 o'clock and the paddle at 3 o'clock; with a roller separator, align valve and roller. For dismounting, position the valve at 11:30 and the machine arm at 12 o'clock. Remove the outer bead, reset those positions, then remove the inner bead.

steps.title: Separate the sensor and old valve
steps.body: Discard the sensor-to-valve screw and separate the sensor. For snap-in valves, use the suitable remover and wooden block to remove and discard the stem without damaging the wheel. For bolt-on valves, discard the nut, washer and stem. Inspect any sensor intended for reuse; replace it if damaged.

steps.title: Assemble the correct valve type
steps.body: Attach the new stem to the sensor before installing the assembly in the wheel, using a new sensor screw tightened to 1.5 Nm. For snap-in valves, lubricate with soapy water and use the installer and wooden block, pulling parallel to the hole axis. For bolt-on valves, replace the discarded nut and washer; hold the sensor against rotation while tightening the nut to 8 Nm.

steps.title: Mount the tire and establish pressure
steps.body: Use fast-drying, corrosion-inhibiting bead lubricant. Align the valve and machine arm at 6 o'clock for the bottom bead, then reposition likewise for the top bead. Set pressure from the driver-door or door-pillar label using a digital gauge. If beads will not seat, follow the complete [staged bead-seating procedure](#/document/G1686509) before exceeding the sidewall maximum. Finish at label pressure and reinstall the wheel through the referenced procedure.

steps.title: Train a new sensor
steps.body: Enter learn mode using Ford diagnostic equipment or the manual ignition/brake sequence in [Sensor Location Calibration](#/document/G1686523). Confirm one horn sound and a flashing TPMS indicator. Train left front, right front, right rear, then left rear with the TPMS tool at each valve-stem sidewall. Begin each activation within 2 minutes of the preceding horn; allow up to 6 seconds with the tool held in place.

steps.title: Activate sleeping sensors when fresh readings are needed
steps.body: Activation wakes sensors and is separate from location training. Following [Sensor Activation](#/document/G1686522), switch ignition on and activate each sensor at least twice. If the warning remains after pressure adjustment and activation, continue with TPMS diagnosis.

watchFor.title: A bead refuses to seat
watchFor.body: The escalation procedure requires relubrication, remote inflation equipment, eye and ear protection, at least 3.65 m (12 ft) separation, and an OSHA-approved safety cage for its higher-pressure stage. Follow both staged pressure limits; replace the tire if it will not seat at the final limit.

watchFor.title: Severe sensor battery damage
watchFor.body: Dispose of sensors through hazardous-material procedures. If released battery chemicals contact skin or eyes, flush with water for at least 15 minutes and obtain prompt medical attention. Swallowed battery material requires immediate physician contact.

notes: A serviceable sensor reused from the previous wheel does not require retraining merely because the wheel is replaced or the tire is dismounted.
A new tire or wheel requires a new valve stem; a new wheel also requires a new sensor screw.

diagnostics.finding: A sensor does not respond to the activation tool.
diagnostics.meaning: The first unsuccessful attempt does not establish sensor failure.
diagnostics.next: Rotate the wheels at least one-fourth turn and retry, then try the customer activation tool if available. If training still fails, retry with the vehicle doors open.

diagnostics.finding: The activation tool flashes green or beeps.
diagnostics.meaning: Tool feedback does not confirm that the BCM received the sensor transmission.
diagnostics.next: Use the vehicle's training confirmations to establish recognition.

verification.title: Confirm training completion
verification.body: Look for TIRE TRAINING COMPLETE where a message center is fitted. Without one, successful completion means switching ignition off produces no horn sound. Two horn sounds indicate unsuccessful training.

verification.title: Record the trained identifiers
verification.body: Use the scan tool to locate the updated sensor identifiers in the BCM and document them on the applicable warranty claim.

verification.title: Confirm the pressure outcome
verification.body: Verify label pressure with the digital gauge. A warning that remains after adjustment and activation requires further diagnosis.
