Wheel/tire disassembly and assembly, snap-in and bolt-on sensor branches, and protected bead seating.
New-sensor location training, entry methods, completion checks and identifier recording.
Separate sensor wake-up activation and nonresponse follow-up.

guides.title: Diagnose dynamic-suspension warnings and VDM voltage faults
guides.summary: Use suspension fault codes and battery-to-module voltage comparisons to distinguish charging, supply, connection and suspension-control concerns.
guides.introduction: The vehicle dynamics control module (VDM) adjusts magnetic fields inside the dampers to change their resistance to movement. Height sensors and messages about braking, steering and body motion help it choose the damping force. A detected fault can disable this adjustment and leave the suspension feeling firm, so a harsh ride does not automatically mean worn dampers.
guides.why: The VDM needs a stable electrical supply and reliable information. Battery events, poor connections and incomplete configuration can produce suspension warnings without proving that the module or a damper has failed.
searchTerms: VDM not responding to scan tool

when.summary: When a suspension warning, harsh ride, VDM communication failure or relevant diagnostic trouble code is present.
notes: Confirm the current concern before using a component-replacement decision.

prepare.title: Arrange the necessary capability
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, correct flex probes, good inspection lighting and connector information. Programming, calibration and restraint-system connector work require the corresponding capabilities.

prepare.title: Establish dependable power
prepare.detail: Verify battery state of charge exceeds 70%. Inspect battery cables and terminal cleanliness and tightening. Check battery junction box (BJB) fuse 66 (5A) and body control module (BCM) fuse 25 (30A). Review previous repairs and applicable service information.

steps.title: Choose the route from symptoms and codes
steps.body: Retrieve diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). A VDM that will not communicate requires network diagnosis. The DRIVE CONTROL MALFUNCTION SERVICE REQUIRED message or a harsh ride calls for VDM code diagnosis; with no codes, investigate the general suspension. Use the distinctions below to select the appropriate chart action rather than treating every warning as a voltage fault.

steps.title: Confirm low or interrupted supply — Test A
steps.body: P0562:16 and P1794:18 concern low supply voltage; U3006:2F indicates an irregular shutdown and restart, often following sudden power loss. Clear the VDM codes, switch ignition off and on, then self-test. No recurrence can reflect an earlier low battery. If a code returns, apply A2's combined check for voltage codes elsewhere and charging codes in the powertrain control module (PCM). A matching result redirects to charging diagnosis; otherwise perform the battery condition test. A failed battery follows the replacement route.

steps.title: Compare reported voltage with measured voltage — A4–A6
steps.body: With ignition on, record battery voltage and compare it with the VDM_Supply_V parameter identification (PID) value. Agreement within 0.2 volt leads to A7. Otherwise follow A5's ignition sequence, disconnect C4585 and check supplies at pins 16 and 32 against battery voltage. Both must be within 1 volt. A failed supply requires fuse checks, then open/high-resistance circuit repair or investigation of a short if a fuse has failed. A6 checks ground pin 47: below 3 ohms leads to A8; otherwise repair the ground circuit.

steps.title: Check overcharging — B1–B2
steps.body: For P0563:17 or P1794:17, first apply B1's cross-module voltage-code and PCM charging-code check. If it does not redirect diagnosis, switch off lights and accessories, then run the engine at approximately 1,500 RPM for 3 minutes while monitoring battery voltage. A reading of 13–15.2 volts leads to B3; otherwise diagnose charging. Do not exceed 2,000 RPM: if that happens, stop and restart the engine before repeating this check.

steps.title: Determine whether high-voltage codes recur — B3
steps.body: Switch ignition off and on, clear VDM codes, switch off and on again, then run the VDM self-test. If P0563:17 or P1794:17 returns, continue to B4. If neither returns, the earlier record may have resulted from battery charging or jump starting.

steps.title: Confirm connections before condemning the VDM
steps.body: At A7 or B4, switch ignition off and inspect the specified VDM and in-line connectors. Replace corroded connectors or terminals, clean module pins and replace damaged, bent, pushed-out or spread terminals as appropriate. At A8 or B5, reconnect and latch everything, then operate the system. If the concern remains, follow an applicable technical service bulletin; without one, the branch directs VDM replacement. If it clears, address the connection's root cause.

steps.title: Complete programming and calibration when required
steps.body: A new VDM needs vehicle-specific programming. Calibration is also required after replacement, disassembly, disconnection or removal of the VDM, a height sensor, front or rear lower control arm, front strut or rear shock. Neutralize the suspension by driving a short distance, then calibrate using the scan tool with the vehicle stationary, level and empty of passengers and cargo. Do not calibrate while raised or immediately after lowering.

watchFor.title: Restraint-module connector precautions
watchFor.body: For U0452:68 connector inspection, switch ignition off and wait one minute before disconnecting the specified connectors. Follow the restraint-system diagnostic requirements.

watchFor.title: Misleading electrical readings
watchFor.body: Voltage on a circuit can corrupt resistance readings. A normal unloaded supply reading also cannot exclude excessive resistance; follow the complete diagnostic branch.

notes: The linked charging-system procedure is specifically for the 5.2L engine. Charging diagnosis on another engine requires its matching procedure.

diagnostics.finding: A corner-specific damper-solenoid circuit DTC is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The chart distinguishes shorts to ground or battery, opens, excessive current and abnormal resistance. Wiring, connectors, the damper assembly or VDM can be responsible.
diagnostics.next: Use Test C. Check harness routing, damage and connector contamination. The solenoid is serviced with the shock or strut.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B14C1:64 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Damper temperature information has failed a plausibility check.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test D.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code C1121:4B is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A damper-solenoid overtemperature condition is reported.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose other damper-solenoid codes first. Clear the code, cycle ignition on–off–on and self-test. If it returns, inspect struts and rear shocks for leakage or damage and replace affected components as necessary.

diagnostics.finding: A height-sensor or sensor-supply circuit DTC is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The chart separates affected corners, supply-voltage faults, shorts, opens, stuck signals and implausible signals.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test E.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code C1124:55 or C1124:56 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Height-sensor configuration is missing or incompatible; these codes are automatically set in a new VDM.
diagnostics.next: Calibrate the VDM and sensors using scan-tool instructions, clear codes and repeat the self-test.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code C103E:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: With all four height sensors correctly configured and no height-sensor codes, unchanged height information indicates the shipping-block condition.
diagnostics.next: Remove the shipping blocks from the front struts and rear shock absorbers.

diagnostics.meaning: Configuration or software faults can follow incomplete programmable module installation (PMI).
diagnostics.next: Check service history. After recent VDM work, repeat PMI and height calibration. Without recent VDM service, follow the new-VDM route for failure to retain configuration.

diagnostics.meaning: Communication is lost with the anti-lock brake system (ABS) module, Gateway Module A (GWM) or restraints control module (RCM), respectively.
diagnostics.next: Use Tests G, F or H respectively.

diagnostics.meaning: Invalid information concerns ABS steering/braking data, gateway engine/body/cluster data or RCM vehicle-motion data, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Retrieve and diagnose the originating module's codes. If it cannot communicate, use network diagnosis. With no originating codes, follow the listed VDM, source-module and in-line connector inspections for an intermittent concern.

diagnostics.meaning: The VDM reports a watchdog, software-supervision or internal-electronic fault.
diagnostics.next: Clear codes, run the VDM self-test and record all results. Replace the VDM if the relevant code returns.

diagnostics.finding: U3000:4B or U3000:98 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Calculated VDM temperature is excessive, potentially because of ambient conditions or internal current.
diagnostics.next: Switch ignition off and allow at least 30 minutes of cooling. Clear codes, self-test and record results. Diagnose other VDM codes first; replace the VDM if the thermal code returns.

verification.title: Check operation after correction
verification.body: Confirm connectors are seated and latched, operate the system and repeat the required VDM self-test. Where calibration was necessary, complete it before judging the final result.

verification.title: Keep a useful diagnostic record
verification.body: Record battery voltage, the VDM PID comparison, relevant circuit readings and all returned DTCs. Distinguish a nonrecurring battery-event code from a fault that persists after testing.

applicability.equipment: Vehicle dynamic suspension with magneto-rheological dampers

guides.title: Diagnose adaptive damper and gateway faults, and check height-sensor wiring
guides.summary: Use suspension self-tests and targeted electrical measurements to distinguish damper, wiring and gateway faults, with defined stopping points for height-sensor checks.
guides.introduction: The vehicle dynamics control module (VDM) adjusts damping through electromagnetic coils inside the struts and rear shocks. Their magnetic field changes resistance to fluid flow. Height sensors and messages from other modules tell the VDM how the vehicle is moving. These tests separate electrical and communication problems that can interrupt that control and leave the suspension feeling firm.
guides.why: A fault code identifies a detected condition, not necessarily a failed component. Wiring resistance can affect both damper operation and estimated temperature, while missing network messages can originate outside the suspension system.

when.summary: When suspension self-tests identify damper, height-sensor or gateway communication faults.
notes: Confirm the concern is present before following a component-replacement decision.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a capable scan tool, digital multimeter, good lighting, Rotunda Flex Probes and the specified connector diagrams. This work requires confident terminal identification and controlled ignition-on voltage testing.

prepare.title: Establish reliable starting conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge greater than 70%. Review previous repairs and related module codes. Inspect harness routing, damage and contamination; check height-sensor linkages are connected correctly.

prepare.title: Control measurement conditions
prepare.detail: Follow each test's ignition and connector-disconnection instructions. For on-vehicle solenoid resistance measurements, allow the vehicle to cool to garage ambient temperature.

steps.title: Choose the correct diagnostic branch
steps.body: With ignition on, run the VDM self-test. Use Test C for damper circuit codes, Test D for B14C1:64, Test E for height-sensor codes and Test F for U0146:00. Repair damper circuit faults before investigating temperature plausibility. Other codes follow the VDM diagnostic trouble code (DTC) chart.

steps.title: Test the damper wiring
steps.body: Follow [Test C](#/document/G1694674): C110X:11 or C110X:1A leads to C2 ground-short checks; C110X:12 to C3 voltage checks; C110X:13, C110X:19 or C110X:1B to C4 continuity checks. Disconnect VDM C4585 and the suspect damper with ignition off. C2 requires greater than 10,000 ohms to ground; C3 uses ignition on and requires no voltage; C4 requires less than 3 ohms end-to-end. Passing branches reach C5: ignition off, resistance between the isolated conductors must exceed 10,000 ohms. Repair failing circuits.

steps.title: Separate a coil fault from a connection fault
steps.body: At C6, measure across the specified component-side solenoid terminals with ignition off. Resistance between 1 and 3 ohms advances to C7 connector inspection; outside that range directs replacement of the affected front strut or rear shock. Inspect all related connectors, repair defects, then complete C8 using the reconnection and operating check below.

steps.title: Investigate damper temperature plausibility
steps.body: When B14C1:64 is the only code, [Test D](#/document/G1694674) checks connectors at D2 before measuring solenoid resistance at D3. The acceptable range is again between 1 and 3 ohms. A failed measurement directs strut or shock replacement followed by scan-tool Damper Cold Start Initialization. Passing measurements lead to the D4 operating check.

steps.title: Check height-sensor insulation and continuity
steps.body: In [Test E](#/document/G1694674), ground/open, stuck-signal, plausibility and C1B14:16 concerns enter E2. With ignition off, disconnect C4585 and the suspect sensors. Each specified sensor terminal must measure greater than 10,000 ohms to ground; then E3 checks each mapped wire for less than 3 ohms end-to-end. On failure, inspect both sensor connectors on the affected axle; repair terminals or, if connectors are sound, the affected circuits. After E3 passes, plausibility faults proceed to E4. Stop C1B14:16 testing at E3; ground/open and stuck-signal branches stop before E5.

steps.title: Record height-sensor voltage observations
steps.body: Battery-short codes and C1B14:17 enter E4 directly. With ignition off, disconnect C4585 and the suspect sensors, then switch ignition on. Record voltage from each specified sensor-connector pin—1, 2 and 3—to ground. This check ends with those observations: do not make an E4 pass/fail decision or continue into E5.

steps.title: Confirm whether gateway communication loss returns
steps.body: For [Test F](#/document/G1694674), run the ignition-on Network Test. If the gateway module (GWM) does not respond, follow Communications Network diagnosis. If it passes, run the VDM self-test, clear codes, switch ignition off and on, repeat the self-test and record the results. If U0146:00 does not return, the system is operating correctly at that time.

steps.title: Resolve supply and gateway codes first
steps.body: If U0146:00 returns, review the recorded VDM codes at F3. P0562:16 or P1794:18 directs Test A; P0563:17 or P1794:17 directs Test B. With none present, perform the GWM self-test at F4. Any gateway codes lead to its DTC chart; no codes leads to F5.

steps.title: Check replacement history and other modules
steps.body: At F5, verify recent VDM/GWM replacements have the correct parts and configuration; use as-built data if configuration is suspect. Return swapped modules to their original vehicles and obtain new replacements. Operate the system. If the symptom remains, F6 tests all modules: U0146:xx in another module requires checking OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins before directing GWM replacement. Follow an applicable bulletin instead. Without matching codes elsewhere, continue to F7.

steps.title: Complete the damper or gateway operating check
steps.body: F7 inspects all VDM and related in-line connectors with ignition off. For C8, D4 or F8, reconnect the applicable connectors securely, confirm their latches engage and operate the system. If the concern remains, check OASIS for applicable bulletins; follow one if available, otherwise the test directs VDM replacement. If operation recovers, address the underlying connector fault.

watchFor.title: Terminal defects
watchFor.body: Renew corroded connectors or terminals and clean module pins. Replace damaged, bent or pushed-out pins and spread terminals as necessary.

watchFor.title: Damage caused during testing
watchFor.body: Do not force probes into terminals or apply power or ground directly to module-controlled components. Follow the specified isolated-circuit measurements.

notes: Use the linked connector tables for the correct vehicle corner; damper and height-sensor terminal assignments differ.
Height-sensor observations here do not authorize sensor or module replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B14C1:64 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: One damper's estimated temperature differs implausibly from the others; the estimate depends on harness and solenoid resistance.
diagnostics.next: Resolve damper circuit codes first, then follow Test D.

diagnostics.finding: A height-sensor fault is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The code table distinguishes battery shorts, ground/open faults, absent travel, disagreement between sensors and low or high supply voltage.
diagnostics.next: Use E1 to select the branch and preserve the E3/E4 stopping points.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0146:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The VDM is missing gateway-relayed messages from the body control, instrument cluster or powertrain control module.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test F. A nonreturning code may reflect high network traffic or an intermittent fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0121:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The VDM is missing messages from the anti-lock brake system control module.
diagnostics.next: Treat this as a separate communication concern; the gateway replacement decisions in Test F do not apply.

verification.title: Complete programming and calibration when required
verification.body: Program a new VDM with the correct vehicle information. VDM, height-sensor, strut or rear-shock disconnection or replacement requires VDM calibration. First neutralize the suspension with a short drive; then calibrate using the scan tool on level ground, stationary, without passengers or cargo. Do not calibrate raised or immediately after lowering.

verification.title: Record the outcome accurately
verification.body: Retain measurements, repaired connector locations and the operating-check result. For Test F, record the codes retrieved after clearing and cycling the ignition. For height-sensor work, record the stopping point and observations without claiming the fault is resolved.

guides.title: Diagnose adaptive suspension communication codes U0121:00 and U0151:00
guides.summary: Trace missing brake or restraints-module messages through network, configuration and connector checks before selecting a module repair.
guides.introduction: The vehicle dynamics control module (VDM) adjusts magnetic-fluid dampers using sensor and network information. The anti-lock brake system (ABS) module supplies braking and steering information; the restraints control module (RCM) supplies vehicle-motion measurements. Missing information can affect suspension control, and some faults produce a firm ride.
guides.why: A communication code identifies missing information. Network faults, supply problems, incorrect configuration and poor connections must be separated before replacing the sending module or VDM.

when.summary: Use when the VDM records U0121:00 or U0151:00 on a vehicle with adaptive damping.

prepare.title: Diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Have a scan tool capable of network tests, module self-tests, configuration and VDM calibration, plus wiring diagrams and a good inspection light. Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%.

prepare.title: Service information and access
prepare.detail: Review recent module work and arrange access to Ford service bulletins and as-built configuration data. Any restraints-system follow-up requires the linked airbag procedures and appropriate service capability.

steps.title: Identify the missing participant
steps.body: With ignition on, run the Network Test. Test G checks whether the ABS module responds; Test H checks the RCM. A nonresponding module leads to Communications Network diagnosis before continuing.

steps.title: Establish whether the code returns
steps.body: Run the VDM self-test, clear diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), switch ignition off and on, then repeat the self-test and record its results. If the relevant communication code does not return, the system operates correctly at this time; high network traffic or an intermittent fault may explain the earlier code.

steps.title: Resolve prerequisite faults
steps.body: If the code returns, review VDM codes first. P0562:16 or P1794:18 directs you to Test A; P0563:17 or P1794:17 directs you to Test B. Otherwise, self-test the ABS module for Test G or RCM for Test H. Diagnose any codes there before proceeding.

steps.title: Check previous module replacement
steps.body: Verify correct parts and configuration after recent VDM, ABS or RCM work. Suspect programmable module installation (PMI) requires configuration using as-built data. Return a module borrowed from another vehicle and obtain a new replacement. Operate the system again; a resolved symptom can indicate incorrect replacement or configuration.

steps.title: Compare reports from other modules
steps.body: If the symptom remains, self-test all modules. Look for U0121:xx in other modules for Test G, or U0151:xx for Test H. If found, check Ford's OASIS service-information system for applicable technical service bulletins and follow one if available. Without an applicable bulletin, this branch specifies a new ABS module for G or RCM for H.

steps.title: Inspect the VDM connections
steps.body: If no other module reports the matching communication fault, switch ignition off and disconnect VDM and related inline connectors. Inspect for corrosion, bent or damaged pins, pushed-out pins and spread terminals. Replace defective connector parts as directed and clean corroded module pins.

steps.title: Reconnect and reassess
steps.body: Reconnect every connector fully, ensuring it seats and latches, then operate the system. If the concern remains, check applicable bulletins; follow one if available, otherwise this branch specifies a new VDM. If operation recovers, address the underlying connector or terminal problem.

steps.title: Complete required VDM setup
steps.body: A new VDM requires scan-tool programming. VDM disconnection or replacement also requires calibration. Neutralize the suspension with a short drive first, then calibrate on level ground, stationary and without passengers or cargo. Do not calibrate while raised or immediately after lowering.

watchFor.title: A disappearing fault
watchFor.body: A code that fails to return does not justify continuing to a module-replacement verdict.

watchFor.title: Temporary connector recovery
watchFor.body: Reseating can restore communication while corrosion or poor terminal contact still needs correction.

notes: Keep each test's sending module consistent throughout: ABS for Test G, RCM for Test H.

diagnostics.finding: The VDM records diagnostic trouble code U0121:00.
diagnostics.meaning: Test G addresses communication with the ABS module.
diagnostics.next: Begin with its Network Test response, then follow the repeat-code and fault-priority checks.

diagnostics.finding: The VDM records diagnostic trouble code U0151:00.
diagnostics.meaning: Required RCM messages are missing from the high-speed controller area network.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test H, including RCM self-test results and the comparison with other modules.

verification.title: Confirm operation
verification.body: Operate the system at the specified reassessment points and establish whether the original observable concern remains.

verification.title: Keep a diagnostic record
verification.body: Record the repeated VDM self-test results, other modules' matching codes, and required programming or calibration completion.

Diagnose restraints-system codes found during Test H.
ABS module removal and installation only at the supported Test G replacement endpoint.
RCM removal and installation only at the supported Test H replacement endpoint.
VDM removal and installation after connector checks and bulletin review identify that endpoint.
Suspension network operation and required VDM programming and calibration conditions.

guides.title: Replace and calibrate a front suspension height sensor
guides.summary: Refit the correct side-specific height sensor with its linkage vertical, then calibrate the adaptive suspension at its settled ride height.
guides.introduction: A front suspension height sensor converts suspension movement into a changing voltage signal. The vehicle dynamics control module (VDM) combines height-sensor information with other vehicle inputs to control damping at each wheel. Replacing or reconnecting a sensor therefore involves both a mechanical installation and a calibration that teaches the system the vehicle's zero position.
guides.why: Sensor orientation affects the relationship between suspension movement and the signal reaching the control module. The linkage must be vertical after installation to avoid component damage or failure. Calibration also depends on the vehicle's physical position: suspension that has just been lowered from a hoist has not yet settled into the required neutral position.

when.summary: When diagnosis calls for sensor replacement, or a removed or disconnected sensor is being refitted.
notes: Calibration is required after sensor removal or disconnection, including when the original sensor is reused.

prepare.title: Provide lifting and fastening capability
prepare.detail: Use a hoist at the specified lifting points and a torque wrench suitable for the sensor retainers. Keep hoist adapters clear of suspension parts and mounting brackets.

prepare.title: Arrange the complete calibration
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool capable of running Ride Height Calibration, a suitable short driving area and a level surface for the stationary calibration.

prepare.title: Identify the correct assembly
prepare.detail: Confirm which side is being serviced and note the component positions before removal. Left-hand and right-hand sensor assemblies are not interchangeable.

steps.title: Lift and document the installation
steps.body: Position the vehicle on a hoist using the lifting procedure. Note the sensor, bracket and linkage positions so the replacement can reproduce the correct arrangement.

steps.title: Disconnect the sensor and arm bracket
steps.body: Disconnect the sensor electrical connector, then remove the retainer securing the sensor arm bracket to the lower suspension arm. This releases the linkage attachment before the sensor assembly is removed.

steps.title: Remove the sensor assembly
steps.body: Remove the sensor bracket mounting retainer and take out the sensor. Keep the side-specific requirement in mind when selecting the assembly to install.

steps.title: Refit and check linkage orientation
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Tighten both the arm bracket-to-lower arm retainer and the sensor bracket mounting retainer to 177 lb.in (20 Nm). Reconnect the electrical connector and confirm that the linkage is vertical.

steps.title: Settle the suspension
steps.body: Lower the vehicle and drive it a short distance, such as around a parking lot, to neutralize the suspension. Do not perform calibration while the vehicle is raised or immediately after lowering it.

steps.title: Learn the zero position
steps.body: Place the vehicle on a level surface, stationary and without passengers or cargo. Connect the scan tool, select Ride Height Calibration and follow its directions through completion.

watchFor.title: Linkage installed at an angle
watchFor.body: Correct a nonvertical linkage before proceeding. Calibration does not compensate for an installation that can damage the mechanism.

notes: The illustration shows the left-hand assembly. The right-hand procedure is similar, but the assemblies remain side specific.

diagnostics.finding: A suspension warning message or unusually firm ride is present.
diagnostics.meaning: Depending on the detected fault, the VDM can deactivate dynamic suspension and produce a firm feel. This does not identify a height sensor as the failed part.
diagnostics.next: Establish the system fault before deciding to replace the sensor.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical completion
verification.body: Check the correct-side assembly, vertical linkage, secured retainers and connected electrical connector.

verification.title: Record calibration completion
verification.body: Record the side serviced and the scan tool's calibration result. An interrupted or unsuccessful routine leaves the required zero-position learning incomplete.

procedures.purpose: Front height sensor removal, side-specific installation, retainer tightening and required Ride Height Calibration.
Height-sensor operation and the settling, loading and level-surface prerequisites for zero-position calibration.
Vehicle lifting points and hoist-positioning precautions.

guides.title: Replace and calibrate a rear suspension height sensor
guides.summary: Install the correct-side rear height sensor with its linkage vertical, then perform scan-tool Ride Height Calibration.
guides.introduction: The rear suspension height sensor follows suspension movement through a linked arm and returns a variable voltage to the vehicle dynamics control module (VDM). The module combines height information with other vehicle signals to control adaptive damper force. Replacing the sensor restores this measurement point; calibration then teaches the system the vehicle's settled zero position.
guides.why: The left and right sensors are side-specific, and the linkage must stand vertically after installation to avoid damage or failure. Calibration also depends on the vehicle's physical condition: a suspension freshly lowered from a hoist has not necessarily settled into its neutral position.

when.summary: When diagnosis requires rear height sensor replacement, or sensor removal or disconnection requires recalibration.
notes: Calibration is required after a height sensor is installed new, disassembled, disconnected or removed.
A firm suspension feel or warning message alone does not prove a height sensor has failed.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and fastening capability
prepare.detail: Use a hoist following the designated lifting points and stamped-triangle locations. Keep adapters clear of suspension, brackets and other vulnerable components. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare the correct sensor and scan tool
prepare.detail: Identify the side being serviced and obtain its matching sensor assembly. Have torque equipment and a scan tool capable of running Ride Height Calibration.

prepare.title: Plan calibration conditions
prepare.detail: Provide a level surface, an unloaded vehicle and space for a short settling drive. Calibration requires the vehicle to be stationary with no passengers or cargo.

steps.title: Lift the vehicle and record the arrangement
steps.body: Follow the [lifting procedure](#/document/G1663631). Before removal, note the sensor, bracket and linkage positions. The [sensor procedure](#/document/G1694677) illustrates the left side; the right follows a similar removal sequence.

steps.title: Remove the sensor assembly
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector. Remove the sensor arm bracket-to-lower-arm bolt, then remove the sensor bracket bolt and take out the assembly. Keeping this order releases the electrical connection and linkage before the sensor mounting.

steps.title: Install the correct-side assembly
steps.body: Reverse removal with the sensor intended for that side. Tighten both the sensor bracket bolt and the arm bracket-to-lower-arm bolt to 177 lb.in (20 Nm). Reconnect the electrical plug. Ensure the linkage is vertical after installation.

steps.title: Settle the suspension
steps.body: Lower the vehicle and drive it a short distance, such as around a parking lot, to neutralize the suspension. Do not calibrate with the vehicle raised or immediately after lowering it.

steps.title: Run Ride Height Calibration
steps.body: Place the settled vehicle on a level surface, stationary and without passengers or cargo. Connect the scan tool, select Ride Height Calibration and follow its directions. The [suspension operating description](#/document/G1694672) explains these required zero-position learning conditions.

watchFor.title: Incorrect side or linkage angle
watchFor.body: Left and right assemblies cannot be interchanged. A linkage that is not vertical requires correction before the repair is complete.

watchFor.title: Calibrating an unsettled vehicle
watchFor.body: Skipping the settling drive or leaving passengers or cargo in the vehicle prevents the required calibration conditions from being met.

notes: Reinstalling the original sensor after removal still requires calibration.

diagnostics.finding: The suspension feels firm and a suspension message appears.
diagnostics.meaning: Depending on the diagnostic trouble code, the VDM may have disabled dynamic suspension. Its electrical checks include height sensors, their circuits and damper coil circuits.
diagnostics.next: Read and diagnose the recorded fault before deciding that the height sensor itself requires replacement.

verification.title: Mechanical installation
verification.body: Confirm the correct-side sensor is installed, both bolts are tightened, the connector is engaged and the linkage is vertical.

verification.title: Record calibration completion
verification.body: Record successful completion of the scan-tool routine with the vehicle settled, level, stationary and unloaded. An incomplete routine leaves the calibration requirement outstanding.

procedures.purpose: Rear suspension height sensor removal, side-specific installation and Ride Height Calibration.
Required lifting-point and hoist-positioning guidance.
VDM sensor operation, suspension fault behavior and required calibration conditions.

guides.title: Replace and calibrate the vehicle dynamics control module
guides.summary: Remove the vehicle dynamics control module through the load-space trim, program a new module and complete ride-height calibration.
guides.introduction: The vehicle dynamics control module (VDM) controls the firmness of the adaptive suspension dampers. It combines suspension-height measurements with information about braking, steering and vehicle movement, then varies electrical current to each damper. That current changes a magnetic field inside the damper, restricting fluid flow to adjust damping. Replacement therefore involves both fitting the module and preparing its electronic control system for the vehicle.
guides.why: A new module needs the correct vehicle information, and calibration teaches the system its reference suspension position. These are different tasks. Calibration with the suspension hanging, freshly lowered or carrying passengers or cargo can establish an unsuitable reference. Static electrical discharge can also damage the module during handling.

when.summary: When VDM replacement is justified by diagnosis, or the module must be removed and refitted.
notes: Calibration is required after VDM removal or disconnection as well as replacement.
A firm ride or suspension message does not, by itself, identify a failed VDM.

prepare.title: Provide electronic service capability
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool capable of new-module programming and the Ride Height Calibration routine. Follow its instructions for both operations.

prepare.title: Protect the module
prepare.detail: Use handling precautions that prevent static electrical charges from reaching the module.

prepare.title: Plan access and calibration conditions
prepare.detail: Access is through the load-space floor, rear trim and right-hand side trim. Arrange a level calibration location and a short drive to settle the suspension beforehand.

steps.title: Expose the module
steps.body: Remove the load-space floor panel and rear trim panel, then position the right-hand load-space trim aside. This provides access to the electrical connector and module retainers.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the VDM
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector, remove the retainers and remove the module. Maintain static-discharge precautions while handling the exposed unit.

steps.title: Install the module and restore the trim
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Secure the VDM retainers to 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm), reconnect the electrical connector and restore the displaced and removed load-space panels.

steps.title: Program a new module
steps.body: When fitting a new VDM, use the diagnostic scan tool to program the correct vehicle information. Follow all tool directions; ride-height calibration does not replace this configuration step.

steps.title: Settle the suspension
steps.body: Before calibration, neutralize the suspension by driving a short distance, such as around a parking lot. Do not calibrate with the vehicle raised or immediately after lowering it.

steps.title: Carry out ride-height calibration
steps.body: Place the vehicle stationary on a level surface with no passengers or cargo. Connect the scan tool and run Ride Height Calibration, following its directions through completion.

watchFor.title: Incorrect calibration conditions
watchFor.body: Suspension position must be neutral before the system learns its reference. Lifting history, vehicle movement or an added load can interfere with that condition.

watchFor.title: Skipped programming
watchFor.body: A physically installed new module still requires the correct vehicle information for proper suspension operation.

notes: The VDM also monitors height-sensor and damper-coil circuits during its initial electrical check when the ignition is switched on.

diagnostics.finding: A suspension message appears and the ride becomes firm.
diagnostics.meaning: A detected system fault may cause the VDM to deactivate dynamic suspension. Sensors, damper coils and their circuits are among the monitored parts; this response does not prove a module defect.
diagnostics.next: Use the diagnostic trouble codes and appropriate system diagnosis to establish the repair before replacing the VDM.

verification.title: Confirm electronic completion
verification.body: Record successful new-module programming when applicable and the scan tool's completed Ride Height Calibration result.

verification.title: Confirm physical completion
verification.body: Check that the connector is reconnected, module retainers are tightened and the load-space trim and floor panel are restored.

procedures.purpose: VDM access, removal, installation, retainer tightening and required Ride Height Calibration.
Dynamic-suspension operation, new-VDM programming requirements and the conditions required for valid ride-height calibration.

guides.title: Diagnose driveshaft clunks, shudder and cruising vibration
guides.summary: Use the operating conditions of a driveline noise or vibration to choose joint, support, angle, balance and runout checks.
guides.introduction: The driveshaft carries turning force from the transmission to the rear axle. Its joints accommodate driveline angles, while its support and balance help it rotate smoothly. This diagnosis separates looseness, binding, alignment and rotational faults so that a clunk or vibration leads to a relevant inspection rather than an assumed replacement.
guides.why: Different faults can produce similar sensations. Joint play can become noticeable as drive takes up, while incorrect angles, imbalance or a damaged support can disturb rotation. The circumstances in which the symptom occurs are therefore part of the evidence.
searchTerms: clunk moving off after a stop

when.summary: When a verified driveline clunk, buzz, rumble, shudder or cruising vibration needs investigation.
notes: Confirm the reported condition before using the symptom chart to justify component replacement.

prepare.title: Describe the operating condition
prepare.detail: Establish whether the concern occurs during direction changes, moving off, acceleration, cruising or deceleration. Review previous repairs and applicable service information.

prepare.title: Arrange inspection and measurement access
prepare.detail: Plan safe underbody access and the capability to inspect joints, rotate the driveshaft and perform the linked angle, runout and balance procedures. Obtain their specifications before making adjustments.

steps.title: Verify the concern and inspect for obvious damage
steps.body: Confirm the reported symptom, then visually inspect for obvious mechanical or electrical damage. Correct an evident cause where possible before proceeding. If the cause remains unclear, select the matching condition in the [driveshaft symptom chart](#/document/G2214728).

steps.title: Investigate clunks and take-up noises
steps.body: For a loud clunk from reverse to drive, inspect the constant-velocity (CV) joint and universal joint for wear or damage. A clunk as the vehicle moves forward after stopping particularly directs attention to excessive joint play. Confirmed wear or damage can require a new driveshaft.

steps.title: Separate binding from angle-related shudder
steps.body: Grunting with shudder from a complete stop points toward joint binding. Acceleration shudder from low speed or rest has two routes: check driveline angles, and inspect the joints and coupling shaft for wear or damage. Use the findings to select correction or driveshaft replacement.

steps.title: Follow the buzz and coast-noise branches
steps.body: A buzz unchanged between cruising and coasting calls for [driveline angle measurement](#/document/G2214729). A rumble or boom during deceleration, generally related to driveshaft speed over a broad speed range, calls for inspection for shaft damage, missing balance weights or undercoating.

steps.title: Work through cruising-vibration causes
steps.body: Inspect the center-bearing support insulator for wear or damage and rotate the shaft to check for roughness. Inspect axle pinion-flange bolts and tighten them to the specified value where required. Check pinion-flange runout, shaft balance and runout, joint condition and driveline angles through their respective procedures.

steps.title: Carry out the repair supported by the findings
steps.body: Use [runout and balancing](#/document/G2214730) for rotational measurement and balance work. Use [driveshaft removal and installation](#/document/G2214904) when the chart calls for replacement. Follow the applicable specifications for flange runout, angles and fasteners; the symptom alone does not establish the required repair.

watchFor.title: Visible balance clues
watchFor.body: Missing weights, shaft damage and undercoating are specifically identified inspection findings when imbalance is suspected.

watchFor.title: Several possible vibration sources
watchFor.body: A cruising vibration also warrants support, flange, joint and angle checks, even when imbalance seems plausible.

notes: The chart directs driveshaft replacement where necessary for joint or support faults; it does not provide a separate joint-rebuilding process.

diagnostics.finding: Damaged support insulator or rough rotation
diagnostics.meaning: The center-bearing support is a possible source of cruising vibration.
diagnostics.next: Follow the driveshaft replacement route as necessary.

diagnostics.finding: Excessive measured runout
diagnostics.meaning: The rotating shaft or pinion flange deviates excessively from its intended rotational path.
diagnostics.next: Apply the appropriate shaft procedure or flange specification and repair according to the findings.

verification.title: Recheck the original condition
verification.body: Confirm whether the reported noise or vibration remains under the operating condition used to identify it.

verification.title: Record the evidence
verification.body: Document joint and support findings, measured angles or runout where checked, and the correction made against the applicable specification.

procedures.purpose: Initial inspection and symptom-based driveshaft diagnosis.
Concern verification and preliminary diagnostic practices.
Driveshaft removal, installation and applicable flange-fastener requirements.
Driveline angle measurement for buzz, shudder or vibration.
Driveshaft runout measurement and balancing investigation.

guides.title: Overhaul the driveshaft universal joint
guides.summary: Renew the universal joint with a complete matched kit while preserving driveshaft orientation and protecting the shaft from damage.
guides.introduction: The driveshaft universal joint transfers rotation between yokes while allowing their angle to change. Its bearing cups support the joint inside the yokes. This job removes the driveshaft, presses out the cups, cleans and inspects their seating surfaces, and installs a complete joint kit. It requires controlled bench work as well as the capability to remove and reinstall the driveshaft.
guides.why: Driveshaft condition and component orientation matter to smooth, reliable operation. Incorrect reassembly can introduce imbalance, while clamping the shaft in a vise can dent or locally fracture it. The specified pressing tool removes the bearing cups without using the driveshaft tube as a clamping surface.

when.summary: When a driveshaft universal joint requires renewal and the shaft is ready for controlled bench disassembly.
notes: This is a joint overhaul procedure; it does not establish the cause of a driveline complaint.

prepare.title: Arrange vehicle access and bench equipment
prepare.detail: Have the equipment and capability required by the driveshaft removal procedure, plus Installer/Remover, C-Frame and Screw 205-086 (T74P-4635-C). Arrange the work without clamping the driveshaft assembly in a vise or similar fixture.

prepare.title: Prepare matched replacement parts
prepare.detail: Use a complete universal-joint kit and replacement snap rings. Keep kit components together; components from different kits must not be mixed.

steps.title: Remove the driveshaft
steps.body: Follow [Driveshaft removal and installation](#/document/G2214904) to remove the assembly. This provides access for the controlled pressing operations described in the joint procedure.

steps.title: Mark the original relationship
steps.body: Before separating components, index-mark the driveshaft for reassembly. These marks preserve the original relationship between parts. Remove and discard the snap rings after marking.

steps.title: Press out the bearing cups
steps.body: Follow the illustrated sequence in [universal-joint disassembly](#/document/G2214732). Use tool 205-086 to press out the cups and remove the driveshaft yoke, then press out the remaining cups and remove the joint. Do not substitute vise clamping of the shaft for the specified operation.

steps.title: Clean and inspect the cup surfaces
steps.body: Clean and inspect the bearing-cup surfaces before assembly. This exposes their condition rather than enclosing dirt or visible damage beneath the replacement cups.

steps.title: Assemble and reinstall
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence using [universal-joint assembly](#/document/G2214732). Install the joint kit as a complete assembly, retain the indexed orientation, and use new snap rings. Reinstall the driveshaft through its separate removal and installation procedure.

watchFor.title: Damage from holding fixtures
watchFor.body: Never clamp the driveshaft assembly in vise jaws or a similar fixture. Local damage can lead to driveshaft failure in service.

watchFor.title: Lost orientation
watchFor.body: Do not treat index marks as optional: incorrect component orientation can create imbalance.

notes: The pressing illustration shows the specified C-frame tool acting at a bearing cup; it does not authorize clamping the shaft elsewhere.

diagnostics.finding: Index marks are absent or no longer readable.
diagnostics.meaning: The intended reassembly relationship has not been established.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the component orientation before assembly rather than guessing.

verification.title: Confirm assembly details
verification.body: Check that the cup surfaces were cleaned and inspected, the kit remained complete, the index marks were followed, and discarded snap rings were replaced.

verification.title: Complete vehicle installation
verification.body: Finish the driveshaft installation using its linked procedure, including its attachment requirements.

procedures.purpose: Universal-joint bench disassembly and assembly, including indexing, bearing-cup pressing, inspection and complete-kit installation.
Driveshaft removal before bench work and installation after joint assembly.

guides.title: Measure driveshaft operating angles on the 5.2L Mustang
guides.summary: Measure the driveshaft's angular relationships under controlled ride-height conditions and use the results to direct mounting or suspension inspection.
guides.introduction: Driveline angularity describes the relationship between the engine crankshaft, driveshaft and rear axle pinion. A joint's operating angle is the difference between the directions of the components it connects. Incorrect geometry can cause vibration or shudder, even when the shaft itself has not been identified as faulty. This procedure establishes the geometry and directs inspection when the readings fall outside the stated targets.
guides.why: Ride height, spring condition and mounting positions affect the readings. Joint faults must be checked first, and a shaft's slope must be related to the correct reference surface. A reading taken with the wrong zero or with the suspension in the wrong position can lead to an incorrect repair decision.

when.summary: When investigating vibration or shudder that may involve incorrect driveline angles.
notes: Inspect universal joints and constant-velocity joints before assessing angularity.
Choose measurement locations for the actual transmission, joint arrangement and single-piece or multiple-piece shaft.

prepare.title: Establish the specified vehicle position
prepare.detail: Use a level surface, such as a drive-on hoist or alignment rack. Keep the vehicle unloaded, inflate all tires to their normal operating pressures and verify that curb-position ride height is within specification.

prepare.title: Prepare the angle-measuring equipment
prepare.detail: Use Anglemaster II Driveline Inclinometer/Protractor 164-R2402. Identify clean reference surfaces and provide a record for reference locations, slope directions and operating-angle results.

steps.title: Check the joints before measuring geometry
steps.body: Inspect universal joints, commonly called U-joints, and constant-velocity joints, or CV joints, for correct operation. Address an identified joint problem before treating an angle measurement as an explanation for the complaint.

steps.title: Select and establish the end references
steps.body: Follow the illustrated branches in the [angle measurement procedure](#/document/G2214729). For flex-coupling/CV-joint arrangements with a manual transmission, establish the transmission reference at the drain plug using ALT-ZERO. The axle reference is a clean, flat drive-axle surface. Keep each measurement associated with its reference. The fluid-pan-bolt calibration branch is conditional on an automatic transmission; it is not a reason to assume that equipment is fitted.

steps.title: Measure the front and rear relationships
steps.body: Measure the driveshaft slope at the illustrated front and rear positions using the appropriate reference. The single-piece-shaft branch also requires front and rear operating-angle measurements. Preserve the reference and slope direction in the record so the two ends can be assessed correctly.

steps.title: Measure the center joint when fitted
steps.body: For a multiple-piece shaft, rotate it until the flange U-joint cup is parallel with the floor. Zero the instrument on a clean shaft section ahead of the center support bearing, then measure behind the center-support-bearing U-joint at the indicated location. That relative reading establishes the center joint's operating angle.

steps.title: Calculate and compare the operating angles
steps.body: When connected components slope in the same direction, subtract the smaller slope from the larger. When they slope in opposite directions, add the measurements. For U-joint connections, the stated ideal is angles equal or within one degree of each other, a maximum operating angle of 3 degrees and at least one-half degree of continuous operating angle.

steps.title: Direct corrective inspection from the result
steps.body: If the angle is outside specification, inspect the engine and transmission mounts, center-support-bearing mounting, rear suspension, rear axle and its mounting, and frame for wear or damage. Repair or adjust the identified condition to obtain the correct angle.

watchFor.title: An uncontrolled ride-height condition
watchFor.body: Load, tire pressure and ride height influence angularity. Establish the required conditions before using readings to authorize corrective work.

watchFor.title: Lost slope direction or reference
watchFor.body: An unsigned number alone can obscure whether slopes should be added or subtracted.

notes: The stated U-joint targets describe the angle between connected yokes, rather than an isolated shaft's slope relative to the floor.

diagnostics.finding: A U-joint or CV joint does not operate correctly.
diagnostics.meaning: The preliminary joint check has identified a condition requiring attention.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the joint condition before drawing conclusions from angularity.

diagnostics.finding: Operating angles fall outside the stated targets.
diagnostics.meaning: The measured geometry requires correction; the reading does not identify which mounting component is responsible.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the listed mounts, support, suspension, axle and frame, then repair or adjust the cause.

verification.title: Record the geometry and final result
verification.body: Record vehicle setup, reference surfaces, slope directions and calculated operating angles. After correction, repeat the affected measurements under the same setup and record whether the required angular relationships have been achieved.

procedures.purpose: Set up the vehicle, select transmission and shaft-layout measurement branches, calculate operating angles and direct corrective inspection.

guides.title: Check driveshaft runout and balance on the 5.2L
guides.summary: Trace a road-speed-related driveline vibration through inspection, runout measurement and the appropriate driveshaft balancing method.
guides.introduction: The driveshaft carries rotation from the transmission toward the rear axle. A shaft that runs eccentrically or has an uneven mass distribution can produce a floorpan tremor or a rumble, hum or boom. Runout measures how far the rotating shaft departs from a true path; balancing corrects uneven mass distribution. These checks therefore answer different questions.
guides.why: Balancing comes after inspection and runout checks because added weight cannot correct a damaged shaft or an out-of-true mounting flange. Keeping the original tire pressures and vehicle load preserves the baseline complaint. Supporting the driveline near its normal curb-weight position also matters: changing its operating angle can change the condition being investigated.

when.summary: When a repeatable road-speed-related vibration requires driveshaft inspection, runout checking or balancing.
notes: Driveline vibration has a higher frequency and lower amplitude than high-speed shake.
The concern should relate to road speed rather than acceleration or deceleration; it may diminish while coasting in NEUTRAL.

prepare.title: Safe access and measurement
prepare.detail: Use the specified lifting points and a twin-post hoist or frame hoist with jackstands, keeping the shaft near its curb-weight angle. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Have holding fixture and dial indicator 100-002 (TOOL-4201-C).

prepare.title: Choose the balancing capability
prepare.detail: Instrumented balancing requires a Vehicle Communication and Measurement Module (VCMM), Vehicle Measurement System (VMS), accelerometer, reflective tape, photo-tachometer and suitable weights. The alternative method uses hose clamps. Obtain the applicable runout limits through the Specifications reference in the complete procedure.

steps.title: Establish the unchanged baseline
steps.body: Visually inspect the vehicle and reproduce the complaint on a road test before making adjustments. Do not change tire pressures or vehicle load. Note the road speed and character of the vibration for later comparisons.

steps.title: Inspect the shaft and joints
steps.body: Following the [lifting guidance](#/document/G1663631), inspect for damage, undercoating and incorrectly seated universal joints (U-joints). Rotate the shaft slowly by hand, feeling for joint binding or end play. Remove the shaft to inspect slip-yoke splines for galling, dirt, rust or incorrect lubrication. Clean it or replace U-joints as necessary; replace a damaged shaft. Road-test after corrections.

steps.title: Measure persistent vibration concerns
steps.body: Use the [runout procedure](#/document/G2214730) and dial indicator, turning the shaft through the axle. Measure front, center and rear; measure those locations on every section of a multiple-piece shaft. Excessive front or center runout requires shaft replacement. If only rear runout is excessive, mark its high point and continue with indexing.

steps.title: Separate shaft eccentricity from flange effects
steps.body: Mark the shaft-to-pinion-flange relationship, disconnect it, rotate it 180 degrees and reconnect. Recheck rear runout. If still excessive, mark the new high point and compare the marks using the decisions below. If runout becomes acceptable, road-test again. With acceptable shaft, flange and pinion runout but persistent vibration, proceed to balancing.

steps.title: Set up instrumented balancing
steps.body: For the VCMM/VMS method, mount an accelerometer near the transmission or differential end. Clean the shaft for reflective tape and position the photo-tachometer approximately 20 degrees from perpendicular to the tape surface. Keep the sensor fixed throughout testing. Run the first balance test with the shaft unmodified.

steps.title: Apply the correct test-weight branch
steps.body: For tapped pinion flanges, number the holes in the direction of rotation, starting with the top hole. Run the second test with the specified test-weight set screw in hole No. 1, remove it, then install the directed weight combination. For untapped flanges, use the shaft-size-appropriate test weight secured by a metal band near the tube-to-yoke weld. Mark its location and run the second test. Remove that weight and secure the recommended correction weight at the directed position using a metal band and epoxy. Results are referenced to the test-weight location.

steps.title: Verify the instrumented correction
steps.body: After either flange branch, run the third VCMM/VMS test to verify the repair. Keep the measurement setup unchanged so the result can be compared with the earlier tests.

steps.title: Use the hose-clamp method as an alternative
steps.body: Mark four approximately equal sectors near the shaft rear. Test one clamp head at each position at the complaint road speed, choosing the least vibration; equal adjacent results call for a position between them. If vibration persists, add a second clamp at that position. If there is no improvement, move the heads equal distances in opposite directions, initially separating them about 13 mm (1/2 in). Increase separation and retest until the best combination or acceptable vibration is reached. Tighten the clamps in their final positions; they remain installed.

watchFor.title: Restricted indexing positions
watchFor.body: Circular flanges permit quarter-turn positions, half-round flanges only two positions, and six-bolt constant-velocity joint flanges sixth-turn positions.

watchFor.title: Changing measurement conditions
watchFor.body: A moved photo-tachometer or changed test-weight reference undermines the comparison between balance runs.

notes: The full procedure gives test-weight selection details for each flange and shaft-size branch. Aftermarket test weights and clamps are permitted.

diagnostics.finding: The two rear runout high-point marks are within 25 mm (1 in) of each other.
diagnostics.meaning: The driveshaft itself is eccentric.
diagnostics.next: Install a new driveshaft.

diagnostics.finding: The high-point marks are on opposite sides, 180 degrees apart.
diagnostics.meaning: The slip yoke or pinion flange is responsible for the runout pattern.
diagnostics.next: Check pinion-flange runout. Excessive flange runout indicates a bent pinion. If flange and pinion runouts are acceptable, road-test and balance only if vibration persists.

verification.title: Repeat the complaint condition
verification.body: Recheck at the original road-test speed after corrections. Confirm instrumented repairs with the third balance test, or confirm the best hose-clamp result with the clamps securely tightened.

verification.title: Record the comparison
verification.body: Record runout at each measured location, indexing results, balance-test results or final clamp positions, and the vibration observed at the original road speed.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L driveshaft inspection, runout decisions, flange indexing, instrumented balancing and hose-clamp balancing.
Identify approved lifting points and safe vehicle support for underbody inspection and measurement.

guides.title: Remove and refit the driveshaft
guides.summary: Remove the driveshaft while protecting its joints, then restore its indexed position using new attachment bolts.
guides.introduction: The driveshaft carries rotation from the transmission to the rear drive unit (RDU). Its joints accommodate changes in alignment, while a center bearing supports the assembly where fitted. This job involves removing the exhaust for access, disconnecting both ends of the shaft and carefully controlling its weight throughout removal and installation.
guides.why: A disconnected driveshaft can bend its joints farther than they tolerate. The flex coupling must not articulate beyond 4 degrees; universal joints and the constant-velocity (CV) joint must not exceed 15 degrees. Index marks preserve the original flange relationship, while clean, fully seated mating surfaces allow the new bolts to clamp the connections correctly.

when.summary: When the driveshaft requires replacement or removal, or inspection identifies a cracked flex coupling.
notes: Identify the three-bolt flex coupling or four-bolt transmission flange before choosing the installation branch.
Center-bearing operations apply only where that bearing is fitted.

prepare.title: Arrange controlled support
prepare.detail: Provide secure underbody access and support for the driveshaft. An assistant may be needed during removal and is required for the rear-flange installation.

prepare.title: Gather tools and new fasteners
prepare.detail: Have a flat-headed screwdriver, a way to make index marks, suitable torque equipment and new transmission-flange, pinion-flange and, where fitted, center-bearing bolts.

steps.title: Clear the exhaust
steps.body: Remove the muffler and tailpipe using the procedure for the fitted engine. This provides the access needed to support and move the shaft without forcing its joints.

steps.title: Mark and release the rear connection
steps.body: Mark the driveshaft relative to the pinion flange. Remove and discard the flange bolts, support the shaft, then use a flat-headed screwdriver in the pinion-flange slot to separate the connection. A tight coupler may remain engaged until the center-bearing retainers are removed; do not gain clearance by over-articulating the shaft.

steps.title: Disconnect the transmission end
steps.body: For a three-bolt connection, mark the flex coupling relative to the transmission flange. For a four-bolt connection, mark the driveshaft relative to that flange. Remove and discard the applicable bolts, keeping the released end supported.

steps.title: Remove the shaft and inspect the coupling
steps.body: With assistance as needed, remove and discard the center-bearing bolts where fitted, then remove the driveshaft within its joint-angle limits. Inspect the flex coupling, if fitted, and replace it if cracked.

steps.title: Position the shaft and secure the front
steps.body: Follow the installation sequence in the [driveshaft procedure](#/document/G2214904): align the flex coupling and position the shaft to the RDU flange before installing new center-bearing bolts. Align the front index marks and install new bolts for the correct flange type. Do not force the flex-coupling bushing onto the transmission output shaft.

steps.title: Seat the rear flange and restore the exhaust
steps.body: With an assistant supporting the shaft, remove contamination, including blue Loctite, from the mating surfaces. Align the rear index marks and fully seat the shaft in the pinion before starting any bolts. Install new bolts in a star pattern and tighten all attachments to their specified values. Reinstall the engine-specific muffler and tailpipe.

watchFor.title: A hanging shaft
watchFor.body: Maintain support at each release point; allowing an end to drop can exceed a joint's permitted movement.

watchFor.title: Bolts being used to pull the flange together
watchFor.body: The rear connection must already be fully seated before its bolts are started.

notes: The three-bolt and four-bolt transmission connections have different tightening specifications.

diagnostics.finding: Cracks in the fitted flex coupling.
diagnostics.meaning: The coupling does not meet the installation inspection requirement.
diagnostics.next: Replace the flex coupling before reassembly.

verification.title: Check the completed assembly
verification.body: Confirm matching index marks, full rear-flange seating, new required bolts and restored exhaust components.

verification.title: Record fastening completion
verification.body: Record the flange type and confirm that each applicable attachment was tightened to its own specification.

procedures.purpose: Complete driveshaft removal and installation, including flange variants, joint limits and fastener specifications.
Remove and reinstall the muffler and tailpipe on the 2.3L engine.
Remove and reinstall the muffler and tailpipe on the 3.7L engine.
Remove and reinstall the muffler and tailpipe on the 5.0L engine.
Remove and reinstall the muffler and tailpipe on the 5.2L engine.

guides.title: Diagnose rear differential noise, shudder and oil leaks
guides.summary: Use the noise conditions, lubricant level, mounting condition, leak source and gear contact pattern to choose the correct rear-axle repair.
guides.introduction: The rear drive pinion turns the ring gear and differential, which deliver torque to the halfshafts while allowing different wheel speeds during cornering. Noise can originate in gear contact, bearings or mountings; leakage can involve both sealing surfaces and housing pressure. This job identifies the repair path before dismantling or adjusting the axle.
guides.why: The same general complaint can have different causes. Backlash is clearance between meshing gear teeth, while bearing preload establishes the load on the bearings. Incorrect settings can affect noise and tooth contact. A blocked vent can also damage seal lips, so replacing a leaking seal alone may leave the cause in place.

when.summary: When rear-axle noise, a take-up clunk, acceleration shudder or differential lubricant leakage is present.
notes: Verify the conditions that produce the complaint before selecting a repair.

prepare.title: Arrange inspection and adjustment capability
prepare.detail: Provide access to the housing, seals, flange, vent and mountings. Gear-pattern, backlash, preload and driveline-angle work require the equipment and competence specified by their individual procedures.

prepare.title: Identify the differential type
prepare.detail: Establish whether the carrier is Traction-Lok or Torsen before planning internal repair. The Torsen carrier is serviced as an assembly.

steps.title: Start with visible damage
steps.body: Inspect the housing, seals and pinion flange. Correct an obvious confirmed cause where possible. If none is visible, reproduce the symptom and use the [noise and vibration chart](#/document/G2214741).

steps.title: Classify the noise and check lubricant
steps.body: Note whether the sound changes under acceleration, deceleration, turning or initial movement. Check lubricant level using Differential Fluid Level Check and fill to its specification. Low lubricant is a listed possibility for whine and a Reverse-to-Drive clunk.

steps.title: Investigate mountings when the vehicle shudders
steps.body: For grunting or shudder during acceleration, inspect axle and suspension fasteners, mounts, positioning, wear and damage. Tighten or repair as directed by Axle Assembly. Check [driveshaft angles](#/document/G2214729) where the symptom chart calls for it.

steps.title: Trace leakage and check ventilation
steps.body: Clean the leaking area enough to locate its origin, then verify lubricant level. Check the housing vent whenever leakage occurs. Clear a blocked vent; replace it if it cannot be cleared, because trapped pressure promotes seal-lip wear.

steps.title: Inspect the sealing surfaces
steps.body: Examine the pinion seal, flange journal and seal bore for damage or trapped metal. Follow the flange-replacement criteria for seal damage or journal wear; a pinion-seal leak requires a new seal and a vent check. At halfshaft seals, inspect the journal and clean bore, and protect the lip during installation.

steps.title: Assess tooth contact before selecting an adjustment
steps.body: Acceptable drive and coast patterns are centered, clear of the tooth top and free of hard pressure lines. The contact-pattern branches distinguish correct backlash needing a thicker or thinner pinion-position shim from correct pinion position needing increased or decreased backlash. Use the actual pattern and measured setup to select the appropriate adjustment or damaged-gear replacement route.

watchFor.title: Seal damage during shaft installation
watchFor.body: Do not let shaft splines contact the seals. A cut lip, displaced seal spring or damaged bore can create another leak.

notes: A noise description narrows the inspection; it does not prove that a gear or bearing needs replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Howl changes with acceleration or deceleration.
diagnostics.meaning: Contact error, bearing preload or gear damage is possible.
diagnostics.next: Inspect tooth contact and setup; also consider lubricant level and housing damage for general whine.

diagnostics.finding: A loud clunk occurs when changing from Reverse to Drive.
diagnostics.meaning: Low lubricant or excessive backlash is possible.
diagnostics.next: Check fluid level, then measure and adjust backlash as required.

diagnostics.finding: A clunk occurs as the vehicle moves forward after stopping.
diagnostics.meaning: The chart identifies pinion gears as a possible source.
diagnostics.next: Follow the drive-pinion front-bearing inspection route and replace only as established.

diagnostics.finding: Grinding, popping or chatter occurs during turns.
diagnostics.meaning: Differential side gears or pinion gears may be damaged.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the carrier and its serviceable components.

diagnostics.finding: A chuckle occurs on coast, or a knock remains unchanged by load.
diagnostics.meaning: Coast chuckle points toward contact or coast-side tooth damage; a load-independent knock points toward drive-side tooth damage.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the corresponding tooth surfaces and replace the ring-and-pinion set as necessary.

diagnostics.finding: Continuous low-pitched scraping begins at low speed.
diagnostics.meaning: Pinion bearing wear or damage is possible.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the pinion bearings before selecting replacement.

verification.title: Confirm the inspection findings
verification.body: Establish the correct lubricant level, vent condition and exact leak source. Where gear setup was inspected, assess both drive and coast contact.

verification.title: Record the repair decision
verification.body: Record symptom conditions, confirmed defects and any measured backlash or contact-pattern findings, together with the next required procedure.

procedures.purpose: Rear-axle symptom diagnosis, leakage analysis and contact-pattern interpretation.
Ring-gear backlash measurement and adjustment route.
Drive-pinion and ring-and-pinion replacement route.
Pinion front-bearing inspection and replacement route.
Differential-carrier inspection and removal/installation route.
Driveshaft-angle measurement for acceleration shudder.

guides.title: Overhaul the Traction-Lok clutch-type differential carrier
guides.summary: Rebuild the clutch-type differential carrier with preserved clutch-pack order, specified lubrication, new bearings and fasteners, and a side-gear torque check.
guides.introduction: The differential transfers ring-gear rotation to the rear halfshafts while allowing the wheels to turn at different speeds in a corner. In the clutch-type limited-slip unit, clutch packs resist relative movement to provide limited-slip action. This bench procedure dismantles and rebuilds those internal parts and renews the carrier bearings. It applies to the clutch-type Traction-Lok unit; the Torsen carrier is serviced only as a complete assembly.
guides.why: Clutch order, side-to-side separation, lubrication and shim thickness all affect how the assembled differential resists movement. Bearing and fastener replacement requirements must also be preserved. The final side-gear torque check assesses clutch resistance before installation, while carrier installation remains a separate axle-setup operation involving bearing preload and ring-gear backlash.

when.summary: When the clutch-type differential carrier requires bench service of its clutches or bearings.
notes: Identify the differential type before disassembly; the Torsen assembly does not use this clutch-pack overhaul path.

prepare.title: Provide bench and axle-service capability
prepare.detail: Arrange carrier removal and installation capability, a vise, torque measurement tools, a brass punch, copper or soft-face hammer and rubber mallet.

prepare.title: Gather the special tools
prepare.detail: Use puller 205-D072 with step plate 205-D061, bearing installer 205-1016 with handle 205-153, and differential clutch gauge 205-022.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement parts and materials
prepare.detail: Have new differential bearings, ring-gear bolts and a pinion-shaft lock bolt. Use Motorcraft XL-3 friction modifier meeting EST-M2C118-A and Motorcraft SAE 75W-85 Premium Synthetic Hypoid Gear Lubricant, XY-75W85-QL, meeting WSS-M2C942-A.

steps.title: Remove the carrier
steps.body: Follow the linked Differential Carrier removal procedure to bring the assembly to the bench. Keep that procedure available for final installation and the associated axle work.

steps.title: Remove the bearings and ring gear
steps.body: Use the specified puller and step plate to remove and discard the differential bearings. Remove and discard the ring-gear bolts, then remove the ring gear with the brass punch and soft-face hammer.

steps.title: Release the shaft, spring and gears
steps.body: Remove and discard the differential pinion-shaft lock bolt, then remove the shaft. Carefully remove the tensioned S-spring. Remove the differential pinion gears and their thrust washers, followed by the side gears and clutch assemblies. Keep each clutch pack in its original sequence and separate from the opposite side.

steps.title: Prepare and assemble the clutch packs
steps.body: Lubricate the steel clutch plates with the specified friction modifier. Soak the friction plates in it for no less than 15 minutes. Assemble each pack on its respective side gear without exchanging plates, discs or shims between sides.

steps.title: Install the shimmed side gears and pinion gears
steps.body: Fit two shims totaling 0.110 in (2.8 mm) to each side-gear and clutch-pack assembly; do not use more than two shims per side. Lubricate and install the side-gear assemblies with the specified gear lubricant. Lubricate and install the differential pinion gears and thrust washers.

steps.title: Restore the spring and shaft
steps.body: Install the S-spring, using a rubber mallet if needed to seat the tensioned spring. Install the pinion shaft and a new shaft lock bolt, tightening it to the procedure's specification.

steps.title: Install the ring gear
steps.body: Position the ring gear and install new ring-gear bolts. Tighten them to specification in a cross pattern so the tightening sequence follows the required assembly method.

steps.title: Install new differential bearings
steps.body: Use bearing installer 205-1016 and handle 205-153 to fit the new bearings. The bearings removed during disassembly are discarded.

steps.title: Measure side-gear resistance
steps.body: Use clutch gauge 205-022 and the vise to check the torque required to rotate one side gear. With original clutch plates, the specified initial minimum break-away torque is 20 lb.ft (27 Nm). The minimum torque needed to keep a side gear turning with new plates may vary; distinguish that running measurement from initial break-away.

steps.title: Reinstall the carrier
steps.body: After completing the bench checks, follow the linked carrier installation procedure. Housing-side bearing shims establish differential bearing preload and ring-gear backlash, so completing the clutch check does not replace the installation setup.

watchFor.title: Stored spring tension
watchFor.body: Control the S-spring during removal and installation; it remains a tensioned component.

watchFor.title: Mixed clutch parts
watchFor.body: Preserve both the order within each pack and its original side. Keep the corresponding shim with that side.

watchFor.title: Applying the wrong torque interpretation
watchFor.body: The stated original-clutch minimum concerns initial break-away. New-clutch continuing-rotation torque is described as variable.

notes: The differential is serviced as an assembly with its spider gears and side gears; their removal during this procedure does not establish separate replacement service.
Use the complete procedure for the individual shaft-lock and ring-gear tightening specifications.
