diagnostics.finding: Initial break-away torque with original clutch plates is below the specified minimum.
diagnostics.meaning: The rebuilt carrier has not met the stated original-clutch torque requirement.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the clutch assembly condition before treating the bench check as passed and reinstalling the carrier.

verification.title: Record the clutch check
verification.body: Record whether the clutch plates are original or new, the measured torque and whether it represents initial break-away or continuing rotation. Compare original-plate break-away against the stated minimum.

verification.title: Confirm assembly and installation completion
verification.body: Confirm the required new bearings and fasteners were installed, the ring-gear bolts were tightened in a cross pattern, and the linked carrier installation procedure is complete.

procedures.purpose: Disassemble and assemble the clutch-type limited-slip carrier, including clutch preparation, shimming, bearing replacement and side-gear torque checking.
Remove the differential carrier before bench work and reinstall it afterward.
Explain differential operation, housing-side preload and backlash adjustment, and the distinction between Traction-Lok and assembly-only Torsen service.

guides.title: Drain and refill the rear differential — 5.2L
guides.summary: Drain the differential through its fitted drain arrangement, refill with the specified lubricant and friction modifier, and complete the cooler-pump filling cycle where equipped.
guides.introduction: The rear differential transfers driveshaft torque to the rear halfshafts while allowing the wheels to turn at different speeds through a corner. Its lubricant protects the meshing gears and supporting bearings. This job replaces that lubricant and restores the correct level, including an additional filling stage for vehicles with a differential cooler.
guides.why: The measured lubricant and friction-modifier additions both matter. A cooler-equipped axle also needs its pump operated before the final top-up because circulating fluid through the cooler circuit can change the level in the housing. Identifying the drain arrangement first establishes whether the job involves a plug, cooler connections or removal of the housing cover.

when.summary: When differential lubricant must be drained and replenished, including after work that empties the housing.
notes: Check whether the housing has a drain plug and whether a differential cooler is fitted before choosing the draining route.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underside access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the specified lifting points. Position the vehicle in NEUTRAL and keep the hoist adapters clear of suspension parts and the differential cover.

prepare.title: Have the filling equipment ready
prepare.detail: Prepare fluid collection and filling equipment, the specified lubricant and additive, and suitable torque tools. Cooler-equipped vehicles also require a scan tool capable of operating the differential cooler pump.

steps.title: Lift at the approved points
steps.body: Follow [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631). Locate the stamped lifting-point triangles and check adapter clearance before raising the vehicle. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

steps.title: Drain through the fitted arrangement
steps.body: Where a drain plug is fitted, remove it and drain the gear lubricant. On cooler-equipped vehicles, remove the cooling-line retaining clip, disconnect and position the line aside, then remove and inspect the cooling-line fitting. Without a drain plug, remove the housing cover using [Differential Housing Cover](#/document/G2214747).

steps.title: Restore the drain connections
steps.body: Reinstall the drain plug, where fitted, to 25 lb.ft (34 Nm). Reinstall the cooler fitting to 17 lb.ft (23 Nm), then restore the line and retaining clip. If the cover was removed, complete its sealing and installation procedure before filling.

steps.title: Add the specified lubricant and modifier
steps.body: Remove the fill plug. Add 1.50 L of Motorcraft SAE 75W-85 Premium Synthetic Hypoid Gear Lubricant, XY-75W85-QL, meeting WSS-M2C942-A. Add 4.0 oz (0.118 L) of Motorcraft Additive Friction Modifier, XL-3, meeting EST-M2C118-A. The lubricant level must be within 9 mm (0.354 in.) of the fill-plug opening. Install the fill plug to 25 lb.ft (34 Nm).

steps.title: Complete the cooler-equipped filling stage
steps.body: If a differential cooler is fitted, operate its pump with a scan tool for two minutes. Top off with the specified gear lubricant, confirm the final level and secure the fill plug again. Follow the full [draining and filling procedure](#/document/G2214742) for this branch.

watchFor.title: An uninspected cooler fitting
watchFor.body: Inspect the fitting while it is removed; its condition must be addressed before restoring the connection.

watchFor.title: A skipped pump cycle
watchFor.body: The initial measured fill does not complete the cooler-equipped procedure. Pump operation and a subsequent top-up remain necessary.

notes: Use the housing-cover procedure for its sealing requirements; the cover is not simply a substitute drain plug.

verification.title: Confirm the final filled condition
verification.body: Check the specified level and fill-plug torque, with all disturbed drain and cooler connections restored.

verification.title: Record the filling result
verification.body: Record the lubricant and additive used, the final level and, where applicable, completion of the two-minute cooler-pump cycle and top-up.

procedures.purpose: Complete 5.2L differential draining and filling procedure, including lubricant, additive and cooler-pump requirements.
Approved lifting points and precautions for underside access.
Housing-cover removal and installation when the differential has no drain plug.

applicability.equipment: With or without a differential cooler

guides.title: Check and top up the 5.2L differential fluid
guides.summary: Check lubricant level at the differential fill opening, add the specified gear lubricant as needed and tighten the fill plug.
guides.introduction: The rear differential receives torque from the driveshaft and passes it to the rear halfshafts while allowing them to turn at different speeds through corners. Gear lubricant protects the working gear and bearing surfaces inside the housing. This 5.2L procedure checks the existing level and restores it through the fill opening.
guides.why: The fill opening provides the reference for the level measurement. Checking against that reference establishes whether lubricant needs adding. Clean handling protects the internal components from contamination, and using the specified lubricant preserves the intended lubrication characteristics. Correct plug tightening closes the housing after the check.

when.summary: When the differential lubricant level needs checking or a confirmed low level requires topping up.

prepare.title: Provide hoist access
prepare.detail: Use the specified lifting points and protect the axle, rear cover, suspension and mounting brackets from hoist contact. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare lubricant and measuring capability
prepare.detail: Have clean dispensing equipment, a way to check the distance below the fill opening and a suitable torque wrench. Use Motorcraft SAE 75W-85 Premium Synthetic Hypoid Gear Lubricant, XY-75W85-QL, meeting WSS-M2C942-A.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle
steps.body: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on a hoist using the [jacking and lifting procedure](#/document/G1663631). Identify the correct lifting locations by their stamped triangle markings.

steps.title: Open the fill point
steps.body: Locate and remove the differential fluid fill plug shown in the [level-check procedure](#/document/G2214894). The opening is the reference for the following measurement.

steps.title: Check and correct the level
steps.body: Check that the lubricant is within 9 mm (0.354 in.) below the fill opening. If needed, add clean specified gear lubricant until the level meets that requirement.

steps.title: Close the housing
steps.body: Install the differential fill plug and tighten it to 25 lb.ft (34 Nm). Confirm the level before closing the opening.

watchFor.title: Hoist contact with the housing
watchFor.body: Position lifting equipment carefully to avoid damage to the axle or rear cover.

watchFor.title: Contaminated lubricant
watchFor.body: Use clean lubricant and dispensing equipment when topping up.

diagnostics.finding: The lubricant sits more than 9 mm below the fill opening.
diagnostics.meaning: The level is outside the stated range.
diagnostics.next: Top up with the specified lubricant and recheck before installing the plug.

verification.title: Record the level and closure
verification.body: Record the initial level finding, the lubricant used if topping up, the final level result and confirmation of fill-plug torque.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L differential fluid level check, specified top-up lubricant, level requirement and fill-plug tightening.
Correct lifting points and precautions for positioning the vehicle on a hoist.

guides.title: Measure and adjust rear differential ring gear backlash
guides.summary: Measure ring gear free play and redistribute differential bearing shim thickness to bring backlash within the specified range.
guides.introduction: The drive pinion turns the ring gear, which is bolted to the differential case. Backlash is the small amount of free movement between the meshing teeth. Shims between the differential bearing cups and housing position the carrier and establish bearing preload, so adjustment requires controlled measurement and careful carrier removal and refitting.
guides.why: Backlash changes by increasing one side’s shim thickness and decreasing the other by the same amount. This moves the carrier without changing total shim thickness. Keeping reused bearing parts in their original locations and measuring housing spread protects the accuracy of the adjustment and the housing itself.

when.summary: When measured ring gear backlash requires correction during rear differential service.
notes: Have the rear-axle Specifications (205-02), including backlash limits and the shim-selection chart, available before selecting shims.

prepare.title: Prepare for precision differential work
prepare.detail: Arrange access to the carrier and bearing caps. Have selected shims ready before refitting because the carrier and bearing cups must be held in position until the shims are installed.

prepare.title: Gather measuring and installation equipment
prepare.detail: Use a dial indicator with holding fixture, clutch housing gauge 308-021 (T75L-4201-A), differential shim installer 205-220, a 12” / 300mm C-clamp, wooden blocks, tire lever, wrench, soft-face copper hammer and torque wrench.

steps.title: Measure the existing backlash
steps.body: Mount the dial indicator at a 90 degree angle to the ring gear tooth. Move the ring gear and carrier back and forth through free play only. Compare the reading with the rear-axle specification.

steps.title: Determine the shim change
steps.body: Use the backlash chart referenced by the [adjustment procedure](#/document/G2214744). Increase one bearing shim’s thickness and decrease the opposite shim by the same amount. If backlash is zero, the prescribed trial change adds 0.50 mm (0.020 in) to the right-hand shim and subtracts the same amount from the left-hand shim; refit and recheck to obtain a reading before final selection.

steps.title: Identify parts before removal
steps.body: Mark the bearing caps and preserve the original locations of their bolts. Remove the bolts and caps. Mark any bearing cups and shims that will be reused so they return to their original positions.

steps.title: Measure and apply housing spread
steps.body: Install the dial indicator and clutch housing gauge with the gauge tip inside the axle housing guide hole, then zero it. Fit the C-clamp at the 12:00 and 6:00 positions with the specified protective wooden blocks between the clamp and housing. Tighten until measured housing spread is 0.020” / 0.50 mm.

steps.title: Remove the carrier
steps.body: Remove the dial indicator. Protect the housing sealing surface with a wooden block, then use the tire lever, block and wrench as directed to remove the carrier, bearing cups and shims. Keep the clamp in place for refitting.

steps.title: Refit the carrier and right-hand shim
steps.body: Install and hold the carrier and bearing cups in place. Fit the selected or original right-hand shim with its chamfer facing outboard; if the original is unavailable, use the largest available shim as directed. Position the differential toward the right-hand side and install that bearing cap with its bolts finger-tight.

steps.title: Install the left-hand shim and cap
steps.body: Using the shim installer and soft-face copper hammer, fit the selected left-hand backlash shim with its chamfer outboard. If the selected or original shim is unavailable, use the largest shim that can be installed by hand. The clamp can be removed after this shim is installed. Fit the left-hand cap with its bolts finger-tight.

steps.title: Tighten and measure again
steps.body: Tighten the bearing cap bolts to 71 lb.ft (96 Nm). Rotate the differential several times to confirm free rotation, then reinstall the dial indicator and make the final backlash check against the specification.

watchFor.title: Housing damage
watchFor.body: The protective blocks prevent direct clamp loading that can crack the housing. Control spread with the gauge.

watchFor.title: Mixed locations or reversed shims
watchFor.body: Return reused caps, bolts, cups and shims to their identified locations. Shim chamfers face outboard.

notes: The Torsen differential carrier is serviced as an assembly only; this adjustment does not authorize internal carrier disassembly.

diagnostics.finding: Backlash is above or below specification.
diagnostics.meaning: Carrier position requires correction through paired shim changes.
diagnostics.next: Use the specified chart, preserve total shim thickness and remeasure after assembly.

diagnostics.finding: The initial reading shows zero backlash.
diagnostics.meaning: A measurable clearance must be established before final selection.
diagnostics.next: Use the prescribed right-hand/left-hand trial change and recheck.

verification.title: Confirm free rotation
verification.body: After cap-bolt tightening, rotate the differential several times and confirm that it turns freely.

verification.title: Record the final backlash
verification.body: Record the final dial-indicator reading and compare it with the applicable rear-axle specification before accepting the adjustment.

procedures.purpose: Measure backlash, select shims, remove and refit the carrier, and perform the final adjustment checks.
Understand rear differential construction, shim functions and the Torsen carrier service limitation.

guides.title: Remove and refit the rear differential assembly
guides.summary: Support and remove the rear differential, then reinstall it with new mounting and driveshaft bolts, preserved flange alignment and a fluid-level check.
guides.introduction: The rear differential receives rotation from the driveshaft through its pinion and ring gear, then delivers torque to the rear halfshafts. Its internal arrangement allows the wheels to turn at different speeds when cornering. This job removes the complete housing from its mounts for replacement or further service.
guides.why: The differential is heavy and must be supported before its mounting bolts are removed. The driveshaft joint also needs deliberate handling: pulling on the tube can damage its constant-velocity (CV) joint. Marking the flange relationship provides an installation reference.

when.summary: When a confirmed repair or replacement requires removal of the complete rear differential.
notes: Select the muffler and tailpipe procedure for the installed engine.

prepare.title: Arrange support and separation tools
prepare.detail: Provide a transmission jack for the differential, support for the disconnected driveshaft and a flat-headed screwdriver for the pinion-flange separation slot.

prepare.title: Obtain new fasteners
prepare.detail: Have new differential mounting bolts and driveshaft-to-pinion-flange bolts. The removed bolts from both locations are discarded.

prepare.title: Plan the surrounding work
prepare.detail: Have the applicable exhaust, rear-halfshaft and differential-fluid-level procedures available. If differential cooling equipment is fitted, establish its connection-handling requirements before lowering the housing.

steps.title: Clear the exhaust and halfshafts
steps.body: Remove the muffler and tailpipe assembly through the engine-specific procedure. Then remove both rear halfshafts through the linked halfshaft procedure, freeing the differential's output connections.

steps.title: Mark and separate the driveshaft
steps.body: Index-mark the driveshaft and pinion flange before removing and discarding their connecting bolts. Support the driveshaft. Insert the screwdriver into the pinion-flange slot and pry the joint from the flange, then separate it. Do not pull on the driveshaft tube.

steps.title: Disconnect the vent and lower the differential
steps.body: Disconnect the differential vent tube. Position the transmission jack to support the differential before removing its mounting fasteners. Remove and discard the mounting bolts, then remove the differential with the jack.

steps.title: Position the unit and secure its mounts
steps.body: Use the transmission jack to install the differential. Start the new mounting bolts hand-tight only. Then tighten the forward mounting bolts followed by the rear mounting bolts, using the specified torque in the axle procedure.

steps.title: Restore the vent and driveshaft connection
steps.body: Reconnect the vent tube. Position the driveshaft against the pinion flange with the removal marks aligned. Install new driveshaft-to-flange bolts and tighten them to the specified value.

steps.title: Reinstall the halfshafts and exhaust
steps.body: Install both rear halfshafts through their complete procedure. Then reinstall the muffler and tailpipe assembly using the procedure for the vehicle's engine.

steps.title: Check differential fluid level
steps.body: Perform the linked Differential Fluid Level Check after reassembly. Use that procedure's checking method and requirements to establish the final fluid condition.

watchFor.title: Unsupported assembly weight
watchFor.body: The transmission jack must carry the differential before its mounting fasteners are removed.

watchFor.title: Driveshaft-joint damage
watchFor.body: Use the flange slot for separation and support the driveshaft. Pulling the tube to release the joint can damage it.

notes: The axle overview includes Traction-Lok and Torsen arrangements. The Torsen differential carrier is serviced as an assembly; internal carrier work has a separate scope from removing the complete housing.

verification.title: Confirm connections and fastening
verification.body: Confirm that new mounting and driveshaft bolts were used, tightening followed the specified sequence, flange marks align and the vent tube is reconnected.

verification.title: Record the fluid-level result
verification.body: Record completion of the differential fluid-level check and any correction required by that procedure.

procedures.purpose: Complete rear differential removal and installation, support, replacement bolts and tightening sequence.
2.3L: muffler and tailpipe removal and installation for differential access.
3.7L: muffler and tailpipe removal and installation for differential access.
5.0L: muffler and tailpipe removal and installation for differential access.
5.2L: muffler and tailpipe removal and installation for differential access.
Removal and installation of both rear halfshafts.
Required differential fluid-level check after reassembly.

guides.title: Remove and refit a Traction-Lok or Torsen differential carrier
guides.summary: Remove the differential carrier with controlled housing spread, preserve bearing-part locations, and verify ring-gear backlash after refitting.
guides.introduction: The differential carrier supports the ring gear and the mechanism that allows the rear wheels to turn at different speeds when cornering. Bearings locate it within the rear drive housing. Shims beside the bearing cups establish bearing preload and ring-gear backlash—the clearance between the meshing ring and pinion teeth. Removing the carrier therefore requires controlled measurement and careful tracking of parts.
guides.why: Housing spread creates the clearance needed to remove and install the carrier. It must be measured, and the clamp contact points must be protected against cracking. Bearing cups, shims, caps and cap bolts also have established locations that must be preserved when reused. Returning those parts correctly does not eliminate the final backlash check.
searchTerms: ring gear backlash after carrier installation

when.summary: When an established repair requires differential-carrier removal or replacement.
notes: The illustrated limited-slip procedure also applies similarly to the Torsen carrier.
The Torsen carrier is serviced only as an assembly.

prepare.title: Arrange supported bench work
prepare.detail: Use holding fixture 307-003 (T57L-500-B). Have the Differential Housing Cover procedure available for opening and closing the assembly; vehicle-level access must be addressed before this bench sequence.

prepare.title: Prepare the spreading and extraction equipment
prepare.detail: Use gauge 308-021 (T75L-4201-A), a dial indicator, a 12” / 300 mm C-clamp, a tire lever, a wrench and wooden protection. The clamp requires 2” x 2” x ¾” wood blocks at its housing contact points.

prepare.title: Prepare for measured reassembly
prepare.detail: Have differential-shim installer 205-220, a soft-face copper mallet, suitable torque equipment, and the selected or original shims ready. Maintain identifiable locations for every part that will be reused.

steps.title: Open and secure the assembly
steps.body: Remove the differential housing cover using its dedicated procedure, then secure the differential assembly on the holding fixture. This provides support while the bearing retention and carrier are removed.

steps.title: Identify the bearing components
steps.body: Mark the bearing caps before removing their bolts and the caps. Preserve each bolt’s original location as well. Mark the shims and carrier-bearing cups if they will be reused, so they return to their original positions.

steps.title: Measure the housing spread
steps.body: Install the gauge and dial indicator with the gauge tip inside the rear drive unit (RDU) housing guide hole, then zero the indicator. Position the protected C-clamp at the housing’s 12 and 6 o’clock positions. Tighten it until the measured spread is 0.020” / 0.50 mm.

steps.title: Extract the carrier and inspect the case
steps.body: Remove the dial indicator while retaining the clamp. Place a wood block on the housing sealing surface and use the tire lever, block and wrench in the illustrated arrangement to remove the carrier, bearing cups and shims. Remove the clamp, then inspect the differential case.

steps.title: Prepare the housing for installation
steps.body: Reinstall and zero the gauge and indicator, then repeat the protected clamping arrangement to obtain 0.020” / 0.50 mm spread. Have the selected or previously removed shims immediately available. Their chamfers must face outboard.

steps.title: Insert the carrier and bearing cups
steps.body: Remove the dial indicator and install the carrier and its bearing cups. Hold them in position until the shims are installed; they must remain supported during the following operations.

steps.title: Install the right-hand shim and cap
steps.body: Install the right-hand ring-gear backlash shim. If the original right-hand shim is unavailable, install the largest available shim as directed. Move the differential toward the right-hand side and install that bearing cap with its bolts only finger-tight.

steps.title: Install the selected left-hand shim
steps.body: Use the shim installer and soft-face copper mallet to install the selected left-hand backlash shim, chamfer outward. The clamp can be removed after the selected shim is installed. Fit the left-hand bearing cap with its bolts only finger-tight.

steps.title: Tighten the caps and check backlash
steps.body: Tighten the bearing-cap bolts to 71 lb.ft (96 Nm). Check ring-gear backlash using the linked adjustment procedure and follow its requirements before considering the carrier installation complete.

steps.title: Close the assembly
steps.body: Remove the differential assembly from the holding fixture and reinstall the housing cover using the dedicated cover procedure. This completes the carrier removal-and-refit sequence.

watchFor.title: Unmeasured spread or unprotected clamp contact
watchFor.body: Use the dial indicator to establish spread and the specified wood blocks to protect the housing against cracking.

watchFor.title: Mixed locations or reversed shims
watchFor.body: Return reused cups, shims, caps and cap bolts to their identified locations. Both bearing shims require their chamfers facing outboard.

notes: The largest available right-hand shim is the specified installation branch when the original is unavailable; it is not a substitute for checking and adjusting backlash.

verification.title: Record backlash
verification.body: Record the measured ring-gear backlash and confirm it meets the requirements of Ring Gear Backlash Adjustment.

verification.title: Confirm retention and closure
verification.body: Verify cap locations and bolt torque, completion of case inspection, and housing-cover installation through its dedicated procedure.

procedures.purpose: Carrier removal and installation for the illustrated limited-slip differential and similar Torsen application, including controlled housing spread and shim installation.
Required ring-gear backlash check and adjustment after the carrier and bearing caps are installed.
Explain carrier support, shim-controlled preload and backlash, and the Torsen assembly-only service restriction.

guides.title: Remove and Reseal the Differential Housing Cover
guides.summary: Remove the differential assembly, renew the cover’s silicone seal, reinstall the assembly and refill it with clean differential fluid.
guides.introduction: The rear differential transfers driveshaft rotation to the rear halfshafts while allowing them to turn at different speeds during a corner. Its cast housing cover closes the rear of the assembly and retains the fluid used by the gears and bearings. The cover joint uses silicone sealant as its gasket. Servicing this joint involves removing the differential assembly, preparing the mating surfaces and rebuilding the seal before refilling.
guides.why: A successful seal depends on the condition of both mating surfaces and the specified sealant application. Simply tightening the cover does not renew that joint. The cover bolts also have low-profile external Torx heads requiring the specified socket. Although the cover work is straightforward once accessible, assembly removal and refitting make this a substantial workshop repair.

when.summary: When the differential cover needs removal, replacement or resealing.
notes: If investigating a fluid leak, establish that the cover joint is the repair target before beginning assembly removal.
The cover procedure requires the differential assembly to be removed from the vehicle.

prepare.title: Plan the complete access operation
prepare.detail: Use the linked axle assembly procedure for removal and installation, including its lifting, support and fastening requirements. Have the capability to complete that work before opening the cover.

prepare.title: Gather the sealing equipment
prepare.detail: Provide an EPL16 socket for the low-profile external Torx cover bolts, a plastic scraper and a torque wrench. Use Motorcraft Ultra Silicone Sealant TA-29 meeting WSS-M4G323-A8.

prepare.title: Prepare for refilling
prepare.detail: Have clean differential fluid selected through the linked draining and filling procedure. Use that procedure for the applicable fluid and fill requirements.

steps.title: Remove the differential assembly
steps.body: Follow the axle assembly removal procedure to make the differential available for cover service. Complete its access and support operations before proceeding to the cover.

steps.title: Remove the cover
steps.body: Use the EPL16 socket to remove the cover bolts, then remove the differential housing cover. The supplied illustration identifies the cover and its perimeter fasteners.

steps.title: Prepare both mating surfaces
steps.body: Clean the cover and housing mating surfaces using a plastic scraper and the linked room-temperature-vulcanizing silicone sealing-surface preparation procedure. This prepares the joint for a fresh, consistent seal.

steps.title: Apply the specified sealant
steps.body: Apply a 2mm bead of the specified Motorcraft Ultra Silicone Sealant to form the cover gasket. Follow the complete cover procedure for its application rather than choosing an arbitrary bead size.

steps.title: Install and secure the cover
steps.body: Install the differential housing cover and its bolts. Tighten the cover bolts to 46 Nm to secure the newly sealed joint.

steps.title: Reinstall and refill
steps.body: Reinstall the differential assembly using the axle assembly procedure. Then fill it with clean differential fluid using the separate draining and filling procedure.

watchFor.title: Residual sealant at the joint
watchFor.body: Both mating faces require preparation before the new bead is applied. Follow the specified cleaning method with the plastic scraper.

watchFor.title: Incorrect socket engagement
watchFor.body: The low-profile external Torx bolts specifically require an EPL16 socket for removal.

notes: The fluid specification and filling method belong to the draining and filling procedure; the cover procedure does not supply substitute values.

verification.title: Confirm the complete repair path
verification.body: Confirm the cover is secured, differential installation is complete and the clean-fluid refill has been performed.

verification.title: Record fastening and filling completion
verification.body: Record the cover-bolt torque completion and the refill result established through the applicable draining and filling procedure.

procedures.purpose: Differential housing cover removal, mating-surface preparation, sealant application and installation.
Required removal and installation of the differential assembly for cover access.
Required cleaning and preparation of the silicone-sealed cover and housing mating surfaces.
Differential draining and filling requirements, including the clean-fluid refill after installation.

guides.title: Remove and refit the rear drive pinion flange while preserving bearing preload
guides.summary: Measure the pinion's turning resistance before removal, preserve flange alignment and set the new nut using the correct preload reference.
guides.introduction: The drive pinion flange connects the driveshaft to the rear axle's pinion, which turns the differential ring gear. Its retaining nut also controls the preload on the pinion's opposed tapered roller bearings through a collapsible spacer. Removing this flange therefore involves more than undoing and retightening a nut: the repair must preserve both its alignment and the bearing adjustment.
guides.why: Brake drag can distort the initial turning-resistance measurement, which is why the rear calipers and pads must be removed. Tightening the pinion nut compresses the spacer. Exceeding the permitted increase in turning resistance damages that spacer and requires its replacement, so gradual adjustment and repeated measurement are central to this job.

when.summary: When the drive pinion flange must be removed for repair or associated pinion-seal work.
notes: Choose brake and driveshaft procedures for the fitted equipment. The flange procedure identifies separate GT500 branches.

prepare.title: Prepare measuring and flange tools
prepare.detail: Use a dial-type torque wrench suitable for Nm or lb-in torque-to-turn measurements, holding fixture 205-126 (T78P-4851-A), installer 205-233 (T85T-4851-AH), a puller and marking equipment.

prepare.title: Plan the surrounding work
prepare.detail: Provide the capability and access required for rear brake-disc and driveshaft removal. Obtain a new pinion nut; the removed nut must be discarded. Include a new pinion seal if seal replacement is necessary.

steps.title: Remove the brake and driveshaft loads
steps.body: Follow the equipment-specific rear brake-disc removal procedure, ensuring the rear calipers and pads are removed for accurate measurement. Remove the rear driveshaft next, using the applicable branch identified in the [flange procedure](#/document/G2214749).

steps.title: Measure and record torque to turn
steps.body: Before loosening the nut, use the dial-type wrench to measure and record the drive pinion's rotational resistance. This is the reassembly reference for the assembled differential, not the tightening torque applied to the nut.

steps.title: Remove the nut and mark the flange
steps.body: Hold the flange with the specified holding fixture, remove the pinion nut and discard it. Mark the flange and pinion stem to preserve their relative angular position, then remove the flange with a puller.

steps.title: Address the seal and install the flange
steps.body: If necessary, fit a new seal using the [pinion seal procedure](#/document/G2214751). Align the previously applied flange and stem marks, then install the flange with the specified installer.

steps.title: Select the applicable preload target
steps.body: For the assembled differential, use the recorded reference: final torque to turn must be at that value or no more than 0.3 Nm (3 lb-in) above it. When no differential carrier is installed, the separate target is 2 to 3 Nm (16–29 in-lbs).

steps.title: Install and adjust the new nut
steps.body: Hold the flange with the holding fixture and install the new nut. Tighten in small increments, checking rotational resistance against the applicable target. If the assembled-differential reference is exceeded by more than 0.3 Nm (3 lb-in), stop: a new collapsible spacer is required.

steps.title: Restore the surrounding assemblies
steps.body: Install the rear driveshaft, then restore the rear brake discs and associated brake components through their applicable procedures. Finish preload measurement before restoring components that introduce brake drag.

watchFor.title: A missing or contaminated baseline
watchFor.body: An unrecorded initial reading, or one taken with brake drag present, cannot reliably guide the prescribed assembled-differential adjustment.

watchFor.title: Confusing torque measurements
watchFor.body: The specified targets describe resistance to rotating the pinion, not a fixed tightening torque for the pinion nut.

notes: Use the carrier-absent target only when the differential carrier is actually absent.
For GT500 equipment, follow the specifically named brake-disc and driveshaft procedures in the flange instructions.

diagnostics.finding: Final rotational resistance exceeds the recorded reference by more than the permitted increase.
diagnostics.meaning: The collapsible spacer has been damaged by excessive adjustment.
diagnostics.next: Replace the collapsible spacer; do not treat the flange installation as complete.

verification.title: Record the preload result
verification.body: Record the initial and final torque-to-turn readings and confirm that the final value meets the applicable assembled-differential or carrier-absent target.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly
verification.body: Verify aligned flange/stem marks, installation of a new nut, and completion of the applicable driveshaft and rear brake installation procedures.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the drive pinion flange, including torque-to-turn measurement and conditional preload targets.
Rear brake-disc removal and installation for the listed 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications; use the separately identified GT500 branch where applicable.
Rear driveshaft removal and installation for the applicable configuration.
Replace the drive pinion seal when required during flange removal.

guides.title: Replace the front drive pinion bearing and reset the pinion
guides.summary: Replace the front pinion bearing through full drive-pinion removal, renewing the required bearing parts and restoring pinion depth and preload.
guides.introduction: The drive pinion receives rotation from the driveshaft and turns the differential ring gear. Opposed tapered roller bearings support it and hold its position under load. The front bearing is the outer pinion bearing addressed in the full drive-pinion procedure. Replacing it is a specialist axle setup job: the required path also removes the inner bearing and bearing cups, renews the collapsible spacer and establishes the pinion's working position and bearing load again.
guides.why: The bearing cup is the surface on which the bearing rollers run, so the outer bearing and its cup must be replaced together. Bearing depth determines where the pinion teeth meet the ring gear. Preload, maintained by the collapsible spacer and pinion nut, controls the bearing loading. Neither setting can be established reliably by returning parts to an assumed previous position.

when.summary: When the front drive pinion bearing requires replacement and the complete pinion setup can be performed.
notes: Plan for full drive-pinion removal rather than an external bearing exchange.

prepare.title: Provide axle setup capability
prepare.detail: Have the full Drive Pinion procedure and its referenced Differential Carrier and Drive Pinion Seal procedures available. This work requires bearing installation, precision shim selection and torque-to-turn measurement.

prepare.title: Assemble the specified tools
prepare.detail: Provide a hydraulic press, bearing separator, rubber mallet, punch and copper hammer, plus the specified thread protector, bearing and cup installers, and complete pinion-depth gauge equipment listed in Drive Pinion.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement parts
prepare.detail: The full procedure discards both pinion bearings, both bearing cups and the collapsible spacer. Obtain their replacements and follow the associated carrier and seal procedures for their additional requirements.

steps.title: Open the assembly through the prerequisite procedures
steps.body: Remove the differential carrier and drive pinion seal as directed by their references in Drive Pinion. Remove the drive pinion outer shim to reach the pinion and outer bearing.

steps.title: Free the pinion without damaging its threads
steps.body: Use thread protector 205-229 and a rubber mallet to tap the pinion free of the outer bearing. Remove the pinion, discard the outer bearing and discard the collapsible spacer.

steps.title: Remove the remaining bearing parts
steps.body: Use the bearing separator and hydraulic press to remove and discard the inner bearing. Remove its shim. Use the punch and copper hammer to remove and discard the bearing cups.

steps.title: Seat the new cups
steps.body: Install new inner and outer bearing cups with the specified installers. Confirm both are correctly seated before gauging; an incorrectly seated cup can cause component damage and compromise the setup.

steps.title: Build the depth-gauge arrangement
steps.body: Assemble the specified gauge components finger-tight initially. Align the gauge block at 45 degrees to the axle centerline and install the handle. Apply the specified gauge-setting torque, check tool location, then install the gauge tube and bearing caps at the prescribed cap-bolt torque. Follow the complete procedure for this tool arrangement.

steps.title: Select the depth shim by feel
steps.body: Use flat, clean adjustment shims between the gauge block and tube. The correct selection produces slight drag; do not force a shim into the gap. An excessively thick choice produces a deep tooth contact. Remove the gauge tools afterward, preserving the bearing caps' correct installation orientation.

steps.title: Press on the inner bearing and fit a new spacer
steps.body: Using the specified plate, bearing installer and hydraulic press, firmly seat the new inner bearing and selected adjustment shim on the pinion. Install a new collapsible spacer.

steps.title: Restore the outer bearing and pinion
steps.body: Install the new outer pinion bearing, outer shim and pinion in the sequence specified by Drive Pinion. The new outer cup installed earlier completes the required replacement of the bearing's running surfaces.

steps.title: Set final drag before restoring the carrier
steps.body: Follow Drive Pinion Seal for the seal and associated flange and pinion-nut work. With no differential carrier installed, the specified pinion torque to turn is 2.5 to 3.9 Nm (22–34 lb-in). Complete the differential carrier installation through its referenced procedure after this stage.

watchFor.title: Gauge torque confused with final drag
watchFor.body: The depth-gauge tool setting and the completed pinion's torque-to-turn check are separate instructions. Do not substitute one value for the other.

watchFor.title: Carrier type
watchFor.body: If a Torsen differential is fitted, its carrier is serviced as an assembly only.

notes: The front-bearing procedure requires cup replacement and directs the work through the complete Drive Pinion procedure; it provides no shortcut around that setup.

diagnostics.finding: An adjustment shim enters the gauge gap only when forced.
diagnostics.meaning: The selection does not meet the slight-drag criterion and risks a shim thicker than required.
diagnostics.next: Select a flat, clean shim that gives the specified slight drag.

diagnostics.finding: Final pinion drag is outside the specified range with the carrier removed.
diagnostics.meaning: The required pinion bearing setting has not been achieved.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the setup through the complete pinion and seal procedures before installing the carrier.

verification.title: Confirm the depth-setting work
verification.body: Check cup seating, the selected shim's fit, firm inner-bearing seating and preservation of bearing-cap orientation.

verification.title: Record final pinion drag
verification.body: Record the measured torque to turn and confirm it was measured with the differential carrier removed.

verification.title: Complete the associated installation
verification.body: Confirm that the referenced drive pinion seal and differential carrier installation procedures have been completed.

procedures.purpose: Front drive pinion bearing replacement requirement, including renewal of the matching outer bearing cup.
Full drive-pinion removal and installation, bearing and cup replacement, depth-shim selection, new spacer and final pinion drag setting.

guides.title: Replace the rear differential drive pinion seal
guides.summary: Remove the drive pinion flange, renew the oil seal with its dedicated installer and complete the flange installation procedure.
guides.introduction: The drive pinion seal retains lubricant around the rotating input to the rear differential. The driveshaft turns the pinion flange, which turns the pinion and ring gear to transmit drive to the halfshafts. Replacing this seal requires removing the flange first. Although the seal itself has a short replacement sequence, the surrounding pinion assembly needs controlled reassembly.
guides.why: The pinion bearings operate with preload maintained by a collapsible spacer and adjusted through the pinion nut. Flange removal and installation therefore form an important part of the repair. The seal instructions do not provide a substitute pinion-nut setting: use the complete flange procedure for that work and the specified installer for the new seal.

when.summary: When lubricant leakage has been traced to the drive pinion seal, or the seal otherwise requires renewal.
notes: Include drive pinion flange removal and installation in the repair plan.

prepare.title: Have the specified seal tools
prepare.detail: Prepare a flat-headed screwdriver for seal removal and drive pinion oil seal installer 205-208 (T83T-4676-A) for installation. Obtain a replacement seal before dismantling.

prepare.title: Prepare for flange work
prepare.detail: Be equipped to complete the linked Drive Pinion Flange procedure. Understand that the pinion nut affects bearing preload through the collapsible spacer before disturbing the assembly.

steps.title: Remove the drive pinion flange
steps.body: Follow the removal phase of [Drive Pinion Flange](#/document/G2214749). This exposes the seal while keeping the flange-related operations within their complete technical sequence.

steps.title: Remove and discard the seal
steps.body: Use a flat-bladed screwdriver to remove the seal as illustrated in [Drive Pinion Seal](#/document/G2214751). Discard the removed seal; it is replaced during reassembly.

steps.title: Install the replacement seal
steps.body: Use installer 205-208 (T83T-4676-A) to fit the new drive pinion oil seal. Follow the installation arrangement in the seal procedure rather than estimating a fitting method from the removal illustration.

steps.title: Reinstall the flange
steps.body: Complete the installation phase of the drive pinion flange procedure. Keep its instructions governing the pinion assembly part of this job, because pinion-nut adjustment affects bearing preload.

watchFor.title: Casual pinion-nut adjustment
watchFor.body: The pinion nut adjusts a bearing arrangement that uses a collapsible spacer. Follow the flange procedure rather than choosing a generic tightening value.

watchFor.title: Reusing the removed seal
watchFor.body: The old seal is explicitly discarded. Have the new seal and correct installer ready before removal.

verification.title: Confirm seal replacement
verification.body: Confirm that the discarded seal was replaced using the specified drive pinion oil seal installer.

verification.title: Confirm flange installation is complete
verification.body: Check completion against the linked flange installation procedure. The seal repair remains incomplete until that dependent assembly work is finished.

procedures.purpose: Drive pinion seal removal, discard and installation using the dedicated oil seal installer.
Drive pinion flange removal before seal access and complete flange installation after seal replacement.

guides.title: Remove and install the rear axle drive pinion
guides.summary: Remove the drive pinion, renew its bearings and cups, select its depth shim and establish the specified bearing turning resistance.
guides.introduction: The drive pinion receives rotation from the driveshaft and turns the differential ring gear. Opposed tapered roller bearings support it, while a depth shim controls its position relative to the ring gear. A collapsible spacer and pinion nut establish bearing preload. Removing the pinion therefore involves precision bearing setup as well as dismantling: the final assembly must have both the correct position and the correct resistance to turning.
guides.why: An incorrectly seated bearing cup changes the setup and can damage components. A depth shim that is too thick places tooth contact too deep. Bearing preload is a separate requirement from pinion depth, and the gauging-tool torque must not be confused with the final pinion turning-resistance specification.

when.summary: When an established rear-axle repair requires drive-pinion removal and bearing setup.
notes: This is precision axle work requiring a hydraulic press and the specified depth-gauging equipment.

prepare.title: Provide removal and pressing equipment
prepare.detail: Have a hydraulic press, bearing separator, rubber mallet, punch, copper hammer and drive-pinion thread protector. Use the dedicated bearing-cup installers, bearing installer and bearing/oil-seal plate.

prepare.title: Provide the complete depth-gauge arrangement
prepare.detail: The setup uses the gauge block, pinion-depth-gauge adapter, pinion-aligning adapter, gauge disc, handle and gauge tube identified in the complete procedure. Equipment must also measure the specified low rotational torque.

prepare.title: Plan for discarded parts and prerequisites
prepare.detail: Provide new inner and outer pinion bearings, bearing cups and collapsible spacer. Have the separate differential-carrier and pinion-seal procedures available for their removal and installation requirements.

steps.title: Open the axle in the required order
steps.body: Remove the [differential carrier](#/document/G2214746), then complete the removal phase of the [drive pinion seal procedure](#/document/G2214751). These operations provide access for pinion removal.

steps.title: Release the pinion
steps.body: Remove the outer pinion shim. Fit the thread protector and use a rubber mallet to tap the pinion free of its outer bearing. Remove the pinion, then remove and discard the outer bearing and collapsible spacer.

steps.title: Remove the remaining bearings and cups
steps.body: Use the bearing separator and hydraulic press to remove and discard the inner bearing, then remove its shim. Use the punch and copper hammer to remove and discard the bearing cups. Follow the [drive-pinion procedure](#/document/G2214748) for the complete tool arrangement.

steps.title: Seat the new bearing cups
steps.body: Install new inner and outer cups with their specified installers. Confirm correct seating before gauging; an incompletely seated cup makes the subsequent shim selection unreliable.

steps.title: Assemble and load the depth gauge
steps.body: Assemble the gauge block, adapters and disc in the housing finger-tight initially. Align the block at 45 degrees to the axle centerline. Install the handle and tighten the gauging tool to 18 lb.in (2 Nm), which reproduces the bearing-preload condition for gauging. Check tool location, then install the gauge tube and bearing caps, tightening the cap bolts to 71 lb.ft (96 Nm).

steps.title: Select the depth shim and remove the gauges
steps.body: Use a clean, flat adjustment shim as the gauge between the block and tube. Correct selection produces slight drag; do not force the shim into the gap. Preserve bearing-cap orientation while removing the caps and bolts, then remove the gauge tube, handle and remaining gauging tools.

steps.title: Press on the inner bearing
steps.body: Install the selected adjustment shim and new inner bearing using the hydraulic press, bearing/oil-seal plate and pinion-bearing installer. Both must be firmly seated on the pinion.

steps.title: Reassemble the pinion support
steps.body: Install a new collapsible spacer, then install the new outer pinion bearing, outer shim and pinion. The discarded spacer and bearings are not reused.

steps.title: Complete the seal and carrier installation
steps.body: Follow the pinion-seal installation procedure. During flange and nut installation, with the differential carrier still removed, pinion drag torque must be 2.5 to 3.9 Nm (22-34 lb-in). Establish that condition before reinstalling the differential carrier through its separate procedure.

watchFor.title: A shim that needs force
watchFor.body: Forcing a shim into the gauge gap can select an excessive thickness and produce deep tooth contact.

watchFor.title: Mixed bearing-cap orientation
watchFor.body: Keep each cap in its correct installation orientation during gauge removal and final assembly.

notes: The Torsen differential carrier is serviced as an assembly; this pinion procedure does not authorize dismantling its internal mechanism.

diagnostics.finding: Pinion turning resistance is outside the specified range with the carrier removed.
diagnostics.meaning: The required final bearing-preload condition has not been established.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the setup using the complete pinion and seal procedures before installing the carrier.

verification.title: Record the setup results
verification.body: Record the selected adjustment shim and measured pinion drag torque, noting that the carrier was removed during the final turning-resistance measurement.

verification.title: Complete the linked assembly phases
verification.body: Confirm that the pinion-seal and differential-carrier installation procedures are complete and that bearing-cap orientation has been preserved.

procedures.purpose: Drive-pinion removal, bearing and cup renewal, depth-shim selection and installation setup.
Differential-carrier removal before pinion work and installation after pinion setup.
Pinion-seal removal and installation, including the associated flange and nut work referenced by the pinion procedure.
Rear-axle operating layout, bearing-preload arrangement and Torsen carrier service limitation.

guides.title: Replace a rear differential halfshaft seal
guides.summary: Remove the rear halfshafts, install a new differential outlet seal with the specified tools, then refit the shaft components and check fluid level.
guides.introduction: The differential receives rotation from the driveshaft and delivers it to the rear wheels through the halfshafts, allowing the wheels to turn at different speeds when cornering. A halfshaft seal retains lubricant where a shaft exits the differential housing. Replacing that seal renews the sealing point, but reaching it requires the rear-halfshaft removal work first.
guides.why: The old seal is discarded because this procedure requires a new sealing component. The specified installer and handle provide the prescribed installation method. Checking differential fluid afterward is essential to finishing the job: replacing the seal does not establish that the housing contains the correct lubricant level.

when.summary: When a rear halfshaft seal has been identified as the leakage source or otherwise requires replacement.
notes: Oil near a halfshaft outlet warrants confirming the leak origin before selecting the seal for replacement.

prepare.title: Plan the halfshaft work
prepare.detail: Arrange safe under-vehicle access and the lifting, support and mechanical capability required by the applicable rear-halfshaft procedure. Have that procedure available for removal and reinstallation.

prepare.title: Obtain the new seal and specified tools
prepare.detail: Use installer 206-034 (T88P-20202-B), named Installer, Wheel Speed Sensor Ring, with handle 205-907, named Handle, 32 Driver. These are the tools specified for this seal installation.

prepare.title: Prepare the fluid-level procedure
prepare.detail: Have Differential Fluid Level Check, section 205-02, available so the final check uses the correct method and fluid information.

steps.title: Remove the rear halfshafts
steps.body: Follow the applicable halfshaft removal procedure. The seal operation begins with the rear halfshafts removed; complete the access work before attempting to extract the seal.

steps.title: Remove and discard the seal
steps.body: Identify the seal at the differential outlet using the illustration. Remove it and discard it, keeping the requirement for a new seal clear throughout the repair.

steps.title: Install the new seal
steps.body: Use the specified 206-034 installer and 205-907 handle to install the replacement. Follow the complete seal procedure for the installation operation.

steps.title: Refit the halfshaft components
steps.body: Reinstall the rear halfshaft using the applicable halfshaft procedure, completing the restoration of every component removed for access.

steps.title: Check differential fluid level
steps.body: Carry out Differential Fluid Level Check after reassembly. Use that procedure to establish whether the lubricant level needs correction.

watchFor.title: An incomplete access plan
watchFor.body: Halfshaft removal and reinstallation are substantial prerequisites; their fastener requirements and installation details must remain part of the job.

notes: Although the specified installer is named for a wheel-speed sensor ring, it is expressly listed for installing this halfshaft seal.
The illustration identifies the outlet seal; use the written removal sequence to determine the required access work.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly
verification.body: Confirm that a new seal was installed with the specified tools and that the halfshaft installation procedure is complete.

verification.title: Record the lubricant result
verification.body: Record the differential fluid-level check and any correction made under the fluid-level procedure.

procedures.purpose: Rear halfshaft seal removal, mandatory replacement, installation with the specified tools and final differential fluid-level check requirement.

guides.title: Replace the rear stub shaft pilot bearing
guides.summary: Replace the rear halfshaft pilot bearing with the specified removal and installation tools, then fit a new halfshaft seal.
guides.introduction: The stub shaft pilot bearing supports the halfshaft where it enters the rear differential. The procedure also calls it the rear halfshaft pilot bearing. The halfshaft connects to a differential side gear and carries rotation toward the wheel, while the differential allows the wheels to turn at different speeds through corners. This repair renews the local shaft support and the adjacent seal.
guides.why: Access requires removing the halfshaft seal before extracting the bearing. Both parts must be renewed: the bearing is discarded during removal, and installation calls for a new seal. The dedicated bearing remover and installer set provide the specified method for extracting the old bearing and fitting its replacement.

when.summary: When the rear halfshaft pilot bearing has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Plan the bearing and halfshaft seal work together; seal removal is the first access operation.

prepare.title: Arrange the bearing tools
prepare.detail: Have bearing cup remover 308-047 (T77F-1102-A) and a slide hammer. Installation requires handle 205-907, halfshaft pilot bearing installer 205-504 and rear axle pilot bearing installer 205-1013.

prepare.title: Prepare parts and access
prepare.detail: Obtain a new pilot bearing and a new rear halfshaft seal. Be equipped to complete the linked halfshaft seal removal and installation procedure, which is an essential part of this job.

steps.title: Remove the halfshaft seal
steps.body: Follow the removal phase of [Rear Halfshaft Seal](#/document/G2214752). Removing the seal exposes the bearing for the specified extraction operation.

steps.title: Extract and discard the bearing
steps.body: Use the bearing cup remover with the slide hammer as shown in [Stub Shaft Pilot Bearing](#/document/G2274512). Remove the rear halfshaft pilot bearing and discard it; this operation is followed by replacement.

steps.title: Install the new pilot bearing
steps.body: Use the specified handle and both pilot bearing installers to fit the replacement bearing. Follow the installation arrangement in the bearing procedure so the new part is installed with the intended tooling.

steps.title: Fit the new seal and complete reassembly
steps.body: Return to the installation phase of the halfshaft seal procedure and install a new seal. Complete that linked procedure to restore the parts disturbed for bearing access.

watchFor.title: Missing replacement seal
watchFor.body: The bearing job ends with a new halfshaft seal, even when bearing replacement was the original reason for opening the assembly.

watchFor.title: Incomplete installer set
watchFor.body: The installation specifies the handle and both bearing installers; arrange the complete set before removing the old bearing.

verification.title: Confirm both replacement stages
verification.body: Confirm that the new pilot bearing was installed before the new halfshaft seal, and that neither discarded part was reused.

verification.title: Close the access procedure
verification.body: Check that the linked halfshaft seal installation has been completed, including the reassembly required by that procedure.

procedures.purpose: Rear stub shaft pilot bearing removal and installation, including mandatory bearing replacement and the specified tooling.
Prerequisite rear halfshaft seal removal and installation of the required new seal after bearing replacement.

guides.title: Diagnose rear halfshaft clunks, shudder and cruising vibration
guides.summary: Use the symptom's timing, joint condition, hub-nut torque and outer-joint seating to direct rear halfshaft repairs.
guides.introduction: Rear halfshafts transmit drive from the differential to the rear wheel hubs. Their constant velocity (CV) joints accommodate changing angles as the suspension moves. Wear, binding or an insecure hub connection can produce different noises and vibrations. This diagnosis distinguishes those possibilities before selecting a halfshaft or hub repair.
guides.why: A clunk during a direction change points toward a different check from a clunk when pulling away. Correct joint seating also matters: binding can cause shudder or vibration without establishing that the entire halfshaft needs replacement.

when.summary: Investigate a rear driveline clunk, acceleration shudder or cruising-speed vibration.
notes: The Reverse-to-Drive selector test applies only to vehicles with those selector positions.

prepare.title: Arrange inspection and torque-checking access
prepare.detail: Provide safe access to the rear halfshafts and hubs, and a torque wrench for the hub-nut check. Obtain the applicable Rear Halfshaft procedure for the specified torque and corrective work.

steps.title: Identify exactly when the concern occurs
steps.body: Confirm whether the complaint happens during a direction change, when moving forward after a stop, during acceleration from rest or at cruising speed. These conditions select different checks; the word 'clunk' alone is not enough.

steps.title: Look for an obvious mechanical cause
steps.body: Inspect hardware, CV-joint boots, joints and halfshafts for looseness or visible damage. Correct an evident cause where possible before pursuing the symptom chart. A boot finding belongs in the inspection record but does not by itself establish the condition of the joint.

steps.title: Follow the matching symptom branch
steps.body: Inspect joint wear for a direction-change clunk, check hub-nut torque for a forward-start clunk, and check outer-joint seating for acceleration shudder or cruising vibration. If hub-nut torque is outside specification, the prescribed action is a new hub nut; do not treat retightening the existing nut as the completed repair.

steps.title: Carry out the justified repair and protect the seals
steps.body: Use the Rear Halfshaft procedure for joint seating corrections or halfshaft replacement. If installation is required, prevent the splines from contacting the halfshaft seal. For seal work, use the Rear Halfshaft Seal procedure: the bore must be clean, the lip protected from cuts or tears, and the journal free of nicks, gouges and roughness.

watchFor.title: Seal damage during installation
watchFor.body: Splines can cut the seal lip, while a damaged journal can compromise the sealing surface.

notes: The symptom chart identifies possible causes. Confirm the associated mechanical finding before choosing a replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Loud clunk from Reverse to Drive
diagnostics.meaning: CV joints may be worn or damaged.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the joints; replace the rear halfshaft as necessary.

diagnostics.finding: Clunk when moving forward after a stop
diagnostics.meaning: The hub nut may be loose.
diagnostics.next: Check torque against specification and install a new nut if it is incorrect.

diagnostics.finding: Grunting with shudder during acceleration from rest
diagnostics.meaning: A halfshaft CV joint may be binding.
diagnostics.next: Check outer-joint seating in the hub and repair as necessary.

diagnostics.finding: Vibration at cruising speed
diagnostics.meaning: A CV joint may be binding or damaged.
diagnostics.next: Check outer-joint seating in the hub and follow the indicated repair.

verification.title: Confirm the mechanical correction
verification.body: Recheck the relevant finding: joint condition, correct outer-joint seating or hub-nut torque using the applicable repair procedure.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the symptom condition, inspection findings, hub-nut torque assessment where applicable and the repair selected.

procedures.purpose: Rear halfshaft inspection, symptom-specific diagnosis and seal-handling precautions across the listed engines.

guides.title: Disassemble and inspect the rear halfshaft inner CV joint before boot repair
guides.summary: Remove the inner joint housing, cage and boot in a controlled sequence, ending with a cleaned and inspected cage.
guides.introduction: The inner constant velocity (CV) joint transmits drive through the rear halfshaft while accommodating movement. Its cage locates the joint balls, and the flexible boot retains grease and excludes contamination. Opening the joint for boot work exposes loose balls and retaining hardware, so controlled disassembly matters as much as removing the boot.
guides.why: The balls can fall out when the housing and cage are separated. The clamps, housing retaining ring and cage circlip are discarded during removal. Keeping those decisions clear prevents loose parts being lost and removed retaining hardware being mistaken for reusable parts.

when.summary: Use when inner CV boot work requires opening a removed rear halfshaft and inspecting its joint cage.
notes: This bench task ends at cage cleaning and inspection.

prepare.title: Prepare the tools and work area
prepare.detail: Have the listed flat-headed screwdriver, boot clamp pliers, rubber mallet and three-leg puller available. Arrange a contained bench area to catch loose balls. Cage extraction specifically requires the three-leg puller.

prepare.title: Identify the specified lubricant
prepare.detail: The joint lubricant is Motorcraft Constant Velocity Joint Grease XG-5, specification WSS-M1C258-A1. Lubrication belongs to the later repair phase, beyond this disassembly and inspection task.

steps.title: Remove the rear halfshaft
steps.body: Complete the [Rear Halfshaft removal procedure](#/document/G2214772) before starting joint disassembly. This establishes the removed-shaft access required for the bench work.

steps.title: Open the housing end of the boot
steps.body: Following the [inner CV joint procedure](#/document/G2214770), remove and discard the large boot clamp. Move the boot to expose the inner housing retaining ring, then remove and discard that ring.

steps.title: Separate the housing and release the cage
steps.body: Remove the inner joint housing while controlling the exposed parts: the cage balls are free to fall out. Remove and discard the cage circlip, continuing to contain the balls.

steps.title: Pull the cage from the shaft
steps.body: Use the three-leg puller to remove the joint cage. Keep the loose balls controlled throughout extraction; removing the cage does not make them captive.

steps.title: Remove the remaining clamp and boot
steps.body: Remove and discard the small clamp, then remove the boot. Keep both discarded clamps and both discarded retaining parts separate from the components awaiting inspection.

steps.title: Clean and inspect the cage
steps.body: Clean the cage and inspect its condition. The inspection stage presents the cage assembled; it does not establish a full joint-reassembly sequence. Record the observed condition and retain the dismantled components for the next repair decision.

watchFor.title: Loose joint balls
watchFor.body: Account for the balls during housing removal, circlip removal and puller extraction.

watchFor.title: Premature return to service
watchFor.body: A cleaned cage is an inspection result. The halfshaft remains dismantled and is not ready to refit.

notes: Boot installation, greasing, installation of replacement retainers and clamps, full joint reassembly and halfshaft installation remain separate work.

verification.title: Confirm the disassembly boundary
verification.body: Confirm that the housing, cage and boot have been removed and that both clamps, the housing retaining ring and cage circlip have been discarded.

verification.title: Record the inspection result
verification.body: Confirm that the balls are accounted for and the cage has been cleaned and inspected. Record its condition without treating the boot repair as complete.

procedures.purpose: Inner CV housing, cage and boot removal through cage cleaning and inspection only.
Prerequisite rear-halfshaft removal to provide bench access.

guides.title: Replace the right rear outer constant velocity joint boot
guides.summary: Renew the serviceable right-hand outer joint boot, distribute its grease, vent the boot during assembly, and secure it with new clamps.
guides.introduction: A constant velocity (CV) joint transmits drive through the halfshaft while accommodating changes in angle. Its flexible boot holds grease around the joint and helps keep contamination out. This repair restores that enclosure around the outer joint. Only the right-hand rear halfshaft outer boot is serviceable by this procedure, and the work includes removing and reinstalling the inner CV joint boot.
guides.why: The boot and its clamps work together to contain the joint’s lubricant. Removed clamps must be discarded and replaced. Grease must be distributed through both the boot and housing, and air must be allowed to escape while the housing is installed. Cleaning and inspecting the cage before closure helps establish whether the joint is suitable for reassembly.
searchTerms: right rear outer CV joint boot

when.summary: When the right-hand rear outer CV joint boot needs replacement and the joint is suitable for reassembly.
notes: Do not apply this outer-boot service procedure to the left-hand halfshaft.
Allow for the linked inner-boot procedure at both the beginning and end of the job.

prepare.title: Plan the complete access sequence
prepare.detail: Be equipped and capable of carrying out the Inner Constant Velocity Joint Boot removal and installation procedure, including its prerequisites. That work is required to complete this outer-boot repair.

prepare.title: Prepare the assembly tools and materials
prepare.detail: Have a small flat-blade screwdriver, boot clamp pliers, the replacement boot, new boot clamps, and the grease sachet used for the joint assembly.

prepare.title: Provide a clean working area
prepare.detail: The joint cage must be cleaned and inspected before fresh grease and the boot enclose it. Keep the prepared parts and grease free of contamination.

steps.title: Remove the inner joint boot
steps.body: Complete the removal phase of the linked inner CV joint boot procedure first. Preserve its sequence and requirements rather than starting with the outer boot in isolation.

steps.title: Remove the outer boot and discard its clamps
steps.body: Remove and discard the outer CV joint boot clamps, then remove the boot. The illustration identifies both clamps as discarded parts.

steps.title: Inspect the cage and distribute the grease
steps.body: Clean and inspect the CV joint cage before assembly. Distribute the grease sachet evenly between the CV joint boot and housing so lubricant is placed in both parts of the enclosure.

steps.title: Install the housing while venting the boot
steps.body: Install the CV joint housing with a small flat-blade screwdriver inserted beneath the boot seat to let air escape. Use the screwdriver for this specified venting action while the housing is being fitted.

steps.title: Clamp the boot and restore the inner end
steps.body: Use boot clamp pliers to install new outer-boot clamps. Then complete the installation phase of the linked inner CV joint boot procedure.

watchFor.title: Air trapped during housing installation
watchFor.body: Retain the specified venting step before securing the boot with its new clamps.

watchFor.title: An unsuitable joint hidden by a new boot
watchFor.body: Complete the cage inspection before closing the assembly; replacing the enclosure does not establish that the joint itself is serviceable.

diagnostics.finding: Cleaning reveals a concern with the CV joint cage.
diagnostics.meaning: The joint’s condition needs resolution before boot installation can be considered a complete repair.
diagnostics.next: Assess the joint before reassembly; this boot procedure does not provide cage wear limits.

verification.title: Confirm the assembly sequence
verification.body: Confirm grease was distributed in the boot and housing, air was vented during housing installation, new clamps were installed with boot clamp pliers, and inner-boot installation is complete.

verification.title: Record the cage inspection
verification.body: Record the cage’s inspected condition before the boot is closed around the joint.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the serviceable right-hand rear outer CV joint boot, including grease distribution, venting, and new clamps.
Carry out the required inner CV joint boot removal before outer-boot work and its installation afterward.

guides.title: Remove and install a rear halfshaft
guides.summary: Remove the rear halfshaft, renew its differential seal and retaining circlip, and verify secure engagement before restoring the differential fluid level.
guides.introduction: The rear halfshaft carries drive from the differential to the rear wheel. Its constant velocity (CV) joints accommodate movement between the differential and wheel as the suspension travels. Removing it involves the wheel knuckle as well as the connection inside the differential, so careful handling matters throughout the job.
guides.why: The inner circlip retains the shaft inside the differential, while the seal keeps lubricant around the rotating connection. Both require attention whenever the shaft comes out: the circlip is discarded and the seal must be replaced. Rough handling can damage a joint or cut a boot internally without leaving an obvious external mark.

when.summary: When a rear halfshaft requires replacement or must be removed for related driveline work.
notes: Seal replacement is required after every halfshaft removal, even when the same shaft will be refitted.

prepare.title: Plan the suspension access
prepare.detail: Have the lifting, support and suspension-service capability needed for the wheel-knuckle procedure. Follow its complete removal and installation requirements before working at the differential.

prepare.title: Have the replacement parts ready
prepare.detail: Prepare a new inner halfshaft circlip, a new halfshaft seal and a pry bar. Arrange to check and correct the differential fluid level after assembly.

steps.title: Remove the wheel knuckle
steps.body: Follow the [wheel-knuckle procedure](#/document/G1686658) to clear the outer end of the halfshaft. Support and handle the shaft as an assembly; never pick it up or hold it solely by either CV joint.

steps.title: Release the inner connection
steps.body: Use a pry bar as shown in the [halfshaft procedure](#/document/G2214772) to release the shaft from the differential. Do not hammer it out or use the shaft itself to lever another component into position.

steps.title: Inspect and renew the sealing and retaining parts
steps.body: Inspect the inner seal-running surface and splines for damage, then remove and discard the inner circlip. Replace the differential-side halfshaft seal using the [seal procedure](#/document/G2214752), and install a new circlip on the shaft.

steps.title: Seat the halfshaft positively
steps.body: Insert the halfshaft until the circlip is fully seated. Correct engagement can be felt as the clip snaps into the differential side-gear groove. Pull on the inner end afterward to establish that the circlip has locked.

steps.title: Restore the suspension and fluid level
steps.body: Install the wheel knuckle using its complete procedure. Finish by checking and topping off the rear differential fluid using the Differential Fluid Level Check referenced in the halfshaft procedure.

watchFor.title: Boot contact and hidden impact damage
watchFor.body: Keep the boots away from sharp edges and hot exhaust components. Do not drop an assembled shaft: impact can cut a boot from inside even when its outside looks intact.

watchFor.title: A shaft that appears seated
watchFor.body: Insertion alone does not establish retention. The required pull check is made at the inner end after installation.

notes: Do not use a hammer during either removal or installation.
A new seal does not eliminate the need to inspect the shaft surface that runs through it.

diagnostics.finding: Damage is visible on the inner sealing surface or splines.
diagnostics.meaning: The mating surfaces need attention before the assembly can be considered ready for installation.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the damage before refitting; do not rely on a new seal or circlip to compensate for it.

verification.title: Record retention and lubrication
verification.body: Confirm and record that the inner-end pull check established circlip retention and that the differential fluid level was checked and corrected.

verification.title: Confirm assembly completion
verification.body: Verify that the wheel-knuckle installation is complete and that the shaft boots were not trapped, cut or exposed to damaging contact during the work.

procedures.purpose: Rear halfshaft removal, inspection, seal and circlip renewal requirements, installation and final fluid check.
Remove and reinstall the rear wheel knuckle for halfshaft access.
Replace the rear halfshaft seal whenever the shaft is removed.

guides.title: Diagnose brake pedal, drag, vibration and noise concerns
guides.summary: Use the complaint to select hydraulic, vacuum-assistance, mechanical or anti-lock brake checks before choosing a repair.
guides.introduction: The master cylinder supplies hydraulic pressure to the brakes, while the vacuum booster reduces the pedal effort needed. Calipers press the pads against the discs, and the anti-lock brake system (ABS) controls pressure when needed. Similar symptoms can originate in different parts of this chain. This diagnostic path distinguishes pressure loss, restricted release and poor assistance from suspension concerns and normal operating noise.
guides.why: A sinking pedal does not by itself prove master-cylinder failure, and pedal pulsation can be normal ABS operation. Isolating the fault avoids replacing parts that cannot correct the complaint.

when.summary: When braking causes abnormal pedal feel, pulling, drag, warning indicators, persistent noise or vibration.
notes: Confirm the concern is present before following a replacement decision.
Match replacement procedures to the fitted engine, transmission and calipers. The linked engine-specific booster procedures do not cover the 5.2L.

prepare.title: Provide diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Arrange Ford diagnostic knowledge, an ABS-capable scan tool, vacuum/pressure tester, leak-free master-cylinder outlet plugs, torque tools and pressure-bleeding capability.

prepare.title: Provide suitable access and test conditions
