prepare.detail: Road testing requires the capability to perform the prescribed speeds and surface comparisons. For wheel-rotation checks, use the specified lifting points and proper stands or a suitable hoist; never work beneath a jack-only supported vehicle.

steps.title: Inspect and choose the complaint branch
steps.body: Check previous repairs and obvious damage or leaks. Pulling calls for inspection of calipers, guides, hoses, pads and discs, plus tires, alignment and suspension. Light-force lockup also requires brake-component inspection and possible ABS diagnosis. Erratic travel calls for checking pedal binding, obstructions, booster-rod engagement and fastener torque.

steps.title: Start low or sinking pedal diagnosis with hydraulics
steps.body: Find and repair leaks, then bleed as directed. For low or spongy travel, inspect calipers, guide pins and flexible hoses during application. Use the bypass test below when indicated. A sinking pedal can also require hydraulic-control-unit diagnosis or inspection of the pedal simulator spring, cam and booster interface.

steps.title: Reproduce vibration through Pinpoint Test A
steps.body: Follow the specified brake warm-up, light-braking test and, if necessary, moderate-to-heavy test. Compare firm, dry conditions with the specified lower-traction surfaces. Pulsation confined to lower-traction conditions is normal ABS operation. For A4 parking-brake isolation, first identify the parking-brake design: skip this step with drum-in-hat or electronic parking brakes. In the applicable branch, vibration directs diagnosis rearward; no vibration directs it forward. Release the parking brake immediately afterward.

steps.title: Inspect suspension before correcting discs
steps.body: The front branch checks suspension first, then front discs. Repair suspension defects or service discs as indicated and road-test again. Remaining vibration leads to rear suspension and rear-disc checks. Never machine discs with cross-drilled friction surfaces.

steps.title: Trace inadequate booster vacuum
steps.body: With the parking brake applied, transmission in NEUTRAL and engine warm at idle, test at the booster side of the vacuum sensor/check valve. The specified range is 51–74 kPa (15–22 in-Hg). If low, test at the hose: adequate hose vacuum directs check-valve replacement. With a fitted vacuum pump, inspect the hose before replacing the pump. Without a pump, diagnose the engine’s low-vacuum condition.

steps.title: Check assistance and retained vacuum
steps.body: After establishing supply and reconnecting the valve, stop the engine and exhaust vacuum with repeated pedal applications. Hold the pedal and start the engine: downward movement confirms assistance; no movement directs booster replacement. Next idle for at least 20 seconds, stop and wait 10 minutes. A hard pedal then directs a new vacuum sensor/check valve and retest, followed by booster replacement only if the condition remains.

steps.title: Isolate master-cylinder bypass
steps.body: Disconnect the master-cylinder tubes and plug its outlets without leakage. Apply lightly for 10 seconds, release, then apply heavily. Failure to maintain pedal height indicates internal leakage and directs a new master cylinder. If height holds, reconnect and torque the tubes. Bleed after installation.

steps.title: Separate local drag from a release problem
steps.body: Apply and release the brakes, then check wheel rotation. One dragging wheel points toward its caliper or parking-brake mechanism. For excessive drag at multiple wheels, check stoplamp-switch installation and pedal free play, then follow the compensator-port test to loosen and move the master cylinder away from the booster. Drag disappearing directs booster replacement; drag remaining directs master-cylinder replacement. Also consider hoses, caliper guides and the hydraulic control unit through the symptom chart.

watchFor.title: Noise that can be normal
watchFor.body: First-application squeal can result from humidity and cold pads. Intermittent squeal can accompany temperature, water, mud or snow. Low-speed groaning during light brake application is also listed as acceptable.

watchFor.title: Noise requiring inspection
watchFor.body: Continuous squeal requires pad inspection. Continuous grinding or moaning requires checking pads, discs and hardware against specifications. For rattles, inspect guide pins and bolts, pad clips and springs, and disc-shield fastening.

watchFor.title: Shudder after releasing the pedal
watchFor.body: Use the brake-drag branch when vibration occurs after release, rather than assuming the applied-brake vibration test identifies the cause.

notes: Use the linked Brake System Pressure Bleeding instructions whenever bleeding is directed. Choose the sequence for the fitted calipers and steering position.

diagnostics.finding: The red brake and yellow ABS indicators are illuminated together.
diagnostics.meaning: ABS diagnostic trouble codes may explain the warning combination.
diagnostics.next: Retrieve the codes and follow ABS and stability-control diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: The red brake indicator stays on or never illuminates.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible sources include fluid-level or parking-brake switches, wiring, the instrument cluster or body control module.
diagnostics.next: Follow instrumentation diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Steering-wheel nibble or pedal pulsation follows vehicle speed during braking.
diagnostics.meaning: A brake or suspension concern is indicated.
diagnostics.next: Follow Pinpoint Test A rather than treating every pulsation as ABS operation.

diagnostics.finding: Pedal effort remains excessive.
diagnostics.meaning: Vacuum supply, the check valve, booster or brake pads may be involved.
diagnostics.next: Complete the booster tests and inspect pads as directed.

verification.title: Repeat the relevant operating check
verification.body: Retest the original complaint after repair. Use the prescribed road test for vibration, wheel-rotation check for drag and component retests for vacuum assistance or bypass.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the reproduced symptom, decisive measurement or isolation result, repair and final check. If vibration cannot be reproduced, record that outcome without claiming a component repair.

procedures.purpose: Symptom charts, vibration diagnosis and all three component tests.
Diagnostic methods and preliminary checks.
Correct lifting points and vehicle support.
Red brake-warning indicator diagnosis.
Tire-related pulling diagnosis.
Suspension and alignment diagnosis.
Permitted brake-disc machining.
Front-disc replacement for 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications.
Rear-disc replacement for 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications.
2.3L EcoBoost booster removal and installation.
3.7L Duratec booster removal and installation.
5.0L booster removal and installation.
Engine diagnosis for low vacuum without a brake vacuum pump.
Master-cylinder removal, installation and tube fastening.
Correct stoplamp-switch installation.
Pressure-bleed after hydraulic work using the fitted caliper and left- or right-hand-drive sequence; follow the additional scan-tool cycle when a new hydraulic control unit requires it.

guides.title: Machine eligible brake discs with an on-vehicle lathe
guides.summary: Restore excessively corroded or pitted brake-disc surfaces only after confirming that their design and remaining thickness permit machining.
guides.introduction: Brake pads grip the disc’s friction surfaces to slow the wheel. Machining removes metal from those surfaces, so it can address excessive corrosion, rust or pitting only while sufficient disc thickness remains. This job requires an on-vehicle brake lathe and an operator who can correctly align and control it.
guides.why: Lathe alignment establishes the finished disc’s running accuracy. Thickness checks protect the remaining usable material, while correct cutting depth controls surface finish and tool heating. Machining is expressly excluded as a treatment for brake noise.

when.summary: When excessive disc-surface corrosion, rust or pitting warrants machining and the disc passes eligibility checks.
notes: Do not machine discs with cross-drilled friction surfaces.
Squeal, squeak, moan, groan, grunt or grinding concerns require brake diagnosis instead.

prepare.title: Arrange specialist machining capability
prepare.detail: Use an on-vehicle lathe only. Read its operating instructions and review vehicle preparation, mounting, runout adjustment, cutting, opposite-side operation and lathe maintenance before starting.

prepare.title: Have measuring and support equipment ready
prepare.detail: Provide disc-thickness measurement equipment, mechanic’s wire to support the caliper assembly, and a dial indicator if the lathe lacks automatic runout adjustment.

prepare.title: Identify the fitted brake system
prepare.detail: Obtain the applicable minimum disc thickness, wheel and brake fastening procedures, and service-mode instructions for any fitted electric parking brake or electric brake booster.

steps.title: Make the brake system safe and expose the disc
steps.body: Activate brake system service mode before work on an equipped electric brake booster system. For rear-disc work with an electric parking brake, activate its service mode. Remove the wheel and tire using the applicable procedure.

steps.title: Confirm that machining is permitted
steps.body: Check the friction-surface design and measure disc thickness. Do not machine a cross-drilled disc or one thinner than the minimum disc thickness plus 0.6 mm (0.0236 in).

steps.title: Prepare the disc and support the caliper
steps.body: Remove the caliper and anchor-plate assembly bolts and support the assembly with mechanic’s wire. Leave the brake hose connected and unloaded. Remove, clean and reinstall the disc using the applicable brake-disc procedure.

steps.title: Mount the adapter and lathe
steps.body: If the opposing disc could rotate during machining, secure it with two wheel nuts finger tight. Fit the hub adapter using the fastening arrangement specified for the actual hub; a five-stud hub uses five wheel nuts. Install the lathe.

steps.title: Establish correct alignment
steps.body: Automatic runout adjustment is preferred. Otherwise, adjust lathe oscillation with a dial indicator on a suitable surface. The target is 0.000 mm (0.000 in), with a maximum indicated runout of 0.050 mm (0.002 in).

steps.title: Machine and clean the disc
steps.body: Center the cutting head, adjust the bits and install the chip deflector/silencer. Use the specified cut depth of 0.10–0.40 mm (0.004–0.015 in). Follow the lathe’s cutting sequence, then remove the lathe, silencer, adapter and wheel nuts. Remove metal shavings.

steps.title: Measure again and reassemble
steps.body: Measure finished thickness; replace the disc if below its minimum specification. Remove any temporary opposing-disc nuts. Refit the caliper assembly and wheel with the applicable fastening instructions. Existing pads may remain if their friction material meets specification. Deactivate electric parking brake service mode if activated.

watchFor.title: Unexpected brake application
watchFor.body: Omitting the required service mode can cause brake application; an electric brake booster system may also register a false leak fault and lose braking performance.

watchFor.title: Unsuitable cutting depth
watchFor.body: Overly light cuts heat and wear the bits faster; overly heavy cuts produce poor surface finish.

notes: Use the applicable Mustang brake procedure; unrelated Raptor and other vehicle branches are not instructions for this job.

diagnostics.finding: Excessive corrosion, rust or pitting on the braking surface
diagnostics.meaning: Machining may be appropriate if design and thickness permit it.
diagnostics.next: Complete the eligibility checks before mounting the lathe.

diagnostics.finding: Brake noise without an established machining justification
diagnostics.meaning: Noise alone does not authorize disc machining.
diagnostics.next: Follow brake-system diagnosis and testing.

verification.title: Record the thickness decision
verification.body: Record initial and finished thickness against the applicable minimum, and whether the disc was retained or replaced.

verification.title: Confirm setup and restoration
verification.body: Correct lathe adjustment removes the need for separate runout and thickness-variation measurements. Confirm temporary hardware is removed, assemblies are secured and electric parking brake service mode is deactivated if used.

procedures.purpose: Disc eligibility, on-vehicle lathe preparation and machining, final thickness decision, and brake reassembly.

guides.title: Bleed Brake Components on the 5.2L Mustang
guides.summary: Prime a newly installed master cylinder and complete the required system bleeding after opening a brake hydraulic connection.
guides.introduction: The master cylinder turns brake-pedal movement into hydraulic pressure. Air compresses within that hydraulic circuit, so removing it is part of restoring the system after component work. This job has two paths: a new master cylinder needs priming through a bleeding set, while a disconnected caliper, wheel cylinder, hose or tube requires system pressure bleeding.
guides.why: Priming a new master cylinder limits the air introduced into the rest of the brake circuit. Clear, bubble-free fluid at its bleeding tubes establishes the priming endpoint, but system bleeding must still follow. Cleanliness also matters: removing the reservoir cap and opening tube connections creates opportunities for foreign material to enter the hydraulics.

when.summary: After installing a new master cylinder or disconnecting a brake hydraulic component.
notes: Pressure bleeding is required whenever a hydraulic brake component has been disconnected.
Use the master-cylinder priming steps only for that component; the other listed components proceed to system bleeding.

prepare.title: Arrange the bleeding equipment
prepare.detail: Have a master cylinder bleeding set, an assistant to operate the pedal, and the equipment and capability required by the Brake System Pressure Bleeding procedure.

prepare.title: Obtain the correct fluid and specifications
prepare.detail: Use clean brake fluid specified in Brake System—General Information. Obtain that section's brake-tube fitting tightening specifications before opening the connections.

steps.title: Clean and fill the reservoir
steps.body: For master-cylinder priming, make sure the area around the reservoir cap is clean and free of foreign material. Remove the cap and fill with the specified clean brake fluid.

steps.title: Fit the master-cylinder bleeding set
steps.body: Loosen and remove the brake-tube fittings, then install the bleeding set as shown in the [component bleeding procedure](#/document/G1694693). The set provides the temporary fluid path used to prime the cylinder.

steps.title: Purge the master cylinder
steps.body: Have the assistant pump the brake pedal slowly. Continue until clear, bubble-free fluid flows from the brake tubes. Use that visible condition to judge completion rather than choosing an arbitrary number of pedal strokes.

steps.title: Restore the brake-tube connections
steps.body: Remove the bleeding set, reconnect the brake-tube fittings and tighten them to the specified values. Refill the reservoir with the specified clean brake fluid before proceeding.

steps.title: Complete system pressure bleeding
steps.body: Follow the referenced Brake System Bleeding and Brake System Pressure Bleeding procedures. This remains necessary after master-cylinder priming and is the required path after disconnecting a caliper, wheel cylinder, hose or tube.

watchFor.title: Spilled brake fluid
watchFor.body: Immediately wash any affected component with cold water if brake fluid is spilled.

watchFor.title: Bubbles still present
watchFor.body: Fluid containing visible bubbles has not reached the stated master-cylinder priming endpoint.

notes: Fluid specifications, fitting tightening values and the full pressure-bleeding sequence belong to the referenced technical procedures.

diagnostics.finding: Clear, bubble-free fluid flows during master-cylinder priming.
diagnostics.meaning: The local priming endpoint has been reached; this does not establish that the entire brake system is bled.
diagnostics.next: Restore the tube connections, refill the reservoir and complete system pressure bleeding.

verification.title: Record both bleeding stages
verification.body: For a new master cylinder, record that bubble-free flow was obtained and that system pressure bleeding was completed. For other disconnected components, record completion of pressure bleeding.

verification.title: Confirm restoration
verification.body: Confirm the bleeding set has been removed, the brake-tube fittings tightened to specification and the reservoir refilled as directed.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L brake component bleeding: master-cylinder priming and the required system-bleeding path after hydraulic component disconnection.

guides.title: Replace a four-piston front brake caliper
guides.summary: Remove and refit the four-piston front caliper on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L or 5.0L engine, renew the required fasteners and seals, and pressure-bleed all four brakes.
guides.introduction: Four pistons can put a serious squeeze on a brake disc; unfortunately, they cannot squeeze the air out of their own plumbing. I’ll walk you through reaching the caliper, removing its pads and hose connection, fitting the replacement, and finishing the pressure bleed. The caliper itself comes off with two mounting bolts. Giving those bolts and the hydraulic connection the right treatment is where the care belongs.
guides.why: The caliper uses brake-fluid pressure to push its pistons against the pads, which grip the rotating brake disc and slow the car. Disconnecting its hose opens that hydraulic circuit, so replacement includes sealing the exposed openings, fitting new hose sealing washers and caliper mounting bolts, and bleeding out air before returning the car to service.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang four piston front brake caliper replacement
brake caliper flow bolt sealing washers

when.summary: Use this procedure when an established repair calls for removing or replacing a four-piston front brake caliper.
notes: Applies to 2015 Mustang models with the 2.3L or 5.0L engine and four-piston front calipers.
This is a replacement procedure. It does not establish a caliper fault from a noise, pedal complaint or braking symptom.

prepare.title: Confirm the job and its boundary
prepare.detail: Confirm the fitted front caliper has four pistons, identify left-hand drive (LHD) or right-hand drive (RHD), and determine whether the rear calipers incorporate the parking brake. This guide covers front-caliper replacement and its required pressure bleed. A job that also replaces the master cylinder or hydraulic control unit needs its separate service procedure; stop here rather than treating this bleed as completion of that additional work.

prepare.title: Have the replacement parts ready
prepare.detail: Obtain the correct replacement caliper, two new caliper mounting bolts and two new brake-hose sealing washers for each caliper being removed. If fitting new pads, have the complete pad kit, including its new hardware, supplied lubricant and lubricant instruction sheet.

prepare.title: Arrange access and tools
prepare.detail: Have a suitable hoist, or a workshop jack and floor stands of adequate capacity, plus wheel chocks. You need a brake pad spreader, suitable fastener tools, torque wrenches covering the wheel and caliper fasteners and the low bleeder torques, and suitable seals for open hydraulic connections. Pressure bleeding requires a Brake/Clutch System Pressure Bleeder/Filler with a compatible reservoir adapter, its operating instructions, a hose and a clean fluid container.

prepare.title: Gather fluids, lubricant and protection
prepare.detail: Use Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid, PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2. Have enough clean fluid in the pressure bleeder to complete all four wheel ends. For wheel refitting, use Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, only at the wheel pilot interface. Wear eye and ear protection and protective gloves when handling sharp parts. Read the materials’ safety information and keep cold water ready to wash brake fluid off paint immediately.

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start before working around the car
steps.body:
If equipped, disable remote start through the central display at Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle.
Before working under the hood at the brake-fluid reservoir, inspect the cooling fans for cracks, damage or separation; a damaged fan must be replaced before underhood work continues. Fans can operate with the ignition off, so keep clear and disable them before any work nearby. These precautions come before reaching into the engine compartment. See [service safety precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Secure the Mustang and lift at the marked points
steps.body:
Work on a hard, level surface. Set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground before jacking. Check that the jack, stands or hoist can carry the vehicle’s weight, including cargo and modifications.
For the hoist method, position the vehicle with the transmission in Neutral. Locate the triangles stamped into the body structure: they identify the lifting points along the sides near the front and rear wheels. Position the lifting equipment at those points, keeping adapters and arms clear of suspension, steering, exhaust, brackets and the axle or rear cover. Check underbody clearance before entering a drive-on lift.
If using a workshop jack, support the raised vehicle on floor stands before working. Never get underneath a car held only by a jack. Do not use the emergency wheel-change jack for this repair or lift against either bumper. The later rear parking-brake cycling must be possible without compromising vehicle support. See [jacking and lifting](#/document/G1663631).

steps.title: Remove the wheel at the caliper being replaced
steps.body:
With the vehicle securely supported, remove the five wheel nuts and lift the wheel and tire assembly away. Do not use heat on a seized wheel nut; it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing.
The other wheels must also come off for the full-system bleed. You can remove them now if the car is securely supported for access to all four brakes, or remove them during the bleeding setup below. Tire removal from the wheel is unnecessary. See [wheel removal and refitting](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Remove the pad spring, pin clip and two pins
steps.body:
At the exposed front caliper, remove the brake pad spring from across the pad opening. Next remove the brake pad pin clip, then withdraw both brake pad pins. Keep these parts together for refitting unless a new pad kit will replace them.
These are the pad-retaining parts, not the two caliper mounting bolts behind the caliper. I like to keep those two families of hardware separate; a tray is cheaper than a game of ‘where the hell did that clip go?’ See [four-piston pad removal](#/document/G1693790).

steps.title: Retract the pistons and take out the pads
steps.body:
Use a brake pad spreader between the pads to push them apart and compress the caliper pistons, as shown by the spreader acting through the caliper opening. Then remove the pads.
This clears the pads before the caliper’s hydraulic connection and mounting bolts are disturbed.

steps.title: Disconnect the brake hose and seal the openings
steps.body:
Remove the flow bolt securing the brake-hose fitting to the caliper. This bolt forms the hydraulic connection through the hose fitting. Separate the fitting from the caliper and discard both sealing washers; the joint has one washer on each side of the fitting.
Seal every exposed hydraulic opening as the connection is separated, and position the disconnected hose aside. Keep the openings protected until reconnection. If brake fluid reaches paint, immediately wash the affected area with cold water. See [caliper replacement](#/document/G1693778).

steps.title: Remove the two mounting bolts and lift off the caliper
steps.body:
Support the caliper while removing its two mounting bolts from the rear mounting points, then take the caliper away from the disc. Discard both bolts.
The mounting bolts are the two fasteners attaching the caliper to the vehicle behind the disc-facing body. Do not confuse them with the other bolts visible on the caliper assembly.

steps.title: Fit the replacement caliper with new mounting bolts
steps.body:
Position the replacement caliper over the disc at its mounting points. Install two new mounting bolts and tighten them to 115 Nm (85 lb.ft).
Keep the hydraulic connection sealed until you are ready to attach the hose.

steps.title: Reconnect the hose with two new sealing washers
steps.body:
Remove the temporary seals as you reconnect the hose. Assemble the flow bolt with a new sealing washer on each side of the hose fitting, and attach the fitting to the caliper in its original position.
Tighten the flow bolt to 40 Nm (30 lb.ft). The hose connection and mounting bolts have different torques; this is no place for one heroic setting on the wrench.

steps.title: Refit the pads and their retaining hardware
steps.body:
Reverse the pad-removal actions: position the pads in the caliper, install the two brake pad pins, refit the pin clip and reinstall the pad spring. Check that the pins, clip and spring are seated in their retaining positions.
If installing new pads, use all new hardware and lubricant supplied with the pad kit. Apply that lubricant only as directed by the kit’s instruction sheet. See [four-piston pad installation](#/document/G1693790).

steps.title: Seat the pads and check the reservoir
steps.body:
With the caliper, hose connection and pad hardware assembled, depress the brake pedal. Check the brake-fluid reservoir and top up as necessary with PM-20 fluid meeting WSS-M6C65-A2.
This completes the pad-refitting action; the hydraulic system still needs the pressure bleed that follows.

steps.title: Fit the pressure-bleeder adapter
steps.body:
Clean the area around the brake-fluid reservoir cap so dirt cannot fall inside, then remove the cap. Check the level against the reservoir’s MIN and MAX marks and fill with clean specified brake fluid.
Install the compatible pressure-bleeder adapter on the reservoir according to the equipment manufacturer’s instructions. Attach the bleeder tank hose to the adapter fitting and make sure the tank contains enough clean specified fluid for the entire bleed. See [pressure-bleeding setup](#/document/G2361881).

steps.title: Apply pressure and expose the remaining brakes
steps.body:
Open the bleeder tank valve and apply 207–345 kPa (30–50 psi) to the brake system.
If any wheels remain installed, remove their five nuts and wheel assemblies with the vehicle securely supported as described earlier. All four wheel ends must be accessible. Keep the vehicle stable independently of the parking brake, because the applicable rear-caliper procedure requires releasing and applying it.

steps.title: Choose the correct wheel-end bleeding order
steps.body:
Left and right mean the vehicle’s sides as viewed from the driver’s seat facing forward.
For LHD: 1. right rear; 2. left rear; 3. right front; 4. left front.
For RHD: 1. left rear; 2. right rear; 3. left front; 4. right front.
Follow the appropriate order. At each four-piston front caliper, bleed the inner screw first and the outer screw second. ‘Inner’ means toward the vehicle’s centre; ‘outer’ means toward the wheel. See [bleeding sequence](#/document/G2361881).

steps.title: Prepare the catch hose at the first wheel end
steps.body:
Remove the bleeder screw’s protective cap, if fitted. Partially fill a clean fluid container with clean specified brake fluid. Put the hose’s discharge end beneath the fluid surface and connect its other end to the bleeder screw.
Keep the discharge end submerged so you can watch the outgoing fluid and bubbles.

steps.title: Bleed the screw until the fluid is clear and bubble-free
steps.body:
Loosen the bleeder screw 180°, or half a turn. Leave it open until clear, bubble-free brake fluid flows through the hose, then close the screw.
Disconnect the hose and tighten the screw to the correct value: rear caliper, 11 Nm (97 lb.in); four-piston front caliper, 8 Nm (71 lb.in). These small values are in pound-inches, not pound-feet. Move the fluid container clear when finished at the screw. See [fluid and bleeder specifications](#/document/G1694687).

steps.title: Complete the normal bleed at all remaining wheel ends
steps.body:
Repeat the catch-hose setup and half-turn bleeding operation at the remaining wheel ends in the selected LHD or RHD order. Continue each screw until its discharge is clear and bubble-free, then close it, disconnect the hose and torque it.
At each front caliper, complete the inner screw before repeating the operation at the outer screw. Tighten each front screw to 8 Nm (71 lb.in), and each rear screw to 11 Nm (97 lb.in). Maintain the pressure-bleeder supply throughout.

steps.title: Cycle and rebleed rear integral parking-brake calipers, if fitted
steps.body:
If the rear calipers incorporate the parking brake, their internal fluid passages require an additional operation. With the vehicle securely supported, apply and release the parking brake five times.
At the rear bleeder, connect the hose with its discharge end submerged in the fluid container, loosen the screw 180° and let fluid flow until it is clear and bubble-free. Close the screw, disconnect the hose and tighten it to 11 Nm (97 lb.in).
Complete this additional bleed at both rear calipers, retaining their relative order for LHD or RHD, and repeat the cycling and bleeding as necessary. Skip this additional phase when the rear calipers do not have an integral parking brake.

steps.title: Replace the bleeder caps and check the closed connections
steps.body:
Refit every bleeder screw cap that was removed. Before putting the wheels back, confirm that both front bleeders at each four-piston caliper and the rear bleeders are closed and tightened.
Look at the repaired hose joint and bleeder connections for escaping fluid while the system remains pressurised. A visible leak means the job cannot proceed to driving; correct the connection and complete bleeding again as required. This is an assembly completion check, not a diagnosis of other brake faults.

steps.title: Clean the wheel interfaces and lubricate only the pilot
steps.body:
For every removed wheel, clean corrosion, dirt and foreign material from its flat mounting face and the corresponding hub or brake-disc mounting face. Make sure any rotor-to-hub fasteners are secure and do not obstruct those faces.
Also clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the round centre opening that locates it on the hub. Apply a thin film of Motorcraft XL-2 nickel anti-seize only at the interface between that bore and the hub pilot.
Keep anti-seize off the flat wheel-to-disc mounting faces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and disc friction surfaces. The little locating bore gets the lubricant; the rest does not need a damn paint job. See [wheel installation](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Fit the wheels finger-tight and lower the vehicle
steps.body:
Position each wheel on its hub and install all five nuts finger-tight. Keep the wheel-stud and wheel-nut threads clean and dry.
Before lowering, reapply the parking brake after completing the rear-caliper cycling. Restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground, and keep the vehicle restrained afterward; do not lower an unrestrained vehicle in Neutral.
Clear tools and equipment from beneath the car, lower it safely and remove the lifting supports as appropriate. Final wheel-nut tightening must take place with the vehicle resting on its tires. Keep the stationary car secured while finishing the work.

steps.title: Release bleeder pressure and finish the reservoir
steps.body:
Close the bleeder tank valve and release the system pressure before removing the pressure-bleeding equipment and reservoir adapter.
Fill the reservoir with clean PM-20 brake fluid meeting WSS-M6C65-A2, checking its MIN and MAX markings, and install the reservoir cap. Immediately wash any brake-fluid spill on paint with cold water.

steps.title: Torque all wheel nuts in a star pattern
steps.body:
With the car resting on its tires, tighten every wheel’s nuts in a star/cross pattern to 204 Nm (150 lb.ft), using clean, dry threads.
The illustrated five-nut sequence is top, lower left, upper right, upper left, lower right when viewed from outside the wheel. Crossing the wheel as you tighten helps it seat evenly and avoids brake-disc runout that can contribute to roughness, shudder and vibration.

steps.title: Confirm brake operation and restore the car for use
steps.body:
Depress the brake pedal after final assembly and confirm that it provides braking resistance before moving the car. Recheck the reservoir level and inspect the repaired hydraulic connection for leakage. An abnormal pedal or a leak means the repair is not ready for driving.
Confirm the wheel nuts are torqued, the reservoir cap is installed and all tools and lifting equipment are clear. Restore the transmission and parking brake from their service positions, and remove wheel chocks only when the car is secured and ready to move. Restore remote start to its previous setting after all service work is finished, if it was enabled beforehand.
Once these completion checks are satisfactory, road-test the vehicle to confirm braking operation. Arrange to retighten every refitted wheel’s nuts within 160 km (100 mi).

watchFor.title: Brake fluid and open connections
watchFor.body: Seal all hydraulic openings during replacement. Immediately wash brake fluid off paint with cold water.

watchFor.title: Single-use mounting bolts and washers
watchFor.body: Discard the two removed caliper mounting bolts and both hose sealing washers. Install new replacements; the flow bolt itself is not identified for discard.

watchFor.title: Three very different torque ranges
watchFor.body: Caliper mounting bolts: 115 Nm (85 lb.ft). Hose flow bolt: 40 Nm (30 lb.ft). Bleeders: front four-piston 8 Nm (71 lb.in), rear 11 Nm (97 lb.in). Keep pound-inches and pound-feet distinct.

watchFor.title: Parking-brake release during bleeding
watchFor.body: Rear integral parking-brake calipers require five apply/release cycles and additional bleeding. Vehicle support must remain secure with the parking brake released.

watchFor.title: Wheel cleanliness is a safety requirement
watchFor.body: Debris between mounting faces can prevent proper seating and allow nuts to loosen. Keep those faces clean and anti-seize confined to the pilot interface.

notes: The caliper and pad instructions apply to both listed engines only when four-piston front calipers are fitted.
Wheel-nut final tightening is 204 Nm (150 lb.ft) on clean, dry threads with the vehicle resting on its tires. Retighten within 160 km (100 mi) after refitting.
The pad spring, pin clip and pins refit in reverse removal order; use the new hardware and lubricant instructions when installing a new pad kit.

diagnostics.finding: The car is left-hand drive.
diagnostics.meaning: Its prescribed wheel-end bleeding order starts at the right rear.
diagnostics.next: Bleed right rear, left rear, right front, then left front; at each front caliper, do the inner screw before the outer.

diagnostics.finding: The car is right-hand drive.
diagnostics.meaning: Its prescribed wheel-end bleeding order starts at the left rear.
diagnostics.next: Bleed left rear, right rear, left front, then right front; at each front caliper, do the inner screw before the outer.

diagnostics.finding: A rear caliper incorporates the parking brake.
diagnostics.meaning: Its internal fluid path needs parking-brake operation during bleeding.
diagnostics.next: Apply and release the parking brake five times, rebleed the rear calipers until the discharge is clear and bubble-free, and repeat as necessary.

diagnostics.finding: Bubbles remain in the discharge hose.
diagnostics.meaning: That bleeder has not yet reached the required clear, bubble-free endpoint.
diagnostics.next: Continue the prescribed pressure bleed with adequate clean fluid in the equipment. Do not move on as though that screw is finished.

diagnostics.finding: Fluid escapes from the reassembled hose connection or a closed bleeder.
diagnostics.meaning: The hydraulic assembly has not passed its completion check.
diagnostics.next: Keep the vehicle out of service, correct the leaking connection and complete the required bleeding before reassessing readiness.

diagnostics.finding: The pedal remains abnormal after assembly and bleeding.
diagnostics.meaning: The replacement work has not established that the car is ready to drive; the pedal complaint alone does not identify a failed component.
diagnostics.next: Do not road-test. Resolve the assembly or bleeding problem and obtain further brake-system diagnosis if it persists.

verification.title: Mechanical assembly
verification.body: Confirm two new caliper mounting bolts at 115 Nm (85 lb.ft), two new hose sealing washers with the flow bolt at 40 Nm (30 lb.ft), and correctly seated pads, pins, clip and spring.

verification.title: Bleeding completion
verification.body: Confirm all four wheel ends were bled in the correct LHD/RHD order, each front inner screw preceded its outer screw, and applicable rear parking-brake cycling and rebleeding were completed. Front bleeders must be at 8 Nm (71 lb.in), rear bleeders at 11 Nm (97 lb.in).

verification.title: Hydraulic closure
verification.body: Confirm the bleeder caps and reservoir cap are fitted, the reservoir level is correct, pressure-bleeding equipment is removed, and the repaired connections show no leakage. Check pedal operation before moving.

verification.title: Wheels and return to service
verification.body: Confirm clean mounting faces, lubricant confined to the pilot interface and all wheel nuts tightened in a star pattern to 204 Nm (150 lb.ft) with the car on its tires. Complete the road test only after the stationary checks are satisfactory, and retighten the nuts within 160 km (100 mi).

Pressure-bleeder setup, operating pressure, LHD/RHD sequence, inner-before-outer front bleeding, rear parking-brake cycling and hydraulic closure.
Specified brake fluid and the exact four-piston front and rear bleeder screw torques.
Wheel removal, mounting-face and pilot-bore cleaning, restricted anti-seize application, wheel-nut torque, tightening pattern and retightening requirement.

stepGroups.summary: Prevent startup, support the vehicle, remove the wheel and clear the caliper of its pads.

stepGroups.summary: Seal the hydraulic openings, renew mounting bolts and washers, and restore the hose and pads.

guides.title: Replace a 6-piston front brake caliper on the 5.0L
guides.summary: Remove and refit the 6-piston front caliper with new mounting bolts and hose washers, then pressure-bleed the brake system.
guides.introduction: The front brake caliper uses hydraulic pressure to press the pads against the brake disc. Removing it separates both its mechanical mounting and its brake-hose connection. This procedure covers the 5.0L application equipped with 6-piston front calipers, including the required pad-removal prerequisite, replacement hardware and final bleeding operation.
guides.why: The mounting bolts secure the caliper, while the washers seal the hydraulic hose connection. Both have explicit discard instructions, so they must be replaced during installation. Opening the hose connection also makes brake-system bleeding a required finishing phase. Clean, sealed openings help protect the hydraulic circuit while it is disconnected.

when.summary: When an established repair requires removal or replacement of a 6-piston front brake caliper.
notes: This procedure gives the replacement path; it does not diagnose the cause of a braking complaint.

prepare.title: Prepare the correct hardware and tools
prepare.detail: Have new caliper mounting bolts, new brake-hose sealing washers, suitable tools and torque equipment. The removed mounting bolts and washers must not return to service.

prepare.title: Arrange hydraulic protection and bleeding
prepare.detail: Provide suitable means to seal every opened connection and the equipment and capability for Brake System Pressure Bleeding in section 206-00. Have the linked 6-piston brake-pad procedure available for removal and installation.

steps.title: Remove the brake pads
steps.body: Follow Brake Pads — Vehicles With: 6-Piston Brake Caliper before removing the caliper. This is the first required phase and provides the equipment-specific pad handling and installation details.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the caliper
steps.body: Remove the brake-hose flow bolt, disconnect the hose and discard the sealing washers. Seal all openings. Remove the two caliper mounting bolts, discard them and remove the caliper. If brake fluid reaches paintwork, immediately wash the affected area with cold water.

steps.title: Refit with replacement hardware
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Install the caliper with new mounting bolts and tighten them to 115 Nm. Reconnect the hose with new sealing washers and tighten the flow bolt to 40 Nm. Reinstall the pads using the dedicated 6-piston procedure.

steps.title: Complete pressure bleeding
steps.body: Perform Brake System Pressure Bleeding after reassembly. Follow that complete procedure for the hydraulic finishing phase; bolting the caliper back into place does not complete a repair that opened the brake circuit.

watchFor.title: Old hardware mixed with new parts
watchFor.body: Keep the discarded caliper mounting bolts and hose sealing washers separate from installation hardware. Follow the flow-bolt and washer instructions for the exact fitted caliper.

watchFor.title: Fluid on paint or exposed openings
watchFor.body: Wash paint contamination immediately with cold water and keep disconnected hydraulic openings sealed.

notes: The illustrated pair of mounting bolts is the pair that must be discarded.

verification.title: Confirm the completed assembly
verification.body: Verify installation of new mounting bolts and sealing washers, the specified fastener tightening and completion of the pad installation.

verification.title: Confirm hydraulic completion
verification.body: Confirm that the required brake-system pressure-bleeding procedure has been completed before closing the repair.

procedures.purpose: 5.0L 6-piston front caliper removal and installation, including discarded hardware, tightening and the pressure-bleeding requirement.
Equipment-specific brake-pad removal before caliper service and pad installation during reassembly.

authoring.method: Codex source review of fastener language and required HCU commissioning

guides.title: Replace the front brake caliper with the SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Remove and refit the SVT front caliper with new mounting bolts and hose washers, then pressure-bleed the brake system.
guides.introduction: The front brake caliper converts hydraulic pressure into clamping force at the brake pads. This job separates the caliper from its brake hose and mounting, then removes the pad-retaining components so they can be installed during reassembly. Opening the hose connection makes restoration of the hydraulic system a required part of the repair.
guides.why: The hose connection washers and caliper mounting bolts must be discarded during removal and replaced for installation. Sealing every open connection protects the hydraulic system while it is exposed. Pressure bleeding is required after reassembly because reconnecting the hose alone does not complete the hydraulic work.
searchTerms: SVT Performance Package front brake caliper replacement
SVT brake pad pins and spring retainer

when.summary: When an established front-brake repair requires removal or replacement of the SVT Performance Package caliper.

prepare.title: Arrange brake-service capability
prepare.detail: Provide safe access and support for front-brake work. Have hydraulic-brake service capability and the equipment and complete instructions for Brake System Pressure Bleeding available before disconnecting the hose.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement parts and sealing equipment
prepare.detail: Have new hose-connection washers, new caliper mounting bolts, suitable means of sealing openings and appropriate torque tools. If fitting new pads, retain all hardware, lubricant and instructions supplied with the pad kit.

steps.title: Disconnect the brake hose
steps.body: Remove the caliper flow bolt and disconnect the hose. Discard the washers and seal all openings. If brake fluid reaches paintwork, immediately wash the affected area with cold water.

steps.title: Remove the caliper
steps.body: Remove the caliper mounting bolts and take off the caliper. Discard those bolts and keep the replacements ready for reassembly.

steps.title: Remove the pad components
steps.body: Remove the brake pad pins, followed by the pads, then the brake pad spring retainer clip. Keep the component positions clear so the reverse sequence can be followed during assembly.

steps.title: Prepare the contact surfaces
steps.body: Clean the pad-to-caliper contact surfaces and apply the lubricant supplied with the brake pad kit as directed by its instruction sheet. If installing new pads, install all new hardware supplied with them.

steps.title: Reassemble and reconnect
steps.body: Reverse removal to install the spring retainer clip, pads and pins, then the caliper. Tighten the new mounting bolts to 136 lb.ft (185 Nm). Reconnect the hose with new washers and tighten the flow bolt to 35 lb.ft (48 Nm).

steps.title: Pressure-bleed the brake system
steps.body: Complete the required Brake System Pressure Bleeding procedure after reconnecting the hose. Use that procedure for the bleeding method and its completion requirements.

watchFor.title: Exposed hydraulic openings
watchFor.body: Keep every opening sealed while disconnected; do not leave the hose or caliper connection exposed during the remaining work.

watchFor.title: Discarded parts returning to service
watchFor.body: The removed hose washers and caliper mounting bolts are not installation parts. Reassembly requires replacements.

notes: This procedure is specific to the SVT Performance Package front caliper. Its fasteners and tightening values must remain with this brake configuration.

verification.title: Check mechanical assembly
verification.body: Confirm installation of the pad spring clip, pads and pins, new caliper bolts and new hose washers, with both connections tightened to their respective specifications.

verification.title: Record hydraulic completion
verification.body: Record completion of the required pressure-bleeding procedure after hose reconnection. Do not treat mechanical assembly alone as completion of the repair.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L SVT Performance Package front caliper removal, pad-component transfer, installation and required pressure-bleeding referral.

guides.title: Replace the front brake caliper anchor plate with 2-piston calipers
guides.summary: Remove the wheel, support the caliper, remove the pads and clips, and replace the anchor plate with new mounting bolts. Reassemble with the correct clip orientation and brake and wheel tightening values.
guides.introduction: The caliper gets the glory for stopping the car; the anchor plate does the unglamorous job of keeping the whole performance in position. I think of it as the brake assembly’s dependable stagehand—with two bolts you absolutely must replace. This guide covers the 2015 Mustang with a 2.3L or 3.7L engine and 2-piston front brake calipers.
guides.why: The anchor plate is the fixed bracket that supports the brake pads and carries the sliding caliper. Replacing it means moving the caliper aside, removing the pads and separating the upper and lower pad clips. Supporting the caliper protects its hose, while new anchor-plate bolts, correctly positioned clips and accurate tightening restore the assembly properly.

when.summary: Use this procedure when anchor-plate removal or replacement is already part of an established front-brake repair.
notes: This procedure applies to the 2-piston front caliper arrangement on 2015 2.3L and 3.7L Mustangs.
Compressing the caliper pistons is an additional branch when fitting new brake pads.

prepare.title: Establish the repair and confirm the brake configuration
prepare.detail: Confirm the vehicle has 2-piston front calipers and obtain the correct replacement anchor plate if replacing it. This is a removal and installation procedure; it does not establish a wear limit or a diagnostic test for deciding whether the plate needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and caliper support
prepare.detail: Use a hoist rated for the vehicle’s weight, including cargo and modifications, and wheel chocks for ground restraint. Have a suitable caliper support hook or hanger ready before removing its bolts. The lifting route here uses a hoist with all four wheels clear of the ground. Review [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631).

prepare.title: Gather fasteners, tools and conditional pad parts
prepare.detail: Have two new anchor-plate mounting bolts, suitable fastener tools and torque tools covering 24 lb.ft (32 Nm), 85 lb.ft (115 Nm) and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). If fitting new pads, have a C-clamp, a worn brake pad, and the replacement pad kit with all its hardware, lubricant and instruction sheet.

prepare.title: Gather the correct materials
prepare.detail: For the wheel pilot interface, use Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2. For any necessary brake-fluid top-up, use Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2. Read the materials’ safety information before use. The fluid specification is in [Specifications](#/document/G1694687).

prepare.title: Protect yourself before starting
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. Keep any cleaning solvents away from ignition sources. Apply the relevant startup and lifting precautions below before beginning access; see [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Restrain the vehicle and prevent an unexpected start
steps.body:
Position the vehicle on a hard, level surface, apply the parking brake and chock the wheels remaining on the ground.
If remote start is fitted, disable it through the central display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before service. Select Neutral for the hoist work while maintaining the parking brake and wheel restraints, then switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle. Keep the engine off throughout the job.

steps.title: Position the hoist at the marked lifting points
steps.body:
Locate the triangles stamped into the body structure beside the lifting points. The lifting illustration shows four locations along the side structure, behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels. Position the hoist adapters at those designated points.
Check that the arms and adapters clear the suspension, steering linkage, exhaust, mounting brackets, stabilizer brackets and axle or rear cover. Never lift against a bumper. If positioning the vehicle on a drive-on lift, first check for underbody interference.
Raise and securely support the vehicle on the correctly positioned hoist with all four wheels fully clear of the ground. Leave the parking brake applied; this front-brake job does not require releasing it. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack, and do not use the emergency wheel-changing jack for this repair.

steps.title: Remove the front wheel and tire
steps.body: Remove the five wheel nuts and take off the wheel and tire to expose the front brake assembly. Do not apply heat to a seized wheel nut: it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. Set the wheel aside for cleaning before refitting. The full wheel procedure is [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Remove the caliper guide-pin bolts and support the caliper
steps.body:
Identify the two guide-pin bolts at the upper and lower ends of the caliper. These attach the movable caliper to its carrier; they are separate from the anchor plate’s mounting bolts.
Arrange the support hanger, remove both guide-pin bolts, and lift the caliper away from the pads. Hang or support it beside the assembly with the brake hose still connected. Its weight must be carried by the support, never by the hose. Do not disconnect the hose for this operation. See [2-Piston Brake Pads](#/document/G1693786).

steps.title: Record the pad positions, then remove both pads
steps.body: Before disturbing the pads, note how each sits in the carrier and which pad is on each side of the brake disc. Remove the inner and outer pads from the anchor plate, keeping their positions identifiable if they will be reused. The disc stays in place.

steps.title: Remove and identify the upper and lower pad clips
steps.body:
Remove the clips from the upper and lower pad-contact positions on the anchor plate. These clips form the seats for the ends of the pads.
Compare the two clips and identify the one with the tab. Keep it identified as the upper clip: the tabbed clip must go at the top when the brake is assembled.

steps.title: Remove the anchor plate and discard its two bolts
steps.body:
With the caliper supported and the pads and clips removed, support the anchor plate and remove its two mounting bolts. They are the upper and lower bolts securing the fixed carrier beside the disc, as shown in the anchor-plate illustration.
Lift away the plate and discard both mounting bolts. Their next career is in the scrap bin. The replacement operation is [Brake Caliper Anchor Plate](#/document/G1693782).

steps.title: Install the anchor plate with new bolts
steps.body: Position the replacement plate, or the original plate if this was removal for access, in its mounting location. Install two new anchor-plate bolts and tighten both to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). Do not reuse the discarded bolts.

steps.title: Refit the two pad clips in their correct positions
steps.body:
Fit the upper and lower clips to their respective seats on the anchor plate. Put the clip with the tab at the top.
If installing new pads, use all the new hardware supplied with the pad kit. Apply the kit’s lubricant according to its instruction sheet; the wheel anti-seize is reserved for the wheel pilot interface.

steps.title: If fitting new pads, retract the caliper pistons
steps.body:
For new pads, use a C-clamp and a worn brake pad to press the two caliper pistons back into their bores. Position the worn pad across the piston faces so the clamp acts through the pad, as illustrated.
Keep the caliper supported and protect the attached hose during this operation. When reinstalling the existing pads, this piston-compression step is not an automatic requirement of anchor-plate replacement.

steps.title: Install the pads and restore the caliper
steps.body:
Install the pads in the anchor-plate clips, restoring their recorded positions when reusing them. Position the caliper over the pads without trapping or loading the brake hose.
Install the two caliper guide-pin bolts and tighten them to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm). Remove the temporary hanger only after the caliper is secured. Check that the hose is free of the support and is not carrying the caliper’s weight.

steps.title: Apply the brake pedal and check the fluid level
steps.body:
With the brake assembly reassembled and the vehicle stationary, depress the brake pedal.
Before checking the reservoir under the hood, confirm the ignition remains off and the key is out. Visually check the cooling fans for damage, cracks or separation; a damaged fan requires replacement before underhood work continues. Fans can operate with the ignition off, so keep clear. If the work would put you near a fan, have it disabled before proceeding.
Check the brake-fluid reservoir level and top up as necessary with Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2.

steps.title: Clean the wheel mounting surfaces and central pilot bore
steps.body:
Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel’s flat mounting surface and the matching hub or brake-disc mounting surface. Check that any fasteners attaching the disc to the hub are secure and do not obstruct the wheel’s seating surface.
Also clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the large center hole that fits over the hub’s locating lip. The bore needs cleaning before lubricant is applied; cleaning only the flat face leaves half the job waiting.

steps.title: Apply a thin film of anti-seize only at the pilot interface
steps.body:
Apply a thin coat of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 only where the wheel pilot bore meets the hub pilot.
Keep it off the flat wheel-to-disc mounting surfaces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and brake-disc friction surfaces. The wheel-stud and wheel-nut threads must remain clean and dry for their tightening specification.

steps.title: Refit the wheel and install the nuts finger tight
steps.body: Position the wheel over the hub pilot and studs, seat it against the mounting surface, and install all five wheel nuts finger tight at this stage. Final tightening is performed with the vehicle resting on its tires.

steps.title: Confirm the parking brake and restore ground restraints while lowering
steps.body:
Before lowering, confirm the parking brake is applied. If it was released for any reason during raised service, reapply it now, while all four wheels are still fully clear of the ground and the vehicle remains securely supported on the hoist.
Lower the vehicle under control. As the tires reach the ground, restore wheel chocks before unloading and withdrawing the hoist supports. Maintain the parking brake and chocks while the transmission remains in Neutral. Once grounded and restrained, restore the transmission to its normal parked position.

steps.title: Tighten the wheel nuts in the five-point star sequence
steps.body:
With the vehicle resting on its tires, tighten the five wheel nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), using clean, dry stud and nut threads.
Follow the illustrated star sequence. With one nut at the top, tighten: top, lower left, upper right, upper left, then lower right. This crosses the wheel rather than moving around adjacent nuts. An incorrect pattern can contribute to brake-disc runout—side-to-side variation as the disc turns—and subsequent brake roughness or vibration.

steps.title: Complete the assembly check and arrange the wheel-nut recheck
steps.body:
Confirm that the brake-pedal application and reservoir check are complete, the caliper support has been removed, and all brake and wheel fasteners have received their correct tightening values.
Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after refitting the wheel. Keep the vehicle parked and restrained until the work and checks are finished.

watchFor.title: The caliper hose must never become the hanger
watchFor.body: If the caliper’s weight pulls on its hose, support and reposition the caliper before proceeding. Allowing it to hang from the hose can damage the hose.

watchFor.title: Two bolt sets, two different tightening values
watchFor.body: The anchor plate requires new mounting bolts tightened to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). The caliper guide-pin bolts tighten to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm). Identify the bolt set by what it attaches before tightening.

watchFor.title: The tabbed pad clip belongs at the top
watchFor.body: Check the physical tab before fitting the pads. The upper and lower clips are different; correct an exchanged clip before restoring the caliper.

watchFor.title: Contamination can compromise wheel seating
watchFor.body: Clean both flat mounting faces and the central pilot bore. Keep anti-seize confined to the pilot interface, with the wheel fastener threads and brake friction surfaces clean.

notes: The brake hose remains connected, and the brake disc remains installed during this anchor-plate operation.
Use the new pad kit’s own hardware and lubrication instructions when replacing pads.
The brake-pedal application and fluid-level check complete reassembly; they do not establish a diagnosis for an unrelated brake complaint.

diagnostics.finding: The tabbed clip is at the bottom, or its original position was lost.
diagnostics.meaning: The clip arrangement needs correction before the pads and caliper are installed.
diagnostics.next: Identify the clip with the tab and install it at the upper anchor-plate position; fit the other clip at the bottom.

diagnostics.finding: New brake pads are being installed.
diagnostics.meaning: The new-pad installation branch applies in addition to anchor-plate replacement.
diagnostics.next: Use all supplied new pad hardware and the kit’s lubricant instructions. Retract the caliper pistons with a C-clamp acting through a worn pad before fitting the caliper over the new pads.

diagnostics.finding: The reservoir needs topping up after assembly.
diagnostics.meaning: The completion check requires the specified brake fluid.
diagnostics.next: Top up as necessary with Motorcraft DOT 4 LV PM-20 meeting WSS-M6C65-A2; see [Specifications](#/document/G1694687).

diagnostics.finding: A wheel nut is seized.
diagnostics.meaning: Normal wheel removal cannot continue.
diagnostics.next: Stop wheel removal and arrange an appropriate seized-fastener repair. Do not use heat on the nut because it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing.

verification.title: Verify the brake fasteners and hardware
verification.body: Confirm two new anchor-plate bolts were installed at 85 lb.ft (115 Nm), both guide-pin bolts were tightened to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm), and the tabbed pad clip is at the top.

verification.title: Verify the caliper and fluid completion actions
verification.body: Confirm the temporary caliper hanger is removed, the hose is free of it, the brake pedal has been depressed and the reservoir level has been checked and corrected as necessary.

verification.title: Verify wheel installation and vehicle restraint
verification.body: Confirm the wheel nuts were tightened in the star sequence to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) with the vehicle on its tires. Confirm the parking brake was applied before lowering and chocks were restored as the tires reached the ground.

verification.title: Record the wheel-nut follow-up
verification.body: Arrange retightening within 160 km (100 mi) of wheel installation.

procedures.purpose: Primary anchor-plate removal and installation, including discarded mounting bolts and 85 lb.ft (115 Nm) installation torque.
Required 2-piston caliper and pad access, caliper support, clip orientation, new-pad piston retraction, guide-pin bolt torque and pedal/fluid completion checks.
Wheel removal and installation, mounting-face and pilot-bore cleaning, restricted XL-2 application, wheel-nut torque, star sequence and retightening interval.
Marked lifting-point identification, safe hoist positioning and restrictions on jack-only support.
Brake-fluid material specification: Motorcraft DOT 4 LV PM-20 meeting WSS-M6C65-A2.
Relevant startup prevention, personal protection, material handling, underhood fan precautions and vehicle lifting/restraint requirements.

stepGroups.title: Secure, lift and expose the brake
stepGroups.summary: Prevent starting, position the hoist correctly and remove the wheel.

stepGroups.title: Clear the pads and remove the carrier
stepGroups.summary: Support the caliper, identify the pad hardware and discard the anchor-plate bolts.

stepGroups.title: Install the anchor plate and rebuild the brake
stepGroups.summary: Use new mounting bolts, restore clip orientation and refit the pads and caliper.

stepGroups.title: Complete brake checks and refit the wheel
stepGroups.summary: Apply the pedal, check fluid and prepare the wheel’s mounting and pilot surfaces.

stepGroups.title: Lower, tighten and verify
stepGroups.summary: Restore ground restraints, torque the wheel nuts and arrange their follow-up check.

guides.title: Replace a front brake disc with the SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Remove and refit the front brake disc on a 2015 Mustang with the 5.2L engine and SVT Performance Package, including safe caliper support, new caliper bolts and the complete wheel installation sequence.
guides.introduction: The brake disc gets squeezed for a living; getting it off the car should be the less dramatic part of its day. I’ll walk you through exposing the disc, moving the caliper and pads aside, and putting everything back with clean mating surfaces and the right tightening sequence. The trick is keeping the heavy caliper supported while giving the disc room to leave.
guides.why: The disc rotates with the wheel while the caliper presses the brake pads against it to slow the car. Its mounting surfaces must be clean so it seats properly. Supporting the caliper protects the flexible brake hose, replacing its mounting bolts meets the installation requirement, and tightening the wheel evenly helps prevent brake disc runout—sideways wobble as the disc turns.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang 5.2L SVT Performance Package front brake disc
front brake caliper mounting bolt torque

when.summary: Use this procedure when a front brake disc needs removal, refitting or replacement on the 2015 5.2L Mustang with the SVT Performance Package.
notes: Have two new caliper mounting bolts ready, even when refitting the original disc.
The torque values here apply to this configuration; do not transfer the caliper specification to another brake package.

prepare.title: Establish the job’s starting point
prepare.detail: This procedure covers removal and installation after the decision to service the disc. Assessing disc reuse requires separate wear and runout specifications; freeing a seized disc requires an appropriate separate method.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting equipment and caliper support
prepare.detail: Arrange a suitable hoist, tools for the wheel nuts and two caliper mounting bolts, a torque wrench capable of the specified tightening values, and a secure caliper hanger or support. If a jack is used, floor stands are required before anyone goes underneath. The vehicle’s emergency jack is only for changing a deflated tire, not this repair.

prepare.title: Gather parts and cleaning materials
prepare.detail: Have two new caliper mounting bolts and, if replacing it, a brake disc matching this application. For the disc mating surfaces, use a wire brush and Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner — VOC Compliant or Motorcraft Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A or PM-4-B. For the wheel’s central locating interface, have Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2.

prepare.title: Plan wheel handling
prepare.detail: Removing the wheel assembly does not require removing the tire from the wheel. If separate tire service becomes necessary on carbon fiber or alloy wheels, use a center-clamp tire changer such as Hunter Auto 34, Revolution, TC3900 or equivalent. Do not use a table-top machine that grips inside the wheel and rides on its front flange. Balancing equipment must avoid contact with the wheel face; Hunter Road Force Touch GSP9700 is an example. The wrong equipment can damage the wheel.

steps.title: Locate the marked lifting points
steps.body:
Before lifting, use a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Confirm the jack or hoist is rated for the vehicle, including cargo and modifications. If using a jack, support the vehicle on suitable stands at the designated points before going underneath; a jack alone is not a support. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

Before raising the car, find the triangles stamped into the body or frame at the lifting points. The lifting illustration identifies four locations along the vehicle’s sides; use the actual stamped marks to identify them on the car. Raising it elsewhere can let it shift or fall.

Use the [Jacking and Lifting overview](#/document/G1663631) alongside these instructions. Never apply jack pressure to either bumper.

steps.title: Position the car and raise it safely
steps.body:
With the transmission in Neutral, position the vehicle on the hoist as directed by the [Wheel and Tire procedure](#/document/G1686507).

Before driving onto a drive-on lift, check for underbody interference. Position hoist adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering components. On a two-column hoist, make sure the forks clear suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets where fitted, and avoid contact that could damage the axle or rear cover.

Raise the vehicle with the supports correctly located. Never get underneath a vehicle held only by a jack; use floor stands.

steps.title: Remove the five wheel nuts and wheel assembly
steps.body: Remove the five wheel nuts, then take the wheel and tire assembly off the hub to expose the front brake assembly. Do not use heat on a seized wheel nut: it can damage both the wheel and wheel bearing. If a nut will not release without heat, stop this removal sequence and arrange a suitable method for the seized fastener.

steps.title: Remove the two caliper bolts and support the caliper with its pads aside
steps.body:
Identify the two caliper mounting bolts shown at the upper and lower mounting locations in the [SVT brake disc procedure](#/document/G1716189). Arrange the caliper hanger or support before releasing the assembly.

Remove both bolts and discard them. Move the caliper and brake pads aside together, clear of the disc, with the hose still connected. Support the caliper independently so its weight does not pull on the brake hose.

Do not let the caliper hang from the hose. The hose carries brake fluid; it is not a lifting strap, however convenient it looks.

steps.title: Lift the brake disc off the hub
steps.body: With the caliper and pads supported out of the way, carefully draw the disc outward off the hub and its five wheel studs. Support the disc as it comes free and set it down carefully. Keep control of it throughout removal and installation.

steps.title: Clean the disc-to-hub mating surfaces
steps.body:
Before fitting the disc, clean the surfaces where the disc and hub meet using a wire brush and Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner — VOC Compliant or Motorcraft Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A or PM-4-B.

Look at the contact surfaces as you clean: corrosion, dirt or other material must not remain trapped between them. These are the seating surfaces behind the disc, distinct from the broad friction faces that the pads squeeze.

steps.title: Refit the disc, then secure the caliper with new bolts
steps.body:
Carefully place the disc back over the five studs and onto its cleaned hub seat. Bring the supported caliper and brake pads back into their installed position around the disc.

Install two new caliper mounting bolts and tighten them to 136 lb.ft (185 Nm). Do not reuse the discarded bolts. Once the caliper is secured, remove its temporary support and confirm that the hose is not carrying the caliper’s weight.

steps.title: Clean the wheel mounting face and central pilot bore
steps.body:
Clean corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel’s mounting face and the corresponding hub or brake disc surface it contacts. Also clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the round opening that fits over the hub’s locating shoulder. I treat that bore as its own cleaning task; wiping the flat face alone misses it.

Check that any fasteners attaching the disc to the hub are secure and do not interfere with the wheel’s seating surfaces. Debris or interference at this joint can allow the wheel nuts to loosen and the wheel to come off while driving, causing loss of control and serious injury or death.

steps.title: Apply a thin film of anti-seize only at the pilot interface
steps.body:
Apply a thin coat of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, only where the cleaned wheel pilot bore meets the hub pilot, its central locating shoulder.

Keep it off the flat wheel-to-disc mounting surface, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and disc friction faces. The wheel stud and nut threads must remain clean and dry for the specified torque. This is a small, precise application; the whole assembly does not need to look like a silver crime scene.

steps.title: Install the wheel and finger-tighten all five nuts
steps.body:
Before lowering, make sure the parking brake is applied. Restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground, and keep the vehicle restrained for final wheel-nut tightening. Do not lower an unrestrained vehicle in Neutral.

Position the wheel and tire assembly on the hub and install all five wheel nuts. Tighten them only finger tight at this stage.

Lower the vehicle until it is resting on its tires before performing final tightening.

steps.title: Torque the wheel nuts in the illustrated star pattern
steps.body:
With the vehicle resting on its tires, tighten the wheel nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), using clean, dry wheel stud and wheel nut threads.

Viewed from outside the wheel, the illustrated five-nut sequence is: 1 top, 2 lower left, 3 upper right, 4 upper left, 5 lower right. Follow that star/cross sequence rather than proceeding around the rim. Uneven tightening can produce high brake disc runout and accelerate brake roughness, shudder and vibration.

steps.title: Apply the brake pedal and verify operation
steps.body:
After reassembly, apply the brake pedal several times to verify correct brake system operation, as required by the [brake disc procedure](#/document/G1716189).

Confirm that the disc and caliper are installed, the two new caliper bolts have been torqued, and all five wheel nuts have received their final tightening. If the pedal check does not confirm correct operation, resolve that issue before returning the vehicle to use.

steps.title: Retighten the wheel nuts within 100 miles
steps.body:
Arrange to retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) of reinstalling the wheel. Use the same star pattern and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) specification, with the vehicle resting on its tires and the threads clean and dry.

Wheels can loosen after initial tightening. This follow-up is a required part of completing the wheel installation.

watchFor.title: Caliper support throughout disc access
watchFor.body: Keep the caliper supported from the moment its mounting bolts are released until it is secured again. Allowing it to hang from its flexible hose can damage the hose.

watchFor.title: Discarded bolts returning to service
watchFor.body: Both removed caliper mounting bolts must be replaced. The installation torque for the new bolts is 136 lb.ft (185 Nm).

watchFor.title: Anti-seize migrating beyond the central pilot
watchFor.body: The thin lubricant film belongs only between the wheel pilot bore and hub pilot. Keep mounting faces, wheel fasteners, pads and disc friction surfaces free of it.

watchFor.title: Unsafe lifting contact
watchFor.body: Use the triangle-marked lifting points. Misplaced supports can damage nearby components or allow the car to shift or fall. A jack alone is never adequate support for working underneath.

watchFor.title: Wheel tightening sequence and follow-up
watchFor.body: Final torque is applied with the car resting on its tires, in the five-nut star pattern. Retighten within 160 km (100 mi); omitting this can leave a wheel vulnerable to loosening.

notes: The caliper bolt torque is 136 lb.ft (185 Nm); the wheel nut torque is 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). Keep those two specifications distinct.
The linked wheel and lifting procedures also cover other engines, but this brake disc article applies only to the 2015 5.2L SVT Performance Package configuration.

diagnostics.finding: A wheel nut is seized.
diagnostics.meaning: Wheel removal is blocked; heating the nut risks damage to the wheel and wheel bearing.
diagnostics.next: Do not apply heat. Arrange a suitable seized-fastener removal method before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: Corrosion, dirt or foreign material remains on a seating surface.
diagnostics.meaning: The disc or wheel cannot seat against a clean mounting interface. Contamination at the wheel joint can contribute to loosening.
diagnostics.next: Continue cleaning the affected mating surfaces before installation. Clean the wheel’s central pilot bore as well as its flat mounting face.

diagnostics.finding: A disc-to-hub fastener interferes with the wheel mounting surface.
diagnostics.meaning: The wheel cannot seat properly against its mounting surface.
diagnostics.next: Correct the fastener’s security and interference before installing the wheel.

diagnostics.finding: Anti-seize has reached a prohibited surface or a wheel fastener.
diagnostics.meaning: The application no longer meets the clean mounting, dry-thread or brake-surface requirements.
diagnostics.next: Stop assembly and correct the contamination before proceeding. Do not tighten lubricated wheel threads using the clean, dry-thread torque specification.

diagnostics.finding: Repeated brake-pedal application does not confirm correct brake operation.
diagnostics.meaning: The required completion check has not passed.
diagnostics.next: Keep the vehicle out of use and have the brake operation issue evaluated and corrected before release.

verification.title: Disc and caliper assembly
verification.body: Confirm that the disc mating surfaces were cleaned, the disc was carefully refitted, and the caliper and pads were restored with two new bolts tightened to 136 lb.ft (185 Nm). Confirm that the temporary caliper support has been removed.

verification.title: Wheel seating and tightening
verification.body: Confirm clean wheel mounting surfaces and a cleaned pilot bore, with XL-2 confined to the pilot interface. Verify that all five nuts were tightened in the illustrated star pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), on clean, dry threads with the vehicle resting on its tires.

verification.title: Brake operation
verification.body: Apply the brake pedal several times and verify correct brake system operation. This is the specified post-assembly functional check.

verification.title: Wheel nut follow-up
verification.body: Record the requirement to retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after wheel installation.
