guides.title: Replace the front brake disc shield: 2015 Mustang 5.2L with SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Remove the wheel, support the caliper and remove the disc to reach the shield’s two bolts. Reassemble with new caliper bolts, clean mounting surfaces and the correct tightening sequence.
guides.introduction: The brake disc shield is a modest protective panel with an impressive entourage: to reach its two bolts, the wheel, caliper and brake disc all need to move. Apparently even sheet metal gets a security detail. I’ll walk you through that access, then back out again with the hose supported, the mounting faces clean and every fastener tightened to its own specification.
guides.why: The shield stays stationary beside the rotating brake disc and acts as a protective barrier. Replacing it means temporarily disturbing components that hold the brake and wheel together. The important work is supporting the caliper without loading its hose, replacing its discarded mounting bolts and restoring clean, properly tightened connections.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang 5.2L SVT Performance Package brake disc shield

when.summary: Use this procedure when removal or replacement of the front brake disc shield has already been established as necessary on a 2015 Mustang 5.2L with the SVT Performance Package.
notes: The brake-disc and caliper instructions here apply specifically to this SVT Performance Package configuration.
This is a replacement procedure, not a test for deciding whether a shield causes a particular noise.

prepare.title: Have the replacement parts ready
prepare.detail: Have the correct replacement shield if replacing it, plus two new caliper mounting bolts. The removed caliper bolts must be discarded. The shield bolts are reinstalled; they are not identified as discard-after-removal fasteners.

prepare.title: Gather tools and caliper support
prepare.detail: Arrange a suitably rated hoist, wheel chocks, appropriate fastener tools, a wire brush and a secure caliper-support hook or hanger. Have torque tools capable of accurately applying 106 lb.in (12 Nm), 136 lb.ft (185 Nm) and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). The smallest value is in pound-inches, not pound-feet.

prepare.title: Prepare the specified cleaning materials
prepare.detail: Use Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner – VOC Compliant or Motorcraft Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A or PM-4-B, for the brake-disc mating surfaces. Have Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, for the wheel’s central locating interface only.

prepare.title: Protect yourself and define the stopping point
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. Read the chemicals’ safety information and keep solvents away from ignition sources. If a seized fastener or disc prevents ordinary removal, stop for an appropriate release procedure rather than improvising; do not use heat on a seized wheel nut.

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start
steps.body: Before working around or beneath the car, disable remote start if fitted through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup on the central display. Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle so another person cannot start it during service. These precautions apply before the lifting and brake work begins. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Secure the car and locate the lifting points
steps.body:
Position the car on a hard, level surface. Apply the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground.

Check that the lifting equipment is rated for the car’s weight, including cargo and modifications. Locate the triangles stamped into the body sheet metal or frame: they identify the correct lifting points. The lifting illustration shows four locations along the sides of the underbody. Confirm the actual stamped triangles on the car before placing the lift arms. See [Jacking and Lifting – Overview](#/document/G1663631).

steps.title: Position the car on the hoist in Neutral and raise it
steps.body:
With the car restrained, place the transmission in Neutral as directed by the [Wheel and Tire procedure](#/document/G1686507), and position it on the hoist. Keep the parking brake applied; this front-brake job does not call for its release.

Place the hoist adapters at the identified lifting points. Check that the arms and adapters will not strike the suspension, exhaust, steering linkage, mounting brackets, stabilizer brackets, axle or rear cover. Check underbody clearance before driving onto any drive-on lift.

Raise the vehicle using the hoist’s operating instructions. Never support it at either bumper. The emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this repair; if a service jack is used during positioning, never get beneath the car until it is supported on suitable stands. Do not run the engine to power the wheels during this work.

steps.title: Remove the front wheel and tire
steps.body:
Remove the five wheel nuts, then take the wheel and tire off the hub. Do not heat a seized nut: heat can damage both the wheel and wheel bearing.

With the wheel removed, identify the large caliper around the disc’s outer edge. The disc is the circular braking surface mounted over the five wheel studs. The shield sits behind it, so the disc must come off before the shield bolts become accessible.

steps.title: Remove the caliper bolts and support the caliper with its pads
steps.body:
Arrange the support hook or hanger before removing the caliper. Remove its two mounting bolts and discard them.

Move the caliper and brake pads aside together and secure the caliper to the support. Leave the brake hose connected. The illustration shows a hanger supporting the caliper; the hose must not carry its weight. Check that the supported position does not pull on the hose before letting go of the caliper. See the matching [SVT Performance Package Brake Disc procedure](#/document/G1716189).

This is where a proper hanger earns its keep. A brake hose is a fluid line, not a damn coat hook.

steps.title: Remove the brake disc
steps.body:
Handle the disc carefully and remove it from the hub, clearing the five wheel studs. Keep it safely supported while moving it away.

With the disc removed, the hub flange and studs remain in place. Behind and below the hub is the curved, ribbed shield. There is no hub-removal step in this shield replacement.

steps.title: Remove the shield’s two bolts
steps.body:
Identify the two bolts securing the shield at its raised mounting ears, one on either side of the hub’s lower area. Support the shield, remove both bolts and take the shield away.

Note its orientation before removal: the broad curved portion extends below the hub, with its shaped opening and mounting ears fitting around the surrounding components. See [Brake Disc Shield – SVT Performance Package](#/document/G1716190).

steps.title: Fit the shield and tighten its bolts
steps.body:
Position the shield in the same orientation as the removed part, align both mounting ears and install the two bolts. Tighten both to 106 lb.in (12 Nm).

Check that both ears are seated at their mounting points and the shield is secured. Keep this torque separate from the much higher caliper and wheel-nut values.

steps.title: Clean the disc mating surfaces and reinstall the disc
steps.body:
Before refitting the disc, clean the surfaces where the disc and hub meet using a wire brush and Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner – VOC Compliant or Motorcraft Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A or PM-4-B. Remove dirt, corrosion and foreign material that would prevent the parts from seating together.

Carefully position the disc back over the wheel studs and onto the hub. Keep lubricant off its friction surfaces—the areas contacted by the brake pads.

steps.title: Restore the caliper and pads with new bolts
steps.body:
Return the supported caliper and brake pads to their installed position around the disc. Install two new caliper mounting bolts and tighten them to 136 lb.ft (185 Nm).

Remove the support hanger only after the caliper is secured. Confirm that the hose is not caught or pulled by the restored assembly. The old bolts stay in the discard pile; this is not their comeback tour.

steps.title: Clean the wheel mounting faces and central pilot bore
steps.body:
Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel’s flat mounting face and the corresponding mounting face on the hub or brake disc. Check that any fasteners attaching the disc to the hub are secure and do not obstruct the wheel seating flat.

Also clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the round center opening that locates over the hub’s raised center, called the hub pilot. The wheel illustration calls for cleaning this bore as well as treating its locating interface.

Apply only a thin film of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, at the interface between that bore and the hub pilot. Keep it off the flat wheel-to-disc mounting faces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and disc friction surfaces. The wheel-stud and wheel-nut threads must remain clean and dry.

steps.title: Install the wheel with the nuts finger tight
steps.body:
Position the wheel over the hub pilot and five studs, making sure its mounting face seats against the disc. Install all five nuts finger tight only at this stage.

Do not perform the final torque tightening while the vehicle is suspended. The specified final tightening is done with the vehicle resting on its tires.

steps.title: Restore restraints before and during lowering
steps.body:
Before lowering, set or confirm the parking brake is fully applied. Clear tools and loose equipment from beneath the vehicle.

Lower the car under control. As the tires reach the ground, restore chocks to the ground wheels before completing the lowering operation. Then bring the vehicle fully to rest on its tires, with the parking brake applied and the wheels blocked.

steps.title: Tighten the five wheel nuts in the illustrated star sequence
steps.body:
With the vehicle resting on its tires, tighten the wheel nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), using clean, dry stud and nut threads.

Follow the illustrated five-point star: top nut, lower-left nut, upper-right nut, upper-left nut, then lower-right nut. If the wheel is rotated, use the same crossing pattern rather than tightening adjacent nuts around the circle.

The crossing sequence helps avoid excessive brake-disc runout—side-to-side wobble as the disc turns—which can contribute to brake roughness, shudder and vibration. See [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Apply the brake pedal and arrange the wheel-nut recheck
steps.body:
With the car stationary and restrained, apply the brake pedal several times to verify correct brake-system operation before returning the vehicle to use. If correct operation cannot be confirmed, stop and resolve the brake fault before driving.

Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after reinstalling the wheel, using the same 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) specification and star pattern. That follow-up matters because a reinstalled wheel can loosen after its initial tightening.

watchFor.title: Caliper weight reaching the hose
watchFor.body: Support the caliper before moving it aside and maintain that support until it is bolted back in place. A hanging caliper can damage the brake hose.

watchFor.title: Three fastener groups, three different torques
watchFor.body: Shield bolts: 106 lb.in (12 Nm). New caliper bolts: 136 lb.ft (185 Nm). Wheel nuts: 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). Do not confuse pound-inches with pound-feet.

watchFor.title: Lubricant spreading beyond the pilot
watchFor.body: XL-2 belongs only in a thin film between the wheel pilot bore and hub pilot. It must not reach the flat mounting faces, studs, nuts, pads or disc friction surfaces.

watchFor.title: A wheel that cannot seat flat
watchFor.body: Dirt, corrosion or an interfering disc fastener can prevent proper wheel seating. Correct the obstruction before installation; an improperly seated wheel can loosen in service.

watchFor.title: Neutral during raised service
watchFor.body: Neutral does not restrain the vehicle. Maintain the parking brake and ground-wheel chocks during setup, confirm the parking brake before lowering and restore chocks as the tires reach the ground.

notes: No tire demounting or balancing is needed for shield access. If separate tire work is added on carbon-fiber or alloy wheels, use a center-clamp tire changer and a balancer that does not contact the wheel face. Avoid tabletop changers that grip inside the wheel and bear on its front flange.
The shield replacement uses reverse-order reassembly: shield, disc, caliper with pads, then wheel. The cleaning requirements and replacement caliper bolts remain essential parts of that sequence.

diagnostics.finding: A wheel nut is seized.
diagnostics.meaning: Normal wheel removal cannot proceed, and heating the nut risks wheel and bearing damage.
diagnostics.next: Stop and obtain an appropriate non-heat removal method before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: The positioned-aside caliper pulls on its hose or cannot be securely supported.
diagnostics.meaning: The hose is being loaded rather than the support carrying the caliper.
diagnostics.next: Support and reposition the caliper securely before removing the disc.

diagnostics.finding: Corrosion, dirt or a protruding fastener prevents a mounting face from seating flat.
diagnostics.meaning: The disc or wheel cannot be correctly installed on an obstructed mating surface.
diagnostics.next: Clean the mating surfaces and correct any fastener interference before reassembly. Do not use tightening force to overcome the obstruction.

diagnostics.finding: Correct brake operation cannot be confirmed after several pedal applications.
diagnostics.meaning: The required completion check has not passed; it does not by itself identify the failed component.
diagnostics.next: Do not drive the car. Resolve the brake fault before returning it to service; further fault isolation is outside this replacement procedure.

verification.title: Shield and brake assembly secured
verification.body: Confirm the shield’s two bolts were tightened to 106 lb.in (12 Nm), the disc mating surfaces were cleaned and the two new caliper bolts were tightened to 136 lb.ft (185 Nm). Confirm the caliper hanger has been removed.

verification.title: Wheel correctly seated and tightened
verification.body: Confirm the mounting faces and central pilot bore were cleaned, XL-2 was confined to the pilot interface and all five nuts were tightened on clean, dry threads to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) in the star pattern with the car resting on its tires.

verification.title: Brake operation and restraints restored
verification.body: Complete the repeated brake-pedal applications and confirm correct operation before use. The parking brake must have been applied before lowering, with ground-wheel chocks restored as the tires reached the ground.

verification.title: Follow-up wheel-nut tightening scheduled
verification.body: Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) of wheel installation.

guides.title: Replace the front brake disc shield
guides.summary: Remove the wheel, support the caliper and remove the brake disc to replace the matching shield. Includes all supported shield layouts, replacement caliper bolts, tightening values and wheel refitting.
guides.introduction: The brake disc shield gets the glamorous job of standing behind a spinning disc and catching the road’s nonsense. Replacing it means persuading the wheel, caliper and disc to leave the stage first. I’ll walk you through that access work, the different shield shapes and the reassembly that makes this a finished brake job rather than a collection of parts beside the car. This guide covers 2015 Mustangs with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine and 2-, 4- or 6-piston front calipers.
guides.why: The shield is the stationary protective plate behind the brake disc. Its outline and mounting points vary with the fitted brakes. Matching the complete shape and bolt pattern matters: the full-height and lower-only six-piston designs are distinct parts, even though their bolts share a tightening value.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang front brake disc shield replacement

when.summary: When the fitted front brake disc shield has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Identify the fitted caliper configuration and match the replacement shield to the actual shield’s complete outline and attachment pattern.
For six-piston brakes, select between the full-height three-bolt shield and lower-only two-bolt shield by the installed hardware. Transmission or body style alone is insufficient to select the part.

prepare.title: Define the job before dismantling
prepare.detail: This is a matching-shield replacement procedure, without a measured shield-wear or clearance test. If the fitted hardware does not match a branch below, or a seized wheel or disc prevents the described removal, obtain the matching repair instructions before forcing parts.

prepare.title: Have the replacement parts ready
prepare.detail: Obtain the correct shield and two new caliper assembly mounting bolts for each caliper removed. Both mounting bolts are discarded on the 2-, 4- and 6-piston arrangements. These are the bolts securing the caliper assembly to its mounting, not unrelated guide-pin fasteners.

prepare.title: Gather lifting, support and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Use a suitably rated hoist, or an adequately rated workshop jack with floor stands, and wheel chocks. Have tools that fit the wheel nuts, caliper assembly bolts and shield bolts; a caliper support hook; and torque tools covering 20 Nm, 115 Nm and 204 Nm. The vehicle’s emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this repair.

prepare.title: Prepare cleaning materials and protection
prepare.detail: Have a wire brush, Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner—VOC Compliant or Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A or PM-4-B, and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2. Wear eye and ear protection, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. Read the chemicals’ safety information and keep solvents away from ignition sources.

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start and restrain the car
steps.body: On a hard, level surface, apply the parking brake and chock every wheel that will remain on the ground. Before working around the vehicle, disable remote start, if fitted, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup on the central display. Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person starting it. These precautions apply before the lifting and wheel work begins. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Locate the correct lifting points
steps.body:
Find the triangles stamped into the body structure at the lifting points along each side, behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels. Position the lifting equipment at the corresponding points, as shown in [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631).

Check that the equipment’s capacity covers the vehicle, cargo and modifications. Keep hoist arms and adapters clear of suspension parts, steering linkage, exhaust, mounting brackets, stabilizer brackets and axle or rear-cover components. Never lift against either bumper. If using a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving onto it.

steps.title: Select Neutral and raise onto proper support
steps.body:
With the parking brake applied and ground wheels chocked, place the transmission in Neutral for the wheel-removal work. Raise the vehicle on the correctly positioned hoist.

If using a workshop jack, support the raised vehicle on floor stands before working underneath or reaching into the work area; never rely on the jack alone. Leave all wheels still on the ground chocked. This job does not require releasing the parking brake.

steps.title: Remove the front wheel
steps.body: Remove the five wheel nuts, then take the wheel and tire assembly off the hub. Do not use heat on a seized wheel nut: it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. Set the wheel aside with its mounting surface protected. The tire stays on the wheel throughout this job. See [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Identify the caliper mounting bolts and arrange its support
steps.body:
Confirm whether the fitted front caliper is the 2-, 4- or 6-piston type. Locate the two caliper assembly mounting bolts at the rear of the assembly, one above the other. On the 2-piston arrangement, identify the assembly mounting pair rather than the separate guide-pin fasteners.

Arrange a suitable support hook before removing the bolts so the caliper and pads can be held aside without their weight loading the flexible brake hose. The hose remains connected; no hydraulic connection is opened for this access work.

steps.title: Remove the caliper assembly and support it aside
steps.body:
Remove the two assembly mounting bolts for the fitted caliper. Discard both bolts on every supported branch: 2-piston, 4-piston and 6-piston.

Move the caliper and brake pads clear of the disc and support the assembly with the hook. Make sure the hose is not carrying its weight or being pulled as you position it. Do not let the caliper hang from the hose. I keep the support arranged before the last bolt comes out; a brake hose makes a lousy hammock. See [Brake Disc](#/document/G1693784).

steps.title: Remove the brake disc
steps.body: With the caliper and pads supported clear, withdraw the disc from the hub and wheel studs. The shield and its attachment bolts are now exposed behind the hub flange. Leave the hub assembly installed; shield access here does not call for hub removal.

steps.title: Match the exposed shield to the correct branch
steps.body:
For 2-piston brakes, identify the large shield extending above and below the hub, secured by three bolts around the hub mounting area.

For 4-piston brakes, the shield also has three attachment bolts. Match its complete outline and mounting points to the replacement.

For 6-piston brakes, distinguish the two designs by the actual installed part. The full-height shield extends above and below the hub and uses three bolts. The lower-only shield sits beneath the hub and uses two bolts, one at each upper mounting ear of that lower panel. Match both shape and bolt count; do not substitute one design for the other. See [Brake Disc Shield](#/document/G1693785).

steps.title: Remove the shield
steps.body: Support the shield by hand, remove its three attachment bolts—or the two bolts on the lower-only six-piston design—and take the shield away from its mounting position. Keep its orientation clear so the replacement follows the same outline around the hub.

steps.title: Install the matching shield and tighten its bolts
steps.body:
Position the replacement in the same orientation. Check that its mounting holes align with the original attachment points before installing the bolts; a wrong shield should not be persuaded into place with bolt tension.

Install all three bolts on the 2-piston, 4-piston and full-height six-piston arrangements, or both bolts on the lower-only six-piston arrangement. Tighten every shield attachment bolt to 177 lb.in (20 Nm). This value applies only to the shield bolts.

steps.title: Clean the disc mating surfaces and refit the disc
steps.body:
Use a wire brush and Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner PM-4-A or PM-4-B to clean the brake disc mating surfaces—the contact surfaces that must seat together when the disc is installed. Remove dirt, corrosion and foreign material from the hub/disc seating interface.

Refit the disc over the wheel studs and onto the hub. Confirm that it seats correctly and that the shield remains in its intended position behind it, with no visible contact between the shield and disc.

steps.title: Refit the caliper with two new mounting bolts
steps.body:
Bring the supported caliper and brake pads back over the disc into their original position. Keep the hose free from strain while positioning the assembly.

Install two new caliper assembly mounting bolts and tighten both to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). This applies to the 2-, 4- and 6-piston assembly mounting branches. Remove the support hook once the assembly is secured. Do not apply this value to unrelated guide-pin fasteners.

steps.title: Clean the wheel mounting face and central bore
steps.body:
Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel’s flat mounting face and the corresponding hub or brake-disc mounting face. Check that any disc-to-hub retaining fasteners, if present, are secured and do not stand proud between the wheel and its mounting surface.

Also clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the round hole that locates the wheel on the hub’s raised center—and the corresponding hub pilot. The bore needs cleaning too, not just the broad flat face. Contamination trapped between mounting faces can allow the wheel nuts to loosen.

steps.title: Apply anti-seize only at the pilot interface
steps.body:
Apply a thin film of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 only where the wheel’s pilot bore fits over the hub pilot.

Keep it off the flat wheel-to-disc mounting surfaces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and disc friction surfaces. Wheel stud and nut threads must remain clean and dry for the specified tightening value. This is a thin locating-surface film, not an invitation to butter the whole damn hub.

steps.title: Fit the wheel and start all five nuts
steps.body: Position the wheel on the hub and install all five wheel nuts. Tighten them finger tight at this stage. Final tightening is performed with the vehicle resting on its tires, as described in [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Restore restraints before and during lowering
steps.body:
Before beginning to lower, confirm that the parking brake is applied. Keep the chocks at every wheel already on the ground.

Lower the vehicle using the lifting equipment’s normal procedure. As raised wheels reach the ground, restore their ground-wheel chocks before releasing the remaining lifting support. Once the car rests on its tires and is chocked, restore the parked transmission position: Park for an automatic, or a gear for a manual.

steps.title: Torque the wheel nuts in the five-point star sequence
steps.body:
With the vehicle resting on its tires, tighten all five wheel nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), using clean, dry stud and nut threads.

Follow a star/cross pattern. With a nut at the top, the illustrated order is top, lower left, upper right, upper left, then lower right. If the wheel is rotated, use the same crossing pattern from the corresponding starting point. Working around adjacent nuts can introduce disc runout—side-to-side wobble that contributes to brake roughness and vibration.

steps.title: Check brake operation before moving the car
steps.body:
Apply the brake pedal several times to verify correct brake-system operation. If operation is not correct, do not drive the car; have the brake assembly checked before proceeding. This is the completion check after reassembly, not a diagnosis of a pre-existing brake complaint.

Confirm that tools and the caliper support hook have been removed. Retighten the wheel nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) in the same star pattern within 160 km (100 mi) after refitting the wheel.

watchFor.title: Three separate tightening values
watchFor.body: Shield bolts: 177 lb.in (20 Nm). New caliper assembly mounting bolts: 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). Wheel nuts: 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). Notice the shield’s inch-pound unit; it is not a foot-pound value.

watchFor.title: Discard both caliper mounting bolts on every branch
watchFor.body: The two assembly mounting bolts require replacement on the 2-piston arrangement as well as the 4- and 6-piston arrangements. Keep these separate from the shield bolts and any guide-pin fasteners.

watchFor.title: The caliper must have independent support
watchFor.body: Check the support as you move the caliper aside and again before refitting it. A connected hose must never carry the caliper’s weight.

watchFor.title: Six-piston shields are not interchangeable
watchFor.body: A full-height three-bolt shield and a lower-only two-bolt shield share a torque specification, not a shape. Select the replacement by the complete fitted outline and mounting pattern.

watchFor.title: Clean mounting faces and dry threads matter
watchFor.body: Dirt or corrosion between wheel mounting faces can compromise attachment. Keep anti-seize confined to the central pilot interface; it must not reach the flat mounting faces, fastener threads or braking surfaces.

notes: The access sequence is wheel, supported caliper and pads, brake disc, then shield. Reassembly reverses that sequence, with disc mating-surface cleaning, new caliper mounting bolts and wheel preparation included.
The wheel is removed as an assembly; tire removal and wheel balancing are outside this job.
Do not run the engine to power the drive wheels during this repair.

diagnostics.finding: A 2- or 4-piston front caliper is fitted, and the exposed shield has three attachment bolts.
diagnostics.meaning: This matches the corresponding three-bolt shield branch.
diagnostics.next: Match the replacement’s full outline and attachment points. Install all three shield bolts at 177 lb.in (20 Nm).

diagnostics.finding: Six-piston brakes have a full-height shield extending above and below the hub with three attachment bolts.
diagnostics.meaning: The installed hardware matches the full-height six-piston branch.
diagnostics.next: Use the matching full-height replacement and tighten all three shield bolts to 177 lb.in (20 Nm).

diagnostics.finding: Six-piston brakes have a lower-only shield secured by two bolts at its upper mounting ears.
diagnostics.meaning: The installed hardware matches the lower-only six-piston branch.
diagnostics.next: Use the matching lower-only replacement and tighten both shield bolts to 177 lb.in (20 Nm).

diagnostics.finding: The replacement’s outline or mounting holes differ from the removed shield.
diagnostics.meaning: The replacement has not been matched to the installed arrangement.
diagnostics.next: Stop installation and obtain the matching part. Do not bend the shield or use bolt tension to overcome the mismatch.

diagnostics.finding: The caliper’s weight pulls on the connected brake hose.
diagnostics.meaning: The support arrangement is inadequate.
diagnostics.next: Support the caliper immediately and reposition the hook so it carries the assembly’s weight before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: Brake operation is not correct when the pedal is applied several times after reassembly.
diagnostics.meaning: The brake-disc reassembly completion check has not passed.
diagnostics.next: Keep the car stationary and have the brake assembly checked before driving.

verification.title: Confirm the shield arrangement and attachment
verification.body: Check that the installed shield matches the removed part’s outline and bolt pattern. Confirm completion of 20 Nm tightening at every shield bolt and check that the refitted disc seats correctly without visible shield contact.

verification.title: Confirm caliper reassembly
verification.body: Verify that two new assembly mounting bolts were installed and tightened to 115 Nm, the support hook is removed and the connected hose is free from the caliper’s weight or strain.

verification.title: Confirm wheel attachment and ground restraints
verification.body: Verify clean mounting faces, anti-seize confined to the pilot interface, clean and dry fastener threads, and all five wheel nuts tightened in a star pattern to 204 Nm with the car on its tires. Confirm that the parking brake and ground-wheel chocks were restored during lowering.

verification.title: Complete the brake check and wheel-nut follow-up
verification.body: Apply the brake pedal several times and verify correct operation before moving the car. Arrange wheel-nut retightening within 160 km (100 mi).

stepGroups.summary: Restore ground restraints, torque the wheel nuts and complete the brake-operation check.

guides.title: Replace Front Brake Pads with 2-Piston Calipers
guides.summary: Replace the front brake pads on a 2015 Mustang 2.3L or 3.7L with 2-piston front calipers, including clip orientation, piston retraction, wheel installation and final pedal and fluid checks.
guides.introduction: Brake pads have a wonderfully unreasonable job: squeeze a spinning disc and persuade a Mustang to stop having so much fun. I’ll walk you through reaching the pads, supporting the caliper, fitting the different upper and lower clips, and putting everything back with the correct tightening values. This guide applies to the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L or 3.7L engine and 2-piston front brake calipers.
guides.why: The pads provide the friction surfaces that press against the brake disc to slow the wheel. The caliper’s two pistons apply that pressure. New, thicker pads need room, so the pistons must be compressed back into the caliper before reassembly. Supporting the displaced caliper protects its brake hose, while correct clip placement keeps the pad hardware in its intended positions.
searchTerms: front caliper guide pin bolt torque

when.summary: Use this procedure when the front pads require replacement or must be removed for related service.
notes: Confirm the fitted front brakes use 2-piston calipers. Engine size alone does not establish the brake configuration.
The wear limits in the decision rows help interpret established measurements; noises or pedal complaints alone do not establish that pad replacement is the correct repair.

prepare.title: Arrange safe lifting and caliper support
prepare.detail: Have a suitable hoist and a secure way to support the caliper while its hose remains connected. The illustration shows a support hook. Locate the stamped triangles identifying the lifting points before raising the car. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; use floor stands. The emergency wheel-changing jack is not suitable for this repair.

prepare.title: Gather the pad kit and tools
prepare.detail: Have the correct replacement pads, every new hardware item and lubricant supplied with their kit, and the kit’s lubricant instruction sheet. You will also need a C-clamp, a worn brake pad for piston compression, tools for the wheel nuts and two guide-pin bolts, and a torque wrench suitable for 24 lb.ft (32 Nm) and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). Keep a worn pad until piston retraction is complete—it still has one useful job left.

prepare.title: Have the specified materials ready
prepare.detail: For the wheel’s central locating interface, use Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2. For any final reservoir top-up, use Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid, PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2. Keep the wheel anti-seize separate from the pad-kit lubricant.

prepare.title: Set the practical boundary
prepare.detail: This is a pad removal and installation procedure with the hydraulic connections left assembled. Wear-limit comparisons below assume reliable measurements. Obtain the matching service procedure if you need to measure pad or disc wear, investigate excessive wear or disc runout, replace a disc, open or bleed the hydraulic system, or establish a bedding-in routine.

steps.title: Position and lift the Mustang
steps.body:
Before lifting, use a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Confirm the jack or hoist is rated for the vehicle, including cargo and modifications. If using a jack, support the vehicle on suitable stands at the designated points before going underneath; a jack alone is not a support. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

With the transmission in Neutral, position the vehicle on a hoist. Identify the lifting locations by the triangles stamped into the body or frame; the lifting illustration identifies locations along both sides of the car.

Position the hoist adapters at the correct points without contacting suspension parts, steering linkage, exhaust, mounting brackets or stabilizer brackets. Keep the lifting equipment clear of the axle and rear cover. Do not lift against either bumper. With a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving onto it.

Incorrect lifting placement can allow the vehicle to shift or fall. Never get underneath a car supported only by a jack; support it with floor stands. See [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631).

steps.title: Remove the front wheel and tire assembly
steps.body: Remove the five wheel nuts, then remove the wheel and tire together to expose the caliper and brake disc. Do not use heat on a seized wheel nut; it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. The tire stays mounted on the wheel for this job. See [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Remove the two guide-pin bolts and support the caliper
steps.body:
Identify the upper and lower guide-pin bolts shown at the ends of the caliper. Remove both bolts, move the caliper away from the pads and position it aside with secure support.

Keep the brake hose connected. Do not allow the caliper to hang from the hose: the caliper’s weight can damage it. Maintain that support throughout pad removal and piston compression. The anchor plate—the bracket carrying the pads and their clips—remains in place. See [2-Piston Brake Pads](#/document/G1693786).

steps.title: Record the pad positions, then remove the pads
steps.body:
Before lifting anything out, note how the pads and surrounding components are positioned. Identify the pad on each side of the disc and retain that layout information for reassembly.

Remove the pads from the anchor plate. Keep a worn pad available for the C-clamp operation if you are installing new pads.

steps.title: Remove and distinguish the upper and lower clips
steps.body:
Remove the brake pad clips from the top and bottom of the anchor plate. Compare them before setting them aside: they are different, and the clip with the tab belongs at the top.

Keep that distinction clear when laying out the replacement hardware. These two clips may look like candidates for a quick mix-and-match; they are not feeling that cooperative.

steps.title: Compress the pistons if fitting new pads
steps.body:
For new pads, place a worn brake pad across the two piston faces as illustrated. Use a C-clamp acting through that pad to compress the pistons back into their caliper bores, making room for the thicker replacement pads.

Keep the caliper supported and the hose free of its weight while positioning and operating the clamp. Remove the clamp and worn pad when compression is complete. This piston-retraction operation is conditional on installing new pads.

steps.title: Fit the clips and prepare the pads
steps.body:
When installing new pads, use all new hardware and lubricant included in the pad kit. Follow the kit’s instruction sheet for where its lubricant goes.

Install the upper and lower clips on the anchor plate, placing the tabbed clip at the top. Check the clip positions before fitting the pads; correcting a swapped clip is much easier while everything is still in plain sight.

steps.title: Install the pads and refit the caliper
steps.body:
Fit the pads into the clipped anchor plate on their respective sides of the disc, using the positions noted during removal. Return the caliper over the pads while maintaining its support until it is secured.

Install both guide-pin bolts and tighten them to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm). Confirm the hose is not carrying the caliper’s weight, then remove the temporary caliper support.

steps.title: Clean the wheel mounting surfaces and central bore
steps.body:
Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel’s mounting face and the corresponding mounting surface at the hub and brake disc. Also clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the hole that locates the wheel on the hub’s raised center.

Check that any fasteners securing the disc to the hub are secured and do not interfere with the wheel’s mounting surface. Contamination or interference here can allow the wheel nuts to loosen and the wheel to come off in motion, causing loss of control and serious injury. See [Wheel and Tire installation](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Apply anti-seize only at the wheel’s locating interface
steps.body:
Apply a thin film of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, only where the wheel pilot bore meets the hub pilot.

Keep it off the flat wheel-to-disc mounting surfaces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and disc friction surfaces. The illustration’s cleaning and lubricant callouts both point to the central bore; cleaning the flat face alone does not complete this preparation.

steps.title: Position the wheel and finger-tighten the nuts
steps.body:
Place the wheel and tire assembly back on the hub and install all five wheel nuts. Tighten them only finger tight at this stage.

The final torque specification requires clean, dry wheel-stud and wheel-nut threads. Do not lubricate those threads with the pilot-bore anti-seize.

steps.title: Lower onto the tires and torque in a star pattern
steps.body:
Before lowering, make sure the parking brake is applied. Restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground, and keep the vehicle restrained for final wheel-nut tightening. Do not lower an unrestrained vehicle in Neutral.

Lower the vehicle until it rests on its tires before final tightening. Tighten the five wheel nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) in a star/cross pattern.

Using the illustrated orientation, the sequence is: top, lower left, upper right, upper left, lower right. Follow those alternating positions around the wheel. Incorrect tightening order can produce excessive disc runout—side-to-side wobble as the disc rotates—and contribute to brake roughness, shudder and vibration.

steps.title: Depress the brake pedal and check the reservoir
steps.body:
With reassembly complete, depress the brake pedal. Then check the brake-fluid level in the reservoir and top up as necessary with Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid, PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2.

These are required completion actions after installation. See [Brake System Specifications](#/document/G1694687) for the fluid specification.

steps.title: Arrange the required wheel-nut retightening
steps.body:
Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after the wheel is reinstalled. Use the same star pattern and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) specification, with the vehicle resting on its tires and the threads clean and dry.

Wheels can loosen after their initial tightening. Treat this as part of finishing the job, even though it happens after the tools first go back in the drawer.

watchFor.title: The brake hose must not support the caliper
watchFor.body: Keep the displaced caliper securely supported during removal, piston compression and reassembly. Its weight can damage the flexible hose.

watchFor.title: The tabbed clip goes at the top
watchFor.body: Compare the two clip types before installation. The upper anchor-plate position takes the clip with the tab.

watchFor.title: Kit lubricant and wheel anti-seize have different jobs
watchFor.body: Apply pad-kit lubricant according to its instruction sheet. Restrict XL-2 anti-seize to the wheel pilot-bore/hub-pilot interface; keep it off friction surfaces, wheel mounting faces and wheel fasteners.

watchFor.title: Clean wheel seating is safety-critical
watchFor.body: Do not install the wheel over corrosion, dirt or an interfering disc-retaining fastener. Poor seating can allow wheel nuts to loosen and the wheel to detach.

watchFor.title: Final wheel torque belongs on the ground
watchFor.body: Perform final tightening with the vehicle resting on its tires. Use clean, dry threads, the star pattern and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), then retighten within 160 km (100 mi).

notes: The 24 lb.ft (32 Nm) value applies to the two caliper guide-pin bolts removed for pad access.
The wheel and lifting references cover additional engines, but this pad article remains limited to the 2015 2.3L and 3.7L applications with 2-piston front calipers.

For related tire-shop work on alloy or carbon-fiber wheels, use a center-clamp tire changer, such as a Hunter Auto 34, Revolution, TC3900 or equivalent, and a wheel balancer that does not contact the wheel face, such as a Hunter Road Force Touch GSP9700. Table-top changers that grip inside the wheel and ride on its front flange, and balancers that contact the wheel face, can damage the wheel.

diagnostics.finding: The front caliper configuration does not match the 2-piston arrangement.
diagnostics.meaning: This pad procedure and its brake-specific values do not apply to that configuration.
diagnostics.next: Use the matching brake procedure before removing the caliper or selecting replacement parts.

diagnostics.finding: An established brake-pad thickness measurement is below 0.118 in (3 mm).
diagnostics.meaning: The pad is below the specified minimum thickness.
diagnostics.next: Replace the pads using this procedure and all hardware and lubricant supplied with the new-pad kit.

diagnostics.finding: An established pad taper measurement exceeds 0.118 in (3 mm) in any direction.
diagnostics.meaning: The variation in pad thickness exceeds the permitted taper wear.
diagnostics.next: Arrange assessment of the excessive wear before treating pad replacement as the complete repair; the measurement alone does not establish its cause.

diagnostics.finding: An established front-disc thickness measurement is below 1.122 in (28.5 mm).
diagnostics.meaning: The disc is below the minimum thickness for the 2-piston front brake arrangement.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the disc condition through the matching disc service procedure before completing the brake repair.

diagnostics.finding: An established installed-disc runout measurement exceeds 0.002 in (0.05 mm).
diagnostics.meaning: The disc’s side-to-side movement exceeds the specified maximum.
diagnostics.next: Have the runout assessed through the appropriate measuring and repair procedure. Check wheel mounting cleanliness and tightening practice during this job, without assuming either establishes the cause.

diagnostics.finding: The clip with the tab is in the lower anchor-plate position.
diagnostics.meaning: The two clip types have been interchanged.
diagnostics.next: Correct their positions before installing the pads and caliper: the tabbed clip belongs at the top.

verification.title: Confirm the brake assembly is complete
verification.body: Confirm the tabbed clip is at the top, the pads are installed in their intended positions, all applicable new kit hardware has been fitted, and both guide-pin bolts have been tightened to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm). Confirm the temporary caliper support has been removed after securing the caliper.

verification.title: Confirm wheel seating and tightening
verification.body: Confirm the mounting faces and pilot bore were cleaned, XL-2 was restricted to the pilot interface, and the five nuts were tightened on clean, dry threads in a star pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) with the car resting on its tires.

verification.title: Complete the pedal and fluid checks
verification.body: Confirm the brake pedal was depressed after reassembly and the reservoir level checked, with any necessary top-up using PM-20 fluid meeting WSS-M6C65-A2. These confirm completion of the installation actions; they do not establish the cause of a separate braking complaint.

verification.title: Keep the wheel-nut follow-up
verification.body: Make sure the required retightening within 160 km (100 mi) is scheduled, and carry it out using the specified torque and star pattern.

guides.title: Replace front brake pads in four-piston calipers
guides.summary: Remove the wheel, release the pad spring and retaining pins, retract the pistons and fit the pads with their kit hardware. Finish with correct wheel installation, pedal operation and a brake-fluid level check.
guides.introduction: Four pistons do the squeezing, while a spring and two pins keep the brake pads from pursuing careers elsewhere. Those small retainers deserve your attention just as much as the big caliper. I’ll walk you through reaching them, making room for the new pads and putting everything back in order, including the wheel mounting details that are easy to rush.
guides.why: Brake pads provide the friction material that the caliper pistons press against the rotating brake disc to slow the car. Retracting the pistons creates room for replacement pads. After assembly, operating the brake pedal takes up the resulting clearance, and checking the reservoir confirms the brake-fluid level.
searchTerms: brake pad spring and retaining pins

when.summary: Use this replacement procedure for a 2015 Mustang with a 2.3L or 5.0L engine and four-piston front brake calipers, once pad replacement has been established.
notes: Confirm the fitted front caliper type before ordering pads or starting work. Engine size alone does not identify the brake configuration.
This is a pad replacement procedure, not a diagnosis for noise, vibration or poor braking.

prepare.title: Arrange proper lifting equipment
prepare.detail: Have a suitable hoist and identify the vehicle’s triangle-marked lifting locations before raising it. The vehicle’s emergency jack is intended only for changing a deflated tire, not this service. Never get underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; use floor stands whenever working underneath a jacked vehicle.

prepare.title: Gather the pad kit and tools
prepare.detail: Have the correct four-piston front brake pad kit, its instruction sheet, a brake pad spreader tool, wheel-nut removal equipment and a torque wrench capable of 150 lb-ft (204 Nm). New pads require every new hardware item supplied in their kit.

prepare.title: Keep the two lubricants distinct
prepare.detail: Use the brake pad kit’s lubricant exactly where its instruction sheet directs. For the wheel’s central locating interface, obtain Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2. These are separate applications; I keep them separate on the bench so the wrong tube cannot volunteer for the job.

prepare.title: Have the correct brake fluid available
prepare.detail: For topping up after assembly, use Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid, PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2.

prepare.title: Recognize when the job needs additional instructions
prepare.detail: This procedure covers pad replacement through the caliper opening with the hydraulic connections intact. It does not provide methods for measuring pad wear, disc thickness or installed disc runout, repairing seized parts, or bleeding the hydraulic system. If an inspection or a difficulty during the work calls for one of those operations, obtain the matching service procedure before proceeding. The pad kit’s instruction sheet is also necessary for its lubricant placement.

steps.title: Position and raise the vehicle at the marked lifting points
steps.body:
Before lifting, use a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Confirm the jack or hoist is rated for the vehicle, including cargo and modifications. If using a jack, support the vehicle on suitable stands at the designated points before going underneath; a jack alone is not a support. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

With the transmission in Neutral, position the vehicle on a hoist. Locate the triangles stamped into the body or frame and use the corresponding lifting locations. The lifting illustration shows four locations along the sides of the underbody, near the front and rear wheel areas.

Check adapter clearance before lifting: avoid the suspension, exhaust, steering linkage, mounting brackets and stabilizer brackets where fitted. On a two-column hoist, also avoid contact that could damage the axle or rear cover. Never lift against either bumper. If using a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving onto it.

Raising the vehicle at an incorrect location can make it shift or fall. See [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631).

steps.title: Remove the wheel and tire assembly
steps.body:
Remove the five wheel nuts, then remove the wheel and tire assembly to expose the front caliper and brake disc. If a wheel nut is seized, do not apply heat: it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. Resolve that obstruction before continuing.

Keep the wheel nuts available for reassembly with their threads clean and dry. See [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Remove the brake pad spring
steps.body:
Locate the pad spring across the exposed pad area of the caliper. Remove it first, following the arrangement shown in [Four-Piston Brake Pads](#/document/G1693790). Note its position so you can restore the same arrangement during assembly.

I keep the spring and retainers together as they come out; the garage floor already has enough tiny trophies.

steps.title: Remove the pin clip, then both pad pins
steps.body:
Remove the brake pad pin clip. With the clip removed, withdraw the two brake pad pins from the caliper. Both pins must come out before pad removal.

Keep track of how the pins and clip fit together. The reassembly order is pads, both pins, pin clip, then spring.

steps.title: Retract the caliper pistons and remove the pads
steps.body:
Use a brake pad spreader tool to compress the caliper pistons. The tool illustration shows its working faces bearing against the pads and spreading them apart toward the opposing pistons. Position the tool in that arrangement and operate it to create removal clearance.

Remove the spreader and withdraw the pads through the caliper opening once there is sufficient clearance. This pad access sequence leaves the caliper mounted and its brake hose connected.

steps.title: Prepare the replacement pads and install them
steps.body:
Read the pad kit’s instruction sheet before applying its lubricant. Apply the supplied lubricant only as directed and account for all new hardware supplied with the new pads; do not selectively leave kit replacement hardware on the bench.

Fit the replacement pads into the caliper in the corresponding positions established during removal. The retracted pistons provide the space needed for installation. Keep lubricant away from the pad friction material and brake disc friction surfaces.

steps.title: Reinstall the pins, pin clip and spring
steps.body:
Install both brake pad pins, reinstall the pad pin clip, then reinstall the brake pad spring. This reverses the retaining-hardware removal order.

Before covering the assembly with the wheel, confirm that both pins are installed and that the clip and spring are back in their intended positions. Use the new versions wherever these parts were supplied in the pad kit.

steps.title: Clean the wheel mounting faces and central pilot bore
steps.body:
Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel mounting face and the mating hub/brake-disc mounting surface. Check that any fasteners securing the disc to the hub are secure and do not obstruct the wheel’s seating surfaces.

Also clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the center hole that locates over the hub’s raised central pilot. Clean this bore before applying the lubricant in the next step; cleaning only the flat mounting face misses part of the job.

Contamination between the mounting surfaces can allow the wheel nuts to loosen and the wheel to come off, causing loss of control and serious injury or death.

steps.title: Apply a thin film of XL-2 only at the pilot interface
steps.body:
Apply a thin coat of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, only to the interface between the wheel pilot bore and hub pilot.

Keep it off the flat wheel-to-disc mounting surfaces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and disc friction surfaces. The pilot gets the thin film; spreading it around the whole mounting area creates a damn cleanup job and risks component damage.

steps.title: Refit the wheel and finger-tighten the five nuts
steps.body: Position the wheel on the hub and install all five wheel nuts. At this stage, tighten them only finger tight. The wheel-stud and wheel-nut threads must remain clean and dry for the specified final torque.

steps.title: Lower onto the tires and torque the nuts in a star pattern
steps.body:
Before lowering, make sure the parking brake is applied. Restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground, and keep the vehicle restrained for final wheel-nut tightening. Do not lower an unrestrained vehicle in Neutral.

Lower the vehicle so it rests on its tires before final tightening. Tighten the five wheel nuts in a star/cross pattern to 150 lb-ft (204 Nm).

The illustrated order is top, lower left, upper right, upper left, then lower right. This describes the positions as viewed in the illustration; follow the same crossing sequence around your wheel.

Do not tighten consecutively around the circle. An incorrect pattern can produce excessive brake-disc runout—sideways wobble as the disc rotates—and contribute to brake roughness, shudder and vibration.

steps.title: Operate the brake pedal and check the reservoir
steps.body:
After assembly, depress the brake pedal to take up the clearance created by piston retraction. Then check the brake-fluid level in the reservoir and top up as necessary with Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid, PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2.

Treat pedal operation and the reservoir check as required completion actions. Do not move the vehicle with unresolved pedal operation or an incomplete brake assembly. See [Brake Specifications](#/document/G1694687).

steps.title: Arrange the wheel-nut retightening
steps.body:
Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after the wheel is reinstalled. Use the same star/cross pattern and 150 lb-ft (204 Nm) torque with the vehicle resting on its tires.

Wheels can loosen after initial installation. Put the distance reminder somewhere you will actually see it before this small follow-up becomes a large problem.

watchFor.title: Incorrect lifting contact
watchFor.body: Use the triangle-marked lifting locations and check hoist contact and clearance before raising the car. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

watchFor.title: Retaining hardware omitted during assembly
watchFor.body: The completed caliper needs both pad pins, the pin clip and the pad spring. New pads also require every replacement hardware item supplied with their kit.

watchFor.title: Lubricant in the wrong place
watchFor.body: Pad-kit lubricant placement comes from the kit instruction sheet. XL-2 anti-seize belongs only at the wheel pilot bore/hub pilot interface. Keep wheel mounting faces, threads and brake friction surfaces free of anti-seize.

watchFor.title: Wheel seating obstructed by dirt or fasteners
watchFor.body: Clean both mating mounting surfaces and the central pilot bore. Check that rotor-to-hub fasteners do not interfere with wheel seating. Obstructed seating can lead to loose wheel nuts.

watchFor.title: Final tightening performed while the wheel is hanging
watchFor.body: Perform final wheel-nut tightening with the vehicle resting on its tires, using clean, dry threads and the star/cross sequence.

notes: The relevant wear limits are: brake pad minimum thickness 0.118 in (3 mm), maximum pad taper wear in any direction 0.118 in (3 mm), four-piston front brake disc minimum thickness 1.201 in (30.5 mm), and maximum installed brake disc runout 0.002 in (0.05 mm). These are inspection limits, not an instruction to add disc testing to every pad replacement.

Removing the complete wheel and tire does not require tire-changing or balancing machinery. If separate tire service is undertaken on carbon-fiber or alloy wheels, use a center-clamp tire changer such as Hunter Auto 34, Revolution, TC3900 or equivalent, and a balancer that does not contact the wheel face, such as Hunter Road Force Touch GSP9700. Tabletop changers that grip inside the wheel and ride on its front flange, and balancers that contact the wheel face, can damage the wheel.

diagnostics.finding: An established inspection finds pad thickness below 0.118 in (3 mm).
diagnostics.meaning: The pad is below the specified minimum thickness.
diagnostics.next: Replace the pads using this procedure and install all new hardware and lubricant supplied with the kit as directed.

diagnostics.finding: An established inspection finds pad taper wear greater than 0.118 in (3 mm) in any direction.
diagnostics.meaning: The pad exceeds the permitted taper, meaning its wear differs too much across its surface.
diagnostics.next: Address the out-of-limit pads and obtain an appropriate inspection of the uneven wear before treating replacement as a complete repair. The wear pattern alone does not establish a cause.

diagnostics.finding: An established inspection finds a four-piston front brake disc thinner than 1.201 in (30.5 mm).
diagnostics.meaning: The disc is below the minimum thickness for this brake configuration.
diagnostics.next: Arrange disc service using the matching procedure before completing the brake repair. New pads do not correct an undersize disc.

diagnostics.finding: A separate installed-disc runout check reports more than 0.002 in (0.05 mm).
diagnostics.meaning: Disc runout exceeds the specified maximum.
diagnostics.next: Use the matching disc inspection and correction procedure. Do not assume pad replacement alone resolves the finding.

diagnostics.finding: A seized wheel nut prevents removal.
diagnostics.meaning: Wheel access is blocked; it does not establish a brake-pad fault.
diagnostics.next: Stop wheel removal and obtain suitable seized-fastener assistance. Do not use heat on the wheel nut.

diagnostics.finding: The fitted front caliper is not the four-piston configuration.
diagnostics.meaning: This pad-retaining arrangement and its brake-specific values do not establish the correct procedure for that caliper.
diagnostics.next: Use instructions matching the fitted brake configuration before removing its hardware.

verification.title: Pad assembly is complete
verification.body: Before wheel installation, confirm the pads, both pad pins, pin clip and spring are installed, with all applicable new kit hardware accounted for.

verification.title: Wheel installation is complete
verification.body: Confirm the mounting faces and pilot bore were cleaned, XL-2 was confined to the pilot interface, and all five nuts were tightened in the star pattern to 150 lb-ft (204 Nm) with the vehicle resting on its tires.

verification.title: Pedal and fluid completion actions are done
verification.body: Confirm the brake pedal was depressed after assembly and the reservoir level was checked and topped up as necessary with PM-20 fluid meeting WSS-M6C65-A2. These are assembly completion checks, not a diagnosis of the wider brake system.

verification.title: Wheel-nut follow-up is recorded
verification.body: Record the need to retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) of reinstallation.
