guides.title: Replace front brake pads: 2015 Mustang 5.0L with 6-piston calipers
guides.summary: Reach the pads through the caliper opening, remove their retaining hardware, retract the pistons and refit the pads. Finish with correct wheel installation, pedal operation and a brake-fluid level check.
guides.introduction: Six pistons sound like they ought to demand six times the drama. Thankfully, these front pads come out through the caliper opening after a small collection of retainers steps aside. I’ll walk you through that collection in order, including the wheel refit—because getting the brakes right and the wheel wrong would be a spectacularly annoying own goal.
guides.why: The pads are the replaceable friction material that the caliper pistons press against the spinning brake disc to slow the car. Their pins and spring clip keep them retained in the caliper. Retracting the pistons makes room for replacement pads; restoring the hardware, operating the pedal and checking the fluid complete the job.

when.summary: Use this procedure when the front pads need replacement or removal for related work on a 2015 Mustang 5.0L fitted with 6-piston front calipers.
notes: Confirm the fitted calipers before starting. These pad-retaining instructions and the caliper pin-bolt torque apply to the 6-piston arrangement.
This is a replacement procedure, not a diagnosis of brake noise, vibration or reduced braking.
There is no replacement interval given here. The brake-pad minimum thickness is 0.118 in (3 mm), with maximum taper wear of 0.118 in (3 mm) in any direction.

prepare.title: Gather lifting equipment and restraints
prepare.detail: Have a hoist rated for the vehicle’s actual weight, including cargo and modifications, plus wheel chocks. The wheel-access route uses Neutral and a hoist. If a jack is used during handling, its capacity must also be adequate; support the vehicle on floor stands afterward and never get underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. The emergency tire-changing jack is not suitable for this service.

prepare.title: Gather the pad tools and parts
prepare.detail: Have a brake pad spreader, tools matching the actual retaining hardware and wheel nuts, and a torque wrench suitable for 22 lb.ft (30 Nm) and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). For new pads, have all new hardware and lubricant supplied with the pad kit, together with its lubricant application sheet.

prepare.title: Keep the two lubricants straight
prepare.detail: Pad-kit lubricant goes only where the kit instructions direct. The wheel pilot uses a thin film of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2. Have suitable cleaning materials for the wheel mounting faces and central pilot bore. Read the safety information for the materials you use; keep any flammable cleaning solvents away from ignition sources.

prepare.title: Have the correct brake fluid ready
prepare.detail: For a necessary reservoir top-up, use Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid, PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2. See [Brake System Specifications](#/document/G1694687).

prepare.title: Set the practical boundary before dismantling
prepare.detail: This job covers pads and their retainers with the caliper mounted and its hydraulic connections intact. Arrange separate brake assessment if a disc, piston or hydraulic fault needs attention. The thickness and runout limits below are reference limits; measuring methods and those additional repairs require their own procedures.

prepare.title: Wear protection
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. Review the task-relevant precautions in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start
steps.body:
Before working around the car, disable remote start, if fitted, through the Central Display: Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person starting it.

Before the later underhood fluid check, inspect the cooling fans with the ignition off for damage, cracks or separation. A damaged fan must be replaced before underhood work continues. Fans can operate with the ignition off; if your work brings you near them, have them disabled before reaching nearby.

steps.title: Restrain the car and identify the lifting points
steps.body:
Position the car on a hard, level surface. Set the parking brake and chock all wheels that remain on the ground. With those restraints in place, select Neutral for the wheel-removal operation.

Find the stamped triangles identifying the lifting points. The lifting illustration places these along the lower body sides, behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels. Locate the actual stamped marks on the car; do not substitute a nearby suspension part or an approximate position. See [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631).

steps.title: Position the hoist and raise the vehicle
steps.body:
Position the lift arms at the identified lifting points and check their clearance before raising. Keep adapters and forks clear of suspension, steering linkage, exhaust, brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets; also avoid contact that could damage the axle or rear cover. Never apply lifting pressure to either bumper.

If using a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving onto it. Raise and support the car correctly before removing a wheel. Do not use the engine to power the drive wheels during this work.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and expose the caliper
steps.body:
Remove the five wheel nuts, then remove the wheel and tire assembly. Do not use heat on a seized wheel nut; it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing.

The wheel opening now gives access to the caliper’s open outer window and pad retainers. This pad operation leaves the caliper mounted and the brake hose connected. The full wheel procedure is [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Identify and remove the two brake pad pins
steps.body:
Look across the caliper opening: one transverse pad pin is near the upper end and the other near the lower end. These are separate from the single pin bolt nearer the middle of the caliper.

Remove both brake pad pins first. Keep their identity and positions clear for refitting; this is a small hardware collection, but it deserves better than a mystery pile.

steps.title: Remove the spring retainer clip, then the pin bolt
steps.body:
Remove the brake pad spring retainer clip spanning the exposed pad area. Then remove the separate brake caliper pin bolt near the middle of the opening.

Keep this order: two pad pins, spring retainer clip, then caliper pin bolt. The pin bolt’s installation torque is 22 lb.ft (30 Nm). See [6-piston Brake Pads](#/document/G1693791).

steps.title: Retract the caliper pistons with the pads still fitted
steps.body:
Use a brake pad spreader to compress the caliper pistons before removing the pads. The illustrated tool bears against the opposing pads and spreads them outward toward the caliper bodies, pushing the pistons back.

Keep the old pads in place for this operation, then remove the tool once the pistons have been compressed.

steps.title: Remove both pads and consider any existing wear measurements
steps.body:
Withdraw the two pads from the caliper opening, one from each side of the brake disc. Note their positions so the replacement pads can be oriented correctly.

If wear measurements are part of the work, compare them with the limits in the diagnostic rows below. A pad change does not resolve an out-of-limit disc or establish the cause of excessive taper.

steps.title: Prepare and install the replacement pads
steps.body:
When fitting new pads, use all new hardware supplied with the pad kit. Apply the kit’s lubricant according to its instruction sheet before completing assembly; do not guess the application points.

Install the pads into their corresponding positions on either side of the disc. Keep wheel anti-seize away from the pads and disc friction surfaces. Those two lubricants have different jobs, however tempting the nearest tube may be.

steps.title: Restore the retaining hardware in reverse order
steps.body:
Refit the brake caliper pin bolt and tighten it to 22 lb.ft (30 Nm).

Next refit the brake pad spring retainer clip, then reinstall both brake pad pins through their original paths. Use the replacement pieces supplied with the new-pad kit wherever provided.

Before covering the assembly with the wheel, confirm both pads are in position and the bolt, spring clip and both pins have been restored.

steps.title: Clean the wheel mounting faces and pilot bore
steps.body:
Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel’s flat mounting face and the mating mounting surface on the hub or brake disc. Check that any fasteners attaching the disc to the hub are secured and do not stand in the way of those mating surfaces.

Also clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the circular hole that locates over the hub’s raised center. Clean this bore before lubricating it; cleaning only the flat mounting face misses the illustrated pilot-bore treatment.

Contamination trapped between mounting faces can let the wheel nuts loosen and the wheel detach.

steps.title: Lubricate only the pilot interface and refit the wheel
steps.body:
Apply a thin film of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, only at the interface between the wheel pilot bore and the hub pilot.

Keep it off the flat wheel-to-disc mounting faces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and disc friction surfaces. Wheel stud and nut threads must be clean and dry for the specified torque.

Position the wheel on the hub and install all five nuts finger tight at this stage.

steps.title: Restore restraints before completing the lowering operation
steps.body:
Before lowering, set or confirm the parking brake is applied; this must happen while the vehicle is still raised. Keep existing ground-wheel chocks in place.

Lower carefully. As raised tires reach the ground, pause and restore wheel chocks at the wheels now on the ground before completing the descent. Do not wait until the car is fully lowered to restore those restraints.

Finish lowering until the vehicle rests on its tires, ready for final wheel-nut tightening.

steps.title: Torque the wheel nuts in the illustrated star pattern
steps.body:
With the vehicle resting on its tires, tighten the five wheel nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) using a star/cross pattern.

For the illustrated wheel orientation, the order is: top, lower left, upper right, upper left, lower right. On a differently rotated wheel, preserve the same crossing sequence rather than working around adjacent nuts.

The torque applies to clean, dry stud and nut threads. The crossing sequence helps prevent brake-disc runout that can contribute to roughness, shudder and vibration.

steps.title: Operate the brake pedal and correct the fluid level
steps.body:
With the car restrained, depress the brake pedal after installation. Then check the brake-fluid reservoir level under the hood, observing the startup and fan precautions established before the work.

Top up only as necessary with Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid, PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2. See [Brake System Specifications](#/document/G1694687).

Do not treat installation as complete until the pedal has been operated and the reservoir level checked.

steps.title: Record the wheel-nut follow-up
steps.body:
Arrange to retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after reinstalling the wheel. Use the same 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) specification and star pattern with the car resting on its tires.

Keep the parking brake and chocks in use until the stationary checks are finished and you are ready to move the car.

watchFor.title: Three different retaining parts
watchFor.body: The two pad pins, spring retainer clip and single caliper pin bolt are distinct parts. Remove them in that order and install them in reverse. The 22 lb.ft (30 Nm) torque belongs to the caliper pin bolt.

watchFor.title: Incomplete new-pad kit installation
watchFor.body: Install every new hardware item supplied with the new pads. Use the kit’s lubricant instructions rather than transferring assumptions from another pad design.

watchFor.title: Anti-seize on the wrong surface
watchFor.body: XL-2 belongs only at the wheel pilot-bore/hub-pilot interface. Keep the mounting faces, threads and braking surfaces free of it.

watchFor.title: A wheel that cannot sit flush
watchFor.body: Before refitting, remove mounting-face debris and check for interference from disc-to-hub fasteners. Do not use wheel-nut tightening to conceal an obstructed mounting interface.

watchFor.title: Unsafe support or missing restraints
watchFor.body: Never work underneath a car supported only by a jack. Neutral makes the parking brake and ground-wheel chocks essential; confirm the parking brake before lowering and restore chocks as the tires reach the ground.

notes: Applicability is limited to the 2015 Mustang 5.0L with 6-piston front brake calipers.
Keep the two critical fastening values separate: brake caliper pin bolt, 22 lb.ft (30 Nm); wheel nuts, 150 lb.ft (204 Nm).
The wheel stays assembled with its tire for this access operation; tire-changing and balancing machinery are not needed.
The post-installation pedal and fluid checks complete the replacement operation; they are not a diagnosis of a separate braking complaint.

diagnostics.finding: A pad-thickness measurement reaches or falls below 0.118 in (3 mm).
diagnostics.meaning: The pad has reached or passed the specified minimum thickness.
diagnostics.next: Replace the pads using the matching kit and its supplied hardware and lubricant instructions. See [Brake System Specifications](#/document/G1694687).

diagnostics.finding: Measured pad taper exceeds 0.118 in (3 mm) in any direction.
diagnostics.meaning: The difference in pad thickness across the pad exceeds the permitted taper wear.
diagnostics.next: Have the excessive uneven wear assessed before returning the car to service; do not assume new pads alone explain or correct it.

diagnostics.finding: The 6-piston front brake disc measures below 1.244 in (31.6 mm) thick.
diagnostics.meaning: The disc is below the minimum thickness for this front-brake configuration.
diagnostics.next: Arrange the appropriate disc repair before completing the brake work. Do not use the 2-piston or 4-piston disc limits.

diagnostics.finding: Installed brake-disc runout has been measured above 0.002 in (0.05 mm).
diagnostics.meaning: The disc's measured side-to-side variation as it rotates exceeds the specified maximum.
diagnostics.next: Arrange further assessment. During this pad job, still clean the wheel mounting faces and use the prescribed wheel-nut star pattern; those actions do not establish the cause of an existing runout problem.

diagnostics.finding: The wheel mounting faces or central pilot bore contain corrosion, dirt or foreign material.
diagnostics.meaning: The wheel is not ready for correct installation.
diagnostics.next: Clean the flat mating faces and the pilot bore. Check for disc-fastener interference, then apply XL-2 only at the pilot interface before refitting.

diagnostics.finding: The retaining hardware cannot be restored correctly or the caliper pin bolt cannot be tightened to specification.
diagnostics.meaning: Pad retention has not been completed.
diagnostics.next: Keep the vehicle out of service and resolve the fastening problem before installing the wheel and returning the car to use.

verification.title: Pad retention completed before wheel installation
verification.body: Both pads are installed, the caliper pin bolt is tightened to 22 lb.ft (30 Nm), the spring retainer clip is restored and both pad pins are installed. All replacement hardware supplied with new pads has been used.

verification.title: Wheel seating and torque completed
verification.body: The wheel mounting faces and pilot bore were cleaned, XL-2 was confined to the pilot interface, and all five wheel nuts were tightened in a star pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) with the car resting on its tires and the threads clean and dry.

verification.title: Pedal and reservoir checks completed
verification.body: The brake pedal has been depressed after installation. The reservoir level has been checked and, if necessary, corrected with PM-20 fluid meeting WSS-M6C65-A2.

verification.title: Restraints and follow-up accounted for
verification.body: The parking brake was confirmed before lowering, ground-wheel chocks were retained or restored as tires reached the ground, and wheel-nut retightening is planned within 160 km (100 mi).

stepGroups.summary: Remove the retainers in order, retract the pistons and withdraw both pads.

stepGroups.title: Install pads and restore retention

guides.title: Replace the front brake pads with the SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Replace the front pads by supporting the caliper on temporary longer bolts, removing the disc and retracting the pistons with a pad spreader.
guides.introduction: The front brake pads press against the brake disc to produce braking friction. This SVT Performance Package procedure creates pad-removal space by sliding the caliper onto temporary longer bolts and removing the disc. Understanding that arrangement matters: the brake hose must remain protected while the caliper is moved.
guides.why: The caliper pistons and their protective boots can be damaged by levering through the sight hole. The hose can also be damaged if the caliper hangs from it or moves with the steering turned. Correct support, controlled piston retraction and clean pad contact surfaces protect the surrounding parts while the pads are replaced.
searchTerms: SVT Performance Package front brake pads

when.summary: When front pad replacement is required, or the pads must be removed for brake service.
notes: This procedure covers pad removal and installation; it does not provide pad-wear limits or diagnose a braking complaint.

prepare.title: Arrange wheel access and caliper support
prepare.detail: Follow the linked wheel-removal procedure. Have the specified M14 x 180 temporary bolts ready before releasing the caliper mounting bolts.

prepare.title: Gather the brake-service equipment and parts
prepare.detail: Use a brake pad spreader and suitable torque equipment. Obtain new upper and lower caliper bolts. For new pads, retain all hardware, lubricant and application instructions supplied with the pad kit.

steps.title: Remove the wheel
steps.body: Remove the wheel and tire using the linked procedure to expose the front caliper and disc.

steps.title: Transfer the caliper onto longer bolts
steps.body: Remove and discard the upper caliper bolt, then loosely install an M14 x 180 bolt seven full turns. Repeat for the lower bolt. This establishes the temporary support before the caliper is moved.

steps.title: Create access behind the caliper
steps.body: Set the wheels straight ahead. Slide the caliper back along the longer bolts, then carefully remove the brake disc. Keep the caliper supported throughout.

steps.title: Retract the pistons and remove the pads
steps.body: Compress the caliper pistons with the brake pad spreader. Remove the pad pins, then withdraw the pads. Follow this order rather than using the caliper sight hole as a levering point.

steps.title: Prepare the pad contact surfaces
steps.body: Clean the pad-to-caliper contact surfaces. When fitting new pads, install all hardware supplied in the kit and apply its lubricant according to the kit instruction sheet.

steps.title: Reassemble the brake and wheel
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, replacing the temporary bolts with new caliper mounting bolts. The specified upper and lower bolt torque is 136 lb.ft (185 Nm). Refit the wheel through its separate procedure.

watchFor.title: Hose strain
watchFor.body: Do not let the caliper hang from the hose. Keep the wheels straight ahead before sliding the caliper.

watchFor.title: Piston or boot damage
watchFor.body: Do not pry through the caliper sight hole to retract the pistons.

notes: The longer bolts are temporary service supports; the discarded original caliper bolts must not be reused.

verification.title: Restore pad contact and check fluid
verification.body: After assembly, depress the brake pedal. Check the reservoir level and top up as necessary using the brake fluid specified in the linked specifications.

verification.title: Record the final checks
verification.body: Record installation of new caliper bolts, their final tightening and completion of the pedal and reservoir-level checks.

procedures.purpose: Exact front brake-pad removal and installation sequence for the 5.2L SVT Performance Package.
Wheel and tire removal and installation for access to the front brake.
Applicable brake-fluid specification for the final reservoir-level correction.

guides.title: Replace a front brake hose with the SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Replace the front flexible brake hose, renew the caliper connection washers and pressure-bleed the brake system.
guides.introduction: The flexible hose carries hydraulic pressure from the fixed brake tube to the front caliper while accommodating movement at the wheel. This repair disconnects both ends of the hose and releases its mounting points. On the 5.2L application with the SVT Performance Package, completing the job includes pressure bleeding after installation.
guides.why: Opening a brake connection can admit contamination and air. Sealing the openings protects the hydraulic circuit, while bleeding removes air introduced during the work. The caliper connection washers are discarded because the refitted joint requires new sealing washers.
searchTerms: SVT Performance Package front brake hose replacement

when.summary: When the front flexible brake hose requires replacement on the 5.2L SVT Performance Package application.
notes: Allow for pressure bleeding as part of the repair, not as a separate optional operation.

prepare.title: Hydraulic repair capability
prepare.detail: Arrange safe access to the front caliper, hose supports and brake tube connection. Have suitable tightening equipment, a replacement hose, new caliper connection washers and means to seal every opened connection.

prepare.title: Bleeding and paint protection
prepare.detail: Have the equipment and instructions required by Brake System Pressure Bleeding in Section 206-00. Protect painted surfaces and have cold water available for immediate washing if brake fluid is spilled.

steps.title: Disconnect the caliper end
steps.body: Follow the [front flexible hose procedure](#/document/G1716192). Remove the caliper flow bolt, disconnect the hose and discard the washers. Seal the exposed openings to keep foreign material out of the hydraulic system.

steps.title: Release the supports and brake tube connection
steps.body: If fitted, remove the flexible hose bracket mounting bolt. Disconnect the brake tube fitting and seal the openings. Then remove the remaining hose retaining bolt and take out the hose, preserving the specified removal order.

steps.title: Install the replacement in reverse order
steps.body: Refit the hose and tighten its retaining bolt to 25 Nm. Connect the brake tube fitting at 18 Nm, then refit the optional bracket bolt at 20 Nm. Fit new washers at the caliper connection and tighten the flow bolt to 48 Nm. Each value belongs to its particular connection.

steps.title: Pressure-bleed the brake system
steps.body: Carry out Brake System Pressure Bleeding in Section 206-00 after installation. Use that procedure for the bleeding setup and execution; fastening the new hose alone does not remove air from the opened circuit.

watchFor.title: Fluid on paint
watchFor.body: Immediately wash the affected painted area with cold water if brake fluid is spilled.

watchFor.title: Open hydraulic ports
watchFor.body: Keep all openings sealed while disconnected. Clean hydraulic handling is part of this repair.

notes: The separate flexible hose bracket is conditional equipment; remove and refit it only when present.
The washers are discarded. The procedure does not direct replacement of the caliper flow bolt.

verification.title: Connections and supports restored
verification.body: Confirm that new caliper washers are installed, both hydraulic connections are secured and all applicable hose mounting points are tightened.

verification.title: Bleeding completed
verification.body: Complete the required pressure-bleeding procedure and its completion checks before returning the brake system to service.

procedures.purpose: Front flexible brake hose removal and installation for the 5.2L SVT Performance Package, including washer disposal and the required pressure-bleeding handoff.

guides.title: Replace a front brake flexible hose
guides.summary: Replace the flexible connection between the front brake tube and caliper, renew its sealing washers and pressure-bleed the brake system.
guides.introduction: The flexible hose carries hydraulic pressure from the rigid brake tube to the moving front caliper. Replacing it opens the hydraulic circuit at both ends. The repair therefore includes restoring the connections and bleeding the system before the brakes return to service.
guides.why: Open connections admit contamination and air. Air compresses under pressure and interferes with hydraulic brake operation, so tightening the fittings alone does not finish this repair. The caliper connection also depends on sound sealing washers.

when.summary: When a front brake hose requires replacement or removal as part of an established repair.
notes: Identify the fitted caliper before selecting the appropriate removal branch.

prepare.title: Prepare for an open hydraulic circuit
prepare.detail: Arrange access to the caliper connection, brake-tube union and hose mountings. Have suitable caps or plugs to seal every opening, replacement sealing washers and torque tools.

prepare.title: Have bleeding capability ready
prepare.detail: Obtain the Brake System Pressure Bleeding procedure and the equipment it requires before disconnecting the hose. Bleeding is a required part of completion.

steps.title: Detach the caliper end
steps.body: Follow the branch for the fitted 2-, 4- or 6-piston caliper. Remove the caliper flow bolt and detach the hose, sealing the exposed openings. At the illustrated joint, discard both sealing washers and use new ones during installation.

steps.title: Release the remaining hose attachments
steps.body: If fitted, remove the flexible-hose bracket mounting bolt. Disconnect the brake-tube fitting, then remove the hose mounting bolt and hose. Keep all disconnected openings sealed throughout the work.

steps.title: Install the hose and restore the joints
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Tighten the hose mounting bolt to 18 lb.ft (25 Nm), the brake-tube fitting to 155 lb.in (17.5 Nm), and the optional bracket bolt to 177 lb.in (20 Nm). Reconnect the caliper joint with new sealing washers; the flow-bolt torque is 30 lb.ft (40 Nm) for each listed caliper branch.

steps.title: Bleed the brake system
steps.body: Complete Brake System Pressure Bleeding after installation. Use that procedure for the actual bleeding method; do not return the vehicle to service with the required hydraulic work unfinished.

watchFor.title: Brake fluid on paint
watchFor.body: Immediately wash any affected paintwork with cold water.

watchFor.title: Unsealed openings
watchFor.body: Keep both hose ends and their mating openings protected until each connection is reassembled.

notes: The caliper piston count selects the branch, but all three branches specify the same flow-bolt torque.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical and hydraulic completion
verification.body: Check that both hydraulic connections and all applicable hose mountings have been restored to their specified torque.

verification.title: Record the bleeding completion
verification.body: Record completion of the required pressure-bleeding procedure as part of the hose repair.

procedures.purpose: Front brake hose removal and installation for 2-, 4- and 6-piston calipers, followed by the referenced pressure-bleeding procedure.

guides.title: Replace the SVT Performance Package rear brake caliper
guides.summary: Remove and install the rear caliper using new mounting bolts and hose-sealing washers, then bleed the brake system.
guides.introduction: The rear caliper uses hydraulic pressure to press the brake pads against the disc. On this 5.2L SVT Performance Package arrangement, removal also involves the parking-brake cable's shoe actuation lever and support bracket. The job opens the hydraulic circuit, so mechanical reassembly must be followed by brake-system bleeding.
guides.why: Sealing exposed hydraulic openings protects the fluid path during removal. The hose connection requires fresh washers, and the caliper mounting bolts must also be renewed. Cleaning and correctly lubricating the pad contact surfaces prepares the caliper for proper pad movement after assembly.

when.summary: When the SVT Performance Package rear caliper requires removal or replacement.
notes: Have the applicable Brake System Pressure Bleeding procedure available before opening the hydraulic connection.

prepare.title: Arrange access and hydraulic-service capability
prepare.detail: Follow the linked SVT rear Brake Pads procedure for access. Have suitable means to seal all exposed openings and the capability and equipment required by the pressure-bleeding procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement parts
prepare.detail: Have new caliper mounting bolts, new brake-hose sealing washers and a torque wrench. If fitting new pads, retain all hardware, lubricant and instructions supplied with the pad kit.

steps.title: Remove the rear pads
steps.body: Follow Brake Pads — Vehicles With: SVT Performance Package. Complete that access phase before disconnecting the hose or removing the caliper mounting hardware.

steps.title: Disconnect the hydraulic hose
steps.body: Remove the caliper flow bolt and disconnect the brake hose. Discard the sealing washers and seal every exposed opening to protect the hydraulic system during the remaining work.

steps.title: Free the parking-brake cable
steps.body: Disconnect the cable from the parking-brake shoe actuation lever. Press the retaining tabs inward and detach the cable from its bracket.

steps.title: Remove the bracket and caliper
steps.body: Remove and discard the mounting bolts. Remove the bracket, followed by the caliper. Keep the bracket and cable arrangement identifiable for reassembly.

steps.title: Prepare the pad contact surfaces
steps.body: Clean the brake pad-to-caliper contact surfaces and apply the lubricant supplied with the brake pad kit according to its instruction sheet. If fitting new pads, install all new hardware and lubricant supplied with that kit.

steps.title: Reassemble with new fasteners and washers
steps.body: Reverse removal to restore the caliper, bracket, cable and hose connections. Tighten the new caliper mounting bolts to 81 lb.ft (110 Nm). Reconnect the hose using new sealing washers and tighten the flow bolt to 35 lb.ft (48 Nm). Complete pad installation through the linked SVT procedure.

steps.title: Bleed the brake system
steps.body: Carry out Brake System Pressure Bleeding as required by the caliper installation procedure. Opening the hose connection makes bleeding part of completing this repair; use the applicable bleeding instructions for its equipment, sequence and completion checks.

watchFor.title: Brake fluid on paint
watchFor.body: Immediately wash affected paintwork with cold water if fluid is spilled.

watchFor.title: Reused sealing or mounting parts
watchFor.body: The removed hose washers and caliper mounting bolts are discarded parts. Prepare their replacements before reassembly.

watchFor.title: Unsealed openings
watchFor.body: Keep hydraulic openings sealed while disconnected so the exposed fluid path remains protected.

notes: The parking-brake cable connection described here is at the shoe actuation lever. Restore that connection and its bracket retention during reassembly.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical completion
verification.body: Confirm the bracket and cable retention are restored, pad contact surfaces are prepared, and the required new bolts and washers are installed.

verification.title: Record fastening and bleeding completion
verification.body: Record tightening of the mounting bolts and hose flow bolt to their respective specifications, and completion of the required brake-system pressure bleed.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L SVT Performance Package rear caliper removal and installation, hose sealing, parking-brake cable release, new fasteners and required final bleeding.
SVT Performance Package rear brake-pad removal and installation before and after caliper replacement.

guides.title: Remove and refit the rear brake caliper anchor plate
guides.summary: Remove the rear brake pads and caliper for access, then refit the anchor plate with new mounting bolts.
guides.introduction: The rear brake caliper anchor plate supports the brake pads and locates the caliper assembly beside the disc. Removing it involves the pad-service sequence first. The job finishes by restoring the pad and caliper arrangement, seating the brakes with the pedal and checking the reservoir level.
guides.why: The brake hose must remain free of the caliper's weight throughout the work because hanging the assembly from it can damage the hose. The anchor-plate bolts are discarded during removal. Correct piston-to-pad alignment also matters: the rear caliper incorporates a parking-brake mechanism that affects piston retraction.
searchTerms: rear caliper piston will not retract

when.summary: When rear brake service requires removal or replacement of the caliper anchor plate.
notes: Plan the work together with the rear Brake Pads procedure.

prepare.title: Provide wheel access and caliper support
prepare.detail: Arrange safe vehicle lifting and wheel removal using the procedure referenced by Brake Pads. Have a means of supporting the caliper independently of its hose.

prepare.title: Have replacement fasteners and suitable tools
prepare.detail: Obtain new anchor-plate bolts and a torque wrench. A brake caliper piston retractor is required if new pads will be installed.

steps.title: Remove the pads for access
steps.body: Follow the rear Brake Pads procedure: remove the wheel and tire, remove the caliper bolts, and position the supported caliper aside. Remove the pads and their clips.

steps.title: Release the anchor plate
steps.body: Remove the two anchor-plate mounting bolts and the plate. Discard those bolts. Keep the caliper supported while the mounting area is exposed.

steps.title: Install the anchor plate
steps.body: Reverse the plate-removal operation using new mounting bolts. Tighten them to 129 lb.ft (175 Nm). This is the anchor-plate specification.

steps.title: Prepare the pads and piston
steps.body: If fitting new pads, use the piston retractor to compress the caliper piston. Apply moderate to heavy force toward the piston so the internal parking-brake clutch cone engages. Restore the clips and pads, and ensure the piston notch aligns with the pin on the inboard pad.

steps.title: Restore the caliper and wheel
steps.body: Refit the caliper without disturbing the piston-notch alignment. Tighten its bolts to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm), then complete wheel and tire installation using the referenced wheel procedure.

steps.title: Seat the brakes and check fluid
steps.body: Depress the brake pedal. Check the brake-fluid reservoir level and top up as necessary with the fluid specified in Brake System — General Information.

watchFor.title: Hose carrying the assembly
watchFor.body: Support the caliper whenever its fasteners are removed; the hose must not carry the caliper or anchor-plate assembly.

watchFor.title: Different bolt specifications
watchFor.body: Keep the anchor-plate and caliper mounting operations distinct. Their tightening specifications differ.

notes: Piston retraction is conditional on installing new brake pads.

diagnostics.finding: The piston does not compress during new-pad preparation.
diagnostics.meaning: Insufficient inward force can prevent the internal parking-brake clutch cone from engaging.
diagnostics.next: Follow the retractor method and required inward loading in the Brake Pads procedure; resistance alone does not establish caliper failure.

verification.title: Confirm assembly and completion
verification.body: Confirm new anchor-plate bolts were used, both bolt groups were tightened correctly, and the piston notch matches the inboard-pad pin.

verification.title: Record the final checks
verification.body: Record completion of pedal application and the reservoir-level check, including any necessary top-up.

procedures.purpose: Rear caliper anchor-plate removal and installation, including discarded bolts and mounting torque.
Rear pad and caliper access, conditional piston retraction, pad alignment and final pedal/fluid checks.

guides.title: Remove and Replace the Rear Brake Caliper
guides.summary: Disconnect the rear caliper’s parking-brake cable and hydraulic hose, replace the caliper, then bleed and adjust the brake systems.
guides.introduction: The rear caliper applies the pads to the brake disc. This assembly also has a parking-brake lever operated by a cable, so removal involves both a hydraulic connection and a mechanical connection. Installing the caliper is only part of the job: opening the hose connection requires brake bleeding, and disturbing the cable requires parking-brake adjustment.
guides.why: Air admitted through an open hydraulic connection affects brake operation. The hose connection also uses sealing washers that must be discarded during removal and renewed during installation. Keeping openings sealed protects the hydraulic circuit, while the final cable adjustment restores the parking brake’s working relationship with the caliper lever.

when.summary: When diagnosis or other repair work requires rear brake caliper removal or replacement.
notes: Plan for hydraulic bleeding and parking-brake adjustment before disconnecting the caliper.

prepare.title: Wheel access and support
prepare.detail: Have suitable vehicle-lifting and support capability and follow the Wheel and Tire procedure for access.

prepare.title: Hydraulic service capability
prepare.detail: Prepare suitable opening seals, new hose-connection sealing washers and torque equipment. Have the equipment and complete instructions for Brake System Pressure Bleeding in section 206-00.

prepare.title: Protect the finish
prepare.detail: Arrange to contain brake fluid. Any fluid spilled on paintwork must be washed off immediately with cold water.

steps.title: Expose the caliper and release cable tension
steps.body: Remove the wheel and tire using [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507). Loosen the parking-brake cable adjustment nut before trying to disconnect the cable.

steps.title: Disconnect the parking-brake cable
steps.body: Disconnect the cable from the caliper lever, detach it from the bracket and position it aside. Both attachment points must be released before removing the caliper.

steps.title: Disconnect the hose and remove the caliper
steps.body: Following [Brake Caliper](#/document/G1693752), remove the hose flow bolt and disconnect the hose. Discard its sealing washers and seal all openings. Remove the two caliper mounting bolts and lift away the caliper.

steps.title: Install the caliper and restore connections
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, using new sealing washers at the hose connection. Tighten the caliper bolts to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm) and the flow bolt to 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm). Restore the cable’s bracket and lever connections and complete wheel installation under its procedure.

steps.title: Bleed and adjust
steps.body: Complete Brake System Pressure Bleeding in section 206-00. Then carry out [Parking Brake Cable Adjustment](#/document/G1693766). These are required completion phases, rather than optional responses to a noticeable problem.

watchFor.title: Reused sealing washers
watchFor.body: The removed washers are discard items. Do not reinstall them when reconnecting the hose.

watchFor.title: Unsealed hydraulic openings
watchFor.body: Keep every opening sealed while disconnected, as required by the caliper procedure.

notes: This is a caliper removal and installation job; it does not establish the cause of a braking complaint or provide a caliper overhaul procedure.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical and hydraulic completion
verification.body: Confirm the hose and caliper fasteners are tightened, the cable is connected at its lever and bracket, and wheel installation is complete.

verification.title: Record the required follow-up work
verification.body: Record completion of brake-system pressure bleeding and parking-brake cable adjustment. Follow the completion checks in each full procedure before returning the vehicle to service.

procedures.purpose: Rear caliper removal and installation, including hose washers and cable disconnection.
Wheel and tire removal and installation for caliper access.
Required parking-brake cable adjustment after caliper installation.

guides.title: Replace the rear brake disc: 2015 Mustang 5.2L with SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Release the parking-brake cable, support and move the caliper aside, then replace the rear disc. Reassemble with two new mounting bolts tightened to 81 lb.ft (110 Nm), and refit the wheel using the specified cleaning and tightening procedure.
guides.introduction: The rear brake disc looks ready to leave once the wheel is off, but the parking-brake cable and caliper still have custody papers. I’ll walk you through releasing them in order, supporting the caliper without straining its hose, and getting the disc back onto clean seating surfaces. This job applies to the 2015 Mustang with the 5.2L engine and SVT Performance Package.
guides.why: The disc turns with the wheel, giving the brake pads surfaces to grip when you press the pedal. Its seating surfaces need to be clean so it sits properly against the hub. The caliper must remain independently supported while it is moved aside, and the two bolts marked for discard must be replaced. Wheel cleaning and tightening matter too: careless assembly here can undermine otherwise careful brake work.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang 5.2L SVT Performance Package rear brake disc

when.summary: Use this procedure when rear brake-disc replacement has already been established as necessary, or when the disc needs removal for associated work.
notes: This is a removal and installation job, not a way to decide whether a braking complaint needs a new disc.

prepare.title: Confirm the job and its limits
prepare.detail: Confirm the vehicle is a 2015 Mustang 5.2L with the SVT Performance Package, and obtain the correct replacement rear disc if replacing it. Have two new bolts ready for the caliper/bracket mounting positions identified below. Disc wear limits, runout measurements, seized-disc extraction, caliper piston retraction and hydraulic repairs require separate instructions; do not improvise those operations as part of this job.

prepare.title: Gather cleaning materials and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Have a wire brush, Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner — VOC Compliant or Motorcraft Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A or PM-4-B, and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2. Use suitable fastener tools and torque equipment capable of 81 lb.ft (110 Nm) and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm).

prepare.title: Arrange safe lifting and caliper support
prepare.detail: Use a suitable hoist and a caliper support hook or equivalent independent support. The vehicle’s emergency jack is intended only for changing a deflated tire; do not use it for this repair. Never get underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack: floor stands are required when using jack support. Identify the stamped triangles marking the lifting locations before raising the vehicle.

prepare.title: Keep the three procedures together
prepare.detail: The actions below combine the [rear brake-disc procedure](#/document/G1716401), [wheel removal and installation](#/document/G1686507), and [jacking and lifting precautions](#/document/G1663631). I’ve included the relevant access and reassembly work here so you can keep the sequence straight.

steps.title: Position the vehicle and identify the lifting points
steps.body:
Before lifting, use a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Confirm the jack or hoist is rated for the vehicle, including cargo and modifications. If using a jack, support the vehicle on suitable stands at the designated points before going underneath; a jack alone is not a support. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on the hoist. Locate the triangles stamped into the body or frame; the lifting illustration shows four marked locations along the sides of the underbody. Use these designated locations. Lifting elsewhere can allow the vehicle to shift or fall.
Before using a drive-on lift, check for underbody interference. Position hoist adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering components. On a two-column hoist, also keep the lifting forks clear of mounting brackets, stabilizer mounting brackets where fitted, the axle and rear cover. Never apply lifting pressure to either bumper.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle and remove the rear wheel
steps.body:
Raise and securely support the vehicle using the identified lifting points. Remove the five wheel nuts and take off the wheel and tire assembly to expose the rear brake disc and caliper.
Do not use heat on a seized wheel nut; it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. A stubborn nut does not earn permission to bring out the torch.

steps.title: Disconnect the parking-brake cable from the lever
steps.body:
With all four wheels fully clear of the ground and the vehicle securely supported, release the parking brake before working on its cable or moving the rear caliper assembly. The car must remain securely supported while the parking brake is released.

Behind the disc, locate the parking-brake cable end where it connects to the parking-brake shoe actuation lever, beside the coil spring shown in the illustration. This lever transfers the cable’s pull to the parking-brake mechanism. Disconnect the cable end from the lever before trying to move the caliper assembly aside.

steps.title: Release the cable housing from its bracket
steps.body: Follow the cable to the retaining fitting seated in the bracket opening. Press its three retaining tabs inward, as shown in the close-up, and withdraw the fitting from the bracket. The cable end and its housing retention are separate connections; both must be free before proceeding.

steps.title: Support the caliper and remove the mounting bolts
steps.body:
Arrange the support hook so it can carry the caliper’s weight independently of the flexible brake hose. Identify the two mounting bolts behind the caliper, one above the other in the illustration. Remove both bolts and discard them.
Keep the caliper supported as the fastening arrangement is released. Never allow it to hang from its brake hose; the load can damage the hose.

steps.title: Remove the bracket and position the caliper aside
steps.body: Remove the bracket after releasing the two bolts, then move the caliper aside far enough to clear the disc. Leave the brake hose connected and maintain independent support throughout the disc work. Check that moving the caliper has not made the hose carry its weight or pull tight.

steps.title: Remove the brake disc
steps.body: With the caliper clear, withdraw the disc outward over the five wheel studs and off the hub. The disc illustration shows the complete disc being removed from the hub. Keep the removed bolts separate from the new hardware so they cannot sneak back into service.

steps.title: Clean the disc seating surfaces and install the disc
steps.body:
Use the wire brush and Motorcraft PM-4-A or PM-4-B brake cleaner to clean the disc mating surfaces, including the seating interface between the disc and hub. Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material that would remain trapped between the faces. Check the faces before assembly and continue cleaning if deposits remain.
Position the replacement disc, or the removed disc if this was an access operation, over the wheel studs and onto the hub. Confirm that it seats against the cleaned mating surface.

steps.title: Restore the caliper and bracket with new bolts
steps.body:
Bring the supported caliper back into its installed position and reinstall the bracket. Fit two new bolts in place of the discarded bolts and tighten them to 81 lb.ft (110 Nm).
Keep the caliper supported until it is secured. Then remove the temporary support and check that the brake hose is free of the support and is not carrying an unintended load.

steps.title: Reconnect the parking-brake cable
steps.body: Push the cable-housing fitting back into its bracket so the retaining tabs hold it in place. Reconnect the cable end to the parking-brake shoe actuation lever. Check both connections directly: the housing must be retained in the bracket, and the cable end must be engaged with the lever. One connection does not substitute for the other.

steps.title: Clean the wheel mounting faces and central pilot bore
steps.body:
Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel’s flat mounting surface and the corresponding hub/disc mounting surface. Check that any fasteners attaching the disc to the hub are secured and do not interfere with the wheel seating flat.
Also clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the center opening that fits over the hub’s locating shoulder. The cleaning callout includes this bore, not just the flat wheel face.
These surfaces must be clean before wheel installation. Contamination can allow the wheel nuts to loosen and the wheel to come off while driving, with a risk of loss of control and serious injury.

steps.title: Apply anti-seize only at the pilot interface and fit the wheel
steps.body:
Apply a thin film of Motorcraft XL-2 High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant only where the wheel pilot bore meets the hub pilot. The pilot is the central locating fit; it is separate from the flat clamping faces.
Keep anti-seize off the wheel-to-disc mounting face, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and disc friction surfaces. The wheel stud and nut threads must be clean and dry for the specified torque.
Position the wheel on the hub and install all five wheel nuts finger tight at this stage. The little tube has one very specific job here; enthusiasm is not a lubricant specification.

steps.title: Lower onto the tires and torque the wheel nuts
steps.body:
Before lowering, make sure the parking brake is applied. Restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground, and keep the vehicle restrained for final wheel-nut tightening. Do not lower an unrestrained vehicle in Neutral.

Lower the vehicle until it rests on its tires before final tightening. Tighten all five wheel nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), using a star/cross pattern.
With one nut at the top, the illustrated sequence is: top, lower left, upper right, upper left, lower right. If the wheel is rotated, preserve that same across-the-wheel pattern.
Do not tighten consecutively around the circle. Uneven tightening can create excessive disc runout—side-to-side movement as the disc turns—and accelerate brake roughness, shudder and vibration.

steps.title: Complete the brake check and schedule wheel-nut retightening
steps.body:
Apply the brake pedal several times to verify correct brake-system operation after installation. If operation is abnormal, keep the vehicle out of use until the problem has been assessed and corrected.
Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after the wheel is reinstalled, using the specified torque and star pattern. Wheels can loosen after initial tightening; missing this follow-up can result in serious injury.

watchFor.title: The hose becoming the caliper support
watchFor.body: Watch the hose while moving and supporting the caliper. If the hose begins carrying the load, reposition the independent support before continuing.

watchFor.title: Old bolts mixed with installation hardware
watchFor.body: The two removed caliper/bracket mounting bolts are discard items. Use two new bolts and tighten them to 81 lb.ft (110 Nm).

watchFor.title: Anti-seize spreading beyond the central pilot
watchFor.body: A thin film belongs only between the wheel pilot bore and hub pilot. Keep the flat wheel mounting face, studs, nuts, pads and disc friction surfaces free of it.

watchFor.title: A wheel that cannot seat against clean faces
watchFor.body: Remaining deposits or interfering disc-to-hub fasteners must be addressed before installing the wheel. Wheel-nut torque cannot compensate for an obstructed mounting face.

notes: The tire stays mounted on the wheel for this disc job. If separate tire work is added on carbon-fiber or alloy wheels, Ford requires a center-clamp tire changer, such as a Hunter Auto 34, Revolution, TC3900 or equivalent. Do not use a table-top machine that grips inside the wheel and rides on its front flange.

For separate balancing work on carbon-fiber or alloy wheels, use a balancer that does not contact the wheel face, such as a Hunter Road Force Touch GSP9700. Machines that contact the wheel face can damage it.

diagnostics.finding: Corrosion, dirt or foreign material remains on a disc seating face or wheel mounting face.
diagnostics.meaning: The parts are not ready to be clamped together on clean mating surfaces.
diagnostics.next: Continue cleaning before assembly. Use the wire brush and PM-4-A or PM-4-B cleaner for the disc mating surfaces, and remove contamination from the wheel and hub/disc mounting faces.

diagnostics.finding: The cable housing is outside its bracket or the cable end is not engaged with the lever after reassembly.
diagnostics.meaning: The parking-brake cable reconnection is incomplete.
diagnostics.next: Seat the housing fitting so its retaining tabs hold it in the bracket, reconnect the cable end to the actuation lever, and confirm both connections before fitting the wheel.

diagnostics.finding: A wheel nut is seized during removal.
diagnostics.meaning: Normal wheel removal cannot continue with that nut secured.
diagnostics.next: Stop for an appropriate seized-fastener removal method. Do not apply heat, because it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing.

diagnostics.finding: Brake operation is abnormal during the repeated pedal applications after assembly.
diagnostics.meaning: The required completion check has not passed; this result alone does not identify the cause.
diagnostics.next: Keep the vehicle out of use and obtain further brake-system assessment before driving.

verification.title: Confirm the mechanical reassembly
verification.body: Check that the disc is seated, the caliper and bracket are secured with two new bolts torqued to 81 lb.ft (110 Nm), the temporary support is removed, and both parking-brake cable connections are restored. These are assembly checks, not additional diagnostic tests.

verification.title: Confirm wheel installation
verification.body: Confirm that the wheel mounting faces and pilot bore were cleaned, XL-2 was confined to the pilot interface, and all five nuts were tightened in a star pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) with clean, dry threads and the vehicle resting on its tires.

verification.title: Verify brake operation
verification.body: Apply the brake pedal several times and confirm correct brake-system operation before returning the vehicle to use.

verification.title: Complete the wheel-nut follow-up
verification.body: Arrange wheel-nut retightening within 160 km (100 mi) of wheel installation. Use 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) and the star/cross pattern.

procedures.purpose: Rear brake-disc removal and installation for the SVT Performance Package, including cable release, caliper support, two replacement mounting bolts, cleaning and brake-pedal verification.
Wheel removal, mounting-face and pilot-bore cleaning, restricted XL-2 application, wheel-nut torque and star sequence, and the required retightening interval.
Stamped-triangle lifting-point identification, secure vehicle support and hoist-clearance precautions.

stepGroups.title: Lift the vehicle and expose the brake
stepGroups.summary: Identify the correct lifting points and remove the rear wheel.

stepGroups.title: Release the cable and remove the disc
stepGroups.summary: Disconnect both cable attachments, support the caliper and clear the disc.

stepGroups.title: Seat the disc and restore the brake assembly
stepGroups.summary: Clean the mating surfaces, install new bolts and reconnect the cable.

stepGroups.title: Clean and refit the wheel
stepGroups.summary: Prepare the mounting faces and pilot, then torque the nuts in a star pattern.

stepGroups.title: Check operation and arrange retightening
stepGroups.summary: Perform the pedal check and retain the wheel-nut follow-up requirement.

guides.title: Replace the rear brake disc shield with the SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Replace the rear brake disc shield by removing the parking brake shoes and rear hub, then rebuilding those assemblies with the required new fasteners.
guides.introduction: The brake disc shield is the stationary plate behind the rear brake disc. On the 5.2L Mustang with the SVT Performance Package, reaching its mounting bolts requires removal of both the parking brake shoes and the wheel bearing and hub assembly. The shield itself is straightforward to replace; most of the work lies in gaining access and correctly restoring the brake and hub assemblies.
guides.why: The hub connects the wheel to the rear suspension and halfshaft, so its fastening requirements remain critical even when the original repair concerns only the shield. The spindle nut and hub bolts must be renewed, and the hub installation includes both cross-pattern tightening and a staged spindle-nut tightening sequence.
searchTerms: SVT rear brake disc shield replacement
rear hub removal for brake shield

when.summary: When an inspected rear brake disc shield requires replacement on a car with the SVT Performance Package.
notes: This is a removal and installation job; it does not establish whether a brake noise originates at the shield.

prepare.title: Plan the brake and hub access work
prepare.detail: Arrange safe wheel-off access and the capability to remove and reinstall the package-specific parking brake shoes, rear brake disc and hub. Follow the prerequisite procedures reached through the shield instructions.

prepare.title: Have the puller and replacement hardware ready
prepare.detail: The rear hub procedure specifies tool 205-D070 (D93P-1175-B), Remover, Front Wheel Hub. Obtain a new spindle nut and four new hub bolts, plus suitable torque and angle-tightening equipment.

steps.title: Remove the parking brake shoes
steps.body: Begin with the SVT Performance Package parking brake shoe procedure referenced by the [shield procedure](#/document/G1716402). Complete that access phase before removing the hub. Keep track of components already removed so the overlapping brake and hub procedures remain a coherent job.

steps.title: Release the halfshaft and remove the hub
steps.body: Follow the [rear wheel bearing and hub procedure](#/document/G1686657). Remove and discard the spindle nut, then use the specified remover to press the halfshaft from the hub. Complete the required brake-disc access, discard the four hub bolts and remove the bearing and hub assembly.

steps.title: Remove the exposed shield
steps.body: With the parking brake shoes and hub out of the way, remove the shield bolts and lift away the shield. This is the component replacement phase; the preceding removals provide access to its otherwise obstructed mounting area.

steps.title: Install the replacement shield
steps.body: Position the shield and reinstall its bolts, reversing its removal. Tighten the shield bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). Keep this specification separate from the much higher hub-fastener tightening requirements.

steps.title: Restore the hub and brake assemblies
steps.body: Reverse the access work through the hub and package-specific parking brake procedures, coordinating their shared disc and wheel access. Install four new hub bolts and tighten them in a cross pattern. Apply the brake to prevent halfshaft rotation while completing the full staged tightening sequence for the new spindle nut.

watchFor.title: Discarded hardware returning to service
watchFor.body: The removed spindle nut and four hub bolts must not return to service. Keep discarded hardware separate and follow the distinct shield-attachment instructions.

watchFor.title: Unsuitable suspension fasteners
watchFor.body: Replacement suspension fasteners must be the same or equivalent quality and design. Their role in retaining the hub makes substitution with lesser-quality parts unacceptable.

notes: The linked hub procedure applies to several engines; the shield and parking brake access here are specifically for the SVT Performance Package.
The illustration shows the hub-removal access area and the hub bolts designated for disposal.

verification.title: Confirm shield and brake reassembly
verification.body: Confirm the shield bolts are tightened and all parking brake, brake-disc and wheel installation work required by the access procedures is complete.

verification.title: Confirm hub fastening
verification.body: Verify that new hub bolts received cross-pattern tightening and that the new spindle nut received every stage of its specified tightening sequence.

Rear wheel bearing and hub removal and installation, including halfshaft release, replacement fasteners and staged tightening.
