guides.title: Replace the rear brake disc shield
guides.summary: Reach the rear shield by removing the wheel, supporting the caliper assembly aside and removing the disc. Reassemble with new caliper assembly bolts, clean mounting surfaces and the correct tightening sequence.
guides.introduction: The rear brake disc shield has three little bolts and a whole brake assembly guarding the entrance. Typical. I’ll walk you through getting that assembly safely out of the way, replacing the shield and putting everything back with the right fasteners and torque. This applies to the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine.
guides.why: The shield is the stationary protective plate behind the rotating brake disc. Replacing it means disturbing the disc, caliper mounting and wheel mounting, so the important work extends beyond those three shield bolts. I treat the supported brake hose, replacement caliper bolts and clean mounting faces as part of the shield job—not optional housekeeping.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang rear brake disc shield replacement

when.summary: Use this procedure when the rear brake disc shield needs removal or replacement.
notes: Applies to 2015 Mustang 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications.
The shield is reached through the rear brake-disc removal sequence.

prepare.title: Establish the repair before dismantling
prepare.detail: This is a removal-and-replacement walkthrough. A scraping noise alone does not establish that the shield needs replacing; no noise-isolation test, shield rejection measurement or seized-disc removal method is included.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and caliper support
prepare.detail: This walkthrough uses a vehicle hoist, matching the wheel-removal sequence. Its capacity must cover the vehicle, cargo and modifications. Have wheel chocks and a suitable hanger or independent support for the complete caliper-and-anchor-plate assembly. If using a jack for any positioning work, use correctly rated equipment and floor stands; never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. The emergency wheel-change jack is unsuitable for this repair.

prepare.title: Have the shield, replacement bolts and torque tools ready
prepare.detail: Have the correct replacement rear shield and two new caliper-and-anchor-plate mounting bolts for each assembly removed. Those two bolts are discarded during removal. Have suitable fastener tools and torque tools covering 106 lb.in (12 Nm), 129 lb.ft (175 Nm) and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm).

prepare.title: Gather cleaning and lubrication materials
prepare.detail: Use a wire brush and Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner – VOC Compliant or Motorcraft Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A or PM-4-B, for the brake-disc mating surfaces. Have cleaning cloths and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, for the wheel pilot interface.

prepare.title: Protect yourself before handling parts and chemicals
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged components. Read the safety information for the cleaners and lubricant before use. Keep solvents away from ignition sources.

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start
steps.body: Before working around or beneath the car, disable remote start, if fitted, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup on the central display. Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle. Keep it away from anyone who might start the car. These precautions come before the lifting and brake work. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Position and raise the car securely
steps.body:
Begin on a hard, level surface with the parking brake applied and the wheels chocked. Put the transmission in Neutral for hoist positioning while maintaining the ground-wheel restraints.
Locate the triangles stamped into the body structure: they identify the lifting locations along the sides, behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels. Place the hoist adapters at the marked locations. Check that the arms and adapters clear the suspension, exhaust, steering linkage, brackets, axle and rear cover. Do not lift against either bumper.
Raise and secure the vehicle on the hoist before starting wheel removal. Keep every wheel remaining on the ground chocked. Do not use the engine to turn the drive wheels during this job. See [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631).

steps.title: Release the parking brake and remove the rear wheel
steps.body:
With all four wheels fully clear of the ground and the car securely supported on the hoist, release the parking brake for the rear brake work. Remove the five wheel nuts, then remove the wheel and tire together to expose the rear disc and caliper.
Do not use heat on a seized wheel nut; it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. If a nut cannot be removed without heat, stop and resolve that obstruction before continuing. See [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Support and move the complete caliper assembly aside
steps.body:
Identify the two bolts securing the caliper and its anchor plate—the mounting bracket—to the rear wheel carrier. Arrange the hanger or support before releasing the assembly.
Remove both bolts and discard them. Move the caliper and anchor plate aside together, supporting their full weight independently of the brake hose. Keep the connected hose and parking-brake cable unstressed; this access sequence does not require opening a hydraulic connection or disconnecting the cable.
The caliper is heavy enough without asking its hose to moonlight as a lifting strap. Keep the support in place throughout the shield work. See [Brake Disc](#/document/G1693754).

steps.title: Remove the rear brake disc
steps.body:
With the caliper assembly clear, withdraw the disc outward over the five wheel studs and off the hub. This exposes the shield behind the hub flange, the circular part carrying the wheel studs.
The illustrated access leaves the hub and its central nut in place. If the disc will not withdraw, stop rather than inventing a hammering, heating or pulling operation.

steps.title: Remove the shield’s three bolts and take the shield away
steps.body:
Note the shield’s orientation, including its open section beside the caliper location. Viewed from outside the wheel opening, its three mounting bolts sit around the hub flange: one toward the upper left and two lower down, one on each side.
Remove those three bolts and take the open-sided shield away from behind the hub flange. Keep the caliper assembly supported and avoid disturbing its hose or cable while working around it. See [Brake Disc Shield](#/document/G1693755).

steps.title: Install and tighten the shield
steps.body:
Position the replacement shield in the same orientation as the removed part, with its open section at the caliper location. Align the three mounting holes and install the three bolts.
Tighten the shield bolts to 106 lb.in (12 Nm). Check the torque tool’s units before tightening: this is a pound-inch specification.

steps.title: Clean the disc mating surfaces and refit the disc
steps.body:
Use the wire brush and Motorcraft PM-4-A or PM-4-B brake cleaner to clean the brake-disc mating surfaces where the disc seats against the hub. Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material that would prevent the disc from seating properly.
Slide the disc back over the wheel studs and seat it against the hub. Keep lubricant away from its braking faces—the surfaces squeezed by the brake pads.

steps.title: Refit the caliper assembly with new bolts
steps.body:
Bring the supported caliper-and-anchor-plate assembly back into position around the disc, keeping its hose and cable free of strain or trapping. Install two new assembly mounting bolts and tighten them to 129 lb.ft (175 Nm).
Only remove the temporary caliper support after the assembly is secured. Confirm that the support or hanger has been removed from the working area.

steps.title: Clean the wheel mounting faces and central pilot bore
steps.body:
Clean corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel’s flat mounting face and the corresponding mounting face on the brake disc or hub. Any disc-to-hub fasteners present must be secured and must not stand between the wheel and its mounting face.
Also clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the large center hole that fits over the hub’s locating shoulder—and the corresponding hub pilot. I clean the bore as well as the flat face; wiping only the broad, obvious surface leaves half the seating job unfinished.
Do not fit the wheel while debris prevents flat, full contact. Contamination at these faces can allow the wheel nuts to loosen.

steps.title: Apply anti-seize only at the locating interface
steps.body:
Apply a thin film of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, only where the wheel pilot bore meets the hub pilot.
Keep it off the flat wheel-to-disc mounting faces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and disc friction surfaces. The wheel stud and wheel nut threads must remain clean and dry for the final torque specification.

steps.title: Install the wheel with the nuts finger-tight
steps.body: Position the wheel over the studs and onto the hub pilot. Install all five wheel nuts and tighten them only finger-tight at this stage. Final tightening comes with the vehicle resting on its tires.

steps.title: Check brake operation before lowering
steps.body:
Apply the brake pedal several times to verify correct brake-system operation, as required after the disc work. If normal brake operation is not restored, do not drive the car; resolve that problem before returning it to service.
As a reassembly check, confirm that the shield has all three bolts secured and that the caliper assembly is mounted with its two new bolts. These checks confirm completion of the work; they do not diagnose an unrelated brake fault.

steps.title: Restore restraints before and during lowering
steps.body:
Reapply the parking brake before lowering the vehicle. Confirm that tools, the caliper hanger and other loose equipment are clear.
Lower the hoist in a controlled manner. As the tires reach the ground, restore the wheel chocks; keep any wheels already on the ground chocked throughout. Once the car is resting on its tires, return the transmission from Neutral to its normal parked setting. Keep the parking brake applied and chocks in place for final wheel tightening.

steps.title: Torque the wheel nuts on the ground in a star pattern
steps.body:
With the vehicle resting on its tires and the stud and nut threads clean and dry, tighten all five wheel nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) in a star/cross pattern.
For a wheel oriented with one nut at the top, the illustrated order is: top, lower left, upper right, upper left, lower right. If the wheel is rotated differently, follow the same five-point star across the wheel rather than moving around neighboring nuts.
The crossing order matters: uneven tightening can produce excessive brake-disc runout, meaning the disc turns with a sideways wobble that can contribute to brake roughness, shudder and vibration.

steps.title: Arrange the wheel-nut follow-up
steps.body: Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after reinstalling the wheel. Use the same 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) specification, clean and dry threads, star pattern and vehicle-resting-on-tires conditions. Put that reminder somewhere more dependable than the garage’s collective memory.

watchFor.title: A brake hose carrying the caliper’s weight
watchFor.body: The caliper and anchor plate must remain independently supported while aside. A hanging assembly can damage the brake hose. Reposition the support immediately if the hose becomes loaded.

watchFor.title: Pound-inches versus pound-feet
watchFor.body: Shield bolts: 106 lb.in (12 Nm). New caliper assembly bolts: 129 lb.ft (175 Nm). Wheel nuts: 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). Check the tool scale each time you change fastener groups.

watchFor.title: Reusing the discarded assembly bolts
watchFor.body: The two removed caliper-and-anchor-plate mounting bolts are not refitted. Install new bolts before tightening the assembly to 129 lb.ft (175 Nm).

watchFor.title: Lubricant spreading beyond the pilot
watchFor.body: The anti-seize film belongs only between the central wheel bore and hub pilot. Flat mounting faces, fastener threads and braking surfaces must stay free of it.

watchFor.title: Lowering with the parking brake still released
watchFor.body: Reapply the parking brake while the car is still raised. Restore chocks as the tires reach the ground, before completing the lowering and final wheel tightening.

notes: The wheel and tire come off as one assembly; tire dismounting and balancing are not part of this shield replacement.
The shield, caliper assembly and wheel each have a different fastening requirement. Finish one group deliberately before moving to the next.

diagnostics.finding: A wheel nut will not release without considering heat.
diagnostics.meaning: Wheel removal is blocked, and heating the nut risks wheel and wheel-bearing damage.
diagnostics.next: Stop the shield job and arrange a suitable non-heat fastener-removal solution.

diagnostics.finding: The caliper assembly pulls on its hose or cable when positioned aside.
diagnostics.meaning: Its position or support is unsuitable for continuing the access work.
diagnostics.next: Support the assembly’s weight and reposition it within the connections’ available movement before removing the disc or shield.

diagnostics.finding: The brake disc does not withdraw after the caliper assembly has been moved clear.
diagnostics.meaning: An access obstruction remains; the shield cannot yet be reached through the normal removal sequence.
diagnostics.next: Stop and obtain an appropriate disc-release method rather than escalating force or disturbing the central hub nut.

diagnostics.finding: Corrosion or debris keeps the wheel from contacting its mounting face fully.
diagnostics.meaning: The wheel is not ready for tightening, and clamping it over contamination can lead to loosening.
diagnostics.next: Remove the wheel and clean the mating faces and central pilot bore before refitting.

diagnostics.finding: Repeated brake-pedal applications do not restore normal brake operation.
diagnostics.meaning: The required completion check has failed.
diagnostics.next: Keep the vehicle out of service and have the brake concern investigated before driving.

verification.title: Shield and caliper fastening completed
verification.body: Confirm three shield bolts tightened to 106 lb.in (12 Nm), and two new caliper-and-anchor-plate bolts tightened to 129 lb.ft (175 Nm). Confirm the caliper support has been removed and its hose and cable are not trapped or strained.

verification.title: Clean seating and controlled lubrication
verification.body: Confirm the disc mating surfaces, wheel mounting faces and central pilot bore were cleaned. The XL-2 film must be confined to the wheel-bore/hub-pilot interface, with fastener threads and braking surfaces free of lubricant.

verification.title: Brakes and parking restraints restored
verification.body: Confirm the brake pedal was applied several times and correct brake operation verified. The parking brake must have been reapplied before lowering, with chocks restored as the tires reached the ground.

verification.title: Wheel tightened and follow-up scheduled
verification.body: Confirm all five wheel nuts were tightened on the ground in a star pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), using clean, dry threads. Retighten within 160 km (100 mi).

procedures.purpose: Rear brake disc shield removal, reverse-order installation and three-bolt tightening specification.
Rear disc access, complete caliper assembly support, replacement mounting bolts, mating-surface cleaning and brake-pedal completion check.
Wheel removal, mounting-face and pilot-bore preparation, XL-2 application limits, wheel-nut torque, star sequence and follow-up tightening.
Triangle-marked lifting locations, hoist positioning and restrictions on jack-only support and emergency-jack use.
Startup prevention, personal protection, chemical handling, lifting capacity, parking-brake use and ground-wheel restraints.

applicability.equipment: Rear disc brakes with a separate brake disc shield and a caliper-and-anchor-plate assembly.

stepGroups.title: Prevent startup and lift safely
stepGroups.summary: Disable remote start, restrain the car and establish secure raised support.

stepGroups.title: Expose the rear shield
stepGroups.summary: Remove the wheel, support the complete caliper assembly and withdraw the disc.

stepGroups.title: Replace the shield
stepGroups.summary: Remove the three shield bolts, position the replacement and tighten correctly.

stepGroups.title: Rebuild the brake and wheel mounting
stepGroups.summary: Clean the disc seating surfaces, install new caliper bolts and prepare the wheel carefully.

stepGroups.title: Verify, lower and torque
stepGroups.summary: Check brake operation, restore restraints, tighten the wheel on the ground and arrange its follow-up.

guides.title: Remove and refit a rear brake disc
guides.summary: Remove the rear wheel, support and move the caliper-and-anchor assembly aside, then remove or replace the disc. Reassemble with new mounting bolts and the correct brake and wheel tightening values.
guides.introduction: The rear brake disc gets squeezed for a living; getting it off the car should involve less drama. I’ll walk you through moving the caliper assembly out of the way, keeping its weight off the brake hose, and putting everything back with clean mounting faces and correctly tightened fasteners. This guide covers the illustrated rear brake arrangement on 2015 Mustangs with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine.
guides.why: The disc, also called the rotor, turns with the wheel. The brake pads grip its broad friction surfaces to slow the car. Its mounting faces must sit cleanly together, while the anchor plate—the bracket supporting the caliper—must be securely fastened. Supporting the assembly protects the brake hose; replacing its mounting bolts and correctly tightening the wheel finishes the mechanical work.
searchTerms: rear caliper anchor plate bolt torque

when.summary: Use this procedure when rear brake-disc removal or replacement has already been established as necessary.
notes: This is a removal and refitting job, not a diagnosis based on brake noise, vibration or appearance.
The engine applicability is 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L for the 2015 model year; the broader wheel and lifting references do not extend this article to the 5.2L.

prepare.title: Know the job’s boundary
prepare.detail: Confirm that the rear brake arrangement matches the illustrated assembly and obtain the correct replacement disc if replacing it. Disc thickness limits, runout measurements and methods for freeing a seized disc require separate service instructions; this procedure does not establish those decisions.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and caliper support
prepare.detail: Have a suitable hoist and a suitable hook or support for the caliper-and-anchor assembly. If using a service jack, support the vehicle on floor stands before working underneath; never rely on a jack alone. The vehicle’s emergency jack is for changing a deflated tire, not this repair.

prepare.title: Have replacement bolts and tightening equipment ready
prepare.detail: Obtain two new caliper-and-anchor plate mounting bolts for each assembly removed. Have suitable hand tools for the fitted fasteners and a torque wrench capable of 129 lb.ft (175 Nm) and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). Removed assembly mounting bolts must be discarded even if they look reusable.

prepare.title: Gather the cleaning and lubricating materials
prepare.detail: Have a wire brush, cleaning cloths, Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner—VOC Compliant / Motorcraft Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A or PM-4-B, and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2. The cleaner is for preparing the disc mating surfaces; the anti-seize belongs only at the wheel’s central locating interface.

steps.title: Locate the lifting points and raise the vehicle
steps.body:
Before lifting, use a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Confirm the jack or hoist is rated for the vehicle, including cargo and modifications. If using a jack, support the vehicle on suitable stands at the designated points before going underneath; a jack alone is not a support. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

With the transmission in Neutral, position the vehicle on the hoist. Find the triangles stamped into the body or frame that identify the correct lifting points. The lifting illustration shows four locations along the sides of the underbody; use the actual stamped marks to locate them on the car.
Position the hoist adapters without contacting suspension, exhaust or steering linkage components. On a two-column hoist, keep the lifting forks clear of suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, if fitted, and avoid damage to the axle or rear cover. Before driving onto a drive-on lift, check for underbody interference.
Do not lift against either bumper. If a service jack is used, support the vehicle on floor stands before getting underneath. Incorrect lifting can let the vehicle shift or fall. See [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631).

steps.title: Remove the rear wheel and tire
steps.body:
Remove the five wheel nuts, then take the wheel-and-tire assembly off the studs to expose the brake disc and caliper. Keep the nuts ready for reinstallation with their threads clean and dry.
Do not use heat to release a seized wheel nut: it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. See [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Support and move the caliper-and-anchor assembly aside
steps.body:
With all four wheels fully clear of the ground and the vehicle securely supported, release the parking brake before working on its cable or moving the rear caliper assembly. The car must remain securely supported while the parking brake is released.

Arrange the hook or other suitable support before releasing the assembly. Identify the two bolts securing the caliper-and-anchor plate assembly to its mounting; these are the two mounting fasteners highlighted behind the assembly in the illustration.
Remove both bolts and discard them. Move the caliper and anchor plate aside together, supporting their weight with the hook or support. The illustrated brake hose and parking-brake cable remain connected while the assembly is positioned aside.
Do not let the assembly hang from the brake hose or pull against its connections. Position it so the disc can come off without the assembly or its attached lines being strained. The hose carries brake fluid, not a damn caliper.

steps.title: Remove the brake disc
steps.body:
With the supported caliper-and-anchor assembly clear, draw the disc outward off the hub and over the wheel studs. The disc is the large circular component surrounding the hub; the central axle nut remains in place for this operation.
Keep the supported assembly clear while removing the disc. This is the disc-removal endpoint shown in the [Brake Disc procedure](#/document/G1693754).

steps.title: Clean the disc mating surfaces
steps.body:
Before installing the retained or replacement disc, use a wire brush and Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner—VOC Compliant / Motorcraft Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A or PM-4-B, to clean the surfaces where the disc and hub meet.
Look for corrosion, dirt or other material trapped on these mating faces. Remove it before fitting the disc so it can seat directly against its mounting surface. A layer of crud is a lousy precision spacer.

steps.title: Refit the disc and secure the brake assembly
steps.body:
Place the disc back over the wheel studs and onto its hub mounting surface. Confirm that it sits against the cleaned mating face without trapped material.
Bring the supported caliper-and-anchor assembly back into its original position around the disc. Install two new mounting bolts and tighten them to 129 lb.ft (175 Nm).
Remove the temporary support once the assembly is secured. Check that the brake hose and parking-brake cable are no longer caught by the support and are not trapped or pulled by the repositioned assembly.

steps.title: Clean the wheel mounting faces and central pilot bore
steps.body:
Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel’s mounting face and the corresponding hub or brake-disc mounting face. Clean the wheel’s central pilot bore as well—the round opening that locates the wheel on the raised center of the hub. The cleaning callout includes this bore, not just the flat back of the wheel.
If any fasteners securing the disc to the hub are present, make sure they are secure and do not interfere with the wheel seating against its mounting face. Contamination or interference here can allow the wheel nuts to loosen, potentially allowing the wheel to come off while driving.

steps.title: Apply anti-seize only at the wheel’s locating interface
steps.body:
Apply a thin film of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, only where the wheel pilot bore contacts the hub pilot. The hub pilot is the raised central locating section that fits inside the wheel’s center opening.
Keep the lubricant off the flat wheel-to-disc mounting face, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and disc friction surfaces. The clean, dry stud and nut threads are part of the wheel torque requirement; this is no place for enthusiastic extra grease.

steps.title: Install the wheel with the nuts finger tight
steps.body:
Position the wheel-and-tire assembly over the five studs and against its mounting face. Install all five wheel nuts and tighten them only finger tight at this stage.
Check that the wheel is seated against the mounting face before proceeding. Final tightening is performed with the vehicle resting on its tires.

steps.title: Lower the vehicle and torque the wheel in a star pattern
steps.body:
Before lowering, make sure the parking brake is applied. Restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground, and keep the vehicle restrained for final wheel-nut tightening. Do not lower an unrestrained vehicle in Neutral.

Lower the vehicle until it rests on its tires. With the wheel stud and wheel nut threads clean and dry, tighten the five nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) in a star/cross pattern.
Using the illustrated wheel orientation, the order is: top → lower left → upper right → upper left → lower right. Carry that crossing pattern around the wheel rather than tightening neighboring nuts in a circle.
Incorrect tightening order can produce excessive disc runout—sideways wobble as the disc turns—which accelerates brake roughness, shudder and vibration.

steps.title: Apply the brake pedal and check the completed assembly
steps.body:
Apply the brake pedal several times to verify correct brake-system operation. Do this before considering the car ready to move.
Confirm that the caliper-and-anchor assembly is secured with new bolts tightened to 129 lb.ft (175 Nm), its temporary support has been removed, and the wheel nuts have received their final 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) torque with the vehicle on its tires. These are completion checks, not a new diagnostic test. If brake operation is not correct, leave the car out of service until the fault is resolved.

steps.title: Arrange the required wheel-nut retightening
steps.body:
Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after reinstalling the wheel. Use the same star pattern and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) specification, with clean, dry threads and the vehicle resting on its tires.
Wheels can loosen after their initial tightening. Record the mileage or set a reminder before putting the tools away.

watchFor.title: An unsupported caliper assembly
watchFor.body: The brake hose must never carry the assembly’s weight. Keep the hook or support carrying it throughout disc removal and refitting.

watchFor.title: Reusing the two mounting bolts
watchFor.body: Discard both removed caliper-and-anchor plate mounting bolts. Reassembly requires new bolts tightened to 129 lb.ft (175 Nm).

watchFor.title: Anti-seize spreading beyond the pilot
watchFor.body: Only the wheel pilot bore-to-hub pilot interface receives the thin lubricant film. Keep the wheel mounting faces, studs, nuts, pads and disc friction surfaces free of it.

watchFor.title: Wheel tightening shortcuts
watchFor.body: Final torque is 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), applied in a star pattern with the vehicle resting on its tires and the stud and nut threads clean and dry. Retightening within 160 km (100 mi) is required.

notes: The caliper and anchor plate move aside as one assembly; this procedure does not call for opening the hydraulic connection.

Tire removal from the wheel and wheel balancing are not required for disc access. If separate tire work is undertaken on alloy or carbon-fiber wheels, use a center-clamp tire changer and a balancer that does not contact the wheel face. Table-top changers that grip the wheel internally and ride on its front flange can damage it.

diagnostics.finding: A wheel nut is seized.
diagnostics.meaning: Wheel removal cannot proceed normally, and heating the nut risks wheel and wheel-bearing damage.
diagnostics.next: Stop this removal path and obtain an appropriate seized-fastener removal method. Do not apply heat.

diagnostics.finding: The caliper-and-anchor assembly pulls on or hangs from the brake hose.
diagnostics.meaning: The support is not carrying the assembly correctly, creating a risk of hose damage.
diagnostics.next: Stop moving the assembly and reposition its support so the hose carries no assembly weight. Resolve any suspected hose damage before returning the car to service.

diagnostics.finding: Corrosion, dirt or foreign material remains between mounting faces.
diagnostics.meaning: The disc or wheel cannot seat directly against its intended mounting surface; contamination at the wheel mounting faces can contribute to wheel-nut loosening.
diagnostics.next: Clean the affected faces before installing the disc or wheel. Include the wheel’s central pilot bore in the cleaning.

diagnostics.finding: Brake operation is not correct after several pedal applications.
diagnostics.meaning: The final operational check has not passed; completing the fastening work alone does not make the car ready to use.
diagnostics.next: Keep the vehicle out of service and have the brake fault diagnosed and corrected before driving.

verification.title: Disc and brake assembly secured
verification.body: Confirm that the disc was installed against cleaned mating surfaces and the caliper-and-anchor assembly was fitted with two new bolts tightened to 129 lb.ft (175 Nm).

verification.title: Support removed and connections clear
verification.body: Confirm that the temporary caliper support has been removed and the brake hose and parking-brake cable are not trapped or pulled by the reassembled components.

verification.title: Wheel installation completed
verification.body: Confirm clean mounting faces, a cleaned central pilot bore, anti-seize confined to the pilot interface, and all five wheel nuts tightened in a star pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) with the vehicle resting on its tires.

verification.title: Brake operation and follow-up
verification.body: Apply the brake pedal several times and verify correct operation. Arrange wheel-nut retightening within 160 km (100 mi) of wheel reinstallation.

procedures.purpose: Rear brake-disc removal and installation, including supporting the caliper-and-anchor assembly, replacing its two mounting bolts, cleaning mating surfaces and checking brake operation.
Wheel removal and installation, pilot-bore cleaning and lubrication, wheel-nut torque and star sequence, and the required retightening interval.
Identify triangle-marked lifting points and apply vehicle-support and hoist-clearance precautions.

applicability.equipment: Rear disc brakes with the illustrated caliper-and-anchor plate assembly.

stepGroups.title: Lift the car and expose the brake
stepGroups.summary: Use the marked lifting points, then remove the rear wheel.

stepGroups.title: Support the caliper and remove the disc
stepGroups.summary: Move the complete caliper-and-anchor assembly aside without loading the hose.

stepGroups.title: Clean and rebuild the brake
stepGroups.summary: Seat the disc on clean mating faces and install new assembly mounting bolts.

stepGroups.title: Prepare and install the wheel
stepGroups.summary: Clean the wheel faces and pilot bore, confine lubricant to the pilot, and torque the nuts in a star pattern.

stepGroups.title: Check operation and arrange retightening
stepGroups.summary: Verify brake operation and complete the required wheel-nut follow-up.

guides.title: Replace the brake pads — SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Replace the pin-and-spring-retained brake pads on a 2015 5.2L Mustang with the SVT Performance Package, including safe wheel access, piston retraction, lubrication and wheel tightening.
guides.introduction: These pads have a small entourage: two retaining pins and a spring stand between you and the friction material. I’ll walk you through getting that entourage out of the way, making room with a piston retractor, and putting everything back where it belongs. This article covers the illustrated pin-and-spring caliper arrangement on the 2015 5.2L Mustang with the SVT Performance Package.
guides.why: The caliper pistons push the pads against the brake disc, turning the car’s motion into heat through friction. Retracting those pistons creates clearance for replacement pads. The pins retain the pads, while the spring keeps the assembly correctly loaded. Clean contact surfaces and correctly placed lubricant help the pads sit and move as intended; applying the brake pedal afterward returns them to their working position.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang 5.2L SVT Performance Package brake pads
brake pad retaining pins and spring

when.summary: Use this procedure when the pads in the illustrated SVT Performance Package caliper require replacement or removal for related work.
notes: The brake pad minimum thickness is 0.118 in (3 mm). Maximum taper wear—the difference in thickness across a pad in any direction—is also 0.118 in (3 mm).
These are service limits, not a diagnosis of noise, vibration or poor braking. A pad replacement alone does not establish the cause of a braking complaint.

prepare.title: Confirm the brake arrangement and the job boundary
prepare.detail: Match the caliper to the arrangement described here: two pins across its outer opening, a central pad spring, and a pad on each side of the disc. This is a pad replacement procedure; disc measurement setups, hydraulic repairs and repairs to seized pins or pistons require separate instructions. The pad limits are useful only with a reliable thickness assessment; a measurement method and datum are not established here.

prepare.title: Gather the tools and replacement materials
prepare.detail: Have a brake caliper piston retractor or suitable brake pad spreader, wheel-nut tools, a torque wrench capable of 150 lb-ft (204 Nm), appropriate lifting equipment and wheel chocks. Have cleaning brushes and cloths for the contact surfaces. For new pads, obtain the correct kit with its instruction sheet, all supplied replacement hardware and its lubricant.

prepare.title: Keep the two lubricants separate
prepare.detail: Use the pad kit’s lubricant on the pad-to-caliper contact areas according to its instruction sheet. For the wheel’s central locating interface, use Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2. These are separate applications; neither belongs on the brake friction surfaces.

prepare.title: Have the correct brake fluid available
prepare.detail: If the final reservoir check requires a top-up, use Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid, PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2. See [Brake System Specifications](#/document/G1694687).

prepare.title: Protect yourself before handling parts and chemicals
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the car, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. Read the safety information for the cleaning materials and lubricants you use. Keep solvents away from ignition sources.

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start
steps.body: Before working around or underneath the car, disable remote start, if fitted, through the central display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person starting it during service. Keep these precautions in place for the later underhood reservoir check. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Restrain the car and prepare the lifting equipment
steps.body:
Position the car on a hard, level surface. Set the parking brake and block all wheels that will remain on the ground before selecting Neutral for the wheel-removal operation.

Use a hoist with sufficient capacity for the vehicle, including cargo and modifications. If using a service jack and floor stands, both must be suitable for the load; support the raised vehicle on stands and never get underneath it while it rests only on a jack. The emergency tire-changing jack is not suitable for this service work.

steps.title: Locate the lifting points and raise the vehicle
steps.body:
Find the triangles stamped into the body or frame near the four lifting locations along the side sills, just behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels. Use these marked locations to identify the correct lifting points; do not choose a nearby panel because it looks sturdy.

With the transmission in Neutral, position the hoist adapters at the correct points and check that the arms and pads clear the suspension, exhaust, steering linkage, brackets, stabilizer mounting brackets and axle or rear cover. Never lift against either bumper. If using a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving onto it. Raise and support the car using the lifting equipment’s operating instructions. See [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631).

steps.title: Remove the wheel and expose the caliper
steps.body:
Remove the five wheel nuts, then remove the wheel and tire assembly. Do not apply heat to a seized wheel nut: it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing.

With the wheel clear, locate the caliper opening, the two pins crossing it and the spring between them. The pad operation takes place through this opening with the caliper mounted and the hydraulic connections undisturbed. See [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Remove the two retaining pins, then the spring
steps.body:
Before moving anything, note how the pins pass across the opening and how the spring sits against the pads. Withdraw both brake pad retaining pins, then remove the brake pad spring. Keep their orientation clear for reassembly, even when the new kit supplies replacements.

The pins come out before the spring. Resist the machinery’s invitation to turn this into a puzzle with all the pieces mixed together.

steps.title: Retract the pistons with the pads still in place
steps.body:
Position the brake caliper piston retractor or pad spreader in the exposed pad opening. Use it to spread the existing pads away from the disc and compress the caliper pistons back into the caliper, creating clearance for removal.

Use the retractor for this operation rather than improvising leverage against the disc. If the pistons do not retract with the appropriate tool, stop for a caliper assessment instead of escalating the force.

steps.title: Remove the pads from both sides of the disc
steps.body:
Remove the retractor and withdraw the two pads through the caliper opening, one from each side of the disc. Keep track of their original positions if they are being removed for related work rather than replaced.

The [SVT Performance Package pad procedure](#/document/G1716403) uses this direct access: pins, spring, piston retraction, then pads.

steps.title: Check whether the removed pads are eligible for reuse
steps.body:
If considering reuse, compare a reliable thickness assessment with the service limits: minimum pad thickness 0.118 in (3 mm), and maximum taper wear 0.118 in (3 mm) in any direction. A pad below the minimum or beyond the taper limit is not suitable for reuse.

Use the findings in the diagnostics section to decide what happens next. Passing these two limits alone does not explain a braking complaint or prove that every part of the brake is serviceable.

steps.title: Clean the pad-to-caliper contact areas
steps.body:
Clean the small support/contact areas at the ends of the caliper’s pad opening—the four areas where the pad edges bear against the caliper. The illustration shows a brush and wiping action at these locations. Clean the corresponding contact areas on any pads being reused.

The aim is clean seating surfaces, not a shiny caliper for its own sake. Keep removed material and cleaning products away from the pad and disc friction faces.

steps.title: Lubricate only the intended pad contact surfaces
steps.body:
Apply the lubricant supplied with the brake pad kit to the pad-to-caliper contact surfaces, following the kit’s instruction sheet. The illustration highlights the narrow contact edges at the ends of the pad, rather than its broad friction face.

When installing new pads, use all new hardware supplied with the kit as well as its lubricant. Do not substitute wheel anti-seize for the kit lubricant, and do not coat the friction material or disc.

steps.title: Install the pads, spring and retaining pins
steps.body:
Reverse the removal sequence: insert the pads into their working positions on either side of the disc, position the brake pad spring in its original orientation, then reinstall the two retaining pins through their original paths to retain the assembly. Use the kit’s new hardware wherever supplied.

Before moving on, visually confirm that both pads occupy their intended positions, the spring is correctly positioned, and both pins are fully installed through the retaining arrangement. If the assembly will not return to its observed configuration, resolve that before fitting the wheel.

steps.title: Clean the wheel mounting faces and central bore
steps.body:
Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel mounting face and the matching mounting face on the hub or brake disc. Check that any fasteners securing the disc to the hub are secure and do not project into or interfere with the wheel’s seating surfaces.

Also clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the circular hole that locates over the hub’s raised center. The bore needs cleaning as well as the flat mounting face. Contamination trapped between mounting faces can let the wheel nuts loosen after installation.

steps.title: Apply the wheel pilot anti-seize and refit the wheel
steps.body:
Apply only a thin film of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 at the interface between the wheel pilot bore and the hub pilot.

Keep it off the flat wheel-to-disc mounting faces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and disc friction surfaces. The wheel stud and nut threads must remain clean and dry for the specified torque.

Position the wheel on the hub and install all five wheel nuts finger tight at this stage.

steps.title: Restore parking restraint before and during lowering
steps.body:
Before beginning to lower the car, confirm that the parking brake is applied; restore it now if it was released during raised service. Keep the transmission and lifting operation under control.

As the tires reach the ground, restore wheel chocks at the ground wheels before completing the lowering operation. Leave the car restrained while it settles fully onto its tires and while you perform final wheel-nut tightening.

steps.title: Tighten the wheel nuts on the ground in a star pattern
steps.body:
With the vehicle resting on its tires, tighten the five wheel nuts to 150 lb-ft (204 Nm), using clean, dry stud and nut threads.

Follow a star/cross sequence. With one nut treated as the top position, tighten: top, lower-left, upper-right, upper-left, lower-right. Cross the wheel between successive nuts rather than tightening adjacent nuts around the circle. This helps avoid brake disc runout—side-to-side disc movement that can contribute to shudder and vibration.

steps.title: Apply the brake pedal and check the reservoir
steps.body:
After assembly, depress the brake pedal to return the pads and pistons to their working relationship.

Before working under the hood, keep the ignition off and the key removed. With the ignition off, inspect the cooling fans for damage, cracks or separation; do not continue underhood work with a damaged fan. Fans can run with the ignition off, so they must be disabled before any work close to them.

Check the brake fluid reservoir level and top up only as necessary with Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2. Refit the reservoir cap after the check.

steps.title: Finish the installation and plan the wheel-nut recheck
steps.body:
Account for the tools and removed parts. Confirm that the pads, spring, pins and wheel are installed, the pedal has been depressed, and the reservoir check is complete. Keep the vehicle parked and restrained if the pedal response is abnormal or any assembly detail remains unresolved.

Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after reinstalling the wheel. Add that reminder now; a wheel-nut recheck is a much better souvenir than a loose wheel.

watchFor.title: Pad lubricant and wheel anti-seize have different jobs
watchFor.body: Use the kit lubricant at the pad contact areas and XL-2 only at the wheel pilot interface. Keep both away from the brake friction faces, and keep wheel fastener threads clean and dry.

watchFor.title: New pads require the kit’s new hardware
watchFor.body: Install all replacement hardware supplied with the pad kit. Do not carry an old spring or pin into the installation simply because it is already on the bench.

watchFor.title: The mounting faces must seat directly together
watchFor.body: Clean both wheel and hub/disc mounting faces, and check for interfering disc-retaining fasteners. Material trapped between the faces can cause wheel-nut loosening.

watchFor.title: An abnormal pedal is an unfinished job
watchFor.body: Pedal application after assembly is a completion action, not proof that an unexplained hydraulic problem has been repaired. Keep the car stationary if the pedal response is abnormal.

notes: This article applies to the 2015 5.2L Mustang with the SVT Performance Package. Shared wheel and lifting instructions do not extend the pad procedure to other engines or brake configurations.

Tire removal from the wheel and balancing are unnecessary for pad access. If separate tire work is undertaken on carbon fiber or alloy wheels, use a center-clamp tire changer and a balancer that does not contact the wheel face. Tabletop changers that grip inside the wheel and ride on the front flange can damage it.

diagnostics.finding: A reliable pad thickness assessment is below 0.118 in (3 mm).
diagnostics.meaning: The pad is below the minimum service thickness.
diagnostics.next: Replace the pads using the correct kit and its supplied hardware and lubrication instructions.

diagnostics.finding: Pad taper exceeds 0.118 in (3 mm) in any direction.
diagnostics.meaning: The difference in thickness across the pad exceeds the permitted taper wear.
diagnostics.next: Do not reuse the affected pad. Arrange an assessment of the uneven wear before considering the brake service complete; these limits alone do not identify its cause.

diagnostics.finding: Pads remain within both stated wear limits, but a braking complaint exists.
diagnostics.meaning: Those two limits do not establish the cause of the complaint or validate the rest of the brake.
diagnostics.next: Obtain a diagnosis appropriate to the complaint rather than treating pad replacement as a proven cure.

diagnostics.finding: A retaining pin will not withdraw or the pistons will not retract with the appropriate tool.
diagnostics.meaning: Routine pad replacement cannot proceed as described.
diagnostics.next: Stop and obtain the matching caliper assessment or repair instructions. Do not invent a heat, hammering or extra-force remedy.

diagnostics.finding: Corrosion, debris or a projecting fastener prevents the wheel from seating against its mounting face.
diagnostics.meaning: The wheel cannot clamp correctly against the hub/disc.
diagnostics.next: Clean the mounting surfaces and resolve the interference before installing and tightening the wheel.

diagnostics.finding: The pedal response is abnormal after reassembly.
diagnostics.meaning: The completion check has not been satisfied; the cause is not established by this pad procedure.
diagnostics.next: Keep the car stationary and restrained, and obtain the appropriate brake diagnosis before driving.

verification.title: Pad retention is complete
verification.body: Both pads are in position on opposite sides of the disc, the spring is correctly oriented, and both retaining pins are fully installed. All new hardware supplied with a new-pad kit has been used.

verification.title: Wheel installation is complete
verification.body: The mounting faces and central pilot bore were cleaned, XL-2 was confined to the pilot interface, and the wheel nuts were tightened on clean, dry threads to 150 lb-ft (204 Nm) in a star pattern with the car resting on its tires.

verification.title: Parking restraint was restored at the correct time
verification.body: The parking brake was applied before lowering began, and wheel chocks were restored as the tires reached the ground. The car remains restrained until the work and final checks are complete.

verification.title: Pedal and fluid checks are complete
verification.body: The brake pedal has been depressed after assembly, the reservoir level checked and corrected if necessary with PM-20 fluid meeting WSS-M6C65-A2, and the reservoir cap refitted. An abnormal pedal response requires further work before driving.

verification.title: The wheel-nut recheck is scheduled
verification.body: Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) of wheel reinstallation.

procedures.purpose: Primary SVT Performance Package pad removal and installation: retaining pins, spring, piston retraction, contact-surface cleaning, kit hardware and lubrication, and final pedal application.
Wheel removal and refitting, mounting-face and pilot-bore preparation, XL-2 application, wheel-nut torque and star sequence, and the required recheck.
Brake fluid identification and the pad minimum-thickness and maximum-taper limits.
Identify triangle-marked lifting points, arrange safe support and prevent damage from incorrect lifting-equipment placement.
Apply relevant startup prevention, personal protection, chemical handling, parking, chocking, lifting and underhood fan precautions.

stepGroups.summary: Prevent starting, arrange lifting and restraint, and remove the wheel.

stepGroups.title: Release the retainers and remove the pads
stepGroups.summary: Remove the pins and spring, retract the pistons and assess pad reuse limits.

stepGroups.title: Prepare the contacts and install the pads
stepGroups.summary: Clean and lubricate the intended surfaces, then restore the pads and retaining hardware.

stepGroups.summary: Prepare the wheel interface, restore restraints and apply the final wheel-nut torque.

guides.title: Replace the rear brake pads
guides.summary: Replace the rear pads on a 2015 Mustang with a 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine, correctly retract the parking-brake caliper piston, and refit the wheels with the specified torque.
guides.introduction: Rear brake pads have a small backstage complication: the parking brake also has opinions. The pads squeeze both sides of the brake disc to slow the wheel, while a mechanism inside the rear caliper lets the parking brake apply the same assembly. I’ll walk you through getting the caliper out of the way, replacing the pads and lining everything up again—without turning piston retraction into a garage arm-wrestling championship.
guides.why: New pads need more room than worn ones, so the caliper piston must retract into its housing. On this rear caliper, moderate to heavy pressure toward the piston engages the internal parking-brake clutch cone, a coupling that allows retraction. During refitting, the notch in the piston must meet the locating pin on the inner pad. Supporting the caliper, making that alignment and tightening the fasteners correctly are essential parts of the job.
searchTerms: rear brake piston notch and pad pin

when.summary: Use this procedure when replacing or removing the pads on the illustrated rear brake assembly.
notes: Retracting the piston is conditional on installing new pads.
The brake-pad minimum thickness is 0.118 in (3 mm); maximum taper wear in any direction is 0.118 in (3 mm). These are service limits, not a diagnosis of why a pad wore.
This procedure applies to the rear caliper shown. It does not provide front-pad replacement instructions or extend to the 5.2L application.

prepare.title: Confirm the assembly and the job boundary
prepare.detail: Match the rear assembly to the illustrated arrangement: two caliper attachment bolts, a parking-brake cable and lever, and pads retained in clips above and below the disc. Have pads matched to this application. For a different caliper, obtain its matching procedure. The wear figures below require a separate, verified measurement method; pad/disc measuring techniques and the installed-disc runout test are not covered here. Use the operating instructions for your particular piston retractor rather than assuming a universal turning direction.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and caliper support
prepare.detail: Have a hoist rated for the vehicle’s weight, including cargo and modifications, wheel chocks and an independent caliper support or suitable support hook. Locate the triangle-stamped lifting points before raising the car. The emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this service. If a workshop jack is used during positioning, support the vehicle on suitable stands before working; never get underneath a vehicle held only by a jack.

prepare.title: Gather the working equipment
prepare.detail: Have a brake caliper piston retractor, suitable tools for the wheel nuts and two caliper bolts, and torque equipment capable of 24 lb.ft (32 Nm) and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). Have cleaning materials for the wheel mounting surfaces and central pilot bore. Keep track of the two pad-support clips and their installed orientation.

prepare.title: Have the correct fluids and lubricant
prepare.detail: Use Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, only at the wheel pilot interface. For any brake-fluid top-up, use Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid, PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2. Read the material safety information before use and keep any flammable cleaning solvents away from ignition sources.

prepare.title: Protect yourself and prevent an unexpected start
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. Disable remote start, if fitted, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around or beneath the car. Switch the ignition off and remove the key. Before underhood work, inspect the cooling fans with the ignition off; a cracked, damaged or separating fan must be replaced before proceeding. Fans can run with the ignition off, so disable them before working nearby.

steps.title: Restrain the car before positioning the lift
steps.body: Work on a hard, level surface. Complete the startup-prevention actions above, apply the parking brake and chock every wheel that will remain on the ground. Confirm that the lifting equipment has adequate capacity. Follow the relevant precautions in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Position the hoist at the marked lifting points
steps.body:
Locate the stamped triangles in the body structure along both sides of the car: the illustrated lifting locations are behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels. Position the hoist adapters at the corresponding lifting points, following [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631).

Check that the arms and adapters clear the suspension, exhaust, steering linkage, mounting brackets, stabilizer brackets and rear axle cover. Do not lift against either bumper. If using a drive-on lift for positioning, check underbody clearance before driving onto it.

steps.title: Select Neutral, raise and secure the vehicle
steps.body:
With the parking brake applied and ground wheels chocked, select Neutral as directed by the [wheel procedure](#/document/G1686507). Raise the vehicle and secure it on the hoist’s supports before beginning brake work. Keep any wheels still on the ground chocked.

Release the parking brake only after all four wheels are fully clear of the ground and the raised vehicle is securely supported on the hoist, before removing the rear caliper. Do not use the engine to turn the drive wheels during this job.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and tire
steps.body: Remove the five wheel nuts, then lift the wheel and tire away to expose the rear brake disc and caliper. Do not use heat on a seized wheel nut; it can damage both the wheel and wheel bearing. If a nut cannot be removed without heat, resolve that fastening problem before continuing.

steps.title: Remove the two caliper bolts and support the caliper
steps.body:
Following the [rear brake-pad procedure](#/document/G1693756), remove the two bolts at the upper and lower ends of the caliper where it attaches to the sliding supports. Move the caliper aside enough to uncover the pads.

Support the caliper independently using a suitable hook or support at its body. Leave the brake hose and parking-brake cable connected, positioning the assembly without pulling on either. Do not let the caliper hang from the brake hose; its weight can damage the hose.

steps.title: Lift out the inner and outer pads
steps.body: Remove the pad on each side of the brake disc from the carrier, the fixed support that remains beside the disc. Note which pad sits toward the hub and driveshaft: this is the inboard pad. Identify its locating pin and the matching notch in the caliper piston so you can check their relationship during refitting.

steps.title: Remove the two pad-support clips
steps.body: Remove the clips from the upper and lower pad-contact areas of the carrier. Note how each clip wraps around its support and where the pad ends sit. The clips come out after the pads and go back before them; keeping their orientation straight saves a surprisingly annoying little puzzle.

steps.title: Retract the piston if installing new pads
steps.body:
Keep the caliper supported and use the brake caliper piston retractor to retract the piston into its bore. Engage and operate the retractor according to its instructions while applying moderate to heavy force toward the piston.

That inward force engages the internal parking-brake clutch cone. Without enough force, the mechanism will not engage and the piston will not compress. If it does not retract, check the tool engagement and inward loading before concluding that the caliper has failed. Stop if correct tool operation still does not retract it; do not substitute an improvised forcing method.

If reinstalling the existing pads, this procedure does not call for piston retraction.

steps.title: Refit the clips, then install the pads
steps.body: Refit the upper and lower support clips in their original positions and orientation. Install the inner and outer pads into the carrier on their respective sides of the disc, with their ends seated in the clips. Confirm that the inboard pad’s locating pin faces the piston.

steps.title: Align the piston notch and secure the caliper
steps.body:
Before placing the caliper over the pads, align the notch in the piston with the locating pin on the inboard pad. Check that the pin actually enters the notch as the caliper comes into position. If the caliper will not sit correctly, lift it back and correct the alignment; do not use the bolts to pull a misaligned assembly together.

Install both caliper attachment bolts and tighten each to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm). Remove the temporary caliper support after the caliper is secured. Confirm that the hose and parking-brake cable are not trapped or pulled by the refitted assembly.

steps.title: Depress the brake pedal and check the fluid
steps.body:
With the pads and caliper installed, depress the brake pedal. Then check the brake-fluid reservoir under the hood, observing the startup and cooling-fan precautions in preparation.

Top up as necessary with Motorcraft DOT 4 LV High Performance Motor Vehicle Brake Fluid, PM-20, meeting WSS-M6C65-A2, as listed in [Brake System Specifications](#/document/G1694687). This pad replacement does not require opening the brake hose or bleeder screw.

steps.title: Clean the wheel mounting faces and central bore
steps.body:
Before refitting the wheel, remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel’s flat mounting face and the corresponding mounting surface at the hub and brake disc. Check that any rotor-to-hub retaining fasteners are secured and do not obstruct those mating faces.

Also clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the round opening that fits over the hub’s raised locating section. Clean this bore before applying lubricant. Dirt between the flat faces can prevent proper seating and allow the wheel nuts to loosen.

steps.title: Lubricate only the pilot interface and fit the wheel
steps.body:
Apply a thin film of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2, only where the wheel pilot bore meets the hub pilot.

Keep it off the flat wheel-to-disc mounting faces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and disc friction surfaces. The wheel-stud and nut threads must be clean and dry for the specified torque.

Position the wheel on the hub and install all five nuts finger tight only at this stage.

steps.title: Restore the parking brake before lowering
steps.body:
With the rear brake assemblies complete and the wheels installed, apply the parking brake before beginning to lower the vehicle. Lower under control. As the tires reach the ground, restore wheel chocks at the ground wheels before removing the lifting support completely. Retain any chocks already protecting wheels that stayed on the ground.

Complete the lowering so the vehicle rests on its tires before final wheel-nut tightening.

steps.title: Torque the five wheel nuts in a star pattern
steps.body:
With the vehicle resting on its tires, the parking brake applied and ground-wheel restraints in place, tighten the wheel nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) in a star/cross pattern.

With one nut positioned at the top, the illustrated sequence is: top, lower left, upper right, upper left, lower right. Follow the same crossing relationship if the wheel is rotated. Tightening around the circle can introduce disc runout—side-to-side wobble—which contributes to brake roughness, shudder and vibration.

steps.title: Finish with an assembly check and wheel-nut reminder
steps.body:
Confirm that both clips and both pads are installed, the inboard pin is aligned with the piston notch, both caliper bolts have been torqued and all five wheel nuts have received their final torque. Confirm that the brake pedal was depressed and the reservoir level checked. Remove tools and temporary supports before releasing the vehicle from service.

If the pedal does not establish normal braking resistance or any assembly check remains unresolved, keep the vehicle stationary and resolve the problem before driving. This is a completion check, not a hydraulic diagnostic procedure.

Arrange to retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) of wheel reinstallation. Put that reminder somewhere more dependable than garage optimism.

watchFor.title: The caliper’s weight reaching the brake hose
watchFor.body: Stop moving the caliper and adjust its independent support. The flexible hose must not carry the assembly’s weight.

watchFor.title: A piston that resists retraction
watchFor.body: The internal parking-brake mechanism needs moderate to heavy inward loading to engage during retraction. Resistance alone does not prove caliper failure; check the retractor setup before making a parts decision.

watchFor.title: The inboard pad pin missing the piston notch
watchFor.body: Correct the alignment before securing the caliper. Do not force the assembly together with the attachment bolts.

watchFor.title: Anti-seize spreading beyond the pilot
watchFor.body: Keep lubricant confined to the central locating interface. Flat wheel mounting faces, wheel-stud and nut threads, pads and disc friction surfaces must remain free of it.

watchFor.title: Lowering while the parking brake remains released
watchFor.body: Apply the parking brake before lowering. Restore ground-wheel chocks as the tires reach the ground, before completely removing lifting support.

notes: The 24 lb.ft (32 Nm) value applies to the two caliper attachment bolts removed in this procedure. The wheel nuts require 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) on clean, dry threads.

Removing the wheel and tire as an assembly does not require tire-changing or balancing equipment. If separate tire work is commissioned for alloy or carbon-fiber wheels, use a center-clamp tire changer and a balancer that does not contact the wheel face. Table-top changers that grip inside the wheel and bear on its front flange can damage it.

The rear-disc reference limits are 0.390 in (9.9 mm) minimum for a solid disc and 0.925 in (23.5 mm) minimum for a vented disc. The maximum installed brake-disc runout is 0.002 in (0.05 mm). Match the disc type before using a thickness limit; a vented disc has internal passages between its friction faces.

diagnostics.finding: The fitted rear caliper does not match the illustrated two-bolt, cable-operated arrangement.
diagnostics.meaning: These access, retraction and fastening instructions do not establish the procedure for that configuration.
diagnostics.next: Obtain the matching brake-pad procedure before loosening the caliper. Do not borrow these instructions for a front caliper or another rear-brake design.

diagnostics.finding: The piston does not retract while using the piston retractor.
diagnostics.meaning: Insufficient force toward the piston can prevent the internal parking-brake clutch cone from engaging. This finding alone does not establish a failed caliper.
diagnostics.next: Verify the retractor’s engagement and operation, then apply the specified moderate to heavy inward force. If the piston still will not retract, stop and obtain further assessment before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: The inboard pad’s pin does not meet the piston notch, or the caliper does not sit correctly over the pads.
diagnostics.meaning: The required assembly alignment has not been achieved.
diagnostics.next: Reposition the caliper, correct the piston-notch alignment and check the pad and clip seating before installing and torquing the bolts.

diagnostics.finding: A verified pad-thickness measurement is below 0.118 in (3 mm).
diagnostics.meaning: The pad is below the minimum thickness listed in [Brake System Specifications](#/document/G1694687).
diagnostics.next: Replace the pads matched to this rear assembly. The thickness result does not establish the cause of wear.

diagnostics.finding: Verified pad taper wear exceeds 0.118 in (3 mm) in any direction.
diagnostics.meaning: The pad exceeds the maximum taper-wear limit; taper means the pad thickness differs across its surface.
diagnostics.next: Do not approve that pad for reuse. Arrange assessment of the uneven wear rather than assuming that replacing pads explains or corrects its cause.

diagnostics.finding: A verified rear-disc thickness is below the limit for its disc type, or verified installed runout exceeds 0.002 in (0.05 mm).
diagnostics.meaning: The disc is outside the applicable reference limit: 0.390 in (9.9 mm) minimum for solid discs or 0.925 in (23.5 mm) minimum for vented discs.
diagnostics.next: Pause the pad-only repair and arrange the appropriate disc inspection and repair. Use [Brake System Specifications](#/document/G1694687) for the matching limit.

diagnostics.finding: The brake pedal does not establish normal braking resistance after reassembly.
diagnostics.meaning: The brake-service completion check has not passed; this observation does not identify a particular hydraulic fault.
diagnostics.next: Keep the vehicle stationary and obtain brake-system assessment before driving.

verification.title: Pad and caliper assembly
verification.body: Both support clips and pads are seated, the inboard pad pin engages the piston notch, and both caliper attachment bolts are tightened to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm). The caliper support is removed and neither hose nor parking-brake cable is trapped or tensioned.

verification.title: Pedal and fluid completion
verification.body: The brake pedal has been depressed and normal braking resistance established. The reservoir level has been checked, with any necessary top-up using PM-20 DOT 4 LV fluid meeting WSS-M6C65-A2.

verification.title: Wheel seating and fastening
verification.body: The flat mounting faces and central pilot bore were cleaned. XL-2 is confined to a thin film at the pilot interface. All five nuts were tightened in a star pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), with clean, dry threads and the vehicle resting on its tires.

verification.title: Restraints and follow-up
verification.body: The parking brake was restored before lowering and ground-wheel chocks restored as the tires reached the ground. Wheel-nut retightening is scheduled within 160 km (100 mi).
