guides.title: Replace the rear brake flexible hose with the SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Replace the rear caliper's flexible hydraulic hose, renew its sealing washers and complete brake-system pressure bleeding.
guides.introduction: The rear flexible brake hose carries hydraulic pressure between the fixed brake tube and the caliper while accommodating movement at the wheel. Brackets support its route, and sealing washers close the connection around the caliper flow bolt. This job replaces the hose on the 5.2L vehicle with the SVT Performance Package.
guides.why: Opening a brake connection introduces a path for contamination and air. Sealing disconnected openings protects the hydraulic system, while new washers restore the caliper connection's seal. The bracket locations and individual tightening specifications also matter: the hose must be supported correctly, and each connection needs its own specified clamping force. Pressure bleeding is a required final phase.
searchTerms: SVT Performance Package rear brake hose

when.summary: When inspection or diagnosis has established that the rear flexible brake hose requires replacement.
notes: Arrange for pressure bleeding before opening the hydraulic system.

prepare.title: Provide safe underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the specified lifting points. Locate their stamped triangle markings and position adapters clear of suspension parts, brackets, the axle and rear cover. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare for hydraulic work
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools, torque control, clean means of sealing every opening and new caliper connection washers. Pressure-bleeding equipment and the Brake System Pressure Bleeding procedure are needed to finish the job.

prepare.title: Protect painted surfaces
prepare.detail: If brake fluid reaches paintwork, immediately wash the affected area with cold water.

steps.title: Position the vehicle on the hoist
steps.body: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, raise it using the [jacking and lifting instructions](#/document/G1663631). Check adapter clearance before lifting so access does not damage nearby components.

steps.title: Disconnect the hydraulic connections
steps.body: Following the [SVT hose procedure](#/document/G1716404), remove the caliper flow bolt and disconnect the hose. Discard the washers. Disconnect the brake tube fitting and keep all exposed openings sealed.

steps.title: Release the hose supports
steps.body: Remove the upper hose bracket bolt, then the lower bracket bolt and hose. Identify the bracket positions so the replacement follows the illustrated installation route.

steps.title: Install the replacement in reverse order
steps.body: Refit the lower and upper brackets, reconnect the brake tube, then reconnect the hose at the caliper using new washers. Tighten the lower bracket bolt to 30 Nm, upper bracket bolt to 25 Nm, tube fitting to 17.5 Nm and caliper flow bolt to 48 Nm.

steps.title: Pressure-bleed the brake system
steps.body: After installation, complete Brake System Pressure Bleeding in section 206-00. Use that procedure for the bleeding method and its requirements; reconnecting the hose alone does not complete the hydraulic work.

watchFor.title: Unsealed openings
watchFor.body: Keep openings sealed throughout the disconnected phase to prevent contamination entering the brake system.

watchFor.title: Different bracket settings
watchFor.body: The upper and lower hose bracket bolts have different tightening specifications. Keep their locations identified during reassembly.

notes: The illustration identifies the caliper flow-bolt connection and the washers that must be discarded.

verification.title: Confirm complete reassembly
verification.body: Check that both brackets and both hydraulic connections are installed, the caliper washers were renewed and each fastener received its specified torque.

verification.title: Record completion of bleeding
verification.body: Record washer renewal and completion of the prescribed pressure-bleeding procedure before closing the job.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L SVT Performance Package rear brake hose removal, installation, washer renewal and required bleeding phase.
Lifting-point identification and hoist-positioning precautions.

guides.title: Adjust the SVT Performance Package parking brake cable
guides.summary: Set cable tension so both rear wheels resist rotation at the first parking-brake position and spin freely when released.
guides.introduction: The parking-brake cables transmit movement from the hand lever to the rear brake mechanisms. Their adjustment establishes how much braking action develops as the lever moves. For this 5.2L SVT Performance Package procedure, the setting is checked at the first click, followed by a released-brake check with the rear suspension hanging freely.
guides.why: Too much cable tension can leave the rear brakes dragging after the lever is released. Tightening until a wheel locks also overshoots the specified setting. Checking wheel rotation repeatedly lets you stop when resistance appears, then confirm that releasing the lever removes that resistance from both sides.
searchTerms: rear wheels drag with parking brake released

when.summary: When parking-brake cable adjustment is required on a 5.2L vehicle with the SVT Performance Package.
notes: Complete both the first-click resistance check and the fully released free-rotation check.

prepare.title: Provide suitable lifting access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the lifting points identified by stamped triangles. Position adapters clear of suspension, exhaust, steering and mounting components; check underbody clearance where applicable.

prepare.title: Arrange access to the adjuster and wheels
prepare.detail: Have suitable access to the cable adjustment nut and both rear wheels so rotation can be checked frequently during adjustment.

steps.title: Position the vehicle
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on the hoist using the Jacking and Lifting procedure.

steps.title: Establish the lever position
steps.body: Set the parking brake to its first click or position. This is the specified reference position for adjusting cable tension.

steps.title: Adjust while checking both wheels
steps.body: Raise the vehicle and tighten the cable adjustment nut, checking rear-wheel rotation often. Stop when both wheels have resistance and no longer spin freely. Neither wheel may be locked.

steps.title: Confirm full release
steps.body: Lower the vehicle as needed while keeping the wheels off the ground and the suspension in full rebound. Release the parking brake and confirm that both rear wheels spin freely.

watchFor.title: Overtightening
watchFor.body: A locked wheel at the first click is beyond the required setting. Check rotation throughout adjustment.

watchFor.title: Unsafe support
watchFor.body: Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. The vehicle's emergency tire-change jack is unsuitable for this work, and bumpers must not be used as lifting points.

notes: Keep both rear wheels off the ground for the released-brake check; full rebound means the suspension is hanging rather than carrying vehicle weight.

diagnostics.finding: A rear wheel locks at the first lever position.
diagnostics.meaning: The required resistance-without-locking condition has not been met.
diagnostics.next: Correct the adjustment and repeat the checks on both wheels.

diagnostics.finding: Either wheel fails to spin freely with the parking brake released.
diagnostics.meaning: The final release check has failed.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the remaining resistance before accepting the adjustment.

verification.title: Record both operating states
verification.body: Record that each rear wheel has resistance without locking at the first click and spins freely with the lever released at full rebound.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L SVT Performance Package parking-brake cable adjustment and wheel-rotation acceptance checks.
Correct lifting points, support precautions and hoist-clearance requirements.

guides.title: Adjust the parking brake shoes with the SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Remove the rear brake disc, measure its internal drum, and set the parking brake shoes to a diameter 0.59 mm (0.023 in) smaller before reassembling.
guides.introduction: Your rear brake disc has a little drum-brake side hustle hiding inside it. The parking brake shoes press outward against that internal drum to hold the car when parked. I’ll walk you through uncovering them, measuring the actual drum and setting the shoes to match. This is a job for a gauge, not the traditional garage measuring instrument known as “that’ll probably do.”
guides.why: The shoes need a defined resting clearance inside the drum. Measuring the disc’s internal diameter gives you the target for its matching shoe assembly: the widest shoe diameter must be 0.59 mm (0.023 in) smaller. That figure is the difference between two diameters, not a gap to set separately at each shoe.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang 5.2L SVT Performance Package parking brake shoe adjustment

when.summary: For parking brake shoe clearance adjustment on a 2015 Mustang with the 5.2L engine and SVT Performance Package.
notes: Use this procedure when shoe clearance adjustment is required; it does not establish the cause of a parking brake complaint.
Keep each removed rear disc and its recorded drum measurement associated with the shoe assembly it came from.

prepare.title: Know the working boundary
prepare.detail: This procedure sets shoe diameter and covers the access and reassembly needed to do it. It does not provide shoe or drum wear limits, cable diagnosis, a seized-adjuster repair, or a parking brake holding-performance test. If damaged parts or an adjuster that will not move prevent the dimensional setting, resolve that repair before continuing.

prepare.title: Gather measuring and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have a caliper gauge capable of measuring the drum’s inside diameter and the shoes’ widest outside diameter, a way to record both readings, a screwdriver for the shoe adjuster, suitable fastener tools, and a torque wrench capable of 81 lb.ft (110 Nm) and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). Arrange a support hook for the caliper so its hose never carries its weight.

prepare.title: Have new bolts and the specified materials ready
prepare.detail: Obtain two new caliper mounting-bracket bolts for each rear disc removed; the removed bolts must be discarded. Have a wire brush, Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner – VOC Compliant / Motorcraft Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A or PM-4-B, and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2.

prepare.title: Arrange suitable lifting and personal protection
prepare.detail: Use a hoist rated for the vehicle’s actual weight, including cargo and modifications, and have wheel chocks ready. Wear eye and ear protection, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. Read the materials’ safety information and keep solvents away from ignition sources. The vehicle’s emergency tire-changing jack is not suitable for this service.

steps.title: Restrain the car and prevent an unexpected start
steps.body: Begin on a hard, level surface. Apply the parking brake and chock the wheels to prevent movement. Before service, disable remote start if fitted through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup on the central display. With the car restrained, select Neutral for lifting, switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person starting it. Keep the parking brake applied until the car is securely supported and you are ready to disconnect its cable. See [relevant service precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Lift at the marked points, then release the parking brake
steps.body:
Locate the stamped triangles in the body structure identifying the lifting points: the illustrated locations are along the sides, behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels. Position the hoist adapters at those designated points and check that the arms clear the suspension, steering and exhaust parts, mounting brackets, axle and rear cover. Never lift against a bumper.

Raise the car and engage the hoist’s supporting locks before working around the brakes. With all four wheels fully clear of the ground and the car securely supported on the hoist, release the parking brake for cable disconnection and shoe adjustment. Keep any wheels remaining on the ground chocked. Do not run the engine to turn the wheels. See [jacking and lifting points](#/document/G1663631).

steps.title: Remove the rear wheel
steps.body: Remove the five wheel nuts and lift the wheel off the hub. Do not use heat on a seized wheel nut: it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. Put the wheel where its mounting surfaces will stay clean and protected. The [wheel and tire procedure](#/document/G1686507) also covers its refitting requirements, which are included below.

steps.title: Disconnect the cable end from the shoe actuation lever
steps.body: At the back of the rear brake assembly, find the parking brake cable end beside its exposed coil spring. Disconnect that end from the parking brake shoe actuation lever—the lever the cable pulls to operate the shoes. Keep track of how the end engages the lever so you can restore the same connection.

steps.title: Release the cable casing from its bracket
steps.body: Follow the cable casing to the bracket it passes through. Press its three retaining tabs inward and withdraw the cable fitting from the bracket. This releases the casing attachment as well as the cable end disconnected in the previous step. Leave the hydraulic brake hose connected.

steps.title: Remove the mounting bracket and support the caliper
steps.body:
Arrange a support hook for the caliper. Remove the two bolts securing the caliper mounting bracket and discard them; these are the bracket attachment bolts, not an instruction to dismantle the caliper.

Remove the bracket and position the caliper aside with its weight carried by the support. Do not let it hang from the brake hose. Check that the hose is not being pulled as you make room for the disc. These access actions come from the [SVT Performance Package brake-disc procedure](#/document/G1716401).

steps.title: Remove the rear brake disc
steps.body: Withdraw the disc from the hub and wheel studs. Its removal exposes the curved parking brake shoes around the hub and the drum surface inside the disc’s central section. Keep this disc identified with this side of the car; its internal diameter will determine this shoe setting.

steps.title: Measure and record the drum’s inside diameter
steps.body:
Turn the removed disc so you can reach its internal cylindrical drum surface. Using the caliper gauge, measure across that surface through the center to obtain the inside diameter, or ID. Measure the drum that surrounds the parking brake shoes, rather than the disc’s broad outer braking ring or its small central hub opening.

Record the diameter and the side of the car. I keep that number beside me for the rest of the adjustment; memory has enough jobs already.

steps.title: Measure the shoes and calculate the target
steps.body:
Use the caliper gauge across the outer lining surfaces of the opposed shoes at their widest diameter. Keep the measurement across the full shoe assembly rather than taking an off-center chord.

Calculate the target using one unit system throughout:
Target shoe diameter = recorded drum ID − 0.59 mm.
Or, using inches: target shoe diameter = recorded drum ID − 0.023 in.

The specified allowance applies to the diameter as a whole. Do not subtract it from each side.

steps.title: Remove the backing plate access plug
steps.body: Find the small removable plug in the rear face of the backing plate, the fixed metal plate behind the shoes. The illustrated plug sits low on that plate, beside the suspension upright. Remove it to open the adjuster access hole.

steps.title: Turn the adjuster and remeasure
steps.body:
Use the screwdriver through the backing plate opening to rotate the toothed shoe adjuster. With the disc removed, you can identify the adjuster beside the vertical shoe spring.

Make a small adjustment, then remeasure the shoes at their widest outside diameter. Use the measured change to establish whether that direction is moving toward your target; reverse direction if it moves away. Continue until the shoes measure 0.59 mm (0.023 in) less than this disc’s recorded drum ID. There is no substitute click count here—the gauge gets the final vote.

Record the final shoe diameter beside the drum measurement. See the [parking brake shoe adjustment procedure](#/document/G1717972).

steps.title: Refit the backing plate plug
steps.body: Reinstall the access plug in the backing plate and check that it is seated in the opening. Do this now, while access is clear, before the disc and caliper go back.

steps.title: Clean the disc mating surfaces and reinstall it
steps.body:
Use the wire brush and Motorcraft PM-4-A or PM-4-B brake parts cleaner to clean the brake disc mating surfaces—the contact surfaces where the disc seats against the hub. Remove dirt, corrosion and foreign material that would prevent proper seating.

Refit the matching disc over the studs and onto the hub. If it will not seat over the shoes, stop and recheck the matching drum measurement and shoe diameter rather than forcing it into place.

steps.title: Restore the caliper and bracket with new bolts
steps.body:
Bring the supported caliper and its mounting bracket back into their original positions around the disc. Install two new mounting-bracket bolts and tighten them to 81 lb.ft (110 Nm).

Make sure the brake hose is free of pulling or trapping before removing the caliper’s temporary support.

steps.title: Reconnect the parking brake cable
steps.body: Reverse the cable removal: seat the cable casing fitting in its bracket so its retaining tabs engage, then reconnect the cable end to the parking brake shoe actuation lever. Check both attachments directly—the casing must be retained in the bracket and the cable end must be engaged with the lever. Leave the parking brake released until the remaining reassembly and pedal check are complete.

steps.title: Prepare the wheel mounting faces and pilot bore
steps.body:
Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel’s flat mounting face and the corresponding hub/disc mounting face. Any rotor-to-hub retaining fastener present must be secured without obstructing the wheel’s seating surface. Contamination or an obstruction here can allow wheel nuts to loosen.

Also clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the circular opening that locates the wheel on the hub’s raised center. Apply a thin film of Motorcraft XL-2 anti-seize only at the interface between this bore and the hub pilot. Keep it off the flat wheel-to-disc mounting faces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, pads and disc friction surfaces. The stud and nut threads must remain clean and dry.

steps.title: Install the wheel finger tight
steps.body: Position the wheel squarely on the hub and install all five wheel nuts finger tight. Final torque is applied with the vehicle resting on its tires. If you are adjusting the other rear side, complete the same work using that side’s own drum measurement before returning the car to the ground.

steps.title: Check reassembly and operate the brake pedal
steps.body:
Confirm that the access plug is installed, the disc and caliper bracket are refitted, the new bracket bolts have been torqued, both parking brake cable attachments are restored, and the caliper support has been removed.

Apply the brake pedal several times to verify correct brake system operation, as required after disc installation. If operation is not correct, do not return the vehicle to use.

steps.title: Restore the parking brake before lowering
steps.body:
Apply the parking brake before beginning to lower the car. Clear tools and people from the lowering area, then lower using the hoist’s normal release procedure.

As the tires reach the ground, restore wheel chocks before the hoist stops supporting the car; retain any chocks already restraining ground wheels. Once the car is resting on its tires, keep the parking brake applied and the wheels chocked for final wheel-nut tightening.

steps.title: Torque the wheel nuts in the five-point star pattern
steps.body:
With the car resting on its tires and the stud and nut threads clean and dry, tighten all five nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) in a star/cross pattern.

Using the illustrated wheel orientation, the sequence is top, lower left, upper right, upper left, then lower right. Crossing the wheel between nuts helps avoid uneven disc seating and excessive disc runout, which can contribute to brake shudder and vibration.

steps.title: Keep the measurements and schedule the nut recheck
steps.body:
Keep the drum ID and final shoe diameter together for each adjusted side, confirming the 0.59 mm (0.023 in) diameter difference. Record completion of the bracket-bolt and wheel-nut torques.

Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after reinstalling a wheel, using the same clean, dry thread requirement, star pattern and 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) torque. Initial tightening does not cancel that follow-up.

watchFor.title: Measuring the wrong circular surface
watchFor.body: The drum measurement comes from the internal cylindrical surface inside the disc’s center section. The shoe measurement goes across the widest outside span of the opposed linings. Neither measurement is taken across the outer disc friction ring.

watchFor.title: Treating the allowance as a gap at each shoe
watchFor.body: The complete shoe diameter must be 0.59 mm (0.023 in) smaller than the drum ID. Applying that allowance separately at both sides produces the wrong setting.

watchFor.title: Letting the hose become the caliper support
watchFor.body: Support the caliper while it is aside and while bringing it back into position. Its weight must never hang from the hydraulic hose.

watchFor.title: Reusing the discarded bracket bolts
watchFor.body: Use two new caliper mounting-bracket bolts for each removed assembly and tighten them to 81 lb.ft (110 Nm). Keep that specification separate from the wheel-nut torque.

watchFor.title: Putting anti-seize everywhere
watchFor.body: XL-2 belongs only in a thin film between the cleaned wheel pilot bore and hub pilot. The flat mounting faces and the wheel fastener threads must stay free of it.

notes: The tire stays on the wheel for this job; tire changing and wheel balancing are not part of the adjustment.
Keep each disc with its own measurement throughout the work. One side’s drum ID is not a substitute for measuring the other side.

diagnostics.finding: The drum ID minus the measured shoe diameter is greater than 0.59 mm (0.023 in).
diagnostics.meaning: The shoe diameter is smaller than the adjustment target.
diagnostics.next: Rotate the adjuster in the direction that increases the measured shoe diameter, checking with the gauge until the specified difference is reached.

diagnostics.finding: The drum ID minus the measured shoe diameter is less than 0.59 mm (0.023 in), or the shoes measure larger than the drum.
diagnostics.meaning: The shoe diameter is larger than the adjustment target.
diagnostics.next: Rotate the adjuster in the direction that reduces the measured shoe diameter and remeasure until the specified difference is reached.

diagnostics.finding: The adjuster will not turn or the target diameter cannot be obtained.
diagnostics.meaning: A dimensional adjustment cannot be completed; this does not identify which component is responsible.
diagnostics.next: Stop the adjustment and have the mechanical fault assessed before reassembly for service. Do not substitute cable adjustment or a guessed number of clicks.

diagnostics.finding: The disc will not seat over the adjusted shoes.
diagnostics.meaning: Successful fit has not been established, even if a target reading was recorded.
diagnostics.next: Do not force the disc. Recheck that it matches the measured side, repeat its drum ID measurement and repeat the widest shoe-diameter measurement.

diagnostics.finding: Brake system operation is not correct when the pedal is applied several times after reassembly.
diagnostics.meaning: The required completion check has not passed.
diagnostics.next: Keep the vehicle out of use until the brake fault is resolved; the shoe-diameter setting alone does not clear it for driving.

verification.title: Dimensional setting recorded
verification.body: For each adjusted side, the recorded drum ID exceeds the final widest shoe diameter by 0.59 mm (0.023 in).

verification.title: Brake assembly complete
verification.body: The backing plate plug is seated, the disc is installed, two new caliper mounting-bracket bolts are tightened to 81 lb.ft (110 Nm), the cable casing and cable end are reconnected, and the caliper hose carries no suspended weight.

verification.title: Brake pedal check completed
verification.body: The brake pedal has been applied several times and correct brake system operation verified after disc installation.

verification.title: Restraints and wheel fastening restored
verification.body: The parking brake was applied before lowering, wheel chocks were restored as the tires reached the ground, and the wheel nuts were tightened on the ground in a star pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) with clean, dry threads.

verification.title: Follow-up arranged
verification.body: Wheel-nut retightening is due within 160 km (100 mi) of wheel reinstallation.

guides.title: Replace the left-hand parking brake cable
guides.summary: Remove the left-hand cable from the equalizer, supporting brackets and brake caliper, then refit it and complete the parking-brake adjustment.
guides.introduction: The left-hand (LH) parking brake cable carries mechanical pull from the equalizer to the brake caliper lever. Brackets retain the cable casing so movement of the inner cable can operate the lever. This job releases both end connections and the intervening supports, then restores the assembly and its adjustment.
guides.why: Loosening the adjustment first releases cable tension for disconnection. The end fittings also have retaining tabs that must be released deliberately. Correct routing, bracket fastening and final adjustment all contribute to transmitting the parking-brake pull correctly.

when.summary: When repair requires removal or replacement of the left-hand parking brake cable.
notes: This procedure covers cable replacement; it does not establish the cause of a parking-brake performance complaint.

prepare.title: Plan underbody and wheel-off access
prepare.detail: Arrange suitable vehicle lifting and support capability and follow the Wheel and Tire procedure for wheel removal and installation.

prepare.title: Select the exhaust procedure
prepare.detail: Removing the muffler and tailpipe provides access. Use the procedure matching the fitted 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine.

prepare.title: Prepare for fastening and adjustment
prepare.detail: Have tools for the bracket fasteners and a torque wrench. Keep the main cable procedure and separate Parking Brake Cable Adjustment procedure available throughout the job.

steps.title: Remove the exhaust assembly for access
steps.body: Remove the muffler and tailpipe assembly using the engine-specific procedure. This is the first access operation in the cable replacement sequence.

steps.title: Release the equalizer end
steps.body: Loosen the parking brake cable adjustment nut. Press both retaining tabs inward to release the LH cable casing from its bracket. Rotate the cable, slide its pin upward and detach it from the equalizer. Releasing the tabs and moving the pin are separate actions.

steps.title: Free the intermediate cable supports
steps.body: Remove the cable bracket nut, then the bracket bolt, followed by the pair of bracket bolts identified in the main procedure. Keep their locations clear for installation: the paired bolts have different tightening specifications.

steps.title: Disconnect the caliper end
steps.body: Remove the wheel and tire, then the remaining cable bracket bolt. Disconnect the cable from the brake caliper lever. Press both tabs inward at the caliper bracket, release the cable casing and remove the cable.

steps.title: Install in reverse order
steps.body: Restore the cable's route, caliper bracket retention and lever connection, then reinstall the supports and equalizer connection in reverse sequence. Use the location-specific fastener torques in the main procedure. Refit the wheel and exhaust assembly through their respective procedures.

steps.title: Complete the cable adjustment
steps.body: Carry out Parking Brake Cable Adjustment after installation. This is a required completion phase; use that procedure to establish the adjustment rather than relying on the nut's previous position.

watchFor.title: Retaining tabs still engaged
watchFor.body: Both tabs must be pressed inward at each specified casing connection before the fitting can leave its bracket.

watchFor.title: Different bracket tightening values
watchFor.body: Do not use a single torque for every bracket fastener. Match each location to the main procedure.

notes: The cable sequence is shared across the listed engines, but muffler and tailpipe removal uses a separate engine-specific procedure.

verification.title: Confirm the installation sequence is complete
verification.body: Confirm both cable ends, all supports, the wheel and the exhaust assembly have been reinstated with their specified fastening requirements.

verification.title: Confirm adjustment completion
verification.body: Complete the linked cable-adjustment procedure and its requirements before considering the replacement finished.

guides.title: Replace the right-hand parking brake cable
guides.summary: Replace the right-hand parking brake cable, restore its mountings and end connections, and complete the cable adjustment.
guides.introduction: The right-hand parking brake cable carries pull from the equalizer to the rear brake caliper lever. Its outer casing is held by brackets and retaining tabs so the inner cable can move the lever. Replacement involves both ends and the intermediate supports, with muffler and tailpipe removal providing access. The cable procedure is shared across the listed engines, but exhaust removal follows the engine-specific procedure.
guides.why: Loosening the adjuster releases cable tension before the end connection is separated. Correctly seated casing retainers provide the fixed support the cable needs, while the final adjustment establishes the operating setting after installation.

when.summary: When inspection has established that the right-hand parking brake cable requires replacement.
notes: This is a replacement procedure; it does not establish cable failure from a parking-brake complaint alone.

prepare.title: Arrange underbody access
prepare.detail: Provide supported access and the capability to remove the muffler and tailpipe assembly and wheel. Select the exhaust procedure for the fitted engine.

prepare.title: Prepare for refitting
prepare.detail: Have tools for the cable adjuster and bracket fasteners, plus a torque wrench. Keep the mounting locations identifiable because the specified fastener torques differ.

steps.title: Remove the exhaust assembly for access
steps.body: Remove the muffler and tailpipe using the linked 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L procedure. This provides access for releasing the cable and its supports.

steps.title: Release the equalizer end
steps.body: Loosen the parking-brake cable adjustment nut. Press both retaining tabs inward and detach the right-hand cable casing from its bracket. Rotate the cable, slide its pin upward and separate it from the equalizer.

steps.title: Release the intermediate supports
steps.body: Remove the successive bracket bolts and nut in the main procedure’s order, including the grouped bracket bolts. Note the cable routing and each support position so installation can reverse the same path.

steps.title: Disconnect the caliper end
steps.body: Remove the wheel and tire, then the remaining cable bracket bolt. Disconnect the cable from the caliper lever. Press the two casing-retainer tabs inward, release the casing from the caliper bracket and remove the cable.

steps.title: Install and adjust
steps.body: Reverse removal to install the replacement cable, restoring its end connections, brackets, wheel and engine-specific exhaust assembly. Apply the location-specific fastener torques in the complete procedure. Finish with the linked Parking Brake Cable Adjustment procedure.

watchFor.title: Retainers still engaged
watchFor.body: Release both tabs at each casing connection before withdrawing it; the equalizer end also requires the specified rotation and upward pin movement.

watchFor.title: Mixed bracket torque requirements
watchFor.body: Do not use one tightening value for every mounting. Match each fastener to its position in the procedure.

notes: Final cable adjustment is a separate required operation after refitting; installation alone does not complete the job.

verification.title: Check the completed installation sequence
verification.body: Confirm that both cable ends, casing retainers, intermediate supports, wheel and exhaust assembly have been restored through the reverse procedure.

verification.title: Complete the adjustment endpoint
verification.body: Finish the linked cable-adjustment procedure and its requirements before recording the replacement as complete.

guides.title: Replace the parking brake control and front cable assembly
guides.summary: Remove the parking brake lever and front cable through underbody and console access, then complete the correct cable adjustment.
guides.introduction: The parking brake control turns movement of the hand lever into a pull on the front cable. That cable connects to the equalizer, which transfers the pull into the rest of the parking brake cable system. The control and front cable come out as an assembly. This repair therefore crosses two work areas: beneath the vehicle for cable access and inside the cabin beneath the floor console.
guides.why: The cable adjustment must be loosened before the front cable is disconnected, so the connection can be released without working against its existing tension. The cable's retaining tabs, control mounting fasteners and parking brake switch all need to be restored during assembly. Final cable adjustment establishes the working setting after those connections have been disturbed; simply bolting the lever back in does not complete the repair.

when.summary: When the parking brake control or its attached front cable requires removal or replacement.
notes: Choose the final adjustment procedure by fitted equipment, including the SVT Performance Package where present.

prepare.title: Arrange underbody and console access
prepare.detail: Have suitable vehicle support and the capability to remove the engine-specific muffler and tailpipe assembly, followed by the floor console.

prepare.title: Prepare for fastening and adjustment
prepare.detail: Have torque equipment suitable for the control bolts and mounting nut, and the correct standard or SVT Performance Package cable-adjustment procedure.

steps.title: Remove the muffler and tailpipe assembly
steps.body: Use the matching engine procedure to expose the cable work area. Separate references cover the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L. For the 5.2L route, follow the Muffler and Tailpipe reference to section 309-00D in the parking brake control procedure.

steps.title: Release the front cable
steps.body: Loosen the parking brake cable adjustment nut. Rotate the cable outward, then pull the pin and cable upward to disconnect them from the equalizer. Release the retaining tabs and disconnect the front cable from its bracket.

steps.title: Expose the control inside the cabin
steps.body: Remove the floor console through its linked procedure. Remove the parking brake switch bolt and position the switch aside before removing the control.

steps.title: Remove the control and cable together
steps.body: Remove the two control bolts, then the mounting nut. Remove the parking brake control and front cable assembly, keeping the cable's path and attachment locations clear for installation.

steps.title: Reinstall in reverse order
steps.body: Fit the control and front cable assembly. Tighten the control bolts to 22 lb.ft (30 Nm) and the mounting nut to 150 lb.in (17 Nm). Restore the switch, console, bracket tabs, equalizer connection and muffler and tailpipe assembly through the reverse removal sequence.

steps.title: Set the cable adjustment
steps.body: Complete Parking Brake Cable Adjustment, or the separate Vehicles With: SVT Performance Package procedure when that package is fitted. Use that procedure's setting and completion checks rather than treating the old adjustment-nut position as a finished adjustment.

watchFor.title: Different fasteners use different torque units
watchFor.body: The mounting nut specification is given in pound-inches; the control bolt specification is in pound-feet. Keep the fasteners and settings distinct.

watchFor.title: Incomplete cable retention
watchFor.body: Reinstallation includes both the equalizer pin connection and the front cable's bracket tabs. Restoring only the control mounting leaves the cable installation unfinished.

verification.title: Check restored attachments
verification.body: Confirm the control fasteners, switch, cable bracket retention and equalizer connection are restored, and the console and muffler and tailpipe assembly are installed.

verification.title: Record adjustment completion
verification.body: Record whether the standard or SVT Performance Package adjustment procedure was used and its completion result.

guides.title: Remove and replace the brake master cylinder
guides.summary: Remove the brake master cylinder, renew its mounting nuts and complete the bleeding branch appropriate to replacement or temporary removal.
guides.introduction: The brake master cylinder converts brake-pedal input into hydraulic pressure for the braking system. Its reservoir supplies fluid, and manual-transmission vehicles also have a clutch supply connection that must be addressed during removal. The job changes or temporarily removes the cylinder, opens hydraulic connections and therefore requires the appropriate bleeding work before completion.
guides.why: Air introduced into a hydraulic circuit can compress instead of transmitting pedal movement effectively. That makes bleeding part of the repair, not an optional final task. Sealing open connections protects the system from contamination, and the cylinder’s mounting nuts must be replaced after removal.

when.summary: When the master cylinder requires replacement or must be removed to reach another component.
notes: Choose the bleeding route according to whether a new cylinder is installed or the original cylinder is refitted.
Manual-transmission vehicles also require clutch bleeding.

prepare.title: Arrange hydraulic-service capability
prepare.detail: Have the applicable bleeding procedures and equipment ready before opening the system. For manual-transmission vehicles, provide a suitable suction device for emptying the reservoir.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement nuts and closures
prepare.detail: Obtain new master-cylinder mounting nuts, suitable closures for hydraulic openings, and torque tools for the mounting nuts and brake-tube fittings.

prepare.title: Protect painted surfaces
prepare.detail: If brake fluid reaches paintwork, wash the affected area immediately with cold water.

steps.title: Disconnect the manual-transmission supply branch
steps.body: On manual-transmission vehicles, remove the reservoir cap and siphon out the brake fluid with a suitable suction device. Disconnect the clutch master-cylinder tube and detach its bracket from the master-cylinder studs.

steps.title: Release the electrical and brake connections
steps.body: On all vehicles, disconnect the fluid-level sensor connector and detach the harness retainer from the reservoir. Disconnect the two brake-tube fittings, ensuring all openings are sealed.

steps.title: Remove the cylinder and discard its nuts
steps.body: Remove the two mounting nuts and the brake master cylinder. Discard both nuts; the [removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1692560) requires replacement fasteners.

steps.title: Reinstall the cylinder and connections
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence using new mounting nuts. Tighten the nuts to 23 Nm and the brake-tube fittings to 27.5 Nm. Restore the sensor connector, harness retainer and, where applicable, the clutch tube, bracket and reservoir cap.

steps.title: Complete the correct bleeding operations
steps.body: For a new cylinder, follow [Component Bleeding](#/document/G1694693) to bleed the master cylinder. If the original cylinder was removed for access and refitted, follow Brake System Pressure Bleeding. Manual-transmission vehicles additionally require clutch bleeding.

steps.title: Complete the replacement check
steps.body: When a new master cylinder has been installed, road-test the vehicle after the required bleeding work is complete. Record that result separately from the hydraulic assembly work.

watchFor.title: Open hydraulic ports
watchFor.body: Keep all disconnected openings sealed. Leaving them exposed defeats the contamination precaution required during removal.

watchFor.title: Reused mounting nuts
watchFor.body: Do not reinstall the discarded cylinder mounting nuts.

notes: Manual-transmission vehicles need clutch bleeding after the hydraulic supply has been opened. The linked procedure is used by both MT82 and 3160 installation instructions; follow it with the fitted gearbox’s restoration requirements.
Use the complete named Brake System Pressure Bleeding procedure when refitting a cylinder removed for access; no substitute bleeding sequence is given here.

diagnostics.finding: A new master cylinder is being installed.
diagnostics.meaning: The replacement branch requires master-cylinder bleeding and a road test.
diagnostics.next: Complete Component Bleeding, any applicable clutch bleeding and the road test.

diagnostics.finding: The original cylinder is being refitted after access work.
diagnostics.meaning: The procedure directs brake-system pressure bleeding.
diagnostics.next: Complete that bleeding route and clutch bleeding if the vehicle has a manual transmission.

verification.title: Confirm assembly completion
verification.body: Confirm new mounting nuts, tightened tube fittings, restored electrical connections and the applicable clutch supply attachments.

verification.title: Record the hydraulic completion route
verification.body: Record whether the cylinder was renewed or reused, which bleeding operations were completed, and the road-test result when replacement required it.

procedures.purpose: Master cylinder removal and installation, including manual-transmission preparation and conditional bleeding and road-test requirements.
Master-cylinder bleeding when a new cylinder is installed.
Required clutch-system bleeding after the manual-transmission clutch supply is restored.

authoring.method: Codex review of engine-specific linked completion requirements

guides.title: Replace the brake pedal and bracket with a 3160 or MT82 manual transmission
guides.summary: Remove and refit the combined brake/clutch pedal assembly while protecting its switches and renewing the specified retaining parts.
guides.introduction: The brake pedal transfers your foot pressure to the brake booster through its push rod. Its supporting bracket forms part of the brake/clutch pedal assembly, so replacement also involves clutch hydraulic connections and pedal switches. This is a coordinated cabin and engine-compartment repair.
guides.why: Pedal position matters because the switches depend on their plungers being correctly compressed. Moving a pedal during switch installation can damage the switch or leave it incorrectly adjusted. The booster connection also needs correct clevis alignment and a new locking pin.
searchTerms: manual Mustang brake pedal bracket replacement

when.summary: Use when an established repair requires removal or replacement of the brake pedal and bracket assembly.
notes: Select the cruise-switch procedure for the fitted standard or adaptive cruise equipment.

prepare.title: Arrange access and assistance
prepare.detail: Have an assistant available to move the booster/master-cylinder assembly away from the dash panel. Cruise-switch access requires driver knee-airbag removal; arrange the necessary restraint-system capability and follow its complete safety procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare fluid handling and replacement parts
prepare.detail: Have a suitable suction device, fluid collection equipment, clutch-bleeding capability, a new booster push-rod clevis-locking pin and four new mounting nuts. Wash any brake fluid spilled on paint immediately with cold water.

steps.title: Disconnect the clutch hydraulic connections
steps.body: Remove the reservoir cap and siphon out the brake fluid. Disconnect the clutch master-cylinder supply tube from the reservoir. Spread the clutch-tube clip, push it downward into its released position and disconnect the tube.

steps.title: Remove the pedal switches before pedal work
steps.body: Remove the stoplamp switch with the brake pedal at rest and its switch plunger compressed. Arrange knee-airbag removal for cruise-switch access. Keep the clutch pedal at rest and the deactivator-switch plunger compressed. Standard cruise requires removing the switch before disconnecting its connector; adaptive cruise requires disconnecting the connector first.

steps.title: Free the wiring and booster linkage
steps.body: Disconnect the accelerator-pedal and starter-inhibitor-switch connectors. Release the six harness retainers and move the wiring aside. Remove and discard the booster push-rod clevis-locking pin, then position the push rod aside.

steps.title: Remove the pedal assembly with assistance
steps.body: Have the assistant pull the booster and master-cylinder assembly away from the dash panel. Do not pry on the booster. Remove the four bolts and four nuts, discard the nuts and remove the brake/clutch pedal assembly.

steps.title: Refit the assembly and mechanical connection
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Before installing the assembly retainers, align the booster push-rod clevis with the brake-pedal attachment point. Use four new nuts and tighten the mounting hardware as specified in the linked procedure. Attach the aligned push rod with a new locking pin and restore the harness routing and connectors.

steps.title: Install the switches and restore clutch hydraulics
steps.body: Reverse the appropriate switch-removal procedures. Keep the clutch pedal at rest during deactivator-switch installation. Install the stoplamp switch only with the booster push rod attached and brake pedal at rest; do not push, pull or move the pedal. Reconnect the hydraulic tubes and complete clutch filling and bleeding using the linked procedure.

watchFor.title: Switch resistance is not a cue to force it
watchFor.body: Trying to rotate a switch with its plunger extended can damage it. Establish the required pedal and plunger positions before removal.

watchFor.title: Clevis misalignment
watchFor.body: Align the booster connection before fitting retainers. The discarded locking pin must not be reused.

notes: The linked clutch-bleeding operation applies to both MT82 and 3160 installations despite its MT82 section label.

verification.title: Confirm assembly completion
verification.body: Check that the clevis is aligned, the push rod is attached with its new pin, new nuts are installed, wiring is retained and both switches were installed with their pedals at rest.

verification.title: Record the hydraulic completion
verification.body: Record completion of the clutch-bleeding procedure and specified mounting-hardware tightening before closing the repair.

procedures.purpose: Complete brake/clutch pedal assembly removal and installation for 3160 and MT82 transmissions.
Stoplamp-switch removal and installation.
Standard-cruise deactivator-switch removal and installation, including knee-airbag access.
Adaptive-cruise deactivator-switch removal and installation with at-rest clutch-pedal handling.
Clutch hydraulic bleeding after reconnection for either transmission.

guides.title: Replace the brake booster on 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L Mustangs
guides.summary: Replace the vacuum brake booster using the correct engine-specific access sequence, renew discarded hardware and bleed the disturbed hydraulic systems.
guides.introduction: The brake booster uses vacuum assistance to reduce the pedal effort needed to operate the brake master cylinder. Replacement involves the engine compartment and pedal connection, including removal of the master cylinder and brake tubes. The three engine procedures share that purpose but differ in cowl access, nearby components and battery-disconnection requirements.
guides.why: Opening the brake circuit makes bleeding part of the repair. Manual-transmission vehicles also require clutch bleeding after their reservoir connection is disturbed. The stoplamp switch must be handled with the pedal at rest, and specified mounting hardware and the pushrod locking pin must be renewed.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the brake booster requires replacement.
notes: These procedures cover replacement, not diagnosis of the cause of a brake-assistance complaint.

prepare.title: Arrange hydraulic-service capability
prepare.detail: Have torque tools and the equipment and instructions for Brake System Pressure Bleeding (206-00). Manual-transmission vehicles also need a suitable reservoir suction device and the linked clutch-bleeding procedure.

prepare.title: Obtain replacement hardware
prepare.detail: Prepare new master-cylinder mounting nuts, booster mounting nuts and a booster pushrod clevis-locking pin. The 5.0L procedure additionally discards the cross-brace nuts.

prepare.title: Protect painted surfaces
prepare.detail: If brake fluid reaches paintwork, immediately wash the affected area with cold water.

steps.title: Begin the correct engine access sequence
steps.body: Remove the cowl panel grille. On the 5.0L, disconnect the battery cables using the linked procedure. On all three engines, detach the vacuum check valve from the booster and position it aside.

steps.title: Disconnect the manual-transmission reservoir connection
steps.body: For manual-transmission vehicles, remove the reservoir cap and siphon out the brake fluid with a suitable suction device. Disconnect the clutch master-cylinder tube and detach its bracket from the master-cylinder studs.

steps.title: Remove the cowl obstruction
steps.body: Detach the battery-cable retainer. On the 2.3L and 3.7L, remove the cowl-extension bolts and nuts, then the extension. On the 5.0L, remove the cross brace and discard its nuts, remove the cowl-extension bolts and extension, then release the noise-generator clamp and pin-type retainer and position the generator aside.

steps.title: Remove the master cylinder and tubes
steps.body: Disconnect the fluid-level sensor and detach the reservoir wiring retainer. Disconnect the brake tubes at the hydraulic control unit (HCU), then unclip them. Remove and discard the master-cylinder nuts, and remove the master cylinder with its brake tubes.

steps.title: Release the remaining engine-side connections
steps.body: Disconnect the vacuum-sensor connector. On the 2.3L, detach the fuel pressure line from its intake-manifold clip and position it aside; on the 3.7L, release it from the valve-cover clip. Follow the respective engine procedure for these access differences.

steps.title: Remove the stoplamp switch before disturbing the pedal
steps.body: Keep the brake pedal at rest and remove the switch using its linked procedure. The switch plunger must be compressed for rotation in the bracket; removing it with the plunger extended during pedal application can damage it.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the booster
steps.body: Remove and discard the pushrod clevis-locking pin, then position the pushrod aside. Remove and discard the booster mounting nuts and remove the booster.

steps.title: Install in reverse order
steps.body: Reverse the matching engine procedure, using new hardware wherever disposal was specified and its stated tightening values. Attach the booster pushrod before installing the stoplamp switch. Keep the pedal at rest and do not press, pull or otherwise move it during switch installation.

steps.title: Bleed and complete the repair
steps.body: Carry out Brake System Pressure Bleeding. On a manual-transmission vehicle, also bleed the clutch using its linked procedure. If a new brake booster was installed, complete the required road test after reassembly and bleeding.

watchFor.title: Reusing the locking pin
watchFor.body: The pushrod clevis-locking pin is single-use. Fit a new one whenever it has been removed.

watchFor.title: Incorrect switch adjustment
watchFor.body: Installing the stoplamp switch with the pedal displaced can misadjust or damage it. The pushrod must already be attached and the pedal must remain at rest.

notes: Tightening instructions appear within the removal procedures as well as the installation path. Use the values belonging to the selected engine and fastening location.

verification.title: Confirm required finishing work
verification.body: Confirm completion of brake bleeding, clutch bleeding when applicable, and the road test required after installing a new booster.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the engine and transmission configuration, renewed hardware, completed bleeding procedures and the road-test result.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost booster removal and installation, including intake-manifold fuel-line clip access.
3.7L Duratec booster removal and installation, including valve-cover fuel-line clip access.
5.0L booster removal and installation, including battery, cross-brace and noise-generator access.
Cowl panel grille removal and installation for access on all three engines.
Stoplamp-switch removal and installation with the required pedal position.
Clutch-system bleeding for manual-transmission vehicles after reassembly.
Battery cable disconnection and reconnection required by the 5.0L booster procedure.

guides.title: Replace the brake vacuum pump — 2.3L EcoBoost
guides.summary: Remove the brake vacuum pump, assess its housing gasket, and reinstall the pump with its drive coupling correctly aligned to the camshaft.
guides.introduction: The brake vacuum pump supplies vacuum for power brake assistance. On this engine, the pump couples to the camshaft, so replacement involves both a sealed housing joint and a mechanical drive connection. Access requires removing cowl and engine-cover components, followed by lifting the vehicle and clearing the pump covers and nearby wiring.
guides.why: Correct coupling alignment is the critical installation precaution: misalignment can damage the camshaft or pump. Clean mating faces allow the housing gasket to seal properly. The gasket is inspected and replaced according to its condition, rather than automatically discarded. Restoring the ground wire and harness retention is also part of completing the access work.

when.summary: When the 2.3L brake vacuum pump requires removal or replacement after the service need has been established.
notes: This is a pump removal and installation job; it does not establish the cause of a brake-assistance complaint.

prepare.title: Arrange access and lifting capability
prepare.detail: Have a suitable hoist, hand tools and torque tools for the cowl, brackets, covers, ground connection and pump fasteners. Follow the approved lifting-point instructions with the vehicle in NEUTRAL.

prepare.title: Prepare for gasket assessment
prepare.detail: Keep the pump mating faces free of foreign material and have a replacement housing gasket available if inspection shows it is needed. Be ready to establish correct camshaft-to-pump coupling alignment before fastening the pump.

steps.title: Remove the cowl access components
steps.body: Remove the cowl vent panel using [Cowl Panel Grille](#/document/G1693246), then remove the cowl-extension bolts, nuts and extension. Keep the bolts and nuts distinguished because their installation torques differ.

steps.title: Clear the upper brackets and cover
steps.body: Remove the bracket and engine appearance cover in the sequence shown in the [pump procedure](#/document/G1692576). Detach the fuel-line bracket from the intake manifold to complete this stage of access.

steps.title: Lift the vehicle and uncover the pump
steps.body: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on the hoist using [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631). Remove the cylinder-head ground-wire bolt and detach the wire. Release the wiring-harness retainer, then remove the retainers and both the brake-vacuum-pump and high-pressure-fuel-pump covers.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the vacuum pump
steps.body: Release the vacuum-tube coupling and disconnect the tube. Remove the pump bolts and pump. Inspect the housing gasket and replace it as necessary. Ensure both mating faces are clean and free of foreign material before reassembly.

steps.title: Align the drive and reinstall the pump
steps.body: Correctly align the camshaft and vacuum-pump couplings before installing the pump. Do not proceed with fastening while alignment is uncertain. Tighten the pump bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm), then restore the vacuum-tube connection.

steps.title: Restore the access components
steps.body: Reverse the remaining removal sequence, restoring the covers, wiring-harness retainer and cylinder-head ground wire. Reattach the fuel-line bracket and reinstall the appearance cover, bracket, cowl extension and vent panel. Apply each component's own tightening value from the pump procedure.

watchFor.title: Resistance caused by coupling misalignment
watchFor.body: Resolve alignment before securing the pump; incorrect engagement can damage either the pump or camshaft.

watchFor.title: Confusing cover removal with fuel-system work
watchFor.body: The access sequence removes the high-pressure fuel-pump cover and detaches a fuel-line bracket. Keep the fuel connections intact during these operations.

notes: Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Position hoist adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering components.

diagnostics.finding: The housing gasket is unfit for reuse on inspection.
diagnostics.meaning: The pump's housing joint requires a replacement gasket.
diagnostics.next: Renew the gasket and ensure the mating faces are clean before fitting the pump.

verification.title: Confirm the pump installation
verification.body: Confirm correct coupling alignment, completed gasket assessment, specified pump-bolt tightening and reconnection of the vacuum tube.

verification.title: Confirm access reassembly
verification.body: Check that the ground wire, harness retainer, both pump covers, fuel-line bracket and cowl components have all been restored.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost brake-vacuum-pump removal and installation, gasket assessment and drive-coupling alignment.
Cowl vent-panel removal and installation for pump access.
Approved hoist positioning and lifting precautions.

guides.title: Replace the brake booster vacuum sensor
guides.summary: Disconnect and remove the brake vacuum sensor, then install it in exactly its original position and reconnect it.
guides.introduction: The brake booster uses a pressure difference to help the driver apply the brakes, and its vacuum sensor provides an electrical indication of the vacuum condition. This job removes that sensing component and restores its electrical connection. It does not replace the booster or establish why a brake-system complaint occurred.
guides.why: The critical installation requirement is positional: the sensor must return to exactly the position from which it was removed. Observing that position before disturbing the component makes the final installation check meaningful, especially when the original sensor will no longer be available as a fitted reference.

when.summary: When the brake booster vacuum sensor requires removal or replacement.
notes: Use this procedure after establishing that sensor removal is the required work.

prepare.title: Identify the component and its position
prepare.detail: Use the illustration in [Brake Vacuum Sensor](#/document/G1698171) to identify the sensor and electrical connector. Obtain a clear view of the installed sensor before disconnecting anything.

prepare.title: Preserve an installation reference
prepare.detail: Note the sensor body's orientation and connector position while it is still fitted. The work requires careful connector handling and enough access to restore this arrangement accurately.

steps.title: Establish the original position
steps.body: Inspect the fitted sensor and retain a clear reference to its exact installation position. Do this before removal, when its relationship to the surrounding assembly can still be seen.

steps.title: Disconnect the electrical connector
steps.body: Disconnect the brake booster vacuum sensor connector identified in the illustration. This separates the sensor from the vehicle wiring before the sensor is removed.

steps.title: Remove the sensor
steps.body: Remove the brake booster vacuum sensor following the linked procedure. Keep the original-position reference available for installation; do not rely on remembering a convenient connector orientation afterward.

steps.title: Restore the sensor and connection
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure. Install the sensor in exactly its original position, then reconnect its electrical connector. The same positioning requirement applies whether refitting the original sensor or installing a replacement.

watchFor.title: A different installed orientation
watchFor.body: Do not rotate or reposition the sensor simply to make connector access easier.

notes: This replacement operation provides no electrical test values or component-failure criteria; fault diagnosis is a separate task.

verification.title: Compare the installation position
verification.body: Check the installed sensor against the position established before removal.

verification.title: Confirm reconnection
verification.body: Confirm that the sensor's electrical connector has been reconnected as part of the reverse installation sequence.

procedures.purpose: Brake booster vacuum sensor removal and installation, including the exact-position requirement.

guides.title: Replace and program the anti-lock brake system module
guides.summary: Begin module programming with the original ABS module installed, remove the hydraulic assembly, replace the cleanly separated module and complete programming.
guides.introduction: The anti-lock brake system (ABS) helps maintain steering control during hard braking by preventing wheel lock. It also participates in stability and traction control. The electronic ABS module works with the hydraulic control unit (HCU), which manages brake-fluid pressure. These are separately supplied components: a replacement ABS module does not include an HCU. This repair combines electronic configuration work with removal and refitting of the hydraulic assembly.
guides.why: Programmable Module Installation (PMI) must begin while the original module is still installed, allowing the diagnostic tool to start the replacement process in the correct state. Cleanliness at the module-to-HCU interface is equally important: brake fluid or foreign material entering the module's mating side can damage the component.
searchTerms: ABS module not responding to scan tool
brake pedal pulsation during ABS operation

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the ABS module requires replacement.
notes: Noise and pedal pulsation during ABS or stability-control intervention can be normal and do not establish module failure.

prepare.title: Arrange programming capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of the prescribed PMI process. If the original module cannot communicate, be prepared to supply As-Built Data when the tool requests it.

prepare.title: Plan the hydraulic work
prepare.detail: Have the complete HCU removal and installation procedure available and the capability to carry out its hydraulic-system work and completion requirements.

prepare.title: Prepare a clean assembly area
prepare.detail: Obtain the correct replacement module and new retainers. Provide a clean, dry working area and suitable tools for separating the module from the HCU without introducing fluid or debris.

steps.title: Begin PMI before removal
steps.body: With the current ABS module installed, begin PMI using the diagnostic scan tool and follow its on-screen instructions. The [ABS module procedure](#/document/G1692579) places this step before hydraulic assembly removal.

steps.title: Remove the hydraulic control unit
steps.body: Follow the [HCU removal procedure](#/document/G1692580). Complete the access and hydraulic work specified there before separating the electronic module.

steps.title: Clean the mating area
steps.body: Make sure both the HCU and ABS module are clean and free of brake fluid and foreign material. Protect the module's mating side throughout separation and assembly.

steps.title: Separate the module
steps.body: Remove the three screws and the ABS module. Discard the removed retainers. Keep the HCU available for reassembly; a new electronic module does not arrive with a replacement hydraulic unit.

steps.title: Install the module and hydraulic assembly
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure using new retainers. Tighten the specified module fasteners to 44 lb.in (5 Nm), then reinstall the HCU and complete the requirements of its installation procedure.

steps.title: Finish module programming
steps.body: Use the diagnostic scan tool to complete PMI, following every on-screen instruction. Mechanical installation alone does not complete the module replacement.

watchFor.title: Fluid at the electronic interface
watchFor.body: Do not allow brake fluid or foreign material to enter the mating side of the ABS module; component damage can result.

watchFor.title: Starting programming too late
watchFor.body: The PMI process must begin with the original module still installed, even when communication problems may require the As-Built Data path.

notes: The ABS module and HCU are separate service components.
Longer pedal travel immediately after ABS or stability-control activation can also be a normal operating condition.

diagnostics.finding: The original ABS module does not respond to the diagnostic tool.
diagnostics.meaning: The PMI process may require As-Built Data; lack of response alone does not establish the underlying fault.
diagnostics.next: Follow the tool's prompted replacement path and any requested data entry.

diagnostics.finding: Noise or pedal pulsation occurs during ABS or stability-control intervention.
diagnostics.meaning: These effects can accompany normal system operation.
diagnostics.next: Establish a fault through diagnosis before deciding to replace the module.

verification.title: Confirm hydraulic and mechanical completion
verification.body: Confirm installation of new retainers, correct module-fastener tightening and completion of the HCU installation requirements.

verification.title: Record programming completion
verification.body: Confirm and record successful completion of the scan tool's PMI sequence, including any prompted As-Built Data steps.

procedures.purpose: Begin and complete ABS module PMI, separate the module from the HCU and install the replacement.
Remove and reinstall the hydraulic control unit as the prerequisite hydraulic phase of module replacement.

guides.title: Replace a front wheel speed sensor
guides.summary: Release the front sensor wiring, clean the sensor area and install the replacement in a cavity free of foreign material.
guides.introduction: A front wheel speed sensor provides wheel-rotation information used by the anti-lock braking system, or ABS, and stability control. These systems help control wheel locking and vehicle traction through braking and engine-torque intervention. Replacing the sensor involves its electrical connector, several harness retainers and a mounting bolt; it is not simply a matter of pulling the sensor from the wheel assembly.
guides.why: Cleaning before removal helps keep loose material out of the sensor opening. Inspecting the cavity before installing the replacement provides a clean mounting location. Restoring all harness retainers returns the wiring to its intended supported path around the wheel and suspension.
searchTerms: brake pedal pulsation during ABS operation

when.summary: After diagnosis identifies a front wheel speed sensor requiring replacement, or when related work requires removal.
notes: Brake pedal pulsation during ABS operation does not by itself establish a sensor fault.

prepare.title: Arrange safe wheel access
prepare.detail: Have the lifting and support capability required by the wheel-and-tire procedure. Be prepared to move the fender splash shield aside to reach the electrical connection.

prepare.title: Prepare cleaning and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Provide compressed air for cleaning around the sensor and a torque tool suitable for its mounting bolt. Identify the original harness routing before releasing its retainers.

steps.title: Expose the electrical connection
steps.body: Remove the wheel and tire using the linked procedure. Remove the splash-shield retainer and position the fender splash shield aside to reach the sensor wiring.

steps.title: Disconnect the first harness section
steps.body: Disconnect the front wheel speed sensor electrical connector and detach the two associated harness retainers. Free this section before working down toward the sensor.

steps.title: Clean around the installed sensor
steps.body: Use compressed air to clean the area surrounding the sensor while it is still installed. This precedes opening the sensor cavity.

steps.title: Remove the sensor
steps.body: Detach the two remaining sensor harness retainers shown near the wheel assembly. Remove the mounting bolt and the front wheel speed sensor.

steps.title: Inspect the cavity and install the replacement
steps.body: Before installing a new sensor, inspect the housing and make sure the cavity is clean and free of foreign material. Fit the sensor and tighten its mounting bolt to 133 lb.in (15 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the wiring and wheel
steps.body: Reverse the remaining removal operations. Reattach both groups of harness retainers, reconnect the electrical connector, restore the splash shield and its retainer, and reinstall the wheel and tire.

watchFor.title: Unsecured harness sections
watchFor.body: There are two separate pairs of harness retainers in the removal sequence. Restore both groups when routing the replacement sensor wiring.

watchFor.title: Foreign material in the cavity
watchFor.body: Do not install the new sensor until the housing inspection confirms a clean cavity.

notes: ABS and stability-control features vary with fitted equipment; sensor replacement does not establish which optional features a vehicle has.

diagnostics.finding: Noise or brake pedal pulsation during an ABS or stability-control event
diagnostics.meaning: These can be normal characteristics of system intervention.
diagnostics.next: Establish the actual fault through diagnosis before deciding to replace a sensor.

diagnostics.finding: Longer pedal travel immediately after an ABS or stability-control activation
diagnostics.meaning: The system description identifies this as a possible operating characteristic.
diagnostics.next: Consider the timing of the complaint during diagnosis rather than treating it as proof of sensor failure.

verification.title: Confirm physical installation
verification.body: Check sensor fastening, connector engagement, both pairs of harness retainers and splash-shield restoration. These checks confirm assembly; resolution of the original concern remains part of the applicable diagnostic work.

procedures.purpose: Front wheel speed sensor removal and installation, harness release, compressed-air cleaning and cavity inspection.
Required wheel-and-tire removal and installation for sensor access.
Explain ABS and stability-control functions and normal intervention characteristics relevant to the complaint.

guides.title: Replace a rear wheel speed sensor
guides.summary: Replace the rear wheel speed sensor after cleaning its surroundings, then restore its mounting, connector and harness retainers.
guides.introduction: The rear wheel speed sensor reports wheel rotation to the anti-lock brake system (ABS) and stability-control system. That information supports control of wheel locking, wheelspin and vehicle stability. The sensor is reached after removing the wheel and tire; its lead connects to the vehicle harness and is secured by two retainers.
guides.why: Cleaning before removal reduces the chance of loose dirt entering the sensor opening. The cavity must also be clean before a new sensor is installed. Restoring both harness retainers keeps the lead in its intended route beside the moving suspension, rather than leaving it hanging from the sensor or connector.
searchTerms: brake pedal pulsation during ABS operation

when.summary: After diagnosis establishes that a rear wheel speed sensor requires replacement.
notes: Normal ABS or stability-control sensations alone do not justify replacing a sensor.

prepare.title: Arrange wheel-removal access
prepare.detail: Use the linked wheel-and-tire procedure for supported access and refitting requirements.

prepare.title: Prepare cleaning and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have compressed air for the surrounding area, tools for the connector, retainers and mounting bolt, and torque equipment suitable for 80 lb.in (9 Nm).

steps.title: Remove the wheel and tire
steps.body: Follow the [wheel-and-tire procedure](#/document/G1686507) to expose the affected rear sensor and its harness route.

steps.title: Clean before opening the mounting
steps.body: Use compressed air to clean the area surrounding the rear wheel speed sensor while it remains installed. This removes loose contamination before the sensor cavity is exposed.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the sensor
steps.body: Follow the [rear sensor procedure](#/document/G1692582): disconnect the electrical connector, detach both harness retainers, then remove the mounting bolt and sensor. Freeing the harness first allows the assembly to be removed without pulling against its retained lead.

steps.title: Inspect the cavity and refit
steps.body: Before installing a new sensor, inspect the housing and ensure the cavity is clean and free of foreign material. Reverse removal, tightening the sensor bolt to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Restore both retainers, reconnect the electrical connector and reinstall the wheel and tire.

watchFor.title: Debris inside the housing
watchFor.body: Exterior cleaning does not replace the required cavity inspection before fitting the new sensor.

watchFor.title: Unsecured sensor lead
watchFor.body: Restore both retainers and the illustrated harness route during installation.

notes: The replacement sequence specifies mechanical refitting and cavity cleanliness; it does not prescribe a sensor calibration.

diagnostics.finding: Noise or pedal pulsation during ABS/stability operation, or increased pedal travel immediately afterward.
diagnostics.meaning: These can be normal system characteristics and do not establish a sensor fault.
diagnostics.next: Evaluate the reported condition through system diagnosis before selecting sensor replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Foreign material remains in the sensor cavity.
diagnostics.meaning: The required installation condition has not been met.
diagnostics.next: Remove the contamination before installing the new sensor.

verification.title: Confirm installation
verification.body: Check the mounting-bolt tightening, electrical reconnection, both harness retainers and completion of wheel installation.

verification.title: Record the physical checks
verification.body: Record that the cavity was clean before insertion and that the sensor fastening and harness restoration were completed.

procedures.purpose: Rear wheel speed sensor removal and installation, including cleaning, harness retainers and bolt torque.
Wheel and tire removal and installation for sensor access.

guides.title: Replace the stability and traction control switch through the SYNC front controls module
guides.summary: Service the integrated stability and traction control switch by removing the front controls module and configuring its replacement.
guides.introduction: The stability and traction control switch forms part of the Front Controls Interface Module (FCIM). Traction control helps limit drive-wheel spin during acceleration, while electronic stability control can apply braking and reduce engine torque to help control a skid. Servicing this switch therefore follows the FCIM replacement route, which involves console trim, electrical connections and vehicle-specific module configuration.
guides.why: The switch is integrated into a larger controls unit, so access and programming are central parts of the repair. Capturing the existing configuration before removing a module being replaced preserves the information that must be transferred into the new FCIM.

when.summary: When diagnosis or physical damage justifies servicing the integrated stability and traction control switch.
notes: A traction or stability-control complaint alone does not establish that the switch or FCIM needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange module-programming capability
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool capable of carrying out Programmable Module Installation (PMI). Configuration capture must happen before removal when fitting a new module.

prepare.title: Prepare for console and instrument-panel access
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover and suitable fastening tools available. Follow the installation details contained in the FCIM removal procedure, including its specified tightening torques.

steps.title: Begin the FCIM programming process
steps.body: Follow the scan tool's prompts to begin PMI before removing the module. If a new FCIM is being fitted, upload the existing configuration now so it can be downloaded after installation.

steps.title: Open the console access route
steps.body: Release the right-hand and left-hand console side panels with the interior trim remover. Remove the stowage mat and upper console bolts, then remove the selector bezel, move the boot aside and disconnect its electrical connector.

steps.title: Remove the upper console trim
steps.body: Open the console lid and remove the front retainers on both sides. Release the clips, move the gear-selector cover aside and remove the upper trim panel while disconnecting its electrical connections. Remove the stowage tray to continue access.

steps.title: Expose and remove the FCIM
