steps.body: Follow the instrument-panel center-finish-panel reference within the [FCIM procedure](#/document/G1704003). Remove the trim cover, then the FCIM bolts, and disconnect the module's electrical connectors. This is the component-removal route specified for the integrated switch.

steps.title: Refit the module and surrounding trim
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, reconnecting the FCIM and restoring the finish panel, tray, console trim and selector components. Apply the FCIM procedure's installation torques as each fastening stage is completed.

steps.title: Complete configuration when replacing the module
steps.body: For a replacement FCIM, finish PMI using the diagnostic scan tool and follow its prompts to download the configuration. The programming completion step is specifically required when replacing the component.

watchFor.title: Configuration not captured
watchFor.body: Removing the old module before uploading its configuration disrupts the stated replacement sequence. Resolve configuration capture before proceeding.

watchFor.title: Hidden electrical connections
watchFor.body: The selector area, upper console trim and FCIM each have electrical connections in the removal sequence. Release them as directed before taking the associated component away.

notes: The FCIM procedure illustrates an automatic transmission; it states that manual-transmission access is similar.

diagnostics.finding: Noise or brake-pedal pulsation occurs during an ABS or stability-control event.
diagnostics.meaning: These can be normal system effects; temporarily increased pedal travel can also follow intervention.
diagnostics.next: Do not use these effects alone to condemn the switch. Establish the actual control complaint before replacing the FCIM.

verification.title: Confirm programming completion
verification.body: For a new FCIM, confirm that the scan-tool PMI sequence completed and record the configuration-transfer result.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly
verification.body: Check that every disconnected connector, removed retainer and trim component has been restored through the reverse installation sequence.

procedures.purpose: Establishes that stability/traction switch removal and installation uses the FCIM service route.
Provides SYNC FCIM access, removal, installation, fastening details and replacement-module PMI requirements.

guides.title: Replace an outer tie rod end
guides.summary: Replace the outer tie rod end with a proper separator, renew its retaining nut and check front toe after reassembly.
guides.introduction: The outer tie rod end connects the steering linkage to the wheel spindle. It carries the steering rack’s push and pull to the wheel while its joint accommodates movement. Although this vehicle uses electric power-assisted steering, this connection remains mechanical. The outer end is separately serviceable, so replacing it does not require replacing the complete steering gear.
guides.why: Disconnecting the battery protects the steering gear during linkage work. A separator releases the joint without hammering the spindle, and recording the removal turns preserves a useful installation reference. That reference does not establish correct wheel alignment: front toe still needs checking.
searchTerms: front toe after tie rod replacement

when.summary: When the outer tie rod end has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Heavy steering alone does not establish that the outer tie rod end is faulty.

prepare.title: Arrange separation and alignment equipment
prepare.detail: Have a tie rod end remover, suitable torque equipment, safe wheel-removal capability and access to front-toe measurement and adjustment.

prepare.title: Identify the fastening specification
prepare.detail: Obtain a new outer tie rod end nut. The stud-nut torque has separate SVT and non-SVT build-date branches; select the applicable branch before reassembly.

steps.title: Isolate the steering system and remove the wheel
steps.body: Disconnect the battery ground cable using [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356). Then remove the wheel and tire using [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507). Battery disconnection is required whenever this steering linkage is serviced.

steps.title: Release the fasteners
steps.body: Follow the [tie rod end procedure](#/document/G1686682). Loosen the jam nut, which locks the threaded adjustment, then remove and discard the outer tie rod end nut.

steps.title: Separate the joint from the spindle
steps.body: Use the tie rod end remover to release the outer end from the wheel spindle. Position the tool carefully around the protective boot. Do not strike the spindle with a hammer.

steps.title: Record the threaded position
steps.body: Unscrew the outer tie rod end while counting and recording the turns required to remove it. Keep that record available for fitting the replacement.

steps.title: Install and secure the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, using the recorded turns as the installation reference. Reconnect the joint with a new retaining nut, applying the correct vehicle-specific torque, and tighten the jam nut to its specified torque.

steps.title: Restore access parts and check toe
steps.body: Refit the wheel and reconnect the battery through their procedures. Check front toe and adjust it if necessary using the Front Toe Adjustment procedure referenced from the tie rod article.

watchFor.title: Separator damage
watchFor.body: Poor tool placement can damage the outer joint’s boot. Hammering the spindle can damage the spindle itself.

watchFor.title: An apparently unchanged adjustment
watchFor.body: Matching the removal turns is only a starting reference; it does not replace the required toe measurement.

notes: Where selectable steering is fitted, battery disconnection returns its setting to Standard.

diagnostics.finding: Steering feels unusually heavy.
diagnostics.meaning: The electric assistance system can reduce or remove assistance in response to faults; heavy effort does not identify a failed outer joint.
diagnostics.next: Establish whether the concern involves the linkage or steering assistance before choosing this repair.

verification.title: Fasteners completed
verification.body: Confirm the discarded stud nut was replaced and both the stud nut and jam nut were tightened to their applicable specifications.

verification.title: Alignment result recorded
verification.body: Record the front-toe check and any adjustment made. Keep this result distinct from the recorded removal-turn count.

procedures.purpose: Outer tie rod end removal and installation, including fastener branches and the required front-toe follow-up.
Required battery ground disconnection and reconnection.
Wheel and tire removal and installation for access.

guides.title: Replace an inner tie rod and reseal the steering rack
guides.summary: Replace the inner tie rod while protecting the steering rack, fitting a new steering stop and restoring the airtight bellows seal.
guides.introduction: The inner tie rod connects the steering rack to the outer tie rod end, transmitting rack movement to the wheel while allowing the linkage to articulate. It is separately serviceable on the electric power-assisted steering system. This repair also renews the steering stop and protective bellows boot; those parts are essential to a successful replacement.
guides.why: Loosening or tightening the joint without holding the rack can damage the steering gear. The bellows seal matters just as much: steering movement can draw water and dirt through a poorly sealed boot, and water damages both the gear and the inner joint's grease.

when.summary: When an inner tie rod has been identified for replacement.
notes: For right-hand inner tie rod work, the left-hand outer tie rod end and bellows boot must also be removed to reach the rack-holding location.

prepare.title: Arrange rack-holding capability
prepare.detail: Use rack holding tool 204-816, a suitable crow's-foot or open-end wrench, and boot clamp pliers. Plan for the two-person operation shown in the illustration and access to the fitted underbody shields.

prepare.title: Have the replacement sealing parts ready
prepare.detail: Provide a new inner tie rod, steering stop, bellows boot and inner and outer clamps. Use Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-E1, specification ESA-M1C75-B, at the specified boot mating surfaces.

steps.title: Remove the outer tie rod end
steps.body: Follow the [Tie Rod End procedure](#/document/G1686682). For right-hand work, also arrange the left-side access described above; the holding tool cannot be used on the right side of the gear.

steps.title: Open the underbody access
steps.body: Remove the shields applicable to the vehicle using the [inner tie rod procedure](#/document/G1686681). Where a V-brace is fitted, the brace and shield can come off together without separating them.

steps.title: Expose the joint and position the rack
steps.body: Remove and discard both bellows clamps. Move the boot aside far enough to reach the inner joint, move the steering stop aside, and position the rack completely to the left.

steps.title: Hold the rack and remove the tie rod
steps.body: Secure the rack with tool 204-816 before applying loosening force. Reverse the tool for right-hand tie rod removal. Remove and discard the inner tie rod, then remove and discard the steering stop.

steps.title: Install the joint and seat the new stop
steps.body: Position the new steering stop and install the new inner tie rod with the rack securely held, again reversing the tool for right-hand work. Tighten to the specified torque. Press the stop into place by hand until it clicks and cannot be separated by hand.

steps.title: Restore the airtight boot seal
steps.body: Apply the specified grease to the steering gear's boot mating surface and the boot groove on the tie rod. Seat the new boot over the housing bead and rod groove. Install the new inner clamp with boot clamp pliers, then install the new outer clamp.

steps.title: Reassemble the linkage and access parts
steps.body: Thread the jam nut onto the inner tie rod. Refit the applicable V-brace and shields, observing their specified fastener tightening. Reinstall the outer tie rod end through its separate procedure.

watchFor.title: An apparently secure but leaking boot
watchFor.body: Zip ties do not provide the required airtight seal. Keep water out of the joint grease and use the specified new clamps.

watchFor.title: A stop that needs force
watchFor.body: Do not strike the steering stop. Hand pressure, an audible click and resistance to hand removal are the specified seating criteria.

notes: The rack holding tool always acts on the left-hand side, including when servicing the right-hand tie rod.

verification.title: Confirm stop seating
verification.body: After assembly, turn the steering wheel lock-to-lock to ensure the steering stops are fully seated.

verification.title: Confirm boot positioning
verification.body: Check that the new boot is correctly seated over both the steering gear housing bead and the inner tie rod groove, with both new clamps installed.

procedures.purpose: Complete inner tie rod removal and installation, including rack holding, steering stop replacement, bellows sealing and fitted shield branches.
Outer tie rod end removal and installation required for access and final reassembly.

guides.title: Rebond loose leather on the steering wheel
guides.summary: Prepare the exposed wheel surface and bond loose leather back into its original position with the specified gel adhesive.
guides.introduction: The steering wheel passes the driver's input into the steering-column shaft. Its leather covering forms the hand-contact surface, and a loose section can lift away from the wheel beneath it. This repair prepares the exposed attachment area and secures the leather in its original position, with smoothing and tucking to restore a neat finish.
guides.why: The repair depends on preparing the attachment surface, spreading the specified adhesive evenly and holding the leather in contact while the bond forms. Grooved areas must remain free of sanding and adhesive. Pulling on the repair to test it can disturb the bond, so the prescribed pressure and setting time matter.

when.summary: When a loose section of steering-wheel leather needs bonding back into its original position.
notes: Wheel removal is conditional: use the separate removal procedure if access requires it.

prepare.title: Obtain the specified adhesive
prepare.detail: Use Motorcraft Instant Gel Adhesive TA-19-C, specification WSS-M2G401-B5, and suitable sanding material for the exposed attachment area.

prepare.title: Plan access before applying adhesive
prepare.detail: Make sure the leather can be positioned, smoothed, tucked and held under pressure. If wheel removal is necessary, have the capability to complete [Steering Wheel removal and installation](#/document/G1693262), including its prerequisites.

steps.title: Expose the attachment area
steps.body: Remove the steering wheel only if necessary, using the linked procedure. Move the loose leather aside so the underlying area to be bonded is accessible.

steps.title: Prepare and coat the wheel
steps.body: Sand the area where the leather will be reattached, avoiding any grooved area. Apply the specified adhesive evenly to the wheel's attachment surface, again keeping it out of grooves.

steps.title: Restore the leather's position
steps.body: Return the loose leather to its original position. Smooth it and tuck it in for a neat appearance, then apply pressure for at least 30 seconds until it bonds to the wheel.

steps.title: Allow the bond to set
steps.body: The adhesive should be completely set after 5 minutes. Do not pull on the repair area. If the wheel was removed, reinstall it through the separate steering-wheel procedure after completing the bonding work.

watchFor.title: Grooves becoming part of the repair surface
watchFor.body: Both the sanding and adhesive instructions exclude grooved areas, where applicable. Keep preparation confined to the intended attachment area.

watchFor.title: Disturbing the leather during setting
watchFor.body: Arrange the leather before maintaining pressure, and avoid a pull test afterward.

notes: The specified pressure duration and setting time serve different purposes; holding the leather briefly does not replace the setting period.
A loose-cover repair does not establish a remedy for steering-column or shaft concerns.

verification.title: Inspect the finish without pulling
verification.body: Confirm the leather is in its original position, smoothed and neatly tucked. Check visually that the repaired area remains seated after the setting period.

verification.title: Complete conditional wheel installation
verification.body: If the wheel was removed, complete all installation requirements in the linked steering-wheel procedure.

procedures.purpose: Complete leather-cover bonding procedure, including adhesive specification, groove exclusions and setting requirements.
Conditional steering-wheel removal and installation when needed to access the leather repair.

guides.title: Replace the steering column coupling and check the lower shaft
guides.summary: Replace the coupling with the steering wheel restrained, renew the disconnected shaft bolts and complete the required lower-shaft collapsed check.
guides.introduction: The steering column coupling joins the lower steering shaft to the steering gear, completing the mechanical path from steering wheel movement to the gear. The lower shaft is collapsible and must be measured whenever it is disconnected from the upper shaft or coupling. Coupling replacement therefore includes a shaft-condition check as well as removal and installation.
guides.why: The dash seal must be loosened before working at the steering gear so the shaft is not forced against its mounting constraints. Hammering, prying or forcing the components can damage the steering connection. Restraining the wheel also protects the column's electrical components from rotation while the shaft system is disconnected.

when.summary: When a confirmed repair requires steering column coupling removal or replacement.
notes: Identify left-hand-drive or right-hand-drive configuration before selecting the lower-shaft bolt torque.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and wheel restraint
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and a steering wheel holding device, such as Hunter 28-75-1 or equivalent. Follow the lifting-point and hoist-clearance precautions; never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare hardware and inspection capability
prepare.detail: Have new bolts for both disconnected shaft connections, suitable torque equipment and access to the Steering Column Collapsed Check procedure. Do not estimate the lower shaft's acceptable condition by appearance alone.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle and restrain the wheel
steps.body: Place the vehicle in NEUTRAL and position it on the hoist. Set the steering wheel straight ahead and secure it with the holder. Keep it restrained throughout the period when the shaft connections are separated.

steps.title: Loosen the dash seal
steps.body: Following the [coupling procedure](#/document/G1725743), remove the dash-seal nuts, loosen the seal and hand-start the nuts again. Minimize damage to the sealer foam and avoid separating the seal brackets from their retainer pins.

steps.title: Separate the lower shaft from the coupling
steps.body: Remove and discard the lower-shaft connection bolt, then pull the shaft apart from the coupling without hammering or prying. The installation torque for this connection is 22 lb.ft (30 Nm) on left-hand-drive vehicles and 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm) on right-hand-drive vehicles.

steps.title: Remove the coupling from the steering gear
steps.body: Remove and discard the coupling-to-gear bolt, then pull the coupling away from the steering gear. Keep the dash seal loose during this work. Resistance must not be overcome by forcing the shaft or its universal joint.

steps.title: Install the coupling and restore the seal
steps.body: Reverse removal with new shaft bolts. Tighten the coupling-to-gear bolt to 22 lb.ft (30 Nm), and use the correct drive-side specification for the lower-shaft connection. Keep the seal loose until the connections are restored, then tighten its nuts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm).

steps.title: Complete the lower-shaft inspection
steps.body: Perform the [Steering Column Collapsed Check](#/document/G1721912). Disconnection itself makes this measurement necessary; completing the coupling installation does not establish that the collapsible shaft is within its required limits.

watchFor.title: Reusing a shaft bolt
watchFor.body: The removed shaft bolts must be discarded. Reuse can lead to fastener failure, shaft separation and loss of steering control.

watchFor.title: Damaging the dash seal
watchFor.body: Excessive foam or bracket damage can allow engine noise, fumes, air or water into the passenger compartment.

notes: The illustrated procedure shows left-hand drive; right-hand-drive work is similar but uses a different lower-shaft connection torque.

verification.title: Record the collapsed-check result
verification.body: Record the lower-shaft measurement and disposition required by the linked collapsed-check procedure before treating the repair as complete.

verification.title: Confirm connections and sealing
verification.body: Confirm both shaft connections use new, correctly tightened bolts and that the dash seal is restored without excessive foam or bracket damage.

procedures.purpose: Steering column coupling removal and installation, including drive-side torque differences and mandatory new bolts.
Safe lifting-point selection and hoist positioning.
Required lower steering shaft measurement after disconnection.

guides.title: Remove and refit the steering column lower shaft
guides.summary: Disconnect and reinstall the collapsible lower steering shaft using new bolts, then complete its required collapsed check.
guides.introduction: The lower steering shaft connects the upper column shaft to the coupling leading to the steering gear. It transmits steering-wheel movement and incorporates a collapsible section. Whenever either end is disconnected, the shaft must be measured using the collapsed-check procedure, even if it appears undamaged.
guides.why: Forcing this assembly can damage steering components. Allowing the disconnected column to rotate can damage its electrical components. Loosening the dash seal first, holding the wheel straight ahead and renewing the shaft bolts are essential parts of the repair.

when.summary: When lower-shaft removal or replacement is required; measure it after disconnection from either end.
notes: Select the correct left-hand-drive or right-hand-drive fastening branch.

prepare.title: Arrange safe access and wheel restraint
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the prescribed lifting points. Have a steering-wheel holding device, such as Hunter® 28-75-1 or equivalent, to maintain the straight-ahead position.

prepare.title: Prepare fasteners and inspection capability
prepare.detail: Have new shaft bolts, suitable torque tools and the Steering Column Collapsed Check procedure available. Its measurement and acceptance criteria are required to finish the job.

steps.title: Position the vehicle and hold the wheel
steps.body: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on the hoist using the [lifting procedure](#/document/G1663631). Secure the steering wheel straight ahead with the holding device. Maintain that position while the shaft system is disconnected.

steps.title: Loosen the dash seal before separating the shaft
steps.body: Follow the [lower-shaft procedure](#/document/G1721916) to loosen the dash seal and remove its nuts. Loosen the seal as directed, then hand-start the nuts. Minimize damage to the sealer foam and keep the dash-seal brackets attached to their retainer pins.

steps.title: Remove and discard the shaft bolts
steps.body: Remove the common shaft bolt and the applicable left-hand-drive or right-hand-drive bolt. Discard the removed bolts; they must not be reused. The handedness branches are alternatives, not instructions to remove an additional bolt from every vehicle.

steps.title: Separate the shaft without force
steps.body: Pull the lower shaft apart from the coupling, then from the upper steering shaft. Do not hammer, pry or force the assembly. If separation is resisted, check that the dash seal and its fasteners have been loosened before proceeding.

steps.title: Refit with new bolts
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence while keeping the dash seal loose for shaft engagement. Use new shaft bolts. The common bolt is tightened to 22 lb.ft (30 Nm); the handedness-specific bolt uses 22 lb.ft (30 Nm) on left-hand-drive vehicles or 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm) on right-hand-drive vehicles. Restore the dash seal and tighten its nuts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm).

steps.title: Complete the collapsed check
steps.body: Inspect and measure the lower shaft using [Steering Column Collapsed Check](#/document/G1721912). Follow that procedure’s decision criteria before returning the steering system to service; visual appearance alone does not complete this check.

watchFor.title: Damaged dash sealing
watchFor.body: Excessive foam or bracket damage can allow engine noise, fumes, air or water into the passenger compartment.

watchFor.title: Column rotation or forced engagement
watchFor.body: Keep the wheel restrained and stop if assembly requires hammering, levering or force.

notes: The illustration shows left-hand drive; use the right-hand-drive branch where applicable.
Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

diagnostics.finding: The lower shaft has been disconnected from the upper shaft or coupling
diagnostics.meaning: A collapsed-shaft measurement is required.
diagnostics.next: Complete the specified check regardless of whether replacement was initially planned.

verification.title: Confirm fastening and sealing
verification.body: Confirm new shaft bolts were fitted using the correct handedness branch and that the dash seal and its fasteners are restored.

verification.title: Record the measured result
verification.body: Record the collapsed-check measurement and the resulting decision against the linked procedure’s criteria.

procedures.purpose: Lower steering shaft removal and installation, including handedness-specific fasteners.
Vehicle lifting points and support precautions.
Required lower-shaft inspection and measurement after disconnection.

guides.title: Replace the steering column upper shaft
guides.summary: Replace the upper steering shaft while preserving steering-wheel position, renewing the shaft bolts and checking the collapsible lower shaft.
guides.introduction: The upper steering shaft carries steering-wheel movement from the column to the lower shaft, which connects toward the steering gear. This repair opens that mechanical connection and disturbs the seal where the shaft passes through the dash. It also requires driver knee airbag removal, so the work combines steering repair with restraint-system access.
guides.why: Holding the wheel stationary protects the column’s electrical components while the shafts are disconnected. New shaft bolts are essential because reused bolts can fail and allow separation. The lower shaft is collapsible and must be measured whenever disconnected; simply reconnecting it does not establish that its length remains correct.

when.summary: When the upper steering shaft requires replacement following inspection or other established repair findings.
notes: The illustrations show left-hand drive; the right-hand-drive procedure is similar.
Plan for the lower-shaft collapsed check whenever the upper and lower shafts are separated.

prepare.title: Secure access and steering position
prepare.detail: Arrange a hoist, a steering-wheel holder and suitable torque tools. Use the designated lifting points and never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Have the required parts and capabilities
prepare.detail: Obtain new steering shaft bolts. Arrange competent restraint-system work and follow the complete driver knee airbag procedure, including its safety prerequisites.

steps.title: Position the vehicle and hold the wheel
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on the hoist. Keep the steering wheel straight ahead using the holding device, then move the column fully upward and rearward. Maintain wheel restraint throughout shaft disconnection.

steps.title: Release the dash seal carefully
steps.body: Follow the dash-seal sequence in the upper-shaft procedure: loosen the seal, remove its nuts, free the seal further and hand-start the nuts again. Preserve the foam and keep the seal brackets attached to their retainer pins.

steps.title: Partially separate the lower connection
steps.body: Remove and discard the bolt connecting the upper and lower shafts. Partially pull the shafts apart to loosen the connection. Do not hammer, pry or force either shaft.

steps.title: Remove the upper shaft
steps.body: Remove the driver knee airbag using its linked procedure. Remove the upper-shaft retaining nuts and discard the column-end shaft bolt. Pull the upper shaft away from the steering column, then separate it from the lower shaft and remove it.

steps.title: Reconnect the column end
steps.body: Install the upper shaft and connect it to the steering column. Fit a new bolt and tighten it to 22 lb.ft (30 Nm). Seat the dash seal and hand-start its nuts.

steps.title: Secure the lower connection and seal
steps.body: Connect the upper shaft to the lower shaft using a new bolt, tightened to 22 lb.ft (30 Nm). Tighten the dash-seal nuts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Restore the driver knee airbag through its complete installation procedure.

steps.title: Check the collapsible lower shaft
steps.body: Perform the linked Steering Column Collapsed Check. Use that procedure’s measurement and acceptance criteria before considering the steering repair complete.

watchFor.title: A joint that needs force
watchFor.body: Hammering, prying or forcing the column or shafts can damage steering components and compromise steering control.

watchFor.title: Damaged seal foam or displaced brackets
watchFor.body: Excessive damage can admit engine noise, fumes, air or water into the passenger compartment.

notes: Keep the steering column from rotating whenever its shaft system is disconnected.

verification.title: Connections and sealing
verification.body: Confirm both shaft connections contain new, correctly tightened bolts and the dash seal is seated with its nuts tightened.

verification.title: Record the lower-shaft result
verification.body: Record the collapsed-check measurement and its acceptance result using the linked procedure.

procedures.purpose: Complete upper steering shaft removal and installation, including new bolts and dash-seal handling.
Identify approved lifting points and hoist precautions.
Remove and reinstall the driver knee airbag with the required restraint-system precautions.
Measure and assess the collapsible lower shaft after disconnection.

guides.title: Remove and replace the steering column
guides.summary: Depower the restraints, remove the column without shaft rotation or force, and install it with new specified fasteners.
guides.introduction: The steering column supports the steering-wheel shaft in bearings and connects it through the upper and lower shafts to the steering gear. Removing it also involves electrical connections, the steering column control module (SCCM) and the driver knee airbag. Replacement requires a new column because its precise construction is essential to steering integrity.
guides.why: Uncontrolled rotation can damage the clockspring and column electrical components. Hammering, prying or forcing the column can damage steering parts, while reused shaft bolts can fail and allow separation. Correct restraint-system handling and careful fastening are therefore central parts of this repair.
searchTerms: security pack steering column lock transfer

when.summary: When an established repair requires column removal or replacement.
notes: Use a new replacement column; repaired, rebuilt, aftermarket and remanufactured columns are prohibited.
The security-pack lock-module transfer applies only when installing a new component.

prepare.title: Arrange the required capability
prepare.detail: The work requires competence with supplemental restraint system (SRS) depowering, airbag removal and steering assembly. Use the linked procedures for those phases.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement fasteners
prepare.detail: Obtain new column-shaft and column-mounting bolts. Keep the different front and rear mounting fasteners identified, and have suitable torque-control equipment.

prepare.title: Protect the removed column
prepare.detail: Retain the original box and upper and lower packing foams for protection against shipping damage.

steps.title: Center the wheels and depower the restraints
steps.body: Set the front wheels straight ahead to protect the clockspring. Depower the SRS through its complete linked procedure before beginning the airbag-related work.

steps.title: Select the correct control-module branch
steps.body: For a new column, remove the SCCM using its procedure. When a new component is not being installed, remove the column shrouds, disconnect the SCCM harness connectors, detach its pin-type retainer and position the harness aside.

steps.title: Remove the knee airbag and free the wiring
steps.body: Remove the driver knee airbag through its linked procedure. Move the column fully up and rearward, then remove the retainers and disconnect the column electrical connectors. The illustrated electronic-lock arrangement has a similar removal sequence on vehicles without that lock.

steps.title: Separate the upper shaft
steps.body: Prevent column rotation while the shaft system is disconnected. Remove and discard the shaft bolt, then separate the upper steering column shaft from the column. Do not hammer, pry or force the connection.

steps.title: Release the column mountings
steps.body: Support the column and follow the illustrated mounting-bolt removal stages. Remove and discard both groups of mounting bolts, then remove the column. Preserve identification of the front and rear locations because their fasteners are not interchangeable.

steps.title: Complete the security-pack branch
steps.body: With the security pack, remove the steering column lock module using its linked procedure only when installing a new component. Protect the removed column with its original box and packing foams when preparing it for shipping.

steps.title: Reassemble with new fasteners
steps.body: Reverse the applicable removal sequence without forcing the column or shafts. Tighten new mounting bolts in their correct locations to 25 Nm and the new shaft bolt to 30 Nm. For a new column, remove the anti-rotation pin and spindle bolt only after the steering system is fully assembled. Complete the referenced module and restraint installation requirements.

watchFor.title: Rotation while disconnected
watchFor.body: Keep the column from turning throughout shaft separation and reassembly; the straight-ahead starting position alone does not prevent later rotation.

watchFor.title: Fasteners that look similar
watchFor.body: Front and rear mounting bolts must remain in their specified positions even though their tightening torques are the same.

notes: Left-hand-drive illustrations also describe the similar right-hand-drive arrangement.

diagnostics.finding: Additional work disconnects the lower shaft from the upper shaft or coupling
diagnostics.meaning: The lower shaft is collapsible and must be measured after either disconnection.
diagnostics.next: Complete the applicable lower-shaft measurement procedure before treating that additional shaft work as finished.

verification.title: Record the fastening result
verification.body: Confirm and record new shaft and mounting bolts, correct front/rear locations and completed tightening.

verification.title: Confirm final assembly
verification.body: For a new column, confirm the anti-rotation pin and spindle bolt were removed after full steering assembly. Finish the referenced SRS return-to-service requirements before releasing the vehicle.

procedures.purpose: Steering column removal and installation, including replacement branches, new fasteners and final anti-rotation restraint removal.
Required SRS depowering before the column and airbag work.
SCCM removal and installation when installing a new column.
Column-shroud removal and installation for the existing-component access branch.
Driver knee airbag removal and installation.
Security-pack steering column lock module removal and installation for a new column.
Explain the column and shaft arrangement and the conditional lower-shaft measurement requirement.

guides.title: Remove and Refit the Steering Wheel
guides.summary: Remove the steering wheel after completing the driver-airbag procedure, preserve the clockspring position, and refit the wheel to its specified torque.
guides.introduction: The steering wheel turns a shaft supported by bearings inside the steering column. The column shafts carry that movement to the steering gear. Removing the wheel exposes the clockspring behind it and requires disconnecting the wheel-switch wiring. The driver airbag must come off first, making restraint-system work an essential prerequisite even though the wheel itself has a short removal sequence.
guides.why: The clockspring rotor must stay in its established position while the steering wheel is absent. Starting with the front wheels straight ahead and securing the rotor prevents accidental movement that could damage the clockspring. Correct bolt tightening secures the wheel to the steering shaft.

when.summary: When the steering wheel needs replacement or removal for access to another repair.
notes: The illustrated arrangement is left-hand drive; right-hand drive follows a similar procedure.

prepare.title: Arrange the airbag prerequisite
prepare.detail: Have the capability to complete the linked Driver Airbag removal and installation procedure, including its restraint-system precautions. These wheel instructions do not replace that procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare for controlled removal
prepare.detail: Have tape for securing the clockspring rotor, suitable bolt tools, and a torque wrench capable of 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm). Establish the straight-ahead front-wheel position before removal.

steps.title: Set the wheels straight and remove the airbag
steps.body: Make sure the front wheels are straight ahead. Complete [Driver Airbag removal](#/document/G1696301) before working on the wheel connector or central bolt.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the wheel
steps.body: Disconnect the steering-wheel switches electrical connector. Remove the central steering-wheel bolt and then the wheel, following [Steering Wheel removal and installation](#/document/G1693262).

steps.title: Secure the clockspring
steps.body: Tape the clockspring rotor to its outer housing to keep it from rotating while the wheel is removed. Preserve that position throughout the remaining work.

steps.title: Refit in reverse order
steps.body: Remove the retaining tape without disturbing the rotor position, install the steering wheel and tighten its bolt to 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm). Reconnect the wheel-switch connector, then reinstall the driver airbag using its dedicated procedure.

watchFor.title: Clockspring movement
watchFor.body: If the rotor turns or its position becomes uncertain, resolve the alignment before continuing. Do not guess at a replacement position.

watchFor.title: Incomplete airbag work
watchFor.body: The job remains unfinished until the driver airbag has been reinstalled through its complete procedure.

notes: Keep the straight-ahead setup and clockspring restraint intact during any work performed while the wheel is off.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly
verification.body: Confirm the rotor restraint has been removed, the wheel-switch connector is reconnected, and driver-airbag installation is complete.

verification.title: Record bolt tightening
verification.body: Record that the steering-wheel bolt was tightened to 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm).

procedures.purpose: Steering-wheel removal and installation, including clockspring restraint and central-bolt tightening.
Required driver-airbag removal before wheel removal and reinstallation after the wheel is secured.

guides.title: Diagnose push-button ignition and steering-column electrical faults
guides.summary: Separate start-button, indicator, supply-voltage and steering-lock concerns using the appropriate module tests and circuit checks.
guides.introduction: The START/STOP button contains two contacts that signal the body control module (BCM), which selects ignition mode and operates the run/start relay. The button and its indicator belong to the front controls interface module (FCIM); the button cannot be serviced separately. The steering column control module (SCCM) handles column and wheel controls. This diagnosis distinguishes their electrical faults from battery, wiring, key-recognition and configuration problems.
guides.why: A module can lose functions because its supply is unsuitable or its connections are poor. Checking those conditions first prevents a stored fault or an unresponsive button from becoming an unsupported parts diagnosis.

when.summary: Use when ignition-mode, indicator or column-lock operation is incorrect, or relevant module fault codes are recorded.
notes: Apply steering-lock checks only where an electronic steering-column lock is fitted.
Component replacement decisions require the concern to be present, except where the particular test explicitly addresses a historical code.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, specified terminal probes, fused jumper wires and the prescribed test lamp. Live measurements and connector isolation require experience with Ford diagnostic methods and vehicle-specific wiring diagrams.

prepare.title: Establish reliable starting conditions
prepare.detail: Inspect battery cables, wiring, connectors and relevant fuses; check previous repairs and applicable technical service bulletins. Verify battery state of charge exceeds 70% and resolve charging concerns before ignition diagnosis. Follow each step's ignition and disconnection instructions.

steps.title: Route the actual complaint
steps.body: Read codes across modules and diagnose circuit faults before performance faults. Use the charts in the linked diagnostic procedure: lighting, wiper, cruise, message-center and audio switch faults belong to their respective systems. A key-not-detected message leads to passive anti-theft system (PATS) diagnosis.

steps.title: Test A: investigate no power in ON
steps.body: Check battery condition first. B108A:01, B108A:24 or B1142:29 then directs testing to the button inputs. Otherwise follow the indicator and key-recognition checks. Monitor START_STOP_1 and START_STOP_2 parameter identification (PID) data while operating the button. Follow the corresponding short, open, supply, ground and prescribed fused-bypass tests to distinguish wiring from FCIM or BCM concerns. During the no-power complaint, continuous indicator flashing leads to instrument-panel-cluster/BCM network testing, the run/start fuse check and examination of communication codes across modules.

steps.title: Tests B and C: distinguish indicator failures
steps.body: For an inoperative indicator, Test B starts with the engine running: adequate indicator-feed voltage leads to FCIM checks; insufficient voltage leads through short-to-ground and continuity tests toward wiring or BCM checks. For an always-on indicator, Test C isolates the BCM. Continued illumination leads to a short-to-voltage check, then FCIM checks if no stray voltage exists; extinguishing leads to BCM checks.

steps.title: Test D: establish the steering-lock complaint and test entry
steps.body: Confirm operation against the lock/unlock conditions and inspect the specified lock fuse. B1026:87 concerns missing messages; B1026:92 concerns messages received while the relay is not activated. B1184:11 and B1184:15 concern relay-control shorts or an open. These observations do not independently authorize replacement. Within an established test branch, D3–D6 assess relay-coil ground/control; D8–D14 assess supply, switched feeds, module ground and local interconnect network (LIN) wiring. D7 uses temporary known-good relay substitution and requires its removal afterward. If entry to the applicable branch is unconfirmed, stop before performing its tests or authorizing relay/module replacement.

steps.title: Test E: investigate SCCM low supply voltage
steps.body: Clear B11D9:16 and repeat the SCCM self-test. If it returns, check powertrain-control-module charging codes, then battery condition and full charge. Record battery voltage and compare VBAT_SCCM with it using the specified 0.2 volt tolerance. A mismatch leads to supply and ground checks; agreement leads to connector/module checks. Disconnect the negative battery cable before the specified ground-resistance measurement to avoid false readings.

steps.title: Test F: investigate SCCM high supply voltage
steps.body: For B11D9:17, first check other modules for charging or high-voltage codes. With lights and accessories off, monitor battery voltage while running the engine at approximately 2,000 rpm for 3 minutes. A rise to 16.5 volts or higher requires overcharging diagnosis. Otherwise cycle the ignition, clear SCCM codes and repeat its self-test; a returning code reaches the SCCM replacement decision.

steps.title: Test G: trace the run/start input
steps.body: P2533:14 means body control module B (BCMB) detected no run/start-input voltage during its self-test. Check the disconnected BCMB input as directed. Voltage above 11 volts leads to BCMB connector checks. Insufficient voltage leads to continuity testing back to the BCM: a failed circuit needs repair, while satisfactory continuity leads to BCM checks.

steps.title: Resolve connections before module decisions
steps.body: At the relevant endpoint, inspect connectors for corrosion, bent or damaged pins and pushed-out terminals. Replace affected terminals/connectors, clean module pins, reconnect securely and retest. Follow applicable technical service bulletins first. Persistent FCIM/BCM concerns require the vehicle identification number-specific guided routine; SCCM/BCMB replacement follows only the corresponding completed diagnostic branch.

watchFor.title: Normal flashing mistaken for a fault
watchFor.body: The indicator normally flashes with ignition ON and the engine stopped, stays illuminated with the engine running and goes out in OFF.

watchFor.title: Mechanical load on a fitted lock
watchFor.body: “Turn the wheel while starting” can indicate torque against the lock. Follow the prescribed wheel-load relief sequence before treating it as an electrical failure.

watchFor.title: Damaged test connections
watchFor.body: Use the specified probe adapters and only the directed fused bypasses. Improvised power or ground connections can damage components.

notes: The BCM withholds steering-lock power while the engine runs or the vehicle moves; account for this when assessing lock operation.
A replacement electronic steering lock requires BCM-to-lock configuration/training. This guide ends at diagnosis and the appropriate repair or programming procedure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1240:15 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The indicator circuit may be open or shorted to battery voltage.
diagnostics.next: Choose Test B for an inoperative indicator or Test C for an always-on indicator. B1240:11 instead identifies a short-to-ground concern for Test B.

diagnostics.finding: B11D9:16 or B11D9:17 does not return during its prescribed retest
diagnostics.meaning: The event may be historical: battery discharge for the low-voltage code, or charging/jump-starting for the high-voltage code.
diagnostics.next: Record the normal retest result; do not infer SCCM failure from the stored code alone.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U2100:00 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: Initial module configuration is incomplete.
diagnostics.next: After recent module work, repeat programmable module installation as directed by the scan tool. Without recent work, the chart directs SCCM replacement for failure to retain configuration.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U2101:00 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: Steering-wheel switch functions do not match SCCM configuration.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the SCCM and switches against the parts catalog and correct mismatched components.

diagnostics.finding: B1026:05, B1026:51 or B1026:56 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The fitted steering lock has a programming or configuration concern.
diagnostics.next: Follow BCM-to-lock training. Use the exact chart route for other lock codes; B1026:04 and B1026:93 require other recorded faults to be diagnosed first.

verification.title: Recheck the affected function
verification.body: Restore disconnected connectors and the battery connection as directed, verify secure latching and repeat the complaint check. Perform the prescribed SCCM self-tests for voltage faults.

verification.title: Retain the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record battery voltage, its comparison with VBAT_SCCM where applicable, circuit findings and whether codes returned. If connector work restored operation, identify and address the connection's underlying fault.

procedures.purpose: Primary DTC charts and Tests A–G for the listed engine variants; steering-lock branches require confirmed entry.
Electrical testing capability, probe selection, circuit isolation and module-diagnosis prerequisites.
Ignition indicator states, button operation and fitted steering-lock operating conditions.
PATS diagnosis when key recognition prevents ignition operation.
Network diagnosis when Test A identifies communication concerns.
Battery disconnect/connect procedure required during Test E.
Scan-tool configuration/training for the fitted electronic steering lock.
Separate SCCM removal and installation after a supported replacement decision.
Separate BCMB removal and installation after completing its diagnostic branch.

guides.title: Replace the Steering Column Control Module
guides.summary: Remove and refit the steering column control module, beginning and completing scan-tool configuration when installing a new unit.
guides.introduction: The steering column control module (SCCM) connects steering-column and steering-wheel switch inputs with other vehicle systems over the High Speed Controller Area Network 2 (HS2-CAN). These inputs include lighting, wiper and fitted steering-wheel controls. Replacement therefore involves electrical configuration as well as removing the assembly from the column.
guides.why: For a new module, programmable module installation (PMI) must begin while the current SCCM is still installed. Removing it first disrupts the prescribed configuration sequence. If it cannot communicate, the scan tool may request As-Built Data. The electrical connectors, screw retainers and retaining clip also need separate release steps; pulling the assembly before releasing them risks damage.

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies SCCM replacement, or other work requires its removal and refitting.
notes: Switch symptoms alone do not establish that the SCCM needs replacement.
Left-hand drive is illustrated; right-hand drive is similar.

prepare.title: Configuration capability
prepare.detail: For a new component, have a compatible diagnostic scan tool and access to the As-Built Data if the tool requests it. Keep the current SCCM installed until the initial PMI stage has been performed.

prepare.title: Steering-wheel and trim access
prepare.detail: Be equipped to follow the complete steering-wheel removal procedure, including its safety prerequisites, and the column-shroud procedure. Have suitable connector-release tools and torque equipment for the module retainers.

steps.title: Start configuration if fitting a new module
steps.body: With the current SCCM still installed, begin PMI using the diagnostic scan tool and follow its prompts. If the module does not respond, follow any request for As-Built Data. This stage is only required when installing a new component.

steps.title: Remove the access components
steps.body: Remove the [Steering Wheel](#/document/G1693262), then the [Steering Column Shrouds](#/document/G1692617). Complete the prerequisites in those procedures before reaching the module.

steps.title: Release the electrical connections
steps.body: Following [SCCM Removal and Installation](#/document/G1693270), detach the retainer and disconnect the clockspring electrical connector. Then disconnect the SCCM electrical connector.

steps.title: Release the module from the column
steps.body: Remove the module retainers, pull the SCCM retaining clip and remove the assembly from the steering column. The clip is a separate release operation after the retainers are removed.

steps.title: Reassemble the column
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure. Secure the module retainers to 27 lb.in (3 Nm), restore both electrical connections and the detached retainer, then reinstall the shrouds and steering wheel using their procedures.

steps.title: Finish new-module configuration
steps.body: If a new SCCM was installed, complete PMI with the diagnostic scan tool, following all on-screen instructions. An existing module being refitted does not invoke the procedure’s new-component PMI steps.

watchFor.title: Starting removal before PMI
watchFor.body: The current module must remain installed for the beginning of the new-module PMI process, even when communication may be unavailable.

watchFor.title: Confusing control and lock modules
watchFor.body: The SCCM interfaces with switches. The electronic steering-column lock is a separate system with its own module and configuration requirements.

notes: Apply functional checks to the controls actually fitted to the vehicle; the overview describes several possible steering-wheel functions.

diagnostics.finding: The current SCCM does not respond during PMI setup.
diagnostics.meaning: The scan tool may need As-Built Data to continue the replacement process; nonresponse is not itself a complete fault diagnosis.
diagnostics.next: Follow the tool’s prompts before proceeding with module removal.

diagnostics.finding: The original SCCM is being reinstalled.
diagnostics.meaning: The configuration instructions are explicitly conditional on installing a new component.
diagnostics.next: Complete reverse installation without treating the new-module PMI steps as unconditional.

verification.title: Confirm assembly security
verification.body: Confirm the retaining clip, retainers, clockspring connector and SCCM connector are restored and the access-component procedures are complete.

verification.title: Record configuration completion
verification.body: For a new module, record the scan tool’s completed PMI result and whether As-Built Data was required.

verification.title: Check the affected controls
verification.body: Confirm operation of the relevant fitted lighting, wiper and steering-wheel controls through their normal operating checks.

procedures.purpose: SCCM removal and installation, including conditional pre-removal and post-installation PMI.
Steering-wheel removal and installation with its access and safety prerequisites.
Steering-column shroud removal and installation.
Identify the column and steering-wheel controls that interface through the SCCM.

guides.title: Replace and configure the steering column lock module
guides.summary: Replace the steering column lock module with new retaining fasteners, then complete the configuration and training required for a new module.
guides.introduction: The steering column lock module (SCLM) secures the steering column to deter theft. The body control module (BCM) commands it to lock or unlock through a local interconnect network (LIN), and the lock module reports its position and faults. Replacement involves both mechanical access beneath the column and electronic configuration: fitting the new unit alone does not make it ready to operate.
guides.why: A lock fault can prevent starting, but mechanical load against the lock can also stop it releasing. Establish the cause before replacement. A new module must receive the correct configuration through the existing BCM; missing configuration can leave the column locked and the vehicle unable to start.

when.summary: When diagnosis establishes that the steering column lock module needs replacement or removal.
notes: A steering-lock message or no-start condition alone does not establish that the module needs replacing.

prepare.title: Arrange configuration capability before removal
prepare.detail: For a new module, the scan tool must capture the BCM configuration before removal and return it to the same BCM afterward. Confirm access to programmable module installation (PMI) and electronic steering column lock (ESCL) training.

prepare.title: Prepare for airbag and column access
prepare.detail: Have the driver-knee-airbag and column-shroud procedures available. Airbag removal requires the appropriate restraint-service capability and all preparation and restoration specified by that procedure.

prepare.title: Workshop capability
prepare.detail: Diagnostic scan tool with programmable module installation and steering-lock training capability; spherical cutter; flat-bladed screwdriver; new break-away retaining fasteners; driver-knee-airbag service capability.

steps.title: Capture the configuration
steps.body: When installing a new lock module, begin PMI for the BCM with the diagnostic scan tool before removing the module. Follow the on-screen instructions to upload the configuration that will establish the new lock's relationship with the vehicle.

steps.title: Expose the lock module
steps.body: Remove the driver knee airbag using its dedicated procedure, then remove the steering column shrouds. This provides access to the module, its wiring and its retaining fasteners.

steps.title: Release the wiring
steps.body: Release the retainers and detach the lock-module electrical connectors as shown in the removal procedure. Free the retained wiring before moving the module.

steps.title: Remove the security fasteners
steps.body: On both sides, use the spherical cutter to cut a slot in the lock-module bolt. Use the flat-bladed screwdriver to remove the retainers, discard them and remove the module. These break-away fasteners must not be reused.

steps.title: Install and restore access components
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence using new retaining fasteners. Tighten each break-away bolt until its hex head separates, following the installation details. Reconnect the wiring and restore the shrouds and knee airbag through their respective procedures.

steps.title: Configure and train a new module
steps.body: Complete BCM PMI, downloading the saved information back into the same BCM. Then carry out the BCM-to-ESCL configuration/training in the anti-theft key programming procedure. Both operations are required when the lock module is replaced.

watchFor.title: Steering load mistaken for failure
watchFor.body: Wheels resting against a curb can load the lock enough to prevent unlocking.

watchFor.title: Installation without training
watchFor.body: A physically installed but unconfigured module can retain the steering lock and set programming or configuration faults.

notes: The illustrated vehicle is left-hand drive; the procedure identifies right-hand-drive removal as similar.
Configuration capture, PMI completion, ESCL training and the specified BCM fault-code check apply when installing a new component.

diagnostics.finding: “Turn the wheel while starting” appears.
diagnostics.meaning: The lock may be unable to release because of torque applied to the steering column.
diagnostics.next: Turn the vehicle off, rotate and hold the wheel in one direction while turning the vehicle on. If the message returns, repeat while holding the wheel in the other direction.

diagnostics.finding: “Steering Malfunction” appears.
diagnostics.meaning: The electronic steering-lock system has detected a fault; this does not by itself identify the failed component.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose the system before proceeding with module replacement.

verification.title: Confirm the electronic result
verification.body: After new-module configuration and training, run the BCM self-test. Clear the diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), retrieve them again and record whether all codes have cleared.

verification.title: Check normal lock behavior
verification.body: Confirm unlocking through a supported entry or valid-key start request. Assess locking against the normal delayed-accessory sequence described in the system-operation procedure; locking is not immediate when the ignition is switched off.

procedures.purpose: Complete SCLM removal, new-fastener installation, BCM PMI and post-replacement checks.
Driver knee airbag removal and installation for safe module access.
Steering column shroud removal and restoration.
BCM-to-ESCL configuration and training after lock-module replacement.
Normal steering-lock operation, timing and message interpretation.

guides.title: Replace the left steering-column lighting switch
guides.summary: Remove the steering-column shrouds and replace the left multifunction switch while protecting its terminals and trim retainers.
guides.introduction: The left multifunction switch is the steering-column stalk used for the turn signals, low/high-beam selection and flash-to-pass. It mounts on the left side of the steering column control module (SCCM), through which the column switches communicate with other vehicle systems. Replacement changes the switch itself after the surrounding upper and lower shrouds have been removed.
guides.why: Most of the access work involves releasing concealed trim tabs in a particular order. Adjusting the column and rotating the steering wheel provide access to those tabs. At the switch, the main precaution is protecting the component terminals: bent or damaged terminals can compromise the connection even when the replacement is mechanically secure.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the left steering-column multifunction switch needs replacement.
notes: A lighting complaint alone does not establish that the stalk has failed.
The procedures show left-hand drive; right-hand-drive access is similar.

prepare.title: Prepare trim and fastener tools
prepare.detail: Use an interior trim remover and a flat-bladed screwdriver for the specified shroud releases. Have suitable tools for the shroud screws and a torque tool capable of the switch’s low setting.

prepare.title: Understand the access boundary
prepare.detail: The switch procedure requires removal of the column shrouds. Its illustration omits the steering wheel for clarity; wheel removal is not a listed step.

steps.title: Position the column and release the gap hider
steps.body: Fully extend and lower the steering column. Following [Steering Column Shrouds](#/document/G1692617), use the interior trim remover to release the upper gap-hider tabs, disconnect it from the upper shroud and position it aside.

steps.title: Remove the upper and lower shrouds
steps.body: Release the upper-shroud tabs. Rotate the steering wheel 90 degrees and release the accessible tab with the flat-bladed screwdriver, then rotate it 180 degrees and release the other tab. Release the outer clips on both sides and remove the upper shroud. Remove the lower-shroud screws and lower shroud.

steps.title: Remove the left multifunction switch
steps.body: Remove the switch retainers and withdraw the left switch using [Steering Column Multifunction Switch LH](#/document/G1693271). Protect the component terminals throughout removal.

steps.title: Install the replacement switch
steps.body: Reverse the switch removal sequence, making sure its terminals are not bent or damaged as it is fitted. Tighten the retainers to 9 lb.in (1 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the column trim
steps.body: Reverse the shroud removal procedure. Refit the lower shroud and screws, engage the upper shroud’s clips and tabs, and reconnect the upper gap hider. Correct engagement restores the trim around the stalk.

watchFor.title: Terminal damage
watchFor.body: Do not force the switch into position if its terminals are misaligned or damaged.

watchFor.title: A shroud that remains attached
watchFor.body: Check the specified tab and clip releases before pulling harder. The steering-wheel rotations are part of gaining access.

notes: The attached illustration shows the upper-shroud access stage.

diagnostics.finding: Turn signals, beam selection or flash-to-pass do not respond correctly.
diagnostics.meaning: These functions use the left multifunction switch and its connection through the SCCM, but the symptom does not isolate the switch.
diagnostics.next: Establish the fault before using this replacement procedure.

verification.title: Confirm the mechanical installation
verification.body: Check the switch retainers, terminal condition and engagement of the shrouds and gap hider.

verification.title: Check the switch functions
verification.body: Check turn-signal control, low/high-beam selection and flash-to-pass after reassembly.

procedures.purpose: Left multifunction switch removal and installation, including terminal protection and retainer torque.
Required upper and lower steering-column shroud removal and refitting for switch access.

guides.title: Replace the Right Steering-Column Wiper and Washer Switch
guides.summary: Remove the steering-column shrouds and replace the right multifunction switch while protecting its electrical terminals.
guides.introduction: The right multifunction switch controls the windshield wipers and washer. It mounts on the right side of the steering column control module, which provides the interface between the column switches and other vehicle systems. Replacement renews this driver control and its electrical connection; reaching it requires careful removal of the surrounding column trim.
guides.why: The shrouds use several tabs and clips, some reached by rotating the steering wheel. Releasing them in sequence gives access without forcing the trim. At the switch, the key precaution is protecting the component terminals: bent or damaged terminals can compromise the connection even when the replacement switch is mechanically secure.

when.summary: When the right multifunction switch has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Left-hand-drive illustrations are used; right-hand-drive work is similar.
Leave the steering wheel installed; it is removed from the switch illustration for clarity.

prepare.title: Gather the trim and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover, a flat-bladed screwdriver, suitable retainer tools and a torque tool capable of the switch's specified low tightening value.

prepare.title: Arrange column access
prepare.detail: Allow room to fully extend and lower the steering column and rotate the steering wheel as required by the shroud procedure.

steps.title: Release the upper gap hider
steps.body: Follow [Steering Column Shrouds](#/document/G1692617). Fully extend and lower the column. Use the interior trim remover to release the tabs, disconnect the upper gap hider from the upper shroud and position it aside.

steps.title: Release the upper shroud
steps.body: Release the upper shroud tabs. Rotate the steering wheel 90 degrees and release the accessible shroud tab with the flat-bladed screwdriver, then rotate the wheel 180 degrees and release the next tab. Release the outer clips on each side and remove the upper shroud.

steps.title: Remove the lower shroud
steps.body: Remove the lower shroud screws and lift away the lower shroud. This completes the specified access work before handling the switch.

steps.title: Remove the right multifunction switch
steps.body: Follow the [right multifunction switch procedure](#/document/G1693272). Remove its retainers and withdraw the switch, making sure the component terminals are not bent or damaged.

steps.title: Install the switch and restore the trim
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure, maintaining terminal alignment while installing the switch. Tighten its retainers to 9 lb.in (1 Nm). Reinstall the lower and upper shrouds and reconnect the upper gap hider by reversing their access sequence.

watchFor.title: A shroud that remains attached
watchFor.body: Check the specified tabs and outer clips before applying more force; several separate retention points must be released.

watchFor.title: Terminal damage
watchFor.body: Bent or damaged component terminals must not be overlooked during removal or installation.

notes: The right switch operates the wipers and washer. Turn-signal and headlamp selection belong to the left multifunction switch.

diagnostics.finding: The wipers or washer do not respond as expected.
diagnostics.meaning: The right switch supplies the driver's request through the column module; the symptom alone does not establish switch failure.
diagnostics.next: Establish the cause through wiper and washer diagnosis before choosing replacement.

verification.title: Confirm switch installation
verification.body: Confirm the terminals remain undamaged and the switch retainers are tightened to specification.

verification.title: Confirm trim restoration
verification.body: Verify the lower shroud screws, upper shroud tabs and side clips, and upper gap hider have all been restored.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the right steering-column multifunction switch, preserving terminal condition and the specified retainer torque.
Remove and reinstall the upper and lower steering-column shrouds and gap hider for switch access.

guides.title: Replace the steering wheel multifunction switches
guides.summary: Remove the driver airbag for access, service the required upper or lower switch assemblies and restore their connectors and mountings.
guides.introduction: The steering wheel switches let the driver operate several systems without reaching away from the wheel. The left upper switch serves the message center, the right upper switch serves the audio system, and the lower switches serve cruise control and SYNC. These switches can be serviced separately from the steering wheel, but access requires removal of the driver airbag.
guides.why: A switch is part of a control path that also includes connectors, steering column electronics and other vehicle modules. An unresponsive button therefore does not prove the switch has failed. Once replacement is justified, the important distinctions are safe airbag access, the upper-versus-lower removal branches, and which retainers have a specified tightening value.
searchTerms: steering wheel audio buttons not responding
steering wheel cruise control switch replacement

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies an upper or lower steering wheel switch requiring replacement.
notes: Identify the affected switch group before beginning airbag removal.

prepare.title: Provide airbag service capability
prepare.detail: The technician must be able to complete the linked Driver Airbag procedure, including its safety prerequisites and removal and installation requirements. The switch procedure does not replace those instructions.

prepare.title: Prepare for small electrical assemblies
prepare.detail: Have suitable retainer tools and a torque wrench capable of the specified 44 lb.in (5 Nm) setting. Keep the upper switch retainers distinguishable from the switch-and-bezel and lower-switch retainers.

steps.title: Identify the switch being serviced
steps.body: Match the affected function to its upper or lower switch position. Plan the appropriate branch; removing an assembly for access does not automatically require separating every switch from its bezel.

steps.title: Remove the driver airbag
steps.body: Complete the safety prerequisites and removal sequence in the Driver Airbag procedure. This provides the required access to the steering wheel switch assemblies.

steps.title: Remove the switch-and-bezel assemblies
steps.body: Remove their retainers, disconnect the electrical connectors and take out the switch-and-bezel assemblies. Keep the connectors associated with their original assembly positions for reinstallation.

steps.title: Separate upper switches only when required
steps.body: When installing new upper steering wheel switches, remove the retainers and upper switches on both sides as shown in the procedure. This additional separation is specifically conditional on installing new upper switches.

steps.title: Follow the lower-switch branch where applicable
steps.body: For lower steering wheel switches, remove the retainers, disconnect the electrical connectors and remove the switches. Retain this connector-release step rather than pulling an electrically attached assembly away.

steps.title: Reassemble and restore the airbag
steps.body: Reverse the applicable removal sequence and reconnect the electrical connectors. Tighten the switch-and-bezel mounting retainers and lower-switch retainers to 44 lb.in (5 Nm). Complete driver airbag installation through its linked procedure.

watchFor.title: Applying one torque to every small retainer
watchFor.body: The stated tightening value accompanies the switch-and-bezel assemblies and lower switches. No separate upper-switch retainer torque is given; do not transfer that value to them by assumption.

notes: The steering column stalks and rear-mounted paddle shifters are separate switch types with different service procedures.

diagnostics.finding: A steering wheel control does not operate its associated function.
diagnostics.meaning: The complaint identifies the affected function, but the switches communicate through other electronics and modules.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the fault before replacing a switch; this removal procedure does not provide an electrical diagnosis.

verification.title: Confirm assembly completion
verification.body: Confirm that the serviced switches and bezels are retained, their connectors are reconnected, and driver airbag installation is complete.

verification.title: Record the repair outcome
verification.body: Record which switch positions were serviced and whether the original control complaint remains. A continuing complaint requires further diagnosis of the relevant system.

procedures.purpose: Switch-and-bezel removal, conditional upper-switch separation, lower-switch removal and reverse installation.
Required driver airbag removal and installation for access to the steering wheel switches.
Steering wheel switch locations, controlled functions and their connection through the steering column electronics.

guides.title: Inspect engine bearings and interpret their wear patterns
guides.summary: Compare exposed bearing surfaces with six characteristic damage patterns to direct inspection of lubrication, seating and journal condition.
guides.introduction: Engine bearings support rotating journals while lubrication separates their working surfaces. Once a bearing is accessible during engine repair, its surface can preserve useful evidence of how it has been operating. This inspection interprets that evidence; the engine-specific repair procedures still determine access, dimensional checks and assembly requirements.
guides.why: Different marks point toward different problems. Replacing a worn bearing without addressing dirty oil, poor lubrication, incorrect seating or journal damage can leave the underlying condition unresolved. Visual interpretation therefore guides the next inspection, while the correct engine specifications govern the repair decision.

when.summary: When bearings are exposed during engine repair and their condition must be assessed.
notes: Use the specifications for the identified engine; this is a general visual inspection.
A wear pattern directs investigation but does not supply a dimensional acceptance limit.

prepare.title: Establish engine identity and access
prepare.detail: Identify the engine before selecting specifications or replacement parts. Bearing access and any further dismantling require the appropriate engine procedure and engine-repair capability.

prepare.title: Maintain contamination-free conditions
prepare.detail: Keep all engine parts free of contamination during the repair. Foreign material introduced while handling parts can cause premature engine failure.

steps.title: Examine each bearing as an identifiable component
steps.body: Keep the bearing's original location associated with the inspection result. Obtain a clear view of its working surface so any finding can be related to the corresponding journal and seating.

steps.title: Compare the surface markings
steps.body: Use the [bearing inspection illustrations](#/document/G1661742) to distinguish cratering, spot glazing and scratching. These patterns point respectively toward fatigue, incorrect seating and dirty engine oil.

steps.title: Inspect wear depth and both edges
steps.body: Look for exposed base material and compare the two edges. Exposed base material indicates poor lubrication. Wear at both edges points to journal damage; wear at one edge calls for distinguishing a tapered journal from a bearing that was not seated.

steps.title: Turn the finding into a repair decision
steps.body: Use the pattern to direct further inspection, then apply the engine-specific minimum and maximum specifications to the affected components. A component outside specification must be refinished where permissible or replaced. If it cannot be refinished to specification, install a new component.

watchFor.title: One-edge wear has two stated explanations
watchFor.body: Do not select journal taper as the cause without also considering whether the bearing was correctly seated.

watchFor.title: Appearance does not establish serviceability
watchFor.body: Visual comparison identifies a damage pattern. It does not replace the engine-specific specifications used to accept, refinish or replace components.

notes: Keep the surface observation and the final cause assessment distinct in the repair record.

diagnostics.finding: Cratering
diagnostics.meaning: Fatigue failure.
diagnostics.next: Assess the affected components against the engine-specific repair specifications.

diagnostics.finding: Spot glazing
diagnostics.meaning: Incorrect seating.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the bearing seating before assembly.

diagnostics.finding: Scratching
diagnostics.meaning: Dirty engine oil.
diagnostics.next: Address contamination as part of the repair and keep replacement or retained parts contamination free.

diagnostics.finding: Base material exposed
diagnostics.meaning: Poor lubrication.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the lubrication condition and assess the affected components before rebuilding.

diagnostics.finding: Both edges worn
diagnostics.meaning: Journal damage.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the corresponding journal using the engine-specific specifications.

diagnostics.finding: One edge worn
diagnostics.meaning: A tapered journal or a bearing that was not seated.
diagnostics.next: Check both journal condition and bearing seating before deciding the repair.

verification.title: Confirm the disposition
verification.body: Check that the decision to retain, refinish or replace each affected component follows the correct engine specifications.

verification.title: Record the inspection
verification.body: Record the bearing location, observed pattern, corresponding journal or seating findings, and resulting repair decision.

procedures.purpose: General engine-bearing visual inspection and interpretation of six characteristic damage patterns.

guides.title: Measure connecting-rod bearing clearance with Plastigage
guides.summary: Measure assembled connecting-rod bearing clearance with Plastigage after confirming that the crankshaft journals meet the correct engine specifications.
guides.introduction: A connecting-rod bearing runs around its crankshaft journal with a small clearance that accommodates the lubricating oil film. Plastigage measures this assembled gap by being compressed between the bearing and journal. This check supports internal engine repair decisions; it begins with access to the connecting-rod bearing cap, not with a complete engine dismantling sequence.
guides.why: The journal must already be within specification for this check to be valid. Correct cap tightening establishes the assembled condition, while keeping the crankshaft still preserves the Plastigage reading. Both the measured clearance and the shape of the flattened material matter: an uneven width can reveal a problem that a single reading would conceal.
searchTerms: tapered or damaged connecting rod bearing

when.summary: During internal engine repair, after confirming that the connecting-rod journals are within specification.
notes: Use the specification and tightening instructions for the actual engine being worked on.

prepare.title: Engine-specific information and capability
