prepare.detail: Obtain the appropriate Section 303-01 journal limits, bearing-clearance specification and cap-tightening instructions. Follow that engine's access, fastener and final assembly requirements rather than treating this general check as a complete overhaul procedure.

prepare.title: Measurement and cleanliness
prepare.detail: Have Plastigage, its reading scale and the equipment needed to tighten the cap correctly. Keep all engine parts free of contamination; foreign material during engine repair can cause premature failure.

steps.title: Establish that the journal is suitable for checking
steps.body: Confirm that the crankshaft connecting-rod journal meets the applicable engine specifications before beginning the [bearing-clearance check](#/document/G1661743). A journal outside those limits must be addressed before this measurement can serve its intended purpose.

steps.title: Expose the bearing and position the Plastigage
steps.body: Remove the connecting-rod bearing cap and bearing as directed. Position a piece of Plastigage across the bearing surface at the illustrated measuring location. Its compressed width will provide the clearance reading.

steps.title: Tighten without rotating the crankshaft
steps.body: Install the bearing-cap assembly and tighten it to the correct engine specification. Do not turn the crankshaft during this operation. Remove the cap again so the flattened Plastigage can be examined without disturbing the reading.

steps.title: Read the clearance and assess its consistency
steps.body: Measure the Plastigage and compare the result with the engine-specific clearance limits. It should be smooth and flat. Examine its width along the measuring strip as well as taking the reading; a changing width indicates a tapered or damaged connecting rod or connecting-rod bearing.

watchFor.title: Crankshaft movement during the check
watchFor.body: Rotation can disturb the compressed material. Preserve the stationary assembled condition required for the measurement.

watchFor.title: A plausible reading on an unsuitable journal
watchFor.body: The prerequisite journal checks still apply even if the Plastigage appears smooth.

notes: Engine identification determines which specifications and repair procedures apply.
A uniform Plastigage width must still be compared with the specified clearance range.

diagnostics.finding: The flattened Plastigage changes width.
diagnostics.meaning: The connecting rod or its bearing may be tapered or damaged.
diagnostics.next: Investigate those components under the engine-specific inspection and repair criteria before continuing assembly.

diagnostics.finding: Measured clearance is outside the applicable specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The assembly does not meet the required condition.
diagnostics.next: Determine which component requires correction. Refinish only where permitted; install a new component when it cannot be brought within specification by refinishing.

verification.title: Validate the measurement
verification.body: Confirm that journal suitability was established, cap tightening followed the correct specification, the crankshaft remained still and the Plastigage was smooth and flat.

verification.title: Record the result and decision
verification.body: Record the measured bearing clearance, the applicable engine limit and any changing-width observation. Establish whether correction is required before proceeding with engine-specific assembly.

procedures.purpose: General Plastigage check of connecting-rod bearing journal clearance; engine-specific specifications and cap-tightening requirements come from the appropriate Section 303-01.

guides.title: Check crankshaft main bearing clearance with Plastigage
guides.summary: Measure assembled main bearing clearance and inspect the Plastigage pattern for evidence of taper or damage.
guides.introduction: Main bearings support the crankshaft while allowing it to rotate on an oil film. The clearance between a journal and its bearing must match the engine specification. Plastigage is a compressible measuring strip: tightening the cap flattens it, and its resulting width indicates the assembled clearance.
guides.why: This check is meaningful only after the crankshaft journals themselves meet specification. Correct cap tightening reproduces the assembled fit; turning the crankshaft during the test disturbs the strip and undermines the reading.

when.summary: When main bearing clearance needs checking during engine repair and the crankshaft journals already meet specification.
notes: Use the clearance limits and cap-tightening requirements for the identified engine.

prepare.title: Engine repair capability
prepare.detail: Arrange access to the main bearing caps through the applicable engine procedure. This is an internal-engine measurement requiring contamination-free parts and controlled assembly.

prepare.title: Measuring and tightening equipment
prepare.detail: Have Plastigage, its comparison scale and equipment capable of applying the engine-specific cap-tightening specification.

steps.title: Establish the prerequisites
steps.body: Identify the engine and obtain its specifications from the appropriate Section 303-01. Confirm that the main bearing journals meet those specifications before testing bearing clearance. Clearance measurement cannot substitute for checking journal condition.

steps.title: Position the measuring strip
steps.body: Remove the main bearing cap and bearing as directed in the linked procedure. Place a piece of Plastigage across the main bearing surface in the illustrated position. Keep the parts free of foreign material.

steps.title: Load the bearing assembly
steps.body: Install the cap and tighten it to the applicable engine specification. Do not turn the crankshaft. The tightened assembly compresses the strip to represent the available clearance.

steps.title: Read the clearance and pattern
steps.body: Remove the cap and compare the flattened Plastigage with its scale. Check the pattern along its length as well as the clearance reading: it should be smooth and flat. Compare the result with the correct engine limit before continuing assembly.

watchFor.title: Changing strip width
watchFor.body: A changing width indicates taper or damage in the crankshaft or bearing; one apparently acceptable reading does not clear the whole surface.

notes: The general check does not provide a universal clearance or cap torque. Engine-specific values are essential.

diagnostics.finding: The measured clearance is outside the engine specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The assembled fit is unacceptable.
diagnostics.next: Determine which component requires refinishing or replacement; replace a component that cannot be refinished to specification.

diagnostics.finding: The Plastigage width varies.
diagnostics.meaning: The crankshaft or bearing may be tapered or damaged.
diagnostics.next: Evaluate both components before accepting the assembly.

verification.title: Record the measurement
verification.body: Record the bearing location, measured clearance, applicable engine limit and whether the strip was smooth and uniform.

verification.title: Accept or correct the fit
verification.body: Continue the engine-specific assembly only after the journal condition and measured clearance satisfy their specifications.

procedures.purpose: General Plastigage method for checking crankshaft main bearing journal clearance using engine-specific specifications.

guides.title: Replace a cylinder block core plug
guides.summary: Extract the core plug, assess its bore and install the correct replacement using the cup-type or expansion-type method.
guides.introduction: Core plugs close openings in an engine casting. Their seal depends on both the plug and the surrounding bore, so replacing a leaking plug involves more than fitting another piece into the opening. This repair covers extraction, bore inspection and two installation branches: cup-type plugs and expansion-type plugs.
guides.why: Bore damage can prevent a replacement plug from sealing. Installation technique also matters: a distorted cup sealing surface or an expansion plug expanded before it is seated can leave a leak. Keep the work contamination-free because foreign material introduced during engine repair can cause premature engine failure.

when.summary: When a core plug requires replacement and access to the plug has been established.
notes: Identify the engine and actual plug type before selecting replacement parts or an installation branch.

prepare.title: Establish access and cleanliness
prepare.detail: Arrange the engine-specific access work before beginning this exposed-plug repair. Keep parts and the work area free of contamination.

prepare.title: Prepare extraction and installation tools
prepare.detail: Have slide hammer 100-001 (T50T-100-A), a commercially available body dent puller attachment or freeze-plug puller, and a freeze-plug installer.

prepare.title: Obtain the specified sealant
prepare.detail: Both installation branches use Motorcraft Threadlock 262, TA-26, specification WSK-M2G351-A6. Arrange machining capability if inspection reveals bore damage that prevents correct sealing.

steps.title: Extract the existing core plug
steps.body: Remove the plug with the specified slide hammer and suitable commercial attachment or freeze-plug puller. Removal exposes the bore for the inspection that determines how the repair should proceed.

steps.title: Inspect the sealing bore
steps.body: Look for damage that would interfere with correct sealing. If the bore is damaged, bore it for the next oversize plug. An oversize plug is identified by OS stamped on the flat on its cup side.

steps.title: Install a cup-type plug when fitted
steps.body: Lightly coat the plug and bore with the specified sealant, then install the plug with a freeze-plug installer. Avoid disturbing or distorting the cup’s sealing surface. Its flanged edge must finish below the bore’s chamfered edge to seal effectively.

steps.title: Use the alternative expansion-type method when fitted
steps.body: For an expansion-type plug, lightly coat the plug and bore with the same specified sealant and install it using a freeze-plug installer. Do not contact the crown: that can expand the plug before it is seated and cause leakage.

steps.title: Finish the selected installation
steps.body: After installing the applicable plug type, remove excess sealant. Check the completed installation against the requirements for that type rather than applying both installation branches to one plug.

watchFor.title: Damage that sealant cannot correct
watchFor.body: A damaged sealing bore requires the specified oversize repair path. Extra sealant is not the prescribed response to bore damage.

watchFor.title: Premature expansion or cup distortion
watchFor.body: Avoid crown contact on expansion-type plugs and protect the sealing surface on cup-type plugs throughout installation.

notes: The block core plug is illustrated; cylinder-head core-plug work is described as similar. The illustration does not establish which plug type is fitted to every engine.

diagnostics.finding: Bore damage would interfere with the plug seal.
diagnostics.meaning: A replacement plug alone does not address the damaged sealing surface.
diagnostics.next: Bore for the next oversize plug and use the corresponding replacement.

verification.title: Check the applicable installation requirements
verification.body: For a cup-type plug, confirm that its flange is below the bore chamfer and its sealing surface remains undistorted. For either type, confirm that excess sealant has been removed.

verification.title: Record an oversize repair
verification.body: If machining was necessary, record the bore repair and the oversize plug installed.

procedures.purpose: Core-plug extraction, bore assessment, oversize repair and the separate cup-type and expansion-type installation methods.

guides.title: Check the cylinder block sealing face for distortion
guides.summary: Measure cylinder block flatness with a calibrated straightedge and feeler gauges before deciding whether the block can be reused.
guides.introduction: The cylinder block’s upper sealing face supports the cylinder head and its gasket. Distortion can prevent those surfaces from meeting evenly. This inspection measures the gap beneath a known-flat straightedge so the block’s condition can be compared with the specification for the actual engine.
guides.why: The straightedge is the reference surface for the measurement. An inaccurate edge or foreign material between the tools and block can produce a misleading result. The tool’s calibration tolerance and the engine’s permitted distortion are separate limits.
searchTerms: block straightedge and feeler gauge inspection

when.summary: When engine repair requires deciding whether the cylinder block sealing face is within specification.
notes: Obtain the applicable engine specification from Section 303-01 before interpreting the measurement.

prepare.title: Arrange access and clean working conditions
prepare.detail: The block sealing face must be accessible for measurement. Follow the appropriate engine procedures for access, and keep engine parts free of contamination.

prepare.title: Use a verified reference edge
prepare.detail: Have a feeler gauge set and a manufacturer-calibrated straightedge, such as Snap-On GA438A or equivalent, flat within 0.005 mm (0.0002 in) per running foot of length.

steps.title: Identify the engine and its acceptance limit
steps.body: Confirm whether the block belongs to the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine. Select that engine’s flatness specification; the shared checking method does not establish a common allowable gap.

steps.title: Check the measuring setup
steps.body: Confirm straightedge calibration and contamination-free contact surfaces. For the stated calibration requirement, a 61 cm (24 in) edge must be flat within 0.010 mm (0.0004 in) from end to end.

steps.title: Measure the separation
steps.body: Use the straightedge and feeler gauge set to inspect the block for flatness, following the illustrated arrangement in the linked procedure. The gauge measures separation between the block surface and the reference edge.

steps.title: Decide the repair path
steps.body: Compare the measured condition with the engine-specific limit. A component outside specification requires refinishing or replacement; replacement is necessary when it cannot be refinished to specification.

watchFor.title: A false reference
watchFor.body: An ordinary ruler or an unverified straightedge does not establish the required measuring accuracy.

notes: This check establishes surface flatness; engine-specific specifications govern the repair decision.

diagnostics.finding: Measured distortion exceeds the applicable engine limit.
diagnostics.meaning: The block does not meet the required condition for reuse.
diagnostics.next: Determine whether permissible refinishing can restore specification; otherwise replace the block.

verification.title: Record a traceable result
verification.body: Record the engine identity, measured gap, applicable limit and resulting reuse, refinishing or replacement decision. Confirm that the straightedge meets its calibration requirement.

procedures.purpose: Cylinder block flatness inspection for the listed engines.
Engine identification, contamination control and component disposition principles.

guides.title: Measure cylinder bore taper before deciding on machining
guides.summary: Compare bore diameters through piston-ring travel to determine whether the cylinder meets its engine-specific wear and taper limits.
guides.introduction: The cylinder bore provides the running surface for the piston rings. Its diameter can vary along the distance the rings travel, leaving a tapered bore rather than a consistently sized cylinder. This check measures that variation at several heights and in both illustrated directions. It is a precision measurement stage within engine repair, with access to the bore already established through the appropriate engine procedure.
guides.why: A single diameter reading cannot establish taper. Comparing readings at corresponding directions and different heights reveals how the bore changes along ring travel. Engine identification also matters: this general procedure supplies the measurement pattern, while the applicable engine section supplies the limits and permitted oversize.

when.summary: When an accessible cylinder bore needs a wear assessment before reuse or machining.
notes: Obtain the specification from the appropriate engine section, 303-01, before making an acceptance decision.

prepare.title: Identify the engine and its limits
prepare.detail: Have the correct engine identification, bore wear specification, taper specification and next permitted oversize available.

prepare.title: Prepare for accurate measurement
prepare.detail: Use suitable bore-diameter measuring equipment and a clean, accessible bore. Keep engine parts free of contamination throughout the work.

prepare.title: Arrange machining capability if needed
prepare.detail: Accurate bore measurement requires engine inspection skills. Any required boring belongs with a workshop capable of machining to the applicable engine dimensions.

steps.title: Establish the measurement pattern
steps.body: Use the [cylinder bore taper procedure](#/document/G1661747) and its illustration to identify the two measurement directions. Locate the top, middle and bottom of piston-ring travel.

steps.title: Measure at every required location
steps.body: Measure the bore in both directions at each of those heights. Record each reading against its height and direction so the comparisons remain traceable.

steps.title: Compare diameter and taper with specification
steps.body: Verify that the bore measurements satisfy the engine's wear limit. Compare readings along each measurement direction through ring travel to establish taper, then assess that difference against the applicable specification.

steps.title: Choose the supported repair path
steps.body: If taper is outside specification, the procedure directs boring the cylinder to the next oversize limit. Confirm that permitted limit for the identified engine. A component that cannot be refinished to specification requires replacement.

watchFor.title: Readings without location labels
watchFor.body: Unlabelled measurements make it difficult to distinguish a change with depth from a difference between directions.

watchFor.title: Assumed oversize dimensions
watchFor.body: The general check gives no universal machining diameter. Use the specification for the actual engine.

notes: The illustration establishes measurement directions; it does not supply an engine-specific wear limit.

diagnostics.finding: Bore wear and taper meet the applicable limits.
diagnostics.meaning: This check does not identify a need to bore the cylinder.
diagnostics.next: Retain the results with the remaining engine inspection findings.

diagnostics.finding: Taper exceeds specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The bore changes diameter beyond the permitted amount through ring travel.
diagnostics.next: Use the specified next-oversize machining path, or replace the component if it cannot be refinished to specification.

verification.title: Record the measurement decision
verification.body: Confirm the record contains both directions at every required height, the applicable limits and the resulting reuse, machining or replacement decision.

procedures.purpose: Measure cylinder bore taper and apply the machining decision using specifications from the appropriate engine section.

guides.title: Check a cylinder head for distortion
guides.summary: Measure cylinder-head flatness with a calibrated straightedge and feeler gauges, then compare the results with the correct engine limits.
guides.introduction: The cylinder head’s gasket face must provide a suitable mating surface against the engine block. A distortion check measures departures from flatness that can prevent that joint from sealing properly. This is an inspection of an accessible head; removing and reinstalling it are separate engine-specific operations.
guides.why: A straightedge bridges the surface while feeler gauges measure gaps beneath it. Gasket residue, sealant or liquid can hold the straightedge away from the metal and produce a misleading result. The measuring tool must also be sufficiently flat to distinguish head distortion from error in the tool itself.

when.summary: When an accessible cylinder head needs a flatness assessment before a reuse or repair decision.
notes: Obtain the appropriate engine specification before judging the measurements.

prepare.title: Use suitable measuring equipment
prepare.detail: Provide a feeler-gauge set and a manufacturer-calibrated straightedge flat within 0.005 mm (0.0002 in) per running foot, such as Snap-On GA438A or equivalent.

prepare.title: Prepare a clean inspection surface
prepare.detail: Remove gasket material, silicone sealant, oil and coolant. The head surface must be clean and dry, with contamination kept away from engine components.

steps.title: Identify the applicable limit
steps.body: Confirm the engine and obtain its specification from the appropriate engine section. The shared measuring method does not establish a common allowable distortion for every engine.

steps.title: Check readiness to measure
steps.body: Confirm the surface is bare, clean and dry and that the straightedge meets the stated calibration requirement. Residue beneath the edge invalidates the comparison.

steps.title: Measure in the illustrated sequence
steps.body: Follow the numbered paths in the [flatness-check illustration](#/document/G1661748), completing the lengthwise paths before the transverse paths. Use feeler gauges to measure gaps beneath the seated straightedge without lifting it to admit a thicker blade.

steps.title: Record and evaluate the readings
steps.body: Record the measured gaps by inspection position and compare them with the engine’s specification. If the head fails, determine whether permitted refinishing can restore it; replace a component that cannot be brought within specification.

watchFor.title: Tool accuracy is not the acceptance limit
watchFor.body: The straightedge calibration figure describes the tool. It is not the allowable distortion of the cylinder head.

notes: The illustration defines inspection paths; the applicable engine specification governs acceptance.

diagnostics.finding: Gasket residue, sealant, oil or coolant remains on the surface.
diagnostics.meaning: The setup is not ready for a valid flatness check.
diagnostics.next: Clean and dry the surface, then repeat the inspection.

diagnostics.finding: A measurement exceeds the engine-specific limit.
diagnostics.meaning: The head fails the flatness requirement.
diagnostics.next: Assess permissible refinishing or replacement using the applicable specifications.

verification.title: Retain a usable inspection result
verification.body: Confirm every illustrated path was checked. Record the engine specification used, the largest measured gap and its position, and the resulting reuse, refinishing or replacement decision.

procedures.purpose: Cylinder-head flatness measurement and numbered inspection sequence.
General engine inspection principles and decisions for components outside specification.

applicability.equipment: Cylinder-head flatness inspection for 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines, using engine-specific acceptance limits.

guides.title: Clean an exhaust manifold and check sealing-face warpage
guides.summary: Clean the manifold, measure its sealing-face distortion and determine whether it can be reused with new gaskets and applicable fasteners.
guides.introduction: The exhaust manifold collects exhaust gas from the engine and directs it into the exhaust system. Its gasket face must provide a sufficiently flat surface for the joint to seal. This bench inspection removes deposits that could interfere with measurement, then uses a calibrated straightedge and feeler gauges to assess warpage. It establishes a reuse or replacement decision before the manifold is installed again.
guides.why: Deposits beneath a straightedge can produce a misleading gap, while an inaccurate straightedge can make the measurement unreliable. Cleaning comes first. The prescribed plastic scraper removes material from the gasket faces without relying on a metal cutting edge, and the service instructions require new sealing and fastening parts even when the manifold passes inspection.

when.summary: When an exhaust manifold is being serviced and its sealing face needs assessment for reuse.
notes: Use the appropriate engine procedure for manifold removal and installation.

prepare.title: Gather cleaning materials
prepare.detail: Use a suitable solvent and a plastic scraping tool. Keep the manifold and other engine parts free of contamination.

prepare.title: Use a calibrated measurement reference
prepare.detail: Have feeler gauges and a straightedge calibrated by its manufacturer to be flat within 0.005 mm (0.0002 in) per running foot, such as Snap-On® GA438A or equivalent.

prepare.title: Prepare the installation parts
prepare.detail: Identify the correct new exhaust manifold gaskets and applicable studs, nuts and/or bolts for the engine being serviced.

steps.title: Clean the manifold
steps.body: Clean the exhaust manifold with a suitable solvent as directed in the [cleaning and inspection procedure](#/document/G1661749). Remove contamination before judging the sealing surface.

steps.title: Clear the gasket sealing faces
steps.body: Use the plastic scraper to remove material from the gasket faces. The straightedge must bear on the actual sealing surface rather than remaining gasket material or deposits.

steps.title: Measure sealing-face warpage
steps.body: Use the calibrated straightedge and feeler gauge set to check the sealing surface as illustrated. Assess the measurable gap against the specified warpage limit.

steps.title: Decide whether to reuse or replace
steps.body: If warpage is greater than 0.76 mm (0.0299 in), install a new exhaust manifold. When the manifold is serviced, use new gaskets and applicable studs, nuts and/or bolts regardless of whether the original manifold passes this check.

watchFor.title: An unverified straightedge
watchFor.body: An ordinary ruler is not an established flatness reference. The stated manufacturer calibration is part of the measurement requirement.

watchFor.title: A clean appearance mistaken for acceptable flatness
watchFor.body: Cleaning exposes the surface; the straightedge and feeler-gauge check establishes its measured condition.

notes: The prescribed response to excessive warpage is manifold replacement; this procedure does not provide a resurfacing allowance.

diagnostics.finding: Warpage is greater than 0.76 mm (0.0299 in).
diagnostics.meaning: The sealing surface exceeds the specified distortion limit.
diagnostics.next: Replace the exhaust manifold.

diagnostics.finding: Measured warpage does not exceed the limit.
diagnostics.meaning: The manifold passes this sealing-face warpage check.
diagnostics.next: Continue the engine-specific installation procedure using new required gaskets and fasteners.

verification.title: Record the inspection result
verification.body: Record the measured warpage and the reuse or replacement decision. Confirm that the required new installation parts are available before reassembly.

procedures.purpose: Clean the exhaust manifold, measure sealing-face warpage and apply the replacement and new-hardware requirements.

guides.title: Inspect the dual-mass flywheel on 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Assess surface condition, bearing condition and flywheel movement using the correct engine-specific acceptance limits.
guides.introduction: A dual-mass flywheel has a primary mass attached to the crankshaft and a secondary mass carrying the clutch contact surface. Internal springs allow controlled movement between them to cushion changes in transmitted torque. Some movement and heat marking are normal. This inspection separates acceptable wear from damage requiring replacement, using visual checks, rotational tests and a supported bench measurement.
guides.why: Cleaning methods, applied force and measurement location affect this inspection. The 5.2L uses different rotational and axial criteria from the 2.3L and 3.7L. These flywheels cannot be machined, so an unacceptable result requires replacement rather than resurfacing.

when.summary: When an exposed dual-mass flywheel needs a reuse-or-replace decision during repair.
notes: Select the inspection procedure by engine before measuring or tightening anything.

prepare.title: Arrange access and measurement capability
prepare.detail: The inspection begins with the flywheel exposed and includes removal for bench testing. Have flywheel holding tool 303-103, dial-indicator holding fixture 100-002, a suitable long screwdriver or bar, stable support blocks and torque-controlled installation capability.

prepare.title: Prepare for the engine-specific test
prepare.detail: The 5.2L requires controlled application of the specified load. Obtain new flywheel bolts for every variant. Use a dry cloth only: no cleaning fluid, compressed air or cleaning between the masses.

steps.title: Inspect the clutch face and applicable pilot bearing
steps.body: Clean only the bolt connection and clutch surfaces. Replace a flywheel with large cracks or clutch scoring; minor heat cracks, discoloration and the minor heat scoring described in the procedure are acceptable. On the 2.3L and 5.2L, also inspect the pilot bearing for excessive wear, heat damage and smooth operation. An unacceptable bearing requires a new flywheel.

steps.title: Check the internal support components
steps.body: Inspect the hub bushing for wear on all variants. On the 2.3L and 3.7L, inspect the plastic friction control plate between the masses for damage or melting. Replace as required; a damaged friction control plate prevents a valid rotational-freeplay inspection.

steps.title: Measure rotational freeplay with light pressure
steps.body: Turn the secondary mass counterclockwise and mark both masses. Turn it clockwise using light hand pressure to the end of freeplay, then mark the primary mass opposite the secondary mark. Measure between the primary marks. Replace above 14 degrees (6.5 ring gear teeth) for the 2.3L or 3.7L, or above 16 degrees (7 ring gear teeth) for the 5.2L.

steps.title: Test spring engagement in both directions
steps.body: Install the flywheel holding tool. Using the suitable bar or screwdriver, firmly rotate the secondary mass clockwise and then counterclockwise. Beyond freeplay, the internal springs should engage with increasing resistance. If the secondary mass does not rotate, replace the flywheel.

steps.title: Remove and support the flywheel
steps.body: Remove the flywheel and discard its bolts. Inspect its crankshaft mounting flange for rust or residual thread locking compound and clean as necessary. Place the flywheel on blocks on a firm, level surface so it is stable and level, then remove the holding tool.

steps.title: Measure axial movement on the 2.3L or 3.7L
steps.body: Place the dial indicator on the outer upper surface of the secondary mass. Press lightly downward at the opposite point and record deflection. Repeat at 45 degree intervals. Replace if any reading exceeds 1.1 mm (0.043 in).

steps.title: Use the alternative axial test on the 5.2L
steps.body: Position the indicator on the clutch mounting surface 130 mm (5.12 in) from center. Apply 50 N (11.24 lb) at the opposite point on the secondary mass and zero the indicator. Move that load to the opposite side. Replace if peak-to-peak displacement exceeds 2.8 mm (0.11 in).

steps.title: Inspect the engine and transmission mounting features
steps.body: On the 5.2L, remove the crankshaft position sensor ring first. Check engine dowel installation and condition, the rear spacer plate for damage or warping, the crankshaft flange for rust or compound, and transmission dowel holes for damage or elongation. Renew damaged dowels or the spacer plate as necessary and clean the flange. Reinstall the sensor ring on the 5.2L.

steps.title: Refit using the correct bolt procedure
steps.body: Fit the serviceable or replacement flywheel with new bolts finger tight and install the holding tool. Follow the engine-specific illustrated tightening order: the 2.3L and 5.2L have different staged torque schedules, while the 3.7L has a single specified torque. Remove the holding tool afterward.

watchFor.title: Mixing measurement methods
watchFor.body: The light-pressure axial test and the 5.2L loaded peak-to-peak test have different limits and cannot be substituted for each other.

watchFor.title: Unnecessary replacement or resurfacing
watchFor.body: Minor acceptable heat marks alone do not justify replacement. Machining is prohibited on all three variants.

notes: Use the 2.3L inspection article for its own measurements and reinstallation details; the linked 3.7L flywheel removal procedure applies only to the 3.7L.

diagnostics.finding: Rotational or axial movement exceeds the applicable limit.
diagnostics.meaning: The flywheel fails its engine-specific movement criterion.
diagnostics.next: Install a new dual-mass flywheel.

diagnostics.finding: Only minor acceptable heat cracks or discoloration are present.
diagnostics.meaning: These marks alone do not impair flywheel function.
diagnostics.next: Continue the remaining checks before deciding on reuse.

verification.title: Record the inspection decision
verification.body: Record engine variant, surface and bearing findings, rotational freeplay and axial readings, then state the reuse-or-replace decision.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly
verification.body: Verify new bolts, completion of the correct tightening sequence, removal of the holding tool and, on the 5.2L, restoration of the sensor ring.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost flywheel inspection, pilot-bearing checks, movement limits and staged reinstallation.
3.7L Duratec flywheel inspection, movement limits and single-torque reinstallation.
5.2L flywheel inspection, loaded axial measurement, sensor-ring handling and staged reinstallation.
3.7L flywheel removal and installation when replacement is required.
5.2L flywheel removal and installation when replacement is required.

guides.title: Measure piston diameter at the specified skirt location
guides.summary: Measure the piston perpendicular to its pin at the prescribed height, then compare the result with the correct engine specification.
guides.introduction: A piston moves within the cylinder and transfers combustion force through its pin to the connecting rod. Its outside diameter is one of the dimensions checked during engine inspection. This procedure establishes exactly where to take that measurement so the result can be compared meaningfully with the specification for the identified engine.
guides.why: Measuring at a different height or in a different direction can produce a reading that does not represent the specified check. Cleanliness also matters: foreign material can interfere with a dimensional measurement and can cause premature failure if carried into a rebuilt engine.

when.summary: During engine inspection when an accessible piston's diameter must be checked against its specification.
notes: This dimensional check forms part of a wider engine inspection.
Obtain the appropriate engine specification before making a reuse or replacement decision.

prepare.title: Identify the engine
prepare.detail: Use the correct engine identification and obtain its piston-diameter specification from the appropriate Section 303-01.

prepare.title: Prepare for accurate measurement
prepare.detail: Have suitable precision outside-diameter measuring equipment and a means of locating the prescribed measuring height. Keep the piston and other engine parts free of contamination.

steps.title: Locate the measurement direction
steps.body: Identify the piston-pin axis. The diameter check is made 90 degrees from that axis, as shown in the [piston diameter procedure](#/document/G1661750). Establish this orientation before positioning the measuring equipment.

steps.title: Set the measuring height and take the reading
steps.body: Locate the point 41 mm (1.61 in) down from the top of the piston. Measure the diameter at that height in the specified direction. Use the illustration to keep the height and orientation together as a single defined measuring location.

steps.title: Compare with the applicable limit
steps.body: Compare the measured diameter with the specification for the identified engine. Keep the actual reading with that specification so the acceptance decision can be checked. A general measurement location does not establish a common acceptable diameter for every engine.

watchFor.title: An incorrect reference point
watchFor.body: A reading taken parallel to the pin or at another skirt height does not complete this prescribed check.

notes: Engine dismantling, piston removal and reassembly require their own engine-specific procedures.

diagnostics.finding: The diameter is outside the applicable specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The piston does not meet the dimensional requirement.
diagnostics.next: Determine whether an approved refinishing option applies; install a new component if specification cannot be restored.

diagnostics.finding: The diameter meets the applicable specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The piston passes this diameter check.
diagnostics.next: Continue the remaining engine inspection before deciding overall serviceability.

verification.title: Record the dimensional result
verification.body: Record piston identity, measured diameter, units, applicable limit and acceptance decision. Confirm that the reading was taken at the specified height and orientation.

procedures.purpose: Locate and perform the prescribed piston-diameter measurement.
Apply engine identification, cleanliness and dimensional acceptance principles.

guides.title: Clean and inspect pistons during engine repair
guides.summary: Inspect the piston’s principal surfaces, clean its ring grooves and oil holes, and investigate connecting-rod alignment when skirt damage is present.
guides.introduction: A piston carries combustion force to the connecting rod through its pin. The crown faces combustion, the ring lands support the rings, the pin bosses support the pin, and the skirt guides the piston in the cylinder. This inspection examines those areas and removes deposits from the ring grooves and oil-ring holes.
guides.why: Cleaning must reveal the metal without damaging it. Skirt wear marks, scoring or glazing also require a connecting-rod check: a bent or twisted rod may affect how the piston runs in the bore. The appearance alone does not establish that the rod is damaged.

when.summary: When pistons are accessible during engine repair, particularly if skirt wear, scoring or glazing is found.
notes: This is an inspection stage; engine-specific procedures govern piston access, measurements and reassembly.

prepare.title: Prepare the inspection work
prepare.detail: Have a piston ring groove scraper and the capability to handle exposed engine components without contamination. Obtain the specifications and connecting-rod inspection procedure for the engine being repaired.

steps.title: Clean without damaging the piston
steps.body: Clean the piston sufficiently to expose its inspection surfaces. Do not use a caustic cleaning solution or wire brush, because either can damage the piston.

steps.title: Inspect all principal areas
steps.body: Examine the ring lands, pin bosses, skirts and piston tops. The illustration identifies these distinct areas; inspecting only the crown would leave the ring-support, pin-support and guiding surfaces unchecked.

steps.title: Follow up on skirt damage
steps.body: If the skirt has wear marks, scores or glazing, check the connecting rod for bending or twisting using the applicable engine procedure. Keep this additional check separate from the decision about piston serviceability.

steps.title: Clean the grooves and oil passages
steps.body: Use a piston ring groove scraper to clean the ring grooves and make sure the oil-ring holes are clean. Remove cleaning debris before the component proceeds to further inspection or assembly.

watchFor.title: A clean appearance mistaken for approval
watchFor.body: Visual inspection does not replace engine-specific dimensional limits. Components outside specification require the appropriate repair or replacement decision.

notes: Engine repair parts must remain free of contamination; foreign material can cause premature engine failure.

diagnostics.finding: Wear marks, scores or glazing on the skirt.
diagnostics.meaning: The connecting rod needs an alignment inspection.
diagnostics.next: Check for a bent or twisted rod before completing the repair decision.

diagnostics.finding: A component fails its applicable specifications.
diagnostics.meaning: It is not serviceable in its present condition.
diagnostics.next: Determine whether it can be refinished within specification; install a new component if it cannot.

verification.title: Record the inspection outcome
verification.body: Record the condition of the inspected areas and any required connecting-rod check. Confirm that ring grooves and oil-ring holes are clean and that any specification failure has a resolved repair decision.

procedures.purpose: Piston cleaning, visual inspection and skirt-condition follow-up during engine repair.
General engine contamination control and specification-based repair or replacement principles.

guides.title: Check piston ring end gap
guides.summary: Measure the top and second piston ring end gaps in their cylinder bores and compare them with the correct engine specifications.
guides.introduction: A piston ring forms a seal against the cylinder wall while moving with the piston. Its split ends need clearance, including room for expansion as the ring heats up. This check measures that clearance with the ring inside the bore. It belongs within engine repair work, when the rings and cylinders are accessible.
guides.why: The measurement depends on both the ring and the bore containing it. A tapered or out-of-round cylinder cannot provide a sound basis for accepting ring fit. Careful positioning also protects the ring and cylinder surface, while keeping rings assigned to their original pistons preserves the identity of the parts being checked.

when.summary: During engine repair, when checking the fit of the top and second piston rings.
notes: Obtain the appropriate Section 303-01 specifications for the engine being repaired.

prepare.title: Arrange engine access and measuring equipment
prepare.detail: Have the cylinder bore accessible, a piston without rings, and a feeler gauge set. Engine disassembly and subsequent assembly require the applicable engine procedures.

prepare.title: Confirm bore condition and part identity
prepare.detail: Establish that cylinder taper and out-of-round are within specification before measuring ring gaps. Keep parts contamination-free and each ring associated with its own piston.

steps.title: Select the correct limits
steps.body: Identify the engine and obtain its top-ring and second-ring end-gap specifications. The shared checking method covers the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines, but acceptance limits must come from the appropriate engine section.

steps.title: Position the top ring
steps.body: Carefully place the top piston ring into its cylinder. Use a piston without rings to push it to the bottom of ring travel, establishing the specified measuring position without damaging the ring or bore.

steps.title: Measure both ring gaps
steps.body: Measure the top ring's end clearance with the feeler gauge. Position the second ring in the same manner and measure its end gap. Keep the readings identified by cylinder and ring position.

steps.title: Decide whether the fit is acceptable
steps.body: Compare each reading with its corresponding specification. Resolve an out-of-specification result through the applicable engine repair requirements before assembly; this checking procedure provides no ring-modification method.

watchFor.title: Ring or bore damage
watchFor.body: Handle rings carefully during insertion and positioning. Do not transfer rings between pistons.

notes: Keep foreign material out of engine components throughout the work.

diagnostics.finding: Cylinder taper or out-of-round is outside specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The bore does not meet the prerequisite for accepting ring fit.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the bore condition using the applicable engine specifications and repair procedure.

diagnostics.finding: Either ring gap is outside its specified limits.
diagnostics.meaning: That ring-and-bore combination has not passed the fit check.
diagnostics.next: Determine the permitted corrective work; replace a component that cannot be restored to specification.

verification.title: Record the fit decision
verification.body: Record the cylinder, ring position, measured gap, applicable limits and acceptance result. Confirm both rings were checked at the bottom of ring travel.

procedures.purpose: Top and second piston ring end-gap checking method for the listed engines.
Engine identification, contamination precautions and specification-based repair decisions.

guides.title: Select a replacement piston to match the cylinder bore
guides.summary: Confirm acceptable bore geometry, measure the bore in two directions and select the matching piston size and fit grade.
guides.introduction: A piston must move within its cylinder with the fit specified for that engine. Selecting a replacement therefore starts with the cylinder's measured condition. This check chooses both the piston size range and the finer grade within that range; it is one stage of engine repair, before fitting the piston.
guides.why: Taper means the bore diameter changes along its depth; out-of-round means it differs around its circumference. Choosing a piston cannot correct either condition. The bore must meet both limits before its measurements can be used for piston selection.
searchTerms: cylinder taper and out of round

when.summary: When a replacement piston must be matched to a cylinder during engine repair.

prepare.title: Identify the engine and specifications
prepare.detail: Use the correct engine identification and the applicable Section 303-01 specifications. Bore limits and piston-grade interpretation must match that engine.

prepare.title: Prepare for precision measurement
prepare.detail: The bore must be accessible, and engine parts must be free of contamination. Have suitable bore-measuring equipment and the skill to assess taper and out-of-round.

steps.title: Establish that the bore is suitable
steps.body: Confirm that cylinder taper and out-of-round are within the engine-specific limits before fitting a piston. If the bore fails those limits, resolve its condition through the appropriate refinishing or replacement path first.

steps.title: Measure in both indicated directions
steps.body: Measure the cylinder bore in the two directions shown in the [piston-selection check](#/document/G1661753). These measurements establish the bore size used for selection; they do not replace the prerequisite geometry checks.

steps.title: Choose the piston size range
steps.body: Select the piston size from the measured, acceptable cylinder bore using the applicable engine specifications. Do not choose solely from the marking on the removed piston.

steps.title: Choose the grade within that size
steps.body: New pistons are divided into three categories within each size range for a more precise fit. Choose the piston with the correct paint spot or specific size-grade marking, and associate that selection with the cylinder measured.

watchFor.title: A size choice made before bore acceptance
watchFor.body: A piston selected from one diameter does not make an excessively tapered or out-of-round cylinder acceptable.

watchFor.title: An unidentified grade
watchFor.body: The broad size range alone does not complete selection. Verify the paint marking or specific grade against the engine requirements.

notes: If a component is outside specification and cannot be refinished, the engine guidance calls for a new component. Keep all engine repair parts contamination-free.

diagnostics.finding: Cylinder taper or out-of-round exceeds the applicable limit.
diagnostics.meaning: The bore is not ready for piston fitting.
diagnostics.next: Determine the permitted refinishing or replacement action before selecting the final piston.

verification.title: Record the selection
verification.body: Record the cylinder identification, bore readings, accepted geometry checks, selected piston size and paint color or size grade.

verification.title: Confirm the basis for fit
verification.body: Check that the selected size and grade correspond to the measured bore and the correct engine specifications.

procedures.purpose: General bore measurement and piston size/grade selection check.
Engine identification, cleanliness and out-of-specification component guidance.

guides.title: Neutralize the powertrain and drivetrain mounts
guides.summary: Allow the installed powertrain and drivetrain mounts to settle through a prescribed vehicle movement before securing their fasteners.
guides.introduction: The mounts support the engine and drivetrain while accommodating movement between these assemblies and the vehicle. Neutralizing adjusts their installed position so they are not held twisted or strained. The mounts remain installed: their fasteners are loosened, the vehicle moves a short distance forward and backward, and the fasteners are tightened again.
guides.why: A mount can be damaged if the adjustment twists or strains it. The controlled movement provides the settling action, while the mount-specific fastening instructions determine how to loosen and secure the assembly correctly for the particular engine and drivetrain.

when.summary: When the repair being performed calls for neutralizing the installed powertrain or drivetrain mounts.
notes: This adjustment provides no stand-alone diagnosis of a failed mount.

prepare.title: Mount-specific instructions
prepare.detail: Have the correct loosening and tightening instructions for the fitted engine, drivetrain and mounts available before beginning. They govern any special fastening requirements.

prepare.title: Access and controlled movement
prepare.detail: Arrange the fastening tools and access required by those instructions, together with a clear area in which the vehicle can travel the prescribed distance in both directions.

steps.title: Loosen the specified mount fasteners
steps.body: Use the [neutralizing procedure](#/document/G1661756) together with the applicable mount instructions. Loosen the powertrain and drivetrain mount fasteners, but do not remove them. Retaining the fasteners is an explicit condition of this adjustment.

steps.title: Let the assemblies settle
steps.body: Start the vehicle and move forward 0.6–1.2 m. Then reverse the same distance. Throughout this movement, avoid twisting or straining the mounts; the purpose is to settle their installed position without damaging them.

steps.title: Secure the mounts
steps.body: Tighten the powertrain and drivetrain mount fasteners using the instructions for the actual mounts fitted. Complete the prescribed fastening before proceeding to the normal-operation test.

steps.title: Test normal operation
steps.body: Test the system for normal operation after tightening. Assess the result of the adjustment rather than assuming that completing the forward-and-reverse movement has resolved the reason for the work.

watchFor.title: Mount distortion
watchFor.body: Do not continue an adjustment that twists or strains a mount; the procedure specifically warns that this can cause damage.

watchFor.title: Unspecified fastening details
watchFor.body: The general neutralizing procedure supplies no universal mount torque. Use the engine- and mount-specific instructions.

verification.title: Fastening complete
verification.body: Confirm that every loosened mount fastener has been tightened according to its applicable procedure.

verification.title: Record the operating result
verification.body: Record whether normal operation was restored and whether the concern that prompted the adjustment remains.

procedures.purpose: General mount-neutralizing adjustment, including the movement sequence and requirement for mount-specific fastening instructions.

guides.title: Clean and prepare metal engine surfaces for RTV sealing
guides.summary: Remove old sealant and contamination, then prepare the metal joint surfaces so fresh RTV can form a reliable seal.
guides.introduction: Room-temperature-vulcanizing silicone, usually called RTV, seals joints between engine components. Its ability to seal depends on the condition of both mating surfaces: old silicone, oil and cleaning residue can interfere with adhesion. This job prepares metal surfaces for resealing; sealant application and component assembly follow the relevant engine repair procedure.
guides.why: Scratches can become leak paths, while cleaning debris entering an oil passage can cause engine damage. Cleaning also has a specific chemical sequence: brake cleaner removes oil, Motorcraft Engine Shampoo and Degreaser removes residual brake cleaner, and the final preparation wipe leaves a coating that improves the base for RTV.

when.summary: When a metal engine joint is being opened and resealed with RTV.
notes: This process does not apply to composite or plastic components.
Access, sealant selection and assembly requirements remain specific to the component being repaired.

prepare.title: Gather the cleaning equipment
prepare.detail: Have plastic scrapers or plastic razor blades, clean lint-free towels and isopropyl alcohol of at least 90 percent strength. Latex gloves are recommended to reduce surface contamination.

prepare.title: Arrange the cleaning products in order
prepare.detail: Prepare silicone gasket remover, the specified brake cleaner, Motorcraft Engine Shampoo and Degreaser ZC-20, and Motorcraft Metal Surface Prep Wipes ZC-31-B. Use the specified Motorcraft shampoo; another brand can compromise the seal.

steps.title: Protect the engine and control oil drain-down
steps.body: Cover exposed cavities with clean lint-free towels. For oil-pan repairs, first flush residual oil from the block interior, skirt stiffener and drain-back ports with brake cleaner, then wipe away bulk oil and cleaner. This reduces contamination arriving after the joint has been cleaned.

steps.title: Remove the old silicone
steps.body: Lift loose sealant by hand or with a plastic scraper or razor blade. Apply gasket remover and let it work for several minutes. Remove the softened residue with a lint-free towel and plastic tool, repeating the remover application as needed.

steps.title: Use a bristle disc only under the permitted conditions
steps.body: A grade 120 nylon bristle disc may be used only on parts removed from both the engine and vehicle that can be thoroughly washed and cleaned afterward. Remove all tool debris before installation. Do not use this method where debris could enter the engine.

steps.title: Remove oil and cleaning residue
steps.body: For oil-pan repairs, repeat the internal brake-cleaner flush and wipe away bulk liquid. Clean the sealing surfaces with brake cleaner, wipe dry and inspect for remaining oil. Then use Motorcraft Engine Shampoo and Degreaser and dry with a clean lint-free towel.

steps.title: Apply the final preparation coating
steps.body: Apply Metal Surface Prep Wipes only to dry surfaces. Moisten the entire metal area that will receive RTV, then discard the wipe after its single use. Allow the coating to air dry for approximately 2 minutes; do not rinse it or dry it with a towel.

steps.title: Correct contamination before assembly
steps.body: If the prepared surface becomes contaminated, or preparation fluid beads up, clean the affected area with a lint-free towel soaked in the specified isopropyl alcohol. Apply a fresh preparation wipe and air dry again. Remove protective towels carefully without dropping debris into cavities.

watchFor.title: Tools that create leak paths
watchFor.body: Do not use metal scrapers, wire brushes, power sanding or grinding discs, or abrasives other than the specifically permitted nylon bristle disc.

watchFor.title: Contamination after the final wipe
watchFor.body: Toweling the final coating can contaminate the surface. Keep the prepared joint clean until the component-specific sealing operation.

notes: Use the complete cleaning procedure for product selection and the exact sequence.

diagnostics.finding: Oil remains visible after brake cleaning.
diagnostics.meaning: The surface is not ready for the remaining preparation stages.
diagnostics.next: Remove the contamination before proceeding.

diagnostics.finding: Preparation fluid beads on the metal.
diagnostics.meaning: The affected area requires cleaning and preparation again.
diagnostics.next: Use the specified alcohol cleaning and fresh preparation-wipe sequence.

verification.title: Confirm readiness for RTV
verification.body: Check that the prepared surfaces have air dried, remain uncontaminated and have no remaining sealant or oil. Confirm that cleaning debris has not been left in exposed cavities or on removed parts.

procedures.purpose: Complete metal RTV sealing-surface cleaning and preparation procedure, including the oil-pan and removed-part branches.

guides.title: Measure valve-guide wear before deciding on cylinder-head replacement
guides.summary: Measure each valve-guide bore in two directions at three depths and compare the results with the correct engine specification.
guides.introduction: A valve guide supports the valve stem as the valve moves. Its bore can wear unevenly, so a single diameter reading cannot describe its condition. This check maps the bore along its length and determines whether the cylinder-head assembly meets the engine's dimensional requirements.
guides.why: Valve guides tend to develop an hourglass wear pattern: the middle can differ from the ends. Measuring at the top, middle and bottom, in two directions, reveals variation that a single convenient measurement could miss.

when.summary: During cylinder-head repair when valve-guide bore wear must be assessed.
notes: The applicable engine specification is required before a measurement can be classified as acceptable.

prepare.title: Obtain the correct limits
prepare.detail: Identify the engine and obtain its valve-guide specification from the appropriate Section 303-01. The general measurement procedure supplies no universal diameter limit.

prepare.title: Prepare for precision measurement
prepare.detail: Provide a ball gauge, micrometer and access to the guide bore. Keep engine parts contamination-free. Engine-specific dismantling and reassembly are separate from this dimensional check.

prepare.title: Workshop capability
prepare.detail: Accessible cylinder-head valve guides, a ball gauge and a micrometer; engine-specific diameter specifications required.

steps.title: Set up an identifiable measurement record
steps.body: Identify the guide being checked and provide separate entries for each direction at the top, middle and bottom. Keeping locations distinct allows the eventual decision to reflect the whole bore rather than an isolated reading.

steps.title: Gauge the bore at every required location
steps.body: Follow the [valve-guide diameter check](#/document/G1661754), using the ball gauge in two directions at each depth. If access requires it, insert the gauge from the combustion-chamber side. Do not omit an end measurement because the middle appears satisfactory.

steps.title: Measure the gauge with the micrometer
steps.body: For each gauged position, measure the ball gauge with the micrometer and record the resulting diameter against its location and direction. The gauge captures the internal size; the micrometer supplies the dimensional reading.

steps.title: Apply the engine-specific replacement decision
steps.body: Compare the recorded diameters with the appropriate specification. If a valve guide is outside specification, this procedure directs installation of a new cylinder-head assembly. It does not provide a guide-refinishing or separate guide-replacement route.

watchFor.title: A satisfactory middle reading hiding worn ends
watchFor.body: An hourglass pattern is the reason all specified depths must be checked.

notes: The illustration explains the general inspection area; it does not establish a diameter limit or an exact engine variant.

diagnostics.finding: A valve guide is outside the applicable diameter specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The cylinder head fails this guide-diameter check.
diagnostics.next: Install a new cylinder-head assembly as directed.

diagnostics.finding: All required readings meet specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The guide passes this dimensional check.
diagnostics.next: Retain the results; this finding does not establish the condition of unrelated cylinder-head features.

verification.title: Record a traceable decision
verification.body: Confirm both directions at every required depth are recorded, along with the engine specification used and the resulting pass or replacement decision.

procedures.purpose: General valve-guide bore measurement and cylinder-head replacement criterion.

guides.title: Measure valve stem diameter during engine repair
guides.summary: Measure each intake and exhaust valve stem at the illustrated positions and compare every reading with the identified engine's specification.
guides.introduction: A valve stem guides the valve's movement as its head opens and closes the intake or exhaust passage. Stem diameter is therefore one part of assessing whether the valve remains suitable for service. This job is a dimensional check on accessible valves during engine repair. It does not describe cylinder-head disassembly or valve removal.
guides.why: One reading does not cover all the positions specified along the stem. Measuring each illustrated location gives the required basis for comparison. The acceptance limits must come from the correct engine section; a general measurement procedure does not establish a common limit for every engine.

when.summary: During engine repair when intake and exhaust valves are accessible for dimensional inspection.
notes: Use the appropriate engine repair procedure to obtain access before beginning this check.

prepare.title: Identify the engine and limits
prepare.detail: Obtain the applicable valve-stem specification from the engine's Section 303-01 before deciding whether readings pass.

prepare.title: Prepare clean parts and measurement capability
prepare.detail: Keep the valves and working area contamination free. Arrange equipment capable of measuring stem outside diameter accurately enough for the applicable limits.

steps.title: Identify the valve being checked
steps.body: Associate each result with the individual intake or exhaust valve so that the final decision applies to the correct component.

steps.title: Locate the illustrated measurement positions
steps.body: Use the [valve-stem check illustration](#/document/G1661755). Its arrows identify upper, middle and lower positions along the stem. Measure at those positions rather than choosing a single convenient point.

steps.title: Measure every intake and exhaust valve
steps.body: Measure and record the stem diameter at each indicated position for every valve. Keep the individual readings available for comparison.

steps.title: Compare and decide
steps.body: Verify each diameter against the appropriate engine specification. If a component fails specification, determine whether permitted refinishing is possible; install a new component when it cannot be refinished to specification.

watchFor.title: Unconfirmed acceptance limits
watchFor.body: Do not make a reuse decision using a remembered limit or a specification from another engine.

notes: This diameter check does not by itself establish the condition of every other part of the valve assembly.

diagnostics.finding: All specified stem readings meet the applicable limits
diagnostics.meaning: The valve passes this dimensional check.
diagnostics.next: Retain the results with the component's inspection record.

diagnostics.finding: A stem reading falls outside specification
diagnostics.meaning: The component does not meet the dimensional requirement.
diagnostics.next: Assess permitted refinishing or replace the component if it cannot be brought within specification.

verification.title: Complete the measurement record
verification.body: Confirm every intake and exhaust valve has readings for all illustrated positions, the applicable limits and a recorded disposition.

procedures.purpose: Valve-stem diameter measurement locations and specification comparison.
General engine cleanliness, identification and out-of-specification component requirements.

guides.title: Overhaul the 2.3L EcoBoost engine
guides.summary: Remove, inspect and rebuild the 2.3L EcoBoost engine, then reinstall it and complete the required checks and misfire-monitor correction.
guides.introduction: This turbocharged, direct-injection engine uses overhead camshafts to operate the valves and a pressure-fed lubrication system to protect its bearings, timing components and turbocharger. An overhaul opens these systems for inspection and measured rebuilding. It combines vehicle removal, precision bench work, engine timing and final commissioning; each phase depends on the preceding work being correct.
guides.why: The crankshaft pulley and timing sprocket rely on friction rather than locating keys. Loosening the pulley bolt releases that relationship, so incorrect positioning can damage valves and pistons. Cleanliness, bearing selection and controlled assembly also matter: debris or an incorrect clearance can undermine an otherwise careful rebuild.

when.summary: When internal damage or measured wear justifies engine removal, inspection and rebuilding.
notes: Confirm engine identification before ordering parts; build revisions affect the crankshaft sprocket and timing-chain tensioner.
Choose the transmission branch throughout removal, bench work and installation.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and precision assembly capability
prepare.detail: Provide a vehicle hoist, engine crane and lifting brackets, mounting stand, transmission support, measuring equipment, torque-and-angle tools, piston ring compressor, timing tools and the specified seal and injector tools. A compatible diagnostic scan tool is needed at completion.

prepare.title: Make the vehicle and fuel system ready
prepare.detail: Follow the lifting procedure with the vehicle in NEUTRAL. Use the specified lifting points and never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Release fuel pressure, disconnect the battery ground and drain the cooling system and engine oil in the removal sequence. Plan the matching fuel-system restoration and leak checks before any commissioning step starts the engine.

prepare.title: Organize parts and replacement supplies
prepare.detail: Provide clean, identified storage for bearings, caps, tappets and shims. Prepare the specified sealants and every replacement required by the discard instructions, including fasteners, seals, gaskets, the high-pressure fuel tube, cylinder-head temperature sensor and turbocharger oil supply filter.

steps.title: Remove the engine with the transmission supported
steps.body: Follow [engine removal](#/document/G1660475). Mark the hood position, remove the access components and disconnect the cooling, intake, fuel, vacuum and electrical connections. Support the air-conditioning compressor aside. For the 6R80, mark a converter stud against the flexplate and discard the converter nuts, rotating the crankshaft only clockwise. Fit the lifting brackets and crane, support the transmission bellhousing with the jack and wooden block, then release the remaining mounting connections in sequence and lift out the engine.

steps.title: Mount the engine and strip its external systems
steps.body: Use [engine disassembly](#/document/G1660477). Remove the automatic flexplate or manual clutch and flywheel before mounting the engine on its stand. Discard the specified fasteners; loosen the clutch pressure plate evenly and control friction dust without compressed air. Remove the harness, manifolds, turbocharger, cooling parts and accessories in order. When opening the high-pressure fuel tube, wrap the pump flare nut with a shop towel to catch residual fuel; discard the tube. Extract injectors along their axes with the specified tools.

steps.title: Secure timing before opening the valve train
steps.body: Establish top dead center using the crankshaft timing peg and camshaft alignment tool before loosening the pulley bolt. Follow the alignment retry sequence if the camshaft tool will not fit. Hold the pulley with the strap wrench and use the specified impact equipment for removal; discard its bolt and washer. Remove the timing drive and variable camshaft timing units. Record camshaft lobe positions, cap orientation and tappet locations, then release the camshaft caps progressively in the illustrated sequence before removing the head.

steps.title: Expose and inspect the lower engine
steps.body: Remove the sump, pickup, rear seal and oil-pump drive. Index the balance shaft assembly at top dead center and preserve its shim positions; do not dismantle the assembly. Identify connecting rods, caps and bearings before removing the pistons and crankshaft. Protect cylinder walls and journals throughout. Inspect pistons and check cylinder-head and block distortion through the referenced procedures. Clean head-gasket faces with a plastic scraper, clear bolt holes and keep debris out of oil and coolant passages.

steps.title: Measure and assemble the crankshaft, pistons and balancer
steps.body: Follow [engine assembly](#/document/G1660482). Record journal and housing measurements and use its charts to select bearings. Original bearing-beam and connecting-rod bolts are used for the prescribed measuring stages, then discarded before final assembly with new bolts. Lubricate bearings, retain any reused bearing positions and perform the crankshaft fore-and-aft positioning before tightening the beam. Measure end play. Install correctly oriented pistons with the specified ring-gap arrangement and verify smooth crankshaft rotation after each rod cap. Refit the indexed balancer and shims, check gear meshing and measure backlash at every specified crankshaft position.

steps.title: Build the lubrication system and cylinder head
steps.body: Return the crankshaft to the prescribed timing position. Prime the oil pump with clean engine oil and turn it by hand before installation. Assemble its drive using the correct sprocket-and-washer branch, then fit the rear seal, pickup with a new gasket and aligned oil pan. Install the head with a new gasket and new torque-to-yield bolts. If the head, valves, tappets or camshafts are new, follow the complete piston-positioning and valve-clearance sequence, record each clearance and select tappets accordingly. Original reused parts follow the separate assembly branch.

steps.title: Complete camshaft timing and front sealing
steps.body: Install lubricated camshafts in their recorded orientation, applying the prescribed rear-cap sealant and progressive tightening sequence. Fit the alignment tool, new variable camshaft timing unit bolts and timing drive. Reset the fitted tensioner by its own procedure and release its pin only after tightening its bolts. Counterhold the camshafts with a wrench when tightening the timing units. Seal the front cover, install the front seal and align the pulley. Keep the crankshaft at top dead center while tightening its new bolt and washer with hand tools and a universal pulley holder. Align the crankshaft position sensor with its specified tool.

steps.title: Restore fuel delivery and external assemblies
steps.body: Fit new injector seals using the installation and sizing tools. Keep lower Teflon seals dry and install injectors within 15 minutes of sizing; seat the rail by hand without impact and use new rail bolts. Fit the high-pressure pump drive at zero cam lift, inspect its tappet, and install the pump with a new O-ring, new bolts and new fuel tube. Restore the separator, correctly oriented knock sensors, covers, new cylinder-head temperature sensor, vacuum pump, cooling system, accessories and turbocharger. Renew discarded turbocharger hardware, filter and seals; fully seat oil tubes before tightening and fit the lower coolant inlet tube first. Finish the intake, harness and transmission-specific flywheel/clutch or flexplate assembly using the specified special fasteners.

steps.title: Install and reconnect the engine
steps.body: Follow [engine installation](#/document/G1660484), including lubrication of the automatic converter pilot or manual input shaft. Align the marked automatic converter stud with the flexplate. Transfer support between crane, transmission support and the prescribed engine support as directed while securing mounts and transmission attachments. Renew converter nuts where applicable and the catalytic-converter gasket and nuts. Restore grounds, starter, supported compressor, hoses, fuel couplings, wiring, intake connections and hood using its index marks.

steps.title: Fill and commission the completed assembly
steps.body: Install a new oil filter, reconnect the battery and fill with the engine oil specified for this engine. Before any engine-running cooling-system or commissioning step, complete [fuel-system restoration](#/document/G1671508): reconnect the fuel pump driver module (FPDM), restore the rear seat cushion, cycle the ignition and wait 3 seconds to pressurize the system. Check for fuel leaks before starting. Start only after that check and check again for fuel leaks while running. Complete the cooling-system vacuum-filling and bleeding procedure and restore the underbody shield in its specified sequence. Check the exhaust for leaks. Run the Powertrain Control Module misfire monitor profile correction routine with the diagnostic scan tool, then road-test the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Alignment tools cannot substitute for counterholding
watchFor.body: The camshaft alignment tool is for positioning only. The crankshaft peg prevents travel past top dead center in one direction but does not prevent reverse rotation. Follow the separate pulley removal and installation holding methods.

watchFor.title: Sprocket and tensioner revisions
watchFor.body: Flat-faced sprockets require diamond washers on both sides; inspect and reuse undamaged washers. Laser-etched sprockets must never have them. Replacing an early sprocket means fitting the laser-etched service part and discarding its diamond washers. A cast-iron tensioner requiring replacement becomes an aluminum unit with new bolts.

watchFor.title: Different tensioner reset mechanisms
watchFor.body: For an aluminum tensioner, spread the ratchet wire clip, compress the plunger in a soft-jawed vise and pin the body. The cast-iron procedure separately compresses the plunger and releases and retracts the ratchet before pinning; never compress its ratchet assembly.

watchFor.title: Sealant timing and contamination
watchFor.body: The oil pan, front cover, valve cover and sealed rear camshaft caps have 10-minute securing requirements. Follow the specified cleaning and reapplication instructions if a window is missed. Keep sealant out of bearing journals and remove excess from pump mounting faces.

notes: Maintain a replacement checklist through disassembly: clutch/flywheel or flexplate fasteners, bearing bolts, head bolts, timing-unit bolts, pulley hardware, fuel-system consumables, discarded turbocharger hardware, crankshaft seals and specified gaskets must not be returned to service.
Some gaskets and O-rings are inspection-dependent rather than automatic replacements. Follow each assembly instruction, including the valve-cover solenoid seals and intake-manifold gaskets.
Do not clean injector tips with compressed air or the injector-bore brush. Replace the fuel rail pressure sensor if it is removed from the rail.

diagnostics.finding: Crankshaft end play is outside the specified range.
diagnostics.meaning: The assembled crankshaft does not meet the required axial-clearance check.
diagnostics.next: Record the measurement and install new parts as necessary before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: Balance shaft damage, rough rotation or unacceptable gear backlash is found.
diagnostics.meaning: A damaged assembly requires replacement; an incorrect backlash measurement requires the dedicated adjustment procedure.
diagnostics.next: Do not dismantle the balancer. Use the Balance Shaft Backlash procedure when the measured clearance is outside specification.

diagnostics.finding: The high-pressure fuel pump tappet has flat spots or scoring.
diagnostics.meaning: The contacting pump and drive-lobe components also require inspection.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the pump and tappet drive lobe and replace damaged components as necessary.

diagnostics.finding: Metal debris is present in the intake manifold following upper-engine failure.
diagnostics.meaning: Retained debris can damage the rebuilt engine.
diagnostics.next: Install a new intake manifold.

verification.title: Keep a measured assembly record
verification.body: Record bearing-selection measurements, crankshaft end play, all specified balancer backlash readings and valve clearances when that branch applies. Resolve unacceptable results before closing the engine.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical assembly checks
verification.body: Confirm smooth rotation after each connecting-rod cap and correct balancer gear meshing. Account for removal of timing and alignment tools and completion of the specified tightening sequences.

verification.title: Record commissioning results
verification.body: Record restoration of the FPDM connection and both the pre-start and running fuel-leak checks. Also record the exhaust leak check, completion of the misfire monitor profile correction routine and the road-test result.
