guides.title: Remove, overhaul and refit the 2.3L EcoBoost cylinder head
guides.summary: Combine cylinder-head removal, valve and injector bench work, and installation while preserving timing, sealing surfaces and component locations.
guides.introduction: The aluminum cylinder head carries the valves and camshafts and houses the direct fuel injectors. Its gasket seals the joint to the block, while internal passages carry oil and coolant. Overhaul combines several separate skills: engine timing, condition assessment, controlled valve-spring work and precise injector sealing. The extent of replacement depends on inspection findings.
guides.why: Debris in internal passages can cause engine failure, and scratches across an aluminum sealing face can create leak paths. Reused valve-train parts must return to their original locations. The crankshaft pulley and timing sprocket rely on friction clamping rather than a key, so loosening the pulley bolt without the prescribed locking tools can lose timing and damage the engine.

when.summary: When established cylinder-head, gasket or valve repair requires head removal and inspection.
notes: Use inspection results to determine replacement parts; this operation does not itself diagnose the original complaint.

prepare.title: Prepare for engine and fuel-system work
prepare.detail: Provide a correctly positioned hoist, oil-drain equipment, hose-clamp tools and the engine-specific timing equipment. Have the fuel-pressure release, battery, cooling, intake, camshaft and turbocharger procedures ready.

prepare.title: Set up a protected bench
prepare.detail: Protect the head's gasket face and organize location-marked parts storage. Provide the specified valve-spring compressor set and adapters, valve-seal tools, injector extractor and slide hammer, bore brush, seal installer and Teflon-seal sizer.

prepare.title: Plan replacement parts
prepare.detail: Provide new head bolts and gasket, fuel-rail bolts, injector sealing parts and clips, cylinder-head temperature sensor, coolant-outlet gasket, the mandatory coolant-tube O-ring and oil filter. Replace other parts according to inspection.

steps.title: Isolate the vehicle and establish timing access
steps.body: Place the vehicle in NEUTRAL on the hoist and remove the appearance cover. Release fuel pressure, disconnect the battery ground and drain coolant through the 2.3L procedures. Remove the turbocharger, intake manifold and camshafts. Never loosen the crankshaft pulley bolt before installing the required crankshaft and camshaft locking tools.

steps.title: Disconnect the head and preserve component locations
steps.body: Remove and identify the tappets for reuse. Detach the fuel-rail wiring, insulator shield, injector and fuel-rail pressure sensor connections, coolant-temperature connections and crankcase-vent tube connections. Disconnect the specified coolant tubes, radiator, bypass and heater hoses, and ground wire. Discard the designated coolant-tube O-ring; inspect the other tube O-ring and replace it if necessary.

steps.title: Lift the head and assess the joint
steps.body: Remove the head and discard its bolts and gasket. Clean the mating faces with a plastic scraper; do not use metal scrapers, wire brushes or abrasive discs. Clear coolant, oil and debris from the block's bolt holes. Check both head and block distortion using their dedicated procedures before deciding the joint is suitable for assembly.

steps.title: Strip the head and extract the injectors
steps.body: Remove the coolant outlet, discard its gasket, remove the ground connection and discard the cylinder-head temperature sensor. Clean around the fuel rail before opening it. Withdraw the rail along the injector axes and discard its bolts. Extract injectors remaining in the head with the specified remover and slide hammer. Remove the clips and sealing parts; pull each lower Teflon seal away from the injector before carefully cutting it.

steps.title: Disassemble and inspect the valves
steps.body: Clear the spark-plug wells before removing the plugs. Use the specified spring tools to release the collets, retainers and springs, then remove the stem seals and valves. Keep reusable parts identified. Inspect seats, stem ends, valve faces, edges, heads and margins for scoring, pitting, burning, erosion, distortion, cracks and wear; renew defective parts.

steps.title: Rebuild the valve assemblies
steps.body: Oil the valve stems and return reused valves to their original positions. Lubricate the stem seals and install them with the specified installer. Refit springs, retainers and collets with the compressor tools and specified multipurpose grease, checking collet seating. Install the spark plugs to the bench procedure's specification; discard any plug that has been dropped.

steps.title: Prepare and size the injector seals
steps.body: Clean injector bores with the dedicated brush, but never brush or use compressed air on injector tips. Fit new lower Teflon seals dry with the installer, transferring each seal from the guide immediately. Seat it fully in its groove. Apply the sizer with its larger opening toward the seal, turning 180 degrees while pushing; after one minute, turn it back 180 degrees and remove it. Install injectors into the head within 15 minutes of sizing.

steps.title: Finish the injector and bench assembly
steps.body: Fit the injector seal and a new fuel-resistant O-ring, lubricating only the O-ring with clean engine oil. Fit the clip with its anti-rotation finger engaged in the rail-cup groove. Install the rail by pressing above the injectors and use new bolts. Replace the fuel-rail pressure sensor if removed from the rail. Install a new cylinder-head temperature sensor, the ground connection and the outlet with a new gasket.

steps.title: Install the head and restore connections
steps.body: Fit a new head gasket and new torque-to-yield head bolts using the complete illustrated tightening sequence. Reconnect the coolant plumbing and ground. Lubricate tube O-rings with clean coolant and fully seat the specified tube before tightening its bolt. Restore the wiring, sensor insulation, vent tube and rail shield. Oil and refit tappets in their original locations, then install camshafts, intake manifold and turbocharger through their procedures.

steps.title: Renew fluids and complete the repair
steps.body: Drain the engine oil, reinstall the drain plug and replace the oil filter, lubricating its seal with clean oil. Fill with the specified engine oil. Reconnect the battery, fill and bleed the 2.3L cooling system, reinstall the appearance cover and road test the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Injector body damage
watchFor.body: A knife must not contact the injector while cutting its lower seal. Nicks or gouges compromise the precision sealing area.

watchFor.title: Uncontrolled spring release
watchFor.body: Use the prescribed compressor tooling and verify collet seating during assembly.

notes: Do not rest the unprotected gasket face on the bench.
Use the separate bench and vehicle-installation tightening instructions; similarly named fasteners can belong to different joints.

diagnostics.finding: Valve burning, cracking, scoring or excessive wear is found.
diagnostics.meaning: The affected part requires a serviceability decision.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the associated seat and install new parts as necessary.

diagnostics.finding: Head or block distortion is suspected.
diagnostics.meaning: A clean surface alone does not establish an acceptable gasket joint.
diagnostics.next: Complete the linked distortion measurements before installation.

verification.title: Confirm assembly details before closure
verification.body: Check collet seating, component locations, injector clip engagement, seal-sizing timing and installation of all required new parts.

verification.title: Record the completed result
verification.body: Retain distortion findings and replacement decisions, and record completion of timing assembly, fluid servicing and the required road test.

guides.title: Rebuild piston assemblies: 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Renew piston rings and pin retainers while preserving the piston-to-rod relationship and each engine’s specific assembly details.
guides.introduction: The piston receives combustion pressure and transfers that force through its pin to the connecting rod. Compression rings seal against the cylinder wall, while oil-control rings regulate the oil film. This bench overhaul separates those parts for inspection and rebuilds the assembly. It begins with the piston assembly already removed; engine dismantling and installation into the cylinder are separate operations.
guides.why: These engines share the same basic arrangement, but their assembly details differ. Ring facing, gap placement and piston orientation establish the intended sealing arrangement. Pin-retainer gap direction is particularly easy to confuse: the 5.2L requirement is opposite to the stated 3.7L and 5.0L requirement.

when.summary: During engine overhaul when piston assemblies need inspection, new rings or replacement pistons or connecting rods.
notes: Select the procedure for the actual engine before choosing parts or beginning assembly.

prepare.title: Arrange engine bench-work capability
prepare.detail: Have the removed assembly, a clean working area and the Piston Inspection procedure available. Inspection must establish whether existing components can be retained.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement parts
prepare.detail: Obtain new piston rings and piston pin retainers. Both are discarded during dismantling, even when the piston and connecting rod will be reused.

prepare.title: Use the correct assembly oil
prepare.detail: The 3.7L specifies SAE 5W-20 synthetic blend oil meeting WSS-M2C945-B1; the 5.2L specifies Motorcraft SAE 5W-50 full synthetic oil meeting WSS-M2C931-E1. The 2.3L and 5.0L instructions call for clean engine oil; do not borrow another variant’s specification.

steps.title: Record the original relationship
steps.body: Before separating a piston and connecting rod intended for reuse, mark their relative orientation. Keep that relationship identifiable throughout inspection so the parts can be reunited as originally assembled.

steps.title: Dismantle the assembly
steps.body: Remove and discard the rings, then remove and discard the pin retainers. Withdraw the piston pin and separate the piston from the connecting rod.

steps.title: Inspect before rebuilding
steps.body: Follow [Piston Inspection](#/document/G1661751). The 3.7L procedure calls for inspection of the piston and rod; the 5.0L and 5.2L procedures also explicitly require cleaning them. Resolve their suitability before fitting new rings.

steps.title: Orient the piston and rod
steps.body: Restore the marks on reused components. With new 3.7L or 5.0L components, the rod orientation marks and piston crown arrow face the engine front. On the 5.2L, identify the left-hand or right-hand piston, then face its crown arrow and the connecting-rod bump toward the engine front.

steps.title: Fit the pin and new retainers
steps.body: Position the piston on its rod, lubricate the pin with the appropriate clean oil and install it. Fit new retainers. Their gaps face the piston crown on the 3.7L and 5.0L, but the piston bottom on the 5.2L. Follow the 2.3L procedure separately.

steps.title: Install the oil-control rings
steps.body: Lubricate and fit the oil-control components using the matching procedure. The 5.2L explicitly sequences the lower oil-control ring, expander and upper ring. Keep each engine’s ring arrangement separate.

steps.title: Install the compression rings
steps.body: On the 3.7L, both compression-ring “O” marks face the crown. On the 5.0L, install the lower ring with its “O” upward and hook downward, then the upper ring with its “O” upward. The 5.2L uses the same stated facing directions with identification marks. Use the separate 2.3L instructions.

steps.title: Set the ring gaps
steps.body: Use the engine-specific assembly layout for exact gap placement. The 2.3L identifies both oil segments and the spacer. The 3.7L and 5.0L layouts group the expander and lower-compression gap location. The 5.2L identifies all gaps separately, referencing the expander to a centerline parallel to the pin bore.

watchFor.title: Opposite retainer directions
watchFor.body: Do not carry the 3.7L or 5.0L crown-facing retainer-gap rule into a 5.2L assembly.

watchFor.title: Missing orientation information
watchFor.body: Resolve uncertain piston-to-rod orientation before assembly; resemblance between engines is insufficient.

notes: The ring-removal illustration identifies discarded components; use the assembly procedure for gap placement.

verification.title: Check the completed bench assembly
verification.body: Confirm piston orientation, new retainers, correct retainer-gap direction, ring facing and the prescribed ring-gap layout before proceeding with engine assembly.

guides.title: Check and adjust balance-shaft gear backlash on the 2.3L EcoBoost
guides.summary: Measure balancer gear clearance with master shims, select the required adjustment shims and verify backlash at every specified crankshaft position.
guides.introduction: The balance shafts help counter the shaking forces of the four-cylinder engine. The crankshaft drives the balancer through gears, and backlash is the small free movement between their mating teeth. This procedure adjusts that clearance with mounting shims while preserving the balancer's timing.
guides.why: Gear clearance must be checked around the rotation, not at one convenient position. The specified measuring height and control of crankshaft movement make the readings repeatable; the timing marks preserve the relationship between the crankshaft and balance shafts.

when.summary: When checking or adjusting balancer gear clearance during internal work on the 2.3L EcoBoost engine.
notes: This procedure begins with access to the balancer unit and crankshaft gears and ends with verified backlash.

prepare.title: Prepare for precision engine work
prepare.detail: You need the capability to position the crankshaft accurately, remove and refit the balancer, and obtain repeatable dial-indicator readings. Use the engine identification information when obtaining replacement parts.

prepare.title: Gather the specified equipment
prepare.detail: Use crankshaft timing peg 303-507, holding fixture with dial indicator 100-002 (TOOL-4201-C), a 5-mm Allen wrench, worm clamp, file, screwdriver and torque wrench. Have No. 50 master shims and the complete adjustment-shim table available.

steps.title: Establish and mark top dead center
steps.body: Install the timing peg and turn the crankshaft slowly clockwise until its balance weight contacts the peg. This establishes top dead center (TDC). Mark the top of the balancer unit and its shafts so their TDC position can be restored.

steps.title: Remove and inspect the complete balancer
steps.body: Remove the bolts, balancer unit and adjustment shims from its seating faces. Inspect the gear for damage and check that the shaft turns smoothly. Replace a damaged or malfunctioning unit; its precision internal construction must not be disassembled.

steps.title: Install the master shims
steps.body: Fit No. 50 master shims, which are 1.50 mm thick. Keep the shaft marks at TDC and lower the unit slowly into position to avoid gear interference. Tighten the bolts in stages: 25 Nm, then 42 Nm.

steps.title: Check meshing and restore the measurement reference
steps.body: Remove the timing peg and rotate the crankshaft to check for gear-meshing problems. Reinstall the peg, turn slowly clockwise back to TDC, then remove the peg again before proceeding with the measurements.

steps.title: Set up the measuring fixture
steps.body: Follow the [procedure's illustrated arrangement](#/document/G1660459). File a mark on the Allen wrench 80 mm above the driven-gear shaft center and position the dial indicator at that height. Keep the wrench and worm clamp clear of the housing. Use the illustrated screwdriver position at the No. 1 crankweight to control rotational and thrust movement while measuring.

steps.title: Measure and select adjustment shims
steps.body: Rotate clockwise and measure at 10, 30, 100, 190, 210 and 280 degrees, resetting the equipment between measurements. Record all six readings. Use the complete table's metric columns to identify measured backlash, adjustment-shim number and shim thickness. The selection table serves a different purpose from the final acceptance range.

steps.title: Refit with the selected shims
steps.body: Remove the balancer and install the selected shims on its seating faces. Re-establish crankshaft TDC with the timing peg. With the shaft marks at TDC, install the unit slowly and tighten the bolts to 25 Nm, then 42 Nm. Remove the timing peg.

steps.title: Repeat the complete backlash check
steps.body: Use the same fixture, measuring height and crankweight-control method at all six positions, resetting between readings. Final backlash must be within 0.040–0.140 mm throughout. If backlash exceeds the specified range, install a new balancer unit and repeat the procedure.

watchFor.title: Fixture contact changes the reading
watchFor.body: The Allen wrench and worm clamp must not touch the balancer housing. Contact can interfere with the movement being measured.

watchFor.title: Timing peg left installed
watchFor.body: Remove the peg before the free-rotation and backlash-measurement phases, following the sequence above.

notes: Use metric values for shim selection; do not use the table's inconsistent printed inch equivalents.
The master-shim row is a selection-table entry, not the final acceptable backlash range.

diagnostics.finding: The balancer gear is damaged or the shaft does not turn smoothly.
diagnostics.meaning: The unit has damage or a mechanical malfunction that shim adjustment cannot correct.
diagnostics.next: Replace the complete balancer unit.

diagnostics.finding: Backlash exceeds the specified range after the selected shims are installed.
diagnostics.meaning: The final assembly has not met the clearance requirement.
diagnostics.next: Install a new balancer unit and repeat the adjustment procedure.

verification.title: Confirm all measurement positions pass
verification.body: Accept the adjustment only when all six final readings are within 0.040–0.140 mm and the required gear-meshing check has found no interference.

verification.title: Keep the measurement record
verification.body: Record the master-shim readings, selected shim number and thickness, and final reading at each crankshaft position.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost general procedure for timed balancer removal and refitting, illustrated measuring setup, shim selection and final backlash verification.

guides.title: Check and adjust valve clearance on the 2.3L or 3.7L engine
guides.summary: Measure each valve at the camshaft base circle and replace only the tappets needed to restore the engine-specific clearance.
guides.introduction: Both engines use direct-acting mechanical buckets: each camshaft lobe acts on a bucket-shaped tappet above a valve. Clearance is the small gap measured while the lobe is not lifting that valve. Adjustment is made by selecting a different tappet thickness, so a measurement check can become camshaft and timing work if a gap is outside specification.
guides.why: Measuring on the rising or falling part of a lobe produces a misleading result. Temperature, tappet identification and the correct engine specification also matter. A thicker tappet reduces clearance; a thinner one increases it. Keeping every reading tied to its valve location makes that correction deliberate rather than approximate.

when.summary: When valve clearance needs checking, with adjustment only where a measured gap is outside specification.
notes: Camshaft removal is conditional; acceptable measurements do not justify replacing tappets.

prepare.title: Prepare measurement and records
prepare.detail: Use a feeler gauge and a location-based record distinguishing intake and exhaust valves. Identify the engine before selecting specifications or interpreting tappet markings.

prepare.title: Allow for the adjustment phase
prepare.detail: Have access to the matching camshaft removal and installation procedure and the capability to complete its timing work if replacement tappets are needed.

steps.title: Expose the valve train
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove the valve cover and air-cleaner outlet pipe through their respective procedures. On the 3.7L, remove the appropriate left-hand or right-hand valve cover and allow the engine to reach room temperature before measuring.

steps.title: Position each valve for measurement
steps.body: Bring each cam lobe to its base circle, pointing away from the tappet. For the 2.3L, turn the engine clockwise only and use only the crankshaft bolt. For the 3.7L, rotate through the crankshaft pulley bolt as specified. Measure each gap with the feeler gauge and record its exact location.

steps.title: Compare against the correct limits
steps.body: The 2.3L fully installed limits are 0.19–0.31 mm for intake and 0.30–0.42 mm for exhaust. The 3.7L limits are 0.15–0.25 mm for intake and 0.36–0.46 mm for exhaust, with a midrange clearance preferred. Keep these engine-specific ranges separate.

steps.title: Calculate and identify replacement tappets
steps.body: For the 2.3L, required tappet thickness equals measured clearance plus existing tappet thickness minus nominal clearance; the nominal values are 0.25 mm intake and 0.36 mm exhaust. Choose the nearest available size and mark its destination. For the 3.7L, use its selection calculation with the existing tappet thickness and the preferred midrange clearance.

steps.title: Interpret the thickness markings correctly
steps.body: On the 2.3L, the marking supplies only the decimal portion: 0.650 identifies a 3.650 mm tappet. On the 3.7L, the marking gives the thickness directly: 3.310 identifies 3.31 mm. Confirm this before ordering or fitting parts, because the same reading method does not apply to both engines.

steps.title: Adjust only where required and restore access components
steps.body: If any clearance is outside specification, follow the appropriate camshaft procedure to remove the cams and install the selected tappets in their marked locations. Complete camshaft installation and confirm the resulting clearances. Refit the valve cover and any removed intake pipe through their matching procedures.

watchFor.title: An uncertain lobe position
watchFor.body: Reposition the lobe before accepting a reading. A partly lifting cam does not provide a valid clearance measurement.

watchFor.title: Lost valve locations
watchFor.body: Do not separate measurements, original tappet thicknesses and replacement choices from their installation positions.

notes: This is a selective tappet replacement operation, not an adjustment screw procedure.
The room-temperature requirement is stated explicitly for the 3.7L branch.

diagnostics.finding: All measured gaps fall within the applicable range.
diagnostics.meaning: The clearance check does not call for tappet replacement.
diagnostics.next: Retain the recorded measurements and complete reassembly.

diagnostics.finding: A gap falls outside its intake or exhaust range.
diagnostics.meaning: That location requires a thickness correction.
diagnostics.next: Select a replacement using the matching engine's calculation and perform the camshaft procedure.

verification.title: Confirm fully installed clearances
verification.body: Check the final gaps against the applicable engine limits after adjustment.

verification.title: Retain the measurement record
verification.body: Record valve locations, initial gaps, selected tappet thicknesses and final gaps so the result can be checked.

guides.title: Remove and install camshafts on the 2.3L or 3.7L engine
guides.summary: Remove and refit the camshafts through the correct engine branch, preserving piston clearance, bearing-cap locations and valve-clearance requirements.
guides.introduction: Camshaft lobes open the valves through mechanical bucket tappets. Variable camshaft timing, or VCT, changes the cams' relationship to the crankshaft to control valve events. Removing the cams interrupts that relationship and also releases valve-spring loading from their bearing caps. This repair therefore combines controlled mechanical unloading, lubrication, valve-clearance decisions and exact timing restoration.
guides.why: With timing components disconnected, turning a camshaft or crankshaft at the wrong point can bring valves and pistons together. The engines use different safe working positions and tools. Bearing caps must retain their original locations, and new valve-train parts can alter clearance even when they appear identical to the parts removed.

when.summary: When camshaft replacement or related cylinder-head and tappet work requires camshaft removal.
notes: Use the complete engine-specific procedure alongside this guide; illustrated positions and tightening sequences are essential.

prepare.title: Prepare the 2.3L branch
prepare.detail: Provide camshaft alignment tool 303-1565, crankshaft timing peg 303-507, a feeler gauge, clean engine oil and Motorcraft TA-16 gasket maker. Arrange hoist access and the fuel-pressure release and VCT procedures.

prepare.title: Prepare the 3.7L branch
prepare.detail: Provide camshaft holding tools 303-1248, chain-tensioner hold-down tool 303-1530, a feeler gauge and the specified engine oil. Identify the left-hand or right-hand bank and retain its numbered bearing caps in order.

prepare.title: Protect the engine interior
prepare.detail: Keep cleaning debris out of oil and coolant passages. Record component positions before dismantling, and do not rotate disconnected timing components unless the procedure directs it.

steps.title: Remove the VCT equipment through the matching procedure
steps.body: For the 2.3L, put the vehicle in NEUTRAL on the hoist, release fuel-system pressure and remove the VCT units. For the 3.7L, remove the VCT unit for the bank being serviced. These prerequisite procedures establish the timing access needed for the following work.

steps.title: Unload and remove the camshafts
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove the alignment tool, VCT oil-control solenoids and front cap. Record cap locations, orientations and the cylinder No. 1 lobe positions. Loosen bearing caps in the illustrated sequence, two turns at a time, until unloaded; remove the cams, inspect bores for scratches detectable by touch and clean the rear cap. On either 3.7L bank, remove the tensioner and cam holding tools, mark intake and exhaust cams and remove the numbered caps and cams as illustrated.

steps.title: For new 2.3L parts, establish clearance-checking space
steps.body: New heads, valves, tappets or cams require the preliminary clearance-check sequence; original parts skip it. Install the crankshaft bolt and washer, mark the bolt at 12 o'clock, remove the timing peg and rotate clockwise 270 degrees to place the mark at 9 o'clock. This moves the pistons below the block deck. Lubricate and temporarily install the cams and caps using the specified staged sequence.

steps.title: Measure and select 2.3L tappets
steps.body: Remove the spark plugs. Turn the cams using their flats to place each lobe at base circle, then measure and record every gap. Fully installed limits are 0.19–0.31 mm intake and 0.30–0.42 mm exhaust. Select thickness using measured clearance plus existing tappet thickness minus the nominal clearance of 0.25 mm intake or 0.36 mm exhaust. A marking of 0.650 means 3.650 mm. Mark replacement locations, reinstall the plugs and progressively remove the temporary cam installation.

steps.title: Return the 2.3L to its final installation position
steps.body: After that preliminary check, reinstall the crankshaft timing peg and rotate the crankshaft clockwise 90 degrees until it contacts the peg. Lubricate and install any selected replacement tappets. Original-part installations follow their direct installation branch without adding this checking cycle.

steps.title: Seal and secure the 2.3L camshafts
steps.body: Apply the illustrated 1 mm TA-16 beads to the exhaust rear bearing-cap mating surfaces and secure the cap within 10 minutes. Keep sealant out of the journal; if contaminated or timed out, remove it and clean the affected surfaces. Oil the cams, journals and caps. Install with the recorded lobe positions and alignment slots already correct, so the alignment plate fits without rotating the cams. Follow the final cap-tightening sequence, wipe excess sealant from the fuel-pump housing joint, reinstall the solenoids and fit the alignment tool.

steps.title: Install the 3.7L cams in the safe working position
steps.body: Keep the crankshaft in the specified freewheeling position, with its dowel at 9 o'clock, until installation and clearance work are complete. Follow each bank's illustrated neutral cam position; do not infer it from the other engine. Lubricate the cams, place seal gaps at 12 o'clock and fit the numbered caps and oil tube. Apply the initial tightening stages, loosen the cap bolts, then repeat the prescribed tightening stages.

steps.title: Check 3.7L clearance and restore timing positions
steps.body: Confirm tappet clearances through the 3.7L clearance procedure; checking and adjustment are mandatory when components are new. Use a camshaft sprocket bolt for the directed cam rotation. After adjustment, remove that bank's oil tube, move its cams to top dead centre, or TDC, and install the cam holding and tensioner hold-down tools. Once the required bank work is complete, rotate the crankshaft clockwise 60 degrees to the specified TDC position, with its dowel at 11 o'clock.

steps.title: Complete VCT installation and road test
steps.body: Install the VCT units through the matching engine procedure and complete its timing and reassembly requirements. Both camshaft procedures finish with a road test.

watchFor.title: Alignment tool used as a reaction tool
watchFor.body: The 2.3L alignment tool establishes position only; using it to prevent engine rotation can damage the engine.

watchFor.title: Sealant or cap-position errors
watchFor.body: Keep sealant away from bearing journals and preserve every cap's location and orientation.

notes: The 3.7L illustrations omit VCT oil-control solenoids for clarity; that note is not an instruction to remove them.
Use the 2.3L exhaust rear camshaft-bearing-cap sealant illustration only with that engine’s procedure.

diagnostics.finding: New valve-train components are being installed.
diagnostics.meaning: Their dimensions can change the resulting valve clearance.
diagnostics.next: Complete the applicable measurement and tappet-selection branch before restoring final timing.

diagnostics.finding: Measured clearance is outside the applicable specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The installed tappet thickness requires correction.
diagnostics.next: Select and install the correct tappet, then confirm the resulting clearance.

verification.title: Confirm the mechanical completion points
verification.body: Check cap placement, required clearance results, engine-specific timing positions and completion of the VCT installation procedure before operation.

verification.title: Record measurements and the road-test result
verification.body: Retain required clearance measurements and replacement locations, and record the outcome of the prescribed road test.

guides.title: Replace the crankshaft front seal on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Replace the front crankshaft oil seal using the engine-specific pulley, timing and installation procedure, then complete misfire-monitor correction.
guides.introduction: The crankshaft front seal retains engine oil where the rotating crankshaft passes through the front cover. Reaching it requires removing the crankshaft pulley. The engines share this purpose, but their access, installation tools and fastening procedures differ substantially.
guides.why: On the 2.3L, the pulley and timing sprocket rely on friction rather than a key. Loosening the pulley bolt also releases the sprocket unless the prescribed timing setup is maintained. Across all variants, damage to the crankshaft or cover during seal extraction can undermine the new seal.

when.summary: When a front crankshaft seal leak is confirmed or the seal requires renewal during engine repair.
notes: Identify the engine before selecting tools, lubricant, access procedures or tightening stages.
Oil around the pulley is a reason to establish the leak source, not proof that the seal has failed.

prepare.title: Provide engine-specific tooling
prepare.detail: Have the specified seal remover and installers, pulley removal and holding equipment, torque-and-angle tools and a diagnostic scan tool. The 2.3L additionally requires timing and sensor-alignment tools and an air impact wrench with at least 1/2-in drive for pulley-bolt removal.

prepare.title: Prepare parts and access
prepare.detail: Obtain a new seal and crankshaft pulley bolt, plus the specified washer arrangement. Keep exposed engine areas clean. For the 2.3L, position the vehicle in Neutral on a hoist using the approved lifting points.

steps.title: Clear access for the selected engine
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove the accessory belt, disconnect the air-conditioning compressor wiring and retainers, and unbolt and support the compressor aside; remove and disconnect the crankshaft position sensor. On the 3.7L, remove the degas bottle and compressor belt. The 5.0L requires the cooling fan/shroud and both accessory and compressor belts removed. The 5.2L procedure specifies the fan/shroud and compressor belt.

steps.title: Establish 2.3L timing before loosening the pulley
steps.body: Rotate clockwise to the specified position with the first piston 45 degrees before top dead center, using the guide holes. Remove the engine plug, install timing peg 303-507, then rotate clockwise until the crankshaft contacts it at top dead center. Remove both camshaft position sensors and check the trigger-wheel orientation. If incorrect, remove the peg, turn clockwise three-fourths of a revolution and repeat the prescribed positioning sequence. Install camshaft holding tools 303-1686 only when correctly aligned.

steps.title: Remove the pulley with the correct reaction support
steps.body: On the 2.3L, maintain top dead center and hold the pulley with damper tool 303-1689 while removing its bolt with the specified impact wrench. Remove any fitted diamond washer. The other engines use a three-leg puller; the 5.0L and 5.2L procedures also use the old pulley bolt during pulling. Retain an old bolt only for the removal operations that explicitly require it.

steps.title: Renew the seal without damaging its surroundings
steps.body: Use remover 303-409 and discard the seal. The 2.3L and 5.2L use the old crankshaft bolt during seal removal; discard it afterward. Follow the selected engine's lubrication and installer instructions. For the 2.3L, remove the through-bolt from installer 303-096. For the 5.0L seal installation, use only the plate from tool 303-335 with installer 303-1531.

steps.title: Refit the 2.3L pulley while maintaining timing
steps.body: Restore the correct diamond-washer arrangement where applicable. Lubricate the crankshaft and pulley, position the pulley access hole at 6 o'clock and install the M6 alignment bolt. Hold the pulley with the damper tool and tighten the new crankshaft bolt and washer using hand tools and the specified stages. Remove the M6 bolt afterward.

steps.title: Refit the 3.7L or V8 pulley
steps.body: Use the specified installers and lubricate the sealing surfaces as directed for that engine. On the 5.0L and 5.2L, apply the specified silicone sealant to the pulley Woodruff-key slot and secure the assembly within 5 minutes; otherwise remove the sealant and clean the area before restarting. Use a strap wrench and a new bolt with the specified washer. Follow the individual tightening stages: the 5.0L and 5.2L sequences differ.

steps.title: Restore 2.3L sensor alignment
steps.body: Reconnect the crankshaft position sensor and fit its bolts finger-tight. Align it to the pulley trigger-wheel tooth with tool 303-1521, tighten the bolts, then remove the alignment tool. Remove the timing peg and reinstall the engine plug. These operations preserve the sensor's relationship to the pulley.

steps.title: Restore the removed equipment
steps.body: For the 2.3L, refit and reconnect the compressor, remove the camshaft holders, then install both camshaft position sensors and the accessory belt. For the 3.7L, restore the compressor belt and degas bottle. For the V8s, restore the compressor belt, the 5.0L accessory belt where applicable, and the fan/shroud using the linked procedures.

watchFor.title: Alignment tools used as torque restraints
watchFor.body: The 2.3L camshaft holders are for alignment only. Its timing peg prevents travel beyond top dead center in one direction but still permits counterclockwise movement; the separate damper holder is essential.

watchFor.title: Mixed sprocket hardware
watchFor.body: Early 2.3L engines have diamond washers on both sides of the sprocket. Laser-etched sprockets require none. When replacing an early sprocket with the laser-etched service part, discard the old sprocket and diamond washers.

notes: Use each engine's specified lubrication materials and complete tightening procedure; similar-looking pulley assemblies do not establish interchangeable specifications.

diagnostics.finding: A retained 2.3L diamond washer shows damage after cleaning.
diagnostics.meaning: It cannot be reused in the original washer-equipped arrangement.
diagnostics.next: Replace the damaged washer. Reuse an undamaged washer where required, and never fit diamond washers with a laser-etched sprocket.

verification.title: Complete the correct profile routine
verification.body: For the 2.3L and 5.2L, run the Powertrain Control Module (PCM) Misfire Monitor Profile Correction routine. For the 3.7L and 5.0L, perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction using the diagnostic scan tool.

verification.title: Road test and record completion
verification.body: Road test the vehicle. Record the engine variant, completed scan-tool routine and road-test result.

guides.title: Replace the crankshaft rear oil seal by engine variant
guides.summary: Renew the rear crankshaft oil seal using the correct retainer-sealing or seal-installation method for the fitted engine.
guides.introduction: The rear crankshaft seal retains engine oil where the rotating crankshaft exits toward the transmission. Access is behind the flywheel or flexplate. The 2.3L and 3.7L procedures include sealing a retainer joint, while the 5.0L and 5.2L procedures use tools to remove and seat the seal in its bore.
guides.why: A clean sealing surface and correctly seated seal are essential to containing oil. Retainer installation must preserve the applied silicone bead and meet its assembly deadline. The V8 crankshaft sensor ring needs careful handling, and the 5.2L seal has its own installation orientation.
searchTerms: oil leak at rear of engine

when.summary: When repair calls for replacement of the crankshaft rear oil seal after the leak source is established.
notes: Choose the engine branch before ordering parts or arranging installation tools.
Plan access through the applicable flywheel or flexplate procedure and its support requirements.

prepare.title: Prepare retainer-service materials
prepare.detail: For 2.3L and 3.7L work, obtain Motorcraft High Performance Engine RTV Silicone TA-357 and follow the sealing-surface preparation procedure. RTV means room-temperature-vulcanizing silicone. The 2.3L also needs installer 303-328, oil-drain equipment, a new oil filter and the specified engine oil.

prepare.title: Provide the V8 seal tools
prepare.detail: The 5.0L uses remover 303-519 with slide hammer 100-001. The 5.2L uses a universal seal puller. Both use installer 303-1250 with handle 205-153. Confirm replacement parts against engine identification.

prepare.title: Use the correct assembly lubricant
prepare.detail: The 3.7L specifies clean SAE 5W-20 synthetic-blend oil for the seal. The 5.0L specifies clean engine oil; the 5.2L specifies Motorcraft SAE 5W-50 Full Synthetic Motor Oil.

prepare.title: Arrange the required scan-tool completion
prepare.detail: On the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L, have a diagnostic scan tool capable of the specified misfire-monitor profile-correction routine. Flywheel or flexplate restoration includes this electronic completion step; a road test is a separate check.

steps.title: Expose the rear seal
steps.body: Remove the applicable flywheel or flexplate on the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L; remove the flywheel on the 5.2L. For the 3.7L and both V8s, remove the crankshaft sensor ring and engine-to-transmission spacer plate. Inspect the V8 sensor ring and discard it if dropped or visibly damaged.

steps.title: Remove the seal using the engine's method
steps.body: On the 3.7L, first disconnect and remove the crankshaft position (CKP) sensor, then remove the oil-pan-to-rear-seal bolts. On the 2.3L and 3.7L, unbolt and remove the rear-seal assembly and discard the seal; complete [RTV surface preparation](#/document/G1692003). On the 5.0L, use its specified remover and slide hammer. On the 5.2L, use a universal seal puller. Discard the removed seal in every branch.

steps.title: 2.3L: seal and install the retainer
steps.body: Follow [the 2.3L procedure](#/document/G1660464): apply a 3 mm silicone bead to the oil-pan surface and 5 mm beads at the T-joints. Fit installer 303-328. Introduce the retainer at an angle above the pan flange, then tilt it onto the block without scraping away sealant. Seat the seal, tighten the bolts in the illustrated sequence and remove the tool. Secure the assembly within 10 minutes; otherwise remove the sealant, clean and restart.

steps.title: 3.7L: complete its separate retainer procedure
steps.body: Follow [the 3.7L bead paths](#/document/G1681514) for the separate 5 mm and 3 mm silicone beads. Lubricate the seal with specified oil. Angle the retainer above the pan flange and tilt it onto the block, installing and tightening it within 10 minutes of sealant application. Tighten the retainer bolts in sequence and the oil-pan bolts through their torque-and-angle stages. Reinstall and reconnect the CKP sensor.

steps.title: 5.0L: install the lubricated seal
steps.body: Lubricate the seal bore and lips with clean engine oil. Position installer 303-1250 on the crankshaft, slide the new seal onto it and use handle 205-153 to install it through [the 5.0L procedure](#/document/G1685316).

steps.title: 5.2L: preserve the unique seal orientation
steps.body: Lubricate the retaining-plate bore and seal lips with specified 5W-50 oil. Position installer 303-1250, check the seal orientation in [the 5.2L installation detail](#/document/G1800269), and slide on the new seal. Install it using the specified handle and installer.

steps.title: Complete oil service and reassembly
steps.body: On the 2.3L, drain the oil after seal installation, refit the drain plug, discard the filter and fit a new filter with its seal lubricated. Follow the stated tightening instructions and refill using [2.3L oil specifications](#/document/G1660452). Restore the sensor ring and spacer plate on the applicable engines, then reinstall the correct flywheel or flexplate.

steps.title: Complete the engine-specific misfire-monitor routine
steps.body: After restoring the flywheel or flexplate, perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction with a diagnostic scan tool on the 3.7L and 5.0L. On the 5.2L, use the Powertrain Control Module (PCM) Misfire Monitor Profile Correction routine. Follow the relevant flywheel or flexplate procedure for that engine; do not transfer this requirement to the 2.3L branch.

steps.title: Road test after assembly and required electronic completion
steps.body: Perform the road test required by the selected rear-seal procedure after reassembly and any applicable profile-correction routine. Record the result separately from the scan-tool operation.

watchFor.title: Incorrect silicone on the 3.7L
watchFor.body: Use the specified Motorcraft sealant. The procedure warns that unsuitable sealant can cause excessive oil foaming and serious engine damage.

watchFor.title: Sealant scraped from the joint
watchFor.body: Preserve the angled retainer approach on the 2.3L and 3.7L so the oil-pan flange does not wipe away the bead.

notes: Use the tightening sequences and seal illustrations for the selected engine. The 5.2L seal orientation is unique to its procedure.

diagnostics.finding: A 5.0L or 5.2L crankshaft sensor ring was dropped or shows visible damage.
diagnostics.meaning: The ring is unsuitable for reuse under the stated inspection rule.
diagnostics.next: Discard it and install a replacement during reassembly.

verification.title: Confirm branch completion
verification.body: Confirm seal installation and surrounding reassembly against the selected procedure. Record completion of the required oil and filter change on the 2.3L.

verification.title: Record the applicable profile correction
verification.body: For the 3.7L and 5.0L, record completion of Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction. For the 5.2L, record the PCM Misfire Monitor Profile Correction result. Keep that record distinct from the subsequent road-test result.

verification.title: Record the road-test result
verification.body: Perform the required road test after reassembly and record the repair outcome and any remaining concern.

guides.title: Reseal or replace the engine front cover — 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Remove and reseal the engine front cover using the correct engine-specific timing controls, seals, installation sequence and final scan-tool routine.
guides.introduction: The front cover encloses the engine’s timing drive and seals its front face against oil leakage. Removing it exposes sealing joints and requires access through surrounding drive, cooling and electrical components. The four engines share this purpose, but their procedures differ substantially: the 2.3L requires precise crankshaft and camshaft positioning, while the V8 covers require particular care around the variable camshaft timing components.
guides.why: Cleanliness protects oil passages and internal engine parts from abrasive debris. Correct sealant placement and assembly timing prevent future leaks. On the 2.3L, loosening the pulley bolt also releases the friction-clamped crankshaft timing sprocket, so losing alignment can cause severe engine damage. On the V8s, projecting variable camshaft timing solenoid pins can strike the valve tips during cover installation.

when.summary: When the front cover requires resealing, replacement or removal for another established engine repair.
notes: Identify the engine and relevant build details before ordering parts or choosing an installation sequence.

prepare.title: Arrange safe access and timing capability
prepare.detail: Place the vehicle in neutral on a hoist at the specified lifting points. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Have the complete engine-specific procedure available before disturbing the pulley or applying sealant.

prepare.title: Stage tools and consumables
prepare.detail: Use Motorcraft High Performance Engine RTV Silicone TA-357. The 2.3L also uses TA-16 gasket maker, tools 303-507, 303-1565, 303-1689, 303-409, 303-096 and 303-1521. The 3.7L uses 205-150, 205-153 and alignment pins 307-399. Obtain the new seals, gaskets, fasteners and filters required by the selected procedure.

prepare.title: Workshop capability
prepare.detail: Suitable hoist; engine-specific seal and alignment tools; torque and angle tools; fluid collection equipment; diagnostic scan tool. The 2.3L additionally requires crankshaft/camshaft timing tools, a damper holding tool, an air impact wrench for removal and hand tools for installation.

steps.title: Clear the engine-specific access path
steps.body: Follow the complete removal route for the [2.3L](#/document/G1945803), [3.7L](#/document/G1681517), [5.0L](#/document/G1685320) or [5.2L](#/document/G1800273). The 3.7L and V8 routes require cooling-system draining. Both V8 routes disconnect the battery ground and positive cables; the 5.0L first requires fuel-pressure release. Remove the specified intake parts, valve covers, coolant components and applicable underbody shield assembly.

steps.title: Establish 2.3L timing before releasing the pulley
steps.body: Remove the vacuum pump, rear intake camshaft cap and pump adapter, holding the camshaft flats for adapter removal. Support the air-conditioning compressor aside and remove the crankshaft position sensor. Position the crankshaft as instructed at 45 degrees before top dead center, install timing peg 303-507, then turn clockwise against it. Fit camshaft alignment tool 303-1565. This alignment tool must never carry engine-turning loads.

steps.title: Remove the 2.3L pulley and seal without losing position
steps.body: Keep the crankshaft at top dead center. Hold the pulley with 303-1689 and remove its bolt using an air impact wrench with at least a 1/2-in drive. Account for any diamond washer. Temporarily install the old pulley bolt for the seal-removal sequence, discard the front seal, then remove and discard that bolt. Remove the tensioner, coolant pump pulley and cover after moving the turbocharger vacuum valve and harness clear.

steps.title: Release the other covers at their intended interfaces
steps.body: On the 3.7L, move the generator and intake support bracket clear, then use only the illustrated pry pads to release the cover; service its coolant-pipe seal with the specified tools. On the V8s, remove the pump and thermostat-housing O-rings, wiring attachments, tensioner and cover fasteners. Discard the cover gaskets. Rock the 5.2L cover forward off its dowels, lift it away and inspect the oil-pan gasket.

steps.title: Prepare clean sealing surfaces
steps.body: Follow [RTV surface preparation](#/document/G1692003), keeping debris out of the engine. Thoroughly wash the 3.7L cover after cleaning. Install new V8 cover gaskets and fully depress the variable camshaft timing solenoid pins. Prepare the 3.7L coolant-pipe seal, alignment pins and locating dowels before applying sealant.

steps.title: Seal and secure the cover within its working window
steps.body: Use the selected procedure’s bead pattern and fastening sequence. Secure the 2.3L cover within 10 minutes. On the 3.7L, install the cover and initial bolts within 4 minutes, then complete the remaining bolts within 35 minutes. Both V8s require final tightening within 5 minutes; alternatively, tighten fasteners 6–11 to 8 Nm within that window and finish all fasteners within 1 hour. If the applicable limit is missed, remove the sealant and clean again. Protect the 5.2L oil-pan gasket while positioning the cover and rocking it back onto the dowels.

steps.title: Restore the 2.3L friction joint and sensor alignment
steps.body: Install a new lubricated front seal using 303-096 as directed. Fit a required, serviceable diamond washer only with the appropriate sprocket. Lubricate and position the pulley, use the M6 alignment bolt, and install a new crankshaft bolt and washer. Hold the damper at top dead center and tighten using hand tools only. Remove the M6 bolt, align the crankshaft position sensor with 303-1521, tighten it, then remove the alignment tool and timing peg and reinstall the engine plug.

steps.title: Finish the 2.3L upper-engine assembly
steps.body: Restore the compressor and remove the camshaft alignment tool. Hold the camshaft flats while installing the vacuum-pump adapter. Apply TA-16 to the rear intake camshaft cap as illustrated and secure it within 10 minutes; otherwise remove the gasket maker. Wipe excess from the vacuum-pump sealing face. Reinstall the pump, valve cover, belt and intake pipe, and finish tightening the coolant pump pulley.

steps.title: Restore cooling components and service fluids on the other engines
steps.body: Reinstall the 3.7L support bracket, generator, tensioner, pump, crankshaft seal and valve covers in sequence. On both V8s, restore wiring and grounds and install new coolant-pump and thermostat-housing O-rings lubricated with the specified coolant. Complete the intake and cover-related work. Change engine oil and filter on the 3.7L and both V8s; do not lubricate the replacement filter seal on the 3.7L or 5.0L. Follow the separate 5.2L oil-service procedure. Reconnect V8 batteries and complete the applicable cooling-system fill and bleed.

steps.title: Complete the electronic correction and road test
steps.body: Run the Powertrain Control Module Misfire Monitor Profile Correction routine for the 2.3L and 5.2L, or Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction for the 3.7L and 5.0L. Each engine procedure finishes with a road test.

watchFor.title: A timing peg is not a complete rotation lock
watchFor.body: The 2.3L peg prevents clockwise travel past top dead center but permits counterclockwise movement. Maintain the required position during pulley removal and installation.

watchFor.title: Incorrect silicone on the 3.7L
watchFor.body: The specified silicone is required; an unsuitable product can cause excessive oil foaming and serious engine damage.

notes: The illustrated 2.3L pulley installation calls for two people and prohibits impact-tool tightening.
Use each engine’s complete fastening diagram; bolt positions, torque stages and sealing patterns are not interchangeable.

diagnostics.finding: The 2.3L camshaft alignment tool will not enter the offset slots.
diagnostics.meaning: The prescribed crankshaft/camshaft position has not been established.
diagnostics.next: Remove the timing peg, turn the crankshaft clockwise three-fourths of a revolution and repeat the specified positioning steps.

diagnostics.finding: An early 2.3L sprocket uses diamond washers.
diagnostics.meaning: Its friction-joint arrangement differs from the later laser-etched sprocket.
diagnostics.next: Clean and inspect the washer; reuse it only if undamaged. If replacing the early sprocket, discard its washers and install the laser-etched service sprocket without diamond washers.

verification.title: Confirm assembly prerequisites are complete
verification.body: Check the applicable sealant deadline, fastening sequence, timing-tool removal, sensor alignment, wiring restoration and fluid-service steps before operation.

verification.title: Record the completed result
verification.body: Record the engine variant, completed scan-tool correction and road-test outcome so the mechanical repair and required electronic completion are documented separately.

guides.title: Replace the left-hand engine mount: engine-specific access and support
guides.summary: Replace the left-hand engine mount using the correct lifting equipment, clearance procedure and reassembly sequence for the installed engine.
guides.introduction: The left-hand (LH) engine mount supports the engine while helping isolate vibration and control movement. Replacing it requires temporarily transferring that load to an engine support bar. The four engines share this principle, but their access work, lifting arrangements and connections differ.
guides.why: Both engine-mount nuts must be released for the specified lifting operation. Correct support protects the engine and surrounding structure; careful reassembly restores the mount, electrical grounds and any vacuum or oil-cooler connections disturbed for access.

when.summary: When LH engine-mount replacement or removal is required for an established repair.
notes: Select the procedure by engine before dismantling; lifting heights and mount-nut torques are not interchangeable.

prepare.title: Provide safe vehicle and engine support
prepare.detail: Use a hoist at the specified lifting points, with the vehicle in NEUTRAL. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. This job requires confidence handling a supported engine.

prepare.title: Match the lifting tools
prepare.detail: Use support bar 303-F072. The 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L use lifting bracket 303-050; the 3.7L uses engine lift eye 303-1245.

prepare.title: Plan variant-specific supplies
prepare.detail: Have torque equipment and the applicable battery/access procedures available. The 5.2L requires new strut-tower cross-brace nuts and an engine-oil level check after its cooler hoses are reconnected.

steps.title: Establish the correct access route
steps.body: Follow only the engine branch below. On the V8 engines, verify engine identification when selecting replacement parts. Position the hoist using the [lifting procedure](#/document/G1663631), checking adapter clearance around suspension and underbody components.

steps.title: Remove the 2.3L mount and bracket
steps.body: Follow the [2.3L procedure](#/document/G1945804): remove the appearance cover, fit lifting brackets to both sides of the cylinder head, disconnect battery ground and remove the radiator top shield. Remove both mount-bracket nuts, disconnect the LH vacuum tube and remove the mount bolts. Install the support bar and raise the engine 26 mm (1.0 in). Remove the underbody shield, detach the bracket-stud harness retainer and ground wire, then remove the bracket fasteners, bracket and mount.

steps.title: Use the 3.7L body-style access sequence
steps.body: The [3.7L procedure](#/document/G1681518) begins with cowl-grille removal. On convertibles, disconnect the negative cable, detach its retainer, disconnect the positive cable and remove the cowl extension. For both body styles, remove the air-cleaner outlet pipe and air cleaner, fit the lift eye, remove both mount nuts and radiator top shield, then support and raise the engine. Remove the mount bolts and mount; no lifting height is specified here.

steps.title: Prepare and lift either V8
steps.body: For [5.0L](#/document/G1685321) or [5.2L](#/document/G1800274), disconnect both battery cables and remove the brace and its harness retainer where fitted. Discard the 5.2L brace nuts. Remove the 5.0L appearance cover and radiator top shield; remove the intake components and both mount nuts on either engine. The 5.2L also requires both underbody shields and oil-cooler hose disconnection. Support-bar feet must rest on body structure, not fenders. Raise 50 mm (2 inch), then remove the mount bolts and mount.

steps.title: Install the mount before settling the engine
steps.body: Tighten mount bolts according to the selected procedure. On the 2.3L, first position the mount and bracket without their bolts; install the mount bolts, start the bracket bolt and stud bolt finger-tight, tighten the other bracket bolts, then tighten the bolt and stud bolt. Restore the ground wire, harness retainer and underbody shield before lowering.

steps.title: Restore the 2.3L connections
steps.body: Lower the engine and remove the support bar. Reconnect the vacuum tube, tighten both mount-bracket nuts, restore the radiator top shield and battery ground, remove both lifting brackets and install the appearance cover. The 2.3L mount-bracket nuts require 125 Nm; the other engines listed here use 63 Nm.

steps.title: Complete the 3.7L or V8 installation
steps.body: After lowering, the 3.7L receives its radiator shield, mount nuts, intake components and cowl parts; convertibles reconnect positive cable, retainer, then negative cable. On the 5.2L, reconnect cooler hoses and restore both shields before the mount nuts. Finish each V8's intake, brace and battery work. Refit 5.0L cover grommets to the intake manifold before the cover. Check and adjust 5.2L oil level using Castrol EDGE Supercar 5W-50, WSS-M2C931-C.

watchFor.title: Body-panel loading
watchFor.body: The V8 support-bar instructions expressly prohibit placing the feet on the fenders.

watchFor.title: A connection left behind
watchFor.body: Pay particular attention to the 2.3L bracket ground and vacuum tube, and the 5.2L cooler-hose connections.

notes: The 2.3L coolant tube is omitted from an illustration for clarity; that note does not instruct its removal.

verification.title: Confirm fastening and restoration
verification.body: Check off the selected engine's tightening sequence, removed access parts, electrical connections and lifting-tool removal.

verification.title: Record the variant-specific result
verification.body: Record the engine branch used and, for the 5.2L, completion of the oil-level inspection and any adjustment.

guides.title: Replace the right engine mount on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Support and raise the engine through its specified lifting attachments, replace the right mount and restore the connections disturbed for access.
guides.introduction: The right-hand (RH) engine mount carries engine weight while helping isolate engine movement from the body. Replacing it requires transferring that load to an engine support bar. Access differs substantially: the 2.3L has a vacuum connection, the 3.7L requires moving the air-conditioning compressor, and the 5.2L requires opening oil-cooler hose connections.
guides.why: Both engine-mount nuts must be released for the prescribed lift, even though only the right mount is being replaced. Correct support placement prevents body damage, and the engine-specific lifting height and bracket sequence provide removal clearance without treating attached components as lifting restraints.

when.summary: When assessment has established that the RH engine mount requires replacement.
notes: Identify the engine and, on 2.3L, whether the transmission is 6R80 automatic or MT82 manual.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting capability
prepare.detail: Position the vehicle in NEUTRAL on a hoist using the marked lifting points. Never work beneath jack-only support. Check hoist-adapter and underbody clearance using the lifting procedure.

prepare.title: Use the specified engine attachments
prepare.detail: All variants use support bar 303-F072. Use lifting bracket 303-050 on 2.3L and the V8s, or lift eye 303-1529 on 3.7L. Have torque-controlled tools, new 5.2L brace nuts and the specified 5.2L oil available.

steps.title: Prepare the 2.3L access route
steps.body: Follow the [2.3L procedure](#/document/G1660510). Remove the appearance cover and fit lifting brackets to both sides of the cylinder head. Remove the battery cover and radiator top shield. Remove both mount nuts, disconnect the RH mount vacuum tube and remove the mount bolts. The coolant tube omitted from an illustration is identified as removed for clarity.

steps.title: Prepare the 3.7L access route
steps.body: Follow the [3.7L procedure](#/document/G1681519). Remove the battery cover, air-cleaner outlet pipe, air cleaner and air-conditioning (A/C) compressor belt. Disconnect the compressor connector and harness retainer, loosen its captive stud bolts and bolt, and position the compressor aside. Fit the lift eye, remove both mount nuts and remove the radiator top shield.

steps.title: Prepare the V8 access route
steps.body: Use the [5.0L](#/document/G1685322) or [5.2L](#/document/G1800275) procedure. Disconnect both battery cables and remove the brace where fitted, discarding its nuts on 5.2L. The 5.0L also requires appearance-cover and radiator-top-shield removal. Remove the outlet pipe, cowl grille, battery tray, cowl extension and battery heat shield. Disconnect the camshaft position (CMP) sensor and harness retainers, move the harness aside and remove the sensor. Remove both mount nuts. On 5.2L, remove the underbody shields and disconnect the oil-cooler hoses before lifting.

steps.title: Transfer the engine load to the support
steps.body: Install the support bar in the applicable arrangement. Raise the 2.3L engine 26 mm, raise the 3.7L using its specified lift-eye arrangement, or raise either V8 50 mm. On the V8s, place the support-bar legs on body structure; resting them on the fenders can damage the body.

steps.title: Remove the mount
steps.body: On 2.3L with 6R80, remove the transmission-tube bracket nut and move the bracket aside. On either 2.3L transmission variant, remove the engine-mount bracket bolt, stud bolt and remaining bracket bolts, then the bracket and mount. On the other engines, remove the mount bolts and mount after raising the engine.

steps.title: Install the mount with the correct bracket sequence
steps.body: On 2.3L, position the mount and engine bracket before installing their bolts. Tighten the mount bolts to 70 Nm, start the bracket bolts finger-tight, then install and tighten its bolt and stud bolt before tightening the remaining bracket bolts. Restore the 6R80 tube bracket where applicable. On 3.7L and the V8s, install the mount and tighten its bolts to 70 Nm before lowering the engine.

steps.title: Lower the engine and rebuild access
steps.body: Lower the engine and remove the support as directed. Reconnect the 2.3L vacuum tube before fitting mount nuts. On 5.2L, reconnect the oil-cooler hoses and refit both underbody shields before the mount nuts. Tighten both mount nuts to 125 Nm on 2.3L or 63 Nm on the other engines. Restore each access route, including lifting-attachment removal, the 3.7L compressor and belt, and V8 sensor wiring. Refit 5.0L appearance-cover grommets to the manifold first. Use new 5.2L brace nuts, reconnect V8 batteries and check the 5.2L oil level.

watchFor.title: Different mount-nut specifications
watchFor.body: The 2.3L mount-nut torque differs from the 3.7L and V8 specification.

watchFor.title: Oil lost during 5.2L access
watchFor.body: Inspect and adjust the final engine oil level with Castrol EDGE Supercar 5W-50 meeting WSS-M2C931-C.

notes: The 3.7L route moves the A/C compressor aside; it does not direct refrigerant-line disconnection.

verification.title: Confirm restoration
verification.body: Check the applicable vacuum connection, compressor belt and wiring, CMP sensor, oil-cooler connections, shields and mount fasteners against the installation procedure.

verification.title: Record completion
verification.body: Record the engine and transmission branch, mount-fastener tightening and, for 5.2L, the completed oil-level adjustment.

guides.title: Remove and install the automatic-transmission flexplate on 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engines
guides.summary: Remove the automatic transmission, service the flexplate using the engine-specific fastener requirements, and complete the required misfire-monitor correction.
guides.introduction: The flexplate is the engine-mounted drive plate connecting the crankshaft to the automatic transmission's torque converter. Its toothed outer rim provides the starter's engagement surface. Reaching it requires transmission removal, so this is a substantial driveline repair even though the plate itself has relatively few attachments. The three engine variants share the overall access path but use different bolt and tightening instructions.
guides.why: Flexplate fasteners secure a rotating connection that carries engine torque. Their specified tightening method must match the engine. The 2.3L requires new special bolts, and the 5.0L uses non-reusable torque-to-yield bolts. All three branches also require a scan-tool correction after repair, including when the original flexplate is refitted.

when.summary: When flexplate repair or replacement has been established, or it must be removed during related engine work.
notes: Select the engine-specific procedure before ordering parts or planning transmission removal.

prepare.title: Lifting and transmission-removal capability
prepare.detail: Use suitable hoist facilities and the complete engine-specific transmission procedure. Locate the designated lifting points and check adapter clearance. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; the emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this work.

prepare.title: Holding, tightening and scan equipment
prepare.detail: The 2.3L and 5.0L procedures specify flywheel holding tool 303-103 (T74P-6375-A). Have appropriate torque equipment, angle measurement for the 5.0L branch, and a diagnostic scan tool capable of Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction.

prepare.title: Correct replacement fasteners
prepare.detail: Obtain new special flexplate bolts for the 2.3L and new flexplate bolts for the 5.0L. Use engine identification information when selecting parts.

steps.title: Prepare the vehicle using its engine branch
steps.body: For the 2.3L and 3.7L, place the vehicle in NEUTRAL and position it on a hoist as directed. Follow the [lifting guidance](#/document/G1663631), including correct support locations and clearance around suspension, steering, exhaust and underbody components. For the 5.0L, begin with its transmission-removal procedure.

steps.title: Remove the automatic transmission
steps.body: Use the [2.3L transmission procedure](#/document/G1692044), [3.7L transmission procedure](#/document/G1692046) or [5.0L transmission procedure](#/document/G1692048). This exposes the flexplate; complete the applicable access sequence before working on its fasteners.

steps.title: Remove the flexplate and handle the bolts correctly
steps.body: On the 2.3L and 5.0L, install holding tool 303-103 before removing the bolts and plate, and discard those bolts. On the 3.7L, remove the bolts and flexplate as directed by its procedure.

steps.title: Install with the engine-specific tightening method
steps.body: For the [2.3L](#/document/G1945806), use new special bolts, never standard bolts, and tighten through 50 Nm, 80 Nm and 112 Nm stages. For the [3.7L](#/document/G1681522), align the offset hole, which permits only one installation position, and tighten to 80 Nm in the illustrated sequence. For the [5.0L](#/document/G1685324), fit new bolts and tighten first to 20 Nm, then a further 60°.

steps.title: Remove the holding tool and reinstall the transmission
steps.body: Remove holding tool 303-103 on the branches where it was fitted. Reinstall the automatic transmission through the same engine-specific procedure used for removal.

steps.title: Complete the electronic correction and conditional road test
steps.body: After repairs, perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction with the diagnostic scan tool on every engine branch. If a new flexplate was installed, road test the vehicle afterward.

watchFor.title: Mixing tightening methods
watchFor.body: The 5.0L torque-and-angle method is distinct from the 2.3L staged torque method and the 3.7L torque-and-sequence instruction.

watchFor.title: Ignoring the 3.7L indexing hole
watchFor.body: Align the offset hole to establish the correct position, then use that procedure's illustrated tightening order.

notes: Follow the fastener and tightening instructions for the fitted engine; keep discarded bolts separate from installation hardware.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical completion
verification.body: Confirm the applicable tightening process is complete, any holding tool has been removed, and the transmission installation is finished.

verification.title: Record scan-tool correction
verification.body: Record completion of Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction for the repaired vehicle.

verification.title: Record the replacement road test
verification.body: When a new flexplate was fitted, record completion of the required road test.

guides.title: Flywheel replacement for 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Remove and install the manual-transmission flywheel using the correct engine-specific fasteners, tightening stages and final misfire-monitor correction.
guides.introduction: The flywheel connects the rear of the crankshaft to the clutch and provides the rotating surface against which the clutch works. Removing it requires clutch access first. Although the four engine versions follow a similar overall path, their bolt requirements and tightening methods differ substantially. This is an advanced repair that also requires a diagnostic scan tool after mechanical assembly.
guides.why: Correct bolt clamping keeps the flywheel secured to the crankshaft. Reusing bolts designated for disposal, substituting ordinary bolts where special ones are required, or borrowing another engine's tightening schedule can compromise that attachment. The final electronic correction is also part of the repair: mechanical reassembly alone does not finish the prescribed work.
searchTerms: misfire monitor correction after flywheel replacement

when.summary: When flywheel removal or replacement is required during clutch or engine repair.
notes: Identify the installed engine before selecting parts and instructions.

prepare.title: Arrange clutch access and safe lifting
prepare.detail: Have the matching clutch procedure and suitable lifting facilities available. Use the identified lifting points, check hoist clearance and never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare the engine-specific equipment
prepare.detail: The 2.3L and 5.0L procedures require flywheel holding tool 303-103. Have suitable torque equipment, angle measurement for the 5.0L final stage, and a scan tool supporting the specified correction routine.

prepare.title: Obtain the correct fasteners
prepare.detail: Plan new special flywheel bolts for the 2.3L and new torque-to-yield bolts for the 5.0L and 5.2L. Follow the separate 3.7L fastener and tightening instructions for that engine.

steps.title: Remove the clutch through the matching engine procedure
steps.body: Follow the linked clutch disc and pressure plate procedure for the installed engine. The 2.3L and 3.7L flywheel instructions begin with the vehicle in NEUTRAL on a hoist. Complete the specified clutch removal before working on the flywheel.

steps.title: Release the flywheel attachment
steps.body: Install holding tool 303-103 on the 2.3L or 5.0L. Remove the flywheel bolts and flywheel. Discard the bolts on the 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L; the two V8 procedures explicitly identify their bolts as non-reusable torque-to-yield fasteners.

steps.title: Position the flywheel and correct bolts
steps.body: Fit the flywheel using the fasteners required by its engine procedure. The 2.3L requires special new bolts, not standard substitutes. On the 3.7L, one of the eight mounting holes is offset, so the flywheel fits in only one position.

steps.title: Apply the exact tightening schedule
steps.body: For the 2.3L, tighten in stages to 50 Nm, 80 Nm and 112 Nm. The 3.7L uses 80 Nm. The 5.0L uses 10 Nm, 20 Nm and then 60°. The 5.2L uses 10 Nm, 20 Nm and then 80 Nm. Complete every stage in order, then remove holding tool 303-103 where fitted.

steps.title: Reinstall the clutch
steps.body: Complete clutch installation through the same engine-specific procedure used for removal. Its assembly requirements remain part of the job; the flywheel instructions do not replace them.

steps.title: Complete the electronic correction
steps.body: For the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L, perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction with the scan tool. For the 5.2L, use the Powertrain Control Module (PCM) Misfire Monitor Profile Correction routine.

watchFor.title: Similar V8 stages with different endings
watchFor.body: The 5.0L finishes with an angle turn; the 5.2L finishes with a torque setting. Their initial stages do not make the complete schedules interchangeable.

notes: Use the engine identification information when ordering replacement parts; parts can differ within an engine family.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical completion
verification.body: Check that the correct fasteners and tightening stages were used, the holding tool has been removed where applicable, and clutch installation is complete.

verification.title: Record the correction result
verification.body: Record the engine variant and successful completion of its specified scan-tool routine.
