guides.title: Remove and refit the intake manifold: 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Remove the intake manifold using the correct engine branch, assess its condition and seals, then restore its plumbing and electrical connections.
guides.introduction: The intake manifold distributes incoming air to the engine’s cylinders. Its surrounding hoses, wiring and supports must be released before it can move freely. The engines share this purpose, but the 2.3L removal route differs substantially from the V8 procedures, particularly around the fuel system and rear connections.
guides.why: Clean sealing surfaces protect the engine from contamination. Metal left inside a manifold after valve or piston damage can damage the repaired engine, while incorrect gasket reuse can compromise the intake seal.

when.summary: When manifold repair or removal is required, or during inspection following upper-engine damage.
notes: Confirm the engine variant before selecting parts and procedures; check the V8 engine identification labels.

prepare.title: Arrange the required capability
prepare.detail: Have suitable torque tools, including angle-tightening capability for the V8 procedures. The 2.3L requires a hoist; use the marked lifting points and never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare the correct replacement parts
prepare.detail: Have new V8 manifold gaskets and new 5.2L strut-brace nuts available. Keep debris from entering exposed engine passages during cleaning.

steps.title: Establish engine-specific access
steps.body: For the 2.3L, place the vehicle in NEUTRAL on a hoist and remove the appearance cover. For either V8, release fuel pressure and disconnect both battery cables using their procedures. Remove the strut brace if fitted on the 5.0L; on the 5.2L, remove it and discard its nuts. Remove the 5.0L appearance cover, then the applicable V8 air-cleaner outlet pipe, cowl grille, extension and initial heater-hose support.

steps.title: Release the 2.3L external connections
steps.body: Follow the [2.3L procedure](#/document/G1660523). Disconnect the evaporative-emission purge coupling, release the fuel and vapor tubes from their retainer, and move the disconnected purge valve aside. Release the manifold pressure/temperature sensor and throttle wiring, charge-air-cooler outlet tube, rear vacuum coupling and coolant-tube mounting nut.

steps.title: Release the V8 plumbing and fuel connections
steps.body: Use the [5.0L procedure](#/document/G1685326) or [5.2L procedure](#/document/G1800279). Release the vacuum, crankcase ventilation and evaporative-emission connections, throttle wiring and remaining heater-hose support. Disconnect both injector banks and the fuel supply. Remove the 5.0L fuel-rail insulators; disconnect the 5.2L fuel-pressure sensor. Remove the rail bolts, leaving the rail with the manifold.

steps.title: Move the manifold only far enough to release its rear attachments
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove the mounting bolts, move the manifold back, disconnect the positive crankcase ventilation tube and detach the knock-sensor connector retainers. On either V8, loosen the manifold bolts and lift it upward and forward to disconnect the rear wiring and retainers. Then remove the manifold.

steps.title: Assess the manifold and sealing surfaces
steps.body: After upper-engine failure, inspect for metal debris; replace the manifold if any is found. Discard V8 gaskets and clean and inspect their sealing surfaces. The 2.3L gaskets may be reused only if free of nicks, cuts and abrasions.

steps.title: Reconnect concealed attachments before seating
steps.body: On the 2.3L, attach the knock-sensor retainers and crankcase ventilation coupling, then position the manifold on the coolant-tube stud with the tube correctly located. On the V8s, fit new gaskets and reconnect rear wiring before final positioning. Follow the engine-specific tightening instructions, including the V8 manifold and fuel-rail torque-and-angle stages.

steps.title: Restore the surrounding assemblies
steps.body: Reconnect each branch’s tubes, wiring, retainers and supports in installation order. Restore V8 fuel connections, insulators where applicable, cowl parts and inlet pipe. Put the 5.0L cover grommets on the manifold before fitting its cover. Refit the applicable brace, using new 5.2L nuts, and reconnect the V8 battery cables.

watchFor.title: Trapped rear connections
watchFor.body: Do not fully seat the manifold before reconnecting the attachments reached by its partial movement.

watchFor.title: Coolant-tube position on the 2.3L
watchFor.body: The tube must be correctly positioned as the manifold is installed on its stud.

notes: Use each engine’s own coupling and tightening instructions throughout.

diagnostics.finding: Metal debris inside the manifold following upper-engine failure
diagnostics.meaning: Reusing the manifold risks further engine damage.
diagnostics.next: Install a new manifold.

guides.title: Oil pan replacement and resealing for 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Remove and reseal the oil pan using the correct engine-support, subframe, sealing and reassembly procedure for your engine.
guides.introduction: The oil pan collects the engine oil that the pickup supplies to the lubrication pump. Its sealing joint keeps that oil inside the engine. This is an advanced in-vehicle repair: the engine needs support from above, and the front subframe must be lowered for access. The four engines share that approach, but their pan seals, pickup connections and installation sequences differ.
guides.why: Clean sealing surfaces prevent leakage, while keeping debris out protects the engine’s oil supply. Correct pickup-seal installation is especially important on the V8 engines. The work also disturbs steering and subframe attachments, so their replacement fasteners, alignment and completion checks are essential parts of the repair.

when.summary: When the oil pan requires replacement or its sealing joint requires resealing.
notes: Oil around the pan alone does not establish which joint needs repair.
Follow the 6R80 automatic or MT82 manual branch where specified; convertible and cooler-equipped branches apply only where fitted.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and support capability
prepare.detail: Have a hoist, adjustable subframe stand, oil-drain equipment, steering-wheel holding device and torque/angle tools. Use engine support bar 303-F072 with brackets 303-050 for the 2.3L and V8 engines, or lift eyes 303-1245 and 303-1529 for the 3.7L. Support-bar feet belong on body structure, never the fenders.

prepare.title: Have replacement parts ready before opening
prepare.detail: All variants require a new oil filter, steering-column shaft bolt, rear subframe bolts and front subframe nuts. The 5.0L also needs a new baffle/gasket and pickup O-ring; the 5.2L needs a new pan gasket, pickup seal and cross-brace nuts. Prepare TA-357 room-temperature-vulcanizing (RTV) silicone and the specified cleaning materials. The 5.2L requires a diagnostic scan tool for ride-height calibration.

steps.title: Establish engine-specific access
steps.body: Position the vehicle in Neutral on the hoist and follow the applicable battery-disconnection sequence. Loosen the steering-column dash seal carefully and hold the wheel straight ahead. The 2.3L needs upper-cover access; the 3.7L requires cowl access and moving the air-conditioning compressor aside after removing its belt and disconnecting its electrical connection. Its convertible branch adds cowl-extension work. V8 access includes intake, cowl and battery-tray components, plus removal of the camshaft position sensor.

steps.title: Support the engine and drain the oil
steps.body: Support the cooling module and install the engine-support equipment in the engine’s listed order. Release the mount attachments; disconnect the 2.3L mount vacuum tubes where directed. Raise V8 engines 50 mm. Remove the wheels and appropriate shields, drain the oil and discard the filter. On the 5.2L, draining and disconnecting the oil-cooler hoses occur before raising the engine.

steps.title: Release and lower the subframe
steps.body: With the dash seal already loosened, disconnect the steering shaft without hammering, prying or forcing it. Discard its bolt and secure the shaft to the frame rail. Release brake-line and wiring retainers, plus the applicable cooler brackets. On the 5.2L, disconnect both front ride-height sensors and their arm brackets. Support and mark the subframe before discarding its specified fasteners and lowering it 102 mm. On the 2.3L and 3.7L, follow the staged bellhousing-fastener loosening sequence; never exceed 5 mm.

steps.title: Remove the pan and prepare the joint
steps.body: Follow the selected engine’s remaining bracket and fastener sequence. The 2.3L and 3.7L require engine-to-transmission separation limited to 5 mm; use only the illustrated pry pads on the 3.7L. Remove the pan and the seals identified for replacement. Follow the RTV surface-preparation procedure, keeping debris out of the engine. Thoroughly wash the 3.7L pan after cleaning.

steps.title: Reseal the 2.3L pan
steps.body: Follow the [2.3L removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1945808). Apply a 3 mm sealant bead and install the pan finger-tight. Tighten the front-cover-to-pan fasteners first to align the pan flush with the block, then tighten the pan bolts. Secure the pan within 10 minutes. If that limit is missed, remove the sealant, clean again and allow drying until no wetness remains or 10 minutes have elapsed, whichever is longer. Draw the engine and transmission together using the specified alternating lower-bolt sequence.

steps.title: Reseal the 3.7L pan
steps.body: Follow the [3.7L removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1681525), including its additional sealant at the front-cover and rear-retainer joints. Install and align the pan within 4 minutes; complete final pan-bolt tightening within 60 minutes. Keep the pan close to the transmission, then slide it forward to avoid wiping away sealant. Draw the engine and transmission together without final torque, then follow the pan, front-cover and bellhousing tightening sequence. The automatic has an additional bottom bellhousing-to-pan bolt.

steps.title: Reseal the 5.0L pan
steps.body: Follow the [5.0L removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1685456). Apply joint sealant, install the new baffle/gasket, then refit the pickup with a new O-ring before installing the pan. If the front cover has been removed, apply sealant only at the rear-retainer joints at this stage. Complete installation and tightening within 5 minutes. Alternatively, tighten fasteners 7, 8, 9 and 10 to 8 Nm within that window and finish all fasteners within 1 hour. Use the illustrated stud positions and staged tightening sequence.

steps.title: Reseal the 5.2L pan
steps.body: Follow the [5.2L removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1800281). Install the new gasket and pickup seal, lubricating the seal’s inner bore with the specified clean engine oil. Apply joint sealant. Press the outside of the pan at the pickup location until the tube fully engages the pump seal. Complete tightening within 5 minutes, or tighten fasteners 6, 7, 13 and 15 to 8 Nm within that window and finish all fasteners within 1 hour. Follow this engine’s stud positions and tightening stages.

steps.title: Restore the supporting systems
steps.body: Raise and realign the subframe to its marks, using the specified alignment tool on the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L. Fit new subframe hardware and tighten in the prescribed cross pattern. Restore steering with a new shaft bolt, wiring, brake-line retainers and any cooler or sensor connections. Complete the engine-specific filter, shield, wheel, engine-mount and upper-access installation sequence, removing temporary supports when directed. Restore the dash seal and battery connections in the listed order.

watchFor.title: Expired sealant working time
watchFor.body: If neither the normal V8 tightening deadline nor its permitted staged alternative is met, remove the sealant and clean the joint again. Tightening cured sealant later does not restore the specified sealing process.

watchFor.title: Damaged steering seals or forced shaft connections
watchFor.body: Protect the dash-seal foam and retaining brackets against damage that could admit fumes, air or water. Never force the steering shaft into position.

notes: For the 2.3L sealant bead, use 3 mm; the paired imperial dimension is inconsistent.

Filter-seal preparation differs: lubricate the 2.3L filter seal with clean oil, but do not lubricate the 3.7L filter gasket or 5.0L filter O-ring. Follow the separate oil-service procedure for the 5.2L.

verification.title: Complete the steering inspection
verification.body: Carry out the Steering Column Collapsed Check after reconnecting the lower shaft. Installing the new bolt does not replace this inspection.

verification.title: Restore the oil supply
verification.body: Confirm the new filter is installed and fill with clean engine oil according to the selected engine’s specifications. Do not transfer oil specifications or quantities between engines.

verification.title: Record the 5.2L calibration result
verification.body: After restoring both front ride-height sensor connections and completing reassembly, carry out Ride Height Calibration with the diagnostic scan tool and record its completion result.

guides.title: Replace the oil pressure switch on 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L engines
guides.summary: Remove and install the oil pressure switch using the access, reuse and tightening requirements for the identified engine.
guides.introduction: The oil pressure switch provides an electrical indication associated with pressure in the engine lubrication system. It does not produce that pressure: the oil pump supplies oil to the engine's lubricated components. This repair disconnects the switch wiring and removes the threaded switch, then restores the connection using the engine-specific installation requirements.
guides.why: These switches share a purpose but have different installation rules. The 2.3L switch must be discarded after removal, while the 3.7L and 5.0L procedures permit reuse with specified thread sealant. Their tightening instructions also differ, so identifying the engine is essential before starting.

when.summary: When switch replacement is justified or the switch must be removed during another engine repair.
notes: An oil-pressure warning does not by itself prove that the switch has failed.

prepare.title: Identify the engine and installation method
prepare.detail: Select the matching procedure before obtaining parts. Have suitable torque equipment; the 5.0L installation also requires controlled angle tightening.

prepare.title: Provide safe access
prepare.detail: Position the vehicle in neutral on a hoist. Use the marked lifting points and check clearance around suspension, exhaust and steering components. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare sealant only for the applicable reuse branch
prepare.detail: For a reused 3.7L or 5.0L switch, use Motorcraft Thread Sealant with PTFE (polytetrafluoroethylene), TA-24-B, specification WSK-M2G350-A2.

steps.title: Follow the matching access route
steps.body: Use the [2.3L](#/document/G1660469), [3.7L](#/document/G1681526) or [5.0L](#/document/G1685328) procedure. The illustrated switch beside the oil filter belongs to the 2.3L procedure; use the correct engine procedure to identify the working location.

steps.title: Remove the fitted 3.7L underbody assembly
steps.body: On the 3.7L, identify whether the vehicle has an underbody shield alone or a subframe bracket and shield assembly. Loosen the two front bolts, remove the remaining bolts and remove the fitted assembly. Keep its fasteners associated with their illustrated locations.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the switch
steps.body: Disconnect the oil pressure switch electrical connector, then remove the switch. Discard the removed 2.3L switch. For the 3.7L and 5.0L, retain the distinction between installing a replacement and reinstalling the existing switch.

steps.title: Seal and tighten for the identified engine
steps.body: Apply the specified thread sealant if reusing a 3.7L or 5.0L switch. Install the 2.3L replacement to 15 Nm, the 3.7L switch to 18 Nm, or the 5.0L switch to 14 Nm followed by 180°. Keep these three instructions separate.

steps.title: Restore the connector and shielding
steps.body: Reverse the remaining removal operations. Reconnect the switch wiring and reinstall any removed 3.7L shield or bracket assembly. Use its illustrated fastener groups and corresponding torques.

watchFor.title: A reused 2.3L switch
watchFor.body: Removal requires discarding this switch; the reuse instructions for the other engines do not apply.

watchFor.title: Mixed tightening instructions
watchFor.body: The 5.0L torque-and-angle method must not be transferred to either of the other engines.

notes: Switch installation is not an oil-pressure measurement or a substitute for diagnosing an unresolved pressure complaint.

verification.title: Confirm completed installation
verification.body: Confirm the correct tightening method was completed, the connector is reattached and any removed shielding is secured.

verification.title: Record the installation branch
verification.body: Record the engine, whether the switch was new or reused, and the applicable sealant and tightening work.

guides.title: Replace the engine oil pump: 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Follow the engine-specific access, pump installation and reassembly sequence while preserving timing, steering integrity and oil-pan sealing.
guides.introduction: The oil pump supplies the engine's lubrication circuit. On the 5.0L and 5.2L, an internal-gear pump at the front of the block is driven by flats on the crankshaft, while an integral relief valve limits pressure. These engines share a broad pump-installation method, but the access work differs substantially from the 2.3L and 3.7L. This is a major engine repair involving timing components or a lowered subframe, rather than a simple external pump exchange.
guides.why: Contamination can damage the engine through its oil passages. Incorrect timing restoration can compromise engine operation, while forcing the steering shaft or reusing its bolt can create a steering-control hazard. Oil-pan sealant also has engine-specific working times. Each branch must therefore remain a complete sequence, with its own fasteners, seals and checks.

when.summary: When engine repair has established that the oil pump requires replacement.
notes: These replacement procedures do not establish that an oil-pressure complaint is caused by the pump.
The 2.3L and 3.7L procedures distinguish 6R80 automatic and MT82 manual access; the 3.7L also has convertible-specific cowl work.

prepare.title: Provide lifting and timing capability
prepare.detail: Use a hoist at the specified lifting points, oil-drain equipment and appropriate engine-repair tools. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare engine and subframe support
prepare.detail: The 2.3L uses engine lifting brackets 303-050 and support bar 303-F072; the 3.7L uses lift eyes 303-1245 and 303-1529 with that support bar. Both require adjustable subframe support.

prepare.title: Prepare branch-specific equipment and parts
prepare.detail: The 3.7L requires camshaft holding tools 303-1248 and a soft-jawed vise for its tensioner. The 2.3L requires a round-ended steel rule for pan alignment. Have the specified sealant, replacement pickup seal, oil filter and required new steering/subframe fasteners ready.

steps.title: Select the complete engine procedure
steps.body: Identify the engine before ordering parts. Place the vehicle in NEUTRAL on the hoist. Use the [2.3L](#/document/G1945809), [3.7L](#/document/G1681527), [5.0L](#/document/G1685329) or [5.2L](#/document/G1800282) procedure throughout; their access and tightening instructions are not interchangeable.

steps.title: Prepare upper access on the 2.3L or 3.7L
steps.body: Follow the branch's battery-disconnection and front-cover sequence. Loosen the steering-column dash seal without damaging its foam or brackets, then hold the steering wheel straight ahead. The 3.7L additionally requires cowl access, convertible cowl-extension work where fitted, and moving the disconnected A/C compressor aside after belt removal. Install the specified lifting attachments, support the cooling module and engine, and release the mount attachments in the engine procedure's order. On the 2.3L, disconnect the specified mount vacuum tubes; place support-bar feet on body structure near the strut towers, never on the fenders.

steps.title: Preserve 3.7L valve timing
steps.body: After front-cover removal, rotate the crankshaft clockwise only to align the timing marks. Remove the oil tubes and install the camshaft holding tools at top dead center. If colored chain links are not visible, mark the links at both intake timing units and the crankshaft sprocket exactly as illustrated. Remove the tensioner, arm and lower left guide, then position the chain aside and remove the sprocket.

steps.title: Lower the subframe on the 2.3L or 3.7L
steps.body: Remove the wheels and applicable shields, drain the oil and discard the filter. With the dash seal already loosened, disconnect the lower steering shaft without hammering or prying; discard its bolt and secure the shaft to the frame rail. Release electric power-assisted steering harness and brake-line retainers. Mark and support the subframe, discard the specified mounting fasteners and lower it by the prescribed distance. Move automatic-transmission cooling-tube brackets aside at the point specified for that engine. Remove the oil pan; on the 3.7L, use only the illustrated pry pads.

steps.title: Remove the pump through the appropriate route
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove the pickup and discard its gasket, release the compressed tensioner spring carefully, move the pump chain aside and remove the sprocket and pump. On the 3.7L, remove the pickup, discard its O-ring and remove the pump. For the 5.0L, remove timing chains, crankshaft sprocket and oil pan before the pump fasteners. For the 5.2L, remove timing chains and oil pan, then the sprocket and pump. Clean the specified mating and sealing surfaces without introducing debris.

steps.title: Install the pump and pickup components
steps.body: Prime the 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L pumps with 2 tablespoons of oil and rotate them by hand as directed. For either V8, align the pump rotor with the crankshaft flats, seat the pump against the block and hold it there throughout the illustrated staged tightening sequence. Follow the separate 2.3L or 3.7L pump tightening instructions. Restore the 2.3L sprocket, chain and tensioner, hooking its spring around the shoulder bolt. Install a new 2.3L pickup gasket or new 3.7L pickup O-ring.

steps.title: Seal the 2.3L or 3.7L oil pan
steps.body: Use the specified Motorcraft TA-357 silicone pattern. On the 2.3L, secure the pan within 10 minutes and align its front face flush with the block using the steel rule. If that window is missed, remove the sealant, clean again and allow drying until no wetness remains or 10 minutes have passed, whichever is longer. On the 3.7L, apply the additional beads at the rear-retainer joints, install and align the pan within 4 minutes, and finish tightening within 60 minutes. Keep it close to the transmission before sliding it forward to avoid wiping away sealant. Follow the illustrated bolt sequence and transmission-specific bellhousing attachments.

steps.title: Restore the subframe and steering
steps.body: Raise and align the subframe to the original marks using the specified alignment tool. Install new front nuts and rear bolts, then tighten in the prescribed cross patterns. Restore cooling-tube brackets, structural attachments and line retainers in branch order. Reconnect the steering shaft without force, install a new shaft bolt and perform the [steering-column collapsed check](#/document/G1721912). Install a new oil filter: lubricate its seal on the 2.3L, but do not lubricate the gasket on the 3.7L.

steps.title: Complete timing and engine closure
steps.body: For the 3.7L, install the crankshaft sprocket with its timing dot outward and align the chain links with the timing marks. Reset and pin the tensioner in the soft-jawed vise, install it, remove the pin and verify timing before removing the camshaft tools and restoring the oil tubes and front cover. For the 5.0L, reinstall the oil pan, sprocket and timing chains in that order. For the 5.2L, reinstall the sprocket, oil pan and timing chains using its own linked procedures.

steps.title: Restore access components and refill
steps.body: Complete each engine's support-removal and mount-refastening sequence. Restore shields, wheels, cooling-module attachments, mount vacuum connections where applicable, front cover, compressor and cowl components as required. Remove the steering-wheel holding device and reposition the dash seal. Reconnect the battery as directed and refill with the oil specified for that engine.

watchFor.title: Steering resistance or damage
watchFor.body: Never hammer, pry or force the shaft. Loosening the dash seal before shaft work and replacing the shaft bolt are mandatory.

watchFor.title: Spring and sealant constraints
watchFor.body: Handle the compressed 2.3L tensioner spring carefully. Keep the 2.3L and 3.7L sealant working times separate.

notes: Automatic-transmission cooling-tube brackets and oil-pan attachments differ from manual-transmission arrangements.
The 3.7L procedure does not give the pump-priming instruction used by the other three engines; follow its own installation branch.

diagnostics.finding: The 3.7L primary chain's colored links are not visible.
diagnostics.meaning: The original timing relationships need explicit replacement reference marks before chain removal.
diagnostics.next: Mark the illustrated intake-unit and crankshaft-sprocket links before disturbing the chain.

verification.title: Record the 3.7L timing post-check
verification.body: Verify all timing marks and the specified link counts before closure: 48 links between the right and left intake references, and 35 between the left intake and crankshaft references.

verification.title: Complete the steering check
verification.body: For the 2.3L and 3.7L, record the lower-shaft collapsed-check result after reconnection and confirm the dash seal is restored.

verification.title: Confirm lubrication restoration
verification.body: Confirm the required pickup seal and filter replacement, applicable pump priming and engine-specific oil refill are complete.

guides.title: Replace Timing Chains on the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L
guides.summary: Remove and install the timing chains using the locking, positioning and tensioner procedures specific to the fitted engine.
guides.introduction: Timing chains synchronize the crankshaft and camshafts so valve movement follows piston movement. The variable camshaft timing (VCT) assemblies operate within that mechanically established relationship. This repair opens the engine front, removes the chain and its supporting components, then restores timing before reassembly. The four engines require distinct procedures.
guides.why: Crankshaft position, rotation direction and tensioner resetting are engine-specific. In particular, the 2.3L crankshaft sprocket depends on friction clamping, while the two V8 procedures use different crankshaft positions and different installation movements. Mixing these instructions can damage the engine.

when.summary: When timing-chain removal or renewal is required for an established engine repair.
notes: Select the complete procedure for the fitted engine before beginning.
The 5.0L procedure specifically supersedes the approach used on earlier engines.

prepare.title: Match tools to the engine
prepare.detail: The 2.3L uses camshaft alignment tool 303-1565; the 3.7L uses camshaft holding tools 303-1248; both V8s use crankshaft holding tool 303-448. Arrange the specified vise, retaining pins, counterholding tools and torque equipment.

prepare.title: Prepare access and protect the engine
prepare.detail: Keep foreign material out of engine passages and the oil pan. The 2.3L requires a hoist with the transmission in neutral and high-pressure fuel-pump drive removal. Follow all prerequisites in its fuel-pump-drive and front-cover procedures.

prepare.title: Use proper lifting support
prepare.detail: Use the marked lifting points and correctly positioned hoist adapters. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; the emergency wheel-changing jack is unsuitable for this repair.

steps.title: Complete the engine-specific access procedure
steps.body: Remove the appropriate engine front cover. On the 2.3L, first remove the high-pressure fuel-pump drive unit. Before loosening its crankshaft pulley bolt, install the specified crankshaft and camshaft locking tools: loosening that bolt also releases the unkeyed crankshaft sprocket.

steps.title: 2.3L: release and remove the chain
steps.body: Follow the [2.3L procedure](#/document/G1660471). Fit the camshaft alignment tool in the rear slots. Counterhold with an open-ended wrench while loosening the exhaust, then intake VCT bolts. For a cast-iron tensioner, release its ratchet, compress it through the chain arm and pin it before removal. Remove the fitted tensioner, arm, chain and guide, then discard the VCT bolts.

steps.title: 2.3L: rebuild and release the correct tensioner
steps.body: Install new VCT bolts, then the guide, chain and arm. If an aluminum tensioner needs resetting, spread its ratchet wire clip, compress the plunger in a soft-jawed vise and pin both holes. For a reusable cast-iron tensioner, compress only the plunger, hold the ratchet released with a pick, retract the ratchet arm and pin it. Tighten the installed tensioner before removing its pin. Counterhold and tighten the intake, then exhaust VCT bolts to 40 Nm followed by 60°. Remove the alignment tool.

steps.title: 3.7L: establish references and remove the chain
steps.body: Follow the [3.7L procedure](#/document/G1681528). Rotate the crankshaft clockwise only, aligning the illustrated intake VCT marks. Remove the left oil tube and fit its camshaft holding tool, then repeat on the right. If colored links are invisible, mark the chain at both intake VCT marks and the two links straddling the crankshaft mark. Remove the tensioner, arm, lower left guide, VCT oil control solenoids and chain. Keep the solenoids clean.

steps.title: 3.7L: restore timing and the oil-control components
steps.body: Align the chain links with the VCT and crankshaft marks, then install the lower left guide and arm. Release the tensioner ratchet detent, compress the plunger in a soft-jawed vise, align its retaining holes and pin it. Install and tighten the tensioner before releasing the pin. Slight camshaft movement may be needed for alignment or slack removal. Complete the link-count check below. Refit the solenoids without force, then remove each holding tool and reinstall the right and left oil tubes using their separate staged tightening instructions.

steps.title: V8s: remove the right chain before the left
steps.body: For the [5.0L](#/document/G1685330), rotate clockwise to a crankshaft keyway position of 12 o'clock; for the [5.2L](#/document/G1800283), use 9:30. The right VCT mark must be on top; if necessary, turn clockwise one complete revolution. Remove the right tensioner, arm, guide and chain. For left-chain removal, turn clockwise to 5 o'clock on the 5.0L or 12:30 on the 5.2L. Any slight movement needed to free an arm or guide must be followed by returning to that bank's specified position.

steps.title: 5.0L: install left first, then reposition clockwise
steps.body: With the keyway at 5 o'clock, align the left chain's colored links with the VCT and crankshaft sprocket marks. Install its guide and arm, returning to that position after any permitted slack adjustment. Compress the tensioner plunger against a vise edge, pin it, install and tighten it, then remove the pin. Rotate clockwise one complete revolution, then continue clockwise to 12 o'clock. Install the right chain, guide, arm and pinned tensioner using the corresponding marks and release sequence.

steps.title: 5.2L: install left first, then reposition counterclockwise
steps.body: Install the left chain at 12:30, aligning its colored links with the VCT and crankshaft marks, then fit the guide and arm. Reset each tensioner by compressing its plunger, holding the ratchet lock released with a small screwdriver, retracting the ratchet arm and inserting a pin. Install and tighten the tensioner before releasing it. Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise to 9:30 for right-chain installation. Fit the right chain, guide, arm and tensioner; restore 9:30 after any permitted slack adjustment.

steps.title: Complete the correct engine's reassembly
steps.body: After the applicable timing and tensioner checks, install the engine front cover using its own procedure. On the 2.3L, subsequently reinstall the high-pressure fuel-pump drive unit. Complete the associated access procedures rather than treating chain installation as the end of the repair.

watchFor.title: 2.3L alignment-tool overload
watchFor.body: Tool 303-1565 establishes alignment only. Use an open-ended wrench to resist camshaft turning during VCT bolt work.

watchFor.title: 2.3L cast-iron ratchet damage
watchFor.body: Do not compress the ratchet assembly while resetting this tensioner.

watchFor.title: 3.7L solenoid installation resistance
watchFor.body: Excessive force can damage the camshaft mega cap and render the cylinder head unusable. Inspect for burrs, sharp edges or contamination; clean external surfaces only. A slight twisting motion aids installation.

notes: If a 2.3L cast-iron tensioner requires replacement, fit the specified aluminum tensioner and discard its existing mounting bolts in favor of new bolts.

verification.title: Record the 3.7L timing post-check
verification.body: Verify every timing mark. There must be 48 links between the right and left intake VCT colored links, and 35 links between the left intake colored link and the two crankshaft sprocket links. Record the counts.

verification.title: Confirm the selected branch is complete
verification.body: Confirm required chain alignment, tensioner installation and retaining-pin removal. Remove the specified camshaft tools before completing front-cover installation.

guides.title: Remove and reseal the 2.3L EcoBoost valve cover
guides.summary: Renew the valve-cover gasket, replace damaged solenoid seals only as needed, and restore the cover with correctly placed silicone sealant.
guides.introduction: The valve cover encloses the oil-lubricated camshaft area at the top of the 2.3L engine. Its gasket seals the cover to the cylinder head, while separate seals surround the variable camshaft timing (VCT) oil-control solenoids. This repair restores those sealing interfaces without treating every seal as a mandatory replacement.
guides.why: Debris entering the open engine can damage oil-fed components. Scratches in the mating faces create leak paths, and the silicone application has a strict assembly window. Clean preparation and an organized installation matter as much as fitting the new gasket.

when.summary: When a valve-cover sealing repair is established or the cover must be removed for engine access.
notes: Every cover removal requires a new cover gasket; solenoid-seal replacement depends on damage.

prepare.title: Have the sealing materials ready
prepare.detail: Provide a new valve-cover gasket and Motorcraft High Performance Engine RTV Silicone TA-357, specification WSE-M4G323-A6. RTV means room-temperature-vulcanizing silicone.

prepare.title: Prepare for selective seal replacement
prepare.detail: Damaged VCT seals require handle 205-153 and seal remover/installer 303-1247. Have suitable low-range torque equipment and a clean work area ready before opening the engine.

steps.title: Clear the top of the cover
steps.body: Remove the appearance-cover nuts and cover, then detach the fuel-supply tube retainer from the valve-cover stud. Remove the ignition coils using the [coil-on-plug procedure](#/document/G1673188), then remove the oil-level indicator. Releasing the fuel-tube retainer is the access operation specified here.

steps.title: Release the attached connections
steps.body: Disconnect the crankcase-vent quick-release connector, VCT solenoid connectors and camshaft position (CMP) sensor connectors. Detach the harness retainers, then remove the exhaust CMP sensor and its bolt. These connections must be clear before lifting the cover.

steps.title: Remove the cover and assess its seals
steps.body: Loosen the cover fasteners, remove the cover and discard its gasket. Inspect the VCT oil-control solenoid seals. Remove and discard a seal only if damaged, using the specified handle and remover/installer rather than improvising the extraction.

steps.title: Prepare the mating surfaces
steps.body: Keep foreign material out of the engine and make the mating faces clean. Follow [RTV surface cleaning and preparation](#/document/G1692003). Do not use metal scrapers, wire brushes, power abrasive discs or other abrasive methods: their scratches and gouges can become oil-leak paths.

steps.title: Fit the gasket and apply the specified sealant
steps.body: Install new VCT seals with the special tools only where damaged seals were removed. Fit a new cover gasket. Following the six locations identified in the [valve-cover procedure](#/document/G1660472), apply a 5.5 mm (0.22 in) bead of the specified silicone. Have the cover and tightening equipment ready before application.

steps.title: Secure the cover and restore its connections
steps.body: Secure the cover within 10 minutes of silicone application and tighten its fasteners to 10 Nm. If that window is missed, remove the sealant and clean the sealing area before restarting. Install the exhaust CMP sensor at 7 Nm. Restore harness retainers, CMP and VCT connectors, crankcase vent, oil-level indicator, coils and fuel-tube retainer. Install the appearance cover and tighten its nuts to 9 Nm.

watchFor.title: Contamination during cleaning
watchFor.body: Removed gasket material is still foreign material; keep it out of oil passages, coolant passages and the oil pan.

watchFor.title: Uncertain sealant placement
watchFor.body: Use the installation sealing-location illustration. The cover-removal views do not establish the six silicone application sites.

notes: The cover gasket and the VCT solenoid seals have different replacement rules; do not confuse them.

diagnostics.finding: A VCT oil-control solenoid seal is damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: That seal requires replacement during the cover repair.
diagnostics.next: Remove it with the specified tools and install a new seal before fitting the cover.

diagnostics.finding: The VCT seals are undamaged.
diagnostics.meaning: Their replacement is not required by this procedure.
diagnostics.next: Retain them and renew the valve-cover gasket.

verification.title: Record the sealing completion
verification.body: Confirm the new gasket, all six silicone locations, assembly within the time limit and completion of cover tightening.

verification.title: Check the restored attachments
verification.body: Confirm the sensor and solenoid connectors, vent connector, harness retainers, coils, dipstick and fuel-tube retainer are restored.

guides.title: Replace Mustang variable camshaft timing units by engine
guides.summary: Replace the variable camshaft timing units while preserving engine-specific chain timing, tensioner operation and new-fastener requirements.
guides.introduction: Variable camshaft timing (VCT) units change camshaft timing relative to the chain drive, altering when the valves operate. The twin independent systems on the 5.0L and 5.2L vary intake and exhaust timing to support power, economy and emissions control. Replacing these units opens the timing drive, making accurate reassembly central to the repair.
guides.why: The engines share a purpose but use different tensioner handling, camshaft positioning and fastening sequences. Foreign material entering oil or coolant passages or the oil pan can cause engine failure. Cleanliness and exact timing procedures are essential throughout.

when.summary: When a VCT unit requires replacement after diagnosis, or timing-drive repair requires its removal.
notes: Confirm the engine identity and obtain the matching timing-chain procedure before beginning.
The 3.7L secondary-tensioner replacement branches apply only when those tensioners are being replaced.

prepare.title: Timing-drive capability
prepare.detail: This work requires engine-timing experience, the equipment specified by the matching timing-chain procedure, camshaft-holding wrenches where directed, and torque-and-angle tightening capability.

prepare.title: Parts and engine-specific equipment
prepare.detail: Obtain new VCT bolts for every engine. The 3.7L requires hold-down tool 303-1530; any removed secondary tensioner must be replaced. The 5.2L requires an assistant for controlled intake-camshaft movement.

prepare.title: Clean working conditions
prepare.detail: Keep debris out of the engine. For 3.7L replacement tensioners, have the specified SAE 5W-20 synthetic blend engine oil for their O-rings and mega-cap bores.

steps.title: Remove the correct timing chain
steps.body: Follow the complete chain-removal route for the [2.3L](#/document/G1660471), [3.7L](#/document/G1681528), [5.0L](#/document/G1685330) or [5.2L](#/document/G1800283). On the V8 engines, remove the right-hand VCT units first when servicing both banks. Continue only with the branch for the identified engine.

steps.title: Service the 2.3L units
steps.body: Following the [2.3L unit procedure](#/document/G1945810), remove the units and discard their bolts. Discard any fitted washers; washers are not required during installation. Install the units with new bolts, leaving those bolts untightened. Their tightening belongs to the subsequent timing-chain installation procedure.

steps.title: Release the 3.7L units with tensioners retained
steps.body: For each applicable bank in the [3.7L procedure](#/document/G1681532), compress the secondary tensioner and fit tool 303-1530 through the rear guide hole, bearing against the mega cap to hold it collapsed. Remove and discard the VCT bolts, then remove the units. The ordinary removal sequence covers the left bank before the right bank; solenoids shown absent for clarity need not be removed for this branch.

steps.title: Use the optional 3.7L tensioner-replacement branch
steps.body: Only when replacing a secondary tensioner, remove the hold-down tool, exhaust oil-control solenoid, tensioner shoe and then the tensioner by pushing upward from below. Do not reuse that tensioner. Oil the new tensioner's O-rings and mega-cap bore, keeping its shipping clip fitted. Push it fully down until it snaps into place, install the shoe, then remove and discard the shipping clip.

steps.title: Complete 3.7L timing and tensioner assembly
steps.body: Follow the right-bank installation branch before the left. Align colored chain links with the VCT timing marks and unit holes with camshaft dowels; make only the slight camshaft movements directed. Install new bolts using the specified four-stage sequence. For a new tensioner, follow its dedicated sequence through pressing the chain and top shoe fully down and releasing them to activate tension, refitting the exhaust solenoid and refitting the hold-down tool. Complete the bank-specific VCT steps, confirm the chain is centered on its guides and remove the tool.

steps.title: Remove V8 units using the correct release method
steps.body: On the [5.0L](#/document/G1685333), discard the bolts and slide the units and secondary chain forward 2 mm before depressing the tensioner and turning it counterclockwise 90 degrees. On the [5.2L](#/document/G1800286), discard the bolts, depress and turn the tensioner counterclockwise 90 degrees, then have an assistant hold the intake camshaft by its flats while the assembly slides off. This prevents spring pressure binding the locating pin. Remove and inspect the 5.2L VCT oil filters for debris or damage; replace as necessary.

steps.title: Install the 5.0L assemblies
steps.body: Install the left bank before the right. Align the intake mark between the consecutive colored links and the exhaust mark with the single colored link. The exhaust mark is approximately at 2 o'clock on the left bank and 1 o'clock on the right. Slight exhaust-camshaft rotation using its flats may be needed. Turn the tensioner 90 degrees with its ramp forward, fully seat the units and center the chain. Hold the camshafts by their flats while tightening new bolts through the specified stages; install each bank's timing chain as directed.

steps.title: Install the 5.2L assemblies
steps.body: Install the left bank before the right. Use the same stated intake and exhaust colored-link relationships, but place the exhaust timing mark approximately at 12 o'clock on each bank. Have an assistant turn the intake camshaft counterclockwise by its flats until the locating pin engages. Fully seat the units, turn the tensioner 90 degrees with its ramp forward, and hold the camshafts while tightening new bolts through the specified stages. Install the applicable bank's timing chain.

steps.title: Finish timing-drive assembly and road test
steps.body: Complete the matching timing-chain installation procedure, including the deferred 2.3L VCT-bolt tightening where applicable. After the engine is fully reassembled, road test the vehicle as required by every engine branch.

watchFor.title: Resistance at a 3.7L oil-control solenoid
watchFor.body: Do not force it into the mega cap. Inspect for burrs, sharp edges or contamination, clean only external surfaces as needed and use the permitted slight twisting motion.

watchFor.title: 5.2L camshaft spring load
watchFor.body: Valve spring pressure tends to rotate the intake camshaft clockwise when the units are removed. Maintain the directed assistant control.

notes: Use the exact tightening stages in the engine-specific article; the 3.7L sequence differs from the V8 sequences, and the 2.3L defers tightening to chain installation.

diagnostics.finding: A 5.0L secondary chain is not centered over the tensioner.
diagnostics.meaning: The VCT assemblies require seating correction.
diagnostics.next: Reposition the assemblies until fully seated and the chain is centered.

diagnostics.finding: A 5.2L VCT oil filter contains debris or is damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: The required filter inspection has identified a service concern.
diagnostics.next: Replace the filter as necessary; this finding alone does not prove a VCT unit has failed.

verification.title: Confirm branch-specific assembly
verification.body: Confirm timing-mark alignment, unit seating, new-bolt tightening and all applicable tensioner activation and hold-down-tool removal steps before completing the chain procedure.

verification.title: Record the road-test result
verification.body: Record completion of the required road test and whether the original diagnosed concern remains.

guides.title: Remove, rebuild and reinstall the 3.7L V6 engine
guides.summary: Rebuild the 3.7L engine through controlled removal, measured component selection, precise valve timing and scan-tool commissioning.
guides.introduction: The pistons and connecting rods turn the crankshaft, while overhead camshafts operate the valves. Pressurized oil protects the bearings and supplies the timing-chain tensioners and variable cam timing (VCT) system. An overhaul opens these linked systems for inspection and replacement of damaged or worn components, then restores their clearances, timing and sealing before the engine returns to the vehicle.
guides.why: A successful rebuild depends on measurements and assembly discipline. Incorrect bearing selection can compromise lubrication; misplaced timing components can cause internal damage. Dirt left in oil passages or metal debris retained in an intake manifold can damage newly installed parts.

when.summary: When inspection establishes internal damage or wear requiring engine removal and measured rebuilding.
notes: Component measurements determine what needs replacement; dismantling does not establish that every part is unusable.
Follow the fitted transmission branch. Convertibles also require cowl access work and additional battery-cable disconnection.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and bench capability
prepare.detail: Provide a vehicle hoist, floor crane, specified engine lift eyes, leveling strap, mounting stand, and trolley jack with wooden block for transmission support. This work requires engine measurement, timing and staged torque-angle tightening capability.

prepare.title: Have the dedicated equipment ready
prepare.detail: Required equipment includes camshaft holding and tensioner hold-down tools, bearing-measurement equipment, a dial indicator, feeler gauge, piston-ring compressor, pulley puller, specified seal installers and a clutch alignment tool for the manual transmission. Commissioning requires a diagnostic scan tool.

prepare.title: Prepare clean parts and materials
prepare.detail: Provide clean SAE 5W-20 engine oil, the specified Motorcraft room-temperature-vulcanizing (RTV) silicone, cleaning materials and prescribed replacement parts. Protect exposed passages and keep indexed components organized throughout the work.

steps.title: Isolate the engine and clear access
steps.body: Follow [engine removal](#/document/G1681556). Place the vehicle in neutral on the hoist, release fuel pressure and disconnect battery ground before disconnecting fuel or electrical connections. Complete convertible cowl access where applicable. Drain coolant, mark the hood hinge positions and remove the hood. Remove the coolant reservoir, air cleaner, outlet pipe and air-conditioning compressor belt, then disconnect the specified hoses, fuel connections, harnesses and grounds.

steps.title: Support the transmission and lift the engine
steps.body: Position the air-conditioning compressor aside, install the lift eyes and complete underside access. Drain the oil, discard the filter, remove the starter and support the catalytic converters before releasing their connections. On automatics, disconnect the transmission wiring and remove and discard the torque-converter nuts. Follow the bellhousing sequence, support the engine with the crane and leveling strap, and support the transmission with the jack and wooden block before removing mount brackets and lifting the engine out.

steps.title: Mount and strip the engine
steps.body: Begin [bench disassembly](#/document/G1681557) by removing the automatic flexplate or manual clutch and flywheel. Index a reusable pressure plate and loosen its bolts evenly in the specified star pattern; discard those bolts. Remove the sensor ring and spacer plate, then mount the stand bolts into the cylinder block only. Strip accessories, wiring, intake parts, coils and covers. Drain remaining block coolant and remove the exhaust manifolds, coolant pump and front cover in sequence.

steps.title: Dismantle timing and internal components
steps.body: Rotate the crankshaft clockwise to the specified timing position and install the camshaft holding tools. Mark chain links if their colored marks are invisible. Use the tensioner hold-down tool when removing secondary chains and VCT units. Keep camshafts, caps, tappets, rods, pistons and bearings identified by position and orientation. Remove heads, oil pan, pickup, pump, rear seal, support brace and rotating assembly. Retain original rod bolts solely for the later bore measurement. Inspect pistons and measure head and block distortion before choosing replacement parts.

steps.title: Select bearings from codes and measurements
steps.body: Start [engine assembly](#/document/G1681560) with clean passages and the piston oil-cooling valves. Record block and crankshaft codes and use the correct main-bearing selection charts for each journal. Temporarily assemble each correctly oriented rod cap with its original bolts to measure its bore; remove and discard those bolts afterward. Measure crankshaft rod journals in the specified directions and select bearings from the chart.

steps.title: Build the lubricated rotating assembly
steps.body: Install lubricated main bearings, crankshaft and correctly oriented thrust washers. Use new main-cap vertical and side bolts, following the thrust-seating and tightening sequence. Measure and record crankshaft end play. Install lubricated pistons with the specified ring positions and original orientation, protecting bores and journals. Use new rod bolts and confirm smooth crankshaft rotation after each piston. Fit the support brace with new bolts, rear seal, oil pump and pickup with a new O-ring. Seal and align the oil pan flush with the block as directed.

steps.title: Assemble the heads and establish valve timing
steps.body: Install head gaskets and new head fasteners, including the discarded small bolts. Keep the crankshaft dowel at 9 o'clock until camshaft installation and valve-clearance work are complete. Refit lubricated tappets in their original locations. Complete the right bank, then the left: position camshaft seal gaps at 12 o'clock, follow the cap tightening sequence, check clearances, and fit the secondary timing assemblies using holding tools and new VCT bolts. Only when instructed, rotate the crankshaft clockwise 60 degrees to the dowel's 11 o'clock position. Install the primary chain and tensioner, then verify timing marks and the specified link counts.

steps.title: Seal and finish the engine
steps.body: Complete the oil tubes, front cover, coolant components, manifolds, covers, wiring and accessories through the assembly procedure. Observe sealant bead locations and installation windows. Renew prescribed gaskets, crankshaft seals, exhaust studs and nuts, coolant-pump seals and thermostat O-ring; renew cover tube seals only when damaged. Use a new crankshaft pulley bolt. After lifting the engine from its stand, refit the sensor ring and spacer plate. The manual branch requires clutch alignment, original pressure-plate indexing and new special pressure-plate bolts; the automatic branch uses the offset flexplate hole to establish orientation.

steps.title: Return the engine to the vehicle
steps.body: Follow [engine installation](#/document/G1681561). Grease the automatic torque-converter pilot hub and align the paint marks, or grease the manual input shaft as specified. Mate the engine and transmission while keeping the right catalytic converter clear of the exhaust studs. Restore mounts and bellhousing fasteners before removing supports. Use new automatic torque-converter nuts and new catalytic-converter connection nuts. Refit the starter, a new oil filter with its gasket unlubricated, fitted underbody protection, wheels, compressor, electrical connections, grounds, hoses and intake components.

steps.title: Refill and commission
steps.body: Complete the applicable cowl work and battery reconnection. Fill engine oil to the engine specification and vacuum-fill and bleed the cooling system through its dedicated procedure. Reinstall the hood using its index marks and reconnect the washer hoses. Start the engine and check the exhaust for leaks, perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction with the scan tool, then road-test the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Cleaning damage and trapped debris
watchFor.body: Use plastic scraping tools on head and block gasket faces; metal scrapers, wire brushes and abrasive power discs can create leak paths. Protect exposed cavities and wash cleaning debris from the front cover. Never use compressed air to disperse clutch dust.

watchFor.title: Forced covers or timing components
watchFor.body: Use the designated front-cover and oil-pan pry pads. Gently release valve covers stuck to VCT seals. Do not use power tools on the specified primary-chain guide bolts. If a VCT solenoid resists installation, inspect for burrs or contamination instead of forcing it.

watchFor.title: Sealant installation windows
watchFor.body: Use the specified Motorcraft silicone: an unsuitable product can cause oil foaming. Rear-seal-retainer and valve-cover installation and tightening have 4-minute limits. The front cover and 6 bolts must be installed within 4 minutes, with remaining bolts installed and tightened within 35 minutes. Missed front-cover or valve-cover windows require sealant removal, cleaning and reapplication.

notes: Connect both banks' VCT solenoid connectors at completion. A later assembly instruction says to disconnect the left-bank connectors; the dedicated left- and right-bank valve-cover installation procedures explicitly require connection.

diagnostics.finding: Metal debris is found in an intake manifold after valve or piston damage.
diagnostics.meaning: Retained debris can damage the repaired engine.
diagnostics.next: Install a new affected intake manifold before completing assembly.

diagnostics.finding: A cylinder head requires replacement.
diagnostics.meaning: Head replacement also requires a new secondary timing-chain tensioner.
diagnostics.next: Include the corresponding tensioner in the replacement work.

diagnostics.finding: Valve tappet clearance is outside specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The mechanical tappet size does not provide the required clearance.
diagnostics.next: Follow Valve Clearance Adjustment and install correctly sized tappets before proceeding with timing assembly.

diagnostics.finding: Crankshaft rotation is no longer smooth after a piston is installed.
diagnostics.meaning: The required assembly check has failed.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the assembly problem before installing further piston assemblies.

verification.title: Retain the measurement results
verification.body: Record bearing-selection codes, rod bore and journal measurements, and crankshaft end play. Confirm component inspection results and clearances against the applicable specifications.

verification.title: Confirm timing and cover sealing
verification.body: Complete the timing-mark and link-count post-check before closing the engine. Confirm valve-cover VCT seals sit below the tops of the solenoid electrical connectors.

verification.title: Complete running checks
verification.body: Check the running exhaust system for leaks, complete Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction and perform the specified road test.

guides.title: Strip and rebuild the 3.7L cylinder head subassembly
guides.summary: Disassemble and rebuild either 3.7L cylinder head while preserving valve-component positions and renewing the specified bank-specific parts.
guides.introduction: The 3.7L engine’s aluminum cylinder heads carry the valves beneath dual overhead camshafts. The valves control gas flow and seal the combustion chambers; their springs close them, while stem seals control oil passage along the stems. This bench overhaul sequence covers valves, springs, seals and head-mounted fittings. Arrange the separate cylinder-head removal, timing and refitting work before beginning.
guides.why: Reusable valve components must return to their original positions. The specified spring-compressor arrangement controls spring force during collet removal and installation, and the seal installer guides the stem seal into place. Left-hand and right-hand heads have different fittings, so their rebuilding sequences must remain distinct.

when.summary: When an already-accessible 3.7L cylinder head requires valve-component service or preparation of a replacement head.
notes: This guide begins with the cylinder head already removed. Follow the separate head-removal, timing and refitting procedures to reach and finish this bench work.

prepare.title: Organize components and tools
prepare.detail: Identify the head’s side and provide marked storage for every reusable valve component. Use the specified compressor tools and stem-seal installer; this work requires competent control of loaded valve springs.

prepare.title: Prepare the required replacement parts
prepare.detail: Provide new exhaust manifold nuts, studs and gasket. The right-hand head also requires a new cylinder head temperature (CHT) sensor. If replacing a cylinder head, replace the secondary timing chain tensioners as directed through the Variable Camshaft Timing (VCT) Unit procedure.

prepare.title: Use the specified lubricant
prepare.detail: For stem-seal installation, have clean SAE 5W-20 synthetic blend engine oil meeting WSS-M2C945-B1.

prepare.title: Workshop capability
prepare.detail: 3.7L cylinder-head bench work; valve-spring tools 303-300, 303-350, 303-1249 and 303-1418; stem-seal installer 303-470; torque tools and component identification storage.

steps.title: Strip the left-hand head fittings
steps.body: For the left-hand head, remove the ground strap and bolt, then the exhaust manifold heat shield and bolts. Remove the manifold and discard its nuts. Carry out the linked manifold cleaning and inspection, discard the studs and gasket, and remove the timing chain guide pin.

steps.title: Strip the right-hand head fittings
steps.body: For the right-hand head, remove the exhaust manifold and discard its nuts. Clean and inspect the manifold, then discard the studs and gasket. Remove the timing chain tensioner arm and timing chain guide pins. Remove and discard the CHT sensor.

steps.title: Remove plugs and organize the valve parts
steps.body: Remove the spark plugs using the [3.7L spark-plug procedure](#/document/G1675559). Mark reusable components before separating them so each can return to its original position.

steps.title: Disassemble each valve position
steps.body: Use the specified compressor arrangement shown in the cylinder-head procedure to remove the valve collet, spring retainer and spring. Remove the stem seal, then the valve. Repeat this sequence at each valve position, preserving the component identification.

steps.title: Install the valves and stem seals
steps.body: Install each valve in its assigned position. Lubricate the stem seal with the specified clean engine oil and install it with tool 303-470. The dedicated installer provides the required installation method.

steps.title: Reassemble the springs and plugs
steps.body: Use the spring-compressor tools to install each spring, retainer and collet. Repeat for every valve, retaining original positions for reused parts. Install the spark plugs through the linked ignition procedure.

steps.title: Rebuild the right-hand fittings
steps.body: Install the timing chain tensioner arm and guide pins, then a new CHT sensor. Install new exhaust manifold studs and a new gasket. Fit the manifold with new nuts and complete both tightening stages specified in the cylinder-head procedure.

steps.title: Rebuild the left-hand fittings
steps.body: Install the timing chain guide pin, new manifold studs and a new gasket. Install the manifold with new nuts and complete both tightening stages. Refit the heat shield and ground strap, tightening their bolts to the specified values.

watchFor.title: Head replacement changes the tensioner requirement
watchFor.body: Do not reuse the secondary timing chain tensioners when replacing a cylinder head; the procedure warns that engine damage may result.

watchFor.title: Parts that must not return
watchFor.body: Keep discarded manifold hardware, gaskets and the removed right-hand CHT sensor out of the reusable-parts groups.

notes: The illustrated compressor setup shows the specified tools working together; a generic compressor illustration is not an alternative setup.

verification.title: Check the bench assembly
verification.body: Confirm all reused components occupy their original positions, each valve position has its spring, retainer and collet installed, and the correct bank-specific fittings are restored.

verification.title: Record required renewals
verification.body: Record the renewed manifold parts, right-hand sensor where applicable, completion of staged manifold tightening and the secondary tensioner replacement requirement if the head was replaced.

guides.title: Remove and refit the left cylinder head on the 3.7L V6
guides.summary: Remove the left cylinder head, inspect its sealing surfaces, and reinstall it with new fastening and sealing parts before completing timing and exhaust checks.
guides.introduction: The left-hand cylinder head closes that bank's cylinders and carries the valves and overhead camshafts. On the 3.7L engine, the camshaft lobes act through mechanical bucket tappets, so those tappets must remain associated with their original positions. This repair opens the head-to-block joint and requires the camshaft and intake-manifold work to be completed as part of the same job.
guides.why: A new gasket cannot compensate for an unacceptable sealing surface. Dirt, scratches and distortion can undermine the repaired joint, while reused head bolts cannot provide the prescribed fastening process. Replacing the head also triggers a separate requirement for a new secondary timing-chain tensioner.

when.summary: When diagnosis establishes a need to remove the left cylinder head or repair its sealing joint.
notes: Inspect head and block distortion before deciding whether the existing head can be reinstalled.
A replacement cylinder head requires a new secondary timing-chain tensioner.

prepare.title: Prepare for engine and timing work
prepare.detail: Provide a hoist, torque and angle capability, oil-drain equipment, a protected bench and the equipment required by the camshaft and lower intake-manifold procedures.

prepare.title: Arrange clean handling and replacement parts
prepare.detail: Have lint-free towels, a plastic gasket scraper, a new head gasket, new head bolts and M6 bolt, new catalytic-converter flange nuts and an oil filter. Use the specified SAE 5W-20 synthetic-blend engine oil.

steps.title: Isolate the engine and clear access
steps.body: Follow the [head procedure](#/document/G1681515). Position the vehicle in Neutral on a hoist, release fuel pressure and disconnect the battery ground. Disconnect the left heated oxygen sensor and catalyst-monitor sensor connectors. Remove and discard the left catalytic-converter flange nuts and clean the converter-to-manifold sealing surfaces.

steps.title: Remove the camshafts and intake components
steps.body: Complete the removal portions of the [camshaft procedure](#/document/G1681512) and [lower intake-manifold procedure](#/document/G1681524), including their prerequisites. Remove the head ground strap, disconnect the camshaft-position sensor connectors, release the harness retainer and remove the sensors.

steps.title: Preserve the valve-train positions
steps.body: Remove the upper left timing-chain guide bolt with hand tools; power tools can damage the guide. Mark and remove the valve tappets so each reusable part can return to its original location. Inspect them and replace components as necessary. Remove and discard the M6 bolt.

steps.title: Lift the head and inspect the joint
steps.body: Protect exposed cavities with clean towels. Remove and discard the head bolts, lift off the head and discard its gasket. Use a plastic scraper to remove gasket traces without scratching either aluminum face. Support the head with its gasket side upward and check both head and block distortion using the linked inspection procedures.

steps.title: Install the head with new fasteners
steps.body: Install a new gasket and the head with new bolts. Follow the illustrated numbered sequence through all tightening stages: 20 Nm, 35 Nm, 90°, 90° and 45°. Install the new M6 bolt at 10 Nm. If the head is replaced, include the required new secondary timing-chain tensioner in the timing work.

steps.title: Restore the valve train and exhaust
steps.body: Lubricate the tappets with clean specified oil and return them to their original positions. Refit the guide using hand tools. Lubricate the camshaft-position sensor O-rings, install the sensors and reconnect the harness and ground strap. Install the lower intake manifold and left camshafts through their complete procedures. Refit the catalytic converter with new flange nuts and reconnect both exhaust-sensor connectors.

steps.title: Renew the oil and complete reassembly
steps.body: Drain the engine oil, reinstall the drain plug and discard the oil filter. Install a new filter without lubricating its seal, using the specified staged tightening. Fill with clean engine oil to the 3.7L specification, then reconnect the battery ground.

watchFor.title: Gasket-face damage
watchFor.body: Do not use metal scrapers, wire brushes or abrasive discs. Never rest the unprotected gasket face directly on the bench.

watchFor.title: Debris falling into the engine
watchFor.body: Keep passages covered during cleaning and remove the towels carefully so trapped material does not fall inside.

watchFor.title: Mixing tappets or reusing head bolts
watchFor.body: Tappets return to their marked positions. The head bolts and separate M6 bolt must be renewed.

notes: The head-bolt illustration identifies the tightening order; use it together with the staged tightening instructions.
The new oil-filter seal is specifically installed without lubrication in this procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The head or block fails its distortion inspection.
diagnostics.meaning: The sealing joint is not ready for reassembly.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the failed inspection according to the applicable distortion procedure before installing the gasket.

verification.title: Check the completed repair
verification.body: Start the engine and check the exhaust system for leaks, then road test the vehicle.

verification.title: Record inspection and test results
verification.body: Record head and block distortion results, whether the head and secondary tensioner were replaced, and the exhaust-leak and road-test outcomes.

applicability.equipment: 3.7L Duratec V6, left-hand cylinder head, with twin independent variable camshaft timing.

guides.title: Remove and refit the 3.7L right-hand cylinder head
guides.summary: Remove the right-hand cylinder head, assess its sealing surfaces and reinstall it with new fasteners, correctly positioned tappets and fresh engine oil.
guides.introduction: The 3.7L V6’s aluminum cylinder head carries the valves and overhead camshafts for one bank. Its camshaft lobes act directly on mechanical bucket tappets above the valves. Removing the right-hand head opens the head-gasket joint and requires disturbing the camshafts, intake and exhaust connections, so this repair includes substantial timing-system work.
guides.why: The gasket faces must remain clean and undamaged to seal again. Tappets return to their original positions, while the head bolts must be replaced because their tightening process permanently stretches them. Replacing the head also requires a new secondary timing-chain tensioner.

when.summary: When an established head or gasket repair requires removal of the 3.7L right-hand cylinder head.
notes: Plan the camshaft and lower-intake operations as part of the repair, including all their prerequisites.

prepare.title: Arrange access and timing capability
prepare.detail: Use a hoist at the designated lifting points; never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Have the 3.7L camshaft and lower-intake procedures available, along with torque-and-angle equipment and oil-drain equipment.

prepare.title: Prepare parts and clean storage
prepare.detail: Provide a new head gasket, head bolts, M6 bolt, catalytic-converter flange nuts and oil filter. Have clean SAE 5W-20 oil meeting WSS-M2C945-B1, lint-free towels, a plastic scraper and indexed storage for tappets. Add a secondary timing-chain tensioner if replacing the head.

steps.title: Isolate the engine and release exhaust connections
steps.body: With the vehicle in neutral on the hoist, release fuel pressure and disconnect the battery ground. Disconnect the right-hand heated oxygen sensor and catalyst-monitor connectors. Remove and discard the catalytic-converter flange nuts and clean the converter-to-manifold sealing surfaces.

steps.title: Expose the head and preserve tappet positions
steps.body: Remove the right-hand [camshafts](#/document/G1681512), then the [lower intake manifold](#/document/G1681524). Disconnect and remove the camshaft position sensors. Remove the upper timing-chain guide using hand tools, disconnect the cylinder-head temperature sensor, and index the tappets before removal. Inspect them and replace damaged components as necessary.

steps.title: Lift the head and clean the joint
steps.body: Remove and discard the M6 bolt and head bolts, then lift off the head. Discard the gasket. Cover exposed cavities with clean lint-free towels and use a plastic scraper to remove gasket remains from both mating faces. Protect the aluminum surfaces and support the head with its gasket face upward.

steps.title: Check whether the mating surfaces can be reused
steps.body: Perform the linked head and block distortion checks before assembly. Keep cleaning debris out of passages when removing the protective towels. A new gasket does not remove the need to assess the surfaces it will seal.

steps.title: Install the gasket and tighten new bolts
steps.body: Fit the new gasket and position the head. Follow the numbered illustration in the [head procedure](#/document/G1681516), completing the stages of 20 Nm, 35 Nm, 90°, 90° and 45° in order. Install the new M6 bolt at 10 Nm. If the head is replaced, include the required new secondary timing-chain tensioner.

steps.title: Restore the valve train and connections
steps.body: Lubricate tappets with clean specified engine oil and return them to their original positions. Reconnect the temperature sensor, reinstall the timing guide, and lubricate the camshaft-position-sensor O-rings before installation. Refit the lower intake manifold and right-hand camshafts through their complete procedures. Install new converter flange nuts and reconnect both exhaust-sensor connectors.

steps.title: Renew the oil and complete the repair
steps.body: Drain the engine oil and reinstall the drain plug to the head procedure’s specification. Replace the oil filter without lubricating its seal, then fill with clean specified oil using the 3.7L capacity information. Reconnect the battery ground, start the engine, check the exhaust system for leaks and road test.

watchFor.title: Timing-guide damage
watchFor.body: Do not use power tools to remove the upper right-hand timing-chain guide bolt.

watchFor.title: Scratched sealing faces
watchFor.body: Metal scrapers, wire brushes and abrasive discs can create leak paths. Never rest the head’s gasket face unprotected on the bench.

notes: The head-replacement requirement for a new secondary tensioner is conditional; retain that distinction when planning parts.

diagnostics.finding: Head or block distortion does not meet the applicable specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The mating surface has not passed the required inspection.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the condition before installing the gasket and head.

verification.title: Record the mechanical checks
verification.body: Record head/block distortion results, completion of the bolt-tightening stages and whether head replacement required a new secondary tensioner.

verification.title: Confirm completion in the vehicle
verification.body: Confirm the oil and filter replacement, complete the running exhaust-leak check and record the road-test result.
