guides.title: Replace the left exhaust manifold: 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Follow the engine-specific route to remove and reseal the left exhaust manifold, including engine support and steering-shaft work where required.
guides.introduction: The left-hand exhaust manifold collects exhaust from that cylinder bank and routes it toward the catalytic converter. Its joints must seal correctly after removal. Access differs substantially between these engines: the 5.0L manifold and catalytic converter are serviced as an assembly, while the 5.2L procedure removes the converter separately and also disconnects oil cooler hoses.
guides.why: The V8 procedures create clearance by supporting and raising the engine. Incorrect support can damage the body, while forcing the steering shaft or reusing its discarded bolt can compromise steering control. Correct engine identification also prevents mixing manifold hardware, tightening sequences and reassembly requirements.

when.summary: When an identified left-side exhaust repair requires manifold removal or replacement.
notes: Choose the complete procedure for the installed engine before starting; the three access routes are not interchangeable.

prepare.title: Provide safe lifting and engine support
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the designated lifting points identified by stamped triangles. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Check hoist adapters for interference with suspension, steering and exhaust parts.

prepare.title: Prepare the V8 support equipment
prepare.detail: Both V8 routes specify lifting bracket 303-050 and support bar 303-F072. The 5.0L also specifies 303-290B and adapters 303-290-01 and 303-290A-03A. Place support legs on the body structure, never the fenders.

prepare.title: Obtain the correct renewal parts
prepare.detail: Provide new manifold gaskets, studs and nuts. Also provide the branch-specific discarded parts: 3.7L converter flange nuts, steering-shaft bolts where removed, and 5.2L cross-brace nuts. The 5.2L materials include Motorcraft Silicone Gasket Remover ZC-30-A and Castrol EDGE Supercar 5W-50, specification WSS-M2C931-C.

steps.title: Identify the engine and establish access
steps.body: Position the vehicle in NEUTRAL on the hoist using the [lifting procedure](#/document/G1663631). Follow only the matching engine branch below. Both V8 branches require disconnecting the negative/ground and positive battery cables through [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356).

steps.title: 3.7L: remove the manifold
steps.body: Remove the [air cleaner](#/document/G1675694). Disconnect the left heated oxygen sensor and catalyst monitor sensor connectors. Remove and discard the converter flange nuts, remove the heat shield, then remove the manifold and discard its nuts, gasket and studs. Clean the converter mating surfaces and perform [manifold cleaning and inspection](#/document/G1661749).

steps.title: 3.7L: install and reseal
steps.body: Follow [G1681520](#/document/G1681520) to install new studs, gasket and manifold nuts, using its two-stage tightening. Refit the heat shield and converter with new flange nuts, reconnect both sensors and install the air cleaner. Start the engine and check the exhaust for leaks.

steps.title: 5.0L: prepare the engine-support installation
steps.body: For left-hand-drive, rear-wheel-drive vehicles, loosen the dash seal carefully, hand-start its nuts and position the steering straight ahead. Remove the intake outlet pipe and air cleaner, both engine-mount nuts, radiator sight shield and cross brace after moving the positive cable aside. Remove the battery tray, cowl grille, cowl extension and battery heat shield. Install the specified support arrangement and raise the engine 45 mm.

steps.title: 5.0L: clear the shaft and remove the assembly
steps.body: In the left-hand-drive, rear-wheel-drive branch, discard the lower steering-shaft bolt, separate the coupling without force and secure the shaft to the frame rail. Remove the muffler inlet pipe, move the air deflector aside and remove the engine-mount bracket. Disconnect both exhaust sensor connectors and release the harness retainers. Remove the manifold/converter assembly and discard the manifold nuts, gasket and studs.

steps.title: 5.0L: rebuild in the prescribed sequence
steps.body: Reverse [G2262730](#/document/G2262730), renewing discarded parts and cleaning all exhaust connections. Finger-tighten the manifold nuts, then use the illustrated sequence and both tightening stages. Restore the support, mount, steering, intake, body-access and battery connections as directed. Inspect the lower steering shaft after reassembly where disconnected, and check the exhaust for leaks.

steps.title: 5.2L: clear the steering and raise the engine
steps.body: Loosen the dash seal, hand-start its nuts and hold the steering wheel straight ahead with a holding device. Remove the underbody shields and [left catalytic converter](#/document/G1805802), then disconnect the oil cooler hoses. Discard the steering-shaft bolt, separate the lower coupling without force and secure the shaft to the frame rail. Remove the intake assembly, release the harness retainer, remove the cross brace and discard its nuts. Remove both engine-mount nuts, install the support tools and raise the engine 50 mm.

steps.title: 5.2L: renew the manifold joint
steps.body: Disconnect the heated oxygen sensor connector and harness retainer, then remove the left mount bracket and manifold, discarding the manifold nuts. Clean and inspect the manifold, then discard the gasket and studs. Install new studs, gasket and nuts using [G1800276](#/document/G1800276), including its illustrated tightening sequence. Restore the mount bracket, sensor connection and retainer, lower the engine, remove the tools and install the mount nuts.

steps.title: 5.2L: restore steering, oil and access parts
steps.body: Reconnect the steering shaft with a new bolt and perform the [Steering Column Collapsed Check](#/document/G1721912). Reconnect the oil cooler hoses; install the converter, shields and cross brace with new nuts. Restore the harness retainer and intake assembly, remove the steering holding device, seat and tighten the dash seal, then reconnect the battery. Inspect and adjust the engine oil level with the specified oil.

watchFor.title: Steering shaft resistance
watchFor.body: Never hammer, pry or force the shaft. On the 5.2L, the dash seal and fasteners must be loosened before removing or installing the lower joint at the steering gear.

watchFor.title: Damaged dash sealing
watchFor.body: Protect the sealer foam and retain the dash-seal brackets on their pins. Damage can admit noise, fumes, air or water.

notes: On the 5.0L, sensors can remain in a manifold assembly being reused, but their electrical connectors must still be disconnected.
If both 5.0L manifolds are being removed, use the engine-support setup specified by the right-hand manifold procedure.

verification.title: Complete the applicable exhaust check
verification.body: The 3.7L procedure requires starting the engine and checking for exhaust leaks; the 5.0L procedure also requires an exhaust leak check.

verification.title: Complete steering and oil checks
verification.body: Perform the lower steering-shaft inspection after the applicable 5.0L shaft work and after 5.2L reassembly. On the 5.2L, confirm the engine oil level has been inspected and adjusted.

guides.title: Remove and refit the right-hand exhaust manifold: 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Renew the right-hand exhaust manifold joints using the correct engine-specific access, replacement hardware and reassembly procedure.
guides.introduction: The right-hand exhaust manifold collects exhaust gas from one cylinder bank and directs it into the catalytic converter. Removing it exposes the cylinder-head sealing joint for inspection, resealing or manifold replacement. Access differs considerably: the 3.7L procedure is relatively direct, while both V8 procedures require engine support and removal of surrounding equipment.
guides.why: The gasket and fasteners maintain the seal between the manifold and cylinder head. All three procedures require new manifold studs, nuts and a gasket. On the V8 engines, controlled engine movement creates working clearance; supporting the engine incorrectly can damage the body. The 5.0L refrigerant connection and 5.2L oil-cooler connections introduce separate restoration requirements.

when.summary: When inspection calls for manifold removal, replacement or renewal of its sealing joints.
notes: Confirm the engine and transmission before selecting the procedure; the V8 access operations are different.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and engine support
prepare.detail: Use a hoist at the specified lifting points, with the vehicle in NEUTRAL. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Both V8 procedures require engine support bar 303-F072 and lifting bracket 303-050 (T70P-6000).

prepare.title: Prepare the correct replacement parts
prepare.detail: Obtain new manifold studs, nuts and gasket. The 3.7L also requires new converter flange nuts; the 5.0L requires a new compressor-fitting O-ring and gasket; the 5.2L requires replacement strut-brace nuts.

prepare.title: Match workshop capability to the engine
prepare.detail: The 5.0L requires refrigerant recovery and charging equipment and capability. Both V8s require battery disconnection and supported engine lifting. Use a torque wrench and the selected article's tightening instructions.

steps.title: Open the 3.7L exhaust joint
steps.body: Follow the [3.7L removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1681521). Disconnect the right-hand heated oxygen sensor (HO2S) and catalyst monitor sensor connectors. Remove and discard the converter flange nuts, clean the converter-to-manifold sealing surfaces, and remove the coolant-tube bolt from the cylinder head.

steps.title: Create upper access on the 5.0L
steps.body: Follow the [5.0L procedure](#/document/G1685323): recover refrigerant, disconnect both battery cables, and remove the strut brace if fitted, appearance cover and radiator top shield. Disconnect the compressor fitting and discard its seals. Remove the air-cleaner outlet pipe, cowl grille, battery tray, cowl extension and battery heat shield. Disconnect the manual-transmission HO2S connection, then free the camshaft position (CMP) sensor wiring and remove the sensor.

steps.title: Support and clear the 5.0L engine
steps.body: Remove both engine-mount nuts, install the support equipment and raise the engine 50 mm. Place support-bar legs on body structure, never the fenders. Remove the right-hand converter and starter. On the automatic, disconnect the HO2S connector and move the transmission cooling tubes and brackets aside. Release oil-pan wiring retainers, detach the mount-bracket ground strap, and remove the right-hand engine-mount bracket.

steps.title: Create access on the 5.2L
steps.body: Use the [5.2L procedure](#/document/G1800277). Disconnect both battery cables; remove the brace and discard its nuts. Remove the cowl grille, battery tray, compressor belt, cowl extension and heat shield. Disconnect CMP and HO2S wiring, remove the CMP sensor and engine-mount nuts, then remove the underbody shields, right-hand converter and starter. Disconnect the oil-cooler hoses before raising the engine 50 mm with the specified support equipment.

steps.title: Finish 5.2L clearance and remove the manifold
steps.body: On the 5.2L, detach the ground strap, move wiring and any transmission cooler tubes aside, and remove the right-hand mount bracket. Release compressor wiring retainers and position the compressor aside. For every engine, remove the manifold and discard its nuts, gasket and studs. Follow Exhaust Manifold Cleaning and Inspection before deciding whether the manifold is suitable for refitting.

steps.title: Rebuild the manifold joint
steps.body: Install new studs, gasket and nuts using the selected engine's procedure. The 3.7L and 5.0L specify staged nut tightening; the 5.2L requires finger-tight installation followed by tightening in the illustrated sequence. Their tightening instructions are not interchangeable. On the 3.7L, reinstall the coolant-tube bolt, converter with new flange nuts, and both sensor connections.

steps.title: Restore the V8 lower components
steps.body: On the 5.0L, restore the mount bracket, ground strap, wiring and automatic-transmission tube brackets, then the starter and converter. On the 5.2L, reinstall the compressor and retainers, mount bracket, any cooler tubes, wiring, ground strap and oil-cooler hoses; refit the starter, converter and shields. Lower the engine onto its mounts and install the mount nuts in the applicable sequence.

steps.title: Close the V8 engine compartment
steps.body: Restore the CMP sensor, oxygen-sensor connections, harness retainers, heat shield, cowl extension and removed access components. On the 5.0L, reconnect the compressor fitting with new seals and place appearance-cover grommets on the intake manifold before fitting the cover. Restore braces and their wiring retainers, using new brace nuts on the 5.2L. Reconnect battery cables through the battery procedure, then complete the engine-specific finishing checks.

watchFor.title: Uncontrolled engine support
watchFor.body: Do not remove the V8 mount bracket without the specified support arrangement. Support-bar feet on the fenders can damage the body.

watchFor.title: Variant-specific connections
watchFor.body: The 5.0L opens a refrigerant fitting; the 5.2L procedure moves the compressor aside and disconnects oil-cooler hoses. Keep these operations with their respective engine.

notes: Use engine identification information when ordering V8 parts; parts can differ within an engine family.

diagnostics.finding: Leakage is suspected near the manifold.
diagnostics.meaning: The cylinder-head joint and converter joint are separate sealing locations; the complaint alone does not establish that the manifold needs replacement.
diagnostics.next: Identify the affected joint and use the specified manifold cleaning and inspection procedure after removal.

verification.title: 3.7L exhaust check
verification.body: Start the engine and check the exhaust system for leaks. Record the result.

verification.title: 5.0L refrigerant restoration
verification.body: Complete the specified A/C recovery, evacuation and charging procedure after reconnection.

verification.title: 5.2L oil-level check
verification.body: Inspect and adjust engine oil level using Castrol EDGE Supercar 5W-50 meeting WSS-M2C931-C.

guides.title: Replace the 3.7L front-cover coolant-pipe seal
guides.summary: Remove the coolant pump, extract the coolant-pipe seal with the dedicated tool and seat its replacement before refitting the pump.
guides.introduction: This seal closes the joint between the coolant pipe and the engine front cover. On the 3.7L engine, the coolant pump must be removed to reach it. The repair uses a dedicated remover/installer that first extracts the old seal and then supports the replacement as it is driven into position. This is precision sealing work rather than a general pry-out operation.
guides.why: The tool must be engaged and operated in the specified order to release the seal. Correct seating and a damage inspection are equally important during installation. Cleanliness matters throughout: debris entering an oil passage, coolant passage or the oil pan can cause engine failure, including debris produced while cleaning the sealing area.

when.summary: When the front-cover coolant-pipe seal requires replacement during 3.7L engine repair.
notes: Plan the complete coolant-pump removal and installation alongside the seal work.

prepare.title: Dedicated seal tooling
prepare.detail: Have water tube seal remover/installer 303-1528 and a brass hammer. Be able to control the tool’s engagement, extracting screw and installation position.

prepare.title: Pump access and cleanliness
prepare.detail: Follow the linked 3.7L coolant-pump procedure for its preparation, removal and refitting requirements. Arrange cleaning so foreign material cannot enter engine passages or the oil pan.

steps.title: Remove the coolant pump
steps.body: Complete the removal phase of the [3.7L coolant-pump procedure](#/document/G1694559). This provides the access required for the seal tool; the seal replacement sequence begins after the pump has been removed.

steps.title: Engage the removal tool
steps.body: Reset the center bolt of tool 303-1528 to its retracted position. Screw the tool onto the front-cover coolant-pipe seal until it bottoms out. This establishes the tool engagement required before extraction.

steps.title: Release and extract the seal
steps.body: Give the tool a slight inward tap with the brass hammer to loosen the radial seal in the front cover. Then turn the tool’s center bolt clockwise to remove the seal. Follow the illustrated arrangement in the [seal procedure](#/document/G1681523).

steps.title: Clean and install the replacement
steps.body: Clean the front-cover coolant-pipe seal area while keeping debris out of the engine. Position the replacement seal on the special tool, then position the tool into the front cover. Tap the tool with the brass hammer until the seal bottoms out.

steps.title: Inspect before restoring the pump
steps.body: Inspect the installed seal for correct placement and damage before covering the area. Once it is satisfactory, complete the coolant-pump installation using its linked procedure and all associated refitting requirements.

watchFor.title: Contamination from cleaning
watchFor.body: Material removed from the sealing area must not fall into coolant or oil passages or the oil pan.

watchFor.title: Incorrect tool sequence
watchFor.body: Retract the center bolt before threading the tool onto the old seal; the inward release tap precedes turning the extracting screw.

watchFor.title: Damage during seating
watchFor.body: A seal that has bottomed out still requires inspection. Seating depth alone does not establish that it is undamaged.

notes: Use the brass hammer and specified tool for both the release and installation operations.

diagnostics.finding: The installed seal is damaged or incorrectly positioned.
diagnostics.meaning: The required installation inspection has failed.
diagnostics.next: Correct the seal installation before refitting the coolant pump.

verification.title: Record the exposed-seal inspection
verification.body: Confirm and record that the seal is fully seated, correctly installed and free of visible installation damage before the pump is refitted.

verification.title: Complete pump reassembly
verification.body: Confirm the coolant-pump installation and its associated completion requirements have been carried out.

procedures.purpose: 3.7L front-cover coolant-pipe seal extraction, cleaning, installation and inspection using tool 303-1528.
3.7L coolant-pump removal for seal access and installation after the seal inspection.

guides.title: Remove and reseal the 3.7L lower intake manifold
guides.summary: Remove the lower intake manifold with its fuel rail attached, inspect for contamination and reinstall it with new gaskets.
guides.introduction: The 3.7L engine uses composite upper and lower intake manifolds to route incoming air toward the cylinders. The lower assembly also carries the fuel rail and has coolant connections that must be released for removal. This job opens the lower manifold sealing joints while allowing the fuel rail to remain attached to the assembly.
guides.why: Fuel pressure must be released before opening the fuel connection, and coolant must be drained before disturbing its connections. Cleanliness is especially important once the engine is open: material entering oil or coolant passages can cause engine failure. Following valve or piston damage, metal trapped in the intake manifold can damage the repaired engine if the manifold is reused.

when.summary: When the lower manifold needs resealing, replacement or removal during engine repair.
notes: After upper-engine damage, inspect the manifold for metal debris before deciding to reuse it.

prepare.title: Arrange access and fluid-system capability
prepare.detail: Use a hoist with the vehicle in NEUTRAL and follow the specified lifting points. Have the capability to release fuel pressure and drain, vacuum-fill and bleed the 3.7L cooling system.

prepare.title: Prepare for clean assembly
prepare.detail: Have new lower intake manifold gaskets and a suitable torque wrench ready. Plan the cleaning work so loosened material cannot enter the engine's passages.

prepare.title: Keep the fuel rail with the manifold
prepare.detail: The fuel rail does not need to be removed from the lower manifold. Fuel-tube disconnection and injector electrical disconnection are still required.

steps.title: Depressurize and isolate
steps.body: Position the vehicle on the hoist, release fuel-system pressure using the 3.7L procedure, and disconnect the battery ground cable. Drain the cooling system before opening the manifold's coolant connections.

steps.title: Remove the upper access components
steps.body: Remove the upper intake manifold. Disconnect the fuel-tube quick-release coupling through its dedicated procedure, remove the fuel-rail sound insulators, and remove the thermostat housing. These operations free the lower assembly without separating its fuel rail.

steps.title: Lift out the lower manifold
steps.body: Disconnect the fuel-injector electrical connectors and the coolant tube at the back of the lower manifold. Remove the manifold bolts and lift off the assembly following the [complete lower manifold procedure](#/document/G1681524). Remove and discard the lower manifold gaskets.

steps.title: Inspect before closing the engine
steps.body: Clean and inspect all sealing surfaces while keeping debris out of the engine. If this work follows upper-engine failure, particularly valve or piston damage, inspect the manifold for metal debris. Finding metal requires a new intake manifold.

steps.title: Install the manifold and reconnect its services
steps.body: Fit new lower manifold gaskets, install the manifold and tighten its bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). Reconnect the rear coolant tube and injector connectors. Reinstall the thermostat housing and sound insulators, then reconnect the fuel-tube coupling using its specified procedure.

steps.title: Restore the upper assembly and cooling system
steps.body: Reinstall the upper intake manifold and reconnect the battery ground cable. Complete cooling-system filling through the draining, vacuum-filling and bleeding procedure. If a new intake manifold was installed, road test the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Cleaning debris entering the engine
watchFor.body: Material produced while cleaning gasket surfaces is itself a contamination hazard. Keep it out of oil passages, coolant passages and the oil pan.

watchFor.title: Metal following engine damage
watchFor.body: Do not treat manifold cleaning as an alternative to replacement when metal debris is found after upper-engine failure.

notes: The lower manifold gaskets are discarded during removal; this procedure does not authorize their reuse.

diagnostics.finding: Metal debris is present in the intake manifold after valve or piston damage.
diagnostics.meaning: The manifold can carry damaging material into the repaired engine.
diagnostics.next: Install a new intake manifold and carry out the required road test after assembly.

verification.title: Complete fluid restoration
verification.body: Finish the specified cooling-system filling and bleeding operation after all coolant connections and the upper manifold are installed.

verification.title: Record the replacement decision and result
verification.body: Record the debris inspection finding and whether the manifold was renewed. When a new manifold was fitted, record the required road-test result.

guides.title: Remove and refit the 3.7L upper intake manifold
guides.summary: Remove the 3.7L upper intake manifold, inspect it and its sealing surfaces, and reinstall it with new gaskets and the specified staged tightening.
guides.introduction: The 3.7L Duratec uses composite upper and lower intake manifolds to carry incoming air toward the cylinders. The upper section connects to the throttle body and several hoses, tubes and electrical components. This job separates that section from the lower manifold for repair or access, then restores its seals and connections.
guides.why: The joint must seal correctly after separation, so the removed gaskets are discarded. Inspection is especially important after valve or piston damage: metal trapped in the intake manifold can enter the repaired engine and cause further damage. Finding debris requires manifold replacement.

when.summary: When upper-intake removal is needed for repair or access, or debris is found after upper-engine failure.
notes: Inspect the manifold for metal debris when the engine is repaired or replaced following upper-engine failure.

prepare.title: Have the connection procedures ready
prepare.detail: Use the 3.7L air-cleaner-outlet-pipe procedure for access and the specified quick-release-coupling procedure for the evaporative-emissions (EVAP) purge connection.

prepare.title: Prepare the replacement seals and tightening equipment
prepare.detail: Have new upper-manifold gaskets available before dismantling. Installation requires both a torque stage and an additional angle stage for the manifold bolts.

prepare.title: Workshop capability
prepare.detail: Hose clamp remover/installer; suitable hand tools; torque wrench and angle-tightening capability; new upper intake manifold gaskets.

steps.title: Clear the air pipe and vacuum hose
steps.body: Remove the air cleaner outlet pipe. Disconnect the vacuum hose from the upper manifold with the hose clamp tool, then detach its retainers from the throttle body and manifold. This frees the hose from the assembly being lifted.

steps.title: Release the purge connection
steps.body: Disconnect the EVAP purge-valve electrical connector and detach its wiring retainers. Release the purge quick-release coupling using the linked coupling procedure so its locking arrangement is handled correctly.

steps.title: Free the remaining tubes, wiring and support
steps.body: Disconnect and move aside the positive crankcase ventilation (PCV) tube. Disconnect the throttle-body and manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor connectors, release the wiring retainers and remove the upper-manifold support bolt.

steps.title: Remove the manifold and inspect the joint
steps.body: Remove the manifold bolts and lift off the upper manifold. Remove and discard its gaskets, then clean and inspect the upper- and lower-manifold sealing surfaces. If the work follows upper-engine failure, check for metal debris and replace the manifold if any is found.

steps.title: Fit new gaskets and secure the manifold
steps.body: Install new gaskets, position the upper manifold and install its bolts. Tighten the manifold bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm), then through an additional 45°. Install the support bolt and tighten it to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). The support bolt does not receive the manifold bolts' additional angle stage.

steps.title: Restore the electrical and tube connections
steps.body: Attach the wiring retainers and reconnect the throttle body and MAP sensor. Reconnect the PCV tube, the EVAP quick-release coupling, its wiring retainers and the purge-valve connector.

steps.title: Restore the vacuum hose and air pipe
steps.body: Reconnect the vacuum hose with the hose clamp tool and attach its retainers to the throttle body and upper manifold. Reinstall the air cleaner outlet pipe through its dedicated procedure.

watchFor.title: A manifold still held by a connection
watchFor.body: Finish releasing the specified hoses, wiring retainers and support bolt before lifting the manifold.

watchFor.title: Debris after engine damage
watchFor.body: Do not reuse a manifold containing metal debris after upper-engine failure; the procedure requires replacement.

notes: These installation details apply to the 3.7L upper intake manifold.
New gaskets are required even when the original manifold is being refitted.

diagnostics.finding: Metal debris is found in the manifold following valve, piston or other upper-engine damage.
diagnostics.meaning: The intake can retain material capable of damaging the repaired or replacement engine.
diagnostics.next: Install a new intake manifold.

verification.title: Check the restored connections
verification.body: Confirm the support bolt, electrical connectors, quick-release coupling, PCV tube, vacuum hose, retainers and air cleaner outlet pipe have all been restored.

verification.title: Complete the required road test
verification.body: If a new intake manifold was installed, road test the vehicle and record the outcome, including any remaining concern.

guides.title: Reseal the left valve cover on 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Remove the left valve cover, renew its gasket and any damaged passage seals, then restore the engine-specific connections.
guides.introduction: The left-hand (LH) valve cover contains oil around the valve gear. Separate seals close the openings around the spark plug tubes and variable camshaft timing (VCT) solenoids. Removing the cover allows gasket renewal and inspection of these seals. The sealing work is similar across these engines, but the V8 access route also involves fuel connections and battery isolation.
guides.why: A new gasket needs clean mating surfaces and correctly sealed front-cover joints. Cleaning debris entering the engine can cause serious damage, while a displaced solenoid seal can create another oil leak. Prepare the installation before applying silicone because the permitted assembly time differs by engine.

when.summary: When the LH cover needs removal or its gasket or passage seals require repair.
notes: Establish the leak location before choosing which sealing joint to repair.

prepare.title: Arrange parts and seal tools
prepare.detail: Have a new cover gasket, Motorcraft TA-357 silicone and tools 205-153, 205-142 and 303-1247 for any damaged seals. The 5.2L also requires new strut-brace nuts.

prepare.title: Prepare for clean, controlled work
prepare.detail: Use torque-controlled tools and the sealing-surface cleaning procedure. The 3.7L specifies a plastic scraper, gasket remover, brake-parts cleaner and metal preparation wipes. V8 work requires fuel-pressure release and battery-disconnection capability.

steps.title: Clear the 3.7L cover
steps.body: Following the [3.7L procedure](#/document/G1681530), remove the crankcase vent tube and oil level indicator. Release the fuel-supply and evaporative-emissions (EVAP) tube retainer, then remove the LH ignition coils. Disconnect the oil-pressure switch and VCT solenoids and release their harness retainers so wiring cannot hold the cover down.

steps.title: Clear the V8 cover
steps.body: Use the [5.0L](#/document/G1685331) or [5.2L](#/document/G1800284) route. Release fuel pressure, then disconnect both battery cables. Remove the brace where fitted; discard its nuts on 5.2L. Remove the air cleaner, cowl grille and extension. The 5.0L additionally requires appearance-cover and air-cleaner outlet-pipe removal, followed by moving the sound-enhancement pipe aside. Release the EVAP coupling and retainers, move the fuel safety clip and remove the fuel tube through its quick-release couplings. Remove the coils, disconnect VCT wiring, then remove the dipstick and unlock its tube by pressing the tab and rotating counterclockwise.

steps.title: Lift the cover and inspect its seals
steps.body: Loosen the cover bolts, remove the cover and discard its gasket. On 3.7L, gently wiggle the cover if a solenoid adheres to its seal; excessive force can damage both. Inspect the solenoid and spark plug tube seals. Remove only damaged seals with the specified tools.

steps.title: Prepare the sealing surfaces
steps.body: Follow [RTV sealing-surface preparation](#/document/G1692003), keeping debris out of the engine. RTV means room-temperature-vulcanizing silicone. On the V8 covers, clean the gasket groove with soap and water or a suitable solvent. Install replacements for damaged seals using the corresponding removal and installation tools.

steps.title: Fit the gasket and seal the front joints
steps.body: Apply an 8 mm bead of TA-357 at the engine-front-cover-to-cylinder-head joints. On 3.7L, apply silicone before fitting the new gasket; on the V8s, fit the gasket first. Install the cover and tighten its bolts to 10 Nm within 4 minutes on 3.7L or 5 minutes on either V8. If that window is missed, remove the sealant and clean the sealing area before restarting.

steps.title: Restore the engine-specific connections
steps.body: On 3.7L, check solenoid-seal height, then restore wiring, coils, tube retainers, dipstick and vent tube. On the V8s, push the dipstick tube home, rotate clockwise and confirm its tab locks. Restore wiring, coils, fuel couplings and safety clip, EVAP fittings and removed access parts in the installation order. Refit 5.0L appearance-cover grommets to the intake manifold first. Use new 5.2L brace nuts and reconnect the battery last.

watchFor.title: Raised 3.7L solenoid seals
watchFor.body: The seals must sit below the tops of the solenoid electrical connectors; incorrect seating can leak oil.

watchFor.title: Sealant installation delay
watchFor.body: The time limit includes tightening the cover, not merely placing it on the engine.

notes: Removing the cover does not automatically require replacement of undamaged spark plug tube or VCT seals.

diagnostics.finding: A plug-tube or VCT seal is damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: That passage seal requires renewal in addition to the discarded perimeter gasket.
diagnostics.next: Replace it with the specified tool before installing the cover.

verification.title: Confirm seating and reconnection
verification.body: Check 3.7L solenoid-seal height, V8 dipstick-tube locking, fuel safety-clip installation and harness retention as applicable.

verification.title: Record the sealing work
verification.body: Record the engine variant, seals renewed, cover torque and completion within the applicable sealant window.

guides.title: Reseal the right valve cover on 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Renew the right valve-cover gasket and damaged passage seals while following the heater-tube or battery-area access route for the engine.
guides.introduction: The right-hand (RH) valve cover keeps lubricating oil around the valve gear while sealing around the spark plug tubes and variable camshaft timing (VCT) solenoids. This repair removes the cover, replaces its perimeter gasket and addresses damaged passage seals. On 3.7L, the heater-tube attachment must be released; on the V8s, access extends into the battery tray and cowl area.
guides.why: Successful resealing depends on protecting the exposed engine from debris and preserving the small seals around components passing through the cover. The front-cover-to-head joints need a measured silicone application, followed promptly by cover installation and tightening.

when.summary: When the RH valve cover needs removal or its gasket or passage seals require repair.
notes: Identify the leaking joint before deciding which seal needs attention.

prepare.title: Gather the sealing equipment
prepare.detail: Have a new cover gasket, Motorcraft TA-357 silicone and torque-controlled tools. Damaged solenoid seals use tool 205-142 with handle 205-153; spark plug tube seals use 303-1247 with that handle.

prepare.title: Plan access and replacement parts
prepare.detail: V8 access requires battery disconnection and battery-tray removal. Obtain new strut-brace nuts for 5.2L. Prepare a clean working area and follow the sealing-surface preparation procedure.

steps.title: Release the 3.7L attachments
steps.body: Follow the [3.7L RH procedure](#/document/G1681531). Remove the RH ignition coils and positive crankcase ventilation (PCV) tube. Disconnect the VCT solenoids and release the harness retainers. Remove the heater-tube bolt and detach its retainer from the valve-cover stud so the tube attachment does not restrain the cover.

steps.title: Open the V8 access route
steps.body: Follow the [5.0L](#/document/G1685332) or [5.2L](#/document/G1800285) procedure. Disconnect both battery cables. Release the brace harness retainer and remove the brace where fitted; discard the nuts on 5.2L. Remove the 5.0L appearance cover. On both V8s, remove the cowl grille, battery tray, cowl extension and battery heat shield, then the RH coils. Disconnect VCT wiring and release its retainers.

steps.title: Remove the cover without loading the solenoids
steps.body: Loosen the cover bolts and lift the cover away. On 3.7L, if a solenoid sticks to its seal, carefully wiggle the cover until the bond releases. Excessive force can damage the solenoid and seal. Discard the perimeter gasket and inspect the solenoid and spark plug tube seals.

steps.title: Prepare the cover and renew damaged seals
steps.body: Remove damaged passage seals with the specified tools and install their replacements. Undamaged seals do not require renewal. Clean the V8 gasket groove with soap and water or a suitable solvent. Follow [RTV surface preparation](#/document/G1692003) for the mating surfaces; RTV is room-temperature-vulcanizing silicone. Keep cleaning residue out of oil and coolant passages.

steps.title: Seal the front joints and fit the cover
steps.body: Use an 8 mm bead of TA-357 at the engine-front-cover-to-cylinder-head joints. On 3.7L, apply it before installing the new gasket; on either V8, install the gasket first. Fit the cover and tighten its bolts to 10 Nm. Complete fitting and tightening within 4 minutes on 3.7L or 5 minutes on the V8s. If time expires, remove the sealant and clean the area before repeating.

steps.title: Restore the released attachments
steps.body: On 3.7L, confirm solenoid-seal height, refit the heater-tube retainer and bolt, reconnect the harness and solenoids, then install the PCV tube and coils. On the V8s, restore wiring and coils, heat shield, cowl extension, battery tray and grille. Put the 5.0L appearance-cover grommets on the intake manifold before refitting the cover. Refit the brace with new nuts on 5.2L and reconnect the battery.

watchFor.title: Incorrect 3.7L seal height
watchFor.body: The VCT seals must sit below the tops of the solenoid electrical connectors to avoid oil leakage.

watchFor.title: Debris at an open engine
watchFor.body: Cleaning material entering the oil passages, coolant passages or oil pan can cause engine failure.

notes: Use the engine-specific installation instructions for heater-tube, heat-shield, cowl and brace fastener torques.

diagnostics.finding: A passage seal is damaged during inspection.
diagnostics.meaning: Renewing the perimeter gasket alone will leave that damaged seal in service.
diagnostics.next: Replace the affected seal before refitting the cover.

verification.title: Check the restored attachments
verification.body: Verify 3.7L VCT-seal seating and heater-tube retention, or V8 battery-area reassembly, together with coil and solenoid connections.

verification.title: Record the repair
verification.body: Record which seals were replaced and confirm the cover reached its specified torque within the engine's sealant window.

guides.title: Overhaul the 5.0L V8 engine
guides.summary: Remove, dismantle, measure, rebuild and reinstall the 5.0L engine, preserving its bearing selection, valve timing and transmission-specific requirements.
guides.introduction: The 5.0L V8 uses overhead camshafts with twin independent variable camshaft timing to control its valves. A crankshaft-driven oil pump supplies the bearings and lubrication system. An overhaul brings these assemblies apart for inspection and restores their fit, sealing and timing before the engine returns to the vehicle. This is specialist work involving engine lifting, precision measurement and staged torque-and-angle tightening.
guides.why: Bearing grades establish the crankshaft’s running clearance, while chain alignment establishes the relationship between pistons and valves. Incorrect selection or timing can cause serious damage. Clean passages, correctly matched components and carefully timed sealant application matter just as much as replacing worn parts.

when.summary: When established internal damage or measured wear requires engine removal and comprehensive rebuilding.
notes: Verify engine identification before ordering parts; revisions within the engine family can affect parts selection.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and precision equipment
prepare.detail: Provide a vehicle hoist, floor crane, engine stand, lifting bracket 303-F047 and support bar 303-F072. The work also needs crankshaft holding and seal tools, a three-leg puller, piston ring compressor, clearance-measuring equipment and torque-and-angle tools. Have an assistant available for engine installation and a diagnostic scan tool for final correction.

prepare.title: Plan replacement parts
prepare.detail: Renew discarded main-cap fasteners, connecting-rod bolts, head bolts, variable camshaft timing bolts, pulley bolt, crankshaft seals, timing oil filters, oil cooler, oil-pan baffle/gasket, specified O-rings and gaskets, and removed exhaust studs/nuts. Include a new steering shaft bolt and the applicable flywheel, flexplate, clutch pressure-plate or torque-converter fasteners.

prepare.title: Organize the bench
prepare.detail: Keep reusable caps, bearings, followers and adjusters identified by original position. Arrange clean storage and the specified sealing materials before assembly. Obtain the 5.0L specifications and piston subassembly procedure before making reuse decisions.

steps.title: Make the vehicle safe and open access
steps.body: Follow [engine removal](#/document/G1685335): place the vehicle in neutral on the hoist, release fuel pressure, disconnect both battery cables and drain coolant. Loosen the steering dash seal and hold the steering wheel straight ahead. Mark the hood position, then complete the listed intake, cooling, battery-tray and cowl access operations.

steps.title: Disconnect the underside and transmission interfaces
steps.body: Drain the oil, discard the filter and disconnect the cooler hoses, wiring and exhaust connections. Separate the steering shaft without hammering or prying; discard its bolt and secure the shaft. Follow the automatic branch for transmission wiring, cooling-tube brackets and discarded converter nuts, or the manual branch for the rear cover fasteners.

steps.title: Support and extract the engine
steps.body: Place support-bar feet on body structure, never the fenders. Raise the engine as directed, remove the mount brackets and left catalytic converter, and position the air-conditioning compressor aside. Transfer support to the crane; support the transmission at its bellhousing with the jack and wooden block, never its pan. Separate and lift the engine. Remove the applicable flexplate or clutch/flywheel assembly, marking a reusable pressure plate and discarding specified fasteners.

steps.title: Dismantle the upper engine in sequence
steps.body: Use [bench disassembly](#/document/G1685337). Remove the rear seal before mounting the engine on its stand, then strip wiring, covers and accessories. Remove right-hand timing components at the specified crankshaft position, followed by the left-hand components. Remove each front camshaft mega cap before the remaining caps. Keep reusable valve-train parts indexed. Remove the heads only when cool, and always before removing the crankshaft.

steps.title: Inspect the heads and dismantle the bottom end
steps.body: Check head and block mating surfaces for distortion. Protect exposed cavities and avoid scratching aluminum gasket faces. Remove the sump, pickup, pump and rear seal retainer. Inspect bore tops and perform the prescribed ridge/carbon preparation before withdrawing pistons upward. Preserve rod/cap orientation, then remove the main caps, crankshaft and cooling jets. Follow the separate piston procedure for subassembly work.

steps.title: Select bearings and build the rotating assembly
steps.body: Begin [engine assembly](#/document/G1685342) by recording block and crankshaft bearing codes. Use the chart for mains 1 and 5 separately from the chart for mains 2, 3 and 4; each result identifies upper/lower grades. Align oil passages and lubricate bearings. Install the thrust washer with its groove rearward and seat it as directed. Check end play and turning torque. Verify piston/ring clearances, then install pistons without contacting cooling jets or scratching journals. Refit matching cracked rod caps with new bolts.

steps.title: Restore lubrication and install the heads
steps.body: Prime the oil pump with 2 tablespoons of clean engine oil and rotate it by hand before installation. Follow the individual sealing and tightening sequences for the rear retainer, baffle, pickup and pan. Install the new oil cooler. Seat the crankshaft position sensor correctly and flush before bolting it down. Fit new head gaskets and head bolts using the complete staged tightening instructions.

steps.title: Time the left bank before the right bank
steps.body: Start left-hand assembly with the crankshaft keyway at 5 o’clock. Follow the illustrated camshaft positions and colored-link alignment, using new timing oil filters and timing-unit bolts. Release the installed tensioner’s holding pin. Rotate clockwise one complete revolution, then continue clockwise to the 12 o’clock keyway position before right-hand assembly. Follow only the instructed crankshaft movements; temporary guide/arm adjustments must return to the specified position.

steps.title: Close and dress the engine
steps.body: Fully depress the variable camshaft timing solenoid pins before installing the front cover. Follow each joint’s sealant deadline, fit new front and rear crankshaft seals with the specified installers, and install the pulley with a new bolt and original washer. Restore accessories, covers, coils, sensors, grounds and harness retainers. Confirm the oil-level tube locks in place. The rear seal is installed after lifting the engine off its stand.

steps.title: Refit the engine using the correct transmission branch
steps.body: Follow [engine installation](#/document/G1685344). For MT82, align the clutch with its tool, retain pressure-plate indexing or align new-part paint dots, and lubricate the input shaft. For 6R80, lubricate the converter pilot and align its marked relationship to the flexplate. Restore mounts, exhaust, steering, wiring and hoses; use the new steering bolt and perform the collapsed-column check. Install the new oil filter without lubricating its seal, fill engine oil, reconnect the battery, then fill and bleed cooling.

watchFor.title: Sealant deadlines differ
watchFor.body: The rear retainer has a 4-minute securing limit. Pan and front-cover work have 5-minute limits with specifically defined staged alternatives requiring final tightening within 1 hour. Pulley and valve-cover sealing also have 5-minute limits. Follow the exact fastener instructions; exceeded limits require removing sealant and cleaning.

watchFor.title: Protect sealing faces and friction-component handling
watchFor.body: Do not use metal scrapers, wire brushes or abrasive discs on head/block gasket faces. Do not breathe clutch dust or disperse it with compressed air; use the prescribed approved dust-removal methods.

notes: Replace spark-plug tube and variable camshaft timing solenoid seals only when damaged seals were removed.
Use this engine’s timing sequence exactly; an earlier engine’s alignment method is not interchangeable.

diagnostics.finding: Crankshaft turning torque exceeds 6 Nm (53 lb-in), or a measured clearance fails the 5.0L specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The rotating assembly has not met its assembly checks.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the fit or assembly problem before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: A lash adjuster or roller follower is damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: Associated camshaft lobes and valves also require inspection.
diagnostics.next: Inspect those components and replace damaged parts.

diagnostics.finding: The crankshaft sensor ring was dropped or has visible damage.
diagnostics.meaning: It cannot be reused under the removal procedure.
diagnostics.next: Install a replacement sensor ring.

verification.title: Record internal assembly results
verification.body: Record bearing codes and selected grades, bearing-clearance checks, crankshaft end play and turning torque, piston/ring clearances, and head/block inspection results against the applicable specifications.

verification.title: Complete installed-engine checks
verification.body: Confirm the steering-column inspection, fluid filling and cooling-system bleeding are complete. Perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction with a diagnostic scan tool, then road test the vehicle.

guides.title: Strip and reassemble a 5.0L cylinder head
guides.summary: Disassemble and rebuild the valves, springs, seals and head-mounted fittings of a prepared 5.0L cylinder head.
guides.introduction: The 5.0L V8 uses aluminum cylinder heads with intake and exhaust valves operated by overhead camshafts. Valve springs close the valves, while retainers and keys hold each spring assembly together. Valve-stem seals control oil at the guides. This bench operation services those parts and the head-mounted coolant outlets and sensors, with different fitting sequences for the left-hand and right-hand heads.
guides.why: Cleanliness is critical: debris entering oil passages, coolant passages or the oil pan can cause engine failure. Reused components must return to their original positions. Controlled spring compression is essential to removing and installing the retaining keys, and all specified discarded seals and sensors must be renewed.
searchTerms: left and right cylinder head assembly

when.summary: When a removed 5.0L cylinder head requires valve, valve-stem-seal or head-fitting service.
notes: Begin with the head prepared for bench disassembly. Vehicle removal, camshaft and timing work, and engine refitting are separate phases.

prepare.title: Arrange the spring-compressor equipment
prepare.detail: Use the specified compressor components: 303-300, 303-350, 303-1249 and 303-1418. This work requires the capability to control spring load and handle the small retaining keys.

prepare.title: Prepare a clean, organized bench
prepare.detail: Provide marked storage for components by original location, clean engine oil, and torque tools suitable for the listed fasteners. Keep cleaning debris away from all internal passages.

prepare.title: Gather the required new parts
prepare.detail: Have new valve-stem seals for either head, a new coolant-outlet gasket for the left head, and a new cylinder head temperature sensor and coolant-outlet O-ring for the right head. The outlet O-ring uses clean Motorcraft Orange coolant, VC-3-B, specification WSS-M97B44-D.

steps.title: Identify the head and mark reusable parts
steps.body: Establish whether the head is left-hand or right-hand before stripping its fittings. Mark components so anything reused returns to its original location. Keep this organization through both disassembly and assembly.

steps.title: Strip the left-hand head fittings
steps.body: For the left-hand head, remove the coolant-outlet bolts and outlet, then discard its gasket. Remove the bolts, camshaft position (CMP) sensors and radio interference capacitor.

steps.title: Strip the right-hand head fittings
steps.body: For the right-hand head, remove the CMP sensor and its bolt. Remove and discard the cylinder head temperature (CHT) sensor. Remove the coolant-outlet bolt and outlet, and discard the O-ring.

steps.title: Remove the plugs and valve assemblies
steps.body: On either head, remove the spark plugs. Use the specified compressor equipment to remove each valve's keys, retainer and spring. Remove and discard the valve-stem seal, then withdraw the valve. Repeat for the remaining valves while preserving their locations.

steps.title: Install new seals and return the valves
steps.body: Lubricate each new valve-stem seal and valve-guide bore with clean engine oil. Install the new seal, then install the valve into the head. Return reused valves to their original positions.

steps.title: Rebuild the spring assemblies
steps.body: Using the specified compressor equipment, install each spring, retainer and set of keys. Repeat for all remaining valves. Install the spark plugs and tighten them to 15 Nm.

steps.title: Restore the right-hand head fittings
steps.body: Install a new CHT sensor and tighten it to 11 Nm. Install the CMP sensor and bolt at 10 Nm. Lubricate a new coolant-outlet O-ring with the specified clean coolant, install the outlet pipe, and tighten its fastener to 10 Nm.

steps.title: Restore the left-hand head fittings
steps.body: Install the coolant outlet with a new gasket and tighten its bolts to 10 Nm. Refit the CMP sensors, radio interference capacitor and bolts, also tightening to 10 Nm.

watchFor.title: Uncontrolled spring load
watchFor.body: Keep the spring controlled by the specified compressor while removing or installing its keys. Do not improvise around an inadequately supported spring.

watchFor.title: Mixed locations or reused discard parts
watchFor.body: Maintain component identification throughout the work. Renew every removed valve-stem seal and the head-specific discarded gasket, O-ring or CHT sensor.

notes: Use the engine identification information when selecting replacement parts; revisions can differ within the same engine family.

diagnostics.finding: Foreign material enters an oil or coolant passage during stripping or cleaning.
diagnostics.meaning: Contamination can cause engine failure after reassembly.
diagnostics.next: Restore cleanliness before continuing and prevent further debris from entering the passages.

verification.title: Account for every valve assembly
verification.body: Confirm that each valve has its new seal, spring, retainer and keys installed, and that reused components occupy their original locations.

verification.title: Record the completed head assembly
verification.body: Record the head side, required new parts and completed tightening checks for spark plugs, sensors and coolant outlet before the head proceeds to engine assembly.

procedures.purpose: 5.0L cylinder-head bench disassembly and assembly, including common valve work and separate left/right fitting sequences.

guides.title: Service the left-hand camshafts on the 5.0L and 5.2L V8
guides.summary: Remove and inspect the left-hand camshafts, followers and lash adjusters, then restore their positions with new variable-timing oil filters.
guides.introduction: The left-hand cylinder bank has separate intake and exhaust camshafts. Their lobes act through roller followers, while hydraulic lash adjusters take up valve-train clearance. Variable camshaft timing (VCT) changes valve timing to suit operating conditions. This job removes those camshafts and their associated followers and adjusters for inspection or replacement.
guides.why: The front bearing mega cap must come off before the other bearing caps to avoid engine damage. Reused components must return to their original positions, and the camshafts must be aligned as illustrated before fastening. Cleanliness protects the oil passages that serve the engine and its hydraulic components.

when.summary: When confirmed camshaft or valve-train damage, or another engine repair, requires left-bank camshaft removal.
notes: If both banks are being serviced, remove the right-hand camshafts first.
Early-build 5.2L engines do not have spring clips on the roller followers.

prepare.title: Plan the complete timing work
prepare.detail: Have the VCT-unit removal and installation procedure for the actual engine and the capability to complete its prerequisites. Provide suitable torque-and-angle tools and a clean way to retain each component's original position.

prepare.title: Gather new filters and assembly oil
prepare.detail: Obtain new VCT system oil filters. The 5.0L procedure calls for clean engine oil; the 5.2L specifies SAE 5W-50 oil meeting WSS-M2C931-E1 for the listed assembly lubrication.

steps.title: Remove the left-hand timing units
steps.body: Follow the [5.0L VCT-unit procedure](#/document/G1685333) or [5.2L VCT-unit procedure](#/document/G1800286). If both banks are involved, complete right-hand camshaft removal first. Remove and discard the VCT system oil filters.

steps.title: Release the bearing caps in the required order
steps.body: Remove the bolts and front camshaft bearing mega cap first. Then remove the remaining bearing caps and bolts, followed by the intake and exhaust camshafts. Preserve the original locations of all components that may be reused.

steps.title: Remove and inspect followers and adjusters
steps.body: Remove the roller followers and hydraulic lash adjusters. Where spring clips are fitted, separate the adjusters from those clips. Inspect the followers and adjusters for damage; any damage requires inspection of the associated camshaft lobes and valves as well.

steps.title: Reassemble and lubricate the valve-train parts
steps.body: Replace damaged components as necessary. Attach adjusters to follower spring clips where fitted, lubricate with the appropriate clean engine oil and reinstall the components. Return every reused component to its original location; follow the clip-free arrangement on early 5.2L engines.

steps.title: Position the camshafts accurately
steps.body: Lubricate the 5.0L camshafts before installation, or the journals and lobes specifically identified for the 5.2L. Install the intake and exhaust camshafts with their D-slots aligned exactly as shown in the selected engine procedure. The 5.0L instruction identifies this as the neutral position.

steps.title: Fit all caps before tightening
steps.body: Install the bearing caps and bolts without tightening, then install the front mega cap and its bolts, also loose. Only after all are positioned should the bolts be tightened through the stages in the applicable camshaft procedure.

steps.title: Restore the VCT system
steps.body: Install new VCT system oil filters into the camshafts. Reinstall the left-hand VCT units through the matching engine procedure, completing its timing and reassembly requirements before road testing.

watchFor.title: Clip-free 5.2L hardware
watchFor.body: Do not assume an early 5.2L follower is missing a part merely because it has no spring clip. Identify the actual arrangement before separating or assembling components.

watchFor.title: Contamination during open-engine work
watchFor.body: Keep cleaning debris and other foreign material out of oil passages, coolant passages and the oil pan; contamination can cause engine failure.

notes: Use each engine’s own D-slot illustration for camshaft positioning.

diagnostics.finding: A hydraulic lash adjuster or roller follower is damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: The inspection must extend to the contacting camshaft lobes and valves.
diagnostics.next: Inspect those related parts and replace damaged components as necessary before reassembly.

verification.title: Confirm the assembly requirements
verification.body: Confirm reused parts returned to their original positions, the camshafts were aligned using the correct illustration, all cap-tightening stages were completed and new VCT oil filters were installed.

verification.title: Road test and record the result
verification.body: Road test the vehicle after completing the VCT-unit installation. Record the damaged parts found, components renewed and road-test outcome.

5.2L left-hand camshaft removal and installation, including early-build follower differences and specified lubrication.

guides.title: Remove and install the right-hand camshafts on 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Service the right-hand intake and exhaust camshafts while preserving component positions, bearing-cap order and engine-specific timing requirements.
guides.introduction: The right-hand cylinder head contains intake and exhaust camshafts whose lobes operate the valves through roller followers supported by hydraulic lash adjusters. The adjusters maintain the working relationship between these moving parts. Variable camshaft timing, or VCT, changes valve timing through units attached to the camshafts. This repair removes those units first, then exposes the camshafts and their supporting valve-train components.
guides.why: Clean oil passages and correctly assembled bearing supports are essential to engine survival. Debris introduced during repair can cause engine failure. The front bearing mega cap must come off before the other caps, reusable parts must return to their original positions, and the camshaft D-slots must match the engine-specific alignment illustration.

when.summary: When confirmed camshaft or related valve-train damage requires repair, or associated engine work requires camshaft removal.
notes: Use the engine identification information to select parts and the matching timing procedure.

prepare.title: Arrange internal-engine and timing capability
prepare.detail: Have the capability and equipment required by the matching VCT unit procedure before beginning. Its timing prerequisites remain part of this repair.

prepare.title: Organize a clean working area
prepare.detail: Keep removed caps, camshafts, followers and lash adjusters associated with their original locations. Prevent foreign material from entering oil passages, coolant passages or the oil pan.

prepare.title: Prepare lubrication and replacement parts
prepare.detail: Have clean engine oil and new VCT system oil filters for the 5.0L. The 5.2L specifies Motorcraft SAE 5W-50 Full Synthetic Motor Oil, XO-5W50-QGT, meeting WSS-M2C931-E1.

steps.title: Remove the right-hand timing units
steps.body: Complete the [5.0L VCT procedure](#/document/G1685333) or [5.2L VCT procedure](#/document/G1800286) through removal before working on the bearing caps. Remove the VCT oil filters from the camshafts; discard them on the 5.0L.

steps.title: Release the camshaft bearing supports
steps.body: Follow the [5.0L camshaft procedure](#/document/G1685314) or [5.2L camshaft procedure](#/document/G1800267). Remove the front mega-cap bolts and mega cap first, then the remaining bearing-cap bolts and caps. Remove the intake and exhaust camshafts.

steps.title: Remove and inspect the followers and adjusters
steps.body: Remove the roller followers and hydraulic lash adjusters. Separate adjusters from the follower spring clips where fitted. Early-build 5.2L engines do not have these clips. Inspect the followers and adjusters; damage requires inspection of the camshaft lobes and valves as well.

steps.title: Reassemble and lubricate the valve-train parts
steps.body: Replace damaged components as necessary. Assemble the adjusters onto the follower spring clips where fitted, lubricate with clean engine oil and reinstall. Return reusable components to their original positions, using the specified oil for the 5.2L.

steps.title: Position the camshafts
steps.body: Lubricate the camshafts before installation; the 5.2L specifically identifies the journals and lobes. Install the intake and exhaust camshafts with the D-slots aligned exactly as illustrated in the selected procedure. The 5.0L instruction identifies this as the neutral position.

steps.title: Install and tighten the bearing caps
steps.body: Install the individual bearing caps and bolts without tightening, then install the front mega cap and its bolts without tightening. Only then carry out the engine's specified staged tightening instructions. Do not tighten caps as each is placed.

steps.title: Restore the timing assemblies
steps.body: Install the VCT oil filters, using new filters on the 5.0L. Reinstall the right-hand VCT units through the matching timing procedure, completing its required operations before returning the vehicle to service.

watchFor.title: Mixed component locations
watchFor.body: Reusable parts must retain their original locations throughout removal, inspection and installation.

watchFor.title: Damage beyond the first failed part
watchFor.body: A damaged follower or adjuster calls for inspecting the associated camshaft lobes and valves before deciding the repair scope.

notes: The absence of follower spring clips on an early-build 5.2L is a documented construction difference.

diagnostics.finding: Damage to a hydraulic lash adjuster or roller follower
diagnostics.meaning: The repair may involve more than the initially removed component.
diagnostics.next: Inspect camshaft lobes and valves, then replace damaged parts as necessary.

verification.title: Complete the road test
verification.body: Both engine procedures finish with a road test after camshaft and VCT installation.

verification.title: Record the repair and result
verification.body: Record the damage found, parts replaced and road-test result against the original repair concern.

guides.title: Replace the 5.0L or 5.2L crankshaft rear seal and service its retainer
guides.summary: Renew the rear crankshaft sealing arrangement using the correct engine-specific retainer, sensor and seal-installation sequence.
guides.introduction: The rear crankshaft seal retains engine oil where the rotating crankshaft exits the back of the engine. Its retainer plate forms a separate sealed joint with the block, and the crankshaft position sensor sits nearby. This repair reaches the area behind the flywheel or flexplate. The 5.0L and 5.2L paths differ significantly: the 5.0L requires oil-pan removal, while the 5.2L procedure replaces the retainer plate and sensor and releases the pan-to-retainer attachments.
guides.why: A new seal cannot compensate for a poorly sealed retainer joint. Clean surfaces, the prescribed sealant working time and the proper installer all matter. The crankshaft sensor ring also needs careful handling: dropping it requires replacement even when damage is not obvious. The 5.2L adds a unique seal orientation and a separate sensor-bonding process.
searchTerms: 5.2L rear seal retainer and crankshaft sensor

when.summary: When repair of the rear crankshaft seal or retainer sealing joint is required.
notes: Oil near the engine-to-transmission joint should be traced before committing to this extensive access work.

prepare.title: Plan the access work
prepare.detail: Provide the capability and equipment required by the applicable flywheel or flexplate procedure. The 5.0L also requires its oil-pan removal and installation procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare tools and materials
prepare.detail: Both engines use seal installer 303-1250 and handle 205-153. The 5.0L additionally uses remover 303-519 with slide hammer 100-001. Have the specified Motorcraft TA-357 silicone; the 5.2L also requires Loctite 7649 Primer, Loctite 638 Sealer, a replacement retainer and replacement crankshaft position sensor.

steps.title: Expose and inspect the rear components
steps.body: Remove the 5.0L flexplate or flywheel, or the 5.2L flywheel, using the matching procedure. Remove the crankshaft sensor ring and engine-to-transmission spacer plate. Inspect the ring and discard it if dropped or visibly damaged.

steps.title: Follow the correct removal branch
steps.body: For the [5.0L](#/document/G1685317), extract and discard the seal with the specified remover and slide hammer, disconnect and remove the crankshaft position (CKP) sensor, remove the oil pan, then remove the retainer. For the [5.2L](#/document/G1800270), disconnect the sensor, remove the pan-to-retainer bolts, loosen the sensor bolt and remove the retainer bolts. Discard the retainer plate and CKP sensor.

steps.title: Prepare and seal the retainer joint
steps.body: Follow the [RTV surface-cleaning procedure](#/document/G1692003). On the 5.2L, prime the replacement retainer's sensor bore with Loctite 7649 and allow 2 minutes to dry without contamination. Apply the specified silicone bead to the block and secure the retainer within 4 minutes; if that time is exceeded, remove the sealant and clean again. Follow the staged tightening instructions. The 5.2L retainer is tilted up into position before its sequenced tightening and pan-to-retainer bolt installation.

steps.title: Install the new crankshaft seal
steps.body: Lubricate the seal bore and lips with clean engine oil; the 5.2L specifies Motorcraft SAE 5W-50 full synthetic oil meeting WSS-M2C931-E1. Position installer 303-1250 on the crankshaft, slide the new seal onto it and install with handle 205-153. For the 5.2L, follow its seal-orientation detail exactly; do not copy the orientation of an earlier V8 seal.

steps.title: Restore the sensor and surrounding assemblies
steps.body: Reinstall and reconnect the 5.0L CKP sensor, then reinstall its oil pan. For the new 5.2L sensor, apply a 2 mm bead of Loctite 638 around its barrel, 25 mm from the bottom end, before installation. Tighten and reconnect the sensor as specified. Restore the sensor ring and spacer plate, followed by the engine's appropriate flywheel or flexplate.

steps.title: Complete the road test
steps.body: After completing the linked installation procedures, road test the vehicle as required by both rear-seal procedures. Record the outcome against the concern that prompted the repair.

watchFor.title: Dropped sensor ring
watchFor.body: A ring that has been dropped must be discarded, even without visible damage.

watchFor.title: Mixing engine procedures
watchFor.body: The 5.2L replacement sensor, priming process and unique seal orientation are specific requirements, not optional additions to the 5.0L method.

notes: The 5.2L primer remains effective for up to 30 days after application, provided the primed surface is protected from other substances.
The 5.0L illustration of seal extraction should not be treated as the 5.2L seal-orientation instruction.

diagnostics.finding: The retainer was not secured within the sealant working time.
diagnostics.meaning: The sealing process no longer meets the required installation condition.
diagnostics.next: Remove the sealant, clean the sealing area and repeat the application and installation.

verification.title: Check the engine-specific completion points
verification.body: Confirm the CKP connector is attached, the sensor ring passed inspection or was replaced, and the correct seal-installation branch was completed.

verification.title: Record the road-test result
verification.body: Record completion of the required road test and whether the original concern remains.

guides.title: Remove and refit the left cylinder head on the 5.0L V8
guides.summary: Remove the left cylinder head, inspect its mating surfaces and reinstall it with a new gasket and bolts before restoring timing, fluids and exhaust connections.
guides.introduction: The left-hand (LH) aluminum cylinder head carries the valves and overhead camshafts for one bank of the 5.0L engine. Its gasket seals the head-to-block joint around combustion chambers and fluid passages. Removing the head is a major repair involving camshaft work, exhaust access and temporary changes to engine support, followed by surface inspection and controlled bolt tightening.
guides.why: A new gasket depends on suitable mating surfaces and the correct clamping load. Scratches can form leak paths, trapped liquid or debris must be cleared from bolt holes, and torque-to-yield head bolts must be replaced. Camshaft and engine-support procedures are essential parts of the job.

when.summary: After diagnosis establishes a need to remove the LH cylinder head for repair or further inspection.
notes: Confirm engine identification when selecting replacement parts.

prepare.title: Arrange specialist engine capability
prepare.detail: Have a hoist, lifting bracket 303-050, support bar 303-F072, torque-and-angle tools, compressed air and oil-drain equipment. The work also requires fuel-pressure release, cooling-system service and camshaft-timing capability.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement parts and clean working conditions
prepare.detail: Obtain a new head gasket, new head bolts, a new oil filter and engine oil selected through the 5.0L specifications. Keep cleaning debris out of the exposed engine.

steps.title: Lift the vehicle and drain the cooling system
steps.body: Follow the [5.0L LH head procedure](#/document/G1685318). With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a hoist at the specified lifting points. Release fuel-system pressure and drain the cooling system through their respective procedures.

steps.title: Remove the intake, camshaft and exhaust dependencies
steps.body: Disconnect the LH heated oxygen sensor (HO2S) and catalyst-monitor sensor connectors and release their harness retainers. Remove the intake manifold, LH camshaft and LH catalytic converter in that order, following each linked removal procedure and its prerequisites.

steps.title: Restore mount support before lifting off the head
steps.body: Install the LH engine-mount bracket, bolts and stud bolt. Use the support tools to lower the engine onto the LH mount, then remove the tools. Disconnect the camshaft position (CMP) sensors and ignition-interference capacitor, move the ground wire aside and detach the head harness retainer. Remove and discard the head bolts, lift off the head and discard its gasket.

steps.title: Clean and assess both mating surfaces
steps.body: Clean the head and block without metal scrapers, wire brushes, abrasive discs or other abrasive methods. Clear all coolant, oil and debris from the block's head-bolt holes using compressed air. Perform the separate cylinder-head and cylinder-block distortion checks before deciding the joint is ready for assembly.

steps.title: Install the gasket, head and new bolts
steps.body: Fit a new gasket and install the head with new torque-to-yield bolts. Follow the complete seven-stage 5.0L tightening instruction, including its intermediate 180° loosening stage. Do not reduce it to a single torque setting. Restore the head harness retainer, ground wire, CMP connectors and interference-capacitor connection.

steps.title: Reopen access and restore the removed assemblies
steps.body: Fit the lifting bracket and support bar with its legs on body structure, clear of the fenders. Raise the LH side of the engine 25 mm and remove the LH mount bracket. Install the LH catalytic converter, LH camshaft and intake manifold in that order using their complete installation procedures, including timing and support restoration.

steps.title: Reconnect the exhaust sensors and renew the oil
steps.body: Reconnect both LH exhaust-sensor connectors and retain their harnesses. Drain the engine oil and reinstall the drain plug. Discard the old oil filter and install a new one using its specified torque-and-angle stages without lubricating the O-ring. Fill with clean oil to the 5.0L specification.

steps.title: Fill, bleed and road test
steps.body: Complete the cooling-system filling and bleeding procedure, then road test the vehicle. This final operating check follows completion of the mechanical, electrical and fluid-restoration work.

watchFor.title: Damaged sealing faces
watchFor.body: Abrasive cleaning can scratch or gouge the head and block, creating leak paths beneath a new gasket.

watchFor.title: Unsafe vehicle support
watchFor.body: Use the marked lifting locations and never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

notes: The exhaust-connector illustrations show an automatic transmission; the manual-transmission arrangement is similar.

diagnostics.finding: A mating surface does not satisfy its distortion check.
diagnostics.meaning: The joint has not been established as suitable for reassembly.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the condition using the applicable head or block inspection procedure before installing the gasket.

verification.title: Confirm assembly milestones
verification.body: Confirm completion of the head-bolt stages, camshaft installation, sensor reconnections, oil and filter renewal, and cooling-system bleeding.

verification.title: Record inspection and operating results
verification.body: Record the head and block inspection results and the road-test outcome, including any unresolved original concern.
