guides.title: Remove and refit the right-hand cylinder head on the 5.0L V8
guides.summary: Remove the right-hand cylinder head, inspect its mating surfaces and reinstall it with a new gasket and bolts before renewing fluids.
guides.introduction: The right-hand cylinder head closes one bank of cylinders and carries its valves and overhead camshafts. Its gasket seals the joint to the cylinder block. Removing the head involves fuel-pressure release, cooling-system draining, camshaft work and a controlled transfer of engine support.
guides.why: A new gasket needs sound, clean mating surfaces and the correct bolt loading. Scratches can create leak paths, contamination can enter engine passages, and the torque-to-yield head bolts cannot be reused. The support sequence also matters: the engine must be carried by the prescribed mount or support equipment throughout the work.

when.summary: When a confirmed cylinder-head or gasket repair requires removal of the right-hand head.
notes: This removal procedure is not a diagnostic test proving a head or gasket fault.
Use the engine identification information when selecting replacement parts.

prepare.title: Provide lifting, support and timing capability
prepare.detail: Use a hoist at the approved lifting points, engine lifting bracket 303-050 and support bar 303-F072. Have the capability and equipment required by the linked right-hand camshaft procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare for clean assembly
prepare.detail: Have fuel-pressure-release and cooling-system service capability, oil drain equipment, compressed air and torque-and-angle tools. Obtain a new head gasket, new head bolts, a new oil filter and the specified refill fluids.

steps.title: Depressurize and drain before dismantling
steps.body: With the vehicle in Neutral, position it on the hoist. Follow [Fuel System Pressure Release](#/document/G1702146), then drain the cooling system through [the 5.0L cooling procedure](#/document/G1694583). Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

steps.title: Remove the connected assemblies
steps.body: Remove the [intake manifold](#/document/G1685326), [right-hand camshafts](#/document/G1685314) and [right-hand exhaust manifold](#/document/G1685323), in that order. Complete their access, timing and support requirements as part of this job.

steps.title: Transfer engine weight back to the mount
steps.body: Install the right-hand engine mount bracket, bolts and stud bolts, tightening them as specified. Use the lifting bracket and support bar to lower the engine onto the right-hand mount, then remove those special tools.

steps.title: Disconnect and lift off the head
steps.body: Disconnect the heater hose, camshaft position sensor connector and cylinder head temperature (CHT) sensor connector. Remove and discard the head bolts, remove the cylinder head, then discard the gasket.

steps.title: Clean and inspect the joint
steps.body: Clean and inspect both mating surfaces using the linked head and block distortion procedures. Do not use metal scrapers, wire brushes, power abrasive discs or other abrasive methods. Clear coolant, oil and foreign material from the block's head-bolt holes with compressed air while keeping debris out of engine passages.

steps.title: Install the gasket, head and new bolts
steps.body: Fit a new gasket, position the head and install new torque-to-yield bolts. Follow the numbered tightening illustration and every tightening, loosening and angle stage in [the head procedure](#/document/G1685319). Reconnect the heater hose and both sensor connectors.

steps.title: Restore access for reassembly
steps.body: Reinstall the lifting bracket and support bar, then raise the right-hand side of the engine 25 mm (1 inch). Remove the mount bracket, bolts and stud bolts. Reinstall the exhaust manifold, right-hand camshafts and intake manifold through their respective procedures, including their support and timing operations.

steps.title: Renew the oil and restore the cooling system
steps.body: Drain the engine oil and reinstall the drain plug to specification. Discard the old filter and install a new one without lubricating its O-ring; use this procedure's staged filter-tightening instruction. Fill with clean oil to [5.0L Specifications](#/document/G1685306), then fill and bleed the cooling system through the linked procedure.

watchFor.title: Support removed before the weight transfer
watchFor.body: The removal sequence lowers the engine onto the reinstalled mount before the special support tools are removed. Preserve that order.

watchFor.title: Abrasive damage to sealing faces
watchFor.body: Cleaning must not scratch or gouge the head or block. A damaged face can remain a leak path beneath a new gasket.

notes: The dry oil-filter O-ring instruction belongs to this 5.0L repair procedure; retain it during the final oil service.

diagnostics.finding: Head or block mating-surface inspection identifies distortion.
diagnostics.meaning: A new gasket alone does not establish a serviceable joint.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the finding using the applicable distortion procedure before committing to reassembly.

verification.title: Complete restoration and road testing
verification.body: Confirm the linked reassembly operations, oil refill and cooling-system filling and bleeding are complete, then road test the vehicle.

verification.title: Record the repair result
verification.body: Record the mating-surface inspection results, installation of new gasket and head bolts, completion of the tightening stages, and the road-test outcome.

guides.title: Replace the engine oil cooler — 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Remove, inspect and replace the oil cooler using the correct connections, access route and fluid checks for your engine.
guides.introduction: The oil cooler transfers heat away from engine oil, which supplies the engine’s bearings and oil galleries. The two engines use different arrangements: the 5.0L procedure disconnects coolant hoses and removes the oil filter, while the 5.2L procedure disconnects oil tubes and requires access through the left wheel area. Identify the engine before ordering parts or beginning work.
guides.why: Secure connections and correct fluid levels protect the lubrication system after reassembly. Metal inside a cooler is especially significant: replacing the cooler without correcting the underlying mechanical concern can lead to engine failure.

when.summary: When the oil cooler requires removal for inspection or replacement.
notes: Check engine identification information to obtain the correct parts.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underside access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the linked lifting procedure. Locate the lifting points by their stamped triangles and check adapter clearance. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare the engine-specific supplies
prepare.detail: For the 5.0L, have hose locking pliers, a new cooler gasket and a new oil filter. Have suitable torque equipment and the specified replenishment fluids. The 5.2L also requires left wheel removal.

steps.title: Identify the branch and lift the vehicle
steps.body: Place the vehicle in NEUTRAL and position it on the hoist. Follow only the cooler procedure matching the engine; the two access and connection sequences are not interchangeable.

steps.title: Remove the 5.0L cooler
steps.body: For either the shield alone or the bracket-and-shield assembly, loosen the two front bolts and remove the remaining bolts and assembly. Discard the oil filter. Clamp the coolant hoses with hose locking pliers, disconnect them, then remove the cooler retainer and cooler.

steps.title: Remove the 5.2L cooler
steps.body: Remove the underbody shielding and left wheel. Remove the bracket and air duct, then release the shield retainers and position the shield aside. Remove the retaining clips, disconnect the oil cooler tubes and remove the cooler fasteners and cooler.

steps.title: Inspect before installing another cooler
steps.body: Inspect the removed cooler and address any metal or aluminum contamination using the diagnostic decision below. On the 5.0L, remove and discard the cooler gasket.

steps.title: Reassemble the 5.0L arrangement
steps.body: Install a new gasket, cooler and retainer. Reconnect the coolant hoses and remove the locking pliers. Install a new filter without lubricating its O-ring, using the specified tightening stages. Refit the applicable shield assembly using its illustrated fastener groups and torque values.

steps.title: Reassemble the 5.2L arrangement
steps.body: Install the cooler, reconnect its tubes and install the retaining clips. Restore the shield, air duct and bracket. Apply the distinct bracket-to-cooler and bracket-to-frame tightening specifications, then reinstall the left wheel and underbody shielding.

steps.title: Restore the fluid levels
steps.body: Inspect and adjust engine oil level on either engine. On the 5.0L, also inspect and adjust coolant level in the degas bottle. Keep the fluid requirements specific to each engine.

watchFor.title: Hoses left clamped
watchFor.body: Remove the 5.0L hose locking pliers after reconnecting the coolant hoses.

watchFor.title: Different shield fasteners
watchFor.body: The 5.0L shield and bracket-and-shield arrangements have different tightening groups; use the matching illustration.

notes: 5.0L coolant: Motorcraft Orange Concentrated Antifreeze/Coolant, VC-3-B, specification WSS-M97B44-D.
5.2L oil: Motorcraft SAE 5W-50 Full Synthetic Motor Oil, XO-5W50-QGT, specification WSS-M2C931-E1.

diagnostics.finding: Metal or aluminum material inside either cooler.
diagnostics.meaning: An underlying mechanical concern exists and can cause engine failure if left unresolved.
diagnostics.next: Complete the mechanical diagnosis directed to Section 303-00 before treating cooler replacement as the completed repair.

verification.title: Confirm the correct completion checks
verification.body: Verify the engine oil level on both engines and the degas-bottle coolant level on the 5.0L. Confirm the disturbed connections, retainers and shielding have been restored.

applicability.equipment: 5.0L or 5.2L engine; underbody shielding and cooler connections differ by engine and equipment.

guides.title: Replace Secondary Timing Chain Tensioners on the 5.0L or 5.2L
guides.summary: Renew the secondary chain tensioner and shoe, restore camshaft timing-unit alignment and activate the replacement tensioner.
guides.introduction: Each secondary timing chain connects the intake and exhaust variable camshaft timing (VCT) assemblies on its cylinder bank. The hydraulic tensioner acts through a shoe to keep the chain tensioned. Replacement requires removing the VCT assemblies and restoring their precise relationship to the chain and camshafts.
guides.why: This is engine-timing work: correct seating, chain alignment and controlled tensioner release all matter. The replacement tensioner is shorter than the earlier design, so its appearance alone cannot establish whether it is fully installed.

when.summary: When secondary timing-chain tensioner renewal is required during engine repair.
notes: Identify the engine and serviced bank before selecting parts and procedures.

prepare.title: Arrange timing-work capability
prepare.detail: Have the engine-specific VCT and primary timing-chain procedures, camshaft counterholding wrench, torque-and-angle equipment and, for 5.2L installation, an assistant.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement parts and a clean work area
prepare.detail: Use replacement tensioners and shoes, with shipping clips retained until instructed. Have clean engine oil for the seals and bore. Keep debris out of oil passages, coolant passages and the oil pan.

steps.title: Remove the VCT assemblies in the required order
steps.body: Follow the [5.0L VCT procedure](#/document/G1685333) or [5.2L VCT procedure](#/document/G1800286). If servicing both banks, remove the right-hand secondary tensioner before the left-hand one.

steps.title: Discard the removed shoe and tensioner
steps.body: After removing that bank's VCT assemblies, remove and discard the shoe. Push the tensioner upward from beneath the camshaft mega cap—the cap containing its bore—and discard it too.

steps.title: Seat the replacement tensioner and shoe
steps.body: When servicing both banks, follow the left-hand installation phase first. Leave the shipping clip fitted. Oil the tensioner O-ring seals and mega-cap bore, then push the tensioner fully downward until it snaps into place. Install the replacement shoe; its tabs contact the front of the mega cap.

steps.title: Align the secondary chain and fit the VCT assemblies
steps.body: Place the intake timing mark between the two consecutive colored chain links and the exhaust mark at the single colored link. For the 5.0L, follow its illustrated installation position. For the 5.2L, position the exhaust mark approximately at 12 o'clock; have an assistant turn the intake camshaft counterclockwise using its flats until the locating pin engages, then slide both assemblies fully onto the camshafts.

steps.title: Secure the assemblies while counterholding
steps.body: Hold each camshaft with a wrench on its flats while installing the intake and exhaust VCT assembly bolts. Both engine procedures specify 15 Nm followed by 90°. Counterholding keeps tightening force from turning the camshaft.

steps.title: Release and activate the tensioner
steps.body: Remove and discard the shipping clip only now. Press the secondary chain and tensioner top shoe downward until the tensioner bottoms out, then release them. The tensioner should spring upward and tension the chain.

steps.title: Restore the primary timing drive
steps.body: Install the corresponding primary chain using the [5.0L timing-chain procedure](#/document/G1685330) or [5.2L timing-chain procedure](#/document/G1800283). When doing both banks, complete the left-hand chain installation before repeating the tensioner installation sequence on the right-hand side and installing its chain.

watchFor.title: Premature clip removal
watchFor.body: Keep the shipping clip fitted through tensioner seating, chain alignment and VCT bolt tightening.

watchFor.title: Contamination during cleaning
watchFor.body: Material scraped from gasket surfaces can enter engine passages and cause engine failure.

notes: Use engine identification information when ordering parts; revisions can differ within an engine family.

diagnostics.finding: The replacement tensioner does not extend below the mega cap.
diagnostics.meaning: This is a feature of the revised, shorter design.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the snap-in seating and correct shoe-tab position.

verification.title: Confirm seating and timing
verification.body: Check full tensioner seating, shoe position, colored-link alignment and fully seated VCT assemblies before release.

verification.title: Confirm activation
verification.body: Verify that the tensioner springs upward and tensions the chain, then complete the engine-specific primary-chain installation.

guides.title: Remove, overhaul and reinstall the 5.2L V8 engine
guides.summary: Rebuild the 5.2L engine through controlled removal, inspection, bearing selection, valve timing, sealing and installation.
guides.introduction: The 5.2L engine combines a flat-plane crankshaft with double overhead camshafts and twin independent variable camshaft timing. Its bearings depend on pressurized oil, while its chains keep piston and valve movement synchronized. An overhaul opens these closely related systems, allowing damaged or worn components to be inspected and renewed before the engine is rebuilt and returned to the vehicle.
guides.why: Cleanliness, component identity and assembly order determine whether the rebuilt engine can survive. Debris can obstruct lubrication, mismatched connecting-rod caps can change bearing clearance, and incorrect camshaft phasing can cause serious internal damage. This is specialist engine work requiring measurement and controlled lifting, not simply replacement of visible worn parts.

when.summary: When established internal damage or measured wear requires engine removal and a full strip-down.
notes: Identify the engine build before ordering parts; components can differ within the same engine family.
Use measured condition to decide what needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and bench capability
prepare.detail: Provide a vehicle hoist, floor crane, engine stand, lifting bracket 303-F047, support bar 303-F072, and a trolley jack with wooden block. Support-bar feet belong on the body structure, and transmission support belongs under the bell housing.

prepare.title: Prepare measuring and assembly equipment
prepare.detail: Have clearance and end-play measuring capability, torque and angle tools, a piston ring compressor, clutch aligner, crankshaft holding tool and the specified seal installers and puller. An assistant is required during the camshaft/VCT operations.

prepare.title: Organize clean parts and replacements
prepare.detail: Keep reusable parts identified by original position. Prepare the specified engine oil, coolant, sealants and primer, plus every gasket, seal and fastener designated for replacement in the linked phases.

steps.title: Isolate the vehicle and clear access
steps.body: Follow the [removal phase](#/document/G1800288): place the vehicle in Neutral on the hoist, release fuel pressure, disconnect both battery cables and drain coolant. Loosen the steering-column dash seal and hold the steering wheel straight ahead. Index-mark the hood, then remove the prescribed intake, cooling, cowl, exhaust and starter components. Drain engine oil, discard the filter and disconnect the oil-cooler hoses.

steps.title: Separate and lift the engine
steps.body: Disconnect the steering shaft without hammering or prying; discard its bolt and secure the shaft to the frame rail. Use the support bar while removing mount brackets and positioning the air-conditioning compressor aside. Move transmission cooler tubes only if fitted. Transfer engine support to the crane, support the transmission beneath its bell housing, remove the remaining joining fasteners and lift the engine clear.

steps.title: Strip external components on the bench
steps.body: Begin the [disassembly phase](#/document/G1800290). Index-mark a reusable pressure plate and loosen its bolts evenly. Discard pressure-plate and flywheel bolts. Inspect the crankshaft sensor ring before mounting the engine on its stand. Remove the harness, covers, manifolds, pulley, coolant pump, oil pan and front cover in sequence. Retain the original pulley washer; renew discarded seals, gaskets and hardware.

steps.title: Remove timing components and heads in order
steps.body: Turn clockwise to the specified 9:30 crankshaft-keyway position and confirm the right-hand VCT timing mark is uppermost before dismantling that bank. An assistant must restrain the intake camshaft as the VCT assemblies come off. Remove each front camshaft mega cap before the remaining caps. Turn clockwise to 12:30 for the left-hand bank. Keep followers and lash adjusters identified. Remove the cylinder heads only when cool, and always before removing the crankshaft.

steps.title: Inspect and dismantle the bottom end
steps.body: Protect exposed passages and aluminum gasket faces. Check head and block distortion using their linked procedures. Remove the oil-filter adapter, discarded rear seal-retainer plate and crankshaft-position sensor, sprocket and pump. Inspect bore tops before withdrawing pistons. Preserve connecting-rod/cap orientation and avoid scratching journals or bores. Complete the [piston subassembly work](#/document/G1800293), then remove main caps, crankshaft, bearings and cooling jets.

steps.title: Select bearings and rebuild the rotating assembly
steps.body: Start the [assembly phase](#/document/G1800295) by recording block and crankshaft bearing codes. Use separate selection charts for mains 1 and 5 and for mains 2, 3 and 4. Install cooling jets and lubricated bearings with oil passages aligned. Orient the thrust-washer groove rearward, seat the washer as directed and install new discarded main-cap fasteners. Check end play and crankshaft turning torque before fitting pistons. Check piston and ring clearances, position ring gaps correctly, and install matched rod caps with new bolts.

steps.title: Restore lubrication and time the camshafts
steps.body: Prime the oil pump with 2 tablespoons of clean engine oil and rotate it by hand before installation. Refit the rear retainer and crankshaft-position sensor with their specified primer and sealant treatment. Install new head gaskets and head bolts. Assemble the left-hand camshafts and chains first at the specified 12:30 keyway position; then turn counterclockwise to 9:30 for the right-hand bank. Follow the illustrated D-slots, colored links and timing marks exactly, using new VCT bolts and the specified VCT filters.

steps.title: Seal and dress the engine
steps.body: Fully depress the VCT solenoid pins before fitting the front cover. Observe each joint's bead pattern and deadline: the rear retainer has a 4-minute securing window; the front cover, oil pan, pulley and valve covers have specified 5-minute requirements. The front-cover and oil-pan 1-hour alternatives apply only after their designated preliminary fasteners are tightened on time. Engage the pickup tube fully into its new seal. Refit accessories, new manifold studs and nuts, gaskets, covers and harness. Replace spark-plug-tube and VCT solenoid seals only where damaged seals were removed.

steps.title: Complete the rear seal and clutch assembly
steps.body: Transfer the engine to the crane for rear-seal installation, following the unique seal orientation shown in the assembly illustration. Refit the sensor ring, spacer and flywheel with new flywheel bolts. Align a reused pressure plate to its index marks; align replacement parts by their paint dots. Center the clutch disc and tighten new pressure-plate bolts progressively in the prescribed star pattern.

steps.title: Reinstall and recommission
steps.body: Follow the [installation phase](#/document/G1800297), including input-shaft lubrication, engine/transmission alignment and controlled support transfers. Restore mounts, grounds, hoses, wiring and removed components. Install a new steering-shaft bolt and perform the steering-column collapsed check before completing dash-seal installation. Use new cross-brace nuts and an oil filter, fill engine oil, reconnect the battery, and fill and bleed the cooling system. Complete the scan-tool misfire-profile routine before the road test.

watchFor.title: Contamination and damaged sealing faces
watchFor.body: Do not use metal scrapers, wire brushes or abrasive discs on head/block sealing faces. Protect openings during cleaning. Never blow clutch friction dust away with compressed air.

watchFor.title: Lost component identity
watchFor.body: Cracked connecting-rod caps must remain matched and correctly oriented. Reused valve-train components return to their original locations; early engines may lack follower spring clips.

watchFor.title: Expired sealant or incorrect timing
watchFor.body: Remove sealant and clean the joint if its permitted assembly window expires. Rotate the crankshaft only as directed during timing work.

notes: Use the linked 5.2L cooling procedure for draining, vacuum filling and bleeding; the installation phase contains a cooling cross-reference labeled 5.0L.
The detailed phases supply the tightening sequences, bearing charts and illustrations needed at the bench.

diagnostics.finding: A crankshaft sensor ring has been dropped or shows visible damage.
diagnostics.meaning: It is unsuitable for reuse.
diagnostics.next: Discard it and install a replacement.

diagnostics.finding: A roller follower or hydraulic lash adjuster is damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: Related camshaft lobes and valves also require inspection.
diagnostics.next: Inspect those components and replace damaged parts before assembly.

verification.title: Record the mechanical results
verification.body: Record both bearing codes, selected grades, measured clearances and crankshaft end play against the 5.2L specifications. Crankshaft torque-to-turn must not exceed 6 Nm (53 lb-in) at the prescribed assembly check.

verification.title: Complete vehicle checks
verification.body: Confirm the steering-column collapsed check and prescribed fluid filling are complete. Perform the Powertrain Control Module Misfire Monitor Profile Correction routine with a diagnostic scan tool, then road test and record the result.

guides.title: Disassemble and rebuild a 5.2L cylinder head
guides.summary: Service the removed cylinder head's valves, springs, stem seals and bank-specific fittings while preserving reusable parts in their original locations.
guides.introduction: The 5.2L engine's aluminum cylinder heads carry the valves operated by its overhead camshafts. Valve springs close the valves, retainers and keys secure the springs, and stem seals control oil passing along the valve stems. This bench procedure dismantles and rebuilds those components, with different coolant fittings and sensors on the left and right heads.
guides.why: Reusable components must return to their original positions. Cleanliness protects the engine's oil and coolant passages, while the specified spring-compressor arrangement controls spring load during key removal and installation. The right-head temperature sensor also needs special attention: it must be replaced, and a broken tip must not remain in the head.
searchTerms: broken cylinder head temperature sensor tip

when.summary: When a removed 5.2L cylinder head requires valve, spring or valve-stem-seal service.
notes: This is the cylinder-head bench phase; engine removal, head installation and camshaft timing are separate operations.

prepare.title: Provide the spring-compressor arrangement
prepare.detail: Use tools 303-300, 303-350, 303-1249 and 303-1418 as illustrated. This work requires the ability to control loaded valve springs and handle their small retaining keys.

prepare.title: Prepare parts and assembly fluids
prepare.detail: Have new valve-stem seals. The left head needs a new coolant-outlet gasket; the right needs a new outlet O-ring and cylinder head temperature sensor. Use Motorcraft SAE 5W-50 Full Synthetic Motor Oil and the specified Motorcraft Orange coolant for their respective lubrication steps.

prepare.title: Organize a clean bench
prepare.detail: Identify the head and replacement parts from the engine identification information. Mark reusable components so each returns to its original location.

steps.title: Strip the left-head fittings when applicable
steps.body: Remove the coolant-outlet bolts and outlet, discarding its gasket. Remove the heat shield and fasteners, then the intake and exhaust camshaft position (CMP) sensors, radio interference capacitor and their fasteners.

steps.title: Strip the right-head fittings when applicable
steps.body: Remove the CMP sensor and its bolt, then remove the cylinder head temperature (CHT) sensor. Inspect its tip before discarding the sensor. Remove any broken tip from the head bore before a replacement is installed. Remove the coolant-outlet bolt and outlet, and discard the O-ring.

steps.title: Release the first valve spring
steps.body: For either head, remove the spark plugs. Fit the specified compressor tools as shown in the [disassembly procedure](#/document/G1800292), then remove the valve keys, retainer and spring. Keep the parts identified by valve position.

steps.title: Remove the seal and valve
steps.body: Remove and discard the valve-stem seal, then remove the valve from the head. Repeat the spring, seal and valve removal sequence for the remaining valves while maintaining the original-location identification.

steps.title: Install new stem seals and the valves
steps.body: Lubricate each new stem seal and its valve-guide bore with clean specified engine oil. Install the new seal first, then install the valve into the head. This preserves the stated assembly order and supplies lubrication at the guide and seal.

steps.title: Reassemble each spring
steps.body: Use the specified compressor arrangement to install the spring, retainer and keys. Return reusable parts to their marked positions and repeat for the remaining valves. Install the spark plugs using the tightening value in the assembly procedure.

steps.title: Complete the right head
steps.body: Install a new CHT sensor, then the CMP sensor and its bolt. Lubricate the new coolant-outlet O-ring with clean specified engine coolant before installing the outlet pipe. Use the separate sensor and outlet tightening specifications.

steps.title: Complete the left head
steps.body: Install the heat shield, intake and exhaust CMP sensors, and radio interference capacitor with their fasteners. Install the coolant outlet with a new gasket. Follow the [assembly phase](#/document/G1800292) for the attachment tightening values.

watchFor.title: Spring load during key handling
watchFor.body: Keep the spring controlled by the specified tools while removing or installing its retaining parts.

watchFor.title: Mixed valve positions
watchFor.body: Preserve the identification throughout cleaning and assembly so reused parts return to their original locations.

notes: The left outlet uses a gasket; the right outlet uses a coolant-lubricated O-ring. Obtain the parts for the correct bank.

diagnostics.finding: The removed right-head CHT sensor has a missing tip.
diagnostics.meaning: A broken portion may remain in the cylinder-head bore.
diagnostics.next: Remove the fragment before fitting the new sensor. Replace the sensor even when its removed tip is intact.

verification.title: Account for each valve assembly
verification.body: Confirm each valve has its new stem seal, spring, retainer and keys, and that reusable components occupy their marked locations.

verification.title: Record bank-specific completion
verification.body: Record the right-head sensor-tip inspection and sensor replacement when applicable. Confirm the correct new outlet seal, fittings and spark plugs are installed and tightened.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L cylinder-head bench disassembly and assembly, including left/right fittings and valve-spring tooling.

guides.title: Change the engine oil and filter on the 2015 Mustang 5.2L V8
guides.summary: Drain the oil, renew the fitted spin-on or cartridge filter, and refill with 10.0 qt (9.5 L) of the specified 5W-50 full synthetic oil.
guides.introduction: Ten quarts of oil, and the drain plug still wants to be handled by hand. I like that arrangement: save the muscle for carrying the fresh oil, rather than bullying the oil pan. I’ll walk you through underside access, the two filter arrangements and their different tightening values, then closing everything up and refilling.
guides.why: The engine’s oil pump feeds pressurized oil to the crankshaft and connecting-rod bearings and through the engine’s internal oil passages. The filter removes contamination from that circulating oil. Changing both renews the lubricant and filter, while careful sealing keeps that fresh oil inside the engine where it earns its keep.

when.summary: Use this procedure when an oil-and-filter change is required or engine work calls for draining and renewing the oil.
notes: Identify the filter actually fitted to the vehicle before purchasing parts. Both arrangements are covered here.
This is a maintenance procedure, not a diagnosis for an oil-pressure warning or engine noise.
No maintenance interval is established here.

prepare.title: Match the engine and replacement parts
prepare.detail: Confirm the 5.2L engine using its identification label, which includes displacement, engine part number and build information. Use those identifiers when selecting replacement parts because parts can differ within an engine family. Obtain either the correct complete spin-on filter or the correct cartridge element with new housing O-rings. See [Engine identification](#/document/G1800261).

prepare.title: Gather oil and collection equipment
prepare.detail: Have Motorcraft SAE 5W-50 Full Synthetic Motor Oil, XO-5W50-QGT for the US or Canada, ready before draining. The service fill including the filter is 10.0 qt (9.5 L). Use oil-drain equipment with capacity for that quantity and room to avoid overflow. Read the oil’s material safety information before handling it. See [5.2L specifications](#/document/G1800259).

prepare.title: Prepare the filter tools and seals
prepare.detail: Have a torque wrench and an oil-filter cap wrench that fits the spin-on filter. Cartridge service requires suitable tooling for the housing’s external drive feature, a clean lint-free cloth and two new housing O-rings. Keep clean engine oil available to lubricate the replacement seals. The smallest O-ring supplied with the cartridge kit is not used on this application.

prepare.title: Arrange proper underside access
prepare.detail: This procedure uses a hoist with the transmission in Neutral. Confirm that the hoist can carry the vehicle, including cargo and modifications, and have wheel chocks ready. Locate the stamped triangular lifting-point marks before raising. The emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this job. Never work underneath jack-only support; a vehicle raised with a jack requires floor stands. See [Jacking and lifting](#/document/G1663631).

prepare.title: Keep startup and cooling-fan hazards under control
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection, and use protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. Cooling fans can operate with the ignition off. If access requires working near a fan, obtain the vehicle-specific fan-disabling instructions and disable it before approaching; switching the ignition off alone is insufficient. See [Health and safety precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start
steps.body:
Before working around or underneath the car, disable remote start if fitted: use the Central Display’s Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup controls.

Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle so another person cannot start it during service. Keep the engine off throughout draining, filter replacement and refilling.

steps.title: Secure the car and position the hoist
steps.body:
Position the vehicle on a hard, level surface. Apply the parking brake and chock all wheels remaining on the ground before selecting Neutral.

Locate the stamped triangles identifying the lifting points along the underside edges, behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels. Position the hoist adapters at those marked points. Do not lift against either bumper.

Check that the adapters and lifting arms clear the suspension, exhaust, steering linkage, mounting brackets, stabilizer brackets, axle and rear cover. For a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving onto it. The [lifting overview](#/document/G1663631) provides the supporting lifting-point guidance.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle for underside access
steps.body:
With the transmission in Neutral, raise the vehicle on the correctly positioned hoist. Keep the parking brake applied; this oil change does not require its release. Maintain chocks at any wheels that remain on the ground.

Do not go underneath until the vehicle is properly supported by the hoist. Do not use the engine to turn the drive wheels during this work.

steps.title: Remove the small service-access cover
steps.body:
Find the small rectangular cover set into the larger underside panel. Its lower edge has a rounded projecting tab with a single retainer through it.

Remove that retainer first, then remove the cover and keep both for reassembly. This opens the filter service area without removing the entire surrounding panel. The next two steps are alternatives: use only the one matching the fitted filter.

steps.title: Spin-on filter: remove and discard the complete filter
steps.body:
Position the oil-drain equipment beneath the filter. Identify the complete cylindrical metal filter screwed onto the engine’s filter adapter; it projects downward at an angle beside the ribbed engine casting.

Unscrew and remove the filter, collecting the escaping oil. Discard the complete old filter. Continue at the oil-pan draining step.

steps.title: Cartridge filter: drain the housing and remove its contents
steps.body:
Position the oil-drain equipment beneath the cartridge housing. This arrangement has a reusable screw-on housing with an external drive feature at its closed end.

Loosen the housing and allow its oil to drain before removing the housing completely. Note the positions of the existing housing O-rings before removing them.

Remove and discard the old filter element and housing O-rings. Look inside both the removed housing and the engine-mounted filter adapter, and make sure every component of the old element has been removed. I count the old pieces before introducing new ones; mystery leftovers are a lousy bonus feature.

steps.title: Release the oil-pan drain plug by hand
steps.body:
Move the drain equipment beneath the oil-pan drain opening. Identify the plug with the broad hand-grip tabs projecting from the lower portion of the pan.

Turn the plug counterclockwise exactly 120 degrees by hand, then pull it out of the pan. Collect the oil and allow it to drain.

Do not use tools to remove this plug.

steps.title: Refit the drain plug without tools
steps.body:
After the oil has drained, push the plug back into the oil pan. Turn it clockwise exactly 120 degrees by hand.

Do not add tool-assisted tightening or extra rotation. Overtightening can damage the plug and possibly the oil pan. This is a hand-operated closure, not a threaded bolt requiring a torque-wrench value.

steps.title: Spin-on filter: lubricate the seal and tighten to 17 lb.ft (23 Nm)
steps.body:
Before fitting the new spin-on filter, wipe the engine sealing surface and threads with a clean rag.

For a spin-on arrangement, lubricate the sealing O-ring on the new filter with clean engine oil. This is the ring around the filter’s open mounting face.

Install the new filter onto the adapter. Fit the oil-filter cap wrench over the filter’s closed end and connect the torque wrench through the service opening. Tighten to 17 lb.ft (23 Nm).

Continue at the closure checks. The cartridge-housing tightening value belongs to a different arrangement.

steps.title: Cartridge filter: clean and inspect the reusable housing
steps.body:
For a cartridge arrangement, wipe the housing threads and O-ring sealing surfaces with a clean lint-free cloth.

Visually examine the housing and the internal stem—the central support inside it—for damage. Look specifically for cracks and for separation of the stem from the housing. If either part is damaged, install a new oil-filter housing assembly before continuing; a new element and seals cannot repair a damaged housing.

steps.title: Cartridge filter: renew both housing seals and the element
steps.body:
Install the two new housing O-rings in the corresponding seal locations noted during removal, and lubricate them with clean engine oil. O-rings are the flexible rings that seal the reusable housing against oil leakage.

Do not reuse the old seals. Leave out the smallest O-ring supplied with the filter kit; it is not used on this application.

Install the new filter element in the housing. Confirm that no old element components remain in the housing or adapter before bringing them together.

steps.title: Cartridge filter: install the housing and tighten to 18 lb.ft (24 Nm)
steps.body:
Install the housing and new element into the engine-mounted adapter. Use suitable tooling on the housing’s external drive feature and a torque wrench to tighten the housing to 18 lb.ft (24 Nm).

This value is for the cartridge housing. The spin-on filter uses 17 lb.ft (23 Nm). Keeping those two numbers with their own parts saves a surprising amount of damn confusion.

steps.title: Check the closures and replace the access cover
steps.body:
Before covering the service area, confirm that the drain plug has been pushed fully into place and turned clockwise 120 degrees by hand. Confirm that the fitted filter arrangement has its new filter, required new seals and correct tightening value.

Return the small rectangular access cover to its opening, then reinstall the retainer through the rounded lower tab. Confirm that the cover is retained.

steps.title: Restore restraints before and during lowering
steps.body:
Remove the drain equipment and loose tools from beneath the vehicle, and make sure everyone is clear.

Before lowering, positively confirm that the parking brake is applied; reapply it now if it was released. Lower the vehicle using the hoist. As the wheels reach the ground, restore wheel chocks before removing the hoist support completely. Keep the ignition off and the transmission in Neutral during this transition.

steps.title: Open the hood and check the fan before underhood work
steps.body:
With the ignition still off and the key removed, open the hood. From clear of the fans, visually check them for damage, cracks or separation before beginning underhood work.

If a fan is damaged, stop underhood work until it has been replaced. Keep clear of the fan area during filling, and observe the fan-disabling prerequisite if nearby work is necessary.

steps.title: Refill through the engine oil-filler opening
steps.body:
Locate the oil-filler cap on top of the engine cover area, beside the ignition-coil connections. Remove the cap and fill through that opening with clean Motorcraft SAE 5W-50 Full Synthetic Motor Oil, XO-5W50-QGT.

The specified service fill including the replacement filter is 10.0 qt (9.5 L). Measure the refill using that specification, then reinstall the filler cap. See [5.2L oil specification and capacity](#/document/G1800259).

steps.title: Complete the assembly and refill checks
steps.body:
Confirm that the filler cap, underside access cover and retainer are back in place. Check accessible areas around the drain plug and filter joint for escaping fresh oil. If oil is escaping, leave the engine off and correct the affected closure before using the car.

Record the oil product, quantity and fitted filter type. Finish with the dipstick check below; measured fill alone is not the final level check. An oil-life display reset is a separate operation.

steps.title: Check the actual oil level on level ground
steps.body:
With the car on level ground, keep the engine off and allow 15 minutes for oil to drain into the pan. Set the parking brake and securely engage first gear. Protect yourself from engine heat when opening the hood.

Carefully withdraw the dipstick, wipe it clean, insert it fully, then withdraw it again to read the level. If the oil lies between its lower and upper holes, the level is acceptable: do not add more oil. If it is below the lower hole, add enough of the specified oil to bring it between the holes. Finish by fully seating the dipstick.

This is the model-specific method in Ford’s [2015–2016 Shelby GT350 supplement, printed page 36](https://www.fordservicecontent.com/Ford_Content/Catalog/owner_information/2015-2016-Mustang-Shelby-GT350-Supplement-version-1_su_EN-US_07_2015.pdf#page=39).

watchFor.title: Neutral removes the transmission’s restraint
watchFor.body: Apply the parking brake and chock ground wheels before selecting Neutral. Confirm the parking brake before lowering, and restore chocks as the wheels reach the ground.

watchFor.title: The drain plug is hand-operated
watchFor.body: Removal is counterclockwise 120 degrees, followed by pulling the plug out. Installation is pushing it in, then clockwise 120 degrees. Tools and extra tightening can damage the plug or pan.

watchFor.title: Cartridge parts can remain in either location
watchFor.body: Check both the reusable housing and engine-mounted adapter. Removing the main element does not prove that every element component came out.

watchFor.title: New cartridge seals are required
watchFor.body: Renew both housing O-rings and lubricate them with clean engine oil. Reusing the old seals can cause leakage. The kit’s smallest O-ring is unused here.

watchFor.title: Filter torque depends on the fitted arrangement
watchFor.body: Tighten the spin-on filter with a cap wrench and torque wrench to 17 lb.ft (23 Nm). Tighten the cartridge housing to 18 lb.ft (24 Nm).

notes: The 10.0 qt (9.5 L) quantity is the 5.2L service fill including the oil filter.
Use engine identification information to select parts; do not assume every filter or housing listed for a V8 Mustang fits this engine.
The [engine overview](#/document/G1800261) explains the pressurized lubrication system. Its internal engine details are not additional oil-change operations.

diagnostics.finding: A complete disposable metal filter is screwed onto the adapter.
diagnostics.meaning: The vehicle has the spin-on arrangement.
diagnostics.next: Replace the complete filter, oil its new sealing ring and tighten with a cap wrench and torque wrench to 17 lb.ft (23 Nm).

diagnostics.finding: A reusable housing contains a removable filter element.
diagnostics.meaning: The vehicle has the cartridge arrangement.
diagnostics.next: Drain and remove the housing, renew the element and two housing O-rings, inspect the housing and stem, and tighten the installed housing to 18 lb.ft (24 Nm).

diagnostics.finding: The cartridge housing or internal stem is damaged, cracked or separating.
diagnostics.meaning: The reusable housing assembly is unsuitable for continued service.
diagnostics.next: Install a new oil-filter housing assembly before completing the cartridge-filter installation.

diagnostics.finding: An old filter-element component remains in the housing or adapter.
diagnostics.meaning: Cartridge removal is incomplete.
diagnostics.next: Remove the remaining component before installing the new element. If all components cannot be accounted for or removed, pause assembly rather than installing the new filter over them.

diagnostics.finding: Fresh oil is escaping at the drain plug or filter joint after refilling.
diagnostics.meaning: The service closure requires correction; refilling alone does not confirm sealing.
diagnostics.next: Keep the engine off. Re-establish safe access if needed and check the affected closure against its installation branch. Do not try to cure leakage by adding force to the hand-operated drain plug.

diagnostics.finding: A cooling fan has visible damage, cracks or separation.
diagnostics.meaning: Underhood work must stop because the fan can fail during operation.
diagnostics.next: Have the damaged fan replaced before continuing underhood service. Fan replacement is outside this oil-change procedure.

verification.title: Correct oil and measured quantity
verification.body: Confirm Motorcraft SAE 5W-50 Full Synthetic Motor Oil, XO-5W50-QGT, and the 10.0 qt (9.5 L) service fill including the replacement filter.

verification.title: Correct filter branch completed
verification.body: For spin-on service, confirm a new lubricated filter tightened to 17 lb.ft (23 Nm). For cartridge service, confirm a sound housing and stem, a new element, two new lubricated housing O-rings, no retained old element components and housing tightening to 18 lb.ft (24 Nm).

verification.title: All openings closed
verification.body: Confirm the drain plug was installed by hand through its 120-degree clockwise movement, the filler cap is installed, and the service cover and retainer are secured. Resolve any visible escaping fresh oil before use.

verification.title: Vehicle returned to restrained ground support
verification.body: Confirm the parking brake was applied before lowering, wheel chocks were restored as the wheels reached the ground, and all drain equipment and loose tools have been removed.

verification.title: Dipstick level confirmed
verification.body: After the 15-minute drainback wait on level ground, verify the wiped and fully reinserted dipstick reads between its lower and upper holes. Do not add oil when it already lies within that range. Fully seat the dipstick afterward.

guides.title: Remove and refit the 5.2L left cylinder head
guides.summary: Remove the left cylinder head, inspect its sealing joint and reinstall it with a new gasket and new torque-to-yield bolts.
guides.introduction: The left-hand cylinder head closes one bank of cylinders and carries the valves and overhead camshafts. Its joint with the block must contain combustion pressure while keeping oil and coolant in their intended passages. This repair opens that joint and includes the surrounding intake, camshaft, exhaust and engine-support work needed to reach it.
guides.why: Debris entering an engine passage can cause engine failure, while scratches across a sealing face can become leak paths. The head bolts stretch during tightening and must be replaced. Engine support also changes during this procedure, so the mount and support-bar sequence matters as much as the head installation.

when.summary: When diagnosis or planned engine repair requires removal of the 5.2L left cylinder head.
notes: Confirm engine identification before obtaining replacement parts.
Plan for camshaft and timing work through the dedicated left-camshaft procedure.

prepare.title: Provide lifting and engine support
prepare.detail: Use a suitable hoist, engine lifting bracket 303-050 and support bar 303-F072. Follow the marked lifting points; never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare for engine repair
prepare.detail: Have new head bolts and a new head gasket, torque-and-angle tightening equipment, compressed air for bolt-hole cleaning, and the capability to release fuel pressure and vacuum-fill and bleed the cooling system.

steps.title: Make the vehicle and fluid systems ready
steps.body: Place the vehicle in NEUTRAL and position it on the hoist using [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631). Complete the [5.2L fuel-pressure release](#/document/G1794916), then drain the cooling system using its [draining, vacuum-filling and bleeding procedure](#/document/G1807369).

steps.title: Remove the assemblies above and beside the head
steps.body: Remove the [intake manifold](#/document/G1800279), [left camshaft assembly](#/document/G1800266) and [left exhaust manifold](#/document/G1800276), in that order. Follow each complete procedure, including the camshaft timing requirements; these are substantial access phases.

steps.title: Return the engine to its left mount
steps.body: Install the left engine-mount bracket, bolts and stud bolt, tightening them to 55 Nm. Use the lifting bracket and support bar to lower the engine onto the left mount, then remove those special tools. This restores mount support before the head is detached.

steps.title: Disconnect and lift off the head
steps.body: Remove the ground-strap nut and move the strap aside. Disconnect the camshaft position (CMP) sensors and ignition interference capacitor, then detach the harness retainer. Remove and discard the cylinder-head bolts, remove the head and discard its gasket.

steps.title: Prepare and assess the sealing joint
steps.body: Clean the head and block mating faces without metal scrapers, wire brushes, power abrasive discs or other abrasive methods. Clear coolant, oil and debris from the block's head-bolt holes with compressed air. Inspect both faces using [Cylinder Head Distortion](#/document/G1661748) and [Cylinder Block Distortion](#/document/G1661746) before proceeding.

steps.title: Install the head with new fastening parts
steps.body: Fit the new gasket, head and new bolts using the [head installation procedure](#/document/G1800271). Its tightening stages are 30 Nm, 50 Nm, then an additional 90° and another 90°. Restore the harness retainer, sensor and capacitor connectors, and ground strap; tighten the ground-strap nut to 9 Nm.

steps.title: Restore access assemblies and cooling
steps.body: Refit the lifting bracket and support bar with the bar's legs on body structure. Raise the left side of the engine 25 mm, then remove the mount-bracket bolts, stud bolt and bracket. Reinstall the left exhaust manifold, left camshaft assembly and intake manifold through their complete procedures. Fill and bleed the cooling system, then road test.

watchFor.title: Support-bar feet on the fenders
watchFor.body: The fenders are not the specified support surface. Position the legs on body structure to prevent damage.

watchFor.title: Contaminated bolt holes or sealing faces
watchFor.body: Clear trapped fluids and debris before assembly, and prevent cleaning residue from entering oil or coolant passages.

notes: This procedure applies to the left head of the 5.2L engine. Use its dedicated intake, camshaft and exhaust procedures throughout.

diagnostics.finding: The head or block mating face fails its distortion inspection.
diagnostics.meaning: The sealing joint requires further evaluation before reassembly.
diagnostics.next: Follow the applicable distortion procedure's limits and decisions before fitting the new gasket.

verification.title: Confirm assembly prerequisites
verification.body: Confirm new head bolts and gasket were used, all tightening stages were completed, electrical connections were restored and cooling-system filling and bleeding are complete.

verification.title: Record the road-test result
verification.body: Carry out the required road test and record the result, including any remaining concern.

guides.title: Remove and refit the right cylinder head on the 5.2L V8
guides.summary: Remove the right cylinder head, inspect the head and block surfaces and rebuild the joint with a new gasket and torque-to-yield bolts.
guides.introduction: The right-hand (RH) cylinder head houses the valves and overhead camshafts for one bank of the 5.2L V8. Its gasket seals the combustion chambers and fluid passages where the aluminum head meets the block. This job combines intake, camshaft and exhaust-manifold removal with head inspection, staged bolt tightening and restoration of the heater and sensor connections.
guides.why: Correct gasket sealing depends on surface condition and controlled bolt loading. Reusing torque-to-yield bolts or damaging the mating faces undermines that repair. Because the camshafts are chain driven, their removal and installation require the complete timing procedure as part of the head work.

when.summary: After diagnosis establishes that the RH cylinder head must be removed for repair or inspection.
notes: Use the engine identification information to select the correct replacement parts.

prepare.title: Arrange engine and timing capability
prepare.detail: Have a vehicle hoist, lifting bracket 303-050, support bar 303-F072, torque-and-angle tools and compressed air. The job requires fuel-pressure release, cooling-system service and the complete RH camshaft procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare the sealing parts
prepare.detail: Obtain a new head gasket and new head bolts. Provide clean working conditions so dismantling and surface preparation cannot introduce debris into oil or coolant passages.

steps.title: Prepare the vehicle and fluid systems
steps.body: Follow the [5.2L RH head procedure](#/document/G1800272). Position the vehicle in NEUTRAL on a hoist using the marked lifting points. Release fuel-system pressure and drain the cooling system through the 5.2L procedures before dismantling.

steps.title: Remove the assemblies above and beside the head
steps.body: Remove the intake manifold, RH camshaft and RH exhaust manifold in that order. Follow each linked removal procedure, including its access and timing prerequisites. These are substantial phases of the repair and must be completed before proceeding to the head.

steps.title: Settle the engine onto its mount
steps.body: Install the RH engine-mount bracket, bolts and stud bolts. Using the lifting bracket and support bar, lower the engine onto the RH mount, then remove the support tools. This restores the prescribed support arrangement before the cylinder head is removed.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the head
steps.body: Disconnect the heater hose, camshaft-position sensor connector and cylinder-head-temperature (CHT) connector. Remove and discard the head bolts, lift off the head and discard the gasket. Keep debris out of the newly exposed engine passages.

steps.title: Inspect the joint before reassembly
steps.body: Clean the head and block mating surfaces without metal scrapers, wire brushes, power abrasive discs or other abrasive methods. Clear coolant, oil and foreign material from the block's head-bolt holes with compressed air. Apply the separate head and block distortion procedures to establish whether both faces are suitable for assembly.

steps.title: Install the new gasket and bolts
steps.body: Position the new gasket and head, then install new torque-to-yield bolts. Follow the illustrated bolt order through all tightening stages: 30 Nm, 50 Nm, an additional 90°, then another 90°. The torque settings and angle stages together establish the specified clamping load; old bolts must not be reused.

steps.title: Reconnect and rebuild the surrounding assemblies
steps.body: Reconnect the heater hose, camshaft-position sensor and CHT connector. Reinstall the support tools, raise the RH side of the engine 25 mm and remove the RH mount bracket. Install the RH exhaust manifold, RH camshaft and intake manifold in that order, completing their timing, support and installation requirements.

steps.title: Restore coolant circulation and test
steps.body: Fill and bleed the cooling system using the 5.2L procedure, then road test the vehicle. Complete the filling and bleeding operation before the final operating assessment.

watchFor.title: Scratched or gouged mating faces
watchFor.body: Damage from abrasive cleaning can create a leak path even with a new gasket.

watchFor.title: Liquid or debris in bolt holes
watchFor.body: The holes must be cleared before new bolts are fitted; do not assemble over retained coolant, oil or foreign material.

watchFor.title: Vehicle lifting errors
watchFor.body: Check lifting-point and adapter placement, and never work beneath jack-only support.

notes: Keep the tightening illustration in its shown orientation when identifying bolt positions.

diagnostics.finding: Head or block distortion does not meet the applicable inspection requirements.
diagnostics.meaning: Gasket replacement alone has not established a suitable sealing joint.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the surface condition through the relevant inspection procedure before reassembly.

verification.title: Confirm the rebuild
verification.body: Confirm all head-bolt stages, camshaft installation, heater-hose and sensor connections, and cooling-system filling and bleeding are complete.

verification.title: Record the final results
verification.body: Record head and block inspection results, completion of the tightening sequence and the road-test outcome.

guides.title: Replace the 5.2L primary timing chain tensioners
guides.summary: Replace the applicable primary chain tensioner while preserving the chain’s original alignment with the crankshaft sprocket and variable camshaft timing unit.
guides.introduction: The 5.2L engine uses chain-driven camshafts and hydraulic timing chain tensioners. Its variable camshaft timing (VCT) system changes valve timing during operation. This repair replaces a right-hand or left-hand primary tensioner while retaining the chain’s existing engagement with its sprockets.
guides.why: Removing a tensioner takes away chain support. The chain must remain in its original position at both the crankshaft sprocket and VCT unit; incorrect indexing can cause valve and piston damage. Cleanliness is equally important because debris entering engine passages or the oil pan can cause engine failure.

when.summary: When repair requires replacement of a 5.2L right-hand or left-hand primary timing chain tensioner.
notes: This operation preserves existing chain timing; it is not a substitute for establishing correct timing after chain displacement.

prepare.title: Confirm parts and engine identity
prepare.detail: Use the engine identification information when obtaining replacement parts. Engine displacement alone does not identify every part revision.

prepare.title: Prepare for internal engine work
prepare.detail: Have the capability and equipment required by the engine-front-cover procedure, a clean work area, a vise, a suitable tensioner holding pin, a torque wrench and an angle-measuring tool.

steps.title: Remove the front cover
steps.body: Complete the [5.2L engine front cover removal](#/document/G1800273). Keep foreign material, including debris from gasket-surface cleaning, out of oil passages, coolant passages and the oil pan throughout the repair.

steps.title: Mark and remove the right-hand tensioner
steps.body: If servicing the right-hand side, scribe matching location marks on its chain and VCT unit, then on its chain and crankshaft sprocket assembly. Preserve both relationships while removing the primary tensioner bolts and tensioner.

steps.title: Mark and remove the left-hand tensioner
steps.body: If servicing the left-hand side, make the corresponding chain-to-VCT and chain-to-crankshaft scribe marks before removing its tensioner. Each side needs its own identifiable marks; do not rely on the opposite side’s alignment.

steps.title: Install the left-hand tensioner
steps.body: For the left-hand installation, compress the plunger using an edge of a vise and insert a suitable pin into the housing hole. Verify the crankshaft-to-chain marks, then the VCT-to-chain marks. Install the tensioner and tighten its bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm), followed by 25°. Remove the holding pin.

steps.title: Install the right-hand tensioner
steps.body: Repeat the compression and pinning method for the right-hand tensioner. Verify its crankshaft and VCT scribe-mark alignments before installation. Tighten its bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm), followed by 25°, then remove its holding pin. When both sides are serviced, the installation sequence is left-hand followed by right-hand.

steps.title: Reinstall the front cover
steps.body: After completing the applicable branches of the [tensioner procedure](#/document/G2051731), reinstall the engine front cover through its dedicated procedure. Maintain the same contamination control during closing work.

watchFor.title: Displaced chain marks
watchFor.body: Do not continue tensioner installation if either required pair of scribe marks no longer aligns. Valve and piston damage can result from a changed chain position.

watchFor.title: A holding pin left installed
watchFor.body: Remove each tensioner’s holding pin after its mounting bolts have received both tightening stages.

notes: Only carry out the side-specific branches needed for the tensioner being serviced.

diagnostics.finding: The chain’s scribe marks do not align with the crankshaft sprocket or VCT unit before installation.
diagnostics.meaning: The required check that original chain indexing has been preserved has failed.
diagnostics.next: Stop and establish correct chain alignment before proceeding; installing a tensioner does not correct displaced timing.

verification.title: Record alignment for each serviced side
verification.body: Record confirmation of both chain-to-crankshaft and chain-to-VCT alignment separately for the right-hand and left-hand sides that were serviced.

verification.title: Confirm tensioner and cover completion
verification.body: Confirm completion of both bolt-tightening stages, removal of every installed holding pin and completion of the engine-front-cover installation.

guides.title: Diagnose coolant loss, overheating and slow warm-up on the 2.3L EcoBoost
guides.summary: Use coolant inspection, pressure testing and complaint-specific checks to distinguish leaks, circulation faults and misleading temperature indications.
guides.introduction: The belt-driven pump circulates coolant through the engine, radiator, heater and turbocharger circuits. A thermostat at the lower radiator-hose connection controls radiator flow, while the degas bottle accommodates expansion and removes air. Because this is a cold-side thermostat, its opening can cycle during warm-up before radiator coolant becomes warm enough to keep it open.
guides.why: Temperature complaints can arise from coolant loss, restricted airflow, poor circulation or inaccurate indication. Checking level, condition and fault codes before replacing parts helps distinguish these causes and avoids mistaking normal thermostat behavior for failure.

when.summary: Coolant is disappearing, temperature is too high or low, or the cooling fan or fitted block heater behaves incorrectly.
notes: Apply block-heater and active-grille-shutter checks only when that equipment is fitted.

prepare.title: Cool-system access
prepare.detail: Allow the engine to cool before opening the pressure cap. Use the cooling-system safety procedure and Ford diagnostic methods.

prepare.title: Testing capability
prepare.detail: Have a scan tool, cooling-system pressure tester and adapters, coolant refractometer, nitrite test kit and combustion-gas leak tester. Electrical diagnosis requires suitable probes and a multimeter.

steps.title: Inspect before reproducing the complaint
steps.body: Check cold coolant level, cap installation, leaks, wet cabin flooring, belt and tensioner condition, airflow obstruction and electrical damage. Record codes. Reproduce the condition by running the engine only when coolant is correctly filled and no fail-safe-cooling codes are present.

steps.title: Assess coolant condition and concentration
steps.body: Clear pink or light-red coolant can be normal. Incorrect coolant, rust or stop-leak sediment requires the appropriate flushing and refill route. Suspected Gold coolant contamination needs nitrite testing because orange color may remain unchanged. Oil sheen or milky brown coolant calls for engine investigation. Check acceptable-looking coolant with a refractometer; normal concentration is 48% to 50%, with climate-specific limits in the procedure.

steps.title: Pressure-test the cap and system separately
steps.body: Inspect the cap and bottle sealing surfaces. The cap must hold 145 kPa +/- 21 kPa. Slowly pressurize the system to 124 - 138 kPa and observe for approximately 2 minutes; pressure should remain steady. Repair external leaks. Pressure loss without a visible leak requires internal-leak investigation. Refit the cap to its hard stop.

steps.title: Follow Test A for coolant loss
steps.body: After inspection and pressure testing, check coolant for oil, engine oil for coolant, then test for combustion gases using the tester instructions. Positive findings lead to engine diagnosis; none alone identifies a particular gasket or casting. With these checks passed, Test A identifies the cooling system as operational.

steps.title: Follow Test B for overheating
steps.body: Check powertrain control module (PCM) codes. Without P0217 or P1299, actual overheating is unverified and gauge diagnosis follows. Address applicable grille-shutter codes, obstructions and missing deflectors. Then follow the leak, contamination and fan checks. The fan check uses MAX A/C and HI blower; failure leads to powertrain electrical diagnosis.

steps.title: Distinguish pump and thermostat operation
steps.body: Follow each specified 30-minute run with MAX HEAT. A heater outlet hose that remains cold leads to pump replacement. A hot lower radiator hose leads to gauge diagnosis; a cold one leads to thermostat inspection. Both thermostat-inspection outcomes in Test B call for a new housing; the undamaged-thermostat branch adds radiator replacement if overheating persists.

steps.title: Follow Test C for insufficient warm-up
steps.body: With P0125 or P0128 present, check cold coolant level: low level leads to Test A; correct level leads to thermostat-housing replacement and code clearing. Returning codes require cylinder head temperature (CHT) and engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor checks. Without these codes, investigate the gauge or the fitted manual or dual automatic climate-control system.

steps.title: Handle fan and block-heater complaints
steps.body: Missing fan speeds or continuous operation leads to powertrain electrical diagnosis. Remove fan/shroud debris and retest noise; persistent noise or a detached blade requires a fan assembly. For a fitted block heater, replace a cable with any circuit above 5 ohms, or a heater outside 30 to 40 ohms.

watchFor.title: Hot coolant and protective shutdown
watchFor.body: Never loosen the cap while the engine runs or the system is hot. Fail-safe cooling can restrict output and shut the engine down; it is not permission to continue an overheating test.

watchFor.title: Misleading thermostat bench tests
watchFor.body: Inspect for an unseated valve, debris, broken or distorted parts and wax leakage. Do not force the thermostat open with hot water or another heat source.

notes: Use specified Motorcraft Orange coolant. Concentrate meets WSS-M97B44-D; prediluted coolant meets WSS-M97B44-D2. Use distilled water when mixing concentrate.
For a removed-radiator leak test, clean it first and use clean water and the specified maximum pressure. Water used for copper/brass radiator testing can contain chemicals that damage aluminum.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0217 or P1299 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P0217 reports sensed overheating; P1299 reports activation of overtemperature protection.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test B rather than assuming thermostat failure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0125 or P0128 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P0125 concerns insufficient temperature for closed-loop fuel control; P0128 concerns failure to reach the thermostat monitor's required temperature.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test C, including its coolant-level decision.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0480, P0481 or P1285 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P0480 and P0481 concern fan-control circuits; P1285 reports cylinder-head overtemperature.
diagnostics.next: Use Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis. Route other PCM codes to 2.3L electronic-engine-control diagnosis.

verification.title: Confirm the repair outcome
verification.body: Retest normal operation after correcting an obvious cause. After Test C's thermostat repair, clear codes and investigate sensor operation if they return.

verification.title: Record measurable results
verification.body: Record coolant concentration, cap and system pressure results, leak findings, codes and the final symptom check.
