guides.title: Diagnose coolant loss, overheating and slow warm-up on the 3.7L
guides.summary: Use coolant inspection, pressure testing and complaint-specific checks to distinguish leaks, circulation faults, fan problems and misleading temperature indications.
guides.introduction: The 3.7L cooling system uses a belt-driven pump to circulate coolant through the engine, radiator and heater circuit. Its thermostat controls radiator flow, while the degas bottle accommodates expansion and removes air. Diagnosis follows three main paths: coolant loss, overheating, or failure to reach operating temperature. Separate checks address fan and optional block-heater complaints.
guides.why: This engine has a cold-side thermostat at the lower radiator hose connection. It can cycle during warm-up before remaining open, so an initially cool hose does not establish failure. Coolant level, contamination, airflow and temperature indication must also be checked before replacing parts.

when.summary: When coolant disappears, temperature is abnormal, cooling codes are stored, or fan or block-heater operation is suspect.
notes: Use block-heater and active-grille-shutter branches only where the relevant equipment is fitted.

prepare.title: Start with a cold system
prepare.detail: Never loosen the pressure cap while the engine is running or the cooling system is hot. Read the cooling-system safety precautions before pressure testing or opening the system.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool, cooling-system pressure tester with cap and bottle adapters, coolant refractometer, nitrite test kit and combustion-gas tester. Electrical complaints require appropriate circuit-testing capability and Ford diagnostic knowledge.

prepare.title: Use the specified coolant
prepare.detail: The specified materials are Motorcraft Orange concentrate meeting WSS-M97B44-D or prediluted coolant meeting WSS-M97B44-D2. Use distilled water for mixture adjustment.

steps.title: Verify the complaint and inspect first
steps.body: Check cold coolant level, cap installation and stored codes. Inspect hoses, joints, housings, radiator, pump, degas bottle, heater core and engine sealing areas for damage or leakage. Check belt condition, tensioner, fan wiring and airflow. Note steam, coolant odor, wet interior flooring, unusual exhaust smoke and oil/coolant contamination. Initial running reproduction requires correct filling and no fail-safe cooling codes. Repair obvious faults and test normal operation before continuing.

steps.title: Assess coolant condition and concentration
steps.body: Clear coolant changing from orange to pink or light red is acceptable. Incorrect coolant requires chemical flushing. Suspected Gold coolant contamination needs a nitrite test because appearance may remain unchanged; detected nitrite requires flushing and refilling. Sediment, darker orange debris or rusty brown coolant also require flushing. Oil sheen or milky brown coolant needs engine investigation, with pressure testing for suspected oil entry. If appearance is acceptable, measure concentration: the recommended range is 48%–50%. Follow the stated climate-specific limits; strengthen with concentrate, dilute with distilled water, and top up with the specified mixture.

steps.title: Pressure-test the cap and system correctly
steps.body: Inspect cap and bottle threads, seals and sealing surfaces; replace defective parts. Test the cap separately to its specified holding pressure. Using the bottle adapter, slowly pressurize the system to 124–138 kPa (18–20 PSI) and observe for approximately 2 minutes. Pressure should hold. Investigate any drop for external or internal leakage. Do not exceed the specified maximum or pump rapidly. After a satisfactory test, remove the equipment and tighten the cap to its hard stop.

steps.title: Follow Test A for coolant loss
steps.body: After inspection, correct the cold level and pressure-test for external leaks. If none appear, inspect coolant for engine oil or transmission fluid, inspect engine oil for coolant, then use the combustion-gas tester according to its instructions. Engine oil in coolant, coolant in engine oil, or detected combustion gases directs engine diagnosis. If all Test A checks are negative, that test identifies the cooling system as operational.

steps.title: Establish the overheating route in Test B
steps.body: Run the powertrain control module (PCM) self-test. Without P0217 or P1299, actual overheating remains unverified; check temperature-gauge operation and route other codes appropriately. With a confirmed overheating code, inspect front-end damage, condenser/radiator obstructions and missing air deflectors. Continue through level, pressure, internal-leak, combustion-gas and coolant-condition checks. Relevant active-grille-shutter codes require their separate diagnosis where fitted.

steps.title: Check fan operation and circulation in order
steps.body: After the preceding Test B checks, select MAX A/C and HI blower with the engine running. An inoperative fan requires the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis procedure. B11 and B12 each specify a 30-minute engine run before selecting MAX HEAT and assessing their hose. A cold heater outlet hose at B11 directs pump replacement. At B12, a hot lower radiator hose directs gauge diagnosis; a cold hose leads to thermostat inspection. B13 directs thermostat replacement whether damage is visible or not. On its no-visible-damage branch, continued overheating after replacement directs radiator replacement.

steps.title: Follow Test C for inadequate warm-up
steps.body: After initial inspection, check for P0125 or P0128. If neither is present, the test identifies the cooling system as operational and directs suspected gauge or climate-control faults to their own procedures. With either code present, check cold coolant level: low coolant returns to Test A; correct level directs thermostat replacement. Clear codes after that repair. If the code returns, check cylinder head temperature (CHT) sensor operation.

steps.title: Use the specified component inspections
steps.body: Thermostat replacement must follow Test B, Test C or visual inspection. Inspect the removed thermostat for an unseated valve, trapped material, damaged frame or spring, wax leakage and distortion; remove debris or broken pieces when replacing a damaged unit. Do not test it with hot water or another heat source. A removed radiator must be cleaned and leak-tested in clean water at its specified maximum pressure. Never reuse water used for copper/brass radiator testing.

steps.title: Address separate fan and block-heater complaints
steps.body: Missing fan speeds, incorrect operation or continuous running follow the electrical diagnostic route. For noise, remove foreign material and retest; persistent noise or a detached blade requires a new fan assembly. For an inoperative block heater, check all three power-cable circuits: any resistance above 5 ohms directs cable replacement. Heater resistance outside 30–40 ohms directs heater replacement.

watchFor.title: Escalating overtemperature warnings
watchFor.body: Fail-safe cooling can reduce cylinder operation and eventually stop the engine. Stop the engine when overheating warnings indicate it is approaching critical limits.

watchFor.title: A distinctive 3.7L leak location
watchFor.body: Oil or coolant leaking from the front-left weep hole behind the generator indicates a channel-cover gasket failure. The channel cover plate requires replacement through the engine repair procedure.

notes: Use the Diagnostic Methods prerequisites, including electrical-system checks and preliminary inspection, before interpreting test results.
Use the radiator test's specified maximum pressure; do not substitute the separate cap-test specification.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0125 or P0128 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P0125 concerns insufficient temperature for closed-loop fuel control; P0128 concerns failure to reach the thermostat monitor's expected operating temperature.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test C, including the coolant-level decision.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0217 or P1299 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P0217 records sensed engine overtemperature; P1299 records cylinder-head overtemperature protection activation.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test B without assuming a thermostat or pump has failed.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0480 or P0481 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These identify Fan 1 and Fan 2 control-circuit concerns respectively.
diagnostics.next: Use Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1285 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A cylinder-head overtemperature condition has been recorded.
diagnostics.next: Use the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis route specified for this code.

diagnostics.finding: Other PCM diagnostic trouble codes are retrieved.
diagnostics.meaning: They require the engine-controls diagnostic route rather than an assumed cooling-component replacement.
diagnostics.next: Use the 3.7L Electronic Engine Controls procedure.

verification.title: Confirm normal operation after correction
verification.body: Recheck coolant level, condition and concentration as applicable, and test the system for normal operation before advancing to further diagnosis.

verification.title: Record the measured result
verification.body: Retain retrieved codes, pressure-test observations and concentration readings. For the Test C thermostat repair, record whether the code returns after clearing; recurrence requires the CHT sensor check.

guides.title: Diagnose coolant loss, overheating and slow warm-up on the 5.0L
guides.summary: Use coolant inspection, pressure testing and the correct symptom branch to distinguish leaks, circulation faults and misleading temperature indications.
guides.introduction: The belt-driven coolant pump moves heat from the engine toward the radiator and heater core. A cold-side thermostat controls radiator flow, while the degas bottle accommodates expansion and removes air. This diagnosis separates coolant loss, excessive temperature and poor warm-up before committing to replacement parts.
guides.why: The cold-side thermostat can cycle during warm-up before staying open, so an early cool hose is not enough to condemn it. Low coolant, trapped air, gauge faults and climate-control problems can also imitate other cooling faults.
searchTerms: engine takes too long to warm up

when.summary: Coolant is disappearing, temperature is abnormal, or cooling codes, fan problems or block-heater concerns are present.

prepare.title: Begin with a cold cooling system
prepare.detail: Never loosen the pressure cap with the engine running or the system hot. Pressurized coolant and steam can escape forcefully.

prepare.title: Prepare diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use Ford diagnostic methods, a scan tool, appropriate electrical test equipment, a pressure tester with cap and bottle adapters, refractometer, nitrite test kit and combustion-gas tester. Complete the battery and charging prerequisites before electrical diagnosis.

prepare.title: Use the specified coolant
prepare.detail: Use the specified Motorcraft Orange coolant and distilled water where mixing is required. Follow the 5.0L draining, vacuum-filling and bleeding procedure after coolant service.

steps.title: Establish the complaint and inspect first
steps.body: Check the cold level and cap installation, record powertrain control module (PCM) diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), and inspect leaks, damaged components, belt drive, airflow, fan wiring and sensor connections. Reproduce the running complaint only with correct coolant fill and no fail-safe-cooling codes. Correct obvious faults and retest before proceeding.

steps.title: Evaluate coolant condition and concentration
steps.body: Clear pink or light-red coolant can be a normal change from orange. Incorrect coolant requires chemical flushing; suspected Motorcraft Gold contamination needs nitrite testing because appearance may remain normal. Rust or sediment requires flushing. Oil sheen or milky-brown coolant also requires engine-leak investigation. Check acceptable-looking coolant with a refractometer: normally maintain 48%–50%, observing the specified climate exceptions. Correct weak mixture with concentrate, strong mixture with distilled water.

steps.title: Test the cap and system separately
steps.body: Inspect the cold cap and bottle sealing surfaces. Replace damaged parts, or parts contaminated by coolant expelled through the cap, as directed. The cap must hold 145 kPa ±21 kPa. Slowly pressurize the system to 124–138 kPa and observe for approximately 2 minutes without pressure loss. Repair visible leaks; unexplained loss requires internal-leak checks. Refit the cap to its hard stop.

steps.title: Follow Test A for coolant loss
steps.body: After inspection and pressure testing, check coolant for oil, engine oil for coolant, then use the combustion-gas tester according to its instructions. Any positive internal-leak finding leads to engine diagnosis. If the sequence finds no external leak, fluid crossover or combustion gases, Test A identifies the cooling system as operational.

steps.title: Start Test B by verifying overheating
steps.body: Without P0217 or P1299, actual overheating is unverified: investigate gauge operation and other engine codes. With the relevant code, check front-end damage, radiator/condenser obstruction and missing air deflectors. Continue through level, pressure, fluid-crossover, combustion-gas and coolant-condition checks. Then select MAX A/C and high blower speed; an inoperative fan requires the electrical fan diagnostic route.

steps.title: Separate pump, thermostat and radiator concerns
steps.body: After earlier Test B checks pass, follow its separate 30-minute MAX HEAT checks. A cold heater outlet hose directs pump replacement; a hot outlet advances to the lower-radiator-hose check. A hot lower hose directs gauge diagnosis. A cold lower hose leads to thermostat inspection and replacement. In the undamaged-thermostat branch, continued overheating after replacement directs radiator replacement.

steps.title: Follow Test C for inadequate warm-up
steps.body: For P0125 or P0128, check the cold coolant level. Low coolant returns to Test A; correct level directs thermostat replacement and code clearing. A returning code requires cylinder-head temperature (CHT) sensor checks. Without these codes, investigate a suspected gauge or fitted climate-control fault instead of assuming the thermostat has failed.

steps.title: Address fan and optional block-heater complaints
steps.body: Fan speed faults or continuous running require Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis. For noise, remove foreign material and retest; persistent noise or a detached blade requires a new fan assembly. For a fitted block heater, any of its three cable circuits above 5 ohms requires a new cable; heater resistance outside 30–40 ohms requires a new heater.

steps.title: Use the correct removed-component tests
steps.body: Inspect thermostat seating, foreign material, frame, spring and wax reservoir. Remove loose debris and replace a damaged thermostat; do not test it using hot water or another heat source. Clean a removed aluminum radiator before leak-testing in clean water, never water used for copper/brass radiators. Obtain the applicable specification-table pressure limit before that bench test.

watchFor.title: Fail-safe warnings
watchFor.body: A red-zone indication and powertrain warning can progress to restricted operation and shutdown. Do not continue running into these warnings to reproduce the complaint.

watchFor.title: Evidence away from the radiator
watchFor.body: Wet cabin flooring or coolant odor warrants heater-core inspection. Excessive white or light-gray exhaust and fluid contamination warrant internal-leak investigation.

notes: Use the active-grille-shutter diagnostic branch only when that equipment is fitted.
Use 5.0L electronic-engine-control diagnostics for other PCM codes, and the climate-control procedure matching the installed controls.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0125 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: Required temperature for closed-loop fuel control was not reached in time.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test C, beginning with inspection and coolant level.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0128 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The thermostat monitor did not see the required operating temperature in time.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test C; the code alone does not establish a failed thermostat.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0217 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The CHT sensor indicated engine overheating.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test B to establish the cause.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1299 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: Cylinder-head overtemperature protection became active.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test B and investigate the overheating condition.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0480 or P0481 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The code concerns the fan 1 or fan 2 control circuit, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Use Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1285 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: A cylinder-head overtemperature condition was detected.
diagnostics.next: Follow the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis route specified by the code chart.

verification.title: Confirm operation after correction
verification.body: Recheck coolant condition, concentration and cold level, then test for normal operation under the original complaint conditions when safe. Complete the prescribed filling and bleeding after opening the system.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record code results, coolant concentration, pressure-test results and the branch that identified the cause. After Test C repairs, a returning code requires the specified CHT investigation.

guides.title: Diagnose coolant loss, overheating or slow warm-up on the 5.2L
guides.summary: Separate coolant leakage, poor heat rejection, slow warm-up and misleading temperature indications before choosing a repair.
guides.introduction: The belt-driven coolant pump circulates coolant through the engine, radiator and heater core. A temperature-operated thermostat controls radiator flow, while the degas bottle accommodates expansion and removes air. Diagnosis checks whether coolant is contained, circulating correctly and transferring heat to the outside air.
guides.why: This engine uses a cold-side thermostat at the lower radiator hose connection. It can cycle during warm-up until radiator coolant becomes warm enough to hold it open. An early hose-temperature check can therefore mislead, and an unusual gauge reading alone does not establish overheating.
searchTerms: engine does not reach operating temperature

when.summary: Use when coolant disappears, temperature seems abnormal, cooling warnings appear or the electric fan behaves incorrectly.
notes: Reproduce the complaint only with the coolant correctly filled and no fail-safe cooling codes present.
Active grille shutter diagnosis applies only where that equipment is fitted.

prepare.title: Start with a cold system
prepare.detail: Switch the engine off and allow it to cool before opening the pressure cap. Hot coolant and steam can escape forcefully even when the cap is loosened slightly.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of powertrain control module (PCM) self-tests, a coolant refractometer, pressure tester with suitable cap and bottle adapters, combustion-gas tester and nitrite test kit. Running-engine and electrical checks require Ford diagnostic competence.

prepare.title: Use the specified coolant
prepare.detail: Use Motorcraft Orange prediluted coolant VC-3DIL-B, specification WSS-M97B44-D2, or concentrate VC-3-B, specification WSS-M97B44-D, mixed with distilled water.

steps.title: Establish the complaint and inspect
steps.body: Follow [Inspection and Verification](#/document/G1807367). Check cold coolant level and cap installation, then record diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Inspect hoses, joints, housings, radiator, pump, bottle and engine plugs for leakage or damage. Include heater-core odor or wet flooring, airflow restrictions, drive belt and tensioner condition, fan wiring and sensor connections. Correct obvious faults and retest before continuing.

steps.title: Distinguish harmless color changes from contamination
steps.body: Clear pink or light-red coolant can be normal. Murky discoloration, sediment or rust requires investigation and flushing; incorrect coolant requires chemical flushing. Suspected Motorcraft Gold contamination needs a nitrite test because appearance may remain normal. Oil sheen or milky-brown coolant leads to engine-leak diagnosis. If appearance is acceptable, measure concentration: normally 48% to 50%, with climate exceptions in the procedure. Correct weak mixture with concentrate and strong mixture with distilled water.

steps.title: Follow Test A for coolant loss
steps.body: Inspect the cold cap and bottle sealing surfaces; replace defective components or a cap contaminated by expelled coolant as directed. Test the cap separately at 145 kPa ± 21 kPa. Slowly pressurize the system to 124–138 kPa and observe for approximately 2 minutes; pressure should remain steady. Repair external leaks. With no external leak, inspect coolant for oil, engine oil for coolant, then test for combustion gases according to the tester instructions.

steps.title: Confirm overheating before following Test B
steps.body: P0217 or P1299 directs Test B toward cooling-system checks. Without either code, overheating is unverified: investigate gauge operation and route other codes appropriately. Check front-end damage, radiator/condenser obstruction and missing air deflectors, then coolant level, pressure retention, fluid cross-contamination, combustion gases and coolant condition in sequence.

steps.title: Check fan operation and coolant circulation
steps.body: At B10, select MAX A/C with the blower at HI; a non-operating fan requires electrical diagnosis. B11 specifies a 30-minute engine run, followed by MAX HEAT and a heater-outlet-hose temperature check; a hose that is not hot directs pump replacement. B12 separately specifies a 30-minute run and MAX HEAT before checking the lower radiator hose. A hot lower hose directs gauge diagnosis; otherwise continue to thermostat inspection.

steps.title: Inspect the thermostat and follow the resulting repair path
steps.body: Look for an unseated valve, lodged material, damaged frame or spring, and a leaking or bulging wax reservoir. Remove loose debris or broken pieces. Do not heat-test the thermostat in water. B13 directs replacement whether visible damage is found or not; after the undamaged-thermostat branch, continued overheating directs radiator replacement. Thermostat replacement must follow Test B, Test C or visual inspection.

steps.title: Follow Test C for inadequate warm-up
steps.body: P0125 concerns insufficient temperature for closed-loop fuel control; P0128 concerns failure to reach the thermostat monitor's expected temperature. With either code, check cold coolant level. Low level returns to Test A; correct level directs thermostat replacement and code clearing. If the code returns, check cylinder head temperature (CHT) sensor operation. Without these codes, investigate the gauge or the fitted climate-control system.

steps.title: Use the separate removed-radiator test when needed
steps.body: Clean the radiator before immersion testing in clean water. Never use water previously used to test copper/brass radiators: residual chemicals can damage aluminum. Establish the specified maximum test pressure before applying air; do not substitute the cap-test criterion.

watchFor.title: Escalating temperature warnings
watchFor.body: Fail-safe power reduction or a flashing powertrain warning demands a safe stop. Do not continue a warm-up test into an overheating event.

watchFor.title: Pressure loss without a visible leak
watchFor.body: This can indicate an internal engine leak. Oil/coolant mixing, unusual white exhaust or detected combustion gases requires engine diagnosis.

notes: The degas bottle carries the pressure cap; there is no radiator cap.
Restore coolant using the applicable flushing, vacuum-filling and bleeding procedures after contamination correction or cooling-system repairs.

diagnostics.finding: Test A finds no external leak, fluid cross-contamination or combustion gases.
diagnostics.meaning: The coolant-loss routine reaches its operational conclusion.
diagnostics.next: Record the negative findings; investigate a different remaining complaint through its own routine.

diagnostics.finding: P0480, P0481 or P1285 is stored.
diagnostics.meaning: These codes route to Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis, rather than directly proving a failed fan or sensor.
diagnostics.next: Follow that diagnostic route; send other PCM codes to Electronic Engine Controls.

diagnostics.finding: The fan is noisy, continuously running or missing a speed.
diagnostics.meaning: Noise can come from foreign material or the motor; incorrect operation requires circuit diagnosis.
diagnostics.next: Remove foreign material and retest noise. Persistent noise or a detached blade requires a new fan assembly; electrical operating faults follow Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis.

verification.title: Confirm the corrected condition
verification.body: Test for normal operation after correcting an identified cause. After pressure testing, remove the tester and install the bottle cap to its hard stop.

verification.title: Record the outcome
verification.body: Record pressure retention, coolant concentration, relevant leak-test findings and DTC results, including whether a warm-up code returns after clearing.

guides.title: Flush cooling-system contamination — 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Remove cooling-system deposits using aluminum-safe cleaner and the correct radiator and engine backflushing route for each engine.
guides.introduction: Coolant carries engine heat to the radiator, where it passes to the outside air. Rust, sludge and other deposits reduce cooling efficiency. Flushing combines chemical cleaning with water flow through the radiator and engine to loosen and remove this material. The hose connections and thermostat arrangements differ between engines, so selecting the correct route matters as much as selecting the cleaner.
guides.why: Reversed or pulsating flow loosens sediment more effectively than steady flow in the normal direction. However, flushing pressure can damage the radiator, and opening a hot system can release scalding coolant. Water left after flushing also affects the final coolant mixture; the 5.0L procedure specifically requires a concentration measurement and correction.

when.summary: When rust, sludge or other foreign material requires removal from the cooling system.
notes: Overheating alone does not establish that contamination is the cause.
This is condition-based cleaning, not a stated periodic service interval.

prepare.title: Cool the system before opening it
prepare.detail: Never loosen the pressure cap while the engine is running or the cooling system is hot. Allow it to cool again if the cleaner’s operating instructions have heated it.

prepare.title: Control pressure and collect waste
prepare.detail: Keep radiator internal pressure at or below 138 kPa (20 psi). Collect used coolant and flushing water containing antifreeze or cleaner for disposal under applicable requirements.

steps.title: Apply cleaner and drain
steps.body: Use the specified Motorcraft cleaner, which is suitable for aluminum radiators, and follow its package directions. Then drain through the engine-specific cooling-system procedure. Choose the complete flushing route for the [2.3L](#/document/G1673125), [3.7L](#/document/G1694550), [5.0L](#/document/G1694584) or [5.2L](#/document/G1807370).

steps.title: Backflush the radiator through the correct opening
steps.body: For the 2.3L and both V8s, disconnect the upper and lower radiator hoses and introduce flushing water through the lower radiator opening. The 3.7L instead requires radiator removal: orient it with the upper hose connection at the top and flush through that upper connection. Maintain the radiator pressure limit throughout.

steps.title: Open the engine flushing route
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove the thermostat housing; its thermostat and housing are serviced together. On the 3.7L and 5.2L, remove the thermostat and reinstall the coolant inlet connection without it before flushing. On the 5.0L, remove the thermostat and coolant inlet connection, leaving the connection off for the engine flush.

steps.title: Backflush the engine
steps.body: Introduce water through the lower radiator hose on the 2.3L. Use the upper radiator hose on the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L. These routes are engine-specific. After flushing the 5.0L, reinstall its coolant inlet connection without the thermostat as directed before proceeding to thermostat installation.

steps.title: Restore the cooling circuit
steps.body: Reinstall the 2.3L thermostat housing assembly or the separate thermostat on the other engines using the applicable removal-and-installation procedure. Reinstall the 3.7L radiator. Reconnect the radiator hoses on the other engines, then complete the correct engine-specific filling and bleeding procedure to restore coolant circulation.

steps.title: Measure and correct the 5.0L mixture
steps.body: Compensate for flushing water remaining in the system. Idle the engine for 5 minutes to mix coolant and water, then measure concentration with a coolant/battery refractometer or similar instrument. Observe the cool-system opening precaution when sampling or adjusting. Use concentrated coolant to reach the specified concentration; do not substitute an assumed mixture.

watchFor.title: Persistent heavy deposits
watchFor.body: Severe contamination may need a cooling-system pressure flusher when solvent cleaning is insufficient. This does not remove the radiator pressure limit.

watchFor.title: Premature conclusions during V8 warm-up
watchFor.body: The 5.0L and 5.2L cold-side thermostats can open and close repeatedly during warm-up before remaining open. That behavior alone does not establish a blockage.

notes: The 5.0L concentration check is an explicit final phase of its flushing procedure; no concentration percentage is supplied here.

diagnostics.finding: Chemical cleaning does not remove severe contamination effectively.
diagnostics.meaning: Solvent treatment alone is insufficient.
diagnostics.next: Use the specified pressure-flushing method with suitable equipment and controlled radiator pressure.

diagnostics.finding: The 5.0L mixture is too dilute after flushing.
diagnostics.meaning: Residual flushing water has affected coolant concentration.
diagnostics.next: Adjust with concentrated coolant to the engine’s specified concentration.

verification.title: Confirm the circuit is restored
verification.body: Confirm thermostat or housing installation, radiator and hose reconnection, and completion of the applicable filling and bleeding procedure.

verification.title: Record the measured 5.0L result
verification.body: Record the refractometer concentration and any correction made, separately from noting that filling and bleeding are complete.

applicability.equipment: Motorcraft Premium Cooling System Flush; controlled water supply and backflushing equipment; coolant and contaminated-water collection equipment; tools for the applicable radiator, hoses and thermostat work; engine-specific filling and bleeding equipment. A coolant/battery refractometer is required for the 5.0L concentration check.

guides.title: Backflush the Heater Core and Restore the Cooling System
guides.summary: Clean the heater core with the specified cooling-system flush, rinse thoroughly and complete the engine-specific filling and bleeding procedure.
guides.introduction: The heater core transfers heat from engine coolant to cabin air. Coolant must circulate through its passages for that heat transfer to work. Backflushing cleans those passages against the normal direction of flow, after which the cooling system must be rinsed, refilled and cleared of air.
guides.why: The cleaning chemical, water rinse and final coolant fill are separate stages. Leaving out the rinse leaves cleaning material in the circuit; leaving out bleeding can leave air where coolant needs to circulate. Opening a hot system also exposes you to pressurized steam and coolant.

when.summary: When heater-core cleaning is indicated during investigation or repair of a coolant-flow concern.
notes: Weak cabin heat alone does not establish that the heater core is restricted.

prepare.title: Let the engine cool
prepare.detail: Do not open the pressure relief cap while the engine is running or the cooling system is hot.

prepare.title: Arrange the complete cooling-system service
prepare.detail: Have Premium Cooling System Flush, water for thorough rinsing, and the equipment and refill materials required by the fitted engine's draining, vacuum filling and bleeding procedure.

steps.title: Partially drain the cooled system
steps.body: Follow the appropriate draining procedure for the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L. Establish this access before introducing cleaner; the job begins with a partial cooling-system drain.

steps.title: Select and use the specified flush
steps.body: Backflush the heater core with Premium Cooling System Flush, following its package directions. The 3.7L and 5.2L procedures explicitly name Motorcraft Premium Cooling System Flush VC-1. The 2.3L and 5.0L procedures direct product selection through their engine cooling specifications.

steps.title: Rinse thoroughly with water
steps.body: After the chemical cleaning stage, thoroughly flush with water before refilling. This removes the cleaning material from the core and completes the required preparation for the final coolant fill.

steps.title: Fill and bleed for the fitted engine
steps.body: Complete the matching Engine Cooling System Draining, Vacuum Filling and Bleeding procedure. Treat air removal as part of the repair, because filling the reservoir alone does not establish that the coolant circuit has been properly filled.

watchFor.title: Hot, pressurized coolant
watchFor.body: Even slight loosening of a hot pressure cap can release steam and liquid forcefully.

watchFor.title: An incomplete rinse
watchFor.body: Do not proceed to the final coolant fill before the thorough water-flushing stage is complete.

notes: On the 5.0L and 5.2L, the cold-side thermostat can cycle during warm-up. Early warm-up behavior alone is not evidence of a restricted heater core.

verification.title: Confirm the cleaning sequence
verification.body: Confirm that package-directed chemical cleaning was followed by a thorough water rinse.

verification.title: Confirm cooling-system restoration
verification.body: Complete all filling and bleeding requirements in the corresponding engine procedure.

guides.title: Replace the engine block heater on the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L
guides.summary: Drain the correct cooling system, replace the block heater and restore its protected wiring route before filling and bleeding.
guides.introduction: The block heater uses electrical heat to warm the engine through its coolant. Removing it opens the cooling system, so the repair includes coolant draining and a complete filling and bleeding stage. The 2.3L additionally requires starter motor removal for access; the 3.7L and 5.0L procedures proceed directly to the heater after draining.
guides.why: The heater must be tightened correctly at its coolant connection, and its wiring must remain secured away from hot or rotating components. Correct filling and bleeding restores the cooling circuit after the opening has admitted air. A nearby coolant leak should be located accurately before assuming the heater is responsible.

when.summary: When a block-heater fault has been established or heater removal is required for related repair work.
notes: Select coolant-service instructions by engine, even though the heater tightening specification is shared.

prepare.title: Prepare for coolant service
prepare.detail: Have the matching engine’s draining, vacuum filling and bleeding procedure available, together with its required equipment and coolant specifications. Follow its precautions before opening the cooling system.

prepare.title: Prepare electrical and access work
prepare.detail: Ensure the heater is disconnected from its power supply. For the 2.3L, follow the starter procedure’s preparation requirements before removing the starter; this prerequisite is part of the access work.

steps.title: Drain the matching cooling system
steps.body: Use the coolant procedure for the [2.3L](#/document/G1673124), [3.7L](#/document/G1694549) or [5.0L](#/document/G1694583). Complete draining before disconnecting and removing the heater.

steps.title: Create access on the 2.3L
steps.body: Remove the starter motor using the [2.3L starter procedure](#/document/G1673178), including its prerequisites. The 3.7L and 5.0L heater procedures do not specify starter removal.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the heater
steps.body: Observe how the heater wiring is routed and secured, then disconnect its electrical connector. Remove the block heater using the correct engine procedure. Use the illustration for your selected engine to identify the connector and heater location.

steps.title: Install the heater and restore its wiring
steps.body: Install the heater and tighten it to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm), as specified for each of these engines. Reconnect the electrical connector and secure the wiring away from rotating or hot components. Reinstall the starter on the 2.3L by reversing its removal procedure.

steps.title: Fill and bleed the system
steps.body: Complete the engine-specific filling and bleeding procedure after reassembly. Follow that procedure’s full sequence so the cooling system is restored after heater removal.

watchFor.title: Wiring exposed to heat or movement
watchFor.body: A connected plug is not enough: the heater wiring must also be routed and secured away from hot and rotating parts.

watchFor.title: A different leak source on the 3.7L
watchFor.body: Oil or coolant at the front-left weep hole behind the generator points to the channel cover plate’s sealing system, not automatically to the block heater.

notes: The replacement sequence does not establish an electrical diagnosis; heater performance testing requires the applicable diagnostic information.

diagnostics.finding: Oil or coolant leaks from the 3.7L weep hole behind the generator.
diagnostics.meaning: The cooling-system description identifies a failed channel cover plate gasket and requires replacement of the plate.
diagnostics.next: Follow the applicable engine repair path for the channel cover plate instead of treating this location as evidence for heater replacement.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical and wiring completion
verification.body: Verify the heater was tightened to specification, its connector is attached and its wiring is secured clear of the stated hazards. Confirm starter reinstallation on the 2.3L.

verification.title: Record coolant-service completion
verification.body: Record the engine variant and completion of its filling and bleeding procedure, keeping that result distinct from any separate heater electrical test.

guides.title: Replace the coolant pump on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Replace the coolant pump with the correct engine-specific seals, tightening sequence, belt protection and cooling-system filling procedure.
guides.introduction: The belt-driven coolant pump circulates coolant through the engine so heat can be carried away. On the V8 systems described here, coolant also feeds a separate heater circuit. Pump replacement opens the cooling system and disturbs the accessory drive, so the repair includes resealing the pump, restoring the drive and removing air during filling. Access and fastening differ by engine.
guides.why: Coolant must be kept off the drive belts. Removed pump seals must be renewed, and the V8 pump must enter its cavity straight: rotating it after insertion can damage the O-ring and cause leakage. Engine-specific tightening and bleeding are essential to completing the repair correctly.

when.summary: When diagnosis or inspection establishes that the coolant pump or its sealing joint requires repair.
notes: Overheating alone does not establish pump failure.
Select the engine procedure before ordering seals or applying tightening values.

prepare.title: Provide cooling-system service capability
prepare.detail: Have the engine-specific draining, vacuum-filling and bleeding procedure and its required equipment available before opening the cooling system.

prepare.title: Prepare seals and coolant
prepare.detail: All engines require a new pump O-ring; the 3.7L also requires a new gasket. V8 heater outlet tube transfer requires a new tube O-ring. Lubricate seals with the specified clean Motorcraft Orange coolant, VC-3-B, WSS-M97B44-D.

prepare.title: Prepare drive and hose tools
prepare.detail: Have waterproof plastic for belt protection, suitable torque tools and angle-tightening capability where required. The V8 procedures specify a hose clamp remover/installer.

steps.title: Select the engine branch and drain
steps.body: Use the complete pump procedure for the [2.3L](#/document/G1673128), [3.7L](#/document/G1694559), [5.0L](#/document/G1694591) or [5.2L](#/document/G1807373). Drain through that engine's cooling-system procedure before removing pump connections.

steps.title: Clear the intake and loosen the pulley bolts
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove the engine appearance cover and retainers first. Remove the air cleaner outlet pipe on every engine using its matching cross-reference. Loosen the coolant pump pulley bolts before moving or removing the accessory belt.

steps.title: Release the drive and protect the belts
steps.body: On the 2.3L, turn the tensioner counter clockwise and position the accessory belt aside, then completely cover both the accessory and air-conditioning belts with waterproof plastic. On the other engines, remove the accessory belt through its dedicated procedure and completely cover the air-conditioning compressor belt.

steps.title: Remove the remaining access components
steps.body: On the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L, remove the thermostat housing before removing the pump pulley. Remove the pulley on every engine. On the V8s, disconnect the heater outlet hose and release the clamp to disconnect the lower degas-bottle hose from the heater outlet tube.

steps.title: Remove the pump and renew the seals
steps.body: Remove the pump bolts and pump. Discard its O-ring; on the 3.7L, discard the gasket as well. For V8 new-component installation, remove the heater outlet tube and discard its O-ring. Refit the tube with a new coolant-lubricated O-ring and tighten its bolt to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). Clean and inspect the V8 pump sealing surface for debris or damage.

steps.title: Install using the correct engine method
steps.body: Fit a new pump O-ring lubricated with clean specified coolant, plus the new gasket on the 3.7L. The 2.3L pump bolts tighten to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). The 3.7L's seven bolts require the illustrated sequence, first 89 lb.in (10 Nm), then 45°. For either V8, align the bolt holes before inserting the pump straight into its cavity; do not rotate it once inserted. Tighten V8 pump bolts first to 177 lb.in (20 Nm), then 60°.

steps.title: Restore hoses, pulley and accessory drive
steps.body: Reconnect the V8 heater and degas-bottle hoses and position the clamp. Install the pulley bolts finger tight. Refit the thermostat housing where removed, remove the belt protection and reinstall the accessory belt. On the 2.3L, turn the tensioner counter clockwise to return the belt. Finally tighten pulley bolts to 20 Nm on the 2.3L, 24 Nm on the 3.7L or 25 Nm on either V8.

steps.title: Refill and complete the engine branch
steps.body: Reinstall the air cleaner outlet pipe. On the 2.3L, refit the appearance cover and retainers using their separate specified fastener torques. Fill and bleed through the matching engine procedure. The 5.2L procedure additionally requires a road test.

watchFor.title: Twisting a V8 pump into place
watchFor.body: Rotation after insertion can damage the new O-ring and create a leak.

watchFor.title: Coolant reaching a belt
watchFor.body: Position and fully protect the specified belts before exposing the pump area to remaining coolant.

watchFor.title: Rising temperature after repair
watchFor.body: On the V8s, overheating warnings can progress to restricted operation and engine shutdown. Do not continue operating an overheating engine.

notes: The V8 heater outlet tube transfer is conditional on new-component installation.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0125 or P0128 on a 5.0L or 5.2L.
diagnostics.meaning: These codes relate to thermostat monitoring; they do not prove coolant pump failure.
diagnostics.next: Investigate thermostat and cooling-system operation before deciding on pump replacement.

diagnostics.finding: P1285 or P1299 on a 5.0L or 5.2L.
diagnostics.meaning: These indicate overheating and escalation of fail-safe cooling, rather than identification of a failed pump.
diagnostics.next: Establish and rectify the overheating cause. Use a scan tool to clear the applicable fault after repair as required to extinguish the malfunction indicator.

verification.title: Confirm engine-specific assembly
verification.body: Confirm the required new seals, correct pump and pulley tightening, restored hoses and clamps, and removal of belt protection.

verification.title: Record completion of filling and testing
verification.body: Record the engine variant and completion of its filling and bleeding procedure. For the 5.2L, also record the required road-test result.

guides.title: Replace the cooling fan motor and shroud using the correct engine procedure
guides.summary: Remove and refit the fan assembly with engine-specific intake access and the additional coolant work required on the 2.3L.
guides.introduction: The electric cooling fan moves air through the radiator, and its shroud directs that airflow. The motor and shroud are removed together after clearing intake components and the coolant degas bottle. Access differs between engines: the 2.3L procedure also opens the upper radiator hose and requires draining, filling and bleeding the cooling system.
guides.why: Choosing the correct engine sequence avoids unnecessary coolant disturbance and ensures enough access to remove the assembly. Harness retainers are equally important: they keep the wiring in its intended position around the fans. An overheating complaint alone does not establish that the fan assembly needs replacement.
searchTerms: cooling fan motor and shroud replacement

when.summary: When fan assembly replacement has been justified or the motor and shroud must be removed for related access.
notes: Identify the engine before selecting the intake-removal and coolant-service instructions.

prepare.title: Select the access route
prepare.detail: Use the separate fan procedure for the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L. The 5.2L begins with the outlet pipe; the other procedures begin intake removal with the air cleaner.

prepare.title: Plan the 2.3L coolant work
prepare.detail: Have the complete draining, vacuum filling and bleeding procedure available before opening the system, including its equipment and handling precautions.

prepare.title: Workshop capability
prepare.detail: Engine-specific intake and fan access; torque tools. The 2.3L additionally requires a hose clamp remover/installer and the equipment specified for cooling-system draining, vacuum filling and bleeding.

steps.title: Drain first where required
steps.body: On the 2.3L, drain the cooling system through [the applicable coolant procedure](#/document/G1673124) before removing intake components. The supplied 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L fan-removal sequences do not call for draining.

steps.title: Clear the intake components
steps.body: On the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L, remove the air cleaner followed by its outlet pipe, using the matching engine references. On the 5.2L, remove the outlet pipe first and then the air cleaner; follow the outlet-pipe reference within that engine’s fan procedure.

steps.title: Move the bottle and release the harness
steps.body: Remove the degas bottle bolts and position the bottle aside. Disconnect the fan electrical connectors and detach the wiring harness retainers so the assembly can be removed without pulling on its wiring.

steps.title: Release and remove the fan assembly
steps.body: On the 2.3L, use a hose clamp remover/installer to release the clamp and disconnect the upper radiator hose. For every engine, remove the fan mounting bolts and then remove the cooling fan motor and shroud.

steps.title: Reinstall in reverse order
steps.body: Refit the assembly and tighten the mounting bolts to the applicable specification. Restore the upper radiator hose on the 2.3L, reconnect the fan wiring and secure its retainers. Refit the degas bottle and intake components in reverse removal order.

steps.title: Complete the coolant stage
steps.body: On the 2.3L, fill and bleed the cooling system using the same engine-specific coolant procedure. This is a required completion stage after the radiator hose has been opened.

watchFor.title: Loose fan wiring
watchFor.body: Restore the harness retainers as well as the electrical connectors; the illustrated routing belongs to the 2.3L procedure.

watchFor.title: Escalating overheat warnings
watchFor.body: On the 5.0L and 5.2L, the described fail-safe strategy can progress from warnings to cylinder deactivation and engine shutdown. Stop rather than continuing to run an overheating engine.

notes: Positioning the degas bottle aside is common to all four procedures; disconnecting the upper radiator hose is specified only in the 2.3L sequence.

diagnostics.finding: P0125 or P0128 on the described 5.0L or 5.2L cooling system.
diagnostics.meaning: These diagnostic trouble codes concern thermostat monitoring, not direct confirmation of a failed fan.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the indicated cooling-system concern before authorizing fan replacement.

diagnostics.finding: P1285 or P1299 on the described 5.0L or 5.2L system.
diagnostics.meaning: Overheating or fail-safe operation has been detected; the code does not identify the fan as the cause.
diagnostics.next: Address the overheating cause and rectify the fault before clearing the diagnostic trouble code.

verification.title: Check restored connections
verification.body: Confirm the fan and bottle fasteners are tightened, electrical connectors and harness retainers are restored, and the intake components are installed.

verification.title: Record engine-specific completion
verification.body: Record the engine variant and, for the 2.3L, completion of radiator-hose reconnection and the full filling and bleeding procedure.

guides.title: Replace the coolant degas bottle on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Isolate and empty the degas bottle, disconnect its hoses, replace it and restore the specified coolant mixture and level.
guides.introduction: The degas bottle holds surplus coolant, accommodates expansion, helps remove air and provides the cooling system's service-fill point. It also participates in system pressurization. Replacing it therefore involves more than exchanging a container: its hose connections, pressure cap and final coolant fill all need to be restored correctly.
guides.why: Hot coolant remains hazardous under pressure, and even slightly loosening the cap can release steam and liquid forcefully. Clamping the lower hose before emptying the bottle limits coolant movement through that connection. Selecting the correct engine procedure keeps hose access and component positioning tied to the actual installation.

when.summary: When the degas bottle requires removal or replacement after the cooling concern has been assessed.
notes: Coolant loss or overheating alone does not identify the bottle as the failed component.

prepare.title: Allow the engine to cool
prepare.detail: Do not open the cooling system while the engine is running or the system is hot. The 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures additionally require a thick cloth over the cap while releasing pressure.

prepare.title: Prepare the specified equipment
prepare.detail: Have a fluid suction gun, locking pliers and a hose clamp remover/installer, together with tools for the mounting bolts.

prepare.title: Identify the correct refill
prepare.detail: The procedures specify Motorcraft Orange concentrated coolant VC-3-B, WSS-M97B44-D, or Orange prediluted coolant VC-3DIL-B, WSS-M97B44-D2. Establish the recommended mixture and fill level before emptying the bottle; concentrate and prediluted coolant require different preparation.

steps.title: Select the engine-specific route
steps.body: Use the matching removal and installation procedure: [2.3L](#/document/G1673131), [3.7L](#/document/G1694561), [5.0L](#/document/G1694593) or [5.2L](#/document/G1807375). Their overall sequence is shared, but their illustrations show the relevant hose layout and access.

steps.title: Open the cooled system
steps.body: Once the engine and cooling system have cooled, remove the pressure relief cap. Apply the thick-cloth precaution required for the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L branches.

steps.title: Isolate and empty the bottle
steps.body: Clamp the lower degas-bottle hose using the specified locking pliers, then siphon coolant from the bottle with the fluid suction gun. Emptying it before disconnecting the hoses reduces the coolant remaining in the component being handled.

steps.title: Release the upper connections and mountings
steps.body: Use the hose clamp remover/installer to release the upper-hose clamps and disconnect the hoses. Remove the bottle mounting bolts so it can be repositioned for lower-hose access.

steps.title: Disconnect the lower hose
steps.body: Position the bottle as shown for the selected engine. Release the lower-hose connection with the hose-clamp tool and remove the bottle.

steps.title: Install and refill
steps.body: Reverse removal, reconnecting the lower hose and restoring the bottle mountings and upper connections. Tighten the mounting bolts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Release the temporary lower-hose clamp. Fill with the recommended coolant mixture to the specified level and restore the pressure cap.

watchFor.title: Heat or pressure before opening
watchFor.body: A pressure cap must not be loosened on a running engine or hot system. Allow cooling before proceeding.

watchFor.title: A temporary clamp left installed
watchFor.body: The lower-hose isolation is temporary; reverse that operation when restoring the cooling connections.

notes: Use the illustration for your selected engine to identify the lower-hose connection.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical restoration
verification.body: Check that all disconnected hoses and their clamps are restored, the temporary clamp is removed and the mounting bolts have received the specified torque.

verification.title: Confirm the refill
verification.body: Verify the coolant product, mixture and final fill level against the selected engine's requirements, and confirm the pressure cap is installed.

guides.title: Replace the radiator using the correct engine-specific sequence
guides.summary: Remove and refit the radiator while preserving the different refrigerant, charge-air and cooler arrangements for each engine.
guides.introduction: The radiator transfers heat from engine coolant to outside air. It sits beside other heat exchangers, so replacing it involves more than disconnecting coolant hoses. The 2.3L procedure removes the air-conditioning condenser and takes out the radiator with the charge air cooler (CAC). The 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures position the condenser aside, with additional differences in transmission-cooler attachments.
guides.why: Choosing the correct sequence protects neighboring systems and keeps their installation requirements intact. On the turbocharged engine, debris entering open air passages can damage the turbocharger compressor vanes. The cooling system must also be filled and bled correctly after the radiator is installed.
searchTerms: 2.3L radiator and charge air cooler removal

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies a radiator requiring replacement or another repair requires its removal.
notes: Overheating alone does not establish that the radiator has failed.
Identify the engine and any fitted transmission cooler before beginning.

prepare.title: Prepare coolant and fan access
prepare.detail: Have a hose clamp remover/installer and the equipment and capability required by the engine-specific draining, vacuum-filling, bleeding and fan/shroud procedures.

prepare.title: Arrange 2.3L refrigerant service
prepare.detail: The 2.3L procedure requires R1234YF refrigerant recovery before disconnection. Arrange the referenced recovery, evacuation and charging capability, new O-ring seals and the specified seal lubricant.

prepare.title: Protect open passages
prepare.detail: For 2.3L work, prepare to seal disconnected refrigerant openings and cover open turbocharger air-system ports. Inspect and clean intake components before reassembly.

steps.title: Recover refrigerant where required, then drain coolant
steps.body: On the 2.3L, recover refrigerant first using the procedure referenced in its radiator instructions. For every engine, drain coolant using its matching cooling-system procedure below. Keep the engine-specific instructions with the job through refilling.

steps.title: Disconnect the lower connections
steps.body: On the 2.3L, disconnect and seal the condenser outlet line, disconnect the CAC inlet tube and boost-pressure sensor connector, release the lower radiator hose, then disconnect the CAC outlet tube. On the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L, release the lower radiator hose at this stage.

steps.title: Remove the fan and upper connections
steps.body: Use the matching fan/shroud procedure. Remove the radiator sight shield on the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L. On the 2.3L, disconnect and seal the compressor outlet line, then disconnect the upper coolant hose. On the other engines, disconnect both the upper radiator hose and upper coolant hose.

steps.title: Release the upper mounts and condenser
steps.body: Remove the upper radiator support fasteners and brackets, then position the radiator toward the engine. Release the condenser's upper tabs. Remove the condenser on the 2.3L; position it aside on the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L.

steps.title: Release the applicable transmission-cooler attachment
steps.body: If equipped, remove the cooler mounting bolts and position the transmission fluid cooler aside on the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L. On the 5.2L, the specified conditional action is removal of the transmission cooler tube bracket bolt.

steps.title: Remove the radiator
steps.body: Remove the radiator on the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L. On the 2.3L, remove the radiator and CAC together, then remove the bolt and separate them using the illustrated [2.3L procedure](#/document/G1694534).

steps.title: Reassemble and complete fluid service
steps.body: Reverse the selected engine's removal sequence, applying its fastener and connection specifications. On the 2.3L, install new O-ring seals lubricated only with the specified material and complete the referenced refrigerant-service process. Fill and bleed the cooling system using the matching engine procedure.

watchFor.title: Illustration access
watchFor.body: Several illustrations show the front bumper removed for clarity. That note does not add bumper removal to these radiator procedures.

watchFor.title: Turbocharger contamination
watchFor.body: Even small particles can damage compressor vanes. Keep open ports covered and inspect and clean the affected components before installation.

notes: The selected radiator procedure contains installation details within its removal steps; use those details during reassembly.

diagnostics.finding: A 5.0L or 5.2L has thermostat-monitor codes P0125 or P0128.
diagnostics.meaning: These codes relate to monitored thermostat operation and do not establish a radiator failure.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the cooling-system diagnosis before selecting radiator replacement.

verification.title: Confirm the complete installation
verification.body: Confirm restoration of the hoses, clamps, mounts, fan assembly and variant-specific connections disturbed during removal. For the 2.3L, include the boost-pressure connector, CAC tubes and new refrigerant seals.

verification.title: Record fluid-service completion
verification.body: Record completion of the correct engine's filling and bleeding procedure and, for the 2.3L, the required refrigerant service. Coolant addition alone does not complete the specified filling and bleeding phase.

guides.title: Replace the thermostat housing using the correct engine procedure
guides.summary: Drain the cooling system, replace the thermostat housing with the engine-specific sealing arrangement, then refill and bleed the system.
guides.introduction: The thermostat housing forms the coolant connection around the temperature-controlled valve that governs flow through the radiator. Housing service opens the cooling circuit and disturbs its seals and hose connections. The 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L share that purpose, but their access, seals and fastening methods differ.
guides.why: A seal that is suitable for inspection and possible reuse on one engine may require mandatory replacement on another. The 3.7L also uses a staged torque-and-angle tightening sequence. Protecting the accessory belts prevents coolant contamination, and completing the correct filling and bleeding procedure restores the coolant circuit after it has been opened.

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies a thermostat-housing or housing-seal repair requiring removal.
notes: A thermostat monitoring code alone does not establish that the housing needs replacement.

prepare.title: Prepare cooling-system service
prepare.detail: Use the engine-specific draining, vacuum filling and bleeding procedure, including its precautions and required equipment. Have a hose clamp remover/installer and appropriate torque tools.

prepare.title: Prepare seals and belt protection
prepare.detail: Have the applicable housing seal available. The 3.7L requires a new O-ring; the 5.0L and 5.2L require new housing gaskets. Prepare waterproof plastic for the accessory belts on those three engines.

steps.title: Drain the correct cooling circuit
steps.body: Complete the draining stage of the procedure for the actual engine before opening the housing or hoses. Keep the same engine-specific procedure available for final filling and bleeding.

steps.title: Follow the 2.3L removal branch
steps.body: Remove the engine appearance-cover nuts and cover, then remove the air cleaner. Disconnect the fuel rail pressure sensor electrical connector. Release the clamps and disconnect the lower radiator hose and coolant hose with the clamp tool. Remove the housing bolts and housing, then inspect the O-ring and replace it if necessary.

steps.title: Follow the 3.7L removal branch
steps.body: Remove the air cleaner outlet pipe and completely cover the accessory drive belts with waterproof plastic. Release the coolant-hose clamps and disconnect the hoses. Remove the housing bolts and housing, then discard the removed O-ring.

steps.title: Follow the 5.0L or 5.2L removal branch
steps.body: Remove the applicable air cleaner outlet pipe and completely cover the accessory belts. Disconnect the lower radiator hose from the coolant inlet connection and remove the housing bolts. Lift the upper radiator hose T-connector spring clip until its end reaches the coupling detent, then separate the housing from the T-connector. Discard the housing gasket.

steps.title: Install the engine-specific seal and housing
steps.body: For 2.3L, refit the inspected or replacement O-ring and housing; tighten the bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). For 3.7L, fit a new O-ring lubricated with clean Motorcraft Orange coolant VC-3-B, specification WSS-M97B44-D. Tighten its four bolts in the illustrated sequence to 71 lb.in (8 Nm), then a further 45°. For 5.0L and 5.2L, install a new housing gasket and reverse the housing-removal sequence; housing bolt torque is 89 lb.in (10 Nm).

steps.title: Restore hoses and access components
steps.body: Reconnect the applicable hoses and clamps. On 2.3L, restore the fuel rail pressure sensor connection, air cleaner and appearance cover. On 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L, remove the waterproof belt covering and restore the air cleaner outlet pipe. Complete the V8 quick-connect reassembly through the matching housing procedure.

steps.title: Fill and bleed the system
steps.body: Complete the engine-specific cooling-system filling and bleeding procedure. Use its prescribed process rather than treating housing installation or adding coolant alone as completion.

watchFor.title: Seal rules transferred between engines
watchFor.body: The 2.3L inspection option does not replace the mandatory new O-ring requirement on 3.7L or the new gasket requirement on either V8.

watchFor.title: Coolant on accessory belts
watchFor.body: Maintain the specified waterproof protection while opening the 3.7L and V8 connections, then remove it during reassembly.

watchFor.title: V8 overheating indications
watchFor.body: A red temperature indication or powertrain warning calls for stopping the engine. Fail-safe cooling is not a reason to continue operating an overheating engine.

notes: The 5.0L and 5.2L use a cold-side thermostat at the lower radiator hose connection. Repeated opening and closing during initial warm-up can be normal as cooler radiator coolant reaches it.

diagnostics.finding: P0125 or P0128 is present on 5.0L or 5.2L.
diagnostics.meaning: The thermostat monitor has detected an operating concern; this does not identify a leaking or defective housing by itself.
diagnostics.next: Establish the cooling-system fault before selecting housing replacement.

verification.title: Confirm the sealing and connection work
verification.body: Confirm the correct seal decision, engine-specific fastening method, restored hose connections and removal of any belt protection.

verification.title: Record cooling-system completion
verification.body: Record the engine variant and completion of its prescribed filling and bleeding process.

guides.title: Replace the thermostat on the 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine
guides.summary: Replace the thermostat and its sealing ring, protect the accessory belts from coolant, and restore the cooling system using the engine-specific filling and bleeding procedure.
guides.introduction: The thermostat is a temperature-operated valve that controls coolant flow through the radiator. Replacing it changes the valve that regulates this flow, while a new O-ring seals its housing connection. The three engines follow a similar repair sequence, but intake access and cooling-system servicing must follow the matching engine procedure.
guides.why: A correctly installed thermostat still depends on a sealed connection and properly filled cooling system. Trapped air can interfere with circulation, and coolant spilled onto the accessory belts causes contamination. On the 5.0L and 5.2L, the thermostat sits on the cold side of the circuit, where coolant returns from the radiator; repeated opening and closing during initial warm-up can be normal.

when.summary: When cooling-system diagnosis establishes that the thermostat requires replacement.
notes: A temperature complaint or thermostat-monitor code does not establish the failed component by itself.
The cold-side operating description applies to the supplied 5.0L and 5.2L information.

prepare.title: Arrange cooling-system service
prepare.detail: Have the equipment and capability required by the matching draining, vacuum filling and bleeding procedure. Complete its safety prerequisites before opening the system.

prepare.title: Prepare the seal, coolant and protection
prepare.detail: Have the correct replacement thermostat and new O-ring, waterproof plastic for the belts, and a torque wrench suitable for the connector bolts. The specified coolant is Motorcraft Orange Concentrated Antifreeze/Coolant VC-3-B, WSS-M97B44-D.

steps.title: Drain the cooling system
steps.body: Follow the draining procedure for the installed engine before disturbing the thermostat connection. This controls coolant loss when the housing is opened and establishes the correct route for refilling afterward.

steps.title: Create the correct intake access
steps.body: On the 3.7L and 5.0L, remove the air cleaner outlet pipe. On the 5.2L, remove the air cleaner. Use the corresponding intake procedure rather than assuming these access operations are interchangeable.

steps.title: Cover the accessory belts
steps.body: Completely cover the accessory drive belts with waterproof plastic before opening the coolant connection. Leave no exposed belt surface in the spill area.

steps.title: Remove the thermostat and old seal
steps.body: Remove the connector bolts, detach the coolant inlet connector and remove the thermostat. Discard the O-ring; the installation requires a new seal.

steps.title: Install and seat the replacement
steps.body: Lubricate the new O-ring with clean specified coolant and install it with the thermostat. Fully seat the coolant connection on the thermostat housing before tightening its bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). The bolts should secure an already seated connection.

steps.title: Restore access parts and coolant
steps.body: Reverse the remaining removal operations, removing the belt protection once coolant-spill work is finished. Reinstall the engine-specific intake components, then fill and bleed the cooling system through the matching procedure.

watchFor.title: Connection not fully seated
watchFor.body: An unevenly seated connection can compromise the seal. Correct its seating before applying the specified bolt torque.

watchFor.title: Overheating during assessment
watchFor.body: The 5.0L and 5.2L cooling descriptions identify a red temperature gauge and powertrain warning as reasons to stop the engine. Do not continue running it to wait for the thermostat to open.

notes: Normal cold-side thermostat cycling during warm-up must not be confused with a sticking valve.

diagnostics.finding: P0125 or P0128 on the 5.0L or 5.2L
diagnostics.meaning: The powertrain control module has detected a thermostat-monitor malfunction; the code alone does not isolate the cause.
diagnostics.next: Complete cooling-system diagnosis before selecting replacement as the repair.

verification.title: Confirm the mechanical installation
verification.body: Confirm that a new coolant-lubricated O-ring was installed, the connection is fully seated and the connector bolts received the specified torque.

verification.title: Complete filling and bleeding
verification.body: Finish the engine-specific cooling-system procedure before evaluating warm-up behavior.
