guides.title: Drain, refill and bleed the 5.2L engine cooling system
guides.summary: Recover the coolant, refill with the correct mixture and complete the air-purging sequence using either vacuum or conventional filling.
guides.introduction: Coolant carries heat from the engine to the radiator and also supplies the heater core. The degas bottle provides expansion space, separates air and serves as the filling point. This job restores the coolant supply after draining or repairs, with a controlled bleeding sequence to remove trapped air.
guides.why: The 5.2L engine has a cold-side thermostat that can open and close repeatedly during warm-up before remaining open. Filling the bottle alone does not establish that coolant has circulated throughout the system. Correct concentration, sufficient warm-up and the prescribed purge cycles all contribute to engine protection.

when.summary: After cooling-system draining or repairs, or when contaminated coolant requires replacement.
notes: Clear coolant changing from orange to pink or light red does not, by itself, require replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange safe access and collection
prepare.detail: Use a hoist, drain hose, clean fluid container and thick cloth for the pressure cap. Follow the marked lifting points and clearance precautions; never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare the filling equipment
prepare.detail: Have the ROB75240 coolant/battery refractometer and, for vacuum filling, a cooling-system vacuum tester and refiller. Use the specified Motorcraft Orange coolant and distilled water as required.

steps.title: Cool, lift and drain
steps.body: Allow the engine to cool before opening the system. Cover the expansion-tank cap with a thick cloth while releasing pressure. Put the vehicle in NEUTRAL and position it on the hoist. Remove whichever illustrated underbody shields are fitted, then drain through a hose at the radiator drain valve into a clean container.

steps.title: Establish the correct mixture
steps.body: Measure concentration before adjusting it. The normal target is 48/52 to 50/50 coolant to distilled water. Use VC-3DIL-B prediluted coolant, specification WSS-M97B44-D2, to maintain that range; use VC-3-B concentrate, specification WSS-M97B44-D, and/or distilled water for other corrections. After flushing, prepare the mixture from concentrate and distilled water.

steps.title: Choose one filling route
steps.body: Close the radiator drain valve. For vacuum filling, reinstall the shields and follow the filler manufacturer's instructions to fill and bleed. Without a vacuum filler, disconnect the heater inlet hose and fill the degas bottle until coolant emerges from the heater inlet tube. Reconnect the hose, reinstall the shields and fill the bottle to MAX FILL.

steps.title: Perform the initial purge
steps.body: Tighten the degas-bottle cap to its hard stop and switch the climate control off. Run the engine at 3,500 rpm for 30 seconds, then switch it off and wait 1 minute to allow large air pockets to purge.

steps.title: Check the initial level safely
steps.body: Allow cooling before opening the cap; the timed pause does not make a hot system safe to open. The initial level instruction uses the top of MAX FILL when warm or the top of MIN FILL LEVEL when cold. Adjust as necessary and secure the cap before running again.

steps.title: Warm through and complete the purge cycles
steps.body: Idle until normal operating temperature and until the cooling fan has cycled on at least once, the specified indication of a fully open thermostat. Complete five cycles consisting of 3,500 rpm for 30 seconds, idle for 30 seconds, then engine off for 1 minute.

steps.title: Finish the refill
steps.body: Allow the engine to cool before reopening the system. Complete the final level check, topping up to MAX FILL if necessary, and reinstall the pressure-relief cap.

watchFor.title: Concentration outside the permitted limits
watchFor.body: Extreme-climate adjustments must remain between 40% and 60% coolant. Too much reduces overheat protection; too little reduces freeze and corrosion protection.

watchFor.title: Temperature continuing to rise
watchFor.body: An overheating warning calls for stopping the engine, not continuing the purge sequence.

notes: Do not mix coolant types or add alcohol, methanol or brine. Ford does not recommend recycled coolant for this system; clean recovered coolant is a separate reuse provision.
An in-vehicle drain recovers less than 80% of system capacity, so concentration must be measured rather than assumed.

diagnostics.finding: Coolant is dirty, rusty or contaminated.
diagnostics.meaning: It is unsuitable for reuse.
diagnostics.next: Replace it and recycle or dispose of the recovered fluid correctly.

diagnostics.finding: A non-specified coolant has been used.
diagnostics.meaning: Correct corrosion protection cannot be assumed.
diagnostics.next: Carry out the required chemical flushing procedure before refilling.

verification.title: Confirm circulation and final fill
verification.body: Confirm the fan-cycle indication, completed purge cycles, final level and secure cap.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record measured concentration and the temperature condition associated with the level check.

procedures.purpose: Complete 5.2L draining procedure, coolant selection, and both vacuum and conventional filling/bleeding branches.
Correct lifting points and hoist-clearance precautions for drain access.

guides.title: Replace fuel injectors through the engine-specific fuel rail procedure
guides.summary: Select the correct fuel rail service path, renew the required injector seals and parts, and complete the prescribed fuel-system restoration.
guides.introduction: Fuel injectors meter fuel supplied by the fuel rail. On every engine covered here, injector service is directed through the fuel rail removal and installation procedure. That direction does not itself require replacing the entire rail: the detailed 2.3L and 3.7L paths include removing injectors from it. The 2.3L additionally requires high-pressure tube replacement and precisely installed lower injector seals.
guides.why: Injector sealing depends on more than fitting the injector back into its socket. The 2.3L lower Teflon seals must remain dry, be sized correctly and enter the head without impact. Support-ring orientation also matters because incorrect installation can cause fuel leakage. The 3.7L uses new O-rings lubricated with clean engine oil, so its sealing method must remain separate.

when.summary: After diagnosis establishes an injector repair need requiring fuel rail service.
notes: These are repair paths, not tests proving an injector has failed.

prepare.title: Prepare for fuel-system work
prepare.detail: Use a technician equipped for the selected engine's fuel-system procedure. The detailed 2.3L and 3.7L paths require fuel-pressure release and battery disconnection before access work.

prepare.title: Prepare 2.3L special tooling
prepare.detail: Have injector remover 310-206, slide hammer 307-005, injector-bore brush 310-205, seal installer 310-207 and Teflon seal sizer 303-1567. The tube installation also requires torque-wrench adapter calculations and torque-and-angle capability.

prepare.title: Prepare required replacement parts
prepare.detail: For 2.3L, provide a new high-pressure tube, rail bolts, injector clips, O-rings, support rings and lower Teflon seals. For 3.7L, provide new injector O-rings.

steps.title: Choose the rail procedure before opening the system
steps.body: Use the dedicated 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L fuel rail procedure linked below. The following detailed branches concern 2.3L and 3.7L. For either V8, obtain its access, sealing, fastening and completion requirements from its own rail procedure.

steps.title: Release pressure and create access
steps.body: For 2.3L and 3.7L, complete the referenced fuel-pressure release and battery-disconnection procedures. Remove the intake manifold on 2.3L or upper intake manifold on 3.7L. On 2.3L, disconnect the high-pressure pump connector and remove the specified pump, drive-unit and brake-vacuum-pump insulators and associated retainers, including the heated oxygen sensor connector retainer.

steps.title: Remove the 2.3L tube and rail
steps.body: Wrap the pump flare nut with a shop towel to absorb residual fuel during loosening. Release the tube supports and flare nuts, then discard the high-pressure tube. Free the rail connector, harness retainers and insulator, and disconnect injector and fuel rail pressure sensor connectors. Clear surrounding dirt with compressed air before extraction. Discard the rail bolts and withdraw the rail along the injector axes.

steps.title: Separate and clean the 2.3L injectors
steps.body: Remove the injectors and discard their clips. If an injector remains in the head, use the specified remover and slide hammer with minimal force; gentle hand movement may free it. Clean the head bores with the injector brush and remove residual fuel and foreign material. Do not brush injector tips or clean them with compressed air.

steps.title: Follow the simpler 3.7L rail branch
steps.body: Disconnect the feed tube using its quick-release coupling procedure. Remove both rail insulators, disconnect injector connectors, and remove the rail bolts and rail. Release the retaining clips and injectors; discard all injector O-rings. Install new O-rings lubricated with clean engine oil and refit the retaining clips and injectors. Install the rail and tighten its bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm).

steps.title: Renew and size the 2.3L seals
steps.body: Discard the O-rings and support rings, noting their orientation. Pull each lower Teflon seal away before carefully cutting it off without marking the injector. Install each new lower seal dry with the arbor and pusher, transferring it immediately to avoid excessive expansion. Seat it fully in its groove. Fit the sizer with its larger opening toward the seal, pushing while turning 180 degrees. Confirm the seal is in the sizing portion; after one minute, turn back 180 degrees and remove the tool.

steps.title: Assemble and seat the 2.3L rail
steps.body: Fit new support rings with the large-diameter step toward the new O-ring, then fit new O-rings and clips. Engage each clip's anti-rotation finger in the rail-cup groove. Keep the lower seals dry. Press the rail into the head by hand without impact, hand-start new bolts 3 and 4, then release the pressing force. Fit the remaining bolts and follow the illustrated sequence: 10 Nm, release to 0 Nm, wait 5 s, tighten to 14 Nm, then add 30°.

steps.title: Install the new 2.3L high-pressure tube
steps.body: Restore the injector and pressure-sensor connections, rail insulator and harness attachments. Fit the new tube with flare nuts and bracket fasteners initially finger tight. Calculate the required wrench setting for the adapter and follow the tube's staged flare-nut tightening and subsequent bracket fastening. Restore the removed insulators, wiring retainers and pump connector; spreading the pump-insulator openings reduces damage risk.

steps.title: Restore the engine and fuel pressure
steps.body: On 3.7L, reconnect injector connectors, both rail insulators and the feed coupling. Restore the applicable intake manifold on each engine, reconnect the battery through its procedure, then pressurize the fuel system using the prescribed engine-specific process.

watchFor.title: Pressure sensor removed from the 2.3L rail
watchFor.body: The fuel rail pressure sensor must be replaced if it is removed from the rail.

watchFor.title: Lubrication carried across branches
watchFor.body: Clean engine oil is specified for the new 3.7L O-rings. The 2.3L lower Teflon seals must not be lubricated.

notes: Use the exact 5.0L and 5.2L rail procedures for those engines; neither detailed branch above supplies their specifications.

diagnostics.finding: Fuel leakage follows 2.3L injector installation.
diagnostics.meaning: Incorrect support-ring orientation is one possible assembly cause, not a confirmed diagnosis.
diagnostics.next: Review the sealing work through the 2.3L rail procedure, including the large-diameter step facing the new O-ring.

verification.title: Confirm sealing and assembly requirements
verification.body: For 2.3L, confirm seal sizing, support-ring orientation, clip engagement and replacement of the specified single-use parts. For 3.7L, confirm all injector O-rings were renewed and lubricated as specified.

verification.title: Record completion
verification.body: Record the engine variant, required parts renewed, and completion of the applicable reassembly and fuel-system pressurization procedure.

guides.title: Replace the fuel pump driver module, including the 5.2L twin-module assembly
guides.summary: Access the fuel pump driver module beneath the rear seat and follow the engine-specific mounting procedure for a single module or the 5.2L pair.
guides.introduction: The fuel pump driver module (FPDM) is part of the pump’s electrical control system. It sits beneath the rear seat cushion on the left-hand side. The 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L procedures service a single mounted module. The 5.2L uses two modules on a bracket, adding an assembly-removal and bracket-disassembly phase.
guides.why: Engine identification matters because the bracket arrangement and tightening specifications differ. The seat cushion also needs deliberate release: pulling it up without pressing its locking tabs can damage them. Restoring the seat includes keeping the seatbelt webbing straight and the belts and buckles available to occupants.

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies an FPDM for replacement or its assembly must be removed for service.
notes: Choose the engine-specific procedure before disconnecting or unfastening the module.

prepare.title: Select the correct installation branch
prepare.detail: Use the [2.3L procedure](#/document/G1673144), [3.7L procedure](#/document/G1691951), [5.0L procedure](#/document/G1692000) or [5.2L procedure](#/document/G1805342). The 5.2L bracket work is a separate branch.

prepare.title: Provide seat access and torque equipment
prepare.detail: Arrange access to the rear cushion’s front locking tabs and have suitable tools for the module retainers and their specified tightening torques.

steps.title: Release and remove the rear seat cushion
steps.body: Follow [Rear Seat Cushion](#/document/G1692168). Move both front seats fully forward. Press in the locking tabs at the front of the rear cushion to release it from the floor, then lift, release and remove the cushion.

steps.title: Remove the single module on 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L
steps.body: For these engines, disconnect the FPDM electrical connector. Remove its retaining nuts and lift out the module. Continue with the single-module installation branch.

steps.title: Remove and separate the 5.2L assembly
steps.body: For the 5.2L, disconnect the FPDM electrical connectors and remove the assembly retainers. Swing the assembly out from beneath the trim panel and remove it. Then remove the module retainers and separate both FPDMs from their bracket.

steps.title: Install the correct module arrangement
steps.body: On 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L engines, install the FPDM and tighten its retaining nuts to 44 lb.in (5 Nm). On the 5.2L, install the modules onto their bracket and tighten those retainers to 71 lb.in (8 Nm); install the assembly and tighten its retainers to 71 lb.in (8 Nm).

steps.title: Reconnect the electrical connections
steps.body: After securing the module or assembly, reconnect the single FPDM connector on the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L, or the FPDM connectors on the 5.2L.

steps.title: Restore the rear seat
steps.body: Install the cushion by reversing its removal procedure. Make sure the seatbelt webbing is not twisted and that the seatbelts and buckles remain accessible to the occupants.

watchFor.title: Seat tabs resisting release
watchFor.body: Press the locking tabs inward before lifting the cushion; forcing it upward risks breaking the tabs.

watchFor.title: Torque transferred between layouts
watchFor.body: Use the specification for the actual engine and mounting location. The single-module specification differs from the 5.2L bracket and assembly specification.

notes: Removing both 5.2L modules from the bracket is part of the assembly procedure; it does not itself establish that both modules are faulty.

verification.title: Mounting branch completed
verification.body: Record the engine branch used and confirm its mounting fasteners were tightened. On the 5.2L, check both the module-to-bracket and assembly-to-vehicle retainers.

verification.title: Connections restored
verification.body: Confirm the electrical connector or connectors have been reconnected before completing seat installation.

verification.title: Occupant access restored
verification.body: Confirm the cushion is reinstalled with untwisted webbing and accessible seatbelts and buckles.

guides.title: Remove and refit the fuel rail on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Service the fuel rail and injector seals through the correct engine branch, preserving its pressure-release, replacement-part and tightening requirements.
guides.introduction: The fuel rail distributes pressurized fuel to the injectors and holds their connections in position. Opening that assembly disturbs seals as well as fuel and electrical connections. The engines share this purpose, but the 2.3L adds a high-pressure tube and dry Teflon injector seals that require dedicated installation and sizing tools.
guides.why: Residual fuel pressure can remain at a connection after the initial pressure-release operation. Dirt, damaged seals or incorrectly oriented support rings can also cause leakage after reassembly. Tightening methods differ by engine, so select one complete engine procedure and retain its sequence throughout the repair.

when.summary: When confirmed rail, injector or seal work requires opening the fuel-rail assembly.
notes: A leak identifies a condition needing investigation; it does not by itself establish that the rail needs replacement.

prepare.title: Fuel-system capability
prepare.detail: Use a technician equipped for the engine's fuel-pressure release, battery isolation, clean assembly and specified torque or torque-angle tightening. The 2.3L tube tightening also requires the torque-wrench adapter calculation.

prepare.title: Required replacement parts
prepare.detail: All branches require new injector O-rings. The 2.3L additionally requires new high-pressure tube, rail bolts, injector clips, support rings and lower Teflon seals. The 5.2L requires replacement strut-tower-brace nuts.

prepare.title: 2.3L special tools
prepare.detail: Prepare slide hammer 307-005 with injector remover 310-206, injector-bore brush 310-205, seal installer 310-207 and Teflon seal sizer 303-1567. Extraction must use minimal force.

steps.title: Release pressure and isolate the battery
steps.body: Follow the pressure-release procedure for the actual engine, then its battery disconnection instructions. The 5.0L and 5.2L procedures specify disconnecting both ground and positive cables. Complete these prerequisites before opening fuel connections.

steps.title: Open access on the 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L
steps.body: On 3.7L, remove the upper intake manifold, disconnect the feed coupling and remove both rail insulators. On 5.0L, remove the optional brace and appearance cover, disconnect the supply coupling, then move heater hoses, supports and vacuum tubing aside and remove the insulators. On 5.2L, detach the harness retainer, discard the brace nuts, remove the brace, move heater hoses and supports, disconnect the supply coupling and move the vacuum assembly aside.

steps.title: Open the 2.3L high-pressure branch
steps.body: Remove the intake manifold, disconnect the fuel-pump connector and remove the pump noise insulator, spreading its openings to reduce damage. Release the heated oxygen sensor connector retainer and the retainers for the pump-drive and brake-vacuum-pump insulators. Remove those insulators. Wrap the pump flare nut with a shop towel while loosening it to absorb residual fuel. Remove the tube hardware and discard the high-pressure tube, then release the rail connector, harness retainers and rail insulator.

steps.title: Remove the rail and separate the injectors
steps.body: Disconnect injector connectors; also disconnect the fuel rail pressure (FRP) sensor on 2.3L and 5.2L, and the actuator vacuum hose on 5.2L. For 2.3L, clear surrounding dirt with compressed air before removal, discard the rail bolts and pull along the injector axes. Remove the injectors and discard their clips; gently extract any injectors left in the head with the specified tools. Clean the injector bores with the bore brush, never the injector tips. For the other engines, remove the retaining bolts, rail, injectors and clips, then discard all injector O-rings.

steps.title: Renew and size the 2.3L injector seals
steps.body: Discard the O-rings and support rings, noting their orientation. Pull each lower Teflon seal away from the injector before carefully cutting it off without scratching the injector. Install new lower seals dry. Transfer each seal immediately from the installer arbor into its groove, confirm seating, then fit the sizer with its larger opening toward the seal while turning it 180 degrees. Confirm the seal is in the sizing portion; after one minute, turn back 180 degrees and remove the tool. Fit new support rings with the large step toward the new O-ring, then fit new O-rings and clips.

steps.title: Renew seals on the other engines
steps.body: On 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L, lubricate new injector O-rings with clean engine oil and install the retaining clips. The 5.2L requires the correct fuel-resistant upper and lower seals; they look similar but are not interchangeable. For 5.0L and 5.2L, fit new clips or reuse undamaged clips after gently squeezing their sides back into shape. Align the injector-retainer flats with the rail-cup flats on those two engines.

steps.title: Install the injectors and secure the rail
steps.body: On 2.3L, engage each clip's anti-rotation finger in the rail-cup groove. Hand-press the rail into the head without impact, start the designated new bolts and release hand pressure before tightening. Follow its complete staged sequence, including torque release and the 5-second wait. The 3.7L uses its specified bolt torque; 5.0L and 5.2L use their torque-plus-angle sequence. Apply the FRP-sensor replacement decisions below before completing assembly.

steps.title: Restore connections, insulation and access parts
steps.body: Reconnect the engine-specific electrical connections and restore the rail insulators where fitted. On 2.3L, install a new high-pressure tube, initially finger-tighten its connections and brackets, then complete the flare-nut stages and bracket tightening using the required adapter calculation. Restore all pump insulators, retainers and the intake manifold. On the other engines, follow their installation order for vacuum tubing, the 5.2L actuator hose, fuel coupling, heater-hose supports and hoses, and intake or cover components. Put displaced 5.0L cover grommets onto the intake manifold before installing the cover. Refit braces where applicable, using new nuts on 5.2L.

steps.title: Reconnect and repressurize
steps.body: Reconnect the battery through its procedure, then pressurize the fuel system using the engine-matched pressure-release procedure's return-to-service instructions.

watchFor.title: Cleaning or lubricating the wrong surface
watchFor.body: Never clean 2.3L injector tips with compressed air or a brush, and never lubricate their lower Teflon seals. Oil lubrication of the other engines' O-rings must not be transferred to those seals.

watchFor.title: Reusing discarded hardware
watchFor.body: Keep the 2.3L tube, rail bolts and clips, and the 5.2L brace nuts out of the reusable-parts group.

notes: Use the selected engine procedure for all torque values and illustrated tightening locations.

diagnostics.finding: The 2.3L FRP sensor has been removed from the rail.
diagnostics.meaning: Removal requires replacement of that sensor.
diagnostics.next: Install a new sensor; do not reuse it.

diagnostics.finding: The 5.2L FRP sensor needs replacement.
diagnostics.meaning: Its branch permits replacement as needed and gives a dedicated sensor torque.
diagnostics.next: Follow the 5.2L sensor installation detail before rail installation.

verification.title: Complete pressure restoration
verification.body: Confirm completion of the correct repressurization routine and check the serviced fuel connections for leakage. Any leakage requires correction.

verification.title: Record engine-specific completion
verification.body: Record the engine branch, renewed seals and mandatory replacement parts, completed tightening sequence and condition after repressurization.

guides.title: Replace the 2.3L EcoBoost high-pressure fuel pump drive unit
guides.summary: Replace the fuel pump drive unit after removing the pump and rear engine-bay obstructions, then restore its sealing faces and staged bolt tightening.
guides.introduction: The high-pressure fuel pump drive unit provides the mechanical drive for the fuel pump. This repair replaces the drive assembly after the pump has been removed. Access also requires battery disconnection, cowl and brace removal, and moving a coolant line aside, so much of the work involves reaching the unit and restoring everything around it.
guides.why: Clean mating faces allow the drive-unit gasket to seal correctly. The mounting bolts require an initial torque followed by an angle stage, making ordinary tightening by feel unsuitable. Brace hardware also needs careful separation: the nuts removed with the optional brace at the beginning are discarded and replaced during installation.

when.summary: When the 2.3L high-pressure fuel pump drive unit has been assessed as requiring replacement.
notes: This replacement procedure does not establish whether a fuel-system complaint is caused by the drive unit.

prepare.title: High-pressure fuel service capability
prepare.detail: Use the linked high-pressure pump procedure for its removal, installation and safety prerequisites before disturbing the pump or its fuel connections.

prepare.title: Access and electrical isolation
prepare.detail: Have the battery-disconnection and cowl-grille procedures available, together with the tools needed for the brace, extension and drive-unit fasteners.

prepare.title: Parts and controlled tightening
prepare.detail: Provide new nuts for the optional brace if fitted. Assess the drive-unit gasket for replacement as necessary, and have torque and angle-tightening capability.

steps.title: Disconnect the battery and optional brace
steps.body: Disconnect both battery cables using the [battery procedure](#/document/G1692356), then release the battery cable retainer. If equipped, remove the initial strut tower cross brace and discard its nuts.

steps.title: Open the cowl access
steps.body: Remove the [cowl panel grille](#/document/G1693246). Next remove the strut tower cross brace bolts and nuts and lift out that brace. Remove the cowl extension bolts and extension to expose the pump area.

steps.title: Remove the pump and move the coolant line
steps.body: Complete the [2.3L high-pressure fuel pump removal](#/document/G1689353). Then remove the coolant-line retaining bolts and position the line aside for drive-unit access; the drive-unit procedure calls for repositioning the line.

steps.title: Remove the drive assembly
steps.body: Remove the drive-unit mounting bolts and lift off the assembly following the [drive-unit procedure](#/document/G1673143). Keep foreign material away from the exposed mating faces.

steps.title: Install the drive unit
steps.body: Make sure the mating faces are clean and free of foreign material. Replace the gasket as necessary. Install the drive unit and tighten its bolts to 15 Nm, followed by a further 60°.

steps.title: Restore the coolant line and pump
steps.body: Return the coolant line to position and tighten its retaining bolts to 12 Nm. Reinstall the high-pressure fuel pump through its own procedure, completing that operation before closing the cowl access.

steps.title: Rebuild the access area
steps.body: Install the cowl extension, then the cross brace and its bolts and nuts, using their individual specifications in the drive-unit procedure. Refit the cowl grille. If fitted, reinstall the optional brace with new nuts. Reconnect the battery cable retainer and both battery cables through the battery procedure.

watchFor.title: Confusing the brace hardware
watchFor.body: Keep the optional brace's discarded nuts separate from the hardware removed later in the access sequence.

watchFor.title: Incomplete bolt tightening
watchFor.body: The drive-unit installation requires both the initial torque and the angle stage.

notes: Gasket replacement is conditional; the procedure does not require automatic replacement in every case.

verification.title: Record the drive-unit tightening
verification.body: Record completion of the 15 Nm and 60° stages, together with whether the gasket was replaced.

verification.title: Confirm restoration
verification.body: Check that the pump installation is complete, the coolant line is secured, both brace stages applicable to the vehicle are restored, and the battery cable retainer and cables are connected.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the 2.3L EcoBoost high-pressure fuel pump drive unit, including access hardware and tightening specifications.
Perform the prerequisite 2.3L high-pressure fuel pump removal and subsequent installation.
Disconnect and reconnect both battery cables.
Remove and reinstall the cowl panel grille for drive-unit access.

guides.title: Replace the 2.3L EcoBoost high-pressure fuel pump
guides.summary: Replace the high-pressure fuel pump while inspecting its drive tappet and renewing the required seal, bolts and fuel tube.
guides.introduction: The high-pressure fuel pump raises fuel pressure for the engine's fuel system. A cam-driven tappet transfers mechanical movement into the pump. Replacement therefore involves both fuel connections and the pump's drive interface: tappet condition, cam-lobe position and controlled bolt tightening all matter to the installation.
guides.why: Fuel pressure must be released before opening the system, and residual pressure in the high-pressure tube needs separate containment. The pump must be installed with its drive lobe at bottom dead center. Required new parts and staged tightening are integral to the repair.

when.summary: When pump replacement is justified, or tappet wear requires inspection of the pump and its drive lobe.
notes: This mechanical replacement procedure does not establish a pump fault from an engine symptom.

prepare.title: Arrange the required capability
prepare.detail: Use a technician equipped for high-pressure fuel work, battery isolation, controlled engine rotation and torque-angle tightening. Have shop towels, clean engine oil and the torque equipment needed for the flare nuts, including adapter-setting calculations.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement items
prepare.detail: Have a new high-pressure fuel tube, pump mounting bolts and pump O-ring seal. If a strut tower cross brace is fitted, its removed nuts must also be replaced.

steps.title: Release pressure and disconnect the battery
steps.body: Complete [Fuel System Pressure Release](#/document/G1671508), then disconnect both battery cables through [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356). Do not loosen fittings or plugs on the pump body; follow the specified hose and tube disconnections.

steps.title: Clear the pump access
steps.body: If a cross brace is fitted, detach the harness retainer, move the positive cable aside, and remove the brace, discarding its nuts. Remove the engine appearance cover, disconnect the pump connector and remove its noise insulator, spreading the openings to reduce damage. Disconnect the supply hose using [Quick Release Coupling](#/document/G1671510).

steps.title: Remove insulation and the high-pressure tube
steps.body: Detach the heated oxygen sensor (HO2S) connector retainer from the pump bracket. Remove the pump-drive and brake-vacuum-pump insulation and their retainers, including the harness retainer. Wrap the pump-end flare nut with a shop towel to absorb residual fuel during loosening. Remove the tube securing nut and bolt, disconnect the flare nuts, and discard the tube.

steps.title: Remove the pump and inspect its drive
steps.body: Remove the pump bracket. Alternately loosen the pump bolts one complete revolution at a time, then discard them and remove the pump. Discard its O-ring and remove the drive tappet. Inspect for flat spots or scoring; if present, inspect the pump and tappet drive lobe and replace components as necessary.

steps.title: Position and lubricate the drive
steps.body: Following [pump installation](#/document/G1689353), turn the crankshaft only clockwise to place the pump cam lobe at bottom dead center (BDC). Lubricate the tappet and drive-unit bore with clean engine oil. Align the tappet notch with the bore groove during installation, then fit and oil a new pump O-ring.

steps.title: Seat the pump evenly
steps.body: Install the pump with new bolts loosely fitted. Alternately tighten each bolt one complete revolution until seated, then apply the specified two-stage torque-and-angle sequence. Reinstall and tighten the pump bracket.

steps.title: Fit the new high-pressure tube
steps.body: Install the new tube with its flare nuts, bracket bolt and bracket nut finger-tight. Calculate the correct torque-wrench setting using the adapter formulas specified in [the pump procedure](#/document/G1689353). Apply its three-stage flare-nut tightening sequence, then tighten the bracket nut and bolt to their respective specifications.

steps.title: Restore insulation and connections
steps.body: Refit both drive-area insulators and their retainers, the harness retainer and HO2S connector retainer. Reconnect the supply hose through the coupling procedure. Refit the pump insulator, spreading its openings, then reconnect the pump connector and install the appearance cover. If fitted, install the cross brace with new nuts and restore the positive cable and harness retainer.

steps.title: Reconnect and pressurize
steps.body: Reconnect both battery cables through the battery procedure. Complete fuel-system pressurization using [Fuel System Pressure Release](#/document/G1671508); this is the final specified service operation.

watchFor.title: Incorrect installation position
watchFor.body: The pump drive lobe must be at BDC before pump installation. Do not turn the crankshaft counterclockwise.

watchFor.title: Reusing discarded items
watchFor.body: The removed tube, pump bolts, O-ring and any removed cross-brace nuts are not installation parts.

notes: Use the tightening stages and adapter calculations in the 2.3L pump procedure; bracket fasteners and flare nuts have separate requirements.

diagnostics.finding: The drive tappet has flat spots or scoring.
diagnostics.meaning: The pump and tappet drive lobe also require inspection.
diagnostics.next: Inspect both and install new components as necessary before reassembly.

verification.title: Record the inspection outcome
verification.body: Record the tappet findings and any resulting pump or drive-lobe replacement.

verification.title: Confirm completion
verification.body: Confirm required new parts, staged tightening, restored connections and insulation, battery reconnection and prescribed fuel-system pressurization.

2.3L fuel-system pressure release before opening connections and pressurization after assembly.

guides.title: Replace the throttle body on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Remove and refit the throttle body using the correct engine-specific access, gasket treatment and fastening method.
guides.introduction: The throttle body contains the electrically controlled valve that regulates air entering the engine. This job replaces or temporarily removes that assembly and restores its sealed connection to the intake. The basic operation is similar across these engines, but access, gasket reuse and bolt tightening differ enough that choosing the correct procedure is essential.
guides.why: Clean sealing faces help prevent unwanted air entering at the joint. Correct bolt tightening secures the housing without treating every engine alike, while properly seated electrical connectors preserve the connection to the throttle actuator.

when.summary: When diagnosis calls for throttle-body replacement, or the assembly must be removed for related work.
notes: Select the engine-specific procedure before ordering the gasket or beginning removal.

prepare.title: Prepare for the correct tightening method
prepare.detail: Have suitable hand tools and torque equipment. The 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures also require controlled angle tightening.

prepare.title: Plan intake access and gasket replacement
prepare.detail: Have a new gasket for the 2.3L or 5.0L. On the 3.7L and 5.2L, inspect the gasket before deciding whether it can be retained.

steps.title: Expose the throttle body
steps.body: On the 2.3L, loosen the inlet-pipe clamp and move the pipe aside. On the 3.7L, remove the air cleaner outlet pipe. On the 5.0L, first remove the engine appearance cover, then the outlet pipe. On the 5.2L, remove the air cleaner using its dedicated procedure.

steps.title: Release wiring and attached retainers
steps.body: Disconnect the throttle-body electrical connector. On the 2.3L, slide its red locking tab rearward, away from the throttle body, then squeeze the connector while removing it. On the 3.7L, also release the brake vacuum hose retainer and the connector-harness retainer from the housing.

steps.title: Remove the housing and assess the seal
steps.body: Remove the retaining bolts and throttle body. Discard the gasket on the 2.3L and 5.0L. On the 3.7L and 5.2L, inspect the gasket and clean or replace it as needed. Make the mating faces clean and free of foreign material before assembly.

steps.title: Install the gasket and tighten for the engine
steps.body: Fit the required gasket and position the throttle body. The 2.3L bolts require 89 lb.in (10 Nm), following the illustrated sequence in its procedure. The 3.7L requires 89 lb.in (10 Nm), then 90°. The 5.0L requires 62 lb.in (7 Nm), then 60°. The 5.2L requires 89 lb.in (10 Nm), then 60°. Keep these instructions with their respective engines.

steps.title: Restore the electrical connection
steps.body: Reconnect the throttle body. On the 2.3L, fully seat the connector before sliding the red lock forward; the lock will not advance on an incompletely installed connector. On the 3.7L, reattach both the brake vacuum hose retainer and wiring-harness retainer.

steps.title: Restore intake access parts
steps.body: Refit the appropriate pipe or air cleaner. Tighten the 2.3L inlet-pipe clamp to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm). Before refitting the 5.0L appearance cover, move any rubber grommets that remained in the cover back onto the intake manifold.

watchFor.title: Similar housings, different instructions
watchFor.body: Gasket reuse and torque-angle settings are engine-specific. Appearance alone is not a reliable guide to either.

watchFor.title: Contaminated mating faces
watchFor.body: Foreign material at the joint can interfere with sealing even when the gasket and bolts are correct.

notes: These are replacement procedures; they do not establish that a throttle body is the cause of an engine-running complaint.

diagnostics.finding: The 2.3L connector's red lock will not slide forward.
diagnostics.meaning: The connector may not be fully installed.
diagnostics.next: Fully seat the connector, then engage its locking tab.

verification.title: Complete the required road test
verification.body: Road test the 2.3L and 5.2L after installation. On the 3.7L and 5.0L, road test when a new throttle body was installed.

verification.title: Record the outcome
verification.body: Record whether the throttle body was renewed and the result of the required road test, including whether the original complaint remains.

guides.title: Diagnose turbocharger smoke, noise, power loss and oil leaks on the 2.3L EcoBoost
guides.summary: Follow four complaint-specific tests to distinguish turbocharger damage from intake, engine, exhaust and oil-pipe faults.
guides.introduction: The turbocharger uses exhaust energy to compress the engine’s incoming air. A charge air cooler (CAC) cools that compressed air before it reaches the intake manifold. Engine oil lubricates the turbocharger bearings and drains back to the sump. This diagnosis establishes which part of that connected system needs attention.
guides.why: Smoke, noise and reduced power do not automatically identify a failed turbocharger. Intake leaks can create noise, restrictions can reduce airflow, and crankcase ventilation carries some oil into the intake normally. Following the appropriate branch avoids replacing a serviceable turbocharger while leaving the actual fault behind.

when.summary: Use when blue exhaust smoke, excessive noise, loss of power or an external oil leak needs diagnosis.
notes: Choose the matching complaint branch; these are alternative diagnostic paths.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool for powertrain self-tests. Noise diagnosis requires the Chassis/Ear, Engine/Ear and accelerometer equipment specified in Test B.

prepare.title: Protect the intake
prepare.detail: Have suitable covers ready for every opened intake port. Small particles can damage compressor vanes; inspect and clean components before reassembly.

steps.title: Test A: establish the blue-smoke complaint
steps.body: Start the engine and observe the exhaust. If blue smoke is absent, pursue an external oil-leak inspection. If present, check the air cleaner, then intake connections and hoses, then crankcase ventilation. Replace a clogged cleaner or repair the identified intake or ventilation fault before moving farther along the branch.

steps.title: Distinguish normal intake oil from an excessive accumulation
steps.body: After the preceding checks pass, inspect inside the intake pipes and hoses. Excessive oil leads to turbocharger inspection at A6. Without excessive oil, continue with internal-engine blue-smoke diagnosis. Oil presence alone does not justify turbocharger replacement.

steps.title: Test B: locate excessive noise
steps.body: Use the specified listening equipment, accelerometers and scan tool to locate the noise. Noise away from the turbocharger goes to engine-noise diagnosis. If nearby, inspect intake and CAC components for leaks, damage, incorrect alignment or loose installation. Repair leaks; otherwise continue through Test C.

steps.title: Test C: begin power-loss diagnosis electronically
steps.body: With ignition on, run the powertrain control module (PCM) self-tests. Diagnose any diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) through the Master DTC Chart. If none are present, inspect the air cleaner; replace it if clogged and check normal operation.

steps.title: Check the airflow path and wastegate
steps.body: Continue Test C through intake leaks, exhaust restrictions or damage, then wastegate condition. Confirm the wastegate linkage moves freely and inspect its actuator. Repair the fault found at each stage; proceed to turbocharger inspection only when these checks pass.

steps.title: Inspect the turbocharger when A6 or C6 directs
steps.body: Follow the intake procedure to remove the air-cleaner outlet pipe and CAC intake pipe. Inspect compressor-wheel damage, free turbine-shaft rotation and wheel-to-housing contact marks. Damage directs replacement through the turbocharger procedure. An undamaged unit redirects diagnosis to internal-engine causes of the original complaint.

steps.title: Test D: trace external oil to its origin
steps.body: Inspect the supply tube first, including both ends, seals and gaskets. Follow oil tracks back to their source because gravity and vehicle movement can spread oil. A leaking supply tube requires a new tube. Otherwise inspect the return tube similarly and replace it if leaking; if neither leaks, continue engine oil-leak diagnosis.

watchFor.title: Oil carried through ventilation
watchFor.body: Positive crankcase ventilation carries oil vapor into the intake. Turbocharger oil-seal failure generally follows bearing failure, often accompanied by noise or seizure.

watchFor.title: Oil on the housing
watchFor.body: An external turbocharger-body leak is unlikely; supply and return tubes, seals and gaskets are more likely sources.

notes: Use the 2.3L procedures for any repair identified by these tests.

diagnostics.finding: No turbocharger damage at A6 or C6
diagnostics.meaning: The inspection has not established a turbocharger replacement need.
diagnostics.next: Follow internal-engine diagnosis for blue smoke or loss of power, respectively.

verification.title: Check the stated repair outcome
verification.body: After replacing a clogged air cleaner, check the system for normal operation as directed.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic endpoint
verification.body: Record the complaint, relevant codes and physical findings, including whether a repair was identified or engine diagnosis remains necessary.

procedures.purpose: Complete 2.3L EcoBoost diagnostic Tests A–D for smoke, noise, power loss and external oil leaks.
Turbocharger operation, lubrication and intake-contamination precautions.

guides.title: Replace the 2.3L EcoBoost turbocharger coolant return tube
guides.summary: Remove the turbocharger coolant return tube, renew its O-ring and restore the cooling system with clean, undamaged sealing surfaces.
guides.introduction: Engine coolant circulates through the turbocharger's center housing to help control heat between the exhaust-driven turbine and the compressor. The return tube connects this coolant circuit to the water outlet adapter. Servicing it involves the tube, its retaining bracket, a sealed connection at the turbocharger and a hose connection, followed by cooling-system filling and bleeding.
guides.why: A new O-ring cannot reliably seal against residue, deep scratches or a damaged tube. The retaining bracket must also sit square to the O-ring area so the connection is not pulled out of alignment. Cleaning and inspection are therefore central parts of this repair, rather than incidental preparation.

when.summary: When a return-tube leak or damage has been identified, or the tube must be removed during turbocharger service.
notes: This procedure applies to the 2.3L EcoBoost coolant return tube.

prepare.title: Arrange cooling-system service
prepare.detail: Have the equipment and capability required by [Engine Cooling System Draining, Vacuum Filling and Bleeding](#/document/G1673124). Complete its draining prerequisites before opening the tube connections.

prepare.title: Prepare sealing and fastening supplies
prepare.detail: Have a hose clamp remover/installer, nylon brush, new coolant-tube O-ring, clean engine coolant and torque tools. The specified cleaner is Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner—VOC Compliant / Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A or PM-4-B.

steps.title: Drain the cooling system
steps.body: Follow the linked 2.3L cooling-system procedure. Draining prepares the circuit for removal of the turbocharger coolant connection.

steps.title: Release the tube and hose
steps.body: Remove the tube bolt, then the clamp bolt and clamp. Disconnect the tube hose using the hose clamp remover/installer, and remove the tube.

steps.title: Inspect the tube and discard its seal
steps.body: Inspect the tube and sealing surfaces. Check that the retaining bracket is not bent and is square to the O-ring area. Clean with the specified brake cleaner and a nylon brush, then remove and discard the old O-ring.

steps.title: Prepare the new seal and mating bore
steps.body: Install a new O-ring and lubricate it with clean engine coolant. Carefully remove old O-ring residue from the turbocharger bore with a nylon brush and rinse it out with the specified cleaner. Inspect for deep scratches or gouges before seating the connection.

steps.title: Position the assembly before tightening
steps.body: Fit the O-ring end to the turbocharger. Fit the hose and clamp and start the tube and clamp bolts finger-tight. Connect the hose end to the water outlet adapter port using the clamp tool. Tighten the tube bolt, then the clamp bolt; each is specified at 89 lb.in (10 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the coolant circuit
steps.body: Complete filling and bleeding through the linked 2.3L procedure. Use [the complete tube procedure](#/document/G1689382) for the installation details and sealing-surface illustrations.

watchFor.title: Metal-brush damage
watchFor.body: Do not use a metal brush on the sealing areas. Scratching these surfaces can cause leaks and repeat repairs.

watchFor.title: Debris entering disturbed intake parts
watchFor.body: If turbocharger air-intake components are removed during access, cover their open ports. Even small particles can damage the compressor vanes.

notes: Lubricate the new O-ring with clean engine coolant.
The removed O-ring is discarded even if the tube itself is reused.

diagnostics.finding: The bracket is bent or not square to the sealing end.
diagnostics.meaning: The tube may not be held in the correct relationship to its seal.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the tube condition before final installation; tightening the bolts is not a substitute for correct alignment.

diagnostics.finding: Residue, deep scratches or gouges are present in the sealing area.
diagnostics.meaning: The connection may leak despite a new O-ring.
diagnostics.next: Remove residue by the prescribed method and resolve sealing-surface damage before assembly.

verification.title: Check sealing and cooling-system completion
verification.body: Confirm the connections remain free of coolant leakage after completing the prescribed filling and bleeding process.

verification.title: Record the repair essentials
verification.body: Record O-ring renewal, the sealing-surface inspection, tightening of both specified bolts and completion of cooling-system filling and bleeding.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost coolant return-tube removal, seal renewal, inspection and installation.
Required 2.3L EcoBoost cooling-system draining before removal and vacuum filling and bleeding after installation.

guides.title: Replace the 2.3L EcoBoost turbocharger coolant supply tube
guides.summary: Renew the turbocharger coolant supply tube and its seal while preserving clean sealing surfaces and restoring the cooling and exhaust connections.
guides.introduction: The turbocharger uses exhaust energy to compress incoming air. Engine coolant circulates through its center housing, helping manage heat between the hot turbine and the compressor. The supply tube carries coolant into that housing. Replacement involves draining the cooling system, opening the nearby exhaust connections, removing the paired coolant tubes, and separating the supply tube from the return tube.
guides.why: Reliable sealing depends on clean, undamaged ports and correctly aligned tube brackets. Old O-ring residue, scratches, or a bent retaining bracket can cause repeat leaks. Any opened intake ports also need protection: even small debris can damage the compressor vanes. Initial finger-tight assembly allows the tube connections to be positioned before final tightening.

when.summary: When inspection establishes that the 2.3L turbocharger coolant supply tube requires replacement.
notes: Coolant near the turbocharger does not by itself distinguish a tube fault from a seal or sealing-surface problem.

prepare.title: Arrange cooling-system service
prepare.detail: Have the capability and equipment required by the linked 2.3L draining, vacuum filling, and bleeding procedure. Complete its draining phase before disconnecting the tubes.

prepare.title: Gather replacement parts and cleaning materials
prepare.detail: Provide a new supply tube, coolant-tube O-ring seal, and turbocharger flange gasket. Have a hose clamp remover/installer, nylon brush, specified Motorcraft brake cleaner, and clean specified engine coolant.

prepare.title: Protect openings and sealing areas
prepare.detail: Keep debris out of the turbocharger and intake system, covering any opened intake ports. Preserve the sealing surfaces of coolant and oil connections throughout the work.

steps.title: Drain the cooling system
steps.body: Follow the 2.3L Engine Cooling System Draining, Vacuum Filling and Bleeding procedure before opening the coolant connections.

steps.title: Release the exhaust-side access
steps.body: Disconnect the heated oxygen sensor (HO2S) electrical connector. Remove the catalytic converter flange nuts and bracket bolts, then remove and discard the turbocharger flange gasket. Remove the turbocharger exhaust studs only if needed.

steps.title: Remove and separate the coolant tubes
steps.body: Remove the coolant-tube bolts and disconnect the hose using the clamp tool, then remove the tubes. Remove their clamp bolt and clamp. Separate the supply tube from the return tube and discard the supply tube.

steps.title: Inspect and clean the sealing components
steps.body: Check the tube and sealing surfaces, including whether the retaining bracket is bent or out of square with the O-ring area. Remove and discard the coolant-tube O-ring. Clean with the specified brake cleaner and a nylon brush; never use a metal brush.

steps.title: Prepare the replacement assembly
steps.body: Install the new O-ring and lubricate it with clean engine coolant. Assemble the supply and return tubes, fitting their clamp and clamp bolt finger tight. Lubricate the tube O-ring seals. Remove old O-ring residue from the turbocharger bore with a nylon brush, rinse with brake cleaner, and inspect for deep scratches or gouges.

steps.title: Seat and secure the tubes
steps.body: Keep the coolant-tube bolts finger tight during positioning. Fit the O-ring ends to the turbocharger with the lower coolant inlet tube entering first, then connect the hose end to the water outlet adapter. Tighten the tube bolts in the procedure’s stated sequence, followed by the clamp bolt. The tube bolts have different tightening specifications.

steps.title: Restore the exhaust connections
steps.body: If removed, reinstall and tighten the exhaust studs. Fit a new turbocharger flange gasket, then install and tighten the catalytic converter flange nuts and bracket bolts to their respective specifications. Reconnect the HO2S connector.

steps.title: Refill and bleed
steps.body: Complete the linked cooling-system filling and bleeding procedure. The tube procedure specifies Motorcraft Orange Concentrated Antifreeze/Coolant; follow the cooling procedure for its preparation and filling method.

watchFor.title: Abrasive cleaning damage
watchFor.body: A metal brush can damage the sealing area and create leaks. Use nylon and the specified cleaner.

watchFor.title: Premature tightening
watchFor.body: Preserve the finger-tight assembly stages and lower-inlet-first insertion sequence rather than tightening each connection as soon as it is encountered.

diagnostics.finding: A retaining bracket is bent, or a sealing area has deep scratches, gouges, or remaining O-ring residue.
diagnostics.meaning: The connection may not align or seal reliably.
diagnostics.next: Remove residue as specified and resolve damaged or misaligned components before reassembly.

verification.title: Confirm the required renewals and reconnections
verification.body: Confirm the new supply tube, O-ring, and flange gasket are installed, the hose and fasteners are secured, and the HO2S connector is reconnected.

verification.title: Record inspection and cooling completion
verification.body: Record the sealing-surface and bracket inspection results and completion of the specified cooling-system filling and bleeding procedure.

procedures.purpose: Replace the 2.3L EcoBoost turbocharger coolant supply tube, including sealing preparation, assembly sequence, and individual fastener specifications.
Drain, vacuum fill, and bleed the 2.3L EcoBoost cooling system before and after tube replacement.

guides.title: Replace the 2.3L EcoBoost turbocharger oil return tube
guides.summary: Move the air-conditioning compressor aside, renew the turbocharger drain-tube sealing connection and restore the engine oil level.
guides.introduction: Engine oil lubricates the turbocharger bearings and helps cool its center housing. The return tube carries that oil back to the sump. This job restores the drain connection and its sealing surfaces; access requires removing the air-conditioning compressor belt and supporting the compressor aside.
guides.why: Old O-ring residue or damage at a sealing port can cause another leak after reassembly. The tube must also be fully seated before its bolts are tightened, so the fasteners secure an already positioned connection rather than draw it into place.
searchTerms: oil leak at turbo drain tube

when.summary: When a confirmed drain-tube or sealing defect requires repair, or the tube must be removed for service.
notes: Oil around the turbocharger does not by itself identify the return tube as the leaking connection.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underbody access
prepare.detail: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, use a hoist following the lifting procedure. Identify the marked lifting points and check adapter and underbody clearances. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare parts, oil and support
prepare.detail: Have new drain-tube bolts, a new O-ring seal, suitable compressor support and a torque wrench. Use clean SAE 5W-30 synthetic blend engine oil, XO-5W30-Q1SP meeting WSS-M2C946-B1, for seal lubrication and any required top-up.

steps.title: Lift the vehicle and remove the belt
steps.body: Follow [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631), then remove the compressor belt using the [2.3L belt procedure](#/document/G1688221). Correct access lets the compressor be moved without working around its installed drive belt.

steps.title: Move and support the compressor
steps.body: Disconnect the air-conditioning compressor electrical connectors and release the wiring-harness retainers. Remove its mounting bolts, then position and support the compressor aside to expose the oil return tube.

steps.title: Remove the drain tube and inspect its ports
steps.body: Remove and discard the drain-tube bolts, then remove the tube. Clean the sealing ports completely of O-ring residue and inspect the sealing surfaces and line for damage. Follow the [tube procedure](#/document/G1689384) for the connection arrangement.

steps.title: Lubricate, seat and secure the tube
steps.body: Lubricate the new O-ring with clean specified engine oil. Install the tube and make sure it is fully seated before running down the new bolts. Tighten the drain-tube bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the compressor and oil level
steps.body: Position the compressor and tighten its mounting bolts to 18 lb.ft (25 Nm). Reconnect its electrical connectors and harness retainers, reinstall the belt through its dedicated procedure, then check and top off the engine oil as necessary.

watchFor.title: A tube that will not seat
watchFor.body: Do not use bolt tightening to pull an unseated tube into its sealing port. Establish correct seating before fastener rundown.

watchFor.title: Contamination or damaged sealing surfaces
watchFor.body: Pay particular attention to oil-feed, drain and coolant sealing ports encountered during turbocharger work. Residue and damage can cause leaks and repeat repairs.

notes: If turbocharger air-intake components are opened during associated work, cover their ports to keep debris away from the compressor vanes.

diagnostics.finding: O-ring residue or damage is present at a drain-tube sealing port.
diagnostics.meaning: The connection cannot be relied on to seal correctly in that condition.
diagnostics.next: Remove residue and resolve sealing-surface or line damage before installing the tube.

verification.title: Confirm the restored connections
verification.body: Confirm full tube seating, installation of new bolts, correct fastener tightening and restoration of the compressor, belt, connectors and wiring retainers.

verification.title: Confirm engine oil level
verification.body: Check the engine oil after reassembly and top off as necessary with the specified oil.

guides.title: Replace the 2.3L EcoBoost turbocharger oil supply tube
guides.summary: Replace the turbocharger oil supply tube and its oil filter while protecting the intake and restoring clean, fully seated oil connections.
guides.introduction: The turbocharger uses exhaust energy to compress incoming air. Engine oil lubricates its sleeve bearings and helps cool the center housing before returning to the sump. The supply tube carries that oil into the turbocharger. Replacing it involves opening both the oil connection and nearby intake plumbing, so the job combines careful sealing work with strict protection against foreign material.
guides.why: Small particles entering the intake can damage the compressor vanes. Residue or damage at an oil connection can prevent sealing and cause another leak. The replacement tube must also be fully seated before its fasteners are tightened: the bolts secure the connection, rather than pull a poorly aligned tube into place.

when.summary: When the turbocharger oil supply tube has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Oil near the turbocharger calls for locating the leak; it does not by itself identify the supply tube as the cause.

prepare.title: Have both replacement parts ready
prepare.detail: Obtain a new oil supply tube assembly and a new turbocharger oil filter. Both removed items must be discarded.

prepare.title: Prepare for clean assembly
prepare.detail: Have clean engine oil, protection for open intake ports and suitable fastener tools. Use the 2.3L engine specifications for oil selection and topping up.

steps.title: Open the intake access
steps.body: Remove the [air cleaner outlet pipe](#/document/G1675706). Cover exposed intake openings as components come off so dirt cannot reach the compressor.

steps.title: Move the outlet plumbing clear
steps.body: Disconnect the turbocharger bypass-valve electrical connector and detach its harness retainers. Loosen the turbocharger outlet-pipe clamps and remove the pipe, following the [tube replacement procedure](#/document/G1689385).

steps.title: Remove the old tube and filter
steps.body: Remove the oil supply tube retaining bolts, then remove and discard the complete tube assembly. Remove and discard the turbocharger oil filter as well; reusing it is specifically prohibited.

steps.title: Inspect the sealing connections
steps.body: Make sure the exposed sealing ports are completely clean, free from O-ring residue and undamaged. Inspect and clean removed intake components as necessary before reassembly. A damaged sealing surface must be addressed rather than concealed by tightening the connection harder.

steps.title: Install and seat the replacement parts
steps.body: Install the new turbocharger oil filter and lubricate the O-ring seal with clean engine oil. Fully seat the new supply tube and start its retaining bolts finger tight. Tighten the bolts in the procedure's stated order, using the separate specification assigned to each fastener.

steps.title: Restore the intake and oil level
steps.body: Install the turbocharger outlet pipe and tighten its clamps. Reconnect the bypass valve and secure the harness retainers, then reinstall the air cleaner outlet pipe. Check and top off the engine oil using the [2.3L specifications](#/document/G1660452).

watchFor.title: Debris in open ports
watchFor.body: Even small intake debris can damage the compressor. Keep openings protected throughout the repair.

watchFor.title: A tube that will not seat
watchFor.body: Stop and correct alignment or sealing interference before fastener rundown.

notes: The two supply-tube retaining bolts have different tightening specifications; do not treat them as interchangeable.

diagnostics.finding: O-ring residue or damage at an exposed sealing port.
diagnostics.meaning: The connection may not seal reliably after assembly.
diagnostics.next: Remove residue and resolve sealing-surface damage before installing the replacement tube.

verification.title: Confirm reconnection
verification.body: Check that the outlet pipe, clamps, bypass-valve connector and harness retainers have all been restored.

verification.title: Record the oil-level check
verification.body: Record the final engine-oil level and any oil added after assembly.

guides.title: Remove and replace the 2.3L EcoBoost turbocharger
guides.summary: Replace the turbocharger with new specified oil components, seals and mounting hardware, then check lubrication and leaks.
guides.introduction: The turbocharger uses exhaust energy to compress the air entering the engine, allowing it to produce more power. Engine oil lubricates its bearings, while oil and coolant circulate through its center housing. Removing the turbocharger therefore involves its air connections, oil circuit, coolant connection and mounting hardware, with the air-conditioning compressor moved aside for access.
guides.why: Even tiny particles can damage the compressor vanes. Oil and coolant sealing ports must also be completely clean and undamaged: trapped seal residue or a tube tightened before it is seated can leave a leak. The specified discarded parts must be replaced during reassembly.

when.summary: When the turbocharger requires removal for an established repair or replacement.
notes: This procedure provides the replacement path; it does not establish the cause of a performance complaint.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist at the specified lifting points, with the vehicle in NEUTRAL. Provide support for the displaced air-conditioning compressor. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare parts and clean handling
prepare.detail: Have port covers, a torque wrench, specified engine oil, new oil supply and drain tubes, a new turbocharger oil filter, gasket and mounting nuts. Replace mounting studs if removed. Arrange the belt and coolant-tube procedures before starting.

steps.title: Open the access path
steps.body: Raise the vehicle and remove the air-conditioning compressor belt. Disconnect the turbocharger bypass-valve connector and harness retainers, then loosen the outlet-pipe clamps and remove the pipe. Cover exposed air openings immediately.

steps.title: Move the compressor and disconnect the coolant supply
steps.body: Disconnect the compressor electrical connectors and harness retainers. Remove its bolts, then position and support it aside. Remove the turbocharger coolant supply tube using its dedicated procedure, then disconnect the turbocharger control hoses.

steps.title: Remove the oil connections and turbocharger
steps.body: Remove and discard the oil supply tube assembly, oil filter and oil drain tube. Discard the upper mounting nuts, remove the lower heat-shield bolt and remove the shield. Discard the lower mounting nuts, remove the turbocharger and discard its gasket. If studs need removal, discard those too.

steps.title: Install the turbocharger and heat shield
steps.body: Clean the mating faces and inspect the sealing ports and lines for damage or O-ring residue. Install new studs if removed, then the new gasket, turbocharger and new lower nuts. Fit the heat shield, new upper nuts and lower shield bolt finger tight; tighten the upper nuts before the lower shield bolt as directed.

steps.title: Rebuild the oil connections
steps.body: Lubricate the new drain-tube O-ring with clean specified engine oil and fully seat the tube before tightening its bolts. Install a new oil filter. Lubricate the supply-tube O-ring, fully seat the new supply assembly and initially fit its retaining bolts finger tight. Follow the illustrated procedure for their different tightening values.

steps.title: Restore the surrounding components
steps.body: Reconnect the control hoses and install the coolant supply tube through its linked procedure. Refit the compressor, its electrical connectors and harness retainers. Install and clamp the outlet pipe, reconnect the bypass valve and retainers, and install the compressor belt.

steps.title: Check oil and complete the running checks
steps.body: Check and top off engine oil to the engine specification. Start the engine and inspect for leaks. If a new turbocharger was installed, road test the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Contamination at open connections
watchFor.body: Inspect and clean components before reassembly; compressor protection depends on keeping foreign material out throughout the job.

watchFor.title: Unseated oil tubes
watchFor.body: Both oil tubes must be fully seated before fastener rundown. The fasteners must not substitute for correct seating.

notes: Use the 2.3L engine oil specification and the individual fastening values in the linked procedure.

verification.title: Leak and fluid check
verification.body: Confirm the engine oil check is complete and inspect the installed connections with the engine running.

verification.title: Record completion
verification.body: Record the leak-check result and, when a new turbocharger was fitted, the required road-test result.

guides.title: Diagnose accessory-belt noise, wear and tensioner movement
guides.summary: Inspect belt condition, pulley alignment and tensioner operation to identify the cause of accessory-drive noise.
guides.introduction: The accessory belt transfers engine rotation to equipment such as the generator and air-conditioning compressor. Its ribs must engage the pulleys correctly, while the spring-loaded tensioner maintains tension and damps movement. These checks apply to the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines; access and replacement work must follow the matching engine procedure.
guides.why: Small cracks and light rubber deposits can be acceptable. Missing rib material, contamination, poor alignment or a binding tensioner require different responses. Identifying the cause helps prevent a replacement belt from developing the same concern.

when.summary: Investigate accessory-drive noise, visible belt damage, incorrect tracking or unusual tensioner movement.
notes: Judge the belt by condition and symptoms; light pilling alone is not a replacement trigger.

prepare.title: Tools and access
prepare.detail: Have a mechanic's stethoscope or suitable listening device, the correct tensioner operating tool and engine-matched belt/tensioner removal instructions.

prepare.title: Separate static and running checks
prepare.detail: Handle the belt and check pulley rotation with the engine stopped. Running checks require safe observation and listening around moving belts and pulleys.

steps.title: Confirm the concern and inspect the whole drive
steps.body: Identify when the noise occurs. Inspect the belt, pulleys, generator, air-conditioning compressor and hardware for damage, contamination or looseness. Check that the correct belt is installed with every rib engaged in its pulley groove. Correct an obvious cause before continuing.

steps.title: Distinguish surface cracking from belt failure
steps.body: Rubber hardens with age, and small cracks can open as the belt bends over pulleys without making it unacceptable. Replace a belt when cracking exposes the cord at the groove bottom or when chunks are missing. Long strips detached from a rib are chunking and count as failure.

steps.title: Grade rubber deposits between the ribs
steps.body: Pilling consists of small rubber particles collecting in the grooves. In the numbered comparison, examples 1–2 need no action. Examples 3–4 show longer deposits up to 50% of rib height: replace if noise is apparent. Examples 5–6 show heavy deposits that justify replacement because noise and belt stability may be affected.

steps.title: Locate the noise and check pulley behavior
steps.body: Use the listening device to localize noise. Check pulleys for damage, trapped stones, alignment and freedom of rotation. For a chirp, check central tracking on flat pulleys, excessive axial movement and bent flanges; localize the sound at idle. For a metallic rattle, inspect component installation and loose hardware, tightening as required.

steps.title: Test the tensioner with the engine stopped
steps.body: Check for contamination and repair leaks first. Detach the belt at the tensioner using the engine-specific procedure. Move the tensioner through its full stroke and back, checking spring resistance without excessive sticking, grabbing or binding. Some damping friction is normal. Check its pulley for damage, free rotation and alignment. Replace a tensioner that fails these checks.

steps.title: Observe the tensioner dynamically
steps.body: After a satisfactory static check and correct belt refitting, observe it with the engine running. Movement up to 4 mm can occur during rapid acceleration or air-conditioning clutch cycling. Irregular movement without those changes can indicate a bent or out-of-round pulley or shaft, or damaged damping. Uneven belt groove depth can also cause excessive movement; fitting a new belt is the prescribed check for that condition.

watchFor.title: Do not lubricate the belt
watchFor.body: Lubricant can damage its construction. Correct a contamination source and replace the affected belt.

watchFor.title: Do not clean a contaminated tensioner
watchFor.body: Its internal damping mechanism may be damaged. Repair the leak and replace the tensioner as necessary.

notes: Light pilling often clears during normal driving.
Shared diagnostic criteria do not make belt or tensioner replacement procedures interchangeable between engines.

diagnostics.finding: Intermittent twittering chirp, especially at idle
diagnostics.meaning: Pulley misalignment is a possible cause.
diagnostics.next: Check tracking, pulley axial movement and flanges before selecting parts.

diagnostics.finding: Metallic knocking or rattle
diagnostics.meaning: Loose components or hardware may be responsible.
diagnostics.next: Correct installation or fastening and retest.

diagnostics.finding: Excessive tensioner movement
diagnostics.meaning: The belt, pulley or shaft can cause it as well as the tensioner.
diagnostics.next: Use static findings and the belt-condition check to guide replacement.

verification.title: Retest normal operation
verification.body: After each correction, check that the belt tracks correctly and the original noise or abnormal movement is resolved.

verification.title: Record the finding
verification.body: Record belt condition, noise location, tensioner test results and the effect of the repair.
