guides.title: Replace the accessory drive belt tensioner
guides.summary: Release the accessory belt load, replace the engine-specific tensioner and restore the intake components with the belt seated on every pulley.
guides.introduction: The accessory drive belt tensioner keeps the belt loaded against its pulleys as it drives the engine accessories. Replacing it requires releasing that load before removing its mounting fasteners. The 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures differ in access, belt handling and fastening, so identify the engine before beginning.
guides.why: The tensioner must be moved in the specified direction to free the belt. Correct refitting then depends on using the proper mounting torque and seating the belt on every pulley. On the turbocharged 2.3L, opening the intake also introduces a separate concern: even very small particles can damage the turbocharger compressor vanes.

when.summary: When the accessory drive belt tensioner requires replacement.
notes: Follow the procedure for the fitted engine; the tensioner mounting arrangement is not shared across all variants.

prepare.title: Provide tensioner and fastener access
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools to rotate the tensioner under control, remove its mounting fasteners and apply the specified torque.

prepare.title: Plan the intake removal
prepare.detail: Air-cleaner outlet-pipe removal is required across these access routes. The 2.3L also requires engine appearance-cover removal; the 3.7L reaches the tensioner through its complete belt-removal procedure.

prepare.title: Protect the 2.3L intake
prepare.detail: Keep debris out whenever an intake connection is opened. Before reassembly, inspect the turbocharger or engine intake components and clean them if necessary.

steps.title: Remove the engine-specific access components
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove the appearance-cover bolts and nut, then the cover. Remove the air-cleaner outlet pipe for the fitted engine. For the 3.7L, follow the [accessory belt procedure](#/document/G1688121), which begins with outlet-pipe removal.

steps.title: Release the 2.3L pipe connections correctly
steps.body: For the 2.3L outlet pipe, loosen the clamp and position the bypass-valve inlet tube aside, then disconnect and position aside the crankcase ventilation tube. Loosen the three pipe clamps and remove the pipe. Keep particles out of the open intake throughout this work.

steps.title: Unload the belt
steps.body: Rotate the tensioner counterclockwise while controlling its spring load. On the 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L, position the accessory belt aside. On the 3.7L, remove the belt as directed by its belt procedure.

steps.title: Replace and secure the tensioner
steps.body: Remove the mounting bolts and tensioner on the 2.3L or 3.7L; their installation torque is 18 lb.ft (25 Nm). The 5.0L and 5.2L use the specified single mounting bolt at 35 lb.ft (48 Nm). Use the matching procedure to identify the mounting fastener rather than confusing it with the pulley fastener.

steps.title: Restore the belt and intake
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, controlling the tensioner as the belt is returned to its pulleys. Confirm correct seating everywhere. Reinstall the outlet pipe and its connections. On the 2.3L, inspect and clean intake components as necessary, tighten the outlet-pipe clamps to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm), and refit the appearance cover using its individual fastener specifications.

watchFor.title: Mixing mounting specifications
watchFor.body: The 2.3L and 3.7L tensioners use the lower mounting torque; the 5.0L and 5.2L use a different single-bolt specification.

watchFor.title: A belt resting outside its intended track
watchFor.body: Check every pulley after installation. A belt that has been returned to the drive is not necessarily seated correctly.

watchFor.title: Debris entering the turbocharger intake
watchFor.body: On the 2.3L, contamination during outlet-pipe removal can damage the compressor vanes.

notes: Use the tensioner illustration for your selected engine to identify its mounting arrangement.
The 3.7L requires complete accessory-belt removal; the other procedures specify positioning the belt aside.

verification.title: Check the belt on all pulleys
verification.body: Confirm correct belt seating throughout the accessory drive after installation, including the 3.7L belt reinstallation.

verification.title: Confirm the engine-specific installation
verification.body: Check the tensioner mounting torque, restored outlet-pipe connections and, on the 2.3L, intake cleanliness and appearance-cover installation.

guides.title: Replace the A/C compressor belt on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Use the engine-specific removal method, fit the stretch belt with a cable tie and hand rotation, then verify both belts are seated.
guides.introduction: The air conditioning (A/C) compressor belt transfers crankshaft rotation to the compressor pulley. It is a separate stretch belt whose installation uses controlled hand rotation to guide it onto the crankshaft pulley. The engines share that principle, but access, removal and routing differ. The 2.3L and 3.7L procedures use a stretchy-belt remover; the 5.0L and 5.2L procedures require cutting and discarding the old belt.
guides.why: A belt must sit correctly in the pulley grooves before operation. On the 3.7L and both V8 procedures, its lower run must remain above the oil-pan flange during installation to prevent belt and engine damage. Checking the belt after a full hand-turned revolution establishes that it remains seated as the pulleys turn.

when.summary: When compressor-belt repair or related access requires removal; cut belts on the 5.0L and 5.2L must be replaced.
notes: Identify the engine before choosing the removal method and routing sequence.

prepare.title: Prepare fitting tools
prepare.detail: Have cable ties at least 3 mm (0.12 in) wide and tools for controlled crankshaft rotation by hand. The 3.7L procedure specifies stretchy-belt remover 303-1419; use the illustrated remover arrangement for the 2.3L.

prepare.title: Plan engine-specific access
prepare.detail: Have the appropriate air-cleaner outlet-pipe and accessory-belt instructions available. Obtain a replacement belt before cutting a 5.0L or 5.2L belt.

steps.title: Open the access path
steps.body: On the [2.3L](#/document/G1688221), remove the engine appearance cover's bolts and nuts, then the air-cleaner outlet pipe. On the [3.7L](#/document/G1688123), [5.0L](#/document/G1688134) and [5.2L](#/document/G1807247), remove the outlet pipe and accessory drive belt before removing the compressor belt.

steps.title: Remove the compressor belt by its specified method
steps.body: For the 2.3L and 3.7L, turn the crankshaft pulley bolt clockwise to feed the stretchy-belt tool onto the compressor pulley approximately 180°. Fold the tool under the belt's inside as illustrated, then pull firmly in one quick motion. For the 5.0L and 5.2L, cut and discard the belt.

steps.title: Clear the 2.3L installation path
steps.body: Before fitting the 2.3L compressor belt, remove the accessory belt from its tensioner and position it away from the crankshaft pulley. On the other engines, the accessory belt was already removed during access.

steps.title: Position the new belt
steps.body: On the 2.3L, seat the belt on the compressor pulley and place it over the crankshaft pulley's top. For the 3.7L and both V8s, follow the three-stage route: between crankshaft pulley and tensioner, behind the crankshaft pulley, then onto the compressor pulley. Follow the specified rib orientation toward the vehicle front and keep the lower run above the oil pan.

steps.title: Attach the fitting cable tie
steps.body: With the belt seated on the compressor pulley and positioned at the crankshaft pulley's top, pass the specified cable tie through the crankshaft pulley spokes, up and over the belt, and tighten it as illustrated.

steps.title: Walk the belt onto the pulley
steps.body: Rotate the crankshaft by hand 180° to install the belt. The 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L instructions specify clockwise rotation with the belt above the oil-pan flange.

steps.title: Remove the tie and check seating
steps.body: Remove the cable tie, then rotate the crankshaft by hand 360° and verify seating on both pulleys. The 3.7L and both V8 procedures specify clockwise rotation for this check.

steps.title: Restore the accessory drive and intake
steps.body: Install the accessory drive belt and verify correct seating on all its pulleys. Recheck the compressor belt, then reinstall the engine-specific outlet pipe. On the 2.3L, reinstall the appearance cover and tighten its bolts and nuts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm).

watchFor.title: Belt caught below the oil-pan flange
watchFor.body: The 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures warn that this position can damage the belt and engine during installation.

watchFor.title: Lubricants and belt dressing
watchFor.body: The 3.7L and both V8 procedures prohibit fluids or belt dressing on the belts and pulleys, and lubrication of the tensioner; belt material and tensioner damping can be damaged.

notes: The 2.3L and 3.7L removal illustrations show typical applications.
The cable tie is an installation aid and must be removed before the final hand-rotation check.

diagnostics.finding: The compressor belt is not correctly seated after hand rotation.
diagnostics.meaning: The installation has not passed its required seating check.
diagnostics.next: Correct the position through the engine-specific procedure before completing reassembly.

verification.title: Confirm compressor-belt seating
verification.body: After removing the cable tie and completing the prescribed full hand rotation, confirm that the belt is seated on the crankshaft and compressor pulleys.

verification.title: Confirm restored components
verification.body: Check accessory-belt seating on every pulley and confirm outlet-pipe installation. For the 2.3L, also verify appearance-cover fastener tightening.

guides.title: Replace the 5.2L accessory drive belt
guides.summary: Remove the air cleaner outlet pipe, release the belt tensioner and refit the accessory belt with correct seating on every pulley.
guides.introduction: The accessory drive belt transfers engine rotation through a group of pulleys to drive the attached accessories. Its tensioner keeps the belt under working tension. On the 5.2L engine, removing the air cleaner outlet pipe provides the access needed to release that tension and take the belt off.
guides.why: The tensioner must release the belt before removal. Correct routing and seating then matter just as much as getting the belt back onto the engine: a belt resting partly outside a pulley’s intended running surface has not been installed correctly.

when.summary: When the 5.2L accessory belt needs replacement or must be removed for another repair.

prepare.title: Plan the access work
prepare.detail: Have the 5.2L air cleaner outlet-pipe removal and installation procedure available for its connections and refitting details.

prepare.title: Prepare to control the tensioner
prepare.detail: Be able to rotate and hold the tensioner while guiding the belt clear. Review the routing illustration before disturbing the belt.

steps.title: Remove the outlet pipe
steps.body: Remove the air cleaner outlet pipe using the engine-specific procedure. This is the required access operation before working on the belt and tensioner.

steps.title: Release the belt
steps.body: Identify the tensioner and belt path in the illustration. Rotate the accessory drive belt tensioner counterclockwise and remove the belt while its tension is released.

steps.title: Install the belt along the illustrated path
steps.body: Reverse the removal operation, using the tensioner to provide installation clearance. Guide the belt onto the pulleys along the illustrated route, then allow the tensioner to take up the belt.

steps.title: Inspect seating and restore access components
steps.body: Check the belt at every pulley, including portions that are harder to see. Correct any seating problem before completing the reverse removal sequence and reinstalling the air cleaner outlet pipe.

watchFor.title: A belt that is only partly seated
watchFor.body: Do not judge the installation from the most visible pulley alone. The completion requirement applies to every pulley.

notes: Use the routing illustration attached to the 5.2L procedure; another engine’s accessory layout may differ.

verification.title: Confirm the completed installation
verification.body: Verify correct belt seating on all pulleys and completion of the air cleaner outlet-pipe installation.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L accessory drive belt removal and installation, including tensioner direction and final pulley-seating check.

guides.title: Diagnose no crank and related starting faults on the 2.3L EcoBoost
guides.summary: Separate starting authorization, wiring, battery-cable and starter faults through the appropriate symptom and circuit tests.
guides.introduction: The powertrain control module (PCM) energizes the starter relay only after receiving the required starting inputs. The relay then supplies the starter motor. A silent starter can therefore reflect a missing permission signal, an electrical fault or mechanical resistance; it does not automatically mean the starter has failed.
guides.why: Checking battery condition and mechanical freedom first prevents misleading electrical diagnosis. Loaded voltage-drop tests then reveal resistance that can prevent useful starter power even when an unloaded voltage reading looks satisfactory.

when.summary: Use for no crank, slow cranking, unusual starter operation or recorded starting-system faults.
notes: Automatic and manual transmissions have different starting-permission checks.

prepare.title: Diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use Ford diagnostic methods, a compatible scan tool, multimeter, test light with Flex Probe Kit adapters, fused jumper and remote starter switch. Software updates and module decisions require programming and vehicle-specific service-information access.

prepare.title: Electrical and mechanical prerequisites
prepare.detail: Maintain battery voltage above 12.2 volts during Test A; do not use a charger's highest or boost setting. Keep the transmission in PARK or NEUTRAL for cranking tests. Follow the specified ignition and connector states for each measurement.

steps.title: Confirm the complaint and mechanical freedom
steps.body: Inspect battery and generator connections, battery condition and charge, and aftermarket wiring. Follow the accessory-belt procedure to remove the belt and check that the crankshaft and driven accessories rotate without seizure or damage. Correct an obvious cause before continuing.

steps.title: Establish key recognition and module communication
steps.body: For NO KEY DETECTED, move the passive key away from cabin outer edges and retry; a continuing message requires [anti-theft diagnosis](#/document/G1694660). Run the network test for the body control module (BCM), instrument panel cluster and PCM. Resolve [communication failures](#/document/G1813071), then retrieve BCM and PCM self-test codes before choosing the next branch.

steps.title: Check the transmission-specific permission inputs
steps.body: On automatics, check stoplamps, the PCM brake input, BCM IGN_SW_STATE and PCM IN_GEAR in PARK and NEUTRAL. Follow failed checks into brake wiring, [stoplamp](#/document/G1694231), [ignition-control](#/document/G1693269) or [transmission diagnosis](#/document/G1686449). On manuals, check CPP_BOT with the clutch fully depressed. Then check ENG_CRANK; an inactive result leads to PCM confirmation.

steps.title: Separate relay control from starter power
steps.body: Follow A13–A19: test relay control with adapted test-light connections, then relay supply and the specified momentary fused bypass. Cranking through the bypass directs relay replacement. Otherwise check battery-positive voltage to G106 and G108 separately, then to the starter case, followed by starter B-terminal supply. Address cable or mounting faults as directed. If A19 finds no cause, stop before A20; that referral requires a confirmed direct-command procedure.

steps.title: Follow the independent relay and clutch branches
steps.body: A failed relay-control test leads to isolated wiring checks for shorts to ground and opens. A missing clutch input leads through switch-ground and signal continuity checks before switch replacement. For BCM P0830:11, repeat self-test with the clutch switch disconnected: disappearance directs switch replacement; persistence requires the isolated short-to-ground check, followed by circuit repair or BCM confirmation.

steps.title: Measure voltage loss while cranking
steps.body: Fully charge the battery and perform the battery drain check first. Follow the component tests using a remote switch from battery positive to the solenoid S terminal. Measure positive-side drop from the battery positive post to M, and ground-side drop from clean starter housing to battery negative. Record readings at component terminals, not wiring ends. Clean and retest before following the cable or starter replacement branches.

steps.title: Investigate unusual starter noise separately
steps.body: Test B first checks mounting. With ignition off, its remote switch connects C197A pin 1, the B terminal, to C197C pin 1, the S terminal. Noise attributable to engagement leads to drive-gear and ring-gear inspection; otherwise continue [engine diagnosis](#/document/G1804267).

steps.title: Check wake-up faults through Tests C and E
steps.body: Test C repeats the BCM self-test with the PCM disconnected. A disappearing fault leads to PCM confirmation; a persistent fault requires the appropriate short/open checks before BCM confirmation. Test E first checks and updates PCM software, then tests wake-up wiring. Reconnect both modules, clear PCM codes and run PCM self-test. Record returning codes; route accompanying C113A faults through Test C before further PCM decisions.

steps.title: Isolate a persistent crank-detect signal
steps.body: For P2535, Test D measures C1551B pin 47 with the PCM disconnected, then isolates the front controls interface module (FCIM) and BCM in sequence. Voltage disappearing with FCIM disconnection directs its replacement procedure; disappearing with BCM disconnection requires its VIN-specific guided routine. Voltage remaining indicates wiring trouble. No initial voltage leads to PCM confirmation.

steps.title: Confirm module decisions
steps.body: Inspect the indicated module's connectors for corrosion, damaged or pushed-out pins; repair correctly, seat and latch connections, then retest. Follow applicable technical service bulletins before replacement. Supported PCM branches can direct replacement; BCM branches require the vehicle-specific guided routine. A concern that disappears after reconnection still requires attention to the connector fault's cause.

watchFor.title: Protect connector terminals
watchFor.body: Use the Flex Probe Kit for the test light; never push its probe directly into a connector.

watchFor.title: Use the correct wake-up terminal
watchFor.body: For the 2.3L, Tests C and E use PCM C1551B pin 28 to BCM C2280F pin 18. Ground is the reference for the short-to-ground and short-to-voltage measurements.

notes: The push-button ignition switch is part of the FCIM and is not serviced separately.
Other BCM codes require the BCM diagnostic chart; they do not establish a starter fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P06E9 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detected no engine rotation during a crank event.
diagnostics.next: For a no-crank complaint, follow Test A rather than replacing the starter from the code alone.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0830 or P0830:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: PCM P0830 concerns missing clutch-switch activity during vehicle movement; BCM P0830:11 identifies a clutch bottom-of-travel circuit short to ground.
diagnostics.next: Use Test A's appropriate clutch-input or disconnected-switch branch.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code C113A:11 or C113A:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detects a wake-up circuit short to ground, or a short to voltage/open, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Use Test C to distinguish wiring from module-related faults.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P2535 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detected crank-detect voltage while the engine was running.
diagnostics.next: Use Test D's staged isolation of wiring, FCIM, BCM and PCM.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P06E4:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM reports control-module wake-up circuit performance trouble.
diagnostics.next: Confirm current PCM software before Test E; follow applicable service information before any PCM replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Cranking voltage drop exceeds 0.5 volt.
diagnostics.meaning: Resistance is excessive in the measured power or return path.
diagnostics.next: Clean and retest. Persistent M-terminal drop with B-terminal drop below 0.5 volt directs starter replacement; excessive B-terminal drop directs positive-cable attention. Persistent excessive ground drop directs negative-cable replacement. Ground drop below 0.5 volt with continued slow cranking directs starter replacement.

diagnostics.finding: The starter spins without turning the engine, or continues cranking.
diagnostics.meaning: These require engagement or retained-power diagnosis.
diagnostics.next: For free spinning, inspect mounting, engagement and flexplate teeth. For continued cranking, remove the relay: stopping directs relay replacement; continued cranking directs repair of CDC25 (BN/GN) for a short to voltage.

diagnostics.finding: Remote start alone fails, has poor range, or records P1594 or P1595.
diagnostics.meaning: Remote-start operation has separate authorization and fault paths.
diagnostics.next: Use [locks and entry diagnosis](#/document/G1695898) for operation/range. P1594 concerns unattended timeout and P1595 a transmission-not-in-Park shutdown; use [electronic engine controls diagnosis](#/document/G1692929).

verification.title: Repeat the relevant operating check
verification.body: After the directed repair, operate the system and confirm whether the original complaint remains. For Test E, clear PCM codes and repeat PCM self-test after restoring connections.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record cranking voltage-drop readings and returning codes. Identify any unresolved A20 referral or VIN-specific guided routine; reaching either is not a completed repair.

guides.title: Diagnose GT350 no-crank and starter-control faults
guides.summary: Separate battery, starter, clutch-input and control-circuit problems using the supported GT350 diagnostic branches and their defined stopping points.
guides.introduction: The starter turns the engine, but pressing START does not power it directly. The body control module (BCM) supplies start-related information, while the powertrain control module (PCM) energizes the starter relay after recognizing the required inputs. On this manual-transmission GT350, those include a fully applied clutch. Diagnosis therefore checks both the high-current motor circuit and the signals that permit cranking.
guides.why: A silent starter can reflect a missing start request, a clutch-input fault or inadequate electrical supply. Slow cranking can result from resistance in either battery cable. Testing these separately prevents a starter-performance code from being mistaken for proof that the starter itself has failed.

when.summary: Use for no-crank, slow-crank, abnormal starter noise or the specified clutch, wake-up and crank-detect faults.
notes: An engine that cranks normally but will not start requires powertrain symptom diagnosis.
Automatic-transmission and remote-start branches do not establish equipment fitted to this manual-transmission GT350.

prepare.title: Arrange the required capability
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable scan tool, multimeter, test light with Flex Probes, fused jumper and remote starter switch. Have Wiring Diagrams Cells 20 and 23, safe starter access, programming capability and access to VIN-dependent BCM routines.

prepare.title: Control battery voltage and cranking
prepare.detail: Keep battery voltage above 12.2 volts before and during Test A. Do not use a charger's highest or boost setting. Secure the vehicle in Neutral before commanded cranking and positively identify starter terminals before attaching test equipment.

steps.title: Check supply and mechanical freedom
steps.body: Inspect battery and generator connections, battery condition, high-current junction-box connections, the run/start relay and specified fuses. Check added accessories for incorrect wiring. Remove the accessory belt using the 5.2L procedure and verify that the crankshaft and belt-driven components rotate without seizure or damage. Correct an obvious cause before continuing.

steps.title: Establish key recognition and start inputs
steps.body: For NO KEY DETECTED, move a key away from the cabin's outer edges and retry; persistent messages require passive anti-theft diagnosis. Test communication with the BCM, instrument panel cluster and PCM, then retrieve BCM and PCM codes. Watch the clutch-bottom-of-travel parameter identification (PID), CPP_BOT: it should change from NO to YES with full clutch application. Next, ENG_CRANK should change from Inactive to Active during the start request.

steps.title: Separate relay drive from motor supply
steps.body: A8 uses a loaded test-light check across the relay coil connections; confirm its manual-transmission command setup before execution. Where drive is confirmed, A9 checks relay supply and A10 uses an ignition-OFF, momentary fused jumper between relay pins 3 and 5. Cranking supports relay replacement; no cranking leads to A11–A14. Missing coil drive takes A16/A17's isolated short-to-ground and continuity checks, with passing circuits leading to A23.

steps.title: Check grounds and the clutch circuit
steps.body: For A11, connect the positive meter lead to battery positive and the negative lead separately to G106 and G108. A12 uses battery positive and the starter case. Each expects more than 11 volts; failure directs attention to negative cables or starter mounting. A13 checks B-terminal supply. For an incorrect CPP_BOT response, A18–A20 distinguish switch operation, ground and signal continuity. For P0830:11, A21 retests with the clutch switch disconnected: a cleared fault supports switch replacement; a persistent fault takes A22's isolated circuit check.

steps.title: Measure voltage loss while cranking
steps.body: For the component tests, fully charge the battery and perform the battery-drain check. Connect at component terminals, not wiring ends. Measure from battery positive to starter M while operating the remote switch: 0.5 volt or less leads to the ground test. Above that, clean the specified solenoid connections and repeat. Persistent loss requires comparison at B: below 0.5 volt identifies the solenoid/connections and supports starter replacement; above 0.5 volt directs positive-cable cleaning and, if unresolved, replacement.

steps.title: Finish the ground and noise branches
steps.body: Measure cranking voltage loss from the clean starter housing to battery negative. Above 0.5 volt requires cleaning ground connections and retesting; persistent excess supports negative-cable replacement. Below 0.5 volt with continued slow cranking supports starter replacement. For noise, Test B first checks mounting. Its remote-switch test requires verified B/S terminal identity; starter-engagement noise follows the starter procedure, while other noise requires engine diagnosis.

steps.title: Isolate wake-up faults with Test C
steps.body: For C113A:11 or C113A:15, disconnect the PCM as directed, clear BCM codes and repeat its self-test. A disappearing code leads to PCM connection checks. A persistent code requires the matching circuit branch: grounding for C113A:11, or unwanted voltage followed by continuity for C113A:15. Repair failed circuits; passing results lead to BCM connection checks and, if needed, a VIN-guided routine.

steps.title: Use Test D for P2535
steps.body: Check the crank-detect circuit for unwanted voltage with the PCM disconnected. No voltage leads to PCM connection checks. If voltage remains, disconnect the front controls interface module (FCIM): disappearance supports the equipment-matched FCIM replacement route because the start button is not separately serviceable. If voltage remains, disconnect the BCM; disappearance requires its guided routine, while remaining voltage requires circuit repair.

steps.title: Keep Test E within its diagnostic limits
steps.body: For P06E4, check and update PCM software first. Further progression through E2 requires clarification. E3 checks C2280F pin 18 to ground for unwanted voltage; E4 checks continuity to C175B pin 65, expecting less than 3 ohms. Establish the required isolation before performing these individual checks. Failed measurements support circuit repair, but this incomplete sequence cannot authorize PCM replacement. Likewise, if A14 finds no cause, stop before A15.

watchFor.title: Resolve command setup before energizing
watchFor.body: A8 lists a brake-pedal command although this GT350 requires a clutch start input. Test B's C197C/S-terminal identification also needs confirmation. Do not guess a connector substitution or execute an uncertain remote-switch connection.

watchFor.title: Separate module endpoints from code descriptions
watchFor.body: A23, C8 and D4 require connector inspection and repair, confirmation that the concern remains, and applicable bulletin checks before PCM replacement. BCM endpoints require VIN-guided diagnosis. Test E does not provide a replacement verdict within this guide.

notes: A11/A12 are battery-positive reference checks; they are different from the loaded voltage-drop component tests.
At module connector checks, repair corrosion, damaged or pushed-out terminals, then reconnect and confirm that connectors seat and latch.
P1594/P1595 belong to the general remote-start code listings and refer to 5.2L engine-control diagnosis; do not apply automatic-transmission remote-start operation to this GT350.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P06E9 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detected no engine rotation during a crank event; this does not identify the failed component.
diagnostics.next: Use Test A if the engine does not crank. If it does crank, follow powertrain symptom diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0830 or P0830:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P0830 concerns clutch switch A; BCM code P0830:11 specifically identifies detected grounding of the clutch-bottom-of-travel circuit.
diagnostics.next: Use Test A; P0830:11 enters A21's disconnected-switch retest.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code C113A:11 or C113A:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detected a wake-up-circuit short to ground, or a short to battery/open, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test C's code-specific isolation sequence.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P2535 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detected a crank-detect signal short to voltage while the engine was running.
diagnostics.next: Use the dedicated Test D, not the starter-noise Test B.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P06E4 or P162F is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P06E4 concerns module wake-up performance. P162F reports starter disabling after excessive cranking time.
diagnostics.next: P06E4 begins with Test E's software check and bounded follow-up. P162F requires powertrain symptom diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: The starter spins without turning the engine, or continues cranking.
diagnostics.meaning: Free spinning calls for mounting, engagement and ring-gear inspection. Continued cranking requires separating a relay fault from unwanted solenoid-circuit voltage.
diagnostics.next: For continued cranking, the diagnostic relay-removal check distinguishes a relay replacement endpoint if cranking stops from a CDC25 circuit short-to-voltage repair if it continues.

verification.title: Record loaded measurements and operation
verification.body: Record positive and ground voltage-drop readings before and after cleaning or repair. Recheck the original cranking or noise concern; a normal unloaded voltage reading alone does not complete a slow-crank diagnosis.

verification.title: Perform the defined E5 recheck
verification.body: When E5's entry conditions are established, reconnect PCM C175B and BCM C2280F and turn ignition ON. Clear the PCM DTCs, then carry out the PCM self-test. If P06E4 is recorded, retrieve and record all continuous-memory codes; C113A:11 or C113A:15 requires Test C. Clear all codes and rerun the PCM self-test. A returning fault requires applicable service-information checks, without authorizing PCM replacement through this bounded Test E path.

verification.title: Document the stopping point
verification.body: Record the completed tests, supported repair decision and any unresolved command-terminal or routing issue. Reaching A15 or unresolved E2 routing is not a completed no-crank diagnosis.

applicability.equipment: GT350 with manual transmission and push-button start

guides.title: Inspect starter drive gear and flywheel ring gear wear
guides.summary: Inspect both mating gears to decide whether to reinstall the starter, replace it, or replace the affected flywheel or flexplate.
guides.introduction: The starter's small drive gear engages the ring gear on the flywheel or flexplate to turn the engine during starting. Their tooth surfaces reveal how the gears have been engaging. This inspection covers the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures, which share the same wear-based decisions but require their own starter access and replacement instructions.
guides.why: Inspecting both gears distinguishes damage to the starter drive from damage to the ring gear it engages. The stated starter-replacement decision combines incomplete engagement with a scored or damaged drive gear. Ring-gear damage has its own repair decision, so checking only the removed starter can leave the other damaged component unaddressed.

when.summary: When investigating starter gear engagement or checking the starter drive and ring gear for wear or damage.
notes: This is a mechanical inspection; its findings do not diagnose the start-command or electrical-supply circuits.

prepare.title: Select the engine-specific access procedure
prepare.detail: Identify the engine and fitted flywheel or flexplate arrangement. Use that engine's Starter Motor removal and installation article, including all of its access and safety prerequisites.

prepare.title: Plan for the possible repair
prepare.detail: Starter removal provides the inspection access. If the ring gear is damaged, the job expands to the applicable flywheel or flexplate replacement procedure and its required capabilities.

steps.title: Remove the correct starter assembly
steps.body: Follow the Starter Motor procedure for the actual engine. The common inspection decision does not make mounting, access or installation details interchangeable between engines.

steps.title: Inspect both mating gears
steps.body: Check the wear pattern on the starter drive gear and on the flywheel or flexplate ring gear. Look for the specified distinctions: normal wear, incomplete engagement accompanied by drive-gear damage, and scored or damaged ring-gear teeth.

steps.title: Choose the starter disposition
steps.body: If the wear pattern is normal, reinstall the starter through its engine-specific procedure. If the gears have not been fully engaging and the starter drive gear is scored or damaged, install a new starter motor.

steps.title: Address ring-gear damage separately
steps.body: Scored or damaged ring-gear teeth require a new applicable flywheel or flexplate. The 2.3L and 3.7L procedures provide separate replacement references for those components. The 5.0L inspection refers to the engine-section Flywheel procedure, and the 5.2L inspection links to its Flywheel procedure.

steps.title: Complete the selected installation path
steps.body: Finish every replacement indicated by the inspection, then complete starter installation under the matching engine procedure. Do not treat a new starter as completion if the ring gear also met the replacement criterion.

watchFor.title: Replacing a starter from engagement alone
watchFor.body: The stated decision requires incomplete engagement together with a scored or damaged starter drive gear. Preserve that combined finding.

watchFor.title: Inferring transmission equipment
watchFor.body: Generic references to a flywheel or flexplate do not establish that both arrangements apply to every engine. Follow the actual equipment and the engine-specific repair reference.

notes: The illustration accompanies the 2.3L inspection and shows the relationship between the gears; it does not label a particular wear pattern as acceptable or defective.
For a 5.0L ring-gear repair, use the Flywheel reference identified in its inspection article rather than substituting another engine's replacement procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The gear wear pattern is normal.
diagnostics.meaning: The inspection does not call for replacement on the basis of this wear pattern.
diagnostics.next: Reinstall the starter motor.

diagnostics.finding: Engagement is incomplete and the starter drive gear is scored or damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: The stated starter replacement criterion is met.
diagnostics.next: Install a new starter motor using the matching engine procedure.

diagnostics.finding: Flywheel or flexplate ring-gear teeth are scored or damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: The ring-gear replacement criterion is met.
diagnostics.next: Replace the applicable flywheel or flexplate.

verification.title: Record both inspection findings
verification.body: Record the condition of the starter drive gear and ring gear separately, together with the resulting reinstall or replacement decision.

verification.title: Confirm installation completion
verification.body: Confirm that the selected component replacement and engine-specific starter installation procedures are complete.

guides.title: Replace the starter motor: 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Remove and refit the starter, inspect both meshing gears, and use the correct engine and transmission mounting instructions.
guides.introduction: The starter motor turns the engine through its drive gear and the flywheel ring gear. Replacing it requires access beneath the vehicle and disconnection of its battery feed and solenoid-control wire. The engines share this purpose, but access, removal order and mounting requirements differ. Identify the engine and transmission before choosing the procedure.
guides.why: The starter battery terminal can deliver enough current to heat a shorted tool and cause burns. Battery isolation must therefore precede work on that terminal. Inspecting both gears matters because installing another starter does not correct damage to the ring gear it engages.

when.summary: After diagnosis establishes the need for starter replacement, or when the starter must be removed for related work.
notes: A failure to crank does not, by itself, prove that the starter motor is defective.

prepare.title: Safe underside access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the specified lifting points, identified by the stamped triangles. Check adapter clearance around surrounding components. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Battery isolation and fastening
prepare.detail: Have the battery disconnect/connect procedure and suitable hand and torque tools available. Disconnect the battery ground cable at the battery before disconnecting the starter battery lead.

prepare.title: Choose the transmission branch
prepare.detail: The 5.0L instructions distinguish the 10R80 automatic from the MT82 manual. Their starter mounting torques differ.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle and isolate the battery
steps.body: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on a hoist using [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631). Disconnect the battery through [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356) before handling either starter connection.

steps.title: Follow the engine-specific access order
steps.body: On the [2.3L](#/document/G1673178), release the harness retainers from the mounting studbolts, move the harness aside, remove the studbolts and reposition the starter before disconnecting its leads. On the [5.2L](#/document/G1804813), complete the underbody-shield removals before accessing the electrical connections.

steps.title: Disconnect the starter leads
steps.body: Open the solenoid battery-cable cover. Remove the battery-cable nut and disconnect that cable, then remove the solenoid-wire nut and disconnect the control wire. Keep the repositioned 2.3L starter supported while completing these operations.

steps.title: Release the remaining mounts
steps.body: On the [3.7L](#/document/G1692845) automatic, remove the transmission cooling-tube bracket nut and move the bracket aside before removing the starter studbolts. The manual branch proceeds directly to those studbolts. On the [5.0L](#/document/G1692948), use the applicable transmission branch to remove the mounting bolts. Remove the 5.2L mounting bolts as directed. The already-unfastened 2.3L starter can now be removed.

steps.title: Inspect both gears
steps.body: Inspect the starter drive gear and flywheel ring gear using the engine-matched inspection procedure listed below. Establish whether additional gear work is needed before treating starter replacement as the complete repair.

steps.title: Reassemble in the correct reverse order
steps.body: Reverse the selected removal branch; on the 2.3L, reconnect the leads before returning the starter to its mounting position. The 2.3L and 3.7L mounting studbolts use 47.5 Nm. For the 5.0L, mounting bolts use 47.5 Nm with the 10R80 or 25 Nm with the MT82. On the 5.2L, install bolts hand tight, then follow the illustrated tightening sequence: starter-to-engine bolts use 25 Nm and the bracket-to-engine-mount bolt uses 55 Nm. Follow each procedure for terminal and ancillary fastener torques. Restore the cable cover, applicable bracket, harness retainers and shielding, then reconnect the battery.

watchFor.title: Transferring a mounting torque
watchFor.body: Engine size alone does not select the 5.0L mounting specification; the transmission branch is essential.

watchFor.title: Leaving the battery terminal exposed
watchFor.body: Restore its protective cover during reassembly rather than leaving an accessible live connection.

notes: The 5.0L procedure covers 10R80 and MT82 installations. Another transmission requires its matching instructions.

diagnostics.finding: A 2.3L or 3.7L engine does not crank.
diagnostics.meaning: Starter operation also depends on start-request, transmission or clutch, relay and control-module inputs.
diagnostics.next: Establish the cause of the no-crank condition before authorizing a starter solely from the symptom.

diagnostics.finding: Gear inspection identifies damage.
diagnostics.meaning: The starter and ring gear form a meshing pair; replacing the starter may leave another fault present.
diagnostics.next: Follow the engine-specific inspection procedure to determine the additional repair.

verification.title: Reassembly and operation
verification.body: Check restored connections, covers and variant-specific attachments. After battery reconnection and safe return from the hoist, confirm that a start request cranks the engine.

verification.title: Record the mechanical findings
verification.body: Record the engine/transmission branch used and the results of both gear inspections, including any further repair required.

guides.title: Replace ignition coils on the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Remove and inspect coil-on-plug units, replace damaged assemblies or boots as specified, and restore the correct engine-specific connections and tightening.
guides.introduction: A coil-on-plug unit supplies ignition voltage directly to its spark plug through an insulated boot. This job removes the unit and inspects it for physical damage before refitting or replacement. The engines share that basic arrangement, but their access requirements, replacement instructions and mounting-bolt tightening differ.
guides.why: Cleaning around a seated coil keeps loose material from falling into the opening during removal. A slight twist releases the boot seal without forcing it straight upward. Correct tightening matters because the mounting instructions range from a fixed torque to torque followed by an additional angle.

when.summary: When a coil requires removal or replacement, or inspection reveals cracks, rips or tears.
notes: Select the engine procedure before starting; the 3.7L right-hand coils require upper intake-manifold removal.

prepare.title: Match tools to the engine branch
prepare.detail: Provide compressed air for cleaning, suitable hand tools and a torque wrench. The 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L also require controlled angle tightening. Right-hand access on the 3.7L requires the capability and prerequisites in the upper intake-manifold procedure.

steps.title: Expose the coils on the 2.3L or 3.7L
steps.body: On the [2.3L](#/document/G1673188), disconnect the battery through the linked procedure, then remove the appearance-cover nuts, bolts and cover. On the [3.7L](#/document/G1675558), remove the upper intake manifold for right-hand access. That manifold-removal instruction applies to the right-hand bank.

steps.title: Expose the coils on the V8 engines
steps.body: On the [5.0L](#/document/G1675574), remove the appearance cover, release the positive crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve coupling and crankcase ventilation tube coupling, and move them aside before removing the coil covers. On the [5.2L](#/document/G1805373), release the PCV hose couplings, position the hoses out of the way and remove the coil covers.

steps.title: Disconnect, clean and lift out the coils
steps.body: Follow the selected procedure's connector and cleaning sequence. On the 2.3L, release the harness retainers and slide back any cover over a connector locking tab before depressing it. Use compressed air around the coils while they are still seated; the 3.7L places this cleaning before connector disconnection. Remove the mounting bolts, then use a slight twisting motion to release each coil's seal and lift it out.

steps.title: Inspect the specified replaceable part
steps.body: For the 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L, inspect the coil-on-plug assembly for cracks, rips or tears and replace damaged assemblies. The 3.7L instruction specifically calls for replacing rubber boots with this damage. Use that distinction when deciding which part needs renewal.

steps.title: Install and tighten for the exact engine
steps.body: Install the coils and mounting bolts. The 2.3L requires 89 lb.in (10 Nm). The 3.7L requires 62 lb.in (7 Nm), then 50°. Both V8 procedures require 62 lb.in (7 Nm), then 45°. Reconnect the electrical connectors; on the 2.3L, secure the locking tabs and harness retainers.

steps.title: Restore the access components
steps.body: Refit the 3.7L upper intake manifold if removed. On the V8s, refit the coil covers and reconnect the ventilation couplings. Before fitting the 5.0L appearance cover, move any grommets retained in the cover back onto the intake manifold. On the 2.3L, refit the appearance cover, tighten its fasteners to 80 lb.in (9 Nm) and reconnect the battery through its procedure.

watchFor.title: Connector locks and seals
watchFor.body: Release the locking tab rather than pulling against it. Use the specified slight twist when lifting a coil whose boot seal remains attached.

notes: Use the procedure and illustration for your selected engine to identify the coils and their access requirements.

diagnostics.finding: Cracks, rips or tears are visible.
diagnostics.meaning: The assembly or rubber boot has physical damage requiring the engine-specific replacement action.
diagnostics.next: Replace the damaged assembly on the 2.3L, 5.0L or 5.2L; renew the damaged rubber boot on the 3.7L.

verification.title: Confirm tightening and restoration
verification.body: Check that the selected engine's torque and angle were completed, connectors are secured, and disturbed retainers, ventilation couplings and covers are restored. Confirm battery reconnection on the 2.3L and manifold installation where required on the 3.7L.

guides.title: Replace the 5.2L spark plugs
guides.summary: Replace the 5.2L spark plugs with the engine warm to hand touch, clean plug wells and controlled hand-tool tightening.
guides.introduction: Each spark plug delivers the ignition spark inside its cylinder, with an individual coil mounted above it. This job removes the coil-on-plug units to reach the plugs, then reinstalls the ignition components after plug service. Access is straightforward compared with internal engine work, but the temperature of the cylinder heads and the condition of each plug make careful handling essential.
guides.why: Removing plugs when the engine is hot or cold soaked can damage the plug threads or cylinder heads. Dirt around a plug also needs to be cleared before the opening is exposed. A dropped plug can have internal damage that leads to misfire and potentially engine damage, even when the damage is not obvious.

when.summary: When spark-plug service or replacement has been determined necessary on the 5.2L engine.
notes: A cylinder misfire alone does not identify a failed spark plug.

prepare.title: Establish the correct engine temperature
prepare.detail: Plan removal for when the engine is warm and can be touched by hand after cooling down. Do not begin with a hot or cold-soaked engine.

prepare.title: Prepare cleaning and hand tools
prepare.detail: Have compressed air, suitable spark-plug hand tools and a torque wrench capable of the specified setting. Do not use an impact wrench on the plugs.

steps.title: Remove the ignition coils
steps.body: Follow the 5.2L Ignition Coil-On-Plug procedure to remove the coils and expose the plug wells. Keep that procedure available for the return installation.

steps.title: Clear each plug well
steps.body: Before loosening a plug, use compressed air to remove foreign material from its well. This clears debris while the installed plug still closes the cylinder opening.

steps.title: Remove the plugs carefully
steps.body: Confirm the engine remains at the required warm condition, then remove the plugs with hand tools. Discard any plug that is dropped; do not judge it reusable solely by its appearance.

steps.title: Install the plugs and restore the coils
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Tighten the spark plugs to 133 lb.in (15 Nm), then reinstall the coil-on-plug units using their linked installation procedure.

watchFor.title: Unsuitable removal temperature
watchFor.body: Both excessive heat and a cold-soaked engine are prohibited removal conditions because of thread and cylinder-head damage risk.

watchFor.title: Dropped replacement plugs
watchFor.body: The discard instruction applies to a dropped plug before installation as well as one removed from the engine.

notes: The tightening value and temperature instructions here apply to the 5.2L procedure.

verification.title: Confirm the installation
verification.body: Confirm the plugs were tightened to the specified torque, no dropped plug was installed, and the coil-on-plug installation is complete.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L spark-plug removal and installation, temperature precautions and tightening specification.
Remove and reinstall the 5.2L ignition coil-on-plug units for access.

guides.title: Remove and refit the 2.3L EcoBoost crankcase oil separator
guides.summary: Remove the intake manifold to access the crankcase oil separator, inspect its gasket and restore both assemblies correctly.
guides.introduction: The crankcase vent oil separator helps separate carried oil from crankcase ventilation gases. On this engine, the intake manifold must come off to reach it. The work involves removing the separator housing, checking its sealing joint and refitting it with a serviceable gasket or a replacement where needed.
guides.why: The housing depends on clean mating faces and a sound gasket to seal properly. Much of this job concerns access: the intake manifold carries electrical connections, ventilation couplings and tube retainers that must all be restored.

when.summary: When the separator requires removal or replacement, or its gasket needs renewal.
notes: Gasket replacement depends on inspection; removal alone does not require a new gasket.

prepare.title: Provide intake-manifold access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist with the vehicle in NEUTRAL as directed by the intake-manifold procedure. Have suitable hand tools, a torque wrench and the capability to release the specified hose couplings without damaging them.

steps.title: Remove the intake manifold
steps.body: Follow [intake manifold removal](#/document/G1660523). Remove the appearance cover, release the evaporative-emissions purge connections and retainers, and move the purge valve aside. Disconnect the sensor and throttle wiring, move the charge-air cooler outlet tube aside and release the rear vacuum coupling. Free the coolant-tube attachment, move the manifold back, then disconnect the positive crankcase ventilation tube and knock-sensor connector retainers.

steps.title: Remove and examine the separator
steps.body: Follow the [separator procedure](#/document/G1673197) to remove its bolts and housing. Inspect the gasket around the mating perimeter. Replace it as necessary; retain it only if serviceable. Make both mating faces clean and free of corrosion and foreign material before refitting.

steps.title: Refit the housing and manifold
steps.body: Install the separator and tighten its bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). Inspect the intake-manifold gaskets for nicks, cuts and abrasions before reuse. Reconnect the ventilation coupling and knock-sensor retainers as the manifold is positioned. Ensure the coolant tube is correctly located and the manifold fits onto its stud before tightening the manifold and tube attachments to their respective specifications.

steps.title: Restore the remaining connections
steps.body: Complete the manifold installation sequence: reconnect the rear vacuum tube, charge-air outlet, throttle and sensor wiring, purge valve and its couplings. Secure the fuel and evaporative-emissions tubes in their retainer, then refit the appearance cover.

watchFor.title: Coolant-tube positioning
watchFor.body: The coolant tube must be in position when the intake manifold is installed; confirm alignment before tightening.

notes: If this work accompanies upper-engine failure, inspect the intake manifold for metal debris and replace the manifold if debris is found.

diagnostics.finding: The separator gasket is damaged or unserviceable.
diagnostics.meaning: The sealing joint needs attention; this finding alone does not establish an internal separator fault.
diagnostics.next: Renew the gasket and prepare the mating faces before assembly.

verification.title: Check the restored assembly
verification.body: Confirm separator bolt tightening, manifold and coolant-tube positioning, and reconnection of all disturbed couplings, electrical connectors and retainers.

verification.title: Complete the conditional road test
verification.body: If a new intake manifold was installed, road-test the vehicle.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L crankcase vent oil separator removal, gasket inspection and installation.
Required 2.3L intake-manifold access, gasket inspection and restoration.

guides.title: Replace the PCV valve on a 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine
guides.summary: Renew the positive crankcase ventilation valve using the correct engine access sequence and a lubricated new valve seal.
guides.introduction: The positive crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve forms part of the route carrying crankcase vapors into the intake system. A tube connects to the valve through a quick-release coupling, while an O-ring seals the valve into its mounting. The three engines share the replacement principle, but their cover-removal steps differ.
guides.why: Removing this valve damages its locking mechanism, so it must be replaced even if removal was only intended for inspection. Lubricating the new O-ring with clean engine oil helps it seat during installation. Correct coupling release also avoids forcing the attached ventilation tube.

when.summary: When PCV valve replacement is indicated, or whenever the installed valve has been removed.

prepare.title: Identify the engine and connection
prepare.detail: Select the matching valve and quick-release coupling procedures. Be able to release the tube coupling without forcing it.

prepare.title: Have the replacement ready
prepare.detail: Obtain the correct new PCV valve and clean engine oil for its O-ring. Plan to discard the removed valve.

steps.title: Open the appropriate access
steps.body: On the 5.0L, remove the engine appearance cover first. If its rubber grommets remain in the cover, remove them and return them to the intake manifold before later refitting the cover. The 3.7L and 5.2L procedures begin at the tube connection.

steps.title: Release the tube and remaining cover
steps.body: Disconnect the ventilation tube-to-valve quick-release coupling using the engine-specific coupling procedure. On the 5.0L and 5.2L, then remove the right-hand spark plug cover. The 3.7L procedure does not require that cover-removal step.

steps.title: Remove and discard the valve
steps.body: Rotate the valve counterclockwise and remove it. Discard it immediately so the damaged locking mechanism cannot be mistaken for a reusable part.

steps.title: Fit the new valve and restore access parts
steps.body: Lubricate the new valve's O-ring with clean engine oil. Install by reversing the applicable removal sequence: refit the valve, the right-hand spark plug cover where applicable, and the tube connection. Finish the 5.0L by refitting its appearance cover over the correctly positioned grommets.

watchFor.title: Reusing a removed valve
watchFor.body: An apparently intact valve still requires replacement after removal because its locking mechanism is damaged.

notes: The illustrated valve location is for the 3.7L. Use the matching V8 procedure for 5.0L or 5.2L access.

diagnostics.finding: The valve has already been removed.
diagnostics.meaning: It is no longer suitable for reinstallation, regardless of the original reason for removal.
diagnostics.next: Fit a new valve with its O-ring lubricated.

verification.title: Confirm complete reassembly
verification.body: Confirm that a new valve was fitted, the tube coupling is reconnected, and all applicable covers and grommets have been restored.

guides.title: Remove and refit the air cleaner outlet pipe: 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L
guides.summary: Remove the intake outlet pipe using the correct engine-specific tube connections, then restore the pipe, clamps and attached hoses.
guides.introduction: The air cleaner outlet pipe carries filtered air onward through the engine intake and provides connections for other tubes. Its removal is straightforward, but the attached tubes differ substantially between engines. On the 2.3L EcoBoost, keeping debris out is especially important because particles entering the intake can damage the turbocharger compressor vanes.
guides.why: Disconnecting every attached tube before moving the pipe avoids pulling on connections that are still secured. Correct reassembly restores the intended air path and each associated connection. Cleanliness on the turbocharged engine is a component-protection requirement, even when the pipe is only being removed temporarily.

when.summary: When the outlet pipe needs replacement or removal for access.
notes: Select the procedure by engine; the hose arrangements and number of pipe clamps differ.

prepare.title: Prepare for clamps and tube connections
prepare.detail: Have tools suitable for the fitted clamps and a torque wrench capable of their specified tightening value. Identify the engine before disconnecting anything.

prepare.title: Protect the 2.3L intake
prepare.detail: Keep debris from entering any opened turbocharger or engine intake component. Arrange a clean working area before exposing the pipe connections.

steps.title: Identify the connections and gain access
steps.body: Use the matching engine illustration to identify the outlet pipe and its attached tubes. On the 5.0L, remove the engine appearance cover first.

steps.title: Disconnect the engine-specific tubes
steps.body: For the [2.3L](#/document/G1675706), loosen the clamp and move aside the charge air cooler (CAC) bypass-valve inlet tube, then disconnect the crankcase ventilation tube. For the [3.7L](#/document/G1675695), disconnect the brake booster and crankcase ventilation tubes. For the [5.0L](#/document/G1675684), disconnect both brake booster tubes, the crankcase ventilation tube and the resonator air inlet tube.

steps.title: Release and remove the outlet pipe
steps.body: Loosen the three specified pipe clamps on the 2.3L, or the two pipe clamps on the 3.7L and 5.0L, and remove the pipe. Keep the disconnected tubes positioned aside and maintain debris protection at the open intake.

steps.title: Inspect where required and reverse the removal
steps.body: On the 2.3L, inspect the turbocharger or engine intake components and clean them if necessary before installation. Refit in reverse order. Tighten the outlet-pipe clamps identified in each procedure to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm), restore the tube connections and reinstall the 5.0L appearance cover.

watchFor.title: Turbocharger contamination
watchFor.body: Even very small particles can damage compressor vanes; do not leave contamination in the opened 2.3L intake.

watchFor.title: Clamp specification applied too broadly
watchFor.body: The stated torque accompanies the outlet-pipe clamp operation. Do not assume it specifies every other clamp on the attached tubing.

notes: On the 3.7L and 5.0L, a restricted air cleaner element can reduce performance and fuel economy. That condition alone does not establish a need to replace the outlet pipe.

verification.title: Confirm the air path is reassembled
verification.body: Check that the pipe is seated, its specified clamps are tightened and every tube disconnected for the selected engine is reconnected.

verification.title: Complete variant-specific work
verification.body: Confirm the 2.3L intake inspection and any necessary cleaning are complete, and the 5.0L appearance cover is restored.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost outlet-pipe removal and installation, including bypass tubing and intake cleanliness.
3.7L outlet-pipe removal and installation with brake booster and crankcase ventilation connections.
5.0L outlet-pipe removal and installation, including appearance cover and additional tube connections.

guides.title: Remove and refit the air cleaner: 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Remove the air cleaner assembly using the correct engine-specific pipe, wiring and coupling sequence, then restore every connection.
guides.introduction: The air cleaner houses the filtering element in the engine’s intake path. This job removes the assembly for replacement or access to nearby components. Although all four engines use an air cleaner, their connections differ: the 2.3L has intake-temperature wiring, the 5.0L includes airflow wiring and a sound symposer connection, and the 5.2L uses quick-release connections.
guides.why: Loose dirt must stay out of an opened intake. This is especially critical on the 2.3L, where even very small particles can damage turbocharger compressor vanes. Identifying the engine also prevents missed connections and use of the wrong clamp torque.

when.summary: When the air cleaner assembly needs replacement or removal to provide access for another repair.
notes: Assembly removal and scheduled filter-element replacement are different operations.

prepare.title: Select the engine-specific procedure
prepare.detail: Identify the engine before releasing connections. Have suitable fastener tools and a torque tool for the mounting bolt and outlet-pipe or hose clamp.

prepare.title: Prepare for clean disconnection
prepare.detail: Prevent debris entering the intake. For the 5.2L quick couplings, have compressed air to clean retaining-clip areas and blanking plugs for opened tubes or orifices.

prepare.title: Observe 5.2L coupling prerequisites
prepare.detail: Follow the quick-release procedure’s battery ground disconnection and reconnection requirements. Fuel-pressure release applies when servicing a liquid-fuel tube coupling. Identify the actual coupling type before releasing it.

steps.title: Protect the intake before opening it
steps.body: Keep the working area and exposed intake connections free of debris. On the 2.3L, maintain this protection throughout removal because the opened intake leads toward the turbocharger.

steps.title: 2.3L: release the pipe and temperature-sensor wiring
steps.body: Loosen the clamp and position the air outlet pipe aside. Detach the wiring harness retainers and disconnect the intake air temperature (IAT) sensor electrical connectors. Remove the mounting bolt, then remove the air cleaner assembly.

steps.title: 3.7L: release the outlet pipe and mounting
steps.body: Loosen the clamp and position the air cleaner outlet pipe aside. Remove the mounting bolt and remove the assembly. Follow this engine’s sequence and illustration for its layout.

steps.title: 5.0L: free the wiring and sound connection
steps.body: Loosen the clamp and move the outlet pipe away from the air cleaner. Disconnect the mass airflow (MAF) sensor connector. Detach and position the harness and sound symposer away from the housing, then remove the bolt and air cleaner.

steps.title: 5.2L: release the clipped and quick-release connections
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector and detach the clips. Following the coupling prerequisites, clean and release the quick connectors using the matching coupling procedure without tools. Remove the hose clamp, then the mounting bolt and air cleaner.

steps.title: Inspect and reverse the selected removal sequence
steps.body: On the 2.3L, inspect the turbocharger or engine intake components and clean as necessary. Reinstall the assembly and restore the connections for the selected engine. The mounting bolt is 8 Nm on all four variants. The 5.0L outlet clamp is 5 Nm; the specified clamp on the other three variants is 5.4 Nm.

watchFor.title: Damaged quick-release retainers
watchFor.body: Tools can deform coupling clips. Use the release method for the actual fitted type and confirm locking as directed, including the specified pull check where applicable.

watchFor.title: An overlooked attachment
watchFor.body: Before lifting the housing, confirm that the engine-specific wiring, clips and other attachments listed in its procedure have been released.

notes: The 5.0L sound symposer connection and the 5.2L quick-release sequence belong to their respective engine procedures.

diagnostics.finding: Air-filter restriction reaches its maximum on the 3.7L or 5.2L
diagnostics.meaning: The intake overview identifies adverse effects on engine performance and fuel economy.
diagnostics.next: Assess the filter element; reduced performance alone does not establish that the housing needs replacement.

verification.title: Confirm engine-specific restoration
verification.body: Check the mounting bolt, applicable clamp torque, pipe seating and every disturbed electrical or harness attachment. On the 5.0L, include the sound symposer connection.

verification.title: Finish the 5.2L coupling work
verification.body: Complete the fitted coupling’s locking checks and reconnect the battery ground cable as directed by the coupling procedure.
