guides.title: Remove and refit the 2.3L EcoBoost charge-air cooler intake pipes
guides.summary: Follow the separate upper- or lower-pipe access sequence, protect the open air passages, and reconnect the pipes at the specified clamp torque.
guides.introduction: The charge-air cooler (CAC) reduces the temperature of compressed intake air in the turbocharger system. Its intake pipework provides the air path to the cooler. The upper and lower sections have different removal sequences: upper-pipe work includes an electrical connection and bypass tube, while lower-pipe removal requires hoist access.
guides.why: Cleanliness is critical whenever turbocharger air passages are opened. Even small particles can damage the compressor vanes, so every open port must be protected and every component inspected and cleaned before assembly. Correct clamp tightening also matters: these connections use an inch-pound torque setting, which must not be confused with a foot-pound setting.
searchTerms: 2.3L EcoBoost charge air cooler intake pipe
lower charge air cooler pipe removal

when.summary: When an upper or lower CAC intake pipe needs replacement or removal for access.
notes: Choose the upper or lower branch for the pipe being removed; their access steps are different.

prepare.title: Provide clean port protection
prepare.detail: Have suitable clean covers ready before disconnecting the pipework. All opened ports require cleaning, inspection and covering, and all components require inspection and cleaning before reassembly.

prepare.title: Prepare clamp-tightening equipment
prepare.detail: Use appropriate clamp tools and a torque wrench capable of 44 lb.in (5 Nm), the setting specified for the clamps released in this procedure.

prepare.title: Arrange safe lower-pipe access
prepare.detail: Lower-pipe work requires the vehicle in NEUTRAL on a hoist. Identify the lifting points by their stamped triangles and position the hoist adapters without contacting vulnerable suspension, exhaust or steering components.

steps.title: Upper pipe: release its attached connections
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector and detach the wiring-harness retainers. Disconnect the bypass tube and position it aside. Freeing these attachments allows the pipe to be removed without leaving them connected to the moving assembly.

steps.title: Upper pipe: separate the pipe joints
steps.body: Loosen the clamp and move the lower intake pipe aside. Then loosen the upper intake-pipe clamp and remove the upper pipe. Clean and inspect the exposed ports and keep them covered.

steps.title: Lower pipe: establish hoist access
steps.body: For lower-pipe removal, place the vehicle in NEUTRAL and position it on a hoist using the Jacking and Lifting procedure. Confirm the adapters and vehicle clearances before raising it.

steps.title: Lower pipe: release the adjoining pipework
steps.body: Loosen the clamp and position the lower intake pipe aside, then loosen the clamp and position the upper intake pipe aside. Remove the underbody shielding specified for the vehicle where fitted.

steps.title: Lower pipe: remove and protect
steps.body: Loosen the remaining lower-pipe clamp and remove the lower intake pipe. Clean, inspect and cover every open port so the system remains protected during the repair.

steps.title: Reassemble the selected branch
steps.body: After inspecting and cleaning the components, reverse the applicable removal sequence. Tighten the released clamps to 44 lb.in (5 Nm). Restore the bypass tube, connector and harness retainers for upper-pipe work, and the removed underbody shielding for lower-pipe work.

watchFor.title: Uncovered air passages
watchFor.body: Do not leave open ports exposed while other work continues; small debris can damage the turbocharger.

watchFor.title: Unsupported underbody access
watchFor.body: Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. The vehicle’s emergency jack is not intended for this repair.

notes: The upper-pipe illustration identifies its clamp connection; it does not replace the separate lower-pipe access sequence.

verification.title: Check cleanliness and connections
verification.body: Confirm inspection and cleaning are complete, all opened pipe joints are reconnected, and the specified clamp torque has been applied.

verification.title: Check the branch-specific refit
verification.body: Verify all connections, harness retainers and shields disturbed by the chosen removal branch have been restored.

procedures.purpose: Separate upper- and lower-CAC-intake-pipe removal and installation procedures for the 2.3L EcoBoost.
Lifting-point identification, hoist positioning and support precautions for lower-pipe access.

guides.title: Remove and Refit the 2.3L EcoBoost Charge Air Cooler Outlet Pipe
guides.summary: Remove the charge air cooler outlet pipe through its clamped connections while protecting the turbocharger air system from contamination.
guides.introduction: The charge air cooler (CAC) outlet pipe carries cooled, compressed intake air onward toward the engine. Its clamped connections join the pipe to the adjoining air passages. This job disconnects those joints and removes any fitted underbody shields needed for access, allowing the pipe to be removed, inspected and refitted or replaced.
guides.why: Cleanliness matters whenever the turbocharger air system is opened: even tiny particles can damage compressor vanes. Covering open ports promptly and cleaning components before assembly prevents debris from being left inside. Specified clamp tightening also matters when restoring the connections.
searchTerms: 2.3L EcoBoost charge air cooler outlet pipe
charge air cooler outlet pipe clamps

when.summary: When the CAC outlet pipe requires removal, replacement or access-related disconnection.
notes: Remove underbody shields only where fitted, following the applicable access illustrations.

prepare.title: Prepare safe underside access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the designated lifting points identified by stamped triangles. Check adapter and underbody clearance. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; the emergency wheel-change jack is unsuitable for this work.

prepare.title: Prepare clean port protection
prepare.detail: Have clean covers ready before opening either connection, suitable clamp tools, and a torque wrench capable of 44 lb.in (5 Nm). Plan to inspect and clean all removed components before reassembly.

steps.title: Position the vehicle and disconnect the first joint
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a hoist using [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631). Follow the [outlet-pipe procedure](#/document/G1827246) to loosen the first clamp and disconnect the pipe. Cover the opened passages.

steps.title: Clear the underside access
steps.body: Remove each fitted underbody shield shown in the access sequence. This exposes the remaining pipe connection; use the procedure illustrations to identify the applicable shields and attachment locations.

steps.title: Remove and inspect the pipe
steps.body: Loosen the remaining clamp and remove the outlet pipe. Clean and inspect the removed components and exposed ports, then keep every open port covered until assembly.

steps.title: Restore the connections and shields
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Remove protective covers as the clean connections are assembled, tighten each outlet-pipe clamp to 44 lb.in (5 Nm), and reinstall the shields removed for access.

watchFor.title: Unprotected openings
watchFor.body: Do not leave a disconnected air passage exposed while working elsewhere. Contamination can enter before the pipe is ready to refit.

watchFor.title: Incorrect lifting contact
watchFor.body: Hoist adapters must clear suspension, steering, exhaust and mounting components; incorrect contact can damage the vehicle.

notes: The clamp specification is in pound-inches, not pound-feet.

verification.title: Check the restored assembly
verification.body: Confirm both pipe connections are assembled, both clamps are tightened, all temporary port covers are removed, and every removed shield is refitted.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost CAC outlet-pipe removal and installation, including conditional shield access and clamp tightening.
Correct vehicle lifting points, support precautions and hoist-clearance requirements.

guides.title: Replace the charge air cooler on the 2.3L EcoBoost
guides.summary: Remove the charge air cooler through the lower front access area while protecting the intake system and correctly preparing its tube joints for reassembly.
guides.introduction: The charge air cooler (CAC) cools air compressed by the turbocharger before it continues toward the engine. Its inlet and outlet tubes carry that air through the cooler, and the turbocharger boost pressure sensor has an electrical connection at the assembly. Replacement involves removing front-end access parts, separating both air tubes and releasing the cooler from its mountings in the illustrated sequence.
guides.why: Cleanliness is central to this job: even small particles can damage the turbocharger compressor vanes. The tube joints also need specific preparation during installation. Cleaning the clamp areas helps restore the connections correctly, while following the mounting-release sequence avoids pulling against retainers that are still engaged.

when.summary: When a confirmed repair requires removal or replacement of the 2.3L EcoBoost charge air cooler.
notes: This procedure covers physical removal and installation, rather than diagnosing the cause of a boost-related complaint.

prepare.title: Arrange front underside access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the correct lifting points. Check that its adapters clear suspension and other underbody components. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare for clean intake work
prepare.detail: Have suitable hand tools, torque equipment and metal brake parts cleaner for the tube joint clamp areas. Plan to prevent debris entering either disconnected air path and to inspect intake components before assembly.

steps.title: Remove the access components
steps.body: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on the hoist. Remove the [active grille shutter](#/document/G1693244), then remove the four bolts and lower radiator support bracket. These components must be out of the way before the cooler is released.

steps.title: Disconnect the sensor and air tubes
steps.body: Disconnect the turbocharger boost pressure sensor electrical connector from the cooler. Loosen the inlet-tube clamp and separate the inlet tube, then do the same at the outlet tube. Keep dirt and loose debris out of the opened intake components.

steps.title: Release the cooler in the illustrated order
steps.body: Follow the numbered illustration in the [charge air cooler procedure](#/document/G1675707): remove the mounting bolt, release the illustrated retaining feature and disengage the cooler from its supports in the directions shown. Use the illustration to identify those features before attempting removal.

steps.title: Inspect and prepare the air path
steps.body: Inspect the turbocharger or engine air intake components and clean them if necessary. Before installing the cooler tubes, thoroughly clean their joint clamp areas with metal brake parts cleaner. This preparation is an explicit installation requirement.

steps.title: Reinstall the cooler and restore access parts
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, engaging the cooler mountings and installing its bolt. Reconnect both tubes and tighten their clamps to the specified torque, then reconnect the sensor. Reinstall the lower radiator support bracket and active grille shutter using their respective procedures.

watchFor.title: Debris entering an open tube
watchFor.body: Do not continue assembly with contamination present. The intake-system warning applies even to particles small enough to be easily overlooked.

watchFor.title: Retainers still engaged
watchFor.body: The mounting bolt is only one part of the release sequence. Check the illustrated retaining features before trying to remove the cooler.

notes: Use the specified torque for each mounting bolt and tube clamp; these connections do not share one tightening value.
Keep the specified cleaner use focused on the tube joint clamp areas.

verification.title: Confirm intake cleanliness and connections
verification.body: Confirm that inspection and any necessary cleaning are complete, both air tubes are reconnected and their prepared clamp areas are secured.

verification.title: Confirm complete reassembly
verification.body: Check that the sensor connector, cooler retention, lower radiator support bracket and active grille shutter have all been restored.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost charge air cooler removal, illustrated mounting release, cleaning and installation.
Correct lifting points and hoist-positioning precautions.
Active grille shutter removal and installation for cooler access.

guides.title: Find an evaporative-emission leak with scan-tool and smoke testing
guides.summary: Run the electronic leak test, then use controlled smoke testing to locate leakage when the test fails or suspicion remains.
guides.introduction: The evaporative emission (EVAP) system contains fuel vapors and routes them through its canister and purge system. A leak allows vapor to escape from that intended path. This procedure first checks system integrity electronically, then uses visible smoke to identify the location requiring repair.
guides.why: A passing scan-tool test can miss some small leaks. Smoke testing adds a location-based check, but the system must first fill with smoke and the capless filler must return to its closed condition before searching for unintended escape points.
searchTerms: EVAP test passed leak still suspected

when.summary: When an EVAP leak is suspected, including after a passing scan-tool test if suspicion remains.
notes: Use the procedure and fuel-vapor coupling instructions for the installed engine.

prepare.title: Provide the specified test equipment
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of running the EVAP Test and controlling the canister vent solenoid, plus the VACUTEC Smoke Machine Fuel EVAP Emissions System Tester and its supplied halogen light.

prepare.title: Prepare the connection and filler adapter
prepare.detail: Have the engine-specific Quick Release Coupling and Battery Disconnect and Connect procedures available. Locate the supplemental refueling adapter in the jack storage compartment.

steps.title: Run Phase 1: leak verification
steps.body: For the 2.3L and 5.0L, first view the referenced “FDRS EVAP System Test” video. Run the scan-tool EVAP Test. Continue to Phase 2 after a failure, or after a pass when a leak is still suspected.

steps.title: Connect the smoke tester
steps.body: Follow the engine-specific coupling procedure to disconnect the fuel vapor tube from the canister purge valve. That prerequisite includes battery-ground disconnection. Connect the VACUTEC tester to the vapor-tube coupling according to its instructions, then reconnect the battery ground cable using the battery procedure.

steps.title: Close the vent and establish smoke flow
steps.body: Command the canister vent solenoid closed with the scan tool. Insert the supplemental refueling adapter into the capless filler. Introduce smoke and verify that it emerges from the filler-neck area.

steps.title: Purge trapped air when necessary
steps.body: If smoke does not emerge from the filler after pressurization, open the vent solenoid with the scan tool. Once smoke appears at the vent solenoid, close it again. Remove the refueling adapter once smoke is observed at the filler neck.

steps.title: Pressurize and trace the leak
steps.body: Continue introducing smoke for 60 seconds to obtain pressure. Operate the smoke tester's remote start button in intervals of 15 seconds ON and 15 seconds OFF while checking. Follow the EVAP system path with the supplied halogen light to locate escaping smoke.

steps.title: Repair and repeat
steps.body: Repair the identified leaks as necessary, then repeat the leak test until the system passes. Finding one escape point does not finish the job if the repeated test still fails.

watchFor.title: Intentional smoke outlets
watchFor.body: Smoke at the open filler during setup, or at the vent during air purging, serves a test-preparation purpose. Distinguish those observations from leakage during the closed-system check.

watchFor.title: Equipment operating instructions
watchFor.body: Use the VACUTEC manufacturer's connection and operating instructions; the timed remote-button operation belongs to the smoke-testing sequence.

notes: The four engine procedures share the test sequence, but their fuel-vapor coupling prerequisites are engine-specific.

diagnostics.finding: The scan-tool EVAP Test fails.
diagnostics.meaning: Further leak checking is required; the result does not identify a failed component.
diagnostics.next: Proceed to Phase 2 smoke testing.

diagnostics.finding: The EVAP Test passes but a leak remains suspected.
diagnostics.meaning: Some small leaks may escape detection by the electronic test.
diagnostics.next: Proceed to Phase 2 rather than dismissing the concern.

diagnostics.finding: Smoke escapes from an unintended point during the closed-system check.
diagnostics.meaning: The smoke identifies a leakage location.
diagnostics.next: Repair that location and repeat testing until the system passes.

verification.title: Obtain a passing repeat test
verification.body: Repeat the leak test after repair until the system passes.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record the initial EVAP Test result, smoke-leak locations, repairs performed and final passing result.

guides.title: Replace the evaporative-emission canister purge valve
guides.summary: Remove and refit the purge valve using the correct engine-specific access, vapor-line coupling and fastening procedure.
guides.introduction: The evaporative-emission (EVAP) system manages fuel vapor, and the canister purge valve controls its passage toward the engine. This job replaces that valve and reconnects its electrical control and vapor plumbing. The purpose is shared across the engines, but cover removal, coupling arrangements and mounting torque differ.
guides.why: Fuel-related components can contain ignitable vapor even when no liquid fuel is visible. Battery isolation and ignition-source precautions matter throughout the work. Clean, undamaged quick-release couplings are equally important: forcing their clips can deform them and leave an insecure or leaking connection.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the EVAP canister purge valve requires replacement.
notes: The removal procedure does not establish the cause of an emissions complaint.

prepare.title: Remove ignition sources
prepare.detail: Do not smoke, carry lighted tobacco or use open flames near the work. Keep personal electronic devices, including phones and audio equipment, away from fuel-related components.

prepare.title: Prepare for clean, controlled removal
prepare.detail: Have suitable hand tools, a low-range torque wrench, compressed air and blanking plugs available. Identify the engine and its coupling procedure before releasing any connector.

steps.title: Isolate battery power
steps.body: Remove the battery-cover retainers and cover, then disconnect and position the negative cable using the battery procedure. Disconnecting the positive cable is unnecessary for interrupting vehicle power. Keep the ground cable disconnected while working on the EVAP components.

steps.title: Expose the valve using the correct engine branch
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove the appearance-cover nuts and cover. On the 5.0L, remove the appearance cover. On the 5.2L, remove it if equipped. The 3.7L procedure proceeds directly to the valve connections.

steps.title: Release electrical and vapor connections
steps.body: Disconnect the valve electrical connector, then release its vapor coupling or couplings using the engine-specific quick-release procedure. Clean debris from the retaining-clip area before separation and plug open tubes. Do not pry coupling clips with tools. The 2.3L has multiple valve quick connections; the other branches specify a single coupling.

steps.title: Remove and install the valve
steps.body: Remove the mounting bolt on the 2.3L or the mounting bolts on the other engines, then remove the valve. Install in reverse order. Tighten the 2.3L valve bolt to 71 lb.in (8 Nm); tighten the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L valve bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the connections, cover and power
steps.body: Inspect and clean coupling ends, remove the blanking plugs and reconnect the vapor plumbing using the correct retainer sequence. Reconnect the electrical connector and restore the applicable appearance cover. The 2.3L cover nuts require 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Reconnect the negative battery cable, tighten its nut to 44 lb.in (5 Nm), and restore the battery cover.

watchFor.title: Coupling designs release differently
watchFor.body: Use the procedure matching the fitted connector. Do not assume every coupling uses the secondary-lock arrangement described for Type 8.

watchFor.title: Vapor-line work and liquid-fuel work have different prerequisites
watchFor.body: The coupling procedure requires fuel-pressure release when servicing a liquid fuel tube. If work extends into liquid-fuel plumbing, complete that prerequisite before opening it.

notes: After battery reconnection, temporary changes in driving behavior may occur while the powertrain control module relearns adaptive values; driving may be needed for that learning.

verification.title: Confirm coupling retention
verification.body: For the specified Type 1 connection, check that the retainer is flush and locked, then pull on the coupling. For Type 8, push the coupling onto the tube, pull the coupling and fitting to confirm engagement, then lock the secondary tab. Follow the corresponding check for the actual fitted coupling.

verification.title: Check final assembly
verification.body: Confirm the electrical connection, engine-specific valve fastening, any removed appearance cover and the negative battery connection are restored. Physical installation alone does not establish that the original diagnostic complaint is resolved.

guides.title: Replace the evaporative-emission canister vent solenoid
guides.summary: Remove the engine-specific evaporative-emission canister assembly, replace its vent solenoid and restore the shield, connections and mountings.
guides.introduction: The evaporative-emission (EVAP) system handles fuel vapor, and the canister vent solenoid electrically controls a vent path at the canister. This job removes the canister before servicing the solenoid and its shield. The solenoid procedures cover the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines, with separate canister-removal references for each engine.
guides.why: Removing the canister provides access to the solenoid connector and protective shield. Fuel vapor makes ignition control and battery disconnection essential precautions. The shared solenoid sequence does not establish that every canister attachment or coupling is identical, so the access and reinstallation work must stay with the matching engine procedure.

when.summary: When canister vent-solenoid replacement has been established as necessary.
notes: These removal procedures do not provide a diagnostic test proving that the solenoid has failed.
Select the canister and solenoid procedures for the installed engine.

prepare.title: Control fuel-vapor ignition hazards
prepare.detail: Keep smoking materials and open flames away. Do not carry personal electronic devices while working on or near fuel-related components. Disconnect the battery ground cable at the battery before EVAP work.

prepare.title: Arrange safe access
prepare.detail: The supplied 2.3L and 3.7L canister procedures require a hoist. Have suitable lifting capability and follow the applicable canister procedure's lifting and battery-disconnection references.

prepare.title: Prepare connection and tightening tools
prepare.detail: Have tools for the shield and canister attachments, including a torque wrench suitable for the specified low tightening values. Follow the engine-specific quick-release coupling instructions during canister removal.

steps.title: Select the engine procedure and prepare the vehicle
steps.body: Use the matching canister procedure: [2.3L](#/document/G1688006), [3.7L](#/document/G1688029), [5.0L](#/document/G1688054) or [5.2L](#/document/G1805778). Complete its access prerequisites and disconnect the battery ground cable before handling EVAP connections.

steps.title: Remove the canister assembly
steps.body: On the supplied 2.3L and 3.7L routes, disconnect the canister electrical connector, remove the bracket bolts and pin-type retainers, then remove the remaining bolts and nuts to lower the canister. Disconnect the quick-connect couplings and vent hose before removing it. For 5.0L and 5.2L, follow their own linked canister procedures for this phase.

steps.title: Disconnect the solenoid connector
steps.body: With the canister removed, disconnect the solenoid's electrical connector. This is a separate step from disconnecting the canister assembly during vehicle removal. The supplied 3.7L illustration identifies this solenoid connection.

steps.title: Remove the protective shield
steps.body: Remove the shield bolts and the EVAP canister shield to expose the solenoid for removal. All four supplied solenoid procedures specify 62 lb.in (7 Nm) for these shield bolts during installation.

steps.title: Remove and replace the solenoid
steps.body: Follow the matching solenoid procedure: [2.3L](#/document/G1688009), [3.7L](#/document/G1688032), [5.0L](#/document/G1688057) or [5.2L](#/document/G1805781). The supplied 2.3L image shows rotation followed by withdrawal; use the appropriate procedure for the particular assembly without assuming a rotation angle.

steps.title: Restore the canister and vehicle connections
steps.body: Reverse the solenoid-removal sequence: install the solenoid, refit the shield and tighten its bolts, then reconnect the solenoid. Reinstall the canister using the engine-specific reverse sequence, restoring its hoses, couplings, electrical connection and mountings. Complete battery reconnection through the applicable battery procedure.

watchFor.title: Different attachment torques
watchFor.body: The 2.3L and 3.7L canister procedures distinguish bracket hardware from other canister fasteners. Use the applicable attachment value rather than applying the shield-bolt torque throughout.

watchFor.title: Incomplete connection restoration
watchFor.body: The job disturbs electrical connectors, quick-connect couplings and a vent hose. Account for each connection as the canister is refitted.

notes: The canister vent solenoid is distinct from the canister purge valve identified in the supplied 5.0L system diagram.
The removal sequences contain installation torque information, so keep them available throughout reassembly.

verification.title: Check assembly restoration
verification.body: Confirm that the solenoid and shield are installed, both stages of electrical connection are restored, and the canister hoses, couplings and mountings are complete.

verification.title: Record tightening completion
verification.body: Record shield-bolt tightening to 62 lb.in (7 Nm) and completion of the engine-specific canister attachment checks.

guides.title: Replace the Evaporative Emission Canister Ventilation Filter
guides.summary: Remove the engine-specific evaporative emission canister assembly, replace its ventilation filter and restore the shield and connections.
guides.introduction: The evaporative emission system, commonly called EVAP, manages fuel vapour. Its canister ventilation filter protects the ventilation path from dirt. Replacing this filter requires removing the canister, exposing the filter beneath the shield and releasing its retaining tabs. The filter-level sequence is shared across the supplied engine variants, but canister access must follow the procedure for the fitted engine.
guides.why: Although the part being replaced is a filter, this work opens connections on a fuel-vapour system. Ignition precautions and battery disconnection therefore apply. The solenoid is removed only if necessary for access; keeping that step conditional avoids unnecessary handling of another component.

when.summary: When the canister ventilation filter has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Use the filter and canister-removal procedures that match the engine.
The detailed canister access sequence described here applies to the supplied 2.3L and 3.7L instructions.

prepare.title: Control ignition sources
prepare.detail: Do not smoke, carry lighted tobacco, use an open flame or carry personal electronic devices near the fuel-related components. Flammable mixtures may be present.

prepare.title: Arrange access and isolation
prepare.detail: Have suitable lifting capability and follow the applicable canister procedure. The 2.3L and 3.7L procedures require a hoist. Disconnect the battery ground cable at the battery before EVAP work, following Battery Disconnect and Connect.

prepare.title: Prepare for connections and fasteners
prepare.detail: Be able to use the engine-specific quick-release coupling procedure and accurately tighten the shield and canister mounting hardware.

steps.title: Select the correct filter procedure
steps.body: Use the procedure for [2.3L EcoBoost](#/document/G1688008), [3.7L Duratec](#/document/G1688031), [5.0L](#/document/G1688056) or [5.2L](#/document/G1805780). Each starts by removing the EVAP canister.

steps.title: Remove the canister using its engine-specific path
steps.body: Follow the canister procedure for [2.3L](#/document/G1688006), [3.7L](#/document/G1688029), [5.0L](#/document/G1688054) or [5.2L](#/document/G1805778). On the supplied 2.3L and 3.7L paths, disconnect the electrical connector, remove the bracket and mounting hardware, lower the canister, then disconnect the quick-connect couplings and vent hose.

steps.title: Expose the ventilation filter
steps.body: With the canister removed, disconnect the canister solenoid electrical connector. Remove the bolts and canister shield to reach the filter assembly.

steps.title: Remove the solenoid only if necessary
steps.body: If the solenoid must be removed to gain access, follow the matching filter procedure's illustration. This is a conditional operation, not a requirement for every filter replacement.

steps.title: Release and replace the filter
steps.body: Release the retaining tabs and remove the ventilation filter. Install the replacement by reversing that operation, restoring its tab retention before reassembling the surrounding components.

steps.title: Restore the canister assembly
steps.body: Reinstall the solenoid if removed, refit the shield and tighten its bolts to 62 lb.in (7 Nm). Reconnect the solenoid connector. Reverse the applicable canister-removal procedure, restoring its hoses, couplings, electrical connection and mountings, then complete battery reconnection as directed.

watchFor.title: Confusing mounting fasteners
watchFor.body: Use the applicable canister procedure for mounting torques. The filter shield specification is not a blanket value for every bracket fastener.

watchFor.title: Incomplete tab engagement
watchFor.body: The filter is retained by tabs; make sure that retention is restored during installation.

notes: The filter replacement procedures provide no diagnostic test that would identify this part as the cause of an EVAP complaint.

verification.title: Check the filter assembly
verification.body: Confirm the filter tabs are engaged, the solenoid is restored if removed, and the shield and electrical connector are installed.

verification.title: Check the vehicle connections
verification.body: Confirm completion of the engine-specific canister installation, including all disconnected hoses, couplings, connectors and mounting hardware.

guides.title: Replace the evaporative emission canister
guides.summary: Remove and reinstall the underbody vapor canister using the correct engine procedure, including the additional shield and differential-cooler access on the 5.2L.
guides.introduction: The evaporative emission (EVAP) canister stores fuel vapor as part of the system connecting the fuel tank and purge path to the engine intake. It is a separate component from the purge valve. Replacement involves its underbody mountings, electrical connector, vapor couplings and vent hose. The main sequence is similar across engines, but the 5.2L requires additional access work.
guides.why: Fuel vapor can form highly flammable mixtures even though this job does not open a liquid-fuel supply line. Battery isolation and ignition-source control are essential. The canister is lowered before its vapor connections are released, so controlling its movement avoids loading the attached hoses. Correct engine selection also keeps shield and cooler fasteners from being confused with canister mountings.

when.summary: When a repair requires removal or replacement of the EVAP canister.
notes: Use the engine-specific procedure; the 5.2L shield and differential-cooler access steps are additional to the common canister work.

prepare.title: Fuel-vapor precautions
prepare.detail: Exclude smoking, lighted tobacco and open flames. The 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.2L procedures also explicitly prohibit carrying personal electronic devices near the work. Follow the referenced fuel-system safety precautions for the 5.0L.

prepare.title: Safe underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the triangle-marked lifting points. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack, and do not use the emergency tire-changing jack for this job. Check lift clearance and protect suspension, exhaust, steering and axle components when positioning the lift.

prepare.title: Connection and tightening capability
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastener tools and torque equipment, plus the applicable battery and quick-release coupling procedures. Installation torques appear alongside removal steps in each engine's canister procedure.

steps.title: Lift the vehicle and isolate the battery
steps.body: Position the vehicle on a hoist using [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631). Disconnect the battery ground cable using [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356) before disturbing the canister electrical connection. For the 5.0L, follow the [fuel-system safety precautions](#/document/G1693188) referenced by its procedure.

steps.title: Open the 5.2L shield access
steps.body: For the 5.2L only, follow [its canister procedure](#/document/G1805778): remove the rear underbody shield rear bolts, push-pin retainers, front bolts and rivet-style push-pin retainers in the stated order. These fastener groups have different installation requirements.

steps.title: Position the 5.2L cooler components aside
steps.body: On the 5.2L, remove the retainers and position the rear differential fluid cooler aside. Then remove the retainer and position its pump bracket aside. Keep the attached assemblies controlled while gaining access to the canister.

steps.title: Remove the electrical connection and bracket
steps.body: For every engine, disconnect the canister electrical connector. Remove the bracket bolts, pin-type retainers and bracket, following the selected engine procedure so each attachment can be restored correctly.

steps.title: Lower the canister
steps.body: Remove the remaining mounting bolts, then remove the nuts and lower the canister. Support its movement because the vapor couplings and vent hose are still connected at this stage.

steps.title: Release the vapor connections
steps.body: Release the vapor-line couplings using the illustrated method for the fitted connector: [2.3L](#/document/G1671510), [3.7L](#/document/G1671536), [5.0L](#/document/G1671557) or [5.2L](#/document/G1794918). Disconnect the vent hose and remove the canister.

steps.title: Install in reverse order
steps.body: Reconnect the vent hose and vapor couplings, raise and secure the canister, and restore its bracket and electrical connection. Use the torque for each fastener group in the selected engine procedure. On the 5.2L, restore the cooler, pump bracket and shield through the reverse access sequence. Complete battery reconnection using its referenced procedure.

watchFor.title: Hoses carrying the canister's weight
watchFor.body: Lower the canister under control until its connections can be released.

watchFor.title: Mixed installation settings
watchFor.body: The bracket, canister mountings and 5.2L access hardware do not all share one tightening value.

notes: Follow the procedure for your selected engine to identify the canister connections and complete its access sequence.

verification.title: Check restored connections
verification.body: Confirm the quick-connect couplings, vent hose and electrical connector are restored and the canister and bracket are secured.

verification.title: Check variant-specific completion
verification.body: On the 5.2L, confirm the differential cooler, pump bracket and underbody shield are reinstalled. Confirm battery reconnection is complete for every variant.

verification.title: Record tightening completion
verification.body: Record the engine procedure used and completion of its installation torque requirements, including the separate 5.2L access hardware where applicable.

guides.title: Replace the fuel tank pressure sensor and tube
guides.summary: Remove the rear subframe to access and replace the engine-specific fuel tank pressure sensor and tube assembly.
guides.introduction: The fuel tank pressure sensor provides pressure information for the evaporative emissions, or EVAP, system. Its tube assembly forms part of the connected vapor plumbing around the tank. Replacement involves electrical and tube connections, but the major access operation is rear-subframe removal. The procedures for the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines share this overall sequence while directing you to different engine-specific coupling procedures.
guides.why: Fuel-related work can expose highly flammable mixtures, so ignition precautions and battery disconnection are essential even though this is an emissions-system component. Releasing the routing clips as well as the couplings prevents the tube from being pulled against attachments that are still secured. Correct routing on installation restores the assembly without leaving its connections carrying unintended loads.
searchTerms: rear subframe fuel tank sensor access

when.summary: When diagnosis or physical damage establishes that the fuel tank pressure sensor and tube need replacement.
notes: This is an access-intensive replacement procedure, not a test that establishes sensor failure.

prepare.title: Provide lifting and subframe capability
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the complete rear-subframe procedure. Locate lifting points by the stamped triangles and position adapters clear of suspension, steering, exhaust and axle components. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; the emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this job.

prepare.title: Remove ignition hazards
prepare.detail: Do not smoke or have lighted tobacco or open flames nearby. Do not carry personal electronic devices, including phones or audio equipment, while working on or near fuel-related components.

prepare.title: Plan electrical isolation
prepare.detail: The battery ground cable must be disconnected at the battery before working on the EVAP assembly. Have the Battery Disconnect and Connect procedure available.

steps.title: Choose the engine-specific procedure
steps.body: Follow the assembly details for [2.3L](#/document/G1688010), [3.7L](#/document/G1688033), [5.0L](#/document/G1688058) or [5.2L](#/document/G1805782). Use the corresponding tube routing and connection locations throughout the repair.

steps.title: Position and isolate the vehicle
steps.body: Position the vehicle on a hoist using the [lifting instructions](#/document/G1663631). Then disconnect the battery ground cable following [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356), before beginning fuel-related disconnections.

steps.title: Remove the rear subframe
steps.body: Complete the removal phase of the [rear-subframe procedure](#/document/G1686636). This is a required access operation, with its own support and reassembly requirements.

steps.title: Release the first connections and routing
steps.body: Disconnect the initial quick-release coupling, routing clips and fuel tank pressure sensor electrical connector as shown in the selected engine procedure. Then release the separately identified routing clips so the tube is no longer held along that section.

steps.title: Free the remaining tube connections
steps.body: Disconnect the next quick-release coupling and routing clips, then the final coupling and clips before removing the sensor and tube. Use the coupling method for [2.3L](#/document/G1671510), [3.7L](#/document/G1671536), [5.0L](#/document/G1671557) or [5.2L](#/document/G1794918); do not pull the assembly free while a connection remains secured.

steps.title: Install in reverse order
steps.body: Restore the sensor and tube, couplings, routing clips and electrical connector by reversing removal. Reinstall the rear subframe through its complete procedure, then restore the battery connection and finish the lifting operation through their respective instructions.

watchFor.title: A tube still caught in a clip
watchFor.body: The removal sequence releases clips in several stages. Resistance can mean that a routing attachment remains connected; pulling harder can damage the assembly or its connections.

watchFor.title: Hoist interference
watchFor.body: Check adapter placement and underbody clearance before lifting. Incorrect positioning can damage surrounding components or leave the vehicle insecure.

notes: The shared removal sequence does not make the engine-specific coupling instructions or illustrated routing interchangeable.
Replacement alone does not demonstrate sensor accuracy or resolve the cause of an undiagnosed EVAP complaint.

verification.title: Check the restored assembly
verification.body: Confirm that all couplings, routing clips and the sensor electrical connector released during removal have been restored in the engine-specific arrangement.

verification.title: Confirm prerequisite reassembly
verification.body: Confirm completion of the rear-subframe installation and battery reconnection procedures. Do not treat the tube installation alone as completion of the repair.

guides.title: Choose the correct diagnostic path for 2.3L EcoBoost engine-control codes
guides.summary: Use recorded engine-control codes, preliminary checks and fitted equipment to select the correct system test before considering replacement parts.
guides.introduction: The electronic engine control system uses sensor and switch inputs to manage engine outputs through the powertrain control module (PCM). Its software also monitors faults. Because the PCM exchanges information with other systems, a diagnostic trouble code (DTC) recorded there can lead to transmission, braking, climate-control or network diagnosis.
guides.why: A code describes a detected condition, not necessarily a failed component. Distinguishing circuit faults from operating-condition faults, and checking shared electrical supplies, prevents misleading results and unnecessary module replacement.

when.summary: When a current engine-control concern or recorded PCM code needs a system-specific diagnostic route.

prepare.title: Diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable scan tool and Diagnostic Methods. Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. PCM programming requires suitable equipment and knowledge.

prepare.title: Circuit-testing equipment
prepare.detail: For directed electrical checks, have wiring diagrams, a digital multimeter and the required Rotunda Flex Probes. Follow circuit-isolation requirements before resistance measurements.

steps.title: Establish the current concern
steps.body: Review previous repairs and applicable service information. Inspect wiring, connectors and fuses, then relevant intake, vacuum, fluid and mechanical conditions. Do not follow a component-replacement decision when the test's stated concern is absent.

steps.title: Record and prioritize codes
steps.body: Retrieve codes from all network modules. Diagnose circuit-related codes before system or performance codes. Multiple circuit faults warrant checking wiring diagrams for a shared power or ground connection.

steps.title: Find the responsible system
steps.body: Use the [engine-control chart](#/document/G1692929). Its routes separate cooling, charging, oil-pressure/fuel-level instrumentation, starting, brake/vehicle-speed, grille-shutter, reversing-lamp, transmission-control, remote-start and anti-theft concerns. Preserve the exact code: an electrical circuit-low description differs from an actual low-pressure or overtemperature condition.

steps.title: Match fitted equipment
steps.body: Select cruise diagnosis with or without adaptive cruise control, and climate diagnosis for dual automatic or electronic manual temperature control. Transmission referrals distinguish the 6R80 automatic from the MT82 manual; P0720, P0721 and P0722 have routes for both.

steps.title: Keep conditional referrals in order
steps.body: P025C, P0461, P0462, P0463 and P166A first require Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis (PC/ED). Only if referred back, use instrumentation diagnosis for those fuel-level codes or the vehicle identification number-dependent body control module guided routine for P025C/P166A. Other unlisted codes go to PC/ED Section 3 Symptom Charts.

steps.title: Select the named pinpoint test
steps.body: U0121 routes to Test A. U0212, lost steering-column-module communication, routes to B; U0164, lost heating/ventilation/air-conditioning-module communication, to C; P0A14, engine-mount control circuit/open, to D. Continue through the designated test before making a repair decision.

watchFor.title: Direct power can damage outputs
watchFor.body: Do not apply power or ground to module-switched components unless the diagnostic procedure directs it.

notes: The chart names the 6R80 referral as 2.3L EcoBoost (201kW/273PS); retain that specific referral when selecting the transmission article.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1548 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detected low air pressure downstream of the air filter.
diagnostics.next: Check the air-cleaner element and inlet/outlet pipes for restriction, water or contamination; repair as necessary. Retrieve and repair all other DTCs.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1001 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The key-on, engine-off self-test could not complete or the key-on, engine-running (KOER) test aborted.
diagnostics.next: Record all codes and repair self-test or continuous-memory faults first. Clear codes and rerun KOER. If P1001 returns, reprogram the PCM with the latest software and rerun KOER. If it returns again, install a new PCM through the appropriate removal/installation procedure, then program it with the latest software.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0121 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Anti-lock brake system (ABS) messages expected through the gateway module are missing. Listed possible sources include the ABS module, body control module and PCM.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test A and the communications-network explanation; missing messages alone do not identify which module is faulty.

verification.title: Check the directed result
verification.body: For P1001, preserve the required KOER retests. Other branches require their destination procedure's completion checks.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic handoff
verification.body: Record codes, selected equipment branch and test results, distinguishing an identified diagnostic route from a confirmed repair.

guides.title: Diagnose 2.3L EcoBoost communication and engine mount control faults
guides.summary: Trace U0121, U0212, U0164 and P0A14 through their communication, connector and engine-mount circuit checks before replacing components.
guides.introduction: The powertrain control module (PCM) uses sensor inputs and information from other modules to control the engine. These tests address missing module communication and a separate engine mount control circuit. The mount solenoid applies vacuum to the mounts at idle; a malfunction can make idle feel rougher.
guides.why: A communication code identifies missing information, not necessarily a failed sender module. Comparing reports across modules helps locate the concern. For the mount solenoid, checking power and wiring first distinguishes a circuit fault from a solenoid fault.

when.summary: Use for U0121, U0212 or U0164 with an observable concern, or for the P0A14 engine mount control circuit diagnosis.
notes: Communication codes without a current symptom can reflect intermittent conditions or high network traffic.

prepare.title: Provide the necessary diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting network tests, module self-tests and code clearing, plus a digital multimeter and Rotunda Flex Probes. Live-voltage and isolated-circuit testing require electrical diagnostic competence.

prepare.title: Establish reliable starting conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Review previous repairs and whether programmable module installation (PMI) was completed and configured correctly after module replacement.

steps.title: Confirm the communication complaint
steps.body: For Tests A–C, switch ignition on and verify an observable symptom. If none exists, stop this replacement path: the system is operating normally at this time. Record the complaint and codes before clearing them.

steps.title: Check the reporting module's information source
steps.body: Network-test the ABS module for Test A, SCCM for B or FCIM for C. A failed network test leads to communications diagnosis. If it passes, self-test that module and follow its fault referral. Next check body control module (BCM) codes, then PCM self-test results; P0562 or P0563 requires the PCM DTC chart.

steps.title: Establish whether the communication fault returns
steps.body: Clear the diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), wait 10 seconds and repeat the PCM self-test. If the relevant code returns, clear all codes, switch ignition off and on, wait 10 seconds and retrieve all continuous-memory codes. A matching code in another module directs inspection toward the named source module; otherwise inspect the PCM connection.

steps.title: Follow the connector branch before replacement
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect the selected module's connectors. Repair corrosion, damaged or pushed-out terminals, reconnect securely and operate the system. If the concern persists, follow any applicable technical service bulletin. Without one, A8 directs ABS replacement, B8 SCCM replacement and C8 the vehicle-specific FCIM guided routine. The PCM branches direct PCM replacement through its separate removal and installation procedure.

steps.title: Test D: establish the mount solenoid's electrical supply
steps.body: Inspect for loose or corroded solenoid connections and verify battery junction box fuse 42 (15A). Follow D1 with the solenoid disconnected to measure supply voltage. If supply fails the test, an intact fuse leads to circuit repair; a failed fuse requires tracing the possible short using the wiring diagrams.

steps.title: Separate control-wire faults from solenoid failure
steps.body: Follow D2–D4 with the PCM disconnected and the specified ignition states. Check the control wire for a short to voltage, then a short to ground, then an open circuit. Repair a failed circuit test. If all pass, install a new engine mount control solenoid using its separate procedure.

steps.title: Retest before considering the PCM
steps.body: After solenoid replacement, clear codes and repeat the self-test. If P0A14 returns, D5 requires PCM connector inspection, repairs and an operating check. Only a persistent concern after those checks reaches the bulletin check and, when no applicable bulletin exists, PCM replacement.

watchFor.title: Terminal damage from testing
watchFor.body: Use the specified probes without forcing terminals. Do not apply power or ground directly to module-controlled components unless the procedure directs it.

watchFor.title: A fault disappears after reconnection
watchFor.body: Correct the underlying corrosion or terminal-fit problem; reseating alone does not explain or repair its cause.

notes: Follow replacement procedures for access and configuration requirements. A diagnostic replacement decision does not complete installation or programming.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0121 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test A investigates communication with the anti-lock brake system (ABS) module.
diagnostics.next: Check network response and ABS self-test results before the BCM, PCM and recurrence checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0212 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM is missing steering column control module (SCCM) messages through the gateway module (GWM).
diagnostics.next: Use Test B; SCCM self-test codes lead to steering-wheel and column electrical diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0164 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM is missing front controls interface module (FCIM) messages. The heating, ventilation and air conditioning controller is housed there.
diagnostics.next: Use Test C. FCIM self-test faults lead to the appropriate information-and-entertainment diagnosis for touchscreen or non-touchscreen equipment.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0A14 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Unexpectedly high mount-control circuit voltage suggests a short to voltage, an open wire or an open solenoid.
diagnostics.next: Use Test D's supply and control-circuit checks; the code alone does not identify the failed part.

verification.title: Confirm the operating result
verification.body: Operate the system after connector repairs and establish whether the original observable concern remains.

verification.title: Record recurrence and module distribution
verification.body: Record which modules report the communication code after the prescribed clearing and ignition cycle. For P0A14, record the self-test result after solenoid replacement before proceeding to D5.

guides.title: Diagnose engine-control codes and lost module communication on the 3.7L
guides.summary: Route powertrain codes to the correct system and trace missing ABS, steering-column or climate-control messages before considering module replacement.
guides.introduction: The powertrain control module (PCM) uses sensor and switch inputs to control engine outputs, while monitoring operation and emissions. It also exchanges information with other vehicle modules. A diagnostic trouble code (DTC) stored in the PCM can therefore point to a transmission, charging, climate-control or network problem. This job explains that routing and the three tests for missing module messages.
guides.why: A missing message identifies a communication failure, not automatically a failed module. Network faults, incorrect configuration, supply-voltage problems and poor connector contact must be separated before replacement. An old communication code without a present symptom does not justify following the replacement branch.

when.summary: When PCM codes need diagnosis, particularly U0121, U0212, U0164 or an incomplete self-test.
notes: Choose transmission, cruise-control, climate-control and touchscreen branches from the equipment actually fitted.

prepare.title: Establish sound test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Review previous repairs, inspect relevant wiring and connections, and retrieve related codes across the network. Address circuit codes before system or performance codes.

prepare.title: Arrange the required capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool supporting network tests, module self-tests and continuous-memory code retrieval. Follow Diagnostic Methods for electrical testing. Programming and connector repair require appropriate capability; guided routines may require the vehicle identification number (VIN).

steps.title: Route the exact code
steps.body: Start with the [3.7L PCM DTC chart](#/document/G1692931). Preserve distinctions such as circuit low, circuit high, intermittent, incorrect ratio and out-of-self-test-range: these describe different findings. Follow the equipment-specific destination rather than choosing a component from the code's name.

steps.title: Handle P1001 in its specified order
steps.body: P1001 identifies an incomplete key-on, engine-off test or aborted key-on, engine-running test. Retrieve and record all codes, repair self-test and continuous-memory faults first, clear the code and rerun the engine-running self-test. If P1001 returns, update PCM software and repeat the test. Only another return directs PCM replacement, followed by programming with the latest software.

steps.title: Confirm the communication complaint
steps.body: For U0121 use Test A, targeting the anti-lock brake system (ABS) module; for U0212 use Test B, targeting the steering column control module (SCCM); for U0164 use Test C, targeting the front controls interface module (FCIM). Turn the ignition on and confirm an observable symptom. Without one, the test stops: network traffic or an intermittent condition may explain the stored code.

steps.title: Check the network and supporting modules
steps.body: Run a network test. If the target module fails, continue with Communications Network diagnosis. If it passes, perform its self-test and route any codes as described below. With none present, retrieve body control module (BCM) codes and diagnose those if found. Otherwise run the PCM self-test; P0562 or P0563 sends diagnosis to the charging system.

steps.title: Check whether the code returns
steps.body: Consider incorrect or omitted programmable module installation (PMI) after recent module replacement. Clear the DTCs, wait 10 seconds and repeat the PCM self-test. If the target communication code does not return, operation is correct at this time; an intermittent condition remains possible.

steps.title: Determine which connector branch applies
steps.body: If the code remains, clear all DTCs, switch the ignition off and on, wait 10 seconds, then retrieve all continuous-memory DTCs. The same communication code in another module directs inspection of the target module's connectors. If only the PCM records it, inspect the PCM connector.

steps.title: Repair connections and reassess
steps.body: Switch the ignition off before disconnecting. For corrosion, renew affected connectors or terminals and clean module pins. Replace damaged, bent or pushed-out pins as directed. Reconnect securely, ensuring the connectors seat and latch, then operate the system. If the concern disappears, address the underlying connector fault.

steps.title: Use the final branch only if the concern persists
steps.body: Check applicable technical service bulletins and follow any matching bulletin. Without one, the target-module branch directs ABS or SCCM replacement, but the FCIM branch requires a VIN-accessed guided routine. The PCM connector branch directs PCM replacement. Continue through the relevant complete replacement or guided procedure; this diagnostic decision does not itself complete that work.

watchFor.title: A symptom that disappears
watchFor.body: Do not continue to module replacement when the concern is absent. Record the intermittent result.

watchFor.title: Recent module installation
watchFor.body: Incorrect configuration can produce communication codes even when the installed hardware is functional.

notes: For codes not otherwise listed, the chart directs diagnosis to Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis (PC/ED), Section 3 Symptom Charts.

diagnostics.finding: Test A: U0121
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM is missing ABS messages over the high-speed controller area network.
diagnostics.next: Follow the ABS-targeted sequence. ABS self-test codes go to ABS and Stability Control diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Test B: U0212
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM is missing steering-column module messages over the high-speed controller area network.
diagnostics.next: Follow the SCCM-targeted sequence. Its self-test codes go to Steering Wheel and Column Electrical Components diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Test C: U0164
diagnostics.meaning: Climate-control messages from the FCIM, through the gateway module, are missing.
diagnostics.next: Follow the FCIM-targeted sequence. Its self-test codes go to Information and Entertainment diagnosis: SYNC without touchscreen, or the applicable SYNC 2/SYNC 3 touchscreen branch.

diagnostics.finding: Cooling, voltage or starting codes
diagnostics.meaning: Temperature regulation, overtemperature, generator and starting faults have separate diagnostic paths.
diagnostics.next: Use Engine Cooling for P0128/P0217/P1299; Charging System for voltage and generator codes; Starting System for P06E9/P0830/P2535.

diagnostics.finding: Transmission and pedal-switch codes
diagnostics.meaning: The chart distinguishes transmission circuits, speed signals, ratios, solenoids, friction elements and programming faults.
diagnostics.next: Use the 3.7L 6R80 tests where directed. P0720/P0721/P0722 also have an MT82 path. Brake-switch and specified clutch-switch codes, plus U0104, follow the fitted cruise-control branch.

diagnostics.finding: Climate, fuel-level or other system codes
diagnostics.meaning: These codes can be stored in the PCM while requiring diagnosis elsewhere.
diagnostics.next: Match climate faults to dual automatic or electronic manual temperature control. P0461/P0462/P0463 require PC/ED first, then instrumentation if referred; the listed sensor-B and stuck-level codes go directly to instrumentation. P025C/P166A require PC/ED before a VIN-based BCM routine. P0812 goes to reversing lamps, P1501 to ABS, P1594/P1595 to entry-system diagnosis, and P161A to passive anti-theft diagnosis.

verification.title: Check the actual concern
verification.body: After connector repair, operate the affected system and establish whether the original symptom remains.

verification.title: Record the decision
verification.body: Record network and self-test results, whether the code returned after the specified wait, and which other modules stored it. Distinguish a resolved connection fault from an intermittent or referred concern.

guides.title: Diagnose 5.0L engine-control codes and lost module communication
guides.summary: Route engine-control fault codes to the correct system and investigate missing module messages before authorizing replacement.
guides.introduction: The powertrain control module (PCM) uses sensor and switch inputs to command engine hardware and monitor emissions. It also exchanges information with other vehicle modules. A diagnostic trouble code (DTC) identifies a detected condition; this investigation establishes whether that condition comes from another system, a connection, configuration or a module.
guides.why: Missing messages can result from intermittent communication, incorrect configuration or supply-voltage problems. Following the diagnostic order prevents those conditions from being mistaken for a failed module.

when.summary: When PCM codes require system diagnosis, especially U0121, U0212, U0164 or an incomplete self-test.
notes: Identify transmission, adaptive cruise control, climate-control type and touchscreen equipment before choosing a branch.

prepare.title: Diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of network tests, module self-tests and retrieving all-module codes. Programming and guided routines require the appropriate capability and vehicle identification number (VIN).

prepare.title: Establish reliable conditions
prepare.detail: Follow Diagnostic Methods: check battery and charging operation, ensure battery state of charge exceeds 70%, inspect obvious faults and review previous repairs. Record codes before clearing them.

steps.title: Choose the correct diagnostic route
steps.body: Use the [5.0L PCM chart](#/document/G1692933). It directs cooling, charging, instrumentation, starting, reversing-lamp, remote-start and immobilizer faults to their respective systems. Automatic-transmission faults use the 5.0L 6R80 tests; P0720, P0721 and P0722 also have an MT82 manual-transmission route. Unlisted codes go to Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis (PC/ED), Section 3 Symptom Charts.

steps.title: Confirm the communication complaint
steps.body: For Tests A, B and C, switch the ignition on and establish an observable symptom. Without one, stop: operation is normal at this time, and the code may reflect network traffic or an intermittent fault. With a symptom, network-test the module identified below. A failed network test leads to Communications Network diagnosis.

steps.title: Check the communicating modules in order
steps.body: If the target module passes the network test, run its self-test and follow the system-specific destination below for any codes. If none are present, retrieve body control module (BCM) codes and diagnose any recorded there. Otherwise run the PCM self-test; P0562 or P0563 redirects diagnosis to the charging system.

steps.title: Establish whether the communication code returns
steps.body: Consider incorrect or omitted programmable module installation (PMI) if a module was recently replaced. Clear the DTCs, wait 10 seconds and repeat the PCM self-test. If the target communication code does not return, operation is correct at this time; persistent codes require the next comparison.

steps.title: Compare reports from other modules
steps.body: Clear all DTCs, switch ignition off and then on, wait 10 seconds and retrieve all continuous-memory DTCs. If another module reports the same communication code, inspect the target module's connectors. If only the PCM reports it, inspect the PCM connector.

steps.title: Repair connections and retest operation
steps.body: Switch ignition off before disconnecting connectors. Renew corroded connectors or terminals and clean module pins; replace damaged or bent terminals/pins and renew pushed-out pins as necessary. Reconnect securely, ensuring every latch seats, then operate the system. If the concern disappears, address the underlying connector fault.

steps.title: Follow the final module-specific decision
steps.body: For a persistent concern, check Ford OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins and follow any relevant bulletin instead of continuing this test. Without one, the target-module branch directs ABS or steering-column module replacement, but the front-controls branch requires a VIN-specific guided routine. The PCM branch directs PCM replacement through its applicable removal and installation procedure.

watchFor.title: Terminal damage during testing
watchFor.body: Use the specified flex probes when connecting test equipment. Do not force probes into terminals or apply power or ground to module outputs without a directed test.

notes: Circuit faults take diagnostic priority over system or performance codes. A stored code alone does not justify module replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Test A: U0121
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM is missing anti-lock brake system (ABS) messages over the high-speed controller area network (HS-CAN).
diagnostics.next: Use the ABS module in the sequence above; its self-test codes lead to ABS and stability-control diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Test B: U0212
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM is missing steering column control module (SCCM) messages over HS-CAN.
diagnostics.next: Use the SCCM in the sequence; its self-test codes lead to Steering Wheel and Column Electrical Components diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Test C: U0164
diagnostics.meaning: Messages from the front controls interface module (FCIM), housing heating, ventilation and air conditioning controls, are missing through the gateway module.
diagnostics.next: Use the FCIM in the sequence. Its self-test codes lead to SYNC diagnosis without a touchscreen or the applicable SYNC 2/SYNC 3 touchscreen branch.

diagnostics.finding: Codes with equipment-dependent destinations
diagnostics.meaning: Brake/clutch-switch and cruise communication faults distinguish adaptive cruise equipment. Air-conditioning codes distinguish dual automatic temperature control from electronic manual temperature control.
diagnostics.next: Choose the fitted system's chart destination. Clutch switch A goes to starting diagnosis; clutch switch B goes to cruise diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Fuel, temperature and oil-pressure codes
diagnostics.meaning: P0128 concerns thermostat regulating temperature; P1299 indicates overtemperature protection. Oil-pressure circuit codes and P0524, pressure too low, share an instrumentation destination but describe different conditions.
diagnostics.next: Use cooling or instrumentation diagnosis as directed. P0461–P0463 require PC/ED first; P025C and P166A require PC/ED before any referred VIN-specific BCM routine.

diagnostics.finding: P1001: self-test incomplete or aborted
diagnostics.meaning: Other self-test or continuous-memory faults must be repaired before judging the PCM.
diagnostics.next: Retrieve and record all codes, repair those faults, clear codes and rerun the key-on, engine-running self-test. If P1001 returns, program the PCM with the latest software and repeat the test. Only if it returns again, install a new PCM and program it with the latest software.

verification.title: Confirm the branch outcome
verification.body: Record whether the target code returns after the specified retest and whether the original concern remains after connector repairs.

verification.title: Preserve the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record network-test results, module self-test codes and which modules reported the communication fault, together with the resulting repair or referral.

guides.title: Diagnose 5.2L engine-control communication faults and inspect exhaust valves
guides.summary: Trace missing module messages and observe both tailpipe valves to separate communication faults from actuator repair needs.
guides.introduction: The 5.2L powertrain control module (PCM) combines sensor inputs, network messages and software calibration to control the engine. It also commands the exhaust valves in both inboard muffler outlets through a shared pulse-width-modulated (PWM) circuit. This guide follows communication Tests A–C and the physical, operational and calibration checks in actuator Test D1–D3.
guides.why: A missing-message code does not identify a failed module by itself. Likewise, the shared exhaust-control circuit means a performance code cannot identify which valve is affected. Comparing both valves and checking related codes prevents an unsupported replacement decision.
searchTerms: exhaust does not change in Sport mode

when.summary: Use for a present communication concern, recorded PCM faults or exhaust valves that do not respond correctly to drive mode.

prepare.title: Prepare for module diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable scan tool supporting network tests, module self-tests and calibration checks. Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge above 70%. Review previous repairs and applicable Ford service information.

prepare.title: Arrange access and repair capability
prepare.detail: The work requires connector inspection, proper terminal repair and observation of both exhaust outlets with the engine running. Do not force probes into terminals or jumper power or ground to module-controlled components.

steps.title: Route the PCM codes before choosing a test
steps.body: Use the [5.2L PCM chart](#/document/G1807235). It directs cooling, transmission-temperature, fuel-level, oil-pressure, charging, starting, reversing-lamp, cruise/brake-switch, climate, vehicle-speed, remote-start, immobilizer and differential-cooling faults to their respective systems. Match actual cruise and climate equipment. The special self-test and timing-chain decisions are explained below.

steps.title: Confirm the concern and test communication
steps.body: For Tests A–C, switch ignition on and confirm an observable symptom. Without one, the system is operating normally at this time; intermittent communication or network traffic may explain the code. With a symptom, network-test the module identified below. A failed network test requires communication-network diagnosis before continuing.

steps.title: Check the target module and related systems
steps.body: If communication passes, self-test the target module. Route its codes to anti-lock braking, steering-column electrical or information-and-entertainment diagnosis as appropriate. Next retrieve Body Control Module (BCM) codes and diagnose any present. Then self-test the PCM: P0562 or P0563 redirects to 5.2L charging-system diagnosis.

steps.title: Recheck and compare reports across modules
steps.body: Clear codes, wait 10 seconds and repeat the PCM self-test. If the communication code disappears, operation is correct at this time. If it returns, clear all codes, cycle ignition off/on, wait 10 seconds and retrieve all continuous-memory codes. Check other modules for U0121:00 in Test A, U0212 in B or U0164:00 in C.

steps.title: Inspect the module selected by that comparison
steps.body: If another module reports the loss, inspect the target module; otherwise inspect the PCM. With ignition off, disconnect its connectors. Replace corroded connectors or terminals and clean module pins; renew damaged, bent or pushed-out contacts as necessary. Reconnect securely and operate the system. Resolve the underlying connection problem even if reconnection restores operation.

steps.title: Complete the communication branch
steps.body: If the concern persists, check applicable Ford service articles in OASIS. Follow an applicable article instead of continuing the test. Without one, the branch directs replacement of the inspected target module or PCM. Replacement is a separate procedure; select the front-controls procedure matching touchscreen/SYNC equipment. Recent module installation also warrants checking whether programmable module installation (PMI) was omitted or configured incorrectly.

steps.title: Inspect both tailpipe actuators
steps.body: In D1, look for debris, physical damage to the tailpipes or actuators, harness damage, and damaged or disconnected connectors. Correct identified faults. A finding requiring actuator replacement still needs a complete installation and calibration procedure; this inspection does not complete those operations.

steps.title: Compare Normal and Sport operation
steps.body: For D2, start the engine, toggle between Normal and Sport and observe both inboard outlet valves. During this check, both should close fully in Normal and open fully in Sport. One malfunctioning actuator identifies that actuator’s replacement need, with installation/calibration still outstanding. If both malfunction, further electrical diagnosis is required. This result does not establish PCM failure.

steps.title: Check D3 codes and calibration
steps.body: If both valves operate correctly, cycle ignition off/on and self-test the PCM. If P26FE is present, clear all modules’ codes and check applicable OASIS service articles; follow an applicable article. Without an applicable resolution, the concern remains unresolved. If P26FE is absent, address any connector root cause and verify that PCM calibration is current.

watchFor.title: Normal-mode opening
watchFor.body: Normal mode can open the valves according to engine load, engine speed and vehicle speed. Sport forces full opening; normal commanded positions are fully open or fully closed.

watchFor.title: An automatic exhaust self-test
watchFor.body: With ignition off and the PCM asleep, pressing the clutch pedal or start/stop button initiates a self-test that may take up to 9 minutes; the valves open and close twice. Pressing both together starts the engine and may sound like revving without an engine-speed increase.

notes: The actuator inspection stops at D3. Unresolved electrical faults and actuator installation/calibration require their complete applicable procedures before the repair can be finished.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0121 is recorded in the PCM.
diagnostics.meaning: Messages from the anti-lock brake system (ABS) module are missing on the high-speed controller area network.
diagnostics.next: Use Test A, beginning with the ABS module network test.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0212 is recorded in the PCM.
diagnostics.meaning: Messages from the steering column control module (SCCM) are missing.
diagnostics.next: Use Test B, beginning with the SCCM network test.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0164 is recorded in the PCM.
diagnostics.meaning: Heating, ventilation and air-conditioning messages from the front controls interface module (FCIM), through the gateway module, are missing.
diagnostics.next: Use Test C and test the FCIM, which houses the climate-control module.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P26C5, P26C6 or P26C7 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The actuator circuit reports an open, short to ground or short to voltage, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Perform D1–D3 inspections; unresolved faults require further electrical diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P26FE is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: An actuator reports a stuck-open, stuck-closed or unknown position; the PCM cannot identify the side.
diagnostics.next: Observe both valves and follow the D2/D3 decisions.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1001 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The engine self-test did not complete.
diagnostics.next: Record all codes and repair self-test or continuous-memory faults first. Clear codes and rerun the key-on, engine-running self-test. If P1001 returns, update PCM software and rerun. Continued return directs PCM replacement and programming with the latest software.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1060 or P1061 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM estimates excessive timing-chain usage; P1061 also forces limited engine speed.
diagnostics.next: Follow the separate 5.2L timing-chain replacement procedure.

verification.title: Document communication results
verification.body: Record network-test outcomes, self-test codes, reports from other modules and whether the original concern remains after connector work.

verification.title: Document each exhaust valve separately
verification.body: Record left and right positions in both modes, remaining codes, calibration status and any unresolved electrical, installation or calibration work.

Electrical diagnostic prerequisites and connector-handling methods.

Investigate FCIM self-test faults found during Test C.

Separate FCIM replacement for the touchscreen SYNC 2/SYNC 3 branch.
