guides.title: Replace the 2.3L EcoBoost boost pressure sensor
guides.summary: Replace the turbocharger boost pressure sensor by accessing it beneath the vehicle and restoring its mounting and electrical connection.
guides.introduction: The boost pressure sensor measures pressure in the engine’s boosted intake-air path. It supplies information to the powertrain control module (PCM), which uses sensor inputs to manage engine operation. This job replaces the sensor itself; access requires raising the vehicle and removing the underbody shield. The illustration shows the sensor mounted on the charge-air cooler assembly.
guides.why: The sensor is an information source for engine control, so its electrical connection matters as much as its mounting. Correct lifting protects the person working underneath, while controlled tightening protects the small sensor retainer and shield fixings.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the boost pressure sensor needs replacement.
notes: This is a replacement procedure, not a test for deciding whether a driveability concern is caused by the sensor.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underside access
prepare.detail: Use a suitable hoist and the specified lifting points. Identify the stamped triangles and check that the adapters clear suspension, steering, exhaust and underbody components.

prepare.title: Prepare for small fasteners
prepare.detail: Have tools for the shield fixings and sensor retainer, including a torque wrench suitable for their low tightening values.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle
steps.body: Place the transmission in NEUTRAL and position the vehicle on the hoist. Follow the [lifting procedure](#/document/G1663631) before working beneath it.

steps.title: Remove the underbody shield
steps.body: Remove the shield bolts and retainers, then remove the shield to expose the sensor working area. Keep these fixings together for reassembly.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the sensor
steps.body: Disconnect the turbocharger boost pressure sensor electrical connector. Remove the sensor retainer and withdraw the sensor, following the component location shown in the [replacement procedure](#/document/G1692149).

steps.title: Install the replacement and close access
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Secure the sensor retainer to 5 Nm, reconnect the electrical connector, and reinstall the underbody shield and its retainers. Tighten the shield bolts to 2 Nm.

watchFor.title: Unsafe vehicle support
watchFor.body: Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. The emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this repair.

watchFor.title: Incorrect lifting contact
watchFor.body: Bumpers are not lifting points. Incorrect adapter placement can damage nearby components or allow the vehicle to shift.

notes: Keep the sensor-retainer and shield-bolt tightening values distinct.

verification.title: Confirm sensor installation
verification.body: Check that the sensor is retained and its electrical connector has been reconnected.

verification.title: Confirm access closure
verification.body: Check that the shield, bolts and retainers are restored, with the specified tightening completed.

procedures.purpose: Complete boost pressure sensor removal and installation for the 2.3L EcoBoost.
Required lifting-point identification and safe hoist positioning.

guides.title: Replace Mustang camshaft position sensors by engine
guides.summary: Remove and reinstall the appropriate intake or exhaust camshaft position sensor using the access route and seal lubricant specified for the engine.
guides.introduction: A camshaft position (CMP) sensor provides the engine controls with information about camshaft position. Intake and exhaust sensors are separate components, and the larger engines have sensors on both cylinder banks. Replacement involves electrical disconnection, removal of the sensor retainer and careful installation of the oil-sealed sensor.
guides.why: The sensor attachment is straightforward, but access differs substantially between engines and banks. Following the correct branch avoids unnecessary dismantling. Lubricating the O-ring with the specified clean engine oil helps it seat as the sensor is installed.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that a particular CMP sensor requires replacement, or removal is needed for other repairs.
notes: Identify the engine, cylinder bank where applicable, and intake or exhaust sensor before dismantling.

prepare.title: Plan the access work
prepare.detail: Have tools for sensor retainers and a suitable low-range torque wrench. Manifold removal capability is required for the 3.7L right-hand sensors and all 5.0L and 5.2L sensors.

prepare.title: Match the seal lubricant
prepare.detail: Use the matched procedure's clean engine oil: SAE 5W-30 synthetic blend for 2.3L, SAE 5W-20 synthetic blend for 3.7L, SAE 5W-20 full synthetic for 5.0L, or SAE 5W-50 full synthetic for 5.2L.

steps.title: Select the correct sensor branch
steps.body: Use the engine-specific procedure linked below. Right-hand and left-hand banks have different access sequences; the intake and exhaust sensor instructions should not be treated as interchangeable locations.

steps.title: Prepare access on the 2.3L EcoBoost
steps.body: Remove the appearance-cover nuts and cover. Disconnect the low-pressure fuel sensor electrical connector and detach the fuel supply tube retainer from the valve-cover stud. These are connector and retainer operations; the CMP procedure does not call for opening a fuel connection.

steps.title: Prepare access on the 3.7L
steps.body: For the right-hand sensors, remove the [upper intake manifold](#/document/G1681529), then follow the intake-sensor and exhaust-sensor operations. The left-hand branch proceeds directly to the exhaust sensor followed by the intake sensor; the manifold-removal requirement belongs to the right-hand branch.

steps.title: Prepare access on the 5.0L or 5.2L
steps.body: Remove the intake manifold using the [5.0L procedure](#/document/G1685326) or [5.2L procedure](#/document/G1800279). Both engines list intake then exhaust sensor operations on each bank. On the left bank, move the radio ignition interference capacitor aside before removing the exhaust sensor.

steps.title: Remove the sensor being serviced
steps.body: Disconnect its electrical connector, remove its retainer and withdraw the sensor using the selected engine and bank procedure. On the 2.3L, the intake sensor operation precedes the exhaust sensor operation. Keep track of which connector and retainer belong to the serviced location.

steps.title: Lubricate, install and restore access
steps.body: Lubricate the sensor O-ring with the specified clean engine oil before installation. Reverse the applicable removal sequence and tighten the sensor retaining fastener to 10 Nm. Restore any displaced capacitor, tube retainer and electrical connections, and reinstall the applicable manifold. On the 2.3L, tighten the appearance-cover nuts to 9 Nm.

watchFor.title: Different oils despite similar sensors
watchFor.body: The seal-lubrication materials differ by engine. Use the specification in the matching sensor procedure.

watchFor.title: Left-bank exhaust access on the V8 engines
watchFor.body: The interference capacitor must be moved aside for access and restored during reassembly.

notes: These removal and installation procedures do not establish a sensor failure from a symptom or fault code.

verification.title: Confirm installation details
verification.body: Check that the lubricated sensor is installed, its retaining fastener is tightened and its electrical connector is reconnected.

verification.title: Confirm the access route is restored
verification.body: Account for the components removed on the selected branch, including manifold installation, the V8 capacitor or the 2.3L fuel-sensor connector and tube retainer.

guides.title: Replace a catalyst monitor sensor on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Replace the identified catalyst monitor sensor using the correct engine procedure, specified lubricants and a calculated torque-wrench setting.
guides.introduction: The catalyst monitor sensor is an exhaust oxygen sensor used in monitoring catalytic-converter performance. It has a threaded exhaust mounting and an electrical lead connecting it to the vehicle harness. Replacement requires underbody access, disconnection of that lead and controlled removal and tightening of the threaded sensor.
guides.why: The sensor socket changes the tool arrangement used for tightening, so the procedure requires calculation of the correct torque-wrench setting. Removal and installation also specify different materials: penetrating lubricant for removal and high-temperature nickel anti-seize for installation. Choosing the correct engine and sensor side keeps the connector and access instructions relevant.

when.summary: When diagnosis has identified a catalyst monitor sensor that requires replacement.
notes: The 2.3L procedure covers its sensor without separate side branches.
The 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures each distinguish right-hand and left-hand sensors.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the designated lifting points. Check adapter clearance around the exhaust, suspension and steering components. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare the specified service equipment
prepare.detail: Have exhaust gas oxygen sensor socket 303-476 (T94P-9472-A), a torque wrench and the Torque Wrench Adapter Formula referenced by the engine procedure.

prepare.title: Have both specified materials
prepare.detail: Use Motorcraft Penetrating and Lock Lubricant XL-1 for removal and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 for installation.

steps.title: Select the engine and sensor branch
steps.body: Use the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L procedure matching the vehicle. For engines with separate side branches, identify the right-hand or left-hand sensor being replaced before disconnecting anything.

steps.title: Lift and disconnect
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on the hoist following the lifting procedure. Locate the selected sensor using its engine-specific illustration and disconnect its electrical connector before unscrewing the sensor.

steps.title: Remove the selected sensor
steps.body: Follow the applicable removal branch using socket 303-476 and XL-1 penetrating lubricant. The separate right-hand and left-hand instructions on the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines apply to their respective sensor locations.

steps.title: Calculate the installation setting
steps.body: Use the referenced Torque Wrench Adapter Formula to calculate the wrench setting for the specified sensor torque of 35 lb.ft (48 Nm). This torque is stated independently in all four engine procedures; the wrench setting must account for the service-tool arrangement.

steps.title: Install and reconnect
steps.body: Use XL-2 high-temperature nickel anti-seize and the specified sensor socket during installation, then tighten using the calculated setting. Reconnect the electrical connector. If servicing both sides, the multi-sensor procedures list right then left for removal and left then right for installation.

watchFor.title: Torque target confused with wrench setting
watchFor.body: The required sensor torque does not remove the instruction to calculate the adapter-adjusted wrench setting.

watchFor.title: Lubricants used in the wrong phase
watchFor.body: XL-1 and XL-2 have separate roles in this procedure; retain the specified removal and installation materials.

notes: Use the matching engine article to identify the actual sensor location and access.

verification.title: Confirm installation completion
verification.body: Confirm the selected sensor has been tightened using the required calculation and its electrical connector has been reconnected.

verification.title: Record the serviced location
verification.body: Record the engine, sensor side where applicable and calculated torque-wrench setting used.

Remove and install the right-hand or left-hand catalyst monitor sensor on the 3.7L Duratec engine.
Remove and install the right-hand or left-hand catalyst monitor sensor on the 5.0L engine.
Remove and install the right-hand or left-hand catalyst monitor sensor on the 5.2L engine.

guides.title: Replace the clutch pedal position switch
guides.summary: Disconnect the clutch pedal position switch, remove it from its bracket and install the replacement in reverse order.
guides.introduction: The clutch pedal position (CPP) switch provides an electrical indication of clutch-pedal position. Its bracket locates it at the pedal, and its connector joins it to the vehicle wiring. Replacement is a short operation once the faulty component has been identified. The 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures all use the same disconnect, remove and reverse-install sequence.
guides.why: Both interfaces matter: the bracket holds the switch in its working position, while the connector carries its electrical connection. Fitting a replacement without fully restoring either interface leaves the repair incomplete. The removal operation itself does not establish why a pedal-related complaint occurred.

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies the clutch pedal position switch as requiring replacement.
notes: Select the procedure matching the engine before working at the pedal bracket.

prepare.title: Identify the mounting and connector
prepare.detail: Locate the CPP switch at its bracket and examine the matching procedure’s illustration. Be able to reach the electrical connector and bracket retention without pulling on the wiring.

steps.title: Confirm the switch to be removed
steps.body: Match the switch, connector and bracket to the applicable engine procedure. This establishes the component and mounting interface before anything is disconnected.

steps.title: Disconnect the electrical connector
steps.body: Release and unplug the switch connector. Handle the connector body rather than using the wires to pull it free, then keep it clear of the switch removal path.

steps.title: Remove the switch from the bracket
steps.body: Remove the CPP switch using the bracket engagement shown in the applicable procedure. Note how it sits in the bracket so the replacement can return to the correct mounting position.

steps.title: Install in reverse order
steps.body: Fit the replacement switch into the bracket, then reconnect the electrical connector. Complete the mounting before reconnecting the wiring, following the reverse of the removal sequence.

watchFor.title: Incomplete bracket engagement
watchFor.body: A switch that is not properly retained has not been fully installed, even if its connector is attached.

watchFor.title: An unsecured connector
watchFor.body: Confirm the connector is fully engaged after the switch is mounted.

notes: No switch adjustment or electronic relearn is specified within this replacement operation.

verification.title: Confirm completed reassembly
verification.body: Check that the bracket retains the switch and the electrical connector is secured. These checks confirm assembly; they do not independently prove that the original electrical complaint has been resolved.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L CPP switch removal and reverse-order installation.
3.7L CPP switch removal and reverse-order installation.
5.0L CPP switch removal and reverse-order installation.
5.2L CPP switch removal and reverse-order installation.

applicability.equipment: Vehicles fitted with a clutch pedal; engine-specific procedures cover 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L.

guides.title: Replace the crankshaft position sensor by engine variant
guides.summary: Follow the correct engine-specific sensor access and installation route, then complete the scan-tool Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction.
guides.introduction: The crankshaft position (CKP) sensor supplies crankshaft-position information to the engine controls. Its replacement method differs considerably between these engines: the 2.3L needs mechanical alignment, the 3.7L uses bell-housing access, the 5.0L requires intake-manifold removal, and the 5.2L sensor is replaced with the rear-seal retainer kit.
guides.why: Correct installation includes both physical positioning and the specified scan-tool learning step. On the 2.3L, loosening the crankshaft pulley bolt can also release the unkeyed timing sprocket because the assembly relies on friction and diamond washers. That makes an unnecessary pulley-bolt disturbance a serious timing risk.

when.summary: After diagnosis calls for CKP sensor replacement and the engine-specific access route is confirmed.
notes: Complete only the applicable engine branch, followed by the common scan-tool correction.
The replacement procedures do not establish a sensor fault from a symptom alone.

prepare.title: Arrange installation and learning equipment
prepare.detail: Have a scan tool capable of Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction. The 2.3L also requires timing peg 303-507, alignment tool 303-1521 and the equipment specified for its stretchy A/C belt.

prepare.title: Plan the access work
prepare.detail: Provide hoist access for the 3.7L. The 5.0L manifold operation requires fuel-pressure release, battery ground and positive cable disconnection, and new manifold gaskets. Obtain the complete rear-seal-with-retainer-plate kit for the 5.2L.

steps.title: 2.3L: expose and remove the sensor
steps.body: Follow [A/C Compressor Belt](#/document/G1688221) to remove the belt. Disconnect the compressor connectors and harness retainers, remove its bolts and support the compressor aside as illustrated. Remove the CKP sensor bolts, disconnect its connector and remove the sensor. Maintain engine-repair cleanliness.

steps.title: 2.3L: establish position and align the replacement
steps.body: Follow [the 2.3L sensor procedure](#/document/G1692140). Turn the crankshaft clockwise until the first piston is 45° before top dead center, using the front-cover and pulley guide holes. Remove the engine plug bolt, install timing peg 303-507 and rotate clockwise until the crankshaft contacts it. Connect and fit the sensor with finger-tight bolts. Fit alignment tool 303-1521 to the sensor and trigger-wheel tooth, then tighten the sensor bolts to 7 Nm.

steps.title: 3.7L: use the bell-housing access
steps.body: Place the vehicle in NEUTRAL on a hoist. Remove the heat-shield nut, bolt and shield, then move the access plug aside. Withdraw the sensor and its bolt from the bell housing before disconnecting the electrical connector, preventing the sensor from falling inside. Connect and install the replacement using [the 3.7L procedure](#/document/G1692248).

steps.title: 5.0L: reach the sensor through manifold removal
steps.body: Complete [Intake Manifold removal](#/document/G1685326), including pressure release, battery disconnection and the fuel, hose and rear-wiring access steps. The fuel rail can remain with the manifold assembly. Discard the manifold gaskets. Disconnect the CKP connector and remove the sensor bolt and sensor, then fit the replacement using [the 5.0L procedure](#/document/G1692276).

steps.title: 5.2L: replace the sensor with its retainer kit
steps.body: The sensor and crankshaft rear-seal retainer plate must be removed and discarded together. Follow [Crankshaft Rear Seal with Retainer Plate](#/document/G1800270) and install the sensor as part of that kit, as required by [the 5.2L sensor procedure](#/document/G1802182).

steps.title: Restore the applicable access assemblies
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove both special tools, install the engine plug bolt, and restore the compressor, connectors, retainers and belt. Follow the belt procedure's seating checks for both drive belts. On the 3.7L, restore the access plug and heat shield. On the 5.0L, reinstall the manifold with new gaskets and complete all reconnections through its installation procedure.

steps.title: Complete the common learning procedure
steps.body: For every engine, use the scan tool to perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction and follow its on-screen instructions. Treat this as part of sensor installation, after the applicable mechanical work is complete.

watchFor.title: 2.3L pulley-bolt disturbance
watchFor.body: Do not loosen the pulley bolt during this access work. Any repair requiring its loosening needs the specified crankshaft and camshaft locking procedure first.

watchFor.title: The timing peg is a one-direction stop
watchFor.body: The 2.3L crankshaft can still turn counterclockwise with the peg installed. Maintain the required top-dead-center position during alignment.

notes: If the 5.0L manifold operation follows upper-engine failure, inspect the manifold for metal debris. Replace it if debris is found; a newly installed manifold also requires the stated road test.

verification.title: Check the applicable physical installation
verification.body: Confirm sensor fastening and access reassembly against the engine-specific procedure. For the 2.3L, specifically confirm both special tools are removed and both belts are seated correctly.

verification.title: Record the learning result
verification.body: Record successful completion of Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction, or the scan tool's reported reason it could not complete.

guides.title: Replace the 2.3L EcoBoost engine coolant temperature sensor
guides.summary: Replace the coolant temperature sensor using its specified tightening stages, then refill and bleed the 2.3L cooling system.
guides.introduction: The engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor supplies a temperature input to the electronic engine controls. The powertrain control module combines sensor information with its programmed strategy to control engine operation. Replacing this sensor opens a coolant passage as well as disconnecting an electrical input, so the job includes cooling-system draining and restoration.
guides.why: Draining the system reduces coolant loss, but fluid can still escape at the sensor opening. Having the replacement ready helps control that loss. Correct tightening secures the new sensor, and completing the filling and bleeding procedure restores coolant circulation without leaving trapped air.

when.summary: When replacement of the 2.3L engine coolant temperature sensor has been established as necessary.
notes: This is the replacement path; it does not establish the cause of an incorrect temperature signal.

prepare.title: Prepare for coolant handling
prepare.detail: Have the replacement sensor and a shop towel ready, together with the equipment required for the 2.3L cooling-system draining, vacuum filling and bleeding procedure.

prepare.title: Provide safe access and controlled tightening
prepare.detail: Use a vehicle hoist, suitable sensor-removal tools and torque-and-angle capability. Identify the marked lifting points and check that hoist adapters clear suspension and underbody components.

steps.title: Drain the cooling system
steps.body: Begin the [sensor replacement procedure](#/document/G1692142) by completing the [2.3L cooling-system draining procedure](#/document/G1673124). Follow its handling precautions before opening the sensor's coolant passage.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle and stage the replacement
steps.body: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on the hoist using the triangle-marked lifting points. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Keep the new sensor and shop towel close to the work area before removing the old component.

steps.title: Disconnect and exchange the sensor
steps.body: Disconnect the sensor's electrical connector, then remove the sensor, capturing escaping coolant with the towel. Install the replacement using both tightening stages: first 16 Nm, then an additional 180°. The angle stage is part of the installation requirement.

steps.title: Reconnect and restore the cooling system
steps.body: Reconnect the electrical connector as part of reversing removal. Fill and bleed the cooling system using the linked 2.3L procedure, including its specified filling method. Finish that procedure before treating the sensor replacement as complete.

watchFor.title: Residual coolant at the opening
watchFor.body: System draining does not eliminate the need to catch escaping fluid when the sensor is removed.

watchFor.title: Incomplete installation
watchFor.body: Both the electrical reconnection and cooling-system filling and bleeding are required after installing the sensor.

notes: Use the 2.3L cooling procedure for the applicable coolant requirements and filling sequence.

verification.title: Confirm sensor installation
verification.body: Confirm completion of both tightening stages and reconnection of the sensor electrical connector.

verification.title: Record coolant restoration
verification.body: Record that the cooling-system filling and bleeding procedure has been completed, rather than recording only the sensor exchange.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost ECT sensor removal, replacement and two-stage installation tightening.
Required 2.3L cooling-system draining, vacuum filling and bleeding.
Correct vehicle lifting points and safe hoist positioning.

guides.title: Replace the engine mount control solenoid on the 2.3L EcoBoost
guides.summary: Replace the engine mount control solenoid and restore its vacuum connections, electrical connector and mounting retainer.
guides.introduction: The engine mount control solenoid is an electrically operated valve in the mount's vacuum-control plumbing. It connects an electrical command to the vacuum side of the system. This job replaces that external valve assembly, making the electrical connector, vacuum hose connections and mounting retainer the main points of attention.
guides.why: Correct hose connections are necessary for the valve to control the intended vacuum path. The electrical connector supplies the command side, while the retainer secures the assembly. Replacing the valve without restoring all these connections would leave the repair incomplete.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the engine mount control solenoid requires replacement.
notes: A mount-related concern by itself does not establish that the solenoid has failed.

prepare.title: Identify the connections
prepare.detail: Use the component illustration to distinguish the electrical connector, vacuum hose connectors and mounting retainer. Note the existing hose-to-port arrangement before disconnecting it.

prepare.title: Prepare the replacement and tools
prepare.detail: Have the correct replacement solenoid, suitable hand tools and a torque wrench for the 11 Nm retaining-fastener specification.

steps.title: Disconnect the control connections
steps.body: Follow the [replacement procedure](#/document/G1817827). Disconnect the electrical connector and the vacuum hose connectors from the solenoid assembly, keeping their original destinations identifiable for installation.

steps.title: Remove the solenoid
steps.body: Remove the mounting retainer and take out the engine mount control solenoid. This releases the valve assembly after its attached wiring and hoses have been disconnected.

steps.title: Mount the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence to position the replacement solenoid and install its retainer. Tighten the retaining fastener to 11 Nm so the assembly is secured as specified.

steps.title: Restore the vacuum and electrical paths
steps.body: Reconnect the vacuum hoses to their original connections and reconnect the electrical connector. Compare the finished arrangement with the illustrated assembly and the positions noted before removal.

watchFor.title: A missed vacuum connection
watchFor.body: The assembly has several hose connections. Check each connection individually rather than judging completion from the mounted solenoid alone.

watchFor.title: Confusing replacement with diagnosis
watchFor.body: A successful physical installation does not establish the cause of an unresolved mount-control complaint.

notes: The tightening value applies to the mounting retainer; the electrical and vacuum connectors are reconnected through the reverse installation sequence.

verification.title: Check reassembly
verification.body: Confirm that the solenoid is retained at the specified torque, the electrical connector is reconnected and every disconnected vacuum hose is restored to its original connection.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L engine mount control solenoid removal and installation, including electrical/vacuum disconnection and retainer tightening.

applicability.equipment: 2.3L EcoBoost engine mount control solenoid with the illustrated electrical and vacuum connections.

guides.title: Replace the fuel rail pressure sensor on the 2.3L EcoBoost
guides.summary: Release fuel-system pressure, isolate the battery, replace the fuel rail pressure sensor and restore its connector and engine cover.
guides.introduction: The fuel rail pressure (FRP) sensor supplies pressure information to the engine's electronic controls. The powertrain control module (PCM) uses sensor inputs to determine how it operates engine hardware. This job replaces the sensor after the required fuel-pressure release and battery isolation, with access through removal of the engine appearance cover.
guides.why: Pressure release and electrical isolation are separate prerequisites, and their order matters. Once the sensor is replaced, its electrical connector restores the signal path to the controller. The sensor and appearance-cover nuts also have different tightening requirements.

when.summary: After diagnosis identifies the fuel rail pressure sensor as requiring replacement.
notes: The engine controller uses many inputs; a general driveability complaint alone does not identify this sensor as the cause.

prepare.title: Prepare for fuel-system opening
prepare.detail: Have the capability to perform the 2.3L Fuel System Pressure Release procedure and the Battery Disconnect and Connect procedure before removing the sensor.

prepare.title: Arrange removal and tightening tools
prepare.detail: Provide suitable tools for the sensor and cover nuts, plus torque tools capable of applying their separate specified values.

steps.title: Release pressure, then isolate the battery
steps.body: Perform the linked 2.3L fuel-pressure release procedure first. Then disconnect the battery cable through the battery procedure. Complete both prerequisites before opening the sensor connection.

steps.title: Expose and remove the sensor
steps.body: Remove the appearance-cover nuts and lift off the cover. Disconnect the FRP sensor electrical connector, then remove the sensor. The illustration in the sensor procedure identifies the component.

steps.title: Install and reconnect the replacement
steps.body: Install the FRP sensor and tighten it to 24 lb.ft (33 Nm). Reconnect its electrical connector to restore the pressure-signal connection.

steps.title: Restore the cover and battery connection
steps.body: Install the engine appearance cover and tighten its nuts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Reconnect the battery cable using the linked battery procedure.

watchFor.title: Incomplete pressure release
watchFor.body: Battery disconnection does not replace the required fuel-pressure release. Follow the specified release procedure before removing the sensor.

watchFor.title: Different torque requirements
watchFor.body: Keep the sensor tightening value separate from the much smaller appearance-cover nut value.

notes: Use the pressure-release procedure for the 2.3L EcoBoost branch.

verification.title: Confirm sensor and connector installation
verification.body: Confirm that the sensor has received its specified tightening and its electrical connector is reattached.

verification.title: Confirm final reassembly
verification.body: Check that the appearance cover and nuts are installed to specification and battery reconnection is complete.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost FRP sensor removal, installation and component tightening specifications.
Required 2.3L fuel-system pressure release before sensor removal.
Battery-cable disconnection and reconnection surrounding the sensor repair.

guides.title: Replace a heated oxygen sensor on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Replace the identified heated oxygen sensor using the correct engine and side procedure, specified lubricants and an adapter-corrected tightening setting.
guides.introduction: A heated oxygen sensor, abbreviated HO2S, senses oxygen in the exhaust, providing information used by the engine control system. Its heater helps the sensing element reach its working condition. Replacement involves disconnecting its lead and removing the threaded sensor from the exhaust. The engines share tools and materials, but sensor access and connector locations must be taken from the matching engine procedure.
guides.why: This job combines under-vehicle access with a threaded exhaust component and an attached electrical lead. Correct lifting protects the technician and surrounding vehicle parts. The specified socket accommodates the sensor, while the installation procedure requires a calculated torque-wrench setting for the adapter arrangement. The required sensor torque must not simply be assumed to equal the wrench setting.

when.summary: When diagnosis has identified a heated oxygen sensor for replacement or it must be removed for related service.
notes: Identify the engine and affected sensor before ordering parts or choosing the access illustration.

prepare.title: Vehicle lifting capability
prepare.detail: Use a suitable hoist and the Jacking and Lifting procedure. Position the vehicle in NEUTRAL as required by every engine branch.

prepare.title: Sensor tooling and torque calculation
prepare.detail: Have exhaust gas oxygen sensor socket 303-476 (T94P-9472-A), a torque wrench and the Torque Wrench Adapter Formula named in the installation procedure.

prepare.title: Specified materials
prepare.detail: Prepare Motorcraft Penetrating and Lock Lubricant XL-1 for removal and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 for installation.

steps.title: Select the engine and sensor branch
steps.body: Use the [2.3L procedure](#/document/G1692144), [3.7L procedure](#/document/G1692251), [5.0L procedure](#/document/G1692279) or [5.2L procedure](#/document/G1802184). The latter three contain separate right-hand and left-hand sensor operations. Follow the branch for the sensor being serviced.

steps.title: Position and raise the vehicle
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on the hoist. Follow [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631), locating the approved points by the stamped triangles. Check hoist-adapter and underbody clearance before lifting.

steps.title: Disconnect the sensor lead
steps.body: Find and disconnect the HO2S electrical connector using the selected engine illustration. Disconnect before removing the threaded sensor so its lead is free from the vehicle harness.

steps.title: Remove the identified sensor
steps.body: Use the specified penetrating lubricant and oxygen-sensor socket according to the matching removal operation. The 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures present right-hand removal before left-hand removal when both sides are being serviced.

steps.title: Install with the calculated wrench setting
steps.body: Use the specified nickel anti-seize lubricant and sensor socket. Calculate the wrench setting using the referenced adapter formula for a sensor torque of 35 lb.ft (48 Nm). Each supplied engine procedure specifies this value. For both-side work on the 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine, installation is presented left-hand first, then right-hand.

steps.title: Reconnect each serviced sensor
steps.body: Connect the corresponding HO2S electrical connector after installation. Keep each reconnection associated with its engine and side branch so no serviced sensor is left disconnected.

watchFor.title: Unsafe or obstructed lifting
watchFor.body: Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Avoid lifting against bumpers and prevent hoist adapters from contacting suspension, exhaust, steering or axle components.

watchFor.title: Uncorrected torque setting
watchFor.body: The installation explicitly requires the adapter calculation. Resolve that setting before tightening the sensor.

notes: The vehicle's emergency tire-changing jack is not intended for this hoisting operation.
Use the selected engine's illustrations for location; one engine's pictured layout does not establish another engine's access.

verification.title: Confirm installation and connection
verification.body: Confirm each serviced sensor has completed its tightening operation and its corresponding electrical connector is reconnected.

verification.title: Record the tightening result
verification.body: Record the engine, sensor side where applicable, required sensor torque and calculated torque-wrench setting used.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost heated oxygen sensor removal and installation.
3.7L Duratec right-hand and left-hand heated oxygen sensor removal and installation.
5.0L right-hand and left-hand heated oxygen sensor removal and installation.
5.2L right-hand and left-hand heated oxygen sensor removal and installation.
Approved vehicle lifting points, support precautions and hoist-clearance requirements.

guides.title: Replace knock sensors on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Follow the engine-specific access route, replace the knock sensors in their required positions, and restore all disturbed intake connections.
guides.introduction: Knock sensors detect engine vibration associated with abnormal combustion and provide an input to engine control. Their attachment to the engine matters because it couples that vibration into the sensor. The sensor replacement itself is brief, but access differs substantially: the 2.3L uses a lifted-vehicle access route, while the other listed engines require intake-manifold removal.
guides.why: Correct positioning and tightening preserve the intended sensor mounting. Manifold access adds separate fuel, electrical and sometimes cooling-system work. Cleanliness is especially important around exposed engine passages, where debris introduced during repair can cause engine damage.

when.summary: When diagnosis or an established engine repair requires knock sensor removal or replacement.
notes: Choose the procedure by engine before dismantling; the access operations are not interchangeable.

prepare.title: Match capability to the access route
prepare.detail: Prepare suitable torque equipment and vehicle-hoist capability where required. Manifold removal requires fuel-pressure release and battery isolation; the 3.7L also requires cooling-system draining, filling and bleeding.

prepare.title: Prepare for manifold reassembly
prepare.detail: Have new intake-manifold gaskets for the manifold being removed. Plan to keep exposed passages clean and to restore the electrical, fuel and hose connections using the full intake procedure.

steps.title: Use the 2.3L access sequence
steps.body: For the [2.3L](#/document/G1692146), remove the appearance-cover nuts and cover. With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a hoist using the lifting procedure. Detach the knock-sensor connector retainers from the intake manifold and disconnect the connectors. Note component positions before removal.

steps.title: Prepare the 3.7L lower-intake access
steps.body: For the [3.7L](#/document/G1692252), disconnect the knock-sensor connector, then follow the lower-intake procedure. It requires hoisting in NEUTRAL, releasing fuel pressure, disconnecting the battery ground cable and draining coolant. Remove the upper intake and complete the specified fuel, thermostat, injector and coolant-connection work before lifting off the lower manifold. Discard its gaskets.

steps.title: Follow the appropriate V8 procedure
steps.body: For the [5.0L](#/document/G1692281), remove the intake manifold using its linked procedure. The [5.2L sensor procedure](#/document/G1991989) explicitly directs intake removal to that same 5.0L-titled article. Its access work includes fuel-pressure release, both battery cables, the brace if fitted, cowl and intake components, and connected hoses and wiring. Discard the removed manifold gaskets. Note sensor positions, then disconnect their connectors.

steps.title: Replace and secure the sensors
steps.body: Remove the sensor bolts and sensors using the selected engine procedure. Reinstall and tighten the sensor bolts to 177 lb.in (20 Nm), a specification given for each listed engine. On the 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L, restore the component positions noted before removal.

steps.title: Reassemble the intake where removed
steps.body: Clean and inspect the sealing surfaces and install new gaskets. Reverse the relevant manifold-removal sequence, following its own tightening instructions. Both supplied manifold procedures allow the fuel rail to remain with the manifold assembly; rail removal is not automatically required.

steps.title: Restore connections and finish the access work
steps.body: Reconnect the sensor wiring and any detached retainers. Restore all engine-specific fuel, electrical, hose, cover and access components. On the 3.7L, complete cooling-system filling and bleeding. On the V8 intake route, restore the appearance-cover grommets to the manifold if they remained in the cover, and reinstall the brace if fitted.

watchFor.title: Misreading the 3.7L illustration
watchFor.body: Its cylinder heads are removed for clarity. Cylinder-head removal is not a knock-sensor access step.

watchFor.title: Contamination during manifold work
watchFor.body: Keep cleaning residue and other foreign material out of engine passages.

notes: Use the selected engine's intake procedure for its fastener sequence and specifications.

diagnostics.finding: Metal debris is found in the intake manifold after upper-engine failure involving valve or piston damage.
diagnostics.meaning: The manifold can retain material capable of causing further engine damage.
diagnostics.next: For the supplied manifold procedures, install a new manifold when this conditional inspection finds metal debris.

verification.title: Confirm installation details
verification.body: Check sensor positioning, specified bolt tightening, connector engagement and restoration of disturbed intake components.

verification.title: Record the applicable completion work
verification.body: Record cooling-system refill and bleeding for the 3.7L. If a new intake manifold was installed, complete and record the road test required by the manifold procedure.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost knock-sensor removal and installation, including lifted access and retained component orientation.
3.7L Duratec knock-sensor removal and installation after lower-intake removal.
5.0L knock-sensor removal and installation beneath the intake manifold.
5.2L knock-sensor removal and installation, including its explicit intake-procedure cross-reference.
Vehicle lifting prerequisites for the applicable engine access routes.
3.7L lower-intake removal and refitting, including fuel isolation, coolant work and new gaskets.
5.0L intake removal and refitting, also explicitly referenced by the 5.2L sensor procedure.

guides.title: Replace the MAPT sensor: 2015 Mustang 2.3L and 3.7L
guides.summary: Reach, remove and refit the manifold absolute pressure and temperature sensor, with separate instructions and tightening values for each engine.
guides.introduction: The MAPT sensor takes two measurements while occupying very little real estate. Naturally, its tiny retaining fastener still deserves your full attention. I’ll walk you through the cover access on the 2.3L and the direct sensor access on the 3.7L, keeping each engine’s tightening values where they belong.
guides.why: MAPT means manifold absolute pressure and temperature: the sensor measures air pressure and temperature inside the intake manifold for the engine controls. Replacing it involves disconnecting its electrical plug, releasing its mounting and restoring both connections. The important differences are the 2.3L appearance cover, the engine-specific retainer torque and the optional second mounting hole on the 3.7L.

when.summary: Use this procedure when an established repair calls for MAPT sensor removal or replacement.
notes: Choose the instructions for the engine fitted to the car. Complete only that engine’s branch, then carry out the shared completion checks.

prepare.title: Set the job’s boundary
prepare.detail: This procedure covers removing and refitting the sensor after the repair decision has been made. It does not establish whether the sensor is faulty or provide a repair method for a damaged mounting hole.

prepare.title: Prepare tools for small tightening values
prepare.detail: Have a driver that fits the sensor retainer and torque equipment suitable for 35–44 lb.in (4–5 Nm). For the 2.3L, also have a suitable tool for the appearance-cover nuts and torque equipment capable of 80 lb.in (9 Nm). These are inch-pound values; do not read them as foot-pounds.

prepare.title: Keep the engine branches separate
prepare.detail: For the 2.3L, use steps 1–4 and the [2.3L removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1692147). For the 3.7L, use steps 5–7 and the [3.7L removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1701605). Both branches finish at step 8.

prepare.title: Organize the parts
prepare.detail: If replacing the sensor, have the replacement matched to the fitted engine. Keep the removed retainer available for reassembly; on the 2.3L, also keep the four appearance-cover nuts together.

steps.title: 2.3L: remove the engine appearance cover
steps.body:
Remove the four nuts securing the appearance cover, then remove the cover to reach the intake-manifold sensor area. The cover is the large panel marked EcoBoost, with openings through it; its four fastening points are distributed around the panel.

Keep the nuts together for refitting. The cover has earned a brief holiday on the bench.

steps.title: 2.3L: disconnect and remove the MAPT sensor
steps.body:
Locate the small sensor mounted on the ribbed intake manifold. Its electrical connector attaches at one end, and a single retainer passes through the mounting ear beside the sensor body.

Disconnect the MAPT electrical connector first. Handle the connector housing rather than pulling on its wires. Position the disconnected connector and its attached wiring aside, clear of the sensor removal area.

Then remove the retainer and remove the sensor from the manifold. This order leaves the wiring disconnected and clear before the sensor is moved.

steps.title: 2.3L: install the sensor and reconnect it
steps.body:
Place the replacement or removed sensor back into its manifold mounting position. Reinstall its retainer and tighten it to 44 lb.in (5 Nm).

Bring the connector and attached wiring back from their aside position and reconnect the electrical connector to the sensor. Before covering the area, confirm that the sensor is retained and the plug is fully attached.

steps.title: 2.3L: reinstall the appearance cover
steps.body:
Put the appearance cover back over its mounting points and reinstall all four nuts. Tighten the cover nuts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm).

The cover nuts use a different setting from the sensor retainer. Reset the torque tool deliberately; one remembered number should not get to run the whole engine bay. Continue to step 8.

steps.title: 3.7L: locate the sensor on the intake manifold
steps.body:
Find the small MAPT sensor on the broad ribbed wall of the intake manifold. The sensor sits at an angle, with an electrical connector at one end and a retaining fastener through its mounting ear at the other.

The 3.7L removal sequence starts at this connector; there is no preceding appearance-cover removal in this branch.

steps.title: 3.7L: disconnect the connector, then remove the sensor
steps.body:
Disconnect the MAPT electrical connector, handling its housing rather than pulling on the wiring. Position the disconnected connector and its attached wiring aside, clear of the sensor removal area.

Remove the sensor retainer, then remove the sensor from the intake manifold. Keep the retainer for installation.

steps.title: 3.7L: refit the sensor using the appropriate mounting hole
steps.body:
Return the sensor to its manifold mounting position and reinstall the retainer. A second fastener hole is available for use during reinstallation if needed; see the mounting-hole branch under diagnostics.

Tighten the retainer to 35 lb.in (4 Nm). Bring the connector and attached wiring back from their aside position, then reconnect the electrical connector. This engine’s retainer setting is lower than the 2.3L setting.

steps.title: Check the completed assembly
steps.body:
Confirm that the sensor is secured with the correct engine-specific retainer torque and that its electrical connector is fully attached.

On the 2.3L, also confirm that the appearance cover is installed with all four nuts tightened to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Account for removed hardware and tools before finishing.

These are assembly checks. A correctly refitted sensor does not, by itself, prove that the original engine-control concern has been resolved.

watchFor.title: Inch-pounds versus foot-pounds
watchFor.body: The sensor settings are 44 lb.in (5 Nm) on the 2.3L and 35 lb.in (4 Nm) on the 3.7L. The 2.3L appearance-cover nuts use 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Check the tool’s units before tightening.

watchFor.title: Clear the wiring before removing the sensor
watchFor.body: Disconnect the electrical plug and position it and its attached wiring aside before removing the retainer and sensor. During installation, secure the sensor first, then bring the connector and wiring back and reconnect the plug.

watchFor.title: Second mounting hole belongs to the 3.7L
watchFor.body: The optional second-fastener-hole instruction applies to the 3.7L installation. Do not extend that option to the 2.3L.

notes: For engine-control background, the [2.3L system-operation reference](#/document/G1692128) and [3.7L system-operation reference](#/document/G1692272) direct readers to the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis (PC/ED) Manual, Section 1, Description and Operation.
The removal-and-installation sequences end with reversing the removal actions; neither adds a learning or initialization operation.

diagnostics.finding: 3.7L: a different fastener hole is needed during reinstallation.
diagnostics.meaning: The 3.7L installation allows use of a second fastener hole when needed.
diagnostics.next: Use the second hole for the sensor retainer and retain the 3.7L tightening value of 35 lb.in (4 Nm). If the sensor cannot be secured, stop and resolve the mounting problem before returning the car to service.

verification.title: Sensor mounting restored
verification.body: Confirm that the retainer was tightened to 44 lb.in (5 Nm) for the 2.3L or 35 lb.in (4 Nm) for the 3.7L.

verification.title: Electrical connection restored
verification.body: Confirm that the connector and wiring have been brought back from their aside position and that the MAPT connector is fully reconnected to the installed sensor.

verification.title: 2.3L cover restored
verification.body: Confirm that the appearance cover and its four nuts are installed, with the nuts tightened to 80 lb.in (9 Nm).

procedures.purpose: 2.3L MAPT sensor removal and installation, including four-nut appearance-cover access, positioning the disconnected wiring aside and both installation torque values.
3.7L MAPT sensor removal and installation, including positioning the disconnected wiring aside, retainer torque and the optional second fastener hole.
2.3L engine-control background reference directing system-operation reading to PC/ED Manual Section 1.
3.7L engine-control background reference directing system-operation reading to PC/ED Manual Section 1.

applicability.equipment: 2015 Ford Mustang with the 2.3L or 3.7L engine.

authoring.reviewNotes: Removed a fixed-hero claim; the selected illustration changes with the engine filter. Mechanical procedures and specifications are unchanged.

stepGroups.title: 2.3L: uncover and remove
stepGroups.summary: Remove the appearance cover, disconnect and position the wiring aside, then release the sensor.

stepGroups.title: 2.3L: refit and cover
stepGroups.summary: Secure the sensor, reconnect it and restore the cover using the separate torque settings.

stepGroups.title: 3.7L: remove and refit
stepGroups.summary: Work directly at the manifold sensor and use the 3.7L mounting details.

stepGroups.title: Check the finished assembly
stepGroups.summary: Confirm mounting, connection and any removed cover hardware.

guides.title: Replace and configure the powertrain control module
guides.summary: Replace the engine-specific powertrain control module, transfer its configuration when installing a new unit, and complete anti-theft and misfire-monitor setup.
guides.introduction: The powertrain control module (PCM) is the engine-management controller and must carry the correct vehicle configuration. Its replacement combines a short physical removal with essential electronic setup. The 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures share that overall path, but the 5.0L has different fastening instructions.
guides.why: A new controller needs configuration data from the vehicle, so the diagnostic session must begin before the old module is removed. Anti-theft authorization and misfire-monitor learning are separate completion steps. Simply installing the module, or reflashing existing software, does not complete the repair.
searchTerms: PCM misfire monitor neutral profile correction

when.summary: When diagnosis calls for PCM replacement, or the module must be removed and reinstalled.
notes: Configuration download and upload are required when installing a new component.
PCM installation does not require new keys or key programming; it requires a Passive Anti-Theft System parameter reset.

prepare.title: Provide the required diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic tool capable of Programmable Module Installation (PMI), the Passive Anti-Theft System (PATS) parameter reset and Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction.

prepare.title: Identify the engine and fastening arrangement
prepare.detail: Select the matching PCM procedure and have suitable torque tools. The 5.0L instructions include shear bolts and a separately specified nut.

steps.title: Capture configuration before removal
steps.body: When installing a new PCM, identify the vehicle with the diagnostic tool and download the original module information through PMI before disconnecting it. If retrieval fails, follow the tool's instructions for As-Built data or manually selected parameters; do not guess configuration values.

steps.title: Expose and remove the PCM
steps.body: Unclip and position aside the battery junction box (BJB). On the 5.0L, also position its harnesses aside as directed. Disconnect the PCM electrical connectors, then remove the retainers and module using the engine-specific procedure.

steps.title: Install with the correct fasteners
steps.body: Connect the electrical connectors and install the PCM and retainers. The 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.2L retainer specification is 62 lb.in (7 Nm). The 5.0L specifies 80 lb.in (9 Nm), shear bolts tightened until their heads shear off, and 89 lb.in (10 Nm) for the nut. Restore the BJB and any displaced harnesses.

steps.title: Configure the new controller
steps.body: For a new component, upload the saved information through PMI. The replacement must communicate with the diagnostic tool. Follow all prompted key cycles; PMI may also install an available later calibration. Clear network communication diagnostic trouble codes set in other modules during reprogramming.

steps.title: Complete the anti-theft parameter reset
steps.body: Carry out the [PATS parameter reset](#/document/G1672905). This requirement applies across the engine procedures, including the 5.2L. Existing keys do not need replacement or programming merely because the PCM was installed.

steps.title: Complete misfire-monitor learning
steps.body: Perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction after the repair, following the diagnostic tool's instructions. This is a separate learning requirement and remains necessary after the configuration and anti-theft work.

watchFor.title: Disconnecting the original module too early
watchFor.body: Obtain vehicle identification and configuration data before removal so PMI can use the original settings.

watchFor.title: Using another engine's fastening instructions
watchFor.body: The 5.0L retention details differ from the other engines. Match the PCM mounting and connector arrangement to your selected engine.

notes: For a transmission with a programmed solenoid body, unsuccessful PCM data transfer also requires the solenoid-body identification and strategy to be downloaded into the PCM.
Separate module reprogramming should follow a published technical service bulletin recommendation; reinstalling the same software level does not repair hardware.

diagnostics.finding: The original PCM configuration cannot be retrieved.
diagnostics.meaning: PMI may need vehicle-specific As-Built data or parameter selection.
diagnostics.next: Follow the diagnostic tool's recovery prompts and address applicable transmission strategy data.

diagnostics.finding: The replacement PCM does not communicate with the diagnostic tool.
diagnostics.meaning: PMI cannot be completed in that condition.
diagnostics.next: Resolve communication before attempting to finish configuration.

verification.title: Record electronic setup results
verification.body: Record successful PMI when applicable, the PATS parameter reset and Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction as distinct completed operations.

verification.title: Confirm physical and programming completion
verification.body: Check restored connectors, retainers, BJB and harness positions. After reprogramming, confirm that programming-related network communication codes have been cleared.

guides.title: Replace the variable camshaft timing oil control solenoids
guides.summary: Remove the appropriate valve cover, replace the VCT oil control solenoids and restore the cover using the correct engine-specific fastening and sealing procedure.
guides.introduction: Variable camshaft timing (VCT) oil control solenoids regulate the oil used to adjust camshaft timing. Reaching them requires valve-cover removal. The 2.3L has its own access procedure; the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L have separate right-hand (RH) and left-hand (LH) cover routes. This job replaces the solenoids once replacement has been established.
guides.why: The exposed engine must remain clean because debris entering oil passages can cause engine damage. Cover seals also need careful handling: a seal gripping a solenoid can damage both if forced. Correct fastening and timely sealant application are essential parts of restoring the assembly.

when.summary: Use when solenoid replacement is established and the engine and affected cylinder bank are identified.

prepare.title: Prepare for engine access and controlled tightening
prepare.detail: Have the matching valve-cover procedure, a torque wrench suitable for the small fasteners and angle-measuring capability for the 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L.

prepare.title: Have sealing materials ready
prepare.detail: The 2.3L and 3.7L RH cover procedures require new cover gaskets and Motorcraft High Performance Engine RTV Silicone TA-357, specification WSE-M4G323-A6.

prepare.title: Provide seal tools if damage requires replacement
prepare.detail: The 2.3L uses 205-153 with 303-1247. The 3.7L RH VCT seals use 205-153 with 205-142; its spark-plug tube seals use 205-153 with 303-1247.

steps.title: Choose the engine and bank procedure
steps.body: Use the 2.3L solenoid procedure or the correct RH/LH branch for the 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L. Read the associated cover installation instructions before dismantling so its materials, tools and sealing requirements are ready.

steps.title: Release the valve-cover attachments
steps.body: On the 2.3L, follow the cover sequence for the appearance cover, fuel-tube retainer, ignition coils, oil indicator, vent tube, wiring and exhaust camshaft position sensor. On the 3.7L RH side, release coils, crankcase ventilation tube, solenoid connectors, harness retainers and heater-tube attachments. Follow the linked cover procedure for other banks.

steps.title: Lift the cover without loading the solenoids
steps.body: Loosen the cover fasteners and remove the cover. On the 3.7L RH side, gently wiggle a cover whose VCT seal grips a solenoid until it releases. For the 2.3L and 3.7L RH cover, discard the cover gasket and inspect the VCT seals; replace only damaged seals. Also inspect the 3.7L RH spark-plug tube seals.

steps.title: Remove and refit the solenoids
steps.body: Remove their retaining bolts and lift out the solenoids. Install by reversing removal. The 2.3L solenoid bolts tighten to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). On either bank of the 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L, tighten first to 71 lb.in (8 Nm), then through 20°.

steps.title: Restore seals and prepare mating surfaces
steps.body: Keep cleaning debris out of the engine. On the 2.3L, do not use metal scrapers, wire brushes or abrasive discs on sealing faces. Follow the cover's sealing-surface preparation procedure. Install replacement seals with the specified tools where damaged seals were removed.

steps.title: Seal the cover and restore its connections
steps.body: For the 2.3L, install the new gasket, apply sealant at the specified locations and secure the cover within 10 minutes. For the 3.7L RH cover, apply sealant at the front-cover-to-cylinder-head joints, fit the new gasket and tighten within 4 minutes. If either limit is missed, remove the sealant and clean the area again. Follow each engine's cover procedure for tightening and restoring all removed attachments.

watchFor.title: Excessive force during cover removal
watchFor.body: The 3.7L RH procedure specifically warns against forcing a cover that is gripping a solenoid.

watchFor.title: Incorrect seal position
watchFor.body: On the 3.7L RH cover, VCT seals must sit below the tops of the solenoid electrical connectors to prevent oil leakage.

notes: The detailed gasket, seal-tool and sealant-time instructions above apply to the stated cover variants. Use the corresponding cover procedure for every other engine and bank.

verification.title: Check the restored assembly
verification.body: Confirm the cover procedure's connector, harness, tube and ignition-coil installation steps are complete. Check the specified 3.7L RH VCT seal position.

verification.title: Record fastening and sealing completion
verification.body: Record the engine and bank, completed solenoid torque/angle stages and compliance with the applicable cover sealant timing.

guides.title: Replace the oil-pressure sensor — 5.0L Performance Package or 5.2L
guides.summary: Remove and reinstall the oil-pressure sensing component using its engine-specific connector access, sealing condition and tightening method.
guides.introduction: The engine oil-pressure sensing component provides an electrical indication related to the lubrication system’s pressure. Its threaded connection must seal against oil leakage, while its connector carries the electrical signal. The 5.0L procedure calls the component a switch and applies only to Performance Package vehicles; the 5.2L procedure calls it a sensor and includes a protective cover.
guides.why: The two components have different installation tightening instructions despite their similar purpose. The 5.0L uses torque followed by an additional angle, while the 5.2L uses a single torque value. Sealant is specifically required when reusing the removed component. Replacing the sensing component does not itself correct a mechanical oil-pressure problem.

when.summary: When the applicable oil-pressure switch or sensor requires replacement or removal and refitting.
notes: A pressure warning alone does not prove the sensing component is defective.
The 5.0L instructions here apply only to vehicles equipped with the Performance Package.

prepare.title: Select the correct engine branch
prepare.detail: Confirm the engine and, for the 5.0L, Performance Package applicability. Keep its tightening instructions separate from the 5.2L instructions.

prepare.title: Lift the vehicle correctly
prepare.detail: Place the vehicle in neutral on a hoist using the specified lifting points. Check adapter clearance around nearby components. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Workshop capability
prepare.detail: Vehicle hoist, suitable removal tools and torque wrench; angle-tightening capability for the 5.0L; Motorcraft Thread Sealant with PTFE TA-24-B, specification WSK-M2G350-A2, when reusing the component.

steps.title: Expose and disconnect the component
steps.body: On the [5.0L Performance Package](#/document/G1839772), disconnect the oil-pressure switch connector. On the [5.2L](#/document/G1802208), remove the protective cover first, then disconnect the sensor connector.

steps.title: Remove the switch or sensor
steps.body: Unscrew the disconnected component using the appropriate tool. Decide whether it is being replaced or reused, because that decision controls the stated sealant requirement.

steps.title: Apply the reuse sealing instruction
steps.body: If refitting the removed switch or sensor, apply the specified Motorcraft TA-24-B thread sealant. This condition appears in both engine procedures; do not treat it as an instruction to add sealant indiscriminately to every replacement part.

steps.title: Install using the correct tightening method
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure. Tighten the 5.0L switch first to 124 lb.in (14 Nm), then an additional 180°. Tighten the 5.2L sensor to 24 lb.ft (33 Nm). Reconnect the electrical connector and restore the protective cover on the 5.2L.

watchFor.title: Transferring a torque between engines
watchFor.body: The 5.0L angle stage is part of its installation requirement. It must not be added to the 5.2L torque instruction.

watchFor.title: Confusing replacement with diagnosis
watchFor.body: These removal-and-installation procedures do not establish an acceptable oil-pressure reading or identify the cause of a pressure warning.

notes: The tightening values printed alongside removal are installation details, as identified by the procedures.

diagnostics.finding: The removed component will be reused.
diagnostics.meaning: Its threads require the specified sealant before refitting.
diagnostics.next: Apply TA-24-B and complete the appropriate engine-specific tightening sequence.

verification.title: Confirm installation completion
verification.body: Confirm the correct torque or torque-and-angle sequence, connector reconnection and, on the 5.2L, cover installation.

verification.title: Record the branch and work performed
verification.body: Record the engine, 5.0L package applicability where relevant, whether the component was new or reused, and the tightening sequence completed. Keep any unresolved pressure complaint separate from that installation record.

procedures.purpose: 5.0L Performance Package oil-pressure switch removal and installation, including torque-plus-angle tightening.
5.2L oil-pressure sensor removal and installation, including protective-cover access and single-stage torque.
Correct hoist positioning and vehicle-support precautions.

guides.title: Replace the intake manifold runner-control actuators on 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Remove the intake manifold and position sensors, replace the runner-control actuators, and reinstall everything using the correct engine-specific procedures.
guides.introduction: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) actuators move the manifold's runner-control mechanism, while separate position sensors provide information about its position. Actuator replacement is a manifold-off repair on both engines. Although the overall sequence is shared, the manifold access and sensor instructions must follow the engine fitted to the vehicle.
guides.why: Most of the work lies in reaching the actuators and restoring the connections disturbed during manifold removal. Cleanliness protects exposed engine passages, and correct sealing prevents the repair from creating another problem. The actuator and position sensor are separate components, so replacement should follow an established repair decision.

when.summary: When diagnosis or inspection establishes that an IMRC actuator requires replacement.
notes: This is a removal-and-installation path, not a diagnostic test for choosing between an actuator, sensor or another fault.
Use the 5.2L manifold procedure for that engine; the detailed 5.0L access and sealing instructions are engine-specific.

prepare.title: Provide manifold-service capability
prepare.detail: Arrange a clean work area and the tools required by the engine-matched manifold procedure. For the 5.0L, this includes fuel-pressure release, battery ground and positive cable disconnection, and new manifold gaskets.

prepare.title: Prepare controlled tightening
prepare.detail: Use a torque tool suitable for the actuator retainers. The 5.0L manifold and fuel-rail installation also uses staged torque-and-angle tightening; follow those exact stages in its manifold procedure.

steps.title: Select the correct access procedure
steps.body: Use [5.0L manifold removal](#/document/G1685326) or [5.2L manifold removal](#/document/G1800279). On the 5.0L, release fuel pressure before disconnecting both battery cables. Keep foreign material out of exposed engine passages throughout the work.

steps.title: Remove the intake manifold
steps.body: Follow the selected access sequence. On the 5.0L this includes any fitted strut-tower brace, cover and cowl access, hose supports, tubes, electrical connections and fuel connection. The fuel rail need not be separated from the manifold assembly. After releasing the fasteners, raise the manifold and move it forward to disconnect the rear harness connections. Discard the removed 5.0L manifold gaskets and clean and inspect the sealing surfaces.

steps.title: Remove the position sensors
steps.body: For the 5.0L, use the [IMRC position-sensor procedure](#/document/G1710272) to remove the left and right sensors and their retainers. The 5.2L actuator procedure directs sensor removal through its intake-manifold procedure; follow that route for the 5.2L assembly.

steps.title: Remove the actuators
steps.body: Remove the hoses, retainers and actuators using the illustration for the actual engine: [5.0L](#/document/G1692280) or [5.2L](#/document/G1802185). Keep the hose connections and actuator locations identifiable for installation.

steps.title: Refit actuators and sensors
steps.body: Reverse removal to install the actuators, retainers and hoses. Both actuator procedures specify 53 lb.in (6 Nm) for the retainers. Reinstall the sensors through their applicable procedure; the separate 5.0L sensor procedure also specifies 53 lb.in (6 Nm), which should not be assumed for the 5.2L sensors.

steps.title: Restore the manifold and connections
steps.body: Complete the engine-specific manifold installation. On the 5.0L, use new gaskets and the prescribed manifold and fuel-rail tightening stages, then restore fuel, injector, vapor, crankcase, vacuum and electrical connections, supports and access components. Place the appearance-cover grommets on the manifold before fitting the cover, reinstall any fitted brace, and reconnect both battery cables through the battery procedure.

watchFor.title: Debris after upper-engine damage
watchFor.body: For the 5.0L, an engine repair involving upper-engine failure requires inspection of the manifold for metal debris. Finding debris requires a new manifold.

watchFor.title: Assuming both engines assemble identically
watchFor.body: The shared actuator-retainer torque does not make manifold fasteners, sealing requirements or sensor installation details interchangeable.

notes: Installation details appear within the removal procedures, so read both phases before beginning.

diagnostics.finding: Metal debris is found in the 5.0L intake manifold after upper-engine failure.
diagnostics.meaning: The manifold can retain material capable of causing further engine damage.
diagnostics.next: Install a new intake manifold instead of completing actuator work on the contaminated manifold.

verification.title: Confirm assembly restoration
verification.body: Verify actuator retainers were tightened, hoses and sensors were restored, and all connections and sealing work required by the engine-specific manifold procedure are complete.

verification.title: Record the applicable final check
verification.body: If a new intake manifold was installed on the 5.0L, road test the vehicle as required by that manifold procedure and record the result.

5.2L IMRC actuator removal and installation using its engine-specific manifold and sensor access route.
5.0L manifold removal, fuel and battery prerequisites, new gaskets, installation stages and conditional road test.
Remove and reinstall the left and right 5.0L IMRC position sensors.
5.2L manifold removal and installation, including the sensor-removal route referenced by its actuator procedure.

guides.title: Replace the intake manifold runner position sensors — 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Remove the engine-specific intake manifold, service its left- and right-hand runner position sensors, and reinstall the manifold with new gaskets.
guides.introduction: The intake manifold distributes incoming air to the engine. Its intake manifold runner control (IMRC) position sensors provide feedback about the runner-control mechanism's position. Sensor access requires removing the manifold, so most of this repair involves safely disconnecting fuel, air and electrical connections and restoring the manifold's sealed joints afterward.
guides.why: Fuel pressure must be released before the supply connection is disturbed, and both battery cables must be disconnected as directed. Cleanliness protects the exposed engine passages. New manifold gaskets restore the sealing joints opened during removal. The sensor operations are shared between these engines, but their surrounding access work has important differences.
searchTerms: intake manifold runner control position sensor
left and right intake runner sensors

when.summary: When an IMRC position sensor has been identified as requiring removal or replacement.
notes: Choose the intake-manifold procedure for the actual engine before beginning fuel-system or access work.

prepare.title: Plan for manifold removal
prepare.detail: This requires safe fuel-system work, battery disconnection, access around the cowl and careful handling of wiring and quick-release couplings. Follow the prerequisite instructions reached through the appropriate manifold procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement parts and tightening equipment
prepare.detail: Have new manifold gaskets, suitable torque and angle-tightening equipment, and the sensor parts required for the repair. The 5.2L strut-tower cross-brace nuts are discarded during removal and require replacements.

steps.title: Release fuel pressure and isolate the battery
steps.body: Begin with the [5.0L manifold procedure](#/document/G1685326) or [5.2L manifold procedure](#/document/G1800279). Release fuel pressure, then disconnect the battery ground and positive cables. Remove the cross brace where directed; discard its nuts on the 5.2L.

steps.title: Clear the manifold connections
steps.body: Remove the specified air-inlet and cowl components and move the heater-hose supports aside. Disconnect the throttle, evaporative-emissions purge, vacuum, crankcase-vent and fuel connections in the engine-specific sequence. The 5.0L includes appearance-cover and fuel-rail-insulator removal; the 5.2L also requires disconnecting the fuel-pressure sensor.

steps.title: Lift the manifold and release its rear harness
steps.body: Remove the fuel-rail bolts; the rail can remain with the manifold assembly. Loosen the manifold bolts, then move the manifold upward and forward to reach its rear electrical connectors and harness retainers. Release these before removing the assembly. Discard the manifold gaskets and clean and inspect the sealing surfaces without introducing debris into the engine.

steps.title: Remove and reinstall the position sensors
steps.body: With the manifold removed, remove the retainers and left-hand sensor, followed by the retainers and right-hand sensor. Install in reverse order, tightening the retainers to 53 lb.in (6 Nm). Use the [5.0L sensor procedure](#/document/G1710272) or [5.2L sensor procedure](#/document/G1802186).

steps.title: Refit the manifold with new gaskets
steps.body: Install new gaskets and position the manifold. Reattach the rear harness retainers and connectors before settling it into its installed position. Follow the manifold and fuel-rail torque-and-angle stages in the applicable engine procedure.

steps.title: Restore the surrounding components
steps.body: Reconnect the fuel supply, injectors, air and vacuum plumbing, electrical connectors and heater-hose supports. Restore the cowl and air-inlet parts. On the 5.0L, place any appearance-cover grommets that stayed in the cover back onto the manifold before fitting the cover. Restore the cross brace with new nuts on the 5.2L, then reconnect both battery cables.

watchFor.title: Debris after upper-engine failure
watchFor.body: When this work accompanies repair or replacement following valve or piston damage, inspect the manifold for metal debris. Finding metal requires a new manifold.

watchFor.title: Trapped rear connections
watchFor.body: The rear connectors and retainers are released while the manifold is raised and moved forward; reconnect them before final positioning.

notes: The supplied illustration depicts the 5.0L manifold access arrangement; use the 5.2L procedure for that engine's connections and hardware.

diagnostics.finding: Metal debris is found in the manifold after upper-engine failure.
diagnostics.meaning: The manifold can retain material capable of damaging the repaired engine.
diagnostics.next: Install a new manifold and complete the required road test after installation.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly requirements
verification.body: Confirm new manifold gaskets, completed fastener tightening stages, restored fuel and electrical connections, and correct cross-brace hardware.

verification.title: Apply the conditional road test
verification.body: If a new intake manifold was installed, road test the vehicle. Record whether the manifold was replaced and whether that required road test was completed.
