5.2L left- and right-hand IMRC position-sensor removal and installation.
5.0L manifold access, fuel and battery prerequisites, gasket renewal and reinstallation.
5.2L manifold access and reinstallation, including discarded cross-brace nuts and fuel-pressure-sensor connection.

guides.title: Replace intake runner control solenoids on the 5.0L or 5.2L
guides.summary: Replace the intake manifold runner control solenoid using the engine-specific access route, hose connections and fastening requirements.
guides.introduction: The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) solenoids control vacuum used by the intake-runner mechanism. Their hoses connect the solenoids to that operating system. Although the two engines share the component name, their replacement paths differ: the 5.0L requires intake-manifold removal and a solenoid mounting plate, while the 5.2L provides separate left-hand and right-hand solenoid operations.
guides.why: Correct hose connections and engine-specific fastening matter to restoring the vacuum-control arrangement. On the 5.0L, access also opens intake joints and involves the fuel supply, making pressure release, battery disconnection, cleanliness and new manifold gaskets essential parts of the job.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established the need to replace an IMRC solenoid.
notes: Identify the engine before starting; the access steps and solenoid fastener torques differ.
For the 5.2L, identify whether the left-hand or right-hand solenoid is being replaced.

prepare.title: Arrange engine-specific tools and capability
prepare.detail: Have suitable torque equipment for the solenoid fasteners. The 5.0L also requires manifold-removal capability, fuel-system pressure release, battery disconnection and the torque-angle capability specified for manifold and fuel-rail installation.

prepare.title: Prepare for clean 5.0L manifold work
prepare.detail: Have new intake-manifold gaskets ready. Keep foreign material out of the engine and maintain the identity of disconnected hoses and electrical connections.

steps.title: 5.0L: make manifold access safe
steps.body: Follow [Intake Manifold removal](#/document/G1685326). Release fuel-system pressure, then disconnect the battery ground and positive cables using the specified procedures. Remove the fitted strut tower cross brace and its harness attachment, engine appearance cover, air cleaner outlet pipe, cowl panel grille and cowl extension as directed.

steps.title: 5.0L: disconnect and remove the manifold
steps.body: Follow the manifold procedure through moving the heater hoses and supports, disconnecting vacuum, crankcase ventilation and evaporative-emissions connections, electrical connectors and fuel supply, and removing the fuel rail insulators. The fuel rail need not be removed from the manifold assembly. Remove its bolts, loosen the manifold bolts and move the manifold upward and forward to disconnect the rear wiring. Remove the manifold, discard its gaskets, and clean and inspect the sealing surfaces.

steps.title: 5.0L: remove the solenoid assembly
steps.body: Following the [5.0L solenoid procedure](#/document/G1710273), disconnect the six vacuum hoses, remove the three mounting-plate retainers and remove the plate. Remove the two solenoid retainers and the solenoids. During reverse-order installation, tighten the solenoid retainers to 71 lb.in (8 Nm) and the mounting-plate retainers to 53 lb.in (6 Nm).

steps.title: 5.2L: replace the selected side's solenoid
steps.body: Use the left-hand or right-hand branch of the [5.2L solenoid procedure](#/document/G1991988). Disconnect that solenoid's electrical connector and vacuum hoses, then remove its two retainers and the solenoid. Install in reverse order, tightening the retainers to 53 lb.in (6 Nm), and reconnect the hoses and connector.

steps.title: 5.0L: inspect before manifold installation
steps.body: If the engine repair followed upper-engine failure, typically valve or piston damage, inspect the intake manifold for metal debris. Install a new manifold if debris is found. Install new gaskets before positioning the manifold on the engine.

steps.title: 5.0L: complete the manifold installation sequence
steps.body: Reconnect the rear harness and attach its retainers, then position the manifold fully. Follow the linked manifold procedure's staged tightening for the manifold and fuel rail. Restore the fuel supply, injector connectors, insulators, heater-hose supports, crankcase ventilation, evaporative-emissions, throttle and vacuum connections in its installation sequence.

steps.title: 5.0L: restore access components
steps.body: Refit the cowl components and air cleaner outlet pipe. Seat the appearance-cover grommets on the manifold before fitting the cover. Restore any cross brace and harness retainer, then connect the battery cables using the specified procedure. Road test the vehicle if a new intake manifold was installed.

watchFor.title: Different solenoid tightening values
watchFor.body: The 5.0L solenoid retainers use a different torque from the 5.2L solenoid retainers; do not transfer the value between engines.

watchFor.title: Contamination or retained metal debris
watchFor.body: Foreign material introduced during engine work can cause engine failure. A manifold containing metal debris after upper-engine failure must be replaced.

notes: The manifold-removal prerequisite belongs to the 5.0L procedure. Follow the separate side-specific instructions for the 5.2L.

verification.title: Confirm the applicable connections and assembly
verification.body: Check that the selected engine's solenoid fasteners, vacuum hoses and electrical connections are restored. For the 5.0L, also confirm new manifold gaskets and completion of the manifold installation sequence.

verification.title: Record conditional completion
verification.body: Record the engine and solenoid side or assembly replaced. If a new intake manifold was fitted, record completion of the required road test.

procedures.purpose: 5.0L IMRC solenoid removal and installation after manifold removal, including mounting-plate and solenoid fastening.
5.2L left-hand and right-hand IMRC solenoid removal and installation.
Required 5.0L intake-manifold removal and installation, including fuel-pressure release, battery disconnection, new gaskets and conditional road testing.

guides.title: Replace the MAF/IAT sensor on a 2015 Mustang 5.0L or 5.2L
guides.summary: Locate the combined intake-air sensor, disconnect its wiring, remove its two retainers and refit it following the applicable engine-specific installation instructions.
guides.introduction: The intake has a little numbers nerd keeping track of incoming air, and thankfully it takes only two retainers to evict it. The combined mass air flow (MAF) and intake air temperature (IAT) sensor provides information about how much air is entering the engine and its temperature. I’ll walk you through its removal and refitting, keeping the wiring out of the wrestling match and the engine-specific tightening details straight.
guides.why: Disconnecting the electrical plug before removing the sensor keeps its wiring from restraining the loose component. During installation, the sensor is secured before the plug goes back on. Both engines use this sequence, but only the 5.2L procedure provides a numerical retainer torque.

when.summary: Use this procedure when an established repair requires removal or replacement of the combined MAF/IAT sensor.
notes: This is a removal and installation job; it does not establish whether the sensor is faulty.

For engine-control diagnosis, the [5.0L system-operation reference](#/document/G1692302) and [5.2L system-operation reference](#/document/G1802177) direct you to the Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis (PC/ED) Manual, Section 1, Description and Operation. Those references do not provide a sensor test here.

prepare.title: Confirm the engine and tightening information
prepare.detail: Choose the [5.0L procedure](#/document/G1834541) or [5.2L procedure](#/document/G1991990) before starting. Ford specifies reverse-order installation for the 5.0L without giving a numerical sensor-retainer torque. The 5.2L value of 18 lb.in (2 Nm) applies only to the 5.2L; do not substitute it for the 5.0L.

prepare.title: Have the fastening tools and sensor ready
prepare.detail: Have a driver that fits the sensor retainers. For the 5.2L, use torque equipment capable of accurately applying 18 lb.in (2 Nm). If replacing the sensor, have the replacement appropriate to the fitted engine ready. Keep the removed retainers for refitting.

steps.title: Locate the sensor on the intake tube
steps.body:
Before reaching into the engine compartment, switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle. If remote start is fitted, disable it in the vehicle’s Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before starting the work. This prevents someone else or a remote command from starting the engine during service. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

Working at the engine intake, find the large ribbed flexible duct and follow it to the adjoining smooth intake tube. The sensor mounts on the smooth tube close to that junction, beside the large housing shown in the illustration.

In both engine illustrations, the sensor body is blue and its electrical connector is magenta, with the wiring extending downward. These are illustration highlights, not colors to expect on the car. The depicted removal goes directly to the connector and sensor; no intake-duct or housing removal is called for.

steps.title: Disconnect the electrical connector first
steps.body:
Release the sensor’s electrical connector and separate the plug from the sensor. Handle the connector body rather than pulling on its wires.

Move the disconnected plug and its wiring clear of the sensor’s removal path. Leave the sensor retainers installed until the electrical connection is separated. The little plug gets to leave first; it does not need to come along for the ride.

steps.title: Remove both retainers and lift out the sensor
steps.body:
Note how the sensor sits in its mounting so you can restore the same orientation. Remove the two sensor retainers; the illustration marks their removal with an “x2” callout.

With the connector disconnected and both retainers removed, remove the sensor from the intake tube. Keep the retainers together for installation.

steps.title: Return the sensor to its mounting
steps.body: Place the sensor being installed into the intake-tube mounting in the same orientation as the removed unit. Refit both retainers. Keep the electrical connector disconnected while you secure the sensor.

steps.title: Secure the retainers for the correct engine
steps.body:
For the 5.2L, tighten the sensor retainers to 18 lb.in (2 Nm).

For the 5.0L, secure both refitted retainers to complete the reverse installation sequence. Its procedure does not give a numerical torque; do not borrow the 5.2L value.

The 5.2L measurement is in pound-inches, not pound-feet. Check the tool’s units before applying torque.

steps.title: Reconnect the sensor
steps.body:
After securing the sensor, bring the electrical plug back to its connection and reconnect it. Return the wiring to its original route without trapping it beneath the sensor or retainers.

Check that the connector is fully engaged and that both retainers are installed. That completes the reverse of the removal sequence.

watchFor.title: A connector still tethering the sensor
watchFor.body: If the wiring remains attached, stop lifting the sensor and finish disconnecting the plug. Do not use the sensor’s movement to pull the connector apart.

watchFor.title: Pound-inches versus pound-feet
watchFor.body: The 5.2L specification is 18 lb.in (2 Nm). Use pound-inches, not pound-feet, when setting the tool.

notes: The removal and installation procedures do not call for a separate learning or initialization operation. Mechanical completion alone does not prove that an earlier engine-control complaint has been resolved.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical assembly
verification.body: Check that the sensor is back in its original mounting orientation and both retainers are installed and secured. On the 5.2L, confirm that they were tightened to 18 lb.in (2 Nm). Keep that numerical specification specific to the 5.2L installation.

verification.title: Confirm the electrical connection and wiring position
verification.body: Check that the sensor connector is fully engaged and its wiring is clear of the mounting. These are assembly checks, not a sensor-performance test.

guides.title: Replace the 5.2L fuel rail pressure and temperature sensor
guides.summary: Release fuel pressure, isolate both battery cables, replace the sensor using staged tightening, and check for leaks before and after starting the engine.
guides.introduction: The fuel rail pressure and temperature sensor measures those two conditions in the fuel supply. Replacing it involves opening a fuel-system connection, so pressure release and leak checks are central parts of the work. This guide follows the 5.2L procedure, including its use of both fuel pump control modules and its instruction to disconnect both battery cables.
guides.why: Disconnecting the pump-control connectors and running the engine until it stalls provides the prescribed pressure-release sequence. Battery isolation follows that operation. On reassembly, the sensor requires both a torque setting and an additional angle. The separate checks before starting and with the engine running establish whether the serviced fuel connection remains sealed.
searchTerms: 5.2L fuel rail pressure temperature sensor replacement

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the 5.2L fuel rail pressure and temperature sensor requires replacement.
notes: Use the 5.2L pressure-release procedure for this job.

prepare.title: Arrange fuel-system capability
prepare.detail: Be equipped to perform the specified pressure release, work on the fuel connection and carry out controlled engine-running leak checks.

prepare.title: Plan rear-seat and battery access
prepare.detail: The two fuel pump control modules are on the left side beneath the rear seat cushion. Have the rear-seat cushion procedure and the linked battery procedure available.

prepare.title: Prepare staged tightening
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools to apply the sensor's specified torque and subsequent angle, as well as the battery cable-nut torque.

steps.title: Release the fuel pressure
steps.body: Remove the rear seat cushion and disconnect both fuel pump control module electrical connectors. Start the engine and allow it to idle until it stalls, then turn the ignition off. Follow the complete linked 5.2L pressure-release procedure.

steps.title: Disconnect both battery cables
steps.body: Remove the battery cover and disconnect the negative cable, then access and disconnect the positive cable using the battery procedure. Although that general procedure permits negative-only disconnection for ordinary power interruption, this sensor repair specifically requires both cables disconnected.

steps.title: Remove the sensor
steps.body: With pressure released and the battery isolated, disconnect and remove the fuel rail pressure and temperature sensor as directed in the sensor procedure.

steps.title: Install with the specified tightening stages
steps.body: Reverse the sensor removal operation. Apply the specified installation tightening in order: Stage 1 is 53 lb.in (6 Nm); Stage 2 is an additional 25°. Restore the sensor connection.

steps.title: Restore the battery and pump connections
steps.body: Reconnect the battery in reverse disconnection order, using 44 lb.in (5 Nm) for the cable nuts, and restore the covers. Reconnect both fuel pump control module connectors and reinstall the rear seat cushion.

steps.title: Pressurize and check for leaks
steps.body: Cycle the ignition key and wait 3 seconds to pressurize the system. Check for leaks before starting the engine. Once that check is satisfactory, start the engine and check again for leaks.

watchFor.title: Leakage during initial pressurization
watchFor.body: Resolve any leakage before starting the engine; the pre-start check is a required part of the pressure-release procedure's restoration sequence.

watchFor.title: An omitted pump connection
watchFor.body: Both fuel pump control module connectors disconnected for pressure release must be restored.

notes: Battery disconnection can temporarily change driving behavior while the powertrain control module relearns its adaptive values. Driving may be needed for that relearning; it does not replace the fuel leak checks.

verification.title: Confirm assembly and tightening
verification.body: Confirm completion of both sensor-tightening stages, restored battery connections, both pump-control connectors and rear-seat installation.

verification.title: Record both leak-check results
verification.body: Record the result after ignition pressurization and the separate result with the engine running.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L fuel rail pressure and temperature sensor removal and installation, including the two-stage tightening requirement.
5.2L fuel pressure release through both pump-control connectors, followed by reconnection, pressurization and pre-start/running leak checks.
Battery cable disconnection and reconnection; apply the sensor procedure's requirement to disconnect both cables.

guides.title: Overhaul the 6R80 six-speed automatic transmission
guides.summary: Remove the transmission, inspect and rebuild its hydraulic and mechanical assemblies, set the required clearances, then reinstall and complete calibration and fluid checks.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 passes engine power through a torque converter into planetary gears. Electronically controlled hydraulic pressure applies internal clutches to select the gears. Overhaul means complete dismantling, cleaning, inspection, seal renewal and measured reassembly—not simply replacing the clutch plates. The bench procedure serves the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications, but vehicle access, clutch quantities and some internal parts differ.
guides.why: Debris remaining in the converter or cooling circuit can damage rebuilt components. Incorrect clutch clearance, misplaced bearings or mismatched parts can prevent proper operation even when everything looks clean. Electronic calibration also matters: the transmission controller must use the strategy matching the installed solenoid body.

when.summary: When diagnosis and inspection establish internal wear or damage requiring complete transmission rebuilding.
notes: Harsh shifts alone do not establish that an overhaul is needed; an incorrect solenoid strategy can also produce them.

prepare.title: Arrange specialist handling and bench equipment
prepare.detail: You need safe hoist access, a high-lift transmission jack with restraint, torque converter retainer and handling tools, transmission holding fixture, press, specified clutch spring compressors, bearing and seal tools, dial indicator and depth gauges. Bench work includes controlled shop-air piston removal.

prepare.title: Have the supporting procedures and capabilities ready
prepare.detail: Use the engine-specific access procedure and its lifting, starter, driveshaft, exhaust and crossmember prerequisites. Arrange converter flushing, cooler backflushing and a diagnostic scan tool capable of the required corrections and learning procedures.

prepare.title: Prepare fluids and replacement parts
prepare.detail: Use the specified Motorcraft MERCON LV automatic transmission fluid and gasket kit -7153-. Renew seals, gaskets and all designated one-use components, including the filter, discarded clutch retainers, direct clutch hub, roll pin and specified fasteners. Select clutch parts for the actual engine.

steps.title: Choose the correct vehicle access route
steps.body: Start with the [removal entry](#/document/G1692037) and the applicable procedure. All variants require starter and driveshaft removal. The [2.3L procedure](#/document/G1692044) includes the starter insulator, catalytic converter bracket, dust shield and cooler-tube supports. The [3.7L procedure](#/document/G1692046) includes the access cover and left catalyst monitor sensor. The [5.0L procedure](#/document/G1692048) additionally removes the right catalytic converter, left heated oxygen and catalyst monitor sensors, and flexplate inspection cover. Follow the fitted shield or shield-and-subframe-bracket branch.

steps.title: Drain, support and remove the transmission
steps.body: Position the vehicle on the hoist in NEUTRAL. Rotate the crankshaft clockwise only, mark a converter stud against the flexplate and discard the converter nuts. Drain through pan removal, then refit the pan. Disconnect the cooler tubes and selector cable as directed. Restrain the jack-supported transmission with contact at the pan's outer ribs before removing the crossmember. Release wiring and bellhousing attachments in engine-specific order; fit the converter retainer before removing the transmission.

steps.title: Clean the cooling circuit and assess the converter
steps.body: Backflush and clean the cooler circuit whenever overhauling or replacing the transmission. Mount the transmission securely on its bench fixture and remove the converter with its handling tool. Converter flushing is mandatory during overhaul. Use the specified heated, pulsating equipment with flow measurement, filtration and air purge. Follow the full setup, flushing and cooling sequence. Hand flushing is permitted only when compliant heated equipment is unavailable and the fluid contains no metallic contamination.

steps.title: Dismantle in the prescribed order
steps.body: The [disassembly procedure](#/document/G1692070) leads to the [complete overhaul sequence](#/document/G1692066). Remove the pan, filter, connector sleeve, main control, feed seals and pump before extracting clutch and planetary assemblies. Keep plate groups together and identify shims, bearings and orientation marks. Unstake the output flange nut before removal and discard it. Continue through the output bearings and parking mechanism; bearing pullers must contact the bearing rather than the case lip.

steps.title: Rebuild the clutch assemblies
steps.body: Inspect the forward, overdrive, direct, intermediate and low/reverse assemblies. Replace excessively worn or damaged plates; serviceable plates may be reused. Renew the specified piston seals, sealing rings and discarded retainers using the designated compressors and seal-sizing tools. Confirm retaining rings are seated before releasing spring pressure. Soak plates in clean transmission fluid and follow each pack's stacking order. Match engine-specific plate quantities and any replacement intermediate piston height.

steps.title: Measure rather than assume clutch clearance
steps.body: For the forward, overdrive, direct and intermediate clutches, record and average the opposed dial-indicator readings. Correct excessive clearance with a thicker selective snap ring, or insufficient clearance with a thinner one. Low/reverse clearance uses case depth minus clutch-pack height and piston-to-support height; adjust its selective plate and remeasure. Use the [specifications](#/document/G1686431) for the applicable quantities and limits.

steps.title: Rebuild the pump and rear transmission
steps.body: Follow the [assembly route](#/document/G1692071) through the overhaul procedure. Inspect pump gears, surfaces and bushings, then assemble with the alignment marks, gear orientation and new seals specified. Restore the parking mechanism with new discarded hardware. Install the output assembly, planetary components, low/reverse plates, one-way clutch and center support in order, preserving bearing and snap-ring orientations. Measure rear end play with the new flange nut loose; select the correct shim before tightening and staking the nut.

steps.title: Complete the front assembly and hydraulic controls
steps.body: Install the remaining clutch assemblies, selective shim and pump with new pump-to-case bolts and washers. Measure input end play; remove the pump and change the shim if necessary. Renew feed-tube and pump-adapter seals, inspect the thermal bypass valve and align the main control's manual valve with its linkage. Follow the illustrated tightening sequence. Fully seat and lock the connector sleeve, install a new filter, close the pan and install the converter.

steps.title: Refill and reinstall through the correct engine procedure
steps.body: Use the [installation entry](#/document/G1692042) to return to the appropriate engine procedure. Record the strategy identification before fitting a new transmission or a rebuilt unit with a new main control; replace the tag when required. Follow the prefill branch, grease the converter pilot and keep the converter fully seated while aligning the transmission on the engine dowels. Restore attachments with new converter nuts and cooler-tube bolt. Inspect and lubricate cooler seals and backing rings, replacing damaged parts.

steps.title: Restore adjustment and electronic setup
steps.body: Verify selector-cable adjustment and perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction with the scan tool. Download the solenoid strategy if the transmission or main control was replaced. Complete the adaptive learning drive cycle after overhaul, then perform the warm-circulation and final fluid-level checks below.

watchFor.title: Converter flushing hazards
watchFor.body: Watch the converter throughout heated flushing and stop immediately if a leak develops. The converter, adapter and hoses become hot; allow the specified 30-minute cooling period before handling. Never flush the converter with water-based cleaners or mineral spirits.

watchFor.title: Small assembly details with major consequences
watchFor.body: Position the new direct-clutch-hub retaining-ring gap approximately 120° from its original marked location. Hook the pump seal-ring ends together. Do not pull on the wiring harness to disconnect the transmission connector.

notes: The pan gasket is specifically reusable if undamaged.

Use only 9–10 ml of XL-16 additive F after complete fluid replacement or replacement of the overdrive friction plates. Do not use the kit's tracer T syringe; excess additive can cause converter-clutch slip. Supplemental additives and cleaning agents are not permitted during converter flushing.

diagnostics.finding: Converter seal-track groove, damaged studs, threaded pads, hub or bushing, overheating discoloration, water/antifreeze contamination, or diagnostically confirmed malfunction.
diagnostics.meaning: The converter meets a replacement criterion.
diagnostics.next: Install a new or remanufactured converter.

diagnostics.finding: Metallic contamination in the converter-fluid sample.
diagnostics.meaning: Hand flushing is not acceptable.
diagnostics.next: Use the specified heated flushing equipment; do not continue the hand-flushing branch.

diagnostics.finding: Pump wear marks or damaged pump components.
diagnostics.meaning: Light internal scratches can be normal; burned, discolored or scored gears, damaged teeth and damaged bushings require a different decision.
diagnostics.next: Follow the pump inspection criteria and replace the pump where specified, including for damaged input-shaft or converter-hub bushings.

diagnostics.finding: The main-control strategy differs from the scan-tool display.
diagnostics.meaning: Incorrect calibration can cause harsh shifts.
diagnostics.next: Download the matching strategy rather than treating shift feel alone as proof of mechanical failure.

verification.title: Keep the measurement record
verification.body: Retain the clutch readings and calculations, selected adjustment parts, and final rear and input end-play readings. Every clearance must meet its own specification before closing the assembly.

verification.title: Confirm warm circulation and final level
verification.body: During driving, verify transmission fluid temperature reaches 96.7°C–102°C using the scan tool. This circulates fluid through the converter and cooling system to remove trapped air. Then complete the prescribed transmission fluid level check; the installation prefill does not replace it.

guides.title: Diagnose 2.3L 6R80 solenoid and sensor electrical faults
guides.summary: Trace solenoid, temperature and shaft-speed faults on the 2.3L 6R80, and assess range-sensor operation through its supply measurement.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 uses electrically controlled solenoids to operate its hydraulic circuits. Temperature, range and shaft-speed sensors tell the powertrain control module (PCM) how the transmission is operating. These checks distinguish wiring faults, contaminated connections and component failures before replacement becomes justified.
guides.why: Several faults can share one power or return circuit. The PCM can also deliberately switch off solenoid power after detecting a fault. A missing signal or inactive solenoid therefore needs circuit testing, not an immediate parts diagnosis.

when.summary: Use when a verified transmission concern or returning fault code directs electrical testing.
notes: Component-replacement decisions require the relevant concern to be present during testing.
Resolve transmission-range codes before entering either shaft-speed test.

prepare.title: Prepare for Ford electrical diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use a compatible diagnostic scan tool, a digital multimeter with min/max recording, specified Rotunda flex probes and a fused jumper. Verify battery state of charge exceeds 70%. Use [Diagnostic Methods](#/document/G1693185) for circuit isolation and terminal protection.

prepare.title: Plan access and later repair capability
prepare.detail: Identify transmission connector C168 and PCM connector C1551E. Internal checks require the linked pan and leadframe procedures; a justified PCM replacement requires the specified programming and transmission strategy download.

steps.title: Verify the concern and choose the correct branch
steps.body: Inspect for mechanical damage, harness damage and previous repair problems. Check terminals, corrosion, contamination and connector seals whenever disconnected. Run key-on engine-off (KOEO) and key-on engine-running (KOER) self-tests; record diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Repair non-transmission codes first, then transmission codes, and clear and attempt to reproduce continuous-memory codes. Follow the [DTC chart](#/document/G1686449); pass codes with a continuing complaint lead to [Diagnosis By Symptom](#/document/G1686447). Use the commanded-gear solenoid table: an off state can be normal and some states change with vehicle movement.

steps.title: Test A: establish solenoid power and harness integrity
steps.body: The transmission solenoid power control (TSPC) relay inside the PCM supplies every solenoid. For A1, switch ignition off, disconnect C168 and connect the recording voltmeter between pin 7 and ground before switching ignition on. Select a DC range greater than 15 volts. A maximum above 11 volts leads to A4; otherwise follow A2–A3 for supply continuity and a ground short before their PCM decision. A4–A6 then check the suspect control circuit for an open, a ground short and unwanted voltage, in that order.

steps.title: Test A: separate contamination, leadframe and solenoid faults
steps.body: After the harness checks pass, use [pan removal](#/document/G1692033) for A7. Clean metallic contamination from leadframe and solenoid terminals with clean transmission fluid; discard the fitted foam strip when this cleaning branch requires it. A8 checks leadframe continuity and directs replacement if it fails. For A9, remove the leadframe, clean the contacts and record the suspect solenoid's resistance against its own specification; shift solenoid E differs from the others. Replace a failed solenoid. Fit new foam strip FL3Z-14B167-A at the specified A8/A9 endpoints, including a passing A9 result, using [Shift Solenoids](#/document/G1692059).

steps.title: Test B: distinguish a temperature-input fault from overheating
steps.body: The transmission fluid temperature (TFT) sensor changes resistance with fluid temperature. B1 checks the disconnected sensor's scan-tool readings; B2 checks signal voltage. B3 uses the specified fused jumper between C168 pins 5 and 6 to check signal return. Compare each result with its exact limits before proceeding; signal or return opens must be investigated before the applicable PCM endpoint. B4 compares the removed leadframe's sensor resistance with actual temperature. A matching result sends overheating diagnosis to the symptom procedure. A mismatch calls for contamination inspection and cleaning; if no debris is found, the branch directs leadframe replacement.

steps.title: Test C: observe range operation and record supply voltage
steps.body: The transmission range (TR) sensor is integral to the leadframe and reports manual-valve position, including information used for starting and reversing lamps. Begin C1 in Park and confirm range DTCs. In C2, observe scan-tool parameters TR_DC and TR_FREQ in each selector position and during harness movement or the prescribed drive check. Frequency must remain within 100 to 150 Hz, with steady duty cycle inside the position-specific band. Passing results lead to symptom diagnosis. Otherwise perform C3: ignition off, disconnect and inspect C168, then ignition on and measure pin 12 to ground. Record the result and stop this range-sensor path. It does not authorize PCM replacement or advancement to C4.

steps.title: Keep the later range checks separate from the C3 stopping point
steps.body: C4–C6 require an independently established entry; do not infer one from C3. C4 checks C168 pin 4 to ground, then C5 checks pin 4 to pin 11; each requires greater than 4.8 volts to advance. A failed check calls for open-circuit investigation before its PCM/strategy-download endpoint. C6 requires draining fluid and removing the pan to inspect the sensor-to-manual-valve connection and contamination. A connected sensor leads to replacement. If disconnected, reconnect it, clean debris and run KOEO; returning codes then direct sensor replacement.

steps.title: Test D: trace turbine-shaft-speed faults
steps.body: The turbine shaft speed (TSS) signal helps the PCM calculate converter slip and gear ratio. Monitor TSS_SRC through upshifts and downshifts in every gear. If it tracks engine speed and vehicle speed, it is operating correctly at that time. Otherwise D2 checks P0720, P0721 and P0722: their presence leads through shared supply/return checks D3–D6; their absence leads to D7. For this 2.3L installation, D7 uses C168 pin 1 to C1551E pin 27, with ignition off and both connectors disconnected. Resistance below 3 ohms advances to D8, which requires greater than 10,000 ohms to ground. D9 then checks for unwanted voltage with ignition on: voltage directs circuit repair; none directs leadframe replacement and code clearing.

steps.title: Test E: trace output-shaft-speed faults
steps.body: The output shaft speed (OSS) signal provides the other speed measurement used to calculate gear ratio. Monitor OSS_SRC through all gears. A responsive signal passes E1; otherwise E2 checks for TSS codes P0715, P0716 and P0717, which direct the [turbine-shaft-speed checks in Test D](#/document/G1686449), described above. Without those codes, E3 checks continuity from C168 pin 15 to C1551E pin 12, below 3 ohms. E4 requires greater than 10,000 ohms to ground. With both ends still disconnected, E5 checks for voltage with ignition on: repair unwanted voltage, or follow the leadframe-replacement endpoint if none is present.

watchFor.title: D5 requires isolation despite ignition being on
watchFor.body: D5 retains C168 and C1551E disconnected and specifies ignition ON. Before selecting resistance, verify no voltage is present on the isolated C168 pin 12–C1551E pin 22 conductor. Never connect an ohmmeter to an energized circuit. Below 3 ohms reaches D5's PCM endpoint; otherwise repair the circuit.

watchFor.title: Range faults are not cable-adjustment diagnoses
watchFor.body: The listed TR electrical DTCs cannot be caused by incorrect selector-cable adjustment. Some range faults can prevent cranking.

watchFor.title: Forward creep in Neutral needs a different investigation
watchFor.body: P177F can accompany mechanical or hydraulic application of the direct or forward clutch. Its returning-code branch directs internal transmission investigation.

notes: Use the 2.3L wiring column and connector assignments throughout; D7 terminates at C1551E cavity 27.
A passing electrical test establishes operation at that time, not the absence of an intermittent fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0657 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The solenoid supply circuit may be open, grounded or disconnected; protective power shutdown can also affect observations.
diagnostics.next: Inspect and repair as directed, clear the code and follow Test A.

diagnostics.finding: P0741, P1744, gear-ratio or friction-element performance codes return.
diagnostics.meaning: These branches can concern hydraulic or mechanical operation rather than electrical solenoid failure.
diagnostics.next: Follow the individual chart referral to Diagnosis By Symptom.

diagnostics.finding: P1783 returns with temperature-sensor circuit codes.
diagnostics.meaning: The overheating indication must be assessed alongside the temperature-input fault.
diagnostics.next: Resolve TFT circuit codes first; without them, follow Transmission Cooling diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Power, self-test, programming or external-control codes are recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The fault may lie outside the transmission sensor circuits.
diagnostics.next: Use the individual chart branches for power/charging, self-test conditions, SelectShift, door status or reversing lamps. P1001 requires other faults repaired before software escalation; P163E and P163F require reprogramming the original PCM before replacement is considered.

verification.title: Repeat the relevant check
verification.body: After an authorized repair, clear codes and repeat the prescribed self-test, signal observation or drive cycle. Complete any specified PCM programming and transmission strategy download.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic endpoint
verification.body: Save original and returning codes, measured values and test conditions. For C3, retain the supply reading as an observation with range diagnosis still unfinished.

guides.title: Diagnose 3.7L 6R80 automatic transmission fault codes
guides.summary: Use the fault-code chart and five pinpoint tests to distinguish electrical supply, wiring, sensor and solenoid faults from hydraulic transmission concerns.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 selects gears by directing transmission fluid through solenoids to internal clutches. Its powertrain control module (PCM) uses range, temperature and shaft-speed signals to control shifting and the torque converter clutch. These tests trace the electrical causes of a verified concern and identify when diagnosis needs to move into hydraulic operation, cooling or another vehicle system.
guides.why: Several apparent component faults can share one cause. The transmission solenoid power control relay supplies every solenoid, and the PCM can deliberately disable that supply after certain faults. Missing power therefore does not establish that several solenoids have failed.

when.summary: When the 6R80 has a verified operating concern or transmission-related diagnostic trouble codes.
notes: Component-replacement decisions require the relevant concern to be present during testing.

prepare.title: Diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable scan tool for self-tests and live data, plus Wiring Diagrams Cell 30. Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%.

prepare.title: Electrical measurements
prepare.detail: Have a digital multimeter with minimum/maximum recording, Rotunda Flex Probes and a fused jumper. Follow each test's connector and ignition states; voltage present during resistance testing invalidates readings.

prepare.title: Internal access
prepare.detail: Some branches require fluid draining, pan removal and molded leadframe access. Arrange the capability to follow the linked pan and solenoid removal and installation procedures.

steps.title: Confirm the concern and establish diagnostic priority
steps.body: Inspect for mechanical damage, wiring faults and damaged connector terminals or seals. Run key-on engine-off (KOEO) and key-on engine-running (KOER) self-tests and record all diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Repair non-transmission faults first, then transmission faults, prioritizing circuit faults over performance faults. Clear continuous-memory codes and attempt to reproduce them. Use the [code chart](#/document/G1686462) to select the correct branch.

steps.title: Test A: trace transmission control-solenoid faults
steps.body: Check the shared supply before individual control circuits. Connect the recording meter before switching the ignition on: the PCM removes supply power when it detects the disconnected transmission harness. Follow A1–A6 for supply and control-circuit faults. If directed inside, inspect the leadframe-to-solenoid connections for fine metal contamination; discard the foam strip if fitted when contamination is found, and clean terminals with clean transmission fluid. Test leadframe continuity, then record suspect-solenoid resistance against its specification; shift solenoid E has a different range. Replace the failed leadframe or solenoid only at the specified endpoint. The internal-test endpoints require a new foam strip, including a passing solenoid-resistance result.

steps.title: Test B: separate temperature-sensor faults from overheating
steps.body: For transmission fluid temperature (TFT) faults, compare the disconnected-circuit scan readings, check signal voltage, then use only B3's prescribed fused-jumper connection to test the return circuit. These checks distinguish wiring or PCM concerns from the sensor. Remove the leadframe when directed and compare sensor resistance with actual temperature using B4's table. An incorrect relationship requires contamination inspection and cleaning; if no debris is found, the branch specifies leadframe replacement. Correct resistance with an overheating complaint leads to symptom diagnosis.

steps.title: Test C: investigate range signals and related no-crank concerns
steps.body: Select PARK and perform the specified self-tests. Compare transmission range (TR) duty cycle and frequency in each listed selector position, checking stability during harness movement or the prescribed drive check. Correct, stable readings lead to symptom diagnosis. Otherwise test power, signal and ground before draining fluid and inspecting the sensor's connection to the manual valve shaft. If disconnected, reconnect it, clean debris and rerun KOEO; returning codes require sensor replacement. If already connected after the preceding checks, C6 directs sensor replacement.

steps.title: Test D: assess turbine shaft speed
steps.body: Resolve range-sensor codes first. Monitor turbine shaft speed (TSS) using TSS_SRC while the transmission upshifts and downshifts through every gear. Speed that rises and falls with engine speed and vehicle speed passes this check. If abnormal, check for output-speed codes: companion faults lead through shared power and ground checks. Otherwise follow the TSS signal-circuit checks. Repair wiring faults; a passing circuit sequence leads to molded leadframe replacement.

steps.title: Test E: assess output shaft speed
steps.body: After resolving range codes, monitor output shaft speed (OSS) using OSS_SRC through the specified road test. A normal response passes the current check. An abnormal response with companion turbine-speed codes redirects diagnosis to Test D. Otherwise check the OSS signal circuit for an open and shorts to ground or power. Repair any circuit fault; passing those checks leads to leadframe replacement and code clearing.

steps.title: Complete the selected repair and programming path
steps.body: Use the linked removal and installation procedures for internal repairs. Match an individual replacement solenoid's nozzle and band number to the original. Complete every strategy download or PCM programming operation required by the selected branch. A replacement solenoid body needs its matching strategy downloaded.

watchFor.title: Unexpected movement in neutral
watchFor.body: The engine-running neutral check for P177F can reveal forward creep from an internally applied clutch. Treat this as a movement hazard.

watchFor.title: Range codes are not cable-adjustment evidence
watchFor.body: The listed TR sensor codes cannot be caused by an incorrectly adjusted selector cable. Follow the electrical and manual-valve connection tests.

notes: Read the solenoid pre-diagnosis table against selector position, commanded gear and its movement-dependent notes.
Selector-switch, reversing-lamp and vehicle-speed self-test faults have separate chart referrals; they do not automatically justify internal transmission work.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0741 or P1744 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These torque converter clutch performance faults are classified as non-electrical.
diagnostics.next: If they return after clearing, follow Diagnosis By Symptom. Incorrect-ratio and friction-element performance codes also require their chart-directed hydraulic or mechanical path.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0702, P0882, P0883 or P1397 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The chart identifies electrical supply or voltage concerns requiring attention before condemning transmission components.
diagnostics.next: Follow the code-specific circuit inspections and self-tests; recurring faults lead to 3.7L charging-system diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P177F is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A direct or forward clutch may remain mechanically or hydraulically applied in neutral.
diagnostics.next: Perform the prescribed engine-running neutral check. Clear the code; recurrence requires investigation for internal transmission failure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1783 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: An overtemperature condition has been detected, but accompanying temperature-sensor circuit faults can affect interpretation.
diagnostics.next: Clear and recheck. Resolve any TFT circuit codes first; otherwise proceed to transmission-cooling diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1001, P163E or P163F returns.
diagnostics.meaning: P1001 concerns an aborted running self-test; P163E and P163F concern programming or transmission identification data.
diagnostics.next: For P1001, repair other self-test and memory faults first. Follow the chart's reprogramming and retest sequence before PCM replacement, then perform the required strategy download.

verification.title: Repeat the required checks
verification.body: Clear codes and perform the branch-specific self-tests or drive check. Passing tests with a continuing complaint require Diagnosis By Symptom.

verification.title: Confirm strategy agreement
verification.body: Compare the main-control strategy identification with the scan-tool value where applicable. A mismatch requires a strategy download and can cause harsh shifts.

verification.title: Preserve the measured result
verification.body: Retain the original and returning code lists and any recorded solenoid resistance. Distinguish a confirmed repair from a component operating correctly only at the time of testing.

guides.title: Diagnose 5.0L 6R80 automatic transmission faults
guides.summary: Separate wiring, sensor, solenoid and hydraulic concerns using the fault-code chart and the five targeted electrical tests.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 selects gears by directing fluid pressure to internal clutches. Its powertrain control module (PCM) commands solenoids and monitors temperature, selector position and shaft speeds. These tests establish whether an electrical fault explains the concern or whether diagnosis should move to hydraulic, mechanical or external-control systems.
guides.why: Several apparent component failures can share one electrical cause. The transmission solenoid power control relay supplies every solenoid and can deliberately remove power after certain faults. Connector damage, metallic contamination and incorrect test conditions must therefore be separated from an actual failed component.
searchTerms: transmission range fault engine will not crank

when.summary: When a verified transmission concern or returning fault code requires electrical diagnosis.
notes: A passing test establishes operation at that time; it does not explain a continuing complaint.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable scan tool with live parameter ID (PID) data, a recording or min/max multimeter, correct flex probes, a fused jumper and Wiring Diagrams Cell 30. Internal branches require the pan and leadframe procedures.

prepare.title: Establish valid conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Follow each connector and ignition instruction exactly, isolate circuits for resistance testing, and prepare for the specified road tests.

steps.title: Verify the complaint and establish the code sequence
steps.body: Inspect for mechanical damage, harness damage and poor connections; correct an obvious cause first. Perform key-on/engine-off and key-on/engine-running self-tests and record diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Repair non-transmission codes before transmission codes, prioritizing circuit faults over performance faults. Clear continuous-memory codes, attempt to reproduce them and follow the returning code’s chart entry. Pass codes with continuing symptoms lead to Diagnosis By Symptom.

steps.title: Test A: distinguish solenoid wiring from internal faults
steps.body: For chart-directed solenoid faults, establish the meter connections with ignition off and capture supply voltage using min/max before the PCM removes power from the disconnected harness. Follow the supply and control-circuit branches before internal inspection. If directed, remove the pan, inspect for metallic contamination, discard fitted foam when contaminated and clean contacts with clean transmission fluid. Then distinguish leadframe resistance from individual solenoid resistance using each component’s specification.

steps.title: Test B: check transmission fluid temperature sensing
steps.body: The temperature sensor changes resistance as fluid temperature changes. Test B checks the unplugged input, signal voltage and prescribed fused-jumper response before comparing sensor resistance with temperature. Repair circuit faults along the directed branch. Clean metallic contamination; a failed resistance comparison with no debris found directs leadframe replacement. A matching resistance sends an overheating complaint to symptom diagnosis.

steps.title: Test C: check transmission range sensing
steps.body: For range codes or an associated no-crank concern, compare selector-position duty cycle and frequency with the table, including harness movement checks. Correct, steady readings move diagnosis outside the range-sensor system. Failed readings lead through power, signal and ground checks, then manual-valve connection and leadframe inspection. Reconnect a detached sensor, clean debris and retest; replace the sensor only along the specified branch.

steps.title: Test D: check turbine shaft speed
steps.body: Resolve range-sensor codes first. Monitor turbine shaft speed through upshifts and downshifts in every gear; its response should track engine speed and vehicle speed. An abnormal response with companion output-speed codes leads through shared power and ground checks. Otherwise, investigate the turbine-speed signal for opens and shorts. Passing the final signal checks directs molded-leadframe replacement.

steps.title: Test E: check output shaft speed
steps.body: After range faults are resolved, monitor output shaft speed through the same all-gear road test. A responsive signal passes at that time. Companion turbine-speed codes redirect diagnosis to Test D; otherwise check the output-speed signal circuit for an open, short to ground and short to power. Repair a failed circuit; passing these checks directs molded-leadframe replacement.

steps.title: Complete the directed repair and configuration
steps.body: Use the linked removal and installation procedures for internal work. Test A’s leadframe replacement and both final solenoid-resistance outcomes require a new foam strip. Replacement solenoids must match the original nozzle and calibration band. PCM replacement requires the branch’s programming instructions and transmission strategy download.

watchFor.title: A misleading zero-voltage reading
watchFor.body: Measuring solenoid supply after the PCM has switched it off can falsely suggest an open circuit.

watchFor.title: Selector-cable assumptions
watchFor.body: The listed transmission range-sensor DTCs cannot be caused by an incorrectly adjusted selector cable.

notes: Self-test conditions matter: vehicle motion can produce speed-related self-test codes, while P1711 calls for repeated self-tests.
A solenoid-body strategy mismatch can cause harsh shifts; follow the strategy-download procedure when required.

diagnostics.finding: Supply, PCM voltage or electrical-control codes
diagnostics.meaning: Shared power, grounds or connectors may explain several codes.
diagnostics.next: Follow the individual chart entry; voltage-related branches can lead to charging-system diagnosis rather than transmission parts.

diagnostics.finding: Gear-ratio, clutch apply-time or charted non-electrical performance codes
diagnostics.meaning: These can indicate hydraulic or mechanical operation problems.
diagnostics.next: Use Diagnosis By Symptom. P177F specifically calls for checking creep in neutral; a returning code leads to internal-failure investigation.

diagnostics.finding: P1783 overheating code
diagnostics.meaning: A temperature-circuit fault may accompany the reported overtemperature condition.
diagnostics.next: Resolve accompanying temperature-sensor circuit codes first; otherwise follow Transmission Cooling diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Switch, door-status or reverse-lamp codes
diagnostics.meaning: The diagnostic route can leave the transmission.
diagnostics.next: Follow External Controls, Locks/Latches or Reversing Lamps as directed by the chart and observed operation.

diagnostics.finding: PCM self-test or programming codes
diagnostics.meaning: Replacement is conditional on the particular code’s retest or software branch.
diagnostics.next: Follow that sequence exactly; do not replace the PCM solely because a module-related code is stored.

verification.title: Confirm the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Repeat the applicable self-test or road-test branch and attempt to reproduce cleared continuous-memory codes. Continue symptom diagnosis if the complaint remains despite passing electrical tests.

verification.title: Preserve the measured result
verification.body: Retain the original and returning DTCs and the recorded suspect-solenoid resistance, identifying the branch that justified repair.

guides.title: Trace 6R80 engagement, shift and driveability symptoms
guides.summary: Use the precise engagement or shift complaint to select the appropriate 6R80 hydraulic, clutch, converter or external-control diagnosis.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 obtains its ratios by directing hydraulic pressure to clutches around planetary gearsets. The powertrain control module (PCM) controls the electrical components that govern gear selection and pressure. A missing gear can therefore involve a clutch that fails to apply, another that fails to release, or a shared hydraulic problem. This diagnosis narrows the inspection path before dismantling.
guides.why: The symptom chart orders components by disassembly sequence. Following that order helps establish a root cause without jumping from a driving sensation directly to an internal-parts replacement.

when.summary: Use for engagement, shifting, converter, selector, leakage, noise or overheating complaints after DTC review.
notes: The observed complaint must be present before a diagnostic branch justifies replacing a component.

prepare.title: Collect the operating evidence
prepare.detail: Use a suitable diagnostic scan tool and Ford diagnostic practices. Check battery and charging operation, battery state of charge greater than 70%, relevant codes, wiring and previous repairs.

prepare.title: Match capability to the selected branch
prepare.detail: Fluid checks and special tests require their complete procedures. Pump, valve-body and clutch inspections require transmission workshop capability and the applicable access or bench procedure.

steps.title: Read codes before choosing a symptom row
steps.body: Consult the diagnostic trouble code (DTC) chart first; the PCM commonly supplies a diagnostic direction. Resolve circuit codes before system or performance codes. Describe the exact complaint: engagement direction, affected shift, available gears and whether low-gear engine braking remains.

steps.title: Separate individual engagement failures
steps.body: No forward drive leads to forward-clutch diagnosis. No reverse with engine braking in manual first leads to the direct clutch; loss of both reverse and that engine braking leads to low/reverse-clutch diagnosis. Harsh forward and harsh reverse have separate forward- and direct-clutch routes.

steps.title: Investigate delayed or soft engagement
steps.body: Perform the Delayed Engagement Test and check fluid level by the specified procedure. A single affected direction leads to the corresponding forward- or direct-clutch delayed/soft/slipping branch. When both directions are affected, inspect the filter and its pump seal, main pressure regulator and pump.

steps.title: Follow the common-supply path for no drive
steps.body: With neither forward nor reverse, perform the No Forward AND No Reverse Test and check fluid level. Inspect the filter and pump connection, then the main pressure regulator for damage, scoring or sticking, and the pump assembly. Continue to the input-shaft and converter-turbine splines; replace damaged components as necessary.

steps.title: Identify what happens during the affected shift
steps.body: Use the exact shift row in the complete chart. It distinguishes a clutch that should apply, one that may slip while carrying torque, and one that should release. Record whether the shift is absent, harsh, soft or slipping. A transmission that becomes neutral after launch instead follows the low one-way clutch's failure-to-hold branch.

steps.title: Separate converter behavior from gear changes
steps.body: For torque converter clutch (TCC) failure to apply, or continuous application that stalls the engine, check related DTCs and inspect converter hydraulic circuits and the regulator valve. Cycling, shudder or chatter also requires a fluid-level check before the converter diagnostic path.

steps.title: Follow external and supporting-system routes
steps.body: High selector effort, or Reverse indicated while the lever is in Park with no start, directs cable and external-control diagnosis. For no Park, check cable adjustment, the manual lever, then the park pawl and actuator. Route leaks to leakage inspection and overheating to transmission cooling. Investigate noise and vibration through the vehicle noise diagnosis, including accessories, suspension, constant-velocity joints and, for vibration, cooler tubes.

watchFor.title: Restricted gears are not a parts verdict
watchFor.body: The control system can retain limited operation after a fault. A short list of available gears must be interpreted alongside codes and the applicable clutch tests.

watchFor.title: Harsh shifts after solenoid work
watchFor.body: A mismatched solenoid-body strategy can cause harsh shifts. Replacement solenoids also require the matching nozzle and band number.

notes: This workflow selects the next test or inspection. Fluid service, transmission removal and valve-body overhaul each have their own execution requirements.

diagnostics.finding: Abnormal 1–2, 2–3 or 3–4 shift
diagnostics.meaning: The applying-clutch routes are intermediate, direct and overdrive respectively. Each also includes forward-clutch slipping; the other possibilities are a seized low one-way clutch, intermediate failure to release, or direct failure to release respectively.
diagnostics.next: Follow all applicable branches in the matching shift row.

diagnostics.finding: Abnormal 4–5 or 5–6 shift
diagnostics.meaning: The applying-clutch routes are direct and intermediate respectively. Both include overdrive slipping; release faults concern forward and direct respectively.
diagnostics.next: Use the corresponding clutch tests to distinguish application, slipping and release faults.

diagnostics.finding: Only particular groups of gears remain
diagnostics.meaning: The chart separates always-applied and non-applying forward, direct, intermediate, low/reverse and overdrive clutches. The first-and-reverse-only branch also includes a seized low one-way clutch.
diagnostics.next: Match the entire available-gear pattern to the chart, rather than diagnosing from one missing ratio.

diagnostics.finding: No engine braking in low
diagnostics.meaning: The low/reverse clutch may not apply.
diagnostics.next: Follow low/reverse-clutch diagnosis; the symptom alone does not establish which part is damaged.

verification.title: Confirm the selected diagnostic route
verification.body: Record the DTC results, exact engagement or shift complaint, available gears and relevant engine-braking behavior. The selected row should account for the complete observation.

verification.title: Document the inspection conclusion
verification.body: Retain fluid-level and special-test findings where required, plus evidence of damage, sticking or wear from the directed inspections. Distinguish an identified fault from a component still awaiting testing.

guides.title: Diagnose 6R80 automatic-transmission concerns before teardown
guides.summary: Capture fault data and road-test behavior to choose electrical or component testing, then complete the required checks after repair.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 combines planetary gears, hydraulically applied clutches and electronic shift and pressure control. Similar driving complaints can therefore have different causes. This strategy builds an evidence trail before transmission removal and carries the diagnosis through repair, fluid setting and the final road test.
guides.why: Intermittent faults may offer only a brief recording opportunity. Fault codes can also place the transmission in default operation, changing how it behaves. Capturing conditions before clearing codes helps distinguish the original fault from the transmission's protective response.

when.summary: Use when investigating a 6R80 operating concern, especially an intermittent fault or default-mode behavior.
notes: The test path depends on symptoms and recorded conditions; there is no single repair for every transmission complaint.

prepare.title: Capture and interpret data
prepare.detail: Have a scan tool capable of the powertrain control module (PCM) Quick Test and recording transmission parameter identifications (PIDs), meaning live operating values. Obtain the applicable code, clutch-application and solenoid-application charts.

prepare.title: Plan the repair capability
prepare.detail: Arrange fluid sampling and road testing. Any resulting transmission removal, overhaul, adaptive reset, misfire-monitor reset or solenoid-strategy programming requires the corresponding procedures and workshop capability.

steps.title: Save the original diagnostic evidence
steps.body: Begin with the PCM Quick Test. Record every diagnostic trouble code (DTC) and associated freeze-frame data before clearing codes. Freeze-frame conditions provide a useful target for reproducing the event.

steps.title: Perform the preliminary inspection
steps.body: Look for obvious causes, adjust selector-lever linkage and collect a fluid sample. These checks may identify a repair without opening the transmission and preserve evidence of its internal condition.

steps.title: Prepare the recording before driving
steps.body: Select complaint-related PIDs together with general transmission operating data. Configure automatic triggering where possible, including data from before the fault changes state. A recording should capture how the event developed, not merely its aftermath.

steps.title: Reproduce the operating conditions
steps.body: Match freeze-frame conditions when available. Otherwise follow the prescribed warm-up and repeated accelerations from rest through sixth gear, first with shifts near 2000 rpm and then near 3000 rpm. Hold sixth for 30 seconds or until the torque converter clutch applies, using the repetitions specified in the complete procedure.

steps.title: Choose the correct diagnostic branch
steps.body: Review the recording and check for new codes. Some faults need repeated occurrences before setting a code. Electrical codes lead to pinpoint circuit checks; hydraulic, mechanical and performance codes lead to component tests. Without codes, compare the recording with clutch and solenoid application charts to identify systems for component testing.

steps.title: Repair the demonstrated cause
steps.body: Follow component tests from least intrusive to most intrusive. Clean and inspect removed parts, identify the root cause and repair related damage. Clutch failure with fluid heavily contaminated by friction material requires complete disassembly and cleaning: replace all seals and gaskets except the reusable pan gasket. Document findings on the repair order.

steps.title: Restore operation in the required order
steps.body: Complete the initial fluid fill. Clear adaptive tables after overhaul or solenoid-body replacement, and reset the misfire monitor whenever the transmission was removed. Road-test to operating temperature to fill the cooler, perform the adaptive drive cycle if tables were cleared, then set fluid level with the cooler purged of air. Finish with a road test confirming the repair.

watchFor.title: Incorrect solenoid calibration
watchFor.body: A replacement solenoid body requires its strategy file in the PCM and its replacement identification tag. An individual replacement solenoid must match the original injector nozzle and band number.

notes: Initial fluid filling may be completed before transmission installation; it does not replace the final temperature-dependent level setting.

diagnostics.finding: Default or fail-safe operation
diagnostics.meaning: A control fault can restrict operation without proving that a particular gear assembly has failed.
diagnostics.next: Use stored codes and recorded data to select the relevant circuit or component test.

diagnostics.finding: Harsh shifts with mismatched solenoid strategy
diagnostics.meaning: The programmed strategy does not match the installed main control.
diagnostics.next: Follow the required strategy download rather than treating adaptive clearing as an equivalent operation.

verification.title: Confirm completed restoration
verification.body: Verify that applicable resets, the adaptive drive cycle and final fluid-level setting are complete before assessing the post-repair drive.

verification.title: Record the resolved complaint
verification.body: Document the cause, related damage, repairs and post-repair road-test outcome alongside the original diagnostic evidence.

procedures.purpose: Complete 6R80 diagnostic strategy, road-test pattern and repair-completion sequence.
Explain 6R80 operation, default behavior and solenoid-strategy identification.

guides.title: Diagnose 6R80 direct-clutch apply problems
guides.summary: Classify the direct-clutch complaint and follow its control-strategy, solenoid, valve-body or internal-component repair path.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 direct clutch, also called clutch B, applies in third gear, fifth gear and reverse. Shift solenoid B (SSB) controls pressure acting on regulator and latch valves, which govern fluid reaching the clutch. This guide helps select the appropriate service phase when application is absent, continuous, delayed, slipping or harsh.
guides.why: Clutch behavior depends on both hydraulic pressure control and the clutch’s mechanical condition. Incorrect programming, a sticking valve, a restricted passage or damaged seals can produce related complaints. Identifying the condition first prevents a gear-selection symptom from becoming an unsupported diagnosis of worn friction plates.
searchTerms: slipping in third or fifth gear

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies abnormal application or release of the 6R80 direct clutch.

prepare.title: Provide programming and transmission-service capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool for strategy identification and the required download capability. Valve-body work and internal clutch inspection require the corresponding bench-service procedures and expertise.

prepare.title: Identify calibrated replacement parts
prepare.detail: A replacement solenoid must match the original injector nozzle and band number. Check identification before installation.

steps.title: Classify the clutch behavior
steps.body: Use the [direct-clutch diagnostic chart](#/document/G1686450) to distinguish no apply, always applied, delayed/soft/slipping apply and harsh apply. The clutch normally releases in first, second, fourth and sixth gears. Follow the sources listed for the established condition.

steps.title: Check strategy where the complaint calls for it
steps.body: For delayed, soft, slipping or harsh application, consider an incorrect strategy in the Powertrain Control Module (PCM). Compare the strategy etched on the main control with the scan-tool display. A mismatch requires the [Transmission Strategy Download](#/document/G1692055).

steps.title: Follow the solenoid branch
steps.body: The chart lists SSB stuck OFF for no apply and harsh apply, stuck ON for continuous application, and mechanically sticking for delayed/soft/slipping apply. When that source is established, install a matching new solenoid using [Shift Solenoids removal and installation](#/document/G1692059).

steps.title: Inspect the regulator and latch-valve control
steps.body: Use [valve-body removal and installation](#/document/G1692056) with the [overhaul procedure](#/document/G1692065). No apply can involve the clutch B regulator stuck OFF; continuous apply can involve it stuck ON. Delayed or harsh application also lists sticking regulator and latch valves. Disassemble, clean and inspect as directed; damaged valves or bores require a new main control valve body.

steps.title: Inspect fluid passages and the check ball
steps.body: Follow the labelled CLB, DRIVE, REV/DRIVE and VFS2 hydraulic circuits for blockage or leakage. The no-apply branch directs valve-body cleaning and inspection; the always-applied circuit branch directs check-ball inspection. Delayed and harsh branches also call for inspecting separator-plate passages for debris or blockage. Inspect ball valve 1’s check ball for absence or damage where directed.

steps.title: Escalate to internal inspection when indicated
steps.body: Use the [transmission overhaul procedure](#/document/G1692066) to inspect the center support, direct-clutch drum, drum Teflon seals, friction plates and piston seals. Clean or replace components according to wear and damage. For harsh application, also inspect the piston return spring for damage and correct installation.

watchFor.title: Damage that cleaning cannot correct
watchFor.body: A damaged regulator valve or bore calls for valve-body replacement; cleaning alone does not satisfy that branch.

watchFor.title: Fail-safe gear retention
watchFor.body: Loss of control or electrical power can leave third or fifth gear available hydraulically. Gear behavior alone does not prove direct-clutch hardware failure.

notes: Installing a new solenoid body requires its new strategy file and replacement identification tag.

diagnostics.finding: Direct clutch does not apply.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible sources include OFF-state control faults, blocked or leaking circuits, a missing or damaged check ball, and internal wear.
diagnostics.next: Follow the no-apply inspection and repair branches.

diagnostics.finding: Direct clutch remains applied.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible sources include SSB or the regulator stuck ON, hydraulic-circuit concerns and internal damage.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the always-applied branch.

diagnostics.finding: Application is delayed, soft or slipping.
diagnostics.meaning: Strategy, sticking controls, passage or check-ball concerns and internal wear are listed sources.
diagnostics.next: Include strategy verification before selecting mechanical service.

diagnostics.finding: Application is harsh.
diagnostics.meaning: Listed sources also include incorrect strategy, SSB stuck OFF and return-spring installation or damage.
diagnostics.next: Follow the harsh-apply branch, including its spring inspection.

verification.title: Confirm calibration and parts match
verification.body: Verify strategy identification matches the main control and any replacement solenoid matches the original nozzle and band number.

verification.title: Record the service decision
verification.body: Record the complaint category, identified fault and completed service phase, including valve/bore condition or return-spring findings where inspected.
