guides.title: Read 6R80 live data and select permitted output-control tests
guides.summary: Compare transmission commands with measured response and satisfy the enabling conditions before commanding diagnostic outputs.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 uses electronically controlled hydraulic pressure to operate its clutches. Scan-tool parameter identifications (PIDs) expose what the powertrain control module (PCM) requests, what sensors report and which faults the controller recognizes. Output state control (OSC) goes further by temporarily commanding selected outputs. This work gathers diagnostic evidence; it does not itself establish a failed component.
guides.why: A commanded pressure is not a measured hydraulic pressure, and a requested gear is not proof that the transmission achieved it. Keeping commands, measurements and fault status separate makes the data useful.

when.summary: Use when a transmission concern needs live-data comparison or a controlled solenoid, pressure, gear or converter test.
notes: Choose the output test for the complaint; each function has its own enabling conditions.

prepare.title: Provide the correct diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of the listed PIDs, self-tests and output controls. Line-pressure control testing also requires a gauge to observe actual pressure. Road-test functions require competent vehicle operation while collecting diagnostic data.

steps.title: Preserve history and complete self-tests
steps.body: Record continuous diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), then perform key-on engine-off (KOEO) and key-on engine-running (KOER) on-demand self-tests before OSC. Correct DTCs involving transmission range, turbine shaft speed or output shaft speed first; these faults prevent OSC operation. Time since starting and distance since code clearing help place observations in context.

steps.title: Build a useful data set
steps.body: Include accelerator pedal position (APP1), engine load, engine and vehicle speed, coolant and transmission-fluid temperature, and supply voltage. Check range, start-permission, Park/Neutral status and relevant SelectShift or transmission-control-switch inputs. Pair temperature and speed readings with their fault-status channels so unreliable inputs are not treated as valid evidence.

steps.title: Compare gear command with shift response
steps.body: Compare GEAR and theoretical GEAR_RAT with measured TRAN_RAT and turbine/output shaft speeds. Use SHFT_ID and SHFT_TYP to identify the event, then review flare and drop. SHFT_TIME covers command to 10% completion; SHFT_LAG covers 10% to 90%. These channels describe different parts of the shift.

steps.title: Read pressure and converter channels correctly
steps.body: Line-pressure and shift-solenoid A–E channels report commanded pressure, commanded current and fault status. For the torque converter clutch (TCC), compare actual slip TC_SLIPACT with desired slip TC_SLIPDSD alongside pressure, current and fault status. TCC_RAT is an actual speed ratio; 1.0 represents full engagement.

steps.title: Apply stationary output-test conditions
steps.body: Individual solenoid-current commands require Park or Neutral, with KOEO or the engine idling under KOER and APP1 = 0%. The line-pressure command requires Park or Neutral, KOER with engine idle greater than 1000 RPM, and APP1 = 0%. Observe actual pressure on the gauge while commanding pressure changes; a scan-tool command alone does not measure the result.

steps.title: Apply road-test output conditions
steps.body: GEAR_OSC# requires Drive and vehicle speed greater than 10 km/h. TCC_OSC# requires Drive, engine speed greater than 1200 RPM, commanded gear 3, 4, 5 or 6, vehicle speed greater than 3 km/h, brake pedal position input BPP = OFF, and transmission-fluid temperature between 15°C and 115°C. Check every condition before interpreting an unavailable command.

steps.title: Use the firm-shift function only in permitted ranges
steps.body: HRSH_SHFT# temporarily increases pressure during a shift to help identify some concerns. It permits Park, Reverse, Neutral or Drive and excludes M, 2 and 1. This list defines test eligibility; it does not establish which selector positions a particular vehicle has.

watchFor.title: Protective command rejection
watchFor.body: The controller blocks certain gear commands when the engine-speed and vehicle-speed combination could damage the engine. Rejection alone does not prove a transmission fault.

watchFor.title: Engine symptoms under converter load
watchFor.body: Minor cylinder misfires may become noticeable when the converter clutch applies. A complaint that changes with TCC control is not automatically a converter failure.

notes: Use the complete chart for exact scan-tool labels, including solenoid-current controls and fault-status channels.
If harsh shifts follow solenoid-body work, compare its strategy with the scan-tool value. A mismatch requires the correct strategy download.

diagnostics.finding: Commanded and actual gear or converter response differ
diagnostics.meaning: The data identifies a response needing investigation, without isolating a mechanical, hydraulic or electrical cause.
diagnostics.next: Retain the associated speeds, temperatures, commands and fault status for the applicable diagnostic test.

diagnostics.finding: Output control will not activate
diagnostics.meaning: Sensor DTCs or unmet enabling conditions may explain the refusal.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the prerequisite faults and verify the complete condition set before condemning an output.

verification.title: Record commands and responses separately
verification.body: Save the operating conditions, requested output and observed response together. For line-pressure testing, include the gauge result.

verification.title: State the diagnostic result precisely
verification.body: Distinguish an accepted test with an observed response from a blocked or incomplete test. The PID chart supplies definitions and enabling conditions, not universal pass/fail limits.

procedures.purpose: Complete 6R80 PID definitions and output-control enabling criteria.
6R80 hydraulic-control operation and solenoid-strategy context.

guides.title: Perform a preliminary inspection of the 6R80 automatic transmission
guides.summary: Check external faults, selector-cable alignment and fluid contamination to establish the next diagnostic step for a 6R80 concern.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 uses hydraulically operated clutches and planetary gears, with electronic solenoids controlling engagement and shifting. Its fluid both operates those clutches and carries evidence of internal wear. Preliminary inspection looks for visible external causes and meaningful fluid clues before deeper testing or dismantling.
guides.why: A damaged harness, restricted cooler line or incorrectly adjusted selector cable can affect operation without proving internal transmission damage. Fluid appearance also needs careful interpretation: normal aging and small amounts of wear debris should not be mistaken for overhaul evidence.

when.summary: Begin here when investigating a 6R80 operating concern, fluid leak or suspected fluid contamination.
notes: Use the linked Mustang cable-adjustment procedure; the separate 3.5L EcoBoost adjustment branch does not apply here.

prepare.title: Safe underside access
prepare.detail: Use a suitable hoist and identify lifting points by the stamped triangles. Protect nearby suspension, exhaust and steering components when positioning adapters. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; use floor stands where required.

prepare.title: Sampling and capability
prepare.detail: Have facial tissue or white paper for examining a fluid sample. Be prepared to assess harness routing, cooler installation and cable adjustment. Confirmed water/coolant contamination requires transmission-overhaul capability.

steps.title: Define the concern and inspect underhood
steps.body: Establish when the problem occurs and under what conditions. Look for missing or damaged air-induction components. Inspect harness routing, especially near the rear of the cylinder heads, for pinching or chafing. Check cooler mounting and missing air deflectors.

steps.title: Lift in NEUTRAL and inspect underneath
steps.body: Position the vehicle on the hoist with the transmission in NEUTRAL. Inspect the case for leaks and cooler lines for incorrect routing, pinches or kinks. Check cooler mounting and deflectors from below. DRIVE selection belongs to the later cable-adjustment phase.

steps.title: Align the selector positions if adjustment is needed
steps.body: Follow the cable-adjustment procedure: after hoist placement, put the shifter in DRIVE and disconnect the cable from the transmission manual lever. Rotate that lever clockwise to its stop, then counterclockwise 3 detents to establish DRIVE at the transmission.

steps.title: Release and secure the cable adjuster
steps.body: Gently pry the latch up, then push the lock tab down. With the tab released, connect the cable end to the manual control lever. Push the tab upward to lock the adjustment, then pull back on the adjuster to confirm it is secure.

steps.title: Collect a fluid sample
steps.body: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL on the hoist, remove the fill plug and level indicator, if equipped, as directed in the preliminary inspection. Let fluid drip onto tissue or white paper and examine the stain. This sample assesses contamination; it does not establish the exact fluid level.

steps.title: Recognize the water-contamination repair path
steps.body: Water or coolant contamination requires complete disassembly and cleaning. Replace all internal and external seals, friction material, the torque converter, parts with bonded seals, solenoids and transmission fluid filters. Before transmission installation, flush and clean the cooler or coolers and their tubes and hoses. This is a separate overhaul, not a fluid-change remedy.

watchFor.title: Cold fluid can look low
watchFor.body: Exact level requires the specified fluid-temperature range. Below operating temperature, a low indication is expected; sufficiently cold fluid may not register.

watchFor.title: Color and odor are insufficient
watchFor.body: Fluid can darken and develop an odor during normal use. Neither observation alone establishes fluid or transmission condition.

notes: The preliminary inspection establishes visible defects and the next diagnostic direction; it does not complete a temperature-controlled fluid-level check or an internal repair.

diagnostics.finding: Only trace black or shiny particles appear in the sample.
diagnostics.meaning: Small amounts can result from normal wear.
diagnostics.next: Continue diagnosis using the operating concern and other findings; a few particles alone do not establish failure.

diagnostics.finding: Large quantities of black particles appear.
diagnostics.meaning: These are typically burnt friction material.
diagnostics.next: Carry this evidence into further transmission diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Many small-to-medium shiny metallic particles appear.
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive wear of internal hard parts is possible.
diagnostics.next: Investigate internal wear through the appropriate transmission diagnostic path.

diagnostics.finding: The sample is foamy pink.
diagnostics.meaning: Water or engine coolant has entered the transmission.
diagnostics.next: Follow the complete contamination-overhaul path described above.

verification.title: After cable adjustment
verification.body: Verify starting is possible in PARK and NEUTRAL only, and that the reverse lamps illuminate in REVERSE.

verification.title: Record the inspection result
verification.body: Record leak locations, routing or cooler defects, cable-check results and sample appearance. Separate confirmed defects from clues requiring further diagnosis.

procedures.purpose: Complete 6R80 preliminary inspection, fluid interpretation and contamination-repair requirements.
Mustang selector-cable adjustment, adjuster locking and start/reverse-lamp verification.
Lifting points, support precautions and hoist positioning.

guides.title: Diagnose 6R80 delayed engagement, loss of drive and clutch-pressure leaks
guides.summary: Use clutch air checks and recorded transmission behavior to distinguish hydraulic leakage, pump trouble and converter-regulator problems.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 uses fluid pressure to apply internal clutches that select paths through its planetary gears. Its torque converter transfers engine power into the transmission. These three special tests examine different parts of that process: clutch application, initial engagement after parking, and a vehicle with neither forward nor reverse drive.
guides.why: Air testing makes clutch application audible, but some internal seals normally leak air because they depend on hydraulic flow to seal. Recorded vehicle and turbine speeds provide different evidence about pump and converter operation. Choosing the test for the actual complaint prevents a normal feature or unrelated symptom from becoming a replacement decision.

when.summary: When investigating a suspect clutch circuit, delayed initial engagement, or simultaneous loss of forward and reverse.
notes: The combined loss-of-drive test does not apply when only forward or only reverse is missing.

prepare.title: Arrange air-test access
prepare.detail: Use a rubber-tipped blow gun and an air supply capable of applying 40 PSI. Access and positively identify the intended transmission-case clutch port before applying air.

prepare.title: Prepare scan-tool recording
prepare.detail: Select VSS vehicle speed, TRS transmission range, BOO1 brake input, APP% accelerator position, Gear_Mode transmission gear, TFT fluid temperature, TSS_SRC turbine speed, RPM engine speed and Gear_Rat transmission gear ratio.

prepare.title: Plan the moving test
prepare.detail: Use a level parking location with an unobstructed forward path. Read the entire delayed-engagement sequence beforehand: starting, selecting Drive and releasing the brake must occur consecutively.

steps.title: Choose the test for the complaint
steps.body: Use an air check to investigate a particular clutch circuit, the delayed-engagement recording for initial movement after parking, or the combined no-forward/no-reverse test when both directions are unavailable.

steps.title: Identify the clutch air port
steps.body: Use the procedure's port identification for intermediate C, low/reverse D1, direct B, overdrive E or forward A. The unused location and thermal bypass valve are not clutch test ports. Do not infer physical port positions from clutch names.

steps.title: Apply air and observe pressure retention
steps.body: Apply 40 PSI for 2–3 seconds. Listen for the dull thud of piston application. Keep the nozzle firmly sealed against the port, release the trigger and wait 1–2 seconds before removing the gun. Note hissing and whether removal produces a sudden release of retained pressure.

steps.title: Prepare the delayed-engagement cycle
steps.body: Verify transmission fluid temperature at 77 °C (170 °F) or above, then park level for at least 6 hours or overnight. Before starting the timed test, select the recording channels with ignition on and engine off, and release the parking brake.

steps.title: Record movement at idle
steps.body: Start recording, press the brake, start the engine, immediately select Drive and immediately release the brake. Do not press the accelerator. Stop the vehicle after recording for 15 seconds. Measure from BOO1 brake release to VSS reaching 5 Km/h (3 MPH), or note the maximum speed attained.

steps.title: Record simultaneous loss of forward and reverse
steps.body: Run a scan-tool self-test and check diagnostic trouble codes. Select Drive or Reverse and record engine speed and turbine speed while raising engine speed as directed. Use their relationship, followed where required by engine-on and engine-off fluid-level observations, to select the next repair path.

watchFor.title: Normal air leakage
watchFor.body: The low/reverse circuit has an air bleed, and the direct clutch uses scarf-cut seals. Hissing alone does not establish a failed clutch.

watchFor.title: Accelerator input during engagement timing
watchFor.body: The delayed-engagement result depends on movement at idle only. Accelerator use changes the test conditions.

notes: These tests identify the next repair operation. Pump replacement and main-control work continue through the separate overhaul procedures.

diagnostics.finding: Dull thud followed by retained-air release
diagnostics.meaning: The piston applied and the passages demonstrate pressure retention.
diagnostics.next: Interpret any leakage alongside the circuit's normal bleed and seal characteristics; absent release may indicate leakage.

diagnostics.finding: Vehicle reaches 5 Km/h (3 MPH) within 5 seconds
diagnostics.meaning: Operation is normal for this delayed-engagement test.
diagnostics.next: The pump-replacement decision does not apply. Failure to meet the specified timing directs transmission pump replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Turbine speed stays at zero while engine speed rises
diagnostics.meaning: The torque converter is not functioning in the combined loss-of-drive test.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the main control for a stuck converter release regulator valve. The main control may be reused if the valve can be cleaned and freed.

diagnostics.finding: Turbine speed follows engine speed
diagnostics.meaning: The forward and direct clutches are not holding.
diagnostics.next: Compare fluid levels with the engine on and off. An unchanged, high level identifies the pump-replacement branch.

verification.title: Retain the engagement record
verification.body: Record brake-release time, speed reached, elapsed time and fluid-temperature data. Confirm that the timed run used no accelerator input.

verification.title: Preserve the loss-of-drive evidence
verification.body: Keep the engine/turbine-speed recording and, where required, both fluid-level observations with the selected overhaul decision.

procedures.purpose: Complete 6R80 clutch air, delayed-engagement and combined no-forward/no-reverse tests.
6R80 transmission overhaul path when testing directs pump replacement.
6R80 main-control valve-body overhaul path for a stuck converter release regulator valve.

guides.title: Diagnose 6R80 torque converter clutch non-application, stalling or shudder
guides.summary: Match the torque converter clutch complaint to strategy, solenoid, hydraulic-control or internal-wear checks before selecting a repair.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 torque converter transfers engine power into the transmission and contains an integral torque converter clutch (TCC). Applying this clutch reduces converter slip. Its solenoid moves hydraulic regulator valves that change fluid flow through the converter's apply and release passages. Trouble anywhere in that control chain can prevent engagement, prevent release or make engagement unstable.
guides.why: Several hydraulic faults appear under more than one complaint. Calibration also matters: the powertrain control module (PCM) uses a strategy matched to the solenoid body, and individual replacement solenoids must match their original calibration. The symptom selects an inspection path; findings justify the parts.

when.summary: Use when the TCC fails to apply, remains applied and stalls the vehicle, or cycles, shudders or chatters.
notes: This route covers the 6R80 applications with 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L engines.

prepare.title: Identify the transmission and calibration
prepare.detail: Locate the transmission identification and solenoid-body strategy information. Arrange a scan tool and capability for the prescribed Transmission Strategy Download.

prepare.title: Plan specialist access
prepare.detail: Valve cleaning and bore inspection require controlled transmission bench work. Shaft, pump-bushing and clutch repairs require the appropriate full transmission procedures before disassembly.

steps.title: Classify the actual clutch complaint
steps.body: Use the [TCC diagnostic chart](#/document/G1686460) to distinguish failure to apply, remaining applied with stalling, and cycling/shudder/chatter. These conditions share possible causes, but the indicated solenoid and regulator states differ.

steps.title: Check strategy for cycling or shudder
steps.body: Incorrect PCM transmission strategy is a listed cause of unstable TCC operation. Compare the scan-tool strategy with the identification etched on the main control. A mismatch requires the [Transmission Strategy Download](#/document/G1692055). Installing a replacement solenoid body also requires its new strategy and replacement identification tag.

steps.title: Evaluate the TCC solenoid
steps.body: A mechanically stuck-OFF solenoid is listed for non-application, a stuck-ON solenoid for remaining applied, and mechanical sticking for cycling or chatter. When replacement is indicated, follow [Shift Solenoids](#/document/G1692059). Match both injector nozzle and band number to the original. The cycling/shudder replacement branch also requires a strategy download.

steps.title: Inspect regulator valves and hydraulic passages
steps.body: The bypass clutch control regulator can be stuck OFF for non-application or ON for the other complaints. A converter release regulator stuck OFF appears in all three branches. Disassemble, clean and inspect the implicated valves and the CAPLY, CREL, CAPLY F and VFS6 circuits for blockage or leakage. Valve or bore damage directs replacement of the main control or valve body as specified.

steps.title: Follow the internal-wear branch where indicated
steps.body: For failure to apply, inspect input-shaft wear, cut or leaking shaft seals and worn pump bushings; replace affected parts as necessary. Worn or damaged TCC friction material is listed under every complaint and directs TCC replacement through the applicable transmission procedure.

watchFor.title: Calibration mismatch
watchFor.body: Solenoids are individually calibrated. A physically similar replacement does not establish that its nozzle and band number match.

watchFor.title: Contamination versus permanent damage
watchFor.body: Cleaning and inspection establish valve condition. Damaged valves or bores require the directed replacement.

notes: Use the Mustang rear-wheel-drive transmission procedure for internal repairs; the shared four-wheel-drive reference is not a Mustang work path.

diagnostics.finding: TCC does not apply
diagnostics.meaning: Apply pressure may be missing or escaping, or the clutch may be damaged.
diagnostics.next: Follow solenoid, regulator, passage, shaft/seal/bushing and friction-material checks.

diagnostics.finding: TCC remains applied and stalls the vehicle
diagnostics.meaning: The clutch release function may be compromised.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the listed solenoid, regulator, hydraulic-circuit and friction-material causes.

diagnostics.finding: TCC cycles, shudders or chatters
diagnostics.meaning: Strategy mismatch, sticking control components or clutch damage may produce unstable operation.
diagnostics.next: Check strategy and continue through the corresponding mechanical branches.

verification.title: Confirm calibration agreement
verification.body: After a required download, confirm that the PCM strategy agrees with the main-control identification and that replacement-solenoid calibration matches.

verification.title: Record the repair decision
verification.body: Record the complaint, inspection findings and the repair they justify. Complete the selected repair procedure before treating diagnosis as a finished repair.

procedures.purpose: 6R80 TCC diagnosis for non-application, remaining applied and cycling/shudder/chatter.
6R80 converter apply and release hydraulic operation.
6R80 identification, strategy matching and replacement-solenoid calibration requirements.
6R80 shift-solenoid removal and installation when TCC solenoid replacement is indicated.
6R80 transmission strategy download when required by diagnosis or replacement.

guides.title: Run the 6R80 adaptive learning drive cycle
guides.summary: Give the warmed 6R80 transmission the specified acceleration, steady-running, brake-input and stopped periods for adaptive learning.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 automatic transmission uses electronically controlled hydraulic pressure to operate its internal clutches. Those controls influence engagement, shift feel and torque-converter clutch operation. The adaptive learning drive cycle supplies a repeatable driving sequence; it is a controlled finishing procedure, not a diagnosis of every uncomfortable shift.
guides.why: Fluid level, operating temperature and road gradient affect the conditions under which the transmission works. Starting with the correct level on a level road makes the prescribed sequence meaningful. Recording diagnostic trouble codes before clearing them also preserves evidence that could otherwise be lost during preparation.

when.summary: When an applicable transmission repair or configuration procedure calls for the 6R80 adaptive learning drive cycle.
notes: The engine and transmission must be at normal operating temperature, with the transmission fluid at the correct level.

prepare.title: Diagnostic access
prepare.detail: Have equipment capable of reading, recording and clearing diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Preserve the initial code record before clearing anything.

prepare.title: Suitable road-test conditions
prepare.detail: Choose a level road where the required speed, steady running and stops can be performed safely. The driver must be able to maintain the prescribed conditions without compromising traffic safety.

prepare.title: Fluid-level confirmation
prepare.detail: Confirm the transmission fluid is at the correct level using the applicable fluid-level procedure. This drive cycle does not establish or correct the level.

steps.title: Record and clear the codes
steps.body: Record the DTCs, then clear them as directed by the [adaptive learning procedure](#/document/G1692050). Keep the record with the repair information so the original condition remains identifiable.

steps.title: Bring the powertrain to operating temperature
steps.body: Warm both the engine and transmission to normal operating temperature. Begin the learning sequence only when the temperature and fluid-level prerequisites are satisfied.

steps.title: Accelerate through the gears
steps.body: With the selector in D, accelerate moderately from a stop to 80 km/h (50 mph), allowing the transmission to reach 6th gear. Hold vehicle speed and throttle steady for a minimum of 15 seconds.

steps.title: Introduce the brake input
steps.body: While remaining in 6th gear with steady speed and throttle, lightly apply and release the brake to operate the stoplamps. Maintain the speed and throttle for a minimum of 5 seconds. Follow the specified light input without forcing the maneuver in unsuitable traffic.

steps.title: Stop and repeat the sequence
steps.body: Brake to a stop and remain stopped for a minimum of 20 seconds. Repeat the acceleration, brake-input and stopped sequence five times, as specified in the complete procedure.

watchFor.title: Conditions that prevent completion
watchFor.body: If traffic interrupts a hold or the transmission does not reach 6th gear, the prescribed sequence has not been completed as written.

notes: The specified scan-tool action is to record and clear DTCs; the drive-cycle instructions do not add a separate adaptive-memory reset.

diagnostics.finding: The solenoid-body strategy on the main control differs from the strategy displayed by the scan tool.
diagnostics.meaning: The transmission description identifies this mismatch as a cause of harsh shifts.
diagnostics.next: Have the matching strategy downloaded into the powertrain control module; repeating a drive cycle does not perform that configuration.

verification.title: Confirm the prescribed operation
verification.body: Confirm that 6th gear was reached and that the steady-running, brake-input and stopped periods were completed under the required conditions.

verification.title: Record completion
verification.body: Retain the initial DTC record and document the temperature and fluid-level prerequisites, completion of the five repeats, and any remaining shift complaint.

procedures.purpose: 6R80 adaptive learning drive cycle for the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications.
Explain 6R80 hydraulic and electronic control and the separate solenoid-body strategy matching requirement.

guides.title: Exchange 6R80 automatic transmission fluid with a fluid exchanger
guides.summary: Use a fluid exchanger at the cooler return tube, restore the cooler connections and complete the separate transmission fluid level check.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 automatic transmission uses electronically controlled fluid flow to apply internal clutches and select gears. Its fluid therefore participates directly in engagement and shift operation. This exchange method connects a service machine to the return tube after the transmission fluid cooler, allowing the exchange to help remove foreign material trapped in the cooler circuit.
guides.why: Connection location and fluid selection are both essential. The specified return-side connection includes the cooler in the exchange path. Fluid intended for this transmission must be used without supplemental additives or cleaning agents, because those products can cause internal component failure. A completed machine cycle still requires a separate fluid level check.

when.summary: When fluid exchange is required and the cooler connections are compatible with this machine-based procedure.
notes: This method excludes vehicles with solid steel cooler lines or plug-in-design fluid coolers.

prepare.title: Confirm transmission and cooler configuration
prepare.detail: Identify the fitted transmission and inspect its cooler connections before preparing the machine. The case identification tag provides the transmission part number, build date and serial number.

prepare.title: Arrange the machine, fluid and lifting capability
prepare.detail: Have a fluid exchanger, its manufacturer's operating instructions, the specified transmission fluid and a hoist. Obtain the applicable fluid specification through the exchange procedure and have the separate level-check instructions available.

steps.title: Establish that this method applies
steps.body: Confirm the vehicle has the relevant 6R80 installation and does not have either excluded cooler arrangement. Place the vehicle in NEUTRAL and position it on a hoist using the applicable jacking and lifting instructions.

steps.title: Connect on the cooler return side
steps.body: Following the [fluid exchange procedure](#/document/G1692051), connect the exchanger to the transmission fluid cooler return tube after the cooler. Identify that location before opening a connection; it is selected to help carry foreign material out of the cooler circuit.

steps.title: Perform the machine-controlled exchange
steps.body: Operate the fluid exchanger according to its manufacturer's instructions and the transmission specifications referenced by the procedure. Use only fluid specified for this transmission. Do not add a cleaning agent or supplemental transmission additive to the exchange.

steps.title: Disconnect the machine and restore the tubes
steps.body: Once the exchange is complete, disconnect the exchanger and reconnect every transmission fluid cooler tube disconnected for the operation. Complete this restoration before moving to the final fluid level check.

steps.title: Settle the final level through the specified check
steps.body: Carry out the [Transmission Fluid Level Check](#/document/G1692053). Follow that procedure's required conditions and decisions rather than treating the exchanger's completion indication as confirmation of the final transmission fluid level.

watchFor.title: Incompatible cooler connections
watchFor.body: Solid steel cooler lines and plug-in-design fluid coolers are explicit exclusions. Do not adapt this method to those arrangements by assumption.

watchFor.title: Additives or flushing chemicals
watchFor.body: Supplemental transmission fluid additives and cleaning agents are prohibited because they can damage internal transmission components.

notes: The transmission's electronic controls and hydraulic components both influence shift behavior. A shifting complaint alone does not establish that a fluid exchange is the necessary repair.
Use the applicable specifications and level-check procedure for fluid selection and final level decisions.

diagnostics.finding: The cooler has solid steel lines or a plug-in design.
diagnostics.meaning: The specified exchanger connection method does not apply.
diagnostics.next: Stop this procedure and establish an applicable service method before opening the cooler circuit.

verification.title: Confirm cooler-circuit restoration
verification.body: Confirm the exchanger is disconnected and all cooler tubes disturbed during the exchange are reconnected.

verification.title: Record the final fluid level result
verification.body: Record completion and the result of the separate fluid level check, including any correction it required.

procedures.purpose: 6R80 machine fluid exchange, including cooler-design exclusions, return-tube connection and fluid restrictions.
Mandatory transmission fluid level check after exchange and cooler-tube reconnection.
6R80 hydraulic operation and transmission case identification-tag context.

guides.title: Program the 6R80 transmission solenoid body strategy
guides.summary: Match the transmission’s programmed strategy to its installed solenoid body and complete the required adaptive learning drive cycle.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 uses electronically controlled solenoids to direct hydraulic pressure to its internal clutches. The powertrain control module (PCM) uses a solenoid body strategy to control shifting, line pressure and torque converter clutch operation. Because the solenoids are calibrated components, the stored strategy must match the installed solenoid body. This job establishes that match and then completes the specified learning drive.
guides.why: The label contains two different identifiers, and confusing them has consequences. Normal programming requires the complete 13-digit numeric strategy. Using the separate solenoid body identification for file selection can produce only a partial download. Incorrect information can cause driveability problems or transmission damage, while omitting the learning drive can leave erratic shifts.
searchTerms: harsh shifts after main control replacement

when.summary: After installing a new main control or solenoid body, or when its strategy does not match the scan-tool display.
notes: Harsh shifting alone does not prove that the solenoid body needs replacement.

prepare.title: Programming equipment and capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool that supports Transmission Characterization/Solenoid IDN and module strategy downloads. The technician must be able to follow its programming prompts and complete the subsequent road procedure.

prepare.title: Correct identification
prepare.detail: Locate the installed solenoid body tag using Transmission Description. For a new main control, use the replacement tag supplied with the service kit.

prepare.title: Strategy-file availability
prepare.detail: Internet access is required if the scan tool must retrieve the strategy file from the Professional Technician Society (PTS) server.

steps.title: Record the installed component’s codes
steps.body: For a new main control, record the 13-digit strategy and separate 12-character solenoid body identification from its replacement tag. Place that tag over the existing identification tag so future service uses the installed component’s information.

steps.title: Open the characterization function
steps.body: Under the scan tool’s toolbox icon, select Powertrain > Transmission > Transmission Characterization/Solenoid IDN. Follow the displayed instructions. The screen provides fields for both identifiers, but normal strategy-file selection requires the 13-digit strategy.

steps.title: Compare the label with stored information
steps.body: Compare the codes displayed by the tool with the transmission strategy label. If they differ, select the update option. Choose the single repair-operation option that describes the work performed, then proceed to code entry.

steps.title: Enter and validate the strategy
steps.body: Enter the complete 13-digit strategy. The tool checks validity and reports invalid information. Recheck any rejected entry against the correct tag. The identification-based option is reserved for engineering-directed cases where the complete strategy cannot be obtained.

steps.title: Retrieve and download the file
steps.body: If the file is already on the tool, proceed with its download to the module. If absent, the tool requests permission to retrieve it from PTS. Follow the network and scan-tool instructions through to the explicit successful-download message.

steps.title: Complete adaptive learning
steps.body: Road test the vehicle using the [Adaptive Learning Drive Cycle](#/document/G1692050). Use that exact procedure rather than substituting an ordinary drive; the strategy download alone does not complete the job.

watchFor.title: The wrong label field
watchFor.body: The 13-digit strategy contains numbers only. The separate identification field is not a routine substitute for it.

watchFor.title: Illustration values mistaken for vehicle data
watchFor.body: Read the actual installed component’s tag. The illustrated label explains the field locations, not the code to enter for another transmission.

notes: A replacement solenoid body tag must cover the original tag so the physical identification remains consistent with the replacement component.

diagnostics.finding: The installed solenoid body strategy differs from the scan-tool display.
diagnostics.meaning: The stored strategy does not match the installed component; this mismatch can cause harsh shifts.
diagnostics.next: Update the strategy using the correct label information.

diagnostics.finding: The tool rejects the entered strategy.
diagnostics.meaning: The entered information has not passed the tool’s validity check.
diagnostics.next: Verify the complete numeric strategy against the correct tag before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: The required file is absent from the scan tool.
diagnostics.meaning: The file must be retrieved before programming can proceed.
diagnostics.next: Use the prompted PTS retrieval process with internet access.

verification.title: Record the programming result
verification.body: Record the component identifiers, confirm agreement with the scan-tool information and retain the successful-download result.

verification.title: Confirm the learning phase
verification.body: Complete and record the prescribed adaptive learning drive cycle; do not mark the programming repair finished at the download message.

procedures.purpose: 6R80 strategy comparison, code entry, file retrieval and download.
6R80 operating context, solenoid body tag identification and the distinction between strategy and identification.
Required adaptive learning road procedure after strategy programming.

guides.title: Remove, overhaul and reinstall the 6R80 main control valve body
guides.summary: Rebuild the 6R80 hydraulic control assembly while preserving component positions, matching solenoid calibration and completing the required electronic follow-up.
guides.introduction: The main control valve body routes transmission fluid to the clutches that select each gear. Its electronic solenoids regulate pressure, engagement and shifting under powertrain control module commands. Overhaul combines precision bench work with careful installation: hydraulic parts, electrical connections and solenoid calibration must all agree for the transmission to operate correctly.
guides.why: Similar-looking solenoids can have different functions and calibration. Misplaced check balls, incorrectly seated drain-back valves or mismatched strategy data can cause poor shifting or transmission damage. Keeping a reliable component map is therefore part of the repair itself.

when.summary: Use after diagnosis calls for main-control overhaul, solenoid replacement or installation of a new main-control assembly.
notes: Poor shifting alone does not establish that the valve body needs overhaul.

prepare.title: Arrange access and bench capability
prepare.detail: Plan access to the transmission pan, a clean organized bench, a suitable torque tool and Kostal sleeve remover 307-717. Keep the component-location and bolt-sequence diagrams available.

prepare.title: Prepare parts and electronic support
prepare.detail: Obtain a new separator plate and foam strip seal. Have diagnostic capability for adaptive-strategy clearing and, when replacing the assembly, transmission strategy download.

steps.title: Remove the pan and disconnect the assembly
steps.body: Follow the pan/filter procedure. Rotate the transmission connector counterclockwise and withdraw it without pulling the harness. Release the sleeve retainer and remove the sleeve with 307-717. Inspect its seals and replace damaged ones.

steps.title: Catch the valve or plug during removal
steps.body: Remove the main-control bolts and assembly while retaining the case-mounted thermal bypass valve or blank plug. Inspect the valve and discard it if damaged. The procedure specifies a valve without a fluid warmer and a blank plug with one.

steps.title: Map and separate the assembly
steps.body: Mark each solenoid and its bore. Record positions of the 8 check balls, 6 dampers, 2 drain-back valves and springs, and 2 screens. Remove the long leadframe bolts, separate the leadframe and discard any foam strip. Remove the short bolts, separate the body halves, discard the separator plate and retain the mapped loose parts.

steps.title: Service the valve bores in order
steps.body: Record each retaining clip, cap, valve and spring before removal. Clean the exposed assembly and reinstall these parts in their original order. Remove the solenoids and repeat the prescribed bore work on the remaining section. Protect precision-machined surfaces and inspect solenoid screens for flow-restricting debris.

steps.title: Match and reinstall solenoids
steps.body: Replacement solenoids must match the original nozzle/O-ring colors, base part number and service-band suffix. Return every solenoid to its marked bore and tighten its specified fasteners to 53 lb.in (6 Nm). Do not identify replacements by appearance alone.

steps.title: Restore the hydraulic components and upper assembly
steps.body: Reinstall the mapped dampers, check balls, drain-back valves, springs and screens. Leave the identified rear hydraulic passage empty. Install a new foam strip on every leadframe, including one previously without a strip. Align the upper body with the leadframe guide pins, then fit the new separator plate and verify both drain-back valves remain correctly positioned with the plate flush.

steps.title: Join the lower body correctly
steps.body: Locate the lower body on the leadframe studs and align the manual valve with the transmission range sensor. Start the long bolts hand-tight, then install the short bolts. Follow the illustrated sequence: bolts 1 through 6 use 53 lb.in (6 Nm); bolts 7 through 25 use 62 lb.in (7 Nm).

steps.title: Prepare the case and reinstall
steps.body: Check the bias spring, rubber adapter and center-support feed-tube seal positions and orientation. Return any seals retained in the removed assembly to the case. Hold the appropriate valve or plug with petroleum jelly. Align the guide pins and manual valve with its pin, loosely start the specified bolts, then tighten in the illustrated sequence to 71 lb.in (8 Nm).

steps.title: Secure the electrical connection and pan
steps.body: With the sleeve tab unlocked and down, fully seat the sleeve in the leadframe, then lock the tab upward. Reconnect the external connector and rotate clockwise to lock. Complete the linked pan/filter installation procedure before proceeding to a drive cycle.

steps.title: Complete the applicable electronic work
steps.body: After individual solenoid replacement, clear adaptive strategy and perform the Adaptive Learning Drive Cycle. For a new main control, update the solenoid-body strategy file and identification through the strategy-download procedure, and place the new service tag over the existing tag on the transmission case.

watchFor.title: The empty passage resembles a ball seat
watchFor.body: Adding a check ball to the specified empty passage can damage the transmission; use the component-location diagram.

watchFor.title: Initial assembly-to-case gap
watchFor.body: The rubber feed tubes normally prevent the assembly resting flush initially. With alignment verified, the prescribed bolt sequence draws it into place.

watchFor.title: Drain-back valve seating
watchFor.body: Incorrect positioning in the separator plate can damage the transmission. Check seating before closing the body halves.

notes: High-pressure line-pressure control, shift B and shift D solenoids use black nozzles/orange O-rings. Low-pressure torque-converter clutch, shift A and shift C solenoids use brown nozzles/green O-rings.
Etched service bands map to part-number suffixes as follows: 1 to B, 2 to C, 3 to D, 4 to E and 5 to F.
Identify feed-tube seals using the installation diagram: 7G199 black, 7G087 green or orange, and 7G084 blue.

diagnostics.finding: Debris is present on a solenoid screen.
diagnostics.meaning: It may restrict hydraulic flow.
diagnostics.next: Include the restriction in the inspection findings and complete the prescribed cleaning and component assessment.

diagnostics.finding: The etched solenoid-body strategy differs from the scan-tool value.
diagnostics.meaning: The programmed calibration does not match the installed assembly and can cause harsh shifts.
diagnostics.next: Perform the specified transmission strategy download.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical assembly
verification.body: Check the mapped component positions, new plate and foam strip, drain-back valve seating, case seals and securely locked electrical connector.

verification.title: Record calibration and learning
verification.body: Record replacement solenoid bands and locations. For a new assembly, confirm strategy/identification and tag replacement; after solenoid replacement, record adaptive clearing and drive-cycle completion.

procedures.purpose: 6R80 main-control removal, case installation and conditional electronic follow-up.
6R80 bench disassembly, cleaning, solenoid matching and sequenced reassembly.
6R80 solenoid, valve, leadframe and hydraulic-component identification.
6R80 transmission pan, gasket and filter removal and installation.
Adaptive learning drive cycle required after solenoid replacement and adaptive clearing.
Transmission strategy download for a new main control or strategy mismatch.

guides.title: Replace the 6R80 transmission output shaft seal
guides.summary: Remove the driveshaft and output flange, install a new output shaft seal, and secure the flange with a new tightened and staked retaining nut.
guides.introduction: The output shaft seal retains transmission fluid where the rotating output assembly leaves the transmission. The output flange connects that assembly to the driveshaft. Reaching the seal therefore requires driveshaft and flange removal, followed by controlled installation of a new seal. This is an external sealing repair on the 6R80 automatic transmission, with a final fluid-level check before completion.
guides.why: The flange retaining nut is mechanically locked by staking. Its stakes must be removed before the nut is undone to avoid damaging the output shaft. The old nut and output shaft seal are discarded. Dedicated installers position the new seal, and the replacement nut must be both tightened and staked to prevent it from coming loose.

when.summary: When the output shaft seal has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: The work requires driveshaft removal and installation as separate access operations.

prepare.title: Have the access procedure available
prepare.detail: Be equipped to perform the applicable Driveshaft removal and installation procedure before opening the transmission output assembly.

prepare.title: Prepare the specified installers
prepare.detail: Use installer 205-199 (T83T-3132-A1), Installer, Spindle/Axle Shaft, together with 307-715, Installer, Output Seal (4X2). A punch is required for removing and making the nut stakes.

prepare.title: Obtain the required new parts
prepare.detail: Have a new output shaft seal and a new output shaft flange retaining nut. Also have suitable torque equipment and access to the 6R80 fluid-level procedure.

steps.title: Remove the driveshaft
steps.body: Follow the applicable Driveshaft procedure to expose the output flange. Use the [output shaft seal procedure](#/document/G1692057) for the subsequent transmission-side sequence.

steps.title: Remove the nut stakes before loosening
steps.body: Use a punch to remove the stakes from the output shaft flange retaining nut. Only after releasing this mechanical lock should the nut be removed; discard the old nut.

steps.title: Remove the flange and old output seal
steps.body: Remove the output shaft flange seal and the output shaft flange. Then remove and discard the output shaft seal. Keep the flange seal distinct from the output shaft seal being replaced.

steps.title: Install the new output shaft seal
steps.body: Position the new seal on the specified special-tool assembly. Use installers 205-199 and 307-715 to install it as directed, rather than improvising a seating depth or installation method.

steps.title: Restore the flange assembly
steps.body: Install the output shaft flange and its flange seal. Fit a new output shaft flange retaining nut and tighten it to 59 lb.ft (80 Nm).

steps.title: Stake the tightened nut
steps.body: After tightening, use the punch to stake the nut slots. This is the required locking operation that prevents the retaining nut from coming loose.

steps.title: Reinstall the driveshaft and check fluid
steps.body: Install the driveshaft using its applicable procedure, then perform the [transmission fluid-level check](#/document/G1692053). Complete that check rather than assuming the previous level remains correct.

watchFor.title: Turning a nut that is still staked
watchFor.body: The stakes must be removed first. Forcing the retained nut loose can damage the output shaft.

watchFor.title: Reusing a discarded part
watchFor.body: Both the output shaft seal and flange retaining nut require new replacements.

watchFor.title: Tightening without locking
watchFor.body: Torque and staking are separate required operations; completing one does not replace the other.

notes: The output shaft flange seal is removed and reinstalled in this sequence; it is not the same part as the output shaft seal explicitly marked for disposal.

verification.title: Confirm the flange is secured
verification.body: Confirm the new retaining nut has been tightened to specification and its slots staked, and that driveshaft installation is complete.

verification.title: Record the final fluid check
verification.body: Record the result of the prescribed transmission fluid-level check alongside completion of the nut tightening and staking operations.

procedures.purpose: 6R80 output shaft seal removal and installation, including flange removal, new seal and nut requirements, and nut staking.
Transmission fluid-level check after output shaft seal and driveshaft installation.

guides.title: Replace the 6R80 automatic transmission selector shaft seal
guides.summary: Renew the selector shaft seal while preserving the internal selector linkage and correctly reinstalling the parking-pawl actuator.
guides.introduction: The selector shaft passes through the transmission case and links the external selector lever to the internal detent lever and parking mechanism. Its seal keeps transmission fluid inside at that moving connection. Although the seal is at the case wall, replacement requires removal of the main control valve body and temporary dismantling of the selector and park linkage.
guides.why: The spacer, roll pin and park rod establish the linkage's assembled position. Losing the spacer or misplacing the rod would leave more than a fluid leak to correct. The seal installer positions the replacement seal, while careful handling of the selector cable prevents damage during access.
searchTerms: transmission fluid leaking at selector shaft

when.summary: When the selector shaft seal has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Plan for main control valve body removal and installation as part of this repair.

prepare.title: Provide safe underside access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist with the vehicle in NEUTRAL. Locate the triangle-marked lifting points and position adapters clear of nearby components. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare the transmission work
prepare.detail: Have shifter fluid seal installer 307-559, a new selector shaft seal and a new roll pin. Provide the capability and equipment required for the complete main control valve body removal and installation procedure.

steps.title: Disconnect the cable and remove the valve body
steps.body: Follow the [selector shaft seal procedure](#/document/G1692058). Disconnect the selector cable end from the transmission lever without applying force to the cable section between the lever and its bracket. Remove the [main control valve body](#/document/G1692056) using its complete procedure to expose the internal linkage.

steps.title: Withdraw the shaft and linkage
steps.body: Remove the park rod actuating plate and its bolts, then remove and discard the roll pin. Hold the selector lever spacer so it cannot fall while sliding the shaft out of the case. Remove the manual valve detent lever and park pawl actuator rod together, then remove and discard the old seal.

steps.title: Install the replacement seal
steps.body: Place the new selector shaft seal on installer 307-559 and use that tool to install it in the case. Complete this operation before returning the shaft and linkage to their working positions.

steps.title: Reassemble the selector and park linkage
steps.body: Push on the park pawl to position the actuator rod, then install the rod and manual valve detent lever as an assembly. Position the spacer, slide the selector shaft into the case and align the roll-pin hole. Install a new roll pin to secure the assembly.

steps.title: Restore the plate, valve body and cable
steps.body: Hold the park rod down while installing the actuating plate and bolts; tighten the bolts to 12 Nm. Reinstall the main control valve body and complete its associated installation requirements. Reattach the selector cable end while observing the same cable-force restriction used during removal.

watchFor.title: A falling spacer
watchFor.body: Support the selector lever spacer as the shaft comes out and deliberately restore it before reinserting the shaft.

watchFor.title: Park rod positioning
watchFor.body: Pawl positioning is required when installing the rod, and the rod must be held down while the actuating plate is fitted.

watchFor.title: Cable damage during handling
watchFor.body: Do not pull or lever against the unsupported cable section between the selector lever and cable bracket.

notes: The removed seal and roll pin are discarded parts.

If associated valve-body work includes fitting a new solenoid body, its strategy must be downloaded into the powertrain control module. That is a conditional requirement for solenoid-body replacement.

diagnostics.finding: The main control solenoid-body strategy differs from the value displayed by the scan tool during associated work.
diagnostics.meaning: The control calibration does not match the installed solenoid body, which can cause harsh shifts.
diagnostics.next: Download the matching strategy into the powertrain control module before completing that associated repair.

verification.title: Confirm internal assembly before closing access
verification.body: Check that the spacer is present, the new roll pin is installed, and the park rod and actuating plate have been assembled in the prescribed positions.

verification.title: Record completion of the dependent work
verification.body: Confirm the actuating-plate tightening, completion of the valve-body installation procedure and reconnection of the selector cable end.

procedures.purpose: 6R80 selector shaft seal removal, tool-assisted installation and selector/park linkage restoration.
Required 6R80 main control valve body removal and installation for seal access.
Vehicle lifting points, hoist positioning and support precautions.

guides.title: Replace individual solenoids in the 6R80 automatic transmission
guides.summary: Replace the required solenoid while preserving its factory calibration match, valve-body location and leadframe alignment.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 selects gears by directing transmission fluid to internal clutches. Electrical solenoids in its main control valve body regulate that flow, influencing engagement, shifting and torque converter clutch operation. This job replaces individual solenoids after the valve body has been removed. It requires careful identification because physically similar variable force solenoids can have different factory calibrations.
guides.why: The replacement solenoid must match both the original nozzle color and calibration band number. A mismatch can cause harsh or erratic shifts, abnormal engagement or transmission damage. Correct leadframe alignment also matters: its transmission range sensor pin must engage the manual control valve correctly.
searchTerms: solenoid nozzle color and band number

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that an individual 6R80 solenoid requires replacement.
notes: Shift quality complaints alone do not establish which solenoid, if any, needs replacement.

prepare.title: Plan the valve-body work
prepare.detail: This requires automatic-transmission valve-body handling capability. Follow the linked main control valve body procedure for vehicle access, removal and final installation.

prepare.title: Gather matching parts and assembly supplies
prepare.detail: Have a way to identify solenoids and ports, a suitable torque wrench, a new leadframe foam strip seal and Motorcraft MERCON LV fluid, XT-10-QLVC, meeting WSS-M2C938-A.

steps.title: Remove the valve body and separate the leadframe
steps.body: Remove the main control valve body using its complete procedure. Remove the long leadframe bolts and carefully separate the molded leadframe. If a foam strip seal is present, remove and discard it.

steps.title: Expose and identify the solenoids
steps.body: Remove the solenoid bracket bolts and bracket. Before removing multiple solenoids, number each solenoid and its corresponding valve-body port so their locations remain unambiguous.

steps.title: Select the correct replacement
steps.body: Identify whether the unit is normally high, normally low or ON/OFF. For every variable force solenoid, record its nozzle color and band number and obtain a replacement matching both. Pull the required solenoid from its port.

steps.title: Lubricate and install the solenoids
steps.body: Lubricate the solenoid O-rings with the specified transmission fluid, then position each solenoid in its identified port. Refit the bracket and tighten its bolts to 53 lb.in (6 Nm).

steps.title: Reassemble the leadframe
steps.body: Install a new foam strip seal even if none was originally fitted. Position the leadframe while aligning the transmission range sensor pin with the manual control valve. Tighten the long bolts in the illustrated sequence to 53 lb.in (6 Nm).

steps.title: Return the assembly to the transmission
steps.body: Install the main control valve body using the linked procedure and complete its installation requirements. Keep the solenoid identification record with the repair details.

watchFor.title: Color alone is insufficient
watchFor.body: The calibration band must also match. Similar appearance does not establish interchangeability.

watchFor.title: Leadframe positioning
watchFor.body: Confirm sensor-pin alignment before tightening; bolt installation does not establish that the pin is correctly engaged.

notes: Brown-nozzle, normally low units serve the forward clutch (shift solenoid A), intermediate clutch (shift solenoid C) and torque converter clutch. Black-nozzle, normally high units serve the direct clutch (shift solenoid B), line-pressure control and low/reverse/overdrive clutch (shift solenoid D). Shift solenoid E is normally off and operates ON/OFF.
Replacing a complete solenoid body requires its strategy to match the powertrain control module. That separate requirement should not be confused with matching an individual replacement solenoid.

diagnostics.finding: Replacement nozzle color or band number differs from the original.
diagnostics.meaning: The replacement does not meet the required calibration match.
diagnostics.next: Obtain the matching solenoid before assembly.

verification.title: Assembly check
verification.body: Confirm the new foam seal, sensor-pin alignment, bracket tightening and sequenced leadframe tightening before completing valve-body installation.

verification.title: Recorded identification
verification.body: Record the original and replacement nozzle colors, band numbers and installed ports.

procedures.purpose: Individual 6R80 solenoid removal, identification and installation for the listed engines.
Required main control valve body removal and installation surrounding solenoid work.
6R80 hydraulic operation, calibration bands and complete solenoid-body strategy requirements.

guides.title: Replace the 6R80 Automatic Transmission Support Insulator
guides.summary: Support the 6R80 transmission at the specified fluid-pan rib while replacing its support insulator and restoring the mounting fasteners.
guides.introduction: The transmission support insulator forms part of the mounting that supports the transmission and reduces vibration transfer into the vehicle. This procedure applies to the 6R80 six-speed automatic transmission with the listed 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L engines. The work takes place beneath the vehicle and uses temporary transmission support while the insulator is removed. The transmission’s weight must remain controlled throughout the change.
guides.why: The temporary support has a specific contact location: the wooden block and stand must bear on the outer rib of the transmission fluid pan. Choosing a different area changes where the supporting force enters the assembly and risks damage. Vehicle lifting is equally important because the technician works underneath while releasing part of the transmission mounting.

when.summary: When the 6R80 transmission support insulator has been identified for removal or replacement.
notes: Confirm the fitted transmission before using this procedure.
The replacement sequence requires a hoist and separate temporary support for the transmission.

prepare.title: Arrange safe under-vehicle access
prepare.detail: Use the jacking and lifting procedure to position the vehicle on a hoist. Identify the correct lifting points and check that adapters clear the suspension, exhaust, steering components and axle cover.

prepare.title: Prepare the transmission support
prepare.detail: Provide a vehicle/axle stand and wooden block suitable for the prescribed support operation. Be able to position their contact at the outer rib of the transmission fluid pan.

prepare.title: Prepare for controlled fastening
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools and a torque wrench for the insulator nuts and bolts. These fastener groups have different tightening specifications.

steps.title: Position and raise the vehicle
steps.body: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on the hoist using the linked lifting procedure. Locate the designated lifting points and check for interference before raising it.

steps.title: Remove the insulator nuts
steps.body: Remove the transmission support insulator nuts as the first mounting-disconnection step. Keep their installation requirement distinct from that of the insulator bolts.

steps.title: Support the transmission at the specified rib
steps.body: Use the stand and wooden block to support the transmission. Make sure their contact is on the outer rib of the transmission fluid pan before proceeding to remove the insulator bolts.

steps.title: Remove the insulator
steps.body: With the transmission supported, remove the bolts and the transmission support insulator. The supplied illustration identifies the insulator and its bolt attachment beneath the transmission.

steps.title: Install in reverse order
steps.body: Refit the insulator and tighten its bolts to 103 Nm. Reverse the temporary-support operation once the insulator is installed, then restore the insulator nuts and tighten them to 80 Nm. Follow the complete procedure while transferring support back to the mounting.

watchFor.title: Support away from the outer pan rib
watchFor.body: The specified rib contact is a required support condition. Check the stand and block position before releasing the insulator bolts.

watchFor.title: Unsafe vehicle support
watchFor.body: Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. The emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this repair, and bumpers are not lifting points.

notes: The vehicle certification label has a transmission-code location marked TR; the transmission case also carries an identification tag.
On a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance first. On a two-column hoist, position the forks clear of suspension components and mounting brackets.

verification.title: Confirm the restored mounting
verification.body: Confirm the insulator is installed, both fastener groups are secured and the temporary transmission support has been removed after restoring the mounting.

verification.title: Record the separate torque results
verification.body: Record completion of the insulator bolt tightening at 103 Nm and the insulator nut tightening at 80 Nm.

procedures.purpose: 6R80 automatic transmission support insulator removal and installation for the listed 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications, including temporary support and fastener torques.
Required vehicle lifting-point identification, hoist positioning and under-vehicle support precautions.

guides.title: Diagnose 6R80 transmission cooling, leaks and cooler-tube vibration
guides.summary: Inspect cooler flow paths, leaks, tube contact and fluid condition to determine whether the concern needs cooling-system repair or transmission diagnosis.
guides.introduction: The automatic transmission sends fluid through tubes to an external oil-to-air cooler ahead of the radiator, then receives the cooled fluid back. Air passing over the cooler carries away heat. This diagnosis checks that cooling path and distinguishes its faults from incorrect fluid level or contamination inside the transmission.
guides.why: Restricted tubes or a plugged cooler interfere with cooling, while leaks reduce the available fluid. Overfilling also causes trouble: rotating parts can churn the fluid into foam, creating erratic control pressure, vent losses and possible damage. Cooler-tube contact can transmit vibration without being a fluid-flow fault.
searchTerms: vibration through seat changes with engine speed

when.summary: When the transmission overheats, cooling components leak, or engine-speed-related vibration suggests cooler-tube contact.
notes: Cooler backflushing is also required when the transmission is overhauled or replaced.

prepare.title: Arrange inspection and diagnostic access
prepare.detail: Provide access to the cooler and its tubes, and equipment to retrieve transmission diagnostic trouble codes. Use the engine-specific diagnostic reference if the cause is not visually apparent.

prepare.title: Prepare for fluid assessment
prepare.detail: Have a facial tissue for the fluid-stain check and follow the linked fluid-level procedure. If solids are found, further work requires transmission-pan removal and inspection capability; cleaning requires the separate backflushing procedure.

steps.title: Confirm the complaint and inspect the cooling path
steps.body: Begin with the operating verification in [Transmission Cooling](#/document/G1694304), then inspect for obvious concerns. For overheating, examine the cooler and tubes for plugging, damage, bends or crushing. Correct identified faults and install new cooling components wherever a transmission-fluid leak is found.

steps.title: Check tube contact when vibration is the complaint
steps.body: If a high-frequency vibration is felt through the seat or gear shifter and changes with engine speed, inspect the cooler tubes for grounding against surrounding structure. Here, grounding means physical contact that carries vibration. Repair the tube concern rather than treating this symptom alone as evidence of internal transmission failure.

steps.title: Establish the correct fluid level
steps.body: Use the [Transmission Fluid Level Check](#/document/G1692053). Both high and low levels can cause malfunction. Low fluid may produce poor engagement or slipping and can indicate a seal or gasket leak; an excessive level may explain foaming or loss from the vent.

steps.title: Investigate an unexplained concern
steps.body: If inspection does not reveal the cause, retrieve diagnostic trouble codes and follow the matching transmission chart: [2.3L](#/document/G1686449), [3.7L](#/document/G1686462) or [5.0L](#/document/G1686463). Keep the engine-specific diagnostic paths separate rather than transferring test details between them.

steps.title: Assess contamination and plan the required cleaning
steps.body: After checking level, place a drop of fluid on facial tissue and examine the stain. Solid material requires pan removal for further inspection. If pan sediment confirms contamination or transmission failure, repair the transmission and clean the cooler and tubes. For any overhaul or replacement transmission, [backflush the cooler](#/document/G1694306).

watchFor.title: Debris beyond the cooler
watchFor.body: Solid material is a reason to inspect the transmission pan; replacing a cooling component alone does not address confirmed internal contamination.

watchFor.title: Fluid escaping from the vent
watchFor.body: Overfilling can cause aeration and vent loss, so establish the level before deciding where the fluid loss originates.

notes: Use the separate level-check and backflushing procedures for their equipment, operating conditions and execution details.

diagnostics.finding: Overheating without visible cooler damage
diagnostics.meaning: Incorrect level, plugging or another transmission concern remains possible.
diagnostics.next: Check level and follow the appropriate engine-specific diagnostic chart.

diagnostics.finding: Solids in the tissue stain
diagnostics.meaning: Further inspection is needed; the stain alone does not establish the internal failure.
diagnostics.next: Inspect pan sediment before deciding on transmission repair.

verification.title: Recheck the original condition
verification.body: Repeat the operating verification after the identified repair, inspect cooling components for leakage and confirm fluid level using the specified procedure.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record the original symptom, level and contamination findings, identified leak or tube damage, and whether required cooler cleaning or backflushing was completed.

2.3L automatic-transmission DTC chart and pinpoint tests.

5.0L automatic-transmission DTC chart and pinpoint tests.
Required 6R80 fluid-level checking procedure.
Cooler backflushing and cleaning after contamination, overhaul or transmission replacement as directed.

guides.title: Replace the automatic transmission fluid cooler on 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L models
guides.summary: Disconnect the cooler tubes, follow the engine-specific access route, replace the cooler and complete the transmission fluid level check.
guides.introduction: The external transmission fluid cooler sits in front of the radiator. Fluid travels from the automatic transmission through the cooler and back through its tubes, transferring heat to passing air. Replacement opens that fluid circuit and requires access through the front cooling assembly. The three engines share the cooler's purpose, but their access procedures differ.
guides.why: The tube fittings have secondary latches and require a dedicated disconnect tool. Access also needs careful planning: the 2.3L procedure removes the air-conditioning condenser, while the 3.7L and 5.0L procedures reposition it. Finishing the mechanical work is only part of the job because the transmission fluid level must then be checked and adjusted.

when.summary: When the external automatic transmission fluid cooler has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Select the procedure by its engine-specific title before starting access work.

prepare.title: Obtain the disconnect and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Use special service tool 307-695, Tool, Quick Disconnect, for the cooler tube fittings. Have torque equipment suitable for the cooler and any radiator-bracket fasteners.

prepare.title: Arrange the correct access capability
prepare.detail: For the 2.3L, arrange the refrigerant-service capability required by the linked condenser-removal procedure. For the 3.7L or 5.0L, have the matching air-cleaner outlet-pipe procedure available.

prepare.title: Plan the fluid-level check
prepare.detail: Use the complete 6R80 fluid-level procedure for its checking conditions and adjustment method. Do not estimate the final level from the amount lost.

steps.title: Select the engine-specific path
steps.body: Use the [2.3L procedure](#/document/G1694308), [3.7L procedure](#/document/G1694310) or [5.0L procedure](#/document/G1694311). Keep the selected access sequence through removal and reinstallation.

steps.title: Disconnect the cooler tubes
steps.body: Remove the tube-fitting secondary latches first. Then use tool 307-695 to disconnect the fittings. Removing the secondary latches does not replace the tool-assisted release step.

steps.title: On the 2.3L, remove the condenser
steps.body: Follow the complete [2.3L condenser procedure](#/document/G1676761), including its refrigerant-system requirements. This branch calls for condenser removal; the other engines' repositioning method is not a substitute.

steps.title: On the 3.7L or 5.0L, create access around the radiator
steps.body: Remove the matching air-cleaner outlet pipe, then the pushpins and radiator sight shield. Remove the radiator-bracket bolts and brackets. Move the radiator toward the engine, release the upper tabs and position the condenser aside.

steps.title: Remove the cooler
steps.body: With the selected access work complete, remove the cooler bolts and the cooler. Keep the cooler fasteners distinct from the radiator-bracket fasteners used on the 3.7L and 5.0L.

steps.title: Reverse the selected removal sequence
steps.body: Install the cooler and tighten its bolts to 53 lb.in (6 Nm). On the 3.7L and 5.0L, tighten the radiator-bracket bolts to 97 lb.in (11 Nm). Restore the engine-specific access components, tube fittings and secondary latches.

steps.title: Set the transmission fluid level
steps.body: Follow the [6R80 transmission fluid level check](#/document/G1692053) and adjust as necessary. This is a required completion step after cooler replacement.

watchFor.title: Mixing condenser access methods
watchFor.body: Condenser removal belongs to the 2.3L branch; repositioning belongs to the 3.7L and 5.0L branches.

watchFor.title: Omitted secondary latches
watchFor.body: Reverse-order installation includes restoring the secondary latches after reconnecting the cooler tube fittings.

notes: The 3.7L and 5.0L procedures show the front bumper removed for clarity; that note is not a separate bumper-removal instruction.
Use the engine-matched outlet-pipe procedure even though the remaining access sequences are similar.

verification.title: Confirm the assembly is restored
verification.body: Confirm cooler fastening, tube connections and secondary latches, together with the condenser, radiator supports and intake components disturbed by the selected branch.

verification.title: Record the final fluid-level result
verification.body: Record completion of the specified transmission fluid level check and whether adjustment was necessary.
