guides.title: Replace transmission cooler tubes on 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L models
guides.summary: Replace the automatic-transmission cooler tubes using the correct quick-disconnect tool, engine-specific access sequence and final fluid-level procedure.
guides.introduction: The automatic transmission sends fluid through an external cooler ahead of the radiator and receives it back through the cooler tubes. Air passing over the cooler carries away heat from the fluid. This job replaces the connecting tubes and restores their supported, sealed connections. The three engine versions share the same general sequence, but the 3.7L requires additional access work at the left-hand catalyst monitor sensor.
guides.why: The quick-connect fittings have secondary latches that must be removed before disconnection and restored afterward. The transmission connection uses band seals and backing rings, which require lubrication during assembly. Brackets secure the tube routing, while the final fluid-level check addresses any fluid lost during the work.

when.summary: When a transmission cooler tube or its connection has been identified as requiring repair or replacement.
notes: Choose the procedure by engine; the catalyst monitor sensor removal applies to the 3.7L branch.

prepare.title: Provide safe underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist with the vehicle in NEUTRAL. Follow the lifting procedure, locating the triangle-marked lifting points and checking hoist clearance. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Have the fitting tool and specified fluid
prepare.detail: Use quick-disconnect tool 307-695. Seal and backing-ring lubrication requires Motorcraft MERCON LV Automatic Transmission Fluid, XT-10-QLVC, specification WSS-M2C938-A.

prepare.title: Prepare for engine-specific work
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastening and torque equipment. For the 3.7L, also have the catalyst monitor sensor procedure available; all versions require the 6R80 fluid-level procedure.

steps.title: Lift using the correct procedure
steps.body: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on the hoist using [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631). Check that the adapters and lifting equipment will not contact vulnerable underbody components.

steps.title: Disconnect the cooler fittings
steps.body: Remove the fittings' secondary latches, then use tool 307-695 to disconnect the cooler tube fittings. Follow the matching [2.3L](#/document/G1694309), [3.7L](#/document/G1694316) or [5.0L](#/document/G1694318) procedure.

steps.title: Release the supports and additional access
steps.body: Remove the bracket-to-engine mount nut and bracket-to-transmission nut. On the 3.7L, next remove the left-hand catalyst monitor sensor using its [removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1692247).

steps.title: Remove the tubes and prepare the seals
steps.body: Remove the retaining bolt and cooler tubes. If necessary, remove the backing rings and band seals from the transmission. Lubricate the band seals and backing rings with the specified transmission fluid for assembly.

steps.title: Attach the tubes at the transmission
steps.body: Position the tubes, attach them to the transmission and install the bolt to the specified torque. On the 3.7L, reinstall the left-hand catalyst monitor sensor at this stage.

steps.title: Restore the brackets and fitting locks
steps.body: Install and tighten the bracket-to-transmission nut, followed by the bracket-to-engine mount nut, using the matching procedure's torque specifications. Connect the cooler tube fittings and reinstall their secondary latches.

steps.title: Complete the fluid-level check
steps.body: Check and adjust the transmission fluid level using the [6R80 fluid-level procedure](#/document/G1692053). Tube installation alone does not establish the correct operating fluid level.

watchFor.title: Missing secondary latches
watchFor.body: Fitting reconnection is incomplete until the secondary latches have also been installed.

watchFor.title: Incorrect seal assumptions
watchFor.body: The procedure calls for conditional removal and lubrication of the band seals and backing rings; it does not direct blanket disposal of those parts.

verification.title: Check assembly completion
verification.body: Confirm the transmission attachment, both bracket attachments and fitting secondary latches are restored. On the 3.7L, include catalyst monitor sensor reinstatement.

verification.title: Record the fluid-level result
verification.body: Record completion of the prescribed fluid-level check and whether adjustment was required.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost transmission cooler tube removal and installation.
3.7L Duratec transmission cooler tube removal and installation, including left-hand catalyst monitor sensor access.
5.0L transmission cooler tube removal and installation.
Correct lifting points, hoist positioning and underbody support precautions.
3.7L catalyst monitor sensor removal and installation required during cooler tube access.
Final 6R80 transmission fluid-level check and adjustment.

guides.title: Inspect 6R80 shift-interlock operation and SelectShift paddle inputs
guides.summary: Check selector mechanics, brake-interlock inputs and isolated paddle circuits while preserving the limits of each diagnostic branch.
guides.introduction: The selector cable connects the cabin lever to the transmission's manual control lever. The brake shift interlock actuator mechanically blocks movement from Park until the body control module (BCM) energizes it after a brake-pedal input. Steering-wheel paddles are separate momentary switches that request manual shifts in Sport. These checks distinguish mechanical resistance, interlock faults and missing electrical requests.
guides.why: A stiff selector and an unresponsive paddle involve different mechanisms. Verifying cable retention, brake operation and switch responses prevents an electrical symptom from being mistaken for internal transmission damage.
searchTerms: shifter will not release from Park

when.summary: The selector binds, the Park interlock behaves incorrectly, or a paddle request is not recognized.
notes: This guide supports inspection and specified isolated checks; it does not provide a continuous replacement route from every initial symptom.

prepare.title: Prepare the diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool with powertrain control module (PCM) datalogger access, a voltmeter/ohmmeter and suitable terminal probes. Identify the engine before selecting PCM terminals; the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L connections differ.

prepare.title: Plan safe paddle access
prepare.detail: Paddle component testing requires supplemental restraint system depowering and driver-airbag removal using the linked procedure. This requires airbag-service capability. Establish the specified safe access and electrical isolation before testing, and follow the airbag procedure for installation and return to service.

steps.title: Inspect the selector mechanism first
steps.body: Verify the complaint and inspect the lever, knob, cable, manual control lever, wiring and connectors. Confirm cable retaining clips are fully seated at both the transmission bracket and the front of the selector, with correct routing and secure retainers. Correct visible damage first. Check adjustment for an incorrect gear relationship, and inspect bracket security and bezel alignment.

steps.title: Observe brake lamps and interlock power
steps.body: At A1, apply the brake: if the stoplamps do not illuminate, follow stoplamp diagnosis. A2 checks disconnected floor-shifter connector C3245 pin 4 to ground with ignition ON. Expected voltage is greater than 11 volts with the brake applied and 0 volts when released. Record both readings; these observations alone do not establish an actuator-replacement decision.

steps.title: Keep ground and BCM checks separate
steps.body: A5 specifies less than 3 ohms from C3245 pin 5 to ground. Perform it only with a verified unpowered, isolated test setup; a failed result calls for circuit repair, while a pass does not establish an A6 conclusion. Independently, A7 requires ignition OFF and inspection of all BCM connectors. Correct corrosion and damaged, bent or pushed-out pins, reconnect securely and retest. A persistent concern requires the vehicle identification number (VIN) for the BCM Guided Routine.

steps.title: Observe the paddle requests
steps.body: For B1, switch ignition ON and monitor PCM parameter identifiers (PIDs) SST_U and SST_D in the datalogger. Each should be low with its corresponding paddle pressed and high when released. Correct responses establish that these inputs work at that time. An abnormal response needs an established diagnostic setup before further conclusions.

steps.title: Test the paddle switches independently
steps.body: After the airbag prerequisites, disconnect the switch being tested. B2 checks upshift C2428 component-side pins 1 and 2; B7 checks downshift C2429 component-side pins 3 and 4. Each requires less than 1.5 ohms when its paddle is pressed and greater than 10,000 ohms when released. A failure directs replacement of that particular switch. A passing B2 permits B3; the downshift component result stands independently.

steps.title: Follow the conditional upshift wiring branch
steps.body: At B3, ignition OFF: inspect disconnected C2428. With ignition ON, measure pin 1 to ground. Greater than 11 volts reaches a continuation outside this guide; stop before B12. Otherwise, B4 requires ignition OFF, PCM disconnection and connector inspection, followed by the engine-specific continuity test from C226A pin 10. Require less than 3 ohms, then greater than 10,000 ohms to ground at B5. Repair a failed circuit.

steps.title: Interpret B6 only after its preceding checks
steps.body: After the applicable B2–B5 outcomes, reconnect the PCM and disconnect steering column control module (SCCM) C226A. B6 checks component-side C226A pin 10 to C218B pin 12. Less than 3 ohms selects the engine-specific PCM replacement route plus Transmission Strategy Download. A failed result selects clockspring replacement, followed by SCCM replacement only if the concern remains. These endpoints depend on the complete preceding branch and its established setup.

steps.title: Keep downshift circuit checks bounded
steps.body: In a separately established B8 setup, switch ignition OFF, disconnect and inspect C2429, then switch ignition ON and measure pin 4 to ground. Greater than 11 volts stops before B12. Otherwise, B9 requires ignition OFF, PCM disconnection and inspection, then engine-specific continuity from C226A pin 9: less than 3 ohms. B10 requires greater than 10,000 ohms from that pin to ground. Repair failures; a pass stops before B11.

watchFor.title: Identify the actual switch contacts
watchFor.body: The paddle circuit identifies separate switching and illumination contacts. Keep testing on the specified switch terminals, away from airbag igniter connections.

watchFor.title: Avoid premature module decisions
watchFor.body: A code or abnormal B1 response alone does not justify replacing the PCM, SCCM, clockspring or selector assembly.

notes: For binding or override failure, inspect the bezel, lever and cable for damage. Manual-lever or internal damage requires separate transmission assessment. Engine-speed-related selector vibration calls for checking cable routing, contact and security.
Ignition-key locking concerns lead to steering-column electrical diagnosis; a missing Park indication leads to instrumentation diagnosis after checking cable retention and routing.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1319:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The brake shift interlock output circuit has a short-to-ground indication.
diagnostics.next: Begin with stoplamp operation and the supported interlock checks; inspect wiring and terminals before identifying a failed actuator or BCM.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1319:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The brake shift interlock output circuit has a short-to-power or open-circuit indication.
diagnostics.next: Compare brake-applied and released voltage observations, then establish the applicable circuit-test setup.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0815, P0816 or P0819 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detected a high signal during an upshift request, downshift request, or either request in the shift-to-range correlation check, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Observe B1 responses and use the correctly established switch or circuit checks. These codes do not prove internal transmission damage.

verification.title: Recheck the original complaint
verification.body: After connector correction, operate the system and determine whether the concern remains. Confirm the expected paddle high/low responses where applicable, and complete the required airbag restoration procedure after access.

verification.title: Record observations and boundaries
verification.body: Record stoplamp operation, brake-applied/released voltage, paddle PID states and isolated resistance results. Identify any branch stopped before A6, B11 or B12; do not record those paths as completed diagnoses.

procedures.purpose: 6R80 external-control inspection, interlock observations and conditional paddle checks for 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L.
Identify upshift/downshift switching contacts and the associated column circuit.
Selector cable adjustment when inspection identifies a range-relationship concern.
Selector assembly and bezel removal/installation when physical inspection establishes damage.
Stoplamp diagnosis when A1 finds no brake-lamp operation.
Driver-airbag service prerequisites and removal/installation for paddle access.
Upshift paddle removal and installation following a failed isolated B2 switch test.
Downshift paddle removal and installation following a failed isolated B7 switch test.
6R80 Transmission Strategy Download required by the conditional B6 PCM-replacement route.
SCCM removal and installation for the conditional column-component route identified in B6.
Separate steering-column diagnosis for ignition-key locking complaints.
Separate instrumentation diagnosis when the Park indication does not illuminate.

applicability.equipment: 6R80 automatic transmission with SelectShift paddle switches

guides.title: Manually release an automatic transmission selector stuck in Park
guides.summary: Use the brake shift interlock override to move the selector into Neutral, then verify brake-light operation before driving.
guides.introduction: The brake shift interlock normally prevents the automatic transmission selector from leaving Park until the brake pedal is applied with the ignition on. Its actuator is built into the selector assembly and mechanically blocks the selector’s detent mechanism. This procedure manually releases that block when the normal release fails, allowing the selector to move into Neutral.
guides.why: In normal operation, the brake pedal position switch provides the input that allows the body control module to energize the interlock actuator. An override bypasses the mechanical restraint without establishing why it failed to release. Neutral also leaves the transmission output shaft free to turn, making the parking brake and applied brake pedal essential during the release.
searchTerms: cannot shift out of Park with brake applied
Park release and brake lights not working

when.summary: When the selector will not leave Park with the ignition on and the brake pedal applied.
notes: The override releases the selector; the cause of the failed normal release still needs attention.

prepare.title: Secure the vehicle
prepare.detail: Fully apply the parking brake before exposing or operating the override. Moving into Neutral removes the transmission’s Park restraint.

prepare.title: Prepare access to the selector
prepare.detail: Have a small screwdriver for the actuator and be ready to lift the selector bezel carefully from its front corners.

steps.title: Apply the parking brake and switch off
steps.body: Fully apply the parking brake, then set the ignition switch to the 0 position, meaning ignition off. This is the starting condition for the manual release.

steps.title: Lift the selector bezel
steps.body: Starting at the front corners, carefully pry the bezel upward and position it out of the way. This exposes the actuator on the selector lever assembly.

steps.title: Operate the manual release
steps.body: Use a small screwdriver to push forward on the brake shift interlock actuator. Apply the brake pedal, press the selector knob button and move the selector into N, or Neutral.

steps.title: Start the engine
steps.body: With the selector in Neutral, start the engine. Maintain control of the vehicle with the brakes because Neutral does not hold the transmission output shaft.

steps.title: Restore the bezel
steps.body: Snap the bezel back into place after starting the engine. Verify brake-light operation before any driving.

watchFor.title: Brake lights may also be inoperative
watchFor.body: A blown fuse is a possible reason the override is needed, and the brake lights may not work. Do not drive until their operation has been verified.

notes: The actuator is integral to the selector assembly. Successful manual release does not establish that the actuator itself caused the fault.

diagnostics.finding: The selector remains in Park with ignition on and the brake pedal applied.
diagnostics.meaning: The normal interlock release has not occurred.
diagnostics.next: Secure the vehicle and follow the manual override sequence when release is necessary.

diagnostics.finding: The brake lights do not operate when checked.
diagnostics.meaning: The interlock complaint may coincide with a blown fuse and loss of brake-light operation.
diagnostics.next: Investigate and correct the fault before driving.

verification.title: Confirm release and trim restoration
verification.body: Confirm that the selector reached Neutral, the engine started and the bezel was snapped back into place.

verification.title: Record the brake-light result
verification.body: Check and record whether the brake lights operate before allowing the vehicle to be driven.

procedures.purpose: Manual activation of the automatic transmission brake shift interlock override.
Explain normal interlock operation and why Neutral does not restrain vehicle movement.

guides.title: Adjust the automatic transmission selector cable
guides.summary: Align the cabin selector and transmission manual lever in DRIVE, lock the cable adjustment and verify starting and reverse-lamp operation.
guides.introduction: The selector cable links the cabin shifter to the transmission's manual control lever. Its adjustment makes the selected cabin position correspond to the transmission position. The procedure establishes DRIVE independently at both ends, then locks the cable to preserve that relationship.
guides.why: Adjusting against an incorrectly positioned lever can preserve a range mismatch. The final starting and reverse-lamp checks provide practical confirmation that the selector positions correspond to the required functions.
searchTerms: engine does not start in park or neutral

when.summary: When service work requires resetting the selector cable's relationship to the transmission manual lever.
notes: A starting or reverse-lamp complaint alone does not prove that cable adjustment is the cause.

prepare.title: Safe underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the specified lifting points, identified by stamped triangles. Never work under a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Lift clearance
prepare.detail: Check adapter placement and underbody clearance to avoid the suspension, exhaust, steering linkage and axle components. Do not lift through the bumpers or use the emergency tire-changing jack for this work.

prepare.title: Adjustment access
prepare.detail: Be able to reach the transmission manual lever and release the cable adjuster's latch gently without damaging its locking features.

steps.title: Position the vehicle and cabin selector
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on the hoist using the linked lifting procedure. Then move the cabin shifter to DRIVE. This establishes the cabin end of the adjustment.

steps.title: Set the transmission lever independently
steps.body: Disconnect the selector cable from the manual lever. Rotate the manual lever clockwise until it stops, then counterclockwise through 3 detents. This places the transmission lever in DRIVE rather than relying on the existing cable setting.

steps.title: Release the adjustment lock
steps.body: Gently pry the adjuster latch upward, then push the lock tab down into its released position. The illustrated open position shows the tab displaced downward; release it before reconnecting the cable end.

steps.title: Reconnect and secure the cable
steps.body: With the lock tab released, connect the cable end to the manual control lever. Push the tab upward to lock the adjustment. Pull back on the adjuster afterward to confirm that it is securely installed.

steps.title: Check the selected functions
steps.body: Verify that the vehicle starts in PARK and NEUTRAL only, and that the reverse lamps illuminate in REVERSE. If either check fails, the adjustment has not established an acceptable result and further investigation is required.

watchFor.title: An unsecured adjuster
watchFor.body: A tab that appears closed still needs the specified pull-back check; an insecure adjustment cannot reliably preserve lever alignment.

notes: The brake shift interlock is a separate mechanism within the selector assembly. It normally requires the brake pedal to be pressed with the ignition in RUN before leaving PARK.

diagnostics.finding: Starting is possible outside PARK or NEUTRAL, or reverse-lamp operation is incorrect.
diagnostics.meaning: The required completion checks have failed; the observation does not identify the cable as the sole cause.
diagnostics.next: Recheck lever positioning and adjuster security, then investigate any remaining control-system fault.

verification.title: Record the functional result
verification.body: Record the adjuster security check, starting permission in PARK and NEUTRAL only, and reverse-lamp operation in REVERSE.

procedures.purpose: Automatic transmission selector cable adjustment and required starting and reverse-lamp checks.
Correct lifting points, support precautions and hoist clearance requirements.

guides.title: Replace the SelectShift downshift paddle switch
guides.summary: Replace the steering-wheel downshift switch through the driver-airbag and left-hand speed-control switch access path.
guides.introduction: The SelectShift paddles let the driver request manual gear changes from the steering wheel. The downshift paddle provides the request for a lower gear. This repair replaces its electrical switch and reconnects the surrounding steering-wheel controls. Access requires removing the driver airbag, so restraint-system work is a central part of this otherwise compact switch replacement.
guides.why: The left-hand speed-control switch obstructs access to the paddle switch connection and mounting screw. Removing these parts in order gives access without pulling against their wiring. Correct airbag depowering, reconnection and retention matter because the airbag must remain safe during service and operate correctly in a crash.

when.summary: When repair assessment has established that the steering-wheel downshift paddle switch requires replacement.
notes: The replacement procedure does not itself diagnose an unsuccessful manual-shift request.

prepare.title: Restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Have the Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) depowering and repowering procedures named in the Driver Airbag article available. Follow their complete instructions before handling airbag connections.

prepare.title: Access tools
prepare.detail: Prepare a 3 mm Allen key for the airbag spring clips and suitable hand tools for the speed-control and paddle-switch screws.

prepare.title: Understand the access sequence
prepare.detail: Read the Driver Airbag and Downshift Paddle Switch procedures together. Keep the airbag work within the prescribed SRS isolation sequence throughout removal and installation.

steps.title: Depower the SRS and release the driver airbag
steps.body: Follow the depowering procedure referenced by [Driver Airbag](#/document/G1696301). At each steering-wheel side opening, insert the Allen key and angle its inner end upward and toward the front of the vehicle. Press the spring clip to release the corresponding retainer, ease the airbag away, and disconnect its three electrical connectors.

steps.title: Remove the left-hand speed-control switch
steps.body: Remove its screws and reposition the switch enough to reach its electrical connector. Disconnect the connector before taking the switch away. This clears the access required by the [downshift paddle procedure](#/document/G1702525).

steps.title: Remove the downshift paddle switch
steps.body: Disconnect the paddle-switch electrical connector, then remove its mounting screw and the switch. Keeping the connector release ahead of component removal avoids using the wiring to restrain the loose switch.

steps.title: Install the replacement switch and restore the adjacent control
steps.body: Reverse the switch-removal sequence: fit the paddle switch and screw, reconnect its connector, then reconnect and secure the left-hand speed-control switch.

steps.title: Refit the airbag and repower the SRS
steps.body: With the SRS still depowered, reconnect all three airbag connectors. Align the airbag with the steering wheel and push it into place so its retainers engage the spring clips. Complete the prescribed SRS repowering procedure.

watchFor.title: Airbag reconnection while powered
watchFor.body: The SRS must be depowered before reconnecting the airbag. Incorrect handling can cause accidental deployment.

watchFor.title: Incomplete airbag retention
watchFor.body: Both released retainers must engage their spring clips during refitting; simply positioning the airbag against the wheel does not complete installation.

notes: In manual S operation, the paddles provide manual gear selection. That operating description does not establish that a switch is faulty whenever a requested shift does not occur.

verification.title: Check restoration of the steering-wheel assembly
verification.body: Confirm the paddle and speed-control switches are secured and connected, and the airbag retainers are engaged.

verification.title: Record restraint-system completion
verification.body: Record completion of airbag refitting and the required SRS repowering procedure alongside the switch replacement.

procedures.purpose: Downshift paddle switch removal and installation for the listed 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications.
Required driver-airbag access, connector handling, retention and references to SRS depowering and repowering.

applicability.equipment: Automatic transmission with SelectShift steering-wheel paddles

guides.title: Replace the automatic-transmission selector lever assembly
guides.summary: Check cable retention, remove the console-mounted selector assembly, and complete installation with the required cable adjustment.
guides.introduction: The selector assembly moves the transmission's manual control lever through a cable. It also contains the brake shift interlock actuator, which mechanically prevents movement out of Park until the required brake and ignition conditions are met. Replacement involves both the cable connection and console trim, followed by adjustment so the selector and transmission positions agree.
guides.why: An unseated cable-to-bracket clip can make the cable bind and stop the transmission manual shaft from fully returning to Park. That can produce high shift effort or a no-start complaint. Checking retention first can identify a problem that does not require replacing the selector assembly.

when.summary: When diagnosis calls for selector replacement, after checking cable-clip seating for no-start or high-effort complaints.

prepare.title: Access and tools
prepare.detail: Provide a suitable hoist, interior trim remover, screwdriver and torque tools for the cable retainer and selector fasteners. Have the complete selector cable adjustment procedure available.

prepare.title: Safe vehicle support
prepare.detail: Position the vehicle on the hoist in Neutral using the specified lifting points. Neutral leaves the transmission output shaft free to turn. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

steps.title: Check cable retention before removal
steps.body: Verify that the cable-to-bracket clips are fully seated at both the transmission and selector assembly. Resolve an unseated connection before condemning the assembly for high effort or failure to reach Park.

steps.title: Disconnect the selector cable carefully
steps.body: Follow the [selector removal procedure](#/document/G1694272). Use the screwdriver close to the post and turn it as directed to release the cable end. Do not pull or pry on the cable itself. Remove the cable retainer bolt and disconnect the cable from the assembly.

steps.title: Open the console access
steps.body: Starting at the front corners, carefully lift the bezel, position it aside and disconnect its electrical connector. Open the console lid. Release the right-side trim clips and remove that panel and its front screws, then repeat on the left. Move the seats rearward if access requires it.

steps.title: Remove the upper trim and assembly
steps.body: Release the upper-trim clips, position the selector bezel and boot aside, and remove the console upper trim while disconnecting its electrical connectors. Disconnect the selector assembly connector, then remove the mounting bolts, nuts and assembly.

steps.title: Install and reconnect
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, restoring the electrical connections and console trim. Tighten the selector mounting bolts and nuts to 9 Nm and the cable retainer bolt to 7 Nm. Handle the cable end without loading or levering against the cable.

steps.title: Adjust the selector cable
steps.body: Complete [Selector Lever Cable Adjustment](#/document/G1694288) after installation. This is the required final adjustment between the cabin selector and transmission control lever; attaching the cable alone does not complete the job.

watchFor.title: Cable-end damage
watchFor.body: Prying away from the post or pulling the cable can damage its end and create another selection problem.

watchFor.title: An unresolved interlock complaint
watchFor.body: The interlock also depends on the brake-pedal switch, ignition switch and body control module. A selector removal procedure does not establish which part caused an interlock fault.

diagnostics.finding: High shift effort or a no-start complaint accompanies an unseated cable-to-bracket clip.
diagnostics.meaning: Cable binding can prevent the manual shaft from reaching Park completely.
diagnostics.next: Correct the retention concern and reassess before replacing the selector.

verification.title: Confirm adjustment and original complaint
verification.body: Confirm cable adjustment is complete and reassess any original high-effort or no-start complaint.

verification.title: Check interlock operation
verification.body: Confirm the selector can leave Park with ignition in RUN and the brake pedal pressed, consistent with the described interlock operation.

procedures.purpose: Selector assembly removal and installation for the automatic-transmission application.
Correct lifting points and vehicle-support precautions.
Required selector cable adjustment after assembly installation.
Range-selection and brake shift interlock operation used to understand completion checks.

guides.title: Remove and refit the automatic selector lever bezel
guides.summary: Release the selector surround, disconnect its wiring and separate the knob, boot and bezel for service.
guides.introduction: The selector bezel finishes the console opening around the automatic gear lever and its boot. Beneath this trim, the selector assembly operates the transmission through a cable and includes the brake shift interlock. Bezel removal involves both trim retainers and an electrical connection, followed by removal of the knob, boot and bezel together.
guides.why: The surround must be released from its front corners before the assembly is removed. Lifting it carelessly can strain its retainers or wiring. Separating the boot and bezel only after removing the complete assembly gives access without pulling against the attached knob.

when.summary: When the selector bezel needs service or the knob, boot and bezel assembly must be removed for access.

prepare.title: Secure the vehicle
prepare.detail: The procedure requires S rather than P. Keep the vehicle secured against movement; the transmission's parking pawl locks the output shaft only in P.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim and connector handling
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for careful prying and screw removal. Be ready to support the released surround while disconnecting its electrical connector.

steps.title: Position the lever and release the surround
steps.body: Move the selector to S. Starting at the front corners, carefully pry the bezel upward and position it out of the way. The illustration identifies five retaining clips; release the trim without pulling on its wiring.

steps.title: Remove the complete assembly
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector before lifting the parts away. Remove the screws, then remove the shifter knob, boot and bezel as one assembly.

steps.title: Separate the bezel and boot
steps.body: Remove the boot and bezel from the shifter knob. Keep the parts supported during separation so the boot does not carry the weight or force of the other components.

steps.title: Reassemble in reverse order
steps.body: Refit the boot and bezel to the knob, reinstall the assembly and screws, reconnect the electrical connector, and seat the bezel. Check that the boot is not trapped as the trim settles into place.

watchFor.title: Wiring still attached
watchFor.body: A released bezel is not yet free to remove. Disconnect its connector before removing the assembly.

notes: This operation services the trim assembly; selector-cable adjustment is a separate operation.

diagnostics.finding: The selector will not move out of P.
diagnostics.meaning: Park release depends on brake shift interlock operation, including the brake input and ignition state.
diagnostics.next: Evaluate the interlock concern before treating bezel replacement as the remedy.

verification.title: Check the completed surround
verification.body: Confirm that the screws, electrical connector and retaining clips are restored and the boot sits correctly.

procedures.purpose: Automatic selector bezel removal, knob/boot separation and reverse-order installation.
Selector range and brake shift interlock operation for distinguishing trim work from a control concern.

guides.title: Replace and adjust the automatic transmission selector cable
guides.summary: Check the cable mounting clips, replace the selector cable when needed, and align its adjustment with both levers in Drive.
guides.introduction: The selector cable connects the cabin gear selector to the transmission's manual control lever. Its mounting points hold the cable housing while movement inside the cable selects the transmission range. Replacement restores this mechanical connection; adjustment makes the cabin selection agree with the transmission lever position.
guides.why: An unseated mounting clip can let the cable bind and prevent the transmission lever from returning fully to Park. That can cause high shift effort or a no-start concern without proving the cable needs replacement. Correct seating and adjustment therefore matter as much as installing the cable itself.

when.summary: When selector-cable replacement is justified after checking both cable-to-bracket clips for full seating.
notes: Check the clips at both the transmission and selector lever assembly before replacing a cable for no-start or high-effort concerns.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underside access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the specified lifting points. The lifting procedure identifies them by stamped triangles and warns against working beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Have the release and tightening tools ready
prepare.detail: Use a screwdriver for the illustrated cable-end release and a torque tool suitable for the cable retainer bolts: 62 lb.in (7 Nm).

steps.title: Check seating and position the vehicle
steps.body: Verify that both cable-to-bracket clips are fully seated. With the vehicle in Neutral, position it on the hoist using the lifting procedure. Then place the selector lever in Drive for cable removal.

steps.title: Release the selector end without loading the cable
steps.body: Place the screwdriver close to the selector post and turn it as illustrated to lift the cable end off. Do not pull or pry on the cable itself; this can damage its end. Remove the selector cable retainer bolt and disconnect the cable from the selector assembly.

steps.title: Free the remaining attachments
steps.body: Disconnect the cable retainer from the transmission. Disconnect the cable from the transmission manual lever and remove the cable bolt. Release the remaining cable retainer and remove the cable.

steps.title: Install and secure the replacement cable
steps.body: Position the cable, connect its retainer and install the retainer bolt. Reconnect the transmission retainer and the cable at the selector assembly. With the selector still in Drive, install its retainer bolt and connect the cable end. Tighten the specified retainer bolts to 62 lb.in (7 Nm).

steps.title: Set the transmission lever to Drive
steps.body: Rotate the transmission manual lever clockwise until it stops, then counterclockwise through 3 detents. This establishes the transmission's Drive position before the cable adjustment is locked.

steps.title: Connect and lock the adjustment
steps.body: Gently lift the adjuster latch, then push the lock tab down to release it. With the tab released, connect the cable end to the manual control lever. Push the tab upward to lock the adjustment, then pull back on the adjuster to confirm secure engagement.

steps.title: Verify range-dependent operation
steps.body: Verify that the vehicle starts in Park and Neutral only, and that the reverse lamps illuminate in Reverse. These checks establish whether the installed cable and adjustment produce the required range-related behavior.

watchFor.title: Cable-end damage during release
watchFor.body: Keep the screwdriver's lifting action close to the post. Pulling on the cable puts the force through the part being reused or replaced.

watchFor.title: An unsecured adjuster
watchFor.body: Moving the locking tab is not the final check: the procedure also requires pulling back on the adjuster to confirm it is secure.

notes: The brake shift interlock is integral to the selector assembly. A selector that will not leave Park does not, by itself, identify a defective cable.

diagnostics.finding: High shift effort or a no-start concern occurs with a cable-to-bracket clip unseated.
diagnostics.meaning: Cable binding may prevent the transmission manual shaft from reaching Park fully.
diagnostics.next: Correct clip seating and reassess the concern before deciding to replace the cable.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical retention
verification.body: Confirm the cable retainers are connected, the specified bolts are tightened and the locked adjuster passes its pull-back check.

verification.title: Record the functional results
verification.body: Record starting permission in Park and Neutral only, plus reverse-lamp operation in Reverse. Failed checks require correction before the job is complete.

procedures.purpose: Complete selector cable removal, installation, Drive-position adjustment and functional verification.
Correct lifting points, hoist positioning and supported-vehicle precautions.

guides.title: Replace the automatic transmission selector lever knob
guides.summary: Release the console bezel, remove the knob with its boot and bezel, and separate the knob for replacement.
guides.introduction: The selector knob is the handgrip on the automatic transmission's range selector. A cable connects the selector assembly to the transmission's manual control lever. This job removes the knob, boot and bezel together before separating the knob; it does not involve opening the transmission.
guides.why: The bezel is retained by clips, and an electrical connector must be disconnected before the assembly is removed. Starting at the specified front corners gives a controlled release path. Pulling the whole assembly away before disconnecting it would place strain on its wiring.

when.summary: When the selector knob needs replacement or removal for access to the knob, boot and bezel assembly.
notes: The removal position is S.
The brake shift interlock belongs to the selector assembly; a selection complaint does not by itself justify replacing the knob.

prepare.title: Secure the vehicle
prepare.detail: Prevent vehicle movement before selecting S. Park normally locks the transmission output shaft, and that parking lock is not available with the lever moved to S.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim removal
prepare.detail: Have a suitable trim-prying tool and a driver that fits the retaining screws. Make space to position the released bezel aside without pulling on its connector.

steps.title: Move the selector to S
steps.body: Position the shifter in S before beginning trim removal. This establishes the lever position used by the removal procedure.

steps.title: Release the bezel and connector
steps.body: Starting at the front corners, carefully pry the bezel upward and position it out of the way. The illustration identifies five retaining clips. Disconnect the electrical connector before lifting the assembly away.

steps.title: Remove the assembly and separate the knob
steps.body: Remove the retaining screws, then remove the shifter knob, boot and bezel together. With the assembly removed, separate the knob from the boot and bezel.

steps.title: Reassemble in reverse order
steps.body: Fit the knob to the boot and bezel, return the assembly to the lever and reinstall its screws. Reconnect the electrical connector and seat the bezel clips carefully.

watchFor.title: Resistance during bezel removal
watchFor.body: Continue the careful clip-release operation from the front corners. Do not use the wiring to restrain or support the lifted assembly.

notes: S also provides manual range operation through the steering-wheel SelectShift paddles; those switches are separate from this knob-removal job.

diagnostics.finding: The lever will not leave Park.
diagnostics.meaning: The brake shift interlock intentionally blocks movement until the prescribed ignition and brake conditions are met.
diagnostics.next: Check operation with the ignition in RUN and the brake pedal pressed before attributing the complaint to the knob.

verification.title: Confirm secure reassembly
verification.body: Confirm the knob assembly is retained, the boot and bezel are seated, and the electrical connector is reconnected.

verification.title: Confirm normal selector operation
verification.body: With the vehicle secured, confirm the reassembled knob operates the selector normally and that Park release follows the ignition-and-brake interlock conditions.

procedures.purpose: Remove and reinstall the automatic selector knob, including bezel release and assembly separation.

guides.title: Replace the SelectShift Upshift Paddle Switch
guides.summary: Replace the steering-wheel upshift paddle after safely removing the driver airbag and right-hand speed-control switch.
guides.introduction: The SelectShift upshift paddle is an electrical switch mounted on the steering wheel that lets the driver request a higher transmission gear. Access requires removal of the driver airbag and the right-hand speed-control switch. Although the paddle itself has a short removal sequence, the restraint-system work makes this an advanced repair.
guides.why: The supplemental restraint system (SRS) must be depowered before airbag removal and remain depowered when its connectors are reattached. Incorrect handling can cause accidental deployment or compromise restraint operation in a crash. Moving the neighboring switch first provides access to its connector and then to the paddle without pulling on connected wiring.

when.summary: When diagnosis calls for upshift paddle replacement or the switch must be removed for related work.
notes: A missing upshift response alone does not prove that the paddle switch has failed.

prepare.title: Restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Use the complete SRS Depowering and SRS Repowering procedures in section 501-20B, together with the Driver Airbag procedure. Do not substitute an assumed isolation sequence.

prepare.title: Access tools
prepare.detail: Have a 3 mm (0.125 inch) Allen key for the airbag spring clips and suitable tools for the switch screws. Plan to release each electrical connector before removing its component.

steps.title: Depower and remove the driver airbag
steps.body: Follow [Driver Airbag](#/document/G1696301), beginning with SRS depowering. Through each side access hole, angle the Allen key upward and toward the vehicle front to release the spring clip. Separate the airbag from the wheel and disconnect its three electrical connectors.

steps.title: Remove the right-hand speed-control switch
steps.body: Following [Upshift Paddle Switch](#/document/G1702526), remove the speed-control switch screws and position the switch to reach its electrical connector. Disconnect the connector and remove the switch.

steps.title: Replace the upshift paddle
steps.body: Disconnect the paddle’s electrical connector, then remove its screw and the switch. Reverse these operations to install the replacement, and restore the speed-control switch connection and screws.

steps.title: Restore the airbag and restraint system
steps.body: With the SRS still depowered, reconnect the three airbag connectors. Align the airbag and push it into the wheel so its retainers engage the spring clips. Complete the prescribed SRS repowering procedure.

watchFor.title: Reconnecting an energized restraint component
watchFor.body: Confirm the SRS remains depowered before reconnecting the airbag; this requirement also applies during installation.

watchFor.title: Pulling a switch against its wiring
watchFor.body: Position the right-hand switch only far enough to access and release its connector before removing it.

notes: In manual S position, the steering-wheel paddles provide manual gear selection. Use that operating context when checking the repaired control.

verification.title: Confirm restraint reassembly
verification.body: Confirm all airbag connectors and spring-clip retainers are engaged and SRS repowering is complete.

verification.title: Check the repaired control
verification.body: Once the restraint system is returned to service, verify the upshift request during an appropriate SelectShift function check and confirm the disturbed speed-control switch is reconnected.

procedures.purpose: Upshift paddle and right-hand speed-control switch removal and reverse installation.
Driver airbag removal and installation, including required SRS depowering and repowering.
SelectShift manual S operating context for checking the upshift control.

applicability.equipment: Automatic transmission with SelectShift paddle switches

guides.title: Replace the clutch disc and pressure plate on a manual Mustang
guides.summary: Remove the transmission, inspect the flywheel and refit the clutch with correct alignment, new bolts and the required scan-tool correction.
guides.introduction: The pressure plate clamps the clutch disc against the flywheel so engine torque can pass into the transmission. Releasing that clamping force permits gear changes. Servicing the disc and pressure plate requires transmission removal, careful handling of the spring-loaded assembly and preservation of its alignment with the flywheel.
guides.why: Uneven bolt release can damage the pressure plate. Incorrect rotational alignment can introduce clutch vibration, while an off-centre disc complicates transmission installation. The pressure-plate bolts are discarded during removal, and all engine branches require a Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction after repairs.

when.summary: When clutch repair is established or the disc and pressure plate must be removed for related work.
notes: Vibration alone does not establish which clutch or flywheel component needs replacement.

prepare.title: Plan the transmission work
prepare.detail: Have the capability and equipment required by the exact transmission removal and installation procedures. The 5.2L uses the 3160 branch; the other listed engines use MT82 procedures.

prepare.title: Prepare alignment and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Provide a clutch alignment tool, new pressure-plate bolts, appropriate torque and angle equipment, and a scan tool capable of the required profile correction.

prepare.title: Control friction dust
prepare.detail: Do not breathe clutch dust or blow it away with compressed air. Remove it using government-approved techniques.

steps.title: Remove the correct transmission
steps.body: Follow the engine-specific removal reference to expose the clutch. Complete those access and support requirements before disturbing the pressure plate.

steps.title: Preserve alignment and release the load
steps.body: If reusing the assembly, index-mark the pressure plate against the flywheel before loosening it. Release the bolts one turn at a time in a star pattern until spring load is fully released. Remove the pressure plate and disc, then discard the bolts. The 5.2L explicitly separates reuse and replacement branches, but both require even unloading.

steps.title: Assess the flywheel
steps.body: For 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L, inspect for damage, burn marks and wear; replace the flywheel when necessary. For 3.7L, use its dedicated flywheel inspection procedure to decide whether it is serviceable. Installing a clutch without addressing an unsuitable mating surface leaves that defect in the torque path.

steps.title: Centre the disc and align the pressure plate
steps.body: Position the disc with the clutch alignment tool. Return a reused assembly to its index marks. When installing a new pressure plate and/or flywheel, bring their paint dots as close together as possible. Install new pressure-plate bolts progressively, one turn at a time in a star pattern.

steps.title: Apply the engine-specific tightening specification
steps.body: The 2.3L bolts tighten to 35 Nm. The 3.7L and 5.0L use 63 Nm followed by 60°. The 5.2L uses 34 Nm followed by 60°, whether its pressure plate is new or reused. Follow the matching clutch procedure throughout; these specifications are not interchangeable.

steps.title: Reinstall and perform the electronic completion step
steps.body: Install the transmission through its matching installation procedure. Then use the scan tool to perform Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction, following the on-screen instructions. This is part of completing the repair on every listed engine.

watchFor.title: Lost reference marks
watchFor.body: A reused pressure plate needs its original rotational relationship to the flywheel. Preserve the marks through cleaning and handling.

watchFor.title: Uneven pressure-plate loading
watchFor.body: Do not fully release or tighten individual bolts while the others remain loaded; use the prescribed progressive star pattern.

notes: The 5.2L transmission is the 3160 despite the clutch article's inherited MT82 section label.

diagnostics.finding: Flywheel damage, heat marking or wear is found.
diagnostics.meaning: The mating surface requires an engine-appropriate serviceability decision.
diagnostics.next: Follow the applicable inspection instruction and replace the flywheel when required.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical completion
verification.body: Confirm alignment, new pressure-plate bolts, the correct tightening stages and completion of the transmission installation procedure.

verification.title: Record the scan-tool result
verification.body: Record successful completion of Misfire Monitor Neutral Profile Correction.

guides.title: Replace the MT82 pilot bearing on 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L engines
guides.summary: Remove the clutch assembly, extract the pilot bearing with the specified remover, and drive its replacement into the crankshaft.
guides.introduction: The pilot bearing supports the transmission input shaft where it meets the engine, allowing relative rotation when the clutch is disengaged. Replacing it restores that bearing support. The bearing operation is brief, but access requires removal of the clutch disc and pressure plate, so the work must be planned around the correct engine-specific clutch procedure.
guides.why: Extraction and installation use different tools: the remover withdraws the bearing, while a driver installs its replacement. Selecting the correct clutch procedure also matters because a shared pilot-bearing operation does not make the surrounding engine-specific work interchangeable.

when.summary: When pilot-bearing replacement is required on a 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine with the MT82 transmission.
notes: Clutch removal provides access; it does not by itself establish that the pilot bearing needs replacement.

prepare.title: Plan the clutch access work
prepare.detail: Have the capability and equipment required by the clutch-disc and pressure-plate procedure for the fitted engine. Complete its prerequisites before attempting bearing removal.

prepare.title: Prepare the bearing tools
prepare.detail: Use pilot-bearing remover 308-001 (T58L-101-B). Have a driver available for installing the replacement bearing in the crankshaft.

steps.title: Remove the clutch assembly
steps.body: Follow the linked clutch-disc and pressure-plate removal procedure for the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine. This exposes the pilot bearing for the dedicated extraction operation.

steps.title: Extract the pilot bearing
steps.body: Use special tool 308-001 (T58L-101-B) to remove the bearing. The illustration shows the specified remover acting at the central bearing location.

steps.title: Install the replacement
steps.body: Position the pilot bearing in the crankshaft, then install it using a driver. Follow the pilot-bearing installation procedure without adding an assumed installation dimension.

steps.title: Restore the clutch
steps.body: Install the clutch disc and pressure plate using the same engine-specific procedure selected for removal. Bearing installation alone does not complete the repair.

watchFor.title: Different 5.2L arrangement
watchFor.body: The pilot bearing is not separately serviceable on the 5.2L engine. That application requires a new flywheel and is outside this separate-bearing replacement path.

notes: Use the engine-specific clutch instructions for the surrounding work; the bearing procedure supplies the extraction and installation method.

verification.title: Bearing and clutch installation complete
verification.body: Confirm that the replacement bearing has been installed in the crankshaft and that clutch-disc and pressure-plate installation is complete under the matching engine procedure.

procedures.purpose: Pilot-bearing extraction and installation for the listed MT82 applications.
2.3L EcoBoost clutch-disc and pressure-plate removal and installation for bearing access.
3.7L Duratec clutch-disc and pressure-plate removal and installation for bearing access.
5.0L clutch-disc and pressure-plate removal and installation for bearing access.

guides.title: Replace the clutch pedal assembly on a left-hand-drive MT82 Mustang
guides.summary: Replace the clutch pedal through the combined brake-and-clutch pedal assembly, then restore its connections and bleed the clutch.
guides.introduction: The clutch pedal operates the hydraulic clutch controls so the driver can disengage drive for gear changes. On this left-hand-drive MT82 installation, the clutch pedal is serviced as part of the brake pedal assembly. Replacement therefore involves the shared bracket, brake-booster pushrod, pedal switches and clutch hydraulic connections.
guides.why: The shared assembly makes brake-pedal alignment and switch position part of a clutch repair. Incorrect switch handling can damage its plunger or adjustment, while opening the clutch hydraulic connections requires bleeding afterward.

when.summary: When clutch-pedal repair requires replacement of the combined brake-and-clutch pedal assembly.
notes: The clutch pedal is not serviced separately in this procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare parts and workshop support
prepare.detail: Have a suitable fluid suction device, fastening tools, a torque wrench, a new booster pushrod clevis-locking pin and replacement mounting nuts. An assistant is required to move the booster and master cylinder assembly.

prepare.title: Plan the complete repair
prepare.detail: Allow access to the reservoir and pedal assembly. Have the switch procedures and MT82 Clutch System Bleeding procedure referenced by the bracket procedure available before opening the hydraulic connections.

steps.title: Drain the reservoir and release clutch connections
steps.body: Follow the [brake pedal and bracket procedure](#/document/G1692562). Remove the reservoir cap and siphon out the brake fluid. Disconnect the clutch master-cylinder supply tube, then spread and push down the retaining clip to release the clutch master-cylinder tube.

steps.title: Remove the switches before disturbing the pedals
steps.body: Remove the stoplamp switch with the brake pedal at rest. Remove the cruise-control deactivator switch with the clutch pedal at rest. Follow their referenced procedures: each switch plunger must be compressed for the switch to rotate without damage.

steps.title: Free the wiring and booster pushrod
steps.body: Disconnect the accelerator-pedal and starter-inhibitor electrical connectors. Release the harness retainers and move the harness aside. Remove and discard the booster pushrod clevis-locking pin, then position the pushrod aside.

steps.title: Remove the combined pedal assembly
steps.body: Have the assistant pull the brake booster and master cylinder assembly away from the dash panel. Remove the mounting bolts, discard the mounting nuts and withdraw the brake-and-clutch pedal assembly. Do not pry on the booster.

steps.title: Install and align the replacement
steps.body: Reverse removal using the specified fastening requirements. Align the booster pushrod clevis with the brake-pedal attachment before installing retainers, and use a new locking pin and mounting nuts. Reconnect the wiring and hydraulic tubes. Install the stoplamp switch only with the pushrod attached and brake pedal untouched at rest.

steps.title: Bleed the clutch
steps.body: Complete the MT82 Clutch System Bleeding procedure referenced by the bracket article. Reconnecting the tubes alone does not complete the hydraulic work.

watchFor.title: Brake fluid on paint
watchFor.body: Immediately wash any affected paintwork with cold water.

watchFor.title: Switch installation with a displaced pedal
watchFor.body: Pressing or pulling the brake pedal during stoplamp-switch installation can cause incorrect adjustment and switch damage.

notes: Use the MT82 clutch-bleeding procedure for this job; the shared bracket article also names another transmission.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical connections
verification.body: Check pushrod-clevis alignment, the new locking pin and replacement nuts, and that electrical connectors and harness retainers have been restored.

verification.title: Confirm completion of installation
verification.body: Verify that stoplamp-switch installation used the required pedal position and that clutch bleeding has been completed.

procedures.purpose: Left-hand-drive MT82 clutch-pedal service through the combined pedal assembly.
Combined pedal and bracket removal and installation, including switch precautions and the clutch-bleeding reference.

guides.title: Inspect and replace the MT82 clutch slave cylinder
guides.summary: Remove the transmission, inspect the clutch slave cylinder and release bearing, and reinstall the assembly with a new tube retaining clip.
guides.introduction: The clutch slave cylinder converts hydraulic pressure into movement of the clutch release bearing. It sits inside the MT82 transmission bellhousing, so access requires transmission removal. Inspection covers the protective boot, fluid sealing and bearing condition before the transmission goes back into the vehicle.
guides.why: The bearing must turn smoothly while carrying pressure, not merely spin freely when unloaded. The hydraulic tube also needs secure retention, which is why installation requires a new retaining clip even when an inspected cylinder is being refitted.
searchTerms: clutch slave cylinder leaking brake fluid

when.summary: When slave-cylinder inspection or renewal is required, particularly for leakage, boot damage or a rough release bearing.
notes: Rough bearing rotation under applied pressure specifically calls for a new clutch slave cylinder.

prepare.title: Arrange transmission-removal capability
prepare.detail: Prepare the workshop and equipment required by the matching engine-specific MT82 removal and installation procedures. The 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L paths are separate.

prepare.title: Control friction dust
prepare.detail: Do not inhale clutch dust or blow it from friction components or containers with compressed air. Use government-approved removal techniques; this dust can cause serious lung disease and other health effects.

prepare.title: Have the installation items ready
prepare.detail: Obtain a new retaining clip and a torque wrench suitable for the cylinder fasteners. Have a replacement cylinder available if inspection establishes the need.

steps.title: Remove the transmission
steps.body: Follow the removal procedure for the installed engine. Complete its prerequisites before opening access to the slave cylinder; reaching this component is a substantial transmission-removal operation.

steps.title: Release the cylinder and tube
steps.body: Remove the slave-cylinder bolts. Pull the cylinder outward and release its tube from the retaining clip, following the [slave-cylinder procedure](#/document/G1701833). The illustrated clip is part of the tube-retention arrangement.

steps.title: Inspect the complete assembly
steps.body: Look for a damaged boot, leaking brake fluid and a worn or damaged release bearing. Rotate the bearing while applying pressure. If rotation feels rough, install a new slave cylinder.

steps.title: Install with a new retaining clip
steps.body: Fit the new clip first. Position the slave cylinder in the transmission while inserting its tube through the clip. Install the cylinder bolts and tighten them to 97 lb.in (11 Nm).

steps.title: Reinstall the transmission
steps.body: Use the installation procedure matching the engine and complete all of its required reassembly and completion work. Cylinder attachment is only one phase of returning the clutch and transmission to service.

watchFor.title: Chemical exposure
watchFor.body: Read product-label cautions and the available material safety data sheet. Seek medical advice for exposure emergencies or persistent irritation.

watchFor.title: An incomplete bearing check
watchFor.body: A free spin without applied pressure does not perform the specified loaded-rotation inspection.

notes: The specified response to rough bearing rotation is replacement of the slave cylinder assembly.

diagnostics.finding: The release bearing rotates roughly while pressure is applied.
diagnostics.meaning: The assembly meets the stated replacement criterion.
diagnostics.next: Install a new clutch slave cylinder.

diagnostics.finding: The boot is damaged, brake fluid is leaking, or the bearing is visibly worn or damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: Inspection has identified a cylinder or bearing defect requiring attention.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the defect before reinstalling the transmission, and complete the loaded bearing check.

verification.title: Record the inspection result
verification.body: Record boot condition, any brake-fluid leakage, visible bearing damage and the result of rotating the bearing under pressure.

verification.title: Confirm secure installation
verification.body: Confirm that the tube passes through the new retaining clip, the cylinder bolts are tightened correctly and the matching transmission installation procedure is complete.

guides.title: Overhaul the MT82 manual transmission: 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L
guides.summary: Remove the MT82, inspect its internal components, rebuild the transmission with the required seals and assembly checks, then reinstall and restore its fluid and clutch hydraulics.
guides.introduction: The MT82 provides six forward ratios and reverse through constantly meshed gears. Synchronizers help match rotational speeds before their sleeves connect the selected gear to a shaft. Shift forks, rails and an interlock control those movements. This overhaul opens the transmission, exposes the gears and bearings for inspection, and rebuilds the main assembly. It is specialist gearbox work: understanding the sequence is useful for planning, but execution requires the engine-specific procedures and their dedicated tooling.
guides.why: Small assembly errors have substantial consequences. Incorrect synchronizer orientation can damage engagement parts; incompletely seated shafts can cause noise and heavy shifting; and a binding support or rear case can damage the housing. The checks during assembly establish correct positioning before later components conceal it.

when.summary: When established repair needs require internal MT82 inspection or replacement of worn or damaged components.
notes: Noise or difficult selection alone does not identify the failed part.
Follow the removal, disassembly, assembly and installation procedures for the same engine throughout the job.

prepare.title: Arrange specialist handling and bench equipment
prepare.detail: Provide secure underbody access, a transmission jack with safety strap, a transmission holding fixture, hydraulic press, the specified pullers and installers, and an assistant for the holding and pressing operations. Use protective gloves when handling sharp components.

prepare.title: Control dust and organize components
prepare.detail: Use approved friction-dust removal methods; never blow clutch dust away with compressed air. Keep synchronizer components in their original order and provide a way to preserve sleeve-to-hub index marks.

prepare.title: Prepare engine-matched materials and replacement parts
prepare.detail: Obtain new input and output shaft seals and a replacement countershaft bolt cover. Use the fluid, threadlock and gasket maker specified by the applicable assembly article. The 2.3L tooling includes additional puller-adapter, front-detent access and input-seal installation requirements.

steps.title: Remove the transmission using the engine-specific access sequence
steps.body: Follow the [2.3L removal](#/document/G1687341), [3.7L removal](#/document/G1695873) or [5.0L removal](#/document/G1695875). Disconnect the battery and support the transmission before gearshift-lever and crossmember removal. Remove the starter and release wiring; drain the fluid because disassembly is planned. The 2.3L also requires converter-support, inspection-cover and coolant-tube-bracket access. The 5.0L requires the right catalytic converter and left heated oxygen and catalyst-monitor sensors to be removed in the stated order. Disconnect the clutch hydraulic tube, strap the gearbox to the jack, withdraw it from the clutch and lower it.

steps.title: Mount the gearbox and strip the external components
steps.body: Use the [2.3L disassembly](#/document/G1687342), [3.7L disassembly](#/document/G1708820) or [5.0L disassembly](#/document/G1709101). Clean the gearbox and secure it in the holding fixture. Remove and inspect the slave cylinder, retaining any fitted spacer. Discard the input seal and countershaft bolt cover, using the prescribed shallow drilling method for the cover. Select fourth gear and use the holding tools and assistant to remove the countershaft bolt. Remove the output flange, discard its seal, then remove the sensor, switch, reverse-fork pivots and detents.

steps.title: Open the case and inspect the lower-gear assemblies
steps.body: Pull off the rear case with the specified equipment. Select neutral and align the rail grooves with the interlock before removing the reverse fork and rail. Remove the shift shaft and work through reverse, first and second gear components in order. Record synchronizer-ring positions and index-mark the first/second sleeve to its hub. Inspect gears, needle bearings, synchronizers, forks and rails as they become accessible. Pull the center support evenly to protect both it and the case.

steps.title: Release the shaft assemblies without binding
steps.body: Unlock the center-bearing cage tabs and expand the cages only slightly for removal. Remove the remaining forks and rails. With an assistant, support the case on the specified flat press surfaces and remove the countershaft and output shaft together without binding. The countershaft bolt must already be out. Remove the input shaft only when damage to it, its seal or its bearing requires removal; prevent it from dropping during pressing.

steps.title: Lubricate, install and measure the shafts
steps.body: Begin the [2.3L assembly](#/document/G1708833), [3.7L assembly](#/document/G1687344) or [5.0L assembly](#/document/G1709102). Lubricate components with the specified transmission fluid. During the prescribed bearing-heating operations, never exceed 120°C (248°F). Orient the output roller-bearing cage with its smaller diameter toward the input shaft, and retain the fifth-gear ring and cone with petroleum jelly. Install the shaft assemblies and check both seating depths before proceeding.

steps.title: Secure the center support and selector mechanism
steps.body: Install the third/fourth and fifth/sixth forks and rails, ensuring their pivot bolts actually engage the forks. Follow the temporary two-gear locking sequence, fit the center bearings without overstretching their cages, and loosely fit the support. Tighten the countershaft bolt with the gearbox vertical and input shaft downward. Remove the support, release the two-gear lock, then reinstall and tighten the support evenly. Refit the spring, spacers and interlock plate, checking that the plate moves freely.

steps.title: Rebuild first, second and reverse engagement parts
steps.body: Follow the ring-identification and tab-engagement instructions at each layer. The first/second hub's long shoulder and the sleeve groove face second gear; restore the sleeve-to-hub index marks and pressure pieces. Install the shift shaft in neutral before its stop pin. Fit reverse components and align the rail grooves with the interlock in neutral before installing the reverse fork and rail. For the 2.3L, the reverse sleeve's tapered side faces reverse gear. Refit the magnet.

steps.title: Seal and close the case in fourth gear
steps.body: Select fourth gear before fitting the rear case. Clean mating faces using the specified sealing-surface preparation; metal scrapers, wire brushes and abrasive discs can create leak paths. Apply the prescribed thin coating of gasket maker and install the rear case within 10 minutes. Draw it on evenly with the specified tools, keeping the rails free from binding. Complete pivot-bolt engagement, dowel positioning, case tightening and detent installation in order.

steps.title: Finish the bench assembly
steps.body: Refit the reverse switch, connector retainer and output shaft speed sensor. Install the new output seal and output flange with the specified tools. Clean the flange-bolt threads, apply the prescribed threadlock dot and follow its tighten–loosen–retighten stages. Install the replacement countershaft cover and new input seal, then refit the slave cylinder, its tube and any spacer. If a new synchronizer was installed, add one bottle of XL-18 as specified.

steps.title: Reinstall and restore the operating systems
steps.body: Follow the [2.3L installation](#/document/G1687346), [3.7L installation](#/document/G1695877) or [5.0L installation](#/document/G1695879). Clean the input shaft and apply only the specified small amount of grease to its splines and pilot-bearing surface. Restore the bellhousing attachment, hydraulics, wiring, starter, engine-specific brackets or exhaust components, support and gearshift lever in that article's order. Complete [transmission filling](#/document/G1687327), reconnect the battery, then [fill and bleed the clutch hydraulics](#/document/G1704358).

watchFor.title: Resistance during case or support installation
watchFor.body: Stop and correct shaft seating, rail alignment or uneven loading. Forcing these assemblies can damage the support or housing.

watchFor.title: Misaligned synchronizer tabs
watchFor.body: The tabs must enter their specified gear or hub slots. Ring identification, hub orientation and sleeve index marks are functional assembly requirements.

notes: The 3.7L and 5.0L assembly articles specify Motorcraft Dual Clutch Transmission Fluid XT-11-QDC, WSS-M2C200-D2. The 2.3L article directs fluid selection to its specifications; follow that reference.
The MT82 bearing arrangement does not require preload shims. Correct seating remains essential.

diagnostics.finding: The clutch release bearing feels rough while rotating under pressure.
diagnostics.meaning: The slave-cylinder inspection identifies rough rotation as grounds for replacement.
diagnostics.next: Install a new clutch slave cylinder; also inspect its boot, fluid leakage and bearing condition.

diagnostics.finding: The first/second synchronizer sleeve is worn or damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: The specified repair is replacement of the first/second synchronizer assembly.
diagnostics.next: Replace the assembly and preserve the required installation orientation.

diagnostics.finding: Gears, bearings, synchronizer rings, forks, rails or the center support show wear or damage.
diagnostics.meaning: These inspections determine which internal components require renewal.
diagnostics.next: Replace affected components as directed by the applicable disassembly procedure.

verification.title: Record shaft-seating measurements before closing
verification.body: Record the rear fourth-gear surface at 25.4–38.1 mm below the case deck and the countershaft front surface at 0.635–1.905 mm deeper than its front bearing. Correct an out-of-range result before continuing.

verification.title: Confirm the assembly checkpoints
verification.body: Confirm locked bearing-cage tabs, engaged fork pivots, free interlock movement, correct neutral alignment during reverse installation and fourth-gear selection during case closure.

verification.title: Record final service completion
verification.body: Record transmission filling and clutch bleeding as completed, together with whether new synchronizers required XL-18. Confirm the engine-specific installation sequence and staged flange-bolt tightening are complete.
