guides.title: Diagnose MT82 shifting problems, transmission noise and speed-sensor faults
guides.summary: Separate clutch, linkage, lubrication, internal transmission and output-speed signal faults before choosing a repair.
guides.introduction: The MT82 uses constantly meshed gears and synchronizers to provide smooth gear selection. The clutch disconnects engine drive during shifts, while fifth gear connects the input and output shafts directly. Difficult selection or noise can therefore originate outside the gearbox itself. Diagnosis follows the mechanical drive path first, with a separate electrical test for the output shaft speed sensor.
guides.why: Clutch drag can resemble a synchronizer fault, and driveline noise can sound like transmission damage. Comparing temperature, gear, load and clutch position helps separate these causes. Checking lubricant before driving also prevents a diagnostic road test from worsening a low-fluid condition.

when.summary: Investigate difficult shifts, clutch concerns, leaks, abnormal noise or recorded output-speed sensor faults.
notes: Correct an obvious cause before continuing through further tests.

prepare.title: Arrange mechanical testing
prepare.detail: Use a technician familiar with Ford diagnostics, a controlled area for clutch engagement tests, and suitable road-test conditions. Have a white cloth, cable tie and tape measure available.

prepare.title: Prepare for electrical diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, specified flex probes and engine-matched wiring diagrams. Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Follow the prescribed ignition and connector states for each measurement.

steps.title: Document the concern and inspect lubricant
steps.body: Record the conditions that reproduce the complaint. For noise or leakage, check fluid level before driving using the fluid-level procedure. Examine fluid dripped onto a white cloth for contamination or metal. Low fluid requires investigation of the leak as well as correction of the level.

steps.title: Check clutch hydraulics and pedal reserve
steps.body: Check reservoir level, leaks, pedal binding and floor-mat interference. Attach a tape measure to the lower pedal with a cable tie. Fully depress the clutch, start the engine and select first gear. Record pedal-to-steering-wheel-seam distance, then slowly release until movement begins or engine speed noticeably falls. Reserve of at least 1 in (25mm) passes; less directs diagnosis to the clutch-control chart.

steps.title: Separate clutch slip from selector trouble
steps.body: For the prescribed slip test, idle the engine with the parking brake applied, select fourth, raise speed to 2,000 rpm and slowly release the clutch. Stalling indicates no slip; continued running indicates slip. Inspect the gearshift mechanism for damage, missing or loose fasteners and binding.

steps.title: Compare noise under different operating conditions
steps.body: Follow the parked and road-test sequence in the main procedure. Compare neutral with the clutch pressed and released, note pedal pulsation and changes with engine speed, then evaluate all gears including reverse. In the noisy gear, compare clutch-down operation with the gear retained against coasting in neutral with the clutch released. Match results to the symptom charts.

steps.title: Apply the 3.7L flywheel checks where relevant
steps.body: For the 3.7L dual-mass flywheel branch, check boom during highest-gear acceleration from 1000 rpm to 2000 rpm at wide open throttle and whether it stops on accelerator release. Also assess gentle acceleration from idle to 2000 rpm, clutch cycling at idle in neutral, neutral start-up and neutral shut-down. Excessive rattle, harsh vibration or the specified metallic shut-down noise leads to clutch removal and flywheel inspection, not automatic replacement.

steps.title: Follow the output-speed sensor circuit branch
steps.body: In Pinpoint Test A, monitor the powertrain control module (PCM) parameter identification (PID) OSS_SRC while shifting through the gears. A steady rise and fall with road speed means the fault is not currently present. Otherwise inspect sensor mounting and connections, then test its power supply. A reading above 10.5 volts leads to signal and return checks; a lower reading leads to power-circuit open/short checks. The 3.7L and 5.0L branches additionally isolate camshaft sensors sharing that supply; the 2.3L branch differs.

steps.title: Complete the electrical decision before replacing parts
steps.body: Use the engine-specific connector tables for every circuit measurement. Passing signal and return open/short checks directs sensor replacement; failed checks direct wiring repair. The PCM branch requires connector inspection, repair and an operating recheck. If the concern remains, check applicable Ford service articles before following the PCM replacement decision.

watchFor.title: Low fluid or excessive heat
watchFor.body: Do not drive with low transmission fluid. Change lubricant immediately if exposure above 135°C (275°F) lasted more than 20 minutes.

watchFor.title: Misidentified leakage
watchFor.body: Identify the fluid source. Clean exposed surfaces, check vent breathing and inspect for fresh leakage before condemning a seal or case.

notes: Internal bearing failure leads to removal, disassembly, cleaning and inspection. The bearing-failure branch requires preload resetting if new tapered bearings are installed.
The linked output shaft speed sensor replacement procedure applies to the 2.3L engine.

diagnostics.finding: Selection is difficult only when cold.
diagnostics.meaning: Higher cold selection effort can be normal.
diagnostics.next: Reassess when warm. Persistent difficulty requires lubricant, clutch-release, pilot-bearing and internal selector checks.

diagnostics.finding: The clutch drags, chatters or has abnormal pedal effort.
diagnostics.meaning: Hydraulic faults, binding, contamination or friction-component damage can cause different versions of this complaint.
diagnostics.next: Follow the matching clutch chart; bleed when directed, inspect for leaks and repair any contamination source.

diagnostics.finding: A gear will not select, the transmission stays in gear or it jumps out.
diagnostics.meaning: Linkage, rail/interlock, synchronizer, mounting or pilot-bearing faults require different inspections.
diagnostics.next: Use the exact symptom row. A reverse-only problem also calls for checking a reverse-lamp switch ball stuck extended.

diagnostics.finding: Noise changes with clutch position, load or gear.
diagnostics.meaning: Gear rollover disappears with clutch disengagement or gear engagement; release-bearing rub disappears with clutch engagement. Light-acceleration first/second-gear rattle and mild extreme-speed whine can be acceptable.
diagnostics.next: Compare like vehicles where directed. Loaded growl, hissing or knocking warrants gear/bearing investigation; coast rumble also requires driveline-angle and driveshaft checks.

diagnostics.finding: Rearward howl or whine occurs at full operating temperature.
diagnostics.meaning: The apparent transmission noise may originate elsewhere.
diagnostics.next: At complaint speeds, use fifth gear’s direct drive comparison. Persistent noise directs suspension diagnosis; absent noise leads back to gear-noise analysis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0720:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Output speed appears zero while engine speed and load indicate acceleration; this code illuminates the malfunction indicator lamp.
diagnostics.next: Follow Pinpoint Test A rather than assuming sensor failure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0721:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The output-speed signal is erratic.
diagnostics.next: Use the drive-cycle signal check and subsequent circuit tests.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0722:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A no-signal fault accompanies P0720 and can be stored after a single faulty drive cycle without independently illuminating the malfunction indicator lamp.
diagnostics.next: Follow Pinpoint Test A.

verification.title: Repeat the relevant operating check
verification.body: Confirm whether the original concern remains under its recorded conditions. For the electrical branch, verify steady OSS_SRC changes with vehicle speed.

verification.title: Record the evidence
verification.body: Keep pedal-reserve measurements, fluid findings, noise comparisons and circuit results with the resulting repair decision. A fault absent during testing is not a confirmed failed component.

guides.title: Overhaul the MT82 countershaft assembly
guides.summary: Disassemble and inspect the MT82 countershaft, then rebuild its gears, needle bearings and synchronizer components in the required order.
guides.introduction: The MT82 countershaft carries gears that transfer torque between the transmission shafts. Its third- and fourth-gear synchronizer assembly matches rotational speeds during selection before locking the selected gear to the countershaft. This bench overhaul exposes the gears, bearings, synchronizer rings and shaft so worn or damaged components can be replaced.
guides.why: Correct press support protects the shaft and gear teeth, while ring orientation and tab engagement determine whether the synchronizers assemble correctly. A misplaced needle bearing can be damaged during pressing even when the outside of the assembly appears properly aligned.

when.summary: When transmission investigation requires countershaft inspection or replacement of its damaged components.
notes: This work starts with the countershaft available for bench disassembly; gearbox removal and case assembly are separate phases.
Replace components according to their inspected condition.

prepare.title: Arrange specialist press capability
prepare.detail: Use a hydraulic press, bearing separator, installer 308-130 (T87T-7025-DH), and handle 205-153 (T80T-4000-W). Removing fifth and sixth gears may require up to 18,000 pounds of force. Do not heat the gears.

prepare.title: Prepare lubricants and component tracking
prepare.detail: Have Motorcraft Dual Clutch Transmission Fluid XT-11-QDC meeting WSS-M2C200-D2, plus petroleum jelly for retaining the third-gear needle bearing. Keep synchronizer components organized and record their positions before removal.

steps.title: Set up the countershaft safely
steps.body: Follow the tooling arrangements in the [countershaft procedure](#/document/G1687361). Hand-tighten the bearing puller and support the countershaft throughout press operations to protect the shaft and gears.

steps.title: Press off fifth and sixth gears
steps.body: Remove fifth gear using the specified tools, bearing separator and press, then remove sixth gear using its specified setup. Inspect each gear for wear or damage and replace it as necessary.

steps.title: Remove the third-gear components
steps.body: Remove third gear and its needle bearing, inspecting both. Note the synchronizer ring positions before removing the third-gear ring assembly. Inspect every ring component and replace worn or damaged parts.

steps.title: Strip and inspect the fourth-gear group
steps.body: Remove the third/fourth synchronizer snap ring, then press off fourth gear and the synchronizer assembly with the specified tooling. Note ring positions before separating fourth gear, its ring assembly and the synchronizer. Inspect each. Remove the fourth-gear needle bearing without overexpanding its cage and inspect it. Check the countershaft for scoring and worn or damaged splines; replace defective components.

steps.title: Begin lubricated assembly
steps.body: Lubricate all components with the specified transmission fluid before assembly. Install the fourth-gear needle bearing without overexpanding its cage.

steps.title: Rebuild the fourth-gear synchronizer group
steps.body: Identify the fourth-gear outer synchronizer ring by its one notch. Fit the ring assembly and fourth gear with the synchronizer sleeve groove facing away from fourth gear. Engage the six ring tabs in the six gear slots and the three ring tabs in the three synchronizer slots. Press the group into place with the bearing separator, then install the snap ring.

steps.title: Prepare third gear and sixth gear
steps.body: Identify the third-gear outer ring by its two notches. Position sixth gear, third gear and the third-gear ring assembly on the bearing separator. Engage the six ring tabs in the gear slots. Apply petroleum jelly to hold the third-gear needle bearing in place and install the bearing.

steps.title: Press the third-gear group into place
steps.body: Keep the third-gear needle bearing from sliding down the countershaft while pressing sixth gear, third gear and the third-gear ring assembly into position. Engage the three synchronizer ring tabs in the three synchronizer assembly slots.

steps.title: Install fifth gear
steps.body: Use the bearing separator and hydraulic press to install fifth gear. Complete the countershaft assembly checks before proceeding with the remaining transmission assembly work.

watchFor.title: Misaligned synchronizer parts
watchFor.body: Incorrect sleeve direction or tabs outside their intended slots can damage the synchronizer and ring assemblies.

watchFor.title: Needle-bearing displacement
watchFor.body: Do not allow the third-gear bearing to slide during pressing. Avoid spreading the fourth-gear bearing cage excessively during either removal or installation.

notes: The third- and fourth-gear ring identification marks differ; preserve that distinction throughout the rebuild.
The specified transmission fluid is also the assembly lubricant for this MT82 procedure.

diagnostics.finding: A gear, needle bearing or synchronizer component shows wear or damage.
diagnostics.meaning: That component requires a replacement decision based on its inspected condition.
diagnostics.next: Install a new component as necessary before rebuilding the countershaft.

diagnostics.finding: The shaft is scored or its splines are worn or damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: Renewing surrounding gears alone does not address the shaft defect.
diagnostics.next: Replace the countershaft as necessary.

verification.title: Assembly relationships
verification.body: Confirm the ring identities, sleeve-groove direction, tab engagement and snap-ring installation during assembly, before later components conceal them.

verification.title: Record the bench result
verification.body: Record which components were replaced and confirm that the third-gear needle bearing remained in position during pressing.

procedures.purpose: Complete MT82 countershaft subassembly disassembly, inspection and press assembly.

guides.title: Overhaul the MT82 output-shaft sixth-gear and synchronizer assembly
guides.summary: Strip the removed MT82 output shaft, inspect its sixth-gear components and rebuild the assembly with correct lubrication and synchronizer alignment.
guides.introduction: The MT82 output shaft carries drive toward the transmission output. Its fifth/sixth synchronizer provides two different connections: fifth gear locks the input and output shafts together for direct drive, while sixth locks sixth gear to the output shaft. This bench job services that synchronizer assembly, sixth gear, its needle bearing and the associated shaft surfaces.
guides.why: A press can damage sound parts if its force is carried through an unsupported shaft or poorly positioned separator. Assembly also depends on the synchronizer ring sitting in the correct slots. Lubrication protects the contacting surfaces during assembly, but it cannot compensate for worn splines, a damaged bearing race or incorrect ring alignment.

when.summary: When transmission dismantling calls for inspection or repair of the output-shaft sixth-gear assembly.
notes: This sequence begins with the output-shaft subassembly removed; vehicle removal and transmission case dismantling are separate operations.

prepare.title: Press-work capability
prepare.detail: Use a hydraulic press and bearing separator with suitable support for the output shaft. Hand-tighten the separator to avoid damaging the gear.

prepare.title: Assembly lubricant
prepare.detail: Have Motorcraft Dual Clutch Transmission Fluid XT-11-QDC, specification WSS-M2C200-D2, ready to lubricate every component before reassembly.

prepare.title: Inspection and replacement planning
prepare.detail: Keep the gear, needle bearing, synchronizer ring, cone and retainers identifiable as they are removed. Replacement decisions follow the condition of each component.

steps.title: Remove the synchronizer assembly
steps.body: Remove the fifth/sixth synchronizer snap ring. With the shaft supported and the separator hand-tightened, use the hydraulic press to remove the synchronizer assembly. Inspect the assembly and the sixth-gear synchronizer ring and cone for wear or damage.

steps.title: Strip and inspect sixth gear
steps.body: Remove sixth gear, followed by its needle bearing. Inspect each separately and replace worn or damaged parts. Keeping these decisions separate avoids treating a damaged bearing as evidence that every adjacent component needs replacement.

steps.title: Assess the shaft and pocket-bearing race
steps.body: Inspect the output shaft for scoring and worn or damaged splines; replace the shaft when necessary. Inspect the pocket-bearing inner race. If that race is damaged, remove its snap ring and fit a new inner race.

steps.title: Lubricate and align the synchronizer parts
steps.body: Lubricate all components with the specified fluid. Position the fifth/sixth synchronizer assembly on the bearing separator and press as directed, then install the sixth-gear synchronizer ring and cone. All three ring tabs must engage the three assembly slots.

steps.title: Rebuild the sixth-gear stack
steps.body: Install the sixth-gear needle bearing and sixth gear in the prescribed order. Use the separator and hydraulic press to install the fifth/sixth synchronizer assembly and sixth gear, maintaining shaft support throughout.

steps.title: Restore retention
steps.body: Install the fifth/sixth synchronizer assembly snap ring. Confirm the retainer is installed and the required ring-to-slot alignment has been maintained before the subassembly returns to transmission assembly.

watchFor.title: Misaligned synchronizer tabs
watchFor.body: Pressing together parts with the ring tabs outside their slots can damage both the ring and synchronizer assembly.

watchFor.title: Excessive separator clamping
watchFor.body: The separator is hand-tightened; additional clamping force risks gear damage.

notes: The MT82's input and output shafts share an axis. The overview illustration shows the broader shaft arrangement, not the press setup.

diagnostics.finding: Scoring or worn or damaged output-shaft splines.
diagnostics.meaning: The shaft itself requires a replacement decision, independent of the removable sixth-gear components.
diagnostics.next: Install a new output shaft as necessary.

diagnostics.finding: Damage confined to the pocket-bearing inner race.
diagnostics.meaning: The procedure provides a separate inner-race replacement operation.
diagnostics.next: Remove its snap ring and replace the race.

verification.title: Confirm assembly details
verification.body: Check component lubrication, synchronizer tab engagement and installation of the synchronizer snap ring.

verification.title: Record inspection decisions
verification.body: Record the condition and replacement decision for the shaft, gear, needle bearing, synchronizer components and pocket-bearing race.

Fifth- and sixth-gear powerflow and identification of output-shaft components.

guides.title: Disassemble and reassemble an MT82 synchronizer
guides.summary: Separate and rebuild the MT82 synchronizer subassembly while preserving the original positions of its sleeve, hub, pressure detents and removable endstops.
guides.introduction: Synchronizers help match rotational speeds before a sliding sleeve engages the selected drive path. In the MT82 manual transmission, shift forks move those sleeves to establish the chosen gear. This bench operation concerns the synchronizer hub, sleeve and pressure detents, including sleeve endstops where they are removable.
guides.why: The central requirement is to preserve the installed relationship of the parts. Small endstops can fall away during separation, losing the information needed for correct refitting. Recording positions before movement is therefore part of the repair, rather than something to reconstruct once the parts are scattered on the bench.

when.summary: When an MT82 synchronizer requires subassembly work during transmission repair.
notes: Begin after the synchronizer has been made accessible through the appropriate transmission and shaft disassembly procedures.
This is a bench subassembly operation within gearbox work.

prepare.title: Provide gearbox bench-work capability
prepare.detail: The technician must be able to identify the synchronizer components and retain their installed relationships throughout separation and assembly.

prepare.title: Arrange position records and parts control
prepare.detail: Have a way to note or mark installed positions and keep the sleeve, hub, pressure detents and any removable endstops associated with their original assembly.

steps.title: Record the assembled relationships
steps.body: Before removing anything, note or mark the installed positions of the sleeve, pressure detents and hub. Use the [synchronizer procedure](#/document/G1687363) to identify the parts; do not rely on remembering their positions after separation.

steps.title: Separate the components without losing endstop positions
steps.body: Disassemble the sleeve, pressure detents and hub while preserving the recorded relationships. Where endstops are removable, prevent them from dropping off the sleeve, record their installed positions and then remove them. Do not assume every sleeve has removable endstops.

steps.title: Hold removable endstops during refitting
steps.body: Where applicable, install and hold the endstops on the synchronizer sleeve. Keep them in place as the sleeve is installed on the hub, so the small parts retain their intended relationship during assembly.

steps.title: Restore the original arrangement
steps.body: Reassemble the hub, sleeve and pressure detents in their original positions. Compare the completed arrangement with the notes or marks made before disassembly before returning the subassembly to the surrounding transmission assembly work.

watchFor.title: Endstops falling away unnoticed
watchFor.body: Control them during separation so their original positions remain known.

watchFor.title: Treating all MT82 synchronizers as identical
watchFor.body: First and second gears use triple synchronizers, third and fourth use double synchronizers, and fifth, sixth and reverse use single synchronizers.

notes: The sleeve establishes the drive connection under shift-fork movement; fifth gear uses its sleeve to connect the input and output shafts for direct drive.

verification.title: Compare against the position record
verification.body: Confirm that the hub, sleeve and pressure detents occupy their recorded original positions.

verification.title: Account for removable endstops
verification.body: Confirm that each removed endstop has been refitted and retained during sleeve-to-hub assembly.

guides.title: Service MT82 case bearings and the shift-shaft seal
guides.summary: Remove, inspect and refit MT82 case bearings, reverse-idler components and the shift-shaft seal using controlled heating and correct bearing orientation.
guides.introduction: The MT82 transmission case supports the bearings that locate its rotating shafts. Its shift-shaft seal retains fluid around the selector shaft, while the reverse idler helps reverse output rotation. This job begins with stripped case halves on the bench and ends with serviced case subassemblies ready for continued transmission assembly.
guides.why: Correct bearing orientation protects the case, and controlled heating assists installation without overheating the housing. Lubrication, specified threadlock and accurate tightening preserve the assembled components and their retention.

when.summary: During stripped-case overhaul when bearings or shift components show wear, or the shift-shaft seal leaks.
notes: Vent-tube, clutch-tube clip and shift-shaft detent removal are conditional steps for case replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange specialist bench capability
prepare.detail: Have the specified bearing tools and handle, brass drift, soft-faced hammer, heat gun and torque wrench. Case replacement also requires detent remover 308-812 and a slide hammer.

prepare.title: Confirm assembly materials
prepare.detail: Obtain the recommended transmission fluid and threadlock from the MT82 specifications. Plan controlled case heating and component inspection before beginning installation.

steps.title: Remove the input and countershaft bearings
steps.body: Remove the retaining bolts, then use tool 308-202 with handle 205-153 to remove the input shaft bearing and countershaft bearing. Inspect each for wear or damage and install replacements as necessary.

steps.title: Release retained hardware and the reverse idler
steps.body: If replacing the case, remove the clutch slave-cylinder tube retaining clip and vent tube. Use a brass drift to tap the dowel pins flush with the case. Remove the reverse-idler bolt and assembly; inspect its gear, needle bearing and shaft individually.

steps.title: Remove the output bearing and conditional parts
steps.body: Remove the output-bearing retaining bolts and extract the bearing with 307-664 and handle 205-153. Inspect it for wear or damage. For case replacement, remove the shift-shaft detent with 308-812 and a slide hammer. Remove the shift-shaft seal if leakage is present.

steps.title: Clean and inspect before assembly
steps.body: Clean and inspect both case halves. Inspect the shift shaft and shift-rail bearing, replacing worn or damaged components as necessary. Lubricate all components with the recommended transmission fluid before reassembly.

steps.title: Refit the seal, detent and output bearing
steps.body: Install the shift-shaft seal if removed, then reinstall a removed detent with a soft-faced hammer. Heat the case without exceeding 120°C (248°F). Install the output bearing using 307-541 and handle 205-153, with the outer-race groove facing inside. Apply specified threadlock and tighten its retaining bolts to 36 Nm.

steps.title: Reassemble the reverse idler
steps.body: Install the shaft, gear and needle bearing, followed by the bracket. Apply specified threadlock to the bracket bolt and tighten it to 27 Nm. This restores the supported idler assembly in the reverse power path.

steps.title: Install the countershaft and input bearings
steps.body: Heat the case again within the same maximum limit. Use 307-557 with handle 205-153 for the countershaft bearing, then 307-626 with that handle for the input bearing. Face the input bearing’s outer-race groove inward. Apply threadlock and tighten the bearing retaining bolts to 36 Nm.

steps.title: Restore the vent and tube clip
steps.body: If removed, lightly lubricate the vent-tube O-ring with recommended transmission fluid and install the tube with its notch toward the front of the case. Refit the clutch slave-cylinder tube retaining clip if removed.

watchFor.title: Excessive case temperature
watchFor.body: Heating above 120°C (248°F) can damage the transmission case.

watchFor.title: Reversed bearing orientation
watchFor.body: The input and output bearings require their outer-race grooves facing inside the case; incorrect orientation can cause case damage.

notes: The MT82 bearing arrangement requires neither preload adjustment nor shims.
Complete gearbox assembly and vehicle installation remain separate stages after this case-subassembly work.

diagnostics.finding: A removed bearing or reverse-idler component shows wear or damage.
diagnostics.meaning: That component requires a replacement decision based on its condition.
diagnostics.next: Install new affected components as necessary before case-subassembly completion.

diagnostics.finding: Leakage is present at the shift-shaft seal.
diagnostics.meaning: The seal requires attention during case service.
diagnostics.next: Remove it during disassembly and complete the specified seal installation during assembly.

verification.title: Check the completed subassemblies
verification.body: Confirm input/output bearing groove orientation, reverse-idler assembly, and restoration of any removed seal, detent, vent and clip. Check vent-notch direction.

verification.title: Record the assembly results
verification.body: Record inspected and renewed components, compliance with the heating limit, threadlock application and final retaining-bolt and bracket-bolt tightening.

procedures.purpose: MT82 transmission-case bearing/seal disassembly, supported cleaning and inspection, and subassembly installation for 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications.
MT82 shaft and bearing arrangement, including the absence of preload shims.
Identify transmission-case components and understand the reverse-idler power path.

guides.title: Replace the MT82 input shaft seal — 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L
guides.summary: Remove the clutch slave cylinder, extract and discard the input shaft seal, and install its replacement with the engine-specific service-tool arrangement.
guides.introduction: The MT82 is a fully synchronized six-speed manual transmission. Its input shaft receives drive through the clutch, and the input shaft seal retains transmission fluid where that shaft passes through the front housing. The seal sits behind the clutch slave cylinder, so this repair combines a clutch-control access operation with a short, specialized seal replacement. It does not require the geartrain disassembly described by a transmission overhaul.
guides.why: Extraction and installation use different tools because they perform different jobs: the remover pulls out the old seal, while the installer places the replacement in the housing. The 2.3L application requires an additional input-seal installer alongside the front-seal installer. That distinction must be preserved even though the three engine procedures otherwise follow the same sequence.

when.summary: When an MT82 input shaft seal has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Establish the source of any fluid leakage before committing to seal replacement.
Choose the installation procedure by engine as well as transmission type.

prepare.title: Plan the access work
prepare.detail: Arrange a workshop capable of completing the linked clutch slave cylinder removal and installation procedure and working at the exposed transmission front housing. Treat that prerequisite as part of the overall job.

prepare.title: Prepare the extraction tools
prepare.detail: All three applications require input shaft seal remover 308-375 and a slide hammer. Have a replacement seal available because the removed seal is discarded.

prepare.title: Prepare the correct installation tools
prepare.detail: The 3.7L and 5.0L use front seal installer 308-806. The 2.3L uses 308-806 together with input shaft seal installer 308-937.

steps.title: Confirm the transmission and engine branch
steps.body: Confirm that the vehicle has the MT82 and select the matching engine procedure. The transmission identification tag is on its right-hand side near the driveshaft flange if identification is needed.

steps.title: Remove the clutch slave cylinder
steps.body: Complete [Clutch Slave Cylinder](#/document/G1701833) removal before working on the seal. This clears the component fitted ahead of the seal and provides the required access for the extraction tool.

steps.title: Extract and discard the old seal
steps.body: Use remover 308-375 with a slide hammer as shown in the selected seal procedure. Remove the input shaft seal and discard it; the installation phase calls for its replacement.

steps.title: Install the replacement with the correct tool combination
steps.body: For the [2.3L](#/document/G1708838), use installers 308-806 and 308-937 together. For the [3.7L](#/document/G1687336) or [5.0L](#/document/G1709100), use installer 308-806. Follow the corresponding illustrated arrangement to position the new seal.

steps.title: Refit the clutch slave cylinder
steps.body: Return to the linked clutch slave cylinder procedure and complete its installation. The seal operation ends with the slave cylinder refitted; its installation requirements remain part of completing this repair.

watchFor.title: Missing the additional 2.3L installer
watchFor.body: The 2.3L installation specifies both 308-806 and 308-937. The single-installer arrangement shown for the other engines must not be substituted.

watchFor.title: Underestimating access
watchFor.body: Having the seal tools ready does not complete the clutch slave cylinder prerequisite. Plan the access and restoration work before starting extraction.

notes: Use the installation-tool arrangement shown in the procedure for your engine.
This repair replaces a sealing component; it does not alter the transmission’s synchronizers, bearings or internal gear selection mechanism.

verification.title: Confirm the seal replacement
verification.body: Verify that the removed seal was discarded and the replacement was installed using the tool arrangement specified for the fitted engine.

verification.title: Confirm completion of the prerequisite procedure
verification.body: Check that clutch slave cylinder installation is complete before treating the seal repair as finished.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L MT82 input shaft seal removal and installation using 308-806 with 308-937.
3.7L MT82 input shaft seal removal and installation using 308-806.
5.0L MT82 input shaft seal removal and installation using 308-806.
Required clutch slave cylinder removal for seal access and installation after seal replacement.

guides.title: Replace the MT82 manual transmission output shaft seal
guides.summary: Replace the rear output seal by removing the driveshaft and flange, then reinstall the flange with its prescribed tooling and bolt-tightening sequence.
guides.introduction: The MT82 output shaft delivers transmission torque through the rear flange to the driveshaft. A seal in the rear transmission case retains lubricant around this rotating connection. Access requires removing the flange and temporarily removing the transmission crossmember, while leaving the internal gears assembled. The job is therefore as much about secure support and correct flange installation as it is about replacing the seal.
guides.why: Once the crossmember is removed, the transmission needs a strapped transmission jack to carry and stabilize it. Dedicated installers control placement of the new seal and flange. The flange bolt also has a specific tighten–loosen–retighten sequence and thread-locking preparation; simply tightening it once to a final value does not complete the prescribed installation.

when.summary: When the MT82 output shaft seal has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Fluid near the rear flange warrants identifying its origin before selecting this repair.
This procedure applies to the MT82 installation covered for 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L engines.

prepare.title: Provide supported underbody access
prepare.detail: Arrange safe vehicle access for driveshaft removal and a transmission jack with a safety strap. Have the separate driveshaft procedure available.

prepare.title: Gather the removal and installation tools
prepare.detail: Use a two-leg puller for flange removal; handle 205-153 with rear-seal installer 308-811; flange installers 308-808 and 308-809; and companion-flange tool 308-938 for the flange bolt.

prepare.title: Prepare the replacement seal and fastener supplies
prepare.detail: Have a new output shaft seal, suitable torque equipment and the thread-locking adhesive specified through the primary procedure's Specifications reference. The removed seal must be discarded.

steps.title: Remove the driveshaft
steps.body: Follow the [driveshaft removal procedure](#/document/G2214904) to expose the transmission output flange. Its separate installation requirements remain part of completing this repair.

steps.title: Support the transmission before removing its mounting
steps.body: Place the transmission on the transmission jack and secure it with the safety strap. Remove the bolts, transmission support insulator and crossmember only after this support is established.

steps.title: Remove the flange and old seal
steps.body: Remove the output shaft flange bolt, then withdraw the flange with the two-leg puller. Remove and discard the output shaft seal, following the [seal procedure](#/document/G1687337).

steps.title: Install the new seal and flange
steps.body: Place the new seal on handle 205-153 and installer 308-811, then install it with those tools. Install the output shaft flange using tools 308-808 and 308-809. The seal and flange use different installation arrangements.

steps.title: Prepare and tighten the flange bolt
steps.body: Fit tool 308-938. Clean the output shaft bolt threads and apply one dot of the specified thread-locking adhesive to their lower end. Tighten to 200 Nm, loosen five turns, then tighten to 180 Nm.

steps.title: Restore the mounting and driveshaft
steps.body: Install the support insulator and crossmember. Use the primary procedure's illustrated fastener locations to apply the correct torque to each bolt group. Reinstall the driveshaft using its linked procedure.

watchFor.title: Support interrupted during the repair
watchFor.body: Keep the transmission supported and strapped while its normal crossmember support is removed.

watchFor.title: Fastener groups confused
watchFor.body: The support mounting has separate torque callouts. Identify their illustrated positions rather than applying one value to every bolt.

notes: Tool 308-809 is named a synchronizer gear-pack installer, but this operation uses it for flange installation; internal gear disassembly is not part of the sequence.

verification.title: Record the flange-bolt installation
verification.body: Record completion of thread preparation, adhesive application and all three tightening stages.

verification.title: Confirm restored support and driveline attachment
verification.body: Confirm the support insulator and crossmember fasteners were tightened at their correct locations and driveshaft installation is complete.

procedures.purpose: MT82 output shaft seal removal and installation, including flange tooling and staged bolt tightening.
Driveshaft removal for seal access and installation after transmission support is restored.

guides.title: Replace the output shaft speed sensor on the 2.3L MT82
guides.summary: Drain the MT82, replace its output shaft speed sensor and restore the electrical connection and specified transmission fill.
guides.introduction: The output shaft speed (OSS) sensor monitors rotation at the transmission's output. On the 2.3L EcoBoost MT82 manual transmission, it is an externally mounted component retained by a bolt and connected to the vehicle wiring. Replacement leaves the internal gears assembled, but the procedure requires draining and refilling the transmission.
guides.why: This repair combines a small electrical component with transmission-fluid service. The vehicle must be safely supported and level for the work, and the sensor fastener has a different tightening requirement from the fluid plugs. Completing the sensor installation without restoring the transmission fill would leave an essential part of the job unfinished.

when.summary: When diagnosis or an established repair calls for OSS sensor removal or replacement on the 2.3L MT82.
notes: The removal procedure does not establish which symptoms or electrical faults justify sensor replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange safe, level access
prepare.detail: Use a vehicle hoist and the linked jacking and lifting procedure. The vehicle must be in neutral and level for the fluid service.

prepare.title: Prepare for draining and filling
prepare.detail: Have fluid collection equipment, a fluid suction gun, suitable hand tools and torque tools. Establish the applicable MT82 fluid specification and filling requirements before draining.

steps.title: Position the vehicle
steps.body: With the transmission in neutral, position the vehicle on the hoist using the lifting procedure. Maintain a level attitude for the subsequent draining and filling operations.

steps.title: Drain and remove the sensor
steps.body: Remove the transmission drain plug and drain the fluid. Disconnect the OSS electrical connector, then remove the retaining bolt and sensor. The illustration identifies the sensor and its bolt on the transmission housing.

steps.title: Install and reconnect the sensor
steps.body: Install the sensor and its retaining bolt, tightening the bolt to 10 Nm. Reconnect the OSS electrical connector. Follow the dedicated 2.3L sensor procedure for this removal and installation phase.

steps.title: Restore the transmission fill
steps.body: Refit the drain plug and tighten it to 35 Nm. Following Transmission Draining and Filling, remove the fill plug and use a fluid suction gun to fill with the specified transmission fluid. Install the fill plug and tighten it to 35 Nm. Use the applicable specifications for the fill rather than assuming a quantity.

watchFor.title: Confusing the tightening values
watchFor.body: The sensor bolt uses 10 Nm; the drain and fill plugs use 35 Nm. These are separate fastener requirements.

watchFor.title: An unfinished fluid service
watchFor.body: Draining is part of sensor removal here. Refilling and installing the fill plug are required before the repair is complete.

notes: The MT82 overview describes its fluid as lasting the transmission's service life without a routine service change; draining here is required by the sensor repair.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical completion
verification.body: Check that the sensor bolt is tightened, the electrical connector is connected, both plugs are installed at their specified torque and the prescribed fill is complete.

procedures.purpose: OSS sensor removal and installation specifically for the 2.3L EcoBoost MT82.
Required vehicle jacking and hoist-positioning guidance before underbody access.
MT82 draining and filling sequence, level-vehicle requirement, suction-gun use and fluid-plug tightening.

guides.title: Replace the MT82 transmission support insulator
guides.summary: Support and strap the installed MT82 transmission while removing its support insulator, then refit the assembly with the specified bolt and nut torques.
guides.introduction: The transmission support insulator forms part of the mounting for the MT82 six-speed manual gearbox. It carries support loads while limiting direct vibration transfer into the vehicle structure. This repair exchanges the external support component while a transmission jack controls the gearbox during removal and refitting.
guides.why: Removing a support changes how the transmission is held. The transmission jack carries the assembly during the relevant stage, and the retaining strap secures it to the jack. The insulator’s bolts and nuts have different tightening specifications, so identifying the two fastener groups is part of completing the job correctly.

when.summary: When the MT82 support insulator requires replacement or removal during an established repair.
notes: Confirm the vehicle has the MT82 transmission before using this procedure.

prepare.title: Lifting and transmission support
prepare.detail: Provide a vehicle hoist, transmission jack and retaining strap. The work requires competence in lifting the vehicle and securing the transmission while its support is removed.

prepare.title: Fastener access and torque control
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the insulator nuts and bolts and a torque wrench capable of both installation settings. Keep the two fastener groups identifiable.

steps.title: Position the vehicle on the hoist
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a hoist. Follow the [lifting procedure](#/document/G1663631), using the marked lifting points and checking that hoist adapters clear suspension components and mounting brackets.

steps.title: Remove the nuts and secure the gearbox
steps.body: Follow the [insulator procedure](#/document/G1687338): remove the transmission support insulator nuts, then support the transmission with the transmission jack. Secure the transmission to the jack with the retaining strap before removing the insulator bolts.

steps.title: Remove the insulator
steps.body: With the transmission supported and strapped, remove the support insulator bolts and the insulator. Maintain controlled support while the mounting component is absent.

steps.title: Install and tighten the support
steps.body: Install the insulator and its bolts, tightening the bolts to 76 lb.ft (103 Nm). Then install the insulator nuts and tighten them to 52 lb.ft (70 Nm). Complete both fastening stages before withdrawing temporary transmission support.

watchFor.title: Inadequate support
watchFor.body: The required transmission jack and retaining strap work together. Never get beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; the vehicle’s emergency jack is unsuitable for this repair.

notes: Removal releases the nuts before the supported bolt-removal stage. Installation secures the bolts before the nuts.

verification.title: Both fastener groups completed
verification.body: Confirm the bolts received 76 lb.ft (103 Nm) and the nuts received 52 lb.ft (70 Nm), and that the installed support is secure before removing the jack and strap.

procedures.purpose: MT82 transmission support insulator removal and installation for the supplied 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications.
Approved lifting points, hoist positioning and vehicle-support precautions.

guides.title: Overhaul the 5.2L 3160 six-speed manual transmission
guides.summary: Remove, dismantle, assemble and reinstall the 3160 transmission, setting shaft end play and restoring its controls and clutch hydraulics.
guides.introduction: The 3160 transfers engine torque through an input shaft, countershaft and output shaft. Its constantly meshed gears provide different ratios, while synchronizers and shift forks select the power path. Interlocks prevent simultaneous gear engagement. This overhaul opens the gearbox, removes its shaft and selector assemblies, then rebuilds their precise mechanical relationships.
guides.why: Shaft clearance depends on the housing gasket and selected shims. Incorrect clearance changes bearing support, while misaligned synchronizer parts can be damaged during installation. Controlled heating, proper pullers and careful handling of small interlock parts are central to a successful rebuild.

when.summary: When a confirmed internal repair requires transmission removal and bench disassembly.
notes: This is not scheduled fluid maintenance; the gearbox overview specifies no routine service fluid change.
Cooler-tube handling and conditional pump-drive alignment apply where transmission fluid cooling is fitted.

prepare.title: Vehicle and bench support
prepare.detail: Provide a hoist, transmission jack with safety strap, an assistant and transmission holding fixture 307-003. The job requires safe vehicle lifting and specialist gearbox bench capability.

prepare.title: Assembly equipment and materials
prepare.detail: Have the specified flange tools, gear and bearing pullers, seal installers, punch and dial-indicator fixture 100-002. Prepare gaskets, selectable shims, a new output-flange nut, specified grease and PTFE thread sealant. Heat only the designated components, never above 260°F or longer than 15 minutes.

prepare.title: Friction dust
prepare.detail: Do not breathe clutch dust or disperse it with compressed air. Remove it using approved techniques. Keep this precaution separate from solvent cleaning and air drying of transmission components.

steps.title: Open the vehicle access path
steps.body: Follow [transmission removal](#/document/G1794241): disconnect the battery and remove the upper right-hand catalytic-converter nut. Use the matching [3160 gearshift procedure](#/document/G1796480), which includes neutral selection, hoisting, boot and driveshaft removal, and supported transmission lowering. Continue with the support insulator, damper, crossmember, starter, right-hand converter and left-hand catalyst monitor sensor.

steps.title: Disconnect and lower the gearbox
steps.body: Where fitted, move cooler tubes aside and recover any seals or backing rings left in the case. Release wiring and drain the transmission for disassembly. Secure it to the jack, disconnect the vent and clutch hydraulic tube, and record each bellhousing bolt or studbolt location. Withdraw the input shaft from the clutch before lowering the unit.

steps.title: Begin controlled bench disassembly
steps.body: Clean the exterior and use an assistant to mount the gearbox in its fixture. Follow [disassembly](#/document/G1849271): discard the output-flange nut, pull the flange, and remove the external detents, reverse switch and pin, extension housing and slave cylinder. Separate the clutch housing to remove the selector lever, then temporarily reunite the housings as directed.

steps.title: Strip the gear and selector assemblies
steps.body: Use the prescribed pullers to remove the reverse and third/fourth gear stacks, bearings and synchronizers, followed by gates, spacers and detents. Retain the interlock pin when withdrawing the reverse shaft. Keep the 5–6 shaft in neutral and hold the 3–4 shaft while releasing its detent. Remove the remaining fourth gear, case, shift shafts, countershaft, output assembly and input components in sequence.

steps.title: Build the core and measure both shaft clearances
steps.body: Begin [assembly](#/document/G1849280) with the input components, fifth-gear synchronizer, output shaft and forks, countershaft and shift shafts. Fit the clutch-housing gasket and temporarily torque the case bolts as specified. Measure input/output end play at the output shaft. For the separate countershaft check, contact and lift the shorter countershaft. Record both readings and select shims targeting 0.0127–0.0889 mm.

steps.title: Restore interlocks and shift gates
steps.body: Install the plungers, interlock pins and support. Keep the 5–6 shaft neutral and support the 3–4 shaft until its detent secures it. Install the reverse shaft and remaining detents, applying specified thread sealant to the designated plugs. Continue through the heated fourth gear, selector finger, spacers, gates and roll pins in assembly order.

steps.title: Assemble the remaining gear stacks
steps.body: Install the fourth-gear bearing and synchronizer components. Align the upper synchronizer ring with the heated 3–4 hub and maintain alignment as it seats. Match sleeve spline indentations to hub detent slots. Complete the third and reverse assemblies, bearings, races, spacers, retainers and fork roll pins, heating only the components identified in the assembly procedure.

steps.title: Install the selected shims and close the unit
steps.body: Separate the clutch housing again, install the selector lever, pivot and clip, then fit the selected shims beneath the front bearing races. Refit the races, gasket and housing, aligning the cooling-pump drive where applicable. Complete the extension housing, switches, detents and tone wheel. Install shaft seals with the specified tools, fit the flange with its new nut, and reinstall the slave cylinder and tube clip.

steps.title: Reinstall the transmission and its connections
steps.body: Follow [installation](#/document/G1794243). Apply a small amount of specified grease to the cleaned input splines and pilot-bearing surface. Restore bellhousing fasteners to their recorded locations, then hydraulic, vent and electrical connections. Inspect cooler seals and backing rings and replace damaged items. Restore the exhaust components, starter, supports and matched 3160 gearshift assembly, including driveshaft and boot restoration.

steps.title: Restore fluid and hydraulic operation
steps.body: Complete [3160 transmission filling](#/document/G1794233), reconnect the battery using its procedure, and fill and [bleed the clutch hydraulic system](#/document/G1704358). Use the linked procedures for the required filling and bleeding details.

watchFor.title: A shaft can fall into the case
watchFor.body: The 3–4 shift shaft needs support whenever its retaining detent is absent. Losing an interlock pin also compromises correct selector assembly.

watchFor.title: A synchronizer ring catches during installation
watchFor.body: Stop and restore the specified ring-to-hub alignment. Continuing installation with the ring misaligned can damage it.

watchFor.title: Clearance measured without the gasket
watchFor.body: That reading cannot establish the specified end play. Both shaft checks require the clutch-housing gasket to be fitted.

notes: Use the 5.2L/3160 gearshift procedure G1796480 for restoration.
The installation procedure lists MERCON LV fluid at the cooler-seal operation; obtain transmission fill requirements from the dedicated 3160 filling procedure.

diagnostics.finding: A cooler-tube seal or backing ring remains in the transmission case
diagnostics.meaning: The connection has not separated with all its sealing parts accounted for.
diagnostics.next: Remove the retained parts and inspect the seals and backing rings before reconnecting the tubes.

diagnostics.finding: Measured shaft end play does not meet the specified target
diagnostics.meaning: The shim selection must change to establish the required axial clearance.
diagnostics.next: Determine the correct shim with the gasket fitted and install it beneath the appropriate front bearing race.

verification.title: Record the clearance result
verification.body: Keep separate records of input/output and countershaft measurements and their selected shims, documenting the 0.0127–0.0889 mm target for each.

verification.title: Confirm assembly completion
verification.body: Check that the new flange nut, selector retainers, interlocks, housing gaskets, seals and slave-cylinder tube clip have been installed through the assembly sequence.

verification.title: Confirm vehicle restoration
verification.body: Verify completion of the 3160 gearshift and driveshaft restoration, transmission filling, battery connection and clutch hydraulic bleeding.

procedures.purpose: Remove the 5.2L 3160 transmission from the vehicle.
Disassemble the 5.2L 3160 transmission on the bench.
Assemble the 5.2L 3160 transmission and establish shaft end play.
Install the 5.2L 3160 transmission and restore its vehicle connections.
Remove and reinstall the matching 3160 gearshift lever assembly.
Drain and fill the 3160 transmission.
Disconnect and reconnect the battery.
Complete the clutch hydraulic bleeding referenced by transmission installation.

guides.title: Diagnose shifting problems and noise in the 5.2L 3160 manual transmission
guides.summary: Separate fluid, clutch, shift-control, gearbox and driveline concerns before deciding whether the 3160 transmission needs internal repair.
guides.introduction: The 3160 transfers engine torque to the driveshaft through constantly meshed gears, with synchronizers helping the selected gear engage smoothly. Difficult selection or an unfamiliar sound can originate in the clutch, its hydraulics, the shift mechanism or the driveline. Diagnosis establishes which system needs attention before the transmission is removed.
guides.why: Fluid condition, clutch position, selected gear and engine load change what rotates and carries torque. Comparing those conditions is more useful than judging a sound alone: some gear noise is normal, while driving with low lubricant can cause damage.

when.summary: Investigate difficult shifting, gear clash, disengagement, leakage, abnormal noise or clutch-related vibration.
notes: Verify that the reported concern is present before following a component-replacement decision.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a technician familiar with Ford diagnostic methods and controlled road testing. Have the linked fluid procedures and symptom charts available.

prepare.title: Gather observations
prepare.detail: Record operating temperature, affected gears, pedal behavior, load, previous repairs and towing history. Have a white cloth for examining a fluid sample.

steps.title: Establish fluid condition before driving
steps.body: Document the complaint and check fluid level, especially with noise or leakage. Do not drive with a low level. Examine fluid dripped onto a white cloth for contamination or metal. Correct observed causes before continuing; use the linked level-check and draining/filling procedures.

steps.title: Separate clutch and hydraulic concerns
steps.body: Check the clutch reservoir level and investigate leaks if low. Check pedal binding and floor-mat interference. For the prescribed slip test, apply the parking brake, select 4th with the engine idling, raise speed to 2,000 rpm and slowly release the clutch. Stalling indicates no slip; continued running indicates slip.

steps.title: Inspect the external shift mechanism
steps.body: Look for damage, missing or loose fasteners and binding. Correct these before attributing restricted movement to internal rails, forks or synchronizers.

steps.title: Compare parked noise conditions
steps.body: Follow the parked tests with the clutch fully applied and released, observing abnormal pedal pulsation. Compare neutral noise, the prescribed parking-brake-applied movement toward first gear, and changes with engine speed. Record the speed at which a noise diminishes.

steps.title: Compare driving and coasting conditions
steps.body: Evaluate every gear, including reverse. In the loudest gear, compare clutch applied with the gear retained, then clutch applied followed by neutral and clutch released while coasting. For forward-gear noise, also check unwanted component contact and housing-bolt tightness before internal inspection.

steps.title: Distinguish gearbox noise from rear-vehicle noise
steps.body: For apparent rear whine at full operating temperature, repeat the complaint in 5th, which directly couples the input and output shafts. Persistent noise directs investigation toward the suspension/axle path; absent noise directs further gear-noise analysis. Coast-related rumble also warrants driveshaft angle, damage and balance checks.

steps.title: Follow the relevant flywheel test
steps.body: For acceleration boom, the specified test uses highest gear from 1000 rpm to 2000 rpm at wide-open throttle; disappearance on throttle release prompts clutch removal and flywheel inspection. Harsh vibration during gentle acceleration between idle and 2000 rpm has the same next step. Also investigate excessive rattle while slowly cycling the clutch in neutral, rattle during neutral start-up, or harsh metallic noise during the final revolutions at shutdown.

watchFor.title: Overheated lubricant
watchFor.body: Change lubricant immediately if exposure above 135°C (275°F) for more than 20 minutes is suspected.

watchFor.title: Noise that changes with clutch position
watchFor.body: Normal gear rollover disappears with clutch disengagement or gear engagement. Release-bearing rub disappears with clutch engagement; damaged-bearing noise is usually stronger under load or coast.

notes: The fluid has no routine service-change requirement, but overheating or a diagnosed lubricant concern requires corrective action.
Internal inspection, clutch removal and flywheel work are separate procedures requiring the appropriate workshop capability.

diagnostics.finding: Gear selection requires more force only when cold.
diagnostics.meaning: This can be normal.
diagnostics.next: Retest warm before deciding that repair is necessary.

diagnostics.finding: Shifting remains difficult or gears clash.
diagnostics.meaning: Lubricant, pilot-bearing binding, loose pressure-plate bolts, synchronizers or forks may contribute.
diagnostics.next: Use the matching chart branch to inspect the external and internal causes.

diagnostics.finding: The lever moves but no gear engages.
diagnostics.meaning: The lever, selector arm, rail bushings or lever plate may be damaged.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the lever and internal selector components.

diagnostics.finding: One gear is unavailable, or the transmission stays locked in a gear.
diagnostics.meaning: Restricted linkage or internal travel differs from an interlock fault.
diagnostics.next: For reverse alone, check the reverse-lamp switch ball. For a locked gear, inspect gears, rails, forks, synchronizers and interlocks.

diagnostics.finding: The transmission jumps out of gear.
diagnostics.meaning: Mounting, pilot-bearing or internal engagement wear may be responsible.
diagnostics.next: Check mounting bolts, then the specified flywheel and synchronizer/fork/gear inspections.

diagnostics.finding: There is light-acceleration rattle in first or second, or mild whine at extreme speed.
diagnostics.meaning: These can be acceptable gear-contact sounds.
diagnostics.next: Compare the exact operating conditions with the noise, vibration and harshness chart.

diagnostics.finding: Clatter, squeal, loaded growl, hissing or knocking is abnormal.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible causes include reverse-idler wear, backlash, mismatched gears or bearing damage.
diagnostics.next: Use gear and load dependence to select inspection; check metal contamination with heavy-acceleration rumble.

diagnostics.finding: Fresh leakage appears after cleaning.
diagnostics.meaning: Fluid identity, venting, seals, case defects or plug threads need investigation.
diagnostics.next: Identify the fluid, check the vent, operate and reinspect before selecting repair.

diagnostics.finding: Bearing damage is established.
diagnostics.meaning: Lubrication, towing, shaft/bore condition or incorrect preload may underlie the failure.
diagnostics.next: Remove, disassemble and clean as directed; inspect related parts before replacement.

verification.title: Confirm the diagnostic direction
verification.body: Compare the completed road-test observations with both symptom charts and pursue another system if the transmission does not explain the concern.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Document fluid findings, clutch-test outcome, affected gears and how temperature, pedal position, speed and load changed the complaint.

Required diagnostic methods and preliminary-check principles.
3160 transmission fluid-level check.
3160 lubricant draining and filling when indicated.
3160 gearshift-lever removal and installation if damaged.
3160 transmission removal for indicated internal inspection.
3160 bench disassembly for gears, bearings and shift components.
5.2L clutch disc and pressure-plate removal and installation.
5.2L flywheel removal and installation for the specified pilot-bearing/flywheel branches.
5.2L flywheel inspection after the relevant noise or vibration test.
Suspension-system diagnostic route for persistent apparent rear whine.

authoring.method: Codex source review with verified engine-specific access and practical symptom terminology

guides.title: Overhaul the 5.2L 3160 transmission clutch housing
guides.summary: Strip and inspect the clutch housing, then reinstall its oil-pump components and bearing cups to the specified intermediate assembly stage.
guides.introduction: The aluminum clutch housing does more than enclose the clutch end of the transmission. It carries shaft-bearing components, an input-shaft oil seal and an oil pump used for transmission-fluid cooling. Its shift-shaft bearings also help guide the mechanism that selects gears. This job services the housing as a transmission subassembly; it begins with the housing accessible on the bench and ends before the bearing shims are installed.
guides.why: The bearing cups, shims and housing belong to a controlled assembly sequence. Installing the shims prematurely would bypass that sequence. Inspection is equally important: damaged shift-shaft bearings require a new clutch housing under this procedure, rather than an improvised repair to the bearing locations.

when.summary: During transmission overhaul when the clutch housing requires stripping, inspection or replacement.
notes: This is a bench subassembly operation, not a diagnosis of clutch engagement or a complete transmission removal procedure.

prepare.title: Plan for gearbox bench work
prepare.detail: Use a clean work area, suitable component-handling equipment and a torque wrench. The technician must be comfortable handling bearing cups, shims, seals and retaining rings.

prepare.title: Keep components identifiable
prepare.detail: Keep the input-shaft and countershaft bearing components and shims distinguishable as they are removed. Their locations matter when the wider transmission assembly continues.

steps.title: Remove the housing gasket
steps.body: Begin the disassembly sequence in the [clutch-housing procedure](#/document/G1849273) by removing the clutch housing gasket. The illustrated perimeter gasket identifies the joint being opened.

steps.title: Remove the bearing races, shims and seal
steps.body: Remove the front input-shaft and countershaft bearing races and their shims, followed by the input-shaft seal. The paired illustrations identify the bearing-cup locations; they do not establish a replacement shim thickness.

steps.title: Strip the oil-pump components
steps.body: Remove the oil-pump pick-up tube, then the oil-pressure regulator. Remove the snap ring and oil pump last. Following this order separates the oil-handling components before housing inspection.

steps.title: Inspect the shift-shaft bearings
steps.body: Clean the shift-shaft bearings and inspect them for damage. If damage is present, install a new clutch housing. This is the explicit housing-replacement decision in the procedure.

steps.title: Reassemble the oil circuit
steps.body: Install the oil pump and its snap ring, then install the oil-pressure regulator and tighten it to 28 Nm. Install the oil-pump pick-up tube afterward, preserving the stated assembly order.

steps.title: Install the bearing cups without shims
steps.body: Install the input-shaft bearing cup and countershaft bearing cup. Leave the shims out at this stage. The assembly phase supplied for this job ends here; it does not authorize guessing the subsequent shim, seal or gasket installation steps.

watchFor.title: Damaged shift-shaft bearings
watchFor.body: Cleaning alone does not resolve bearing damage. The specified response is clutch-housing replacement.

watchFor.title: Premature completion
watchFor.body: Bearing cups installed without shims represent an intermediate assembly state, not a transmission ready for installation.

notes: The oil pump discussed here is inside the transmission clutch housing; it is separate from the engine oil pump.

diagnostics.finding: Damage found in a cleaned shift-shaft bearing.
diagnostics.meaning: The housing fails the specified inspection.
diagnostics.next: Replace the clutch housing before continuing assembly.

verification.title: Check the assembly stage
verification.body: Confirm the pump and snap ring, regulator, pick-up tube and bearing cups are installed, with the bearing shims still excluded.

verification.title: Record the inspection result
verification.body: Record whether the shift-shaft bearings passed inspection or required a replacement housing.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L 3160 clutch-housing bench disassembly, bearing inspection and partial subassembly reassembly.

guides.title: Service the 3160 manual transmission countershaft bearings
guides.summary: Press the front and rear roller bearings off the removed 3160 countershaft, then install the rear bearing followed by the front bearing.
guides.introduction: The countershaft carries gears that transfer torque between the input and output sides of the 3160 manual transmission. Its bearings support the rotating shaft and help maintain the geartrain’s position. In most forward ratios and in reverse, power passes through the countershaft; fifth gear instead provides direct drive by locking the input and output shafts together. This job is limited to the front and rear roller bearings on an already-removed countershaft.
guides.why: These bearings require hydraulic-press operations, with a bearing separator specified for removal. That makes this specialist bench work rather than an external gearbox repair. Correct support and control of the press operation matter because the load is being applied to fitted bearing and shaft components. The installation order is also explicit: the rear bearing goes on before the front bearing.

when.summary: When an already-removed 3160 countershaft requires front or rear roller-bearing service.
notes: Bearing service must follow a justified overhaul decision; this procedure does not diagnose transmission noise or shifting complaints.
Transmission removal, gearbox disassembly and final gearbox assembly are separate operations.

prepare.title: Confirm the transmission
prepare.detail: Identify the 3160 application before selecting parts and procedures. Its identification tag is on the top right-hand side of the transmission and includes assembly and build information.

prepare.title: Provide specialist bench equipment
prepare.detail: Have a hydraulic press and bearing separator, together with the capability to support and control each bearing operation safely. Do not begin pressing without an established setup for the component.

prepare.title: Keep the bearing positions distinct
prepare.detail: Identify the front and rear bearing locations before disassembly. The component description distinguishes these bearings from other countershaft races, gears and synchronizer parts.

steps.title: Remove the front roller bearing
steps.body: Begin the disassembly phase of the [countershaft procedure](#/document/G1849274). Use the hydraulic press and bearing separator to remove the front roller bearing. This is the first bearing-removal operation specified for the subassembly.

steps.title: Remove the rear roller bearing
steps.body: Use the hydraulic press and bearing separator to remove the rear roller bearing. Keep its location clearly distinguished from the front bearing and from other bearing-related components in the geartrain.

steps.title: Install the rear roller bearing
steps.body: Begin assembly by pressing the rear roller bearing onto the countershaft with the hydraulic press. The accompanying illustration identifies this bearing and its shaft location; it is not a complete press-fixture layout.

steps.title: Install the front roller bearing
steps.body: Use the hydraulic press to install the front roller bearing. This completes the stated countershaft bearing assembly sequence, ready for the remaining transmission assembly operations.

watchFor.title: Uncertain press support
watchFor.body: Resolve the tooling setup before applying force. The bearing illustration does not specify press adapters, support dimensions or force limits.

watchFor.title: Confusing bearings and races
watchFor.body: The transmission contains additional countershaft bearing-related parts. Use the component identification information to avoid treating every listed race or bearing as part of this short operation.

notes: The different power paths through the gearbox explain why operation varies by selected ratio; they do not establish a bearing fault.
This subassembly procedure does not provide final transmission adjustment values or an acceptance test for the assembled gearbox.

verification.title: Confirm the subassembly sequence
verification.body: Confirm that the rear roller bearing and then the front roller bearing have been installed with the hydraulic press.

verification.title: Continue the gearbox overhaul
verification.body: Treat bearing installation as completion of this subassembly operation. Complete the applicable transmission assembly and verification procedures before returning the gearbox to service.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L 3160 countershaft front and rear roller-bearing disassembly and assembly using a press and bearing separator.
3160 transmission overview and identification-tag information.
3160 gear powerflow and identification of countershaft bearings, races and related geartrain components.

guides.title: Remove and install the 5.2L 3160 input-shaft bearing
guides.summary: Use a hydraulic press and bearing separator to remove the input-shaft bearing, then press the roller bearing onto the shaft during assembly.
guides.introduction: The input shaft brings engine torque into the 3160 manual transmission. Most ratios transfer that torque through the countershaft; fifth gear connects the input and output shafts through the synchronizer sleeve for direct drive. The input-shaft bearing supports this rotating assembly. This job covers bearing removal and installation on the bench, with the shaft already accessible outside the assembled gearbox.
guides.why: Bearing service is a controlled pressing operation. The removal phase specifically requires a bearing separator together with the hydraulic press, while installation requires the press. Correct component identification matters because the input-shaft bearing, its housing cup and the adjacent output-shaft front roller bearing are distinct parts.

when.summary: When input-shaft bearing service is required during a 3160 gearbox overhaul.
notes: This operation is not a diagnosis of transmission noise or difficult shifting.

prepare.title: Bench access
prepare.detail: Have the input shaft removed through the applicable gearbox disassembly process. Transmission removal and case dismantling are separate prerequisites.

prepare.title: Press equipment and capability
prepare.detail: Provide a hydraulic press, bearing separator and an operator experienced in transmission-bearing work. Establish a suitable support arrangement before applying force.

steps.title: Identify the bearing on the shaft
steps.body: Use [Input Shaft](#/document/G1849276) and the geartrain identification view to distinguish the bearing being serviced from the separate bearing cup and neighboring output-shaft bearing.

steps.title: Press the bearing off
steps.body: Use the bearing separator with the hydraulic press to remove the input-shaft bearing. The separator is part of the specified removal equipment; the finished-assembly illustration does not establish its positioning or the press support arrangement.

steps.title: Press the roller bearing onto the shaft
steps.body: For assembly, use the hydraulic press to install the input-shaft roller bearing on the input shaft. Follow the illustrated component orientation without inventing a press force or installation-depth measurement.

steps.title: Return the subassembly to gearbox assembly
steps.body: Once the bearing operation is complete, continue through the applicable transmission assembly process. Bearing pressing alone does not establish the completed gearbox’s shim selection or adjustment.

watchFor.title: Treating the photograph as a press setup
watchFor.body: The illustration identifies the installed bearing; it does not show press adapters, support locations or an acceptance measurement.

notes: The bearing procedure provides no press-force, installed-height or clearance specification. Do not substitute an assumed value.

verification.title: Confirm the subassembly
verification.body: Check component identity and orientation against the installation illustration. Any dimensional acceptance must come from the applicable gearbox assembly requirements.

verification.title: Record the scope completed
verification.body: Record bearing removal and installation separately from completion of the remaining transmission assembly and checks.

procedures.purpose: 3160 input-shaft bearing bench disassembly and assembly for the 5.2L application.
3160 powerflow and identification of the input-shaft bearing, bearing cup and adjacent geartrain parts.

guides.title: Rebuild the output-shaft subassembly in the 3160 six-speed manual transmission
guides.summary: Strip and rebuild the output-shaft gears, bearings and synchronizers with controlled pressing, heating and component alignment.
guides.introduction: The 3160 transmission’s output shaft transfers drive toward the rear differential. Its gears remain meshed with their partners, while synchronizer sleeves lock the selected gear to the shaft. The first–second sleeve selects those two ratios; the fifth–sixth sleeve also provides the direct connection between input and output shafts in fifth gear. This job covers the output-shaft bench subassembly after it has been removed from the gearbox.
guides.why: The gears, roller bearings, synchronizer assemblies and detents form an ordered stack. Incorrect sleeve alignment can disrupt the relationship between the sleeve and its detents. The specified heating temporarily expands tightly fitted bearing components for assembly, but excessive temperature or heating time can damage them. This requires gearbox rebuilding experience rather than ordinary external transmission service skills.

when.summary: During a gearbox repair that requires output-shaft gear, bearing or synchronizer disassembly.
notes: The bench procedure begins with the shaft accessible; transmission removal and case disassembly are separate work.

prepare.title: Provide the pressing equipment
prepare.detail: A hydraulic press and bearing separator are required for the specified disassembly operations. The operator must be able to support the assembly appropriately while separating fitted components.

prepare.title: Control heat and component order
prepare.detail: Provide a controlled means of heating and monitoring temperature and time. Arrange the removed components in their working order, keeping synchronizer assemblies and detents identifiable.

steps.title: Remove the sixth-gear end components
steps.body: Remove the snap ring, then the fifth–sixth synchronizer hub, sleeve and detents. Lift off the sixth-gear three-piece synchronizer assembly, sixth gear and its roller bearing in that order.

steps.title: Press off the first-gear group
steps.body: Use the hydraulic press and bearing separator to remove the roller bearing and first gear. Then remove the first-gear roller bearing and its three-piece synchronizer assembly, retaining their order for rebuilding.

steps.title: Separate the second-gear group
steps.body: With the press and bearing separator, remove second gear, the first–second synchronizer hub and sleeve, and the first-gear roller-bearing inner race. Remove the second-gear roller bearing to finish the specified strip.

steps.title: Rebuild second gear and its synchronizer
steps.body: Install the second-gear roller bearing, second gear and its three-piece synchronizer assembly. Install the first–second hub, sleeve and three detents. Align the sleeve’s indented internal splines with the hub’s detent slots.

steps.title: Fit the first-gear bearing race
steps.body: Heat the first-gear bearing race to 260°F and install it on the output shaft. Do not exceed that temperature or heat the component for longer than 15 minutes.

steps.title: Rebuild first gear
