steps.body: Install the first-gear three-piece synchronizer assembly, followed by the roller bearing and first gear. Align the synchronizer with the slot in the gear so the mating features occupy their intended positions.

steps.title: Fit the rear bearing and sixth gear
steps.body: Heat the rear bearing to 260°F and install it, observing the same 15-minute maximum heating time. Install the sixth-gear roller bearing, sixth gear and its three-piece synchronizer assembly.

steps.title: Complete the fifth–sixth synchronizer
steps.body: Install the hub, sleeve and detents, then install the snap ring. Again, align the sleeve’s indented internal splines with the hub’s detent slots. Use the complete output-shaft procedure to check the final component sequence.

watchFor.title: Misaligned sleeve features
watchFor.body: Check the indented splines against the detent slots on both synchronizer hubs before completing assembly.

watchFor.title: Uncontrolled heating
watchFor.body: Both heated components have an explicit temperature and time limit; prolonged heating is not an acceptable way to resolve a fitting problem.

notes: Identify the cause of a gear-selection complaint before committing to an output-shaft rebuild.

verification.title: Check the specified assembly relationships
verification.body: Confirm both sleeve-to-detent alignments, the first-gear synchronizer-to-slot alignment and installation of the final snap ring.

verification.title: Record the controlled assembly
verification.body: Record the bearing-race and rear-bearing heating temperatures and durations before handing the shaft back to the gearbox assembly operation.

procedures.purpose: Complete 3160 output-shaft bench disassembly and assembly, including pressing, heating and synchronizer alignment.
Explain gear powerflow and identify output-shaft gears, bearings, hubs, sleeves and detents.

guides.title: Overhaul the 5.2L 3160 manual transmission case
guides.summary: Prepare the transmission case for reassembly by cleaning its magnet, inspecting the shift shaft bearings and installing the output shaft bearing races.
guides.introduction: The aluminum case supports the working parts of the 3160 six-speed manual transmission. Its bearing races support rotating shafts, while separate shift shaft bearings guide the mechanism that selects gears. This bench operation deals with the stripped case, its guide plate, magnet and bearing races; it is one stage within a transmission overhaul.
guides.why: The shift shaft bearings are a decisive inspection point: damage requires a new transmission case. The output shaft bearing races also use different installation tools, so identifying each location matters before assembly begins.

when.summary: During transmission overhaul when the stripped case requires inspection and bearing-race installation.
notes: Begin with the case accessible as a subassembly; vehicle removal and complete gearbox teardown are separate operations.

prepare.title: Provide transmission bench capability
prepare.detail: This work requires controlled bearing-race removal and installation, component identification and careful inspection of the case bearings.

prepare.title: Have the specified tools ready
prepare.detail: Use a punch or drift for race removal. Installation requires handle 205-153, center support bearing installer 307-655 and differential bearing cup installer 308-163.

steps.title: Remove the guide plate and bearing races
steps.body: Following the disassembly phase of the [case procedure](#/document/G1849278), remove the guide plate bolt and plate. Drive the bearing races out with the specified punch or drift. Keep the race locations identified so the installation tools can be matched correctly.

steps.title: Clean and decide whether the case is reusable
steps.body: Clean the magnet, which collects magnetic particles from the transmission fluid. Clean and inspect the shift shaft bearings for damage; the illustration highlights these bearing locations. If damage is present, install a new transmission case rather than continuing assembly with the damaged case.

steps.title: Install each race with its assigned tooling
steps.body: For the output shaft bearing race, use handle 205-153 with installer 307-655. For the rear output shaft bearing race, use handle 205-153 with installer 308-163. Follow the assembly phase of the case procedure for their placement; the shared handle does not make the two installers interchangeable.

steps.title: Refit the guide plate
steps.body: Install the guide plate and its bolt after completing the internal cleaning, inspection and race installation. Tighten the bolt to 106 lb.in (12 Nm), completing this case-subassembly operation before the wider transmission assembly continues.

watchFor.title: Damaged shift shaft bearings
watchFor.body: The prescribed remedy is case replacement. This operation does not provide an individual shift shaft bearing repair.

watchFor.title: Confusing removal and installation tools
watchFor.body: The punch or drift is specified for removing races; assembly calls for the named handle and installers.

notes: The component description identifies the case, magnet, guide plate and surrounding transmission parts if their names are unfamiliar.

diagnostics.finding: Damage found while inspecting the cleaned shift shaft bearings.
diagnostics.meaning: The case fails the stated reuse condition.
diagnostics.next: Install a new transmission case before proceeding with assembly.

verification.title: Confirm the completed subassembly
verification.body: Check that the magnet is clean, both specified bearing races are installed and the guide plate is secured.

verification.title: Record the inspection decision
verification.body: Record the shift shaft bearing condition, whether the case was replaced and completion of the guide plate bolt tightening.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L 3160 transmission case disassembly and assembly, including bearing inspection, race tooling and guide plate tightening.
Identify the case, bearings, magnet and guide plate within the 3160 transmission.

guides.title: Drain and refill the 5.2L 3160 manual transmission
guides.summary: Restore the transmission fluid level, including the required circulation and second fill when a transmission cooler is fitted.
guides.introduction: The 3160 manual transmission transfers engine torque to the driveshaft through its gears and shafts. Its fluid supports the working components, and an internal pump supplies fluid for cooling. Draining and filling restores the working fluid after a job that requires it to be removed.
guides.why: The fill opening establishes the level only when the vehicle is level. A cooler-equipped transmission needs an additional circulation step: the first fill does not account for fluid that must enter the cooling circuit. Skipping the second fill leaves that transmission underfilled.

when.summary: When work on the 3160 transmission requires its fluid to be drained and refilled.
notes: The transmission fluid is intended to last the transmission's service life; no routine change interval is specified.

prepare.title: Arrange level hoist access
prepare.detail: Use a suitable hoist and the designated lifting points. Check adapter clearance and never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Obtain the specified materials
prepare.detail: Have the transmission fluid and plug thread sealer specified by the procedure's Specifications references, a drain container, filling equipment and a torque wrench.

prepare.title: Identify the cooler branch
prepare.detail: Confirm whether a transmission fluid cooler is fitted. That branch requires running the engine with the transmission in Neutral and the clutch pedal released.

steps.title: Position the vehicle level
steps.body: Place the transmission in Neutral and position the vehicle on the hoist using the [lifting procedure](#/document/G1663631). Keep it level throughout draining and filling so the fill-hole height remains a valid reference.

steps.title: Drain and reseal the drain plug
steps.body: Follow [Transmission Draining and Filling](#/document/G1794233). Remove the drain plug and drain the fluid. Apply the specified thread sealer and reinstall the plug to 21 lb.ft (28 Nm).

steps.title: Make the initial fill
steps.body: Remove the fill plug and add the specified transmission fluid until it reaches the bottom of the fill hole. This is the final level-setting stage for vehicles without a transmission fluid cooler.

steps.title: Circulate fluid on cooler-equipped vehicles
steps.body: Loosely install the fill plug. With the transmission remaining in Neutral, start the engine and idle for 2 minutes with the clutch engaged, meaning the clutch pedal released. Turn the engine off, then refill to the bottom of the fill hole.

steps.title: Complete the fill-plug installation
steps.body: For all vehicles, apply the specified thread sealer to the fill plug and install it to 21 lb.ft (28 Nm). Complete this final installation after the cooler circulation and top-up when that branch applies.

watchFor.title: The wrong clutch position
watchFor.body: The cooler circulation step requires the pedal released. Holding it down does not follow the specified filling procedure.

watchFor.title: A tilted vehicle
watchFor.body: A fill-hole reading taken with the vehicle tilted does not establish the specified level.

notes: Use the bottom of the fill hole as the level reference; do not substitute an assumed fluid quantity.

diagnostics.finding: A cooler-equipped transmission received only the initial fill
diagnostics.meaning: The cooling system has not been accounted for and the transmission will be underfilled.
diagnostics.next: Perform the specified circulation, stop the engine and refill to the bottom of the opening.

verification.title: Confirm the final level and closure
verification.body: Confirm the bottom-of-hole level was reached at the correct stage and both plugs received thread sealer and final tightening.

verification.title: Record the filling branch
verification.body: Record cooler fitment and, where applicable, completion of the 2-minute circulation and subsequent top-up.

procedures.purpose: Drain and fill the 5.2L 3160 transmission, including the cooler-specific circulation branch.
Select lifting points and position the hoist safely.

applicability.equipment: 3160 6-speed manual transmission, with or without a transmission fluid cooler

guides.title: Check the fluid level in the 5.2L 3160 manual transmission
guides.summary: Set the transmission fluid level at the fill-hole edge, including the required circulation and refill sequence when a cooler is fitted.
guides.introduction: The 3160 six-speed manual transmission transfers engine torque to the driveshaft through its gears, shafts and synchronizers. Its fluid serves the internal working components, and an oil pump provides for fluid cooling. On vehicles with a transmission cooler, setting the level includes filling the cooling circuit before making the final level check.
guides.why: The bottom of the fill hole provides the level reference only when the vehicle is level. A cooler-equipped transmission can appear full before fluid has circulated through its cooling system. The required engine-idling stage fills that circuit; omitting it leaves the transmission underfilled.

when.summary: When the 3160 transmission fluid level needs checking or restoring.
notes: The transmission fluid is intended to last the transmission's service life; this is not a scheduled fluid-change instruction.

prepare.title: Provide level, secure access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the designated lifting points. Locate the stamped triangles, check adapter and underbody clearance, and never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Do not use the emergency tire-changing jack for this task.

prepare.title: Identify materials and equipment
prepare.detail: Have the transmission fluid and fill-plug thread sealer specified for the 3160 in Specifications (308-03), suitable filling equipment and a torque wrench. Establish whether a transmission fluid cooler is fitted.

prepare.title: Plan the cooler-equipped operating step
prepare.detail: Provide the capability to control the vehicle safely during the prescribed engine-idling phase while it remains in NEUTRAL on the hoist.

steps.title: Position the vehicle level
steps.body: Place the transmission in NEUTRAL and position the vehicle on a hoist using [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631). Confirm that the vehicle is level before following [Transmission Fluid Level Check](#/document/G1794234).

steps.title: Establish the initial level
steps.body: Remove the fill plug and add the specified transmission fluid to the bottom of the fill hole. This is the level target, rather than an assumed fill quantity. Vehicles without a cooler proceed to final plug sealing.

steps.title: Circulate fluid through the cooler, if fitted
steps.body: Loosely install the fill plug. Start the engine and let it idle for 2 minutes with the clutch engaged, meaning the clutch pedal is released. Keep the transmission in NEUTRAL during this circulation stage.

steps.title: Restore the level after circulation
steps.body: For cooler-equipped vehicles, refill the transmission to the bottom of the fill hole after the required circulation. This second fill accounts for fluid now occupying the cooling system.

steps.title: Seal and tighten the fill plug
steps.body: For all vehicles, apply the specified thread sealer to the fill plug and install it. Tighten the plug to 21 lb.ft (28 Nm). The temporary loose installation used for cooler circulation is not the finished installation.

watchFor.title: Vehicle tilted during filling
watchFor.body: A tilted vehicle changes the relationship between the fluid surface and fill-hole edge, defeating the prescribed level reference.

watchFor.title: Clutch pedal held down
watchFor.body: The cooler circulation step specifically requires the clutch engaged with the pedal released.

notes: Use the 3160-specific fluid and sealer requirements for this 5.2L application.

diagnostics.finding: Fluid is below the bottom of the fill hole with the vehicle level.
diagnostics.meaning: The transmission has not reached the specified fill-level target.
diagnostics.next: Add the specified fluid and complete the cooler branch if applicable.

diagnostics.finding: A cooler-equipped transmission has received only its initial fill.
diagnostics.meaning: The cooling circuit has not been accounted for by the required circulation and refill sequence.
diagnostics.next: Perform the prescribed idle stage and refill to the bottom of the fill hole.

verification.title: Confirm final level and closure
verification.body: Verify the final fill reached the bottom of the fill hole with the vehicle level, and that the plug received thread sealer and its specified tightening torque.

verification.title: Record the applicable result
verification.body: Record cooler fitment, completion of the circulation step when required, and the final level check.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L 3160 manual-transmission fluid-level procedure, including the cooler-equipped circulation branch and final plug installation.
Vehicle lifting points, support precautions and hoist-clearance requirements.

applicability.equipment: 3160 6-speed manual transmission; transmission fluid cooler if fitted

guides.title: Replace the 5.2L 3160 transmission extension housing gasket
guides.summary: Remove the transmission’s rear extension housing, renew its case-joint gasket and restore the fluid and any disturbed cooler connections.
guides.introduction: The 3160 six-speed manual transmission has an aluminum extension housing around its rear output-shaft area. A gasket seals the joint between this housing and the main case. Replacing it requires draining the transmission and removing the gearshift lever and output flange before the housing can slide off the shaft.
guides.why: A new gasket needs clean mating faces to seal correctly. Cooler-equipped versions add another inspection task: seals and backing rings can remain in the case when the tubes are withdrawn, so every piece must be accounted for before reassembly.
searchTerms: transmission fluid leak at rear housing

when.summary: For a confirmed extension-housing joint leak or gasket renewal after removing the housing.
notes: Fluid near the rear of the transmission does not by itself identify the housing gasket as the cause.

prepare.title: Plan the connected procedures
prepare.detail: This requires transmission-housing work, controlled fluid drainage and accurate torque tightening. Arrange access and capability for the separate gearshift-lever, output-flange and draining/filling procedures.

prepare.title: Prepare the gasket and specified materials
prepare.detail: Have a new housing gasket, Motorcraft Thread Sealant with PTFE TA-24-B (WSK-M2G350-A2), and Motorcraft MERCON LV Automatic Transmission Fluid XT-10-QLVC (WSS-M2C938-A). Cooler seals and backing rings are replaced if damaged.

steps.title: Drain the transmission
steps.body: Remove the drain plug and drain the fluid. Apply the specified thread sealant to the plug and reinstall it at 21 lb.ft (28 Nm), following the [gasket procedure](#/document/G1805396).

steps.title: Remove the lever and output flange
steps.body: Complete [gearshift lever removal](#/document/G1796480), followed by [output shaft flange removal](#/document/G1805399). These are separate access operations with their own installation requirements.

steps.title: Move cooler tubes aside where fitted
steps.body: Remove the cooler-tube nuts and bolts and position the tubes aside. Inspect the case to confirm the seals and backing rings came out with the tubes. Remove any that remain stuck in the case.

steps.title: Release wiring and withdraw the housing
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connectors and harness retainers, then position the harness aside. Remove the housing bolts and slide the extension housing off the output shaft.

steps.title: Renew the case-joint gasket
steps.body: Clean the old gasket material from both the transmission case and extension-housing sealing surfaces. Fit a new gasket on the case, install the housing and tighten its fasteners to 24 lb.ft (33 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the wiring and cooler connections
steps.body: Reconnect the electrical connectors and retainers. If cooler tubes were removed, inspect their backing rings and seals and replace damaged pieces. Use the specified fluid for the seal installation step. Refit the tubes, matching each fastener to its tightening callout in the complete procedure; the cooler fasteners do not all share one torque.

steps.title: Restore the flange, lever and fluid
steps.body: Reinstall the output flange, then the gearshift lever, using their procedures. Fill the transmission using [Transmission Draining and Filling](#/document/G1794233) for the correct filling method and final level.

watchFor.title: A seal left behind
watchFor.body: Check inside the cooler-tube connection in the case; inspecting only the removed tube can miss a retained seal or backing ring.

watchFor.title: Gasket residue
watchFor.body: Clean both mating faces before positioning the replacement gasket.

notes: The fluid drain and refill are part of opening this housing, not a newly introduced maintenance interval.

diagnostics.finding: A cooler-tube seal or backing ring is damaged
diagnostics.meaning: That sealing component is unsuitable for reuse.
diagnostics.next: Install a new seal or backing ring as necessary.

diagnostics.finding: The origin of rear-transmission fluid leakage is uncertain
diagnostics.meaning: The housing gasket, output-shaft seal and flange sealing parts are distinct components.
diagnostics.next: Establish the leaking joint before selecting this gasket repair.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly and filling
verification.body: Confirm the housing, harness, applicable cooler tubes, output flange and gearshift lever are restored, and complete the linked filling procedure.

verification.title: Record the sealing work
verification.body: Record gasket renewal, cooler seal/backing-ring inspection and any replacements, together with completion of the transmission refill.

procedures.purpose: 3160 extension housing removal, gasket renewal and installation.
3160 gearshift lever removal and installation for access.
3160 output shaft flange removal and installation.
3160 transmission draining and final filling.

applicability.equipment: 3160 six-speed manual transmission; transmission fluid cooler if equipped

guides.title: Replace the input shaft seal on the 5.2L 3160 manual transmission
guides.summary: Remove the transmission and clutch slave cylinder, renew the input shaft seal with the specified tools, then reinstall and restore the fluid and clutch systems.
guides.introduction: The input shaft carries drive from the clutch into the gearbox. Its seal sits in the clutch housing around the shaft, retaining transmission lubricant at the front of the gearbox. Replacing it is a short operation once exposed, but reaching it requires transmission removal and clutch slave-cylinder access.
guides.why: The old seal must be discarded after extraction. The dedicated remover and installers control how force is applied around the shaft and housing. Most of the work lies in supporting the transmission correctly and restoring the connections disturbed for access.

when.summary: Renew an input shaft seal requiring replacement, including any seal removed during service.
notes: This is a replacement procedure; it does not establish the source of an unidentified fluid leak.

prepare.title: Arrange transmission access
prepare.detail: Provide the capability to remove and reinstall the gearbox safely, using a transmission jack and safety strap. Follow the linked 3160 removal and installation procedures for the surrounding components and connections.

prepare.title: Have the seal tools ready
prepare.detail: Obtain a new input shaft seal, remover 308-375 with a slide hammer, front-seal installer 308-806 and input-shaft-seal installer 308-957.

prepare.title: Control clutch dust
prepare.detail: Do not breathe friction-component dust or blow it away with compressed air. Use approved dust-removal methods when working around the clutch.

steps.title: Remove the transmission for access
steps.body: Follow the 3160 transmission removal procedure, beginning with battery disconnection. Remove the required surrounding components, disconnect the hydraulic and electrical connections, and support the gearbox with the strapped transmission jack before withdrawing it. Note bellhousing bolt and studbolt locations. If cooler tubes are fitted, account for their seals and backing rings when disconnected.

steps.title: Expose the seal behind the slave cylinder
steps.body: Remove the slave-cylinder bolts, release its tube from the retaining clip and draw the cylinder outward off the input shaft. These access operations are detailed in the matching 3160 disassembly procedure; gearbox internals do not need dismantling for this seal replacement.

steps.title: Extract and discard the old seal
steps.body: Use input shaft seal remover 308-375 with the slide hammer to remove the seal from the clutch housing. Discard it immediately so it cannot be mistaken for a reusable part.

steps.title: Install the replacement seal
steps.body: Place the new seal on the input shaft. Use installers 308-806 and 308-957 together to install it in the clutch housing, following the seal procedure for tool positioning.

steps.title: Restore the slave cylinder
steps.body: Install the slave cylinder in the clutch housing, secure its tube in the retaining clip and install its bolts. The matching 3160 assembly procedure specifies 97 lb.in (11 Nm) for these bolts.

steps.title: Reinstall and complete the service
steps.body: Follow the 3160 installation procedure. Clean the input shaft and apply the specified small amount of grease to its splines and pilot-bearing surface. Restore the correctly positioned fasteners, hydraulic tube, vent, wiring and removed components. Replace damaged cooler-tube seals or backing rings where fitted. Fill the transmission, reconnect the battery, then fill and bleed the clutch hydraulic system using the referenced procedures.

watchFor.title: Missing cooler-tube sealing parts
watchFor.body: A seal or backing ring can remain in the transmission case when a cooler tube is removed. Check the case as well as the tube.

watchFor.title: Grease placement
watchFor.body: The installation instruction applies grease to the shaft splines and pilot-bearing surface; it is not a seal-lubrication instruction.

notes: Use the 3160-specific access and completion procedures linked here. The seal operation does not call for input-shaft removal or gearbox overhaul.

verification.title: Check the completed seal access work
verification.body: Confirm the replacement seal is installed in the clutch housing, the slave cylinder is refitted, its tube is clipped in place and its bolts are tightened to specification.

verification.title: Confirm the installation endpoints
verification.body: Check completion of transmission filling, battery reconnection and clutch hydraulic filling and bleeding. Include cooler sealing-part inspection where applicable.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L 3160 input shaft seal removal and installation with the dedicated tools.
5.2L 3160 transmission removal for access, including support and connection handling.
3160 slave-cylinder removal steps only, to expose the input shaft seal.
3160 seal and slave-cylinder installation details, including tube retention and bolt torque.
5.2L 3160 transmission installation and fluid, battery and clutch-hydraulic completion.

guides.title: Replace the selector shaft seal on the 5.2L 3160 manual transmission
guides.summary: Renew the selector shaft seal after removing the driveshaft and gearshift lever assembly with the transmission properly supported.
guides.introduction: The selector shaft carries gear-lever input into the transmission's shifting mechanism. Its seal closes the opening around the shaft in the extension housing, helping retain transmission fluid while allowing selector movement. Replacing this small seal requires substantial access work: the driveshaft and gearshift lever assembly must be removed, and the transmission is lowered with support.
guides.why: The new seal depends on undamaged contact surfaces. Scratching the selector shaft or gouging the extension housing during extraction can undermine the repair. Controlled transmission support is equally important because the crossmember fasteners are removed during gearshift-lever access.

when.summary: When leakage is traced to the selector shaft seal, or the seal has been removed and requires renewal.
notes: Confirm the transmission and leak location before ordering parts or beginning driveline removal.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and support
prepare.detail: This work requires a hoist, a transmission jack and competence in supported transmission lowering. Follow the jacking and lifting instructions referenced by the Gearshift Lever procedure.

prepare.title: Plan the complete access work
prepare.detail: Have a new selector shaft seal ready. Follow the separate Driveshaft and Gearshift Lever Boot procedures called out by the lever instructions, including their installation requirements.

prepare.title: Prepare for careful extraction
prepare.detail: Use the seal-removal illustration to identify the seal and extraction access. Protect both the shaft and housing rather than using either sealing surface as a careless levering point.

steps.title: Set up the vehicle and remove access parts
steps.body: With the transmission in N, position the vehicle on a hoist. Follow the Gearshift Lever access sequence to remove its boot and the driveshaft. These are prerequisites to removing the lever assembly.

steps.title: Support and lower the transmission
steps.body: Support the crossmember with a transmission jack before removing its bolts. Lower the transmission as directed by the Gearshift Lever procedure to obtain the necessary access.

steps.title: Remove the gearshift lever assembly
steps.body: Remove the lever assembly bolts, then the nuts and assembly. Completing this access phase exposes the selector shaft seal for replacement.

steps.title: Extract and discard the old seal
steps.body: Remove the selector shaft seal using the illustrated access. Work carefully around the shaft and extension housing: neither may be scratched or gouged. Discard the removed seal.

steps.title: Install the replacement seal
steps.body: Install a new selector shaft seal at the opening shown in the seal installation illustration. Preserve the shaft and housing surfaces throughout installation.

steps.title: Restore the lever and driveline
steps.body: Install the lever assembly and nuts, then its bolts using their individual specifications. With the jack supporting the crossmember, raise the transmission and install its bolts. Finish by reinstalling the driveshaft and gearshift lever boot through their respective procedures.

watchFor.title: Extraction damage
watchFor.body: A damaged shaft or housing surface needs assessment before continuing; fitting a new seal does not remove that damage.

watchFor.title: Unsupported crossmember
watchFor.body: Establish transmission-jack support before loosening the crossmember bolts and maintain controlled support during lowering and raising.

notes: The driveshaft is a shared prerequisite in the seal and lever procedures. Coordinate the work so it is removed and installed once.

diagnostics.finding: Oil is present near the extension housing but its origin is unclear.
diagnostics.meaning: The transmission has separate selector shaft and output shaft seals; general wetness does not identify which seal is leaking.
diagnostics.next: Establish the leak origin before selecting the seal repair.

verification.title: Check restored assemblies
verification.body: Confirm the new seal, lever assembly, crossmember, driveshaft and boot are installed before concluding the access work.

verification.title: Record fastener completion
verification.body: Record tightening against the Gearshift Lever specifications: assembly nuts 11 Nm, lever bolt 15 Nm, lever-to-transmission bolt 40 Nm, and crossmember bolts 63 Nm.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L 3160 selector shaft seal removal, discard requirement and new-seal installation.
3160 gearshift lever access and refitting, including transmission support, lowering and fastener torques.

guides.title: Replace the 5.2L 3160 manual-transmission fluid temperature sensor
guides.summary: Raise the vehicle safely, replace the transmission fluid temperature sensor and complete the specified transmission refill.
guides.introduction: The transmission fluid temperature (TFT) sensor measures the temperature of the lubricant inside the 3160 manual transmission. This gearbox transfers engine torque to the driveshaft and includes an oil pump for fluid cooling. Sensor replacement combines an electrical disconnection with work at the transmission housing and the listed drain-and-refill sequence.
guides.why: Safe underbody access is the first requirement. Correct tightening then matters at both the drain plug and sensor, which have different torque specifications. Completing the transmission-specific filling procedure restores the fluid needed by the gearbox; sensor installation alone does not finish the job.

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies a faulty TFT sensor on the 5.2L vehicle with the 3160 manual transmission.
notes: The replacement procedure supplies no electrical fault thresholds; establish the need for replacement through diagnosis.

prepare.title: Arrange safe lifting
prepare.detail: Use a suitable hoist and follow [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631). Identify the prescribed lifting points by their stamped triangles and check adapter clearance around suspension, exhaust, steering and axle components.

prepare.title: Prepare fluid-service equipment
prepare.detail: Have a drain container, suitable removal tools and torque tools. Obtain the fluid and filling equipment required by [Transmission Draining and Filling](#/document/G1794233) for this 3160 transmission.

steps.title: Position the vehicle on the hoist
steps.body: Place the transmission in NEUTRAL and position the vehicle on the hoist. Check for underbody interference before using a drive-on lift, and position lifting adapters carefully before raising the vehicle.

steps.title: Drain the transmission
steps.body: Follow the listed removal sequence by removing the drain plug and draining the fluid. The procedure also expressly requires drainage when transmission disassembly is needed. The drain plug's installation torque is 21 lb.ft (28 Nm).

steps.title: Remove the sensor
steps.body: Disconnect the TFT sensor electrical connector, then remove the sensor. Follow [the sensor removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1809313) for identification and access.

steps.title: Install and reconnect the sensor
steps.body: Install the TFT sensor and tighten it to 97 lb.in (11 Nm), then connect its electrical connector. Use the sensor specification at this step, keeping it distinct from the drain-plug torque.

steps.title: Complete the transmission refill
steps.body: Ensure the drain plug is installed to its specified torque, then fill the transmission using the linked 3160 draining and filling procedure. Follow that procedure for the correct fluid and filling requirements.

watchFor.title: Unsupported underbody work
watchFor.body: Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. If using a jack, support the vehicle with floor stands. The emergency wheel-change jack is unsuitable for this service.

watchFor.title: Incorrect lifting contact
watchFor.body: Do not lift against either bumper. Incorrect lift points or adapter placement can damage components or allow the vehicle to shift.

notes: The 3160 overview describes its fluid as a service-life fill. Draining and refilling for this repair does not establish a routine change interval.

verification.title: Confirm installation completion
verification.body: Check that the sensor is tightened, its electrical connector is connected and the transmission filling procedure is complete.

verification.title: Record the service result
verification.body: Record the sensor and drain-plug tightening values and completion of the 3160 refill. Keep the original diagnostic finding with the repair record so installation completion remains distinct from confirmation that the original concern is resolved.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L 3160 manual-transmission TFT sensor removal and installation, including draining and the separate sensor and drain-plug torques.
Required lifting-point identification, support precautions and hoist-clearance guidance.
3160 manual-transmission fluid draining and filling requirements used to complete sensor replacement.

guides.title: Remove and refit the 5.2L 3160 transmission output flange
guides.summary: Remove the output flange with the transmission supported, then refit it with a new retaining nut and the correct support-fastener torques.
guides.introduction: The output flange connects the transmission's output shaft to the driveshaft, carrying torque toward the rear differential. This job works at the rear of the installed 3160 gearbox: the driveshaft and rear support assembly are removed for access, the flange is pulled off, and the connection is rebuilt.
guides.why: Removing the crossmember takes away the transmission's rear support. A safety stand carries that load during the work, while dedicated holding tools restrain the flange for controlled nut removal and tightening.

when.summary: When an established repair requires removal or replacement of the transmission output flange.
notes: This operation does not establish the cause of a driveline complaint.

prepare.title: Arrange supported underbody access
prepare.detail: Provide safe vehicle access, a safety stand and a wooden block to support the transmission before removing its insulator and crossmember.

prepare.title: Have the specified equipment and parts
prepare.detail: Use rear flange holding tool 308-807, drive pinion flange holding tool 205-478, a two-leg puller and torque-tightening equipment. Obtain a new flange nut and have the Driveshaft procedure in section 205-01 available.

steps.title: Remove the driveshaft
steps.body: Follow the Driveshaft removal procedure in section 205-01 to expose the transmission flange. That separate procedure governs the driveshaft's own removal and later installation requirements.

steps.title: Support the transmission and remove the rear support
steps.body: Place the safety stand and wooden block beneath the transmission before removing support fasteners. With the load supported, remove the transmission support insulator and crossmember to gain access.

steps.title: Release and pull the flange
steps.body: Use both specified holding tools to restrain the output flange. Remove and discard its retaining nut, then withdraw the flange with the two-leg puller. Keep the discarded nut out of the installation parts.

steps.title: Install the flange, washer and new nut
steps.body: Fit the flange onto the output shaft, install the washer and loosely fit a new nut. Restrain the flange with the specified holding tools and tighten the nut to 143 Nm. Follow the complete [output flange procedure](#/document/G1805399) for tool placement and sequence.

steps.title: Restore the support assembly and driveshaft
steps.body: Install the transmission support insulator and crossmember. Tighten the three center transmission/insulator attachments, identified as group 1, to 103 Nm. Tighten the four outboard crossmember-to-body bolts, group 2, to 63 Nm. Complete driveshaft installation using its own procedure.

watchFor.title: Support removed before the load is carried
watchFor.body: The safety stand and wooden block must support the transmission before the insulator and crossmember are removed.

watchFor.title: Three distinct tightening requirements
watchFor.body: The flange nut, center support attachments and outboard body bolts have different torque values. Do not apply one value to the whole assembly.

notes: The flange retaining nut is a required new part.
Use these values only for the specified 5.2L 3160 transmission operation.

verification.title: Confirm complete reassembly
verification.body: Confirm the flange washer and new nut are installed, both support-fastener groups are tightened, and driveshaft installation is complete.

verification.title: Record the tightening results
verification.body: Record completion of the flange-nut tightening and each support-fastener group separately so the different requirements remain identifiable.

procedures.purpose: Complete output shaft flange removal and installation for the 5.2L 3160 manual transmission, including support removal and restoration.

guides.title: Replace the 5.2L 3160 manual transmission support insulator
guides.summary: Replace the transmission support insulator with the gearbox secured on a strapped transmission jack, then tighten its bolts and nuts to their separate specifications.
guides.introduction: The transmission support insulator supports the gearbox at its mounting point while limiting vibration transfer into the body. The 3160 manual transmission transfers engine torque toward the rear differential through the driveshaft. This repair changes its external support insulator without opening the transmission case or disturbing the internal geartrain.
guides.why: Supporting the vehicle on a hoist does not independently support the transmission when its mounting is removed. A transmission jack carries that load, and a retaining strap secures the gearbox to the jack. The insulator bolts and nuts also have different tightening requirements, so identifying the two fastener groups matters.

when.summary: When the transmission support insulator has been assessed as requiring replacement.
notes: This is an external mounting repair; the procedure does not diagnose an internal transmission fault.

prepare.title: Hoist and lifting capability
prepare.detail: Use the specified lifting points, identified by stamped triangles, and check hoist-adapter clearance. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Do not lift against a bumper or use the emergency tire-changing jack for this operation.

prepare.title: Secure transmission support
prepare.detail: Provide the specified transmission jack and retaining strap, with the capability to support and secure the gearbox before removing the insulator bolts.

prepare.title: Controlled fastener tightening
prepare.detail: Have a torque wrench suitable for both installation specifications. Keep the insulator nuts and bolts identifiable throughout the repair.

steps.title: Position the vehicle for access
steps.body: Place the transmission in NEUTRAL and position the vehicle on a hoist. Follow the [lifting overview](#/document/G1663631), checking that the lifting equipment does not interfere with suspension components, mounting brackets or the underbody.

steps.title: Remove the nuts and secure the gearbox
steps.body: Remove the transmission support insulator nuts. Next support the transmission with the transmission jack and secure it to the jack using the retaining strap, as directed in the [insulator procedure](#/document/G1794238).

steps.title: Remove the supported insulator
steps.body: With the transmission supported and secured, remove the insulator bolts and the insulator. Keep the jack and strap supporting the gearbox throughout this mounting removal.

steps.title: Install and tighten the replacement
steps.body: Install the transmission support insulator and its bolts. Tighten the bolts to 103 Nm. Install the insulator nuts and tighten them to 70 Nm. Complete both fastener groups before withdrawing temporary transmission support.

watchFor.title: Transmission resting unsecured on the jack
watchFor.body: The retaining strap is specified equipment and must secure the transmission before the insulator bolts are removed.

watchFor.title: One torque applied to every fastener
watchFor.body: Use 103 Nm for the insulator bolts and 70 Nm for its nuts.

notes: If transmission identification is needed, the 3160 identification tag is on the top right-hand side of the transmission.

verification.title: Confirm the restored mounting
verification.body: Verify that the insulator, bolts and nuts are installed and secured before ending the supported-work phase.

verification.title: Record both tightening results
verification.body: Record completion of the 103 Nm bolt tightening and 70 Nm nut tightening as separate checks.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the support insulator for the 5.2L application with the 3160 manual transmission.
Identify safe lifting points and hoist-placement precautions for underbody access.

guides.title: Rebuild the MT82 manual gearshift lever
guides.summary: Remove the MT82 gearshift assembly, inspect its supporting parts, rebuild the lever and reinstall it with the correct seals and retainers.
guides.introduction: The floor-mounted gearshift lever transfers your hand movement to the transmission through its attached linkage. Bushings support that movement, while the isolator, anti-rattle washer and surrounding seals control unwanted movement and vibration. This job combines removal from the vehicle with bench disassembly, inspection and reassembly; releasing the console trim is only the beginning.
guides.why: The transmission must be supported and lowered to release the assembly. On the bench, the order of the sleeve, bushing, isolator and washer matters: these parts locate and support the lever. The anti-rattle washer belongs above the roll pin, and the bolt discarded during disassembly must be replaced.

when.summary: When inspection identifies damaged gearshift components or the lever assembly requires bench repair.
notes: A gear-selection complaint alone does not establish which external-control component needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange supported underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and transmission jack, with the vehicle in neutral. Identify the marked lifting points and check adapter clearance. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim and bench work
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover, punch and suitable tightening equipment. Arrange the driveshaft removal and installation procedure referenced by the vehicle procedure, and obtain the required new bench-assembly bolt.

steps.title: Release the console boot
steps.body: Follow the [removal procedure](#/document/G1688571). Unscrew the knob counterclockwise. Release the boot from the console with the trim remover, beginning at the front sides and working rearward, then release its retainers and remove it.

steps.title: Create clearance below the vehicle
steps.body: Remove the driveshaft using its applicable procedure. Support the crossmember with the transmission jack before removing its bolts and lowering the transmission. Remove the gearshift lever nuts.

steps.title: Remove and inspect the assembly
steps.body: Remove the lever-to-transmission bolt and lever bolt, then withdraw the assembly toward the rear. Inspect the rubber boot, service-kit parts, rear isolator, tunnel seal and foam gasket, and front hub bushing. Replace damaged components as necessary.

steps.title: Disassemble the lever on the bench
steps.body: Follow the [bench procedure](#/document/G1703200): remove the boot, tunnel seal, isolator, steel sleeve and polymer bushing. Remove the anti-rattle washer, noting its position above the roll pin. Drive out the roll pin with a punch, then remove and discard the bolt.

steps.title: Rebuild in the specified order
steps.body: Install a new bolt, followed by the roll pin and anti-rattle washer. Refit the polymer bushing, steel sleeve, isolator, tunnel seal and boot in that order. This restores the supporting parts around the lever without changing their arrangement.

steps.title: Reinstall the lever and surrounding parts
steps.body: Return to the vehicle installation procedure. Install the assembly, its two bolts and its nuts using their individual torque specifications. Raise the supported transmission and secure the crossmember. Reinstall the driveshaft, attach the boot retainers, seat the boot in the console and install the knob.

watchFor.title: Washer position
watchFor.body: Installing the anti-rattle washer below the roll pin changes the specified assembly arrangement.

watchFor.title: Different bolt requirements
watchFor.body: The discarded bench-assembly bolt requires replacement; do not confuse it with the separately identified installation fasteners.

notes: The service kit includes the roll pin, spring, plastic blocker, shoulder bolt and anti-rattle washer.

diagnostics.finding: Damage to a boot, seal, isolator, bushing or service-kit component
diagnostics.meaning: Inspection has identified a component requiring attention within the external controls.
diagnostics.next: Replace damaged components as necessary before reinstalling the assembly.

verification.title: Confirm assembly and attachment
verification.body: Check the washer arrangement, required new bolt, completed fastening stages and restored boot retainers against the two procedures.

verification.title: Record the repair
verification.body: Record the damaged components found and those replaced, including any seal or bushing work.

procedures.purpose: MT82 gearshift lever bench disassembly and assembly for the listed engines.
MT82 gearshift lever removal, inspection and installation in the vehicle.
Correct vehicle lifting points and support precautions.

guides.title: Replace the MT82 manual gearshift lever boot
guides.summary: Remove the threaded knob, release the boot’s five console clips and three lever-collar retainers, then refit the assembly in the correct order.
guides.introduction: The gearshift boot gets a front-row seat to every gear change, yet its own removal depends on a handful of plastic clips. Naturally, the little things get the last word. I’ll walk you through freeing the console surround, releasing the boot from the lever and putting everything back without turning a simple trim job into a wrestling match. This guide covers 2015 Mustangs with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine and MT82 6-speed manual transmission.
guides.why: The boot covers the opening around the cabin gearshift lever while allowing the lever to move. That lever passes your movement to the transmission through the external shift controls. The visible console boot has two separate attachments: five clips around its outer surround and three retainers at its collar around the lever. Releasing both sets in order lets the boot come away without pulling against an attachment that is still engaged.

when.summary: Use this procedure when replacing the visible console gearshift boot or removing it for access.
notes: The external controls also contain a separate tunnel seal, foam gasket and boot. Identify the cabin console boot before ordering or removing parts.
This procedure applies to the MT82 manual transmission on all three listed engines.

prepare.title: Gather the trim tool and boot
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover ready. If replacing the boot, have the replacement assembly matched to your vehicle and compare its outer clip positions and lever-collar attachments with the removed assembly before fitting it.

prepare.title: Plan a cabin-only job
prepare.detail: Access is through the center console around the gearshift lever; no lifting or underhood work is needed. This procedure ends with the visible console boot and knob installed. Dismantling the lever mechanism or the separate tunnel sealing parts requires their own repair instructions.

prepare.title: Prepare for safe handling
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged components. Keep the ignition off and remove the key to prevent another person starting the vehicle. The relevant general precautions are in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Park and prevent an unintended start
steps.body:
Park on a level surface, apply the parking brake and leave it applied throughout the job. Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle.

If a remote-start feature is fitted, disable it before beginning through the central display: Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Keep the vehicle on the ground for this procedure.

steps.title: Unscrew and remove the gearshift knob
steps.body:
Turn the gearshift knob counterclockwise until it unscrews from the lever, then lift it off and put it aside. This clears the top of the lever so the boot can be removed later.

The knob is the threaded attachment here; save the trim remover for the surround. The removal and refitting sequence is covered in [Gearshift Lever Boot](#/document/G1688160).

steps.title: Release the five console clips from front to rear
steps.body:
Locate the seam between the boot’s outer surround and the floor console. The front is the end nearest the dashboard controls.

Use the interior trim remover to release the surround at its front sides first. Work rearward along the sides, then free the rear portion. There are five perimeter retaining clips: two toward the front, two farther back along the sides and one at the rear curved end.

Lift the released surround enough to reach beneath the boot. If one area remains held, return to that attachment with the trim remover before lifting farther. I’d let each clip have its turn; hauling on the whole surround only gives the stubborn one more leverage.

steps.title: Release the three collar retainers and lift off the boot
steps.body:
With the outer surround raised, look beneath the boot at the collar around the gearshift lever. Locate the three retainers securing that collar to the cylindrical section below it.

Release those three retainers, then lift the boot assembly upward and off the lever. These are separate from the five clips that held the surround to the console. If the boot still catches at the collar, check that all three retainers are released before continuing upward.

steps.title: Fit the boot over the lever and attach the collar
steps.body:
Orient the boot so its front edge faces the dashboard and its outer surround matches the console opening. Lower the boot over the gearshift lever.

Align the collar with its attachment around the lever and engage all three collar retainers. Check each attachment before seating the outer surround, while you can still see and reach beneath it.

steps.title: Seat the surround in the floor console
steps.body:
Align the surround’s five perimeter clips with their receiving positions in the console. Press the surround down at the attachment locations until it is seated around the opening.

Check the front sides, both side edges and the rear curved end. If an edge remains raised, check the corresponding clip’s alignment and engagement before pressing again. A proud corner needs attention, not a harder slap.

steps.title: Reinstall the knob and check the completed assembly
steps.body:
Place the knob onto the lever’s thread and turn it clockwise to install it. Check that the knob is secure and correctly positioned.

Confirm the boot collar remains attached, the outer surround sits evenly in the console and no boot material is trapped beneath its edge. These are checks of your reassembly; they do not diagnose the transmission or shift mechanism.

watchFor.title: Two different sets of retainers
watchFor.body: The five perimeter clips release the surround from the console. The three retainers beneath the raised boot release its collar from the lever. Freeing the outer clips alone does not free the whole boot.

watchFor.title: A surround that resists lifting
watchFor.body: Stop pulling and revisit the held area with the interior trim remover, maintaining the front-to-rear release sequence. An engaged clip must be released before that portion can lift.

watchFor.title: A collar that remains caught
watchFor.body: Keep the surround raised and check the three collar attachments. Do not use the console edge as a lever to pull the collar free.

notes: The [External Controls - Overview](#/document/G1688155) explains how the floor-mounted lever operates the transmission and identifies the visible boot separately from the tunnel sealing components.
Boot replacement does not require removal of the lever’s service-kit parts, bushings or rear isolator.

diagnostics.finding: The outer surround lifts in some places but stays attached at one edge.
diagnostics.meaning: A perimeter attachment may still be engaged.
diagnostics.next: Return to that area with the interior trim remover and release the attachment before lifting the surround farther.

diagnostics.finding: The surround is free of the console, but the boot will not lift off the lever.
diagnostics.meaning: The collar may still be held by one or more of its three retainers.
diagnostics.next: Look beneath the raised boot, locate all three collar retainers and confirm each is released before removing the assembly.

diagnostics.finding: An edge of the surround remains raised after installation.
diagnostics.meaning: The nearby clip may be misaligned or incompletely engaged.
diagnostics.next: Check that clip and its receiving position, realign the surround and seat it again. Recheck the entire perimeter before installing the knob.

verification.title: Confirm both attachment stages
verification.body: Before seating the surround, verify all three collar retainers are attached. After seating it, confirm the five perimeter positions hold the surround evenly against the console.

verification.title: Confirm the finished trim and knob
verification.body: Check that the boot material is clear of the surround’s seating edge and the knob is installed securely in its correct position. Remove the trim tool and loose parts from the cabin, leaving the parking brake applied.

procedures.purpose: Removal and installation of the gearshift knob and console boot, including the five perimeter clips and three collar retainers.
Explain the floor-mounted shift controls and distinguish the console boot from the separate tunnel sealing components.
Relevant startup-prevention and personal-protection precautions for the cabin trim work.

stepGroups.title: Secure the car and remove the knob
stepGroups.summary: Prevent an unintended start and clear the top of the lever.

stepGroups.title: Release and remove the boot
stepGroups.summary: Free the five console clips, then the three lever-collar retainers.

stepGroups.title: Refit the boot and knob
stepGroups.summary: Attach the collar, seat the surround and check the finished assembly.

guides.title: Replace the gearshift lever boot on a 2015 5.2L Mustang
guides.summary: Protect and unscrew the shift knob, release the boot’s five console clips and three inner retainers, then refit the boot and knob with Motorcraft TA-25-B threadlock.
guides.introduction: The gearshift boot gets a workout every time you change gear, yet its reward is usually being ignored until it needs replacing. I give its plastic attachments more respect than its humble job title suggests: the knob comes off first, the console surround releases from front to rear, and the boot’s inner retainers come last. A little patience here saves turning a trim job into a plastic-confetti incident.
guides.why: The boot is the flexible cover around the gearshift lever where it passes through the floor console. The lever carries your gear-selection movement to the transmission; the boot covers the opening while allowing that movement. Its outer surround clips into the console, and its central opening attaches around the lever’s collar. Those are separate attachments, so lifting the surround alone does not free the boot. The [external-controls overview](#/document/G1796478) explains how the lever, knob and boot fit into the system.

when.summary: Use this procedure when replacing the gearshift lever boot or removing it for access on a 2015 Mustang with the 5.2L engine and the illustrated manual gearshift arrangement.
notes: This is a boot removal and installation procedure, not a test for difficult shifting or an internal transmission fault.
The knob must be removed before the boot can come off the lever.

prepare.title: Park and prevent an unintended start
prepare.detail: Park on a level surface, apply the parking brake, switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle. Keep the car on its wheels for this cabin task; lifting and underhood access are unnecessary.

prepare.title: Gather the specified tools and materials
prepare.detail: Have an 8-inch rubber strap wrench, an interior trim remover, 2-inch-wide delicate-surface painter’s tape and Motorcraft Threadlock and Sealer TA-25-B ready. Have the replacement boot ready if you are replacing rather than temporarily removing it.

prepare.title: Handle the material safely
prepare.detail: Read the safety information sheet for TA-25-B before use and follow its handling precautions. Wear eye protection, and use protective gloves if handling any sharp-edged parts. The relevant precautions are in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

prepare.title: Know the refitting limit
prepare.detail: Knob installation calls for TA-25-B but gives no numerical tightening torque or application quantity. Use the specified material without borrowing a tightening value from a different shifter or transmission.

steps.title: Wrap the knob before applying the strap wrench
steps.body: Apply 2-inch-wide delicate-surface painter’s tape around the full circumference of the gearshift knob. Cover the surface where the rubber strap will grip so the strap bears on the protective tape. I put the tape on before the wrench comes anywhere near the finish—this is a grip job, not an engraving job.

steps.title: Unscrew and remove the knob
steps.body: Wrap the 8-inch rubber strap wrench around the protected knob. Turn the knob counterclockwise to loosen it, then unscrew it completely and lift it off the lever. Leave the protective tape on for refitting and set the knob aside. The threaded upper section of the lever is now exposed. This is the first removal action in the [gearshift lever boot procedure](#/document/G1796481).

steps.title: Release the boot surround from the console
steps.body:
Place the interior trim remover at the seam between the boot surround and the floor console, starting at the front sides nearest the dashboard controls. Release those attachment points first, then work rearward along the surround.

There are five retaining clips around the surround’s perimeter. Lift the surround progressively as the clips release; if one area remains held down, return the trim remover to that area rather than pulling the whole assembly harder. Once the perimeter is free, lift the surround enough to reach its attachment around the lever. The boot is still attached at its center.

steps.title: Release the three inner retainers and remove the boot
steps.body:
Look beneath the lifted boot at its central opening. Around the lever, below the exposed threaded section, a circular collar has three retaining points that engage the boot’s central opening.

Release all three retainers from the boot, supporting the assembly as you work. Once the center is disengaged, lift the boot and surround over the knob-free lever and remove them. Keep the perimeter clips and central retainers in mind as two separate sets of attachments; freeing one set does not free the other.

steps.title: Check the attachment points before refitting
steps.body:
With the boot removed, look at all five perimeter clips and the three central retaining points. Check that each is present and that no broken piece obstructs its mating opening. Also look at the corresponding openings in the surround and at the boot’s center.

This is an assembly check, not a wear measurement. If an attachment is broken or cannot engage, resolve that damaged attachment before pressing the boot back into place. More pressure will not persuade a broken clip to grow back.

steps.title: Attach the boot at the lever collar
steps.body: Lower the boot over the lever with its front edge facing the dashboard and its rounded rear edge facing rearward. Align the central opening with the collar around the lever, then engage all three inner retainers. Check each attachment before lowering the surround into the console; once the perimeter is seated, these inner connections are harder to see.

steps.title: Seat the surround in the floor console
steps.body:
Align the five perimeter clips with their corresponding console openings. Press the surround into place at the attachment points until the clips engage and the surround sits evenly in the console.

Look around the entire edge. If one section remains raised, lift that area enough to check alignment and correct it before pressing again. Keep the flexible boot clear of the joint between the surround and console.

steps.title: Refit the knob with the specified threadlock
steps.body:
Use Motorcraft Threadlock and Sealer TA-25-B at the knob’s threaded attachment, then install the knob by turning it clockwise onto the lever. Keep the protective tape in place through installation. Once the knob is installed, remove the tape from its surface.

Finish by checking the boot’s seating and clearing the tools and tape from the cabin. The [boot procedure](#/document/G1796481) places knob installation after both the inner retainers and the console surround have been refitted.

watchFor.title: A surround that lifts on one side but stays anchored elsewhere
watchFor.body: A perimeter clip may still be engaged. Work the trim remover at the held section and continue the front-to-rear release sequence instead of twisting the surround.

watchFor.title: The boot remaining attached after the surround is free
watchFor.body: The three retainers at the central collar are a second attachment. Release them before trying to lift the boot off the lever.

watchFor.title: Tape shifting out of the wrench’s contact area
watchFor.body: Stop and restore full protective coverage before continuing knob removal. Keep the rubber strap against the taped surface.

notes: The knob, boot and lever assembly are separate parts of the manual transmission’s external controls.
The five perimeter clips and three central retainers are attachment counts, not tightening sequences.

diagnostics.finding: The surround is partly released but one section remains held down.
diagnostics.meaning: A perimeter attachment has not yet disengaged.
diagnostics.next: Return the interior trim remover to that section, release the clip locally and continue rearward. Do not use the free side as a handle to force the rest out.

diagnostics.finding: All five perimeter clips are free, but the boot remains attached around the lever.
diagnostics.meaning: The central collar retainers still hold the boot.
diagnostics.next: Lift the surround enough to see the collar and release its three retaining points before removing the boot.

diagnostics.finding: A retaining point is broken, missing or unable to engage during installation.
diagnostics.meaning: The boot cannot be confirmed fully retained at that location.
diagnostics.next: Identify and resolve the damaged attachment before completing installation. Do not treat a flush-looking surround as proof that a broken attachment is secure.

diagnostics.finding: The refitted surround has a raised edge.
diagnostics.meaning: A clip may be misaligned, or boot material may be caught at the console joint.
diagnostics.next: Reopen the affected area, check the clip and mating opening, clear any trapped boot material and reseat the surround.

verification.title: Confirm both sets of attachments
verification.body: Confirm that all three central retainers were engaged before the surround was lowered, and that all five perimeter clips are seated. Check that the surround rests evenly around its full edge without trapped boot material.

verification.title: Confirm the knob and cabin are finished
verification.body: Confirm that the knob is installed with TA-25-B, all protective tape is removed and no tools or loose pieces remain around the lever. These are completion checks for the boot replacement, not transmission diagnostic tests.

procedures.purpose: Gearshift boot removal and installation, including taped knob protection, strap-wrench removal, console and central retainers, and TA-25-B use.
Explain the floor-mounted manual gearshift lever and the relationship between the lever assembly, knob and boot.
Apply relevant precautions for preventing unintended starts, personal protection and safe handling of the specified material.

applicability.equipment: Floor-mounted manual-transmission gearshift lever and console-mounted gearshift boot.

stepGroups.title: Protect and remove the knob
stepGroups.summary: Tape the knob and unscrew it with the specified rubber strap wrench.

stepGroups.title: Release and check the boot
stepGroups.summary: Free the five console clips and three inner retainers, then check the attachment points.

stepGroups.title: Refit the boot and knob
stepGroups.summary: Reconnect the inner retainers, seat the console surround and reinstall the knob with TA-25-B.

guides.title: Replace the gearshift lever assembly — 5.2L with 3160 manual transmission
guides.summary: Remove and reinstall the external gearshift lever assembly while supporting and lowering the 3160 transmission for access.
guides.introduction: The floor-mounted gearshift lever sends the driver’s movement through a lever attached to the transmission. Its assembly belongs to the external controls, together with the knob and boot. Replacing it involves work above and below the floor: the boot and driveshaft come off, and the transmission is lowered on a transmission jack to reach the assembly.
guides.why: The crossmember supports the transmission, so its bolts must not be released until a transmission jack supports it. The lever assembly also has several different attachments with different tightening requirements. Treating them as one generic set of shifter bolts risks leaving an attachment incorrectly secured.

when.summary: When the 3160 gearshift lever assembly requires replacement or removal for access.
notes: A shifting complaint alone does not establish that the external lever assembly is faulty.

prepare.title: Provide separate vehicle and transmission support
prepare.detail: Position the vehicle in neutral on a hoist. Use the marked lifting points and check hoist-adapter clearance. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; the transmission jack supports the transmission during this operation.

prepare.title: Prepare the associated removal procedures
prepare.detail: Have the gearshift boot procedure and the applicable driveshaft procedure available. Both components must be removed before the transmission is lowered.

prepare.title: Workshop capability
prepare.detail: Vehicle hoist, transmission jack, suitable hand tools and torque wrenches for the lever assembly and transmission crossmember.

steps.title: Remove the boot and driveshaft
steps.body: Remove the [gearshift lever boot](#/document/G1796481), then remove the driveshaft using its applicable procedure. This establishes the access required by the [3160 lever procedure](#/document/G1796480).

steps.title: Support and lower the transmission
steps.body: Support the crossmember with the transmission jack before removing its bolts. Lower the transmission under controlled support to expose the gearshift assembly attachments. The illustration shows the jack beneath the crossmember during this operation.

steps.title: Detach the lever assembly
steps.body: Remove the gearshift lever assembly bolts, then remove the nuts and lift away the assembly as directed. Keep track of the separate attachment positions so the lever bolt and lever-to-transmission bolt return to their proper locations.

steps.title: Install and secure the replacement assembly
steps.body: Install the assembly and tighten its nuts to 97 lb.in (11 Nm). Tighten the gearshift lever bolt to 133 lb.in (15 Nm), then the gearshift lever-to-transmission bolt to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm). These are distinct fastening operations.

steps.title: Restore the transmission mounting and access parts
steps.body: With the jack supporting the crossmember, raise the transmission and install the crossmember bolts to 46 lb.ft (63 Nm). Reinstall the driveshaft through its procedure, then reinstall the gearshift lever boot.

watchFor.title: Uncontrolled movement when releasing the crossmember
watchFor.body: Establish transmission-jack support before removing the crossmember bolts, and retain support while raising and refastening it.

watchFor.title: Confusing the attachment torques
watchFor.body: The assembly nuts, lever bolt, lever-to-transmission bolt and crossmember bolts each have their own specified tightening value.

notes: This procedure applies to the 3160 external controls associated with the 5.2L job; it does not provide an internal gearbox diagnosis.

verification.title: Confirm complete reassembly
verification.body: Verify all four attachment groups have received their specified tightening, then confirm that the driveshaft and boot installation procedures are complete.

verification.title: Record fastening completion
verification.body: Record completion of the lever attachments and crossmember tightening separately, since they secure different parts of the installation.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L/3160 gearshift lever assembly removal and installation, including transmission lowering and crossmember restoration.
3160 gearshift lever boot removal and installation.
Vehicle lifting points and support precautions.

guides.title: Diagnose exhaust noise, vibration, odors and restriction
guides.summary: Use the exhaust symptom checks to distinguish leaks, loose supports, internal damage, restriction and normal operating characteristics.
guides.introduction: The exhaust carries combustion gases through catalytic converters and mufflers while its isolators limit vibration transfer into the body. Damage, leakage or unwanted body contact can produce quite different complaints. This inspection uses the sound, temperature, load and visible condition to choose the appropriate repair or further engine diagnosis.
guides.why: A rattle does not automatically identify a failed converter, and rust or cooling noises can be normal. Checking installation, supports and leaks first connects the symptom to a physical fault.

when.summary: For exhaust noise, vibration, unusual odor, visible corrosion or suspected restriction associated with reduced power.
notes: Use the procedure matching the fitted engine; apply the 5.0L exhaust-actuator branch only where that equipment is fitted.

prepare.title: Arrange inspection and noise-reproduction access
prepare.detail: Provide safe access to the exhaust, its supports and nearby bodywork. Have a rubber mallet for light tapping and an assistant with a shop towel for the prescribed small-leak listening check.

prepare.title: Identify the operating conditions
prepare.detail: Establish whether the complaint occurs cold, warm, at idle, during acceleration or after shutdown. Note fumes, smoke and any change in performance.

steps.title: Check the installation and visible condition
steps.body: Inspect crushed pipes, damaged mufflers or tailpipes, converters, hanger brackets and heat shields. Verify clamp position and tightening against the matching engine procedure. If nothing obvious explains the complaint, follow its symptom branch.

steps.title: Separate restriction from other performance faults
steps.body: Low power with a crushed pipe, damaged converter or loose obstruction leads to Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis (PC/ED). For possible frozen muffler condensate, check drain holes for foreign material, park indoors to thaw and test normal operation. Continue to PC/ED if the concern remains.

steps.title: Investigate burning smells
steps.body: For a burning odor at idle, possibly with smoke, inspect for trapped foreign material and missing heat shields. Repair or replace affected components. Evaluate sulfur odor separately using the distinctions below.

steps.title: Locate rattles, squeaks and buzzing
steps.body: Check shields for looseness and trapped debris. Secure loose shields with the specified worm-gear clamp; replace missing shields or affected components if noise persists. Inspect isolators, hangers and fasteners. Move the exhaust to reveal body contact, then lightly tap the muffler and converters with a rubber mallet to locate loose baffles or converter elements.

steps.title: Trace leaks and flow-related sounds
steps.body: Whistling, booming, humming or ticking that changes as the engine warms can indicate leakage; cold sputtering also calls for leak and damage checks. Inspect punctures, clamps, gaskets, sensors and welds, and look for grayish-white or black soot. Use the assistant-and-shop-towel listening check as directed. Hissing with normal performance still requires leak and loose-internal checks. Confirm enlarged drain holes as a noise source before replacing components.

steps.title: Follow vibration into the supports and body
steps.body: Drone, clunking, idle buzzing and engine drumming require checks of isolators, brackets, fasteners and body clearance. Acceleration thumping points toward misalignment checks; vibration following engine speed calls for checking isolator strain. Very low-frequency interior drumming can result from exhaust vibration exciting body resonance. Repair the identified support, alignment or component concern.

steps.title: Check fitted 5.0L exhaust actuators
steps.body: Where applicable, inspect actuator mechanisms for damage, debris and restricted movement. Clear restrictions associated with low power or incorrect valve positioning. Repair or replace components as necessary when cleaning does not resolve the identified concern.

watchFor.title: Fumes accompanying noise
watchFor.body: Inspect the entire exhaust for leakage; soot can identify the escape point.

watchFor.title: Noise from inside a component
watchFor.body: A loose muffler baffle or converter element requires component assessment even when external supports appear sound.

notes: Clamps must be correctly positioned as well as tightened. Each engine-specific procedure supplies its applicable details.

diagnostics.finding: A slight sulfur or rotten-egg smell occurs occasionally
diagnostics.meaning: Fuel sulfur can produce this normal catalytic-converter characteristic.
diagnostics.next: No repair is required for that condition; suspected rich running or misfire requires PC/ED diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Surface rust is visible without perforations
diagnostics.meaning: Heat and road-salt exposure can produce normal surface corrosion.
diagnostics.next: Inspect for perforation before deciding that replacement is justified.

diagnostics.finding: Pinging occurs after a hot engine is switched off
diagnostics.meaning: Exhaust expansion and contraction during cooling can produce normal pinging.
diagnostics.next: No repair is indicated for this specific cooldown characteristic.

verification.title: Recheck the identified condition
verification.body: Verify correct installation, secure supports and clearance at the repaired area. Repeat the relevant noise or leak check; after thawing suspected frozen condensate, explicitly test for normal operation.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record the reproduced symptom, physical finding and action taken, including whether the outcome was repair, a normal characteristic or referral to PC/ED.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost exhaust performance, odor, corrosion, noise and vibration diagnosis.
3.7L Duratec exhaust performance, odor, corrosion, noise and vibration diagnosis.
5.0L exhaust diagnosis, including restricted or incorrectly positioning exhaust actuators where fitted.
5.2L exhaust performance, odor, corrosion, noise and vibration diagnosis.

guides.title: Remove and refit the 2.3L EcoBoost catalytic converter
guides.summary: Remove the converter from its exhaust connections and mounting, then refit it with new nuts and gasket and check for leaks.
guides.introduction: The catalytic converter treats exhaust gases as they pass through the exhaust system. This assembly has connections for a heated oxygen sensor (HO2S) and a catalyst monitor sensor, as well as an exhaust clamp, isolator and mounting bolts. The job can involve removing an existing converter for reuse or installing a replacement, and that distinction affects whether the sensors can remain fitted.
guides.why: Both sensor electrical connectors must be disconnected even when their sensors stay in the converter. The exhaust connections must be cleaned before assembly, and the removed nuts and gasket are discarded. These requirements separate the electrical connections safely and provide the specified starting condition for rebuilding the exhaust joints. A leak check completes the work.

when.summary: When the 2.3L converter needs removal for repair access or a confirmed replacement requirement.
notes: This procedure covers removal and installation; it does not establish whether the catalyst itself has failed.

prepare.title: Provide secure underside access
