prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the specified lifting points. Check adapter clearance around the exhaust and suspension, and never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare the replacement sealing parts
prepare.detail: Have new connection nuts and a new gasket available, together with suitable fastening and torque-measuring equipment. Plan to clean every exhaust connection before reassembly.

prepare.title: Decide whether the converter is being reused
prepare.detail: If the original converter is retained, both sensors may remain installed in it. For replacement work involving sensor removal or fitting, obtain the applicable sensor instructions; the exhaust fastener settings are not sensor installation specifications.

steps.title: Position the vehicle
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a hoist using the linked lifting procedure. Identify the sensor connections, exhaust clamp, isolator and converter mounting.

steps.title: Release the first connection and sensor wiring
steps.body: Disconnect the heated oxygen sensor electrical connector. Remove and discard the connection nuts identified in the procedure, then disconnect the catalyst monitor sensor electrical connector.

steps.title: Separate the rear exhaust connection
steps.body: Loosen the clamp, release its tab and slide the clamp back onto the muffler. Separate the muffler and tailpipe from the catalytic converter; loosening the clamp alone does not complete the specified release.

steps.title: Remove the converter and gasket
steps.body: Detach the exhaust isolator, then remove the mounting bolts and catalytic converter. Remove and discard the gasket so it cannot be inadvertently reused during assembly.

steps.title: Clean and rebuild the connections
steps.body: Clean all exhaust connections and reverse the removal sequence using new nuts and a new gasket. Tighten the connection nuts to 40 Nm, the exhaust clamp to 48 Nm and the converter mounting bolts to 25 Nm. Restore the isolator and both sensor electrical connections.

watchFor.title: Sensors retained but wiring still attached
watchFor.body: Leaving sensors installed in a reused converter does not remove the requirement to unplug their electrical connectors before removal.

notes: The fastening values in this guide apply to the 2.3L EcoBoost converter procedure.

diagnostics.finding: An exhaust leak remains after assembly.
diagnostics.meaning: The required leak check has not passed; this finding alone does not establish catalyst failure.
diagnostics.next: Locate and correct the leaking connection, then repeat the exhaust leak check.

verification.title: Check and record exhaust sealing
verification.body: Check the exhaust system for leaks after installation. Record the result and any connection that required correction.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost catalytic converter removal and installation, sensor-retention option, replacement nuts and gasket, and final leak check.
Correct lifting points and precautions for underside access.

guides.title: Replace the muffler and tailpipe assembly
guides.summary: Remove and refit the rear exhaust using the correct engine branch, then complete alignment, fastening and leak checks.
guides.introduction: The muffler and tailpipe assembly reduces exhaust noise and carries exhaust gases to the rear outlets. Its rubber hanger isolators support the assembly while limiting vibration transfer to the body. The repair differs by engine: the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L procedures include a partial-replacement option, while the 5.2L path includes tailpipe actuator wiring and a rear axle air deflector.
guides.why: The long assembly needs support as its joints and hangers are released. On the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L, incorrect support can damage the flexible joint, while an inaccurate partial-replacement cut can create noise, vibration and harshness or require replacement of the entire assembly. Clean joints, correct clamp sequencing and outlet alignment matter during reassembly.

when.summary: When rear exhaust repair requires assembly removal or an applicable partial replacement.
notes: Choose the engine procedure before separating joints or planning a cut.
The convertible brace operation applies within the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L procedures.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and assembly support
prepare.detail: Use a hoist with the vehicle in NEUTRAL and follow the lifting procedure. Locate the marked lifting points and check adapter clearance. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Arrange assistance for handling the assembly.

prepare.title: Prepare the applicable materials
prepare.detail: Have torque tools and, for partial replacement, suitable cutting equipment. Convertible brace reassembly in the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L procedures requires cleaned retainers and Motorcraft Threadlock and Sealer TA-25-B.

steps.title: Create access for the fitted arrangement
steps.body: For a convertible covered by the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L procedure, remove the brace and retainers. For 5.2L, remove the rear axle air deflector in order: rear bolts, push-pin retainers, front bolts, rivet-style push-pin retainers, then the deflector.

steps.title: Release the front connections
steps.body: On 2.3L, loosen the clamp and separate the assembly from the catalytic converter; on 3.7L and 5.0L, release the connections to the catalytic converters. On 5.2L, disconnect both tailpipe actuator electrical connectors and detach their wiring retainers, then loosen the clamp nuts, release the locking tabs and move the clamps rearward.

steps.title: Remove the supported assembly
steps.body: Remove the left- and right-hand rear exhaust hanger isolator bracket bolts from the rear subframe. Unhook the rear isolators and lower the muffler and tailpipe assembly with assistance.

steps.title: Perform partial replacement only where specified
steps.body: For 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L partial replacement, align the new component with the old assembly before marking the cut. Cut the resonator away only at the position illustrated in that engine's procedure. This cutting branch is not specified for 5.2L.

steps.title: Prepare joints and refit the assembly
steps.body: Clean all exhaust connections. For partial replacement, assemble the front muffler to the rear muffler entry pipes, initially tightening the clamps only enough for handling while retaining adjustment. Follow the illustrated joint-clamp tightening sequence, then install the assembly and rear isolators. Secure the rear hanger brackets to the subframe.

steps.title: Finish alignment and variant-specific reassembly
steps.body: On 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L, align the decorative tips with the rear bumper openings before completing the specified clamp sequence. Refit an applicable convertible brace with cleaned, threadlocked retainers. On 5.2L, reverse its removal sequence, restoring the clamps, actuator connections, wiring retainers and air deflector; its front and rear deflector bolts have different tightening values.

steps.title: Check the completed exhaust
steps.body: With reassembly complete, check the exhaust system for leaks. Use the selected engine procedure for the exact clamp sequences and fastening values.

watchFor.title: Flexible-joint loading
watchFor.body: For 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L, do not excessively bend or twist the exhaust, or let it hang from the flexible joint.

watchFor.title: Rubber deterioration
watchFor.body: Those same procedures prohibit oil- or grease-based lubricants on the isolators because they can deteriorate the rubber.

notes: The 5.2L hanger-removal illustration is identified as a similar application; use the 5.2L written sequence for its equipment.

diagnostics.finding: Decorative tips do not align with the bumper openings on 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L.
diagnostics.meaning: The installation still needs positional adjustment.
diagnostics.next: Adjust the tips before completing the final clamp tightening sequence.

verification.title: Confirm completion
verification.body: Confirm the applicable tip alignment, hanger fastening, brace or deflector installation, and any actuator wiring reconnection.

verification.title: Record the leak-check result
verification.body: Record the engine variant and final exhaust leak-check result after the connections have been cleaned, assembled and tightened.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L muffler and tailpipe removal, optional partial replacement, installation and leak check; includes the convertible brace branch.
3.7L muffler and tailpipe removal, optional partial replacement, installation and leak check; includes the convertible brace branch.
5.0L muffler and tailpipe removal, optional partial replacement, installation and leak check; includes the convertible brace branch.
5.2L muffler and tailpipe removal and installation, including the rear axle air deflector, actuator wiring and locking clamps.
Correct lifting points, vehicle support and hoist-clearance precautions.

guides.title: Replace the left catalytic converter: 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Remove and refit the left catalytic converter using the engine-specific route, including manifold replacement on the 5.0L.
guides.introduction: The left-hand (LH) catalytic converter treats exhaust gases to reduce pollutants. Its service arrangement differs substantially between engines: the 3.7L and 5.2L have separate converter removal procedures, while the 5.0L converter is serviced with the left exhaust manifold. Follow only the branch for your engine.
guides.why: Clean joints and the specified replacement hardware help the exhaust seal properly. The 5.0L also requires controlled engine lifting and, on the applicable steering layout, careful steering-shaft separation.

when.summary: When diagnosis justifies converter replacement, or the left converter must be removed for access.
notes: The 5.0L job requires substantially more access and support work than the other engine branches.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underside access
prepare.detail: Select NEUTRAL and position the vehicle on a hoist using the lifting overview. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Plan the 5.0L support work
prepare.detail: Have the specified engine lifting bracket, support bars and adapters, and the capability to perform the applicable steering-shaft work.

prepare.title: Obtain replacement hardware
prepare.detail: Allow for new converter nuts on the 3.7L; nuts and a gasket on the 5.2L; and manifold nuts, studs and a gasket on the 5.0L. Any removed steering-shaft bolt must also be replaced.

steps.title: 3.7L: release the separate converter
steps.body: Following the 3.7L procedure, loosen the muffler clamps, release their tabs and slide them back. Separate the muffler and tailpipe from the converters. Disconnect the heated oxygen sensor (HO2S), remove and discard the nuts, then disconnect the catalyst monitor sensor and remove the converter.

steps.title: 5.2L: release the clamp and flange
steps.body: Disconnect the catalyst monitor sensor and detach its wiring retainer. Loosen the clamp nuts, release the locking tab and move the clamp rearward. Remove and discard the flange nuts, remove the converter and discard its gasket.

steps.title: 5.0L: establish access
steps.body: Use the linked manifold procedure. Disconnect both battery cables. On left-hand-drive, rear-wheel-drive vehicles, loosen the dash seal as directed and set the steering straight ahead. Follow the procedure through removal of the intake components, both engine-mount nuts, radiator sight shield, cross brace, battery tray, cowl components and battery heat shield.

steps.title: 5.0L: support the engine and clear the steering shaft
steps.body: Install the specified engine-support equipment with its legs on body structure near the strut towers, never on the fenders. Carefully raise the engine 45 mm. On the left-hand-drive, rear-wheel-drive branch, discard the lower steering-shaft bolt, separate the shaft from its coupling and secure it to the frame rail.

steps.title: 5.0L: remove the manifold and converter assembly
steps.body: Remove the muffler inlet pipe, position the air deflector aside and remove the engine-mount bracket. Disconnect both exhaust-sensor connectors and detach the harness retainers. Remove the manifold, discarding its nuts, gasket and studs.

steps.title: Refit using the applicable tightening method
steps.body: Clean all exhaust connections and reverse the relevant removal sequence with the required new parts. Tighten the 5.2L converter nuts evenly. On the 5.0L, start the manifold nuts finger-tight, then follow the illustrated tightening sequence and stages. Use the torque specifications for that engine.

steps.title: Restore the surrounding components
steps.body: Reconnect the sensors and restore wiring retainers and all displaced components. On the 5.0L, complete engine-mount, steering, access-component and battery reassembly through the manifold procedure before final checks.

watchFor.title: Steering-shaft damage
watchFor.body: Never hammer, pry or force the steering column or shafts. Incorrect handling or reuse of the shaft bolt can compromise steering control.

watchFor.title: Damaged dash sealing
watchFor.body: On the applicable 5.0L branch, protect the sealer foam and bracket retainers; damage can admit noise, fumes, air or water.

notes: When reusing the converter or manifold, the sensors may remain installed: both sensors on the 3.7L and 5.0L, and the catalyst monitor sensor on the 5.2L. Their electrical connectors must still be disconnected.
If both 5.0L manifolds are being removed together, use the engine-support setup specified by the right-hand manifold procedure.

verification.title: Check exhaust sealing
verification.body: Check the exhaust system for leaks after installation and record the result.

verification.title: Complete the applicable steering inspection
verification.body: After the 5.0L steering shaft has been reassembled, perform the referenced Steering Column Collapsed Check and record its result.

procedures.purpose: 3.7L: separate left catalytic converter removal, installation and exhaust leak check.
5.0L: establishes that the left converter is serviced with the left exhaust manifold.
5.2L: left converter removal and installation, including clamp, new flange hardware and gasket.
5.0L: complete manifold/converter assembly procedure, engine support and applicable steering-shaft work.
Correct vehicle lifting points and hoist-positioning precautions.

guides.title: Replace the right catalytic converter — 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L
guides.summary: Remove and refit the right catalytic converter using the correct engine-specific sensor, clamp, gasket and fastening sequence.
guides.introduction: The right-hand (RH) catalytic converter treats exhaust gases as they pass through the exhaust system. Its connections must seal properly, and the associated sensor wiring must be released before the assembly moves. These engine variants share the same overall repair purpose, but their connections, sensor-release details and converter-nut torque differ. Select the fitted engine’s branch before beginning.
guides.why: Clean mating connections and the specified replacement hardware are central to restoring an exhaust-tight assembly. Sensor connectors must be disconnected even when a converter is only being removed temporarily. Correct lifting is equally important because the work takes place beneath the vehicle and involves separating exhaust components.

when.summary: When the right catalytic converter requires replacement or removal for another established repair.
notes: Follow only the branch for the fitted engine, then complete the common installation and leak check.

If reusing the converter, the 3.7L and 5.0L instructions allow the heated oxygen sensor (HO2S) and catalyst monitor sensor to remain installed, but require their electrical connectors to be disconnected. The 5.2L instruction covers the catalyst monitor sensor.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a suitable hoist and the specified lifting points. Have the capability to support and handle the exhaust during separation.

prepare.title: Obtain replacement hardware
prepare.detail: All three branches discard the converter attachment nuts. The 5.0L and 5.2L branches also discard the gasket. Have the correct replacements and torque tools ready.

steps.title: Place the vehicle on a hoist
steps.body: With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on a hoist using [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631). Locate the triangle-marked lifting points and check hoist-adapter clearance from the suspension, exhaust and steering components.

steps.title: For the 3.7L, release the rear connection and sensors
steps.body: Follow [3.7L converter removal](#/document/G1688091). Loosen the clamps, release the tab and slide the clamps back onto the muffler. Separate the muffler and tailpipe from the converters. Disconnect the HO2S connector, remove and discard the converter nuts, then disconnect the catalyst monitor connector and remove the RH converter.

steps.title: For the 5.0L, separate the correct exhaust connections
steps.body: Follow [5.0L converter removal](#/document/G1688105). Loosen the clamps, release the tabs and move the clamps back onto the muffler. Separate the muffler and tailpipe from the RH converter and left-hand muffler inlet pipe. Disconnect the catalyst monitor connector, observing the retained-sensor disconnection requirement. Access the converter nuts from the engine bay, remove and discard them, remove the converter and discard its gasket.

steps.title: For the 5.2L, release the wiring before the clamp
steps.body: Follow [5.2L converter removal](#/document/G1805803). Disconnect the catalyst monitor connector and detach its wiring retainer. Loosen the clamp nuts, release the locking tab and move the clamp rearward. Remove and discard the converter nuts, remove the RH converter and discard the gasket.

steps.title: Clean and refit using the selected engine procedure
steps.body: Clean all exhaust connections before assembly and reverse the relevant removal sequence. Fit new nuts and, for the 5.0L and 5.2L, a new gasket. Converter attachment nuts tighten to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm) on the 3.7L and 5.0L, or 35 lb.ft (48 Nm) on the 5.2L. Tighten the 5.2L nuts evenly. The exhaust clamp setting is 35 lb.ft (48 Nm). Restore all released connectors and retainers.

steps.title: Check the completed exhaust assembly
steps.body: Check the exhaust system for leaks after installation. A leaking connection requires correction before the repair is complete.

watchFor.title: Unsafe lifting or support
watchFor.body: Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. The emergency wheel-changing jack is not suitable for this work.

watchFor.title: Transferring specifications between engines
watchFor.body: The 5.2L converter-nut setting differs from the 3.7L and 5.0L setting. Keep the selected engine procedure with the job.

notes: Follow the selected engine’s converter connection details and replace the nuts and gaskets identified for that variant.

diagnostics.finding: An exhaust leak remains after reassembly.
diagnostics.meaning: The completed exhaust system has not passed its required sealing check.
diagnostics.next: Locate the leaking connection and correct its assembly using the applicable engine procedure.

verification.title: Confirm branch-specific reassembly
verification.body: Check replacement nuts, the required new gasket, sensor connections and the 5.2L wiring retainer where applicable.

verification.title: Record the leak-check result
verification.body: Record whether the exhaust system passed the final leak check and any connection that required correction.

procedures.purpose: RH catalytic converter removal and installation for the 3.7L, including HO2S and catalyst monitor disconnection.
RH catalytic converter removal and installation for the 5.0L, including engine-bay nut access and gasket replacement.
RH catalytic converter removal and installation for the 5.2L, including wiring-retainer release, new gasket and evenly tightened attachment nuts.
Lifting-point identification, vehicle support and hoist-clearance precautions.

guides.title: Replace the 5.0L muffler inlet pipe
guides.summary: Separate the exhaust connections, release the inlet pipe’s ball clamp and bracket tab, then refit and check for leaks.
guides.introduction: The muffler inlet pipe carries exhaust toward the muffler assembly through a removable section of the exhaust system. This job opens the neighboring clamped connections and releases the inlet pipe’s own ball-clamp joint and retaining tab. It is an underbody repair requiring proper hoist access and careful reassembly of the exhaust joints.
guides.why: Exhaust connections must be clean before they are reassembled so their mating surfaces can seat properly. The bracket tab must be released along with the ball clamp before the pipe is removed. The two clamp locations have different tightening specifications, and a final leak check establishes whether the reassembled system seals.

when.summary: When the muffler inlet pipe requires replacement or removal for access.
notes: An exhaust leak needs to be located before deciding which pipe or connection requires repair.

prepare.title: Safe underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and identify the approved lifting points from the stamped triangles. Position adapters clear of exhaust, suspension and other underbody components.

prepare.title: Joint and clamp work
prepare.detail: Have suitable clamp tools, torque equipment and the means to clean every exhaust connection opened during the job.

steps.title: Position the vehicle on the hoist
steps.body: Place the transmission in NEUTRAL and follow the [jacking and lifting procedure](#/document/G1663631). Check lift clearance and adapter placement before raising the vehicle; incorrect contact can damage the exhaust or make the vehicle unstable.

steps.title: Separate the adjoining exhaust assembly
steps.body: Following the [5.0L inlet-pipe procedure](#/document/G1689452), loosen the clamps and separate the muffler and tailpipe from the right-hand catalytic converter and left-hand muffler inlet pipe. These connections must be released before removing the inlet pipe.

steps.title: Release and remove the inlet pipe
steps.body: Loosen the ball clamp, release the bracket tab and remove the muffler inlet pipe. Account for both the clamped joint and the retaining tab rather than trying to withdraw the pipe while either remains engaged.

steps.title: Clean, refit and check
steps.body: Clean all opened exhaust connections before assembly. Reverse the removal sequence, restoring the inlet pipe and bracket engagement, then the muffler and tailpipe connections. Tighten the ball clamp to 30 Nm and the adjoining muffler/tailpipe clamps to 48 Nm. Check the exhaust system for leaks.

watchFor.title: Incorrect vehicle support
watchFor.body: Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. The vehicle’s emergency jack is not intended for this repair.

watchFor.title: Confusing clamp specifications
watchFor.body: Keep the inlet pipe’s ball-clamp specification separate from the adjoining exhaust-clamp specification.

notes: This sequence and its clamp specifications apply to the 5.0L exhaust arrangement.

diagnostics.finding: An exhaust leak remains after reassembly.
diagnostics.meaning: The repair has not passed its required sealing check.
diagnostics.next: Locate and correct the leaking connection, then repeat the check.

verification.title: Assembly completion
verification.body: Confirm the bracket tab is restored and each opened clamp is tightened to its correct specification.

verification.title: Recorded leak-check result
verification.body: Record whether the completed exhaust-system leak check passed and identify any connection requiring further correction.

procedures.purpose: 5.0L muffler inlet pipe removal, installation, clamp tightening and final exhaust leak check.
Approved lifting points, hoist positioning and vehicle-support precautions.

guides.title: Remove and inspect the 5.2L exhaust tailpipe actuator
guides.summary: Remove the tailpipe actuator and spring, then check the exhaust valve for free movement and weld-bead obstruction.
guides.introduction: The exhaust tailpipe actuator operates a valve flap at the muffler outlet. Removing the actuator and its spring lets you examine valve movement directly. This separates a mechanical restriction in the tailpipe from assumptions about the actuator’s electrical operation.
guides.why: Supporting the muffler before releasing its hangers controls its weight during access. Checking the exposed valve matters because an obstructed flap cannot move properly even if the actuator itself is serviceable.

when.summary: When actuator removal is required or the tailpipe valve needs direct inspection for restricted movement.

prepare.title: Lifting and muffler support
prepare.detail: Arrange a vehicle hoist and transmission jack. Use the specified lifting points and check adapter clearance around the exhaust and suspension. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Parts handling
prepare.detail: Prepare to keep the removed actuator and spring together and discard the actuator mounting nuts.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle and expose the muffler
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on the hoist. Remove the rear underbody shield: release its rear bolts, push-pin retainers, front bolts and rivet-style push-pin retainers in that order.

steps.title: Disconnect and lower the supported assembly
steps.body: Disconnect the actuator electrical connectors and wire guides on both sides. Support the muffler assembly with the transmission jack before removing the hanger-bracket bolts. Lower the jack 6 inches (152 mm) for access.

steps.title: Remove the actuator and spring
steps.body: Remove and discard the actuator mounting nuts, then remove the actuator. Remove its spring. The left-side procedure also applies similarly to the right side; keep the muffler supported throughout.

steps.title: Check the exposed valve
steps.body: Rotate the top of the valve by hand to assess free movement, turning clockwise to the fully open position. Inspect the flap inside the tailpipe tip, specifically checking whether weld beads restrict its travel.

watchFor.title: Interference during valve travel
watchFor.body: Record where movement becomes restricted and whether the flap contacts a weld bead.

notes: This mechanical inspection does not establish whether the actuator operates electrically.

diagnostics.finding: The flap contacts a weld bead or does not move freely.
diagnostics.meaning: A mechanical restriction is present.
diagnostics.next: Record the obstruction and obtain the applicable repair direction; this inspection does not authorize modifying the valve or weld.

verification.title: Record the inspection outcome
verification.body: Document free movement, ability to reach fully open and any visible obstruction.

verification.title: Leave the assembly safely supported
verification.body: Completion is the actuator and spring removed with findings recorded and the muffler supported. Reassembly and readiness to drive remain outstanding.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L actuator access, removal and mechanical valve inspection.
Vehicle lifting points and hoist positioning precautions.

guides.title: Diagnose a fuel tank that fills slowly
guides.summary: Use visual inspection, evaporative-emissions fault codes and fuel-tank pressure during filling to distinguish a venting restriction from a filler-pipe or tank concern.
guides.introduction: As fuel enters the tank, displaced air must leave through the filler pipe or onboard refueling vapor recovery system. A restriction in either path can impede filling. The engine-specific tests share a diagnostic sequence that separates vapor-system restrictions from filler-pipe and tank concerns.
guides.why: A slow fill does not identify a failed tank or canister. Pressure observations with the vapor system connected, then disconnected only when directed, help locate the restriction. The tank-replacement decision belongs at the end of the specified branches.

when.summary: When the slow-to-fill concern is present during testing.
notes: Other fuel-system complaints go to Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis (PC/ED).

prepare.title: Provide diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of reading evaporative-emissions codes and Fuel Tank Pressure (FTP) data. Follow Ford diagnostic methods, including preliminary checks and review of previous repairs.

prepare.title: Plan the correct service access
prepare.detail: Vapor-coupling disconnection and filler-pipe or tank removal require the applicable service procedures and their precautions. Choose removal and installation instructions for the fitted engine.

steps.title: A1: Inspect the filling and venting components
steps.body: Inspect the filler pipe, its vent tube if equipped, the evaporative emission (EVAP) system, tank inlet check valve and fuel level vent valve for damage. Both valves are part of the tank. Correct an identified cause by repair or replacement; otherwise continue to A2.

steps.title: A2: Check for EVAP diagnostic trouble codes
steps.body: Connect the scan tool and retrieve diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Any EVAP DTC sends the diagnosis to PC/ED; a code is not proof of a failed component. With no EVAP codes, proceed to A3.

steps.title: A3: Observe pressure during filling
steps.body: Monitor FTP while filling. Normal behavior starts at 2.6 volts and rises 0.3 to 0.7 of a volt from that starting value. Consult PC/ED reference information. An in-specification result leads to A5; an out-of-specification result leads to A4.

steps.title: A4: Separate the EVAP venting path
steps.body: Disconnect the fuel tank-to-EVAP canister quick-connect coupling at the canister and monitor FTP during filling again. If pressure now meets specification, inspect the EVAP system for blockage or restriction, repair it where possible and replace affected components if it cannot be repaired. If pressure remains outside specification, continue to A5.

steps.title: A5: Inspect the filler-pipe assembly
steps.body: Remove the assembly using the engine-specific procedure. Check the filler pipe and vent tube, if fitted, for blockage or restriction. Repair the restriction where possible; otherwise replace the affected pipe or vent tube. If neither is restricted, proceed to A6.

steps.title: A6: Evaluate the tank inlet check valve
steps.body: Inspect for restriction or sticking. Repair a restriction if possible; otherwise install a new tank. If the valve is neither restricted nor sticking, A6 also directs tank replacement. Apply this final decision only after following the preceding diagnostic branches.

watchFor.title: Normal pressure does not end the investigation
watchFor.body: An acceptable connected-system FTP result directs inspection of the filler pipe; it does not establish that the slow-fill complaint is resolved.

watchFor.title: Capless assembly limits
watchFor.body: On the 5.0L and 5.2L Easy Fuel capless assemblies, do not modify the filler pipe. Assembly service requires replacement.

notes: Use the matching engine procedure even though the slow-fill decision sequence is shared.

diagnostics.finding: FTP becomes normal only with the tank-to-canister connection disconnected.
diagnostics.meaning: The test directs attention to blockage or restriction in the EVAP system.
diagnostics.next: Locate the restriction before deciding which component needs replacement.

verification.title: Evaluate the filling observations
verification.body: Compare observed filling with the normal condition of steady fuel flow, and interpret FTP using its starting value and rise.

verification.title: Record the branch evidence
verification.body: Record EVAP codes, connected and disconnected FTP results when tested, and the restriction found or final A6 replacement decision.

guides.title: Check low-side fuel pressure on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Measure fuel supply pressure through the correct engine-specific connection after pressure release, controlled reconnection and a leak inspection.
guides.introduction: This check measures the low-pressure fuel supply. On the 2.3L engine, the gauge connects ahead of the high-pressure pump; on the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines, it connects between the jumper tube and fuel rail. The result helps assess fuel delivery, but it does not by itself identify which component caused an abnormal reading.
guides.why: The gauge must be installed at the correct connection after pressure release. Pump-control connectors disconnected during that release must be restored before testing, or the setup can produce a misleading result. The leak inspection comes before completing the pressure test, and residual fuel must be drained deliberately before removing the kit.

when.summary: When fuel-system diagnosis requires a measured low-pressure supply reading.
notes: Use the pressure specification and test conditions applicable to the engine being checked.

prepare.title: Obtain the test equipment
prepare.detail: Use Fuel Pressure Test Kit 310-D009 (D95L-7211-A) and an appropriate container for fuel drained from the kit.

prepare.title: Arrange the required capabilities
prepare.detail: Be competent in pressurized-fuel work, the engine-specific pressure-release and quick-coupling procedures, and battery disconnection and reconnection.

prepare.title: Have the acceptance criteria ready
prepare.detail: Obtain the applicable engine's fuel-pressure specification before interpreting the reading. No numerical pressure range is supplied here.

steps.title: Select the engine path
steps.body: Use the [2.3L](#/document/G1671507), [3.7L](#/document/G1671533), [5.0L](#/document/G1671554) or [5.2L](#/document/G1794915) check. For the 2.3L, first remove the nuts and engine appearance cover.

steps.title: Release pressure before disconnecting
steps.body: Carry out the matching Fuel System Pressure Release procedure, then disconnect the battery ground cable using the [battery procedure](#/document/G1692356). Preserve this order before opening the fuel coupling.

steps.title: Install the gauge in the supply connection
steps.body: Follow the engine-specific quick-release coupling procedure. On the 2.3L, disconnect the jumper tube from the high-pressure pump and install the kit between them. On the other engines, install it between the jumper tube and fuel rail.

steps.title: Restore pump control and battery power
steps.body: Reconnect the fuel pump driver module (FPDM) connector disconnected during pressure release on the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L. On the 5.2L, reconnect both Fuel Pump Control Module connectors. Then reconnect the battery ground cable.

steps.title: Inspect for leaks before testing
steps.body: Perform the required key-on, engine-off (KOEO) visual fuel-leak inspection before completing the pressure test. A leaking connection must be addressed before continuing.

steps.title: Measure and compare
steps.body: Check pressure against the range in the applicable engine's Specifications section. Record the engine, reading, test conditions and specified range so the result can be interpreted accurately.

steps.title: Drain the kit and restore the system
steps.body: After testing, disconnect the battery ground cable. Open the kit's drain valve and collect residual fuel in the appropriate container. Remove the kit by reversing installation and restore the original connections. On the 2.3L, reinstall the appearance cover and tighten its nuts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm).

steps.title: Check the restored fuel connection
steps.body: After the original fuel connection and battery power are restored, complete the matching pressure-release procedure’s end-of-service checks. Confirm that the pump-control connector or connectors and rear seat cushion are restored, cycle the ignition and wait 3 seconds to pressurize the system. Inspect for leaks before starting, then start the engine and check for leaks again. The earlier check with the tester fitted does not verify the connection disturbed when the tester was removed.

watchFor.title: Unrestored pump connectors
watchFor.body: Verify the pressure-release disconnections have been reversed before interpreting absent pressure, especially the two-connector 5.2L branch.

watchFor.title: Wrong pressure circuit
watchFor.body: The 2.3L procedure measures supply to the high-pressure pump; it is not a high-pressure outlet test.

notes: KOEO is explicitly the leak-inspection condition; use the applicable specification to establish the pressure-measurement conditions.
Use the gauge-connection illustration for your selected engine; the connection arrangement is not universal.

diagnostics.finding: A leak is visible during the KOEO inspection.
diagnostics.meaning: The test connection is not ready for pressure measurement.
diagnostics.next: Stop and address the leak using the required pressure-release and coupling procedures.

diagnostics.finding: Pressure falls outside the applicable specified range.
diagnostics.meaning: Supply pressure does not meet the requirement under the tested conditions; this does not identify a failed pump by itself.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the setup and restored control connections, then continue fuel-system diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Pressure is within the applicable range.
diagnostics.meaning: The measured supply pressure meets the requirement under those conditions.
diagnostics.next: Retain the result and continue investigating any remaining complaint.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Keep the measured pressure, engine, test conditions and comparison range together.

verification.title: Confirm restoration
verification.body: Confirm the kit is removed, original fuel and electrical connections are restored, and the 2.3L appearance cover is refitted where removed.

verification.title: Verify the final connection under pressure
verification.body: Record a leak-free inspection of the restored original connection before engine start and again with the engine running.

guides.title: Release fuel pressure before fuel-system service
guides.summary: Disable the fuel pump control module connection or connections, run the engine to a stall, and restore fuel pressure with checks for leaks after service.
guides.introduction: The fuel pumps supply pressurized fuel to the engine, and system pressure can remain after the pumps stop. This procedure reduces that pressure before a repair that calls for it. Access is beneath the left-hand side of the rear seat cushion. The 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L procedures disconnect one module connector; the 5.2L requires both fuel pump control module connectors to be disconnected.
guides.why: Turning the ignition off alone does not establish that the fuel system is depressurized. Disabling the pump supply and allowing the engine to consume available fuel reduces pressure in a controlled sequence. On gasoline turbocharged direct-injection systems, the procedure removes most pressure from both the low- and high-pressure sides. That wording matters: an engine stall does not certify that every fuel connection is pressure-free.

when.summary: Before a fuel-system repair that requires fuel pressure to be released.
notes: This is a service prerequisite, not a test proving that a fuel pump or control module has failed.

prepare.title: Identify the connector arrangement
prepare.detail: Confirm the engine variant and use the rear seat cushion removal procedure to reach the modules on the left-hand side.

prepare.title: Plan the subsequent fuel repair
prepare.detail: Have the component-specific repair procedure available, including any residual-pressure precautions. High-pressure fuel work requires the appropriate service capability beyond this pressure-release sequence.

steps.title: Expose and disconnect the pump controls
steps.body: Remove the rear seat cushion. Disconnect the fuel pump control module connector identified as FPDM in the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L procedure. On the 5.2L, disconnect both fuel pump control module connectors; its system has two modules.

steps.title: Run the engine until it stalls
steps.body: Start the engine and allow it to idle until it stalls, then turn the ignition OFF. This is the prescribed pressure-reduction step. Follow the selected fuel-component procedure for the actual repair, retaining its precautions for any remaining pressure.

steps.title: Restore the electrical connections after service
steps.body: Once the fuel-system work is complete, reconnect the single module connector or both 5.2L connectors as applicable. Reinstall the rear seat cushion using its removal and installation procedure.

steps.title: Repressurize and check in two stages
steps.body: Cycle the ignition key and wait 3 seconds to pressurize the system. Check for leaks before starting the engine. If that check is satisfactory, start the engine and check for leaks again with the system operating.

watchFor.title: Residual pressure on direct-injection equipment
watchFor.body: The low- and high-pressure statement is conditional on gasoline turbocharged direct injection. It neither identifies every engine here as direct-injected nor promises complete pressure removal.

watchFor.title: Leakage before startup
watchFor.body: If fuel leaks during the initial pressurization check, do not proceed to engine startup. Return to the serviced connection or component.

diagnostics.finding: The engine stalls after the correct module connector or connectors are disconnected.
diagnostics.meaning: This is the expected outcome of the pressure-release sequence, not evidence of pump failure.
diagnostics.next: Turn the ignition OFF and continue under the component-specific service instructions.

verification.title: Confirm restored connections
verification.body: Check that the correct connector count has been reconnected and the rear seat cushion has been installed.

verification.title: Record both leak checks
verification.body: Record the results of the check after ignition cycling and the separate check with the engine running.

3.7L Duratec pressure release using its single module connector and post-service restoration sequence.
5.0L pressure release using its single module connector and post-service restoration sequence.
5.2L pressure release requiring both fuel pump control module connectors and subsequent leak checks.

guides.title: Drain both sides of the saddle-type fuel tank
guides.summary: Lower the fuel level through the capless filler, then drain the left and right tank saddles through their separate service openings.
guides.introduction: The saddle-shaped fuel tank has left and right sections that must each be emptied during complete draining. The initial transfer through the filler lowers the fuel beneath the pump mounting flange; it does not finish the job. Access beneath the rear seat then allows the remaining fuel to be removed through the pump-and-sender opening and the separate fuel-level-sensor opening.
guides.why: Opening the tank before lowering the fuel level can release fuel at the mounting flange. The float arms are easily damaged during handling, and the flange sealing surfaces determine whether the tank can seal correctly afterward. Damaged sealing surfaces require component replacement rather than polishing or reshaping.

when.summary: When a repair requires the fuel tank to be completely drained.
notes: Choose the pressure-release and fuel-coupling procedures for the actual engine.
The draining endpoint leaves the tank units positioned aside; subsequent installation requires the applicable component procedures.

prepare.title: Provide fuel-transfer capability
prepare.detail: Use Fuel Tanker 100 GPM, special tool 292-00004, and fuel tank lock-ring tool 310-123. This work requires controlled fuel transfer, storage and fuel-system pressure release.

prepare.title: Prepare filler and cabin access
prepare.detail: Locate the supplemental refueling adapter in the luggage compartment. Prepare a 6 ft. length of 5/8 in. semi-rigid fuel drain tube and access to the rear seat cushion.

steps.title: Release pressure before disconnecting the battery
steps.body: Complete the engine-specific Fuel System Pressure Release procedure, then disconnect the battery ground cable using the battery procedure. Preserve this order before opening fuel connections.

steps.title: Lower the level through the filler
steps.body: Insert the supplemental adapter and drain tube into the Easy Fuel filler until the tube reaches the tank. Connect the tanker and remove as much fuel as possible through this route. This first transfer lowers fuel below the pump-and-sender flange and removes most residual fuel from the filler pipe.

steps.title: Open the pump-and-sender access
steps.body: Remove the rear seat cushion and position the pump access cover aside. Disconnect the electrical connector and fuel-tube quick-release coupling using the engine-matched coupling procedure. Carefully engage the lock-ring tool and remove the ring without damaging the unit.

steps.title: Empty the left saddle
steps.body: Position the pump-and-sender unit aside without damaging its float arm. Use the tanker to drain the left saddle completely. Inspect the unit flange and tank O-ring contact surfaces, then remove and discard the pump-and-sender O-ring.

steps.title: Empty the right saddle
steps.body: Position the fuel-level-sensor access cover aside. Clean the connections, flange and immediate surrounding area before disconnecting the electrical connector. Carefully remove the lock ring, move the sensor aside while protecting its float arm, and drain the right saddle completely.

steps.title: Assess the second sealing joint
steps.body: Inspect the fuel-level-sensor flange and tank O-ring contact surfaces, then remove and discard its O-ring. If either opening has a bent, scratched or corroded sealing contact area, replace the affected unit or tank. Do not polish or adjust these surfaces.

watchFor.title: Fuel remaining after the filler transfer
watchFor.body: Little or no further fuel coming through the filler tube does not establish that both saddles are empty.

watchFor.title: Fragile float arms
watchFor.body: Both the pump-and-sender unit and the separate level sensor require careful handling while positioned aside.

notes: Discard both removed O-rings; plan replacement seals for the subsequent installation.
The shared draining sequence does not make engine-specific pressure-release or coupling instructions interchangeable.

diagnostics.finding: A flange sealing contact area is bent, scratched or corroded.
diagnostics.meaning: The sealing joint requires more than O-ring renewal.
diagnostics.next: Install a new pump-and-sender unit, fuel-level sensor or fuel tank as appropriate to the damaged surface.

verification.title: Record the draining result
verification.body: Confirm that the left and right saddles were each completely drained, rather than recording only the initial filler transfer.

verification.title: Document sealing-surface condition
verification.body: Record any flange damage and required replacement, and confirm that both old O-rings were discarded before handing the tank over to the next repair phase.

guides.title: Disconnect and reconnect fuel and vapor quick-release couplings
guides.summary: Separate and reconnect the correct coupling type while protecting its retaining clip and keeping contamination out of the fuel system.
guides.introduction: Quick-release couplings join fuel and vapor tubes with hand-operated retainers. This job opens that connection for service, then restores its mechanical lock. The retainer design determines the release sequence, so identifying the coupling comes before pulling on the tube.
guides.why: Dirt can damage the connector and contaminate precisely manufactured fuel-injection components. Tools can deform the retaining clip and cause leaks. Switching the engine off alone does not establish that fuel pressure has been released.
searchTerms: fuel quick connector will not release

when.summary: When fuel-system service requires a liquid-fuel or vapor-tube quick-release connection to be opened.

prepare.title: Identify the retainer
prepare.detail: Match the connection to Type 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 8 in the procedure for your engine.

prepare.title: Prepare for clean fuel work
prepare.detail: Have compressed air and clean blanking plugs ready. You must be able to perform the applicable fuel-pressure-release and battery-disconnection procedures.

steps.title: Release pressure and disconnect the battery
steps.body: For a liquid-fuel coupling, first complete the matching engine pressure-release procedure. On the 5.0L, remove the rear seat cushion to reach the fuel pump driver module (FPDM) on the left, disconnect its electrical connector, run the engine at idle until it stalls, then switch the ignition off. For every coupling type, disconnect the battery ground cable using the linked battery procedure before separating the connection.

steps.title: Clean before opening
steps.body: Use compressed air to remove foreign material around the retaining clip before separating a connection that will be reused. Maintain absolute cleanliness and fit blanking plugs to every exposed tube or opening as soon as it is separated.

steps.title: Release the matching coupling by hand
steps.body: Type 1: follow the complete numbered tab movements, then pull straight off the tube. Type 2: press the lower release point, lift the retainer, then pull straight away. Type 3: press the locking tab in its illustrated release direction. Type 4: press both release points, move the retainer as shown, then lift the coupling straight off. Type 5: press the release points, lift the retaining clip, then pull straight off. Type 8: release the secondary locking tab, depress the primary locking tab, then separate the coupling. Use the individual diagrams for direction; do not transfer one type’s movements to another.

steps.title: Reconnect using the same type’s locking sequence
steps.body: Type 1: inspect and clean both ends, follow its connection diagrams, press the retainer flush with its tabs locked, and perform the specified pull check. Type 2: align and push straight onto the tube, then press the clip down. Type 3: hold the tab in its release position while pushing the coupling on, then return the tab to its locking position. Type 4: align and push straight onto the tube in the illustrated direction. Type 5: push onto the tube, then press the clip down. Type 8: push onto the tube, pull on the coupling and fitting to confirm retention, then lock the secondary tab.

steps.title: Restore the disconnected services
steps.body: After securing the coupling, reconnect the battery ground cable through the battery procedure. On the 5.0L, also reconnect the FPDM electrical connector and reinstall the rear seat cushion before returning the fuel system to service.

watchFor.title: A retainer that needs force
watchFor.body: Do not pry or squeeze it with tools. Deforming the clip can create a fuel leak.

watchFor.title: An unsecured connection
watchFor.body: If the prescribed pull check releases the coupling, revisit its connection sequence before proceeding.

verification.title: Confirm the mechanical lock
verification.body: Check the applicable clip or tab position and complete the Type 1 or Type 8 pull check as directed.

verification.title: Complete the engine-specific return to service
verification.body: Follow the matching pressure-release procedure’s completion instructions. For the 5.0L, cycle the ignition key, wait 3 seconds and check for leaks before starting. Then start the engine and check again.

guides.title: Disconnect and reconnect fuel-system spring lock couplings
guides.summary: Separate and reconnect spring lock fuel or vapor tubes using the correct release tool and the pressure-release procedure for your engine.
guides.introduction: A spring lock coupling joins a tube to another fuel-system component using an internal spring retainer. The joint must be deliberately released before the parts can separate. This job covers disconnection and reconnection on the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines, including the external safety clip where fitted. It is normally part of another repair that requires opening a fuel or vapor tube.
guides.why: Pulling against an engaged retainer can damage the connection. Dirt around the retaining clip can also cause damage during separation, while contamination entering an open tube threatens the fine clearances in fuel-injection equipment. Liquid-fuel connections require pressure release before opening; cleanliness remains essential for both liquid and vapor connections.

when.summary: When a spring lock liquid-fuel or vapor tube must be separated for an associated repair.
notes: Identify the engine and whether the connection carries liquid fuel before choosing the prerequisite procedure.

prepare.title: Have the release and cleaning equipment ready
prepare.detail: Use spring lock coupling disconnect tool 310-S039 (T90T-9550-S). Have compressed air, clean engine oil and suitable plugs for all opened tubes and orifices.

prepare.title: Arrange the prerequisite work
prepare.detail: You must be able to complete the engine-specific fuel-pressure release where required and the Battery Disconnect and Connect procedure before separating the joint.

steps.title: Release liquid-fuel pressure
steps.body: For a liquid-fuel tube, complete the pressure-release procedure matching the engine: 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L. This conditional step precedes opening the coupling. The coupling procedure does not call for fuel-pressure release when servicing a vapor-tube connection.

steps.title: Isolate power and clean the coupling
steps.body: Disconnect the battery ground cable using the linked battery procedure. Before separating a connector that will be reused, use compressed air to remove foreign material from its retaining-clip area. Remove the external fuel-tube safety clip if fitted.

steps.title: Release the internal spring and separate the tube
steps.body: Fit the disconnect tool around the tube and push it into the spring lock coupling to release the retainer. Separate the coupling from the tube, then plug every open tube and orifice to prevent contamination during the associated repair.

steps.title: Lubricate and reconnect
steps.body: When ready to close the connection, apply clean engine oil to the tube end. Align the coupling with the tube and push it on until fully seated. Correct alignment allows the tube to enter the connector without forcing the joint sideways.

steps.title: Secure the joint and restore power
steps.body: Refit the safety clip where equipped. Pull on the coupling to confirm engagement, then reconnect the battery ground cable according to the battery procedure.

steps.title: Complete the liquid-fuel service leak checks
steps.body: When a liquid-fuel repair is complete, finish the engine-specific fuel-pressure-release procedure’s restoration sequence. Reconnect the fuel-pump control-module connector used for pressure release; the 5.2L uses two connectors. Restore the rear seat cushion, cycle the ignition key and wait 3 seconds to pressurize the system. Check for leaks before starting the engine, then start it and check for leaks again. Keep this return-to-service check separate from confirming that the mechanical connections are latched.

watchFor.title: Contamination at the retainer
watchFor.body: Clean the clip area before separation and keep opened passages plugged throughout the work.

watchFor.title: A coupling that looks seated but releases
watchFor.body: Appearance alone does not establish retention. Complete the specified pull check before restoring power.

notes: The coupling operation is shared across these engines, but each liquid-fuel pressure-release reference remains engine-specific.

diagnostics.finding: The coupling separates during the pull check.
diagnostics.meaning: Full engagement has not been established.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the seating and retention check before completing the connection.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical retention
verification.body: The coupling must remain engaged when pulled, with its safety clip installed if fitted.

verification.title: Confirm electrical restoration
verification.body: Complete battery ground-cable reconnection through the linked battery procedure.

verification.title: Verify completed liquid-fuel work
verification.body: For a completed liquid-fuel repair, confirm that the fuel-pump control-module connection or connections have been restored and that both the pre-start and running leak checks are complete.

guides.title: Replace the fuel level sender
guides.summary: Remove the fuel pump and sender unit, replace its level-sensing component, and reinstall the assembly using the matching engine procedure.
guides.introduction: The fuel level sender follows the fuel level through a float arm and provides an electrical level signal. It attaches to the fuel pump and sender unit but can be removed separately once that assembly is out of the tank. The small retaining feature is only part of the job: tank access, fuel connections and sealing require equal care.
guides.why: Lowering fuel below the mounting flange reduces spillage when the tank is opened. Pressure release precedes disconnection, while correct assembly alignment and a renewed seal are essential to closing the tank properly.
searchTerms: fuel pump and sender unit removal

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the fuel level sender requires replacement.
notes: An incorrect gauge reading alone does not establish that the sender is faulty.

prepare.title: Arrange fuel-handling capability
prepare.detail: The 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.2L access procedures specify fuel tanker 292-00004 and fuel-tank locking-ring tool 310-123. They also require the supplemental refueling adapter and a 6 ft. length of 5/8 in. semi-rigid fuel drain tube.

prepare.title: Select the engine-specific procedure and parts
prepare.detail: Have the matching pressure-release, battery-disconnection and quick-release-coupling instructions available. Arrange a new pump-unit O-ring for the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.2L procedure. Use the 5.0L pump-unit procedure to establish its own tools, preparation and sealing requirements.

steps.title: Prepare the correct fuel system
steps.body: Select the matching pump-unit procedure before starting. For 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.2L, release fuel-system pressure as directed, then disconnect the battery ground cable. Follow the 5.0L procedure for its preparation and access sequence. For 5.2L, use G1794941.

steps.title: Lower the fuel level and expose the unit
steps.body: For 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.2L, install the supplemental refueling adapter and drain tube through the capless filler until the tube enters the tank. Connect the fuel tanker and remove as much fuel as possible, lowering the level below the mounting flange. Remove the rear seat cushion, then lift the access cover aside.

steps.title: Remove the pump and sender assembly
steps.body: Those three access procedures next disconnect the electrical connector and external fuel-tube quick-release coupling. Remove the locking ring with the specified tool. Disconnect the internal fuel-tube coupling before withdrawing the assembly; lifting it does not by itself release that connection. Follow each engine's coupling instructions.

steps.title: Release the sender using its own attachment details
steps.body: On 2.3L and 5.0L, disconnect the sender electrical connector, release the locking tab and remove the sender. On 3.7L, disconnect the connector, depress the top locking tab and slide the sender downward off its mount. On 5.2L, disconnect the connector, release the clip lock and remove the sender. Keep the detachment method specific to the engine.

steps.title: Install the replacement sender
steps.body: Reverse the matching sender-removal sequence so the sender is retained on its mount and its electrical connector is restored. Use the engine-specific sender article for this phase before returning the complete unit to the tank.

steps.title: Refit and close the tank
steps.body: Reverse the matching pump-unit removal sequence, including the internal connection. For 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.2L, install a new O-ring and make the unit's alignment tabs meet the tank tabs before tightening the locking ring. Restore the external connections, access cover and rear cushion in the prescribed sequence. Follow the 5.0L installation requirements separately.

watchFor.title: An internal connection still attached
watchFor.body: On the described 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.2L assemblies, release the internal coupling before removing the unit.

watchFor.title: Tabs that do not meet
watchFor.body: Correct the assembly's position before tightening the locking ring; tightening is not a substitute for alignment.

notes: The 3.7L sender slides downward after its top tab is depressed. Do not transfer that illustrated direction to another engine's attachment.

verification.title: Confirm retention and sealing details
verification.body: Check sender retention and electrical reconnection. For the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.2L assembly installation, confirm the new O-ring and matching alignment tabs before completing the locking-ring step.

verification.title: Complete the engine-specific return to service
verification.body: For 5.2L, complete the pressure-release procedure's restoration requirements, electrical reconnection and leak checks before return to service. Use the matching engine instructions for the other variants' completion checks.

guides.title: Replace the fuel level sensor in the saddle-type tank
guides.summary: Drain the tank in stages, access both tank units and replace the fuel level sensor while protecting its connections and sealing surfaces.
guides.introduction: The fuel level sensor provides information about the fuel remaining in the tank. Its replacement requires more than opening its own access cover: the pump and sender unit must first be moved aside so remaining fuel can be removed from the left-hand saddle. This shared route applies to the listed engines, with separate pressure-release and coupling procedures for each.
guides.why: Pressure release and fuel removal solve different problems. Releasing pressure prepares the fuel connections for service; draining lowers fuel below the openings. Clean connections, undamaged seal contact surfaces and correctly aligned new seals are essential when closing the tank.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the separate fuel level sensor requires replacement.
notes: An incorrect level indication alone does not establish which component requires replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange fuel-service capability
prepare.detail: Use the 292-00004 Fuel Tanker 100 GPM and 310-123 fuel-tank lock-ring tool. This work requires controlled fuel transfer and access to the applicable pressure-release, battery and coupling procedures.

prepare.title: Prepare the drain connection and seals
prepare.detail: Have the supplemental refueling adapter from the luggage compartment and a 6 ft. length of 5/8 in. semi-rigid fuel drain tube. Arrange new seals for the opened pump/sender and fuel level sensor assemblies.

steps.title: Release pressure and disconnect the battery
steps.body: Follow the pressure-release procedure for the actual 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine first. Then disconnect the battery ground cable using the battery procedure.

steps.title: Withdraw fuel through the filler
steps.body: Insert the supplemental adapter and drain tube through the capless filler until the tube enters the tank. Connect the fuel tanker and remove as much fuel as possible, lowering fuel below the pump/sender flange and removing residual fuel from the filler pipe.

steps.title: Open the pump and sender access
steps.body: Remove the rear seat cushion and move the pump access cover aside. Disconnect the electrical connector and external fuel quick-release coupling. Carefully engage the lock-ring tool and remove the ring, then position the unit aside without damaging its float arm.

steps.title: Empty the left-hand saddle and inspect the seal area
steps.body: Use the tanker to completely drain remaining fuel from the left-hand saddle. Inspect the pump/sender flange and tank O-ring contact surfaces. Do not polish or adjust them; replace the affected unit or tank if the sealing area is bent, scratched or corroded. Remove and discard the O-ring.

steps.title: Release the fuel level sensor
steps.body: Move its access cover aside. Clean the connections, flange and immediate surrounding area before disconnecting the electrical connector. Carefully position the lock-ring tool and remove the sensor lock ring without damaging the sensor.

steps.title: Disconnect the internal fuel tube
steps.body: Release the internal tube-to-sensor quick-connect coupling using the engine-specific coupling procedure. This connection must be released before the sensor can be taken away without pulling on the internal tube.

steps.title: Reseal and reassemble
steps.body: Install a new fuel level sensor O-ring and make sure the sensor and tank alignment tabs meet before tightening its ring. Reverse the removal sequence, renewing the discarded pump/sender seal and restoring both units, their connections, access covers, rear cushion and battery connection.

steps.title: Prime the fuel system and check for leaks
steps.body: Finish the engine-specific fuel-pressure-release procedure’s restoration sequence. Reconnect the fuel-pump control-module connector used for pressure release; the 5.2L uses two connectors. Restore the rear seat cushion, cycle the ignition key and wait 3 seconds to pressurize the system. Check for leaks before starting the engine, then start it and check for leaks again. Keep this return-to-service check separate from confirming that the mechanical connections are latched.

watchFor.title: Damage during tool placement
watchFor.body: Careless lock-ring tool engagement can damage either tank unit. Protect the pump/sender float arm while positioning that unit aside.

watchFor.title: Contamination at the opening
watchFor.body: Clean around the sensor before opening its mounting so dirt is not carried into the tank or sealing joint.

notes: Keep pressure-release and quick-release coupling instructions matched to the engine throughout the job.

diagnostics.finding: A pump/sender or tank O-ring contact area is bent, scratched or corroded.
diagnostics.meaning: The sealing surface is unsuitable for reassembly.
diagnostics.next: Replace the affected pump/sender unit or tank; do not polish or reshape the contact area.

verification.title: Check assembly conditions
verification.body: Confirm new seals, sensor tab alignment before ring tightening, and restoration of all disconnected tubes and electrical connectors.

verification.title: Record the sealing decision
verification.body: Record flange condition, any component replacement required by damage, and renewal of the discarded and specified-new seals.

verification.title: Record both fuel-leak checks
verification.body: Confirm that the fuel-pump control-module connection or connections have been restored and that both the pre-start and running leak checks are complete.

guides.title: Replace the fuel supply lines
guides.summary: Replace the routed fuel line using the engine-specific tank, exhaust and coupling procedures, including the additional filter connections on the 5.2L.
guides.introduction: The fuel supply line carries pressurized fuel from the tank toward the engine. Retainers support its route, while shields protect the underbody installation. Every engine covered here requires fuel-tank removal, but engine-end access and coupling locations differ. The 5.2L also has connections at an in-line fuel filter.
guides.why: A tube must be correctly routed and securely connected, not merely pushed into position. Retainers prevent unsupported sections, and locked couplings contain fuel pressure. Pressure can remain after the pump stops, so tank-removal prerequisites matter before opening the system.

when.summary: When inspection or diagnosis establishes that a fuel supply line needs replacement.

prepare.title: Prepare for tank and underbody work
prepare.detail: Safe underbody support and fuel-system servicing capability are required. Follow the matching fuel-tank procedure and its safety prerequisites before disconnecting lines.

prepare.title: Match the engine and coupling method
prepare.detail: Have the applicable spring-lock procedure ready. The 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L also require left-hand catalytic-converter removal; the 5.2L requires quick-release coupling instructions and a suitable residual-fuel container.

steps.title: Remove the fuel tank
steps.body: Use the fuel-tank removal and installation procedure for the fitted engine. This is the first operation in every fuel-line replacement path.

steps.title: Open the engine-end access
steps.body: On the [2.3L](#/document/G1671578), remove the appearance-cover nuts and cover, disconnect the fuel-line-to-rail spring-lock coupling, then remove the heat-shield nuts and shield. On the [3.7L](#/document/G1671600), [5.0L](#/document/G1671612) and [5.2L](#/document/G1794940), remove the left-hand catalytic converter, then the heat shield.

steps.title: Release the initial retainers and remaining engine connection
steps.body: Release the line from its retainers. On the 3.7L, disconnect the spring-lock coupling at the fuel rail. On the 5.0L and 5.2L, disconnect the spring-lock coupling at the fuel-rail jumper tube. The 2.3L connection was released earlier.

steps.title: Remove the underbody protection
steps.body: Remove the splash shield's nuts, bolts and push-pins, then the fuel-tank deflector nuts and deflector. Keep each fastener group associated with its component for refitting.

steps.title: Disconnect the 5.2L filter connections
steps.body: On the 5.2L only, disconnect the quick-release couplings at the fuel filter. Carefully drain residual fuel from the lines and filter into a suitable container; removing the tank does not eliminate this remaining fuel.

steps.title: Remove and replace the line
steps.body: Release the remaining retainers and remove the fuel line. Install by reversing the matching engine procedure, restoring its routing, retainers, shields, connections and removed assemblies with the specified fastener torques.

steps.title: Complete the specified coupling checks
steps.body: For the 5.0L and 5.2L, make sure the tubes are fully seated and their quick-connect or quick-release couplings are locked. Pull on the tubes to confirm retention, then pressurize the system and check for leaks.

watchFor.title: Neighbouring tubes in the bundle
watchFor.body: The 5.0L and 5.2L underfloor arrangement groups fuel and vapor tubes alongside brake tubes. Identify the intended line before releasing retainers.

notes: Use each engine's procedure for torque values and coupling details; the shared repair purpose does not make the removal sequences interchangeable.

diagnostics.finding: A tube fails the specified 5.0L or 5.2L pull check.
diagnostics.meaning: The coupling has not securely retained the tube.
diagnostics.next: Correct its seating and locking using the applicable coupling procedure before pressurization.

verification.title: Confirm complete reassembly
verification.body: Check that the line retainers, splash shield, tank deflector and all engine-specific removed components have been restored.

verification.title: Record connection-test results
verification.body: For the 5.0L and 5.2L, record successful pull checks and the result of the pressurized leak check. Complete the applicable tank and coupling procedures for every engine.

guides.title: Replace the in-tank fuel pump and sender unit
guides.summary: Release fuel pressure, lower the tank level and replace the pump-and-sender assembly through the rear-seat access opening with a new seal.
guides.introduction: The tank-mounted assembly supplies pressurized fuel and carries the sender that reports fuel level. Replacement involves connections both above the tank and inside it. Access is through an opening beneath the rear seat cushion, but the tank must first be prepared so fuel sits below the unit's mounting flange. The four engine procedures share this access sequence while retaining engine-specific pressure-release and coupling instructions.
guides.why: Fuel pressure can remain after pump operation stops, so pressure release must precede disconnection. Lowering the fuel level addresses a separate problem: fuel reaching the open mounting flange. During installation, a new O-ring and correctly engaged alignment tabs establish the prescribed seal and unit position before the lock ring is tightened.

when.summary: When diagnosis calls for replacement of the tank-mounted fuel pump and sender assembly.
notes: The removal sequence does not diagnose a fuel-pressure or gauge complaint.
Use the matching 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L procedure and replacement assembly.

prepare.title: Arrange controlled fuel recovery
prepare.detail: Provide fuel tanker 292-00004, the supplemental refueling adapter from the luggage compartment, and a 6 ft. length of 5/8 in. semi-rigid fuel drain tube.

prepare.title: Prepare access and sealing parts
prepare.detail: Have lock-ring tool 310-123 and a new pump-and-sender O-ring seal. Provide access to the rear seat cushion and the engine-matched pressure-release and quick-coupling procedures.

prepare.title: Respect the capless filler
prepare.detail: Use the supplemental adapter for drain-tube entry. The Easy Fuel capless filler assembly must not be modified.

steps.title: Release pressure, then disconnect the battery
steps.body: Complete the fuel-pressure release procedure for the fitted engine. Next, disconnect the battery ground cable using [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356). Do not substitute battery disconnection for pressure release.

steps.title: Drain below the mounting flange
steps.body: Insert the supplemental adapter and specified drain tube through the capless filler until the tube enters the tank. Connect the fuel tanker and remove as much fuel as possible. This removes fuel from the filler pipe and lowers the tank level below the pump mounting flange.

steps.title: Open the rear-seat access
steps.body: Remove the [rear seat cushion](#/document/G1692168), then remove and position aside the pump-and-sender access cover. This exposes the external electrical and fuel connections.

steps.title: Disconnect the external connections
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector and external fuel-tube quick-release coupling. Use the coupling procedure for the fitted engine so the connector is released by its intended mechanism.

steps.title: Unlock and disconnect the assembly
steps.body: Remove the lock ring with tool 310-123. Following the engine-specific removal procedure, disconnect the internal fuel-tube quick coupling and remove the pump-and-sender unit. The internal connection must be released before the assembly is fully removed.

steps.title: Refit with a new seal and correct alignment
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, restoring the internal connection and installing a new O-ring seal. Ensure the alignment tabs on the unit and fuel tank meet before tightening the lock ring.

steps.title: Restore the external connections and access
steps.body: Reconnect the external fuel coupling and electrical connector, restore the access cover and rear seat cushion, and complete battery reconnection through its procedure. Follow the applicable coupling instructions during reconnection as well as removal.

steps.title: Prime the fuel system and check for leaks
steps.body: Finish the engine-specific fuel-pressure-release procedure’s restoration sequence. Reconnect the fuel-pump control-module connector used for pressure release; the 5.2L uses two connectors. Restore the rear seat cushion, cycle the ignition key and wait 3 seconds to pressurize the system. Check for leaks before starting the engine, then start it and check for leaks again. Keep this return-to-service check separate from confirming that the mechanical connections are latched.

watchFor.title: Fuel still at the flange
watchFor.body: For a completely full tank, the procedure describes removing approximately 3 gallons to lower the level. The operative requirement is fuel below the mounting flange.

watchFor.title: Tabs not aligned
watchFor.body: Establish the specified alignment before tightening the lock ring; tightening is not a substitute for positioning the assembly.

notes: The 5.2L assembly contains two electric pumps. Its internal equipment should not be inferred from the other engine variants.
The 5.0L and 5.2L descriptions identify a separately serviceable level sender, so a fuel-level complaint alone does not justify complete assembly replacement.

diagnostics.finding: A 5.0L or 5.2L vehicle stopped after a collision.
diagnostics.meaning: Its collision-triggered pump shut-off feature may explain pump inactivity.
diagnostics.next: Follow the applicable shut-off and diagnostic guidance before treating inactivity as proof of pump failure.

verification.title: Confirm sealing before closing access
verification.body: Confirm a new O-ring was installed and the tank and unit alignment tabs met before lock-ring tightening.

verification.title: Confirm complete reassembly
verification.body: Confirm both internal and external fuel couplings, the electrical connection, access cover, rear seat cushion and battery reconnection are complete.

verification.title: Record both fuel-leak checks
verification.body: Confirm that the fuel-pump control-module connection or connections have been restored and that both the pre-start and running leak checks are complete.
