guides.title: Replace the Easy Fuel capless fuel tank filler pipe
guides.summary: Replace the filler pipe through the left rear wheel opening after lowering the fuel level and disconnecting its tank hose and vapor connection.
guides.introduction: The filler pipe carries fuel from the capless refueling inlet to the tank. Its associated vapor tube has a separate quick-release connection, so removing the assembly involves both liquid-fuel and vapor connections. Access is behind the left rear wheel splash shield. The four engine procedures share the same main sequence, but each directs you to its own fuel-system coupling procedure.
guides.why: Lowering the fuel level below the filler-pipe inlet reduces the fuel released when the tank connection is opened. It does not empty every low point in the pipe, so residual fuel still needs controlled collection. Correct support and careful reconnection matter because the work combines an elevated vehicle with an open fuel connection.

when.summary: When the fuel tank filler pipe requires replacement or removal for an associated repair.
notes: Select the procedure for the fitted engine before disconnecting the vapor coupling.

prepare.title: Arrange supported access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the specified lifting points, identified by stamped triangles. Check adapter and underbody clearances. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare fuel removal equipment
prepare.detail: Have Fuel Tanker 100 GPM, tool 292-00004, the supplemental refueling adapter, a 6 ft. length of 5/8 in. semi-rigid fuel drain tube and a suitable residual-fuel container.

prepare.title: Plan the supporting work
prepare.detail: Have the battery, wheel and engine-specific quick-release coupling procedures available, together with tools capable of applying the specified fastener and hose-clamp torques.

steps.title: Position the vehicle and disconnect the battery
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on the hoist. Disconnect the battery ground cable using the linked battery procedure before opening the fuel connections.

steps.title: Lower the fuel level through the capless inlet
steps.body: Retrieve the supplemental refueling adapter from the luggage compartment. Insert it and the specified drain tube until the tube enters the tank. Connect the tanker and remove approximately one-eighth tank, approximately 2 gallons. This amount is described for a completely full tank; its purpose is to lower fuel below the filler-pipe inlet and remove most fuel retained in the pipe.

steps.title: Expose the filler pipe
steps.body: Remove the left rear wheel using the wheel procedure. Remove the splash-shield retainers and position the shield aside to reach the pipe, its mountings and the tank connection.

steps.title: Disconnect the liquid and vapor connections
steps.body: Position the collection container before releasing the tank-hose clamp. Carefully disconnect the filler pipe and collect remaining fuel. Then disconnect the vapor tube using the quick-release procedure for the fitted engine.

steps.title: Exchange and reconnect the assembly
steps.body: Remove the retaining fasteners and withdraw the filler pipe. Install in reverse order: secure the replacement pipe, reconnect the vapor coupling and reconnect the tank hose. The pipe retainers tighten to 18 lb.ft (25 Nm), and the tank-hose clamp to 53 lb.in (6 Nm).

steps.title: Restore access components
steps.body: Refit the splash shield and wheel, following the wheel installation procedure. Restore the battery connection using its linked procedure and complete the remaining reverse-order installation work.

watchFor.title: Fuel remaining after draining
watchFor.body: A lowered tank level does not mean the filler pipe is dry. Keep the container ready as the hose separates.

watchFor.title: Capless assembly modification
watchFor.body: The 5.0L and 5.2L system descriptions prohibit modifying the filler assembly and specify replacement with a new assembly.

notes: The illustrated wheel-opening view belongs to the 2.3L procedure; use the procedure matching the vehicle for its complete instructions.

verification.title: Confirm reconnection and reassembly
verification.body: Check that the vapor coupling is reconnected, the tank hose and pipe retainers are secured to their specified torques, and the splash shield, wheel and battery connection have been restored.

guides.title: Replace the serviceable in-line fuel filter on the 5.2L engine
guides.summary: Release fuel pressure, replace the bracket-mounted filter and verify both quick-release connections under pressure.
guides.introduction: The 5.2L fuel system has a serviceable in-line filter in the fuel path supplying the engine. The filter traps material carried by the fuel before it reaches downstream components. Replacement requires underbody access, removal of a protective splash shield and disconnection of the filter's fuel-line couplings.
guides.why: Switching the engine off does not release fuel pressure: the pump module contains a check valve that maintains it. Even after the pressure-release procedure, fuel can remain inside the lines and filter. Correctly locked couplings and a pressurized leak check are essential parts of completing the repair.

when.summary: When replacement of the 5.2L engine's serviceable in-line fuel filter is required.
notes: This replacement procedure does not establish a service interval or diagnose a restriction.

prepare.title: Provide safe underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist at the designated lifting points, checking clearance around surrounding components. Never work beneath jack-only support.

prepare.title: Prepare for pressurized fuel work
prepare.detail: Have the capability to follow the 5.2L fuel-pressure release and quick-release coupling procedures. Obtain an appropriate container for residual fuel.

prepare.title: Gather replacement and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Have the replacement filter, splash-shield fastener tools and a torque wrench suitable for the filter bracket bolt.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle and release fuel pressure
steps.body: Place the transmission in Neutral and position the vehicle on a hoist using the [lifting procedure](#/document/G1663631). Carry out [Fuel System Pressure Release](#/document/G1794916) before disconnecting the filter.

steps.title: Remove the protective shield
steps.body: Following the [filter replacement procedure](#/document/G1794944), remove the nuts, bolts and push-pins securing the splash shield, then remove the shield. Prepare the fuel container before opening either connection.

steps.title: Disconnect the filter lines
steps.body: Release the fuel-line quick-release couplings using the [coupling procedure](#/document/G1794918). Carefully drain residual fuel from the lines and filter into the container; pressure release does not empty these parts.

steps.title: Replace the filter in its bracket
steps.body: Loosen the bracket bolt and remove the filter from the bracket. Install the replacement by reversing the removal operation. Tighten the bracket bolt to 44 lb.in (5 Nm).

steps.title: Secure the lines and check under pressure
steps.body: Fully seat both fuel lines and lock their quick-release couplings. Pull on the lines to confirm they are retained. Pressurize the system and check for leaks, then complete the reverse removal sequence, including splash-shield refitting.

watchFor.title: Residual fuel after depressurizing
watchFor.body: Fuel remaining in the filter and lines must still be collected when the connections are opened.

watchFor.title: A connection that only appears seated
watchFor.body: Visual alignment alone is insufficient. The installation requires both correct locking and a pull check.

notes: The filter illustration identifies the couplings and bracket fastening; it does not provide an alternative coupling-release method.

diagnostics.finding: A fuel line does not remain secure during the pull check
diagnostics.meaning: The coupling has not demonstrated correct seating and locking.
diagnostics.next: Correct the connection before pressurizing the system.

diagnostics.finding: Fuel leakage appears during the pressure check
diagnostics.meaning: The installation is not ready for service.
diagnostics.next: Release pressure before reopening the connection, correct the cause and repeat the pressurized leak check.

verification.title: Verify retention and protection
verification.body: Confirm both lines passed the pull check, the bracket bolt was tightened and the splash shield was restored.

verification.title: Record the leak-check result
verification.body: Record that the system was pressurized and whether either filter connection showed leakage.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L in-line fuel filter removal, installation and final connection checks.
Release 5.2L fuel-system pressure before opening the circuit.
Release and reconnect the 5.2L fuel-line quick-release couplings.
Establish safe hoist access to the underbody filter.

guides.title: Replace the accelerator pedal and sensor assembly
guides.summary: Replace the complete electronic accelerator pedal assembly while keeping the ignition off during electrical disconnection and reconnection.
guides.introduction: The accelerator pedal is an electrical input to the engine management system. Its accelerator pedal position (APP) sensor tells the powertrain control module (PCM) how the driver is moving the pedal. The PCM then commands the electronic throttle to change its opening. This repair replaces the pedal and sensor together as an assembly.
guides.why: Disconnecting the pedal with the ignition on can set diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), confusing subsequent diagnosis. Secure mounting is also important: the pedal must remain fixed to its mounting points while the driver operates it.

when.summary: When diagnosis calls for replacement of the accelerator pedal and sensor assembly.
notes: Limited performance alone does not identify the pedal assembly as the failed component.

prepare.title: Prevent unintended starting
prepare.detail: Review the linked health and safety precautions. Disable remote start if equipped, switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle.

prepare.title: Prepare the working area and tools
prepare.detail: Arrange access to the pedal connector and mounting nuts. Use appropriate eye protection and a torque wrench suitable for the small mounting fasteners.

steps.title: Establish the ignition-off condition
steps.body: Confirm the ignition is OFF before touching the pedal connector. Keep it off throughout the connector work to avoid creating service-induced fault codes.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the assembly
steps.body: Disconnect the pedal sensor electrical connector. Remove the three mounting nuts and take out the pedal and sensor assembly together, as shown in the [replacement procedure](#/document/G1687937).

steps.title: Secure the replacement pedal
steps.body: Position the replacement assembly on its mounting points and reinstall the three nuts. Tighten them to 9 Nm; these fasteners secure the complete pedal unit.

steps.title: Restore the electrical connection
steps.body: Reconnect the pedal sensor connector with the ignition still OFF. This completes the reverse removal sequence and restores the pedal’s signal connection to engine management.

watchFor.title: Ignition left on
watchFor.body: An ignition-on disconnection can introduce DTCs that were not part of the original complaint.

watchFor.title: Unexpected starting
watchFor.body: Turning off the ignition does not replace the requirement to disable an equipped remote-start feature before service.

notes: The service operation replaces the pedal and sensor assembly together; it does not describe separate sensor adjustment.

diagnostics.finding: Acceleration-control failure produces limited performance.
diagnostics.meaning: Engine management can provide a limp-home mode after a system failure; that behavior does not isolate the pedal.
diagnostics.next: Establish the fault before authorizing assembly replacement.

verification.title: Check the completed installation
verification.body: Confirm all three mounting nuts are tightened and the sensor connector is fully reconnected.

verification.title: Record the service conditions
verification.body: Record assembly replacement and any known ignition-on disconnection so later fault assessment can distinguish the original complaint from service events.

procedures.purpose: Complete accelerator pedal and sensor assembly removal and installation.
Required general service precautions, including remote-start disabling and prevention of unintended starting.

guides.title: Diagnose dual automatic climate control faults
guides.summary: Use fault codes, pressure measurements and an ordered function check to locate automatic climate control concerns before replacing components.
guides.introduction: Dual Automatic Temperature Control (DATC) maintains selected cabin temperatures, with separate driver and passenger settings. It coordinates heating, cooling, blower speed and air doors; air conditioning also removes humidity. This diagnosis separates pressure-sensor and compressor-relay electrical faults from airflow, temperature-control and intermittent complaints.
guides.why: A fault code identifies an abnormal signal, not necessarily a failed component. Comparing electronic readings with physical conditions, then isolating circuits in order, prevents wiring faults or misleading operating conditions from becoming unnecessary parts replacements.
searchTerms: driver side temperature will not change

when.summary: Use when climate operation is incorrect, relevant fault codes are stored, or an intermittent complaint cannot be reproduced.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting powertrain control module (PCM) and front controls interface module (FCIM) self-tests and parameter identification (PID) readings, a digital multimeter, correct Flex Probe adapters and a refrigerant manifold gauge set. Gauge connection and live electrical testing require appropriate competence.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging-system condition; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Inspect previous repairs, wiring and connectors. Have Wiring Diagrams Cell 55 and the relay component test in Cell 149 available.

steps.title: Establish the complaint and select its diagnostic route
steps.body: Follow the [DATC diagnostic charts](#/document/G1676857). Record codes and perform PCM, then FCIM self-tests. Resolve circuit codes before performance complaints. Network codes can follow low voltage or previous repairs: inspect network connections and test the battery before considering a module. A module that will not communicate needs network diagnosis.

steps.title: Use the symptom chart to separate functions
steps.body: Reduced airflow starts with the cabin filter, then refrigerant condition, unwanted compressor operation or blower performance. Insufficient cooling requires the engine-specific refrigerant tests before temperature-door diagnosis. Heat concerns route to F; inlet and distribution doors to D and E; driver and passenger temperature control to I and J; a dead blower to K, incorrect speeds to L. Variable-compressor and clutch-request faults route to R and S.

steps.title: Test A: compare pressure before testing wiring
steps.body: For P0532 or P0533, let refrigerant temperature stabilize to ambient, then compare manifold pressure with PCM ACP_PRESS. Agreement within ±103 kPa (15 psi) directs you to disregard these codes and use the symptom chart. Otherwise, follow A2–A5: isolate the specified PCM, pressure-transducer, generator-current-sensor and, if fitted, boost-sensor connections; test for voltage shorts, ground shorts, opens and cross-shorts in that order. Use the engine-specific pinout. Only after these checks pass does the path call for pressure-transducer replacement and an operating retest.

steps.title: Test B: prove relay supply and control
steps.body: For P0645, inspect battery junction box fuses 23 and 42. Test both relay supplies, then component-test the relay. If it passes, isolate the PCM and relay and test the control wire for unwanted voltage, a ground short and an open. The PCM normally energizes the relay by grounding its coil when cooling is requested and pressure permits.

steps.title: Test C: reproduce an uncoded complaint systematically
steps.body: After both self-tests pass, check every blower speed and outlet mode. Warm the engine, switch air conditioning off and sweep both temperature settings from cold to warm and back. Check that cold-setting outlet air approaches ambient with cooling off. Then, with ambient above 0°C (32°F), request cooling and check compressor operation. Finally, select recirculation at maximum blower speed and listen for increased airflow noise. Follow each failed function to its specified symptom test.

steps.title: Finish Test C with sensor and touchscreen comparisons
steps.body: Compare actual driver-footwell, driver-panel and cabin-sensor air temperatures with LDFTEMP, LDPT and INT_TEMP respectively. Discharge-temperature disagreement routes to M; cabin-temperature disagreement routes to N. Exercise every touchscreen climate and audio function. A touchscreen failure transfers diagnosis to the information and entertainment system; passing the full sequence establishes correct operation at that time.

steps.title: Escalate persistent A or B faults carefully
steps.body: At A6 or B6, inspect PCM connectors, replace damaged terminals or connectors, clean module pins as directed and ensure secure latching. Recheck operation. If the concern remains, check applicable technical service bulletins before following the engine-specific PCM replacement procedure. Do not replace components when the required fault is absent.

watchFor.title: Air-inlet calibration can be misleading
watchFor.body: The inlet actuator reverses direction electrically and reports position through feedback. Binding during calibration can create a false travel limit and select the wrong air source.

watchFor.title: Noise and pressure need separate evidence
watchFor.body: Compressor pulley roughness leads to clutch and field-coil work; excessive plenum hissing calls for a refrigerant-level check. A discharging relief valve requires pressure comparison to distinguish a faulty valve from excessive pressure caused by restriction.

notes: For B10B8:63, attempt button cleaning, clear codes and repeat the self-test; a returning code requires the VIN-dependent FCIM guided routine.

Remote-start-only concerns require checking Auto or Last User Settings and network operation. Sensor-code routes distinguish discharge temperature (M), cabin temperature, humidity and sensor fan (N), sunlight (O), evaporator temperature (P) and sensor supply (Q).

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0532 or P0533 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Pressure-transducer feedback is electrically low or high respectively; this does not establish refrigerant charge.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test A, beginning with the gauge-to-PID comparison.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0645 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Relay-control voltage does not match the PCM's commanded state.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test B before condemning the relay or PCM.

diagnostics.meaning: A mechanical fault concerns the driver-temperature, passenger-temperature, inlet or distribution door respectively.
diagnostics.next: Inspect for binding or damaged linkage or doors first; replace the corresponding actuator only if no mechanical condition is found.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1464 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: An air-conditioning request may have been present during self-test.
diagnostics.next: Switch climate control off, clear codes and repeat the self-test; a returning code routes to H.

verification.title: Confirm the relevant function
verification.body: Repeat the operating check that exposed the concern. A successful intermittent check means the system operates correctly now; repair any identified connector fault's root cause.

verification.title: Record the evidence
verification.body: Record codes, pressure comparison, relevant temperature/PID comparisons and the function that passed or selected the next diagnostic branch.

guides.title: Diagnose airflow, heating and A/C faults with dual automatic temperature control
guides.summary: Use the complaint-specific tests to separate door-control faults, inadequate heater coolant flow and inhibited or failed A/C clutch operation.
guides.introduction: Dual automatic temperature control (DATC) maintains independently selected driver and passenger temperatures. Air doors control incoming air and outlet direction, the heater core transfers engine-coolant heat, and air conditioning (A/C) cools and dehumidifies. Because these functions depend on different physical systems, a weak heater, wrong outlet direction and an inactive compressor need different diagnostic routes.
guides.why: The front controls interface module (FCIM) drives door motors and monitors their position. Wiring faults can imitate failed actuators, while a binding distribution door can teach an incorrect travel limit during calibration. A/C operation also depends on permission from the powertrain control module (PCM), so an idle compressor does not establish compressor failure.

when.summary: Use for an inoperative inlet door, incorrect outlet direction, insufficient heat or inoperative A/C on DATC vehicles.
notes: Choose the test matching the current complaint; these are separate diagnostic branches.

prepare.title: Electrical testing
prepare.detail: Arrange scan-tool network tests, self-tests, live data and active commands; a digital multimeter; correct probe adapters; and Wiring Diagrams Cell 55. Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge above 70%. Diagnose PCM trouble codes first because they may inhibit A/C.

prepare.title: Thermal and refrigerant testing
prepare.detail: Have a suitable temperature-measuring device, cooling-system pressure-test and bleeding capability, manifold gauges, and access to refrigerant leak detection, recovery, evacuation and charging equipment. Use the cooling and refrigerant procedures appropriate to the fitted engine.

steps.title: Test the correct air-door circuits
steps.body: Use Test D for the inlet door at C282 and Test E for incorrect outlet direction at distribution actuator C232. Follow each test's exact connector-isolation and ignition sequence in [DATC diagnosis](#/document/G1676857). Check for voltage shorts, ground shorts, opens and circuits shorted together. Repair a failed circuit check. Only after all pass does the test direct replacement of the corresponding actuator, followed by an operating check.

steps.title: Establish coolant supply for weak heat
steps.body: In Test F, check coolant level with ignition off. If low, pressure-test: repair a leak and retest, or fill and bleed if no leak is found. At operating temperature, select floor, full warm and lowest blower speed. Hold 3,500 RPM for 30 seconds, then idle for 30 seconds. Measure the heater inlet hose; if it is not hot, perform the prescribed cooling-system bleed before comparing outlet temperature.

steps.title: Start inoperative-A/C diagnosis with pressure and communication
steps.body: Inspect battery junction box fuses 23 (10A) and 42 (15A). Test G requires pressure above 290 kPa (42 psi); otherwise find and repair leaks, then recharge. Network-test FCIM and PCM, routing a failure to network diagnosis. Compare the gauge reading with PCM pressure data. A disagreement beyond ±103 kPa (15 psi) leads to pressure-transducer Test A. Next, verify fan operation during the key-on, engine-off self-test; diagnose a non-operating fan.

steps.title: Validate temperatures and fitted shutters
steps.body: Allow cabin and exterior temperatures to stabilize to ambient, potentially requiring at least 6 hours. Compare applicable PCM temperature readings as G5 directs. Test the disconnected evaporator sensor against G6's resistance table and ambient reading; replace it if outside specification. If active grille shutters are fitted, allow at least 30 seconds of idle calibration, then command full opening and closing. Diagnose failed movement before proceeding.

steps.title: Trace the driver's A/C request
steps.body: A parameter identification (PID) is a scan-tool data value. Select PANEL and press A/C: FCIM CC_SW_AC should show Active. If not, follow G17's FCIM checks. If active, check PCM AC_REQ with the engine running. A Yes result proceeds to G11; otherwise perform G10's ambient-temperature reset: press and release A/C and Recirc together, then press A/C again within 2 seconds. Start the engine, select full cold, PANEL and A/C, then retest. If the compressor remains off, continue to G11.

steps.title: Separate control inhibition from clutch failure
steps.body: Activate PCM ACC_CMD. If the compressor starts, follow G18 to identify an input or strategy withholding normal operation. If it does not, continue through G12–G16's relay, supply, ground and clutch checks. Successful active-command operation means PCM replacement will not resolve the inhibiting condition.

steps.title: Follow the relay and field-coil branch
steps.body: Check relay feeds under G12. If inadequate, verify the specified fuses and investigate a short if a fuse has failed. Use only G13's specified fused relay bypass. If the clutch engages, remove the jumper and replace the relay. Otherwise retain the jumper for G14's field-coil supply measurement, then remove it on either result. Repair a failed supply circuit; with supply correct, continue to the ignition-off ground-circuit check.

steps.title: Assess clutch clearance after electrical checks
steps.body: Measure clutch air gap at 3 equally spaced positions using the clutch procedure. A gap greater than 0.6 mm (0.0236 in) calls for adjustment. If the gap is not greater and the preceding circuit checks passed, the test directs replacement of the clutch and field coil.

steps.title: Complete the FCIM or inhibition branch
steps.body: For persistent door faults after actuator replacement, or an incorrect A/C switch response, inspect FCIM connectors. Renew corroded or damaged connectors and terminals, clean module pins, correct pushed-out pins and reconnect securely. Retest, then check technical service bulletins if unresolved. Follow an applicable bulletin; otherwise use the vehicle-identification-number-dependent FCIM guided routine. For G18 with normal inputs, investigate intermittent connections and recent module work, including incomplete programmable module installation.

watchFor.title: Probe and jumper damage
watchFor.body: Use the correct adapters and prescribed fused jumper only. Do not apply power or ground directly to module-controlled components outside the directed test.

watchFor.title: A pressure reading is not a charge measurement
watchFor.body: Static pressure alone cannot establish that refrigerant quantity is correct.

notes: Only evaluate temperature sensors and grille shutters actually fitted. General inhibition entries mentioning stop-start or auxiliary systems do not establish that this vehicle has them.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1086:11, B1086:12 or B1086:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These indicate distribution-motor short to ground, short to voltage or open circuit respectively. Shorts can restrict movement to one direction; an open prevents movement.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test E's circuit checks before condemning the actuator.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B11E7:12 or B11E7:14 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The distribution-door feedback indicates a short to voltage, or a short to ground/open respectively.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test E; the code does not distinguish wiring from actuator failure by itself.

diagnostics.finding: Heater outlet temperature is similar to inlet temperature, within approximately 6–17°C [10–30°F].
diagnostics.meaning: After Test F's coolant-flow checks, attention moves to temperature-door operation.
diagnostics.next: Use Test I for inadequate driver-side heat or Test J for passenger-side heat. If the outlet does not meet F4's comparison, the test directs heater-core replacement.

diagnostics.finding: The compressor operates under active command but not normal A/C demand.
diagnostics.meaning: G18 considers pressure, charge, temperature, engine protection, load, battery condition and missing-message inhibits.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose an abnormal inhibiting input using the applicable engine-control procedure. With normal inputs, investigate intermittent connections and module configuration history.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1464 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: PCM detected an A/C request during its self-test; this relates to an always-commanded-on complaint.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the request and the relay, wiring or control-module path rather than treating it as proof of failed cooling hardware.

verification.title: Repeat the original operating check
verification.body: Confirm the repaired door responds, the correct outlets deliver air, or heat returns as appropriate. For restored A/C, use the refrigerant-system test matching the engine.

verification.title: Record the deciding measurements
verification.body: Record the failed and corrected circuit readings, heater-hose comparison, pressure comparison or request/command response. Include any remaining codes or intermittent concern.

guides.title: Diagnose constant A/C, incorrect temperatures or no blower with dual automatic climate control
guides.summary: Use Tests H–K to separate A/C command faults, individual temperature-door faults and blower power or control failures.
guides.introduction: Dual Automatic Temperature Control (DATC) maintains selected cabin temperatures and allows separate driver and passenger settings. The front controls interface module (FCIM) commands the temperature-door actuators and sends a pulse-width modulation (PWM) signal to the blower speed control. Air conditioning (A/C) also removes moisture. These functions have different electrical paths, so matching the test to the complaint matters.
guides.why: Incorrect outlet temperature can arise from wiring, actuator feedback or a door that bound during calibration. Similarly, a silent blower may lack power or a control signal. Testing these paths prevents replacing a working motor or control module.
searchTerms: driver side temperature control not working

when.summary: When A/C stays commanded on, either temperature setting responds incorrectly, or the blower does not operate.
notes: These tests apply to DATC equipment and require the complaint to be present.

prepare.title: Establish electrical readiness
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, verify battery state of charge exceeds 70%, and retrieve relevant module codes. Diagnose circuit codes before broader performance complaints.

prepare.title: Provide the required diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use a digital multimeter, correct connector probe adapters and a scan tool that reads FCIM and powertrain control module (PCM) parameter identifiers (PIDs). Test H also requires manifold gauges and refrigerant-service capability.

prepare.title: Follow the connection sequence
prepare.detail: Have the wiring diagrams available. Observe each step's ignition state and connector isolation; resistance tests require isolated, unpowered circuits.

steps.title: Test H: check why A/C remains on
steps.body: Component-test the clutch relay and replace it if it fails. If it passes, disconnect the relay and compressor clutch field coil as directed, then check for unwanted voltage in the coil supply circuit. Voltage remaining in this isolated circuit calls for wiring repair.

steps.title: Compare A/C sensor information and commands
steps.body: Allow cabin and exterior temperatures to equalize, then compare evaporator-sensor resistance with the temperature table and PCM ambient-temperature reading. Check that CC_SW_AC becomes Active when the button is pressed and Inactive when released. Compare gauge pressure with ACP_PRESS; disagreement beyond ±103 kPa (15 psi) directs pressure-transducer replacement. Follow H6–H7's AC_REQ branches to the appropriate FCIM or PCM check.

steps.title: Test I: diagnose the driver temperature door
steps.body: Isolate all components listed in I1, including the other actuators and temperature/humidity sensor. Test the driver actuator circuits for voltage shorts, ground shorts, opens and shorts between wires, in that order. Repair any failed circuit. If every circuit check passes, replace the driver actuator through its installation procedure and test operation before proceeding to I5.

steps.title: Test J: diagnose the passenger temperature door
steps.body: Repeat the corresponding isolation and circuit tests using the passenger-specific pin map. Its continuity checks involve both FCIM connectors C2402A and C2402B; the driver map does not apply. Passing all circuit tests directs passenger-actuator replacement. If the complaint remains afterward, continue to J5's FCIM checks.

steps.title: Test K: establish blower power and control
steps.body: Inspect BJB fuse 10 (40A), where BJB means battery junction box. Test the blower relay, its supply, dedicated ground and FCIM control circuit. Then check speed-control supply and ground, followed by PWM circuit checks. Follow the specified panel-mode and highest-speed selections so measurements represent a commanded blower.

steps.title: Distinguish the blower motor from its speed control
steps.body: At K10, more than 11 volts across the disconnected motor connector directs motor replacement. Otherwise, test the motor wiring for opens and shorts between its circuits. Only after those checks pass does K12 direct speed-control replacement. Retest; an unresolved complaint continues to K13.

steps.title: Complete the relevant module endpoint
steps.body: Inspect module connectors, repair corrosion or damaged/displaced terminals, reconnect securely and operate the system. Persistent FCIM concerns require checking technical service bulletins, then the vehicle identification number (VIN)-dependent guided routine when no bulletin applies. H9's PCM branch similarly checks bulletins before directing PCM replacement.

watchFor.title: A false temperature-door endpoint
watchFor.body: Binding during calibration can be learned as the door's travel limit, leaving outlet temperature wrong despite a commanded endpoint.

watchFor.title: Incorrect probing
watchFor.body: Wrong adapters can damage terminals. Do not apply power or ground directly to module-controlled circuits unless the diagnostic procedure directs it.

notes: For Tests I and J, continuity must be less than 3 ohms; the specified isolation checks must exceed 10,000 ohms. Use each test's exact pin pairs.
A blower stuck at full speed needs the incorrect-operation branch; it is not the same observation as an inoperative motor.

diagnostics.finding: Driver-side B1081:11, B1081:12 or B1081:13, or passenger-side B1082:11, B1082:12 or B1082:13, is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The suffixes indicate motor-circuit short to ground, short to battery or open circuit, respectively. Shorts can restrict movement to one direction; an open prevents movement.
diagnostics.next: Use Test I for the driver side or Test J for the passenger side.

diagnostics.finding: B11E5:12, B11E5:14, B11E6:12 or B11E6:14 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These identify driver or passenger door-position feedback faults. The :12 suffix indicates excessive voltage; :14 indicates low voltage from a ground short or open.
diagnostics.next: Test the corresponding side's circuits before replacing its actuator.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B10AF:11 or B10AF:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: B10AF:11 indicates a grounded relay-control circuit. B10AF:15 can indicate an open, leaving the relay inactive, or a battery short, holding it on.
diagnostics.next: Check the relay and its circuits; the code alone does not establish relay failure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B10B9:12 or B10B9:14 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A PWM short to voltage can stop the blower. B10B9:14 can describe a ground short causing full speed or an open causing no operation.
diagnostics.next: Match the actual blower behavior to the diagnostic branch and test the PWM circuit.

verification.title: Repeat the affected function
verification.body: After repair, operate the relevant A/C, driver-temperature, passenger-temperature or blower controls and confirm normal response. Actuator and speed-control replacement branches explicitly require this check before module diagnosis.

verification.title: Record supporting results
verification.body: Keep the relevant switch/request PID states, pressure comparison, circuit measurements and final operating response. Document whether the complaint remains or requires the VIN-dependent routine.

guides.title: Diagnose blower speed and sensor faults with dual automatic temperature control
guides.summary: Trace incorrect blower operation and climate-sensor circuit faults through the wiring, connectors and component checks that determine the next repair.
guides.introduction: Dual Automatic Temperature Control (DATC) maintains separate driver and passenger temperature settings using controlled airflow and sensor feedback. The front controls interface module (FCIM) is central to these tests. Choose the diagnostic branch that matches the current complaint or recorded diagnostic trouble code (DTC).
guides.why: A wiring fault can resemble a failed sensor or controller. Air-discharge thermistors change resistance with temperature, so reliable circuit measurements and sound connector contacts are essential before replacing parts.

when.summary: When blower speed is incorrect or climate-sensor circuit codes are recorded.
notes: The relevant concern must be present during diagnosis; an absent intermittent fault does not justify following a replacement branch.

prepare.title: Prepare for electrical diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, correct Rotunda Flex Probes and Wiring Diagrams Cell 55. This work requires confident connector identification, circuit isolation and live voltage measurement.

prepare.title: Establish a reliable starting point
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Record related module codes, investigate circuit faults first, and inspect previous repairs, fuses and harness damage.

steps.title: Test L: establish whether the blower operates
steps.body: With ignition on, select PANEL and compare minimum and maximum blower settings. No operation at any setting directs you to Test K in the [climate diagnosis procedure](#/document/G1676857). If the blower operates but behaves incorrectly, continue through Test L.

steps.title: Test L: separate wiring faults from speed-control faults
steps.body: Follow L2–L4 to check the pulse-width modulation control circuit for shorts to voltage and ground, then the relay-coil control circuit for a voltage short. Follow L5 with the relay disconnected: a continuously running fan points to a voltage short in circuit CH402 (YE/GN). Otherwise inspect and repair speed-control connectors, reconnect and retest. Replace the speed control only at L6; persistent trouble proceeds to L7.

steps.title: Test M: check the discharge-temperature sensor circuit
steps.body: These thermistors decrease resistance as temperature rises. Disconnect the suspect driver-side register or footwell sensor and perform M1 with ignition and climate controls on. A reading of 4.7–5.1 volts directs sensor replacement, code clearing and another self-test. Otherwise check signal and return circuits for voltage shorts, ground shorts, opens and a short together. Passing those checks also directs sensor replacement; a returning code leads to M9.

steps.title: Test N: isolate the cabin temperature and humidity circuits
steps.body: Inspect the sensor harness for chafing. Follow N1's ignition and disconnection sequence for the air-distribution, both temperature-door and air-inlet actuators, cabin sensor, body control module (BCM) fuse 21 (5A), and FCIM. Check all six sensor circuits for voltage shorts, ground shorts, opens and shorts together. Repair connectors and reconnect as directed before retesting. Replace the sensor only if N5 still finds the concern; continued trouble leads to N6.

steps.title: Test O: test the sunload-sensor wiring
steps.body: Follow the prescribed isolation of the sunload sensor, FCIM and BCM connectors. Check for shorts to voltage, shorts to ground, open circuits and shorts between the sensor circuits. Repair any failed circuit. If all checks pass, install a new sunload sensor and test operation; persistent trouble leads to O5.

steps.title: Complete the applicable FCIM branch
steps.body: At L7, M9, N6 or O5, inspect FCIM connectors. Replace damaged or corroded terminals, clean module pins and correct pushed-out pins; reconnect until seated and latched. Retest and address the cause of any connection problem. If the concern remains, check Ford OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins and follow a matching bulletin. Otherwise continue with the FCIM guided routine using the vehicle identification number.

watchFor.title: Probe and isolation errors
watchFor.body: Use the exact ignition states, connector sequence and probe adapters specified. Do not measure resistance on a powered circuit or apply jumper power to module-controlled components.

watchFor.title: Different sensor pin assignments
watchFor.body: Register and footwell sensor signal pins differ. Use the relevant connector table rather than copying the other sensor's connections.

notes: Use each pinpoint test's specified resistance limits and pin pairs rather than a generic continuity rule.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B10B5:11, B10B5:15, B10B6:11 or B10B6:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: B10B5 identifies the left panel sensor and B10B6 the left floor sensor. Suffix :11 indicates a ground short; :15 indicates a battery short or open.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test M to distinguish wiring, sensor and FCIM faults.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B105A:12 or B105A:14 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: B105A:12 indicates excessive cabin-sensor fan-circuit voltage with the fan inactive. B105A:14 indicates no voltage with the fan active, suggesting a ground short or open.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test N before replacing the sensor assembly.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A61:11, B1A61:15, B1A69:12 or B1A69:14 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: B1A61 identifies cabin-temperature feedback: ground short or battery short/open respectively. B1A69 identifies humidity input: battery short or ground short/open respectively.
diagnostics.next: Use Test N's complete circuit and connector checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A63:11, B1A63:15, B1A64:11 or B1A64:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: B1A63 concerns right solar feedback; B1A64 concerns left solar feedback. Suffix :11 indicates a ground short; :15 indicates a battery short or open.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test O.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1B71:11 or B1B71:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive evaporator-reference voltage drop indicates a ground short; no drop indicates a voltage short or open, respectively. Both faults cause calculated evaporator temperature and compressor shutdown.
diagnostics.next: Continue evaporator-sensor circuit diagnosis before attributing the loss of cooling to the compressor.

verification.title: Repeat the affected test
verification.body: Confirm normal operation after repair. Following discharge-sensor replacement, clear DTCs and repeat the self-test; a returning code requires the next diagnostic branch.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record initial codes, circuit readings, repairs and operating or self-test results so the repair is supported by evidence.

guides.title: Diagnose EMTC climate-control faults, pressure-sensor codes and clutch-relay faults
guides.summary: Use code-directed electrical tests and an ordered functional check to identify the next repair path for manual climate-control complaints.
guides.introduction: Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC) uses the control-panel selections to set outlet temperature, airflow direction and blower speed. Air conditioning also removes moisture. These checks distinguish refrigerant-pressure feedback and compressor-relay faults from problems with the blower, doors or control requests, including complaints that cannot initially be reproduced.
guides.why: The powertrain control module (PCM) reads the pressure transducer and grounds the compressor-clutch relay when conditions permit. Incorrect feedback or a control-circuit fault can interrupt cooling without proving that the compressor itself has failed.

when.summary: Use for climate-control complaints, relevant diagnostic codes, or an intermittent concern with no reproducible fault.
notes: Follow the EMTC controls fitted to the vehicle when checking temperature selection.

prepare.title: Prepare for pressure and electrical testing
prepare.detail: Have a compatible scan tool, manifold gauge set, digital multimeter, correct Flex Probe adapters and wiring diagrams. This requires competence with refrigerant gauge connections and live electrical measurements.

prepare.title: Check the starting conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge above 70%. Inspect previous repairs and loose or corroded connections. Use the separate engine-specific PCM connector tables and each test's ignition and isolation instructions.

steps.title: Use the code and symptom charts together
steps.body: Identify whether the complaint concerns cooling, heating, airflow, blower speed or communication. Reduced airflow starts with cabin-filter inspection; insufficient cooling calls for the engine-specific refrigerant tests before pursuing the temperature door. Network codes can follow low voltage or programming, so inspect battery and network connections before suspecting a module.

steps.title: Test A: compare actual and reported pressure
steps.body: For P0532 or P0533, let the air-conditioning system stabilize to ambient temperature. With ignition on, compare manifold pressure with the PCM ACP_PRESS parameter identification (PID). If readings agree within ±103 kPa (15 psi), the test directs you to disregard those codes for this diagnosis and follow the symptom chart. Otherwise continue circuit testing.

steps.title: Test A: isolate the pressure-sensor circuits
steps.body: Disconnect the specified PCM connector, pressure transducer, generator current sensor and turbocharger boost pressure sensor if fitted. Follow A2–A5 in order for shorts to voltage, shorts to ground, opens and shorts between circuits. Repair failures. If every circuit passes, install a pressure transducer using its separate procedure and retest; only a remaining concern advances to the PCM checks.

steps.title: Test B: diagnose P0645 at the clutch relay
steps.body: Inspect the specified battery junction box fuses. Remove the relay with ignition off, then check its specified supplies with ignition on. Investigate failed fuses or supply circuits. Component-test the relay using Wiring Diagrams Cell 149 and replace it only if it fails. If it passes, isolate the PCM and relay and check the control wire for shorts to voltage, shorts to ground and an open, in that order.

steps.title: Complete the PCM decision when directed
steps.body: At A6 or B6, switch ignition off and inspect PCM connectors. Correct corrosion, damaged terminals and pushed-out pins, then latch connectors and retest. If the concern persists, check applicable technical service bulletins before following the engine-specific PCM replacement procedure.

steps.title: Test C: check blower, outlets and heating
steps.body: For an unreproduced complaint without codes, run the PCM self-test, then the front controls interface module (FCIM) self-test; route any codes through their charts. In panel mode, check every blower speed: no operation routes to J; wrong speeds or failure to shut off routes to K. At maximum blower, check every outlet mode; incorrect distribution routes to E. Warm the engine, switch A/C off and move temperature from cold to hot and back. Weak heat routes to F; no temperature change routes to I.

steps.title: Test C: check compressor requests and recirculation
steps.body: With the engine running, A/C off, panel mode and cold selected, outlet air should approach ambient temperature. Warmer air routes to I; significantly colder air with the clutch engaged routes to H. Above 0°C (32°F), request A/C in panel mode: no compressor operation routes to G. Finally, at maximum blower in panel mode, switch recirculation from off to on. Increased airflow noise completes the functional check; no increase routes to D.

watchFor.title: Recirculation faults can be electrical or mechanical
watchFor.body: Motor-circuit shorts can allow movement in only one direction; an open prevents movement. Feedback faults misreport position, while binding during calibration can establish a false end stop.

watchFor.title: Protect terminals and measurement validity
watchFor.body: Do not force probes into connectors. Follow Diagnostic Methods for resistance-test isolation; a disconnected supply-voltage check alone cannot rule out excessive resistance under load.

notes: Compressor-control code P06A0 routes to N; clutch-request code P193E routes to O. Sensor and reference-supply codes have separate chart paths.
For remote-start-only complaints, verify the message-center Auto or Last User Settings selection, installed remote-start equipment and network operation.

Pulley-bearing roughness directs clutch and field-coil replacement; excessive plenum hissing calls for refrigerant-level testing. For a discharging relief valve, compare high-side pressure with the specified opening pressure: below it directs valve replacement; above it directs restriction repair.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic code P0532 or P0533 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: Pressure-sensor feedback is electrically low or high respectively; neither code alone establishes refrigerant quantity.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test A's gauge comparison and circuit checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic code P0645 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detects unexpected clutch-relay control voltage for the commanded state.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test B through supply, relay and control-wire testing.

diagnostics.finding: Door-actuator code B1081:07, B1083:07 or B1086:07 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: These identify mechanical faults involving temperature, recirculation or distribution respectively.
diagnostics.next: Inspect door and linkage binding or damage first; replace the corresponding actuator only if no such condition is found.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic code P1464 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: An active climate-control request may have placed A/C demand outside self-test conditions.
diagnostics.next: If climate control was on, switch it off, clear codes and repeat the self-test. A returning code routes to H.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic code B10B8:63 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: A control button has remained activated too long.
diagnostics.next: Attempt button cleaning, clear codes and repeat the self-test. If it returns, use the vehicle-identification-number-specific FCIM guided routine.

verification.title: Check the affected function
verification.body: Retest after the directed correction. Completing all Test C checks establishes correct operation at that time, without proving an intermittent complaint permanently resolved.

verification.title: Record evidence and the next decision
verification.body: Record codes, ambient conditions, gauge/PID comparison, functional results and any remaining pinpoint-test referral.

guides.title: Diagnose airflow, weak heat and inoperative A/C with EMTC
guides.summary: Trace air-door, heater and air-conditioning complaints through the electrical, coolant-flow and compressor-control checks for Electronic Manual Temperature Control.
guides.introduction: Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC) uses your panel selections to control outlet temperature, airflow direction and blower speed. Electric actuators position the air doors, hot coolant supplies the heater core, and air conditioning cools and dehumidifies cabin air. These tests separate problems in those systems before directing a repair.
guides.why: Similar complaints can have different causes. Poor heat can come from coolant circulation or a temperature door, while a compressor may remain off because the powertrain control module (PCM) is deliberately protecting the system. Testing the circuits and control inputs prevents premature component replacement.

when.summary: Use when the inlet door fails, outlet selection is incorrect, heat is inadequate, or the A/C does not operate.
notes: Confirm the complaint is present before following a component-replacement decision.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical testing capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool supporting network tests, self-tests and active commands, plus a digital multimeter and correct terminal probe adapters. Check battery condition, wiring and repair history; diagnose PCM trouble codes first.

prepare.title: Arrange thermal and refrigerant testing
prepare.detail: Have a suitable temperature measuring device, cooling-system pressure tester and refrigerant manifold gauges. Cooling-system filling and bleeding, refrigerant leak repair and recovery/charging require the appropriate procedures and equipment.

prepare.title: Use the exact circuit instructions
prepare.detail: Follow the linked test's ignition states, connector isolation and pin tables. Test D uses inlet actuator connector C282; Test E uses distribution actuator connector C232. Inspect battery junction box fuses 23 (10A) and 42 (15A) for Test G.

steps.title: Test D: trace an inoperative inlet door
steps.body: Follow D1-D4 in order: check for unwanted voltage, shorts to ground, open circuits and circuits shorted together. Complete the specified sensor, actuator and module disconnections before measuring. Repair a failed circuit. If every circuit check passes, install a new inlet-door actuator and test operation; a continuing complaint leads to D5.

steps.title: Test E: trace incorrect outlet selection
steps.body: Follow E1-E4 using the distribution actuator's own pin map and the same sequence of electrical fault checks. Repair failed wiring; passing results direct a new distribution-door actuator. Retest airflow direction and continue to E5 if the complaint remains. The front controls interface module (FCIM) uses actuator feedback to determine door position.

steps.title: Test F: establish coolant supply before blaming an air door
steps.body: Check coolant level. If low, pressure-test: repair leaks and retest, or fill and bleed when no leak is found. At operating temperature, select floor outlets, full warm and minimum blower speed. Hold 3,500 RPM for 30 seconds, then idle for 30 seconds. Measure inlet-hose temperature; bleed as directed if it is not hot. Compare outlet temperature using F4's approximately 6-17°C [10-30°F] criterion. A passing comparison directs temperature-door diagnosis and Test I; a failed comparison directs heater-core replacement.

steps.title: Test G: establish pressure and communication
steps.body: With ignition off, check refrigerant pressure. At or below 290 kPa (42 psi), find and repair leaks, then recharge. Above that threshold, run the network test; communication failures require network diagnosis. Compare gauge pressure with the PCM's ACP_PRESS parameter identification (PID), its live pressure reading. A mismatch outside G3's tolerance directs pressure-transducer diagnosis.

steps.title: Check fan operation and temperature inputs
steps.body: Run the key-on, engine-off self-test and confirm the cooling fan operates during it. Diagnose a failure before continuing. Let cabin and exterior temperatures stabilize to ambient, potentially requiring at least 6 hours, then compare applicable temperature PIDs. Diagnose suspect readings. Check evaporator-sensor resistance against G6's temperature table; an out-of-range result directs replacement. Where active grille shutters are fitted, allow their idle calibration and verify commanded opening and closing under G7.

steps.title: Follow the A/C request through the modules
steps.body: In PANEL mode with A/C selected, check FCIM CC_SW_AC: an inactive reading leads to G17. If active, check PCM AC_REQ. A missing request leads to the ambient-temperature reset: press A/C and Recirc together, release, then press A/C again within 2 seconds. Run the engine with full cold, PANEL and A/C selected. Restored compressor operation requires the engine-specific refrigerant performance test; otherwise continue to G11.

steps.title: Separate a control inhibition from a clutch power fault
steps.body: Command the compressor through PCM ACC_CMD. If it operates, continue to G18. If not, follow G12's relay-supply checks and fuse decisions. Use only G13's specified fused relay bypass. Engagement with the bypass directs a new relay after removing the jumper. Otherwise retain the jumper for G14's field-coil feed measurement, then remove it. Repair a failed feed circuit.

steps.title: Finish the clutch electrical and mechanical checks
steps.body: With ignition off, check the field-coil ground through G15. Repair a failed ground. If it passes, measure clutch air gap at 3 equally spaced locations. A gap greater than 0.6 mm (0.0236 in) requires adjustment; otherwise G16 directs a new clutch and field coil.

steps.title: Investigate why an operable compressor is being inhibited
steps.body: G18 checks pressure, temperature, engine-load, battery and network conditions that can disable A/C. Diagnose any abnormal input. If the PCM can command the clutch on, PCM replacement will not resolve the inhibition. With normal inputs, investigate intermittent wiring or connectors and recent module replacement with incomplete or incorrect installation/configuration.

steps.title: Resolve the FCIM connector branches
steps.body: For D5, E5 or G17, inspect all FCIM connectors. Replace damaged, bent or pushed-out terminals; repair corrosion with the specified connector/terminal replacement and module-pin cleaning. Reconnect securely and retest. A remaining complaint requires checking applicable Technical Service Bulletins, then the vehicle-identification-number-dependent FCIM guided routine if no bulletin applies.

watchFor.title: False learned door travel
watchFor.body: Binding during calibration can be interpreted as an end stop, leaving airflow at unexpected outlets.

watchFor.title: Misleading static pressure
watchFor.body: Static refrigerant pressure alone cannot establish that the charge quantity is correct.

notes: These paths apply to EMTC. Use only temperature sensors, shutters and control-strategy conditions applicable to the fitted vehicle.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1086:11 or B1086:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The distribution-motor circuit indicates a short to ground or voltage respectively; movement may be limited to one direction.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test E before condemning the actuator.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1086:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: An indicated open distribution-motor circuit prevents movement.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test E's circuit checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B11E7:12 or B11E7:14 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The feedback circuit indicates excessive voltage, or a short to ground/open circuit, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Test the feedback wiring through Test E; the code does not establish actuator failure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1464 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detected an A/C request during its self-test.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the request condition. For an always-commanded-on complaint, possible sources include the relay, wiring, PCM and FCIM.

verification.title: Repeat the affected operating check
verification.body: Confirm normal inlet-door, outlet-selection or heating operation after the directed repair. Verify restored A/C operation with the refrigerant test for the installed engine.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record relevant codes, measurements, command responses and the final operating result, including any unresolved intermittent concern.

guides.title: Diagnose A/C, temperature and blower faults with electronic manual temperature control
guides.summary: Separate constant A/C operation, incorrect outlet temperature and blower faults using the appropriate electrical and scan-data tests.
guides.introduction: Electronic manual temperature control (EMTC) lets you select outlet temperature, air distribution and blower speed. Its front controls interface module (FCIM) manages the controls, while a relay and electronic speed controller supply the blower. The blower command uses pulse width modulation (PWM), varying electrical pulses to control speed. These tests distinguish incorrect commands from circuit, sensor, actuator and motor faults.
guides.why: The same symptom can have different causes: a blower control wire shorted to ground can produce full speed, while an open wire stops operation. A temperature door that binds during calibration can also teach an incorrect travel limit, leaving outlet temperature wrong even when the control responds.

when.summary: When A/C stays on, outlet temperature responds incorrectly, or the blower stops or runs at the wrong speed.
notes: These branches apply to EMTC; dual automatic temperature control uses a different diagnostic path.

prepare.title: Prepare for electrical diagnosis
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge above 70%. Record relevant diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Have Wiring Diagrams Cells 54 and 149, a digital multimeter, correct flex-probe adapters and relay-testing capability.

prepare.title: Arrange scan and refrigerant measurements
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool that reads FCIM and powertrain control module (PCM) parameter identification (PID) data. Test H also requires a manifold gauge set and the capability to make refrigerant-pressure measurements.

steps.title: Test H: check why A/C remains on
steps.body: Follow H1–H3 in the [EMTC diagnostic procedure](#/document/G1681095). Component-test the clutch relay and replace it if it fails. With ignition off, disconnect the relay and clutch coil; with ignition on, voltage at C100 pin 1 indicates a circuit short to voltage. If none exists, switch off and stabilize cabin and exterior temperatures. Compare disconnected evaporator-sensor resistance with the chart using the PCM ambient air temperature (AAT) PID; an out-of-range result directs sensor replacement.

steps.title: Test H: compare the switch and pressure information
steps.body: In panel mode, check CC_SW_AC: it should show Active while the A/C button is pressed and Inactive when released. Incorrect status goes to H8. Otherwise, compare manifold pressure with ACP_PRESS. A difference outside ± 103 kPa (15 psi) directs pressure-transducer replacement; agreement allows the request-signal checks to continue.

steps.title: Test H: follow the request-signal branches exactly
steps.body: With panel mode selected and the A/C indicator off, AC_REQ should read No. A No result goes to H9, the PCM connector check. Otherwise, disconnect FCIM C2402A with ignition on as specified in H7 and reread AC_REQ: No also goes to H9; a continuing request goes to H8, the FCIM connector check.

steps.title: Test I: isolate the temperature-door wiring
steps.body: Follow I1–I4’s connector and ignition sequence, including isolation of the temperature/humidity sensor and all three door actuators. Test the driver-side temperature actuator circuits for shorts to voltage, shorts to ground, opens and shorts together, in that order. Repair failed circuits. If all checks pass, replace the driver-side temperature door actuator and test operation. A remaining concern advances to I5’s FCIM connector check.

steps.title: Test J: establish the blower relay supply
steps.body: For an inoperative blower, inspect battery junction box (BJB) fuse 10 (40A), then component-test the relay. Replace a failed relay. Follow J2–J5 through the relay supply, coil ground, control-circuit short-to-ground and continuity checks. If the fuse has failed, investigate the cause of the short using the wiring diagrams.

steps.title: Test J: distinguish the motor from its controller
steps.body: Continue J6–J12: check speed-controller supply with panel mode and maximum blower selected, its ground, then the PWM circuit for a voltage short or open. More than 11 volts across the disconnected motor connector directs motor replacement. Otherwise, test the motor wiring for opens and shorts together. Passing those checks directs speed-controller replacement and an operational retest; a remaining fault advances to J13.

steps.title: Test K: investigate incorrect speed or continuous running
steps.body: Try minimum and maximum blower settings in panel mode; no operation returns to Test J. Otherwise, check PWM wiring for voltage and ground shorts, then relay-control wiring for a voltage short. Follow K5’s reconnection sequence with the relay removed. Continuous running then identifies a short to voltage in CH402 (YE/GN). Otherwise, inspect speed-controller connectors; persistent trouble directs controller replacement, retesting and, if necessary, K7.

steps.title: Complete connector checks before module decisions
steps.body: At FCIM, PCM or speed-controller checks, replace corroded or damaged terminals/connectors, clean module pins and correct pushed-out pins. Reconnect securely and operate the system. Persistent FCIM or PCM concerns require an applicable technical service bulletin check through OASIS. Follow any matching bulletin; otherwise FCIM endpoints require the vehicle identification number (VIN) guided routine, while H9 directs the engine-appropriate PCM replacement procedure.

watchFor.title: Connector damage during testing
watchFor.body: Use the correct adapters and prescribed isolation sequence. Forcing probes into terminals can create faults; voltage remaining in a circuit invalidates resistance measurements.

watchFor.title: Temporary improvement after reseating
watchFor.body: If reconnecting restores operation, still correct the underlying corrosion, terminal damage or poor retention.

notes: Follow the full removal and installation procedure for any component replacement selected by these tests.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1081:11, B1081:12 or B1081:13 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The temperature-actuator motor circuit indicates a ground short, voltage short or open respectively. Shorts can limit travel to one direction; an open prevents movement.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test I’s wiring checks before its actuator decision.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B11E5:12 or B11E5:14 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: Temperature-door feedback indicates a voltage short, or a ground short/open, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Use Test I to distinguish wiring faults from the actuator.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B10AF:11 or B10AF:15 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The relay-control circuit indicates a ground short, or voltage short/open. An open leaves the relay inactive; a battery short can hold it on.
diagnostics.next: Use Test J for no blower operation or Test K for incorrect operation.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B10B9:12 or B10B9:14 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: A PWM voltage short stops the blower. With B10B9:14, a ground short produces full speed, while an open stops operation.
diagnostics.next: Select Test J or K from the observed behavior.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1B71:11 or B1B71:15 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The evaporator-sensor circuit indicates a ground short, or voltage short/open. The module substitutes calculated temperature and shuts off the compressor.
diagnostics.next: Continue with the applicable evaporator-sensor circuit diagnosis; these codes alone do not prove sensor failure.

verification.title: Reproduce the original operating conditions
verification.body: Operate the repaired system and confirm A/C command response, temperature response or blower operation as appropriate. After actuator or speed-controller replacement, continue to the specified FCIM check if the concern persists.

verification.title: Record the decisive results
verification.body: Record relevant codes, PID observations, pressure comparisons and circuit measurements alongside the observed symptom and final operational result.

procedures.purpose: EMTC Tests H–K for constant A/C, temperature-control and blower faults.
Electrical preparation, safe terminal probing and circuit measurement methods.
Evaporator-temperature sensor removal and installation after Test H identifies an out-of-range sensor.
A/C pressure-transducer removal and installation after the pressure comparison fails.
Driver-side temperature-door actuator removal and installation after Test I wiring checks pass.
Blower motor removal and installation after Test J confirms its replacement endpoint.
Blower speed-controller removal and installation when Test J or K directs replacement.

guides.title: Diagnose cabin temperature and humidity sensor circuit faults with EMTC
guides.summary: Check the sensor wiring and connectors before deciding whether the cabin sensor or its control-module path needs further work.
guides.introduction: Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC) uses the panel selections to control outlet temperature, air distribution and blower operation. The cabin temperature and humidity sensor measures conditions inside the vehicle. Test P checks its electrical paths to the front controls interface module (FCIM) and its fused supply before directing sensor replacement or further module diagnosis.
guides.why: An unwanted connection to power, ground or another wire can corrupt a sensor circuit, while an open prevents the intended connection. Checking these faults separately avoids replacing a sensor for a wiring problem. Correct probe adapters also prevent the test itself from damaging terminals.

when.summary: When a current sensor-circuit concern and one of Test P's listed diagnostic codes direct this investigation.
notes: Do not follow a component replacement decision when the concern is absent.

prepare.title: Establish valid electrical conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, verify battery state of charge above 70%, and retrieve relevant diagnostic trouble codes. Inspect previous repairs, harness routing and obvious connector damage.

prepare.title: Arrange access and test capability
prepare.detail: Use a digital multimeter, correct terminal probe adapters and connector information for Test P. Access is needed to the listed actuators, sensor, FCIM connectors and body control module (BCM) fuse. Follow the ignition sequence exactly.

steps.title: P1: isolate the circuits and check for unwanted voltage
steps.body: Follow [Test P](#/document/G1681095): with ignition off, disconnect the air distribution, driver-side temperature, passenger-side temperature and air inlet actuators, then sensor C233 and BCM fuse 21 (5A). Switch ignition on, then disconnect FCIM C2402A and C2402B. Check every C233 terminal to ground. Any voltage requires circuit repair; no voltage permits P2.

steps.title: P2: check for shorts to ground
steps.body: Reconnect FCIM C2402A, switch ignition off, then disconnect C2402A again as directed. Measure each sensor circuit to ground. Every resistance must exceed 10,000 ohms. Repair a circuit that fails this isolation check before continuing.

steps.title: P3: prove each intended connection
steps.body: Use the exact pin pairs to check continuity from C233 to both FCIM connectors and to the component side of the BCM fuse 21 cavity. Each path must measure less than 3 ohms. A failed path requires wiring or terminal repair, rather than a sensor replacement.

steps.title: P4: check the circuits against one another
steps.body: Measure every listed combination of sensor terminals, not just neighboring terminals. Each pair must exceed 10,000 ohms. This establishes that wires intended to remain separate have not become connected through harness damage or connector faults.

steps.title: P5: restore connections and evaluate the sensor
steps.body: Inspect disconnected connectors. Replace damaged, bent or pushed-out terminals; address corrosion with new connectors or terminals and clean module pins as directed. Restore the fuse and connections, ensuring connectors latch, then operate the system. If the concern remains, follow [sensor removal and installation](#/document/G1676817), install a new sensor and test again. Continue to P6 only if the concern persists.

steps.title: P6: investigate the FCIM connection path
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect all FCIM connectors and repair terminal faults. Reconnect and retest. If the concern remains, check applicable technical service bulletins and follow any relevant instructions. Otherwise, continue with the FCIM guided routine, which requires the vehicle identification number. This branch does not establish an immediate FCIM replacement decision.

watchFor.title: Resistance measurements on energized wiring
watchFor.body: Residual circuit voltage invalidates resistance readings. Preserve the specified isolation and ignition states when changing from voltage to resistance tests.

watchFor.title: A fault that disappears after reconnection
watchFor.body: Loose or corroded terminals may explain the recovery. Find and correct the connection defect before closing the job.

notes: This is an EMTC electrical diagnostic path; separate automatic driver and passenger temperature regulation belongs to the dual automatic system.

diagnostics.finding: One or more of B105A:12, B105A:14, B1A61:11, B1A61:15, B1A69:12 or B1A69:14 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These codes direct Test P's in-vehicle temperature and humidity sensor circuit investigation.
diagnostics.next: Establish circuit condition first, then follow the connector, sensor and FCIM decisions in order.

verification.title: Confirm operation after each repair stage
verification.body: Operate the climate system after connector repairs and after sensor replacement. A remaining concern must proceed to the next specified stage.

verification.title: Record the findings and stopping point
verification.body: Record the entry codes, failed circuit or passing measurements, connector repairs and functional result. If FCIM guided diagnosis remains necessary, record that handoff rather than declaring the concern resolved.

procedures.purpose: EMTC Test P: sensor circuit isolation, voltage and resistance checks, sensor evaluation and FCIM handoff.
Electrical prerequisites, safe terminal probing and valid circuit measurement methods.
In-vehicle temperature and humidity sensor removal and installation when P5 directs replacement.

guides.title: Measure and adjust the A/C compressor clutch air gap
guides.summary: Measure the clutch clearance at three positions and adjust its spacers to meet the specification for the fitted compressor.
guides.introduction: The air-conditioning clutch connects the belt-driven pulley to the compressor when cooling is required. Its air gap is the clearance between the clutch plate and pulley. Spacers between the plate hub and compressor shaft set that clearance. This job measures the gap and changes the spacer arrangement; it does not establish that a cooling complaint is caused by the clutch or compressor.
guides.why: The clearance must allow the clutch to engage and release correctly. Measuring around the plate gives a more useful picture than taking one reading. The fitted compressor also determines the final fastener torque, so identifying its type is part of the repair rather than a detail to decide afterward.
searchTerms: clutch air gap out of specification

when.summary: When measured compressor-clutch clearance falls outside its applicable specification.
notes: Use the installed compressor's specification and tightening branch; the cabin temperature-control system does not identify that branch.

prepare.title: Obtain the acceptance specification
prepare.detail: Have the applicable Group 412 air-gap specification and clutch/field-coil removal and installation instructions available. The adjustment procedure refers to those instructions rather than giving a universal clearance.

prepare.title: Prepare measurement and adjustment equipment
prepare.detail: Use a suitable feeler gauge, a torque wrench and the required clutch-service tools and spacers. For some vehicles, a shim kit is available only with the clutch assembly.

prepare.title: Workshop capability
prepare.detail: Fixed or external variable displacement A/C compressor

steps.title: Measure before disturbing the clutch
steps.body: Following the [air-gap adjustment procedure](#/document/G1890620), measure between the clutch plate and pulley at 3 equally spaced positions. Record each reading and compare it with the applicable Group 412 specification.

steps.title: Remove the clutch by its service procedure
steps.body: If adjustment is required, remove the A/C clutch using the applicable clutch and field-coil instructions. Access to the spacers is through clutch removal; the gap is not adjusted by changing belt tension.

steps.title: Change the spacer arrangement
steps.body: Add or remove spacers between the clutch plate hub and compressor shaft until the clearance meets specification. The cross-section identifies this location; it does not supply a universal spacer thickness or stack.

steps.title: Tighten and remeasure
steps.body: Complete clutch installation and use the correct tightening branch: 20 Nm for a fixed compressor or 14.5 Nm for an external variable displacement compressor, abbreviated EVDC. Recheck the gap at all 3 positions after tightening.

watchFor.title: Choosing torque by appearance
watchFor.body: The illustration shows a spring-rubber clutch, with other designs described as similar. Identify the compressor before selecting its torque.

watchFor.title: Relying on one measurement
watchFor.body: A satisfactory reading at one position does not replace the required checks around the plate.

notes: Do not invent a target gap from the illustration. Use the applicable dimensional specification before deciding whether adjustment has passed.

diagnostics.finding: The measured gap is outside specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The spacer-controlled clearance requires correction; this finding alone does not condemn the compressor.
diagnostics.next: Adjust the spacer arrangement and repeat the measurements after installation.

diagnostics.finding: All required gap readings meet specification.
