guides.title: Remove and replace the center air registers
guides.summary: Release the passenger-side dash end panel, remove the long upper trim and unplug its connector, then release the eight retaining clips around each center register.
guides.introduction: Two little air outlets have recruited a surprisingly wide stretch of dashboard as their entourage. I’ll walk you in from the passenger-side end panel, unplug the upper trim, and reach the register clips from behind. The trick is releasing each attachment patiently; dashboard plastic has never improved its manners under brute force.
guides.why: The center registers are the adjustable outlets that aim heated or cooled air into the cabin. The climate controls choose the temperature, blower speed and air distribution; these outlets direct the air at the dashboard. Each register clips into the upper trim panel, so removing that panel gives access to the attachments that hold the outlet in place.

when.summary: Use this procedure when a center air register needs removal or replacement.
notes: The illustrated arrangement has center gauges. Vehicles without center gauges use a similar removal and reverse-order installation procedure.
The procedure applies to all four listed engines; there is no engine-specific removal branch.

prepare.title: Gather the trim tool and protect the removed panel
prepare.detail: Have a trim-removal wedge ready, as pictured for both trim panels. Prepare a clean, protected surface where the long upper panel can rest with its rear retaining clips accessible. Have the replacement register ready if you are replacing an outlet.

prepare.title: Set up for stationary cabin work
prepare.detail: Park securely with the parking brake applied. This work is performed inside the cabin and needs no lifting. If remote start is fitted, disable it through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before switching off the ignition. Remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person starting it. Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling sharp edges.

prepare.title: Keep the repair boundary clear
prepare.detail: This job covers the outlets and their trim attachments. It does not determine the cause of inadequate heating, cooling or blower operation. On EMTC, the panel settings control temperature, distribution and blower speed; on DATC, automatic control maintains the selected cabin temperatures and allows separate driver and passenger settings.

steps.title: Secure the vehicle and identify the access panels
steps.body: Complete the stationary-work precautions above before touching the trim. From the passenger side, identify the small dash end panel beside the glovebox and the long upper trim panel that carries the two round center outlets and extends above the glovebox. These come off in that order. The [center register procedure](#/document/G1676807) provides the removal and reverse-order installation sequence.

steps.title: Release the passenger-side dash end panel
steps.body:
Open the passenger door for access to the end of the dashboard. Place the trim-removal wedge at the end panel’s perimeter seam and ease the panel away, working near its retaining points. The illustration shows three clips distributed through the upper, middle and lower portions of this panel.

Support the panel as the clips release, then remove it. If one area remains attached, work at that attachment instead of bending the whole panel around it. The wedge is there to persuade a clip, not audition as a crowbar.

steps.title: Unclip the long center upper trim panel
steps.body:
Use the trim-removal wedge at the upper trim panel’s perimeter to begin separating it from the dashboard. Work along the panel, supporting the released portions while freeing the remaining attachments. The illustrated panel has 13 retaining clips spread across its width, including the area around the round outlets and the passenger-side extension.

Once the panel is unclipped, hold it close to the dashboard until its electrical connection is accessible. Do not pull the panel away against the wiring.

steps.title: Disconnect the upper trim wiring and position the panel
steps.body:
Locate the electrical connector on the rear of the upper trim. In the center-gauge arrangement, the illustration places it behind the central gauge area. Support the panel, release the connector latch and separate the connector by its body without pulling on the wires.

Remove the panel and place it on the protected surface with its rear accessible. Vehicles without center gauges are serviced similarly; identify the electrical connection on the actual panel before separating it.

steps.title: Release the register retaining clips from the rear
steps.body:
Identify the two round register bodies on the rear of the removed trim, one on either side of the center gauge area in the illustrated arrangement. Each register has eight retaining clips around its circumference.

Support the register while releasing its clips from the trim. Work around the body and separate the register only when its attachments are free. If it remains caught at one point, locate and release that remaining clip before continuing. Repeat for the other register if it also needs removal.

steps.title: Install the registers into the removed trim
steps.body:
Position each removed or replacement register in its matching trim opening, aligning the retaining clips with their receiving features. Seat the register and engage the eight clips around its body.

Look around the full circumference from the rear to confirm that every clip has engaged and the register sits evenly in the opening. If part of the register stands away from the trim, correct the alignment and clip engagement before reinstalling the panel.

steps.title: Reconnect the wiring and reinstall the upper trim
steps.body:
Bring the upper trim back to the dashboard while supporting its weight. Reconnect the electrical connector and confirm its latch has engaged before pressing the panel into place.

Align the panel’s retaining clips with their dashboard locations, making sure the wiring is clear of the seating edges. Press at the clip locations along the panel until all 13 illustrated attachments are engaged. Check the panel’s seating along its entire length; one proud corner is a reason to check alignment, not hit it harder.

steps.title: Refit the side panel and check the completed assembly
steps.body:
Align the passenger-side dash end panel with its three retaining locations and press it into place. Confirm that it sits evenly against the surrounding trim.

Check that both center registers remain secured in the upper panel and that their adjustable vanes can be moved normally. Confirm the upper trim is fully seated, its electrical connector is reattached, and no wiring is trapped at an edge. Remove the tool and protective materials from the cabin.

watchFor.title: A released panel still has a wiring tether
watchFor.body: Support the upper trim until the connector is unplugged. Its electrical wiring must not carry the panel’s weight.

watchFor.title: A clip remains engaged
watchFor.body: Local resistance during removal calls for checking the attachment at that location. Avoid bending the panel or pulling on the register face to overcome an unreleased clip.

watchFor.title: Uneven seating during installation
watchFor.body: Check clip alignment and wiring clearance before applying more pressure. Complete the register seating checks while the rear of the upper panel is still accessible.

notes: Installation reverses removal: registers into upper trim, electrical connector reconnected, upper trim installed, then passenger-side end panel installed.
The pictured retaining counts are three for the side panel, 13 for the upper trim panel and eight for each center register.
The [EMTC overview](#/document/G1681091) explains manual climate-control operation; the [DATC overview](#/document/G1676851) explains automatic and separate driver/passenger temperature control.

diagnostics.finding: The upper trim is unclipped but cannot be moved away freely.
diagnostics.meaning: The electrical connector may still be attached, or a retaining clip may remain engaged.
diagnostics.next: Support the panel, inspect its rear connection and remaining attachment points, then disconnect or release the attachment before removing it.

diagnostics.finding: A register remains attached after some retaining clips have been released.
diagnostics.meaning: One or more of its eight clips may still be holding it to the trim.
diagnostics.next: Work around the register from the rear, identify the retained point and release it before separating the outlet.

diagnostics.finding: A register or trim panel does not sit evenly during refitting.
diagnostics.meaning: Its clips may be misaligned or incompletely engaged; wiring may obstruct the upper panel.
diagnostics.next: Pause installation, check the receiving locations and wiring clearance, then reseat the component and confirm all retaining points engage.

verification.title: Register retention and adjustment
verification.body: Before reinstalling the upper trim, visually confirm all eight clips on each installed register are engaged. After assembly, confirm the outlets remain seated while their adjustable vanes are moved.

verification.title: Trim and connector completion
verification.body: Confirm the upper trim connector was latched before the panel was seated, the upper trim is secured across its full width, and the passenger-side end panel is flush and retained at all three points. These are assembly checks, not tests of heating or cooling performance.

guides.title: Remove and refit the climate control housing using the correct engine procedure
guides.summary: Remove the climate control housing behind the instrument panel, then restore its refrigerant and coolant connections using engine-specific instructions.
guides.introduction: The climate control housing forms the cabin heating and cooling assembly behind the instrument panel, with connections to the heater core and air-conditioning evaporator. Removing it opens both the refrigerant and engine-coolant circuits. The work therefore combines substantial interior access with controlled fluid-system service, even though the housing itself comes out as an assembly.
guides.why: Open refrigerant connections must stay protected from contamination, and their seals require the correct installation materials. Refrigerant oil replacement and cooling-system filling are part of completing the repair. Engine variants share the general removal path, but their fastener details, hose access and finishing procedures must remain with the correct engine.

when.summary: When an established repair requires removal or replacement of the climate control housing.
notes: Select the engine-specific procedure before starting; the housing instructions do not diagnose a heating or cooling complaint.

prepare.title: Arrange the required service capabilities
prepare.detail: Provide refrigerant recovery, evacuation and charging capability, instrument-panel removal capability, and equipment for the correct engine’s cooling-system filling and bleeding procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare connection protection and materials
prepare.detail: Have suitable caps or other protective closures, specified seal lubricant and the required clean polyalkylene glycol (PAG) refrigerant oil. Obtain new O-rings where required by the selected engine procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare the engine-specific access
prepare.detail: The 5.0L route also requires engine appearance-cover removal and locking pliers to clamp the heater hoses before disconnection.

steps.title: Recover refrigerant and remove the instrument panel
steps.body: Choose the housing procedure for the fitted engine. Recover the refrigerant before opening the air-conditioning circuit, then remove the instrument panel following its complete access procedure and prerequisites.

steps.title: Disconnect and protect the refrigerant lines
steps.body: Remove the nut and thermostatic expansion valve (TXV) bracket. Disconnect the condenser outlet and evaporator outlet lines, immediately protecting their open ports against debris.

steps.title: Disconnect the heater-core hoses
steps.body: Disconnect the heater-core inlet and outlet hoses. On the 5.0L, first remove the appearance cover and clamp the hoses with locking pliers. If cover grommets remain in the cover, move them onto the intake manifold before refitting it.

steps.title: Release the housing mountings
steps.body: Follow the selected procedure’s illustrated sequence for the bolts, washers, nuts and retaining bracket, then remove the housing. Keep the hardware associated with its mounting location.

steps.title: Position and fasten the housing
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, using the chosen engine’s fastener locations and tightening specifications. The 3.7L has a different torque at the second nut-and-washer location; use its own mounting instructions.

steps.title: Restore the connections and refrigerant oil
steps.body: Remove protective closures before reconnecting the hoses and lines. The 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures specifically require new O-rings lubricated only with the specified material. Follow the selected connection instructions and add the correct amount of clean PAG oil using Refrigerant Oil Adding.

steps.title: Complete refrigerant and cooling-system service
steps.body: Finish reassembly through the instrument-panel procedure. Use the linked recovery, evacuation and charging procedure to restore refrigerant service, and fill and bleed the cooling system using the procedure for the fitted engine.

watchFor.title: Unprotected openings
watchFor.body: Protect openings throughout removal, but remove every temporary closure before its connection is assembled.

watchFor.title: Borrowed specifications
watchFor.body: Do not transfer seal lubricant, oil quantity, charge quantity or cooling-system instructions between engine variants.

notes: Electronic manual temperature control and dual automatic temperature control provide different cabin controls; neither changes the need to select the correct engine service route.

verification.title: Check connection and mounting completion
verification.body: Confirm that the housing and bracket are fastened to the engine-specific instructions, the hoses and lines are reconnected, and required new seals were installed.

verification.title: Record fluid-service completion
verification.body: Record the selected engine, refrigerant-oil addition, completion of refrigerant service, and completion of the matching cooling-system fill and bleed.

guides.title: Replace the air-conditioning condenser using the engine-specific access procedure
guides.summary: Recover the refrigerant, create clearance around the radiator, replace the condenser and complete the applicable sealing and refrigerant-service work.
guides.introduction: The air-conditioning condenser releases heat from the refrigerant into the outside air. It forms part of the cooling assembly at the front of the vehicle, so replacement involves refrigerant connections as well as radiator-area access. The 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures share this approach, but their intake access, underbody work and stated seal requirements must remain tied to the correct engine.
guides.why: Opening a refrigerant circuit requires controlled recovery and clean working practices. Dirt admitted through an uncovered connection remains inside the system. Moving the radiator assembly provides clearance for the condenser retaining tabs, while the correct seal lubricant and refrigerant oil requirements protect the reassembled circuit.

when.summary: When diagnosis or physical damage has established that the air-conditioning condenser requires replacement.
notes: A cabin cooling complaint alone does not establish that the condenser needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange refrigerant-service capability
prepare.detail: Have the equipment and capability for refrigerant recovery, evacuation and charging. Obtain the applicable seal materials and refrigerant oil requirements through the linked procedures; do not assume quantities or lubricants across variants.

prepare.title: Prepare clean, supported access
prepare.detail: Have suitable caps or other port protection and a hoist. Use the marked lifting points and check adapter clearance. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

steps.title: Recover refrigerant and raise the vehicle
steps.body: Select the condenser procedure for the installed engine. Recover the refrigerant before disconnecting either line, then place the vehicle in NEUTRAL and position it on a hoist using the lifting instructions.

steps.title: Open the lower and upper access areas
steps.body: Remove the underbody shield hardware; on the 5.2L, complete both specified underbody-shield removal steps. Disconnect the condenser outlet line and immediately protect its openings. Remove the radiator sight shield, disconnect the compressor outlet line and protect those openings as well.

steps.title: Clear the radiator mounting area
steps.body: Remove the engine-specific air cleaner and air cleaner outlet pipe. Unbolt and position the coolant degas bottle aside, then remove the upper radiator brackets. These removals create the space needed to reposition the cooling assembly.

steps.title: Release the condenser
steps.body: Lift the radiator off its lower support and move the radiator, transmission fluid cooler assembly, cooling fan motor and shroud toward the engine. Release the condenser tabs and remove the condenser using the arrangement shown for the applicable engine.

steps.title: Install the condenser and reconnect the circuit
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. For the 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L, install new O-ring seals lubricated only with the specified material. Follow the 3.7L procedure for that engine. Remove protective caps or tape as each connection is reassembled.

steps.title: Restore the surrounding assemblies
steps.body: Return the radiator assembly to its lower support and reinstall its upper brackets, the degas bottle, intake components and shields. Tighten each connection and mounting fastener to the specification in the selected engine procedure.

steps.title: Complete refrigerant servicing
steps.body: Add the correct amount of clean polyalkylene glycol (PAG) oil using the [refrigerant oil procedure](#/document/G1912330). Complete the applicable evacuation and charging work through the [refrigerant service procedure](#/document/G1912323); oil addition and refrigerant charging are separate requirements.

watchFor.title: Unprotected openings
watchFor.body: Keep disconnected refrigerant ports covered throughout removal. Remove all protective material before making the connections.

watchFor.title: Illustration-only bumper removal
watchFor.body: The front bumper is shown removed for clarity. The condenser instructions do not make that illustration a separate bumper-removal requirement.

notes: Use the engine-specific intake procedures referenced within the selected condenser procedure.
Match the condenser release arrangement to the selected engine’s procedure.

verification.title: Check mechanical restoration
verification.body: Confirm that the condenser tabs are engaged, the radiator is restored to its supports and every displaced bracket, intake component, line and shield has been reinstalled.

verification.title: Confirm refrigerant-service completion
verification.body: Record completion of the applicable oil-adding and recovery, evacuation and charging procedures, including their required final checks.

guides.title: Replace the A/C condenser outlet line
guides.summary: Replace the condenser outlet line using the engine-specific access sequence, protected refrigerant connections and the required refrigerant service.
guides.introduction: The air-conditioning (A/C) condenser outlet line carries refrigerant onward from the condenser toward the thermostatic expansion valve (TXV). The sealed refrigerant circuit supports cabin cooling and moisture removal. Replacement involves opening that circuit, moving nearby wiring and releasing the line from its clips and bracket; access differs significantly between engines.
guides.why: Refrigerant must be recovered before a connection is opened. Open fittings also need immediate protection because dirt introduced during a line replacement can remain inside the system. The compressor inlet connection is disconnected for this job as well, so protecting only the condenser connection is insufficient.

when.summary: When a condenser outlet line has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Poor cooling alone does not establish that this line is faulty.
Choose the procedure for the installed engine before starting; access and installation requirements are not identical.

prepare.title: Arrange refrigerant service
prepare.detail: This work requires refrigerant recovery, evacuation and charging equipment and the capability to use it correctly. Have clean caps or suitable protective coverings ready for every opened connection.

prepare.title: Prepare safe underbody access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist at the specified lifting points, identified by the stamped triangles. Check adapter and underbody clearance; never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Plan the engine-specific parts and access
prepare.detail: The 5.2L procedure requires replacement strut-tower cross-brace nuts, new O-ring seals, specified seal lubricant and the correct amount of clean polyalkylene glycol (PAG) refrigerant oil.

steps.title: Recover refrigerant and raise the vehicle
steps.body: Complete refrigerant recovery through the linked refrigerant-service procedure. With the vehicle in NEUTRAL, position it on the hoist. Recovery precedes opening any refrigerant fitting.

steps.title: Expose and disconnect the condenser connection
steps.body: On the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L, remove the underbody shield bolts and retainers. The 5.2L has successive underbody-shield removal operations. Follow its own sequence, then disconnect the condenser outlet fitting and protect the opening.

steps.title: Release the compressor-side access
steps.body: On the 5.2L, first detach the wiring-harness retainer and remove the strut-tower cross brace, discarding its nuts. Disconnect the compressor inlet fitting on the applicable engine and seal the exposed openings.

steps.title: Free the wiring and line clips
steps.body: Detach the wiring retainers and move the harness aside. Release the two condenser outlet line clips so the line can be removed without pulling against its retained sections.

steps.title: Reach the expansion-valve end
steps.body: The 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L require battery-tray removal followed by the battery heat shield and its bolts. These operations are not listed for the 2.3L. Remove the TXV bracket nut and bracket, detach the line and remove it.

steps.title: Install the replacement line
steps.body: Reverse the appropriate engine's removal sequence. Remove protective coverings as connections are assembled. On the 5.2L, install and lubricate new O-rings using only the specified material, replenish clean PAG oil through the applicable oil-adding procedure and replace the discarded cross-brace nuts.

steps.title: Complete refrigerant service
steps.body: Finish evacuation and charging through the linked refrigerant-service procedure, using the applicable specifications. Refit the clips, wiring retainers, brackets and access components through the engine-specific installation sequence.

watchFor.title: Unprotected openings
watchFor.body: Keep disconnected tubes and fittings protected throughout removal and installation; remove the protection before joining them.

watchFor.title: Mixed fastener settings
watchFor.body: The battery heat-shield fasteners have separate torque assignments. Follow the applicable procedure rather than applying one setting to every fastener.

notes: The 5.2L seal and oil instructions belong to that engine's procedure; do not transfer its requirements or quantities to another variant.

verification.title: Check the completed installation
verification.body: Confirm the line connections, clips and TXV bracket are restored, wiring is retained again and all engine-specific access components are installed.

verification.title: Record refrigerant-service completion
verification.body: Record the engine variant and completion of recovery, evacuation and charging, including any oil addition required by the applicable procedure.

guides.title: Replace the driver-side dashboard air register
guides.summary: Remove the surrounding dashboard trim in sequence, release the driver-side register and restore the panels and electrical connections.
guides.introduction: The driver-side register is the dashboard outlet through which conditioned air reaches the driver. The climate-control system determines air temperature, distribution and blower operation; the register provides the final outlet into the cabin. Replacing it involves several surrounding trim panels because its retaining clips are reached after the instrument-cluster trim is removed.
guides.why: This is a layered trim-removal job. Some panels use bolts as well as clips, and the lighting-switch and left-hand finish panels have electrical connections to release. Following the sequence keeps attached wiring and the steering-column gap hider from being pulled as the panels are separated.

when.summary: When the driver-side register requires replacement or removal during dashboard repair.
notes: A broader heating or cooling complaint needs climate-system diagnosis before selecting a register repair.

prepare.title: Prepare trim and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Use an interior trim remover and tools for the illustrated bolts. Have a torque tool suitable for the specified 27 lb.in (3 Nm) trim-fastener tightening.

prepare.title: Plan the center-panel prerequisite
prepare.detail: Begin with the linked instrument panel center finish panel procedure. Be ready to support removed panels while releasing their electrical connectors.

steps.title: Remove the center finish panel
steps.body: Complete the linked center finish panel removal procedure before working through the driver-side trim. Follow its fitted-equipment instructions for any panel electrical connection.

steps.title: Release the left-hand instrument panel trim
steps.body: Use the interior trim remover to release the clips and remove the left-hand trim panel. This is the next access layer in the specified sequence.

steps.title: Remove the lighting-switch trim
steps.body: Remove its bolt, release its clips and separate the panel. Disconnect the electrical connector before removing the panel fully. Keep track of this fastener for the specified installation torque.

steps.title: Remove the left-hand finish panel
steps.body: Remove its bolts and release its clips with the trim remover. Disconnect its electrical connector, then remove the finish panel so the remaining lower and cluster trim can be reached.

steps.title: Clear the lower cover and cluster trim
steps.body: Release the lower instrument panel cover clips and position the cover aside. Remove the instrument panel cluster trim bolts and release its clips. Detach the gap hider from the upper steering-column trim cover as the cluster trim is removed.

steps.title: Separate the register assembly
steps.body: Release the register's retaining clips and remove the driver-side register assembly. The illustration identifies the clips holding the register to its surrounding trim; release these before separating the parts.

steps.title: Reassemble the dashboard
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, starting with the register. Restore the cluster trim and gap hider, lower cover, left-hand finish panel, lighting-switch trim and remaining panels. Reconnect the disconnected electrical connectors. Tighten the cluster-trim, left-hand finish-panel and lighting-switch trim bolts to 27 lb.in (3 Nm). Finish by reinstalling the center finish panel through its linked procedure.

watchFor.title: Bolts still holding a panel
watchFor.body: The lighting-switch, left-hand finish and cluster trim panels have bolts in addition to clips; release both forms of attachment.

watchFor.title: Gap hider still attached
watchFor.body: Detach it from the upper steering-column cover before taking the cluster trim away, and restore it during installation.

notes: The lower instrument panel cover is positioned aside during access; the procedure does not call for its complete removal.
The register removal procedure is not restricted to either manual or dual automatic temperature control.

verification.title: Confirm the completed trim assembly
verification.body: Check register and panel clip engagement, restoration of the gap hider and electrical connectors, and tightening of the specified trim bolts.

procedures.purpose: Driver-side register removal and installation through the left-hand dashboard and cluster trim.
Required center finish panel removal before register access and reinstallation afterward.

guides.title: Replace the driver-side temperature door actuator
guides.summary: Replace the driver-side temperature door actuator with its timing marks aligned and keep it unpowered whenever it is detached from the door shaft.
guides.introduction: The temperature door actuator moves the door that controls delivered air temperature. Electronic manual temperature control uses the selected setting to determine outlet temperature, while dual automatic temperature control maintains a selected cabin temperature and permits separate driver and passenger settings. This repair replaces the driver-side actuator and restores its mechanical relationship with the temperature door.
guides.why: Moving the door to its mid-position, when possible, unloads tension and makes actuator replacement easier. The timing marks then provide the installation reference. Power must not be applied while the actuator is disconnected from the door shaft, so position changes should be made while the assembly is still coupled.
searchTerms: driver side temperature door actuator replacement
driver vent temperature does not change

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the driver-side temperature door actuator requires replacement.
notes: An unwanted outlet temperature alone does not prove that the actuator has failed.

prepare.title: Identify the attachment points
prepare.detail: Use the illustration to identify the actuator, its connector and the two retainers. Prepare suitable hand tools and access to those attachments.

prepare.title: Plan the door position
prepare.detail: If the installed system can still move the temperature door, arrange to place it at mid-position before disconnecting the actuator.

steps.title: Unload the door where possible
steps.body: Place the temperature door in its mid-position while the actuator remains attached. This reduces the tension that can make removal and replacement more difficult. The instruction is conditional on being able to move the door.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the actuator
steps.body: Disconnect the driver-side actuator connector, remove the illustrated retainers and remove the actuator from the temperature door shaft. Keep it unpowered while detached.

steps.title: Inspect and align the timing marks
steps.body: Before installing the replacement, inspect the timing marks and align them. Use these references to establish the correct relationship between the actuator and door rather than powering the detached actuator to change its position.

steps.title: Restore the attachment and connection
steps.body: Install the actuator by reversing removal: fit it to the door shaft, restore the retainers and reconnect its electrical connector. Maintain the required alignment during assembly.

watchFor.title: Power applied to a detached actuator
watchFor.body: Do not bench-run the actuator or reconnect it for powered adjustment while it is off the temperature door shaft.

watchFor.title: Unresolved timing-mark alignment
watchFor.body: Resolve alignment before securing the actuator. Its installed position must follow the timing marks.

notes: Driver and passenger settings can be independent on dual automatic temperature control vehicles; identify the driver-side component before removal.

verification.title: Confirm the mechanical reference
verification.body: Confirm that the timing marks were inspected and aligned before installation.

verification.title: Confirm complete reassembly
verification.body: Verify that the actuator is attached to the temperature door shaft, both retainers are restored and the electrical connector is connected.

procedures.purpose: Driver-side temperature door actuator removal and installation, including mid-position preparation, the detached-power prohibition and timing-mark alignment.

guides.title: Replace the evaporator outlet line on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Replace the evaporator outlet line using the correct engine access procedure, then evacuate and recharge the sealed refrigerant circuit.
guides.introduction: The evaporator outlet line carries refrigerant away from the cabin evaporator as part of the air-conditioning circuit. Replacing it opens that circuit, so the job includes refrigerant recovery and controlled recommissioning. The engines share the component’s purpose, but access differs substantially: the V8 procedures require removal of surrounding battery and cowl components.
guides.why: Dirt or moisture entering an open refrigerant connection can compromise the system. Refrigerant must therefore be recovered before disconnection, and exposed ports protected immediately. Correct routing and fastening support the line without loading its connections. Engine-specific instructions matter particularly for the cross brace, heat shield and replacement seals.

when.summary: When the evaporator outlet line has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Poor cooling alone does not establish that this line needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange refrigerant service capability
prepare.detail: Use refrigerant identification equipment and Ford-approved R134A management equipment, following the equipment instructions. Recovery requires connections to both service ports.

prepare.title: Prepare protection and replacement materials
prepare.detail: Have suitable port caps or covers. The 5.2L procedure requires replacement cross-brace nuts, new O-ring seals, specified seal lubricant and the correct clean polyalkylene glycol (PAG) oil.

prepare.title: Plan V8 access
prepare.detail: Have the battery-tray and cowl-panel procedures available. The 5.0L procedure also explicitly requires disconnection of both battery cables.

steps.title: Identify and recover the refrigerant
steps.body: Check refrigerant purity before recovery. Connect to both service ports and record any oil removed for replacement later. After recovery, observe the vacuum for about 2 minutes; repeat recovery if it does not remain stable.

steps.title: Open the 5.0L access route
steps.body: Disconnect the battery ground and positive cables. If a strut tower cross brace is fitted, detach its wiring-harness retainer and remove the brace. Remove the cowl panel grille, battery tray, cowl extension and battery heat shield in the specified sequence.

steps.title: Open the 5.2L access route
steps.body: Remove the battery tray, detach the harness retainer, and remove the cross brace, discarding its nuts. Then remove the cowl panel grille, cowl extension and battery heat shield. Keep the heat-shield fastener groups identified because their tightening specifications differ.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the line
steps.body: For the 2.3L and 3.7L, proceed directly here after recovery. Remove the nut and thermostatic expansion valve (TXV) bracket, then disconnect the outlet line. Seal the openings immediately. Remove the remaining nuts and lift out the line, following the applicable engine illustration.

steps.title: Install the line and restore access components
steps.body: Reverse the applicable removal sequence, using that engine’s fastening specifications. Remove protective caps as connections are assembled. On the 5.2L, install and lubricate new O-rings using only the specified material, and use replacement cross-brace nuts. Restore any disconnected battery cables through the battery procedure.

steps.title: Evacuate the closed circuit
steps.body: Follow the recovery, evacuation and charging procedure to reach the specified vacuum. Continue pumping for at least 45 minutes, then stop the pump and observe the gauge for 10 minutes to establish whether vacuum is held.

steps.title: Restore oil and refrigerant
steps.body: Use the applicable refrigerant-oil procedure to establish the correct clean PAG oil amount, including oil removed during recovery. Set the correct vehicle refrigerant charge on the service unit and charge according to its instructions.

watchFor.title: Contaminated refrigerant
watchFor.body: Keep contaminated refrigerant out of ordinary recovery equipment. It requires designated recovery equipment and the prescribed disposal route.

watchFor.title: Unprotected ports
watchFor.body: Cover every opening while disconnected; remove the protection before assembling the connection.

notes: After battery reconnection, temporary changes in driving behavior can occur while the powertrain control module relearns its adaptive settings.

diagnostics.finding: Vacuum falls during the recovery pause.
diagnostics.meaning: Recovery has not reached the required stable condition.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the recovery sequence until vacuum remains stable for 2 minutes.

verification.title: Confirm circuit readiness
verification.body: Confirm the specified evacuation vacuum was achieved and held through the 10-minute observation before charging.

verification.title: Record the service result
verification.body: Record recovered oil, oil restored, refrigerant charge and vacuum-hold result alongside the engine-specific line replacement.

guides.title: Replace the evaporator temperature sensor through climate-control housing renewal
guides.summary: Replace the housing assembly containing the evaporator temperature sensor using the removal and installation procedure for the vehicle’s engine.
guides.introduction: The evaporator temperature sensor monitors temperature at the air-conditioning evaporator. It is available only as part of the climate-control housing, so this repair involves housing renewal rather than extracting and replacing a separately supplied sensor. The housing belongs to the system that heats, cools and distributes cabin air; air conditioning also reduces cabin-air humidity.
guides.why: The scale of the repair comes from access to the housing and its connected systems. On the 5.2L, removal opens refrigerant and heater connections and requires instrument-panel removal. Cleanliness, new refrigerant seals and correct fluid restoration therefore matter as much as fitting the replacement assembly.

when.summary: Use after diagnosis has established that evaporator temperature sensor replacement is necessary.
notes: A cooling complaint alone does not establish a sensor fault.
Select the housing procedure for the fitted engine before beginning access work.

prepare.title: Confirm the replacement assembly
prepare.detail: Arrange the climate-control housing containing the sensor. Do not plan a separate sensor extraction or an access shortcut.

prepare.title: Prepare for the engine-specific access work
prepare.detail: Follow the linked housing procedure for the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L. The 5.2L route requires refrigerant-recovery capability, instrument-panel removal, protected fluid openings and subsequent cooling-system filling and bleeding.

prepare.title: Have sealing and fluid materials ready
prepare.detail: For the 5.2L, provide new O-ring seals, the specified seal lubricant and the correct clean polyalkylene glycol (PAG) refrigerant oil. Obtain material specifications and oil-adding instructions from the applicable Group 412 procedures.

steps.title: Follow the correct housing access route
steps.body: Use the sensor procedure together with the housing procedure for the installed engine. The 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L each have their own removal and installation article; the 5.2L has a separate route. Keep their mounting and fluid-service instructions with their respective variants.

steps.title: Recover refrigerant and expose the housing on the 5.2L
steps.body: Recover refrigerant using the appropriate recovery procedure before opening refrigerant connections. Remove the instrument panel as directed to gain access to the housing and its mounting points.

steps.title: Disconnect the 5.2L housing connections
steps.body: Remove the thermostatic expansion valve (TXV) bracket and disconnect the condenser outlet and evaporator outlet lines. Protect every open port against contamination. Disconnect the heater-core inlet and outlet hoses as directed.

steps.title: Release and remove the housing
steps.body: For the 5.2L, follow the illustrated sequence for the bolts, washers, nuts and bracket before removing the housing. Use the corresponding mounting sequence for other engines. Housing removal provides the replacement route for the sensor contained within it.

steps.title: Install the replacement and restore connected systems
steps.body: Reverse the applicable removal procedure and observe its installation details. On the 5.2L, remove protective coverings before reconnecting, install new lubricated O-rings using only the specified material, add the correct amount of clean PAG oil, and fill and bleed the cooling system using the 5.2L procedure.

watchFor.title: Unprotected openings
watchFor.body: Dirt entering exposed refrigerant or housing connections can contaminate the system. Keep openings protected until reconnection.

watchFor.title: Reusing refrigerant seals
watchFor.body: The 5.2L installation requires new O-rings and the specified lubricant; retaining old seals does not follow the installation route.

notes: Use each engine’s own fastener specifications and fluid-service directions. The 5.2L details here do not establish requirements for the other engines.
Manual and dual automatic temperature-control systems differ in cabin controls, but those differences do not establish a separate sensor-replacement method.

verification.title: Confirm installation completion
verification.body: Check that the applicable reverse-removal sequence is complete, mounting hardware is tightened to that procedure’s specifications and protective materials have been removed from reconnected openings.

verification.title: Confirm the 5.2L service requirements
verification.body: Verify completion of new-seal lubrication, the specified refrigerant-oil addition, and engine-cooling-system filling and bleeding before considering the housing installation complete.

Climate-control housing removal and installation for the 2.3L EcoBoost.
Climate-control housing removal and installation for the 3.7L Duratec.

guides.title: Replace the A/C evaporator through climate control housing replacement
guides.summary: Replace the evaporator as part of the climate control housing, following the access and restoration procedure for the fitted engine.
guides.introduction: The evaporator is the air-conditioning heat exchanger that cools cabin air and helps remove moisture. It sits inside the climate control housing behind the instrument panel. For this repair, the evaporator is available only with the housing, so the work involves removing that assembly, transferring components as required and installing the replacement housing.
guides.why: This is substantial access work rather than a separate evaporator-core exchange. Choosing the correct engine procedure keeps refrigerant connections, housing mountings and cooling-system restoration tied to the vehicle being repaired. Clean openings and correctly prepared seals protect the refrigerant circuit during reassembly.

when.summary: Use after diagnosis has established that the evaporator requires replacement.
notes: A cooling complaint alone does not establish an evaporator fault.

prepare.title: Choose the engine procedure
prepare.detail: Have the housing removal and installation procedure for the fitted 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine available before dismantling.

prepare.title: Arrange workshop capability
prepare.detail: The detailed 5.2L route requires refrigerant recovery, instrument-panel removal and subsequent cooling-system filling and bleeding. Arrange the equipment and capability for those operations.

prepare.title: Prepare the replacement and protection
prepare.detail: Have the replacement housing and suitable caps or tape for openings. The 5.2L installation requires new refrigerant O-ring seals, specified seal lubricant and the correct refrigerant oil.

steps.title: Establish the complete housing route
steps.body: Begin with the evaporator procedure, then follow the housing procedure matching the engine. The 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L routes are separate references; use the dedicated 5.2L route for that engine.

steps.title: Complete preliminary access
steps.body: For the 5.2L, recover refrigerant using the applicable Group 412 recovery procedure, then remove the instrument panel using its complete procedure. These operations provide access and prepare the refrigerant circuit for disconnection.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the housing
steps.body: On the 5.2L, remove the nut and thermostatic expansion valve (TXV) bracket, then disconnect the condenser outlet and evaporator outlet lines. Cover open ports immediately. Disconnect the heater-core inlet and outlet hoses, remove the specified fasteners and bracket in sequence, and remove the housing.

steps.title: Transfer the required components
steps.body: Move components from the old housing to the replacement as required by the evaporator procedure. This transfer prepares the new assembly for installation; the repair does not call for extracting and replacing a separately supplied evaporator core.

steps.title: Install through the matching engine procedure
steps.body: Reverse the applicable housing-removal sequence, using its installation details and fastening specifications. Remove temporary opening protection before making connections. On the 5.2L, install new O-ring seals lubricated only with the specified material.

steps.title: Complete fluid restoration
steps.body: For the 5.2L, add the correct amount of clean polyalkylene glycol (PAG) refrigerant oil through the applicable oil-adding procedure, then fill and bleed the cooling system. Follow the restoration requirements attached to each other engine's housing procedure.

watchFor.title: Unprotected refrigerant openings
watchFor.body: Dirt can enter while lines and ports are disconnected. Keep openings protected until the connection is ready to be assembled.

watchFor.title: Incomplete installation
watchFor.body: Housing fitment alone does not complete the 5.2L job: new seals, correct lubrication, oil addition and cooling-system filling and bleeding remain required.

notes: Manual and dual automatic climate controls request temperature differently, but this evaporator repair still uses the climate control housing replacement route.
Use engine-specific fastening and fluid instructions; do not carry 5.2L values into another engine's procedure.

verification.title: Check assembly restoration
verification.body: Confirm required components were transferred and the housing, connections, brackets and instrument-panel installation have been completed through the applicable procedure.

verification.title: Record required service completion
verification.body: For the 5.2L, record new seal installation, specified lubricant and refrigerant-oil addition, and completion of cooling-system filling and bleeding.

2.3L EcoBoost climate control housing removal and installation.
3.7L Duratec climate control housing removal and installation.
5.0L climate control housing removal and installation.
