guides.title: Replace the footwell air discharge temperature sensor
guides.summary: Replace the footwell temperature sensor through the driver knee-airbag opening, following the required restraint-system depowering and repowering procedures.
guides.introduction: The footwell air discharge temperature sensor measures the temperature of air delivered toward the occupants’ feet. Replacing it changes the sensing component at that outlet. Although the sensor itself has a short removal sequence, reaching it requires removal of the driver knee airbag, making restraint-system handling the most demanding part of the job.
guides.why: An airbag must remain safe during handling and work correctly afterward. Incorrect repair can cause an accidental deployment or compromise protection in a crash. The supplemental restraint system (SRS) must be depowered before airbag work and before reconnecting the component. Reattaching the trim is not the final step: the prescribed SRS repowering procedure is also required.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the footwell air discharge temperature sensor requires removal or replacement.
notes: A cabin-temperature complaint alone does not establish that this sensor has failed.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: The technician must be able to follow the complete SRS depowering and repowering procedures referenced by the Driver Knee Airbag procedure. Do not substitute an improvised isolation method.

prepare.title: Prepare lower instrument-panel access
prepare.detail: Have suitable trim and fastener tools and torque equipment for the knee-airbag work. Follow the applicable left-hand-drive or right-hand-drive connector and harness-retainer instructions.

steps.title: Depower the restraint system
steps.body: Start with [Driver Knee Airbag](#/document/G1696302) and follow its SRS depowering reference before removing airbag connections. Keep the restraint system depowered throughout removal and reconnection.

steps.title: Remove the driver knee airbag
steps.body: Follow the linked access sequence through the instrument-panel trim, lighting-switch trim, lower trim and ambient-air-temperature grille panel. Release their connectors and the grille tether as directed. Remove the specified nuts and screws, release the airbag clips, then detach and disconnect the airbag connector. Right-hand-drive vehicles also require release of the harness pin-type retainer.

steps.title: Remove and replace the sensor
steps.body: Use the location and removal illustration in [Footwell Air Discharge Temperature Sensor](#/document/G1676814). Remove the sensor, then disconnect its electrical connector in the stated sequence. Install by reversing these actions: reconnect the sensor and refit it at the discharge outlet.

steps.title: Restore the airbag and trim
steps.body: With the SRS still depowered, reverse the knee-airbag removal procedure. Restore the applicable harness retention, connectors, airbag attachments, grille tether and trim. Use the fastening requirements in that procedure rather than estimating tightness.

steps.title: Repower the restraint system
steps.body: Finish with the SRS repowering procedure referenced by the knee-airbag instructions. This is a required part of restoring the vehicle after sensor access.

watchFor.title: Reconnecting an energized restraint system
watchFor.body: The airbag installation warning specifically requires depowering before reconnection; accidental deployment can cause serious injury.

watchFor.title: Incomplete harness or trim restoration
watchFor.body: The access work includes electrical connectors, clips, a tether and a drive-side-specific harness retainer. Account for each during reassembly.

notes: The sensor illustration locates the component and connector; it does not establish a fault or prescribe an electrical test.

verification.title: Confirm sensor installation
verification.body: Confirm the sensor is refitted and its electrical connector is reconnected, completing the reverse removal sequence.

verification.title: Confirm restraint-system restoration
verification.body: Confirm the knee airbag and access trim are fully installed and the referenced SRS repowering procedure has been completed.

procedures.purpose: Footwell air discharge temperature sensor removal and installation after driver knee-airbag access.
Required driver knee-airbag access and refitting, including drive-side differences and references to SRS depowering and repowering.

guides.title: Replace the HVAC control assembly for the fitted SYNC system
guides.summary: Service the HVAC control module through its combined front-control assembly, following the access procedure for the vehicle's SYNC equipment.
guides.introduction: The heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) controls determine how the cabin is heated, cooled and ventilated. With electronic manual temperature control, the driver's selections determine outlet temperature, air distribution and blower operation. Dual automatic temperature control instead maintains selected cabin temperatures and allows separate driver and passenger settings. The HVAC module is available only as part of the front controls interface module (FCIM), so replacement is an assembly-level job.
guides.why: Identifying the fitted controls establishes the correct access route and the expected behavior afterward. A manual temperature setting and an automatic cabin-temperature target have different meanings. The replacement decision must also account for the combined assembly: the HVAC removal procedure does not describe extracting a separately supplied climate-control module from it.

when.summary: When replacement or removal of the combined HVAC/front-control assembly has been established as necessary.
notes: This removal procedure does not establish the cause of a heating, cooling or blower complaint.

prepare.title: Identify the fitted interface
prepare.detail: Confirm whether the vehicle has SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3, and identify manual or dual automatic temperature control before selecting the linked procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare for the complete assembly procedure
prepare.detail: Have the tools and capability required by the applicable interface-module procedure. Follow its access, connector and installation requirements when carrying out the work.

steps.title: Establish the service assembly
steps.body: Use the [HVAC control-module procedure](#/document/G1676816) to establish the replacement scope. Its service note identifies the HVAC module as part of the FCIM; select the assembly appropriate to the fitted equipment.

steps.title: Choose the correct access route
steps.body: For SYNC, follow the [FCIM procedure](#/document/G1704003). For SYNC 2/SYNC 3, the HVAC procedure directs you to the [front display interface module (FDIM) procedure](#/document/G1704008). That access reference does not change the stated FCIM service-assembly requirement.

steps.title: Remove the assembly through that procedure
steps.body: Carry out the applicable interface-module removal sequence, including its trim access and electrical connections. The HVAC article delegates these physical operations to the equipment-specific procedure.

steps.title: Reinstall and check the fitted controls
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence and complete the applicable interface procedure's installation requirements. Once assembled, check the controls against the operating functions of the fitted manual or automatic system.

watchFor.title: Equipment mismatch
watchFor.body: Confirm the SYNC version before beginning access. The HVAC article cites different interface procedures for the named equipment.

watchFor.title: Different temperature-control behavior
watchFor.body: Manual control selects outlet-air temperature; automatic control selects a desired cabin temperature and permits driver overrides.

notes: Air conditioning also reduces cabin-air humidity in both climate-control arrangements.

verification.title: Confirm completed assembly
verification.body: Check that the connections and components disturbed during the selected interface-module procedure have been restored.

verification.title: Check the applicable control functions
verification.body: For manual control, check temperature, distribution and blower selections. For dual automatic control, check temperature selection, separate driver/passenger settings and blower override.

procedures.purpose: Establish the combined HVAC/FCIM service arrangement and the equipment-dependent removal and installation route.
Front controls interface module removal and installation for vehicles with SYNC.
Front display interface module removal and installation route referenced for vehicles with SYNC 2/SYNC 3.

applicability.equipment: SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3; electronic manual or dual automatic temperature control

guides.title: Replace the in-vehicle temperature and humidity sensor
guides.summary: Release the small lower dashboard cover, unplug and unclip the cabin temperature and humidity sensor, then refit the sensor and cover.
guides.introduction: The dashboard has its own little weather station—and thankfully, replacing it does not require evicting the entire dashboard. The in-vehicle temperature and humidity sensor measures cabin warmth and moisture for the climate-control system. I’ll walk you through releasing its cover, separating the electrical plug from the mounting clips, and putting everything back without turning a small trim job into a plastic confetti festival.
guides.why: Replace this sensor when climate-system diagnosis identifies it as faulty. A cabin comfort complaint alone does not establish sensor failure. With [Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC)](#/document/G1681091), the temperature setting controls outlet-air temperature. With [Dual Automatic Temperature Control (DATC)](#/document/G1676851), it selects the cabin temperature the system works to maintain, with separate driver and passenger settings and manual overrides. Both systems reduce cabin-air humidity during A/C operation.

when.summary: When the in-vehicle temperature and humidity sensor requires removal or replacement.
notes: Applies to 2015 Mustangs with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
The removal and reverse-order installation sequence applies across the listed engines; no separate EMTC or DATC removal branch is identified.

prepare.title: Gather the trim tool and sensor
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover ready. If replacing the sensor, have the replacement ready before opening the dashboard cover.

prepare.title: Make the parked car safe to work on
prepare.detail: Apply the parking brake. If remote start is fitted, disable it through the Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before beginning service. Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person starting it. This job is performed inside the cabin with the vehicle on the ground. See the [general service precautions](#/document/G1693189).

prepare.title: Protect yourself around the trim
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts.

prepare.title: Establish the repair before removing parts
prepare.detail: This article covers physical removal and installation. Checking the sensor’s electrical accuracy requires a separate climate-control diagnostic procedure; there is no resistance, voltage or humidity acceptance test here.

steps.title: Locate the small lower dashboard cover
steps.body: Find the small cover immediately to the right of the steering wheel, between the steering-column area and the center control stack. Its face has narrow slots. This is the cover carrying the sensor; the illustrated access does not require removing the center controls or steering wheel. The [sensor removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1676817) shows this location.

steps.title: Release the cover’s four retaining clips
steps.body:
Use the interior trim remover at the cover’s edge to ease it away from the dashboard. Release the four retaining clips shown around its rear perimeter, supporting the cover as it comes free. The removal illustration shows the cover moving downward.

Lower it only far enough to reach the rear-mounted sensor and its wiring. Keep the cover supported so its weight does not hang from the electrical lead. A trim clip can be stubborn; the wiring is not a useful tug handle.

steps.title: Disconnect the sensor’s electrical plug
steps.body:
Look at the back of the released cover. The sensor projects from its mounting, with the wiring plug connected at its upper end. Release the plug’s locking feature and draw the plug out of the sensor, holding the connector housing rather than pulling on the wires.

Move the disconnected lead aside to give the sensor room to come out. The connector lock and the two side mounting tabs perform different jobs: unplug first, unclip second.

steps.title: Release the two side tabs and remove the sensor
steps.body:
Locate the opposed retaining tabs on the sides of the sensor where it meets the cover’s mounting cradle. Press both tabs inward, toward the sensor body, as shown by the inward-pointing arrows in the rear-view illustration. With the tabs released, withdraw the sensor from the cover.

Keep track of its installed orientation so the replacement returns to the same position. If it remains held, check that both tabs have cleared their catches before applying more force.

steps.title: Fit the sensor and reconnect its wiring
steps.body:
Install the replacement in the same orientation, reversing the removal movement. Seat it in the cover’s mounting until both side retaining tabs engage. Check that neither side remains loose or partly out of its catch.

Reconnect the electrical plug and make sure its lock engages. Return the lead to its position behind the cover, clear of the cover’s retaining clips.

steps.title: Refit the lower dashboard cover
steps.body:
Bring the cover back to its dashboard opening. Check that the wiring is behind it without being trapped, then align all four perimeter clips with their receiving positions. Press the cover into place, reversing its removal, until it sits evenly and is retained around its edges.

I check the alignment before pressing harder: a misplaced clip will not become better aligned through sheer enthusiasm.

steps.title: Check the completed assembly
steps.body:
Check that the cover is flush with the surrounding dashboard and does not have an unsecured edge. Remove the trim tool and any loose parts from the driver’s footwell and pedal area.

These are installation checks: the sensor should be retained, its connector locked and the cover secure. They confirm the assembly is back together; they do not measure sensor accuracy.

watchFor.title: Cover pulling against its wiring
watchFor.body: Support the released cover while reaching the connector. Stop lowering it if the lead becomes taut, and disconnect the plug before moving the cover farther.

watchFor.title: One sensor tab still engaged
watchFor.body: The sensor has retaining features on both sides. If it resists removal after unplugging, check both tabs rather than levering against the sensor body.

watchFor.title: A cover that will not sit evenly
watchFor.body: Check clip alignment and the wiring behind the cover before pressing again. A trapped lead or displaced clip needs repositioning before the cover is seated.

notes: Installation reverses removal: seat the sensor, reconnect its plug, then reinstall the cover.
Keep manual outlet-temperature selection and automatic cabin-temperature selection distinct when discussing the original climate complaint.

diagnostics.finding: The sensor remains attached after its electrical plug is disconnected.
diagnostics.meaning: Its mechanical retaining tabs have not both released.
diagnostics.next: Press the two opposed side tabs inward and check that both clear their catches before withdrawing the sensor.

diagnostics.finding: The refitted sensor is loose on one side.
diagnostics.meaning: The mounting is not fully engaged.
diagnostics.next: Reseat the sensor in its original orientation and confirm both retaining tabs engage before reconnecting and closing the cover.

diagnostics.finding: The original climate concern continues after replacement.
diagnostics.meaning: Replacing the sensor has not resolved the concern; this alone does not identify another failed component.
diagnostics.next: Continue diagnosis for the fitted EMTC or DATC system before replacing more parts.

verification.title: Sensor and connector secured
verification.body: Before closing the cover, confirm that both sensor retaining tabs are engaged and the electrical connector is fully seated with its lock engaged.

verification.title: Cover and wiring correctly positioned
verification.body: Confirm that the wiring is clear of the clips, all four cover clips retain the cover, and its face sits evenly against the surrounding dashboard.

verification.title: Driver’s work area clear
verification.body: Confirm that tools and loose parts have been removed from the footwell and pedal area before returning the vehicle to use.

procedures.purpose: Lower instrument-panel cover access, connector disconnection, sensor release and reverse-order installation.
Explain how the electronic manual climate controls select outlet temperature and reduce humidity during A/C operation.
Explain automatic cabin-temperature control, individual temperature settings and manual overrides.
Apply relevant startup-prevention and personal-protection precautions before interior service.

applicability.equipment: Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC) or Dual Automatic Temperature Control (DATC).

stepGroups.title: Open the sensor access
stepGroups.summary: Locate and release the small cover while supporting its wiring.

stepGroups.title: Remove and fit the sensor
stepGroups.summary: Disconnect the plug, release both mounting tabs and install the sensor.

stepGroups.title: Close and check
stepGroups.summary: Refit the cover and confirm the assembly and driver’s footwell are ready.

guides.title: Replace the passenger-side dashboard air register
guides.summary: Remove the surrounding dashboard trim, release the passenger air register from its clips and refit the assembly in reverse order.
guides.introduction: The passenger-side register is the dashboard outlet that directs delivered cabin air. The climate-control system determines heating, cooling and blower operation; the register provides the local outlet. This repair replaces that outlet assembly after the surrounding trim is removed. It is a relatively short trim job, but access includes an electrical connector at the center upper trim panel.
guides.why: The passenger finish panel must come off before the register’s retaining clips are released. Following that sequence exposes the actual attachments instead of pulling against them through the dashboard opening. Reconnecting the center trim and using the specified finish-panel retainer torque are part of completing the repair.

when.summary: When the passenger-side air register requires removal or replacement.
notes: The procedure shows a vehicle with center gauges and describes the version without gauges as similar.

prepare.title: Identify the trim sequence
prepare.detail: Locate the instrument-panel side trim, center upper trim and passenger finish panel. Be ready to disconnect the center upper trim’s electrical connector as that panel is removed.

prepare.title: Prepare for clips and small fasteners
prepare.detail: Have suitable trim-fastener tools and a torque tool capable of the specified inch-pound setting. Keep the finish-panel retainers available for reinstallation.

steps.title: Remove the access trim
steps.body: Follow the [Passenger Side Register procedure](#/document/G1676818). Remove the instrument-panel side trim first, then the center upper trim panel, disconnecting its electrical connector. Use the appropriate layout for a vehicle with or without center gauges.

steps.title: Remove the passenger finish panel
steps.body: Remove its retainers and lift away the passenger-side finish panel. This provides access to the register attachment rather than leaving the surrounding trim to resist removal.

steps.title: Release the register
steps.body: Release the retaining clips and remove the register assembly. The illustration identifies the clip attachments; it does not establish a separate levering direction or special tool method.

steps.title: Install the register and restore the trim
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Engage the register clips, refit the passenger finish panel and tighten its retainers to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm). Reconnect the center upper trim’s electrical connector and restore the center and side trim panels.

watchFor.title: A connected center trim panel
watchFor.body: Disconnect its electrical connector during removal and restore it during installation.

watchFor.title: Incorrect torque units
watchFor.body: The passenger finish-panel retainer specification is in inch-pounds, not foot-pounds.

notes: Electronic manual temperature control uses panel selections to control temperature, distribution and blower operation.
Dual automatic temperature control permits separate driver and passenger temperature settings; a temperature difference alone does not establish register damage.

verification.title: Confirm the reversed assembly sequence
verification.body: Check that the register clips are engaged, finish-panel retainers are tightened, the center trim connector is reconnected and the removed trim panels are restored.

procedures.purpose: Passenger-side register removal and installation, including surrounding trim access and finish-panel retainer torque.

guides.title: Replace the passenger-side temperature door actuator
guides.summary: Unload the temperature door where possible, disconnect and replace its passenger-side actuator, then restore its mounting and electrical connection.
guides.introduction: The temperature door actuator moves a door in the heating and air-conditioning unit to regulate delivered air temperature. This job replaces the passenger-side actuator and reconnects its electrical supply. On vehicles with Dual Automatic Temperature Control (DATC), the passenger can select a temperature independently of the driver. The repair concerns temperature-door movement; blower speed and air-distribution selections are separate functions.
guides.why: The procedure recommends placing the temperature door at its mid-position, if possible, before removing the actuator. This unloads tension on the door and makes actuator replacement easier. Treat that as a helpful preparation condition: an actuator that cannot move may prevent it, and the instruction does not make mid-position an absolute prerequisite.
searchTerms: passenger side temperature door actuator replacement

when.summary: When the passenger-side temperature door actuator has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: A temperature complaint alone does not establish an actuator failure.
Identify the fitted temperature-control arrangement; independent passenger temperature selection applies to DATC.

prepare.title: Identify the actuator and its attachments
prepare.detail: Use the component illustration to identify the passenger-side actuator, electrical connector and retainers. Have tools suited to the actual retainers and access to the unit.

prepare.title: Reduce door tension where possible
prepare.detail: Arrange the temperature door in its mid-position before disconnecting the actuator, if its condition allows.

steps.title: Prepare the door position
steps.body: If possible, place the temperature door at mid-position. This reduces the tension acting through the actuator connection during removal.

steps.title: Disconnect the electrical connector
steps.body: Disconnect the passenger-side temperature door actuator connector before removing its mounting retainers.

steps.title: Remove the actuator
steps.body: Remove the retainers and withdraw the passenger-side actuator. The illustration identifies the actuator and its mounting points; the replacement sequence does not call for dismantling the actuator.

steps.title: Install the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: position the replacement actuator, install its retainers and reconnect the electrical connector. Restore both its mechanical attachment and electrical connection.

watchFor.title: Tension during removal
watchFor.body: If mid-position could not be achieved, the tension-reducing preparation has not been completed; keep that condition in mind while removing the actuator.

notes: With Electronic Manual Temperature Control, the temperature setting determines outlet temperature; with DATC, it represents the desired cabin temperature.

verification.title: Confirm installation completion
verification.body: Check that the replacement passenger-side actuator is mounted with its retainers installed and its electrical connector reconnected.

procedures.purpose: Passenger-side temperature door actuator removal and installation, including the conditional mid-position preparation.

guides.title: Replace the A/C receiver drier using the correct engine access route
guides.summary: Replace the receiver drier through the engine-specific access route, then restore the refrigerant system's oil balance, vacuum and charge.
guides.introduction: The air-conditioning (A/C) receiver drier helps manage liquid refrigerant and moisture within the refrigerant circuit. Replacing it opens that circuit, so removing the small component is only part of the job. Refrigerant must first be identified and recovered, and the completed system must be evacuated and charged. Access differs significantly: the 2.3L requires condenser removal, while the other listed engines use underbody access.
guides.why: Contamination can enter through an open connection, and contaminated refrigerant can spoil recovery equipment's stored supply. Oil removed during recovery also needs to be accounted for. Correct access, sealing and refrigerant servicing are therefore as important as securing the replacement drier.

when.summary: When receiver-drier replacement has been established as part of a refrigerant-system repair.
notes: Select the procedure by engine before dismantling; the access and seal instructions are not identical.
These replacement procedures do not diagnose poor cooling.

prepare.title: Arrange refrigerant-service capability
prepare.detail: Use refrigerant identification equipment and the Ford-approved R134A management equipment specified in the recovery procedure, following equipment instructions.

prepare.title: Prepare lifting and service materials
prepare.detail: Provide hoist access using the lifting procedure, with the transmission in NEUTRAL. Obtain the applicable charge, oil and seal-lubrication specifications before opening the system.

prepare.title: Plan the required seals
prepare.detail: The 2.3L condenser procedure and the 5.2L drier procedure require new O-ring seals lubricated only with the specified material. Protect exposed openings against contamination.

steps.title: Identify and recover the refrigerant
steps.body: Check purity before recovery. Connect to both high- and low-side service ports; low-side-only recovery is prohibited. Record any oil recovered. After recovery, confirm the vacuum remains stable for about 2 minutes, repeating the recovery sequence if it does not.

steps.title: Follow the correct access branch
steps.body: For the 2.3L, follow the condenser procedure: remove the required shields and intake components, disconnect and cover refrigerant ports, reposition the degas bottle and cooling assembly, then release the condenser. For the 3.7L and 5.0L, remove the underbody shield bolts and retainers. For the 5.2L, complete both specified underbody-shield removal operations.

steps.title: Remove the receiver drier
steps.body: Remove the air deflector, then the drier attachment bolts, retainer and drier. On the 2.3L this follows condenser removal. Keep the engine-specific illustrations and instructions with the work so access details are not transferred between variants.

steps.title: Install and close the system
steps.body: Reverse the applicable removal sequence. The drier attachment bolts are tightened to 80 lb.in (9 Nm) in all four procedures. Fit the required new O-rings for the 2.3L condenser connections and 5.2L drier, using the specified lubricant. Remove temporary port protection when reconnecting.

steps.title: Restore the correct oil quantity
steps.body: Follow Refrigerant Oil Adding for the correct amount of clean polyalkylene glycol (PAG) oil. Account for the oil recovered, which must be replaced, alongside the applicable component-replacement requirements. Do not guess an oil quantity or transfer one between engines.

steps.title: Evacuate and charge
steps.body: Evacuate to at least 99.4 kPa (29.5 in-Hg) of vacuum, as close to 101.1 kPa (30 in-Hg) as possible, and continue pumping for at least 45 minutes. Stop the pump and observe vacuum retention for 10 minutes. Set the correct refrigerant charge amount and charge according to the service-unit instructions.

watchFor.title: Contaminated refrigerant
watchFor.body: Do not recover it into the normal bulk supply. Follow the contamination route, including dedicated contaminated-refrigerant recovery equipment and the specified disposal requirements.

watchFor.title: Misread access illustration
watchFor.body: The 2.3L condenser illustration notes that the bumper is removed for clarity; that note is not an instruction to remove it.

notes: The 3.7L and 5.0L underbody-shield fasteners have their own installation setting; do not use the drier-bolt setting for them.

diagnostics.finding: Vacuum is lost during the post-recovery observation.
diagnostics.meaning: The recovery procedure has not reached its required stable-vacuum condition.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the prescribed recovery sequence until vacuum remains stable for 2 minutes.

verification.title: Confirm evacuation completion
verification.body: Verify the specified evacuation and vacuum-hold stages before completing charging.

verification.title: Record the service result
verification.body: Record recovered oil, oil added, the vacuum-hold result and the refrigerant charge used for the vehicle.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost receiver-drier removal and installation after condenser removal.
3.7L Duratec receiver-drier removal through underbody access, installation and oil-restoration requirement.
5.0L receiver-drier removal through underbody access, installation and oil-restoration requirement.
5.2L receiver-drier replacement, including shield access, contamination protection, new O-rings and oil restoration.
Required 2.3L condenser removal and installation, including access components and new connection seals.
Refrigerant identification, recovery, evacuation, vacuum observation and charging.
Vehicle lifting requirements for hoist access.
Determine and add the appropriate refrigerant-system oil quantity.

guides.title: Replace the dashboard sunload sensor
guides.summary: Release the sensor’s two opposing retaining tabs inward with an interior trim remover, lift the housing and unplug it. Reconnect and seat the replacement. Applies to 2015 Mustangs with 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engines.
guides.introduction: The sunload sensor is the dashboard’s tiny sunbather, except it has to report for work. It senses sunlight reaching the vehicle, an indication of the solar heat contributing to cabin warmth. You’ll find it on top of the dashboard near the windshield. I’ll walk you through releasing its retained housing, handling the electrical connection and putting the replacement back without turning a small job into a dashboard wrestling match.
guides.why: Two opposing side retaining tabs hold the sensor in the dashboard opening, with an electrical connector underneath. Pressing those tabs inward releases the housing so you can lift it enough to disconnect the plug. Installation reverses that order: connect the wiring, then seat the housing. Climate-control operation depends on the fitted system: electronic manual temperature control follows the panel selections, while dual automatic temperature control maintains selected cabin temperatures and allows separate driver and passenger settings.

when.summary: Use this procedure when the sunload sensor has already been identified for removal or replacement.
notes: Applies to the 2015 Mustang with 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engines.
A cabin-temperature complaint alone does not identify the sunload sensor as the faulty part.

prepare.title: Have the trim tool and replacement ready
prepare.detail: Use an interior trim remover, the tool identified in the [sunload sensor procedure](#/document/G1676821). If replacing the sensor, have the correct replacement for the vehicle ready before releasing the original.

prepare.title: Establish the working boundary
prepare.detail: This is a cabin-side removal and installation job. Reach the sensor directly from the top of the dashboard; no surrounding dashboard panels need to be removed for this sequence. Electrical fault testing, sensor readings and calibration procedures are outside this replacement procedure.

prepare.title: Protect yourself while handling trim
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection when servicing the vehicle, and protective gloves when handling sharp edges. Review the relevant [general service precautions](#/document/G1693189). The car stays on the ground throughout this job.

steps.title: Park and prevent an unintended start
steps.body: Set the parking brake. If remote start is fitted, disable it through the central display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle before working.

steps.title: Locate the sensor and reach its housing edge
steps.body: From inside the cabin, locate the small sensor on the upper dashboard close to the windshield, in the center area above the center vents. The [sunload sensor procedure](#/document/G1676821) identifies this location. Clear your access so you can control the interior trim remover and support the sensor as it comes free.

steps.title: Press the opposing retaining tabs inward and release the housing
steps.body:
Work the interior trim remover at the edge where the sensor housing meets the dashboard. Use it to press the two opposing side retaining tabs inward, toward the center of the sensor housing. Release both tabs before easing the housing out of its opening.

Watch whether the housing is coming free. If one side remains held, stop lifting and reposition the trim remover to press that side’s retaining tab inward. Pulling harder is a poor substitute for releasing the damn tab.

steps.title: Lift the sensor and disconnect its plug
steps.body:
Lift the released sensor only far enough to reach the electrical connector underneath. Support the housing so its weight and your removal force are not carried by the wires.

Release the connector’s retention and separate the plug from the sensor by holding the connector body. Keep the disconnected plug accessible at the dashboard opening, then remove the sensor completely.

steps.title: Reconnect the replacement before seating it
steps.body:
Compare the replacement’s housing, opposing retaining tabs and connector interface with the removed sensor before installation. If they do not match, resolve the part selection before proceeding.

Support the replacement above the opening and reconnect the electrical plug in its matching orientation. Make sure the connector is fully engaged before lowering the sensor. This little plug deserves its moment of attention before it disappears beneath the dashboard again.

steps.title: Seat the housing and check the finished installation
steps.body:
Position the connected sensor in its dashboard opening, keeping the wiring clear of the seating edge. Press the housing into its installed position so both side retaining tabs engage, completing the reverse of removal.

Check that the sensor sits evenly in the opening and remains retained without being held by hand. Remove the trim tool and any loose items from the dashboard.

watchFor.title: A housing that is still retained
watchFor.body: Resistance during lifting can mean one or both side retaining tabs remain engaged. Stop pulling, support the housing and use the interior trim remover to press the retained tab inward toward the center of the housing. Ease the sensor out only after both opposing tabs are released.

watchFor.title: Wiring carrying the removal force
watchFor.body: Once the housing is free, keep it supported while reaching the plug. Separate the connector by its body rather than pulling on its wires.

watchFor.title: A plug trapped beneath a seated sensor
watchFor.body: Reconnect the electrical connector before installing the housing. As the sensor enters the opening, keep the wiring away from the edge so it is not caught under the housing.

notes: For operating context, [EMTC](#/document/G1681091) uses panel selections to determine heating or cooling, air distribution and blower operation. [DATC](#/document/G1676851) maintains selected cabin temperatures, allows individual driver and passenger settings and permits manual overrides.

diagnostics.finding: The sensor housing will not lift free.
diagnostics.meaning: One or both opposing side retaining tabs may still be engaged.
diagnostics.next: Stop pulling. Use the interior trim remover to press the retained tab inward toward the center of the housing. Release both tabs and ease the housing out before attempting to disconnect the plug.

diagnostics.finding: The replacement does not match the removed housing or connector interface.
diagnostics.meaning: The replacement has not been established as suitable for this installation.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the part match before connecting or pressing the sensor into the dashboard.

diagnostics.finding: The installed sensor sits unevenly or will not remain in place.
diagnostics.meaning: The housing has not completed its mechanical installation.
diagnostics.next: Release the opposing side tabs inward again with the trim remover. Lift the housing, check that wiring is clear of the seating edge and examine both retaining tabs before reseating it. Do not force a housing with damaged retention into place.

verification.title: Confirm the electrical connection
verification.body: Before seating the housing, confirm that the plug is fully connected and its retention is engaged.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical retention
verification.body: After installation, check that the sensor sits evenly in its opening, stays in place and has no wiring caught beneath its edge. These are installation checks, not proof of the sensor’s electrical performance.

verification.title: Finish the work area
verification.body: Remove tools and loose parts from the dashboard. If you disabled remote start for this work, restore the desired setting only after the installation and tool checks are complete.

procedures.purpose: Primary sensor removal and reverse-order installation, including the interior trim remover, dashboard location and inward release of the opposing side retaining tabs.

applicability.equipment: Dashboard sunload sensor; electronic manual temperature control (EMTC) or dual automatic temperature control (DATC), as fitted.

stepGroups.summary: Prevent unintended starting and reach the sensor from inside the cabin.

stepGroups.summary: Press the opposing retaining tabs inward, lift the housing and disconnect its electrical plug.

guides.title: Replace the A/C expansion valve on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L models
guides.summary: Recover the refrigerant, replace the thermostatic expansion valve using the correct engine access sequence, and complete oil replenishment and refrigerant servicing.
guides.introduction: The thermostatic expansion valve (TXV) meters refrigerant entering the air-conditioning evaporator, where the system absorbs heat from cabin air. Air conditioning (A/C) also reduces cabin humidity. Replacement opens the refrigerant circuit, regardless of whether the vehicle has manual or dual automatic temperature control.
guides.why: Open refrigerant connections need immediate protection from dirt. Seal lubricant and refrigerant-oil replenishment have specific requirements. Access also changes with the engine: the V8 procedures include battery and brace work that is absent from the listed 2.3L and 3.7L sequences.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established a need to replace the thermostatic expansion valve.
notes: A cooling complaint alone does not establish that the valve requires replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange refrigerant-service capability
prepare.detail: Have equipment and capability for the applicable recovery, evacuation and charging procedure before opening any connection. Obtain the required refrigerant-oil amount through the oil-adding procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare clean connections and replacement parts
prepare.detail: Have suitable caps or other port protection, the specified seal lubricant and required seals. The 5.2L branch also requires replacement strut-tower cross-brace nuts.

steps.title: Recover the refrigerant
steps.body: Begin with the applicable [recovery procedure](#/document/G1912323). Complete recovery before loosening the valve connections; removing the valve is only one part of servicing the opened refrigerant circuit.

steps.title: Follow the engine-specific access branch
steps.body: On 5.0L vehicles, disconnect the battery ground and positive cables; if a cross brace is fitted, detach its battery-cable retainer and remove the brace nuts and brace. On 5.2L vehicles, disconnect the battery, detach the harness retainer, discard the brace nuts and remove the strut-tower cross brace. Use the [battery procedure](#/document/G1692356).

steps.title: Disconnect and protect the lines
steps.body: The 2.3L and 3.7L sequences proceed from recovery to the valve connections. Remove the retaining nut and TXV bracket, then disconnect the condenser outlet and evaporator outlet lines. Protect every exposed port and fitting against contamination.

steps.title: Replace the valve and reconnect
steps.body: Remove the valve bolts and TXV, then follow the applicable installation sequence in reverse. The 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L procedures explicitly require new O-rings lubricated only with the specified material. Tighten valve bolts to 62 lb.in (7 Nm) and the line-bracket nut to 133 lb.in (15 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the engine-specific access components
steps.body: Refit the brace and retainers where removed, using new cross-brace nuts on the 5.2L. Complete battery reconnection through its dedicated procedure. Follow the 5.0L procedure’s own brace installation details when that optional brace is fitted.

steps.title: Complete oil and refrigerant servicing
steps.body: All engine branches require the correct amount of clean polyalkylene glycol (PAG) oil through [Refrigerant Oil Adding](#/document/G1912330). Complete evacuation and charging through the applicable refrigerant-service procedure. Obtain quantities from those procedures rather than assuming they are shared between variants.

watchFor.title: Port protection left in place
watchFor.body: Remove caps, tape and other protective materials before reconnecting the valve and lines.

watchFor.title: Confusing oil replenishment with seal lubrication
watchFor.body: The instruction to add PAG oil does not replace the requirement to use the specified seal-lubricating material.

notes: The illustrations show the 2.3L valve connections; follow the appropriate engine procedure for surrounding access.
The 3.7L installation instruction specifies reverse-order reassembly and correct PAG-oil replenishment; retain that branch’s own requirements.

verification.title: Confirm connection and access restoration
verification.body: Confirm that protective materials are removed, joints are reassembled, required new seals are installed and all removed battery, brace and retainer components are restored.

verification.title: Record the refrigerant-service completion
verification.body: Record the applicable oil amount used and the completion results required by the recovery, evacuation and charging procedure.

guides.title: Diagnose interior switch backlighting that stays dark, stays on or will not dim
guides.summary: Use the affected lighting group, stored faults and circuit checks to separate switch, wiring, network and module problems.
guides.introduction: The headlamp switch contains the dimmer controls. The body control module (BCM) combines their request with ambient-light information, then supplies pulsed voltage to directly wired lamps and sends brightness messages to networked modules. Door modules control their own switch illumination, while steering-wheel lighting passes through the clockspring. Identifying which lights misbehave is therefore the first useful test.
guides.why: A dark switch can have a missing supply, a poor ground or an internal fault. Several affected lamps may share a circuit or message. Following the correct branch prevents a wiring problem from being mistaken for a failed module.
searchTerms: steering wheel switch lights not working
passenger door switch illumination not working

when.summary: Use when instrument-panel or switch backlighting fails, remains illuminated or does not respond to dimmer commands.
notes: The complaint must be present during testing before a replacement decision is followed.
Use memory-switch, convertible-top and paddle-switch branches only where fitted.

prepare.title: Establish reliable electrical test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Inspect previous repairs, wiring, fuses and connectors. Use a diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, Rotunda Flex Probes and the specified wiring information: Cells 71 and 100, plus Cell 149 for the dimmer component test.

prepare.title: Prepare for controlled testing
prepare.detail: Follow each step's ignition and connector states. Isolate circuits before resistance measurements and follow Diagnostic Methods for battery disconnection. Have a shop light for Test C. Do not apply improvised power or ground to module outputs.

prepare.title: Arrange safe steering-wheel access
prepare.detail: Before G4 or G5, follow the complete Driver Airbag procedure and its Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) depowering requirements. Only then follow the prescribed illumination-test ignition states. These checks do not authorize live SRS probing.

steps.title: Classify the complaint and record faults
steps.body: Operate the parking lamps and dimmer, comparing directly wired lamps, networked displays, door switches and steering-wheel switches. Retrieve diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) from the relevant modules. Diagnose circuit faults first; several codes may share a power or ground problem.

steps.title: Use Test A when all illumination refuses to dim
steps.body: With B1436:01 present, check the dim-up and dim-down circuits for unwanted voltage, opens, shorts to ground and a short between them, in that order. Without that code, enter the dimmer component test directly. A failed component test directs headlamp-switch replacement; a passing result leads to the BCM connection check.

steps.title: Use Test B when all directly wired lamps are dark
steps.body: B1315:15 enters B2: disconnect the headlamp switch as directed and check C205 pin 15 for unwanted voltage. Repair a positive finding; if no voltage is present, stop this branch without executing B3 or authorizing BCM replacement. B1315:11 independently enters B4, with the headlamp switch and BCM disconnected, to check for a short to ground before B5. Without either code, return to the symptom chart.

steps.title: Use Test C for individual dark components
steps.body: Check the affected component's feed, then its specified ground pair. Use parking lamps, full dimmer brightness and a shop light over the ambient sensor. For a dark headlamp switch, set maximum brightness before disconnecting it. Both checks must exceed 11 volts before the test directs component replacement; a failed check directs circuit repair. Select the connector pair for the actual fitted control.

steps.title: Use Test D when all directly wired lamps stay on
steps.body: If networked illumination works normally, retrieve codes. B1315:15 returns to Test B and its stopping point. Otherwise, disconnect BCM C2280B as directed: lamps remaining illuminated indicate unwanted circuit voltage. Lamps going out lead to D3. At A7, B5 or D3, repair connector corrosion, damaged or displaced terminals, reseat and latch connectors, then retest. Persistent faults require the specified service-article check before the BCM replacement decision.

steps.title: Use Test E for driver-door lock or memory-switch lighting
steps.body: First confirm the switch locks and unlocks the doors; otherwise follow lock-system diagnosis. For dark illumination, E2–E4 separate adequate supply, an open and a ground short, directing switch, circuit or driver door module (DDM) repair. For illumination always on, E5 disconnects the DDM: continued lighting identifies a circuit fault; extinguished lighting directs DDM replacement. E6 separately provides connector repair, retesting and Technical Service Bulletin checks.

steps.title: Use Test F for passenger-door switch lighting
steps.body: Confirm both lock operation and window travel before illumination diagnosis; functional failures require their respective system diagnosis. The passenger switches share illumination power and ground. For dark lighting, test the affected switch's feed, continuity and ground-short condition. For lighting always on, disconnect the passenger door module (PDM): continued lighting identifies a circuit fault. Passing circuit checks lead to F6 connector inspection, retesting and bulletin review before module replacement.

steps.title: Use Test G for steering-wheel lighting
steps.body: G1 first redirects a whole-system failure to B or D. If all steering-wheel lamps alone are dark, G2/G3 separate supply and ground faults at the clockspring input. After the required airbag access, G4 distinguishes clockspring failure from the steering-wheel assembly. If only some wheel lamps are dark, G5 checks each suspect switch's supply and ground: a passing result directs switch replacement; a failure directs circuit repair, or wheel replacement if the circuit cannot be repaired. Stop if only steering-wheel lamps remain continuously lit; this condition has no defined continuation here.

steps.title: Follow the network-specific decisions
steps.body: For all networked illumination inoperative, perform a network test: all modules passing directs BCM replacement; failed communication requires network diagnosis. For the instrument panel cluster (IPC), or front controls interface module (FCIM) and its integral hazard switch, successful communication directs replacement of the affected module; no communication requires network diagnosis. For a front display interface module (FDIM) that will not dim, test communication with the accessory protocol interface module (APIM). No communication follows the network referral; successful communication is a stopping point without a replacement decision.

watchFor.title: Normal behavior that resembles a fault
watchFor.body: With autolamps in daylight, the message center can remain at full brightness. Non-dimmable window-switch lighting follows accessory-relay operation. Check the relevant operating conditions before condemning a control.

watchFor.title: A single lamp remaining on
watchFor.body: The symptom chart directs replacement for a single non-network illuminated component that remains on. Use the dedicated door-switch branches where applicable, and do not extend that general instruction to the unresolved steering-wheel-only condition.

notes: A networked module receiving missing or invalid dimming information can default to nighttime brightness; this does not establish a failed dimmer.
The hazard and start/stop switches are integral to the FCIM and are not serviced separately.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1436:01 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detects an electrical fault in a dim-up or dim-down circuit.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test A before choosing a switch or module.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1315:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive backlighting-circuit current indicates a possible short to ground.
diagnostics.next: Enter the separately isolated B4 branch.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1315:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Backlighting current is lower than expected; the description covers short-to-battery or open conditions.
diagnostics.next: Match the complaint to B or D, preserving the stop after a negative B2 voltage check.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U2010:00 is recorded for a door module.
diagnostics.meaning: The corresponding switch-illumination circuit has an open or ground-short concern.
diagnostics.next: Use E for the driver door or F for the passenger door.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U1000:00 or U3000:49 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: U1000:00 identifies disabled solid-state driver protection; U3000:49 identifies internal module electronic failure.
diagnostics.next: Follow BCM diagnosis rather than treating either code alone as replacement authorization.

verification.title: Repeat the original operating check
verification.body: After the directed repair, operate the affected lighting and dimmer again. Where reconnection restores operation, correct the underlying terminal or connector defect.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record the active complaint, codes, circuit readings and final response. Clearly identify any branch stopped without a completed fault decision.
