guides.title: Diagnose Mustang gauges, warning messages and chimes
guides.summary: Separate cluster faults from incorrect inputs, communication problems and normal warning behavior before choosing a pinpoint test.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) presents information from switches and other modules through gauges, messages and audible warnings. A warning can therefore originate elsewhere in the vehicle. This diagnostic starting point identifies which signal, display or communication path needs further testing.
guides.why: Replacing the cluster cannot correct an upstream sensor fault or missing network message. The reporting module, fitted equipment and current symptom determine the correct diagnostic route.

when.summary: Use when gauges, messages or chimes behave incorrectly, or a scan identifies a related diagnostic trouble code.
notes: Apply equipment-specific rows only where the corresponding feature is fitted.

prepare.title: Diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable scan tool and the Diagnostic Methods procedure. Verify battery state of charge exceeds 70% and check charging-system operation.

prepare.title: Electrical inspection
prepare.detail: Review previous repairs and inspect wiring, fuses and connections. Use the specified flex probes for terminal testing; do not jumper module outputs unless directed.

steps.title: Establish the complaint and scan all modules
steps.body: Confirm the concern is present and record diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) by reporting module. Diagnose circuit codes before performance codes. A module that cannot communicate requires Communications Network diagnosis, rather than an immediate replacement decision.

steps.title: Check the common supply for widespread failures
steps.body: For a dead cluster or multiple failed indications, begin Test A by inspecting body control module (BCM) fuse 13 (7.5A). The IPC receives constant battery power from the BCM, but ignition status arrives over high-speed Controller Area Network 3 (HS-CAN3). Either path matters.

steps.title: Choose the precise gauge or display complaint
steps.body: Distinguish an inoperative reading from an incorrect one. For digital speed, first establish that the message center works. For missing distance-to-empty or average fuel economy, check speedometer, fuel gauge and odometer operation before the vehicle identification number (VIN)-guided IPC route.

steps.title: Separate message display from the requesting system
steps.body: Where directed, open and close the driver door to check message response. Certain brake, door, key/start, anti-theft and tire-pressure complaints instead require the gateway module (GWM) C2431 connector disconnected with ignition OFF, followed by ignition ON. Missing multiple popups leads to Test A; successful popups lead to the affected system. This deliberately introduces an unrelated fault.

steps.title: Identify the chime path
steps.body: All chimes absent leads to Test A; chimes heard only from the IPC leads to Test BD. The IPC backs up audio-system chimes. Parking-aid and blind-spot/cross-traffic alerts use rear speakers; other audio chimes use front speakers. Higher-priority warnings can delay lower-priority ones.

steps.title: Follow the engine and equipment branch
steps.body: Low-oil-pressure indications and codes P0521, P0522, P0523 or P0524 use Test AO for 2.3L, 3.7L and non-performance-package 5.0L, or AP for performance-package 5.0L and 5.2L. Powertrain fuel-level codes first follow powertrain diagnostics, reaching Test C when directed.

watchFor.title: Airbag secondary chime
watchFor.body: Silence is normal without an indicator fault. If IPC self-test records P1534:01, use the VIN-guided IPC routine and diagnose restraints-control-module codes.

watchFor.title: Warnings may report real faults
watchFor.body: A working message display does not establish that oil pressure, brakes or another monitored system is healthy.

notes: Oil-change messages depend on oil life: 1–5% for ENGINE OIL CHANGE SOON and 0% for OIL CHANGE REQUIRED. Follow Owner's Literature for resetting.
Tire-training messages depend on the training procedure. MyKey prevents Belt-Minder deactivation; an administrator key is required.

diagnostics.finding: IPC code U0401:00 or U0401:81 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Powertrain data for speed or temperature is invalid; this differs from lost communication.
diagnostics.next: Repair relevant non-network codes first. If the powertrain module has none, diagnose the observable symptom.

diagnostics.meaning: The applicable chart identifies incomplete or incompatible configuration.
diagnostics.next: Check service history. Repeat Programmable Module Installation after related service; without recent service, follow the affected module's replacement branch.

diagnostics.finding: U3000:41, U3000:42, U3000:44 or U3000:46 returns after clearing and self-test.
diagnostics.meaning: A checksum or memory fault persists.
diagnostics.next: IPC findings require a VIN-guided routine; information center module (ICM) findings direct ICM replacement. Keep voltage and missing-calibration codes on their separate chart branches.

verification.title: Check a new warning response
verification.body: With doors closed and ignition OFF, switch ON, allow cluster prove-out, then open the driver door. Confirm the door-ajar display and one chime; use the chart if either is absent.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record returning codes, reporting modules, observed responses and the selected follow-on test. Complete that test before selecting parts.

procedures.purpose: Module-specific DTC charts, symptom routing and initial Test A inspection.
Electrical diagnostic prerequisites and correct circuit-testing methods.
Diagnosis when a module does not communicate.
Restraint-system diagnosis for related warning-indicator faults.

guides.title: Diagnose cluster, virtual gauge, fuel gauge and speedometer faults
guides.summary: Separate display faults from missing network information, fuel-sender problems and wiring faults using the complaint-specific cluster tests.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) turns electrical inputs and messages from other modules into gauges, warnings and driver information. It also controls warning-chime requests, with most sounds delivered through the audio system. These tests distinguish a cluster-wide problem from an individual virtual gauge, incorrect fuel indication or an inoperative speedometer.
guides.why: A gauge can display a programmed fallback when information disappears. Likewise, an empty fuel indication can result from an electrical fault. Testing communication, inputs and commanded gauge movement prevents these responses from being mistaken for proof that the cluster needs replacement.

when.summary: Use when cluster functions fail together, a virtual gauge disappears, fuel indication is incorrect or the speedometer fails.
notes: Confirm the complaint is present before following a replacement decision.
Choose the matching pinpoint test; these are separate diagnostic paths.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of network tests, module self-tests and active gauge commands, plus a digital multimeter, fused jumper wires and Rotunda Flex Probes. Check charging-system operation and battery state of charge above 70%.

prepare.title: Prepare access and supporting procedures
prepare.detail: Have the connector diagrams and vehicle identification number available. Inspect wiring, previous repairs, the fuel tank and gauge needle for damage. Fuel-unit removal requires the applicable Group 310 procedure and its precautions.

steps.title: Test A: investigate widespread cluster failures
steps.body: With ignition on, run the network test. Any equipped module failing leads to network diagnosis. If all pass, check gateway module (GWM) continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), then perform the IPC self-test. Gateway codes lead to network diagnosis; IPC codes lead to its DTC chart. With neither, continue through the vehicle-specific IPC guided routine.

steps.title: Test B: establish whether the virtual gauge is selected
steps.body: Perform the body control module (BCM) self-test and verify cluster functions; broader failures return to Test A. Check the message-center selection. If selecting the gauge restores it, operation is normal. If it was unselected and remains absent after selection, use the IPC guided routine. An already-selected gauge proceeds through the remaining Test B checks.

steps.title: Follow the oil-pressure branch and module checks
steps.body: For a missing oil-pressure display, compare the low-pressure reconfigurable telltale with the engine running, first connected and then disconnected at the specified pressure-switch connector; switch ignition off before disconnecting. It should be off connected and on disconnected. Failure leads to Test AO for 2.3L, 3.7L and non-Performance Package 5.0L, or AP for Performance Package 5.0L and 5.2L. Otherwise, continue with IPC and powertrain control module (PCM) self-tests, then GWM codes, following each fault referral before the IPC guided routine.

steps.title: Test C: separate fuel-input circuit faults
steps.body: Start with the IPC self-test. Short-to-ground codes enter C2; open/high-input codes enter C6. Follow the prescribed disconnection or fused-jumper test and one-minute wait before retesting. The resulting code change directs testing toward the fuel unit or wiring. C3–C12 distinguish shorts to ground, crossed signal/return circuits, shorts to voltage and open circuits.

steps.title: Check fuel-gauge movement and tank transfer
steps.body: Without IPC codes, use C13 to command FUELLEVEL through empty, quarter, half, three-quarter and full indications. A failed sweep leads to cluster checks. A successful sweep, or P1243:06, leads to tank inspection. Replace a damaged tank as directed. Inspect transfer-tube connections and fuel units using their removal procedures; repair identified damage. For P1243:06 with these items sound, C15 directs fuel-pump-module replacement.

steps.title: Distinguish sender wear from connections and resistance
steps.body: C16 checks fuel-unit connectors before float testing. If the concern remains, check for a smooth resistance change through float travel. Repeat a failed sweep with the sender input disconnected: passing now identifies the assembly for replacement; continued failure identifies the float-and-card sender. A successful initial sweep leads to high-resistance checks of both signal/return circuits. C21 then checks IPC connections; persistent faults require a bulletin check before the guided routine.

steps.title: Test D: isolate an inoperative speedometer
steps.body: Run IPC and anti-lock brake system (ABS) module self-tests, then check GWM codes, following the corresponding diagnostic referral whenever codes appear. If these checks pass, use the SPDOMETER active command. The specified sweep and return directs diagnosis toward PCM codes; failure directs the IPC guided routine. This tests gauge response without relying on incoming vehicle-speed information.

watchFor.title: Incorrect speed rather than no speed
watchFor.body: Check tire size against the certification label and consider tire-size or axle-ratio configuration. An aftermarket gauge face can miscalibrate or bind the speedometer or tachometer needle.

watchFor.title: Test-induced fuel codes
watchFor.body: Disconnection and jumper tests deliberately change the input. Follow the instructions identifying which existing codes to disregard at that stage.

watchFor.title: Connector damage
watchFor.body: Replace damaged terminals, correct corrosion and ensure connectors latch. Repair the cause of poor connections rather than relying on reseating alone.

notes: The axle-temperature virtual gauge branch is SVT-only. The battery-voltage gauge uses the cluster's always-powered voltage input with filtering.
Warnings can temporarily replace the selected message-center display; acknowledge them with OK to regain full message-center functionality.

diagnostics.finding: The accelerometer dot disappears.
diagnostics.meaning: After 5 seconds, missing acceleration messages set U0121:00, invalid messages set U0415:00 and unknown messages set U0415:81.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test B and the IPC DTC chart to investigate the information supply.

diagnostics.finding: A virtual gauge holds its reading, then blanks its digital value.
diagnostics.meaning: Brief message loss holds the previous indication. Sustained loss sets U0100:00 for the engine-related gauges: air-fuel ratio and axle temperature move low, cylinder-head temperature hot, oil pressure zero, oil/inlet-air/transmission temperatures cold, and vacuum-boost to rest.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test B. Invalid oil, inlet-air or transmission-temperature data instead sets U0401:00 after 5 seconds.

diagnostics.meaning: The :11 codes indicate low inputs consistent with shorts to ground; :13 indicates open circuits or shorts to voltage. These faults default the fuel gauge to empty.
diagnostics.next: Use C2 for :11 and C6 for :13.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1243:06 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The pump side reaches low fuel before the opposite side indicates empty, suggesting a transfer-tube or jet-pump concern.
diagnostics.next: Enter C14; inspect the tank and transfer components before the replacement decision.

diagnostics.finding: PCM fuel-level performance, circuit or stuck-signal codes are recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These distinguish out-of-range changes, low/high circuit inputs and readings inconsistent with fuel use.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test C using the IPC codes to select the branch.

verification.title: Reset fuel-gauge timers and confirm operation
verification.body: After any fuel-gauge repair, remove BCM fuse 13 (7.5A) for one minute, then reinstall it. Operate the system and confirm whether the original concern remains.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record module-test results and commanded versus observed gauge movement. A successful active command establishes display response; unresolved input faults still require their directed diagnosis.

procedures.purpose: Exact Tests A–D for cluster, virtual-gauge, fuel-gauge and speedometer diagnosis across the listed engines.
Electrical preparation, terminal protection, meter use and fused-jumper methods.
Network diagnosis when module communication or GWM checks fail.

guides.title: Diagnose incorrect speedometer, odometer and tachometer indications
guides.summary: Use configuration checks, module self-tests and commanded gauge movements to distinguish incorrect readings from missing data or cluster faults.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) displays road speed, accumulated distance and engine speed using information from vehicle control modules. A wrong reading can originate in vehicle configuration, missing messages or the gauge itself. Tests E through H separate these causes, with different command scales for standard and SVT clusters.
guides.why: Commanding a gauge tests its response independently of normal incoming information. Correct movement redirects attention toward configuration or data sources; failed movement requires the vehicle-specific cluster routine.

when.summary: When speed indication is incorrect, the odometer is inoperative, or the tachometer is inactive or inaccurate.
notes: The complaint must be present before acting on a component-replacement decision.

prepare.title: Provide the required diagnostic functions
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting module programming views, self-tests, parameter identifications (PIDs) and gauge active commands. Have the vehicle identification number for guided routines and capability for road comparisons and controlled engine-speed testing.

prepare.title: Check the starting condition
prepare.detail: Verify battery and charging operation, battery state of charge above 70%, previous repairs and relevant circuit faults before performance diagnosis.

steps.title: E: verify speedometer configuration
steps.body: With ignition on, compare installed tire size, the certification label and programmed tire size. Correct the tires or configuration as required. Next compare actual vehicle configuration with the programmed axle ratio; correct the axle or programming if mismatched. These checks establish whether the speed calculation uses the right vehicle information.

steps.title: E: test the speedometer response
steps.body: Run the IPC self-test and follow its diagnostic trouble code (DTC) chart for recorded faults. If clear, self-test the anti-lock brake system (ABS) and diagnose any codes there. With both clear, command the IPC SPDOMETER PID in 10% increments. Compare each indication with E5’s standard or SVT table; failure directs the IPC guided routine.

steps.title: E: compare indicated and reported road speed
steps.body: Compare the speedometer with the powertrain control module (PCM) vehicle-speed PID, VSS, at 32 km/h (20 mph), 64 km/h (40 mph) and 97 km/h (60 mph), using E6’s permitted ranges. If correct, observe operation at varied speeds and frequent stops: the needle must start at and fully return to zero. Either failure directs the IPC guided routine.

steps.title: F: follow the odometer display and fault records
steps.body: With ignition on, an ERROR display directs the IPC guided routine. Otherwise self-test the IPC and follow its DTC chart if faults appear. With none, check Gateway Module A (GWM) continuous-memory codes: recorded faults direct communications diagnosis. If none are recorded, diagnose all PCM DTCs through the applicable powertrain diagnostic procedure.

steps.title: G: test an inoperative tachometer
steps.body: Check IPC self-test codes first, then GWM continuous-memory codes, following their respective diagnostic routes. If clear, select TACH_IND and set the scan tool to 0 rpm before commanding the gauge on and off. It should rise to approximately 800 rpm except SVT, or 900 rpm for SVT, then return to zero. A pass directs PCM DTC diagnosis; a failure directs the IPC guided routine.

steps.title: H: investigate an inaccurate or erratic tachometer
steps.body: Verify the original Ford gauge-face applique is fitted; an aftermarket face can alter calibration or bind the needle. Self-test the PCM first, then the IPC, diagnosing recorded faults before continuing. With codes clear, initialize TACH_IND to 0 rpm and command 10% increments: each should add approximately 800 rpm for the base cluster or 900 rpm for SVT.

steps.title: H: compare the tachometer with engine-speed control
steps.body: If the active command passes, follow H4’s PCM rpm PID procedure at 1,000, 1,500, 2,000 and 2,500 rpm. Compare the needle with the exact tolerance bands in the linked test. Passing establishes correct operation at this time; either command-test or comparison failure directs the IPC guided routine.

watchFor.title: A cold indication caused by missing information
watchFor.body: The temperature gauge defaults to C after 5 seconds or longer without required coolant-temperature or overheat-request information, or with invalid temperature data. That indication alone does not establish a cold engine; continue with temperature-gauge diagnosis.

notes: Choose command ranges by the fitted cluster. Standard and SVT scales are not interchangeable.

diagnostics.finding: The odometer displays ERROR.
diagnostics.meaning: This identifies corrupted or failed non-volatile memory.
diagnostics.next: Follow F1’s vehicle-specific IPC guided routine.

diagnostics.finding: The odometer displays dashes.
diagnostics.meaning: The odometer-count message from the GWM has been missing or invalid for at least 5 seconds.
diagnostics.next: Follow F’s IPC, gateway and PCM diagnostic sequence.

diagnostics.finding: The tachometer briefly freezes or becomes sluggish.
diagnostics.meaning: Briefly missing or invalid engine-speed messages can leave the needle at its last valid reading.
diagnostics.next: Use H to distinguish data faults from an incorrect gauge response.

verification.title: Confirm the applicable endpoint
verification.body: Speedometer verification requires E’s command, road-comparison and return-to-zero checks. Accurate tachometer operation requires H’s command and engine-speed comparisons. F and G can redirect diagnosis without establishing a completed repair.

verification.title: Keep an interpretable result
verification.body: Record configuration findings, module DTCs, commanded values, observed indications and the diagnostic route selected.

procedures.purpose: Tests E–H, including standard/SVT command tables, road-speed tolerances and tachometer comparison limits.
Vehicle identification information for tire-size and axle-configuration checks.
Communications diagnosis when gateway fault records direct it.
Diagnostic prerequisites and interpretation of module input/output testing.

applicability.equipment: Standard or SVT instrument panel cluster

guides.title: Diagnose an inactive vacuum-boost gauge or incorrect ABS, airbag and brake warning lamps
guides.summary: Use module self-tests and commanded display checks to separate gauge or warning-lamp faults from network and system-input problems.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) displays warnings requested by other modules; the information center module (ICM) operates the separate gauge pack. A lamp can work electrically yet display incorrectly because its requesting module or communication path has a fault.
guides.why: Active commands test the display independently of normal requests. Missing messages can switch the anti-lock brake system (ABS) or airbag warning on, so an illuminated lamp does not establish a failed cluster.
searchTerms: airbag warning light never comes on

when.summary: When the vacuum-boost gauge is inactive, ABS/airbag indication is incorrect, or the brake warning never illuminates.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic access
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable scan tool with module self-tests and active commands, a multimeter, required flex probes, fused jumper and Wiring Diagrams Cell 60. Have the vehicle identification number available for guided routines.

prepare.title: Confirm the complaint
prepare.detail: Verify battery charge exceeds 70%. Inspect brake-switch damage, wiring and connectors. For a brake lamp staying on, verify fluid level, parking-brake release and correct base-brake/parking-brake operation.

prepare.title: Workshop capability
prepare.detail: ICM vacuum-boost gauge pack for Test M, except SVT; warning-lamp branches selected by complaint

steps.title: Test M: inactive vacuum-boost gauge
steps.body: For the ICM gauge pack, except SVT, run the ignition-on ICM self-test and follow its code chart if faults appear. Otherwise command TURBO_GAUGE_ICM. A rest-to-full-stop-and-back sweep directs diagnosis of powertrain control module codes; a failed sweep directs ICM replacement.

steps.title: Test N: ABS lamp never or always on
steps.body: Run IPC and then ABS self-tests, following any recorded-code referrals before continuing. Command ABS_LAMP on/off. A failed response requires the VIN-specific IPC guided routine. If it responds, check gateway module (GWM) continuous-memory codes. With none present, an always-on complaint directs ABS-module replacement; a never-on complaint reaches the operating-correctly endpoint.

steps.title: Test O: airbag lamp never or always on
steps.body: Run IPC, then restraints control module (RCM) self-tests, then check GWM continuous-memory codes. Resolve faults through their respective diagnostic paths. Command AIRBAG_LMP on/off. A failed response requires IPC guided diagnosis; a correct response with the lamp still always on directs RCM replacement. The never-on branch then reaches the operating-correctly endpoint.

steps.title: Test P: brake lamp never on
steps.body: Command PBA_LMP on/off. Failure requires IPC guided diagnosis. If successful, check GWM codes, then apply the parking brake. Illumination leads to the fluid-switch branch at P7; no illumination leads to the parking-brake-switch checks.

steps.title: Separate parking-brake switch and wiring faults
steps.body: Follow P4’s ignition-off disconnection and fused-jumper connection across C306 pins 1 and 2, then switch ignition on. Illumination directs switch replacement. Remove the jumper after either result. If unlit, test ground and signal continuity to the body control module (BCM); repair opens or continue to P8.

steps.title: Evaluate the fluid-level input
steps.body: At P7, establish whether fluid is currently or was reportedly low. Disconnect C124 with ignition off, switch on and wait one minute. Illumination with a current/reported low level directs reservoir or master-cylinder replacement as required; without that history, operation is correct. No illumination leads to P8.

steps.title: Complete the BCM connection check
steps.body: Inspect BCM connectors for corrosion, bent or pushed-out pins; repair, latch securely and retest. If the concern persists, check applicable technical service bulletins in OASIS. Without an applicable bulletin, continue through the VIN-specific BCM guided routine. If reseating restores operation, address the underlying connector fault.

watchFor.title: Communication can hold a warning on
watchFor.body: Missing ABS or airbag requests for 5 seconds or longer cause the IPC to default that warning on.

watchFor.title: Keep restraint work within its procedure
watchFor.body: These airbag-lamp checks use scan-tool commands. RCM replacement is separate restraint-system work with its own safety prerequisites.

notes: A brake lamp that stays on needs its separate diagnostic path after the fluid, parking-brake and wiring pre-checks; Test P addresses a lamp that never illuminates.
Do not apply component-replacement endpoints when the complaint is absent.

diagnostics.finding: BCM code B1048:01 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detects an open brake-fluid-level switch input.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the switch connection, terminals and wiring for an open.

diagnostics.finding: BCM code B1048:7B is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detects a low-fluid-level input.
diagnostics.next: Verify actual fluid level and base-brake operation before further diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: BCM code C1D00:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The parking-brake input circuit is shorted to ground.
diagnostics.next: Verify brake release and inspect the switch wiring; the code alone does not establish switch failure.

verification.title: Confirm the commanded response
verification.body: Record the gauge’s full sweep or each lamp’s commanded on/off response, plus the original complaint after any connection repair.

verification.title: Document the decision
verification.body: Record module codes, fluid-level history and the reached endpoint. A referral to a guided routine or separate repair procedure remains further work.

Diagnostic prerequisites, terminal protection and circuit testing.
Communication diagnosis when gateway codes are recorded.
ICM removal and installation after a failed gauge command.
ABS-module replacement at Test N’s specified endpoint.
Restraint-system diagnosis when RCM self-test codes appear.
RCM removal and installation after Test O.
Master-cylinder repair path selected by the fluid-switch test.

guides.title: Check MIL, rear fog and seat-belt indicators, with initial PRNDL diagnosis
guides.summary: Separate indicator faults from incorrect module inputs, and trace a missing automatic gear indication to the supported diagnostic stopping point.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) turns information from other modules into visible warnings and gear indications. A lamp that stays on or never lights can reflect an incorrect request, lost communication or a display fault. These tests check the malfunction indicator lamp (MIL), rear fog indicator and seat-belt warning, plus the initial checks for the automatic-transmission gear-position display, called PRNDL.
guides.why: Commanding an indicator with a scan tool establishes whether it can switch on and off. It does not establish whether its normal input is correct. Checking module faults and communication first prevents a working cluster from being mistaken for the cause.
searchTerms: engine warning light never comes on
seat belt warning light never comes on
gear display does not show P

when.summary: When an indicator stays on or never lights, or the automatic gear display is blank or never shows P.
notes: Reproduce the complaint before following a component-replacement decision.

prepare.title: Establish reliable electrical conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge greater than 70%. Inspect wiring, connections and previous repairs; record diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs).

prepare.title: Have the required diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting module self-tests, live parameter identification (PID) data and indicator commands. Voltage checks require a digital multimeter, Rotunda Flex Probes, Wiring Diagrams Cell 60 and competence with live electrical measurements.

prepare.title: Prepare for the correct follow-up
prepare.detail: Have the vehicle identification number (VIN) available for Guided Routines. Buckle or restraints-module replacement requires the linked replacement procedure and its restraint-system safety prerequisites.

steps.title: Test the MIL — U
steps.body: With ignition ON, run the IPC self-test. Refer recorded codes to the IPC DTC chart. If none are recorded, check Gateway Module A (GWM) continuous-memory codes; any codes require Communications Network diagnosis. Otherwise command the MIL PID on and off. If it responds, diagnose all powertrain control module (PCM) codes for an always-on complaint; a never-on complaint is operating correctly at this time. Failure to follow commands requires the VIN-specific IPC Guided Routine.

steps.title: Separate rear fog-lamp operation from its indicator — W
steps.body: With the rear fog lamps selected and ignition ON, observe the actual lamps as they are switched on and off. Incorrect operation leads to Fog Lamps diagnosis. If they work, follow the IPC/GWM code checks described in Test U, then command R_FOG_IND. Correct indicator response directs diagnosis of all body control module (BCM) codes; incorrect response requires the IPC Guided Routine.

steps.title: Compare buckle status with the seat-belt indicator — X
steps.body: After the IPC/GWM code checks, monitor restraints control module (RCM) PID SBELT_D_ST while buckling and unbuckling the driver belt. It must report BUCKLED and UNBUCKLED correctly; otherwise the branch directs a new buckle. If status is correct, command SBLT_LAMP on and off. Correct lamp response directs a new RCM through its full replacement procedure; incorrect response requires the IPC Guided Routine.

steps.title: Triage the missing PRNDL indication — V1–V4
steps.body: Verify transport mode is inactive. With ignition ON, perform the IPC self-test: P1706:00 leads to V5, while other codes lead to the IPC chart. With no IPC codes, test the BCM, check GWM continuous-memory codes, then test the PCM. Refer faults respectively to BCM diagnosis, network diagnosis or engine-specific diagnosis for transmission-related PCM codes. If no transmission-related code is recorded, stop at V7 for further selector-switch diagnosis.

steps.title: Measure the park-detect input without exceeding the stopping point — V5–V6
steps.body: At V5, turn ignition OFF, disconnect IPC C220, then turn ignition ON and measure C220 pin 4 to ground. No voltage leads to the V7 stopping point. If voltage is present, turn ignition OFF, disconnect selector lever C3245, then turn ignition ON and repeat the same measurement for V6. Record the result and stop: neither V6 voltage outcome establishes a selector or IPC replacement decision here. Do not bypass V7 to enter V8.

watchFor.title: A dark indication can be a communication fallback
watchFor.body: Missing gear/shift-mode, rear fog request or driver-buckle messages preserve the last indication for less than 5 seconds, then turn that indication off. The stability/traction sliding-car indicator differs: it retains its last state briefly for a missing or invalid request, but turns on after 5 seconds without a request.

notes: V8–V10 provide isolated-circuit reference values only: C220 pin 4 to C3245 pin 1 must be less than 3 ohms; C220 pin 4 to ground must exceed 10,000 ohms; C3245 pin 2 to ground must be less than 3 ohms. A failed check identifies a circuit-repair requirement, but these values do not create a route around V7. Resistance testing requires an isolated, unpowered circuit.

V11 describes replacing corroded connectors or terminals, cleaning module pins, replacing damaged, bent or pushed-out pins, then seating and latching the IPC connector and operating the system. A persistent concern leads to applicable technical service bulletins, then the VIN-specific IPC Guided Routine if none apply. A cleared concern still requires correcting the connection's root cause. This remains reference information beyond the PRNDL stopping point.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1706:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The IPC detected a park input above 16 km/h (10 mph). This conflicting information does not prove that the selector switch has failed.
diagnostics.next: Follow V5 and, only if voltage is present, the V6 measurement. Respect the stated stopping points.

verification.title: Verify the applicable branch result
verification.body: Compare commanded indicator states with the visible response and buckle data with actual belt operation. A successful lamp command does not close an unresolved input or module diagnosis.

verification.title: Record what was established
verification.body: Retain codes, command responses, buckle status and any park-detect voltage readings. Record whether PRNDL diagnosis stopped at V6 or V7; do not report it as a completed selector diagnosis.

procedures.purpose: IPC diagnosis: complete indicator Tests U, W and X; bounded PRNDL V1–V6 checks and V8–V11 reference information.
Electrical diagnostic prerequisites, probe selection and valid circuit measurements.
Communications Network diagnosis when the GWM code checks direct it.
BCM diagnosis for the rear fog and PRNDL branches.
Fog Lamps diagnosis when the actual rear lamps operate incorrectly.
Front Seatbelt Buckle removal and installation following the X3 result.
RCM removal and installation following the complete X4 decision.
Transport Mode Deactivation when required before PRNDL diagnosis.

applicability.equipment: Rear fog lamps for Test W; automatic transmission for Test V

guides.title: Diagnose stability and tire-pressure indicators and message-center controls
guides.summary: Use commanded lamp checks and steering-wheel input tests to separate cluster faults from system requests, settings and switch-circuit problems.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) displays information received through wiring and the vehicle network. Its message center uses the left steering-wheel switch for navigation and temporarily replaces selected pages with warnings. Tests Y, Z, AA and AB address two distinct stability indicators, the tire-pressure warning lamp and message-center control faults.
guides.why: A working lamp can display a genuine system concern or a communication fallback. Commanding it directly separates display capability from incoming requests. For navigation faults, several steering-wheel switches and the clockspring must be distinguished before replacing the column module.
searchTerms: sliding car OFF light not working
tire pressure warning light always on
steering wheel menu buttons not working

when.summary: Use when a stability or tire-pressure indicator stays on or never lights, or message-center navigation fails.
notes: Reproduce the concern before following replacement decisions; do not replace components from these tests when the complaint is absent.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation and verify battery state of charge exceeds 70%. Review previous repairs, wiring and related diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), addressing circuit faults before performance faults.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting module self-tests, live parameter identification (PID) data and active lamp commands. Have a tire-pressure gauge, administrator key, electrical meter, Rotunda Flex Probes and a fused jumper for the directed switch test.

prepare.title: Prepare for steering-wheel access
prepare.detail: AB4–AB15 require airbag or clockspring access. Complete the linked procedures' restraint-system safety prerequisites and follow every ignition-off disconnection and ignition-on test state. Probe only the specified switch circuits, never airbag igniter circuits.

steps.title: Test Y: check the sliding-car indicator
steps.body: Follow [Test Y](#/document/G1693940): self-test the IPC, then the anti-lock brake system (ABS) module, then check Gateway Module A (GWM) continuous-memory DTCs. Route faults to the corresponding cluster, ABS or communications diagnosis. With no codes, command TC/IVD/RSCLMP on and off. If it responds, a never-on complaint is considered normal; a persistent always-on complaint directs ABS-module replacement. Failure to respond requires the vehicle identification number (VIN)-based IPC Guided Routine.

steps.title: Test Z: check the sliding-car OFF indicator
steps.body: Check IPC and GWM codes first. Identify the key type: an administrator key leads through Z4's AdvanceTrac always-on setting check; a MyKey proceeds to Z5. Where testing continues, command STAB_TC_LMP on and off. Nonresponse requires the IPC Guided Routine. If it responds, use an administrator key and left steering-wheel controls to change the traction-control menu setting on and off. A changing selection passes; an unchanged selection redirects to stability-control-cannot-be-disabled diagnosis.

steps.title: Test AA: check the tire-pressure warning indicator
steps.body: First compare every tire's pressure with the vehicle certification label and correct discrepancies. If pressures meet specification, self-test the IPC and body control module (BCM), then check GWM continuous-memory codes. Follow the relevant fault diagnosis before proceeding. Command the tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) lamp through TPMWARN_LMP. A responsive lamp with a never-on complaint passes; a responsive lamp that remains on in normal operation requires TPMS diagnosis. Nonresponse requires the IPC Guided Routine.

steps.title: Test AB: distinguish switch input from display behavior
steps.body: Acknowledge displayed warnings with OK before assessing navigation. Self-test the IPC and steering column control module (SCCM); route the switch codes as described below. With no codes, compare left, right, up, down and OK PIDs with actual switch positions. Matching inputs lead to the IPC Guided Routine. Mismatched inputs lead to AB4: after airbag access and disconnection of both upper switches, approximately 5 volts at the specified left-switch terminals directs left-switch replacement; otherwise continue to AB16.

steps.title: Isolate the switch responsible for a held-input code
steps.body: For B137F:09, follow AB5–AB7. Disconnect all steering-wheel switches, connect only the left upper switch and test navigation. Failure directs its replacement. If it passes, connect the right upper switch; newly failed navigation directs right-upper replacement. Next connect the left lower switch: failure directs left-lower replacement, while continued correct navigation directs right-lower replacement.

steps.title: Locate a switch-input short to ground
steps.body: For B137F:11, follow AB8–AB10, switching ignition off before each separation and on for each SCCM self-test. Disconnect the left upper switch, then the upper clockspring connector, then remove the clockspring as directed. B137F:17 appearing at those respective stages directs replacement of the left upper switch, steering wheel or clockspring. If it never appears, continue to AB16.

steps.title: Separate switch failure from an open circuit
steps.body: For B137F:17, follow AB11's fused-jumper connection from C2998 pin 2 to ground. If the SCCM then records B137F:11, remove the jumper and replace the left switch. Otherwise remove it and follow AB12–AB15: test the signal and return paths through the steering-wheel harness, then the clockspring. Each specified path must measure less than 3 ohms. A failed wheel-harness path directs steering-wheel replacement; a failed clockspring path directs clockspring replacement. Passing paths lead to AB16.

steps.title: Complete the SCCM connection check
steps.body: At AB16, turn ignition off, inspect SCCM connectors, repair corrosion or damaged/pushed-out terminals, reconnect securely and retest. If the concern remains, check the On-Line Automotive Service Information System (OASIS) for applicable technical service bulletins (TSBs). Follow a matching bulletin; otherwise AB16 directs SCCM replacement. Carry any prescribed replacement through its linked removal and installation procedure.

watchFor.title: The fused jumper fails
watchFor.body: During AB11, a failed jumper fuse requires repair of a short to voltage in the signal circuit. Do not treat it as an open-switch result.

watchFor.title: An indicator changes after communication is lost
watchFor.body: The OFF indicator initially retains its previous state, then defaults off when its request remains missing. Missing TPMS messages can produce flashing followed by steady illumination.

notes: A MyKey with AdvanceTrac configured always on prevents traction-control disabling; fault and active-event indication still operates.
Acknowledging a warning restores message-center access but does not establish that the underlying vehicle condition has been repaired.

diagnostics.finding: The SCCM records diagnostic trouble code B137F:09.
diagnostics.meaning: A message-center switch input was detected as pressed for 2 minutes or longer.
diagnostics.next: Use AB5–AB7 to isolate the switches rather than assuming the left navigation switch is responsible.

diagnostics.finding: The SCCM records diagnostic trouble code B137F:11.
diagnostics.meaning: The message-center switch input circuit is shorted to ground.
diagnostics.next: Use AB8–AB10 and observe whether isolation changes the result to B137F:17.

diagnostics.finding: The SCCM records diagnostic trouble code B137F:17.
diagnostics.meaning: The switch input circuit has an open or short to voltage.
diagnostics.next: Use AB11's controlled jumper test, then the wheel-harness and clockspring continuity checks if required.

diagnostics.finding: The compass displays dashes after direction messages are missing for more than 5 seconds.
diagnostics.meaning: This is the cluster's fallback for lost direction information; communication, the global positioning system module or the IPC may be involved.
diagnostics.next: Continue compass-specific diagnosis. Dashes alone do not identify a failed component.

verification.title: Confirm the relevant function
verification.body: Repeat the applicable lamp on/off command or test message-center navigation in every switch position. For Test Z, confirm the administrator-key menu selection changes as directed.

verification.title: Record observed and commanded results
verification.body: Record DTCs, commanded versus observed lamp states, switch PID responses, circuit results and the resulting diagnostic decision.

guides.title: Diagnose compass, range-estimate and outside-temperature display complaints
guides.summary: Separate driving-history effects, display settings, communication faults and temperature-sensor problems before choosing a repair.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) combines information from several modules to operate its displays. Distance to empty (DTE) depends on fuel information and driving history, while outside temperature comes from a separate sensor. These checks also cover an inactive SVT performance shift indication and explain the behavior of the fitted blind-spot off indicator.
guides.why: A displayed value can be misleading even when its sensor works. Outside-temperature filtering deliberately slows rising readings to reduce heat-soak errors. Comparing the sensor’s physical temperature, its electronic reading and the displayed value helps locate where the disagreement begins.

when.summary: Use when a compass, range estimate, outside-temperature display or fitted SVT shift indication has a current complaint.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting network tests, module self-tests and live data, an infrared temperature scanner, and a resistance meter with the specified Rotunda Flex Probes. Check battery and charging-system operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%.

prepare.title: Preserve fuel-economy history
prepare.detail: Record Running Average Fuel Economy (RAFE) before disconnecting the battery, removing the IPC or removing body control module (BCM) fuse 13 (7.5A). These interruptions require driving over time for DTE calculations to adjust.

steps.title: AC: Investigate an inoperative compass
steps.body: With ignition on, self-test the global positioning system module (GPSM). Diagnose any recorded diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) through the applicable information-and-entertainment procedure. If none appear, self-test the IPC and follow its DTC chart for any codes. Only the code-free path directs GPSM replacement.

steps.title: AD: Investigate the range estimate
steps.body: Review extended idling, frequent remote starting, grades, overfilling and partial refueling with the driver; fuel alcohol content can also influence the concern. Explain how changed use affects the estimate. If use has not changed, switch ignition on and verify fuel-gauge operation. A faulty indication leads to Pinpoint Test C. A correct gauge requires further DTE diagnosis beyond these initial checks.

steps.title: AE1: Reset the outside-temperature display
steps.body: With ignition on, press and release A/C and Recirc together, then press A/C again within 2 seconds. A correct reading establishes normal operation at this time. Otherwise continue with communication checks.

steps.title: AE2–AE6: Check the temperature message path
steps.body: Network-test the powertrain control module (PCM), gateway module (GWM) and front controls interface module (FCIM). Diagnose failed communication first. Then perform the FCIM self-test, check GWM continuous-memory codes and perform the PCM self-test, stopping at any codes for the specified module diagnosis. If these checks pass, an incorrect reading leads to AE7; another display concern requires the VIN-specific FCIM guided routine.

steps.title: AE7–AE8: Compare sensor input with display behavior
steps.body: Measure and record the ambient air temperature (AAT) sensor-body temperature. With ignition on, compare it with the PCM’s AAT parameter identification (PID), or live-data value. Agreement within ±3°C (±5°F) leads to driving above 33 km/h (20 mph). A display moving toward actual temperature passes; failure to update directs heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) module replacement. Disagreement leads to resistance testing.

steps.title: AE9–AE10: Separate sensor resistance from wiring resistance
steps.body: For 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L engines, switch ignition off and follow AE9’s engine-specific PCM disconnection and terminal instructions. Compare resistance with its temperature table. A matching result leads to AE11. Otherwise disconnect sensor C132 and measure between component-side pins 1 and 2 using AE10’s table. A matching sensor reading identifies excessive circuit resistance for repair; an incorrect reading leads to AE12.

steps.title: AE11–AE12: Inspect airflow and the sensor connection
steps.body: At AE11, remove leaves, paper or other obstructions to restore airflow. If the area is clear, proceed to AE12. At AE12, disconnect C132 and inspect for water, corrosion, damaged pins or pushed-out pins. Repair those defects; if none exist, the branch directs a new AAT sensor.

steps.title: AF: Check an inactive SVT performance shift indication
steps.body: Use the message center to verify the function is enabled; turn it on if disabled. If already enabled, self-test the IPC, head-up display (HUD) and PCM in sequence, then check GWM continuous-memory codes. Follow the IPC chart, HUD/collision-warning, engine or network diagnostic branch for any codes. If all are clear, AF directs HUD replacement.

watchFor.title: 5.2L resistance-test boundary
watchFor.body: AE1–AE8 apply to the 5.2L, but AE9’s PCM terminals do not establish a 5.2L measurement. Obtain the engine-specific procedure before continuing that resistance branch.

watchFor.title: An absent symptom
watchFor.body: Do not follow a component-replacement decision when the complaint is no longer present during testing.

notes: The PCM reads temperature-dependent sensor resistance and sends the value through the gateway to the front controls. Rising temperatures update slowly according to vehicle speed; falling temperatures update faster.

diagnostics.finding: The outside-temperature display holds its last value or shows dashes.
diagnostics.meaning: An invalid or missing temperature message retains the last reading for less than 5 seconds; at 5 seconds or longer, the display shows dashes.
diagnostics.next: Follow AE communication and module checks before condemning the sensor.

diagnostics.finding: The Blind Spot Information System off indicator never illuminates or remains on.
diagnostics.meaning: Missing or invalid left/right detection messages retain the last indicator state for less than 5 seconds, then default it off.
diagnostics.next: Investigate communication, gateway, side-detection modules and IPC through the appropriate diagnosis; indicator state alone does not identify the failed part.

verification.title: Recognize the supported pass conditions
verification.body: AE1 passes when resetting restores the correct reading; AE8 passes when driving updates it toward actual temperature. Explain the update strategy to the driver.

verification.title: Record results and remaining work
verification.body: Keep RAFE, self-test results, sensor temperature, AAT live data and any resistance readings. Identify further DTE diagnosis or a guided routine as pending where required.

procedures.purpose: AC–AF diagnosis and BLIS indicator behavior; AE9 measurements are limited to 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L, and AF is SVT only.
Electrical diagnostic prerequisites, live-data interpretation and terminal-safe measurement methods.
Diagnose failed network tests and gateway communication codes.
HVAC control-module removal and installation when AE8 directs replacement.
Diagnose HUD codes encountered in the SVT shift-indication path.
HUD removal and installation when the completed SVT AF path directs replacement.

applicability.equipment: 4.2-inch display or touchscreen for outside temperature; SVT only for performance shift indication; Blind Spot Information System where fitted

guides.title: Diagnose drive-mode, temperature, launch-control and low-fuel indicators
guides.summary: Determine whether an unexpected dashboard indicator reflects normal conditions, a setting, missing network information or a fault requiring further diagnosis.
guides.introduction: A reconfigurable telltale (RTT) is an indicator displayed by the instrument panel cluster (IPC). The cluster uses vehicle inputs and network messages to decide what to show. These checks test the display's response, then trace the information behind each affected indicator.
guides.why: An illuminated warning can represent a real condition or a fallback response to missing information. Conversely, an unlit indicator may be correct for the current settings or fuel level. Establish those conditions before considering module replacement.

when.summary: When a covered indicator stays on unexpectedly or fails to appear under the reported operating conditions.
notes: Module-replacement decisions require the concern to be present during diagnosis.

prepare.title: Prepare the vehicle and diagnostic access
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation and verify battery state of charge above 70%. Have a scan tool supporting cluster, gateway and powertrain tests, the vehicle identification number for guided routines, and instructions for cluster Dealer Test Mode.

prepare.title: Establish the complaint
prepare.detail: Record which indicator is affected and whether it is always or never on. Check related trouble codes, previous repairs and applicable technical service information. For low-fuel diagnosis, identify administrator-key or MyKey use.

steps.title: Prove basic message-center response
steps.body: Each test begins with ignition on and all doors, hood and luggage lid closed. Acknowledge warnings with OK. Observe the door-ajar indicator, open the driver door and clear its popup. The indicator must be off when closed and on when open. A failed response leads to the VIN-dependent IPC guided routine.

steps.title: Test AK: drive-mode indicators
steps.body: Run the IPC self-test and follow its diagnostic trouble code (DTC) chart for recorded faults. Otherwise check gateway module A (GWM) continuous-memory codes, directing faults to network diagnosis. Then run the powertrain control module (PCM) key-on, engine-off self-test. Diagnose PCM codes through the applicable engine procedure. With no codes, AK accepts a never-on complaint as operating correctly at that time; a persistent always-on complaint directs PCM replacement through the engine-specific procedure.

steps.title: Test AL: engine over-temperature indicator
steps.body: Follow the same IPC, GWM and PCM test order. With no codes, AL likewise accepts the never-on condition at that time and directs PCM replacement for a persistent always-on condition. Missing or invalid temperature/request messages hold the previous indication for less than 5 seconds; at 5 seconds or longer, the cluster turns the warning on.

steps.title: Test AM: launch-control indicator never appears
steps.body: After the common display check, verify launch control is enabled through the message center. Disabled launch control explains the absent indication and is a normal result. If enabled, follow IPC self-test results, GWM memory codes and then PCM-code diagnosis. This branch does not establish module failure merely because the indicator remains absent.

steps.title: Test AN: compare low-fuel indication with measured conditions
steps.body: First verify normal fuel-gauge operation; any gauge complaint goes to Test C. Record distance to empty (DTE), enter Dealer Test Mode and read the second Inst Fuel1 value, labelled FLPM. Compare it with AN3's exact paired fuel-value/DTE criteria, including administrator-key and MyKey conditions. When criteria are met, an illuminated warning is correct and an absent warning requires the IPC guided routine. When criteria are not met, those decisions reverse.

watchFor.title: A launch-control flash can indicate lost information
watchFor.body: A missing launch-control message holds the last indication for less than 5 seconds. After 5 seconds, the cluster flashes the launch-control image for 2 seconds.

watchFor.title: Recognize the separate oil-warning branch
watchFor.body: For 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L without the Performance Package, missing engine-speed or oil-warning messages hold the previous indication for less than 5 seconds, then turn the warning on. Possible causes include wiring, the switch, base-engine conditions, tachometer operation and control/network faults.

notes: Acknowledging a popup restores message-center access; it does not resolve the condition behind the warning.
The oil-warning information here does not establish measured engine oil pressure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0521 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detected oil-pressure-switch signal variation outside its permitted range.
diagnostics.next: Continue applicable oil-pressure input diagnosis; the code alone does not identify the failed component.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0522 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detected a short to ground on the oil-pressure-switch input.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose the input circuit before replacing components.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0523 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detected an open oil-pressure-switch input.
diagnostics.next: Trace the input circuit and connections.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0524 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detected low oil pressure.
diagnostics.next: Continue applicable engine oil-pressure diagnosis rather than treating this solely as a display fault.

verification.title: Confirm the applicable decision
verification.body: Compare the indicator's actual state with the completed test's conditions. Retain any directed engine, network or guided-routine work as an outstanding diagnostic action.

verification.title: Record evidence for the result
verification.body: Record self-test results and the door-ajar response. For AN, retain DTE, FLPM, key type and warning state together so the threshold decision can be checked.

procedures.purpose: Tests AK–AN, exact low-fuel comparisons, associated DTC routing and introductory oil-warning fault information.
Diagnostic prerequisites and safeguards against unsupported module replacement.
Network diagnosis when gateway trouble codes are recorded.
Cluster operation and Dealer Test Mode access for AN3.

applicability.equipment: Drive-mode and launch-control features where fitted; administrator-key or MyKey operation as applicable

guides.title: Diagnose low-oil-pressure, overspeed and wrench warnings
guides.summary: Separate engine-pressure, circuit, communication and configuration faults when these dashboard warnings stay on or never appear.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) combines wired inputs and messages from other modules to display warnings. Its reconfigurable telltales (RTTs) are warning symbols within the display. These tests establish whether an unexpected indication comes from the reported vehicle condition, its electrical input, missing messages or configuration.
guides.why: A warning symbol is the end of a signal path, so replacing the cluster first can miss the cause. Oil-pressure testing is especially important: a functioning warning circuit cannot establish that the engine has adequate lubrication.

when.summary: Use when the relevant warning is consistently absent or illuminated unexpectedly.
notes: Component-replacement decisions require the complaint to be present during testing.

prepare.title: Establish the vehicle and electrical condition
prepare.detail: Identify engine, Performance Package and market specification. Check battery/charging condition, battery state of charge above 70%, wiring and previous repairs; diagnose circuit-related trouble codes first.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Have a capable scan tool, digital multimeter, approved terminal flex probes and fused jumper. Oil-pressure testing requires the engine-specific procedure and equipment. Follow each step's ignition state and connector isolation.

steps.title: Check the shared message-center function
steps.body: With ignition on, close the doors, hood and luggage lid, then acknowledge warnings with OK. Open the driver door and clear its popup. The door-ajar symbol must be off when closed and on when open. Failure routes to the vehicle-identification-number-specific IPC guided routine.

steps.title: Check supporting gauges and cluster faults
steps.body: For oil-pressure tests AO/AP, start the engine and verify the tachometer; failure routes to Test G. For overspeed Test AQ, verify the speedometer; failure routes to Test D. Then perform the IPC self-test and follow its diagnostic trouble code (DTC) chart before continuing. Test AR proceeds directly from the message-center check to this self-test.

steps.title: AO: investigate a missing oil warning
steps.body: Use AO for 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L without Performance Package. Disconnect the appropriate pressure switch with ignition off, then observe the warning with ignition on. Illumination directs switch replacement. Otherwise, check the input circuit for a short to ground; repair a failed circuit or proceed to AO11.

steps.title: AO: investigate a warning that stays on
steps.body: Check gateway module (GWM) memory codes, then powertrain control module (PCM) self-test codes; route faults to network or engine diagnosis. With no codes, apply only AO8's specified fused jumper. If the warning extinguishes, remove it and test actual oil pressure: repair low pressure or replace the switch if pressure is satisfactory. Otherwise retain the jumper for AO10's open-circuit check, then remove it and follow the circuit-repair or AO11 branch.

steps.title: AP: test the performance-engine pressure signal
steps.body: Use AP for 5.0L Performance Package and 5.2L. Check actual oil pressure first. With pressure satisfactory, check sensor supply voltage. A satisfactory supply leads through signal-circuit checks for unwanted voltage, an open and grounding; passing these directs PCM replacement, code clearing and retesting. An incorrect supply leads through voltage-reference and return-circuit checks; passing these directs sensor replacement, clearing and retesting. Repair failed circuits. Persistent warnings proceed to AP13.

steps.title: Complete AO11 or AP13 when directed
steps.body: Inspect all PCM connectors with ignition off. Renew corroded or damaged terminals, correct pushed-out pins, clean module pins and latch connectors securely. Retest. If the complaint remains, check Ford's online service-information system for applicable technical service bulletins before the prescribed PCM replacement.

steps.title: AQ: confirm overspeed-market configuration
steps.body: After passing speedometer and IPC checks, confirm GCC build specification. A non-GCC vehicle needs no correction through this branch. For a GCC vehicle, perform scan-tool-directed Programmable Module Installation using as-built data.

steps.title: AR: trace the wrench-warning request
steps.body: After the IPC check, self-test the body control module (BCM), perform the PCM key-on/engine-off self-test, then retrieve GWM memory codes. Follow any faults into their respective diagnostics. With all checks clear, an absent wrench warning is normal; a continuously illuminated warning directs PCM replacement.

watchFor.title: Missing messages change indications
watchFor.body: AP oil-pressure and AR wrench warnings retain their previous state briefly, then default on after 5 seconds of missing relevant messages. Overspeed defaults off after 5 seconds of missing or invalid speed data.

notes: The steering-mode background identifies communication, electric power-assisted steering, GWM and IPC concerns. Its indication retains the previous state briefly, then defaults off after 5 seconds of missing or invalid steering-effort data.

diagnostics.finding: PCM diagnostic trouble code P0521 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Oil-pressure input variation is outside module parameters.
diagnostics.next: Follow the applicable pressure and circuit diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: PCM diagnostic trouble code P0522 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The oil-pressure input indicates a short to ground.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose the circuit before condemning a component.

diagnostics.finding: PCM diagnostic trouble code P0523 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The oil-pressure input indicates an open circuit.
diagnostics.next: Follow the applicable circuit checks.

diagnostics.finding: PCM diagnostic trouble code P0524 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detects low oil pressure.
diagnostics.next: Establish actual pressure and repair any mechanical pressure concern.

verification.title: Confirm and record the outcome
verification.body: Record the applicable test, self-test results, pressure/circuit findings and final warning behavior. Complete AP's required clearing and retest after replacement. Correct the root cause of connector faults even if reseating restores operation.
