Electrical prerequisites, terminal probing and circuit-test methods.
Communication diagnosis when GWM faults are present.
BCM fault diagnosis following AR self-test results.
Configuration information supporting AQ's as-built programming branch.

applicability.equipment: 5.0L Performance Package where fitted; Gulf Cooperative Countries (GCC) market equipment for overspeed testing

guides.title: Diagnose steering and damper indicators, brake warnings and fuel-inlet messages
guides.summary: Separate message-center faults from steering, suspension, brake and engine-system concerns using Tests AS through AV.
guides.introduction: The message center is part of the instrument panel cluster (IPC). It receives wired and network information, then displays warnings and reconfigurable telltales (RTTs)—indicators whose displayed state changes with vehicle conditions. A missing indicator can reflect either a display problem or a system that never produces the expected state.
guides.why: These tests first establish basic display operation, then check the relevant vehicle function and communication records. This sequence prevents a missing or persistent warning from being treated as proof that the cluster itself has failed.
searchTerms: check fuel fill inlet message stays on

when.summary: A steering/damper indicator stays off, a ceramic-brake warning behaves incorrectly, or the fuel-inlet message stays on.
notes: Tests AT and AU are SVT-only branches; confirm the corresponding suspension or brake equipment is fitted.

prepare.title: Scan access and operating information
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool that supports IPC self-tests and gateway module A (GWM) continuous memory diagnostic trouble codes (CMDTCs). Have the vehicle identification number (VIN) for the IPC guided routine and the owner's mode-selection instructions.

prepare.title: Preliminary checks
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge above 70%. Review previous repairs and obvious wiring faults. The ceramic-brake branch also requires competent brake-pad inspection.

steps.title: Establish a clear display baseline
steps.body: Switch ignition ON, close all doors, the hood and luggage lid, and acknowledge each warning with OK. For AS, AT and AV, check that the door-ajar telltale is off with the driver door closed. Open the door, clear the popup and confirm the telltale is on. AU instead checks that the door-ajar message appears with the door open and disappears when closed. Failure directs you to the VIN-based IPC guided routine.

steps.title: Check the function behind the indication
steps.body: Before scanning further, AS checks whether selecting steering modes changes steering effort; AT checks whether the damper-control system changes state using its switch; AU checks brake-pad wear. These establish whether the underlying system needs attention first. AV proceeds directly to the IPC self-test.

steps.title: Run the cluster self-test
steps.body: When the preceding checks pass, perform the IPC self-test. Any diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) go to the IPC DTC chart in the linked instrumentation procedure. Continue to the gateway check only when no IPC codes are recorded.

steps.title: Check the gateway's stored faults
steps.body: Retrieve GWM CMDTCs. Any recorded codes direct diagnosis to the Communications Network procedure. The gateway check helps distinguish a message-delivery concern from a fault within the system requesting the indication.

steps.title: Follow the complaint-specific endpoint
steps.body: If the gateway has no codes, use the appropriate decision below. A clean cluster and gateway scan does not establish that steering, suspension, brake sensing or evaporative-emissions operation is correct.

watchFor.title: An extinguished warning can reflect missing information
watchFor.body: For damper indication, missing or invalid data retains the last state for less than 5 seconds, then turns the indication off. Missing brake-wear and fuel-inlet requests follow the same timing. An absent display alone therefore does not confirm system health.

notes: Convertible-top warnings also retain their previous state for less than 5 seconds of missing requests, then default off. A persistent top warning requires separate diagnosis of the top system, moveable roof control module A, gateway and IPC.

diagnostics.finding: The steering-mode telltale never illuminates.
diagnostics.meaning: Test AS distinguishes missing indication from failure to change steering effort.
diagnostics.next: If effort does not change, diagnose electric power-assisted steering. That is also the endpoint when IPC and GWM checks find no codes.

diagnostics.finding: The SVT damper-control telltale never illuminates.
diagnostics.meaning: Test AT checks actual damper-system response before investigating display communication.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose Vehicle Dynamic Suspension if switch operation does not change system state, or if IPC and GWM checks are clear.

diagnostics.finding: The SVT ceramic-brake warning is never or always displayed.
diagnostics.meaning: Test AU requires pad condition to be established before further electronic diagnosis.
diagnostics.next: Replace worn pads through the applicable brake procedure. With acceptable pads and clear IPC/GWM checks, diagnose all brake-sensor DTCs in the vehicle dynamics module (VDM).

diagnostics.finding: The check-fuel-fill-inlet message remains displayed.
diagnostics.meaning: Test AV can lead to an evaporative-emissions or powertrain-control concern.
diagnostics.next: With clear IPC/GWM checks, diagnose all powertrain control module (PCM) DTCs using the engine-appropriate procedure. If the message is instead never on, no current condition requires its display.

verification.title: Repeat the relevant observation
verification.body: Confirm the door-ajar baseline and record the actual steering-mode, damper-switch, pad-condition or fuel-message result.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic handoff
verification.body: Retain IPC and GWM results and identify the system requiring further work. Completing these checks does not itself complete that system's repair.

procedures.purpose: Tests AS–AV, door-ajar baseline checks, IPC DTC chart and complaint-specific decisions.
Preliminary electrical checks and diagnostic methods.
Steering-effort mode and electric power-assisted steering diagnosis reached by AS.
Damper-system diagnosis reached by AT and VDM brake-sensor diagnosis reached by AU.
Network diagnosis when GWM codes are recorded.

applicability.equipment: SVT damper-control and ceramic-brake equipment where applicable

guides.title: Trace persistent message-center warnings and a missing adaptive-cruise chime
guides.summary: Diagnose persistent convertible-top, engine-on and hill-start-assist messages, or an inoperative adaptive-cruise warning chime, using tests AW–AZ.
guides.introduction: The message center belongs to the instrument panel cluster (IPC), which combines vehicle inputs into warnings and coordinates audible alerts. A persistent message can reflect a problem in the system supplying information. These tests first check a familiar display or chime function, then direct diagnosis toward the relevant module or feature.
guides.why: The door-ajar indicator and safety-belt chime provide useful checks of shared warning functions. Passing either check does not prove the roof, engine-status, hill-start or cruise-control system is working correctly.
searchTerms: hill start assist warning stays on
adaptive cruise warning chime not working

when.summary: When one of the named warnings remains displayed or the adaptive-cruise warning chime fails to sound.
notes: AW applies to the convertible top; AX applies only to push-button-start vehicles.
Select AY for hill-start-assist warnings and AZ for the adaptive-cruise warning chime.

prepare.title: Prepare for module diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting module self-tests and continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Arrange vehicle identification number (VIN) access for IPC guided routines.

prepare.title: Check the foundations
prepare.detail: Verify the concern is present, review previous repairs, check battery and charging operation, and confirm battery state of charge exceeds 70%. Resolve relevant circuit codes first.

steps.title: Check display response for AW, AX or AY
steps.body: With ignition ON, close all doors, the hood and luggage compartment lid. Acknowledge each warning with OK. Observe the door-ajar reconfigurable telltale (RTT), open the driver door, clear the popup and observe again. It should be off with the door closed and on when open. An incorrect response leads to the VIN-based IPC guided routine.

steps.title: Self-test the cluster
steps.body: After a correct display check, self-test the IPC. Diagnose recorded codes through its DTC chart before continuing. A clear result allows the complaint-specific route below.

steps.title: AW: Follow a persistent convertible-top message
steps.body: Check Gateway Module A (GWM) continuous-memory codes. Any codes lead to Communications Network diagnosis. With none recorded, diagnose all Moveable Roof Control Module-A (MRCMA) codes. The display check alone does not establish a roof-system repair.

steps.title: AX: Follow a persistent engine-on message
steps.body: On push-button-start vehicles, self-test the body control module (BCM) first; recorded codes lead to BCM diagnosis. If clear, check GWM memory and diagnose any network codes. If that is also clear, diagnose all powertrain control module (PCM) codes using the appropriate engine procedure.

steps.title: AY: Follow a persistent hill-start-assist message
steps.body: Check GWM continuous-memory codes and follow Communications Network diagnosis if any are recorded. Otherwise, diagnose the hill-start-assist feature through Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) and Stability Control diagnosis.

steps.title: AZ: Establish the basic chime response
steps.body: Follow AZ1's ignition OFF/ON and driver-belt unbuckling sequence, monitoring the safety-belt chime during the OFF-to-RUN check. It should sound for approximately 6 seconds. If it does not, use the IPC guided routine. If it does, self-test the IPC, resolve its codes, then check GWM memory and resolve any network codes.

steps.title: AZ: Compare the cruise indicator with operation
steps.body: With the preceding checks clear, verify whether the adaptive-cruise RTT illuminates while adaptive cruise is active. If it illuminates, continue cruise-control system diagnosis. If it does not, continue with Pinpoint Test AI in the instrumentation procedure. Neither result alone justifies replacing the cluster.

watchFor.title: Acknowledgment is not a repair
watchFor.body: Pressing OK clears the displayed warning so other functions can be checked; the condition requesting it may remain.

watchFor.title: Chime priorities and backup operation
watchFor.body: A higher-priority warning can delay another chime. The IPC can also provide required chimes when audio-system chime output fails, so audible output does not prove every speaker path works.

notes: Japan-only backup-chime complaints use a separate diagnostic path involving communications, reverse lamps, GWM and IPC; AZ does not resolve that complaint.

diagnostics.finding: The engine-on warning remains displayed.
diagnostics.meaning: Its inputs include engine status, driver-door status, transmission gear-display mode and vehicle speed. Missing messages retain the last indication for less than 5 seconds; a loss lasting 5 seconds or longer switches the warning off.
diagnostics.next: Follow AX's IPC, BCM, gateway and PCM decisions rather than assuming prolonged message loss explains the displayed warning.

diagnostics.finding: The hill-start-assist warning remains displayed.
diagnostics.meaning: A missing hill-start status message retains the previous indication for less than 5 seconds, then defaults the warning off at 5 seconds or longer.
diagnostics.next: Follow AY to distinguish cluster or gateway faults from a hill-start-assist feature concern.

verification.title: Verify the baseline and complaint separately
verification.body: Confirm the specified door-indicator or belt-chime response. Then complete the verification required by the system diagnosis reached; a passed baseline alone does not close the original complaint.

verification.title: Record the handoff
verification.body: Record the selected test, observed warning behavior, module codes and final diagnostic destination, including the cruise RTT result for AZ.

procedures.purpose: Exact AW–AZ tests, IPC DTC chart, guided-routine decisions and Test AI handoff.
Electrical diagnostic prerequisites and interpretation of module tests.
Network diagnosis when gateway continuous-memory codes are recorded.
BCM diagnosis following AX self-test codes.
Cruise-control diagnosis for vehicles with adaptive cruise control after the AZ indicator check.

applicability.equipment: Convertible top, push-button start, hill start assist or adaptive cruise control, according to the complaint.

guides.title: Diagnose warning chimes that are missing, stay on or sound only from the cluster
guides.summary: Separate warning-request, network, lighting and audio faults using the diagnostic branch that matches the chime complaint.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) receives warning requests, prioritizes them and controls the chimes. Most sound through the audio speakers; the cluster also provides backup sound when the audio path fails. Blind Spot Information System (BLIS) and Cross Traffic Alert (CTA) warnings use the rear speakers. These tests distinguish a missing warning request from a failure to reproduce its sound.
guides.why: A working cluster sounder does not establish that the speaker path works. Conversely, a continuous chime may reflect an incorrect lighting, door or ignition input. Checking those inputs before replacing modules keeps the diagnosis tied to the actual cause.
searchTerms: backup warning chime not working Japan
blind spot cross traffic warning chime missing
chime sounds only from instrument cluster

when.summary: When a warning chime is missing, sounds continuously, or comes only from the cluster instead of the audio speakers.
notes: Choose the complaint-specific branch; the Japan-only backup-chime test is not a general parking-aid test.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of module self-tests and live data, a digital multimeter, connector information and Rotunda Flex Probes. The audio branch requires controlled live-voltage measurements and isolated resistance testing.

prepare.title: Establish valid conditions
prepare.detail: Confirm the concern is present, check battery and charging operation, and verify battery state of charge is greater than 70%. Inspect previous repairs and obvious wiring damage. Do not replace modules for an absent intermittent concern.

steps.title: BA and BB: establish whether the basic chime operates
steps.body: For either missing backup or BLIS/CTA sound, check the driver safety-belt warning during the OFF-to-RUN transition with the belt unbuckled. Expect approximately 6 seconds of sound. If absent, the next step is the vehicle identification number (VIN)-dependent IPC guided routine.

steps.title: BA: investigate the Japan-market backup warning
steps.body: Apply the parking brake, select reverse and check the reverse lamps. Incorrect operation leads to reversing-lamp diagnosis. Otherwise, perform the IPC self-test, then the powertrain control module (PCM) self-test, then check gateway module A (GWM) continuous-memory codes. Follow IPC, engine or network diagnosis respectively for recorded faults. With no codes, continue to the VIN-dependent IPC routine.

steps.title: BB: investigate missing BLIS/CTA sound
steps.body: After the belt chime passes, run the IPC self-test and then check GWM continuous-memory codes. Follow the IPC code chart or communications diagnosis when directed. If both checks are clear, diagnose BLIS/CTA itself: the missing sound may originate in the system requesting the warning.

steps.title: BC: check what may be requesting a continuous chime
steps.body: Cycle the ignition OFF and ON and investigate illuminated warnings or message-center indication concerns first. Next, switch the headlamps OFF, close all doors and wait one minute; headlamps and parking lamps should be off. Check interior-light response to opening and closing the driver door. Route failures to the corresponding lighting diagnosis. On automatics, verify the gear-position display shows PARK with the selector in PARK; a mismatch leads to Pinpoint Test V. Manuals skip that check.

steps.title: BC: compare ignition inputs with actual operation
steps.body: Run the body control module (BCM) self-test and address its codes first. Monitor the parameter identifications (PIDs) IGN_SW_ACC, IGN_SW_RUN and IGN_SW_KEY_IN while selecting ACC, OFF and RUN. Incorrect correspondence directs diagnosis to ignition-switch outputs to the BCM. Correct correspondence leads to the VIN-dependent IPC routine.

steps.title: BD: follow the fitted audio-system branch
steps.body: With ignition ON, self-test the IPC, audio front control module (ACM) and accessory protocol interface module (APIM), following any code referrals. The 2.3L automatic additionally requires a digital audio control module C (DACMC) self-test. Its touchscreen branch proceeds directly to the audio digital signal processing (DSP) module self-test; other branches check AM/FM operation first. Radio faults require audio diagnosis. A working non-touchscreen system proceeds to BD17; touchscreen routes continue through BD6.

steps.title: BD: distinguish missing audio signals from wiring faults
steps.body: At BD6, no DSP codes leads to BD17; the two open-input codes below select left- or right-hand circuit tests. Other codes require their audio-system diagnostic procedures. Follow BD7–BD16 for connector pins, ignition states and limits: check fluctuating AC voltage with the DSP disconnected and radio operating. A signal leads to BD19. Without one, disconnect the ACM as directed and test for unwanted voltage, shorts to ground, opens and wires shorted together. Repair failed circuits.

steps.title: BD: inspect connections before condemning a module
steps.body: At BD17 for the ACM or BD19 for the DSP, switch ignition OFF and inspect the module connectors. Replace corroded connectors or terminals, clean module pins, and renew damaged or pushed-out pins as necessary. Reconnect securely and retest. If the concern remains, check applicable technical service bulletins through OASIS and follow any matching bulletin.

steps.title: BD: follow the remaining module decision
steps.body: Without an applicable bulletin, BD17 directs ACM replacement using the correct audio-equipment procedure, followed by a normal-operation test. If speaker chimes still fail, BD18 checks IPC connections using the same inspection and bulletin process before requiring its VIN-dependent guided routine. BD19 directs DSP replacement when its concern persists without an applicable bulletin.

watchFor.title: Normal sounds can mislead
watchFor.body: The turn-signal tick-tock normally comes from the IPC. A higher-priority warning can also replace or delay a lower-priority chime.

watchFor.title: A reconnection is not the whole repair
watchFor.body: If reseating a connector restores operation, address the corrosion, pin damage or poor connection that caused the interruption.

notes: Use the exact connector and measurement instructions in Tests BA–BD; do not improvise module jumper connections.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B13F8:13 is recorded by the audio DSP module.
diagnostics.meaning: Audio Input 2: Circuit Open identifies a detected open on the left-hand chime signal circuits between the ACM and DSP.
diagnostics.next: Follow BD7–BD11 for the left-hand rear signal path before deciding between wiring and module action.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B13FA:13 is recorded by the audio DSP module.
diagnostics.meaning: Audio Input 4: Circuit Open identifies a detected open on the right-hand chime signal circuits between the ACM and DSP.
diagnostics.next: Follow BD12–BD16 for the right-hand rear signal path.

diagnostics.finding: The missing sound is the forward-collision warning chime.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible causes include the collision-warning system, communications, GWM or IPC.
diagnostics.next: Continue with collision-warning diagnosis; this complaint does not establish a failed sounder.

verification.title: Confirm the relevant sound path
verification.body: Operate the system after connector repair or directed replacement. After ACM replacement, specifically confirm that chimes sound through the audio system.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record the original complaint, module-test results, circuit findings and whether operation returned or a guided routine remains necessary.

ACM removal and installation for SYNC audio when BD17 directs replacement.
ACM removal and installation for SYNC 2/SYNC 3 touchscreen audio when BD17 directs replacement.
Audio DSP removal and installation for the touchscreen-system BD19 replacement branch.
Further diagnosis when the complaint concerns the forward-collision warning chime.

applicability.equipment: Japan-market backup warning chime; Blind Spot Information System/Cross Traffic Alert; SYNC or touchscreen audio, as applicable

guides.title: Diagnose missing warning and seat-memory chimes
guides.summary: Trace missing collision, headlamps-on, ignition-engine-on and memory-stored chimes through sound, input and module checks to the appropriate diagnostic path.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) controls warning chimes from requests sent by other modules. Most warnings sound through the front audio speakers, with the cluster providing backup for required chimes. These tests determine whether investigation should follow the common chime function, an operating input, network communications or the system requesting the warning.
guides.why: A silent warning does not identify a failed speaker or cluster. The warning request and its operating conditions must be checked alongside the ability to produce sound.
searchTerms: forward collision warning chime not working
headlights left on no warning chime
seat memory saves without confirmation chime

when.summary: When a fitted warning or memory-stored feedback chime fails under its normal operating conditions.
notes: Confirm the concern is currently present before drawing component-replacement conclusions.

prepare.title: Scan-tool and vehicle information
prepare.detail: Have a scan tool capable of IPC self-testing and reading relevant module codes. The vehicle identification number (VIN) is needed if testing directs you to the IPC guided routine.

prepare.title: Establish valid conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge above 70%. Review previous repairs and use the warning-chime operation description to establish the complaint's operating conditions.

steps.title: Check the shared chime function
steps.body: All four tests begin with the driver safety-belt warning. With the belt unbuckled, transition ignition from OFF to RUN and listen for approximately 6 seconds. If the chime does not operate, use the VIN-specific IPC guided routine. Otherwise continue the selected complaint's checks.

steps.title: Check ignition-engine-on warning inputs
steps.body: For Test BG, open the driver door and observe the door-ajar indicator or message. No indication leads to Test AJ. On a vehicle fitted with an automatic transmission, shift through its ranges while observing the range display (PRNDL). A mismatch leads to Test V; matching indications allow IPC testing. This range-display branch does not apply to a manual-transmission vehicle; do not use it as a substitute for the matching warning conditions.

steps.title: Check whether memory actually stores
steps.body: For Test BH, verify that the memory-set procedure successfully changes the stored preferences. If it cannot, continue with front-seat diagnosis. Successful storage permits the chime investigation to continue to the IPC self-test.

steps.title: Run the cluster self-test
steps.body: Tests BE and BF reach this stage directly after a successful safety-belt chime check; BG and BH first require their input checks. Run the IPC self-test. Recorded diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) lead to the IPC DTC chart in the [diagnostic article](#/document/G1693940).

steps.title: Check gateway codes and follow the complaint
steps.body: If the IPC self-test records no codes, read Gateway Module A (GWM) continuous-memory DTCs. Any recorded codes lead to communications-network diagnosis. With none recorded, follow the complaint-specific destination below. This is a diagnostic handoff, not an instruction to replace a module.

watchFor.title: Chime priority
watchFor.body: A higher-priority warning can replace or delay another chime. Account for competing warnings when confirming the complaint.

watchFor.title: A partial pass
watchFor.body: A working safety-belt chime establishes sound operation for that check; it does not prove that another system's warning request reaches the cluster.

diagnostics.finding: The forward collision warning chime is inoperative.
diagnostics.meaning: Test BE applies to the fitted collision-warning system.
diagnostics.next: After passing the common chime check and finding no IPC or GWM codes, diagnose collision warning and collision avoidance.

diagnostics.finding: The headlamps-on warning chime is inoperative.
diagnostics.meaning: Test BF investigates the cluster, gateway and body-control path.
diagnostics.next: After the common checks pass without IPC or GWM codes, diagnose all body control module (BCM) DTCs.

diagnostics.finding: The ignition-engine-on warning chime is inoperative.
diagnostics.meaning: Test BG also checks door-ajar indication and, on an automatic-transmission vehicle, transmission-range indication.
diagnostics.next: After those checks pass and no IPC or GWM codes are recorded, diagnose any BCM DTCs.

diagnostics.finding: Memory preferences store successfully but the feedback chime is missing.
diagnostics.meaning: Test BH can proceed beyond the memory-set function check.
diagnostics.next: If IPC and GWM checks record no codes, diagnose any driver seat module (DSM) DTCs through Front Seats.

diagnostics.finding: The parking-aid chime is inoperative.
diagnostics.meaning: This separate complaint can involve parking-aid operation, communications, the gateway or cluster; it normally sounds through rear speakers.
diagnostics.next: Follow the parking-aid chime diagnostic path rather than assuming the front-speaker warning checks resolve it.

verification.title: Confirm the applicable preliminary checks
verification.body: Confirm the approximately 6-second safety-belt chime and, where applicable, correct door-ajar and range indications or successful memory storage.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic handoff
verification.body: Record IPC self-test results, GWM codes and the selected next procedure. These results direct further diagnosis; they do not establish a completed repair.

Operating conditions for each warning and memory-stored chime.
Network diagnosis when GWM codes are recorded.
Collision-warning diagnosis after Test BE preliminary checks pass.
BCM code diagnosis reached through Tests BF and BG.
Memory-set feature or DSM code diagnosis reached through Test BH.
Related system diagnosis for vehicles with rear parking aid.
Electrical diagnostic prerequisites and interpretation of current concerns.

applicability.equipment: Forward collision warning or memory seats for their respective tests; automatic transmission for the transmission-range display check

guides.title: Diagnose missing parking-aid, parking-brake, alarm and seatbelt chimes
guides.summary: Use working comparison chimes, warning inputs and module data to identify why a particular audible warning is missing.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) coordinates warning chimes, but most tones play through the audio speakers. Rear parking-aid warnings use the rear speakers; the cluster provides backup sound when the audio chime path fails. Diagnosis therefore checks both the warning request and where the sound is produced.
guides.why: A working comparison chime helps distinguish a general sound-path problem from a missing request. Belt-Minder also depends on buckle information, vehicle speed and configuration, so silence does not by itself identify a faulty buckle or module.

when.summary: When a parking-aid, parking-brake, perimeter-alarm or seatbelt warning chime fails under its operating conditions.
notes: Select BI, BJ, BK or BL by the actual complaint; these are separate diagnostic branches.

prepare.title: Scan-tool and vehicle setup
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting module self-tests, continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) and buckle live data. Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge above 70%. Have an administrator key and the vehicle identification number (VIN).

prepare.title: Controlled testing and restraint capability
prepare.detail: Arrange controlled vehicle-motion testing for the speed-dependent branches. Restraint faults and component replacement require the linked supplemental restraint system procedures and appropriate capability; buckle state is checked through scan data.

steps.title: Establish a comparison chime
steps.body: For BI, BJ and BK, check the safety-belt chime during the ignition OFF-to-RUN transition; it should sound for approximately 6 seconds. BI and BJ specify an unbuckled driver belt. If this baseline chime is absent, follow the VIN-specific IPC guided routine. BL instead begins with the headlamps-on comparison described below.

steps.title: BI: locate the sound and test parking aid
steps.body: Listen again during OFF-to-RUN. If the safety-belt chime comes from the IPC rather than audio speakers, check gateway module (GWM) continuous-memory codes first; recorded codes lead to Communications Network diagnosis. Otherwise continue to the parking assist control module (PAM) self-test. PAM codes lead to rear Parking Aid diagnosis. With none, run the IPC self-test: follow its code chart if codes appear, or diagnose the audible parking aid if none appear.

steps.title: BJ: confirm the parking-brake warning input
steps.body: Check the complaint while moving at least 10 km/h, applying the parking brake only enough to illuminate its indicator without damaging the rear brakes. If applying the brake does not illuminate the indicator, follow Test P. Otherwise run the IPC self-test, then check GWM memory codes. Follow the IPC chart or network diagnosis for recorded faults; if neither reports codes, diagnose all body control module (BCM) codes.

steps.title: BK: prove the perimeter alarm operates
steps.body: Arm the alarm with the remote key, wait approximately 15 seconds, then open the driver door using its interior handle. If the alarm does not sound after 12 seconds, diagnose the perimeter alarm. If it does, follow the same IPC self-test, GWM memory-code and BCM-code sequence used in BJ.

steps.title: BL: separate general chime and speed-input problems
steps.body: With ignition OFF, turn the headlamps on and open the driver door. No headlamps-on chime leads to the VIN-specific IPC routine. If it works, check the approximately 6-second safety-belt chime at OFF-to-RUN. If that chime works, a Belt-Minder complaint requires a working speedometer; failure leads to Test D. Then run the IPC self-test. A safety-belt-chime complaint goes directly to that self-test; an absent comparison safety-belt chime proceeds to the BCM test.

steps.title: BL: follow module results and buckle data
steps.body: After a clear IPC self-test where required, test the BCM, then the restraints control module (RCM), then check GWM memory codes. Stop at recorded faults and use BCM, supplemental restraint system or network diagnosis respectively. If clear, monitor the RCM buckle parameter identifications (PIDs), SBELT_D_ST and SBLT_P_ST. Each must display BUCKLED and UNBUCKLED as its belt is fastened and released. A failed comparison directs replacement of the affected buckle using its complete procedure.

steps.title: BL: establish the seating-position configuration
steps.body: Use an administrator key to check Belt-Minder activation for the affected seat. MyKey forces Belt-Minder on and prevents disabling it; a previously disabled administrator setting remains disabled when using an administrator key. Activate the feature if off. With earlier checks passed and activation confirmed, sounding above 10 km/h with the belt unfastened is normal. Always sounding with the belt fastened, or never sounding above that speed with it unfastened, directs RCM replacement through the complete restraint procedure.

watchFor.title: A working backup can conceal the failed sound path
watchFor.body: Hearing a tone from the cluster does not establish that the audio speakers are producing their chimes.

watchFor.title: Competing warnings
watchFor.body: The IPC prioritizes chimes; a higher-priority request can replace or delay another warning.

notes: Missing turn-signal/hazard or turn-signal-left-on chimes follow a separate path involving turn-signal indication, communication, BCM, GWM and IPC concerns. BI–BL do not resolve that complaint.

diagnostics.finding: The rear parking-aid chime is absent but the comparison chime operates.
diagnostics.meaning: The parking-aid request and its sound route still need checking.
diagnostics.next: Follow BI through sound location, PAM and IPC tests.

diagnostics.finding: The brake indicator or perimeter alarm fails its functional check.
diagnostics.meaning: The underlying warning input or alarm operation is not established.
diagnostics.next: Use Test P for the brake indicator or perimeter-alarm diagnosis before continuing the chime branch.

diagnostics.finding: A buckle PID does not follow fastening and release.
diagnostics.meaning: BL8's buckle-state comparison has failed after the preceding module checks.
diagnostics.next: Follow the affected buckle replacement procedure; do not substitute direct probing of restraint circuits.

verification.title: Repeat the complaint-specific check
verification.body: Recheck the relevant warning under the same ignition, alarm, parking-brake or Belt-Minder conditions used to establish the fault.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record chime location, relevant module codes, buckle PID responses and the administrator-key activation setting, distinguishing a repaired fault from a configuration change.

procedures.purpose: Diagnosis: BI rear parking-aid chime, BJ parking-brake chime, BK perimeter-alarm chime and BL safety-belt/Belt-Minder; includes referrals to Tests P and D.
Diagnostic prerequisites and precautions against unnecessary component replacement.

Supplemental restraint system diagnosis when the RCM self-test records codes.

Check and activate Belt-Minder for the affected seating position.

applicability.equipment: Rear parking aid for Test BI; perimeter alarm for Test BK

guides.title: Trace missing parking-aid chimes and related module communication faults
guides.summary: Use module tests, timed code rechecks and targeted connector inspections to identify the next repair or guided diagnostic step.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) controls warning chimes using messages from other modules. Parking-aid chimes sound through the rear speakers, while the cluster provides backup for required chimes if audio-system chime output fails. A missing sound can therefore involve message delivery as well as audio output. These tests distinguish restraints, cluster, parking-assist and radio communication paths.
guides.why: A lost-communication code identifies missing information, not a proven failed module. Battery condition, network faults, gateway operation, connections and configuration can all affect delivery. Checking both the sending and receiving modules prevents a stored communication complaint from becoming an unjustified replacement.

when.summary: Use when an observable chime or display concern accompanies a matching module communication code.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of network tests, module self-tests and retrieving continuous-memory codes from all modules. Check battery and charging-system operation and verify battery state of charge exceeds 70%.

prepare.title: Plan connector access
prepare.detail: Connector inspection requires terminal-repair capability. Restraints control module (RCM) access requires supplemental restraint system (SRS) service capability and the linked SRS/RCM precautions before disconnection.

steps.title: Confirm the symptom before following a code
steps.body: With ignition on, verify an observable concern. BU, BV, BW and BX all stop if none is present: clear the diagnostic trouble code (DTC) and record normal operation at this time. High network traffic or an intermittent condition may explain the stored code.

steps.title: Test the sending module for the chosen path
steps.body: BU network-tests and self-tests the RCM; its self-test codes lead to SRS diagnosis. BV tests the IPC; codes lead to its DTC chart. BW network-tests the parking aid module (PAM), then self-tests the body control module (BCM), which incorporates parking aid. BCM codes require the fitted rear-parking-aid or SYNC 3 camera-equipped parking-aid diagnosis. BX tests the audio front control module (ACM); codes lead to network diagnosis. Any failed network response also requires network diagnosis.

steps.title: Screen the gateway and recheck the receiving module
steps.body: Check gateway module (GWM) continuous-memory codes and diagnose any through Communications Network. Next, self-test the information center module (ICM) for BV or IPC for the other paths. U3003:16 or U3003:17 requires that receiver’s DTC chart. Clear codes, wait 10 seconds and repeat its self-test. If the original code disappears, the system operates correctly at this time. BW continuation requires vehicle-specific routing, with gateway screening treated as a prerequisite.

steps.title: Use the connector inspection whenever directed
steps.body: Switch ignition off and follow the selected module’s access precautions. Inspect its connectors for corrosion, damaged or bent pins and pushed-out pins. Replace affected connectors or terminals and clean module pins as directed. Reconnect until seated and latched, then operate the system. Address the cause of connector damage. If the concern remains, check applicable technical service bulletins (TSBs); follow an applicable bulletin instead of continuing the test.

steps.title: BU: Localize persistent U0151:00
steps.body: For this restraints communication path, clear all codes, cycle ignition off/on, wait 10 seconds and retrieve continuous-memory codes from all modules. U0151:87 in the BCM selects RCM connector inspection at BU8; its absence selects IPC inspection at BU9. If the concern survives inspection and no TSB applies, BU8 directs RCM replacement, while BU9 stops for the VIN-specific IPC guided routine.

steps.title: BV: Localize persistent U0155:00
steps.body: Clear all codes, cycle ignition off/on, wait 10 seconds and retrieve all-module continuous-memory codes. U0155:87 in the BCM selects IPC inspection at BV8; its absence selects ICM inspection at BV9. With the concern still present and no applicable TSB, the IPC branch requires its VIN-specific guided routine; the ICM branch directs replacement.

steps.title: BW: Keep parking-assist diagnosis within its routing
steps.body: At BW7, persistent U0159:00 calls for BCM connector inspection and an operational recheck. If the concern remains without an applicable TSB, stop for the VIN-specific guided routine. BW8 is a separate IPC connector check when vehicle-specific routing directs it; an unresolved result requires the IPC guided routine. U0184 does not provide a route into BW8.

steps.title: BX: Follow the radio path and its final recheck
steps.body: Persistent U0184:00 leads to ACM connector inspection. If the concern remains and no TSB applies, replace the ACM using the fitted SYNC or touchscreen procedure. Clear codes and repeat the IPC self-test. If U0184:00 remains, BX8 directs IPC connector inspection, an operational check and TSB review; an unresolved result requires the VIN-specific IPC guided routine.

watchFor.title: Recent module replacement
watchFor.body: Incorrect or omitted Programmable Module Installation (PMI) can leave configuration wrong. Investigate that history before condemning another module.

watchFor.title: Chime priority
watchFor.body: A higher-priority warning can replace or delay a lower-priority chime; establish the actual missing function before testing.

notes: A replacement decision begins the linked removal-and-installation procedure. A VIN-specific guided routine is a stopping point here, including the unresolved BW7 outcome.

diagnostics.finding: DTC U0155:00 is stored in the ICM.
diagnostics.meaning: IPC messages arriving through the gateway have been missing for 5 seconds or longer.
diagnostics.next: Follow BV to distinguish the IPC, communication path and ICM.

diagnostics.finding: DTC U0159:00 is stored in the IPC.
diagnostics.meaning: Parking-assist messages from the BCM-integrated PAM through the gateway have been missing for 5 seconds or longer.
diagnostics.next: Follow BW’s parking-aid checks and vehicle-specific continuation.

diagnostics.finding: DTC U0184:00 is stored in the IPC.
diagnostics.meaning: Radio messages from the ACM through the gateway have been missing for 5 seconds or longer.
diagnostics.next: Use BX, including its post-ACM IPC recheck.

diagnostics.finding: DTC U0212:00 is stored in the IPC.
diagnostics.meaning: Steering column control module (SCCM) messages through the gateway have been missing for 5 seconds or longer.
diagnostics.next: Continue SCCM/network diagnosis, considering battery voltage, gateway and IPC as possible contributors; BU–BX do not resolve this code.

verification.title: Check operation after reconnecting
verification.body: Operate the affected system after each directed connector repair. A disappearing concern supports a connection-related cause; correct that cause rather than relying solely on reseating.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic endpoint
verification.body: Record the symptom, originating module, exact codes, timed self-test results and BCM subtype-code findings where used. State whether operation returned, replacement was directed or a guided routine remains pending.

guides.title: Activate or deactivate the driver or passenger Belt-Minder reminder
guides.summary: Change one front-seat Belt-Minder setting through a timed buckle sequence and confirm acceptance at the safety-belt warning indicator.
guides.introduction: Belt-Minder provides a reminder associated with front-seat belt use. The driver and front passenger settings are controlled independently. This procedure changes the selected reminder setting through the belt buckle and ignition sequence; the safety-belt warning indicator provides the confirmation. A diagnostic scan tool can also perform activation or deactivation.
guides.why: Timing and buckle speed are part of the command. If the buckle sequence is too fast, the restraints control module (RCM) may miss an input. Keeping the other seating position unbuckled also preserves the required conditions while changing the selected seat.

when.summary: When the driver or front passenger Belt-Minder setting needs to be activated or deactivated.
notes: A MyKey programmed key prevents deactivation, re-enables a previously disabled reminder and prevents its usual 5-minute timeout.

prepare.title: Read the required safety information
prepare.detail: Read the [general service safety precautions](#/document/G1693189) before beginning, then establish the parked, engine-off starting conditions below.

prepare.title: Choose the seat and method
prepare.detail: Select the driver or front passenger position. Use the manual sequence below or a diagnostic scan tool. For the manual method, be ready to watch the indicator and follow the timing windows.

steps.title: Secure the vehicle and establish the starting state
steps.body: Apply the parking brake. Select Park for an automatic transmission or Neutral for a manual transmission. Switch the ignition OFF and unbuckle both front safety belts.

steps.title: Wait for the initial indicator to go out
steps.body: Turn the ignition to RUN without starting the engine. Wait until the safety-belt warning indicator turns off, approximately 1 minute. The next two buckle-sequence steps must both finish within 30 seconds of that event.

steps.title: Enter the three-cycle sequence
steps.body: At the selected seat, buckle and unbuckle the belt 3 times at a moderate rate, ending unbuckled. Leave the other seat’s belt unbuckled. After this step, the warning indicator turns off.

steps.title: Enter the final cycle
steps.body: Within 7 seconds of the indicator turning off, buckle and unbuckle the selected belt once more at a moderate rate. Keep this action within the overall 30-second window.

steps.title: Observe confirmation
steps.body: Starting from its off state, the warning indicator flashes for 4.5 seconds to confirm activation or deactivation. After that confirmation, the procedure is complete. Change the other seat separately if required.

watchFor.title: Rushed buckle inputs
watchFor.body: A rapid sequence can go unrecognized and require repetition. Use a moderate, deliberate rate while still meeting the timing limits.

watchFor.title: Restricted-key behavior
watchFor.body: Belt-Minder remaining active with a MyKey programmed key is expected behavior, not evidence that the reminder system has failed.

notes: The same confirmation pattern is used for enabling and disabling; the flashes alone do not distinguish the resulting setting.

diagnostics.finding: The confirmation flash does not occur.
diagnostics.meaning: Successful completion has not been confirmed; a missed buckle input or timing requirement may explain it.
diagnostics.next: Re-establish the starting conditions and repeat the sequence at a moderate rate, observing both timing windows.

verification.title: Confirm acceptance
verification.body: Observe the specified 4.5-second warning-indicator flash after the final buckle/unbuckle action.

verification.title: Record the selected position
verification.body: Record which seat was changed, the intended setting and whether the confirmation appeared.

procedures.purpose: Independent driver or front passenger Belt-Minder activation/deactivation, timing and confirmation.
General service safety precautions to review before changing the reminder setting.

referenceReview.summary: Replaced unlinked section or procedure references with exact current local destinations; retained primary scope and diagnostic thresholds.

guides.title: Remove and replace the optional Information Center Module
guides.summary: Release the center instrument-panel trim, disconnect the optional Information Center Module and replace or refit its screw-mounted assembly.
guides.introduction: The Information Center Module (ICM) is an optional unit mounted to the instrument panel center finish panel. Access comes through the clipped trim panels, after which screws release the module itself. Understanding that arrangement helps you separate trim removal from module removal and avoid pulling against the electrical connection behind the panel.
guides.why: The trim is retained by clips, while the module is secured by screws and connected to the vehicle wiring. Each attachment needs to be released in sequence. Also establish which display or warning function is involved before choosing this repair: the message center belongs to the instrument panel cluster (IPC), which also controls warning chimes.

when.summary: When the fitted ICM requires removal, replacement or access behind its mounting panel.

prepare.title: Trim and screw tools
prepare.detail: Use an interior trim remover and suitable tools for the module screws. Be ready to support the center panel while disconnecting its electrical connector.

prepare.title: Confirm the fitted assembly
prepare.detail: Check that the vehicle has the optional ICM and identify its connector and screw locations in the removal illustration.

steps.title: Release the right-hand instrument-panel trim
steps.body: Use the interior trim remover to release the clips and remove the right-hand trim panel. This opens the prescribed access path to the center finish panel.

steps.title: Remove the center finish panel
steps.body: Release its clips with the trim remover. As the panel comes free, disconnect the ICM electrical connector so the harness does not remain attached while the panel is removed.

steps.title: Separate the module from the panel
steps.body: Remove the ICM mounting screws shown in the illustration and lift the module from its mounting position. Keep the screws available for reassembly.

steps.title: Install the module and restore the trim
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: position and secure the ICM, reconnect its electrical connector and refit the center finish panel. Reinstall the right-hand trim panel, ensuring the clips engage.

watchFor.title: A panel that remains attached
watchFor.body: Check for retained clips or the electrical connection before pulling farther. The connector is disconnected during center-panel removal.

diagnostics.finding: The complaint concerns message-center warnings or warning chimes.
diagnostics.meaning: Those functions involve the IPC and, for many chimes, the audio-system speakers; the complaint alone does not identify the optional ICM.
diagnostics.next: Establish the affected component before replacing the center-panel module.

verification.title: Confirm physical reassembly
verification.body: Check that the module screws are installed, the electrical connector is attached and both trim panels are secured by their clips.

verification.title: Record the work performed
verification.body: Record whether the ICM was replaced or refitted, separately from the diagnosis of the original complaint.

procedures.purpose: ICM removal from and installation into the center finish panel.
Right-hand trim and center finish-panel removal, connector disconnection and reinstallation.
Identify the IPC message center when distinguishing a warning-display complaint.
Identify IPC and audio-system responsibilities for warning chimes.

guides.title: Replace the instrument cluster lens
guides.summary: Remove the instrument cluster, exchange its screw-and-tab-retained lens, and reinstall the cluster using its required access and scan-tool procedures.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) lens is the transparent cover through which the driver reads the gauges, indicators and message center. Lens replacement changes that cover while retaining the cluster behind it. Although the lens itself has a short removal sequence, reaching it requires removal of the IPC and several surrounding trim panels. The cluster is also an electronic module, so its parent removal procedure includes scan-tool preparation and an odometer record.
guides.why: Screws and retaining tabs both secure the lens; releasing only one type of attachment leaves the cover restrained. The surrounding trim also uses clips and electrical connections that must be dealt with in sequence. Keeping the original odometer information and following the IPC scan-tool instructions preserves the distinction between a cover repair and replacement of the electronic cluster.

when.summary: When the IPC lens requires removal or replacement and the cluster can be removed using its complete procedure.
notes: Replacing the lens does not repair the electronics that operate gauges, messages or warning chimes.
If the IPC itself is also being replaced, its configuration must be uploaded before removal and downloaded after installation.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim and module removal
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover and a diagnostic scan tool capable of the IPC PMI process. Programmable Module Installation (PMI) is the scan-tool sequence specified by the parent IPC procedure.

prepare.title: Record the odometer
prepare.detail: Record the original IPC odometer value. If display failure prevents this, perform the diagnostic routine. If the value still cannot be obtained, the customer supplies an approximate value.

steps.title: Begin the IPC procedure
steps.body: Follow [IPC removal and installation](#/document/G1693928), beginning its scan-tool PMI instructions and recording the odometer. Keep the original cluster identified if only its lens is being changed.

steps.title: Remove the surrounding panels
steps.body: Remove the instrument panel center finish panel using its referenced procedure. Release the left-hand instrument panel trim, then remove the lighting switch panel and left-hand finish panel, disconnecting their electrical connectors as directed.

steps.title: Free and remove the cluster
steps.body: Position the lower instrument panel cover aside. Remove the IPC trim panel and detach the gap hider from the upper steering-column trim cover. Remove the IPC bolts, release its clips and disconnect its electrical connector.

steps.title: Exchange the lens
steps.body: Following the [IPC lens procedure](#/document/G1743568), remove the screws, release the retaining tabs and remove the lens. Fit the replacement by reversing that sequence, making sure its tabs engage before completing the screw attachment.

steps.title: Reinstall the IPC and trim
steps.body: Reverse the cluster removal sequence, restoring its connector, clips and bolts, the gap hider, and the surrounding panels and connectors. Use the separate fastener specifications in the IPC procedure; the trim and cluster attachments do not all share one torque.

steps.title: Finish the electronic sequence
steps.body: Complete IPC PMI following the scan-tool prompts. If the electronic module was replaced as part of the work, download the configuration saved from the original module.

watchFor.title: Lens still restrained
watchFor.body: Resistance after removing the screws can mean retaining tabs remain engaged. Release them before separating the lens.

watchFor.title: Unresolved warning messages
watchFor.body: The message center displays information received from vehicle systems. A warning message is not evidence that the replacement lens is faulty.

notes: The lens illustration shows its attachment points; vehicle access is covered by the separate IPC procedure.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly
verification.body: Check that the lens screws and tabs, IPC connector and mountings, gap hider and removed trim have all been restored.

verification.title: Retain the odometer record
verification.body: Keep the original odometer reading, or identify the customer-supplied value as approximate when the specified diagnostic route could not recover it.

verification.title: Complete PMI
verification.body: Confirm the IPC scan-tool sequence has been completed, including configuration transfer when the module was replaced.

procedures.purpose: IPC lens removal and installation after the cluster is removed.
IPC access, removal, installation, odometer recording and scan-tool PMI requirements.

guides.title: Replace and configure the instrument panel cluster
guides.summary: Capture the cluster configuration and odometer information before removal, then install the replacement and complete scan-tool programming.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) presents gauges, indicators and message-center information using inputs from vehicle systems. It also controls warning-chime requests. Replacement therefore involves both physical removal and electronic setup. The surrounding trim provides access, while programmable module installation (PMI) transfers the configuration needed by a new cluster.
guides.why: Configuration information must be uploaded before the original module is removed and downloaded to the replacement afterward. The odometer reading also needs to be recorded before access to the original cluster is lost. Working through the trim sequence exposes concealed clips, connectors and the steering-column gap hider without pulling against attached parts.

when.summary: After diagnosis establishes that the IPC needs replacement, or when the cluster must be removed for access.
notes: A warning displayed by the cluster can originate in another vehicle system; the message alone does not establish cluster failure.

prepare.title: Arrange module-programming capability
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool capable of carrying out IPC PMI and following its on-screen instructions. Begin replacement work while the original module is still installed.

prepare.title: Prepare trim access
prepare.detail: Use an interior trim remover and suitable controlled-tightening tools. Have the center finish-panel procedure available and keep the different trim fasteners identifiable.

steps.title: Begin PMI and record mileage
steps.body: Use the scan tool to begin IPC PMI. When installing a new module, upload the original configuration before removal. Record the original odometer value; if its display has failed, follow the retrieval branch below.

steps.title: Open the center and left trim areas
steps.body: Remove the instrument panel center finish panel using its linked procedure. Release the clips and remove the left-hand instrument panel trim panel with the interior trim remover.

steps.title: Remove the switch and finish panels
steps.body: Remove the lighting-switch panel bolts, release its clips and disconnect its electrical connector. Then remove the left-hand finish-panel bolt, release that panel’s clips and disconnect its connector.

steps.title: Expose the cluster surround
steps.body: Release the lower instrument panel cover clips and position the cover aside. Remove the IPC trim-panel bolts, release its clips and detach the gap hider from the upper steering-column trim cover.

steps.title: Remove the IPC
steps.body: Remove its bolts, release the clips and disconnect the electrical connector as the cluster is removed. Keep the connector accessible for installation.

steps.title: Install the cluster and restore the trim
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, reconnecting the cluster and panel connectors and restoring the gap hider. Apply each procedure step’s specified tightening value to its corresponding fasteners.

steps.title: Complete electronic installation
steps.body: Use the diagnostic scan tool to finish IPC PMI following the on-screen instructions. For a new cluster, complete the configuration download required after installation.

watchFor.title: Different tightening units
watchFor.body: The IPC mounting specification uses lb.ft, while adjacent trim specifications use lb.in. Read the value and unit together.

watchFor.title: Chime complaints
watchFor.body: Most warning chimes sound through audio speakers. The IPC sounds the turn-signal tick and provides backup chimes, so a chime complaint needs diagnosis before cluster replacement.

diagnostics.finding: The original odometer value cannot be read because the IPC display has failed.
diagnostics.meaning: Direct recording of the original reading is unavailable.
diagnostics.next: Perform the specified diagnostic routine. If it still cannot obtain the value, obtain the customer’s approximate odometer value and identify it as an estimate.

verification.title: Confirm physical installation
verification.body: Check restoration of disconnected connectors, trim clips, fasteners and the steering-column gap hider.

verification.title: Record programming and odometer information
verification.body: Record completion of the scan-tool PMI process and the odometer value used, including whether it came from the original display, diagnostic retrieval or a customer estimate.

procedures.purpose: IPC removal and installation, original configuration capture, odometer handling and completion of PMI.
Instrument panel center finish-panel removal and installation required for cluster access.

guides.title: Replace the horn
guides.summary: Replace the horn assembly through the left front wheel opening, then restore its electrical connection and mounting.
guides.introduction: The horn converts electrical power into an audible warning. Pressing the steering-wheel horn control sends a ground signal through the clockspring to the body control module (BCM). The BCM operates a relay that supplies power to the horn. This repair replaces the sound-producing assembly, reached by removing the left front fender splash shield.
guides.why: A silent horn does not identify which part of that electrical chain has failed. Establishing the fault before replacement avoids changing a working horn. During installation, secure mounting and a fully connected electrical plug are both necessary for a successful repair.

when.summary: When fault diagnosis identifies the horn assembly as requiring replacement.
notes: This is a component replacement procedure; a failure to sound can also involve the horn control circuit.

prepare.title: Plan wheel-opening access
prepare.detail: Arrange suitable vehicle support and the capability to remove and refit the left front wheel and tire. Have the wheel-and-tire procedure available for its separate fastening requirements.

prepare.title: Prepare fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have tools for the splash-shield retainers and horn bolt, plus a torque wrench suitable for the horn mounting specification.

steps.title: Expose the horn
steps.body: Follow the [fender splash shield procedure](#/document/G1693247): remove the left front wheel and tire, release the shield retainers, and remove the shield. This opens access to the horn and its connector.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the assembly
steps.body: Disconnect the horn electrical connector, then remove the mounting bolt and horn. Use the [horn illustration](#/document/G1688199) to identify the connector and common mounting point.

steps.title: Fit the replacement horn
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, securing the horn in its mounting position and reconnecting the electrical plug. Tighten the horn bolt to 106 lb.in (12 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the wheel opening
steps.body: Refit the splash shield and its retainers, then reinstall the wheel and tire using the applicable wheel procedure. Complete this access work before returning the vehicle to use.

watchFor.title: Unresolved silence
watchFor.body: If the horn still does not sound, return to electrical diagnosis. Replacing the horn does not establish that its power supply or command circuit is operating.

notes: The steering-wheel horn control operates through the clockspring and BCM; this replacement is performed at the horn in the front wheel-opening area.

diagnostics.finding: The horn does not sound when commanded.
diagnostics.meaning: The symptom can arise anywhere along the switch, clockspring, BCM, relay or horn path.
diagnostics.next: Identify the failed part of the circuit before authorizing horn replacement.

verification.title: Installation complete
verification.body: Confirm the horn mounting bolt is tightened, the connector is engaged, and the splash shield and wheel are refitted.

verification.title: Normal horn response
verification.body: Operate the normal horn control and confirm that the horn sounds.

guides.title: Diagnose silent or false rear parking aid alerts
guides.summary: Trace rear parking aid complaints through operating settings, network messages, shared sensor wiring and individual sensor checks.
guides.introduction: Rear parking aid uses ultrasonic sensors to detect nearby objects and request warning tones through the rear speakers. The parking assist control module (PAM) shares its housing with the body control module (BCM), but communicates separately. Diagnosis must distinguish sensor faults from missing gear information, disabled settings and audio problems.
guides.why: The sensors share power and return circuits. One shorted sensor or damaged shared wire can affect the whole system, so replacing the sensor named by a code is not always justified.
searchTerms: parking sensors beep with no obstacle

when.summary: When rear parking aid is silent, produces unexplained tones or records a diagnostic trouble code.
notes: Confirm the complaint is present before following a test toward component replacement.

prepare.title: Prepare for electrical diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, Rotunda Flex Probes and the specified wiring diagrams. Verify battery state of charge exceeds 70% and check charging-system operation.

prepare.title: Inspect before disconnecting
prepare.detail: Check previous repairs, harness damage and connector seating. Follow each test's ignition and isolation instructions; resistance measurements require an unpowered, isolated circuit.

steps.title: Establish the correct diagnostic route
steps.body: Record the complaint and diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Inspect the bumper sensors and harness. Use the symptom and DTC charts in [Parking Aid](#/document/G1693946): circuit faults take priority over performance complaints, and a module that will not communicate requires network diagnosis.

steps.title: Test A: trace missing audible assistance
steps.body: With ignition ON, run the network test, then PAM and instrument panel cluster (IPC) self-tests, following any recorded faults before continuing. Confirm parking aid is enabled. Apply the parking brake, select REVERSE and check that the PAM transmission-range parameter, TRANSGR, reads YES. An incorrect result redirects diagnosis to the fitted transmission. Next, switch ignition OFF, open the driver door and turn the headlamps ON. A missing warning chime redirects diagnosis to the instrumentation and chime system; a working chime leads to the BCM checks.

steps.title: Test B: isolate a sensor short
steps.body: For B1B58:11, inspect the bumper harness first. If sound, progressively disconnect sensors in this order: left outer, left inner, right inner, right outer. Switch ignition OFF before each disconnection, then ON to clear codes and repeat the PAM self-test. If B1B58:11 disappears, replace the sensor just disconnected.

steps.title: Test B: check the shared supply wiring
steps.body: If the code remains with all sensors disconnected, switch ignition OFF and disconnect BCM connector C2280D. Follow the pin table to measure supply-to-ground and supply-to-return resistance. Each must exceed 10,000 ohms. Repair a failed circuit; passing results lead to the BCM connector checks.

steps.title: Test C: distinguish open wiring from sensor failure
steps.body: B1B44:14, B1B46:14, B1B48:14 and B1B50:14 identify right outer, right inner, left outer and left inner sensor circuits respectively. Multiple sensor codes first require bumper-harness inspection. With ignition OFF, disconnect the suspect sensors and BCM connector. Using the position-specific tables, each sensor circuit must measure less than 3 ohms end-to-end, and its signal circuit more than 10,000 ohms to ground. Repair failures. If wiring passes, replace implicated sensors when fewer than all are affected; faults at all sensors lead to BCM checks.

steps.title: Complete the module decision
steps.body: With ignition OFF, inspect BCM and related inline connectors. Correct corrosion, damaged terminals and pushed-out pins, then reconnect securely and operate the system. If the concern persists, check applicable technical service bulletins before the test's BCM replacement decision. Replacement requires programmable module installation (PMI). If reconnection restores operation, repair the underlying connector problem.

watchFor.title: False tones without codes
watchFor.body: Clean dirty sensors and bumper with high-pressure water; let ice between sensors and bezels melt. Correct seating and check elevation alignment. A missing, damaged or misaligned isolator ring requires sensor replacement.

watchFor.title: Restricted-key behavior
watchFor.body: A MyKey restricted key hides the parking aid menu and prevents deactivation. That behavior is normal.

notes: Use the 6R80 or MT82 transmission references only where fitted; the MT82 reference does not cover the 5.2L application.
Object shape, surface, weather and obstructions can affect detection; moving objects may not be detected.

diagnostics.finding: A sensor DTC identifies a short to battery or internal failure.
diagnostics.meaning: The chart separates subtype :12 signal-voltage faults from subtype :96 internal-failure reports.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test D for :12 or Test E for :96 rather than extending Test C.

diagnostics.finding: A lost-communication or invalid-data DTC is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Missing messages and received but faulted data require different investigations.
diagnostics.next: Use the named network test for communication loss. For invalid data, repair non-network codes in the chart-specified modules first, then diagnose any remaining observable symptom.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U2024:41 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The configuration checksum check failed.
diagnostics.next: Clear and repeat the PAM self-test. If repeated, install As-Built data from Professional Technician Society as directed, then retest; another recurrence leads to BCM replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U2100:00 or U2101:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Configuration is incomplete or incompatible.
diagnostics.next: Check service history. Recent module work leads to As-Built configuration; without recent service, the chart directs BCM replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3000:44, U3000:45, U3000:46 or U3000:49 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The module reports a memory or internal electronic fault.
diagnostics.next: For U3000:49, address other codes first. Clear and repeat the self-test; recurrence of the applicable code leads to BCM replacement.

verification.title: Confirm the diagnostic result
verification.body: Restore connections, repeat the relevant self-test and operate the system to determine whether the original concern remains.

verification.title: Record the evidence
verification.body: Record returning codes, sensor positions, measured circuit results and the observed response after repair.
