guides.title: Diagnose rear parking sensors and communication faults
guides.summary: Use sensor circuit tests, live distance readings and module communication checks to identify why rear parking assistance is disabled or unreliable.
guides.introduction: Rear parking aid uses ultrasonic echoes to estimate obstacle distance and request warning tones through the rear speakers while reversing. Its sensors share power and ground but return individual signals. The parking assist control module (PAM) is integral to the body control module (BCM), yet communicates as a separate network node. A sensor or communication fault can disable the system.
guides.why: Several sensor codes can point to shared bumper wiring rather than several failed sensors. Communication codes identify missing messages, not necessarily a failed transmitting module. Comparing live readings, reproducing faults and checking connections prevents unsupported replacement.
searchTerms: rear parking sensors not detecting objects
rear parking sensor distance reading incorrect

when.summary: Use for rear parking-aid faults involving the listed sensor codes or missing powertrain, braking or steering messages.
notes: Confirm parking aid is enabled and record whether the complaint is currently present.

prepare.title: Provide scan and circuit-testing capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of module self-tests, network tests and live distance readings, plus a digital multimeter and proper terminal probes. Diagnostic Methods specifies Rotunda Flex Probes (NUD105-R025F) or Terminal Probe Kit 418-S035. Have access to a known-good sensor and the Azimuth System Check test-object guidance.

prepare.title: Preserve evidence and protect circuits
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation and state of charge above 70%. Record codes with their originating modules before clearing. Verify sensor and module connectors are seated and latched before disconnecting. Isolate and unpower circuits for resistance measurements; follow the specified ignition states for voltage tests.

steps.title: Select the sensor branch from the self-test
steps.body: Perform the PAM self-test using [Parking Aid](#/document/G1693946). Test D addresses the listed :12 codes; Test E addresses the listed :96 codes. Route other codes through the PAM diagnostic trouble code (DTC) chart. Multiple sensor faults in Test D require inspecting the rear bumper harness for opens, shorts, grounding damage and corrosion before individual circuit decisions.

steps.title: Test sensor wiring before replacement
steps.body: D3 disconnects the suspect sensors and BCM connector before checking signal circuits for unwanted voltage. Repair any short found. Then isolate and unpower the circuits for D4's signal-to-supply resistance check. A failed check directs circuit repair. If wiring passes and only some sensors have the specified codes, replace those sensors. If all have them, continue to the BCM connector endpoint.

steps.title: Compare live distance readings with the surroundings
steps.body: For Test E, clean the bumper and sensors with high-pressure water, confirm flush mounting and clear the detection area. Monitor the distance parameter identifications (PIDs): LRI_DIST, LRO_DIST, RRI_DIST and RRO_DIST. Each should read 2,540 mm (100 in) with no object present. Then move a suitable test object into and out of each detection zone; the reading should approximately follow its distance from the bumper.

steps.title: Use substitution to separate sensor and system faults
steps.body: If either distance check fails, switch ignition off and fit a known-good sensor using the sensor replacement procedure. Switch ignition on, clear codes and repeat the PAM self-test. A resolved concern directs new-sensor installation; a remaining concern leads to E5's BCM connector checks. Passing both distance checks also leads to E5, where the current complaint must be reassessed.

steps.title: Establish the powertrain communication path
steps.body: F1 first requires a scan-tool vehicle session; failure leads to the dedicated no-communication procedure. F2 clears PAM codes, operates the system and checks continuous-memory codes. Continue to F3 only when U0100:00 returns. Perform the powertrain control module (PCM) key-on, engine-off self-test and diagnose any resulting engine codes first. With none, clear all codes, cycle ignition and wait 10 seconds. U0100 or U0101 in another module selects the PCM connector endpoint; otherwise select the BCM endpoint.

steps.title: Check braking-system communication independently
steps.body: For U0121:00, G1 requires an observable symptom. Without one, clear the code and record normal operation at that time. With a symptom, network-test the anti-lock brake system (ABS) module and gateway module (GWM); a failure requires network diagnosis. Next, run the ABS self-test and diagnose its codes in ABS and Stability Control. Gateway memory codes require network diagnosis before continuing.

steps.title: Locate a returning ABS communication concern
steps.body: After those checks pass, clear codes, operate parking aid and recheck PAM memory. If U0121:00 does not return, operation is currently correct, although the fault may have been intermittent. If it returns, clear all codes, cycle ignition and wait 10 seconds before scanning every module. U0121 in another module directs the ABS connector endpoint; otherwise continue to the BCM endpoint.

steps.title: Complete the selected module endpoint
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect the selected module's connectors and related inline connections. Replace damaged or displaced terminals, repair corrosion and clean module pins. Reconnect securely and retest. If the concern persists, check applicable technical service bulletins and follow any relevant bulletin before replacement. Otherwise follow the selected module replacement decision and any vehicle identification number (VIN)-guided handoff. BCM replacement requires programmable module installation (PMI). Choose the PCM replacement article for the fitted engine. Follow the full BCM replacement sequence when that endpoint is reached; configuration, key handling and equipped-system initialization extend beyond physically swapping the module.

watchFor.title: Conditions that distort detection
watchFor.body: Ice, dirt, incorrect sensor alignment, heavy precipitation and obstructing accessories can alter detection. An object's material and shape also affect its ultrasonic echo.

watchFor.title: An absent complaint
watchFor.body: Do not replace a module merely because an old communication code remains in memory when its diagnostic complaint cannot be reproduced.

notes: An isolated returning U0101:00 needs its confirmed diagnostic path. Absence of U0100:00 does not establish normal operation while U0101:00 persists.

diagnostics.finding: PAM records B1B44:12, B1B46:12, B1B48:12 or B1B50:12.
diagnostics.meaning: Test D checks the affected sensor signal circuit for unwanted voltage and a short to its supply circuit.
diagnostics.next: Follow D1–D5, checking shared bumper wiring first when multiple sensors report faults.

diagnostics.finding: PAM records B1B44:96, B1B46:96, B1B48:96 or B1B50:96.
diagnostics.meaning: These identify right outer, right inner, left outer and left inner sensor internal-failure or incorrect attenuation-time concerns, respectively; attenuation describes signal decay.
diagnostics.next: Use Test E's mounting, distance and known-good substitution checks before condemning a sensor.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0100:00 returns in PAM after clearing and operating the system.
diagnostics.meaning: PAM has detected missing PCM messages for 5 seconds or more.
diagnostics.next: Follow F3–F6, using engine self-test results and other modules' codes to select the correct connector checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0101:00 remains without returning U0100:00.
diagnostics.meaning: The recorded concern is lost transmission-control communication; it does not establish PCM or BCM failure.
diagnostics.next: Record the originating module and stop this isolated-code path for the correct confirmed diagnostic. Do not continue automatically to F3 or module replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0121:00 is recorded in PAM.
diagnostics.meaning: ABS messages have been missing for 5 seconds or more.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test G's symptom, network, module self-test and returning-code decisions.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0131:00 is recorded in PAM.
diagnostics.meaning: Power steering control module messages have been missing for 5 seconds or more; network, gateway, steering-control or PAM concerns are possible.
diagnostics.next: Continue with communications-network and power-steering diagnosis. This observation alone does not authorize steering-gear replacement.

verification.title: Repeat the relevant functional checks
verification.body: Confirm clear-area and test-object readings after sensor work. Operate parking aid and repeat the prescribed self-tests and communication-code checks after repairs.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Save before-and-after codes by module, sensor readings, substitution results and final operation. Keep an unresolved isolated U0101:00 explicitly open.

guides.title: Diagnose rear parking aid communication faults
guides.summary: Trace parking aid communication codes through network tests, module checks and connector inspections before deciding whether replacement is justified.
guides.introduction: Rear parking aid uses ultrasonic sensors to detect nearby objects and requests warning tones through the rear speakers while reversing. Its parking assist control module (PAM) is built into the body control module (BCM), but communicates as a separate network node. Missing messages can therefore disable parking aid even when the bumper sensors themselves are working.
guides.why: Communication codes identify missing information, not necessarily a failed module. These tests distinguish an intermittent event, a wider network problem and a fault affecting only the parking aid's communication path.

when.summary: Use when rear parking aid has a communication code, especially with an observable operating fault.
notes: An unavailable parking aid menu can be normal with a MyKey restricted key.

prepare.title: Arrange network diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of network tests, module self-tests and continuous-memory diagnostic trouble code (DTC) retrieval. Have Wiring Diagrams Cell 14 and Ford service bulletin information available.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Review previous repairs and inspect wiring. Connector repairs require suitable terminal tools and the specified flex probes if measurements are needed.

steps.title: Confirm the fault is present
steps.body: Switch the ignition on and check for an observable symptom. If none exists, clear the code as directed. High network traffic or an intermittent fault may explain it; do not replace a module for an absent concern.

steps.title: Follow the code's network route
steps.body: Use the individual test routes below in [Parking Aid](#/document/G1693946). A failed network test goes to communications diagnosis. Relevant self-test or gateway codes must be investigated before continuing toward a parking aid module decision.

steps.title: Check whether the PAM code returns
steps.body: After the preceding checks pass, clear codes, operate parking aid and retrieve PAM continuous-memory codes. If the target code does not return, operation is correct at this time. A returning U0140:00 proceeds directly to BCM connector inspection.

steps.title: Compare other modules
steps.body: For returning U0131:00, U0146:00 or U0155:00, clear all codes, switch ignition off and on, wait 10 seconds, then read every module. The corresponding code elsewhere directs inspection toward the steering module, gateway or instrument cluster respectively. If confined to the PAM, inspect the BCM.

steps.title: Inspect the selected connections
steps.body: With ignition off, disconnect the selected module's connectors and related inline connectors. Replace corroded connectors or terminals and clean module pins; renew damaged, bent or pushed-out pins as required. Reconnect securely, confirm latches engage and retest. Correct the cause of connector damage.

steps.title: Resolve a persistent concern through its branch
steps.body: Check applicable technical service bulletins before replacement; follow an applicable bulletin instead of continuing the test. Otherwise follow the selected BCM, gateway or cluster replacement direction. The steering branch calls for the electric power-assisted steering symptom chart and steering gear/control-module work. BCM replacement requires programmable module installation (PMI); it is not complete merely when plugged in.

watchFor.title: Detection limits can resemble faults
watchFor.body: Dirt, ice, sensor alignment and poorly reflecting objects can affect detection. The system may not detect moving objects.

notes: PAM and BCM communicate separately on high-speed Controller Area Network 1 (HS-CAN1), despite sharing an assembly.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0131:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test H investigates the power steering control module (PSCM) communication path.
diagnostics.next: Network-test PSCM and gateway module A (GWM), then self-test PSCM and check GWM memory. PSCM codes lead to power steering diagnosis; GWM codes lead to network diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0140:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test I addresses PAM communication with BCM being lost for 5 seconds or more.
diagnostics.next: Network-test and self-test BCM. Diagnose BCM self-test codes before rechecking PAM.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0146:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test J addresses expected gateway messages missing for 5 seconds or more.
diagnostics.next: Network-test GWM and inspect its continuous-memory codes before rechecking PAM.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0155:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test K addresses instrument panel cluster (IPC) messages missing for 5 seconds or more.
diagnostics.next: Network-test IPC and GWM, self-test IPC, then check GWM memory. IPC codes lead to instrumentation diagnosis; GWM codes lead to network diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0212:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: PAM has missed steering column control module messages for 5 seconds or more.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the steering-column and gateway/network path before selecting a repair.

verification.title: Confirm operation
verification.body: Operate parking aid after the directed correction and check whether the original concern remains.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record returning PAM codes and, where directed, which other modules stored the matching communication code. Distinguish an absent intermittent concern from a confirmed repair.

guides.title: Diagnose rear parking camera image and feature faults
guides.summary: Trace missing or distorted camera images, guidelines, alerts, zoom and video delay through the correct display-specific diagnostic branch.
guides.introduction: The rear camera helps you see and align the vehicle while reversing. Its image, guidelines and parking alerts depend on several components working together. Video travels over shielded wiring to the display system, while the camera communicates with the body control module (BCM) through the local interconnect network (LIN). Diagnosis separates camera faults from wiring, settings, vehicle inputs and display concerns.
guides.why: A working picture does not establish that every camera feature has the inputs it needs. Likewise, a black screen or stored code alone does not identify a failed camera.

when.summary: When the rear camera image or its guidelines, visual alerts, manual zoom or video delay do not operate correctly.
notes: Confirm the complaint is present before following a branch that directs component replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a suitable scan tool, digital multimeter, Rotunda Flex Probes and Wiring Diagrams Cell 145. Follow Diagnostic Methods, including battery and charging checks and battery state of charge greater than 70%.

prepare.title: Identify the display
prepare.detail: The touchscreen branch uses the accessory protocol interface module (APIM); the smaller display uses the front control/display interface module (FCDIM). Confirm camera configuration after replacement and check connector seating before disconnecting it.

steps.title: Match the complaint to its branch
steps.body: Use the symptom chart in the linked Parking Aid procedure. Check lens cleanliness, luggage-lid closure and relevant feature settings. On touchscreen vehicles, reset the APIM before Tests B–F. Frozen or slow touchscreen operation remaining after reset needs APIM and display diagnosis; the smaller display routes directly to FCDIM diagnosis.

steps.title: Test A: missing video or an unavailable-camera message
steps.body: Clean the lens, apply the parking brake and check that reversing lamps illuminate only in reverse throughout gear selection. Incorrect operation routes to reversing-lamp diagnosis. Perform the network test, then BCM and display-module checks in the prescribed order; the touchscreen reset occurs within this sequence. At A8, observe the display for 30 seconds in reverse: an unavailable-camera message leads to circuit testing; failure to meet that condition routes to the relevant display-module diagnosis.

steps.title: Test the missing-video electrical path
steps.body: A9–A17 check camera supply and ground, video wiring for shorts and opens, then LIN wiring. Follow each ignition state, connector isolation and display-specific pin assignment exactly. A failed supply check requires inspection of fuse 66 (5A) in the battery junction box and the appropriate circuit investigation; a blown fuse requires finding the short.

steps.title: Test B: distorted or poor-quality images
steps.body: Inspect the lens for debris and scratches. If cleaning does not restore the image, check supply, shield ground and the shielded video pair using the correct display branch. Dirt or outside electromagnetic interference can explain an intermittent image concern. Persistent faults proceed through camera checks, then FCDIM or APIM checks if necessary.

steps.title: Test C: missing visual parking alerts
steps.body: Enable the alert first. Run the parking assist control module self-test and repair its faults before continuing, because visual alerts depend on the audible parking-aid system. Then check BCM and display-module codes. The smaller-display branch checks the camera before the FCDIM; the touchscreen branch proceeds to APIM checks.

steps.title: Test D: missing fixed or active guidelines
steps.body: Confirm settings and lid closure; active lines require steering-wheel rotation. Check network communication, BCM and the fitted display module. Active-line complaints additionally require anti-lock brake system and power steering control module self-tests. Compare the BCM DOOR_SW_LUGG parameter identification (PID) with actual lid movement; disagreement routes to latch-system diagnosis. Passing inputs lead to camera checks, then BCM connector checks and its vehicle-identification-number-specific guided routine.

steps.title: Tests E and F: delay or manual zoom
steps.body: For video delay, Test E checks enablement, network communication, reverse-gear input and the fitted display module before its connector and component checks. For manual zoom, Test F checks network communication, BCM and display-module codes before inspecting the camera connection. An unresolved zoom fault reaches camera replacement only through that branch.

steps.title: Complete the selected component-check branch
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect the specified connectors for corrosion, damaged or pushed-out pins; repair and latch them securely. Retest and address the cause of connector damage. Allow at least 2 minutes for APIM reinitialization after reconnection. At persistent-fault endpoints, check applicable technical service bulletins before the directed camera or FCDIM replacement, APIM Hardware Test or BCM guided routine.

watchFor.title: Invalid electrical measurements
watchFor.body: Powered voltage tests and isolated resistance tests require different setups. Follow the exact branch rather than probing connected circuits indiscriminately.

notes: After battery discharge/disconnection or module disconnection/replacement, active guidelines may need learning: drive on a flat, smooth road at 32 km/h (20 mph) or more for approximately 30 seconds, hands loosely on the wheel with minimal correction. If still absent, the procedure allows disconnecting the battery for 5 minutes with the driver's door open, then driving 5 miles in normal city traffic before repeating the learning drive.
Other BCM codes route to BCM diagnosis; other APIM or FCDIM codes route to information and entertainment diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: BCM code B115E:01, B115E:02 or B115E:08 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These indicate an electrical failure, invalid camera LIN data or a LIN communication fault, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test A; its BCM self-test routes these codes to A9.

diagnostics.finding: B115E:49 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detected an internal camera electronic fault.
diagnostics.next: Clear codes and repeat the self-test; replace the camera if this code returns.

diagnostics.finding: B115E:55 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The camera is not configured.
diagnostics.next: Perform camera configuration with the diagnostic scan tool.

diagnostics.finding: B115E:9A is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: On-demand self-test prerequisites were not met.
diagnostics.next: Close the luggage lid fully and diagnose other BCM codes.

diagnostics.finding: The APIM or FCDIM records C1001:01.
diagnostics.meaning: No camera video signal was detected in reverse.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test A.

diagnostics.finding: The camera image is upside down.
diagnostics.meaning: The symptom chart identifies an internal camera fault or an incorrect camera.
diagnostics.next: Install the correct new rear camera using its replacement procedure.

verification.title: Retest the original function
verification.body: Operate the system after each directed repair. Confirm the original image or feature complaint has cleared and verify replacement-camera configuration.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record relevant self-test results, circuit findings and feature operation. If the concern disappears during testing, retain that intermittent finding rather than assuming a component failed.

procedures.purpose: Complete camera diagnostic charts and Tests A–F for both display variants.
Required electrical diagnostic methods and probing precautions.
Rear camera removal and installation when directed.
BCM fault diagnosis.
SYNC display-system and module diagnosis.
Incorrect reversing-lamp or gear-input diagnosis.
FCDIM removal and installation when directed.
Rear audible parking-aid fault diagnosis.
Incorrect luggage-lid position-input diagnosis.

applicability.equipment: Rear parking aid camera with 8-inch touchscreen or 4.2-inch centerstack display

guides.title: Check rear parking-aid distance readings with positioned targets
guides.summary: Place targets at specified distances behind the rear bumper and compare their detection with scan-tool parking-aid readings.
guides.introduction: The rear parking aid uses ultrasonic echoes to detect objects and estimate their distance from the bumper. Its azimuth is the horizontal area it monitors behind the vehicle. This check places objects at known locations so you can assess sensor distance readings; it does not establish maximum detection range.
guides.why: Target position and the reflected sound affect detection. The inner and outer sensors have different coverage, so the staggered arrangement matters. Warning tones also depend on vehicle movement and obstacle distance, making scan-tool readings essential during this stationary check.
searchTerms: rear parking aid silent when stationary

when.summary: Use when rear parking-aid object detection or reported distance needs checking against known target positions.
notes: This is the rear-system check with reverse selected.

prepare.title: Prepare the targets and location
prepare.detail: Use a level surface and upright PVC or similar pipe targets matching the procedure's 9 cm diameter (3 in I.D.) specification and 100 cm (39 in) length. I.D. means internal diameter.

prepare.title: Prepare distance measurement and live data
prepare.detail: Have a means of measuring from the rear bumper and a diagnostic scan tool that displays parking-aid sensor distance parameter identifications (PIDs). The check requires an operator to maintain the brake controls with the engine running.

steps.title: Check conditions that affect detection
steps.body: Confirm the parking aid is enabled through the message center. Note any disabled warning, covered sensors, incorrect alignment or add-on equipment obstructing the detection area. Dirt, ice, heavy rain and snow can affect echoes and must be considered before interpreting a missed target.

steps.title: Arrange the staggered targets
steps.body: Follow the position diagram for the lateral arrangement. Place the outboard P1 and P5 targets 25 cm (10 in) from the rear bumper, intermediate P2 and P4 targets 50 cm (20 in) away, and centered P3 150 cm (59 in) away. Measure from the bumper; do not arrange every target in one straight row.

steps.title: Activate the rear system while holding the vehicle
steps.body: Switch the ignition on with the engine running. Apply the parking brake and keep your foot on the brake pedal, then select reverse. Maintain these braking conditions while taking the readings.

steps.title: Check detection through the scan tool
steps.body: Monitor the sensor distance PIDs and verify detection at P1, P2, P3, P4 and P5. Compare the reported distances with the known layout. Use the live data to assess the farther targets: silence alone does not mean those targets are undetected.

watchFor.title: Stationary warning behavior
watchFor.body: The system provides stationary audio warnings only for obstacles less than 12 in (30 cm) from the bumper. Farther targets may be detected without a warning tone.

notes: P1–P5 identify target positions, not five separate sensors. Actual sensor arrangement may differ from the diagram.
A MyKey restricted key prevents disabling parking aid through the message-center menu.

diagnostics.finding: A positioned target is absent from the distance readings
diagnostics.meaning: Detection is inconsistent with the check, but target reflection, positioning, sensor obstruction or alignment may contribute.
diagnostics.next: Recheck the setup and visible detection conditions before proceeding to fault diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: The message center reports parking aid disabled
diagnostics.meaning: A detected sensor, communications-network or parking-aid module fault can disable the system.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the disabling fault before interpreting this as a distance-accuracy result.

verification.title: Confirm each specified position
verification.body: Verify object detection at all five positions using distance PIDs, retaining the specified staggered layout.

verification.title: Record the measured result
verification.body: Record each position, its bumper-to-target distance, the corresponding PID readings and any missed detection or warning message.

procedures.purpose: Rear azimuth check, target geometry, activation and scan-tool monitoring.
Exact rear-bumper distances for target positions P1–P5.

guides.title: Check rear parking sensor aim when an empty area triggers a warning
guides.summary: Compare rear parking sensor distance data with audible warnings to identify possible downward sensor aim from bumper misalignment.
guides.introduction: The rear parking aid uses ultrasonic sensors to detect reflected sound and estimate the distance to nearby objects. It warns through the rear audio speakers when reverse is selected. This elevation check asks whether the sensors are aimed downward enough to detect the ground as an obstacle.
guides.why: Sensor direction depends on correct bumper installation. A downward-tilted bumper can create an apparent obstacle even when the area is clear. Both scan-tool readings and sound matter: silence alone is not a passing result, especially if a fault has disabled the system.
searchTerms: rear parking aid beeps with no obstacle

when.summary: When rear parking aid reports an obstacle in a clear area or bumper alignment is in question.
notes: This is a stationary check with the engine running and reverse selected.

prepare.title: Provide live sensor data
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of displaying parking-aid sensor-distance parameter identification (PID) data.

prepare.title: Control the test conditions
prepare.detail: Use a clear rear detection area. Be able to maintain the parking brake and continuous foot-brake application during the check.

steps.title: Establish whether the system is available
steps.body: Check for a parking-aid-disabled message and confirm the system has not been switched off through the message center. A disabled system cannot establish correct sensor aim simply by remaining quiet.

steps.title: Set up the stationary reverse check
steps.body: Follow the [Elevation System Check](#/document/G1672937): turn the ignition on with the engine running, apply the parking brake and keep your foot on the brake pedal. Select reverse to activate the rear sensors.

steps.title: Compare readings with the clear area
steps.body: Monitor the sensor-distance PIDs and listen for an audible warning. The required result is that no object is detected. Note any sensor reporting an object even if there is no warning tone.

steps.title: Follow the alignment decision
steps.body: If a warning sounds or a PID reports an object, check that the bumper is installed correctly and is not tilted downward, pointing a sensor toward the ground. Continue through Parking Aid diagnosis and testing; this check does not itself authorize sensor replacement.

watchFor.title: Obstructions and environmental effects
watchFor.body: Add-on devices can cause false alerts. Dirt, ice, heavy rain and snow can also impair object detection.

notes: Use the reverse branch for this rear-parking-aid application. The general procedure's Drive branch concerns front sensors and does not establish that front sensors are fitted.

diagnostics.finding: No warning and no object reported
diagnostics.meaning: The system passes the empty-area elevation check under these conditions.
diagnostics.next: Record the readings; this does not establish detection of every possible obstacle.

diagnostics.finding: A warning or an object-distance reading in the clear area
diagnostics.meaning: Incorrect bumper installation may be directing a sensor toward the ground.
diagnostics.next: Inspect bumper position and continue the diagnostic procedure.

diagnostics.finding: Parking-aid-disabled message
diagnostics.meaning: A sensor, network or parking aid module fault can disable operation.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the disabling concern before interpreting silence as a pass.

verification.title: Repeat after an alignment correction
verification.body: Under the same clear-area and brake-held conditions, confirm there is neither an object indication nor an audible warning.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the sensor-distance readings, warning behavior and bumper alignment findings.

procedures.purpose: Perform the rear sensor elevation check and follow its bumper-alignment decision.
Understand rear sensor operation, detection limitations and warning behavior.
Identify system enablement and the significance of a disabled warning.

guides.title: Replace a rear parking aid sensor and check its alignment
guides.summary: Remove the rear bumper cover to replace the selected parking aid sensor, then check horizontal and vertical detection alignment.
guides.introduction: Rear parking aid sensors use reflected ultrasonic sound to detect suitable objects behind the vehicle. With reverse selected, the parking aid module (PAM) calculates distance and requests warning tones through the rear speakers. Replacing a sensor involves the wiring and retaining clips behind the bumper cover, followed by checks that establish whether the sensors are correctly aligned.
guides.why: A sensor can be electrically connected yet aimed incorrectly. Its orientation affects what it detects, so secure clip engagement alone does not complete this job. Equally, a disabled system does not identify a particular sensor: sensor, network and module faults can all disable parking assistance.
searchTerms: rear parking sensors not detecting objects

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies a rear parking aid sensor for replacement, or it must be removed during bumper work.
notes: Check installation, contamination and operating conditions before treating missed detections as proof of sensor failure.

prepare.title: Plan bumper-cover access
prepare.detail: Be prepared to remove and reinstall the rear bumper cover and release its harness guides, clips and retainers using the linked procedures.

prepare.title: Arrange alignment checks
prepare.detail: Have the Azimuth System Check and Elevation System Check available. Their specified setups are needed to complete the repair.

steps.title: Remove the rear bumper cover
steps.body: Use [Rear Bumper Cover](#/document/G1694215) to obtain access to the sensor mountings and wiring behind the cover.

steps.title: Clear the harness and reinforcement
steps.body: Following [Rear Parking Aid Sensor](#/document/G1693924), separate the wiring harness guides and move the harness aside. Remove the pin-type retainers, release the clips and remove the bumper-cover reinforcement.

steps.title: Release the selected sensor
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector belonging to the sensor being serviced. Release its retaining clips and remove the sensor from its mounting.

steps.title: Reassemble the bumper components
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence to install the sensor, reconnect it, refit the reinforcement and return the harness to its guides. Reinstall the bumper cover through its procedure.

steps.title: Check both directions of alignment
steps.body: Perform the [Azimuth System Check](#/document/G1672936) for horizontal alignment and the [Elevation System Check](#/document/G1672937) for vertical alignment. Use their findings to establish whether the installation is satisfactory.

watchFor.title: Obscured or misaligned sensors
watchFor.body: Dirt, ice and incorrect installation can prevent detection. Heavy rain, snow and an object’s reflective properties also affect performance.

watchFor.title: Blocked detection area
watchFor.body: Add-on devices can intrude into the detection zone and cause false audible alerts.

notes: The system assists with detecting certain objects and may not detect moving objects.
The sensors share voltage and ground circuits, so system-wide symptoms do not automatically justify replacing every sensor.

diagnostics.finding: The message center reports parking aid disabled.
diagnostics.meaning: A sensor, communications-network or PAM fault can disable the system.
diagnostics.next: Identify the fault before selecting a sensor for replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Objects are missed or unexpected tones occur.
diagnostics.meaning: Alignment, contamination, weather, object characteristics or obstructions can affect detection.
diagnostics.next: Assess those conditions and complete the specified alignment checks after installation.

verification.title: Installation restored
verification.body: Confirm the sensor clips, connector, harness guides, reinforcement and bumper-cover attachments have been restored.

verification.title: Alignment results recorded
verification.body: Record the outcomes of both the azimuth and elevation checks, including any correction required.

procedures.purpose: Rear parking aid sensor removal and installation behind the bumper cover.
Rear bumper cover removal and installation for sensor access.
Required horizontal, or azimuth, parking aid alignment check.
Required vertical, or elevation, parking aid alignment check.

guides.title: Replace and initialize the rear parking aid camera
guides.summary: Access the camera through the luggage compartment lid trim, replace the unit and complete its scan-tool initialization.
guides.introduction: The rear parking aid camera supplies the image used when reversing or reverse parking. The picture appears on the vehicle's fitted center display, with camera-system features including guidelines and zoom. The camera communicates with the body control module through a Local Interconnect Network (LIN) circuit. Replacement involves both removing the camera from its bracket and configuring it electronically afterward. The illustrated access is for a coupe; convertible access is similar.
guides.why: The luggage compartment lid trim is retained around the emergency release handle and latch cover, so those pieces must be released in the proper order. Gentle work at the latch-cover tab avoids forcing the cover against its attachment. Once the camera is installed, the prescribed initialization remains essential to completing the replacement.
searchTerms: no camera image when reverse is selected

when.summary: When the rear parking aid camera has been identified for replacement or requires removal.
notes: A missing reverse image alone does not establish that the camera needs replacement.

prepare.title: Prepare trim access
prepare.detail: Have a flat-bladed screwdriver for releasing the latch cover and suitable equipment for the trim retainers and camera screws.

prepare.title: Arrange electronic configuration
prepare.detail: Have a scan tool capable of running LIN New Module Initialization. Plan this before removing the camera so the repair can be completed.

steps.title: Release the handle and latch cover
steps.body: Press down the emergency release handle's retaining tab and remove the handle. Insert a flat-bladed screwdriver between the latch cover and latch, then gently pry the cover away to disengage it from the latch tab.

steps.title: Expose and disconnect the camera
steps.body: Remove the trim retainers and luggage compartment lid trim panel. Disconnect the rear camera electrical connector before releasing the camera assembly.

steps.title: Remove the camera from its bracket
steps.body: Remove the camera screws, remove the bracket and then remove the camera. Follow that sequence so the retaining bracket is released before the camera is taken out.

steps.title: Install and initialize
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure to fit the camera, bracket, connector, trim panel, latch cover and emergency release handle. Configure the camera through the scan-tool path Electrical > Service Functions > LIN New Module Initialization, following the tool's instructions.

watchFor.title: A latch cover that still resists removal
watchFor.body: Check its engagement with the latch tab and release it gently rather than increasing force against an attached cover.

watchFor.title: Unfinished electronic setup
watchFor.body: Do not treat physical installation as completion while the specified LIN initialization remains unfinished.

notes: The camera's visual alert feature works with the rear audible parking aid system; keep checks appropriate to the vehicle's fitted equipment.

verification.title: Check reassembly
verification.body: Confirm the camera bracket and connector are secured and the trim retainers, latch cover and emergency release handle are re-engaged.

verification.title: Record initialization
verification.body: Record successful completion of LIN New Module Initialization.

verification.title: Confirm the reversing image
verification.body: Check that selecting reverse displays the rear camera image on the fitted center display.

procedures.purpose: Rear parking aid camera removal and installation, coupe and similar convertible access, and scan-tool initialization.
Camera-system operation, display behavior, LIN communication and equipment-dependent parking aid features.

guides.title: Diagnose charging voltage faults and generator noise on the 2.3L EcoBoost
guides.summary: Separate battery, wiring, generator, clutch and control faults using the appropriate charging-system test.
guides.introduction: The belt-driven generator converts mechanical power into electrical power for the battery and vehicle systems. Its regulator works to a voltage target commanded by the powertrain control module (PCM). These tests distinguish incorrect output from voltage lost through connections, inaccurate control-module readings and mechanical noise.
guides.why: A discharged battery or noisy generator does not establish which part failed. Corroded connections can show normal voltage without a load, then lose voltage while supplying current. Comparing commanded voltage, measured voltage and loaded circuit losses helps locate the actual fault.

when.summary: When charging voltage is abnormal, the battery discharges, or noise appears to come from the generator.
notes: The concern must be present before following a diagnostic replacement decision.

prepare.title: Establish valid battery conditions
prepare.detail: Verify battery state of charge above 70%. Tests A and B require battery voltage greater than 12.2 volts before and throughout testing, with no battery charger attached.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool with PCM self-tests and active commands, a digital multimeter, fused jumpers, Flex Probes and the specified circuit loads. Obtain Wiring Diagrams Cell 12. This work includes live measurements and controlled engine-running tests.

steps.title: Inspect and select the complaint branch
steps.body: Check previous repairs, wiring, battery junction box (BJB) connections, battery condition and diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). For discharge complaints, also inspect the front-end accessory drive, generator clutch and ignition-off drain. Correct obvious faults first. In the [charging diagnosis](#/document/G2560182), use Test A for high voltage, B for low voltage or discharge, and C for noise. Resolve circuit codes before performance codes.

steps.title: Test A: compare charging voltage with its target
steps.body: Perform the PCM self-test first. Compare measured idle battery voltage with the generator voltage desired parameter identification (PID), GENVDSD. Agreement within ±0.5 volt leads to A6; disagreement leads to the unloaded and loaded “A” sense checks. A failed sense check requires checking BJB fuse 36 (10A), then repairing the circuit or investigating the cause of a blown fuse.

steps.title: Test A: separate connection, output and control faults
steps.body: Reconnect the generator connector for the loaded wiring wiggle test and ground voltage-drop check. Repair excessive variation or ground loss before continuing. A8 determines whether output requires generator replacement. Otherwise, follow A9–A13 for the prescribed fused-jumper communication comparison, PCM supply-voltage comparison and, where directed, loaded power and ground checks. Use the exact connection instructions for each stage.

steps.title: Test B: prove the charging power path
steps.body: After the PCM self-test, inspect and repair generator terminals, then latch the connectors. Check the positive output connection against battery voltage. A failure leads to the output nut, BJB MEGA fuse (275A) and circuit checks. Test positive-cable and ground voltage drop with headlamps and blower operating. Then command GENVDSD to 14 volts and compare battery voltage within ±0.5 volt.

steps.title: Test B: follow the output or supply branch
steps.body: If output does not follow the command, B11 requires the Test J clutch check: a good clutch leads to generator replacement; a failed clutch leads to clutch replacement. If output follows the command, B7–B10 assess PCM supply indication, loaded feeds and grounds, then voltage tracking during the prescribed brief wide-open-throttle checks with accessories off. A passing result with no connector fault leads to the [battery drain check](#/document/G1692357).

steps.title: Complete any PCM investigation before replacement
steps.body: At A13 or B12, inspect all PCM connectors, repair corrosion or damaged/displaced terminals, reconnect and retest. Persistent concerns require checking applicable service bulletins and campaigns before the PCM replacement decision. Follow an applicable bulletin instead of continuing the test. Where the branch directs PCM replacement, clear DTCs from all modules afterward.

steps.title: Test C: locate the mechanical noise
steps.body: Inspect the belt and tensioner through the [2.3L accessory-drive diagnosis](#/document/G1673162), then check generator mounting and alignment. Use a stethoscope or equivalent to locate unusual running noise. Noise elsewhere requires engine diagnosis. Confirmed generator noise leads to Test J: replace the generator only if the clutch passes; otherwise replace the clutch. Sound matching the normal-noise reference, with accessories on and no other symptoms or DTCs, is considered normal.

steps.title: Route warning messages and radio interference correctly
steps.body: A warning indicator concern without charging DTCs leads to [instrumentation diagnosis](#/document/G1693940); load-shed and Battery Saver messages lead to Test H. Radio interference leads to Test D. Restore an aftermarket audio unit to original equipment condition first, and inspect accessory wiring for generator-circuit connections or routing near generator wiring. During disconnected-generator radio testing, keep engine speed below 2,000 RPM; exceeding it requires switching off and restarting the test.

watchFor.title: An unsuitable sense-circuit load
watchFor.body: Use the specified 250–350 mA incandescent 12-volt test lamp. An LED lamp cannot load this circuit correctly. Connect through Flex Probes, never the lamp probe directly.

watchFor.title: Temporary recovery after reconnecting
watchFor.body: A restored connection can hide an intermittent fault. Correct the terminal or corrosion problem rather than treating reconnection alone as the repair.

notes: Generator, clutch and PCM replacement decisions lead to their separate technical procedures; these diagnostic checks do not describe replacement work.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0563 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detected excessive system voltage; recent charging or jump-starting can also set this code.
diagnostics.next: Evaluate the circumstances and follow Test A.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0562 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Voltage remained sufficiently below the PCM's desired generator voltage to trigger the monitor.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test B, including cable and ground checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1397 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Voltage was outside the self-test range; a discharged battery or recent jump-start may contribute.
diagnostics.next: Establish battery condition and follow the observed voltage complaint.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0620 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The charging procedure requires its dedicated circuit investigation.
diagnostics.next: Go to Test F.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0625 or P0626 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The charging procedure requires a different circuit investigation.
diagnostics.next: Go to Test G.

verification.title: Confirm operation under the specified conditions
verification.body: Repeat the applicable branch's operating checks after repair and confirm the original concern is absent.

verification.title: Record the comparisons
verification.body: Retain battery voltage, commanded and reported values, loaded voltage drops, DTCs and the branch outcome so the diagnosis is traceable.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost charging diagnosis: symptom routing, Tests A–C and radio-interference prerequisites.
Electrical diagnostic prerequisites, terminal protection, circuit loading and fused-jumper methods.
Battery drain investigation when Test B passes without a connector fault.
2.3L EcoBoost accessory-drive diagnosis during Test C.
Charging warning-indicator diagnosis when charging DTCs are absent.

guides.title: Diagnose battery-saver messages, current-sensor faults and generator clutch operation — 2.3L EcoBoost
guides.summary: Follow Tests H, I and J to distinguish energy-management messages, battery-current sensing faults and generator clutch problems.
guides.introduction: The belt-driven generator supplies electrical power, while the battery current sensor helps the body control module (BCM) assess stored charge. Load shedding limits electrical demand when needed. The generator clutch allows its rotor to overrun as the accessory drive slows, so an electrical warning and a clutch fault require different checks.
guides.why: A battery-saver message does not establish generator failure. Connector condition, charge estimation and module communication must be checked before replacement decisions; clutch testing separately evaluates mechanical operation.

when.summary: When load-shed messages appear, battery-current sensor codes recur, or generator clutch operation requires testing.

prepare.title: Electrical testing
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, multimeter, oscilloscope and suitable terminal probes. Test I requires battery voltage above 12.2 volts before and throughout testing, with no battery charger attached.

prepare.title: Mechanical access
prepare.detail: Test J requires generator removal, a small screwdriver, a 17 mm hex bit and socket wrench. Obtain a new pulley cap because the removed cap must be discarded.

steps.title: Test H: establish where the message appears
steps.body: Complete Inspection and Verification and correct obvious causes. If battery saver appeared only in the centerstack with the engine running, follow Information and Entertainment System diagnosis. Otherwise test network communication with the accessory protocol interface module (APIM), BCM and powertrain control module (PCM); failed communication requires network diagnosis.

steps.title: Check codes before charge estimation
steps.body: Run the PCM self-test, then retrieve continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) across modules. Route battery/charging codes through the appropriate charts; APIM or audio control module codes follow information/entertainment diagnostics. With no relevant codes, inspect the BCM BAT_ST_CHRG parameter.

steps.title: Relearn low indicated charge
steps.body: Below 50%, remove accessories from power outlets and the inverter, if fitted. Secure the key away from the vehicle and leave it undisturbed for at least 6 hours. Recheck BAT_ST_CHRG: 50% or more supports explaining energy-management operation and returning the vehicle. An initially adequate reading, or a persistently low reading after relearning, leads to connector checks.

steps.title: Finish the load-shed branch
steps.body: Inspect inline connector C1046 for poor engagement, corrosion and damaged or displaced terminals. If satisfactory, inspect and reseat BCM connectors with ignition off, then operate the system. A persistent concern requires checking applicable service information before the test directs BCM replacement.

steps.title: Test I: establish whether the sensor fault returns
steps.body: Inspect the sensor, battery terminals, connector C1646 and battery junction box fuse F7 (60A). Repair connector defects. Clear all module codes and run the BCM self-test. A returning fault leads to C1046 inspection, including water intrusion, then circuit isolation tests.

steps.title: Separate wiring, sensor and BCM faults
steps.body: Follow I4–I8 in order: test unintended connections between C1046 circuits, end-to-end continuity, shorts to ground, shorts to voltage, then BCM reference output. The reference must be 4.7–5.0 volts. If satisfactory, perform I9's prescribed engine-running oscilloscope test at C1646 pin 3. A matching waveform directs sensor replacement; an incorrect waveform or reference voltage leads to BCM connector checks and the service-information decision in I10.

steps.title: Test J: inspect and turn the clutch
steps.body: Remove the generator through the named Generator Pulley procedure. Heat damage directs clutch replacement and accessory-drive inspection. Otherwise remove and discard the cap. Hold the pulley and turn the shaft clockwise with the hex bit: roughness or seizure directs clutch replacement. Counterclockwise rotation must provide spring resistance; absent resistance or free reverse rotation also directs clutch replacement. If it does not rotate freely in reverse, J4 directs generator replacement.

watchFor.title: Heat damage has a possible external cause
watchFor.body: A loose accessory belt or weak or binding tensioner can overheat the pulley; replacing the clutch alone may leave that cause unresolved.

watchFor.title: Protect test connections
watchFor.body: Use the specified circuit isolation and ignition states. Back-probe only where directed for the operating waveform test.

notes: The undisturbed period relearns charge state; it is not a charging operation.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B130C:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detects a short to battery in the sensor control circuit.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test I before condemning the sensor.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B130C:14 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The sensor control circuit is open or shorted to ground.
diagnostics.next: Inspect connections and complete Test I's circuit checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1438:03 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM is not receiving the expected current indication.
diagnostics.next: Follow connector, wiring, reference-voltage and waveform checks in Test I.

verification.title: Confirm the applicable endpoint
verification.body: After connector work, operate the system and confirm whether the concern remains. Complete any directed generator work through the referenced procedure and install a new pulley cap.

verification.title: Record diagnostic results
verification.body: Record returning codes, charge-state readings, circuit measurements and waveform findings. Preserve the clutch's directional results so the final replacement decision is traceable.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost load-shed Test H, battery-current sensor Test I and generator clutch Test J.
Electrical testing methods and connector precautions.
Centerstack-only battery-saver and relevant entertainment-module diagnosis.
Routing other battery/charging-related trouble codes.
2.3L accessory-drive diagnosis after clutch heat damage.

guides.title: Diagnose charging voltage faults and generator noise on the 3.7L Mustang
guides.summary: Trace charging complaints through battery, wiring, generator control and mechanical checks before deciding which component needs repair.
guides.introduction: The belt-driven generator converts engine movement into electrical power, supplying the vehicle and replenishing the battery. Its internal regulator follows commands from the powertrain control module (PCM). Consequently, a discharged battery or abnormal voltage can originate in the battery, drive system, connections or control circuits. Tests A, B and C distinguish high voltage, low voltage and generator noise.
guides.why: A corroded connection may show normal voltage until current flows. Loaded measurements reveal these losses, while comparing measured voltage with commanded voltage helps distinguish a generator fault from inaccurate sensing or control.

when.summary: When charging voltage is abnormal, the battery discharges, or noise appears to come from the generator.
notes: Confirm the complaint is present before using a diagnostic replacement decision.

prepare.title: Establish a valid battery baseline
prepare.detail: Verify battery state of charge exceeds 70%. Tests A and B require battery voltage above 12.2 volts before and throughout testing, with no battery charger attached.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool with PCM self-test and active-command functions, a digital multimeter, fused jumpers and Flex Probes. The sense-circuit load requires a 250–350 mA incandescent 12-volt test lamp; an LED lamp is unsuitable. PCM circuit tests use a suitable load such as a headlamp bulb.

prepare.title: Prepare for running-engine checks
prepare.detail: These tests require live-circuit and running-engine diagnostic skills, wiring diagrams and a stethoscope or equivalent listening device.

steps.title: Inspect and choose the diagnostic branch
steps.body: Inspect battery and generator connections, engine and battery grounds, the high-current battery junction box (BJB), fuses, fusible links and wiring. Check the front end accessory drive (FEAD), battery condition and ignition-off drain. Correct obvious faults, retrieve codes from all modules and diagnose PCM codes before body control module (BCM) codes.

steps.title: Test A: compare actual and requested voltage
steps.body: At idle, compare battery voltage with the generator voltage desired parameter identifier (PID), GENVDSD. Agreement within ±0.5 volt leads to A6. Otherwise, follow A4–A5 to check the generator sense circuit unloaded and loaded, including its fuse. A voltage loss under load points toward a connection or wiring fault.

steps.title: Complete the high-voltage branch
steps.body: With the headlamps and heater blower operating as specified, check intermittent wiring behavior and ground voltage drop. A8 directs generator replacement if its output exceeds 15.2 volts. Otherwise, follow A9 onward through the fused-jumper command/monitor comparison, PCM supply-voltage comparison and loaded power/ground tests.

steps.title: Test B: establish a sound charging path
steps.body: Inspect and repair generator terminals, then check the B+ positive supply connection, retaining nut and high-current MEGA fuse. Perform the loaded positive-cable and ground voltage-drop checks. Only after these pass, command GENVDSD to 14 volts: battery voltage outside ±0.5 volt directs generator replacement.

steps.title: Separate low-voltage control faults from discharge
steps.body: Continue through the PCM supply-voltage PID, VPWR, and loaded supply/ground checks. B10 then specifies momentary wide-open-throttle accelerations with accessories off. A passing result leads to connector correction or battery-drain testing. A failing result directs generator replacement with an automatic transmission; a manual transmission first requires Test J's generator-clutch check.

steps.title: Test C: locate the noise before replacing parts
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect belt and tensioner condition, mounting bolts and alignment. Then use the listening device with the engine running. If the generator is the source, the automatic-transmission branch replaces it; the manual-transmission branch checks the clutch first. Replace a failed clutch, or the generator if the clutch passes. Noise elsewhere requires engine diagnosis.

steps.title: Route radio interference and display complaints
steps.body: For radio interference, restore factory audio equipment before Test D and check added-accessory wiring near generator circuits. During generator-disconnected testing, keep engine speed below 2,000 rpm; exceeding it requires switching off and restarting the test. Load-shed and Battery Saver messages lead to Test H. A charging-indicator complaint without codes leads to instrumentation diagnosis.

watchFor.title: Protect connector terminals
watchFor.body: Use Flex Probes for loads and jumper connections; never push the test-lamp probe directly into a connector.

watchFor.title: Do not jump straight to a PCM
watchFor.body: At A13 or B12, repair corrosion and damaged or displaced pins, latch connectors and retest. If the concern persists, follow any applicable technical service bulletin before the specified PCM replacement decision.

notes: A discharged battery can reflect accessory use or excessive aftermarket loads rather than generator failure.
Use the linked replacement procedures only when the applicable diagnostic branch directs replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0563 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detected high system voltage; recent charging or jump-starting can also set this code.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test A after checking the recent battery history.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0562 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: System voltage remained below the PCM's desired generator voltage.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test B, including wiring and ground checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1397 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Voltage was outside the self-test range; recent jump-starting or discharge can contribute.
diagnostics.next: With P0562 use Test B; with P0563 use Test A.

diagnostics.finding: P0620, P065B, P0625 or P0626 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These identify generator control or field-terminal circuit concerns.
diagnostics.next: Use Test F for P0620/P065B and Test G for P0625/P0626.

diagnostics.finding: P0A5A, P0A5B or P0A5C is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The generator current-sensor circuit has a range/performance, low or high signal concern, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test E before condemning the sensor.

diagnostics.finding: B130C:12, B130C:14 or B1438:03 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These concern load-shed circuit shorts/open circuits or the battery current sensor's signal format.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose PCM codes first, then follow Test I.

verification.title: Recheck operation
verification.body: Remove temporary jumpers as directed, restore connections and repeat the applicable operating checks. Correct the underlying terminal fault even if reconnecting temporarily removes the symptom.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Keep measured battery voltage, commanded voltage, VPWR and voltage-drop results with the final branch decision. Clear all module codes when directed by a PCM replacement branch.

guides.title: Diagnose generator interference, current-sensor and control faults on the 3.7L
guides.summary: Follow Tests D–G to distinguish generator-related radio noise, current-sensor faults and charging command or monitor circuit failures.
guides.introduction: The generator supplies electrical power through its heavy B+ cable. The powertrain control module (PCM) commands output through the generator command circuit, GENCOM, and receives feedback through the generator monitor circuit, GENMON. A Hall-effect current sensor around the B+ cable measures current without interrupting that cable. These tests establish which part of that arrangement is failing before a generator, sensor or PCM is replaced.
guides.why: A cable can show battery voltage without carrying current reliably. Loaded measurements and wiring movement expose resistance or intermittent connections. The generator can also produce fallback voltage despite a control fault, so voltage alone does not prove normal regulation.
searchTerms: system off to save battery message

when.summary: Use for radio interference, generator current-sensor codes, P0620/P065B, P0625/P0626 or battery-saver messages.
notes: Choose the test from the actual complaint and recorded codes; these checks are specific to the 3.7L procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare the battery and diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Tests E and F require battery voltage greater than 12.2 volts before and during testing, with no battery charger attached. Use a scan tool supporting PCM self-tests, live data and active commands, a multimeter, fused jumper and Flex Probe Kit.

prepare.title: Prepare for loaded and running checks
prepare.detail: The sense-circuit test requires a 250–350 mA incandescent 12-volt test lamp; an LED lamp is unsuitable. Connect it through flex probes, never directly into terminals. These procedures require competence with engine-running measurements and high-current battery connections.

prepare.title: Identify the correct terminals
prepare.detail: On the 3.7L, C102D pin 1 is the main B+ connection. C102B pin 1 carries monitor feedback, pin 2 carries regulator commands and pin 3 supplies the fused sense circuit. Inspect generator, battery and battery junction box (BJB) connections before testing.

steps.title: Select the branch and establish battery condition
steps.body: Record the complaint and codes. Test E begins with a PCM self-test: P0562 redirects to the low-voltage diagnosis in Test B before sensor diagnosis. Tests F and G begin with battery condition and state-of-charge checks; charge or replace a failing battery as directed. For G, also inspect for abnormal ignition-off drain.

steps.title: Test D: determine whether the generator causes radio interference
steps.body: Reproduce the noise at idle on the affected station. Switch the ignition off, disconnect C102B and C102D, and protect the battery-fed cable from grounding before restarting at idle. Noise remaining directs audio-system diagnosis for the fitted touchscreen or non-touchscreen system. Noise disappearing directs generator replacement.

steps.title: Test E: inspect and test the current-sensor circuits
steps.body: For P0A5A, inspect sensor damage, corrosion, connector attachment, B+ cable routing through the sensor and trapped debris. P0A5B begins with reference-supply and signal-return checks: each specified voltage measurement must be between 4.8 and 5.2 volts. P0A5C enters the feedback-circuit checks. Follow E5–E8 through shorts to voltage, ground, reference or return, then continuity to the PCM, repairing failed circuits.

steps.title: Complete the current-sensor decision
steps.body: At E9, repair damaged, corroded or displaced terminals and seat the sensor connector correctly. Clear codes in all modules and repeat the PCM self-test. A returning code directs repair or sensor replacement, followed by another clear-and-self-test cycle. Only a fault that returns after this work proceeds to E10 for PCM connection and bulletin checks.

steps.title: Tests F and G: verify the main charging cable
steps.body: Use the 3.7L B3/B4 main-cable checks. After connector inspection, compare C102D pin 1 to ground with recorded battery voltage; it must be within 0.5 volt. Investigate the B+ nut, MEGA fuse and cable if it fails. Then idle the engine with headlamps on and blower high. Place the positive meter lead at C102D pin 1 and the negative lead at battery POSITIVE. The cable drop must be less than 0.5 volt while gently moving the wiring; excessive drop directs connection or cable repair.

steps.title: Separate sense, command and monitor faults
steps.body: Load-test the sense circuit in F4, and in G4 for P0625. Its voltage must remain within ±0.5 volt of battery voltage; failure directs fuse 36 and circuit checks. P0626 proceeds from G3 to monitor-circuit testing. F5–F7 test GENCOM; G5–G7 test GENMON. Follow the specified disconnections and ignition states while checking unwanted voltage, ground shorts and continuity, including the wiring movement checks.

steps.title: Test G: check generator internal resistance
steps.body: After the monitor circuit passes, G8 checks isolated generator B+-to-case resistance; G9 checks each regulator terminal to the case. A failed specified resistance limit directs generator replacement. Passing both checks leads to G10, rather than proving that the generator is serviceable.

steps.title: Compare command and monitor data before the final decision
steps.body: At F8 or G10, reconnect the PCM and fit the specified fused jumper between C102B pins 1 and 2. Compare scan-tool parameter identification (PID) values GENMON and GENCMD while moving the wiring. G10 additionally commands GENVDSD to 14 volts. Agreement within 5% directs generator replacement; disagreement directs PCM checks. Remove the jumper on either outcome. At E10, F9 or G11, repair and reseat PCM connectors, retest and check applicable Technical Service Bulletins before following a persistent-fault PCM replacement decision.

watchFor.title: Battery-positive is the voltage-drop reference
watchFor.body: The loaded main-cable measurement is between generator B+ and battery positive. Measuring to chassis ground instead measures supply voltage and cannot establish that cable's voltage loss.

watchFor.title: A failed fuse needs a cause
watchFor.body: When a MEGA or sense-circuit fuse fails, investigate the possible short using the wiring information before proceeding.

watchFor.title: Fallback output can conceal lost control
watchFor.body: Certain command or monitor faults allow steady fallback charging above the specified engine speed while the charging warning remains active. Do not interpret that output as a passed control test.

notes: Repair connector defects at their root. A fault disappearing after reconnection can indicate an intermittent terminal problem.
The charging diagram includes other engines; use the 3.7L connector and PCM branches.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0A5A is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detects no current through the sensor without accompanying sensor-circuit codes.
diagnostics.next: Start with E2's physical and installation inspection.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0A5B or P0A5C is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P0A5B indicates feedback voltage too low, potentially from an open or ground short; P0A5C indicates feedback too high, potentially from a voltage short.
diagnostics.next: Enter E3 for P0A5B or E5 for P0A5C.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0620 or P065B is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P0620 concerns command, sense or B+ circuit faults. P065B records a reported internal regulator failure.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test F's battery, supply, circuit and comparison checks before replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0625 or P0626 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P0625 indicates low monitor feedback and can also involve sense or B+ supply. P0626 indicates high feedback from an open or voltage short. Either can involve the generator or PCM.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test G, retaining its different P0625 and P0626 routes.

diagnostics.finding: A battery-saver message appears with the engine off.
diagnostics.meaning: Low battery charge or elapsed accessory operation can trigger normal load shedding to preserve starting power.
diagnostics.next: Compare the conditions with charging-system operation before treating the message as a fault.

diagnostics.finding: A load-shed message appears with the engine running, or only on the front audio/information display.
diagnostics.meaning: This pattern indicates that the audio system has detected a fault.
diagnostics.next: Follow diagnosis for the fitted audio system; inspect battery, generator, BJB, C1046 and engine-ground connections.

verification.title: Repeat the specified fault check
verification.body: For sensor work, complete the clear-and-PCM-self-test sequence. For connector repairs, operate the system again. Remove every diagnostic jumper; after a PCM replacement endpoint, clear codes in all modules as directed.

verification.title: Keep a useful measurement record
verification.body: Record battery voltage, main-cable voltage drop, sense-circuit results, PID comparison and returning codes. For radio interference, record whether the noise persisted with the generator disconnected.
