guides.title: Diagnose 3.7L battery-saver messages, current-sensor faults and generator-clutch concerns
guides.summary: Trace battery-saver messages through energy-management checks, test the battery-current-sensor circuits and identify abnormal generator-clutch operation.
guides.introduction: The body control module (BCM) uses the sensor on the negative battery cable to assess battery charge with the engine off. The powertrain control module (PCM) manages generator operation while running. The generator clutch lets its rotor continue turning as the accessory drive slows. [Tests H, I and J](#/document/G1692957) address separate message, sensor and clutch concerns; choose the route matching the complaint.
guides.why: A battery-saver message can reflect charge estimation, communication or connection problems. Sensor codes require circuit checks, while an overheated clutch may point back to belt or tensioner trouble. These distinctions matter because replacing a component without finding the cause can leave the original concern unresolved.
searchTerms: battery saver message with engine running
generator pulley turns freely both ways

when.summary: When a battery-saver message, current-sensor fault code or suspected generator-clutch problem needs investigation.
notes: These routes do not settle every charging-system symptom. Component replacement requires the relevant concern and completed diagnostic branch.

prepare.title: Electrical equipment and readiness
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool with network tests, self-tests and live data, a multimeter, approved terminal probes and a Terminal Release Kit. Follow Diagnostic Methods for battery readiness. Test I requires battery voltage above 12.2 volts throughout, with no charger attached.

prepare.title: Time and bench access
prepare.detail: Allow an undisturbed battery-learning period if H7 requires it. Clutch checks require generator removal, a small screwdriver, a 17 mm hex bit and socket wrench, plus a new pulley cap once the old cap is removed.

steps.title: H1–H2: establish where and when the message appears
steps.body: Perform inspection and verification and correct an obvious cause. Operate the charging system to confirm the complaint. A battery-saver message appearing only in the centerstack with the engine running follows the appropriate infotainment diagnosis: SYNC without a touchscreen, or SYNC 2/SYNC 3 with a touchscreen.

steps.title: H3–H5: check communication and stored faults
steps.body: For other message conditions, network-test the accessory protocol interface module (APIM), BCM and PCM. Resolve failed communication first. If they pass, run the PCM self-test and follow its charging-code chart for related faults. With none, retrieve all continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs); route BCM, audio-module and other charging codes to their respective charts.

steps.title: H6–H7: evaluate the learned battery charge
steps.body: Read the BCM BAT_ST_CHRG parameter identification (PID). At 50% or more, continue to H8. Below 50%, remove accessories from the lighter, power outlets and inverter where fitted. Secure the key away from the vehicle and leave it undisturbed for at least 6 hours. Recheck with ignition on: reaching 50% supports reviewing energy-management operation before return to service; remaining below it leads to H8.

steps.title: H8: inspect the inline connection
steps.body: Check C1046 for secure connection, then disconnect and inspect for corrosion, bent or damaged terminals and pushed-out pins. Correct any defect. If none is found, continue to H9’s BCM connection and operation check described below.

steps.title: I1–I2: begin the battery-current-sensor route
steps.body: Run the PCM self-test. If P0562 is present, follow charging-system Test B before continuing. Otherwise inspect the sensor for damage, corrosion, connector disconnection, ground-cable routing through the sensor and trapped debris. Repair defects and proceed to I14; an undamaged installation proceeds to I3.

steps.title: I3–I6: separate reference-voltage faults
steps.body: Disconnect the sensor as directed and test its reference supply. A reading of 4.8–5.2 volts leads to I7. Above that range, I4 requires temporarily releasing BCM C2280F pin 3 with the Terminal Release Kit and reconnecting the BCM: voltage remaining means circuit repair; no voltage requires restoring the terminal before I15. Below range, I5 checks for a ground short and I6 for an open. Repair failures; passing both leads to I14.

steps.title: I7–I8: test the signal return and respect the stopping point
steps.body: Measure between the sensor reference and return terminals. A reading of 4.8–5.2 volts leads to I10. Otherwise I8 checks the return for voltage to ground: any voltage requires circuit repair. If none is present, stop for a verified, isolated I9 signal-return test. This result cannot be used to advance directly to sensor or BCM replacement.

steps.title: I10–I14: test feedback and confirm the sensor connection
steps.body: Follow I10–I13 in order for feedback shorts to voltage, shorts to ground, opens and cross-shorts to reference or return, observing the specified ignition and connector states. Repair failures. At I14, inspect and repair the sensor connector, reconnect sensor and BCM, clear all module DTCs and self-test the BCM. A returning code directs further repair or sensor replacement; clear and repeat the self-test afterward. Another return leads to I15.

steps.title: H9 or I15: establish whether the BCM concern remains
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect all BCM connectors. Correct corrosion and damaged, bent or displaced terminals, then reconnect so they seat and latch. Operate the system again. If the concern remains, check OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins and follow any matching bulletin. With none applicable, the reached test directs BCM replacement and clearing all module DTCs. If operation is restored, address the connection’s root cause.

steps.title: J1–J4: check the generator clutch on the bench
steps.body: Remove the generator using the [3.7L procedure](#/document/G1692120). Heat damage calls for a new clutch and accessory-drive inspection. Otherwise pry off and discard the cap through its rubber center button. Hold the pulley and turn the shaft with the 17 mm hex bit: clockwise movement must be smooth and free. Roughness or seizure requires a new clutch. Counterclockwise movement must first provide spring resistance; no resistance, or subsequent free rotation, also requires a new clutch. Normal directional behavior leaves other generator faults to further applicable diagnosis.

watchFor.title: A recurring cause of clutch overheating
watchFor.body: A loose accessory-drive belt or weak or binding tensioner can overheat the pulley. A heat-damaged clutch therefore requires accessory-drive investigation as well as replacement.

watchFor.title: Invalid resistance results
watchFor.body: Use each test’s required circuit isolation and ignition state. Do not perform continuity checks through powered circuits or force probes into terminals.

notes: The battery-current sensor on the negative cable and generator-current sensor on the generator battery cable are different components.
Use the shared pulley procedure with the matched 3.7L generator procedure for replacement work. Fit a new cap after cap removal; a normal clutch test alone does not justify generator replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B130C:12 or B130C:14 is recorded in the BCM.
diagnostics.meaning: B130C:12 identifies a short to battery in the battery-current-sensor control circuit; B130C:14 identifies a short to ground or an open.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test I’s circuit branches before selecting a sensor or BCM repair.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1438:03 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM has no current indication from the battery-current sensor, with a frequency-modulated or pulse-width-modulated signal fault.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the sensor installation and connections, then follow the reference, return and feedback tests. The code alone does not establish sensor failure.

verification.title: Confirm electrical results
verification.body: After I14 work, clear DTCs and repeat the BCM self-test. After H9 or I15 connector work, operate the system and verify whether the original concern remains.

verification.title: Record the branch outcome
verification.body: Record BAT_ST_CHRG before and after any relearn, circuit readings, returning codes and clutch heat/directional findings. Identify an I9 stopping point or unresolved generator concern explicitly.

guides.title: Diagnose 5.0L battery-saver messages, sensor connections and generator-clutch faults
guides.summary: Trace battery-saver messages, inspect the battery-current-sensor circuit and identify supported mechanical faults in the 5.0L generator clutch.
guides.introduction: The belt-driven generator supplies regulated electrical power, while the battery current sensor on the negative cable helps the Body Control Module (BCM) monitor battery charge and manage electrical loads. The generator clutch, where fitted, lets its rotor continue spinning as the accessory drive slows. Test H investigates load-shed messages, Test I checks sensor connections and isolated cross-shorts, and Test J separately examines the removed generator's clutch.
guides.why: Message location, stored faults and reported battery charge determine the diagnostic route. Connector damage can interrupt sensor information, while clutch heat damage can originate in the belt drive. Keeping these branches separate prevents an unsupported replacement decision.
searchTerms: battery saver warning with engine running

when.summary: When a 5.0L displays a battery-saver message, records battery-current-sensor faults or needs generator-clutch inspection.
notes: Choose the branch matching the concern; a battery-saver message does not automatically require generator removal.
Replacement decisions require the relevant concern to be present.

prepare.title: Prepare for scan and circuit testing
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting network tests, module self-tests and live data, a digital multimeter, Rotunda Flex Probes and Wiring Diagrams Cell 12. Follow Diagnostic Methods, including battery state of charge above 70%, and inspect fuses, wiring and previous repairs.

prepare.title: Observe Test I and bench-test prerequisites
prepare.detail: Battery voltage must remain greater than 12.2 volts before and during Test I, with no charger attached. Test J requires generator-removal capability, a small screwdriver, a 17 mm hex bit, a socket wrench and a new pulley cap.

steps.title: Identify where the battery-saver message appears
steps.body: Begin Test H with Inspection and Verification in the 5.0L charging procedure and correct an obvious cause. Operate the charging system to establish the complaint. A message appearing only in the centerstack with the engine running leads to SYNC information-and-entertainment diagnosis, using the appropriate touchscreen or non-touchscreen route.

steps.title: Establish communication and follow charging-related codes
steps.body: With ignition on, run the Network Test. The accessory protocol interface module (APIM), BCM and Powertrain Control Module (PCM) must pass; otherwise follow communications-network diagnosis. Next perform the PCM self-test and address battery or charging codes through its chart. Then retrieve all continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Route BCM codes to the charging procedure's BCM chart, APIM or audio control module (ACM) codes to information-and-entertainment diagnosis, and other relevant codes to the general DTC charts.

steps.title: Evaluate the BCM's charge estimate
steps.body: With no relevant codes, read BCM BAT_ST_CHRG parameter identification (PID) with ignition on. At 50% or more, proceed to H8. Below 50%, remove accessories from the lighter, power outlets and any fitted direct-current/alternating-current inverter. Store the key securely away from the vehicle and leave it undisturbed for at least 6 hours. Recheck with ignition on. A reading of 50% or more supports low charge as the possible cause; review energy-management operation with the owner. A lower reading leads to H8.

steps.title: Finish the message branch at H8–H9
steps.body: Inspect C1046 for secure connection, then disconnect it to examine terminals and repair defects. If no concern is found, switch ignition off and inspect every BCM connector. Replace damaged, corroded or displaced terminals as required, clean module pins and reconnect securely. Operate the system. If the concern persists, check applicable technical service bulletins through OASIS. Follow an applicable bulletin; only when none addresses the continuing concern does H9 direct BCM replacement through the appropriate service procedure.

steps.title: Check sensor connections and code recurrence
steps.body: For Test I, inspect the battery current sensor, disconnect C1646 and check its pins and the battery terminals. Repair damage or corrosion and reconnect C1646. With ignition on, clear all modules' DTCs and perform the BCM self-test. If the target code does not return, address any connector root cause and follow charts for other BCM codes. If it returns, switch ignition off and inspect disconnected C1046 for loose pins, damage, corrosion and water intrusion.

steps.title: Perform the isolated cross-short check, then stop if it passes
steps.body: For I4, keep ignition off and disconnect BCM C2280F, inline C1046 and sensor C1646. Using proper circuit isolation, measure C1046 pin 12 to every other pin on each connector half, testing male and female sides separately. A reading below 10,000 ohms directs repair of the identified shorted wires. If none is below that threshold, further applicable electrical diagnosis is required; these checks do not establish a sensor or BCM replacement decision.

steps.title: Inspect the removed generator clutch for overheating
steps.body: For Test J, remove the generator using the [5.0L removal procedure](#/document/G1692122). Heat damage directs clutch replacement and inspection of the front end accessory drive (FEAD). A loose belt or weak or binding tensioner can overheat the pulley, so investigate that cause as well.

steps.title: Check clutch rotation in both directions
steps.body: Without heat damage, pry the cap off through its central rubber button and discard it. Insert the 17 mm hex bit into the clutch shaft. Hold the pulley firmly and turn the shaft clockwise: roughness or seizure directs clutch replacement. Counterclockwise movement should have spring-like resistance; no resistance directs replacement. If resistance is present, check whether the shaft nevertheless rotates freely counterclockwise; that also directs replacement. Fit a new cap using the applicable pulley procedure.

watchFor.title: A normal direction check has a limited meaning
watchFor.body: Normal clutch movement alone does not authorize generator replacement or complete charging diagnosis. Continue applicable generator fault diagnosis if the concern remains.

watchFor.title: Repair the cause of connector trouble
watchFor.body: Secure reconnection may restore operation temporarily. Address corrosion, water intrusion and damaged or pushed-out terminals rather than treating a disappearing code as a complete repair.

notes: The battery sensor on the negative cable is distinct from the generator current sensor on the generator's positive cable.
The 50% BAT_ST_CHRG branch threshold is separate from the preliminary battery-condition prerequisite.
A passing I4 ends these sensor checks. H9's BCM replacement decision belongs only to the completed load-shed-message branch.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B130C:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM has flagged the battery-current-sensor control circuit for a short to battery.
diagnostics.next: Follow I1–I4; the code alone does not condemn the sensor.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B130C:14 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detects an open or ground in the battery-current-sensor control circuit.
diagnostics.next: Inspect connections and perform the isolated checks. Passing the cross-short check does not rule out an open.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1438:03 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM has no battery-current indication; this code identifies a frequency-modulated or pulse-width-modulated signal failure.
diagnostics.next: Check connections, code recurrence and cross-shorts before further applicable sensor diagnosis.

verification.title: Confirm the applicable branch result
verification.body: After H9 connection work, operate the system and determine whether the original message concern remains. For Test I, retain the BCM self-test result after I2's code clearing.

verification.title: Record measurements and remaining work
verification.body: Record message location, network results, codes, BAT_ST_CHRG before and after any relearn, I4 readings and clutch observations. Identify any required follow-on diagnosis explicitly.

guides.title: Diagnose high voltage, battery discharge or generator noise on the 5.2L
guides.summary: Trace charging complaints through battery and wiring checks, commanded-voltage tests and mechanical diagnosis before selecting a repair.
guides.introduction: The belt-driven generator converts engine power into electrical power for the battery and vehicle. Its internal regulator follows a voltage target from the powertrain control module (PCM). Diagnosis compares the requested output with actual voltage, checks the paths carrying current and separates generator noise from accessory-drive faults.
guides.why: A poor connection can show normal voltage without a load yet lose voltage when current flows. Loaded measurements therefore matter as much as scan-tool readings, and a discharged battery does not by itself prove generator failure.

when.summary: When charging voltage is abnormal, the battery discharges, generator noise occurs or charging-related codes are recorded.
notes: Recent jump-starting or charging can explain stored high-voltage or self-test-range codes.

prepare.title: Electrical test equipment
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool with active commands, digital multimeter, flex probes, fused jumpers and specified circuit loads. The sense-circuit test requires a 250–350 mA incandescent 12-volt lamp; an LED lamp is unsuitable.

prepare.title: Battery and running-engine capability
prepare.detail: Verify battery state of charge exceeds 70%. Tests A and B require battery voltage above 12.2 volts throughout, with no charger attached. Prepare for loaded running tests, stethoscope checks and Test B’s prescribed momentary wide-open-throttle checks.

steps.title: Confirm the complaint and inspect the current paths
steps.body: Inspect battery and generator connections, engine and battery grounds, the high-current battery junction box (BJB), fuses, fusible links and wiring. Check the front-end accessory drive (FEAD), battery condition and abnormal ignition-off drain. Correct obvious faults, record codes and consult applicable technical service bulletins before selecting a pinpoint test.

steps.title: Follow Test A for high voltage
steps.body: After its code check, compare measured battery voltage at idle with generator voltage desired (GENVDSD), a scan-tool parameter identification (PID). A mismatch leads to unloaded and loaded sense-circuit checks, including the specified fuse branch. Continue through the wiring wiggle test, loaded ground checks and generator-output decision in the prescribed order.

steps.title: Complete Test A’s control and supply checks
steps.body: If directed onward, follow A9’s fused-jumper and scan-tool comparison exactly. Its result selects PCM connector inspection or comparison of PCM supply voltage (VPWR) with battery voltage. An inaccurate supply reading requires the specified loaded PCM power and ground checks before the module decision.

steps.title: Follow Test B for low voltage or discharge
steps.body: Inspect generator connectors, its positive supply connection and the specified high-current fuse. Perform loaded positive-cable and ground voltage-drop tests, then command GENVDSD to 14 volts. If battery voltage fails to follow within ±0.5 volt, continue to clutch Test J before choosing generator or clutch replacement. Otherwise follow VPWR, loaded PCM supply/ground and repeated acceleration checks. Normal results with no connector fault lead to the battery drain test.

steps.title: Follow Test C for mechanical noise
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect the belt, tensioner and generator mounting for damage, looseness or misalignment. If satisfactory, use a stethoscope or equivalent with the engine running to locate the noise. A different source requires engine diagnosis. Confirmed generator noise leads to clutch Test J: a failed clutch directs clutch replacement; a passing clutch directs generator replacement.

steps.title: Make the final PCM decision
steps.body: At the Test A or B module branch, switch ignition off, repair corrosion or damaged and displaced terminals, then reconnect and retest. Replace the PCM only if the concern persists and no applicable bulletin redirects the repair. That replacement branch requires clearing diagnostic trouble codes in all modules.

steps.title: Prepare separately for radio-interference diagnosis
steps.body: Radio interference routes to Test D. Restore original audio equipment before testing and inspect aftermarket wiring for generator-circuit connections or proximity. During the disconnected-generator test, keep engine speed below 2,000 rpm: exceeding it can make the generator self-excite and requires switching ignition off and restarting the test.

watchFor.title: Faults hidden by unloaded readings
watchFor.body: Passing an unloaded voltage check does not establish that a connection can carry current.

watchFor.title: Terminal and belt damage
watchFor.body: Use flex probes for test connections; keep listening equipment clear of the moving accessory drive.

notes: Load-shed and Battery Saver messages route to Test H. A warning indicator that is always or never on, without charging codes, routes to instrumentation diagnosis.
Other body control module codes follow that module’s diagnostic chart.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0563 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detected excessive system voltage.
diagnostics.next: Use Test A, considering recent charging or jump-start history.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0562 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: System voltage stayed below the PCM’s desired generator voltage.
diagnostics.next: Use Test B.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1397 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Voltage was outside the self-test range; recent jump-starting or discharge can contribute.
diagnostics.next: With P0562 use Test B; with P0563 use Test A.

diagnostics.finding: Generator control or field-circuit codes are recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P0620 and P065B concern generator control; P0625 and P0626 identify low or high field-terminal circuit conditions.
diagnostics.next: Use Test F for P0620/P065B and Test G for P0625/P0626. Tests A and B divert to these circuit tests when specified.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0A5A, P0A5B or P0A5C is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The generator current-sensor circuit has a range/performance, low or high condition respectively.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test E; these codes do not establish generator failure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B130C:12, B130C:14 or B1438:03 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These identify load-shed circuit short-to-battery, short-to-ground/open or battery-current-sensor signal faults respectively.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test I.

verification.title: Retest the original concern
verification.body: Operate the system under the selected test’s conditions. A currently absent concern does not justify component replacement.

verification.title: Retain measured results
verification.body: Record battery voltage, relevant commanded and measured PIDs, and loaded circuit readings. Document whether the final branch resolved the fault or directed battery-drain, clutch or other diagnosis.

guides.title: Investigate 5.2L battery-saver warnings, current-sensor faults and clutch operation
guides.summary: Follow the 5.2L load-shed diagnostic, check sensor connections and cross-shorts, and assess abnormal generator-clutch behavior.
guides.introduction: The 5.2L charging system combines regulated generator output with battery monitoring and load management. A current sensor on the negative battery cable supplies information used by the Body Control Module (BCM). Separately, the generator clutch allows the rotor to keep turning when the accessory drive slows. This guide follows three branches: battery-saver messages, initial sensor-circuit checks and mechanical clutch inspection.
guides.why: A battery-saver warning needs its display location, network status and battery information checked together. The 5.2L sensor prechecks also include a specified battery-junction-box fuse. Clutch testing examines a different failure mechanism and requires removal of the generator.
searchTerms: generator clutch free in both directions

when.summary: When a 5.2L has a load-shed message, battery-current-sensor codes or a generator clutch requiring mechanical examination.
notes: Select Test H, I or J according to the concern; they are separate diagnostic routes.
Confirm the concern is present before following a component-replacement decision.

prepare.title: Check battery condition and arrange diagnostic access
prepare.detail: Use a module-capable scan tool, digital multimeter, Rotunda Flex Probes and Wiring Diagrams Cell 12. Follow Diagnostic Methods, including battery state of charge above 70%. For sensor faults, inspect the sensor, its connector and battery junction box (BJB) fuse F7 (60A).

prepare.title: Meet the electrical and mechanical test conditions
prepare.detail: Test I requires battery voltage greater than 12.2 volts throughout, with no charger attached. For Test J, arrange 5.2L generator-removal capability, a small screwdriver, a 17 mm hex bit, a socket wrench and a replacement pulley cap.

steps.title: Verify the load-shed complaint before choosing its route
steps.body: Start Test H with Inspection and Verification in the 5.2L charging procedure. Correct any obvious cause. Operate the charging system and establish where the warning appears. If it occurs only in the centerstack while the engine runs, follow SYNC information-and-entertainment diagnosis for the fitted touchscreen or non-touchscreen arrangement.

steps.title: Check the network, then the stored charging evidence
steps.body: Turn ignition on and run the Network Test. The accessory protocol interface module (APIM), BCM and Powertrain Control Module (PCM) must pass; a failure leads to communications-network diagnosis. Perform the PCM self-test and follow its chart for battery or charging codes. If none are present, retrieve all continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Use the charging procedure's BCM chart for BCM faults, information-and-entertainment diagnosis for APIM or audio control module (ACM) faults, and general DTC charts for other relevant codes.

steps.title: Decide whether the charge estimate needs relearning
steps.body: With no relevant codes, read BCM BAT_ST_CHRG parameter identification (PID), ignition on. A reading of 50% or more leads directly to H8. Below 50%, unplug accessories from the lighter, outlets and any fitted direct-current/alternating-current inverter. Keep the key securely away from the vehicle and leave the vehicle undisturbed for at least 6 hours. Recheck with ignition on. At 50% or more, low charge may explain the message; review energy-management operation with the owner. Otherwise continue to H8.

steps.title: Complete the message branch through connector checks
steps.body: Check C1046 security, disconnect it and inspect for corrosion, damaged pins or displaced terminals. Correct defects. If none are found, perform H9 with ignition off: inspect all BCM connectors, replace defective terminals or connectors, clean module pins and reconnect securely. Operate the system. A continuing concern requires an OASIS check for applicable technical service bulletins. Follow an applicable bulletin; if none addresses the concern, H9 directs BCM replacement using the appropriate service procedure.

steps.title: Inspect the sensor connections and repeat the BCM test
steps.body: For I1, disconnect C1646, inspect sensor pins and battery-terminal connections, repair corrosion or damage, then reconnect. For I2, turn ignition on, clear DTCs in all modules and run the BCM self-test. If the target code stays absent, address the connector root cause and use the charts for other BCM codes. If it returns, turn ignition off, disconnect C1046 and inspect for security, damage, corrosion and water intrusion.

steps.title: Check isolated wiring for contact between circuits
steps.body: For I4, leave ignition off and disconnect C2280F at the BCM, C1046 and sensor C1646. Follow the circuit-isolation methods before measuring. On each half of C1046, measure pin 12 to every other pin, checking male and female halves separately. Resistance below 10,000 ohms identifies a short requiring wiring repair. If no reading is below the threshold, stop these checks and obtain further applicable sensor-circuit diagnosis; neither sensor nor BCM replacement follows from this result alone.

steps.title: Look for clutch overheating on the removed generator
steps.body: Remove the generator using the [5.2L procedure](#/document/G1804021). Heat damage directs replacement of the clutch and diagnosis of the front end accessory drive (FEAD). Inspect the drive because a loose belt or weak or binding tensioner can cause pulley overheating.

steps.title: Test smoothness and reverse resistance
steps.body: If no heat damage is found, insert a small screwdriver through the cap's central rubber button, pry off the cap and discard it. Hold the pulley firmly while using a 17 mm hex bit to turn the clutch shaft clockwise; it should move smoothly and freely. Roughness or seizure directs clutch replacement. Turn counterclockwise: absent spring-like resistance also directs replacement. If resistance exists, check for free counterclockwise rotation; that abnormal result likewise directs replacement. A new cap must be installed through the pulley procedure.

watchFor.title: A clutch can pass these checks while another concern remains
watchFor.body: Normal directional behavior does not justify replacing the generator. Further applicable generator diagnosis is required when the original concern remains.

watchFor.title: Water and terminal defects need a lasting repair
watchFor.body: C1046 water intrusion, corrosion and displaced pins can disturb sensor information. Correct the underlying defect and ensure repaired connectors seat and latch securely.

notes: These sensor checks end after I4. They do not complete every electrical test or authorize jumping to a downstream replacement decision.
The complete Test H message branch has its own conditional BCM replacement endpoint.
The battery current sensor and generator current sensor are separate components; the latter monitors generator output for powertrain control.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B130C:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM reports a short-to-battery condition in the battery-current-sensor control circuit.
diagnostics.next: Use I1–I4 to inspect connections and isolated wiring; do not select a sensor from the code alone.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B130C:14 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detects an open or ground in the battery-current-sensor control circuit.
diagnostics.next: Follow the connector and cross-short checks. An unresolved open requires further applicable diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1438:03 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM has no battery-current indication, with a frequency-modulated or pulse-width-modulated signal failure reported.
diagnostics.next: Check the sensor connections, code recurrence and isolated wiring before proceeding beyond this diagnostic scope.

verification.title: Check the result where each branch permits
verification.body: H9 requires operating the system after reconnecting the BCM and determining whether the concern remains. I2 establishes whether the target code returns after clearing and the BCM self-test.

verification.title: Preserve a useful diagnostic record
verification.body: Record warning location, network and code results, charge readings before and after relearning, fuse inspection, I4 measurements and clutch behavior. State which further diagnosis or repair is required.
