guides.title: Test battery condition and investigate unwanted battery drain
guides.summary: Use battery-health information, connection checks and an approved battery analyzer to distinguish battery failure from an excessive vehicle drain.
guides.introduction: The maintenance-free 12-volt battery supplies direct-current power and stabilizes the vehicle's electrical supply. Its negative-ground cable system includes battery and generator current sensors. This diagnosis checks the battery itself, its connections and the vehicle's ignition-off demand so that a replacement decision addresses the actual complaint.
guides.why: Battery condition is assessed from terminal voltage under a controlled discharge, rather than voltage alone. Loose connections can interfere with power delivery, an incompletely charged battery can produce misleading retest results, and excessive drain can remain after a new battery is installed.

when.summary: When battery condition is in question, charge repeatedly falls, or battery-health information recommends replacement.
notes: Connected vehicle battery-health data is conditional equipment; verify availability before choosing that branch.

prepare.title: Use the required diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Have a Ford-approved diagnostic battery charger and a diagnostic scan tool for checking connected vehicle data. The work requires safe battery isolation and the capability to perform the separate battery-drain procedure.

prepare.title: Plan disconnection and retesting
prepare.detail: Follow Battery Disconnect and Connect as referenced by the condition test. If auxiliary batteries are actually fitted, they must also be disconnected to remove vehicle power. Fully charge the battery before retesting.

steps.title: Inspect the battery and its power connections
steps.body: Inspect the battery, mounting, wiring, terminals and connectors, including high-current battery junction box connections. These checks identify connection or mounting concerns that must be considered alongside the battery's test result.

steps.title: Establish whether connected health data exists
steps.body: Follow A1 in the [battery condition test](#/document/G1931208). If connected data is available, review its battery-health report. A recommendation to replace the battery directs replacement first, followed by A5 to check for excessive drain. Without that recommendation, continue to terminal inspection; vehicles without connected data also take that route.

steps.title: Check terminals and chassis grounds
steps.body: With ignition off, verify that battery terminals and battery/chassis grounds are clean and tight. Correct any defect and retest the battery. When connections pass, vehicles without a health report proceed to the charger test; vehicles with a report proceed to the drain check.

steps.title: Test the isolated main battery when directed
steps.body: Remove the battery cables using the referenced disconnection procedure and test with the approved diagnostic battery charger. A satisfactory result leads to A5. An analyzer result of REPLACE BATTERY or REPLACE-BAD CELL directs battery replacement through the linked removal-and-installation procedure.

steps.title: Check for excessive ignition-off drain
steps.body: At A5, keep ignition off and reconnect all battery cables. Check applicable technical service bulletins and special service messages for software updates or related conditions. Carry out the separate Battery Drain Check; if drain is excessive, repair the identified circuit.

steps.title: Resolve the remaining replacement decision
steps.body: A normal drain result does not override an analyzer instruction to replace the battery or a bad cell. Follow that replacement instruction where present. Return a faulty lead-acid battery to an authorized recycling facility.

watchFor.title: A replacement does not establish that drain is normal
watchFor.body: The connected-health replacement branch specifically continues to the drain check. Complete that check rather than ending diagnosis when the new battery is fitted.

watchFor.title: An undercharged retest can mislead
watchFor.body: Failure to fully charge before retesting can produce false readings. Preserve the distinction between needing charge and receiving a replacement instruction.

notes: Use the linked drain procedure for its test setup and acceptance criteria; the battery condition test does not specify a substitute current limit.
Connected-data and auxiliary-battery branches apply only when that equipment is present.

diagnostics.finding: Battery terminals or chassis grounds are loose or unclean.
diagnostics.meaning: A connection fault is present and may affect power delivery.
diagnostics.next: Correct the connection condition and retest before interpreting the battery complaint.

diagnostics.finding: The vehicle exhibits excessive parasitic drain.
diagnostics.meaning: An excessive electrical demand remains with ignition off.
diagnostics.next: Identify and repair the responsible circuit through the Battery Drain Check procedure.

verification.title: Confirm the applicable endpoint
verification.body: Verify clean, secure terminals and grounds, the battery-health or analyzer decision, and the drain-check result. After a drain repair, confirm correction using that procedure.

verification.title: Record the evidence for the decision
verification.body: Record whether connected health data was available, its recommendation or the analyzer result, connection repairs and the drain finding. Identify any replacement or circuit repair performed.

procedures.purpose: Battery condition Test A, including connected-data, terminal, analyzer and drain-check branches.
Battery removal and installation when the diagnostic result directs replacement.
Measure and diagnose excessive parasitic battery drain.
General diagnostic prerequisites and sound electrical measurement practices.

guides.title: Charge a Discharged Battery on the 5.2L Mustang
guides.summary: Disconnect the battery and recharge it with the specified diagnostic charger after allowing a cold battery to warm.
guides.introduction: The maintenance-free battery supplies the vehicle's 12-volt electrical system and helps stabilize its voltage. Normal electrical loads continue to draw some power with the vehicle switched off. Extended parking, especially when interrupted only by short drives with heavy electrical loads, can leave the battery partially or deeply discharged.
guides.why: The vehicle charging system maintains charge during normal use, but it cannot quickly restore a deeply discharged battery to near full charge during a brief idle. An external charger is required. Battery temperature also matters because a cold battery does not readily accept charge.
searchTerms: cold battery will not readily charge

when.summary: When the battery is discharged, including after extended parking or repeated short drives with heavy electrical loads.
notes: A discharged battery is not, by itself, proof that the battery is faulty.

prepare.title: Apply the required safety instructions
prepare.detail: Before beginning, read and follow Safety Warnings in General Information. Be able to carry out the battery disconnect and connect procedure.

prepare.title: Use the specified diagnostic charger
prepare.detail: Have special service tool 162-00036, the GR-1-190 Diagnostic Charger, and its manufacturer's operating instructions.

steps.title: Allow a cold battery to warm
steps.body: Before charging, allow the battery to reach approximately 5°C (41°F). This may require 4 to 8 hours at room temperature. Poor charge acceptance while cold should not be treated as a conclusive battery fault.

steps.title: Disconnect the battery
steps.body: Follow [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356) before attaching the charger. Use that procedure for the vehicle-specific disconnection requirements.

steps.title: Connect the charger in the stated order
steps.body: Following [Battery Charging](#/document/G1692355), connect the positive red charger clamp to the positive battery post, then connect the negative black clamp to the negative battery post.

steps.title: Run and finish the charging process
steps.body: Charge according to the charger manufacturer's instructions. Follow its finishing instructions, then use the battery connection procedure when returning the vehicle to service.

watchFor.title: Expecting a short idle to recover a deep discharge
watchFor.body: Use an external charger; brief engine idling is not the specified recovery method.

notes: If the battery is established to be faulty, return it to an authorized lead-acid battery recycling facility.

diagnostics.finding: The battery became discharged during extended parking.
diagnostics.meaning: Normal key-off loads can cause this, particularly when short drives do not replace the energy used.
diagnostics.next: Recharge using the specified process before drawing conclusions about battery condition.

verification.title: Record the charger result
verification.body: Record the charger's final indication and whether its charging process completed. Use its instructions to interpret the result; this procedure supplies no separate voltage threshold.

verification.title: Complete reconnection
verification.body: Confirm the battery has been returned to service using the linked disconnect and connect procedure.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L battery charging procedure, including warming a cold battery, charger identification and clamp connection order.
Disconnect the battery before charging and reconnect it when returning the vehicle to service.

guides.title: Disconnect and reconnect the battery on the 5.2L
guides.summary: Interrupt vehicle electrical power at the negative battery connection, then reconnect the disturbed cables and restore their covers.
guides.introduction: The maintenance-free battery supplies direct-current power and helps stabilize voltage in the vehicle’s negative-ground electrical system. Disconnecting its negative cable opens the normal electrical return path. This job provides that power interruption and restores the connection afterward; positive-cable removal is an additional branch when the work requires it.
guides.why: The important distinction is whether you need to interrupt vehicle power or disconnect both cables. Negative-cable disconnection alone provides the stated power interruption, so the positive terminal need not be disturbed for that purpose. Reconnection also affects learned operating behavior: the powertrain control module (PCM) may need driving time to relearn its adaptive strategy.

when.summary: When repair work requires battery power to be interrupted and subsequently restored.
notes: Disconnecting the positive cable is unnecessary when the purpose is only to interrupt vehicle electrical power.

prepare.title: Access and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have tools for the battery-cover retainers and terminal nuts, with torque control suitable for 44 lb.in (5 Nm). Identify which cable connections the intended work requires.

steps.title: Remove the battery cover
steps.body: Remove the retainers and lift away the battery cover as shown in the [disconnect and connect procedure](#/document/G1692356). This exposes the cable connections.

steps.title: Disconnect the negative cable
steps.body: Loosen the negative-terminal nut and position the negative cable aside so it remains disconnected. Together with cover removal, this completes the prescribed steps for interrupting vehicle electrical power.

steps.title: Disconnect the positive cable only if required
steps.body: If the work also requires positive-cable removal, position its protective cover aside, loosen the terminal nut and move the cable aside. Preserve the negative-first disconnection sequence.

steps.title: Reconnect in reverse order
steps.body: If both cables were removed, reconnect the positive cable and restore its cover before reconnecting the negative cable. If only the negative cable was removed, reconnect that connection. Tighten each disturbed terminal nut to 44 lb.in (5 Nm), then refit the battery cover and retainers.

watchFor.title: Adaptive behavior after reconnection
watchFor.body: Some abnormal driving symptoms can occur while adaptive values are relearned. Their appearance immediately after reconnection does not by itself establish a separate component failure.

notes: The cable system incorporates battery-current and generator-current sensors.

diagnostics.finding: Drive behavior changes after battery disconnection and reconnection.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM may still be relearning its adaptive strategy.
diagnostics.next: The vehicle may need to be driven to allow relearning; no fixed driving duration or distance is specified.

verification.title: Connections and covers restored
verification.body: Confirm every disturbed terminal nut is tightened to specification and the positive-terminal cover, if moved, and battery cover are back in place.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L battery power interruption, optional positive-cable disconnection and reverse-order reconnection.

guides.title: Find a parked battery drain on the 5.2L Mustang
guides.summary: Measure settled battery current without resetting the modules, then isolate an excessive draw to its circuit and underlying cause.
guides.introduction: The battery supplies the vehicle's electrical system even when the engine is stopped. Some modules continue drawing current normally; a drain check establishes whether consumption remains excessive after the vehicle has had time to sleep. It then separates a circuit problem, an awake module, an external input or an unfused load from a battery complaint.
guides.why: Interrupting battery continuity can reset the modules and erase the condition being investigated. Opening doors normally, keeping keys nearby or testing before shutdown has finished can also change the result. A thermal camera helps locate active circuits, but the in-line ammeter provides the current measurement needed to confirm the finding.
searchTerms: module will not go to sleep

when.summary: When the battery loses charge while parked and excessive key-off current is suspected.
notes: Charge and test the battery first using the referenced Battery Charging procedure. Do not begin while deep-sleep or battery-saver warnings are present.

prepare.title: Use suitable electrical test equipment
prepare.detail: Provide a meter that reads milliamps and has 10 amp capability, a 30A fused jumper, wiring diagrams and, preferably, a thermal camera. A test lamp or voltmeter is not an accurate substitute for the in-line ammeter.

prepare.title: Resolve equipment-dependent wake conditions
prepare.detail: If over-the-air updates are fitted and enabled, check the specified Over The Air Update Dashboard and let active updates finish. If an automatic-transmission gear-position display is fitted, verify Park indication and operation.

steps.title: Activate the systems and prepare the parked vehicle
steps.body: Drive for at least 5 minutes over 48 km/h (30 mph). Disable approach detection and the perimeter alarm if fitted, then park and switch off. Open the hood and doors and manually close their latch mechanisms with a suitable tool so access can remain open during testing.

steps.title: Make every test location accessible
steps.body: Use Wiring Diagrams Cell 13 to identify fuse boxes and arrange access without switching on lights. If auxiliary batteries are actually fitted, disconnect them through the referenced Battery Disconnect procedure so the primary-battery measurement includes all draws.

steps.title: Insert the meter without breaking continuity
steps.body: Connect the fused jumper between the negative battery cable and post, then disconnect the cable while preserving that bridge. Lock with the key fob and move all keys/fobs at least 50 feet away. Connect the meter between the negative cable terminal and post, then remove the jumper.

steps.title: Let the vehicle sleep and measure
steps.body: Wait at least 90 minutes, allowing for region and vehicle options. Note the current and compare with a similarly equipped vehicle. Use the thermal camera, if available, to inspect the fuse panel and battery junction box for a suspect heat signature.

steps.title: Identify the fused circuit
steps.body: For excessive current, remove main-box fuses one at a time and note the drop. When a fuse brings current to an acceptable level, reinstall it and allow another shutdown period of at least 90 minutes before continuing.

steps.title: Separate the circuit's loads
steps.body: Continue with subsystem fuses and component disconnections, leaving them disconnected until isolation is finished. If necessary, remove all relevant fuses and test each individually by installing, measuring and removing it. Isolate aftermarket electrical connections from factory wiring; disconnect suspected modules individually and check their hardwired and network inputs before condemning a module.

steps.title: Investigate feeds outside the fuse boxes
steps.body: If the draw remains unexplained, use the wiring diagrams to find battery feeds that bypass the fuse boxes and isolate them. Disconnect the generator electrical connections and retest if necessary; an internal generator short can cause a drain.

steps.title: Restore connections and initialization
steps.body: After testing, restore the disconnected circuits and battery connections. Perform Power Door Window Initialization if one-touch-up windows are fitted. Use the complete [Battery Drain Check](#/document/G1692357) for the isolation sequence and referenced supporting procedures.

watchFor.title: Resetting the test
watchFor.body: Refit the fused jumper before changing meter settings or lead sockets. If continuity is broken, repeat the shutdown waiting procedure.

watchFor.title: Mistaking an awake module for a failed module
watchFor.body: A module may be responding correctly to an incorrect input. Establish what keeps it awake before choosing a repair.

notes: Apply optional-equipment branches only to verified fitment. The shared power roller shutter initialization branch is outside this Mustang job.

diagnostics.finding: Settled current exceeds the applicable factory-equipment allowance in the 25–50 mA range.
diagnostics.meaning: The parked draw is excessive for the vehicle's equipment; continuous module consumption alone is not necessarily abnormal.
diagnostics.next: Isolate fuses and loads while preserving valid shutdown conditions.

diagnostics.finding: The drain is approximately 1 amp.
diagnostics.meaning: A continuously illuminated engine-compartment, glove-compartment or interior lamp is a typical possibility, not a confirmed diagnosis.
diagnostics.next: Check those loads and confirm the responsible circuit by its measured current drop.

verification.title: Confirm an acceptable settled draw
verification.body: After correcting the cause, repeat the settled-current measurement under the same shutdown conditions.

verification.title: Record the electrical result
verification.body: Record the initial and final current, shutdown waiting period, isolating fuse or component, and any input found to be keeping a module awake.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L battery drain measurement, uninterrupted meter connection, sleep timing, fused and unfused circuit isolation, and applicable initialization.

guides.title: Replace and route the Mustang battery cable assembly
guides.summary: Remove and reinstall the battery cable assembly using the correct engine-specific connections, supports and transmission branches.
guides.introduction: The battery cables connect the battery to the vehicle’s electrical system and provide its ground return. The assembly also carries battery and generator current sensors, so replacement involves smaller electrical connections as well as heavy cable terminals. This job follows the cable from the battery area around the engine and gearbox, restoring every attachment during installation.
guides.why: Cable routing and supports keep the assembly positioned without pulling on terminals or leaving wiring free to rub. Correct tightening matters at each attachment, but a drawing’s torque belongs to its particular fastener. Similar-looking layouts and repeated callout numbers do not make engine variants interchangeable.

when.summary: When a battery cable assembly needs replacement or its routing, connections or retaining points need correction.
notes: These procedures cover cable connections and routing; removal of obstructing components requires their separate access procedures.

prepare.title: Match the vehicle layout
prepare.detail: Select the appropriate engine procedure and identify transmission-dependent branches. The general Battery Cables procedure includes 5.2L applicability and retains its own equipment conditions.

prepare.title: Lifting and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Use a suitable hoist, terminal and fastener tools, and torque tools covering the selected procedure’s specifications. Locate the marked lifting points and check adapter clearance.

prepare.title: Plan access
prepare.detail: Arrange access to the battery area, engine-front connections, generator, starter and gearbox route. Obtain the Battery Disconnect and Connect procedure before beginning.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle and isolate the battery
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on the hoist using the lifting procedure. Disconnect the battery using the dedicated procedure before releasing cable connections. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

steps.title: Release the battery-area attachments
steps.body: Follow the matching drawing for the terminal clamps, adjacent battery-top cable connection, body-side cable eyelets, battery junction box terminals and support bracket. Release the separately marked connectors and retainers too. Treat these as distinct attachment groups so each returns to its original location.

steps.title: Follow the front-engine route
steps.body: Release the indicated plugs and retainers along the lower/front engine route. The 2.3L and 3.7L drawings distinguish these from later threaded attachments. The 5.0L and general procedures also identify a support-bracket fastener below the crank pulley; its tightening specification does not apply to surrounding clips or plugs.

steps.title: Disconnect generator and starter branches
steps.body: Follow the generator drawing for its output terminal, separate plug and retainers. The 2.3L layout additionally identifies a support bracket below the generator and a threaded hex-base component distinct from its plug. At the starter, identify the large cable terminal and smaller control terminal by their actual positions. Follow the 3.7L drawing for its additional eyelet and support attachment, or the 5.0L/general drawing for its engine-side eyelet.

steps.title: Release the applicable gearbox branch
steps.body: The 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L procedures make the rearward branch and subsequent gearbox connections manual-transmission-only. Follow each layout’s marked plugs and retaining positions. The general procedure instead marks one lower/rear connection as optional and includes a bellhousing-area harness bracket; do not import the other articles’ manual-only condition. Once all applicable attachments are released, remove the assembly.

steps.title: Install in reverse order
steps.body: Return the assembly along the prescribed route, restoring gearbox attachments, engine connections, supports and battery-area connections in reverse removal order. Reconnect the indicated sensor and harness plugs. Tighten each threaded attachment to its own drawing specification, restore protective terminal covers and complete the Battery Disconnect and Connect procedure.

watchFor.title: Changing callout numbers
watchFor.body: Starter terminal callout numbers differ between engine drawings. Identify the physical terminal before choosing its torque.

watchFor.title: Unidentified connections
watchFor.body: Use the illustrated location for unlabelled plugs and the optional gearbox connection; do not assume a sensor identity.

notes: Manual-transmission illustrations in the named engine procedures describe the automatic layout as similar, while retaining explicit manual-only branches.

verification.title: Check routing and retention
verification.body: Compare the installed assembly with the applicable drawings. Confirm every required clip, bracket, eyelet, plug and protective cover is restored without straining the wiring.

verification.title: Check fastening and reconnection
verification.body: Confirm each terminal and support fastener received its own specified torque, then verify completion of the battery connection procedure.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L EcoBoost cable removal, routing, fastener specifications and reverse-order installation.
3.7L Duratec cable removal, engine attachments, manual-transmission branches and installation.
5.0L cable removal, engine attachments, manual-transmission branches and installation.
General cable removal and installation, including 5.2L applicability and its optional gearbox connection.
Correct lifting points, vehicle support and hoist-clearance precautions.
Battery isolation before removal and reconnection after installation.

guides.title: Replace and correctly position the battery current sensor
guides.summary: Replace the battery current sensor while preserving its cable position and installing its tape tab facing away from the battery.
guides.introduction: The battery current sensor monitors current flowing through the battery cable. It is a separate component attached to the cable, rather than the battery itself. The cable system also includes a generator current sensor, so identifying the correct sensor matters. This replacement depends on preserving both the battery sensor’s location along the cable and its direction.
guides.why: The sensor must be installed in the proper position and orientation to function correctly. An index mark preserves its original location after removal, while the tape tab provides a clear orientation reference. Fresh electrical tape secures the refitted sensor; reconnecting its plug alone does not complete the installation.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the battery current sensor requires replacement or removal.
notes: This replacement procedure does not establish the cause of a battery or charging complaint.

prepare.title: Prepare marking and fastening materials
prepare.detail: Have a suitable cable-marking method, electrical tape, tools for the battery-cover retainers and cable nut, and a torque wrench.

prepare.title: Identify the sensor and its orientation
prepare.detail: Use the battery current sensor illustration to locate the component. Be ready to note the tape-tab direction and mark the cable before removing the original tape.

steps.title: Expose and identify the sensor
steps.body: Follow [Battery Current Sensor](#/document/G1692364). Remove the battery-cover retainers and cover. Note the orientation and position of the sensor’s tape tab before disturbing the cable.

steps.title: Free the cable and mark the location
steps.body: Remove the nut, disconnect the battery cable retainer and position the cable as directed. Disconnect the sensor electrical connector. Index-mark the cable at the sensor so its installation location remains identifiable.

steps.title: Remove and position the replacement
steps.body: Remove and discard the tape securing the sensor, then remove the sensor. Position the replacement at the cable’s index mark with its tape tab pointing away from the battery. Secure it with electrical tape.

steps.title: Reconnect and restore the cover
steps.body: Connect the sensor electrical connector. Restore the battery cable position, install the wire retainer and nut, and tighten the nut to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Reinstall the battery cover and its retainers.

watchFor.title: Lost position reference
watchFor.body: Mark the cable before removing the sensor. Its location must be preserved during replacement.

watchFor.title: Reversed sensor orientation
watchFor.body: The tape tab must point away from the battery; correct orientation is required for proper function.

notes: Discard the removed securing tape and use electrical tape for installation.

verification.title: Check before covering
verification.body: Confirm the sensor aligns with the index mark, the tape tab faces away from the battery, and the securing tape and electrical connection are in place.

verification.title: Confirm cable retention
verification.body: Confirm the cable and retainer are restored, the nut is tightened to specification, and the cover retainers are installed.

procedures.purpose: Battery current sensor removal and installation, including cable indexing, mandatory orientation, tape replacement and cable fastening.

guides.title: Remove and replace the battery tray
guides.summary: Remove the battery, refit or replace its supporting tray, and restore the battery hold-down and electrical connections.
guides.introduction: The battery tray forms the mounting base for the battery, while a separate hold-down clamp keeps the battery secured to that base. The battery supplies the vehicle's electrical system and helps stabilize its voltage. Tray work is a mechanical mounting repair, but reaching the tray requires the battery to be disconnected and lifted out first.
guides.why: Following the battery removal sequence keeps electrical disconnection separate from lifting the battery and unbolting its support. During assembly, the tray bolts and battery clamp perform different jobs and have different tightening values. If a new battery is installed at the same time, the battery monitoring system also requires a scan-tool reset after reconnection.

when.summary: When the battery tray needs replacement or removal to gain access beneath it.
notes: Battery replacement is a separate decision from tray replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange battery removal
prepare.detail: Follow the Battery procedure and its Battery Disconnect and Connect prerequisite. Plan a controlled lift clear of the tray after removing the hold-down.

prepare.title: Prepare fastening and reset capability
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastener tools and a torque wrench for the tray and battery clamp. A scan tool is required for the battery monitoring system reset if a new battery will be fitted.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the battery
steps.body: Use the [Battery removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1692362). Disconnect the battery through its referenced procedure, remove the hold-down bolt and clamp, and lift out the battery. This exposes the tray fasteners.

steps.title: Remove the tray
steps.body: Remove the tray bolts and lift out the tray following the [Battery Tray procedure](#/document/G1692365). Keep the tray fasteners distinct from the battery hold-down hardware so their installation requirements remain clear.

steps.title: Secure the tray and battery
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Position the tray and tighten its bolts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). Reinstall the battery and secure its hold-down clamp and bolt to 71 lb.in (8 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the electrical connection
steps.body: Complete reconnection through the battery procedure. If a new battery was installed, use the scan tool to reset the battery monitoring system after the battery is connected.

watchFor.title: Confusing the fasteners
watchFor.body: The tray mounting bolts and battery hold-down bolt use different torque values; apply the value for the actual joint.

notes: If a faulty lead-acid battery is replaced during this work, return it to an authorized recycling facility.

diagnostics.finding: A new battery is fitted during the tray repair.
diagnostics.meaning: The new-battery installation adds a battery monitoring system reset requirement.
diagnostics.next: Carry out the scan-tool reset after reconnecting the battery.

verification.title: Confirm the mounting is complete
verification.body: Check that the tray bolts and battery hold-down have been installed and tightened to their respective values, and that battery reconnection is complete.

verification.title: Record battery replacement and reset
verification.body: Record whether the existing battery was retained or replaced. If replaced, record completion of the battery monitoring system reset.

procedures.purpose: Remove and reinstall the battery tray and apply its mounting-bolt torque.
Remove and reinstall the battery, tighten its hold-down and perform the reset when fitting a new battery.

guides.title: Remove or replace the battery on a 5.2L Mustang
guides.summary: Disconnect and remove the battery, secure it correctly on installation, and reset the Battery Monitoring System when fitting a new battery.
guides.introduction: The maintenance-free battery supplies the vehicle's 12-volt electrical system and helps stabilize its voltage. The cable system includes battery and generator current sensors, so replacing the battery has both mechanical and electronic completion steps. This job covers removal and refitting or replacement; a new battery additionally requires a scan-tool Battery Monitoring System reset after connection.
guides.why: The cables must be disconnected before the battery is lifted out, and the hold-down must be restored to secure it. Correctly completing a replacement also includes the monitoring reset. Power interruption can affect learned engine-control values, so temporary changes in driving behavior after reconnection need to be understood in that context.

when.summary: When a faulty battery needs replacing or the battery must be removed for another repair.
notes: Removing and refitting the same battery does not trigger the new-battery reset instruction.

prepare.title: Access and tightening equipment
prepare.detail: Have tools for the battery-cover retainers, cable nuts and hold-down bolt, plus torque equipment suitable for the specified fasteners.

prepare.title: Replacement capability
prepare.detail: If fitting a new battery, have a scan tool capable of performing the Battery Monitoring System reset.

steps.title: Disconnect the cables in sequence
steps.body: Follow [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356). Remove the cover retainers and cover, then loosen and position the negative cable aside. Move the positive cable cover, loosen its nut and position that cable aside for battery removal.

steps.title: Release the hold-down and remove the battery
steps.body: Remove the hold-down bolt and clamp, then lift out the battery. Releasing the clamp frees the battery from its mounting.

steps.title: Install, secure and reconnect
steps.body: Reverse removal: position the battery, fit the clamp and tighten its bolt to 8 Nm. Reconnect the positive cable before the negative cable, tightening each cable nut to 5 Nm. Restore the positive cable cover and battery cover with its retainers.

steps.title: Complete the new-battery branch
steps.body: After connecting a new battery, use the scan tool to reset the Battery Monitoring System (BMS). If the original battery was refitted, this replacement-specific step does not apply.

watchFor.title: Confusing isolation with removal
watchFor.body: Disconnecting only the negative cable interrupts vehicle power. Physically removing the battery also requires disconnecting the positive cable.

notes: Return faulty lead-acid batteries to an authorized recycling facility.

diagnostics.finding: Driving behavior changes after battery reconnection.
diagnostics.meaning: The powertrain control module (PCM) may be relearning its adaptive strategy.
diagnostics.next: The vehicle may need to be driven for relearning. This observation alone does not establish a battery fault.

verification.title: Confirm installation
verification.body: Confirm the hold-down, both cable connections, protective covers and retainers are restored at the specified tightening values.

verification.title: Record the replacement reset
verification.body: Record whether a new battery was fitted and, when applicable, completion of the BMS reset after connection.

procedures.purpose: Battery removal and installation for this 5.2L job, hold-down tightening and conditional new-battery BMS reset.
Battery-cover access, cable disconnection and reconnection, cable-nut tightening and adaptive-relearning note.

guides.title: Replace and correctly position the generator current sensor
guides.summary: Replace the generator current sensor while preserving its cable position and installing its tape tab facing away from the generator.
guides.introduction: The generator current sensor is attached to the battery cable near the battery junction box (BJB). It senses current in the cable as part of the vehicle’s electrical system. The cable also carries a separate battery current sensor, so identifying the correct component matters. This repair replaces the generator sensor and restores its electrical connection and physical attachment to the cable.
guides.why: The sensor must occupy the correct position and face the correct direction to function properly. Marking its location before removal preserves information that would otherwise disappear when the securing tape is discarded. Battery disconnection is also essential because the procedure releases a battery-cable connection at the junction box.

when.summary: When the generator current sensor requires replacement or removal from the battery cable.
notes: This is a replacement procedure; it does not establish the cause of a charging-system complaint.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical isolation
prepare.detail: Have the linked Battery Disconnect and Connect procedure available for both ends of the job. Removing the junction-box cover does not isolate the cable.

prepare.title: Gather the fitting materials
prepare.detail: Prepare a way to index-mark the cable, fresh electrical tape, suitable fastener tools and a torque wrench capable of the cable-nut setting.

steps.title: Disconnect the battery and uncover the junction box
steps.body: Complete [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356) for disconnection. Release the BJB cover retainer and remove the cover to expose the cable connection and sensor.

steps.title: Record the sensor position before releasing it
steps.body: Note the position and orientation of the sensor’s tape tab. Remove the cable nut and reposition the battery cable, then disconnect the sensor electrical connector. Index-mark the cable at the sensor so the replacement can return to the same location.

steps.title: Replace and secure the sensor
steps.body: Remove and discard the securing tape, then remove the sensor. Position the replacement at the cable index mark with its tape tab pointing away from the generator. Secure it with fresh electrical tape and reconnect its electrical connector.

steps.title: Restore the cable and battery connection
steps.body: Return the battery cable to position and tighten its nut to 89 lb.in (10 Nm). Install the BJB cover, then reconnect the battery using the linked procedure.

watchFor.title: Losing the original mounting position
watchFor.body: Make the cable mark before removing the sensor or its tape. The replacement must return to that position.

watchFor.title: Reversed sensor orientation
watchFor.body: The tape tab must face away from the generator. A securely taped sensor can still be incorrectly oriented.

notes: The discarded securing tape is replaced with electrical tape during installation.

diagnostics.finding: The fitted sensor is away from the index mark or its tape tab faces the generator.
diagnostics.meaning: Its installation does not meet the required position or orientation.
diagnostics.next: Correct the mounting before completing reassembly.

verification.title: Confirm the sensor installation
verification.body: Check the cable mark, tab direction, fresh tape and reconnected electrical connector before fitting the cover.

verification.title: Confirm electrical reassembly
verification.body: Verify that the cable nut received the specified torque, the cover is retained and battery reconnection is complete.

procedures.purpose: Generator current sensor removal and installation for the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L applications.
Required battery disconnection before cable work and reconnection after reassembly.

guides.title: Replace the alternator on 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines
guides.summary: Isolate the battery, follow the engine-specific access and belt procedure, then replace and reconnect the alternator.
guides.introduction: The generator, commonly called the alternator, uses engine-driven belt rotation to supply electrical power and charge the battery. Replacement involves its mounting, electrical connector and positive charging cable. The four engine variants share that purpose, but their intake access, belt-tensioner work and some tightening specifications differ.
guides.why: Disconnecting the battery ground before working on the positive charging connection prevents an accidental electrical path through a tool. Finger-starting the B+ terminal nut protects the terminal from damage. On the 2.3L, all mounting fasteners must also be installed finger-tight before final tightening so the generator can seat correctly.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established the need for generator replacement, or removal is required for related work.
notes: A charging concern requires diagnosis before deciding to replace the generator.
Select the procedure by engine; the access and tightening details are not interchangeable.

prepare.title: Plan battery isolation and fastening
prepare.detail: Have suitable battery-service, fastener and torque tools. Follow the battery disconnect/connect procedure, with the ground disconnected before generator work starts.

prepare.title: Provide belt and intake access
prepare.detail: Be able to control the accessory-belt tensioner or remove it as the engine branch requires. On the 2.3L, keep debris out of the opened turbocharger intake system.

steps.title: Disconnect the battery ground
steps.body: Begin with the [battery disconnect/connect procedure](#/document/G1692356). Complete isolation before touching the generator connector or B+ cable, the positive charging connection.

steps.title: Open the engine-specific access
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove the engine appearance-cover nuts and bolts, remove the cover and air cleaner, then loosen the charge-air-cooler (CAC) tube clamp and position the tube aside. Prevent all debris entry: even small particles can damage the turbocharger compressor vanes. On the other engines, remove the applicable air cleaner.

steps.title: Release the belt using the correct branch
steps.body: On the 2.3L and 3.7L, rotate the accessory-drive tensioner counterclockwise and position the belt aside. On the 5.0L and 5.2L, remove the tensioner using the respective linked tensioner procedure.

steps.title: Disconnect the generator wiring
steps.body: On the 3.7L, first detach the harness retainer from the valve-cover stud bolt. Disconnect the generator electrical connector, move the B+ protective cover aside, remove the terminal nut and position the cable clear. Keep the protective cover available for reassembly.

steps.title: Remove the generator
steps.body: For the 2.3L, remove the generator nut and bolts, position the battery cable clear and remove the unit. For the 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L, remove the mounting nut and bolt, then remove the generator. Follow the matching engine illustration for the attachment locations.

steps.title: Install and secure the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the applicable removal procedure. On the 2.3L, install every generator mounting bolt and nut finger-tight before fully tightening any of them. Use the selected engine's mounting specification.

steps.title: Reconnect and restore the removed components
steps.body: Finger-start the B+ terminal nut on every variant. Its tightening value is 17 Nm on the 2.3L and 5.2L, and 18 Nm on the 3.7L and 5.0L. Restore the connector, protective cover and applicable cable or harness retainers. Refit the belt or tensioner, air cleaner and any removed tube or appearance cover in reverse order, using their specified tightening values. Finish with the battery connection procedure.

watchFor.title: Resistance when starting the terminal nut
watchFor.body: Do not use tightening force to overcome a nut that has not started correctly by hand.

watchFor.title: Debris at the 2.3L intake opening
watchFor.body: Keep the opened intake path clean throughout removal and reassembly to protect the turbocharger.

notes: The featured mounting illustration is for the 5.0L engine; use the corresponding illustration for other engines.

verification.title: Check restored connections and access components
verification.body: Confirm secured generator mountings, the connected electrical plug, covered B+ terminal, restored retainers and completion of the applicable belt, intake and battery procedures.

verification.title: Record engine-specific tightening
verification.body: Record the engine variant and confirm the mounting and B+ terminal values used match its procedure.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L generator removal and installation, including CAC-tube access and finger-tight assembly of all mountings.
3.7L generator removal and installation, including belt release and valve-cover harness-retainer handling.
5.0L generator removal and installation, with tensioner removal as an access prerequisite.
5.2L generator removal and installation, including its B+ terminal specification.
Disconnect and reconnect the battery before and after generator work.
Remove and reinstall the 2.3L air cleaner.
Remove and reinstall the 3.7L air cleaner.
Remove and reinstall the 5.0L air cleaner.
Remove and reinstall the 5.0L accessory-drive belt tensioner.
Remove and reinstall the 5.2L air cleaner.
Remove and reinstall the 5.2L accessory-drive belt tensioner.

guides.title: Replace the generator clutch pulley
guides.summary: Remove the generator, replace its clutch pulley using the specified impact-tool method, and reinstall it through the matching engine procedure.
guides.introduction: The generator, also called the alternator, supplies electrical power while the engine runs. Its clutch pulley lets the internal rotor continue spinning as the accessory drive slows. Pulley replacement requires removing the generator for bench access.
guides.why: Battery isolation protects the exposed positive connection. Starting threads by hand prevents damage, while the specified tightening method secures the pulley without mechanically locking the rotor.

when.summary: Replace the clutch pulley when inspection or the applicable charging-system tests establish a clutch fault.
notes: At the 5.0L low-voltage test's failed commanded-output check, automatic-transmission vehicles proceed to generator replacement; manual-transmission vehicles proceed to clutch testing.

prepare.title: Safety and capability
prepare.detail: Follow Health and Safety Precautions before starting. Be equipped to disconnect the battery, release the accessory drive and remove the generator.

prepare.title: Bench equipment
prepare.detail: Have a small screwdriver, 17 mm hex tool, socket wrench for clutch testing, impact gun, 75 Nm torque stick and new pulley cap.

steps.title: Isolate power and establish access
steps.body: Disconnect the battery ground through the applicable procedure. On the [2.3L](#/document/G1936311), remove the appearance cover and air cleaner, reposition the charge air cooler tube, then turn the tensioner counterclockwise and move the belt aside. The [5.0L](#/document/G1692122) and [5.2L](#/document/G1804021) require air-cleaner and tensioner removal. Follow the separate [3.7L procedure](#/document/G1692120) for its access sequence.

steps.title: Remove the generator
steps.body: Follow the matching engine procedure to disconnect the electrical connector and protected B+ positive-output cable, then remove the mountings and generator. On the 2.3L, reposition the battery cable as directed.

steps.title: Inspect and uncover the clutch
steps.body: Check for heat damage. Insert the small screwdriver through the cap's central rubber button and pry the cap off. Discard it even if testing establishes that the clutch can remain in service.

steps.title: Remove the pulley
steps.body: Follow the [pulley removal procedure](#/document/G1827428): use the 17 mm hex tool and a couple of short impact-gun bursts. The shaft and rotor will turn. Never insert anything into the generator fins to restrain them.

steps.title: Install and tighten the pulley
steps.body: Start the pulley by hand. Hold its outer diameter and use the 17 mm hex tool, 75 Nm torque stick and impact gun for 3–4 seconds, as specified in the [installation procedure](#/document/G1827428). The tightening specification is 75 Nm; rotor movement remains expected.

steps.title: Cap and reinstall
steps.body: Fit a new cap with its rubber button facing inward. Reverse the matching generator removal procedure, using its fastening specifications. Finger-start the B+ nut before tightening. On the 2.3L, install every generator bolt and nut finger-tight before final tightening. Restore the drive, intake components and battery connection through the applicable procedures.

watchFor.title: Protect the turbocharger
watchFor.body: On the 2.3L, keep debris out of opened intake components; even small particles can damage compressor vanes.

watchFor.title: Investigate overheating
watchFor.body: A loose accessory belt or weak or binding tensioner can overheat the clutch pulley.

notes: The shared pulley procedure's 1.5L generator-access branches do not apply to this Mustang job.

diagnostics.finding: The clutch shows heat damage or fails directional rotation checks.
diagnostics.meaning: With the pulley held firmly, the shaft should turn smoothly clockwise and have spring resistance without free rotation counterclockwise.
diagnostics.next: For the 2.3L, 5.0L and 5.2L, follow Pinpoint Test J. Replace a heat-damaged, rough, seized or incorrectly free-running clutch; investigate the accessory drive when heat damage is present.

diagnostics.finding: The clutch passes within an established low-output or generator-noise diagnosis.
diagnostics.meaning: The clutch checks have not identified the cause of that complaint.
diagnostics.next: The applicable diagnostic path directs generator replacement. Noise or a discharged battery alone does not establish a pulley fault.

verification.title: Check the completed repair
verification.body: Confirm cap orientation and engine-specific fastening requirements, then operate the charging system and recheck the original complaint.

verification.title: Record the outcome
verification.body: Record the clutch findings and whether the original noise or charging concern remains.

guides.title: Diagnose poor radio reception, speed-related volume faults and ignition pops with SYNC
guides.summary: Trace reception, automatic-volume and ignition-popping complaints through their antenna, wiring and control checks before replacing the audio module.
guides.introduction: The audio front control module (ACM) receives radio signals, adjusts speed-compensated volume and mutes its output during starting to prevent speaker pops. Reception also depends on the antenna, its cable and its ground connection. Coupe and convertible antenna arrangements require different diagnostic routes.
guides.why: Electrical interference, corroded antenna mounts and interrupted control signals can resemble an internal radio fault. Testing each path separately establishes which repair is justified.

when.summary: Use when radio reception, speed-compensated volume or ignition-related speaker noise is reproducibly abnormal.
notes: On convertibles, continuous searching can also reflect no available channel in the selected Radio Data System (RDS) category.

prepare.title: Electrical testing and access
prepare.detail: Arrange a multimeter, wiring and connector information, a jumper cable and competence in live electrical and charging-system tests. Antenna testing requires access to the ACM, console cable junction and rear antenna components.

prepare.title: Diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool, the owner's instructions for volume settings, and access to Ford's OASIS technical service bulletins (TSBs). Module replacement also requires configuration capability.

steps.title: Separate engine interference from antenna faults
steps.body: Use Test A for coupes and Test B for convertibles. Compare reception with the engine running and stopped. Engine-only interference leads to the prescribed generator B+ isolation test. Reception restored by isolation directs generator replacement for the actual engine. Otherwise, switch off, reconnect B+, inspect coils and wiring, then investigate body or engine grounding if ignition components pass.

steps.title: Check the coupe grid and AM supply branch
steps.body: For reception faults not confined to engine operation, compare coupe reception with rear defrost activated and deactivated. Defrost-only interference directs careful antenna-grid inspection and repair. AM-only faults proceed through A5–A7 or B4–B6 for amplifier-feed voltage, shorts and continuity; FM or combined complaints proceed to coaxial-cable testing.

steps.title: Isolate the antenna cables
steps.body: Follow A8–A15 or B7–B14 to test the front cable first, then reconnect the console junction and test the rear section. Check unwanted voltage, core-to-ground isolation, core and shield continuity, and core-to-shield isolation in order. Repair or replace the section that fails, using the specified ignition and disconnection states.

steps.title: Distinguish antenna failure from mounting corrosion
steps.body: Next test the coupe amplifier or convertible right-hand rear fender mast unit for shorts and grounding. Poor body grounding with sound shield-to-base continuity directs corrosion repair and correct mounting torque; failed internal continuity directs replacement. On coupes, also inspect the on-glass antenna circuits and connections before the final ACM check.

steps.title: Test speed-compensated volume
steps.body: Test C first checks the speedometer; incorrect operation redirects diagnosis to instrumentation. Compare volume at different speeds with compensation off, then at maximum. Constant volume when off and speed-related changes at maximum establish normal operation. Otherwise retrieve continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs); U0155:00 redirects to Test AI, while its absence leads to C4.

steps.title: Check the start-muting signal
steps.body: For ignition pops, Test D checks whether the ACM receives its starting signal. With ignition off, disconnect the ACM and specified powertrain control module connector and remove the battery junction box starter relay. Follow D1's distinct 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L/5.2L connector instructions. Repair a failed start-sense continuity path before proceeding to D2.

steps.title: Complete the ACM decision
steps.body: At A22, B20, C4 or D2, inspect ACM connectors for corrosion, damaged terminals and pushed-out pins. Repair, reconnect and latch them, then reproduce the complaint. If it persists, follow an applicable TSB; without one, the branch directs ACM replacement. If it clears, address the connection's underlying defect.

steps.title: Preserve replacement configuration
steps.body: Before module removal, start the scan-tool session and obtain original configuration data. Follow ACM installation and programmable module installation (PMI) instructions. Reflashing unchanged software does not repair hardware; separate reprogramming is limited to published TSB directions.

steps.title: Begin low-frequency-noise checks
steps.body: For the 2.3L/5.2L low-frequency-noise complaint, check audio-system modifications and obstructed fitted midwoofer outlets. On vehicles with active noise control (ANC), microphone installation or damage is another possible cause. These preliminary checks and the codes below do not establish a failed controller.

watchFor.title: Exposed generator cable
watchFor.body: The disconnected B+ battery-positive terminal must never contact a conductive surface; the isolation test can otherwise cause injury or vehicle damage.

watchFor.title: Fragile glass conductors
watchFor.body: The coupe's grid material lies on the glass surface and can be scraped away during inspection or cleaning.

notes: ANC is identified for the 2.3L. The 2.3L and 5.2L both have additional control electronics integrated into the ACM; apply noise-control checks to the fitted function.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0155:00 is recorded in an audio module.
diagnostics.meaning: Test C requires a separate diagnostic branch before an ACM decision.
diagnostics.next: Continue with Pinpoint Test AI.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3000:92 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The integrated controller detected ANC performance or incorrect operation during the Active Diagnostics Test.
diagnostics.next: Complete noise-control diagnosis after the modification, obstruction and microphone checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3000:94 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The integrated controller detected unexpected ANC operation.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the noise-control system; the code alone does not justify replacement.

verification.title: Repeat the original operating conditions
verification.body: Recheck reception under its triggering conditions, Test C's off/maximum volume behavior, or ignition cycling, as applicable.

verification.title: Record the outcome
verification.body: Record the failed test, measurements, retrieved codes and final operation. After reprogramming, clear communication codes generated by that process.

guides.title: Separate 2.3L active-noise symptoms from distortion and missing sound on SYNC vehicles
guides.summary: Classify engine-related noise, isolate local speaker distortion, and follow the appropriate electrical tests for total silence or an inoperative left-front door speaker.
guides.introduction: The audio front control module (ACM) sends alternating-current (AC) signals to the speakers. Poor sound can come from the speaker, nearby vibrating trim, wiring or module connections. Active noise control (ANC) adds another possibility on equipped 2.3L vehicles: an engine-related noise may change when ANC is disabled. These checks separate those complaints before a repair is chosen.
guides.why: A noise disappearing when ANC is disabled identifies an operating condition, not a failed microphone. Similarly, a silent speaker may have lost its signal, and distortion may come from trim touching an otherwise healthy speaker. Controlled comparisons prevent replacing the wrong part.
searchTerms: low frequency noise with audio off
left front door speaker not working
audio noise changes when driver door opens

when.summary: Use when low-frequency noise, local distortion, total loss of sound or a silent left-front door speaker is reproducible.
notes: Tests F, G and H cover the applicable SYNC configurations across the listed engines. ANC microphone checks do not apply to 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L.
Shared sound-enhancement equipment on 2.3L and 5.2L does not make the 5.2L an ANC application.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of network tests and module self-tests, an electrical meter, and the connector information in Wiring Diagrams Cells 132 and 13. Live voltage tests require competent circuit identification.

prepare.title: Prepare playback and access
prepare.detail: Have digital media such as a CD or MP3 available for distortion tests, plus access to the affected trim and speaker.

prepare.title: Gate the moving-wheel test
prepare.detail: E4 requires a trained workshop hoist operator and verified lifting guidance. Without those prerequisites, stop after the stationary checks.

steps.title: Select the complaint and check relevant codes
steps.body: Use the matching test in [audio diagnosis](#/document/G1692891). For equipped 2.3L ANC complaints, E1 self-tests the ACM and digital audio control module C (DACMC). Route speaker or ANC-microphone diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) to their respective module charts. Continue to E2 only when those codes are absent.

steps.title: Compare ANC operating states while stationary
steps.body: For E2, close the luggage lid and doors, switch the ignition on and audio off, and compare the symptom before and after starting. Only an engine-on-only symptom advances to E3. In E3, compare the engine-speed range with the driver's door closed, then open to disable ANC. A symptom remaining with the door open returns to ordinary audio diagnosis; disappearance leads to E4.

steps.title: Complete the controlled E4 classification
steps.body: The trained operator must have all four wheels clear of the ground and surrounding objects. With the luggage lid and doors closed, engine running and audio off, compare the symptom through the engine-speed range in various gears, then repeat with the driver's door open. Persistence returns to audio diagnosis. Disappearance supports ANC-dependent classification; stop here before E5–E14. This result does not authorize microphone, DACMC or ACM replacement.

steps.title: Locate distortion with Test F
steps.body: For distortion affecting some speakers, play digital media and use balance and fade to isolate each corner. Pressure on nearby trim that reduces the noise directs trim repair. Otherwise remove the suspect trim and check grilles, joints, handles, locks, harness routing, storage contents, belt anchors and retractors, and fasteners. Check water-shield bonding and ensure it does not obstruct the speaker's air path.

steps.title: Separate water damage from speaker or mounting noise
steps.body: F3 checks the cone, magnet and basket for watermarks. If present, correct the shield or affected seals, dry the speaker and retest. Without watermarks, F4 removes the speaker while leaving it connected and holds it clear of surrounding surfaces during playback. Persistent noise calls for speaker replacement; disappearance directs repair of the surrounding noise source.

steps.title: Trace total silence through Test G
steps.body: G1 checks ACM network communication; failure goes to network diagnosis. G2 checks the powertrain control module (PCM) for P0616 or P0617 and redirects either code to the engine-specific Starting System procedure. Otherwise, G3 switches ignition off and disconnects ACM C240A, the starter relay and PCM C175B. With ignition on, any voltage from C240A pin 3 to ground requires circuit repair; no voltage leads to G4.

steps.title: Test the silent left-front door speaker with H
steps.body: Disconnect door-speaker connector C523 with ignition off, then operate AM/FM audio. Fluctuating AC voltage between pins 1 and 4 directs speaker replacement. Otherwise H2 disconnects the ACM and left-front tweeter and checks for unwanted voltage. With ignition off, H3–H5 then check shorts to ground, continuity and wires shorted together. Repair failed circuits; use the exact connector setup and limits in Test H before advancing to H6.

steps.title: Finish G4 or H6 before considering the ACM
steps.body: Inspect ACM connectors for corrosion, damaged or pushed-out pins; repair and latch them securely before retesting. If the fault remains, check OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins and follow any matching bulletin. With none applicable, these branches direct ACM replacement. Capture vehicle configuration with the scan tool before removal, then follow the ACM procedure and programmable module installation requirements.

watchFor.title: A shared circuit can silence either speaker
watchFor.body: The left-front door speaker and A-pillar tweeter share an audio signal. Their shared circuit codes do not identify which speaker has failed; Test H specifically addresses the door-speaker complaint.

watchFor.title: Repair the cause of loose connections
watchFor.body: Sound returning after reconnecting the ACM is not a reason to ignore corrosion or displaced terminals.

notes: The ACM and integrated DACMC support programmable module installation; their configuration chart lists no separate adaptive learning requirement.
Reinstalling the same software does not repair a hardware fault. Follow published bulletin guidance for reprogramming.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1142:27 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The ACM detected a short to voltage on its start-signal circuit. The described 3.7L start-muting arrangement can then suppress audio continuously while warning chimes sound only from the instrument cluster.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test G and the applicable engine wiring; do not treat the code alone as an ACM failure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0616 or P0617 is recorded in the PCM.
diagnostics.meaning: Test G requires starting-system diagnosis before continuing the audio investigation.
diagnostics.next: Use the Starting System reference matching the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.

diagnostics.finding: B1A01:01, B1A01:11, B1A01:12 or B1A01:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These indicate general electrical failure, short to ground, short to voltage or an open respectively on the shared left-front speaker circuits. B1A01:11 and B1A01:12 disable the output.
diagnostics.next: For a silent door speaker, follow H1–H6 to distinguish speaker, wiring and module-connection faults.

verification.title: Repeat the relevant operating check
verification.body: After repair, repeat digital-media playback for distortion or the applicable sound-output test. Confirm the original complaint is absent.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record codes, circuit readings and the repair decision. For ANC classification, record engine and door states and whether E4 was completed; do not record classification alone as a completed repair.

procedures.purpose: SYNC diagnosis: bounded 2.3L ANC classification in E1–E4, local distortion in F, total silence in G and left-front door-speaker diagnosis in H.
Confirm audio equipment and the distinction between 2.3L ANC applicability and shared sound-enhancement equipment.

guides.title: Diagnose silent tweeters and right-side speakers with SYNC
guides.summary: Use individual speaker signal and circuit tests to distinguish speaker faults from wiring or audio-module faults.
guides.introduction: The six-speaker SYNC system's Audio Front Control Module (ACM) supplies electrical audio signals to the speakers. The right front door speaker and A-pillar tweeter share a signal. These checks establish whether a silent speaker receives that signal, then examine its wiring before considering the ACM.
guides.why: Silence does not necessarily mean a speaker has failed. A circuit fault can interrupt the signal or make the ACM disable an output. Disconnecting the specified companion speaker prevents that shared branch from confusing wiring measurements.
searchTerms: left A-pillar tweeter has no sound
right front door speaker not working

when.summary: When an A-pillar tweeter, right front door speaker or convertible right rear quarter-panel speaker is silent.
notes: Choose the test by speaker location and body style.

prepare.title: Prepare the measuring equipment
prepare.detail: Use a meter capable of alternating-current audio, direct-current voltage and resistance measurements, plus Wiring Diagrams Cell 132 and connector views. A diagnostic scan tool supports fault-code reading and replacement-module configuration.

prepare.title: Plan component access
prepare.detail: Use the appropriate speaker and ACM removal procedures. Switch ignition off before the specified disconnections; operate the audio system or switch ignition on only where directed.

steps.title: Select the exact speaker test
steps.body: In the [speaker diagnostic procedure](#/document/G1692891), Test I addresses the left front A-pillar tweeter; J addresses the right front A-pillar tweeter; K addresses the right front door speaker; L addresses the convertible's right rear quarter-panel speaker. Each begins by checking the audio signal.

steps.title: Check whether audio reaches the connector
steps.body: With ignition off, disconnect the affected speaker, then operate AM/FM radio. Measure fluctuating alternating-current voltage across the harness terminals: I uses C9063 pins 1 and 3; J uses C9065 pins 1 and 3; K uses C612 pins 1 and 4; L uses C396 pins 1 and 4. A fluctuating signal directs replacement of that speaker. No signal leads to wiring tests.

steps.title: Isolate the circuit correctly
steps.body: Switch ignition off and disconnect ACM C240A. For I, also disconnect left front door speaker C523; for J, disconnect right front door speaker C612; for K, disconnect right tweeter C9065. Test L specifies no additional companion-speaker disconnection.

steps.title: Check unwanted voltage and grounding
steps.body: With ignition on, measure each specified speaker wire to ground. Any voltage directs circuit repair. If none is present, switch ignition off and measure resistance from each wire to ground. Both readings must exceed 10,000 ohms; otherwise repair the affected circuit.

steps.title: Check continuity and separation
steps.body: Follow the selected test's terminal map to measure each wire back to C240A; each must be below 3 ohms. Then measure between the speaker wires: resistance must exceed 10,000 ohms. Failed continuity identifies an interrupted path; failed separation identifies unwanted contact between the wires. Repair the circuit that fails.

steps.title: Resolve connectors before replacing the ACM
steps.body: If wiring passes, switch ignition off and inspect all ACM connectors. Clean corrosion or replace damaged terminals, including bent or pushed-out pins. Reconnect until seated and latched, then operate the system. If silence persists, check OASIS for applicable Technical Service Bulletins (TSBs); follow one if present. Otherwise, the test directs ACM replacement. Begin a scan-tool session before removal to capture configuration, then follow the SYNC ACM procedure and Programmable Module Installation (PMI) process.

watchFor.title: Disabled output
watchFor.body: A short-circuit code can explain an absent audio signal without proving the speaker or ACM has failed.

watchFor.title: Temporary recovery
watchFor.body: Sound returning after connector reconnection still requires correction of the underlying pin or connector problem.

notes: B1A02 codes concern the shared right front circuits. B1A03 codes concern the convertible's right rear quarter-panel speaker or the coupe's right parcel-shelf speaker. A coupe parcel-shelf complaint requires its body-specific diagnostic procedure before choosing parts.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A02:01 or B1A03:01 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The ACM detected a general electrical failure in the corresponding speaker circuit group.
diagnostics.next: Use the location-specific signal and wiring tests to identify the cause.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A02:11 or B1A03:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A short to ground was detected and the affected speaker output is disabled.
diagnostics.next: Locate and repair the short using the selected circuit test.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A02:12 or B1A03:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A short to voltage was detected and the affected speaker output is disabled.
diagnostics.next: Follow the isolated-circuit voltage check before selecting a replacement component.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A02:13 or B1A03:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The ACM detected an open in the corresponding speaker circuits.
diagnostics.next: Check the mapped wiring and connections; the code alone does not establish speaker failure.

verification.title: Confirm sound after reconnection
verification.body: Operate the audio system with connectors securely latched and determine whether the original speaker complaint remains.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the selected test, signal and circuit findings, repair and final operation. If module reprogramming occurred, clear communication codes generated during programming.

guides.title: Diagnose silent rear speakers or unresponsive SYNC inputs
guides.summary: Distinguish rear-speaker and wiring faults from audio-module, SYNC-module and connected-device concerns.
guides.introduction: The audio front control module (ACM) supplies the electrical signal that drives the speakers. The accessory protocol interface module (APIM) handles SYNC functions associated with phone, voice and media inputs. A silent rear speaker and a system that ignores every SYNC input therefore need different diagnostic paths.
guides.why: An AM/FM signal check separates a speaker-output concern from a SYNC input concern. Network and controlled media tests then establish whether SYNC itself responds. Neither silence nor a circuit code alone proves that a module needs replacement.
searchTerms: SYNC voice phone and media inoperative

when.summary: When a specified rear speaker is silent or SYNC does not respond to phone, voice and media inputs.

prepare.title: Prepare for signal and network testing
prepare.detail: Arrange connector access, a multimeter capable of alternating-current voltage and resistance measurements, a diagnostic scan tool, MIT 105-00120 and Wiring Diagrams Cell 132.

prepare.title: Preserve module configuration
prepare.detail: Before removing a module, let the scan tool identify the vehicle and obtain configuration data. Replacement module configuration uses Programmable Module Installation (PMI).

steps.title: Choose the correct rear-speaker test
steps.body: In [Tests M–O](#/document/G1692891), M covers the coupe right parcel shelf speaker at C485; N covers the coupe left at C484; O covers the convertible left rear quarter-panel speaker at C395. With ignition off, disconnect the selected speaker. Operate AM/FM and measure across pins 1 and 4. Fluctuating alternating-current voltage directs replacement of that speaker; no signal leads to circuit testing.

steps.title: Check the isolated speaker wiring
steps.body: Switch ignition off and disconnect ACM C240A. With ignition on, check both speaker circuits for unwanted voltage. Switch off for resistance tests: each circuit must exceed 10,000 ohms to ground, have less than 3 ohms end-to-end, and exceed 10,000 ohms to its partner. Follow the selected test's pin map and repair any failed circuit before proceeding.

steps.title: Check ACM connections before condemning the module
steps.body: Inspect all ACM connectors for corrosion, bent or damaged terminals and pushed-out pins. Repair, reconnect securely and operate the system. If the concern persists, check applicable technical service bulletins first. Only when none addresses the concern does the branch direct [ACM replacement](#/document/G1704002).

steps.title: Test P: establish APIM communication and input operation
steps.body: For unresponsive SYNC, run the scan-tool network test. An APIM that fails requires [communications-network diagnosis](#/document/G1813071). If it passes, connect MIT 105-00120 and test Bluetooth, Universal Serial Bus (USB) and audio-input-jack output, entering each mode through the VOICE steering-wheel switch.

steps.title: Reset and repeat only as directed
steps.body: If every input works, perform a Master Reset using the owner's instructions and review operation with the owner. If inputs fail, disconnect the battery for 1 minute, reconnect it and repeat the MIT tests. A successful retest also leads to Master Reset and an operation review. If the owner's device alone still fails afterward, the test identifies that device as the fault.

steps.title: Follow the remaining SYNC fault
steps.body: After an unsuccessful power reset, individual failed sources lead to the SYNC symptom chart; a VOICE-switch concern leads to Test X. If all inputs remain inoperative, perform the APIM Hardware Test, which requires the vehicle identification number. This is a diagnostic handoff, not an automatic APIM replacement decision.

watchFor.title: Master Reset erases personal information
watchFor.body: It restores preference defaults and deletes paired Bluetooth devices, the phone book and call histories.

watchFor.title: A disabled speaker output
watchFor.body: Short-circuit detection can disable the output. Establish circuit condition before interpreting silence as a failed speaker.

notes: B1A04 codes below concern the coupe left parcel shelf or convertible left rear quarter-panel speaker.
If all APIM stereo outputs malfunction, the dedicated output branch considers the device, wiring/connectors, APIM and ACM.
ACM and APIM configuration lists no separate adaptive learning or calibration. Reinstalling the same software does not repair hardware.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A04:01 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The ACM detected a general electrical failure in the left rear speaker circuits.
diagnostics.next: Use Test N or O for the body style.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A04:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A short to ground was detected and speaker output is disabled.
diagnostics.next: Follow the applicable speaker circuit checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A04:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A short to voltage was detected and speaker output is disabled.
diagnostics.next: Locate and repair the affected circuit.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A04:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: An open was detected in the left rear speaker circuits.
diagnostics.next: Check the selected branch's continuity paths and terminals.

verification.title: Repeat the affected function
verification.body: Operate the repaired speaker or repeat every SYNC input test. Confirm connectors seat and latch correctly.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record the speaker location, circuit measurements, APIM network result and which MIT inputs passed before and after reset.
