guides.title: Diagnose missing or distorted SYNC audio, voice prompts and microphone input
guides.summary: Separate device, wiring, connector and module faults affecting SYNC music, spoken prompts, microphone input and the audio input jack.
guides.introduction: The accessory protocol interface module (APIM) handles SYNC audio sources and microphone input. It sends stereo music and separate mono audio, including voice prompts, to the audio front control module (ACM). These tests trace where sound is lost before directing a repair or further module testing.
guides.why: Hearing a prompt and having your command recognized test different signal paths. Controlled audio sources separate vehicle faults from device problems, while isolated wiring measurements distinguish unwanted electrical connections from broken conductors.
searchTerms: no sound from SYNC audio sources

when.summary: When SYNC music, voice prompts, voice recognition, outgoing call audio or the audio input jack operates incorrectly.
notes: Choose the branch matching the complaint; these are alternative diagnostic paths.

prepare.title: Prepare for controlled electrical testing
prepare.detail: Use the Multi-Media Interface Tester (MIT) 105-00120, RCA Adapter 105-00121, a voltage/resistance meter and POM6411 back-probe tool. Have Wiring Diagrams Cell 132 and the applicable connector tables available.

prepare.title: Arrange the required capability
prepare.detail: Live signal testing, connector repair and battery disconnection require competent electrical handling. Module decisions also require access to Ford OASIS service information and the vehicle identification number (VIN) for the APIM Hardware Test.

steps.title: Q1: Establish whether every stereo source is affected
steps.body: Test Bluetooth, USB ports and RCA jacks with the MIT and adapter. If every source produces poor, distorted or missing sound, continue to Q2. If only some fail, use the SYNC symptom chart. Correct operation with the tester identifies the customer's device as the concern.

steps.title: Q2–Q5: Trace the stereo signal
steps.body: Play SYNC audio with connectors connected and back-probe ACM C240B using the Q2 terminal table. Fluctuating alternating-current (AC) voltage leads to Q8; its absence leads to Q3. Switch ignition OFF, disconnect ACM C240B and APIM C2383, then switch ON for the short-to-voltage check. Any voltage requires circuit repair. Switch OFF and leave both disconnected for Q4–Q5: ground resistance must exceed 10,000 ohms and end-to-end resistance must be below 3 ohms. Repair a failed circuit; otherwise continue to Q6.

steps.title: Q6: Check the isolated stereo conductors against one another
steps.body: Keep ignition OFF and ACM C240B and APIM C2383 disconnected. Measure between C240B pin pairs 12–13, 12–25, 12–26, 13–25, 13–26 and 25–26. Every resistance must exceed 10,000 ohms to proceed to Q7. Record any failed pair and stop that branch until a repair direction is confirmed. Q7 or Q8 cannot close a failed Q6 result.

steps.title: R1–R2 and S1–S2: Separate prompt and switch faults
steps.body: In AM/FM mode, press VOICE. For the missing-mono-output complaint, a correct prompt ends Test R with an explanation of feature operation. Without a prompt, check the right-hand lower volume, seek/call, VOICE and MUTE switches: failed operation leads to Test X; correct operation leads to R3. For voice-recognition or outgoing-call complaints, a correct prompt leads to S3; no prompt routes through the same switch checks, then R or X.

steps.title: R3–R7: Test the mono audio path
steps.body: With connectors connected, back-probe C240B pins 8 and 21 while repeatedly pressing VOICE in AM/FM mode. Fluctuating AC voltage leads to R9; no signal leads to R4. With ignition OFF, disconnect C240B and C2383, then switch ON for voltage testing. Switch OFF for the ground, continuity and short-together checks, leaving both disconnected. Follow R4–R7 tables: no voltage, ground and inter-conductor resistance above 10,000 ohms, and continuity below 3 ohms. Repair a failed circuit; passing results lead to R8.

steps.title: S3–S7: Isolate microphone wiring before the microphone
steps.body: Switch ignition OFF and disconnect APIM C2383, leaving the microphone connected for S3. Switch ON and test the listed microphone circuits for unwanted voltage. If none is present, switch OFF and disconnect overhead-console microphone C930. Follow S4–S6 for ground resistance, continuity and conductor separation using their exact terminal tables and limits. Repair failed circuits. If all pass, reconnect C2383 and install a new microphone through its replacement procedure. Test a spoken command after the AM/FM-mode VOICE prompt: success identifies the microphone; continued failure leads to S8.

steps.title: T1–T5: Reset and isolate the audio input jack
steps.body: Remove devices from USB and the audio input jack. Disconnect the battery for 1 minute, reconnect it and wait at least 2 minutes before testing jack playback with the MIT. If it still fails, switch ignition OFF and disconnect jack C2362 and APIM C2383. Switch ON for T2 voltage checks, then OFF for T3–T4 ground and continuity checks. Repair failed circuits. Passing results lead to reconnecting C2383, installing a new jack and repeating MIT playback. Continued failure leads to T6.

steps.title: Complete the applicable module decision
steps.body: At Q7/R8/S8/T6, inspect the APIM connector; at Q8/R9, inspect all ACM connectors. Follow the named step with ignition OFF, repairing corrosion, damaged or bent terminals and pushed-out pins, then seat and latch the connectors. Q7/R8/S8 require at least 2 minutes for APIM initialization. Retest. If the concern remains, check OASIS for applicable Technical Service Bulletins (TSBs) and follow one if present. Without an applicable TSB, the APIM branches require its Hardware Test; the ACM branches direct ACM replacement through its complete procedure.

watchFor.title: Probe-induced faults
watchFor.body: Use POM6411 for back-probing. Forcing ordinary probes into connectors can damage terminals and create additional electrical faults.

watchFor.title: Temporary recovery after reconnection
watchFor.body: Restored operation can indicate a connection problem. Correct the underlying corrosion or terminal damage rather than relying on reseating alone.

notes: These Q–T paths belong to SYNC. SYNC 2/SYNC 3 uses separate test numbering and connector assignments.
The MIT receives power from the USB port. The USB1 code information below identifies possible fault areas; it does not complete USB-port diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: The APIM records B1D79:01, B1D79:11, B1D79:12 or B1D79:13.
diagnostics.meaning: Respectively, these indicate no microphone detected during the on-demand self-test, a microphone-circuit short to ground, a short to battery voltage or an open circuit.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test S to distinguish wiring, microphone and APIM causes.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1252:04 is recorded for front USB1.
diagnostics.meaning: The APIM detected a failure in its internal front-USB-port circuitry.
diagnostics.next: Record the finding and continue dedicated USB1 diagnosis before selecting a replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1252:11 is recorded for front USB1.
diagnostics.meaning: A short to ground or over-current condition was detected; the port/cable or customer's USB device can cause it.
diagnostics.next: Continue USB1 diagnosis without treating the code as proof of APIM failure.

verification.title: Repeat the relevant functional check
verification.body: Confirm tester playback, audible prompt operation or spoken-command recognition as appropriate. After a successful jack reset, continued failure limited to the customer's device identifies a device concern.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record the branch, connector states, measured results and functional retest. Keep a failed Q6 pair explicitly unresolved until its repair direction is confirmed.

guides.title: Diagnose SYNC USB, Bluetooth and right-hand lower steering-wheel switch faults
guides.summary: Use controlled device tests and switch-circuit checks to locate SYNC connection faults and unresponsive right-hand lower steering-wheel controls.
guides.introduction: On this SYNC system, the accessory protocol interface module (APIM) handles Universal Serial Bus (USB) and Bluetooth connections. The steering column control module (SCCM) reads steering-wheel switches through wiring and the clockspring. These tests distinguish device, cable, switch, connection and module problems.
guides.why: A USB port can supply power without delivering usable audio. Similarly, a button can move normally while sending an incorrect electrical input. Test equipment and scan-tool readings distinguish these conditions.
searchTerms: steering wheel volume buttons not working
steering wheel voice button not working

when.summary: When either USB port, Bluetooth pairing or the right-hand lower steering-wheel switches fail or behave incorrectly.

prepare.title: Test equipment
prepare.detail: Have USB test unit MIT 105-00120, a diagnostic scan tool, a multimeter and Wiring Diagrams Cell 132. Bluetooth testing also permits MIT 420-373; use an equivalent verification tool only if MIT is unavailable, or a compatible device only if neither is available.

prepare.title: Access and capability
prepare.detail: USB tests require APIM and cable access. Test X can require driver-airbag removal and therefore needs airbag-service capability and the complete removal and installation procedures.

steps.title: Tests U and V: check power and reset the affected USB path
steps.body: With ignition ON, connect MIT 105-00120 to the front port for Test U or rear port for Test V. If it powers up, remove devices from both USB ports and the audio input jack. Disconnect the battery for 1 minute, reconnect, switch ignition ON and allow at least 2 minutes for APIM initialization. Retest with both the test unit and audio system in USB mode. Successful audio confirms recovery; a customer device that still fails is the remaining fault. No power or unsuccessful audio leads to the code check.

steps.title: Read the port-specific codes and inspect connections
steps.body: Clear APIM diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) and run its self-test. Front codes B1252:04 or B1252:11, or rear codes B12B8:04 or B12B8:11, direct cable inspection. With ignition OFF, disconnect the front cable’s black end or rear cable’s grey end at the APIM. Inspect both cable ends and the module port; remove debris. Cable damage requires a new port/cable; APIM port damage directs the VIN-guided APIM Hardware Test.

steps.title: Separate a loose connector from a failed USB cable
steps.body: If inspection finds no damage, reconnect and repeat the USB audio test. Recovery identifies a seating problem. If audio still fails, or the matching codes were absent, install a new port/cable and retest. Continued failure leads to the APIM connector checks below.

steps.title: Test W: verify Bluetooth pairing independently
steps.body: Connect the verification device to USB, select its Bluetooth mode and pair it with the APIM. Monitor scan-tool parameter identifications (PIDs) BT_PAIR and BT_CONN. If both read “Yes,” perform the Master Reset described in the owner’s instructions and review pairing with the customer. Continued failure of their device identifies a device concern. If either PID fails to read “Yes,” continue to APIM connector checks.

steps.title: Test X: compare lower-switch inputs with button operation
steps.body: With ignition ON, monitor SCCM PIDs while pressing each right-hand lower switch. If some, but not all, readings are wrong or stuck, replace that switch pack. If all are wrong, clear instrument panel cluster (IPC) codes, cycle ignition OFF–ON, wait at least 10 seconds and run its self-test. U0212:00 directs IPC diagnosis; otherwise continue to X3. Correct switch readings lead directly to SCCM connector checks.

steps.title: Test X3: check the switch supply safely
steps.body: Turn ignition OFF and wait one minute for backup power to deplete before removing the driver airbag using its complete procedure. Accidental deployment can cause serious injury or death. Disconnect both lower switch connectors, then follow X3’s powered measurements at the switch connector. Approximately 5 volts at the specified points directs replacement of the right-hand lower switch; an unsuccessful result leads to harness tests.

steps.title: Tests X4–X9: isolate the wheel harness and clockspring
steps.body: With ignition OFF and clockspring C218B disconnected, perform the listed harness checks for shorts to ground, opens and shorts between circuits. A failure directs a new steering wheel. If all pass, reconnect C218B, disconnect C218C and perform the corresponding clockspring checks. A failure directs a new clockspring; passing all checks leads to SCCM connector inspection. Use every circuit pair and limit in the test tables.

steps.title: Complete the APIM or SCCM decision
steps.body: With ignition OFF, inspect the relevant module connectors. Clean corroded module pins and replace damaged connectors, terminals or pins. Reconnect and latch securely; allow the APIM at least 2 minutes to initialize. Operate the system. If the concern remains, check OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins and follow any matching bulletin. Otherwise APIM branches require the vehicle identification number (VIN) for the Hardware Test; Test X directs SCCM replacement.

watchFor.title: Master Reset erases personal settings
watchFor.body: It restores preference defaults and deletes the phone book, call histories and paired Bluetooth devices.

watchFor.title: A connection repair needs a cause
watchFor.body: If reseating restores operation, address the underlying connector or pin problem rather than leaving damaged contacts in service.

notes: Before removing a module for replacement, start the scan-tool session and capture configuration. Follow programmable module installation (PMI) requirements for the replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B12B8:04 or B12B8:11 returns during the APIM self-test.
diagnostics.meaning: B12B8:04 reports a detected failure in internal rear-USB circuitry. B12B8:11 reports a short to ground or overload that can originate in the port/cable or customer device.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test V’s inspection and isolation decisions before selecting a module repair.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1380:09, B1380:11 or B1380:17 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These indicate a right-hand switch stuck for more than 2 minutes, a short to ground or a short to voltage respectively. They can concern either the upper or lower switch pack.
diagnostics.next: Use Test X for the lower-switch complaint. An upper-switch complaint requires its corresponding diagnostic path.

verification.title: Prove the affected function
verification.body: Confirm USB audio with the test unit, Bluetooth pairing and connection through both PIDs, or agreement between lower-switch positions and scan readings, as applicable.

verification.title: Record the outcome
verification.body: Record the affected port or switch, returning codes, PID results and the operation restored by reset, reconnection or replacement.

guides.title: Diagnose SYNC controls, display faults and active-noise-control microphone codes
guides.summary: Trace failed SYNC controls and display responses through switch inputs, module communication and isolated microphone circuits.
guides.introduction: On these SYNC vehicles, the front controls interface module (FCIM) receives dashboard button inputs, while the front control/display interface module (FCDIM) presents information. Steering-wheel inputs pass through the steering column control module (SCCM). Active noise control (ANC) uses separate microphones to monitor cabin sound. A failed button, blank screen and microphone circuit code therefore require different tests.
guides.why: Live switch data separates an input problem from a downstream response problem. Network tests establish whether modules can exchange commands. Circuit isolation then distinguishes damaged wiring from a microphone or module fault, avoiding replacement based on the complaint alone.
searchTerms: right steering wheel buttons not working

when.summary: When SYNC controls or the display malfunction, or an applicable ANC microphone circuit code is recorded.
notes: The left rear quarter-panel microphone concern applies to convertibles only.

prepare.title: Provide the necessary diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting network tests, module self-tests, live parameter identifications (PIDs), display commands and module configuration. Circuit work requires voltage and resistance measurement with the exact connector information.

prepare.title: Plan airbag access correctly
prepare.detail: Steering-wheel circuit diagnosis requires competent supplemental restraint system work. Before driver-airbag removal, turn ignition off and wait one minute for backup power to deplete, then follow the complete airbag procedure. Test only the identified switch circuits, never airbag deployment circuits.

prepare.title: Capture configuration before removal
prepare.detail: Start a vehicle-identified scan session before removing modules so configuration can be retrieved for Programmable Module Installation (PMI). Follow each replacement procedure's programming requirements.

steps.title: Y: Compare every upper-right switch with live data
steps.body: With ignition on, monitor the SCCM's Up, Left, Down, Right and OK PIDs while pressing each button. Some incorrect responses direct right-hand upper-switch replacement. If all are incorrect, clear instrument panel cluster (IPC) codes, cycle ignition off and on, wait at least 10 seconds and self-test the IPC. Follow its diagnostic chart if U0212:00 returns. Correct responses lead directly to Y13.

steps.title: Y: Check supply, then isolate the switch wiring
steps.body: After the prescribed airbag removal, disconnect both upper steering-wheel switches. Y3 checks for approximately 5 volts between C2999 pins 2 and 3 with ignition on; that result directs right-hand switch replacement. Otherwise, follow Y4–Y12's exact disconnections and measurements: test the airbag switch harness, steering-wheel harness and clockspring in sequence for ground shorts, opens and wires shorted together. A failed stage directs replacement of its corresponding airbag, steering wheel or clockspring assembly.

steps.title: Y: Check the SCCM connection endpoint
steps.body: At Y13, switch ignition off, inspect SCCM connectors and repair corrosion, damaged or bent pins and pushed-out terminals. Reconnect securely and operate the system. If the complaint remains, check applicable Technical Service Bulletins (TSBs); follow an applicable bulletin, otherwise replace the SCCM. If operation returns, address the underlying connector defect.

steps.title: Z: Diagnose dashboard audio controls
steps.body: Network-test the audio front control module (ACM), accessory protocol interface module (APIM) and FCIM. A failure leads to communications diagnosis. If all pass, self-test all three and follow their diagnostic trouble code (DTC) charts. With no codes, inspect and repair the FCIM connector with ignition off, reconnect and retest. A remaining concern leads to applicable TSB instructions or the VIN-dependent FCIM guided routine.

steps.title: AA: Establish what the display can still do
steps.body: With ignition and audio on, check every FCIM button; incorrect button operation returns to Z. Next network-test the FCDIM. A communication failure follows network diagnosis. A completely blank display goes to AA6 connector inspection. Otherwise, command all liquid-crystal display segments on with LCD_SEG. Missing segments also lead to AA6; if all illuminate, check stored lost-communication codes before proceeding. At AA6, repair and reseat the connector, retest, check applicable TSBs and replace the FCDIM only if directed.

steps.title: AB: Isolate the overhead ANC microphone circuits
steps.body: For B116A:01, follow AB1–AB4 in order. Disconnect ACM C240B with ignition off, then perform the specified ignition-on voltage check. Switch ignition off for resistance checks, disconnecting microphone C9222 where directed. Check for voltage shorts, ground shorts, opens and wires shorted together. Repair any failed circuit before moving to component replacement.

steps.title: AB: Use the microphone replacement as a controlled test
steps.body: After the circuits pass, reconnect C240B and install a new overhead ANC microphone. Clear codes from digital audio control module C (DACMC), cycle ignition off and on, wait at least 5 seconds and self-test it. If B116A:01 returns, inspect and repair all ACM connectors, reconnect and retest. A persistent concern requires the TSB check before ACM replacement; DACMC is integrated into that assembly.

watchFor.title: A latched connector can still have poor terminal contact
watchFor.body: Corrosion and displaced pins can interrupt operation. Restored function after reconnection still requires correction of the underlying defect.

watchFor.title: Engine equipment changes the microphone branch
watchFor.body: This SYNC configuration lists ANC for the 2.3L only. DACMC presence on a 5.2L does not establish ANC microphone applicability.

notes: Reinstalling the same software level does not repair hardware. Limit reprogramming to the prescribed PMI process or an applicable published TSB.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0212:00 returns in the IPC during Y2.
diagnostics.meaning: The switch test requires the IPC diagnostic branch before further switch-circuit testing.
diagnostics.next: Use the IPC DTC chart; this result alone does not establish a failed switch.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B116A:01 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Although labeled Handset Microphone: General Electrical Failure, this test assigns it to the overhead ANC microphone circuits monitored by DACMC.
diagnostics.next: Follow AB's wiring checks before microphone isolation and ACM assessment.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B117A:01 is recorded on an ANC-equipped convertible.
diagnostics.meaning: Backup Microphone: General Electrical Failure identifies a detected fault in the left rear quarter-panel ANC microphone circuits.
diagnostics.next: Use diagnosis for that microphone location; the overhead microphone pin tests are a different circuit.

verification.title: Confirm operation at the connector checkpoints
verification.body: Operate the affected controls or display after reconnecting the SCCM, FCIM or FCDIM. Record whether the original complaint remains before taking a replacement branch.

verification.title: Record the microphone isolation result
verification.body: Record whether B116A:01 returns after the replacement microphone, code clearing, ignition cycle and timed self-test. No return identifies the original microphone as the cause.

verification.title: Complete module configuration
verification.body: Carry out required PMI and follow scan-tool key-cycle instructions. After reprogramming, clear communication codes generated in other modules during the process.

applicability.equipment: SYNC with 4.2-inch non-touchscreen display; ANC tests apply to equipped 2.3L vehicles

guides.title: Diagnose SYNC noise-control microphones and lost module communication
guides.summary: Use Tests AC–AF to distinguish active-noise-control microphone faults from missing powertrain or body-module messages.
guides.introduction: The SYNC audio system combines audio hardware with information received from other vehicle modules. On the 2.3L, active noise control (ANC) also uses cabin microphones. Its digital audio control module C (DACMC) is integrated into the audio front control module (ACM). These tests separate microphone wiring and component faults from communication faults involving the powertrain control module (PCM) or body control module (BCM).
guides.why: A microphone code can originate in wiring, while a communication code can reflect supply voltage or a temporary interruption. Confirming the symptom, testing circuits and identifying which modules report a returning code prevents premature module replacement.

when.summary: When the listed microphone codes are recorded, or a SYNC concern accompanies PCM or BCM communication codes.
notes: ANC microphone location depends on body style. The 5.2L also has an integrated DACMC, but ANC is identified for the 2.3L only.

prepare.title: Electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of module self-tests and reading continuous-memory codes, plus voltage/resistance measuring equipment and the applicable connector diagrams. Be able to access microphone and module connectors without damaging terminals.

prepare.title: Configuration and guided procedures
prepare.detail: Before removing a module, establish a scan-tool session and obtain its configuration data. Replacement may require programmable module installation (PMI) and specific learning or calibration. The BCM Guided Routine requires the vehicle identification number (VIN).

steps.title: Select the test by code and equipment
steps.body: Record the symptom and reporting modules, then use [Tests AC–AF](#/document/G1692891). AC addresses the left-hand rear quarter-panel ANC microphone; AD selects the rear center headliner microphone on a coupe or right-hand rear quarter-panel microphone on a convertible.

steps.title: Prove microphone circuit integrity
steps.body: For AC or AD, switch ignition off before disconnecting ACM C240B. Follow the sequence: shorts to voltage with ignition on, shorts to ground with ignition off, then opens and shorts between wires with the relevant microphone disconnected. Use the branch-specific pins and limits; repair a failed circuit before continuing.

steps.title: Isolate the microphone
steps.body: If circuit tests pass, reconnect the ACM and install the specified new ANC microphone. Clear DACMC codes, cycle ignition off and on, wait at least 5 seconds and run its self-test. A cleared target code identifies the microphone fault; a persistent code leads to ACM connector evaluation.

steps.title: Confirm a communication fault is active
steps.body: AE and AF first require an observable symptom. If present, clear all continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes, cycle ignition, wait at least 10 seconds and retrieve them again. No symptom or no returning target code means the system operates correctly at that time; intermittent conditions or network traffic remain possible.

steps.title: Resolve supply-voltage codes first
steps.body: For AE, PCM codes P0562 or P0563 lead to the charging-system diagnostic route for the fitted engine. For AF, BCM codes U3006:16, U3006:17 or U3006:1C lead to BCM diagnosis. Perform the specified audio/navigation module self-tests; U3003:16 leads to Test AQ and U3003:17 to AR.

steps.title: Use the reporting pattern
steps.body: After voltage checks, a returning U0100:00 or U0140:00 in multiple modules leads to PCM or BCM connector checks respectively. A single reporting module with a continuing symptom leads to the General Audio System Symptom Chart.

steps.title: Repair connections before the final module decision
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect the implicated ACM, PCM or BCM connectors. Correct corrosion, damaged or pushed-out pins, reconnect securely and retest. For a continuing concern, follow an applicable Technical Service Bulletin. Without one, AC/AD direct ACM replacement, AE directs engine-appropriate PCM replacement, and AF directs the VIN-specific BCM Guided Routine.

watchFor.title: Connector faults that temporarily disappear
watchFor.body: If reseating restores operation, address the underlying terminal or connector defect.

watchFor.title: Programming is a separate operation
watchFor.body: Follow required PMI and calibration procedures after replacement. Reinstalling the same software does not repair hardware.

notes: Keep AC and AD microphone pin assignments separate throughout testing.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B117A:01 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test AC concerns the left-hand rear quarter-panel ANC microphone circuit.
diagnostics.next: Test wiring before microphone isolation and ACM evaluation.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B13F5:01 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The backup-microphone electrical fault concerns the rear center headliner ANC microphone on a coupe or right-hand rear quarter-panel microphone on a convertible.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test AD for the correct body style.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0100:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: An audio/navigation module missed PCM messages for more than 5 seconds with ignition in RUN.
diagnostics.next: Use AE to confirm recurrence, check voltage faults and compare reporting modules.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0140:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A reporting module missed BCM messages for more than 5 seconds with ignition in RUN.
diagnostics.next: Follow AF through voltage checks and the reporting-pattern decision.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0142:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The ACM or DACMC missed Body Control Module B (BCMB) messages for more than 5 seconds with ignition in RUN.
diagnostics.next: Continue with the specific BCMB communication diagnosis before deciding on parts.

verification.title: Confirm the branch result
verification.body: Verify the microphone self-test result or reproduce the original communication-related symptom after repair. Complete any directed module configuration and calibration; clear communication codes generated during programming.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Save original and returning codes with their reporting modules, circuit results, connector repairs and final operating condition. Record an absent or unduplicated concern without treating it as proof of component failure.

guides.title: Diagnose SYNC communication faults with body, restraints, cluster and parking modules
guides.summary: Trace recurring SYNC communication codes through symptom confirmation, voltage checks and connector inspection before deciding on module work.
guides.introduction: SYNC exchanges information with controllers elsewhere in the vehicle, including the instruments, restraints and parking assistance. A missing message can affect an entertainment-system function without a speaker being defective. These tests identify which communication concern needs attention and establish whether further module diagnosis is justified.
guides.why: A communication code records a missing message, not proof that a controller has failed. Checking recurrence, supply-voltage faults and the reporting modules helps distinguish an intermittent event from a persistent shared problem.
searchTerms: audio system does not operate correctly

when.summary: When a SYNC concern accompanies communication codes involving body, restraints, instrument or parking controllers.
notes: Test letters here apply to the SYNC procedure; SYNC 2/SYNC 3 uses different test assignments.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic access
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable scan tool for continuous-memory codes and module self-tests. Have connector-repair capability, access to OASIS technical service bulletins (TSBs), and the vehicle identification number (VIN) for guided routines.

prepare.title: Plan restraints-system work separately
prepare.detail: Handling restraints control module (RCM) connectors requires Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) service capability and the linked depowering and repowering procedures.

steps.title: Confirm the observable concern
steps.body: With ignition ON, reproduce the reported behavior. If no symptom is present, these tests identify correct operation at this time; high network traffic or an intermittent condition may explain the stored code.

steps.title: Establish whether the code returns
steps.body: Clear all continuous memory diagnostic trouble codes (CMDTCs), switch ignition OFF and then ON, wait at least 10 seconds, and retrieve them again. Check the reporting modules identified below. If the target code does not return, do not proceed directly to replacement.

steps.title: Follow the code-specific checks
steps.body: Use the diagnostic decisions below in order. For receiving audio/control modules, U3003:16 directs you to SYNC Test AQ and U3003:17 to Test AR. For AG, repeat the clear/cycle/retrieve sequence when checking body control module B for U3003:62.

steps.title: Depower before RCM connector handling
steps.body: Follow the SRS depowering procedure and its initial warning-indicator assessment. With no SRS fault, switch ignition OFF, wait one minute and keep it OFF throughout repair. If faults are present, follow the specified fuse isolation, scan confirmation, battery disconnection and waiting sequence; address SRS faults before unrelated repairs.

steps.title: Restore sound connector contact
steps.body: At the branch's specified controller, switch ignition OFF and inspect its connectors; the cluster branch specifies its single connector. Clean corroded pins or renew connectors/terminals as directed, and replace damaged, bent or pushed-out contacts. Reconnect until fully seated and latched. Correct the underlying cause of contact damage.

steps.title: Retest before escalating
steps.body: After RCM work, repower and prove out the SRS before operating the system. If the concern persists, check OASIS and follow any applicable TSB. Without an applicable bulletin, AG directs body control module B replacement, AH directs RCM replacement, and AI/AJ direct VIN-dependent cluster/body-module guided routines respectively.

watchFor.title: An isolated communication report
watchFor.body: For AG, AH and AI, failure to meet the multiple-module condition redirects an observable concern to the General Audio System symptom chart.

watchFor.title: Restraints warning indications
watchFor.body: A lamp that fails to illuminate, stays lit or flashes—or a warning chime/message—requires SRS diagnosis before release.

notes: U016A:00 identifies missing global positioning system module messages at the SYNC interface. Its fault definition does not provide a complete diagnostic path here.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0142:00 returns in the audio front control module (ACM) or digital audio control module C (DACMC).
diagnostics.meaning: Test AG concerns lost communication with body control module B (BCMB).
diagnostics.next: Address BCMB U3003:62 first. Then check voltage faults in ACM, accessory protocol interface module (APIM), DACMC, front controls interface module (FCIM) and global positioning system module (GPSM). U0142:00 in both ACM and DACMC leads to BCMB connector inspection.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0151:00 returns in APIM or FCIM.
diagnostics.meaning: Test AH concerns an RCM airbag-deployment notification missing for more than 5 seconds with ignition in RUN.
diagnostics.next: Check RCM voltage faults through SRS diagnosis, then APIM/FCIM voltage faults. U0151:00 must be present in both receivers before proceeding to the RCM connector branch.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0155:00 returns in ACM, APIM, FCIM or GPSM.
diagnostics.meaning: Test AI concerns missing instrument panel cluster (IPC) messages.
diagnostics.next: Check IPC voltage faults through instrumentation diagnosis, then voltage faults in those receiving modules. Recurrence in more than one receiver leads to IPC connector inspection.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0159:00 returns in the front control/display interface module (FCDIM).
diagnostics.meaning: Test AJ concerns missing parking assist control module messages; that function is integral to the body control module (BCM).
diagnostics.next: Address BCM U3006:16 or U3006:17 through BCM diagnosis, then check FCDIM voltage faults. Continue to BCM connector inspection if those checks pass.

verification.title: Confirm operation and retain the results
verification.body: Operate the affected function after reconnection. Record whether the symptom remains and which modules retained each code; distinguish correct operation now from a confirmed permanent repair.

verification.title: Complete SRS restoration when applicable
verification.body: Follow the repowering branch, restoring removed fuses and battery connections as directed. With all airbags installed and connected, perform the prescribed prove-out: the lamp illuminates for approximately 6 seconds, then remains off through approximately 30 seconds without a chime or SRS message. Complete the directed CMDTC clearing.

guides.title: Diagnose lost communication between SYNC and audio modules
guides.summary: Use Tests AK–AN to separate active communication faults from stored events before repairing connections or proceeding to module-specific work.
guides.introduction: SYNC depends on messages exchanged among electronic modules. The audio front control module (ACM) provides radio functions, while the accessory protocol interface module (APIM) handles SYNC. The global positioning system module (GPSM) and front controls interface module (FCIM) also participate. A communication code identifies a missing exchange; these tests establish whether the fault is active and what to investigate next.
guides.why: An intermittent connection, abnormal supply voltage or heavy network traffic can produce communication codes. Reproducing the symptom and checking whether a code returns helps avoid unnecessary module replacement.

when.summary: When a SYNC or audio complaint accompanies one of the communication codes covered by Tests AK–AN.
notes: Digital audio control module C (DACMC) is integrated into the ACM on the 2.3L and 5.2L variants.

prepare.title: Provide module diagnostic access
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of clearing and retrieving continuous-memory codes and running module self-tests. Arrange connector access, terminal-repair capability and access to Ford technical service bulletins.

prepare.title: Preserve configuration before replacement
prepare.detail: Start the scan session and obtain vehicle identification and available configuration data before removing a module. Replacement work requires the applicable installation procedure and programmable module installation (PMI) capability.

steps.title: Confirm an observable symptom
steps.body: Begin the applicable [AK–AN test](#/document/G1692891) and verify the complaint with ignition ON where directed. Without an observable symptom, the test ends with the system operating correctly at that time; the stored code may reflect traffic or an intermittent fault.

steps.title: Check whether the code returns
steps.body: With ignition ON, clear all continuous memory diagnostic trouble codes (CMDTCs). Switch ignition OFF, then ON, wait at least 10 seconds and retrieve codes again. Continue only if the specified code returns in the reporting module identified below.

steps.title: Resolve voltage faults first
steps.body: Run the required self-tests: APIM/GPSM for AK, ACM/APIM for AL, ACM/DACMC for AM, and ACM/APIM/FCIM for AN. Recorded U3003:16 directs Test AQ; U3003:17 directs Test AR. Follow those voltage paths before continuing the communication diagnosis.

steps.title: Apply Test AN's additional gate
steps.body: For U0253:00, review whether both ACM and FCIM recorded the code. Both must report it to proceed to AN5. Otherwise, an observable symptom directs the General Audio System symptom chart; without a symptom, the system is operating correctly at that time.

steps.title: Inspect the appropriate connections
steps.body: With ignition OFF, inspect GPSM connections for AK, all ACM connections for AL and AM, or the APIM connector for AN. Clean corroded module pins or renew affected connectors/terminals; replace damaged, bent or pushed-out pins as directed. Reconnect securely. After APIM reconnection, wait 2 minutes for re-initialization before operating the system.

steps.title: Follow the persistent-fault decision
steps.body: If the concern remains, check applicable technical service bulletins and follow any matching bulletin. Without one, AK directs GPSM replacement; AL and AM direct ACM replacement. AN directs the APIM Hardware Test, which requires the vehicle identification number (VIN) to access its guided routine.

watchFor.title: A connector reseat is only part of the repair
watchFor.body: If operation returns, address the underlying connector or pin defect. Simply moving the connection may temporarily hide it.

notes: Test AM inspects and potentially replaces the ACM because the applicable DACMC is integrated into it.
Reprogramming with unchanged software does not repair hardware. Follow bulletin and module-installation requirements rather than treating reflashing as a general cure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U016A:00 returns in the APIM.
diagnostics.meaning: The fault remains after the prescribed clear-and-recheck cycle.
diagnostics.next: Follow AK through APIM/GPSM voltage checks and GPSM connector inspection.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0184:00 returns in the APIM.
diagnostics.meaning: Radio messages from the ACM are missing.
diagnostics.next: Follow AL; its return-code decision specifically checks the APIM.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0237:00 returns in the ACM.
diagnostics.meaning: Messages from DACMC are missing.
diagnostics.next: Follow AM for the applicable integrated DACMC/ACM equipment.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0253:00 returns in the ACM or FCIM.
diagnostics.meaning: APIM messages are missing.
diagnostics.next: Follow AN, including its both-modules requirement before APIM connection checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0256:00 is recorded in the ACM or front control/display interface module.
diagnostics.meaning: FCIM messages were missing for more than 5 seconds with ignition in RUN.
diagnostics.next: Continue with FCIM communication diagnosis before selecting a replacement.

verification.title: Check actual operation
verification.body: After connector work and required initialization, operate the system and determine whether the original symptom remains.

verification.title: Keep the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record reporting modules, returning codes, voltage-test results and the resulting repair or hardware-test handoff. A non-returning code establishes correct operation at that time.

procedures.purpose: SYNC communication Tests AK–AN, voltage-test and symptom-chart handoffs, and U0256:00 identification.
GPSM removal and installation when Test AK directs replacement.
ACM removal and installation when AL or the applicable integrated-DACMC Test AM directs replacement.
Configuration-data capture, PMI and programming requirements before module replacement.

guides.title: Diagnose SYNC control, display and module-voltage faults
guides.summary: Separate missing control or display messages from supply-voltage faults before repairing SYNC wiring or replacing a module.
guides.introduction: This SYNC system shares information between the audio unit, controls and non-touchscreen display. The audio front control module (ACM) and accessory protocol interface module (APIM) can report missing messages from other units. These tests distinguish communication trouble from voltage problems that can disrupt module operation.
guides.why: A communication code alone does not identify failed hardware. Checking voltage first, then comparing reports from both receiving modules, prevents a supply fault or intermittent connection from being mistaken for a defective controller.

when.summary: When SYNC modules record control/display communication faults or low- or high-supply-voltage codes.

prepare.title: Provide electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, voltmeter and Wiring Diagrams Cell 132. The voltage branches require connector access, live measurements and an engine-running charging check.

prepare.title: Preserve configuration
prepare.detail: Start the scan-tool vehicle session before removing modules so configuration can be captured for programmable module installation (PMI). Have the vehicle identification number (VIN) available for guided routines.

steps.title: Confirm and reproduce the communication fault
steps.body: For Tests AO and AP, verify an observable symptom with ignition ON. If absent, stop that branch. Otherwise clear all continuous memory diagnostic trouble codes (CMDTCs), switch ignition OFF then ON, wait at least 10 seconds and retrieve codes. Continue only if the relevant code returns in the ACM or APIM.

steps.title: Compare the receiving modules
steps.body: Self-test the ACM, APIM and the interface module identified below. Address low- or high-voltage codes through AQ or AR first. With none, the communication code must occur in both ACM and APIM before interface-connector inspection. If only one reports it and a symptom remains, use the General Audio System symptom chart.

steps.title: Establish the low-voltage cause in Test AQ
steps.body: Clear the suspect module's codes, wait at least 15 seconds and repeat its self-test. If U3003:16 returns, self-test the powertrain control module (PCM); voltage codes lead to engine-specific charging diagnosis. Otherwise check battery condition and full charge. A deficient battery leads to undervoltage diagnosis before module testing.

steps.title: Compare battery, supply and ground-path voltage
steps.body: With ignition OFF, record battery voltage and disconnect the suspect module. Turn ignition ON and use AQ4's module-specific terminals: supply-to-ground voltage must be within 0.2 volts of the recorded battery voltage. Otherwise repair high resistance. Next use AQ5's supply-to-module-ground terminals; voltage must exceed 11 volts. Failure again directs circuit repair. This is a voltage measurement, despite the ground-continuity step title.

steps.title: Separate charging overvoltage in Test AR
steps.body: Clear codes, wait at least 10 seconds and self-test again. If U3003:17 persists, retrieve all CMDTCs. High-voltage codes such as B1676, P0563 or U3003:17 in multiple modules lead to charging diagnosis. Otherwise turn off lights and accessories, run at approximately 2,000 RPM for 3 minutes and monitor battery voltage. Reaching 15.5 volts or higher also leads to engine-specific charging diagnosis.

steps.title: Inspect the module reached by the test
steps.body: With ignition OFF, inspect its connectors. Clean corroded module pins or replace affected connectors and terminals; replace damaged, bent or pushed-out pins. Reconnect and latch securely. After APIM reconnection, wait at least 2 minutes for reinitialization before checking operation.

steps.title: Complete the directed repair decision
steps.body: If the concern remains, check OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins and follow any matching bulletin. Without one, ACM, display-module and global positioning system module (GPSM) branches direct replacement. APIM branches require its Hardware Test and VIN-guided routine; controls-interface branches require the VIN-guided routine. Follow the applicable installation and configuration procedure.

watchFor.title: Historical voltage events
watchFor.body: A disappearing low-voltage code may reflect a discharged battery; a disappearing high-voltage code may follow charging or jump-starting.

notes: On 2.3L and 5.2L vehicles, digital audio control module C (DACMC) is integrated into the ACM; its branches use ACM connectors and replacement procedures.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0256:00 returns.
diagnostics.meaning: Front controls interface module (FCIM) communication is under investigation.
diagnostics.next: Use Test AO; include FCIM in the self-tests.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0257:00 returns.
diagnostics.meaning: Front control/display interface module (FCDIM) network messages are missing.
diagnostics.next: Use Test AP; include FCDIM in the self-tests.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3003:16 returns.
diagnostics.meaning: The reporting module detects supply voltage below its threshold.
diagnostics.next: Use Test AQ's battery, supply and ground-path checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3003:17 returns.
diagnostics.meaning: The reporting module detects supply voltage above its threshold.
diagnostics.next: Use Test AR to distinguish charging overvoltage from a module concern.

verification.title: Confirm restored operation
verification.body: Operate the system after reconnecting and completing any required initialization. Correct the root cause of connector damage even when reseating restores operation.

verification.title: Keep the diagnostic results
verification.body: Record returning codes by module, the battery/supply readings and the charging-test result. These establish why the selected repair branch applies.

5.2L charging-system diagnosis when directed by AQ or AR.

guides.title: Diagnose audio, touchscreen and connection problems with SYNC 2 or SYNC 3
guides.summary: Use the complaint, fitted equipment and module test results to distinguish reception, compatibility, wiring, configuration and hardware faults.
guides.introduction: The Audio Front Control Module (ACM) handles radio and disc functions, the Accessory Protocol Interface Module (APIM) supports SYNC, and the digital signal processing (DSP) module serves the speaker system. Their connections explain why a silent speaker, frozen touchscreen and failed phone feature need different diagnostic paths.
guides.why: A diagnostic trouble code (DTC) identifies a detected condition, not necessarily a failed part. Correct symptom selection and repeat testing prevent normal reception behavior or incomplete configuration from becoming an unnecessary module replacement.

when.summary: When an audio, display, navigation, media connection or SYNC function fails or behaves incorrectly.
notes: Select branches for the actual body style and fitted navigation, satellite radio or Shaker equipment.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable diagnostic scan tool, module programming capability and vehicle identification number for guided routines. Electrical testing requires wiring diagrams, a digital multimeter and specified flex probes.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Review previous repairs and inspect relevant fuses, wiring and connectors.

steps.title: Identify the exact complaint first
steps.body: For a SYNC concern, consult the SYNC symptom chart before connecting the scan tool. Establish which sources, controls or speakers fail. Unless a test states otherwise, its complaint must be present before following a replacement decision.

steps.title: Follow the SYNC reset branch
steps.body: Use the prescribed APIM reset for the listed services, audio-output, voice, call, steering-switch, media-hub and pairing complaints. If the concern remains, follow its individual pinpoint test. For an isolated Bluetooth feature, check compatibility, then device firmware and the manufacturer's reset instructions.

steps.title: Separate media and reception behavior
steps.body: Inspect a troublesome disc and try a known-good one before the chart's ACM replacement decision. HD Radio delays, dropouts, metadata errors and volume changes can originate in reception or broadcasting. For coupe reception, an empty Radio Data System category, antenna grid, coaxial cable, amplifier, corrosion or electrical interference are possible sources.

steps.title: Choose the matching symptom route
steps.body: AM/FM reception uses Test A for coupe or B for convertible; satellite audio uses C and SIRIUS data uses D. Distinguish distorted speakers, total silence and individual speaker failures. Display operation uses AH, changing brightness BD, navigation AI and voice navigation AK. A battery-saver message requires an APIM self-test, then engine-appropriate charging diagnosis if no codes appear.

steps.title: Read codes in their reporting-module chart
steps.body: Diagnose circuit codes before performance codes. A nonresponding module leads to communications-network diagnosis. Invalid-data codes direct attention to the sending module's codes; without those, diagnose the observable symptom. Front Controls Interface Module (FCIM) seat, climate and rear-defogger codes lead to those systems, not automatically to audio repairs.

steps.title: Separate configuration from persistent internal faults
steps.body: Follow configuration-code instructions using vehicle-specific as-built data or APIM Standard Programming. For internal faults, preserve the chart's distinction between repeating a self-test and retrieving continuous-memory codes after clearing and waiting at least 10 seconds. Persistent APIM faults generally require its hardware test; specified FCIM faults require guided routines. Follow replacement instructions only after their stated checks.

watchFor.title: An integrated module
watchFor.body: Digital Audio Control Module C (DACMC) applies only to the 2.3L and 5.2L and is integrated into the ACM. Its specified persistent checksum or memory faults direct ACM replacement.

watchFor.title: Protect connections and configuration
watchFor.body: Do not apply power or ground to module outputs unless directed. Capture configuration with the scan tool before removing a module.

notes: ACM code B1D19:4B indicates overheating: allow cooling and clear the code. DACMC code U3000:94 is disregarded without an observable symptom; with one, use Test G.

For 911 Assist or Vehicle Health Report concerns, check account registration and recent instrument-cluster or restraints-module service. Repeat Programmable Module Installation when indicated; without recent service, follow the APIM hardware-test branch.

diagnostics.finding: ACM code B1A56:21 appears after bezel diagnostics.
diagnostics.meaning: The plant-oriented antenna test depends on locally available broadcast frequencies.
diagnostics.next: Disregard this code in that circumstance.

diagnostics.finding: APIM code U3000:88 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Network communication failed previously; communication is currently possible.
diagnostics.next: Inspect APIM wiring for damage or corrosion, clear the code, wait at least 10 seconds and repeat the network test.

diagnostics.finding: FCIM code U1000:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive current has disabled a climate-control output.
diagnostics.next: Address other FCIM codes and correct the cause first; clear, wait at least 10 seconds and repeat the self-test. Recurrence requires the guided routine.

diagnostics.finding: Global Positioning System Module code U3000:09 returns after clearing, waiting at least 10 seconds and self-testing.
diagnostics.meaning: The component-failure indication requires a further reset check.
diagnostics.next: Disconnect the battery for 1 minute, reconnect, clear codes, wait at least 10 seconds and repeat the self-test. Replace the module only if the code returns.

verification.title: Confirm the branch outcome
verification.body: Repeat the affected function after the directed action and complete its specified self-test, memory-code retrieval or network test.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the complaint, reporting module, exact codes, retest outcome and any remaining pinpoint-test or repair requirement.

guides.title: Diagnose poor radio reception with SYNC 2/SYNC 3
guides.summary: Trace weak reception or continuous seeking through interference, antenna wiring and grounding, with separate initial checks for satellite radio.
guides.introduction: The antenna feeds radio signals to the Audio Front Control Module (ACM). Coupes use an on-glass antenna and amplifier; convertibles use a right-hand rear fender-mounted mast antenna. These tests separate electrical interference, interrupted signal paths and poor grounds before directing component replacement.
guides.why: Radio interference can originate outside the radio itself. Testing cable sections separately identifies where a fault enters the signal path, while checking the antenna mounting ground prevents corrosion from being mistaken for an internal component failure.
searchTerms: radio reception worsens with rear defroster

when.summary: When poor reception, continuous seeking or a satellite-radio complaint can be reproduced.
notes: Do not follow component-replacement decisions when the complaint is absent.
A selected Radio Data System (RDS) category without available channels can also explain unsuccessful seeking.

prepare.title: Prepare for electrical diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use a digital multimeter, specified flex probes, connector diagrams and a diagnostic scan tool. Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Address relevant circuit diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) first.

prepare.title: Arrange access and capability
prepare.detail: Expect access to the ACM, console cable junction and antenna components. Generator isolation requires competent handling of its battery-positive cable and testing with the engine running.

steps.title: Separate engine interference from antenna faults
steps.body: Use [Test A for coupes or Test B for convertibles](#/document/G1702418). Compare reception with the engine running and stopped. For engine-only interference, switch ignition off before disconnecting the generator B+ cable. Keep its terminal from touching any conductive surface, then restart and compare. Restored reception directs engine-specific generator replacement. Otherwise, switch off, reconnect the cable and inspect coils, housings and harnesses. Repair defects; if these are sound, temporarily ground the specified vehicle parts to the frame and provide a permanent ground where this eliminates noise.

steps.title: Check the coupe's defroster relationship
steps.body: For complaints not confined to engine operation, compare coupe reception with the rear defroster activated and deactivated. If reception deteriorates only with it activated, inspect and repair the on-glass antenna grid. Its surface-applied material can be scraped away.

steps.title: Follow the AM-only supply branch
steps.body: For AM-only concerns, follow A5–A7 or B4–B6: check amplifier supply at the coupe's C4082 or convertible's C4823. Voltage above 11 volts leads to cable testing. Otherwise, isolate the ACM and test the supply circuit for grounding and an open. Repair a failed circuit; if both circuit checks pass, proceed directly to A22 or B20.

steps.title: Test the front and rear coaxial paths
steps.body: Follow A8–A15 or B7–B14. Disconnect the ACM antenna cable and console junction to isolate the front section. Test for unwanted voltage, grounding of the central conductor, broken conductor or shield, and conductor-to-shield contact. Reconnect the junction and disconnect the antenna end to test the rear path. Observe each ignition state and measurement limit; repair or replace the section that fails.

steps.title: Reconnect and assess the antenna component
steps.body: With ignition off, reconnect the antenna-end coaxial connection. A16–A18 or B15–B17 repeat the voltage and short-circuit checks with the component included. A failure now directs replacement of the coupe amplifier or convertible mast antenna, after the cable path has passed.

steps.title: Distinguish mounting corrosion from internal failure
steps.body: Check shield continuity to ground. If it fails, remove the amplifier or antenna and measure shield-to-unpainted-base continuity. Resistance below 1 ohm directs inspection and repair of mounting corrosion, followed by installation at the specified torque. Failed internal continuity directs component replacement.

steps.title: Finish the antenna and ACM checks
steps.body: On the coupe branch, A21 checks the amplifier connector, on-glass circuits and grid connections for damage. At A22 or B20, repair corroded, bent or pushed-out ACM terminals, reconnect securely and operate the system. If the complaint remains, check Ford's OASIS service information for applicable Technical Service Bulletins (TSBs). Follow an applicable bulletin; otherwise, the test directs ACM replacement. Capture module configuration before removal and follow Programmable Module Installation (PMI) instructions.

steps.title: Route satellite complaints separately
steps.body: For satellite reception, sound-quality or no-sound complaints, check subscription status and antenna line-of-sight obstructions. The receiver's electronic serial number (ESN) is associated with the vehicle identification number (VIN) when service is activated; an incorrect match is another possible cause. Use satellite circuit codes to guide further diagnosis before selecting hardware.

watchFor.title: Exposed generator terminal
watchFor.body: Contact between the disconnected B+ terminal and a conductive surface can cause injury or vehicle damage.

watchFor.title: Misleading resistance readings
watchFor.body: Follow the specified isolation conditions. Voltage remaining in a circuit can corrupt resistance measurements.

notes: Generator replacement procedures differ by engine; use the procedure for the fitted engine.
Satellite service and circuit checks here establish the next diagnostic direction, not a completed satellite component diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A89:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The ACM detected a short to ground on the satellite-radio coaxial circuit.
diagnostics.next: Continue satellite circuit diagnosis; the code alone does not identify a failed antenna or ACM.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A89:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The ACM detected an open in the satellite-radio coaxial circuit.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the satellite signal path. Both satellite codes can be continuous or on-demand.

verification.title: Repeat the complaint conditions
verification.body: Operate the radio after repairs and secure reconnection. Repeat the engine-running comparison and, where relevant, the coupe defroster comparison.

verification.title: Record the outcome
verification.body: Record the failed test, repair and whether reception recovered. If reconnecting the ACM restores operation, address the underlying terminal or connector defect.

guides.title: Diagnose satellite radio, SIRIUS data and speed-compensated volume faults with SYNC 2/SYNC 3
guides.summary: Separate subscription, reception, media-hub, wiring and module faults affecting satellite audio, SIRIUS data services or automatic volume adjustment.
guides.introduction: Satellite audio reaches the audio front control module (ACM) through the antenna and coaxial cables. Equipped SIRIUS data services also depend on navigation media and the accessory protocol interface module (APIM). Speed-compensated volume uses the audio digital signal processing (DSP) module to adjust loudness as road speed changes. Choose Test C for satellite sound problems, Test D for unavailable data services, or Test E for incorrect volume compensation.
guides.why: An expired subscription, obstructed antenna or incorrect setting can resemble failed hardware. Checking these first, then isolating cables and connections, gives component replacement a sound basis.

when.summary: Satellite sound is absent or poor, SIRIUS data is unavailable, or speed-compensated volume behaves incorrectly.
notes: Test D applies to equipped factory-navigation vehicles. Follow its map-card checks for the corresponding fitted media hub; Ford does not support adding these services without factory navigation.

prepare.title: Confirm the complaint and electrical condition
prepare.detail: The concern must be present before following replacement decisions. Check previous repairs, related service bulletins, battery and charging operation, and battery state of charge above 70%. Retrieve related diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) from all modules.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting module self-tests and live data, a digital multimeter, Rotunda Flex Probes or the specified terminal probe kit, and the MIT 105-00120 tester. Circuit work requires the wiring diagrams, correct connector access and competence with energized voltage tests.

steps.title: Test D: establish map-card and media-hub operation
steps.body: Install and fully seat a missing map-data SD (Secure Digital) card, then retest; replace a damaged card. Check both USB (Universal Serial Bus) ports with MIT 105-00120. Power from only one port directs media-hub replacement; neither port powering it directs Test Z. If both supply power, remove connected devices, disconnect the battery for 1 minute, reconnect it and allow at least 2 minutes for APIM initialization. Test audio through each port. One failing port directs hub replacement; both failing directs Test AA.

steps.title: Tests C and D: prove subscription and reception
steps.body: For C, an expired radio subscription requires reactivation. For D, inspect Travel Link subscription information independently of the radio subscription: all categories expired requires reactivation; only some expired directs D30. Otherwise, monitor the SAT_SIG_STR parameter identification (PID) in an open location. Seek Good, Very Good or Excellent reception, then retest multiple radio channels or data services. Recovery identifies obstruction. If still faulty with usable reception, try promotional channel 184. If it works, retrieve the electronic serial number (ESN) on channel 0, have SIRIUS confirm it and the vehicle identification number (VIN), and request activation 2–3 times. Allow up to 30 minutes. Failed reception, promotional-channel reception or activation leads to self-tests.

steps.title: Use module self-tests to choose the electrical branch
steps.body: With ignition ON, clear ACM codes and run its self-test. Follow the antenna-code decisions below; send other codes to the ACM DTC chart. With no ACM codes, C proceeds to C20. D instead clears and self-tests the APIM: U1A00:87 directs data-link testing, other codes use the APIM chart, and no codes directs D29.

steps.title: Separate cable faults from antenna faults
steps.body: Follow C7–C19 or D12–D24 in the [complete diagnostic procedure](#/document/G1702418). First isolate the front cable at the ACM and console connection. Prove it before reconnecting the console joint and disconnecting the antenna to test the rear cable. Perform the prescribed voltage-short, ground-short, continuity and core-to-shield checks. Repair or replace the failing cable section. Then reconnect the antenna for its tests. Failed antenna electrical checks direct replacement. If shield grounding fails, check continuity to the bare antenna base: passing continuity directs mounting-surface corrosion repair and correct installation torque; failure directs antenna replacement.

steps.title: Test D: investigate missing data-link messages
steps.body: At D25–D28, disconnect ACM C240B and APIM C2383. Test the SIRIUS Data Link (SDL) for voltage shorts, ground shorts, opens and wires shorted together, using the specified pins and limits. Repair the failing circuit; a passing link directs D30.

steps.title: Test E: compare volume response with compensation off and at maximum
steps.body: Check speedometer operation first; an incorrect reading directs instrumentation diagnosis. With AM/FM selected, compare volume at different road speeds with compensation off, then at maximum. Constant volume when off and speed-related changes at maximum are normal. If incorrect, retrieve continuous-memory codes from all audio modules. U0155:00 directs Test AS; otherwise proceed to DSP connector inspection.

steps.title: Resolve connections before condemning a module
steps.body: At C20/D29 inspect ACM connectors; at D30 inspect the APIM connector; at E4 inspect DSP connectors. With ignition OFF, repair corrosion, damaged or bent terminals and pushed-out pins, then reconnect securely. Allow at least 2 minutes for APIM initialization. Retest the complaint. If it persists, check applicable Technical Service Bulletins (TSBs) in OASIS and follow any matching bulletin. Without one, ACM and DSP branches direct replacement; the APIM branch directs its VIN-dependent Hardware Test.

watchFor.title: Invalid measurements or damaged terminals
watchFor.body: Follow each test's connector isolation and ignition state: voltage checks use ignition ON and resistance checks use ignition OFF. Do not force probes into terminals.

watchFor.title: Popping when the ignition is cycled
watchFor.body: The ACM normally mutes during START. An open between splice S101 and the ACM can allow voltage spikes to produce speaker pops. This complaint requires its own wiring, connector and ACM diagnosis.

notes: Before a justified module replacement, capture the original configuration with the scan tool and follow the module installation and Programmable Module Installation (PMI) requirements.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A89:11 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The ACM detected a satellite-antenna circuit short to ground.
diagnostics.next: Enter C7 or D12 to isolate the cable and antenna; the code alone does not identify the failed component.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A89:13 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The ACM detected an open satellite-antenna circuit.
diagnostics.next: Enter C7 or D12 and follow the complete cable-to-antenna sequence.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U1A00:87 is recorded in the APIM
diagnostics.meaning: Messages from the ACM are missing on the SDL circuits.
diagnostics.next: Follow D25–D28 before the APIM connection and hardware-test decision.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0155:00 is stored in an audio module
diagnostics.meaning: Test E requires a separate diagnostic branch before its DSP decision.
diagnostics.next: Follow Pinpoint Test AS.

verification.title: Repeat the affected function
verification.body: Confirm normal sound across multiple satellite channels, correct SIRIUS data operation, or the specified off-versus-maximum volume response. Address the root cause of any connector fault even if reconnection restores operation.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record subscription status, signal-strength reading, self-test codes, relevant circuit results and final operating behavior so the repair decision is traceable.

guides.title: Diagnose SYNC 2/SYNC 3 popping, speaker distortion and loss of sound
guides.summary: Separate ignition-related popping, active-noise-control booming, local speaker rattles and complete silence before choosing a repair.
guides.introduction: The audio front control module (ACM) supplies audio signals, while the audio digital signal processing (DSP) module drives the speakers. On equipped 2.3L cars, active noise control (ANC) also uses microphones and digital audio control module C (DACMC), integrated into the ACM, to counter cabin noise. Follow the matching complaint in [tests F–I](#/document/G1702418); these are separate diagnostic routes.
guides.why: A vibrating trim panel can imitate a damaged speaker, and a short at one speaker can trigger protection that silences several outputs. Checking operating conditions, mounting and circuits first prevents an apparently convincing symptom from becoming an unsupported module diagnosis.
searchTerms: speakers pop when ignition is switched
low frequency booming with engine running
left front door woofer not working

when.summary: When ignition popping, engine-related booming, local distortion or complete loss of audio can be reproduced.
notes: Module replacement decisions require the concern to be present during testing.

prepare.title: Electrical testing capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, multimeter, Rotunda Flex Probes and the POM6411 back-probe tool where specified. Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge above 70%.

prepare.title: Access and running tests
prepare.detail: Allow for trim, speaker and module-connector access. ANC testing requires competence in running the vehicle in gear on a hoist, with all four wheels off the ground and clear of contact.

steps.title: F: investigate popping during ignition cycling
steps.body: With ignition off, disconnect the ACM and the engine-specific powertrain control module (PCM) connector, and remove the battery junction box starter relay. Follow F1’s matching engine pin map: both start-sense paths must measure less than 3 ohms. Repair a failed circuit; passing results lead to the ACM connector and operation check at F2.

steps.title: G1–G4: establish whether ANC causes the booming
steps.body: For ANC-equipped 2.3L cars, check audio modifications and blocked midwoofer outlets. Self-test DACMC and DSP; follow their charts for microphone or speaker codes. With doors and luggage lid closed and audio off, compare engine-off and running conditions. Only an engine-running symptom proceeds. Compare engine speeds stationary, then in various gears on the hoist. Opening the driver’s door disables ANC: noise that remains returns to general audio diagnosis; disappearance advances the ANC test.

steps.title: G5–G13: follow service history and body-specific microphone checks
steps.body: No recent overhead-console, headliner or microphone work leads from G5 to G14. Otherwise, check overhead microphone seating at G6 and microphone/bezel damage at G7; correct installation or replace damaged parts as directed. An undamaged coupe follows G7 → G12 → G13: check rear microphone seating, gap-free bezel bonding at all four corners and damage before G14. An undamaged convertible stops here for G8’s side-microphone checks; do not bypass them.

steps.title: G14–G20: separate ANC signal loss from circuit faults
steps.body: Using G14’s hoisted running conditions and POM6411, check the specified ACM outputs for fluctuating alternating-current (AC) voltage. No fluctuation leads to G19’s ACM check. If present, follow G15–G18 in order: shorts to voltage, shorts to ground, opens and shorts between circuits, including the shield where specified. Observe each disconnection and ignition state, and repair failed circuits. Passing all checks leads to G20’s DSP check.

steps.title: H1–H2: isolate local distortion and rattles
steps.body: Play digital media and use fade/balance to isolate the affected zone. If pressure on nearby trim reduces the noise, repair that trim. Otherwise remove it and inspect grilles, joining pieces, handles, locks, harnesses, water-shield placement and bonding, loose contents, belt hardware and speaker brackets. Correct loose or broken parts and use specified fastener torques.

steps.title: H3–H4: distinguish water damage from speaker-generated noise
steps.body: Inspect the speaker cone, magnet and basket for watermarks. If present, correct water-shield or sealing faults, dry the speaker and test operation. Without watermarks, remove the speaker while leaving it connected and hold it clear of surrounding parts during playback. Noise remaining in the isolated speaker calls for replacement; noise that disappears requires locating the surrounding rattle.

steps.title: I1–I3: begin complete-silence diagnosis
steps.body: Network-test the ACM and DSP first; a nonresponding module needs communications diagnosis. If both pass, self-test the DSP and address speaker fault codes through its chart. With no speaker codes, select AM/FM and press the steering-wheel VOICE switch. A correct audible prompt leads to I4; no prompt leads to I5.

steps.title: I4–I5: test the appropriate signal
steps.body: I4 checks fluctuating AC voltage across DSP connector C2385A pins 7 and 8 during AM/FM operation: present leads to I10, absent to I9. I5 specifies an AC-voltage measurement from C2385C pin 1 to ground: 3.5–8.5 volts leads to I10. An out-of-range I5 result stops this route pending further enable-circuit diagnosis; it does not authorize ACM or DSP replacement.

steps.title: Complete the module check reached by the test
steps.body: F2, G19 and I9 check ACM connections; G20 and I10 check DSP connections. With ignition off, repair corrosion and damaged, bent or pushed-out terminals, reconnect securely and retest. If the concern persists, check OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins and follow any matching bulletin. With none applicable, the reached test directs replacement of that module using its linked procedure.

watchFor.title: Terminal damage during testing
watchFor.body: Never force probes into connectors. Use back-probing only where specified; resistance tests require the circuit isolation stated in the procedure.

watchFor.title: Engine and body differences
watchFor.body: ANC microphone checks apply only to equipped 2.3L cars, not the 5.2L. A convertible reaching G8 still requires its side-microphone diagnosis.

notes: Before a justified module replacement, capture original configuration with the scan tool and follow programmable module installation requirements. Replacement remains a separate removal, installation and configuration operation.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3000:92 or U3000:94 is recorded in DACMC.
diagnostics.meaning: U3000:92 identifies an ANC fault during the Active Diagnostics Test; U3000:94 identifies unexpected ANC operation.
diagnostics.next: On ANC-equipped 2.3L cars, follow the microphone, speaker and signal checks rather than treating either code as proof of module failure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1142:27 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The ACM detected a short to voltage on the start-signal circuit.
diagnostics.next: Follow the applicable circuit diagnosis before making an ACM replacement decision.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B13FB:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The DSP detected an enable-circuit short to ground, which can mute all speakers.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test I; an out-of-range I5 result requires further enable-circuit testing.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B13F9:13 accompanies an inoperative left-front door woofer.
diagnostics.meaning: The DSP detected an open in the left-hand audio feed from the ACM.
diagnostics.next: Investigate that signal circuit before condemning the speaker or either module.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A01:01, B1A01:11, B1A01:12 or B1A01:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These identify, respectively, general electrical failure, short to ground, short to battery or an open in the left-front woofer circuit. The two short-circuit codes disable speaker output.
diagnostics.next: Continue the matching speaker-circuit diagnosis, considering wiring, connections, speaker and module outputs.

verification.title: Reproduce the original operating conditions
verification.body: After the directed repair, repeat ignition cycling, ANC comparisons or digital-media playback as appropriate. Confirm that the original concern is absent.

verification.title: Record the decision
verification.body: Record codes, measurements and the branch reached, including any convertible microphone or failed-enable stopping point. Distinguish restored operation from diagnosis awaiting continuation.
