guides.title: Diagnose silent front speakers with SYNC 2/SYNC 3
guides.summary: Trace a silent left-front or center speaker through its signal, wiring and module checks to identify the correct repair.
guides.introduction: Speakers turn electrical audio signals into sound. The audio front control module (ACM) sends the left-channel signal to the audio digital signal processing (DSP) module, which feeds the speakers. These tests distinguish speaker failure from damaged wiring, poor connections and missing module input.
guides.why: The left-front midwoofer and A-pillar tweeter share an output. Ground-short and voltage-short faults disable the affected output, so silence alone does not prove that a speaker needs replacement.
searchTerms: left front door speaker not working

when.summary: When a left-front door speaker, left A-pillar tweeter or center instrument-panel speaker is silent.
notes: The complaint must be present during testing; do not follow replacement decisions for an absent concern.

prepare.title: Electrical testing capability
prepare.detail: Use a multimeter, diagnostic scan tool and Rotunda Flex Probes. Competent live-circuit testing and connector identification using Wiring Diagrams Cell 133 are required.

prepare.title: Establish reliable conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge above 70%. Inspect previous repairs and wiring; scan for relevant diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), addressing circuit faults first.

steps.title: Choose the speaker test and check its signal
steps.body: Use [Tests J–M](#/document/G1702418): J covers the left-front door woofer; K, the door midwoofer; L, the A-pillar tweeter; M, the center instrument-panel speaker. Switch ignition off and disconnect that speaker. Operate AM/FM and measure the specified terminal pair. Fluctuating alternating-current (AC) voltage directs speaker replacement; absent signal requires circuit checks.

steps.title: Isolate the output wiring
steps.body: With ignition off, disconnect DSP C2385B for J or C2385C for K/L/M. For K, also disconnect tweeter C9063; for L, disconnect midwoofer C513. Switch ignition on and measure each speaker wire to ground. Any voltage requires repair of that circuit.

steps.title: Check output-circuit integrity
steps.body: Switch ignition off. Following the selected pin map, check ground isolation, end-to-end continuity and isolation between wires. Isolation readings must exceed 10,000 ohms; continuity must be below 3 ohms. Repair any failing circuit. Passing all output checks in M leads directly to DSP connector inspection.

steps.title: Trace the left-channel input for J, K and L
steps.body: With ignition off, reconnect the DSP output connector and disconnect C2385A. Switch ignition on, operate AM/FM and check pins 7 and 8 for fluctuating AC. Signal present leads to DSP inspection. Otherwise, disconnect ACM C240A with ignition off and follow the input-circuit voltage, ground-short, open and wire-to-wire checks. Use ignition on for voltage checks and off for resistance.

steps.title: Inspect the module selected by the results
steps.body: Passing input-wiring checks selects ACM inspection; a present input signal selects DSP inspection. With ignition off, inspect all connectors on that module. Correct corrosion and repair or replace damaged, bent or pushed-out pins and terminals as directed. Seat and latch the connectors, then operate the system again.

steps.title: Resolve a persistent module concern
steps.body: Check OASIS for applicable Technical Service Bulletins (TSBs); follow a matching bulletin instead of continuing the test. Without an applicable bulletin, replace the module identified by the branch. Start a scan-tool session before removal to retain configuration, then follow its replacement procedure and Programmable Module Installation (PMI) guidance.

watchFor.title: Testing can create another fault
watchFor.body: Do not force probes into terminals or apply power or ground directly to module outputs. Keep resistance-test circuits isolated and unpowered.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B13F9:13 or B13F7:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: An open is detected in the left or right ACM-to-DSP audio input, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Follow input-circuit diagnosis for the affected side; neither code proves module failure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A03:01, B1A03:11, B1A03:12 or B1A03:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Respectively: general electrical failure, ground short, voltage short or open in the shared left-front midwoofer/tweeter circuits.
diagnostics.next: Choose K or L according to the silent speaker.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A08:01, B1A08:11, B1A08:12 or B1A08:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Respectively: general electrical failure, ground short, voltage short or open in the center speaker circuits.
diagnostics.next: Follow M; its successful wiring checks lead to DSP inspection.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A07:01, B1A07:11, B1A07:12 or B1A07:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Respectively: general electrical failure, ground short, voltage short or open in the shared right-front midwoofer/tweeter circuits.
diagnostics.next: Use right-side diagnosis in the linked article; the left-side pin assignments do not apply.

verification.title: Confirm the original concern
verification.body: Operate the system after reconnection. If sound returns, address the root cause of any connector or terminal defect.

verification.title: Record the outcome
verification.body: Record the affected speaker, decisive measurements, repair and whether the original silence remains.

guides.title: Diagnose silent right-front speakers and right-rear faults with SYNC 2/SYNC 3
guides.summary: Separate speaker, wiring and audio-module faults at the right front, and perform the supported right-rear checks.
guides.introduction: The audio front control module (ACM) sends sound signals to the audio digital signal processing (DSP) module, which supplies the speakers. The right-front A-pillar tweeter and door midwoofer share an audio signal; the door woofer uses a separate output. Testing along this signal path helps establish why a speaker is silent.
guides.why: A wiring short can disable an output, making a working speaker silent. Disconnecting the specified modules and shared speaker branches allows meaningful circuit measurements before an expensive component is condemned.
searchTerms: coupe right parcel shelf speaker not working

when.summary: A right-front or right-rear speaker is silent and the concern is present during testing.
notes: Tests N, O and P cover the right-front speakers. Q1–Q3 cover the convertible rear quarter-panel speaker; coupe rear coverage here is fault-code classification.

prepare.title: Prepare for electrical diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, an AC/DC voltmeter and ohmmeter, and Rotunda Flex Probes for terminal access. Check battery and charging operation, confirm battery state of charge exceeds 70%, and inspect previous repairs, wiring and connectors.

prepare.title: Establish valid test conditions
prepare.detail: Record related diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) and address circuit faults first. Follow each ignition and connector instruction in the linked tests. Resistance measurements require isolated, unpowered circuits; do not substitute back-probing for disconnected continuity tests.

steps.title: Check the affected front speaker's signal
steps.body: Use N1 for the A-pillar tweeter, O1 for the door midwoofer or P1 for the door woofer. With ignition OFF, disconnect that speaker, then operate AM/FM and measure across its specified terminals. Fluctuating alternating-current (AC) voltage directs replacement of that speaker through its removal and installation procedure. No signal leads to circuit testing.

steps.title: Test the front speaker wiring in sequence
steps.body: Follow N2–N5, O2–O5 or P2–P5. With ignition OFF, disconnect the specified DSP output connector; N/O also require disconnecting the other shared speaker. With ignition ON, any voltage from either speaker wire to ground requires circuit repair. Switch ignition OFF: require greater than 10,000 ohms to ground, less than 3 ohms along each specified wire, then greater than 10,000 ohms between wires. Repair any failed circuit.

steps.title: Determine whether the DSP receives the right-hand signal
steps.body: At N6/O6/P6, switch ignition OFF, reconnect the DSP output connector and disconnect DSP C2385A. With ignition ON and AM/FM operating, check for fluctuating AC voltage between C2385A pins 3 and 4. A signal leads to the DSP connector check at N12/O12/P12; no signal leads to N7/O7/P7.

steps.title: Check the ACM-to-DSP input wiring
steps.body: For N7–N10, O7–O10 or P7–P10, switch ignition OFF and disconnect ACM C240A. Check each input wire for unwanted voltage with ignition ON. With ignition OFF, check ground isolation, end-to-end continuity and isolation between the wires, using the preceding resistance limits and the exact terminal pairs in the procedure. Repair failures; passing all checks leads to the ACM check.

steps.title: Resolve the selected front-module branch
steps.body: At N11/O11/P11 or N12/O12/P12, switch ignition OFF and inspect all connectors of the selected module. Clean corroded module pins and renew defective connectors, terminals or damaged, bent or pushed-out pins. Reconnect securely and operate the system. If the concern remains, check OASIS for applicable Technical Service Bulletins (TSBs); follow a relevant bulletin. Only when none applies does that completed branch direct module replacement.

steps.title: Perform the convertible rear checks through Q3
steps.body: For Q1, ignition OFF: disconnect C396, operate AM/FM and check for fluctuating AC voltage across pins 1 and 4. A signal directs rear quarter-panel speaker replacement. Otherwise, switch ignition OFF and disconnect DSP C2385B. At Q2, ignition ON: any voltage from either speaker wire to ground requires repair. If none is present, Q3 requires ignition OFF and greater than 10,000 ohms from each wire to ground; repair failures. A pass leaves continuity unproved: stop before Q4 until a verified applicable continuity test is available.

steps.title: Understand the remaining rear diagnostic stages
steps.body: Q5 assesses a short between speaker wires. Q6 checks the incoming right-hand audio signal: present leads toward DSP assessment; absent leads through Q7–Q10 voltage-short, ground-short, open and crossed-wire checks. Q11/Q12 cover ACM/DSP connectors, retesting and bulletin-dependent replacement decisions. These later stages do not bypass the unresolved continuity check or independently justify module replacement.

watchFor.title: Protect connector terminals
watchFor.body: Forced probes can spread terminals and create an intermittent connection. Replace damaged terminals and address the cause of corrosion or poor retention.

watchFor.title: Keep the complaint present
watchFor.body: Do not apply a component-replacement conclusion when the original concern cannot be reproduced.

notes: For an authorized ACM or DSP replacement, start the scan-tool session and obtain configuration data before removal. Follow the specific installation procedure and Programmable Module Installation (PMI) requirements.
The linked convertible rear-speaker replacement procedure applies to 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L applications.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B13F7:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The DSP detected an open in the right-hand audio input circuits from the ACM.
diagnostics.next: Test the input wiring; the code alone does not identify a failed module.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A07:01, B1A07:11, B1A07:12 or B1A07:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These identify, respectively, general electrical failure, a ground short, a voltage short or an open in the shared right-front tweeter/midwoofer circuits. The short codes disable the output.
diagnostics.next: Use N or O according to the affected speaker and isolate both shared branches as directed.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A05:01, B1A05:11, B1A05:12 or B1A05:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These identify, respectively, general electrical failure, a ground short, a voltage short or an open in the right-front woofer circuits. The short codes disable the output.
diagnostics.next: Follow P; silence does not establish that the woofer itself failed.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A06:01, B1A06:11, B1A06:12 or B1A06:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These identify, respectively, general electrical failure, a ground short, a voltage short or an open in the convertible right-rear quarter-panel or coupe right parcel-shelf speaker circuits. The short codes disable the output.
diagnostics.next: Match the body style. Use Q1–Q3 for the convertible; obtain the applicable coupe diagnostic path for further parcel-shelf testing.

verification.title: Confirm operation after connector correction
verification.body: Seat and latch the connectors, operate the audio system and determine whether the original concern remains. If it clears, address the underlying connector defect.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic endpoint
verification.body: Record the affected speaker, codes, measured results and completed branch. A passing Q3 result must remain documented as incomplete continuity testing, not a module diagnosis.

guides.title: Diagnose silent rear speakers or a Shaker subwoofer with SYNC 2/SYNC 3
guides.summary: Trace a silent rear audio output through its speaker, wiring, signal source and amplifier before deciding what needs replacement.
guides.introduction: The audio front control module (ACM) supplies audio to the digital signal processing (DSP) module, which feeds the rear speakers. Shaker equipment also uses a separate subwoofer amplifier. These tests follow that signal path to distinguish a failed speaker from a missing input, damaged circuit or module connection.
guides.why: Silence does not identify the failed part. A circuit fault can interrupt sound or cause an output to be disabled, while poor terminal contact can imitate module failure.
searchTerms: right parcel shelf speaker not working

when.summary: A coupe rear speaker, convertible left rear speaker or fitted Shaker subwoofer is currently inoperative.
notes: Do not replace components from these tests when the complaint cannot be reproduced.

prepare.title: Prepare for electrical diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, a digital multimeter and Wiring Diagrams Cell 133. Connector testing requires Rotunda Flex Probes or Terminal Probe Kit 418-S035; the specified subwoofer back-probes require POM6411.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge greater than 70%. Inspect previous repairs, fuses and harness damage; read related module diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) and address circuit faults first.

steps.title: Choose the correct rear-speaker test
steps.body: Use R for the coupe right parcel-shelf speaker, T for the coupe left parcel-shelf speaker, or U for the convertible left rear quarter-panel speaker. Disconnect the respective speaker with ignition off, operate AM/FM and check for fluctuating alternating-current voltage as directed. A signal directs replacement of that speaker; no signal leads to circuit testing.

steps.title: Check the speaker output wiring
steps.body: Follow the chosen test's connector and ignition states. Check, in order, for voltage intrusion, a short to ground, an open and wires shorted together. The specified resistance checks require greater than 10,000 ohms for isolation and less than 3 ohms for continuity. Repair a failing circuit before proceeding.

steps.title: Separate input faults from DSP faults
steps.body: Restore the prescribed connections and test the ACM input at the DSP: R checks the right channel; T and U check the left. A fluctuating audio signal leads to DSP connection checks. Without it, test the input wiring for the same four fault types; passing wiring leads to ACM connection checks.

steps.title: For the subwoofer, establish power and ground
steps.body: Begin test S with amplifier supply and ground checks, each requiring greater than 11 volts at the specified test points. If supply fails, check body control module (BCM) fuse 5 (20A); repair the feed if the fuse is sound. A failed ground-path check directs circuit repair.

steps.title: Check subwoofer enable and audio signals
steps.body: Back-probe the enable circuit with POM6411. S3 accepts 3.5–5 volts; otherwise check for shorts to voltage, ground and an open before continuing. Next back-probe the audio input. A fluctuating signal leads to amplifier connection checks; no signal leads through audio-wiring checks, then DSP checks if wiring passes.

steps.title: Resolve the indicated module endpoint
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect the indicated module's connectors for corrosion, bent or damaged terminals and pushed-out pins. Repair, reconnect securely and operate the system. If the concern persists, check Ford OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins and follow any matching bulletin. Otherwise the branch directs ACM, DSP or complete subwoofer/amplifier/enclosure replacement.

steps.title: Prepare any confirmed module replacement
steps.body: Before removing an ACM or DSP module, identify the vehicle and capture configuration with the scan tool. Follow its linked removal/installation procedure and Programmable Module Installation requirements.

watchFor.title: Probe damage
watchFor.body: Never force probes into terminals. Back-probe only where instructed; resistance checks require the prescribed unpowered, isolated circuit.

watchFor.title: Sound returns after reconnection
watchFor.body: Address the underlying connector or pin defect even if reseating restores operation.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A09:02 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The DSP detected a signal-circuit failure toward the subwoofer amplifier.
diagnostics.next: Follow S; the code alone does not condemn the amplifier assembly.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B13F9:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: An open was detected in the left ACM-to-DSP audio input.
diagnostics.next: Follow the input-circuit branch of T or U.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A02:01 or B1A02:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These indicate, respectively, a general electrical failure or an open in the left rear speaker circuits.
diagnostics.next: Use T for coupe or U for convertible.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A02:11 or B1A02:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These indicate, respectively, a short to ground or voltage; either disables the speaker output.
diagnostics.next: Follow the appropriate left rear circuit checks before replacing a speaker.

diagnostics.finding: All fitted SYNC Services features are unavailable or inaccurate.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible causes include account or subscription registration/status, phone-number registration, active-phone selection, reception, server availability or an obstructed GPS antenna sightline.
diagnostics.next: Check these conditions before further accessory protocol interface module (APIM) or global positioning system module (GPSM) diagnosis; this complaint does not establish module failure.

verification.title: Recheck the original complaint
verification.body: Operate the system after connector repair or the directed repair and confirm the affected output works.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record the selected test, circuit readings, connector defects and whether the original concern remains.

guides.title: Diagnose SYNC 2/SYNC 3 services, audio output and microphone faults
guides.summary: Separate phone and service problems from stereo-output, voice-prompt, microphone and shared media-hub faults before selecting a repair.
guides.introduction: The accessory protocol interface module (APIM) handles SYNC functions and sends stereo media audio and mono voice prompts to the audio front control module (ACM). The microphone supplies speech input, while the global positioning system module (GPSM) supports location functions. These checks establish which part of that chain needs attention.
guides.why: Missing music, missing prompts and poor outgoing speech involve different circuits. Comparing sources and testing signals before replacing parts helps distinguish a device problem, a damaged connection and a module fault.
searchTerms: no sound from Bluetooth or USB

when.summary: Use when SYNC services, media sound, voice prompts or outgoing speech currently fail or operate incorrectly.
notes: Choose the test matching the complaint; an intermittent symptom that is absent does not justify the test's replacement endpoint.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge above 70%. Inspect previous repairs and wiring damage; diagnose related circuit trouble codes before performance complaints.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic equipment and access
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, MIT 105-00120, RCA Adapter 105-00121 and Wiring Diagrams Cell 133. Have Ford bulletin access and the vehicle identification number for the APIM guided hardware routine.

prepare.title: Protect terminals
prepare.detail: Use POM6411 for the specified live back-probing tests and appropriate Rotunda Flex Probes for disconnected terminals. Follow each test's ignition and connector states; isolate circuits before resistance measurements.

steps.title: V1–V4: separate service access from vehicle operation
steps.body: For fitted SYNC Services, disable caller-ID blocking and test the customer's phone connection away from the vehicle. A subscription message leads to checking the owner account, active subscription and registered phone selected as Active; correct missing prerequisites. Only one number can be Active. If these are already correct, continue to V5. A service-selection prompt leads to V4: pair the registered phone, ensure reception, start the vehicle in an open location and request Directions. Note each download progress message.

steps.title: V5–V8: investigate location or transfer faults
steps.body: Where directed, run APIM and then GPSM self-tests, following the relevant code chart if either records faults. With no codes, V7 checks APIM connections and operation. Persistent trouble requires a bulletin check, then the APIM Hardware Test if no bulletin applies; continue to V8 if unresolved. V8 checks GPSM connections and operation with an unobstructed sky view. Persistent trouble without an applicable bulletin leads to GPSM replacement.

steps.title: W1–W2: compare stereo sources and check the signal
steps.body: Test fitted Bluetooth, USB and RCA sources with the specified test equipment. Correct operation points to the customer's device; faults affecting only some sources go to the SYNC symptom chart. If all sources fail, play audio and perform W2's live alternating-current voltage measurement at ACM C240B. A fluctuating signal leads to W8's ACM checks; no signal leads to W3.

steps.title: W3–W6: isolate the stereo conductors
steps.body: With ACM C240B and APIM C2383 disconnected, follow W3–W5 for shorts to voltage, shorts to ground and opens, repairing identified faults. At W6, keep both connectors disconnected and ignition off. Measure every pair among C240B pins 12, 13, 25 and 26. Every resistance must exceed 10,000 ohms to continue to W7. If any pair fails, record the readings and stop that branch pending a confirmed repair direction.

steps.title: X: distinguish missing prompts from switch faults
steps.body: In AM/FM mode, press VOICE. A correct prompt calls for explaining normal feature operation. Otherwise, check the listed volume, seek/call, VOICE and MUTE switches; faulty controls lead to Test AF. With working controls, X3 measures the mono signal while VOICE is pressed repeatedly. A fluctuating signal leads to X9's ACM checks. No signal leads through X4–X7's voltage-short, ground-short, open and short-together checks; passing circuits lead to X8.

steps.title: Y: isolate microphone input faults
steps.body: For poor recognition or outgoing call audio, check the prompt first. If absent, Y2 routes working switches to Test X and faulty switches to Test AF. With a correct prompt, follow Y3–Y6: disconnect the APIM for voltage testing, then switch ignition off and disconnect overhead-console microphone C930 for resistance checks. Repair shorts or opens as directed. Passing circuits lead to Y7: reconnect the APIM, install a new microphone using its procedure and test a spoken command. Restored recognition identifies the microphone; continued trouble leads to Y8.

steps.title: Complete the connection and module decision
steps.body: At connector checks, switch ignition off, correct corrosion, renew damaged or pushed-out terminals and latch connectors fully. Address the cause of the damage. W7, X8 and Y8 require at least 2 minutes for APIM reinitialization before retesting; persistent faults require applicable bulletin instructions or the APIM Hardware Test. W8 and X9 inspect all ACM connectors and retest; persistent faults without an applicable bulletin lead to ACM replacement through its separate procedure.

watchFor.title: Probe damage can create another fault
watchFor.body: Never force probes into terminals. Poor probe contact can also make a working audio signal appear absent.

notes: Before removing a module, identify the vehicle and obtain configuration data with the scan tool. Follow the applicable replacement and programming procedures.

diagnostics.finding: The SYNC Services call connects, but directions do not download.
diagnostics.meaning: The progress messages distinguish location, server and transfer problems.
diagnostics.next: No location obtained: V5. Location obtained but route not sent, or no expected progress messages: possible server issue; contact the Ford Technical Hotline. Route sent but download incomplete: V8.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B116A:01 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The APIM detects a microphone-circuit short to voltage, short to ground or open.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test Y; the code alone does not prove microphone failure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B117A:01 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The APIM detects a short to voltage or open in the microphone shield.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test Y's circuit checks before selecting a component.

diagnostics.finding: All fitted media-hub functions fail together.
diagnostics.meaning: Loss of the hub's APIM-supplied power or ground disables all hub functions.
diagnostics.next: Continue input and shared-supply diagnosis, considering the device, hub, wiring and APIM; this observation does not establish hub failure.

verification.title: Repeat the affected function
verification.body: Confirm the complete directions download, correct stereo sources, audible prompt or spoken-command response applicable to the branch.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic endpoint
verification.body: Save codes, measurements and retest results. Keep a failed W6 branch explicitly unresolved; successful independent checks do not close it.

applicability.equipment: SYNC 2/SYNC 3; SYNC Services and media-hub connections as fitted

guides.title: Diagnose media-hub USB, SD-card and audio-input faults on SYNC 2/SYNC 3
guides.summary: Separate device problems, media-hub failures, connection faults and SYNC module concerns using Pinpoint Tests Z, AA, AB and AC.
guides.introduction: The media hub connects external music sources to the Accessory Protocol Interface Module (APIM), which handles SYNC functions. Its Universal Serial Bus (USB) ports and Secure Digital (SD) card slot share a connection to the APIM. Comparing their operation helps locate a fault without immediately replacing the hub or module.
guides.why: A device conflict, lost power or damaged connector can resemble failed electronics. Known-good media and carefully sequenced electrical checks distinguish these causes.
searchTerms: SD card music will not play
RCA audio input has no sound

when.summary: When fitted media-hub inputs fail together, or USB, SD-card or RCA audio operation is incorrect.
notes: Use only the branches matching the inputs actually fitted; the system heading does not establish that every vehicle has SD or RCA connections.

prepare.title: Confirm a testable complaint
prepare.detail: Reproduce the fault, review previous repairs and service bulletins, and check battery and charging-system condition. Battery state of charge must exceed 70% before diagnostics.

prepare.title: Arrange the diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use an APIM-capable scan tool, digital multimeter, specified terminal-safe flex probes, Multi-Media Interface Tester 105-00120, RCA Adapter 105-00121 and a known-good non-navigation SD card containing music. Circuit testing requires electrical diagnostic capability and the connector information.

steps.title: Choose the complaint branch and reset where directed
steps.body: Use [Pinpoint Tests Z–AC](#/document/G1702418). For widespread failure, Z starts with an APIM self-test and routes voltage codes before resetting. Z, AB and AC then require all devices removed, battery disconnection for 1 minute, reconnection and at least 2 minutes for APIM initialization. AA uses the button reboot described below.

steps.title: Test Z: establish hub power and ground
steps.body: With the prescribed connector and ignition states, check supply voltage and then voltage through the hub ground circuit. Both readings greater than 11 volts direct hub replacement. Otherwise, test for supply-to-ground-circuit shorts, opens, supply shorts to ground and ground-circuit shorts to voltage, in that order. Repair failed circuits; passing circuits lead to the final APIM checks.

steps.title: Test AA: compare both USB ports
steps.body: Connect the tester to each port. Power from only one directs hub replacement; no power from either returns to Z. If both supply power, remove USB devices and hold SEEK UP and POWER together for approximately 10 seconds. After startup completes, test audio through each port. One failing port directs hub replacement; two failing ports require shared-connection checks.

steps.title: Follow AA through the shared USB connection
steps.body: Try known-good SD music: successful playback directs hub replacement. Otherwise, inspect and reseat the USB inline connection, hub connection and APIM connection sequentially, switching ignition off before each disconnection. Remove debris, inspect damage, then reboot and retest after each reconnection. If unresolved, install a new USB cable and retest, then a new hub if necessary; persistent failure proceeds to APIM checks.

steps.title: Test AB: separate an SD-slot fault from shared failure
steps.body: After the power reset, test known-good SD music. If it fails, test both USB ports. Both working, or only one failing, directs hub replacement. If both fail, clear APIM codes and run its self-test. B1252:11 or B1252:13 leads to cable and connector inspection; neither code leads to cable substitution.

steps.title: Complete AB's code-dependent checks
steps.body: Inspect the USB cable, its ends and both connector ports with ignition off. Damaged cable or hub requires replacement; APIM-port damage directs the APIM Hardware Test. With no damage, repeat code clearing and self-test: returning codes lead to final APIM checks. Absent codes direct a new cable and SD playback retest; continued failure also leads to APIM checks.

steps.title: Test AC: trace the RCA audio-input circuits
steps.body: After the power reset, try playback with the tester and RCA adapter. Continued failure requires hub and APIM disconnection, followed by the specified tests for shorts to voltage, shorts to ground and opens. Repair failed circuits. If wiring passes, replace the hub and retest; persistent failure proceeds to APIM checks.

steps.title: Finish with connections before module escalation
steps.body: At each branch's final APIM check, switch ignition off, inspect its connector and repair corrosion, bent or damaged terminals and pushed-out pins. Reconnect securely and retry. If the concern remains, check Ford OASIS service information for applicable technical service bulletins; follow one if present. Otherwise, perform the vehicle-identification-number-dependent APIM Hardware Test.

watchFor.title: Terminal damage during testing
watchFor.body: Use the specified flex probes. Follow each step's ignition and connector states; powered wiring can invalidate resistance measurements.

watchFor.title: A fault that disappears
watchFor.body: Do not continue replacement decisions when the complaint is absent. Correct the underlying cause of any loose or corroded connection.

notes: If known-good playback works after the Z or AB reset but the customer's device still fails, investigate that device.
Bluetooth pairing failure is a separate complaint: device incompatibility and the APIM are possible causes, but these media-input tests do not establish a pairing diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: APIM diagnostic trouble code U3003:16 or U3003:17 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The APIM has recorded low or high supply voltage, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Follow Pinpoint Test BB for U3003:16 or BC for U3003:17 before continuing Z.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1252:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The APIM detected a USB-cable short to ground or overcurrent; the cable, port or connected USB/SD device may be responsible.
diagnostics.next: Follow the relevant USB or SD branch rather than treating the code as proof of hub failure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1252:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The APIM detected an open in the USB cable path.
diagnostics.next: Follow the cable and connector checks, including AB's clear-and-retest decisions when diagnosing SD operation.

verification.title: Demonstrate restored playback
verification.body: Repeat the affected mode with known-good equipment after the prescribed reset, connection repair or replacement. Check each USB port individually.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record which inputs passed, the action that restored operation and, for AB, whether the specified codes returned after clearing and self-test.

guides.title: Diagnose SYNC 2/SYNC 3 pairing and audio-control faults
guides.summary: Separate Bluetooth-device problems, steering-wheel switch circuit faults and front-control concerns using the appropriate SYNC diagnostic branch.
guides.introduction: SYNC controls reach the infotainment system through different paths. The accessory protocol interface module (APIM) handles Bluetooth pairing, the steering column control module (SCCM) reads steering-wheel switches, and the front controls interface module (FCIM) handles the front controls. The front display interface module (FDIM) provides the touchscreen. Identifying which path fails keeps diagnosis focused.
guides.why: Live switch data reveals whether a button press reaches its controller. Circuit isolation then separates the switch, harness and clockspring—the electrical connection across the rotating steering wheel. Network checks and controlled resets establish whether front-control symptoms originate elsewhere.
searchTerms: SYNC Bluetooth device will not pair
right steering wheel buttons not working

when.summary: When Bluetooth pairing, right-hand steering-wheel switches or front audio controls fail or respond incorrectly.
notes: Confirm the complaint is present before following replacement decisions.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool with network tests, module self-tests and live parameter identifications (PIDs), plus the Test AD Bluetooth verification equipment. Circuit work requires a digital multimeter, Rotunda Flex Probes and the specified connector information.

prepare.title: Check the electrical baseline
prepare.detail: Confirm battery and charging operation and battery state of charge above 70%. Inspect previous repairs and relevant connections; diagnose circuit-related diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) before performance concerns.

prepare.title: Provide airbag-service capability
prepare.detail: Intrusive switch testing requires driver-airbag removal. Follow its complete procedure, including ignition OFF and a one-minute wait for backup power depletion. Accidental deployment can cause serious injury. Test only the identified switch circuits, never airbag igniter terminals.

steps.title: Test AD: prove the Bluetooth connection
steps.body: Connect the specified verification tool to USB and pair it with the APIM in Bluetooth mode. Use an equivalent tool only if the specified tool is unavailable, and a compatible Bluetooth device only if neither tool is available. Monitor BT_PAIR and BT_CONN. If both read Yes, SYNC works at that time: perform the Master Reset, review pairing with the customer and retry. If only the customer's device still fails afterward, this branch identifies a device concern.

steps.title: Test AD: investigate a failed verification attempt
steps.body: If either PID does not read Yes, switch ignition OFF and inspect the APIM connector. Correct corrosion, bent or damaged terminals and pushed-out pins; reconnect and latch securely. Wait at least 2 minutes for initialization, then retest. If the fault remains, check applicable technical service bulletins (TSBs). Follow an applicable bulletin; otherwise perform the APIM Hardware Test through its vehicle identification number (VIN)-specific guided routine.

steps.title: Tests AE and AF: compare button presses with live data
steps.body: With ignition ON, monitor SCCM PIDs while operating every affected switch. AE covers the right-hand upper arrows and OK; AF covers lower voice, mute, volume, seek and phone/end functions. If only some readings are wrong, replace that switch pack. If all are wrong, clear IPC codes, cycle ignition OFF then ON, wait at least 10 seconds and run the instrument panel cluster (IPC) self-test. A returning U0212:00 directs the IPC code-chart route. If absent, continue circuit testing. If all button readings were correct initially, go directly to the SCCM connector check.

steps.title: Check switch-circuit supply
steps.body: After safe airbag removal, disconnect both upper switch connectors for AE or both lower connectors for AF. Turn ignition ON and measure the branch-specific connector pairs. Approximately 5 volts directs replacement of the affected right-hand switch. Otherwise, continue the relevant isolated circuit checks; use the exact pin assignments in the complete test.

steps.title: Locate a harness or clockspring fault
steps.body: AE checks the airbag harness first, then the steering-wheel harness, then the clockspring. AF checks the steering-wheel harness, then the clockspring. Follow each specified disconnection and reconnection, checking for shorts to ground, opens and shorts between circuits on isolated, unpowered circuits. A failed upper airbag-harness check directs driver-airbag replacement; a wheel-harness failure directs steering-wheel replacement; a clockspring failure directs clockspring replacement. Passing all checks leads to the SCCM check.

steps.title: Finish the SCCM branch
steps.body: With ignition OFF, inspect every SCCM connector and repair terminal defects as described for the APIM. Reconnect securely and operate the switches. If the concern remains, follow any applicable TSB; without one, replace the SCCM. If operation returns, address the underlying connector fault.

steps.title: Test AG: establish display and network operation
steps.body: Check the FDIM first; an incorrect display transfers diagnosis to Test AH. If it works, network-test the audio front control module (ACM), APIM, audio digital signal processing (DSP) module and FCIM. Route any nonresponding module to its communications test. If all pass, disconnect the battery for 1 minute, reconnect it, turn infotainment on and retest the controls. Normal operation confirms the reset corrected the concern.

steps.title: Test AG: resolve a persistent front-control concern
steps.body: If the reset does not help, self-test all four audio modules and follow the corresponding charts for any codes. With no codes, switch ignition OFF, inspect and repair FCIM connector defects, reconnect and retest. Persistent failure requires an applicable TSB or, if none applies, the VIN-specific FCIM guided routine. Restored operation points to a connection concern whose root cause still needs attention.

watchFor.title: Master Reset erases personal data
watchFor.body: It restores preferences and removes paired devices, phone books, call histories, Wi-Fi connections and saved navigation destinations. It also cancels an update download or installation in progress.

watchFor.title: Preserve module configuration
watchFor.body: Before module replacement, identify the vehicle and capture configuration with the scan tool. Follow the replacement procedure's Programmable Module Installation requirements. Reprogramming is appropriate only when a published TSB recommends it.

notes: Display concerns can involve network communication, touchscreen calibration, configuration, an object pressing the screen, the FDIM or APIM. Test AH is the next diagnostic path, not an automatic display-replacement decision.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1380:09 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The SCCM detected an upper or lower right-hand switch stuck for more than 2 minutes.
diagnostics.next: Use AE or AF to compare switch readings and isolate the cause.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1380:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A right-hand switch circuit short to ground was detected.
diagnostics.next: Follow the applicable switch and circuit checks; the code alone does not identify the failed assembly.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1380:17 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A right-hand switch circuit short to voltage was detected.
diagnostics.next: Follow AE or AF rather than assuming the switch itself failed.

diagnostics.finding: The APIM records diagnostic trouble code B108E:01.
diagnostics.meaning: It detected a general electrical error from the FDIM.
diagnostics.next: Continue through the display diagnostic route.

diagnostics.finding: The APIM records diagnostic trouble code U0162:00.
diagnostics.meaning: It detected an internal FDIM connection or liquid-crystal display panel concern.
diagnostics.next: Follow display diagnosis before selecting a replacement.

verification.title: Repeat the affected operation
verification.body: Confirm pairing and connection PIDs, button-to-PID agreement, or normal front-control operation as appropriate. Observe the APIM initialization wait before judging its connector repair.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record the tested device or switches, original and returning codes, network results, circuit findings and response to each applicable reset or connector repair.

guides.title: Diagnose SYNC 2/SYNC 3 touchscreen, navigation, compass and voice-navigation faults
guides.summary: Follow the complaint-specific tests to distinguish display, connection, map-card, positioning and voice-command problems before replacing components.
guides.introduction: The front display interface module (FDIM) provides the touchscreen, while the accessory protocol interface module (APIM) runs the SYNC interface. The global positioning system module (GPSM) supplies positioning information. Navigation also depends on the correct map data. These tests separate a screen problem from faults in the information, connections or commands reaching it.
guides.why: A blank screen can result from lost network communication, and an apparently dead touchscreen can be held active by surrounding trim. Missing map data, route preferences and cabin noise can also resemble component failures. Checking these causes in order prevents unnecessary replacement.

when.summary: When the touchscreen, factory navigation, compass or spoken destination entry fails or behaves incorrectly.
notes: Choose AH for display faults, AI for navigation, AJ for compass operation or AK for spoken destination entry.
The navigation branches require confirmed factory equipment; they do not provide a navigation retrofit path.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Reproduce the complaint, check battery and charging operation, and confirm battery state of charge exceeds 70%. Record diagnostic trouble codes before clearing them. Replacement decisions require the concern to be present.

prepare.title: Arrange the required capability
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool, Ford service-information access, programming capability, MIT 105-00120, compressed air and the specified trim-access procedures available. A known-good map card must have the correct software version. Capture module configuration before removing modules.

steps.title: AH: reboot and classify the display complaint
steps.body: With ignition ON, hold SEEK UP and POWER on the front controls interface module (FCIM) together for 10 seconds. The screen goes black during restart. Retest: blank or other faults lead to AH4, distorted images to AH12, frozen or touch-unresponsive screens to AH2, and slow response to AH10.

steps.title: Separate touch response from audio operation
steps.body: Adjust AM/FM volume while watching the screen. A volume pop-up with responding sound leads to crack inspection; a pop-up without sound leads to the audio symptom chart. No pop-up calls for touchscreen calibration, then AH13 if unsuccessful. Inspect for cracks with the FCIM removed. Without cracks, reconnect the FCIM without installing it and run the Bezel Diagnostics Touchscreen Activation Test. Correct response calls for careful trim alignment; failed response leads to AH14.

steps.title: Check communication or image quality
steps.body: For blank-screen complaints, run the network test before checking whether the APIM KEYPOS parameter matches ignition OFF and ON. Failed communication requires network diagnosis; an incorrect ignition value requires ignition-input diagnosis. Then follow the code decisions below. For distorted images, use the RGB Pixel Test and Display Test Pattern: a reproduced defect leads to AH13.

steps.title: Follow the display or APIM connection endpoint
steps.body: At AH13, switch ignition OFF, remove and separate the display and APIM using the specified access procedure, and carefully clean their connection with compressed air. Reassemble with secure fastenings and latched connectors, then retest. Persistent faults require applicable service-article checks and the vehicle-identification-number (VIN) guided FDIM routine. Cracks also lead to that service-information check and routine. A failed repair after display replacement, or an AH14 referral, requires APIM connector inspection before its guided routine.

steps.title: AI: confirm navigation equipment and media-hub operation
steps.body: Confirm factory navigation through VIN-specific build data. Check both universal serial bus (USB) ports with MIT 105-00120: power from only one calls for a new media hub; neither leads to Test Z. If both power it, remove connected devices, disconnect the battery for 1 minute, reconnect and allow at least 2 minutes for initialization. Test audio through both ports: one failing calls for a hub; both failing leads to Test AA.

steps.title: Check the navigation map card
steps.body: An “Insert Nav SD Card” or “Navigation SD Card Fault” message calls for checking that the secure digital (SD) map card is present and fully seated. Release it with the slot's push-to-release action before inspecting its case and pins. Replace a damaged card. If an undamaged card is suspect, test a known-good card of the correct software version when available; successful operation identifies the original card for replacement.

steps.title: Continue navigation diagnosis beyond the card
steps.body: Check GPSM communication and run APIM/GPSM self-tests; follow their code charts for faults. With no codes, AI11 directs APIM Standard Programming using “Full Flash/Force CIP” instead of the Service Pack installation. After initialization, retest. Persistent faults lead to GPSM connector checks and an open-sky test, then applicable service bulletins and GPSM replacement if directed. If still unresolved, inspect APIM connections, allow at least 2 minutes for initialization, and follow the service-bulletin check and APIM Hardware Test/guided routine.

steps.title: AJ: isolate an incorrect or missing compass
steps.body: Test APIM and GPSM network communication, then their self-tests. Resolve communication failures or codes through the relevant diagnosis. With neither present, inspect the GPSM connection and retest away from tall buildings or large trees. A continuing concern requires applicable service-bulletin checks before GPSM replacement.

steps.title: AK: establish voice-navigation conditions and preferences
steps.body: Use ignition ON, an open location and a fully seated navigation card; run the vehicle for at least one minute before testing. Confirm factory navigation. AK2 specifies APIM Standard Programming with “Full Flash/Force CIP”; retest after initialization. If unsuccessful, check route, traffic and avoid-area preferences. Correcting restrictions may resolve the complaint and calls for explaining their operation.

steps.title: Separate voice recognition from destination data
steps.body: In AM/FM mode, press the steering-wheel VOICE switch. No audible prompt leads to Test X. In a quiet cabin, say “help”; incorrect recognition leads to Test Y. If recognized, select the requested destination manually and confirm its road and address exist. Successful routing points toward map-data content or format, with a map update potentially available. Failed manual routing leads to AI.

watchFor.title: Pressure against the touchscreen
watchFor.body: The resistive-panel check expects one contact at a time. Trim or wiring touching the screen can block other input; a precise touch responds better than a broad thumb contact.

watchFor.title: Connector damage
watchFor.body: With ignition OFF, inspect the relevant module connectors for corrosion, bent or pushed-out pins. Clean module pins or renew damaged connectors and terminals as directed, latch connections fully and correct the underlying cause.

notes: For the map interface covered by AK, hold a finger off-center to scroll; dragging and two-finger pinching are not supported.
Follow programming prompts and clear communication codes generated in other modules during programming.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0162:00 is recorded in the APIM.
diagnostics.meaning: AH requires a clear-and-repeat self-test before selecting the next connection check.
diagnostics.next: If it returns, follow AH14; if it clears, continue to AH8.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B108E:01 is recorded in the APIM.
diagnostics.meaning: Its persistence determines which connection check follows.
diagnostics.next: Clear and repeat the self-test: a returning code leads to AH13; a cleared code leads to AH14.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1215:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The APIM sets this code when the map-data SD card is missing; navigation loss while it is removed is normal.
diagnostics.next: Follow AI to check the card and media-hub operation.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B116A:01 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The “Handset Microphone: General Electrical Failure” entry concerns overhead-console active noise control microphone circuits.
diagnostics.next: For the 2.3L active noise control system, pursue circuit diagnosis. Wiring, connectors, the microphone and its controlling module remain possible causes; this does not establish a failed voice-recognition microphone.

verification.title: Repeat the original operation
verification.body: After initialization or repair, repeat the exact actions that caused the complaint. Recheck touch operation after reinstalling the FCIM and assess positioning functions in an open location.

verification.title: Record the resolved branch
verification.body: Record the original symptom, network/self-test findings, repeated-code results, corrective action and final functional result. A successful reboot alone does not explain a recurring fault.

guides.title: Diagnose SYNC 2/SYNC 3 noise-control microphone faults and lost PCM messages
guides.summary: Use microphone circuit tests and communication checks to distinguish wiring faults, microphone failures, voltage problems and module concerns.
guides.introduction: Active noise control (ANC) uses microphones to sense cabin noise so the audio system can counter it. The digital audio control module C (DACMC) is integrated into the audio front control module (ACM) on 2.3L and 5.2L vehicles, but ANC is specified for the 2.3L. Tests AL–AN address its microphone circuits. Test AO separately investigates missing powertrain control module (PCM) messages reported by audio or navigation modules.
guides.why: A microphone code identifies an affected circuit, not necessarily a failed microphone. Likewise, missing PCM messages can accompany voltage problems or intermittent network traffic. Following the electrical checks and retest sequence prevents an expensive module replacement from becoming the first experiment.
searchTerms: U0100:00 audio lost communication with PCM

when.summary: Use for an applicable ANC microphone code or a current audio concern accompanied by U0100:00.
notes: Confirm body style and fitted equipment before selecting a microphone circuit.
An old communication code without an observable symptom does not justify module replacement.

prepare.title: Prepare for circuit and scan-tool testing
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, approved Rotunda flex probes and Wiring Diagrams Cell 133. Check battery and charging operation and verify battery state of charge exceeds 70%.

prepare.title: Preserve configuration before replacement
prepare.detail: Start the scan-tool session and obtain original module configuration before removing a module. Replacement can require Programmable Module Installation (PMI); follow scan-tool directions if original data cannot be retrieved.

steps.title: Match the code to its actual circuit
steps.body: Use AL for the overhead-console microphone, AM for the convertible's left-hand rear quarter-panel microphone, and AN for the coupe's rear-center headliner or convertible's right-hand rear quarter-panel microphone. Use AO for U0100:00. Record the reporting module and complaint before clearing anything.

steps.title: Check microphone wiring in the prescribed order
steps.body: For AL–AN, disconnect ACM connector C240B with ignition off, then switch ignition on for the short-to-voltage check; any voltage requires circuit repair. Switch ignition off for resistance tests. Check for shorts to ground, disconnect the microphone for end-to-end continuity, then check whether the wires are shorted together. Isolation checks require more than 10,000 ohms; continuity requires less than 3 ohms. Use the selected test's exact pins.

steps.title: Use a new microphone only after the circuit passes
steps.body: Reconnect the ACM and install the correct new microphone through the microphone replacement procedure. Clear DACMC codes, switch ignition off and on, wait at least 5 seconds and run its self-test. If the target code clears, the test identifies the original microphone as inoperative. If it remains, continue to the ACM connector checks.

steps.title: Resolve a persistent microphone-code branch
steps.body: Inspect all ACM connectors with ignition off. Clean corroded module pins or replace affected connectors and terminals; replace damaged or displaced pins. Reconnect securely and operate the system. If the concern persists, check applicable technical service bulletins. Follow an applicable bulletin; otherwise the branch directs ACM replacement and its configuration procedure.

steps.title: Establish whether U0100:00 is repeatable
steps.body: AO first requires an observable symptom. If present, clear all continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes, cycle ignition off and on, wait at least 10 seconds and retrieve them again. If U0100:00 does not return, the branch concludes that high network traffic or an intermittent condition may explain the earlier result.

steps.title: Resolve voltage faults before blaming PCM communication
steps.body: Run the PCM self-test first. P0562 or P0563 directs diagnosis to the engine-specific charging-system procedure. If PCM voltage codes are absent, self-test the ACM, DACMC and global positioning system module (GPSM). U3003:16 directs test BB; U3003:17 directs test BC.

steps.title: Use the distribution of U0100:00 to choose the next action
steps.body: With voltage faults excluded, compare recorded self-tests. A code in only one module with a symptom directs the General Audio System symptom chart. A code in multiple modules leads to PCM connector inspection, repair and an operating check. Persistent trouble then requires the bulletin check before engine-specific PCM replacement; a concern resolved by reconnecting still requires correction of the connector's root cause.

watchFor.title: Power invalidates resistance measurements
watchFor.body: Follow the ignition and isolation instructions for each test. Do not force probes into terminals or use back-probing to establish continuity.

watchFor.title: Replacement requires more than connecting the module
watchFor.body: Complete PMI as directed. PCM replacement also requires its specified misfire-monitor neutral-profile correction and applicable transmission-strategy requirements if original PCM data cannot be transferred.

notes: Use the engine-specific PCM procedure reached through AO6; the microphone branches do not establish ANC applicability for every engine.
Reinstalling the same software version does not repair a hardware failure. Follow published programming directions and the replacement module's configuration requirements.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B116A:01 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test AL addresses the overhead-console ANC microphone circuit.
diagnostics.next: Complete AL's wiring checks before its new-microphone isolation test.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B117A:01 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The DACMC detected a general electrical failure on the convertible's left-hand rear quarter-panel ANC microphone circuits.
diagnostics.next: Follow AM for that microphone and its wiring.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B13F5:01 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The DACMC detected a general electrical failure on the coupe's rear-center headliner or convertible's right-hand rear quarter-panel ANC microphone circuits.
diagnostics.next: Follow AN using the body-style-specific microphone connector.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0100:00 is recorded in the ACM, DACMC or GPSM.
diagnostics.meaning: PCM messages were missing for more than 5 seconds with ignition in RUN.
diagnostics.next: Follow AO's symptom, repeatability, voltage and multiple-module checks before a PCM decision.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0140:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Body control module messages were missing for more than 5 seconds in RUN. Reporting modules can include the ACM, DACMC, GPSM, accessory protocol interface module or front controls interface module.
diagnostics.next: Continue through the body-control communication diagnostic route; AO's PCM replacement decision does not apply.

verification.title: Confirm the repair under the prescribed conditions
verification.body: Complete the timed DACMC self-test or AO communication retest appropriate to the branch, and operate the system to check the original complaint.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record the final microphone code result or which modules still report U0100:00, together with the observed symptom. After programming, clear communication codes generated in other modules and complete required learning.

guides.title: Diagnose SYNC 2/SYNC 3 communication faults
guides.summary: Trace recurring communication codes through symptom confirmation, voltage checks, module comparisons and connector inspection before considering replacement.
guides.introduction: The audio and SYNC modules exchange information with other vehicle controllers. A communication code identifies information that a receiving module did not receive; it does not establish which component failed. These tests investigate communication with the body, restraint and instrument-cluster controllers.
guides.why: Supply-voltage faults and poor connections can interrupt messages. Checking these first, then comparing which modules report the fault, helps distinguish a shared communication problem from an individual audio-system concern.

when.summary: An observable audio/SYNC concern accompanies U0140:00, U0142:00, U0151:00 or U0155:00.

prepare.title: Diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of module self-tests and clearing/retrieving continuous memory diagnostic trouble codes (CMDTCs). Have the vehicle identification number (VIN) available for guided routines.

prepare.title: Electrical and restraint precautions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, confirm battery state of charge exceeds 70%, and inspect previous repairs and obvious wiring damage. Restraint-module connector work requires qualified supplemental restraint system capability and the applicable safety procedure.

steps.title: Confirm the present concern
steps.body: With ignition ON, reproduce the symptom and select AP, AQ, AR or AS in the linked diagnostic procedure. If no symptom is observable, stop this replacement-oriented path: the system is operating correctly at this time.

steps.title: Check whether the code returns
steps.body: With ignition ON, clear all CMDTCs. Switch ignition OFF, then ON, wait at least 10 seconds and retrieve them again. If the selected code does not return in the specified receiving modules, the recorded event may reflect high network traffic or an intermittent condition.

steps.title: Follow the voltage checks in order
steps.body: Perform the source-module check identified below first. If it passes, self-test the receiving modules listed in that pinpoint test. Receiving-module U3003:16 directs diagnosis to Test BB; U3003:17 directs it to Test BC.

steps.title: Compare reporting modules
steps.body: Continue to connector inspection only when the selected communication code appears in more than one specified receiver; AR requires both APIM and FCIM. Otherwise, a remaining symptom goes to the General Audio System Symptom Chart. Without a symptom, stop.

steps.title: Inspect the relevant controller connections
steps.body: Switch ignition OFF and follow the applicable access precautions. Inspect all connections at the implicated body or restraint controller, or the instrument-cluster connector. Clean corroded pins or replace affected connectors/terminals; replace damaged or bent pins/terminals and pushed-out pins as necessary. Reconnect securely, confirming seating and latch engagement, then operate the system.

steps.title: Take the specified escalation
steps.body: If the concern remains, check Ford service information through OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins. Follow an applicable bulletin instead of continuing this test. Otherwise, AP and AS require VIN-based guided routines; AQ directs BCMB replacement and AR directs RCM replacement through their complete installation procedures.

watchFor.title: Reseating is not the whole repair
watchFor.body: If operation returns after reconnection, address the cause of any connector or pin damage.

notes: Before directed module replacement, let the scan tool identify the vehicle and obtain configuration data. Follow programmable module installation and module-specific completion requirements.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0140:00 returns.
diagnostics.meaning: Test AP investigates communication with the body control module (BCM).
diagnostics.next: Self-test the BCM. Route U3006:16, U3006:17 or U3006:1C to its BCM diagnostic procedure before receiver testing.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0142:00 returns.
diagnostics.meaning: Test AQ concerns missing body control module B (BCMB) messages.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the clear, ignition-cycle, wait and retrieval sequence to check BCMB U3003:62. If present, follow BCMB diagnostics.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0151:00 returns.
diagnostics.meaning: Test AR concerns a missing restraints control module (RCM) airbag-deployment notification message.
diagnostics.next: Route RCM U3003:16 or U3003:17 through restraint-system diagnostics. Otherwise compare the accessory protocol interface module (APIM) and front controls interface module (FCIM).

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0155:00 returns.
diagnostics.meaning: Test AS concerns missing instrument panel cluster (IPC) messages.
diagnostics.next: Route IPC U3003:16 or U3003:17 through instrumentation diagnostics before testing receivers.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0159:00 is recorded by the APIM.
diagnostics.meaning: Parking assist module (PAM) messages are missing; the PAM is integrated into the BCM.
diagnostics.next: Use the parking-assist communication diagnostic path. Like U0142:00, U0151:00 and U0155:00, its trigger is missing messages for more than 5 seconds with ignition in RUN.

verification.title: Functional result
verification.body: Operate the system after connector repair and establish whether the original symptom remains.

verification.title: Recorded result
verification.body: Retain module-by-module self-test results, code recurrence and the selected next route. If programming occurs, clear communication codes generated during programming.

guides.title: Diagnose recurring SYNC 2/SYNC 3 module communication faults
guides.summary: Use tests AT–AW to distinguish intermittent communication records, voltage faults and connector problems before selecting a module repair.
guides.introduction: SYNC depends on messages exchanged between the accessory protocol interface module (APIM), audio front control module (ACM) and other controllers. A communication code means expected information stopped arriving. These tests establish whether the fault is present, repeats after clearing and survives voltage and connection checks.
guides.why: High network traffic or an intermittent condition can leave a stored code while operation is normal. Supply-voltage faults also need their own diagnosis before a missing-message complaint can support a module-replacement decision.

when.summary: When an observable SYNC or audio concern accompanies one of the communication codes covered by AT–AW.
notes: Without an observable symptom, these tests identify the system as operating correctly at that time.

prepare.title: Prepare the vehicle and scan tool
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Use a scan tool capable of network code retrieval, module self-tests and configuration capture. Inspect relevant wiring and previous repairs.

prepare.title: Prepare for connector work
prepare.detail: Terminal inspection and repair skills are required. Use the specified Rotunda Flex Probes if connecting test equipment; forced probes can damage terminals.

steps.title: Confirm and record the complaint
steps.body: Reproduce the observable symptom and record which modules contain the codes. Stop the replacement path if no symptom is present. Start scan-tool vehicle identification before removing modules so original configuration data can be obtained.

steps.title: Repeat the communication-code check
steps.body: With ignition on, clear all continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes. Switch ignition off, then on; wait at least 10 seconds and retrieve all codes. Continue only if the relevant code returns in the module identified below.

steps.title: Resolve voltage faults first
steps.body: For AT, self-test the body control module (BCM), then APIM. For AU, test APIM and global positioning system module (GPSM); for AV, ACM and APIM; for AW, ACM, audio digital signal processing (DSP) module and digital audio control module C (DACMC). Route BCM U3006:16 or U3006:17 to BCM diagnosis. Route U3003:16 to test BB and U3003:17 to BC.

steps.title: Inspect the branch's connections
steps.body: After the preceding checks pass, switch ignition off. Inspect all BCM connectors for AT, the GPSM connector for AU, and all ACM connectors for AV. AW reaches ACM connector inspection only when U0237:00 appears in both reporting modules. Correct corrosion, damaged or bent terminals and pushed-out pins; reconnect securely.

steps.title: Reoperate and choose the supported endpoint
steps.body: If the concern disappears, address the connection defect's root cause. If it persists, check applicable technical service bulletins and follow their instructions. With no applicable bulletin, AT directs the VIN-specific BCM guided routine, AU a new GPSM, and AV or the completed AW branch a new ACM.

steps.title: Carry the repair through its installation procedure
steps.body: Follow the component-specific removal, installation and configuration instructions. Programmable Module Installation (PMI) configures replacement modules using captured data or scan-tool-directed alternatives. Follow programming key-cycle prompts and clear communication codes created during reprogramming.

watchFor.title: Integrated functions
watchFor.body: The parking assist control module (PAM) is integrated into the BCM. On 2.3L and 5.2L vehicles, DACMC is integrated into the ACM; apply AW to that fitted arrangement.

watchFor.title: Unnecessary reflashing
watchFor.body: Reinstalling the same software cannot repair hardware. Follow published bulletin directions when prescribing reprogramming.

notes: The missing-message thresholds below apply with ignition in RUN. A named missing sender is a diagnostic lead, not proof that its hardware failed.

diagnostics.finding: U0159:00 returns in the APIM.
diagnostics.meaning: Test AT follows the parking-assist communication branch through the integrated PAM/BCM.
diagnostics.next: Complete BCM and APIM voltage checks, then the BCM connection branch.

diagnostics.finding: U016A:00 returns in the APIM.
diagnostics.meaning: GPSM messages were missing for more than 5 seconds.
diagnostics.next: Follow AU's voltage checks and GPSM connection branch.

diagnostics.finding: U0184:00 returns in the APIM.
diagnostics.meaning: Radio messages from the ACM were missing for more than 5 seconds.
diagnostics.next: Follow AV's voltage checks and ACM connection branch.

diagnostics.finding: U0237:00 returns in the ACM or audio DSP module.
diagnostics.meaning: DACMC messages were missing for more than 5 seconds.
diagnostics.next: After voltage checks, continue AW5 only if both modules record it. Otherwise use the General Audio System symptom chart if a symptom remains; without one, stop.

diagnostics.finding: U0238:00 is recorded by the ACM or APIM.
diagnostics.meaning: Audio DSP messages were missing for more than 5 seconds.
diagnostics.next: Continue diagnosis of DSP communication loss; this finding does not establish AW's ACM-replacement decision.

verification.title: Confirm the functional result
verification.body: Operate the affected system after reconnecting and determine whether the original symptom remains.

verification.title: Retain the recorded evidence
verification.body: Save the repeat-code and self-test results, especially whether U0237:00 appeared in both ACM and DSP. Record the resulting repair or diagnostic referral.

guides.title: Diagnose SYNC 2/SYNC 3 audio and display communication faults
guides.summary: Use recurring communication codes, module self-tests and connector checks to choose the correct audio or display diagnostic path.
guides.introduction: The radio, sound processor, controls and touchscreen exchange information to operate together. The accessory protocol interface module (APIM) also carries messages for the touchscreen, which is attached to it rather than independently networked. Tests AX through BA distinguish an active communication problem from a stored event and establish which component needs further attention.
guides.why: Busy network traffic, intermittent connections and abnormal supply voltage can produce communication codes. Confirming the complaint and comparing reports from different modules helps avoid replacing a component solely because its name appears in a fault description.

when.summary: An observable audio or display concern accompanies one of these communication codes.
notes: Without a present symptom, these tests do not justify module replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic access
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of module self-tests and continuous-memory code retrieval. Have the vehicle identification number (VIN), guided routines and Ford OASIS technical service bulletin (TSB) information available.

prepare.title: Establish sound electrical conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, confirm battery state of charge exceeds 70%, and inspect relevant wiring and previous repairs. Connector work requires competent terminal inspection and repair.

steps.title: Confirm the complaint
steps.body: With ignition ON, reproduce the symptom. If none is observable, the applicable test ends with the system operating correctly at that time; an intermittent fault remains possible.

steps.title: Check whether the code returns
steps.body: With ignition ON, clear all continuous memory diagnostic trouble codes (CMDTCs). Switch ignition OFF, then ON, wait at least 10 seconds and retrieve them again. Continue only if the selected code returns in a reporting module identified below.

steps.title: Test the relevant module group
steps.body: AX and BA require self-tests of the audio front control module (ACM), APIM and audio digital signal processing (DSP) module. AY adds the front controls interface module (FCIM). AZ tests ACM, APIM and FCIM. Route U3003:16 to Test BB and U3003:17 to Test BC before continuing.

steps.title: Compare the recorded reports
steps.body: Apply the multiple-module criteria below. If the criterion is unmet but the symptom remains, use the General Audio System symptom chart in the linked diagnosis. If the symptom has disappeared, record that the system currently operates correctly.

steps.title: Inspect the component reached by the test
steps.body: With ignition OFF, inspect DSP connectors for AX5, the APIM connector for AY5 or BA5, or FCIM connectors for AZ5. Clean corroded module pins or replace affected connectors/terminals; replace damaged, bent or pushed-out pins as directed. Reconnect securely and latch every connector. AY5 specifically requires a 2-minute APIM initialization wait.

steps.title: Operate the system and follow the remaining branch
steps.body: If the concern disappears, address the underlying connector defect. If it remains, check OASIS and follow an applicable TSB. Without one, AX directs DSP replacement, AY and BA require the APIM Hardware Test, and AZ proceeds to the VIN-based FCIM guided routine.

watchFor.title: A display code can involve its gateway
watchFor.body: U0257:00 can accompany U0253:00 because display messages pass through the APIM. Preserve BA's display-first sequence.

notes: Before removing a module for replacement, start an identified-vehicle scan session to capture its configuration. Follow the component-specific installation and configuration requirements.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0238:00 returns in the ACM or APIM.
diagnostics.meaning: Test AX requires matching reports from both modules before proceeding to DSP connector checks.
diagnostics.next: If both report it and voltage faults are absent, continue to AX5.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0253:00 returns in the ACM, audio DSP module or FCIM.
diagnostics.meaning: APIM messages were missing for more than 5 seconds with ignition in RUN.
diagnostics.next: When more than one module reports it, proceed to AY5.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0256:00 returns in the ACM or APIM.
diagnostics.meaning: FCIM messages were missing for more than 5 seconds with ignition in RUN.
diagnostics.next: Both modules must report it before proceeding to AZ5.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0257:00 returns in the ACM or audio DSP module.
diagnostics.meaning: This display-related code records missing APIM messages.
diagnostics.next: If both report it, BA4 directs a new front controls/display interface module (FDIM). Clear and retrieve codes afterward; proceed to BA5 only if U0257:00 remains.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3003:16 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Supply voltage fell below threshold. Previous low battery voltage, wiring, terminals, connectors or module faults remain possible.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test BB; this code alone does not identify a failed module.

verification.title: Confirm actual operation
verification.body: Operate the affected system after connector work and establish whether the original concern remains.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Save returning codes and reporting modules, the symptom outcome, and any required hardware-test or guided-routine handoff.
