guides.title: Diagnose SYNC 2/SYNC 3 voltage codes and changing screen brightness
guides.summary: Separate low or high module supply voltage from display settings, lighting inputs and communication faults before choosing a repair.
guides.introduction: The front display interface module (FDIM) provides the touchscreen. Automatic brightness depends on a dimming message sent from the body control module (BCM) to the accessory protocol interface module (APIM). These tests distinguish power-supply problems affecting entertainment modules from changes caused by settings or missing control information.
guides.why: A voltage code does not condemn a module, and changing brightness can be normal. Checking shared supplies, connections and messages prevents replacing functioning electronics.

when.summary: When an entertainment module records U3003:16 or U3003:17, or touchscreen brightness changes unexpectedly.
notes: Reproduce the complaint before following a module-replacement decision.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting module self-tests and network tests, a digital multimeter, and Rotunda Flex Probes (NUD105-R025F or Terminal Probe Kit 418-S035). Have the vehicle identification number available for guided routines.

prepare.title: Establish the starting condition
prepare.detail: Check previous repairs, wiring and battery/charging operation. Battery state of charge must exceed 70% before diagnostics; BB subsequently requires a fully charged, sound battery.

steps.title: Recheck the recorded voltage code
steps.body: With ignition on, clear the affected module’s diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). For U3003:16, wait at least 15 seconds before repeating its self-test; for U3003:17, wait at least 10 seconds. Continue through BB or BC only if the respective code returns.

steps.title: BB: establish the low-voltage source
steps.body: Run the powertrain control module (PCM) self-test. Voltage-related codes direct diagnosis to the charging procedure for the fitted engine. Otherwise check battery condition and full charge; a failed check directs undervoltage diagnosis. With these checks passed, switch ignition off, record battery voltage and disconnect the affected module.

steps.title: BB: compare supply and ground measurements
steps.body: Switch ignition on and use BB4’s exact connector table. Supply-to-ground voltage must be within 0.2 volts of the recorded battery voltage. Then use BB5’s specified supply-to-module-ground pair; the reading must exceed 11 volts. Either failed check directs repair of high circuit resistance before module assessment.

steps.title: BC: distinguish shared overvoltage from a module concern
steps.body: Retrieve all continuous-memory DTCs. High-voltage codes in multiple modules direct engine-specific charging diagnosis. Otherwise turn off all lights and accessories, run the engine at approximately 2,000 RPM for 3 minutes and monitor battery voltage. A rise to 15.5 volts or higher also directs charging diagnosis; a lower result advances to connector checks.

steps.title: Finish the voltage branch at the affected module
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect its connectors. Clean corrosion or replace affected terminals/connectors; renew damaged, bent or pushed-out pins, then seat and latch connections. For APIM voltage tests, allow at least 2 minutes for re-initialization before operating the system. If the complaint persists, check applicable technical service bulletins in Ford’s OASIS system and follow any relevant bulletin. Otherwise BB/BC direct replacement of the indicated audio front control, audio digital signal processing or global positioning system module, an APIM Hardware Test, or the front controls interface module (FCIM) guided routine.

steps.title: BD: check settings, then reboot
steps.body: Review Settings > Display, including Auto mode and Auto Dim. If settings explain the behavior, demonstrate their operation to the owner. Otherwise, with ignition on, hold SEEK UP and POWER on the FCIM together for 10 seconds. The screen goes black as reboot starts. After startup, reproduce the original conditions.

steps.title: BD: trace brightness inputs
steps.body: If the concern remains, illuminate and then cover the ambient light sensor. In both conditions, adjust panel brightness while observing the FCIM and instrument panel cluster. Incorrect backlighting directs illumination diagnosis. Otherwise network-test the APIM and BCM; failures direct communications diagnosis. If both pass, retrieve APIM continuous-memory DTCs and follow its DTC chart for any present.

steps.title: BD: remove power and reassess
steps.body: With no APIM codes, switch ignition off, disconnect the negative battery cable, wait 1 minute and reconnect it. Switch ignition on and retest. If the complaint persists, inspect and repair the APIM connector as above. Continued failure requires the bulletin check, followed by the vehicle-specific APIM guided routine when no bulletin applies.

watchFor.title: Connector damage caused during testing
watchFor.body: Use the specified probes without forcing terminals. BB5 requires a voltage measurement despite its continuity-check heading.

watchFor.title: An intermittent recovery
watchFor.body: Reseating a connector can restore operation temporarily. Address the cause of corrosion or poor pin contact.

notes: The digital audio control module C branch directs audio front control module replacement; this function is integrated into that module on the 2.3L and 5.2L.
Before an authorized replacement, obtain module configuration data with the scan tool and follow the specific installation/configuration procedure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3003:16 does not return after the prescribed retest.
diagnostics.meaning: A previous low-battery condition may explain the stored code.
diagnostics.next: The test identifies correct operation at this time; do not infer module failure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3003:17 does not return after the prescribed retest.
diagnostics.meaning: Earlier battery charging or jump starting may explain the high-voltage record.
diagnostics.next: Avoid replacement based solely on that historical code.

verification.title: Confirm operation under the original conditions
verification.body: Operate the system after connection repairs. After a successful brightness reboot or power interruption, duplicate the conditions that originally produced the complaint.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record the affected module, returning codes, battery reference voltage, circuit readings and final branch reached. A referral to charging diagnosis or a guided routine remains further work.

guides.title: Program the SYNC accessory protocol interface module
guides.summary: Use the prescribed diagnostic and USB connections to update SYNC software or provision a replacement accessory protocol interface module.
guides.introduction: The accessory protocol interface module (APIM) is part of the SYNC information and entertainment system. Programming changes its software and applications, or restores the required software when replacement hardware is installed. The programming choice matters: updating an existing module and provisioning a new one are distinct operations.
guides.why: This process depends on vehicle power, workstation power, communication cables and an online software download. A disrupted connection or incorrectly configured browser can interrupt programming. The procedure also deletes paired phones, so successful programming still leaves phone pairing to be restored afterward.

when.summary: When an APIM needs an authorized software update, an applicable upgrade, or provisioning after replacement.
notes: Install a replacement APIM before beginning programming.
Custom programming is for available upgrades or directions in a technical service bulletin or field service action.

prepare.title: Review service and charging precautions
prepare.detail: Follow the linked health and safety precautions and the battery-charging precautions they reference. Disable remote start before service and use the required protective equipment.

prepare.title: Prepare the programming workstation
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool with up-to-date Integrated Diagnostic System (IDS) software and patches. The workflow requires the specified Internet Explorer service interface; a hardwired Internet connection is strongly recommended.

prepare.title: Provide power and communications
prepare.detail: Have a battery charger, external power for the scan tool, a vehicle communication module (VCM), and the specified SYNC USB 2.0 A-male-to-A-male programming cable. Allow time for the online download.

steps.title: Complete any hardware replacement
steps.body: If fitting a new APIM, install it first using the applicable hardware procedure. The linked APIM removal-and-installation article is specifically labeled for SYNC 2/SYNC 3; confirm that equipment applicability before using it.

steps.title: Stabilize power
steps.body: Connect the vehicle battery charger and select its low-charge setting. Connect the negative charger lead to a clean chassis ground, not the negative battery post. Plug the diagnostic scan tool into an external power supply.

steps.title: Connect both communication paths
steps.body: Connect the scan tool to the VCM and the VCM to the vehicle data link connector. Connect the specified USB cable between the scan tool and vehicle USB port. Where front and rear ports are fitted, use the front port, USB1. Close IDS, then place the ignition in ON/RUN.

steps.title: Establish the online session
steps.body: Open Internet Explorer on the scan tool and access the technician service publication website. Run OASIS using “Read VIN & DTCs” to read the vehicle identification number and diagnostic trouble codes. Resolve the browser/VCM status conditions described in diagnostics. Select “SYNC” from the OASIS tab to display “Last Recorded State — Software.”

steps.title: Choose the correct programming purpose
steps.body: Select Standard to update the APIM and currently installed applications. Select Custom to display available software options, including applications not previously installed. Select Module Replacement to provision newly installed hardware. Then select “Read SYNC”; the vehicle identity, APIM assembly and software levels are compared with the last recorded online state, and available software is displayed.

steps.title: Program and follow the prompts
steps.body: Select “Program SYNC” and follow the scan tool directions through completion. Keep the VCM and USB cable connected unless an on-screen instruction explicitly directs disconnection.

watchFor.title: Browser configuration errors
watchFor.body: Follow the website's “SYNC - Software Programming” guidance when directed; incorrect browser settings can stop programming.

watchFor.title: Lost phone pairings
watchFor.body: Paired phones are deleted by this operation. Their absence afterward is an expected consequence.

notes: The prescribed workflow uses both the VCM connection and the separate USB programming cable.

diagnostics.finding: “Read VIN & DTCs” is green with a red VCM icon.
diagnostics.meaning: The procedure directs additional programming setup guidance for this displayed state.
diagnostics.next: Open “SYNC - Software Programming” under “Service Tips” and follow its instructions.

diagnostics.finding: “Read VIN & DTCs” is red with a grey VCM icon.
diagnostics.meaning: Browser pop-up handling and programming configuration require attention.
diagnostics.next: Enable pop-ups, follow the Internet Explorer pop-ups, then follow “SYNC - Software Programming” under “Service Tips.”

verification.title: Confirm the completion message
verification.body: Require the scan tool to display “Programming has been successfully completed.” A started download or programming session does not establish completion.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the vehicle identity, selected programming mode and displayed completion result; note that phone pairings were deleted.

guides.title: Run audio bezel diagnostics with SYNC, SYNC 2 or SYNC 3
guides.summary: Enter the equipment-specific diagnostic menus to exercise speakers and displays, read module information and record findings for further diagnosis.
guides.introduction: Bezel diagnostics uses the audio controls and display to access built-in checks and identification information. It can exercise speaker outputs, display supported screen tests and retrieve module details or a satellite-radio identifier. Menu availability and entry buttons depend on the fitted system. A failed check narrows the investigation; it does not by itself identify a component for replacement.
guides.why: The two procedures specify different button combinations, especially without a CD player. Speaker testing also moves between the audio control module (ACM) and digital signal processing (DSP) module according to equipment. Choosing the correct branch prevents an unavailable menu or unsuccessful entry attempt from being mistaken for a module failure.

when.summary: When checking audio or display operation, or retrieving module identifiers and satellite-radio information.
notes: Available tests depend on the display, controls and audio equipment actually fitted.

prepare.title: Review service precautions
prepare.detail: Review the linked Health and Safety Precautions. Disable remote start before applicable service work and use the specified personal protection.

prepare.title: Identify the controls
prepare.detail: Identify SYNC generation, CD-player provision and display type. The front controls interface module (FCIM) is the audio control panel; the display may be a front control/display interface module (FCDIM) or front display interface module (FDIM).

steps.title: Set the operating state
steps.body: Switch the ignition ON and operate the audio system in AM/FM mode. Use the entry sequence in the procedure matching the installed equipment.

steps.title: Enter using the SYNC procedure
steps.body: In [G1839609](#/document/G1839609), a CD-equipped system uses EJECT held first, then SEEK UP pressed and held within 1 second. Without a CD player, simultaneously hold steering-wheel SEEK UP and FCIM TUNE UP.

steps.title: Enter using the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedure
steps.body: In [G1818028](#/document/G1818028), SYNC equipment with an integrated CD player uses simultaneous control-panel EJECT and SEEK UP. Without an integrated CD player, simultaneously hold steering-wheel SEEK UP and control-panel SEEK UP. Hold until entry; this can take up to 20 seconds.

steps.title: Allow the speaker test to finish
steps.body: If supported, the Speaker Walk-Around Test begins and identifies each speaker on the display. Afterward, use the AHU menu, which identifies the ACM, for speaker testing without DSP; use DSP Diagnostics where that module provides the test.

steps.title: Select the relevant information menu
steps.body: For FCDIM equipment, AHU, EFP/EFP-ICP and supported MFD menus provide software, hardware and calibration numbers. MFD identifies the display. On touchscreen equipment, accessory protocol interface module (APIM) menus provide part/software, configuration and location information. G1839609 lists Global Positioning System (GPS) information; G1818028 also lists IVSU Versions. Other menus identify the ACM, DSP, controls or display.

steps.title: Capture findings and exit
steps.body: Record the relevant test observations and identifiers. If satellite radio is equipped, retrieve its electronic serial number (ESN). Exit with the control-panel On/Off button or Exit Diagnostics.

watchFor.title: Unsupported menu choices
watchFor.body: An absent option may reflect equipment. Do not assume every listed test is available.

watchFor.title: Different control-module labels
watchFor.body: EFP identifies controls communicating over Controller Area Network (CAN); ICP identifies controls using Local Interconnect Network (LIN). G1818028 also provides SDM display identification.

notes: The shared no-SYNC entry and CHR menu branch is outside this SYNC-equipped guide.

diagnostics.finding: A speaker is silent during the walk-around test.
diagnostics.meaning: The commanded output needs investigation; this does not establish a failed speaker.
diagnostics.next: Record the indicated speaker and continue the applicable audio diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: A reception concern needs assessment.
diagnostics.meaning: AHU Radio Signal Strength provides an observation, not a specified pass/fail verdict here.
diagnostics.next: Record the reading; FCDIM equipment may require OK to display it.

diagnostics.finding: A display or touchscreen concern is present.
diagnostics.meaning: Supported MFD Display Test or APIM Touchscreen Activation, Display Test Pattern and red/green/blue (RGB) Pixel Test address different display functions.
diagnostics.next: Record the failing function. Touch Screen Calibration belongs only to the applicable G1839609 touchscreen branch.

diagnostics.finding: Touchscreen-system audio output needs checking.
diagnostics.meaning: APIM Tones Test provides an additional output check; G1839609 also lists Rear Tones Test where equipped.
diagnostics.next: Run the supported test and record the observed output.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostics cannot be entered because controls, display or an applicable audio module are inoperative.
diagnostics.meaning: Identification must be obtained another way while the inoperative component is diagnosed.
diagnostics.next: Read the module label for its part number. For satellite-radio identification unavailable through diagnostics or channel 0, use the ACM label; continue the appropriate Group 415 diagnosis.

verification.title: Recorded diagnostic result
verification.body: Retain the entry procedure used, available tests, observations and required module identifiers. The G1839609 satellite identifier is a 12-digit ESN.

verification.title: Exit confirmed
verification.body: Confirm the system has left bezel diagnostics using On/Off or Exit Diagnostics.

procedures.purpose: SYNC bezel entry, equipment-dependent display and audio menus, satellite ESN retrieval and exit.
SYNC 2/SYNC 3 bezel entry, option-dependent module menus, functional checks and exit.
General health and safety prerequisites for service work.

guides.title: Reset the SYNC, SYNC 2 or SYNC 3 interface module
guides.summary: Cold-boot the SYNC interface, perform a Master Reset only if needed, and verify audio operation before continuing diagnosis.
guides.introduction: The Accessory Protocol Interface Module (APIM) supports the SYNC functions used with connected devices and audio inputs. Resetting it restarts its software and, when necessary, clears stored settings through a Master Reset. The procedures cover both SYNC and SYNC 2/SYNC 3 installations; use the procedure matching the fitted system and test only the inputs actually present.
guides.why: A software restart can resolve a concern without erasing personal settings. A Master Reset has broader consequences, so the decision to continue should follow the cold-boot result. Connected devices can also affect SYNC operation. Testing the vehicle’s audio paths and then addressing the device helps avoid unnecessary module diagnosis or replacement.

when.summary: When a SYNC concern calls for an APIM reset before further symptom-based diagnosis.
notes: A Master Reset may be unnecessary if the cold boot resolves the concern.
Navigation and connected-app deletion consequences apply only where the corresponding equipment is fitted.

prepare.title: Have the correct operating instructions
prepare.detail: Use the matching vehicle Owner’s Literature for the Master Reset menu procedure. Know the original concern so its status can be checked after restarting.

prepare.title: Prepare the specified audio tester
prepare.detail: Full verification uses MIT 105-00120 for USB, the audio input jack/socket if fitted, and Bluetooth. Testing fitted RCA inputs also requires RCA Adapter 105-00121.

prepare.title: Understand the data loss
prepare.detail: Master Reset restores factory preferences and erases stored phone books, call histories and Bluetooth pairings. It also erases saved navigation destinations where fitted.

steps.title: Disconnect external devices
steps.body: Turn the ignition OFF. Remove devices connected to USB ports, the audio input jack/socket, SD slot and RCA jacks, wherever those connections are fitted. Then turn the ignition ON.

steps.title: Cold-boot the APIM
steps.body: Follow either [SYNC APIM Reset](#/document/G1813075) or [SYNC 2/SYNC 3 APIM Reset](#/document/G1813259). Simultaneously hold the front controls interface module (FCIM) power and seek-up buttons for 8 seconds, then release them.

steps.title: Decide whether Master Reset is needed
steps.body: Check whether the original concern has cleared. If it has, a Master Reset may be unnecessary. If further reset work is needed, perform Master Reset using the matching Owner’s Literature, with its deletion consequences understood.

steps.title: Verify the available audio paths
steps.body: Use MIT 105-00120 to test audio output through USB, the audio input jack/socket if fitted, and Bluetooth. Where RCA jacks are fitted, test them with RCA Adapter 105-00121. Reaching the end of a reset menu alone does not complete this verification.

steps.title: Address a continuing device concern
steps.body: If the concern remains, power the connected device off and back on. Where possible, battery removal and reinstallation may be needed to complete its reboot. Delete SYNC from the device’s Bluetooth menu before pairing it again.

steps.title: Continue diagnosis if necessary
steps.body: If needed, follow the device manufacturer’s instructions for a Master Clear, Master Reset or Factory Data Reset. If a concern is still present, return to the Symptom Charts rather than treating the unsuccessful reset as proof of APIM failure.

watchFor.title: Additional equipped-system data loss
watchFor.body: Saved navigation destinations include home, favorites and previous destinations. Where a telematics control unit (TCU) and the corresponding MyFord Mobile service are fitted, associated app device pairings are also deleted.

watchFor.title: Confusing vehicle and device resets
watchFor.body: A device factory reset is a separate, potentially data-erasing action. Follow that device’s instructions rather than applying the vehicle’s reset sequence to it.

notes: The reset sequence is shared by the two supplied SYNC procedures; fitted controls, inputs and optional features determine which supporting instructions apply.

diagnostics.finding: The concern clears after the cold boot.
diagnostics.meaning: Further clearing of stored vehicle settings may be unnecessary.
diagnostics.next: Complete the specified audio-function verification.

diagnostics.finding: The concern remains after APIM reset.
diagnostics.meaning: The connected device remains a possible contributor.
diagnostics.next: Reboot the device, remove its SYNC pairing and pair again; continue to the Symptom Charts if unresolved.

verification.title: Record reset and test results
verification.body: Record whether cold boot alone or Master Reset was used, which fitted audio inputs were tested, and whether the original concern remains.

procedures.purpose: APIM cold boot, conditional Master Reset, audio verification and device follow-up for vehicles with SYNC.
APIM cold boot, conditional Master Reset, audio verification and device follow-up for vehicles with SYNC 2 or SYNC 3.

guides.title: Replace an A-Pillar Speaker on a Coupe or Convertible
guides.summary: Remove the body-style-specific A-pillar trim, release the speaker retaining tabs, and restore the speaker wiring and trim attachments.
guides.introduction: The A-pillar speaker turns an electrical audio signal into sound beside the windshield. It is retained in the pillar trim by tabs, so the trim must be removed before the speaker can be released. The speaker procedures for SYNC and SYNC 2/SYNC 3 use the same basic sequence, while coupe and convertible trim require different access work.
guides.why: The important differences are in the trim attachments. Coupe access includes the door weatherstrip and a tether anchor; convertible access begins with the sun visor. Following the correct path allows the wiring and retainers to be released deliberately and restored in the proper order.

when.summary: When an A-pillar speaker requires removal or replacement after the audio concern has been assessed.
notes: A sound complaint alone does not establish that the speaker has failed.
Use only the trim-access branch matching the vehicle body style.

prepare.title: Identify the applicable procedures
prepare.detail: Choose the SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3 speaker procedure and the coupe or convertible trim procedure before beginning.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim and connector work
prepare.detail: Be able to release trim clips, retainers and speaker tabs without forcing the panel. Allow room to reach the speaker connector before taking the trim completely away.

steps.title: Select the speaker procedure
steps.body: Use [A-Pillar Speaker — SYNC](#/document/G1694045) or [A-Pillar Speaker — SYNC 2/SYNC 3](#/document/G1693889), according to the fitted system. Both begin with removal of the A-pillar trim.

steps.title: Coupe: release the weatherstrip and tether
steps.body: Follow [Coupe A-Pillar Trim Panel](#/document/G1692599). Remove the pin-type retainer and move the door weatherstrip aside. Release the trim clips and disconnect the tether anchor. Disconnect the speaker connector where fitted, then release the remaining clips and remove the panel.

steps.title: Convertible: remove the visor and release the trim
steps.body: Follow [Convertible A-Pillar Trim Panel](#/document/G1692609). Remove the sun-visor cap, release its clip and remove the visor, disconnecting its electrical connector if equipped. Release the pillar-trim retainers, disconnect the speaker connector where fitted, and release the clips to remove the panel.

steps.title: Release and replace the speaker
steps.body: With the panel removed, release the speaker retaining tabs and remove the speaker. Install the replacement by reversing this operation, making sure the tabs retain it in the panel.

steps.title: Reconnect and restore the trim
steps.body: Reverse the applicable trim-removal sequence, reconnecting the speaker wiring. On the coupe, restore the tether anchor, clips, weatherstrip and pin-type retainer. On the convertible, restore the trim retainers and clips, then the visor, its connector if equipped, clip and cap.

watchFor.title: Panel still connected
watchFor.body: A released trim panel may still be attached by the speaker wiring or, on a coupe, the tether. Complete those disconnections before removing it.

watchFor.title: Unseated speaker tabs
watchFor.body: Check that the speaker is retained before refitting the panel, while its mounting tabs remain accessible.

notes: The trim procedures illustrate the right side of a left-hand-drive vehicle; the opposite side and right-hand drive are similar.
Match the pillar-trim access procedure to the coupe or convertible body style.

verification.title: Check speaker and trim retention
verification.body: Confirm the speaker tabs are engaged, its connector is reconnected, and the attachments required by the selected body-style procedure are restored.

procedures.purpose: A-pillar speaker removal and installation for vehicles with SYNC.
A-pillar speaker removal and installation for vehicles with SYNC 2/SYNC 3.
Coupe trim access and refitting, including the weatherstrip retainer and tether anchor.
Convertible trim access and refitting, including sun-visor removal and conditional electrical connections.

applicability.equipment: SYNC, SYNC 2 or SYNC 3; coupe or convertible

guides.title: Replace the SYNC USB cable at the APIM or media hub
guides.summary: Install a replacement USB cable alongside the existing harness using the correct SYNC routing, then remove both ends of the original cable.
guides.introduction: The Universal Serial Bus (USB) cables connect the vehicle's ports with the SYNC interface hardware. The Accessory Protocol Interface Module (APIM) is part of that system, but the cable path changes with the fitted display: non-touchscreen SYNC uses direct APIM connections, while touchscreen systems also use a media hub. This job replaces an internal cable while leaving its taped-in original body within the wiring harness.
guides.why: The original USB cables cannot be removed separately from the harness. The prescribed repair therefore overlays a new cable, secures it to prevent noise and vibration, and cuts both ends off the old cable. Correct endpoint identification prevents confusing the direct-to-APIM and media-hub arrangements.

when.summary: When replacement of an identified internal USB cable is required.
notes: This is a cable-replacement operation, not a procedure for removing the original cable intact.
Identify the fitted display and affected cable route before selecting the access procedure.

prepare.title: Identify the connection layout
prepare.detail: Establish whether the vehicle has AM/FM/CD/SYNC or a touchscreen display, and identify the front or rear cable being replaced.

prepare.title: Prepare access and fastening materials
prepare.detail: Have the replacement cable and tape or zip ties ready. The work requires floor-console and APIM removal using the procedures for the fitted system.

steps.title: Remove the console and matching APIM
steps.body: Remove the [floor console](#/document/G1693973). For AM/FM/CD/SYNC, follow the [SYNC APIM procedure](#/document/G1704004); for a touchscreen display, use the [SYNC 2/SYNC 3 APIM procedure](#/document/G1704012). These are equipment-specific access paths even though both expose the cable connections.

steps.title: Select the correct cable endpoints
steps.body: On AM/FM/CD/SYNC vehicles, both the front USB port cable and the rear port cable in the floor console route directly to the APIM. On touchscreen vehicles, the front USB port cable routes to the media hub; the rear cable at the console media hub routes directly to the APIM. Trace the intended branch before installing the replacement.

steps.title: Overlay and secure the replacement
steps.body: Follow the routing illustration for the applicable branch in the [SYNC cable procedure](#/document/G1694056) or [SYNC 2/SYNC 3 cable procedure](#/document/G1693905). Lay the new cable along the harness and make the corresponding connections. Secure it with tape or zip ties as necessary so it cannot move around and create noise, vibration and harshness concerns.

steps.title: Disable the original cable and restore access parts
steps.body: After confirming which cable is the original, cut both ends off it as directed. Leave its taped-in length within the harness; do not try to extract it. Reinstall the APIM and floor console through their matching installation procedures.

watchFor.title: Applying the wrong equipment branch
watchFor.body: The touchscreen front cable terminates at the media hub. The non-touchscreen front cable runs directly to the APIM.

watchFor.title: Loose replacement routing
watchFor.body: An unsecured overlay can move against surrounding parts. Retain it along the illustrated harness route before closing the console.

watchFor.title: Cutting the wrong cable
watchFor.body: Positively identify the disconnected original USB cable before removing its ends.

notes: APIM removal provides access; it does not by itself mean the APIM needs replacement.
The routing illustration must be read with its equipment branch, rather than treated as a universal port layout.

verification.title: Check the replacement path
verification.body: Confirm the new cable follows the applicable route, reaches the correct endpoints and is retained with tape or zip ties.

verification.title: Confirm completion before closing
verification.body: Check that both original cable ends have been removed and the APIM and console have been reinstalled. Record the equipment branch and cable replaced.

procedures.purpose: USB cable replacement and equipment-dependent routing in the SYNC section.
USB cable replacement and equipment-dependent routing in the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 section.
Floor console removal and installation for cable access.
AM/FM/CD/SYNC APIM removal and installation.
Touchscreen SYNC 2/SYNC 3 APIM removal and installation.

guides.title: Replace the APIM on SYNC, SYNC 2 or SYNC 3
guides.summary: Remove the appropriate display assembly, exchange the accessory protocol interface module and complete the required software and display setup.
guides.introduction: The accessory protocol interface module (APIM) provides electronics used by the SYNC information and entertainment system. It is attached behind the display, so access involves surrounding controls and trim. Original SYNC and SYNC 2/SYNC 3 use different removal paths and fasteners. A new module also needs the correct software level before the replacement is complete.
guides.why: The display and its attached electronics come apart in a defined order. Following the matching equipment branch protects trim clips and connectors and prevents small mounting screws from being overtightened. Software programming, display calibration and control-module configuration are separate requirements with different triggers.

when.summary: When APIM replacement is required or the module must be removed for display-related work.
notes: Select the access and programming procedures by fitted SYNC equipment.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim and module work
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover, suitable fastener tools and a torque tool capable of the specified low settings. Arrange access to the equipment-specific APIM programming procedure before installing a new module.

prepare.title: Preserve configuration if replacing the controls
prepare.detail: If the front controls interface module (FCIM) is also being replaced, begin programmable module installation (PMI) with a diagnostic scan tool and upload its configuration before removal. Removing and refitting the existing FCIM does not make this a replacement operation.

steps.title: Original SYNC: remove the display and APIM
steps.body: Follow the [front control/display interface module procedure](#/document/G1704851) to remove the FCDIM. Then remove the APIM bolts and module and disconnect its electrical connectors, following [the SYNC APIM procedure](#/document/G1704004). Continue with the common refitting and programming steps below.

steps.title: SYNC 2/SYNC 3: open the console access
steps.body: Follow [FCIM removal](#/document/G1704007): release the console side trims, remove the stowage mat and upper bolts, then remove the selector bezel and position the boot aside while disconnecting its connector. Open the console lid and remove the front retainers. Release the upper trim, position the selector cover aside, disconnect the panel connectors and remove the stowage tray.

steps.title: SYNC 2/SYNC 3: remove the finish panel and controls
steps.body: Use the [center finish-panel procedure](#/document/G1693976) to release the right-hand instrument-panel trim and then the center finish panel. Disconnect the optional module connector if fitted. Remove the trim cover, FCIM bolts and FCIM, disconnecting its electrical connectors to free the display access.

steps.title: SYNC 2/SYNC 3: separate the APIM from the display
steps.body: Following [front display interface module removal](#/document/G1704008), remove the FDIM mounting bolts and disconnect its electrical connectors. Remove the screws joining the APIM to the FDIM and separate them as directed in [the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 APIM procedure](#/document/G1704012).

steps.title: Refit the matching assembly
steps.body: Reverse the appropriate removal sequence and reconnect the disturbed wiring. Original SYNC APIM bolts tighten to 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm); SYNC 2/SYNC 3 APIM screws tighten to 9 lb.in (1 Nm). Use the individual access procedures for the display, controls and console fastener settings.

steps.title: Complete programming and display setup
steps.body: Program a new APIM using [SYNC programming](#/document/G1692895) or [SYNC 2/SYNC 3 replacement programming](#/document/G1672954), as applicable. After reinstalling the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 FDIM, complete touchscreen calibration through its linked procedure. If a new FCIM was installed, finish PMI and download its configuration.

watchFor.title: Fasteners from different assemblies
watchFor.body: Keep APIM, display, controls and console fasteners identified by location; their tightening settings are not interchangeable.

watchFor.title: Panels still attached by wiring
watchFor.body: Release the specified electrical connectors as each panel or module is removed rather than pulling the assembly away with wiring attached.

notes: The SYNC 2/SYNC 3 console-access sequence applies to both automatic and manual transmission layouts.

verification.title: Confirm physical reassembly
verification.body: Check that each disturbed connector has been reconnected and the display, controls and trim have been refitted through the reverse removal sequence.

verification.title: Record completed setup
verification.body: For a new APIM, record completion of the correct software-level programming. Also record touchscreen calibration and FCIM PMI when those operations apply.

procedures.purpose: Original SYNC APIM removal, installation and replacement-programming requirement.
SYNC 2/SYNC 3 APIM separation from the FDIM and installation.
Original SYNC FCDIM removal and installation for APIM access.
Program a replacement APIM on original SYNC equipment.
Program a replacement APIM on SYNC 2/SYNC 3 equipment.
SYNC 2/SYNC 3 display removal, installation and touchscreen-calibration handoff.
Matching FCIM and console access; conditional configuration transfer for FCIM replacement.
Center finish-panel removal and installation, including the optional electrical connector.

guides.title: Replace an active noise control microphone: front, coupe rear or convertible rear
guides.summary: Access the identified active noise control microphone through the appropriate trim, release its retaining tabs and connector, and restore the assembly.
guides.introduction: An active noise control (ANC) microphone provides cabin-sound information to the noise-control system. Replacing it involves releasing its mounting tabs and electrical connection, but reaching it depends on its location and the body style. The front microphone is accessed through the overhead console; rear access differs substantially between a coupe and a convertible.
guides.why: Choosing the correct access branch avoids disturbing unrelated trim. The microphone must be released from its retaining features rather than pulled free with them engaged, and its electrical connection must be restored during installation. Confirm the actual equipment first: the system feature overviews identify ANC on the 2.3L only.

when.summary: When an identified ANC microphone requires replacement or removal during related interior work.
notes: Confirm the microphone location, body style and installed infotainment system before selecting the access route.
A cabin-noise concern alone does not establish that a microphone needs replacement.

prepare.title: Select the matching procedure
prepare.detail: Use the SYNC microphone procedure or the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 version for the installed system. Both describe front, coupe-rear and convertible-rear access branches.

prepare.title: Arrange the required trim access
prepare.detail: Be prepared to remove the overhead console, lower the coupe headliner, or remove the convertible rear seat backrest and upper loadspace trim. Follow the complete access procedure named for the selected branch.

steps.title: Identify the microphone being serviced
steps.body: Confirm whether the repair concerns the front microphone or a rear microphone. Follow only the relevant location and body-style branch below; these are alternative access routes.

steps.title: Front microphone: remove the overhead console
steps.body: Remove the console using its linked procedure. Release the microphone retaining tab and disconnect its electrical connector, then remove the microphone. The attachment and connector are separate release points.

steps.title: Coupe rear microphone: lower the headliner
steps.body: Use the Headliner - Lowering procedure referenced in the microphone article. Once access is available, release the microphone tabs, remove the microphone from its mounting and disconnect the electrical connector.

steps.title: Convertible rear microphone: open the loadspace trim access
steps.body: Remove the rear seat backrest using the convertible-specific procedure. Position the safety-belt guide aside, release the trim clips and remove the upper loadspace trim panel. Disconnect the electrical connector, then release the microphone tabs and remove it. The illustrated right-hand operation also applies similarly on the left.

steps.title: Install and restore the selected access route
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence for the branch used, reconnecting the electrical connection and engaging the microphone retainers. Restore the overhead console, coupe headliner, or convertible trim, safety-belt guide and backrest through their respective installation instructions.

watchFor.title: Confusing microphone functions
watchFor.body: The system descriptions also list a SYNC microphone. Confirm that the identified part is the ANC microphone before following this replacement route.

watchFor.title: Missing a convertible access step
watchFor.body: The rear seat backrest, safety-belt guide and upper loadspace trim all form part of convertible access. Restore each item during reassembly.

notes: Do not infer ANC fitment on another engine solely from the broad applicability of a microphone removal article.

verification.title: Confirm microphone attachment
verification.body: Check that the microphone is retained by its tabs and its electrical connector is reconnected before closing the access area.

verification.title: Confirm interior restoration
verification.body: Verify completion of the selected console, headliner or convertible trim installation, including the safety-belt guide and backrest where disturbed.

procedures.purpose: ANC microphone removal and installation for SYNC, covering front, coupe-rear and convertible-rear locations.
ANC microphone removal and installation for SYNC 2/SYNC 3, covering the same location and body-style branches.
Overhead-console removal and installation for front-microphone access.
Convertible rear-seat-backrest removal and installation for rear-microphone access.

applicability.equipment: Active noise control with SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3; coupe or convertible

guides.title: Replace the audio front control module on SYNC-equipped vehicles
guides.summary: Remove the audio module through the correct SYNC access route and transfer its configuration when fitting a replacement.
guides.introduction: The audio front control module (ACM) is part of the vehicle's radio and entertainment system and contains the disc mechanism addressed by this procedure. It sits behind the front controls. Replacing it involves both physical installation and configuration transfer, so a mechanically secure replacement is only part of the job.
guides.why: Configuration must be captured before the original module is removed and transferred to its replacement afterward. Access also changes with the fitted entertainment system: SYNC 2/SYNC 3 requires removal of the touchscreen display in addition to the front controls. Selecting the correct branch keeps both the dismantling and programming sequence appropriate to the vehicle.

when.summary: When diagnosis calls for ACM replacement, or the module must be removed for access.
notes: An audio complaint or trapped disc alone does not prove that the ACM needs replacement.
Configuration completion is required when replacing the component.

prepare.title: Identify the entertainment system
prepare.detail: Select the SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedure before removing trim. Their access paths differ.

prepare.title: Arrange programming capability
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool capable of programmable module installation (PMI). Capture the existing module configuration before removing an ACM that will be replaced.

prepare.title: Prepare for controlled fastening
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastener tools and a torque tool appropriate for the specified ACM and, where applicable, display bolts.

steps.title: Remove any media
steps.body: Eject media from the ACM before dismantling. If a disc will not eject, leave it in place rather than forcibly extracting it.

steps.title: Begin configuration transfer
steps.body: Follow the scan-tool prompts to begin ACM PMI and upload its configuration before removal. On SYNC 2/SYNC 3 vehicles equipped with a digital audio control module C (DACMC), also begin that module's PMI process. These replacement preparations must precede physical removal.

steps.title: Remove the front controls
steps.body: Remove the front controls interface module (FCIM) using the matching [SYNC procedure](#/document/G1704003) or [SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedure](#/document/G1704007).

steps.title: Follow the appropriate display branch
steps.body: For SYNC, proceed to the ACM. For SYNC 2/SYNC 3, first remove the front display interface module (FDIM) bolts, disconnect its electrical connectors and remove the display.

steps.title: Exchange the ACM and rebuild
steps.body: Remove the ACM bolts, disconnect its electrical connectors and remove the module. Reverse removal to install it. Tighten ACM bolts to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm). The SYNC 2/SYNC 3 FDIM bolts also use 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm); follow the separate FCIM procedure for its installation.

steps.title: Complete replacement programming
steps.body: For a replacement ACM, complete PMI with the scan tool so the captured configuration is downloaded. On the applicable SYNC 2/SYNC 3 branch, also complete DACMC PMI. Follow the full [SYNC](#/document/G1704002) or [SYNC 2/SYNC 3](#/document/G1704006) module procedure.

watchFor.title: Configuration not captured
watchFor.body: Removing the original module before starting the replacement workflow bypasses the required configuration upload.

watchFor.title: Additional programming branch
watchFor.body: The SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedure requires a separate DACMC sequence where fitted; completing ACM PMI alone does not complete that branch.

notes: The equipment overviews identify DACMC within the ACM on the described 2.3L and 5.2L configurations.
Match the audio-unit access arrangement to the fitted SYNC equipment.

verification.title: Confirm physical installation
verification.body: Check that disconnected connectors are restored, the module is secured, and any removed display and front controls are installed.

verification.title: Record programming completion
verification.body: Record completion of ACM PMI and, where required, DACMC PMI after replacement. Do not treat a completed bolt-up as completion of configuration transfer.

procedures.purpose: ACM removal, installation and replacement configuration for vehicles with SYNC.
ACM removal and installation for SYNC 2/SYNC 3, including display access and conditional DACMC programming.
FCIM removal and installation for the SYNC access branch.
FCIM removal and installation for the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 access branch.

guides.title: Replace the floor-console audio input jack on a 2015 Mustang with SYNC
guides.summary: Open the console storage lid, release the small input-panel bezel, unplug its two connectors and release the jack’s upper and lower retaining tabs. Applies to 2015 Mustangs with SYNC and the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
guides.introduction: The little LINE IN socket gets a remarkably comfortable home under the console lid. Unfortunately, replacing it means evicting its plastic surround first. I’ll walk you through freeing that panel, disconnecting the wiring and releasing the jack without turning a small trim job into a damn console wrestling match.
guides.why: The audio input jack gives an external audio source a connection to the car’s entertainment system. The round LINE IN socket sits beside a USB opening in a small removable panel. That panel’s surround is called the bezel. Removing it first exposes the electrical connectors and the tabs that hold the jack in place, so each part can be released without pulling against the next.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang SYNC audio input jack replacement
Mustang auxiliary input jack retaining tabs

when.summary: Use this procedure when the audio input jack needs removal or replacement for an established repair.
notes: The same removal and installation sequence applies to the listed 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L applications with SYNC.

prepare.title: Make room at the console
prepare.detail: Clear the floor-console storage area so you can reach the small LINE IN/USB panel beneath the lid and support it when released.

prepare.title: Have a trim wedge and the replacement ready
prepare.detail: The removal illustration shows a trim-removal wedge. Have one ready for the bezel, along with the correct replacement audio input jack for your vehicle. Compare its connector locations and retaining features with the removed part before installation.

prepare.title: Set the working boundary
prepare.detail: This is a removal and replacement procedure, with no electrical fault test or exact trim-tool insertion point defined. Establish the need for replacement before buying a jack. If the bezel will not release with controlled trim-tool pressure, stop and resolve its retention before applying more force.

steps.title: Open the floor-console storage lid
steps.body: Raise the lid between the front seats. Locate the small panel marked LINE IN, with the USB opening alongside it. This is the bezel you need to release; the adjacent circular power socket is a separate feature. The access and replacement sequence is covered in [Audio Input Jack](#/document/G1704850).

steps.title: Release the audio input jack bezel
steps.body:
Use the trim-removal wedge at the bezel edge to ease the small panel out of the console opening. Keep the panel supported as it comes free: its wiring is still connected behind it.

Move it only far enough to reach the rear connectors. I treat the freed panel as something to hold, not something to leave dangling from two expensive little leashes.

steps.title: Disconnect both rear electrical connectors
steps.body:
With the bezel supported, locate the two connectors shown behind the panel. Depress each connector’s locking feature, as indicated by the release arrows, and separate the connector from the jack assembly.

Hold the connector housings while unplugging them; do not pull on the wires. Disconnect both before trying to separate the jack from its bezel.

steps.title: Release the upper and lower tabs and remove the jack
steps.body:
Look behind the bezel for the retaining tabs at the top and bottom of the jack housing. The illustration shows the upper tab moving upward and the lower tab moving downward, away from the jack.

Move both tabs clear of the housing, then withdraw the jack from the bezel. The tab-release movements come first; the jack’s withdrawal is the second movement. If it remains caught, check that both tabs are clear before pulling again. More enthusiasm is not a substitute for releasing the other clip.

steps.title: Fit the replacement jack into the bezel
steps.body:
Orient the replacement like the removed jack and slide it back into the bezel, reversing the withdrawal movement. Allow the upper and lower retaining tabs to engage.

Check that the jack stays seated in the bezel before reconnecting the wiring. If it shifts out of position, correct the seating and tab engagement now, while you can still see the back.

steps.title: Reconnect both electrical connectors
steps.body:
Support the assembled bezel and reconnect each plug to its corresponding connection on the jack. Seat both connectors and check that their locking features engage.

Keep the wiring behind the panel clear of the bezel edge as you bring the assembly back toward the console opening.

steps.title: Refit the bezel and close the console lid
steps.body:
Return the bezel to its console opening and press it into its seated position. Check around its edge for an even fit and confirm the jack remains retained when the panel is installed.

Close the console lid and confirm it moves normally. Installation reverses the removal order: jack into bezel, connectors onto jack, bezel into console.

watchFor.title: A released bezel still attached to wiring
watchFor.body: Support the panel until both connectors are disconnected. Its freedom from the console does not mean it is ready to carry away.

watchFor.title: One retaining tab still engaged
watchFor.body: The jack has upper and lower retention points. Check both before increasing withdrawal force.

watchFor.title: Wiring caught behind the bezel edge
watchFor.body: Keep both wiring connections behind the panel and clear of its seating edge during installation. If the panel will not seat evenly, bring it back out and check the routing.

notes: The [Information and Entertainment System overview](#/document/G1692884) identifies the audio input jack as part of the SYNC audio system and lists front and rear USB ports/cables separately. This procedure covers the console audio input jack; it does not extend to replacing those USB cables.

diagnostics.finding: A connector will not separate from the jack.
diagnostics.meaning: The connector has not yet been released; resistance alone does not establish an electrical fault.
diagnostics.next: Support the panel, check that the connector’s locking feature is depressed and separate it by its housing without pulling the wires.

diagnostics.finding: The jack stays caught after an attempted tab release.
diagnostics.meaning: The jack has not cleared its mechanical retention.
diagnostics.next: Check the upper and lower tabs together, move them clear of the housing and withdraw the jack only after both release.

diagnostics.finding: The installed jack moves out of its seated position.
diagnostics.meaning: Its retention is not secure enough to finish reassembly.
diagnostics.next: Recheck the jack’s orientation, seating and engagement with both retaining tabs before installing the bezel.

verification.title: Confirm jack retention
verification.body: Check that the jack is seated in the bezel and held by its upper and lower retaining tabs.

verification.title: Confirm both connections
verification.body: Before seating the bezel, verify that both electrical connectors are fully reconnected and their locking features are engaged.

verification.title: Confirm console reassembly
verification.body: Check that the bezel sits evenly in its opening, no wiring is trapped at its edge and the console lid opens and closes normally.

procedures.purpose: Primary procedure for console-lid access, bezel removal, electrical disconnection, jack retaining-tab release and reverse-order installation.
System context identifying the audio input jack within the SYNC entertainment system and distinguishing separately listed USB ports and cables.

stepGroups.title: Reach the console input panel
stepGroups.summary: Open the storage lid and release the bezel while supporting its connected wiring.

stepGroups.title: Disconnect and remove the jack
stepGroups.summary: Unplug both connectors, clear the two retaining tabs and withdraw the jack.

stepGroups.title: Install and secure the assembly
stepGroups.summary: Seat the replacement jack, reconnect the wiring and restore the bezel.

guides.title: Replace the radio antenna amplifier with SYNC, SYNC 2 or SYNC 3
guides.summary: Lower the headliner, replace the audio unit antenna amplifier and reconnect its electrical connectors before restoring the trim.
guides.introduction: The audio unit antenna amplifier works on the incoming radio signal used by the audio system. It is reached by lowering the headliner, so careful interior access is a substantial part of this otherwise short replacement. Separate procedures cover SYNC and SYNC 2/SYNC 3 vehicles, with the same stated amplifier removal and installation sequence.
guides.why: The amplifier has both a bolted attachment and electrical connections. Removing its attachment gives access to release the unit, but the connectors must also be disconnected before it is taken away. During installation, restoring every connection and tightening the mounting bolt completes the signal path and mechanical attachment before the headliner conceals them.

when.summary: When the audio unit antenna amplifier has been identified for replacement or requires removal for related service.
notes: A reception concern alone does not establish an amplifier fault.

prepare.title: Identify the fitted audio system
prepare.detail: Select the SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedure that matches the vehicle. The system overviews distinguish SYNC's non-touchscreen display from the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 touchscreen arrangement.

prepare.title: Prepare for headliner access
prepare.detail: Be equipped to lower and restore the headliner using the Headliner - Lowering procedure referenced by both amplifier procedures.

prepare.title: Prepare fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the amplifier bolt and a torque wrench capable of 106 lb.in (12 Nm).

steps.title: Select the procedure and lower the headliner
steps.body: Use [Audio Unit Antenna Amplifier — SYNC](#/document/G1694047) or [Audio Unit Antenna Amplifier — SYNC 2/SYNC 3](#/document/G1693893). Lower the headliner using the referenced access procedure to expose the amplifier.

steps.title: Release the amplifier and its connections
steps.body: Remove the mounting bolt and release the amplifier from its mounting location. Keep control of the unit while disconnecting its electrical connectors, then remove it.

steps.title: Reconnect and secure the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: reconnect the electrical connectors, position the amplifier and install its bolt. Tighten the bolt to 106 lb.in (12 Nm), as specified in both equipment procedures.

steps.title: Restore the headliner
steps.body: Confirm the amplifier attachment and connector installation before restoring the headliner through the access procedure. This finishes the interior work after the concealed component is secured.

watchFor.title: A connector left disconnected
watchFor.body: Both procedures call for disconnecting the electrical connectors. Account for every disturbed connection during reverse-order installation.

watchFor.title: Closing access too early
watchFor.body: Complete the bolt and connector checks while the amplifier remains accessible.

notes: The matching procedure should be selected by fitted audio equipment, even though the stated replacement sequence and bolt torque agree.

verification.title: Check the concealed assembly
verification.body: Confirm the amplifier is secured, all disturbed electrical connectors are reconnected and the headliner has been restored.

verification.title: Record the mounting-bolt check
verification.body: Record completion of the 106 lb.in (12 Nm) mounting-bolt torque check before restoring the headliner.

procedures.purpose: Audio unit antenna amplifier removal and installation for vehicles with SYNC.
Audio unit antenna amplifier removal and installation for vehicles with SYNC 2/SYNC 3.

guides.title: Replace an AM/FM antenna cable on a SYNC-equipped Mustang
guides.summary: Fit a replacement AM/FM antenna cable alongside the existing wiring harness, using the access route for the body style and cable section.
guides.introduction: The antenna cable carries the received radio signal to the audio unit. Its original routing is built into the vehicle wiring harness, so replacement means adding a new cable along that harness while leaving the original cable in place. Access changes substantially between the front and rear sections, and between coupe and convertible bodies.
guides.why: The inline connection beneath the floor console divides the access work. Identifying the required section first avoids unnecessary interior dismantling. Following the illustrated harness route and securing the overlay prevents the replacement cable from becoming a source of noise, vibration and harshness.
searchTerms: antenna cable connection under floor console

when.summary: When an AM/FM antenna cable section has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Choose the access branch by body style and cable section before removing trim.
This is a cable replacement procedure; it does not establish the cause of a radio reception complaint.

prepare.title: Plan the interior access
prepare.detail: Be equipped to remove the floor console and, where required, the audio unit. Coupe rear-cable work requires headliner lowering; convertible rear-cable work requires luggage-compartment trim access.

prepare.title: Have the replacement and supports ready
prepare.detail: Provide the replacement AM/FM antenna cable and tape or zip ties to secure it along the vehicle harness. Keep the appropriate body-style routing illustration available during installation.

steps.title: Select the equipment procedure and cable section
steps.body: Use the [SYNC cable procedure](#/document/G1694048) or [SYNC 2/SYNC 3 cable procedure](#/document/G1693894) as applicable. Locate the inline connection beneath the floor console and establish which section is being replaced. The original harness-integrated cable stays in the vehicle.

steps.title: Open the console and audio-unit access
steps.body: Remove the floor console for every access branch. Coupe front-cable work also requires removal of the Audio Front Control Module (ACM). The convertible audio-unit access branch likewise specifies console and ACM removal. Use the linked console and ACM procedures for their individual removal and installation details.

steps.title: For a coupe rear cable, lower the headliner
steps.body: After removing the console, lower the headliner using the Headliner — Lowering procedure in Section 501-05. This provides the additional access specified for the coupe rear section; it is a separate branch from coupe front-cable work.

steps.title: For a convertible rear cable, expose the luggage-compartment route
steps.body: Remove the loadspace trim panel and spare tire cover. If fitted, remove the subwoofer and amplifier unit. Remove the pin-type retainers, then position the right-hand luggage-compartment side trim panel aside to expose the rear cable route.

steps.title: Lay in the replacement cable
steps.body: Overlay the new cable on the existing vehicle wiring harness, following the routing illustration for the relevant body style. Preserve the harness as an assembly rather than attempting to extract its original antenna cable.

steps.title: Secure the overlay and restore access parts
steps.body: Attach the replacement cable to the harness with tape or zip ties as necessary to prevent movement and noise. Check its route before covering it, then reinstall the components removed for access using their respective installation procedures.

watchFor.title: An original cable that will not separate
watchFor.body: The original cable is part of the wiring harness. Resistance to removal is not a reason to pull harder; the specified repair is an overlay.

watchFor.title: Unsupported replacement cable
watchFor.body: Loose sections can create noise after the trim is restored. Secure the overlay along its illustrated route.

notes: The convertible subwoofer and amplifier removal applies only when that equipment is fitted.
Use the body-style-specific routing view; an illustration should not be treated as a universal route.

verification.title: Routing and retention
verification.body: Confirm that the new cable follows the applicable illustrated harness route and is secured with tape or zip ties where necessary.

verification.title: Access work completed
verification.body: Confirm that the console, audio unit and any headliner or luggage-compartment components disturbed for this cable section have been restored.

procedures.purpose: Antenna cable replacement by overlay for vehicles with SYNC, including coupe and convertible access branches.
Antenna cable replacement by overlay for vehicles with SYNC 2/SYNC 3, including front and rear cable access.
Floor console removal and installation for access to the antenna cable inline connection.
Audio Front Control Module removal and installation where required by the cable access branch.
Convertible loadspace trim panel removal and installation for rear-cable access.
Removal and installation of the subwoofer and amplifier unit when fitted in the convertible rear-cable access area.

applicability.equipment: SYNC, SYNC 2 or SYNC 3; coupe or convertible

guides.title: Replace the audio antenna on a coupe or convertible
guides.summary: Follow the body-specific repair path: replace the rear window glass on a coupe or remove the mast, base and antenna assembly on a convertible.
guides.introduction: The audio antenna receives broadcast radio signals for the sound system. Its physical arrangement depends on the body: the coupe antenna forms part of the rear window glass, while the convertible has a removable mast and an antenna assembly reached through the luggage compartment. The SYNC and SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedures use the same body-specific sequence.
guides.why: Identifying the antenna arrangement first determines the scale of the work. A coupe requires fixed-glass replacement capability. On a convertible, opening the trim access and releasing the antenna tabs in sequence lets the assembly come free before its electrical connector is disconnected.

when.summary: When antenna damage or completed reception diagnosis justifies replacement.
notes: Poor reception alone does not establish that the antenna needs replacement.
Check the body style and whether a subwoofer and amplifier obstruct convertible access.

prepare.title: Choose the correct procedure
prepare.detail: Use the [SYNC procedure](#/document/G1694046) or [SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedure](#/document/G1693892), then follow the coupe or convertible branch.

prepare.title: Arrange the appropriate capability
prepare.detail: Coupe work requires fixed-glass replacement equipment and capability. Convertible work requires access to the right-hand luggage-compartment trim, tools for the retainers and mounting nut, and a torque wrench suitable for the antenna nut.

steps.title: Coupe: follow the fixed-glass replacement path
steps.body: The antenna is part of the rear window glass. Replace that glass using [Fixed Glass](#/document/G1695948), including its installation requirements. The convertible mast and base removal steps do not apply to this branch.

steps.title: Convertible: open the luggage-compartment access
steps.body: Remove the spare tire cover. If fitted, remove the [Subwoofer and Amplifier Unit](#/document/G1704011). This clears the equipment that must be removed before moving the side trim.

steps.title: Move the right-hand side trim aside
steps.body: Remove the pin-type retainers and position the right-hand luggage-compartment side trim panel aside. This exposes the antenna assembly without requiring the panel to be treated as part of the antenna.

steps.title: Remove the external mast and base
steps.body: Remove the antenna mast, followed by the mounting nut and antenna base. Keep this fastening arrangement distinct from the retaining tabs that hold the remaining antenna assembly.

steps.title: Release the antenna and disconnect it
steps.body: Press the retaining tabs inward, remove the antenna assembly and then disconnect its electrical connector. The illustration shows the tab release and connector as separate actions; release the housing before trying to pull it free.

steps.title: Install and restore the access area
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Reconnect and secure the antenna, install the base and tighten its mounting nut to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm), then refit the mast. Restore the side trim, its pin retainers, any removed subwoofer and amplifier, and the spare tire cover.

watchFor.title: Wrong antenna selected
watchFor.body: The equipped SYNC 2/SYNC 3 system identifies a separate satellite-radio antenna. Establish which antenna the repair concerns before removing components.

watchFor.title: Tabs still engaged
watchFor.body: Resistance at the convertible antenna housing calls for checking the retaining tabs, rather than pulling harder on the assembly or its wiring.

notes: HD Radio capability is identified with Shaker equipment; it does not change the supplied antenna removal sequence.

verification.title: Confirm body-specific completion
verification.body: For a convertible, check that the electrical connector, antenna retention, mounting nut, mast and removed trim are restored. For a coupe, complete the checks required by the fixed-glass procedure.

procedures.purpose: Audio antenna removal and installation for SYNC-equipped coupes and convertibles.
Audio antenna removal and installation for SYNC 2/SYNC 3-equipped coupes and convertibles.
Required fixed-glass replacement procedure for the coupe's rear-window antenna.
Removal and installation of the subwoofer and amplifier when fitted and obstructing convertible antenna access.

applicability.equipment: SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3; coupe or convertible

guides.title: Replace and configure the 4.2-inch SYNC display module
guides.summary: Save the module configuration, remove the console and dashboard trim to reach the FCDIM, then reinstall the display and complete its scan-tool configuration.
guides.introduction: The little SYNC screen has quite the entourage: getting it out means persuading a surprising amount of console trim to leave first. I’ll take you through that procession in order, keeping the display separate from the button panel below it. The front control/display interface module, or FCDIM, provides the 4.2-inch non-touchscreen display. The front controls interface module, or FCIM, is the separate control panel you must remove to reach it. Both belong to the wider [information and entertainment system](#/document/G1692884), so a display complaint alone does not prove the screen module has failed.
guides.why: When replacing the FCDIM, its existing vehicle configuration must be saved before removal and transferred into the replacement afterward. Ford calls this programmable module installation, or PMI. I treat that electronic handover as part of the replacement itself: the bolts hold the module in place, but they cannot tell it how this Mustang is equipped.

when.summary: Use this procedure when diagnosis has established that the FCDIM needs replacement, or when the existing module must be removed and reinstalled for access.
notes: Applies to 2015 Mustangs with the specified SYNC 4.2-inch non-touchscreen FCDIM and 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engines.
The selector-trim illustrations show an automatic transmission; Ford describes the manual-transmission procedure as similar.
The dashboard finish-panel illustration includes the optional ICM. Disconnect and reconnect its electrical connector only if fitted.

FCDIM replacement requires configuration capture before removal and PMI completion after installation. Merely removing and reinstalling the original module does not require the replacement-only final PMI step.

prepare.title: Arrange the electronic handover first
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool capable of performing FCDIM and FCIM PMI. Keep the original modules installed for the initial scan-tool work. A replacement FCDIM requires its configuration to be uploaded before removal; if that cannot be accomplished, stop before dismantling and resolve configuration recovery with appropriate service support. Recovery instructions are outside this procedure.

prepare.title: Gather tools and the intended replacement
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover, tools that fit the actual fasteners, and a torque tool capable of accurately applying 18 lb.in (2 Nm) and 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm). If replacing the display, arrange the correct FCDIM for this vehicle and display arrangement. Keep removed fasteners grouped by location so the console hardware does not become a tiny, expensive jigsaw.

prepare.title: Prepare the car and protect yourself
prepare.detail: Work with the vehicle stationary on the ground and the parking brake set. If remote start is fitted, disable it through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before service. Follow the scan tool's ignition instructions during PMI; before physically dismantling the interior, switch the ignition off and remove the key to prevent another person starting the car. Wear eye and ear protection while servicing, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged components. See [health and safety precautions](#/document/G1693189).

prepare.title: Plan space for panels and wiring
prepare.detail: Make room to place the console side panels, upper console panel, dashboard finish panel and FCIM safely aside. As each wired panel comes loose, support it while releasing its connector locks; do not let a panel hang from its wiring.

steps.title: Begin FCDIM and FCIM PMI before removing anything
steps.body:
With both modules still installed, use the diagnostic scan tool to begin FCDIM PMI and follow its on-screen instructions. If fitting a new FCDIM, upload its configuration to the tool before removal.

Next begin FCIM PMI as directed in the [FCIM procedure](#/document/G1704003). If the FCIM itself will also be replaced, save its configuration before removing it. Access to the FCDIM normally involves removing and reinstalling the existing FCIM; that does not make it a replacement.

Once the preliminary scan-tool work permits dismantling, switch the ignition off and remove the key before proceeding.

steps.title: Remove the right-hand console side trim
steps.body: Find the small floor-console side panel below the front of the center stack on the right-hand side. Use the interior trim remover at the panel edge to release its five retaining clips, working around the panel rather than pulling hard against clips that are still engaged. Remove the panel.

steps.title: Remove the left-hand console side trim
steps.body: Use the interior trim remover to release the five clips securing the corresponding left-hand floor-console side panel. Take the panel away once the clips are free. These two panels expose the sides of the console's front attachment area.

steps.title: Lift out the stowage mat and remove the upper console bolts
steps.body: Lift the mat out of the small stowage area immediately below the center-stack switches and ahead of the selector. Remove the two floor-console upper bolts revealed beneath it. Keep these bolts separate from the side retainers removed later.

steps.title: Release the selector bezel, move the boot aside and unplug it
steps.body:
Use the interior trim remover to release the selector-lever bezel. The automatic-transmission illustration shows five clips around its perimeter and release points at its forward edge.

Position the selector-lever boot aside, then release the lock on its electrical connector and disconnect it. Leave the selector trim supported without pulling on the harness. Ford describes the manual-transmission arrangement as similar; use the corresponding bezel and boot on that car rather than expecting the automatic markings and shape.

steps.title: Open the console lid and remove the front side retainers
steps.body:
Open the floor-console storage lid. At the front of the console, remove the two right-hand side retainers exposed by the side-panel removal, then remove the two left-hand side retainers.

Their installation torque is 18 lb.in (2 Nm) on both sides. Keep all four identified for reassembly.

steps.title: Lift off the upper console trim and disconnect its wiring
steps.body:
Release the eight clips holding the floor-console upper trim panel—the long panel containing the cupholders and extending forward around the selector. Use the interior trim remover to assist the clip release, then lift the panel upward as its clips disengage.

Keep the gear-selector cover positioned aside while lifting the upper panel clear. Support the panel, disconnect the electrical connectors underneath it, and remove it. I like to pause here and account for the connectors: a trim panel is a poor tool for discovering how far a harness stretches.

steps.title: Remove the stowage tray
steps.body: With the upper console trim removed, lift out the stowage-area tray beneath the center-stack switches. This is the molded tray that remained below the mat and its two bolt recesses; the illustration shows it lifting upward.

steps.title: Release the right-hand dashboard trim panel
steps.body: Use the interior trim remover to release the three clips securing the narrow right-hand instrument-panel trim panel beside the glovebox. Remove this panel first, as shown in the [instrument panel center finish-panel procedure](#/document/G1693976).

steps.title: Remove the dashboard center finish panel
steps.body:
Release the clips securing the wide instrument-panel center finish panel, which runs across the upper center stack and passenger-side dashboard. The illustration identifies thirteen clips; work around the panel with the interior trim remover and support it as it comes free.

If the optional ICM is fitted, release and disconnect its electrical connector behind the panel before taking the panel away. A car without that module does not need this connector operation.

steps.title: Remove the small lower center-stack trim cover
steps.body: Use the interior trim remover to release the small rectangular trim cover below the switch row, between the USB-port area and the round power outlet. Remove the cover to expose the lower FCIM mounting area.

steps.title: Unbolt and disconnect the FCIM
steps.body:
Remove the four FCIM mounting bolts: two at the top of the control-panel assembly and two in its lower mounting area. Support the assembly and draw it clear far enough to reach the rear electrical connectors.

Release the connector locks and unplug the electrical connectors, then remove the FCIM. The bolts will be tightened to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm) during installation. You should now have access to the separate display module behind the control-panel opening.

steps.title: Remove the FCDIM and disconnect its rear connector
steps.body:
Identify the rectangular display module below the center air outlets. Remove its four mounting bolts, one at each corner of the side mounting brackets, while supporting the module.

Move the FCDIM out of its mounting position, release the locking tab on the rear electrical connector, and unplug it. Remove the module. This is the final hardware-removal stage of the [FCDIM procedure](#/document/G1704851).

steps.title: Connect and fasten the display module
steps.body:
Reconnect the rear electrical connector to the replacement FCDIM, or to the original module if it is being reused. Make sure the connector is fully seated and its lock engaged, then position the module and its brackets at the four mounting points.

Install the four bolts and tighten them to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm). Keep the harness clear of the mounting surfaces as the module seats.

steps.title: Refit the FCIM and its lower trim cover
steps.body:
