Reconnect the electrical connectors at the back of the FCIM and confirm their locks engage. Position the panel without trapping wiring, install its four bolts, and tighten them to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm).

Refit the small rectangular lower trim cover between the USB-port area and power outlet, seating it in its original opening.

steps.title: Restore the dashboard finish panels
steps.body:
If the optional ICM connector was disconnected, reconnect and lock it before bringing the wide center finish panel back against the dashboard. Align the panel's thirteen clips with their mounting locations and seat the panel evenly.

Then align and engage the three clips on the narrow right-hand instrument-panel trim panel beside the glovebox. Check the adjoining panel edges sit flush before moving on.

steps.title: Put the stowage tray back
steps.body: Return the molded stowage-area tray to its position below the center-stack switches. Seat it in the opening and align its bolt recesses for the console hardware that will be restored later.

steps.title: Reconnect and seat the upper console trim
steps.body:
Support the floor-console upper trim panel above the console and reconnect the electrical connectors underneath it. Confirm each connector lock has engaged.

Keep the gear-selector cover positioned aside while lowering the panel into place. Align the eight retaining clips, check that wiring is clear of the edges and clip locations, then seat the panel. The cupholder section and forward console edges should lie evenly against the surrounding trim.

steps.title: Install the left-hand and right-hand console retainers
steps.body:
Reinstall the two left-hand front console retainers, followed by the two right-hand front retainers. Tighten each to 18 lb.in (2 Nm).

These are inch-pound values. A small trim fastener does not need the full motivational speech from a long wrench.

steps.title: Restore the console lid, selector wiring, boot and bezel
steps.body:
Close the console storage lid. Reconnect the electrical connector disconnected at the selector trim and confirm its lock engages.

Return the selector boot and gear-selector cover from their aside positions. Align the selector-lever bezel and engage its retaining clips; the illustrated automatic bezel has five. Check that the boot is seated rather than caught beneath the bezel.

steps.title: Reinstall the console upper bolts and stowage mat
steps.body: Install the two floor-console upper bolts through the stowage-area recesses, restoring their original attachment. Return the mat over the bolt recesses and lay it flat in the tray.

steps.title: Refit both console side panels
steps.body:
Refit the left-hand floor-console side panel first, aligning and engaging its five clips. Then refit the right-hand panel in the same way, engaging its five clips.

Check the panel edges meet the console evenly and that neither panel remains loose at a clip location.

steps.title: Complete replacement PMI and check the finished installation
steps.body:
If the FCIM was replaced, complete its PMI using the diagnostic scan tool and download the saved FCIM configuration as directed on screen. If the original FCIM was simply removed and reinstalled, its replacement-only completion step does not apply.

If the FCDIM was replaced, complete FCDIM PMI and download the configuration saved before removal, following the tool's on-screen instructions. Reinstalling the original FCDIM does not require this replacement-only completion step.

After the required programming is complete, check normal display and control operation and review the physical installation checks below. An unfinished PMI operation is an unfinished replacement, however tidy the dashboard looks.

watchFor.title: Configuration must be captured before a replacement is disconnected
watchFor.body: Begin the scan-tool process while the original modules are installed. Capture FCDIM configuration before replacing the display, and FCIM configuration before replacing the control panel if that additional replacement is planned.

watchFor.title: The display and control panel are different modules
watchFor.body: The FCIM comes out to provide access. Its four mounting bolts and the FCDIM's four mounting bolts both use 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm), but each module has its own connectors and PMI process.

watchFor.title: Panel resistance deserves a closer look
watchFor.body: Before pulling harder, look for a clip that remains engaged or a connector still attached. Release the relevant attachment with the trim remover or connector lock and support the panel as it comes free.

watchFor.title: Keep the small torque values straight
watchFor.body: The four console front side retainers use 18 lb.in (2 Nm). The FCIM and FCDIM mounting bolts use 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm). Do not apply those module values to unrelated trim hardware.

notes: This is a removal, installation and configuration article. It does not establish an electrical fault test or a basis for condemning the FCDIM.
Install the access trim in reverse removal order. Clip-retained panels and the stowage-area upper bolts are restored without borrowing a tightening value from another fastener.
The automatic selector is illustrated and the manual procedure is described as similar; no separate manual-specific selector dismantling sequence is established here.

diagnostics.finding: A blank or otherwise troublesome display is the only reason being considered for replacement.
diagnostics.meaning: The display is one component in a system that also contains separate audio, SYNC and control modules. The complaint alone does not identify a failed FCDIM.
diagnostics.next: Establish the fault through appropriate diagnosis before buying or replacing the module. This article provides no circuit tests or failure thresholds.

diagnostics.finding: The FCIM is being reused after removal for display access.
diagnostics.meaning: Removing the control panel for access is different from replacing it.
diagnostics.next: Begin its PMI process as directed before removal, reinstall its original connectors and hardware, and omit the replacement-only final FCIM PMI completion step.

diagnostics.finding: An electrical connector is present on the optional ICM behind the wide dashboard finish panel.
diagnostics.meaning: That panel has an additional wired attachment.
diagnostics.next: Support the panel, disconnect the ICM connector before removal, and reconnect it before seating the panel during reassembly.

diagnostics.finding: The manual-transmission selector trim does not release using the corresponding bezel-and-boot operations.
diagnostics.meaning: The automatic illustration is not enough to establish additional manual-specific dismantling.
diagnostics.next: Stop at the selector trim and obtain matching instructions for that arrangement before forcing or dismantling additional parts.

diagnostics.finding: A replacement module's final PMI process does not complete.
diagnostics.meaning: The required configuration handover remains unresolved.
diagnostics.next: Retain the scan tool's failure information and resolve the programming issue before treating the replacement as finished. Do not use further parts replacement as a substitute for completing configuration.

verification.title: Confirm module mounting and connector engagement
verification.body: Confirm the FCDIM's four bolts and FCIM's four bolts were tightened to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm), their connectors were fully seated and locked, and wiring was clear of mounting surfaces.

verification.title: Confirm console and dashboard restoration
verification.body: Confirm the four console front side retainers were tightened to 18 lb.in (2 Nm), both stowage-area upper bolts are installed, and the mat and tray are restored. Check the dashboard finish panels, lower trim cover, upper console panel, selector bezel and both console side panels are seated. Confirm the optional ICM and console electrical connectors were reconnected wherever disconnected.

verification.title: Confirm the required configuration transfer
verification.body: For every module actually replaced, confirm its PMI completed and its saved configuration was downloaded. A reused module does not require the replacement-only final step.

verification.title: Check ordinary operation after assembly
verification.body: Check that the display operates and responds to the reinstalled controls, and that the selector boot, bezel and console lid sit and move normally. These are completion checks, not a diagnostic test proving every part of the entertainment system is fault-free. If the original complaint remains, return to diagnosis.

procedures.purpose: Primary FCDIM removal and installation, four mounting bolts, 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm) tightening torque and replacement configuration transfer through PMI.
Identify the 4.2-inch non-touchscreen display arrangement and explain its place among the separate information and entertainment system components.
Provide the complete console and FCIM access sequence, connector operations, reverse-order refitting, console-retainer and FCIM torques, transmission qualifier and FCIM PMI requirements.
Remove and reinstall the right-hand instrument-panel trim and wide center finish panel, including the optional ICM electrical connection.
Apply relevant remote-start prevention, key control and personal-protection precautions before service.

stepGroups.title: Save configuration before dismantling
stepGroups.summary: Begin the module installation processes with the original hardware connected.

stepGroups.title: Open the console access
stepGroups.summary: Remove side trim, selector trim, console attachments, upper trim and the stowage tray.

stepGroups.title: Remove dashboard trim and the FCIM
stepGroups.summary: Release the finish panels and disconnect the control assembly to expose the display.

stepGroups.title: Remove and install the FCDIM
stepGroups.summary: Disconnect the display, install the intended module and tighten its four mounting bolts.

stepGroups.title: Restore controls and interior trim
stepGroups.summary: Reconnect the control panel and restore the dashboard and console in reverse order.

stepGroups.title: Complete programming and check the result
stepGroups.summary: Finish PMI for replaced modules and confirm the assembled display and trim operate normally.

guides.title: Replace the front controls interface module on SYNC-equipped vehicles
guides.summary: Remove the console and center-panel trim, replace the FCIM, and transfer its configuration using the applicable scan-tool procedure.
guides.introduction: The front controls interface module (FCIM) forms part of the information and entertainment system's front controls. It works alongside separate display, audio and SYNC components. Access requires dismantling the upper floor-console trim and instrument-panel center finish panel. Installing a replacement also requires transferring the original module configuration.
guides.why: The trim comes apart in a defined order because clips, retainers and electrical connections remain hidden until surrounding pieces are moved. The electronic sequence matters just as much: configuration must be uploaded before the old module is removed so it can be downloaded into the replacement.

when.summary: When the FCIM requires removal or has been identified for replacement.
notes: Select the procedure by the fitted information and entertainment system.
Both procedures illustrate an automatic transmission; their instructions state that manual-transmission access is similar.

prepare.title: Provide configuration capability
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool capable of the FCIM programmable module installation (PMI) process. Replacement requires configuration capture before removal and transfer after installation.

prepare.title: Prepare for interior dismantling
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover, suitable fastener tools and a torque wrench for the small console and module fasteners. Keep access available around both sides of the floor console.

steps.title: Select the system and begin PMI
steps.body: Use [the SYNC procedure](#/document/G1704003) for the non-touchscreen system or [the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedure](#/document/G1704007) for the touchscreen system. Begin PMI following the scan-tool prompts. If replacing the module, upload its configuration before proceeding with removal.

steps.title: Open the console access
steps.body: Release the clips and remove the right and left console side trim panels with the trim remover. Remove the stowage mat and console upper bolts. Remove the selector-lever bezel, position the boot aside and disconnect its electrical connector.

steps.title: Remove the console upper trim
steps.body: Open the console lid and remove the front retainers on both sides. Release the clips, move the gear-selector cover aside and remove the upper trim panel, disconnecting its electrical connectors. Remove the stowage tray to complete this access stage.

steps.title: Expose the FCIM
steps.body: Remove the [instrument panel center finish panel](#/document/G1693976), then remove the trim cover with the interior trim remover. This exposes the FCIM mounting bolts without forcing the surrounding trim.

steps.title: Exchange the module and rebuild the trim
steps.body: Remove the FCIM bolts, disconnect its electrical connectors and remove the module. Install in reverse order. Tighten the FCIM bolts to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm) and the console side-front retainers to 18 lb.in (2 Nm). Restore each connector as its panel is refitted.

steps.title: Complete replacement programming
steps.body: When a replacement FCIM has been installed, complete PMI using the diagnostic scan tool and its on-screen instructions, including downloading the saved configuration. This final PMI step is specified only for component replacement.

watchFor.title: Configuration not captured
watchFor.body: Do not move ahead with a module exchange before the required configuration upload has been completed.

watchFor.title: Trim still attached
watchFor.body: Resistance during panel removal can indicate a remaining fastener, clip or electrical connection. Follow the access sequence before moving a panel farther.

notes: The SYNC and SYNC 2/SYNC 3 articles share this removal sequence, but each remains the procedure for its named equipment.

verification.title: Confirm interior reassembly
verification.body: Verify that the module and disconnected panel connectors are restored, the trim clips are seated and the specified fasteners are tightened.

verification.title: Record the programming result
verification.body: For a replacement module, confirm configuration download and completion of the scan-tool PMI instructions. Record the completion result and whether the original module was retained or replaced.

procedures.purpose: FCIM removal and installation for vehicles with SYNC, including pre-removal configuration capture and replacement-only PMI completion.
FCIM removal and installation for vehicles with SYNC 2/SYNC 3, including pre-removal configuration capture and replacement-only PMI completion.
Instrument-panel center finish-panel removal and installation required for FCIM access.

guides.title: Replace the left front door midwoofer or woofer
guides.summary: Remove the window-switch bezel and door trim, replace the selected speaker, and restore the latch cable, wiring and panel retainers with the correct tightening values.
guides.introduction: A door speaker should deliver the bass line, not audition as a kazoo. Once the speaker needing replacement has been identified, I’ll walk you through reaching it without turning the door trim into a collection of plastic souvenirs. The midwoofer and woofer turn electrical audio signals into sound by moving their cones; both sit behind the complete door trim panel.
guides.why: The speaker grille is not the access route for this repair. The door trim must come off, which means releasing its fasteners and clips, unplugging the window switch and panel wiring, and disconnecting the interior-handle latch cable. I take those attachments in stages so the panel’s weight never hangs from a wire or cable.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang left front door speaker replacement

when.summary: Use this guide when an identified left front door midwoofer or woofer requires removal or replacement.
notes: Applies to 2015 Mustang models with 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engines and SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3 equipment.
Service only the speaker selected for replacement; removing the trim does not require removing both speakers.

The trim illustrations show the right door, with the left door handled similarly. Left-hand-drive illustrations also apply similarly to right-hand-drive vehicles; use front, rear, upper and lower door positions to orient yourself.

prepare.title: Gather the trim and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have a trim-removal wedge, tools matching the fitted fasteners, and a low-range torque tool covering 13–48 lb.in (1.5–5.4 Nm). Keep the upper bolt, center bolt, two lower retainers and speaker bolts separated so each returns to its own location.

prepare.title: Have the correct replacement ready
prepare.detail: Obtain the replacement for the selected left front midwoofer or woofer and the fitted audio system. Compare its mounting shape and electrical connection with the removed unit before installation. The smaller midwoofer has a roughly square mounting carrier; the larger woofer has a round mounting flange. Each illustrated unit uses three mounting bolts.

prepare.title: Set the execution boundary
prepare.detail: Start with the affected speaker already identified. This guide covers removal and installation; electrical fault isolation, speaker resistance limits and audio-module tests require a separate diagnostic procedure. If the fitted door or speaker mounting differs from the arrangements described here, get matching instructions before dismantling farther.

prepare.title: Make room to handle the panel
prepare.detail: Allow enough space to open the left front door and support the detached trim panel while releasing its wiring and latch cable. Have a protected place ready for the panel and window-switch bezel.

prepare.title: Protect yourself at the exposed door
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged components or exposed door metal. The task is performed with the vehicle on the ground; no lifting or underhood access is needed.

steps.title: Secure the vehicle and prevent an unexpected start
steps.body: Park the vehicle and apply the parking brake. If remote start is fitted, disable it through the central display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before beginning work around the vehicle. Switch the ignition and audio system off and remove the key from the vehicle. Keep the ignition off while disconnecting and reconnecting the door components.

steps.title: Match the audio configuration and select the speaker
steps.body:
For SYNC, use the [left front speaker procedure](#/document/G1694049); for SYNC 2/SYNC 3, use the [corresponding speaker procedure](#/document/G1693897). Both give the same removal sequence and speaker-bolt torque.

For orientation, the [SYNC overview](#/document/G1692884) describes six speakers and a 4.2-inch non-touchscreen display. The [touchscreen-system overview](#/document/G1702412) describes an 8-inch display with nine speakers without Shaker or ten with Shaker. These descriptions help identify equipment; they do not establish which speaker has failed. Keep the replacement matched to the fitted system.

steps.title: Remove the interior-handle bolt cover and upper bolt
steps.body:
At the interior door-release handle recess, remove the small cover concealing the upper trim-panel bolt. Remove the bolt and retain the cover separately. Its installation torque is 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm).

This begins the [door-trim access procedure](#/document/G1692600). The whole panel will come away later; leave it supported by its remaining attachments for now.

steps.title: Lift out the window-switch bezel and unplug the switch
steps.body:
Use the trim-removal wedge to lift the long window-switch bezel from the armrest, releasing its four retaining clips. Lift the switch and bezel together, then release and disconnect the electrical connector beneath the switch. Handle the connector housing rather than pulling on its wires.

For speaker access, leave the switch attached to its bezel. The separate switch-to-bezel removal is needed only when replacing the switch itself. The [window-switch procedure](#/document/G1695936) covers that conditional operation.

steps.title: Remove the center bolt and two lower retainers
steps.body:
With the switch bezel out, remove the center trim-panel bolt from the exposed armrest opening. Its installation torque is 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm).

Next remove the two retainers along the bottom edge of the trim panel. Their installation torque is 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm). Keep these apart from the two trim bolts: they do not share a tightening value.

steps.title: Release the rear upper corner
steps.body:
Start at the rear upper portion of the panel—the end nearest the door latch, away from the hinges. Ease that portion away from the door, release the upper clip, then release the two pin-type retainers below it. Pin-type retainers are the push-in fasteners holding the panel to the door.

Work at the attachment locations rather than bending a broad section of trim. If the panel remains firmly held, locate the next attachment before pulling farther. Plastic clips have enough opinions already.

steps.title: Release the rear and lower edge
steps.body: Move to the rear and lower portion of the panel. Release the pin-type retainer near the rear bottom corner first, then release the clip near the lower front speaker area. Ease this section away only far enough to free those attachments; the front edge and top are still attached.

steps.title: Release the remaining front-edge retainers
steps.body:
At the front of the door, nearest the hinges, release the lower pin-type retainer beside the speaker area, followed by the upper pin-type retainer farther up the front edge. The illustrated front-edge stage has two pin-type retainers in total.

The panel perimeter should now be free of its staged clips and pins. Do not pull it straight away from the door yet.

steps.title: Lift the panel up and out, then detach its connections
steps.body:
Support the panel and lift it up and out to release its top edge from the door. Hold it close enough that its remaining connections are not stretched.

Disconnect the panel electrical connectors where fitted. At the back of the interior door handle, release the latch-cable retainer and detach the cable connection. This cable links the interior handle to the door latch. Set the panel on the protected surface only after the wiring and cable are free.

steps.title: Midwoofer branch: remove the smaller speaker
steps.body:
Use this step only if the midwoofer is being serviced. Locate the smaller speaker in its roughly square carrier. Its three mounting bolts sit on the left, right and lower mounting ears.

Support the carrier, remove all three bolts, and move the speaker clear of its mounting. Release and disconnect the electrical connector at the lower side of the carrier. Set the speaker aside without loading its cone or hanging it from the wiring.

steps.title: Woofer branch: remove the larger speaker
steps.body:
Use this step only if the woofer is being serviced. Locate the larger round speaker lower in the door. Its three mounting bolts are spaced around the flange, with one on the left, one toward the upper right and one at the bottom.

Support the speaker, remove the three bolts, and move it clear of the opening. Release and disconnect its electrical connector near the lower-left side. Leave the other speaker installed unless it also requires service.

steps.title: Connect and secure the replacement speaker
steps.body:
Compare the replacement carrier or flange and connector with the removed speaker. If they do not match, resolve the part selection before fitting it.

Reconnect the electrical connector, position the speaker against its mounting, and install its three bolts. Confirm the connector is seated and the wiring is clear of the mounting face. Tighten each mounting bolt to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm). This value applies to both the midwoofer and woofer in both covered audio procedures.

Support the speaker by its carrier or flange while working. The cone is here to move air, not hold the damn assembly.

steps.title: Reconnect the panel and locate its top edge
steps.body:
Bring the trim panel back to the door and support it while reconnecting the latch cable to the interior handle and securing its retainer. Reconnect the panel electrical connectors where fitted. Transfer parts as necessary if a replacement panel is being installed.

Keep the window-switch connector accessible at the armrest opening. Check that the cable and wiring are not trapped behind the panel. Reverse the removal movement to locate the top edge, bringing the panel inward and lowering it into position.

steps.title: Seat the perimeter retainers in reverse order
steps.body:
Align each retainer with its door opening before pressing the panel into place at that attachment.

First seat the front-edge upper pin-type retainer, then the lower one. Next engage the clip near the lower front speaker area and the pin-type retainer near the rear bottom corner. Finish the rear upper section by seating its two pin-type retainers and then its upper clip.

Check that the perimeter sits against the door. A bolt should not be used to drag a misaligned panel into place.

steps.title: Refit the lower retainers and center bolt
steps.body:
Install the two lower trim-panel retainers and tighten them to 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm).

Install the center bolt through the exposed armrest opening and tighten it to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm). Keep the switch connector clear while tightening the bolt.

steps.title: Reconnect and seat the window-switch bezel
steps.body:
Reconnect the window-switch electrical connector. Locate the switch-and-bezel assembly in the armrest opening, align its four retaining clips and press it into place until the bezel sits evenly.

If the switch was separately replaced, secure it to the bezel before this step: the driver-side assembly uses three retainers, while the passenger-side switch uses a retaining tab. Reassemble the applicable arrangement in reverse order. Driver and passenger roles depend on the vehicle’s steering position.

steps.title: Install the upper bolt and cover
steps.body:
Install the upper trim-panel bolt in the interior-handle recess and tighten it to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm). Refit its cover.

Check that the cover and switch bezel sit flush, the panel is seated around its edges, and every removed fastener has returned to its location.

steps.title: Check the trim and handle before closing the door
steps.body:
With the door still open, confirm that the interior handle moves and returns normally, its cable retainer is secured, and no wiring or cable is trapped at the panel edges. If the handle binds or its connection is uncertain, correct that before closing the door.

These are reassembly checks: the goal is to verify that the attachments disturbed during access have been restored.

steps.title: Check the restored door functions and audio
steps.body:
Once everything is connected and secured, switch the ignition on as needed and check the window switch through its normal operation. Check that the door closes, latches and opens normally.

Play a familiar audio source at a moderate level and confirm that the replaced speaker produces sound. Check that the trim remains seated during normal door use. If a function disturbed during the repair does not work, switch the ignition off before reopening the panel and checking the relevant connection.

watchFor.title: Inch-pounds, not foot-pounds
watchFor.body: Speaker bolts take 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm), upper and center trim bolts take 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm), and lower trim retainers take 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm). Confirm the torque tool’s units before tightening.

watchFor.title: A panel that still feels anchored
watchFor.body: Stop pulling and check the upper bolt, center bolt, both bottom retainers and the staged perimeter attachments. After those are released, the panel comes up and out; its cable and wiring still need to be disconnected.

watchFor.title: Wiring carrying the weight
watchFor.body: Support the speaker and trim panel while unplugging them. Neither the electrical harness nor the latch cable should carry a removed component’s weight.

watchFor.title: A proud edge after refitting
watchFor.body: Check the retainer alignment and look for trapped wiring or cable before tightening further. Seating pressure belongs at the aligned attachment, not across the middle of the trim.

notes: The speaker procedures use reverse-order installation. The detailed steps above also restore the prerequisite window switch, trim attachments and latch cable.

The audio overviews list active noise cancellation for the 2.3L only and electronic sound enhancement for the 2.3L and 5.2L only. Those features do not change the speaker-removal steps or justify applying their equipment descriptions to every engine.
The window switch normally stays assembled to its bezel throughout this speaker repair.

diagnostics.finding: The trim remains firmly attached after its visible fasteners are removed.
diagnostics.meaning: The perimeter clips or pin-type retainers may still be engaged, or the top edge has not yet been lifted free.
diagnostics.next: Recheck the rear-upper, rear/lower and front-edge release stages. Release the top with the specified upward-and-outward movement while supporting the panel.

diagnostics.finding: The replacement speaker has a different mounting carrier, flange or connector.
diagnostics.meaning: The replacement does not match the unit being removed.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the part and audio-system match before installation; do not modify the mounting or force the connector.

diagnostics.finding: The trim will not sit evenly during reassembly.
diagnostics.meaning: An attachment may be misaligned, or wiring or the latch cable may be caught behind the panel.
diagnostics.next: Support and ease the affected section back away, check the routing and attachment alignment, then seat it before tightening the trim fasteners.

diagnostics.finding: The interior handle binds or the window switch does not operate after reassembly.
diagnostics.meaning: A connection disturbed during access needs to be checked before assuming a separate component failure.
diagnostics.next: Keep the door open if the handle connection is uncertain. Switch the ignition off and check the latch-cable attachment or window-switch connector, as applicable.

verification.title: Speaker installation
verification.body: The selected speaker matches the removed unit’s mounting and connector, its connector is seated, and all three mounting bolts are tightened to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm).

verification.title: Trim fastening
verification.body: The perimeter clips and pin-type retainers are engaged. Both lower retainers are tightened to 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm); the center and upper bolts are tightened to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm). The upper cover and window-switch bezel sit evenly.

verification.title: Connections and normal operation
verification.body: The latch cable and applicable electrical connectors are restored, the interior handle returns normally, the door latches and opens normally, the window switch operates, and the replaced speaker produces sound during ordinary playback.

guides.title: Replace the right-hand front door midwoofer or woofer
guides.summary: Reach the selected right-hand front door speaker, replace it, and refit the door trim with its wiring, latch cable and fasteners correctly restored.
guides.introduction: A door speaker should move air; getting to it shouldn't feel like negotiating with a plastic escape room. I'll walk you through the door panel's fasteners and staged clip releases, then the much shorter business of changing the speaker. This covers 2015 Mustangs with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine and SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3.
guides.why: The speaker turns an electrical audio signal into sound by moving its cone. The midwoofer handles lower and middle frequencies; the woofer concentrates on lower notes. Both sit behind the door trim. Most of this job is reaching the selected speaker without damaging the panel, then restoring the window-switch connection and inside-handle cable so the door works properly afterward.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang right front door speaker replacement

when.summary: Use this procedure after the right-hand front door midwoofer or woofer has been identified as needing replacement.
notes: Replace the selected speaker; removing both is unnecessary unless both require work.
Right-hand means the vehicle's right side. It is the passenger side on a left-hand-drive car and the driver side on a right-hand-drive car.

prepare.title: Identify the audio system and replacement speaker
prepare.detail: Match the replacement to the fitted audio system and the speaker being replaced. The SYNC overview describes six speakers and a 4.2-inch non-touchscreen display. The touchscreen overview describes an 8-inch display with nine speakers without Shaker or ten with Shaker. Those descriptions help identify equipment; they do not make the speakers interchangeable. See the [SYNC overview](#/document/G1692884) and [touchscreen-system overview](#/document/G1702412).

prepare.title: Establish the repair boundary
prepare.detail: This is a mechanical replacement procedure. It does not provide electrical fault tests or speaker resistance limits, so identify the failed component before buying parts or opening the door.

prepare.title: Gather tools and protect yourself
prepare.detail: Have a trim-removal tool, tools that fit the actual fasteners, and a torque wrench suitable for 13–48 lb.in (1.5–5.4 Nm). Have the correctly matched replacement speaker ready. Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling sharp door edges. Keep the removed panel and switch assembly somewhere their finished surfaces will be protected.

prepare.title: Keep the car stationary and prevent starting
prepare.detail: Work with the car on the ground and the parking brake applied; lifting is unnecessary. If remote start is fitted, disable it through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before service. Turn the ignition and audio system off and remove the key from the vehicle. The relevant precautions are in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Choose the right-hand speaker branch
steps.body:
Use the [SYNC speaker procedure](#/document/G1694050) or [SYNC 2/SYNC 3 speaker procedure](#/document/G1693898) for the fitted system. Both cover separate midwoofer and woofer branches with the same mounting-bolt torque.

The midwoofer illustration shows a smaller speaker with a roughly square mounting face and three projecting mounting ears. The woofer illustration shows a larger round mounting flange with three bolts around its perimeter. Match the actual component and replacement rather than choosing by engine size.

steps.title: Remove the inside-handle cover and upper panel bolt
steps.body:
Open the right-hand door. In the interior door-handle recess, remove the small cover that conceals the upper trim-panel bolt, then remove that bolt. Keep the cover and bolt together.

This begins the [door trim removal sequence](#/document/G1692600). Its illustrations show a right-hand door on a left-hand-drive car; right-hand-drive access is similar.

steps.title: Lift out the window-switch and bezel assembly
steps.body:
Use the trim-removal tool to lift the window-switch bezel—the surrounding trim piece—out of the armrest, releasing its four retaining clips. Bring the switch and bezel out together, then release and disconnect the window-switch electrical connector beneath them. Hold the connector body rather than pulling its wires.

Set the complete assembly aside. For speaker access, leave the switch attached to its bezel; separating those parts is only necessary when replacing the switch itself. See [Front Door Window Control Switch](#/document/G1695936).

steps.title: Remove the center bolt and two lower retainers
steps.body:
With the switch assembly removed, remove the center trim-panel bolt exposed at the armrest opening. Then remove the two fastened retainers along the panel's bottom edge.

Keep these lower retainers separate from the upper and center bolts: they use a different tightening value during refitting.

steps.title: Release the upper rear edge
steps.body:
At the rear of the door—the latch end—ease the upper rear portion of the trim panel away from the door. Release the upper rear clip first, followed by the two pin-type retainers farther down that rear edge.

Pin-type retainers are push-in attachments holding the panel to the door. Work at their attachment points rather than bending a broad section of panel. The damn clips are small; the panel doesn't need to audition as a spring.

steps.title: Release the rear and bottom of the panel
steps.body:
Move the rear and lower portion of the panel away from the door. Release the pin-type retainer near the lower rear corner first, then the clip near the bottom front area beside the large speaker grille.

Keep the panel supported as these attachments release. It is still attached at the front and along the top.

steps.title: Release the two front pin-type retainers
steps.body:
At the hinge end of the door, position the panel away from the metal door structure. Release the lower front pin-type retainer, then the upper front pin-type retainer. These are the two attachments shown along the front edge above the large speaker-grille area.

Once the perimeter attachments are free, prepare to lift the panel rather than continuing to pull it straight outward.

steps.title: Lift the panel clear and disconnect its remaining attachments
steps.body:
Lift the trim panel up and out to release its top edge from the door. Support it close to the door while reaching behind the inside-handle area.

Disconnect the panel's electrical connectors where fitted. At the back of the interior handle, release the latch cable's retaining attachment and detach the cable from the handle assembly. This cable links the inside handle to the door latch. Set the panel aside only after both the wiring and cable are free; neither should carry the panel's weight.

steps.title: Remove the selected speaker
steps.body:
For the midwoofer, support the smaller speaker and remove the three bolts through its mounting ears. Move it away from the door enough to reach the connector at its lower side, release the connector lock and unplug it.

For the woofer, support the larger round speaker and remove its three perimeter bolts. Move it away enough to reach the connector near the lower edge, release the connector lock and unplug it.

Remove only the selected component. Keep its wiring accessible for reconnection.

steps.title: Connect and mount the replacement speaker
steps.body:
Compare the replacement's mounting shape, three bolt locations and connector with the removed speaker before fitting it. If those features do not match, resolve the part selection before proceeding.

Reconnect the electrical connector, position the speaker against its mounting face and install all three bolts. Tighten the bolts to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm). This value applies to both the midwoofer and woofer branches in both linked speaker procedures. Confirm that the wiring is clear of the mounting face.

steps.title: Reconnect the panel and seat its top edge
steps.body:
Transfer panel parts as necessary before refitting. Bring the panel close to the door while supporting its weight. Reattach the latch cable to the inside-handle assembly and restore its retaining attachment, then reconnect the fitted electrical connectors.

Keep the cable and wiring clear of the panel's seating surfaces and leave the window-switch connector accessible through its opening. Reverse the lift-out movement to engage the panel's top edge and lower it into position.

steps.title: Restore the perimeter retainers in reverse order
steps.body:
Align the attachments with their receiving holes before pressing them home. Restore the upper front pin-type retainer, then the lower front one. Next engage the clip beside the lower front speaker-grille area and the lower rear pin-type retainer. Finish with the two rear-edge pin-type retainers and the upper rear clip.

Check the panel's seating as you go. If an edge remains standing away from the door, check the alignment at that attachment and the routing behind it before applying more force. Trim clips don't become more cooperative when shouted at, though the temptation is understandable.

steps.title: Refit the lower retainers and center bolt
steps.body:
Install the two lower trim-panel retainers and tighten them to 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm). Reinstall the center bolt through the armrest opening and tighten it to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm).

These are inch-pound values. Keep the torque wrench's units in view.

steps.title: Refit the window switch, upper bolt and cover
steps.body:
Reconnect the window-switch electrical connector. Align the bezel's four clips with the armrest opening and press the complete assembly back into place.

Reinstall the upper bolt in the interior-handle recess and tighten it to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm), then refit its cover. This completes the reverse removal sequence.

steps.title: Check the completed repair
steps.body:
Before closing the door, confirm that the panel sits fully in place and the switch bezel and handle-recess cover are seated. Confirm that the inside handle operates the latch before relying on it with the door closed.

With hands and tools clear, switch the ignition on as needed and check the window switch. Play audio at a modest level to confirm sound from the replaced speaker. These are completion checks for the connections disturbed during the job; they do not establish the cause of any remaining audio fault.

watchFor.title: A panel that is loose but still tethered
watchFor.body: Released perimeter clips do not mean the panel is free. Its top edge must lift out, and its fitted wiring and inside-handle cable must be detached before it can be set aside.

watchFor.title: Three different fastening values
watchFor.body: Speaker bolts: 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm). Upper and center panel bolts: 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm). Lower panel retainers: 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm). Do not apply one value to every fastener.

watchFor.title: Wiring or cable caught behind the panel
watchFor.body: Before seating the panel, keep its wiring and latch cable clear of attachment points and seating surfaces. Keep the window-switch plug accessible until the switch assembly is reconnected.

watchFor.title: Unnecessary switch disassembly
watchFor.body: Removing the switch and bezel as one assembly provides speaker access. The switch-to-bezel retainers are only disturbed when installing a replacement switch.

notes: The two right-hand speaker procedures give the same mechanical removal sequence and 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm) speaker-bolt torque.
The window-switch illustrations show a left-hand door; the procedure states that the right-hand side is similar.
The panel and switch refit by reversing removal. No additional numeric tightening value is needed for their push-in clips or the passenger-side switch retaining tab.

diagnostics.finding: The exposed speaker has a smaller, roughly square mounting face with three projecting mounting ears.
diagnostics.meaning: This matches the illustrated midwoofer branch.
diagnostics.next: Use the matching midwoofer replacement and remove its three mounting bolts and electrical connector.

diagnostics.finding: The exposed speaker has a large circular flange with three perimeter bolts.
diagnostics.meaning: This matches the illustrated woofer branch.
diagnostics.next: Use the matching woofer replacement and remove its three mounting bolts and electrical connector.

diagnostics.finding: The replacement's mounting shape, bolt locations or connector differs from the removed speaker.
diagnostics.meaning: The replacement does not match the component being refitted.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the part and audio-equipment match before installation; do not force the connector or mounting.

diagnostics.finding: The window switch itself also needs replacement.
diagnostics.meaning: Switch-to-bezel separation becomes necessary, with the branch determined by driver or passenger position rather than RH alone.
diagnostics.next: With the bezel assembly removed and unplugged, remove the three retainers and lift the driver-side switch from its bezel. For the passenger-side switch, release its retaining tab and remove it from the bezel. Install the replacement by reversing that branch, then reconnect and refit the assembly. See [Front Door Window Control Switch](#/document/G1695936).

diagnostics.finding: The inside handle or window switch fails the completion check after reassembly.
diagnostics.meaning: A connection disturbed during panel removal needs rechecking.
diagnostics.next: Turn the ignition off before reopening the panel. Recheck the latch-cable attachment for a handle problem or the switch connector for a window-control problem, then repeat the relevant completion check.

diagnostics.finding: An audio complaint remains after the replacement is fitted and its connector is confirmed attached.
diagnostics.meaning: The replacement procedure alone cannot establish whether the remaining fault concerns the speaker, wiring or another audio-system component.
diagnostics.next: Obtain diagnostic instructions matched to the fitted audio system before replacing more parts.

verification.title: Speaker secured
verification.body: The selected speaker's connector is attached, its mounting face is seated, and all three bolts are tightened to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm).

verification.title: Door trim restored
verification.body: The latch cable and fitted electrical connectors are reattached. The top edge, perimeter clips, pin-type retainers, switch bezel and handle cover are seated. Both lower retainers are tightened to 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm), and the upper and center bolts to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm).

verification.title: Disturbed functions checked
verification.body: The inside handle operates the latch before the door is closed, the window switch operates, and the replaced speaker produces sound during the modest-volume completion check.

guides.title: Replace the GPS module with SYNC, SYNC 2 or SYNC 3
guides.summary: Remove and refit the dashboard GPS module, preserving its configuration through scan-tool programming when installing a replacement.
guides.introduction: The global positioning system module (GPSM) provides positioning information within the information and entertainment system. It is mounted beneath the instrument-panel speaker grille. Replacing it involves both physical access and, for a new module, transferring the vehicle's configuration. The procedures cover SYNC and SYNC 2/SYNC 3 separately; navigation remains an equipment-dependent feature.
guides.why: A replacement module needs the configuration held by the original unit. Saving that information before removal keeps the programming sequence intact. Removing the surrounding trim first also gives access to the module's mounting, allowing it to be released without using its electrical lead as a handle.

when.summary: When GPS module replacement has been established as necessary, or the module must be removed for access.
notes: A compass or navigation concern alone does not establish that the GPSM needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange programming capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of the programmable module installation (PMI) process. Keep the original module installed until its configuration has been uploaded when fitting a new unit.

prepare.title: Plan dashboard access
prepare.detail: Follow the center finish panel procedure before removing the speaker grille. Identify whether the vehicle uses SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3 so the correct module procedure is selected.

steps.title: Begin the programming sequence
steps.body: Open the applicable [SYNC procedure](#/document/G1694051) or [SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedure](#/document/G1693899). Begin GPSM PMI with the scan tool and follow its prompts. For a new module, upload the existing configuration before removing the original unit.

steps.title: Expose the module
steps.body: Remove the [instrument panel center finish panel](#/document/G1693976), then remove the instrument-panel speaker grille. This establishes the access needed to release the GPSM from its mounting.

steps.title: Release the GPSM and disconnect it
steps.body: Pull the module upward to release it, then disconnect its electrical connector. Support the module while separating the connection so its wiring does not carry the removal force.

steps.title: Refit and finish configuration
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: reconnect the module, seat it in its mounting and reinstall the grille and center finish panel. When installing a new component, complete PMI with the scan tool, following the prompts to download the saved configuration.

watchFor.title: Configuration not saved
watchFor.body: If a new module is planned, do not disconnect the original before completing the required configuration upload.

watchFor.title: Equipment assumptions
watchFor.body: SYNC 2/SYNC 3 can include navigation, but its presence must be established from the vehicle's fitted equipment.

notes: The final PMI completion step is specifically required when installing a new component.

verification.title: Confirm physical reassembly
verification.body: Check that the electrical connector is reconnected, the GPSM is seated and both removed trim pieces are installed.

verification.title: Record the programming result
verification.body: For a new module, record completion of the scan tool's PMI sequence and configuration download.

GPSM removal, installation and replacement-module PMI for vehicles with SYNC 2/SYNC 3.
Center finish panel removal and installation for module access.

guides.title: Replace the instrument-panel speaker with SYNC, SYNC 2 or SYNC 3
guides.summary: Remove the center trim and speaker grille, exchange the instrument-panel speaker and restore its connector and mountings.
guides.introduction: The instrument-panel speaker converts an electrical audio signal into sound through its grille. Replacement involves a small amount of dashboard trim removal followed by disconnecting the speaker itself. The SYNC and SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedures use the same removal sequence, although the surrounding audio systems differ. Choose the procedure matching the fitted system.
guides.why: The center finish panel must come off before the speaker grille. Releasing the trim clips with the specified trim tool gives access without treating the panel as a rigid, bolted part. An optional electrical connection behind the finish panel must also be disconnected before that panel is moved away.

when.summary: When the instrument-panel speaker needs replacement or removal for access.
notes: Establish the reason for replacement through the appropriate audio diagnosis; this procedure is a removal and installation path.

prepare.title: Trim and fastener tools
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover, suitable speaker-bolt tools and torque equipment capable of accurately applying the small specified tightening value.

prepare.title: Identify the fitted connections
prepare.detail: The center finish panel may have an optional ICM electrical connector. Follow the actual panel configuration and disconnect that connector if fitted.

steps.title: Open the center-panel access
steps.body: Follow the [center finish panel procedure](#/document/G1693976). Use the interior trim remover to release the right-hand instrument-panel trim clips and remove that panel. Release the center finish panel clips, then disconnect its optional electrical connector before removing the panel.

steps.title: Remove the grille and release the speaker
steps.body: Remove the instrument-panel speaker grille. Remove the speaker bolts and lift the speaker sufficiently to reach its electrical connector. Follow the [SYNC procedure](#/document/G1704852) or [SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedure](#/document/G1704856), according to the fitted equipment.

steps.title: Disconnect and exchange the speaker
steps.body: Disconnect the speaker’s electrical connector and remove the speaker. During refitting, reverse this sequence: reconnect the electrical connection, position the speaker and install its bolts. Tighten the speaker bolts to 2.5 Nm.

steps.title: Restore the dashboard trim
steps.body: Refit the speaker grille. Reconnect the optional center-panel connector if it was disconnected, then reinstall the center finish panel and right-hand trim in reverse removal order. Make sure the released clips engage so the panels are retained.

watchFor.title: A tethered finish panel
watchFor.body: If the optional connector is present, disconnect it before carrying the center panel away from the dashboard.

watchFor.title: Small speaker fasteners
watchFor.body: Use the specified low tightening value rather than judging tightness by feel.

notes: Removal instructions also contain the speaker’s installation torque.

verification.title: Speaker installation
verification.body: Confirm the speaker connector is attached and the mounting bolts are tightened to specification.

verification.title: Trim restoration
verification.body: Confirm the grille, center finish panel and right-hand trim are refitted, including any optional panel connection.

procedures.purpose: Instrument-panel speaker removal and installation for vehicles with SYNC.
Instrument-panel speaker removal and installation for vehicles with SYNC 2/SYNC 3.
Right-hand trim and center finish panel removal and refitting to access the speaker grille.

guides.title: Replace the SYNC microphone through the overhead console
guides.summary: Replace the complete overhead console to renew the integrated SYNC microphone, with initialization when the new console includes an intrusion sensor.
guides.introduction: The SYNC microphone provides voice input to the information and entertainment system. It is built into the overhead console and cannot be replaced separately. The repair therefore exchanges the console assembly, including disconnecting and reconnecting its electrical connections. The same replacement rule applies to the separate SYNC and SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedures; body style and intrusion-sensor equipment determine the additional work.
guides.why: Understanding the assembly boundary prevents unnecessary attempts to extract a microphone that is not separately serviceable. Coupe access requires lowering the headliner before releasing the console. A replacement console equipped with an intrusion sensor also needs electronic initialization and a body-control-module fault check, so securing the trim is not always the final operation.

when.summary: When microphone replacement has been determined necessary on a vehicle equipped with SYNC.
notes: Identify coupe or convertible body style and whether the new console includes an intrusion sensor before starting.

prepare.title: Provide trim-removal capability
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover and the overhead-console procedure available. Coupe work also requires the Headliner - Lowering procedure referenced there.

prepare.title: Plan for the complete assembly
prepare.detail: Obtain the appropriate overhead console for the vehicle's fitted equipment. The microphone is not a separate replacement item.

prepare.title: Arrange conditional scan-tool access
prepare.detail: A new console equipped with an intrusion sensor requires a diagnostic scan tool capable of Local Interconnect Network (LIN) New Module Initialization and Body Control Module (BCM) self-testing.

steps.title: Select the applicable microphone procedure
steps.body: Use the SYNC procedure or the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 procedure as appropriate. Both lead to replacement of the overhead console; neither provides a separate microphone-removal operation.

steps.title: Prepare access for the body style
steps.body: On a coupe, lower the headliner using the procedure referenced by the overhead-console article. The convertible branch proceeds directly to releasing the console clips.

steps.title: Release and disconnect the console
steps.body: Use the interior trim remover to release the clips. Disconnect the electrical connectors and remove the console. Keep removal controlled so the assembly is free of its connectors before it is taken away.

steps.title: Install the replacement assembly
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure, reconnecting the electrical connectors and securing the console clips. On a coupe, complete the corresponding headliner restoration.

steps.title: Initialize an equipped replacement console
steps.body: If the new component has an intrusion sensor, run Toolbox > Electrical > Service Functions > LIN New Module Initialization. Then carry out the BCM self-test, clear its diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), and retrieve them again to confirm they have cleared. These additional operations apply only to a new component equipped with the sensor.

watchFor.title: Overlooking coupe access
watchFor.body: The coupe sequence starts with lowering the headliner. Do not substitute the convertible's direct-access sequence.

watchFor.title: Treating all consoles alike
watchFor.body: The intrusion-sensor condition determines whether electronic initialization and the BCM code check are required.

notes: A microphone complaint needs diagnosis before assembly replacement; these procedures specify the replacement method.

diagnostics.finding: BCM codes remain or return after the required clear-and-retrieve sequence.
diagnostics.meaning: The required confirmation that all BCM codes have cleared has not been achieved; this alone does not identify a microphone fault.
diagnostics.next: Record the returned codes for further diagnosis.

verification.title: Confirm physical installation
verification.body: Confirm the console connectors and clips are restored and any lowered headliner has been reinstalled.

verification.title: Record the conditional electronic result
verification.body: For a new console with an intrusion sensor, record completion of LIN initialization and the BCM code retrieval confirming that all DTCs have cleared.

procedures.purpose: Establish the integrated-microphone replacement requirement for vehicles with SYNC.
Establish the integrated-microphone replacement requirement for vehicles with SYNC 2/SYNC 3.
Remove and install the overhead console by body style and perform intrusion-sensor initialization and BCM verification when required.

guides.title: Replace a coupe parcel-shelf speaker
guides.summary: Reach the rear speaker by removing the seat cushion, side trim and parcel shelf, then replace it and tighten its three mounting bolts to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm). Applies to 2015 Mustang coupes with 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engines and SYNC or SYNC 2/SYNC 3.
guides.introduction:
The speaker gets three bolts. Naturally, the Mustang surrounds them with enough trim to make those bolts feel important. I’ll walk you through that trim, including the rear-seat releases and the easily overlooked tether clips, so you can reach the speaker without turning the cabin into a plastic clip treasure hunt.

The parcel-shelf speaker sits beneath the shelf behind the rear backrests. It turns the audio system’s electrical signal into sound. Both covered speaker procedures use the same access sequence and mounting torque; the fitted audio system still matters when choosing the replacement.
guides.why: Most of this job is gaining access. The door-sill trim, rear cushion, rear side panels and D-pillar panels overlap the route to the parcel shelf. Releasing their attachments in order lets the panels come away without forcing them. Reassembly also needs care around the seat belts: a working speaker is no consolation for a buckle buried under the seat.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang coupe parcel shelf speaker replacement

when.summary: Use this guide when a parcel-shelf speaker has been selected for replacement or needs to be removed for access.
notes: This is a removal and installation job, with the same mechanical sequence across the four listed engines.
Both rear side trim panels and both D-pillar trim panels must come off to remove the parcel shelf, even when replacing only one speaker.

prepare.title: Match the replacement to the fitted audio system
prepare.detail: Confirm the car’s audio equipment before choosing a speaker. The SYNC overview describes six speakers and a 4.2-inch non-touchscreen display. The touchscreen overview describes an 8-inch display, nine speakers without Shaker or ten with Shaker, plus an audio digital signal processing module; Shaker also has a subwoofer amplifier. These differences do not change the access steps here. This guide does not establish whether an audio fault originates in the speaker, wiring or electronics, and provides no resistance test or speaker interchange specification. See the [SYNC overview](#/document/G1692884) and [touchscreen-system overview](#/document/G1702412).

prepare.title: Prepare for small fasteners and several kinds of clips
prepare.detail: Have tools suitable for releasing the trim attachments and removing the speaker bolts, plus a torque tool that accurately applies 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm). Keep each panel’s attachments together and provide a clean place for the removed cushion and trim. The speaker is the replacement component; keep track of the existing bolts, panel clips, tether clips and shelf retainers for refitting.

prepare.title: Keep the work at ground level and prevent unintended starting
prepare.detail: This access route stays inside the cabin and needs no lifting. Set the parking brake. Move both front seats fully forward while their adjustment is available. If remote start is fitted, disable it through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before starting service. Then switch the ignition and audio system off and remove the key from the vehicle. Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling sharp edges. Relevant precautions are in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Set up the cabin for access
steps.body:
With the car parked and the parking brake applied, move both front seats to their full forward positions. Disable remote start if fitted, then turn the ignition and audio system off and remove the key from the vehicle.

Work through the following trim operations on both sides. The illustrated access is left-hand drive, with the right side shown for several panels; the corresponding operations are similar on right-hand-drive cars and on the opposite side.

steps.title: Move the door-opening weatherstrips aside
steps.body: At each door opening, position the weatherstrip aside where it overlaps the sill and rear side trim. Leave it clear of the scuff plate—the long trim strip along the door sill—so that strip can be removed. You are moving the seal out of the way, rather than removing unrelated door trim. See [Loadspace Trim Panel - Coupe](#/document/G1692601).

steps.title: Release and remove both scuff plates
steps.body:
Release the scuff plate’s clips and lift the plate away from the sill. The illustration identifies five clip positions along the long edge of the panel and two additional attachments along the lower sill area. Account for both sets rather than pulling harder when one area remains held.

Repeat on the other side and keep the attachments with their respective plates.

steps.title: Press the rear-cushion locking tabs before lifting
steps.body:
Find the two locking-tab locations at the front edge of the rear seat cushion, one on each side. Press each locking tab inward to release the cushion from the floor. The close-up shows the release beneath the cushion’s front edge.

Only after the tabs are released, lift and release the cushion, then remove it from the cabin. Do not try to overcome a locked tab by hauling upward: that can damage it. This is the critical handling detail in [Rear Seat Cushion](#/document/G1692168).

steps.title: Fold both rear backrests down
steps.body: Release each rear backrest latch and position the backrest down. The illustration places the release near the upper outboard corner of the backrest. Fold both sections to open access to the side trim and the front edge of the parcel shelf.

steps.title: Move the belt guides aside and remove the rear side panels
steps.body:
On each side, position the safety-belt guide aside, then release the clips securing the loadspace trim panel—the large interior side panel beside the rear seat—and remove the panel.

The panel illustration shows five spring-clip positions around the upper and side edges, two push-type attachments toward the rear edge, and a separate attachment at the lower forward end. Work through those attachment locations instead of treating the panel as one big pull handle.

Keep the belt webbing clear as the panel comes away. This operation does not call for removing the belt anchorages.

steps.title: Remove both D-pillar panels, including their tethers
steps.body:
The D-pillar trim panels are the upper panels beside the rear window. Release the two ordinary clips shown on each panel, then move the panel away only far enough to reach its tether attachment.

Disconnect the tether clip before taking the panel out. A tether is a separate retaining connection, so a panel can remain attached after its ordinary clips have released. Repeat on the other side. See [Parcel Shelf - Coupe](#/document/G1692602).

steps.title: Remove the parcel shelf
steps.body:
Remove the two pin-type retainers at the left and right ends of the shelf’s front edge, behind the folded backrests. Lift the parcel shelf free and remove it to expose the speaker mounting area.

Keep the retainers with the shelf. At this point, the trim obstacle course has finally delivered its prize: access to the speaker.

steps.title: Remove the speaker’s three mounting bolts
steps.body:
Identify the speaker you are removing. Its illustration shows three bolts spaced around the circular mounting rim: one toward the upper left, one at the right and one near the bottom.

Remove all three bolts while supporting the speaker. Lift the speaker only far enough to reach its electrical connection; do not let its weight hang from the wiring. Both [the SYNC speaker procedure](#/document/G1694054) and [the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 speaker procedure](#/document/G1693902) use this arrangement.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the speaker
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical plug at the side of the speaker, near the left-hand mounting area in the illustration. Hold the plug housing when separating it, rather than pulling on the wires. Once disconnected, remove the speaker and retain its three bolts.

steps.title: Connect and fasten the replacement speaker
steps.body:
Reconnect the electrical plug to the replacement speaker and make sure the connection is engaged. Position the speaker in its mounting opening with the wiring clear of the mounting rim.

Install the three mounting bolts and tighten them to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm). Use the small-torque tool prepared for the job. The unit is pound-inches, not pound-feet.

steps.title: Refit the parcel shelf and its two retainers
steps.body: Place the parcel shelf back in its original position, making sure it sits correctly over the speaker area. Reinstall the two pin-type retainers at the ends of the front edge. Confirm the shelf is seated before covering its edges with the pillar trim.

steps.title: Reconnect the D-pillar tethers and seat the panels
steps.body: On each side, reconnect the tether clip first, then align the D-pillar panel and engage its two ordinary clips. Check that the tether is connected and the panel is seated before moving on. Merely pressing the panel into place does not restore a forgotten tether.

steps.title: Refit both rear side panels and restore the belt guides
steps.body:
Position each loadspace trim panel, align its attachments and engage the five spring clips, two push-type attachments and lower forward attachment. Restore the safety-belt guide to its original position.

Keep the safety-belt webbing untwisted and clear of the panel attachments. Check that the belts remain accessible rather than disappearing behind the newly fitted trim.

steps.title: Raise and latch the rear backrests
steps.body: Return both backrests to their upright positions and make sure their latches engage. Check that the belt webbing is clear as each backrest closes. Confirm each backrest stays latched rather than simply resting upright.

steps.title: Reinstall the rear seat cushion
steps.body:
Position the cushion back in place, keeping the belts and buckles accessible above it. Reverse the removal movement to seat the cushion and engage both front locking locations.

Check that both sides are retained and that no belt webbing is twisted or trapped beneath the cushion. The buckles must remain available to the occupants.

steps.title: Restore the scuff plates and weatherstrips
steps.body:
Align each scuff plate with its attachment locations and engage its clips, including the five along the long edge and the two additional lower attachments. Return the door-opening weatherstrip to its original position over the adjoining trim edges.

Check the fit of both sides. A raised corner deserves a look at the attachment beneath it, not a harder thump.

steps.title: Check the finished installation
steps.body:
Confirm that the shelf and surrounding panels are seated, both backrests are latched, the cushion is retained and all belts and buckles are accessible with untwisted webbing.

Turn the audio system on and use ordinary playback to confirm that the refitted speaker produces sound. This is a completion check, not a test that identifies the cause of any remaining audio fault. Return the front seats to suitable positions and restore the remote-start setting if you disabled it for the work.

watchFor.title: Rear-cushion tabs must be released
watchFor.body: Press the front locking tabs inward before lifting the cushion. Pulling upward against locked tabs can damage them.

watchFor.title: A loose pillar panel may still be tethered
watchFor.body: Release the ordinary D-pillar clips, then disconnect the separate tether clip. Reconnect the tether during installation before seating the panel.

watchFor.title: Keep the speaker’s torque units straight
watchFor.body: The three mounting bolts take 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm). Do not substitute pound-feet or estimate this small torque with a large wrench.

watchFor.title: Belts need a clear route through reassembly
watchFor.body: Watch the webbing as the side panels, backrests and cushion go back. Leave every belt untwisted and every buckle accessible to its occupant.

notes: The same speaker removal and installation actions apply to the covered SYNC and SYNC 2/SYNC 3 configurations; choose the replacement for the actual fitted audio system.

The trim and rear-cushion procedures use reverse-order installation. Their clips, guides and retainers are restored by engagement; the numeric tightening requirement here belongs to the speaker mounting bolts.
Neither a battery disconnection nor removal of a safety-belt anchorage is part of this access sequence.

diagnostics.finding: The rear cushion remains held at its front edge.
diagnostics.meaning: A front locking tab may still be engaged with the floor.
diagnostics.next: Stop lifting and press the locking tab inward at the held location before trying to release the cushion again.

diagnostics.finding: A D-pillar panel moves away but remains attached.
diagnostics.meaning: The separate tether clip may still be connected after the ordinary clips have released.
diagnostics.next: Support the panel, reach the tether attachment and disconnect it before removing the panel.

diagnostics.finding: A refitted panel sits proud or a belt disappears behind the trim.
diagnostics.meaning: The panel or belt routing has not been fully restored.
diagnostics.next: Reopen the affected area, clear the belt from the attachment locations and realign the panel before engaging its clips. Recheck the belt for twists and accessibility.

diagnostics.finding: The speaker remains silent during the final playback check.
diagnostics.meaning: Playback alone cannot distinguish an installation connection issue from an audio-system fault.
diagnostics.next: Switch the audio system and ignition off before reopening the area to check the speaker connection. If the connection is restored correctly and the fault remains, obtain diagnosis for the fitted audio system before selecting more replacement parts.

verification.title: Speaker connection and mounting completed
verification.body: Before covering the speaker, confirm its plug is engaged, its wiring is clear of the mounting rim and all three bolts have been tightened to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm).

verification.title: Every trim connection restored
verification.body: Confirm both parcel-shelf pin retainers, both D-pillar tethers and their panel clips, both rear side panels, both belt guides, both scuff plates and the weatherstrips are back in position.

verification.title: Rear seating ready for occupants
verification.body: Check that both backrests latch, both front cushion locking locations retain the cushion, and the belts and buckles are accessible with untwisted webbing.

verification.title: Ordinary audio operation checked
verification.body: Confirm sound from the installed speaker using normal playback. Treat a remaining fault as a reason for further diagnosis, rather than proof that another speaker is needed.
