guides.title: Custom-program the SYNC 2 or SYNC 3 APIM
guides.summary: Install a specified SYNC software level or application, complete the online configuration report and calibrate the touchscreen.
guides.introduction: The Accessory Protocol Interface Module (APIM) runs SYNC software and applications within the information and entertainment system. Custom programming displays available software choices for a supported upgrade or a directed repair. It is appropriate when the required selection is known; if it is unknown, the procedure directs you to standard programming, which selects the latest levels automatically.
guides.why: Programming depends on stable power, working communications and completion of every stage. It clears stored diagnostic information, so codes must be saved first. Returning the flash drive to the diagnostic tool at the end completes configuration and reports the installation; omitting this can remove features such as navigation, if equipped, and SYNC Services.

when.summary: When a supported upgrade or service instruction requires a known APIM software level or application.
notes: A technical service bulletin (TSB) or field service action (FSA) may specify the required selection.
Allow for programming stages that can each take 20 minutes or longer.

prepare.title: Prepare the programming environment
prepare.detail: Use the required diagnostic scan tool with current Integrated Diagnostic System (IDS) software and patches. A hardwired Internet connection is strongly recommended. Provide enough disk space for files that may exceed 2 GB and, if required, a USB flash drive of at least 1 GB.

prepare.title: Prepare power and connection equipment
prepare.detail: Have a battery charger and an external power supply for the diagnostic tool. For Full Flash programming, have the SYNC USB 2.0 A-male-to-A-male cable and A-female-to-Mini-B-female 5-pin adapter.

prepare.title: Review service precautions
prepare.detail: Follow Health and Safety Precautions and its relevant battery-charging guidance. Disable remote start before work around the vehicle, and plan for the engine-running stage required by the programming prompts.

steps.title: Establish the powered session
steps.body: Connect the charger on its low setting, with the negative lead on a clean chassis ground, not the negative battery post. Externally power the scan tool. Connect it through the vehicle communication module (VCM) to the diagnostic link connector (DLC), close IDS and place the ignition in ON/RUN.

steps.title: Open the service programming workflow
steps.body: Using Internet Explorer on the diagnostic tool, open the technician service-publication website and run OASIS using “Read VIN & DTCs.” Address the connection-icon and browser conditions described below before continuing.

steps.title: Save codes and read the module
steps.body: Use the website's Toolbox to retrieve and record all continuous memory diagnostic trouble codes before programming clears them. From OASIS, select SYNC, review “Last Recorded State — Software,” then choose “Custom” and “Read SYNC” to compare installed assembly and software levels with the online record.

steps.title: Choose the specified software
steps.body: Select the directed software level and requested or directed application. If the level is unknown, stop custom programming and use Standard Programming. A green check means an application is already current. Let the tool select Service Pack or Full Flash; do not force a Full Flash/Force CIP unless directed by a TSB or FSA.

steps.title: Make the direct connection only for Full Flash
steps.body: For Full Flash/Force CIP, remove the media hub and disconnect the vehicle USB cable. If inaccessible there, access the inline connector using the cable procedure. Connect the specified adapter to the vehicle cable, then connect the A-male-to-A-male cable between the adapter and diagnostic tool. Otherwise, skip this connection stage.

steps.title: Begin programming and follow the engine-start prompt
steps.body: Select “Program SYNC.” If a “WMA SBOOT” Hardware Wizard appears, install the requested driver and select Retry. When prompted, disconnect the charger, start the engine and select OK. Do not interrupt the ensuing stage, which may take 20 minutes or longer.

steps.title: Prepare the flash drive
steps.body: Connect the flash drive to the diagnostic tool and follow its instructions to download Service Pack and Application files. If no USB port is free, the direct vehicle USB cable may be unplugged at this stage to make room. Keep the VCM connected.

steps.title: Restore the vehicle USB path and load applications
steps.body: Reinstall the media hub or reconnect the inline connector as applicable. When prompted, move the flash drive to the media hub. The update should begin automatically and may take 20 minutes or longer. APIM resets during this stage are normal.

steps.title: Complete configuration and online reporting
steps.body: After both diagnostic-tool and flash-drive programming finish, return the flash drive to the diagnostic tool and select OK. This initiates the remaining automated configuration and reports the installation to the Ford online database.

steps.title: Calibrate the touchscreen
steps.body: Complete the linked Touchscreen Calibration procedure after programming. Treat calibration as part of finishing the job.

watchFor.title: Interrupting communications
watchFor.body: Do not disconnect the VCM or USB cable during programming unless the tool directs it. The explicit flash-drive port-sharing stage does not permit disconnecting the VCM.

watchFor.title: Normal display changes
watchFor.body: The touchscreen may momentarily go blank during programming. This alone does not establish a module fault.

watchFor.title: Using the wrong USB path
watchFor.body: Only applications on a flash drive may be loaded through the media hub; follow the specified direct-cable arrangement when Full Flash requires it.

notes: The download stage can also take 20 minutes or longer.

diagnostics.finding: “Disk Space Error” appears.
diagnostics.meaning: The diagnostic tool lacks sufficient free storage for the download.
diagnostics.next: Create additional free disk space.

diagnostics.finding: “Read VIN & DTCs” is green with a red VCM icon.
diagnostics.meaning: The workflow directs you to the connection guidance.
diagnostics.next: Follow “SYNC - Software Programming” under Service Tips.

diagnostics.finding: “Read VIN & DTCs” is red with a grey VCM icon.
diagnostics.meaning: Browser setup requires attention before programming.
diagnostics.next: Enable pop-ups, follow the Internet Explorer prompts, then follow “SYNC - Software Programming” under Service Tips.

verification.title: Confirm all completion stages
verification.body: Confirm diagnostic-tool programming, flash-drive programming, final automated configuration, online reporting and touchscreen calibration are complete.

verification.title: Retain the diagnostic record
verification.body: Keep the pre-programming code record for any further diagnosis; programming clears the continuous memory codes.

guides.title: Program and provision a replacement SYNC 2/SYNC 3 APIM
guides.summary: Configure a newly installed APIM through the prescribed programming, USB application-loading, online reporting and touchscreen-calibration stages.
guides.introduction: The accessory protocol interface module (APIM) supports SYNC functions within the information and entertainment system. A new module needs software and vehicle-specific provisioning after physical installation. This process compares software records, selects the required programming method, loads applications and completes configuration through the Ford online database.
guides.why: Stable power and uninterrupted communication matter during programming. Returning the USB flash drive to the diagnostic tool is also essential: that action starts remaining configuration steps. Omitting it can leave features such as navigation or SYNC services unavailable even after applications appear to have loaded.

when.summary: After a new APIM is installed and requires replacement programming and provisioning.
notes: Use the Module Replacement workflow for this job.
Allow uninterrupted time: several individual stages may take 20 minutes or longer.

prepare.title: Review service precautions
prepare.detail: Read the linked health and safety precautions before starting. Disable remote start for service around the vehicle and follow the applicable battery-charging precautions.

prepare.title: Prepare the diagnostic workstation
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool with current Integrated Diagnostic System (IDS) software and patches, external power and adequate free disk space. A hardwired Internet connection is strongly recommended; programming downloads can exceed 2GB.

prepare.title: Prepare USB equipment
prepare.detail: Have a USB flash drive of at least 1GB if required. Full Flash programming uses the specified SYNC USB 2.0 A Male to A Male Cable and A Female to Mini B Female 5-Pin Adapter.

steps.title: Install the replacement and establish power
steps.body: Install the new module using the [APIM removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1704012). Connect a battery charger on its low setting, with the negative lead on a clean chassis ground rather than the negative battery post. Connect the diagnostic tool to external power.

steps.title: Connect communication and set ignition
steps.body: Connect the diagnostic tool to the vehicle communication module (VCM), then the VCM to the data link connector. Close IDS and place the ignition in ON/RUN. Follow the referenced push-button ignition information where applicable.

steps.title: Establish online access and preserve fault information
steps.body: Open Internet Explorer on the diagnostic tool, access the technician service publication site and run the Online Automotive Service Information System (OASIS) using Read VIN & DTCs. A green button with a red VCM icon directs you to SYNC - Software Programming under Service Tips. For a red button with a grey icon, enable and follow browser pop-ups first, then use that same document. Retrieve and record all continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes through Toolbox before programming clears them.

steps.title: Select the replacement programming package
steps.body: From OASIS, select SYNC to display Last Recorded State — Software. Select Module Replacement, then Read SYNC. The tool compares module and software levels with Ford's stored record and selects the latest software. Select applications where required; a green check indicates an application already has the latest level. Let the tool choose Service Pack or Full Flash. Override with Full Flash/Force CIP only when directed by a technical service bulletin or field service action.

steps.title: Make the direct USB connection for Full Flash
steps.body: For Full Flash/Force CIP, remove the media hub and disconnect the vehicle USB cable. If inaccessible there, access its inline connector using the cable procedure. Attach the specified adapter to the vehicle cable and connect it to the diagnostic tool with the specified male-to-male cable. Other programming paths skip this direct-connection branch.

steps.title: Run the applicable programming phase
steps.body: Follow the [replacement programming procedure](#/document/G1672954) and its prompts. In the Full Flash sequence, select Program SYNC. If a Hardware Wizard requests WMA SBOOT, install the driver and select Retry. Do not disconnect the VCM or USB cable unless instructed. When prompted, disconnect the charger, start the engine and select OK; do not interrupt the running stage.

steps.title: Prepare the flash drive and restore vehicle USB connections
steps.body: Connect the flash drive to the diagnostic tool and follow the prompts to download Service Pack and Application files. If a USB port is needed, the direct vehicle USB cable may be unplugged at this specified stage; keep the VCM connected. Reinstall the media hub and reconnect the inline connector if disturbed.

steps.title: Load applications through the media hub
steps.body: When prompted, move the flash drive from the diagnostic tool to the media hub. Only Applications on a flash drive are loaded into the APIM through the hub. The update should begin automatically, and module resets during this stage are normal. Allow the process to finish.

steps.title: Report completion and calibrate the touchscreen
steps.body: After both programming stages finish, return the flash drive to the diagnostic tool and select OK. This reports installation to the Ford online database and initiates remaining automated configuration. Then perform [touchscreen calibration](#/document/G1702410).

watchFor.title: Expected display behavior
watchFor.body: The touchscreen may briefly go blank during programming. Follow the tool prompts rather than disconnecting equipment in response.

watchFor.title: Missing final configuration
watchFor.body: Leaving the flash drive in the vehicle instead of returning it to the diagnostic tool can cause loss of feature functionality.

notes: Browser configuration is part of the procedure; bypassing its Service Tips instructions can cause programming errors.

diagnostics.finding: Disk Space Error appears.
diagnostics.meaning: The diagnostic workstation lacks space for the programming download.
diagnostics.next: Create additional free hard-drive space before continuing.

verification.title: Confirm configuration and calibration
verification.body: Confirm completion of programming, the final flash-drive return and automated configuration, and touchscreen calibration.

verification.title: Preserve the job record
verification.body: Retain the pre-programming fault-code record and confirm the software-installation report was completed through the final OK step.

Review required general and applicable system service precautions.
Install the replacement APIM before programming.

Access and restore the USB inline connection when access through the media hub is insufficient.

guides.title: Update SYNC software with APIM Standard Programming
guides.summary: Update the SYNC module and applications, complete the final configuration and installation report, and calibrate the touchscreen.
guides.introduction: The Accessory Protocol Interface Module (APIM) supports SYNC functions and applications within the information and entertainment system. Standard Programming compares its software with Ford's recorded state and selects the update path. The work includes software transfer, vehicle configuration and final reporting, all of which are needed to retain the intended features.
guides.why: Stable power and uninterrupted communication protect the programming process. Existing continuous-memory fault codes must be saved because programming clears them. Returning the flash drive to the diagnostic tool at the end triggers remaining configuration and reporting; skipping this can cause loss of navigation, where fitted, and SYNC Services.

when.summary: When the APIM and installed applications require a software update through Standard Programming.
notes: Several programming stages can take 20 minutes or longer; allow time for the complete sequence.

prepare.title: Prepare the programming workstation
prepare.detail: Use the required diagnostic tool with current Integrated Diagnostic System (IDS) software and patches. Prefer wired Internet. Provide sufficient hard-drive space for files that can exceed 2 GB and, if required, a USB flash drive of at least 1 GB.

prepare.title: Prepare power, access and cables
prepare.detail: Read the health and battery-charging precautions and disable remote start. Have a low-setting battery charger, external power for the diagnostic tool, and the specified SYNC USB A-male-to-A-male cable and A-female-to-Mini-B-female adapter for Full Flash.

steps.title: Establish power and vehicle communication
steps.body: Connect the charger on its low setting, with its negative lead on clean chassis ground, not the negative battery post. Power the diagnostic tool externally. Connect it to the vehicle communication module (VCM), then connect the VCM to the diagnostic link connector (DLC). Close IDS and place the ignition in ON/RUN.

steps.title: Open the service session and save fault codes
steps.body: In Internet Explorer, open the technician service-publication website and run OASIS using “Read VIN & DTCs.” Resolve communication indicators as described below. Use “Toolbox” to retrieve and record all continuous memory diagnostic trouble codes (CMDTCs) before programming clears them.

steps.title: Let Standard Programming select the update
steps.body: From OASIS, select “SYNC,” then “Standard” and “Read SYNC.” The tool compares the APIM assembly, processor and application software levels with the recorded state. Select required applications; a green check means an application is already current. Accept the selected Service Pack or Full Flash method. Override to “Full Flash/Force CIP” only when directed by a technical service bulletin, field service action or specific pinpoint test.

steps.title: Connect directly for Full Flash only
steps.body: For Full Flash, access and disconnect the vehicle USB cable through the [media hub](#/document/G1704009), or use the [USB inline-connector access procedure](#/document/G1693905). Connect the specified adapter to the vehicle cable and the A-male-to-A-male cable between that adapter and the diagnostic tool. The Service Pack path proceeds to flash-drive preparation.

steps.title: Run the Full Flash programming stage
steps.body: Select “Program SYNC.” If prompted for the “WMA SBOOT” driver, install it and select “Retry.” When directed, disconnect the battery charger, start the engine and select “OK.” Do not interrupt that stage or disconnect the VCM or USB cable unless an on-screen instruction permits it.

steps.title: Prepare the flash drive and restore vehicle USB connections
steps.body: Follow the prompts to download Service Pack and application files onto the flash drive. At this stage only, the direct vehicle USB cable may be unplugged from the tool if needed to free a port; keep the VCM connected. Reinstall the media hub and reconnect any disconnected inline connector.

steps.title: Install applications and finish configuration
steps.body: When prompted, move the flash drive to the media hub. Installation should start automatically, and APIM resets are normal. Once both programming portions finish, return the flash drive to the diagnostic tool and select “OK” to complete automated configuration and report the installation to Ford's database.

steps.title: Calibrate the touchscreen
steps.body: Complete [Touchscreen Calibration](#/document/G1702410) after programming. Treat this as the final required operation, separate from downloading or installing software.

watchFor.title: Temporary display changes
watchFor.body: The touchscreen may briefly go blank during programming, and the APIM may reset during application installation.

watchFor.title: Incorrect USB use
watchFor.body: Only the permitted flash-drive application-loading route uses the media hub; follow the direct-cable instructions for Full Flash.

diagnostics.finding: “Read VIN & DTCs” is green with a red VCM icon.
diagnostics.meaning: The programming setup needs the prescribed browser/communication guidance.
diagnostics.next: Follow “SYNC - Software Programming” under “Service Tips.”

diagnostics.finding: “Read VIN & DTCs” is red with a grey VCM icon.
diagnostics.meaning: Browser pop-ups and configuration require attention.
diagnostics.next: Enable pop-ups, follow the Internet Explorer prompts, then follow “SYNC - Software Programming” under “Service Tips.”

diagnostics.finding: A “Disk Space Error” appears.
diagnostics.meaning: The diagnostic workstation lacks download space.
diagnostics.next: Create additional free hard-drive space before continuing.

verification.title: Confirm the complete programming sequence
verification.body: Confirm diagnostic-tool and flash-drive programming, final configuration/reporting and touchscreen calibration are all complete.

verification.title: Preserve the recorded results
verification.body: Retain the pre-programming CMDTC record and record successful completion of the final installation-reporting stage.

guides.title: Calibrate the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 touchscreen
guides.summary: Measure and accept new touchscreen calibration settings, then clear stored continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes.
guides.introduction: The front display interface module (FDIM) is the touchscreen through which you select information and entertainment functions. Calibration establishes the relationship between the displayed targets and the positions you touch. This operation updates those settings without removing the display.
guides.why: A fully charged battery is an explicit prerequisite because inadequate charge can leave the touchscreen inoperative. Completing the target sequence only measures the new settings: you must also accept them before finishing the procedure.

when.summary: When touchscreen calibration is required.
notes: Calibration can be performed through diagnostic scan-tool prompts or the specified audio-button sequence.

prepare.title: Confirm battery condition and safety prerequisites
prepare.detail: Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) before starting. Make sure the vehicle battery is fully charged before activating calibration.

prepare.title: Arrange access to the controls and scan tool
prepare.detail: The manual route uses the audio power, EJECT and SEEK buttons. A suitable diagnostic scan tool is needed to clear stored codes afterward. No stylus is required.

steps.title: Choose the calibration route
steps.body: Follow the diagnostic scan-tool calibration prompts, or use the following button sequence in [Touchscreen Calibration](#/document/G1702410). For the button route, press the front controls interface module (FCIM) audio power button and operate the audio system in AM/FM mode.

steps.title: Enter the calibration function
steps.body: Press and hold EJECT. Within 1 second, also press and hold SEEK UP until the speaker walk-around test begins. Then press and hold SEEK DOWN to enter touchscreen calibration. The speaker test is an intermediate stage in this entry sequence.

steps.title: Complete the touch targets
steps.body: Touch and hold each target as it appears on the display. Follow the displayed points through the sequence so the system can measure the new calibration.

steps.title: Accept the settings and clear stored codes
steps.body: When the display reports that new calibration settings have been measured and asks for Enter to accept them, touch anywhere on the touchscreen. Then clear all continuous memory diagnostic trouble codes (CMDTCs).

watchFor.title: Insufficient battery charge
watchFor.body: Do not begin calibration with an inadequately charged battery; touchscreen operation can be lost.

watchFor.title: Stopping at the measurement message
watchFor.body: The message still requires a touch to accept the measured settings.

notes: If the specified button route cannot be followed, use the diagnostic scan-tool prompts rather than improvising a different combination.

verification.title: Confirm acceptance
verification.body: Confirm that the calibration measurement message appeared and that the new settings were accepted.

verification.title: Record completion
verification.body: Record calibration acceptance and completion of the CMDTC-clearing operation.

procedures.purpose: SYNC 2/SYNC 3 touchscreen activation, calibration acceptance and stored-code clearing.
Required general safety precautions before calibration.

guides.title: Replace the SYNC 2 or SYNC 3 touchscreen display
guides.summary: Remove the front display interface module, separate its attached electronics, refit the assembly and complete touchscreen calibration.
guides.introduction: The front display interface module (FDIM) is the touchscreen through which the driver operates the SYNC information and entertainment system. It works with other modules, including the attached accessory protocol interface module (APIM). Display replacement involves removing the assembly from the center stack and separating these two components. The job finishes with touchscreen calibration so touch input is correctly aligned with the display.
guides.why: The display mountings and the screws joining the APIM to the display have different tightening values. Keeping those fastener groups distinct helps preserve the assembly during reinstallation. Calibration is also a required part of the repair: securing the screen and reconnecting its wiring does not complete the touch-input setup.

when.summary: When removal or replacement of the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 front display interface module is required.
notes: Arrange access to the touchscreen calibration procedure before starting the hardware work.

prepare.title: Prepare for center-stack access
prepare.detail: Be able to remove and reinstall the front control panel using the linked Front Control/Display Interface Module procedure. That access operation comes before display removal.

prepare.title: Control the small fasteners
prepare.detail: Have suitable bolt and screw tools and torque equipment capable of the specified low tightening values. Keep display mounting bolts separate from the APIM attachment screws.

prepare.title: Plan the calibration stage
prepare.detail: Have the linked Touchscreen Calibration procedure and the capability to carry it out after the display assembly is installed.

steps.title: Remove the front control panel
steps.body: Use the [Front Control/Display Interface Module](#/document/G1704851) access procedure cited by the display repair. This clears the front of the display assembly so its mountings can be reached.

steps.title: Release the display assembly
steps.body: Following [Front Display Interface Module](#/document/G1704008), remove the display mounting bolts, release the display and disconnect its electrical connectors. Support the assembly while disconnecting it so the wiring does not carry its weight.

steps.title: Separate the APIM
steps.body: Remove the attachment screws and separate the APIM from the FDIM. Keep this fastening group identifiable for reassembly; these screws use a lower tightening value than the display mounting bolts.

steps.title: Reassemble and reinstall
steps.body: Reverse removal. Attach the APIM to the display and tighten its screws to 9 lb.in (1 Nm). Reconnect the electrical connectors and install the display mounting bolts at 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm). Restore the front control panel using its linked procedure.

steps.title: Calibrate the touchscreen
steps.body: Complete [Touchscreen Calibration](#/document/G1702410) after installation. Use that procedure for the actual calibration sequence rather than assuming that reconnecting the display establishes touch alignment.

watchFor.title: Fastener values exchanged
watchFor.body: The APIM screws and display mounting bolts have separate torque specifications. Apply each value to its own fastening group.

watchFor.title: Calibration left unfinished
watchFor.body: Keep calibration in the repair plan even when removal and refitting appear straightforward.

verification.title: Confirm assembly restoration
verification.body: Check that the APIM is attached, the display connectors are reconnected, both fastening groups are secured correctly and the front control panel is restored.

verification.title: Record calibration completion
verification.body: Record whether the linked touchscreen calibration completed successfully. An incomplete calibration leaves a required stage of the repair outstanding.

procedures.purpose: SYNC 2/SYNC 3 FDIM removal and installation, APIM separation and the two attachment torque specifications.
Front control panel removal and installation required to access the FDIM.
Required touchscreen calibration after FDIM installation on SYNC 2/SYNC 3 equipment.

guides.title: Remove and refit the SYNC 2 or SYNC 3 media hub
guides.summary: Remove, disconnect and refit the floor-console media hub on a 2015 Mustang with SYNC 2 or SYNC 3 and a 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
guides.introduction: The media hub gives your music somewhere to plug in; the console supplies somewhere for the cable to become a small, infuriating octopus. It is the user-facing media connection panel inside the console storage compartment. I’ll walk you through releasing that panel, disconnecting its rear plugs and putting it back securely. The hub belongs to the wider SYNC audio and control system described in the [information and entertainment overview](#/document/G1702412), so removing it is a repair action, not proof that it caused a media complaint.
guides.why: The hub must first come out of its console mounting to expose its electrical connectors. Supporting it while releasing those connections keeps the wiring from becoming a removal handle. Refitting reverses that order: connect the wiring while the rear is accessible, then seat the hub in the console.

when.summary: Use this procedure when the media hub needs to be removed, refitted or replaced following an established repair decision.
notes: A media connection complaint alone does not identify the hub as the faulty part.
The removal and installation sequence applies to all four listed engines with the specified SYNC equipment.

prepare.title: Have a trim-removal wedge ready
prepare.detail: Use the broad, flat trim-removal wedge illustrated in the [media hub procedure](#/document/G1704009). Keep room in the console compartment to support the released hub and reach its rear plugs.

prepare.title: Identify the fitted hub and the job boundary
prepare.detail: Locate the rectangular media connection panel beside the round power socket inside the console. If replacing it, have a replacement matched to the fitted vehicle equipment and connections. This procedure covers physical removal and refitting; electrical fault testing and any configuration work require separate, vehicle-matched instructions. If the mounting or connector arrangement differs from the illustration, resolve that difference before forcing anything apart.

steps.title: Open the console lid and locate the hub
steps.body:
Raise the floor-console lid to expose the storage compartment, as shown in the [media hub procedure](#/document/G1704009).

Find the rectangular media panel on the compartment wall beside the round power socket. The illustrated panel has media openings on its face; this whole rectangular unit is the component to release.

steps.title: Ease the hub out of its console opening
steps.body:
Use the illustrated trim-removal wedge at the hub’s edge to ease the unit out of its mounting. Draw it outward into the open storage compartment while supporting its body.

Move it only far enough to reach the rear electrical connectors. I treat this as a trim-release job: once the panel moves, the wiring gets no vote in how much farther it travels.

steps.title: Release the rear electrical connectors
steps.body:
With the hub supported outside its opening, examine the rear connections before separating them. The illustration shows three plugs: two larger connectors side by side and a smaller connector alongside them. Note which plug belongs in each socket.

Release each connector’s retaining feature at the positions indicated by the illustration’s arrows, then separate the connector body from the hub. Hold the plug body rather than pulling its cable. Once all electrical connectors are detached, remove the hub from the compartment.

steps.title: Reconnect the hub while its rear remains accessible
steps.body:
Position the original or matching replacement hub near the console opening. Return each electrical connector to its corresponding rear socket and engage its retaining feature.

Check that every disconnected plug has been reattached and is seated securely before moving the hub into the panel. This is the convenient moment to catch a missed connection; fishing it out again is a particularly dull encore.

steps.title: Seat the hub and finish the console
steps.body:
Guide the connected wiring back through the console opening without trapping it between the hub and surrounding panel. Return the hub to its original orientation and seat it fully in the opening.

Check that the rectangular face sits evenly against the surrounding panel and remains secure. Lower the console lid and confirm that it closes normally.

watchFor.title: Wiring restraining the released hub
watchFor.body: If the hub stops moving because its cables are taut, stop drawing it outward. Support the unit and reach the connector retainers before continuing.

watchFor.title: A connector that will not separate
watchFor.body: Check that its retaining feature has released before applying more pulling force. Do not use the cable to overcome a stubborn latch.

watchFor.title: Uneven seating during refitting
watchFor.body: If one edge remains proud of the console panel, stop pressing and check for a trapped wire or an obstruction at the opening. Seat the unit only after the obstruction is cleared.

notes: The installation sequence is the reverse of removal: reconnect the electrical plugs, seat the hub, then close the console lid.
The illustrated connector count and layout help identify the work area; use the actual fitted connections when keeping track of the plugs.

verification.title: Confirm the connections before seating
verification.body: Account for every plug disconnected during removal and confirm that each is reattached with its retaining feature engaged.

verification.title: Confirm physical completion
verification.body: The hub should sit evenly and securely in its opening, with no wiring caught around its perimeter. The console lid should close normally. These checks confirm reassembly; they do not establish whether an earlier media fault has been repaired.

Context for the media hub’s place within the SYNC information and entertainment system.

guides.title: Overlay a replacement satellite radio antenna cable on a coupe or convertible
guides.summary: Replace the required satellite antenna cable section by routing and securing a new cable alongside the existing vehicle harness.
guides.introduction: The satellite antenna cable carries the antenna’s signal to the audio equipment. On these SYNC 2 and SYNC 3 installations, the original cable is incorporated into the wiring harness and cannot be removed separately. Replacement therefore means installing an overlay cable. An inline connection beneath the floor console divides the access work into front and rear sections, with different rear routes for coupe and convertible bodies.
guides.why: Identifying the body style and cable section first determines which interior components must come out. Front-section work requires access to the audio module, while rear-section work reaches toward the antenna through the headliner or luggage compartment. Following the existing harness route provides a defined path for the replacement and allows it to be secured along its length.
searchTerms: satellite antenna cable under floor console

when.summary: When the front or rear satellite antenna cable section has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Identify the affected section before removing trim; this replacement operation does not itself isolate a reception fault.

prepare.title: Choose the correct access branch
prepare.detail: Establish coupe or convertible body style and front or rear cable section. All branches begin with floor-console removal.

prepare.title: Prepare for interior disassembly
prepare.detail: Have the applicable console, audio-module and trim procedures available. Coupe rear work requires headliner lowering; convertible rear work may also require subwoofer and amplifier removal.

prepare.title: Provide the overlay and its attachments
prepare.detail: Use the replacement satellite antenna cable and tape or zip ties to secure it to the vehicle harness as prescribed.

steps.title: Expose the inline connection
steps.body: Remove the floor console using its removal and installation procedure. This gives access to the inline satellite cable connection beneath it and establishes the joining point for the cable sections.

steps.title: Open front-section access
steps.body: For front cable replacement on either body style, remove the Audio Front Control Module (ACM) using its dedicated procedure. This provides access at the audio-equipment end of the route.

steps.title: Open coupe rear-section access
steps.body: For a coupe rear cable, lower the headliner after removing the console. Follow the headliner-lowering procedure referenced by the cable article so the overhead portion of the route becomes accessible.

steps.title: Open convertible rear-section access
steps.body: Remove the loadspace trim panel. Remove the luggage-lid interior trim by first removing its latch cover and push pins. Disconnect the indicated electrical connector, then remove the luggage-compartment weatherstrip and spare-tire cover. If fitted, remove the subwoofer and amplifier unit. Remove the pin-type retainers and move the right-hand luggage-compartment side trim aside.

steps.title: Install the replacement overlay
steps.body: Leave the original harness-integrated cable in place. Follow the correct coupe or convertible routing illustration and lay the replacement cable along the vehicle wiring harness. Secure it with tape or zip ties as necessary, completing the replacement section’s connections at the existing connection points.

steps.title: Restore the opened interior
steps.body: Check the cable route and attachments while they remain visible, then use the relevant access procedures to reinstall the audio equipment and trim. Reconnect the electrical connector disconnected during convertible rear access and restore the weatherstrip and covers.

watchFor.title: Attempting to extract the original cable
watchFor.body: The original cable belongs to the main harness. The prescribed repair leaves it there and adds the replacement alongside it.

watchFor.title: Using the wrong body route
watchFor.body: The coupe and convertible have separate routing illustrations and different rear access requirements.

notes: Subwoofer and amplifier removal applies only when that equipment is fitted and obstructs the specified convertible rear access.

verification.title: Confirm the installed route
verification.body: Check that the overlay follows the applicable routing illustration and is secured to the existing harness with the prescribed attachments.

verification.title: Confirm access restoration
verification.body: Check the reinstalled connectors, trim retainers and covers for the branch used, and record which cable section was replaced.

guides.title: Satellite radio antenna replacement for SYNC 2/SYNC 3
guides.summary: Replace the satellite radio antenna using the coupe headliner access or convertible luggage-lid access, then seat and secure its base.
guides.introduction: The satellite radio antenna receives the signal used by the vehicle's satellite radio feature, where fitted. Its external base is retained from inside the body and connects to the audio system through a wiring harness. The replacement task is similar on both body styles, but reaching the retaining hardware is different.
guides.why: The retaining bolt, retainer and electrical connector must be released before the antenna can be removed. During installation, feeding the harness through the opening and seating the base establishes the antenna's position before securing it. A new antenna has a specific handling provision: its bolt does not need to be removed from the base.

when.summary: When the satellite radio antenna has been identified for replacement or requires removal for related work.
notes: A reception complaint alone does not establish that the antenna needs replacement.

prepare.title: Plan the body-style access
prepare.detail: For a coupe, be equipped to lower and restore the headliner using the Headliner - Lowering procedure. For a convertible, access is through the luggage compartment lid interior trim.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim and retaining hardware
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the retaining bolt and trim retainers, plus a torque wrench capable of the specified small-fastener torque. Keep the removed retainer and trim hardware organized.

steps.title: Expose the antenna attachment
steps.body: On a coupe, lower the headliner. On a convertible, remove the luggage compartment lid latch cover and push pins, then remove the interior trim panel. Follow the appropriate body-style branch in [Satellite Radio Antenna](#/document/G1704010).

steps.title: Release and remove the antenna
steps.body: Remove the antenna retaining bolt, followed by the retainer. Disconnect the electrical connector, then remove the antenna. This sequence releases both its mechanical attachment and its connection to the vehicle harness.

steps.title: Feed the harness and seat the replacement
steps.body: Pass the antenna harness through the opening and install the base until seated. When fitting a new antenna, leave its bolt in the base; removing that bolt is unnecessary.

steps.title: Complete retention and restore access trim
steps.body: Complete the antenna retention and electrical reconnection using the procedure's installation details. The retaining bolt torque is 62 lb.in (7 Nm). Restore the coupe headliner or the convertible lid trim, push pins and latch cover after the attachment is complete.

watchFor.title: Base not fully seated
watchFor.body: Check the harness passage and base seating before completing the attachment; the installation sequence specifically requires the base to be seated.

watchFor.title: Wrong access route
watchFor.body: Use the coupe or convertible branch that matches the vehicle. The convertible procedure calls for luggage-lid trim removal.

notes: Satellite radio is optional equipment within the SYNC 2/SYNC 3 system covered here.

verification.title: Check the completed installation
verification.body: Confirm that the base is seated, retention is complete, the electrical connector is reconnected and the disturbed interior trim has been restored.

verification.title: Record the retaining-bolt check
verification.body: Record completion of the 62 lb.in (7 Nm) retaining-bolt torque check.

procedures.purpose: Satellite radio antenna removal and installation for SYNC 2/SYNC 3, with separate coupe and convertible access branches.

guides.title: Remove and refit the Shaker subwoofer and amplifier unit
guides.summary: Remove the three-bolt lower cover, release the subwoofer unit’s upper bolt and two lower mounting bolts, unplug the amplifier connector, and refit everything using the correct inch-pound torques.
guides.introduction:
The Shaker subwoofer gives the bass somewhere to live; unfortunately, that somewhere comes with bolts and an electrical connector. I’ll walk you through removing the lower cover, supporting the assembly while unplugging it, and putting everything back without giving the little cover bolts the big mounting bolts’ treatment.

The subwoofer produces the low notes, while its amplifier supplies the electrical power that drives the speaker. This job removes and refits that assembly.
guides.why: The important details are the two mounting stages, the connector behind the unit, and the different tightening settings. Supporting the assembly protects its wiring, while keeping the cover bolts separate prevents a small fastening job from becoming a stripped-thread pain in the ass.

when.summary: Use this procedure when the fitted Shaker subwoofer and amplifier assembly needs removal, replacement or refitting for an established repair.
notes: Applies to 2015 Mustang models with 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engines and the Shaker audio system with SYNC 2/SYNC 3.
Confirm the fitted audio equipment before selecting a replacement. The system overview distinguishes Shaker installations, which include a subwoofer amplifier, from non-Shaker installations.

prepare.title: Set the scope before ordering parts
prepare.detail: This procedure handles the complete subwoofer assembly and its external connection. Establish the need for replacement separately; internal speaker or amplifier repair and electrical fault testing are outside this job.

prepare.title: Gather fastening tools and keep the bolts identified
prepare.detail: Have tools that fit the installed bolts and a torque wrench suitable for both 21 lb.in (2.4 Nm) and 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm). Keep the three cover bolts separate from the upper unit bolt and two lower mounting bolts.

prepare.title: Make room to support the assembly
prepare.detail: Clear the working area around the enclosure in the luggage compartment. Leave enough room to support the unit while reaching the electrical connector behind it. If replacing the assembly, have the correct replacement for the fitted Shaker installation ready.

steps.title: Locate the Shaker enclosure and identify the lower cover
steps.body:
Open the luggage compartment and locate the Shaker enclosure against the side bodywork. Identify the large circular speaker grille and the separate lower cover running beneath it. The first three bolts belong to that lower cover: one toward each end and one near the middle.

I’d identify these before picking up a tool—the round grille and its surrounding hardware are not the first things to dismantle. The removal sequence is shown in [Subwoofer and Amplifier Unit](#/document/G1704011).

steps.title: Remove the three lower-cover bolts and take off the cover
steps.body:
Remove all three bolts securing the lower speaker cover, then take the cover away from the enclosure. Keep the cover and its bolts together.

With the cover removed, identify the unit’s mounting arrangement: one upper bolt toward the outer edge of the enclosure and two lower bolts, one at each mounting foot.

steps.title: Release the upper mounting bolt, then the two lower bolts
steps.body:
Remove the single upper mounting bolt first. Support the enclosure, then remove the two lower mounting bolts at its feet.

Keep control of the assembly once the lower bolts are out. Its electrical connector is still attached, so do not carry the unit away or let its weight pull on the wiring.

steps.title: Disconnect the amplifier connector and remove the assembly
steps.body:
While supporting the enclosure, move it only far enough to reach behind it. Locate the electrical connector at the lower edge of the finned amplifier housing.

Disconnect the plug by handling its housing rather than pulling its wires. Once the connector is free, remove the subwoofer assembly from the mounting area. The connector, rather than the cable, is the part that needs persuading.

steps.title: Return the assembly and reconnect its wiring
steps.body:
Bring the original or replacement assembly back to its mounting area and support it while reconnecting the electrical plug at the amplifier. Make sure the plug is fully seated.

Guide the enclosure into position with the wiring clear of its mounting feet and contact surfaces. Do not use the mounting bolts to force an obstructed assembly into place.

steps.title: Secure the two lower mounts, then the upper mount
steps.body:
Reverse the mounting removal order: install the two lower mounting bolts, then the single upper mounting bolt. Start the bolts with the enclosure correctly aligned.

Tighten both lower mounting bolts to 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm). Tighten the upper mounting bolt to 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm) as well. Both mounting groups use the same torque.

steps.title: Refit the lower cover and tighten its three bolts
steps.body:
Before covering the mounting area, confirm that the connector is attached, the wiring is clear and all three unit mounting bolts have been tightened.

Return the lower cover to position, align its three bolt locations and install the cover bolts. Tighten all three to 21 lb.in (2.4 Nm). This is the lighter setting—give the torque wrench a fresh setting before the cover gets its turn.

watchFor.title: Inch-pounds and foot-pounds are different units
watchFor.body: The settings are 21 lb.in (2.4 Nm) for the cover and 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm) for the unit mounts. Do not apply either number as lb.ft.

watchFor.title: An unsecured enclosure can load the connector
watchFor.body: Support the assembly while removing the lower mounting bolts and while disconnecting or reconnecting the plug. Keep its movement within the available wiring slack until it is unplugged.

watchFor.title: Keep wiring out of the mounting surfaces
watchFor.body: As the assembly returns to position, check that the cable is not trapped beneath a mounting foot or between the enclosure and adjacent bodywork. Reposition the wiring before tightening if it is caught.

notes: The [Information and Entertainment System overview](#/document/G1702412) identifies the subwoofer amplifier as Shaker equipment. Other audio components listed there are context for the system, not additional parts to remove for this job.

verification.title: Confirm the connection before closing the area
verification.body: Check that the amplifier plug is fully reconnected and that its wiring remains clear when the enclosure is seated.

verification.title: Account for all unit mounting bolts
verification.body: Confirm that the two lower mounting bolts and the single upper mounting bolt are installed and tightened to 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm).

verification.title: Confirm the cover is fully refitted
verification.body: Check that the lower cover sits in position and all three cover bolts are installed and tightened to 21 lb.in (2.4 Nm). Collect the tools and account for any loose fasteners before finishing.

procedures.purpose: Lower-cover removal, illustrated upper and lower mounting-bolt sequence, amplifier connector location, assembly removal and reverse-order installation with both torque settings.
Identify the Shaker subwoofer amplifier within the audio system and distinguish Shaker from non-Shaker equipment.

stepGroups.title: Locate the enclosure and remove its cover
stepGroups.summary: Identify the correct cover and expose the unit’s mounting points.

stepGroups.title: Release and disconnect the assembly
stepGroups.summary: Remove the upper and lower mounting bolts, support the enclosure and unplug the amplifier.

stepGroups.title: Reconnect, mount and cover
stepGroups.summary: Reconnect the assembly and refit the mounts and cover using their respective torques.

guides.title: Diagnose inoperative daytime running lamps using the front fog lamps
guides.summary: Check fog-lamp operation, the BCM’s START/STOP input and module connections to determine the next diagnostic path for inoperative daytime running lamps.
guides.introduction: On vehicles equipped with this daytime running lamp (DRL) system, the body control module (BCM) operates the front fog lamp assemblies for daytime lighting. The diagnostic sequence first checks whether those lamps work through their normal fog-lamp control, then checks an ignition input and the BCM connections.
guides.why: Working fog lamps establish that the shared lamps can operate. The next question is whether the BCM recognizes the START/STOP button input. This sequence separates a lamp-system problem from an input or connection problem before further module diagnosis.
searchTerms: fog lamps work but daytime running lights do not

when.summary: Use this test when fitted daytime running lamps fail to operate and the complaint is currently present.
notes: Confirm the fitted system’s operating conditions before treating lamps that are off as a fault.

prepare.title: Check the electrical starting point
prepare.detail: Verify battery and charging operation and battery state of charge above 70%. Review previous repairs, inspect fuses and harnesses, and check network modules for related diagnostic trouble codes.

prepare.title: Arrange scan-tool and connector access
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable scan tool that can display BCM live data. Connector inspection requires familiarity with terminal condition and fit. Use the specified flex probes if terminal testing becomes necessary.

steps.title: Confirm the complaint and communication
steps.body: Reproduce the DRL failure under the fitted system’s operating conditions. If a module will not communicate with the scan tool, follow Communications Network diagnosis first; a fuse, wiring connection or module fault can interrupt access.

steps.title: Run A1: operate the fog lamps
steps.body: Switch ignition on, select PARKLAMPS and activate the front fog lamps, with the high beams off. If the fog lamps fail, follow Fog Lamps diagnosis. If they operate correctly, continue to A2.

steps.title: Run A2: observe the ignition input
steps.body: Display the BCM Ignition Switch 1 parameter identification (PID), START_STOP_1. Watch it while pressing and releasing the START/STOP button. A changing state leads to A3. If it does not change, diagnose ignition state through Steering Wheel and Column Electrical Components.

steps.title: Run A3: inspect and retest BCM connections
steps.body: Disconnect and inspect all BCM connectors. Replace corroded connectors or terminals and clean module pins; replace damaged, bent or pushed-out pins as necessary. Reconnect securely and test again. If the concern persists, check OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins and follow any relevant bulletin. Otherwise, continue into the BCM guided routine using the vehicle identification number (VIN).

watchFor.title: Temporary recovery after reconnection
watchFor.body: If the lamps recover, identify and correct the root cause of any connector or terminal defect.

watchFor.title: Unnecessary module replacement
watchFor.body: A persistent complaint at A3 requires the VIN-specific guided routine; this test does not establish a replacement decision by itself.

notes: Do not apply power or ground directly to module-controlled lamps unless a diagnostic procedure specifically directs it.

diagnostics.finding: Fog lamps work and START_STOP_1 changes correctly
diagnostics.meaning: The preliminary lamp-operation and ignition-input checks pass, but the DRL complaint remains unresolved.
diagnostics.next: Complete BCM connector inspection and the applicable bulletin or guided-routine branch.

verification.title: Verify the original function
verification.body: After the identified correction, confirm normal DRL operation under the fitted system’s operating conditions.

verification.title: Record the decision path
verification.body: Record fog-lamp operation, START_STOP_1 response and connector findings. If the complaint remains, record the outstanding guided-routine result rather than marking the repair complete.

procedures.purpose: Complete DRL Pinpoint Test A, including fog-lamp checks, ignition-input monitoring and BCM connector decisions.
Electrical diagnostic prerequisites, scan-tool data interpretation and terminal-handling methods.
Exterior-lighting operating conditions and component descriptions for confirming the complaint.

Ignition-state diagnosis when START_STOP_1 does not change during Test A2.

guides.title: Diagnose HID headlamp, beam-switch and manual-leveling faults
guides.summary: Separate headlamp supply, wiring, switch-input and leveling faults before deciding whether a bulb, ballast, assembly or control module needs attention.
guides.introduction: High-intensity discharge (HID) headlamps depend on a bulb, ballast, electrical supplies and sound grounds. The body control module (BCM) controls lighting outputs, while the steering column control module (SCCM) reads the multifunction switch. Diagnosis compares the requested function with the electrical response. China-market low-beam relay and manual-leveling arrangements require their own test branches.
guides.why: A dark lamp can result from a missing supply or a protective shutdown rather than a failed bulb. Likewise, a lamp that stays on may have an unwanted voltage feed. Distinguishing these conditions prevents replacing parts while leaving the electrical fault active.

when.summary: Use when a low beam, high beam, flash-to-pass function or fitted manual-leveling system fails to respond correctly.
notes: Choose the China or except-China branch before testing low beams.
A module that does not communicate requires communications-network diagnosis first.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting BCM and SCCM self-tests and switch data, a multimeter, and the applicable wiring and connector information. China-market relay tests require a fused jumper.

prepare.title: Inspect and identify the circuit
prepare.detail: Inspect lamps and relevant switches for damage. For failed low beams, check battery junction box (BJB) fuses 33 and 35. Follow each test's ignition, switch and connector-disconnection sequence; use the bulb procedure for any HID substitution.

steps.title: Match the complaint to the diagnostic route
steps.body: Record diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), affected side and whether the beam is absent or continuously illuminated. In the headlamp procedure, A/B cover failed low beams, C failed high beams, D/E continuous low beams, F continuous high beams, G flash-to-pass and H China-market manual leveling. Other BCM or SCCM codes go to their respective diagnostic charts.

steps.title: Test failed low beams outside China—Test A
steps.body: Both lamps failing leads to A9's BCM connection checks. For one failed lamp, A2–A8 distinguish ballast supply, BCM low-beam feed, isolated wiring and grounds. A missing BCM feed requires the specified self-test and voltage retest before further circuit checks. Once directed to bulb substitution, use a known-good bulb from the same vehicle and remove it afterward. If it does not restore operation, inspect the internal harness before choosing ballast replacement or harness repair.

steps.title: Test China-market low-beam relays—Test B
steps.body: With both lamps out, check the shared relay-ground path first. With one out, check relay feeds and ground, then use the specified fused bridge between relay socket pins 3 and 5. Illumination identifies the relay replacement branch. Otherwise, continue to the downstream lamp supply, grounds and bulb checks. Remove the jumper when directed. Missing relay-control voltage requires the BCM self-test retest and isolated circuit checks.

steps.title: Check failed high beams—Test C
steps.body: Confirm low beams work first; otherwise return to A or B. For both high beams failing, compare the HIGH_BEAM_SW parameter identification (PID) with stalk position. For an individual failure, C3 requires ignition and headlamp switch OFF before disconnecting the affected lamp. Then turn ignition ON and select HEADLAMPS and HIGH BEAM. Measure C1021 pin 12 on the left or C1041 pin 12 on the right to ground: the criterion is greater than 11 volts. C4 repeats this high-beam measurement after BCM self-test, code clearing and repeat self-test. Passing voltage directs internal-harness inspection; failing directs C5/C6 wiring checks. C6's left-side continuity branch applies only outside China.

steps.title: Trace low beams that stay on—Tests D and E
steps.body: If both remain on with the switch OFF, test the headlamp switch, its ground and its signal circuits for opens and shorts. For one continuously lit lamp outside China, Test D isolates the low-beam output and checks for unwanted voltage. In China, Test E first removes the relay: a lamp that remains lit indicates a downstream short to voltage. If it goes out, test the relay-control circuit with the BCM disconnected.

steps.title: Trace high beams that stay on—Test F
steps.body: With LOW BEAM selected, both high beams remaining on requires comparing HIGH_BEAM_SW with stalk position. A mismatch leads to multifunction-switch replacement and retesting before SCCM diagnosis. For one affected lamp, F3 checks its disconnected high-beam feed: no voltage selects the assembly replacement branch. Voltage requires F4's BCM-disconnected check to distinguish a wiring short from the BCM route.

steps.title: Separate flash-to-pass failure—Test G
steps.body: Check ordinary high-beam operation first; failure returns to C. Otherwise monitor FLASH-to-PASS while operating the stalk. A mismatch directs switch replacement and retesting, followed by SCCM checks if needed. A matching input directs BCM connection checks.

steps.title: Check manual-leveling response and supplies—Test H
steps.body: For China-market leveling, turn ignition ON, select HEADLAMPS, release the leveling control, select setting 4 and press it until it locks down. If neither beam moves, H2 checks C205 pin 9 to ground with ignition and headlamp switch OFF and C205 disconnected. If either moves, H3 checks the inoperative module's pin 1 to ground at C1024 or C1044, disconnecting with ignition OFF before turning it ON. Both supply criteria are greater than 11 volts. If a failed supply check leads to F68, stop for vehicle-specific fuse confirmation.

steps.title: Complete the leveling ground and command checks
steps.body: After H3 passes, H4 requires greater than 11 volts between module pins 1 and 3; failure directs ground-circuit repair. H5 isolates the relevant connectors and checks command-circuit continuity to C205 pin 1. Less than 3 ohms selects assembly replacement for one failed side. For both sides, continue through H6's unwanted-voltage check and H7's short-to-ground check. Only the completed passing sequence selects headlamp-switch replacement.

steps.title: Resolve connections before module decisions
steps.body: At the applicable BCM or SCCM endpoint, inspect connectors for corrosion, bent or damaged terminals and pushed-out pins. Repair the cause, seat and latch connectors, then operate the system again. Persistent faults require the specified technical-service-bulletin check; BCM escalation uses the guided routine requiring the vehicle identification number.

watchFor.title: F68 requires vehicle-specific confirmation
watchFor.body: F68 is in the BJB. Confirm its rating from the vehicle fuse legend and current configuration before fuse service. Do not select or increase its rating, or use an unresolved leveling supply fault to justify module replacement.

watchFor.title: Supply voltage does not finish every branch
watchFor.body: Passing C3/C4 directs internal-harness inspection. Repair identified damage; replace the assembly if the harness cannot be repaired. If the harness is sound and the fault remains unexplained, retain that unresolved result.

notes: After a failed bulb substitution, a sound internal harness selects ballast replacement; repair a faulty harness or replace the assembly if it cannot be repaired.

diagnostics.finding: A beam-output DTC ends in :11, or B1D00:15, B1D01:15, B1D02:15 or B1D03:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The :11 beam faults indicate shorts to ground. The listed :15 codes require symptom context: the failed-beam branches address opens, while continuously illuminated branches address unwanted voltage.
diagnostics.next: Select the affected low- or high-beam test and market branch before identifying a replacement part.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U1000:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive current has temporarily disabled a BCM output.
diagnostics.next: Address other fault codes and correct the cause, then clear codes and repeat the self-test to enable the output.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3000:49 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: An excessive-current fault has permanently disabled an output.
diagnostics.next: Correct the excessive-current cause before any BCM replacement and follow the vehicle-specific guided routine.

diagnostics.finding: The SCCM records B1007:09 or B1D36:09.
diagnostics.meaning: The chart identifies a high-beam-switch or turn-indicator-switch component fault.
diagnostics.next: Follow the left multifunction-switch replacement route and test operation; the chart selects SCCM replacement only if the concern persists.

verification.title: Repeat the affected function
verification.body: Confirm the original low-beam, high-beam, flash-to-pass or leveling complaint is resolved after the directed repair and connector reconnection.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record before-and-after codes and relevant measurements. Where U1000:00 occurred, document the repeat self-test and restored output. Record unresolved supply or guided-routine branches as unfinished diagnosis.

guides.title: Diagnose parking, side-marker and license-plate lamps that fail or stay on
guides.summary: Use the pattern of failed lamps, module fault codes and isolated circuit measurements to distinguish bulb, wiring, connection and output-protection faults.
guides.introduction: The body control module (BCM) controls separate lighting outputs, while some lamps share a supply and ground. That makes the failure pattern useful: one dark license lamp suggests a different starting point from both rear side markers and both license lamps going dark together. These checks also cover lamps that remain on and unequal signature-lamp brightness.
guides.why: A lamp needs both a supply and a return path to ground. Checking voltage against chassis ground first prevents mistaking a missing supply for a bad lamp ground. The BCM can also disable an overloaded output, so absent voltage does not by itself establish module failure.

when.summary: Use when parking, marker or license lamps are dark, remain on, or signature lamps have unequal brightness.
notes: Use the appropriate China or Except China rear-lamp connector branch. Signature-brightness Test C applies only to Except China vehicles.
The individual front parking-lamp path has defined stopping points; it does not provide a complete module-replacement decision.

prepare.title: Use the required diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Have a BCM-capable scan tool, an electrical meter and familiarity with Ford diagnostic methods. Use Wiring Diagrams Cell 92 for parking lamps and Cell 85 for signature lamps.

prepare.title: Identify connectors before measuring
prepare.detail: Follow each test's ignition, switch and disconnection sequence. Resistance checks require the specified circuits isolated with ignition off. Confirm connector cavities from the linked wiring and connector information.

steps.title: Classify the complaint before choosing a branch
steps.body: With ignition on and the switch at PARKING LAMPS, use A1 in [lamp diagnosis](#/document/G1694229) to identify the affected group. All parking lamps out routes to A26. Count failed sections within each rear assembly: one or two of its three sections out directs assembly replacement; all three out requires A21–A25. Record diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) before clearing them. A module that will not communicate requires network diagnosis.

steps.title: Check groups of side-marker and plate lamps
steps.body: A2–A5 cover both front side markers; A6–A9 cover both rear side markers and both plate lamps. Initial supply above 11 volts directs repair of the group's open ground. Otherwise follow the prescribed self-test, clear and repeat sequence, then recheck supply. Restored voltage directs the stated bulb replacement. Continued low supply requires isolated continuity and short-to-ground checks; repair failures, or advance to A26 when both pass.

steps.title: Separate an individual bulb fault from its wiring
steps.body: A10–A12 cover one front side marker; A18–A20 cover one rear side marker or plate lamp. Supply above 11 volts permits measuring across the connector's supply and ground: above 11 volts directs bulb replacement, while a failed check directs ground-circuit repair. If supply is low, check continuity to the specified BCM terminal. Repair failed continuity; passing continuity routes to A26.

steps.title: Respect the front parking-lamp stopping points
steps.body: At A13, supply above 11 volts allows A15's supply-to-lamp-ground check: above 11 volts directs bulb replacement; otherwise repair the ground circuit. Low A13 supply leads to A14's self-test and recheck. Restored voltage directs bulb replacement; if supply remains low or absent, stop for further diagnosis. Do not use that missing supply to condemn the ground. Separately, A16 documents continuity from C156 pin 2 to C2280F pin 30, or C1042 pin 2 to C2280F pin 37, with ignition off and the specified connectors disconnected. Resistance must be less than 3 ohms; otherwise repair the circuit. A passing result ends this check without authorizing a BCM decision.

steps.title: Investigate a completely dark rear assembly
steps.body: A21 first checks stoplamp operation; failed stoplamps require their own diagnosis. With stoplamps working, A22 checks parking-lamp supply using the market-specific connector. Above 11 volts directs assembly replacement. Otherwise A23 repeats the self-test and voltage check; restored supply gives the same replacement decision. Continued low supply leads to A24 continuity and A25 short-to-ground checks. Repair failures; passing checks lead to A26.

steps.title: Trace lamps that remain illuminated
steps.body: Test B first checks whether low beams remain on with the switch off; if so, use headlamp diagnosis. Otherwise switch ignition off and disconnect the relevant BCM output connector: C2280C for rear markers/plate lamps, C2280E for rear parking lamps, C2280F for front parking lamps or C2280G for front side markers. Switch ignition on. Lamps still illuminated indicate an affected circuit requiring repair; lamps going out lead to B3.

steps.title: Compare unequal signature-lamp brightness
steps.body: For Except China vehicles, Test C disconnects the dimmer light-emitting diode (LED) signature lamp's headlamp connector. With ignition on and parking lamps selected, voltage above 11 volts at pin 5 to ground directs headlamp-assembly replacement. Otherwise, with ignition off and C2280G disconnected, check continuity to C2280G pin 3. Less than 3 ohms leads to C3; a failed check requires circuit repair.

steps.title: Finish the connector and module assessment
steps.body: At A26, B3 or C3, inspect BCM connectors for corrosion, damaged pins and pushed-out terminals. Repair, reconnect securely and retest. If the fault remains, check OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins and follow any matching instructions. Otherwise continue through the vehicle-identification-number-specific BCM guided routine. These checks alone do not authorize BCM replacement.

watchFor.title: An output may be deliberately disabled
watchFor.body: Correct the excessive-current fault before attempting to restore an output. Clearing codes cannot substitute for repairing a short.

watchFor.title: Shared loads must be isolated correctly
watchFor.body: Follow every disconnection in the short-to-ground tests. The front side-marker branch also disconnects the headlamps on Except China vehicles.

notes: The intact supply tests use less than 3 ohms for continuity and greater than 10,000 ohms for isolation from ground. Do not transfer those limits into the front parking-lamp A17 path; this guide stops before that decision.

Front parking lamps use separate left/right outputs at C2280F. Rear side markers and license lamps share C2280C pin 12. Identify circuits physically rather than deriving a pin assignment from a code name.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B10F3:11 or B10F3:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These retain the name Left Front Position Light. B10F3:11 indicates a short to ground; B10F3:15 indicates a short to battery or open circuit.
diagnostics.next: Use Test A for an inoperative lamp. For B10F3:15 with a continuously illuminated lamp, use Test B.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B10F4:11 or B10F4:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These retain the name Right Front Position Light, with short-to-ground and short-to-battery-or-open meanings respectively.
diagnostics.next: Use Test A for an inoperative lamp, or Test B for B10F4:15 with the lamp continuously illuminated.

diagnostics.finding: Other parking-lamp output codes are recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The chart distinguishes Rear Park Lamps Output, Front Park Lamps Output and Left/Right Front Position/Sidemarker faults. Short-to-battery-or-open descriptions require the actual dark or continuously-on symptom to select the route.
diagnostics.next: Use the complete DTC chart with the affected lamp group and wiring; do not assume a bulb or BCM has failed.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1447:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The parking-lamp switch input has a short-to-ground fault.
diagnostics.next: Follow Headlamps diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U1000:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive current has temporarily disabled an output.
diagnostics.next: Address other codes and repair the cause, then clear DTCs and repeat the self-test to enable the output.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3000:49 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The output has been permanently disabled after excessive-current limits were exceeded.
diagnostics.next: Correct the overload and address other codes before proceeding through the VIN-specific BCM guided routine or installing a replacement module.

verification.title: Confirm the complaint is resolved
verification.body: Check affected lamps with parking lamps selected and with the switch off. Recheck signature brightness or stoplamp operation where those branches were involved. Complete the required post-repair self-test.

verification.title: Record results and any remaining boundary
verification.body: Record affected lamps, codes, connector measurements and final operation. For an unresolved front parking-lamp supply fault, record the stopping point and readings without declaring the ground or BCM defective.
