guides.title: Diagnose reversing lamps that stay off or stay on
guides.summary: Compare the reported gear position with lamp-output measurements to distinguish lamp, wiring, switch and control-module concerns.
guides.introduction: The reversing lamps at the bottom of the rear bumper illuminate when reverse is selected. Their operation depends on gear information reaching the powertrain control module (PCM) and the body control module (BCM) supplying the lamps. Diagnosis therefore separates an incorrect gear indication from a fault in the lamp's electrical path.
guides.why: A dark lamp can result from a bulb, an interrupted circuit or an output deliberately disabled by excessive current. A continuously lit lamp can instead reflect an incorrect reverse input or a supply wire shorted to voltage.

when.summary: A reversing lamp fails to illuminate in reverse, remains illuminated outside reverse, or has a related circuit code.
notes: Use the engine, transmission and market branch fitted to the vehicle.
A2's engine-start instruction applies only to its GT500 branch; do not transfer that requirement to other variants.

prepare.title: Provide electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool with PCM parameter identification (PID) data and BCM self-tests, a digital multimeter, Rotunda Flex Probes, fused jumper leads and the reversing-lamp wiring diagram. Access to module connectors and VIN-specific diagnostic workflows may be needed.

prepare.title: Secure and assess the vehicle
prepare.detail: Apply the parking brake before gear-selection tests. Confirm the complaint is present, check battery and charging health, and verify battery state of charge above 70%. Follow the specified ignition and connector-isolation sequence for each measurement.

steps.title: Identify the symptom and market arrangement
steps.body: Inspect the bulb and record diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). An unresponsive module requires communications-network diagnosis first. For one failed China-market reversing lamp, replace a defective bulb; if the bulb is sound, replace the assembly. Both China-market lamps inoperative, or the inoperative lamp elsewhere, enter Test A. Lamps staying on enter Test B.

steps.title: Compare actual gear selection with PCM data
steps.body: With ignition on, A1 checks the indication in reverse; B1 checks it through the selector positions. Automatic vehicles use GEAR, 5.0L manuals use GEARPOS_MAN, and other manual branches use REV_SW. Incorrect automatic information needs transmission-range diagnosis. Incorrect 5.0L manual information needs neutral-position-sensor diagnosis. The 2.3L and 3.7L manual branches can continue to their switch tests. For 5.2L, stop the gear-input investigation here and obtain its engine-specific diagnostic path before any C169 or PCM electrical testing.

steps.title: Test supply and ground for an inoperative lamp
steps.body: When reverse is correctly reported, A2 checks the disconnected lamp supply using the market-specific connector. More than 11 volts leads to A4's supply-to-lamp-ground check. A passing result directs bulb replacement except China, or assembly replacement for China; a failed ground check requires circuit repair. Missing supply leads to A3's BCM self-test, code clearing and repeat self-test, with any overcurrent cause corrected before re-enabling a protected output. Restored voltage directs the same market-specific bulb or assembly decision.

steps.title: Trace a supply that remains absent
steps.body: If A3 still finds no adequate supply, switch the ignition off and disconnect the BCM connector specified by A5. Check the supply circuit for a short to ground, then use A6 to check continuity to the BCM. Repair a failed circuit and follow the recorded protection-code recovery requirements. Passing both circuit checks leads to the A11 BCM connector assessment.

steps.title: Use the switch bypass only on the applicable manual branch
steps.body: For a missing reverse indication on 2.3L or 3.7L manuals, A7 disconnects C169 with ignition off. Fit the specified fused jumper from pin 1 to ground, then read REV_SW with ignition on. Remove the jumper after the observation. If reverse appears, A8 bridges pins 1 and 2: reverse appearing now directs switch replacement; failure identifies a ground-circuit concern. Remove that jumper too. If A7 never produces reverse, continue only as described in the next step.

steps.title: Observe the engine boundary for the open-input check
steps.body: For 3.7L, A9 uses ignition off and PCM C1381B disconnected, measuring between C169 pin 1 and C1381B pin 32. Resistance below 3 ohms leads to A10; otherwise repair the circuit. For 2.3L, stop this path before the A9 measurement and obtain the correct engine-specific input-circuit test. This branch does not establish a 2.3L PCM replacement decision through A10.

steps.title: Separate a stuck lamp supply from a false reverse input
steps.body: If B1 reports gears correctly, B2 disconnects BCM C2280C with ignition off, then checks illumination with ignition on. A lamp still lit indicates a supply short to voltage; repair that circuit. If it goes out, continue to B6. For a false reverse indication on 2.3L or 3.7L manuals, B3 disconnects the switch with ignition off and rereads REV_SW with ignition on. An indication that clears directs switch replacement; one that remains leads to B4.

steps.title: Isolate the false-input circuit
steps.body: B4 applies to the listed 2.3L and 3.7L PCM connectors. With ignition off and the appropriate PCM connector disconnected, measure C169 pin 1 to ground. Resistance greater than 10,000 ohms leads to B5; otherwise repair the short to ground. This B4/B5 route remains distinct from the 2.3L stopping point in A9.

steps.title: Complete the applicable module connector assessment
steps.body: At A10 for 3.7L, B5 for 2.3L/3.7L, or BCM checks A11/B6, inspect all corresponding module connectors. Renew defective connectors or terminals, clean corroded module pins, replace damaged or pushed-out pins, and reconnect securely. Retest and correct the underlying connection problem. If the concern remains, follow applicable service articles; only when none addresses it does the branch direct the specified PCM or BCM replacement workflow, with VIN entry as required.

watchFor.title: A jumper fuse fails
watchFor.body: Use the wiring diagram to investigate the possible short before continuing the bypass test.

watchFor.title: A fault disappears during testing
watchFor.body: Do not treat an absent complaint as proof that a module needs replacement. Investigate connector condition and the cause of the intermittent fault.

notes: The 5.0L manual neutral-position-sensor referral is separate from the C169 switch tests.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1277:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detected a short to ground in the reversing-lamp output circuit.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test A to locate the circuit fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1277:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The output circuit has an open or short-to-voltage indication.
diagnostics.next: Use Test A for inoperative lamps or Test B for continuously illuminated lamps.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U1000:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive current has temporarily disabled the BCM output driver.
diagnostics.next: Address other codes and correct the cause, then clear codes and complete a successful self-test to restore the output.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3000:49 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM output has been permanently disabled after excessive-current limits were exceeded.
diagnostics.next: Correct the overcurrent cause and address other codes before following service information and the VIN-based BCM replacement decision.

verification.title: Confirm gear and lamp behavior together
verification.body: Repeat the applicable test: confirm reverse is correctly reported, the lamp illuminates in reverse and it does not remain illuminated outside reverse. Complete required output-driver self-tests after circuit repair.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic endpoint
verification.body: Record engine, transmission, market branch, gear indications, DTCs, measurements and final lamp behavior. Where an engine-specific input test is still required, retain that as an unresolved next step.

procedures.purpose: Lamp/output and gear-observation diagnosis across the listed variants; A7–A8 and B3–B5 for 2.3L/3.7L manuals, A9–A10 for 3.7L only, and the separate 5.0L sensor referral.
Electrical prerequisites, safe terminal probing, fused jumpers and valid circuit measurements.

applicability.equipment: Manual or automatic transmission; China-market rear-lamp arrangement where fitted

guides.title: Diagnose Mustang brake lamps that will not light or stay on
guides.summary: Trace brake-lamp faults through the pedal switch, lamp circuits and control modules using the correct market-specific diagnostic branch.
guides.introduction: The brake-pedal switch signals that you are braking. The body control module (BCM) controls the high mounted stoplamp and, on China-market vehicles, the rear stoplamps. Elsewhere, body control module B (BCMB) controls the rear lamp segments. These checks distinguish switch, wiring, lamp and controller faults.
guides.why: Missing lamp voltage does not automatically condemn a controller: an excessive-current fault can disable its output. Checking supplies, grounds and connections establishes why the lamp fails before replacement.
searchTerms: one rear brake lamp segment not working

when.summary: Use when any brake lamp fails to illuminate, stays illuminated, or a stoplamp circuit fault is recorded.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, volt/ohmmeter, correct connector probe adapters and a fused jumper. Ford diagnostic knowledge is required for live measurements, module self-tests and fault interpretation.

prepare.title: Identify the correct circuits
prepare.detail: Have Wiring Diagrams Cell 90 and connector information available. Confirm market and engine before choosing terminals. Follow each test's ignition and disconnection sequence; the switch supply remains live with ignition off.

steps.title: Classify the complaint and read fault codes
steps.body: Observe the lamps with the pedal released and applied. Use Test A for all lamps dark, B for individual or grouped faults outside China, C for China-market faults, and D for all lamps continuously lit. Read the diagnostic trouble code (DTC) charts and run on-demand tests: several BCMB circuit codes are on-demand only. A nonresponding module requires communications-network diagnosis first.

steps.title: Test the common supply when every lamp is dark
steps.body: In Test A, verify battery junction box fuse 20 (10A). With ignition off and C278 disconnected, check for greater than 11 volts at pin 1. Missing voltage requires fuse or supply-circuit diagnosis. Otherwise, jumper pins 1–4 with a fused lead and switch ignition on. Lamps lighting directs switch replacement. If they remain dark, retain the jumper, switch ignition off, disconnect BCM C2280A and check pin 1. Missing voltage identifies an input-circuit fault; correct voltage leads to BCM checks. Remove the jumper after this measurement.

steps.title: Separate high mounted lamp faults from circuit faults
steps.body: Follow B3–B8 or C3–C8. With supply present, test the lamp ground before replacing the lamp. With supply absent, perform the prescribed self-test/reset and remeasure: restored voltage directs lamp replacement; continued loss requires short-to-ground and continuity checks. For a lamp stuck on, disconnect the lamp and BCM as directed and test for unwanted voltage before assessing the BCM.

steps.title: Follow the non-China rear-lamp branch
steps.body: For one dark segment, B10–B12 check supply, shorts to ground and continuity to the BCMB; correct supply directs rear-assembly replacement. If an entire side is dark, B13–B15 use supply, reset/retest and ground checks. A stuck-on segment follows B9 for a short to voltage. Follow the resulting branch to BCMB connector checks when required.

steps.title: Use the different China-market decisions
steps.body: Test C directs rear-assembly replacement for an individual failed inner or middle stoplamp. When both are dark on one side, C10–C14 distinguish supply loss, driver shutdown, ground failure, shorts and opens. Lamps staying on follow C9's short-to-voltage check. These rear circuits lead to the BCM.

steps.title: Isolate the input when all lamps stay on
steps.body: In Test D, switch ignition off, disconnect C278, then switch ignition on. Lamps extinguishing directs switch replacement. Otherwise, keeping C278 disconnected, switch ignition off and disconnect the powertrain control module (PCM): C1551B for 2.3L, C1381B for 3.7L, or C175B for 5.0L/5.2L. Switch ignition on again. Lamps extinguishing leads to PCM connector checks. If they remain lit, voltage at C278 pin 4 identifies a circuit short to voltage; no voltage leads to BCM checks.

steps.title: Resolve connections before condemning a module
steps.body: At the directed BCM, BCMB or PCM endpoint, inspect connectors for corrosion, bent terminals and pushed-out pins. Renew affected connectors or terminals, clean module pins as directed, reconnect securely and retest. If the concern remains, check Ford OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins and follow them before the prescribed module replacement.

watchFor.title: Jumper fuse failure
watchFor.body: If the jumper fuse fails, investigate the circuit short using the wiring diagram before continuing.

watchFor.title: A fault disappears after reconnection
watchFor.body: Find and correct the underlying terminal or connector problem; restored operation alone does not explain its cause.

notes: The linked high mounted stoplamp replacement procedure applies specifically to coupe vehicles.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code C0040:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detected a short to voltage on the stoplamp-switch input during its on-demand self-test.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test D to distinguish the switch, wiring, PCM and BCM.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U1000:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive current has temporarily disabled a module output.
diagnostics.next: Address other DTCs and correct the cause, then clear codes and repeat the self-test to enable the output.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3000:49 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: An excessive-current fault has permanently disabled a module output.
diagnostics.next: Correct the cause first and follow bulletin checks before replacement. For the non-China rear-segment branch through B11/B16, the affected controller is the BCMB.

verification.title: Confirm lamp operation
verification.body: Check all rear segments and the high mounted lamp with the pedal applied and released. Confirm the original fault is gone.

verification.title: Record the final result
verification.body: Record the repaired circuit or component, lamp behavior and required repeat self-test results, including whether driver-protection codes return.

guides.title: Diagnose turn signals and hazard lamps that fail or stay on
guides.summary: Separate switch, lamp, wiring and control-module faults using the correct market and equipment branch.
guides.introduction: Turn signals communicate direction; hazards flash all turn lamps together. The steering column control module (SCCM) reads the stalk, while the body control module (BCM) coordinates lamp operation. Rear light-emitting diode (LED) assemblies also return an outage signal. Diagnosis separates the driver's request, the lamp's electrical supply and that feedback before choosing a repair.
guides.why: A dark lamp can result from a missing command, damaged wiring or a protective output shutdown. Replacing a module before correcting excessive current can damage its replacement.

when.summary: When turn signals or hazards fail, remain on, flash rapidly, or produce related diagnostic trouble codes.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable diagnostic scan tool, a voltage/resistance meter and the applicable connector information. These tests require Ford diagnostic-method knowledge and controlled live measurements.

prepare.title: Identify the fitted configuration
prepare.detail: Confirm market, memory seats and indicator locations. Follow each test's ignition, hazard-switch and disconnection instructions; resistance checks require the specified isolated, ignition-off circuit.

steps.title: Classify the complaint and read the codes
steps.body: Observe left, right and hazard operation, including whether lamps extinguish. Record diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) by module. Distinguish ground-short reports from battery-short/open reports using the DTC chart. Rear stop/turn segment codes go to Stoplamps diagnosis; unrelated codes go to their module-specific diagnosis. Resolve scan-tool communication failures through Communications Network testing.

steps.title: Test A: check a failed or continuously active turn function
steps.body: With ignition on, compare the SCCM's left and right switch-input data with stalk position. Matching inputs lead to BCM connector checks. Incorrect inputs direct replacement of the left multifunction switch; test operation afterward. If the concern remains, follow the SCCM connector and module decision.

steps.title: Tests B and C: isolate an individual lamp fault
steps.body: Use B outside China and C for China. For front, mirror and applicable hood lamps that stay on, disconnect the specified controller output: continued illumination identifies a short to voltage. For unlit lamps, follow the flashing-supply, output-reset and ground branches before choosing lamp replacement or circuit repair. Memory-seat mirror circuits use the driver door module (DDM) or passenger door module (PDM); other listed mirror/hood branches use the BCM.

steps.title: Apply the distinct rear-lamp branches
steps.body: Outside China, a rear lamp staying on, or failing alongside its stoplamp, requires Stoplamps diagnosis. If its stoplamp works, B checks the outage circuit before the Body Control Module B (BCMB) endpoint. For China, one or two failed turn elements within a rear assembly direct assembly replacement; all three failing require BCM supply and ground checks. Continuously lit China rear lamps follow the BCM supply-isolation branch.

steps.title: Test D: diagnose hazards that fail or stay on
steps.body: Run the BCM self-test. If B1D35:11 is recorded, disconnect the front controls interface module (FCIM), clear codes and repeat the test. A returning code leads to a short-to-ground check; a cleared code leads to continuity testing. Without that code initially, check the hazard-switch voltage signal: greater than 11 volts leads to FCIM connector checks; lower voltage leads to continuity testing and the BCM decision.

steps.title: Test E: trace rear-lamp feedback faults
steps.body: B1265:23 and B1266:23 report left and right feedback stuck low, associated with an open or ground short. B1265:24 and B1266:24 report feedback stuck high, associated with a voltage short. Follow E's checks for voltage short, ground short and continuity in that order. Passing circuits direct rear-assembly replacement, code clearing and a BCMB self-test. A returning code leads to E4's BCMB checks.

steps.title: Complete the directed connector and module decision
steps.body: At module-check endpoints, replace corroded connectors or terminals, clean module pins and renew damaged or pushed-out terminals as directed. Reconnect securely and retest. Persistent faults require checking applicable technical service bulletins before the directed replacement. BCM and FCIM endpoints requiring a vehicle identification number (VIN) must continue through their guided routines.

watchFor.title: Normal hazard timing can conceal an outage
watchFor.body: A front or rear outage causes faster turn flashing, but hazards retain their normal timing. Inspect every lamp.

notes: China rear turn-lamp power comes from the BCM, while outage feedback goes to BCMB. The China/Europe wiring identifies left C412 pin 5 to C4368A pin 8, and right C415 pin 5 to C4368A pin 20.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U1000:00 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The reporting BCM or BCMB has temporarily disabled an output because of excessive current.
diagnostics.next: Address other DTCs and correct the cause first; then clear codes and repeat the self-test to enable the output.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3000:49 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: Excessive current has caused permanent output-driver shutdown.
diagnostics.next: Correct the excessive-current fault before replacement. Follow the VIN-dependent BCM routine or the directed BCMB replacement procedure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1D36:09 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The SCCM reports a turn-indicator switch component failure.
diagnostics.next: Replace the left multifunction switch, clear codes and run the SCCM self-test. Replace the SCCM only if this DTC returns.

verification.title: Confirm operation
verification.body: Retest left, right and hazard operation after the directed repair. Confirm the original failed or continuously illuminated lamp now responds correctly.

verification.title: Record the outcome
verification.body: Record the repaired circuit or component, observed lamp operation and relevant repeated self-test results. A returning feedback code requires continuing Test E, not declaring completion.

guides.title: Check front fog-lamp vertical aim
guides.summary: Check the top of each fog lamp's bright zone against a target 101.6 mm (4 in) below lamp-center height at approximately 7.6 m.
guides.introduction: Front fog-lamp aim determines where the bright part of the beam falls relative to the vehicle. This job establishes the vehicle's test position and checks that beam height on a wall or screen. It ends with a visual aim finding; mechanical adjustment is a separate task.
guides.why: Tire inflation, vehicle load and ground slope affect the lamp's position relative to the screen. Clean lenses make the bright zone easier to identify. Controlling these conditions helps distinguish an actual aim concern from a misleading setup.
searchTerms: front fog lamp aim too high
front fog lamp aim too low

when.summary: When front fog-lamp beam height needs checking or the lamps appear incorrectly aimed.
notes: Consult the state vehicle inspection center for recommended visual-aim tolerance ranges.

prepare.title: Provide a suitable checking area
prepare.detail: Use level ground facing a vertical wall or screen, with a means of measuring vehicle distance, lamp-center height and vertical beam position.

prepare.title: Establish the specified vehicle condition
prepare.detail: Check tire inflation. Remove other loads and leave a half tank of fuel. Clean fog lamps and headlamps; confirm the headlamps operate and are correctly aimed.

steps.title: Position the vehicle
steps.body: Park on the level surface approximately 7.6 m from the vertical wall or screen directly ahead. Establish this distance before assessing the beam.

steps.title: Establish the height references
steps.body: Identify fog-lamp center height on the screen and use the vehicle centerline as the diagram's orientation reference. The target for the top of the high-intensity zone is 101.6 mm (4 in) below the lamp-center height.

steps.title: Illuminate the front fog lamps
steps.body: Place ignition in RUN, turn the parking lamps on and keep high beams off. Operate the front fog-lamp switch integrated into the headlamp switch; these are the conditions that permit front fog-lamp operation.

steps.title: Compare the bright-zone upper edge
steps.body: Follow the [visual aim check](#/document/G1694166), comparing the top edge of each high-intensity zone with the target. Use the bright zone's upper edge rather than its center or lower edge. Horizontal aim is neither required nor adjustable.

watchFor.title: A setup that changes the result
watchFor.body: Incorrect inflation, extra load, sloping ground or dirty lenses make the comparison unreliable. Correct these conditions before judging aim.

notes: This check establishes beam position. It does not provide a mechanical adjustment method.

diagnostics.finding: The upper edge of a fog lamp's high-intensity zone differs from the target.
diagnostics.meaning: The observed vertical aim differs from the specified reference position.
diagnostics.next: Recheck setup and assess the difference against the recommended local tolerance. If correction is needed, continue with the applicable adjustment procedure.

verification.title: Record the visual result
verification.body: Record the test distance, setup condition and each lamp's upper-edge position relative to the target, including any remaining need for correction.

procedures.purpose: Vehicle setup and front fog-lamp visual vertical-aim check.
Front fog-lamp switch location and required operating conditions.

guides.title: Adjust vertical headlamp aim using the VOL or VOR cutoff
guides.summary: Set each low-beam cutoff against a measured screen reference using the aiming rule marked on its headlamp lens.
guides.introduction: The low-beam pattern has a boundary between its bright and dark areas called the cutoff. Vertical adjustment positions that boundary relative to the road. The headlamp system uses a dual-beam high-intensity discharge arrangement, but this aiming procedure works from the low-beam pattern and the lens identification. It adjusts aim; it does not diagnose a lamp that fails to illuminate.
guides.why: Vehicle height, loading and tire inflation all affect where the beam lands. The reference line also changes with headlamp optical-center height. Finally, Visually Optically Aligned Left (VOL) and Visually Optically Aligned Right (VOR) headlamps use different portions of the cutoff and different target positions. Ignoring any of these distinctions can produce an incorrect adjustment.

when.summary: When functioning low beams need their vertical aim checked or corrected.
notes: Horizontal aim is not adjustable.
Use the applicable vehicle-inspection guidance for visual-aim tolerance ranges.

prepare.title: Arrange a suitable aiming area
prepare.detail: Use level ground facing a vertical wall or screen at least 2.4 m wide, with space to park approximately 7.6 m away. Work in darkness so the cutoff is clearly visible.

prepare.title: Gather measuring and adjustment equipment
prepare.detail: Have a measuring tool, a 2.4 m length of masking tape, a way to cover one headlamp, and the appropriate adjuster tool. Locate the adjustment screw using the owner's literature.

steps.title: Identify the lens marking
steps.body: Look for VOL and SAE or VOR and SAE molded into each lens. These markings determine which cutoff edge to use; they do not simply identify the left or right side of the vehicle.

steps.title: Establish the vehicle conditions
steps.body: Correct the tire pressures, use the vehicle's normal loading, clean the headlamps and confirm that they operate correctly. Park on level ground approximately 7.6 m from the wall directly ahead. If air suspension is fitted, its switch must be on.

steps.title: Measure and mark the reference height
steps.body: Identify the low-beam optical center, using its lens marking where provided or the applicable reflector, bulb, LED shield or projector inner-lens center. Measure its height above the ground and record it. Below 95 cm, place the tape reference at that height. From 95–105 cm, place it 1.3 cm lower. Above 105 cm, place it 2.5 cm lower.

steps.title: Find the actual cutoff
steps.body: Switch on the low beams and open the hood. Locate the horizontal boundary with the greatest change between light and dark. Use this cutoff rather than the center of the brightest patch; beam-pattern appearance can vary.

steps.title: Adjust the first headlamp
steps.body: Cover the other headlamp. For VOR, align the distinct cutoff on the right portion of the pattern with the horizontal reference line. For VOL, position the distinct left-side cutoff edge 5 cm below that line. Turn the adjustment screw as needed, preserving the applicable height correction already built into the reference line.

steps.title: Adjust the remaining headlamp
steps.body: Swap the cover and repeat the appropriate VOL or VOR adjustment for the other lamp. Each marking's rule applies to either side of the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Two overlapping patterns
watchFor.body: Covering the opposite lamp is necessary to identify the cutoff of the lamp being adjusted.

watchFor.title: Applying the VOR target to a VOL lamp
watchFor.body: A VOL cutoff belongs below the reference line; placing it directly on the line loses its required offset.

notes: The air-suspension condition applies only where that equipment is actually fitted.

diagnostics.finding: A headlamp does not operate correctly.
diagnostics.meaning: The entry conditions for visual aiming have not been met.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the operating concern before adjusting aim.

verification.title: Confirm both cutoff positions
verification.body: Check each lamp separately against its correct target with the vehicle still under the original setup conditions.

verification.title: Retain the measured result
verification.body: Record the optical-center measurement, resulting reference height and VOL or VOR marking so the completed adjustment has a clear measured basis.

procedures.purpose: Complete vertical headlamp aiming procedure, including setup, height corrections and separate VOL/VOR targets.

guides.title: Replace an HID headlamp ballast
guides.summary: Remove the headlamp assembly, replace its ballast, and reinstall the lamp with its aim adjusted.
guides.introduction: The ballast supplies the electrical power needed by the high intensity discharge (HID) headlamp bulb. It is a separate component attached to the headlamp assembly. Replacement involves removing the front bumper cover and headlamp first, then disconnecting the ballast once its mounting screws have been removed.
guides.why: Most of this job concerns access and careful handling. Moving the headlamp and ballast exposes their electrical connectors, but neither component should be pulled away while still connected. Headlamp adjustment completes the work because the assembly has been removed from its mounting position.

when.summary: When the ballast has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: A headlamp fault alone does not establish ballast failure; the system also includes a replaceable bulb, switches and control modules.

prepare.title: Plan the access work
prepare.detail: Have the front bumper cover removal procedure available. Removing the headlamp is a prerequisite, so allow for body-panel access as well as the electrical component work.

prepare.title: Prepare fastening and handling equipment
prepare.detail: Use tools suitable for the headlamp and ballast screws, plus a torque wrench appropriate for the headlamp mounting fasteners. Be ready to support the assembly while disconnecting it.

steps.title: Remove the headlamp assembly
steps.body: Follow [Headlamp Assembly](#/document/G1694118): remove the front bumper cover, remove the lamp mounting screws and position the lamp forward. Disconnect its electrical connector before removing the assembly.

steps.title: Expose the ballast connector
steps.body: Follow [Ballast removal and installation](#/document/G1794146). Remove the ballast screws and reposition the ballast for connector access, keeping the connected wiring free of strain.

steps.title: Separate and replace the ballast
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector and remove the ballast. Install the replacement by reversing these operations: reconnect it, return it to its mounting position and reinstall its screws.

steps.title: Restore the headlamp and bumper
steps.body: Reverse the headlamp removal sequence, reconnecting the lamp and securing the assembly. Use the distinct front and side mounting torque specifications in the headlamp procedure. Refit the bumper cover and perform Headlamp Adjustment.

watchFor.title: Wiring carrying the component's weight
watchFor.body: Support the headlamp and ballast as they are moved for connector access; disconnect each before taking it away.

watchFor.title: Mixed mounting specifications
watchFor.body: The headlamp front and side mounting fasteners have different tightening requirements.

notes: The ballast replacement sequence contains no separate programming or initialization step.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly
verification.body: Check that the ballast and headlamp connectors are reconnected and that the ballast, headlamp and bumper cover are secured.

verification.title: Complete headlamp adjustment
verification.body: Perform the adjustment required after headlamp installation and record its completion.

procedures.purpose: Ballast removal and installation after the headlamp assembly has been removed.
Headlamp removal and installation, including bumper-cover access, mounting specifications and the final headlamp-adjustment requirement.

guides.title: Replace a halogen front fog lamp bulb
guides.summary: Replace the halogen bulb through the front wheel-arch access, then restore the liner and wheels and check lamp operation.
guides.introduction: The front fog lamps are operated through the fog lamp switch integrated into the headlamp switch and the body control module (BCM). A halogen lamp has a separately removable bulb at the rear of its housing. Access for this job requires a hoist, front wheel removal and moving the inner fender liner aside.
guides.why: Confirming the lamp type prevents applying the bulb procedure to a light-emitting diode (LED) assembly. Correct operating conditions also matter: a fog lamp that is not enabled by the lighting controls can appear inoperative even when its bulb is serviceable.
searchTerms: halogen front fog lamp bulb replacement
fog lamp bulb wheel arch access

when.summary: When a halogen front fog lamp bulb requires replacement.
notes: LED fog lamps are serviced as assemblies; this bulb-removal procedure does not apply to them.

prepare.title: Arrange safe access
prepare.detail: Use a correctly positioned vehicle hoist and the equipment required by the wheel-and-tire procedure. Identify the marked lifting points and check hoist-adapter clearance.

prepare.title: Identify the fitted lamp
prepare.detail: Confirm that the vehicle has a halogen fog lamp before obtaining the replacement bulb and beginning removal.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle and remove the front wheels
steps.body: Follow [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631), then remove the front wheels and tires using the [Wheel and Tire procedure](#/document/G1686507). This provides access to the inner fender liners.

steps.title: Expose the rear of the lamp
steps.body: Remove the push pins and position the inner fender liner aside. Keep the liner clear so the electrical connector and bulb can be reached.

steps.title: Remove the bulb
steps.body: Disconnect the front fog lamp electrical connector. Turn the bulb counterclockwise and remove it from the housing, as shown in the illustration.

steps.title: Install and restore the access area
steps.body: Reverse removal: fit and secure the replacement bulb, reconnect the electrical connector, reposition the liner and install its push pins. Refit the front wheels and tires using their complete installation procedure.

watchFor.title: Unsuitable lifting support
watchFor.body: Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. The vehicle’s emergency jack is not intended for this hoisting job.

notes: Where daytime running lamps are fitted, that system also uses the fog lamp assemblies.

diagnostics.finding: The fog lamp does not illuminate during a check.
diagnostics.meaning: The operating conditions may not be satisfied; darkness alone does not prove bulb failure.
diagnostics.next: Check with the ignition in RUN, parking lamps on and high beams off, then operate the fog lamp switch.

verification.title: Check assembly and lighting
verification.body: Confirm that the connector, liner, push pins and wheels are restored. Check fog lamp operation under the specified enabling conditions.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install a halogen front fog lamp bulb.
Identify lifting points and safe hoist positioning.
Remove and reinstall the front wheels and tires.
Establish the front fog lamp operating conditions used for the functional check.

guides.title: Replace and adjust a front fog lamp assembly
guides.summary: Replace the front fog lamp through the lower air-deflector opening, restore its connections and complete the required lamp adjustment.
guides.introduction: The front fog lamps provide an additional forward lighting function controlled through the headlamp switch and Body Control Module (BCM). On vehicles equipped with daytime running lamps, these assemblies also provide that lighting function. This job replaces the complete fog lamp assembly and finishes with adjustment of the lamps.
guides.why: Removing the lower air deflector exposes the lamp’s connector and mounting screws. Disconnecting the wiring before withdrawing the assembly keeps the harness from being pulled with it. Correct installation includes both the specified screw torque and the separate adjustment procedure, because a securely mounted lamp still needs the correct aim.

when.summary: When inspection or diagnosis establishes that a front fog lamp assembly needs replacement.
notes: The removal illustration shows a halogen lamp; the light-emitting diode (LED) lamp procedure is similar.
Plan lamp adjustment as part of replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and lower access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist at the designated lifting points. Check hoist adapters for interference with nearby components and never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare for removal and adjustment
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the air-deflector push pins, screws and lamp screws, plus a torque tool suitable for the specified fasteners. Have the linked fog lamp adjustment procedure available.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle
steps.body: Lift the vehicle according to the jacking and lifting procedure. Locate the approved points by their stamped triangle markings; the bumper is not a lifting point.

steps.title: Remove the lower air deflector
steps.body: Remove its push pins and screws, then remove the deflector. This opens the access route used by the lamp procedure and exposes the electrical connection behind the assembly.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the lamp
steps.body: Disconnect the front fog lamp electrical connector. Remove the lamp mounting screws and withdraw the assembly. Follow the illustrated halogen arrangement or the similar LED arrangement as fitted.

steps.title: Install the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Secure the fog lamp with its screws tightened to 15 lb.in (1.7 Nm), reconnect the electrical connector and reinstall the lower air deflector with its screws and push pins.

steps.title: Adjust the fog lamps
steps.body: Carry out the linked Front Fog Lamp Adjustment procedure after installation. Use its setup and aiming instructions to complete the repair.

watchFor.title: Incorrect operating conditions
watchFor.body: For fog lamp operation, the ignition must be in RUN, the parking lamps on and the high beams off.

watchFor.title: Adjustment omitted
watchFor.body: Replacing the assembly does not complete the job until the required fog lamp adjustment has been performed.

notes: This procedure concerns the front assemblies; the separate rear fog lamp system is outside this job.

diagnostics.finding: A fog lamp is being checked with the high beams on.
diagnostics.meaning: The stated conditions for front fog lamp operation are not satisfied.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the operating check with the correct lighting and ignition conditions before judging the assembly.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly and operation
verification.body: Check the connector, lamp mounting screws and air-deflector attachments. Check fog lamp operation under the stated enabling conditions.

verification.title: Record adjustment completion
verification.body: Confirm and record completion of the linked fog lamp adjustment procedure.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the front fog lamp assembly through lower air-deflector access.
Use the approved vehicle lifting points and hoist precautions.
Adjust the front fog lamps after assembly replacement.

applicability.equipment: Front fog lamps, halogen or LED

guides.title: Remove and replace the front marker lamp
guides.summary: Remove the front bumper cover and grille cover to replace the marker lamp, then verify its integrated lighting functions.
guides.introduction: The front marker lamp assembly contains the front parking lamp, front side marker and front turn lamp. Replacing the assembly therefore concerns several lighting functions at the same mounting location. Access requires removal of the front bumper cover, followed by the front bumper grille cover before the marker lamp's mounting screws can be removed.
guides.why: The grille cover uses both screws and retaining tabs, so removing its screws alone does not release it. Working through the bumper and grille-cover sequence exposes these attachments in order. The bumper's fender bracket teeth also need inspection because they help retain the cover when it is reinstalled.

when.summary: When the front marker assembly requires replacement or removal for an established repair.
notes: A missing parking, marker or turn function identifies the complaint but does not alone prove the complete assembly has failed.
Vehicles with a fog lamp are illustrated; the procedure is similar without one.

prepare.title: Plan front bumper access
prepare.detail: Arrange a hoist and the capability to remove the front wheels using the lifting and wheel procedures referenced in the bumper-cover instructions.

prepare.title: Prepare for mixed attachments
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for push pins, screws and bolts, and torque control for the low-torque lamp and grille-cover screws.

steps.title: Expose the bumper-cover attachments
steps.body: Follow the front bumper procedure: raise the vehicle, remove the front wheels and lower air deflector, and release the specified push pins on both sides. Position the inner fender liners aside, disconnect the electrical connectors and separate the cover from the fender brackets.

steps.title: Remove the front bumper cover
steps.body: Remove the radiator sight shield and, if fitted, the license plate bracket. Move the outer hood-seal edges aside to reach the bolts. Remove the remaining cover screws, lift the cover off its alignment pins and pull it forward. Inspect the fender bracket teeth and address damage through the bumper procedure.

steps.title: Remove the front bumper grille cover
steps.body: Remove its screws, release the tabs and then remove the grille cover. Both attachment types must be released before the cover comes away.

steps.title: Remove the marker lamp
steps.body: Identify the marker assembly using the lamp illustration, then remove its mounting screws and lift out the assembly. The adjacent fog lamp shown in the illustration does not add a fog-lamp removal step.

steps.title: Reassemble in reverse order
steps.body: Install the marker lamp, then refit the grille cover with its tabs and screws. Both sets of screws use 1.7 Nm. Reinstall the bumper cover using its own fastening specifications and restore the electrical connections, liners, lower air deflector and wheels.

watchFor.title: Tabs still engaged
watchFor.body: Release the grille-cover tabs after removing the screws rather than trying to pull the retained cover away.

watchFor.title: Different bumper fasteners
watchFor.body: Use the bumper procedure's individual torque settings when reinstalling the cover; the lamp-screw setting does not apply throughout the bumper assembly.

notes: The left-side lamp is shown; the right-side removal and installation sequence is similar.

diagnostics.finding: Only one integrated lighting function is missing
diagnostics.meaning: The assembly houses parking, side-marker and turn functions, so a complaint should identify which function is affected.
diagnostics.next: Establish the electrical repair requirement before replacing the assembly solely because one function is absent.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical installation
verification.body: Check the marker mounting screws, grille-cover tabs and screws, and restored bumper attachments and electrical connections.

verification.title: Check and record the lighting functions
verification.body: Confirm the parking and front side-marker illumination, then check the corresponding turn signal and hazard operation. Record which functions operate after reassembly.

procedures.purpose: Front marker lamp and front bumper grille-cover removal and installation, with or without fog lamps.
Prerequisite front bumper-cover removal and installation, including bracket inspection.
Identify the parking, side-marker and turn functions integrated into the front marker assembly.

guides.title: Replace a front turn signal bulb through the wheel opening
guides.summary: Access the front turn signal from behind the inner fender liner, remove its bulb holder and replace the bulb.
guides.introduction: The front turn signal is integrated into the front marker lamp assembly. It flashes with the corresponding direction request, and it also participates in hazard-warning operation. This repair reaches the removable bulb through the front wheel opening. The wheel and liner access take more preparation than the bulb exchange itself: the holder must first be released from the lamp, then the bulb separated from the holder.
guides.why: Correct lifting and wheel handling are essential because access begins underneath and beside the raised vehicle. At the lamp, separating the connector, holder and bulb in the stated order prevents confusion between the electrical connection and the holder's retaining action.

when.summary: When diagnosis justifies replacing a front turn signal bulb that does not illuminate.
notes: A lamp that does not flash is a complaint to investigate, not proof that the bulb has failed.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting capability
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and follow [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631). Identify the designated lifting points by the stamped triangles and position adapters clear of vulnerable surrounding components.

prepare.title: Prepare for wheel and liner access
prepare.detail: Have the wheel-removal equipment and [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507) procedure available, along with suitable means to release and reinstall the liner push pins.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle correctly
steps.body: Position and raise the vehicle on a hoist using the linked lifting guidance. Check adapter clearance around suspension, exhaust, steering components and mounting brackets before lifting.

steps.title: Open access through the wheel housing
steps.body: Remove the front wheels and tires using the wheel procedure. Remove the inner-fender push pins and position the liner aside. This exposes the rear of the front turn lamp without adding an unsupported lamp-assembly removal step.

steps.title: Disconnect the lamp wiring
steps.body: Disconnect the front turn signal electrical connector before releasing the bulb holder. Identify the turn-signal connection using the [bulb procedure](#/document/G1694117) and its illustration.

steps.title: Remove the holder, then the bulb
steps.body: Rotate the turn signal bulb holder counterclockwise and withdraw it from the lamp. Once the holder is out, separate the bulb from it. These are distinct actions within the bulb-removal step.

steps.title: Install the replacement bulb and holder
steps.body: Reverse the removal actions: fit the bulb into its holder, return the holder to the lamp and secure it by reversing the release rotation. Reconnect the turn signal electrical connector.

steps.title: Restore the liner and wheels
steps.body: Return the inner fender liner to position and reinstall its push pins. Refit the wheels using the complete wheel-installation procedure, including its fastening requirements, and finish the hoist operation before checking lamp operation.

watchFor.title: Unsuitable vehicle support
watchFor.body: Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. The supplied emergency jack is intended for changing a deflated tire, not this workshop access job.

watchFor.title: Incorrect lifting contact
watchFor.body: Do not apply jack pressure to either bumper. Poorly positioned hoist adapters can also damage underbody, suspension or steering components.

notes: Use the linked wheel procedure for installation specifications; the bulb procedure does not provide wheel-fastening values.

diagnostics.finding: The front turn lamp remains inoperative after the bulb is fitted.
diagnostics.meaning: Replacing the bulb has not resolved the complaint. Turn-signal operation also involves switching, wiring and electronic control.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the disturbed connection and holder are restored, then continue the applicable exterior-lighting diagnosis.

verification.title: Check directional and hazard operation
verification.body: Command the corresponding turn signal and confirm that the front lamp flashes. Check hazard operation, during which all turn lamps should flash.

verification.title: Record the repair result
verification.body: Record whether normal lamp operation returned or the original complaint remains, and confirm that the liner and wheel installation are complete.

procedures.purpose: Provides front turn signal access, connector disconnection, holder rotation, bulb separation and reverse installation.
Provides lifting-point identification, support warnings and hoist-positioning precautions.
Provides removal and installation of the front wheel and tire assemblies required for bulb access.

guides.title: Replace the headlamp assembly and reset its aim
guides.summary: Remove the front bumper cover to exchange the headlamp assembly, then restore the bodywork and adjust the low-beam aim.
guides.introduction: The headlamp assembly holds the optical components that shape and direct the light. The high intensity discharge (HID) system uses a replaceable bulb and a dual-beam pattern, so assembly replacement is a different operation from bulb replacement. Removing the housing requires bumper-cover access, and installation finishes with headlamp adjustment.
guides.why: The front and side mounting fasteners have different tightening requirements. Bumper-cover alignment pins and fender brackets also need careful handling. After refitting, correct aim depends on vehicle loading, tire pressure and the lens's optical marking, not simply whether the lamp illuminates.
searchTerms: front bumper removal for headlamp access

when.summary: When a headlamp assembly requires replacement or removal for access.
notes: A lamp that does not illuminate does not by itself establish that the complete housing needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange bodywork access
prepare.detail: Have hoist access and the capability to remove the front wheels and bumper cover using [Front Bumper Cover](#/document/G1694213), including its lifting and wheel-procedure references.

prepare.title: Prepare fastening and aiming equipment
prepare.detail: Use torque equipment suitable for the small mounting fasteners. Provide level ground, a dark aiming area, measuring equipment, masking tape and a vertical wall or screen at least 2.4 m (8 ft) wide.

steps.title: Clear the lower bumper attachments
steps.body: Raise the vehicle on a hoist and remove the front wheels and tires. Remove the lower air deflector and its fasteners. On both sides, remove the specified push pins, move the inner fender liners aside and disconnect the electrical connectors.

steps.title: Release and remove the bumper cover
steps.body: Detach the cover from the fender brackets on both sides. Remove the radiator sight shield and, if fitted, the license plate bracket. Move the outer hood-seal edges aside and remove the bolts. Remove the remaining cover screws, lift the cover off its alignment pins and pull it forward. Inspect the fender bracket teeth.

steps.title: Remove the headlamp
steps.body: Follow [Headlamp Assembly](#/document/G1694118): remove its mounting screws and move the assembly forward. Disconnect the electrical connector, then remove the assembly from the vehicle.

steps.title: Refit the assembly and bodywork
steps.body: Reverse removal, reconnecting the headlamp and seating it in its mounts. Tighten the front mounting bolts to 74 lb.in (8.4 Nm) and the side mounting bolt to 28 lb.in (3.2 Nm). Restore the bumper cover, connectors, liners, deflector and wheels using their applicable installation details.

steps.title: Establish the aiming conditions
steps.body: Follow [Headlamp Adjustment](#/document/G1694148). The vehicle must be level, normally loaded and correctly tire-inflated; lamps must be clean and operate correctly. Read the lens marking to identify Visually Optically Aligned Left (VOL) or Right (VOR). Use the owner's literature to locate the adjusting screw.

steps.title: Measure and mark the reference
steps.body: Park approximately 7.6 m (25 ft) from the wall or screen. Measure and record the low-beam optical-center height, then position the horizontal reference line using the height-dependent offset in the adjustment procedure. Consult the applicable inspection guidance for visual-aim tolerances.

steps.title: Set each low-beam cutoff
steps.body: In the dark aiming area, switch on the low beams and open the hood. Cover the opposite lamp while adjusting each side. For VOR lamps, align the right-hand cutoff with the reference line. For VOL lamps, position the left-hand cutoff 5 cm (2 in) below it. Repeat for the other lamp; horizontal aim is not adjustable.

watchFor.title: Using the wrong beam feature
watchFor.body: The cutoff is the sharpest light-to-dark boundary. Use the side of the pattern appropriate to the lens marking.

watchFor.title: Incorrect torque units
watchFor.body: The headlamp fastener values are in pound-inches, and the side mounting value differs from the front value.

notes: The reference-line position depends on measured optical-center height; do not assume one height offset applies to every installation.

diagnostics.finding: Fender bracket teeth are damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: The bumper-cover attachment needs attention during reassembly.
diagnostics.next: If required, remove and replace the bracket using the bumper-cover procedure.

verification.title: Confirm operation and aim
verification.body: Confirm correct lamp operation and the appropriate cutoff position for both headlamps.

verification.title: Record the aiming basis
verification.body: Record optical-center height, lens marking and the final aim result.

procedures.purpose: Headlamp assembly removal, electrical disconnection and installation with distinct front and side mounting torques.
Front bumper-cover removal for access, bracket inspection and bodywork reassembly.
Post-installation vertical aiming with height-dependent reference lines and separate VOL/VOR branches.

guides.title: Replace an HID headlamp bulb and adjust the beam
guides.summary: Remove the headlamp assembly, replace its spring-retained HID bulb, then restore the correct vertical beam aim.
guides.introduction: The high-intensity discharge (HID) headlamp uses a replaceable bulb in a dual-beam lighting system. The bulb is retained inside the assembly by spring tabs and protected by a rear cover. This repair requires removal of the headlamp assembly, including front bumper cover access, and finishes with headlamp adjustment.
guides.why: A working replacement bulb does not establish that the beam is correctly aimed. The aiming procedure depends on vehicle loading, tire pressure, measured lamp height and the marking on the lens. Choosing the wrong cutoff reference can leave an otherwise functioning headlamp incorrectly adjusted.

when.summary: When headlamp bulb replacement is justified, with assembly removal and beam adjustment included in the job.
notes: A non-illuminating headlamp is a complaint to investigate, not proof that its bulb has failed.

prepare.title: Plan assembly removal
prepare.detail: Have the equipment and capability for front bumper cover and headlamp assembly removal. Bulb access follows assembly removal and electrical disconnection; this procedure does not call for live electrical testing.

prepare.title: Prepare an aiming area
prepare.detail: Use level ground and a dark environment with a vertical wall or screen at least 2.4 m (8 ft) wide. Have measuring equipment and masking tape for the reference line, plus access to the vertical adjuster.

steps.title: Remove the headlamp assembly
steps.body: Follow [Headlamp Assembly](#/document/G1694118), including its front bumper cover prerequisite. Remove the mounting screws, move the assembly forward, disconnect its electrical connector and remove the assembly.

steps.title: Release the bulb
steps.body: Follow [Headlamp Bulb](#/document/G1694119): remove the bulb cover and disconnect the bulb connector. Release the spring tabs before withdrawing the bulb. The retaining springs must be released rather than overcome by pulling on the bulb.

steps.title: Install the bulb and assembly
steps.body: Reverse the bulb-removal sequence, restoring the spring retention, connector and cover. Reinstall the headlamp and bumper cover through the assembly procedure. Use the appropriate mounting specification: the front and side headlamp fasteners have different torques.

steps.title: Establish the aiming reference
steps.body: Identify Visually Optically Aligned Left (VOL) or Visually Optically Aligned Right (VOR) markings on the lens. With correct tire pressures, normal vehicle loading and clean, functioning lamps, position the vehicle approximately 7.6 m (25 ft) from the screen. Measure and record the low-beam optical-center height, then use the height-dependent reference-line instructions in [Headlamp Adjustment](#/document/G1694148).

steps.title: Adjust each low-beam cutoff
steps.body: Turn on the low beams and open the hood. Cover one headlamp while adjusting the other. For VOR lamps, align the distinct right-side cutoff with the reference line. For VOL lamps, position the left-side cutoff 5 cm (2 in) below that line. Repeat for the remaining lamp; horizontal aim is not adjustable.

watchFor.title: Wrong aiming branch
watchFor.body: Use the lens marking to choose the VOL or VOR procedure; their cutoff positions differ.

watchFor.title: Unreliable setup
watchFor.body: Incorrect loading, tire inflation or an unlevel surface changes the beam reference and undermines the adjustment.

notes: Use the owner's information to locate the adjustment screw and the applicable inspection guidance for aiming tolerances.

diagnostics.finding: The headlamp does not illuminate.
diagnostics.meaning: The system includes a bulb, ballast, connections and controls; the symptom alone does not isolate the bulb.
diagnostics.next: Establish the need for bulb replacement before selecting a part.

diagnostics.finding: The lamp operates but its cutoff misses the specified position.
diagnostics.meaning: Illumination is present, but vertical adjustment remains necessary.
diagnostics.next: Check the setup and adjust using the lens-specific branch.

verification.title: Confirm operating lamps and aim
verification.body: Ensure the lamps operate correctly and both low-beam cutoffs meet their respective aiming references.

verification.title: Retain the measured height
verification.body: Record the headlamp optical-center-to-ground measurement used to establish the reference line.

procedures.purpose: Headlamp bulb removal and installation through the cover, electrical connector and spring retainers.
Headlamp assembly removal and installation, including bumper-cover access and mounting requirements.
Post-installation vertical aiming, including entry conditions, height-dependent reference lines and VOL/VOR branches.

guides.title: Replace the dashboard headlamp switch
guides.summary: Remove the left-hand dashboard trim, disconnect and release the headlamp switch, then reinstall the switch and finish panels.
guides.introduction: The headlamp switch provides the driver's lighting selections to a system that also includes the body control module, lamp assemblies and other controls. It incorporates the front fog-lamp switch and participates in automatic lighting control. This job replaces the dashboard switch assembly through the left-hand finish panel; it does not involve removing the headlamps themselves.
guides.why: The switch is retained by tabs behind the panel, so gaining access before releasing it protects the surrounding trim. Lighting behavior also depends on operating conditions and other components. A lamp that stays off, or remains on after shutdown, does not by itself establish that the dashboard switch is faulty.
searchTerms: front fog lamps will not turn on
autolamps stay on after ignition off

when.summary: When the headlamp switch requires replacement after the lighting complaint has been assessed.
notes: Check the operating conditions for the affected lighting function before condemning the switch.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim access
prepare.detail: Use a non-marring trim tool and a suitable tool for the finish-panel screw. Be able to support the panel while accessing the switch connector and retaining tabs.

steps.title: Remove the access trim
steps.body: Use the non-marring tool to remove the trim panel. This exposes the finish-panel attachment without relying on a metal edge against the visible trim.

steps.title: Move the finish panel aside
steps.body: Remove its screw and position the left-hand dash finish panel aside. Create enough access to handle the connector and switch retainers directly.

steps.title: Disconnect and release the switch
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector first. Release the retaining tabs shown in the illustration, then remove the switch from the panel. Follow this order so the wiring does not restrain the switch during removal.

steps.title: Install the switch and restore the panel
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: seat and retain the switch, reconnect its electrical connector, restore the finish panel and screw, and reinstall the trim. Confirm that the tabs have secured the switch before closing access.

watchFor.title: Switch still caught in its opening
watchFor.body: Check the retaining tabs rather than forcing the switch against the panel.

notes: China-market rear fog-lamp controls are a separate equipment branch; their operation should not be assumed for every switch.

diagnostics.finding: Front fog lamps do not illuminate
diagnostics.meaning: Their stated operating conditions require ignition in RUN, parking lamps on and high beams off.
diagnostics.next: Establish those conditions before interpreting the result as a fault.

diagnostics.finding: Exterior lamps remain on after ignition shutdown in autolamp operation
diagnostics.meaning: The system includes an adjustable delayed switch-off function.
diagnostics.next: Check the selected delay before treating continued illumination as a failed switch.

verification.title: Confirm installation
verification.body: Check that the switch is retained, its connector is connected and both panels are restored.

verification.title: Assess the affected lighting function
verification.body: Operate the relevant control under its stated conditions, accounting for fog-lamp restrictions and the autolamp delay.

procedures.purpose: Headlamp switch removal and installation through the left-hand dash finish panel.

guides.title: Replace the coupe high-mounted stoplamp
guides.summary: Lower the rear headliner, release the stoplamp and its sealing tape, prepare the mating surface and reinstall the lamp.
guides.introduction: The high-mounted stoplamp provides a brake indication high at the rear of the coupe. Applying the brake pedal supplies voltage to this lamp and the rear stoplamps. The assembly is retained by nuts, tabs and two-sided sealing tape, with its electrical connection reached after lowering the rear of the headliner. Replacing it therefore includes restoring both the lamp attachment and the sealed mating surface.
guides.why: Removing the nuts does not release every attachment: the tabs and sealing tape must also be freed. During installation, adhesive residue can interfere with the tape connection, so surface cleaning and alcohol preparation are separate required operations. The small retaining-nut torque also matters; secure installation depends on the specified fastening and sealing sequence.

when.summary: When the coupe high-mounted stoplamp needs removal or replacement after the fault has been established.
notes: A lamp that does not illuminate needs diagnosis; that symptom alone does not prove the lamp assembly has failed.

prepare.title: Arrange headliner access
prepare.detail: Have the Headliner - Lowering procedure from Interior Trim and Ornamentation available. Only the rear of the headliner is specified for lowering in this operation.

prepare.title: Prepare fastening and sealing equipment
prepare.detail: Provide suitable nut-removal tools, a torque wrench for the stated low tightening torque, 3M Specialty Adhesive Remover and an alcohol pad. Establish the appropriate sealing-tape provision for the lamp before dismantling.

steps.title: Lower the rear of the headliner
steps.body: Follow Headliner - Lowering to expose the stoplamp attachments and wiring. Use that procedure for the trim-access details rather than pulling the headliner down around remaining attachments.

steps.title: Release the mechanical and electrical attachments
steps.body: Following the [stoplamp procedure](#/document/G1694146), remove the retaining nuts, disconnect the electrical connector and release the tabs. Keep the sealing tape in mind: the lamp remains attached until that bond is released.

steps.title: Release the sealing tape and remove the lamp
steps.body: Release the two-sided seal tape and remove the assembly. The illustration shows the lamp lifting away once the internal attachments and tape have been released.

steps.title: Clean and prepare the mating surface
steps.body: Use 3M Specialty Adhesive Remover to clean the mating surface. Then prepare it with an alcohol pad. Preserve this order so the sealing connection is restored against a prepared surface.

steps.title: Refit the lamp and restore the headliner
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, restoring the two-sided sealing-tape connection, engaging the tabs and reconnecting the electrical connector. Install the retaining nuts and tighten them to 36 lb.in (4.1 Nm). Complete restoration of the headliner through its access procedure.

watchFor.title: An assembly still bonded in place
watchFor.body: Do not assume the lamp is free after removing its nuts. Tabs and sealing tape are separate retaining features.

watchFor.title: Incomplete surface preparation
watchFor.body: Adhesive-remover cleaning and alcohol-pad preparation are both required before reinstallation.

notes: The sealing tape is part of the installation; reconnecting the wiring and tightening the nuts alone does not finish the job.

diagnostics.finding: The high-mounted stoplamp does not illuminate when the brake pedal is applied.
diagnostics.meaning: Expected stoplamp operation is absent, but the symptom does not distinguish a lamp fault from a problem in its electrical supply or connection.
diagnostics.next: Establish the fault before replacing the assembly; this removal procedure does not provide electrical pinpoint tests.

verification.title: Check stoplamp operation
verification.body: Apply the brake pedal and confirm that the high-mounted stoplamp illuminates, consistent with the described stoplamp operation.

verification.title: Check installation completion
verification.body: Confirm that the tabs, electrical connector, sealing-tape connection and retaining nuts have been restored and that the headliner access work is complete.

procedures.purpose: Coupe high-mounted stoplamp removal, sealing-surface preparation and installation.
Stoplamp operating description supporting the brake-pedal functional check.

guides.title: Replace a hood-mounted turn signal lamp
guides.summary: Access the hood indicator beneath the insulation panel, release its connector and retainers, and reinstall the lamp securely.
guides.introduction: On vehicles with hood turn signals, these lamps provide an additional flashing indication of the selected turn direction. This equipment is used without exterior-mirror turn signals. The lamp is reached from beneath the hood after removing the insulation panel. Its electrical connector, screws and retaining tabs must all be released to remove the assembly.
guides.why: The screws and tabs secure the lamp in different ways. Removing only the screws leaves the tabs engaged, so pulling on the lamp can damage its mounting. Disconnecting the wiring before extracting the assembly also keeps removal force away from the connector and harness. An unlit lamp warrants diagnosis before assuming the lamp itself has failed.

when.summary: When a hood turn signal lamp needs replacement or removal for access.
notes: The illustrated procedure shows the left-hand lamp; the right-hand operation is similar.

prepare.title: Expose the underside of the hood
prepare.detail: Arrange access to the insulation-panel pushpins and the lamp mounting area. Have suitable tools for releasing the pushpins and removing the lamp screws.

prepare.title: Identify the affected side
prepare.detail: Confirm which lamp requires work and whether the vehicle has the hood-mounted indicator equipment described here.

steps.title: Remove the insulation panel
steps.body: Remove the hood-insulation pushpins and take down the panel. This exposes the lamp's connector and mechanical retainers so they can be released directly.

steps.title: Disconnect and release the lamp
steps.body: Disconnect the hood-lamp electrical connector, remove the screws, then release the retaining tabs. The illustration in the [lamp removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1794149) identifies these separate attachments. Remove the lamp once they are free.

steps.title: Install the lamp
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: position the lamp, engage its tabs, install the screws and reconnect the electrical connector. Check that the lamp is seated before covering the mounting area.

steps.title: Restore the hood insulation
steps.body: Reinstall the insulation panel and its pushpins. Confirm that the panel is retained and that the lamp connection remains undisturbed.

watchFor.title: A lamp that remains attached
watchFor.body: Check for engaged tabs after the screws are removed. Do not use the wiring to pull the assembly free.

notes: This operation removes the lamp assembly; no separate bulb replacement operation is specified.

diagnostics.finding: A hood indicator does not flash.
diagnostics.meaning: The turn-signal system also includes wiring, switches and control modules, so this observation alone does not identify a failed lamp.
diagnostics.next: Establish the cause before choosing replacement; use this procedure when lamp removal is required.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical retention
verification.body: Check that the lamp tabs, screws, connector and insulation pushpins have all been restored.

verification.title: Check the lighting functions
verification.body: Operate the corresponding turn signal and the hazard function. The selected side should flash with the turn command, and all turn lamps should flash with hazards. Record whether the original complaint remains.

procedures.purpose: Remove and reinstall either hood-mounted turn signal lamp; the left-hand side is illustrated.
Explain hood-lamp equipment applicability and normal turn-signal and hazard operation.

applicability.equipment: Hood-mounted turn signal lamps, without exterior-mirror turn signals

guides.title: Replace the autolamp light sensor
guides.summary: Release the light sensor with a non-marring tool, disconnect it and install its replacement in reverse order.
guides.introduction: The light sensor provides the ambient-light input used by the autolamp system. Together with the headlamp switch and body control module (BCM), it supports automatic switching of the exterior lamps as lighting conditions change. Replacement exchanges the sensor at the top of the instrument panel; the illustration shows it raised from its opening near the windshield.
guides.why: The surrounding trim is exposed during removal, making a non-marring tool important. Raising the sensor first provides access to its electrical connector. Understanding the autolamp delay also helps distinguish a normal period of illumination after shutdown from a fault that needs diagnosis.

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies the light sensor as requiring replacement.
notes: An automatic-lighting complaint alone does not identify the sensor as the failed component.

prepare.title: Use a trim-safe tool
prepare.detail: Have a non-marring tool suitable for releasing the sensor without marking the surrounding surface.

prepare.title: Identify the sensor and connector
prepare.detail: Use the removal illustration to recognize the raised sensor and its connector beneath it. Plan to disconnect the connector after lifting the sensor from its retained position.

steps.title: Release and raise the sensor
steps.body: Using the non-marring tool, release the light sensor and position it upward as directed in the [light sensor procedure](#/document/G1694122). Raise it far enough to access the electrical connection without using the wiring to pull it free.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove it
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector, then remove the sensor. The illustration identifies the connection below the raised sensor; it does not call for dismantling the sensor housing.

steps.title: Connect and seat the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: reconnect the electrical connector, return the sensor to its opening and secure it in its retained position. Confirm that the connector remains attached as the sensor is seated.

watchFor.title: Trim damage
watchFor.body: Keep the specified non-marring tool against the trim during release rather than substituting an exposed metal prying edge.

watchFor.title: Normal delayed switch-off
watchFor.body: Autolamps can remain illuminated after ignition-off. The factory default is 20 seconds, and the message center allows adjustment up to approximately 3 minutes.

notes: The autolamp system includes the headlamp switch and BCM as well as the sensor.

diagnostics.finding: Exterior lamps remain on briefly after shutdown.
diagnostics.meaning: This can be the selected autolamp delay.
diagnostics.next: Check the configured delay before treating the behavior as a sensor fault.

verification.title: Check fit and autolamp behavior
verification.body: Confirm the sensor is seated and connected. Check the system's light-sensitive automatic switching, allowing for the selected delay after ignition-off.

procedures.purpose: Release, disconnect, replace and reinstall the light sensor.
Understand autolamp components and the adjustable shutdown delay.

guides.title: Replace a front parking lamp bulb
guides.summary: Reach the front parking lamp through the wheel housing, remove its twist-lock holder and replace the separate bulb.
guides.introduction: The front parking lamp is integrated into the front marker lamp assembly. Its bulb can be separated from a removable holder behind the lamp. The replacement itself is straightforward, but access requires a hoist, front-wheel removal and moving the inner fender liner aside.
guides.why: Releasing the holder before separating the bulb avoids forcing the bulb while the holder remains mounted. Vehicle support is the more demanding part of this small repair: correct lifting points and clearance around the hoist adapters are essential before working in the wheel housing.

when.summary: When the front parking lamp bulb needs replacement.
notes: An unlit parking lamp is a reason to investigate; this removal procedure does not establish that the bulb is the cause.

prepare.title: Arrange safe lifting
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and identify the lifting points by the stamped triangles. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; floor stands are required when using jack support. The emergency tire-changing jack is not suitable for this repair.

prepare.title: Prepare wheel-housing access
prepare.detail: Have suitable wheel-removal and push-pin tools, the replacement bulb and the Wheel and Tire procedure available for removal and correct refitting.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle and remove the front wheels
steps.body: Follow [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631), then remove the front wheels and tires using [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507). Check hoist positioning and underbody clearance before lifting.

steps.title: Expose and disconnect the parking lamp
steps.body: Following [Parking Lamp Bulb](#/document/G1694123), remove the inner fender liner push pins and position the liner aside. Disconnect the front parking lamp electrical connector to free the holder for removal.

steps.title: Remove the holder and exchange the bulb
steps.body: Rotate the bulb holder counterclockwise and withdraw it from the lamp. Separate the bulb from the holder, then install the replacement bulb into the holder.

steps.title: Restore the lamp and wheel housing
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure: refit and secure the holder, reconnect the electrical connector, restore the liner and push pins, and reinstall the front wheels and tires using their procedure.

watchFor.title: Incorrect lifting contact
watchFor.body: Do not apply jack pressure to the bumpers. Keep lifting equipment clear of suspension, exhaust, steering components and vulnerable brackets.

watchFor.title: Holder still locked in place
watchFor.body: The holder must be rotated counterclockwise before withdrawal; pulling the bulb is not the holder-release operation.

notes: This is a separate bulb-and-holder replacement, with access through the inner fender liner.

verification.title: Confirm the lamp is reassembled
verification.body: Verify that the bulb is seated in its holder, the holder is secured in the lamp and the electrical connector is reconnected.

verification.title: Confirm access components are restored
verification.body: Check that the liner push pins are refitted and wheel installation has been completed according to the Wheel and Tire procedure.

procedures.purpose: Front parking lamp bulb removal and installation, including liner access and bulb-holder release.
Correct lifting points, vehicle-support precautions and hoist-clearance requirements.
Front wheel and tire removal and installation needed for lamp access.

guides.title: Remove and replace a rear lamp assembly
