guides.summary: Reach either rear lamp through the trunk, remove the trim and shield, disconnect the wiring, and release three mounting nuts. Includes the optional right-hand subwoofer access and all refitting torques.
guides.introduction: Three nuts hold the rear lamp in place, but the trunk trim insists on being the opening act. I’ll walk you through those layers, including the subwoofer that can stand between you and the right-hand lamp. Each rear lamp provides rear parking, brake and turn-signal lighting, with the turn lamps also serving the hazard warning function.
guides.why: Working through the trim in order exposes the lamp’s electrical connector and mounting nuts without forcing the surrounding panels. The job replaces or temporarily removes the complete lamp assembly; the separate reversing lamp beneath the rear bumper is a different component.

when.summary: Use this procedure when a complete rear lamp assembly requires replacement or removal for adjacent work.
notes: Applies to 2015 Mustang models with 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L and 5.2L engines.
The right-hand coupe arrangement is illustrated; left-hand lamp and convertible operations are similar.
Remove the optional subwoofer and amplifier only when accessing the right-hand lamp.
A lighting fault alone does not establish that the assembly needs replacement.

prepare.title: Identify the lamp and audio configuration
prepare.detail: Choose the right-hand or left-hand lamp before taking the trunk apart. For right-hand access, check whether the luggage-compartment subwoofer and amplifier unit is fitted. The audio steps below cover the illustrated SYNC 2/SYNC 3 unit. If a different audio installation obstructs access, obtain its matching removal instructions before proceeding. This article covers complete-assembly removal and refitting, not electrical fault diagnosis or internal lamp repair.

prepare.title: Gather tools and organize the fasteners
prepare.detail: Have hand tools that fit the actual bolts and nuts, a tool suitable for releasing the trim pin and clips, and a torque wrench capable of accurately applying 21 lb.in (2.4 Nm), 55 lb.in (6.2 Nm), and, when removing the audio unit, 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm). Keep the lamp nuts, audio bolts and trim retainers in separate groups. If replacing the lamp, have the correct assembly for the vehicle and side.

prepare.title: Prepare protection and a stationary work area
prepare.detail: Work with the car parked on level ground and the parking brake applied. This access is through the trunk and does not require lifting. Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. Complete the startup-prevention actions in the first step before beginning removal.

steps.title: Prevent an unexpected start
steps.body: If remote start is fitted, disable it through the central display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Switch the ignition and exterior lighting off, and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent someone starting it during the work. Keep the parking brake applied throughout the job. These precautions come from the [service safety instructions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Open the trunk and remove the floor cover
steps.body: Open the luggage-compartment lid. Lift out the broad spare-tire cover forming the trunk floor and put it aside. For a left-hand lamp, or a right-hand lamp without the optional subwoofer, go directly to the scuff-plate step.

steps.title: Right-hand lamp with subwoofer: remove the lower speaker cover
steps.body: At the trunk-mounted subwoofer, locate the separate lower cover beneath the circular speaker grille. Remove its three bolts and withdraw the cover. Keep these bolts separate from the larger unit’s mounting bolts: their refitting torque is only 21 lb.in (2.4 Nm). This and the next step expand the [subwoofer and amplifier procedure](#/document/G1704011).

steps.title: Right-hand lamp with subwoofer: disconnect and remove the unit
steps.body:
Support the subwoofer and amplifier unit while removing its mounting bolts: one at the upper outer side and two through the lower mounting feet. Disconnect the electrical connector at the finned amplifier on the back of the unit, then remove the unit from the trunk. Support it as it comes free so its weight does not hang from the wiring.

Both the side mounting bolt and the two lower mounting bolts use a refitting torque of 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm). The speaker has had its say; now there is room to reach the lamp.

steps.title: Remove the trunk scuff plate
steps.body: The scuff plate is the wide trim piece across the rear edge of the trunk opening, surrounding the latch opening. Remove its four thumb-nut retainers, then lift the plate upward and out. Set it aside with its retainers. This clears the rear edge of the side trim.

steps.title: Move the appropriate side trim inward
steps.body: Remove the pin-type retainer near the upper rear edge of the side trim beside the lamp. Move the right-hand or left-hand trim panel inward into the trunk to uncover the lamp mounting area. Position the panel aside rather than trying to remove it completely.

steps.title: Release the shield above the lamp
steps.body: Locate the small shield directly above the rear lamp at the edge of the trunk opening. Release its three clips and lift the shield upward off the lamp. If it resists, check that all three clips have released before pulling harder. The shield is a separate access piece, not part of the lamp housing.

steps.title: Disconnect the lamp and remove its three nuts
steps.body:
From inside the trunk, disconnect the rear lamp’s electrical connector. Confirm the connector halves are separated before moving the lamp.

Support the lamp from outside while removing the three mounting nuts from its studs inside the body. Once all three nuts are off, draw the assembly rearward out of its body opening, keeping the disconnected wiring clear. The [rear lamp procedure](#/document/G1694124) covers this arrangement for either side.

steps.title: Install the lamp and tighten its mounting nuts
steps.body:
Position the replacement or retained assembly in the body opening, guiding its studs through their mounting holes and keeping the wiring clear of the mounting surfaces. Support the lamp while installing all three nuts.

Tighten the lamp mounting nuts to 55 lb.in (6.2 Nm). These are inch-pounds, not foot-pounds. Reconnect the lamp’s electrical connector and make sure it is fully engaged.

steps.title: Restore the lamp shield and side trim
steps.body: Place the shield back above the lamp and engage all three clips. Return the side trim panel to its original position, making sure it does not trap the lamp wiring. Reinstall the side trim’s pin-type retainer.

steps.title: Refit the scuff plate
steps.body: Place the scuff plate back across the rear trunk opening, with the latch opening correctly aligned. Reinstall its four thumb-nut retainers. Check that the plate sits in its original position and that the adjacent side trim is properly located before moving on.

steps.title: Refit the optional right-hand audio unit
steps.body:
If removed, position the subwoofer and amplifier unit back in its mounting location and reconnect its electrical connector. Install the upper outer side bolt and the two bolts through the lower mounting feet. Tighten these mounting bolts to 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm).

Refit the separate lower speaker cover and its three bolts. Tighten the cover bolts to 21 lb.in (2.4 Nm). Keep those two audio torque values straight—the little cover does not need the full damn concert.

steps.title: Replace the floor cover and check the finished fit
steps.body: Refit the spare-tire cover. Confirm that the lamp is seated in its opening, its connector is engaged, the shield and trim are secure, and no tools or loose fasteners remain in the trunk. Close the luggage-compartment lid and confirm it closes normally.

steps.title: Check the lighting functions
steps.body:
With the vehicle stationary and the parking brake still applied, use the normal lighting controls to check rear parking illumination, the turn signal on the serviced side, and hazard operation. Apply the brake pedal and observe the serviced stoplamp, using an assistant if needed.

These are completion checks after refitting. If a function fails, switch the lighting and ignition off before reopening the work area, then use the relevant finding below to choose the next action.

watchFor.title: Different retainers at each access layer
watchFor.body: The scuff plate has four thumb-nut retainers, the side trim has a pin-type retainer, and the lamp shield has three clips. Release the correct attachment before moving each part; extra pulling does not substitute for an unreleased retainer.

watchFor.title: A lamp or audio unit hanging from its wiring
watchFor.body: Disconnect the lamp before withdrawing it. Support the audio unit while its mounting bolts and connector are released. Neither harness should carry the removed component’s weight.

watchFor.title: Confusing the three tightening values
watchFor.body: Lamp nuts: 55 lb.in (6.2 Nm). Audio-unit mounting bolts: 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm). Lower speaker-cover bolts: 21 lb.in (2.4 Nm). Use the value for the actual fastener group.

watchFor.title: Trim or wiring caught during refitting
watchFor.body: Check the wiring route before returning the side trim, and check the trim position before securing the scuff plate. If a panel will not sit in its original position, reopen that layer and correct the obstruction before fastening it.

notes: Left-hand access skips subwoofer removal. Right-hand access also skips it when the unit is not fitted.
Refitting reverses removal: lamp, shield, side trim, scuff plate, optional audio unit, then spare-tire cover.
The reversing lamp is beneath the rear bumper fascia and is not part of either rear lamp assembly.
The [exterior lighting overview](#/document/G1694241) explains the lamp functions and the switches and control modules involved.

diagnostics.finding: The right-hand lamp is obstructed by the illustrated subwoofer and amplifier unit.
diagnostics.meaning: The optional audio equipment must come out before continuing the lamp-access sequence.
diagnostics.next: Remove the three-bolt lower cover, then support and unbolt the unit, disconnect its electrical connector, and remove it as described in steps 3–4.

diagnostics.finding: The shield or trim will not lift or move aside after removal begins.
diagnostics.meaning: An attachment may still be engaged; resistance alone does not establish that the panel needs replacement.
diagnostics.next: Recheck the four scuff-plate thumb nuts, the side-trim pin, or the three shield clips, according to the part being moved. Release the remaining attachment before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: A parking, brake, turn-signal or hazard function fails after refitting.
diagnostics.meaning: The completion check has failed. The assembly participates in these functions, but switches, wiring and control modules also affect operation.
diagnostics.next: Turn the lighting and ignition off and remove the key before returning to the connector. Confirm the lamp connector is fully engaged and the wiring was not trapped during assembly. If operation remains incorrect, obtain function-specific electrical diagnosis before replacing more parts.

diagnostics.finding: Only the reversing lamp is inoperative.
diagnostics.meaning: That complaint concerns the separate lamp beneath the rear bumper, rather than the rear lamp assembly removed here.
diagnostics.next: Direct further diagnosis to the reversing-lamp system. Use the [lighting overview](#/document/G1694241) to identify that system’s components.

verification.title: Lamp mounting and connection
verification.body: Confirm all three lamp nuts were tightened to 55 lb.in (6.2 Nm), the lamp is seated in its body opening, and its electrical connector is fully engaged.

verification.title: Access parts restored
verification.body: Confirm the shield’s three clips, side-trim pin and four scuff-plate thumb nuts are restored. Check the spare-tire cover is back in place and the trunk closes normally.

verification.title: Optional audio equipment restored
verification.body: If removed, confirm the audio connector is reconnected, the side and two lower unit bolts are tightened to 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm), and the three lower-cover bolts are tightened to 21 lb.in (2.4 Nm). Check normal audio operation after reassembly.

verification.title: Lighting operation confirmed
verification.body: Confirm the serviced lamp performs its rear parking, brake, turn-signal and hazard functions. These checks verify the finished work; they do not establish the cause of any remaining electrical fault.

procedures.purpose: Primary rear lamp removal and reverse-order installation, including trim access, three mounting nuts and their tightening torque.
Conditional right-hand access through removal and refitting of the optional subwoofer and amplifier unit, including both audio fastener torque values.
Explain rear lamp functions, distinguish the separate reversing lamp, and place completion-check findings in system context.
Relevant startup-prevention and personal-protection precautions before vehicle service.

applicability.equipment: With or without the optional luggage-compartment subwoofer and amplifier unit; the audio-unit procedure used here is identified for SYNC 2/SYNC 3.

stepGroups.title: Secure the car and open the trunk
stepGroups.summary: Prevent startup and remove the trunk floor cover.

stepGroups.title: Clear optional right-hand audio equipment
stepGroups.summary: Remove the lower cover and the subwoofer/amplifier unit when fitted.

stepGroups.title: Expose the lamp
stepGroups.summary: Remove the scuff plate, position the side trim aside and release the shield.

stepGroups.title: Remove and refit the assembly
stepGroups.summary: Disconnect the lamp, release its three nuts and refit at the correct torque.

stepGroups.title: Restore trim and optional audio equipment
stepGroups.summary: Reverse the access sequence and check the finished fit.

stepGroups.title: Check the lighting
stepGroups.summary: Confirm parking, brake, turn-signal and hazard operation.

guides.title: Replace the reversing lamp switch on a manual-transmission Mustang
guides.summary: Reach the transmission-mounted switch from below, disconnect and free its wiring, replace the switch, and tighten it to 20 lb.ft (27 Nm).
guides.introduction: Reverse deserves a little announcement before the Mustang starts backing up. This small transmission-mounted switch helps provide it: selecting reverse makes the reversing lamps illuminate at the bottom of the rear bumper fascia. I’ll walk you through replacing the switch and restoring its wiring without letting a modest electrical job become a damn harness repair.
guides.why: The switch provides the manual transmission’s reverse-selection input to the lighting system. Its short wiring lead and supported connector need to be freed before the switch is turned out of the transmission. I give those connections attention first; the switch should come out alone, without recruiting the wiring for company.
searchTerms: Mustang manual transmission reverse light switch

when.summary: Use this replacement procedure when the manual-transmission reversing lamp switch has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Applies to 2015 Mustangs with a manual transmission and a 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.

prepare.title: Confirm the job and replacement part
prepare.detail: Have the correct reversing lamp switch for the fitted manual transmission. This article covers mechanical replacement; electrical fault isolation requires a separate diagnostic procedure. A lamp that stays dark does not, by itself, establish switch failure.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting equipment and hand tools
prepare.detail: Use a vehicle hoist rated for the Mustang’s actual weight, including cargo and modifications, wheel chocks, a suitable tool for removing the switch, and a torque wrench capable of applying 20 lb.ft (27 Nm). Have eye and ear protection, plus protective gloves for handling sharp-edged components.

prepare.title: Identify the lifting points before raising
prepare.detail: The lifting illustration shows four support locations along the outer underbody, behind the front wheels and ahead of the rear wheels. Find the stamped triangle at each actual lifting point before positioning an adapter. Review the [lifting precautions](#/document/G1663631) and the task-relevant [service safety precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Prevent movement and unintended starting
steps.body:
Position the vehicle on a hard, level surface, apply the parking brake and chock the wheels remaining on the ground.

If remote start is fitted, disable it through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around or beneath the car. Turn the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person starting it. Wear eye and ear protection; use protective gloves where sharp edges are present.

steps.title: Position the hoist and raise the vehicle
steps.body:
Locate the stamped triangles at the four lifting positions and place the hoist adapters at those designated points. Before lifting, check that the arms and adapters clear the exhaust, suspension, steering linkage, mounting brackets and stabilizer brackets. Avoid contact that could damage the axle or rear cover. Never lift against either bumper.

If using a drive-on hoist, check underbody clearance before driving onto it. Raise and secure the vehicle according to the hoist’s operating instructions, confirming correct support before going underneath. On an arm-type hoist, establish that all four wheels are fully clear of the ground and the vehicle is securely supported. Keep the parking brake applied throughout this repair.

The [jacking and lifting overview](#/document/G1663631) identifies the required support precautions. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; the emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this job.

steps.title: Find the switch and trace its short lead
steps.body:
From beneath the vehicle, look at the upper portion of the ribbed transmission casing below the large exhaust pipe. The illustrated switch has a raised, round-topped body seated in the casing, with a short electrical lead running to a connector retained at a wiring harness guide. Nearby rigid lines cross the casing; distinguish those from the switch’s flexible lead.

Trace the lead from the switch to its connector before disturbing anything. The access sequence in the [switch replacement procedure](#/document/G1694126) begins here with the wiring connection.

steps.title: Disconnect the connector and release it from the harness guide
steps.body:
Release the electrical connector’s locking feature and separate the connector halves, handling their housings rather than pulling on the wires. Then detach the switch connector from the wiring harness guide.

Note how the connector sits in the guide and how the lead passes around the nearby lines. Move the freed connector and lead aside so they can move with the switch during removal. Do not leave the lead attached to its support while turning the switch.

steps.title: Remove the reversing lamp switch
steps.body:
With the electrical connection separated and the connector free of the guide, use a suitable tool on the switch body to unscrew it from the transmission casing. Withdraw the switch and its short lead together.

Keep track of the original lead arrangement so the replacement can return to the same supported position.

steps.title: Install the replacement and apply the specified torque
steps.body:
Fit the correct replacement switch into the transmission opening. Start the threads carefully so the switch enters squarely, keeping its lead free rather than winding it around nearby components.

Tighten the reversing lamp switch to 20 lb.ft (27 Nm). This is the switch’s installation torque; do not apply it to the connector or wiring guide.

steps.title: Restore the harness support and electrical connection
steps.body:
Reverse the wiring-release sequence: attach the connector to the wiring harness guide, then reconnect the electrical connector fully.

Return the lead to its original arrangement around the nearby lines. Confirm that the connector is retained by the guide and that the electrical connection is latched. The lead should not be trapped between components or displaced against the exhaust.

steps.title: Check the assembly and lower the vehicle
steps.body:
Before leaving the underside, confirm that the switch has been tightened to 20 lb.ft (27 Nm), the connector is fully engaged, and its guide attachment is restored. Remove tools and clear the lowering area.

Keep the parking brake applied before and during lowering. As the wheels reach the ground, restore wheel chocks before releasing the vehicle from the hoist and moving its arms or adapters away.

steps.title: Check reversing-lamp operation with the vehicle stationary
steps.body:
With the vehicle fully on the ground, parking brake applied and wheels chocked, have a driver remain at the controls with the service brake held. Keep the engine off and switch the ignition on for the lamp check.

Have an observer stand safely to one side, clear of the vehicle’s travel path, and watch the reversing lamps at the bottom of the rear bumper fascia. Select reverse and confirm illumination; select Neutral and confirm that the reversing lamps go out. This checks the result of the repair rather than diagnosing individual circuit components.

Turn the ignition off, remove the key and return the transmission to its normal parked gear. Keep the parking brake and chocks in place until the vehicle is ready to be moved. The expected lamp response is described in the [exterior lighting overview](#/document/G1694241).

watchFor.title: A lifting point you cannot positively identify
watchFor.body: Stop before raising the vehicle if you cannot locate a stamped triangle or position the adapter correctly. Supporting another convenient-looking part of the underbody can allow the vehicle to shift or fall.

watchFor.title: Wiring still tied to the guide
watchFor.body: Unplugging the electrical connection and releasing the connector from its guide are separate actions. Complete both before unscrewing the switch so the lead is not pulled or twisted against its support.

watchFor.title: A connector that will not release or latch
watchFor.body: Check the connector’s locking feature and housing alignment instead of forcing it or pulling the wires. Do not finish the repair with the connection partly engaged or its guide attachment unsecured.

notes: The manual-transmission switch is part of a system that also includes the reversing lamp, powertrain control module (PCM) and body control module (BCM). Automatic-transmission vehicles use a transmission range sensor for the reverse-selection input.
I treat the final wiring check as part of replacement, not tidying up. A correctly tightened switch still needs its electrical connection and harness support restored.

diagnostics.finding: The vehicle has an automatic transmission.
diagnostics.meaning: The reverse-selection input comes from a transmission range sensor rather than this manual-transmission switch.
diagnostics.next: Use diagnosis appropriate to the automatic transmission. The [lighting overview](#/document/G1694241) explains the system distinction; this replacement procedure does not apply.

diagnostics.finding: The switch, lead or connector arrangement cannot be matched to the described transmission location.
diagnostics.meaning: The intended component has not been positively identified.
diagnostics.next: Stop before unplugging or unscrewing another component. Confirm the fitted manual transmission and identify the switch using the [replacement procedure](#/document/G1694126).

diagnostics.finding: The reversing lamps fail to illuminate in reverse or remain illuminated after reverse is deselected.
diagnostics.meaning: The operational result is incorrect, but that observation alone does not identify the failed circuit component.
diagnostics.next: Turn the ignition off. Recheck the restored connector engagement and harness attachment, then obtain electrical diagnosis if the fault remains. Use the [lighting overview](#/document/G1694241) for system context; do not condemn another switch or a control module from lamp behavior alone.

verification.title: Mechanical installation
verification.body: Confirm the replacement switch is installed and tightened to 20 lb.ft (27 Nm).

verification.title: Wiring restoration
verification.body: Confirm the electrical connector is latched, its attachment to the harness guide is restored, and the short lead follows its original arrangement without being trapped or displaced against the exhaust.

verification.title: Stationary operation and final restraint
verification.body: Confirm the reversing lamps illuminate when reverse is selected and go out when it is deselected during the secured, engine-off check. Finish with ignition off, key removed, the transmission returned to its parked gear, parking brake applied and wheel chocks retained until moving the car.

procedures.purpose: Identify, remove and install the reversing lamp switch, restore its connector and guide attachment, and apply the specified installation torque.
Identify the four lifting locations and position lifting equipment without damaging nearby components.
Explain the manual-transmission reverse-selection input, reversing-lamp location and expected operation.
Apply startup prevention, personal protection, vehicle restraint and hoist-capacity precautions relevant to underbody service.

stepGroups.summary: Disconnect and detach the connector, remove the switch, and tighten its replacement.

guides.title: Replace the reversing lamp in the rear bumper
guides.summary: Remove the rear bumper cover to replace the reversing lamp, then restore the cover attachments and electrical connections.
guides.introduction: The reversing lamp sits at the bottom of the rear bumper fascia and illuminates when REVERSE is selected. Its replacement requires removing the bumper cover, which also involves wheel-area fasteners, rear lamp assemblies and bumper wiring. Most of the work is creating access and safely handling the cover rather than removing the lamp itself.
guides.why: The cover remains connected by brackets and wiring after its visible fasteners are removed. Releasing these attachments in sequence prevents the cover from pulling on the harness. The lamp and cover screws also have low tightening values, so controlled tightening matters when restoring their mountings.

when.summary: When the reversing lamp has been identified as requiring replacement or removal.
notes: A lamp that stays dark in REVERSE needs diagnosis before replacement is treated as the remedy.

prepare.title: Provide supported access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist at the designated triangle-marked lifting points. Check adapter clearance and never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare for bumper-cover removal
prepare.detail: Have tools for push pins, screws and wheel removal, plus torque equipment suitable for the lamp's small screws. Arrange an assistant for the cover handling shown in the removal illustration.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle and disconnect the lamp
steps.body: Raise the vehicle using the lifting procedure, then disconnect the reversing lamp electrical connector. This is the first electrical disconnection in the lamp replacement sequence.

steps.title: Free the bumper-cover attachments
steps.body: Follow the [rear bumper cover procedure](#/document/G1694215). Remove the initial push pins and screws, disconnect the specified bumper harness connections and separate the wiring guide. Remove the rear wheels, then the wheel-area screw and push pins on both sides, the cover-to-bracket screws and the rear lamp assemblies.

steps.title: Release and remove the cover
steps.body: Release the cover sides from their brackets and the center from the rear brackets. Position the cover for connector access, disconnect the rear bumper harness and remove the cover with assistance. Inspect both side brackets and the rear brackets; use the cover procedure for any required bracket replacement.

steps.title: Replace the reversing lamp
steps.body: Following the [lamp procedure](#/document/G1694125), remove its retaining screws and lift the lamp from the cover. Install the replacement in reverse order and tighten the lamp screws to 15 lb.in (1.7 Nm).

steps.title: Reassemble the rear bumper
steps.body: Reverse the cover-removal sequence, restoring the wiring connections and guide, bracket engagement, rear lamps, fasteners and wheels. The cover procedure specifies 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm) for its identified screws; follow its linked wheel procedure for wheel installation. Reconnect the reversing lamp.

watchFor.title: Cover still attached to wiring
watchFor.body: Position the cover for connector access before carrying it away from the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Damaged mounting brackets
watchFor.body: Inspect the side and rear brackets while exposed; their condition affects how the cover is retained.

notes: Lamp-screw and bumper-cover screw tightening values differ.

diagnostics.finding: The reversing lamp does not illuminate when REVERSE is selected.
diagnostics.meaning: The system also includes a reversing switch on manual transmissions or a range sensor on automatics, plus the powertrain and body control modules. Darkness alone does not identify the failed component.
diagnostics.next: Establish that lamp replacement is justified before dismantling the bumper.

verification.title: Confirm attachment and operation
verification.body: Check that the cover is retained by its brackets and fasteners and all disturbed connectors are restored. With the vehicle secured for a stationary check, confirm that selecting REVERSE illuminates the lamp.

verification.title: Record the outcome
verification.body: Record reversing-lamp operation and any bracket damage corrected during access.

procedures.purpose: Reversing lamp removal, installation and lamp-screw tightening.
Rear bumper cover access, wiring disconnection, bracket inspection and reassembly.
Safe lifting points and hoist positioning.

guides.title: Replace a rear side lamp bulb
guides.summary: Safely lift your 2015 Mustang, reach the illustrated rear side lamp from underneath the rear bumper, and replace its bulb before refitting the holder and wiring.
guides.introduction: A rear side lamp bulb can fit in your pocket, yet replacing it somehow books the whole hoist. Typical. I’ll walk you through access behind the rear bumper’s outer corner, the separate connector, bulb and holder operations, and getting the car safely back onto its wheels.
guides.why: The rear side lamp helps other road users see the car from the side. Its bulb makes the light, its holder keeps the bulb positioned in the lamp, and its electrical connector supplies power. This is a replacement job once the bulb needs changing; darkness alone does not prove the bulb is the culprit.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang rear side lamp bulb replacement
rear bumper side lamp bulb holder removal

when.summary: Use this procedure for the illustrated rear bumper side-lamp arrangement on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
notes: The replacement sequence is common to all four listed engines.
The front side-marker lamps are integrated into the front marker lamp assemblies; this article covers the illustrated rear arrangement.
Arrange suitable hoist access before starting.

prepare.title: Have the correct bulb ready
prepare.detail: Obtain a replacement bulb confirmed for your vehicle and rear lamp position. The bulb number and wattage are not identified here. This job covers the illustrated connector, bulb and removable holder; a different lamp arrangement, an obstructed access route or an electrical fault needs matching repair information before proceeding.

prepare.title: Arrange the lifting equipment
prepare.detail: Use a hoist rated for the vehicle’s actual weight, including cargo and modifications, on a hard, level working surface. Have wheel chocks ready. Review the four triangle-marked lifting locations in [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631) before positioning the arms.

prepare.title: Protect yourself
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when reaching past sharp body edges. Keep the key under your control throughout the underside work. The relevant startup and lifting precautions are in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Prevent startup, switch the lamps off and restrain the car
steps.body:
Before working around or underneath the car, disable remote start, if fitted, through the central display: Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle.
Select lamps off at the headlamp switch and visually confirm that the rear side lamp is off before disconnecting it. Autolamps can keep exterior lamps illuminated after ignition-off: the factory delay is 20 seconds, adjustable to approximately 3 minutes. Ignition-off alone is not confirmation that the lamps are off.
Set the parking brake and chock the wheels while they remain on the ground. Leave the parking brake applied throughout this job.

steps.title: Position the hoist and raise the vehicle
steps.body:
Locate the triangles stamped into the body or frame at the four side lifting locations, one near each wheel. These identify the correct support areas shown in [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631).
Position the hoist adapters at those locations. Before lifting, check that the arms and adapters will not contact suspension parts, mounting brackets, stabilizer mounting brackets, exhaust or steering components, or damage the axle or rear cover. Never lift against either bumper.
For a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving onto it and retain wheel restraints on the platforms. Raise and secure the vehicle using the hoist’s operating instructions. Verify that it is securely supported before going underneath.

steps.title: Find the rear side-lamp connection from underneath
steps.body:
At the rear side lamp being serviced, look upward behind the rear bumper’s outer corner, beside the exhaust and muffler area visible in the illustration. Find the short wiring lead running along the inside of the bumper cover to a small connector beside the molded reinforcing ribs. That connector plugs into the rear side-lamp bulb-holder area.
Identify this rear connection before pulling anything. The front marker assembly is a different location. The [Side Lamp Bulb procedure](#/document/G1694127) reaches the illustrated rear connection directly from underneath, without a wheel, bumper-cover or liner removal step.

steps.title: Disconnect the electrical connector
steps.body:
With the lamps switched off and the side lamp confirmed off, release the connector’s retaining feature and unplug it from the side lamp. Hold the connector body rather than pulling on its wires, then move the disconnected lead aside enough to reach the bulb and holder without loading the wiring.
The plug, bulb and holder are separate parts of this little operation. Giving each its own moment saves a surprising amount of plastic-related swearing.

steps.title: Release the holder from the lamp
steps.body: With the wiring disconnected, turn the bulb holder counterclockwise and withdraw it from the lamp. This brings the bulb out of the lamp housing while it remains seated in its holder. Keep the holder supported for the bulb change.

steps.title: Remove the bulb from the extracted holder
steps.body: With the holder out of the lamp, remove the old bulb from it. The bulb is the small rounded element projecting from the end of the holder. Keep the holder ready for the replacement; it is reused rather than discarded with the bulb.

steps.title: Fit the bulb, then secure the holder in the lamp
steps.body:
Install the correct replacement bulb into the removed holder and confirm that it is seated. Then return the holder-and-bulb assembly to the lamp opening and turn the holder clockwise to secure it.

Confirm that the holder is seated and retained before reconnecting its electrical plug. This reverses the holder-extraction and bulb-removal operations; the twist-in holder has no numeric tightening torque in this procedure.

steps.title: Reconnect and check the assembly
steps.body:
Reconnect the electrical connector and confirm its retaining feature has engaged. Return the short wiring lead to its original route along the inside of the rear bumper cover, clear of the holder and nearby edges.
Before leaving the underside, check that the holder is retained, the bulb is seated, the connector is attached and no loose parts or tools remain.

steps.title: Lower the car with its restraints in place
steps.body:
Clear everyone and all equipment from beneath the vehicle. Confirm the parking brake is still applied before lowering.
On an arm-type hoist, lower under control and restore wheel chocks as the tires reach the ground, before withdrawing the lifting arms. On a drive-on lift, keep the wheel restraints in place through lowering. Leave the car restrained until you are ready to move it.

steps.title: Check the rear side lamp’s operation
steps.body:
With the car on the ground and restrained, use the headlamp switch to turn on the parking lamps and observe the repaired rear side lamp from outside. Confirm that it illuminates, then switch the lamps off.
This is a completion check, not an electrical diagnosis. If it remains dark, use the decision rows below before buying another bulb. The [Exterior Lighting Overview](#/document/G1694241) explains the parking and side-marker lamp system.

watchFor.title: A jack is not safe underbody support
watchFor.body: Never get underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack. Jack-raised vehicles require suitable floor stands. The vehicle’s emergency jack is intended for changing a deflated tire, not this repair.

watchFor.title: Incorrect lifting contact
watchFor.body: Stop if an adapter does not align with a triangle-marked lifting location or an arm contacts a nearby component. Correct its position before raising the vehicle; incorrect support can damage the car or allow it to shift or fall.

watchFor.title: Automatic lighting can remain on
watchFor.body: Complete the lamps-off check before unplugging the connector. The autolamp delay can leave exterior lamps illuminated even though the ignition is off.

notes: The installation sequence reverses removal: holder, bulb, electrical connector.
Keep the engine off throughout this repair; lamp access does not require underhood work.

diagnostics.finding: The holder, bulb or connector is not fully seated during the assembly check.
diagnostics.meaning: Reassembly is incomplete; this does not establish an electrical fault.
diagnostics.next: With the lamps off, correct the affected connection or seating before lowering or repeating the operating check. If the car has already been lowered, repeat the startup-prevention, restraint and hoist steps before reaching underneath again.

diagnostics.finding: The repaired rear side lamp illuminates when the parking lamps are selected.
diagnostics.meaning: The replacement passes its basic operating check.
diagnostics.next: Switch the lamps off and finish the job.

diagnostics.finding: The rear side lamp remains dark with the correct bulb installed and the assembly fully connected.
diagnostics.meaning: Bulb replacement has not resolved the concern; the cause remains unconfirmed.
diagnostics.next: Arrange diagnosis of the side-lamp circuit. Do not condemn wiring or a control module from this result alone. Use the [Exterior Lighting Overview](#/document/G1694241) for system context.

verification.title: Mechanical completion
verification.body: The holder is seated and retained, the bulb is installed, the connector is engaged and the wiring follows its original route.

verification.title: Safe return to the ground
verification.body: The parking brake remained applied, wheel restraints were retained or restored as the tires reached the ground, and the hoist arms were withdrawn only after the car was supported on its wheels.

verification.title: Lighting completion
verification.body: The repaired rear side lamp illuminates with the parking lamps selected. A lamp that remains dark requires further diagnosis.

guides.title: Remove and replace the side turn signal lamp
guides.summary: Disconnect and release the bumper-mounted side lamp, removing the rear bumper cover first when side obstacle detection is fitted.
guides.introduction: The side turn signal is a small electrical lamp held in the rear bumper cover by a retaining tab. Its connector supplies the electrical connection, while the tab secures the lamp in its opening. The lamp-release sequence is short, but access changes with vehicle equipment: side obstacle detection requires rear bumper cover removal first.
guides.why: Selecting the equipment branch determines how much surrounding bodywork must be removed. At the lamp itself, disconnecting the wiring before releasing the tab keeps the electrical connection from restraining the unit as it is withdrawn. Proper lifting is necessary because the procedure begins with the vehicle on a hoist.

when.summary: When the side lamp requires removal or replacement after the repair requirement has been established.
notes: Confirm whether side obstacle detection is fitted before planning bumper access.
A lamp that does not operate still needs its cause established; this removal procedure is not a circuit test.

prepare.title: Arrange safe lifting
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the specified lifting points identified by the stamped triangles. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack or apply lifting pressure to a bumper.

prepare.title: Allow for equipment-dependent access
prepare.detail: For vehicles with side obstacle detection, prepare for rear-wheel, rear-lamp and bumper-cover removal through the linked bumper procedure.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle correctly
steps.body: Follow the lifting overview and position the hoist adapters carefully to avoid underbody and component interference. The vehicle's emergency tire-changing jack is not intended for this work.

steps.title: Remove the bumper cover when required
steps.body: With side obstacle detection, follow the rear bumper procedure: release the specified fasteners, harness connections and guides, remove the rear wheels and lamp assemblies, then release the cover from its brackets. Position it aside to disconnect the remaining bumper harness before removal. Inspect the side and rear brackets as directed. Without this equipment, proceed to the lamp-release step.

steps.title: Disconnect and release the lamp
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector first. Release the retaining tab, then remove the side turn signal from the cover as illustrated. Follow this order so neither the connector nor the tab remains attached as the lamp comes away.

steps.title: Install and restore access parts
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence to seat and retain the lamp and reconnect its wiring. If the bumper cover was removed, complete its installation procedure, including the harness connections, guides, brackets, rear lamps, wheels and remaining fasteners.

watchFor.title: Bumper harness still attached
watchFor.body: During cover removal, position the cover aside for connector access before taking it away.

watchFor.title: Damaged cover brackets
watchFor.body: The bumper procedure calls for inspection of the side and rear brackets and provides their removal steps when required.

notes: The left-side lamp is illustrated; the right-side procedure is similar.

verification.title: Confirm lamp retention
verification.body: Check that the lamp is seated, the retaining tab is engaged and the electrical connector is restored.

verification.title: Confirm conditional reassembly
verification.body: Where the cover was removed, check that its bracket attachments and all disconnected bumper harness connections and guides have been restored.

guides.title: Replace the brake-pedal stoplamp switch
guides.summary: Replace the stoplamp switch on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine, keeping the brake pedal untouched during removal and installation.
guides.introduction: Your Mustang’s brake lights have a tiny stage manager tucked above the pedal. The stoplamp switch makes the announcement when you brake, and replacing it is a short disconnect-and-twist job. I’ll walk you through finding it, releasing it and fitting its replacement. Tiny part, surprisingly strict manners: the brake pedal must stay untouched while the switch is being removed or installed.
guides.why: The switch sits on the brake-pedal assembly. Pressing the pedal causes electrical power to reach the rear stoplamps and high-mounted stoplamp, telling following traffic that you are braking. Pressing or pulling the pedal during switch removal or installation can misadjust or damage the switch.

when.summary: Use this procedure when diagnosis has established that the stoplamp switch needs replacement.
notes: A brake-light complaint alone does not establish that the switch has failed.
The same removal and installation instructions apply to the listed 2015 engine configurations.

prepare.title: Have the replacement ready
prepare.detail: Have the correct replacement stoplamp switch for your vehicle ready before disconnecting the old one. No special tool, lubricant or separate replacement fastener is called for in this operation.

prepare.title: Plan access from the driver's footwell
prepare.detail: Work beneath the dashboard at the upper brake-pedal assembly. Arrange your position so you can reach the switch and connector without leaning on, pressing or pulling the brake pedal. The replacement operation covers direct access to the switch; electrical fault testing, switch adjustment and removal of any obstructing trim require their own instructions.

prepare.title: Protect yourself
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection for service work, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged brackets or nearby components. Review the relevant [service precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Secure the parked car and prevent an unintended start
steps.body: Apply the parking brake and leave the vehicle on the ground throughout this job. If remote start is fitted, disable it through the central display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle before reaching into the pedal area.

steps.title: Locate the switch above the brake pedal
steps.body:
From the driver's footwell, look upward beneath the dashboard toward the brake-pedal mounting bracket near the steering column. Find the small upright switch fitted into the bracket, with an electrical plug on its upper end and a short wiring loop leading away from it.
Identify the connector and switch body before reaching in. The [stoplamp-switch procedure](#/document/G1694129) calls for disconnecting this plug and rotating the switch; it does not call for removing the pedal assembly or its surrounding bracket.

steps.title: Disconnect the electrical plug
steps.body:
Leave the brake pedal at rest. Release the retaining feature at the top of the electrical plug and disconnect the plug from the switch. Handle the connector body rather than pulling its wires, then position the disconnected plug and wiring loop clear of the switch.
Keep your hands and arms from moving the brake pedal throughout removal.

steps.title: Turn the switch clockwise and remove it
steps.body:
Grip the switch body, turn it clockwise to release it from its mounting, and remove it. Do not press or pull the brake pedal to create clearance or help the switch release.
The switch comes out by rotation; nearby pedal hardware is not part of this removal. A small job deserves a small amount of dismantling.

steps.title: Fit and retain the replacement switch
steps.body:
Keep the brake pedal undisturbed. Place the replacement switch into the same mounting position, then turn it counterclockwise to retain it, reversing the removal movement. Installation is the reverse of removal; no separate pedal adjustment is part of this operation.
If the switch will not seat or remain retained, stop rather than forcing it or moving the pedal to make it fit.

steps.title: Reconnect the plug and clear the pedal area
steps.body:
Reconnect the electrical plug to the installed switch and make sure its retaining feature is engaged. Return the wiring loop clear of the pedal's movement. Confirm that the switch remains retained in its bracket.
Continue to leave the brake pedal untouched until the switch is fully installed and connected. Remove your tools and move out of the footwell before operating the pedal.

steps.title: Check the stoplamps after assembly
steps.body:
With the car still parked and the parking brake applied, press and release the brake pedal while a helper observes the rear stoplamps and high-mounted stoplamp. Confirm that all illuminate during pedal application and switch off after release.
This is a completion check, not a test that isolates a failed component. If any stoplamp behaves incorrectly, resolve the fault before driving.

watchFor.title: Do not move the pedal during switch handling
watchFor.body: Pressing or pulling the brake pedal during removal or installation can misadjust or damage the switch. Do not use the pedal as a handhold or move it for clearance.

watchFor.title: A loose switch or connector is unfinished work
watchFor.body: Before operating the pedal, confirm that the switch is retained in its mounting and the electrical plug is attached with its retainer engaged.

notes: Clockwise releases the switch; counterclockwise refits it by reversing removal.
The stoplamp system also includes the rear lamp assemblies, high-mounted stoplamp and body-control electronics. Body Control Module B is included except on China-market vehicles.

diagnostics.finding: The stoplamps do not operate correctly before replacement.
diagnostics.meaning: The symptom could involve the switch, lamps or body-control electronics; it does not identify the switch by itself.
diagnostics.next: Establish the failed component before replacing parts. The [exterior-lighting overview](#/document/G1694241) explains the system's components and basic operation.

diagnostics.finding: The brake pedal was pressed or pulled while the switch was being removed or installed.
diagnostics.meaning: The switch may have been misadjusted or damaged.
diagnostics.next: Stop and have the switch's condition and adjustment assessed before accepting the installation. Do not improvise a pedal or switch adjustment.

diagnostics.finding: The replacement switch will not seat or remain retained.
diagnostics.meaning: Installation is incomplete.
diagnostics.next: Leave the pedal undisturbed and resolve the fit or retention problem before reconnecting and operating the assembly.

diagnostics.finding: One or more stoplamps fail to illuminate, or remain illuminated after pedal release.
diagnostics.meaning: The completed installation has not passed its functional check; the result alone does not identify the cause.
diagnostics.next: Recheck switch retention and connector attachment, then obtain stoplamp-system diagnosis if operation remains incorrect. Do not drive until the fault is resolved.

verification.title: Assembly is secure
verification.body: The switch is retained in its bracket, its electrical connector is attached, and the wiring is clear of pedal movement.

verification.title: Every stoplamp responds
verification.body: After assembly, both rear stoplamps and the high-mounted stoplamp illuminate when the pedal is pressed and extinguish when it is released.

verification.title: The footwell is clear
verification.body: Remove tools and loose items from the pedal area before returning the vehicle to service.

guides.title: Diagnose PCM, ABS and vehicle dynamics module communication faults
guides.summary: Separate network-wide faults from individual module power, ground, wiring and connector problems before considering replacement.
guides.introduction: Electronic modules exchange commands and status over twisted wire pairs called controller area networks (CAN). The diagnostic scan tool reaches these networks through the data link connector (DLC). This guide covers initial fault routing, gateway diagnostic codes and the individual non-response tests for the powertrain control module (PCM), anti-lock brake system (ABS) module and vehicle dynamics control module (VDM).
guides.why: A module cannot communicate without working power, ground and data connections. A missing response therefore does not establish module failure. High-speed CAN networks HS-CAN1 and HS-CAN2 connect directly to the DLC; the gateway carries HS-CAN3 and medium-speed CAN messages through HS-CAN2.
searchTerms: PCM not responding to scan tool
warning lights only with scanner connected
no start with diagnostic tool connected

when.summary: Use when a module currently fails to respond, a whole network is unavailable, or gateway diagnostic codes require evaluation.
notes: Apply the VDM branch only when that module is fitted.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check previous repairs, wiring damage, battery and charging operation. Battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Diagnose circuit-related diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) before system-performance codes.

prepare.title: Have electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a compatible scan tool, digital multimeter, wiring diagrams and specified Rotunda Flex Probes. Follow Diagnostic Methods for circuit isolation, including battery disconnection for ground-resistance measurements. Never force probes into terminals.

steps.title: Route the actual communication complaint
steps.body: Run the network test. The symptom chart routes complete HS-CAN1, HS-CAN2, HS-CAN3 and medium-speed CAN failures to Tests AD, AE, AF and AG respectively. DLC power loss, or starting and warning-light problems occurring only with the tool connected, route to AH. Other individual modules have their own chart entries.

steps.title: Test A: establish the PCM communication path
steps.body: A “pass” or DTC beside the PCM means its network fault is not currently present. If another listed HS-CAN1 module responds, complete Powertrain Control/Emissions Diagnosis Test QA before continuing. With ignition off, check DLC termination resistance: 54–66 ohms advances to connector inspection; an out-of-range result requires PCM-to-DLC continuity checks. Use the separate 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L/5.2L connector table and repair circuits failing the less-than-3-ohm requirement.

steps.title: Test B: check the ABS module
steps.body: Check the specified battery junction box fuses. Disconnect the ABS connector with ignition off, then switch ignition on for supply measurements. Each specified supply must exceed 11 volts. Switch ignition off for the ground and HS-CAN2 continuity checks; each must measure less than 3 ohms. Repair a failed circuit before continuing.

steps.title: Test C: check the VDM
steps.body: Check its specified battery junction box and body control module fuses. Follow the same staged approach using the VDM connector table: ignition-on supplies greater than 11 volts, then ignition-off ground and HS-CAN2 continuity below 3 ohms. A failed fuse requires investigation of the possible short.

steps.title: Inspect connections before the replacement decision
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect the relevant module connectors and the in-line connectors identified by its test. Replace corroded or damaged terminals, clean module pins and correct pushed-out pins. Reconnect fully and operate the system. If the concern remains, check Ford OASIS service information for applicable technical service bulletins; follow a matching bulletin before the test's module-replacement endpoint.

watchFor.title: Temporary recovery after reconnection
watchFor.body: Communication returning after disturbing a connector points toward a connection concern. Address its root cause; reseating alone may leave the fault intermittent.

notes: The chart routes integrated parking-aid communication concerns to body control Test I and integrated digital-audio concerns to audio Test M.
A restraints control module non-response routes to Test D. Its preliminary check identifies body control module fuse 35 (5A); these PCM, ABS and VDM tests do not authorize restraint-circuit testing.

diagnostics.finding: Gateway DTC U2100:00 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: Initial configuration is incomplete, commonly following incomplete or incorrect programmable module installation.
diagnostics.next: Review service history and install Professional Technician Society As-Built data through the scan tool's Module Programming > As-Built instructions.

diagnostics.finding: Gateway DTC U3000:44, U3000:45 or U3000:49 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: These identify data-memory, program-memory or internal electronic failure respectively.
diagnostics.next: Retrieve all continuous-memory DTCs. If the relevant code is retrieved, follow gateway replacement. If absent, the gateway operates correctly at present and the concern may be intermittent.

verification.title: Confirm present operation
verification.body: Operate the system after circuit or connector correction and establish whether the original concern remains. Do not replace a module under these tests when its concern is absent.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Retain network responses, retrieved codes, circuit measurements and the repair or next test selected.

guides.title: Diagnose restraint, steering-column or instrument-cluster modules that will not communicate
guides.summary: Trace scan-tool nonresponse through the affected module's power, ground, network wiring and connector checks.
guides.introduction: Electronic modules exchange commands and status over shared twisted-wire networks. A module can stop answering a diagnostic scan tool because its power, ground or message path is interrupted. These tests cover the restraints, occupant-classification, steering-column and instrument-cluster modules; the cluster's diagnostic messages also pass through a gateway.
guides.why: No response does not prove a module has failed. Each test uses a particular connection state, and the restraint-module sequence alternates between depowered work and specified powered measurements. Following that sequence protects both the technician and the validity of the readings.
searchTerms: instrument cluster not responding to scan tool

when.summary: Use when the scan tool currently cannot communicate with one of the modules covered by Tests D–G.
notes: Select the test for the missing module; do not substitute one network branch's resistance limits for another.

prepare.title: Arrange the required capability
prepare.detail: This work requires restraint-system and live electrical diagnostic skills, a diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, wiring diagrams and Rotunda Flex Probes.

prepare.title: Check the electrical foundation
prepare.detail: Verify battery and charging operation and battery state of charge greater than 70%. Inspect wiring and previous repairs, and address relevant circuit trouble codes first.

prepare.title: Have the restraint procedures available
prepare.detail: Use the complete supplemental restraint system (SRS) depowering and repowering procedures wherever Test D requires them.

steps.title: Test D: restraints control module
steps.body: With ignition off, depower the SRS before disconnecting the restraints control module (RCM). Inspect the specified terminals; D1 damage requires a new harness and SRS repowering. With terminals sound, repower as directed for the supply-voltage test, then check the module's case ground. Depower again before checking both high-speed controller area network 2 (HS-CAN2) wires to the data link connector (DLC). Continue to connector inspection and repowering before retesting operation.

steps.title: Test E: occupant classification system module
steps.body: Switch ignition off and wait one minute before disconnecting the occupant classification system module (OCSM). Follow E1–E3 through supply voltage, ground continuity and both HS-CAN2 wires to the DLC. Repair a failed circuit before proceeding; satisfactory readings lead to the module and in-line connector inspection.

steps.title: Test F: steering column control module
steps.body: With ignition off and the scan-tool cable removed from the DLC, check HS-CAN2 termination resistance. A reading between 54 and 66 ohms leads to steering column control module (SCCM) supply and ground checks. An out-of-range reading leads instead to continuity checks between the SCCM and DLC; satisfactory continuity advances to F5's connector check.

steps.title: Test G: instrument panel cluster
steps.body: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) uses HS-CAN3, with diagnostic messages translated through the gateway module onto HS-CAN2. Disconnect the negative battery cable, scan-tool cable and gateway connector as directed. Termination resistance between 108 and 132 ohms leads to IPC supply testing; otherwise check the IPC-to-gateway wires. Follow G3–G4's battery reconnection for voltage testing and disconnection for ground testing, then restore the connection when directed.

steps.title: Inspect connections before a module decision
steps.body: At the selected test's final step, inspect module and in-line connectors. Replace damaged or corroded terminals as directed, clean module pins, correct pushed-out pins and reconnect securely. Retest the concern. Restored operation calls for correcting the connection's root cause, rather than proceeding with replacement.

steps.title: Follow the correct unresolved-fault endpoint
steps.body: If nonresponse remains, check applicable technical service bulletins and follow any matching instructions. Without an applicable bulletin, Tests D, E and F direct the corresponding replacement procedure. Test G instead requires the vehicle identification number to access the IPC guided routine.

watchFor.title: Accidental restraint deployment
watchFor.body: Never probe airbag or curtain-airbag connectors, or back-probe deployable-device connectors. Never dismantle or tamper with pretensioners, load limiters or inflators; accidental deployment can cause serious injury or death.

watchFor.title: Invalid resistance readings
watchFor.body: Voltage present in a circuit can corrupt an ohmmeter reading. Preserve the prescribed ignition, battery and connector states.

notes: For a separate instrument center module nonresponse concern, the initial checks identify HS-CAN1 and BCM fuse 32 (10A). Continue its dedicated diagnosis rather than applying the IPC branch.

diagnostics.finding: The module supply measurement does not exceed 11 volts.
diagnostics.meaning: The required supply has not been established.
diagnostics.next: Check the body control module (BCM) fuse: RCM 35 (5A), OCSM 22 (5A), or SCCM/IPC 13 (7.5A). With an intact fuse, repair the circuit; with a failed fuse, investigate the short using the wiring diagrams.

diagnostics.finding: A specified ground or network continuity test fails its less-than-3-ohms limit.
diagnostics.meaning: The tested connection does not satisfy that branch's continuity requirement.
diagnostics.next: Repair the affected wire or, for D3, the RCM case ground before continuing.

verification.title: Confirm communication and restraint readiness
verification.body: Restore connections and power as directed, then confirm the affected module responds. The SRS must be fully operational and free of faults before vehicle release.

verification.title: Record the completed diagnosis
verification.body: Record the missing module, decisive readings, connector repairs and final communication result, including SRS fault status where applicable.

guides.title: Diagnose missing communication with body, information-center and front-control modules
guides.summary: Trace an unresponsive module through its power supply, ground, network wiring and connectors before reaching the appropriate repair decision.
guides.introduction: Vehicle modules exchange commands and status over paired Controller Area Network (CAN) wires. The diagnostic scan tool reaches high-speed CAN networks 1 and 2 directly through the data link connector (DLC). Gateway Module A (GWM) translates messages for medium-speed CAN (MS-CAN) and high-speed CAN 3 (HS-CAN3). These tests identify why particular modules cannot answer the scan tool.
guides.why: A module needs electrical power, a sound ground and an intact communication path to respond. Testing those separately distinguishes wiring and connector faults from a module concern. The front-controls test also checks network termination, so its sequence differs from the other branches.
searchTerms: ICM not responding to scan tool

when.summary: When the scan tool currently cannot communicate with the ICM, BCM, BCMB or FCIM.
notes: Confirm the affected module is fitted and the communication concern is present before following a replacement decision.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, Rotunda Flex Probes and the branch's wiring diagrams. Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Review related trouble codes and previous repairs.

prepare.title: Follow each electrical setup
prepare.detail: Observe the specified ignition, battery-cable and connector sequence at every measurement. Voltage present during resistance testing can corrupt results, and forced probes can damage terminals.

steps.title: Choose the module-specific path
steps.body: Identify the missing module in [Communications Network diagnosis](#/document/G1813071). Tests H and I check high-speed CAN 1 (HS-CAN1) connections to the DLC. Tests J and K check MS-CAN connections to the gateway, which carries diagnostic messages through high-speed CAN 2 (HS-CAN2).

steps.title: Test H: information center module
steps.body: For an unresponsive information center module (ICM), check supply voltage, ground and both HS-CAN1 wires to the DLC. The supply must exceed 11 volts; ground and each network continuity measurement must be below 3 ohms. A failed supply check leads to body control module fuse 32 (10A) and its circuit.

steps.title: Test I: body control module
steps.body: For the body control module (BCM), first check battery junction box fuse 7 (60A). Follow I1–I3 through the supply, all specified ground circuits and both HS-CAN1 connections to the DLC. Repair failed circuits before proceeding to connector inspection and the module decision.

steps.title: Test J: body control module B
steps.body: For body control module B (BCMB), check BCM fuses 28 (20A) and 36 (15A), both supply feeds, ground and both MS-CAN wires to the gateway. Each supply must exceed 11 volts; ground and network continuity must be below 3 ohms. A good feed alone does not establish that both supplies are intact.

steps.title: Test K: front controls interface module
steps.body: For the front controls interface module (FCIM), disconnect the negative battery cable, scan-tool cable and gateway connector as directed. Measure MS-CAN termination: 108–132 ohms advances to supply and ground checks. Outside that range, test both FCIM-to-gateway wires; passing continuity advances directly to K5. The supply branch includes BCM fuse 12 (7.5A).

steps.title: Inspect connectors and follow the correct endpoint
steps.body: Repair corrosion, damaged terminals and pushed-out pins in the affected module and in-line connectors. Reconnect securely and retest operation. If the concern remains, check Ford's OASIS service-information system for applicable technical service bulletins and follow any that apply. With none applicable, H and J direct ICM or BCMB replacement. I and K require the vehicle identification number (VIN) to access the BCM or FCIM guided routine.

watchFor.title: An unloaded supply reading has limits
watchFor.body: A normal voltage reading with the module disconnected does not exclude excessive resistance under load.

watchFor.title: A blown fuse needs investigation
watchFor.body: Use the wiring diagrams to identify possible circuit shorts before considering the supply fault resolved.

notes: For BCM and FCIM, reaching the VIN-dependent guided routine is a diagnostic handoff, not authorization to replace the module.

diagnostics.finding: A supply, ground or network measurement fails its branch limit.
diagnostics.meaning: The electrical path required for communication has not passed.
diagnostics.next: Repair the identified circuit or investigate its fuse before advancing.

diagnostics.finding: Communication returns after connectors are reseated.
diagnostics.meaning: A connector or terminal problem may have caused the concern.
diagnostics.next: Address its root cause rather than leaving a temporary recovery.

diagnostics.finding: The front control/display interface module (FCDIM) does not respond.
diagnostics.meaning: Its diagnostic route uses HS-CAN3 through the gateway to HS-CAN2.
diagnostics.next: Check BCM fuse 32 (10A), then continue the FCDIM-specific diagnosis; H–K do not complete that path.

verification.title: Repeat the communication and operation checks
verification.body: Restore test-disconnected connections and the battery cable as directed, reconnect the scan tool and confirm whether the affected module responds and the system operates correctly.

verification.title: Record the outcome
verification.body: Record the failed check, repair and communication result. If a guided routine is required, record that next step without marking the module concern resolved.

guides.title: Diagnose a SYNC display, audio, GPS or interface module that will not communicate
guides.summary: Check the affected module's power, ground and equipment-specific network connections before following its replacement or guided-test endpoint.
guides.introduction: Vehicle modules exchange commands and status over paired communication wires. The gateway module (GWM) transfers diagnostic messages between networks. Consequently, a module missing from a scan-tool session may have lost power, ground or its communication path. Tests L–O distinguish these causes for the display, audio, positioning and SYNC interface modules.
guides.why: The modules do not all use the same network route. In particular, touchscreen and non-touchscreen APIM installations assign some connector pins differently. Correct equipment identification and terminal-safe measurements are essential to avoid misleading results or damage.
searchTerms: display module not responding to scan tool

when.summary: When the diagnostic scan tool cannot communicate with the display, ACM, GPSM or APIM.
notes: Use the test for the module actually missing from the network test; an entertainment-system symptom alone does not select a replacement.

prepare.title: Confirm the fault and electrical condition
prepare.detail: Verify the concern is present, check battery and charging operation, and confirm battery state of charge exceeds 70%. Record network results and diagnostic trouble codes; address circuit-related codes first.

prepare.title: Prepare for accurate measurements
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, wiring diagrams and Rotunda Flex Probes or the specified terminal probe kit. Follow ignition and connector states exactly. Resistance checks require unpowered circuits; disconnect the battery for ground-resistance measurements as described in Diagnostic Methods.

steps.title: Check the affected module's supply
steps.body: Switch ignition OFF and disconnect the applicable connector: display C2123, audio C240A, GPSM C2398 or APIM C2383. With ignition ON, each test checks pin 1 to ground for greater than 11 volts. A failed result requires checking body control module (BCM) fuse 32 (10A), except the audio module uses fuse 33 (20A). With a sound fuse, repair the supply circuit; with a failed fuse, investigate the short using the wiring diagrams.

steps.title: L: test the front control/display interface module
steps.body: With ignition OFF, check the front control/display interface module (FCDIM) ground at C2123 pin 9. Then check its high-speed controller area network 3 (HS-CAN3) paths: C2123 pins 4 and 5 connect to GWM C2431 pins 16 and 15 respectively. Each resistance must be less than 3 ohms. Repair a failing circuit before continuing to L4.

steps.title: M: test the audio control module
steps.body: Check the audio control module (ACM) ground at C240A pin 13. Disconnect GWM C2431 for the network checks: C240A pins 14 and 15 connect to C2431 pins 16 and 15 respectively. Each ground or network resistance must be less than 3 ohms. The ACM communicates through HS-CAN3 and the gateway to the scan tool's HS-CAN2 connection.

steps.title: N: test the positioning module
steps.body: Check the global positioning system module (GPSM) ground at C2398 pin 6. With GWM C2431 disconnected, check C2398 pins 2 and 3 to C2431 pins 23 and 22 respectively. Each resistance must be less than 3 ohms. These are medium-speed controller area network (MS-CAN) paths; the gateway transfers diagnostic messages to HS-CAN2.

steps.title: O: select the correct APIM wiring branch
steps.body: The accessory protocol interface module (APIM) uses C2383 grounds 37 and 38 in the non-touchscreen branch, and 37 in the touchscreen branch. Check HS-CAN1 from pins 53/54 to data link connector C251 pins 6/14. With GWM C2431 disconnected, non-touchscreen HS-CAN3 uses C2383 pins 16/17 to gateway pins 16/15; touchscreen HS-CAN3 uses 19/20 to 16/15. Touchscreen equipment additionally checks MS-CAN from 16/17 to gateway 23/22. Each resistance must be less than 3 ohms.

steps.title: Inspect connections before the final decision
steps.body: Switch ignition OFF and inspect the affected module and related in-line connectors. Clean module pins and renew corroded connectors or terminals, damaged pins and pushed-out pins as directed. Reconnect until fully seated and latched, then retest. A persistent fault requires checking applicable Ford technical service bulletins. Without an applicable bulletin, L, M and N direct module replacement using the specified equipment-matched procedure; O directs a vehicle-identification-number-specific APIM guided routine.

watchFor.title: Passing voltage with an unloaded connector
watchFor.body: The supply check identifies an open feed; it does not prove the circuit can carry its operating load without excessive voltage loss.

watchFor.title: Damaged terminals or invalid resistance readings
watchFor.body: Do not force meter probes into terminals or measure resistance on powered circuits. Repair the actual connection fault rather than relying on temporarily improved contact after reconnection.

notes: Use the less-than-3-ohm limits specified by these pinpoint tests.
If the complaint disappears during testing, do not continue to a module-replacement verdict without reproducing it.

diagnostics.finding: Power, ground and the specified network paths pass, but the module still does not respond.
diagnostics.meaning: The test has reached connector inspection and the service-information decision, not automatic proof of internal failure.
diagnostics.next: Complete L4, M4, N4 or O6 and follow its particular endpoint.

diagnostics.finding: The audio digital signal processing module also fails to respond.
diagnostics.meaning: The DSP uses HS-CAN3 through the gateway and HS-CAN2; possible causes include its fuse, wiring, terminals, connectors or module.
diagnostics.next: Check BCM fuse 27 (30A), then continue its dedicated diagnosis. This preliminary check does not justify replacement.

verification.title: Confirm communication and operation
verification.body: After repair and reconnection, repeat the network check and operate the affected system to confirm the original concern is absent.

verification.title: Record the electrical result
verification.body: Record the equipment branch, connector and pin pairs tested, measured voltage and resistances, repaired fault and final scan-tool response.
