guides.title: Diagnose scan-tool communication loss at audio, radio transceiver, steering or driver-seat modules
guides.summary: Check the nonresponding module's supplies, grounds, network wiring and connectors before following its specific repair decision.
guides.introduction: The controller area network (CAN) carries messages over paired wires. High-speed (HS-CAN) and medium-speed (MS-CAN) branches reach the scan tool through the data link connector (DLC). The gateway module (GWM) translates traffic between branches. A module can disappear from a scan because its electrical supply or communication path has failed.
guides.why: A module needs power, ground and an intact message path to answer. Checking these separately distinguishes a wiring fault from a module fault, while the final connector inspection can expose intermittent contact problems.
searchTerms: audio DSP not responding to scan tool
power steering module scan tool nonresponse

when.summary: When an installed audio, radio transceiver, steering or driver-seat module currently fails to answer the scan tool.
notes: Replacement decisions require the nonresponse to be present during testing.

prepare.title: Tools and test capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, Rotunda Flex Probes and the branch-specific wiring diagrams. You need live-voltage and isolated-resistance testing skills and access to the module and related connectors.

prepare.title: Electrical readiness
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Follow Diagnostic Methods, including battery disconnection for ground-resistance measurements. Body control module (BCM) and battery junction box (BJB) fuse locations differ by branch.

steps.title: Confirm and document nonresponse
steps.body: Choose the matching [pinpoint test P–S](#/document/G1813071). Record related diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), inspect previous repairs and damaged wiring, and diagnose circuit DTCs before performance concerns.

steps.title: Check every supply
steps.body: Switch ignition off and disconnect the specified module connectors. Switch on for voltage measurements: each listed feed must exceed 11 volts. Steering and driver-seat tests each check two feeds. If a reading fails, check the designated fuse; repair an open feed or investigate the cause of a blown fuse.

steps.title: Check the grounds
steps.body: Switch ignition off and establish the prescribed isolated test conditions. Each listed ground must measure less than 3 ohms. Check both driver-seat module grounds. Repair a failed ground before progressing.

steps.title: Check both network conductors
steps.body: Follow the branch's connector-disconnection instructions. DSP, radio transceiver and driver-seat paths are tested to the disconnected gateway; steering is tested to the DLC. Each conductor must measure less than 3 ohms. Repair any failing path.

steps.title: Repair connector defects and retest
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect module and related in-line connectors. Clean module pins or replace corroded connectors/terminals; replace damaged, bent or pushed-out pins as appropriate. Restore disconnected connections, ensure they latch, and check whether the module now responds.

steps.title: Follow the correct final decision
steps.body: If nonresponse persists, check Ford OASIS service information for technical service bulletins (TSBs). Follow an applicable bulletin. Otherwise use the module-specific destination below; the steering branch requires further guided diagnosis.

watchFor.title: Unloaded voltage has limits
watchFor.body: A disconnected supply passing its voltage check does not establish its ability to carry current. Excessive resistance under load requires appropriate voltage-drop diagnosis.

notes: Find the cause of a failed circuit before adding wiring or replacing a fuse.

diagnostics.finding: The audio digital signal processing (DSP) module does not respond: Test P.
diagnostics.meaning: Its supply, ground or HS-CAN3 connection to the gateway may be open.
diagnostics.next: Check BCM fuse 27 (30A) and complete P. Persistent nonresponse after the checks and bulletin review directs DSP replacement.

diagnostics.finding: The radio transceiver module (RTM) does not respond: Test Q.
diagnostics.meaning: It communicates on MS-CAN through the gateway to HS-CAN2.
diagnostics.next: Check BCM fuse 32 (10A) and complete Q. If all checks pass and no bulletin applies, replace the RTM.

diagnostics.finding: The power steering control module (PSCM) does not respond: Test R.
diagnostics.meaning: It communicates with the scan tool through HS-CAN2.
diagnostics.next: Check the BJB high-current MIDI fuse (125A) and fuse 64 (5A). After R and bulletin review, persistent nonresponse leads to the electric power-assisted steering (EPAS) symptom chart; its guided routine requires the vehicle identification number (VIN).

diagnostics.finding: The driver seat module (DSM) does not respond: Test S.
diagnostics.meaning: Its MS-CAN messages reach the scan tool through the gateway and HS-CAN2.
diagnostics.next: Check BJB fuse 12 (30A) and BCM fuse 2 (7.5A). After S passes and no bulletin applies, persistent nonresponse directs DSM replacement.

diagnostics.finding: The front seat climate control module (SCME) does not respond.
diagnostics.meaning: It also uses MS-CAN through the gateway and HS-CAN2.
diagnostics.next: Check BJB fuse 14 (30A), then continue the SCME-specific diagnosis. This preliminary check does not establish a replacement decision.

verification.title: Confirm restored communication
verification.body: Operate the system after reconnecting and confirm the affected module answers the scan tool. If reseating restored operation, correct the underlying connector or pin problem.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record the original nonresponse, supply/ground/network measurements, connector repairs and final communication result or required guided-diagnosis destination.

guides.title: Diagnose seat climate, door or left side obstacle modules that will not communicate
guides.summary: Check module power, ground, network continuity and connectors before deciding whether an unresponsive module needs replacement.
guides.introduction: These modules exchange commands and status over the medium-speed Controller Area Network (MS-CAN), a shared wire pair. The gateway module translates messages between MS-CAN and the high-speed network HS-CAN2 used by the diagnostic scan tool. A missing response can therefore originate in the module's electrical connections rather than its electronics.
guides.why: Each pinpoint test checks supply, ground and communication wiring before evaluating the module. Following that order prevents an open wire, damaged terminal or failed fuse from being mistaken for module failure.
searchTerms: left side obstacle module not communicating

when.summary: When one of the named modules currently fails to respond to the diagnostic scan tool.

prepare.title: Confirm test readiness
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, verify battery state of charge exceeds 70%, and scan all modules for related diagnostic trouble codes. The no-response concern must be present.

prepare.title: Prepare for electrical measurements
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, required Rotunda Flex Probes and wiring diagrams. Follow Diagnostic Methods for resistance-test isolation, including battery disconnection for ground-resistance measurements.

steps.title: Choose the module-specific test
steps.body: Select T, U, V or W using the findings below. Use its connector views and exact probe locations in [Communications Network](#/document/G1813071); similar test sequences do not make the connectors interchangeable.

steps.title: Check the supply circuits
steps.body: With ignition off, disconnect the specified module connector; switch ignition on for voltage measurements. Each specified feed must exceed 11 volts. If it fails, check the designated fuse. With a good fuse, repair the feed; with a failed fuse, use wiring diagrams to identify possible short-circuit causes.

steps.title: Check the ground
steps.body: Switch ignition off and follow the resistance-test isolation requirements. The specified ground path must measure less than 3 ohms. Repair a failing circuit before continuing.

steps.title: Check both network wires
steps.body: Disconnect the specified module network connection and gateway connector C2431. Each MS-CAN wire must measure less than 3 ohms end to end. Test T additionally requires disconnecting SCME connector C3265C. Repair whichever circuit fails.

steps.title: Inspect and restore connections
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect module and related in-line connectors. For corrosion, install new connectors or terminals and clean module pins. Replace damaged or bent terminals/pins, and pushed-out pins as necessary. Reconnect everything fully, ensuring connectors seat and latch.

steps.title: Make the final branch decision
steps.body: Operate the system again. If the concern persists, check Ford's OASIS service-information system for applicable technical service bulletins. Follow an applicable bulletin instead of continuing this test. Without one, the test directs replacement of the affected module through its separate installation procedure.

watchFor.title: An unloaded voltage pass has limits
watchFor.body: The disconnected supply check detects opens but does not establish that the circuit can carry its operating load.

watchFor.title: A recovered connection still needs attention
watchFor.body: If reseating restores operation, address the root cause of connector or pin damage.

notes: For right-hand side obstacle module nonresponse, the preliminary check is battery junction box fuse 66 (5A). Continue with right-hand-specific diagnosis; Test W's connector assignments apply to the left-hand module.

diagnostics.finding: The front seat climate control module (SCME) does not respond.
diagnostics.meaning: Test T applies and checks two supply feeds.
diagnostics.next: Use T1–T4; the designated fuse is battery junction box (BJB) fuse 14 (30A).

diagnostics.finding: The driver door module (DDM) does not respond.
diagnostics.meaning: Test U applies to the driver-door communication path.
diagnostics.next: Verify BJB fuse 11 (30A), then follow U1–U4.

diagnostics.finding: The passenger door module (PDM) does not respond.
diagnostics.meaning: Test V applies; its fuse location differs from the driver's.
diagnostics.next: Verify body control module (BCM) fuse 26 (30A), then follow V1–V4.

diagnostics.finding: The left-hand side obstacle detection control module (SOD-L) does not respond.
diagnostics.meaning: Test W applies to the left-hand module.
diagnostics.next: Verify BJB fuse 66 (5A), then follow W1–W4.

verification.title: Confirm recovery
verification.body: After reconnection, operate the system and confirm whether the original no-response concern remains.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the tested module, supply and resistance readings, connector repairs and final response status.

Side obstacle module removal and installation if Test W directs left-module replacement.

applicability.equipment: Front seat climate control, driver/passenger door modules or side obstacle detection, as applicable

guides.title: Diagnose nonresponding obstacle, cruise, display and roof modules
guides.summary: Check power, ground, communication wiring and connector condition before replacing a module that does not respond to the scan tool.
guides.introduction: Vehicle modules exchange commands and status over paired communication wires. Some connect directly to the diagnostic scan tool through the data link connector (DLC); others communicate through the gateway module (GWM). A missing response can therefore result from lost power, a poor ground, broken communication wiring or a connector fault as well as the module itself.
guides.why: Following the electrical path in order prevents a wiring fault from being mistaken for a failed controller. Connector inspection remains necessary even when continuity measurements pass.
searchTerms: right side obstacle module not responding
head up display module not responding
scan tool cannot communicate with module

when.summary: When a fitted module covered by Tests X, Y, Z or AA does not respond to the diagnostic scan tool.
notes: Confirm fitted equipment before selecting a branch; the module list does not establish equipment on every vehicle.

prepare.title: Prepare for electrical diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use a compatible diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, required Rotunda Flex Probes and vehicle wiring diagrams. Check battery and charging operation, confirm battery state of charge exceeds 70%, and inspect previous repairs.

prepare.title: Protect terminals and measurement validity
prepare.detail: Use the specified connector disconnections and ignition states. Follow Diagnostic Methods for battery isolation during resistance testing; do not force probes into terminals or use back-probing for continuity checks.

steps.title: Confirm which fitted module is missing
steps.body: Verify the current nonresponse and check other modules for related diagnostic trouble codes. Select X for right-hand side obstacle detection, Y for adaptive cruise, Z for the collision-warning head up display, or AA for moveable roof module A. Do not replace a module for a concern that is absent.

steps.title: Establish that supply voltage reaches the module
steps.body: With ignition off, disconnect the selected module; switch ignition on for its supply measurement. Each branch requires greater than 11 volts. A failed reading directs a fuse check, then circuit repair if the fuse is sound. A failed fuse requires investigation of possible shorts using the wiring diagrams.

steps.title: Check the ground path
steps.body: Switch ignition off and follow the branch's ground measurements. Each specified ground must measure less than 3 ohms. Test both grounds in Test X. Repair a failed ground before advancing, because the controller needs a complete electrical path to operate.

steps.title: Check both communication wires
steps.body: Use the exact connector pairs in the linked pinpoint test. X and AA test the medium-speed Controller Area Network (MS-CAN) to the disconnected gateway. Y and Z test high-speed Controller Area Network 2 (HS-CAN2) to the DLC. Each wire must measure less than 3 ohms; repair the circuit that fails.

steps.title: Inspect connections and make the replacement decision
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect module and related in-line connectors. Replace corroded connectors or terminals and clean module pins; replace damaged, bent or pushed-out terminals as directed. Reconnect and latch everything, then operate the system. If the concern persists, check applicable technical service bulletins through OASIS and follow any relevant bulletin. Only when none applies does the branch direct module replacement using its matching procedure.

steps.title: Recognize the separate roof-module B starting point
steps.body: Moveable roof control module B (MRCMB) also communicates over MS-CAN through the gateway to HS-CAN2. Its preliminary check is BJB fuse 15 (20A). Continue with its dedicated diagnosis after that check; Test AA's module-A measurements do not establish a module-B replacement decision.

watchFor.title: Voltage without current capability
watchFor.body: An unloaded voltage reading can identify an open supply but cannot establish that a circuit is free of excessive resistance.

watchFor.title: A connection that works after reseating
watchFor.body: Find and correct the terminal or connector defect; temporary recovery alone does not explain the root cause.

notes: BJB means battery junction box. Obtain the vehicle-specific replacement procedure before removing a roof controller.

diagnostics.finding: The right-hand side obstacle detection control module does not respond: Test X.
diagnostics.meaning: The SODR branch checks its supply, both grounds and MS-CAN connection to the gateway.
diagnostics.next: Use connector C4370 and BJB fuse 66 (5A), then follow X1–X4.

diagnostics.finding: The adaptive cruise control module does not respond: Test Y.
diagnostics.meaning: The cruise control module (CCM) communicates with the scan tool through HS-CAN2.
diagnostics.next: Use connector C1582 and BJB fuse 66 (5A), then follow Y1–Y4.

diagnostics.finding: The collision-warning head up display module does not respond: Test Z.
diagnostics.meaning: The head up display (HUD) module also uses HS-CAN2.
diagnostics.next: Use connector C2395 and BJB fuse 66 (5A), then follow Z1–Z4.

diagnostics.finding: Moveable roof control module A does not respond: Test AA.
diagnostics.meaning: The MRCMA diagnostic path passes through the gateway from MS-CAN to HS-CAN2.
diagnostics.next: Use connector C4830 and BJB fuse 17 (20A), then follow AA1–AA4.

verification.title: Confirm restored operation
verification.body: After connector or circuit repair, reconnect and latch the specified connectors and repeat the operation that exposed the concern. Recheck the original scan-tool nonresponse.

verification.title: Record the basis for the decision
verification.body: Keep the module identity, supply and resistance readings, connector findings and post-repair response together. Replacement should follow the completed branch, not the initial missing response alone.

guides.title: Trace HS-CAN2 communication loss when all modules stop responding
guides.summary: Use connector checks, electrical measurements and controlled module isolation to identify supported repair routes for a complete HS-CAN2 communication failure.
guides.introduction: High-speed controller area network 2 (HS-CAN2) carries messages over a shared twisted wire pair. A wiring fault, poor diagnostic connection or one connected module can disrupt communication across that pair. Pinpoint Test AE separates these possibilities when all HS-CAN2 modules fail to respond; it does not treat widespread communication loss as proof that several modules have failed.
guides.why: Resistance readings require an unpowered circuit, while voltage checks require the specified powered condition. Fresh scan results are equally important: the network-test application can otherwise display an earlier result and falsely suggest that disconnecting a module changed nothing.
searchTerms: scan tool cannot communicate with modules
modules stop working when scan tool connected

when.summary: When all HS-CAN2 modules fail a fresh network test and the communication concern is currently present.
notes: Do not authorize module replacement through this test when the original concern is absent.
Adaptive cruise control, head-up display and vehicle-dynamics branches apply only after confirming the equipment is fitted.

prepare.title: Establish a reliable starting condition
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging-system operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Review previous repairs, relevant service information and accessible diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Investigate related circuit faults and obvious wiring, fuse or connector damage.

prepare.title: Provide the correct diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a network-capable scan tool, digital multimeter, wiring/connector information and proper flex probes. AE1 specifies the violet Rotunda probe 300-08039 for terminal fit. Restraint-module connector work requires supplemental restraint system depowering and repowering procedures; fuse isolation is not a substitute for those precautions.

steps.title: Check the diagnostic connection — AE1–AE2
steps.body: With ignition off and the scan cable disconnected, inspect data link connector (DLC) pins 3, 4, 5, 11 and 16. If fit or damage concerns exist, check applicable OASIS service articles and follow them; without an applicable article, AE1 directs replacement of Gateway Module A (GWM). Otherwise inspect GWM connector C2431, repair terminal faults, latch it securely and retest. Continue only if the concern remains.

steps.title: Measure termination, ground isolation and voltage — AE3–AE5
steps.body: Disconnect battery negative and measure between C251 pins 3 and 11. A reading of 54–66 ohms leads to AE4; anything else leads to AE6. At AE4, both pins must measure greater than 1,000 ohms to ground; otherwise use AE12. If they pass, reconnect battery negative and turn ignition on for AE5. More than 6 volts on either circuit requires circuit repair; otherwise continue to AE13.

steps.title: Follow the abnormal-resistance branch — AE6–AE10
steps.body: At AE6, 108–132 ohms leads to AE7: disconnect GWM C2431 and repeat. The same range leads to AE8; another result leads to GWM confirmation at AE23. AE8 disconnects steering column control module (SCCM) C226A and checks C226A pin 3 to C251 pin 3, and pin 4 to pin 11. Both below 3 ohms lead to AE29; otherwise repair the circuit. If AE6 was outside its range, AE9 sends a reading below 3 ohms to AE11. Otherwise AE10 directs DLC/circuit repair above 10,000 ohms; other readings require waiting 5 minutes and repeating the pinpoint test because a module capacitor may still be discharging. Repair the circuit if the concern persists.

steps.title: Isolate a measured short — AE11–AE12
steps.body: Disconnect fitted modules one at a time using the listed connectors: anti-lock brake system (ABS), cruise control module (CCM), head-up display (HUD), occupant classification system module (OCSM), power steering control module (PSCM), restraints control module (RCM), SCCM and vehicle dynamics control module (VDM). AE11 looks for line-to-line resistance rising above 3 ohms; AE12 looks for resistance to ground rising above 1,000 ohms. A change routes respectively to AE22, AE24, AE25, AE27, AE26, AE28, AE29 or AE30. Without a change, repair the circuits; AE12 also directs reconnecting all modules.

steps.title: Separate gateway, steering-column and brake routes — AE13–AE15
steps.body: Use the exact fuse removals in the linked test. Close and reopen the network-test application before every rerun. AE13 disables GWM and SCCM together: if all other modules pass, restore the fuse and use AE14; otherwise restore it and use AE15. AE14 disconnects SCCM: a pass requires reconnecting it and continuing to Test F; a failure leads to Test AC. AE15 disables ABS: restore its fuses after testing, then use Test B if the others pass, or AE16 if they do not.

steps.title: Check optional equipment and steering assistance — AE16–AE19
steps.body: AE16 checks for adaptive cruise control or vehicle dynamics. If absent, go to AE19. If fitted, AE17 disables the applicable CCM/HUD or VDM supplies. Restore the removed fuses: a pass leads to AE18, a failure to AE19. AE18 tests with HUD disconnected, then with VDM disconnected, where fitted. HUD isolation restoring communication requires reconnecting HUD before Test Z; VDM isolation restoring it leads to Test C. Otherwise reconnect the modules and use Test Y. AE19 disables PSCM: restore its fuses, then use Test R if other modules pass, or AE20 if they do not.

steps.title: Follow the supported restraint-system isolation route — AE20–AE21
steps.body: AE20 disables RCM and OCSM through their specified fuses. If all other modules pass, reinstall the fuses and proceed to AE21. Using the required restraint precautions, AE21 tests with RCM C310B disconnected. Reconnect C310B after either result: a pass leads to Test D, a failure to Test E. If AE20 continues to fail, stop this route and record the unresolved communication loss; that result does not establish a replacement decision.

steps.title: Confirm the implicated module’s connections — AE22–AE30
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect the named module’s connectors and specified in-line connectors. Replace corroded connectors or terminals and clean module pins; replace damaged, bent or pushed-out pins as required. Reconnect securely and operate the system. If the concern disappears, address the connection fault’s root cause. If it persists, check applicable technical service bulletins and follow their instructions. Without an applicable bulletin, these branches direct replacement of the corresponding module, except AE26: persistent PSCM concerns go to the electric power-assisted steering symptom chart and its vehicle-identification-number-dependent guided routine.

watchFor.title: Symptoms appear when the scan tool is connected
watchFor.body: Spread DLC ground terminals 4 and 5 can leave the scan tool improperly grounded and corrupt network traffic. Investigate terminal fit before interpreting the resulting module failures.

watchFor.title: Invalid measurements
watchFor.body: Keep the battery disconnected for resistance testing and follow AE5’s powered conditions for voltage testing. Do not force probes into terminals or use airbag igniter circuits as network test points.

notes: HS-CAN3 diagnostic messages reach the scan tool through GWM and HS-CAN2. Its separate fault context lists fuses, wiring/terminals/connectors, GWM and the fitted audio, infotainment, display and instrument-cluster modules as possible sources. Loss of access alone does not identify one of those modules as defective; Pinpoint Test AF is a separate investigation.

diagnostics.finding: Communication or resistance changes when one module is isolated.
diagnostics.meaning: The result selects that module’s confirmation or dedicated diagnostic route; it does not independently prove internal failure.
diagnostics.next: Follow the named branch, including connector repair and applicable service-information checks.

diagnostics.finding: Other modules still fail the network test at AE20.
diagnostics.meaning: The supported isolation route has reached an unresolved result.
diagnostics.next: Record the failed AE20 result without assigning a pass, replacement module or presumed recovery.

verification.title: Verify the completed route
verification.body: Complete its specified fuse and connector reconnections and required restraint-system repowering. Operate the system and obtain fresh network-test results. Clear DTCs from all modules after completing diagnosis because isolation itself can set network codes.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record measurements, isolated modules, fresh network responses, connector repairs and the resulting test destination. Keep a persistent negative AE20 result explicitly unresolved.

guides.title: Trace loss of HS-CAN3 communication across all modules
guides.summary: Check the diagnostic connection, measure the network circuits and isolate fitted modules to identify the next diagnostic route.
guides.introduction: High-speed controller area network 3 (HS-CAN3) carries module messages over a twisted pair of wires. Gateway Module A (GWM) transfers those messages to HS-CAN2 so the diagnostic scan tool can read them. When every HS-CAN3 module stops responding, the shared wiring, gateway path and diagnostic connection all need consideration.
guides.why: A connection fault or one module affecting the shared wires can interrupt communication with several modules. Isolation identifies the next check; it does not, by itself, prove that the disconnected module needs replacement.
searchTerms: modules become inoperative with scan tool connected

when.summary: When a current network test shows every HS-CAN3 module unresponsive.
notes: Module-replacement decisions require the concern to be present during testing.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a network-capable scan tool, digital multimeter, connector information and Ford service-article access. The work requires competent live-voltage testing and terminal repair.

prepare.title: Protect terminals and readings
prepare.detail: Verify battery state of charge exceeds 70%. Have the specified violet Rotunda 300-08039 flex probe for the diagnostic socket. Follow each branch's ignition and disconnection conditions; voltage present during resistance measurement can invalidate the result.

steps.title: Check the diagnostic connection — AF1–AF3
steps.body: With ignition off and the scan-tool cable removed, inspect data link connector (DLC) pins 3, 4, 5, 11 and 16. Damage or poor fit requires checking applicable service articles; follow a matching article, or the GWM replacement route if none applies. Otherwise inspect and repair GWM connector C2431, reconnect securely and operate the system. If the concern persists, network-test the restraints control module (RCM). A pass leads to AF4; failure transfers diagnosis to HS-CAN2 Pinpoint Test AE.

steps.title: Measure termination and unwanted connections — AF4–AF6
steps.body: Disconnect GWM C2431. Resistance between harness pins 16 and 15 must be 108–132 ohms to proceed to AF5; otherwise use AF7. AF5 checks each pin to ground: both readings must exceed 1,000 ohms, otherwise use AF12. Passing readings lead to AF6. With ignition on, measure each pin's voltage to ground. A reading above 6 volts requires circuit repair; otherwise continue to AF13.

steps.title: Separate termination faults from open wiring — AF7–AF10
steps.body: AF7 checks the same pins on the GWM component side. A 108–132-ohm result leads to AF9; otherwise AF8 checks the harness side. AF8 passes to AF10 at 108–132 ohms, or to AF26 otherwise. For AF9, disconnect instrument panel cluster (IPC) C220 and check C220 pin 12 to C2431 pin 16, then pin 13 to pin 15. Both below 3 ohms lead to AF24; otherwise repair the affected circuit. AF10 measures between C2431 pins 16 and 15: below 3 ohms leads to AF11, otherwise AF13.

steps.title: Find which disconnection changes a short — AF11–AF12
steps.body: Disconnect modules individually in the specified order: accessory protocol interface module (APIM), audio front control module (ACM), audio digital signal processing module (DSP), front control/display interface module (FCDIM), then IPC. Include optional modules only when fitted. In AF11, look for resistance between the wires to rise above 3 ohms; in AF12, look for resistance to ground above 1,000 ohms. A successful change selects AF21, AF22, AF23, AF25 or AF24 respectively. If no module produces the required change, repair the wiring; AF12 also directs reconnecting all modules.

steps.title: Separate the gateway and cluster routes — AF13–AF14
steps.body: Remove body control module (BCM) fuse 13 (7.5A), run a fresh network test and reinstall the fuse regardless of the result. If all other HS-CAN3 modules pass, AF14 disconnects IPC C220 for another test. Reconnect the IPC afterward: restoration leads to Pinpoint Test G, while continued failure leads to Pinpoint Test AC. If AF13 did not restore communication, proceed to AF15.

steps.title: Follow the fitted display branch — AF15–AF17
steps.body: Without an APIM or FCDIM, continue to AF18. Otherwise AF16 removes BCM fuse 32 (10A), tests communication and reinstalls the fuse. Restoration routes touchscreen equipment to Test O, equipment without SYNC to Test L, and a 4.2-inch display with SYNC to AF17. AF17 again specifies fuse 32 removal, testing and reinstallation: restoration leads to Test O; failure leads to AF18. Failure at AF16 also leads to AF18.

steps.title: Test audio isolation and recognize the stopping point — AF18–AF20
steps.body: AF18 removes BCM fuse 33 (20A), tests and reinstalls it. Restoration leads to Test M. Otherwise check whether a DSP is fitted. With a DSP, AF20 removes BCM fuse 27 (30A); restoration leads to Test P after reinstalling removed fuses. If no DSP is fitted, or AF20 does not restore communication, restore the test configuration and stop this diagnostic path. Communication remains unresolved, and that outcome does not authorize module replacement.

steps.title: Confirm the selected module route — AF21–AF26
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect the selected module's connectors and related in-line connections. Replace corroded connectors or terminals and clean module pins; replace damaged, bent or pushed-out pins as necessary. Reconnect securely and operate the system. Correct the connection's root cause if the concern clears. If it persists, follow any applicable technical service bulletin. Without one, APIM and IPC require vehicle identification number (VIN)-based guided routines; ACM, DSP, FCDIM and GWM follow their specified replacement procedures.

watchFor.title: The scan tool can introduce the symptom
watchFor.body: Spread DLC ground terminals 4 and 5 can leave the scan tool improperly grounded and corrupt network traffic.

watchFor.title: Old results can look like a new test
watchFor.body: Close the network-test application before rerunning it, or the display can revert to the previous results.

notes: Use only the optional-module and display/SYNC branches that match the fitted vehicle equipment.

diagnostics.finding: Other HS-CAN3 modules respond after a module is disabled.
diagnostics.meaning: The change identifies a diagnostic route involving that module or its connections.
diagnostics.next: Follow the specified confirmation check or named pinpoint test before deciding on replacement.

diagnostics.finding: All medium-speed controller area network (MS-CAN) modules are unresponsive.
diagnostics.meaning: This is a separate network complaint, although scan-tool messages also reach it through the gateway and HS-CAN2.
diagnostics.next: Use the MS-CAN diagnostic route and Wiring Diagrams Cell 14. Its possible sources include fuses, wiring, terminals, connectors, the gateway and fitted network modules.

verification.title: Restore and check operation
verification.body: Restore connectors and fuses as prescribed. After a completed correction, operate the system and run a fresh network test. Clear test-generated diagnostic trouble codes from all modules after completing diagnosis.

verification.title: Record the actual outcome
verification.body: Record measurements, isolation changes, fresh network results and the next required test. An unresolved stopping point must not be recorded as healthy communication.

guides.title: Diagnose lost MS-CAN communication and scan-tool power
guides.summary: Separate diagnostic-connector faults, shared network wiring faults and module interference before choosing the appropriate repair path.
guides.introduction: The medium-speed controller area network (MS-CAN) lets body and convenience modules exchange messages over a shared pair of wires. Gateway Module A (GWM) translates those messages for the diagnostic scan tool. When every MS-CAN module stops responding, the common connection deserves attention before individual modules. Pinpoint Test AG addresses that complaint; Test AH separately investigates a data link connector (DLC) that cannot power the scan tool.
guides.why: A poor scan-tool ground can disturb network traffic and create apparent module failures. Disconnecting a module may restore communication, but that result identifies a diagnostic direction rather than proving the module needs replacement. Fresh tests and complete restoration of temporary disconnections make the findings trustworthy.
searchTerms: scan tool will not power up
modules stop working when scan tool connected

when.summary: When all MS-CAN modules fail the network test, or the diagnostic connector cannot power the scan tool.
notes: Confirm the complaint is currently present before following a replacement decision.
Select optional-module branches from the equipment actually fitted.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a network-capable diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, wiring and connector information, and correct terminal adapters. DLC terminal-fit inspection specifies the violet Rotunda flex probe 300-08039. Access to Ford service information and vehicle-identification-number guided routines may be required.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging-system operation, with battery state of charge greater than 70%. Record initial network results and diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Inspect previous repairs, harness damage and common supplies. Disconnect the battery for resistance measurements and restore power only as the relevant voltage or network test directs.

steps.title: Inspect the diagnostic connection first
steps.body: With ignition off and the scan cable disconnected, AG1 checks DLC terminals 3, 4, 5, 11 and 16; AH1 checks 4, 5 and 16. Terminal damage requires the specified Ford service-information check: follow an applicable article, or the directed GWM replacement route if none applies. AG2/AH2 then inspect GWM connector C2431, repair terminal defects, reconnect securely and check whether the complaint remains.

steps.title: Establish which network needs diagnosis
steps.body: AG3 requires the restraints control module (RCM) to pass a network test before continuing with MS-CAN measurements. Failure redirects diagnosis to high-speed controller area network 2 through Test AE. It does not establish an MS-CAN module failure or authorize a replacement.

steps.title: Distinguish termination faults from damaged wiring
steps.body: Follow AG4–AG10 exactly at C2431 pins 23 and 22. The termination checks use 108–132 ohms; component-side and harness-side results lead to different branches. AG9 checks continuity to the front controls interface module (FCIM), with readings less than 3 ohms required. Other branches check shorts to ground, unwanted voltage and the two data wires shorted together. In AG6, voltage greater than 6 volts requires repair of the affected circuit.

steps.title: Isolate a measured short
steps.body: When directed to AG11 or AG12, disconnect the listed fitted modules in the prescribed sequence while monitoring resistance. Recovery means greater than 3 ohms between data wires for AG11, or greater than 1,000 ohms to ground for AG12. A qualifying change selects that module's AG29–AG42 connector-confirmation step. No qualifying change directs circuit repair. Restore temporary disconnections before subsequent operational verification.

steps.title: Use the gateway, control-panel and door isolation checks
steps.body: Enter AG13 only when AG6 or AG10 directs it. AG13–AG16 disable the gateway, FCIM, Body Control Module B, driver door module and passenger door module using their specified fuses. A successful isolation requires every other MS-CAN module to pass a fresh network test; its routes are AC, K, J, U and V respectively. Restore each tested supply and verify the original configuration before another standalone check.

steps.title: Separate the infotainment-related branches
steps.body: AG17 first checks for an accessory protocol interface module (APIM) or global positioning system module (GPSM). AG18 tests their shared supply with the radio transceiver module (RTM), where fitted. Only if all other MS-CAN modules pass does AG19 follow, after restoring the fuse. Its individual GPSM and RTM checks route successful isolation to N and Q. If neither restores communication, Test O applies only under that successful AG18 entry condition; it is not permission to replace the APIM.

steps.title: Check fitted seat and roof modules
steps.body: AG20–AG25 identify the driver front seat module, front seat climate control module and convertible-top equipment before testing their supplies. With all other MS-CAN modules passing, successful isolation routes to S for the driver seat, T for seat climate, AA for roof module A or AB for roof module B. Restore every removed fuse and verify the original configuration. An unsuccessful isolation requires further circuit diagnosis; do not continue with earlier supplies disabled.

steps.title: Keep the side-obstacle checks conditional
steps.body: AG26 checks for left and right side-obstacle detection modules. AG27 disables their shared supply. Only when all other modules pass may you restore that fuse and perform AG28 by disconnecting the right module. If all other modules then pass, reconnect it and follow X; otherwise reconnect it and follow W. Without the successful AG27 result, those AG28 routes are not established.

steps.title: Confirm the directed module endpoint
steps.body: AG29–AG42 require ignition-off inspection of the selected module and inline connectors. Replace damaged terminals or connectors, clean corroded module pins, repair pushed-out pins, latch connections and operate the system again. Persistent concerns require an applicable technical service bulletin check before the directed replacement. APIM and FCIM endpoints instead require vehicle-identification-number guided routines. GPSM replacement information must match the fitted SYNC or touchscreen system.

steps.title: Follow AH separately for missing scan-tool power
steps.body: Begin with AH's specified body-control-module fuse checks. AH3 checks DLC supply: greater than 11 volts leads to DLC ground checks; a lower result leads to gateway supply checks. Insufficient gateway supply requires fuse or circuit diagnosis. AH5/AH6 use ground resistance less than 3 ohms to select scan-tool repair. Failed gateway ground checks lead to AH7 connector inspection and operational confirmation, followed by its bulletin or GWM decision. Keep these decisions within the AH sequence.

watchFor.title: Old network results displayed as new
watchFor.body: Close the Network Test application before rerunning it; otherwise the display can return to the previous results.

watchFor.title: A temporarily working connection
watchFor.body: If reseating a connector removes the complaint, identify and repair the terminal or connection defect responsible. A successful reseat alone does not explain the root cause.

notes: Use the linked test's exact fuse locations, ratings, connector sides and module list. Different equipment branches must not share assumed fuse details.
Module removal, replacement and configuration are separate procedures reached only after the diagnostic conditions are satisfied.

diagnostics.finding: Modules become inoperative only when the scan tool is connected.
diagnostics.meaning: Spread DLC ground terminals can leave the tool improperly grounded and corrupt message traffic.
diagnostics.next: Perform AG1 or AH1 terminal-fit inspection before condemning network modules.

diagnostics.finding: An isolation test fails, or its network retest has not been performed.
diagnostics.meaning: Restored communication has not been demonstrated; the result cannot establish normal operation or a failed module.
diagnostics.next: Restore all temporary disconnections and fuses, retest the original configuration and continue the applicable circuit diagnosis.

verification.title: Verify the complete vehicle configuration
verification.body: Reconnect every temporarily disconnected module and reinstall every removed fuse. Close the test application and run a fresh network test. Claim normal operation only after the required modules pass and the original complaint is absent.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record initial and final network responses, relevant measurements and which isolation changed the result. After completing diagnosis, clear DTCs from all modules because the testing itself can generate network faults.
