guides.title: Start an IDS session when vehicle communication fails
guides.summary: Use manual vehicle identification when IDS cannot establish its initial session, then follow network diagnosis if the powertrain control module remains unresponsive.
guides.introduction: The Integrated Diagnostic System (IDS) first tries to communicate with the powertrain control module (PCM). Once that connection is established, it attempts communication with the other vehicle modules. A failure at this first stage can prevent automatic session setup. This procedure supplies vehicle identification manually so the diagnostic process can continue.
guides.why: The message about missing PCM communication describes a failed connection, not a confirmed defective module. Manual identification separates the session-identification step from the remaining communication problem and provides a clear point at which to continue with network diagnosis.

when.summary: When IDS cannot establish a vehicle session and reports no communication with the powertrain control module.
notes: For push-button-start vehicles, use the Push Button Ignition Switch procedure in section 211-05 to establish the required ignition state.

prepare.title: Scan equipment and identification access
prepare.detail: Have IDS available and access to the PCM label or the vehicle's Detailed Vehicle Specification on the service-information screen. The diagnostic connector is beneath the instrument panel.

prepare.title: Service precautions
prepare.detail: Review the [general health and safety precautions](#/document/G1693189). Disable remote start before work around the vehicle and use the specified eye and ear protection. If accessing the PCM label requires work near cooling fans, follow the fan precautions before approaching them.

steps.title: Attempt the normal session
steps.body: Connect the diagnostic equipment and turn the ignition to RUN, following the applicable ignition-switch procedure. Begin the [IDS session procedure](#/document/G1693129) and allow its initial attempt to communicate with the PCM.

steps.title: Recognize the failed initial connection
steps.body: If a session cannot be established, IDS may report that no communication can be established with the PCM. Remember that the normal attempt to contact other modules follows successful PCM communication.

steps.title: Choose manual identification
steps.body: When IDS asks whether to retry communication, select NO. This moves the process toward entering the vehicle's identifying information manually.

steps.title: Enter a valid PCM identifier
steps.body: Enter a PCM part number, tear tag or calibration number to identify the vehicle and start a session. The PCM label carries its part number and four-character tear tag. If those cannot be found, double-click the vehicle identification number at the upper left of the PTS service-information screen and obtain the tear tag from Detailed Vehicle Specification.

steps.title: Follow the remaining communication fault
steps.body: If communication is still unavailable after manually entering the PCM part number, follow the [Communications Network diagnosis](#/document/G1813071) for a PCM that does not respond to the scan tool. Complete that diagnostic path before making a component-replacement decision.

watchFor.title: Session opening versus communication
watchFor.body: Entering identification and opening a session does not, by itself, demonstrate that PCM or other module communication has been restored.

diagnostics.finding: IDS cannot establish its initial PCM connection.
diagnostics.meaning: Automatic session setup has failed; the message alone does not identify the cause.
diagnostics.next: Select NO at the retry prompt and enter a supported vehicle identifier.

diagnostics.finding: The PCM remains unresponsive after manual identification.
diagnostics.meaning: The communication concern remains beyond the identification step.
diagnostics.next: Continue with the PCM-no-response path in Communications Network diagnosis.

verification.title: Check session and communication separately
verification.body: Confirm whether the vehicle session opens and whether PCM communication is actually available.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the identifier used, the session outcome and any remaining communication message so the next diagnostic phase starts from an established result.

procedures.purpose: IDS session recovery through manual PCM identification when automatic communication fails.
Required general service precautions before diagnostic work.
Follow-on network diagnosis when the PCM still does not respond after manual identification.

guides.title: Replace Gateway Module A and transfer its configuration
guides.summary: Capture the existing gateway configuration before removal, install the replacement and complete programmable module installation.
guides.introduction: Gateway Module A (GWM) translates and forwards messages between vehicle communications networks. Two networks reach the diagnostic scan tool through this gateway rather than connecting directly to it. The module therefore forms part of the diagnostic communication route as well as the vehicle’s shared-message system. Replacement includes transferring its configuration, not just exchanging the mounted unit.
guides.why: The configuration must be uploaded while the original module is still installed, then downloaded into the new module. Starting that process before disconnection preserves the required sequence. The mechanical work is brief, but installation remains incomplete until the scan-tool programming instructions have been followed.

when.summary: When Gateway Module A is to be replaced, with its configuration captured before removal.
notes: These replacement steps do not provide a test that condemns the gateway for a communication complaint.

prepare.title: Provide programming capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of performing programmable module installation (PMI) for the GWM, including configuration upload and download.

prepare.title: Arrange module access and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Identify the module, mounting nuts and electrical connector from the procedure illustration. Have suitable tools and torque equipment for the mounting nuts.

steps.title: Begin PMI with the original module installed
steps.body: Follow [Gateway Module A](#/document/G1693123) and the scan tool’s on-screen instructions to begin PMI. When installing a new module, upload the existing configuration before removing the original unit.

steps.title: Remove the gateway
steps.body: Remove the mounting nuts and withdraw the GWM, then disconnect its electrical connector. Keep this mechanical sequence after the required configuration capture.

steps.title: Connect and mount the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure to reconnect and position the replacement module. Tighten the mounting nuts to 89 lb.in (10 Nm).

steps.title: Complete the configuration transfer
steps.body: Use the diagnostic scan tool to complete GWM PMI, following the on-screen instructions. Download the captured configuration into the replacement module as part of this process.

watchFor.title: Premature disconnection
watchFor.body: Removing the original module before uploading its configuration interrupts the required replacement sequence.

watchFor.title: Incomplete scan-tool procedure
watchFor.body: A physically installed gateway is not a completed replacement. Resolve an interrupted or unavailable PMI process before treating the job as finished.

notes: The vehicle’s diagnostic connector is under the instrument panel; the linked illustration identifies the gateway mounting and connector arrangement.

verification.title: Mechanical installation completed
verification.body: Confirm the electrical connector is reconnected and the module is secured with its mounting nuts tightened to specification.

verification.title: Programming result recorded
verification.body: Record that the original configuration was uploaded and that the replacement module’s PMI process, including configuration download, was completed.

procedures.purpose: Gateway Module A removal and installation, including configuration capture before removal and PMI completion afterward.

guides.title: Diagnose perimeter alarm failures and unwanted activations
guides.summary: Use alarm history, switch inputs and directed circuit tests to distinguish arming, hood-switch, intrusion-sensor and alarm-output faults.
guides.introduction: The body control module (BCM) coordinates the perimeter alarm, using entry-point switches, key information and the intrusion/inclination sensor to recognize unauthorized access. It then operates the horn and lamps. Diagnosis separates a missing input, failed output, wiring problem and incorrect operating condition before selecting a repair.
guides.why: An alarm that stays silent may never have armed, may not detect the entry, or may have an output fault. Unwanted activation requires identifying the recorded trigger. These distinctions prevent a working sensor or BCM from being replaced for a fault elsewhere.

when.summary: When the alarm fails to arm or respond, activates unexpectedly, or stores a relevant BCM fault code.
notes: Replacement decisions in pinpoint tests require the stated concern to be present; use recorded history to investigate intermittent complaints.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, confirm battery state of charge exceeds 70%, inspect previous repairs, wiring and connectors, and retrieve related module codes. Diagnose circuit faults before system-performance faults.

prepare.title: Prepare for circuit testing
prepare.detail: Use the Diagnostic Methods procedure, correct probe adapters and Wiring Diagrams Cell 117. Follow each test's ignition and connector-isolation instructions. Use fused jumpers only where directed.

prepare.title: Workshop capability
prepare.detail: Ford-capable diagnostic scan tool; digital multimeter; correct terminal probe adapters; fused jumper wires; applicable wiring diagrams and Ford diagnostic capability.

steps.title: Identify the complaint and recorded trigger
steps.body: Disarm the alarm before attempting BCM communication. Retrieve codes and, for unwanted activation, record ALARM_EVT_1 through ALARM_EVT_4. Route the complaint through the diagnostic findings below before choosing a pinpoint test.

steps.title: Test A: hood opening does not trigger the alarm
steps.body: Inspect the hood latch for damage. Monitor the hood-switch parameter identification (PID), HOOD_SW, while disconnecting the switch. An AJAR reading directs latch replacement. Otherwise, test the input for a short to ground; repair a failed circuit or proceed to the BCM connection check.

steps.title: Test B: intrusion sensing does not trigger the alarm
steps.body: Inspect BCM fuse 18 (5A), then test sensor supply and ground. Missing supply with a sound fuse requires a supply-wire continuity check; a sound wire directs BCM assessment. With supply and ground satisfactory, test the LIN circuit for shorts to voltage, shorts to ground and an open. Inspect the overhead-console harness before replacing the sensor. Repair harness faults or replace the console as directed. Initialize a replacement sensor, retest, and proceed to BCM assessment if the concern remains.

steps.title: Test C: no arming or turn-signal confirmation
steps.body: Close the hood before the BCM self-test and resolve retrieved codes first. Then check closed-door and closed-luggage-lid indications, hazard-lamp operation and remote keyless entry (RKE) lock/unlock operation in order. Follow the corresponding lighting, instrumentation or entry-system diagnostic branch when a check fails. If these checks pass, assess BCM connections.

steps.title: Test D: investigate B1305:01
steps.body: Follow the specified fused-jumper tests for the hood switch. If substituting the closed switch clears the code, replace the latch. If grounding the input clears it, repair the switch ground circuit. Remove each jumper after its self-test. If the code persists, test input-wire continuity before proceeding to BCM assessment.

steps.title: Resolve the common BCM branch
steps.body: Inspect BCM connectors for corrosion, bent or damaged terminals and pushed-out pins; repair them as directed and reconnect securely. Retest the concern. If it remains, check applicable technical service bulletins through OASIS; follow a relevant bulletin or the vehicle-identification-number-specific guided BCM routine. If reconnection resolves it, still correct the underlying connector fault.

watchFor.title: Testing an armed vehicle
watchFor.body: An attempted scan-tool session can trigger the alarm and temporarily block BCM diagnostics.

watchFor.title: An open hood during self-test
watchFor.body: B1305:01 can set simply because the hood is open; close it before the arming diagnostic self-test.

notes: A replacement intrusion/inclination sensor requires LIN New Module Initialization.
If directed BCM replacement becomes necessary, it requires programmable module installation, at least 2 programmed keys and a parameter reset.

diagnostics.meaning: These distinguish a LIN short to ground, communication faults or a reported sensor obstruction.
diagnostics.next: Use Test B. A code is not sufficient evidence to replace the sensor.

diagnostics.meaning: B109F:49 identifies internal sensor failure; B109F:55 identifies missing configuration.
diagnostics.next: For B109F:49, install and initialize a new sensor. For B109F:55, perform LIN New Module Initialization. Route other unlisted codes to BCM diagnostics.

diagnostics.finding: Recorded unwanted-alarm event.
diagnostics.meaning: Panic indicates commanded operation; Door Ajar, Interior Motion Detected, Tilt Detected and Hood Ajar identify different inputs.
diagnostics.next: Explain panic-button operation for Panic; diagnose door switches for Door Ajar, use Test B for motion/tilt, and Test D for Hood Ajar. A RUN transition without a valid passive anti-theft key read is another listed possible cause.

diagnostics.finding: Only a door, luggage-lid or horn response is missing.
diagnostics.meaning: The complaint belongs to a particular input or output path.
diagnostics.next: For door entry, diagnose courtesy lamps failing to illuminate with the door open. For luggage entry, diagnose the incorrect lid-ajar indication. For absent horn output, use horn diagnostics.

verification.title: Repeat the original operating condition
verification.body: After repair, test normal operation with the relevant entry point closed through its 20-second arming countdown. Allow for the driver-door's 12-second activation delay when applicable. Confirm the repaired input and required alarm outputs.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record initial codes, alarm-event history, failed circuit checks, repairs and the repeat-test outcome. Confirm required sensor initialization is complete and distinguish historical triggers from a newly reproduced event.

procedures.purpose: Complete code and symptom charts, Pinpoint Tests A–D, connections and pass/fail limits.
Electrical diagnostic prerequisites, probing, meter use and fused-jumper methods.
Arming conditions, alarm delays, scan-access protection and sensor initialization requirements.
BCM diagnosis for other codes and directed module assessment.
Door-ajar and courtesy-lamp diagnostic branches.
Incorrect luggage-compartment-lid ajar indication.
Absent horn output during alarm activation.
Hood latch replacement when Test A or D directs it.
Overhead-console removal and replacement when Test B directs it.
Turn-signal or hazard-output faults found in Test C.
RKE lock/unlock faults found in Test C.

guides.title: Replace and initialize the intrusion sensor
guides.summary: Remove the intrusion sensor through the overhead console and initialize a new unit before checking the body control module for remaining faults.
guides.introduction: The intrusion sensor monitors movement inside the passenger compartment using ultrasonic acoustic pulses when the perimeter alarm is armed. It reports detected movement to the body control module (BCM), which controls the alarm horn and lamps. The sensor communicates through the Local Interconnect Network (LIN). Replacement includes both physical installation and a scan-tool initialization so the new component can be brought into service correctly.
guides.why: The BCM receives several alarm inputs, so an unexpected alarm does not by itself identify a faulty intrusion sensor. Correct diagnosis separates interior movement detection from door, hood, luggage-lid and other alarm inputs. During replacement, the bracket and sensor clips must be released in sequence. A new sensor also requires initialization and a BCM fault check; plugging it in is not the end of the job.

when.summary: When diagnosis calls for intrusion sensor replacement or the sensor must be removed for access.
notes: The initialization and BCM self-test sequence is required when installing a new component.

prepare.title: Arrange overhead-console access
prepare.detail: Follow the overhead console removal and installation procedure. Be prepared to release screws, an electrical connector and the sensor assembly clips.

prepare.title: Have the required scan capability
prepare.detail: For replacement, use a diagnostic scan tool that supports LIN New Module Initialization and BCM self-tests, fault clearing and fault retrieval.

prepare.title: Disarm before diagnostic communication
prepare.detail: Disarm the perimeter alarm using a valid programmed key or the supported electronic unlocking method before starting a BCM scan session.

steps.title: Remove the overhead console
steps.body: Use the [overhead console procedure](#/document/G1693978) to expose the intrusion sensor assembly. This is the required access route.

steps.title: Remove the bracket and sensor assembly
steps.body: Following the [intrusion sensor procedure](#/document/G1696466), remove the screws, disconnect the electrical connector and remove the bracket and sensor assembly.

steps.title: Release the sensor retainers
steps.body: Release the clips and position the sensors aside. Release the next clips and remove the intrusion sensor. Follow this staged release rather than trying to pull the sensor through engaged retainers.

steps.title: Reassemble the hardware
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Restore the sensor clips, bracket assembly, connector and screws, then reinstall the overhead console.

steps.title: Initialize a new component
steps.body: If a new sensor has been installed, select Toolbox > Electrical > Service Functions > LIN New Module Initialization on the diagnostic scan tool and carry out the procedure.

steps.title: Complete the new-component fault check
steps.body: For a new component, carry out the BCM self-test. Clear the diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), then retrieve them from the BCM again to confirm they have cleared.

watchFor.title: Alarm activation during scan-tool access
watchFor.body: Attempting BCM communication while the alarm is armed can activate the alarm and block programming, data monitoring and self-tests for 10 minutes.

watchFor.title: Confusing movement and tilt detection
watchFor.body: Intrusion sensing detects passenger-compartment movement. Inclination sensing detects sufficient vehicle tilt; these are different alarm inputs.

notes: Refitting the existing component does not invoke the two new-component-only steps in this replacement procedure.
The perimeter alarm and the transmitter-operated panic alarm have different activation paths.

diagnostics.finding: The alarm activates unexpectedly.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM may be responding to intrusion sensing or another monitored alarm input.
diagnostics.next: Establish the triggering input before condemning the intrusion sensor.

diagnostics.finding: BCM DTCs return after initialization and clearing.
diagnostics.meaning: The required fault-clearance confirmation has not been achieved.
diagnostics.next: Record the returned codes and continue diagnosis rather than treating installation as complete.

verification.title: Check physical reassembly
verification.body: Confirm the sensor retainers, bracket, connector and overhead console are restored.

verification.title: Record the electronic result
verification.body: For a new sensor, record completion of LIN initialization, the BCM self-test and the final retrieved DTC result.

procedures.purpose: Intrusion sensor removal, installation, new-module initialization and BCM fault verification.
Overhead console removal and installation for sensor access.
Alarm inputs, disarming methods, network protection and intrusion/inclination sensor operation.

guides.title: Program passive anti-theft keys with a diagnostic scan tool
guides.summary: Use authenticated scan-tool security access to program passive keys, then confirm key acceptance and successful engine starting.
guides.introduction: The passive anti-theft system (PATS) permits starting when a valid programmed key is detected and the body control module (BCM) and powertrain control module (PCM) complete their authorization exchange. Programming registers both the anti-theft and remote keyless entry (RKE) functions together. PATS does not switch off an already running vehicle.
guides.why: A key can be undetected because of battery condition, placement or interference, so programming is not the automatic answer to every no-start complaint. During programming, successful key recognition and successful engine starting are separate results. Alarm-active access also depends on exact timing and an uninterrupted authenticated session.
searchTerms: key programmed but vehicle will not start

when.summary: When adding or replacing passive keys, erasing stored keys, or completing required BCM replacement work.
notes: Select the function that matches the repair; adding a key and erasing keys are different operations.

prepare.title: Check power and key batteries
prepare.detail: Passive-key batteries must measure at least 2.5 volts. Follow [Diagnostic Methods](#/document/G1693185), including checking vehicle battery and charging operation and confirming battery state of charge above 70% before diagnostics.

prepare.title: Prepare authenticated diagnostic access
prepare.detail: Use a compatible scan tool with an active Internet connection; a hardwired connection is strongly recommended. Have valid Dealership or Aftermarket credentials. Keep the service-publication session active and prevent scan-tool power saving from interrupting a timed session.

prepare.title: Confirm the backup starting position
prepare.detail: Use the Owner's Literature to establish the passive key's correct orientation in the backup starting location. Correct placement is necessary for programming.

steps.title: Establish the session and choose the operation
steps.body: Follow [Anti-Theft Key Programming](#/document/G1672905). Establish a vehicle session and select TOOLBOX > Body > Security > PATS Functions. Available operations include Program Additional Key, Erase and Program Keys, Parameter Reset and Customer Spare Key Programming Enable/Disable. If alarm activity does not prevent access, proceed to security authorization.

steps.title: Select the conditional alarm-access route
steps.body: If the perimeter alarm activates and no valid programmed key is available, use the keypad-code route only if a keyless-entry keypad is actually fitted. Otherwise follow the timed no-keypad route below. Push-button-start vehicles require blank-path vehicle identification using the tear tag for that route.

steps.title: Prepare the no-keypad alarm session
steps.body: Remove the horn fuse to avoid nuisance, establish the scan-tool session and select PATS Functions without advancing past the check mark. If a hood-latch switch is fitted and the hood is open for charging, place the latch in its closed position. Latch the driver-door striker while leaving the door open for access; close the other doors and luggage compartment. If the exterior lights are not flashing, disconnect and reconnect the battery.

steps.title: Initiate and observe the timed access window
steps.body: Request key erasure and advance through the screen stating that 2 keys are needed to start. Ignore the next error only as directed, exit and re-enter PATS Functions, then pause at the ignition-on prompt or main menu. The erase request starts a 10-minute BCM timer. Refit the horn fuse when flashing stops, within 4–5 minutes of the erase command. Another 5–6 minutes later, at 9–11 minutes from initial data-link access, a single chirp marks the 1-minute access window. Immediately continue to security authorization. If no chirp occurs, restart the procedure.

steps.title: Obtain security authorization
steps.body: Select the appropriate PATS operation and follow the prompts. At Gaining Security Access, confirm Internet connectivity and select Yes. When arriving from the no-keypad alarm route, select Erase Keys. Choose Dealership or Aftermarket and enter valid credentials when prompted.

steps.title: Program the passive keys
steps.body: Place each passive key correctly in the backup starting location and follow the scan-tool instructions. Door-lock and hazard-flasher cycling indicates acceptance. Continue through the programming error described in the procedure if it appears; an alarm after the first key is also specifically permitted to be ignored while programming the second key.

steps.title: Verify starting and resolve authorization if needed
steps.body: Start the vehicle. If it will not start, use PATS Programming to perform the required parameter reset or module initialization for the BCM, PCM or anti-lock braking system (ABS) module as necessary. If starting still fails, repeat the procedure from its beginning. After the second unsuccessful attempt, use the specified alternate route.

steps.title: Use the alternate timed route only when required
steps.body: Remove the horn fuse and select PATS Functions without advancing. Disconnect and reconnect the battery, then open and close the driver door to begin the 10-minute alarm event. Open the driver door at 4.5 minutes so the event continues. At 10 minutes, flashing stops and the 1-minute access period begins; a connected horn gives one chirp. Switch ignition ON by pressing the start button once, select Erase and Program Keys, and immediately continue through security authorization and the on-screen instructions.

watchFor.title: Session interruption
watchFor.body: Keep the scan tool awake and the authenticated website session active throughout the wait. A lost session can prevent use of the short access window.

watchFor.title: Temporary alarm setup
watchFor.body: Restore the horn fuse after the alternate route, and restore temporary latch positions before closing the door or hood.

notes: Unlimited Key Mode and Program Unlimited Key Code are non-push-button-start branches. Unlimited Key Mode is intended for fleet use and is outside this passive-key route.
Only the specific errors identified by the programming procedure are instructions to continue; they are not a general reason to ignore diagnostic faults.

diagnostics.finding: A programmed key starts the vehicle only from the backup location and its remote buttons do not work.
diagnostics.meaning: A depleted key battery can cause this combination.
diagnostics.next: Check the battery against the required voltage and replace a depleted battery before treating the concern as lost programming.

diagnostics.finding: No Key Detected appears with a key near an interior edge or a charger.
diagnostics.meaning: Detection range or charger interference can prevent recognition.
diagnostics.next: Move the key to another interior location and away from the charger, then retry.

diagnostics.finding: A control module has been replaced.
diagnostics.meaning: BCM and PCM replacement have different key requirements.
diagnostics.next: BCM replacement requires programmable module installation, at least 2 programmed keys and a parameter reset. PCM replacement requires programmable module installation and a parameter reset, without key reprogramming.

verification.title: Confirm acceptance and actual starting
verification.body: Record the lock/hazard acknowledgement for programmed keys and the final engine-start result. A programming acknowledgement alone does not complete the starting check.

procedures.purpose: Authenticated key programming, conditional alarm-access timing, starting verification and alternate recovery sequence.
Diagnostic prerequisites, battery checks and disciplined fault assessment before programming.
Passive-key detection, backup starting and the distinct BCM and PCM replacement requirements.

guides.title: Program a spare passive key using two programmed keys
guides.summary: Add a passive key through the backup starting location, then confirm that it operates the remote locking and starts the vehicle.
guides.introduction: The Passive Anti-Theft System (PATS) allows starting when it recognizes a programmed key inside the vehicle. Each passive key also contains the remote keyless entry (RKE) transmitter. This procedure teaches the body control module both functions of an additional key, using two keys the vehicle already recognizes.
guides.why: Programming depends on a precise sequence of key changes and START/STOP button presses. Correct positioning in the backup starting location lets the vehicle read each key directly through the PATS center antenna. Keeping the doors closed and meeting every timing requirement are conditions of this procedure. Checking both starting and remote operation establishes that both functions work.
searchTerms: add key using two programmed keys
new key will not start vehicle

when.summary: When adding a spare passive key with two programmed keys available and spare-key programming enabled.
notes: This method requires spare-key programming to be enabled.
Consult the Owner's Literature for the backup starting location, key orientation and maximum programmed-key allowance.

prepare.title: Arrange the keys before starting
prepare.detail: Have both previously programmed keys and the unprogrammed key ready. Identify them clearly so the timed sequence is easy to follow.

prepare.title: Prepare the cabin and timing
prepare.detail: Locate the backup starting position before beginning. Close every door and keep them closed until programming is complete. Complete the entire programming sequence within 30 seconds.

steps.title: Present the first programmed key
steps.body: Following the [programming procedure](#/document/G1672906), place the first programmed passive key in the backup starting location and press START/STOP. Wait 5 seconds, press START/STOP again, then remove that key.

steps.title: Present the second programmed key
steps.body: Within 10 seconds, place the second programmed key in the backup starting location and press START/STOP. Wait 5 seconds, press START/STOP again, then remove the second key. Keep the overall 30-second limit in mind.

steps.title: Present the new key
steps.body: Wait 5 seconds after removing the second key. Place the unprogrammed passive key in the backup starting location and press START/STOP. Keep the key correctly oriented and the doors closed through completion.

steps.title: Verify the result or repeat the prescribed sequence
steps.body: Check that the new key operates the RKE transmitter functions and starts the vehicle. If programming fails, wait at least 10 seconds and rotate the key 180 degrees before repeating the procedure.

watchFor.title: A missed timing window
watchFor.body: The individual waits and the overall time limit both apply. Arrange the keys beforehand so searching for the next key does not interrupt the sequence.

watchFor.title: Interference near the key
watchFor.body: Some phone or laptop chargers can interfere with key detection. Move the key away from a nearby charger if a detection concern occurs.

notes: The backup starting location can also recognize a programmed key when its battery is depleted.

diagnostics.finding: No Key Detected appears.
diagnostics.meaning: The message does not by itself prove that the key is faulty or unprogrammed; position, interference or a depleted key battery can affect detection.
diagnostics.next: Check positioning and orientation, use the backup starting location, and consult the supplied PATS operation information if the concern persists.

verification.title: Record both functional results
verification.body: Record successful remote operation and successful starting with the new key. A result for only one function leaves verification incomplete.

procedures.purpose: Exact two-programmed-key sequence, timing, retry instructions and final verification.
Passive-key operation, backup starting and distinctions between programming and key-detection concerns.

guides.title: Replace the PATS center antenna beneath the floor console
guides.summary: Remove the console upper trim to replace the center antenna used for passive-key detection and backup starting.
guides.introduction: The Passive Anti-Theft System (PATS) allows starting when it recognizes a programmed key inside the vehicle. Its center antenna receives commands from the body control module and sends a low-frequency signal that activates the key. Mounted beneath the console trim, it also detects a key placed in the rear cup holder backup starting location, including when the key battery is depleted.
guides.why: A No Key Detected message does not establish that this antenna has failed. Key position, charger interference and other shared keyless-system components can affect recognition. Once diagnosis justifies antenna replacement, careful console removal protects the clips and wiring that must be released before the antenna becomes accessible.
searchTerms: passive key not detected inside vehicle

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies a faulty center antenna, or the antenna must be removed during console service.
notes: The illustrated access procedure uses an automatic transmission; manual-transmission access is similar.

prepare.title: Arrange trim access
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover and suitable tools for the console retainers. The upper panel has electrical connections that must be disconnected before removal.

prepare.title: Establish the starting concern
prepare.detail: Have a programmed passive key available. Review the key-position and interference checks in the system-operation article before treating a recognition complaint as an antenna fault.

steps.title: Release the console side trim
steps.body: Use the interior trim remover to release the clips and remove the right-hand side panel, then release the left-hand side panel. These panels provide access for the upper-trim removal sequence.

steps.title: Free the selector boot
steps.body: Remove the selector-lever bezel with the trim remover. Disconnect its electrical connector and position the selector-lever boot aside so it can be accommodated as the upper trim is lifted.

steps.title: Remove the front retainers
steps.body: Open the console lid, then remove the right-hand and left-hand front retainers. Keep these identified for reassembly; their installation torque is 18 lb.in (2 Nm).

steps.title: Lift away the upper trim
steps.body: Release the upper-panel clips, position the selector boot as required and disconnect the electrical connectors. Remove the panel only after these connections are free.

steps.title: Exchange the antenna
steps.body: Remove the antenna retainers and lift the antenna from the underside of the upper trim. The illustration identifies its mounting beneath the cup-holder area. Fit the replacement by reversing this part of the procedure.

steps.title: Reassemble the console
steps.body: Follow [the complete removal and installation sequence](#/document/G2153308) in reverse. Reconnect the upper-panel wiring, position the boot, engage the clips and tighten the front retainers to their specified torque before completing the bezel and side-trim installation.

watchFor.title: Wiring still attached
watchFor.body: The upper trim has electrical connections. Releasing its clips does not make it ready to lift away.

watchFor.title: Backup-key orientation
watchFor.body: The programmed key must be correctly oriented in the rear cup holder backup location for the backup-starting check.

notes: PATS prevents unauthorized starting; it does not disable an already running vehicle.
Control-module replacement and its programming requirements are separate from this antenna replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Recognition improves when the key is moved away from a door pocket, sun visor or nearby charger.
diagnostics.meaning: Key location or interference can explain the concern without proving an antenna defect.
diagnostics.next: Recheck recognition with the key in a suitable interior position before proceeding with replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Normal passive starting fails, but backup starting recognizes the programmed key.
diagnostics.meaning: Backup recognition can work when the key battery is depleted; this result alone does not isolate the original fault.
diagnostics.next: Continue the key and PATS diagnosis using the system-operation information.

verification.title: Check recognition and record the result
verification.body: Check ignition operation with the programmed key inside the vehicle and correctly positioned in the backup location. Record whether the original recognition concern remains.

verification.title: Check console completion
verification.body: Confirm the disconnected wiring is reconnected, the boot is positioned correctly and the trim clips and retainers are secured.

procedures.purpose: Complete center-antenna removal and installation, including automatic-transmission console access with manual-transmission access noted as similar.
Explain passive-key recognition, backup starting, interference and the distinction between antenna service and module programming.

guides.title: Diagnose an inoperative sun-visor universal transmitter
guides.summary: Use the transmitter indicator, programming response and vanity-lamp operation to separate pairing problems from an electrical or visor concern.
guides.introduction: The universal transmitter in the left-hand sun visor learns a hand-held remote's radio-frequency code and stores it for use with a selected button. It can operate compatible garage doors, gates, lighting or security systems and store three unique codes. Diagnosis begins with its indicator, not with dismantling the visor.
guides.why: A lit indicator shows that programming checks are appropriate, but it does not establish successful receiver pairing. The transmitter and left vanity lamp share power and ground circuits, making the vanity lamp a useful comparison when the transmitter indicator stays dark.
searchTerms: sun visor transmitter will not program

when.summary: When a universal-transmitter button does not operate its intended receiver or the indicator does not illuminate.
notes: Confirm the concern is present before using a replacement decision.

prepare.title: Gather the programming items
prepare.detail: Have the customer's hand-held transmitter, a new or fresh transmitter battery and the Owner's Literature available. A fresh battery supports accurate radio transmission during training.

prepare.title: Arrange receiver access
prepare.detail: Be able to verify receiver operation and complete any additional rolling-code pairing steps. Electrical faults beyond these functional checks follow the separate interior-lighting diagnosis.

steps.title: Observe the indicator
steps.body: Press a universal-transmitter button and note whether its indicator illuminates. In [Test A](#/document/G1696482), illumination leads to programming checks; no illumination leads to the vanity-lamp comparison. The initial check uses the indicator rather than a direct voltage measurement.

steps.title: Train an illuminated transmitter
steps.body: Clear the universal transmitter and program it using the Owner's Literature, with the customer's hand-held remote. Follow that sequence without substituting guessed button timings. Observe whether the resulting light is continuous or rapidly flashing.

steps.title: Complete pairing or repeat unsuccessful training
steps.body: A continuous light indicates fixed-code programming: verify the receiver operates. Rapid flashing indicates rolling-code programming, which may still require receiver-side steps. If neither successful indication appears, repeat programming using the Owner's Literature and referenced HomeLink assistance. Persistent programming failure directs replacement of the left-hand sun visor.

steps.title: Use the vanity lamp when the indicator is dark
steps.body: Check the left-hand vanity mirror lamp. If it works correctly, Test A directs replacement of the left-hand sun visor, which contains the transmitter. If it also fails, follow [Interior Lighting](#/document/G1694266) diagnosis to investigate the shared electrical concern.

watchFor.title: Rapid flashing is not the finish line
watchFor.body: A rolling code can be learned before pairing with the receiver is complete.

notes: The transmitter is serviced as part of the left-hand sun visor in this diagnostic path.

diagnostics.finding: Slow blinking
diagnostics.meaning: The transmitter is searching for a programming code.
diagnostics.next: Continue or repeat the prescribed training sequence.

diagnostics.finding: Both transmitter indicator and vanity lamp are inoperative
diagnostics.meaning: The shared power and ground circuits make an interior-lighting concern relevant.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose that concern before condemning the visor.

verification.title: Demonstrate receiver operation
verification.body: Verify the intended receiver responds to the programmed button. Record the final indicator behavior and whether receiver-side rolling-code pairing was required; indicator behavior alone is not a completed functional check.

guides.title: Diagnose cruise-control switches and brake or clutch inputs
guides.summary: Use fault codes, live switch readings and targeted circuit checks to establish why cruise control will not operate or cancel correctly.
guides.introduction: The powertrain control module (PCM) maintains road speed through the electronic throttle. Steering-wheel requests reach it through the steering column control module (SCCM) and the vehicle network. Brake switches and, on manual-transmission cars, the clutch deactivator switch tell the PCM when to release speed control. This diagnosis separates incorrect inputs, wiring faults and connection problems before considering replacement parts.
guides.why: Cruise control can be disabled by a detected fault without displaying a dedicated warning. A stored code identifies the affected signal, not necessarily a failed switch. Comparing actual pedal movement with scan-tool parameter identifications (PIDs) reveals what the controller sees; circuit testing then establishes why that information is wrong.
searchTerms: cruise control does not cancel with clutch

when.summary: Use when cruise control or its switches misbehave, clutch cancellation fails, or relevant fault codes are recorded.
notes: Confirm the concern is present before following a replacement decision.
A MyKey speed restriction can prevent a higher set speed without indicating a component fault.

prepare.title: Prepare for electrical diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable scan tool, digital multimeter, correct flex-probe adapters, fused jumper wires and Wiring Diagrams Cell 31. Check battery and charging operation, confirm battery state of charge exceeds 70%, and inspect previous repairs, wiring and connectors.

prepare.title: Plan steering-wheel access
prepare.detail: Test A7 requires driver-airbag removal. This phase needs restraint-system capability and the complete driver-airbag removal and installation procedure before switch-circuit access.

steps.title: Record faults and choose the correct route
steps.body: Run PCM and SCCM self-tests. Use the code distinctions below before replacing anything. A module that does not communicate requires network diagnosis; an indicator that stays on or never illuminates requires instrument-cluster diagnosis. For a restricted set speed, verify MyKey settings with an administrator key and check operation with that key if necessary.

steps.title: Check brake-input agreement
steps.body: A2 checks that BOO1 and BOO2 are both OFF with the pedal released and ON when applied. If they disagree, enter Test B: first check all stoplamps, including the high-mounted lamp. B2 adds the important intermediate position: light pressure should produce BOO1 ON and BOO2 OFF; firm pressure should produce both ON.

steps.title: Separate brake-switch and wiring faults
steps.body: An incorrect BOO1 takes B3's engine-specific voltage test. An incorrect BOO2 takes B4's resistance test, followed as directed by ground continuity, unwanted grounding and signal continuity checks in B5–B7. Only B7's passing jumper-assisted circuit result supports replacing the brake pedal position switch assembly; failed circuit checks require wiring repair. Correct signals lead to PCM connection checks.

steps.title: Observe the manual-transmission clutch input
steps.body: CPP_TOP must read YES with the clutch released and NO when pressed. For A3's always-NO result, A4 disconnects C2354 with ignition OFF, then checks the PID with ignition ON: YES supports switch replacement; remaining NO requires circuit repair. An always-YES result, or failure to cancel with the clutch, reaches Test C. Record the pedal/PID response and stop there for further clutch-cancellation diagnosis; this referral does not authorize replacement.

steps.title: Follow Test D for clutch fault codes
steps.body: For P0833 or P170A, D1 uses the same CPP_TOP expectation. An always-NO result enters D2: resistance below 3 ohms takes D5; otherwise continue to D3. D3 disconnects C2354 and connects pins 2 and 3; its passing resistance result supports switch replacement, otherwise repair the circuit. A correctly changing PID takes D4: clear codes and repeat the PCM self-test. Returning clutch codes or no codes both lead to D5; other codes follow their own chart.

steps.title: Check each steering-wheel request
steps.body: In A5, operate ON, OFF, RESUME, CANCEL and both SET directions while watching SCCM PIDs. One incorrect switch response supports left-hand switch replacement; several incorrect responses require A7. Approximately 2.5 volts on the specified circuits supports replacement after switching ignition OFF and waiting one minute, followed by airbag installation. Otherwise, A8/A9 check the steering-wheel harness for opens and grounding, then A10 checks continuity through the clockspring. Follow the distinct steering-wheel or clockspring replacement endpoint only when its test fails.

steps.title: Finish the applicable range and module checks
steps.body: On automatic-transmission vehicles, A6 verifies that the transmission-range PID agrees with DRIVE; disagreement requires external-controls diagnosis. Passing inputs lead to the designated PCM or SCCM connection check. With ignition OFF, inspect connectors for corrosion, bent or pushed-out pins, repair them and latch connectors securely. Recheck operation and consult applicable technical service bulletins before any module replacement. If operation returns, address the connection fault's root cause.

watchFor.title: Do not flatten the brake sequence
watchFor.body: BOO2 remaining OFF under light pedal pressure is expected in B2. Treating both brake inputs as identical can produce a false diagnosis.

watchFor.title: Keep clutch replacement equipment-specific
watchFor.body: Use the standard-cruise or adaptive-cruise deactivator-switch procedure that matches the vehicle. Keep the clutch pedal at rest during switch installation.

notes: Use the actual engine's connector and pin assignments throughout brake and clutch circuit testing.
A1 sends B137F:11 and B137F:17 to A5; its other SCCM-code branch refers to steering-wheel and column electrical diagnosis.
Automatic-transmission range checks apply only where that transmission is fitted.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0504, P0572, P0573 or P1703 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P0504 indicates incorrect brake-signal correlation; P0572 indicates an open or persistently OFF stoplamp signal; P0573 indicates a short-to-voltage or persistently ON signal; P1703 indicates an unsuitable or noncycling stoplamp input during self-test.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test B, beginning with actual stoplamp operation and staged pedal-input checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B137F:09, B137F:11 or B137F:17 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These identify a stuck cruise switch, a switch-circuit short to ground, or a switch-circuit short to voltage, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Enter Test A and follow A1's code-specific routing before switch or harness testing.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0833 or P170A is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P0833 indicates missing clutch-switch changes while vehicle movement is detected and disables cruise. P170A indicates a high or noncycling top-of-travel input during self-test.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test D; any referral to Test C ends at observing and recording CPP_TOP within this guide.

verification.title: Confirm the affected input and operation
verification.body: Repeat the relevant pedal or steering-switch observation, then operate the system to determine whether the original concern remains.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Retain the initial codes, pedal/PID states and circuit findings. For Test D, record the repeated PCM self-test result and whether diagnosis reached a repair endpoint or the clutch-cancellation stopping point.

guides.title: Diagnose adaptive cruise-control switches and brake inputs
guides.summary: Trace an adaptive cruise-control complaint through module faults, steering-wheel commands and pedal signals before choosing a circuit or component repair.
guides.introduction: Adaptive cruise control needs reliable driver commands as well as information about surrounding traffic. The powertrain control module (PCM) monitors separate stoplamp and cruise-deactivation inputs, while manual-transmission vehicles also have a clutch pedal position (CPP) switch. These checks distinguish an incorrect input from wiring, connection or communication faults.
guides.why: A working brake lamp does not establish that both brake inputs are correct. Likewise, an unresponsive cruise button can result from its switch, steering-wheel wiring or clockspring. Following the signal through the system avoids treating a symptom or diagnostic trouble code (DTC) as proof that a particular part has failed.
searchTerms: cruise control does not disengage with clutch

when.summary: When adaptive cruise control will not operate, its buttons respond incorrectly, or brake/clutch input faults are recorded.
notes: Clutch checks apply to manual transmissions; transmission-range checks apply to automatics.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable scan tool for module self-tests and live parameter identifications (PIDs), plus access to applicable technical service bulletins (TSBs).

prepare.title: Prepare for circuit and airbag access
prepare.detail: Have a meter, correct connector probe adapters, a fused jumper and Wiring Diagrams Cell 31. Steering-wheel testing requires the driver-airbag procedure; clutch-switch access requires the driver-knee-airbag procedure and its safety prerequisites.

steps.title: Establish the fault route
steps.body: Run PCM, steering column control module (SCCM), cruise control module (CCM) and anti-lock brake system (ABS) self-tests. Follow the DTC chart; the listed SCCM switch-pack codes lead to A6. If no codes are recorded, follow A2: clear continuous-memory codes with ignition on, cycle ignition off/on, wait at least 10 seconds and retrieve codes again. A module that cannot communicate needs network diagnosis.

steps.title: Compare both brake inputs
steps.body: In A3, BOO1 and BOO2 should both read Off with the pedal released. Light application changes BOO1 to On; firm application changes both to On. Correct responses lead to A4 for manuals or A6 for automatics. Incorrect responses lead to Test B, which first checks all stoplamps, including the high-mounted lamp; lamp faults go to stoplamp diagnosis.

steps.title: Separate brake-switch and wiring faults
steps.body: B3 checks the stoplamp voltage signal when BOO1 is incorrect. B4–B7 investigate incorrect BOO2 through deactivator continuity, ground integrity, unwanted grounding and signal continuity using the prescribed fused jumper. Passing B7 directs replacement of the brake pedal position/stoplamp switch; failed wiring checks direct circuit repair. Passing input checks lead to B8. Use the engine-specific connector tables; these measurements provide no 5.2L PCM pin assignment.

steps.title: Record the manual-transmission clutch response
steps.body: CPP_TOP should read YES with the clutch released and NO when pressed. A4 directs A5 when that response agrees or remains NO. In A5, switch ignition off, disconnect the CPP switch, then switch ignition on: a YES reading directs CPP-switch replacement; NO directs circuit repair. A response that remains YES leads toward Test C. Stop that route at recording pedal position and CPP_TOP response until confirmed diagnostic routing is available; Test C does not authorize replacement here.

steps.title: Check steering-wheel commands and automatic range
steps.body: A6 compares each on/off, cancel/resume, set and gap command with its SCCM PID. One incorrect switch response directs left-hand switch-pack replacement; multiple incorrect responses require A8–A12. With correct switch responses, automatics must show DRIVE correctly in the transmission-range PID before A13; an incorrect range indication goes to transmission external-controls diagnosis. Manuals proceed to A13.

steps.title: Localize multiple switch failures
steps.body: After the required driver-airbag removal, A8 checks switch supply voltage. A passing result directs ignition off, a one-minute wait, switch replacement and airbag installation. Otherwise test steering-wheel harness continuity and isolation, then clockspring continuity. Failed A9/A10 checks direct steering-wheel replacement; failed A11 directs clockspring replacement. Use the exact connector tables rather than probing by appearance.

steps.title: Complete the applicable repair endpoint
steps.body: At A12, A13 or B8, inspect the relevant SCCM or PCM connectors for corrosion, damaged terminals and pushed-out pins. Repair, latch securely and retest. Persistent concerns require the specified TSB check before module replacement. If A5 establishes a CPP-switch replacement, use the adaptive procedure: remove the knee airbag, disconnect the connector and remove the switch. Install with the clutch at rest without pressing, pulling or moving it, then reverse removal.

watchFor.title: Match the switch procedure to cruise equipment
watchFor.body: The adaptive procedure disconnects the connector before removing the switch. The standard-cruise procedure removes the switch first. Do not exchange these sequences; the adaptive at-rest installation precaution prevents incorrect adjustment and switch damage.

notes: Use the initial DTC chart to separate radar alignment/blockage, overheating, voltage, configuration and network concerns. Invalid-data faults generally require diagnosis of non-network faults in the sending module. Configuration faults require the directed Programmable Module Installation process.

A communicating CCM reporting U0001:88 describes an earlier bus-off event; inspect wiring and connectors. Overtemperature can resolve after cooling. The listed CCM checksum, memory and internal-electronics faults require clearing, retesting and another self-test before replacement.

Weather-related blockage, MyKey speed restrictions and cruise-indicator faults have separate routes. Unexpected or absent automatic braking calls for CCM/front-bumper damage checks and retesting; field-of-view limitations can contribute. Persistent braking noise requires brake-system diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: The PCM records P0504, P0572, P0573 or P1703.
diagnostics.meaning: These identify incorrect brake-input sequencing, an open/always-off stoplamp signal, a short-to-voltage/always-on signal, or an incorrect self-test response respectively.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test B; none establishes switch failure without the corresponding checks.

diagnostics.finding: The SCCM records B137F:09, B137F:11 or B137F:17.
diagnostics.meaning: These indicate a stuck switch, a switch-circuit short to ground or voltage above threshold respectively.
diagnostics.next: Continue at A6 and follow the single-switch or multiple-switch branch.

diagnostics.finding: The PCM records P0833 or P170A.
diagnostics.meaning: P0833 means clutch-switch transitions were absent while vehicle movement was detected; P170A concerns a high or non-cycling top-of-travel input during self-test.
diagnostics.next: Continue with Test D separately. Any referral to Test C stops at recording CPP_TOP behavior and obtaining confirmed routing.

verification.title: Recheck the affected function
verification.body: After the prescribed repair, operate the system and repeat the relevant input or connector-endpoint check. Address the cause of terminal damage even if reseating restores operation.

verification.title: Record the result and stopping point
verification.body: Record DTCs, pedal positions, PID responses and the completed branch. A recorded CPP_TOP response alone does not establish that clutch-operated cruise disengagement has been repaired.

Adaptive-cruise deactivator-switch replacement, including clutch-at-rest installation.
Standard-cruise deactivator-switch replacement only when matching that fitted equipment.
Driver-airbag removal and installation required for steering-wheel circuit access.
Steering-wheel switch replacement when directed by Test A.
Stoplamp-switch replacement when established by Test B.
Network diagnosis for missing module communication.

guides.title: Diagnose adaptive-cruise clutch signals, lost communication and radar alignment
guides.summary: Use clutch-switch data, ordered network tests and radar alignment checks to distinguish adaptive-cruise input, communication and mounting faults.
guides.introduction: Adaptive cruise control depends on reliable driver inputs, brake-system messages and correctly aligned radar. On a vehicle with a clutch pedal, the top-of-travel switch tells the powertrain control module (PCM) whether the pedal is released. The cruise control module (CCM) also needs messages from the anti-lock brake system (ABS). These checks separate those dependencies before reaching a repair decision.
guides.why: A stored communication code can reflect an intermittent interruption rather than a failed module. Clutch-switch adjustment and radar mounting also matter: an incorrectly installed switch can be damaged, while a misaligned sensor can produce a fault without an internal module failure.
searchTerms: lost communication with cruise control module

when.summary: Use for the listed clutch-input, ABS/cruise communication or radar-alignment codes on an adaptive-cruise-equipped vehicle.
notes: D2/D3 terminal checks and their replacement conclusions apply only to the identified 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L configurations.
For 5.2L clutch diagnosis, record pedal data and obtain confirmed engine-specific terminal and setup information before circuit-test or replacement decisions.

prepare.title: Arrange scan and circuit testing
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of PCM pedal data, network tests, module self-tests and continuous-memory code retrieval. Circuit testing requires a multimeter and exact connector identification.

prepare.title: Plan physical access only when needed
prepare.detail: Switch access requires driver knee airbag removal using its applicable restraint-system precautions. Radar work requires safe hoist capability, lower-air-deflector access and the complete radar-alignment procedure; vertical alignment requires front bumper cover removal.

steps.title: Observe clutch-switch behavior—Test D1
steps.body: For P0833 or P170A, turn ignition ON and monitor the PCM CPP_TOP parameter identification (PID) while pressing and releasing the clutch. The expected reading is NO pressed and YES released. Correct switching leads to D4. A constant NO leads to D2 on an identified engine configuration. A constant YES is a stopping point: record it and obtain confirmed diagnostic routing without inferring switch or PCM replacement.

steps.title: Follow the constant-NO circuit branch—D2/D3
steps.body: Turn ignition OFF and disconnect the appropriate PCM connector. Measure to ground at C1551B pin 6 for 2.3L, C1381B pin 8 for 3.7L, or C175B pin 8 for 5.0L. Resistance less than 3 ohms leads to D5. Otherwise, disconnect switch C2354, connect its harness pins 2 and 3, and repeat the same PCM-terminal measurement. Now less than 3 ohms selects switch replacement; otherwise repair the circuit. Do not transfer these terminals or conclusions to 5.2L.

steps.title: Recheck codes and connections—D4/D5
steps.body: When D1 switches correctly, clear codes and repeat the PCM self-test. P0833, P170A or no recorded codes lead to D5; other codes require the engine-specific PCM chart. At D5, switch ignition OFF, inspect PCM connectors, repair corrosion or damaged and pushed-out terminals, and reconnect securely. Retest operation. A persistent concern requires checking applicable technical service bulletins before the PCM replacement endpoint. If a switch is replaced through D3, follow the adaptive-cruise switch procedure and keep the clutch pedal at rest throughout installation.

steps.title: Establish the ABS communication fault—Test E
steps.body: For CCM U0121:00 or PCM U0121, verify an observable symptom with ignition ON. Without one, record normal operation at this time and a possible intermittent condition. With a symptom, network-test the ABS module; failure redirects to network diagnosis. If it passes, self-test the CCM, ABS and PCM and resolve low/high-voltage codes first. Then retrieve gateway module (GWM) continuous-memory codes; any recorded code redirects to network diagnosis.

steps.title: Apply Test E's final communication decision
steps.body: After those prerequisites pass, clear codes and repeat CCM and PCM self-tests. If U0121:00 or U0121 persists, clear all codes, turn ignition OFF then ON, wait 10 seconds, perform the self-test and retrieve continuous-memory codes from all modules. Both CCM U0121:00 and PCM U0121 select the ABS-module replacement route. If only the CCM sets its code, select CCM replacement; if only the PCM sets its code, select the appropriate PCM replacement procedure. These decisions depend on completing the preceding checks.

steps.title: Separate lost cruise-module communication—Test F
steps.body: For PCM U0104, first require an observable symptom, a passing CCM network test, no unresolved CCM battery-voltage codes and no GWM continuous-memory codes. Network failures or GWM codes redirect to network diagnosis. Clear all codes, cycle ignition OFF/ON, wait 10 seconds and repeat the PCM self-test. If U0104 remains, clear all codes again, repeat the ignition cycle and 10-second wait, then retrieve all modules' continuous-memory codes. U0104 in other modules selects CCM replacement; no U0104 in other modules selects PCM replacement.

steps.title: Inspect and align the radar—Test G
steps.body: For B142E:78 or B1433:54, place the vehicle in NEUTRAL and position it on a hoist using the lifting procedure. Remove the front lower air deflector and inspect the CCM bracket. Repair or replace a damaged bracket as directed. With an undamaged bracket, perform both vertical and horizontal alignment; remove the front bumper cover for vertical alignment. Successful alignment identifies misalignment as the cause. Failure to align through the complete procedure selects CCM replacement.

watchFor.title: Keep the clutch pedal still during switch installation
watchFor.body: Do not press, pull or otherwise move the pedal. Installing the switch away from the at-rest position causes incorrect adjustment and can damage the switch.

watchFor.title: Check recent module installation
watchFor.body: Before Test E's final decision, consider whether programmable module installation was omitted or configured incorrectly after a recent module replacement.

notes: Communication faults that do not recur after the specified tests can reflect high network traffic or an intermittent condition; that outcome does not identify a failed module.
Module replacement is a handoff to the appropriate removal, installation and configuration procedures, not completion of those operations.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0833 or P170A is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test D calls for checking the clutch top-of-travel signal and its circuit; the code alone does not establish switch failure.
diagnostics.next: Observe CPP_TOP first and respect the constant-YES and engine-specific stopping points.

diagnostics.finding: The CCM records U0121:00 or the PCM records U0121.
diagnostics.meaning: Expected ABS messages are missing. PCM communication can also depend on messages through the gateway.
diagnostics.next: Complete Test E's symptom, network, voltage, gateway and recurrence checks before applying its module decision.

diagnostics.finding: The PCM records U0104.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM has lost expected cruise-module messages, directly or through the gateway.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test F, including its separate PCM retest and all-module recurrence check.

diagnostics.finding: The CCM records U3003:16 or U3003:17.
diagnostics.meaning: These are the low- and high-battery-voltage branches respectively.
diagnostics.next: Follow cruise-control Test Q for U3003:16 or Test R for U3003:17 before continuing the communication decision.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B142E:78 or B1433:54 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The radar horizontal alignment is outside its accepted range; the descriptions distinguish incorrect alignment from missing calibration.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the bracket and perform the complete vertical and horizontal alignment procedures.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code C1A67:96 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The CCM detects an internal sensor failure or invalid radar data.
diagnostics.next: Record the finding and obtain the dedicated sensor diagnostic procedure before making a replacement decision.

verification.title: Confirm the branch-specific result
verification.body: Recheck operation after connector or switch work. For communication concerns, use the specified self-tests and recurrence checks. For alignment, confirm the CCM aligns correctly through the complete procedure.

verification.title: Keep an actionable diagnostic record
verification.body: Record pedal readings in both positions, engine-specific measurements, reporting modules before and after code clearing, and the alignment outcome. Clearly retain any constant-YES or unconfirmed-terminal condition as an unresolved diagnosis.

guides.title: Diagnose adaptive cruise radar blockage and communication faults
guides.summary: Use Tests H–K to distinguish a recurring cruise-module fault, weather-related radar obstruction and missing powertrain or body-module messages.
guides.introduction: Adaptive cruise depends on a forward-looking radar sensor and information exchanged between control modules. The cruise control module (CCM) can lose operation because its view is obstructed, its mounting changes or required messages disappear. Each complaint follows a different test.
guides.why: A stored code alone does not select a replacement module. These checks establish recurrence, inspect the radar's physical conditions and eliminate network or voltage faults before replacement.

when.summary: Use for recurring C1A67:96, rain/snow-related cruise loss, or CCM communication codes U0100:00 and U0140:00.
notes: Choose the matching test; the branches are not a single mandatory sequence.

prepare.title: Scan and network capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool supporting module self-tests, network tests and horizontal radar aim. Have Wiring Diagrams Cells 14 and 31 and access to vehicle-specific guided routines.

prepare.title: Physical access
prepare.detail: Test I requires trained hoist operation with the vehicle in NEUTRAL under the lifting procedure. Have radar-alignment capability before correcting the mounting.

steps.title: Test H: establish whether C1A67:96 returns
steps.body: With ignition ON, clear continuous-memory codes from all modules. Switch OFF, then ON, wait at least 10 seconds and run the CCM self-test. Check continuous and on-demand results. If C1A67:96 is absent, operation is currently normal; inspect the connector and high-speed Controller Area Network 2 (HS-CAN2) wiring for corrosion.

steps.title: Test H: inspect connections before replacement
steps.body: If the code returns, switch ignition OFF and inspect the disconnected CCM connector. Replace corroded terminals/connectors, clean module pins and renew damaged or displaced pins as needed. Reconnect securely and operate the system. If the concern remains, check OASIS for applicable Technical Service Bulletins and follow one if available; otherwise follow CCM replacement.

steps.title: Test I: inspect the radar's surroundings
steps.body: For rain/snow-related loss, inspect both sides of the front bumper cover on the hoist. Repair damage or replace the cover as necessary. If undamaged, inspect the cover and sensor for debris, moisture, snow or ice, cleaning any obstruction found.

steps.title: Test I: check mounting and aim
steps.body: If unobstructed, inspect the bracket for looseness or damage; correct mounting or renew grommets as necessary, then align the sensor. Its plastic face should be perpendicular to the ground. Obvious vertical error requires vertical and horizontal alignment procedures. Otherwise perform horizontal aim and CCM self-test. Successful aim without C1A67:97 establishes normal operation; failure directs CCM replacement.

steps.title: Test J: trace U0100:00 powertrain communication loss
steps.body: First establish a scan-tool vehicle session; failure directs network diagnosis. Repeat the clearing, ignition cycle and timed CCM test described in Test H. If U0100:00 returns, check gateway module (GWM) codes, then the powertrain control module (PCM) key-on, engine-off self-test, then CCM voltage codes. Resolve findings through their designated branches. Only after these checks, U0100:00 in multiple modules directs engine-specific PCM replacement; otherwise it directs CCM replacement.

steps.title: Test K: trace U0140:00 body-module communication loss
steps.body: Proceed only with an observable symptom. Check body control module (BCM) network response, GWM codes, then CCM/BCM self-tests and voltage faults. Address those branches first. Clear codes and repeat CCM self-test. If U0140:00 persists, clear all codes, switch ignition OFF then ON, wait 10 seconds and retrieve all-module codes. Recurrence elsewhere requires a vehicle identification number (VIN)-guided BCM routine; recurrence only in CCM directs CCM replacement.

watchFor.title: Intermittent results
watchFor.body: A non-returning communication code may reflect network traffic or an intermittent fault; it does not justify replacement.

notes: For U0140:00 after module replacement, consider incorrect or omitted Programmable Module Installation (PMI).
After a connector repair resolves Test H, address the cause of corrosion or pin damage.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code C1A67:97 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Radar obstruction is detected, or road targets have been absent for an extended period.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test I; previous water/snow buildup or sparse rural roads can explain a successful retest.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3003:16 or U3003:17 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Module voltage is below or above its threshold, respectively.
diagnostics.next: For CCM, follow Test Q or R respectively; for BCM, follow BCM diagnostics.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0151:00 is recorded in CCM.
diagnostics.meaning: Yaw-rate messages from the restraints control module are missing over HS-CAN2.
diagnostics.next: Continue diagnosis of that communication loss before selecting either module for replacement.

verification.title: Confirm the branch outcome
verification.body: Verify operation after connection repairs. For Test I, record successful horizontal aim and absence of C1A67:97.

verification.title: Preserve the decision evidence
verification.body: Record returning codes, which modules reported them and the resulting repair or guided-routine referral.

Lifting prerequisites for bumper and radar inspection.

guides.title: Diagnose adaptive cruise control communication faults
guides.summary: Use Tests L–O to separate intermittent communication codes, network faults and module-specific adaptive cruise repair decisions.
guides.introduction: Adaptive cruise control relies on messages exchanged between the cruise control module (CCM) and other vehicle modules. Missing messages can produce a communication diagnostic trouble code (DTC) without proving which module failed. These tests establish whether the concern is present, check the communicating modules and compare which modules report the same loss.
guides.why: A historical code, incomplete module configuration or a wider network fault can mislead diagnosis. The replacement decisions become valid only after the symptom, network and self-test checks have passed.

when.summary: When an observable adaptive cruise concern accompanies U0151:00, U0155:00, U0158:00 or U0212:00.
notes: Choose the branch for the recorded code and fitted module; do not infer equipment from a code list.

prepare.title: Scan-tool capability
prepare.detail: Use a tool capable of network tests, individual-module self-tests, clearing codes and retrieving continuous-memory codes from all modules.

prepare.title: Configuration and repair access
prepare.detail: Have recent module-replacement history, the vehicle identification number (VIN), configuration support and the applicable installation procedures available. Restraints-module replacement requires the dedicated SRS procedure and suitable competence.

steps.title: Confirm an observable concern
steps.body: With ignition ON, verify the complaint before advancing through [Tests L–O](#/document/G1693153). If no symptom is present, the test ends with normal operation at this time; high network traffic or an intermittent condition may explain the stored code.

steps.title: Check the relevant module on the network
steps.body: Run the network test for the module identified in the diagnostic entries below. A failure redirects to Communications Network diagnosis. For Test M, after the instrument cluster passes, retrieve gateway module (GWM) continuous-memory codes; any recorded code also redirects to network diagnosis.

steps.title: Run both module self-tests
steps.body: Self-test the CCM and the affected module. If U3003:16 or U3003:17 is recorded in the CCM, follow Test Q or R respectively. For the other module, use its SRS, instrumentation, collision-warning or steering-column diagnostic procedure before continuing.

steps.title: Check configuration and repeat the CCM test
steps.body: Recent module installation can leave incorrect configuration or incomplete programmable module installation (PMI). Review that history, clear the DTCs and repeat the CCM self-test. If the communication code disappears, record normal operation at this time. If it remains, continue.

steps.title: Determine whether other modules report the loss
steps.body: Clear all DTCs, switch ignition OFF and then ON, and wait 10 seconds. Retrieve continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes from every module. Record whether the same communication code appears outside the CCM; that distinction controls the final branch.

steps.title: Follow the matching repair decision
steps.body: Apply the code-specific decisions below only after completing the preceding checks. A code confined to the CCM directs CCM replacement. A shared code directs the named module's repair path, with the instrument cluster requiring a VIN-specific guided routine.

watchFor.title: Skipping the network referral
watchFor.body: A module that fails the network test requires network diagnosis before the later replacement decision.

watchFor.title: Incomplete replacement setup
watchFor.body: Installing a module without completing its required configuration can create communication faults.

notes: Use the selected module's complete installation procedure for replacement and required setup.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0151:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test L investigates communication with the restraints control module (RCM).
diagnostics.next: After L1–L4 pass, the same code in other modules directs RCM replacement; otherwise replace the CCM.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0155:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test M concerns missing instrument panel cluster (IPC) or gateway messages.
diagnostics.next: After M1–M5 pass, a shared code requires the VIN-specific IPC guided routine; otherwise replace the CCM.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0158:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test N concerns missing head up display (HUD) module messages.
diagnostics.next: After N1–N4 pass, a shared code directs HUD module replacement; otherwise replace the CCM.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0212:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test O concerns missing steering column control module (SCCM) messages.
diagnostics.next: After O1–O4 pass, a shared code directs SCCM replacement; otherwise replace the CCM.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3000:63 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The CCM detected too many collision-mitigation braking activation requests and recorded a circuit/component protection timeout.
diagnostics.next: Use its separate diagnostic route. Possible sources include the front bumper cover, CCM bracket and CCM; Tests L–O do not determine that fault's cause.

verification.title: Preserve the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record the observed symptom, network results, both self-test results and which modules retained the communication code after the prescribed ignition cycle.

verification.title: Distinguish diagnosis from completed repair
verification.body: A code that disappears during the CCM retest supports normal operation at that time. A replacement decision still requires completion of the selected installation procedure and its required checks.
