guides.title: Diagnose adaptive cruise module, voltage and cluster-data faults
guides.summary: Follow Tests P–S to distinguish cruise module damage, supply faults and missing instrument-cluster data.
guides.introduction: Adaptive cruise control depends on its cruise control module (CCM), an undamaged mounting arrangement, stable power and timely information from other modules. These tests address four specific diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), separating faults that require physical repair from charging, connection, programming and communication problems.
guides.why: A stored voltage or communication code can reflect a past event. Confirming whether it returns prevents replacing the CCM for a battery or network problem.

when.summary: When adaptive cruise diagnosis identifies U3000:63, U3003:16, U3003:17 or U0423:82.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical and scan-tool capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool supporting module self-tests, network tests and programming, plus a meter, correct probe adapters and Wiring Diagrams Cell 31.

prepare.title: Prepare for the prescribed measurements
prepare.detail: Provide access to the battery and CCM connector C1582. Follow battery-disconnection instructions for resistance measurements; incorrect isolation produces false readings.

steps.title: Test P: inspect damage before choosing software or replacement
steps.body: For U3000:63, inspect the CCM, bracket and front bumper cover. Repair or replace damaged parts using their procedures. If none is damaged, install an available CCM software update following scan-tool programming instructions. If no update is available, the branch directs CCM replacement.

steps.title: Test Q: establish whether low voltage is current
steps.body: With ignition on, repeat the CCM self-test. If U3003:16 is absent, a previous low-voltage event may explain it. If present, run the powertrain control module (PCM) self-test and follow any charging-system codes. Otherwise check battery condition and full charge; the failed battery-check branch directs battery replacement.

steps.title: Test Q: compare module supply with battery voltage
steps.body: Switch ignition off and disconnect C1582. Switch ignition on, record battery voltage, then measure C1582 pin 10 to ground. It must be within 0.2 volt of the recorded value; otherwise repair supply-circuit high resistance. If it passes, switch ignition off and check pin 4 to ground. Resistance must be less than 3 ohms; otherwise repair ground-circuit high resistance.

steps.title: Test Q: inspect connections before the final decision
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect the CCM connector for corrosion, bent, damaged or pushed-out pins. Replace affected connectors or terminals as directed and clean module pins. Reconnect securely and operate the system. If the concern persists, check OASIS for an applicable technical service bulletin and follow it; without one, replace the CCM. If operation returns, address the connection's root cause.

steps.title: Test R: distinguish overcharging from a historical event
steps.body: With ignition on, retrieve continuous-memory codes from all modules. U3003:17, P0563 or P0626 occurring across more than one module leads to charging-system diagnosis. Otherwise turn off lights and accessories, run the engine at approximately 2,000 rpm for 3 minutes and monitor battery voltage. A rise to 15.5 volts or higher also leads to charging diagnosis. Below that threshold, stop the engine, switch ignition on, clear continuous-memory codes and run the CCM self-test. Replace the CCM only if U3003:17 remains.

steps.title: Test S: trace missing data through the network
steps.body: For U0423:82, switch ignition on and confirm an observable symptom. Without one, the system is operating normally at this time. With a symptom, run the network test: an instrument panel cluster (IPC) failure leads to network diagnosis. If it passes, retrieve gateway module (GWM) codes; any also lead to network diagnosis. Next run the IPC self-test and follow any cluster codes, then the CCM self-test and its code chart.

steps.title: Test S: perform the final recheck
steps.body: If the preceding tests produce no codes, clear codes, wait 10 seconds and repeat the CCM self-test. Persistent U0423:82 requires the VIN-dependent IPC guided routine. If it clears, high network traffic or an intermittent condition may explain it. Recent module replacement also warrants checking whether programmable module installation was completed and configured correctly.

watchFor.title: Connector damage during testing
watchFor.body: Use the correct probe adapters; unsuitable probes can damage terminals and introduce another fault.

watchFor.title: Charging and jump-start history
watchFor.body: A stored U3003:17 can originate during earlier battery charging or jump starting.

notes: The charging-system referrals explicitly identify 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L branches. For a 5.2L reaching that decision, obtain its engine-specific charging procedure before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: The CCM records U3003:16.
diagnostics.meaning: It detected battery voltage below 9.5 volts for more than 500 ms.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test Q to distinguish battery, charging, circuit and module causes.

diagnostics.finding: The CCM records U3003:17.
diagnostics.meaning: It detected battery voltage above 16.5 volts for 500 ms.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test R; its running-voltage decision threshold differs from the code's trigger threshold.

diagnostics.finding: The CCM records U0423:82.
diagnostics.meaning: Expected adaptive-cruise data from the gateway or instrument cluster was missing for 5 seconds or longer.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test S's symptom, network and module sequence.

verification.title: Confirm the branch endpoint
verification.body: Use the specified operational check or repeat self-test; a historical code alone does not establish an active failure.

verification.title: Keep a diagnostic record
verification.body: Record original and returning codes, battery and supply readings, ground resistance, network results and the resulting repair or referral.

guides.title: Replace the cruise control deactivator switch
guides.summary: Replace the deactivator switch through the driver knee-airbag opening, following the conventional or adaptive cruise-control procedure.
guides.introduction: The cruise control deactivator switch provides a means of cancelling cruise operation. Both conventional and adaptive cruise systems are controlled by the powertrain control module (PCM), with driver commands supplied through steering-wheel switches. Although the deactivator switch is a small component, reaching it requires removal of the driver knee airbag, making restraint-system handling a central part of this repair.
guides.why: Correctly depowering the supplemental restraint system (SRS) is essential before airbag removal and reconnection. The adaptive-cruise procedure adds a separate mechanical precaution: installing the switch with the clutch pedal away from its resting position causes incorrect adjustment and damages the switch.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the cruise control deactivator switch needs replacement.
notes: Cruise disengagement alone is not proof of switch failure.
Select the conventional or adaptive cruise procedure from the vehicle's actual equipment.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Use the driver knee-airbag procedure and its referenced SRS depowering and repowering procedures. This job requires the ability to perform those operations precisely, not just remove dashboard trim.

prepare.title: Prepare trim and fastener access
prepare.detail: Have suitable hand tools and torque equipment for the trim and airbag fasteners. Identify the steering position: right-hand-drive removal includes an additional airbag harness pin-type retainer.

steps.title: Depower the restraint system
steps.body: Follow the SRS depowering procedure referenced by the driver knee-airbag article before starting airbag access. Do not substitute an assumed waiting period or an improvised electrical-disconnection sequence.

steps.title: Remove the surrounding trim
steps.body: Follow the airbag access sequence: remove the left instrument-panel trim, lighting-switch trim and subsequent trim panel, disconnecting their connectors as directed. Detach the ambient air temperature grille panel, its connector and tether.

steps.title: Remove the driver knee airbag
steps.body: Remove the under-panel nuts and screws, release the clips and separate the airbag from the instrument panel. Detach and disconnect its connector. On right-hand-drive vehicles, also release the harness pin-type retainer.

steps.title: Remove the switch using the correct branch
steps.body: For conventional cruise control, remove the deactivator switch and then disconnect its electrical connector. For adaptive cruise control, disconnect the connector before removing the switch. Use the matching procedure for the exact removal action.

steps.title: Fit the switch and restore the airbag
steps.body: Reverse the selected switch-removal sequence. Under the adaptive-cruise procedure, keep the clutch pedal at rest throughout switch installation: do not press, pull or otherwise move it. With the SRS still depowered, reinstall the airbag and surrounding trim through their procedure.

steps.title: Repower the restraint system
steps.body: Complete the referenced SRS repowering procedure after reassembly. Restoring the trim alone does not complete this repair.

watchFor.title: Clutch movement during adaptive-switch installation
watchFor.body: An off-rest pedal position can damage the switch as well as leave it incorrectly adjusted.

watchFor.title: Airbag reconnection with the system powered
watchFor.body: The restraint system must remain depowered when its component is reconnected.

notes: The access illustration shows the knee airbag and its connection; it is not a switch-adjustment diagram.

diagnostics.finding: Cruise speed varies on a steep hill or the system disengages after a substantial speed loss.
diagnostics.meaning: Both system overviews describe this as possible operating behavior; it does not by itself identify a failed deactivator switch.
diagnostics.next: Establish the cause of the complaint before selecting switch replacement.

verification.title: Confirm the installation condition
verification.body: For the adaptive-cruise branch, confirm that installation took place with the clutch pedal at rest and undisturbed.

verification.title: Record restraint-system restoration
verification.body: Record which cruise-control procedure was used and completion of the driver knee-airbag installation and SRS repowering procedure.

guides.title: Align the adaptive cruise control radar
guides.summary: Set the radar module vertically, then complete its horizontal alignment through the diagnostic scan tool.
guides.introduction: Adaptive cruise control uses radar inside the cruise control module (CCM) to measure the distance and relative speed of a vehicle ahead. That information supports requests to adjust vehicle speed and apply the brakes. Alignment establishes the radar's direction: vertical pitch is adjusted mechanically, while horizontal alignment is completed through software. Both phases belong to this job.
guides.why: The vehicle must be level so that the radar is aligned to a valid reference. A damaged mounting bracket can prevent correct alignment, and debris around the bumper cover can obstruct radar sensing. Completing the mechanical adjustment alone leaves the software calibration unfinished.
searchTerms: adaptive cruise control will not engage

when.summary: When the radar requires alignment or the message center displays FRONT SENSOR NOT ALIGNED.
notes: A sensor-blocked message has a different meaning and does not by itself justify adjusting the radar.
Inspect and repair bracket damage before attempting alignment.

prepare.title: Arrange level access
prepare.detail: Use a wheel alignment bay station and the front bumper cover removal procedure to expose the CCM.

prepare.title: Have both adjustment methods available
prepare.detail: Prepare a combination square level, an E20 Torx bit and a diagnostic scan tool with the Integrated Diagnostic System (IDS) CCM calibration function.

prepare.title: Plan the running-engine phase
prepare.detail: The engine must remain running throughout horizontal calibration. Arrange the work so this stage can proceed without interruption.

steps.title: Expose the radar and establish the reference
steps.body: Remove the [front bumper cover](#/document/G1694213), then place the vehicle on the wheel alignment bay station. The level vehicle provides the reference for the vertical measurement.

steps.title: Inspect the mount and locate the adjuster
steps.body: Inspect the CCM bracket for damage and repair it as necessary before continuing. Locate the alignment screw using the [radar alignment procedure](#/document/G1693156); adjusting against a damaged bracket may not produce a correct result.

steps.title: Set vertical pitch
steps.body: Place the combination square level against the face of the CCM. Keep it in position while using the E20 Torx bit to adjust the screw until the module is vertical and level. The illustration shows the level applied directly to the module face.

steps.title: Clean and reinstall the cover
steps.body: Remove debris from both the front and back of the bumper cover before reinstalling it. This completes the physical access and adjustment phase while addressing material that could obstruct the radar.

steps.title: Complete horizontal calibration
steps.body: Start the engine and follow the scan-tool prompts under IDS: Toolbox > Electrical > Cruise Control > CCM Calibration. Horizontal alignment is a software calibration and requires no manual adjustment. Leave the engine running until the entire routine finishes.

watchFor.title: Calibration cancellation
watchFor.body: Stopping the engine during horizontal alignment cancels the procedure and leaves the system non-functional.

watchFor.title: Other reasons for unavailable cruise control
watchFor.body: Radar obstruction and invalid vehicle-motion information can disable adaptive cruise control independently of alignment.

notes: The scan tool identifies the horizontal result as Alignment Offset; the stated specification is ±3.0 degrees.

diagnostics.finding: FRONT SENSOR NOT ALIGNED appears.
diagnostics.meaning: Adaptive cruise control cannot engage because the radar is not correctly aligned.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the bracket and complete both alignment phases.

diagnostics.finding: ADAPTIVE CRUISE NOT AVAILABLE SENSOR BLOCKED SEE MANUAL appears.
diagnostics.meaning: Debris or conditions that prevent detection of targets can trigger this message.
diagnostics.next: Address the obstruction or detection conditions before treating the complaint as an alignment fault.

verification.title: Confirm completion
verification.body: Confirm that the module was level before cover installation and that the scan-tool calibration completed without cancellation.

verification.title: Record the alignment result
verification.body: Record the calibration outcome and reported Alignment Offset against the stated specification. Adaptive cruise control resumes once alignment is correct and the radar can properly detect targets.

procedures.purpose: Perform mechanical vertical alignment and scan-tool horizontal calibration.
Remove and reinstall the front bumper cover for radar access.
Interpret alignment and obstruction messages and the horizontal offset specification.

guides.title: Replace and align the adaptive cruise control module
guides.summary: Remove the front radar module, inspect its mounting grommets and complete the required radar alignment after installation.
guides.introduction: The cruise control module (CCM) contains the radar that measures the distance and relative speed of a vehicle ahead. It requests speed changes from the powertrain control module and braking from the anti-lock braking system module to maintain the selected following gap. Replacement involves both a physical mounting job behind the front bumper cover and a required alignment procedure.
guides.why: The radar needs a secure mounting position and correct aim to detect targets properly. Damaged grommets must be replaced, and installation is incomplete until alignment is performed. An unavailable adaptive cruise system can also reflect obstruction or another system input, so a warning message alone does not prove the CCM has failed.
searchTerms: ADAPTIVE CRUISE NOT AVAILABLE SENSOR BLOCKED

when.summary: When the CCM requires replacement or removal for an established repair.
notes: Arrange radar alignment before removing the module; refitting it is only part of the job.

prepare.title: Arrange access and calibration capability
prepare.detail: Use the front bumper cover procedure for access. Have the equipment and capability required by the complete radar alignment procedure, including a suitable scan tool for the horizontal alignment check.

prepare.title: Prepare for mounting repairs
prepare.detail: Have a torque wrench suitable for the bracket fasteners and replacement grommets if inspection reveals damage. Bracket removal is conditional, rather than required for every module removal.

steps.title: Remove the front bumper cover
steps.body: Follow the linked bumper cover procedure to expose the CCM and its bracket. Identify the electrical connector and the module's retaining studs before separating the assembly.

steps.title: Disconnect and release the module
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector and gently pry the CCM from its retaining studs. Inspect the mounting grommets and replace any damaged ones so the module can be correctly retained.

steps.title: Remove the bracket only if required
steps.body: Separate the wiring harness guide. Remove the bracket's two bolts and nut, then slide the bracket left and down to remove it. Preserve that movement sequence when planning its refit.

steps.title: Reinstall the mounting assembly
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. If the bracket was removed, restore it and tighten its bolts and nut to 80 lb.in (9 Nm), then restore the harness guide. Refit the module on its grommets and studs, reconnect it and reinstall the bumper cover.

steps.title: Align the radar
steps.body: Complete the linked vertical and horizontal radar alignment procedure. Horizontal alignment is a scan-tool calibration check identified as Alignment Offset; use that procedure's conditions and acceptance criteria to establish completion.

watchFor.title: Alignment warning after installation
watchFor.body: FRONT SENSOR NOT ALIGNED means adaptive cruise will not engage. Recheck alignment through the specified procedure.

watchFor.title: Automatic braking has an operating limit
watchFor.body: During any operational assessment, remember that adaptive cruise releases automatic braking at 20 km/h (12 mph); the driver must take over braking.

notes: The module is gently released from retaining studs; the separate bracket is secured with bolts and a nut.

diagnostics.finding: A sensor-blocked message appears.
diagnostics.meaning: Snow, ice, rain or debris can obstruct detection; prolonged driving without detectable traffic can also trigger the condition.
diagnostics.next: Address obstruction and reassess when targets can be detected or after a key cycle before deciding on replacement.

diagnostics.finding: A cruise or collision-warning malfunction accompanies an invalid yaw-rate input.
diagnostics.meaning: Adaptive cruise can be disabled because of information supplied by another system.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the input fault through appropriate diagnosis rather than treating the warning as proof of CCM failure.

verification.title: Mounting and alignment completion
verification.body: Confirm sound grommets, secure mounting, restored electrical connection and completion of the radar alignment procedure.

verification.title: Record the alignment result
verification.body: Record completion of vertical alignment and the scan-tool Alignment Offset result against the linked procedure's specification.

procedures.purpose: Adaptive cruise CCM removal, grommet inspection, optional bracket removal and installation.
Front bumper cover removal and installation for radar-module access.
Required vertical and horizontal cruise-control radar alignment after installation.
Radar operation, warning-message distinctions and scan-tool alignment context.

guides.title: Diagnose missing or excessive forward collision warnings
guides.summary: Trace collision-warning complaints through settings, communication, temperature and voltage checks before deciding whether a module needs replacement.
guides.introduction: Forward collision warning uses the radar in the cruise control module (CCM) to assess vehicles ahead. It commands red light-emitting diodes (LEDs) in the head-up display (HUD), a warning chime through the instrument panel cluster (IPC), and audio muting. Because these functions depend on exchanged messages, an unlit warning bar can result from a network, temperature or power problem rather than failed LEDs.
guides.why: The order of testing separates unavailable information from a defective display. Heat can temporarily disable the LEDs, previous battery events can leave stored faults, and poor connector contact can interrupt otherwise functional electronics. A diagnostic trouble code (DTC) identifies a test path, not automatically a failed part.

when.summary: When collision warnings are unavailable, the warning bar fails to illuminate, excessive warnings occur, or related DTCs are recorded.
notes: For excessive warnings, check sensitivity and whether a MyKey restricted key is in use; verify operation with an administrator key.
A sensor-blocked message leads to adaptive cruise-control diagnosis.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of Ford network tests and module self-tests, a digital multimeter, Wiring Diagrams Cell 136, and the specified Rotunda Flex Probes or Terminal Probe Kit. Connector measurements require suitable adapters.

prepare.title: Establish reliable starting conditions
prepare.detail: Follow Diagnostic Methods: verify the complaint, inspect prior repairs and obvious wiring or fuse faults, check battery and charging operation, and confirm battery state of charge exceeds 70%. Address circuit DTCs before system-performance faults.

steps.title: Test A: follow the complete warning-system complaint
steps.body: For an inoperative forward collision warning system, begin the [diagnostic sequence](#/document/G1693174) with CCM and HUD network tests. A failure leads to Communications Network diagnosis. If both pass, run HUD self-tests, then CCM self-tests. Follow recorded DTCs; route CCM overtemperature code C1132:4B to Test E and other CCM codes to adaptive cruise-control diagnosis. With no codes, check IPC message-center operation before the final HUD connector check.

steps.title: Test B: distinguish an unlit HUD from a communication failure
steps.body: Move the vehicle away from extreme heat or sunload and observe the LEDs while switching to RUN. Illumination establishes that the LEDs currently work; temperature may explain the complaint. If they remain dark, test HUD network communication, then run HUD and CCM self-tests in that order. Follow their DTC routes before reaching the connector check.

steps.title: Test C: investigate missing CCM messages
steps.body: For U0104:00, first confirm an observable symptom. Without one, the system may currently be normal after an intermittent event or high network traffic. Otherwise, check CCM network communication and self-test results, then check the HUD for voltage DTCs. After those branches, clear codes and repeat the HUD self-test. If U0104:00 persists, the prescribed sequence is CCM replacement, clearing and retesting, followed by HUD replacement only if the code remains.

steps.title: Test D: investigate missing gateway messages
steps.body: For U0146:00, confirm the symptom, test gateway module (GWM) communication and retrieve its continuous-memory codes. Network failures or GWM codes lead to network diagnosis. Address HUD self-test codes, then clear codes, wait 10 seconds and repeat the HUD self-test. If U0146:00 remains, clear all codes, cycle ignition, wait 10 seconds and run the continuous-memory self-test across all modules. The code in other modules directs GWM replacement; its absence elsewhere directs HUD replacement. Consider incorrect or omitted Programmable Module Installation after recent module replacement.

steps.title: Test E: distinguish heat protection from HUD failure
steps.body: CCM code C1132:4B means HUD overtemperature. Check HUD network communication first. Away from extreme heat or sunload, repeat the RUN LED prove-out. Working LEDs support a temporary temperature event. Otherwise, run the HUD self-test and follow any codes; with none recorded, continue to the connector check.

steps.title: Test F: recheck the internal temperature-sensor circuit
steps.body: U210A:16 indicates a temperature-sensor circuit reading below its valid range; U210A:17 indicates one above it. Cycle ignition, clear HUD continuous-memory codes and retrieve them again. A returning code leads to the connector check. A code that does not return may reflect a previous intermittent internal fault.

steps.title: Test G: trace low supply voltage
steps.body: For U3003:16, clear codes and repeat the HUD self-test. If it returns, run the powertrain control module (PCM) key-on, engine-off self-test and follow engine-specific diagnostics for recorded codes. Confirm the battery is healthy and fully charged. With ignition off, disconnect HUD connector C2395; switch ignition on and record battery voltage. Measure pin 4 to ground, then pin 4 to pin 1. Each must be within 0.2 volt of the recorded battery voltage. Repair a failing supply or ground circuit; passing results lead to the connector check.

steps.title: Test H: investigate voltage outside the valid range
steps.body: For U3003:1C, retrieve all modules' continuous-memory codes. Charging-system codes in multiple modules lead to charging diagnosis. Otherwise, switch off lights and accessories and monitor battery voltage with the engine at approximately 2,000 rpm for 3 minutes. A rise to 15.5 volts or higher also leads to charging diagnosis. Below that threshold, cycle ignition, clear HUD memory and repeat its self-test. A returning code leads to the connector check; a cleared code may relate to earlier charging or jump starting.

steps.title: Complete the connector endpoint before replacement
steps.body: Where Tests A, B, E, F, G or H direct it, switch ignition off and inspect the HUD connector. Replace corroded connectors or terminals, clean module pins, and replace damaged, bent or pushed-out pins as required. Reconnect until fully seated and latched, then operate the system. If the concern remains, check Ford OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins and follow one if present; otherwise these endpoints direct HUD replacement. If operation returns, correct the underlying connector problem.

watchFor.title: Visibility and heat are different effects
watchFor.body: Strong sunlight or sunglasses can obscure the warning LEDs. Excessive compartment temperature can actually disable them temporarily, leaving the audible warning available.

watchFor.title: An absent complaint changes the decision
watchFor.body: Do not replace modules through a symptom-based test when its required complaint is not present. A HUD that will not communicate needs network diagnosis first.

notes: Engine-control and charging referrals must match the engine. For 5.2L, establish the applicable engine-specific procedure before taking those referrals; do not substitute another engine's checks.
SVT performance shift indication is another HUD function. Identify the actual complaint before applying collision-warning tests.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0405:68 is recorded in the HUD.
diagnostics.meaning: The HUD received invalid CCM network data containing a faulted input.
diagnostics.next: Retrieve and repair non-network DTCs in the other network modules.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0447:68 is recorded in the HUD.
diagnostics.meaning: The HUD received invalid data from the gateway.
diagnostics.next: Retrieve and repair non-network DTCs in the other network modules.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3000:41 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The HUD reports a general checksum failure.
diagnostics.next: Clear the codes and repeat the self-test. Replace the HUD only if U3000:41 returns.

verification.title: Check operation after the directed repair
verification.body: Repeat the applicable self-test and operational check. Confirm connector seating and LED prove-out where the selected test requires them.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record returning versus cleared codes, modules affected, battery and connector measurements, and whether the original concern remains.

applicability.equipment: Forward collision warning with adaptive cruise control

guides.title: Remove and replace the head-up display module
guides.summary: Release the dashboard-mounted head-up display, disconnect its wiring and refit it without damaging the retaining tab or surrounding trim.
guides.introduction: The head-up display (HUD) contains the red light-emitting diodes (LEDs) used for the forward collision warning above the instrument panel. The instrument panel cluster (IPC) provides the audible warning separately. On SVT vehicles, the HUD also provides selectable performance shift indications. This job removes or replaces the display module; it does not replace the radar sensor that determines collision risk.
guides.why: An apparently missing warning does not necessarily mean the display has failed. Strong sunlight and sunglasses can make the LEDs difficult to see, while high passenger-compartment temperature can temporarily suppress them. Once removal is justified, releasing the retaining tab with a non-marring tool protects the dashboard finish and avoids forcing the module out against its retention.

when.summary: When the HUD requires removal for access or diagnosis has established a need for replacement.
notes: Confirm whether the complaint concerns collision warnings or the SVT performance shift indication.

prepare.title: Protect the dashboard finish
prepare.detail: Have a non-marring trim tool available and identify the release location in the removal illustration.

prepare.title: Establish the complaint
prepare.detail: Note display settings, viewing conditions and any IPC warning message before treating an absent visual warning as a module fault.

steps.title: Check the reason for removal
steps.body: Review the fitted display function and the circumstances of the complaint. For collision-warning operation, the display receives a flash command from the cruise control module; the HUD is only one part of that warning chain.

steps.title: Release and raise the display
steps.body: Following the [HUD removal procedure](#/document/G1693176), use the non-marring tool to release the tab and position the HUD upward. The illustration identifies the release area above the instruments.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove
steps.body: With the connector accessible, disconnect it and remove the HUD. Raising the module first gives access to the connection without pulling the display away while it remains wired.

steps.title: Reconnect and refit
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: reconnect the electrical connector, return the HUD to its installed position and engage its retention.

watchFor.title: Temporary loss of visible output
watchFor.body: Heat-related LED suppression can leave the audible warning operating. Poor visibility in sunlight is also different from an electrical failure.

notes: On SVT vehicles, performance shift mode, shift points and display intensity are selected through the IPC message center.

diagnostics.finding: A collision-warning unavailable, sensor-blocked or malfunction message appears.
diagnostics.meaning: The system has reported a fault or limitation; the message does not identify the HUD as the failed component.
diagnostics.next: Establish the system fault before replacing the display.

verification.title: Check assembly
verification.body: Confirm the connector is attached and the module is seated with its retaining tab engaged.

verification.title: Observe the applicable confirmation
verification.body: For collision-warning equipment, observe the brief HUD and/or chime activation associated with confirmation of the last setting at an ignition cycle. Record which output occurred; a chime alone does not establish LED operation.

procedures.purpose: HUD module removal and reverse-sequence installation.
Collision-warning operation, visibility and temperature limitations, and SVT performance shift indication.

guides.title: Diagnose blind-spot and cross-traffic alerts, mirror lamps and blocked-sensor warnings
guides.summary: Trace missing or inconsistent alerts to operating conditions, settings, obstruction, wiring, configuration or communication faults before replacing components.
guides.introduction: The Blind Spot Information System (BLIS) uses radar modules behind the rear bumper sides to detect vehicles alongside the car during forward travel. Cross Traffic Alert (CTA) uses those modules while reversing, adding a chime and message to the mirror warning lights. The left and right side obstacle detection modules are called SODL and SODR. Their warning light-emitting diodes (LEDs) are integral to the mirror glass. Diagnosis separates detection problems from failures in the warning displays or their supporting circuits.
guides.why: A missing warning does not identify a failed radar module. Obstruction, incorrect gear information, disabled settings and lost network messages can produce similar complaints. Following the appropriate test also distinguishes a faulty mirror light from the wiring and module that supply it.
searchTerms: blind spot mirror light always on
blind spot mirror light not working
cross traffic chime without mirror warning
cannot turn off cross traffic alert

when.summary: When alerts malfunction, mirror warning lights behave incorrectly, a blocked-sensor message appears or settings cannot be changed.
notes: Confirm the complaint under appropriate operating conditions; weather, nearby parked vehicles and rapidly passing targets can affect detection.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, fused jumper and Rotunda Flex Probes. Obtain Wiring Diagrams Cells 146 and 14. Circuit testing requires correct connector identification and the prescribed ignition states.

prepare.title: Establish reliable starting conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging-system operation, with battery state of charge above 70%. Review previous repairs and applicable service information. Inspect wiring, fuses and connections; record relevant module codes before clearing them.

steps.title: Identify the affected function
steps.body: Start the engine and observe both mirror lights: they should illuminate and then extinguish after approximately 3 seconds. A continuously illuminated light leads to Test C; an inoperative light leads to Test D. A module that does not respond to the scan tool requires communications-network diagnosis.

steps.title: Follow Test A for poor or missing BLIS alerts
steps.body: After confirming the complaint, inspect rear bumper sides for obstructions, then bumper and module brackets for damage. Continue through network testing, SODL/SODR codes, message-center operation and the enabled setting, without a MyKey restricted key. Apply the parking brake and check that reversing lamps illuminate only in reverse. Then check the powertrain control module (PCM) key-on, engine-off self-test, gateway module (GWM) stored codes and recent module configuration work.

steps.title: Follow Test B for poor or missing cross-traffic alerts
steps.body: This includes a CTA chime without its mirror warning. After the startup-light and operating checks, Test B checks network communication and side-module codes before message-center operation, enabling, reverse input, PCM self-test and gateway codes. Bumper obstruction and damage checks follow those checks, then configuration history. Recent side-module service directs installation of the appropriate Ford as-built data.

steps.title: Isolate a constantly illuminated mirror light with Test C
steps.body: Confirm that the light remains on during the specified observation. Disconnect the affected side module and test for unwanted supply-circuit voltage. Disconnecting the mirror then separates vehicle wiring from a mirror fault. Follow the mirror-harness inspection: a sound harness leads to glass replacement; an unrepairable harness requires a mirror. No unwanted voltage leads to the module-connector branch.

steps.title: Trace an inoperative light with Test D
steps.body: Check network operation and self-test results first. Follow the short-to-ground check where directed, then the prescribed fused-jumper illumination test; remove the jumper afterward. Illumination leads toward module checks. Otherwise, test the LED, supply and ground paths. An open LED leads to glass replacement. The later mirror-harness branch distinguishes repairable wiring from a complete mirror replacement. Use the exact connector locations and limits in the linked test.

steps.title: Follow Test E for a blocked-sensor message
steps.body: Inspect for debris, mud, snow or ice and clean affected areas. If unobstructed, inspect the bumper, sensors and brackets for damage. If those checks pass, follow the affected module's connector branch. A blocked state alone does not establish sensor failure.

steps.title: Follow Test F when the systems cannot be switched off
steps.body: A MyKey restricted key normally prevents these menu changes. Otherwise, test communication with the instrument panel cluster and both side modules, retrieve side-module self-tests, then check message-center switching. CTA normally returns to enabled after an ignition cycle; BLIS remains disabled until manually enabled.

steps.title: Use the code-specific communication and configuration branches
steps.body: Use Tests G, H and I as distinguished below. Follow each test's clearing sequence and ignition-cycle waits. Without an observable symptom, these communication-code tests direct clearing the code rather than component replacement. Diagnose circuit faults and the specified non-network faults before pursuing module failure.

steps.title: Complete the relevant connector and module decision
steps.body: Where directed, switch the ignition off and inspect module and in-line connectors. Replace damaged terminals, correct corrosion and ensure connectors latch. Retest operation and address the cause of connection damage. Persistent faults require the applicable service-bulletin check before the selected test authorizes module replacement.

watchFor.title: Warning lights can accompany blockage
watchFor.body: Read the message center before treating illuminated mirror lights as an electrical short. Heavy rain can also cause a blocked state.

watchFor.title: Protect terminals and module outputs
watchFor.body: Use proper probes and only the jumper connection directed by Test D. Isolate circuits for resistance measurements; do not improvise power or ground connections.

notes: Keep bumper stickers and body filler away from the rear bumper sensor areas.
BLIS and CTA assist observation; they are not collision-prevention systems. Some functional faults do not store a code.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B11D6:11 or B11D6:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: B11D6:11 indicates an LED circuit short to ground. B11D6:15 can indicate a short to battery or an open circuit.
diagnostics.next: Use Test D for B11D6:11. For B11D6:15, select Test C if the light stays on or Test D if it is inoperative.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0100:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The side module has lost PCM messages routed through the gateway.
diagnostics.next: Test G checks PCM scan access, code recurrence, PCM self-test, side-module non-network faults, gateway codes and matching faults elsewhere. Only its final connector and service-information branch can lead to PCM replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0101:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Transmission-control messages are missing. In this diagnostic path, the transmission control module is within the PCM and is not separately serviceable.
diagnostics.next: Test H checks PCM network response, side-module non-network faults, gateway codes and recurrence in other modules before the PCM connector and replacement decision.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0146:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Gateway messages are missing.
diagnostics.next: Test I checks gateway network response and codes, side-module non-network faults and recurrence elsewhere before gateway connector inspection and any replacement decision.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0401:86 or U0402:86 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The side module has received invalid powertrain data.
diagnostics.next: Retrieve and repair non-network codes in other network modules. If no PCM codes exist, diagnose the observable symptom.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U2100:00 or U3002:62 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Configuration is incomplete or the stored vehicle identification number does not match the network.
diagnostics.next: Check service history. After recent module work, U2100:00 requires as-built data; U3002:62 requires repeating programmable module installation. Without recent service, the chart directs module replacement for failure to retain configuration.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U2300:55 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The side module cannot detect vehicle identification number information on the network.
diagnostics.next: Retrieve and repair non-network codes in all other modules.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3000:44, U3000:45, U3000:46 or U3000:49 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These identify data-memory, program-memory, calibration/parameter-memory or internal-electronic faults respectively.
diagnostics.next: Clear the affected side module's codes and repeat its self-test. Replace that module only if the relevant code returns.

verification.title: Confirm restored operation
verification.body: Repeat the affected function and mirror-light checks. After cleaning a blockage, perform one key cycle and drive: the side modules need to detect 2 good targets to clear the blocked condition.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record the affected side, original complaint, initial codes and required repeat-test results. If a fault cannot be reproduced, document that outcome without treating it as proof that a component needs replacement.

applicability.equipment: Blind Spot Information System (BLIS) with Cross Traffic Alert (CTA)

guides.title: Replace a blind-spot detection module or its mounting bracket
guides.summary: Remove the rear bumper cover to service the left or right radar module, completing programmable module installation when replacing the module.
guides.introduction: The side obstacle detection modules sit behind the rear bumper cover, rearward of the rear wheels. The left module (SODL) and right module (SODR) use radar to detect targets for the Blind Spot Information System (BLIS) and Cross Traffic Alert (CTA). This job replaces a module or services its mounting bracket, with an additional scan-tool process whenever a module is replaced.
guides.why: A blocked sensor, a system fault and an operating limitation are different conditions. Establishing which is present avoids treating every missed alert as a failed module. When replacement is justified, programmable module installation (PMI) must begin before removal and finish after installation.

when.summary: When diagnosis requires replacement of a side obstacle detection module, or its mounting bracket needs service.
notes: PMI applies when replacing SODL or SODR; it is not specified for bracket-only work with the original module retained.

prepare.title: Identify the side and repair scope
prepare.detail: Establish whether the left module, right module or bracket requires service. Check the rear bumper sides for debris, stickers or damage that could affect detection.

prepare.title: Arrange programming and access
prepare.detail: For module replacement, have a diagnostic scan tool capable of the required PMI process. Prepare to remove and reinstall the rear bumper cover using its linked procedure.

steps.title: Begin PMI when replacing a module
steps.body: Before removal, use the diagnostic scan tool to begin PMI for the affected SODL or SODR. Follow its on-screen instructions. Omit this step when retaining the existing module.

steps.title: Expose the module
steps.body: Remove the rear bumper cover using the linked procedure. This provides access to the radar module and its bracket.

steps.title: Remove the module
steps.body: Disconnect the module’s electrical connector, remove its screws and remove SODL or SODR. Module removal is also the prerequisite for removing the bracket.

steps.title: Service the bracket if required
steps.body: With the module removed, disconnect the wiring-harness guide. Remove the bracket screws and the side obstacle detection module bracket.

steps.title: Reassemble and finish programming
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure, restoring the bracket, harness guide, module connection and bumper cover as applicable. If a module was replaced, complete PMI with the scan tool, following the on-screen instructions.

watchFor.title: Obstructed radar area
watchFor.body: Do not place bumper stickers or body filler over the rear bumper areas near the modules. Mud, snow and heavy rain can also degrade detection.

watchFor.title: System limits
watchFor.body: BLIS assists the driver; it does not prevent contact. Rapidly passing targets and obstructed cross-traffic views can produce missed alerts without establishing module failure.

notes: BLIS operates in forward gear above its activation threshold; CTA operates in reverse. A MyKey restricted key prevents either system from being switched off through the message center.

diagnostics.finding: A SENSOR BLOCKED message appears.
diagnostics.meaning: Blocked operation is a normal response to degraded detection, not itself a system fault.
diagnostics.next: Address visible obstruction and reassess. The state can self-clear; cycling the ignition may clear it temporarily, but persistent blockage can trigger it again.

diagnostics.finding: BLIND SPOT SYSTEM FAULT or CROSS TRAFFIC SYSTEM FAULT appears.
diagnostics.meaning: A system concern exists, but the message alone does not identify a failed module. Some concerns store diagnostic trouble codes; others are symptom-based.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose the concern before choosing replacement. Remember that a CTA fault may not appear until reverse is selected.

verification.title: Observe startup indications
verification.body: At startup, the modules command the exterior-mirror indicators on for approximately 3 seconds. Check the indications and message center, including whether a CTA fault appears when reverse is selected.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the side serviced, whether the module or bracket was changed, PMI completion when applicable, and any remaining warning messages.

procedures.purpose: Left or right module and bracket removal, installation and conditional PMI.
Rear bumper cover removal and installation for module access.
Operating indications, blocked-sensor behavior and detection limitations.

applicability.equipment: Blind Spot Information System and Cross Traffic Alert

guides.title: Diagnose BCM fault codes and communication problems
guides.summary: Use body control module fault codes, network response and self-test conditions to select the correct electrical or configuration diagnostic path.
guides.introduction: The body control module (BCM) reads switches, sensors and messages from other controllers, then operates functions such as lighting, locks and ignition-state messaging. A fault recorded here can concern an external circuit, another controller or configuration data. This job establishes which diagnostic path will distinguish those possibilities.
guides.why: Shared electrical supplies, missing messages and protective output shutdowns can affect several functions. Understanding what a code actually reports prevents a wiring or configuration problem from being mistaken for module failure.
searchTerms: BCM not responding to scan tool

when.summary: A body electrical function malfunctions, the BCM records fault codes, or a module will not communicate.

prepare.title: Establish electrical readiness
prepare.detail: Use Ford diagnostic capability and a suitable scan tool. Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70% before diagnostics.

prepare.title: Prepare for circuit testing
prepare.detail: Have wiring diagrams and the specified Rotunda flex probes available. Confirm the complaint is present unless the selected test explicitly permits otherwise.

steps.title: Confirm the affected function
steps.body: Check previous repairs and inspect relevant wiring, fuses and connectors. Distinguish the BCM from body control module B, which handles functions including ambient lighting and convertible controls.

steps.title: Read the network before choosing a component
steps.body: Retrieve diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) across the network. Diagnose circuit codes before system or performance codes; several circuit faults may share a supply or ground. A module that does not respond requires Communications Network diagnosis, considering fuses, connections and the module.

steps.title: Match the complete code to the complaint
steps.body: Use the BCM chart to route lighting, security, restraint and other faults to their own systems. Antenna codes B10C7:01, B11C6:01 and B11CA:01 require passive anti-theft diagnosis for starting complaints, but locks-and-entry diagnosis for passive-entry complaints. Starting-system referrals must match the engine.

steps.title: Separate supply faults from output protection
steps.body: Input-power codes route to Test K for low voltage and Test L for high voltage; U3006:1C uses Test S. U1000:00 routes to Test R because excessive current can cause protective circuitry to disable an output.

steps.title: Handle unlisted codes in sequence
steps.body: Repair other DTCs first. With no other codes present, clear and repeat the self-test. If an unlisted code returns, verify the module part number; only with the correct module installed should the specified As-Built configuration be loaded.

steps.title: Continue through the selected diagnostic
steps.body: Follow the exact system or pinpoint test before deciding on repair. Use commanded output tests where directed: a functioning output shifts attention toward its inputs. Do not apply power or ground directly to module-controlled components unless instructed.

watchFor.title: Repeated short circuits
watchFor.body: Repeated faults can exhaust an output's protection capability. Correct the circuit fault before any resulting module replacement.

watchFor.title: Equipment-specific entries
watchFor.body: Apply steering-lock and SYNC 3 camera branches only where that equipment is fitted.

notes: BCM replacement requires programmable module installation; a replacement decision is not the end of the configuration work.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0100:87 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM missed powertrain control module (PCM) messages on the high-speed Controller Area Network.
diagnostics.next: Use Test A, considering network, charging-system, PCM and BCM causes.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U2100:00 or U2200:00 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: U2100:00 indicates incomplete configuration; U2200:00 indicates corrupt configuration memory.
diagnostics.next: For U2100:00, check recent programming history. Install the specified As-Built data. If U2200:00 returns after clearing and self-testing, use the BCM guided routine with the vehicle identification number.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U1A4C:55 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: Build or end-of-line mode is active.
diagnostics.next: A factory-mode message requires the deactivation procedure. Without that message, clear and retest; recurrence requires the vehicle-identification-number-based BCM guided routine.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U2005:85 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: A speed signal was detected during the BCM self-test.
diagnostics.next: Meet the scan-tool entry conditions with the vehicle stationary. Diagnose observable symptoms, clear and retest; recurrence calls for investigating PCM or anti-lock brake system codes causing false speed information.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3000:49 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM reports an internal electronic failure.
diagnostics.next: Address all other DTCs first, clear and repeat the self-test. Recurrence requires the BCM guided routine with the vehicle identification number.

verification.title: Repeat the appropriate self-test
verification.body: Use the selected chart branch's clearing and retest sequence under its required conditions.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic handoff
verification.body: Record the complaint, returning codes and next test. Complete that test before treating the fault as resolved.

Electrical prerequisites, module testing and terminal-safe measurement methods.
BCM operation, protective output shutdown and replacement configuration requirements.
Diagnosis when a module does not respond to the scan tool.
Passive anti-theft diagnosis for antenna-related starting complaints.
Locks-and-entry diagnosis for antenna-related passive-entry complaints.
Mode deactivation when directed by the U1A4C:55 chart branch.

guides.title: Diagnose BCM lost-communication codes
guides.summary: Trace missing controller messages through communication, voltage, self-test and connector checks before deciding on further repair.
guides.introduction: The body control module (BCM) coordinates body electrical functions and exchanges information with other controllers. These tests concern the powertrain control module (PCM), body control module B (BCMB), anti-lock brake system (ABS) module and power steering control module (PSCM). Gateway Module A (GWM) carries messages between networks. The aim is to establish why information is missing and which diagnostic path to follow.
guides.why: The controller recording a missing message is not necessarily faulty. Comparing communication, voltage and other modules’ reports helps distinguish a network problem from a connection or controller concern.
searchTerms: module does not respond to scan tool

when.summary: When the BCM records U0100:87, U0142:87, U0121:87 or U0131:87.

prepare.title: Diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting network tests, module self-tests and continuous memory diagnostic trouble codes (CMDTCs). Ford-specific diagnostic knowledge and connector-repair skills are needed.

prepare.title: Vehicle and service information
prepare.detail: Have the vehicle identification number (VIN), service history and access to Ford’s On-Line Automotive Service Information System (OASIS), technical service bulletins (TSBs) and guided routines.

steps.title: Check recent module work
steps.body: If the fault followed module replacement, check whether programmable module installation (PMI) was completed correctly. Missing or incorrect configuration can create communication concerns.

steps.title: Establish communication
steps.body: Follow the applicable [BCM test](#/document/G1692965) with ignition ON. Test A requires a scan-tool vehicle session. Tests B–D first require an observable symptom; if absent, clear the code and stop. Otherwise network-test BCMB, ABS or PSCM respectively. Failed communication leads to the matching [network diagnosis](#/document/G1813071).

steps.title: Follow Test A’s self-test sequence
steps.body: Clear codes, wait 10 seconds and read BCM memory. If U0100:87 returns, run the PCM key on, engine off self-test. Refer voltage-related codes to Electronic Engine Controls for the fitted engine. With none present, run the BCM self-test; any recorded codes go to its DTC chart. If U0100:87 did not return, operation is correct at this time.

steps.title: Follow Tests B–D’s preliminary gates
steps.body: After communication passes, clear codes, wait 10 seconds and read BCM memory. U3006:16, U3007:16, U3013:16 or U3014:16 directs Test K; U3006:17, U3007:17, U3013:17 or U3014:17 directs Test L. Otherwise perform the partner self-test described below. If it permits continuation, clear codes, wait 10 seconds and recheck the original BCM code; stop if absent.

steps.title: Compare reports from other modules
steps.body: For a persistent code after the preceding checks, clear codes, switch ignition OFF then ON, wait 10 seconds and retrieve all CMDTCs. U0100, U0142, U0121 or U0131 in another module selects the corresponding partner’s connector check. Otherwise inspect BCM connections.

steps.title: Inspect and restore connections
steps.body: With ignition OFF, disconnect and inspect the selected module’s connectors. Replace corroded connectors or terminals and clean module pins; replace damaged, bent or pushed-out pins as necessary. Reconnect fully, ensuring every connector seats and latches, then operate the system. Address the cause of connector damage even if operation returns.

steps.title: Use the correct escalation
steps.body: If the concern remains, check OASIS and follow any applicable TSB instead of continuing this test. Without an applicable bulletin, the partner branches specify a new PCM, BCMB or ABS module using its dedicated installation procedure. The PSCM branch hands off to the VIN-specific electric power-assisted steering (EPAS) routine; BCM branches require the VIN-specific BCM routine.

watchFor.title: A code that disappears
watchFor.body: High network traffic or an intermittent fault can leave stored codes. A clear retest establishes present operation, not a permanent cure.

watchFor.title: Restraint-system boundaries
watchFor.body: Restraint work requires dedicated depowering and repowering procedures. Never probe airbag or seatbelt deployable-device connectors.

notes: Guided-routine handoffs do not by themselves authorize module replacement.

diagnostics.finding: The BCM records U0100:87.
diagnostics.meaning: Test A investigates communication with the PCM.
diagnostics.next: Use the PCM-session and self-test sequence above.

diagnostics.finding: The BCM records U0142:87.
diagnostics.meaning: BCMB messages received through the GWM are missing.
diagnostics.next: Test B: any BCMB self-test code requires BCMB diagnosis before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: The BCM records U0121:87.
diagnostics.meaning: ABS module messages received through the GWM are missing.
diagnostics.next: Test C: voltage-related ABS self-test codes lead to ABS and stability-control diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: The BCM records U0131:87.
diagnostics.meaning: PSCM messages received through the GWM are missing.
diagnostics.next: Test D: any PSCM self-test code leads to Power Steering diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: The BCM records U0151:87.
diagnostics.meaning: Supplemental restraint system messages from the restraints control module are missing through the GWM; network, battery voltage or either controller may be involved.
diagnostics.next: Use dedicated restraint/network diagnosis; Tests A–D do not resolve this code.

verification.title: Confirm operation
verification.body: After connector repairs, operate the affected system and determine whether the original concern remains.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record returning codes, reporting modules, self-test results and the resulting repair or diagnostic handoff.

guides.title: Diagnose BCM communication faults with restraints, instruments, audio and the driver door
guides.summary: Trace BCM missing-message codes through network, voltage, self-test and connector checks to identify the correct repair path.
guides.introduction: The body control module (BCM) uses switch inputs and messages from other modules to operate functions such as lighting, locks and wipers. Communication faults mean expected information is missing. Tests E–H investigate the restraints, instrument cluster, audio and driver-door links, separating a network interruption from a supply, connection or module problem.
guides.why: Unstable voltage and incorrect replacement-module configuration can interrupt communication. Checking these first, then comparing which modules report the missing message, gives a reasoned basis for choosing where to inspect.

when.summary: Use when the BCM records one of these missing-message codes; first establish whether an observable symptom is present.
notes: Without a current symptom, Tests E–H direct code clearing rather than component replacement.

prepare.title: Scan and configuration access
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of network tests, module self-tests and continuous-memory code retrieval. Have the vehicle identification number available for guided routines.

prepare.title: Check voltage and repair history
prepare.detail: Verify battery and charging operation and battery state of charge above 70%. Recent module replacement warrants checking configuration and programmable module installation (PMI).

prepare.title: Prepare for the selected module
prepare.detail: Restraints control module connector work requires restraint-system service capability and the full procedure's safety prerequisites. Select audio procedures for the vehicle's fitted SYNC equipment.

steps.title: Verify the complaint before following the code
steps.body: Turn ignition on and establish an observable symptom. If none is present, clear the code and stop this replacement decision path. High network traffic or an intermittent fault may explain a stored code.

steps.title: Check communication with the named module
steps.body: Network-test the code's counterpart: restraints control module (RCM), instrument panel cluster (IPC), audio front control module (ACM), or driver door module (DDM). A failed network test leads to Communications Network diagnosis. A communicating module permits the voltage and self-test checks that follow.

steps.title: Resolve BCM voltage codes first
steps.body: Clear codes, wait 10 seconds and read BCM continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes. U3006:16, U3007:16, U3013:16 or U3014:16 direct Pinpoint Test K. U3006:17, U3007:17, U3013:17 or U3014:17 direct Test L. Follow those branches before continuing the missing-message investigation.

steps.title: Run the counterpart's self-test
steps.body: Test E redirects RCM voltage-related codes to restraint-system diagnosis; Test F redirects IPC voltage-related codes to instrumentation diagnosis. Test G redirects any ACM codes to the matching entertainment-system procedure. Test H runs the DDM self-test and redirects any codes to locks, latches and entry-system diagnosis.

steps.title: Determine whether the missing message persists elsewhere
steps.body: If the preceding checks allow continuation, clear codes, wait 10 seconds and recheck the original BCM code. If absent, the fault may be intermittent. If present, clear again, cycle ignition off then on, wait 10 seconds and retrieve all continuous-memory codes. The corresponding U0151, U0155, U0184 or U0199 in another module selects counterpart connector checks; otherwise inspect the BCM.

steps.title: Repair connections and follow the resulting decision
steps.body: Inspect the selected module's connectors. Replace corroded connectors or terminals, clean module pins, and renew damaged, bent or displaced pins as directed. Reconnect securely and operate the system. If the concern persists, check applicable service bulletins and follow any matching instructions. Without one, the completed branches direct RCM, ACM or DDM replacement, or a vehicle-specific guided routine for IPC or BCM. Any BCM replacement requires PMI.

watchFor.title: A code after module replacement
watchFor.body: Incorrect configuration or omitted PMI can produce these faults. Include that history before condemning another module.

watchFor.title: A concern that disappears after reconnection
watchFor.body: Find and correct the connector or terminal's underlying problem; reseating alone does not explain corrosion or poor pin retention.

notes: The gateway module carries the IPC, ACM and door-module messages to the BCM. Gateway and network concerns remain possible, especially when several communication faults occur together.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0151:87 is recorded in the BCM.
diagnostics.meaning: Test E investigates communication with the RCM.
diagnostics.next: Check RCM network response and voltage-related self-test codes before selecting RCM or BCM connector checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0155:87 is recorded in the BCM.
diagnostics.meaning: Expected IPC messages through the gateway are missing.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test F; persistent IPC-side concerns lead to its guided routine.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0184:87 is recorded in the BCM.
diagnostics.meaning: Expected radio/ACM messages through the gateway are missing.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test G, including all ACM self-test codes and the fitted SYNC procedure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0199:87 is recorded in the BCM.
diagnostics.meaning: Expected DDM messages through the gateway are missing.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test H and diagnose any DDM self-test codes through the locks procedure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0200:87 is recorded in the BCM.
diagnostics.meaning: Expected passenger door module messages through the gateway are missing.
diagnostics.next: Continue with passenger-door communication diagnosis to distinguish voltage, network, gateway and module causes.

verification.title: Confirm the observed function
verification.body: After connector repair, operate the affected system and determine whether the original concern remains. Continue the selected branch if it does.

verification.title: Preserve the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record network-test outcomes, counterpart self-test codes and which modules retain the missing-message code after the specified clearing, ignition cycle and 10-second waits.

guides.title: Diagnose BCM communication, fuel-pump relay and supply-voltage faults
guides.summary: Separate passenger-door communication faults, fuel-pump relay circuit faults and abnormal BCM supply voltage before deciding whether a module needs replacement.
guides.introduction: The body control module (BCM) turns switch inputs and network messages into functions such as lighting and locking. It also grounds the fuel-pump relay coil. These diagnostic paths investigate the messages, electrical supply and connections that allow those functions to work.
guides.why: A stored code can reflect battery history, wiring resistance or a poor connection. Establishing which condition is present prevents an unnecessary module replacement.

when.summary: When passenger-door communication, fuel-pump relay or BCM supply-voltage codes require diagnosis.

prepare.title: Electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Have a network-capable scan tool, digital multimeter, specified Rotunda Flex Probes and the relevant wiring diagrams. Follow the connector and ignition states in each pinpoint test.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Verify battery state of charge above 70%. For resistance measurements, follow Diagnostic Methods for battery disconnection and circuit isolation so existing voltage cannot corrupt the reading.

steps.title: Test I: establish whether the passenger-door concern is active
steps.body: With ignition ON, confirm an observable symptom. If none exists, clear the diagnostic trouble code (DTC); intermittent conditions or heavy network traffic may explain it. Otherwise run the network test. A passenger door module (PDM) that fails requires communication-network diagnosis.

steps.title: Test I: eliminate voltage and door-system faults
steps.body: If the PDM passes, clear codes, wait 10 seconds and read BCM continuous-memory codes. Route returning low- or high-voltage codes to Test K or L. Otherwise run the PDM self-test; its recorded codes lead to locks and entry-system diagnosis. If none are recorded, repeat the BCM clear/wait/recheck. A disappearing U0200:87 indicates correct operation at this time.

steps.title: Test I: choose the correct connector inspection
steps.body: If U0200:87 persists, clear codes, cycle ignition OFF then ON, wait 10 seconds and retrieve all continuous-memory codes. U0200 in another module directs inspection of the PDM connections; otherwise inspect the BCM connections. Use the final connector decision below.

steps.title: Test J: isolate the fuel-pump relay circuit
steps.body: P0230:14 indicates an open or short to ground in the relay-coil circuit. Inspect battery junction box (BJB) fuse 49 (30A). With ignition OFF, substitute a known-good relay, then switch ON, clear codes and run the BCM self-test. If the code clears, install a new relay. If it returns, follow J2: disconnect BCM C2280F with ignition OFF, then measure pin 26 to ground with ignition ON. A reading above 11 volts leads to BCM connector checks; a lower reading requires fuse investigation or circuit repair.

steps.title: Test K: trace low supply voltage
steps.body: With ignition ON, clear codes, wait 10 seconds and run the BCM self-test. If the codes disappear, previous low battery voltage may explain them. If they return, diagnose charging-system codes first, then check battery condition and full charge. Investigate discharge causes; replace a failed battery. Follow K4 supply comparisons and K5 ground checks: feeds must be within 0.2 volt of recorded battery voltage and ground resistance below 3 ohms. Repair excessive resistance.

steps.title: Test L: distinguish overcharging from stored history
steps.body: Retrieve all module codes and diagnose charging-system codes first. Otherwise turn off lights and accessories, then monitor battery voltage with the engine at approximately 2,000 rpm for 3 minutes. Reaching 16 volts or higher requires overcharging diagnosis. Below that threshold, clear codes, wait 10 seconds and reread BCM continuous memory. Returning high-voltage codes lead to BCM connector inspection.

steps.title: Complete the relevant module-connection decision
steps.body: Inspect the selected module’s connectors. Clean corroded module pins; replace affected connectors, terminals and damaged or pushed-out pins. Reconnect securely and operate the system. If the concern remains, check applicable technical service bulletins through OASIS and follow any matching bulletin. Without one, Test I’s PDM branch directs a new PDM; BCM branches require the vehicle identification number (VIN) to continue the BCM Guided Routine.

watchFor.title: Historical high-voltage codes
watchFor.body: Battery charging or jump-starting can leave high-voltage codes after the event has ended.

watchFor.title: Misleading unloaded readings
watchFor.body: An unloaded voltage reading can miss excessive circuit resistance. Follow Diagnostic Methods when a supply remains suspect.

notes: After recent module installation, investigate incorrect or incomplete programmable module installation (PMI). A replacement BCM requires PMI.
Use charging-system diagnosis for the fitted engine.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3006:16, U3007:16, U3013:16 or U3014:16 returns.
diagnostics.meaning: BCM supply input A, B, C or D respectively is below its expected voltage.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test K through charging, battery, supply and ground checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3006:17, U3007:17, U3013:17 or U3014:17 returns.
diagnostics.meaning: The corresponding BCM supply input reports voltage above its expected threshold.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test L to distinguish active overcharging from a stored event.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0208:87 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM is missing driver front seat module (DSM) messages received through the gateway module (GWM). Possible causes include network, battery-voltage or module concerns.
diagnostics.next: Continue communication diagnosis; this finding alone does not establish which module needs replacement.

verification.title: Confirm operation
verification.body: Operate the affected system after connection repairs and complete the applicable code recheck. Address the cause of any connector damage.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record returning codes, network results and electrical readings, including whether the original symptom remains.
