guides.title: Diagnose BCM communication, protected-output and supply-voltage faults
guides.summary: Use Tests Q, R and S to separate front-controls communication faults, overload protection and abnormal BCM supply voltage.
guides.introduction: The body control module (BCM) uses switch, sensor and network inputs to operate functions including lighting, locks and wipers. Its electronic output switches also monitor excessive current and can shut a circuit down to protect the module. These tests investigate three different fault patterns: communication with the front controls, a disabled output, and voltage outside the module's expected range.
guides.why: A stored code can reflect a temporary network interruption, an external short or a battery-related event. Testing the affected circuit and power supply establishes whether the BCM is responding to a fault elsewhere before module replacement is considered.
searchTerms: BCM voltage code after jump starting

when.summary: When BCM codes U0256:87, U1000:00 or U3006:1C are recorded and require confirmation or fault isolation.
notes: A code without a currently observable concern does not justify automatic module replacement.

prepare.title: Provide the required diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting network tests, module self-tests and live data, plus a digital multimeter and Rotunda Flex Probes. Have power, ground and connector information available. Test S includes engine-running voltage measurements and isolated resistance checks.

prepare.title: Check the electrical baseline
prepare.detail: Inspect wiring, connectors and previous repairs; check battery and charging operation. Battery state of charge must exceed 70% before diagnostics. Test S later requires verification that the battery is healthy and fully charged.

steps.title: Q: confirm the concern and front-controls communication
steps.body: With ignition ON, verify an observable symptom. If none is present, clear U0256:87 as directed; intermittent conditions or heavy network traffic may explain it. If a symptom exists, run the network test. Failure of the front controls interface module (FCIM) to communicate leads to communications-network diagnosis.

steps.title: Q: resolve prerequisite codes and confirm recurrence
steps.body: Clear codes, wait 10 seconds and check BCM continuous-memory codes. Q3 routes its listed supply-code groups to Test K or L before continuing. Otherwise, self-test the FCIM and follow recorded-code diagnosis for the fitted SYNC or touchscreen system. Clear and recheck BCM codes after another 10 seconds. If U0256:87 does not return, the fault is not currently confirmed.

steps.title: Q: use other modules to choose the next inspection
steps.body: If U0256:87 persists, clear codes, cycle ignition OFF and ON, wait 10 seconds and retrieve all continuous-memory codes. U0256 in another module directs inspection to the FCIM at Q7; absence from other modules directs inspection to the BCM at Q8. This uses the spread of the communication complaint to select the next check.

steps.title: R: repair the cause of output protection
steps.body: For U1000:00, review the BCM self-test and correct any companion codes through its code chart first. Once no other codes remain, clear codes, wait 10 seconds and repeat the self-test. A returning U1000:00 requires the vehicle identification number (VIN)-dependent BCM guided routine. If it does not return, Test R identifies the circuit short as repaired.

steps.title: S: investigate charging voltage before local wiring
steps.body: Check the BCM self-test for charging codes, then retrieve codes from other modules. Follow the appropriate charging-system referral before proceeding. With lights and accessories off, run the engine at approximately 2,000 rpm for 3 minutes while monitoring battery voltage. Reaching 16 volts or higher requires overcharging diagnosis. Otherwise, cycle ignition OFF and ON, clear codes, wait 10 seconds and recheck U3006:1C. If absent, previous charging, jump starting or connector trouble may explain it.

steps.title: S: compare battery condition and reported voltage
steps.body: If the code remains, verify battery condition and full charge. Diagnose the cause of discharge; replace a battery that fails its condition check. With a sound, charged battery, idle the engine with the climate blower on high and exterior lights on. Record battery voltage and compare it with the BCM battery-voltage parameter identification (PID), V_BATT_BCM. Agreement within 0.2 volt directs you to turn the engine off and continue to S9.

steps.title: S: isolate a supply or ground discrepancy
steps.body: If the readings disagree, follow S7's connector-disconnection and ignition sequence to check the listed BCM supplies against the recorded battery voltage. Each must be within 0.2 volt. If they pass, follow S8 with ignition OFF and the specified connector disconnected; processor-ground resistances must be less than 3 ohms. Repair high resistance where a check fails.

steps.title: Finish the applicable connector branch
steps.body: At Q7, Q8 or S9, inspect the selected module's connectors. Renew corroded connectors or terminals, clean module pins, and replace damaged or pushed-out pins as necessary. Seat and latch connections, then operate the system. If the concern remains, check technical service bulletins through OASIS and follow any applicable bulletin. Otherwise, continue to the VIN-dependent FCIM or BCM guided routine.

watchFor.title: Repeated resets do not erase overload history
watchFor.body: Clearing codes does not reset the lifetime fault-event counter. U3000:49 accompanying U1000:00 and the circuit-short code indicates the final protection threshold; the circuit must be repaired before module replacement.

watchFor.title: Voltage can invalidate resistance readings
watchFor.body: Follow the isolation and ground-measurement precautions in Diagnostic Methods. Do not force probes into terminals or apply power directly to module-controlled outputs.

notes: Charging-system diagnosis must match the fitted engine.
If BCM replacement is ultimately required, it also requires programmable module installation (PMI); replacement is not complete merely when the connectors are attached.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0256:87 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test Q investigates FCIM communication, including network access, supply-related codes and whether other modules report the same concern.
diagnostics.next: Confirm an observable symptom before following the communication and connector branches.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U1000:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM disabled an output after repetitive overloads reached a protection threshold.
diagnostics.next: Correct companion circuit faults before performing Test R's clear-and-retest sequence.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3006:1C is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Control Module Input Power "A": Circuit Voltage Out of Range identifies an abnormal voltage detected on the BCM supply inputs.
diagnostics.next: Use Test S to distinguish charging, battery, supply, ground and connector causes.

verification.title: Repeat the applicable fault check
verification.body: Confirm operation after connector repairs and complete the branch-specific code recheck. A cleared intermittent code alone does not demonstrate a component repair.

verification.title: Retain measured results
verification.body: Record battery voltage, V_BATT_BCM, their difference and any supply or ground measurements, together with returning codes and the final diagnostic referral.

guides.title: Diagnose BCMB communication faults and compare its reported supply voltage
guides.summary: Separate missing network messages, voltage concerns and protected output faults before deciding whether a module needs further attention.
guides.introduction: Body Control Module B (BCMB) operates ambient lighting, rear lamps and several convertible functions using switch inputs and messages from other modules. It is separate from the Body Control Module (BCM). This investigation checks whether the BCMB is missing information, reporting an unexpected voltage or deliberately shutting down an overloaded output.
guides.why: A communication code identifies missing information, not necessarily a failed sender. Poor connections, charging problems and incomplete configuration can produce similar results. Electronic output protection can also switch off a healthy module’s output to prevent damage.

when.summary: Use when BCMB codes accompany a present concern, or its voltage and output-protection codes require investigation.
notes: Convertible window and luggage-release functions apply only to convertible equipment.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable scan tool for network tests, module self-tests and live data, plus a voltmeter and connector-repair equipment. Begin with battery state of charge above 70%; Test C later requires a healthy, fully charged battery.

prepare.title: Check the starting conditions
prepare.detail: Review previous repairs and service information. Inspect wiring, fuses and connections. Use appropriate flex probes when connecting equipment to terminals; never force probes or apply power or ground directly to module outputs.

steps.title: Route the codes to the affected function
steps.body: Read the [BCMB diagnostic chart](#/document/G1704140). Rear turn-feedback and stop/turn circuit faults lead to exterior-lighting diagnosis; ambient-output faults to interior lighting; global-window faults to glass mechanisms; rear-window-down feedback to convertible-top diagnosis; and run/start circuit faults to steering-column electrical diagnosis. Repair circuit faults before broader system faults.

steps.title: Choose network Test A or B
steps.body: Test A addresses U0140:87: the BCMB is missing BCM messages through the gateway module. Test B addresses U0155:87: it is missing instrument panel cluster (IPC) messages. With ignition on, confirm an observable concern. If none exists, clear the code. Otherwise network-test the BCM for A or IPC for B; a failure requires communication-network diagnosis.

steps.title: Check voltage codes and the sending module
steps.body: After a successful network test, clear codes, wait 10 seconds and read BCMB continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). U3003:62 redirects to Test C. Otherwise self-test the BCM in A or IPC in B and diagnose any recorded codes. If clear, erase codes again, wait 10 seconds and recheck BCMB memory for the original communication code.

steps.title: Determine whether other modules report the loss
steps.body: If the code disappears, operation is normal at this time; intermittent communication or heavy network traffic remains possible. If it persists, clear codes, cycle ignition off then on, wait 10 seconds and retrieve all continuous-memory codes. U0140 in another module selects BCM inspection; U0155 in another selects IPC inspection. Otherwise inspect the BCMB.

steps.title: Inspect and retest the selected module
steps.body: Disconnect its connectors. Replace corroded connectors or terminals and clean module pins; renew damaged, bent or pushed-out contacts as necessary. Reconnect the same module, including the BCM in A7, and ensure every latch seats. Operate the system. If the concern remains, check applicable Ford service articles for BCM/IPC branches or technical service bulletins for BCMB branches. Follow an applicable article; without one, the branch directs replacement of the module just checked. BCM and BCMB replacement requires programmable module installation (PMI).

steps.title: Complete Test C’s preliminary checks
steps.body: Self-test the BCM for charging codes, then with ignition on retrieve codes from all modules; route charging faults to the appropriate diagnosis. If none exist, cycle ignition off/on, clear codes, wait 10 seconds and recheck BCMB U3003:62. A code that disappears may reflect connections, previous charging or jump-starting. If it returns, check battery health and full charge. Investigate discharge causes; replace a battery that fails its condition test.

steps.title: Measure charging voltage and record the comparison
steps.body: Turn off lights and accessories. Run the engine at approximately 2,000 rpm for 3 minutes while monitoring battery voltage. A rise to 15 volts or higher requires overcharging diagnosis. Otherwise cycle ignition off/on, measure and record battery voltage, then read the BCMB voltage parameter identification (PID), VPWR_BCMB. Record whether the readings agree within 0.2 volt. Test C ends here: either result is a measurement finding, not a replacement decision.

steps.title: Follow Test D for a protected output
steps.body: U1000:00 means repeated overloads have triggered output protection. Review the BCMB self-test and correct other codes first using the chart. When no other codes remain, clear codes, wait 10 seconds and repeat the BCMB self-test. Persistent U1000:00 directs BCMB replacement; its absence indicates the circuit short has been repaired and operation is correct at this time.

watchFor.title: A recently installed module
watchFor.body: Incorrect or omitted PMI can create communication faults. Check configuration history before treating the module as defective.

watchFor.title: A connection that temporarily recovers
watchFor.body: Successful operation after reconnection still requires correction of the corrosion, damaged contact or other underlying connection problem.

notes: For unlisted DTCs, repair all other codes first. If none remain, clear and repeat the self-test. If an unlisted code returns, verify the module part number; if correct, install As-Built data from Ford PTS using Module Programming > As-Built.
Use charging-system repair instructions matched to the fitted engine.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0422:68 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCMB received invalid data from the BCM.
diagnostics.next: Retrieve and repair the BCM’s non-network DTCs.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U2100:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: BCMB initial configuration is incomplete.
diagnostics.next: Carry out PMI on the BCMB.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3000:49 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCMB reports an internal electronic failure.
diagnostics.next: Address all other DTCs, clear codes and repeat the self-test. Replace the BCMB only if U3000:49 returns.

verification.title: Confirm the applicable branch result
verification.body: Record whether the original concern remains, which module passed or failed testing, and which codes returned after the specified clearing and waiting sequence.

verification.title: Keep the voltage evidence
verification.body: Record measured battery voltage, VPWR_BCMB and whether their difference meets the 0.2-volt comparison, without declaring a component defective from that result.

guides.title: Deactivate factory mode and complete the transition through transport mode
guides.summary: Use the ignition-type-specific sequence to move the vehicle out of factory mode, then perform transport-mode deactivation.
guides.introduction: During vehicle build, modules including the instrument panel cluster (IPC) and body control module (BCM) can be placed in factory mode. This reduces battery drain during extended periods without use and can alter or disable various functions. Deactivation is a staged process: the ignition sequence changes factory mode to transport mode, and a separate procedure then restores normal operation.
guides.why: The cluster message identifies the current operating mode. Altered electrical functions while a storage mode is active do not, by themselves, establish a defective module. Recognizing the change to transport mode also prevents stopping too early: transport mode still limits functions to conserve battery charge.
searchTerms: electrical functions disabled in factory mode

when.summary: When the message center displays FACTORY MODE CONTACT DEALER.
notes: If TRANSPORT MODE CONTACT DEALER is already displayed, go directly to Transport Mode Deactivation.

prepare.title: Establish battery readiness
prepare.detail: Begin with the ignition off and verify that the battery is fully charged using the Battery guidance in section 414-01.

prepare.title: Identify the ignition arrangement
prepare.detail: Choose the keyed-ignition or push-button branch before starting. For push-button operation, keep one integrated keyhead transmitter (IKT) inside the vehicle as specified by the procedure.

steps.title: Read the displayed mode
steps.body: Confirm the message center shows factory mode. If it already shows transport mode, the factory-to-transport transition has occurred and the separate transport procedure is the appropriate next step.

steps.title: Start from ignition off
steps.body: Place the ignition in the OFF position and verify full battery charge. This is the required starting condition before carrying out the repeated ignition operations.

steps.title: Perform the applicable transition sequence
steps.body: Without push-button start, cycle the ignition from off to on 60 times. With push-button start and the required transmitter inside the vehicle, press the Engine Start/Stop button 120 times. These are alternative branches for different ignition arrangements.

steps.title: Finish with transport-mode deactivation
steps.body: After the factory-mode transition, follow the linked Transport Mode Deactivation procedure. The vehicle automatically moves from factory mode to transport mode after 60 ignition cycles; reaching transport mode is an intermediate result, not normal operation.

watchFor.title: Stopping when the message changes
watchFor.body: A transport-mode message means another deactivation phase remains.

watchFor.title: Mixing cycles and button presses
watchFor.body: Keep the two counts separate: keyed ignition uses off-to-on cycles, while the push-button branch specifies button presses.

notes: Use this process for the displayed factory or transport state; it is not a general reset for unrelated electrical faults.

diagnostics.finding: FACTORY MODE CONTACT DEALER is displayed.
diagnostics.meaning: Factory mode remains active and can alter or disable vehicle functions.
diagnostics.next: Perform the applicable factory-mode transition sequence.

diagnostics.finding: TRANSPORT MODE CONTACT DEALER is displayed.
diagnostics.meaning: The vehicle is in the battery-conserving transport state.
diagnostics.next: Perform Transport Mode Deactivation.

verification.title: Record the state transition
verification.body: Record the starting message and the message reached after the applicable ignition sequence.

verification.title: Confirm the final phase
verification.body: Complete the transport-mode procedure and its confirmation of return to normal operation before treating deactivation as finished.

procedures.purpose: Factory-mode deactivation with separate keyed-ignition and push-button sequences.
Required follow-on deactivation of transport mode to restore normal operation.

guides.title: Deactivate transport mode and confirm normal operation
guides.summary: Use the timed brake-pedal and hazard-switch sequence to leave transport mode, then confirm the message and remote keyless-entry operation.
guides.introduction: Transport mode reduces battery drain while a completed vehicle remains unused for an extended period. Modules including the instrument panel cluster (IPC) and body control module (BCM) use this setting, and some vehicle functions may be altered or disabled. Deactivation changes the operating mode; it does not involve replacing a module. The message shown in the cluster determines whether this particular procedure applies.
guides.why: Transport mode and factory mode require different treatment. Transport mode automatically ends after the vehicle has been driven 80 km (50 mi), while factory mode does not automatically change. For manual transport-mode deactivation, the battery must be fully charged and the two switch-input sequences must be completed within the specified time.

when.summary: When the cluster displays TRANSPORT MODE CONTACT DEALER and manual deactivation is required.
notes: A FACTORY MODE CONTACT DEALER message requires the separate Factory Mode Deactivation procedure.

prepare.title: Review the required safety information
prepare.detail: Read the General Information safety warnings required by the deactivation procedure before starting service.

prepare.title: Prepare for the timed sequence
prepare.detail: Be ready to operate the brake pedal and hazard switch consecutively. Have the remote keyless-entry transmitter available for the final check.

steps.title: Identify the mode
steps.body: Read the cluster message and use [Transport Mode Deactivation](#/document/G1766371) only for transport mode. If the message identifies factory mode, follow the separate factory-mode procedure to select transport or normal operation.

steps.title: Establish the starting conditions
steps.body: Place the ignition OFF and verify that the battery is fully charged. Then place the ignition ON. This is the required starting sequence before entering the timed inputs.

steps.title: Enter the deactivation inputs
steps.body: Press and release the brake pedal five times, then press and release the hazard switch four times, producing two hazard activations. Complete both operations within 10 seconds. Look for NORMAL MODE in the cluster message center as confirmation of successful deactivation.

steps.title: Finish the operating check
steps.body: Start the engine, then place the ignition OFF. Verify that remote keyless entry (RKE) works correctly. The message confirmation and this final functional check are separate parts of completing the procedure.

watchFor.title: Confusing presses with hazard activations
watchFor.body: The requirement is four press-and-release operations, corresponding to two hazard activations.

watchFor.title: Treating altered functions as a failed module
watchFor.body: Transport mode can intentionally change or disable functions. Establish the operating mode before drawing a component-failure conclusion.

notes: The BCM controls transport-mode functionality and remote keyless entry, which makes the final transmitter check relevant to this operation.

diagnostics.finding: TRANSPORT MODE CONTACT DEALER is displayed.
diagnostics.meaning: The vehicle is in the battery-conserving transport setting.
diagnostics.next: Perform the manual deactivation sequence if normal operation is required now.

diagnostics.finding: FACTORY MODE CONTACT DEALER is displayed.
diagnostics.meaning: The vehicle is in a different mode that will not automatically revert.
diagnostics.next: Use Factory Mode Deactivation rather than assuming the transport sequence applies.

diagnostics.finding: NORMAL MODE does not appear after the inputs.
diagnostics.meaning: Successful deactivation has not been confirmed.
diagnostics.next: Check the starting mode, battery charge and timed input sequence against the procedure.

verification.title: Record the mode confirmation
verification.body: Record whether the cluster displayed NORMAL MODE after the timed sequence.

verification.title: Confirm remote operation
verification.body: After starting the engine and switching the ignition OFF, verify and record correct remote keyless-entry operation.

procedures.purpose: Manual transport-mode deactivation, factory-mode distinction, timed inputs and final remote keyless-entry check.

guides.title: Replace and configure the body control module
guides.summary: Remove the body control module and complete the key programming, configuration and equipment-dependent initialization required for a replacement.
guides.introduction: The body control module (BCM) receives switch, sensor and network information and controls functions including lighting, locks, wipers, battery-saving features and vehicle security. Replacing it changes both an electrical component and the vehicle’s stored configuration. The physical exchange is only one part of the repair; a new module also needs security setup and the applicable learning procedures.
guides.why: A disabled output does not automatically mean the BCM has failed. Its field-effect transistor (FET) protection can switch off an overloaded circuit to protect the module. Resolve the underlying circuit fault before deciding on replacement. Once replacement is justified, the programming sequence matters because normal ignition operation depends on programmed keys and a completed security parameter reset.

when.summary: When diagnosis confirms BCM replacement is required, or the module must be removed and refitted.
notes: The extended programming sequence applies to a new BCM.
Parking aid, video rear parking aid and electronic steering-column lock steps apply only when fitted.

prepare.title: Programming capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of programmable module installation (PMI), security parameter reset and the listed configuration functions. Have two keys available.

prepare.title: Diagnostic access and trim tools
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover. Preserve the scan-tool session; if needed, a session can be started using the powertrain control module (PCM) part number or tear tag number on the PCM.

steps.title: Begin the module transfer
steps.body: Start BCM PMI as directed in the [replacement procedure](#/document/G1694185). If the old BCM does not communicate, replacement may require As-Built configuration data. When replacing the BCM, also begin PMI for the integral parking aid module (PAM), if equipped.

steps.title: Remove the trim and module
steps.body: Release the right-hand scuff plate clips with the trim remover, then remove the lower right-hand cowl trim. Release the harness retainer and move the harness aside. Remove the retaining nut and BCM, and disconnect its electrical connectors.

steps.title: Install and maintain diagnostic communication
steps.body: Reverse removal, tightening the retaining nut to 71 lb.in (8 Nm). For a new BCM, continue the remaining steps: normal ignition operation is unavailable until two keys are programmed and the parameter reset is complete. The BCM still communicates with the scan tool with ignition off.

steps.title: Program the keys using the button sequence
steps.body: Do not use the scan tool for this particular key-programming step. Put the first key in the [backup starting location](#/document/G1694657), press START/STOP and wait approximately 6 seconds. Press START/STOP again and remove that key. Place the second key in the backup location and press START/STOP.

steps.title: Prepare and complete BCM programming
steps.body: Before running the BCM PMI installation, use the center display to ensure valet mode is off. A new BCM may arrive in factory mode; perform [factory mode deactivation](#/document/G1766370) if necessary. Complete BCM PMI following the scan-tool instructions.

steps.title: Complete security and system initialization
steps.body: Perform the [security parameter reset](#/document/G1672905), followed by Configuration Engine Immobilizer (CEI) configuration and the battery monitor sensor reset. If video rear parking aid is fitted, carry out its new-module initialization using the scan tool.

steps.title: Restore fitted equipment and preferences
steps.body: If fitted, perform BCM-to-electronic steering column lock (ESCL) configuration/training through the [security programming procedure](#/document/G1672905). Configure the [customer preference parameters](#/document/G1813073), then [train the tire-pressure sensors](#/document/G1686523).

steps.title: Test the BCM and finish parking-aid programming
steps.body: Carry out the BCM self-test, including an on-demand self-test, and repeat the self-test to confirm all diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) have cleared. If PAM is fitted, complete its PMI process afterward.

watchFor.title: Valet mode interrupts programming
watchFor.body: Leaving valet mode active before BCM PMI installation can cause the process to fail.

watchFor.title: Replacement without circuit repair
watchFor.body: An unresolved excessive-current fault can expose the replacement module to the same damaging condition.

notes: The BCM-B is a separate body module; this procedure concerns the BCM.
Clearing FET-related codes does not reset the accumulated fault-event counter.

diagnostics.finding: A protected output shuts down with a short-circuit DTC, possibly accompanied by U1000:00.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM may be protecting an overloaded circuit rather than suffering an internal failure.
diagnostics.next: Correct the circuit fault. Where protection requires a service reset, run the on-demand self-test and clear codes once the test confirms the fault is corrected.

diagnostics.finding: U1000:00 and U3000:49 occur with the associated short-circuit DTC under the FET protection strategy.
diagnostics.meaning: The final fault-tolerance level has been reached; U3000:49 cannot be cleared.
diagnostics.next: Repair the circuit fault, then replace and configure the affected module.

verification.title: Configuration completed
verification.body: Confirm both keys, the parameter reset and every applicable initialization, preference and sensor-training operation are complete.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record the initial and repeated BCM self-test results, including the on-demand test, and confirmation that all DTCs cleared. Record PAM PMI completion when applicable.

procedures.purpose: BCM removal, installation and complete replacement configuration sequence.
Explain BCM operation and distinguish recoverable FET output protection from a replacement-required fault state.
Locate the passive key backup starting position for the prescribed key-programming sequence.
Deactivate factory mode if present in the replacement BCM.
Perform the security parameter reset and conditional BCM-to-ESCL configuration/training.
Restore customer preference programmable parameters.
Train tire-pressure sensor locations after BCM replacement.

guides.title: Replace and configure Body Control Module B
guides.summary: Preserve the existing module configuration, replace Body Control Module B and complete programming and repeated self-tests.
guides.introduction: Body Control Module B (BCM-B) controls ambient lighting, reverse lamps and rear stop/turn lamps. On convertibles it also controls the top and the specified window and luggage-lid release inhibit functions. It responds to switch, sensor and network information, so replacement requires both physical installation and restoration of its configuration.
guides.why: Configuration must be captured before the old module is removed. An inactive output can also be deliberate short-circuit protection rather than immediate evidence of module failure. Repairing the affected circuit and interpreting the protection state prevents an unresolved electrical fault from following the replacement module.

when.summary: When diagnosis establishes that BCM-B replacement is required and any associated circuit fault has been repaired.
notes: A lamp or convertible-function complaint alone does not prove BCM-B failure.

prepare.title: Programming capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of the BCM-B programmable module installation (PMI) process, configuration transfer and on-demand self-testing.

prepare.title: Luggage-compartment access
prepare.detail: Prepare to remove the weatherstrip, spare-tire cover and fitted subwoofer/amplifier, then move the right-hand side trim aside. Have a torque tool suitable for the module's mounting nuts.

steps.title: Begin configuration transfer before removal
steps.body: With the original module still installed, begin BCM-B PMI using the diagnostic scan tool and follow its prompts. When installing a new module, upload the existing configuration before removing the old one so it can be downloaded into the replacement.

steps.title: Expose the module
steps.body: Remove the luggage-compartment weatherstrip and spare-tire cover. If fitted, remove the [subwoofer and amplifier unit](#/document/G1704011). Remove the pin-type retainers and position the right-hand luggage-compartment side trim aside.

steps.title: Remove BCM-B
steps.body: Follow the [module removal procedure](#/document/G1703548): remove the mounting nuts, release the module and disconnect its electrical connectors. Keep the module supported while handling the connections.

steps.title: Install and restore the luggage compartment
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure, reconnecting the electrical connectors and securing the module. Tighten the mounting nuts to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm). Restore the side trim, retainers, fitted audio equipment, spare-tire cover and weatherstrip.

steps.title: Complete programmable module installation
steps.body: Resume and complete BCM-B PMI through the scan-tool prompts. Download the saved configuration into the new module as required by the process.

steps.title: Run and repeat the self-test
steps.body: Carry out the BCM-B self-test, including an on-demand self-test. Repeat the self-test to confirm that all BCM-B diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) have cleared. Investigate any remaining fault before closing the repair.

watchFor.title: Configuration not captured
watchFor.body: Do not remove the original module before completing the required configuration upload for a new-module installation.

watchFor.title: Unrepaired output short circuit
watchFor.body: Repeated fault events accumulate in the module's protection history. Clearing DTCs does not reset that lifetime counter.

notes: The convertible-specific functions apply only to vehicles fitted with a convertible top.

diagnostics.finding: An output has shut down with a short-circuit DTC.
diagnostics.meaning: Field-effect transistor (FET) protection can switch an output off when excessive current is detected.
diagnostics.next: Correct the circuit fault and assess the protection state before deciding that the module requires replacement.

diagnostics.finding: U1000:00 accompanies the affected short-circuit DTC at a recoverable protection level.
diagnostics.meaning: A protection threshold has been reached, but the described strategy permits recovery after repair.
diagnostics.next: Run the on-demand self-test; if it confirms the fault is corrected, use the scan tool's Clear DTC operation.

diagnostics.finding: U1000:00 and U3000:49 accompany the short-circuit DTC at the final protection level.
diagnostics.meaning: The described FET strategy has reached its final tolerance level; U3000:49 cannot be cleared.
diagnostics.next: Repair the circuit fault, then replace and configure the module.

verification.title: Programming and fault clearance
verification.body: Confirm PMI has completed and the repeated self-test establishes that all BCM-B DTCs are cleared.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record PMI completion and the results of the on-demand and repeated self-tests, including any DTCs that remain.

procedures.purpose: BCM-B removal and installation, configuration transfer, PMI completion and required repeated self-tests.
Removal and installation of the fitted subwoofer/amplifier for access; SYNC 2/SYNC 3 reference.
Explanation of BCM-B operation and the shared FET short-circuit protection and recovery strategy.

guides.title: Replace and configure the driver door module
guides.summary: Remove the driver door module behind the door trim and complete its configuration transfer using a diagnostic scan tool.
guides.introduction: The Driver Door Module (DDM) is a vehicle-configured electronic unit mounted behind the driver's front door trim. Its connectors join it to the vehicle wiring, while bolts secure it to the door. Replacement involves both exchanging this physical unit and completing its programming. The small number of fasteners can make the job look simple, but the configuration work is an essential part of the repair.
guides.why: A new module needs the configuration information held by the old one. Uploading that information before disconnection preserves the intended transfer path. Following the separate door-trim procedure also provides the correct access route without treating the surrounding panel as an obstacle to force aside.

when.summary: When diagnosis establishes that the driver door module needs replacement, or it must be removed for associated work.
notes: Identify the module responsible for the complaint before choosing a replacement.

prepare.title: Have the programming equipment ready
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of Programmable Module Installation (PMI). When installing a new module, its configuration must be uploaded from the old module before removal.

prepare.title: Plan door-trim access and fastening
prepare.detail: Have the front-door-trim procedure available, together with suitable tools for the module bolts and controlled tightening to the specified torque.

steps.title: Begin PMI before disconnecting the DDM
steps.body: Connect the diagnostic scan tool and begin the DDM PMI process, following its on-screen instructions. For replacement, ensure the existing configuration has been uploaded before moving on to physical removal.

steps.title: Remove the driver's front door trim
steps.body: Follow [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600) to expose the module. Keep this access phase separate from module removal so the door panel's own fastening and connection requirements are followed.

steps.title: Release the module and its connectors
steps.body: Remove the DDM mounting bolts and disconnect the electrical connectors, then take the module away. The illustration identifies the mounting points and connector-release locations; use those features to distinguish the module attachments from the surrounding door structure.

steps.title: Install the module and restore the trim
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, reconnecting the electrical connectors and securing the module. Tighten the DDM bolts to 44 lb.in (5 Nm), then restore the front door trim using its installation procedure.

steps.title: Complete the DDM programming process
steps.body: Use the diagnostic scan tool to finish PMI as directed on screen. When fitting a new DDM, this includes downloading the configuration captured before removal. Treat this as part of installation rather than optional follow-up work.

watchFor.title: Premature disconnection
watchFor.body: The configuration upload belongs before removal of a module being replaced. Do not leave that step until the old DDM is already disconnected.

watchFor.title: An incomplete installation
watchFor.body: A securely bolted module is only the mechanical portion of the job. The specified installation sequence also requires completion of PMI.

notes: The DDM replacement procedure does not provide a symptom-based test for condemning the module.

diagnostics.finding: The reported problem involves power door locking or remote keyless entry.
diagnostics.meaning: The Body Control Module (BCM) also controls these functions, so a door-related complaint does not identify the DDM by itself.
diagnostics.next: Follow the relevant function's diagnosis before deciding which module, connection or circuit needs repair.

verification.title: Check mechanical completion
verification.body: Confirm that the DDM connectors are attached, the mounting bolts are tightened as specified and the door trim has been fully restored.

verification.title: Record the programming result
verification.body: Confirm and record completion of the scan-tool PMI process, including configuration transfer when a new DDM was installed.

procedures.purpose: Provides DDM removal, installation, bolt torque and the beginning and completion of PMI.
Provides front-door-trim removal and installation for access to the driver door module.

guides.title: Replace and configure the passenger door module
guides.summary: Preserve the passenger door module’s configuration, replace the unit behind the door trim and complete scan-tool programming.
guides.introduction: The passenger door module (PDM) is an electronic control unit mounted behind the passenger front door trim panel. Its replacement has both a physical phase and a configuration phase. Programmable module installation (PMI) begins while the original module is still installed and finishes after the replacement has been connected.
guides.why: When fitting a new PDM, the existing configuration must first be uploaded to the diagnostic scan tool and then downloaded into the replacement. Removing the original module too soon interrupts that required transfer path. Secure mounting and connected plugs alone do not complete the replacement process.

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the passenger door module needs replacement, or removal is required for another repair.
notes: Arrange scan-tool access before removing the module.

prepare.title: Prepare the configuration transfer
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of performing the PDM PMI process. Be ready to follow its on-screen instructions and retain the uploaded configuration for the new module.

prepare.title: Prepare access and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have the equipment required for front door trim-panel removal and a torque tool suitable for the PDM mounting bolts. Review the trim-panel procedure before opening the door assembly.

steps.title: Begin PMI with the original module installed
steps.body: Start the PDM PMI process using the diagnostic scan tool and follow its prompts. If installing a new module, upload the original module’s configuration before removal. Complete this stage before disconnecting the PDM.

steps.title: Remove the front door trim panel
steps.body: Follow the [Front Door Trim Panel procedure](#/document/G1692600). Removing the trim exposes the module’s mounting bolts and electrical connections.

steps.title: Remove the PDM
steps.body: Remove the mounting bolts and module, then disconnect its electrical connectors. Support the unit while separating the connections so its weight is not carried by the wiring.

steps.title: Install the module and restore the trim
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: reconnect the electrical connectors, position the module and install its bolts. Tighten the PDM mounting bolts to 44 lb.in (5 Nm). Reinstall the door trim according to its own procedure.

steps.title: Complete PMI
steps.body: Use the diagnostic scan tool to finish the PDM PMI process, following the on-screen instructions. When a new module is installed, download the configuration captured from the original module into the replacement.

watchFor.title: Disconnecting before configuration capture
watchFor.body: For a new-module installation, keep the original PDM installed until its configuration has been uploaded as required.

watchFor.title: Stopping after physical installation
watchFor.body: The scan-tool completion stage remains necessary after the module and trim have been refitted.

notes: The stated torque applies to the PDM mounting bolts. Door trim fasteners follow the trim-panel procedure.

verification.title: Confirm physical installation
verification.body: Check that the electrical connectors are attached, the module is secured at the specified torque and the door trim has been restored.

verification.title: Record programming completion
verification.body: Record completion of the scan-tool PMI process and, for a new PDM, confirmation that the saved configuration was downloaded into it.

procedures.purpose: Begin PMI, remove and install the passenger door module, and complete configuration transfer.
Remove and reinstall the front door trim panel for PDM access.

guides.title: Replace and configure the radio transceiver module
guides.summary: Remove the radio transceiver module through the body-style-specific trim access and complete its scan-tool configuration.
guides.introduction: The radio transceiver module (RTM) handles radio communication within the vehicle’s electronic systems. It is retained by tabs and connected to the vehicle wiring. Replacing it involves two connected tasks: exchanging the physical module and completing Programmable Module Installation (PMI), the scan-tool process used to prepare and configure the replacement. Coupe and convertible models require different interior trim access, but both follow the same module removal and installation sequence.
guides.why: A replacement module needs the vehicle’s configuration information, so the electronic preparation comes before unplugging the original unit. Removing the module first can interrupt that required transfer. The retaining tabs also need to be released deliberately: pulling on the module while they remain engaged does not follow the intended removal method.

when.summary: When RTM removal or replacement has been justified and its configuration can be handled with a diagnostic scan tool.
notes: This replacement procedure does not establish whether an electronic-system complaint is caused by the RTM.
When installing a new module, upload the original configuration before removing the existing module.

prepare.title: Arrange scan-tool capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of carrying out RTM PMI, including transferring configuration information to a new module.

prepare.title: Identify the access route
prepare.detail: Plan parcel-shelf removal for a coupe or loadspace-trim-panel removal for a convertible. Use the corresponding trim procedure for its fasteners and release method.

steps.title: Begin the electronic preparation
steps.body: With the original RTM still installed, begin PMI and follow the scan-tool prompts. If fitting a new module, upload its configuration information before physical removal. Follow the complete [RTM procedure](#/document/G1694188) through both the preparation and completion phases.

steps.title: Expose the module
steps.body: On a coupe, remove the [parcel shelf](#/document/G1692602). On a convertible, remove the [loadspace trim panel](#/document/G1692610). These are alternative access routes selected by body style.

steps.title: Release and disconnect the RTM
steps.body: Release the retaining tabs and remove the module from its mounting position, then disconnect its electrical connectors. The illustration identifies the tab-retained module and connector area; keep the wiring free while withdrawing the unit.

steps.title: Refit and complete configuration
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence to reconnect and secure the module and restore the appropriate trim. Complete RTM PMI using the scan-tool instructions. For a new module, this includes downloading the configuration information saved before removal.

watchFor.title: Configuration not saved
watchFor.body: If the required upload has not succeeded, resolve that stage before removing a module that is being replaced.

watchFor.title: Incomplete retention
watchFor.body: Check that the module’s tabs have engaged during refitting; trim installation should not be used to hold a loose module in place.

notes: Physical installation and PMI completion are separate parts of the same job.

verification.title: Check the mechanical installation
verification.body: Confirm the electrical connectors are reconnected, the RTM is retained by its tabs and the removed trim is restored.

verification.title: Confirm PMI completion
verification.body: Finish the scan-tool sequence, including the configuration download when a new module has been fitted.

procedures.purpose: RTM removal, installation and scan-tool PMI for coupe and convertible models.
Coupe parcel-shelf removal and installation for RTM access.
Convertible loadspace-trim-panel removal and installation for RTM access.

guides.title: Find body water leaks, wind noise and trim rattles
guides.summary: Locate the entry path or moving component behind body leaks and noises, then select the appropriate sealing, alignment or retention repair.
guides.introduction: Weatherstrips, glass seals, seam sealer and body plugs keep water and unwanted airflow outside. Insulation reduces transmitted road noise, while secure trim and wiring prevent rattles. This diagnosis separates a sealing fault from poor alignment, missing insulation or movement between parts so the repair addresses the actual cause.
guides.why: Water can travel from an opening above the wet area, and airflow can whistle across an exposed edge without entering the cabin. Finding the path matters more than adding material where the symptom is easiest to notice.

when.summary: When water, dust, drafts, wind noise, squeaks or rattles can be reproduced around the body or interior trim.

prepare.title: Leak and noise investigation
prepare.detail: Have soapy water, tape, a water hose, bright light and rubber mallet available. Arrange access behind affected trim or carpet. Alignment and fixed-glass replacement require the capability described in their separate procedures.

steps.title: Reproduce the complaint
steps.body: Review previous repairs and identify the conditions that produce the symptom. For wind noise, drive in four different directions at highway speed or the reported speed, with windows closed, radio off and air-conditioning blower off. This helps distinguish airflow-dependent noise from a persistent rattle.

steps.title: Find openings with cabin pressure
steps.body: Locate and tape off the body vents. Set the blower to HI with recirculation off, and close the doors and windows. Open the hood and spray soapy water along seams and grommets, particularly the A-pillar/fender and hood-hinge areas. Bubbles identify escaping air paths.

steps.title: Trace water and dust paths
steps.body: Inspect near and above the affected area, removing trim or carpet as needed. Use a water-hose or road test to reproduce ingress. A bright light beneath the vehicle can reveal openings at body joints and weld lines when viewed from inside.

steps.title: Check door and glass fit
steps.body: Inspect door gaps, seal retention, scuff plates and damaged pushpins. Correct misalignment or reseat seals before replacing them. Check glass runs for poor seating, puckered corners, spread channels and lips that fail to contact the sheet metal. Use the symptom chart's specific foam, channel or replacement correction for the identified path.

steps.title: Inspect exterior airflow paths
steps.body: Check mirror housings, gaskets, caps and access holes; edges must overlap correctly with airflow. Inspect splash shields, exposed panel edges, hood/grille fit and cowl-screen contact with the windshield. Reseat an incorrectly installed air extractor or replace damaged housing/flaps. Use grille foam or edge correction only at the locations identified in the chart.

steps.title: Isolate movement and missing insulation
steps.body: Restrain a suspected part by hand or use damping or low-friction material to identify a squeak or rattle. Carefully tap the underside of a door with a rubber mallet while listening. Secure loose objects, wiring and retainers; fasten buzzing instrument-panel parts and add foam or felt where needed. Check missing body and mastic insulation for road-noise complaints.

steps.title: Repair the confirmed source
steps.body: Use seam sealer for identified sheet-metal joint leaks and the applicable alignment or glass procedure for fit defects. For aftermarket air deflectors or stone shields, remove them if possible and repeat the road test to establish their contribution. Check original-equipment accessories for correct installation before repair or replacement.

watchFor.title: Do not bend the belt-line flange
watchFor.body: Correct an incorrectly installed inner belt seal by adjusting the seal. Poor glass contact may require glass adjustment; gaps at its ends may require seal adjustment or foam.

watchFor.title: Check the barrier behind the door trim
watchFor.body: Drafts at a handle or speaker can come through a torn or displaced weathershield, an exterior-handle seal or a missing speaker seal. Tape a weathershield hole; replace the shield if its pressure-sensitive adhesive fails.

notes: Silicone spray can reduce weatherstrip friction and squeaks, but must not be used before painting.
For the luggage compartment, follow the luggage-lid branch of the body chart.

diagnostics.finding: Water or wind enters around fixed glass.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible paths include molding, sealant gaps, incorrect glass fit, the rear hood seal or high-mounted stoplamp seal.
diagnostics.next: Inspect those seals and A-pillar applique clips. Use the specified A-pillar foam correction where applicable; sealant gaps or incorrectly installed glass direct replacement through the fixed-glass procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The luggage-compartment perimeter leaks.
diagnostics.meaning: Loose or displaced seals, damaged retainers, scuff-plate position or lid alignment can interrupt sealing.
diagnostics.next: Correct the identified fit issue, replace damaged parts and use the luggage-lid alignment procedure when required.

diagnostics.finding: Water collects inside a door.
diagnostics.meaning: Mud or road tar may be blocking its drain holes.
diagnostics.next: Clear the holes with a punch or screwdriver and check them regularly.

diagnostics.finding: The exterior mirror whistles or vibrates.
diagnostics.meaning: Air gaps, incorrect gasket/cap fit or loose mounting nuts can cause distinct complaints.
diagnostics.next: Correct fit and air paths or tighten mounting nuts as applicable. A trim cap sitting under-flush and causing whistle directs exterior-mirror replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Air or water enters through the floor.
diagnostics.meaning: A plug or grommet may be missing, damaged or incorrectly seated.
diagnostics.next: Check installation and replace damaged or missing plugs and grommets.

verification.title: Repeat the revealing test
verification.body: Repeat the pressure, hose or road test that exposed the fault. For accessory-related noise, compare the result with the accessory removed where possible.

verification.title: Record the confirmed cause
verification.body: Record the entry path or moving component, the correction and whether the original symptom returned under the same test conditions.

procedures.purpose: Complete body leak, wind-noise and rattle symptom chart with location-specific corrections.
Correct front-door alignment when door fit interrupts sealing.
Remove and reinstall or replace the front-door glass run and bracket.
Carry out fixed-glass replacement for sealant gaps or incorrect installation.
Correct luggage-compartment lid fit.
Correct hood alignment where its margins contribute to wind noise.

guides.title: Diagnose active grille shutter movement, power and communication faults
guides.summary: Use trouble codes, isolated circuit measurements and commanded movement to distinguish shutter binding from supply, communication and actuator faults.
guides.introduction: Active grille shutters control airflow through linked blinds, reducing aerodynamic drag and helping the engine warm up. Their smart actuator receives position commands from the powertrain control module (PCM) over a local interconnect network (LIN). This diagnostic path separates an obstructed assembly from an actuator that lacks power, ground or communication.
guides.why: A stationary shutter does not establish actuator failure. The system calibrates after engine starting, may remain partly open with the engine off, and can move fully open following a communication failure. Codes and controlled tests provide the necessary context.
searchTerms: grille shutter will not fully open

when.summary: Use when fitted grille shutters operate incorrectly or the PCM records a grille-shutter fault.
notes: The system may record a fault without giving the driver an indication.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of PCM self-tests and active commands, a digital multimeter, terminal-safe Rotunda Flex Probes and Wiring Diagrams Cell 33. Obtain applicable Ford technical service bulletins (TSBs) through OASIS.

prepare.title: Establish test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation and verify battery state of charge above 70%. Inspect prior repairs and harness damage. Follow the specified ignition states and isolate conductors for resistance checks.

steps.title: A1: inspect and classify the complaint
steps.body: Check battery junction box (BJB) fuse 42 (15A), grille-opening obstructions and the actuator connector. With ignition on, perform the PCM self-test. P05A7, U0046 or U0284 directs supply checks at A2. Without those codes, P059F or P05A1 directs commanded movement at A7. Use the code-specific decisions below for other findings.

steps.title: A2–A3: prove supply and ground
steps.body: Switch ignition off and disconnect actuator C1651. With ignition on, pin 3 to ground must exceed 11 volts. If it fails, verify the fuse: repair the supply circuit if the fuse is sound, or trace the short if it has failed. Switch ignition off; pin 1 to ground must measure less than 3 ohms. Repair a failed ground. Passing checks send P05A7 to A9 and communication codes to A4.

steps.title: A4–A6: isolate the communication conductor
steps.body: With ignition off and C1651 still disconnected, disconnect PCM C1551B. C1651 pin 2 to C1551B pin 50 must measure less than 3 ohms. With ignition on, C1651 pin 2 to ground must show no voltage; with ignition off, resistance to ground must exceed 10,000 ohms. Repair any failed circuit check. Passing U0046 checks continue to A9. For U0284, record passing measurements and stop pending a confirmed next route.

steps.title: A7: observe commanded travel
steps.body: Start the engine and idle for at least 30 seconds to allow calibration. Select PCM parameter identification (PID) GRILL_A_CMD and command 100% open to 0% closed while observing from the front. Full travel means the system operates correctly now; inspect the connector and consider a previous obstruction. Incomplete travel leads to A8.

steps.title: A8: separate mechanical binding from actuator trouble
steps.body: Switch ignition off and remove the actuator using its procedure. Move the shutters manually and remove obstructions. The linked blinds should move freely without binding. Repair binding or replace the shutter assembly if necessary; individual blinds are not separately serviceable. Free movement leads to A9.

steps.title: A9: check connections before replacing the actuator
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect C1651 and the jumper harness. Correct corrosion with new connectors or terminals and clean module pins; replace damaged, bent or pushed-out pins as necessary. Reconnect and latch every disconnected connector, then retest. If the fault remains, follow any applicable TSB; otherwise install a new actuator. If operation returns, address the connection fault's root cause.

steps.title: Use A10 only after its routing is confirmed
steps.body: A confirmed applicable route to A10 requires inspection and repair of both actuator and PCM connectors, reconnection and retesting. Persistent trouble requires a bulletin check, then actuator replacement if no bulletin applies. Clear codes and repeat the self-test; only continued failure on that confirmed route leads to PCM replacement through the applicable engine procedure. Passing U0284 circuit checks alone do not authorize this endpoint.

watchFor.title: Normal calibration can look irregular
watchFor.body: The opening-and-closing sequence may start in either direction and pause between movements. Allow the specified settling time before judging travel.

watchFor.title: An absent complaint changes the decision
watchFor.body: Do not replace components through a fault-present diagnostic endpoint when the concern is no longer present.

notes: Other PCM trouble codes require their applicable engine diagnostic procedures.
Actuator or assembly replacement is a separate removal-and-installation phase; these measurements do not complete that work.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P059F or P05A1 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P059F reports inability to move the shutters; P05A1 reports failure to reach a fully open or closed stop.
diagnostics.next: Follow A7–A8, after resolving any supply or communication codes that take priority.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P05A7 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The actuator reports low supply voltage.
diagnostics.next: Follow A2–A3; passing supply and ground checks lead to A9.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0046 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detects a LIN open or short to voltage or ground.
diagnostics.next: Check supply, ground and the isolated LIN conductor before A9.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0284 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM has not received expected actuator communication.
diagnostics.next: Complete A2–A6. If these pass, preserve the result and obtain confirmed further routing.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P05A2 or P05C0 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P05A2 denotes a control-circuit/open fault; P05C0 denotes shutter-module overtemperature.
diagnostics.next: The code chart directs installation of a new grille shutter actuator using its replacement procedure.

verification.title: Confirm operation at the reached endpoint
verification.body: Reconnect all system connectors and repeat the affected operation. For the movement branch, confirm complete commanded opening and closing after calibration.

verification.title: Record evidence and remaining decisions
verification.body: Save codes, supply voltage, ground and LIN measurements, commanded travel and retest results. Identify any U0284 branch awaiting confirmed routing.
