guides.title: Replace the active grille shutter actuator
guides.summary: Remove the shutter assembly, replace its actuator and verify the automatic startup calibration.
guides.introduction: Active grille shutters regulate airflow through the front of the vehicle to reduce aerodynamic drag and help the engine warm up. Their actuator is a smart motor controlled by the powertrain control module (PCM). It moves one shutter blind, which moves the others through linked connections.
guides.why: Actuator replacement requires removing the complete shutter assembly first. Correctly restoring the linkage matters because the motor depends on the shutters reaching their open and closed end positions during calibration. A blocked shutter or communication fault can resemble an actuator problem.

when.summary: When diagnosis calls for actuator replacement on a vehicle equipped with active grille shutters.
notes: The actuator is separately serviceable; individual shutter blinds are not.

prepare.title: Arrange front-end access
prepare.detail: Be prepared to follow the front bumper cover procedure and remove the complete shutter assembly before working on the actuator.

prepare.title: Gather release and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have a screwdriver for the actuator clip, suitable fastener tools and a torque wrench for assembly refitting.

steps.title: Expose and move the shutter assembly forward
steps.body: Follow the [shutter assembly procedure](#/document/G1693244), including its front bumper cover reference. Detach the ambient air temperature sensor, remove the assembly retainers and bolts, and position the shutters forward to reach the remaining connections.

steps.title: Remove the complete assembly
steps.body: Disconnect the actuator electrical connector. Remove the retainers and bridge link, then remove the shutter assembly. The radiator and condenser are omitted from the access illustration for clarity; that illustration does not require their removal.

steps.title: Release and replace the actuator
steps.body: Use the [actuator procedure](#/document/G1693245). Remove the upper linkage and retainer, then use a screwdriver to push up the retaining clip and remove the motor. Install the replacement by reversing these actions, restoring the clip, retainer and upper linkage.

steps.title: Refit the assembly and observe calibration
steps.body: Reverse the assembly removal, reconnecting the actuator and ambient temperature sensor. Use the assembly procedure's separate tightening values for the main mountings and bridge link. After reassembly, start the engine and observe the automatic calibration through both shutter end positions.

watchFor.title: A pause during calibration
watchFor.body: Calibration can start in either direction, and a long pause between movements can be normal. Do not judge failure from the pause alone.

watchFor.title: Damaged shutter blinds
watchFor.body: A damaged individual blind requires consideration of the shutter assembly; replacing the motor does not repair the blind.

notes: The system may store a diagnostic trouble code (DTC) without giving the driver a warning.

diagnostics.finding: Shutters remain partly or fully open with the engine off
diagnostics.meaning: This can be normal, depending on ambient temperature.
diagnostics.next: Assess startup calibration before condemning the actuator.

diagnostics.finding: Calibration repeatedly retries or does not complete
diagnostics.meaning: A blockage or actuator error may be present. Local interconnect network (LIN) communication failure can also command a fully open position.
diagnostics.next: Investigate mechanical obstruction and reported faults before deciding another actuator is needed.

verification.title: Check the linked movement
verification.body: Confirm the startup sequence reaches the open and closed end positions, then allows the shutters to assume the commanded position.

verification.title: Record the outcome
verification.body: Record whether calibration completed and any remaining PCM grille-shutter fault information.

procedures.purpose: Actuator removal and installation after removing the shutter assembly.
Complete shutter assembly removal, access connections and refitting.
Interpret startup calibration, shutter movement and fault responses.

guides.title: Remove and replace the active grille shutter assembly
guides.summary: Remove the front bumper cover, disconnect the shutter assembly and refit it with its sensor, wiring and bridge link restored.
guides.introduction: The active grille shutter uses linked movable blinds to control airflow through the front of the vehicle. The powertrain control module (PCM) commands their position to reduce aerodynamic drag and help the engine warm up. This job removes the complete shutter assembly. Individual blinds are not serviceable, although the actuator can be serviced separately.
guides.why: The assembly carries both mechanical attachments and electrical connections, so it must be moved forward in stages. Detaching the ambient air temperature sensor and disconnecting the actuator at the specified points prevents the assembly from being pulled away with those connections still attached.

when.summary: When a shutter assembly requires replacement or removal for access after the repair scope has been established.
notes: An open shutter with the engine stopped does not, by itself, establish a fault.
Decide whether the work concerns the complete assembly or the separately serviceable actuator.

prepare.title: Plan bumper access
prepare.detail: Arrange a hoist and the capability to remove the front wheels and bumper cover using the lifting and wheel procedures referenced in the bumper instructions.

prepare.title: Prepare for the fasteners
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the retainers and bolts, with torque control for the different shutter-mounting and bridge-link settings.

steps.title: Remove the front bumper cover
steps.body: Follow the linked bumper procedure through wheel, lower air deflector and liner access, electrical disconnection and cover removal. Lift the cover off its alignment pins before drawing it forward. Inspect the fender bracket teeth as directed so damaged attachments are addressed before refitting.

steps.title: Free the sensor and move the shutter forward
steps.body: Detach the ambient air temperature sensor. Remove the shutter retainers and bolts, then position the assembly forward. This creates access for the remaining connections; the assembly is not yet ready to lift away.

steps.title: Disconnect the actuator and bridge link
steps.body: Disconnect the active grille shutter actuator electrical connector. Then remove the retainers and bridge link in the order shown in the shutter procedure.

steps.title: Remove the assembly
steps.body: Withdraw the shutter assembly using the illustrated removal direction. Treat the frame and linked blinds as an assembly rather than attempting to replace an individual blind.

steps.title: Refit in reverse order
steps.body: Install the shutter, restore the bridge link and actuator connection, and secure the assembly using the specified settings for each fastening point. Reattach the ambient temperature sensor and reinstall the bumper cover through its complete installation sequence.

watchFor.title: Illustration clearance
watchFor.body: The radiator and condenser are omitted from an illustration for clarity. Their removal is not part of this shutter procedure.

watchFor.title: No driver warning
watchFor.body: A shutter fault can be stored in the PCM without an indication to the driver.

notes: Startup calibration can begin in either direction and can pause between opening and closing.

diagnostics.finding: Shutters remain partly or fully open with the engine off
diagnostics.meaning: This can be normal and depends on ambient conditions.
diagnostics.next: Consider operating conditions before treating their resting position as evidence of failure.

diagnostics.finding: Repeated calibration attempts or a persistent fully open position
diagnostics.meaning: Blockage, actuator errors or local interconnect network (LIN) communication faults can affect operation.
diagnostics.next: Establish the fault before choosing an actuator or complete assembly; position alone does not identify the failed part.

verification.title: Check startup operation
verification.body: Observe the automatic calibration after engine start: the system seeks both end positions before moving to its commanded position.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the observed travel and any repeated calibration attempts. Confirm the sensor, connector, bridge link and bumper attachments have been restored.

procedures.purpose: Complete active grille shutter removal and installation, including attachment torques.
Front bumper cover removal and installation for shutter access.
Explain shutter purpose, PCM control and automatic startup calibration.
Explain operating positions, calibration behavior, communication faults and assembly serviceability.

guides.title: Remove and refit the cowl panel grille
guides.summary: Remove the windshield-base grille by releasing its fasteners, then restore the wiper arms to their correct parked positions.
guides.introduction: The cowl panel grille is the broad cover across the bottom of the windshield, beneath the wiper arms. This job removes the grille for replacement or access underneath it. The work involves both clipped body trim and wiper-arm installation, so correct reassembly includes restoring the blade positions.
guides.why: The grille must be released from its clips before it is lifted and pulled out. The wiper motor must also be parked before the arms are installed; otherwise, aligning the blades by appearance alone can leave their positions incorrect.

when.summary: When the cowl grille requires replacement or must be removed for access beneath the windshield.
notes: The illustrated procedure shows left-hand drive; right-hand drive is similar.

prepare.title: Wiper-arm tools
prepare.detail: Have a two-leg puller and a torque wrench available. The puller is specified for removing the arms from their pivots.

prepare.title: Fastener access
prepare.detail: Identify the battery-cover retainers and the grille retainers and clips in the removal procedure before attempting to move the panel.

steps.title: Remove the wiper arms
steps.body: Follow the [wiper pivot-arm removal procedure](#/document/G1694632). Remove the nut covers and nuts, then use the two-leg puller to remove the arms. This clears the components that sit over the grille.

steps.title: Release the cover and grille fasteners
steps.body: Remove the battery-cover retainers and lift away the cover. Next remove the grille retainers, then depress and remove its clips. Depressing the clips releases their locking action before the panel is moved.

steps.title: Lift out and refit the grille
steps.body: Following the [cowl procedure](#/document/G1693246), lift the grille upward first, then pull it out. Install the grille by reversing that sequence, restore its clips and retainers, and reinstall the battery cover and its retainers.

steps.title: Park the motor and install the arms
steps.body: Before installing the arms, turn the ignition ON and command one complete wiper cycle to establish the motor's PARK position. Install the arms with the blades inside the windshield marks. Tighten the arm nuts to 26 lb.ft (35 Nm), turn the ignition off, and install the nut covers.

watchFor.title: Resistance at a clip
watchFor.body: Check that the clips have been depressed and removed before continuing the upward-and-outward removal movement.

watchFor.title: Incorrect blade alignment
watchFor.body: Use both the motor's PARK position and the windshield marks when installing the arms.

notes: The wiper-arm illustrations omit the hood for clarity; hood removal is not a listed step.

verification.title: Restored attachments
verification.body: Confirm that the grille clips, grille retainers and battery-cover retainers have been reinstalled.

verification.title: Wiper installation
verification.body: Confirm that the parked blades are inside the windshield marks, the arm nuts are tightened, and the nut covers are fitted.

procedures.purpose: Complete cowl panel grille removal and reverse-order installation.
Prerequisite wiper-arm removal and final installation, including motor parking, blade alignment and nut tightening.

guides.title: Remove and refit the fender splash shield with the SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Remove the wheel and shield retainers to service the wheel-arch liner, then reinstall the shield and wheel correctly.
guides.introduction: The fender splash shield lines the wheel opening and forms a barrier between wheel-thrown spray and the surrounding body area. On this SVT Performance Package application, access starts by removing the wheel and tire assembly. The shield then comes away after its retainers are released. This guide covers the 5.2L application and includes the wheel-installation requirements that make the access work complete.
guides.why: A shield that is still attached can be damaged by pulling against an overlooked retainer. Wheel refitting deserves equal attention: contamination between mounting faces can prevent proper seating, while incorrect tightening can allow loosening or contribute to brake-disc runout and vibration.

when.summary: When the splash shield needs replacement or removal to reach components behind the wheel-arch liner.
notes: The left-hand side is illustrated; the right-hand side uses a similar procedure.

prepare.title: Arrange safe wheel access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the lifting guidance referenced by the wheel procedure. The wheel-removal sequence specifies placing the vehicle in NEUTRAL before positioning it on the hoist.

prepare.title: Prepare for wheel installation
prepare.detail: Have wheel-fastening and torque equipment, means to clean the mating surfaces, and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 available.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle and remove the wheel
steps.body: Follow [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507), including its hoist-positioning reference. Remove the wheel nuts and wheel assembly to expose the shield. Do not use heat to free a seized wheel nut; it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing.

steps.title: Work through every retainer-removal stage
steps.body: Follow all successive retainer-removal stages in the [splash-shield procedure](#/document/G1944325). Keep track of their locations for reassembly. Complete these stages before trying to withdraw the shield.

steps.title: Remove the shield
steps.body: Withdraw the fender splash shield once its retainers have been released. If it remains held at an attachment point, return to the retainer sequence before applying more force.

steps.title: Refit the shield in reverse order
steps.body: Position the shield in the wheel opening and restore its retainers by reversing removal. Check that the shield has returned to its intended position and that all removed attachments are accounted for.

steps.title: Prepare the wheel and hub interfaces
steps.body: Remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel and hub or brake-disc mounting surfaces. Ensure rotor-to-hub fasteners do not interfere with wheel seating. Apply only a thin coat of XL-2 at the interface between the wheel pilot bore and hub pilot.

steps.title: Install and tighten the wheel
steps.body: Position the wheel and install the nuts finger tight. Final tightening must be performed with the vehicle resting on its tires. With clean, dry stud and nut threads, tighten in a star/cross pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm).

watchFor.title: Lubricant on the wrong surfaces
watchFor.body: Keep anti-seize off wheel-to-disc mounting faces, studs, nuts, brake pads and brake-disc friction surfaces. Its specified location is the pilot interface only.

watchFor.title: Wheel seating problems
watchFor.body: Debris or interfering fasteners between the mounting faces can prevent secure seating and lead to wheel-nut loosening.

notes: Arrange wheel-nut retightening within 160 km (100 mi) after the wheel is reinstalled.

verification.title: Check the shield attachments
verification.body: Confirm that the shield is positioned correctly and every retainer removed during the access sequence has been restored.

verification.title: Record wheel completion and follow-up
verification.body: Record final wheel-nut tightening and the requirement to retighten within 160 km (100 mi) of reinstallation.

procedures.purpose: Provides fender splash-shield retainer removal and reverse installation for the 5.2L SVT Performance Package application.
Provides wheel removal, lifting reference, mounting-surface preparation, wheel-nut tightening and subsequent retightening requirements.

guides.title: Remove and replace the front fender splash shield
guides.summary: Remove the wheel and shield retainers to replace the wheel-arch liner, then restore the wheel using the specified mounting precautions.
guides.introduction: The fender splash shield lines the front wheel opening and forms a barrier between road spray and the surrounding body area. Its removal provides access behind the liner or allows a damaged shield to be replaced. The shield itself is retained mechanically; the significant supporting work is safe wheel removal and correct wheel installation afterward.
guides.why: Both retainer-removal stages must be completed before withdrawing the shield. During wheel installation, dirt or corrosion between mounting faces can prevent proper seating and allow the nuts to loosen. Lubricant belongs only at the specified pilot interface, because the wheel-nut tightening specification depends on clean, dry threads.

when.summary: When the front fender splash shield needs replacement or must be removed for access behind the wheel-arch liner.
notes: The left-hand side is illustrated; the right-hand side is similar.

prepare.title: Arrange wheel access
prepare.detail: Provide a hoist and the capability to follow the vehicle lifting procedure referenced by Wheel and Tire. Position the vehicle in NEUTRAL as directed.

prepare.title: Prepare for wheel installation
prepare.detail: Have torque-controlled wheel-fastening equipment and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 available for the specified pilot interface.

steps.title: Remove the wheel assembly
steps.body:
Before lifting, use a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Confirm the jack or hoist is rated for the vehicle, including cargo and modifications. If using a jack, support the vehicle on suitable stands at the designated points before going underneath; a jack alone is not a support. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

Follow [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507) to lift the vehicle and remove the wheel. Do not apply heat to a seized wheel nut; this can damage the wheel and bearing.

steps.title: Release the shield retainers
steps.body: Complete both retainer-removal stages in the splash-shield procedure. Follow their illustrated locations rather than assuming the first set releases the entire liner.

steps.title: Remove and refit the shield
steps.body: Withdraw the released splash shield. Position the replacement or retained shield and reverse the removal sequence to restore its retainers.

steps.title: Restore the wheel mounting
steps.body:
Before lowering, make sure the parking brake is applied. Restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground, and keep the vehicle restrained for final wheel-nut tightening. Do not lower an unrestrained vehicle in Neutral.

Clean the wheel and hub or brake-disc mounting faces, and ensure rotor fasteners do not interfere. Apply a thin coat of XL-2 only between the wheel pilot bore and hub pilot. Fit the wheel nuts finger-tight, then tighten in a star pattern to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm), with the vehicle resting on its tires.

watchFor.title: Lubricant outside the pilot interface
watchFor.body: Keep anti-seize off mounting faces, studs, nuts, brake pads and brake friction surfaces.

watchFor.title: A shield that remains attached
watchFor.body: Recheck both retainer-removal stages before attempting to withdraw it further.

notes: Wheel-nut torque applies to clean, dry stud and nut threads.

verification.title: Confirm restoration
verification.body: Check that the shield is positioned and retained, and record completion of the wheel’s final star-pattern tightening.

verification.title: Arrange the required wheel-nut recheck
verification.body: Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after wheel installation.

Wheel access, mounting-face preparation, pilot lubrication, final tightening and subsequent wheel-nut recheck.

guides.title: Remove and replace a front fender
guides.summary: Expose the fender's concealed attachments, separate its neighbouring trim connections and reinstall the panel using each fastener's specified tightening value.
guides.introduction: The front fender forms the outer body panel around the front wheel opening. Its attachments extend beyond the visible upper edge: access also involves the splash shield, rocker moulding, bumper-cover bracket, headlamp fastener, weatherstrip and sound insulation. Removing the panel is a sequence of uncovering and releasing these connections.
guides.why: A fender can remain firmly attached after the obvious bolts are removed because trim and insulation conceal further fixings. The attachment groups also use different tightening values. Treating every bolt alike can damage the lighter neighbouring connections during reassembly.

when.summary: When an established body repair requires front-fender removal or replacement.

prepare.title: Plan access through the surrounding trim
prepare.detail: Have the fender splash-shield and rocker-panel moulding procedures available. Both components are removed before the fender attachments are released.

prepare.title: Prepare for different fastener settings
prepare.detail: Use suitable fastener tools and a torque wrench capable of the settings in the fender procedure, including the light bumper-cover and headlamp connections.

steps.title: Remove the splash shield and rocker moulding
steps.body: Follow the [fender splash-shield procedure](#/document/G1693247), then the [rocker-panel moulding procedure](#/document/G1687581). Removing these components opens access to attachments that would otherwise remain covered.

steps.title: Release the bumper and headlamp attachment area
steps.body: Following the locations in the [fender procedure](#/document/G1693248), remove the initial bolts. Remove the bumper-cover attachment bolt and separate the cover from the fender bracket. Next remove the headlamp assembly bolt, followed by the indicated fender bolt.

steps.title: Release the cowl and weatherstrip-covered attachments
steps.body: Remove the cowl-panel-grille-to-fender clip and the next indicated bolt. Position the door weatherstrip aside, then remove the bolt exposed at that stage. Keep these fixings distinct from the earlier groups.

steps.title: Remove the insulation and concealed hardware
steps.body: Remove the retainers and sound insulation. Remove the indicated bolt and nut, then the further sound insulation. Follow this order so the remaining attachment points are exposed before the panel is moved.

steps.title: Remove the final bolts and fender
steps.body: With the earlier connections released, remove the final fender bolts and the panel. Support the panel as it becomes free, rather than leaving its weight on a remaining attachment.

steps.title: Reinstall in reverse order
steps.body: Reverse the complete removal sequence, restoring the insulation, retainers, weatherstrip, cowl clip and neighbouring panel connections. Apply each location's specified torque, then refit the rocker moulding and splash shield through their linked procedures.

watchFor.title: A panel that remains attached
watchFor.body: Recheck the weatherstrip and insulation stages before pulling harder. Their concealed fasteners are part of the removal sequence.

watchFor.title: Using the main bolt setting everywhere
watchFor.body: The bumper-cover connection and headlamp bolt have lower tightening settings than the main fender fasteners. Identify the location before tightening.

notes: The left-hand fender is illustrated; the right-hand procedure is similar. Use the attachment illustrations to locate otherwise unnamed bolts.

verification.title: Confirm all attachment groups
verification.body: Check that the fender fasteners, bumper-cover bracket connection, headlamp bolt and cowl clip have been restored with their applicable tightening values.

verification.title: Confirm the access layers are restored
verification.body: Check the sound insulation and retainers, door weatherstrip, rocker moulding and fender splash shield against the reverse-removal sequence.

procedures.purpose: Complete fender removal and installation, attachment locations and fastener torques.
Prerequisite fender splash-shield removal and final refitting.
Prerequisite rocker-panel moulding removal and final refitting.

guides.title: Remove and replace the hood with SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Remove the hood with an assistant, transfer the specified fittings when installing a new panel, and check its final alignment.
guides.introduction: The hood closes the engine compartment and is positioned by its hinges and latch striker. On this SVT Performance Package application, the job also involves the hood insulation, washer-hose connections and, when replacing the panel, its scoop assembly and tether. Removal for access and installation of a new hood share the lifting sequence but require different preparation of the attached fittings.
guides.why: Marking the hinge positions helps recover the existing fit, while an assistant controls the panel as its hinge nuts are removed. The final alignment check remains necessary because the marks only provide an initial position. Separating the new-panel transfer work also avoids disturbing fittings unnecessarily when the original hood will be refitted.

when.summary: When the hood needs replacement or must be removed for access on a vehicle with the SVT Performance Package.
notes: The scoop, striker latch and hood pad removal steps apply only when installing a new component.

prepare.title: Arrange an assistant
prepare.detail: An assistant is required for hood removal. Agree how the panel will be supported before releasing the hinge attachments.

prepare.title: Prepare marking and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Have a way to index-mark both hinge positions, tools for the retainers and fasteners, and torque control for the fittings being disturbed.

prepare.title: Plan the alignment phase
prepare.detail: Have the Hood Alignment procedure referenced in the hood article available if the final fit needs adjustment.

steps.title: Detach insulation and washer connections
steps.body: Remove the retainers and hood insulation. Detach the windshield-washer hose retainers and couplings so the hose connections are released before the hood is lifted away.

steps.title: Prepare fittings for a replacement hood
steps.body: When installing a new component, remove the nut, scoop tether and scoop assembly. Next remove the striker-latch-to-hood bolts and striker latch, followed by the retainers and hood pad assembly. Keep these parts associated with their attachment locations for reassembly.

steps.title: Mark both hinge positions
steps.body: Index-mark the hood hinge locations before loosening the hood attachments. The right-side illustration also applies to the similar left-side arrangement.

steps.title: Remove the hood with assistance
steps.body: With the assistant controlling the panel, remove the hinge nuts and lift the hood away. Maintain support while the attachments are released so the panel remains controlled throughout removal.

steps.title: Reinstall and restore the fittings
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Use the hinge marks to establish the starting position and apply the specified torque for each attachment. Restore any transferred pad, striker and scoop components, including the scoop tether, then reconnect the washer hose and insulation.

steps.title: Check the completed fit
steps.body: Check hood alignment after installation. If adjustment is necessary, follow the Hood Alignment procedure referenced in the linked hood article.

watchFor.title: Different fastening requirements
watchFor.body: The scoop nut, striker bolts and hinge nuts have different torque settings; use the setting for the attachment being tightened.

watchFor.title: Unsupported panel
watchFor.body: Have the assistant in position before removing the hinge nuts.

notes: This procedure covers the supplied 5.2L application with the SVT Performance Package.

verification.title: Confirm restored attachments
verification.body: Check the washer-hose couplings and retainers, insulation and any transferred scoop, tether, striker and pad components.

verification.title: Record alignment completion
verification.body: Record that alignment was checked and whether adjustment was required before considering the hood installation complete.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the 5.2L SVT Performance Package hood, including conditional component transfers and final alignment referral.

guides.title: Remove, replace and align the hood
guides.summary: Disconnect the hood attachments, remove it with an assistant, transfer components when replacing it, and check alignment after refitting.
guides.introduction: The hood provides opening access to the engine compartment and carries insulation, washer-hose attachments and, when fitted, a scoop. Its hinges establish its position while the hood-mounted striker engages the latch. Removal for access and replacement with a new hood share the main sequence, but component-transfer work is only needed for replacement.
guides.why: The hood is awkward to control once its hinge nuts are removed, so an assistant is required. Marking the hinge positions gives a useful starting reference for installation. Those marks do not replace the final alignment check, especially when a new panel has been installed.

when.summary: When the hood requires replacement or removal for access to other work.
notes: Scoop, striker and hood-pad removal are conditional operations for fitting a new component.

prepare.title: Arrange assistance
prepare.detail: Have an assistant available to control the hood during removal and refitting.

prepare.title: Prepare the fastener and alignment work
prepare.detail: Have suitable hand tools, a torque wrench and a way to index-mark the hinge locations. Keep the Hood Alignment procedure available for the final fit check.

steps.title: Disconnect the attached insulation and washer hose
steps.body: Remove the hood-insulation retainers and insulation. Detach the windshield washer hose retainers and couplings so the hose no longer connects the hood to the surrounding installation.

steps.title: Remove transfer components only when required
steps.body: When fitting a new hood, remove the scoop nuts, brackets and scoop if equipped. For a new hood on all vehicles, remove the striker-to-hood bolts and striker, then the retainers and hood pad assembly. These operations are unnecessary for simply removing and reinstalling the existing hood.

steps.title: Mark and remove the hood
steps.body: Index-mark the hinge locations before loosening their attachments. With the assistant controlling the panel, remove the hinge nuts and hood. Use the [hood procedure](#/document/G1693249) for the attachment locations.

steps.title: Install and restore the attachments
steps.body: Reverse removal, using the hinge marks as the initial positioning reference. Tighten the hood hinge nuts to 17 lb.ft (23 Nm). Where components were transferred, tighten the striker bolts to 106 lb.in (12 Nm) and scoop bracket nuts to 27 lb.in (3 Nm). Restore the pad, washer hose couplings and retainers, and insulation.

steps.title: Check the final panel position
steps.body: Check hood alignment and adjust it as necessary using [Hood Alignment](#/document/G1693220). Complete this step even when the original hinge marks appear to line up.

watchFor.title: A remaining washer-hose connection
watchFor.body: Confirm the couplings and retainers have been detached before attempting to move the hood away.

notes: The hinge operation is illustrated on the right side; the left side is similar.

diagnostics.finding: The hood does not align correctly after refitting.
diagnostics.meaning: The initial hinge position needs further adjustment.
diagnostics.next: Follow Hood Alignment to establish the final fit.

verification.title: Confirm restored attachments
verification.body: Check completion of the hinge fastening, washer-hose connections and insulation installation, plus any striker, scoop or pad transfers.

verification.title: Record the alignment result
verification.body: Record that hood alignment was checked and whether adjustment was necessary.

procedures.purpose: Hood removal and installation, including replacement-only transfers and the optional scoop branch.
Check and correct hood alignment after installation.

authoring.scopeCorrection: Reviewed separate SVT hardware/access procedures; generic scope excludes5.2L. Metadata-only correction; original article rewrite still pending.

guides.title: Align the Front Door and Check Glass Fit
guides.summary: Correct front-door gaps and flushness, then check the striker and the glass alignment for the fitted body style.
guides.introduction: Door alignment controls both the width of the gaps around the door and how evenly its outer surface sits against neighboring panels. The hinges allow adjustment in several directions, while the striker provides the latch engagement point. This job establishes the door’s position against measured body specifications and finishes by checking the glass, whose position changes with the door.
guides.why: A gap can look even while the door still sits too far inward or outward, so margin and flushness need separate checks. The procedure removes the striker before hinge adjustment and treats different adjustment directions separately. Checking the glass afterward matters because correct metal-panel alignment does not automatically establish correct window alignment.

when.summary: When measured front-door gaps or flushness are outside specification.
notes: The left side is illustrated; the right side follows a similar procedure.
The door procedure applies to coupe and convertible, with separate glass-adjustment procedures.

prepare.title: Measure before loosening anything
prepare.detail: Have suitable gap-measuring equipment and the Body and Frame dimensions available. Compare the door with the fender, rocker moulding and body side.

prepare.title: Prepare for controlled adjustment
prepare.detail: Use suitable fastener tools and torque equipment. Identify the illustrated nuts and bolts before starting: the adjustment groups do different jobs, and the fore/aft/tilt bolts have different tightening callouts.

steps.title: Establish the starting position
steps.body: Check front-door-to-body dimensions using [Body and Frame](#/document/G1687516). Note which gaps or flushness measurements need correction so the adjustment addresses a measured difference.

steps.title: Remove the striker
steps.body: Remove the striker assembly and its bolts as directed in [Front Door Alignment](#/document/G1693219). This prepares the door for the hinge-adjustment stages. The striker’s installation torque is given in that procedure.

steps.title: Correct height and inward or outward position
steps.body: Open the door and loosen the specified nuts two turns to permit movement. Adjust the door to the body dimensions, then tighten the nuts. Use this branch for up/down and in/out corrections.

steps.title: Correct fore/aft position and tilt
steps.body: Open the door and loosen the specified bolts two turns. Carefully close it, adjust to specification, then carefully reopen it to tighten the bolts. Follow each illustrated torque callout; the two bolt locations do not share one tightening value.

steps.title: Complete the striker adjustment
steps.body: Refit the striker for the final adjustment stage and follow the specified two-turn loosening instruction to permit movement. Recheck body-to-door dimensions and secure the striker according to the procedure.

steps.title: Check glass fit and finish reassembly
steps.body: Check the front-door glass using [Coupe Glass Adjustment](#/document/G1697266) or [Convertible Glass Adjustment](#/document/G1725016), as applicable. Complete any required glass adjustment and reinstall the remaining removed components.

watchFor.title: Panel contact during movement
watchFor.body: Close and reopen the door carefully while the adjustment bolts are loose. Its position can change as the fasteners permit movement.

watchFor.title: Body-style differences at the glass
watchFor.body: Use the applicable glass dimensions and procedure. Coupe and convertible glass margins are not interchangeable.

notes: Margin means the gap between adjoining parts; flushness describes how far one surface stands inward or outward relative to the other.

diagnostics.finding: Door height or flushness is outside specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The in/out and up/down adjustment branch addresses these directions.
diagnostics.next: Adjust the specified nuts, tighten them and remeasure.

diagnostics.finding: The door needs fore/aft movement or a change in tilt.
diagnostics.meaning: This requires the separate bolt-adjustment branch.
diagnostics.next: Follow the careful close-adjust-open sequence before tightening.

verification.title: Record the final dimensions
verification.body: Record the checked door margins and flushness against the applicable Body and Frame specifications.

verification.title: Confirm glass and reassembly
verification.body: Confirm the body-style-specific glass check is complete, adjusted fasteners are tightened and removed components are installed.

procedures.purpose: Front-door inspection, directional hinge adjustments, striker adjustment and final checks.
Body margin, flushness and body-style-specific dimensional references.
Front-door glass adjustment for a convertible.
Front-door glass adjustment for a coupe.

guides.title: Align the hood gaps and front height
guides.summary: Measure the hood's position, adjust its fore/aft and lateral alignment or front bump stops, then verify the specified gaps and flushness.
guides.introduction: The aluminum hood is a hinged, bolted body panel. Its alignment has two distinct aspects: the gap around its edges and its height relative to adjoining panels. Moving the hood fore/aft or sideways changes its position within the opening; adjusting the front rubber bump stops changes its front height. This procedure covers both adjustments for coupe and convertible bodies.
guides.why: An edge can have a reasonable gap while still sitting too high or low, so appearance alone does not establish correct alignment. Measuring both margin and flushness identifies which adjustment is needed. The latch is removed before adjustment, allowing the prescribed hood-position checks to be made without its engagement influencing the fit.

when.summary: When measured hood gaps or flushness fall outside the specified body-panel tolerances.
notes: The front-panel dimension specifications apply to both coupe and convertible.
The alignment illustration shows a coupe; the convertible procedure is similar.

prepare.title: Have the dimensions available
prepare.detail: Use the Body and Frame front-panel margin and flushness specifications. Prepare measuring equipment suitable for panel gaps and relative surface height.

prepare.title: Prepare for latch and fastener work
prepare.detail: Have the hood-latch removal and installation procedure, suitable fastener tools and a torque wrench available before loosening the hood attachments.

steps.title: Measure the existing fit
steps.body: Compare the hood-to-body dimensions with the [Body and Frame specifications](#/document/G1687516). Check the relevant relationships to the fascia, fenders and cowl filler, distinguishing edge clearance from flushness.

steps.title: Remove the hood latch
steps.body: For either alignment branch, remove the latch using the [hood-latch procedure](#/document/G1695905). This is a prerequisite in the alignment sequence, not an optional final correction.

steps.title: Make the required adjustment
steps.body: For fore/aft or left/right correction, follow the [hood alignment procedure](#/document/G1693220): loosen the indicated bolts 2 turns, move the hood to specification and tighten the specified nuts to 17 lb.ft (23 Nm). For front up/down correction, adjust the rubber bump stops until the hood meets the dimensional specification.

steps.title: Remeasure and restore the latch
steps.body: Check the body-to-hood dimensions again after adjustment and tightening. Once the fit meets specification, reinstall the removed components through their applicable installation instructions.

watchFor.title: Using the wrong adjustment
watchFor.body: Front bump-stop adjustment addresses front height; the hood fastener adjustment provides fore/aft and lateral movement. Choose the branch indicated by the measurements.

notes: Use the specified tolerances rather than trying to make every surrounding gap identical.

diagnostics.finding: Fore/aft or side-to-side hood position is outside specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The hood needs positional adjustment at the indicated fasteners.
diagnostics.next: Use the fore/aft and left/right branch, then recheck the surrounding dimensions.

diagnostics.finding: The front hood height is outside specification.
diagnostics.meaning: The front up/down adjustment is required.
diagnostics.next: Adjust the rubber bump stops and remeasure flushness.

verification.title: Confirm the measured result
verification.body: Check and record final hood gaps and flushness against the applicable front-panel specifications after the adjustment fasteners are tightened.

verification.title: Complete reassembly
verification.body: Confirm that the hood latch and all other removed components have been installed using their prescribed procedures.

procedures.purpose: Inspect and adjust hood fore/aft position, lateral position and front height.
Provide front-panel margin and flushness specifications for coupe and convertible bodies.
Remove the hood latch before alignment and reinstall it afterward.

guides.title: Align the luggage compartment lid on a coupe or convertible
guides.summary: Measure the luggage lid gaps and flushness, adjust its horizontal position and height as needed, then restore the latch.
guides.introduction: The steel luggage compartment lid must sit correctly within the surrounding body opening. Alignment involves both the width of the gaps around it and its height relative to adjacent panels. Fore-and-aft or sideways adjustment changes its position in the opening; the adjusting screws and rubber bump stops establish its vertical relationship. The procedure shows a coupe, with a similar approach for the convertible.
guides.why: A lid can have an acceptable gap yet stand too high or low. Measuring margin and flushness separately prevents correcting one while overlooking the other. Removing the latch before adjustment also allows the lid position to be established without its engagement influencing how the panel sits. The final decision should follow the specified dimensions rather than appearance alone.

when.summary: When measured luggage lid gaps or flushness fall outside the applicable body specifications.
notes: Use the dimensions for the fitted body style, including the convertible-specific rear-panel relationships.

prepare.title: Arrange measurement and fastening capability
prepare.detail: Have suitable means to measure panel gaps and flushness, loosen the mounting fasteners and apply the specified tightening torque.

prepare.title: Select the latch procedure
prepare.detail: Use the coupe or convertible latch removal and installation procedure as appropriate. Latch removal is required for every alignment branch.

steps.title: Measure the starting position
steps.body: Check the lid-to-body dimensions against [Body and Frame](#/document/G1687516). Record gap width and flushness separately so you can identify whether horizontal movement, vertical adjustment or both are needed.

steps.title: Remove the latch
steps.body: Remove the luggage compartment lid latch using the [coupe procedure](#/document/G1695910) or [convertible procedure](#/document/G1709223). Complete this before either adjustment branch.

steps.title: Correct fore-and-aft or sideways position
steps.body: For horizontal alignment, loosen the specified bolts two turns to permit movement. Adjust the lid to the body dimensions, carefully open it, then tighten the specified nuts to 106 lb.in (12 Nm). Use the [alignment procedure](#/document/G1693223) to identify the adjustment points.

steps.title: Correct height with the adjusting screws
steps.body: For up-and-down alignment, adjust the screws and compare the resulting position with the body specifications. Check flushness as well as the surrounding gaps.

steps.title: Set the rubber bump stops
steps.body: Open the lid and adjust its rubber bump stops, then check the lid position against specifications again. This is a separate part of the vertical-alignment sequence.

steps.title: Confirm dimensions and restore the latch
steps.body: Check the body-to-lid dimensions after the adjustments. Once they meet the applicable specifications, install the removed components using the appropriate latch procedure.

watchFor.title: Position changing during tightening
watchFor.body: Open the lid carefully after horizontal adjustment and verify its position after the mounting nuts are tightened.

watchFor.title: Using the wrong rear-panel dimensions
watchFor.body: The convertible has additional relationships involving the top and high-mounted stop lamp. Apply those only to the convertible.

notes: The dimension tables contain separate margin and flushness tolerances; an apparently even gap is not a substitute for checking both.

diagnostics.finding: Measured gaps indicate a fore-and-aft or sideways offset.
diagnostics.meaning: The horizontal alignment branch addresses this positioning error.
diagnostics.next: Adjust the mounting position and remeasure.

diagnostics.finding: The lid stands too high or low relative to the body.
diagnostics.meaning: Vertical alignment needs attention even if gap widths are acceptable.
diagnostics.next: Work through the adjusting-screw and bump-stop sequence.

verification.title: Record final dimensions
verification.body: Record the final margins and flushness against the applicable specifications.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly
verification.body: Confirm the mounting nuts are tightened and the latch and other removed components have been restored.

procedures.purpose: Inspection, horizontal and vertical luggage lid alignment, and final dimensional checks.
Panel margin and flushness specifications, including convertible-specific rear dimensions.
Coupe luggage compartment lid latch removal and installation.
Convertible luggage compartment lid latch removal and installation.

guides.title: Replace a front door check arm
guides.summary: Remove the door trim and watershield to replace the check arm, then restore its mountings and the door's interior connections.
guides.introduction: The check arm restrains the front door as it opens and helps control its travel. Its attachment inside the door means replacement involves both mechanical fasteners and interior trim. The door panel must be released carefully because wiring and the interior latch cable remain connected behind it.
guides.why: Once disconnected, the arm cannot restrain door movement. Controlling the door protects nearby panels, while supporting the trim prevents its remaining cable and electrical connections from carrying the panel's weight.

when.summary: When a front door check arm requires removal or replacement.
notes: A door movement complaint alone does not establish that the check arm needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange controlled access
prepare.detail: Allow room to hold the door steady and support the trim panel during disconnection.

prepare.title: Prepare fastening tools
prepare.detail: Use hand tools and torque equipment suitable for the check-arm hardware and the smaller trim-panel fasteners.

steps.title: Release the external attachment
steps.body: Follow the [check-arm procedure](#/document/G1693222). Control the door and remove the check-arm bolt. Its installation torque differs from that of the nuts inside the door.

steps.title: Remove the door trim
steps.body: Follow [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600): remove the upper bolt cover and bolt, the window control switch through its referenced procedure, the center bolt and lower retainers. Release the clips and pin retainers in the specified rear-upper, rear/lower and remaining-panel sequence. Lift the panel up and out, then disconnect electrical connectors where fitted and release the latch cable.

steps.title: Withdraw the check arm
steps.body: Remove the check-arm nuts, then the front watershield. Remove the check-arm assembly through the resulting access. Preserve this sequence so the shield and surrounding trim do not obstruct withdrawal.

steps.title: Restore the arm and trim
steps.body: Reverse removal. Refit the arm and watershield, tightening the nuts to 106 lb.in (12 Nm). Reconnect the latch cable and applicable connectors before seating the trim; transfer trim parts as necessary. Follow the panel procedure's individual fastening torques. Install the check-arm bolt to 18 lb.ft (25 Nm).

watchFor.title: Attached trim
watchFor.body: Do not pull a partly released panel away while its retainers, latch cable or electrical connections still hold it.

notes: The check-arm procedure shows the left side; the right is similar. Trim instructions show a right-hand door on a left-hand-drive vehicle, with opposite arrangements similar.

verification.title: Confirm fastening and reconnection
verification.body: Check the arm bolt and nuts against their separate torque settings, and confirm the watershield, latch cable, applicable connectors and panel retainers are restored.

procedures.purpose: Front door check-arm removal and installation, including mounting torques.
Door-trim access, staged retainer release, cable disconnection and trim refitting.

guides.title: Remove and refit a front door
guides.summary: Disconnect the door wiring and check arm, remove the door with another technician and check alignment when installing a new door.
guides.introduction: The front door hangs from hinge pivots, while its check arm controls opening travel and its electrical connector joins the door wiring to the body. Removing the door means separating these connections in order. The work is straightforward in outline, but supporting the door while releasing its pivots requires another technician.
guides.why: The electrical connection and check arm must be detached before the door is lifted away. Once the hinge pivot bolts are removed, the technicians must control the door's weight and position. A replacement door also needs its relationship to the body checked through the separate alignment procedure.

when.summary: When a front door must be removed for repair access or replaced.
notes: The illustrated procedure shows the left side; the right side is similar.

prepare.title: Arrange another technician
prepare.detail: A second technician is required for hinge pivot bolt removal and for taking the door off the vehicle. Plan the lift before either pivot is released.

prepare.title: Prepare the fastening and alignment work
prepare.detail: Have suitable hand tools and torque equipment for the check-arm and hinge-pivot bolts. If installing a new door, have the linked front-door alignment procedure available.

steps.title: Disconnect the door wiring
steps.body: Disconnect the front-door electrical connector at the body connection shown in the illustration. This separates the wiring before the door is freed mechanically.

steps.title: Detach the check arm
steps.body: Remove the check-arm bolt. Its installation torque is 18 lb.ft (25 Nm). The check arm must be disconnected before the door can be removed.

steps.title: Release the hinges and lift off the door
steps.body: With the other technician controlling the door, remove the hinge pivot bolts. Together, remove the door from the vehicle. Assistance is required during both operations, not only for the final lift.

steps.title: Refit the door and connections
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence with assistance. Tighten the hinge pivot bolts to 150 lb.in (17 Nm), restore the check-arm attachment and reconnect the wiring. When installing a new door, check door-to-body alignment and adjust it through the linked alignment procedure as necessary.

watchFor.title: An attachment still connected
watchFor.body: Do not lift the door away while its electrical connector or check arm remains attached.

watchFor.title: Loss of support at the pivots
watchFor.body: Keep both technicians engaged while the hinge pivot bolts are released and the door is removed.

notes: The additional alignment check is specifically required when installing a new component.

verification.title: Confirm the restored connections
verification.body: Confirm the hinge pivot and check-arm fasteners are tightened and the door electrical connector is reconnected.

verification.title: Record replacement-door alignment
verification.body: For a new door, record the door-to-body alignment check and any adjustment completed.

procedures.purpose: Front-door removal and installation, including required assistance and fastening details.
Door-to-body alignment checking and adjustment when installing a new front door.

guides.title: Replace the fuel filler door spring
guides.summary: Open the fuel filler door, release the spring's retaining tab with a screwdriver, and slide the replacement into the same mounting.
guides.introduction: A fuel flap has a modest job description, yet one little spring can still make it a nuisance. I'll walk you through releasing its retaining tab and fitting the replacement without turning the surrounding assembly into a screwdriver wrestling arena. This procedure applies to 2015 Mustangs with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
guides.why: The spring supplies spring force for the exterior fuel filler door's movement. Its retaining tab holds the spring component in the door assembly. Releasing that tab before withdrawing the component is the key: the screwdriver operates the catch; it does not need to pry the whole assembly apart.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang fuel filler door spring replacement

when.summary: Use this procedure when the fuel filler door spring has been identified for replacement.
notes: The same replacement sequence applies to all four listed engines.
Access begins with the fuel filler door open.

prepare.title: Have the replacement and screwdriver ready
prepare.detail: Have a replacement fuel filler door spring suitable for the vehicle and a screwdriver ready. Compare the replacement's shape and retaining-tab position with the installed component before removal.

prepare.title: Keep the job within its practical scope
prepare.detail: This is a spring replacement procedure. It does not establish a spring-force test or a way to open a stuck filler door. If the door cannot be opened, resolve that access problem before starting.

steps.title: Open the fuel filler door and locate the spring
steps.body:
Swing the fuel filler door open and leave it open for access. The spring component sits in a small mounting beside the filler opening; the illustration shows it on the right side of the recessed opening. Opening the door exposes the working area directly.

Use the [fuel filler door spring procedure and illustrations](#/document/G1693226) to identify the small cylindrical component and its retaining tab. I would note its orientation and how far it sits in the mounting before disturbing it—that gives the replacement a useful parking reference.

steps.title: Press the spring's retaining tab
steps.body:
Place the screwdriver tip against the retaining tab identified in the close-up illustration. Press the tab to release the spring from the fuel filler door assembly. The close-up marks this release as action 1.

Keep the screwdriver on the tab rather than using the surrounding recess as a prying surface.

steps.title: Withdraw the released spring
steps.body:
With the tab released, slide the spring component out of its mounting along its length, following the withdrawal direction marked as action 2 in the illustration. Keep track of its installed orientation.

If it remains caught, check that the screwdriver is actually depressing the retaining tab before continuing. More leverage is a poor substitute for finding the catch; little plastic fittings are remarkably unimpressed by determination.

steps.title: Fit and retain the replacement
steps.body:
Installation reverses removal. Align the replacement with the mounting in the same orientation as the removed component, then slide it back along the removal path in the opposite direction. Seat it in its original position and allow the retaining tab to engage.

Check that the spring sits in the mounting and that the tab has returned to its retaining position. Simply placing the component in the opening does not finish the job.

steps.title: Check the assembled door
steps.body:
Remove the screwdriver from the recess. Confirm that the spring remains seated, then close and reopen the fuel filler door through its normal movement. Check that the installed component stays in place and does not obstruct the door.

This is a completion check of the assembly you have just disturbed, rather than a measurement of spring strength.

watchFor.title: A tab that has not released
watchFor.body: The illustrated sequence releases the tab before withdrawing the spring. If the component will not slide out, return to the release point instead of levering against the surrounding assembly.

watchFor.title: A replacement that is sitting loose
watchFor.body: The retaining tab must engage as well as the spring being seated. If either condition is missing, correct the installation before treating the job as complete.

notes: The overall illustration establishes access with the door open; the close-up separates tab release from spring withdrawal.

diagnostics.finding: The spring remains held when you try to withdraw it.
diagnostics.meaning: The retaining tab may still be engaged; resistance alone does not establish a failed spring or damaged mounting.
diagnostics.next: Reposition the screwdriver on the illustrated tab, press it to release the component, and then resume withdrawal.

diagnostics.finding: The replacement will not seat or its retaining tab will not engage.
diagnostics.meaning: Installation is incomplete.
diagnostics.next: Check the replacement's orientation and alignment against the removed component. Refit it in the reverse removal direction. If it still cannot be retained, stop rather than forcing the mounting.

verification.title: Seating and retention
verification.body: The replacement occupies the original mounting position and its retaining tab is engaged.

verification.title: Normal door movement
verification.body: With the tool removed, the door can be closed and reopened without the replacement obstructing movement or coming out of its mounting.

procedures.purpose: Fuel filler door spring access, screwdriver-operated retaining-tab release, withdrawal and reverse-sequence installation.

applicability.equipment: Exterior fuel filler door and its spring assembly.

stepGroups.title: Expose and identify the spring
stepGroups.summary: Open the door and establish the component's mounting orientation.

stepGroups.title: Release and remove
stepGroups.summary: Depress the retaining tab before withdrawing the spring.

stepGroups.title: Install and check
stepGroups.summary: Seat the replacement, engage its tab and check normal door movement.

guides.title: Remove and refit the fuel filler door
guides.summary: Open the fuel filler door, release its retaining tab with a screwdriver and slide the door off its hinge. Reverse those actions to refit it.
guides.introduction: The fuel filler door has one small tab doing bouncer duty: until it moves, the door stays on the hinge. I’ll walk you through releasing that attachment without turning a little exterior flap into a big damn project. This procedure applies to the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
guides.why: The fuel filler door is the exterior cover over the refueling opening. Its sliding attachment connects it to the hinge, and a retaining tab keeps it from sliding off during use. Moving that tab back lets you remove the door while leaving the hinge in place.

when.summary: Use this procedure when the fuel filler door itself needs removal, replacement or refitting.
notes: This is a door removal and installation procedure, not a test for a refueling fault.

prepare.title: Have a screwdriver ready
prepare.detail: The retaining tab releases with a screwdriver. If replacing the door, have the replacement ready so you can refit it through the same sliding attachment.

prepare.title: Keep the job at the door-to-hinge connection
prepare.detail: Work from outside the car with the fuel filler door open. This procedure covers separating the door from its hinge; hinge removal, hinge repair and body alignment require separate instructions.

steps.title: Open the door and locate its retaining tab
steps.body: Open the fuel filler door to expose its inner face and hinge attachment. Identify where the door slides onto the hinge and locate the retaining tab at that connection. The second illustration in the [fuel filler door procedure](#/document/G1693224) points the screwdriver toward the tab on the exposed inner face. I’d find that little keeper before putting any pressure on the door.

steps.title: Release the tab and slide the door off the hinge
steps.body:
Hold the door so you can control it as the attachment releases. Place the screwdriver at the retaining tab and gently pry the tab back, then slide the door off the hinge while the tab is released.

Keep the screwdriver working on the tab rather than levering against the painted outer edge. Use the sliding connection to separate the parts; do not try to pull them straight apart. If the door resists sliding, pause and check that the tab has cleared the connection before applying more force. The keeper needs persuasion, not a wrestling match.

steps.title: Slide the door back onto the hinge and engage the tab
steps.body:
Position the removed or replacement door at the hinge attachment. Align the same sliding connection and slide the door back on in the opposite direction to removal. Allow the retaining tab to return to its retaining position as the door seats.

Check that the door is seated and the tab is engaged before letting go. Installation reverses the removal actions; the hinge remains in place.

steps.title: Confirm attachment and normal movement
steps.body:
With the door still open, gently check that it stays secured to the hinge rather than sliding off. Then close and reopen it, watching that the attachment remains seated throughout the movement.

If the connection comes loose, reopen the door and revisit the sliding fit and retaining-tab engagement before considering the job finished. These are completion checks for the attachment you disturbed.

watchFor.title: A tab that has not cleared
watchFor.body: Resistance during removal is a reason to recheck the tab release. Increasing force without checking it risks loading the attachment instead of freeing it.

watchFor.title: Screwdriver contact near paint
watchFor.body: Keep the screwdriver tip focused on the retaining tab and controlled throughout the release so it does not slip across the surrounding surfaces.

notes: No wheel, trim or hinge removal is part of this door replacement sequence.

diagnostics.finding: The door does not slide off after you move the retaining tab.
diagnostics.meaning: The release may be incomplete; resistance alone does not establish a failed hinge or door.
diagnostics.next: Support the door, recheck the screwdriver position and confirm that the tab is clear before trying the sliding movement again. Stop if it still will not release without force.

diagnostics.finding: The refitted door slides loose from its hinge.
diagnostics.meaning: The sliding attachment and retaining tab have not achieved secure retention.
diagnostics.next: Reopen the door, check its seating and restore tab engagement. Do not treat the installation as complete while the door can slide free.

verification.title: The door remains retained
verification.body: Confirm that the sliding attachment stays seated and the retaining tab holds the door on the hinge.

verification.title: Opening and closing preserve the attachment
verification.body: Close and reopen the door, confirming that it remains attached throughout the movement.

procedures.purpose: Fuel filler door removal by releasing the retaining tab and sliding the door from its hinge, followed by reverse-sequence installation.

applicability.equipment: Exterior fuel filler door and hinge.
