stepGroups.summary: Open the door and identify the sliding connection and retaining tab.

stepGroups.title: Release and remove
stepGroups.summary: Move the retaining tab back and slide the door from the hinge.

stepGroups.title: Refit and check
stepGroups.summary: Restore the sliding fit, engage the tab and confirm secure movement.

guides.title: Remove and refit the luggage compartment lid
guides.summary: Disconnect the lid trim, wiring and applicable cable, remove the lid with an assistant, and check alignment after refitting.
guides.introduction: The luggage compartment lid closes the trunk opening and carries trim, latch-related parts and wiring. Struts support it while open, and its hinge attachments locate it on the body. Removing the lid means releasing these connections in sequence; installing a new lid also requires removing the moulding and any fitted rear spoiler for refitting.
guides.why: The lid becomes unsupported as its struts and hinge fasteners are released, so another technician is required for removal. Gentle release of the latch-cover tab protects the cover. Final alignment matters because reinstalling the hinge fasteners alone does not establish that the lid sits correctly in the opening.

when.summary: When the luggage compartment lid must be removed for repair or replacement.
notes: Moulding and rear-spoiler removal are required only when installing a new lid.
Coupe trim access and convertible latch-lock cable disconnection are separate body-style branches.

prepare.title: Arrange assistance and tools
prepare.detail: Have another technician available to support and remove the lid. Prepare a flat-bladed screwdriver, suitable fastener tools and a torque wrench for the lid attachments and convertible cable bolts.

prepare.title: Identify the applicable branches
prepare.detail: Confirm the body style, whether the lid will be replaced and whether a rear spoiler is fitted. Have the applicable trim-transfer and lid-alignment procedures available.

steps.title: Release the emergency handle and latch cover
steps.body: Follow [Luggage Compartment Lid](#/document/G1693217). Press down the emergency-release handle retaining tab and remove the handle. Insert a flat-bladed screwdriver between the latch cover and latch, then gently pry the cover clear of the latch tab.

steps.title: Remove the lid trim
steps.body: Remove the retainers and lid trim panel as directed. For the coupe-specific trim stage, remove the bump-stop rubbers, then the retainers and trim panel identified in that branch. Preserve the body-style sequence when restoring these pieces.

steps.title: Prepare trim for a replacement lid
steps.body: Only when installing a new lid, remove the [luggage compartment lid moulding](#/document/G1687579). If a rear spoiler is fitted, also remove it using [Rear Spoiler](#/document/G1687580).

steps.title: Disconnect wiring and the applicable cable
steps.body: Detach the wiring-harness retainers and disconnect the lid electrical connectors. On a convertible, also detach the latch-lock cable retainers, remove its bolts and position the cable aside. These connections must be free before the lid is lifted away.

steps.title: Support and remove the lid
steps.body: Support the lid while removing the strut on each side. With the aid of another technician, remove the lid mounting nuts and lift the lid away. Keep the assistance in place through separation from the hinges.

steps.title: Refit and align the lid
steps.body: Reverse the applicable removal steps. Tighten the lid mounting nuts to 106 lb.in (12 Nm); on a convertible, tighten the latch-lock cable bolts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Restore struts, wiring, retainers and trim, then check and correct [lid alignment](#/document/G1693223) as necessary.

watchFor.title: A trapped latch-cover tab
watchFor.body: Pry gently at the specified cover-to-latch interface so the cover disengages from its tab.

watchFor.title: An attached connection during lifting
watchFor.body: Check the harness and, on a convertible, the latch-lock cable before moving the detached lid away.

notes: The emergency-release handle and its retaining tab are part of the removal and reverse-installation sequence.

verification.title: Check restored attachments
verification.body: Confirm both struts, electrical connections, harness retainers, trim and emergency-release handle are restored, together with the convertible cable where applicable.

verification.title: Record the alignment result
verification.body: Check lid alignment using the dedicated procedure, adjust if necessary and record whether correction was required.

procedures.purpose: Lid removal and installation, including common operations, coupe trim, convertible cable handling and replacement-only trim removal.
Lid moulding removal and installation when fitting a new luggage compartment lid.
Rear-spoiler removal and installation when a spoiler-equipped lid is replaced.
Required post-installation lid alignment check and adjustment when necessary.

applicability.equipment: Coupe or convertible; rear spoiler if fitted

guides.title: Remove and refit the coupe A-pillar trim
guides.summary: Move the door weatherstrip aside, release the panel clips and tether, and disconnect the optional speaker before removing the trim. Refit in reverse order.
guides.introduction: The A-pillar trim looks like one simple strip of plastic, but behind it there’s a small committee refusing to let go: clips, a tether and sometimes a speaker connection. I work through those attachments in order—“one more tug” is a lousy negotiating strategy here.
guides.why: This panel covers the inside of the front roof pillar beside the windshield and, where fitted, houses a speaker. Moving the door weatherstrip aside exposes its edge. Releasing the clips creates access to the tether, a retaining link behind the trim, and the optional speaker connector. Those connections must be released before the panel can leave the car.

when.summary: Use this procedure when removing or replacing the A-pillar trim on a 2015 Mustang coupe with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
notes: The illustrations show the right-hand panel on a left-hand-drive car. The left-hand panel and right-hand-drive arrangement are similar.
Disconnect and reconnect the speaker electrical connector only if a speaker is fitted.

prepare.title: Locate the panel and its access edge
prepare.detail: Open the door on the side being worked on. Identify the trim running from the dashboard corner up beside the windshield. The door weatherstrip overlaps its door-opening edge; the first illustration places the weatherstrip’s pin-type retainer near the bottom of that edge.

prepare.title: Plan for the concealed attachments
prepare.detail: Review the [A-pillar trim procedure and illustrations](#/document/G1692599). The removal illustration identifies the initial clip and tether release, the optional speaker connector behind the round grille, and the final release near the dashboard. Keep a hand supporting the panel as these attachments are disconnected.

prepare.title: Recognize the release-detail boundary
prepare.detail: The tether anchor and speaker connector are shown, but their precise latch-release motions are not detailed. Once exposed, identify each release before applying force. If its operation is unclear, pause for attachment-specific guidance rather than prying blindly or pulling on the wiring.

steps.title: Remove the weatherstrip retainer and move the seal aside
steps.body:
Locate and remove the pin-type retainer at the lower end of the illustrated weatherstrip section. Keep it for reassembly.
Move the door weatherstrip aside along the A-pillar trim edge until that edge is clear. The weatherstrip stays on the car; only the overlapping section needs to be moved out of the way.

steps.title: Release the initial trim clips
steps.body:
Support the panel and release the initial clips identified by callout 1 in the [removal illustration](#/document/G1692599). Ease the panel away from the pillar enough to reach behind it.
Expect it to remain attached: the tether, optional speaker connection and final clips are separate releases. This is the point where patience earns its garage keep.

steps.title: Disconnect the tether anchor
steps.body:
With the initial clips released, locate the tether attachment behind the panel. The rear-view inset identifies this attachment separately from the trim clips.
Disconnect the tether anchor while supporting the panel. Do not try to free it by pulling the panel farther away.

steps.title: Disconnect the speaker connector if fitted
steps.body:
If the panel carries a speaker, locate its electrical connector behind the round speaker grille, as shown in callout 2. Release the connector and separate it from the speaker while controlling the panel; pull on the connector body rather than the wires.
If there is no speaker connection, continue directly to the final clip release.

steps.title: Release the final clips and remove the panel
steps.body:
Release the remaining clips at the final removal stage, identified by callout 3 near the panel’s lower end at the dashboard corner. Remove the panel once these clips are free.
If it still resists, check which attachment remains engaged before moving it farther. The panel should not be used as a lever against the tether or speaker lead.

steps.title: Begin refitting in reverse removal order
steps.body:
Bring the panel back into its installed position and restore the clip attachments released in the final removal stage. Keep control of the panel and access to its rear connections while completing the reverse sequence.
If a speaker is fitted, reconnect its electrical connector. Then reconnect the tether anchor.

steps.title: Seat the initial clips
steps.body:
Before closing the gap to the pillar, confirm that the tether is attached and the speaker connector is connected where fitted. Check that the speaker lead is clear of the clip locations.
Align and engage the clips released at the start of panel removal. Seat the panel against the pillar, checking that its lower end sits correctly at the dashboard corner.

steps.title: Restore the weatherstrip and pin-type retainer
steps.body:
Return the displaced weatherstrip over the panel’s door-opening edge in its original position. Reinstall the pin-type retainer removed at the beginning.
Check the full section you moved so the seal lies back in place without a folded or trapped edge.

watchFor.title: A loose panel is still an attached panel
watchFor.body: Releasing the initial clips does not release the tether, optional speaker connector or final clips. Support the panel until all applicable attachments are disconnected.

watchFor.title: Resistance at the dashboard end
watchFor.body: The lower end has a separate final release. If the upper portion moves but the bottom stays put, return to that release instead of bending the panel.

watchFor.title: Connections hidden during refitting
watchFor.body: Confirm the tether and optional speaker connection before seating the initial clips. Once the panel is closed against the pillar, those attachments are concealed again.

notes: This is a trim removal and refitting procedure, not a diagnosis of speaker faults or noises behind the pillar.
The completion checks below confirm reassembly; they are not electrical diagnostic tests.

diagnostics.finding: The panel moves after the initial clips release but remains restrained behind it.
diagnostics.meaning: The tether anchor or optional speaker connection may still be attached.
diagnostics.next: Support the panel, look behind it and disconnect the applicable attachment before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: The upper panel is free but the lower end remains held near the dashboard.
diagnostics.meaning: The final clip-release stage is not complete.
diagnostics.next: Release the remaining clips identified by callout 3 before removing the panel.

diagnostics.finding: No speaker or speaker connector is fitted to the panel.
diagnostics.meaning: The optional electrical-disconnection branch does not apply.
diagnostics.next: Continue with the remaining clips during removal, or the tether and clip attachments during refitting.

verification.title: Confirm the concealed attachments
verification.body: Before fully seating the panel, confirm that the tether anchor is reconnected and the speaker connector is restored where fitted.

verification.title: Check panel seating
verification.body: Confirm that the initial and final clip locations are engaged and that the panel sits against the pillar with its lower end correctly positioned at the dashboard corner.

verification.title: Check the door-opening edge
verification.body: Confirm that the displaced weatherstrip is back in place along the trim edge and its pin-type retainer is installed.

procedures.purpose: A-pillar trim removal and reverse-order installation for the coupe, including weatherstrip access, clips, tether anchor and optional speaker connector.

stepGroups.title: Clear the trim edge
stepGroups.summary: Remove the weatherstrip retainer and move the seal aside.

stepGroups.title: Release the panel attachments
stepGroups.summary: Work through the initial clips, tether, optional speaker connection and final clips.

stepGroups.title: Reconnect and refit
stepGroups.summary: Reverse the attachment sequence, seat the trim and restore the weatherstrip.

guides.title: Remove and refit a front door trim panel
guides.summary: Release the concealed fasteners and staged retainers, lift the panel off the door, then disconnect and reconnect its wiring and latch cable.
guides.introduction: The front door trim panel forms the interior door surface and surrounds the window switch and inside release handle. Bolts, clips and pin-type retainers secure it to the door. Even after these attachments are released, electrical connections and the latch cable can still tether the panel. Removal provides access behind the trim or allows the panel itself to be replaced.
guides.why: The panel releases in stages and then lifts upward and outward from the door. Following that sequence avoids pulling against an attachment that is still engaged. The upper and center bolts also use a different tightening specification from the lower retainers, so installation requires more than simply tightening every fastener alike.

when.summary: When replacing the front door trim panel or gaining access to components behind it.
notes: The right door is illustrated; the left door follows a similar procedure.
Retain installation information shown alongside the removal steps.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim and fastener work
prepare.detail: Have suitable trim-release and fastener tools, plus a torque tool capable of the specified low tightening values.

prepare.title: Plan switch removal and panel support
prepare.detail: Have the front door window control switch procedure available. Support the panel during final separation so its electrical connections and latch cable remain accessible.

steps.title: Expose the upper fastening
steps.body: Remove the small cover and upper trim-panel bolt shown in [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600). The cover conceals an attachment that must be released before moving the panel.

steps.title: Remove the switch and remaining threaded attachments
steps.body: Remove the window switch using [Front Door Window Control Switch](#/document/G1695936). Then remove the center trim-panel bolt and lower retainers.

steps.title: Release the rear upper area
steps.body: Position the rear upper portion away from the door. Release the clip, followed by the pin-type retainers, in the illustrated sequence.

steps.title: Continue around the rear and lower portions
steps.body: Position the rear and lower portions away, releasing the indicated pin-type retainer and then the clip. Move the panel farther away and release the remaining pin-type retainers in their illustrated order.

steps.title: Lift off and disconnect
steps.body: Lift the panel upward and outward to release it from the door. Disconnect electrical connectors where fitted, then release the latch cable. Keep supporting the panel until these remaining connections are free.

steps.title: Transfer parts and reinstall
steps.body: Transfer parts as necessary and reverse the removal sequence. Reconnect the latch cable and applicable electrical connectors, engage the panel and retainers, and reinstall the switch and fasteners. Tighten the upper and center bolts to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm); tighten the lower retainers to 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm).

watchFor.title: A section remains firmly attached
watchFor.body: Recheck the fasteners and the illustrated retainer sequence before pulling farther.

watchFor.title: The panel is loose but still tethered
watchFor.body: Electrical connectors and the latch cable are disconnected after lifting the panel free. Do not let its weight pull on them.

notes: The final release is upward and outward; pulling the whole panel straight away does not follow the specified removal sequence.

verification.title: Confirm connections and seating
verification.body: Confirm the latch cable and fitted electrical connectors are reattached, the upper panel mounting is engaged, and the clips and pin-type retainers are seated.

verification.title: Confirm fastener installation
verification.body: Check that the upper and center bolts received their specified torque and the lower retainers received their separate lower torque. Confirm transferred parts, the switch and the fastening cover are installed.

procedures.purpose: Front door trim-panel removal and installation, including staged clip release, connections and fastener torques.
Remove and reinstall the front door window control switch during trim-panel access.

applicability.equipment: Either front door; left-hand-drive arrangement illustrated, with right-hand drive similar.

guides.title: Remove or replace the coupe headliner and transfer its wiring
guides.summary: Release the roof trim and electrical connections, remove the headliner with a helper, and transfer the harness when installing a new panel.
guides.introduction: The headliner forms the finished cabin surface beneath the roof and carries wiring attached along its upper side. Removing it involves the sun visors, surrounding pillar and quarter trim, electrical connections and front-seat clearance. When fitting a new headliner, the existing harness must be transferred with its routing and connector reach preserved.
guides.why: The harness has to reach the body and roof connectors after the panel is installed. Marking its exit points before removal preserves that relationship. Bonding it along the original attachment locations also helps prevent noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) concerns. The large panel needs controlled handling: the removal illustration calls for two people.

when.summary: When the coupe headliner must be removed for access or replaced.
notes: Harness transfer and adhesive work apply only when installing a new headliner.
The procedure illustrates left-hand drive; right-hand drive is similar. Perform the specified operations on both sides.

prepare.title: Arrange a helper and working space
prepare.detail: Plan for two-person panel removal and space to support the original and replacement headliners while transferring wiring.

prepare.title: Prepare trim access
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools and the linked A-pillar and rear quarter trim procedures available. Several electrical connectors are equipment-dependent.

prepare.title: Prepare harness-transfer materials
prepare.detail: For a new headliner, obtain tape, a marking tool, tools for carefully trimming excess adhesive, and 3M™ Super Fast Repair Adhesive 04747. The required amount depends on the headliner and optional harnesses; multiple tubes may be needed.

steps.title: Remove both sun visors
steps.body: On each side, remove the retainer cap, release the retainer and remove the visor. Disconnect its electrical connector if equipped. This frees the visor attachments before the surrounding trim is removed.

steps.title: Release the front trim and connections
steps.body: Remove both [A-pillar trim panels](#/document/G1692599). Detach the wiring-harness and electrical-connector retainers, then disconnect the electrical connector. Remove each sun-visor clip and its retainer. Disconnect the rear-view mirror connector if equipped.

steps.title: Release the rear surrounding trim
steps.body: On both sides, release the D-pillar trim clips, disconnect the tether clip and remove the panel. Then remove both [rear quarter trim panels](#/document/G1692603). Account for the tether connection as well as the ordinary clips.

steps.title: Create clearance and remove the headliner
steps.body: Remove both front-seat head restraints and move both front seats fully forward and fully reclined. With a helper, remove the headliner following the [headliner procedure](#/document/G1692615). Its illustration shows two-person handling through a side door opening.

steps.title: Capture the original harness layout
steps.body: For a new headliner only, use tape to mark the harness at its exit points so the connector lengths are preserved. Carefully remove the harness from the original panel. Mark the original routing and exit positions onto the new headliner.

steps.title: Prepare and position the transferred harness
steps.body: Carefully cut away excess adhesive without damaging the wiring. Place the harness on the new panel along the marked route, leaving enough length to reach the body and roof connectors at the taped positions. Temporarily secure it with tape.

steps.title: Bond the harness along its original attachment path
steps.body: Apply 3M™ Super Fast Repair Adhesive 04747 at the corresponding factory adhesive locations along the full harness-to-headliner length. This restores the supported routing and addresses the procedure's NVH precaution. Transfer other parts as necessary.

steps.title: Reinstall the headliner and interior components
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, restoring the headliner, seat head restraints, surrounding trim, tether clips, visor fittings and applicable electrical connections. Keep the transferred harness exits positioned to reach their intended connectors.

watchFor.title: Harness damage while cutting adhesive
watchFor.body: The procedure specifically warns against damaging the harness during adhesive removal. Keep the cutting operation controlled around the wiring.

watchFor.title: Lost connector reach
watchFor.body: A harness can follow the general roof shape yet leave a connector too short. Preserve the marked exit points and free lengths.

watchFor.title: Incomplete harness bonding
watchFor.body: Restore the factory adhesive locations along the full attachment length to avoid the identified NVH concern.

notes: For refitting the original headliner, omit the new-component harness-transfer steps.
Use the specified adhesive; the procedure provides no substitute or curing interval.

verification.title: Check the transferred harness before installation
verification.body: Confirm that routing and exits match the original layout, connector lengths reach the marked positions, and bonding follows the factory attachment locations.

verification.title: Check completed reassembly
verification.body: Confirm restoration of trim clips and tethers, visor retainers, head restraints, wiring retainers and all applicable visor, mirror and roof/body connections.

procedures.purpose: Headliner removal and installation, including seat clearance, two-person handling and new-panel wiring transfer.
Coupe A-pillar trim removal and installation on both sides for headliner access.
Rear quarter trim removal and installation on both sides for headliner access.

guides.title: Remove and refit the coupe loadspace trim panel
guides.summary: Remove the surrounding trim and rear seat cushion to release the coupe’s loadspace side panel, then restore its clips and safety-belt routing.
guides.introduction: The loadspace trim panel forms the finished interior surface beside the coupe’s rear seating and loadspace. Clips hold it against the body, while the surrounding trim and safety-belt guide affect how it comes away. This job removes the panel for replacement or access behind it, then restores the interior with the belts correctly positioned.
guides.why: The panel needs to be released in sequence because the scuff plate, seat cushion and belt guide are involved in gaining access. Pulling the panel before releasing these items can load its attachments unnecessarily. During refitting, belt routing deserves particular attention: a seated panel is not a finished repair if it leaves twisted webbing or inaccessible buckles.

when.summary: When the coupe’s loadspace side trim needs replacement or removal for access.
notes: The illustrated procedure shows a left-hand-drive vehicle and the right-hand panel; the opposite configurations are similar.

prepare.title: Plan the adjoining seat work
prepare.detail: Have the rear seat cushion removal and installation procedure available. Cushion removal is a required access step.

prepare.title: Identify the panel attachments
prepare.detail: Review the illustrated clip locations and belt-guide relationship before releasing the panel. The work requires controlled handling of clipped interior trim.

steps.title: Clear the doorway trim
steps.body: Following the [panel procedure](#/document/G1692601), position the door weatherstrip aside. Release the clips and remove the scuff plate trim panel to clear the adjoining trim.

steps.title: Open access beside the rear seat
steps.body: Remove the rear seat cushion using the [rear seat cushion procedure](#/document/G1692168). Then release the backrest latch and lower the backrest, following the stated access sequence.

steps.title: Release the loadspace panel
steps.body: Position the safety-belt guide aside, release the panel clips and remove the loadspace trim panel. Use the illustration to locate the attachments rather than treating the whole panel as a single pull-off piece.

steps.title: Refit in reverse order
steps.body: Install the panel and return the belt guide, backrest, cushion, scuff plate and weatherstrip in the reverse sequence. As the trim goes back, make sure the belt webbing remains untwisted and the belts and buckles remain accessible to occupants.

watchFor.title: Belt webbing caught by the refitted trim
watchFor.body: Check belt routing while positioning the panel, before the surrounding parts conceal the area.

notes: Use the same overall sequence for the opposite side while following that side’s actual clip and belt-guide positions.

verification.title: Interior restored
verification.body: Confirm the panel and scuff plate clips are engaged, the weatherstrip is restored and the rear seat components are refitted.

verification.title: Belts ready for occupants
verification.body: Confirm the safety-belt webbing is not twisted and every affected belt and buckle is accessible.

procedures.purpose: Coupe loadspace trim panel removal and installation, including clip locations and belt-routing precautions.
Required rear seat cushion removal and subsequent installation.

guides.title: Remove and refit the coupe parcel shelf
guides.summary: Release the surrounding rear trim on both sides before removing the parcel shelf and restoring the safety-belt routing.
guides.introduction: The coupe parcel shelf forms the interior trim surface behind the rear seat. Its removal involves the adjoining loadspace and D-pillar trim because those panels must come away first. The work is mainly a sequence of clip, tether and pin-retainer releases, followed by careful reassembly around the rear safety belts.
guides.why: Following the trim sequence exposes each attachment before its panel is removed. The D-pillar tether remains connected after the ordinary clips release, while the loadspace trim surrounds the safety-belt routing. Both details matter when freeing the panels and restoring a usable rear seating area.

when.summary: When the coupe parcel shelf needs replacement or must be removed to reach the area beneath it.
notes: The access sequence applies to both sides of the rear interior.

prepare.title: Arrange rear-seat access
prepare.detail: Be ready to remove the rear seat cushion using the procedure referenced in the loadspace-trim instructions and to lower the backrest.

prepare.title: Identify the attachments
prepare.detail: Allow access to the weatherstrips, scuff plates, belt guides, trim clips and D-pillar tether connections before starting.

steps.title: Open the lower trim access
steps.body: On both sides, position the door weatherstrip aside and release the scuff-plate clips to remove the trim. Remove the rear seat cushion through its referenced procedure, then release the backrest latch and lower the backrest.

steps.title: Remove the adjoining side panels
steps.body: Position each safety-belt guide aside, release the loadspace-panel clips and remove the panels. Next release the D-pillar trim clips, disconnect each tether clip and remove the D-pillar panels. Complete both sides before proceeding.

steps.title: Lift out the parcel shelf
steps.body: Remove the shelf's pin-type retainers and then remove the parcel shelf. The surrounding trim has now been cleared in the required order, leaving the shelf free of the attachments identified by this procedure.

steps.title: Restore the shelf and surrounding trim
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, beginning with the shelf and its retainers. Reconnect the D-pillar tethers and clips, then reinstall the loadspace trim and remaining access parts. Keep the safety-belt webbing untwisted and leave belts and buckles accessible to occupants.

watchFor.title: A tether still connected
watchFor.body: Release the D-pillar tether separately before taking the panel away.

watchFor.title: Belt webbing caught during refitting
watchFor.body: Check belt routing as the loadspace panels return to position, before completing the surrounding trim.

notes: Right-side illustrations also guide the similar left-side work; the loadspace procedure likewise describes similar left- and right-hand-drive arrangements.
The illustration shows the prerequisite loadspace-panel removal and adjacent belt routing.

verification.title: Confirm trim retention
verification.body: Check that the shelf retainers, D-pillar tethers and released trim clips have all been restored.

verification.title: Confirm occupant access
verification.body: Verify that safety-belt webbing is untwisted and that occupants can reach the belts and buckles.

procedures.purpose: Coupe parcel shelf removal and installation, including both D-pillar panels.
Prerequisite coupe loadspace-trim removal and refitting with correct safety-belt routing.

guides.title: Remove and refit the coupe rear quarter trim panel
guides.summary: Release the surrounding trim, seatbelt guide and garment hook to remove the rear quarter panel trim and restore it correctly.
guides.introduction: The rear quarter trim finishes the interior beside the rear seating area. Removing it provides access behind the panel or allows a damaged panel to be replaced. The access sequence also involves the C-pillar trim and the seatbelt's upper D-ring guide, so the job includes more than releasing the visible panel clips.
guides.why: Several different attachments hold the surrounding parts: clips, a tether, cover tabs, a garment-hook retainer and the seatbelt guide bolt. Releasing them in order prevents an overlooked attachment from resisting removal. During refitting, correct belt routing matters as much as the appearance of the trim.

when.summary: When the rear quarter trim needs replacement or must be removed for access behind it.
notes: This sequence begins with the coupe loadspace-trim procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim and belt-guide work
prepare.detail: Have suitable hand tools for the retainers and D-ring bolt, plus a torque wrench for reinstalling the seatbelt guide. Keep the covers and retainers identified for refitting.

prepare.title: Use the correct access sequence
prepare.detail: Review the loadspace-trim removal procedure before starting; that panel is removed before the C-pillar trim.

steps.title: Remove the surrounding upper trim
steps.body: Remove the [coupe loadspace trim](#/document/G1692601). Release the C-pillar trim clips, disconnect its tether clip and remove the C-pillar panel. The tether is a separate attachment and must be released before the panel is removed.

steps.title: Move the seatbelt guide aside
steps.body: Release the tabs and remove the D-ring retainer cover. Remove the D-ring bolt and position the seatbelt aside, keeping track of its routing for reassembly.

steps.title: Release the quarter trim
steps.body: Open the garment-hook retainer cover. Remove the retainer and garment hook, then release the rear quarter panel clips and remove the trim. Follow the [complete trim procedure](#/document/G1692603) for this attachment sequence.

steps.title: Refit in reverse order
steps.body: Reinstall the quarter trim and garment hook, then restore the seatbelt guide. Tighten its bolt to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm) and refit the cover. Reconnect the C-pillar tether and clips, and restore the loadspace trim.

watchFor.title: Twisted or concealed belt webbing
watchFor.body: During installation, make sure the webbing is not twisted and that the belts and buckles remain accessible to occupants.

notes: The illustrated left-hand-drive, right-side sequence applies similarly to right-hand-drive vehicles and the opposite side.

verification.title: Check the trim attachments
verification.body: Confirm the clips, tether, garment hook and covers have all been restored.

verification.title: Check restraint access
verification.body: Confirm the D-ring bolt is tightened and the seatbelt webbing lies untwisted, with belts and buckles accessible from the seats.

procedures.purpose: Rear quarter trim removal and installation, including C-pillar trim, garment hook and seatbelt guide.
Coupe loadspace-trim removal and installation for initial access.

guides.title: Remove and refit the steering-column shrouds
guides.summary: Move the gap trim aside, turn the steering wheel to reach the upper-cover tabs, then release the side clips and remove the screw-fastened lower cover.
guides.introduction: Steering-column covers have a talent for making one small plastic tab feel like the strongest part of the car. I'll walk you through their release sequence so the trim can come away without a wrestling match. The upper and lower shrouds form the plastic enclosure around the column; the separate upper gap hider closes the space between that enclosure and the dashboard.
guides.why: The upper cover is retained by tabs and outer clips, while two screws secure the lower cover. Turning the steering wheel exposes the upper-cover tabs in sequence. Releasing each attachment before moving the cover keeps the job controlled and helps avoid damaging the trim.

when.summary: Use this procedure when replacing the steering-column covers or removing them for access to a separate repair.
notes: Applies to the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
The illustrated arrangement is left-hand drive; right-hand drive follows a similar procedure.
The steering wheel stays installed and is rotated to expose the cover tabs.

prepare.title: Gather the release tools
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover for the upper gap hider and a flat-bladed screwdriver for the wheel-accessed shroud tabs. You will also need a driver that fits the lower-cover screw heads.

prepare.title: Allow room for column and wheel movement
prepare.detail: The column must move fully outward and downward, and the wheel must turn through the two access positions. Keep the working area clear so you can reach the tabs behind the wheel.

prepare.title: Keep the work within the trim enclosure
prepare.detail: This procedure ends with removal and refitting of the covers and gap hider. Work on components exposed underneath requires its own procedure. No tightening torque is given for the lower-cover screws; do not substitute a steering-wheel or steering-column fastener torque.

steps.title: Fully extend and lower the steering column
steps.body: Use the column-adjustment lever underneath the column to move the steering wheel fully outward toward you and lower the column fully. Secure the adjustment before working on the covers. This creates the clearance needed around the upper shroud.

steps.title: Release the upper gap hider and position it aside
steps.body:
Find the gap-hiding trim immediately behind the upper column cover, beneath the instrument cluster. Use the interior trim remover to release the tabs along its connection to the upper shroud.
Work along the attachment edge until the tabs are free, then disconnect the gap hider from the shroud and position it aside. It remains separate from the upper cover during the next operations.

steps.title: Turn the wheel 90 degrees and release the first upper-cover tab
steps.body:
Rotate the steering wheel 90 degrees from its starting position. This exposes one of the upper-shroud retaining tabs behind the wheel, beside the steering-wheel hub.
Use the flat-bladed screwdriver at the exposed tab to release it. Direct the tool at the retaining tab rather than using the visible cover edge as a lever. The tab must disengage before the cover can lift away.

steps.title: Turn the wheel another 180 degrees and release the opposite tab
steps.body:
From the first access position, rotate the wheel 180 degrees to expose the tab on the opposite side. This is a half-turn between the two access positions.
Release this second tab with the flat-bladed screwdriver. I treat these as two separate stops: exposing one tab does not release its partner.

steps.title: Release both outer sides and lift off the upper shroud
steps.body:
Release the outer clips on each side of the upper cover. Once the wheel-accessed tabs and both outer sides are free, lift the upper shroud away from the column, clearing the stalk openings as it comes off.
If it remains attached, stop lifting and find the retainer that is still engaged. A stubborn clip is a reason to revisit the release points, not recruit a bigger screwdriver.

steps.title: Remove the two lower-cover screws and the lower shroud
steps.body:
Look underneath the column for the two lower-shroud screws. The underside view identifies two separated screw positions in the lower cover.
Support the cover, remove both screws and retain them for refitting. Remove the lower shroud from around the column. Keep the screws with the lower cover so its fasteners are ready for reassembly.

steps.title: Refit the lower shroud and its screws
steps.body:
Installation follows the reverse of removal, as described in the [steering-column shroud procedure](#/document/G1692617).
Position the lower cover around the column and align its two screw locations. Reinstall the two screws with the cover correctly seated. If a screw will not start properly, reposition the cover and check alignment before continuing.

steps.title: Refit the upper shroud and engage its retainers
steps.body:
Lower the upper cover into position around the column and its stalk openings. Align and engage the outer clips on both sides, then engage the retaining tabs released through the two steering-wheel access positions. Turn the wheel as needed to reach those positions.
Check the cover joint as you work: both sides should be seated, with no edge held up by a tab or clip resting outside its mating location.

steps.title: Reconnect the gap hider and restore the driving position
steps.body:
Bring the upper gap hider back to the upper shroud. Align its attachment tabs and reconnect them along the edge, checking that the whole connection is seated.
Return the steering wheel to its starting orientation. Set the column to your driving position and secure its adjustment. Check that the refitted trim clears the stalks and adjustment lever. That's the plastic jacket back together; give every attachment one final look before calling it done.

watchFor.title: An upper cover that still feels anchored
watchFor.body: Do not force the cover upward. Check both wheel-accessed tabs and the outer clips on each side; any one of them can keep it attached.

watchFor.title: A gap hider mistaken for part of the cover
watchFor.body: Disconnect the gap hider and position it aside before removing the upper shroud. Reconnect it only after the shrouds are installed.

watchFor.title: A raised edge during refitting
watchFor.body: Check the adjacent tab or clip and its mating location. Reposition the cover so the retainer engages correctly rather than pressing harder on an unsupported edge.

notes: The gap-hider connection and upper shroud use mechanical tabs and clips. No electrical connector disconnection is included in this procedure.
These instructions cover trim removal and installation; they do not establish a diagnosis for steering noises, looseness or electrical faults.

diagnostics.finding: The upper cover will not lift after the gap hider is moved aside.
diagnostics.meaning: One or more upper-cover retainers may still be engaged.
diagnostics.next: Revisit the tab exposed at the 90-degree wheel position, the opposite tab reached by the following 180-degree turn, and the outer clips on both sides. Continue removal only after those attachments release.

diagnostics.finding: The lower cover remains attached after one screw is removed.
diagnostics.meaning: There are two lower-cover screw positions to release.
diagnostics.next: Locate and remove the second screw while supporting the cover, then remove the lower shroud.

diagnostics.finding: A cover edge or the gap-hider connection remains unseated after installation.
diagnostics.meaning: The local attachment has not engaged correctly.
diagnostics.next: Check the tab or clip at that location, realign the parts and engage the attachment. Confirm the edge is seated before completing the job.

verification.title: Account for the lower-cover fasteners
verification.body: Confirm both lower-shroud screws are installed and the lower cover is seated.

verification.title: Check the upper-cover attachments
verification.body: Confirm the two wheel-accessed tabs and the outer clips on both sides are engaged. Look along the cover joint for an unseated edge.

verification.title: Check the gap trim and adjustment
verification.body: Confirm the gap hider is connected along its attachment edge, the trim clears the stalks and adjustment lever, and the column adjustment is secured in the chosen driving position. These are reassembly checks, not a steering-system diagnostic test.

procedures.purpose: Column positioning, gap-hider detachment, wheel-accessed tab release, upper-cover clip release, lower-cover screw removal and reverse-order installation.

applicability.equipment: Left-hand-drive or right-hand-drive steering layout; illustrations show left-hand drive.

stepGroups.title: Create clearance and release the gap trim
stepGroups.summary: Position the column and move the upper gap hider aside.

stepGroups.title: Release and remove both covers
stepGroups.summary: Use the wheel positions to reach the tabs, release the outer clips and remove the lower-cover screws.

stepGroups.title: Reassemble the trim enclosure
stepGroups.summary: Refit the lower and upper shrouds, reconnect the gap hider and restore the column position.

guides.title: Remove and refit the front door upper moulding
guides.summary: Lower the glass, remove the exterior triangular sail panel and expose the end fasteners before releasing the moulding’s tabs and sliding it rearward off the door.
guides.introduction: One little screw might look like the boss of this trim strip, but the retaining tabs have formed a committee. I’ll take you through releasing the whole lot without turning a straightforward trim job into an expensive snapping noise. This procedure applies to the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
guides.why: The upper moulding finishes the top edge of the door beside the glass. A rear screw, a pin-type retainer and tabs distributed along its length hold it in place. Removing the end fasteners only starts the job: the tabs must also disengage before the strip can slide off.

when.summary: Use this procedure when replacing the upper door moulding or removing it for another established repair.
notes: The left-hand door is illustrated; the right-hand door uses a similar procedure.
The rear weatherstrip access is illustrated; move the front weatherstrip aside in the same manner.
This is a removal and refitting procedure, not a test for wind noise or water leaks.

prepare.title: Gather the trim and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have a trim-removal tool like the flat tool illustrated for the sail panel, a driver that fits the rear screw and a place to keep the screw and pin-type retainer together.

prepare.title: Identify the parts before pulling
prepare.detail: The sail panel is the small triangular exterior panel on the outside of the door beside the mirror. The upper moulding is the long strip along the door’s upper edge. Weatherstrip at each end covers the fastener access.

prepare.title: Keep the fastening limits in mind
prepare.detail: No tightening torque is given for the rear moulding screw. Refit it carefully without overtightening. The tab illustrations show where the strip attaches, but do not establish a special tool or precise levering motion for releasing each tab.

steps.title: Lower the door glass
steps.body: Put the door glass in the down position before starting removal. Keep it down while removing and refitting the moulding.

steps.title: Remove the exterior triangular sail panel
steps.body: From outside the door, locate the small triangular sail panel beside the exterior mirror. Use the illustrated flat trim-removal tool to ease the panel away from the door at its edge beside the mirror. Release the panel attachment and remove the panel from the working area. This clears the front end of the moulding’s removal path.

steps.title: Move the weatherstrip aside at both ends
steps.body: At the front and rear of the door, move the weatherstrip aside far enough to uncover the moulding fasteners. The illustration shows the end section displaced locally; leave the rest in place. Keep both fastener locations exposed.

steps.title: Remove the rear screw
steps.body: Find the screw at the rear end of the upper moulding, beneath the weatherstrip you have moved aside. Remove it with a correctly fitting driver and keep it for refitting. The strip will still be attached after this screw comes out.

steps.title: Remove the pin-type retainer
steps.body: Locate the separate pin-type retainer at the other end of the moulding. The illustration identifies it by its broad head and ribbed shank. Carefully withdraw it from its mounting hole and keep it with the screw. This is a separate attachment; removing the screw does not release it.

steps.title: Disengage the tabs along the moulding
steps.body:
Carefully release the moulding’s retaining tabs from the door along the full length of the strip. Work through the attachment points along the door’s upper edge rather than pulling the whole strip from one end.

Use care: damaging the tabs or bending the moulding can spoil its retention. If an area remains held, stop pulling and check that attachment point. I’d much rather spend another minute finding a stubborn tab than let the trim announce its retirement with a crack.

steps.title: Slide the released moulding rearward and remove it
steps.body: Once the tabs are disengaged, slide the moulding toward the rear of the car, past the sail-panel area, and remove it from the door. Rearward sliding is a separate action after tab release; do not use that sliding force to drag engaged tabs out of the door.

steps.title: Slide the moulding back into position
steps.body: For installation, reverse the removal movement. With the sail panel still removed, the weatherstrip aside and the glass down, place the moulding at the upper door edge and slide it forward into its installed position. Align its ends and tab locations with the door before engaging the attachments.

steps.title: Engage the tabs along the full length
steps.body: Carefully engage the moulding’s tabs with the door along the strip. Check each attachment area as you go so the moulding sits in position throughout its length. Do not use the end screw to pull a misaligned strip into place.

steps.title: Restore the pin-type retainer and rear screw
steps.body: Reinstall the pin-type retainer in its original hole, then reinstall the screw at the rear of the moulding. This reverses their removal order. Confirm that the retainer is seated and the screw secures the rear end.

steps.title: Return the weatherstrip and exterior sail panel
steps.body: Return the front and rear weatherstrip sections to their original fitted positions. Then position the triangular exterior sail panel beside the mirror, align its attachment and seat it back against the outside of the door. The trim should now be back where it belongs, with the small fasteners accounted for rather than auditioning for a life inside the door.

watchFor.title: Damage while releasing the tabs
watchFor.body: The moulding can be damaged during tab disengagement. Stop if a section remains attached; locate and release that attachment before moving the strip farther.

watchFor.title: A fastener still hidden by weatherstrip
watchFor.body: Expose both ends before trying to release the moulding. A covered screw or pin-type retainer can make an attached strip feel like it merely needs a harder pull.

watchFor.title: Using the screw to correct alignment
watchFor.body: Seat the moulding and engage its tabs before restoring the end fasteners. If the rear screw location does not align, reposition the strip instead of tightening the screw to draw it into place.

notes: The complete removal and reverse-order installation sequence is linked in the [front door upper moulding procedure](#/document/G1697166).

diagnostics.finding: The moulding remains attached after the rear screw is removed.
diagnostics.meaning: The pin-type retainer and the tabs along the moulding are separate attachments that still require release.
diagnostics.next: Remove the pin-type retainer, then carefully disengage the tabs along the entire strip before attempting the rearward slide.

diagnostics.finding: One section remains held while the rest of the moulding has released.
diagnostics.meaning: An attachment at that section may still be engaged.
diagnostics.next: Stop pulling the strip. Check that section and the end fasteners, release the remaining attachment, and only then continue removal.

verification.title: Check the installed moulding
verification.body: Confirm that the strip is positioned along the upper door edge and that its tabs are engaged throughout its length. Gently check for an unsecured section without prying the moulding back off.

verification.title: Account for both end fasteners
verification.body: Confirm that the pin-type retainer is seated and the rear screw has been reinstalled.

verification.title: Check the surrounding trim
verification.body: Confirm that both weatherstrip sections are back in their fitted positions and that the exterior sail panel is seated beside the mirror. These are reassembly checks, not a diagnosis of sealing or window operation.

procedures.purpose: Front door upper moulding removal and installation, including exterior sail-panel access, weatherstrip positioning, end fasteners and lengthwise retaining tabs.

stepGroups.title: Prepare the door and expose the fasteners
stepGroups.summary: Lower the glass, remove the exterior sail panel and move the end weatherstrips aside.

stepGroups.title: Release and remove the moulding
stepGroups.summary: Remove both end fasteners, disengage the tabs and slide the strip rearward.

stepGroups.title: Refit the moulding and surrounding trim
stepGroups.summary: Slide the strip into position, restore its attachments and reseat the weatherstrip and exterior sail panel.

guides.title: Remove or replace the luggage compartment lid moulding
guides.summary: Release the rear exterior trim correctly, restore its bracket engagement and configure the rear camera if fitting a new moulding.
guides.introduction: The luggage compartment lid moulding is the exterior finish panel across the rear of the lid. Screws, W-clips, molded clips and an attachment bracket retain it. Removing the panel also involves disconnecting the rear camera, so fitting a replacement includes an electronic configuration step as well as trim work.
guides.why: The different fasteners need different release actions. Pulling on the panel before releasing them risks damage. During installation, the moulding must engage its bracket before the W-clips latch, ensuring that the panel is located correctly rather than merely held by its clips.
searchTerms: rear camera initialization after moulding replacement

when.summary: When the exterior lid moulding needs removal or replacement; a new moulding also requires camera configuration.

prepare.title: Prepare trim and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have a non-marring trim removal tool, suitable screw tools and a torque wrench capable of the specified low tightening values.

prepare.title: Arrange camera configuration when replacing
prepare.detail: For a new moulding, have a scan tool offering the LIN New Module Initialization service function. LIN means local interconnect network.

steps.title: Expose the fixings and disconnect the camera
steps.body: Follow the [moulding removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1687579). Remove the inner luggage compartment lid trim panel and disconnect the rear parking aid camera electrical connector. Remove the exterior moulding's screw covers and screws.

steps.title: Release each type of clip
steps.body: Disengage the W-clips with the non-marring trim tool, then depress the molded clips to release them. Remove the moulding only after those attachments are disengaged; the molded clips have a separate release action.

steps.title: Handle the bracket only if required
steps.body: If the attachment bracket also needs removal, remove its screws and lift it away. During refitting, tighten those bracket screws to 28 lb.in (3.2 Nm). Bracket removal is conditional, rather than an automatic part of every moulding job.

steps.title: Refit the panel and complete the camera branch
steps.body: Engage the moulding with the lid bracket before engaging the W-clips, then reverse the remaining removal operations. Tighten the moulding screws to 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm), restore covers, camera connection and inner trim. If installing a new moulding, follow the scan-tool instructions at Electrical> Service Functions>LIN New Module Initialization to configure the rear video camera.

watchFor.title: Clips engaging too early
watchFor.body: W-clips must not engage before the moulding is located on the lid bracket.

watchFor.title: Confusing the screw specifications
watchFor.body: The attachment bracket and moulding screws use different tightening values; keep their installation requirements separate.

notes: The camera configuration requirement applies when a new moulding is installed.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical reassembly
verification.body: Check bracket engagement, restored clips, tightened screws, fitted covers and the reconnected camera connector.

verification.title: Record the replacement and configuration result
verification.body: Record whether the original moulding was reused or replaced. For a new moulding, record successful completion of the scan-tool camera configuration.

procedures.purpose: Moulding removal and installation, optional bracket removal and rear-camera configuration for a new moulding.

guides.title: Remove and Refit the Rear Spoiler
guides.summary: Remove the rear spoiler, clean its mounting surface and restore its nut and double-sided tape attachments.
guides.introduction: The rear spoiler shapes airflow over the rear of the car and attaches to the luggage-compartment lid through both threaded fasteners and double-sided adhesive tape. This job releases both attachments, prepares the lid surface and reinstalls the spoiler with the specified tightening and bonding pressure.
guides.why: Removing the nuts does not release the tape bond. During installation, a clean surface allows the tape to contact the lid properly, while the specified pressure establishes adhesion along the spoiler's length. Nut tightening and tape bonding are separate parts of securing the assembly.

when.summary: When the rear spoiler requires replacement or removal for luggage-compartment lid work.

prepare.title: Prepare for interior access
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the luggage-compartment lid trim, rubber grommets and spoiler nuts, plus a torque wrench capable of the specified low tightening value.

prepare.title: Plan the adhesive attachment
prepare.detail: Allow for cleaning residual adhesive and dirt from the lid, and for restoring the double-sided tape attachment during installation.

steps.title: Expose the spoiler fasteners
steps.body: Remove the luggage-compartment lid trim panel, then remove the rubber grommets. This opens access to the spoiler's retaining nuts without disturbing the external attachment first.

steps.title: Remove the nuts and release the spoiler
steps.body: Remove the retaining nuts. Lift the spoiler to detach its double-sided tape from the lid. Expect the adhesive to continue holding the spoiler after the threaded fasteners have been removed.

steps.title: Clean the mounting surface
steps.body: Remove residual adhesive and dirt from the luggage-compartment lid. Complete this preparation before positioning the spoiler so residue does not interfere with contact between the tape and lid.

steps.title: Restore both attachments
steps.body: Refit the spoiler with its double-sided tape attachment in place. Apply approximately 15 lbs. of pressure along its length to ensure adhesion. Install the retaining nuts and tighten them to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm), then reinstall the rubber grommets and lid trim panel.

watchFor.title: Incomplete tape adhesion
watchFor.body: Secured nuts alone do not establish that the adhesive has bonded along the spoiler.

watchFor.title: Overlooking the installation torque
watchFor.body: Use the specified low nut torque when reversing the removal sequence.

notes: The procedure illustrates a single-wing spoiler; other spoiler styles are described as similar.

verification.title: Confirm attachment and access restoration
verification.body: Confirm that the prescribed pressure was applied along the spoiler, the tape adhered, the nuts were tightened to specification, and all grommets and trim were reinstalled.

procedures.purpose: Rear spoiler removal, mounting-surface cleaning and installation with specified torque and bonding pressure.

guides.title: Remove and refit the rocker panel moulding
guides.summary: Move the splash shield aside, remove eight underside pushpins, release eleven body retainers with a rearward movement, then lower the front end to disengage four fender tabs. Refit in reverse order.
guides.introduction: The rocker panel moulding is the long exterior trim beneath the door—the sort of part that can look completely loose while one last attachment quietly ruins your afternoon. It covers and finishes the outside of the sill. I’ll walk you through its separate attachment groups and the movements that release them, so this stays a trim job instead of becoming a tug-of-war.
guides.why: The moulding has several attachment groups that release in sequence. Moving the front splash shield aside opens access, and removing the underside pushpins frees the lower edge. The body retainers release with a rearward movement, starting the work at the rear. Four tabs at the front fender then disengage downward before the moulding comes away.

when.summary: Use this procedure when replacing the rocker panel moulding or removing it for access.
notes: Applies to the 2015 Mustang configurations with 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engines.
The left-hand side is illustrated; the right-hand side uses a similar procedure.
This is a removal and refitting procedure, not a test for determining whether the moulding needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange access to the front wheel arch and underside
prepare.detail: You need to reach the splash shield at the front end of the moulding, the fasteners underneath it and the full length of its outer face. If reaching the underside requires raising the car, use the vehicle-specific lifting and support instructions before beginning; lifting is outside this procedure.

prepare.title: Identify the attachment groups
prepare.detail: Locate three splash-shield pushpins, eight underside pushpins, eleven rocker-panel retainers and four tab retainers at the front fender. Pushpins are separate pin-shaped fasteners; the tabs are attachments that must disengage before the front end can come away. I keep the removed pushpins grouped by location so refitting does not become a small plastic guessing game.

prepare.title: Keep the attachment-direction illustration beside you
prepare.detail: Open the [rocker panel moulding procedure](#/document/G1687581), particularly its third illustration. Arrow 1 points right in the illustrated left-hand view, toward the rear of the car; arrow 2 points downward at the front tabs. These are release movements, distinct from the instruction to begin working at the rear. The stripped-body illustrations do not establish a requirement to remove the door or wheels.

steps.title: Release the splash-shield edge
steps.body: At the front end of the moulding, locate the three vertically arranged pushpin retainers securing the adjacent splash-shield edge. Remove all three, then move the shield partially aside to expose the working area. Leave the shield partially attached; full shield removal is not part of this job.

steps.title: Remove the eight underside pushpins
steps.body: Locate the row of eight pushpin retainers along the underside of the rocker panel moulding. Remove each one and keep them together for refitting. Check the entire row before moving to the outer face: a pushpin left underneath will still hold the lower edge.

steps.title: Start at the rear and move the moulding rearward to release the body retainers
steps.body:
Use arrow 1 in the third illustration of the [rocker panel moulding procedure](#/document/G1687581) beside this step. Begin releasing the retainers at the rear end, beside the rear wheel opening, and work progressively toward the front.

The release movement is rearward along the car—rightward in the illustrated left-hand view. Shift the moulding in that direction to detach the eleven rocker-panel retainers. Starting at the rear describes where to begin working; it does not mean moving the moulding forward.

Support the freed portion as you continue. The four front fender tabs remain connected until the next step.

steps.title: Lower the front end to disengage the four fender tabs, then remove the moulding
steps.body:
With the rocker-panel retainers detached, support the moulding and move its front end downward to disengage the four tab retainers at the fender. This is arrow 2 in the third illustration of the [rocker panel moulding procedure](#/document/G1687581), following the rearward movement shown by arrow 1. Once the tabs are free, remove the moulding from the car.

If the front end remains held, stop and check those four tabs before taking the strip away. One stubborn attachment does not need the help of the entire moulding acting as a lever.

steps.title: Position the moulding and lift the front tabs into engagement
steps.body: Installation reverses the removal movements. Bring the moulding into position beneath the door opening, supporting its full length. Align the four front tab retainers with their fender attachment locations, then lift the front end upward to engage them—the reverse of downward arrow 2 in the third illustration of the [rocker panel moulding procedure](#/document/G1687581). Keep the remaining length supported while restoring the body retainers.

steps.title: Move the moulding forward to restore the eleven body retainers
steps.body:
Align the eleven rocker-panel retainers with their body attachment locations. Move the moulding forward along the car—leftward in the illustrated left-hand view—to engage them. This reverses the rearward movement of arrow 1 in the third illustration of the [rocker panel moulding procedure](#/document/G1687581).

Check the attachment locations progressively back toward the rear, reversing the removal working order. Confirm that each is engaged before installing the underside pushpins; those pushpins should not compensate for an unseated body retainer.

steps.title: Reinstall the eight underside pushpins
steps.body: Align the lower attachment locations and reinstall all eight underside pushpin retainers. Work along the complete row so no position is missed.

steps.title: Return the splash shield and secure its three pushpins
steps.body: Return the partially displaced splash shield to its original position at the front end of the moulding. Align its three attachment locations and reinstall the three pushpin retainers. Finish by checking both ends of the moulding and every attachment group listed below.

watchFor.title: Working order and release direction are different
watchFor.body: Begin releasing the body retainers at the rear and work toward the front, while moving the moulding rearward along the car. Afterward, move the front end downward to disengage the fender tabs. The third illustration’s arrows show these two movements.

watchFor.title: Different attachments need separate release steps
watchFor.body: The underside pushpins, rocker-panel retainers and front fender tabs are separate connections. A loose outer edge does not establish that the underside or front end is free.

watchFor.title: The shield only needs to move partially aside
watchFor.body: Remove its three specified pushpins and move the edge aside for access. Keep this step limited to the required opening.

notes: The attachment counts are three splash-shield pushpins, eight underside pushpins, eleven rocker-panel retainers and four front fender tabs.
Keep the splash-shield pushpins and underside pushpins associated with their original locations.

On the right-hand side, use the same vehicle-relative movements: rearward and then downward for removal; upward and then forward for installation. Screen-left and screen-right descriptions refer only to the illustrated left-hand view.

diagnostics.finding: The moulding remains attached along its lower edge while releasing the body retainers.
diagnostics.meaning: An underside pushpin may still be engaged; released body retainers alone do not free the lower edge.
diagnostics.next: Pause and recheck all eight underside pushpin positions. Remove any remaining pushpin before continuing the body-retainer release, starting at the rear and shifting the moulding rearward.

diagnostics.finding: The body-retainer row is detached, but the front end remains connected.
diagnostics.meaning: The four fender tab retainers are a separate attachment group and may still be engaged.
diagnostics.next: Support the moulding and move its front end downward as shown by arrow 2. Check that all four tabs have disengaged before removing the moulding.

diagnostics.finding: A body attachment location remains visibly unseated during refitting.
diagnostics.meaning: That retainer has not completed its engagement; installing the underside pushpins does not resolve it.
diagnostics.next: Keep the moulding supported, recheck alignment at that location and complete the forward engagement movement before reinstalling the underside pushpins.

verification.title: Account for every moulding attachment
verification.body: Confirm that all four front fender tabs and all eleven rocker-panel retainers are engaged, and that the eight underside pushpins are installed. These are refitting checks, not a separate diagnostic test.

verification.title: Check the moulding position
verification.body: Look along the moulding beneath the door opening and check both ends. Confirm that it is seated at its attachment locations, with no section left visibly detached.

verification.title: Confirm splash-shield restoration
verification.body: Check that the splash shield has returned to its original position and all three removed pushpins are reinstalled.

procedures.purpose: Rocker panel moulding removal and reverse-order installation, including partial splash-shield displacement, attachment counts, rearward body-retainer release and downward front-tab disengagement.

stepGroups.title: Open access and free the underside
stepGroups.summary: Move the splash shield partially aside and remove the eight lower pushpins.

stepGroups.title: Release and remove the moulding
stepGroups.summary: Start at the rear, shift the moulding rearward, then lower the front end to free the fender tabs.

stepGroups.title: Refit and restore the splash shield
stepGroups.summary: Lift the front tabs into place, shift the moulding forward, then restore the underside and splash-shield pushpins.

guides.title: Diagnose power-mirror faults with and without memory
guides.summary: Identify the mirror complaint, then isolate single-mirror movement faults without memory using loaded circuit tests and harness inspection.
guides.introduction: Each exterior mirror uses reversible motors to position the glass. Without memory, the window-control switch supplies motor power and ground through circuits shared by both movement axes. Memory mirrors add door-module control and position feedback. Identifying the fitted system determines which diagnostic path applies.
guides.why: A shared-circuit fault can stop movement in every direction. Loaded tests help distinguish wiring trouble from mirror faults, while careful probing prevents new terminal damage.
searchTerms: one power mirror will not move
mirror moves sideways but not up

when.summary: When mirror movement, heating, mounting or dimming does not behave as expected.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, multimeter, test lamp, Rotunda Flex Probe kit and Wiring Diagrams Cell 124. Never insert the test-lamp probe directly into a connector.

prepare.title: Establish reliable starting conditions
prepare.detail: Confirm battery and charging-system operation and battery state of charge above 70%. Inspect previous repairs, wiring and connectors. Diagnose only while the complaint is present.

steps.title: Identify the complaint and equipment
steps.body: Check both mirrors in every direction and inspect for damage or obstructions. Record diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Separate movement, heating, lighting and mechanical complaints using the symptom chart in [Rear View Mirrors](#/document/G1693886).

steps.title: Use Test A for one completely inoperative non-memory mirror
steps.body: Disconnect the affected mirror with ignition OFF. Switch ON, select that mirror and perform the specified up-command lamp test. Illumination directs inspection of the mirror jumper harness and terminals. If dark, switch OFF, disconnect the window-control switch and test the common circuit: repair a failed circuit; a passing result directs switch replacement.

steps.title: Use Test B for incomplete directional movement
steps.body: First check left/right movement on both mirrors. If both work, follow the up/down branch; otherwise follow the left/right branch. At the prescribed disconnected connector, the lamp must illuminate for both opposite commands and remain off when the switch is released.

steps.title: Trace an incorrect lamp response
steps.body: Follow B3–B5 or B7–B9 in order: test for unwanted voltage, a short to ground, then an open circuit. Preserve each specified ignition state and connector isolation. Repair a failed circuit; passing circuit checks direct replacement of the integrated mirror/window-control switch.

steps.title: Inspect the jumper harness before replacing a motor
steps.body: A correct Test B lamp response leads to B10. Inspect for opens, shorts, corrosion and damaged or pushed-out pins. A sound harness directs motor replacement. Repair harness faults where possible; an irreparable integral harness requires a new mirror assembly.

steps.title: Route memory-mirror faults by side and circuit
steps.body: The driver door module (DDM) controls the left mirror; the passenger door module (PDM) controls the right. Movement, position-feedback and sensor-supply faults go to Test C or D respectively; heater codes go to E. For left memory-mirror complaints, inspect battery junction box fuse 11 (30A). Other door-module codes require locks/latches diagnosis.

watchFor.title: Cleaning and mechanical faults
watchFor.body: Avoid scrapers, abrasives, harsh chemicals and petroleum cleaners. For vibration, distinguish loose housing fasteners from unseated glass, damaged backing plates or loose motor screws. Wind noise calls for checking mirror fit, impact damage and the foam gasket; an irreparable gasket requires mirror replacement.

watchFor.title: Equipment-specific behavior
watchFor.body: Use power-folding branches only when fitted: synchronize before investigating continued folding or housing instability. Unequal folding speeds and unequal mirror defrost rates can be normal. If removable aftermarket deflectors are suspected, remove them and road-test.

watchFor.title: Interior mirror complaints
watchFor.body: Clean blemishes first. For looseness, try fully seating the attached mirror before removal/reinstallation; replace it if the problem remains. Auto-dimming complaints go to Test H.

notes: A failed mirror-selection indicator with normal selection operation directs replacement of the front door window-control switch.

diagnostics.finding: Both exterior mirrors are inoperative.
diagnostics.meaning: The symptom chart first checks whether the driver's window-control switch operates all power windows normally.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose abnormal window operation first. With normal windows, replace the driver's window-control switch; on memory-equipped vehicles, a persistent concern then directs DDM replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1C09:11 or B1C09:15 is recorded in the DDM.
diagnostics.meaning: The horizontal motor circuit draws excessive current for B1C09:11 or insufficient current for B1C09:15, indicating a short-to-ground or short-to-battery/open category respectively.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test C to distinguish the cause before selecting a component.

diagnostics.finding: Mirror heating is inoperative or remains on.
diagnostics.meaning: Mirror heat follows rear-window defrost operation, with different control paths according to memory equipment.
diagnostics.next: Use E with memory and F for inoperative heating without memory. Both heaters continuously on without memory require rear-window defrost diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: A mirror-mounted lamp or blind-spot indicator malfunctions.
diagnostics.meaning: These functions have separate diagnostic paths.
diagnostics.next: Route projection lamps to Interior Lighting, turn indicators to Turn Signal and Hazard Lamps, and blind-spot indicators to Blind Spot Information System diagnosis.

verification.title: Repeat the original complaint
verification.body: Check the affected movements, seating or noise condition again. Continue diagnosis if the original fault remains.

verification.title: Record the decision
verification.body: Record fitted equipment, codes, lamp responses, circuit results and the repair or diagnostic handoff they support.
