applicability.equipment: Power mirrors, with or without memory; heated mirrors and an auto-dimming interior mirror where fitted

guides.title: Diagnose mirror heating, power folding and automatic dimming
guides.summary: Separate heater, folding-circuit and automatic-dimming faults using equipment-specific electrical and operating checks.
guides.introduction: Heated mirror glass clears condensation and frost when rear window defrost operates. Memory-equipped mirrors receive heater power through their door modules; mirrors without memory use the defrost supply. Power folding moves the mirror housings, while the interior auto-dimming mirror adjusts reflectance using ambient-light and glare sensors. Each function needs its own diagnostic path.
guides.why: A cold mirror, stalled housing or dark interior mirror can result from wiring, operating conditions or missing inputs. Loaded heater checks, isolated resistance measurements and controlled lighting tests distinguish these causes before replacement.
searchTerms: auto-dimming mirror stays dark in reverse

when.summary: Use when mirror heating, fitted power folding or interior automatic dimming does not operate correctly.
notes: Confirm which features are fitted and reproduce the concern before following a replacement decision.

prepare.title: Gather electrical and optical test equipment
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, infrared thermometer, test lamp, bright lamp and black electrical tape. These tests require live-circuit diagnostic skills. Use Rotunda Flex Probes (NUD105-R025D); never insert a test-lamp probe directly into a connector.

prepare.title: Establish valid test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation and battery state of charge above 70%. Follow each test's ignition and connector states. Isolate and unpower resistance-test circuits; follow Diagnostic Methods for battery disconnection during ground-resistance measurements. Do not apply substitute power directly to module outputs.

steps.title: Choose the heater test by fitted equipment
steps.body: Use Test E in [Rear View Mirrors](#/document/G1693886) for memory mirrors. Self-test the driver door module (DDM) for a left-side fault or passenger door module (PDM) for a right-side fault. Follow the code branches below. With no codes, run the engine, activate rear defrost and observe rear-window temperature for approximately 30 seconds. If it does not rise, diagnose defrost first. Test F, for mirrors without memory, begins with this same defrost check.

steps.title: Separate memory-mirror heater supply and ground faults
steps.body: E3 connects an adapted test lamp across the disconnected mirror's heater terminals. Illumination only with defrost active leads to jumper-harness inspection. Continuous illumination leads to E4: voltage remaining with the door module disconnected identifies a circuit short to voltage; otherwise inspect the module connections. No illumination leads through E5–E6: a working feed with a separate ground identifies a ground fault; otherwise check feed continuity before the module endpoint.

steps.title: Check heaters without memory
steps.body: After confirming rear defrost, compare both mirror temperatures for approximately 30 seconds. If neither warms, check battery junction box fuse 11 (10A); an intact fuse directs circuit repair, while a blown fuse requires short-circuit investigation. For one cold mirror, F3–F6 check its supply voltage and ground continuity before F7 examines the internal jumper harness.

steps.title: Resolve the heater fault at the correct endpoint
steps.body: At E11 or F7, inspect the jumper harness for actual opens, shorts, corrosion and damaged or displaced terminals. Repair it where possible; an unrepairable harness requires mirror replacement. A sound harness at these heater endpoints directs glass replacement. At E9/E10, repair module connectors, replace damaged terminals, clean corroded module pins and reconnect securely. Retest, then check applicable technical service bulletins before replacing a still-implicated door module.

steps.title: Establish the folding complaint and its stopping point
steps.body: For fitted power folding, remove obstructions and allow any motor lockout from repeated operation to expire; normal operation resumes after approximately 3–10 minutes. Partial manual folding can require synchronization. G1 separates a common fault from a single-mirror fault. For one affected mirror, stop before G10. Inspect the jumper harness for demonstrated wiring or terminal damage, but a visually sound harness does not justify mirror replacement.

steps.title: Trace the common folding circuit through G9
steps.body: If both mirrors malfunction, G2 tests the folding switch integrated into the front door window switch; replace it if it fails. G3–G6 check control-circuit shorts and continuity, relay supply and ground. A missing supply requires checking body control module (BCM) fuse 2 (7.5A) and investigating the circuit or a blown fuse's cause. G7–G9 check unwanted voltage at both mirrors, the specified left-side output continuity, then output shorts to ground. Repair failed circuits; passing G9 directs relay replacement. Synchronize after verified folding repairs.

steps.title: Check the interior mirror's installation and inputs
steps.body: Inspect both light sensors and BCM fuse 23 (10A). In H1, apply the parking brake, switch ignition on and check that reverse lamps illuminate only in Reverse, then select Park. Incorrect lamp operation requires reverse-lamp diagnosis. Confirm the rearward sensor is at the top of the glass. Correct installation or remove sensor obstructions before proceeding.

steps.title: Simulate daylight, darkness and glare
steps.body: H4–H5 require clear glass with both sensors illuminated, then with both covered by opaque material; failure of either check directs mirror replacement. A hand is not an adequate cover. For H6, keep the forward sensor covered and illuminate the rearward sensor: the glass should darken. If it does, H7 checks that selecting Reverse clears it. A successful check ends by selecting Park.

steps.title: Investigate failed dimming or reverse clearing
steps.body: Failure to darken leads through H8–H9 supply and ground checks, including fuse investigation when supply is missing, then H10. Failure to clear in Reverse goes directly to H10. The reverse-inhibit input must have voltage in Reverse and none outside Reverse. Repair a failed circuit; a correct input at the prescribed endpoint directs interior mirror replacement.

watchFor.title: Cleaning damage
watchFor.body: Clean mirrors for inspection without scrapers, razor blades, abrasive pads, harsh chemicals or petroleum-based products.

watchFor.title: Blocked light sensors
watchFor.body: Decals, dirt and aftermarket tint can alter dimming. Explain the effect if an obstruction cannot be removed.

notes: Use the linked tests for connector pins and electrical limits; heater and folding circuits have different test connections.
Folding synchronization requires the applicable procedure; repeated switch operation is not a substitute for it.

diagnostics.finding: DDM diagnostic trouble code B1163:11 or PDM diagnostic trouble code B1164:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The heater circuit needs the E7 short-to-ground check; the code does not establish a failed mirror.
diagnostics.next: Repair a failed circuit. If it passes, E8 reconnects the module with the mirror unplugged and clears codes. B1163:15 or B1164:15 then present directs jumper/glass inspection; otherwise inspect the corresponding module connections.

diagnostics.finding: DDM diagnostic trouble code B1163:15 or PDM diagnostic trouble code B1164:15 is recorded during the initial self-test.
diagnostics.meaning: The next decision requires testing heater output under load.
diagnostics.next: Continue at E3. Other door-module codes require Locks, Latches and Entry Systems diagnosis.

verification.title: Repeat the affected operating test
verification.body: Confirm heater response to defrost, synchronized folding after a verified repair, or the complete clear–dark–Reverse-clear sequence, as applicable.

verification.title: Record the result and any remaining limit
verification.body: Record codes, temperature changes, electrical findings and final operation. Identify any single-mirror folding fault still awaiting its correct diagnostic continuation.

applicability.equipment: Heated exterior mirrors with or without memory; power-folding mirrors and auto-dimming interior mirror where fitted

guides.title: Repair an exterior mirror assembly, glass, motor or fitted lamp
guides.summary: Choose the required mirror repair branch, preserve its option-specific wiring and reassemble the serviced components in reverse order.
guides.introduction: The exterior mirror combines a housing with electrically adjustable glass. Depending on equipment, it can also contain glass heating, position memory, a turn signal, a puddle or projection lamp and a blind-spot indicator. Repair may involve the whole door-mounted assembly or an individual component. These are alternative access paths: removing the complete mirror is not listed as a prerequisite for every internal repair.
guides.why: The assembly-removal sequence changes the door-glass position as access requirements change. The mirror must be supported when its mounting hardware is removed to protect both it and the door. Internal connectors vary with fitted options, and an electrical complaint may come from the integral jumper harness rather than the motor or complete mirror.

when.summary: When damage or a diagnosed fault requires repair of the exterior mirror or one of its serviceable components.
notes: Identify the fitted options and required repair branch before dismantling.
Inspect the jumper harness before replacing a mirror or motor for an electrical concern.

prepare.title: Arrange the appropriate access
prepare.detail: Whole-assembly work requires the front door trim-panel and appropriate speaker procedures. Speaker references are identified for SYNC 2/SYNC 3; follow the equipment applicable to the vehicle.

prepare.title: Prepare for glass and wiring work
prepare.detail: Have a flat-bladed screwdriver for releasing the glass and the capability to handle small screws, tabs and option-specific connectors. Electrical fault assessment must include the mirror jumper harness.

steps.title: Select the repair branch
steps.body: Use the complete [exterior mirror procedure](#/document/G1945075) to choose assembly, glass, motor, cover, turn-signal or puddle-lamp work. For electrical concerns, first inspect the integral jumper harness for open or shorted circuits and damaged or pushed-out pins; attempt harness repair where a harness concern exists.

steps.title: For assembly removal, open the door access
steps.body: Raise the window fully. Remove the [door trim panel](#/document/G1692600) and the appropriate [left](#/document/G1693897) or [right](#/document/G1693898) front door speaker. Remove the door-mounted tweeter if fitted. Remove the rectangular tape cover and, on vehicles without door-mounted tweeters, the additional tape cover specified by the procedure.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the complete mirror
steps.body: Through the lower speaker opening, disconnect the mirror electrical connection and separate the wiring harness guide. Reconnect the window switch and lower the glass fully. Support the mirror while removing its mounting nut and bolts, then remove the assembly.

steps.title: For glass service, release the glass from the motor
steps.body: Position the mirror glass fully inward and upward. Insert a flat-bladed screwdriver between the glass and motor, twist to release the glass and position it aside. Disconnect its electrical connectors, whose number and location depend on fitted options.

steps.title: For motor service, remove the bezel
steps.body: With the glass removed, remove the bezel screws and release its tabs. Remove the motor screws and position the motor aside, then disconnect its electrical connectors and remove it.

steps.title: For cover or turn-signal service, work through the motor branch
steps.body: Remove the motor first. Disconnect the mirror-mounted side turn signal if fitted, then remove the cover screw, release the tabs and remove the cover. With the cover removed, the mirror-mounted turn signal can be removed.

steps.title: For puddle-lamp service, work through the glass opening
steps.body: Remove the mirror glass, press the puddle-lamp retaining tab and lower the lamp. Disconnect its electrical connectors to release it. This branch calls for glass removal rather than the motor-and-cover sequence.

steps.title: Reassemble the branch used
steps.body: Reverse the relevant removal sequence, reconnecting every fitted connector and engaging the screws and tabs disturbed. For whole-assembly work, support the mirror until secured and restore the harness guide, tape covers, speakers, any removed tweeter and door trim.

watchFor.title: Unsupported assembly
watchFor.body: Removing the mounting hardware without supporting the mirror risks damage to the mirror or door surface.

watchFor.title: Different glass connections
watchFor.body: Do not assume both mirrors or replacement assemblies have identical connector arrangements; options determine the connections present.

notes: Memory-equipped mirrors use door-module control and position feedback; non-memory mirrors receive motor voltage and ground from the mirror control switch.

diagnostics.finding: The mirror does not respond to adjustment.
diagnostics.meaning: A wiring defect can interrupt motor operation; the symptom alone does not condemn the motor.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the integral jumper harness and its pins before deciding on motor or assembly replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Heated glass is inactive while rear-window defrost is off.
diagnostics.meaning: Mirror heating operates only while the rear-window defrost system is active.
diagnostics.next: Assess heating with rear defrost active before treating the glass as faulty.

diagnostics.finding: Memory recall stops when the mirror or driver-seat control is operated.
diagnostics.meaning: Manual control input cancels an active memory recall.
diagnostics.next: Distinguish normal cancellation from a recall fault before replacing components.

verification.title: Check the repaired functions and attachments
verification.body: Confirm secure mounting or component retention and complete electrical reconnection. Check glass adjustment; assess fitted memory, heating and any serviced lamp under their normal operating conditions.

verification.title: Record the repair result
verification.body: Record the component serviced, harness findings and results for the affected fitted features, including any unresolved complaint.

Right-hand front door speaker access procedure for applicable SYNC 2/SYNC 3 equipment.

applicability.equipment: Power exterior mirrors; memory, heating and mirror lamps as equipped

guides.title: Remove and refit the interior rear-view mirror by mount type
guides.summary: Use the removal and installation branch matching the fitted mirror mount, including programming or calibration where that branch requires it.
guides.introduction: The interior mirror provides the rearward view through the cabin. A manual mirror uses a driver-operated day/night lever; an auto-dimming mirror uses light sensors to reduce reflected glare. Removal depends on the windshield mounting design, not simply whether the glass dims automatically. The procedure provides six alternative mount types, with different release tools, movements and equipment-dependent finishing steps.
guides.why: The windshield carries the mirror mount, so using the wrong release method can load and damage the glass. Some mirrors slide off after a tab is released, others rotate, and another uses a set screw. Where the applicable assembly includes camera electronics, replacing it also requires a programming sequence that begins before removal and ends with camera alignment.
searchTerms: rear-view mirror stuck on windshield mount

when.summary: When the interior mirror needs replacement or removal for access, after identifying its fitted mounting type.
notes: Use only the matching mount branch. Rain-sensor, compass and camera instructions are conditional equipment requirements.

prepare.title: Read the safety precautions
prepare.detail: Before starting, follow Health and Safety Precautions in section 100-00, referenced by the mirror procedure.

prepare.title: Select the branch-specific tools
prepare.detail: Type 1 uses remover 501-190 and installer 501-191. Type 2 uses remover 501-D118A (501-D118) and installer 501-025. Do not interchange release methods.

prepare.title: Arrange electronic finishing capability
prepare.detail: A new type 4 mirror requires a scan tool for programmable module installation (PMI) of image processing module A (IPMA) and camera alignment. Types 1 and 2 require compass checks when fitted with a compass module requiring calibration.

steps.title: Identify the mount and prepare its connections
steps.body: Match the assembly to the [mirror procedure](#/document/G1693881). For a new type 4 mirror, begin IPMA PMI before removal. Types 3 and 4 require rain-sensor cover removal and mirror disconnection. Type 1 requires disconnection if equipped. For type 6, remove the rain-sensor cover and disconnect that sensor if equipped, then disconnect the mirror connector and unclip its harness.

steps.title: Remove a type 1 sliding mount
steps.body: Adjust remover 501-190 and insert it fully into the mount access hole. Release the locking tab. With a closed hand, bump the remover adjustment handle to move the mirror upward, then slide it off the mount.

steps.title: Remove a type 2 sliding mount
steps.body: Insert remover 501-D118A (501-D118) into the release tab. Pull the tool's lower edge away from the windshield, then slide the mirror off its mount.

steps.title: Remove a type 3 or type 4 rotating mount
steps.body: For type 3, position the assembly to release the indexing tab, inspect the tab and turn the mirror slightly counterclockwise. Continue with the specified 45-degree counterclockwise turn, then pull it off. For type 4, turn the assembly counterclockwise and remove it; do not transfer the type 3 angle to this branch.

steps.title: Remove a type 5 or type 6 mount
steps.body: For type 5, release the locking tab and slide the mirror off. For type 6, loosen the set screw and slide the mirror upward after completing its wiring-disconnection steps.

steps.title: Install sliding-tab types
steps.body: For type 1, slide the mirror over the windshield bracket from above and fully seat it with installer 501-191; seating produces an audible click. Reconnect its connector if equipped. Fully seat type 2 with installer 501-025. Slide type 5 onto its mount until the locking tab engages.

steps.title: Install rotating or set-screw types
steps.body: Install types 3, 4 and 6 by reversing their respective removal sequences. For type 6, apply the specified set-screw torque of 16 lb.in (1.8 Nm). Restore the applicable connectors, harness clips and covers.

steps.title: Complete the equipment-specific finish
steps.body: For types 1 and 2, check compass zone and calibration when required by the fitted compass module. After installing a new type 4 mirror, complete IPMA PMI using the scan-tool instructions, then carry out camera alignment with the scan tool.

watchFor.title: Incomplete type 1 tool insertion
watchFor.body: The remover must be fully inserted into the access hole; incomplete engagement can damage the windshield glass.

watchFor.title: Unexpected connector arrangement
watchFor.body: Connector number and location vary by application. Match the fitted assembly before pulling it away.

notes: The alternative mount branches do not establish that every listed feature is fitted to the vehicle.

diagnostics.finding: An auto-dimming mirror remains bright in daylight or when reverse is selected.
diagnostics.meaning: High reflectance is expected in those conditions.
diagnostics.next: Consider lighting and operating conditions before treating the behavior as a failure.

diagnostics.finding: A manual mirror does not dim automatically.
diagnostics.meaning: Its day/night function is controlled by the driver.
diagnostics.next: Check operation of the lever rather than expecting automatic dimming.

verification.title: Confirm mount retention
verification.body: Check the applicable seating result: the type 1 click, full type 2 seating, type 5 tab engagement, or completion of the reverse installation for the other types.

verification.title: Record required electronic completion
verification.body: Where applicable, record the compass checks or completion of new type 4 IPMA PMI and camera alignment.

guides.title: Diagnose passenger power-seat and driver lumbar faults
guides.summary: Test passenger seat adjustment and driver lumbar circuits, while directing memory-seat and climate-controlled seat complaints to their appropriate diagnostic paths.
guides.introduction: Seat-track motors adjust fore/aft position and cushion height; the lumbar assembly changes backrest support. Passenger adjustment motors receive power directly through the switch, whereas memory-seat movement is managed by the driver seat module (DSM). Identifying the fitted system and the exact failed movement determines which test applies.
guides.why: A motionless seat can result from lost power, damaged wiring, a switch or a motor. Testing separates these causes before replacement, while correct airbag isolation prevents accidental deployment.
searchTerms: passenger power seat will not move
memory seat moves in one-second intervals

when.summary: When a seat adjustment fails, memory movement is incorrect, or seat heating/cooling performs poorly.
notes: Component-replacement decisions require the complaint to be present during testing.

prepare.title: Electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter and specified terminal flex probes. Check battery condition, previous repairs, wiring and connectors; isolate circuits correctly for resistance measurements.

prepare.title: Airbag procedures
prepare.detail: Have the complete Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) depowering and repowering procedures available. These motor tests require controlled access around seat airbag connections.

steps.title: Classify the complaint
steps.body: Use the symptom chart in Front Seats. Passenger adjustment follows Test A; driver lumbar follows B; driver adjustment without memory follows F. Memory movement from the seat switch follows C, memory SET operation follows D, and easy entry/exit follows E. Failed module communication requires network diagnosis.

steps.title: Isolate the appropriate airbag
steps.body: Follow the prescribed SRS depowering sequence before disconnecting passenger airbag connector C219 for Test A or driver airbag connector C3206 for Test B. Continue with the exact electrical-test conditions in the applicable test.

steps.title: Test a passenger seat that fails in every direction
steps.body: Verify battery junction box fuse 13 (30A), then follow A2–A3 to check switch power and ground. Supply must exceed 11 volts and ground resistance must be below 3 ohms. Repair a failed circuit; satisfactory results direct switch replacement. Investigate a blown fuse's short-circuit cause.

steps.title: Separate individual passenger motor faults
steps.body: For a failed horizontal, front-height or rear-height movement, check motor voltage under both switch commands; polarity reverses with direction. Satisfactory voltage directs horizontal-motor replacement or, for either height motor, complete track replacement. Otherwise test both connecting wires: satisfactory continuity directs switch replacement; failed continuity requires circuit repair.

steps.title: Test driver lumbar operation
steps.body: Test B checks voltage across the disconnected lumbar motor while commanding both directions. More than 11 volts in both directions directs lumbar-assembly replacement. Otherwise check both switch-to-motor circuits: resistance below 3 ohms directs switch replacement; an open circuit requires repair.

steps.title: Route memory and climate complaints
steps.body: Retrieve module diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Before memory-seat Test C, check body control module fuse 2 (7.5A) and battery junction box fuse 12 (30A). For remote-key recall, verify transmitter operation and memory association first. Inoperative climate seats follow J; poor performance requires climate-module self-testing, followed by blower, duct, foam-pad and airflow checks when no codes are present.

watchFor.title: Temperature-related shutdown
watchFor.body: Sunload, extreme cabin temperatures or repeatedly switching heating modes can produce overtemperature codes even if the climate system subsequently recovers.

notes: Memory-seat module replacement requires programmable module installation (PMI). A new DSM, driver track or horizontal motor also requires hard-stop/soft-stop setup.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1663, B1664 or B1665 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The DSM did not detect the commanded movement; this does not establish motor failure.
diagnostics.next: Follow C for no movement or D for one-second jogging. Switch-input faults also follow C; position-feedback faults follow D.

diagnostics.finding: Driver door module code B1C03:23, B1C04:23 or B1C05:23 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A memory-button signal is stuck low.
diagnostics.next: Follow D; route other door-module codes through locks and entry-system diagnostics.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B2477 is recorded in the DSM or front seat climate control module (SCME).
diagnostics.meaning: Configuration is missing or lost; this code alone does not prevent basic DSM switch operation.
diagnostics.next: Perform PMI and repeat self-testing. Verify success and clear DSM codes as directed.

diagnostics.finding: Other DSM or SCME codes are recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The charts distinguish voltage, communication, thermoelectric, blower-speed and temperature faults.
diagnostics.next: Follow the matching chart entry. U2050 directs replacement of the reporting module; SCME B1342 directs SCME replacement.

verification.title: Restore and prove out the SRS
verification.body: At A10 or B3, follow depowering instructions again, reconnect the airbag and every disconnected connector, then repower. An unsuccessful SRS prove-out requires airbag diagnosis before completion.

verification.title: Record the outcome
verification.body: Record circuit findings, module self-test results and SRS prove-out. After climate airflow repairs, retest normal operation.

guides.title: Diagnose driver memory seat movement, recall and easy entry/exit faults
guides.summary: Separate seat-switch, motor, position-feedback and network-input faults before replacing memory-seat components.
guides.introduction: The driver front seat module (DSM) powers the seat motors and tracks their position through magnetic Hall-effect sensors. The seat switch requests movement directly; the door-mounted memory buttons send requests through the driver door module (DDM). These tests distinguish failed manual adjustment, failed memory recall and incorrect easy entry/exit operation.
guides.why: A seat that stops moving may have lost its command, electrical supply or position feedback. Separating these paths prevents a wiring fault or missing ignition message from being mistaken for a failed motor.
searchTerms: driver memory seat will not move
seat will not move forward or backward

when.summary: Use when the memory driver's seat fails manual adjustment, memory recall or easy entry/exit.
notes: Confirm the complaint is present; an intermittent condition does not justify replacing components through these tests.

prepare.title: Electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting DSM/DDM self-tests, live parameter identifications (PIDs) and active commands, a multimeter, specified Rotunda Flex Probes and the applicable wiring diagrams. Follow each test's ignition and circuit-isolation requirements.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge above 70%. Inspect previous repairs, harness damage and connectors; address circuit trouble codes before performance faults.

prepare.title: Plan restraint-system isolation
prepare.detail: Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) service capability is required. Follow the linked depowering procedure before disconnecting driver-side airbag connector C3206 where directed. Keep it disconnected during interim module checks; incorrect handling can cause deployment.

steps.title: Start Test C for failed manual adjustment
steps.body: Depower the SRS, disconnect C3206, then follow Test C's ignition sequence. Operate every seat-switch direction and run the DSM self-test. Follow the code branches below; failed communication requires Communications Network diagnosis.

steps.title: Separate switch inputs from motor outputs
steps.body: Without codes, compare switch PIDs with actual switch positions. Incorrect inputs lead through the fuse, switch component, supply, ground and switch-to-DSM wiring checks. Correct inputs lead to active motor commands. If commanded movement works, investigate intermittent connections without replacing components.

steps.title: Isolate the failed movement circuit
steps.body: No movement leads to DSM supply, ground and motor short checks. A single failed axis leads to commanded voltage testing in both directions; polarity reverses with direction. Follow the isolation tests to distinguish wiring from the motor. Height-motor repair requires a seat track; the horizontal motor is serviced separately.

steps.title: Start Test D for failed memory recall
steps.body: Check that the DSM ignition-status PID follows the ignition. If it does, move the seat through its full ranges, center each adjustment and self-test both modules. Without codes, compare memory-button PIDs with button operation to choose the input or position-feedback branch.

steps.title: Trace recall inputs and position feedback
steps.body: Incorrect button inputs require switch resistance, ground and wiring checks before the DDM endpoint. Valid inputs lead to sensor PIDs throughout travel. Missing feedback requires the relevant sensor-circuit checks, with restraint isolation where directed, before track or horizontal-motor replacement.

steps.title: Complete the Test C or D module checks
steps.body: At a module endpoint, inspect and repair corroded, damaged or pushed-out terminals, latch connectors securely and retest. If the fault persists, check applicable Technical Service Bulletins before the directed DSM or DDM replacement. Correct the underlying connector fault if operation returns.

steps.title: Use Test E for easy entry/exit
steps.body: Check the message-center setting, full fore/aft travel and DSM self-test. Diagnose any codes first. Enable a disabled feature and retest. If the complaint remains, compare ignition-status data with ignition mode: disagreement requires ignition-status diagnosis; agreement leads to DSM replacement under E2.

steps.title: Perform required replacement setup
steps.body: A new DSM requires programmable module installation. Reset the DSM hard-stop/soft-stop settings after replacing the DSM, driver seat track or horizontal motor, then complete the applicable restoration and verification.

watchFor.title: Movement in short bursts
watchFor.body: Jog mode indicates lost position feedback. Manual movement can remain possible while memory recall is unavailable.

watchFor.title: Apparently cancelled easy entry/exit
watchFor.body: Seat, memory or mirror-control input can cancel automatic movement. Rearward travel is also limited near the end of the track.

notes: For a driver power seat without memory, the preliminary check is battery junction box fuse 12 (30A). Its switch powers the motors directly; continue with the separate non-memory diagnostic path.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble codes B1663, B1664 or B1665 are recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The DSM sensed no movement from the front-height, rear-height or horizontal motor respectively; this does not establish motor failure.
diagnostics.next: In Test C, all three together lead to C10 supply checks; individual codes lead to their axis-specific tests.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1711, B1715, B1719, B1723, B1727 or B1731 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test C routes these findings to the seat-control-switch component check.
diagnostics.next: Begin C3 and follow its results.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble codes B1952, B1956 or B1964 are recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Rear-height, front-height or horizontal feedback respectively has a short-to-voltage or open-circuit condition.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test D's corresponding sensor branch; all three together lead to D9 sensor-PID checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble codes B1953, B1957 or B1965 are recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Rear-height, front-height or horizontal feedback respectively has a short-to-ground condition.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test D's corresponding circuit branch; all three together lead to D9.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1C03:23, B1C04:23 or B1C05:23 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The corresponding memory-button input is stuck low and ignored by the DDM.
diagnostics.next: Begin D4 switch testing, then check wiring before considering the module.

verification.title: Restore the restraint system
verification.body: At C28 or D21, depower the SRS before reconnecting C3206 and remaining connectors. Repower and confirm successful SRS prove-out; a failed prove-out requires SRS diagnosis.

verification.title: Record the resolved complaint
verification.body: Confirm the affected adjustment, memory recall or easy entry/exit function operates correctly. Record the original codes, decisive test results and final operation.

guides.title: Diagnose climate-controlled front seats that will not heat or cool
guides.summary: Separate seat-control commands, voltage faults and driver-seat blower circuit faults before deciding which repair is justified.
guides.introduction: Each climate-controlled front seat draws cabin air through cushion and backrest blower assemblies containing fans, thermoelectric devices and temperature sensors. The front seat climate control module (SCME), beneath the passenger seat, controls these assemblies independently of the cabin climate system. Diagnosis establishes whether the problem comes from a command, electrical supply, wiring, blower assembly or module.
guides.why: A seat can stop because its controller is protecting the system, rather than because a blower has failed. These tests distinguish those conditions while preserving the precautions needed around seat-mounted airbags.

when.summary: When either climate-controlled seat will not heat or cool, or a relevant seat-module fault code is recorded.
notes: Confirm the concern is present before following component-replacement decisions.

prepare.title: Diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting SCME self-tests, active commands and parameter identification (PID) live data, plus a digital multimeter and specified terminal-safe flex probes. Have wiring diagrams Cells 119 and 123 available. Verify battery state of charge exceeds 70%.

prepare.title: Airbag precautions
prepare.detail: Follow Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) depowering before connector access. K4 isolates passenger airbag connector C219; tests L and M isolate C219 and driver connector C3206. These tests require competence in live electrical measurements and SRS procedures.

steps.title: Test J: Establish communication and retrieve faults
steps.body: Run the SCME self-test using the [Front Seats diagnostic procedure](#/document/G1695509). Follow its DTC chart if diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) appear. Failed communication requires network diagnosis; successful communication without codes leads to active-command testing.

steps.title: Test J: Command the affected seat directly
steps.body: Monitor cushion and backrest temperature PIDs while applying the appropriate seat heat command, which is limited to 15 seconds. If temperatures do not rise momentarily, remove the cushion blower filter as directed and repeat while checking fan movement. If neither response indicates operation, J2 directs SCME replacement.

steps.title: Test J: Compare physical-button requests
steps.body: If active commands work, start the engine and compare seat-mode PIDs with every setting selected on the front controls interface module (FCIM). Matching responses direct an inoperative touchscreen complaint to infotainment diagnosis. Mismatches require the VIN-guided FCIM routine when only seat controls fail, or climate-control diagnosis when other FCIM functions also fail.

steps.title: Test K: Investigate B2486 supply voltage
steps.body: Retrieve all-module memory codes and address powertrain control module charging faults first. Replace a battery that fails its condition test. If it passes but needs recharging, diagnose charging, clear codes and retest. Otherwise follow K3's loaded and unloaded charging checks, then K4–K5's SCME supply and ground measurements, including the harness wiggle check. Repair failed circuits before reassessing the module.

steps.title: Test L: Isolate driver-seat overload faults
steps.body: For B103B or B1111, check the blower circuits for shorts to ground, then voltage, then incorrect loop resistance. Follow the failed branch to the cushion or backrest blower. A short remaining with that blower disconnected identifies wiring; a short disappearing identifies the blower. Component resistance testing likewise separates a faulty assembly from its wiring.

steps.title: Test M: Trace an open driver-seat circuit
steps.body: For B103C, disconnect both driver blower assemblies and the SCME as directed. Check wiring continuity, then unwanted voltage, then each blower's component-side resistance. Repair failed wiring or replace the assembly that fails its resistance test.

steps.title: Resolve connector or module faults
steps.body: At K6, L10 or M4, repair corrosion, damaged or displaced terminals and ensure connectors latch. Keep the specified airbag connectors disconnected during this operational check. If the concern persists, follow any applicable technical service bulletin in OASIS; otherwise replace the SCME. A replacement requires programmable module installation (PMI).

steps.title: Restore the restraint system
steps.body: At K7, L11 or M5, depower the SRS again before reconnecting the isolated airbag connectors and all remaining connections. Follow SRS repowering and verify successful prove-out. An unsuccessful prove-out requires airbag-system diagnosis before returning the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Testing can create thermal faults
watchFor.body: Repeated heat/cool switching can disable a seat. Allow temperatures to approach ambient between modes; resulting codes may need clearing.

watchFor.title: Charging-test speed matters
watchFor.body: During K3, exceeding 2,000 rpm requires stopping and restarting the engine before testing, because generator self-excitation can distort the result.

notes: J2 filter removal provides diagnostic access; the blower filters are not separately serviceable.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B2486 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: Input below 10 volts or above 15 volts puts both seats into standby; jump-starting, charging or discharge can explain its history.
diagnostics.next: Use test K. Operation resumes after voltage returns between 10 and 15 volts and a seat button is selected on.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B103B is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: A driver blower circuit short to ground or excessively low blower resistance causes driver-seat shutdown.
diagnostics.next: Use test L to distinguish wiring, blower and module faults.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1111 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The SCME blower-driver integrated circuit has overheated, causing driver-seat shutdown.
diagnostics.next: Use test L; this is not proof that the seat surface itself overheated.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B103C is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: A driver blower circuit is open, disconnected or has extremely high resistance; the SCME continues normal operation.
diagnostics.next: Use test M to locate the open or failed assembly.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B103D is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: A driver blower circuit short to ground or excessive current overheats the SCME and shuts down that seat.
diagnostics.next: Follow its DTC-chart diagnostic branch before selecting a component for replacement.

verification.title: Confirm the repair response
verification.body: Repeat the applicable operational check and complete successful SRS prove-out wherever airbag connectors were isolated.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record retrieved codes, command responses, failed measurements, the resulting repair and SRS prove-out outcome.

guides.title: Diagnose climate-controlled front seat blower and thermoelectric faults
guides.summary: Use Tests N–Q to distinguish seat wiring faults, failed blower assemblies and climate-control module faults while preserving side-airbag safety.
guides.introduction: Climate-controlled seats move cabin air through cushion and backrest assemblies, where thermoelectric devices heat or cool it before distribution through the seat foam. The front seat climate control module (SCME) controls temperature and blower operation. These tests separate faults in the fan circuits from faults in the thermoelectric circuits within the assemblies.
guides.why: The two circuit types use different terminals and resistance limits; confusing them can condemn a sound assembly. Side-airbag connections are also involved, so restraint isolation and successful restoration are essential parts of the job.

when.summary: Seat heating or cooling is faulty and B103D, B1113, B111B, B111C or B111D is recorded.
notes: A code identifies a diagnostic route, not a component that automatically needs replacement.

prepare.title: Required capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool and a multimeter for voltage and resistance measurements. The technician must be able to perform the exact Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) depowering and repowering procedures; incorrect work can cause accidental deployment.

prepare.title: Identify the circuits
prepare.detail: Use the seat wiring diagrams and connector identification before testing. Follow each test's specified ignition state and connector-isolation sequence.

steps.title: Select the correct side and test
steps.body: Test N concerns the driver blower feed. Tests O and P concern passenger thermoelectric circuits, while Q concerns passenger blower feeds. At SCME C3265A, A/B serve the passenger cushion and C/D serve the passenger backrest. Keep these pairs distinct from blower power terminals.

steps.title: Depower and isolate the restraints
steps.body: Perform SRS depowering before disconnecting the specified airbag connections. Test N isolates both driver C3206 and passenger C219; O, P and Q isolate passenger C219. Disconnect the climate-control components specified by the selected test. Keep the airbag connections isolated during the later functional retest.

steps.title: N: Check the driver blower supply
steps.body: With C3034, C3035 and SCME C3265C disconnected, check pin 16 to ground and the feed pair at pins 16/15 for shorts. Each isolation reading must exceed 10,000 ohms. Then test each blower component-side, positive lead on pin 3 and negative on pin 4: the range is 4000–10,000 ohms. Repair failed circuits or replace the assembly that fails its component test.

steps.title: O: Separate passenger thermoelectric shorts from assembly faults
steps.body: Check C3265A A–D for ground faults and unwanted voltage, then measure the A/B and C/D loops against 0.9–10 ohms. For a short, disconnect the affected cushion C3040 or backrest C3039 assembly and repeat: a remaining fault identifies wiring; a disappearing fault directs assembly replacement. For a failed loop-resistance check, a passing isolated component measurement identifies wiring, while a failing component measurement directs replacement.

steps.title: P: Trace an open passenger thermoelectric circuit
steps.body: With the assemblies and C3265A disconnected, check each corresponding wire for resistance below 3 ohms, then check for unwanted voltage. Repair failed circuits. Test each assembly between component pins 1 and 2 against 0.9–10 ohms. Replace only an assembly that fails; otherwise continue to the module connection checks.

steps.title: Q: Check the passenger blower supply
steps.body: With C3039, C3040 and C3265C disconnected, test pin 8 to ground and pins 7/8 for shorts; isolation must exceed 10,000 ohms. Test both blower assemblies using the same pin 3-positive/pin 4-negative polarity and 4000–10,000-ohm limits as N. Repair the circuit or replace the failed assembly as directed.

steps.title: Complete the module branch and repairs
steps.body: When circuit and component checks pass, switch ignition off and inspect all SCME connectors. Repair corrosion, damaged or displaced terminals, then seat and latch the connectors. Reconnect the other test connections while leaving the specified airbag connections isolated. Operate the system. A persistent concern requires checking applicable technical service bulletins before SCME replacement; a cleared concern requires addressing the connection fault's cause.

watchFor.title: Reversed meter leads
watchFor.body: The blower pin 3/4 resistance tests require the stated polarity. Reversed leads can produce false failures.

watchFor.title: Short scan-tool commands
watchFor.body: Normal seat operation requires the engine running. Scan-tool operation with ignition on and engine off lasts in 15 second intervals; this timeout alone is not a fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B103D is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test N investigates the driver blower feed and driver cushion/backrest blowers.
diagnostics.next: Complete N's circuit and component checks before its SCME branch.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1113 or B111B is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: B1113 identifies passenger thermoelectric output-stage overheating; B111B identifies its overcurrent or short-to-ground condition. The passenger seat system can shut down.
diagnostics.next: Use Test O to distinguish wiring, assemblies and SCME.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B111C is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A passenger thermoelectric circuit is open, disconnected or excessively resistive. The SCME can continue normal operation while recording this fault.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test P's continuity, voltage and component-resistance checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B111D is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A passenger blower circuit fault or excessive current overheats the SCME output stage and shuts down that seat.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test Q.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B19A1 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The passenger cushion blower speed-control circuit is shorted to voltage, causing passenger seat shutdown.
diagnostics.next: Use its dedicated speed-control diagnosis; Tests N–Q do not complete this separate fault path.

verification.title: Restore and prove out the SRS
verification.body: Depower the SRS again before reconnecting C3206 and C219 for N, or C219 for O/P/Q. Restore all disconnected connectors, perform SRS repowering and verify successful prove-out. A failed prove-out requires SRS diagnosis before return to service.

verification.title: Record the repair result
verification.body: Record the original code, affected seat and assembly, circuit/component readings, functional retest result and SRS prove-out result.

guides.title: Diagnose climate controlled seat blower faults B19A1–B19A4
guides.summary: Separate wiring shorts, internal blower faults and module connection problems when a climate controlled front seat stops working.
guides.introduction: Each climate controlled seat has cushion and backrest blower assemblies that distribute heated or cooled air through the seat padding. The front seat climate control module (SCME), beneath the passenger seat, supplies power and a separate blower-speed signal. These tests trace unwanted voltage on that signal circuit.
guides.why: Disconnecting the module and blower separates harness faults from internal blower shorts. Checking connections before replacing the module avoids overlooking damaged terminals.
searchTerms: passenger seat heating and cooling not working

when.summary: When a current seat climate concern accompanies diagnostic trouble code B19A1, B19A2, B19A3 or B19A4.
notes: Confirm the concern is present before following component-replacement decisions.

prepare.title: Electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Have a scan tool, digital multimeter, required Rotunda Flex Probes and Wiring Diagrams Cell 119. Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%.

prepare.title: Restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Execution requires the complete Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) depowering and repowering procedures. Module replacement also requires programmable module installation (PMI) capability.

steps.title: Select the test and isolate the airbags
steps.body: Use the code mapping below and the [exact pinpoint test](#/document/G1695509). Follow [SRS depowering](#/document/G1696297). Tests R/S disconnect passenger airbag in-line C219; T/U disconnect both C219 and driver C3206. Then disconnect SCME C3265C.

steps.title: Check for unwanted voltage
steps.body: With ignition ON, measure the selected speed-control terminal to ground. If voltage is present, switch ignition OFF, disconnect the corresponding blower, then switch ON and repeat. Voltage remaining means repair the circuit and proceed to SRS restoration. No voltage leads to the circuit-to-circuit resistance check.

steps.title: Separate a harness short from a component fault
steps.body: With ignition OFF and the blower disconnected, measure between the specified speed-control and blower-output circuits. Resistance must exceed 10,000 ohms. Otherwise repair the circuits and restore SRS; a passing result leads to the blower check.

steps.title: Check inside the blower assembly
steps.body: Measure the specified component-side terminals. Resistance must exceed 2M ohms. Otherwise install a new blower using the [cushion](#/document/G1695514) or [backrest](#/document/G1695511) procedure, then restore SRS. A passing result leads to module-connection checks.

steps.title: Inspect and reconnect the module
steps.body: With ignition OFF, inspect all SCME connectors. Replace corroded connectors or terminals and clean module pins; replace damaged, bent or pushed-out pins as necessary. Seat and latch the connectors, reconnecting everything except the isolated airbag connectors.

steps.title: Make the module decision
steps.body: Switch ignition ON and operate the system. If the concern disappears, address the connection fault's root cause. If it persists, check applicable technical service bulletins in Ford's OASIS service-information system and follow any relevant bulletin. Without an applicable bulletin, follow [SCME replacement](#/document/G1695512), including required PMI.

steps.title: Restore the restraint system
steps.body: For every repair branch, depower SRS again, reconnect the required airbag connectors and all other disconnected connectors, then follow [SRS repowering](#/document/G1696298).

watchFor.title: Airbag reconnection timing
watchFor.body: Leave the specified airbags disconnected during the module operation check. Departing from SRS procedures risks accidental deployment and serious injury.

watchFor.title: Invalid resistance readings
watchFor.body: Follow the ignition and connector states exactly. Voltage present during resistance testing can corrupt the result.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B19A1 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The passenger cushion blower speed-control circuit requires short-to-voltage testing.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test R.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B19A2 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A passenger backrest blower speed-circuit short to voltage shuts down the passenger seat system.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test S.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B19A3 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A driver cushion blower speed-circuit short to voltage shuts down the driver seat system.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test T.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B19A4 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A driver backrest blower speed-circuit short to voltage shuts down the driver seat system.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test U.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B19A5 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A passenger cushion blower speed-circuit short to ground shuts down the passenger seat system.
diagnostics.next: Use its separate short-to-ground diagnostic path; the voltage-short decisions above do not resolve this code.

verification.title: Confirm SRS prove-out
verification.body: Repair completion requires successful SRS prove-out. If it fails, continue with [SRS diagnosis](#/document/G1696340).

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record the code, voltage and resistance findings, repair branch, operating-check result where performed, and final SRS prove-out outcome.

guides.title: Diagnose climate-controlled seat blower faults and shutdowns
guides.summary: Use blower circuit checks and controlled substitution to distinguish wiring, blower and seat climate module faults.
guides.introduction: Each climate-controlled front seat has cushion and backrest blower assemblies that deliver heated or cooled air through the seat foam. The front seat climate control module (SCME), beneath the passenger seat, supplies power and controls blower speed. These tests investigate blower speed-control faults; an additional overtemperature finding requires a different diagnostic path.
guides.why: A shorted speed-control circuit can shut down the affected seat. Testing the disconnected wiring before substituting a blower prevents a wiring fault from being mistaken for a failed assembly or module.
searchTerms: passenger seat heating and cooling inoperative

when.summary: When a climate-controlled seat concern is present with a blower speed-control or passenger cushion overtemperature code.
notes: A stored diagnostic trouble code (DTC) alone does not justify replacing a component when the concern is absent.

prepare.title: Electrical diagnosis and seat access
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, specified terminal flex probes and Wiring Diagrams Cell 119. Check battery condition and related circuit codes first.

prepare.title: Restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: This work requires Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) depowering and repowering, blower removal procedures and, if needed, programmable module installation capability.

steps.title: Select the test and isolate its circuits
steps.body: Follow Test V, W, X or Y according to the findings below. Depower the SRS first. Passenger tests disconnect airbag connector C219; driver tests disconnect both C3206 and C219. Disconnect the affected blower and SCME connector C3265C as directed.

steps.title: Check both possible short paths
steps.body: Measure the selected speed-control circuit to ground, then to its blower ground circuit at the specified terminals. Each reading must exceed 10,000 ohms. A failed check directs circuit repair followed by final SRS restoration; passing both permits blower substitution.

steps.title: Substitute the corresponding blower
steps.body: Use the linked cushion or backrest removal procedure. Passenger tests use the corresponding driver blower; driver tests use the corresponding passenger blower. Reconnect the tested blower and SCME, start the engine and operate the affected seat. Restored operation directs installation of a new affected blower assembly; otherwise continue to module connections.

steps.title: Inspect and retest module connections
steps.body: Switch ignition off and inspect every SCME connector. Replace corroded connectors or terminals, clean module pins and replace damaged, bent or pushed-out terminals as necessary. Latch the connectors securely and reconnect other disconnected connectors, leaving the specified airbag connectors disconnected. Switch ignition on and retest.

steps.title: Resolve the remaining module decision
steps.body: If the concern remains, check Ford OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins. Follow an applicable bulletin instead of continuing this test; otherwise replace the SCME using its procedure. A new SCME requires programmable module installation (PMI). If reconnection restores operation, correct the underlying connector fault.

steps.title: Restore the restraint system
steps.body: Depower the SRS again before reconnecting the designated airbag connectors and all remaining connectors. Follow the SRS repowering procedure and complete its prove-out check.

watchFor.title: Accidental airbag deployment
watchFor.body: Incorrect restraint-system handling can cause serious injury. Keep the prescribed airbag isolation through the intermediate powered tests.

watchFor.title: Repeated heat/cool switching
watchFor.body: Repeatedly cycling heating or alternating heat and cool can induce overtemperature codes.

notes: Blower filters are integral to their assemblies and are not separately serviceable.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B19A5 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The passenger cushion blower speed-control circuit is the diagnostic target.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test V.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B19A6 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A passenger backrest blower speed-control short to ground has been detected.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test W.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B19A7 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A driver cushion blower speed-control short to ground has been detected.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test X.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B19A8 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A driver backrest blower speed-control short to ground has been detected.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test Y.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B272A is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Passenger cushion blower overtemperature caused seat shutdown; this does not establish blower failure.
diagnostics.next: Continue overtemperature diagnosis, considering wiring, filter restriction, crushed or restricted cushion foam, the blower and SCME. Tests V–Y do not resolve this thermal branch.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record resistance readings, the substitution result and whether connector repair restored operation.

verification.title: Confirm SRS prove-out
verification.body: Successful prove-out completes the selected test. If it fails, continue with SRS diagnosis before returning the vehicle.

guides.title: Diagnose passenger climate-controlled seat faults B272A and B272B
guides.summary: Distinguish restricted airflow, damaged temperature-sensor wiring, blower assembly faults and module problems in the passenger cushion and backrest.
guides.introduction: Climate-controlled seats draw cabin air through filtered blower assemblies, heat or cool it, and distribute it through the foam. The front seat climate control module (SCME) controls blower speed and monitors thermistors—temperature-sensitive resistors. Test Z investigates the passenger cushion under B272A; Test AA investigates the passenger backrest under B272B.
guides.why: Restricted foam can cause genuine overheating, while faulty sensing can report a sudden temperature jump. Comparing airflow, temperature trends and isolated electrical measurements helps identify which repair is justified.

when.summary: Use when B272A or B272B accompanies a passenger-seat heating, cooling or shutdown concern.
notes: Occupying the seat may be necessary to reproduce a restriction caused by crushed foam.

prepare.title: Diagnostic equipment and access
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of SCME self-tests and live temperature data, a digital multimeter and an inductive current probe. Some branches require seat and upholstery removal.

prepare.title: Airbag-system capability
prepare.detail: Follow the linked Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) depowering and repowering procedures exactly. Incorrect seat-harness work can deploy an airbag. Disconnect passenger airbag in-line connector C219 only within the prescribed sequence.

steps.title: Choose the cushion or backrest branch
steps.body: Start the engine, select passenger HIGH heat and run the SCME self-test. An on-demand B272A goes to Z2; B272B goes to AA2. These begin with thermistor circuits. If the relevant code is absent, turn the seat off, clear SCME codes and proceed to temperature monitoring.

steps.title: Reproduce the concern under occupancy
steps.body: Monitor PBKTEMP for the passenger backrest and PCSHTEMP for the cushion. Run HIGH heat for at least 15 minutes while occupying the seat. Gradual rises staying within 15° C (27° F) indicate no current fault. A gradual excessive rise in the affected area leads to airflow checks; a sudden jump leads to thermistor testing.

steps.title: Compare airflow before opening the seat
steps.body: Select HIGH cool on both seats with the engine running. Compare corresponding cushion or backrest exhaust airflow and wiggle the passenger blower harness. Speed changes identify a wiring fault. If airflow initially matches, compare again with both seats occupied: reduced passenger airflow then calls for the corresponding foam pad. Weak initial airflow leads to obstruction and filter inspection.

steps.title: Separate thermistor faults from harness faults
steps.body: For Z2–Z4/Z16–Z17 or AA2–AA4/AA16–AA17, follow the specified SRS isolation. Check shorts to ground where directed, then compare resistance with the ambient-temperature table. Use SCME C3265B pins 2/3 for the cushion and 4/5 for the backrest. If the combined reading fails, test the blower thermistor directly at pins 5/8. A passing component means harness repair; a failing component means blower replacement. Passenger backrest sensor circuits are VHS36 and RHS20.

steps.title: Test blower power and speed control
steps.body: After obstruction checks, follow Z9–Z14 or AA9–AA14 through control continuity, unwanted voltage, grounding and open circuits. For component resistance, polarity matters: positive pin 3 and negative pin 4 must give 4,000–10,000 ohms; positive pin 7 and negative pin 4 must give 240K–400K ohms. Repair failed circuits or replace the corresponding blower assembly when its component test fails.

steps.title: Inspect installation and foam when directed
steps.body: If blower electrical checks pass, remove the [passenger seat](#/document/G1695491) and the relevant [cushion cover](#/document/G1695515) or [backrest cover](#/document/G1702539). Correct blower installation or replace crushed or restricted foam. If both are sound, reinstall the cover and seat before continuing to heating/cooling current tests.

steps.title: Check heating/cooling current and resistance
steps.body: At Z18 or AA18, reconnect the specified climate-system connectors and measure inductively around CHS07 near C3265A pin A for the cushion, or CHS06 near pin C for the backrest. On HIGH heat, 11 amps or more calls for blower replacement. Below this, test the module-to-blower path against 0.9–10 ohms, then isolate blower pins 1/2 if needed. A passing blower with a failed harness reading means wiring repair: CHS07/RHS07 for the cushion, CHS06/RHS06 for the backrest.

steps.title: Evaluate the module only after preceding checks
steps.body: Inspect SCME connectors with ignition off, repair terminal defects and latch them securely. Keep C219 disconnected during the prescribed functional retest. If the concern persists, follow an applicable technical service bulletin; otherwise the branch directs SCME replacement. Finish through Z22 or AA22, including SRS restoration.

watchFor.title: Airbag reconnection timing
watchFor.body: Do not reconnect C219 during the module functional retest. Final reconnection requires another SRS depowering sequence before repowering.

watchFor.title: Protect the harness during current measurement
watchFor.body: Open conduit only as necessary, avoid stressing wires or connectors, and close it after repairs.

notes: The SCME has a continuous voltage supply, but normal seat operation requires the engine running. Engine-off scan-tool commands operate in 15 second intervals.
The module supply circuits join internally, so both seats may operate with one supply open. Seat-specific faults disable the affected seat.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B272A is retrieved on demand.
diagnostics.meaning: Test Z directs diagnosis toward passenger cushion sensing, airflow and heating/cooling circuitry.
diagnostics.next: Begin Z2; do not select a blower or module solely from the code.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B272B is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Passenger backrest temperature exceeded 70° C (158° F) in cool mode or 85° C (185° F) in heat mode for more than 4 seconds, causing passenger-seat shutdown.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test AA to distinguish restricted airflow, sensing faults, wiring and blower faults.

diagnostics.finding: Both passenger temperature readings rise gradually and remain close during reproduction.
diagnostics.meaning: The fault is absent at that time; previous failure, repeated heat/cool switching or excessive cabin temperature may explain it.
diagnostics.next: Record the conditions and readings rather than assuming a component has failed.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B272C is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: This concerns the driver seat: a differential of 60° C (108° F) or more for more than 4 seconds, a disconnected blower or blocked duct can trigger it.
diagnostics.next: Continue driver differential-temperature diagnosis and assess both blower areas; the hotter reading may be correct. The first event invokes recovery, while recurrence after recovery in the same key cycle shuts down the driver seat.

verification.title: Restore and prove out the SRS
verification.body: At Z22 or AA22, follow SRS depowering, reconnect C219 and all remaining connectors, then follow repowering. Completion requires successful SRS prove-out; an unsuccessful result leads to SRS diagnosis.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record on-demand codes, occupied temperature trends, airflow comparisons and applicable resistance/current results, together with the repair and SRS prove-out outcome.

guides.title: Diagnose climate-controlled seat temperature mismatch: B272C and B272D
guides.summary: Trace a driver-seat B272C temperature fault through airflow, blower and electrical checks, and recognize the passenger-seat B272D fault.
guides.introduction: Each climate-controlled seat has cushion and backrest blower assemblies containing a thermoelectric device and a temperature sensor. They condition cabin air and distribute it through the foam. The front seat climate control module (SCME) monitors their temperatures. This guide follows driver-seat Pinpoint Test AB and explains the passenger fault that requires its own diagnostic route.
guides.why: The hotter blower is not necessarily faulty: the other assembly may report an incorrectly low temperature. Restricted airflow, crushed foam and electrical faults can produce similar results. Stabilized readings and separate wiring/component measurements prevent unnecessary replacement.

when.summary: When a climate-controlled seat temperature fault is recorded and the concern needs confirmation or isolation.
notes: Normal seat-button operation requires the engine running; engine-off scan-tool commands operate only in 15 second intervals.

prepare.title: Diagnostic equipment and capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting SCME self-tests and live temperature data, a multimeter and the specified Rotunda Flex Probes. Check battery/charging operation and battery state of charge above 70%.

prepare.title: Seat access and restraint precautions
prepare.detail: Be equipped for seat and upholstery removal and Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) depowering and repowering. Incorrect work can deploy airbags and cause serious injury. Follow the exact restraint procedures before the specified connector operations.

steps.title: Start with the SCME self-test
steps.body: Run the self-test in [Pinpoint Test AB](#/document/G1695509). On-demand B2729 takes priority through Test AF; B2730 through Test AG. Otherwise continue to the temperature comparison.

steps.title: Establish believable temperature readings
steps.body: With seat conditioning off, allow temperatures to stabilize. Compare driver cushion and backrest parameter identifications (PIDs), meaning scan-tool data values, against ambient and passenger readings. Apply AB2's ambient limits: suspect cushion readings lead to AB16; suspect backrest readings lead to AB32.

steps.title: Reproduce the temperature split
steps.body: Cycle the ignition, start the engine and select driver-seat high heat for at least 15 minutes while monitoring both temperatures. Occupant loading may reveal crushed foam. A difference greater than 60° C (108° F) sends a hotter cushion to AB5 or a hotter backrest to AB20.

steps.title: Check performance when no large split appears
steps.body: Follow AB4's Blower Motor Cooling Performance component test. A pass can indicate recovery caused by cabin heat, sunload or occupant loading; clear codes, repeat the self-test and check operation. A failure calls for installation, airflow-restriction and intermittent-wiring checks before clearing and retesting.

steps.title: Inspect the affected air path
steps.body: For AB5 or AB20, switch the ignition off and follow the seat-removal and appropriate cover-removal procedures. Check blower positioning, obstructions, filter restriction and crushed foam. Correct installation or replace the foam as directed; proceed electrically only when the inspection passes.

steps.title: Separate wiring faults from assembly faults
steps.body: Follow each branch's SRS isolation, connector and ignition sequence exactly. AB6–AB19 checks the backrest thermoelectric circuit, then cushion blower, speed-control and temperature-sensor circuits. AB21–AB34 checks the cushion circuit, then backrest circuits. Compare harness-inclusive measurements with component measurements to choose wiring repair or blower replacement. Preserve specified meter polarity and use the temperature-dependent sensor resistance table.

steps.title: Evaluate the module after its circuits
steps.body: At AB35, inspect SCME connectors for corrosion, damaged or displaced pins; repair and latch them securely. Keep both side-airbag in-line connectors disconnected during this operational check. If the concern remains, check applicable Technical Service Bulletins before replacing the SCME. A new module requires programmable module installation (PMI).

steps.title: Restore the restraint connections
steps.body: Follow AB36: depower the SRS before reconnecting the driver and passenger side-airbag in-line connectors and any remaining disconnected connectors, then perform SRS repowering.

watchFor.title: Misleading electrical readings
watchFor.body: Reversed meter leads can invalidate blower and speed-control resistance readings. Follow the specified polarity.

watchFor.title: Different seat, different diagnostic route
watchFor.body: Do not reuse driver Test AB connector assignments for the passenger-seat fault.

notes: Blower filters are integrated into their assemblies and are not separately serviceable.
The SCME supply circuits join internally, so both seats can still operate with one supply circuit open.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B272C is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The driver-seat temperature disagreement needs isolation; it does not identify which blower or circuit has failed.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test AB's stabilized readings, reproduction and branch-specific checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B272D is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The passenger fault can set with a temperature difference of 60° C (108° F) or more for more than 4 seconds, a disconnected blower or a blocked duct.
diagnostics.next: Use passenger-seat diagnostics to investigate airflow, wiring and blower assemblies. Initial recovery may restore operation; another occurrence after recovery in the same key cycle disables that seat.

verification.title: Confirm seat operation and record results
verification.body: Record the original codes, temperature comparisons, decisive measurements and post-repair self-test outcome. Verify normal operation; an unduplicated concern does not justify speculative replacement.

verification.title: Require successful SRS prove-out
verification.body: The repair is complete only when the SRS proves out successfully. A failed prove-out requires Airbag Supplemental Restraint System diagnosis.
