guides.title: Diagnose climate controlled front seat temperature and blower faults
guides.summary: Trace B272D, B272E and B272F through temperature readings, airflow, blower circuits and module connections before replacing parts.
guides.introduction: Each climate controlled seat has cushion and backrest blower assemblies containing a fan, a thermo-electric device and a temperature sensor called a thermistor. Air passes through filters and ducts into the foam pads. The front seat climate control module (SCME), beneath the passenger seat, controls these assemblies. Diagnosis separates restricted airflow, misleading temperature feedback and electrical faults.
guides.why: Temperature stabilization and correct meter polarity prevent false component failures. Seat wiring also includes the Supplemental Restraint System (SRS); incorrect handling can cause accidental deployment and serious injury.

when.summary: When climate controlled seat operation is faulty and the corresponding diagnostic trouble code is recorded.
notes: Reproduce the concern before following a replacement decision; a stored code alone does not establish component failure.

prepare.title: Diagnostic equipment and access
prepare.detail: Use an SCME-capable scan tool, digital multimeter, specified terminal flex probes and wiring information. Check battery/charging operation and battery state of charge above 70%. Seat and upholstery access may be required.

prepare.title: SRS capability
prepare.detail: Follow the exact depowering and connector-isolation instructions. Test AD isolates both front-seat airbag connectors; AC and AE isolate the passenger connector. These are controlled electrical tests requiring SRS service competence.

steps.title: Select the code-specific route
steps.body: Use [Front Seats diagnosis](#/document/G1695509). For B272D, begin AC1 with the SCME self-test: on-demand B272A redirects to Test Z and B272B to Test AA. Otherwise continue AC. B272E uses AD; B272F uses AE.

steps.title: Establish believable temperature readings
steps.body: For AC2, stabilize temperatures with the seats OFF. Compare passenger cushion and backrest parameter identifications (PIDs) with ambient temperature and driver-seat readings. Follow AC2's ambient limits: cushion concerns lead to AC16; backrest concerns lead to AC32.

steps.title: Reproduce the passenger-seat imbalance
steps.body: If baseline readings pass, cycle the ignition, start the engine and command passenger high heat for at least 15 minutes while monitoring temperatures. AC3 routes a difference greater than 60° C (108° F) toward the hotter cushion or backrest. Sitting on the seat may reproduce crushed-foam restriction.

steps.title: Separate airflow trouble from electrical trouble
steps.body: Without that temperature split, perform AC4's blower cooling-performance component test. A pass can indicate recovery caused by cabin heat, sunload or occupant loading; clear codes, repeat the self-test and check operation. A failure requires installation, airflow and intermittent-wiring checks. The hotter-zone branches instead begin with seat/cover removal and inspection of blower placement, filters and foam.

steps.title: Follow the selected AC circuit branch
steps.body: After prescribed SRS isolation, follow AC's voltage-short, ground-short, resistance and thermistor checks. The hotter-cushion branch checks the backrest thermo-electric circuit before cushion blower checks; the hotter-backrest branch begins with cushion circuit checks. Compare module-end and component-end results to distinguish wiring from assemblies, using the temperature/resistance table.

steps.title: Test driver or passenger blower circuits
steps.body: AD and AE check their respective seat's supply/return circuits for unwanted voltage, then opens, then both blower assemblies. Preserve the specified ignition states and meter polarity. Repair failed wiring; replace only the cushion or backrest assembly that fails its component test.

steps.title: Inspect SCME connections before condemning it
steps.body: At AC35, AD4 or AE4, switch ignition OFF and inspect module connectors. Correct corrosion, bent or pushed-out pins, replacing connectors or terminals as directed. Latch connectors securely and retest operation, leaving the specified airbag connectors disconnected.

steps.title: Resolve the module decision
steps.body: If operation returns, address the connector fault's root cause. If the concern remains, check applicable technical service bulletins and follow any matching bulletin. Otherwise follow the SCME replacement route; a new SCME requires programmable module installation.

watchFor.title: Misleading resistance readings
watchFor.body: Blower and speed-control measurements require the stated positive and negative lead positions; reversed leads can falsely condemn an assembly.

watchFor.title: Restricted air distribution
watchFor.body: Crushed foam or obstructed ducts can upset temperatures even when the electrical components work.

notes: The blower filter is integrated and is not separately serviceable.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B272D is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test AC investigates passenger-seat temperature feedback, imbalance and blower performance.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the AC1 prerequisite codes before temperature comparison or circuit testing.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B272E is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: This driver-seat blower circuit fault can reflect opens or shorts to voltage despite its short-to-ground description.
diagnostics.next: Use AD; a single-blower open can also set the code when SCME supply voltage is below 12 volts.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B272F is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: This is the corresponding passenger-seat blower circuit fault, with the same open-circuit and supply-voltage distinctions.
diagnostics.next: Use AE's passenger connectors and measurements.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B2729 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Driver cushion overtemperature has caused shutdown; airflow restriction, wiring, the blower or SCME may contribute.
diagnostics.next: Use the B2729 diagnostic route. Passenger-seat Test AC does not replace that diagnosis.

verification.title: Restore and prove out the SRS
verification.body: At AC36, AD5 or AE5, depower before reconnecting the isolated airbag connectors and other disconnected connectors. Repower using the prescribed procedure. An unsuccessful SRS prove-out requires SRS diagnosis.

verification.title: Record the outcome
verification.body: Record readings, the repair and SRS prove-out. For AC4's completion path, clear codes, repeat the self-test and verify normal seat operation before release.

guides.title: Replace and program the driver memory seat module
guides.summary: Replace the driver front seat module, complete its programming, and establish the seat travel limits.
guides.introduction: The driver front seat module (DSM) controls the memory-equipped driver power seat. It receives adjustment requests, powers the appropriate motors and uses motor position signals to track seat movement. It also supports stored positions and easy entry/exit. Replacement therefore involves both a physical module change and an electronic setup process; installing the module alone does not finish the repair.
guides.why: Programmable module installation (PMI) must begin while the original module is still connected so the scan tool can carry out the required configuration process. After replacement, the module also needs established travel limits. These soft stops halt movement just before the mechanical end stops, reducing unnecessary stress on the seat and motors.
searchTerms: memory seat moves in short bursts

when.summary: When diagnosis establishes that the driver memory seat module requires replacement.
notes: A non-memory power seat uses direct switch control and does not follow this DSM replacement path.
PMI and the replacement-specific travel-learning steps apply when installing a new module.

prepare.title: Provide programming capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of DSM PMI. Keep the original module installed until the initial programming stage has begun; if it cannot communicate, the tool may request As-Built Data.

prepare.title: Provide access and controlled tightening
prepare.detail: The seat must move fully rearward and upward for access. Have suitable screw tools and a torque tool capable of the module's low tightening value.

steps.title: Begin programming with the original module
steps.body: When fitting a new DSM, start PMI with the existing DSM installed and follow the scan-tool prompts. Do this before disconnecting the module. Follow any As-Built Data request if the original module does not respond.

steps.title: Position the driver seat
steps.body: Move the seat to its fully rearward and fully upward position. This creates the working access shown in the [replacement procedure](#/document/G1695506). The left-hand-drive illustration also applies to the similar right-hand-drive arrangement.

steps.title: Remove the module
steps.body: Disconnect the DSM electrical connectors, then remove its screws and lift out the module. Keep the operation focused on the module and its attachments.

steps.title: Install and reconnect
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence to fit the DSM. Tighten its screws to 18 lb.in (2 Nm), then restore the electrical connections.

steps.title: Complete module programming
steps.body: For a new DSM, finish PMI using the diagnostic scan tool and its on-screen instructions. This completes the electronic configuration stage of replacement.

steps.title: Establish the seat's soft stops
steps.body: With a new module installed, operate the seat in every direction through its full travel. Follow the [hard-stop and soft-stop description](#/document/G1695508) when establishing the limits. The module learns a stopping position before the physical end of travel to prevent premature stopping after the vehicle is returned.

watchFor.title: Premature stopping after replacement
watchFor.body: Do not treat a short travel range as an acceptable finished result. Complete programming and the required full-travel operation.

watchFor.title: Different seat systems
watchFor.body: Seat heating and cooling are controlled by a separate climate-controlled seat module; a temperature complaint does not by itself identify a DSM fault.

notes: Travel limits also require setting or resetting after replacement of the driver seat track or horizontal motor.

diagnostics.finding: A seat motor moves briefly, stops, and requires the switch to be released and pressed again.
diagnostics.meaning: This is jog mode, associated with loss of a motor position-sensor signal; a diagnostic trouble code is stored in the DSM.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the position-sensor fault before deciding that the DSM itself needs replacement.

diagnostics.finding: The original DSM does not respond during PMI.
diagnostics.meaning: The scan tool may need As-Built Data to continue the replacement configuration.
diagnostics.next: Follow the scan-tool prompts rather than omitting the initial PMI stage.

verification.title: Confirm learned travel
verification.body: Check that the seat has been operated through its full range in every direction and does not stop prematurely.

verification.title: Record setup completion
verification.body: Record completion of PMI and the full-travel soft-stop setting operation for the new module.

procedures.purpose: Driver front seat module removal, installation, replacement programming and travel-limit setup.
Memory-seat operation, position-sensor jog mode and DSM hard-stop/soft-stop behavior.

guides.title: Replace the front head restraint guide sleeves
guides.summary: Remove and discard the front head restraint guide sleeves, then install new sleeves in their correct positions and refit the restraint.
guides.introduction: The head restraint posts slide through guide sleeves at the top of the front seat backrest. These sleeves guide movement and incorporate the release features used when removing or installing the restraint. This is a mechanical replacement job whose success depends on using new sleeves and keeping their different positions straight.
guides.why: The sleeves must be discarded after removal. Reusing them can cause difficult head restraint adjustment and component failure. The sleeves are also not interchangeable: a sleeve that appears similar still must be installed in its correct position. Those requirements matter more than the small size of the parts might suggest.
searchTerms: front head restraint guide sleeve replacement

when.summary: When a front head restraint guide sleeve needs replacement or has been removed during related work.
notes: Any removed guide sleeve requires replacement with a new sleeve.

prepare.title: Have new, position-correct sleeves
prepare.detail: Identify which replacement sleeve belongs in each position before fitting it. Keep that distinction clear while removing the old parts.

prepare.title: Prepare the removal tool
prepare.detail: Have the specified flat-headed screwdriver and access to the top of the seat backrest. Use the linked procedure for the sleeve removal operation.

steps.title: Release and remove the head restraint
steps.body: Depress the locking tabs and remove the head restraint. This clears its posts from the sleeves and gives access to the parts being replaced.

steps.title: Remove and discard the guide sleeves
steps.body: Remove the sleeves using the flat-headed screwdriver as directed in [Front Head Restraint Guide Sleeve](#/document/G1695520). Discard the removed sleeves immediately so they cannot be mistaken for parts suitable for reinstallation.

steps.title: Fit the new sleeves in their correct positions
steps.body: Install the new guide sleeves, matching each sleeve to its intended position. Do not swap them merely because both guide a head restraint post; their installation positions are not interchangeable.

steps.title: Refit the head restraint
steps.body: Depress the locking tabs and install the head restraint through the new guides. Complete this release-and-insertion action without treating resistance as a reason to interchange the sleeves.

watchFor.title: Difficult adjustment after installation
watchFor.body: Recheck that new sleeves were used and that each occupies its correct position. Difficult adjustment is a stated consequence of reusing sleeves.

watchFor.title: Misreading the illustration
watchFor.body: The illustration represents a typical sleeve arrangement. The backrest cushion is removed for clarity; that note is not an instruction to remove the cushion.

notes: The central replacement requirements are new sleeves, correct positions and use of the locking tabs when refitting the restraint.

diagnostics.finding: A guide sleeve has been removed.
diagnostics.meaning: It must be discarded even if no obvious damage is visible.
diagnostics.next: Install a new sleeve in the correct position.

verification.title: Check parts and positions
verification.body: Confirm all removed sleeves were discarded and the installed replacements occupy their correct positions.

verification.title: Check the refitted restraint
verification.body: Confirm the head restraint has been installed using the locking tabs and check for difficult adjustment, the condition highlighted by the installation warning.

procedures.purpose: Front head restraint removal, guide sleeve removal and discard, and installation of new position-specific sleeves.

guides.title: Replace the front-seat backrest blower on climate-controlled seats
guides.summary: Replace the backrest blower assembly while protecting the upholstery, reconnecting its air manifold and forming the specified tie-strap clearance.
guides.introduction: Each climate-controlled front seat has separate cushion and backrest blower assemblies. The backrest assembly draws cabin air through an integrated filter, heats or cools it with a thermoelectric device (TED), and sends it through a manifold into the foam pad. Its fan, TED and temperature sensor work under seat-system control. This repair replaces the backrest assembly after diagnosis has identified it as the repair target.
guides.why: Access requires lifting the upholstery without pulling its hook-and-loop fastening strips out of the foam. Correct manifold engagement restores the air path, while the installation-specific tie-strap position and temporary spacer establish the required loop clearance.

when.summary: Diagnosis identifies the front-seat backrest blower assembly as requiring replacement.
notes: Weak heating or cooling alone does not establish blower failure.
The blower's integrated air filter is not separately serviceable.

prepare.title: Plan complete seat removal
prepare.detail: Use the linked Front Seat procedure for removal, electrical precautions and reinstallation. Be capable of handling the complete seat and releasing upholstery retainers without damaging the cover or foam.

prepare.title: Prepare the installation items
prepare.detail: Have the replacement blower assembly, a tie strap and a 1 in x 1/8 in section of flat metal stock available. Identify whether the seat has a snorkel before releasing the cover straps.

steps.title: Remove the seat and clear the harnesses
steps.body: Remove the complete front seat using the [Front Seat procedure](#/document/G1695491). Release the electrical connector retainers and position the wire harnesses aside to clear access to the backrest cover.

steps.title: Release the cover straps and insert
steps.body: Detach the backrest cover straps. If a snorkel is fitted, route the straps out through it before positioning the cover aside. Release the pin-type retainers, remove the backrest cover insert and position the cover upward. Move the snorkel aside, if equipped.

steps.title: Lift the upholstery carefully
steps.body: Release the J-clip and draw the cover out from between the seat cushion and backrest cushion. Separate the hook-and-loop strips carefully, then lift the cover. Pulling the cover away forcefully can tear the fastening strips from the foam pad.

steps.title: Disconnect the blower
steps.body: Remove the tie strap. Release the wire-harness retainer and disconnect the blower electrical connector, then disconnect the blower manifold from the backrest cushion. These connections must be free before releasing the assembly.

steps.title: Release the blower retainers
steps.body: Release the horizontal retainer followed by the vertical retainers and remove the blower. Keep track of their engagement points so the replacement can be secured by reversing the removal sequence.

steps.title: Install the blower and form the tie-strap loop
steps.body: Refit the blower, reconnect its manifold and electrical connector, and restore the harness retainer. Use the revised tie-strap location for every installation: around the backrest wire-support framework beside the cushion, next to the white retainer. Follow the [installation detail](#/document/G1695511): place the strap, insert the 1 in x 1/8 in flat metal stock into its opening, tighten the strap, then withdraw the stock.

steps.title: Restore the cover and reinstall the seat
steps.body: Reverse the remaining cover operations, restoring the hook-and-loop strips, J-clip, insert retainers and straps. Return the snorkel and route the cover straps through it where fitted. Restore the harness retainers and reinstall the seat using its dedicated procedure.

watchFor.title: Foam attachment damage
watchFor.body: If a hook-and-loop strip starts lifting from the foam, stop pulling and separate the cover fastening more carefully.

watchFor.title: Incorrect strap position or clearance
watchFor.body: Use the installation-specific loop location, including on seats without a snorkel. Tighten with the flat stock in place and remove it afterward.

notes: The method is common to either front seat; the snorkel adds the specified strap-routing and access operations.

diagnostics.finding: An overtemperature fault remains stored although seat heating or cooling has recovered
diagnostics.meaning: Recovery can leave a stored fault. Repeated mode changes or extreme cabin heat can provoke this behavior.
diagnostics.next: Evaluate the climate-controlled-seat concern before concluding that the blower requires replacement.

verification.title: Check the completed assembly
verification.body: Confirm blower retainer engagement, manifold connection, electrical connection, harness retention and cover attachments. Verify that the tie-strap spacer has been removed.

verification.title: Check seat-climate response
verification.body: After completing seat installation, check response to the selected heating or cooling setting with ignition ON. Avoid repeated heat/cool toggling, which can induce overtemperature recovery.

procedures.purpose: Backrest blower removal and installation, including snorkel branches and revised tie-strap placement.
Complete front-seat removal and reinstallation required for blower access.
Climate-controlled-seat operation, blower assembly construction and overtemperature recovery behavior.

applicability.equipment: Climate-controlled front seats, with or without a backrest blower snorkel

guides.title: Replace a Recaro front-seat backrest cover
guides.summary: Remove the seat, trim attachments and side airbag to replace the Recaro backrest cover while preserving its foam attachments and airbag deployment path.
guides.introduction: The backrest cover is secured over the foam by clips, hooks and hook-and-loop strips. On a seat with a side airbag, the cover also forms part of the intended deployment arrangement. This job replaces the upholstery or removes it for backrest access; it includes separate finishing branches for Recaro and GT 350 Recaro seats.
guides.why: A damaged side-airbag seat cover must be replaced rather than repaired because alterations can affect airbag deployment. Careful separation of the cover also protects attachment strips and hooks embedded in the foam. Pulling too hard can turn a cover job into additional foam damage.

when.summary: When a Recaro backrest cover is damaged or must be removed for backrest service.
notes: Cleaning is permitted; repairing a trim cover on a seat equipped with a side airbag is prohibited.
The left-hand-drive driver seat is illustrated; other seating positions are similar.

prepare.title: Arrange seat and airbag service capability
prepare.detail: Have the complete front-seat and Recaro side-airbag procedures available. Airbag removal requires the relevant supplemental restraint system service capability and the safety prerequisites in that procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare trim tools and replacement parts
prepare.detail: Prepare tools for the guide bolt and trim attachments. Have a new cover when replacing damaged upholstery; inspect bezels before deciding whether they can be reused.

steps.title: Remove the front seat
steps.body: Follow [Front Seat](#/document/G1695491) to remove the assembly. This establishes access for the backrest work.

steps.title: Remove the guide and surrounding bezels
steps.body: If fitted, remove the safety-belt guide by removing its cover and bolt. Remove the front pass-through bezels, then the rear bezels, inspecting both sets for damage and replacing them as necessary. Remove the backrest release-handle bezel.

steps.title: Remove the side airbag
steps.body: Follow [Recaro Seat Side Airbag](#/document/G1709237) before releasing the upholstery. Use that procedure for the airbag's safety requirements, removal and later installation.

steps.title: Free the lower cover attachments
steps.body: Detach the J-clip from the backrest frame and release the cover from the carrier hooks. Carefully release the hook-and-loop strips and hook-and-arrow attachments, then position the cover upward. Avoid pulling their anchors out of the foam.

steps.title: Follow the correct Recaro finishing branch
steps.body: Use the Recaro or GT 350 Recaro branch in [Backrest Cover Removal and Installation](#/document/G1695529). Each requires careful release of the remaining hook-and-loop strips before removing the cover. Remove the backrest carrier only if required.

steps.title: Inspect the airbag deployment area
steps.body: Before installation, inspect the side airbag, its cavity, mounting surface and deployment chute. Remove all foreign material. Replace a damaged airbag or damaged deployment chute rather than reinstalling it.

steps.title: Reassemble in reverse order
steps.body: Refit the carrier if removed, secure the cover attachments, and reinstall the airbag through its dedicated procedure. Refit the bezels, release-handle trim and safety-belt guide where fitted, then reinstall the seat through the front-seat procedure.

watchFor.title: Foam attachments beginning to lift
watchFor.body: Take care during separation: hook-and-loop strips and hook-and-arrow anchors can tear out of the foam pad.

watchFor.title: Damaged or contaminated deployment area
watchFor.body: Resolve damage and remove foreign material before closing the backrest; either can interfere with side-airbag deployment.

notes: Use the seat-specific branch. General information about power, memory or climate-controlled seats does not establish that those features are fitted to a Recaro seat.

verification.title: Confirm deployment-area condition
verification.body: Confirm that the airbag, cavity, mounting surface and chute passed inspection, foreign material was removed, and damaged components were replaced.

verification.title: Confirm trim and seat reassembly
verification.body: Check that the cover attachments and bezels are engaged without torn foam anchors, and that the airbag and seat installation procedures are complete.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the backrest cover using the Recaro or GT 350 Recaro branch.
Remove the complete front seat before upholstery work and reinstall it afterward.
Safely remove and reinstall the side airbag fitted to Recaro seats.

applicability.equipment: Recaro and GT 350 Recaro front seats; seat side-airbag removal is required.

guides.title: Replace a front seat backrest cover
guides.summary: Replace the backrest upholstery while preserving its foam attachments, wiring and side-airbag deployment path.
guides.introduction: The backrest cover fits over the foam and is secured by several different attachments, including hook-and-loop strips, J-shaped clips and hog rings. It also surrounds the side-airbag deployment chute. Where climate-controlled seating is fitted, blower components and cover straps add another layer of routing to preserve during removal.
guides.why: This is upholstery work with a restraint-system consequence. A damaged cover on a seat equipped with a side airbag must be replaced, not repaired; cleaning is permissible. Incorrect cover or chute work can interfere with airbag deployment. Pulling aggressively at hook-and-loop attachments can also tear their mating strips from the foam.

when.summary: When the backrest cover needs replacement or removal for access beneath the upholstery.
notes: Safety-belt guides, belt straps and blower-snorkel operations apply only where those parts are fitted.

prepare.title: Complete the seat-removal prerequisite
prepare.detail: Arrange removal and refitting through [Front Seat](#/document/G1695491), following its complete prerequisites. This work requires competence around seat side airbags; upholstery instructions are not an electrical-disconnection shortcut.

prepare.title: Prepare upholstery and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Have hog ring pliers and suitable torque equipment available. Use a new cover when replacement is required, and be prepared to replace any damaged side airbag or deployment chute discovered during inspection.

steps.title: Remove the seat and guide sleeves
steps.body: Remove the front seat through its linked procedure, then remove the [head restraint guide sleeves](#/document/G1695520). Continue with the [backrest-cover procedure](#/document/G1702539) once those access operations are complete.

steps.title: Clear the belt guides and release-handle trim
steps.body: Remove the inner safety-belt guide if fitted. For an outer guide, remove its cover and front and rear bolts; both bolts have an installation torque of 106 lb.in (12 Nm). Remove the seat release-handle bezel.

steps.title: Free the wiring, straps and insert
steps.body: Release the electrical-connector retainers and move the harnesses aside. Position the cover to detach its straps, routing them out through the blower snorkel if fitted. Move the cover aside, release the insert's pin retainers and position the cover upward. Move the snorkel aside where present.

steps.title: Release the lower cover attachment
steps.body: Release the J-clip and draw the cover out from between the seat cushion and backrest cushion. Carefully separate the hook-and-loop strips and move the cover upward without pulling the foam-mounted strips loose.

steps.title: Free the deployment chute and remaining retainers
steps.body: Detach the side-airbag deployment-chute retainers and pull the chute through the backrest foam. Release the cover J-clips, move the cover upward, release the J-clip from the frame and remove the hog rings.

steps.title: Remove the cover from the foam
steps.body: Position the safety-belt strap as needed where fitted. Carefully separate the remaining hook-and-loop attachment and remove the cover, keeping the foam's attachment strips intact.

steps.title: Inspect and reassemble
steps.body: Inspect the side airbag, its cavity, mounting surface and deployment chute. Remove all foreign material; replace a damaged airbag or damaged chute. Reverse removal, using hog ring pliers and restoring the chute, cover attachments, straps, snorkel and harness retainers before completing guide-sleeve and seat installation.

watchFor.title: Foam attachment strips lifting
watchFor.body: Stop pulling if a hook-and-loop strip begins lifting from the foam. The cover must separate at the fastening surfaces.

watchFor.title: Deployment-path damage or contamination
watchFor.body: Do not close the upholstery over foreign material or damaged airbag components. The required inspection must be resolved before assembly.

notes: The illustrated seat is the left-hand-drive driver's seat; the other seats follow a similar procedure.
The blower illustrations show a snorkel, but its presence must be checked on the actual seat.

verification.title: Confirm complete restoration
verification.body: Check that the deployment chute and all cover attachments are restored, harnesses are retained, and fitted straps and blower components follow their original routing.

verification.title: Record the airbag-area inspection
verification.body: Record the condition of the airbag, cavity, mounting surface and chute, including foreign material removed and any damaged components replaced.

procedures.purpose: Backrest-cover removal, deployment-chute inspection and upholstery installation.
Required front-seat removal and installation surrounding the upholstery work.
Required head-restraint guide-sleeve removal and installation.

guides.title: Replace the front seat backrest release handle
guides.summary: Remove the backrest trim and foam to replace the release handle and restore its cable connection to the recline mechanism.
guides.introduction: The backrest release handle operates a cable connected to the recline mechanism. The handle, cable conduit and cable attachment work together to transmit hand movement to that mechanism. Access requires removal of the backrest cover and foam, with additional steps for Recaro seats and seats with a backrest blower manifold. Most of the work involves uncovering the mechanism without losing the original trim and cable arrangement.
guides.why: The cable’s conduit must be anchored as well as its inner cable connected, so handle movement reaches the recline mechanism correctly. Foam must be moved away from the handle before it can be removed. Where a safety belt guide strap is fitted, retaining its original position is an explicit reassembly requirement.
searchTerms: front seat backrest release handle replacement

when.summary: When the backrest release handle requires replacement or removal during a confirmed mechanical seat repair.
notes: Identify the seat type before selecting the cover and upper-foam removal branches.

prepare.title: Plan the cover-removal work
prepare.detail: Have the appropriate standard-seat or Recaro backrest-cover procedure available and the capability to complete its access and safety requirements.

prepare.title: Preserve the installed arrangement
prepare.detail: Note the cable route, conduit mounting and any safety belt guide strap position before moving the foam. Allow working space for the removed cover and foam.

steps.title: Remove the matching backrest cover
steps.body: Follow the standard [Backrest Cover procedure](#/document/G1702539) or the [Recaro procedure](#/document/G1695529), according to the fitted seat. This exposes the foam and the components surrounding the handle.

steps.title: Follow the equipment-specific foam branch
steps.body: If fitted, disconnect the backrest blower motor manifold from the backrest cushion. Recaro seats require upper-backrest foam removal. On the GT 350 Recaro branch, first pull that foam away from the release handle, then remove it.

steps.title: Remove the remaining backrest foam
steps.body: Record the safety belt guide strap position if present. Pull the backrest foam away from the backrest, then lift it free. This opens access to the release cable and handle mountings.

steps.title: Disconnect the cable at the mechanism
steps.body: Detach the cable conduit and disconnect the cable from the recline mechanism. Position the released cable as directed so the handle can be removed without pulling against its remaining attachments.

steps.title: Remove the handle mountings
steps.body: Remove the release handle’s front bolts. Remove the cable mounting tie strap and the handle’s side bolts, then remove the handle. Keep track of the different mounting locations for reassembly.

steps.title: Rebuild in reverse order
steps.body: Install the handle and restore its side mountings, cable mounting strap and front mountings. Reconnect the cable and anchor its conduit. Refit the foam, preserving the belt guide strap position, reconnect any blower manifold and reinstall the appropriate backrest cover.

watchFor.title: Foam still caught around the handle
watchFor.body: On the GT 350 Recaro seat, clear the upper foam from the handle before lifting it away.

watchFor.title: An unanchored cable conduit
watchFor.body: Reconnect both the cable and its conduit during reverse assembly; attaching only the cable leaves the original arrangement incomplete.

notes: The illustrated left-hand-drive power driver seat is representative; other seats follow the corresponding equipment branches.

verification.title: Check the concealed connections
verification.body: Before the cover conceals them, confirm the handle mountings, cable mounting strap, conduit attachment and recline-mechanism connection are restored.

verification.title: Check the seat-specific restoration
verification.body: Confirm the foam is back in position, the safety belt guide strap matches its original placement and any disconnected blower manifold is reconnected.

procedures.purpose: Release-handle removal and reverse installation, including cable, foam and seat-equipment branches.
Standard front seat backrest-cover removal and installation for handle access.
Recaro front seat backrest-cover removal and installation for handle access.

applicability.equipment: Standard or Recaro front seats, including GT 350 Recaro seats; backrest blower manifold where fitted

guides.title: Remove and refit a front seat backrest
guides.summary: Remove the complete front seat, follow the appropriate trim branch, and detach and reinstall the backrest with its wiring and cover straps correctly routed.
guides.introduction: The backrest is a structural part of the front seat, attached to the lower seat assembly behind the recliner trim. Depending on equipment, it also contains wiring and a climate-control blower. This job separates the backrest from the removed seat; the access sequence differs between a manual driver seat, a manual passenger seat and power seats.
guides.why: The side shields use different release arrangements, so pulling every version in the same direction can load its retainers incorrectly. Wiring and cover straps must be moved clear before the backrest is detached. Correct mounting is critical: objects between seat components, inside structural joints or between the seat and vehicle body can prevent proper installation and increase injury risk.
searchTerms: front seat recline handle retaining clip

when.summary: When a front seat repair requires the backrest to be separated from the lower seat assembly.
notes: The procedure illustrates the left-hand-drive driver seat; other seats are similar except for the stated trim branches.

prepare.title: Complete-seat removal capability
prepare.detail: Use the [Front Seat procedure](#/document/G1695491) for removal and installation of the whole seat, including its safety and electrical prerequisites. Complete that prerequisite before starting backrest separation.

prepare.title: Fasteners and structural assembly
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the seat trim and backrest fasteners and a torque wrench for installation. Keep all structural mating surfaces and joints free of objects.

prepare.title: Identify the seat branch
prepare.detail: Establish whether the seat is power-operated, a manual driver seat or a manual passenger seat. Look for an optional height handle, electrical side-shield connection and backrest blower snorkel.

steps.title: Remove the complete seat
steps.body: Follow [Front Seat removal](#/document/G1695491). The backrest procedure begins with the seat removed, providing access to the side trim, underside retainers and backrest attachments.

steps.title: Remove the recliner trim
steps.body: Remove the screws and recline cover. Release the retaining clip and remove the front seat recline handle. The [backrest procedure illustration](#/document/G1695510) shows the clip behind the handle.

steps.title: Release the manual driver height handle
steps.body: On a manual driver seat with a height-adjusting handle, raise the handle, release its locking tab and slide the handle forward. Complete this branch before trying to remove the side shield.

steps.title: Remove the correct side shield
steps.body: Remove the side-shield screws. For power seats and the manual driver seat, lift the shield's rear upward and outward, push it forward, and disconnect its electrical connector if fitted. For a manual passenger seat, pull the rear outward, lift up and out of the recliner bracket, squeeze the underside retainers together while pulling outward, then slide the shield forward.

steps.title: Clear wiring and cover straps
steps.body: On all seats, release the electrical connector retainers and position the harnesses aside. Detach the backrest cover straps. Where a backrest blower snorkel is fitted, route the straps out through it, then move the cover aside.

steps.title: Detach the backrest
steps.body: With wiring and cover attachments clear, support the backrest, remove its mounting bolts and remove it from the seat assembly. Keep the mounting joints clear for reassembly.

steps.title: Reassemble the seat
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Tighten the backrest bolts to 33 lb.ft (45 Nm), restore the straps through the snorkel where fitted, and refit harness retainers, connectors, shields and handles. Reinstall the complete seat using the [Front Seat procedure](#/document/G1695491).

watchFor.title: A shield that remains attached
watchFor.body: Check the seat-specific release sequence, especially the manual passenger seat's underside retainers.

watchFor.title: Trapped wiring or straps
watchFor.body: Restore routing before closing the trim so the harnesses and cover attachments are not caught in the backrest joint.

notes: The snorkel routing applies only where that blower arrangement is fitted.

verification.title: Check structural assembly
verification.body: Confirm the backrest bolts were tightened correctly and no objects remain within seat joints or between the seat and vehicle body.

verification.title: Check trim and routing
verification.body: Confirm cover straps, harness retainers, electrical connectors, handles and shields are restored for the fitted seat.

verification.title: Record installation completion
verification.body: Record the backrest bolt tightening and completion of the separate whole-seat installation procedure.

procedures.purpose: Backrest removal and installation, including manual-driver, manual-passenger, power-seat and optional blower-snorkel branches.
Required complete front-seat removal before backrest work and complete-seat installation afterward.

guides.title: Replace the climate controlled seat module (SCME)
guides.summary: Replace the module beneath the front passenger seat and complete its scan-tool programming when installing a new unit.
guides.introduction: The front seat climate control module (SCME) manages heating and cooling for both front seats independently of the cabin climate system. Each cushion and backrest contains a blower assembly with a thermoelectric device that changes the temperature of the passing air. The module uses temperature feedback and the selected setting to control these assemblies. Replacing it involves both connector work beneath the passenger seat and, for a new module, transferring the vehicle configuration through programmable module installation (PMI).
guides.why: The programming sequence begins before the original module is disconnected. Starting at that point allows the diagnostic tool to obtain the information needed for replacement. Mechanical access is straightforward, but the connector locking wedges must be released before disconnection and secured again during installation.

when.summary: When diagnosis justifies SCME replacement or the existing module needs removal.
notes: Loss of seat heating or cooling alone does not establish that the module has failed.
The illustrated access is for a left-hand-drive passenger seat; the right-hand-drive passenger seat procedure is similar.

prepare.title: Arrange programming capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of performing SCME PMI. Leave the current module installed until the initial programming stage is complete. If it does not communicate, the tool may request As-Built Data.

prepare.title: Prepare under-seat access
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the module screws and enough access to operate the connector locking wedges. The passenger seat must be moved fully upward and rearward.

steps.title: Begin PMI before removing a module being replaced
steps.body: When installing a new component, begin SCME PMI with the current module still installed and follow the scan-tool prompts. This initial stage is not required merely to remove and reinstall the existing module.

steps.title: Move the passenger seat into the access position
steps.body: Position the seat fully upward and fully rearward. This exposes the module beneath the seat; the attached illustration shows the required seat movements.

steps.title: Release the module and its connectors
steps.body: Following the [removal procedure](#/document/G1695512), remove the screws and position the module aside. Release the connector locking wedges, disconnect the electrical connectors and remove the module.

steps.title: Install and finish programming
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence to reconnect and secure the module. When fitting a new unit, complete SCME PMI using the diagnostic scan tool and follow its remaining instructions.

watchFor.title: Forced connector removal
watchFor.body: A connector that remains retained needs its locking wedge released; pulling harder does not replace this step.

watchFor.title: Repeated heat and cool switching
watchFor.body: Repeatedly restarting heating or alternating heating and cooling can induce an overtemperature condition, complicating assessment of the repair.

notes: During remote start, seat climate adjustments are ignored. Check normal control response after switching the ignition on.

diagnostics.finding: The original SCME does not respond to the scan tool.
diagnostics.meaning: The initial PMI process may be unable to retrieve its configuration normally.
diagnostics.next: Follow the scan tool's As-Built Data prompts if presented.

diagnostics.finding: An overtemperature fault is stored.
diagnostics.meaning: A fault can remain recorded after the seat has recovered and resumed normal operation.
diagnostics.next: Consider the operating circumstances and recovery behavior before treating the code as evidence for module replacement.

verification.title: Confirm installation and programming
verification.body: Confirm the connectors and locking wedges are secured and the module is fastened. For a replacement module, record successful completion of PMI.

verification.title: Check normal seat climate response
verification.body: With the ignition on, confirm the front-seat controls produce the expected heating or cooling response without repeatedly toggling modes.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the SCME beneath the passenger seat, including the programming stages required for a new module.
Explain climate controlled seat operation, temperature feedback and overtemperature recovery behavior.
Identify climate controlled seat components and explain remote-start operating restrictions.

guides.title: Replace a front power-seat adjustment switch
guides.summary: Release the seat's side shield, disconnect its wiring, and replace the adjustment switch behind the control knob.
guides.introduction: The seat control switch translates the selected adjustment into seat movement. On a non-memory driver seat and the power passenger seat, it switches motor circuits directly, with electrical polarity determining direction. On a memory driver seat, it sends an input to the driver seat module (DSM), which powers the appropriate motor. Replacement requires removing the side shield and switch knob.
guides.why: The shield has a defined release movement after its screws are removed: lift its rear, pull outward, then push forward. Following that sequence protects its attachments and exposes the electrical connector. Understanding the memory-seat arrangement also helps distinguish a switch complaint from a motor-position sensor fault.
searchTerms: power seat does not respond to switch
memory seat moves briefly then stops

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies the front seat adjustment switch as requiring replacement.
notes: The left-hand-drive driver seat is illustrated; other seats use a similar removal sequence.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim and connector work
prepare.detail: Provide access to the recline-handle retaining clip, shield screws and electrical connector. Have suitable screw tools and the trim tool illustrated for knob removal.

prepare.title: Identify the seat system
prepare.detail: Determine whether the driver seat has memory, since this changes how switch inputs reach the motors.

steps.title: Remove the handle and shield screws
steps.body: Release the retaining clip and remove the front-seat recline handle. Remove the side-shield screws so the shield can be disengaged.

steps.title: Release the shield in sequence
steps.body: Lift the rear of the shield and pull outward, then push the shield forward. Disconnect its electrical connector before separating it fully from the seat.

steps.title: Remove the switch
steps.body: Remove the seat-control switch knob as illustrated. Remove the switch screws and lift the switch from the shield.

steps.title: Reassemble in reverse order
steps.body: Install the replacement switch and screws, then refit the knob. Reconnect the wiring and reverse the shield-removal sequence. Restore the shield screws, recline handle and retaining clip.

watchFor.title: A shield that remains attached
watchFor.body: Check its specified release movement and connector before pulling harder.

notes: Seat heating and cooling use separate controls; those complaints do not directly identify this adjustment switch.

diagnostics.finding: A memory seat moves for one second, stops, and moves again only after releasing and pressing the switch.
diagnostics.meaning: This jog mode indicates a seat-motor position-sensor fault and sets a diagnostic trouble code in the DSM.
diagnostics.next: Pursue the sensor fault rather than treating the repeated stopping as proof of switch failure.

verification.title: Check fit and operation
verification.body: Confirm that the shield, handle, knob and connector are secure. Operate each adjustment controlled by the replaced switch and check that movement follows the selected direction and stops when released.

procedures.purpose: Complete front-seat control-switch removal and installation.
Explains memory and non-memory switch operation and the memory-seat jog-mode distinction.

applicability.equipment: Power front seat, with or without driver-seat memory

guides.title: Replace the climate-controlled front seat cushion blower
guides.summary: Replace the cushion blower assembly and complete the passenger seat’s occupant-classification reset and restraint-system checks when applicable.
guides.introduction: The cushion blower draws cabin air through an integrated filter, heats or cools it using a thermoelectric device, and sends it through the cushion foam. The fan and thermoelectric device are serviced as an assembly, which also contains temperature sensing; the filter is not separately serviceable. Access requires seat removal and lifting the cushion cover and foam. Passenger-seat work additionally involves the occupant classification system (OCS), which informs restraint operation.
guides.why: Passenger-seat sensing parts are calibrated together. Separating a calibrated assembly or resetting it before the complete seat is rebuilt can make occupant classification incorrect. The mechanical repair, OCS reset and supplemental restraint system (SRS) prove-out therefore form a required sequence. The blower’s thermal protection behavior also means a stored temperature fault does not automatically justify replacement.

when.summary: After diagnosis establishes that the climate-controlled seat cushion blower assembly requires replacement.
notes: Passenger-seat work includes OCS reset and SRS verification after full reassembly.

prepare.title: Arrange seat and restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Follow the complete Front Seat procedure and its safety prerequisites for removal and installation. Provide working space to handle the seat and lift the cushion assembly without separating attached OCS parts.

prepare.title: Provide scan-tool and reset capability
prepare.detail: Passenger-seat work requires a diagnostic scan tool for OCS reset and clearing stored module faults, plus the ability to establish the required voltage and temperature conditions.

steps.title: Remove the seat and side trim
steps.body: Remove the front seat using its linked procedure. Release the recline-handle retaining clip and remove the handle, then remove the side-shield screws. Lift the shield’s rear upward and outward, push it forward and disconnect its electrical connector.

steps.title: Lift the cushion assembly
steps.body: Release the J-clips and raise the front of the cushion cover and foam. On the passenger seat, remove the OCS pin-type retainers and position the cover, foam and OCS upward together. A service-kit OCS is adhered to the foam and must remain with that assembly.

steps.title: Remove the blower
steps.body: Remove the cushion blower mounting screws. Disconnect its electrical connector, release the locking tabs and remove the blower assembly.

steps.title: Reassemble and install the complete seat
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, restoring the blower attachments, cushion assembly, trim and connections. Install the seat using the Front Seat procedure. For a passenger seat, defer SRS prove-out until the OCS reset sequence; first finish the entire repair, including the head restraint, side shield and vehicle installation.

steps.title: Establish conditions and reset passenger-seat sensing
steps.body: The OCS module supply must be greater than 8 volts and less than 18 volts. OCS temperature must be between 6°C and 36°C; after extreme-temperature exposure, keep the vehicle within that range for at least 30 minutes. Leave the passenger seat empty before and during reset. Wait at least 8 seconds after switching the ignition on, perform the scan-tool OCS reset, then cycle the ignition.

steps.title: Follow the reset outcome
steps.body: If the first reset succeeds, proceed to SRS prove-out. If it fails, inspect OCS wiring and connectors, the pressure-sensor hose for kinks or damage, and seat/body harness terminals and connectors. Repair concerns, perform a second reset and cycle the ignition. If that attempt fails, install a new OCS service kit through the linked sensor procedure.

steps.title: Prove out the passenger-seat restraint system
steps.body: Verify all airbags are installed and connected and the ignition is OFF. Wait 10 seconds, switch ON and watch the airbag indicator. It should illuminate continuously for approximately 6 seconds, then extinguish. Continue monitoring for approximately 30 seconds while the restraint controller completes testing.

steps.title: Finish the passenger-seat electronic checks
steps.body: Resolve any SRS faults before proceeding with other repairs. After completing the required checks, use the scan tool to clear all Continuous Memory Diagnostic Trouble Codes from all modules.

watchFor.title: Calibrated OCS assemblies
watchFor.body: Replace OCS parts only in the configuration in which they are supplied. Never separate parts of a calibrated assembly.

watchFor.title: An incomplete seat during reset
watchFor.body: Do not rezero the passenger seat while trim or attached components remain removed, or while anything rests on the cushion.

notes: The left-hand-drive driver seat is illustrated; other seats are similar, with the additional passenger-seat requirements described here.

diagnostics.finding: A temperature-related diagnostic trouble code remains after climate-seat operation recovers.
diagnostics.meaning: Thermal recovery can leave a stored fault even when operation has returned to normal. Repeated heat switching or toggling between heating and cooling can induce overheating.
diagnostics.next: Assess operating conditions and the climate-seat system behavior before condemning the blower. A protective shutdown can turn off the seat indicators and persist until the next ignition cycle.

diagnostics.finding: During SRS prove-out, the airbag indicator fails to illuminate, stays illuminated or flashes.
diagnostics.meaning: The restraint-system check has not passed; flashing may begin only after approximately 30 seconds. With an inoperative indicator, a fault may instead produce 5 sets of 5 beeps or a message-center warning.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose and repair the indicator, when applicable, and all SRS faults before proceeding with other repairs.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical restoration
verification.body: Check that the blower connector, locking tabs and screws are restored, and that the cushion, side shield, handle and seat installation are complete.

verification.title: Record the passenger-seat result
verification.body: Record the OCS reset outcome and ignition cycle. At the end of the 30-second SRS observation, confirm the indicator remains unlit with no chime or SRS message, and record completion of the stored-code clearing.

procedures.purpose: Cushion blower removal and installation, passenger OCS reset conditions and branches, SRS prove-out and stored-code clearing.
Complete front seat removal and installation, including the prerequisites for safe seat access.
OCS sensor/service-kit replacement if the second reset attempt is unsuccessful.
Climate-controlled seat blower operation, thermal recovery and shutdown behavior relevant to interpreting the complaint.

guides.title: Replace a front seat cushion cover
guides.summary: Remove the front seat and cushion trim using the correct seat and occupant-sensor branch, then complete passenger-seat reset and restraint checks.
guides.introduction: The cushion cover is secured to the foam and seat structure by several types of retainers. Beneath a passenger cushion, the Occupant Classification System (OCS) supplies information used by the restraint system. Replacing the upholstery therefore involves careful trim work and, on the passenger seat, OCS reset and Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) verification.
guides.why: Pulling the cover away carelessly can tear its attachments out of the foam. Passenger seats also differ internally: a service-kit OCS is adhered beneath the cushion foam and must move with that assembly. Its calibrated parts, pressure hose and sensor housing need protection. Resetting an incompletely assembled or occupied seat can establish an incorrect weight reference.

when.summary: When the front cushion cover requires replacement or removal for cushion service.
notes: Identify manual or power operation and whether the passenger seat has original-equipment OCS or an OCS service kit.
Follow blower-snorkel and associated trim branches only when fitted.

prepare.title: Arrange seat and restraint-system service capability
prepare.detail: Use the linked Front Seat procedure for removal, installation and its prerequisites. Passenger-seat work requires a diagnostic scan tool capable of OCS reset and clearing stored diagnostic codes.

prepare.title: Plan careful handling
prepare.detail: Identify the trim retainers, wiring attachments and OCS hose route before separating parts. Keep calibrated OCS components together in the configuration supplied.

steps.title: Remove the seat and handles
steps.body: Remove the front seat using its procedure. Release the recline-handle retaining clip and remove the handle. On a manual driver seat, raise the height handle, release its locking tab and slide the handle forward.

steps.title: Release the appropriate side shield
steps.body: Remove the shield screws. On power seats and the manual driver seat, lift the shield's rear upward and outward, push it forward and disconnect its electrical connector if fitted. On a manual passenger seat, pull the rear outward, lift up and out from the recliner bracket, squeeze the underside retainers while pulling outward, then slide the shield forward.

steps.title: Free wiring and cushion attachments
steps.body: Release electrical-connector retainers and move the harnesses aside. Where fitted, detach backrest-cover straps, route them out through the blower snorkel and move the backrest cover aside. Release the applicable J-clips, then lift the front of the cushion cover and foam assembly.

steps.title: Remove the correct cushion assembly
steps.body: For the driver seat or passenger seat with original-equipment OCS, remove the cover and foam together. With a passenger OCS service kit, keep the adhered OCS with the cushion assembly: remove the pin-type retainers, disconnect the sensor connector, carefully bend the bracket tab away and slide off the sensor. Note the hose route through the seat springs, then route the hose and sensor out between the support wires.

steps.title: Separate the cover when replacing a component
steps.body: Only when installing a new component, release the rear portion of the cover from the foam and separate the hook-and-loop strips and hook-and-arrow attachments. Work carefully so neither attachment type tears out of the foam.

steps.title: Reassemble and install the seat
steps.body: Reverse removal, restoring the hose route, wiring retainers, straps, clips, shield and handles. Install the seat through the Front Seat procedure. For an OCS service kit, bend the sensor-bracket tab back. If the passenger seat was serviced, delay SRS prove-out until the OCS reset sequence is complete.

steps.title: Prepare and perform the passenger OCS reset
steps.body: Complete all passenger-seat assembly, including the head restraint and side shield, and correctly install the seat. Keep it empty before and during reset. Voltage at the OCS module must be greater than 8 volts and less than 18 volts. OCS temperature must be within 6°C (42.8°F) to 36°C (96.7°F); after extreme temperatures, keep the vehicle within that range for at least 30 minutes. Wait at least 8 seconds after switching the ignition on, perform the scan-tool OCS reset, then cycle the ignition.

steps.title: Resolve an unsuccessful reset
steps.body: If the first reset succeeds, proceed to SRS prove-out. If it fails, inspect the OCS connector and wiring, pressure-sensor hose for kinks or damage, and seat/body harness terminals and connectors. Repair concerns, perform a second reset and cycle the ignition again. If that attempt fails, install a new OCS service kit using the linked sensor procedure.

steps.title: Prove out the restraints and clear stored codes
steps.body: Perform the SRS checks below after the passenger-seat reset sequence. Diagnose and repair any restraint faults before proceeding with other repairs. Using the scan tool, clear all Continuous Memory Diagnostic Trouble Codes (CMDTCs) from all modules.

watchFor.title: Sensor housing damage
watchFor.body: Excessive force when bending the OCS bracket tab can damage the sensor housing.

watchFor.title: Separating calibrated OCS parts
watchFor.body: Replace OCS parts only in the configuration in which they are supplied. Separating a calibrated assembly can compromise occupant classification and crash protection.

notes: The illustrated seat is the left-hand-drive driver seat; follow the specific branches for the seat being repaired.

diagnostics.finding: The airbag indicator fails to illuminate, remains illuminated or flashes during prove-out.
diagnostics.meaning: An SRS fault requires diagnosis; the indication alone does not identify a failed OCS component.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose and repair the restraint-system concern before continuing other repairs.

verification.title: Observe the complete SRS prove-out
verification.body: Verify all airbags are installed and connected. With the ignition off, wait 10 seconds, then switch it on. The airbag indicator should illuminate continuously for approximately 6 seconds and turn off. Continue monitoring for approximately 30 seconds while the restraints control module completes testing.

verification.title: Check warnings as well as the lamp
verification.body: After 30 seconds, an unlit indicator with no chime or SRS message indicates no SRS fault. An inoperative indicator with a fault can produce five sets of five beeps or a message; repair both the indicator concern and any SRS faults.

verification.title: Record the completed repair
verification.body: Record the OCS reset outcome, any corrective work or service-kit replacement, the final SRS indication/chime/message result and completion of CMDTC clearing.

procedures.purpose: Front cushion-cover removal and installation, manual/power and OCS branches, passenger OCS reset and SRS verification.
Complete front-seat removal and installation, including the prerequisites for accessing the cushion.
OCS sensor/service-kit replacement if the prescribed second reset attempt is unsuccessful.

guides.title: Replace the front seat power lumbar assembly
guides.summary: Replace the backrest-mounted lumbar unit while protecting the upholstery, wiring and side-airbag deployment chute.
guides.introduction: The power lumbar assembly changes the support behind your lower back. Its motor is serviced with the assembly, so this repair replaces the complete backrest-mounted unit. Access involves removing the seat and progressively lifting its trim cover. On seats with a backrest blower, the blower and its snorkel also affect the access route.
guides.why: The main challenge is reaching the lumbar unit without damaging the surrounding seat. Pulling the cover away carelessly can tear the hook-and-loop strips from the foam. The side-airbag deployment chute also passes through this area; its condition and correct restoration matter to how the airbag deploys in a crash.
searchTerms: power lumbar support will not adjust

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies the power lumbar assembly as requiring replacement.
notes: A lumbar adjustment complaint alone does not establish that the assembly has failed.
The illustrated left-hand-drive driver seat is representative; the other seats follow a similar procedure.

prepare.title: Establish safe seat removal
prepare.detail: Be equipped to complete the linked Front Seat removal and installation procedure and its prerequisites. This work exposes parts of the seat side-airbag deployment path.

prepare.title: Identify the fitted backrest equipment
prepare.detail: Check whether a blower and snorkel are present. Have the separate backrest blower procedure available for that branch.

prepare.title: Plan careful trim handling
prepare.detail: Be able to release pin retainers, J-clips and hook-and-loop attachments without pulling their mountings out of the foam.

steps.title: Remove the seat
steps.body: Follow the [Front Seat procedure](#/document/G1695491). With the seat accessible, release the electrical connector retainers and move the wire harnesses aside.

steps.title: Free the cover straps
steps.body: Position the backrest cover to detach its straps. Where a blower snorkel is fitted, route the straps out through it before positioning the cover aside.

steps.title: Open the rear cover access
steps.body: Release the pin-type retainers for the backrest cover insert and move the cover upward. Position the blower snorkel aside where fitted.

steps.title: Release the lower cover attachments
steps.body: Release the J-clip and draw the cover out from between the cushion and backrest. Carefully separate the hook-and-loop strips, then lift the cover; avoid tearing the strips from the foam pad.

steps.title: Free the deployment chute
steps.body: Detach the side-airbag deployment chute retainers and move them aside. Pull the chute through the backrest foam, then release the remaining backrest cover J-clips and move the cover upward.

steps.title: Remove the lumbar unit
steps.body: If fitted, remove the [backrest blower motor](#/document/G1695511). Disconnect the lumbar electrical connector, release its J-hooks and remove the assembly.

steps.title: Inspect and rebuild the backrest
steps.body: Before reversing removal, inspect the side airbag, airbag cavity, mounting surface and deployment chute. Remove all foreign material. Replace a damaged airbag or damaged deployment chute. Install the lumbar assembly and restore the blower, chute, cover attachments, straps and wiring using the [lumbar procedure](#/document/G1695516), then reinstall the seat.

watchFor.title: Airbag damage or contamination
watchFor.body: Damage or foreign material can prevent correct side-airbag deployment and increase the risk of serious injury or death in a crash.

watchFor.title: Cover resistance
watchFor.body: If the cover remains attached, locate the remaining clip, strap or hook-and-loop connection before pulling harder.

notes: The lumbar motor is serviced as part of the power lumbar assembly.
Driver seat module programming and stop-setting requirements concern other specified component replacements; this lumbar replacement procedure does not call for them.

verification.title: Confirm the deployment path is restored
verification.body: Confirm the airbag-area inspection is complete and the chute and its retainers have been restored during reassembly.

verification.title: Check the reversed removal sequence
verification.body: Confirm the lumbar J-hooks and connector, cover attachments, harness retainers and any blower or snorkel are restored before completing seat installation.

procedures.purpose: Complete power lumbar assembly removal and installation, including trim access and side-airbag-area inspection.
Front seat removal before backrest work and installation afterward.
Backrest blower removal and installation when fitted.

applicability.equipment: Front seats with power lumbar adjustment; backrest blower where fitted

guides.title: Replace the power front seat horizontal track motor
guides.summary: Replace the fore-and-aft seat motor, align both seat rails, and establish the travel stops on a memory-equipped driver seat.
guides.introduction: The horizontal seat motor drives both seat-track gearboxes through flexible cables, moving the seat forward and backward. It is the track motor that can be serviced separately; the front and rear height motors are serviced with the track assembly. Memory-equipped driver seats use a driver seat module (DSM) and motor position feedback, so replacement also requires setting the horizontal travel stops.
guides.why: Both rails must remain synchronized or the seat can bind. The motor bolts carry load, making thread condition and installation order important. Work also takes place beside seat wiring associated with the supplemental restraint system (SRS), which must be depowered before disassembly and repowered afterward.
searchTerms: power seat will not move forward or backward

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies the separately serviceable horizontal seat motor as requiring replacement.
notes: Raising the seat fully provides access with the seat remaining in the vehicle.
Memory-seat position-sensor faults require diagnosis rather than automatic motor replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Have the complete SRS depowering and repowering procedures available and be able to perform both. Raise the seat before depowering.

prepare.title: Prepare alignment and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Have an electric drill; two drills operating at similar speeds are the preferred way to drive the rails evenly. Retain the original drive cables and motor bolts for the alignment stage, and obtain new bolts for final motor installation.

steps.title: Raise the seat and depower the SRS
steps.body: Move the seat fully upward, then perform [SRS depowering](#/document/G1696297). Keep that sequence so powered seat adjustment is completed before electrical disassembly.

steps.title: Remove the trim and old motor
steps.body: Release the recline-handle clip and remove the handle and side-shield screws. Lift the shield at the rear, pull outward, move it forward and disconnect its connector. Disconnect the track motor, release the harness retainers and move the harness aside. Remove the motor bolts and motor.

steps.title: Align both seat tracks
steps.body: Install the old motor bolts for the alignment stage and tighten to 21 lb.ft (28 Nm). Insert the original motor drive cables and use the drill arrangement in the [track motor procedure](#/document/G1697264) to drive both gearboxes uniformly. Stop when the front edges of the upper and lower rails are flush on both sides. Never drive the rails to their end-of-travel stops with the drills.

steps.title: Check the inboard track block
steps.body: Remove the motor bolts on both sides after alignment. Verify that the block is present at the rear of the inboard rail. If it is missing, install a new seat track.

steps.title: Engage the replacement motor cables
steps.body: Pull the replacement motor's long cable out of its sheathing, insert it into the gearbox and rotate it to verify engagement. Insert the short cable while positioning the motor, then rotate that cable to verify engagement. Avoid severely bending the short cable.

steps.title: Secure the motor with new bolts
steps.body: Install the new bolts in this order: rear inboard, front inboard, rear outboard, front outboard. Tighten each to 21 lb.ft (28 Nm). Do not cross-thread these load-bearing bolts; cross-threading requires replacement of the seat track.

steps.title: Restore wiring, trim and restraint power
steps.body: Connect the motor and secure the harness retainers. Reconnect the side-shield connector, position the shield and push it rearward, then move its rear inward and downward. Install the screws, recline-handle clip and handle. Perform [SRS repowering](#/document/G1696298).

steps.title: Set memory-seat travel stops
steps.body: On a driver seat with memory, operate the horizontal motor in both directions through its full travel to establish the soft stops and prevent premature stopping. This powered completion step follows the earlier drill-alignment stage.

watchFor.title: Drill-driven end-stop contact
watchFor.body: Reaching a forward or rearward travel stop with the drill requires a new seat track.

watchFor.title: Uneven rail movement
watchFor.body: Drive the rails evenly. Unequal movement can cause binding and defeats the required rail alignment.

notes: Old bolts are used during alignment; new bolts are required for final motor installation.
The illustrated driver seat arrangement is representative; the other seat arrangements follow a similar procedure.

diagnostics.finding: A memory seat moves briefly, stops, and moves again only after releasing and pressing the switch.
diagnostics.meaning: This jog behavior indicates loss of motor position-sensor information, and a diagnostic trouble code is stored in the DSM.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose the position-feedback fault before deciding which component requires replacement.

verification.title: Mechanical alignment and attachment
verification.body: Confirm both pairs of rail front edges were aligned, the rear inboard block was present, and the new bolts were tightened in sequence.

verification.title: Record memory-seat initialization
verification.body: For a memory-equipped driver seat, record completion of the full horizontal travel operation used to set the soft stops.

procedures.purpose: Horizontal front seat track motor removal, rail alignment, replacement and memory-seat completion.
Required SRS depowering before seat trim, wiring and motor disassembly.
Required SRS repowering after seat reassembly.
Memory-seat position feedback, jog behavior and DSM travel-stop operation.

applicability.equipment: Power front seats; driver-seat memory where fitted

guides.title: Replace a front seat track and establish memory-seat travel limits
guides.summary: Transfer the seat components to the replacement track, handle passenger sensing equipment where fitted, and establish memory-seat soft stops.
guides.introduction: The front seat track supports and positions the seat. On power seats, its motors provide fore-and-aft movement and front and rear height adjustment. The height motors are serviced with the track assembly; the horizontal motor can be serviced separately. Replacement involves removing the backrest and cushion assembly, transferring the necessary components, and restoring any equipment associated with that particular seat.
guides.why: Passenger sensing equipment introduces supplemental restraint work into an otherwise mechanical repair. A driver memory seat also needs its electronic travel limits established after track replacement. Without those soft stops, the seat may stop prematurely even though the new track is mechanically capable of further movement.
searchTerms: memory seat stops before full travel
power seat moves in short bursts

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies the track assembly or an integral height motor as requiring replacement.
notes: Identify driver memory equipment and an original-equipment passenger occupant classification system before dismantling.
A horizontal motor fault may be repairable without replacing the complete track.

prepare.title: Plan the dismantling sequence
prepare.detail: Have the backrest and cushion-cover procedures available. The cushion cover and foam are removed together for this job.

prepare.title: Recognize restraint-system work
prepare.detail: An original-equipment passenger occupant classification system (OCS) requires its dedicated removal and installation procedure and the capability to follow its restraint-system precautions.

prepare.title: Identify electronic work
prepare.detail: The driver seat module (DSM) is mounted on a memory-seat track. Replacing the DSM also requires programmable module installation; that requirement is conditional on installing a new module.

steps.title: Remove the backrest
steps.body: Follow the [front seat backrest procedure](#/document/G1695510). This is the first dismantling phase specified for access to the seat track.

steps.title: Remove the cushion assembly
steps.body: Follow the [front seat cushion cover procedure](#/document/G1695515), removing the cover and foam as an assembly. Keep this phase distinct from the backrest work so the seat can be rebuilt in the required reverse order.

steps.title: Remove passenger sensing equipment when applicable
steps.body: If the passenger seat has an original-equipment OCS, remove it using the [OCS sensor procedure](#/document/G1696305). This step applies specifically to that passenger-seat configuration.

steps.title: Transfer components and rebuild the seat
steps.body: Transfer components to the new track as necessary, then reverse the removal sequence using the [seat track procedure](#/document/G1695503) and its linked component procedures. Retain the distinction between transferring an existing DSM and installing a new one.

steps.title: Establish memory-seat soft stops
steps.body: When installing a new driver memory seat track, operate the seat in every direction through its full travel. The DSM establishes a soft stop when an axis reaches its hard limit and the switch is held for approximately one second. Complete the travel in both directions for the moving axes.

watchFor.title: Jog mode
watchFor.body: Movement in short bursts can indicate lost motor-position feedback. Replacing the track without resolving that fault may leave the complaint unchanged.

watchFor.title: Physical and electronic limits
watchFor.body: The hard stop is fixed by the seat design. The DSM sets the soft stop to prevent unnecessary stress at the end of travel.

notes: The same stop-setting requirement applies when a new DSM or horizontal motor is installed.

diagnostics.finding: A memory-seat motor operates briefly and requires repeated switch presses.
diagnostics.meaning: This is consistent with jog mode, which indicates a motor-position sensor fault and sets a diagnostic trouble code in the DSM.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose the position-feedback fault before deciding which component needs replacement.

diagnostics.finding: A new driver memory track stops prematurely.
diagnostics.meaning: The required soft-stop setup may be incomplete.
diagnostics.next: Complete the specified full-travel operation and reassess.

verification.title: Confirm the applicable reassembly phases
verification.body: Confirm completion of the backrest, cushion and, where fitted, OCS installation procedures.

verification.title: Record travel-limit setup
verification.body: For a new driver memory track, record completion of full travel in all directions and whether premature stopping remains.

procedures.purpose: Replace the front seat track, transfer components and set new driver memory-track soft stops.
Remove and reinstall the front seat backrest.
