Remove and reinstall the cushion cover and foam assembly.
Handle the original-equipment passenger OCS when fitted.
Understand memory-seat position feedback, jog mode and hard-stop/soft-stop operation.

guides.title: Remove and reinstall a front seat
guides.summary: Position the seat for bolt access, depower the restraint system and reinstall the seat using the required bolt sequence.
guides.introduction: The front seat is a structural assembly secured to the vehicle body, with electrical connections that depend on its fitted features. Removing the complete seat provides access for an established repair. The job includes supplemental restraint system (SRS) depowering and repowering, as well as controlled installation of the mounting bolts.
guides.why: The seat mountings must clamp together as designed. Objects introduced between the seat and body, or within a structural joint, can interfere with correct operation and increase injury risk. Electrical disconnection must also follow the restraint-system procedure rather than an improvised isolation method.
searchTerms: power seat will not move forward or backward

when.summary: When a confirmed repair requires the complete front seat to be removed.
notes: If a power seat cannot move horizontally to expose the bolts, diagnose that access problem first.

prepare.title: Provide restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Have the complete SRS depowering and repowering procedures available, and the capability to carry them out before disconnecting seat wiring.

prepare.title: Prepare for controlled installation
prepare.detail: Use suitable bolt tools and a torque wrench. Keep the seat-to-body mounting surfaces and internal structural joints free of introduced objects or packing.

steps.title: Position the seat while adjustment is available
steps.body: Move the seat to obtain access to its mounting bolts before depowering the SRS. If a power seat cannot move horizontally far enough, follow [Front Seats diagnosis and testing](#/document/G1695509) for the inoperative horizontal seat-track motor.

steps.title: Depower the restraint system
steps.body: Carry out the complete [SRS depowering procedure](#/document/G1696297). This is a required stage before the seat connectors are disconnected; simply losing seat power does not establish that the restraint system is depowered.

steps.title: Release the covers and electrical connections
steps.body: Remove the front seat shield bolt caps. Disconnect the seat electrical connector or connectors, then position the wiring harness aside so the seat can be removed without remaining attached to it.

steps.title: Remove the seat assembly
steps.body: Remove the mounting bolts and take out the front seat. Keep the mounting locations clear of loose objects, and preserve the wiring access needed when the seat returns.

steps.title: Install the bolts in the specified order
steps.body: Refit the seat using the [front seat installation procedure](#/document/G1695491). Install and tighten the front inboard bolt, front outboard bolt, rear inboard bolt and rear outboard bolt, in that order. Each is tightened to 35 lb.ft (47 Nm).

steps.title: Restore wiring and repower the SRS
steps.body: Complete the remaining reverse-removal operations, restoring the electrical connections and bolt caps. Then carry out the complete [SRS repowering procedure](#/document/G1696298) to finish the restraint-system portion of the job.

watchFor.title: Unwanted material in a mounting joint
watchFor.body: Do not add packing or place objects between seat components and the body, or inside a joint in the seat structure.

watchFor.title: Additional work on a memory seat
watchFor.body: Replacing a module, track or motor can introduce programming or stop-setting requirements beyond complete-seat removal and refitting.

notes: The illustrated seat is the left-hand-drive driver's seat; other front seats use a similar removal and installation process.

For a memory-equipped driver seat, a new driver seat module (DSM) requires programmable module installation (PMI). A new DSM, driver seat track or horizontal motor also requires the DSM hard and soft stops to be set or reset.

diagnostics.finding: The power seat cannot move horizontally to expose its bolts.
diagnostics.meaning: Normal removal access is blocked; this alone does not establish which electrical or mechanical component has failed.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose the inoperative horizontal seat-track motor through the front-seat diagnostic procedure before continuing removal.

verification.title: Record mounting completion
verification.body: Record that the bolts were installed in the prescribed order and each tightened to 35 lb.ft (47 Nm). Confirm that no unwanted objects remain in the mounting joints.

verification.title: Complete the electrical restoration
verification.body: Confirm that the seat connectors and bolt caps are restored and the SRS repowering procedure has been completed.

procedures.purpose: Front seat removal, ordered bolt installation and refitting.
Diagnose an inoperative horizontal power-seat motor when bolt access is blocked.
Required SRS depowering before seat electrical disconnection.
Required SRS repowering after seat installation.
Identify conditional memory-seat programming and stop-setting requirements after component replacement.

guides.title: Remove and refit a coupe rear seat backrest
guides.summary: Remove the rear cushion, release the backrest mounting and hinge, then refit the backrest with its belt correctly routed.
guides.introduction: The rear backrest supports the occupant through connections to the seat hinge and vehicle floor. Removing it involves more than undoing the visible floor fastener: the hinge must disengage, and the backrest must clear its floor stud. This job explains that removal path and the checks that matter when the backrest goes back into the coupe.
guides.why: The mounting joints must sit directly against their intended surfaces. Objects trapped between the seat and body, or inside a seat joint, can prevent correct installation and compromise seat operation. Belt routing matters too: an otherwise secure backrest is not ready for use if the webbing is twisted or the occupant cannot reach the belt and buckle.

when.summary: When rear backrest replacement or access requires removing the backrest.
notes: The left-hand backrest is illustrated; the right-hand side follows a similar procedure.

prepare.title: Arrange cushion access and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Follow the separate rear seat cushion procedure and have suitable tools for the floor fastener, including a torque wrench for installation.

prepare.title: Keep the mounting joints clear
prepare.detail: Remove loose objects from the working area. Nothing may be placed between seat components and the body or within an internal seat-structure joint.

steps.title: Remove the rear cushion
steps.body: Use the [rear seat cushion procedure](#/document/G1692168) to expose the backrest mounting area. Complete this access step before attempting to move the backrest.

steps.title: Release the floor attachment
steps.body: Release the fastener securing the backrest to the floor. The accompanying illustration identifies this attachment; releasing it does not by itself free the hinge or lift the backrest off its stud.

steps.title: Disengage the hinge and lift out the backrest
steps.body: Following the [backrest removal sequence](#/document/G1692165), release the backrest hinge from the pivot hinge. Move the safety belt aside, rotate the backrest toward the outboard side of the vehicle, then lift it clear of the floor stud and remove it.

steps.title: Refit the backrest and cushion
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, restoring the stud and hinge engagement before securing the floor attachment. Tighten the floor fastener to 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm). Keep the belt webbing untwisted and leave both belts and buckles accessible, then reinstall the cushion using its procedure.

watchFor.title: Belt caught behind the backrest
watchFor.body: Keep the belt aside while rotating the backrest, then check its routing before completing installation.

watchFor.title: Obstructed mounting joint
watchFor.body: A loose object within a joint can interfere with correct seating of the components; remove the obstruction before fastening.

notes: Correct hinge and stud engagement is part of installation, not something the floor fastener should be used to force into place.

verification.title: Confirm the mounting
verification.body: Check that the hinge is engaged, the backrest is seated on its floor stud and the floor fastener has received the specified torque.

verification.title: Confirm occupant access
verification.body: Check that the installed cushion and backrest leave the belts and buckles accessible and that the webbing is not twisted.

procedures.purpose: Coupe rear backrest removal and installation, including hinge release, floor attachment and belt-routing requirements.
Rear cushion removal for access and reinstallation after the backrest work.

guides.title: Replace the coupe rear-seat backrest cover
guides.summary: Remove the backrest, release its upholstery attachments without tearing the foam, and refit the cover with the latch strap correctly routed.
guides.introduction: The rear backrest cover forms the upholstery surface over the foam pad. A lower J-shaped retaining clip and hook-and-loop strips secure it, while the backrest latch strap passes through the cover. This job separates the upholstery from the foam and requires the backrest to be removed from the vehicle first.
guides.why: The hook-and-loop attachment must separate without pulling its strips out of the foam. Reinstallation also involves safety-critical seat attachments: nothing may be trapped between seat components and the vehicle body or placed within a seat-structure joint.
searchTerms: rear seat hook and loop strips

when.summary: When replacing the coupe rear backrest upholstery or removing its cover for access to the foam.
notes: The left-hand backrest is illustrated; the right-hand procedure is similar.

prepare.title: Plan the seat-removal prerequisite
prepare.detail: Follow the linked backrest procedure, including its prerequisite rear-seat cushion removal. Have suitable fastener tools and a torque tool for the backrest floor attachment.

prepare.title: Protect the foam attachments
prepare.detail: Allow access to the lower J-clip, hook-and-loop strips and latch-strap opening. Separate these attachments carefully rather than pulling the whole cover away at once.

steps.title: Remove the backrest
steps.body: After removing the rear cushion, release the backrest floor fastener. Release the backrest hinge from the pivot hinge, move the safety belt aside and rotate the backrest toward the outboard side. Lift it off the floor stud and remove it, following the backrest procedure.

steps.title: Release and remove the cover
steps.body: Release the lower J-clip. Carefully separate the cover's hook-and-loop strips from the foam without tearing the strips out of the pad. Pass the latch strap through the cover opening, then remove the cover.

steps.title: Refit the upholstery
steps.body: Reverse the cover-removal sequence. Restore the latch strap through its opening, reconnect the hook-and-loop attachments and engage the lower J-clip. These attachments locate the cover on the foam.

steps.title: Install the backrest and cushion
steps.body: Reverse the backrest-removal sequence, keeping its mounting joints clear of foreign objects. Tighten the floor attachment to 35 lb.ft (47.5 Nm). Ensure the safety-belt webbing is untwisted and the belts and buckles remain accessible, then complete cushion installation.

watchFor.title: Hook-and-loop strips lifting from the foam
watchFor.body: Stop pulling the cover away and separate the fastening surfaces carefully. Pulling harder can tear the foam-mounted strips free.

watchFor.title: Trapped belts or objects at seat joints
watchFor.body: Seat components must be installed without objects between their joints or between the seat and body. Incorrect installation can compromise seat operation.

verification.title: Check upholstery and occupant access
verification.body: Confirm the J-clip and hook-and-loop strips are connected, the latch strap passes through the cover, and the backrest floor fastener is tightened. Verify untwisted, accessible safety belts and buckles.

procedures.purpose: Coupe rear-backrest cover removal and reverse-order installation.
Prerequisite coupe backrest removal and installation, including mounting precautions, floor-fastener torque and belt routing.

guides.title: Remove the coupe rear-seat backrest latch
guides.summary: Remove the backrest cover, release the latch fasteners and drill out the retaining rivet to detach the coupe rear-seat latch assembly.
guides.introduction: The rear-seat backrest latch secures the backrest, and its release strap passes through the upholstery. Removing the latch therefore begins with taking off the backrest cover to expose its attachments. This job ends with the latch removed and the backrest awaiting confirmed reattachment instructions.
guides.why: The cover attaches to the foam with hook-and-loop strips that can tear away from the foam if pulled roughly. Once access is clear, the latch fasteners and rivet must be released before the assembly can be removed; pulling on the release strap does not free those attachments.

when.summary: When the coupe rear-seat backrest latch requires removal for repair or replacement.
notes: The left-hand seat is the reference arrangement; the right-hand side is similar.

prepare.title: Arrange backrest removal
prepare.detail: The backrest must first be removed using the coupe backrest procedure referenced in the cover instructions. Have those instructions available before starting.

prepare.title: Prepare for rivet removal
prepare.detail: An electric drill is required. Confirm the latch reattachment method separately before treating this removal as part of a complete seat repair.

steps.title: Remove the backrest for cover access
steps.body: Follow the backrest-removal prerequisite in the linked coupe cover procedure. With the backrest removed, locate the lower cover attachment and the latch strap before separating the upholstery.

steps.title: Release and remove the cover
steps.body: Release the lower J-clip. Carefully separate the cover's hook-and-loop strips from the foam, then guide the latch strap through the cover opening and remove the cover. Keeping the separation controlled protects the strips' attachment to the foam.

steps.title: Release the latch fasteners
steps.body: Access the rear of the backrest frame and release the three latch fasteners. These attachments must be released before the latch assembly can come away from the frame.

steps.title: Remove the rivet and latch assembly
steps.body: Use the electric drill to remove the retaining rivet, then remove the latch assembly. Stop with the backrest disassembled until the correct reattachment instructions and hardware have been confirmed.

watchFor.title: Hook-and-loop strips pulling out of the foam
watchFor.body: Separate the mating strips carefully instead of pulling the upholstery away forcefully; the strips can tear from the foam pad.

watchFor.title: Confusing a drill size with replacement hardware
watchFor.body: A drill size does not establish the replacement rivet specification. Latch reattachment needs its own confirmed hardware requirements.

notes: Cover refitting and latch reattachment are separate from this removal task. Keep the seat out of use while its latch is detached.

verification.title: Confirm the removal endpoint
verification.body: Confirm that the three latch fasteners have been released, the retaining rivet removed and the latch assembly detached from the backrest frame.

verification.title: Leave a clear repair handoff
verification.body: Record that the latch is removed and reattachment remains outstanding. The backrest has not yet been verified as securely reassembled.

procedures.purpose: Release the rear latch fasteners, drill out the retaining rivet and remove the latch assembly.
Coupe backrest-cover removal, including backrest access, lower J-clip, hook-and-loop strips and latch strap.

guides.title: Replace the rear seat cushion cover
guides.summary: Remove the rear bench cushion, release its upholstery attachments and refit the cover without damaging the foam or trapping the seatbelts.
guides.introduction: The rear seat cushion wears its upholstery like a fitted shirt—with enough hidden attachments to make undressing it a small negotiation. I’ll walk you through releasing the cushion from the floor, freeing the cover underneath and separating the hook-and-loop strips without dragging chunks of foam along for the ride. The trick is releasing each attachment, not winning a tug-of-war.
guides.why: The cover forms the seating surface over the shaped foam. J-clips and pin-type retainers secure it underneath, while hook-and-loop strips hold it against the foam’s contours. These attachments do different jobs: freeing the underside clips does not release the strips inside the cover. Careful separation preserves the foam attachments, and correct reassembly secures the cushion while keeping the rear belts and buckles usable.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang rear seat cushion cover replacement

when.summary: Use this procedure when removing or replacing the rear seat cushion cover on a 2015 Mustang with a 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
notes: The complete rear cushion comes out before its cover is removed.
This is a cover removal and refitting procedure, not a diagnosis of seat noises or discomfort.

prepare.title: Make room for the cushion
prepare.detail: Provide room to move both front seats fully forward and carry the rear cushion out. Have a clean supporting surface where you can turn the cushion over without scuffing its upholstery.

prepare.title: Have the cover ready
prepare.detail: If replacing the upholstery, have a replacement cover that matches the cushion being worked on. Note the existing cover’s orientation and attachment routing before separating it.

prepare.title: Protect yourself and the attachments
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during service, and protective gloves when handling sharp frame edges. Damaged floor-locking tabs or hook-and-loop strips torn out of the foam need a separate repair plan before the seat can be returned to use; repairing those attachments is outside this cover procedure.

steps.title: Prepare the parked vehicle and move both front seats forward
steps.body:
Work with the vehicle parked and the parking brake applied; this job is performed with the vehicle on the ground.

If remote start is fitted, disable it through the Central Display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before starting service. Move both front seats to their full forward positions to open access to the rear cushion. After positioning the seats, switch the ignition off and remove the key to prevent another person starting the vehicle during the work. See the relevant [service precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Press in both front cushion locking tabs
steps.body:
Locate the locking tabs beneath the front edge of the rear cushion, one toward each seating position. The release is at the cushion-to-floor attachment, not at the seatbelt buckle.

Press each locking tab inward to release its attachment from the floor. Do this on both sides before lifting the cushion. Lifting against an engaged tab can damage it; if one side remains held down, return to that release rather than pulling harder.

steps.title: Lift out the complete rear cushion
steps.body:
With both front locking tabs released, lift and release the cushion, then remove it from the vehicle. The cushion comes out as the complete bench beneath the rear backrests; the illustration shows its front edge raised during removal.

Keep the belt webbing and buckles clear as you withdraw it. Place the cushion on your supporting surface and turn it over to expose the underside. These access actions are covered by the [rear seat cushion procedure](#/document/G1692168).

steps.title: Release the cover’s underside clips and pin retainers
steps.body:
Look around the underside of the cushion frame and identify where the cover wraps around it. The underside illustration shows attachment points around the perimeter and along the inner edges, with round pin-type retainers highlighted near the two outer corners.

Release the cover’s J-clips and pin-type retainers from the bottom of the frame. A J-clip is the hooked fastening at the end of an attaching strap. Note how each strap reaches its frame attachment before freeing it. Work around the cushion so no attached section is left resisting the next operation.

steps.title: Feed the attaching straps through the foam openings
steps.body:
Once the underside fastenings are released, pass the J-clip attaching straps through the openings in the foam toward the cover. Free each strap from its route through the pad so the cover is no longer tethered underneath.

If the cover still pulls against the frame, look for a remaining clip, pin retainer or strap before moving on. An overlooked fastening can make a simple upholstery job a pain in the ass very quickly.

steps.title: Separate the hook-and-loop strips and remove the cover
steps.body:
Turn the cushion as needed to reach the cover-to-foam connections. Carefully separate the mating hook-and-loop strips—the two-part fabric fasteners that grip one another—while watching that the foam-side strips stay attached to the pad.

Work progressively at the separating edge rather than pulling the whole cover away at once. The partly removed-cover illustration shows strips running across the shaped seating areas and along their sides, so continue checking for attachments as more of the foam is exposed.

If a strip begins lifting out of the foam, stop pulling in that direction and work carefully at the hook-and-loop joint itself. Once all strips and attaching straps are free, remove the cover. See the [rear seat cushion cover procedure](#/document/G1692169).

steps.title: Position the cover and reconnect its foam attachments
steps.body:
Install the cover by reversing its removal. Orient it over the shaped pad in the same direction as the original and align its mating hook-and-loop strips with those on the foam.

Engage the strips while settling the cover into the cushion’s contours. Check that each connection joins its matching strip and that the foam-side attachments remain in place. The clips underneath cannot do the job of these internal connections.

steps.title: Route the straps and restore the underside fastenings
steps.body:
Feed the J-clip attaching straps back through their corresponding openings in the foam toward the underside of the cushion. Restore their original routes, then reconnect the J-clips and pin-type retainers to the frame, reversing the release sequence.

Check around the underside and inner attachment areas for any loose strap, unhooked clip or unseated pin retainer. Confirm that the cover edges wrap back into their original positions before taking the cushion to the car.

steps.title: Position the belts and reinstall the cushion
steps.body:
Bring the cushion back into the rear seating area. Before lowering it into place, arrange the seatbelts and buckles so they remain accessible above and alongside the cushion as intended. Make sure the belt webbing is not twisted.

Position the cushion in its original location, align the front locking tabs with their floor attachments and lower it into place, reversing removal. Seat both front attachments fully. Keep watching the belts and buckles as the cushion settles; upholstery should not swallow the restraints.

steps.title: Check the finished installation
steps.body:
Check that both front cushion attachments are engaged and that neither side lifts free at its attachment. Confirm the cover sits in the foam’s contours and its edges remain secured.

Check every rear belt and buckle for occupant access and untwisted webbing. If a buckle has disappeared underneath or a belt is trapped, release the cushion again and correct its routing before finishing. Return the front seats to their desired positions after the rear installation is secure.

watchFor.title: Cushion tabs still engaged
watchFor.body: Press the front locking tabs inward before lifting. Resistance at one front attachment means you should revisit that release, not force the cushion upward.

watchFor.title: Foam-side strips pulling loose
watchFor.body: Watch the strip-to-foam connection while separating the cover. The hook-and-loop joint must separate without tearing its anchoring strip from the pad.

watchFor.title: Attaching straps left behind
watchFor.body: A released J-clip does not automatically free its strap from the foam. Pass the straps through their openings before lifting the cover away.

watchFor.title: Hidden buckles or twisted webbing
watchFor.body: Arrange the restraints before seating the cushion, then check them again afterward. Every rear belt and buckle must remain accessible to its occupant.

notes: The cushion-to-floor locking tabs and the cover-to-frame fastenings are separate systems. Release the floor tabs to remove the cushion, then work on the cover attachments on the supporting surface.
Installation reverses removal for both the cover and the complete cushion. Preserve the original attachment locations and strap routes.

diagnostics.finding: One front corner remains attached when the cushion is lifted.
diagnostics.meaning: The locking tab at that floor attachment may still be engaged.
diagnostics.next: Stop lifting and press that tab inward to release it before trying to remove the cushion again.

diagnostics.finding: The cover remains tethered underneath after the visible clips are released.
diagnostics.meaning: A fastening may remain engaged, or an attaching strap may still pass through the foam.
diagnostics.next: Check the underside perimeter and inner attachment areas, release the remaining fastening and feed the strap through its foam opening.

diagnostics.finding: A hook-and-loop strip starts lifting away with the cover instead of staying on the foam.
diagnostics.meaning: The pull is loading the strip’s foam attachment rather than separating the mating fastener surfaces.
diagnostics.next: Stop pulling the cover away and separate the hook-and-loop joint carefully at its edge. If the strip has already torn free, resolve the damaged attachment before refitting.

diagnostics.finding: A belt is twisted or a buckle is inaccessible after refitting.
diagnostics.meaning: The restraint routing was disturbed as the cushion was lowered.
diagnostics.next: Release and lift the cushion again, correct the webbing and buckle positions, then reinstall and repeat the accessibility check.

verification.title: Cover attachments restored
verification.body: Before reinstalling the bench, visually confirm that the hook-and-loop connections are engaged, their foam-side strips remain attached, the straps pass through their original foam openings and all released J-clips and pin retainers are secured.

verification.title: Cushion secured to the floor
verification.body: After installation, confirm both front locking attachments are engaged and neither attachment lifts free during a gentle hand check. This is a reassembly check, not a separate seat-load test.

verification.title: Restraints ready for occupants
verification.body: Confirm every rear seatbelt and buckle is accessible and the webbing is untwisted and clear of the cushion.

procedures.purpose: Cover removal and reverse-order installation, including J-clips, pin retainers, strap routing and protection of foam-mounted hook-and-loop strips.
Complete cushion access, front floor-tab release, cushion removal and installation with correct seatbelt and buckle positioning.
Relevant service precautions for remote-start prevention, key removal and personal protection.

guides.title: Remove and refit the rear seat cushion
guides.summary: Move both front seats fully forward, release the rear cushion’s front locking tabs, lift out the cushion, and refit it with the seatbelts and buckles correctly positioned.
guides.introduction: The rear seat cushion looks like it should simply lift out. Its locking tabs have other opinions. I’ll walk you through releasing those tabs before lifting, then getting the cushion back in without making the seatbelt buckles disappear into upholstery purgatory.
guides.why: The cushion supports the rear occupants and locks to the floor at its front edge. Removing it allows cushion replacement or access beneath the seating area. Pressing the locking tabs inward before lifting protects them from damage; arranging the belts during refitting keeps the rear seating positions ready to use.
searchTerms: rear seat cushion will not release
rear seat buckle trapped under cushion

when.summary: For rear seat cushion removal, replacement or refitting on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
notes: Use this procedure when the cushion itself needs to come out or work beneath it requires access.
This is a removal and installation procedure, not a diagnosis of cushion damage or seating complaints.

prepare.title: Make room on both sides
prepare.detail: Arrange access to both sides of the rear seating area so you can reach both front locking points and carry the released cushion out.

prepare.title: Note the belt and buckle positions
prepare.detail: Before moving the cushion, look at where the seatbelt webbing and buckles emerge. You will need to keep them accessible as the cushion goes back in.

prepare.title: Keep damaged-retainer work separate
prepare.detail: This procedure covers releasing and engaging the cushion’s existing locking tabs. If a tab is damaged or will not retain the cushion, obtain the appropriate repair instructions before returning that seating position to use.

steps.title: Move both front seats fully forward
steps.body: Move the driver’s front seat to its full forward position, then do the same on the passenger side. Both seats need to move to provide working room along the rear cushion’s front edge.

steps.title: Locate the two front locking points
steps.body: Find the locking-tab release locations along the front edge of the rear cushion, one on each side. These tabs secure the cushion to the floor. The inset in the [rear seat cushion procedure](#/document/G1692168) shows the tab and its inward release action; identify that action before pulling on the cushion.

steps.title: Press the locking tabs inward
steps.body:
Press inward on the locking tab at each front locking point to release the cushion from the floor.

The tabs must be pressed in before the cushion is lifted. Pulling upward against engaged tabs can damage them. If the front edge remains held, stop lifting and return to the release tab at the retained location. More muscle is not the missing tool here.

steps.title: Lift and remove the released cushion
steps.body:
After both front locking points have released, lift the cushion away from its installed position and remove it from the vehicle. The removal illustration shows the cushion lifted across its width, with the rear backrests remaining in place.

Watch the belt webbing and buckles as the cushion comes away so they do not get carried along with it.

steps.title: Position the cushion and arrange the belts
steps.body:
Bring the cushion back into the rear seating area and lower it toward its installed position, reversing the removal movement. As you position it, bring the seatbelts and buckles through to their occupant-accessible positions.

Check that the belt webbing—the flat woven strap—is not twisted and that no buckle is disappearing beneath the cushion. I’d sort that now, while the cushion is still easy to move.

steps.title: Engage the cushion and finish refitting
steps.body:
Align the cushion with its floor locking points and lower it fully into position so the front tabs engage, reversing their release during removal. Confirm that both front locking points retain the cushion; do not treat a cushion resting in place as secured.

Check the belt webbing and buckle positions again after seating the cushion. Once the cushion is secured and the belts are accessible, return the front seats to their required positions.

watchFor.title: A front corner that remains held
watchFor.body: Stop lifting and press the locking tab inward at that location. Continuing to pull against an engaged tab risks damaging it.

watchFor.title: Belts disappearing during installation
watchFor.body: Keep the webbing untwisted and the belts and buckles accessible while lowering the cushion. Reposition the cushion if necessary to recover a trapped buckle before finishing.

notes: The illustrated release points are at the cushion’s front edge. The rear backrests remain in place during the illustrated removal.

diagnostics.finding: The cushion remains attached at a front locking point when lifting begins.
diagnostics.meaning: Release at that locking point has not been established.
diagnostics.next: Stop lifting, locate that tab and press it inward before trying to lift the cushion again. Do not force the cushion past the retained point.

diagnostics.finding: A belt is twisted or a buckle is trapped beneath the refitted cushion.
diagnostics.meaning: The belt arrangement does not meet the installation requirement.
diagnostics.next: Release and reposition the cushion as needed, straighten the webbing and bring the belt and buckle into an accessible position, then secure the cushion again.

diagnostics.finding: A front locking point does not retain the installed cushion.
diagnostics.meaning: Installation is incomplete; this observation alone does not establish which part is faulty.
diagnostics.next: Recheck cushion alignment and engagement. If it still will not secure, stop and obtain locking-point repair guidance.

verification.title: Confirm cushion retention
verification.body: Confirm that the cushion is fully positioned and retained at both front floor-locking points. This is an installation completion check, not a separate load test.

verification.title: Check every rear belt and buckle
verification.body: Check that the seatbelt webbing is untwisted and that the belts and buckles remain accessible to their occupants above the installed cushion.

guides.title: Diagnose front power windows with or without a memory driver seat
guides.summary: Separate switch, wiring, motor and door-module faults by following the diagnostic branch for the affected window and fitted seating equipment.
guides.introduction: The regulator motor moves the door glass and controls features such as the short drop that clears the door seal. With a memory driver seat, the driver door module (DDM) receives master-switch commands over the local interconnect network (LIN). Without memory seating, switches send direction signals directly to the motors.
guides.why: A stationary window can result from missing power, a lost command or faulty connections. Testing these paths in order prevents unnecessary component replacement.
searchTerms: passenger window works from one switch

when.summary: When a front window fails to move correctly, or a glass-system complaint needs routing to its appropriate test.

prepare.title: Electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable scan tool, digital multimeter, terminal-safe flex probes, fused jumper and Wiring Diagrams Cell 100. Follow the prescribed ignition and connector states; isolate power for resistance testing.

prepare.title: Establish reliable starting conditions
prepare.detail: Confirm the complaint is present, battery charge exceeds 70%, and inspect wiring, connectors and previous repairs. Diagnose related circuit trouble codes first.

steps.title: Identify shared failures first
steps.body: If both front windows fail without memory seating, check body control module (BCM) fuse 23 (10A); a good fuse directs repair of an open CBP23 circuit. With memory seating, failure from the master switch only requires related DDM codes to be diagnosed first; without related codes, the chart directs master-switch replacement.

steps.title: Test A: driver window without memory seating
steps.body: Check battery junction box fuse 11 (30A), then motor battery feed, delayed-accessory feed and ground. Continue through direction-circuit voltage-short and continuity checks. Only after these pass, perform A6’s specified momentary fused-jumper commands: movement directs master-switch replacement; no movement directs motor replacement.

steps.title: Test B: driver window with memory seating—command path
steps.body: Run the DDM self-test. Communication codes lead through master-switch power, ground and LIN short/open checks, using the coupe or convertible connector branch. Intact ground wiring with a failed ground leads to B16. Passing LIN checks directs switch replacement and retesting. Without codes, compare the DF_WINDSW_DD parameter identification (PID) with switch operation; disagreement directs switch replacement.

steps.title: Test B: motor and module decisions
steps.body: If switch data agrees, test motor feeds, ground and direction circuits for shorts and opens. Correct commanded DDM outputs direct motor replacement. Otherwise, follow B16: inspect and repair module terminals, reconnect securely and retest. A persistent fault requires an applicable service-bulletin check in OASIS before DDM replacement; a cleared fault still requires correcting its connector cause.

steps.title: Test C: passenger window without memory seating
steps.body: Check BCM fuse 26 (30A), then try both switches. Passenger-switch-only operation leads to inter-switch continuity testing; master-switch-only operation adds a passenger-switch supply check. Passing checks identify the respective faulty switch. If neither works, check motor feeds, ground, direction-circuit voltage shorts and continuity before the motor replacement decision.

steps.title: Route other complaints correctly
steps.body: Test D covers the passenger window with memory seating; E–G cover rear quarter windows; H covers one-touch operation; I covers global opening; J covers short drop; K/L cover defrost failure/staying on. For voice- or touchscreen-only defrost complaints, try the instrument-panel switch first: failure leads to K, successful operation to the information-and-entertainment diagnostic path.

watchFor.title: A failed fuse needs investigation
watchFor.body: Use the wiring diagrams to identify the short; fuse replacement alone does not establish the cause.

watchFor.title: Convertible feature differences
watchFor.body: Convertibles lack one-touch up and bounce back. Their rear quarter motors do not require initialization.

notes: Other BCM-B codes route to BCM diagnostics; other door-module codes to locks and entry diagnostics; other front-controls codes to the fitted climate-control diagnostic branch.

diagnostics.finding: DDM code B1088:83 or B1088:87 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The master switch supplied invalid data or its messages are missing, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test B’s power, ground and LIN checks.

diagnostics.finding: DDM code U2013:24 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The switch-pack signal is stuck high.
diagnostics.next: Clear and retest; replace the master switch if a switch remains inoperative or the code returns.

diagnostics.finding: Passenger door module code U2002:24 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: A switch input remains up/down or shorted to ground for greater than 10 seconds.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test D; the code alone does not identify the failed part.

diagnostics.finding: Body Control Module B records B127A:12 or B127A:14.
diagnostics.meaning: The global-window circuit is shorted to battery, or shorted to ground/open, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test I.

diagnostics.finding: The front controls interface module records B1C83:12 or B1C83:14.
diagnostics.meaning: The defrost-relay circuit is shorted to battery, or shorted to ground/open, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Use K for B1C83:12; for B1C83:14 use K if inoperative or L if it will not shut off.

verification.title: Complete the directed repair
verification.body: De-initialize then initialize the door motor wherever directed. Follow the linked replacement procedure for a new motor; DDM replacement requires programmable module installation.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Retest the original complaint from the relevant switches. Record circuit results, switch-data agreement, returning codes and whether connector repair restored operation.

guides.title: Diagnose memory-seat passenger-window and convertible rear quarter-window faults
guides.summary: Separate switch, wiring, motor and module faults while accounting for the convertible roof’s normal window interlock.
guides.introduction: Window switches request movement from electronics inside the regulator motors. With a memory driver seat, the passenger door module (PDM) handles passenger-window commands from either front switch. Convertible rear quarter windows share a switch command, but roof position can deliberately prevent operation. These tests distinguish those control conditions from electrical failures.
guides.why: A stationary window does not establish that its motor has failed. Testing commands, supplies and connections in order prevents replacing a working motor or module.
searchTerms: passenger window works from only one switch
both convertible rear windows not working

when.summary: When the passenger front window or convertible rear quarter windows fail to respond correctly.
notes: The complaint must be present before a pinpoint-test result is used to justify replacement.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, battery state of charge above 70%, previous repairs, wiring and related diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs).

prepare.title: Prepare for electrical diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, Rotunda Flex Probes and the specified wiring diagrams. Follow each test’s ignition and connector states; isolate circuits for resistance measurements.

steps.title: Start Test D with the passenger module
steps.body: For the right-hand front window with memory driver seat, run the PDM self-test with ignition on. Follow the code decisions below. With no codes, compare operation from both front switches.

steps.title: Separate the two switch paths
steps.body: If only the passenger switch works, Test D directs master-switch replacement. If only the master works, follow D5–D8 through return-circuit, command-circuit and switch-component checks. Repair failed wiring or replace a failed switch; follow the specified module branch when directed.

steps.title: Check a window that responds to neither switch
steps.body: Follow D9–D14 through motor battery supply, delayed-accessory supply, ground, then command-wire shorts to voltage, shorts to ground and continuity. Repair failed circuits and de-initialize, then initialize the door motor as directed.

steps.title: Distinguish motor failure from module connections
steps.body: At D15, correct outputs in both commanded directions direct motor replacement. Otherwise follow D16: repair corrosion, damaged or pushed-out terminals, reconnect securely and retest. If the fault remains, check applicable Technical Service Bulletins (TSBs) before PDM replacement. A new PDM requires programmable module installation (PMI).

steps.title: Use Test E when both rear quarter windows fail
steps.body: First place the roof fully open or fully closed and latched. Run the movable roof control module A (MRCMA) self-test and diagnose roof-related codes first. With no codes, check the shared command circuits using the memory-seat or non-memory connections specified in E2. Passing continuity directs master-switch replacement; failed continuity requires circuit repair.

steps.title: Use Test F for the left rear quarter window
steps.body: Check body control module (BCM) fuse 29 (30A), then command-circuit continuity, motor power, delayed-accessory feed and ground in sequence. Investigate a failed fuse for a circuit short. Repair failed circuits; passing all checks directs rear regulator-motor replacement.

steps.title: Use Test G for the right rear quarter window
steps.body: Follow the right-side connector chart and the same ordered checks, using BCM fuse 30 (30A). Replace the motor only at the passing endpoint of G4; otherwise repair the identified circuit.

watchFor.title: Equipment changes connections
watchFor.body: Test E uses different master-switch pins with memory-seat equipment. Use each test’s own connector chart.

watchFor.title: Avoid substitute power feeds
watchFor.body: Do not apply power or ground directly to module-controlled circuits unless the procedure directs it.

notes: Convertible models lack one-touch up and bounce-back. Their rear quarter-window motors require no initialization.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U2002:24 is recorded in the PDM.
diagnostics.meaning: Test D routes this result to switch-circuit checks for a short to ground.
diagnostics.next: If D2 passes, follow D16. Otherwise disconnect the passenger switch and repeat: a cleared short directs switch replacement; a remaining short requires wiring repair.

diagnostics.finding: Other PDM diagnostic trouble codes are recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These require a different diagnostic route before continuing window isolation.
diagnostics.next: Follow Locks, Latches and Entry Systems diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Only the door-window one-touch feature is inoperative.
diagnostics.meaning: Motor initialization or the switch may be involved.
diagnostics.next: Check feature applicability and use the initialization procedure where required.

verification.title: Repeat the complaint
verification.body: Reconnect all connectors, complete required door-motor initialization and operate the affected controls. Correct the root cause of any connector fault even if reseating restores operation.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the test branch, codes, failed measurements, repair and successful operating check.

guides.title: Diagnose one-touch windows, remote opening, short drop and rear defrost
guides.summary: Separate lost window initialization, switch and circuit faults, remote-opening problems and rear-window heating faults before choosing a repair.
guides.introduction: The door-window motors contain electronics that manage automatic movement and the small glass movement needed to clear the door seals. Remote opening adds a shared command from Body Control Module B (BCM-B). Rear defrost uses a separate relay-powered heating grid. These complaints therefore need different tests, even though they concern the same glass.
guides.why: A window can lose its learned operation without having a failed motor. Remote-opening settings and connector faults can also resemble component failures. Following the complaint-specific branch establishes whether the fault lies in a command, wiring, motor or heating circuit.
searchTerms: windows will not open with remote
window does not drop when door opens

when.summary: When an equipped automatic window feature or rear-window defrost repeatedly fails to operate correctly.
notes: Convertibles have no one-touch up or bounce-back feature. Their rear quarter-window motors require no initialization.
Reproduce the complaint before following a test to a component-replacement decision.

prepare.title: Establish reliable electrical conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge greater than 70%. Review related diagnostic trouble codes, previous repairs, wiring damage and applicable service bulletins.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical testing capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, wiring diagrams and Rotunda Flex Probes. Test K requires a Rotunda SGT27000 test lamp or a 250–300 mA incandescent test lamp; connect it through flex probes, never directly into terminals.

steps.title: H: Test the affected one-touch window
steps.body: Perform Power Door Window Initialization. Restored operation identifies lost initialization. If the fault remains, Test H specifies replacing the switch responsible for that request: the master switch for the driver window or a passenger-window request made there, and the passenger switch for a request made locally. Replace the affected motor only if the concern persists after that switch repair.

steps.title: I: Choose the global-open branch
steps.body: With ignition on, run the BCM-B self-test. B127A:12 starts the short-to-voltage branch; B127A:14 starts the short-to-ground/open branch. Test the left and right outputs separately: they serve different sides but join inside BCM-B. Follow Test I's exact connector and ignition-state instructions.

steps.title: I: Isolate the electrical fault
steps.body: Disconnect BCM-B and test the affected output. Isolate its front motor first, then its rear quarter motor on a convertible if needed. A fault that disappears after motor disconnection directs replacement of that motor; a fault remaining after the applicable motors are isolated directs wiring repair. Ground isolation uses greater than 10,000 ohms; continuity checks require less than 3 ohms. If the initial voltage check or subsequent ground/open checks pass, continue to I17.

steps.title: I: Follow the branch without global-open codes
steps.body: Switch ignition off, open and close the driver door, then request remote opening. If any window responds, check continuity to the nonresponding motor: a passing circuit directs motor replacement; a failed circuit needs repair. If none responds, verify Remote Open is enabled, then test lock/unlock with every remote keyless entry transmitter. No working transmitter directs entry-system diagnosis; a working transmitter leads to I17.

steps.title: J: Check short-drop operation
steps.body: Open and close each door while watching the interior lamps. Incorrect lamp response directs interior-lighting diagnosis. Otherwise initialize the affected door window and retry its short drop. If still faulty, switch ignition off and disconnect the affected motor and latch. Test the specified door-ajar input wire: less than 3 ohms directs motor replacement; a failed continuity test directs circuit repair.

steps.title: K: Check heating-grid power and ground
steps.body: Inspect the grid and connectors and check battery junction box fuses 9 (40A) and 66 (5A). Use the coupe or convertible connector branch. With defrost commanded on, grid supply must exceed 11 volts. With ignition off, test its ground. A ground resistance below 3 ohms directs the Grid Wire Test, followed by grid repair or glass replacement. Poor supply directs relay-feed checks; poor ground directs wiring repair.

steps.title: K: Separate relay, output-wire and control faults
steps.body: Check both specified relay feeds. If inadequate, investigate the fuses and circuit, including the cause of any short. With correct feeds, use the prescribed test lamp to assess the Front Controls Interface Module (FCIM) command. A lit lamp leads to relay component testing: a failed relay needs replacement; a passing relay directs output-wire repair. An unlit lamp leads to FCIM disconnection and control-wire short-to-voltage and continuity checks.

steps.title: Finish the appropriate module branch
steps.body: At I17 or K8, inspect module connectors for corrosion, damaged or pushed-out terminals. Repair defects, reconnect every disturbed connector securely and retest. If the fault remains, check applicable service bulletins through OASIS. Without an applicable bulletin, I17 directs BCM-B replacement; K8 requires the VIN-specific FCIM Guided Routine. Replacement of either module requires programmable module installation.

watchFor.title: Incorrect test conditions
watchFor.body: Follow each ignition and disconnection instruction. Voltage corrupts resistance readings, and an unloaded voltage reading alone cannot establish that a circuit carries its normal load.

watchFor.title: Different switch architectures
watchFor.body: Memory-seat vehicles route window commands through door modules. Use the correct wiring diagram and do not apply power or ground directly to module outputs.

notes: Short drop operates on both body styles: the glass lowers to clear the weatherstrip and rises again after door closure.
Global opening requires ignition off and the delayed accessory relay inactive.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B127A:12 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: BCM-B detected voltage on the global-open circuit where it should not be present.
diagnostics.next: Follow I2 through the applicable motor-isolation branch before selecting a repair.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B127A:14 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: BCM-B detected an open or short to ground in the global-open circuit.
diagnostics.next: Start at I7; distinguish ground leakage from an open wire.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1C83:12 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: FCIM detected a short to voltage on the rear-defrost relay control circuit.
diagnostics.next: For an inoperative defrost system, follow Test K and isolate the control circuit before condemning FCIM.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1C83:14 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: FCIM detected an open or short to ground on the rear-defrost relay control circuit.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the circuit in relation to the actual complaint; the code does not prove a failed relay or module.

diagnostics.finding: Rear defrost does not shut off automatically
diagnostics.meaning: Possible causes include the relay, wiring or FCIM. Normal shutdown can follow a timer, an off request, ignition-off or low battery voltage.
diagnostics.next: Pursue the separate automatic-shutoff complaint; Test K's no-heat checks do not establish its repair.

verification.title: Repeat the affected function
verification.body: Recheck one-touch operation, remote opening, door-triggered short drop or rear defrost as appropriate. After connector repairs, confirm the original concern is absent.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record the affected window and switch, codes, measured circuit results, initialization outcome and final functional result.

guides.title: Diagnose rear-window defrost that stays on and locate broken grid lines
guides.summary: Trace unwanted rear-defrost operation through its power feed, relay and control circuit, then test individual heater-grid lines.
guides.introduction: The rear-window grid turns electrical energy into heat to clear the glass. The front controls interface module (FCIM) switches its relay and should release it when the operating timer finishes. Persistent heating requires circuit diagnosis; uneven clearing calls for the separate grid-wire test included here.
guides.why: Removing the relay separates unwanted power at the glass from a relay-control problem. Testing the grid separately prevents a broken heating line from being mistaken for a control-module fault.
searchTerms: rear defroster does not shut off automatically

when.summary: When rear defrost does not shut off automatically, or individual grid lines fail to heat.
notes: Normal cancellation also occurs through the switch, ignition off or battery load management; equipped vehicles also support touchscreen or voice cancellation.

prepare.title: Gather the specified test equipment
prepare.detail: Use a voltmeter, bright inspection lamp and Rotunda Flex Probes. L2 requires a Rotunda Test Lamp SGT27000 or a 250–300mA incandescent test lamp.

prepare.title: Confirm electrical readiness
prepare.detail: Verify the complaint, battery and charging operation, and battery state of charge above 70%. Check related diagnostic trouble codes and previous repairs. Have the vehicle identification number (VIN) available for the FCIM guided routine.

steps.title: L1: Check for power bypassing the relay
steps.body: With ignition off, disconnect the defrost relay and heated-window connector: C402A on a coupe or C402 on a convertible. Turn ignition on and measure pin 1 to ground. Any voltage requires circuit repair; no voltage leads to L2.

steps.title: L2: Test the relay-control output under load
steps.body: Connect the specified lamp between relay socket pin 1, positive, and pin 2, negative, using flex probes. An illuminated lamp leads to L3. If it remains off, Test L directs installation of a new rear-window defrost relay.

steps.title: L3: Isolate an unwanted control-circuit ground
steps.body: Turn ignition off and disconnect FCIM C2402A. Measure relay socket pin 2 to ground under the specified resistance-test conditions. Resistance greater than 10,000 ohms leads to L4; a result that fails this threshold requires circuit repair.

steps.title: L4: Inspect connections before escalating
steps.body: Inspect all FCIM connectors. Replace corroded connectors or terminals, clean module pins and renew damaged or pushed-out terminals as needed. Reconnect every disconnected defrost connection securely and retest. A continuing fault requires an applicable Technical Service Bulletin check, then the VIN-specific FCIM guided routine if no bulletin applies.

steps.title: Inspect and energize the heating grid
steps.body: For the grid-wire test, shine a bright lamp from inside and inspect outside; a brown spot can identify a break. Run the engine at idle and activate defrost; its indicator should illuminate. Measure across the broad red-brown stripes, positive to the battery-positive side and negative to the ground side.

steps.title: Establish supply voltage, then trace each line
steps.body: The stripe-to-stripe reading should be 10–13 volts; a lower reading indicates a loose ground connection. Moving the negative lead to a good ground should not change the reading. Keep that lead grounded and test each grid midpoint, using the findings below to locate interruptions.

watchFor.title: Protect relay-socket terminals
watchFor.body: Never insert the test-lamp probe directly into a connector; use the specified flex-probe connection.

watchFor.title: A fault disappears after reconnection
watchFor.body: Address the connector or terminal defect that caused it, even when operation returns.

notes: If the guided repair requires a new FCIM, programmable module installation (PMI) is required.

diagnostics.finding: A grid midpoint reads approximately 6 volts.
diagnostics.meaning: That line is operating normally.
diagnostics.next: Continue checking the remaining lines.

diagnostics.finding: A grid midpoint reads 0 volt.
diagnostics.meaning: The break lies between the midpoint and the battery-positive side.
diagnostics.next: Move toward that side until the reading changes to 12 volts to locate the interruption.

diagnostics.finding: A grid midpoint reads 12 volts.
diagnostics.meaning: The break lies between the midpoint and ground.
diagnostics.next: Move toward the ground connection until the reading changes to 0 volt, then follow grid-wire repair.

verification.title: Confirm restored control
verification.body: Operate the reconnected system and verify timer-controlled shutoff, switch cancellation and ignition-off cancellation.

verification.title: Record electrical results
verification.body: Record the Test L endpoint, repair and repeat-operation result. For grid work, record supply and affected-line readings before and after repair.

procedures.purpose: Pinpoint Test L for persistent defrost operation and the complete grid-wire component test.
Rear-defrost relay control, normal cancellation conditions and FCIM programming requirement.
Electrical diagnostic prerequisites, circuit isolation and terminal protection.
Heated-window grid-wire repair after locating a break.
