guides.title: Remove and rebond fixed glass
guides.summary: Remove bonded glass, prepare the structural flange and glass correctly, then install a continuous urethane bond and allow it to cure before driving.
guides.introduction: Fixed glass is bonded to the body with urethane adhesive. That bond seals the opening and retains the glass, which matters to restraint-system performance during a crash. This job covers cutting out the glass, deciding whether it can be reused, preparing the body flange and glass, and bonding it back into position. Windshields with a camera bracket or adhesive mouldings must be replaced after removal.
guides.why: The pinch weld—the body flange around the opening—is structural, so corrosion must be repaired. Paint damage can promote rust, contamination can impair adhesion, and gaps in the bead can admit air or water. Successful installation also depends on several separate timing limits: exposed cut urethane, primer drying, installation after bead application and final adhesive curing.

when.summary: When fixed glass requires removal, replacement or rebonding after the repair need has been established.
notes: Camera-related glass selection and alignment requirements apply only when equipped.

prepare.title: Choose a removal method
prepare.detail: A cold knife cuts from outside if its blade reaches the bead; a power glass-removal tool cuts from inside. Glass cut-out wire works from inside and outside with an assistant. Methods may be combined.

prepare.title: Prepare tools and materials
prepare.detail: Have a utility knife, vacuum or soft brush, protective tape and power caulk gun. Select the listed urethane, glass cleaner and a same-brand primer system from the complete procedure, following product instructions.

prepare.title: Plan the entire bonding window
prepare.detail: Arrange any required trim removal, glass handling, corrosion repair capability and curing space. If a windshield has a camera bracket, its replacement must have locating pins and spacers.

steps.title: Decide whether the glass can be reused
steps.body: Discard a removed windshield equipped with a camera bracket or adhesive mouldings. For other fixed glass, choose the appropriate removal method and prepare the new-glass or reusable-glass branch before cutting.

steps.title: Protect the opening and cut out the glass
steps.body: For cold-knife removal, tape the opening perimeter, using multiple layers if needed. Protect adjacent components and avoid scratching paint, primer or the pinch weld. Locating pins may require cutting with a utility knife. Remove the glass; installation must occur within 2 hours of cutting the urethane.

steps.title: Repair and prepare the pinch weld
steps.body: Repair any corrosion and address scratches or exposed metal using the product manufacturer's instructions. When final installation will occur within 2 hours, trim the original urethane to a 1 mm to 2 mm base. Remove dirt with a soft brush or vacuum. Keep mating surfaces clean and avoid touching adhesive surfaces.

steps.title: Prime the flange selectively
steps.body: Apply primer where required: damaged paint exposing bare metal, previously primed areas requiring primer, and damaged clearcoat that has not exposed metal. Minimize primer over remaining urethane. Use the same brand of primer and urethane and allow at least 10 minutes of primer flash time.

steps.title: Prepare new or reusable glass
steps.body: For new glass, clean the inside with the specified Motorcraft Ultra-Clear Spray Glass Cleaner, then apply primer according to its manufacturer's instructions. For reusable glass, inspect and trim the old urethane to a thin bonding layer; prime any areas where it was completely removed. Allow the glass primer at least 10 minutes to dry.

steps.title: Form the continuous adhesive bead
steps.body: Cut the applicator tip to the illustrated specification. Use a power caulk gun to apply a bead 14 mm high and 8 mm wide over the trimmed urethane on the pinch weld. Start and finish at the original overlap points and leave no gaps. Control excess carefully where peripheral mouldings are absent.

steps.title: Set and secure the glass
steps.body: Open the door windows and leave them open during curing to prevent door-closing pressure from disturbing the bond. Remove A-pillar moulding adhesive-strip backings if equipped. Install the glass within 10 minutes of applying urethane, using required locating pins and spacers for a camera-bracket windshield. Press firmly by hand and tape it in the correct position.

steps.title: Finish and allow full curing
steps.body: If necessary, remove excess uncured urethane from the glass with the specified glass cleaner. Reinstall removed components. Keep the glass secured until cured and follow the adhesive manufacturer's curing instructions. Do not drive before the urethane seal has cured.

steps.title: Complete the camera requirement
steps.body: If equipped, carry out the specified camera alignment. Correct physical glass location and completion of camera alignment are both parts of finishing that equipment branch.

watchFor.title: Expired bonding windows
watchFor.body: Cut urethane becomes oxidized and inactive beyond 2 hours. Glass must also be installed within 10 minutes of applying the new bead; primer drying time and final curing are separate requirements.

watchFor.title: Corrosion or bead gaps
watchFor.body: Corrosion compromises the structural flange and must be repaired. Gaps or an uneven bead can produce air and water leaks.

notes: Use the material list in the linked procedure for the approved products. Adhesive product names do not establish the required curing time; follow the manufacturer's instructions.

diagnostics.finding: The removed windshield has a camera bracket or adhesive mouldings.
diagnostics.meaning: Reuse is prohibited for either condition.
diagnostics.next: Install new glass; a camera-bracket replacement must include locating pins and spacers.

verification.title: Check the bond before and during installation
verification.body: Confirm clean prepared surfaces, a uniform gap-free bead, correct glass position and secure tape support.

verification.title: Record timing and completion
verification.body: Record primer drying, installation within both specified windows, completion of the manufacturer's cure requirement and camera alignment where equipped. Confirm removed components are restored before release.

procedures.purpose: Fixed-glass removal methods, mandatory replacement branches, flange and glass preparation, approved materials, urethane application, curing and conditional camera alignment.

guides.title: Repair a broken rear-window defroster grid line
guides.summary: Restore a confirmed break in a rear-window heater or antenna grid line with a carefully prepared conductive repair.
guides.introduction: The rear-window defroster passes electricity through narrow conductive lines to warm the glass and improve rearward visibility. These lines are baked onto the glass surface, so scraping can remove them. Repair builds a conductive bridge across a localized break; the same method also applies to the antenna grid lines.
guides.why: A repair must have enough conductive material to carry current properly. Too few coats or insufficient drying between applications can leave excessive resistance, causing weak defrosting and concentrated heating at the repair. Surface preparation and careful masking also protect the surrounding grid.
searchTerms: rear window defroster line not heating

when.summary: When electrical testing confirms a break in a rear-window heater or antenna grid line.
notes: Appearance alone cannot establish whether a line still conducts electricity.

prepare.title: Confirm the break
prepare.detail: Have a voltmeter or 12V test lamp and the capability to diagnose the affected line. Residue can make a scraped-off conductor look intact.

prepare.title: Gather the repair materials
prepare.detail: Use Motorcraft Ultra-Clear Spray Glass Cleaner, 0000 steel wool, polypropylene film fine line tape and the Mopar Rear Window Defogger Repair Kit. Have the specified Motorcraft lacquer touch-up paint available if the brown layer is missing.

prepare.title: Prepare a safe working area
prepare.detail: Follow the linked health precautions, including disabling remote start, wearing eye and ear protection, and using gloves for sharp-edge handling. Consult the materials' safety information and keep solvents away from ignition sources.

steps.title: Warm and clean the repair area
steps.body: Bring the vehicle to at least 16°C (60.8°F). Clean the entire repair area with the specified glass cleaner and 0000 steel wool to remove dirt, wax, grease, oil and other contamination.

steps.title: Mark and mask the break
steps.body: Mark the break on the outside of the glass. On the repair side, place fine line tape immediately above and below the conductor, with the break centered. Extend the masking 26 mm beyond the affected area in both directions.

steps.title: Restore the brown layer only where needed
steps.body: If the brown layer remains intact, use only silver repair compound. If both layers are missing, apply lacquer touch-up paint across the break first, without overlapping the surviving silver conductor. Additional paint applications may be needed for a color match.

steps.title: Build the conductive bridge
steps.body: Apply silver repair compound in smooth, continuous strokes, overlapping sound conductor by at least 6.35 mm on each side. Apply a minimum of 6 applications. Allow at least 5 minutes between applications of either paint or silver coating.

steps.title: Remove the masking and excess coating
steps.body: Although the coating air-dries in approximately one minute, allow the repair to dry completely before removing the mask. Carefully remove excess compound above or below the line with a razor blade, avoiding the conductor itself.

steps.title: Check operation after drying
steps.body: Allow at least 5 minutes before energizing the repair, then test the system for normal operation. Optimum adhesion develops after approximately 24 hours.

watchFor.title: Damage from cleaning tools
watchFor.body: Do not use scrapers, sharp instruments or abrasive cleaners for routine interior glass cleaning. The specified repair preparation and controlled trimming require particular care around intact lines.

watchFor.title: A thin or rushed repair
watchFor.body: Poor defrosting or excessive localized heating can result from insufficient coating thickness or inadequate drying between coats.

notes: The finished repair initially looks bright silver. It will tarnish over time toward the gold or brown appearance of the surrounding grid.

diagnostics.finding: A line looks intact but feels smooth where it was scraped.
diagnostics.meaning: Visible residue may remain after the raised conductive material has been removed.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the electrical break with a voltmeter or 12V test lamp before coating.

verification.title: Confirm normal operation
verification.body: Check the repaired system after the permitted drying period and confirm the original concern is resolved.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the repaired line locations and the outcome of the normal-operation check.

procedures.purpose: Complete heater and antenna grid repair, including materials, masking, coating, drying and operation check.
General service, sharp-edge and chemical-handling precautions required before repair.

guides.title: Repair a detached heated rear-window terminal
guides.summary: Solder a replacement lead terminal onto sound rear-window bus-bar material and verify heated-glass operation after cooling.
guides.introduction: The heated rear window uses an electrical grid to warm the glass and improve rearward visibility. Its bus bar is the conductive strip that distributes current to the grid, and the lead terminal connects that strip to the wiring. This repair restores a detached terminal where enough sound conductive material remains for the replacement terminal's contact areas.
guides.why: Successful attachment depends on both clean conductive material and controlled heating. The replacement terminal's temperature-sensitive paint indicates when its pre-applied solder is ready. Keeping the terminal still through heating and cooling prevents it from shifting before the joint has set.
searchTerms: heated rear window wire tab repair

when.summary: When a rear-window lead terminal has detached and sound conductive bus-bar material remains for attachment.
notes: A rear window that does not heat needs diagnosis; that symptom alone does not establish a terminal fault.

prepare.title: Temperature and repair materials
prepare.detail: Bring the vehicle to at least 60.8 °F (16 °C). Use Back Glass Terminal Kit 4F1Z-14421-AA, a grey scuff pad of 600 to 1000 grit, and Motorcraft Ultra-Clear Spray Glass Cleaner ZC-23 meeting ESR-M14P5-A.

prepare.title: Controlled soldering capability
prepare.detail: Use an electric soldering gun rated at 100 watts or more, rosin-core solder for tinning its tip, and a regular lead pencil to hold the terminal. Have a way to follow the specified heating and cooling periods.

steps.title: Establish a sound attachment area
steps.body: Locate intact conductive material for the replacement type A terminal. The terminal normally covers the original location, but its contact feet must sit on good conductive material. Space or pillar trim may require positioning above or below the original tab.

steps.title: Clean the bus bar
steps.body: Clean the repair area with the specified grey scuff pad, then the specified glass cleaner. Remove dirt, wax, grease, oil and other contamination so the terminal can attach to the conductive base.

steps.title: Prepare and hold the terminal
steps.body: Follow the [terminal repair procedure](#/document/G1695934). Melt a small amount of rosin-core solder onto the gun tip to improve heat transfer. Position the terminal and hold it with the pencil at 90 degrees; an angled hold can let it slip when the solder melts.

steps.title: Heat until the indicator changes
steps.body: Place the gun tip on top of the terminal, away from its painted areas, and energize it. The terminal already carries solder, flux and temperature-sensitive paint. The paint should liquefy and change color in approximately 25–45 seconds. As soon as the color completely changes on either side, de-energize the gun.

steps.title: Hold the joint and allow it to cool
steps.body: Keep the terminal stationary with the gun and pencil for an additional 30 seconds. Remove both tools, then allow another 2 minutes of cooling before attaching the wiring lead.

steps.title: Reconnect and check heating
steps.body: Attach the electrical lead, turn on the heated rear window and verify operation. Make this check after the full cooling period so reconnecting the lead does not disturb the newly formed joint.

watchFor.title: Unsuitable heat source
watchFor.body: Do not use a flame torch or flame-heated soldering gun. These provide inadequate tip heating, and their exhaust heat can damage nearby plastic trim.

watchFor.title: Missing conductive coating
watchFor.body: Do not place a terminal foot on the original attachment area where conductive material is missing.

diagnostics.finding: No sound conductive base is available for the terminal feet.
diagnostics.meaning: The required attachment condition has not been met.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the bus-bar condition before attempting this terminal repair.

diagnostics.finding: Heating remains absent after reconnection.
diagnostics.meaning: The terminal repair has not established normal system operation. Defrost supply also depends on relay control and can end through timing, ignition state or low-voltage load management.
diagnostics.next: Continue rear-window-defrost diagnosis rather than assuming another terminal is needed.

verification.title: Record the heating result
verification.body: Record whether heated rear-window operation was restored after the specified cooling period and lead reconnection.

procedures.purpose: Complete terminal preparation, soldering, cooling, reconnection and operating check.
Rear-window-defrost relay operation and control conditions relevant to interpreting the final heating check.

guides.title: Initialize the front door window motor
guides.summary: Teach the door-window motor its travel limits and lower soft stop, then verify the automatic functions fitted to the vehicle.
guides.introduction: The door-window regulator motor contains electronics that control automatic travel and the short drop used to clear the door weatherstrip. Initialization establishes the window’s travel limits and lower soft stop. It is needed when fitting a new door-window motor or restoring lost initialization. Convertible equipment needs care: it has no one-touch up or bounce-back feature, and its rear quarter-window motors do not require initialization.
guides.why: The motor must reach both ends of travel and complete the final cycle to establish the required positions. The door must remain closed. During initialization, the glass closes with high force and cannot detect an obstruction, so normal obstacle protection must not be relied upon.

when.summary: After door-window motor replacement or loss of initialization, including power interruption while the glass is moving.
notes: An existing motor must first be de-initialized; a new motor skips that operation.

prepare.title: Make the glass path safe
prepare.detail: Review the health and safety precautions in Section 100-00. Keep all objects and body parts clear of the glass throughout the procedure.

prepare.title: Arrange operating access
prepare.detail: Use the window control switch with the door closed and window power available. For an existing motor, arrange access to the battery cable or window motor fuse for the required interruption while the window is moving.

steps.title: De-initialize an existing motor
steps.body: For an existing motor, disconnect the battery cable or window motor fuse while the window is operating. Reconnect the cable or fuse before continuing. If a new motor has been installed, skip this step.

steps.title: Establish the upper travel limit
steps.body: With the door closed and window fully open, pull and hold the switch UP at its second detent. Continue holding until the glass has stalled against the top run for at least 2 seconds, then release the switch.

steps.title: Establish the lower travel limit
steps.body: Press and hold the switch DOWN at its second detent. Keep holding until the glass has stalled at the bottom of travel for at least 2 seconds. Reaching the bottom without the required hold does not complete this step.

steps.title: Set the lower soft stop
steps.body: Cycle the glass up and down once more. This additional cycle sets the soft stop for downward travel and completes the learning sequence before the operational checks.

watchFor.title: An open door
watchFor.body: The door-window motor will not initialize with the door open.

watchFor.title: An obstruction during learning
watchFor.body: Do not place an object or body part in the opening to test reversal during initialization; obstacle detection is unavailable.

notes: The second detent is the switch position used to request automatic window travel.
Short-drop operation is fitted to both coupe and convertible door windows.

diagnostics.finding: One-touch up and obstacle detection stopped after power was disconnected while a door window was moving.
diagnostics.meaning: That interruption disables these functions where fitted; it does not by itself establish motor failure.
diagnostics.next: Carry out the applicable initialization sequence and check operation.

diagnostics.finding: A convertible has no one-touch up or bounce-back response.
diagnostics.meaning: These features are not fitted to the convertible.
diagnostics.next: Assess only the functions fitted to that vehicle; do not use this absence to condemn the motor.

verification.title: Test the fitted automatic functions
verification.body: Check one-touch down on the door window and one-touch up where fitted. Convertible rear quarter windows are excluded from this initialization and one-touch test.

verification.title: Record the outcome
verification.body: Note which door was initialized, whether the motor was new or existing, and whether each applicable one-touch function operated correctly.

procedures.purpose: Door-window motor de-initialization, travel-limit learning, soft-stop setting and operational verification.
Door-motor operation, effects of interrupted power and convertible feature exceptions.

applicability.equipment: Front power door windows; distinguish coupe functions from convertible equipment.

guides.title: Replace a front-door glass run and adjust the window
guides.summary: Remove the fore or aft door-glass guide, restore its mounting position, then adjust and initialize the front window.
guides.introduction: The fore and aft glass runs guide the front window as it moves inside the door. Their position helps the glass follow the correct path and meet the weatherstrip. Replacing a run changes that mechanical guidance, so the work finishes with glass adjustment and power-window initialization, not simply tightening its mounting hardware.
guides.why: Marking the retainers preserves a useful starting position for installation, while adjustment establishes the final glass fit. The window also short-drops when the door opens and rises into the weatherstrip when it closes. Its mechanical position and learned operation both matter to that movement. A window that does not close correctly can require adjustment or electrical diagnosis; that symptom alone does not identify a failed run.
searchTerms: door window will not close correctly

when.summary: When an identified fore or aft glass-run problem requires removal or replacement.
notes: The left side is illustrated; the right side follows a similar procedure.
Choose the fore or aft access branch before dismantling the door.

prepare.title: Access and position marking
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastener tools, a way to mark retainer positions and a torque wrench. Fore-run access requires speaker removal; aft-run access requires removal of the door glass.

prepare.title: Adjustment and initialization
prepare.detail: Have the coupe or convertible glass-adjustment procedure available, together with the Power Door Window Initialization procedure referenced by the main repair.

steps.title: Identify the guide and retain the correct access path
steps.body: Determine whether the fore or aft run needs work. For the fore branch, install the window control switch and raise the glass fully. The aft branch instead begins by removing the glass through its separate procedure.

steps.title: Remove the fore run when required
steps.body: Remove the front-door speaker for access. Mark the retainer locations, loosen the upper nut and remove the lower nut. Withdraw the fore run while preserving those reference marks for installation.

steps.title: Remove the aft run when required
steps.body: With the glass removed, unbolt and position the driver door module (DDM) aside in the illustrated arrangement where fitted. Mark the run's retainer positions, loosen the upper nut, then remove the lower bolt and aft run.

steps.title: Refit the run and restore access components
steps.body: Reverse the applicable removal branch, using the marks to position the run. Tighten the specified run mounting nuts or bolt to 11 Nm. Refit the displaced module, glass or speaker through the appropriate procedure; the run-fastener torque does not apply to unrelated hardware.

steps.title: Adjust the glass and initialize operation
steps.body: Carry out the body-style-specific door-window glass adjustment. Then perform Power Door Window Initialization as referenced in the main procedure. Use that complete routine rather than improvising a switch-hold sequence.

watchFor.title: Assuming the marks are the final adjustment
watchFor.body: The mounting marks help restore the starting position, but the glass adjustment remains required.

watchFor.title: Expecting coupe features on a convertible
watchFor.body: Convertible models do not have one-touch up or bounce-back operation. Both body styles do have front-window short drop.

notes: Door modules are associated with memory-driver-seat equipment. Moving an existing module aside for access does not make this a module-replacement job.

diagnostics.finding: The glass does not seat correctly after run installation.
diagnostics.meaning: Its final mechanical position still needs to be established.
diagnostics.next: Complete the applicable glass-adjustment procedure, followed by initialization.

diagnostics.finding: One-touch up is unavailable after battery disconnection while the glass was moving.
diagnostics.meaning: On a vehicle equipped with that feature, initialization can be lost.
diagnostics.next: Perform the prescribed initialization before attributing the behavior to the replacement run.

verification.title: Check glass movement and seating
verification.body: Confirm the adjusted glass closes into the weatherstrip and short-drops when the door opens, then reseats when the door closes.

verification.title: Record completion
verification.body: Record which run was serviced, the body-style adjustment completed and the initialization result. Check only the automatic functions fitted to the vehicle.
