Front-door speaker removal and installation for fore-run access.
Front-door glass removal and installation for aft-run access.
Coupe door-window glass adjustment after installation.
Convertible door-window glass adjustment after installation.

guides.title: Replace a front door window control switch
guides.summary: Remove the switch and bezel together, separate the switch using the correct driver or passenger retention method, and restore its electrical connection.
guides.introduction: The door switch requests window movement; electronics in the window motor or door modules carry out that request. The driver’s master switch controls both front windows and, on convertibles, the rear quarter windows. The passenger switch controls its own door glass. This job changes the switch while retaining the bezel, unless the complete assembly is simply being removed and refitted.
guides.why: The bezel and switch have separate retention points. Removing the complete assembly first exposes the connector and the correct switch attachments without forcing the visible trim. Driver and passenger switches separate differently, and memory-seat equipment changes the electrical command path, so an unresponsive window does not by itself identify a failed switch.

when.summary: When a front window switch needs replacement or its switch-and-bezel assembly must be removed for access.
notes: Select the driver or passenger branch by function, rather than assuming the driver is always on the left.
Left-hand-drive illustrations also guide the similar right-hand-drive operation.

prepare.title: Identify the switch and equipment
prepare.detail: Confirm which door is being serviced and whether the vehicle has memory driver-seat equipment. With memory equipment, switch requests pass through door modules; without it, the switches provide low-current commands to the window motors.

prepare.title: Locate the retention points
prepare.detail: Use the illustrations in the switch procedure to identify the bezel clips and driver-switch retainers before applying force.

steps.title: Lift out the switch and bezel together
steps.body: Following the [switch removal procedure](#/document/G1695936), use the illustrated trim lever to release the bezel from the door trim and remove the switch-and-bezel assembly. The same overall method applies to both front doors.

steps.title: Disconnect the electrical connector
steps.body: Disconnect the switch connector once the assembly is accessible. This frees the assembly from the door wiring before any work on the switch-to-bezel attachment.

steps.title: Separate the switch only when replacing it
steps.body: For the driver switch, remove the retainers and lift the switch out of the bezel. For the passenger switch, release its retaining tab and remove the switch. If the existing assembly is only being removed for access, this separation is unnecessary.

steps.title: Install the switch and restore the bezel
steps.body: Reverse the appropriate branch: secure the replacement switch in the bezel with its retainers or tab, reconnect the electrical connector, and reinstall the assembly into the door trim. Check that the switch is retained before seating the bezel.

watchFor.title: Convertible feature differences
watchFor.body: Convertibles do not have one-touch up or bounce-back. Their absence must not be treated as evidence that the replacement switch has failed.

watchFor.title: Conditional initialization
watchFor.body: If the battery was disconnected while a door window was moving, one-touch up and obstacle detection can be disabled. Follow Power Door Window Initialization when that condition applies; switch replacement alone is not stated to require initialization.

notes: The short-drop movement that clears the door weatherstrip is controlled by window-motor electronics responding to the door-ajar signal.

diagnostics.finding: A window does not respond to the switch.
diagnostics.meaning: The missing response could involve the switch command path, door module where fitted, or window motor.
diagnostics.next: Establish the fault before treating switch replacement as the remedy.

diagnostics.finding: A window without memory-seat equipment ignores an unusually quick second-detent command.
diagnostics.meaning: The motor may not have received enough separation between signals to determine the requested direction.
diagnostics.next: Release and operate the switch again before concluding that it is defective.

verification.title: Check the applicable window functions
verification.body: With delayed accessory power active, confirm up and down commands from the serviced switch. Check equipped one-touch functions, respecting the convertible exceptions. At the master switch, check both front-window commands.

verification.title: Record the original complaint result
verification.body: Record which switch and window were affected and whether the same command now works. Note any remaining feature issue separately from the completed switch installation.

procedures.purpose: Both-door switch-and-bezel removal, driver/passenger switch separation and reverse-order installation.
Window command paths, normal operating behavior and the conditional initialization reference.

applicability.equipment: Trim-removal lever as illustrated, suitable tools for the driver-switch retainers, and a replacement switch matching the door and vehicle equipment.

guides.title: Replace and align the front door window glass on a coupe or convertible
guides.summary: Release the door glass from its clips, reinstall it, then complete body-style-specific adjustment and power window initialization.
guides.introduction: The front door glass is carried by the powered window mechanism and seats into the surrounding weatherstrip. On both coupe and convertible models, the short-drop function lowers it slightly when the door opens and raises it again when the door closes. Glass replacement therefore includes mechanical alignment and power window initialization as well as removal and refitting.
guides.why: The glass is retained by bolts and clips whose tangs must be released from the outboard side with a non-marring tool. Forcing the glass before those attachments release risks damage. Adjustment establishes its relationship to the seals, while the required initialization completes the power window setup after the repair.

when.summary: When front door glass requires replacement or removal, followed by adjustment and initialization.
notes: The procedure illustrates the left-hand door; the right-hand side is similar.

prepare.title: Plan the access and glass handling
prepare.detail: Follow the front door speaker removal procedure for access. Have the non-marring tool ready and maintain control of the glass as its attachments are released.

prepare.title: Prepare both finishing procedures
prepare.detail: Select coupe or convertible glass adjustment before starting. Also obtain Power Door Window Initialization through the reference in the glass procedure; it remains a required installation step.

steps.title: Remove the speaker
steps.body: Remove the front door speaker using the [linked speaker procedure](#/document/G1694049). Complete that access work before reaching the glass through the door openings.

steps.title: Remove the watershields
steps.body: Remove the lower watershield followed by the upper watershield, as illustrated. These covers must be restored during reassembly to re-establish the door’s internal water barriers.

steps.title: Position the glass fully up
steps.body: Remove the adhesive access covers, install the front door window control switch and raise the glass to its full-up position. Establish this position before releasing the glass fasteners.

steps.title: Release the glass attachments
steps.body: Remove the glass bolts. From the outboard side of the glass, use a non-marring trim tool to pry back the tang on each clip. Release the clip retention and remove the glass, keeping it controlled as the final attachment releases.

steps.title: Reinstall the glass and access parts
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure, ensuring the glass clips engage. Tighten the glass bolts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Restore the adhesive covers, watershields, speaker and other components disturbed during access.

steps.title: Adjust for the body style
steps.body: Carry out [coupe glass adjustment](#/document/G1697266) or [convertible glass adjustment](#/document/G1725016), as applicable. Use the correct procedure to establish the installed glass position.

steps.title: Initialize the door window
steps.body: Carry out Power Door Window Initialization using the reference within the [glass replacement procedure](#/document/G1695937). Do not substitute a guessed switch-hold sequence for that procedure.

watchFor.title: Prying against the glass
watchFor.body: Direct the non-marring tool at the retaining-clip tang from the specified outboard side.

watchFor.title: Incorrect feature expectations
watchFor.body: Convertible models do not have one-touch up or bounce-back. Their absence is not evidence that the glass repair failed.

notes: Body style determines the adjustment procedure. The short-drop function applies to both coupe and convertible.

diagnostics.finding: One-touch up and obstacle detection are disabled after the battery was disconnected while a suitably equipped door window was moving.
diagnostics.meaning: The window may require initialization; this condition alone does not identify damaged glass or a failed motor.
diagnostics.next: Complete the applicable power door window initialization and reassess operation.

diagnostics.finding: Glass does not clear or reseat into the weatherstrip during door operation.
diagnostics.meaning: Both body styles depend on short-drop movement and correct glass positioning.
diagnostics.next: Revisit the applicable adjustment and initialization procedures before considering the repair complete.

verification.title: Check seating and movement
verification.body: Confirm normal powered movement and that the glass lowers slightly as the door opens, then rises to seat when it closes. Assess one-touch features only where equipped.

verification.title: Record both finishing stages
verification.body: Record the body-style adjustment used, completion of door window initialization and the observed short-drop and closing results.

procedures.purpose: Front door glass removal and installation, including clip release and the required initialization reference.
Front door speaker removal and installation for access; the supplied reference describes the left-hand speaker.
Required front door glass adjustment for coupe models after installation.
Required front door glass adjustment for convertible models after installation.

applicability.equipment: Front door glass handling and regulator access; non-marring trim tool, torque tool, window control switch and access to the applicable glass-adjustment and initialization procedures.

guides.title: Replace a front door window regulator motor
guides.summary: Remove the regulator to replace its motor, then adjust the door glass and complete power-window initialization.
guides.introduction: The window regulator motor drives the mechanism that raises and lowers the door glass. Its integral electronics also control the short drop that clears the weatherstrip when the door opens, together with automatic window functions where fitted. Replacing this motor therefore involves both mechanical installation and restoring the glass position and electronic operation.
guides.why: The glass must clear the grooved weatherstrip during door opening and seat correctly after closing. Glass adjustment establishes its physical fit; initialization is a separate required operation. Skipping either can leave a newly installed motor with an unresolved window concern.

when.summary: When diagnosis has identified the front door window regulator motor as requiring replacement.
notes: A window that does not move is not, by itself, proof of a failed motor.
The left side is illustrated; the right side uses a similar procedure.

prepare.title: Plan the complete access work
prepare.detail: Have the front door regulator removal and installation procedure available. This motor procedure begins with the regulator removed.

prepare.title: Prepare for adjustment and initialization
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastener tools and the correct coupe or convertible glass-adjustment procedure ready, together with Power Door Window Initialization. These finishing operations are part of the repair.

steps.title: Remove the window regulator
steps.body: Follow [Front Door Window Regulator](#/document/G1695938) to remove the assembly. Complete its access and removal sequence before separating the motor.

steps.title: Separate the motor
steps.body: Remove the motor retainers shown in [Front Door Window Regulator Motor](#/document/G1695939), then lift the motor away as illustrated. The image identifies the motor attachments on the removed regulator.

steps.title: Install the replacement and refit the regulator
steps.body: Reverse the motor removal sequence, then reinstall the regulator using its complete procedure. Finish the mechanical assembly before moving on to glass adjustment.

steps.title: Adjust the door glass
steps.body: Carry out [Coupe Door Window Glass Adjustment](#/document/G1697266) or [Convertible Door Window Glass Adjustment](#/document/G1725016), according to body style. Correct positioning allows the glass to meet the weatherstrip properly.

steps.title: Initialize the front door window
steps.body: Carry out Power Door Window Initialization as referenced in the motor procedure. Follow that exact sequence rather than substituting an assumed switch routine. The exception for convertible rear quarter motors does not remove this front-door requirement.

watchFor.title: Glass does not clear or seat in the weatherstrip
watchFor.body: Recheck glass adjustment and short-drop operation before treating the replacement as complete.

watchFor.title: Expectations differ by body style
watchFor.body: Convertibles do not have one-touch up or bounce-back operation; do not use those features as convertible acceptance checks.

notes: Memory-seat equipment changes the command path through the driver and passenger door modules. It does not change the motor procedure's requirement for adjustment and initialization.

diagnostics.finding: The window does not respond to a switch.
diagnostics.meaning: The command path includes switches and, with memory-seat equipment, door modules.
diagnostics.next: Establish the motor fault before replacement; this removal procedure does not isolate an electrical failure.

diagnostics.finding: One-touch up was lost after battery disconnection during window movement.
diagnostics.meaning: That event disables one-touch up and obstacle detection where fitted.
diagnostics.next: Address initialization before assuming another motor is needed.

verification.title: Check movement and short drop
verification.body: Confirm raising and lowering from the applicable controls. Opening the door should lower the glass slightly; closing it should return the glass into the weatherstrip.

verification.title: Confirm the finishing operations
verification.body: Confirm that the correct body-style glass adjustment and front door window initialization were completed, and check the automatic functions fitted to the vehicle.

procedures.purpose: Front door regulator motor removal and installation, including required adjustment and initialization.
Remove and reinstall the regulator assembly to access its motor.
Adjust front door glass after installation on a coupe.
Adjust front door glass after installation on a convertible.
Explain motor command paths, short drop and equipment-dependent window operation.

applicability.equipment: Coupe or convertible front door windows, with or without a memory driver seat.

guides.title: Replace the front door window regulator on a coupe or convertible
guides.summary: Remove the window glass and regulator, install the mechanism in its marked position, then adjust and initialize the door window.
guides.introduction: The regulator carries the door glass and converts the motor's movement into window travel. Its mounting position affects how the glass meets the weatherstrip. The motor also contains electronics for features such as the short drop when a door opens, so a regulator repair includes mechanical alignment and the required window initialization.
guides.why: Marking the mountings preserves a useful starting position, but it does not replace the final glass adjustment. Correct positioning lets the glass clear the weatherstrip when the door opens and seat again when it closes. Coupe and convertible adjustment procedures differ.

when.summary: When diagnosis confirms a regulator fault or the mechanism must be removed for door repairs.
notes: The left-hand side is illustrated; the right-hand procedure is similar.
Convertibles do not have one-touch up or bounce-back features.

prepare.title: Plan the glass work
prepare.detail: Have the front door glass removal procedure and the adjustment procedure for the actual body style available. This job requires removing and handling the glass before releasing the regulator.

prepare.title: Prepare to preserve alignment
prepare.detail: Provide a marker and suitable fastener tools, including controlled tightening capability. Have the regulator-motor procedure ready if installing a new regulator, and obtain the named Power Door Window Initialization procedure before dismantling.

steps.title: Remove the door glass
steps.body: Follow [Front Door Window Glass](#/document/G1695937) to remove the glass first. This separates the glass from the mechanism before the regulator mountings are released.

steps.title: Disconnect and mark the regulator
steps.body: Remove the adhesive tapes, disconnect the regulator electrical connector and move the wiring harness aside. Mark the nut positions before removing the nuts so the regulator can return to its previous mounting position.

steps.title: Rotate the mechanism out of the door
steps.body: Rotate the front half of the regulator rearward, then rotate its rear half forward and remove it. Follow the illustrated movement sequence to bring the mechanism through the door openings.

steps.title: Transfer the motor when installing a new regulator
steps.body: Motor removal is necessary only when installing a new component. Use [Front Door Window Regulator Motor](#/document/G1695939) for removal and subsequent installation instead of treating the motor and regulator as an inseparable assembly.

steps.title: Refit at the recorded positions
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure, aligning the regulator with the marks made before dismantling. Restore its fasteners, electrical connection, harness position and tapes, and reinstall the glass through its own procedure.

steps.title: Adjust and initialize the window
steps.body: Carry out [coupe glass adjustment](#/document/G1697266) or [convertible glass adjustment](#/document/G1725016), as applicable. Then perform Power Door Window Initialization. Mounting marks guide assembly; these final operations establish the finished window setup.

watchFor.title: Mounting positions lost during removal
watchFor.body: Mark before loosening the nuts. Once the mechanism moves, its previous position is no longer a reliable visual reference.

watchFor.title: Harness caught during extraction
watchFor.body: Keep the disconnected harness aside while rotating the regulator through the openings, then restore its original routing during installation.

notes: Short-drop operation is fitted to both body styles. The lack of initialization for convertible rear-quarter motors does not cancel the front door window procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The window does not respond to a switch command.
diagnostics.meaning: Operation also depends on the motor, control signals and, with memory seats, the door modules; this alone does not establish regulator failure.
diagnostics.next: Establish whether the fault is mechanical or in the control/motor system before replacing the regulator.

diagnostics.finding: A coupe loses one-touch up after battery disconnection while the window was moving.
diagnostics.meaning: One-touch up and obstacle detection can be disabled by that interruption.
diagnostics.next: Complete the required initialization before treating the lost feature as a mechanical defect.

verification.title: Check travel and weatherstrip seating
verification.body: Confirm the adjusted glass travels correctly and performs its short drop when the door opens, then returns into the weatherstrip when the door closes. Check one-touch operation only as fitted.

verification.title: Record the completed setup
verification.body: Record the body style, completed glass adjustment and initialization, and the final travel and short-drop results.

procedures.purpose: Complete front door regulator removal and installation, including extraction movements and final setup requirements.
Remove and reinstall the front door glass.
Remove and reinstall the motor when fitting a new regulator.
Adjust the door glass on a coupe after regulator installation.
Adjust the door glass on a convertible after regulator installation.

guides.title: Replace the auxiliary power point socket
guides.summary: Replace the accessory power socket on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine using power point remover 501-194.
guides.introduction: The auxiliary power point spends its life accepting accessory plugs, then develops a remarkably firm handshake when it’s time to leave the car. I’ll walk you through using its dedicated puller to withdraw the socket, reach the wiring connector and fit a new socket. The wing nut does the pulling; enthusiastic wrestling with the cover has no job here.
guides.why: The socket provides the electrical contact for plug-in accessories. It sits inside a retainer—the surrounding holder that stays in place—and connects to the vehicle wiring at the rear. Tool 501-194 engages slots inside the socket, while its receiver cup and wing nut turn a tightening motion into a controlled outward pull.

when.summary: Use this procedure when the auxiliary power point socket has already been identified as needing replacement.
notes: An accessory that will not operate does not, by itself, establish that the socket needs replacing.

prepare.title: Confirm the vehicle and starting point
prepare.detail: This procedure applies to the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine. Start at the accessible power point cover. Access is through the socket opening: open the cover, extract the socket, then disconnect the wiring behind it.

prepare.title: Have the complete socket remover ready
prepare.detail: Use special service tool 501-194, Remover, Power Point, with its extractor, receiver cup and wing nut. The associated tool-kit identifiers are TKIT-2014D-ROW2 and TKIT-2014D-FL_ROW. Have a new power point socket ready for installation.

prepare.title: Know where this repair stops
prepare.detail: This walkthrough covers mechanical socket replacement, not electrical fault-finding. It also does not establish the rear connector’s latch-release method. If you cannot identify how that connector releases, obtain connector-specific instructions before trying to force it apart.

steps.title: Open the cover and expose the socket
steps.body: Swing the hinged power point cover fully clear of the opening. Leave the cover and surrounding retainer in place. You are removing the socket from inside that holder, not pulling the whole covered assembly out of the trim.

steps.title: Engage the extractor in the socket slots
steps.body:
Insert the engaging end of tool 501-194 into the socket. Position it so its engaging features catch the adjacent slots in the socket wall, as illustrated in the [auxiliary power point procedure](#/document/G1693972).

I would pause here to check the engagement before assembling the puller. The tool needs to catch the slots; merely resting inside the opening will not give it the purchase needed to extract the socket.

steps.title: Fit the receiver cup, then the wing nut
steps.body:
Place the receiver cup around the extractor shaft, with the cup’s open end facing the socket and retainer. The illustrated arrangement leaves space inside the cup for the socket to move outward.

Install the wing nut on the exposed threaded shaft and tighten it to bring the pulling assembly together. Keep the cover clear and check that the extractor remains engaged in the socket slots.

steps.title: Pull the socket out of its retainer
steps.body:
Continue tightening the wing nut to draw the socket outward into the receiver cup. Watch the socket move out of the surrounding retainer; that outward movement is the purpose of tightening the nut.

Stop the pulling operation once the socket is free of the retainer. Its rear electrical connector is still attached at this stage, so support the withdrawn socket without pulling on the wiring. Let the screw mechanism do the work—this is where the little damn tool earns its keep.

steps.title: Disconnect the rear electrical connector
steps.body:
With the socket withdrawn and the rear connection accessible, disconnect the electrical connector from the socket. The rear-view illustration shows the wiring plug separating from the back of the cylindrical socket.

Handle the connector body rather than using the wires as a handle. Set the removed socket and extraction tool aside, leaving the vehicle connector accessible for the new socket.

steps.title: Connect the new socket and push it into place
steps.body:
Connect the vehicle wiring connector to the new power point socket while the rear connection is still accessible. Then push the new socket into the existing retainer.

The order matters: connect first, seat second. Finish by checking that the socket is seated in the retainer and the cover can return over the opening.

watchFor.title: Extractor engagement before pulling
watchFor.body: Check that the extractor has caught the adjacent socket slots before loading the wing nut. If it is not engaged, reposition it before continuing.

watchFor.title: Wiring attached during extraction
watchFor.body: The wiring remains connected while the socket comes out of the retainer. Support the freed socket and disconnect the rear plug before carrying the old part away.

watchFor.title: Cup and cover clearance
watchFor.body: The receiver cup surrounds the extraction path. Keep the hinged cover clear while positioning the cup and drawing the socket outward.

notes: Installation calls for a new power point socket.
Wing-nut tightening is an extraction action controlled by the socket coming free; no numerical tightening torque is given.

diagnostics.finding: The extractor is inside the opening but has not caught the socket slots.
diagnostics.meaning: The pulling assembly is not ready to apply extraction force.
diagnostics.next: Reposition the extractor until it engages the adjacent slots, then fit or reset the receiver cup and wing nut.

diagnostics.finding: The socket is free of the retainer but remains attached to the wiring.
diagnostics.meaning: This is the expected stage between mechanical extraction and electrical disconnection.
diagnostics.next: Support the socket and disconnect the rear connector before setting the old socket aside.

diagnostics.finding: An accessory still has no power after the replacement.
diagnostics.meaning: Completing the socket replacement does not establish the condition of the rest of the electrical circuit.
diagnostics.next: Have the power point circuit diagnosed before replacing further parts.

verification.title: Confirm the connection and seating
verification.body: Before pushing the socket home, confirm that its rear electrical connector is connected. After installation, confirm that the new socket is seated in the retainer.

verification.title: Check cover operation
verification.body: Open and close the hinged cover to confirm that it clears the installed socket and returns over the opening. This is a mechanical completion check, not an electrical circuit test.

procedures.purpose: Socket access through the open cover, extraction using tool 501-194 and its receiver cup and wing nut, rear connector disconnection, and installation of a new socket.

applicability.equipment: Auxiliary power point with hinged cover

stepGroups.title: Open the socket and engage the tool
stepGroups.summary: Expose the opening and establish the extractor’s grip in the socket slots.

stepGroups.title: Extract and disconnect
stepGroups.summary: Assemble the puller, withdraw the socket and disconnect its rear wiring plug.

stepGroups.title: Connect and seat the replacement
stepGroups.summary: Reconnect the wiring before pushing the new socket into its retainer.

guides.title: Remove and reinstall the floor console
guides.summary: Release the console trim, concealed fasteners, parking-brake boot and electrical connections in sequence before removing the console.
guides.introduction: The floor console surrounds the gear selector and parking-brake lever and provides the central storage areas. Its outer panels conceal several layers of fasteners and wiring connections. Removing the complete console therefore involves progressively opening the trim and storage areas before the main assembly can come out.
guides.why: A console that appears loose may still be attached by its parking-brake boot, side clips or electrical connectors. Following the release sequence avoids pulling against these remaining attachments. Starting the selector bezel at its front corners also follows the intended trim-removal path.

when.summary: When replacing the floor console or removing it to reach components beneath it.
notes: The procedure illustrates an automatic transmission; the manual-transmission arrangement is similar.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim and fastener work
prepare.detail: Use an interior trim remover, suitable fastener tools and a torque tool capable of the specified low tightening setting. Keep track of which fasteners belong to each stage.

prepare.title: Allow access to the whole console
prepare.detail: The work reaches both console sides, the selector surround, the front stowage area and the storage bin beneath the lid.

steps.title: Open the side trim and front storage area
steps.body: Release the clips and remove the right-hand and left-hand console side trim panels with the trim remover. Remove the stowage-area mat and the upper console bolts exposed beneath it.

steps.title: Release the selector bezel
steps.body: Starting at the front corners, carefully pry the bezel upward and position it aside. Disconnect its electrical connector so the bezel is no longer restrained by its wiring.

steps.title: Remove the upper trim panel
steps.body: Open the console lid and remove the front retainers on both sides. Release the clips, position the gear-selector cover aside and remove the upper console trim panel. Disconnect the electrical connectors as the panel is released.

steps.title: Expose the main console attachments
steps.body: Release and remove both side bolt covers. Remove the storage-bin mat and the two nuts beneath it, then remove the stowage-area tray. Remove the two front upper console bolts.

steps.title: Separate the remaining attachments
steps.body: Release the console clips on both sides. Remove the screws retaining the parking-brake boot to the console and position the boot aside. Disconnect the remaining electrical connectors, then remove the console. The illustration shows these final attachment areas.

steps.title: Reinstall in reverse order
steps.body: Restore the electrical connections, parking-brake boot, clips, fasteners and trim in the reverse removal sequence. Tighten the specified upper console bolts, side front retainers, storage-bin nuts and front upper console bolts to 18 lb.in (2 Nm). Refit the trays and mats.

watchFor.title: Resistance during final removal
watchFor.body: Recheck the side clips, boot screws and electrical connections before pulling farther. These remain after the earlier trim and fasteners have been removed.

watchFor.title: Applying one torque to every attachment
watchFor.body: The listed tightening value applies to the identified bolts, retainers and nuts. The procedure does not assign that value to the parking-brake boot screws.

notes: The parking-brake boot is positioned aside during console removal; the parking-brake lever itself is not removed in this procedure.

verification.title: Check the restored assembly
verification.body: Confirm that the disconnected connectors are reconnected, the boot is attached, the specified fasteners are tightened and the trim clips are engaged. Check that both bolt covers, storage mats and the tray have been reinstated.

procedures.purpose: Complete floor-console removal and reverse-order installation, including trim releases, electrical connections and specified fastener torques.

guides.title: Remove the glove compartment assembly or upper stowage bin
guides.summary: Choose the correct access route for the glove compartment and passenger knee-airbag assembly or the separate upper stowage-bin latch work.
guides.introduction: The glove compartment and passenger knee airbag are serviced together as an assembly. Removing the storage compartment therefore involves a restraint-system component as well as trim, hinges and wiring. The upper stowage-bin latch has a different access route: the instrument panel must be removed before the bin can slide off its mounting bracket. Establish which part needs attention before beginning either branch.
guides.why: Correct restraint-system handling protects against accidental deployment and preserves crash protection. Upper-bin access adds steering-shaft, wiring and instrument-panel work, so a small latch repair can require substantial dismantling. Following the correct branch prevents unnecessary disassembly and keeps its specific fastener and reassembly requirements clear.
searchTerms: passenger knee airbag glove box assembly

when.summary: When the glove compartment assembly or upper stowage-bin latch requires service.
notes: Glove compartment removal follows the Passenger Knee Airbag procedure.
Upper stowage-bin latch access requires instrument-panel removal.

prepare.title: Restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover and the capability to carry out Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) depowering and repowering exactly as directed by the linked procedures.

prepare.title: Additional needs for upper-bin access
prepare.detail: Arrange an assistant for instrument-panel removal. Automatic-transmission vehicles require hoist access for the selector-cable work. Obtain new factory upper cowl bolt-and-washer assemblies and a new steering-column shaft bolt for the discarded fasteners.

steps.title: Select the repair branch and depower the restraints
steps.body: Use the [Passenger Knee Airbag procedure](#/document/G1696323) for the glove compartment assembly, or the [Instrument Panel procedure](#/document/G1693975) for upper-bin access. Depower the SRS before dismantling. Keep it depowered while reconnecting restraint components.

steps.title: Remove the glove compartment assembly when that is the target
steps.body: Release the right-hand instrument-panel trim and center finish panel, disconnecting the finish-panel connector. Open the glove box, detach its damper and press the door sides inward to disengage the stops. Open beyond the stops, disconnect and detach the wiring, then remove the upper and lower screws. Separate the assembly and disconnect its remaining connector. Continue to the reassembly step.

steps.title: Prepare the instrument panel for upper-bin access
steps.body: Move both front seats fully rearward. Follow the instrument-panel procedure through cowl-grille removal, positioning the wiper linkage aside, discarding the upper cowl bolts and removing the floor console. For an automatic transmission, perform the specified hoist, selector-cable and selector-assembly operations. Continue through the applicable body-style trim, driver knee-airbag and hood-release-handle removal.

steps.title: Disconnect the panel without straining steering parts or wiring
steps.body: Secure the steering wheel against rotation, then remove and discard the upper steering-column shaft bolt. Do not hammer, pry or force the column or shafts. Follow the complete connector, harness-retainer, insulation-panel and bracket sequence. Release the parking brake as directed. The A-pillar cross-beam bolts slide outward after loosening; they cannot be fully removed with the doors attached.

steps.title: Remove the panel and release the upper bin
steps.body: With all wiring clear and an assistant supporting the panel, rotate it face down and remove it through the left-hand front door opening. Then follow the [glove compartment procedure](#/document/G1693974): remove the upper-bin bolts, slide the bin off its bracket and remove it.

steps.title: Reassemble the chosen branch
steps.body: Reverse its removal sequence, using each procedure's installation torques. Replace the discarded shaft bolt and upper cowl bolt-and-washer assemblies during instrument-panel installation. Restore the glove-box stops and damper when disturbed. Complete restraint-component connections while the SRS remains depowered, then carry out the required SRS repowering procedure.

watchFor.title: Different glove-box screw torques
watchFor.body: Upper and lower assembly screws have different tightening values; use the Passenger Knee Airbag procedure for their locations and torques.

watchFor.title: Trapped wiring during panel movement
watchFor.body: Confirm connectors and harnesses are free before lifting or rotating the instrument panel.

notes: The passenger knee-airbag procedure illustrates left-hand drive and identifies right-hand drive as similar.
New factory upper cowl bolt-and-washer assemblies are required to prevent water leaks.

verification.title: Confirm the selected assembly is fully restored
verification.body: Check the fasteners, connectors, harness retainers and trim removed in that branch against its reverse installation sequence.

verification.title: Record restraint-system completion
verification.body: Record completion of the required SRS repowering after reassembly; installing the glove compartment alone does not finish this operation.

procedures.purpose: Distinguishes glove compartment assembly service from upper stowage-bin latch access and gives bin removal and installation.
Glove compartment and passenger knee-airbag assembly removal, installation, restraint precautions and repowering requirement.
Instrument-panel removal and installation required for upper stowage-bin access, including automatic-transmission access and replacement fasteners.

guides.title: Remove and refit the instrument panel center finish panel
guides.summary: Remove the right-hand dashboard trim, release the center finish panel’s clips, disconnect the optional ICM connector and refit both panels.
guides.introduction: Thirteen clips give this dashboard trim a surprisingly committed relationship with the car. I’ll walk you through separating them without turning the fascia into a tug-of-war trophy. The center finish panel is the decorative dashboard face around the center vents and across toward the passenger-side vent. It finishes the dashboard’s appearance and conceals the structure behind it; versions with the optional ICM also have an electrical connection to release before the panel can leave the car.
guides.why: The small right-hand trim panel comes off first, followed by the larger center finish panel. An interior trim remover lets you work at the retaining clips instead of bending the decorative face. Supporting the released fascia also keeps its optional electrical connection from carrying the panel’s weight.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang instrument panel center finish panel
Mustang center finish panel ICM connector

when.summary: For removal, replacement or refitting of the center finish panel on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
notes: The removal sequence applies with or without the optional ICM. Only the connector steps depend on that equipment being fitted.
This is a trim removal and installation job, not a diagnostic test for the ICM or other dashboard equipment.

prepare.title: Have an interior trim remover ready
prepare.detail: Use an interior trim remover to release both panels. Identify the small right-hand trim piece beside the outer edge of the glovebox and the larger fascia extending from the center vent area toward the passenger-side vent.

prepare.title: Plan to support the fascia
prepare.detail: Keep a hand supporting the larger panel as its clips release, and have somewhere to rest it with its decorative face protected. An equipped panel remains attached to wiring until the ICM connector is disconnected.

prepare.title: Recognize the connector limit
prepare.detail: The ICM connector is identified in the illustration, but its exact latch movement is not detailed. Identify how its release operates before separating it; if that is unclear, obtain connector-specific guidance rather than forcing the connection.

steps.title: Release and remove the right-hand trim panel
steps.body:
Start with the narrow trim piece beside the right-hand edge of the glovebox. The [removal illustration](#/document/G1693976) identifies three retaining clips arranged down this piece.

Work the interior trim remover behind the panel edge near the clip locations. Release the clips while supporting the trim, moving the tool to the next retained area rather than bending the whole piece away from the dashboard. Once all three clips are free, remove the trim and set it aside.

steps.title: Release the center finish panel’s 13 clips
steps.body:
Move to the larger fascia surrounding the center circular vent area and extending across to the passenger-side vent. The illustration identifies 13 retaining clips distributed across this panel.

Use the interior trim remover at its edges near the illustrated clip locations. Release the clips progressively, supporting the panel as it separates. If one area remains held, work at that retaining point instead of pulling harder on a distant end. Thirteen clips call for patience, not a stronger swear word.

Keep the released panel close to the dashboard until you have checked for the optional ICM wiring connection.

steps.title: Disconnect the optional ICM and remove the fascia
steps.body:
If the ICM is fitted, support the fascia and locate its electrical connector behind the panel, as shown in the illustration’s inset. Release the connector’s locking feature and separate the connection by its housing without pulling on the wires. With the connection detached, remove the fascia and place it on the prepared surface.

If the ICM is not fitted, omit that disconnection step and remove the fascia once its retaining clips are free.

steps.title: Reconnect the ICM before seating the center panel
steps.body:
Bring the center finish panel back to the dashboard and support it close enough to reconnect the wiring without stretching it. If the ICM was disconnected, reconnect its electrical connector and confirm that it is secured before closing the panel against the dashboard.

Position the wiring so it will not be caught between the fascia and its mounting surfaces. Align the panel’s retaining clips with their receiving locations.

steps.title: Seat the center finish panel
steps.body:
With the clips aligned, press the fascia into place at the retaining locations so the 13 clips engage. Keep the panel aligned as you work across it; do not use one seated end as a lever to force the other end home.

Check the perimeter for an evenly seated fit. If a section stands away from the dashboard, check that location for clip alignment or trapped wiring before applying more pressure.

steps.title: Refit the right-hand trim panel
steps.body:
Install the small right-hand trim piece last. Align its three clips with their receiving locations and press at those locations until the piece is retained.

Check that its edges sit correctly against the surrounding dashboard and the refitted fascia. Give both panels a gentle hand check for secure retention. The trim should now be holding the dashboard together visually, rather than auditioning as a loose percussion instrument.

watchFor.title: A released panel can still be connected
watchFor.body: On ICM-equipped cars, support the fascia after its clips release. Do not let the panel hang from its wiring or carry it away before disconnecting the connector.

watchFor.title: Resistance concentrated in one area
watchFor.body: A section that remains held during removal calls for checking the nearby retaining clip. Avoid twisting the fascia or pulling from the opposite end to overcome that resistance.

watchFor.title: A panel that will not sit flush
watchFor.body: During installation, check clip alignment and wiring clearance before pressing harder. A raised edge is a reason to revisit that area, not to increase force across the entire panel.

notes: RH means the vehicle’s right-hand side.
The illustrated fascia has the optional ICM. Its presence does not change the right-hand-trim-first removal sequence.
Installation reverses removal: restore the optional electrical connection, seat the center finish panel, then install the right-hand trim.

diagnostics.finding: The fascia’s clips have released, but an ICM connector still attaches it to the car.
diagnostics.meaning: The panel is mechanically released but remains electrically connected.
diagnostics.next: Support the fascia and disconnect the ICM connector before removing the panel completely.

diagnostics.finding: No optional ICM is fitted.
diagnostics.meaning: The conditional ICM connector operation does not apply.
diagnostics.next: Continue with panel removal or refitting, retaining the same clip-release and installation order.

diagnostics.finding: One area remains retained during removal or stands proud during refitting.
diagnostics.meaning: That area has not completed its release or seating operation; this alone does not identify a failed part.
diagnostics.next: During removal, check the local clip engagement. During refitting, check clip alignment and wiring clearance before continuing.

verification.title: Confirm both panels are retained
verification.body: Check that the center finish panel and right-hand trim sit evenly against their surrounding surfaces and remain secure during a gentle hand check.

verification.title: Confirm the electrical connection was restored
verification.body: If you disconnected the optional ICM, confirm that its connector was secured before the fascia was seated and that its wiring was clear of the panel’s seating surfaces. These are reassembly checks, not an ICM diagnostic test.

procedures.purpose: Removal and installation of the instrument panel center finish panel, including the three-clip right-hand trim, 13-clip fascia and optional ICM electrical connection.

stepGroups.title: Remove the trim and fascia
stepGroups.summary: Release the right-hand trim first, then the center panel and its optional electrical connection.

stepGroups.title: Reconnect and refit
stepGroups.summary: Restore the optional connector, seat the center fascia and install the right-hand trim last.

guides.title: Remove and replace the instrument panel upper section
guides.summary: Separate the dashboard upper section from its cross beam after removing the complete panel and clearing its trim, electronics, steering column and wiring.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel upper section surrounds and supports dashboard trim, displays, grilles and other fittings. Its attachment to the in-vehicle cross beam is reached through extensive disassembly of the removed instrument panel. This is a bench repair involving the passenger knee airbag, steering column and several electronic modules, with different removal paths for the AM/FM/CD/SYNC and touchscreen arrangements.
guides.why: The panel must be turned front to back during the work, so an unsuitable bench can damage it. Wiring remains attached across several disassembly stages and can be trapped or pulled when the upper section separates. The steering-column bolts also require special attention: the front and rear bolts differ, and the removed bolts must be discarded.

when.summary: When the instrument panel upper section requires removal or replacement.
notes: Allow for complete instrument-panel removal before beginning upper-section disassembly.
Select the audio/display branch that matches the fitted equipment.

prepare.title: Provide a suitable work surface
prepare.detail: Support the removed panel on a surface that allows rotation front to back without damage. Organize removed trim, connectors and fasteners by location.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint and steering capability
prepare.detail: Passenger knee-airbag and steering-column removal are part of this job. Follow the dedicated airbag procedure and obtain new steering-column bolts before reassembly.

prepare.title: Prepare for several fastening requirements
prepare.detail: Use tools capable of applying the individual trim, module and structural fastener torques in the complete procedure; these values are not interchangeable.

steps.title: Remove the panel and knee airbag
steps.body: Complete [Instrument Panel removal](#/document/G1693975), place the assembly on the suitable work surface, then remove the [passenger knee airbag](#/document/G1696323) under its dedicated procedure. Continue with the [upper-section procedure](#/document/G1693977).

steps.title: Strip the storage and cluster trim
steps.body: Remove the glove-compartment upper stowage bin and right-hand finish panel. Remove the instrument panel cluster (IPC) trim and detach its gap hider from the upper steering-column cover. Release the cluster, disconnect its connector and release its harness retainer.

steps.title: Clear the upper grilles and speaker
steps.body: Release the defroster grille and disconnect its electrical connector. Remove the speaker grille, then the speaker bolts and speaker. Disconnect the associated connectors and release the harness retainer so this wiring no longer holds the parts together.

steps.title: Follow the fitted audio/display branch
steps.body: For AM/FM/CD/SYNC, remove the front controls interface module (FCIM), front control/display interface module (FCDIM), and accessory protocol interface module (APIM), disconnecting their connectors. For touchscreen vehicles, remove the FCIM and front display interface module (FDIM) with their connectors. Both branches then require audio control module (ACM) removal and disconnection.

steps.title: Remove the steering-column equipment
steps.body: Remove the lower shroud’s bolt and screw, then the shroud. Disconnect the harness, release its retainers and move it aside. Disconnect the column connector and remove the column, noting the different front and rear bolt locations before discarding those bolts.

steps.title: Free the remaining connections and rear attachments
steps.body: Complete the subsequent bolt-removal and three-connector disconnection stage identified in the procedure. From the rear, move the left-hand harness aside, remove the upper-section-to-cross-beam bolts and release the retainers. Repeat that sequence on the right-hand side.

steps.title: Separate the upper section
steps.body: Check that every connector and wire is free to move without obstruction. From the front, remove the five upper-section-to-cross-beam bolts shown in the illustration, then remove the upper section. Do not pull the section away against attached or trapped wiring.

steps.title: Reassemble in reverse order
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, restoring harness retainers and connectors as their components are installed. Fit new steering-column bolts in the correct front and rear positions. Apply each specified torque and complete the dedicated airbag and instrument-panel installation procedures.

watchFor.title: A wire still bridging the separation
watchFor.body: Stop and free the connection or retainer before lifting the upper section away.

watchFor.title: Mixed steering-column bolts
watchFor.body: Front and rear locations use different bolts; location identification must survive disposal of the originals.

notes: The two audio/display arrangements share the overall repair purpose but have different module-removal sequences.

verification.title: Confirm wiring and attachment restoration
verification.body: Check the reversed sequence for restored connectors, harness retainers, trim clips and upper-section attachments, with no wiring hindered.

verification.title: Record the steering-column fastener check
verification.body: Record that new column bolts were fitted in their identified front and rear locations and tightened to the specified value.

procedures.purpose: Upper-section bench removal and installation, including both audio/display equipment branches and steering-column fastener requirements.
Complete instrument-panel removal before bench work and installation afterward.
Required passenger knee-airbag removal and installation using its dedicated restraint-system procedure.

guides.title: Remove and refit the instrument panel
guides.summary: Remove the instrument panel through the left front door after safely disconnecting its restraints, steering shaft, wiring and mounting points.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel is a large assembly secured across the passenger compartment and connected to wiring, the steering column and surrounding trim. Removing it creates substantial access but involves more than cosmetic panels. The automatic-transmission version adds selector removal, and the A-pillar trim procedure depends on whether the car is a coupe or convertible.
guides.why: The supplemental restraint system (SRS) must be depowered before the airbag work. Steering shaft fasteners must be renewed, and the steering wheel must remain secured against rotation to protect the clockspring. New factory upper cowl bolt-and-washer assemblies are also required to prevent water leaks.

when.summary: When an established repair requires removal of the complete instrument panel.
notes: Automatic-transmission vehicles require a hoist for selector cable access.
Use the A-pillar trim procedure for the fitted body style.

prepare.title: Arrange safe access and assistance
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover and an assistant available. The work requires SRS and steering-column service capability, plus correct hoist positioning for the automatic-transmission branch.

prepare.title: Obtain replacement fasteners
prepare.detail: Provide new factory upper instrument panel cowl bolt-and-washer assemblies and a new upper steering column shaft-to-column bolt.

steps.title: Create working space and depower the restraints
steps.body: Move both front seats fully rearward. Carry out [SRS depowering](#/document/G1696297) before proceeding with restraint components. Follow the [instrument panel procedure](#/document/G1693975) throughout, including installation details embedded in its removal sequence.

steps.title: Release the cowl attachments
steps.body: Remove the cowl panel grille. Remove the wiper linkage mounting bolts and position the linkage aside. Remove the instrument panel cowl bolts, discarding the upper bolts for replacement with the specified factory assemblies.

steps.title: Clear the console and automatic selector
steps.body: Remove the floor console. On automatic-transmission vehicles, raise the vehicle on a hoist using the correct lifting points, remove the selector cable bracket bolt and cable, then remove the selector assembly and disconnect its electrical connector.

steps.title: Remove the surrounding trim and knee airbag
steps.body: Remove both A-pillar trims and instrument panel end finish panels, moving the weatherstrips aside as directed. Remove the right scuff plate and lower cowl trim, then the left scuff plate. Follow the separate driver knee-airbag and hood-release-handle procedures. Remove the left cowl trim and release its connectors and harness retainer.

steps.title: Disconnect the steering shaft and remaining wiring
steps.body: Secure the steering wheel against rotation; tilting the column upward eases access. Remove and discard the upper shaft-to-column bolt, then move the shaft aside without hammering, prying or forcing it. Release the remaining harness connections and retainers. Remove the right insulation panel and ambient light, and disconnect wiring at the right lower cowl and behind the glove compartment.

steps.title: Release the panel supports
steps.body: Remove the right and left center fasteners, trim cover and center bracket with its bolts and push pin. Release the parking brake. Loosen the A-pillar-to-crossbeam bolts and slide them outward as far as possible; they cannot be withdrawn fully with the doors attached. Disconnect both A-pillar harnesses and retainers, then remove the remaining left and right panel fasteners.

steps.title: Lift the assembly out with assistance
steps.body: Confirm that no wiring or connectors remain caught. With an assistant, rotate the instrument panel face down and remove it through the left front door opening, protecting the panel as it clears the vehicle.

steps.title: Refit in reverse order
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, using the new cowl assemblies and steering shaft bolt. Apply each fastener's specified torque from the complete procedure. Reinstall the knee airbag and other removed components through their linked procedures, including the applicable restraint-system return-to-service requirements.

watchFor.title: Steering shaft resistance
watchFor.body: Do not overcome resistance by hammering, levering or forcing the shaft or column; damage can compromise steering control.

watchFor.title: Trapped wiring
watchFor.body: Stop moving the panel if a connector or harness is still attached or obstructed.

notes: Seats shown removed in illustrations are for clarity; this operation starts by moving them fully rearward.

verification.title: Check reconnection and retention
verification.body: Review the removal sequence to confirm restoration of connectors, harness retainers, the ambient light, trim and panel supports.

verification.title: Record renewed fasteners
verification.body: Record installation of the new factory upper cowl assemblies and steering shaft bolt, with their specified tightening completed.

procedures.purpose: Complete instrument panel removal and installation, including automatic-transmission access and mounting torques.
Required SRS depowering before restraint-component work.
Remove and reinstall the cowl panel grille.
Remove and reinstall the floor console.
Correct lifting points and hoist precautions for automatic-transmission selector access.
Coupe A-pillar trim removal and installation.
Convertible A-pillar trim removal and installation.
Driver knee-airbag removal and installation.
Hood latch release handle removal and installation.

guides.title: Remove and refit the overhead console on a 2015 Mustang
guides.summary: Remove or replace the overhead console on a coupe or convertible, including coupe headliner access, seatbelt refitting and setup of a new intrusion-sensor-equipped console.
guides.introduction: The overhead console looks like a small job until the coupe's headliner invites half the rear trim to the party. I'll walk you through that access route in order, then put everything back—including the seatbelt anchors. Convertible owners get a shorter route. The console carries the overhead lamps and associated electrical equipment; some versions also contain an intrusion sensor for detecting activity inside the cabin.
guides.why: The console is held by clips and connected to the vehicle wiring. On a coupe, lowering the headliner provides the required access before those clips are released. A new console fitted with an intrusion sensor also needs electronic initialization and a body control module check, so clicking it back into the roof is only the mechanical part of that installation.

when.summary: Use this procedure when the overhead console needs removal, refitting or replacement.
notes: Choose the coupe or convertible route before removing trim.
Determine whether you are refitting the original console or installing a new console equipped with an intrusion sensor.
This is a removal and installation job. An unexplained lamp, alarm or communication fault needs separate diagnosis before replacement is treated as the cure.

prepare.title: Tools and replacement console
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover. For coupe access, also have tools suitable for the illustrated retainers and seatbelt D-ring bolts, plus a torque wrench capable of 30 lb.ft (40 Nm). If replacing the console, match the replacement to the body style and fitted equipment, including the intrusion sensor.

prepare.title: Arrange the conditional electronic work first
prepare.detail: A new console equipped with an intrusion sensor requires a diagnostic scan tool that supports Toolbox > Electrical > Service Functions > LIN New Module Initialization, together with the BCM self-test and code clearing/retrieval. Arrange that capability before starting; mechanical refitting alone does not complete this branch.

prepare.title: Keep the car stationary and prevent unintended starting
prepare.detail: Work with the car parked and the parking brake applied. If remote start is fitted, disable it through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle before dismantling. This cabin job does not require lifting the vehicle or working under the hood.

prepare.title: Protect yourself and organize the trim
prepare.detail: Use eye and ear protection as directed by the general service precautions, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged components. Keep each panel's retainers and tether attachments together so they return to their original locations. The relevant precautions are linked in [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

prepare.title: Understand the coupe access route
prepare.detail: The coupe sequence below follows the 2015 Ford Mustang Workshop Manual, Headliner - Lowering, physical pages 2422–2424. It lowers the headliner inside the car; complete headliner removal is unnecessary. The trim procedures illustrate the right side and left-hand drive, with the opposite side and right-hand drive described as similar.

steps.title: Select the body-style route
steps.body: Complete the preparation above. On a convertible, go directly to step 14: the console procedure starts with releasing its clips. On a coupe, complete steps 2–13 first, working on both sides wherever instructed. I keep the coupe access work in order because a stubborn panel is often still attached to something perfectly innocent.

steps.title: Coupe: remove both sun visors
steps.body: At each visor's roof mounting, remove the retainer cap, then release the retainer beneath it. Remove the visor from its mounting. If it has an electrical connection, support the visor while disconnecting that connector, then set the visor aside. Keep the mounting cap and retainer with the corresponding visor.

steps.title: Coupe: free the weatherstrip beside each A-pillar
steps.body: The A-pillar is the front roof pillar beside the windshield. At the lower end of its door-opening weatherstrip, remove the pin-type retainer shown beside the dashboard end. Move the weatherstrip away from the pillar trim far enough to uncover its edge. Repeat on the other side. See [A-Pillar Trim Panel - Coupe](#/document/G1692599).

steps.title: Coupe: release the A-pillar trim, tether and optional speaker connection
steps.body: Release the A-pillar trim clips and move the panel away only far enough to reach its tether anchor—the retaining connection behind the panel. Disconnect that anchor. If a speaker is fitted in the panel, disconnect its electrical connector behind the speaker grille. Release the remaining clip engagement and remove the panel. Repeat on the other side; do not pull the trim away while its tether or speaker wiring is still attached.

steps.title: Coupe: detach the headliner harness connection
steps.body: With the A-pillar trim removed, find the headliner wiring running down the exposed windshield pillar. Detach its wire-harness retainers and the electrical-connector retainers, then disconnect the electrical connector. Free the retained wiring before lowering the headliner so the harness does not become its suspension strap.

steps.title: Coupe: remove the visor clips and disconnect the mirror if equipped
steps.body: Remove the retainer and the small sun visor support clip from each side of the roof. These are the clips that hold the free ends of the visors, separate from the visor mounts already removed. If the rear-view mirror has an electrical connector, disconnect it at the mirror.

steps.title: Coupe: remove both small upper rear pillar panels
steps.body: Remove the small triangular upper rear pillar panels at both rear corners of the headliner, above the rear seating area. Release their clips, move each panel away enough to reach its tether clip, disconnect the tether and remove the panel. These are the same panels referenced during rear-quarter trim removal, so remove each only once. The headliner procedure calls them D-pillar trim, while the rear-quarter procedure calls them C-pillar trim.

steps.title: Coupe: remove the door-sill scuff trim on both sides
steps.body: Begin the rear-quarter access through the [Loadspace Trim Panel - Coupe procedure](#/document/G1692601). Move the door-opening weatherstrip aside along the sill and rear opening as needed to uncover the trim edges. Release the scuff plate's clips and lift the long trim panel from the door sill. Its illustration shows five clips along the panel and two additional lower clip locations; free the attachments rather than bending the panel around them. Repeat on the other side.

steps.title: Coupe: move the front seats forward and remove the rear cushion
steps.body: Move both front seats fully forward. At the front edge of the rear seat cushion, press in the locking tabs on both sides to release the cushion from the floor. Only after releasing those tabs, lift and disengage the cushion and remove it from the cabin. Pulling upward without pressing the tabs can damage them—this is one of those moments when more muscle just buys more plastic. See [Rear Seat Cushion](#/document/G1692168).

steps.title: Coupe: fold the rear backrests and remove the loadspace side trim
steps.body: Release the rear backrest latch and lower the backrest on each side. Move the safety-belt guide aside, then release the loadspace trim panel's attachments and remove the panel. The large side panel lies below the rear side window and around the belt area. Its rear view shows five spring clips, two pin-type retainers and a lower attachment; check those attachment areas as you free it. Keep the belt clear while removing the panel. Repeat on the other side.

steps.title: Coupe: disconnect the upper seatbelt anchors
steps.body: On each side, release the tabs on the small cover over the seatbelt D-ring—the upper guide through which the shoulder belt runs—and remove the cover. Remove the D-ring bolt and position the seatbelt aside. Keep the belt untwisted and clear of the trim being removed. The installation torque for each D-ring bolt is 30 lb.ft (40 Nm); apply it during reassembly.

steps.title: Coupe: remove the rear quarter trim panels
steps.body: Open the garment hook's retainer cover. Remove the retainer and the garment hook, then release the rear quarter trim clips and remove the panel. The panel extends around the rear side-window opening and down beside the rear seat; its illustration shows six retaining clips. Repeat on the other side. Do not leave the garment hook attached and try to persuade the surrounding trim to stretch.

steps.title: Coupe: position the seats and lower the headliner
steps.body: With both rear quarter panels removed, put both front seats in the fully forward and fully reclined positions. Lower the headliner inside the cabin, supporting it as it comes down. Check that the pillar wiring, mirror connection and removed roof fittings are free rather than taking the load. Keep the headliner supported without forcing or folding it; it stays in the car for this job.

steps.title: Both body styles: release the overhead console clips
steps.body: Locate the console above the front occupants, beside the sun visors. On the coupe, do this after lowering the headliner. On the convertible, start console removal here. Use the interior trim remover to release the two retaining clips at the sides of the console and ease the assembly down. Support it as the clips release; the electrical connectors are still attached. The two body-style arrangements are covered in [Overhead Console](#/document/G1693978).

steps.title: Disconnect the console and remove it
steps.body: With the console supported below its mounting, release the electrical connector locks and unplug the connections on its rear face. The illustrations show larger harness plugs at the lower sides and a smaller connection near the center; disconnect the connections fitted to your assembly before moving it away. Hold the connector bodies rather than pulling on the wires. Once all connections are free, remove the console.

steps.title: Reconnect and fit the original or replacement console
steps.body: Before fitting, compare the console's connector locations and clip positions with the removed assembly. Reconnect each electrical plug to its matching connection and make sure its lock engages. Keep the wiring clear of the mounting edge, align the console and engage both retaining clips. Check that the assembly sits properly in its opening. Convertible owners can now go to step 26; coupe owners continue with cabin restoration.

steps.title: Coupe: raise the headliner back into position
steps.body: Reverse the lowering movement and return the headliner to its roof position. Guide the wiring back toward its original route and keep it clear of the headliner edges and surrounding trim. Support the headliner while restoring the parts removed for access.

steps.title: Coupe: refit the rear quarter trim and garment hooks
steps.body: On both sides, position the rear quarter trim panel with the seatbelt clear and engage its clips at their original mounting points. Reinstall the garment hook and its retainer, then close the retainer cover. Check that the panel edges are seated before installing the belt anchor.

steps.title: Coupe: secure each seatbelt D-ring to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm)
steps.body: Return each seatbelt D-ring to its mounting with the webbing untwisted. Install its bolt and tighten it to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm). Refit the D-ring cover and engage its tabs. Confirm that the belt runs through the guide correctly and remains accessible. Complete both anchors before the car returns to use.

steps.title: Coupe: refit the loadspace trim and belt guides
steps.body: Position each loadspace side trim panel, keeping the seatbelt webbing clear of its edges. Restore its lower attachment, pin-type retainers and spring-clip engagement at the original locations. Return the safety-belt guide to position. Check that neither belt is twisted or trapped behind the panel.

steps.title: Coupe: restore the backrests, rear cushion, sill trim and lower weatherstrip
steps.body:
Raise each rear backrest and engage its latch. Refit the rear cushion by reversing its removal: position it over its mountings, keep the belts and buckles above and accessible, and engage the front locking tabs with the floor retainers. Confirm that the cushion is retained.

Refit both scuff plate trim panels and engage their clips. Return the weatherstrip along the sill and rear door opening to its original position. Keep the front A-pillar section clear until its trim is refitted.

steps.title: Coupe: reconnect the rear pillar tethers and refit the small panels
steps.body: Refit the small upper rear pillar panels removed in step 7. Reconnect each tether clip before seating the trim, then align and engage its retaining clips. Confirm both panels are retained and every disconnected tether is reconnected.

steps.title: Coupe: restore the mirror, visor support clips and headliner harness
steps.body: Reconnect the rear-view mirror electrical connector if it was disconnected. Reinstall each small visor support clip and its retainer. Reconnect the headliner electrical connector at the windshield pillar, then restore the connector retainers and wire-harness retainers so the wiring follows its original retained route.

steps.title: Coupe: refit both A-pillar panels and their weatherstrips
steps.body: Reconnect the speaker electrical connector where fitted. Reconnect the A-pillar trim tether anchor, align the panel and engage its clips. Return the adjacent door weatherstrip to position and reinstall its pin-type retainer near the lower pillar. Repeat on the other side. Check that the trim has not trapped the harness or displaced the weatherstrip.

steps.title: Coupe: refit the visors and restore the seat positions
steps.body: Reconnect each visor's electrical connector if fitted, position the visor in its mounting, engage the retainer and refit the retainer cap. Check that both visors are mounted and can return to their support clips. Return the front seats from the access positions to usable positions, checking that the rear belts and buckles remain accessible.

steps.title: Initialize a new console equipped with an intrusion sensor
steps.body: Perform this step only when installing a new console equipped with an intrusion sensor. Using a compatible diagnostic scan tool, select Toolbox > Electrical > Service Functions > LIN New Module Initialization and carry out that procedure. LIN is the communication network used for this module setup. Refitting the original console, or installing a new console without the sensor, does not trigger this requirement.

steps.title: Complete the conditional BCM self-test and code check
steps.body: For the same new intrusion-sensor-equipped console, carry out the body control module (BCM) self-test. Clear the BCM diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), then retrieve the BCM codes again to confirm that all have cleared. If codes remain or return, retain the results and continue diagnosis before considering the installation complete; a code alone does not establish that the replacement console is faulty.

watchFor.title: A panel still has a tether
watchFor.body: A-pillar and upper rear pillar trim have tether connections behind them. Move a released panel only far enough to disconnect its tether; reconnect the tether before seating the panel during refitting.

watchFor.title: Rear cushion tabs must release before lifting
watchFor.body: Press in the locking tabs at the front of the cushion on both sides. Lifting against locked tabs can damage them.

watchFor.title: Seatbelt restoration is part of the console job on a coupe
watchFor.body: Tighten both removed D-ring bolts to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm). Keep all belt webbing untwisted and all belts and buckles accessible throughout trim and cushion refitting.

watchFor.title: Support the console and headliner
watchFor.body: Clips releasing does not mean the console is electrically disconnected. Support it until its plugs are free. During coupe access, support the lowered headliner without forcing it around attached wiring or trim.

watchFor.title: A new sensor-equipped console needs electronic completion
watchFor.body: LIN initialization comes before the BCM self-test, code clearing and code retrieval. That requirement is conditional on installing a new component equipped with an intrusion sensor.

notes: The coupe access involves both sides of the cabin even though the console sits near the center of the roof.

The headliner-lowering and rear-quarter procedures use D-pillar and C-pillar terminology for upper rear trim operations. Track the actual panels and tethers removed, and refit each physical panel once.
The trim and console refitting operations reverse their removal actions. The critical numeric tightening value in this access route is the seatbelt D-ring bolt torque: 30 lb.ft (40 Nm).

diagnostics.finding: The car is a convertible.
diagnostics.meaning: The overhead-console procedure starts directly with releasing the console clips.
diagnostics.next: Use steps 15–17, then apply steps 28–29 only if installing a new intrusion-sensor-equipped console.

diagnostics.finding: The car is a coupe.
diagnostics.meaning: Headliner lowering is required before releasing the console.
diagnostics.next: Complete the visor, pillar, wiring and rear-trim access in steps 2–14, then restore those parts after console installation.

diagnostics.finding: The original console is being refitted, or the new console has no intrusion sensor.
diagnostics.meaning: The conditional new intrusion-sensor module setup does not apply.
diagnostics.next: Complete mechanical refitting and the physical completion checks.

diagnostics.finding: A new console equipped with an intrusion sensor is being installed.
diagnostics.meaning: Reconnecting the plugs and clips does not finish installation.
diagnostics.next: Perform LIN New Module Initialization, then the BCM self-test, clear the codes and retrieve them again.

diagnostics.finding: BCM codes remain or return after clearing.
diagnostics.meaning: The required confirmation that all codes have cleared has not been achieved.
diagnostics.next: Keep the retrieved code results for further diagnosis. Do not condemn the console solely from code presence.

diagnostics.finding: A belt is twisted, trapped behind trim or a buckle is inaccessible.
diagnostics.meaning: The coupe's restraint-system restoration is incomplete.
diagnostics.next: Correct the belt routing and trim or cushion placement before allowing occupants to use the seat. Confirm both D-ring bolts have been tightened to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm).

verification.title: Console seating and connections
verification.body: Confirm that every disconnected console plug is locked in place, the wiring is clear of the mounting edges and both retaining clips hold the console properly. Check the fitted lamps and controls as an ordinary completion check; this does not replace intrusion-sensor initialization or diagnose an existing electrical fault.

verification.title: Coupe roof and trim restoration
verification.body: Confirm the headliner is back in position; pillar tethers, clips and speaker connections are restored; the headliner harness is connected and retained; and the mirror connection, visors and visor support clips are restored where fitted.

verification.title: Coupe seats and seatbelts
verification.body: Confirm both D-ring bolts were tightened to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm), their covers are attached, the rear backrests latch, and the rear cushion locking tabs retain the cushion. Check that the webbing is untwisted and the belts and buckles are accessible. Confirm the scuff trim and weatherstrips are seated.

verification.title: New intrusion-sensor-equipped console
verification.body: Confirm LIN New Module Initialization was completed, the BCM self-test was performed, and retrieval after clearing shows that all BCM DTCs have cleared.
