stepGroups.summary: Start with the correct coupe or convertible access path.

stepGroups.title: Free the coupe's front roof fittings
stepGroups.summary: Remove the visors and A-pillar trim, then free wiring and mirror connections.

stepGroups.summary: Remove rear pillar, sill, seat and side trim, including the upper belt anchors.

stepGroups.summary: Position the seats, release the console, disconnect it and refit the assembly.

stepGroups.summary: Raise the headliner, refit trim, torque the belt anchors and restore the rear seating.

guides.title: Diagnose difficult door opening and lock or entry faults
guides.summary: Separate handle, cable, latch and alignment problems from electrical lock and keyless-entry concerns before choosing a repair.
guides.introduction: Each door handle pulls a cable that releases the latch. Power locking and passive entry add electrical controls to this mechanical system. Comparing the handles, then isolating their cables, helps identify where movement is being lost or resisted.
guides.why: A stiff door can result from latch friction, misalignment or damaged linkage. Electrical codes require a different route and do not automatically identify a failed component.
searchTerms: door will not open from outside
door will not open from inside

when.summary: Use when a door resists opening or closing, or a lock, trunk-release or entry function fails.

prepare.title: Arrange mechanical access
prepare.detail: Have a screwdriver for latch testing and the capability to remove the door trim and disconnect release cables using the applicable procedures.

prepare.title: Prepare for electrical diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use a suitable diagnostic scan tool and Ford diagnostic practices. Check previous repairs, connections, wiring and fuses. Confirm battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge greater than 70%. Use Rotunda Flex Probes when connecting test equipment to terminals.

steps.title: Choose the complaint-specific route
steps.body: Use the symptom and module-code charts to distinguish mechanical faults from power-lock, remote keyless entry, passive-entry and remote-start concerns. Record diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) by reporting module. Address circuit faults first; invalid-data entries may require diagnosing the sending controller.

steps.title: Test A: compare both handles
steps.body: Try opening the door from inside and outside. An exterior-only problem leads to Test B; an interior-only problem leads to Test C. If neither handle opens it normally, continue with Test A.

steps.title: Test A: separate latch friction from door loading
steps.body: With the door open, use a screwdriver to close the latch fully through two clicks, then operate the handles. If release is stiff, follow Door Latch Lubrication and repeat. Easy release afterward identifies inadequate lubrication; continued stiffness calls for a new latch.

steps.title: Test A: check striker and alignment
steps.body: If the latch released easily during the initial test, check the striker. Correct its adjustment if necessary. If it is correct, check door alignment: adjust a misaligned door, or lubricate the hinges when alignment is correct.

steps.title: Test B: isolate the exterior release
steps.body: For an exterior-only fault, disconnect its cable from the latch and observe handle and cable movement. If nothing binds or is broken, replace the latch. Otherwise, disconnect the cable from the handle reinforcement and operate the handle again. Correct operation now calls for a new cable; continued incorrect operation calls for a new reinforcement.

steps.title: Test C: inspect the interior release
steps.body: For an interior-only fault, remove the trim panel and reconnect the interior handle to its release cable. Observe operation. Repair binding or broken components and linkage; if these operate correctly, replace the latch.

steps.title: Separate trunk latch failure from electrical release
steps.body: For a trunk lid that will not latch, disconnect the latch electrical connector and test with a screwdriver. Failure to latch through two clicks calls for replacement. Successful latching directs diagnosis toward a short in the release circuit using the wiring diagrams.

watchFor.title: A handle that stays out
watchFor.body: A sticking exterior handle is a separate complaint: binding linkage, its return spring or the latch may be involved. Follow Test D.

watchFor.title: An absent complaint
watchFor.body: Do not follow a component-replacement verdict when the complaint required by that test is not currently present.

notes: Incorrect staged unlocking can require programming. Smart-unlock failure directs diagnosis to passive-key detection and the Passive Anti-Theft System.
Use the complete module charts for exact code routing; mirror, window, seat and illumination faults reported by door modules have their own diagnostic paths.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1490:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The lock-indicator circuit has a short-to-battery or open-circuit concern.
diagnostics.next: Use Test L for an inoperative indicator or Test M for one that stays on.

diagnostics.finding: A door module reports diagnostic trouble code U0010:00.
diagnostics.meaning: It previously lost network communication but is communicating to report this code.
diagnostics.next: Check connector and wiring continuity rather than assuming a current module failure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U2100:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Module configuration is incomplete.
diagnostics.next: Perform programmable module installation using as-built data, clear codes and repeat the self-test. Replace the affected module only if the code returns. Door-module U0300:4A follows this configuration route.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3000:04 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The reporting module indicates an internal failure.
diagnostics.next: The chart specifies replacement for the radio transceiver or driver door module. For the passenger door module, clear codes and repeat its self-test first; replace only if the code returns.

verification.title: Repeat the mechanical comparison
verification.body: After the prescribed repair, repeat opening and closing from both handles and confirm the original resistance is resolved.

verification.title: Record the electrical result
verification.body: Where directed, clear codes and repeat the self-test. Record returning codes and the affected function's behavior.

guides.title: Diagnose sticking door handles, latch noises and an inoperative manual door lock
guides.summary: Isolate handle springs, cables, rods, alignment and lubrication faults before deciding whether a door latch or lock cylinder needs replacement.
guides.introduction: The exterior handle releases the door latch through a rod; the interior handle uses a cable. Return springs bring the handles back after release. The driver-door key cylinder operates the lock through another rod. These mechanical connections let similar symptoms originate in different parts.
guides.why: Disconnecting the specified linkage separates handle or cylinder faults from latch resistance. For door noises, checking loose parts, striker position and alignment first prevents a sound elsewhere in the door being mistaken for latch failure.
searchTerms: interior door handle will not return

when.summary: When a door handle sticks, the door squeaks or rattles, or the mechanical key fails to lock and unlock the driver door.
notes: Confirm the complaint while it is present and check for previous repairs or visibly disconnected parts.

prepare.title: Plan the required access
prepare.detail: Be prepared to remove door trim, handles or the lock cylinder. Test D also requires window-regulator removal; use its linked removal and installation procedure.

prepare.title: Have the testing items ready
prepare.detail: Have the mechanical key, a screwdriver for the latch test, the specified latch-lubrication procedure, lock lubricant such as Motorcraft XL-1 and multi-purpose grease such as Motorcraft XL-5.

steps.title: Test D: isolate a sticking exterior handle
steps.body: Remove the window regulator, reinstall the exterior handle strap on its reinforcement and disconnect the handle actuating rod from the latch. Pull and release the handle. If it does not return closed, replace the reinforcement. If it returns, observe the handle and linkage while operating it: repair binding components; if none bind, the test directs a new latch.

steps.title: Test E: check the interior handle and cable
steps.body: Remove the interior handle and test its return action. Failure to return directs handle replacement. If it returns normally, remove and inspect the latch-release cable. Replace a damaged or binding cable; if the cable is sound, replace the latch.

steps.title: Test F: locate the source of door noise
steps.body: Remove the trim panel and repair any loose components inside the door. If none are loose, check striker adjustment, then door alignment. Correct an adjustment fault when found; follow the [door-alignment procedure](#/document/G1693219) where required.

steps.title: Test F: check the lubricated latch
steps.body: If striker adjustment and door alignment are correct, follow [Door Latch Lubrication](#/document/G1695899). Use a screwdriver to close the latch fully through two clicks, then operate it and listen. Persistent original noise directs latch replacement; noise eliminated by lubrication identifies insufficient lubrication.

steps.title: Test G: investigate a freely spinning key cylinder
steps.body: Turn the key toward lock and unlock. If the cylinder rotates freely without operating the lock, remove the trim and check the cylinder-to-latch rod connections. Correct a disconnected rod. If connected correctly, remove the cylinder and turn the key while holding its lever. Free rotation with the lever stationary directs cylinder replacement. Otherwise inspect the rod-to-lever connection: reconnect it if detached; if connected, replace the latch.

steps.title: Test G: try the lubrication branch
steps.body: If the initial test does not show free rotation without locking action, spray lock lubricant such as Motorcraft XL-1 into the cylinder opening for a couple of seconds and operate the key. If locking and unlocking return, apply multi-purpose grease such as Motorcraft XL-5 for a couple of seconds to provide lasting lubrication.

steps.title: Test G: isolate remaining binding
steps.body: If lubrication does not restore operation, remove the cylinder and test it with the key. Replace it if it still binds. If it turns freely, operate the lock linkage and inspect the rod and lever for binding, damage or disconnection. Repair those faults; if none exist, replace the latch. Complete the chosen repair through the applicable removal and installation procedure.

watchFor.title: Spring failure versus linkage drag
watchFor.body: Judge handle return only with the removal and disconnection conditions specified by the test.

watchFor.title: Two different free-rotation checks
watchFor.body: A key turning without unlocking first calls for linkage checks. Cylinder replacement follows the separate test with its lever held stationary.

notes: Use the dedicated latch-lubrication procedure for the latch; the named lock lubricants belong to the cylinder branch.

diagnostics.finding: All door locks are inoperative electrically.
diagnostics.meaning: The electrical fault path includes wiring, terminals, connectors and the body control module.
diagnostics.next: Continue with all-door-lock electrical diagnosis and Wiring Diagrams Cell 117; this observation alone does not establish module failure.

verification.title: Repeat the original operating check
verification.body: After completing installation, confirm the affected handle returns and releases the latch, the key locks and unlocks, or the original noise is absent, as applicable.

verification.title: Record what isolated the fault
verification.body: Record the failed spring, cable, linkage, lubrication or alignment check, the repair performed and the repeat-test result.

guides.title: Diagnose door lock indicators, trunk release and remote-key faults
guides.summary: Separate indicator, luggage-compartment release and remote-key faults using the appropriate circuit, key and module checks.
guides.introduction: The entry system accepts requests from door switches, passive entry and remote keyless entry (RKE). A door lock indicator depends on electrical supply, ground and latch feedback; the luggage-compartment latch needs a release command and a working output circuit. These tests distinguish a failed component from a missing electrical connection or an unrecognized key.
guides.why: Similar symptoms can have different causes. Memory-seat equipment changes the indicator supply path, while remote-key operation depends on programming, synchronization and communication. Testing these relationships prevents an apparently inactive component from being replaced unnecessarily.

when.summary: Use when an indicator, luggage-compartment release or remote-key fault is currently present.
notes: Identify whether memory seats are fitted before selecting an indicator supply-circuit branch.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge greater than 70%. Inspect previous repairs, wiring and connectors; diagnose relevant circuit trouble codes first.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical testing capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, wiring diagrams, Rotunda Flex Probes and fused jumper wires. Latch load testing requires a Rotunda Test Lamp (SGT27000) or 250–300mA incandescent test lamp. Never insert its probe directly into a connector.

prepare.title: Bring every customer key
prepare.detail: Inspect keys for damage and aftermarket replacements. Correct key types, backup-starting instructions and scan-tool programming capability are needed for the remote-key branch.

steps.title: Test L: investigate a dark lock indicator
steps.body: Confirm the locks work from their switches; otherwise use the electrical symptom chart first. Test locked-door feedback and disconnect the latch if the feedback is grounded: a ground that disappears points to the latch; one that remains points to wiring. Next check indicator supply and ground. Correct readings direct indicator-harness replacement. A deficient ground leads toward Body Control Module B (BCM-B). For missing supply, follow the body control module (BCM) branch without memory seats, or the driver/passenger door module branch with memory seats.

steps.title: Test M: investigate an indicator that stays on
steps.body: Check courtesy-lamp operation first; incorrect operation redirects diagnosis to interior lighting. Check unlocked-door feedback next. If feedback is missing, test its wire for continuity before condemning the latch. With feedback correct, disconnect the appropriate supply module and command locking with the remote. Continued illumination identifies a supply-circuit short to voltage; otherwise continue the applicable module connection checks.

steps.title: Test N: separate release-switch faults
steps.body: Inspect the release switches and check BCM fuse 16 (15A), then run the BCM self-test. Follow switch-input short codes through the isolation decisions below. Without those codes, unlock the doors and compare interior, exterior and remote release. If some controls work, follow the prescribed fused-jumper tests: operation across the switch connector points to the switch; operation only with a substitute ground points to its ground circuit. Otherwise check input-wire continuity.

steps.title: Test N: check the latch output under load
steps.body: If no release method works, verify the fuse before testing the disconnected latch circuit with the specified lamp. Watch while pressing and releasing the exterior switch: voltage is supplied only momentarily. Illumination across the latch supply and ground directs latch replacement. Illumination only with a separate ground identifies a ground-circuit fault. No illumination leads to output-wire continuity testing, then BCM checks.

steps.title: Test O: establish which remote functions fail
steps.body: Stop if the correct keys are unavailable. Check both keys for starting in the correctly oriented backup position in the floor console rear cup holder; a failed start redirects diagnosis to the passive anti-theft system (PATS). Check range in an open area away from large metal objects; poor range goes to Test Q. Compare every button on both keys, pressing luggage release twice. A partially working key goes to Test P.

steps.title: Follow the synchronization branch for an inactive key
steps.body: Read the BCM parameter identification (PID) TIC-NONE_OOS. On leads to battery-status testing; Off leads to resynchronization. For O7, place the suspect key in the backup position, switch ignition on, wait 10 seconds, switch off and press a key button within 30 seconds. If unsuccessful, O8 uses a button press on the working key followed by one on the suspect key within 30 seconds.

steps.title: Test batteries or programming when directed
steps.body: If RKE_BATT_LOW indicates a battery concern, test both CR2025 batteries. Unless both exceed 2.5 volts, replace both and seat them correctly without reprogramming. Preserve grease on the circuit-board battery terminals. When the decision path reaches O11, program and retest the suspect key; replace and program a new key only if that test still fails.

steps.title: Investigate complete failure from both keys
steps.body: Follow O12 with a network test of the BCM and radio transceiver module (RTM). Communication failure redirects to network diagnosis. If communication passes, check RTM trouble codes, then BCM codes. Follow the relevant code chart; if neither module reports codes, continue to Test V.

steps.title: Complete the module decision carefully
steps.body: At a module endpoint, inspect its connectors for corrosion, damaged terminals and pushed-out pins. Repair, reconnect securely and retest. If the fault remains, check applicable technical service bulletins before the directed replacement or guided routine. BCM endpoints require the vehicle identification number for that routine. If reconnection restores operation, correct the underlying terminal problem.

watchFor.title: A fault that disappears during testing
watchFor.body: Do not use a pinpoint-test replacement decision when its named concern is no longer present.

watchFor.title: An isolated remote feature
watchFor.body: A button complaint may involve the locks, trunk release, horn, turn signals or remote start, where fitted. Test P continues that distinction.

notes: Without memory seats, Test L uses B1490:11 to select short-circuit isolation; an absent code leads to supply continuity testing. With memory seats, test the relevant door-module supply for shorts and opens.
Any subsequent BCM replacement requires programmable module installation, programming at least 2 keys and the parameter reset procedure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1490:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test L investigates a grounded indicator supply.
diagnostics.next: Disconnect the left, then right indicator harness as directed, clearing and retesting after each. If the code persists, test supply wiring before the BCM endpoint.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1490:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The description covers short to battery or open; the listed trigger is a short to voltage.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test M to separate feedback, supply wiring and module faults.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1219:11 or C1017:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: B1219:11 concerns the interior release-switch input; C1017:11 concerns the exterior input. Both indicate a short to ground.
diagnostics.next: Disconnect the corresponding switch, clear codes and retest. A cleared code directs switch replacement; a remaining code requires input-circuit isolation.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B10AB:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The transmitter and BCM rolling counters are out of synchronization.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test O's synchronization decision; successful resynchronization establishes the cause.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1218:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM received an invalid transmitter identification code.
diagnostics.next: Compare programmed and last-received transmitter identification data, then follow the directed programming checks.

verification.title: Repeat the affected functions
verification.body: Recheck indicator behavior, release controls or both keys as applicable. Confirm the original complaint is absent after restoring test connections.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record initial and final codes, the decisive circuit or key test, and which controls or keys now operate correctly.

guides.title: Check remote-key functions, range, passive entry and factory remote start
guides.summary: Separate a key fault from weak batteries, radio interference, door-handle circuits and conditions preventing factory remote start.
guides.introduction: Remote keyless entry (RKE) sends button commands through the radio transceiver module (RTM) to the body control module (BCM). Passive entry also uses antennas inside the exterior door handles to detect a nearby key. These checks establish which part of that communication and operating path needs attention.
guides.why: A working key cannot operate a faulty latch or horn, and poor radio reception does not automatically mean a failed transmitter. Establishing the vehicle functions first makes later replacement decisions meaningful.
searchTerms: key fob will not lock doors
passive entry not working on one door

when.summary: A remote-key button, operating range, door passive entry or fitted factory remote-start feature is unreliable.
notes: Test R does not diagnose dealer-installed remote-start systems.
Replacement decisions require the complaint to be present during testing.

prepare.title: Gather keys and diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Range diagnosis requires at least two correct programmed keys. Have a scan tool supporting module self-tests and BCM output commands, a digital multimeter and Rotunda Flex Probes. Circuit diagnosis, connector repair and replacement-key programming require suitable workshop capability.

prepare.title: Establish sound test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging-system operation and battery state of charge above 70%. Inspect keys, batteries, handles, wiring and aftermarket entry equipment. Record relevant diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Follow each test's ignition state, connector disconnection and engine-specific terminal table.

steps.title: Prove the vehicle functions before judging a button
steps.body: Follow P1–P4 in order: door-switch lock/unlock, ignition-on BCM HORN_RELAY output command, hazard operation, then ignition-off luggage release with the doors unlocked. Failures lead respectively to Test H, horn diagnosis, hazard-lamp diagnosis or Test N. After these pass, P5 checks key lock/unlock; P6 checks luggage release with two button presses. Failure at either applicable key check calls for replacement and programming. A successful P6 confirms that release operation; stop this sequence there.

steps.title: Observe panic and fitted factory-start functions separately
steps.body: P7 observes whether the fitted panic/locator button produces flashing exterior lamps and a horn/chime response. P8 applies only to factory remote start: close the doors, hood and luggage lid, then from outside press lock followed by remote start twice, with each press within 3 seconds of the previous one. Record these observations separately; they alone do not authorize key replacement. Investigate an inoperative factory-start feature through Test R.

steps.title: Compare keys before diagnosing poor range
steps.body: Test Q begins by confirming the correct keys; stop if they are unavailable. Compare all keys in an open area away from large metal objects at approximately 30 m (98 ft.). If only some keys perform poorly, inspect their CR2025 batteries: both voltages above 2.5 volts direct replacement and programming of the suspect key; otherwise replace both batteries, seat them correctly and do not reprogram. If all keys perform poorly, check location and approach angles. Consistently poor range around the vehicle leads to RTM replacement; angle- or location-dependent loss can indicate environmental interference.

steps.title: Check factory-start permissions and related faults
steps.body: In R1–R5, enable remote start in the message center if disabled, then confirm the instrument-cluster gear display correctly identifies Park. An incorrect display needs instrumentation diagnosis. Perform the BCM self-test, followed by powertrain control module (PCM) key-on/engine-off and key-on/engine-running self-tests; follow the respective DTC charts for faults. With ignition off, test key luggage release, lock and unlock. All three failing leads to Test O; an individual failure leads to Test P.

steps.title: Establish the PCM wake-up result
steps.body: Only after R1–R5 pass, disconnect PCM connector B and, with ignition on, command BCM PCM_WKUP_CTRL. Use the engine-specific R6 terminal table. Above 11 volts leads to R8: ignition off, reconnect PCM B and repeat the closed-vehicle factory-start sequence. Success confirms operation; continued failure here directs replacement and programming of the key. A lower R6 result leads to R7: ignition off, disconnect the specified BCM connector and test wake-up continuity. Resistance below 3 ohms leads to R9; otherwise repair the circuit.

steps.title: Separate shared passive-entry faults from one-door faults
steps.body: Test S first verifies door-switch locking, then key-button locking; failures go to H or O respectively. Compare passive entry at both doors. If both fail, S4–S6 check the shared handle-ground circuit for a short to voltage, short to ground and an open. Repair a failed circuit; passing these checks leads to S16.

steps.title: Check the affected handle's supply and ground
steps.body: For one affected door, S7 checks voltage at the disconnected handle. Insufficient supply leads through supply-circuit short-to-ground and open checks; sound wiring leads to S16. With adequate supply, S10 checks ground continuity before testing the handle. Use the correct left- or right-door connector entries.

steps.title: Distinguish a handle fault from antenna wiring
steps.body: S11 measures the internal antenna on the component side: resistance outside 1–3 ohms calls for a new handle. If it passes, follow the handle procedure to transfer the opposite handle temporarily and reconnect the BCM. Restored operation identifies the suspect handle for replacement. Otherwise, S13–S15 check antenna wiring for voltage shorts, ground shorts and opens before proceeding to S16.

steps.title: Resolve connector faults before a BCM decision
steps.body: At R9 or S16, inspect all BCM connectors. Renew corroded terminals/connectors, clean module pins and replace damaged, bent or pushed-out pins as directed. Seat and latch connections, then retest. Address the underlying cause even if operation returns. If the complaint remains, follow any applicable technical service bulletin; otherwise continue through the vehicle identification number (VIN)-based BCM guided routine.

watchFor.title: Battery-terminal grease
watchFor.body: Do not remove grease from the battery terminals on the circuit board.

watchFor.title: Misleading electrical readings
watchFor.body: Use the specified probes and isolation sequence. Voltage present during resistance testing can invalidate readings; do not apply power or ground to module outputs unless directed.

notes: The passive key also serves the Passive Anti-Theft System (PATS). Weak key batteries do not erase its programmed identity.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B11C6:01 or B11CA:01 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detected an external-antenna circuit fault at the passenger or driver handle respectively.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test S; the code alone does not establish a failed handle.

diagnostics.finding: A handle circuit code B1381:11, B1381:15, B1382:11 or B1382:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: B1381 concerns the left handle and B1382 the right. The :11 codes indicate a short to ground; :15 indicates a short to battery or an open.
diagnostics.next: Use Test S to distinguish wiring, connections and handle faults.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1381:29 or B1382:29 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The left or right touch sensor respectively remained activated for more than 5 minutes.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the handle and continue the applicable passive-entry checks before selecting a replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Luggage-compartment passive entry fails and B10C7:01 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detected a fault at the keyless-entry rear antenna input; wiring, connections, antenna and BCM remain possible causes.
diagnostics.next: Continue with luggage-compartment passive-entry diagnosis. This observation does not establish an antenna replacement decision.

verification.title: Repeat the affected operation
verification.body: Retest the repaired feature under the same conditions. Confirm the relevant key, range, door-entry or factory-start response and explain correct operation when it passes.

verification.title: Record the result by feature
verification.body: Record keys tested, affected doors, engine branch, DTCs, measurements and final responses. Keep any unresolved feature separate from successful checks.

procedures.purpose: Remote-key checks through P6, separate P7/P8 observations, Test Q range diagnosis, Test R factory-start diagnosis and Test S door passive-entry diagnosis for the listed engines.

Scan-tool programming after an independently established replacement-key decision.
RTM removal and installation when the complete Q4 decision directs replacement.
Exterior-handle removal and installation for S12 substitution or confirmed replacement.
Horn diagnosis following failure of the P2 commanded-output check.
Hazard-lamp diagnosis following a failed P3 check.
Instrument-cluster gear-display diagnosis following an incorrect R2 Park indication.
BCM diagnostic follow-up where codes or completed connector checks require it.

applicability.equipment: Passive key system; factory remote start where fitted

guides.title: Diagnose U0208:00 communication faults and P1594/P1595 remote-start shutdowns
guides.summary: Use Tests X and Y to separate seat-module communication problems from remote-start shutdown faults before selecting further diagnosis or module replacement.
guides.introduction: These entry-system tests address two distinct electronic concerns. Test X investigates communication with the driver front seat module when a door module reports U0208:00. Test Y investigates remote-start shutdown codes. During remote starting, the body control module checks conditions such as closed doors and hood, PARK selection and powertrain status before allowing the engine to run for the selected duration.
guides.why: A stored communication code can reflect a temporary condition rather than a failed module. Network operation, voltage-related faults and replacement-module configuration therefore come before replacement decisions. Remote-start codes likewise require powertrain and body-module checks before the body control module is investigated further.
searchTerms: P1595 remote start not in park

when.summary: When U0208:00 accompanies an observable concern, or P1594/P1595 is recorded for remote-start operation.
notes: Use the branch matching the recorded code; these tests do not diagnose every door-lock or starting complaint.

prepare.title: Provide module-level diagnostic access
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of network tests, module self-tests and retrieving continuous-memory codes from all modules. Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge above 70%, and review previous repairs.

prepare.title: Prepare for the possible diagnostic handoff
prepare.detail: Have the vehicle identification number (VIN), applicable technical service information and access to the vehicle-specific BCM guided routine. Module replacement may require programming capability.

steps.title: Test X: confirm an active concern
steps.body: With ignition ON, verify an observable symptom accompanies U0208:00. If none is present, X1 ends with the system operating normally at that time; network traffic or an intermittent condition may explain the stored code. Do not use an inactive complaint to justify replacement.

steps.title: Establish seat-module communication and voltage status
steps.body: Run the network test. If the driver front seat module (DSM) fails, continue with Communications Network diagnosis. If it passes, run the DSM self-test. Voltage-related diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) go to Front Seats diagnosis before continuing.

steps.title: Recheck the reporting door module
steps.body: Clear codes and repeat the driver door module (DDM) or passenger door module (PDM) self-test. If U0208:00 does not return, X4 identifies normal operation at that time. If modules were recently replaced, consider incorrect or omitted programmable module installation (PMI) configuration before treating the code as hardware failure.

steps.title: Use the all-module result to select the replacement branch
steps.body: If U0208:00 persists, clear all DTCs, switch ignition OFF and then ON, wait 30 seconds and retrieve continuous-memory DTCs from every module. U0208 reported by other modules directs DSM replacement. If other modules do not report it, X5 directs replacement of the affected DDM or PDM using its installation procedure.

steps.title: Test Y: diagnose related faults first
steps.body: For P1594 or P1595, review the powertrain control module (PCM) self-test. Diagnose every other PCM code first. If none is present, switch ignition ON and run the body control module (BCM) self-test. Any BCM codes go to the BCM DTC chart in the entry-system diagnostic article.

steps.title: Inspect BCM connections and follow the persistent-fault handoff
steps.body: If Y2 finds no BCM codes, disconnect and inspect its connectors. Replace corroded connectors or terminals and clean module pins; replace damaged, bent or pushed-out terminals as required. Reconnect securely and operate the system. If the concern remains, check applicable technical service bulletins and follow any relevant bulletin. Otherwise, continue through the VIN-dependent BCM guided routine.

watchFor.title: A fault that disappears after reconnection
watchFor.body: Address the underlying terminal or connector defect even when operation returns. Reseating a connection alone does not explain why it failed.

watchFor.title: BCM replacement has programming consequences
watchFor.body: If subsequent diagnosis requires BCM replacement, PMI, programming at least 2 keys and the parameter reset procedure are required.

notes: Test Y's persistent-fault endpoint is the VIN-dependent guided routine; it is not an automatic instruction to replace the BCM.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0208:00 is recorded in a door module.
diagnostics.meaning: Communication with the DSM requires investigation; the code alone does not identify the defective module.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test X's symptom, network, voltage and all-module rechecks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1594 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detected remote start active for more than 30 minutes continuously.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test Y, diagnosing other PCM codes before BCM testing.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1595 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detected remote start active while the transmission was not in PARK.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test Y's powertrain and BCM checks; do not infer a failed transmission or BCM from this code alone.

verification.title: Confirm the branch result
verification.body: For Test X, retain the repeated door-module self-test and prescribed all-module results. For Test Y, operate the system after connector repairs and establish whether the concern remains.

verification.title: Record the decisive evidence
verification.body: Record the observable symptom, modules reporting U0208, voltage-related codes and PCM/BCM self-test results. Identify any required network, seat-system or VIN-guided follow-up.

procedures.purpose: Test X for U0208:00 and Test Y for P1594/P1595, including the BCM DTC-chart handoff.

Communications Network diagnosis when the DSM fails the network test.
Front Seats diagnosis for DSM voltage-related DTCs.
DSM removal and installation when Test X's all-module result directs replacement.
DDM removal and installation when Test X identifies the reporting driver door module.
PDM removal and installation when Test X identifies the reporting passenger door module.
BCM replacement prerequisites for passive anti-theft programming and parameter reset.

applicability.equipment: Driver front seat module for Test X; remote start for Test Y

guides.title: Lubricate the door latch
guides.summary: Apply the specified grease spray to the closed latch, then operate the door to distribute it and remove the excess.
guides.introduction: The door latch holds the door closed and releases when the handle is operated. Lubricating it helps its internal moving surfaces work smoothly. The vehicle also has electrical lock and entry functions, but this procedure is a mechanical lubrication service; it does not establish the cause of an electrical locking or entry complaint.
guides.why: The latch is placed in its fully closed position while the door remains open so lubricant can be applied through the intended opening. Operating the handle and door afterward distributes the grease inside. More grease is not better: excessive lubricant can damage the internal lock motor.
searchTerms: door latch does not release smoothly

when.summary: When a door latch requires lubrication during service.
notes: No routine lubrication interval is specified.

prepare.title: Use the specified lubricant
prepare.detail: Have Motorcraft Multi-Purpose Grease Spray XL-5-A, specification ESB-M1C93-B.

prepare.title: Prepare the latch and cleanup tools
prepare.detail: Have a flat-bladed screwdriver to operate the exposed latch and a cloth to wipe away excess grease.

steps.title: Close the latch with the door open
steps.body: Open the door. Use the flat-bladed screwdriver to move the latch fully closed through 2 clicks. The door itself stays open for the lubricant application.

steps.title: Apply a controlled amount
steps.body: Spray the specified grease into the latch opening for approximately 5 seconds. Use the opening shown in the [lubrication procedure](#/document/G1695899) and avoid excessive application.

steps.title: Release and exercise the latch
steps.body: Use the exterior door handle to reopen the latch. Confirm it has released before moving the door shut, then open and close the door several times to circulate the lubricant.

steps.title: Remove the surplus
steps.body: Open the door again and wipe off excess grease. This completes the distribution and cleanup sequence without leaving unnecessary lubricant around the opening.

watchFor.title: Excess grease
watchFor.body: Do not continue spraying to compensate for a persistent complaint; over-lubrication can damage the internal lock motor.

watchFor.title: Latch remains closed
watchFor.body: If the exterior handle has not reopened the latch, do not attempt to shut the door against it.

notes: Exterior handles may release mechanically or electronically; use the fitted exterior handle to reopen the latch.
The typical left front door illustration represents a similar process for the other door.

verification.title: Confirm the operating sequence
verification.body: Confirm the exterior handle reopened the latch and the door was opened and closed several times to distribute the grease.

verification.title: Confirm cleanup
verification.body: Check that excess grease has been wiped away with the door open.

procedures.purpose: Complete latch positioning, specified lubricant application, operation and cleanup.

guides.title: Change staged unlocking with the remote transmitter
guides.summary: Enable or disable staged unlocking with a simultaneous 4-second hold of the remote’s lock and unlock buttons, then watch for two turn-signal flashes.
guides.introduction: Your Mustang’s remote has a small party trick: hold two buttons together and change its unlocking preference. I’ll walk you through the command and its confirmation so an enthusiastic second attempt doesn’t undo the first. No trim wrestling required.
guides.why: The power-lock system responds to requests from the door switches, passive entry system and Remote Keyless Entry (RKE) transmitter—the key remote. This procedure uses that remote to switch staged unlocking on or off. It changes a preference rather than repairing a lock. The [entry-system overview](#/document/G1695896) explains the different ways the car accepts locking and unlocking requests.
searchTerms: remote lock unlock buttons four seconds

when.summary: Use this procedure when you want to change the staged-unlocking preference on a 2015 Mustang with a 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
notes: The command switches the existing setting to its opposite. It is not a separate enable command and disable command.
Use this as a preference adjustment, not as a test for a faulty transmitter or door lock.

prepare.title: Make the vehicle ready
prepare.detail: Park the vehicle and switch the ignition OFF. Keep the remote with you so another person cannot use it to start the vehicle during the work. Review the applicable [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189). If remote start is fitted, disable it through the central display at Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around the vehicle, then return the ignition to OFF for programming.

prepare.title: Identify the controls and your preferred result
prepare.detail: Have the vehicle’s RKE transmitter ready, identify its lock and unlock buttons, and position yourself where you can observe the turn signals. Note the present door-unlock behavior during ordinary use. This procedure does not define the door-by-door response for each unlock press or provide a separate readout of the enabled/disabled state; use the resulting behavior to judge your preference.

prepare.title: Keep access simple
prepare.detail: The programming command is performed entirely with the transmitter. No component removal, unplugging, lifting, replacement parts or tightening operations are involved.

steps.title: Check that the ignition is OFF
steps.body: Before touching the transmitter buttons, confirm the ignition is OFF. Leave it OFF throughout the programming command.

steps.title: Hold lock and unlock together for 4 seconds
steps.body: Press the RKE transmitter’s lock and unlock buttons simultaneously. Keep both buttons pressed together for 4 seconds, then release them. The complete command is also described in [Staged Unlock Programming](#/document/G1672844).

steps.title: Watch for two turn-signal flashes
steps.body: Observe the turn signals for two flashes. That acknowledgement means the unlocking mode has changed. Once you see it, stop pressing the buttons—the remote needs no encore.

steps.title: Check your preference and toggle again only if needed
steps.body:
Use the remote’s unlock function normally and observe the resulting door-unlock behavior. This is a completion check of your preference, not a component diagnostic test.

If you want the opposite setting, keep the ignition OFF and repeat the simultaneous lock-and-unlock hold for 4 seconds. Look for two turn-signal flashes again, then check the resulting behavior. Each acknowledged command changes the setting again.

watchFor.title: A second command reverses the change
watchFor.body: Do not repeat the button hold automatically after a successful acknowledgement. Another successful command switches the setting back.

watchFor.title: Two flashes confirm a change
watchFor.body: The same acknowledgement accompanies either direction of the toggle. It does not identify the resulting setting as enabled or disabled.

notes: Passive entry and the remote transmitter are different ways to request entry-system operation. Perform this programming command with the transmitter’s lock and unlock buttons.

diagnostics.finding: The turn signals flash twice after the simultaneous 4-second hold.
diagnostics.meaning: The vehicle has acknowledged a mode change.
diagnostics.next: Check the resulting door-unlock behavior during normal remote operation. Keep the setting if it matches your preference.

diagnostics.finding: The acknowledged change produces the opposite behavior from the one you want.
diagnostics.meaning: The toggle worked, but you prefer the other setting.
diagnostics.next: With the ignition OFF, repeat the simultaneous lock-and-unlock hold for 4 seconds once. Observe the two-flash acknowledgement and check the behavior again.

diagnostics.finding: You do not observe the two-flash acknowledgement.
diagnostics.meaning: A successful change has not been confirmed. This alone does not identify a defective component.
diagnostics.next: Check the resulting unlock behavior before sending another command, since you may have missed the flashes. If another attempt is needed, confirm ignition OFF and hold both buttons simultaneously for the full 4 seconds. If acknowledgement remains absent, stop treating this preference-setting procedure as a fault test; transmitter and lock diagnosis require a separate procedure.

verification.title: Confirm the acknowledgement and the preferred behavior
verification.body: Finish with an observed two-flash acknowledgement and a normal-use check that the resulting unlocking behavior suits your preference. Note the behavior you selected so a later adjustment starts with a known preference.

procedures.purpose: Provides the ignition-OFF requirement, simultaneous 4-second button hold, two-flash acknowledgement and repeat-to-toggle instruction.
Provides applicable startup-prevention precautions and the remote-start disabling path.
Explains the power-lock system’s request sources and distinguishes remote-transmitter operation from passive entry.

applicability.equipment: Power door locks and Remote Keyless Entry (RKE) transmitter; remote start, if equipped.

stepGroups.title: Establish the ignition state
stepGroups.summary: Confirm ignition OFF before programming.

stepGroups.title: Change the setting
stepGroups.summary: Send the button command and observe its acknowledgement.

stepGroups.title: Confirm your preference
stepGroups.summary: Check normal unlocking behavior and change back only if desired.

guides.title: Replace the door lock control switch
guides.summary: Remove the front door trim panel, release the lock switch's retaining clips and restore the panel's electrical and latch connections.
guides.introduction: The door lock control switch lets an occupant request powered locking or unlocking. It is one of several ways to request that action: passive entry and the remote keyless entry transmitter can also operate the locks. This job changes the switch in the door trim, rather than the door latch. Most of the work lies in removing and reinstalling the trim panel carefully.
guides.why: The panel is secured by bolts, retainers and clips, then remains connected by wiring where fitted and the latch cable. Following the release sequence gives access to the switch without treating the panel as a loose cover. The switch itself is clip-retained, so its clips must be released before removal.

when.summary: When the door lock control switch has been identified for replacement.
notes: An unanswered lock request alone does not establish that the switch is defective.
The switch procedure shows left-hand drive and the left side; right-hand drive and the opposite side are similar.

prepare.title: Prepare for trim removal
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the panel fasteners and the ability to release trim retainers and switch clips carefully.

prepare.title: Include the window-switch prerequisite
prepare.detail: Follow the front door trim procedure, including its front door window-control-switch removal requirement.

steps.title: Remove the panel fasteners
steps.body: Remove the cover and upper trim-panel bolt, the front door window control switch, the center bolt and the lower retainers in the trim procedure's order.

steps.title: Release and lift off the trim
steps.body: Release the clips and pin-type retainers progressively at the rear upper, rear/lower and front portions. Lift the panel up and out, disconnect electrical connectors where equipped, and release the latch cable.

steps.title: Exchange the lock switch
steps.body: With the panel removed, release the door lock control switch's retaining clips and remove the switch. Install the replacement by reversing those actions so the clips retain it in the panel.

steps.title: Restore the door trim
steps.body: Transfer panel parts as necessary and reverse the trim-removal sequence, reconnecting the latch cable and fitted electrical connectors. Observe the separate tightening specifications for the upper and center bolts and the lower retainers.

watchFor.title: Connections still attached
watchFor.body: Do not pull the released panel away while its latch cable or fitted electrical connectors remain attached.

watchFor.title: Unreleased switch clips
watchFor.body: Release the retaining clips before withdrawing the switch; pulling against them can damage its mounting.

notes: The illustration shows panel removal and its connections; use the switch procedure for the switch's clip-release step.

verification.title: Confirm switch retention
verification.body: Check that the replacement switch is held by its retaining clips.

verification.title: Confirm panel reassembly
verification.body: Verify the latch cable and applicable connectors are reattached and the trim clips, retainers and fasteners are restored.

procedures.purpose: Door lock control switch clip release, removal and installation, with side and steering-position applicability notes.
Required front door trim removal and installation, including fasteners, retainers, electrical connections and latch cable.

guides.title: Remove and replace the driver-door lock cylinder
guides.summary: Remove the driver-door lock cylinder and handle-cover assembly, separate the cylinder, then reinstall with eight full release-screw turns during removal and a final tightening torque of 62 lb.in (7 Nm).
guides.introduction: The driver-door lock cylinder is the Mustang’s old-fashioned bouncer: no batteries, just a key and a firm opinion about access. It provides a mechanical way to lock the driver’s door alongside the power-lock functions. I’ll walk you through reaching its release screw, taking the cylinder and cover out together, and putting them back securely. The small catch is counting screw turns—the handle releases before the mechanism reaches the position needed for reassembly. Apparently, even a door lock enjoys unfinished business.
guides.why: The cylinder fits into the cover at the rear end of the exterior door handle. Removing the cylinder-and-cover assembly lets you separate the cylinder for replacement. The release screw needs eight full revolutions during removal, even though the handle releases earlier, to leave the retaining mechanism ready for installation.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang driver door lock cylinder replacement
door handle lock cylinder cover removal
door lock release screw eight turns

when.summary: For removal or replacement of the driver-door lock cylinder on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
notes: Use this procedure when the mechanical cylinder itself requires removal. A power-lock or passive-entry complaint alone does not establish that the cylinder needs replacing.
The illustrated vehicle is left-hand drive; the right-hand-drive procedure is similar.

prepare.title: Arrange the driver and torque tool
prepare.detail: Have a driver matching the release screw’s illustrated star-shaped recess and a torque tool capable of 62 lb.in (7 Nm). Keep the access grommet and handle-cover components together as they come off.

prepare.title: Have the cylinder and key ready
prepare.detail: If replacing the cylinder, have the correct replacement for the vehicle and the key intended to operate it. This job covers removal and installation of the complete cylinder. Key coding and internal cylinder repair require separate instructions.

prepare.title: Identify the access point
prepare.detail: Open the driver’s door to reach its trailing, latch-side edge. Locate the round access grommet approximately level with the exterior handle. The release screw is reached through that opening. See the [door lock cylinder procedure](#/document/G1695901).

steps.title: Remove the door-edge access grommet
steps.body: With the driver’s door open, remove the round grommet from the trailing edge of the door, beside the exterior handle area. Set it aside for reinstallation. Identify the release screw through the exposed opening before engaging the driver.

steps.title: Turn the release screw counterclockwise through eight full revolutions
steps.body:
Looking directly at the screw head through the door-edge access opening, turn the release screw counterclockwise, following the illustrated release arrow. Count eight complete revolutions.

The handle releases at approximately 6 to 6.5 turns. Continue to the full eight turns: that extra travel is required for installation. I’d count deliberately here; the first movement of the handle is a milestone, not permission to abandon arithmetic.

steps.title: Withdraw the cylinder and handle-cover assembly
steps.body:
After completing all eight release-screw turns, withdraw the lock cylinder and its door-handle cover together from the front door. The illustration shows the assembly moving outward, away from the exterior door surface, at the end of the handle nearest the door’s trailing edge.

Keep the cylinder and cover together during this stage. Separating the cylinder comes next.

steps.title: Separate the cylinder from its cover
steps.body:
With the assembly removed, withdraw the door lock cylinder from the handle cover. In the illustrated left-hand-drive view, the cylinder-removal arrow points left, toward the main handle portion.

Keep the cover for reuse when replacing only the cylinder. Remove the complete cylinder from the cover without dismantling its internal key mechanism.

steps.title: Fit the cylinder into the handle cover
steps.body: Insert the retained or replacement cylinder into the handle cover, reversing its removal direction. Restore the cylinder’s position in the cover before returning the assembly to the door. Check that the two parts are seated together and ready to install as one assembly.

steps.title: Install the assembly and tighten the release screw
steps.body:
Return the cylinder-and-cover assembly to its original opening at the rear end of the exterior handle, reversing the withdrawal movement. Seat the assembly in the door.

Looking directly at the release-screw head through the door-edge opening, turn it clockwise to secure the assembly. Tighten the release screw to 62 lb.in (7 Nm), using the appropriate scale on your torque tool.

steps.title: Restore the access grommet and check the completed work
steps.body:
Check that the cylinder and cover are secured and that the cover sits in its original position against the handle and door. Refit the round grommet into the door-edge access opening.

As completion checks, confirm that the mechanical key operates the driver-door locking function and that the exterior handle still operates normally. These checks confirm the result of reassembly; they do not diagnose the power-lock or passive-entry system.

watchFor.title: Early release does not mean the screw has travelled far enough
watchFor.body: Release at approximately 6 to 6.5 turns is expected. Continue counterclockwise to eight complete revolutions before withdrawing the cylinder-and-cover assembly.

watchFor.title: Keep the two removal stages distinct
watchFor.body: Remove the cylinder and handle cover from the door together first. Separate the cylinder from the cover after that assembly is out.

watchFor.title: Read the torque units carefully
watchFor.body: Tighten the release screw to 62 lb.in (7 Nm). Confirm that the tool is set to the correct units before tightening.

notes: Power locking responds to requests from the door lock switch, passive entry or the remote keyless-entry transmitter. The mechanical driver-door cylinder provides a separate key-operated locking route. The [entry-system overview](#/document/G1695896) explains those functions.
Installation reverses removal: cylinder into cover, assembly into door, release screw secured, then access grommet refitted.

diagnostics.finding: The handle releases after approximately 6 to 6.5 release-screw turns.
diagnostics.meaning: The assembly has reached its initial release point, but the screw has not completed the travel required for installation.
diagnostics.next: Continue counterclockwise until the total reaches eight complete revolutions, then withdraw the cylinder-and-cover assembly.

diagnostics.finding: The original complaint concerns power locking or passive entry.
diagnostics.meaning: Those functions have their own request paths. Their failure alone does not identify a defective mechanical lock cylinder.
diagnostics.next: Establish whether the mechanical cylinder requires service before replacing it. Use the [entry-system overview](#/document/G1695896) to distinguish the functions. Electrical fault testing requires a separate diagnostic procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The refitted assembly is insecure, or the key or handle does not operate normally.
diagnostics.meaning: The installation has not passed its completion checks. That result does not, by itself, identify a failed replacement cylinder.
diagnostics.next: Recheck the cylinder’s seating in the cover, the assembly’s seating in the door and the release-screw tightening. If removal is needed again, repeat the full eight-turn release sequence. Do not force the key or handle.

verification.title: Confirm retention and finish
verification.body: Confirm the cylinder and handle cover are secured in their original positions, the release screw is tightened to 62 lb.in (7 Nm), and the door-edge grommet is refitted.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical operation
verification.body: Check the mechanical key’s driver-door locking action and normal exterior-handle operation after reassembly. Resolve any binding or insecure fit before considering the job complete.

procedures.purpose: Cylinder and handle-cover removal, eight-turn release-screw travel, cylinder separation and reverse-order installation with the specified tightening torque.
Explain the mechanical cylinder’s role alongside power locking, remote keyless entry and passive entry.

applicability.equipment: Driver-door mechanical key lock cylinder; left-hand-drive and right-hand-drive vehicles.

stepGroups.title: Access and release
stepGroups.summary: Expose the door-edge screw and complete its required eight-turn travel.

stepGroups.title: Remove the cylinder
stepGroups.summary: Withdraw the cover assembly, then separate the cylinder.

stepGroups.title: Reassemble and verify
stepGroups.summary: Refit the cylinder and cover, tighten the screw, restore the grommet and check operation.

guides.title: Replace the Exterior Front Door Handle Reinforcement
guides.summary: Remove the front door latch assembly to renew the exterior handle reinforcement and restore its cable connection.
guides.introduction: The exterior front door handle reinforcement supports the outside handle mechanism and its connection to the latch. Replacing it involves working inside the door, where the glass, glass run and window regulator restrict access. The reinforcement procedure therefore begins with latch removal, making the access work a substantial part of this repair.
guides.why: The latch and reinforcement remain connected to operating cables during removal. Following the access sequence lets you withdraw the assembly without treating those connections as loose hardware. The cable-release screw also has a specific action: tightening it releases cable tension. Understanding that action prevents an assumption that every removal operation starts by loosening a screw.

when.summary: When the exterior front door handle reinforcement requires replacement.
notes: The left-hand door is illustrated; the right-hand side follows a similar procedure.
The reinforcement-separation step is specified only when installing a new component.

prepare.title: Plan for the door-access work
prepare.detail: Be equipped to remove the front door glass, exterior handle and aft glass run, and to position the window regulator aside using their referenced procedures.

prepare.title: Have the latch instructions available
prepare.detail: Use the complete latch procedure for fastener locations, cable routing and reassembly details. Have suitable fastener tools and a torque tool for the latch bolts.

steps.title: Create access inside the door
steps.body: Follow [Front Door Latch](#/document/G1695904): remove the front door window glass, exterior handle and aft glass run. Remove the regulator retainers and position its rear portion aside to expose the latch and reinforcement.

steps.title: Release and withdraw the latch assembly
steps.body: Remove the exterior handle reinforcement screw and the latch bolts, then disconnect the electrical connector. Route the interior handle cable through the door as directed while removing the latch assembly. Keep track of its route for installation.

steps.title: Separate the reinforcement for replacement
steps.body: Follow the new-component branch in the [reinforcement procedure](#/document/G1695903) and its latch instructions. Tighten the cable-release screw to release tension, then detach and position the cable aside so the reinforcement can be removed.

steps.title: Install the replacement and return the latch
steps.body: Reverse the separation and removal operations, restoring the cable attachment and route. Reconnect the latch electrical connector and install the reinforcement screw and latch bolts. Tighten the latch bolts to 71 lb.in (8 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the access components
steps.body: Return the regulator and its retainers, then reinstall the glass run, exterior handle and window glass through their respective procedures. Completing these operations restores the parts moved to reach the reinforcement.

watchFor.title: Cable tension remains
watchFor.body: Use the specified screw action to release tension before detaching the reinforcement cable.

watchFor.title: Unnecessary component separation
watchFor.body: Observe the latch procedure's new-component-only notes when deciding which additional cable and rod connections to separate.

notes: This is a mechanical reinforcement replacement. The procedure does not establish the cause of a power-lock or passive-entry complaint.

verification.title: Confirm the internal connections
verification.body: Confirm the reinforcement cable is reattached, the interior handle cable follows its installation route, and the latch connector and fasteners are restored.

verification.title: Confirm access work is complete
verification.body: Verify that the regulator retainers, glass run, exterior handle and window glass have all been reinstalled through their component procedures.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the exterior front door handle reinforcement after latch removal; includes the new-component-only separation condition.
Provide door-access, latch removal, cable-release and installation details needed to reach and replace the reinforcement.

guides.title: Remove and refit an exterior front door handle
guides.summary: Release the exterior handle through its internal screw mechanism, protect its electrical connection and complete the full engagement sequence on installation.
guides.introduction: The exterior handle operates the door from outside, beside the lock-cylinder and cover assembly. It also has an electrical connector reached from inside the door. Removal therefore begins with interior access, even though the part being changed is outside. This guide covers removing and refitting the handle and its adjoining cover assembly.
guides.why: The handle releases before the release screw has completed the travel required for installation. Stopping at the first movement leaves the mechanism short of its specified position. The wiring presents a separate risk: pulling the handle too far outward before disconnecting it can damage the harness.

when.summary: When the exterior front door handle needs replacement or removal for a door repair.
notes: The illustrated left-hand-drive, left-side procedure is similar for right-hand-drive vehicles and the right side.

prepare.title: Plan access from inside the door
prepare.detail: Have the Front Door Trim Panel procedure available. The trim panel and lower watershield must be removed so the handle connector can be reached from inside.

prepare.title: Prepare for controlled screw travel
prepare.detail: Use a suitable driver for the release screw and torque equipment capable of its specified 62 lb.in (7 Nm) final tightening.

steps.title: Expose the release mechanism and connector
steps.body: Remove the [front door trim panel](#/document/G1692600), then the lower watershield and grommet. This establishes the internal access needed to release the assembly and disconnect its wiring.

steps.title: Release the lock-cylinder and cover assembly
steps.body: Hold the front door handle open and turn the release screw 8 turns. Although the handle releases around 6 to 6.5 turns, continue through all 8. Remove the lock-cylinder and door handle cover assembly.

steps.title: Disconnect and exchange the handle
steps.body: Disconnect the handle connector from inside the door before pulling the handle out too far, then remove the handle. For installation, connect the wiring from inside the door and partially insert the handle into the opening.

steps.title: Engage the mechanism and restore the door
steps.body: Install the lock-cylinder and cover assembly and release the handle. Apply light pressure while turning the screw 8 turns: engagement occurs around 6 to 6.5 turns, but complete all 8 before tightening to 62 lb.in (7 Nm). Refit the grommet, lower watershield and trim panel using the [complete handle procedure](#/document/G1695902).

watchFor.title: Early release or engagement
watchFor.body: Movement before the eighth turn is expected; it is not the stopping point.

watchFor.title: Harness tension
watchFor.body: Keep outward handle movement limited until the connector has been disconnected from inside the door.

notes: The release screw's final torque follows the full installation travel; torque alone does not replace the turn-count requirement.

verification.title: Confirm completed retention
verification.body: Confirm the full installation turn count, handle engagement and final release-screw torque.

verification.title: Confirm restored access parts
verification.body: Confirm the handle connector is attached and the grommet, lower watershield and trim panel have been reinstalled.

procedures.purpose: Exterior front door handle removal and installation, connector protection and release-screw travel and torque.
Front door trim panel removal and installation for internal handle access.

guides.title: Remove and replace a front door latch
guides.summary: Gain access through the door's glass and handle components, remove the latch assembly and transfer its connections when installing a new latch.
guides.introduction: The front door latch holds the door closed and works with the handle cables, linkage and electrical locking connection. Lock or unlock requests can come from the door controls, passive entry or the remote keyless entry transmitter. Replacing the latch requires working around the window mechanism and restoring all of these mechanical and electrical connections.
guides.why: The latch sits in a crowded part of the door. Removing the glass, exterior handle and aft glass run creates access, while moving the rear of the regulator clears the removal path. The interior handle cable must be routed through the door as the assembly comes out. Additional separation work is required only when fitting a new component.
searchTerms: door handle will not release door

when.summary: When diagnosis identifies a latch fault, or the latch assembly must be removed for door service.
notes: The procedure illustrates the left-hand door; the right-hand door is similar.
An unsuccessful lock or release request alone does not identify which latch, linkage or control component is responsible.

prepare.title: Plan the prerequisite access work
prepare.detail: Be equipped to remove and reinstall the front door window glass, exterior handle and aft glass run through their linked procedures. This job requires capability with glass handling and the window regulator as well as latch fasteners.

prepare.title: Identify the replacement branch
prepare.detail: Establish whether the existing assembly will be refitted or a new latch installed. Cable, rod and reinforcement separation is conditional on installing a new component.

steps.title: Remove the access components
steps.body: Remove the [front door window glass](#/document/G1695937), then the [exterior front door handle](#/document/G1695902), followed by the aft glass run using [Front Door Glass Run and Bracket](#/document/G1695949). Complete each linked procedure's removal requirements.

steps.title: Move the regulator aside
steps.body: Remove the regulator retainers and position its rear portion aside. Remove the exterior-handle reinforcement screw to continue freeing the latch assembly.

steps.title: Release the latch mounting
steps.body: Remove the front door latch bolts and disconnect the electrical connector. The latch-bolt installation torque is 71 lb.in (8 Nm); retain that distinction from the other screws removed during access.

steps.title: Withdraw the assembly with its cable
steps.body: Route the interior front door handle cable through the door, then remove the latch assembly. Follow the illustrated routing so the cable can accompany the assembly through the opening.

steps.title: Separate parts only for a new component
steps.body: If installing a new latch, remove its interior-handle cable. Remove the exterior-handle reinforcement using the specified sequence: tighten the screw to release cable tension, then detach and position the cable aside. Remove the remaining attachment screws, detach and position aside the cable at the latch, then detach the rod and separate the latch.

steps.title: Reassemble in reverse order
steps.body: Reverse [the complete latch procedure](#/document/G1695904), including the conditional transfers where applicable. Route the interior cable back through the door, reconnect the wiring and tighten the latch bolts to specification. Restore the reinforcement and regulator, then reinstall the glass run, exterior handle and glass through their respective procedures.

watchFor.title: Cable-tension screw direction
watchFor.body: During the new-component branch, the specified screw is tightened to release cable tension. Follow that action rather than assuming every removal operation requires loosening.

watchFor.title: Incomplete linkage restoration
watchFor.body: A new latch requires reconnection of the transferred cables and rod as well as its electrical connector.

notes: Keep the regulator-positioning work distinct from the conditional latch disassembly; the regulator is moved aside during normal latch access.

verification.title: Confirm door functions
verification.body: Confirm the restored handles release the latch and the fitted lock/unlock controls operate it. These are the functions served by the reconnected cables, linkage and electrical connection.

verification.title: Record assembly completion
verification.body: Record latch-bolt tightening, restoration of the cable and rod connections, and completion of the prerequisite glass, handle and glass-run installation procedures.

procedures.purpose: Front door latch removal and installation, including new-component-only cable, rod and reinforcement separation.
Prerequisite front door window-glass removal and subsequent installation.
Prerequisite exterior front door handle removal and subsequent installation.
Aft front door glass-run access and restoration using the glass-run and bracket procedure.

guides.title: Replace the hood latch release cable
guides.summary: Remove the cabin release and routed cable, then restore the latch connection, retaining clips and cowl grommet during installation.
guides.introduction: The hood release cable carries the driver's pull from the interior release to the hood latch. Its route passes through the cowl and continues around the engine compartment to the latch. Replacement therefore involves both interior trim and the radiator sight shield, along with the clips and bracket that locate the cable.
guides.why: The cable ends transmit the pull, while the routing clips and bracket hold the assembly in its intended position. Restoring only the end connections leaves the installation incomplete. The cowl grommet also needs to return to its opening when the new cable is routed through.

when.summary: When the hood latch release cable requires replacement or removal for related repair.
notes: The procedure shows left-hand drive; right-hand drive is similar.
Audio digital signal processing module removal applies only when that module is fitted.

prepare.title: Prepare trim-release tools
prepare.detail: Have an interior trim remover and a 10 mm, 1/4 inch drive socket. The socket is used to release the hood-release-handle clips, rather than as an instruction to remove a fastener.

prepare.title: Plan access at both ends
prepare.detail: Allow access to the driver scuff plate, release handle, cowl trim and radiator sight shield. If fitted, use the Audio Digital Signal Processing (DSP) Module procedure for its removal and refitting.

steps.title: Expose the interior release
steps.body: Remove the DSP module if fitted, then remove the driver door scuff plate with the trim remover. Remove the handle access cover, release the handle clips with the specified socket and remove the handle. Release the clips and remove the left-hand cowl trim panel in the illustrated arrangement.

steps.title: Detach the release assembly
steps.body: Disconnect the cable from the hood latch release, remove the release bolts and remove the release assembly. Free the cable's routing clips and pass the cable through the cowl as directed in the [complete cable procedure](#/document/G1695906).

steps.title: Free the engine-compartment route
steps.body: Remove the radiator sight-shield retainers and shield. Remove the cable grommet, release the routing clips and position the cable aside. Release it from the routing bracket, disconnect its latch-end connection and remove the cable.

steps.title: Install in reverse order
steps.body: Reconnect the latch end and restore the routing bracket, cable clips and grommet as removal is reversed. Route the cable through the cowl, reinstall and reconnect the interior release assembly, then restore the handle, trim, sight shield and any removed DSP module.

watchFor.title: Clips and grommet left out
watchFor.body: Treat the routing attachments as part of the repair. Cable-end engagement does not replace the need to reinstall the bracket, clips and grommet.

watchFor.title: Interior handle clips
watchFor.body: Use the specified clip-release method before removing the handle instead of forcing it away from its mounting.

notes: The engine-compartment illustration identifies the cable route, grommet and clips; use the full procedure for the cabin-side sequence.

verification.title: Confirm the restored cable path
verification.body: Check that both cable ends are connected, the routing bracket and clips are restored, and the cowl grommet is seated.

verification.title: Confirm access components are refitted
verification.body: Check the release assembly, handle and access cover, cowl trim, scuff plate, radiator sight shield and any removed DSP module against the reverse-removal sequence.

procedures.purpose: Remove and reinstall the complete hood latch release cable and its interior and engine-compartment attachments.
Remove and reinstall the audio DSP module where fitted on vehicles with SYNC 2 or SYNC 3.

guides.title: Replace the interior hood-release handle
guides.summary: Remove and refit the interior hood-release handle on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine, using a 10 mm, 1/4-inch-drive socket to release its retaining clips.
guides.introduction: The hood-release handle has an ambitious little job: being your first point of negotiation with everything under the hood. When the handle needs replacing, I’ll walk you through uncovering its mounting, releasing the retaining clips and refitting the handle. The trick is knowing where the clips release; a determined tug is a poor substitute.
guides.why: The interior handle gives your hand the grip and leverage needed to operate the hood-release mechanism. Clips hold the handle on its mounting, and a small access cover conceals the release point. Here, the socket acts as a clip-release aid rather than a tool for undoing a bolt.
searchTerms: interior hood release handle retaining clips

when.summary: Use this procedure when the interior hood-release handle needs removal or replacement.
notes: Applies to 2015 Mustangs with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
The illustration shows a left-hand-drive car. Right-hand-drive removal and installation are similar; locate the equivalent mounting on the fitted layout.
This is a replacement procedure, not a test for deciding whether a hood-release problem originates in the handle, cable or latch.

prepare.title: Have the clip-release socket ready
prepare.detail: Use a 10 mm socket with a 1/4-inch drive. It is inserted at the handle’s exposed retaining point to release the clips.

prepare.title: Identify the handle and access cover
prepare.detail: Look in the driver’s footwell. In the left-hand-drive illustration, the handle sits on the side trim below the steering wheel, beside the footrest. Identify the small cover near the upper end of the handle before disturbing anything.

prepare.title: Keep the work within the handle mounting
prepare.detail: For work extending to the release cable or underhood latch, obtain the matching repair instructions before proceeding beyond this handle removal and refitting operation.

steps.title: Locate the covered retaining point
steps.body: Find the hood-release handle in the driver’s footwell and identify its small access cover. The main view in the [handle procedure](#/document/G1695907) marks this cover near the handle’s upper end as operation 1.
