Keep your attention on the handle itself; this access step does not call for removing the surrounding footwell trim.

steps.title: Remove the handle’s access cover
steps.body: Remove the small access cover from the handle. With it off, locate the central retaining point shown in the illustration’s inset. This is where the socket goes for clip release. The cover-removal method is not detailed further, so do not invent a hidden screw or use the surrounding trim as a pry point.

steps.title: Insert the socket to release the retaining clips
steps.body:
Insert the 10 mm, 1/4-inch-drive socket into the exposed retaining point. Use it to release the clips, following operation 2 in the inset, where the arrows identify the retaining area around the central opening.

The socket is doing clip duty here—there is no bolt-loosening contest to win. Release the retainers before trying to withdraw the handle.

steps.title: Withdraw the released handle
steps.body:
Once the clips release, move the handle away from its mounting in the direction marked 3 in the inset: rightward in that illustration. Note how the handle fits over its mounting so you can reproduce the alignment during installation.

If it remains held at the mounting, return to the clip-release operation. Do not force the handle past retainers that are still engaged.

steps.title: Refit the handle and engage its clips
steps.body:
Install the replacement handle, or refit the removed handle, by reversing its removal movement. Align it with the mounting in its original orientation, return it to its installed position and engage the retaining clips.

Check that it is seated and retained before covering the release point. If it can still slide off the mounting, correct its seating and clip engagement before continuing.

steps.title: Replace the access cover
steps.body: Refit the small access cover after the handle is secured. Return it to the position it occupied before removal and check that it sits properly in its opening. This completes the reverse-order installation described in the [handle procedure](#/document/G1695907).

watchFor.title: Resistance during handle withdrawal
watchFor.body: A handle that remains retained needs another check of clip release. Stop pulling and return the socket to the retaining point rather than increasing force.

watchFor.title: Cover fitted before retention is checked
watchFor.body: Confirm the handle is seated and secured while the retaining point remains accessible. Refit the cover only after that check.

notes: The illustrated sequence is access cover, retaining clips, then handle. Installation reverses that sequence.
The specified 10 mm dimension identifies the clip-release socket; it is not a tightening specification.

diagnostics.finding: The handle will not withdraw after the socket is inserted.
diagnostics.meaning: The handle remains retained; inserting the socket has not yet resulted in a released handle.
diagnostics.next: Recheck the socket’s position at the exposed retaining point and repeat the clip-release operation before attempting withdrawal again.

diagnostics.finding: The refitted handle can slide off its mounting.
diagnostics.meaning: The handle is not securely retained in its installed position.
diagnostics.next: Leave the cover off, check the handle’s alignment and repeat the reverse-order fitting operation until the clips retain it.

verification.title: Handle seated and retained
verification.body: Confirm that the handle occupies its original installed position and cannot simply slide off its mounting. This is an assembly check, not a diagnostic test of the cable or hood latch.

verification.title: Access cover restored
verification.body: Confirm that the access cover is fitted in its opening after the handle has been secured.

procedures.purpose: Illustrated access-cover removal, socket-assisted retaining-clip release, handle removal and reverse-order installation; left-hand drive shown, right-hand drive similar.

applicability.equipment: Interior hood-release handle; left-hand-drive or right-hand-drive layout.

stepGroups.title: Expose the retaining point
stepGroups.summary: Locate the handle and remove its small access cover.

stepGroups.title: Release and remove the handle
stepGroups.summary: Use the specified socket to release the clips, then withdraw the handle.

stepGroups.title: Secure the handle and replace the cover
stepGroups.summary: Reverse the removal sequence and confirm retention before closing the access point.

guides.title: Replace and position the hood latch
guides.summary: Reach the hood latch beneath the radiator sight shield, preserve its mounting position, disconnect its cable and switch connector, then reinstall and tighten it to 80 lb.in (9 Nm).
guides.introduction: The hood latch has a wonderfully stubborn personality: keeping the hood shut is its entire career. The trick when replacing it is preserving where it sits, while remembering that its release cable and electrical connector both need to come along for the ride. I’ll walk you through the access, connections and final positioning without turning two nuts into an epic garage saga.
guides.why: The latch mechanically holds the hood closed. The release cable transfers your pull at the hood-release handle to the latch, while the hood-ajar switch provides an electrical indication of hood position. Marking the mounting location before removal gives you a reference for installation; leaving the nuts finger tight initially lets you restore that position before securing the latch.

when.summary: Use this procedure when an identified repair requires removing or replacing the hood latch on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
notes: This is a removal and installation procedure, not a test for deciding whether a release or hood-ajar complaint requires a new latch.
The illustrations show a left-hand-drive vehicle; the right-hand-drive arrangement is similar.

prepare.title: Start with access to the engine compartment
prepare.detail: Open the hood and make sure it is securely supported before working over the front of the engine compartment. This procedure returns the latch to its recorded mounting position. Opening a hood that is stuck shut, establishing alignment without usable reference marks, and diagnosing a release or switch fault require separate instructions. The connector-lock and cable-retainer release mechanisms are not detailed here; identify how the fitted attachments disengage before applying force.

prepare.title: Gather the fastening and marking tools
prepare.detail: Have a suitable tool for the radiator sight-shield retainers, hand tools that fit the latch nuts, a marking tool and a torque wrench capable of accurately applying 80 lb.in (9 Nm). Keep the eight shield retainers and two latch nuts together for reassembly. Have the replacement latch ready if replacement is the purpose of the job.

prepare.title: Identify what you are removing
prepare.detail: The radiator sight shield is the broad panel across the front of the engine compartment, above the radiator and grille area. The latch sits centrally behind it. In the close-up illustrations, the electrical connector is on the left of the latch and the release-cable attachment is toward its lower right. Use those as illustrated landmarks, checking the actual arrangement on your car.

steps.title: Remove the radiator sight shield
steps.body:
Working from above with the hood open, locate the broad shield across the front of the engine compartment. Remove its eight retainers, including those along the front edge and at the side and upper mounting points shown in the illustration.

Lift the shield clear and set it and its retainers aside. This exposes the centrally mounted hood latch and its two mounting nuts. The access sequence is also covered in [Hood Latch](#/document/G1695905).

steps.title: Mark the latch mounting position before loosening it
steps.body:
Locate the two nuts, one at each upper side of the latch. Mark their positions relative to the surrounding mounting surface so you have usable references for returning the latch to the same location.

Make the marks before either nut is loosened, and check that they will remain readable when the latch comes away. I would rather spend a moment making clear marks than invite an alignment guessing game into the afternoon.

steps.title: Remove the nuts and disconnect the hood-ajar switch
steps.body:
Support the latch as you remove its two mounting nuts. Keep the latch controlled while its cable and wiring remain attached.

Disconnect the hood-ajar switch electrical connector, shown on the left side in the removal illustration. Handle the connector body rather than pulling on the wires. Leave the disconnected vehicle wiring clear of the latch.

steps.title: Disconnect the release cable and lift out the latch
steps.body:
With the latch supported, disconnect the hood-release cable at its attachment toward the lower-right side of the illustrated latch. Free the cable attachment from the latch before trying to carry the assembly away; the cable is a working connection, not a convenient tether.

Once the electrical connector and release cable are both detached, remove the latch. Leave the vehicle-side cable and wiring accessible for reconnection.

steps.title: Connect the latch and start both nuts by hand
steps.body:
Bring the latch into its mounting area and connect the hood-release cable to it. Check that the cable attachment is engaged with the latch before continuing.

Reconnect the hood-ajar switch electrical connector. Position the latch on its mountings and install both nuts finger tight only. The latch must remain movable enough to line up with your reference marks.

steps.title: Restore the marked position and tighten the nuts
steps.body:
Move the latch to the reference positions recorded before removal. Check both mounting points before tightening.

Tighten the two hood-latch nuts to **80 lb.in (9 Nm)**. This is an inch-pound value, not a foot-pound value. Check that the latch remains at the marked position after tightening.

steps.title: Refit the radiator sight shield
steps.body:
Before covering the latch, check that the release cable and hood-ajar connector are connected and that neither the cable nor wiring is caught beneath the shield.

Return the radiator sight shield to its original position and reinstall all eight retainers. Check that the panel is seated and every retainer is engaged. The engine compartment can now have its tidy front cover back.

watchFor.title: Reference marks that disappear with the old latch
watchFor.body: The marks must help locate the installed latch relative to its mounting surface. Check their usefulness before removing the assembly; marks confined to a removable part may leave you without a position reference.

watchFor.title: Tightening before positioning
watchFor.body: Keep both nuts finger tight until the latch has been moved to the recorded references. Apply the final 80 lb.in (9 Nm) torque only after positioning it.

watchFor.title: A mounted latch with an unfinished connection
watchFor.body: The release cable and hood-ajar connector serve different functions. Confirm both are connected before reinstalling the shield; fastening the latch does not complete those connections.

notes: The illustrated access uses eight radiator sight-shield retainers and two hood-latch mounting nuts.
The procedure is the same supplied removal and installation sequence for all four listed engines; the engine-bay appearance in the illustrations does not narrow that applicability.

diagnostics.finding: The mounting references are missing or cannot establish the latch's original position.
diagnostics.meaning: You cannot reliably complete the specified return-to-position installation.
diagnostics.next: Obtain the appropriate hood-latch alignment instructions before final positioning and tightening. Do not choose a location by guesswork.

diagnostics.finding: The cable attachment or electrical connector will not engage during reassembly.
diagnostics.meaning: Reassembly is incomplete; this alone does not establish that the latch, cable or switch is faulty.
diagnostics.next: Keep the hood open and recheck the attachment against its original arrangement. Resolve the engagement problem before covering the latch or attempting normal hood operation.

diagnostics.finding: The hood does not secure or release normally after reassembly.
diagnostics.meaning: The repair has not passed its practical completion check; the cause still needs to be established.
diagnostics.next: Do not drive with an unsecured hood. Recheck the recorded latch position and restored connections, then obtain the appropriate alignment or fault-diagnosis instructions if the problem remains.

verification.title: Confirm the exposed assembly before fitting the shield
verification.body: Check both mounting references, confirm that both nuts were tightened to 80 lb.in (9 Nm), and verify that the release cable and hood-ajar electrical connector are engaged.

verification.title: Account for the access panel and fasteners
verification.body: Confirm that the radiator sight shield is seated and all eight retainers are installed. Remove tools and loose parts from the work area.

verification.title: Check normal operation as a completion check
verification.body: After the assembly checks, confirm that the hood closes securely and that the normal hood-release control releases it. This checks the completed repair; it is not a diagnostic test for the cable or switch. Do not drive until the hood is securely latched.

procedures.purpose: Hood-latch access, removal and installation, including eight shield retainers, two mounting nuts, position marking, release-cable and switch connections, and the 80 lb.in (9 Nm) final torque.

applicability.equipment: Cable-operated hood latch with hood-ajar switch electrical connection; left-hand-drive and right-hand-drive vehicles.

stepGroups.title: Expose the latch and record its position
stepGroups.summary: Remove the front shield and make usable mounting references.

stepGroups.title: Free the latch and its connections
stepGroups.summary: Remove the nuts, unplug the switch and detach the release cable.

stepGroups.title: Reconnect, position and reassemble
stepGroups.summary: Restore both connections, align and torque the latch, then refit the shield.

guides.title: Replace the interior front door handle
guides.summary: Remove the door trim, replace the interior handle and transfer the door lock control switch when fitting a new handle.
guides.introduction: The interior handle operates the door latch through a cable, while the nearby door lock control switch sends an electrical lock or unlock request. These are related controls with different jobs. Handle replacement requires removing the trim panel, releasing its cable and electrical connections, then releasing the handle’s own nut and retaining clips. When fitting a new handle, the lock control switch is removed for transfer.
guides.why: The trim panel is held by fasteners and several groups of clips, so it must be released in stages before being lifted away. The latch cable and any electrical connectors remain attached until deliberately released. Treating the panel as fully free too early can pull on those connections.
searchTerms: door will not open from inside

when.summary: When inspection identifies an interior front door handle that needs removal or replacement.
notes: A door-opening complaint does not by itself distinguish a handle problem from a latch or cable problem.

prepare.title: Trim-removal equipment
prepare.detail: Have tools suited to the panel fasteners and retaining clips, plus a torque tool suitable for the trim-panel installation values.

prepare.title: Plan switch and cable access
prepare.detail: Use Front Door Trim Panel for the access sequence, including its referenced window-control-switch removal instructions. Keep the panel supported while its latch cable and fitted connectors are detached.

steps.title: Remove the trim-panel fasteners
steps.body: Remove the upper bolt cover and upper bolt, then remove the front door window control switch using the instructions referenced in [Front Door Trim Panel](#/document/G1692600). Remove the center bolt and lower retainers.

steps.title: Release the panel in stages
steps.body: Move the rear upper portion away from the door and release its clip and pin-type retainers. Next release the rear and lower portion, then the remaining pin-type retainers as the panel is moved away. Follow the illustrated sequence rather than pulling the whole panel free at once.

steps.title: Lift off and disconnect the trim
steps.body: Lift the panel up and out to release it from the door. Disconnect its electrical connectors where equipped and release the latch cable. The panel can then be removed without leaving those connections attached.

steps.title: Release the interior handle
steps.body: Follow the [handle procedure](#/document/G1695908): release the nut, release the retaining clips and remove the interior front door handle.

steps.title: Transfer the lock switch when replacing the handle
steps.body: Only when installing a new handle, release the door lock control switch retaining clips and remove the switch. Install it in the replacement handle during reverse-order assembly. This removal is unnecessary when refitting the existing handle.

steps.title: Reassemble the handle and trim
steps.body: Reverse the removal operations, restoring the handle attachments, latch cable, fitted connectors and trim retainers. Tighten the upper and center trim-panel bolts to 48 lb.in (5.4 Nm), and the lower trim-panel retainers to 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm). Reinstall the window switch and upper cover.

watchFor.title: Applying a trim torque to the handle
watchFor.body: The stated values belong to the trim-panel fasteners. They are not a tightening specification for the handle nut.

watchFor.title: Confusing electrical locking with handle release
watchFor.body: The lock switch requests power locking or unlocking. An electrical locking complaint alone does not establish that the mechanical handle needs replacement.

notes: Left-hand-drive examples are shown; right-hand-drive work is similar. The handle procedure shows the left side and the trim procedure the right side, with opposite sides similar.
Transfer other trim parts as necessary during panel installation.

verification.title: Confirm the handle attachments
verification.body: Check that the handle nut and retaining clips are restored and that a transferred lock switch is secured by its clips.

verification.title: Confirm the trim reconnections
verification.body: Before completing panel installation, confirm that the latch cable and every disconnected electrical connector are restored. Finish with the panel retainers, bolts, switch and cover installed.

procedures.purpose: Interior front door handle removal and installation, including lock-switch removal only when fitting a new handle.
Front door trim-panel access, staged retainer release, cable and connector disconnection, and trim installation.

guides.title: Replace the Rear Keyless Entry Antenna
guides.summary: Lift out the luggage compartment scuff plate, unplug and release the rear keyless entry antenna, then reinstall the antenna and trim.
guides.introduction: A keyless Mustang should spare you the pocket excavation routine. Its rear antenna helps the entry system communicate with the key, but replacing it still involves a little old-fashioned trim removal. I’ll walk you through the four scuff-plate retainers, the electrical connection and the two antenna retainers in order. This procedure applies to 2015 Mustangs with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine, in coupe or convertible form. The illustrations show the coupe; convertible access is similar.
guides.why: The rear antenna sits behind the luggage compartment scuff plate—the trim across the rear loading edge of the trunk opening. Removing that trim exposes the antenna’s connector and mounting retainers. The antenna belongs to the broader entry system, whose passive-entry functions include door locking or unlocking and luggage compartment latch release; those shared functions do not make every entry complaint an antenna failure.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang rear keyless entry antenna replacement

when.summary: Use this procedure when the rear keyless entry antenna has been identified for replacement or needs to be removed.
notes: A door-locking or luggage-compartment-release complaint alone does not identify the rear antenna as the failed part.
The same removal sequence applies across the listed engines.

prepare.title: Establish the job before removing trim
prepare.detail: This is a physical removal and installation procedure, beginning once the antenna needs to come out. Electrical fault testing is outside its scope; do not use replacement as a test of a suspected keyless-entry fault.

prepare.title: Make room at the luggage compartment opening
prepare.detail: Clear enough space to reach the scuff plate across the rear loading edge and to set the removed trim aside. Open the luggage compartment lid and leave it installed throughout the job.

prepare.title: Keep the two sets of retainers separate
prepare.detail: The scuff plate has four thumb-nut retainers. The antenna behind it has two separate mounting retainers and one electrical connector. Keep the trim retainers together so they are ready for reassembly. Have the replacement antenna ready if replacement is the purpose of the job.

steps.title: Open the luggage compartment and locate the scuff plate
steps.body: Open the luggage compartment lid. Find the broad trim panel spanning the rear loading edge, around the central latch area. This is the luggage compartment scuff plate, and it is the only access trim removed in the [antenna replacement procedure](#/document/G1695909).

steps.title: Remove the four scuff-plate thumb nuts
steps.body: Locate and unscrew the four thumb-nut retainers securing the scuff plate. The illustration shows four retaining points distributed across the panel. Collect all four before lifting the trim; a missing thumb nut has a remarkable talent for extending a small job.

steps.title: Lift the scuff plate out of the opening
steps.body: With the thumb nuts removed, lift the scuff plate upward from the rear loading edge. The illustrated removal arrows point upward on both sides of the central latch opening. Lift the panel clear and set it aside to expose the antenna mounting area behind it.

steps.title: Identify and disconnect the antenna
steps.body: Locate the small rectangular rear keyless entry antenna behind the removed scuff plate. Identify its electrical connector separately from the two mounting retainers. Disconnect the connector first, handling the connector housing rather than pulling on its wire. Leave the disconnected lead clear of the antenna so it will not be pulled as the component comes away.

steps.title: Release the two antenna retainers and remove the antenna
steps.body: Support the antenna, remove its two mounting retainers and take it away from its mounting position. The illustration shows push-type retainers, with an enlarged view of their shape. Keep these separate from the four scuff-plate thumb nuts. Note the antenna’s installed orientation so the replacement can return to the same position.

steps.title: Mount the antenna and reconnect its electrical connector
steps.body: Reverse the antenna removal sequence: position the replacement or retained antenna at its mounting points, install both antenna retainers, then reconnect the electrical connector. Before covering the area, check that both retaining points hold the antenna and that the connector is fully seated. Keep the lead clear of the scuff plate’s seating area.

steps.title: Reinstall the scuff plate and its four thumb nuts
steps.body: Return the scuff plate to the rear loading edge, aligning its central opening with the latch area and its retaining points with their original locations. Lower it into its installed position, reversing the upward removal movement. Refit all four thumb-nut retainers. Check that the panel is seated before treating the nuts as a way to pull it into place.

steps.title: Check the completed installation
steps.body: Confirm that the scuff plate sits in its original position and all four thumb nuts are installed. The antenna’s two retainers and electrical connection should already have been checked before the trim went back on. Once the opening is clear, close the luggage compartment lid. These checks confirm reassembly; they do not establish whether an earlier keyless-entry complaint has been resolved.

watchFor.title: Leave the luggage compartment lid installed
watchFor.body: The antenna illustration omits the lid to improve the view. Lid removal is not part of this job.

watchFor.title: Disconnect before releasing the antenna
watchFor.body: Unplug the antenna before removing its two retainers. Moving a still-connected antenna can pull on the electrical lead.

watchFor.title: Check behind the trim before covering it
watchFor.body: Verify the antenna mounting and connector while they remain visible. Reopening the trim for a forgotten plug is a particularly annoying encore.

notes: The coupe is illustrated, and the convertible follows a similar procedure.
The scuff plate is the protective trim across the rear loading edge of the luggage compartment.

diagnostics.finding: The car has a keyless-entry, door-locking or luggage-compartment-release complaint, but the rear antenna has not been identified as the cause.
diagnostics.meaning: These functions belong to a broader entry system. The complaint alone does not isolate the rear antenna.
diagnostics.next: Establish the fault before replacing the antenna. The [entry-system overview](#/document/G1695896) explains the relationship between passive entry, power locking and luggage compartment release, but is not an antenna test procedure.

verification.title: Antenna secured and connected
verification.body: Before fitting the scuff plate, confirm that both antenna retainers are installed, the antenna is held at its mounting points and the electrical connector is fully seated.

verification.title: Trim restored
verification.body: Confirm that the scuff plate is seated around the central latch area, all four thumb-nut retainers are installed and the electrical lead is clear of the trim.

verification.title: Luggage compartment returned to use
verification.body: Remove the loose retainers and removed parts from the opening, then close the lid. Keep mechanical completion separate from confirmation of any original entry-system fault.

procedures.purpose: Rear keyless entry antenna removal and reverse-order installation, including scuff-plate access, four thumb-nut retainers, the electrical connector and two antenna retainers.
Explain the broader power-locking and passive-entry functions without treating a shared system complaint as proof of antenna failure.

stepGroups.title: Open the antenna access area
stepGroups.summary: Open the lid, remove four thumb nuts and lift out the scuff plate.

stepGroups.title: Disconnect and remove the antenna
stepGroups.summary: Unplug the connector, then release the two antenna retainers.

stepGroups.title: Install the antenna and restore the trim
stepGroups.summary: Secure and reconnect the antenna, refit the scuff plate and check completion.

guides.title: Replace the coupe luggage compartment lid latch
guides.summary: Remove the emergency release handle and lid trim, replace the electrically connected latch, and restore its covers and release handle.
guides.introduction: The luggage compartment lid latch holds the coupe's trunk lid closed and releases it when commanded. The entry system can request latch release through passive entry, while an emergency release handle is also attached at the lid. Replacing the latch involves these nearby release and trim parts before its electrical connector and mounting nuts become accessible.
guides.why: The emergency handle and latch cover each have a retaining feature that must be released deliberately. Pulling the cover without disengaging its tab risks damaging it. Moving the disconnected wiring aside also clears the latch so it can be removed without drawing the harness along with it.

when.summary: When the coupe luggage compartment lid latch requires replacement or removal for related service.
notes: A release complaint requires fault identification before replacement; this operation addresses the latch assembly.

prepare.title: Prepare the trim-release tool
prepare.detail: Use a flat-bladed screwdriver for the latch cover. Be ready to release its retaining tab gently rather than pulling against the attached cover.

prepare.title: Prepare for latch attachment
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the mounting nuts and trim retainers, plus a torque wrench for 62 lb.in (7 Nm). Keep the handle, cover and panel retainers available for reassembly.

steps.title: Remove the emergency release handle
steps.body: Press down the emergency release handle retaining tab, then remove the handle. Begin with this release action as shown in [Luggage Compartment Lid Latch - Coupe](#/document/G1695910), so the retained handle is free before proceeding.

steps.title: Release the cover and remove the trim
steps.body: Insert the flat-bladed screwdriver between the latch cover and latch. Gently pry the cover away while disengaging it from the latch tab. Remove the trim-panel retainers and then the luggage compartment lid trim panel.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the latch
steps.body: Disconnect the electrical connector and position the wiring harness aside. Remove the latch mounting nuts and lift away the latch. Keeping the harness clear separates the electrical connection from the mechanical removal.

steps.title: Install the latch and restore the release parts
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Fit the latch and tighten its mounting nuts to 62 lb.in (7 Nm), then reconnect the harness. Reinstall the trim panel and retainers, latch cover and emergency release handle, restoring their retaining engagements.

watchFor.title: Cover resisting removal
watchFor.body: Confirm that the cover is disengaging from its latch tab. The specified action is gentle prying, not forceful pulling.

watchFor.title: Release handle omitted during reassembly
watchFor.body: The emergency release handle is part of the completed assembly and must be restored after the trim and cover.

notes: This procedure applies to the coupe latch. The mounting-nut torque is for the latch attachment.

verification.title: Check assembly completeness
verification.body: Confirm the latch connector is reconnected, the trim retainers and cover are installed, and the emergency release handle is retained.

verification.title: Record latch fastening
verification.body: Record completion of the mounting-nut torque check before the attachment is concealed by the trim.

procedures.purpose: Coupe luggage compartment lid latch removal and installation, including emergency handle, latch cover and interior trim access.

guides.title: Replace the exterior luggage-compartment release switch
guides.summary: Release the exterior switch from the rear bumper cover, unplug it, then reconnect and secure its replacement. Applies to 2015 Mustangs with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine.
guides.introduction: A trunk button has one small job and an impressive ability to make luggage feel imprisoned. I’ll walk you through replacing the exterior luggage-compartment release switch, located immediately above the rear license-plate recess. It sends an electrical request to release the lid; the latch is the separate mechanism that actually holds the lid shut.
guides.why: The switch has two attachments to undo in order: the retaining feature securing its housing in the bumper cover, then the electrical connector behind it. I release the housing first so the plug becomes accessible without making the wiring do duty as a tow rope.
searchTerms: 2015 Mustang luggage compartment lid release switch

when.summary: Use this procedure when the exterior release switch has been identified as needing replacement.
notes: A lid that does not open when the button is pressed does not, by itself, establish that the switch is faulty.
The entry system also supports luggage-lid release through passive entry; that context does not provide an electrical test for this switch.

prepare.title: Locate the switch and prepare the replacement
prepare.detail: Work at the center of the rear bumper cover, immediately above the license-plate recess. Have the replacement switch and a trim-release wedge of the type illustrated in the removal procedure ready. The retaining feature is at the end of the switch opposite its wiring connector.

prepare.title: Know the limits before applying force
prepare.detail: This procedure covers physical replacement, not electrical fault diagnosis. The precise connector-lock release method is not detailed here. Identify how the plug unlocks before pulling it apart; if that is unclear, obtain the matching connector detail rather than forcing it.

steps.title: Locate the housing and its retaining end
steps.body: Find the small exterior release switch immediately above the rear license-plate recess. Identify the retaining end opposite the electrical connector. The [switch removal procedure](#/document/G1695893) shows this retaining feature as the first release point and the connector as the second.

steps.title: Release the switch from the bumper cover
steps.body:
Use the trim-release wedge to disengage the retaining feature at that end, pressing it inward toward the switch housing as indicated by the release arrow. Ease the housing out of the bumper-cover opening far enough to reach its electrical connector.

Support the freed switch as it comes out. Do not pull on the harness to extract it, and do not keep levering against the bumper if the retaining feature is still engaged.

steps.title: Disconnect the plug and remove the switch
steps.body:
With the housing released and supported, disengage the electrical connector’s locking feature and separate the plug from the switch. Hold the connector body rather than pulling its wires. Remove the disconnected switch from the vehicle.

Keep the vehicle-side plug accessible for installation. That little plug is the next thing you need, so don’t let it become a bumper-cover hide-and-seek champion.

steps.title: Connect the replacement before seating it
steps.body: Bring the replacement switch to the opening while leaving its connector accessible. Attach the vehicle wiring connector and make sure its locking feature engages. This restores the electrical connection before the housing goes back into the bumper.

steps.title: Refit the switch and check the completed installation
steps.body:
Guide the connected switch into its bumper-cover opening, keeping the wiring behind the housing without trapping it at the edge. Seat the switch and engage its retaining feature.

Check that the housing stays seated without being held and that the connector remains attached. Then check the button’s normal luggage-lid release operation under the vehicle’s usual operating conditions. This is a completion check, not an electrical diagnosis.

watchFor.title: The switch remains caught in the opening
watchFor.body: Stop pulling and check that the retaining feature has actually disengaged. More force on a still-retained housing is not the next step.

watchFor.title: The wiring becomes taut
watchFor.body: Support the housing closer to the opening and disconnect the plug before moving the switch farther away. Keep extraction force off the wires.

watchFor.title: The replacement will not stay seated
watchFor.body: Check the retaining feature’s engagement and whether wiring is caught at the opening. Do not treat a loose housing as a finished installation.

notes: Installation reverses the removal order: connect the wiring first, then secure the switch in the bumper cover.
The [entry-system overview](#/document/G1695896) explains passive luggage-lid release as part of the surrounding system; it does not establish a switch-specific fault test.

diagnostics.finding: The exterior button does not release the lid, but the switch has not been confirmed faulty.
diagnostics.meaning: This is a release-system complaint, not proof that this particular component needs replacement.
diagnostics.next: Have the fault identified before buying or replacing the switch. This article provides the physical replacement procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The replacement is connected and retained, but normal lid-release operation is still unsuccessful.
diagnostics.meaning: The operational complaint remains unresolved; the result alone does not identify its cause.
diagnostics.next: Recheck the connection and mounting disturbed during the job. If both are secure, continue with release-system diagnosis instead of guessing another replacement part.

verification.title: Electrical attachment restored
verification.body: Before seating the housing, confirm that the connector is attached and its locking feature is engaged.

verification.title: Mechanical attachment restored
verification.body: Confirm that the switch remains seated in the bumper cover and its retaining feature holds it securely.

verification.title: Normal operation checked
verification.body: Check that pressing the exterior switch releases the luggage lid under the vehicle’s normal release conditions. If it does not, use the unresolved-operation branch above.

procedures.purpose: Switch location, retaining-feature release, electrical disconnection and reverse-order installation.
Context for the surrounding entry system and its passive luggage-lid release function.

applicability.equipment: Exterior luggage-compartment lid release switch mounted in the rear bumper cover.

stepGroups.title: Access and remove the switch
stepGroups.summary: Locate the retaining end, release the housing and disconnect its wiring.

stepGroups.title: Install and check
stepGroups.summary: Reconnect the replacement, secure it in the bumper cover and check completion.

guides.title: Diagnose windshield wiper, washer and rain-sensing faults
guides.summary: Use the affected operating mode, switch data and circuit checks to distinguish control, motor, washer-flow and wiping-surface faults.
guides.introduction: The steering column control module (SCCM) reads the wiper switch and sends requests over the local interconnect network (LIN) to the wiper motor’s control electronics. Those electronics also operate the washer pump. A separate high-speed command provides backup operation, so working high speed does not prove normal communication is intact.
guides.why: Different complaints need different tests. Poor wiping can come from contaminated glass, rain sensing depends on optical contact, and an electrical code can describe wiring rather than a failed module.

when.summary: When wiping, parking, washing or fitted rain-sensitive operation differs from the selected command.
notes: Confirm the complaint is present before following a branch that directs component replacement.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check previous repairs, battery and charging condition, and battery state of charge above 70%. Scan for related diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), addressing circuit codes before performance codes. Inspect the specified fuses, switch, wiring and connectors.

prepare.title: Use suitable diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Have a scan tool with switch parameter identification (PID) data, a multimeter and Wiring Diagrams Cell 81. A13 and H require a Rotunda SGT27000 or 250–300 mA incandescent test lamp with Flex Probes; never insert the lamp probe directly into a connector.

steps.title: All modes inoperative: Test A
steps.body: Start with motor-connector inspection. Follow the code-selected branch through known-good relay substitution or relay-control wiring checks. Other branches compare switch PIDs and check motor supply, ground and the high-speed fail-safe command. Complete the prescribed connector inspections and service-article checks before directed motor, SCCM or body control module (BCM) replacement.

steps.title: Low or intermittent wiping inoperative: Test B
steps.body: Check high speed first; failure returns to A. If low speed works, use E for ordinary intermittent wiping or F for rain-sensitive equipment. With low speed dead, check its switch PID. On equipped vehicles, restoration after rain-sensor isolation directs sensor replacement. Otherwise test LIN wiring before the motor and SCCM confirmation branches.

steps.title: High-speed or manual intermittent faults: Tests C and E
steps.body: C compares the high-speed request PID. E first disables enabled rain sensing to establish manual intermittent operation, verifies low speed, then compares interval-setting PIDs. Correct requests direct motor replacement; incorrect requests direct switch replacement and retesting before SCCM replacement. Failed low speed in E returns to B.

steps.title: Wipers run continuously: Test D
steps.body: Operation with ignition off selects relay-control and supply tests. Without B130F:14, continued running after relay removal identifies a supply-circuit fault; stopping directs relay replacement. If ignition off stops the wipers, check off-command PIDs, isolate the SCCM and test the fail-safe circuit for a ground short before component confirmation.

steps.title: Rain-sensitive operation incorrect: Test F
steps.body: Confirm low speed works; otherwise use B. Rain-sensor communication codes lead to supply, ground and LIN checks. Without those codes, verify feature settings and switch PIDs, then inspect glass, wipe quality and sensor contact. Glass damage near the sensor directs windshield replacement. Clean glass and blades and water-test as specified. Missing or damaged gel requires sensor replacement. Contaminated contact requires cleaning and correct refitting, then motor replacement if unresolved. Sound optical checks continue to circuit and SCCM confirmation.

steps.title: Incorrect parking or poor wiping: Tests G and J
steps.body: G checks mounting-arm and pivot-shaft damage, then aligns the blades with the windshield installation marks. Persistent or uncorrectable alignment follows service-article checks before assembly replacement. J cleans blades with washer fluid and glass with glass cleaner, using lint-free cloths; replace affected blades only if poor cleaning, streaking or chatter remains.

steps.title: Washer failure or continuous washing: Tests H and I
steps.body: H checks freezing conditions and solvent suitability first; incorrect solvent requires warming, draining and refilling. Fluid from disconnected jet hoses identifies a jet concern. A running pump leads to hose inspection; intact hoses direct pump replacement. A silent pump leads through switch PID, loaded supply/ground and wiring checks. For continuous washing, I checks the wash-request PID: an erroneous request directs switch replacement and retesting before SCCM replacement. With no request, continued pumping after motor disconnection identifies wiring; stopping directs wiper-motor replacement.

watchFor.title: Temporary connector recovery
watchFor.body: If reseating restores operation, correct the underlying corrosion, terminal damage or poor retention.

watchFor.title: Rain-sensor contact
watchFor.body: The contact should appear black without bubbles or contamination. The gel lens is not separately replaceable.

notes: Test B notes that battery disconnection and reconnection may be needed after repair to restore wiper operation.
Follow each branch’s specified ignition states, connector isolation and measurement limits in the complete diagnostic procedure.

diagnostics.finding: BCM B130F:12 or B130F:14
diagnostics.meaning: Relay-control faults: short to voltage for B130F:12; an open in A or short to ground in D for B130F:14.
diagnostics.next: Select A or D by the actual symptom.

diagnostics.finding: SCCM B1131:02
diagnostics.meaning: The fail-safe input disagrees with the requested input.
diagnostics.next: Use A or D according to operation.

diagnostics.meaning: Wiper LIN communication failure or short to ground, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Follow B.

diagnostics.finding: SCCM B10AD:02 or B10AD:08
diagnostics.meaning: Rain-sensor communication fault.
diagnostics.next: Follow F’s electrical branch; route other codes through the chart.

verification.title: Repeat functional testing
verification.body: Confirm the original complaint is resolved. After fail-safe circuit repair, check every wiper mode because a second fault may remain.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the failed mode, codes, relevant switch data, repair and successful operating checks.

procedures.purpose: DTC and symptom routing plus complete pinpoint tests A–J.
Diagnostic prerequisites, protected probing and valid electrical measurements.
Control logic, high-speed backup, washer operation and optional rain sensing.
Right-hand multifunction switch removal and installation when directed.
SCCM removal and installation after diagnostic confirmation.
Windshield wiper motor removal and installation when directed.
Rain-sensor removal and installation for applicable equipped vehicles.
Fixed-glass procedure when Test F identifies windshield damage.
Pivot-arm removal, alignment and installation for parking concerns.
Washer-pump removal and installation when Test H directs replacement.

guides.title: Disconnect and reconnect a washer hose coupling
guides.summary: Separate and reconnect C-lock or pinch-type washer hose couplings while protecting their seals and locking features.
guides.introduction: Washer hoses carry fluid from the washer pump toward the windshield. Their couplings let a hose separate from a fitting for service while maintaining a sealed connection during use. This job covers two connector designs: a C-lock with a rotating lock ring and a pinch-type connector released at raised points.
guides.why: The lock holds the connection together; the O-ring seals the fluid passage. Both need care. Tools can damage either coupling design, and leaving a C-lock ring unlocked weakens it, potentially causing poor retention and a leak after assembly.

when.summary: When a washer hose connection must be separated for service or its coupling needs attention.
notes: Choose the branch matching the connector fitted to the hose.

prepare.title: Provide hand access
prepare.detail: Arrange enough access to support and release the connector by hand. Do not use hand tools to disconnect or connect either design.

prepare.title: Identify the locking feature
prepare.detail: Use the rotating-ring instructions for a C-lock and the raised squeeze-point instructions for a pinch-type coupling.

steps.title: C-lock: release without disturbing the seal
steps.body: Following [Washer Hose Coupling](#/document/G1694647), hold the female side at its hose connection to prevent internal rotation. Gently rotate the ring approximately 90 degrees, then slide the coupling off the fitting without losing its O-ring. Leave the ring attached and immediately return it to its original locked position.

steps.title: C-lock: reconnect with the ring locked
steps.body: Verify the ring is locked before inserting the male fitting. The ring flexes slightly to admit the fitting and snaps into engagement. Gently pull on the coupling to confirm that it is seated.

steps.title: Pinch type: release and inspect
steps.body: Squeeze the connector at its two raised points and gently pull the connection apart. Inspect the O-ring and replace it if necessary before reconnecting.

steps.title: Pinch type: engage and check retention
steps.body: Insert the male fitting until the connector locks with an audible click. Gently pull on the coupling to verify correct seating.

watchFor.title: C-lock ring left open
watchFor.body: The ring must return to its locked position while the connection is apart; reconnecting starts with the ring locked.

watchFor.title: A click without a retention check
watchFor.body: The audible snap or click does not replace the specified gentle pull check.

notes: The C-lock ring stays on the coupling throughout disconnection and reconnection.

diagnostics.finding: The pinch-type coupling’s O-ring needs replacement.
diagnostics.meaning: The sealing element requires attention before the connector is reassembled.
diagnostics.next: Replace the O-ring as necessary, reconnect and perform the retention check.

verification.title: Connection retained
verification.body: Confirm the applicable lock engages and the assembled coupling remains seated during a gentle pull.

verification.title: Seal and ring accounted for
verification.body: Confirm the C-lock O-ring was retained, or the pinch-type O-ring was inspected, and that the C-lock ring is locked.

procedures.purpose: Separate disconnection and reconnection methods for C-lock and pinch-type washer hose couplings.

guides.title: Repair a damaged rubber windshield-washer hose
guides.summary: Remove the damaged rubber hose section and join the clean ends with a washer-hose adapter, adding the specified sleeve and clamps if necessary.
guides.introduction: The washer hose carries solvent from the washer pump toward the windshield. A damaged section can let fluid escape before it reaches the glass. This repair restores that liquid path by removing the damaged rubber and connecting the remaining ends with an adapter.
guides.why: The hose material determines the repair route: this splice is permitted only on rubber hose. Clean cuts prepare the ends for the adapter, while the optional rubber sleeve and spring clamps provide the additional securing method described for difficult cases.

when.summary: When damage has been located and verified in a rubber washer hose.
notes: A damaged plastic washer hose requires a new hose.

prepare.title: Repair items
prepare.detail: Provide access to the damaged section, a cutting knife and a windshield-washer hose adapter. If additional securing is necessary, have the specified black rubber hose and spring clamps available.

steps.title: Verify the damaged hose and its material
steps.body: Locate the actual damaged section before cutting. Confirm that it is rubber. Weak or absent wash delivery alone does not establish that the hose needs this repair.

steps.title: Remove the damaged section cleanly
steps.body: Follow the [washer-hose repair procedure](#/document/G1694648) and its illustration. Cut cleanly and remove the damaged portion using the specified 0.5000 in (12.7 mm) cut-out dimension.

steps.title: Connect the remaining ends
steps.body: Install a windshield-washer hose adapter between the cut ends. This reconnects the fluid passage across the removed section.

steps.title: Add the securing sleeve if necessary
steps.body: For difficult cases requiring additional securing, install a segment of 6.4 mm (0.25 in) internal-diameter black rubber hose over both ends of the washer hose and clamp it with spring clamps.

watchFor.title: Plastic hose
watchFor.body: Do not apply this rubber-hose repair to damaged plastic tubing; install a new washer hose.

notes: The washer pump is commanded through the windshield-wiper motor when a wash request is made. A hose repair addresses a verified fluid-path defect.

diagnostics.finding: Verified damage in rubber washer hose.
diagnostics.meaning: The material is eligible for this adapter repair.
diagnostics.next: Remove the damaged portion and join the clean ends.

diagnostics.finding: Verified damage in plastic washer hose.
diagnostics.meaning: The splice procedure does not apply.
diagnostics.next: Install a new washer hose.

verification.title: Repair and delivery
verification.body: Confirm the adapter joins both cut ends and any required sleeve is clamped. Request windshield wash to confirm fluid delivery to the windshield and inspect the repaired joint for leakage.

procedures.purpose: Rubber washer-hose repair, including the cut-out dimension, adapter and conditional sleeve-and-clamp method.

guides.title: Remove and replace the windshield rain sensor
guides.summary: Release the rain sensor, inspect its gel lens and refit or replace it against clean windshield glass.
guides.introduction: The rain sensor uses an infrared beam to detect moisture on the windshield. Water changes the reflected light, and the sensor sends that information to the wiper motor’s control electronics. A gel lens forms the interface between sensor and glass. This job removes the sensor from its bracket and restores that interface with either an undamaged sensor or a replacement.
guides.why: Clean glass and an intact gel lens are central to optical sensing. A missing or damaged lens can leave rain-sensitive wiping inoperative, and this lens cannot be replaced separately. Correct bracket seating and clip engagement hold the sensor in its intended position.

when.summary: When the rain sensor requires removal or its gel lens is damaged or missing.
notes: Intermittent wiping alone does not prove that the sensor has failed.

prepare.title: Prepare the glass cleaner
prepare.detail: Use Motorcraft Ultra-Clear Spray Glass Cleaner ZC-23, specification ESR-M14P5-A, for the windshield contact area.

prepare.title: Protect the optical interface
prepare.detail: Handle the removed sensor so its gel pack can be inspected without introducing dirt or additional damage.

steps.title: Expose and disconnect the sensor
steps.body: Remove the rain-sensor cover, then disconnect its electrical connector to free the sensor from the vehicle wiring.

steps.title: Release the bracket retention
steps.body: Release the retaining-clip tabs and remove the sensor from its mounting bracket. The illustration identifies the tabs and withdrawal direction.

steps.title: Clean and inspect
steps.body: Clean foreign material from the windshield contact area with the specified cleaner. Inspect the gel pack. If it is damaged, install a new sensor rather than attempting a separate lens replacement.

steps.title: Mount and reconnect
steps.body: Place the sensor in the bracket, install its retaining clip and reconnect the electrical connector. Restore the cover after completing the sensor installation.

watchFor.title: Fallback wiping
watchFor.body: A fault in rain-sensitive operation can cause ordinary timed intermittent wiping, so continued blade movement does not establish that rain sensing works.

notes: The removal illustration shows left-hand drive; right-hand-drive removal is similar.

diagnostics.finding: The gel lens is missing or damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: The optical interface is compromised and may prevent rain sensing.
diagnostics.next: Replace the complete rain sensor.

diagnostics.finding: Rain response is absent but intermittent wiping remains.
diagnostics.meaning: The system may be in its fault fallback mode; operation also depends on feature configuration and switch selection.
diagnostics.next: Check that rain sensing is enabled and an auto/intermittent sensitivity setting is selected before attributing the complaint to the sensor.

verification.title: Check the installation
verification.body: Confirm clean glass, an intact gel pack, correct bracket seating, an installed retaining clip and a connected electrical connector.

verification.title: Record the operating result
verification.body: With rain sensing enabled and an auto/intermittent setting selected, confirm the moisture-dependent response. Record whether the original sensor was retained or replaced.

procedures.purpose: Rain-sensor removal, windshield cleaning, gel-pack inspection and installation.
Explain optical sensing, sensitivity selection and intermittent fallback behavior.

guides.title: Replace the windshield washer pump
guides.summary: Drain the washer reservoir, gain access behind the right-hand splash shield, and replace the pump before refilling and checking windshield washing.
guides.introduction: The washer pump sends cleaning fluid from the reservoir to the windshield. Its power comes through a relay inside the windshield wiper motor, following a request from the steering column control module. Replacement therefore addresses the pump itself; a windshield that receives no fluid does not, by itself, establish that the pump has failed.
guides.why: Siphoning the reservoir limits the fluid released when the hose and pump are removed, but residual fluid can still escape. Refilling before the first operation is especially important: the procedure warns that running the pump with an empty reservoir can cause premature pump failure.
searchTerms: washer pump behind right fender splash shield

when.summary: When the washer pump requires removal or replacement after the cause of the washer complaint has been established.
notes: Use the separate splash-shield and hose-coupling procedures for their access and release details.

prepare.title: Fluid handling
prepare.detail: Have a fluid suction gun and a means of collecting escaping washer fluid. The specified refill material is Motorcraft® Premium Windshield Wash Concentrate with Bitterant ZC-32-B2, specification WSS-M14P19-A.

prepare.title: Access and connection procedures
prepare.detail: Review [Fender Splash Shield](#/document/G1693247) and [Washer Hose Coupling](#/document/G1694647). Be able to complete the right-hand shield access before disturbing the pump.

steps.title: Empty the reservoir
steps.body: Use the fluid suction gun to siphon out the windshield washer fluid. Prepare to collect the fluid that remains around the pump and hose connection.

steps.title: Expose the pump
steps.body: Remove the right-hand fender splash shield using the [shield procedure](#/document/G1693247). This provides access to the reservoir-mounted pump and its electrical and fluid connections.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove
steps.body: Disconnect the pump electrical connector, then release the washer hose coupling using the [coupling procedure](#/document/G1694647). Remove the pump, following the upward direction shown in the [pump illustration](#/document/G1694629). Collect escaping fluid as the connections are opened.

steps.title: Install and refill before operation
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure to install the pump, reconnect the hose and electrical connector, and restore the splash shield. Fill the reservoir with the specified washer-fluid material before operating the pump.

watchFor.title: Residual fluid
watchFor.body: An emptied reservoir can still release fluid when the hose or pump is disconnected.

watchFor.title: An early function test
watchFor.body: Do not briefly run the pump to test the connection before refilling. The empty-reservoir warning applies to that operation too.

notes: The washer relay is part of the windshield wiper motor; it is not identified here as a separate relay to replace.

diagnostics.finding: The washer switch is operated but fluid does not reach the windshield.
diagnostics.meaning: The symptom alone does not distinguish the pump from the command, power or fluid-delivery path.
diagnostics.next: Establish the cause before selecting pump replacement; the component description explains the control path.

verification.title: Check fluid delivery
verification.body: With the reservoir filled, request windshield wash and confirm fluid reaches the windshield. Check the disturbed hose connection and pump seating for escaping fluid.

verification.title: Recognize the normal wipe sequence
verification.body: After the washer switch is released, the wipers perform 3 additional wipes. A later courtesy wipe may also occur if that feature is enabled.

procedures.purpose: Washer pump draining, removal, installation and specified refill material.
Remove and reinstall the right-hand fender splash shield for pump access.
Release and reconnect the washer hose coupling.
Explain washer pump control through the windshield wiper motor and normal post-wash wiping.

guides.title: Remove and replace the windshield washer reservoir
guides.summary: Drain the washer reservoir, remove it through the right-hand fender access and refill it before operating the pump.
guides.introduction: The windshield washer reservoir stores the fluid that the washer pump delivers to the windshield. Access is behind the right-hand fender splash shield. Removing the reservoir involves draining its contents, separating the pump connector and hose coupling, and releasing the hose-routing clips and mounting hardware. The pump receives its operating command through the windshield wiper system, so a lack of spray does not by itself identify a reservoir fault.
guides.why: Siphoning first reduces the amount of fluid released during disconnection, although some can still escape from the hose and reservoir. Restoring the hose routing and mounting keeps the assembly in its intended position. Refilling before the first pump operation is essential: running the pump with an empty reservoir can cause premature failure.

when.summary: When the reservoir requires replacement or removal for service.
notes: Establish the reason for removal before disturbing the assembly; the washer delivery system also includes a controlled pump and hose connections.

prepare.title: Prepare to remove and collect fluid
prepare.detail: Have a fluid suction gun and a means of collecting residual fluid when the hose coupling is disconnected.

prepare.title: Plan the access and reconnection work
prepare.detail: Use the right-hand fender splash-shield and washer hose-coupling procedures. Have tools suitable for the reservoir mounting hardware and its specified tightening torque.

prepare.title: Have the specified washer material ready
prepare.detail: The procedure specifies Motorcraft® Premium Windshield Wash Concentrate with Bitterant, ZC-32-B2, meeting WSS-M14P19-A.

steps.title: Siphon the reservoir
steps.body: Remove the washer fluid with the fluid suction gun before opening the connections. This limits spillage during the following operations.

steps.title: Open the right-hand fender access
steps.body: Remove the right-hand fender splash shield using the [splash-shield procedure](#/document/G1693247). This provides access to the reservoir and its connections.

steps.title: Disconnect the pump and fluid hose
steps.body: Be ready to collect escaping fluid. Disconnect the washer pump electrical connector, then separate the washer hose using the [hose-coupling procedure](#/document/G1694647).

steps.title: Release the reservoir
steps.body: Following the [reservoir procedure](#/document/G1694630), release the hose-routing clips, remove the mounting bolts and nut, and remove the reservoir. The illustration identifies these retention points.

steps.title: Reinstall the assembly
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Secure the reservoir mounting bolts and nut to 52 lb.in (5.9 Nm), restore the hose-routing clips, reconnect the hose coupling and pump connector, and reinstall the splash shield.

steps.title: Refill before testing
steps.body: Fill the reservoir using the specified washer material before operating the washer pump. Only then request windshield washing to check delivery.

watchFor.title: Fluid remaining after siphoning
watchFor.body: Draining the reservoir does not eliminate all fluid at the hose connection. Keep collection equipment in place during separation.

watchFor.title: An early functional test
watchFor.body: Do not operate the pump to check the electrical connection while the reservoir is empty.

notes: The mounting torque is stated in pound-inches, with its metric equivalent; do not confuse it with pound-feet.

diagnostics.finding: The windshield receives no washer fluid.
diagnostics.meaning: Delivery depends on fluid availability, the pump and its control path as well as the hose connection.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the cause before replacing the reservoir. If delivery remains absent after correct refilling and reconnection, continue washer-system diagnosis.

verification.title: Check the restored assembly
verification.body: Confirm mounting hardware is tightened, hose-routing clips are restored and the hose and electrical connectors are secured.

verification.title: Confirm filled-system operation
verification.body: After filling, operate the washer control and confirm fluid reaches the windshield. Check the disturbed coupling and reservoir area for escaping fluid.

procedures.purpose: Drain, remove, reinstall and refill the windshield washer reservoir, including mounting torque and pump protection.
Remove and reinstall the right-hand fender splash shield for reservoir access.
Separate and reconnect the washer hose coupling without guessing its release method.

guides.title: Replace the windshield wiper motor
guides.summary: Remove the wiper linkage assembly, separate its links and motor bracket carefully, and install the replacement motor.
guides.introduction: The windshield wiper motor drives the linkage that moves the wiper arms. It also contains operating logic and sensors that monitor arm position, so it does more than simply turn when power is applied. The motor controls wiping modes and the washer relay. Replacement involves removing the linkage assembly and separating the motor from it.
guides.why: The link seals need protection when the links are detached from the motor crank. Damage here can leave poor wiper performance even after the motor has been replaced. Electrical control also matters: high speed has a separate fail-safe command path, so unusual operation does not automatically prove that the motor itself has failed.
searchTerms: wipers only work on high speed
rain sensing wipers use intermittent mode

when.summary: When diagnosis has established that the windshield wiper motor requires replacement.
notes: Identify whether the vehicle has ordinary intermittent or rain-sensitive wipers when assessing the original complaint.

prepare.title: Plan removal of the complete linkage
prepare.detail: Follow the separate [wiper linkage assembly procedure](#/document/G1694633) for access and removal. The motor procedure starts with that assembly removed.

prepare.title: Prepare for careful link and bracket work
prepare.detail: Provide a suitable working area for the removed assembly and fastening equipment capable of applying the motor-bracket torque. Identify both links and their seals before separating them.

steps.title: Remove the wiper linkage assembly
steps.body: Complete the linked assembly-removal procedure before beginning motor separation. This provides access to the links, motor crank and mounting bracket as an assembly.

steps.title: Separate the links from the motor crank
steps.body: Remove the left-hand link, followed by the right-hand link. Protect the link seals throughout separation; the [motor procedure](#/document/G1694635) specifically warns that seal damage can impair wiping.

steps.title: Remove the motor bracket
steps.body: Remove the bracket mounting bolts, then slide the bracket out in the illustrated direction. Keep this sliding movement distinct from removing the motor itself.

steps.title: Separate and replace the motor
steps.body: Remove the windshield wiper motor from the linkage assembly. Install the replacement by reversing the removal sequence, restoring the motor, bracket and link connections.

steps.title: Secure the bracket and reinstall the assembly
steps.body: Tighten the motor-bracket mounting bolts to 115 lb.in (13 Nm). Complete reinstallation using the separate linkage-assembly procedure, which governs the assembly's return to the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Damaged link seals
watchFor.body: Treat any seal damage during separation as a concern requiring attention before the assembly is returned to service.

watchFor.title: Confusing a feature fault with a motor fault
watchFor.body: Rain-sensitive operation can fall back to ordinary intermittent wiping when a rain-sensing fault is detected.

notes: The bracket torque applies to the motor-bracket mounting bolts; do not transfer it to other linkage or vehicle fasteners.
The steering column control module sends normal commands over the Local Interconnect Network, abbreviated LIN.

diagnostics.finding: High-speed wiping works while other modes do not.
diagnostics.meaning: High speed has a direct ground-command fail-safe path that bypasses the motor's normal LIN-controlled logic.
diagnostics.next: Consider command and communication faults before treating this behavior as proof of a failed motor.

diagnostics.finding: Rain-sensitive wiping has changed to timed intermittent operation.
diagnostics.meaning: This is the described fallback behavior for a rain-sensitive feature fault.
diagnostics.next: Investigate that feature rather than selecting a motor solely from this symptom.

verification.title: Check the completed mechanical assembly
verification.body: Confirm that the bracket is secured, both links are reattached with their seals protected, and linkage installation is complete.

verification.title: Check and record the affected function
verification.body: Compare the original complaint with operation after installation. Check the relevant mist, low, high, washer and intermittent or rain-sensitive functions against their described behavior.

procedures.purpose: Motor separation from the removed linkage assembly and reverse-order installation, including bracket torque and seal precautions.
Required removal and reinstallation of the complete wiper linkage assembly.
Operating behavior used to distinguish command, rain-sensing and motor concerns and to assess the repaired function.

guides.title: Remove and refit the windshield wiper arms
guides.summary: Remove the wiper arms with a two-leg puller, establish the motor’s PARK position, and align the blades with the windshield marks.
guides.introduction: The windshield wiper arms connect the motor-driven pivots to the blades that clear the glass. Their installed position determines where the blades rest when the motor parks. This job removes and refits those external arms; correct alignment matters just as much as securely tightening their retaining nuts.
guides.why: The motor has its own position monitoring and operating logic. Its PARK position must be established before the arms are aligned, otherwise correctly tightened arms can still leave the blades resting in the wrong place. The specified puller releases each arm at its pivot without relying on levering against nearby bodywork.

when.summary: When a wiper arm requires removal, replacement, or correction of its installed position.
notes: An operating fault does not by itself establish that a wiper arm needs replacement.

prepare.title: Have the puller and tightening equipment ready
prepare.detail: Use a two-leg puller, suitable tools for the nut covers and retaining nuts, and a torque wrench capable of the specified nut setting.

prepare.title: Identify the alignment marks
prepare.detail: Locate the blade-position marks on the windshield before refitting. The hood is omitted from the illustration for clarity; hood removal is not a listed operation.

steps.title: Expose and remove the retaining nuts
steps.body: Remove the wiper pivot-arm nut covers, then remove the nuts. This releases the fasteners that hold the arms on their pivots, but the arms may still need the specified puller to separate them.

steps.title: Pull the arms from their pivots
steps.body: Use the two-leg puller to remove the windshield wiper pivot arms, following the arrangement illustrated in the linked procedure. Keep the extraction force at the arm-to-pivot connection.

steps.title: Establish the motor’s PARK position
steps.body: Before installing either arm, turn the ignition ON and use the wiper switch to run one complete cycle. Allow the motor to finish in PARK. This gives the blade alignment a defined starting position.

steps.title: Align and secure the arms
steps.body: Install the arms with the blades inside the windshield marks. Fit and tighten the retaining nuts to 26 lb.ft (35 Nm). Turn the ignition OFF, then reinstall the nut covers.

watchFor.title: Positioning before the motor has parked
watchFor.body: Do not use an arbitrary motor stopping point to establish blade alignment. Complete the prescribed parking cycle first.

notes: Rain-sensitive wiping, where fitted, changes how wiping is requested; it does not replace the mechanical blade-alignment step.

diagnostics.finding: The motor reaches PARK but the blades sit outside the windshield marks.
diagnostics.meaning: The installed arm position needs checking.
diagnostics.next: Refit and align the arms using the prescribed PARK-position sequence.

verification.title: Confirm the installed position
verification.body: Check that both blades remain inside their windshield marks after the nuts are tightened.

verification.title: Confirm the fastening sequence is complete
verification.body: Verify the retaining nuts received the specified torque, the ignition is OFF, and the nut covers are installed.

procedures.purpose: Complete wiper-arm removal and installation, including puller use, motor parking, blade alignment and nut tightening.

guides.title: Remove and replace the windshield wiper linkage
guides.summary: Position the wiper motor crank for removal, replace or refit the linkage, and restore motor PARK before installing the wiper arms.
guides.introduction: The wiper linkage transfers motion from the windshield wiper motor to the wiper pivots, producing the sweep across the glass. The motor mounts to this assembly and also contains the control logic for wiping. This job removes the linkage from beneath the cowl and includes additional motor-separation work only when installing a new component.
guides.why: Crank position matters twice, for different reasons. The specified removal position provides access to the mounting bolts and allows linkage separation. Before the wiper arms are installed, the motor must instead be returned to PARK; otherwise the arms can be damaged. Starting all mounting bolts finger-tight also allows the assembly to seat before final tightening.

when.summary: When linkage removal is required or diagnosis has identified a need to replace the wiper linkage assembly.
notes: A change in wiping modes can originate in the controls or communication system; it does not by itself identify a linkage fault.

prepare.title: Prepare cowl access and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Follow the Cowl Panel Grille removal and installation procedure. Have suitable tools for the linkage and motor-bracket fasteners and a torque wrench.

prepare.title: Plan the powered positioning stage
prepare.detail: The procedure intentionally operates the wiper motor before removal. Keep clear of the moving mechanism and complete the required ignition-OFF step before unfastening the assembly.

steps.title: Expose the linkage
steps.body: Remove the cowl panel grille using [Cowl Panel Grille](#/document/G1693246). The hood is shown removed for illustration clarity; the linkage procedure does not direct hood removal.

steps.title: Position the motor crank
steps.body: Follow [Wiper Linkage Assembly](#/document/G1694633): switch the ignition ON and select continuous wiping. Follow its crank-positioning step to reach the specified 270-degree down position, then switch the ignition OFF. This position is required for bolt access and linkage removal from the motor.

steps.title: Remove the assembly
steps.body: Remove the linkage mounting bolts, disconnect the windshield wiper motor electrical connector and remove the linkage assembly. Keep the installation-specific mounting sequence in the linked procedure available for refitting.

steps.title: Separate the motor only for new-component installation
steps.body: When installing a new component, remove the left-hand link from the motor crank, followed by the right-hand link. Remove the motor-bracket mounting bolts, slide the bracket out, then separate the linkage assembly from the motor. Reverse these operations during assembly; the bracket-bolt torque is 115 lb.in (13 Nm).

steps.title: Install and secure the linkage
steps.body: Position the assembly and reconnect the motor electrical connector. Install all mounting bolts finger-tight before final tightening, following the individual bolt sequence in the installation procedure. Tighten the linkage mounting bolts to 80 lb.in (9 Nm).

steps.title: Restore PARK and finish reassembly
steps.body: Return the windshield wiper motor to PARK before installing the wiper pivot arms. Complete the remaining removal steps in reverse, using the cowl procedure for the access parts. Do not use the removal crank position as the arm-installation setting.

watchFor.title: Arms installed before motor PARK
watchFor.body: The procedure specifically warns that this can damage the wiper pivot arms.

watchFor.title: Unnecessary motor separation
watchFor.body: Link removal, bracket removal and separation from the motor are conditional steps for installing a new component.

notes: The motor’s control electronics and the mechanical linkage have different roles; replacing the linkage does not address every possible wiping complaint.

diagnostics.finding: High-speed wiping works during a communication fault.
diagnostics.meaning: The system has a separate high-speed fail-safe signal from the steering column control module that bypasses normal motor control logic.
diagnostics.next: Continue control and communication diagnosis rather than identifying the linkage from this symptom alone.

diagnostics.finding: Equipped rain-sensitive wipers revert to intermittent operation.
diagnostics.meaning: A detected rain-sensitive-system fault can produce this default behavior.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the rain-sensitive function before deciding that mechanical linkage replacement is justified.

verification.title: Confirm assembly and arm installation
verification.body: Confirm connector reconnection, specified fastening and that motor PARK was established before the pivot arms were installed.

verification.title: Check operation
verification.body: Confirm the wipers respond to the requested wiping mode and return to PARK after operation.

procedures.purpose: Linkage removal, conditional motor and bracket transfer, installation fastening sequence and mandatory PARK prerequisite.
Required cowl panel grille removal and installation for access to the wiper linkage.

guides.title: Diagnose an inoperative convertible top and latch or cover warnings
guides.summary: Trace roof operation, window feedback and latch or tonneau-cover signals to distinguish an operating restriction from a wiring, sensor or control fault.
guides.introduction: The roof uses two synchronized electric motors with built-in controllers: Moveable Roof Control Module A (MRCMA) and Module B (MRCMB). They coordinate roof movement with the windows, latch and optional tonneau covers. This diagnosis establishes which required condition or signal is missing before a component is replaced.
guides.why: A roof that refuses to move may be responding correctly to an installed cover, an unreleased latch or missing window feedback. A fault code identifies a condition to investigate; it does not by itself prove that a sensor or motor has failed.
searchTerms: windows do not lower with convertible top

when.summary: Use when roof movement fails, window lowering is missing, latching is difficult or a roof warning persists.
notes: Confirm the complaint is present before following a component-replacement decision.

prepare.title: Prepare for electrical diagnosis
