prepare.detail: Use a Ford-capable diagnostic scan tool, a digital multimeter, Wiring Diagrams Cell 103 and the specified terminal-safe probe adapters. Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%.

prepare.title: Understand the test conditions
prepare.detail: This work requires network testing, live-data interpretation and isolated-circuit measurements. Follow each test's ignition and connector-disconnection instructions; never force probes into terminals.

steps.title: Separate operating restrictions from installation concerns
steps.body: Remove tonneau covers before attempting closure and check battery junction box fuses 15 and 17. For difficult latching, inspect latch, front-striker and top installation. For a security warning, check alignment with the roof closed but unlatched, then latch it correctly.

steps.title: Begin Test A with communication and fault codes
steps.body: Run the Network Test for both roof modules, Body Control Module B (BCMB), the gateway module, Body Control Module (BCM) and powertrain control module. Diagnose any nonresponding module first. Retrieve and record their self-test results, including the powertrain key-on, engine-off test. Resolve codes before continuing, prioritizing circuit faults.

steps.title: Check the information permitting roof movement
steps.body: Follow Test A's live-data branches. Accessory delay must be Active and vehicle speed below 5 km/h (3 mph). Opening requires the latch released and the windows lowered, with both rear windows reporting fully down. Hold the roof switch throughout operation. A latch-state mismatch in MRCMA leads to Test C; a mismatch in MRCMB leads to Test D. Cover-state errors lead to Test B.

steps.title: Follow Test A's switch and window branches
steps.body: The switch parameter identifications, or PIDs, should become Active when pressed and Inactive when released. A continuously Active input leads to Test E; an always-Inactive input requires switch-signal and ground-continuity checks before switch replacement. Missing rear-window feedback requires open-circuit and ground-short checks before replacing the affected motor. If inputs pass, inspect the specified connectors for intermittent faults.

steps.title: Run Test B for tonneau-cover sensor faults
steps.body: A cover-sensor fault may permit opening but prevent closing. Clear the affected module's codes, cycle ignition OFF–ON and, with the roof open, hold UP for 2 seconds. Self-test both roof modules. Returning B1070:12 or B1070:29 starts battery-short testing; B1070:14 starts ground-short testing. MRCMA monitors the left sensor; MRCMB monitors the right.

steps.title: Run Test C for latch-sensor faults
steps.body: A latch-sensor fault may permit closing but prevent opening. Clear MRCMA codes, cycle ignition OFF–ON and, with the roof closed, hold DOWN for 2 seconds. Self-test MRCMA. Returning B1078:12 or B1078:29 starts battery-short testing; B1078:14 starts ground-short testing. The latch switch belongs to the latch/striker assembly.

steps.title: Complete the appropriate sensor-circuit branch
steps.body: In Tests B and C, repair unwanted voltage or failed circuit-isolation checks. The :12 and :14 branches reach sensor replacement only after their specified checks pass. The :29 branch continues through battery-short, ground-short, continuity and signal-to-supply isolation checks before replacement. Use the exact connector tables and limits. If the code does not return, inspect the relevant sensor and module terminals for corrosion, displaced pins or poor fit.

watchFor.title: A speed warning while stationary
watchFor.body: Investigate vehicle-speed data and network faults through the engine-appropriate electronic engine controls procedure; the warning does not establish a roof-motor failure.

watchFor.title: Windows that do not lower
watchFor.body: Record BCMB and MRCMA codes. Missing rear-window full-down feedback can prevent roof movement even when the roof motors are serviceable.

notes: Use the diagnostic chart's separate routes for switch, communication and rear-window feedback codes; these can require testing beyond Tests A–C.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1240:1C is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The monitored latch-sensor signal is below its limit. A sensor-supply fault can prevent roof operation.
diagnostics.next: Continue with Test D; do not infer a failed latch switch from this code alone.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0604:44, P0605:45 or P062F:46 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The reporting roof module detected a memory fault.
diagnostics.next: Clear codes and repeat its self-test after the specified ignition cycle. P062F:46 requires ignition OFF for 20 seconds. Replace that module only if the code returns.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U2011:64 or U3000:49 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These indicate motor-signal plausibility and internal electronic faults respectively.
diagnostics.next: Clear codes and command roof movement with ignition ON. U2011:64 directs replacement if the roof remains inoperative; U3000:49 requires a returning code during the subsequent self-test.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U2011:98 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The reporting motor or system is overheated.
diagnostics.next: Allow at least 2 minutes to cool, clear the code and retry. If operation fails, self-test. A returning code requires ignition OFF and another 2-minute cooling period before clearing and retesting; otherwise investigate other codes and operating conditions.

verification.title: Recheck the original complaint
verification.body: Repeat the relevant roof command and self-tests. Cover PIDs should be Active with covers installed and Inactive with them removed; remove covers before closing.

verification.title: Verify a security-message complaint
verification.body: After confirming alignment and fully latching the roof, test-drive above 5 km/h (3 mph). If the warning does not return, explain the correct latching procedure.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Retain initial and returning codes, the reporting module, relevant PID states and circuit findings. Record whether the concern was reproduced or remains intermittent.

procedures.purpose: Roof symptom and code charts, Test A operation checks, Test B cover sensors and Test C latch-sensor diagnosis.
Electrical diagnostic prerequisites, probe handling and valid circuit measurements.
Roof-motor coordination, window interlocks and sensor operation.
Tonneau-cover sensor replacement when Test B directs it.
Front-striker and latch-switch service when Test C directs replacement.
Roof activation-switch replacement after Test A circuit checks.
Convertible rear-quarter window motor replacement after feedback-circuit diagnosis.
Roof motor/module replacement when the diagnostic chart confirms that decision.
2.3L electronic engine controls diagnosis for vehicle-speed or powertrain faults.
3.7L electronic engine controls diagnosis for vehicle-speed or powertrain faults.
5.0L electronic engine controls diagnosis for vehicle-speed or powertrain faults.

applicability.equipment: Convertible, with or without optional tonneau covers

guides.title: Diagnose convertible-top supply, switch and communication faults
guides.summary: Use roof-module fault codes to distinguish sensor-supply problems, switch-circuit faults and missing network messages.
guides.introduction: The convertible top uses two smart electric motors, called Moveable Roof Control Modules A and B (MRCMA and MRCMB). They coordinate roof movement and wait for operating permissions, including confirmation that the rear windows are down. These checks establish whether a roof that will not move lacks electrical supply, receives an incorrect switch command or is missing information from another module.
guides.why: A stopped roof does not necessarily mean a failed motor. Wiring faults, low supply voltage and missing messages can prevent operation. Testing those inputs first avoids replacing a module that is correctly responding to another problem.

when.summary: Use when roof operation is faulty and the recorded codes lead to Pinpoint Tests D, E, F or G.
notes: Operation requires active accessory delay and speed below 5 km/h (3 mph). Opening requires the latch released; closing requires optional tonneau covers removed.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical and module-diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting network tests, module self-tests and live data, a digital multimeter, correct terminal probe adapters and good lighting. Configuration work requires access to vehicle-specific service information and as-built data.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge greater than 70%. Review previous repairs. Follow each test's ignition and connector-isolation instructions; resistance measurements require an unpowered, isolated circuit.

steps.title: Select the returning fault
steps.body: Record diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Test D clears MRCMA codes, cycles the ignition and repeats its self-test. Test E does this for both roof modules and attempts opening and closing before repeating self-tests. If codes do not return, inspect the specified sensor, switch and module connectors for intermittent damage.

steps.title: Test D: establish sensor-supply wiring integrity
steps.body: For returning P1240:1C, follow D2–D4 in the linked diagnostic procedure. With ignition off and the specified components disconnected, check all listed supply paths for continuity, then shorts to ground. Required results are less than 3 ohms along the paths and greater than 10,000 ohms to ground. Repair failures and inspect every intervening connector before reconnecting.

steps.title: Test D: separate low module power from low sensor voltage
steps.body: Seat and latch the connectors, switch ignition on and record battery voltage. Read the latch-sensor voltage parameter identification (PID), LTCH_SNSR_V, and module-supply PID, VOLT_SUPPLY. Both above 9 volts indicate correct operation at that time. Supply above 9 volts with latch voltage at or below 9 volts leads to a bulletin check, then MRCMA replacement if no bulletin applies. Low supply leads to D6: ignition off, module disconnected and battery junction box fuse 17 removed. Failed feed continuity requires wiring repair; a passing feed directs battery and charging diagnosis.

steps.title: Test E: isolate the roof-switch command
steps.body: B1267:24 and U2013:64 start with the UP circuit; B1268:24 starts with DOWN. With ignition off, disconnect the switch and relevant module, then test the command wire to ground. Resistance must exceed 10,000 ohms. Repair a failing circuit. For U2013:64, check both circuits before condemning the switch. Passing applicable checks lead to switch replacement through the overhead-console procedure.

steps.title: Tests F and G: establish communication
steps.body: For U0140:00, network-test the body control module (BCM) and gateway module (GWM). For U0142:00, test body control module B (BCMB). Resolve failed communication first. Record, clear and retest the specified roof-module codes after an ignition cycle. If the code returns, Test F checks gateway faults before BCM faults; Test G checks BCMB faults.

steps.title: Check replacement history and connections
steps.body: If those modules have no directing faults, verify recent replacement parts and programmable module installation configuration. Correct suspect configuration using as-built data. Return swapped modules to their original vehicles and obtain new replacements. Recheck operation. If the concern remains, switch ignition off and inspect the prescribed module and intervening connectors; repair corrosion or damaged, displaced or spread terminals.

steps.title: Compare communication faults across modules
steps.body: Reconnect and latch everything, then self-test all modules and record continuous-memory codes. Check applicable technical service bulletins before the final decision. U0140:xx beyond the roof modules leads to the vehicle identification number (VIN)-specific BCM routine; roof-only occurrence leads to MRCMA replacement. U0142:xx outside MRCMA leads to BCMB replacement; occurrence only in MRCMA leads to MRCMA replacement. Follow any applicable bulletin instead.

watchFor.title: Terminal damage during testing
watchFor.body: Oversized probes can spread terminals and create a new intermittent fault. Use the correct adapters and repair the underlying connector damage.

watchFor.title: A code that disappears
watchFor.body: Nonreturning communication codes can reflect heavy network traffic or an intermittent condition. Historical codes alone do not justify module replacement.

notes: The overhead roof switch sends ground commands: UP to MRCMA and DOWN to MRCMB. The modules exchange switch status over the medium-speed controller area network.
Charging-system diagnosis must match the fitted engine; the linked 3.7L procedure applies only to that engine.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1267:24 or B1268:24 returns.
diagnostics.meaning: The respective module detected an UP or DOWN ground command lasting longer than 30 seconds.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test E to distinguish a grounded command wire from a faulty switch.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U2013:64 returns.
diagnostics.meaning: Both modules detected ground commands simultaneously, which normal switch operation cannot produce.
diagnostics.next: Check both command circuits through Test E.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0140:00 returns.
diagnostics.meaning: A roof module is missing accessory-delay or ignition-status information from the BCM.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test F through network, configuration and connector checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0142:00 returns.
diagnostics.meaning: MRCMA is missing the rear-window-down status message from BCMB.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test G; this does not by itself prove a window motor has failed.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0294:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: MRCMA is missing vehicle-speed information from the powertrain control module.
diagnostics.next: Continue vehicle-speed message and network diagnosis. Tests D–G do not establish a replacement decision for that module.

verification.title: Confirm the relevant result
verification.body: Repeat the applicable self-test and operating check. In Test D, confirm both voltage PIDs meet the stated threshold; after configuration or connector corrections, determine whether roof operation has recovered.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic endpoint
verification.body: Retain battery voltage, voltage-PID readings and module-by-module code results. Distinguish restored operation from a referral for further diagnosis or replacement.

guides.title: Diagnose convertible-top communication and rear-window feedback faults
guides.summary: Trace roof-module communication faults and missing rear-window-down signals before deciding whether wiring, configuration or a motor module needs repair.
guides.introduction: The convertible top uses smart motors containing Moveable Roof Control Module A (MRCMA) and Moveable Roof Control Module B (MRCMB). They exchange messages to coordinate movement. Body Control Module B (BCMB) confirms that both rear windows are fully lowered before roof movement continues. These tests distinguish missing network messages from faulty window-position feedback.
guides.why: A window can move correctly while its feedback circuit fails. Likewise, a communication code can result from connections or incorrect module configuration. Checking these paths protects the windows and avoids unnecessary module replacement.

when.summary: When roof operation fails with communication or rear-window-down feedback codes.
notes: Operation requires active accessory delay and speed below 5 km/h (3 mph). Release the latch before opening; remove fitted tonneau covers before closing. Hold the roof switch during movement.

prepare.title: Prepare for electrical diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use a network-capable diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter, Rotunda Flex Probes, suitable mating terminals, wiring diagrams and good lighting. Configuration checks require module-programming capability. Check charging-system operation and battery state of charge above 70%.

steps.title: Check communication for the selected test
steps.body: With ignition on, run the Network Test. Test H requires the Powertrain Control Module (PCM) and Gateway Module A (GWM) to pass; I requires MRCMB; J requires MRCMA. Diagnose failed network communication before continuing.

steps.title: Establish whether the code returns
steps.body: For H and I, self-test MRCMA; for J, self-test MRCMB. Record all diagnostic trouble codes, clear them, cycle ignition off and on, then repeat the self-test. A code that does not return may reflect intermittent communication or high network traffic.

steps.title: Check other modules and recent repairs
steps.body: For a returning code, H checks GWM codes, then PCM codes; I checks MRCMB codes; J checks MRCMA codes. Diagnose those faults first. Review relevant module replacements, verify part fitment and programming, and correct suspect configuration using as-built data. Return borrowed modules to their original vehicle and obtain correct new replacements. Operate the roof again.

steps.title: Inspect connections before choosing a module
steps.body: If the symptom persists, switch ignition off. Inspect both roof-module connectors and their intervening connectors; H also includes PCM connections. Replace corroded or damaged terminals, correct pushed-out pins and spread contacts, and clean module pins as directed. Reconnect everything securely, then self-test all modules and record memory codes. Apply the H/I/J decisions below only after checking applicable technical service bulletins; follow a matching bulletin instead.

steps.title: Reproduce rear-window feedback faults with Test K
steps.body: Diagnose roof-module codes before BCMB codes. Clear BCMB codes, cycle ignition, attempt roof operation for at least 10 seconds, then self-test BCMB. If the listed feedback codes do not return, inspect BCMB and both rear-window motor connectors for intermittent faults. Route other BCMB codes to its diagnostic procedure.

steps.title: Separate window movement from feedback
steps.body: Operate the rear windows using the master window switch. Diagnose inoperative windows first. If they work, follow K4 for stuck-low codes or K5 for stuck-high codes. Switch ignition off and disconnect BCMB and the affected motor before using the specified pins for resistance measurements.

steps.title: Complete the feedback terminal checks
steps.body: When circuit resistance passes, follow K6: inspect connectors and use a suitable mating terminal to identify enlarged or deformed contacts. Repair defective connections. Only when these checks pass does K direct replacement of the affected rear-window motor through its removal and installation procedure.

watchFor.title: An intermittent code is not a replacement verdict
watchFor.body: Do not replace a module when the concern is absent during testing.

watchFor.title: Window-switch inhibition can be normal
watchFor.body: Rear-window controls are disabled while the roof is between its fully open and fully closed positions.

notes: Use the fitted engine’s procedure for PCM diagnosis or replacement. Roof-motor and rear-window-motor replacement are separate procedures.

diagnostics.finding: MRCMA records diagnostic trouble code U0294:00.
diagnostics.meaning: Test H investigates communication involving the PCM and gateway.
diagnostics.next: At H7, U0294:xx in other modules directs PCM replacement; otherwise it directs MRCMA replacement, subject to the preceding checks and bulletin search.

diagnostics.finding: MRCMA records diagnostic trouble code U020A:00.
diagnostics.meaning: Convertible-top status messages from MRCMB are missing.
diagnostics.next: At I6, U020A:xx elsewhere directs MRCMB replacement; otherwise it directs MRCMA replacement.

diagnostics.finding: MRCMB records diagnostic trouble code U0207:00.
diagnostics.meaning: Convertible-top status messages from MRCMA are missing.
diagnostics.next: At J6, U0207:xx elsewhere directs MRCMA replacement; otherwise it directs MRCMB replacement.

diagnostics.finding: BCMB records B126E:23 or B126F:23.
diagnostics.meaning: Right or left feedback remains low with accessory delay off, suggesting a short to ground.
diagnostics.next: K4 requires resistance to ground greater than 10,000 ohms; otherwise repair the circuit. A passing result leads to K6.

diagnostics.finding: BCMB records B126E:24 or B126F:24.
diagnostics.meaning: Right or left feedback fails to confirm fully down within 10 seconds, suggesting an open circuit.
diagnostics.next: K5 requires end-to-end resistance below 3 ohms; otherwise repair the circuit. A passing result leads to K6.

verification.title: Confirm the observable result
verification.body: After configuration or connection corrections, operate the system and establish whether the original symptom remains.

verification.title: Retain the diagnostic record
verification.body: Record initial and returning codes, all-module comparison results and feedback-circuit measurements supporting the repair decision.

guides.title: Adjust the convertible top front latch
guides.summary: Correct excessive latch-to-striker distance by adjusting the latch linkage, then restore the front trim and handle.
guides.introduction: The front latch mechanically secures the raised convertible top. Its linkage includes an adjustable ball socket that changes the arm length, a jam nut that holds the setting and a clip that retains the ball joint. This job adjusts that linkage after measuring its relationship to the striker.
guides.why: The measured distance determines whether adjustment is justified. Correct linkage length allows the latch to reach its intended engagement position, while the tightened jam nut and retained ball joint keep that setting secure.

when.summary: Adjust when the measured latch-to-striker distance is greater than 13.5 mm.
notes: A completed adjustment must measure less than 13.5 mm.

prepare.title: Measurement and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have suitable metric measuring equipment, tools for the handle, trim retainers and jam nut, and a torque tool suitable for the trim and handle fasteners.

prepare.title: Position the roof for access
prepare.detail: Keep the vehicle stationary with accessory delay active for roof operation. Release the latch before lowering the roof; remove tonneau covers, if fitted, before raising it. The adjustment uses an approximately 25 percent open position.

steps.title: Establish whether adjustment is required
steps.body: Measure the distance between the latch and striker using the front latch adjustment procedure. Proceed when it exceeds 13.5 mm. Keep the initial measurement so the effect of changing the linkage can be checked.

steps.title: Expose the latch linkage
steps.body: Lower the latch handle and turn it clockwise to release the top. Open the top approximately 25 percent, then remove the handle. Remove the front trim retainers, release the clips beneath the back of the trim and lift the trim away. This exposes the linkage for adjustment.

steps.title: Change the arm length
steps.body: Pull the ball-joint retaining clip and release the ball joint. Loosen the jam nut, then turn the ball socket to adjust the arm length. Use the measured result to guide the adjustment; the procedure does not specify a fixed number of turns.

steps.title: Measure and secure the adjustment
steps.body: Remeasure the latch-to-striker distance and establish a value below 13.5 mm. Tighten the jam nut, reinstall the ball joint and install its clip. The nut holds the adjusted length; the clip retains the joint.

steps.title: Restore the access parts
steps.body: Follow the front-panel procedure's trim restoration sequence: position the trim, engage its rear clips and install the front retainers. Tighten these to 2.8 Nm, then install the latch handle and tighten its fastener to 3.5 Nm.

watchFor.title: A reading at the limit
watchFor.body: Exactly 13.5 mm does not meet the completed-adjustment requirement of less than 13.5 mm.

watchFor.title: An unsecured joint
watchFor.body: Do not overlook the ball-joint clip or leave the jam nut loose after setting the arm length.

notes: The partially open service position provides slack in the top material and surrounding components.

diagnostics.finding: The latch-to-striker distance exceeds 13.5 mm.
diagnostics.meaning: The specified condition for front latch adjustment is present.
diagnostics.next: Adjust the ball socket and verify the resulting distance.

diagnostics.finding: The message center displays TOP NOT SECURE.
diagnostics.meaning: The system reports that the raised top's latch is not fully engaged under the message's operating conditions; the message alone does not identify a linkage-length fault.
diagnostics.next: Check full latch engagement and measure the latch-to-striker distance before choosing adjustment.

verification.title: Record the final measurement
verification.body: Record the initial and final latch-to-striker distances. The final adjustment must be below 13.5 mm.

verification.title: Confirm restoration and engagement
verification.body: Confirm the jam nut, ball-joint clip, trim and handle are secure. Close the top, pull it down to position the latch and turn the handle counterclockwise to secure it fully.

procedures.purpose: Measure and adjust the convertible top front latch linkage.
Restore the front-panel trim and latch handle with their specified fastening torques.

guides.title: Replace convertible top material with the early tension-cord arrangement
guides.summary: Remove and refit the convertible roof covering while preserving its tension-cord routing, cable paths and weatherstrip alignment.
guides.introduction: The convertible top material forms the roof's outer covering. Crossbows, tension cords, cables and edge attachments support its shape as the roof moves. Replacing it requires removing the complete top assembly and headliner, then carefully separating the covering from the frame before rebuilding those attachments.
guides.why: Cord routing and clip positions determine how the covering follows the frame. Drilling beyond a rivet head can enlarge a linkage hole and compromise the replacement rivet. Recording alignment before dismantling makes accurate reassembly possible.
searchTerms: new convertible top hard to latch

when.summary: When the convertible top material requires replacement or removal for repair.
notes: Allow for the recommended uninterrupted closed-roof break-in period after fitting new material.

prepare.title: Arrange roof assembly access
prepare.detail: Be equipped to remove and reinstall the complete top assembly and headliner using the linked procedure.

prepare.title: Gather tools and attachment materials
prepare.detail: Use an electric drill, 4.2 mm drill bit, pneumatic rivet gun, vacuum cleaner and small flat-bladed screwdriver. The specified black multigrip blind rivets are 4 mm in diameter, 15 mm long, with an 11 mm head diameter. Standard double-sided tape can retain crossbow-flap alignment.

steps.title: Remove the roof and preserve alignment references
steps.body: Remove the convertible top assembly, then the headliner. Before removing the front-panel side weatherstrip and bracket assemblies, mark their positions at the retainers and record any shim locations. Work through corresponding attachments on both sides and disconnect the rear-window defrost harness.

steps.title: Release the glass supports and crossbow flaps
steps.body: Press the rear-glass tension-rod retainer tabs with the small screwdriver, then pull the rod from the glass frame. Remove the material push pins behind the front panel. Peel each retaining flap from its crossbow tape; its holes must later align with the rivet holes used for the headliner.

steps.title: Detach the early-production tension cords
steps.body: Record the cord and nylon-strap routing through the frame. Drill only the rivet heads securing the front and center sets, then disconnect the attachments. Do not drill the D-ring retaining rivet; route the tension cord through the D-ring. Vacuum away all rivet shavings from the top assembly.

steps.title: Free the front covering and cable ends
steps.body: Pull the material backward and downward from the front-panel underside clips. Peel it from the tape on both sides, roll it forward and upward over the panel, then fold it back to the first crossbow. Disconnect the front tension-cable ends. If reusing the covering, attach a draw string before withdrawing each cable so it can be pulled back through during installation.

steps.title: Release the rear edge and floating bow
steps.body: Remove the rear-panel lower weatherstrip using its linked procedure. Release the five indicated edge-trim locations beneath it and pull the covering outward. Note the tension-cable routing, then withdraw the cable's front end from the material while leaving the cable attached to the frame. Release the covering from the floating bow and recover its retaining clips.

steps.title: Rebuild the attachments in reverse order
steps.body: Transfer parts as necessary. Place the floating-bow clips on the covering in their proper positions, restore cable routing and reconnect the front cable ends. Restore edge trim, weatherstrip, front clips and taped attachments. Route cords and nylon straps exactly as removed and install the specified rivets. Align crossbow-flap holes, using tape to hold them if helpful. Restore push pins, tension rods, defrost connections, bracket marks and shims; complete headliner and roof installation.

steps.title: Close the roof and allow the material to settle
steps.body: After completing installation and operating checks, leave new material latched and closed for at least 1 week straight. Higher initial latching effort is expected while the material stretches. Opening the roof during this period may lengthen break-in.

watchFor.title: Damaged rivet holes
watchFor.body: Stop drilling once the rivet head is removed. The drill must not pass through the linkage.

watchFor.title: Lost routing or clip positions
watchFor.body: Do not improvise cable paths or floating-bow clip placement. Restore the recorded arrangement.

notes: This roof uses the early tension-cord procedure. The later tension-strap arrangement requires its matching production procedure.

verification.title: Check attachment restoration
verification.body: Confirm routing, clip positions, aligned flap holes, bracket marks, shim locations and defrost connections. Ensure no rivet shavings remain.

verification.title: Confirm normal roof movement before break-in
verification.body: Operate while stationary with accessory delay active, holding the switch. The windows must lower before roof movement. Release the latch before lowering and remove tonneau covers, if fitted, before raising.

verification.title: Record the closed-roof period
verification.body: Record when the new covering was left fully closed and latched so the uninterrupted break-in period can be observed.

procedures.purpose: Complete top-material removal and reverse-order installation using the early tension-cord branch.
Required top assembly and headliner access, removal and restoration.
Rear-panel lower weatherstrip removal and installation for covering-edge access.

applicability.equipment: Convertible with the early tension-cord roof arrangement

guides.title: Remove, strip and refit the SVT Performance Package front bumper cover
guides.summary: Remove the GT-350 or GT-350R bumper cover, dismantle its attached trim and grilles, and reinstall it with the correct splitter arrangement.
guides.introduction: The front bumper cover carries grilles, air ducts, turn-signal supports and several trim pieces. Replacing the cover can therefore involve transferring much more than its painted shell. This job joins vehicle removal, bench disassembly, reassembly and refitting into one path, with separate splitter-removal branches for GT-350 and GT-350R vehicles.
guides.why: The cover is located by alignment pins and retained at several edges. Releasing those attachments in sequence protects the cover and fender brackets. The splitter arrangements differ, and their fasteners must remain associated with the correct locations and tightening instructions.

when.summary: When the bumper cover or its attached grilles, ducts and trim require removal, repair or replacement.
notes: Identify the GT-350 or GT-350R splitter arrangement before beginning.

prepare.title: Arrange safe lifting and wheel removal
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the specified lifting points, identified by the stamped triangles. Check adapter and underbody clearance; never lift against a bumper or work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare for a large, lightly supported assembly
prepare.detail: Arrange an assistant for cover removal, as illustrated. Have suitable fastener tools and torque equipment, and keep screws, clips, push pins and J-nuts grouped by location.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle and remove the front wheels
steps.body: Follow the lifting and wheel procedures to gain access to the liners, splitter attachments and lower cover fasteners. Confirm clearance before positioning the hoist adapters.

steps.title: Remove the correct splitter arrangement
steps.body: For GT-350, remove the specified screw groups from the outside toward the center, then slide the center splitter forward. Through that opening, remove the outer splitter screws and J-nuts. Release both sets of push pins on each side, move the liners aside after removing their retainers, then remove the clips and outer splitters. For GT-350R, follow its outside-to-center screw sequence, remove the screw covers and additional screws, release the push pins, liner retainers and clips, then remove the remaining center screws and slide the center splitter forward.

steps.title: Release the cover's remaining attachments
steps.body: Remove the underbody shield front screws and disconnect the electrical connectors on both sides. Remove each fender-bracket attachment bolt and separate the cover from the bracket. Release the top outer attachments, moving the hood-seal edges aside to reach the bolts, then remove the remaining cover screws.

steps.title: Lift the cover clear and inspect its supports
steps.body: With an assistant, lift the cover up off its alignment pins before pulling it forward from the vehicle. Inspect the fender-bracket teeth. If required, remove the bracket bolts and bracket for replacement.

steps.title: Begin bench disassembly
steps.body: Following the disassembly procedure, remove each air duct and its pin-type retainer, then the bumper reinforcement retainers and reinforcement. On both sides, remove the turn-signal assembly brackets by removing the outer and inner screws and releasing the tabs. Release the turn-signal trim panels and lower radiator grille from their tabs.

steps.title: Remove the remaining trim and seal
steps.body: On both sides, remove the bumper-cover trim panels, upper radiator grille trim panels and upper grille panels using their specified screws and tabs. Release the hood-seal trim pins and remove the seal. Remove the license plate bracket and screws if equipped.

steps.title: Reassemble the cover
steps.body: Reverse the bench disassembly sequence. Seat the locating tabs and trim pins and use the specified tightening values for each screw group so the panels and brackets are secured correctly.

steps.title: Refit the assembled cover
steps.body: Reverse the applicable vehicle-removal sequence, locating the cover on its alignment pins and restoring the fender attachments, upper fasteners, electrical connections, shield, liners and splitter components. Follow the GT-350 or GT-350R fastening details, then reinstall the wheels using their procedure.

watchFor.title: Damaged fender-bracket teeth
watchFor.body: Inspect these while the cover is off; damaged locating teeth need attention before refitting.

watchFor.title: Different screw groups
watchFor.body: Splitter, cover and trim fasteners have different tightening values. Do not apply one value throughout the assembly.

notes: Instructions marked for both sides apply to both sides, even when only one side is illustrated.

diagnostics.finding: Fender-bracket teeth are damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: The cover's side locating attachment requires attention.
diagnostics.next: Use the bracket removal branch and replace the bracket if required before installing the cover.

verification.title: Confirm complete reassembly
verification.body: Check that the alignment pins, side brackets, trim tabs, hood seal and applicable splitter attachments are engaged, and that both electrical connections have been restored.

verification.title: Record bracket condition
verification.body: Record the fender-bracket inspection result and any bracket replacement before completing the job.

SVT Performance Package bumper-cover bench disassembly and assembly.

guides.title: Remove, strip and rebuild the front bumper cover
guides.summary: Remove the front bumper cover, inspect its fender attachments and transfer its grilles, lamp brackets, seal and fitted spoiler components.
guides.introduction: The front bumper cover forms the outer front body surface and carries several attached pieces, including the grilles, fog-lamp brackets and lower spoiler. A cover replacement therefore involves vehicle removal followed by bench disassembly and reassembly. The lower-spoiler work branches according to whether the vehicle has the base or performance spoiler.
guides.why: The cover is retained around the wheel openings and upper edge, and it must lift off alignment pins before moving forward. Its fender-bracket teeth also need inspection because damaged engagement points can undermine refitting. On the bench, releasing each clip or tab avoids loading an attachment that is still locked.

when.summary: When the front bumper cover or its attached components need replacement, repair access or transfer.
notes: Identify the fitted spoiler before planning the bench work; the performance branch includes a riveted reinforcement.

prepare.title: Safe lifting and wheel access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the specified lifting points, identified by stamped triangles. Check adapter clearance from suspension, brackets and other underbody parts. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack or apply lifting pressure to either bumper.

prepare.title: Assistance and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Arrange a second person for cover removal, as shown in the illustration. Have tools for screws, bolts, push pins and clips, plus a torque wrench suitable for the small fastener specifications.

prepare.title: Performance-spoiler capability
prepare.detail: If fitted, provide the capability to remove and restore the spoiler-reinforcement rivets when reversing the disassembly sequence.

steps.title: Expose the lower attachments
steps.body:
Before lifting, use a hard, level surface, set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. Confirm the jack or hoist is rated for the vehicle, including cargo and modifications. If using a jack, support the vehicle on suitable stands at the designated points before going underneath; a jack alone is not a support. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

Raise the vehicle following the [lifting overview](#/document/G1663631), then remove the [front wheels and tires](#/document/G1686507). Remove the lower air deflector's push pins and screws, followed by the deflector.

steps.title: Release both wheel-opening areas
steps.body: Remove the indicated push pins on both sides and move the inner fender liners aside. Disconnect the electrical connectors, then remove each cover-to-fender-bracket bolt and separate the cover from its bracket. The halogen fog-lamp view also represents the similar LED arrangement.

steps.title: Release the upper attachments
steps.body: Remove the radiator sight shield and its push pins. Remove the license plate bracket and screws if fitted. Move aside the outer ends of the hood seal and remove the bolt on each side.

steps.title: Lift the cover off its alignment pins
steps.body: With assistance, remove the remaining cover screws. Lift the cover upward off the alignment pins, then pull it forward off the vehicle. Follow this order in the [removal and installation procedure](#/document/G1694213).

steps.title: Inspect the fender brackets
steps.body: Inspect the bracket teeth for damage before reusing the attachments. If required, remove the bracket bolts and the affected bracket using the conditional branch in the removal procedure.

steps.title: Strip the shared cover components
steps.body: Following the [disassembly and assembly procedure](#/document/G1694220), release the cover-reinforcement clips and remove the reinforcement. On both sides, remove the fog-lamp bracket screws, release the tabs and remove the brackets. Release the upper and lower grille tabs, remove both grilles, then remove the hood seal.

steps.title: Remove the fitted spoiler
steps.body: For either spoiler version, remove the lower spoiler's bolts and push pins and remove the spoiler. For the performance spoiler, additionally remove the rivets and spoiler reinforcement. Keep this extra operation within the performance branch.

steps.title: Reassemble and reinstall
steps.body:
Reverse the applicable bench sequence, then reverse vehicle removal. Restore the alignment-pin engagement, fender attachments, electrical connections, seals, shields, liners and wheels. Use each procedure's individual fastener torque; the cover screws, bracket fasteners and lamp-bracket screws do not all share one setting.

Once the cover, connected components and wheels are restored, make sure the parking brake is applied before lowering. Restore the wheel restraints as the wheels return to the ground, and keep the vehicle restrained while completing the [wheel-installation tightening procedure](#/document/G1686507). Do not lower an unrestrained vehicle in Neutral.

watchFor.title: Pulling forward too soon
watchFor.body: The cover must first lift free of its alignment pins.

watchFor.title: Unreleased bench attachments
watchFor.body: Fog-lamp brackets use both screws and tabs; removing only the screws does not complete their release.

notes: The vehicle's emergency tire-changing jack is not intended to hoist the vehicle for this work.

diagnostics.finding: Damaged fender-bracket teeth
diagnostics.meaning: The cover's side attachment requires attention before reinstallation.
diagnostics.next: Use the conditional bracket-removal operation and resolve the damaged attachment before fitting the cover.

verification.title: Check the restored assembly
verification.body: Confirm that the fitted spoiler branch is fully assembled and that all removed electrical connectors, cover attachments, trim pieces and wheels are restored.

verification.title: Record bracket inspection
verification.body: Record the condition of both fender-bracket tooth sets and any bracket replacement performed.

guides.title: Remove and overhaul the SVT Performance Package rear bumper cover
guides.summary: Remove the rear bumper cover, inspect its mounting brackets and transfer or service its lamps, wiring, reinforcements and lower cover.
guides.introduction: The rear bumper cover carries more than its visible exterior surface. Its assembly includes wiring, lamps, reflectors, a decklid release switch, exhaust outlet heat shields and reinforcing pieces. This job combines vehicle removal with bench disassembly and reassembly, allowing those components to be separated from the cover and restored in a controlled sequence.
guides.why: The cover remains electrically connected after its mounting clips are released. Optional cellular antenna cables also pass through the body and must be disconnected first. Damaged mounting brackets can affect how the cover is retained, so inspecting them is part of removal rather than an optional cosmetic check.

when.summary: When the rear bumper cover or its attached components require removal, replacement or bench service.
notes: Identify the fitted fender lip mouldings, any cellular antennas and the vehicle build date before choosing the relevant branches.
Cellular antenna operations apply only to equipped vehicles; the performance package alone does not establish their presence.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and wheel access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the specified lifting points. Check adapter clearance, never lift against a bumper and never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare for a complete cover strip
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for screws, nuts, push pins, pin-type retainers and releasable tabs, plus torque equipment for the small fasteners. Keep the different fasteners associated with their components.

steps.title: Open the wheel-arch access
steps.body: Raise the vehicle, remove the specified push pins and retainers, then remove the rear wheels and tires. On both sides, release the fenderliner retainers, push pins and screw, and move each liner aside.

steps.title: Remove mouldings, lamps and optional antenna connections
steps.body: Use the small- or large-fender-lip-moulding branch to remove the mouldings on both sides. Remove the rear lamp assemblies. Where cellular antennas are fitted, disconnect each antenna cable from the harness and push its grommet through the body.

steps.title: Release and disconnect the cover
steps.body: Release the cover sides from their brackets, then release its center from the rear brackets. Position the cover aside only far enough to access the electrical connector. Disconnect it before removing the cover completely.

steps.title: Inspect the mounting brackets
steps.body: Inspect the side and rear brackets for damage. Remove brackets only if required. The before-28-Feb-2018 branch uses screws for the side, outer rear and center rear brackets. The after-28-Feb-2018 branch also uses pin-type retainers; its right outer rear bracket requires release of the wiring-harness connector retainer. Follow the matching fastening specifications.

steps.title: Remove the harness and upper attachments
steps.body: On the removed cover, disconnect the harness connectors, release its guides and remove the harness. Release the rear bumper reinforcement tabs. Where fitted, remove the cellular antenna screws and antennas on both sides.

steps.title: Separate the lamps, switch and shields
steps.body: Release the tabs for both license plate lamps and the decklid release switch. Remove both exhaust outlet heat shields, then release both side marker lamps. Remove each rear reflector's nut and release its tabs. Unscrew and remove the reversing lamp.

steps.title: Separate the lower cover
steps.body: Remove the lower reinforcement screws and clips, then the reinforcement. Remove the lower bumper cover screws and release its tabs. The lower cover is now separated without pulling against its remaining retainers.

steps.title: Reassemble the cover
steps.body: Reverse the bench-disassembly sequence. Restore the lower cover, reinforcements, lamps, reflectors, switch, heat shields and any antennas. Route the wiring through its guides and reconnect its electrical connections.

steps.title: Refit the assembly to the vehicle
steps.body: Reverse vehicle removal: reconnect the cover harness, restore the bracket engagement and reconnect any antenna cables and body grommets. Reinstall the rear lamps, mouldings, fenderliners, retainers and wheels using their respective procedures.

watchFor.title: Wiring still attached
watchFor.body: Releasing the cover from the body brackets does not disconnect its harness. Preserve access to that connector before moving the cover away.

watchFor.title: Mixed retention methods
watchFor.body: Some parts use tabs alone; others combine tabs with screws or nuts. Release every specified attachment before separating the component.

notes: Bracket fastening arrangements change across the stated production-date branches; do not select a torque solely by bracket appearance.

diagnostics.finding: A side or rear mounting bracket is damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: The cover's supporting attachment requires attention in addition to the cover itself.
diagnostics.next: Use the applicable build-date branch for bracket removal and restoration.

verification.title: Confirm complete reassembly
verification.body: Check that harness guides, electrical connectors, lamps, shields, reinforcements and lower-cover retainers have all been restored. On antenna-equipped vehicles, include both cables and grommets.

verification.title: Record the bracket inspection
verification.body: Record the side and rear bracket condition, any replacement performed and the build-date branch used.

guides.title: Remove, strip and rebuild the rear bumper cover
guides.summary: Remove the rear bumper cover, inspect its mounting brackets, transfer its electrical and trim components, then rebuild and reinstall it.
guides.introduction: The rear bumper cover is the exterior panel around the rear of the car. Its assembly includes a cover reinforcement, wiring, lamps, reflectors, a decklid release switch and park aid sensors. Renewing or rebuilding the cover therefore involves both vehicle removal and bench disassembly. The GT version adds a separate lower-cover removal stage.
guides.why: The cover is retained by screws, push pins and bracket engagements, with electrical connections released at different stages. Supporting it while those connections are exposed prevents the wiring from carrying the panel. Bracket inspection is equally important: refitting a cover over damaged mountings leaves the underlying attachment problem unresolved.

when.summary: When the rear bumper cover needs replacement, rebuilding or removal for access to its attached components.
notes: The separate lower bumper cover disassembly branch applies to GT vehicles.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting and assistance
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and identify the correct lifting points by their stamped triangles. Have a second person available for cover removal. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack; floor stands are required when supporting a raised vehicle with that method.

prepare.title: Protect the vehicle during lifting
prepare.detail: Do not lift against either bumper or use the emergency tire-change jack for this work. Check drive-on clearance and position hoist adapters clear of suspension, exhaust, steering parts, mounting brackets, the axle and rear cover.

prepare.title: Prepare for access and stripdown
prepare.detail: Have suitable screw, nut and retainer tools and low-range torque equipment. Be able to complete the linked wheel-and-tire and rear-lamp procedures, and keep the different attachment groups organized.

steps.title: Raise the vehicle and release the initial attachments
steps.body: Follow [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631), then the opening sequence in [Rear Bumper Cover removal](#/document/G1694215). Remove the push pins and screws. On both sides, disconnect the rear bumper harness connector and separate its wiring guide.

steps.title: Complete wheel and lamp access
steps.body: Remove the rear wheels and tires using [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507). Remove the specified screw and pushpins on both sides, then the cover-to-bracket screws. Remove the rear lamp assemblies using [Rear Lamp Assembly](#/document/G1694124).

steps.title: Release and remove the cover
steps.body: Release the cover sides from their brackets first, then its center from the rear brackets. Position it aside for access to the remaining bumper wiring connector and disconnect it. With assistance, remove the cover.

steps.title: Inspect the mounting brackets
steps.body: Inspect both side brackets and the rear brackets for damage. When required, follow the removal instructions for the side, outer rear or center rear brackets. Resolve mounting damage before reinstalling the cover.

steps.title: Remove reinforcement, wiring and sensors
steps.body: Follow [Rear Bumper Cover disassembly](#/document/G1694221). Separate the harness guides from the cover reinforcement, remove its pin-type retainers, release its tabs and remove it. Disconnect the harness connectors and guides to remove the harness, then remove the rear park aid sensors.

steps.title: Strip the lamps and remaining fittings
steps.body: Remove the reversing-lamp screws and lamp. Release the tabs for both license plate lamps and the decklid release switch. On both sides, remove the reflector nut, release its tabs and remove the reflector; then release the side-marker tab and remove the lamp.

steps.title: Remove the GT lower cover when applicable
steps.body: For GT vehicles, remove the lower bumper cover screws, release its tabs and remove the lower cover. This additional stripdown stage belongs to the GT branch.

steps.title: Rebuild and reinstall
steps.body: Reverse bench disassembly, then reverse vehicle removal. Reattach the wiring guides and connectors as their stages become accessible. Tighten reversing-lamp screws to 15 lb.in (1.7 Nm) and reflector nuts to 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm). Apply 13 lb.in (1.5 Nm) to the cover and bracket screw groups identified with that value in the removal procedure.

watchFor.title: An electrical connection still attached
watchFor.body: The early harness disconnections do not eliminate the later connector-access step. Support the cover until that remaining connection is released.

watchFor.title: Tabs pulled before release
watchFor.body: Reinforcement, lamps, reflectors and the GT lower cover use tab retention as well as their listed fasteners. Release each attachment before removing the part.

diagnostics.finding: A side or rear mounting bracket is damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: The cover's supporting attachment needs attention before reinstallation.
diagnostics.next: Use the appropriate side, outer rear or center rear bracket removal branch as required, and resolve the damage before fitting the cover.

verification.title: Record bracket condition
verification.body: Record the inspection result for both side brackets and the rear brackets, including any corrective work completed before the cover conceals them.

verification.title: Confirm complete reassembly
verification.body: Check that transferred components, reinforcement, wiring guides and connectors are restored; cover engagements and fasteners are secured; and rear lamps, wheels and tires have been reinstalled through their respective procedures.

guides.title: Remove and refit the front bumper beam with the SVT Performance Package
guides.summary: Remove the front bumper beam after clearing the cover, temperature-sensor bracket, air deflectors and wiring guides.
guides.introduction: On the 5.2L vehicle with the SVT Performance Package, the front bumper is the bolted cross-car member behind the outer bumper cover. Reaching it involves several surrounding pieces: the ambient air temperature sensor bracket, side air panels, radiator air deflector and wiring guides. The beam itself requires an assistant during removal.
guides.why: The air deflectors guide air around the radiator area, while the harness guides control the wiring route. Moving these parts clear before releasing the bumper allows the beam to come away without carrying attached wiring or panels with it. Correct reassembly restores both the bumper mountings and the surrounding air-management pieces.
searchTerms: SVT Performance Package front bumper beam

when.summary: When the front bumper beam requires replacement or removal as part of a front-end repair.
notes: Use the SVT Performance Package bumper-cover procedure for the initial access work.

prepare.title: Arrange an assistant
prepare.detail: Plan to support and handle the beam together while its retaining bolts are removed.

prepare.title: Prepare fastener tools
prepare.detail: Have tools for push pins, pin-type retainers and bolts, plus torque equipment for the distinct bumper and upper/lower air-deflector specifications.

steps.title: Remove the outer cover
steps.body: Follow the [SVT Performance Package front bumper cover procedure](#/document/G1794161). Once access is available, position the ambient air temperature sensor bracket aside to clear the following operations.

steps.title: Move the side air panels clear
steps.body: Remove the push pins. On both sides, release the pin-type retainers and position the air-deflector side panels aside. Keep these panels clear of the beam's removal path.

steps.title: Remove the radiator deflector and release wiring
steps.body: Remove the bolts and radiator air deflector, keeping track of upper and lower fastener positions because their installation torques differ. Separate the wiring harness guides before moving the bumper.

steps.title: Remove the beam and reverse the sequence
steps.body: With an assistant supporting it, remove the retaining bolts and front bumper as shown in the [bumper procedure](#/document/G1794160). Reinstall in reverse order. Tighten bumper bolts to 18 lb.ft (25 Nm), lower radiator-deflector bolts to 71 lb.in (8 Nm), and upper bolts to 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm). Restore the guides, side panels, sensor bracket and outer cover.

watchFor.title: Wiring guides still engaged
watchFor.body: The harness guides must be separated before the beam is removed; do not let the moving bumper pull on the harness.

watchFor.title: Upper and lower deflector fasteners
watchFor.body: Their torque specifications differ. Keep their positions identifiable throughout the job.

notes: The sensor bracket is positioned aside during this sequence; no separate sensor replacement is specified.

verification.title: Confirm complete restoration
verification.body: Check the bumper fastening, harness guides, radiator deflector, both side panels, sensor bracket and outer cover against the reverse removal sequence.

verification.title: Record fastening completion
verification.body: Record completion of the bumper-bolt tightening and the separate upper and lower radiator-deflector tightening operations.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L SVT Performance Package front bumper removal and installation, including deflectors and assistant handling.
SVT Performance Package front bumper cover removal and installation for beam access.

guides.title: Remove and refit the front bumper beam
guides.summary: Remove the front bumper beam after clearing its cover, wiring guides and any fitted grille-shutter or adaptive-cruise hardware.
guides.introduction: The front bumper beam is the transverse structural member behind the outer bumper cover. Removing it involves more than exposing its mounting bolts: sensor brackets, wiring guides and optional equipment occupy the same working area. This job provides the route for beam replacement or removal for access.
guides.why: Clearing the attached equipment first prevents the beam from pulling on wiring as it comes away. Its width also makes controlled support important; plan removal and installation as a two-person operation.

when.summary: When the front bumper beam requires replacement or must be removed for access.
notes: Check whether active grille shutters or adaptive cruise control are fitted before planning the work.

prepare.title: Arrange support and fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have a second person available to support the beam and a torque wrench suitable for its mounting bolts.

prepare.title: Allow for the access procedures
prepare.detail: The bumper cover comes off first. If fitted, the grille shutters and cruise control module with its bracket each require their own removal and installation procedure.

steps.title: Remove the outer cover
steps.body: Follow the [front bumper cover procedure](#/document/G1694213) to expose the beam. Keep the distinction between the cover and the bolted beam clear when identifying the parts being removed.

steps.title: Clear the sensor bracket and optional equipment
steps.body: Position the ambient-air-temperature sensor bracket and wiring-harness guide aside. Remove the [active grille shutter assembly](#/document/G1693244), if fitted. If adaptive cruise control is fitted, remove the [cruise control module and bracket](#/document/G1693160). Complete these access operations before releasing the beam.

steps.title: Separate the guides and remove the beam
steps.body: Separate the wiring-harness guides. With both people supporting the beam, remove the eight illustrated mounting bolts and take the beam away. Keep the displaced wiring clear as the assembly moves.

steps.title: Refit in reverse order
steps.body: Position the beam and install its bolts, tightening them to 18 lb.ft (25 Nm). Reassemble the harness guides, then restore any removed cruise-control and grille-shutter assemblies using their procedures. Return the ambient sensor bracket and wiring guide to position and reinstall the bumper cover.

watchFor.title: A remaining attachment
watchFor.body: If the beam is still restrained after unbolting, check the guides and surrounding equipment before moving it farther.

watchFor.title: Optional equipment affects the work
watchFor.body: Removing a cruise-control module or grille-shutter assembly adds its complete installation procedure to this job.

notes: The beam mounting torque given alongside removal is the installation tightening value.

verification.title: Confirm the beam and surrounding equipment are restored
verification.body: Confirm all eight beam bolts are tightened, the harness guides are joined, the ambient sensor bracket is back in position and every applicable equipment procedure is complete before finishing the cover installation.

procedures.purpose: Front bumper beam removal and installation.

guides.title: Remove and replace the rear bumper beam
guides.summary: Remove the correct rear bumper cover, exchange the bolted bumper beam, and restore the cover attachments and electrical connections.
guides.introduction: The rear bumper in this procedure is the transverse beam behind the exterior bumper cover. The cover must come off before the beam’s mounting bolts are accessible. Although the beam itself has a short removal sequence, the cover access depends on vehicle equipment. Standard, SVT Performance Package and GT500 covers have separate procedures; the detailed access route described here is for the SVT Performance Package.
guides.why: The cover is retained at its sides and rear and also has an electrical connection. Where cellular antennas are fitted, their cables pass through the body and must be released before the cover is removed. Damaged cover brackets also need attention during the job: installing a beam does not correct a damaged cover mounting. Optional bracket removal varies with vehicle build date.

when.summary: When the rear bumper beam requires removal or replacement and the correct cover access procedure is available.
notes: Select the cover procedure by fitted equipment before beginning.
The SVT cover instructions below are not a substitute for the separate standard or GT500 cover procedures.

prepare.title: Arrange access capability
prepare.detail: The SVT cover procedure requires a vehicle hoist, rear wheel and tire removal, fenderliner access and rear lamp removal. Follow the referenced lifting and component procedures.

prepare.title: Identify conditional equipment
prepare.detail: Identify the fitted fender lip mouldings, any cellular antennas and the vehicle build date if cover brackets need removal.

prepare.title: Prepare fastening tools
prepare.detail: Have tools for the cover retainers and beam bolts, including a torque wrench. Use the separate specifications for the beam, mouldings and applicable bracket branch.

steps.title: Open the SVT cover access route
steps.body: For an SVT Performance Package vehicle, follow its [rear bumper cover procedure](#/document/G1794162). Raise the vehicle on a hoist, remove the specified push pins and pin-type retainers, and remove the rear wheels and tires.

steps.title: Release the wheel-opening attachments
steps.body: On both sides, remove the fenderliner retainers, push pins and screw, then position the liner aside. Remove the screws and fender lip moulding using the branch for the fitted small or large moulding.

steps.title: Remove lamps and release antenna wiring
steps.body: Remove the rear lamp assemblies. If cellular antennas are fitted, disconnect the right-hand and left-hand antenna cables from the wiring harness and push their grommets through the body.

steps.title: Detach the cover
steps.body: Release the cover sides from their brackets, then release its center from the rear brackets and position it aside for connector access. Disconnect the electrical connector before removing the cover completely.

steps.title: Inspect the cover brackets
steps.body: Inspect the side and rear brackets for damage. Remove brackets only if required, following the branch for builds before or after 28-Feb-2018. The later branch includes pin-type retainers and separate left- and right-hand outer-bracket instructions; the right-hand operation also releases the wiring-harness connector retainer.

steps.title: Exchange the bumper beam
steps.body: Follow the [rear bumper procedure](#/document/G1694214): remove its bolts and the beam. Install in reverse order, tightening the beam bolts to 18 lb.ft (25 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the cover assembly
steps.body: Reverse the applicable cover procedure. Restore any removed brackets, reconnect the cover wiring and fitted antenna connections, and refit the cover, lamps, mouldings, liners, retainers and wheels using their own procedures and specifications.

watchFor.title: Wiring still attached
watchFor.body: The cover must remain positioned for access until its electrical connector is disconnected. Fitted antenna cables require their separate release steps.

watchFor.title: Mixed bracket specifications
watchFor.body: Do not apply the beam-bolt torque to cover brackets or transfer bracket instructions between build-date branches.

notes: The SVT cover procedure includes later build-date and optional antenna branches; apply them only when they match the vehicle.

diagnostics.finding: A side or rear cover bracket is damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: The cover mounting requires attention in addition to the beam work.
diagnostics.next: Use the applicable optional bracket-removal branch and address the damage before final cover installation.

verification.title: Confirm beam installation
verification.body: Verify that the beam bolts have been tightened to 18 lb.ft (25 Nm).

verification.title: Confirm cover restoration
verification.body: Check that the inspected brackets, cover attachments, electrical connector and any disconnected antenna cables and grommets are restored.

guides.title: Diagnose seatbelt latching, retraction and warning faults
guides.summary: Check belt condition, buckle operation and retractor locking behavior, then route warning-light and chime complaints to the appropriate diagnosis.
guides.introduction: A seatbelt must latch securely, take up slack and lock when vehicle movement demands restraint. All retractors have emergency locking operation. Passenger belts also use automatic locking retractor (ALR) mode to secure child seats. This job distinguishes normal locking behavior, routing interference and mechanical faults from problems with the warning system.
guides.why: A belt that feels tight may simply be in ALR mode, while poor retraction can come from twisted webbing or misplaced trim. Checking these causes before testing the mechanism avoids confusing an installation problem with a failed retractor.

when.summary: When a belt binds, stays slack, latches poorly, or its warning indicator, chime or Belt-Minder behaves incorrectly.
notes: Select the functional test that matches the complaint and the seating position.

prepare.title: Inspect before testing
prepare.detail: Examine webbing for tears, fraying, cuts or stretching, and inspect the buckle and tongue. Check routing and surrounding trim before attributing resistance to the retractor.

prepare.title: Arrange a controlled road-test location
prepare.detail: The locking test requires competent vehicle control and a safe area with dry concrete or an equivalent hard surface. Maximum braking must never be attempted on wet pavement or gravel.

steps.title: Correct external interference
steps.body: For extraction difficulty, consider a web-sensing lock, ALR operation or incorrectly installed trim. For slow retraction or slack, inspect for twists and routing problems. Use the dedicated releasing, tongue-rotation or belt-guide procedure as appropriate; correct trim interference before judging the mechanism.

steps.title: Test the buckle and tongue
steps.body: Insert the tongue without excessive effort, listen for the latch click and pull forcefully on the webbing to confirm retention. Fully press the release button; it should operate without excessive effort and release the tongue easily. Repeat this sequence 3 times. A concern directs replacement of the buckle or retractor as required.

steps.title: Check full extraction and retraction
steps.body: Move the webbing between full extension and its stowed position. It must operate freely without excessive effort or binding. The functional test directs a new retractor if a concern is found or the complaint is verified.

steps.title: Check passenger-belt ALR engagement and release
steps.body: Set an adjustable backrest fully upright and any fitted shoulder-height adjuster fully up or down. Fasten the belt, fully extract it to activate ALR, and let it retract until it stops. Pull to confirm it remains locked. Then unfasten and fully stow it; normal extraction must return. Failure to lock or to leave ALR mode requires a new retractor.

steps.title: Perform the retractor road test
steps.body: Fasten the belts without excessive torso slack and proceed to the safe area. At 24 km/h (14.9 mph), grasp the shoulder harness, lean forward and make a maximum braking application without a skid. Do not jerk the webbing. Each tested belt should lock with minimal extension; replace any retractor that fails to lock.

steps.title: Separate warning faults from mechanical faults
steps.body: For warning complaints, note the airbag-indicator state and follow the diagnostic routing below. Check whether Belt-Minder is activated before investigating an electrical failure. Use the [complete seatbelt tests](#/document/G1883856) for the applicable functional sequence.

watchFor.title: A click does not complete the buckle test
watchFor.body: The forceful webbing pull checks retention after latching; easy insertion alone does not establish that the tongue is held securely.

watchFor.title: Damage and dirt need different responses
watchFor.body: Torn, frayed, cut or stretched webbing is a condition concern. Cleaning or correcting a twist does not resolve damaged webbing.

notes: Use the dedicated Seatbelt Cleaning procedure for soiled webbing.
Passenger Belt-Minder depends on the occupant classification system detecting a passenger above its programmed threshold. MyKey prevents Belt-Minder deactivation.

diagnostics.finding: The seatbelt warning indicator or chime does not operate, and the airbag warning indicator is off.
diagnostics.meaning: The complaint follows the instrumentation and warning-system diagnostic path.
diagnostics.next: Use Instrumentation, Message Center and Warning Chimes diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: The seatbelt warning chime does not operate, and the airbag warning indicator is illuminated.
diagnostics.meaning: The complaint requires supplemental restraint system diagnosis.
diagnostics.next: Follow Airbag Supplemental Restraint System diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Belt-Minder is inoperative.
diagnostics.meaning: The feature may be deactivated, or a wiring or connector concern may be present.
diagnostics.next: Activate it if deactivated; if already active, continue with instrumentation diagnosis.

verification.title: Confirm the relevant functional result
verification.body: Confirm secure latching and easy release, free webbing travel, correct ALR engagement and release where applicable, and successful locking of every retractor included in the road test.

verification.title: Record results by seating position
verification.body: Record the original complaint, corrected routing or trim issue, tests performed and each belt's result. Identify any failed component requiring replacement.
