guides.title: Release a seatbelt locked in its stowed position
guides.summary: Use the appropriate front or rear slack-release sequence, escalating to anchor access or retractor replacement only if the belt remains locked.
guides.introduction: A seatbelt retractor stores webbing on a spool and locks it when restraint is needed. A belt that retracts quickly can sometimes remain locked when stowed without the retractor having failed. Returning a little webbing to the spool may release it. The front and rear procedures create that slack differently, then require a restraint functional test.
guides.why: Only a few millimeters of inward webbing movement may be needed, so controlled feeding is central to this repair. Being able to pull the belt out afterward does not establish that its protective locking functions work correctly. Persistent locking has a defined escalation path rather than calling for immediate replacement.

when.summary: When seatbelt webbing will not extract from its fully stowed position.
notes: Rapid retraction can cause this temporary condition.
Distinguish it from normal automatic locking after a passenger belt has been fully extended.

prepare.title: Identify the seating position and equipment
prepare.detail: Choose the front or rear sequence. Use shoulder-height adjustment or rear-backrest reclining only where actually fitted.

prepare.title: Plan any escalation
prepare.detail: Anchor or pretensioner detachment requires restraint-service capability and the applicable removal and installation instructions, including their safety prerequisites and fastener specifications. Have the appropriate Seatbelt Systems functional test available.

steps.title: Front belt: use the height adjuster where fitted
steps.body: Slowly lower the shoulder-height adjuster so webbing feeds back onto the spool, then try extracting the belt slowly. If the adjuster is already fully down, or this does not release the belt, continue with the pull-and-feed sequence.

steps.title: Front belt: create and return slack
steps.body: Firmly pull out as much belt as possible. Slowly feed the resulting slack into the retractor, then slowly try extracting the belt. If it releases, proceed to restoration and testing. If it remains locked, use the anchor-access stage below.

steps.title: Rear belt: use the seatback to create slack
steps.body: Slowly pull the belt out as far as possible. Compress the backrest foam and recline the rear backrest if equipped, allowing more webbing to return to the spool. Slowly feed in the slack and check whether the belt extracts.

steps.title: Rear belt: repeat with a firm pull
steps.body: If the initial rear sequence does not release the belt, firmly extract as much webbing as possible. Slowly return the slack, then slowly extract the belt again. If it releases, proceed to restoration and testing.

steps.title: Obtain additional slack through the appropriate anchor procedure
steps.body: For a still-locked front belt, follow the applicable procedure to remove the fastener and detach the anchor or anchor-and-pretensioner. For a rear belt, follow its anchor procedure. An inflatable-belt union is a separate equipment-dependent branch requiring confirmed applicability and its own procedure. Feed the freed slack inward, then retry extraction.

steps.title: Restore the attachment or replace the retractor
steps.body: If the belt now extracts, reinstall every removed fastener and tighten to the applicable specification. If it still does not extract after the anchor-slack stage, install a new retractor using the correct removal and installation procedure.

steps.title: Perform the restraint functional test
steps.body: Carry out the appropriate Seatbelt Systems functional test after restoration or replacement. Follow the [release procedure](#/document/G1883858) through this final check; successful webbing release alone is not the completion criterion.

watchFor.title: Confusing automatic locking with a fault
watchFor.body: Passenger-belt Automatic Locking Retractor (ALR) mode engages after full extension and clicks during retraction. Allowing the belt to retract fully disengages this child-seat locking mode.

watchFor.title: Assuming equipment from an illustration
watchFor.body: The illustrated shoulder adjuster is a typical arrangement. It does not establish the equipment fitted to a particular Mustang.

notes: Emergency Locking Retractor (ELR) operation responds to vehicle movement such as hard braking or cornering; use the specified functional test to assess it.

diagnostics.finding: The stowed belt releases after slack is fed inward.
diagnostics.meaning: The release sequence has relieved the locking condition.
diagnostics.next: Restore any disturbed attachments and perform the functional test.

diagnostics.finding: The belt remains locked after the applicable anchor-slack stage.
diagnostics.meaning: The prescribed release sequence has not restored extraction.
diagnostics.next: Replace the retractor, then complete the functional test.

verification.title: Mechanical restoration
verification.body: Confirm all removed attachments are restored and tightened to their applicable specifications.

verification.title: Recorded functional result
verification.body: Record the seating position, whether replacement was needed and the result of the appropriate restraint functional test.

procedures.purpose: Front and rear locked-retractor release sequences, escalation to replacement and required functional testing.
Explanation of emergency and automatic retractor locking modes and their functional-test distinctions.

guides.title: Clean seatbelt webbing safely
guides.summary: Clean fully extended seatbelt webbing using the solution recommended in the vehicle’s Owner’s Literature, without bleaching or re-dyeing it.
guides.introduction: Seatbelt webbing is the flexible part of the restraint that holds an occupant in place. Its retractor stores the unused length and can lock the belt during sudden vehicle movement. Cleaning cares for this load-bearing material, so the choice of cleaning product matters as much as the visible result.
guides.why: Bleaching or re-dyeing can weaken the webbing and increase the risk of serious injury or death in a crash. Fully extracting the belt before cleaning exposes its length for the procedure. The vehicle’s care instructions identify the recommended solution; the product manufacturer’s instructions govern its use.

when.summary: When seatbelt webbing needs cleaning.

prepare.title: Have the care instructions ready
prepare.detail: Locate the seatbelt-care information in the vehicle’s Owner’s Literature and obtain the recommended cleaning solution with its manufacturer’s instructions.

prepare.title: Allow access to the full belt
prepare.detail: Arrange access so the webbing can be fully extracted before any cleaning begins.

steps.title: Select the recommended solution
steps.body: Read the vehicle’s seatbelt-care instructions before choosing a product. Follow the cleaning-solution manufacturer’s directions for preparation and application; do not substitute an invented mixture or concentration.

steps.title: Fully extract the webbing
steps.body: Pull the seatbelt completely out of its retractor before starting the cleaning procedure. Cleaning only the length normally exposed across the seat does not meet this prerequisite.

steps.title: Clean according to the product instructions
steps.body: Use the recommended solution as directed, following any finishing instructions it specifies. Keep bleaching and re-dyeing out of the process, even if discoloration remains. The [seatbelt cleaning procedure](#/document/G1692223) provides the governing care requirements.

watchFor.title: Appearance is not a measure of strength
watchFor.body: A desire to restore the original color must not lead to bleaching or re-dyeing the webbing.

notes: Cleaning is separate from diagnosing a retractor operating concern; the system-operation article identifies the relevant functional tests.

diagnostics.finding: A passenger belt clicks while retracting and will not pull out again after full extraction.
diagnostics.meaning: Full extraction followed by retraction activates Automatic Locking Retractor (ALR) mode, used to secure a child seat.
diagnostics.next: Allow the webbing to retract fully to disengage ALR mode.

verification.title: Confirm the care sequence is complete
verification.body: Check that the belt was fully extracted before cleaning and that the recommended product’s application and finishing instructions were followed.

procedures.purpose: Seatbelt cleaning requirements and prohibited treatments.
Retractor operation, including passenger-belt ALR activation and release.

guides.title: Inspect seatbelts and verify replacement assemblies
guides.summary: Inspect seatbelt condition and mounting integrity, correct damage before replacement, and complete functional testing at every seating position.
guides.introduction: A seatbelt restrains an occupant through its webbing, retractor and attachment points. Those parts must work together: a replacement belt cannot restore protection if the body structure supporting it remains distorted. This job establishes the inspection and repair path, from checking belt condition through correcting damaged retaining areas and testing the finished system. It is especially important after severe loading or collision damage.
guides.why: Visible belt condition is only part of the assessment. The retaining areas carry restraint loads into the body, while the retractor must provide the correct locking behavior. Collision repairs require inspection and correction of all seatbelt components, and the final functional tests cover every seating position rather than only the assembly that was replaced.

when.summary: Inspect periodically, after severe belt loading, and as part of every collision repair.
notes: No fixed inspection interval is specified.
After a collision, use the dedicated Seatbelt Procedure After a Collision in addition to this maintenance path.

prepare.title: Choose the correct inspection route
prepare.detail: Establish whether the belts have experienced severe stress or a collision. Collision work requires the full post-collision inspection, with all seatbelt components corrected as required.

prepare.title: Arrange the necessary repair capability
prepare.detail: Have the appropriate replacement instructions and functional-test procedures available. Damaged or distorted retaining areas require body-repair capability sufficient to restore their original shape and structural integrity.

steps.title: Inspect condition and operation
steps.body: Follow [Seatbelt Maintenance](#/document/G1692224) to inspect the assemblies for damage and correct operating condition. Give particular attention to belts subjected to severe stress. Where the vehicle is undergoing collision repair, apply the dedicated post-collision procedure to all seatbelt components.

steps.title: Check the retaining areas before replacement
steps.body: Before installing a new assembly, inspect its retaining areas for damage and distortion. Restore affected sheet metal to its original shape and structural integrity before fitting the belt. Installing new restraint hardware is not a substitute for repairing its support.

steps.title: Include child-seat mounting areas when applicable
steps.body: If a child safety seat was in use during a collision, inspect its mounting areas and restore the original production configuration. The rear tether anchors form part of the parcel-shelf sheet metal; the lower anchors are located where the rear cushion and backrest meet.

steps.title: Install the required replacement assemblies
steps.body: Use the instructions appropriate to each new seatbelt assembly. This maintenance procedure establishes the required sequence but does not provide assembly-specific removal methods or fastener details.

steps.title: Functionally test every seating position
steps.body: Carry out the appropriate tests in [Seatbelt Systems diagnosis and testing](#/document/G1883856) for all seating positions. Use its prescribed retractor tests to assess locking operation, including the emergency-locking road-test inspection and passenger automatic-locking test where applicable.

watchFor.title: Distorted attachment structure
watchFor.body: The retaining area must regain structural integrity before a new belt is installed.

watchFor.title: Normal child-seat locking mistaken for a jam
watchFor.body: A passenger retractor can intentionally prevent further belt extraction after automatic-locking mode has been engaged.

notes: The emergency locking retractor locks in response to vehicle motion such as hard braking, cornering or an impact.
Warning lamps and reminder chimes do not replace the required mechanical functional tests.

diagnostics.finding: A fully extracted passenger belt clicks while retracting and will not pull out again.
diagnostics.meaning: This is the described automatic locking retractor mode used to secure a child seat, rather than proof of a defective retractor.
diagnostics.next: Allow the webbing to retract fully to disengage that mode, and use the prescribed functional test if operation remains in question.

diagnostics.finding: A retaining point is damaged or distorted.
diagnostics.meaning: The structure supporting the restraint needs correction before replacement assembly installation.
diagnostics.next: Restore the sheet metal’s original shape and structural integrity, then install and test the belt.

verification.title: Confirm structural correction
verification.body: Confirm any damaged retaining areas have been restored before accepting the replacement installation.

verification.title: Record results by seating position
verification.body: Record completion and results of the appropriate functional tests for every seating position, identifying any remaining condition requiring correction.

procedures.purpose: Seatbelt inspection, retaining-area correction requirements and replacement follow-through.
Required functional testing for all seating positions, including the applicable retractor tests.
Explanation of emergency and automatic retractor locking modes and child-seat anchor locations.

guides.title: Inspect and restore seatbelts after a collision
guides.summary: Inspect every seatbelt position, restore damaged attachment areas, replace belts meeting the deployment-and-use criteria and complete all required functional tests.
guides.introduction: A seatbelt restrains an occupant through its webbing, locking mechanism and vehicle attachments. Collision repair therefore includes more than checking whether a buckle closes or a belt retracts. This job establishes which belts require replacement, whether their mounting structure is sound and whether every seating position passes the appropriate functional tests.
guides.why: The belt transfers occupant loads into the body structure. A new assembly attached to distorted sheet metal cannot restore the original arrangement by itself. Inspection and correction of all seatbelt components are required during collision repair because defects can reduce protection in another crash.
searchTerms: seatbelt will not retract after crash

when.summary: As part of every collision repair, including positions where no belt replacement initially appears necessary.
notes: Establish which seating positions were occupied, which belts were used and where deployment occurred.

prepare.title: Plan restraint and structural inspection
prepare.detail: Provide access to all seatbelt components and their attaching areas. Damaged mounting structure requires the capability to restore both its original shape and structural integrity.

prepare.title: Have the functional procedures available
prepare.detail: Use the linked Seatbelt Systems diagnosis and testing procedure for the applicable tests at every seating position.

steps.title: Inspect every seating position
steps.body: Inspect all seatbelt components and identify necessary corrections. Include positions beyond the visibly damaged area. Record belt use and deployment information so the mandatory replacement decision is based on the collision circumstances.

steps.title: Restore the attachment structure
steps.body: Before installing a new belt assembly, inspect its attaching areas for damage and distortion. Restore affected sheet metal to its original shape and structural integrity. If a child seat was in use, inspect its mounting areas and restore the original production configuration.

steps.title: Replace the required belts
steps.body: Install new seatbelts at seating positions where deployment occurred and the belts were used. Correct the other defects identified during inspection; visible appearance alone does not complete the collision assessment.

steps.title: Test all positions
steps.body: Carry out the appropriate functional tests in the linked procedure at every seating position. These include the applicable retractor checks: emergency locking responds to vehicle movement, while passenger automatic locking secures a child seat after full belt extraction.

watchFor.title: Distorted mounting areas
watchFor.body: Complete structural restoration before fitting the replacement belt.

watchFor.title: Inspection limited to occupied seats
watchFor.body: All seatbelt components require inspection, and every seating position requires the appropriate functional testing.

notes: Passenger automatic-locking mode produces clicking during retraction and prevents further extraction; it disengages when the belt fully retracts.

verification.title: Record the collision repair outcome
verification.body: Record findings, structural corrections, belt replacements and functional-test results by seating position. Resolve failed tests before completing the repair.

procedures.purpose: Apply post-collision inspection, attachment restoration and belt replacement requirements.
Perform the appropriate seatbelt functional tests at every seating position.
Understand retractor locking modes and collision inspection of child-seat mounting areas.

guides.title: Correct a seatbelt tongue turned over on the webbing
guides.summary: Pass the seatbelt tongue over an illustrated fold to restore its orientation on the belt.
guides.introduction: The seatbelt tongue is the sliding metal fitting that enters the buckle. If it rotates on the webbing, bringing it toward the buckle can leave the belt twisted. This adjustment uses a temporary fold in the webbing to let the tongue pass into the correct orientation. The work takes place at the exposed belt and tongue.
guides.why: The important relationship is between the tongue and the flat webbing running through its slot. Moving the tongue over the illustrated fold changes that relationship locally. Adding a twist farther along the belt can make the tongue appear better positioned while leaving the webbing incorrectly arranged.

when.summary: When the sliding seatbelt tongue has rotated on the webbing and needs its orientation corrected.
notes: This adjustment addresses tongue orientation; a separate retractor or buckle concern needs its own assessment.

prepare.title: Expose the tongue and webbing
prepare.detail: Arrange the accessible belt so you can see how it enters and leaves the tongue slot, and can form the illustrated fold.

prepare.title: Keep the illustration in view
prepare.detail: Use [the adjustment illustration](#/document/G1692226) to guide the fold and the tongue's movement across it.

steps.title: Identify the turned tongue
steps.body: Trace the webbing through the tongue and establish where its orientation changes. This keeps the correction focused on the tongue rather than moving the twist elsewhere along the belt.

steps.title: Form the illustrated fold
steps.body: Fold the safety belt as shown. The fold provides the local change in webbing orientation needed for the tongue to pass over it.

steps.title: Draw the tongue across the fold
steps.body: Pull the tongue over the folded portion of the belt. Once it has passed over the fold, lay the webbing flat and examine the resulting tongue orientation.

watchFor.title: A twist remains elsewhere
watchFor.body: Check the belt on both sides of the tongue. Correcting its apparent position is incomplete if the webbing still carries the twist.

notes: Retractor locking is a separate function from the tongue's orientation on the belt.

diagnostics.finding: A passenger belt clicks while retracting and will not pull out after being fully extended.
diagnostics.meaning: The automatic locking retractor mode may be engaged. This mode is used to secure a child seat.
diagnostics.next: Allow the webbing to retract fully to disengage that mode; do not interpret this behavior as proof that the tongue adjustment failed.

verification.title: Inspect the corrected lay
verification.body: Confirm that the tongue has passed over the fold, the temporary fold has been removed and the webbing lies flat in the corrected orientation.

procedures.purpose: Illustrated hand adjustment for passing a rotated seatbelt tongue over a fold in the webbing.
Explain passenger-belt automatic locking behavior that may be encountered while handling the webbing.

guides.title: Remove a seatbelt twist at the upper guide
guides.summary: Fold the twisted webbing and feed it through the seatbelt guide to restore a flat belt path.
guides.introduction: The upper seatbelt guide, often called the D-ring, directs the webbing toward the occupant. A twist caught at this guide changes how the belt lies as it passes through. This adjustment corrects the webbing’s orientation by passing a folded section through the guide; it does not involve dismantling the retractor.
guides.why: The fold allows the twisted section to change orientation as it passes through the guide’s opening. Identifying the actual twist also helps distinguish a webbing problem from normal retractor locking, which requires a different response.
searchTerms: shoulder belt will not lie flat

when.summary: When a visible twist is caught at the seatbelt guide.
notes: A belt that will not extend is not, by itself, evidence of a twist.

prepare.title: Review restraint-service precautions
prepare.detail: Read the applicable warnings in Health and Safety Precautions before starting. Follow the general precautions, including preventing an unintended start and using the specified personal protection.

prepare.title: Assess guide access
prepare.detail: Determine whether surrounding trim obstructs the adjustment. Remove trim only where necessary, using the applicable trim procedure.

steps.title: Expose and identify the twist
steps.body: With any necessary trim removed, locate the twisted portion at the D-ring. The illustration shows a typical guide; the same adjustment principle applies to similar guides.

steps.title: Fold the webbing over itself
steps.body: Grasp the belt at the D-ring and fold the twisted portion over itself, as illustrated. Keep the fold at the section that needs to pass through the guide.

steps.title: Feed the fold through the guide
steps.body: Pass the folded portion through the D-ring. This changes the orientation of that section and removes the twist from the webbing.

steps.title: Check the corrected belt path
steps.body: Confirm that the adjusted section now lies flat through the guide. If trim was removed, complete its applicable refitting procedure after checking the webbing.

watchFor.title: Persistent withdrawal problems
watchFor.body: If the webbing is flat but the belt still behaves incorrectly, proceed to the appropriate retractor functional test instead of repeating the twist adjustment.

notes: Correcting a twist does not establish that every retractor or restraint function is operating correctly.

diagnostics.finding: Passenger belt clicks and will not extend after being fully pulled out
diagnostics.meaning: Automatic Locking Retractor mode may be active; this mode secures a child seat.
diagnostics.next: Allow the webbing to retract fully to disengage that mode.

diagnostics.finding: The belt locks during hard braking or cornering
diagnostics.meaning: Emergency Locking Retractor operation can be normal.
diagnostics.next: Use the dedicated retractor functional tests if operation remains in question.

verification.title: Confirm the adjustment result
verification.body: Check that the formerly twisted section is untwisted and passes flat through the D-ring.

procedures.purpose: Seatbelt-guide adjustment by folding and feeding the twisted webbing through the D-ring.
Required general health and safety precautions before restraint service.
Explain normal emergency and automatic retractor locking modes and the route to functional testing.

guides.title: Replace a rear child-seat lower anchor
guides.summary: Remove the rear seat cushion, service the removable child-seat lower anchor, and restore its fasteners and the seatbelt arrangement.
guides.introduction: The lower child-seat anchors sit where the rear seat cushion meets the backrest. They provide attachment points for the Lower Anchors and Tethers for Children (LATCH) system. This job concerns the removable anchor beneath the cushion, identified in the procedure as the child safety seat tether anchor. It is distinct from the upper tether anchors described as part of the parcel-shelf sheet metal.
guides.why: The anchor transfers restraint loads into its vehicle mounting, so correct attachment matters even though the removal sequence is short. Access also requires care: the rear cushion has locking tabs that must be pressed inward before lifting. Pulling the cushion without releasing them can damage the tabs. During reassembly, the seatbelts must remain untwisted and accessible.
searchTerms: rear child seat lower anchor replacement

when.summary: When the removable rear lower anchor needs service, or mounting inspection is required after a collision involving a child seat.
notes: If a child seat was in use during a collision, inspect its mounting areas and restore the original production configuration.
Replacing the removable anchor alone does not establish that collision-affected mounting areas are sound.

prepare.title: Provide access and torque capability
prepare.detail: Allow space to move both front seats fully forward and remove the rear cushion. Have suitable fastener tools and a torque wrench for the anchor retainers.

prepare.title: Identify the correct anchor
prepare.detail: Confirm that the work concerns the removable lower anchor under the rear seat rather than the upper tether mounting at the parcel shelf.

steps.title: Release the rear cushion
steps.body: Following [Rear Seat Cushion](#/document/G1692168), move the front seats fully forward on both sides. Press inward on the locking tabs at the front of the rear cushion to release it from the floor.

steps.title: Lift the cushion and expose the mounting
steps.body: Lift, release and remove the cushion after its tabs are disengaged. This exposes the removable lower anchor. If the work follows a collision in which a child seat was used, inspect the mounting areas before deciding that anchor replacement completes the repair.

steps.title: Remove and refit the anchor
steps.body: Use the [anchor procedure](#/document/G1692228) to remove its retainers and the anchor. Install in reverse order and tighten the retainers to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm), restoring the specified attachment.

steps.title: Reinstall the cushion
steps.body: Reverse the cushion removal procedure. Arrange the seatbelt webbing without twists and keep the belts and buckles accessible to the occupant as the cushion returns to position.

watchFor.title: Cushion will not release
watchFor.body: Check that its locking tabs have been pressed inward before lifting; do not use lifting force to overcome an engaged tab.

watchFor.title: Hidden or twisted belts
watchFor.body: Correct belt routing before finishing cushion installation so the cushion does not conceal the buckles or trap twisted webbing.

notes: The procedure illustrates the right-hand side of a left-hand-drive vehicle; the opposite side and right-hand-drive arrangement are similar.

diagnostics.finding: A child safety seat was in use during a collision.
diagnostics.meaning: The child-seat mounting areas require inspection, regardless of whether the removable anchor is being replaced.
diagnostics.next: Inspect those areas and restore the vehicle to its original production configuration.

verification.title: Confirm anchor fastening
verification.body: Verify that the retainers have been tightened to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm).

verification.title: Check the seating arrangement
verification.body: Confirm the cushion is reinstalled and the seatbelts and buckles are accessible, with no twisted webbing.

procedures.purpose: Removal and installation of the removable rear child-seat lower anchor.
Rear cushion release and refitting, including locking-tab and seatbelt precautions.
Distinction between upper tether and lower LATCH anchors, and collision-related mounting inspection requirements.

guides.title: Replace a front seatbelt buckle
guides.summary: Remove the front seat to replace its belt buckle, restore the attached wiring, and check the restraint system.
guides.introduction: The front seatbelt buckle receives and holds the belt tongue so the belt can restrain the occupant. Its electrical connection also supports recognition of the buckled state for the warning system. Replacement involves the seat-mounted buckle assembly, its retaining fastener and its wiring; the front seat must first be removed to reach these parts properly.
guides.why: The buckle attachment carries restraint loads, while the wiring must remain retained along the seat. Correct tightening secures the assembly, and correct belt routing keeps it usable by the occupant. A warning chime alone does not establish buckle failure because warning behavior also depends on ignition state, timing and, for the passenger reminder, occupant detection.

when.summary: When a front seatbelt buckle requires replacement following restraint-system assessment.
notes: The illustrated arrangement is the passenger seat in a left-hand-drive vehicle; the other front-seat arrangements are similar.

prepare.title: Plan seat removal
prepare.detail: Have the Front Seat removal and installation procedure available and follow its access and safety prerequisites. Buckle access begins with the seat removed.

prepare.title: Prepare fastening and wiring tools
prepare.detail: Use suitable hand tools for the harness retainers and buckle fastener, plus a torque wrench capable of the specified buckle-retainer torque.

prepare.title: Arrange the completion test
prepare.detail: Have the Seatbelt Systems diagnosis and testing procedure available. The buckle replacement requires a subsequent check of active restraint-system operation.

steps.title: Remove the front seat
steps.body: Follow [Front Seat](#/document/G1695491) to remove the affected seat. This exposes the buckle mounting and the wiring routed along the seat frame.

steps.title: Release the buckle wiring
steps.body: Remove the wire-harness retainers, then disconnect the buckle electrical connector. Note the existing retained route so the cable can be restored to its attachment points during assembly.

steps.title: Remove the buckle
steps.body: Remove the retaining fastener and lift away the buckle assembly as shown in [Front Seatbelt Buckle](#/document/G1692229). The mechanical attachment and electrical connection are separate parts of the removal.

steps.title: Fit the replacement and reinstall the seat
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence. Tighten the buckle retaining fastener to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm), reconnect the electrical connector and restore the harness retainers. Reinstall the seat through its own procedure, keeping the belt webbing untwisted and the belt and buckle accessible to the occupant.

steps.title: Check the restraint system
steps.body: Perform the required active restraint-system checks in [Seatbelt Systems](#/document/G1883856). Evaluate the warning behavior under its specified operating conditions rather than treating any chime as a failed replacement.

watchFor.title: Twisted or inaccessible belts
watchFor.body: During installation, make sure the webbing is not twisted and neither the belt nor buckle becomes trapped where an occupant cannot use it.

watchFor.title: Unretained buckle wiring
watchFor.body: Restore the harness retainers as well as the connector. An electrically connected buckle still needs its wiring secured to the seat.

notes: The passenger Belt-Minder reminder depends on the occupant classification system detecting a passenger above its programmed limit.
A MyKey prevents Belt-Minder deactivation; that behavior is not evidence that the buckle has failed.

diagnostics.finding: The warning or reminder behavior appears inconsistent with the buckle position.
diagnostics.meaning: Buckle state is only one input to the warning behavior; ignition timing and passenger occupancy conditions also matter.
diagnostics.next: Use the Seatbelt Systems tests to establish the fault before replacing the buckle or judging the repair unsuccessful.

verification.title: Check installation and accessibility
verification.body: Confirm buckle-retainer tightening, connector engagement, harness retention, untwisted webbing and occupant access.

verification.title: Record the restraint test result
verification.body: Record the outcome of the required active restraint-system operation check and any unresolved finding.

procedures.purpose: Front seatbelt buckle removal and installation, retaining-fastener torque and final restraint-check requirement.
Front seat removal and installation required for buckle access.
Seatbelt-system diagnosis and the required active restraint-system operation check.

guides.title: Replace the front seatbelt retractor and pretensioner on a coupe or convertible
guides.summary: Depower the restraints, remove the front belt assembly through the correct body-style access path, then restore routing and verify operation.
guides.introduction: The seatbelt retractor stores the webbing and locks it when restraint is needed. The pretensioner forms part of the supplemental restraint system (SRS). Replacement therefore involves more than removing a belt spool: electrical isolation, anchor handling and belt routing are essential. Coupe and convertible access differs, and the coupe has a specific lower-anchor rotation during installation.
guides.why: The rear anchor-pretensioner bolt must stay attached and flush with its anchor plate throughout removal and installation. Losing that relationship prevents correct installation and requires a new belt assembly. Routing also matters: the coupe's prescribed lower-anchor twist must not become a twist between the upper D-ring guide and the retractor.

when.summary: When seatbelt-system diagnosis calls for front retractor and pretensioner removal or replacement.
notes: The procedure illustrates left-hand-drive and right-side work; the corresponding opposite arrangements are similar.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Use personnel able to follow the complete SRS depowering, repowering and seatbelt testing procedures. These are required phases, not substitutes for one another.

prepare.title: Prepare body-style access
prepare.detail: Have the appropriate coupe or convertible loadspace-trim procedure, trim and fastener tools, and torque equipment. Convertible work also involves speaker-bracket access and an additional module on the right side.

steps.title: Depower and expose the anchors
steps.body: Follow SRS Depowering before disconnecting restraint components. Remove the loadspace trim using the correct body-style procedure, then move the carpet aside.

steps.title: Release the anchor pretensioner
steps.body: Disconnect its electrical connector and remove the first anchor bolt. While pulling outward on the pretensioner, release the rear bolt from its mounting, keeping it attached and flush with the anchor plate. Both anchor-bolt installation torques are 40 Nm.

steps.title: Clear convertible-only obstructions
steps.body: For right-side convertible work, remove the specified module by detaching its wiring retainers, removing its nut and bolt, and disconnecting its connector. Remove the speaker and bracket assembly by releasing its harness retainer, connector, screw, stud bolt and nuts. Use the individual tightening values in the complete procedure during reassembly.

steps.title: Remove the upper guide and retractor
steps.body: On a convertible, remove the D-ring bolt and move the belt aside, then disconnect the retractor connector and remove its retainer and assembly. On a coupe, follow the illustrated D-ring-cover and bolt removal, then remove the retractor retainer, disconnect the connector and withdraw the assembly.

steps.title: Install the retractor and D-ring
steps.body: Reverse the convertible removal sequence. On a coupe, connect and position the retractor, install its retainer at 40 Nm, then position the belt and install the D-ring bolt at 40 Nm before fitting its cover.

steps.title: Restore the correct lower-belt routing
steps.body: On a coupe, keep the webbing untwisted between D-ring and retractor. Rotate the anchor pretensioner 180 degrees clockwise on the left side or counterclockwise on the right side. On a convertible, ensure the webbing is untwisted and belts and buckles remain accessible. Complete reverse assembly, preserving the rear anchor bolt's attached, flush position.

steps.title: Repower and test
steps.body: Follow SRS Repowering after reassembly, then check the active restraint system using Seatbelt Systems diagnosis and testing.

watchFor.title: Rear anchor bolt displaced from its plate
watchFor.body: Failure to keep it attached and flush requires installation of a new safety belt assembly.

watchFor.title: Applying coupe routing to a convertible
watchFor.body: The specified lower-anchor rotation belongs to the coupe installation branch.

diagnostics.finding: A passenger belt clicks and cannot extend after being fully pulled out and allowed to retract.
diagnostics.meaning: This can be normal automatic locking retractor operation for securing a child seat.
diagnostics.next: Allow full retraction to disengage that mode; use the prescribed functional tests if operation remains in question.

verification.title: Check routing and access
verification.body: Confirm the applicable webbing arrangement, secure anchors and accessible belts and buckles before completing the restraint checks.

verification.title: Record functional completion
verification.body: Record completion of SRS repowering and the results of the required active-restraint operational check.

procedures.purpose: Front retractor and pretensioner removal and installation, including distinct coupe and convertible access and routing.
Required SRS depowering before restraint-component disconnection.
Coupe loadspace-trim removal and installation for belt access.
Convertible loadspace-trim removal and installation for belt access.
Required SRS repowering after reassembly.
Seatbelt diagnosis and functional testing, including the required final active-restraint operation check.

guides.title: Replace a rear seatbelt buckle
guides.summary: Remove the rear cushion, replace the affected buckle at its mounting bolt, and verify restraint operation after restoring untwisted, accessible belts.
guides.introduction: The rear buckle receives the belt tongue and connects that side of the restraint to its body mounting. The retractor performs a different job: it manages webbing movement and locking. Buckle replacement requires access beneath the rear cushion, correct tightening of the mounting bolt and careful positioning when the cushion goes back.
guides.why: The mounting bolt is part of the restraint attachment, so its specified torque matters. Correct installation also means occupants can reach the buckle and wear the belt without twisted webbing. The required final restraint check confirms more than the appearance of the newly fitted part.

when.summary: When inspection or seatbelt diagnosis establishes that a rear buckle requires replacement.
notes: The illustrated procedure shows the right-hand buckle; the left-hand operation is similar.

prepare.title: Arrange cushion access and torque control
prepare.detail: Have the rear cushion removal procedure, suitable bolt tools and a torque wrench for the buckle attachment.

prepare.title: Prepare for the restraint check
prepare.detail: Be able to carry out the active-restraint operational checks in the linked Seatbelt Systems diagnosis and testing procedure.

steps.title: Expose the buckle mounting
steps.body: Remove the rear seat cushion using its dedicated procedure. Identify the affected buckle and its mounting before disturbing the attachment.

steps.title: Remove the buckle
steps.body: Remove the mounting bolt and withdraw the buckle assembly. The attached illustration identifies the right-hand mounting; use the corresponding location for a left-hand repair.

steps.title: Install and position the replacement
steps.body: Reverse the removal operation and tighten the buckle bolt to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm). Restore the cushion while keeping the belt webbing untwisted and ensuring the belts and buckles remain accessible to their occupants.

steps.title: Check the restraint system
steps.body: Carry out the active-restraint operational check in [Seatbelt Systems](#/document/G1883856). Use that procedure to assess any remaining buckle or retractor complaint before considering the job finished.

watchFor.title: Buckle trapped beneath the cushion
watchFor.body: Restore its accessibility during installation; a correctly attached buckle still needs to be reachable by its occupant.

watchFor.title: Child seat used during a collision
watchFor.body: The child-seat mounting areas require inspection and restoration to the original production configuration. Replacing a buckle alone does not address that requirement.

notes: The described Belt-Minder warning functions concern the driver and front passenger; they are not confirmation of rear-buckle operation.

diagnostics.finding: Passenger belt cannot be pulled out after being fully extended and allowed to retract
diagnostics.meaning: Automatic Locking Retractor mode may be active for child-seat restraint; this is distinct from buckle operation.
diagnostics.next: Allow full retraction to disengage that mode and use the specified retractor test if the complaint remains.

verification.title: Confirm attachment and accessibility
verification.body: Confirm the buckle mounting torque, untwisted webbing and accessible belt and buckle positions with the cushion installed.

verification.title: Record the operational result
verification.body: Record the repaired seating position and the result of the required active-restraint check.

procedures.purpose: Rear buckle removal and installation, including mounting torque and belt positioning.
Rear seat cushion removal and installation for buckle access.
Required seatbelt and active-restraint operational diagnosis and testing.

guides.title: Replace a coupe rear seatbelt retractor
guides.summary: Remove the rear seatbelt retractor through the cushion and parcel-shelf access, reinstall it with untwisted webbing and check the seatbelt system.
guides.introduction: The rear seatbelt retractor stores the webbing and allows it to extend for an occupant. Its emergency locking function restrains webbing movement during demanding vehicle motion. Passenger belts also have an automatic locking mode used for child-seat installation. Replacing the coupe retractor involves removing interior access components and restoring both the retractor mounting and the separate belt attachment.
guides.why: Correct mounting, webbing routing and buckle access all contribute to a usable restraint. A twist can remain hidden during trim installation, so check the belt as the interior goes back together. Understanding the normal locking modes also helps avoid replacing a retractor simply because it has entered its child-seat locking mode.
searchTerms: rear seatbelt locked after full extension

when.summary: When seatbelt diagnosis establishes a retractor fault or the assembly must be removed for related work.
notes: The right-hand side is illustrated; the left-hand side uses a similar procedure.

prepare.title: Plan interior access
prepare.detail: Have the rear cushion and coupe parcel-shelf procedures available, together with suitable trim and fastener tools.

prepare.title: Prepare for mounting and testing
prepare.detail: Use a torque wrench suitable for the belt and retractor fasteners. Have the Seatbelt Systems diagnostic procedure available for the required functional checks.

steps.title: Expose the retractor
steps.body: Remove the [rear seat cushion](#/document/G1692168), followed by the [coupe parcel shelf](#/document/G1692602). This provides access to the belt attachment and retractor mounting.

steps.title: Release the belt and retractor
steps.body: Follow the [retractor procedure](#/document/G1692232): remove the separate seatbelt attachment bolt and position the belt aside, then remove the retractor bolts and assembly.

steps.title: Install and restore the interior
steps.body: Reverse removal. Tighten both the retractor mounting bolts and the separate belt attachment bolt to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm). During reassembly, keep the webbing untwisted and leave the belts and buckles accessible to occupants.

steps.title: Check seatbelt operation
steps.body: Complete the applicable checks in [Seatbelt Systems](#/document/G1883856). The operation information directs retractor testing to the automatic locking mode test and emergency locking road-test inspection; follow those controlled test instructions.

watchFor.title: Twisted webbing or inaccessible buckles
watchFor.body: Check routing and occupant access as the parcel shelf and cushion are restored, then check again with the interior assembled.

notes: If a child seat was in use during a collision, inspect its mounting areas and restore them to the original production configuration.

diagnostics.finding: After full extension, the belt clicks while retracting and cannot be pulled out again.
diagnostics.meaning: This is the described behavior of Automatic Locking Retractor (ALR) mode and can be normal.
diagnostics.next: Allow the webbing to retract fully to disengage ALR mode, then assess operation through the prescribed tests.

verification.title: Record the installed-system checks
verification.body: Record correct mounting torque, untwisted webbing, accessible belts and buckles, and the outcome of the prescribed seatbelt functional checks.

procedures.purpose: Coupe rear seatbelt retractor removal and installation, including belt attachment torque and routing requirements.
Rear seat cushion removal and installation for access.
Coupe parcel-shelf removal and installation for retractor access.
Seatbelt diagnosis and required post-installation functional testing.

guides.title: Diagnose airbag warnings and supplemental restraint fault codes
guides.summary: Use the warning behavior, reporting module and complete fault code to select the correct restraint-system diagnostic path.
guides.introduction: The supplemental restraint system (SRS) controls airbags and seatbelt pretensioners. Its restraints control module (RCM) monitors crash sensors and passenger classification information, then energizes appropriate restraints when deployment is necessary. Diagnosis begins by separating deployment-circuit faults from passenger-seat, communication, configuration and warning-indicator concerns.
guides.why: A fault code identifies a detected condition, not automatically a failed airbag or module. Even a connector that appears attached can produce a low-resistance fault: an incompletely seated connector position assurance tab leaves its protective shorting bars engaged.

when.summary: When an airbag warning, restraint-related tone, module communication concern or SRS fault code is present.
notes: Confirm coupe or convertible body style and actual fitted equipment before selecting a branch.
Pedestrian-protection references do not establish that the vehicle has that equipment.

prepare.title: Arrange specialist diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of module self-tests, occupant classification reset and programmable module installation. Electrical testing requires Ford diagnostic knowledge, a digital multimeter and the specified terminal probes.

prepare.title: Establish reliable starting conditions
prepare.detail: Check repair history, battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Confirm the concern is present before applying replacement decisions, except where the chosen test states otherwise.

steps.title: Choose the symptom route
steps.body: A flashing or continuously illuminated airbag indicator calls for RCM and occupant classification system module (OCSM) self-tests. A tone within 60 seconds of ignition ON calls for RCM and instrument panel cluster self-tests. If a module does not respond, follow Communications Network diagnosis.

steps.title: Read the complete code in the correct chart
steps.body: Record the reporting module and full diagnostic trouble code (DTC), including its suffix. The chart distinguishes shorts, opens, low resistance, incorrect components and cross-coupled signals. Follow the exact entry and body-style branch; a shared component name does not make every fault follow the same test.

steps.title: Resolve circuit and communication concerns in order
steps.body: Diagnose circuit faults before system or performance faults. Missing or invalid messages can originate outside the reporting module; inspect the additional module codes directed by the chart. Invalid-data reports from the powertrain or body controller do not justify replacing the RCM unless a pinpoint test directs it.

steps.title: Keep deployment-circuit testing controlled
steps.body: Follow the selected test's SRS isolation requirements. For B147D:11 or B147E:11 on vehicles without pedestrian protection, the chart requires SRS depowering and disconnection of both specified RCM connectors before resistance checks, followed by ignition-on voltage checks. Use its exact terminals and limits to decide between wiring repair and RCM replacement.

steps.title: Separate programming faults from replacement decisions
steps.body: Programmable module installation (PMI) configures a module; As-Built data supplies the vehicle configuration. U0300:00 and U2101:00 require PMI and an on-demand recheck before the specified replacement decision; U2101:00 requires As-Built data. Other memory, internal-failure or end-of-life entries explicitly direct replacement. Follow each entry's programming requirements.

steps.title: Follow passenger-seat and sensor decisions precisely
steps.body: Occupant classification faults may require installation correction, reset or replacement, as detailed below. Specified invalid-data or internal-failure codes for front, door and B-pillar impact sensors direct replacement of the identified sensor; short-to-ground or no-operation entries instead lead to their assigned tests.

steps.title: Handle unlisted RCM codes last
steps.body: Review recent repairs and resolve all listed RCM codes first. If only unlisted codes remain, clear them and repeat the self-test. If they return, verify the RCM part number and install As-Built data through the scan tool's Module Programming menu.

watchFor.title: Unsafe probing
watchFor.body: Do not probe an airbag or pretensioner igniter. Perform only the designated harness measurements under the exact depowering and connector-disconnection conditions.

watchFor.title: A warning without restraint-module codes
watchFor.body: A continuously illuminated indicator with no RCM or OCSM codes leads to instrumentation diagnosis, not automatic restraint-component replacement.

notes: Body control module code B11D8:01 directs an RCM self-test and diagnosis of the resulting RCM codes.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1193:00 is recorded by the RCM.
diagnostics.meaning: Crash-event storage is full and locked, indicating a crash.
diagnostics.next: Install a new RCM and impact sensors, following the referenced inspection and repair requirements after SRS deployment.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1193:00 is recorded by the OCSM.
diagnostics.meaning: The passenger classification module reports locked crash-event storage.
diagnostics.next: Clear OCSM codes and repeat its self-test. If the code returns, install a new occupant classification system (OCS) sensor.

diagnostics.finding: The OCSM records B00C0:11 or B00C0:7B.
diagnostics.meaning: The reported conditions are an occupant classification sensor short to ground or low fluid level.
diagnostics.next: Inspect damage and installation. Repair the cause of damage and replace the OCS as necessary; correct hose routing and any kinks. If neither damage nor installation concerns exist, install a new OCS.

diagnostics.finding: The OCSM records U3000:54.
diagnostics.meaning: Occupant classification calibration is missing.
diagnostics.next: Run OCS Reset and follow every scan-tool instruction. If unsuccessful, verify installation and pressure-hose routing, correct concerns and repeat the self-test. Replace the OCS sensor if the code remains.

verification.title: Check the branch outcome
verification.body: Complete the selected test's self-test, reset or programming checks before treating the fault as resolved.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Retain the original and returning codes, reporting modules, warning behavior and reset or programming outcome.

Diagnostic prerequisites, electrical testing methods and terminal-protection requirements.
SRS depowering when required before circuit testing or component work.
RCM removal and installation when a diagnostic entry directs replacement.
OCS sensor removal and installation, including the installation referenced by inspection and reset decisions.
Communication diagnosis when a module does not respond to the scan tool.
Instrument-cluster, warning-indicator and audible-tone diagnosis when directed by the symptom chart.

guides.title: Diagnose driver airbag stage 1 circuit faults
guides.summary: Trace driver airbag stage 1 faults through the wiring, connectors, clockspring and control module before authorizing component replacement.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) monitors the electrical deployment circuit for the driver airbag. The clockspring maintains its connection as the steering wheel turns. Pinpoint Test A separates wiring and connection problems from faults in the clockspring, airbag or RCM; an airbag warning lamp alone cannot identify the failed part.
guides.why: Small changes in terminal contact can move circuit resistance outside its acceptable range. Moving a connector may temporarily hide the problem, so a disappearing fault code is insufficient: the measured resistance must also be acceptable.

when.summary: When driver airbag stage 1 codes are retrieved, either on demand or in continuous memory.

prepare.title: Qualified restraint-system service
prepare.detail: Pyrotechnic work requires qualified personnel. Follow the linked safety, supplemental restraint system (SRS) depowering and repowering procedures exactly; disconnect components only when directed.

prepare.title: Diagnostic equipment and access
prepare.detail: Use an RCM-capable scan tool, electrical measuring equipment, correct probe adapters and the specified fused jumper where directed. Obtain Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5 and steering-column access instructions. Never probe airbag assembly connectors or back-probe deployable devices.

steps.title: Establish whether the fault is present
steps.body: Run the RCM self-test at A1. Diagnose on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 first through Test AJ. Otherwise, follow the driver-airbag branch for the retrieved code. A code stored only in continuous memory takes the intermittent-fault route.

steps.title: Measure resistance and test for movement sensitivity
steps.body: For open or low-resistance codes, A2–A3 use the DEPLOY_00_R parameter identification (PID) reading. Record it; the desired range is 1.62–4.46 ohms. An initially acceptable reading routes to A19. Otherwise, access the clockspring connectors and monitor while flexing the harness and tilting and rotating the wheel.

steps.title: Trace a low-resistance fault
steps.body: A4–A7 progressively isolate the airbag and clockspring, checking whether the fault changes to an open circuit. That response helps establish RCM operation. If the low-resistance fault remains, the prescribed measurements distinguish circuits shorted together from an RCM concern.

steps.title: Trace an open or high-resistance fault
steps.body: A8–A11 check continuity through the complete path and then the wiring excluding the clockspring. Controlled fused-jumper tests at the specified harness connectors check whether the RCM recognizes low resistance. Follow the exact isolation sequence and remove each jumper when instructed.

steps.title: Separate ground and voltage shorts
steps.body: A12–A14 isolate a ground short by checking fault changes after component disconnection, then circuit resistance to ground. A15–A16 isolate the clockspring and check for unwanted voltage. These branches have different powered-test conditions; follow each prescribed depowering and repowering step.

steps.title: Confirm a component before replacing it
steps.body: At A17–A19, inspect wiring, terminals and connector position assurance (CPA) locks, repair concerns, reconnect everything and repeat the self-test. Replace the identified component only if the original fault returns. Before RCM replacement, check applicable technical service bulletins. Verify replacement part compatibility.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent faults
steps.body: A20 monitors resistance during harness and steering movement; incorrect resistance occurring only during wheel rotation directs clockspring replacement. A21 checks for a recurring ground-short code. A22 checks voltage-short recurrence with the airbag removed under the specified SRS sequence. If unreproduced, A23 inspects wiring, corrosion and connector locks without speculative replacement.

steps.title: Restore connections and check the complete system
steps.body: At A24, reconnect components and repower as directed. Do not perform SRS prove-out during stages that prohibit it. Run the Restraints self-test across applicable modules. Diagnose remaining on-demand faults before clearing codes or releasing the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Connector faults that resemble component failure
watchFor.body: An incompletely seated CPA tab can leave a shorting bar engaged. Never defeat shorting bars; damaged restraint terminals require service connector pigtails.

watchFor.title: Live airbag handling
watchFor.body: Carry the deployment cover away from your body and never place the airbag cover-down.

notes: Additional-module checks apply only to equipment actually fitted.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0001:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The stage 1 circuit has a detected short to ground.
diagnostics.next: Use A12 for an active fault or A21 for a memory-only fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0001:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The circuit has a detected short to voltage.
diagnostics.next: Use A15 for an active fault or A22 for a memory-only fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0001:13 or B0001:1A is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Resistance is respectively above or below the desired range.
diagnostics.next: Use A2 when active or A20 when memory-only; neither code proves airbag failure.

verification.title: Record resistance and fault status
verification.body: Retain the original codes, recorded PID readings and movement-test results. Resistance must be within the desired range even if no on-demand code returns.

verification.title: Confirm the release condition
verification.body: The final Restraints self-test must show no unresolved on-demand faults, and the SRS must be fully operational.

guides.title: Trace cross-coupled airbag and seatbelt circuit faults
guides.summary: Use paired :2B restraint codes to locate unwanted connections between separate device circuits and distinguish wiring faults from a module fault.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) monitors the supplemental restraint system (SRS), including airbag, pretensioner and sensor circuits. A signal cross-coupled code means circuits belonging to separate devices have become electrically connected. This job isolates those circuits, checks the harness and establishes whether a persistent fault warrants RCM replacement.
guides.why: A short within one device’s loop produces a different fault type. Ordinary loop faults also suspend cross-coupled monitoring, so repairing one fault can reveal another. Paired codes identify circuits to investigate; they do not establish that both devices have failed.

when.summary: When an RCM self-test or continuous-memory record contains a restraint DTC with the :2B failure type.
notes: An on-demand fault is currently detected; a continuous-memory-only fault follows the intermittent branch.

prepare.title: Use qualified restraint-system personnel
prepare.detail: Read the pyrotechnic precautions and obtain the exact SRS depowering and repowering procedures. Incorrect isolation or testing can cause deployment.

prepare.title: Prepare the correct test equipment
prepare.detail: Use an RCM-capable scan tool, resistance meter, correct probe adapters and Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5. Never probe airbag assembly connectors or back-probe deployable-device connectors.

steps.title: A1: distinguish present and intermittent faults
steps.body: Perform the RCM self-test with ignition on and identify the diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Diagnose on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 first using Test AJ. Otherwise, current cross-coupled codes lead to A2; continuous-memory-only codes lead to A4. A current fault cannot be cleared until corrected.

steps.title: A2: isolate and compare the affected harness circuits
steps.body: Switch ignition off and depower the SRS using the exact procedure. Disconnect both RCM connectors and every affected device identified by the paired codes. Inspect for damage, then use the device table to measure between the isolated harness circuits of the affected devices—not through an airbag or pretensioner. Every specified comparison must exceed 10,000 ohms. A failing result requires circuit repair, then A5; passing results lead to A3.

steps.title: A3: confirm before condemning the RCM
steps.body: Inspect terminals, inline connectors, damaged wiring and both RCM connector-position-assurance locks. Correct concerns, reconnect all disconnected components and the RCM, then repower without performing the SRS prove-out at this stage. Repeat the RCM self-test. Persistent cross-coupled codes require checking applicable technical service bulletins through OASIS; follow an applicable bulletin, or replace the RCM if none addresses the concern. If the codes disappear, continue with A4.

steps.title: A4: investigate intermittent damage
steps.body: Follow the prescribed depowering and disconnection sequence to inspect affected harnesses thoroughly. Repair damage, then follow repowering and self-test instructions without an intermediate prove-out. A returning on-demand fault sends diagnosis back to A2. If absent, use the specified harness-flex and ignition-cycling checks to seek an intermittent cause. Do not replace components merely because a memory code remains.

steps.title: A5: complete the restraint-system check
steps.body: With ignition off, restore all SRS connections as directed and complete any required repowering, again without an intermediate prove-out. Run the full Restraints self-test. Diagnose every on-demand code from the RCM, occupant classification system module and any other applicable restraint module. Do not clear codes while unresolved faults remain.

watchFor.title: Terminal damage
watchFor.body: Restraint connector terminals must not be repaired individually; use service connector pigtails where terminal repair is needed.

watchFor.title: A connector that looks seated
watchFor.body: An incompletely seated assurance tab can leave a deployable component’s shorting bar engaged, causing a low-resistance fault.

notes: For B1405:2B and B1408:2B, use coupe side-curtain connections or convertible upper-side-airbag connections as applicable.
Select replacement restraint parts by the correct catalog part number; physical similarity does not establish compatibility.

diagnostics.finding: Resistance between affected harness circuits does not exceed 10,000 ohms
diagnostics.meaning: The isolated circuits fail the separation check.
diagnostics.next: Repair the affected wiring and proceed to A5.

diagnostics.finding: Separation checks pass but on-demand codes persist after reconnection
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM-confirmation branch remains active.
diagnostics.next: Check applicable bulletins before the directed module replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Cross-coupled codes remain only in continuous memory
diagnostics.meaning: The fault is intermittent or currently absent.
diagnostics.next: Investigate harness damage and attempt controlled reproduction without speculative parts replacement.

verification.title: Confirm the release condition
verification.body: The final Restraints self-test must show no on-demand faults. The SRS must be fully operational and fault-free before returning the vehicle.

verification.title: Record what was established
verification.body: Document the affected code pair, circuit-separation results and final self-test outcome, distinguishing a repaired fault from one that could not be reproduced.

procedures.purpose: Complete :2B cross-coupled diagnostic path, device connections and A1–A5 decisions.
Required pyrotechnic handling and electrical-testing precautions.
Priority diagnosis of on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17.
Required SRS depowering before instructed disconnections.
SRS repowering at the specified diagnostic stages.

Diagnosis of additional restraint faults found during final self-test.

guides.title: Diagnose SRS incorrect-component faults
guides.summary: Check restraints control module identity and configuration, then verify suspect impact sensors before completing the restraint-system self-test and prove-out.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) monitors the sensors and devices used by the supplemental restraint system (SRS). It compares connected equipment with its configuration. An incorrect-component code ending in :4A indicates a compatibility or configuration concern, which can illuminate the airbag warning indicator. This investigation covers deployment devices, belt and seat sensors, restraint indicators and impact sensors.
guides.why: Physically similar restraint parts can have different applications. Checking part numbers and restoring the correct configuration prevents unnecessary replacement and ensures the module recognizes the intended equipment. An active mismatch must be corrected before its code can remain cleared.

when.summary: When an RCM self-test or continuous-memory record reports an incorrect-component code ending in :4A.
notes: Review recent repairs, particularly module or impact-sensor replacement.
Apply equipment-specific branches only to components confirmed for the vehicle by its parts catalogue and As-Built data.

prepare.title: Qualified restraint-system service
prepare.detail: Pyrotechnic service requires qualified personnel and the prescribed safety precautions. Disconnect or reconnect SRS components only when directed. Never probe airbag connectors or back-probe deployable seatbelt devices, and never move a connected RCM with ignition ON.

prepare.title: Identification and programming resources
prepare.detail: Have a scan tool supporting RCM self-tests, Log Viewer and programmable module installation (PMI), plus vehicle-specific As-Built configuration data and the Ford parts catalogue. Inspect wiring and connectors before advancing through the test.

steps.title: Separate current faults from stored history
steps.body: With ignition ON, perform the RCM self-test in [incorrect-component diagnosis](#/document/G1696390). Establish whether the fault returns on demand or exists only in continuous memory. Apply the priority and exception-code routes below before continuing.

steps.title: Verify the installed RCM
steps.body: Use Log Viewer to retrieve and record the RCM part number, then compare it with the Ford parts catalogue for the vehicle. An incorrect module requires the correct RCM installation procedure, followed by the final SRS checks. A correct part number leads to configuration verification.

steps.title: Restore the correct configuration
steps.body: Carry out PMI using As-Built data and the scan-tool instructions, then repeat the RCM self-test. If the mismatch clears, proceed to final checks. Persistent specified impact-sensor codes lead to sensor identification. For other persistent incorrect-component codes, check applicable Ford technical service bulletins; if none addresses the concern, replace the RCM.

steps.title: Identify suspect impact sensors
steps.body: For the sensor-code branch, turn ignition OFF and perform the complete SRS depowering procedure before gaining access. Record each suspect sensor's part number and compare it with the catalogue. Replace incorrect sensors through their location-specific procedures. If all numbers match, check applicable bulletins before the directed RCM replacement.

steps.title: Follow the intermittent-fault branch when applicable
steps.body: For a memory-only incorrect-component fault, clear RCM codes and repeat its self-test. If no incorrect-component code returns on demand, install no new SRS components. If one returns, follow A5's bulletin check and RCM replacement decision, then continue to final checks.

steps.title: Restore power and check the complete system
steps.body: With ignition OFF, repower the SRS if it was depowered, without performing prove-out yet. Turn ignition ON and run the full Restraints self-test. If any queried restraint module returns an on-demand code, retain the codes and follow [SRS diagnosis](#/document/G1696340) until every fault is resolved.

watchFor.title: Damaged restraint terminals
watchFor.body: Use service connector pigtails where restraint terminals require repair; do not rework the terminals.

watchFor.title: Crash-damaged mounting areas
watchFor.body: Damage at an RCM or impact-sensor mounting area requires restoration to the original configuration and replacement of the original component at that location, even without airbag deployment.

notes: Some general code-table entries identify unexpected impact sensors. Their presence in the table does not establish that pedestrian-protection or other optional hardware is fitted.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B00A0:4A is retrieved on demand.
diagnostics.meaning: This incorrect-component fault has a separate diagnostic route.
diagnostics.next: Follow Pinpoint Test N.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3003:16 or U3003:17 is also retrieved on demand.
diagnostics.meaning: These faults take priority, whether or not an incorrect-component fault is currently present.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose them through Pinpoint Test AJ before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: DTC B1413:4A, B1414:4A, B1415:4A, B1417:4A, B1418:4A or B1419:4A persists after PMI.
diagnostics.meaning: The applicable impact sensor requires part-number verification: B1413/B1417 identify front locations, B1414/B1418 front doors and B1415/B1419 B-pillars, respectively driver/passenger.
diagnostics.next: Follow A4, including SRS depowering, catalogue comparison and the appropriate sensor replacement or RCM decision.

verification.title: Complete the final prove-out
verification.body: Once no on-demand faults remain, clear RCM and occupant classification system module continuous-memory codes and perform SRS prove-out. Release the vehicle only with the SRS fully operational and fault-free.

verification.title: Retain identification results
verification.body: Keep the recorded RCM and suspect-sensor part numbers, catalogue comparisons and final self-test outcome with the repair record.

guides.title: Diagnose acceleration and rotation event codes in the restraints control module
guides.summary: Use a controlled road test, mounting inspection and directed self-tests to distinguish motion-related event codes from a persistent restraints-module fault.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) helps control airbag and pretensioner deployment and supplies motion-sensor data to the stability and traction-control system. It also checks whether that data falls within its expected range. Acceleration and rotation event codes can follow rough roads or aggressive driving, but incorrect mounting or an RCM fault can also cause them. This diagnosis determines whether the event repeats before authorizing repair or replacement.
guides.why: The module needs a secure, clean mounting surface to assess vehicle motion reliably. These particular codes do not request illumination of the airbag warning indicator, so an unlit warning lamp cannot establish that the codes have cleared. Handling a powered restraints module also presents a deployment hazard.
searchTerms: restraints motion codes after rough road

notes: Diagnose any other RCM codes first; they change the starting point for this test.

prepare.title: Arrange restraints-system capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of RCM and complete Restraints self-tests. Have the linked supplemental restraint system (SRS) depowering, repowering and RCM installation procedures available, plus Wiring Diagrams Cell 5.

prepare.title: Plan the road test and inspection
prepare.detail: Choose a route with left and right turns, avoiding rough roads and aggressive driving. Inspect for obvious wiring and connector concerns, but disconnect or reconnect SRS components only when the test instructs.

steps.title: Establish which codes are present
steps.body: With ignition on, perform the RCM self-test and record its results. Continue with this path only when the listed motion-event codes are the only RCM codes retrieved. Otherwise, follow general SRS diagnosis for the other codes first.

steps.title: Clear the events and check for recurrence
steps.body: Clear the RCM codes, drive the planned route gently and repeat the RCM self-test. If no codes return, rough roads or aggressive driving may explain the original events; explain this to the owner. Diagnose any different codes that appear. If only the original event-code group returns, continue to mounting inspection.

steps.title: Depower before checking the mounting
steps.body: Switch the ignition off and follow the complete SRS depowering procedure. Check that RCM hardware is fully seated and correctly tightened, and inspect its mounting surface for damage, corrosion or foreign material. Repair incorrect mounting or install new hardware as necessary, then proceed to the final system checks.

steps.title: Confirm a fault when mounting is correct
steps.body: Before reconnecting anything previously disconnected, inspect terminals, wiring and the connector position assurance (CPA) lever/locks at C310A and C310B; repair defects. Connect the RCM and ensure all SRS components are connected. Repower without proving out yet, clear RCM codes and run its self-test. If the original code returns on demand, check applicable technical service bulletins before the test authorizes RCM replacement.

steps.title: Investigate an intermittent result
steps.body: If the original code does not return, do not replace SRS components. Switch the ignition off, depower again and disconnect C310A and C310B as directed. Inspect locks, loose or spread terminals, frayed connections and damaged harnesses. Repair identified faults; if none are found, continue without speculative replacement.

steps.title: Reconnect and check the complete restraints system
steps.body: Switch the ignition off and wait one minute for backup power to deplete before reconnecting disconnected SRS components. If previously depowered, follow the repowering procedure without proving out yet. Switch the ignition on and run the complete Restraints self-test, including the RCM, occupant classification system module (OCSM) and any additional module applicable to the fitted equipment.

steps.title: Resolve remaining faults before proving out
steps.body: If the final self-test retrieves any on-demand restraints codes, retain them and follow SRS diagnosis until resolved. When none remain, clear RCM and OCSM continuous-memory codes and perform the prescribed SRS prove-out. Release requires a fully operational, fault-free restraints system.

watchFor.title: Never move an energized RCM
watchFor.body: Do not handle, move or change its horizontal mounting position while connected with ignition on. Accidental deployment can cause serious injury or death.

watchFor.title: Confirm replacement compatibility
watchFor.body: If replacement is directed, verify the correct Ford parts-catalog number. A physically similar component from another vehicle may be incompatible.

notes: The one-minute wait at final reconnection does not replace the complete SRS depowering procedure.
Delay SRS prove-out until the final diagnostic stage specifically directs it.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code C0061:68, C0062:68 or C0065:68 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These indicate lateral, longitudinal or vertical acceleration data outside the RCM's expected range, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Check for other RCM codes first, then use the controlled road test to establish recurrence.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code C0063:68 or C0064:68 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: C0063:68 concerns yaw-rate data; C0064:68 concerns roll-rate data outside the expected range.
diagnostics.next: Follow the same recurrence, mounting and confirmation sequence; a stored event alone does not justify replacing the RCM.

diagnostics.finding: The original event code does not return during the confirmation self-test.
diagnostics.meaning: The fault has become intermittent during diagnosis.
diagnostics.next: Follow the depowered connector and harness inspection, then complete the final restraints checks without installing speculative parts.

verification.title: Confirm system readiness
verification.body: Verify that the final Restraints self-test has no on-demand faults, then complete the directed memory clearing and SRS prove-out.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record initial codes, controlled-road-test recurrence, mounting or wiring repairs, confirmation-test results and final prove-out outcome.

procedures.purpose: Complete motion-event-code diagnosis through road testing, mounting inspection and final SRS verification.
Diagnose other initial or final restraints-system codes.
Required SRS depowering before the directed mounting and connector inspections.
