guides.title: Diagnose U0100:00 recorded by a restraints module
guides.summary: Determine whether a missing powertrain-module message is intermittent, shared across modules or isolated to one restraints module.
guides.introduction: The occupant classification system module (OCSM) and restraints control module (RCM) both use messages from the powertrain control module (PCM) over the high-speed controller area network (HS-CAN). U0100:00 means the reporting module did not receive an expected PCM message. This test uses communication checks and comparisons between modules to establish the appropriate repair route.
guides.why: A missing message does not prove the receiving module has failed. Network traffic, intermittent conditions and other recorded module faults must be considered before the test's replacement decisions are valid.
searchTerms: scan tool cannot establish vehicle session

when.summary: When U0100:00 is recorded by the RCM or OCSM.
notes: Keep track of which module originally reported the code; the later comparison depends on that origin.

prepare.title: Arrange module-level scan access
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of establishing a vehicle session, running individual and all-module self-tests, and clearing the selected module's codes.

prepare.title: Inspect without disturbing the system
prepare.detail: Thoroughly inspect wiring and connectors before testing. Disconnect or reconnect supplemental restraint system (SRS) components only when expressly instructed.

prepare.title: Read the restraints precautions
prepare.detail: Pyrotechnic service is restricted to qualified personnel. Never probe deployable-device connectors or move the connected RCM with ignition on. Have access to OASIS Technical Service Bulletins before making a replacement decision.

steps.title: Establish scan-tool communication
steps.body: With ignition on, connect the scan tool and attempt to establish a vehicle session. If that fails, follow Communications Network diagnosis for loss of PCM communication. If successful, follow the branch for the module that originally stored U0100:00.

steps.title: Check whether the original module repeats the fault
steps.body: For an OCSM-origin code, perform the OCSM self-test, clear its codes, wait 10 seconds and repeat its self-test. For an RCM-origin code, perform that same sequence on the RCM. If U0100:00 does not return, the system is operating correctly at that time; high network traffic or an intermittent condition may explain the stored code.

steps.title: Check the PCM before comparing receivers
steps.body: If U0100:00 returns, perform the PCM key-on, engine-off self-test. Recorded P0562 or P0563 must be diagnosed through the applicable engine procedure before proceeding down the communication replacement path.

steps.title: Check the originating restraints module's other codes
steps.body: Repeat the self-test for the original reporting module: OCSM in A5 or RCM in A6. If U3003:16 or U3003:17 is recorded, follow Pinpoint Test AJ. Otherwise continue to the all-module comparison.

steps.title: Compare an OCSM-origin fault
steps.body: Run all-module self-tests. If U0100:00 is also recorded by the anti-lock braking system (ABS) module or RCM, A7 points toward PCM replacement. If neither records it, A7 points toward OCSM replacement. Both outcomes require the bulletin check before replacement.

steps.title: Compare an RCM-origin fault
steps.body: For an RCM-origin concern, A8 asks whether the ABS module or OCSM also records U0100:00. A shared code points toward PCM replacement; absence from both points toward RCM replacement. Again, check bulletins before acting.

steps.title: Apply the bulletin and replacement decision
steps.body: Check OASIS for an applicable Technical Service Bulletin for every replacement branch. If one applies, discontinue this test and follow it. Otherwise follow the directed replacement route. OCSM replacement is referred through the Occupant Classification System Sensor procedure; RCM replacement has its own procedure. Complete the applicable installation requirements separately.

watchFor.title: An intermittent result
watchFor.body: A code that does not return supports the test's operating-correctly-at-present outcome, not proof that every intermittent concern has been eliminated.

watchFor.title: Replacement compatibility
watchFor.body: Verify the Ford part number. Occupant classification components are calibrated assemblies and must remain in the configuration in which they are supplied.

notes: This communication test establishes a diagnostic endpoint; it does not supply the separate module installation procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The OCSM records U0100:00.
diagnostics.meaning: The OCSM missed an expected PCM message.
diagnostics.next: Use the OCSM repeat-test branch, then compare the ABS module and RCM if the fault persists.

diagnostics.finding: The RCM records U0100:00.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM missed an expected PCM message.
diagnostics.next: Use the RCM repeat-test branch, then compare the ABS module and OCSM if the fault persists.

verification.title: Record the repeat-test outcome
verification.body: Record the originating module, whether U0100:00 returned after the specified clearing and waiting sequence, and the other modules that recorded it.

verification.title: Preserve the decision evidence
verification.body: Record the PCM and originating-module self-test results and the applicable bulletin decision. These establish which branch justifies the next repair.

Required pyrotechnic and restraints service precautions.

guides.title: Diagnose lost occupant classification communication: U0154:00
guides.summary: Determine whether missing occupant-classification messages reflect a network concern, an intermittent event or a fault requiring the prescribed component-replacement sequence.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) uses messages from the occupant classification system module (OCSM) alongside other restraint-system inputs. These messages travel over the second high-speed controller area network, HS-CAN2. U0154:00 means an expected message did not arrive; it does not identify which module caused the interruption.
guides.why: A module may communicate during a network test yet have missed a message earlier. Repeating the RCM self-test after clearing memory separates a returning fault from a temporary event. Checking both modules' recorded codes then prevents a communication complaint from obscuring another fault that needs attention first.
searchTerms: lost communication with occupant classification module

when.summary: Use when the RCM records U0154:00 for a missing occupant classification module message.
notes: Choose any eventual occupant classification sensor replacement procedure according to the actual fitted seats.

prepare.title: Scan-tool capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of network testing, RCM and OCSM self-tests, and clearing RCM diagnostic trouble codes. Preserve the self-test results for the later code comparisons.

prepare.title: Restraint-system precautions
prepare.detail: Service requires qualified personnel following the pyrotechnic precautions. Inspect wiring and connections before testing, but disconnect or reconnect supplemental restraint system (SRS) components only when a procedure directs it. Do not probe deployable-device connectors.

steps.title: Check whether the OCSM communicates now
steps.body: With ignition on, run the network test. If the OCSM fails, continue with Communications Network diagnosis. That result changes the diagnostic route: the remaining sequence assumes the OCSM has passed this test.

steps.title: Check whether the missing-message code returns
steps.body: Perform the RCM self-test, retain its results, clear the RCM codes and wait 10 seconds. Repeat the self-test. If U0154:00 does not return, the system is operating correctly at that time; high network traffic or an intermittent condition may explain the earlier entry.

steps.title: Review the RCM's accompanying codes
steps.body: If U0154:00 returns, inspect the recorded RCM results for U3003:16 or U3003:17. Either code directs diagnosis to its dedicated pinpoint test before continuing this communication-fault sequence.

steps.title: Test the OCSM and check service information
steps.body: Run the OCSM self-test and check its recorded results for U3003:16 or U3003:17 as well. Follow their dedicated test if present. If neither is recorded, check applicable Ford service articles and follow any article addressing the concern before proceeding to replacement.

steps.title: Follow the conditional replacement sequence
steps.body: Only after the preceding checks, and with no applicable service article, does this test direct a new RCM. Use the referenced replacement instructions and repeat the RCM self-test. If U0154:00 returns, the next directed repair is a new occupant classification system (OCS) sensor. Select the procedure matching the fitted seats; do not assume multi-contour equipment is present.

watchFor.title: Moving a powered RCM
watchFor.body: Never handle, move or change the RCM's original horizontal mounting position while it is connected and the ignition is on; accidental deployment can result.

watchFor.title: Incorrect or disturbed OCS parts
watchFor.body: Verify the correct replacement part. OCS parts are calibrated as an assembly: retain the supplied configuration, do not separate it, and keep its components and connectors free of contamination.

notes: The initial checks use scan-tool evidence. A stored communication code alone is not an instruction to disconnect sensors or replace modules.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0154:00 returns after clearing and retesting.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM again reports a missing expected OCSM message.
diagnostics.next: With the network test passed, review both modules' specified accompanying codes and applicable service information.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3003:16 or U3003:17 is recorded by the RCM or OCSM.
diagnostics.meaning: The prescribed sequence gives this finding diagnostic priority.
diagnostics.next: Follow the dedicated test identified in the communication procedure before proceeding.

verification.title: Compare recorded results
verification.body: Retain the network-test outcome, initial module codes and repeat RCM self-test result. Identify whether U0154:00 returned or remained absent.

verification.title: Confirm the repair endpoint
verification.body: Repeat the RCM self-test after the directed RCM replacement. Complete any subsequent sensor-replacement procedure, and release the vehicle only with the SRS fully operational and free of faults.

procedures.purpose: U0154:00 network and module diagnosis, including priority-code and seat-specific replacement referrals.
Required pyrotechnic precautions, powered-RCM restrictions and OCS assembly handling.

guides.title: Diagnose restraint-system voltage codes U3003:16 and U3003:17
guides.summary: Check battery condition, charging voltage and module connections before deciding whether a restraint control module needs replacement.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) monitors the supplemental restraint system (SRS), while the occupant classification system module (OCSM) handles passenger classification information. Both monitor their electrical supply. Either can report abnormal voltage and cause the instrument cluster’s airbag warning indicator to illuminate. This diagnosis separates vehicle power problems from wiring, connection or module faults.
guides.why: A voltage code does not establish module failure. Recent jump-starting, charging or battery discharge can leave stored codes, while poor connections can interrupt an otherwise healthy supply. Restraint isolation prevents accidental deployment during connector work.
searchTerms: airbag warning light after jump start

when.summary: When the RCM or OCSM records U3003:16 or U3003:17.
notes: Ask about recent battery charging, discharge, accessories left on or aftermarket electrical loads.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint-system diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use an SRS-trained technician, an all-module diagnostic scan tool, battery-condition testing equipment and a voltage/resistance meter with correct connector probe adapters.

prepare.title: Establish the safety and inspection baseline
prepare.detail: Read the linked pyrotechnic precautions. Inspect harnesses and connectors for damage or looseness, and establish the initial airbag warning-indicator state using the depowering procedure.

steps.title: Retrieve the complete fault picture
steps.body: With ignition ON, retrieve all continuous memory diagnostic trouble codes (CMDTCs). If B1317, B1318, B1676, U3003:16 or U3003:17 appears in any module together with charging-system codes in the powertrain control module, diagnose the charging system first. Otherwise continue to the battery test.

steps.title: Test battery condition
steps.body: Switch ignition OFF and perform the Battery Condition Test. A failed battery requires replacement and clearing all CMDTCs. A passing battery that needed recharging still requires charging-system diagnosis and code clearing. Continue only if it passed without needing recharge.

steps.title: Check charging voltage under the appropriate load
steps.body: Start the engine and measure battery voltage. For U3003:17, switch accessories off. For U3003:16, turn headlights on and the heater/air-conditioning fan to high. The required range is 13–15.2 volts. Outside it, diagnose charging and clear CMDTCs. Within it, low voltage proceeds to feed and ground checks; high voltage proceeds to connector inspection.

steps.title: Isolate the restraints and check the low-voltage feed
steps.body: Follow the linked SRS depowering procedure. With no SRS fault, switch ignition OFF, wait one minute and keep it OFF. With a fault, follow the fuse-removal and network-confirmation sequence, then switch OFF, disconnect the battery and wait at least one minute. Disconnect RCM C310A/C310B or OCSM C3043. Test RCM C310A pin 19 to C2280A pin 4, or OCSM C3043 pin 1 to C2280C pin 23. Resistance must be less than 1 ohm; otherwise repair the feed and clear CMDTCs.

steps.title: Check the ground return
steps.body: With isolation maintained, measure the RCM mounting bracket to ground or OCSM C3043 pin 4 to ground. Require less than 1 ohm. For an RCM failure, correct mounting-surface corrosion and ensure clean fasteners tightened to specification. For an OCSM failure, repair its ground circuit. Clear CMDTCs after repair.

steps.title: Inspect connections and restore power
steps.body: For either code, depower before connector inspection if not already isolated. Replace corroded terminals/connectors as required, clean module pins and renew damaged or displaced pins. Reconnect securely, engaging the RCM connector-position-assurance lock. Follow the linked repowering procedure, including its original-fault-state and fitted-equipment provisions.

steps.title: Decide whether module replacement is justified
steps.body: If the concern remains, check OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins and follow any relevant bulletin. Only when none applies does the test direct replacement of the module that recorded the code, using its separate installation procedure. If the concern disappears, a loose or corroded connection may have caused it.

watchFor.title: Keep measurements on the specified circuits
watchFor.body: Never probe airbag connectors or back-probe deployable seat-belt connectors. OCSM C3043 pin 6 is a belt-tension signal; pin 4 is ground.

notes: Disconnect SRS components only when directed. Verify replacement part numbers in the Ford parts catalog; physical similarity does not establish compatibility.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3003:16 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects below 9 volts with certain SRS faults, or below 6 volts regardless of fault status. The OCSM threshold is below 8 volts.
diagnostics.next: Check battery and charging performance before the affected module’s feed and ground.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3003:17 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects above 16 volts with certain SRS faults, or above 18 volts regardless of fault status. The OCSM threshold is above 18 volts.
diagnostics.next: Check charging voltage with accessories off before proceeding to module-connection verification.

verification.title: Complete SRS repowering and prove-out
verification.body: Restore removed fuses and battery connection as directed. For the fault-present branch, sit upright with the driver seat rearmost and no objects between you and pyrotechnic devices. With all airbags connected, perform the prescribed ignition sequence: OFF for 10 seconds, then ON. Expect approximately 6 seconds of illumination followed by extinction; monitor for approximately 30 seconds. Investigate absent, persistent or flashing illumination, chimes or SRS messages.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Clear all CMDTCs as directed. Record battery results, charging voltage, applicable resistance readings and final concern status. Release the vehicle only with the SRS fully operational and fault-free.

guides.title: Diagnose passenger belt-tension sensor faults B00C2:11 and B00C2:12
guides.summary: Trace passenger belt-tension reference-voltage faults through the buckle, wiring and occupant-classification system, then verify the complete restraint system.
guides.introduction: The belt tension sensor (BTS), incorporated into the passenger safety-belt buckle, works with the occupant classification system (OCS). The occupant classification system module (OCSM) supplies a reference voltage that changes with belt tension. This diagnosis separates a grounded or powered reference circuit from a buckle-sensor fault or an OCS fault before replacement is considered.
guides.why: Connector and wiring defects cause many of these faults. Controlled disconnection and retesting help establish whether the module recognizes a changed circuit condition. Because this work also involves airbag connections, the prescribed supplemental restraint system (SRS) power transitions protect against accidental deployment.

when.summary: When B00C2:11 or B00C2:12 is retrieved from the occupant classification module.
notes: Distinguish a current on-demand fault from a continuous-memory-only record before choosing the test branch.

prepare.title: Use restraint-system diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Read the health and safety precautions. Have an appropriate scan tool, multimeter, correct probe adapters and Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5 available. Disconnect or reconnect SRS components only when the pinpoint step directs it.

prepare.title: Plan the required power transitions
prepare.detail: For fault-present depowering, follow the complete routine: remove the applicable restraint supply fuse, verify the affected restraint modules do not respond to the network test, switch ignition off, disconnect the battery and wait at least one minute. Apply only fitted-equipment branches. During repowering, follow the specified upright driver-seat position, with the seat rearmost and no objects between the occupant and a pyrotechnic device.

steps.title: Inspect and establish whether the fault is active
steps.body: Inspect the passenger buckle and sensor, cushion harness, OCSM and connectors for damage or looseness. With ignition on, perform the OCSM self-test at A1. An on-demand B00C2:11 follows A2; B00C2:12 follows A4. A continuous-memory-only fault follows A6. An active fault cannot be cleared successfully until corrected.

steps.title: Follow the short-to-ground branch
steps.body: At A2, switch ignition off, disconnect buckle connector C3238 and repeat the specified self-test. If B00C2:11 disappears, the test directs passenger buckle replacement and A7. If it remains, A3 requires ignition off and a one-minute wait before disconnecting OCSM C3043. Measure C3238 pin 2 to ground: greater than 10,000 ohms leads to A5; otherwise repair the circuit and proceed to A7.

steps.title: Follow the short-to-voltage branch
steps.body: At A4, switch ignition off and depower the SRS fully. Disconnect passenger airbag inline connector C219, buckle C3238 and OCSM C3043. Repower without proving out the SRS, then switch ignition on and measure C3238 pin 2 to ground. Any voltage requires circuit repair followed by A7; no voltage leads to A5. This measurement is on the belt-sensor circuit.

steps.title: Reconfirm before choosing the OCS replacement path
steps.body: At A5, switch ignition off and inspect disconnected connectors, inline connections and wiring; repair spread, pushed-out or loose terminals and damaged wires. Reconnect the OCSM and buckle as directed. If C219 was disconnected at A4, depower before reconnecting it, then repower without prove-out. With all required restraint connections restored, repeat the OCSM self-test. If the original code remains, check technical service bulletins; without an applicable bulletin, follow the directed OCS sensor replacement. If it disappears, continue to A6 without replacing components.

steps.title: Investigate an intermittent connection
steps.body: At A6, switch ignition off, disconnect C3238, inspect and repair its connections and harness, then reconnect and self-test. A returning on-demand code sends diagnosis back to its ground or voltage branch. Otherwise attempt to reproduce the fault by flexing the harness, cycling ignition and operating other systems sharing that harness. Repair discovered faults; a memory record alone does not justify new SRS parts.

steps.title: Restore connections and test all restraints
steps.body: At A7, switch ignition off. If C219 was disconnected, depower before restoring it and all other disconnected SRS components. Repower as required without prove-out, then perform the scan tool's Restraints self-test. Diagnose every on-demand restraint fault before clearing codes. Only when none remain should you clear the restraints control module (RCM) and OCSM codes and proceed to final prove-out.

watchFor.title: Expected faults during deliberate disconnection
watchFor.body: With C3238 disconnected, an open-circuit fault is normally reported. Its shared buckle-switch connection also produces an RCM fault; these test-induced findings must be interpreted in context.

watchFor.title: Airbag circuits at C219
watchFor.body: C219 includes passenger airbag deployment circuits. Identify the connector correctly and preserve the depower/reconnect sequence; do not probe an airbag igniter.

notes: Confirm replacement SRS part numbers in the Ford parts catalog. Similar-looking parts from another vehicle may be incompatible.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B00C2:11 is retrieved on demand.
diagnostics.meaning: The OCSM detects its belt-tension reference-voltage circuit shorted to ground.
diagnostics.next: Use A2–A3 to distinguish the buckle sensor from wiring before A5 confirmation.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B00C2:12 is retrieved on demand.
diagnostics.meaning: The OCSM detects voltage on the belt-tension reference circuit indicating a short to battery.
diagnostics.next: Follow A4's depowered disconnection and controlled voltage test.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B00A0:09 accompanies the occupant-classification fault.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM has received an OCS fault message and requests the airbag warning indicator.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose the underlying OCSM codes; this accompanying code does not prove the RCM is defective.

verification.title: Complete the SRS prove-out
verification.body: With airbags installed and connected, switch ignition off, wait 10 seconds, then switch it on. The warning indicator should illuminate for approximately 6 seconds and turn off. Monitor for approximately 30 seconds. Failure to light, continued illumination, flashing, a fault chime or an SRS message requires further diagnosis.

verification.title: Record a fault-free completion
verification.body: Record the original codes, repair and final self-test result. Complete the repowering routine's continuous-memory code clearing after faults are resolved. Release the vehicle only with no on-demand restraint faults and a successful prove-out.

guides.title: Diagnose convertible driver upper side airbag faults
guides.summary: Trace B1405 faults through the driver upper side airbag wiring, connections and control module before deciding what needs replacement.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) monitors the electrical deployment loop serving the convertible’s driver upper side airbag. A fault illuminates the airbag warning indicator. Although the diagnostic labels mention a curtain, this test concerns the driver upper side airbag and its seat-backrest wiring.
guides.why: Harness movement and poor terminal contact can change resistance intermittently. A partly seated connector position assurance (CPA) tab can also leave protective shorting bars engaged. A disappearing code therefore does not, by itself, establish a sound repair.

when.summary: An RCM self-test or stored fault record identifies a driver upper side airbag B1405 fault.

prepare.title: Use qualified restraint-system service capability
prepare.detail: Read the pyrotechnic precautions and full supplemental restraint system (SRS) depowering and repowering procedures. Incorrect handling can cause accidental deployment.

prepare.title: Prepare the diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use an RCM-capable scan tool, electrical meter, correct probe adapters and the specified fused-jumper arrangement. Have Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5 available. Never probe an airbag assembly connector or back-probe a deployable device.

steps.title: Identify the active or intermittent branch
steps.body: Inspect accessible wiring and connections, then perform the ignition-on RCM self-test in A1. Record on-demand and continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) separately. If U3003:16 or U3003:17 is also present on-demand, follow Test AJ first. Memory-only B1405 faults enter the intermittent branches.

steps.title: Record deployment-loop resistance
steps.body: For resistance faults, monitor the DEPLOY_11_R parameter identification (PID) value. A2 directs an initial reading within 1.44–3.52 ohms to A12. Otherwise, perform A3’s harness-flex test and record changes. A return into range calls for depowering and repairing the affected connection or harness; persistent low or high resistance selects A4 or A6.

steps.title: Isolate the circuit using the prescribed fault changes
steps.body: Follow A4–A10 for the recorded fault. These tests distinguish wiring faults from a module that correctly recognizes a deliberately changed circuit condition. Follow every ignition, depowering, disconnection and repowering instruction. Use A7’s fused jumper only at its specified harness test points and remove it after testing. Do not perform an SRS prove-out during these repowering stages.

steps.title: Confirm an airbag-side fault before replacement
steps.body: At A11, depower and inspect terminals, inline connections, damaged wiring and CPA locks, including the airbag connector C3464. Correct concerns and reconnect as directed before self-test. If the original fault returns, remove and inspect the seat-backrest harness. Repair damage found; install a new upper side airbag only when that inspection finds no concern.

steps.title: Confirm the control-module branch
steps.body: At A12, inspect and restore the harness and RCM connections before repeating self-test. If the original code returns, check applicable Ford technical service bulletins. Follow an applicable bulletin; otherwise, the test directs RCM replacement using its complete procedure.

steps.title: Investigate faults that disappear
steps.body: A13 monitors resistance while flexing the harness; A14 checks whether a ground-short code returns. A15 uses its prescribed airbag-disconnection sequence to investigate intermittent voltage shorts. Depower before repairs. If the fault cannot be recreated, A16 checks corrosion, terminal fit, wire damage and connector locks. Do not replace components merely because a stored code remains.

steps.title: Restore the system and check all restraint faults
steps.body: Complete A17 with all SRS components reconnected and the prescribed repowering sequence. Run the full Restraints self-test. Diagnose every returned on-demand fault, including faults from other applicable restraint modules, and do not clear codes until all faults are resolved.

watchFor.title: Damaged restraint terminals
watchFor.body: Replace damaged restraint terminals using service connector pigtails; do not repair the terminals themselves.

watchFor.title: Similar-looking replacement parts
watchFor.body: Verify the correct SRS part number in the Ford parts catalog. Physical similarity does not establish compatibility.

notes: Disconnect or reconnect SRS components only when the selected test step instructs it.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1405:11 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detected a short to ground.
diagnostics.next: A8 checks for a change to B1405:13 with the airbag disconnected; an unchanged fault leads to A9 wiring isolation.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1405:12 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The deployment circuit has unexpected voltage.
diagnostics.next: A10 isolates the circuit ends and checks voltage. Voltage requires circuit repair; no voltage leads to A12.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1405:13 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is too high or the circuit is open.
diagnostics.next: After the PID checks, A6 tests continuity; sound wiring proceeds to A7’s controlled change to B1405:1A.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1405:1A is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is below the permitted threshold.
diagnostics.next: A4 checks for a change to B1405:13 after disconnection; otherwise A5 checks for a short between circuits.

verification.title: Record the resistance result
verification.body: Record the final DEPLOY_11_R reading and harness-test response. Resistance must remain within 1.44–3.52 ohms even when no on-demand code is present.

verification.title: Confirm release readiness
verification.body: Record the final Restraints self-test result. The SRS must be fully operational and free of faults before vehicle release.

guides.title: Diagnose passenger upper side-airbag circuit faults on a convertible
guides.summary: Trace passenger upper side-airbag circuit faults through wiring, connectors, the airbag and the restraints control module before replacing components.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) monitors the passenger upper side-airbag deployment circuit and requests the airbag warning indicator when it detects an electrical fault. This diagnosis separates a damaged circuit or connection from an airbag or module fault, including faults that disappear during testing.
guides.why: The measured resistance represents the whole deployment loop. Harness movement and terminal fit can change it, so an absent fault code alone does not establish a repair: resistance must also remain within the required range.
searchTerms: passenger upper side airbag circuit fault

when.summary: When a convertible records B1408:11, B1408:12, B1408:13 or B1408:1A, either currently or in continuous memory.

prepare.title: Use qualified restraints personnel
prepare.detail: Read the pyrotechnic precautions before work. Incorrect supplemental restraint system (SRS) testing can cause deployment. Never probe an airbag assembly connector or back-probe a deployable device.

prepare.title: Prepare the prescribed diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting RCM self-tests and parameter identification (PID) readings, suitable electrical test equipment, correct probe adapters and the prescribed fused jumper. Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5 provide circuit and repair information.

prepare.title: Follow the power-state sequence
prepare.detail: Use the linked SRS depowering and repowering procedures at every instructed transition. Disconnect components only when directed. Intermediate repowering specifically omits SRS prove-out.

steps.title: Establish the active diagnostic branch
steps.body: Inspect accessible wiring and connections, then perform the ignition-on RCM self-test in A1 of the convertible pinpoint test. Address on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 through Pinpoint Test AJ first. Separate current B1408 faults from continuous-memory-only faults, which follow the intermittent branches.

steps.title: Record deployment-loop resistance
steps.body: For current B1408:13 or B1408:1A, follow A2–A3 and record DEPLOY_14_R. An initial reading between 1.44 and 3.52 ohms leads to A12. Otherwise, monitor while flexing the harness and connectors. A return into range directs depowering and connection repair; persistent low or high resistance selects A4 or A6 respectively.

steps.title: Separate resistance faults from component faults
steps.body: Follow A4–A7 for the specified isolated wiring measurements and controlled fault changes. Disconnecting C219 should change a low-resistance fault to an open; the prescribed harness-side fused jumper should change an open to low resistance. These responses lead to airbag confirmation. Other results direct wiring repair or RCM confirmation. Remove the jumper as instructed.

steps.title: Investigate ground and voltage shorts separately
steps.body: A8–A9 check whether disconnecting C219 changes the ground-short fault to an open, then test isolated wiring if necessary. A10 disconnects C219 and the RCM before the prescribed powered voltage check. Unexpected harness voltage requires circuit repair; no voltage leads to RCM confirmation.

steps.title: Inspect connections before confirming a component
steps.body: In A11–A12, depower and inspect damaged wiring, loose or spread terminals, and the RCM connector locks. The airbag branch also checks C3465 locking tabs and its clip. Repair concerns, reconnect all required components and repeat self-test. If the original fault disappears, continue with intermittent diagnosis without replacing components.

steps.title: Apply the component-replacement decisions
steps.body: If A11 reproduces the original code, use the Side Airbag removal procedure to inspect the passenger seat-backrest harness. Repair damage; install a new upper side airbag only if no harness concern is found. If A12 confirms the RCM branch, check applicable technical service bulletins in OASIS before proceeding to RCM replacement.

steps.title: Attempt to reproduce intermittent faults
steps.body: A13 monitors resistance while moving the harness for open or low-resistance concerns. A14 combines harness movement with self-test for a ground short. A15 requires C219 disconnection and the prescribed repowering sequence before recreating a voltage short. Depower before repairing a reproduced concern.

steps.title: Finish the unreproduced-fault inspection
steps.body: If the fault remains absent, follow A16 with the SRS depowered. Inspect corrosion, terminals, wiring and connector-lock seating. Repair identified damage; use service connector pigtails when restraint terminals need repair. If nothing is found, install no speculative components and proceed to A17.

watchFor.title: An attached connector can still cause low resistance
watchFor.body: An incompletely seated connector position assurance (CPA) tab can leave the component’s shorting bars engaged.

watchFor.title: Physical similarity does not establish compatibility
watchFor.body: Verify replacement restraint components against the Ford parts catalog.

notes: The scan-tool labels include “curtain”; this convertible procedure diagnoses the passenger upper side airbag and its associated wiring.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1408:11 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects a passenger deployment-circuit short to ground.
diagnostics.next: Use A8 for a current fault or A14 for an intermittent fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1408:12 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects unexpected deployment-circuit voltage.
diagnostics.next: Use A10 for a current fault or A15 for an intermittent fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1408:13 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is above the desired range.
diagnostics.next: Use A2 for a current fault or A13 for an intermittent fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1408:1A is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is below the desired range.
diagnostics.next: Use A2 for a current fault or A13 for an intermittent fault.

verification.title: Record the resistance result
verification.body: Confirm and record DEPLOY_14_R within 1.44–3.52 ohms, including the required harness test, even when no on-demand code remains.

verification.title: Complete the full restraints self-test
verification.body: Follow A17: restore connections, repower as directed without intermediate prove-out, and run the ignition-on Restraints self-test. This includes the occupant classification system module and any additional module appropriate to fitted equipment. Resolve all on-demand faults before clearing codes. Release the vehicle only with the SRS fully operational and fault-free.

guides.title: Diagnose driver-door impact-sensor faults on a convertible
guides.summary: Trace driver-door impact-sensor codes through connector, wiring and controlled fault-change tests before choosing a sensor or module repair.
guides.introduction: The driver front door side impact sensor supplies information used by the restraints control module (RCM) to assess a side impact. The RCM monitors its electrical circuits and can illuminate the airbag warning indicator when a fault occurs. This diagnosis separates a sensor fault from damaged wiring, poor connections or an RCM concern.
guides.why: A fault code identifies what the RCM detects, not automatically which component needs replacement. Deliberately changing the circuit condition at specified stages establishes whether the RCM recognizes that change.

when.summary: When the RCM records B1414:11, B1414:93, B1427:11 or B14EB:11 on a convertible.
notes: Pedestrian-protection wiring checks apply only if that wiring is fitted.

prepare.title: Use qualified restraints-system service
prepare.detail: Read the pyrotechnic precautions before work. Incorrect supplemental restraint system (SRS) service can cause accidental deployment. Never probe an impact sensor or attempt to test it with a multimeter.

prepare.title: Arrange circuit-testing capability
prepare.detail: Have an RCM-capable scan tool, multimeter, correct connector probe adapters, fused jumper and Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5. Measurements are on the specified wiring connections.

prepare.title: Follow the power-state instructions
prepare.detail: Use the exact depowering and repowering procedures at every instructed transition in the pinpoint test. Disconnect SRS components only when directed; do not perform SRS prove-out during the intermediate repowering stages.

steps.title: Establish whether the fault is present
steps.body: Inspect harnesses and connectors, then perform the ignition-on RCM self-test in A1. Diagnose on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 first. Otherwise, present short-to-ground codes enter A2, while B1414:93 enters A4. A code present only in continuous memory follows the intermittent-fault route, A9.

steps.title: Separate a shorted sensor from shorted wiring
steps.body: In A2, depower, disconnect sensor C567, repower as directed and repeat self-test. A change to B1414:93 directs sensor replacement. Without that change, A3 isolates the RCM and checks for shorts to ground and between circuits, including the conditional pedestrian-protection wiring. Every specified resistance must exceed 10,000 ohms; otherwise repair the circuit.

steps.title: Investigate a no-operation code
steps.body: A4 first checks that C567 and RCM connectors C310A and C310B are seated and locked, with the SRS depowered. Retest after repowering. If B1414:93 persists, A5 isolates the sensor and RCM, then checks the specified harness connections for voltage under the instructed powered conditions. Any voltage requires circuit repair.

steps.title: Check continuity and the RCM response
steps.body: With no unwanted voltage, A6 depowers the system and checks both circuits end to end; each must measure less than 0.5 ohm. Repair a failed circuit. If both pass, follow A7's fused-jumper test exactly. A change from B1414:93 to the specified short-to-ground codes directs sensor replacement. Remove the jumper on either outcome; an unchanged code proceeds to A8.

steps.title: Confirm an RCM fault before replacement
steps.body: In A8, depower and inspect terminals, wiring and connector position assurance locks. Repair defects and reconnect all required SRS components before retesting. If the original code returns on-demand, check OASIS for applicable Technical Service Bulletins; follow any applicable bulletin, otherwise replace the RCM. If the code disappears, continue to A9 without replacing components.

steps.title: Resolve the intermittent branch
steps.body: A9 repeats the depowered connector, harness and lock inspection, then reconnects and retests. A returning short-to-ground code loops to A2; returning B1414:93 loops to A4. If the fault cannot be recreated, do not install new SRS components.

steps.title: Complete the whole restraints check
steps.body: Follow A10 to restore connections and repower as instructed, then run the scan tool's Restraints self-test. Resolve every on-demand code from all modules included in that test before clearing codes or releasing the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Damaged restraint terminals
watchFor.body: Use service connector pigtails when terminals need repair; do not repair the restraint terminals themselves.

watchFor.title: Physically similar replacement parts
watchFor.body: Confirm the correct Ford part number. Appearance alone does not establish SRS compatibility.

notes: An active fault cannot be cleared successfully until it is corrected and no longer appears on-demand.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1414:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects a short to ground on the driver-door sensor feed.
diagnostics.next: Follow A2 and, if required, A3.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1414:93 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible causes include a faulty sensor, feed short to voltage, or an open feed or return.
diagnostics.next: Begin with the connector checks in A4.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1427:11 or B14EB:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These driver-outer and passenger-outer pedestrian-protection codes can also reflect a driver-door sensor or feed short when the relevant wiring is fitted.
diagnostics.next: Follow the conditional short-circuit checks; do not assume a pedestrian sensor has failed.

verification.title: Record the final self-test
verification.body: Record the final on-demand Restraints self-test results and any unresolved codes. The SRS must be fully operational and fault-free before release.

guides.title: Diagnose convertible passenger-door side impact sensor faults
guides.summary: Trace passenger-door impact-sensor faults through connector, wiring and controlled fault-response checks before replacing a sensor or control module.
guides.introduction: The passenger-door side impact sensor provides information used by the restraints control module (RCM) to assess a side impact. The RCM monitors its circuits and requests the airbag warning indicator when it detects a fault. This convertible diagnostic route distinguishes wiring and connection problems from a defective sensor or RCM.
guides.why: Most concerns arise in wiring or connectors. Deliberately changing the reported fault helps establish whether the RCM responds correctly. These checks involve the supplemental restraint system (SRS), so connection changes, depowering and repowering must follow the exact test sequence to prevent accidental deployment and misleading results.

when.summary: When the RCM records B1418:11, B1418:93 or an applicable B1424:11.
notes: Use pedestrian-protection wiring checks only when that wiring is fitted.

prepare.title: Use qualified SRS personnel
prepare.detail: Follow the linked pyrotechnic precautions and complete depowering and repowering procedures. Disconnect or reconnect SRS components only when the pinpoint test directs it.

prepare.title: Prepare diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Have an RCM-capable scan tool, multimeter, correct connector probe adapters, fused jumper wire and Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5. Never probe an impact sensor or deployable-device connector; the electrical checks concern the specified harness circuits.

steps.title: Retrieve faults and choose the branch — A1
steps.body: Inspect for damaged harnesses and loose or damaged connectors. With ignition ON, run the RCM self-test. Diagnose on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 first. Otherwise, active short-to-ground codes lead to A2, B1418:93 leads to A4, and continuous-memory-only faults lead to A9.

steps.title: Test the short-to-ground fault response — A2
steps.body: Turn ignition OFF, depower the SRS and disconnect sensor C644. Repower without proving out the SRS, turn ignition ON and repeat the self-test. A change to B1418:93 directs replacement of the passenger-door sensor, then A10. An unchanged fault leads to A3.

steps.title: Check wiring isolation — A3
steps.body: Turn ignition OFF, depower and disconnect RCM C310A and C310B. Follow A3's ground and cross-circuit resistance checks, including the conditional pedestrian-protection wiring checks. All readings must exceed 10,000 ohms. Repair failing circuits and proceed to A10; passing results lead to A8.

steps.title: Check connections for a no-operation fault — A4
steps.body: With ignition OFF and SRS depowered, make sure C644, C310A and C310B are seated and locked. Repower without prove-out, turn ignition ON and self-test. If B1418:93 clears, proceed to A10; if it remains, continue to A5.

steps.title: Check for voltage and open circuits — A5–A6
steps.body: Turn ignition OFF, depower and disconnect C644 and both RCM connectors. Repower without prove-out and turn ignition ON. Any voltage from either specified C644 harness terminal to ground requires circuit repair, then A10. If none is present, turn ignition OFF and depower before A6's continuity checks. Both paths must measure less than 0.5 ohm; repair failures or continue to A7.

steps.title: Check the no-operation fault response — A7
steps.body: While depowered, reconnect the RCM and fit the specified fused jumper between C644 harness pins 1 and 2. Repower without prove-out, turn ignition ON and self-test. A change to B1418:11 and, if applicable, B1424:11 directs sensor replacement and A10. Otherwise proceed to A8. Remove the jumper in either branch.

steps.title: Confirm a possible RCM fault — A8
steps.body: Turn ignition OFF and depower. Inspect terminals, wiring and connector-position-assurance locks; repair concerns and reconnect all components. Repower without prove-out, turn ignition ON and self-test. If the original code remains, check Ford OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins: follow a relevant bulletin, or replace the RCM if none applies, then A10. If absent, continue to A9 without replacing components.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent faults — A9
steps.body: Turn ignition OFF, depower and disconnect C644 and both RCM connectors. Inspect terminals, wire connections, harness damage and connector locks. Repair concerns, reconnect, repower without prove-out, turn ignition ON and self-test. Recurring codes return to A2 or A4. If the fault cannot be recreated, install no new SRS components and proceed to A10.

steps.title: Run the complete restraints check — A10
steps.body: With ignition OFF, follow A10 to reconnect any remaining disconnected components and repower if previously directed, without prove-out at this stage. Turn ignition ON and run the full Restraints self-test across the modules reported by that menu. Diagnose all on-demand faults before clearing any codes.

watchFor.title: Damaged restraint connector terminals
watchFor.body: Replace affected terminals using service connector pigtails; do not repair the terminals themselves.

watchFor.title: Incorrect replacement components
watchFor.body: Verify the Ford catalog part number. Physically similar SRS components from another vehicle may be incompatible.

notes: Use the linked pinpoint procedure for exact connector tables and every power-state transition.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1418:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects the passenger-door sensor feed circuit shorted to ground.
diagnostics.next: Follow A2 and, if necessary, A3.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1418:93 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible causes include a faulty sensor, a feed short to voltage, or an open feed or return.
diagnostics.next: Start with connection checks at A4.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1424:11 is recorded with the relevant wiring fitted.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible causes include a shorted passenger-door sensor, grounded sensor feed or grounded pedestrian-protection wiring.
diagnostics.next: Use the applicable A2–A3 branch; the code alone does not identify the failed component.

verification.title: Establish release readiness
verification.body: The full Restraints self-test must return no on-demand faults. The SRS must be fully operational and fault-free before vehicle release.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record the original codes, whether they were active or memory-only, the decisive branch results, repairs and final self-test outcome.

guides.title: Diagnose driver airbag stage 2 circuit faults
guides.summary: Trace driver airbag stage 2 faults through the wiring, clockspring, connections and control module before replacing components.
guides.introduction: The driver airbag’s second deployment circuit connects to the restraints control module (RCM) through the clockspring, which maintains electrical continuity as the steering wheel turns. This diagnosis separates connection and wiring problems from faults in the clockspring, airbag or RCM.
guides.why: Harness movement and loose terminals can change resistance enough to cause an intermittent fault. A disappearing code is therefore insufficient: the RCM’s measured deployment-loop resistance must also return to the specified range.

when.summary: An RCM self-test or stored fault identifies a driver airbag stage 2 circuit concern.

prepare.title: Arrange qualified restraint-system diagnosis
prepare.detail: Supplemental restraint system (SRS) work requires qualified personnel following the pyrotechnic precautions. Never probe airbag assembly connectors or back-probe deployable devices. Carry a live airbag with its cover away from your body; never place it cover-down.

prepare.title: Prepare electrical testing and access
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting RCM self-tests and live parameters, a suitable meter, correct probe adapters, and the specified fused jumper. Have Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5 available. Follow the linked shroud, airbag, depowering and repowering procedures at each instructed stage.

steps.title: Establish whether the fault is present
steps.body: Begin with A1 of the driver stage 2 pinpoint test. An on-demand diagnostic trouble code (DTC) identifies a current fault; a continuous-memory-only code follows the intermittent branch. Diagnose on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 first using the voltage-fault procedure.

steps.title: Record resistance and test movement
steps.body: For resistance faults, record the DEPLOY_01_R parameter identification (PID) value. The desired range is 1.62–4.46 ohms. An initially acceptable reading leads to A18. Otherwise, A3 tests the accessible harness while tilting and rotating the wheel; a return to range directs attention to disturbed wiring, connections or the clockspring.

steps.title: Separate causes of low resistance
steps.body: A4–A6 remove the airbag and then isolate the clockspring as directed. A change from low resistance to open circuit leads to airbag or clockspring confirmation respectively. If neither changes the fault, the isolated wiring is checked for a short between circuits before considering the RCM.

steps.title: Trace an open or excessive resistance
steps.body: A7–A10 check continuity through the complete path, then exclude the clockspring when needed. Prescribed fused-jumper tests on the disconnected harness check whether the RCM recognizes deliberately introduced low resistance. Remove each jumper as instructed; the responses determine which component-confirmation branch follows.

steps.title: Follow the correct short-circuit branch
steps.body: For a ground fault, A11–A13 progressively isolate the airbag and clockspring before checking wiring to ground. For unwanted voltage, A14–A15 isolate the airbag and clockspring: an open-circuit response leads to clockspring confirmation, while voltage remaining on isolated wiring requires circuit repair.

steps.title: Confirm before replacing a component
steps.body: A16–A18 inspect wiring, terminals and connector locks, restore all connections, and repeat self-test. Replace the indicated airbag or clockspring only if the original code returns. Before RCM replacement, check applicable technical service bulletins through OASIS. A disappearing fault moves to intermittent diagnosis.

steps.title: Recreate intermittent resistance faults
steps.body: A19 monitors resistance while moving the harness and steering wheel. Incorrect resistance occurring only during wheel rotation directs clockspring replacement. Other reproduced faults require depowering and repair. If resistance remains acceptable, continue to the final connector inspection without speculative replacement.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent shorts and connections
steps.body: A20 tests for a returning ground-fault code during harness movement. A21 requires airbag removal, depowering and controlled repowering before seeking an intermittent voltage fault. If neither reproduces, A22 checks corrosion, damaged wiring and connector retention. Repair findings; do not replace components simply because a stored code exists.

watchFor.title: A connector that looks attached but is not secured
watchFor.body: An incompletely seated connector position assurance (CPA) tab can leave protective shorting bars engaged and produce low resistance.

watchFor.title: Faults deliberately created during testing
watchFor.body: Disconnecting the driver airbag normally produces open-circuit codes on both stages. During isolation tests, repower without performing SRS prove-out when instructed.

notes: Use service connector pigtails when restraint terminals require repair. Confirm replacement restraint part numbers in the parts catalog.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0002:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The stage 2 circuit has a detected short to ground.
diagnostics.next: Use A11–A13 for a current fault or A20 for an intermittent fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0002:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The stage 2 circuit has detected unwanted voltage.
diagnostics.next: Use A14–A15 or the intermittent A21 branch.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0002:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is above the desired range.
diagnostics.next: Start at A2 for a current fault or A19 for an intermittent fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0002:1A is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is below the desired range.
diagnostics.next: Use resistance testing to distinguish connections, wiring and components.

verification.title: Record the resistance result
verification.body: Confirm and record DEPLOY_01_R within 1.62–4.46 ohms, including the relevant movement test. Absence of an on-demand code alone does not establish repair.

verification.title: Complete the restraints self-test
verification.body: At A23, reconnect all components with ignition off and repower as directed. Run Restraints self-test across applicable fitted modules. Resolve every on-demand fault before clearing codes or releasing the vehicle.

guides.title: Diagnose driver knee airbag circuit faults B0004:11, B0004:12, B0004:13 and B0004:1A
guides.summary: Trace driver knee airbag circuit faults through wiring, connectors and controlled module-response tests before authorizing component replacement.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) monitors the driver knee airbag deployment circuit and requests the airbag warning indicator when it detects a fault. This diagnosis separates wiring and connection problems from an airbag or RCM fault. A stored diagnostic trouble code (DTC) identifies a circuit condition; it does not by itself condemn either component.
guides.why: Connector movement can change circuit resistance enough to produce an intermittent warning. Connector position assurance (CPA) tabs also release protective shorting bars: an incompletely seated tab can leave resistance too low even when the connector appears attached.

when.summary: Use when RCM testing records a driver knee airbag B0004 circuit fault, including a memory-only intermittent fault.
notes: The supplemental restraint system (SRS) must be fully operational and free of faults before vehicle release.

prepare.title: Use qualified restraint-service personnel
prepare.detail: Read the pyrotechnic precautions and complete depowering/repowering procedures first. Disconnect or reconnect components only when the pinpoint step directs it.

prepare.title: Prepare diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use an RCM-capable scan tool, appropriate electrical test equipment, correct probe adapters and the prescribed fused jumper. Have Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5 available.

steps.title: Classify the fault with A1
steps.body: Run the ignition-on RCM self-test. Diagnose on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 first. An on-demand B0004 fault follows its active branch; a continuous-memory-only fault follows A13–A15. Clearing memory cannot correct an active fault.

steps.title: Measure resistance through the module
steps.body: For B0004:13 or B0004:1A, record DEPLOY_02_R, the deployment-loop resistance parameter identification (PID). In A2, 1.44–3.52 ohms leads to A12 confirmation. Otherwise perform A3's harness movement test. Movement into range directs depowering and connection/harness repair; persistent low or high resistance selects A4 or A6.

steps.title: Separate low-resistance and open-circuit causes
steps.body: Follow A4–A7 exactly. With the airbag removed through the depowering procedure, a low-resistance fault changing to an open fault leads to airbag confirmation; an unchanged fault requires isolated harness short testing. High resistance requires harness continuity checks, followed where directed by a fused-jumper response test. A change from B0004:13 to B0004:1A leads to airbag confirmation; no change leads to RCM confirmation. Remove the jumper afterward.

steps.title: Follow the ground or voltage branch
steps.body: For B0004:11, A8 checks whether removing the airbag changes the fault to B0004:13. If so, proceed to A11; otherwise A9 checks the isolated wiring for a ground short. A10 checks isolated wiring for unwanted voltage with the specified powered test setup. Repair a detected wiring fault; satisfactory wiring results lead to A12.

steps.title: Confirm before replacing
steps.body: A11 and A12 require depowering, inspecting terminals, wiring and connector locks, correcting defects, reconnecting components and repeating self-test. At A11, recurrence of the original code directs airbag replacement. At A12, check applicable technical service bulletins first; follow one if applicable, otherwise replace the RCM only as directed. If the code disappears, investigate intermittency instead.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent faults
steps.body: A13 monitors resistance while flexing the harness; A14 checks for a returning ground-short code. A15 requires depowering and airbag removal before its powered voltage-short reproduction test. Repair reproduced faults through the specified branch. If unreproduced, A16 inspects corrosion, terminals, damaged wires and CPA locks with the system depowered; do not replace components without a directed finding.

steps.title: Restore and test the complete restraint system
steps.body: At A17, reconnect all components and install the knee airbag in the prescribed power state. Repower if required, without a prove-out at this stage, then run the full Restraints self-test. Resolve every applicable module's on-demand fault before clearing codes or releasing the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Keep measurements on the specified harness circuits
watchFor.body: Never probe airbag assembly connectors or back-probe deployable devices. The controlled fault tests are not permission to measure an airbag igniter directly.

watchFor.title: Damaged terminals and incorrect parts
watchFor.body: Replace damaged restraint connector terminals using service pigtails. Confirm replacement component part numbers; physical similarity does not establish compatibility.

watchFor.title: Live airbag handling
watchFor.body: Carry the airbag with its cover facing away from your body, and never set it down cover-first.

notes: Follow each diagnostic depowering and repowering transition; the test repeatedly specifies repowering without a prove-out at that point.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0004:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The driver knee deployment circuit has a detected short to ground.
diagnostics.next: Use A8 for an active fault or A14 for a memory-only intermittent fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0004:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The circuit has detected unwanted voltage.
diagnostics.next: Use A10 for an active fault or A15 for an intermittent fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0004:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance exceeds the desired range.
diagnostics.next: Use A2 for an active fault or A13 for an intermittent fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0004:1A is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is below the desired range.
diagnostics.next: Use A2 or A13 according to fault status; include CPA seating in inspection.

verification.title: Record resistance stability
verification.body: Record DEPLOY_02_R during the prescribed harness test. It must remain within 1.44–3.52 ohms before the resistance concern is considered repaired, even without an on-demand code.

verification.title: Record the final system result
verification.body: Save the full Restraints self-test outcome. Additional on-demand faults require diagnosis; an unreproduced intermittent concern does not justify speculative parts replacement.

guides.title: Diagnose deployable steering-column faults B0005:11, :12, :13 and :1A
guides.summary: Trace a steering-column deployment-circuit fault through its wiring, connectors, deployable device and control module before choosing a repair.
guides.introduction: The steering column includes a deployable device belonging to the Supplemental Restraint System (SRS). The restraints control module (RCM) monitors its electrical deployment loop and requests the airbag warning indicator when it detects a fault. These tests distinguish a connection problem from a defective column or controller.
guides.why: Terminal movement can change resistance enough to make a fault intermittent. Connector Position Assurance (CPA) tabs also release protective shorting bars: an incompletely seated tab can leave resistance too low. A disappearing warning or absent current code therefore does not, by itself, establish a successful repair.

when.summary: When an RCM self-test or stored fault record identifies a B0005 steering-column deployment-circuit code.
notes: Diagnose on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 first through the linked supply-voltage test.

prepare.title: Use qualified restraint-system personnel
prepare.detail: Read the pyrotechnic precautions and have the SRS depowering and repowering procedures available. Disconnect or reconnect restraint components only when the pinpoint step directs it; never back-probe a deployable-device connector.

prepare.title: Prepare the diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use an RCM-capable scan tool, suitable electrical measuring equipment, correct probe adapters and the fused jumper required by the directed test. Wiring Diagrams Cell 46 identifies the circuit; Cell 5 supports wiring repairs.

steps.title: Establish whether the fault is present
steps.body: Run the ignition-on RCM self-test at A1. An on-demand B0005 code follows its active-fault branch; a continuous-memory-only code follows the intermittent branch. Resolve the specified supply-voltage codes before interpreting the deployment circuit.

steps.title: Record deployment-loop resistance
steps.body: For B0005:13 or B0005:1A, use A2–A3 to monitor the DEPLOY_04_R parameter identification (PID). The required range is 1.44–3.52 ohms. Record baseline and harness-flex readings. Movement that restores the range directs connection or harness repair after depowering; an initially acceptable reading leads to A12.

steps.title: Separate low resistance from an open circuit
steps.body: Follow A4–A7 according to the reading. These steps isolate the column, check harness continuity or cross-circuit shorts, and deliberately change the reported fault. The prescribed fused jumper belongs at the disconnected harness connection, not across the deployable device. Remove it on either test outcome. A correct fault change leads to confirmation, not immediate replacement.

steps.title: Follow the appropriate short-circuit branch
steps.body: For B0005:11, A8 checks whether disconnecting the column changes the fault to an open; otherwise A9 checks isolated wiring for ground shorts. B0005:12 follows A10, which checks isolated wiring for unwanted voltage using its specific depowering, disconnection and repowering sequence.

steps.title: Confirm any component diagnosis
steps.body: At A11 or A12, inspect terminals, wire damage and connector locks before reconnecting and retesting. A confirmed A11 result directs a new steering column including its deployable device. A confirmed A12 result requires checking applicable service bulletins before RCM replacement. If the original fault disappears, continue intermittent diagnosis without replacing components.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent faults
steps.body: A13 monitors resistance during harness movement. A14 repeats self-test while seeking an intermittent ground short. A15 seeks a voltage short with the column disconnected through the prescribed SRS sequence. If the fault cannot be recreated, A16 checks corrosion, terminal fit, wiring and CPA seating; it does not authorize speculative replacement.

steps.title: Restore connections and test the complete system
steps.body: Follow A17 to restore disconnected components, repower as directed and run the complete Restraints self-test. Diagnose every remaining on-demand restraint code before clearing codes or releasing the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Damaged restraint terminals
watchFor.body: Use service connector pigtails where restraint terminals require repair; do not reshape or repair the terminals themselves.

watchFor.title: Incorrect replacement parts
watchFor.body: Verify SRS part numbers in the parts catalog. Similar-looking components from other vehicles may be incompatible.

notes: Intermediate repowering steps explicitly defer SRS prove-out; retain that instruction throughout fault isolation.

diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects a ground short or unwanted voltage respectively.
diagnostics.next: Use A8 or A10; the code alone does not identify the failed component.

diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is above or below the permitted threshold respectively.
diagnostics.next: Begin with the measured PID and follow the corresponding resistance branch.

verification.title: Record the final resistance
verification.body: Confirm and record DEPLOY_04_R within 1.44–3.52 ohms, including the applicable harness test. An absent on-demand code does not excuse an out-of-range reading.

verification.title: Confirm complete restraint-system operation
verification.body: The final Restraints self-test must show no unresolved on-demand faults in the modules it tests. The SRS must be fully operational before vehicle release.

Required pyrotechnic handling and restraint-connector precautions.
Diagnose priority U3003:16 or U3003:17 supply-voltage faults.
Depower the SRS at each directed isolation or repair stage.
Repower the SRS at the prescribed diagnostic and restoration stages.
Remove and install the steering column when A11 confirms replacement.
Remove and install the RCM when its diagnostic branch authorizes replacement.
Diagnose additional restraint-system faults found during final testing.

guides.title: Diagnose passenger airbag stage 1 circuit faults
guides.summary: Use passenger airbag stage 1 resistance and isolation tests to distinguish wiring faults from airbag or control-module faults.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) monitors the passenger airbag’s first deployment circuit for abnormal resistance, grounding and unwanted voltage. This diagnosis follows that circuit through the harness and connections, using controlled fault changes to determine whether the airbag or RCM needs further confirmation.
guides.why: A marginal connection can change with vibration and temporarily stop setting a code. Repair therefore requires acceptable measured resistance as well as a successful self-test. Secure connector locks matter because an incompletely seated lock can leave protective shorting bars engaged.

when.summary: An RCM self-test or stored B0010 code identifies a passenger airbag stage 1 circuit concern.

prepare.title: Prepare qualified electrical diagnosis
prepare.detail: Supplemental restraint system (SRS) servicing requires qualified personnel and the pyrotechnic precautions. Use an RCM-capable scan tool, suitable meter, correct probe adapters and the specified fused jumper. Have Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5 available.

prepare.title: Plan access and safe isolation
prepare.detail: The glove compartment provides access for harness testing. Follow the linked access, depowering and repowering procedures. Never probe airbag assembly connectors or back-probe deployable devices; carry a removed live airbag cover-away and never place it cover-down.

steps.title: Identify the active diagnostic branch
steps.body: Start at A1 with an RCM self-test. Separate current, on-demand diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) from continuous-memory-only faults. Diagnose on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 first. Otherwise select the resistance, ground-short, voltage-short or intermittent branch for the recorded passenger circuit code.

steps.title: Measure resistance and disturb the harness
steps.body: Record the DEPLOY_05_R parameter identification (PID) value. The required range is 1.44–3.52 ohms. An initially acceptable value leads to A13. Otherwise remove the glove compartment and follow A3 while flexing accessible wiring and connectors; a return to range directs connector or harness repair.

steps.title: Investigate low resistance
steps.body: A4 disconnects the passenger airbag under the prescribed power sequence. A change from low resistance to open circuit leads to airbag confirmation. If unchanged, A5–A6 distinguish shorted wiring from an RCM path. The component-side measurement in A6 is at the disconnected RCM, never the airbag.

steps.title: Trace an open circuit
steps.body: A7 tests both isolated wires for continuity. Failed measurements require circuit repair. If continuity passes, A8 uses the prescribed fused jumper on the disconnected harness to introduce low resistance. A matching code change leads to airbag confirmation; no change leads to RCM confirmation. Remove the jumper in either case.

steps.title: Separate ground and voltage faults
steps.body: A9–A10 check whether disconnecting the airbag changes a ground fault to an open, then test isolated wiring if needed. A11 checks for voltage with the airbag and RCM disconnected and the system repowered as directed. Unwanted voltage requires wiring repair; none leads to RCM confirmation.

steps.title: Confirm the suspected component
steps.body: A12–A13 inspect wiring and connector position assurance (CPA) locks, restore all connections, and repeat self-test. Replace the passenger airbag only if its confirmation branch retrieves the original code. Before RCM replacement, check applicable technical service bulletins through OASIS. A disappearing fault requires intermittent diagnosis.

steps.title: Reproduce intermittent faults before choosing parts
steps.body: A14 monitors resistance during harness movement; A15 repeats self-test for a ground fault. A16 requires passenger airbag disconnection through the prescribed depowering and repowering sequence before seeking a voltage fault. If unreproduced, A17 inspects wiring, corrosion and connector retention. Repair findings without speculative component replacement.

watchFor.title: Shorting bars affect interpretation
watchFor.body: In the ground and voltage checks, the RCM connector’s shorting bar means either wire may contain the fault. Never remove or defeat it.

watchFor.title: Expected additional codes
watchFor.body: Disconnecting the passenger airbag normally creates open-circuit codes for both deployment stages and the canister vent. During isolation tests, omit SRS prove-out when instructed.

notes: Use service pigtails when restraint terminals need repair. Check replacement airbag and module part numbers for compatibility.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0010:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The stage 1 circuit has a detected short to ground.
diagnostics.next: Use A9–A10 for a current fault or A15 for an intermittent fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0010:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The stage 1 circuit has detected unwanted voltage.
diagnostics.next: Use A11 or the intermittent A16 branch.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0010:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance exceeds the desired range.
diagnostics.next: Start at A2, or A14 if recorded only in memory.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0010:1A is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is below the desired range.
diagnostics.next: Check resistance, connector seating and the applicable isolation branch.

verification.title: Record acceptable loop resistance
verification.body: Confirm and record DEPLOY_05_R within 1.44–3.52 ohms during the relevant harness test, even if no on-demand code remains.

verification.title: Check the complete restraint system
verification.body: At A18, restore connections with ignition off and repower as directed. Run Restraints self-test across applicable fitted modules. Diagnose every remaining on-demand fault before clearing codes; release requires a fully operational, fault-free SRS.

SRS depowering at instructed diagnostic stages.
SRS repowering at instructed diagnostic stages.
