guides.title: Diagnose B0011 passenger airbag stage 2 circuit faults
guides.summary: Use resistance data, controlled fault changes and connector inspections to distinguish passenger airbag stage 2 wiring faults from airbag or control-module failures.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) monitors the passenger frontal airbag's stage 2 deployment circuit. An electrical fault stores a diagnostic trouble code (DTC) and requests the airbag warning indicator. This test separates wiring, connection, airbag and RCM causes; the code alone does not identify a failed component.
guides.why: Terminal movement and wire strain can change circuit resistance intermittently. A connector position assurance (CPA) tab that is not fully seated can also leave a deployable component's shorting bars engaged. Consequently, an absent current code is insufficient: the measured deployment-loop resistance must be within the desired range.

when.summary: When B0011:11, B0011:12, B0011:13 or B0011:1A is stored in the RCM.
notes: An on-demand code indicates a current fault; a continuous-memory-only code follows the intermittent branch.
Diagnose on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 first through Pinpoint Test AJ.

prepare.title: Establish safe testing capability
prepare.detail: Follow Pyrotechnic Device Health and Safety Precautions. Have an RCM-capable scan tool, suitable electrical measuring equipment, correct probe adapters and the specified fused jumper for the branch requiring it.

prepare.title: Have the exact test and access instructions
prepare.detail: Use A1–A17 in the linked pinpoint procedure, Wiring Diagrams Cell 46 for circuit identification and Cell 5 for repairs. Have glove-compartment removal and SRS depowering/repowering procedures available.

prepare.title: Respect component and connector boundaries
prepare.detail: Disconnect or reconnect supplemental restraint system (SRS) components only when the selected step directs. Never probe an airbag assembly connector or back-probe a deployable device. Measurements and jumpers belong only on the prescribed harness circuits.

steps.title: Retrieve codes and choose the branch — A1
steps.body: Inspect for damaged wiring and loose or damaged connectors, then perform the RCM self-test. Resolve priority U3003 codes first. Route current resistance faults to A2, short-to-ground faults to A8 and short-to-voltage faults to A10. Memory-only faults go to A13, A14 or A15 respectively.

steps.title: Record resistance and test harness sensitivity — A2–A3
steps.body: Monitor the DEPLOY_06_R parameter identification (PID). A reading between 1.44 and 3.52 ohms at A2 leads to A12. Otherwise, remove the glove compartment and monitor while flexing the harness and connectors. If movement brings the reading into range, depower and repair the connection or wiring concern. Persistent low resistance leads to A4; high resistance leads to A6.

steps.title: Separate low-resistance and open-circuit causes — A4–A7
steps.body: Use the prescribed power-state sequence to disconnect the airbag. A low-resistance code changing to an open code leads to airbag confirmation at A11; otherwise A5 checks for a harness short. For high resistance, A6 checks both circuit continuities. If they pass, A7 uses its specified harness-side fused jumper: an open-to-low-resistance code change leads to A11; no change leads to A12. Remove the jumper after either result.

steps.title: Isolate ground and voltage faults — A8–A10
steps.body: At A8, a ground-short code changing to an open code after the prescribed airbag disconnection leads to A11. Otherwise A9 isolates and tests the harness for ground shorts. A10 instead measures for unwanted voltage with the airbag and RCM disconnected under its controlled repowering sequence. Repair detected circuit faults; passing harness checks lead to A12.

steps.title: Confirm before replacing a component — A11–A12
steps.body: Depower, inspect terminals, wiring and connector locks, and correct concerns before reconnecting and repeating the self-test. At A11, return of the original code directs passenger-airbag replacement. At A12, check applicable Technical Service Bulletins in OASIS first; follow an applicable bulletin, otherwise replace the RCM as directed. If the original code disappears, continue with intermittent testing without installing new components.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent resistance faults — A13
steps.body: Monitor and record DEPLOY_06_R while flexing the harness and connectors. An out-of-range result requires depowering and repair. A stable in-range result means the fault cannot presently be recreated; proceed to A16.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent shorts — A14–A15
steps.body: A14 uses harness movement followed by self-test to seek B0011:11. A15 seeks B0011:12 after its specified depowering, passenger-airbag disconnection and repowering sequence. A reproduced fault requires depowering and repair; an unreproduced fault leads to A16 without component replacement.

steps.title: Inspect unresolved intermittent connections — A16
steps.body: Depower and follow the specified disconnection. Inspect for corrosion, loose or spread terminals, frayed connections and damaged wiring. Check the RCM connector locks and passenger-airbag CPA tab for seating and damage. Replace damaged restraint connector terminals using service pigtails; do not repair the terminals themselves.

steps.title: Complete the final restraints test — A17
steps.body: Follow A17's reconnection and repowering sequence, then perform the complete Restraints self-test. Diagnose every remaining on-demand restraint code. Do not clear codes while unresolved faults remain.

watchFor.title: Expected codes during isolation
watchFor.body: Airbag disconnection also creates stage 1 and canister-vent open codes. Intermediate repowering steps expressly defer SRS prove-out.

watchFor.title: Replacement-part and handling errors
watchFor.body: Verify the correct component part number. Carry a live airbag with its deployment face away from the body and never place it face-down.

notes: The article title identifies Test F; its executable steps are labeled A1–A17.
Follow the final self-test for actual vehicle equipment; optional modules in the shared routine do not establish Mustang fitment.

diagnostics.finding: B0011:11 — short to ground.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects a stage 2 circuit grounded unexpectedly.
diagnostics.next: Use A8–A9 when current or A14 when intermittent.

diagnostics.finding: B0011:12 — short to battery.
diagnostics.meaning: Unexpected voltage is present in the monitored circuit.
diagnostics.next: Use A10 when current or A15 when intermittent.

diagnostics.finding: B0011:13 — open circuit.
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is above the desired range.
diagnostics.next: Use A2–A3 and the high-resistance branch, or A13 for memory-only faults.

diagnostics.finding: B0011:1A — resistance below threshold.
diagnostics.meaning: Loop resistance is too low; wiring or connector shorting-bar engagement may be involved.
diagnostics.next: Use A2–A3 and the low-resistance branch, or A13 for memory-only faults.

verification.title: Record resistance and test results
verification.body: Record initial and final codes and harness-test PID readings. Resistance must be within 1.44–3.52 ohms; absence of an on-demand code alone does not establish repair.

verification.title: Confirm full restraint-system readiness
verification.body: All SRS components must be reconnected and the final Restraints self-test must show no on-demand faults. The SRS must be fully operational and fault-free before vehicle release.

procedures.purpose: Passenger frontal airbag stage 2 active and intermittent diagnosis through A1–A17, including exact measurements and branches.
Required pyrotechnic-component qualifications, handling and electrical safety precautions.
Diagnose priority on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 before passenger-airbag codes.
Remove and reinstall the glove compartment for access.
Depower the SRS wherever the selected test step requires.
Repower the SRS at the specified diagnostic and completion stages.
Replace the passenger airbag only after A11 confirms the fault.
Replace the RCM only after A12 confirmation and the required bulletin check.
Diagnose additional restraint faults found during the final self-test.

applicability.equipment: Passenger frontal airbag stage 2 circuit; qualified supplemental restraint system and pyrotechnic-component service personnel.

guides.title: Diagnose passenger knee airbag circuit faults
guides.summary: Use B0013 fault types, measured deployment-loop data and controlled isolation tests to distinguish wiring, connector, airbag and module concerns.
guides.introduction: The passenger knee airbag is part of the supplemental restraint system (SRS). Its deployment circuit carries the electrical command from the restraints control module (RCM), which also monitors the circuit for faults. B0013 codes can reflect poor connections, damaged wiring, unexpected voltage or a component fault. This diagnosis separates those possibilities before authorizing replacement.
guides.why: Harness movement and terminal fit can change circuit resistance enough to make a warning intermittent. The repair therefore requires acceptable live resistance data, even when a fault code no longer returns. Deliberately changing a fault under controlled test conditions also helps establish whether the RCM responds correctly.

when.summary: When B0013:11, :12, :13 or :1A is retrieved as a current or stored passenger knee airbag circuit fault.
notes: Diagnose on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 supply-voltage faults first.

prepare.title: Use qualified restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Pyrotechnic service is restricted to qualified personnel. Read the pyrotechnic precautions and have the complete SRS depowering and repowering procedures available. Disconnect components only at the prescribed steps.

prepare.title: Prepare the test equipment
prepare.detail: Use an RCM-capable scan tool, a multimeter, correct probe adapters and a fused jumper for the specified harness tests. Have Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5. Never probe an airbag assembly connector or back-probe a deployable device.

steps.title: Record the fault and choose its branch
steps.body: Run the RCM self-test with ignition ON. Separate on-demand faults from continuous-memory-only faults, which use the intermittent branches. After resolving any specified supply-voltage codes, route open/low resistance to A2, short to ground to A8, and short to voltage to A10.

steps.title: Assess live resistance for open or low-resistance faults
steps.body: A2 records the DEPLOY_07_R parameter identifier (PID). An in-range reading leads to A12. Otherwise, A3 monitors it while flexing accessible wiring and connectors. If movement brings it into range, depower and repair the affected connection or harness; persistently low or high readings lead to separate isolation tests.

steps.title: Isolate a low-resistance condition
steps.body: A4 follows the prescribed depower, passenger-airbag disconnection, glove-compartment access and repower sequence. A change from low resistance to open leads to airbag confirmation at A11. If unchanged, A5 isolates the RCM and checks for a short between harness circuits; repair a failed check, or proceed to A12.

steps.title: Isolate an open or high-resistance condition
steps.body: A6 checks each wire with the airbag and RCM disconnected; each must measure less than 0.5 ohm. If continuity passes, A7 uses the specified fused jumper on the harness side and checks whether the open code changes to low resistance. Remove the jumper on either result; a change leads to A11, otherwise A12.

steps.title: Separate ground faults from voltage faults
steps.body: For a short to ground, A8 disconnects the airbag under the prescribed power sequence: a change to open leads to A11; otherwise A9 checks isolated wiring to ground. A10 instead isolates both components and checks for unexpected harness voltage after directed repowering. Failed wiring checks require repair; passing checks lead to A12.

steps.title: Confirm the component decision
steps.body: A11 and A12 require depowering, connector and harness inspection, correct reconnection and another self-test. A11 authorizes airbag replacement only if the original code returns. A12 requires checking applicable service bulletins before directed RCM replacement. If the code disappears, continue with intermittent diagnosis instead of installing parts.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent faults
steps.body: A13 monitors resistance during harness movement; A14 checks for a returning ground-short code. A15 uses its specific airbag-disconnection and power sequence before attempting to reproduce a voltage-short code. Depower before repairs. If unreproduced, A16 still requires a depowered connector, harness and locking-tab inspection; no fault found does not justify replacement.

watchFor.title: Partially seated connector locks
watchFor.body: Connector Position Assurance (CPA) tabs release protective shorting bars. A partly seated tab can leave those bars engaged and produce a low-resistance fault.

watchFor.title: Damaged restraint terminals
watchFor.body: Inspect for corrosion, loose terminals and strained wires. Replace damaged restraint connector terminals using service pigtails; do not repair the terminals themselves.

notes: During the specified diagnostic repowering stages, do not perform the SRS prove-out. Follow the procedure's sequence through final testing.
Use the catalog-correct airbag. Carry a live airbag with its deployment cover away from the body, and never place it cover-down.

diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects a short to ground or unexpected voltage respectively.
diagnostics.next: Use A8–A10 for current faults or A14–A15 for intermittent faults.

diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is above or below the desired range respectively.
diagnostics.next: Use live RCM data and the appropriate isolation branch; neither code proves airbag failure.

diagnostics.finding: DEPLOY_07_R outside 1.44–3.52 ohms
diagnostics.meaning: The loop has not met the required resistance condition, even without an on-demand code.
diagnostics.next: Continue diagnosis and record the value during harness testing.

verification.title: Restore connections and test all restraints
verification.body: At A17, switch ignition OFF, reconnect all previously disconnected SRS components and repower as directed without proving out at that stage. Switch ignition ON and run Restraints self-test. Resolve every on-demand code from all fitted modules included in the test before clearing codes or releasing the vehicle.

verification.title: Record resistance and final fault status
verification.body: Retain the DEPLOY_07_R readings, including harness-test results where applicable. Confirm resistance is within 1.44–3.52 ohms and that final testing establishes a fully operational, fault-free SRS.

guides.title: Diagnose driver seatbelt buckle-switch faults
guides.summary: Trace driver buckle-switch codes through connection, circuit and fault-response checks to identify the justified repair.
guides.introduction: The driver seatbelt buckle switch supplies buckle-state information to the restraints control module (RCM). An electrical fault in this monitored circuit can illuminate the airbag warning indicator. Diagnosis distinguishes a faulty switch, wiring damage and module concerns; a switch replacement requires a complete driver buckle assembly.
guides.why: Disconnecting or temporarily joining the specified harness circuits creates a known electrical condition. The RCM's response helps locate the fault. Connector inspection remains essential because moving a poor connection during testing can temporarily make the original fault disappear.

when.summary: When driver buckle-switch codes are retrieved on-demand or remain in continuous memory.

prepare.title: Prepare for restraint-system electrical work
prepare.detail: Qualified personnel need the pyrotechnic precautions, a restraint-capable scan tool, multimeter, correct probe adapters, fused jumper and Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5.

prepare.title: Identify the connections before testing
prepare.detail: Locate buckle connector C3201, driver side-airbag inline connector C3206 and the RCM connectors. Follow each step's exact ignition and supplemental restraint system (SRS) power state; disconnect components only when directed.

steps.title: Inspect the buckle and retrieve codes
steps.body: Check buckle damage, harness damage and loose connectors. Run A1 of the [pinpoint test](#/document/G1696356). Diagnose U3003:16 or U3003:17 first through Test AJ. Active diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) follow their specific branches; continuous-memory-only faults enter A10.

steps.title: Check ground-fault and current-fault responses
steps.body: For B0050:11 or B0050:1D, A2 switches ignition off before disconnecting the buckle, then repeats self-test with ignition on. A change to B0050:13 leads to buckle confirmation at A8. An unchanged B0050:11 requires A3's isolated wiring-to-ground check; unchanged B0050:1D leads to RCM confirmation.

steps.title: Locate unwanted voltage
steps.body: For B0050:12, A4 requires SRS depowering and disconnection of the RCM, side-airbag inline connector and buckle before diagnostic repowering. Measure only the specified buckle harness point. Any voltage requires circuit repair; no voltage leads to A9.

steps.title: Trace an open circuit
steps.body: A5 requires depowering, side-airbag and buckle disconnection, then the specified fused jumper across buckle harness circuits. A change from B0050:13 to B0050:11 leads to A8. Remove the jumper after testing. Without that change, A6–A7 check isolated continuity: below 0.5 ohm for the signal circuit and below 3 ohms for the ground circuit.

steps.title: Confirm the buckle or module decision
steps.body: At A8 or A9, inspect terminals, wiring and Connector Position Assurance (CPA) locks, repair concerns and restore connections before self-test. An original code persisting at A8 directs a new driver buckle including its switch. At A9, check applicable Technical Service Bulletins before RCM replacement. If the fault disappears, continue to A10.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent connections
steps.body: A10 depowers the SRS before buckle disconnection and inspection for corrosion, loose terminals, damaged wiring and faulty connector locks. Repair concerns, reconnect and retest. A returning code re-enters its active branch; an unreproduced fault does not justify installing new components.

steps.title: Restore the complete system
steps.body: A11 requires ignition off, SRS depowering, reconnection of all components and repowering without prove-out at this stage. Switch ignition on and perform the full Restraints self-test. Diagnose remaining on-demand codes before clearing any faults.

watchFor.title: Keep testing at the designated harness points
watchFor.body: The side-airbag connector is disconnected only as directed. Never probe an airbag connector or improvise a jumper connection.

watchFor.title: Repair terminals correctly
watchFor.body: Use service connector pigtails for restraint terminal repairs. Confirm the correct replacement buckle part number.

notes: Do not mistake deliberately induced test codes for the original fault; restore required connections before confirmation self-tests.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0050:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The buckle-switch circuit is reporting a short to ground.
diagnostics.next: Start the active-fault branch at A2.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0050:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The buckle-switch circuit is reporting unwanted voltage.
diagnostics.next: Start the active-fault branch at A4.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0050:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Either buckle-switch circuit may be open.
diagnostics.next: Start the active-fault branch at A5.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0050:1D is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Measured buckle-switch circuit current is outside its acceptable range.
diagnostics.next: Start the active-fault branch at A2.

verification.title: Confirm the final self-test
verification.body: All applicable restraint modules must be free of on-demand faults, with the SRS fully operational before release.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Retain the original code, observed fault-status changes and final self-test result. Distinguish a repaired fault from an intermittent concern that could not be reproduced.

guides.title: Diagnose passenger seatbelt buckle switch circuit faults
guides.summary: Use B0052 fault responses to distinguish passenger buckle-switch problems from wiring, ground and control-module faults.
guides.introduction: The passenger buckle switch reports belt engagement to the restraints control module (RCM). The module monitors the switch circuit for electrical faults and can illuminate the airbag warning indicator when one is detected. Diagnosis determines whether the wiring needs repair, the complete buckle needs replacement, or the module requires further confirmation.
guides.why: A buckle-switch code identifies a circuit condition, not a failed buckle. Controlled disconnection and circuit tests reveal which part of the signal path is responsible.

when.summary: When B0052:11, B0052:12, B0052:13 or B0052:1D is recorded by the RCM.

prepare.title: Prepare for restraint-system electrical work
prepare.detail: Qualified personnel need an RCM-capable scan tool, electrical meter, correct probe adapters and the specified fused jumper. Read the pyrotechnic precautions before starting.

prepare.title: Inspect before isolating circuits
prepare.detail: Check the buckle for damage and inspect wiring and connectors. Follow each prescribed supplemental restraint system (SRS) depowering and repowering step; omit prove-out during interim repowering.

steps.title: Identify the active diagnostic branch
steps.body: Run A1 of the [buckle-switch test](#/document/G1696357). Diagnose on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 through Test AJ first. Current B0052 faults follow their individual branches; codes present only in continuous memory go to A10.

steps.title: Check the response to buckle disconnection
steps.body: For B0052:11 or B0052:1D, A2 switches ignition off before disconnecting C3238, then retests with ignition on. A change to B0052:13 leads to buckle confirmation at A8. An unchanged ground fault goes to A3; unchanged current-out-of-range goes to A9.

steps.title: Find unwanted ground or voltage paths
steps.body: A3 checks the isolated switch wire for a short to ground. A4 checks for unwanted voltage after depowering and disconnecting the RCM, passenger side-airbag inline connector C219 and buckle connector. Follow its prescribed repowered measurement sequence. Repair failed wiring; passing checks lead to A9.

steps.title: Trace an open circuit
steps.body: A5 requires depowering and isolation of C219 and the buckle before its specified fused-jumper test. A change from B0052:13 to B0052:11 leads to A8. Otherwise, A6 checks signal-wire continuity and A7 checks the ground path. Remove the jumper after either result; repair failed circuits or proceed to A9.

steps.title: Confirm buckle or module replacement
steps.body: A8–A9 require depowering, inspection of terminals, wiring and RCM connector locks, correction of defects, and reconnection before self-test. At A8, recurrence of the original code directs replacement of the buckle, which includes the switch. At A9, check OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins; follow any applicable bulletin before considering RCM replacement.

steps.title: Resolve a fault that becomes intermittent
steps.body: If the original code disappears, use A10. Depower, disconnect the buckle and inspect for corrosion, terminal damage and harness damage. Repair defects, reconnect and retest. A returning code re-enters its active branch. If it remains absent, do not install new components.

steps.title: Reconnect and check all restraint modules
steps.body: A11 explicitly requires depowering before final reconnection. Repower without prove-out, switch ignition on and run the complete Restraints self-test. Resolve all on-demand faults before clearing any codes.

watchFor.title: An expected additional fault during testing
watchFor.body: C3238 also carries the belt tension sensor (BTS). Disconnecting it can create a BTS fault in the occupant classification system module (OCSM); account for the test configuration before condemning another component.

watchFor.title: Connector damage
watchFor.body: Use service pigtails for damaged restraint terminals. Never probe airbag assembly connectors or back-probe deployable devices.

notes: Match any replacement buckle or RCM to the Ford parts catalog; similar-looking SRS components may be incompatible.

diagnostics.finding: B0052:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The buckle-switch circuit has a detected short to ground.
diagnostics.next: Begin A2.

diagnostics.finding: B0052:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The buckle-switch circuit has unwanted voltage.
diagnostics.next: Follow A4.

diagnostics.finding: B0052:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detected an open buckle-switch circuit.
diagnostics.next: Follow A5–A7.

diagnostics.finding: B0052:1D is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Switch-circuit current is outside the acceptable range.
diagnostics.next: Begin A2; do not assume buckle failure.

verification.title: Record the fault response
verification.body: Document the original code, induced code changes and whether the original fault returned after reconnection.

verification.title: Confirm the complete system passes
verification.body: Release requires no on-demand restraint faults and a fully operational SRS.

guides.title: Diagnose driver seatbelt anchor pretensioner circuit faults
guides.summary: Use the B0070 diagnostic branches to distinguish driver anchor pretensioner wiring faults from a confirmed pretensioner or restraints control module fault.
guides.introduction: The driver seatbelt anchor pretensioner is a pyrotechnic restraint that helps tighten the belt during a deployment event. The restraints control module (RCM) monitors its electrical deployment loop. This diagnosis investigates the wiring, connections, pretensioner and RCM when the monitored circuit causes an airbag warning.
guides.why: Connector movement can shift resistance enough to create intermittent faults. A code disappearing during testing is therefore insufficient: the recorded loop resistance must also remain within the specified range before the fault is considered repaired.
searchTerms: driver seatbelt anchor pretensioner circuit fault

when.summary: When B0070:11, B0070:12, B0070:13 or B0070:1A is retrieved as a current or stored fault.
notes: A stored code identifies the circuit requiring investigation; it does not by itself justify replacing a restraint component.

prepare.title: Use qualified restraint-system personnel
prepare.detail: Pyrotechnic servicing requires qualified personnel and the linked safety, depowering and repowering procedures. Disconnect or reconnect supplemental restraint system (SRS) components only when the pinpoint test instructs.

prepare.title: Prepare the correct diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting RCM self-tests and deployment-resistance data, suitable electrical test equipment, correct probe adapters and Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5. The prescribed fused jumper is used only on the isolated harness branch, never on the pretensioner itself.

steps.title: Establish whether the fault is current
steps.body: Perform the RCM self-test. An on-demand B0070 fault follows its active-fault branch; a continuous-memory-only code follows intermittent testing. Diagnose on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 first through Pinpoint Test AJ. A current pretensioner fault cannot be cleared until corrected.

steps.title: Measure loop resistance through scan data
steps.body: For active open or low-resistance faults, A2–A3 monitor and record the DEPLOY_29_RES parameter identification (PID). The required range is 1.44–3.52 ohms. If initially within range, follow RCM confirmation. Otherwise flex the accessible harness and connectors as directed; movement that restores the range identifies a connection or wiring concern requiring depowering before repair.

steps.title: Separate low resistance from an open circuit
steps.body: A4–A7 use controlled fault changes and isolated harness measurements. For low resistance, the prescribed depower/disconnect/repower sequence should change the fault to an open; otherwise test for a short between wires. For excessive resistance, check each wire for continuity before the prescribed harness-side fused-jumper test. A change from open to low resistance demonstrates an RCM response. Remove the jumper on either result and follow the indicated confirmation branch.

steps.title: Follow the ground or voltage branch
steps.body: For a ground short, A8 disconnects the pretensioner under the prescribed power sequence and checks whether the fault changes to open. If it does not, A9 isolates the RCM and checks harness insulation to ground. For a voltage short, A10 disconnects both components before repowering for the specified harness voltage measurements. Detected voltage requires circuit repair; no voltage leads to RCM confirmation.

steps.title: Confirm the component before replacement
steps.body: A11–A12 depower the system, inspect wiring and connector locks, repair concerns and restore all required connections before retesting. Only recurrence of the original on-demand fault authorizes the selected branch's replacement: the driver retractor, which includes the anchor pretensioner, at A11; or the RCM after checking applicable technical service bulletins at A12. If the fault disappears, continue with intermittent testing.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent faults
steps.body: A13 monitors and records resistance while flexing connections. A14 checks for a returning ground-short code during harness movement. A15 requires its own depower/disconnect/repower setup before attempting to reproduce a voltage short. Depower before repairing a reproduced fault. If it cannot be reproduced, A16 inspects wiring, terminals and connector locks; do not replace SRS components speculatively.

steps.title: Restore connections and run the final self-test
steps.body: Follow A17 to reconnect all SRS components and repower if previously depowered. Carry out the complete Restraints self-test. Diagnose every remaining on-demand restraint-system fault before clearing codes or releasing the vehicle.

watchFor.title: A connector can appear attached but remain electrically shorted
watchFor.body: Connector Position Assurance (CPA) tabs release the component's protective shorting bars when fully seated. An incomplete or damaged lock can produce a low-resistance fault.

watchFor.title: Restraint connectors need the specified repair
watchFor.body: Replace damaged restraint connector terminals using service pigtails. Never back-probe deployable-device connectors, disassemble the pretensioner or repair the RCM.

notes: Intermediate repowering steps expressly defer SRS prove-out; follow their sequence exactly.
Verify replacement restraint part numbers in the Ford parts catalog; physically similar components may be incompatible.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0070:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detected a deployment-circuit short to ground.
diagnostics.next: Use A8 for an active fault or A14 for a memory-only fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0070:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detected unexpected deployment-circuit voltage.
diagnostics.next: Use A10 for an active fault or A15 for a memory-only fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0070:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is above the desired range.
diagnostics.next: Use A2 for an active fault or A13 for a memory-only fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0070:1A is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is below the desired range.
diagnostics.next: Use A2 for an active fault or A13 for a memory-only fault.

verification.title: Record the resistance result
verification.body: Confirm the recorded DEPLOY_29_RES value remains within 1.44–3.52 ohms during the required harness checks, even when no on-demand code appears.

verification.title: Confirm the complete restraint-system result
verification.body: Record the final Restraints self-test outcome. Release requires an operational, fault-free SRS with no remaining on-demand faults in the applicable restraint modules.

guides.title: Diagnose passenger seatbelt anchor-pretensioner circuit faults
guides.summary: Identify passenger anchor-pretensioner wiring, connection or component faults using RCM resistance data and controlled circuit tests.
guides.introduction: The passenger seatbelt anchor pretensioner tightens the belt when commanded during a qualifying crash. Its deployment circuit is monitored by the restraints control module (RCM). This diagnosis checks the complete electrical loop before deciding whether wiring, the retractor assembly containing the pretensioner, or the RCM needs replacement.
guides.why: Terminal movement can change circuit resistance enough to cause intermittent faults. Connector Position Assurance (CPA) tabs also release protective shorting bars; an incompletely seated tab can leave a low-resistance condition. A disappearing warning alone therefore does not establish a sound repair.

when.summary: When passenger anchor-pretensioner codes are active or stored intermittently.

prepare.title: Use qualified personnel and appropriate equipment
prepare.detail: Read the pyrotechnic precautions. Obtain a scan tool displaying DEPLOY_30_RES and supporting restraint self-tests, a multimeter, correct probe adapters, a fused jumper and Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5.

prepare.title: Follow the controlled power sequence
prepare.detail: Use each test step's supplemental restraint system (SRS) depowering and repowering instructions. Disconnect components only as directed, and do not perform prove-out during diagnostic repowering.

steps.title: Retrieve and classify the codes
steps.body: Inspect wiring and connections, then run the RCM self-test at A1 of the [pinpoint test](#/document/G1696359). Diagnose U3003:16 or U3003:17 first through Test AJ. Separate active diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) from continuous-memory-only faults, which use the intermittent branches.

steps.title: Measure resistance through the RCM
steps.body: For active resistance faults, A2–A3 require recording the DEPLOY_30_RES parameter identification (PID) value. The desired range is 1.44–3.52 ohms. An initially in-range result leads to A12. Otherwise monitor while flexing the harness and connectors; a return to range directs depowering and repair of the affected connection or wiring.

steps.title: Separate low resistance from shorted wiring
steps.body: If resistance remains low, A4 disconnects the pretensioner under the prescribed power sequence. A change from B0072:1A to B0072:13 leads to component confirmation at A11. Without that change, A5 checks the isolated harness for a short between circuits before considering the RCM.

steps.title: Trace excessive resistance or an open circuit
steps.body: A6 checks both isolated wires for continuity. If they pass, A7 uses a fused jumper at the specified harness connector to request a low-resistance response. A change from B0072:13 to B0072:1A leads to A11; no change leads to A12. Remove the jumper after the test.

steps.title: Follow the appropriate short-circuit branch
steps.body: For a ground fault, A8 checks whether disconnecting the pretensioner changes B0072:11 to B0072:13. If not, A9 checks isolated wiring to ground. For B0072:12, A10 performs the prescribed powered harness measurements with the pretensioner and RCM disconnected; any voltage requires circuit repair.

steps.title: Confirm the replacement decision
steps.body: A11 and A12 require terminal, harness and CPA-lock inspection, repair of concerns and reconnection before self-test. At A11, recurrence of the original code directs a new passenger retractor, which includes the anchor pretensioner. At A12, persistent faults require a Technical Service Bulletin check before RCM replacement. A disappearing fault enters intermittent diagnosis.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent faults by their original type
steps.body: A13 monitors and records resistance during harness movement; A14 attempts to reproduce a ground fault with movement and self-test. A15 requires the specified pretensioner disconnection before its powered voltage-fault test. Depower before repairs. If unreproduced, A16 inspects corrosion, terminals, wiring and CPA seating; do not replace components speculatively.

steps.title: Restore and test all restraint circuits
steps.body: At A17, reconnect components and follow the required repowering sequence before the full Restraints self-test. Diagnose every remaining on-demand restraint fault before clearing any codes.

watchFor.title: Use harness test points only
watchFor.body: Never dismantle the pretensioner or back-probe deployable-device connectors. Obtain deployment-loop resistance from the RCM, not by directly measuring the pretensioner.

watchFor.title: Damaged connector hardware
watchFor.body: Inspect the pretensioner connector's CPA tabs and clip. Terminal repairs require service connector pigtails.

notes: Use the correct replacement part number; the directed repair replaces the retractor assembly containing the anchor pretensioner.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0072:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects a deployment-circuit short to ground.
diagnostics.next: Use A8–A9 when active, or A14 when memory-only.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0072:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects unwanted deployment-circuit voltage.
diagnostics.next: Use A10 when active, or A15 when memory-only.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0072:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is excessive or the circuit is open.
diagnostics.next: Use A2 when active, or A13 when memory-only.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B0072:1A is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is below its acceptable threshold.
diagnostics.next: Use A2 when active, or A13 when memory-only.

verification.title: Record acceptable resistance
verification.body: Record DEPLOY_30_RES and the harness-test response. Resistance must be within 1.44–3.52 ohms before considering the fault repaired, even without an active code.

verification.title: Confirm system-wide completion
verification.body: The final Restraints self-test must show no on-demand faults in applicable restraint modules, and the SRS must be fully operational.

guides.title: Diagnose driver seatbelt retractor pretensioner codes B007E
guides.summary: Separate driver pretensioner wiring, connector, retractor and control-module faults using code status and deployment-loop resistance.
guides.introduction: The driver’s retractor pretensioner is a deployable seatbelt component controlled by the restraints control module (RCM). The RCM monitors its electrical deployment loop and requests the airbag warning indicator when a fault is detected. These tests identify the faulty part of that loop before replacement is considered.
guides.why: Connector movement and wire strain can change resistance intermittently. A warning that disappears during testing does not establish a repair: the scan-tool resistance must also be within the specified range. Connector position assurance (CPA) tabs matter because an incompletely seated tab can leave the component’s shorting bars engaged.

when.summary: Use when the RCM reports B007E:11, B007E:12, B007E:13 or B007E:1A, currently or in memory.
notes: A code identifies a circuit condition, not a proven defective pretensioner.

prepare.title: Use qualified restraint-system service
prepare.detail: Pyrotechnic work requires qualified personnel. Read the linked precautions and use the exact supplemental restraint system (SRS) depowering and repowering procedures whenever directed.

prepare.title: Provide the specified diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use an RCM-capable scan tool, electrical measuring equipment, correct probe adapters, the prescribed fused jumper and wiring diagrams. Follow each pinpoint step’s connection and power-state instructions.

steps.title: Retrieve and classify the fault
steps.body: Run the RCM self-test with ignition on. Diagnose on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 first. Current B007E faults follow their active branches; codes present only as continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes follow the intermittent branches. An active fault cannot be cleared into a repair.

steps.title: Evaluate open or low-resistance codes
steps.body: For B007E:13 or B007E:1A, record the DEPLOY_23_R parameter identification (PID) resistance. The required range is 1.44 to 3.52 ohms. An initially in-range reading goes to A12 confirmation. Otherwise, monitor and record resistance while flexing accessible wiring and connectors. A return to range during manipulation directs wiring or connector repair after depowering.

steps.title: Follow the low-resistance branch
steps.body: A4 uses controlled disconnection to check whether B007E:1A changes to open-circuit code B007E:13. That change leads to pretensioner confirmation at A11. If it does not change, A5 checks the isolated harness for a short between circuits and directs either circuit repair or RCM confirmation.

steps.title: Follow the high-resistance branch
steps.body: A6 isolates the components and checks harness continuity. Failed continuity requires circuit repair. If continuity passes, A7 uses the prescribed fused-jumper test to see whether B007E:13 changes to B007E:1A. Remove the jumper as directed. A change leads to A11; no change leads to A12.

steps.title: Separate ground and voltage shorts
steps.body: For B007E:11, A8 checks whether disconnecting the pretensioner changes the fault to an open; otherwise A9 tests the isolated wiring for a ground short. For B007E:12, A10 checks isolated harness circuits for unwanted voltage under its specified power conditions. Repair failed wiring checks; passing checks lead to RCM confirmation.

steps.title: Confirm before replacing a component
steps.body: At A11 or A12, depower and inspect terminals, wiring and connector locks before reconnection and self-test. A11 requires the original fault to return before replacing the driver retractor, which includes the pretensioner. A12 requires the original fault to return and an applicable Ford service-bulletin check before RCM replacement. A disappearing fault goes to intermittent testing.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent faults
steps.body: A13 monitors resistance during harness movement; A14 uses movement and self-test for ground shorts. A15 tests intermittent voltage shorts with the pretensioner disconnected through the prescribed power sequence. If unreproduced, A16 inspects wiring, corrosion, terminals and CPA locks. Repair demonstrated concerns; do not replace components speculatively.

steps.title: Complete the restraint-system check
steps.body: At A17, restore all connections using the required power sequence, then perform the Restraints self-test. Do not perform prove-out during intermediate repowering steps. Diagnose all remaining on-demand restraint faults before clearing codes or releasing the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Unsafe electrical access
watchFor.body: Never back-probe deployable-device connectors or disassemble the pretensioner. Meter and jumper checks apply only to the harness arrangements explicitly specified.

watchFor.title: Terminal damage
watchFor.body: Restraint connector terminals requiring repair need service connector pigtails; do not repair the terminals themselves.

notes: Confirm replacement part numbers in the Ford catalog; physical similarity does not establish compatibility.

diagnostics.meaning: The loop has a detected ground short or voltage short, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Use A8 or A10 rather than assuming the retractor is faulty.

diagnostics.meaning: Loop resistance is above or below the desired range, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Use the recorded PID and fault-change tests to isolate the cause.

verification.title: Record resistance and fault status
verification.body: Retain initial and harness-test readings. Confirm the applicable resistance check is within range, even if an on-demand code has disappeared.

verification.title: Confirm the final system result
verification.body: Record the final Restraints self-test across the RCM, occupant classification system module and any other applicable fitted modules. The SRS must be operational and fault-free.

guides.title: Diagnose passenger seatbelt retractor pretensioner faults B007F
guides.summary: Trace passenger retractor pretensioner circuit faults through wiring, connector and module checks before deciding whether replacement is justified.
guides.introduction: The passenger retractor pretensioner tightens the seatbelt when commanded during a restraint deployment. The restraints control module (RCM) monitors its electrical deployment loop. This diagnosis separates wiring and connection problems from a faulty pretensioner or RCM; an airbag warning light alone cannot identify which has failed.
guides.why: Harness movement and poor terminal contact can change resistance enough to cause an intermittent warning. A disappearing code is therefore insufficient: the measured loop resistance must also return to the specified range.

when.summary: When RCM testing reports B007F:11, B007F:12, B007F:13 or B007F:1A.

prepare.title: Arrange qualified restraint-system diagnosis
prepare.detail: Pyrotechnic servicing requires qualified personnel. Read the safety precautions and have the complete supplemental restraint system (SRS) depowering and repowering procedures available; switching the ignition off does not replace depowering.

prepare.title: Prepare the electrical test equipment
prepare.detail: Use an RCM-capable scan tool, a meter, correct probe adapters and the specified fused jumper. Wiring Diagrams Cell 46 identifies circuits; Cell 5 supports repairs. Change SRS connections only when the selected test instructs.

steps.title: Establish whether the fault is present
steps.body: Run the RCM self-test at [A1](#/document/G1696361). Diagnose on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 first using Pinpoint Test AJ. An on-demand B007F fault follows its active branch; a continuous-memory-only fault follows the intermittent checks.

steps.title: Record resistance for open or low-resistance codes
steps.body: For B007F:13 or B007F:1A, A2 reads the DEPLOY_24_R parameter identification (PID) value. A reading between 1.44 and 3.52 ohms leads to A12. Otherwise, A3 monitors resistance while flexing accessible wiring and connectors. If movement restores the range, depower and repair the affected connection or harness.

steps.title: Separate low resistance from an open circuit
steps.body: Persistently low resistance follows A4–A5: controlled pretensioner disconnection should change the fault to open; otherwise check for shorted wiring. High resistance follows A6–A7: check continuity, then use the prescribed harness-side fused jumper. An open-to-low-resistance change leads to pretensioner confirmation. Remove the jumper whichever result occurs.

steps.title: Follow the ground or voltage branch
steps.body: For B007F:11, A8 checks whether prescribed disconnection changes the fault to open; if not, A9 checks wiring insulation to ground. For B007F:12, A10 isolates the pretensioner and RCM before its powered voltage check. Repair failed wiring checks; passing wiring checks lead to A12.

steps.title: Confirm the replacement decision
steps.body: At A11 or A12, depower, inspect wiring, terminals and connector position assurance (CPA) locks, repair concerns and reconnect before self-testing. A11 requires a new retractor with pretensioner only if the original fault returns. A12 requires checking OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins before RCM replacement; follow any applicable bulletin.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent faults
steps.body: If confirmation no longer reproduces the code, do not replace components. A13 monitors resistance during harness movement; A14 repeats self-test for a ground short. A15 uses its prescribed depower, disconnect and repower sequence to investigate intermittent voltage. Reproduced concerns require depowering and repair.

steps.title: Finish the physical inspection
steps.body: If the fault remains absent, A16 checks for corrosion, damaged wires, loose or spread terminals and damaged or unseated CPA features, including connector C303. Repair identified defects. If none are found, proceed to A17 without speculative replacement.

watchFor.title: A connector can touch electrically without locking correctly
watchFor.body: An unseated CPA tab can leave the component's shorting bar engaged and produce a low-resistance fault.

watchFor.title: Preserve deployable components
watchFor.body: Never back-probe deployable connectors or dismantle the pretensioner. Replace damaged restraint connector terminals using service pigtails.

notes: Confirm replacement part numbers in the Ford parts catalog; physical similarity does not establish compatibility.
Follow every prescribed depowering and repowering transition. Intermediate repowering expressly excludes SRS prove-out.

diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects a ground short or unexpected voltage respectively.
diagnostics.next: Follow A8 or A10; neither code proves pretensioner failure.

diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is above or below the desired range respectively.
diagnostics.next: Start with the recorded PID and follow A2–A7 as directed.

diagnostics.finding: The deliberately induced fault changes as expected
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM recognizes the changed circuit condition.
diagnostics.next: Proceed to A11; inspect and retest before condemning the retractor.

verification.title: Record the resistance result
verification.body: Retain the initial and harness-test readings. Confirm DEPLOY_24_R is within 1.44–3.52 ohms before treating a resistance concern as repaired.

verification.title: Complete the full restraint self-test
verification.body: At A17, restore all connections and power states as directed, then run the complete Restraints self-test. Resolve every on-demand fault returned before clearing codes. Release the vehicle only with the SRS operational and fault-free.

guides.title: Diagnose passenger seat position sensor faults
guides.summary: Trace passenger seat position sensor codes to wiring, connector, sensor or restraints control module faults before replacing components.
guides.introduction: The passenger seat track position sensor provides seat-position information to the restraints control module (RCM). The RCM monitors its circuit as part of the supplemental restraint system (SRS) and requests the airbag warning indicator when a fault persists. This diagnostic path separates circuit problems from confirmed component failures.
guides.why: Most faults involve wiring or connections. Deliberately changing the circuit condition lets the technician check whether the RCM recognizes that change, but a replacement decision still requires the specified confirmation test.

when.summary: Use when passenger seat track sensor codes B00C5:11, :12, :13 or :1D are retrieved.
notes: A code identifies a detected circuit condition; it does not by itself condemn the sensor.

prepare.title: Arrange qualified restraints diagnosis
prepare.detail: Read the pyrotechnic precautions first. Have an RCM-capable diagnostic scan tool, electrical measuring equipment, correct probe adapters, a fused jumper and Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5 available.

prepare.title: Follow the prescribed system states
prepare.detail: Use the linked depowering and repowering procedures wherever directed. Disconnect or reconnect SRS components only at the specified test steps, and omit prove-out during the intermediate repowering stages as instructed.

steps.title: Inspect and establish the active fault
steps.body: Inspect the sensor, harness and connectors for damage. In A1, switch the ignition on and run the RCM self-test. Address on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 through Pinpoint Test AJ first. Otherwise, route active B00C5 faults by suffix; memory-only faults go to A10.

steps.title: Check the response to sensor disconnection
steps.body: For :11 or :1D, follow A2: switch the ignition off, disconnect sensor C3240, then switch on and repeat the self-test. A change to :13 leads to sensor confirmation at A8. An unchanged :11 leads to A3; an unchanged :1D leads to A9.

steps.title: Separate ground and voltage faults
steps.body: A3 checks the remaining :11 fault for a short to ground. A4 checks :12 for unwanted voltage. Follow each branch's distinct RCM isolation sequence; A4 also disconnects the passenger side-airbag inline connector before controlled repowering. Repair a failed circuit, then proceed to A11. Passing results lead to A9.

steps.title: Trace an open-circuit fault
steps.body: For :13, A5 requires depowering and the specified side-airbag and sensor disconnections before installing its fused jumper at the sensor circuit. After controlled repowering, a change to :11 leads to A8. Remove the jumper on either outcome. No change leads through A6 signal-circuit and A7 ground-circuit continuity checks; repair failures, or continue to A9 if both pass.

steps.title: Confirm before replacing
steps.body: At A8 or A9, depower and inspect terminals, wiring and RCM Connector Position Assurance (CPA) locks. Repair concerns and reconnect all required components before retesting. If the original code returns, A8 directs sensor replacement. A9 requires checking applicable technical service bulletins before RCM replacement. Follow the linked installation procedure and verify the correct part number.

steps.title: Handle intermittent faults
steps.body: If the original fault disappears, use A10. With the system depowered, inspect for corrosion, poor terminal fit and damaged wiring; repair concerns, reconnect and retest. A returning code resumes its active-fault branch. If the fault cannot be recreated, do not install new SRS components.

steps.title: Restore and test the complete system
steps.body: At A11, depower, reconnect all SRS components and repower without prove-out as directed. Run the scan tool's Restraints self-test, including the RCM and occupant classification system module. Resolve every remaining on-demand fault before clearing codes or releasing the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Accidental deployment
watchFor.body: Never probe airbag assembly connectors or back-probe deployable-device connectors. The controlled jumper test applies only to the designated seat-sensor circuit.

watchFor.title: Damaged restraint terminals
watchFor.body: Use service connector pigtails where restraint terminals require repair; do not reshape or service those terminals.

notes: All components must be connected for confirmation self-tests; disconnected components can generate additional codes.

diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects a short to ground or voltage, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Start at A2 for :11 or A4 for :12.

diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects an open circuit or current outside its acceptable range, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Start at A5 for :13 or A2 for :1D.

verification.title: Confirm a fault-free restraints system
verification.body: Release requires a fully operational SRS with no unresolved faults. An active fault cannot be cleared successfully until corrected.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record the original code, whether it was on-demand or memory-only, the repair performed and the final Restraints self-test result.

Required pyrotechnic servicing and connector-handling precautions.

SRS repowering at the specified diagnostic stages.

RCM removal and installation only after A9 confirmation and bulletin checks.

guides.title: Diagnose passenger airbag adaptive canister vent faults B11CF
guides.summary: Identify whether a passenger airbag vent fault comes from its wiring, connectors, airbag assembly or restraints control module.
guides.introduction: The adaptive canister vent is a deployable part of the passenger airbag assembly associated with its venting. The restraints control module (RCM) monitors this separate deployment circuit. Diagnosis checks that circuit before authorizing replacement of the passenger airbag, which includes the vent.
guides.why: Small resistance changes at terminals can produce intermittent warnings. Access through the glove compartment allows the relevant harness to be checked, while controlled fault changes help distinguish circuit problems from module faults.

when.summary: When RCM testing reports B11CF:11, B11CF:12, B11CF:13 or B11CF:1A.

prepare.title: Use qualified personnel and exact power procedures
prepare.detail: Read the pyrotechnic precautions. Have the complete supplemental restraint system (SRS) depowering and repowering procedures available. Never probe airbag assembly connectors or back-probe deployable devices.

prepare.title: Prepare access and test equipment
prepare.detail: Use an RCM-capable scan tool, meter, correct probe adapters and specified fused jumper. Follow the glove compartment removal procedure where directed. Wiring Diagrams Cell 46 identifies connections; Cell 5 supports repairs.

steps.title: Choose the active or intermittent route
steps.body: Run the RCM self-test at [A1](#/document/G1696371). Address on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 through Pinpoint Test AJ first. Active B11CF codes follow their individual branches; continuous-memory-only codes go to A13–A15.

steps.title: Measure the vent circuit's resistance
steps.body: For B11CF:13 or B11CF:1A, record the DEPLOY_08_R parameter identification (PID) value at A2. Between 1.44 and 3.52 ohms leads to A12. Otherwise, A3 removes the glove compartment and monitors resistance during harness movement. Movement restoring the range calls for depowering and connection or harness repair.

steps.title: Distinguish shorted wiring from an open loop
steps.body: For persistently low resistance, A4 disconnects passenger airbag connector C256 using the prescribed power sequence. A change to open leads to A11; otherwise A5 checks for shorted wiring. For high resistance, A6 checks continuity before A7's harness-side fused-jumper test. Remove the jumper after testing; the expected open-to-low-resistance change leads to A11, otherwise A12.

steps.title: Investigate ground and voltage faults
steps.body: For B11CF:11, A8 checks for a change to open with C256 disconnected. No change leads to A9's ground-insulation checks. For B11CF:12, A10 isolates the airbag and RCM before checking harness voltage. Repair failed circuit checks; satisfactory wiring results lead to A12.

steps.title: Confirm the airbag or module decision
steps.body: A11 and A12 require depowering, inspection, repair and reconnection before self-test. Check harness damage, terminal fit and connector position assurance (CPA) locks. If the original fault returns at A11, install a new passenger airbag including its vent. At A12, check OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins before replacing the RCM.

steps.title: Recreate intermittent concerns
steps.body: A13 watches resistance while flexing the accessible harness; A14 uses harness movement and self-test for ground faults. A15 requires its prescribed C256 disconnection and power sequence before investigating intermittent voltage. Depower before repairing reproduced concerns. If confirmation loses the fault, use these branches without replacing components.

steps.title: Inspect before closing the diagnosis
steps.body: If movement cannot reproduce the concern, A16 checks corrosion, terminal fit, wire damage and CPA seating and clips. Use service pigtails for damaged restraint connector terminals. Repair identified defects; otherwise proceed to A17 without installing speculative parts.

watchFor.title: Expected extra codes during isolation
watchFor.body: Disconnecting C256 also opens passenger airbag stages 1 and 2. Their temporary open-circuit codes are expected during these tests.

watchFor.title: Airbag handling and connector security
watchFor.body: Carry a live airbag with its cover away from your body; never place it cover-down. Unseated CPA tabs can leave shorting bars engaged and cause low resistance.

notes: Verify replacement compatibility using the Ford parts catalog.
Change connections only as directed. Intermediate repowering excludes SRS prove-out; use the complete procedures for every transition.

diagnostics.finding: B11CF:11 or B11CF:12
diagnostics.meaning: The vent circuit has a detected ground short or unexpected voltage respectively.
diagnostics.next: Use A8 or A10 to separate wiring concerns from component or module faults.

diagnostics.finding: B11CF:13 or B11CF:1A
diagnostics.meaning: The monitored vent-loop resistance is too high or too low respectively.
diagnostics.next: Record DEPLOY_08_R and follow A2–A7 as directed.

diagnostics.finding: The original fault disappears after inspection and reconnection
diagnostics.meaning: The concern has become intermittent; component failure is unconfirmed.
diagnostics.next: Follow A13–A16 instead of replacing the airbag or RCM.

verification.title: Retain a resistance record
verification.body: Record initial and harness-test readings. A resistance concern requires DEPLOY_08_R within 1.44–3.52 ohms, even if no on-demand code remains.

verification.title: Restore and test the complete system
verification.body: At A17, restore all SRS connections and power states as directed, then run Restraints self-test. Diagnose every returned on-demand fault before clearing codes. Complete glove compartment installation through its linked procedure. The SRS must be operational and fault-free before release.
