guides.title: Diagnose restraint-event notification faults B11D8:12 and B11D8:14
guides.summary: Check the crash-notification circuit between the restraint and body modules while preserving the required restraint-system power states.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) sends crash and deployment status to the body control module (BCM), which initiates fuel cut-off when the signal indicates a crash. This job checks that communication circuit. These codes can be stored without illuminating the airbag warning indicator.
guides.why: Most faults arise in wiring or connectors. Controlled disconnection and retesting distinguish those faults from module trouble, while the prescribed supplemental restraint system (SRS) power states protect against accidental deployment and misleading codes.
searchTerms: B11D8:14 short to ground or open
restraint notification code without airbag warning

when.summary: Use when RCM self-test or continuous memory records B11D8:12 or B11D8:14.
notes: A stored code alone does not justify module replacement.

prepare.title: Qualified restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Service requires qualified personnel, the pyrotechnic precautions, and the exact SRS depowering and repowering procedures. Disconnect or reconnect SRS components only when the pinpoint step directs it.

prepare.title: Diagnostic equipment and access
prepare.detail: Use a compatible scan tool, multimeter and correct connector-probe adapters. Have access to technical service bulletins and the vehicle identification number (VIN)-specific BCM guided routine.

steps.title: Distinguish an active fault from a memory record
steps.body: With ignition on, perform the RCM self-test. An on-demand B11D8:14 enters A2; B11D8:12 enters A5. A code present only in continuous memory enters intermittent diagnosis at A8. An active fault cannot be cleared successfully until corrected.

steps.title: Check B11D8:14 wiring
steps.body: Switch ignition off, depower the SRS, and disconnect RCM C310A/C310B and BCM C2280E. A2 requires less than 3 ohms between C310B pin 42 and C2280E pin 49. A3 requires greater than 10,000 ohms from C2280E pin 49 to ground. Repair a failed circuit and proceed to A9.

steps.title: Retest after the open and ground checks pass
steps.body: At A4, inspect terminals and wiring before reconnecting both modules. Repair damage, reconnect, repower without SRS prove-out, and repeat RCM self-test with ignition on. If B11D8:14 remains, follow an applicable bulletin or stop for the VIN-specific BCM guided routine. If absent, use A8.

steps.title: Check whether B11D8:12 changes with BCM isolation
steps.body: At A5, disconnect BCM C2280E as directed and repeat RCM self-test. If B11D8:12 remains, continue to A6. If it disappears or changes, the response indicates the RCM can detect a changed condition: follow applicable bulletins or stop for the VIN-specific BCM guided routine.

steps.title: Isolate a short to voltage
steps.body: At A6, switch ignition off, depower the SRS and disconnect RCM C310A/C310B; the BCM remains disconnected. Repower without prove-out, switch ignition on and measure C2280E pin 49 to ground. Any voltage directs circuit repair and A9. No voltage leads to the separate A7 confirmation path.

steps.title: Confirm the RCM only through A7
steps.body: Switch ignition off and depower again. Inspect and repair wiring and connectors, reconnect both modules, then repower without prove-out. Repeat RCM self-test with ignition on. If the original code returns, follow applicable bulletins; if none apply, replace the RCM through its dedicated procedure and continue to A9. Otherwise use A8.

steps.title: Investigate an intermittent connection
steps.body: At A8, depower with ignition off before disconnecting and inspecting both module connections and the harness. Repair, reconnect, repower without prove-out and retest. A returning code re-enters its active-fault branch. If absent, attempt to reproduce it by flexing the harness, cycling ignition and operating systems sharing the harness; repair findings without speculative component replacement.

watchFor.title: Keep testing away from deployable devices
watchFor.body: Never probe airbag assemblies or back-probe deployable-device connectors. These measurements concern the specified module-harness circuit.

watchFor.title: Respect connector and module limits
watchFor.body: Use service pigtails for damaged restraint connector terminals; do not repair the terminals themselves or tamper with the RCM. Any directed replacement must use the correct vehicle part.

watchFor.title: Do not bypass the BCM guided routine
watchFor.body: An unfinished A4 or A5 guided-routine referral does not authorize BCM replacement, RCM replacement or return to service.

notes: Ignition off is not a substitute for the prescribed SRS depowering procedure.
Do not move the RCM while it is connected with ignition on.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B11D8:12 returns on demand.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detected sustained voltage on the event-notification circuit.
diagnostics.next: Use A5 to check fault-status change, then A6 if the same code remains.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B11D8:14 returns on demand.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detected a sustained ground short or open circuit.
diagnostics.next: Use A2 and A3 to distinguish continuity loss from grounding before A4.

diagnostics.finding: The code appears only in continuous memory or disappears during testing.
diagnostics.meaning: The fault is intermittent rather than currently confirmed.
diagnostics.next: Follow A8; disappearance alone does not justify new restraint components.

verification.title: Complete the A9 restraint-system check
verification.body: After completing the applicable repair path, restore connections and SRS power as directed, without the intermediate prove-out. Run the full Restraints self-test with ignition on, including the occupant classification system module and other modules actually fitted. Diagnose every on-demand fault before clearing any codes.

verification.title: Record the release decision
verification.body: Record the original codes, circuit results and final self-test findings. Return the vehicle only when the SRS is fully operational and fault-free; an outstanding guided routine remains an unresolved diagnostic step.

procedures.purpose: B11D8 circuit diagnosis, distinct module-confirmation paths, intermittent checks and A9 verification.
Mandatory pyrotechnic-device handling and diagnostic precautions.
Exact SRS depowering at the required test stages.
Exact SRS repowering, respecting each instruction to omit prove-out.
RCM removal and installation only when the completed A7 branch directs replacement.
Diagnosis of additional restraint faults found during final self-test.

guides.title: Diagnose driver side airbag circuit faults B1404
guides.summary: Trace driver seat side-airbag resistance, ground and voltage faults through wiring, connectors, the airbag and the restraints control module.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) monitors the driver side airbag deployment circuit and requests the airbag warning indicator when it detects a fault. This is the seat-mounted side airbag circuit. Diagnosis uses measured circuit behavior and carefully controlled fault changes to distinguish connection problems from an airbag or module fault.
guides.why: Connector movement can change deployment-loop resistance enough to create an intermittent warning. Connector Position Assurance (CPA) tabs also release protective shorting bars: an incompletely seated tab can produce low resistance even when the connector appears attached. A disappearing code alone therefore does not establish a sound repair.

when.summary: Use when driver side airbag B1404 faults are present on demand or stored intermittently.
notes: The supplemental restraint system must be fully operational and free of faults before vehicle release.

prepare.title: Use qualified restraint-system personnel
prepare.detail: Follow the pyrotechnic precautions and exact supplemental restraint system (SRS) depowering and repowering procedures. Disconnect or reconnect components only when directed. Never probe an airbag assembly connector or back-probe a deployable device.

prepare.title: Prepare the specified diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting RCM self-tests and DEPLOY_10_R, correct probe adapters, the prescribed fused jumper and wiring diagrams. Measurements and jumper connections belong only at the harness points identified by the test.

steps.title: Retrieve faults and select the correct branch
steps.body: Run the RCM self-test. Diagnose on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 through Pinpoint Test AJ first. Otherwise distinguish an active B1404 fault from a continuous-memory-only fault. Active resistance faults start at A2, ground faults at A8 and voltage faults at A10; intermittent faults use A13–A15.

steps.title: Record deployment-loop resistance
steps.body: At A2, read DEPLOY_10_R, the parameter identification (PID) reporting loop resistance. The required range is 1.44 to 3.52 ohms. An in-range reading routes to module confirmation at A12. Otherwise perform A3’s harness-flex test and record changes. A return to range during movement directs depowering and connection/harness repair; consistently low or high resistance selects the respective isolation branch.

steps.title: Isolate low-resistance and open-circuit faults
steps.body: A4–A7 distinguish wiring from the airbag through controlled fault changes. Follow every depower/disconnect/repower instruction. Disconnecting the airbag should change a low-resistance fault to an open; otherwise test for a wiring short. For an open, check isolated harness continuity before the prescribed harness-side fused-jumper test. Remove that jumper on either outcome. Follow the result to airbag confirmation or module confirmation.

steps.title: Separate ground and voltage faults
steps.body: At A8, a ground fault changing to an open after airbag disconnection leads to airbag confirmation. An unchanged fault requires isolated harness checks at A9. A10 isolates the airbag and RCM before its powered harness-voltage check: any voltage directs circuit repair; no voltage leads to module confirmation. Do not perform SRS prove-out during these temporary test configurations.

steps.title: Confirm a component fault before replacement
steps.body: A11 and A12 require connector, harness and locking-feature inspection, repair of defects, reconnection and another self-test. For a persistent airbag-path fault, inspect the seat-backrest harness before replacing the airbag. For a persistent module-path fault, check applicable Ford technical service bulletins before replacing the RCM. If the original fault disappears, continue intermittent diagnosis without installing parts.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent connections
steps.body: A13 monitors resistance during harness movement; A14 attempts to reproduce the ground code during self-test. A15 checks intermittent voltage faults with the airbag disconnected under its specified power sequence. Reproduced faults require depowering and repair. If unreproduced, A16 still requires a depowered inspection of wiring, terminals, RCM locks and the airbag CPA tab.

steps.title: Restore the complete system
steps.body: Follow A17 to reconnect components with ignition off and repower when required, without an intermediate prove-out. Run the complete Restraints self-test for the fitted restraint-related modules. Resolve every on-demand fault before clearing codes or releasing the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Damaged restraint terminals
watchFor.body: Use service connector pigtails when restraint terminals need repair; do not attempt to repair the terminals themselves.

watchFor.title: A plausible-looking replacement
watchFor.body: Verify the correct part number. A physically similar airbag from another application may be incompatible.

notes: Carry a live airbag with its deployment surface away from the body, and never place it deployment-side down.
Do not move or alter the RCM mounting position while it is connected and the ignition is on.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1404:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects a driver side airbag circuit short to ground.
diagnostics.next: Use A8–A9 for an active fault or A14 for an intermittent fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1404:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects unwanted voltage on the deployment circuit.
diagnostics.next: Use A10 for an active fault or A15 for an intermittent fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1404:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is above the desired range, indicating an open/high-resistance condition.
diagnostics.next: Use A2 and the high-resistance branch, or A13 for a memory-only fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1404:1A is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is below the desired range.
diagnostics.next: Use A2 and the low-resistance branch, or A13 for a memory-only fault; inspect connector seating as directed.

verification.title: Confirm resistance stability
verification.body: Record DEPLOY_10_R and harness-test behavior. The reading must remain within 1.44 to 3.52 ohms; absence of an on-demand code does not replace this requirement.

verification.title: Record the final system result
verification.body: Document the completed Restraints self-test. Any remaining on-demand restraint fault requires further diagnosis before code clearing and vehicle release.

procedures.purpose: Complete driver side airbag B1404 isolation, intermittent testing and final verification.
Mandatory pyrotechnic handling and restraint-service precautions.
Prioritize accompanying on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 faults.
Depower the SRS at each directed test stage.
Repower the SRS in the prescribed diagnostic sequence.
Access the seat-backrest harness and replace the side airbag only when directed.
Replace the RCM only after the confirmation branch.
Diagnose additional restraint faults found during final self-test.

guides.title: Diagnose left curtain airbag circuit faults on a coupe
guides.summary: Trace B1405 curtain-airbag faults through wiring, connections and controlled diagnostic checks before authorizing component replacement.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) monitors the left curtain airbag deployment circuit and supplies deployment current when needed. This diagnosis separates wiring and connector faults from an airbag or module fault; an illuminated airbag warning indicator alone cannot identify the failed part.
guides.why: Terminal fit and harness strain can change circuit resistance as the vehicle moves. A connector assurance tab that is not fully seated can leave protective shorting bars engaged, producing low resistance even though the connector appears attached.

when.summary: When the RCM reports B1405:11, B1405:12, B1405:13 or B1405:1A, either currently or in continuous memory.
notes: A stored code without an on-demand fault follows the intermittent branch.

prepare.title: Use qualified restraint-system personnel
prepare.detail: Read the pyrotechnic precautions first. Supplemental restraint system (SRS) servicing requires qualified personnel and exact depowering and repowering procedures. Disconnect or reconnect components only when instructed.

prepare.title: Arrange the diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use an RCM-capable scan tool, suitable electrical test equipment, correct probe adapters and the specified fused jumper where directed. Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5 provide circuit and repair information. Never probe airbag assembly connectors or back-probe deployable-device connectors.

steps.title: Establish which fault is present
steps.body: Perform the ignition-on RCM self-test in A1 of the [pinpoint procedure](#/document/G1696374). Address on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 through [Test AJ](#/document/G1696405) first. Current resistance faults enter A2, ground faults A8 and voltage faults A10; memory-only faults enter A13–A15.

steps.title: Record resistance and its response to movement
steps.body: For A2–A3, monitor and record the DEPLOY_11_R parameter identification (PID) value. The required range is 1.44–3.52 ohms. An initially acceptable reading leads to A12. If harness movement brings an abnormal reading into range, depower and repair the connection or wiring concern; persistently low or high readings follow their separate branches.

steps.title: Separate resistance faults from component faults
steps.body: Follow A4–A7 exactly. Disconnecting the curtain should change a low-resistance fault to an open; otherwise test for wiring shorted together. For excessive resistance, check circuit continuity before the prescribed harness-side fused-jumper test. An open-to-low-resistance change supports correct RCM fault recognition. Remove the jumper before continuing to A11 or A12 as directed.

steps.title: Investigate ground or unwanted voltage
steps.body: A8 disconnects the curtain under the prescribed depower/repower sequence: a ground-fault change to an open leads to A11. Otherwise A9 checks the isolated wiring for a ground short. A10 checks for unwanted voltage with the curtain and RCM disconnected and the system repowered as specified. Repair failed circuits; passing wiring checks lead to A12.

steps.title: Confirm before replacing anything
steps.body: At A11 or A12, depower, inspect wiring, terminals and connector assurance locks, repair concerns and reconnect all required components before retesting. A11 authorizes a new [curtain airbag](#/document/G1696310) only if the original fault returns. A12 requires checking applicable technical service bulletins before authorizing a new [RCM](#/document/G1696307). A disappearing fault returns to intermittent diagnosis.

steps.title: Pursue intermittent faults without guessing
steps.body: A13 monitors resistance during harness movement; A14 repeats the self-test for an intermittent ground short. A15 requires curtain disconnection through its depower/repower sequence before testing for an intermittent voltage short. Depower before repairs. If unreproduced, A16 checks corrosion, terminal fit, damaged wiring and assurance locks; do not replace SRS components speculatively.

steps.title: Restore the complete system
steps.body: Follow A17 with ignition off and all SRS components reconnected. Repower if previously depowered, without performing an intermediate SRS prove-out. Then run the complete Restraints self-test, rather than checking only the curtain circuit.

watchFor.title: Damaged restraint terminals
watchFor.body: Replace damaged restraint connector terminals using service connector pigtails; do not repair the terminals themselves.

watchFor.title: Unsafe component handling
watchFor.body: Keep a live curtain's tear seam away from your body. Do not move a connected RCM with ignition on.

notes: Match replacement SRS part numbers to the vehicle; physical similarity does not establish compatibility.

diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects a sustained short to ground or unwanted voltage, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Use the matching current or intermittent circuit branch.

diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is excessive or below threshold, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Evaluate the recorded resistance and follow controlled isolation tests; neither code alone condemns the curtain.

verification.title: Record the repaired resistance
verification.body: Confirm and record DEPLOY_11_R within 1.44–3.52 ohms, including the prescribed harness test. Absence of an on-demand code alone is insufficient.

verification.title: Confirm the complete restraint result
verification.body: Resolve all on-demand faults reported by the Restraints self-test before clearing codes. Release the vehicle only with the SRS fully operational and free of faults.

RCM removal and installation when A12 authorizes replacement.

guides.title: Diagnose passenger seat side-airbag circuit faults
guides.summary: Trace B1407 faults through the passenger side-airbag circuit, including the seat-backrest harness, before authorizing replacement.
guides.introduction: The passenger side airbag is housed in the seat backrest. Its deployment circuit connects it to the restraints control module (RCM), which checks electrical integrity and commands deployment when needed. This diagnosis examines the wiring, connections, airbag and module in sequence.
guides.why: Harness strain and changing terminal contact can move deployment-loop resistance outside its acceptable range. The seat-backrest harness must also be inspected before a suspected airbag is replaced.

when.summary: When the RCM records a B1407 passenger side-airbag deployment-circuit fault.

prepare.title: Use qualified personnel and suitable test equipment
prepare.detail: Prepare an RCM-capable scan tool, electrical meter, correct probe adapters and the specified fused jumper. Read the pyrotechnic precautions and inspect wiring and connectors before testing.

prepare.title: Control power and connector changes
prepare.detail: Follow the complete supplemental restraint system (SRS) depowering and repowering procedures at each directed stage. Do not perform SRS prove-out during interim repowering or disconnect components speculatively.

steps.title: Retrieve codes and establish priority
steps.body: Start with A1 in the [passenger side-airbag test](#/document/G1696375). Run the RCM self-test. On-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 must take the Test AJ route first. B1407 faults recorded only in continuous memory follow the intermittent branches.

steps.title: Measure resistance through the scan tool
steps.body: For active open or low-resistance faults, A2–A3 use the DEPLOY_13_R parameter identification (PID) value. Record readings before and during harness movement. The required range is 1.44–3.52 ohms. An initially acceptable reading leads to A12; movement restoring an abnormal reading calls for depowering and connection or wiring repair.

steps.title: Separate low resistance from lost continuity
steps.body: A4 disconnects inline connector C219 to seek an open-code response; an unchanged low-resistance fault leads to A5’s wire-to-wire short check. High resistance follows A6 continuity checks and A7’s prescribed fused-jumper test, which should produce a low-resistance code. Remove the jumper afterward and follow the indicated airbag or module confirmation branch.

steps.title: Investigate shorts to ground or voltage
steps.body: A8–A10 isolate these faults. A ground fault changing to an open code after C219 disconnection leads to A11. Otherwise, check the isolated harness. Repair a detected short; passing wiring tests lead to module confirmation.

steps.title: Inspect the backrest harness before condemning the airbag
steps.body: At A11, depower and inspect wiring, terminals, RCM locks and airbag C3459 connector-position-assurance (CPA) tabs and clip. Repair defects, reconnect all components and retest as directed. If the original code returns, remove and inspect the seat-backrest harness using the Side Airbag procedure. Repair harness damage; install a new airbag only if no harness concern is found.

steps.title: Confirm module faults or pursue intermittents
steps.body: A12 repeats connector inspection and self-test with everything connected. A returning original code requires checking OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins before RCM replacement. If absent, use A13–A15: monitor resistance or repeat self-test during harness movement. The voltage branch requires prescribed depowering, C219 disconnection and repowering. Unreproduced faults proceed to A16’s wiring and CPA inspection without speculative replacement.

steps.title: Complete repairs and restore the system
steps.body: Depower before repairs identified by intermittent testing. Follow A17’s reconnection and repowering sequence, then run the complete Restraints self-test. Diagnose every remaining on-demand restraint fault before clearing codes or releasing the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Direct airbag probing
watchFor.body: Use only specified harness test points. Never probe airbag assembly connectors or back-probe deployable devices.

watchFor.title: Poor connector engagement
watchFor.body: An unseated CPA tab can retain the connector’s shorting action and produce low resistance. Damaged restraint terminals require service pigtails.

notes: Verify replacement SRS part numbers. Carry a live airbag with its deployment cover or tear seam facing away from your body.

diagnostics.finding: B1407:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detected a short to ground in a side-airbag circuit.
diagnostics.next: Use A8–A9.

diagnostics.finding: B1407:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detected unwanted voltage in a side-airbag circuit.
diagnostics.next: Use A10.

diagnostics.finding: B1407:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is above the desired range.
diagnostics.next: Start with A2.

diagnostics.finding: B1407:1A is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is below the desired range.
diagnostics.next: Start with A2.

verification.title: Record electrical stability
verification.body: Document DEPLOY_13_R readings and harness-movement response. Resistance must be within 1.44–3.52 ohms even if no on-demand code remains.

verification.title: Confirm overall restraint operation
verification.body: All components must be connected, the final self-test free of on-demand faults, and the SRS fully operational.

guides.title: Diagnose right-hand curtain airbag circuit faults on a coupe
guides.summary: Trace B1408 faults through the curtain wiring, connectors and control module before deciding whether a component needs replacement.
guides.introduction: The coupe’s right-hand curtain airbag is an electrically deployed restraint. The restraints control module (RCM) monitors its deployment circuit and commands deployment when required. This diagnosis separates connection and wiring problems from curtain or module faults in the supplemental restraint system (SRS).
guides.why: Vibration and strained terminals can alter circuit resistance intermittently. A disappearing fault code is insufficient: the measured deployment-loop resistance must also return to the required range.

when.summary: When an RCM self-test or continuous-memory record identifies a B1408 curtain-circuit fault.

prepare.title: Arrange qualified restraint-system diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use qualified personnel, an RCM-capable scan tool, an electrical meter, correct probe adapters and the specified fused jumper. Read the pyrotechnic precautions and inspect wiring and connections first.

prepare.title: Follow each prescribed power state
prepare.detail: Use the linked depowering and repowering procedures exactly. Disconnect components only when instructed; interim repowering must not include SRS prove-out.

steps.title: Separate active faults from stored events
steps.body: Follow A1 in the [curtain circuit test](#/document/G1696376). Run the RCM self-test with ignition on. Diagnose on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 through Test AJ first. A B1408 code present only in continuous memory takes the intermittent branch.

steps.title: Record resistance and its response to movement
steps.body: For active open or low-resistance faults, A2–A3 monitor the DEPLOY_14_R parameter identification (PID) value. Record resistance before and during harness flexing. The required range is 1.44–3.52 ohms. An initially acceptable reading leads to A12; movement that restores an abnormal reading directs connection or harness repair after depowering.

steps.title: Distinguish a shorted loop from an open loop
steps.body: For persistent low resistance, A4–A5 disconnect the curtain, check for an open-code response and, if unchanged, test for a short between wires. High resistance follows A6 continuity checks before A7’s prescribed harness jumper test. The expected jumper response is a low-resistance code. Remove the jumper after either result and follow the indicated confirmation branch.

steps.title: Isolate ground and voltage faults
steps.body: A8–A10 address shorts to ground or voltage. A ground fault changing to an open code after curtain disconnection leads to A11. Otherwise, test the isolated wiring. Repair detected shorts; passing wiring checks lead to A12.

steps.title: Confirm the component before replacing it
steps.body: For A11–A12, depower and inspect terminals, damaged wires, RCM locks and curtain C9032 connector-position-assurance (CPA) tabs and clip. Repair defects, reconnect all components and repeat self-test as directed. At A11, the original code returning directs curtain replacement. At A12, check OASIS for applicable technical service bulletins before replacing the RCM; follow an applicable bulletin instead.

steps.title: Investigate intermittent faults
steps.body: A13 monitors resistance during harness movement; A14 repeats self-test after movement for ground faults. A15 requires depowering, curtain disconnection and prescribed repowering before recreating voltage faults. Depower before repairs. If unreproduced, A16 inspects wiring, corrosion and connector locks. Do not replace components merely because a stored code remains.

steps.title: Restore connections and test the complete system
steps.body: Follow A17’s ignition, reconnection and repowering sequence, then run the complete Restraints self-test. Diagnose every remaining on-demand restraint code before clearing codes or releasing the vehicle.

watchFor.title: Unsafe probing
watchFor.body: Measure only the specified harness points. Never probe curtain assembly connectors or back-probe deployable devices.

watchFor.title: Connector faults that resemble component failure
watchFor.body: An unseated CPA tab can leave shorting bars engaged. Damaged restraint terminals require service pigtails, not terminal reworking.

notes: Verify replacement SRS part numbers in the Ford parts catalog; physical similarity does not establish compatibility.

diagnostics.finding: B1408:11 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detected a short to ground in a curtain circuit.
diagnostics.next: Use A8–A9.

diagnostics.finding: B1408:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detected unwanted voltage in a curtain circuit.
diagnostics.next: Use A10.

diagnostics.finding: B1408:13 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance exceeds the desired range.
diagnostics.next: Start with A2.

diagnostics.finding: B1408:1A is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Deployment-loop resistance is below the desired range.
diagnostics.next: Start with A2.

verification.title: Record the resistance result
verification.body: Document DEPLOY_14_R readings, including harness-test behavior; resistance must be within 1.44–3.52 ohms.

verification.title: Confirm release readiness
verification.body: The final Restraints self-test must show no on-demand faults, with the SRS fully operational.

guides.title: Diagnose coupe side-impact sensor circuit faults
guides.summary: Trace driver-door and passenger B-pillar impact-sensor faults through connector, wiring and controlled fault-response checks before replacing components.
guides.introduction: The driver-door and passenger B-pillar impact sensors provide crash information to the restraints control module (RCM). The module monitors their electrical communication and requests the airbag warning indicator when a fault appears. This diagnosis separates sensor failures from wiring faults and module concerns.
guides.why: A fault in either sensor circuit can produce codes naming both locations. Deliberately changing the circuit condition, under the prescribed test conditions, establishes whether the RCM recognizes that change and helps prevent replacing the wrong component.

when.summary: When relevant impact-sensor codes accompany an airbag warning or remain in continuous memory.
notes: Pedestrian-protection wiring checks apply only where that wiring exists; wiring may be present without pedestrian sensors.

prepare.title: Arrange qualified restraint-system diagnosis
prepare.detail: Follow the pyrotechnic precautions. Have a scan tool capable of RCM and Restraints self-tests, a multimeter, correct probe adapters, a fused jumper and Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5.

prepare.title: Control access and system power
prepare.detail: Provide access to both sensors and the RCM. Follow each step's ignition, depowering and repowering instructions exactly. Disconnect components only when directed, and omit SRS prove-out during the specified diagnostic repowering steps.

steps.title: Inspect and establish the active fault
steps.body: Inspect harness damage, then run the ignition-on RCM self-test at A1 of the [pinpoint test](#/document/G1696386). Diagnose U3003:16 or U3003:17 first through Test AJ. Distinguish on-demand diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) from continuous-memory-only faults, which enter A15.

steps.title: Separate the two sensors in the short-to-ground branch
steps.body: In A2–A3, use the prescribed depowering cycles to disconnect the driver sensor first. A change to B1414:93 directs driver-sensor replacement. Otherwise reconnect it and disconnect the passenger sensor; a change to B1419:93 directs passenger-sensor replacement. Follow the corresponding sensor removal and installation procedure.

steps.title: Check wiring when sensor isolation does not change the fault
steps.body: A4–A5 isolate the RCM and sensor circuits for resistance checks between wires and to ground, including applicable pedestrian wiring. The specified readings must exceed 10,000 ohms. Repair a failing circuit; passing results lead to RCM confirmation at A14.

steps.title: Investigate simultaneous communication faults
steps.body: When both no-operation codes are active, A6–A7 check the driver circuit first, then the passenger circuit, for unwanted voltage. Follow the exact disconnection and powered-measurement sequence. Any voltage at the specified harness points requires circuit repair; no voltage leads to A14.

steps.title: Investigate a single communication fault
steps.body: Use A8–A10 for the driver sensor or A11–A13 for the passenger sensor. First secure sensor and RCM connectors and retest. If necessary, check isolated circuit continuity, then perform the specified fused-jumper test. The expected change to short-to-ground codes directs replacement of that sensor. Remove the jumper after testing; an unchanged fault leads to A14.

steps.title: Confirm the module or pursue an intermittent connection
steps.body: At A14, inspect terminals, wiring and Connector Position Assurance (CPA) locks, repair concerns and reconnect everything before self-test. If the original code persists, check applicable Technical Service Bulletins before replacing the RCM. A disappearing fault enters A15: inspect disconnected connectors and harnesses, reconnect and retest. Replace no component for an unreproduced fault.

steps.title: Restore the complete restraint system
steps.body: Follow A16 to restore disconnected components and the required power state, then perform the full Restraints self-test. Diagnose other on-demand restraint codes through the linked SRS diagnostic procedure. Do not clear codes while unresolved faults remain.

watchFor.title: Sensor probing is prohibited
watchFor.body: Do not probe an impact sensor or attempt to test it with a multimeter. Measurements belong at the specified harness points.

watchFor.title: Module position matters
watchFor.body: Never move the RCM while it is connected and the ignition is on. Restraint connector terminal repairs require service pigtails.

notes: Confirm replacement part numbers; physical similarity does not establish restraint-component compatibility.

diagnostics.finding: B1414:11 and B1419:11 are retrieved, possibly with B1427:11 and B14EB:11.
diagnostics.meaning: Shared short-to-ground reporting can involve either sensor circuit and applicable pedestrian-protection wiring.
diagnostics.next: Follow A2–A5.

diagnostics.finding: B1414:93 and B1419:93 are both retrieved.
diagnostics.meaning: Voltage on either sensor's feed or return can interrupt communication.
diagnostics.next: Follow A6–A7.

diagnostics.finding: Only B1414:93 is retrieved.
diagnostics.meaning: The driver-door sensor communication path needs connector, continuity and response checks.
diagnostics.next: Follow A8–A10.

diagnostics.finding: Only B1419:93 is retrieved.
diagnostics.meaning: The passenger B-pillar sensor communication path needs connector, continuity and response checks.
diagnostics.next: Follow A11–A13.

verification.title: Confirm system-wide completion
verification.body: The final Restraints self-test must return no on-demand faults from applicable restraint modules. The SRS must be fully operational before release.

verification.title: Record the outcome
verification.body: Record the initial code status, fault changes observed and final self-test result. Identify an unreproduced intermittent concern accurately.

guides.title: Diagnose coupe side-impact sensor circuit faults
guides.summary: Trace passenger-door and driver B-pillar impact-sensor faults through wiring checks, controlled fault changes and restraints self-tests.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) monitors the passenger-door and driver B-pillar impact sensors as part of the supplemental restraint system (SRS). These sensors help the module assess a side impact. Their electrical faults can produce related codes, so a code naming one sensor does not automatically identify the failed part. This diagnosis separates connection problems, damaged wiring, sensor faults and an RCM fault.
guides.why: Controlled changes in the reported fault show whether the RCM recognizes a changed circuit condition. This is more informative than replacing the named sensor, and avoids attempting to measure an impact sensor directly.

when.summary: When coupe restraints testing records B1415:11, B1415:93, B1418:11, B1418:93 or B1424:11.
notes: Pedestrian-protection wiring may be present without pedestrian-protection sensors; use that branch only where the wiring is fitted.

prepare.title: Arrange qualified restraints diagnosis
prepare.detail: Follow the pyrotechnic precautions. Provide a diagnostic scan tool, multimeter, correct probe adapters, fused jumper and Wiring Diagrams Cells 46 and 5.

prepare.title: Plan access and power transitions
prepare.detail: Access the passenger-door sensor, driver B-pillar sensor and RCM. Disconnect or reconnect components only when directed. Follow the linked depowering and repowering procedures at each specified transition; intermediate repowering expressly omits SRS prove-out.

steps.title: Establish which faults are present
steps.body: Run the ignition-on RCM self-test at A1. Diagnose on-demand U3003:16 or U3003:17 first through the linked voltage-fault test. Route other codes through the general SRS diagnosis. Impact-sensor codes present only in continuous memory take the intermittent branch.

steps.title: Separate shorted sensors from ground faults
steps.body: Follow A2–A3 with their depower, disconnect, repower and self-test sequence. Disconnecting the driver sensor must change the ground-short codes to B1415:93 before replacement is directed. Otherwise reconnect it and test the passenger sensor; a change to B1418:93 directs installation of a new passenger sensor.

steps.title: Check the remaining short-circuit branches
steps.body: If sensor isolation does not change the ground fault, A4–A5 test the disconnected harness for grounding and shorts between sensor circuits, including applicable pedestrian wiring. Required resistance is greater than 10,000 ohms. For both no-operation codes together, A6–A7 instead check both sensors’ feed and return wiring for voltage under the prescribed powered conditions. Repair failed circuits.

steps.title: Investigate a single no-operation code
steps.body: A8–A9 cover the driver sensor; A11–A12 cover the passenger sensor. First seat and lock the affected sensor and RCM connectors, then retest. If the code remains, isolate the wiring and check both end-to-end circuits. Each must measure less than 0.5 ohm; repair an open or excessive resistance before proceeding.

steps.title: Use the directed fault-change test
steps.body: With continuity established, follow only the harness-side fused-jumper setup in A10 or A13. The expected response is B1415:11 and B1418:11, plus B1424:11 where applicable. That response directs replacement of the affected sensor. Remove the jumper on either outcome; an unchanged fault leads to A14.

steps.title: Confirm a module fault before replacement
steps.body: At A14 inspect terminals, inline connectors, harness damage and RCM connector-position assurance locks. Repair concerns and reconnect everything before retesting. If the original on-demand code remains, check applicable technical service bulletins before following the RCM replacement decision. A disappearing fault moves to intermittent diagnosis.

steps.title: Resolve intermittent faults and finish testing
steps.body: A15 repeats the depowered connector and harness inspection, then restores connections and retests. A returning code re-enters its matching branch. If the fault cannot be recreated, do not install new SRS components. Finish with A16 and the complete Restraints self-test.

watchFor.title: Do not measure the sensors themselves
watchFor.body: Impact sensors cannot be tested with a multimeter. Measurements and jumper connections belong only at the harness points specified in the pinpoint test.

watchFor.title: Preserve restraint connections
watchFor.body: Damaged restraint connector terminals require service pigtails. Use the correct replacement part and specified mounting torque; do not move a connected RCM with the ignition on.

notes: Most faults in this test arise from connectors or wiring, making the initial inspection an essential diagnostic step.

diagnostics.finding: B1415:11 or B1418:11 is retrieved on-demand.
diagnostics.meaning: Either monitored sensor or either feed circuit can cause the ground-short indication.
diagnostics.next: Begin at A2; do not select a replacement from the code label.

diagnostics.finding: B1415:93 and B1418:93 are retrieved together.
diagnostics.meaning: A voltage short can disrupt communication with both sensors.
diagnostics.next: Begin the voltage checks at A6.

diagnostics.finding: Only B1415:93 or only B1418:93 is retrieved.
diagnostics.meaning: No operation can reflect a sensor, connection or circuit fault.
diagnostics.next: Use A8 for B1415:93 or A11 for B1418:93.

diagnostics.finding: B1424:11 accompanies the side-impact ground-short codes.
diagnostics.meaning: Applicable pedestrian-protection wiring can share the fault indication even without fitted sensors.
diagnostics.next: Include that wiring in the A4 checks.

verification.title: Confirm all restraints faults are resolved
verification.body: Restore all connections and perform A16. Do not clear codes while any on-demand restraints faults remain. The SRS must be operational and fault-free before release.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record the original codes, decisive fault change or circuit finding, repairs and final Restraints self-test result. Identify an unreproduced intermittent concern accurately.

guides.title: Diagnose passenger front impact sensor faults B1417:11 and B1417:93
guides.summary: Use controlled fault-status changes and harness checks to distinguish passenger front impact sensor, connection and restraint-module faults.
guides.introduction: The passenger front impact severity sensor supplies crash information to the restraints control module (RCM). The RCM monitors its circuits and requests the airbag warning indicator when it detects these faults. This diagnosis identifies whether the problem lies in the sensor, its wiring or the module receiving its signal.
guides.why: Most faults involve wiring or connectors. Deliberately changing the circuit condition, exactly as prescribed, checks whether the RCM recognizes that change. This provides useful evidence without attempting to measure the sensor itself.
searchTerms: passenger front impact sensor circuit fault

when.summary: Use when the RCM reports B1417:11 or B1417:93, either during self-test or only in continuous memory.

prepare.title: Qualified restraint-system service
prepare.detail: Follow the pyrotechnic precautions and exact supplemental restraint system (SRS) depowering and repowering procedures. Incorrect actions can cause deployment. Disconnect or reconnect components only when directed; intermediate repowering does not include SRS prove-out.

prepare.title: Equipment and access
prepare.detail: Use a capable scan tool, multimeter for the specified harness tests, fused jumper and wiring information. Never probe an impact sensor or deployable device. Right-hand-drive vehicles require air-cleaner removal at the indicated access steps.

steps.title: Inspect and establish fault status
steps.body: Inspect sensor damage, mounting, orientation, wiring and connectors. Run the RCM self-test. Prioritize U3003:16 or U3003:17 if present. Otherwise, an on-demand B1417:11 starts at A2 and B1417:93 at A5. A sensor code present only in continuous memory follows the intermittent-fault branch at A10.

steps.title: Follow the ground-short branch
steps.body: For B1417:11, depower, disconnect the sensor and repower as instructed. A change to B1417:93 directs sensor replacement. If the code does not change, follow the depowered checks for a feed-to-ground short and a short between the sensor circuits. Repair a failed circuit; passing checks lead to RCM confirmation.

steps.title: Check connections for a no-operation fault
steps.body: For B1417:93, depower and check that the sensor and RCM connectors are seated and locked. Repower and repeat the self-test. If the code disappears, proceed to final checks. If it remains, follow the isolated feed-circuit voltage check and then the depowered feed-and-return continuity checks.

steps.title: Use the prescribed fault-change test
steps.body: After passing those circuit checks, A8 uses a fused jumper at the specified disconnected sensor harness terminals. Follow its power-state sequence exactly. A change from B1417:93 to B1417:11 directs sensor replacement. Remove the jumper as instructed in either outcome; an unchanged fault proceeds to RCM confirmation.

steps.title: Confirm before replacing the RCM
steps.body: Inspect terminals, inline connectors, harness damage and the RCM connector position assurance locks. Reconnect all components and repeat the prescribed self-test. If the original code remains, check applicable technical service bulletins before the RCM replacement branch. If it disappears, continue as an intermittent concern without replacing components.

steps.title: Investigate an intermittent fault
steps.body: A10 repeats the depowered connector, harness and lock inspection, followed by reconnection, repowering and self-test. A returning code restarts its matching branch. If the fault cannot be recreated, do not install new SRS components.

steps.title: Check the complete restraint system
steps.body: Reconnect components and repower as directed, then select the Restraints self-test. This checks the RCM, occupant classification system module and any additional equipped module included by that menu. Diagnose every on-demand fault; do not clear codes until all have been resolved.

watchFor.title: Damaged terminals or crash mountings
watchFor.body: Use service connector pigtails rather than repairing restraint connector terminals. Crash-damaged sensor mounting areas require restoration and replacement of the original sensor, even without airbag deployment.

watchFor.title: Similar-looking replacement parts
watchFor.body: Verify the correct Ford catalog part and use the specified mounting torque. Physical similarity does not establish compatibility.

notes: An impact sensor cannot be tested with a multimeter; the specified electrical measurements are harness tests.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1417:11 is retrieved on demand.
diagnostics.meaning: The RCM detects a ground short on the passenger front impact sensor feed.
diagnostics.next: Begin A2's fault-change test.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1417:93 is retrieved on demand.
diagnostics.meaning: Possible causes include the sensor, a feed voltage short, or an open feed or return.
diagnostics.next: Begin A5 with connector seating checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3003:16 or U3003:17 is also retrieved on demand.
diagnostics.meaning: The diagnostic sequence gives these faults priority.
diagnostics.next: Follow Pinpoint Test AJ first.

verification.title: Confirm fault-free operation
verification.body: Release the vehicle only when the SRS is fully operational and the final Restraints self-test finds no on-demand faults.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record the original code, fault-status changes and final self-test result, including whether an intermittent fault remained unreproduced.

guides.title: Centralize the clockspring on vehicles without adaptive steering
guides.summary: Set the clockspring rotor to its prescribed central position and secure it against further rotation.
guides.introduction: The clockspring maintains electrical connections across the rotating steering-wheel assembly through an internal ribbon wire attached to its rotor. That wire has limited travel. Centralizing establishes the rotor’s correct starting position so it is not already near the end of that travel when returned to service. This procedure adjusts an accessible clockspring; it does not describe removing or reinstalling the steering wheel or airbag.
guides.why: The ribbon wire can act as a stop, but forcing the rotor against it can break an internal connection. Incorrect centralization can also cause premature failure and increase the risk of serious injury or death in a crash. Careful direction changes and an accurate turn count matter more than speed.

when.summary: When clockspring centralization is required or its current central position is uncertain.
notes: This procedure must not be used on vehicles with adaptive steering.

prepare.title: Arrange safe component access
prepare.detail: Any access involving airbag components requires the applicable restraint-system access procedure and appropriate SRS service capability. Begin this adjustment only with the clockspring rotor accessible.

prepare.title: Have adhesive tape ready
prepare.detail: The final rotor position must be secured immediately. Arrange the work so the connector position and complete rotor turns can be followed without interruption.

steps.title: Find the counterclockwise limit gently
steps.body: Turn the clockspring rotor counterclockwise, carefully feeling for resistance. Do not force it farther when resistance is encountered; the ribbon connection can be damaged by over-rotation.

steps.title: Establish the first connector reference
steps.body: Turn the rotor clockwise until its electrical connector is at the 12 o’clock position. This establishes the reference for the counted turns that follow.

steps.title: Make the prescribed counted turns
steps.body: From that reference, turn the rotor clockwise through 3 complete turns, finishing with the electrical connector again at 12 o’clock.

steps.title: Preserve the final position
steps.body: Secure the rotor with adhesive tape. After final positioning, do not allow it to rotate away from that position.

watchFor.title: Using force to find a firm stop
watchFor.body: The internal ribbon is not a mechanical stop to push against. Over-rotation can break its connection and cause component or system failure.

watchFor.title: Losing the reference or turn count
watchFor.body: The connector passes the same clock position repeatedly. Its final appearance alone cannot establish that the correct sequence was completed.

notes: All turning directions refer to the clockspring rotor.
Centralizing does not repair a broken internal ribbon connection.

diagnostics.finding: There is doubt about whether the rotor was correctly centralized.
diagnostics.meaning: The required final position has not been established confidently.
diagnostics.next: Repeat the complete centralizing procedure rather than estimating a correction.

verification.title: Confirm sequence and restraint
verification.body: Confirm that the rotor completed 3 clockwise turns after the first clockwise alignment at 12 o’clock, finishes with the connector at 12 o’clock and is secured against rotation.

procedures.purpose: Clockspring centralizing sequence and rotor securing for vehicles without adaptive steering.

guides.title: Inspect and restore the restraint system after deployment
guides.summary: Determine the required post-collision restraint replacements, inspect related structure and fuel-system damage, and complete the specified resets before vehicle release.
guides.introduction: The supplemental restraint system (SRS) uses airbags and seatbelt pretensioners to respond to a collision. Its restraints control module (RCM) monitors sensors and selects the devices to deploy, so a collision may activate one device or several. Repair must address the deployed equipment, its supporting structure and stored crash information as one coordinated job.
guides.why: Replacing visible airbags alone can leave damaged mounts, deployed belt components or unresolved control-system faults. The occupant classification system (OCS) also needs its own assessment and reset when components are replaced. The vehicle must have a fully operational, fault-free SRS before release.

when.summary: After restraint deployment or collision-related B1193:00 storage requiring the specified inspection and repair.
notes: Rear pretensioner and side-curtain requirements apply only where that equipment is fitted.
Stored crash information must be interpreted by module; the RCM and OCS module have different repair decisions.

prepare.title: Use qualified restraint personnel
prepare.detail: Pyrotechnic service requires qualified personnel and the [pyrotechnic safety precautions](#/document/G1693191). Follow each component's removal, isolation and installation requirements. Never probe airbag connectors or back-probe deployable-device connectors.

prepare.title: Provide diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: A diagnostic scan tool is required to read module faults, perform the OCS Reset when required, clear diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), and check or reset body control module (BCM) crash status.

prepare.title: Handle deployed and live devices correctly
prepare.detail: Do not handle pyrotechnic components immediately after deployment. Use protective gloves, safety glasses and breathing protection against residues. Carry live airbags with the deployment face away from the body and never set them face-down.

steps.title: Establish the deployment and module record
steps.body: Identify every deployed device and read the RCM and occupant classification system module (OCSM) faults. Apply the separate B1193:00 decisions below. When any deployable device has activated, or the RCM contains that code, replace all deployed devices, all impact sensors and the RCM with new components.

steps.title: Inspect structure and mounting points
steps.body: Inspect the instrument panel, its mounts, braces, brackets and knee bolsters; seats and seat mounts; fitted curtains and their mounts; belts, buckles, retractors and anchors; and SRS wiring and connectors. Repair or replace damaged components. Restore damaged RCM or sensor mounting areas to production configuration and replace the component mounted there, even if airbags did not deploy.

steps.title: Restore steering and seatbelt systems
steps.body: Driver-airbag deployment requires a new steering wheel, clockspring and adaptive energy absorption steering column. Replace the corresponding front seatbelt systems after front pretensioner deployment, including retractors, buckles and height adjusters. Rear pretensioner deployment, where equipped, requires new second-row retractors and buckles. Inspect all belt components as part of collision repair.

steps.title: Address side-airbag and curtain damage
steps.body: After seat side-airbag deployment, replace the airbag, backrest cover and foam; inspect its mounting area and replace a deformed backrest frame. After curtain deployment, install a new headliner, roof-pillar upper trim and attaching hardware, including new torque-prevailing J-nuts. Confirm the headliner AIRBAG marking at each roof B-pillar trim interface.

steps.title: Complete occupant-classification repairs
steps.body: If the OCSM stores B1193:00 after a collision, inspect the OCS and repair damage. Required OCS component replacement must use an OCS service kit. Keep calibrated assemblies together and free of contamination. After installing new OCS components, perform the scan-tool OCS Reset as directed.

steps.title: Finish installation and inspect the fuel system
steps.body: Inspect for fuel-system damage or leaks and repair or replace affected parts. Complete restraint installation through each component procedure, including specified mounting torques and connector locking. Clear DTCs from all required modules after repairs.

steps.title: Resolve BCM crash status
steps.body: Read the BCM CRASH parameter identification (PID) value. If present and reading Yes, perform BCM Crash Status Reset under Electrical - Service Functions. A No value or absent parameter does not cancel any remaining repair or SRS verification requirement.

watchFor.title: Steering-column damage without driver-airbag deployment
watchFor.body: A bent, loose or damaged wheel or shaft; binding, sticking, abnormal movement, bearing damage or incorrect shaft length also requires a new adaptive energy absorption column. Use the Steering Column Collapsed Check. Never fit a repaired, rebuilt or remanufactured column.

watchFor.title: Connector and module handling
watchFor.body: Replace damaged restraint terminals with service connector pigtails; do not repair the terminals. Never tamper with restraint components or move a connected RCM with the ignition on.

notes: A connector-position-assurance tab that is not fully seated can leave the component's shorting bars engaged and produce a low-resistance fault. A fault alone does not prove the airbag is defective.

diagnostics.finding: Any deployable device activated, or the RCM stores B1193:00.
diagnostics.meaning: The mandatory post-event replacement scope applies.
diagnostics.next: Install new deployed devices, all impact sensors and a new RCM.

diagnostics.finding: The OCSM stores B1193:00 after a collision.
diagnostics.meaning: The OCS requires inspection; this code does not itself establish which OCS component is damaged.
diagnostics.next: Repair identified damage, use a service kit for required OCS replacement and perform the required reset.

diagnostics.finding: BCM CRASH reads Yes.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM crash status requires resetting.
diagnostics.next: Run BCM Crash Status Reset with the diagnostic scan tool.

verification.title: Establish release readiness
verification.body: Confirm the SRS is fully operational and free of faults, all required collision repairs are complete, and fuel-system damage or leaks have been addressed.

verification.title: Record the final diagnostic result
verification.body: Record replaced devices and sensors, module fault results, any OCS Reset performed, and the BCM CRASH reading and reset action where applicable.

procedures.purpose: Post-deployment replacement decisions, whole-vehicle inspection and final crash-status handling.
Required pyrotechnic handling, mounting, connector and collision-repair precautions.
Check steering-column collapse and shaft length when assessing column replacement.

guides.title: Select and complete the correct restraint-device disposal route
guides.summary: Identify each restraint device and its deployment state, then follow the required return, controlled deployment or disposal procedure.
guides.introduction: Airbags and seatbelt pretensioners use electrically initiated pyrotechnic devices to act rapidly during a collision. Their disposal requires knowing what is fitted and whether every deployment stage has operated. A visibly deployed front airbag can still contain an undeployed stage or active canister vent. This is specialist restraints work: the guide explains the available paths, while the complete device-specific procedure governs preparation and deployment.
guides.why: Removing a device or disconnecting its connector does not establish that it is inert. Inoperative live devices follow a mandatory return route, while scrap devices may require controlled deployment. Correct containment, remote operation and cooling protect the people handling them; identifying all loops and stages prevents a partly deployed device from entering the scrap stream.

when.summary: When an inoperative restraint needs return, or a vehicle or restraint device is being prepared for disposal.
notes: Confirm fitted equipment before selecting a branch. The shared procedure's Safety Canopy®, inflatable-seatbelt, adaptive-retractor and deployable-column branches apply only where those devices are actually fitted.
Treat discolored or damaged airbags as inoperative live airbags requiring return.

prepare.title: Meet the restraints-service prerequisites
prepare.detail: Use a technician equipped for pyrotechnic restraint disposal. Read Pyrotechnic Device Health and Safety Precautions in General Information, section 100-00, and follow the complete SRS depowering procedure.

prepare.title: Identify every device and stage
prepare.detail: Use the system operation and component description to identify fitted airbags, pretensioners and other deployable devices, including multiple stages and an active canister vent where equipped.

prepare.title: Prepare the prescribed deployment equipment
prepare.detail: Remote containment uses a tire and wheel assembly with four additional same-size tires, large enough for the device and securely tied together. The procedure specifies two jumper wires, 20 gauge minimum and at least 9.14 m (30 ft) long, insulating material and a 12-volt battery. Follow its exact pigtail and harness preparation before positioning a device.

steps.title: Classify the device before choosing a route
steps.body: Determine whether it is undeployed and inoperative, already deployed, or requires manual deployment for scrapping. Inoperative airbags, seatbelt pretensioners and inflatable-seatbelt inflators are on the Mandatory Return List.

steps.title: Depower the system and obtain the required access
steps.body: Follow [SRS depowering](#/document/G1696297) before removing a device or accessing its deployment wiring. Use the appropriate restraint or seatbelt removal procedure for remote deployment and return work; the in-vehicle branches have their own connector-access requirements.

steps.title: Complete the inoperative-device return route
steps.body: Remove the undeployed, inoperative device through its component procedure and follow the mandatory return requirements. When installing a new airbag or inflatable-seatbelt inflator, record the new part serial number and vehicle identification number on the supplied prepaid return postcard and send it to Ford. Return the inoperative airbag as directed.

steps.title: Resolve remaining stages in crash-deployed airbags
steps.body: Identify whether a deployed driver or passenger airbag is dual stage. Required manual deployment must ensure both stages and the active canister vent, if fitted, have operated before disposal. A deployed cover alone does not establish completion.

steps.title: Use the correct remote-airbag branch
steps.body: Follow [airbag remote deployment](#/document/G1696296), including all loops and additional deployment features. Where no hard-wired pigtail exists, the procedure distinguishes cutting the vehicle wiring on a scrap vehicle from obtaining the appropriate pigtail kit for a vehicle being retained. Driver airbags sit trim-cover upward on the wheel with the wheel at the bottom. Passenger, knee and seat-side airbags use the center tire with the wheel uppermost after positioning.

steps.title: Use the remote seatbelt-device branch where applicable
steps.body: The remote method covers anchor, buckle and retractor pretensioners, adaptive load-limiting retractors and seatbelt inflators. Position the device in the center tire with the wheel uppermost. A buckle pretensioner additionally requires a nut and bolt of sufficient length and the same diameter used to retain it to the seat. Follow the branch's pigtail preparation.

steps.title: Select the in-vehicle seatbelt branch when required
steps.body: This branch covers anchor, buckle and retractor pretensioners and adaptive load-limiting retractors. After depowering and gaining connector access, its wire preparation leaves at least 101.6 mm (4 in) to work with. Follow the specified jumper connections and insulation sequence.

steps.title: Keep canopy and curtain deployment equipment-specific
steps.body: For the in-vehicle Safety Canopy® or side-air-curtain branch, access the connectors after depowering and follow its wire preparation. Safety Canopy® deployment for a scrap vehicle occurs in its installed position. Where multiple loops exist, prepare all of them using the prescribed connections.

steps.title: Follow the deployable-column branch only when fitted
steps.body: Access may require lowering or removing the column from the instrument panel. Where it lacks a hard-wired pigtail, the procedure specifies retaining the vehicle connector wiring and reconnecting it to the column before completing the prescribed harness preparation.

steps.title: Complete remote operation, cooling and disposal
steps.body: Keep the remote harness ends joined until the prescribed deployment stage, with device-end connections insulated against contact. Follow the selected branch's battery-connection sequence and maintain the specified remote working distance of at least 9.14 m (30 ft). Wait at least 10 minutes after deployment before approaching. Package deployed airbag modules in replacement-module packaging or a suitable polythene bag, then follow applicable contaminated-waste requirements; where none apply, use the ordinary scrap-parts route.

watchFor.title: Partly deployed devices
watchFor.body: Every required loop, stage and active feature must be addressed. Do not infer that all charges operated from the visible condition of the airbag.

watchFor.title: Connector protection mistaken for a safe-state test
watchFor.body: Deployable-component connectors incorporate shorting bars and connector-position assurance tabs. These features do not replace depowering, device identification or the disposal procedure.

notes: Use the exact branch in the complete procedure for containment and wiring; deployment arrangements differ between device types.
The inoperative-device return route remains separate from manual deployment of devices being scrapped.

diagnostics.finding: An airbag is damaged, discolored or inoperative while undeployed.
diagnostics.meaning: It must be handled as an inoperative live airbag.
diagnostics.next: Depower, remove through its component procedure and follow the mandatory return route.

diagnostics.finding: A dual-stage front airbag has deployed in a collision.
diagnostics.meaning: Another stage or active canister vent may remain undeployed.
diagnostics.next: Complete the required remote-deployment procedure before scrapping or disposal.

verification.title: Confirm the disposition of every device
verification.body: Account for each identified device and, where applicable, every deployment stage and feature before releasing the vehicle or components for scrap.

verification.title: Complete the handling record
verification.body: For the return route, confirm the required new-part serial number and vehicle identification number have been recorded and submitted. For disposal, confirm cooling, airbag packaging and the applicable waste route are complete.

procedures.purpose: Select the mandatory-return, deployed-device disposal, remote-deployment or equipment-specific in-vehicle deployment route.
Depower the supplemental restraint system before device removal or deployment-wiring access.
Identify fitted restraint devices, dual-stage airbags and deployment features before selecting a disposal branch.

guides.title: Depower the airbag and seatbelt pretensioner system
guides.summary: Assess the restraint warning indications and follow the appropriate fault-dependent depowering sequence before vehicle service.
guides.introduction: The supplemental restraint system (SRS) includes airbags and seatbelt pretensioners. Its restraints control module (RCM) monitors inputs and supplies deployment current when required. Depowering prepares the vehicle for service, but the required path depends on whether the system reports a fault. Switching off the ignition does not eliminate the prescribed backup-power waiting period.
guides.why: Incorrect actions can cause accidental deployment, so the sequence must be followed precisely. The initial indicator check determines which branch applies. In the fault-present branch, a scan-tool Network Test verifies module isolation before battery disconnection; removing an assumed fuse is not sufficient confirmation.
searchTerms: airbag warning light does not illuminate

when.summary: When planned vehicle service requires the SRS to be depowered.
notes: Diagnose and repair existing SRS faults before proceeding with other repairs.

prepare.title: Use restraint-system service capability
prepare.detail: Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) and the full depowering procedure before starting. Disable remote start before work around the vehicle. Do not depart from the specified restraint-service sequence.

prepare.title: Prepare for the fault-present branch
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool capable of a Network Test, the vehicle's fuse information in Wiring Diagram Cell 11/Section 700-01, and [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356). Identify actual fitted equipment before selecting fuses.

steps.title: Observe the complete warning-indicator check
steps.body: Turn the ignition OFF and wait 10 seconds, then turn it ON. The airbag indicator should illuminate continuously for approximately 6 seconds and then go out. Continue monitoring for approximately 30 seconds while the RCM completes its testing.

steps.title: Select the correct branch
steps.body: A failure to illuminate, continuous illumination or flashing indicates a fault; flashing may begin only after approximately 30 seconds. With an inoperative indicator, a fault can instead produce 5 sets of 5 beeps or a message-center warning. Diagnose the indicator and SRS faults before unrelated repairs. Use the fault-present branch when depowering during that fault work.

steps.title: Depower when no fault is present
steps.body: If the indicator completed its normal check and remains off after 30 seconds, with no chime or SRS message, turn the ignition OFF and wait one minute before service. The ignition must remain OFF until the repair is complete. This branch does not continue into the following fault-present steps.

steps.title: Fault present: isolate the specified module supply
steps.body: Turn the ignition OFF. Remove the RCM fuse or, if equipped, the battery energy control module B (BECMB) fuse(s), using the vehicle's wiring information. Only where a shared 3-blade BECMB/gateway module (GWM) fuse is fitted, install a 2-blade 10A fuse at the GWM position to retain scan-tool network communication.

steps.title: Fault present: verify isolation electronically
steps.body: Turn the ignition ON and perform a Network Test. Verify that the RCM and, if equipped, BECMB do not respond. If either module passes the test, remove the correct fuse and repeat the Network Test. Do not continue until the required nonresponse is verified.

steps.title: Fault present: disconnect the battery and wait
steps.body: Turn the ignition OFF, disconnect the battery using its linked procedure, and wait at least one minute before continuing vehicle service. Keep this order: verified isolation, ignition OFF, battery disconnection, then the waiting period.

watchFor.title: An indicator that never lights
watchFor.body: Do not confuse failure to illuminate during the initial check with the normal condition of going out afterward.

watchFor.title: Loss of all network communication
watchFor.body: An unavailable vehicle network is not the required confirmation of isolated modules. Preserve gateway communication using the conditional fuse instruction where applicable.

notes: BECMB and shared gateway-fuse instructions apply only when the vehicle's actual equipment and wiring identify that branch.
Completion leaves the vehicle prepared for service in a depowered state. Re-enabling the restraints requires the applicable restoration procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The RCM or an applicable BECMB still responds during the isolation Network Test.
diagnostics.meaning: Required module isolation has not been established.
diagnostics.next: Correct the fuse selection and repeat the test before battery disconnection.

diagnostics.finding: The indicator remains off after normal prove-out, with no chime or SRS message after 30 seconds.
diagnostics.meaning: The specified check identifies no SRS fault.
diagnostics.next: Use the ignition-OFF, one-minute waiting branch and keep the ignition OFF throughout repair.

verification.title: Confirm the branch prerequisites
verification.body: For the no-fault branch, confirm the one-minute wait and continued ignition-OFF state. For the fault branch, confirm module nonresponse, battery disconnection and the subsequent wait of at least one minute.

verification.title: Record the depowering result
verification.body: Record the initial warning indications, selected branch and completed waiting period. For the fault branch, also record the Network Test isolation result.

procedures.purpose: SRS warning assessment and separate no-fault and fault-present depowering sequences.
Mandatory general service safety precautions before restraint-system work.
Battery disconnection within the fault-present depowering branch.

guides.title: Repower the supplemental restraint system and verify its self-test
guides.summary: Follow the correct initial-fault branch, restore power where required and confirm that the restraint system completes its warning-indicator test.
guides.introduction: The supplemental restraint system (SRS) includes airbags and seatbelt pretensioners controlled by the restraints control module (RCM). The RCM monitors inputs and commands deployment when required. Repowering returns this system to service after repair; its prove-out sequence checks for faults before the vehicle is released.
guides.why: Incorrect actions can cause accidental deployment, so the sequence must be followed precisely. An airbag lamp going out is meaningful only after its initial illumination and the complete observation period. Some faults appear late, and an inoperative lamp can be accompanied by an audible or displayed warning.
searchTerms: airbag warning light does not illuminate

when.summary: After restraint-system repair, when restoring operation and completing the required SRS prove-out.
notes: The SRS must be fully operational and free of faults before vehicle release.

prepare.title: Use restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: This requires a technician competent in pyrotechnic-system service. Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189), including its system-specific safety references, and disable remote start during servicing.

prepare.title: Establish the correct branch
prepare.detail: Determine whether an SRS fault existed at the beginning of the repair. Have the vehicle’s fuse information from Wiring Diagram Cell 11/Section 700-01 available for the fault-present branch.

prepare.title: Prepare for restoration
prepare.detail: Confirm that all airbags are installed and connected. Have access to the battery connection procedure and a scan tool capable of clearing continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes from all modules.

steps.title: Choose the initial-fault path
steps.body: If no SRS fault was present when repair began, follow that branch directly to the prove-out below. If an SRS fault was present, carry out the fuse, battery and seating sequence first.

steps.title: Restore the specified fuses and battery
steps.body: For the fault-present branch, verify that the ignition is OFF. Install the RCM fuse(s), or the equipment-specific fuse(s) identified by the wiring information. Observe the conditional fuse note below, then connect the battery using [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356).

steps.title: Position yourself before switching on
steps.body: In the fault-present branch, sit upright in the driver seat with no objects between you and any pyrotechnic device. Move the seat fully rearward to maximize distance from the driver airbag, then turn the ignition from OFF to ON.

steps.title: Run the complete prove-out
steps.body: For either branch, verify that all airbags are installed and connected and the ignition is OFF. Wait 10 seconds, then turn the ignition ON. The airbag indicator should illuminate continuously for approximately 6 seconds and then turn off. Continue observing for approximately 30 seconds while the RCM completes testing.

steps.title: Resolve faults and finish the applicable branch
steps.body: If the indicator fails to illuminate, stays on or flashes, diagnose and repair the SRS faults before proceeding with other repairs. For the fault-present branch, after successful repair and prove-out, use the scan tool to clear all Continuous Memory Diagnostic Trouble Codes (CMDTCs) from all modules.

watchFor.title: A connector that appears attached
watchFor.body: An incompletely seated connector position assurance (CPA) tab can leave shorting bars engaged and cause a low-resistance fault. This is a diagnostic possibility, not proof of a failed airbag; corrective work requires the applicable safe SRS procedure.

watchFor.title: Stopping the test early
watchFor.body: Flashing may not begin until approximately 30 seconds after switching the ignition on.

notes: The shared procedure includes a conditional three-blade BECMB/GWM fuse arrangement. Where vehicle wiring confirms that arrangement, remove the two-blade 10A fuse at the GWM position before installing the RCM or applicable BECMB fuse(s). These wiring labels do not establish that this equipment is fitted to the Mustang.

diagnostics.finding: The indicator completes its initial illumination and remains off after 30 seconds, with no chime or SRS message.
diagnostics.meaning: The prove-out indicates no SRS fault is present.
diagnostics.next: Complete the applicable branch and record the result.

diagnostics.finding: The indicator fails to light, remains illuminated or flashes.
diagnostics.meaning: The prove-out has not passed.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose and repair the indicated SRS or warning-indicator fault before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: An inoperative indicator is accompanied by 5 sets of 5 beeps or a message-center warning.
