diagnostics.meaning: An SRS fault exists despite the absence of a working warning lamp.
diagnostics.next: Repair both the indicator concern and the SRS fault.

verification.title: Record the complete result
verification.body: Record initial indicator illumination, its subsequent state and any chime or message throughout the full observation period.

verification.title: Confirm readiness for release
verification.body: Confirm fault-free SRS operation and, for the fault-present branch, completion of the all-module CMDTC clearing step.

procedures.purpose: Execute the appropriate initial-fault branch and complete SRS repowering and prove-out.
Review general service safety and the required system-specific precautions.
Reconnect the battery during the fault-present repowering branch.
Understand RCM monitoring and the role of connector position assurance tabs in fault detection.

guides.title: Replace a B-pillar side impact sensor
guides.summary: Depower the restraint system, access and replace the side impact sensor with flush mounting surfaces, then restore and repower the system.
guides.introduction: The B-pillar side impact sensor contributes information used by the restraints control module to assess a side impact. The module considers sensor inputs before deciding whether restraint deployment is necessary. Replacing this sensor involves more than exchanging an electrical part: its mounting, connection and the prescribed supplemental restraint system (SRS) power procedures are essential parts of the repair.
guides.why: These are critical repair steps for correct restraint operation during a crash. The sensor must attach flush against smooth mating surfaces, and its mounting bolt must be tightened correctly. Depowering before disconnection and repowering after reassembly are separate required procedures; an improvised power-disconnection step is not a substitute for following them.

when.summary: When diagnosis or an applicable restraint repair calls for replacement of a B-pillar side impact sensor.
notes: An airbag warning indicator alone does not establish that this sensor is defective.

prepare.title: Provide restraint-system service capability
prepare.detail: Use a technician equipped to follow the complete SRS depowering and repowering procedures. Have both procedures available before disturbing the sensor connection.

prepare.title: Confirm the sensor and coupe access
prepare.detail: Identify the fitted second-row side impact sensor and use the coupe loadspace-trim access procedure. Body style and component identification must agree before restraint work begins.

prepare.title: Prepare for the mounting requirement
prepare.detail: Have suitable fastener tools and a torque wrench capable of 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm). Allow access to inspect both sensor mating surfaces before installation.

steps.title: Depower the SRS
steps.body: Complete the linked SRS Depowering procedure before working on the sensor. Follow its full sequence and prerequisites rather than treating ignition-off as the completed preparation.

steps.title: Remove the loadspace trim
steps.body: Use the coupe loadspace trim procedure to expose the identified sensor. Follow the specified trim-removal path to gain access without guessing at concealed attachments.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the sensor
steps.body: Use the illustration to identify the electrical connector, mounting bolt and sensor. Disconnect the connector, remove the bolt and then remove the side impact sensor, preserving that order.

steps.title: Establish a flush mounting
steps.body: Check that the impact sensor mating surfaces are smooth and allow flush attachment. Resolve anything preventing that contact before fitting the sensor, then install the mounting bolt and tighten it to 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm).

steps.title: Restore the connection and trim
steps.body: Complete the remaining installation by reversing removal. Reconnect the sensor electrical connector and restore the coupe loadspace trim.

steps.title: Repower the restraint system
steps.body: Carry out the linked SRS Repowering procedure after installation. Follow its complete sequence to finish restoring the system; sensor installation alone does not complete this job.

watchFor.title: A sensor that does not sit flush
watchFor.body: Do not use bolt tightening to compensate for mating surfaces that prevent flush attachment. Smooth, flush contact is an explicit installation requirement.

watchFor.title: Incomplete restraint-system procedures
watchFor.body: Skipping a prescribed step can affect restraint operation during a crash even when the sensor appears physically secure.

notes: The second-row side impact sensor application described here is for the coupe. A convertible trim-access reference does not establish that the convertible uses this sensor.

diagnostics.finding: An airbag warning indicator remains illuminated.
diagnostics.meaning: The restraint controller monitors multiple inputs and connections, so a warning does not identify this sensor as the cause.
diagnostics.next: Follow the applicable restraint-system diagnosis rather than assuming another sensor replacement is required.

verification.title: Confirm the installed condition
verification.body: Confirm flush sensor mounting, the specified bolt tightening, the restored electrical connection and completed trim installation.

verification.title: Record system restoration
verification.body: Record the side serviced and the outcome of the prescribed repowering procedure. Document any remaining restraint warning for diagnosis before considering the repair complete.

procedures.purpose: B-pillar side impact sensor removal and installation, mounting-surface requirement and bolt tightening.
Required SRS depowering before sensor disconnection.
Coupe loadspace trim removal and installation for sensor access.
Required SRS repowering after sensor installation and reassembly.

applicability.equipment: Coupe with the identified second-row side impact sensor

authoring.method: Codex source review against exact component application and completion procedures

guides.title: Replace the clockspring while preserving its centered position
guides.summary: Replace the steering-column clockspring using the required access procedures and retain a new unit’s anti-rotation key until the steering wheel is installed.
guides.introduction: The clockspring provides an electrical connection between the steering column and rotating steering-wheel equipment, including the restraint system. Its internal connection must accommodate steering movement without being driven beyond its intended travel. Replacement therefore includes both electrical reconnection and control of the unit’s rotational position. The retaining screws are only one part of a repair whose installation sequence matters to restraint-system operation.
guides.why: A new clockspring’s anti-rotation key preserves its installation position. Removing that key before the steering wheel is installed creates a mandatory centering requirement; ignoring it can cause component damage or system failure. Restraint connectors also need complete engagement: on deployable components, a partly seated assurance tab can leave internal shorting bars engaged even though the connector pins touch.
searchTerms: airbag warning after steering wheel work

when.summary: When clockspring replacement is required, or centering becomes necessary during its installation.
notes: An airbag warning alone does not establish that the clockspring needs replacement.
Adjustment is conditional, but it is required if a new unit’s key was removed before steering-wheel installation.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint-system repair capability
prepare.detail: Use a technician equipped for supplemental restraint system work. Follow all critical notes and the safety and access requirements of the linked steering-wheel procedure before disturbing the clockspring connections.

prepare.title: Prepare the access and adjustment procedures
prepare.detail: Have the steering-wheel, steering-column-shroud and clockspring-adjustment procedures available. Keep a new clockspring’s anti-rotation key installed while preparing the replacement.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and shrouds
steps.body: Begin the [clockspring procedure](#/document/G1696300) by completing [Steering Wheel removal](#/document/G1693262) and [Steering Column Shrouds removal](#/document/G1692617). Preserve the linked steering-wheel procedure’s unique installation requirements for reassembly.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the clockspring
steps.body: With the required access complete, disconnect the electrical connectors. Remove the retaining screws and the clockspring, as illustrated. Keep the replacement unit’s rotational restraint intact while handling it.

steps.title: Install the replacement with its key retained
steps.body: Reverse the clockspring removal actions to mount and reconnect the unit. If it is new, do not remove its anti-rotation key at this stage: the key must remain until the steering wheel has been installed.

steps.title: Complete adjustment when required
steps.body: If adjustment is needed, use [Clockspring Adjustment](#/document/G1696293). If the new unit’s key has already been removed before wheel installation, centering is mandatory. Use that exact procedure rather than estimating the center position.

steps.title: Restore the steering wheel and access parts
steps.body: Complete installation by reversing the relevant access procedures and following the steering-wheel installation instructions. Remove the anti-rotation key from a new clockspring only after the steering wheel is installed.

watchFor.title: Premature key removal
watchFor.body: Do not continue on the assumption that the clockspring remains centered. Carry out the required adjustment procedure.

watchFor.title: Incomplete restraint-connector engagement
watchFor.body: Where deployable-component connectors were disturbed during access, their connector position assurance tabs must be fully seated. Electrical pin contact alone does not establish correct engagement.

notes: The adjustment procedure is a separate linked operation; no rotation count or centering shortcut is supplied here.
The repair’s restraint-system notes are critical to correct operation during a crash.

diagnostics.finding: A new clockspring’s anti-rotation key was removed before the steering wheel was fitted.
diagnostics.meaning: The installation now requires clockspring centering.
diagnostics.next: Complete the linked adjustment procedure before accepting the assembly.

diagnostics.finding: An airbag warning occurs with an incompletely seated deployable-component assurance tab.
diagnostics.meaning: The restraint control module can detect low circuit resistance because the connector’s shorting bars remain engaged; this finding does not by itself prove clockspring failure.
diagnostics.next: Resolve connector engagement through the applicable restraint procedure and continue prescribed diagnosis if needed.

verification.title: Confirm installation order
verification.body: Confirm the steering wheel was installed before the new clockspring’s key was removed, and that the access parts and connections were restored.

verification.title: Record the centering decision
verification.body: Record whether adjustment was required and, if so, that the linked centering procedure was completed.

procedures.purpose: Clockspring removal and installation, including the new-unit anti-rotation-key requirements.
Required steering-wheel removal and installation, including its unique installation instructions.
Steering-column-shroud removal and refitting for clockspring access.
Conditional clockspring adjustment, mandatory if the new-unit key is removed before wheel installation.
Restraint-system connector assurance and shorting-bar behavior relevant to disturbed deployable-component connections.

guides.title: Remove and Install the Steering-Wheel Driver Airbag
guides.summary: Depower the restraint system, release the driver airbag’s spring retainers, restore its electrical connections and repower through the prescribed procedure.
guides.introduction: The driver airbag sits in the steering wheel and forms part of the Supplemental Restraint System (SRS). The restraints control module monitors sensor information and commands deployment when it determines that deployment is necessary. This job releases the airbag from its spring-clip mountings and disconnects its electrical connections for removal or replacement. Correct mechanical attachment and connector engagement are essential to restoring the assembly.
guides.why: Airbag work requires restraint-system service capability because incorrect actions can cause accidental deployment or compromise operation in a crash. Electrical connector security also affects self-diagnostics. Connector Position Assurance (CPA) tabs secure deployable-component connectors and disengage their protective shorting bars. A connector can appear attached while an incompletely seated tab leaves the shorting bars applied, producing a low-resistance fault.
searchTerms: airbag warning indicator after connector installation

when.summary: When authorized restraint-system repair or steering-wheel access requires driver airbag removal.
notes: An illuminated airbag warning indicator does not by itself prove that the driver airbag needs replacement.
The complete SRS depowering and repowering procedures are mandatory parts of this job.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint-system service capability
prepare.detail: Have the full driver airbag, SRS depowering and SRS repowering procedures available. Follow every required step before handling or reconnecting the component.

prepare.title: Prepare the specified release tool
prepare.detail: Use a 3 mm Allen key to operate the steering-wheel spring clips through the side access holes. Follow the illustrated tool orientation to contact the clips.

steps.title: Depower the restraint system
steps.body: Complete the linked SRS depowering procedure before beginning airbag removal. This prerequisite establishes the required condition for working on the deployable component; do not substitute a guessed isolation or waiting sequence.

steps.title: Release the spring-clip retainers
steps.body: Insert the Allen key into the side opening in the steering-wheel cover. Angle its inserted end upward and toward the front of the vehicle, then push the spring clip to release the airbag retainer. Repeat the specified side-access release operation for the remaining attachment.

steps.title: Separate and disconnect the airbag
steps.body: Pull the released driver airbag away from the steering wheel to access its connections. Disconnect the 3 driver airbag electrical connectors and remove the airbag.

steps.title: Reconnect under depowered conditions
steps.body: Before installation, make sure the SRS remains depowered in accordance with the required procedure. Connect all 3 electrical connectors and fully seat the applicable CPA tabs so the connections are secured and the shorting bars disengage.

steps.title: Engage the airbag mountings
steps.body: Align the driver airbag with the steering wheel and push it into position, engaging the airbag retainers with the spring clips. Correct engagement restores its mechanical attachment.

steps.title: Repower through the prescribed procedure
steps.body: Complete the linked SRS repowering procedure after the connectors and mountings are restored. Follow that procedure for returning the restraint system to service.

watchFor.title: Reconnection before depowering
watchFor.body: The installation warning specifically requires a depowered restraint system before reconnecting the component. Incorrect handling can cause accidental deployment and serious injury.

watchFor.title: A connector with an unseated assurance tab
watchFor.body: Electrical pins can make contact while the shorting bars remain applied. An apparently connected plug is therefore not sufficient evidence of correct installation.

notes: Some release illustrations omit the airbag to show the spring clip clearly; follow the stated tool direction with the assembly in place.

diagnostics.finding: An airbag warning indicator and circuit-resistance-below-threshold fault occur with a CPA tab incompletely seated.
diagnostics.meaning: The shorting bars may still be applied even though the connector pins are touching. This condition does not establish a failed airbag.
diagnostics.next: Have connector engagement checked using the required SRS depowering precautions, then complete the prescribed repowering procedure and reassess the fault.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical and electrical completion
verification.body: Confirm all 3 connectors and their applicable assurance tabs are seated, and the airbag retainers are engaged with the spring clips.

verification.title: Record the restraint-system result
verification.body: Record completion of the repowering procedure and the warning-indicator or self-diagnostic result. An illuminated airbag warning indicator requires further diagnosis.

procedures.purpose: Driver airbag spring-clip release, electrical disconnection, reconnection and installation in the steering wheel.
Mandatory SRS depowering before driver airbag removal and before reconnecting the component.
Mandatory SRS repowering after the driver airbag has been fully installed.

guides.title: Replace the driver knee airbag
guides.summary: Remove the lower instrument-panel trim and knee airbag, restore its attachments, and complete the prescribed SRS repowering procedure.
guides.introduction: The driver knee airbag occupies the lower instrument panel beneath the steering wheel and forms part of the supplemental restraint system (SRS). Its deployment is controlled by the restraints control module. Replacement requires several surrounding trim pieces to be removed before the airbag mounts and connector become accessible. Left-hand-drive and right-hand-drive vehicles share most of the work, with an additional harness retainer on the right-hand-drive branch.
guides.why: SRS depowering controls the risk of accidental deployment during service. Correct mounting and connector engagement are also essential for crash operation. A connector can appear attached while its assurance tab remains incompletely seated, leaving an electrical fault that must not be mistaken automatically for a defective replacement airbag.
searchTerms: airbag warning after knee airbag work

when.summary: When diagnosis or an established repair requires removal or replacement of the driver knee airbag.
notes: The warning indicator alone does not establish that this particular airbag needs replacement.

prepare.title: SRS service capability
prepare.detail: Arrange a technician competent in restraint-system service, with access to the complete depowering and repowering procedures.

prepare.title: Trim and fastener access
prepare.detail: Prepare appropriate trim and fastener tools and low-range torque equipment. Access is needed beside and beneath the instrument panel.

prepare.title: Identify the steering layout
prepare.detail: Use the correct left-hand-drive or right-hand-drive connector-removal branch. The illustration shows left-hand drive.

steps.title: Depower the restraint system
steps.body: Complete [SRS Depowering](#/document/G1696297) before beginning the airbag removal sequence. Use that procedure’s full instructions rather than assuming that an unplugged connector makes the system safe.

steps.title: Remove the side and lighting-switch trim
steps.body: Release the clips and remove the left-hand instrument-panel trim panel. Remove the lighting-switch trim screw, release its clips, detach the panel and disconnect its electrical connector.

steps.title: Clear the remaining trim
steps.body: Remove the next trim panel’s screws, detach it and disconnect its connector. Then detach the ambient-air-temperature grille panel, disconnect its connector and release its tether. Freeing the tether prevents it from remaining attached as the panel is removed.

steps.title: Separate the knee airbag from the panel
steps.body: From beneath the instrument panel, remove the airbag retaining nuts. Remove the screws, disengage the clips and separate the airbag from the panel, keeping it supported while its wiring remains connected.

steps.title: Disconnect the appropriate harness arrangement
steps.body: On left-hand-drive vehicles, detach and disconnect the electrical connector, then remove the airbag. On right-hand-drive vehicles, first detach the harness pin-type retainer, then detach and disconnect the connector and remove the airbag.

steps.title: Refit and repower
steps.body: Confirm that the SRS remains depowered before reconnection. Reverse [Driver Knee Airbag](#/document/G1696302), restoring connector retention, clips, trim wiring and the grille tether. Tighten the airbag nuts to 8 Nm; the airbag screws and lighting-switch trim screw use 2.5 Nm. Finish with [SRS Repowering](#/document/G1696298).

watchFor.title: A panel still held by wiring or its tether
watchFor.body: Release the specified connection before carrying the panel away; clips and screws are not its only attachments.

watchFor.title: Assuming connector contact means full engagement
watchFor.body: The connector assurance feature must be fully seated to secure the connection and disengage the airbag’s shorting bars.

notes: Apply the listed screw torques only to their identified locations; the intervening trim-panel screws do not have a torque stated in this procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The airbag warning remains illuminated after return to service.
diagnostics.meaning: An incompletely seated connector assurance tab can cause a below-threshold resistance fault, but the warning alone does not isolate the cause.
diagnostics.next: Continue SRS diagnosis. Any reconnection work must again follow the depowering requirement.

verification.title: Mechanical restoration
verification.body: Confirm the airbag mounts, trim clips, electrical connections and grille tether are restored, including the extra harness retainer on right-hand-drive vehicles.

verification.title: Record return-to-service results
verification.body: Complete the prescribed repowering procedure and record the resulting airbag-warning status and any unresolved restraint-system fault.

procedures.purpose: Driver knee airbag removal and installation, including both steering-layout branches.
Required SRS depowering before removal and airbag reconnection.
Required SRS repowering after installation.

guides.title: Replace the front door side impact sensor
guides.summary: Depower the restraint system, replace the door-mounted impact sensor with a flush mounting joint, and complete the prescribed repowering procedure.
guides.introduction: The front door side impact sensor supplies information to the supplemental restraint system (SRS). The restraints control module evaluates sensor inputs and determines whether appropriate restraint components need to deploy during a crash. Replacement requires door-trim access, an electrical disconnection and a precisely restored mounting joint. Although the sensor is small, its installation is part of the vehicle's crash-protection system.
guides.why: Correct restraint operation depends on following the repair sequence, including SRS depowering before access and repowering after assembly. The sensor mating surfaces must be smooth and permit flush attachment. Incorrect repair can compromise restraint operation and increase the risk of serious injury or death in a crash.
searchTerms: front door side impact sensor replacement

when.summary: When restraint-system diagnosis identifies a need to remove or replace the front door side impact sensor.
notes: An illuminated airbag warning indicator alone does not identify the door sensor as the failed component.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint-system service capability
prepare.detail: Have the complete SRS depowering and repowering procedures available and the capability to perform them. These are required stages of the repair.

prepare.title: Prepare trim and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Have the front door trim procedure, suitable fastener tools and a torque tool capable of accurately tightening the sensor's small mounting bolts.

steps.title: Depower the restraint system
steps.body: Complete [SRS Depowering](#/document/G1696297) before beginning door-trim and sensor removal. Follow the entire procedure rather than substituting an assumed power-disconnection shortcut.

steps.title: Expose the sensor
steps.body: Remove the front door trim panel using the [door trim procedure](#/document/G1692600). This provides access to the sensor and its connector.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the sensor
steps.body: Following the [side impact sensor procedure](#/document/G1696303), disconnect the electrical connector, remove the mounting bolts and remove the sensor. Preserve this order while the SRS remains depowered.

steps.title: Check the mounting interface
steps.body: Before installation, confirm that the sensor and door mating surfaces are smooth and allow flush attachment. If they cannot meet flush, resolve the mounting condition before fastening the sensor.

steps.title: Install and reconnect
steps.body: Reverse removal: position the sensor, install its bolts and tighten them to 17 lb.in (1.9 Nm). Reconnect the electrical connector and reinstall the front door trim panel.

steps.title: Repower the restraint system
steps.body: Complete [SRS Repowering](#/document/G1696298) after assembly. Repowering is a prescribed procedure, not simply an instruction to restore electrical power by any convenient method.

watchFor.title: A sensor that will not sit flush
watchFor.body: Do not treat tightening the bolts as a way to compensate for an unsuitable mating surface.

watchFor.title: An unresolved airbag warning
watchFor.body: An illuminated indicator after repowering requires further restraint-system diagnosis; physical replacement alone does not establish that the system is fault-free.

notes: Connector Position Assurance (CPA) details for deployable restraint components must not be assumed to describe the door sensor connector.

diagnostics.finding: An airbag warning is associated with below-threshold resistance at a deployable-component circuit.
diagnostics.meaning: A CPA tab that is not fully seated can leave that component's shorting bars engaged even though its connector pins make contact. This does not prove a failed door sensor.
diagnostics.next: Continue the applicable restraint-system diagnosis under its required safety procedures and address the identified connector condition.

verification.title: Confirm mounting and reassembly
verification.body: Confirm flush sensor attachment, correct bolt tightening, connector reconnection and door-trim installation.

verification.title: Record restraint-system completion
verification.body: Record completion of the prescribed repowering procedure and any remaining airbag warning indication. Keep an unresolved warning open for diagnosis.

procedures.purpose: Front door side impact sensor removal and installation, including mounting-surface and bolt-tightening requirements.
Required SRS depowering before sensor access and disconnection.
Front door trim removal and installation for sensor access.
Required SRS repowering after sensor and trim installation.

guides.title: Replace a front impact severity sensor
guides.summary: Replace the selected front impact severity sensor with the restraint system depowered, then restore its flush mounting and repower the system.
guides.introduction: The front impact severity sensor contributes to the vehicle's assessment of a collision. The restraints control module (RCM) monitors sensor inputs and, when deployment is necessary, activates the appropriate supplemental restraint system (SRS) components. This repair replaces the sensor and restores its electrical connection and attachment to the vehicle. The illustration identifies the sensor locations and shows the connector, retaining nut and sensor separately.
guides.why: Both the mounting and the electrical connection matter to correct restraint operation. The sensor's mating surfaces must allow it to sit flush. Depowering and repowering are also integral parts of this repair: follow their complete procedures because incorrect restraint-system work can affect protection during a crash.

when.summary: When restraint-system diagnosis has established that the selected front impact severity sensor requires replacement.
notes: An illuminated airbag warning indicator does not identify this sensor as the failed component.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Use a technician able to follow the complete SRS depowering and repowering procedures. Read both linked procedures before beginning.

prepare.title: Prepare access and tightening equipment
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the radiator upper air-deflector retainers and sensor nut, including a torque wrench capable of the specified sensor-nut setting.

steps.title: Depower the system and expose the sensor
steps.body: Complete the linked SRS depowering procedure first. Then remove the retainers and radiator upper air deflector to reach the sensor being serviced.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the sensor
steps.body: Disconnect its electrical connector, remove the retaining nut and remove the sensor. Follow the illustrated component identification so the connector and mounting attachment are handled as separate operations.

steps.title: Restore the mounting
steps.body: Make sure the mating surfaces are smooth and permit flush contact. Install the sensor by reversing removal, tighten its nut to 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm), and reconnect the electrical connector.

steps.title: Close the access area and repower
steps.body: Refit the radiator upper air deflector and its retainers. Complete the linked SRS repowering procedure, including its prescribed completion checks.

watchFor.title: Uneven mating surfaces
watchFor.body: A sensor that cannot sit flush does not meet the installation requirement. Resolve the mounting condition before completing the repair.

watchFor.title: Incomplete SRS preparation
watchFor.body: Do not substitute an assumed battery-disconnection routine for the specified SRS depowering procedure.

notes: Use the illustration to locate the selected sensor; it does not establish that both illustrated sensors require replacement.

diagnostics.finding: The airbag warning indicator is illuminated.
diagnostics.meaning: The restraint system has detected a fault; connector faults are among the possible causes described for the system.
diagnostics.next: Establish the fault through restraint-system diagnosis before selecting this sensor for replacement.

verification.title: Confirm the physical installation
verification.body: Verify flush attachment, the specified nut torque, a restored electrical connection and refitted air-deflector retainers.

verification.title: Record system restoration
verification.body: Record completion of the SRS repowering procedure and the results of its required checks.

procedures.purpose: Front impact severity sensor removal and installation, including access, mounting condition and nut torque.
Required SRS depowering before sensor removal.
Required SRS repowering after sensor installation.

guides.title: Service the passenger-seat OCS sensor assembly and reset the system
guides.summary: Replace the calibrated passenger-seat occupant-classification assembly as required, reset it under controlled conditions and prove out the restraint system.
guides.introduction: The Occupant Classification System (OCS) uses the passenger-seat cushion bladder and its sensing assembly to provide occupant information to the restraints control module (RCM). The cushion foam, bladder and occupant classification system module (OCSM) are calibrated together. Although access includes removing the sensor from its bracket, replacement must preserve the complete service-kit configuration.
guides.why: Foreign objects beneath the bladder, a kinked pressure hose or an incorrectly assembled cushion can affect classification. Resetting an unfinished seat establishes the wrong baseline. These are crash-restraint components, so successful mechanical assembly must be followed by the prescribed scan-tool reset and Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) prove-out.
searchTerms: airbag warning indicator after seat repair

when.summary: When OCS components or passenger cushion foam need replacement, or cushion work requires an OCS reset.
notes: Cushion disassembly, a new trim cover or installation of an OCS service kit requires a scan-tool reset.
The passenger cushion heater mat is not separately serviceable; use an OCS kit equipped with the heater mat when it needs replacement.

prepare.title: Restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Use a technician equipped for restraint-system work and a diagnostic scan tool capable of OCS reset and clearing module trouble codes. Follow the complete Front Seat procedure and its safety prerequisites.

prepare.title: Correct calibrated assembly
prepare.detail: Obtain the required complete OCS service kit. Do not mix individual foam, bladder or module components, or separate an assembly for replacement.

prepare.title: Reset conditions
prepare.detail: OCSM voltage must be greater than 8 volts and less than 18 volts. OCS temperature must be between 6° C and 36° C. After extreme temperatures, keep the vehicle within that range for at least 30 minutes. The passenger seat must be empty before and during reset.

steps.title: Remove the seat and side shield
steps.body: Remove the passenger seat through the Front Seat procedure. Remove the recline-handle clip and handle, then the cushion side-shield screws. Pull the shield's rear outward and lift it off the recliner bracket. On a manual track, release the underside retainers and slide the shield forward. Disconnect the seat-control-switch connector where fitted.

steps.title: Clear the backrest-cover access
steps.body: Release the electrical-connector retainers and move the harnesses aside. Detach the backrest-cover straps; where a blower snorkel is fitted, route the straps out through it before moving the cover aside.

steps.title: Release the sensor and cushion assembly
steps.body: Disconnect the OCS connector, carefully bend the bracket tab away and slide the sensor off. Excessive bending force can damage its housing. Release the cushion-cover J-clips. Follow the original-equipment branch for lifting the cushion foam and cover, remove the pin-type retainers, and note the hose route before withdrawing the hose and sensor through the cushion support wires.

steps.title: Separate the cover carefully
steps.body: Invert the cushion cover and release its hook-and-loop strips and hook-and-arrow attachments. Work carefully so the attachments are not torn from the foam. Install replacement OCS parts only in the complete configuration in which the service assembly is supplied.

steps.title: Reassemble the cushion and seat
steps.body: Inspect the bladder, cushion pan and support assembly and remove foreign objects. Reverse removal, routing the pressure hose in a natural bend without twisting it or trapping it over the springs. Secure the sensor and bend its bracket tab back. Finish all seat components, including the head restraint and side shield, and reinstall the seat. Do not prove out the SRS yet.

steps.title: Perform the OCS reset
steps.body: Confirm the voltage, temperature and empty-seat conditions. After switching the ignition on, allow at least 8 seconds before issuing the scan-tool OCS reset. Cycle the ignition after the reset. A successful first attempt leads to SRS prove-out; use the diagnostic branches below if it fails.

steps.title: Prove out the restraint system
steps.body: With all airbags installed and connected and the ignition off, wait 10 seconds. Switch the ignition on: the airbag indicator should illuminate continuously for approximately 6 seconds and then extinguish. Continue monitoring for approximately 30 seconds while the RCM completes its tests.

steps.title: Resolve faults and finish
steps.body: Diagnose and repair any abnormal warning indication before proceeding with other repairs. After successful completion, use the scan tool to clear all Continuous Memory Diagnostic Trouble Codes (CMDTCs) from all modules.

watchFor.title: Resetting before final assembly
watchFor.body: The complete seat and all attached parts must be correctly assembled and installed before rezeroing seat weight.

watchFor.title: Partially secured restraint connectors
watchFor.body: Deployable-component connector-position-assurance tabs must be fully seated. A connector can make electrical contact while its unseated tab still leaves the shorting bars engaged and causes an SRS fault.

notes: The left-hand-drive passenger seat is illustrated; the right-hand-drive passenger seat follows a similar procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The first OCS reset fails.
diagnostics.meaning: A wiring, connector or pressure-hose concern may be preventing completion; this alone does not prove the kit has failed.
diagnostics.next: Inspect the OCS connector and wiring, hose for kinks or damage, and seat and body harness terminals and connectors. Repair concerns, perform a second reset and cycle the ignition.

diagnostics.finding: The second reset is unsuccessful.
diagnostics.meaning: The procedure requires replacement of the calibrated service assembly.
diagnostics.next: Install a new OCS service kit and complete assembly, reset and prove-out requirements.

diagnostics.finding: The airbag indicator fails to illuminate, stays lit or flashes.
diagnostics.meaning: The SRS prove-out has not passed; flashing can be delayed until approximately 30 seconds after ignition-on.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose and repair the warning-indicator and SRS concerns before proceeding.

diagnostics.finding: An inoperative indicator is accompanied by five sets of five beeps or an SRS message.
diagnostics.meaning: An SRS fault is being reported through a backup warning.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose and repair both the indicator and any SRS faults.

verification.title: Confirm successful prove-out
verification.body: After the initial lamp check and 30-second monitoring period, confirm the indicator remains unlit with no chime or SRS message.

verification.title: Record reset and diagnostic results
verification.body: Record the reset outcome, any second attempt or kit replacement, the observed indicator sequence and completion of CMDTC clearing from all modules.

procedures.purpose: Passenger-seat OCS access, calibrated service-assembly installation, reset conditions, retry decisions and SRS prove-out.
Complete front-passenger-seat removal and installation prerequisites.

guides.title: Remove and install the passenger airbag
guides.summary: Remove the passenger airbag from its deployment chute, inspect the assembly and cavity, then reinstall it with the required restraint-system depowering and repowering.
guides.introduction: The passenger airbag forms part of the Supplemental Restraint System (SRS). When the restraint control module determines deployment is necessary, it supplies the electrical command to the appropriate restraint components. The passenger module sits in a deployment chute within the instrument panel assembly. This job requires upper-panel removal, careful release of the chute retainers and inspection before reassembly.
guides.why: The chute and its retainers are part of the airbag's installation, so damage, foreign material or incorrect engagement can affect deployment. Electrical precautions are equally important: the SRS must be depowered before work and remain depowered during reconnection. Incorrect repair techniques can cause accidental deployment or impair protection during a crash.

when.summary: When diagnosis, damage assessment or instrument-panel work requires passenger airbag removal or replacement.
notes: The procedure illustrates left-hand drive; right-hand drive is similar.
This work requires SRS service capability and access to the complete depowering and repowering procedures.

prepare.title: Establish the restraint-system procedure
prepare.detail: Have the linked SRS depowering and repowering instructions available. Follow their exact sequence; do not substitute an assumed electrical isolation method or waiting period.

prepare.title: Prepare for instrument-panel work
prepare.detail: Have the upper-panel removal procedure, suitable tools for ducts and brackets, and torque control suitable for the small bracket screws.

prepare.title: Plan the inspection
prepare.detail: Allow for inspection of both the airbag module and instrument panel/deployment chute cavity. Damaged parts must be replaced and foreign material removed before installation.

steps.title: Depower the SRS and remove the upper panel
steps.body: Complete [SRS Depowering](#/document/G1696297), then remove the [instrument panel upper section](#/document/G1693977). These prerequisites establish the required electrical condition and access to the module.

steps.title: Remove the ducts and retaining brackets
steps.body: Following the [passenger airbag procedure](#/document/G1696306), remove the demister duct screws and ducts on both sides. Remove the air conditioning duct and its screws, then the brackets and their screws.

steps.title: Rotate the module out of the chute
steps.body: Pull the deployment chute away from the airbag. Rotate the airbag out while disengaging the four retainers identified in the removal sequence. Continue rotating the module until it comes out of the chute.

steps.title: Inspect the module and deployment space
steps.body: Inspect the airbag and instrument panel/deployment chute cavity for damage and foreign material. Remove foreign material and install new parts wherever damage is found. Complete this inspection before positioning the module for installation.

steps.title: Engage the installation retainers in sequence
steps.body: Position the airbag at the chute and engage the five retainers specified at the beginning of installation. Pull the chute outward to provide clearance, rotate the airbag down into it, then engage the airbag retainers as directed.

steps.title: Restore brackets, ducts and the upper panel
steps.body: Install the brackets and tighten their screws to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm). Install the air conditioning duct and screws, then the demister ducts and screws on both sides. Reinstall the upper panel through its linked procedure. Keep the SRS depowered during component reconnection.

steps.title: Repower the restraint system
steps.body: Complete [SRS Repowering](#/document/G1696298) after reassembly. Follow that procedure through its required checks before considering the job complete.

watchFor.title: Incomplete connector locking
watchFor.body: Connector position assurance (CPA) tabs secure deployable-component connectors and release their shorting bars. A connector can make electrical contact while an incompletely seated tab still causes a fault.

watchFor.title: Damage or debris in the deployment path
watchFor.body: Do not complete installation with damaged parts or foreign material in the module or chute cavity.

notes: Removal releases four retainers at the specified rotation stage; installation begins by engaging five before the module rotates down. Follow each phase's illustrated sequence.

diagnostics.finding: An airbag warning remains after reassembly.
diagnostics.meaning: An incompletely seated CPA tab can leave shorting bars applied and produce a circuit-resistance-below-threshold fault. The warning alone does not establish that the airbag module has failed.
diagnostics.next: Follow the prescribed SRS checks and depower the system before correcting any component connection.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical installation
verification.body: Confirm the inspection found no remaining damage or foreign material, all specified retainers are engaged, and brackets, ducts and the upper panel are restored.

verification.title: Record the restraint-system result
verification.body: Record any damaged parts replaced and the outcome of repowering and system checks. Resolve a remaining airbag warning before closing the repair.

procedures.purpose: Passenger airbag removal, cavity inspection, staged retainer engagement and installation; left-hand drive shown, right-hand drive similar.
Required SRS depowering before removal and before reconnecting restraint components.
Instrument panel upper-section removal and installation for passenger airbag access.
Required SRS repowering after completed reassembly.

guides.title: Remove and refit the passenger knee airbag through the glove box assembly
guides.summary: Depower the restraint system, remove the passenger-side trim and glove box assembly, then refit and repower using the prescribed procedures.
guides.introduction: The passenger knee airbag is a deployable component of the Supplemental Restraint System (SRS). The restraints control module monitors crash-related inputs and supplies deployment current when appropriate. Access for this repair involves the instrument-panel trim, glove box damper and stops, electrical connections and complete glove box assembly. Correct electrical handling is as important as the physical removal.
guides.why: Incorrect restraint-system work can cause accidental deployment or prevent correct operation during a crash. Deployable-component connectors also use Connector Position Assurance (CPA) tabs. A connector can appear attached while its tab remains incompletely seated, leaving its internal shorting arrangement engaged and causing a restraint-system fault.

when.summary: When an established repair requires removal or refitting of the passenger knee airbag through the glove box assembly.
notes: The illustrated arrangement is left-hand drive; the right-hand-drive procedure is similar.
The center finish-panel illustration includes an optional configuration; follow the actual fitted panel.

prepare.title: Provide restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Be equipped to complete the linked SRS depowering and repowering procedures exactly. Read their prerequisites before beginning; the component-removal steps do not replace those electrical safety procedures.

prepare.title: Prepare trim and fastener tools
prepare.detail: Use an interior trim remover and suitable screw-removal and torque tools. Keep the upper and lower glove box screws identifiable because their tightening specifications differ.

steps.title: Depower the restraint system
steps.body: Complete [SRS depowering](#/document/G1696297) before working on the airbag connections. Maintain that depowered condition throughout removal and reconnection.

steps.title: Remove the surrounding trim
steps.body: Following the [passenger knee airbag procedure](#/document/G1696323), release the clips and remove the right-hand instrument-panel trim with the trim remover. Release the center finish-panel clips, remove the panel and disconnect its electrical connector.

steps.title: Open the glove box beyond its stops
steps.body: Open the glove box and detach the door damper. Push each side of the door to disengage its stops, then open it beyond them. This exposes the connections and fasteners needed for assembly removal.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the assembly
steps.body: Disconnect and detach the indicated electrical connector and wire harness. Remove the upper screws, then the lower screws. Separate the glove box assembly from the instrument panel, disconnect the remaining electrical connector and remove the assembly.

steps.title: Refit while the SRS remains depowered
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence, reconnecting and routing the wiring as prescribed. Fully seat applicable CPA tabs. Tighten the upper screws to 22 lb.in (2.5 Nm) and the lower screws to 42 lb.in (4.8 Nm). Restore the door stops, damper and trim.

steps.title: Repower through the prescribed sequence
steps.body: Complete [SRS repowering](#/document/G1696298) after assembly is complete. Follow that procedure's checks rather than treating reconnection alone as completion.

watchFor.title: Reconnecting a powered restraint component
watchFor.body: The SRS must be depowered before reconnection. Incorrect repair actions can cause accidental deployment and serious injury.

watchFor.title: A connector that looks seated
watchFor.body: Physical contact between connector pins does not establish that its CPA tab is fully engaged.

notes: Follow every restraint-system warning and procedural step; correct installation affects protection during a crash.

diagnostics.finding: A restraint-system fault appears after a deployable-component connector has been refitted.
diagnostics.meaning: An incompletely seated CPA tab can leave shorting bars applied and produce a circuit-resistance-below-threshold fault.
diagnostics.next: Use the prescribed SRS diagnostic and depowering approach before correcting connector engagement; the indication alone does not prove airbag failure.

verification.title: Confirm mechanical restoration
verification.body: Check that the wiring is attached, upper and lower screws received their respective tightening values, and the glove box stops, damper and trim are restored.

verification.title: Complete the restraint-system checks
verification.body: Complete the repowering procedure and resolve any reported restraint-system fault before considering the repair finished.

procedures.purpose: Passenger knee airbag removal and installation through instrument-panel trim and glove box assembly removal.
Depower the SRS before removal or reconnection of the restraint component.
Repower the SRS and perform the prescribed completion sequence.

guides.title: Remove and replace the restraints control module
guides.summary: Remove the restraints control module safely, configure a replacement when required and verify supplemental restraint system operation.
guides.introduction: The restraints control module (RCM) monitors occupant-related inputs, switches and crash sensors. When it determines that deployment is necessary, it supplies the electrical output to the appropriate supplemental restraint system (SRS) components. Replacing it therefore involves more than exchanging a box: a new module requires programmable module installation (PMI), followed by the specified system prove-out.
guides.why: Correct configuration, attachment and connector installation affect restraint operation during a crash. The programming process must start before the old module is removed, while electrical disconnection must wait until the SRS has been depowered. Incorrect repair can increase the risk of serious injury or death in a crash.

when.summary: When diagnosis requires RCM removal or replacement.
notes: An airbag warning indication identifies a system concern, not necessarily a failed RCM.

prepare.title: Restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Use a technician equipped for SRS service, with the complete depowering and repowering procedures available. This guide does not replace their electrical safety sequence.

prepare.title: Programming and access
prepare.detail: Have a diagnostic scan tool supporting RCM PMI, tools for floor-console removal and a torque tool suitable for the module mounting nuts.

steps.title: Begin PMI before removing a module that will be replaced
steps.body: With the current RCM still installed, begin PMI and follow the scan-tool instructions. If it does not communicate, the tool may request As-Built Data. This step applies only when installing a new component.

steps.title: Depower the restraint system
steps.body: Complete [SRS Depowering](#/document/G1696297) before disconnecting the module. Follow that procedure in full rather than substituting an assumed shutdown sequence.

steps.title: Expose the RCM
steps.body: Remove the floor console using its linked procedure, then detach the wire harness retainer. This provides access to the module and frees the harness attachment specified for removal.

steps.title: Remove the module
steps.body: Disconnect the RCM electrical connectors, remove the mounting nuts and remove the RCM. The illustration distinguishes the connectors, nuts and module.

steps.title: Restore the mechanical installation
steps.body: Reverse the removal procedure. Install the RCM and tighten its mounting nuts to 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm), reconnect the electrical connectors, restore the harness retainer and reinstall the floor console.

steps.title: Repower and finish replacement-module programming
steps.body: Follow [SRS Repowering](#/document/G1696298). For a new RCM, do not prove out the system yet: first complete PMI using the diagnostic scan tool. The additional PMI step does not apply when refitting the existing component.

steps.title: Prove out a new RCM installation
steps.body: After PMI, verify that all airbags are installed and connected, then perform the timed indicator check below. Diagnose and repair any indicated SRS faults before proceeding with other repairs.

watchFor.title: Partially seated deployable-component connector tabs
watchFor.body: Connector Position Assurance (CPA) tabs release internal shorting bars when fully seated. At deployable components, a connector can make pin contact while an unseated tab still causes a resistance-below-threshold fault.

watchFor.title: Proving out before replacement-module configuration
watchFor.body: A new RCM must complete PMI after repowering and before its prove-out.

notes: Keep the new-component-only PMI requirements distinct from removal and refitting of the existing RCM.

diagnostics.finding: The indicator fails to illuminate, stays illuminated or flashes during prove-out.
diagnostics.meaning: The required warning-indicator sequence has failed; flashing can be delayed until approximately 30 seconds after ignition ON.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose and repair the SRS faults before continuing other repairs.

diagnostics.finding: An inoperative indicator is accompanied by 5 sets of 5 beeps or a message-center warning.
diagnostics.meaning: An SRS fault exists and the warning indicator is inoperative.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose and repair both the warning indicator and the SRS faults.

verification.title: Perform the timed prove-out
verification.body: For a new RCM, verify all airbags are installed and connected. With ignition OFF, wait 10 seconds, then turn ignition ON. The indicator should illuminate continuously for approximately 6 seconds and turn off. Continue monitoring for approximately 30 seconds.

verification.title: Assess the complete result
verification.body: After 30 seconds with ignition ON, an indicator that remains off following its initial illumination, with no chime or SRS message, indicates no SRS fault is present.

verification.title: Record completion
verification.body: Record PMI completion where applicable and the full indicator, chime and message-center observations rather than recording only that the lamp eventually went out.

procedures.purpose: RCM removal, installation, new-component PMI sequence and SRS prove-out.
Required SRS depowering before module disconnection.
Floor-console removal and installation for RCM access.
SRS repowering, with the new-RCM prove-out deferred until PMI is complete.
RCM operating context and deployable-component connector assurance-tab fault behavior.

guides.title: Replace a confirmed faulty seat-track position sensor
guides.summary: Replace the diagnosed driver or passenger seat-track position sensor, then restore and verify the supplemental restraint system.
guides.introduction: The seat-track position sensor supplies seat-position information to the supplemental restraint system (SRS). The restraints control module (RCM) monitors its electrical circuit and requests the airbag warning indicator when it detects a fault. Replacement changes the small sensor attached to the seat track; diagnosis must first distinguish sensor failure from damaged wiring or connections.
guides.why: Most faults in these circuits involve wiring or connectors. Accurate diagnosis avoids replacing a sound sensor, while controlled SRS depowering protects against accidental deployment during service.
searchTerms: airbag warning light seat position sensor

when.summary: After the driver- or passenger-side pinpoint test confirms that the seat-track position sensor requires replacement.
notes: A stored code or illuminated airbag warning indicator alone is not a sensor replacement instruction.

prepare.title: Arrange SRS service capability
prepare.detail: Use a technician familiar with SRS precautions and a scan tool capable of network and Restraints self-tests. Review the health-and-safety precautions referenced by the linked depowering and repowering procedures.

prepare.title: Identify the correct part and mounting
prepare.detail: Confirm the affected seat and catalog part number. Have a suitable screw tool and low-range torque tool. Physically similar restraint components from other vehicles may be incompatible.

steps.title: Confirm the repair decision and depower
steps.body: Follow the appropriate driver or passenger pinpoint test before replacement. Then use the full [SRS depowering procedure](#/document/G1696297). With a fault present, remove the specified restraint-module fuse(s), verify module noncommunication by network test, turn ignition off, disconnect the battery and wait at least one minute. The no-fault branch requires ignition off and a one-minute wait, with ignition remaining off throughout repair.

steps.title: Remove the sensor in sequence
steps.body: Locate the sensor at the seat track using the [removal procedure](#/document/G1696308). Remove its screw first, disconnect the electrical connector, then remove the sensor. Inspect the connector and nearby harness for loose terminals, frayed connections or pinched wires that could explain the original fault.

steps.title: Install and reconnect
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence: position the replacement sensor, reconnect its electrical connector, then install the retaining screw. Tighten the screw to 8 lb.in (0.9 Nm). Complete the electrical reconnection before restoring SRS operation.

steps.title: Restore power through the prescribed route
steps.body: Follow [SRS repowering](#/document/G1696298), restoring the applicable fuse and battery connections. For the fault-present branch, sit upright, keep objects away from pyrotechnic devices and move the driver seat fully rearward before switching on. Where the pinpoint test directs repowering without prove-out, defer prove-out and perform the specified Restraints self-test first.

watchFor.title: Uncontrolled electrical testing
watchFor.body: Incorrect SRS work can cause accidental deployment. Disconnect, reconnect or electrically test restraint components only as directed by the applicable procedure; do not improvise jumper tests.

watchFor.title: A fault that disappears during diagnosis
watchFor.body: If the original code no longer returns on demand, follow the intermittent-fault inspection. Do not install new SRS components merely because a historical code remains.

notes: If U3003:16 or U3003:17 also returns on demand, the sensor tests direct diagnosis through Pinpoint Test AJ first.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B00B5:11, B00B5:12, B00B5:13 or B00B5:1D is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These identify a driver sensor circuit short to ground, short to voltage, open circuit or current out of range, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Use the driver-side pinpoint test to distinguish wiring, sensor and RCM concerns.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B00C5:11, B00C5:12, B00C5:13 or B00C5:1D is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: These identify the corresponding passenger sensor circuit short to ground, short to voltage, open circuit or current out of range.
diagnostics.next: Use the passenger-side pinpoint test; replace the sensor only when its confirmation step directs replacement.

verification.title: Check the complete restraint system
verification.body: Reconnect all required SRS components before the final Restraints self-test. Diagnose every on-demand fault; do not clear codes while faults remain unresolved.

verification.title: Complete warning-indicator prove-out
verification.body: At the prescribed prove-out stage, verify all airbags are connected. With ignition off, wait 10 seconds, then switch on. The indicator should illuminate for approximately 6 seconds and turn off. Continue monitoring for approximately 30 seconds; persistent illumination, flashing, failure to illuminate, a warning chime or SRS message requires diagnosis.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the repaired side, final Restraints self-test and indicator result. Clear continuous-memory codes as directed only after faults are resolved. Release the vehicle only with the SRS fully operational and fault-free.
