Driver seat-track sensor diagnosis, replacement confirmation and final Restraints self-test.
Passenger seat-track sensor diagnosis, replacement confirmation and final Restraints self-test.
SRS depowering using the applicable fault-present or no-fault branch.
SRS repowering, warning-indicator prove-out and prescribed code clearing.

guides.title: Replace a side airbag in a Recaro front seat
guides.summary: Remove the Recaro seat side airbag through the specified cover and deployment-chute sequence, then restore its mounting and electrical connection with the restraint system depowered.
guides.introduction: The seat side airbag is part of the Supplemental Restraint System (SRS). Its deployment chute provides a controlled path through the seat backrest when deployment is commanded. Replacing the airbag therefore involves its connector, mounting, foam opening, chute and cover attachments. Correctly restoring those surrounding parts matters as much as installing the airbag itself.
guides.why: An incorrect repair can affect crash protection or cause accidental deployment. The seat cover also uses several attachment types that can tear away from the foam if separated carelessly. Connector security has an electrical consequence: the SRS uses connector position assurance tabs, and an incompletely seated tab can leave internal shorting bars engaged and produce a resistance fault.

when.summary: When side-airbag replacement is required or authorized seat work requires its removal.
notes: A warning indicator alone does not establish that the airbag needs replacement.
This procedure applies to the Recaro seat construction.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: This work requires a technician competent in SRS handling and access to the SRS depowering General Procedure in section 501-20B. Follow the applicable prerequisites precisely; the system must be depowered before reconnecting the airbag.

prepare.title: Prepare for seat and trim work
prepare.detail: Use the front seat removal procedure, provide access around the removed backrest and have a torque tool suitable for the airbag mounting nuts.

steps.title: Remove the front seat
steps.body: Follow the [front seat procedure](#/document/G1695491), including its prerequisites. Removing the seat provides access to the backrest cover, deployment chute and airbag mounting.

steps.title: Release the initial cover and chute attachments
steps.body: Detach the backrest cover J-clips and move the cover upward. Detach the deployment chute J-clips from the backrest frame, then remove the airbag nuts.

steps.title: Open the cover without tearing the foam attachments
steps.body: Carefully separate the hook-and-loop strips and hook-and-arrow retainers, then raise the cover. Follow the [Recaro airbag sequence](#/document/G1709237): position the chute through the backrest foam and separate the airbag from the frame.

steps.title: Free the chute and remaining cover attachments
steps.body: Separate the deployment chute from the airbag studs, then position the airbag back into the foam pad. Detach the further hook-and-arrow attachments and raise the cover before detaching the airbag from the frame again. Preserve this sequence rather than pulling the assembly out prematurely.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the airbag
steps.body: Slide the connector locking wedge outward, disconnect the electrical connector and remove the airbag. The illustration shows the wedge release associated with this final removal stage.

steps.title: Inspect before reassembly
steps.body: Inspect the airbag, its cavity, mounting surface and deployment chute for damage and foreign material. Remove all foreign material. A damaged airbag requires a new airbag, and a damaged chute requires a new chute.

steps.title: Restore the assembly in reverse order
steps.body: Confirm SRS depowering before reconnecting the component. Reverse the removal sequence, restoring the chute over the studs and through the foam, all frame attachments and the cover retainers. Tighten the airbag nuts to 53 lb.in (6 Nm), then reinstall the seat using its procedure.

watchFor.title: Retainers tearing from the foam
watchFor.body: Separate hook-and-loop and hook-and-arrow attachments carefully; damage to their foam anchorage can occur during cover removal.

watchFor.title: Damage or debris in the deployment path
watchFor.body: Do not close the seat around a damaged chute or foreign material in the airbag cavity.

notes: The restraint control module monitors deployment circuits; a connector fault and a damaged airbag are different findings.

diagnostics.finding: A connector is attached but its assurance tab is not fully seated.
diagnostics.meaning: The terminals may contact while the shorting bars remain engaged, allowing a below-threshold resistance fault and warning indication.
diagnostics.next: Address connector seating through the proper depowered SRS procedure rather than treating the fault as proof of airbag failure.

verification.title: Check the restored deployment path
verification.body: Confirm the cavity is clean, the chute is undamaged and its stud and frame attachments have been restored.

verification.title: Record the installation checks
verification.body: Record the airbag and chute inspection outcome, any required replacements, mounting-nut torque and completion of connector locking and seat reinstallation.

procedures.purpose: Recaro seat side-airbag removal and installation, including cover sequence, deployment-chute inspection and depowered reconnection.
Front seat removal for airbag access and seat reinstallation afterward.
Explain SRS connector assurance tabs, shorting bars and the possible electrical result of an incompletely seated connector lock.

guides.title: Replace a front-seat side or upper side airbag
guides.summary: Replace the seat-mounted airbag while preserving its deployment chute, upholstery attachments and electrical connector locks.
guides.introduction: The seat side airbag is part of the supplemental restraint system (SRS). The restraints control module decides when deployment is necessary, while the seat’s deployment chute provides the intended path through the upholstery. This repair involves both the airbag assembly and careful backrest-trim work. The side-airbag and upper-side-airbag branches share initial access but use different attachments.
guides.why: The cover, foam and deployment chute influence how the airbag emerges during a crash. Damaged trim or an incorrectly restored chute can compromise that path. Electrical connector locks also matter: an incompletely seated connector assurance tab can leave the internal shorting bars engaged and produce a restraint-system fault.

when.summary: When the seat airbag requires replacement or removal, or damage requires renewal of its cover or deployment chute.
notes: An illuminated airbag warning indicator alone does not identify a failed airbag.

prepare.title: Restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: Use a technician competent in SRS and seat-trim work. Have the complete SRS depowering procedure in section 501-20B available; the system must be depowered before reconnecting the airbag.

prepare.title: Seat access and equipment
prepare.detail: Follow the front-seat removal procedure. Have hog ring pliers for the upper-airbag upholstery attachments and torque equipment suitable for the airbag fasteners.

prepare.title: Replacement trim and chute
prepare.detail: Plan to replace damaged components. A front-seat backrest trim cover used with a side airbag cannot be repaired, although cleaning is permitted.

steps.title: Remove the front seat
steps.body: Follow [Front Seat](#/document/G1695491) to remove the seat and establish access to the backrest. Continue with the appropriate branch of [Side Airbag](#/document/G1696309).

steps.title: Free the harness and lower cover
steps.body: Release the electrical connector retainers and move the harnesses aside. Position the backrest cover and detach its straps. Where a blower-motor snorkel is fitted, route the straps out through it before moving the cover aside.

steps.title: Open the backrest upholstery
steps.body: Remove the cover insert and its pin-type retainers, then move the cover upward. Move the snorkel aside if fitted. Release the J-clip and draw the cover out from between the seat cushion and backrest.

steps.title: Expose the deployment chute
steps.body: Partially invert the cover, separating hook-and-loop attachments carefully so they do not tear away from the foam. Detach the chute retainers, pull the chute through the foam, and release the four backrest-cover J-clip retainers.

steps.title: Remove the fitted airbag assembly
steps.body: For the side airbag, remove its nuts and detach it from the frame. For the upper side airbag, first release the frame J-clip, remove the hog rings and carefully detach the hook-and-loop strips, then remove the mounting bolt. In either branch, slide out the connector locking wedge, disconnect the connector and remove the airbag.

steps.title: Inspect the deployment path
steps.body: Inspect the airbag, cavity, mounting surface and deployment chute. Remove foreign material. Replace a damaged airbag or chute. If the airbag cover is damaged, separated from its mounting or exposes airbag material, replace the complete airbag assembly; do not repair it.

steps.title: Reconnect and rebuild the backrest
steps.body: Confirm SRS depowering before reconnection. Reverse removal, tightening the airbag nuts or upper-airbag bolt to 6 Nm. Restore the chute, upholstery attachments, straps and harness retainers; use hog ring pliers where required. Reinstall the seat through its linked procedure.

watchFor.title: Foam attachments pulling loose
watchFor.body: Stop pulling if the hook-and-loop strip starts lifting from the foam. Damage here changes how the upholstery is retained.

watchFor.title: Repairing a deployment component
watchFor.body: Neither a damaged airbag assembly nor an airbag-equipped backrest trim cover is a repairable upholstery item.

notes: The blower-motor snorkel instructions apply only where that equipment is fitted.

diagnostics.finding: A connector assurance tab is not fully seated.
diagnostics.meaning: The connector pins may contact the airbag while its shorting bars remain engaged, producing a below-threshold resistance fault.
diagnostics.next: Resolve connector engagement under the prescribed depowered conditions rather than assuming the airbag has failed.

verification.title: Deployment-path inspection
verification.body: Confirm that foreign material is removed, damaged components are renewed, and the chute and trim attachments are restored.

verification.title: Connector and inspection record
verification.body: Confirm the locking wedge is seated and record the condition of the airbag, mounting area and chute. A warning indicator remaining on when the vehicle is powered requires further diagnosis.

procedures.purpose: Side and upper side airbag removal, damage inspection and installation.
Front-seat removal and installation required for backrest access.

applicability.equipment: Front seats with seat side airbags

guides.title: Restore corrosion protection after body repairs
guides.summary: Protect repaired exterior metal and enclosed body cavities with the specified undercoating and rust inhibitor while keeping door drains clear.
guides.introduction: Body repairs can leave exposed edges, welded flanges and enclosed metal surfaces needing renewed corrosion protection. Undercoating protects exposed repaired surfaces, while rust inhibitor reaches internal rails, door shells and closed channels through an applicator wand. This finishing work follows the metal repair and refinishing stages.
guides.why: Oil, dirt and wax interfere with surface preparation, and neither coating can be welded through. Internal coverage also matters: horizontal surfaces are particularly susceptible to corrosion, while blocked door drains allow moisture to accumulate even inside a coated door.

when.summary: After body welding and refinishing, when exposed repair surfaces and enclosed cavities need corrosion protection.
notes: The illustrations are general references, not vehicle-specific repair maps.

prepare.title: Review body-repair safety
prepare.detail: Follow [Body Repair Health and Safety and General Precautions](#/document/G1693182). Consult each chemical’s material safety data sheet and use the specified protective equipment, including respiratory protection and chemically resistant gloves where directed.

prepare.title: Prepare the application equipment
prepare.detail: Have an undercoating gun, a rust-protection coating gun, a controllable air supply and suitable cavity wands. For best results, the vehicle should be at room temperature.

prepare.title: Use the specified materials
prepare.detail: Prepare the listed ValuGard Premium Undercoating or 3M undercoating, ValuGard Rust Inhibitor or 3M Cavity Wax Plus, and Motorcraft Metal Surface Prep Wipes. Use the product identifiers in the procedure to select the materials.

steps.title: Finish repair work and clean the metal
steps.body: Complete welding and refinishing before applying either coating. Wire-brush the area requiring undercoating, then thoroughly clean and degrease the metal with the specified surface-preparation wipes. Surfaces for rust inhibitor must also be free of oil, dirt, wax, grease and other foreign material.

steps.title: Undercoat the exposed repair surfaces
steps.body: Attach the undercoating canister to its gun and set the air pressure to 552–621 kPa. Apply light mist coats using the fogging pattern. Cover applicable exposed metal and exterior spot-weld flange edges, including repaired rail edges; the material displaces moisture.

steps.title: Set up the cavity-protection gun
steps.body: Attach the rust-inhibitor canister to its dispensing gun and set the air pressure to 448–517 kPa. Select a wand that reaches the enclosed area. The two coating processes use different pressure settings.

steps.title: Fog enclosed rails and channels
steps.body: Insert the wand as far as possible through the access hole. Pull the trigger, wait 2–3 seconds, then slowly withdraw the wand while applying light mist coats. Use this method to cover inner rail surfaces and the closed-channel portions of spot-weld flanges.

steps.title: Protect door and quarter-panel cavities
steps.body: Coat the interior metal surfaces of the door shell with the most suitable wand. Protect exposed repaired edges, quarter-panel flange channels and door-opening flange channels. Pay particular attention to horizontal surfaces, and keep every door drain hole clear.

steps.title: Clean up and check coverage
steps.body: Remove overspray with a mild solvent such as mineral spirits or bug and tar remover. Check accessible treated areas for missed exposed metal, incomplete edge coverage and material obstructing door drainage.

watchFor.title: Further welding after coating
watchFor.body: Neither product can be welded through. Coordinate coating with the completed welding and refinishing work.

watchFor.title: Poor cavity coverage
watchFor.body: A short wand or hurried withdrawal can leave enclosed surfaces untreated. Use suitable reach and the specified fogging sequence.

notes: The full-frame rail illustration is a general example, not a Mustang repair location.
If this follows collision repair, the structural and restraint requirements in the body-repair safety procedure remain part of that repair.

verification.title: Confirm protection of repair areas
verification.body: Check that exposed repaired edges have undercoating and that the applicable enclosed surfaces received rust inhibitor, with attention to horizontal areas.

verification.title: Confirm drainage and cleanup
verification.body: Verify that door drain holes remain open and overspray has been removed.

procedures.purpose: Prepare surfaces and apply exterior undercoating and internal rust inhibitor after body repairs.
Apply chemical-handling, protective-equipment and body-repair safety requirements.

guides.title: Weld-bond replacement body panels
guides.summary: Prepare and bond replacement panels using the specified resistance-spot-welding or MIG plug-welding method, then restore their protective finishes.
guides.introduction: Weld bonding combines metal-bonding adhesive along a panel flange with welded attachments. A successful repair depends on the vehicle's shape, the fit of the replacement panel and the quality of both the adhesive contact and the welds. Resistance spot welding and MIG plug welding share this purpose but require different surface preparation and adhesive placement.
guides.why: Adhesive cannot correct distorted body dimensions or poor panel fit. Welding settings and preparation determine whether the joint forms correctly, while excessive grinding weakens the flange and removes protective coatings. Finishing the visible seam is only part of the job: corrosion protection must also be restored.

when.summary: When a damaged body panel requires replacement using the specified weld-bonding method.
notes: Use the joining method required for the actual panel repair and new genuine Ford replacement components.

prepare.title: Provide body-repair capability
prepare.detail: Arrange frame-machine measurement, panel cutting and flange-repair equipment. Squeeze-type resistance spot welding (STRW) requires suitable welding equipment and destructive sample testing. The alternative method requires metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) equipment and an 8 mm drill bit for plug-weld holes.

prepare.title: Prepare materials and protection
prepare.detail: Use the specified adhesive, surface-preparation wipes, seam sealer and corrosion-protection materials. Follow product labels and Material Safety Data Sheets. Provide side-shield eye protection and a dust mask for grinding, chemical protection as directed, and appropriate welding eye and skin protection for workers in the weld area.

prepare.title: Address collision safety
prepare.detail: Follow [body-repair precautions](#/document/G1693182), including safety-belt inspection and examination of restraint-module and impact-sensor mounting areas and related components for damage, cracks or loose fasteners.

steps.title: Establish geometry and remove the damaged panel
steps.body: Measure the vehicle on a frame machine and straighten it if necessary. Cut away large damaged sections without entering adjacent parts or mating flanges. Drill out the remaining spot welds, remove panel remnants and repair damaged flanges with a hammer and dolly.

steps.title: Prepare the mating metal for the selected method
steps.body: For STRW, limit grinding of the original adhesive flange to 25 mm and remove galvanizing to expose bright metal. For MIG, remove paint, E-coat and galvanizing from the receiving and replacement mating surfaces. Preserve flange thickness and corners. Remove opposite-side E-coat only at the specified weld sites and clean the prepared surfaces.

steps.title: Prepare plug-weld holes and verify fit
steps.body: For MIG, make 8 mm holes matching the original spot-weld count, close to the original positions but not directly over them. Grind only the immediate hole perimeter. After drilling and grinding, clean all mating surfaces on both the vehicle and replacement panel with Motorcraft Metal Surface Prep Wipes ZC-31-B. For either method, complete the specified surface preparation before dry-fitting and clamping the replacement panel. Verify alignment, then remove the panel for adhesive preparation.

steps.title: Prepare adhesive and qualify STRW settings
steps.body: Dispense enough adhesive to confirm even flow from both cartridge components, attach the mixing tip and purge a tip-length. For STRW, prepare a representative sample with a 6–9 mm adhesive bead and weld it. Clamp the sample in a vice, peel it apart with locking pliers and measure the nugget against the [weld specifications](#/document/G1687502). Adjust settings and repeat until acceptable.

steps.title: Apply adhesive and clamp the panel
steps.body: For MIG, protect the vehicle's plug-weld locations with 25 mm tape before applying adhesive, then remove the tape so these areas remain adhesive-free. Apply a 6–9 mm bead to the prepared vehicle flange. Position the panel and slide it if adjustment is needed; do not pull it away. Clamp evenly and tightly, allowing the adhesive's glass beads to control spacing, and remove excess adhesive before it cures.

steps.title: Complete the correct welding process
steps.body: Follow the [joining procedure](#/document/G1687509) and weld specifications. STRW requires insulated clamp tips and settings appropriate to wet or fully cured adhesive; a shunt weld in an adhesive-free area is recommended, especially with cured adhesive. MIG requires plug welding at the prepared, adhesive-free sites. Either method permits welding during or after adhesive cure. Clamps may be removed after welding; follow product handling instructions.

steps.title: Finish cosmetic seams
steps.body: Apply fiber-filled filler to cosmetic section seams and rough-sand it. After adhesive cure, apply conventional filler and block-sand. Apply primer surfacer, required seam sealer and a Ford-approved paint system.

steps.title: Restore corrosion protection
steps.body: Complete the [corrosion-prevention procedure](#/document/G1687508), using the specified undercoating and rust-inhibiting or cavity-wax materials. Protect repaired areas beyond the visible painted surface.

watchFor.title: Adhesive at MIG weld sites
watchFor.body: Keep the plug-weld areas clear; the STRW permission to weld through adhesive does not apply to this branch.

watchFor.title: Restricted sectioning locations
watchFor.body: Do not section body sides at door-hinge or striker anchorages. Welding within 50 mm of these locations can compromise collision protection.

notes: If a Restraints Control Module (RCM) or impact-sensor mounting area is damaged, restore its original production configuration and replace the component mounted there, regardless of airbag deployment.
Adhesive cure times and handling requirements come from the selected product label.

diagnostics.finding: The vehicle is dimensionally incorrect.
diagnostics.meaning: Panel fit cannot yet establish a correct repair.
diagnostics.next: Straighten the vehicle before fitting and joining the replacement panel.

diagnostics.finding: The STRW sample nugget fails the specified size requirement.
diagnostics.meaning: The current welding setup has not demonstrated an acceptable weld.
diagnostics.next: Adjust the welder and repeat destructive sample testing.

verification.title: Record geometry and weld qualification
verification.body: Record dimensional and dry-fit results. For STRW, record the sample nugget measurement and acceptance against the specified requirement.

verification.title: Check completion beyond appearance
verification.body: Confirm the required weld pattern, adhesive handling, seam finishing and corrosion protection are complete.

procedures.purpose: Complete STRW and MIG weld-bonding branches, including preparation, joining and finishing.
Body-repair safety, collision-restraint precautions and restrictions on repair methods and components.
Weld requirements, including the nugget acceptance criteria used for STRW sample testing.
Restore corrosion protection after panel joining and refinishing.

guides.title: Repair plastic panels, cracks and mounting tabs
guides.summary: Identify the plastic, choose the appropriate reinforced or cosmetic repair, and prepare the surface for a compatible refinishing system.
guides.introduction: Plastic body and trim parts differ in how they respond to sanding, cleaners, adhesives and heat. A repair that works on one material may bond poorly or distort another. This job covers identification, the repair-or-replace decision, sheet-molded composite (SMC) panel repairs, thermoplastic repairs, broken tabs and refinishing. The aim is to restore strength, shape and appearance together.
guides.why: Cleaner absorbed into plastic or reinforcing fibers can cause swelling and later failure. Bare polyolefin needs adhesion promoter so repair materials and paint can bond. Alignment also matters: repairing a part on the vehicle, where practical, helps preserve its fitted shape. Adhesive thickness, compatibility and cure must follow the particular product's directions.

when.summary: When a damaged plastic part can economically regain acceptable strength, appearance, fit and durability.
notes: Compare replacement availability and cost with repair time, quality and materials.
Reinforcing cloth may be unnecessary for purely cosmetic damage.

prepare.title: Arrange body-repair tools and materials
prepare.detail: Have ALCV-200, the specified grinding and sanding equipment, vacuum and tack cloth, compressed air, plastic film, suitable reinforcement, plastic-specific cleaners, adhesion promoter and a listed plastic-bonding adhesive. Select compatible filler and a Ford-approved paint system.

prepare.title: Control exposure and heat
prepare.detail: Follow the health and safety precautions, including eye and ear protection, appropriate gloves and chemical safety information. Keep solvents away from ignition sources and disable remote start before working around the vehicle when fitted.

prepare.title: Start with a dry, correctly supported part
prepare.detail: Clean both sides before abrasion and work with the panel dry at 18 C (64.4 F) to 24 C (75.2 F). Keep the part installed where practical to preserve alignment.

steps.title: Identify the material and choose the repair
steps.body: Look for a molded or stamped material designation and use the identification checks in [Plastic Repairs](#/document/G1687510). Select the dedicated SMC, thermoplastic or tab route. Judge whether the finished repair can restore the required strength and appearance at a sensible cost.

steps.title: Clean without soaking the substrate
steps.body: Use cleaners formulated for plastics and remove cleaner or water promptly, using air and suitable heat to assist drying. Never use lacquer thinner or reducer. On SMC, tape the break on both faces while cleaning the surrounding areas to prevent cleaner wicking into exposed fibers.

steps.title: Build the SMC backing repair
steps.body: Expose and sand the rear repair area with 80-grit abrasive, then vacuum and tack away dust. Use a conforming scrap SMC patch or construct a fiberglass-cloth patch on plastic film with adhesive beneath and over the cloth. Compress it against the panel, allow the specified cure, remove the film and smooth roughness.

steps.title: Rebuild the SMC front surface
steps.body: Remove the front masking and grind to the backing patch with a 30 to 40-grit wheel, making a gradual taper to reduce a visible repair outline. Sand with 80-grit abrasive, apply the adhesive-and-cloth pyramid patch, then rough-finish slightly below the original surface. Add plastic repair filler before final sanding, priming and painting.

steps.title: Repair thermoplastic damage
steps.body: Determine whether a backer made from the same plastic is needed. Clean, hand-sand with 80-grit abrasive, clear debris with compressed air and apply adhesion promoter. Build small repairs with adhesive filler above the surrounding surface for sanding. For large holes or cracks, use cloth or equivalent reinforcement 25.4 mm (1 in) larger than the damage, embed it immediately in adhesive and add adhesive for strength and shape. Contour without sanding through.

steps.title: Reconstruct a broken tab
steps.body: Clean and sand the tab area, clear debris and apply promoter. Cut reinforcement to form the tab front and extend backward in a wedge approximately 51 mm (2 in) from the original tab. Prepare and apply the adhesive patch, immediately form its shape, then allow the required cure before shaping with a small angle sander.

steps.title: Prepare the surface for refinishing
steps.body: Match the cleaner to the paint system. Wash with warm water and mild detergent, use plastic cleaner and dry promptly; water beading indicates further cleaning is needed. New parts may need controlled heating to release trapped solvents or mold-release agents. Lightly sand smooth surfaces with 600-grit or finer abrasive; use only a gray scuff pad on grained surfaces.

steps.title: Apply the compatible finish
steps.body: Remove sanding residue and wipe dry. Apply promoter wherever bare plastic is exposed, repeating it after any breakthrough. Use sealer if required against wrinkling or lifting. Refinish flexible and rigid parts separately because flexible parts may require an additive. Follow the Ford-approved paint system; exterior refinishing on the vehicle after cut-in helps color matching. Interior trim may use Motorcraft Interior Spray Paint or another Ford-approved system.

watchFor.title: Heat distortion
watchFor.body: Thermoplastics soften with heat and can lose their shape during drying or refinishing.

watchFor.title: Loss of surface detail
watchFor.body: Aggressive sanding can flatten grain or break through the exterior face while shaping a repaired tab.

notes: The tab illustration is generic and does not establish a Mustang-specific bumper layout.
Use each adhesive, filler and coating manufacturer's directions for material-specific preparation, thickness and cure.

diagnostics.finding: An inconspicuous ground area melts and smears, leaves a ragged edge, or a small sliver floats in water.
diagnostics.meaning: These are the stated polyolefin identification indicators; a waxy or oily appearance is another clue.
diagnostics.next: Use the appropriate plastic repair system and adhesion promoter.

diagnostics.finding: Grinding produces a smooth area and powdery dust, or the sample sinks.
diagnostics.meaning: These are the stated non-polyolefin indicators.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the material designation and select its compatible repair route.

diagnostics.finding: Material crystallizes and hardens during the identification burn test.
diagnostics.meaning: This is the stated indication of a thermosetting plastic.
diagnostics.next: Leave this optional open-flame test to trained personnel exercising the required extreme care and fire precautions.

verification.title: Assess the cured repair
verification.body: Check restored shape, fitted alignment, tab form and acceptable appearance and durability. Confirm the repair has cured according to the material instructions before finishing.

verification.title: Record material and finish decisions
verification.body: Record the identified plastic, repair system and cure completion. Check that exposed plastic received promoter and that the final finish preserves grain and blends with adjacent panels where applicable.

procedures.purpose: Plastic identification, repair-versus-replacement assessment, SMC and thermoplastic repairs, tab reconstruction and refinishing.
Required general service precautions for tools, chemicals, ignition sources and work around the vehicle.

guides.title: Prepare a body repair for welding
guides.summary: Establish the permitted repair method, protect vehicle electronics and prepare the work area before welding body steel.
guides.introduction: A body weld joins metal at a repair location, but its heat, electrical current and radiation also affect the surrounding vehicle and work area. This job establishes the precautions needed before welding begins: deciding whether the component can be repaired, protecting nearby systems and selecting a replacement weld pattern that preserves the original attachment.
guides.why: A sound-looking weld does not by itself establish a suitable repair. Heating certain structural steels to straighten them is prohibited, and some components must be replaced rather than welded. Electronics can be damaged by heat or welding current, while exposed wiring and nearby components need protection from spatter. These decisions belong before the first test weld.

when.summary: Before any body welding, after identifying the material and the permitted repair method.
notes: Vehicle subframes, steering components and suspension components are replacement-only items; do not weld them.

prepare.title: Provide welding and grinding protection
prepare.detail: Use protective clothing and a welding helmet with suitable dark filter lenses. For electric welding, use the deepest shade that still provides adequate visibility. People in the weld area should wear flash safety goggles. Sanding and grinding require eye protection with side shields and a dust mask.

prepare.title: Prepare the equipment and workspace
prepare.detail: Provide ventilation against noxious and oxygen-displacing gases, protective covers, a test sample, and grinding discs and wire brushes dedicated to the material being welded. Follow the welding equipment manufacturer's procedures and settings.

steps.title: Confirm that welding is an appropriate repair
steps.body: Identify the component and steel type using the complete welding precautions. Do not heat boron, martensitic, high-strength steel (HSS) or ultra-high-strength steel (UHSS) components to straighten or repair them. Replace severely bent or kinked components.

steps.title: Depower and protect electrical systems
steps.body: Depower and disconnect supplemental restraint system (SRS) components before welding. Disconnect and isolate the battery ground cable. Disconnect on-vehicle electronic modules and remove or reposition modules and related wiring away from heat-affected areas, protecting them from welding heat and current.

steps.title: Protect the surrounding area
steps.body: Place covers around nearby components and wiring harnesses to intercept spatter. Establish ventilation and protective equipment before welding or surface preparation starts; welding radiation can injure unprotected eyes and skin even though ultraviolet and infrared rays are invisible.

steps.title: Plan the replacement weld pattern
steps.body: Factory welds may be replaced with squeeze-type resistance welding (STRW) spot welds or metal active gas (MAG) plug welds. MAG plug welds must match the original locations and quantity, using 8 mm (0.31 in) holes. Resistance spot welds must match the original quantity and sit adjacent to the original weld locations.

steps.title: Prepare and prove the welding setup
steps.body: Use material-dedicated abrasives and brushes, and weld-through primer where applicable. Set the equipment for the selected weld type and make a test weld on a test sample. ER70S-3 or ER70S-6 wire is typically used for MAG welding on steel.

steps.title: Position the welding ground connection
steps.body: Place the welder ground clamp as close as possible to the weld area. Never attach it to the vehicle subframe. Confirm the component protections and planned weld locations before proceeding with the body repair.

watchFor.title: Heat-straightening a restricted steel
watchFor.body: Heating a damaged structural component is not an acceptable substitute for replacement when the material or damage falls under the stated restrictions.

watchFor.title: An exposed module or harness
watchFor.body: A nearby electronic component needs protection from both heat and current; spatter covers alone do not satisfy those precautions.

diagnostics.finding: The proposed repair involves a vehicle subframe, steering component or suspension component.
diagnostics.meaning: Welding is prohibited for that component.
diagnostics.next: Use replacement service.

verification.title: Confirm readiness before welding
verification.body: Verify electrical isolation, SRS depowering and disconnection, component protection, ventilation, personal protection and completion of the test weld.

verification.title: Check the planned attachment
verification.body: Confirm that weld quantity and placement match the selected replacement method, and that the ground clamp is near the work rather than on the subframe.

procedures.purpose: Complete body-welding precautions, material restrictions, electrical protection and replacement weld requirements.

guides.title: Section and refinish a damaged outer body-side panel
guides.summary: Plan a permitted localized body-side repair, join the replacement section and restore the joint finish, sealing and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: Body-side sectioning replaces a damaged portion of the outer panel while retaining suitable surrounding material. The repair involves more than cutting and welding: the replacement panel determines what can be fitted, the joint construction supports the repair, and sealing and refinishing protect it from moisture. This is specialist collision-repair work with strict limits around structural anchoring areas.
guides.why: Choosing the smallest permitted repair area limits unnecessary removal, but attachment points take priority over convenience. Sectioning near door, belt or striker anchors can affect structural integrity. Horizontal joints also need deliberate sealing because water migrates toward them, making them particularly vulnerable to corrosion.

when.summary: When localized outer body-side damage can be repaired within the permitted sectioning areas.
notes: The left side is illustrated; the right side is similar.
Body-side replacement panels are supplied as two-part panels.

prepare.title: Have the replacement panel first
prepare.detail: Do not begin removing the vehicle body side until the replacement panel is available for reference. Use it when planning the smallest practical repair area.

prepare.title: Establish the prohibited areas
prepare.detail: Do not section at door-hinge, safety-belt or striker anchoring points. Welding within 50 mm (1.96 in) of door-hinge or striker locations may compromise collision integrity. Sectioning in the A-pillar door-hinge portion, B-pillar or quarter-panel dog leg is not approved.

prepare.title: Provide body-repair equipment and materials
prepare.detail: The procedure lists an air body saw, plasma cutter, spherical cutter and spot-weld drill bit, plus resistance spotwelding and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment. Have high-quality weld-through primer, fibre-based and conventional fillers, a specified seam sealer and a Ford-approved paint system.

steps.title: Plan the section against the replacement
steps.body: Use the [sectioning procedure](#/document/G1687519) to choose cut points that minimize the repair area while respecting every anchoring and sectioning exclusion. Remove only as much outer body-side material as necessary.

steps.title: Expose and release the damaged area
steps.body: Remove trim as necessary and drill out the spot welds in the damaged area. Use the appropriate listed cutting equipment to remove the planned section, keeping the actual replacement panel available as the reference.

steps.title: Prepare the joint
steps.body: Where possible, form a lap-joint backer plate from a portion of the old panel to strengthen the joint. Before welding overlapping surfaces or substrates, apply high-quality weld-through primer between them.

steps.title: Weld the replacement section
steps.body: Use resistance spotwelding wherever possible; the procedure identifies it as producing a higher-quality repair. Use the listed MIG/MAG equipment as required for the repair, maintaining the planned joint arrangement and prohibited-area boundaries.

steps.title: Finish and seal the joints
steps.body: Rough-finish sectioning joints with fibre-based body filler. Final-finish the sectioning joints and plug welds with conventional body filler. Properly seal every horizontal joint using a seam sealer listed in the procedure to prevent moisture intrusion.

steps.title: Refinish and restore the trim
steps.body: Refinish with a Ford-approved paint system following its manufacturer’s recommendations. Complete the applicable [corrosion-prevention work](#/document/G1687508), then reinstall the removed vehicle trim.

watchFor.title: A convenient cut through a prohibited area
watchFor.body: The aim of a small repair does not authorize sectioning through an anchoring point or an excluded pillar or dog-leg area. Revise the repair approach before cutting.

watchFor.title: Unsealed horizontal joints
watchFor.body: A finished-looking surface can still admit moisture if the underlying horizontal joint has not been properly sealed.

notes: Select the seam sealer from the products specified in the linked sectioning procedure.
Apply weld-through primer before joining overlapping surfaces, while those surfaces remain accessible.

verification.title: Joint finishing complete
verification.body: Confirm sectioning joints received the specified rough and final finishing, plug welds were final-finished and horizontal joints were properly sealed.

verification.title: Protection and interior restored
verification.body: Confirm refinishing and corrosion prevention are complete and all trim removed for access has been reinstalled.

procedures.purpose: Outer body-side sectioning limits, equipment, joint preparation, welding, filling, sealing and refinishing sequence.
Corrosion-prevention treatment associated with the completed body-panel repair.

guides.title: Replace the fender apron panel reinforcement
guides.summary: Restore body alignment, replace the welded upper and lower apron reinforcements and brackets, then restore sealing, paint and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: The fender apron reinforcement is part of the welded front body structure beneath the removable exterior panels. Its upper and lower sections and associated brackets must be positioned and joined correctly before the hood, fender and headlamp return. This is a structural body repair involving weld removal, replacement-panel fitting, welding and protective finishing.
guides.why: Welding a replacement into a distorted body can preserve the damage in the new assembly. Weld placement also depends on the joining method: replacement resistance spot welds go beside the original positions and match their quantity, while metal active gas (MAG) plug welds must match both factory location and quantity. Sealing and corrosion protection complete the repair after the metalwork.

when.summary: When front-body damage requires replacement of the apron reinforcement assembly.
notes: The left-hand side is illustrated; the right-hand side follows a similar sequence.
Right-hand-side access additionally requires battery removal and reinstallation.

prepare.title: Use a suitably equipped body-repair facility
prepare.detail: Required equipment includes resistance spot welding, metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding, a grinder, spot-weld drill bit, locking pliers and an 8 mm drill bit for the specified replacement fender-bracket holes.

prepare.title: Prepare measurement and joining capability
prepare.detail: Arrange body measurement and dimensional restoration where needed. Follow the joining techniques procedure and protect all adjacent areas against cutting, grinding and welding.

prepare.title: Plan the protective finish
prepare.detail: Have a listed seam sealer, a Ford-approved paint system and the materials and access needed to restore corrosion protection.

steps.title: Remove the access components
steps.body: Remove the hood, fender and headlamp using their respective procedures. For right-hand-side work, also remove the battery. These operations expose the reinforcement and its welded joints.

steps.title: Restore the body dimensions if required
steps.body: Use [Body and Frame](#/document/G1687516) to assess the body and restore it to its pre-damage dimensions when necessary. Complete this correction before removing the reinforcement welds and establishing the replacement position.

steps.title: Remove the upper reinforcement and bracket
steps.body: Follow the weld locations in the [reinforcement procedure](#/document/G1687525). Drill the upper reinforcement spot welds, grind the welds at its rear flange and remove the reinforcement. Then drill out the upper reinforcement bracket welds and remove the bracket.

steps.title: Remove the lower reinforcement
steps.body: Drill the indicated lower reinforcement welds, remove the welds at its rear inner flange and drill those at the reinforcement bracket. Remove the lower reinforcement after these attachments have been released.

steps.title: Fit and weld the lower assembly
steps.body: Clamp the apron panel reinforcement to the lower apron panel reinforcement and resistance spot weld it. Drill the replacement-panel plug-weld holes, install the lower reinforcement and plug weld it. Resistance spot weld the bracket reinforcement to the apron panel, then plug weld the lower panel's rear inner flange.

steps.title: Install the upper assembly and fender bracket
steps.body: Install and weld the upper reinforcement and bracket using the specified MAG and resistance-welding operations. Drill the replacement fender-bracket plug-weld holes with the specified 8 mm bit, then position, clamp and weld the bracket.

steps.title: Finish and protect the repair
steps.body: Complete the metal finishing and seal every repaired area to production level with a listed seam sealer. Refinish with a Ford-approved paint system, then restore corrosion protection using the [corrosion prevention procedure](#/document/G1687508).

steps.title: Reinstall the exterior components
steps.body: Reinstall the hood, fender and headlamp through their individual procedures, plus the battery after right-hand-side work. Use the applicable body margin and flushness specifications when assessing the restored panel relationships.

watchFor.title: Incorrect replacement weld pattern
watchFor.body: Do not put resistance spot welds directly over the original weld locations. MAG plug welds, by contrast, must reproduce the factory locations and quantity.

watchFor.title: Unprotected surrounding areas
watchFor.body: Maintain protection throughout drilling, grinding and welding, including areas beyond the immediately visible joint.

notes: The general body description lists several metal grades; it does not identify the exact grade of this reinforcement. Use the specified joining procedure for the repair.
Panel appearance alone does not establish that underlying body dimensions have been restored.

diagnostics.finding: Body dimensions require correction.
diagnostics.meaning: The replacement reinforcement does not yet have the required body geometry for installation.
diagnostics.next: Restore the vehicle dimensionally before proceeding with reinforcement removal and replacement.

verification.title: Record structural completion
verification.body: Record the dimensional checks and confirm weld quantity and placement against the joining method and reinforcement procedure.

verification.title: Check finish and panel fit
verification.body: Confirm production-level sealing, completed refinishing and restored corrosion protection. Check the reinstalled front-panel relationships against the applicable body specifications.

guides.title: Replace a damaged front side member section
guides.summary: Replace the damaged inner and outer front frame-rail sections, restore their welded joints and corrosion protection, then reinstall the engine and surrounding assemblies.
guides.introduction: The front side member is part of the Mustang’s load-carrying body structure. This repair removes a damaged portion of its inner and outer rail and fits sections cut from a service replacement assembly. Access requires substantial dismantling, including the engine, radiator and front subframe, so this is specialist collision-repair work rather than a straightforward panel replacement.
guides.why: Correct body dimensions establish where the replacement belongs; welding fixes that position permanently. The rail backer strengthens the joint, while seam sealing, paint and restored corrosion protection protect the metal exposed during cutting and welding.
searchTerms: inner and outer frame rail repair

when.summary: When collision repair calls for replacement of the front side member at the specified sectioning locations.
notes: Restore the vehicle to its pre-accident dimensions first if required.
The left-hand repair is illustrated; the right-hand procedure is similar.

prepare.title: Structural repair capability
prepare.detail: Provide body measuring and dimensional restoration capability, an air body saw, locking pliers and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment. Use the Joining Techniques procedure for the joint preparation and welding requirements.

prepare.title: Powertrain access and support
prepare.detail: Arrange vehicle lifting, the engine-specific lifting brackets and supports, a floor crane and the prescribed transmission support. The 5.0L installation requires an assistant. On 5.0L and 5.2L procedures, place support-bar legs on body structure, not fenders; the 5.2L transmission must be supported at its bellhousing, never its fluid pan.

prepare.title: Parts and finishing materials
prepare.detail: Obtain the service rail assembly, prescribed seam sealer, a Ford-approved paint system and corrosion-protection materials. Have the applicable engine procedure’s replacement fasteners, gaskets and oil filter ready, together with a diagnostic scan tool for the finishing routine.

steps.title: Remove the assemblies that obstruct the rail
steps.body: Follow the fender, front bumper, headlamp, engine-specific radiator and engine removal procedures, plus the correct front-subframe procedure. Complete their isolation and support prerequisites before disconnecting assemblies. The 5.2L engine procedure specifically requires fuel-pressure release, battery disconnection, cooling-system draining and later oil draining.

steps.title: Handle the 5.2L radiator access correctly
steps.body: For the 5.2L, drain the cooling system, disconnect the prescribed hoses and remove the fan/shroud and upper support bracket. Move the radiator toward the engine, release the condenser’s upper tabs and position the condenser aside. Remove the transmission-cooler tube bracket bolt if fitted, then remove the radiator.

steps.title: Restore geometry and remove the damaged section
steps.body: Use Body and Frame information to restore pre-accident dimensions where necessary. Mark and saw the inner rail, then the outer rail, at the locations indicated in the Front Side Member Section procedure. Remove the sectioned portion; the cut positions must come from that procedure, not an estimate based on visible damage.

steps.title: Prepare the replacement rail portions
steps.body: Follow Joining Techniques, then mark and cut the replacement inner and outer rail portions from the service assembly. Their separate illustrations clarify each portion; they do not establish an alternative repair location.

steps.title: Check alignment and weld the joint
steps.body: Check dimensional accuracy before welding. Make a backer from a piece of frame rail to strengthen the joint. Fit and clamp the replacement section, seam weld the outer rail, then seam weld the inner-rail joint using the specified welding method.

steps.title: Finish and protect the repaired structure
steps.body: Metal-finish the repair area, seal every affected area to production level with the specified seam sealer, and refinish with a Ford-approved paint system. Restore corrosion protection using the dedicated procedure before completing reassembly.

steps.title: Install the engine using its installation counterpart
steps.body: Use the separate installation document for the fitted engine. The 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L procedures distinguish the 6R80 automatic from the MT82 manual transmission: pilot-hub lubrication and converter alignment belong to the automatic branch; input-shaft lubrication belongs to the manual branch. The 5.0L also specifies clutch/flywheel indexing when those parts are installed. Follow the 5.2L installation independently.

steps.title: Restore the steering connection and surrounding assemblies
steps.body: Where the 5.0L or 5.2L procedure disconnects the steering shaft, keep the dash seal loosened during shaft work, never hammer or force the shaft, install a new shaft bolt and perform the Steering Column Collapsed Check. Complete the applicable subframe, radiator, fender, bumper and headlamp installations, restoring all prescribed grounds, wiring retainers, hoses and brackets.

steps.title: Restore fluids and complete engine commissioning
steps.body: Install the specified new oil filter, refill engine oil and complete the cooling-system filling and bleeding procedure for the fitted engine. Perform its specified misfire-monitor profile correction with the diagnostic scan tool, then complete the road test. Do not transfer fluid specifications or fastening instructions between engines.

watchFor.title: 2.3L and 3.7L replacement parts differ
watchFor.body: Both automatic branches require new torque-converter nuts and clockwise crankshaft rotation. The 2.3L requires a new catalytic-converter gasket and nuts; the 3.7L requires new exhaust attachment nuts. Lubricate the 2.3L oil-filter seal with clean oil, but do not lubricate the 3.7L filter gasket.

watchFor.title: 5.0L and 5.2L one-time parts
watchFor.body: The 5.0L calls for new pressure-plate bolts when installing that assembly, new automatic torque-converter nuts, specified new left catalytic-converter studs, gasket and nuts, and a new steering-shaft bolt. Its new oil-filter O-ring must remain unlubricated. The 5.2L removal discards the cross-brace nuts, steering-shaft bolt and oil filter; provide replacements.

watchFor.title: Damaged steering dash seal
watchFor.body: The 5.2L procedure cautions against damaging the seal foam or pulling its brackets from the retainer pins. Damage can admit noise, fumes, air or water into the passenger compartment.

notes: Use the engine installation documents listed below; an engine removal procedure does not supply the installation sequence.
On the 3.7L, the cowl-extension and associated positive-battery-cable steps apply to the convertible branch.

diagnostics.finding: Body measurements do not match the required dimensions before welding.
diagnostics.meaning: The replacement section is not ready to be permanently joined.
diagnostics.next: Restore and recheck dimensional accuracy using Body and Frame information before welding.

verification.title: Record structural fit
verification.body: Record the dimensional check made before welding and confirm completion of the outer and inner seams, production-level sealing, refinishing and corrosion protection.

verification.title: Complete the variant-specific checks
verification.body: For 2.3L and 3.7L installations, start the engine and check the exhaust for leaks. Confirm the required steering-shaft inspection where applicable, successful completion of the engine-specific misfire-monitor correction and the road-test result.

guides.title: Repair the left front side member and fender apron
guides.summary: Replace damaged left front structural panels or rail sections, restoring their dimensions, welded joints and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: The front side member and fender apron form part of the body structure around the engine compartment. Their shape and joined panels matter to the position of surrounding components. This repair can involve individual apron panels or sectioned inner and outer frame members, depending on the damage. It requires structural measuring, substantial mechanical removal and controlled welding.
guides.why: Welding replacement panels onto a distorted structure preserves the distortion. Dimensions therefore need checking before permanent joining. Weld placement, joint finishing and sealing also matter: the replacement must reproduce the prescribed connections and restore protection wherever cutting and welding expose metal.

when.summary: When damage assessment calls for replacement of the left front apron panels or permitted frame-member sections.
notes: Individual apron panels may be serviced as required; rail sectioning depends on the extent of damage.
For 5.2L vehicles, confirm the correct engine and radiator access procedures before dismantling; the listed references cover those operations only for 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L.

prepare.title: Arrange structural and mechanical capability
prepare.detail: Provide body measuring and dimensional-restoration capability, plus the lifting and support equipment required by the applicable engine and subframe procedures.

prepare.title: Prepare joining equipment and protection
prepare.detail: Have resistance spotwelding equipment, metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment, an air body saw, spot-weld drill, 8 mm drill bit and locking pliers. Protect adjacent areas against cutting, grinding and welding.

prepare.title: Plan the finished repair
prepare.detail: Have replacement panels, the specified seam sealer, corrosion-protection materials and a Ford-approved paint system. Follow Joining Techniques for the prescribed joints.

steps.title: Restore dimensions and create access
steps.body: Restore the vehicle to its pre-damage dimensions if required. Remove the fender apron panel reinforcement, then the bumper and applicable subframe, radiator and engine using their separate procedures. Follow the engine-specific removal and installation references below.

steps.title: Separate the brackets and apron panels
steps.body: Following the illustrated [removal sequence](#/document/G1687526), remove the bracket and fasteners, drill the fender apron bracket welds and remove that bracket. Drill the remaining indicated spot welds and remove the panels in sequence.

steps.title: Make only the required rail cuts
steps.body: Where sectioning is needed, select the illustrated cutline option appropriate to the damage. Mark and cut the inner frame rail, then the outer rail, using the specified drilling and sawing operations. Do not infer cut positions from the bracket illustration.

steps.title: Prepare the replacement sections
steps.body: Use the installation illustrations to mark and cut the outer frame member from the service assembly, followed by the inner member. These preparations establish the replacement sections for the selected repair.

steps.title: Check alignment and join the frame members
steps.body: Check dimensional accuracy before welding. Clamp and weld the outer member, then the inner member, with MIG/MAG equipment as directed. Complete the specified resistance spot welds in the frame-member assembly.

steps.title: Install the apron panels
steps.body: Drill the specified plug-weld holes in the replacement panel with the 8 mm bit. Follow each illustrated apron reinforcement installation and welding stage, using the specified clamps and welding method. The battery-tray reinforcement operation belongs only to the right-hand side.

steps.title: Finish and protect the welded structure
steps.body: Install and resistance-spot-weld the fender apron bracket. Metal-finish the sectioning seams, seal all repaired areas to production level, restore corrosion protection and refinish with the approved paint system.

steps.title: Reassemble the vehicle
steps.body: Install the bracket and tighten its fasteners to 14 Nm. Refit the fender apron panel reinforcement and the removed mechanical components, following the applicable installation procedures rather than treating engine variants as interchangeable.

watchFor.title: Replacement weld locations
watchFor.body: Replacement resistance welds must sit adjacent to the original locations and match their quantity. MAG plug welds must match both the original locations and quantity.

watchFor.title: Misalignment before welding
watchFor.body: Resolve dimensional errors before permanent joining; panel fit alone does not replace the specified body measurements.

notes: The left-hand side is illustrated. Right-hand similarities do not make the right-hand-only battery-tray operation part of this repair.

verification.title: Record dimensional results
verification.body: Record the relevant body measurements and their comparison with Body and Frame specifications before welding.

verification.title: Confirm joint and finish completion
verification.body: Check weld quantity and placement, completed sectioning seams, production-level sealing, restored corrosion protection and completion of the referenced reassembly procedures.

guides.title: Replace the coupe roof panel
guides.summary: Replace the roof panel using the specified bonded and spot-welded joints, reinforcement foam, sealing and refinishing sequence.
guides.introduction: The coupe roof panel joins the roof structure through bonded areas and welded flanges. A stiffener and foam contact points support the panel, while sealed joints protect the finished body. Replacement involves controlled separation of the old skin, preparation of the retained flanges and reconstruction of those connections.
guides.why: A replacement panel needs a correctly shaped body beneath it. Adhesive contact and reinforcement foam must also be checked while accessible: gaps left underneath cannot be corrected by exterior finishing. Preserving these relationships is as important as making the painted roof look smooth.

when.summary: When assessed roof damage requires replacement of the coupe roof panel.
notes: Restore the vehicle to its pre-accident dimensions first if required.

prepare.title: Body-repair equipment and capability
prepare.detail: Provide resistance spotwelding equipment, a spherical cutter or equivalent, grinder, knife, spot-weld drill bit and locking pliers. Arrange a helper for panel removal as illustrated.

prepare.title: Bonding and finishing materials
prepare.detail: Select the specified metal bonding adhesive, flexible foam repair material, seam sealer and roof ditch sealer from the roof-panel procedure. Provide a Ford-approved paint system.

prepare.title: Access and protection
prepare.detail: Protect glass, exterior finishes and interior trim throughout the repair. Complete the linked fixed-glass and side-curtain-airbag procedures and their prerequisites; both are separate operations requiring the appropriate capability.

steps.title: Clear the roof and establish body shape
steps.body: Remove the fixed glass, coupe high-mounted stoplamp, headliner, audio antenna and side curtain airbag using their linked procedures. If needed, restore body dimensions using [Body and Frame](#/document/G1687516) before attaching a replacement roof.

steps.title: Separate the old roof panel
steps.body: Follow the [roof-panel removal procedure](#/document/G1687535). Drill the spot welds at the front and rear flanges. Cut the noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) foam between the panel and the front and rear reinforcements, leaving as much foam on the reinforcements as possible. Cut along the panel edge near the roof ditch flange with the spherical cutter and remove the panel with assistance.

steps.title: Prepare the retained and replacement flanges
steps.body: Remove remaining roof flange material and level the weld nuggets with the grinder. Clean away residue. Abrade the replacement panel's flange area and clean it. Locate the replacement panel, make reference marks and remove it again so its final position is established before adhesive application.

steps.title: Rebuild the bonded support areas
steps.body: Apply the specified bonding adhesive to the roof-panel stiffener and install it. Apply an adhesive bead to the roof rail flange. Apply the specified flexible NVH foam to the front and rear roof reinforcements.

steps.title: Locate, inspect and weld the panel
steps.body: Install the panel to the reference marks. If adjustment is needed, slide it into position; do not lift it away from the body. Check every bonded location for full adhesive contact and add adhesive where needed. Check panel-to-reinforcement contact and fill foam voids. Use locking pliers and resistance spotwelding equipment as directed, including the rear roof-panel flange welds.

steps.title: Finish and seal the repair
steps.body: Metal-finish the repaired area, then seal all required areas to production level with the specified seam sealer. Sand and prime the repair with a Ford-approved paint system. Apply roof ditch sealer, then complete refinishing with the approved paint system.

steps.title: Restore the removed equipment
steps.body: Reinstall the fixed glass, high-mounted stoplamp, headliner, antenna and side curtain airbag through their respective procedures. Preserve the completed sealing and finish during reassembly.

watchFor.title: Incomplete contact beneath the skin
watchFor.body: Adhesive gaps and unsupported reinforcement contact points require correction during installation, before the area becomes inaccessible.

watchFor.title: Lifting a placed panel
watchFor.body: The installation instruction requires sliding for alignment corrections once the panel has been placed.

notes: Bonding adhesive, flexible foam, seam sealer and roof ditch sealer have separate specified roles; keep their application locations distinct.
The convertible dimensional branches do not describe this coupe roof-panel repair.

verification.title: Contact and alignment
verification.body: Confirm the panel follows the reference marks, all required adhesive locations have full contact and reinforcement foam has no remaining contact voids.

verification.title: Finished repair
verification.body: Confirm the required welds, production-level sealing, roof ditch treatment and refinishing are complete. Where dimensional restoration was necessary, record the resulting body measurements against the applicable specifications.

guides.title: Replace the A-pillar outer section and reinforcements
guides.summary: Restore a damaged A-pillar using the permitted outer-panel section, complete inner reinforcements and the specified welded, bonded and sealed joints.
guides.introduction: The A-pillar forms the forward edge of the door opening and carries the door hinges. Its outer panel covers separate structural reinforcements. This repair involves cutting the outer skin, replacing the inner reinforcements at their factory seams and rebuilding the surrounding joints. Coupe and convertible service panels differ, so identify the body style before planning the work.
guides.why: The outer panel and inner reinforcements have different replacement rules. Cutting through an inner reinforcement would depart from the required structural repair. Body dimensions, weld locations, adhesive, noise-control foam and corrosion protection all contribute to the finished result; a tidy painted surface alone does not establish that the structure is correctly restored.

when.summary: When assessed A-pillar damage requires replacement of the outer section and inner reinforcements.
notes: Restore the vehicle to its pre-damage dimensions first where necessary.
Inner A-pillar reinforcements must be replaced at factory seams; sectioning them is prohibited.

prepare.title: Structural repair capability
prepare.detail: Use a body repair facility capable of dimensional restoration, resistance spot welding and MIG/MAG welding, with the correct coupe or convertible service parts.

prepare.title: Cutting and fitting equipment
prepare.detail: Prepare an air body saw, spot-weld drill, grinder, hot-air gun, knife, locking pliers and the specified 8 mm drill for plug-weld preparation.

prepare.title: Bonding and protection materials
prepare.detail: Obtain the specified metal-bonding adhesive, flexible repair foam and seam sealer, together with Ford-approved primer and paint materials.

steps.title: Open access and establish body shape
steps.body: Remove the fixed glass, fender, hood, front door, rocker moulding and body-style-specific A-pillar trim using their individual procedures. Remove the fender bracket and restore body dimensions where required before cutting.

steps.title: Clear the repair area
steps.body: Follow the convertible branch for removal of the vibration damper and reinforcement. Move the carpet and wiring harness away from the repair area, then remove the door hinges from the A-pillar.

steps.title: Remove the outer section
steps.body: Follow the cut locations in the A-pillar procedure and cut only the outer body panel. Drill its spot welds, then soften the noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) foam with the hot-air gun to release the panel. Do not heat the area above 170° C.

steps.title: Release the inner reinforcements
steps.body: Remove the upper reinforcement first by drilling the spot welds, grinding the specified seam welds and softening the foam. Then drill and release the lower reinforcement, using the knife where directed. Maintain the same heat limit throughout.

steps.title: Install the lower reinforcement
steps.body: Prepare its plug-weld holes and apply adhesive and expanding foam at the indicated locations. Clamp the replacement into position, resistance spot weld it and complete the specified plug welds.

steps.title: Install the upper reinforcement
steps.body: Prepare the replacement's plug-weld holes and apply adhesive to the upper flange of the lower reinforcement. Position the upper reinforcement and complete the specified resistance and MIG/MAG welds.

steps.title: Fit the outer replacement section
steps.body: Cut the service panel to the prescribed section and prepare its plug-weld holes. Clamp it accurately, then complete the welding, spot welding and MIG plug welding at the locations shown in the procedure.

steps.title: Finish and protect the joints
steps.body: Metal-finish the repair, apply approved primer and restore sealing to production level. Position, clamp and weld the lower fender bracket; install the upper bracket and reinforcement with their specified fastener torques. Refit the convertible vibration damper where applicable, then refinish and restore corrosion protection.

steps.title: Reassemble and align
steps.body: Install the door hinges, restore carpet and harness routing, and refit the removed glass, panels and trim through their procedures. Adjust the hood and front door as necessary using the alignment procedures.

watchFor.title: Cutting beyond the outer skin
watchFor.body: The permission to section the outer panel does not extend to either inner reinforcement.

watchFor.title: Foam resisting removal
watchFor.body: Use controlled heat within the stated limit; resistance is not a reason to overheat the joint.

notes: The coupe illustrations also guide the similar convertible operations, but convertible hardware and service parts still require their own branch.

verification.title: Check closure fit and protection
verification.body: Confirm hood and door alignment against the applicable body dimensions, and confirm sealing and corrosion protection have been restored.

verification.title: Record the completed structural work
verification.body: Record the dimensional checks, factory-seam reinforcement replacement, completed welds and final alignment results.

guides.title: Replace the A-pillar outer panel on a coupe or convertible
guides.summary: Replace the damaged outer panel through controlled cutting and welding, then restore sealing, finish, corrosion protection and body alignment.
guides.introduction: The A-pillar outer panel forms part of the body side around the front of the door opening. The body-side outer panels are mild steel, while the underlying structure contains other steel types. This repair replaces the outer panel and restores its welded joints, internal foam and protective finishes. Coupe and convertible service panels differ, and coupe access also requires roof-panel removal.
guides.why: An outer panel cannot correct underlying collision distortion by itself. Required dimensional restoration comes first, and cutting must affect only the outer skin. The installation sequence also matters: different joints use different welding methods, seam sealer follows primer, and paint does not eliminate the separate corrosion-protection requirement.

when.summary: When collision damage requires replacement of the A-pillar outer panel.
notes: Use the service panel and dimensional information for the actual body style.
This work requires collision-repair, body-measurement and welding capability.

prepare.title: Provide cutting and welding equipment
prepare.detail: Prepare an air body saw, spot-weld drill bit, 8 mm drill bit, hot-air gun, locking pliers, resistance spot-welding equipment and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment.

prepare.title: Provide restoration materials
prepare.detail: Have the specified flexible foam repair material and seam sealer, plus a Ford-approved primer and paint system. Plan the corrosion-protection work before closing the repair.

prepare.title: Use the complete joint layout
prepare.detail: Follow the full A-pillar procedure for cutting positions, plug-weld holes, foam placement and weld locations. The overview illustration does not replace those individual operations.

steps.title: Establish the correct body shape
steps.body: Identify the coupe or convertible replacement panel. If required, restore the vehicle dimensionally to its pre-accident condition before panel removal, using the Body and Frame procedure.

steps.title: Clear the repair area
steps.body: Remove the correct A-pillar trim, fender, hood, front door and rocker moulding. Remove the roof panel on a coupe only. Position the carpet and wiring harness away from the repair, then remove the front-door hinges from the A-pillar.

steps.title: Cut the outer skin
steps.body: Use the air body saw at the prescribed locations, carefully cutting only the outer body panel. Protecting the inner structure preserves the intended scope of the replacement.

steps.title: Release welds and foam
steps.body: Drill out the spot welds. Use the hot-air gun to soften the noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) foam without heating the area above 170° C. Remove the released A-pillar panel.

steps.title: Prepare the replacement
steps.body: Drill the specified plug-weld holes in the replacement panel with the 8 mm bit. Apply the specified expanding repair foam to the indicated area of the inner reinforcement before fitting the outer panel.

steps.title: Install and weld in sequence
steps.body: Position and clamp the replacement panel, then make the prescribed seam welds using MIG/MAG equipment. Resistance spot-weld the flange areas, then MIG-weld the remaining portion. Follow the full procedure for each joint's location and method.

steps.title: Restore the surface and protection
steps.body: Metal-finish the repair and apply Ford-approved primer. Apply seam sealer after priming, sealing all areas to production level. Refinish with a Ford-approved paint system, then complete the linked corrosion-prevention procedure.

steps.title: Reassemble and align
steps.body: Install the door hinges and reposition the carpet and wiring. Reinstall the appropriate trim, fender, door and rocker moulding, plus the roof panel on a coupe. Reinstall the hood and align it as necessary using Body and Frame information.

watchFor.title: Cutting into underlying structure
watchFor.body: The removal instruction permits cutting the outer panel only. Do not treat the inner reinforcement as part of the same cut.

watchFor.title: Excess heat or incomplete sealing
watchFor.body: Respect the foam-softening temperature limit. After welding, retain the primer-before-sealer order and restore corrosion protection.

notes: The coupe is illustrated; the convertible repair is similar, with body-style-specific parts and access requirements.

verification.title: Confirm repair completion
verification.body: Check that every prescribed weld phase, foam application, sealing operation and corrosion-protection step is complete before considering the panel repair finished.

verification.title: Record dimensional and fit results
verification.body: Compare and record the relevant dimensions, margins and flushness against Body and Frame information. Use the correct coupe or convertible door-opening data and verify the final hood alignment.
