guides.title: Replace the Coupe B-Pillar and Reinforcements
guides.summary: Replace the coupe’s welded B-pillar structure at its factory joints, then restore its foam, sealing and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: The B-pillar forms the rear boundary of the front-door opening and connects with the roof and lower body structure. Its reinforcements are part of that structural connection. Replacement requires access through the roof and quarter-panel areas, removal of several layers of welded parts, and reconstruction in the specified order. This is specialist collision-repair work.
guides.why: The B-pillar reinforcement components are boron steel and must not be sectioned: replacement must take place at factory joints. If the body has moved in the damage, restoring its dimensions first establishes the correct position for the replacement structure. The welding, foam, sealing and corrosion-protection stages each restore a different part of the original assembly.

when.summary: When structural damage requires replacement of the coupe B-pillar or its reinforcements.
notes: The left side is illustrated; the right side is similar.
This procedure requires removal and installation work at the rear roof reinforcement on both sides.

prepare.title: Structural measuring and welding capability
prepare.detail: Arrange body-dimension checking and restoration capability, resistance spot-welding equipment, and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment.

prepare.title: Removal and fitting equipment
prepare.detail: Have a spot-weld drill bit, an 8 mm drill bit for the specified plug-weld holes, and locking pliers. Use the illustrated weld locations and specified joining methods throughout.

prepare.title: Finishing materials and access
prepare.detail: Prepare the specified flexible foam repair material, seam sealer and corrosion-protection process. Plan for roof panel, coupe quarter panel and rear seat cushion removal.

steps.title: Restore the body dimensions if required
steps.body: Before removing the structure, dimensionally restore the vehicle to its pre-damage condition where required. Use [Body and Frame](#/document/G1687516) for the applicable coupe measurements.

steps.title: Expose and clear the repair area
steps.body: Remove the [Roof Panel](#/document/G1687535), [Coupe Quarter Panel](#/document/G1687585) and [Rear Seat Cushion](#/document/G1692168). Position the carpet and wiring harness aside, then remove the rear floor crossmember-to-B-pillar bolts and the noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) foam at the pillar base.

steps.title: Release the rear roof reinforcement
steps.body: Following [B-Pillar and Reinforcement—Coupe](#/document/G1687541), drill out the specified B-pillar-panel spot welds. Drill out the rear roof reinforcement spot welds on both sides and remove that reinforcement assembly.

steps.title: Remove the pillar and inner reinforcements
steps.body: Drill the B-pillar welds exposed at the rear roof reinforcement flange and remove the B-pillar assembly. Continue through the illustrated weld-removal stages to release the inner reinforcements. Keep the factory-joint separation sequence; do not substitute a sectioning cut.

steps.title: Rebuild the inner reinforcement layers
steps.body: Position and clamp the inner reinforcement, then make the specified resistance spot welds and MIG/MAG welds. Drill the designated plug-weld holes in the replacement panel with the 8 mm bit. Install and resistance-spot-weld the next inner reinforcement as illustrated.

steps.title: Install the B-pillar assembly
steps.body: Position and clamp the B-pillar assembly, then install its resistance spot welds. Complete the subsequent illustrated MIG/MAG and resistance spot-welding stages. Follow the location-specific joining method rather than treating every connection alike.

steps.title: Reconnect the roof and lower structure
steps.body: Install and resistance-spot-weld the rear roof reinforcement panel on both sides. Apply the specified NVH expanding foam and install the rear floor crossmember bolts to their specified torque.

steps.title: Finish and protect the repair
steps.body: Metal-finish the repair area, seal every required area to production level and restore corrosion protection using [Corrosion Prevention](#/document/G1687508). These operations complete the protection of the repaired joints.

steps.title: Restore the surrounding assemblies
steps.body: Reposition the carpet and wiring harness, then install the roof panel, coupe quarter panel and rear seat cushion under their respective procedures.

watchFor.title: A proposed sectioning shortcut
watchFor.body: The boron-steel reinforcements cannot be sectioned. Preserve the specified factory-joint replacement approach.

watchFor.title: Incomplete access or joining
watchFor.body: The rear roof reinforcement involves both sides. The pictured flange is only one stage of the complete weld-removal and installation sequence.

notes: Use the flexible foam and seam-sealer products specified in the repair procedure; they serve different purposes.

verification.title: Document dimensional condition
verification.body: Record the applicable body and door-opening measurements and any dimensional restoration performed.

verification.title: Confirm structural and protective completion
verification.body: Confirm every illustrated welding stage is complete, the crossmember bolts are tightened, and foam, production-level sealing and corrosion protection have been restored.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly
verification.body: Check that the wiring and carpet are repositioned and all three prerequisite assemblies have been reinstalled.

guides.title: Replace a front door outer skin and restore its sealed seams
guides.summary: Replace the outer door panel using the specified bonded and crimped joint, verify alignment before final closure, and restore finish and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: The door skin forms the door's exterior surface and joins the inner shell around a folded perimeter, called the hem flange. Replacement requires removing that outer panel while preserving the shell, then bonding and forming the new flange. Noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) mastic pads and anti-flutter foam help control movement and vibration of the broad outer surface. This is specialist body repair involving panel fitting, welding, adhesive work and refinishing.
guides.why: Hinge condition affects the alignment used to position the new skin, so hinge inspection comes first. The replacement flange is initially only partly crimped, allowing the door to be trial-fitted and adjusted before tack welding locks the panel position. Cleaning, sealing and corrosion protection then protect the newly formed joint.

when.summary: When a front door outer panel requires replacement and the door shell is being retained.
notes: The left-hand door is illustrated; the right-hand procedure is similar.
Inspect and repair worn or damaged hinges before using door alignment to position the replacement panel.

prepare.title: Arrange body-repair capability
prepare.detail: The work requires a grinder, hot air gun, knife, locking pliers and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment, together with panel-flanging and refinishing skills.

prepare.title: Prepare the specified materials
prepare.detail: Select the metal bonding adhesive, seam sealer and flexible foam repair material from the products listed in the door-skin procedure. Have required NVH mastic pads and a Ford-approved primer and paint system.

prepare.title: Plan removal and trial fitting
prepare.detail: Allow for removal of the glass, door, mirror, exterior handle and upper moulding, plus temporary door installation during panel alignment.

steps.title: Inspect hinges and strip the door
steps.body: Inspect the upper and lower hinges and replace or rebuild them as necessary. Follow the component procedures to remove the window glass, door, exterior mirror, exterior handle and upper moulding.

steps.title: Separate the damaged outer panel
steps.body: Following the [door-skin procedure](#/document/G1687543), use the grinder to cut carefully through the outer panel only. Remove the outer panel while preserving the retained door shell.

steps.title: Remove the remaining hem flange
steps.body: Use the knife and hot air gun to remove the remaining portion of the old panel's hem flange. The attached illustration identifies the perimeter involved in this operation.

steps.title: Prepare the bonding surfaces
steps.body: Remove all adhesive and foreign material from the shell-to-panel mating surfaces, then remove the e-coat from the mating surface. Install NVH mastic pads on the replacement panel as required.

steps.title: Apply adhesive and foam, then partly form the flange
steps.body: Apply the specified metal bonding adhesive to the shell mating surface and anti-flutter expanding foam at the indicated locations. Install the outer panel and partially crimp its flange using locking pliers.

steps.title: Trial-fit and lock the panel position
steps.body: Temporarily install the door on the vehicle, check alignment and adjust as necessary. Carefully open the door and tack weld to lock the panel in place, then remove the door again.

steps.title: Complete the hem
steps.body: Finish the flanging process. Smooth residual adhesive squeeze-out into the seam so it acts as a sealer, then remove foreign material.

steps.title: Protect and finish the flange
steps.body: Apply Ford-approved primer to the flange area. Seal all required areas to production level with the specified seam sealer, then refinish the door-shell flange using a Ford-approved paint system.

steps.title: Install, refinish and reassemble
steps.body: Install the door, then sand and refinish the exterior repair area. Restore protection through the [corrosion-prevention procedure](#/document/G1687508). Reinstall the window glass, exterior mirror, exterior handle and upper moulding through their component procedures.

watchFor.title: Cutting into the retained shell
watchFor.body: The grinder operation is restricted to the outer panel. Cutting deeper can damage the structure needed to receive the new skin.

watchFor.title: Finishing the flange before alignment
watchFor.body: Keep the flange partially crimped until the temporary installation, adjustment and tack-welding stages are complete.

watchFor.title: Missing seam protection
watchFor.body: Exterior paint alone does not complete the repair. The flange needs its primer, sealing and refinishing stages, followed by restored corrosion protection.

notes: The perimeter illustration shows hem-flange removal; use the complete procedure for adhesive, foam and panel-fitting instructions.
The exterior mirror has a separately named removal and installation procedure that must also be followed.

diagnostics.finding: An upper or lower hinge is worn or damaged.
diagnostics.meaning: Door position may be unreliable during replacement-panel alignment.
diagnostics.next: Replace or rebuild the affected hinge as necessary before continuing.

diagnostics.finding: The temporarily installed door does not align correctly.
diagnostics.meaning: The panel position needs correction before it is locked in place.
diagnostics.next: Adjust alignment before tack welding and final flanging.

verification.title: Confirm the alignment decision
verification.body: Confirm proper alignment at the temporary-installation stage before tack welding establishes the panel position.

verification.title: Confirm complete seam restoration
verification.body: Check that final flanging, primer, production-level sealing, flange refinishing and corrosion protection have all been completed.

verification.title: Complete component reassembly
verification.body: Confirm the door, glass, mirror, handle and upper moulding have been installed through their respective procedures.

guides.title: Replace the rocker panel inner reinforcement at its factory seams
guides.summary: Replace the complete martensitic-steel rocker reinforcement using the specified adhesive, welded joints and corrosion-protection sequence.
guides.introduction: The rocker panel inner reinforcement is part of the body structure along the lower side of the passenger compartment. Its repair involves surrounding panels, body alignment and structural joining. The reinforcement is made from martensitic steel and must be replaced at its factory seams; this procedure does not permit a shortened replacement section or local patch.
guides.why: A replacement fitted to a distorted body can preserve the wrong geometry. Restoring dimensions first, then reproducing the specified bonded and welded joints, establishes the repair's structural arrangement. Primer, seam sealing and corrosion protection complete work that would otherwise leave newly exposed metal vulnerable.

when.summary: When damage assessment calls for complete rocker reinforcement replacement at the factory seams.
notes: The coupe is illustrated; the convertible follows a similar repair with body-style-specific access procedures.
The left side is illustrated and the right side is similar.

prepare.title: Use structural body-repair capability
prepare.detail: Arrange body measurement and dimensional restoration where required, together with resistance spot-welding and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding capability.

prepare.title: Gather removal and joining equipment
prepare.detail: The procedure specifies a spot-weld drill bit, hot-air gun, 8 mm drill bit and locking pliers. Have the complete replacement part, specified metal bonding adhesive and seam sealer, and a Ford-approved paint system ready.

prepare.title: Plan the surrounding work
prepare.detail: Use the correct coupe or convertible quarter-panel, B-pillar and A-pillar trim procedures. Move the carpet and wiring harness away from the repair area before panel removal.

steps.title: Establish the body's starting geometry
steps.body: Assess the body against the applicable Body and Frame dimensions. If required, restore the vehicle to its pre-accident dimensional condition before removing the reinforcement. This gives the replacement assembly the correct structure to fit against.

steps.title: Open the surrounding structure
steps.body: Remove the quarter panel, B-pillar and reinforcement, A-pillar trim, and A-pillar outer panel section and reinforcement through their linked procedures. Select the coupe or convertible instructions where separate procedures are listed, then position the carpet and wiring clear.

steps.title: Release the existing rocker assembly
steps.body: Remove the reinforcement bolt. Drill out the specified rocker-panel spot welds with the spot-weld drill bit, then remove the assembly using the hot-air gun as directed. Keep removal at the factory seams; the reinforcement cannot be sectioned.

steps.title: Prepare the replacement and bonded flange
steps.body: Drill the replacement rocker panel's plug-weld holes using the specified 8 mm bit and the arrangement in the complete procedure. Apply the specified metal bonding adhesive to the inner reinforcement structure's flange area.

steps.title: Install and weld the assembly
steps.body: Position and secure the rocker assembly with locking pliers, then perform the specified MIG welding. Follow with the specified resistance spot welding. These are separate joining operations in the installation sequence; retain both.

steps.title: Restore the fastening and protective finishes
steps.body: Install the reinforcement bolt and tighten it to 22 lb.ft (30 Nm). Metal-finish the repair, prime it with a Ford-approved paint system, and seal all required areas to production level with the specified seam sealer. Complete the corrosion-prevention procedure.

steps.title: Close the surrounding repair
steps.body: Reinstall the quarter panel, B-pillar and reinforcement, A-pillar trim, and A-pillar outer panel section and reinforcement using their applicable procedures. Complete the structural finishing and protection work before it becomes concealed by surrounding parts.

watchFor.title: A proposed sectional repair
watchFor.body: Even localized reinforcement damage does not authorize cutting in a partial section. Replacement must be at the factory seams.

watchFor.title: Unfinished protection
watchFor.body: Welding and metal finishing do not complete the repair. Primer, production-level sealing and restored corrosion protection remain necessary.

notes: Use the specified adhesive and seam-sealer products from the replacement procedure; their application locations are part of the repair.

diagnostics.finding: The body is dimensionally displaced after the accident.
diagnostics.meaning: The surrounding structure may not provide correct replacement-panel alignment.
diagnostics.next: Restore dimensions as required before removing and replacing the reinforcement.

verification.title: Check the completed repair sequence
verification.body: Confirm that the required plug welds, resistance spot welds, reinforcement bolt, primer, sealing and corrosion protection have all been completed.

verification.title: Retain the dimensional result
verification.body: Record the relevant body measurements and compare them with the applicable Body and Frame dimensions, identifying any dimensional restoration performed.

guides.title: Replace a damaged outer rocker panel section
guides.summary: Replace the damaged outer rocker section using seam and resistance spot welding, then restore its finish, sealing and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: The rocker panel runs beneath the door opening and forms part of the body's lower side. This repair replaces a damaged section of its outer panel. Coupe and convertible service parts are identified separately, although the illustrated coupe repair method is similar for the convertible. The work combines controlled panel cutting, welding and restoration of protective coatings.
guides.why: Cutting only the outer panel preserves the material behind it. The replacement needs both seam welding and resistance spot welding in the prescribed locations. Welding and metal finishing also disturb protective coatings, making sealing and corrosion protection essential parts of the repair.

when.summary: When damage calls for partial replacement of the outer rocker panel only.
notes: Damage extending beyond the outer panel requires a repair assessment beyond this section-replacement operation.

prepare.title: Provide body-repair capability
prepare.detail: The job requires an air body saw, spot weld drill bit, resistance spotwelding equipment and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment, with the skills to use them.

prepare.title: Prepare the replacement and finishes
prepare.detail: Select the service part for the body style. Have the specified seam sealer, a Ford-approved paint system and the materials required by the corrosion-prevention procedure.

prepare.title: Plan restraint and interior access
prepare.detail: The front seatbelt retractor and pretensioner must be removed through their dedicated procedure. The carpet and wiring also need to be moved away from the repair area.

steps.title: Clear the repair area
steps.body: Remove the front door, rocker moulding, and front seatbelt retractor and pretensioner using their linked procedures. Position the carpet and wiring harness aside. This provides access to the panel and separates the repair area from the displaced interior components.

steps.title: Remove only the damaged outer section
steps.body: Follow the section boundaries illustrated in the [rocker panel procedure](#/document/G1687544). Carefully cut through the outer panel only with the air body saw, drill out the spot welds and remove the section. The highlighted illustration identifies the removable area; it does not supply cut dimensions.

steps.title: Prepare and weld the replacement section
steps.body: Cut the corresponding section from the replacement service part. Install it and seam weld it with the specified MIG/MAG equipment, then resistance spot weld the panel. These are separate joining operations in the installation sequence.

steps.title: Finish, prime and seal
steps.body: Complete the metal finishing, then prime the repair area with a Ford-approved paint system. Seal all affected areas back to production level with one of the seam sealers specified in the procedure. Sealing must address the repaired joints, not just their visible surfaces.

steps.title: Restore coatings and removed components
steps.body: Refinish with a Ford-approved paint system and carry out [corrosion prevention](#/document/G1687508). Return the harness and carpet to their original positions. Reinstall the door, rocker moulding and seatbelt retractor/pretensioner through their individual installation procedures.

watchFor.title: Cutting into underlying material
watchFor.body: The repair is explicitly limited to the outer panel; do not extend the saw cut into the structure behind it.

watchFor.title: Stopping after paint
watchFor.body: Refinishing does not replace seam sealing or the separate corrosion-protection operation.

notes: Use the correct coupe or convertible service part even though the working method is similar.
No welding settings or section dimensions are specified here; follow the complete repair illustrations and joining procedure.

diagnostics.finding: Damage involves more than the outer rocker skin.
diagnostics.meaning: The stated partial outer-panel repair does not cover the full damage.
diagnostics.next: Establish the appropriate repair scope before cutting a replacement section.

verification.title: Confirm the complete repair sequence
verification.body: Confirm completion of seam welding, resistance spot welding, metal finishing, priming, production-level sealing, refinishing and corrosion protection.

verification.title: Check restoration and record protection
verification.body: Verify that the wiring and carpet are back in their original positions and the removed components are reinstalled. Record the sealing and corrosion-protection work.

guides.title: Replace the rear back panel and reinforcement
guides.summary: Restore the rear body geometry, replace the bonded and welded back panel and reinforcement, then renew sealing and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: The back panel forms part of the rear body, with a reinforcement joined to it and the surrounding structure. Their attachments combine adhesive and welding, so replacement is a body repair rather than a bolt-on panel change. The work includes restoring accident-related distortion when necessary, rebuilding the joints and restoring the protective finish.
guides.why: New panels cannot correct an underlying body shape that remains distorted. Clean bonding surfaces, controlled heat and the specified joining methods are equally important: the completed repair depends on its attachments as well as its visible shape. Sealing and corrosion protection finish the structural work.

when.summary: When rear-body damage requires replacement of the back panel and its reinforcement.
notes: Restore the vehicle to its pre-accident dimensions first if required.
This work requires body measurement, adhesive joining, welding and refinishing capability.

prepare.title: Arrange body-repair equipment
prepare.detail: Provide resistance spot-welding equipment, metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment, locking pliers, a spot-weld drill, an 8 mm drill bit and a hot-air gun.

prepare.title: Prepare materials and technical procedures
prepare.detail: Use the listed metal bonding adhesive and seam sealer, plus a Ford-approved paint system. Have the body dimensions, Joining Techniques and Corrosion Prevention procedures available.

prepare.title: Clear the working area
prepare.detail: Plan removal of the rear bumper and rear lamps. The carpet and wiring harness must be repositioned away from the cutting, heating and welding area.

steps.title: Establish the body geometry
steps.body: Check the vehicle against [Body and Frame](#/document/G1687516). If required, restore its pre-accident dimensions before removing the panels so the replacement parts have correctly positioned attachment points.

steps.title: Remove surrounding parts
steps.body: Remove the rear bumper and rear lamps using their linked procedures. Move the carpeting and wiring harness away from the work. Apply the requirements in [Joining Techniques](#/document/G1687509).

steps.title: Remove the back panel, then the reinforcement
steps.body: Drill out the back-panel spot welds and remove the panel. Then drill out the reinforcement spot welds and remove it. Heat may soften the adhesive during either removal, but must not exceed 170°C.

steps.title: Prepare the reinforcement joints
steps.body: Drill 8 mm plug-weld holes in the replacement reinforcement. Clean the floor-pan flange and reinforcement upper flanges, keeping the component free of foreign material and lubricant. Apply the specified metal bonding adhesive to these surfaces.

steps.title: Install the reinforcement
steps.body: Position and clamp the reinforcement with locking pliers. Resistance spot-weld it, then carry out the specified MIG welding. Follow the attachment sequence in the [back-panel procedure](#/document/G1687558).

steps.title: Prepare and install the back panel
steps.body: Drill its 8 mm plug-weld holes. Ensure the panel is clean and free of foreign material and lubricant before applying the specified adhesive. Position and clamp it, then perform resistance spot welding followed by MIG welding.

steps.title: Restore the protective finish
steps.body: Metal-finish the repair area and seal all areas to production level with the specified seam sealer. Follow [Corrosion Prevention](#/document/G1687508), then refinish with a Ford-approved paint system.

steps.title: Restore the surrounding equipment
steps.body: Return the wiring harness and carpet to position. Reinstall the rear bumper and rear lamp assemblies using their respective procedures.

watchFor.title: Excessive removal heat
watchFor.body: The 170°C limit applies when heating to soften the adhesive; do not exceed it to force separation.

watchFor.title: Contaminated bonding surfaces
watchFor.body: Foreign material or lubricant must be removed before adhesive application. A visually aligned panel still requires correctly prepared joints.

notes: Use the specific adhesive and seam-sealer products listed in the procedure; this repair does not authorize a generic adhesive substitution.
The body contains several steel types. Do not infer a panel’s material or joining requirements from its appearance.

diagnostics.finding: The rear body remains dimensionally displaced.
diagnostics.meaning: The attachment structure has not yet been restored to its pre-accident condition.
diagnostics.next: Complete the required dimensional restoration before panel replacement.

verification.title: Record dimensional results
verification.body: Document the relevant body measurements and rear-panel margins against the Body and Frame information.

verification.title: Check the finished repair
verification.body: Confirm completion of both welding stages, production-level sealing, corrosion protection and approved refinishing, followed by restoration of the harness, carpet, bumper and lamps.

guides.title: Replace the convertible quarter panel
guides.summary: Replace a damaged convertible quarter panel and restore its welded joints, bonded areas, sealing, finish and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: The quarter panel forms the fixed outer body side around the rear wheel opening. This mild-steel panel joins the surrounding body through welded flanges and bonded areas, with foam helping control noise, vibration and harshness (NVH). Replacement involves releasing these connections without damaging the underlying structure, then rebuilding them around a correctly positioned service panel.
guides.why: A new outer panel cannot correct displaced underlying bodywork. Establishing body geometry first protects panel fit, while controlled cutting preserves the inner panels. Welding completes only part of the repair: sealing, paint and corrosion protection must also be restored.

when.summary: When damage calls for convertible quarter-panel replacement after assessment of the surrounding body geometry.
notes: Left-side work includes the fuel filler door and, as equipped, the engine-specific fuel filler pipe.

prepare.title: Body-shop capability
prepare.detail: Arrange dimensional checking and restoration, resistance spot welding, metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding, metal finishing and refinishing.

prepare.title: Tools and repair materials
prepare.detail: Prepare an air body saw, spot-weld drill bit, 8 mm drill bit, hot-air gun, knife and locking pliers. Use the listed metal bonding adhesive, flexible foam repair and seam sealer, plus a Ford-approved paint system.

prepare.title: Access and fuel-system prerequisites
prepare.detail: Have the linked removal-and-installation procedures available before stripping the car. Complete the applicable left-side filler-pipe removal and its prerequisites before panel heating or welding.

steps.title: Restore the body geometry where necessary
steps.body: Assess the damaged area against Body and Frame dimensions. If required, restore the vehicle to its pre-accident condition before removing the quarter panel. The surrounding attachment points must provide the correct shape for the replacement.

steps.title: Remove the top, closures and applicable filler parts
steps.body: Remove the convertible top assembly, front door and luggage compartment lid through their individual procedures. On the left side, remove the fuel filler door and the filler pipe as equipped. Select the pipe procedure for the actual 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine.

steps.title: Expose the panel connections
steps.body: Remove the rocker panel moulding, convertible loadspace trim, rear quarter trim, rear bumper and rear lamp assembly. Remove the affected-side door striker, then position the carpet and wiring harness aside to clear the repair area.

steps.title: Release and remove the damaged panel
steps.body: Follow the cutting and spot-weld locations in the quarter-panel procedure. Cut through the outer panel only, cut its flange and drill out the specified spot welds. Release the adhesive and NVH foam with the knife and hot-air gun as needed. Applied heat must not exceed 170°C.

steps.title: Prepare the replacement for joining
steps.body: Drill the specified plug-weld holes with the 8 mm bit. Apply NVH expanding foam and metal bonding adhesive at the indicated locations. Use the complete procedure to locate these areas; the removal illustration does not establish the installation pattern.

steps.title: Install and weld in the prescribed sequence
steps.body: Position and clamp the replacement, then seam weld it. Continue at the door opening using the specified MIG/MAG and resistance spot-welding methods. MIG weld the flange areas, then weld the upper flanges using the specified MIG/MAG and resistance spot-welding operations. Retain the procedure's location-specific joining methods.

steps.title: Finish, seal and protect the repair
steps.body: Metal-finish the repaired areas, seal all areas to production level and refinish with a Ford-approved paint system. Restore corrosion protection through the separate Corrosion Prevention procedure before completing reassembly.

steps.title: Restore the removed assemblies
steps.body: Reposition the carpet and wiring harness and install the door striker. Reinstall the top, front door, luggage lid, applicable left-side filler parts, rocker moulding, loadspace and quarter trim, rear bumper and rear lamp in the stated installation order, following each assembly's procedure.

watchFor.title: Cutting into retained structure
watchFor.body: The cut-through-outer-panel-only instruction is essential: the inner body remains part of the repaired vehicle.

watchFor.title: Incomplete protection
watchFor.body: Exposed repair areas or incompletely sealed joints mean the job has not reached its required corrosion-protection and sealing endpoint.

notes: Use convertible-specific dimensions where specified, particularly around the top and side glass. Do not substitute coupe geometry.

verification.title: Check adjacent panel fit
verification.body: Compare applicable gaps and flushness at the door, luggage lid, rear lamp, rear fascia, fuel door and convertible top with Body and Frame specifications.

verification.title: Record completion
verification.body: Record the dimensional and panel-fit checks, and confirm that production-level sealing, refinishing, corrosion protection and all listed reassembly operations are complete.

guides.title: Replace the rear floor panel on a coupe or convertible
guides.summary: Replace the damaged welded rear floor, restore its attachments and protective materials, and complete the additional convertible reinforcement work where applicable.
guides.introduction: The rear floor is part of the welded body shell and includes the spare-wheel well and attachments for surrounding panels and brackets. Replacing it involves restoring body shape, separating welded and bonded joints, fitting the new panel, and rebuilding its sealing, sound-deadening and corrosion protection. Convertible bodies also require crossmember and reinforcement work.
guides.why: A replacement panel can preserve existing distortion if the body is not restored before fitting. Weld positions and quantities govern how the new floor joins the surrounding structure. Sealer, foam, mastic and corrosion protection complete those joints and must be restored along with the metal.

when.summary: When assessed rear-body damage requires replacement or permitted sectioning of the rear floor panel.
notes: Select the sectioning plan from the permitted cut points for the actual damage.
Most operations are shared; crossmember and additional reinforcement operations are convertible-only.

prepare.title: Arrange structural repair capability
prepare.detail: Provide body measurement and dimensional restoration capability, resistance spotwelding, metal inert gas (MIG) brazing and MIG/metal active gas (MAG) welding equipment. Follow Joining Techniques for the selected joints.

prepare.title: Prepare separation and fitting tools
prepare.detail: Have a spot-weld drill bit, spherical cutter, straight-edge scraper, knife, hot-air gun, locking pliers and an 8 mm drill bit. Protect adjacent areas from cutting, grinding and welding.

prepare.title: Plan component removal
prepare.detail: Arrange safe access and support for rear-subframe removal and the engine-matched fuel-system and exhaust procedures. Include supplemental restraint system (SRS) depowering and repowering in the work plan.

steps.title: Depower and establish body shape
steps.body: Depower the SRS using its dedicated procedure. If required, dimensionally restore the vehicle to its pre-damage condition using Body and Frame before separating the floor.

steps.title: Clear the working area
steps.body: Remove the rear seat, quarter trim and body-style-specific loadspace trim. Move carpeting, modules and wiring away. Remove the fitted evaporative-emission canister, fuel tank, rear subframe, muffler and tailpipe, back panel and reinforcement, and wheel-and-tire components through their respective procedures.

steps.title: Expose the panel joints
steps.body: On a convertible, drill out the crossmember spot welds and remove the crossmember. Remove the noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) mastic. Heat may assist softening, but must not exceed 170°C.

steps.title: Separate the old floor
steps.body: Drill the floor-seam spot welds and grind away the brazed material. On both sides, drill the lower quarter-panel-extension welds and remove the foam carrier strips. Remove the floor assembly; heat used to soften its adhesive must also remain at or below 170°C.

steps.title: Prepare and fit the replacement
steps.body: Drill the specified plug-weld holes in the replacement floor and both rear floor extensions using the 8 mm bit. Properly position and clamp the floor, then position and clamp the extensions before joining.

steps.title: Rebuild the floor joints
steps.body: Follow the [rear floor procedure](#/document/G1687560) and Joining Techniques for the welding and brazing locations. Complete the floor and extension joints on both sides, including the connections to the quarter-panel extensions.

steps.title: Complete convertible reinforcement
steps.body: For a convertible, install and weld the underbody crossmember. Drill the replacement reinforcement's plug-weld holes, then position, clamp and weld it as directed.

steps.title: Restore brackets and foam
steps.body: Drill the vapor-canister and spare-tire brackets for plug welding, then position, clamp and weld them. Apply the specified NVH expanding foam to the foam carrier strips and install them on both sides.

steps.title: Finish and protect the repair
steps.body: Dress the welds as required, seal every seam to production level and restore NVH material in its original locations. Refinish with a Ford-approved paint system and restore corrosion protection.

steps.title: Reassemble the vehicle
steps.body: Reinstall the removed underbody components, back panel and reinforcement, and wheels using their procedures. Return wiring, modules and carpet to their original positions, install the trim and rear seat, then repower the SRS.

watchFor.title: Substitute weld locations
watchFor.body: Replacement resistance welds must sit adjacent to the original locations and match the factory quantity. MAG plug welds must match both factory location and quantity.

watchFor.title: Heat and nearby components
watchFor.body: The heat allowance for softening material does not remove the need to protect adjacent areas or move wiring and modules away.

notes: The illustrations generally show the coupe and left side; follow the corresponding operations on the right side.
The listed engine-specific canister, tank and exhaust references cover 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L. For a 5.2L vehicle, establish the matching access procedures before removal.

diagnostics.finding: The rear body is dimensionally displaced.
diagnostics.meaning: Correct panel fit depends on restoring the surrounding structure first.
diagnostics.next: Carry out the required dimensional restoration before floor replacement.

verification.title: Record structural completion
verification.body: Record the dimensional assessment and any restoration, and verify that completed welds satisfy the required locations and quantities.

verification.title: Confirm protective and vehicle restoration
verification.body: Check completion of seam sealing, foam, NVH material, refinishing and corrosion protection. Confirm component reinstallation and completion of the SRS repowering procedure.

guides.title: Replace a damaged rear side member at its factory joints
guides.summary: Replace the damaged rear side-member assembly, restore its welded connections and corrosion protection, then refit the removed components.
guides.introduction: The rear side member forms part of the load-carrying rear body structure. Replacement restores its connection to the surrounding panels after accident damage. Although service parts come in several pieces, the repair path described here is complete assembly replacement.
guides.why: The member is made from dual-phase (DP) 800 steel and must not be sectioned. Replacement must use factory joints. Correct body dimensions establish where the new assembly belongs; sound welds, sealing and corrosion protection preserve the repaired structure.

when.summary: When collision damage requires rear side-member replacement at the factory joints.
notes: Choose the service parts needed for the damage while retaining the prohibition on sectioning.

prepare.title: Structural repair capability
prepare.detail: Use a facility equipped for frame measurement, dimensional restoration and structural welding. Read Body Repair Health and Safety and General Precautions before starting.

prepare.title: Joining equipment
prepare.detail: Have a spot-weld drill bit, 8 mm drill bit, locking pliers and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment. Arrange the specified finishing, sealing and corrosion-protection materials.

prepare.title: Access and component removal
prepare.detail: Plan suitable lifting and support for rear-subframe removal and the applicable fuel-system work. Complete the required removals and move vulnerable interior materials before welding.

steps.title: Establish dimensions and the replacement boundary
steps.body: Check the vehicle on a frame machine and restore pre-accident dimensions where necessary using [Body and Frame](#/document/G1687516). Consult the coupe or convertible construction overview and the [rear side-member procedure](#/document/G1687570) to identify service parts and factory joints.

steps.title: Clear the repair area
steps.body: Follow the individual removal procedures for the rear subframe, fuel tank, evaporative-emission canister as equipped, and back panel with reinforcement. Move the carpeting and wiring harness away from the working area to protect them during drilling and joining.

steps.title: Separate the damaged assembly
steps.body: Drill out the required factory spot welds and remove the member from the damaged side or sides. Preserve the mating flanges and adjacent panels. Correct damaged receiving flanges before fitting the replacement; do not create a section joint through the member.

steps.title: Prepare and trial-fit the replacement
steps.body: Clean and prepare mating surfaces without thinning the metal or damaging corners. Prepare the indicated service-panel locations with 8 mm plug-weld holes. Follow the original weld count and near-original positions without placing holes directly over old weld sites. Dry-fit and clamp the assembly to verify fit and alignment.

steps.title: Clamp and complete the joints
steps.body: Use locking pliers and MIG/MAG plug welding at the indicated positions, following [Joining Techniques](#/document/G1687509) and the body-repair specifications. Where the prescribed joint uses adhesive, follow its mixing and cure instructions and keep plug-weld sites adhesive-free. Adhesive is not automatically required at every rail seam.

steps.title: Restore the protective finish
steps.body: Metal-finish the repair as required, seal all areas to production level and refinish with a Ford-approved paint system. Restore corrosion protection using the specified procedure so prepared metal and repaired seams are protected.

steps.title: Refit the removed components
steps.body: Follow the installation procedures for the rear subframe, fuel tank, canister as equipped, and back panel with reinforcement. Reposition the carpeting and wiring harness after the structural and protective work is complete.

watchFor.title: A proposed cut through the member
watchFor.body: DP800 side members cannot be sectioned. Keep the replacement boundary at factory joints.

watchFor.title: Damaged joining surfaces
watchFor.body: Drilling and grinding must preserve flange thickness and corners. Correct flange damage before joining the replacement.

notes: The fuel-tank link applies to the 2.3L engine. Canister links are specific to 2.3L and 5.0L; confirm the matching fuel-system procedure before work on another engine.

verification.title: Record dimensional and fit checks
verification.body: Record the dimensional check and trial-fit results against the applicable body dimensions. Resolve discrepancies before final welding.

verification.title: Check joints and protection
verification.body: Confirm the specified weld locations are completed, sealing matches production level, and refinishing and corrosion protection are restored.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly
verification.body: Check that the removed components have been installed through their individual procedures and that carpeting and wiring are repositioned.

guides.title: Section-repair the rear outer wheelhouse
guides.summary: Replace a damaged section of rear outer wheelhouse sheet metal, then restore its welded seams, sealing, and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: The rear outer wheelhouse is the sheet metal surrounding the rear wheel opening behind the quarter panel. This repair removes the damaged portion and joins a matching section cut from a replacement panel. Access requires the quarter panel procedure appropriate to the body style. Successful work includes restoring body dimensions where necessary, joining the replacement section, and rebuilding the protective finish around the repair.
guides.why: A replacement section must fit a correctly shaped body. Cutting before necessary dimensional restoration can make the new piece fit distorted surrounding metal. The illustrated cutline is only a general guide: damage extent determines the repair boundary. Welding also disturbs protective coatings, so sealing and refinishing are essential parts of completing the repair.
searchTerms: rear wheel arch sheet metal replacement

when.summary: When rear outer wheelhouse damage requires removal and replacement of a sheet-metal section.
notes: The illustration shows the left side of a coupe; the right side and convertible use similar repair principles.
Use the quarter panel removal and installation procedure for the actual body style.

prepare.title: Arrange body-repair capability
prepare.detail: This work requires dimensional assessment and correction where needed, controlled panel sectioning, welding, metal finishing, and corrosion-protection restoration.

prepare.title: Gather the specified equipment
prepare.detail: Provide an air body saw, locking pliers, resistance spotwelding equipment, and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment.

prepare.title: Prepare access and finishing materials
prepare.detail: Have the replacement panel, a seam sealer listed in the wheelhouse procedure, and a Ford-approved paint system. Plan to move the carpet and wiring harness away from the work.

steps.title: Restore dimensions if required
steps.body: Assess the body against the applicable Body and Frame information. Where accident damage has changed its shape, restore the vehicle to its pre-accident dimensions before proceeding.

steps.title: Expose the wheelhouse
steps.body: Remove the quarter panel using either the coupe or convertible procedure. Reposition the carpeting and wiring harness away from the working area before cutting or welding.

steps.title: Mark and remove the damaged section
steps.body: Choose and mark the cutline according to the extent of the damage. Use the illustration as a general guide, then cut out the damaged wheelhouse portion with the air body saw.

steps.title: Prepare and weld the replacement
steps.body: Cut the required section from the replacement panel. Position it with locking pliers and install it using resistance spotwelding as directed in the wheelhouse procedure. Weld the panel seams using MIG/MAG equipment.

steps.title: Finish the repaired metal
steps.body: Metal-finish the repaired area as required using normal body-repair techniques. This prepares the joined sheet metal for the subsequent sealing and finishing work.

steps.title: Restore sealing and corrosion protection
steps.body: Seal all areas to production level with a listed seam sealer. Refinish with a Ford-approved paint system and follow the linked Corrosion Prevention procedure.

steps.title: Restore the surrounding components
steps.body: Return the carpet and wiring harness to position. Install the quarter panel using the correct body-style procedure to complete the access work.

watchFor.title: Treating the drawing as a fixed cut boundary
watchFor.body: The cutline must suit the damage; copying the illustrated line without assessing the panel can leave unsuitable metal in the repair.

watchFor.title: An unfinished protective repair
watchFor.body: Weld completion alone does not finish this job. All repair areas require production-level sealing and the specified refinishing and corrosion-protection work.

notes: The body uses several steel types. General body construction information does not identify the wheelhouse material or supply substitute welding instructions.

diagnostics.finding: The vehicle requires dimensional restoration after the accident.
diagnostics.meaning: The surrounding body geometry must be corrected before fitting the replacement wheelhouse section.
diagnostics.next: Use Body and Frame information to guide restoration before panel sectioning.

verification.title: Check repair completion
verification.body: Confirm the replacement section is welded and metal-finished, all repair areas are sealed and refinished, and the carpet, harness, and correct quarter panel are reinstalled.

verification.title: Record dimensional work where required
verification.body: Where dimensional restoration was necessary, record the applicable body measurements used to establish the restored condition.

guides.title: Remove the rear water drain panel for collision repair
guides.summary: Establish rear-body geometry, create access and separate the welded and foam connections to remove the water drain panel assembly.
guides.introduction: The water drain panel is part of the rear body sheet metal around the luggage-compartment and rear-lamp area. Removing it involves neighboring panels, spot-welded connections and expanding foam between the quarter panel and lamp mounting panel. This operation prepares the damaged area for subsequent collision repair; it ends with the assembly removed and the body’s dimensional condition recorded.
guides.why: A distorted body may need dimensional correction before cutting connections apart. Establishing geometry first preserves a useful reference for later repair. Separating the foam as well as the welds allows the assembly to come away without pulling on material that remains attached.

when.summary: Remove when rear collision damage requires access to, or repair involving, the water drain panel assembly.
notes: Quarter-panel removal depends on the damage and required access.

prepare.title: Arrange body-repair capability
prepare.detail: Use a workshop able to measure rear-body geometry and restore accident distortion when necessary. Have the body-style-specific glass, quarter-panel and closure access procedures available.

prepare.title: Prepare separation equipment
prepare.detail: Use a spot weld drill bit and knife. If heat is needed to soften adhesive or expanding foam, use equipment that allows the specified temperature limit to be observed.

steps.title: Establish the dimensional starting point
steps.body: Check the body against the Body and Frame dimensions and restore it to pre-accident condition if required. Record the relevant geometry before releasing the panel so later work has a defined starting point.

steps.title: Remove the surrounding access components
steps.body: Follow the linked procedures for fixed glass, the back panel and reinforcement, and the luggage compartment lid. Remove the quarter panel as damage requires, choosing the coupe or convertible procedure. Record which surrounding components were removed.

steps.title: Move carpeting and wiring clear
steps.body: Position the carpeting and wiring harness away from the working area before drilling or cutting. Keep them clear of the weld-access and foam-separation areas throughout removal.

steps.title: Release the panel and lamp-panel welds
steps.body: Use the spot weld drill bit to release the welds identified in the removal procedure, then drill the spot welds on the lamp mounting panel. Follow the illustrated locations rather than assuming the visible edge represents every connection.

steps.title: Separate the foam and remove the assembly
steps.body: Cut the noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) expanding foam between the quarter panel and rear lamp mounting panel with a knife. Heat may assist softening adhesive and foam, but must not exceed 170°C. Then drill the reinforcement welds and remove the water drain panel assembly.

watchFor.title: Connections still holding the assembly
watchFor.body: Remaining foam or weld attachments mean separation is incomplete. Confirm the prescribed release work before trying to remove the panel.

watchFor.title: Body-style and side differences
watchFor.body: Use the correct coupe or convertible access instructions. Left- and right-side removal are similar, but identify the actual connections on the working side.

notes: Joining Techniques and Corrosion Prevention support planning for subsequent repair. The applicable panel installation procedure must determine the joining method.
Panel replacement and return-to-service checks are separate from this removal operation.

verification.title: Confirm removal is complete
verification.body: Confirm the water drain panel assembly has been removed after the panel, lamp mounting panel and reinforcement welds and intervening foam were separated.

verification.title: Record the handover condition
verification.body: Keep the body measurements, any dimensional correction and the adjacent-access removal record with the job. These establish the condition handed over for the next repair phase.

Body dimensions and geometry preparation before panel separation.
Fixed-glass removal for access.
Back panel and reinforcement removal for access.

guides.title: Repair paint contamination, etching and delamination
guides.summary: Choose environmental decontamination and controlled surface correction or manufacturing-damage refinishing according to the paint defect.
guides.introduction: Paint defects can involve contamination on the finish, etching into its surface, or failure of the coating itself. These conditions require different work. Environmental treatment removes contamination before polishing is considered; manufacturing-damage repair removes failed coating and rebuilds the finish, with clear coat applied across the affected panel.
guides.why: Iron particles left beneath new paint can produce rust spots again. Cleaning products must remain wet to avoid paint failure, and abrasive correction must stay within the permitted paint-film removal limit. Delamination requires complete removal of the failed coating.

when.summary: When environmental contamination, acid-rain etching or manufacturing-related paint delamination needs correction.
notes: Choose the repair branch according to the defect; refinishing is conditional on the condition of the finish.

prepare.title: Chemical and sanding precautions
prepare.detail: Review the [body repair precautions](#/document/G1693182) and chemical safety data. Wear the specified chemical protection; sanding or grinding requires eye protection with side shields and a dust mask.

prepare.title: Cleaning and finishing capability
prepare.detail: Provide cold-water rinsing, separate clean mitts for each product, Valugard Acid Neutralizer VG-A100G and Alkaline Neutralizer VG-B102G. Abrasive correction and refinishing require control of film removal and the product manufacturer's equipment, pads, speeds and application sequence.

steps.title: Environmental damage: rinse and prepare the first wash
steps.body: Follow the environmental branch of the [paint repair procedure](#/document/G1687576). Flush dust, dirt and foreign material away with cold water. Mix 8 parts water with 1 part acid neutralizer in a bucket.

steps.title: Apply and rinse the acid neutralizer
steps.body: Work quickly from the top toward the sides with a clean twisted lambs wool mitt. Keep the whole vehicle wet and lightly agitate for 5–7 minutes, making 4–5 circuits; severe conditions allow up to 8 minutes. Rinse the mitt frequently. Rinse the vehicle completely with cold water, then dry only horizontal surfaces, leaving the glass undried.

steps.title: Apply the alkaline neutralizer
steps.body: Use this product undiluted. Dispense it from a squirt bottle onto a separate clean closed-loop mitt. Do not apply it directly to plastic trim. Keep the treatment wet and lightly agitate for 5–7 minutes, or up to 8 minutes for severe conditions, then rinse completely with cold water.

steps.title: Shampoo and inspect for remaining particles
steps.body: Shampoo the entire exterior with car wash soap and a clean closed-loop mitt. Rinse with cold water and dry completely. Inspect for remaining ferrous metal particles and repeat the decontamination procedure as necessary before proceeding.

steps.title: Correct remaining surface damage
steps.body: Use one manufacturer's buffing products in its prescribed sequence: rubbing compound, then machine glaze. Acid-rain etching may also require color sanding. Clean corrected areas with a 1-to-1 alcohol-and-water mixture and verify scratch and swirl removal before final polish. Apply final polish by hand, with a dual-action sander and foam pad, or an orbital polisher with the appropriate bonnet. Wash and dry afterward.

steps.title: Manufacturing damage: remove failed coating
steps.body: For the manufacturing-damage branch, wash the repair area with pH-neutral soap and water, then remove trim, emblems and hardware. Sand or media blast the damaged surface, keeping the repair area as small as possible while removing all delamination.

steps.title: Prepare the exposed surface
steps.body: Treat bare metal to prevent flash corrosion. Prime and block sand as necessary before refinishing, then mask adjacent panels against overspray.

steps.title: Restore the coating and fittings
steps.body: Following the paint manufacturer's procedures, spot repair the base coat where needed and apply clear coat to the entire panel. Reinstall the trim, emblems and hardware removed from the repair area.

watchFor.title: Products drying on the finish
watchFor.body: Neither neutralizer may dry on the vehicle; drying can cause paint failure.

watchFor.title: Excessive abrasive correction
watchFor.body: Do not remove more than 0.3 mil of paint film through buffing, polishing or color sanding. Exceeding this limit requires refinishing.

notes: Never paint over iron particles. Complete the specified decontamination first.

diagnostics.finding: Acid-rain discoloration or etching remains after surface correction.
diagnostics.meaning: The damage may be beyond what the permitted correction can restore.
diagnostics.next: Proceed to refinishing when the correction procedure cannot restore the finish.

diagnostics.finding: Coating is delaminating.
diagnostics.meaning: The failed coating must be removed completely.
diagnostics.next: Use the manufacturing-damage preparation and refinishing branch.

verification.title: Environmental repair checks
verification.body: Verify that no ferrous particles remain and that scratches and swirls are removed before final polish.

verification.title: Refinishing completion
verification.body: Confirm that all delamination was removed, the panel received clear coat, and removed fittings were restored.

procedures.purpose: Both repair branches: environmental decontamination and finish correction, and manufacturing-damage preparation and refinishing.
Required body repair precautions, including chemical handling and sanding protection.

guides.title: Remove and refit the front subframe on 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L Mustangs
guides.summary: Support the engine and cooling module, disconnect the steering and suspension, then remove and realign the front subframe using new specified fasteners.
guides.introduction: The front subframe provides mounting points for the suspension control arms, engine isolators and steering gear, while contributing structural support. Removing it separates several load-bearing connections at once. This job covers complete removal and refitting on the 2.3L, 3.7L and 5.0L, with different engine-access and support arrangements for each.
guides.why: The engine and cooling module need support while their supporting structure is removed. Steering-shaft handling, replacement fasteners and subframe alignment directly affect safe reassembly. Reference marks help restore the original position, but the final front-toe check remains necessary.

when.summary: When an established repair requires complete removal or replacement of the front subframe assembly.
notes: This procedure does not cover complete 5.2L subframe removal.
Misalignment can affect suspension and drivetrain operation; an alignment concern alone does not establish that the subframe needs replacement.

prepare.title: Provide lifting and separation equipment
prepare.detail: Arrange vehicle lifting facilities, powertrain lift 300-OTC1585AE, lower-arm ball-joint separator 204-592, a tie-rod end remover, steering-wheel holding device and accurate torque equipment.

prepare.title: Match the engine support
prepare.detail: Use support bar 303-F072 with lifting bracket 303-050 for the 2.3L and 5.0L, or lift eyes 303-1245 and 303-1529 for the 3.7L. Place bar feet on body structure near the strut towers, never on the fenders.

prepare.title: Have replacement fasteners and finishing capability
prepare.detail: Provide new forward subframe bolts and nuts, rearward subframe bolts, stabilizer bracket bolts, tie-rod nuts, front and rear lower-arm ball-joint nuts, and a steering-shaft bolt. Arrange front-toe measurement and adjustment, plus dynamic-suspension recalibration if fitted.

steps.title: Isolate power and protect the steering
steps.body: Disconnect the battery ground cable before steering-gear work. Remove the dash-seal nuts, loosen the seal and hand-start its nuts without damaging the foam or bracket retainers. Hold the steering wheel straight ahead. The loosened seal is essential before separating the lower steering shaft.

steps.title: Open the engine-specific access
steps.body: Follow the appropriate removal article. The 2.3L requires appearance-cover access. The 5.0L requires cross-brace, battery-tray, cowl, battery-heat-shield and air-cleaner removal. On the 3.7L, remove fitted cowl components and disconnect the positive cable where specified; move the air-conditioning compressor belt aside, disconnect its electrical connection and harness retainer, then loosen the captive compressor fasteners and position the compressor aside.

steps.title: Support the engine and cooling module
steps.body: Follow the engine-specific sequence for radiator-shield removal, cooling-module support clips, engine-mount nut removal and engine-support installation. Hold the engine in its normal position; it does not need lifting. On the 2.3L, also disconnect the engine-mount control reservoir vacuum tubes and the right-hand mount tube.

steps.title: Clear the underside and disconnect the shaft
steps.body: Remove the wheels, shields and fitted V-brace as directed; the shield can remain attached to the V-brace. Remove and discard the steering-shaft bolt, separate the shaft from its coupler without force and secure it to the frame rail so lowering the subframe cannot damage it.

steps.title: Separate suspension connections
steps.body: If dynamic suspension is fitted, disconnect both front height-sensor electrical connectors and arm brackets before disturbing the suspension. Support the stabilizer after removing its bracket bolts. Use the specified separators to release both tie-rod ends and both front and rear lower-arm ball joints. Discard their specified nuts and the stabilizer bracket bolts.

steps.title: Mark, support and lower the assembly
steps.body: Disconnect the electric power-assisted steering connectors, release its harness retainers and unclip the crossover brake line. On the 2.3L, remove the front support-bar bolts. Mark the subframe position at the illustrated reference locations. Support it with the powertrain lift, remove and discard the rearward bolts and forward nuts, then lower the assembly. Remove and discard the forward bolts afterward.

steps.title: Install new mounts and restore alignment
steps.body: Install the new forward bolts with their tabs engaged in the body rail. Raise the assembly and align the reference marks before tightening new forward nuts and rearward bolts. For the 3.7L, follow the alignment-tool and cross-pattern tightening details in the linked subframe-refitting section of the oil-pan procedure.

steps.title: Reconnect steering and suspension
steps.body: Restore the 2.3L front support bar, brake-line clips and steering wiring. Reconnect rear and front lower-arm joints, tie rods and stabilizer using new specified fasteners and the applicable torque values. Refit any height-sensor brackets and connectors. Reconnect the steering shaft with a new bolt, then perform the Steering Column Collapsed Check.

steps.title: Restore the engine-specific fittings
steps.body: Refit the shields, V-brace and wheels. Restore the engine mounts and, on the 2.3L, their vacuum connections. Once the mounts carry the engine, remove the temporary support equipment and restore the cooling-module support arrangement. Refit the 3.7L compressor, connector, retainer and belt, or the 5.0L heat shield, cowl, battery tray, brace and air cleaner. Restore other removed covers and brackets.

steps.title: Finish the seal and geometry checks
steps.body: Position and tighten the steering-column dash seal, then reconnect the battery using the battery procedure. Check front toe and adjust if necessary. Where dynamic suspension is fitted, complete the required sensor recalibration after reassembly.

watchFor.title: Steering damage from force or reused bolts
watchFor.body: Never hammer, pry or force the steering shaft, and never reuse its bolt. Damage or detachment can cause loss of steering control.

watchFor.title: Different separation rules
watchFor.body: Do not hammer a tie-rod end free. A light tap at the ball-joint area of the knuckle is permitted only after applying pressure with the specified ball-joint separator.

watchFor.title: Fastener and seal condition
watchFor.body: Use specified-quality suspension fasteners and tightening values. Protect the dash-seal foam and retainers: damage can admit noise, fumes, air or water.

notes: Engine-mount nut torque differs: 125 Nm for the 2.3L and 63 Nm for the 3.7L and 5.0L.
Use the 3.7L oil-pan procedure only for the relevant subframe alignment and refitting details here; oil-pan removal is a separate job.

verification.title: Confirm the required completion checks
verification.body: Complete the steering-column lower-shaft inspection and front-toe check. Confirm disturbed wiring, brake-line clips, mount vacuum lines where fitted and the dash seal are restored.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record the shaft-check outcome, final front-toe measurements and any adjustment, plus completion of dynamic-suspension recalibration where applicable.

guides.title: Remove and replace the rear subframe
guides.summary: Lower the supported rear subframe, transfer components when replacing it, and reinstall it with new required fasteners and final fluid and camber checks.
guides.introduction: The rear subframe bolts to the body, contributes structural support and provides mounting points for the rear suspension arms. It also carries the differential involved in this removal. Changing it disturbs suspension, driveline and potentially cooling-system connections, so the job combines several component procedures with controlled lowering and accurate repositioning.
guides.why: Subframe position affects suspension alignment and drivetrain operation. Index marks preserve installation references, while final camber checking verifies the resulting geometry. Several fasteners must be discarded during removal. Their replacements and specified tightening are essential because these joints secure suspension and driveline components.

when.summary: When the rear subframe requires removal or has been identified for replacement.
notes: Differential and upper-arm transfer are required when installing a new subframe.
Confirm optional suspension sensors and differential cooling connections before lowering.

prepare.title: Provide lifting and suspension capability
prepare.detail: Use the specified 300-OTC1585AE Powertrain Lift beneath the subframe. The workshop must also support the vehicle safely and carry out the linked halfshaft, toe-link, spring and stabilizer-bar procedures.

prepare.title: Prepare replacement fasteners
prepare.detail: Provide new driveshaft-to-pinion bolts and forward and rearward subframe bolts. Component transfer also requires replacement differential mounting bolts and the discarded upper-arm flag-bolt and nut. Use the same or equivalent quality and design.

prepare.title: Plan the completion work
prepare.detail: Have means to support the disconnected driveshaft, make installation reference marks, tighten fasteners correctly, check differential fluid level and check or adjust rear camber.

steps.title: Remove the suspension and axle prerequisites
steps.body: Follow [Rear Subframe](#/document/G1686636), using the linked component procedures. Remove both rear halfshafts, both toe links, both rear springs and the rear stabilizer bar, in that order. If dynamic suspension is fitted, remove both rear ride-height sensors.

steps.title: Separate the driveshaft correctly
steps.body: Index-mark the driveshaft and pinion flange, then remove and discard their connecting bolts. Support the driveshaft. Insert a screwdriver into the pinion-flange slot and pry the joint free. Do not pull on the driveshaft tube: that can damage the constant-velocity (CV) joint.

steps.title: Release the differential connections
steps.body: Disconnect the differential fluid-temperature sensor if fitted. On cooler-equipped vehicles, remove the return-line retaining clip and line, then the supply-line clip and line, positioning both lines aside. Disconnect the differential vent tube.

steps.title: Support and lower the subframe
steps.body: Index-mark the subframe on both sides and position the powertrain lift beneath it. Remove and discard the forward subframe bolts. Remove the bracket bolts and brackets, then remove and discard the rearward subframe bolts. Lower the assembly with the lift.

steps.title: Transfer components when fitting a new subframe
steps.body: Remove and discard the differential mounting bolts and transfer the differential. Remove and discard the upper-arm-to-frame flag-bolt and nut and transfer the arm. Install the transferred components with new fasteners and tighten as specified in the procedure.

steps.title: Raise, locate and secure the subframe
steps.body: Raise the subframe with the powertrain lift. Install new rearward bolts finger-tight, then fit the brackets and their bolts finger-tight. Install new forward bolts. Align the reference marks on both sides before tightening the bracket bolts, forward bolts and rearward bolts in the specified order.

steps.title: Restore differential and driveline connections
steps.body: Reconnect the vent and any fitted temperature sensor. Install the cooling supply line and retaining clip, then the return line and clip, where fitted. Align the driveshaft and pinion-flange index marks and install new connecting bolts to the specified torque.

steps.title: Reinstall the suspension components
steps.body: Install both ride-height sensors if fitted, followed by the stabilizer bar, rear springs, toe links and rear halfshafts. Use each component's installation procedure for its particular assembly and fastening requirements.

steps.title: Complete fluid and alignment checks
steps.body: Check differential fluid level using Differential Fluid Level Check. Check rear camber and adjust it if necessary using Rear Camber Adjustment. These checks remain required even when the removal index marks line up.

watchFor.title: A connection still attached during lowering
watchFor.body: Account for the vent, optional sensor, cooling lines and supported driveshaft before lowering the subframe.

watchFor.title: Discarded fasteners returning to service
watchFor.body: Keep discarded bolts separate from the bracket hardware and replacement fasteners so they cannot be installed accidentally.

watchFor.title: Position fixed before reference alignment
watchFor.body: Keep the rearward and bracket bolts finger-tight at the specified stage; align the marks before final tightening.

notes: Suspension fasteners must not be replaced with parts of lesser quality or a substitute design.
Index marks provide installation references; final rear camber still requires checking.

verification.title: Confirm installation and connections
verification.body: Verify reference-mark alignment, required new fasteners, specified tightening, restored vent and optional cooling connections, and completion of the component installation procedures.

verification.title: Record fluid and camber results
verification.body: Record the differential fluid-level check and rear camber result, including whether adjustment was necessary.
