searchTerms: passenger window will not go down

when.summary: Use this check when investigating the passenger switch or a complaint affecting one of its operating positions.
notes: Confirm that the fitted switch matches C624 and the illustrated contact arrangement before using these terminal connections.

The access illustrations show a left-hand-drive vehicle and the left door; the corresponding right-hand-drive and opposite-door access is described as similar. Use the passenger-specific retaining tab if separating the switch from its bezel.

prepare.title: Gather the testing and access tools
prepare.detail: Have an ohmmeter or self-powered test light and a trim-removal lever of the type illustrated in the switch access procedure. Use test leads that can contact individual switch terminals without spreading them or touching adjacent terminals.

prepare.title: Keep the contact test isolated
prepare.detail: Disconnect the switch from the vehicle harness before testing. Perform every contact check on the switch terminals with no external voltage applied. Do not bridge vehicle-harness terminals or use a powered vehicle circuit for an ohmmeter check.

prepare.title: Understand the result and the endpoint
prepare.detail: A closed circuit means the selected terminals have an electrical path between them; an open circuit means they do not. Use the instrument’s continuity or resistance indication to distinguish those states. There is no numerical resistance acceptance limit for this check. This procedure tests switch contacts; motor operation, vehicle wiring, power supply, illumination and window initialization require separate diagnosis.

prepare.title: Keep replacement conditional
prepare.detail: You can test the switch while it remains attached to the removed bezel—the trim surrounding the switch. Separate the passenger switch from the bezel only if installing a replacement. The driver-side arrangement with three retainers is a different replacement branch.

steps.title: Lift the switch and bezel assembly out of the door
steps.body:
Find the switch bezel in the front passenger door armrest. Using the illustrated trim-removal lever at the bezel edge, carefully lift the bezel and switch together, releasing the four retaining clips shown in the access illustration. Lift the assembly far enough to reach its underside while supporting it so the wiring does not carry its weight.

The access route is through this armrest bezel; the illustrated operation leaves the full door trim panel in place. See [front door window switch access](#/document/G1695936).

steps.title: Disconnect the electrical connector
steps.body:
With the lifted assembly supported, release the electrical connector’s retaining feature and disconnect it from the switch. Hold the connector housing rather than pulling on the wires. Place the disconnected switch and bezel where you can operate the rocker and reach the switch terminals.

Leave the vehicle connector disconnected throughout the contact tests.

steps.title: Identify C624 and establish the terminal orientation
steps.body:
Use the terminal drawing in the [passenger switch contact test](#/document/wiring-149-005). It shows the male terminal face on the switch, with six terminals in one horizontal row. With the connector outline oriented as drawn and its raised locating feature at the top, terminal 1 is at the left and terminal 6 at the right; terminals 2 and 3 are the next two positions after 1.

Make the measurements on that switch-side face. Do not transfer the same left-to-right view to the disconnected harness connector, which faces the opposite way.

Set up your ohmmeter or self-powered test light and confirm that it distinguishes leads touching from leads separated. I like to settle that little argument before asking the switch any questions.

steps.title: Test ordinary up between terminals 1 and 2
steps.body:
Connect one test lead to terminal 1 and the other to terminal 2. Move and hold the switch in its ordinary Up position, before the one-touch position.

Expected result: closed circuit. Record the reading, then release the switch. Keep the test leads on the selected terminals without allowing them to touch each other.

steps.title: Test ordinary down between terminals 1 and 3
steps.body:
Move the leads to terminals 1 and 3. Move and hold the switch in its ordinary Down position, before the one-touch position.

Expected result: closed circuit. Record the reading and release the switch.

steps.title: Check all three terminal pairs with the switch at rest
steps.body:
Leave the rocker fully released in its resting position. Check each pair separately:

- Terminals 1 and 2: open circuit.
- Terminals 1 and 3: open circuit.
- Terminals 2 and 3: open circuit.

Record all three results. Here, an open circuit is the correct result. A contact that stays connected when the switch is released deserves just as much attention as one that never connects.

steps.title: Test both one-touch positions
steps.body:
Move and hold the rocker in the One Touch Up position. The required state is a closed circuit connecting terminals 1, 2 and 3. With a two-lead instrument, check the pairs 1–2, 1–3 and 2–3 separately while holding that position; each should indicate closed.

Repeat those checks while holding the One Touch Down position. Again, terminals 1, 2 and 3 should be connected. Release the rocker after testing.

Keep these results separate from ordinary Up and Down. A successful ordinary-direction check does not establish that its one-touch position also works.

steps.title: Repeat any unexpected result before deciding
steps.body:
If a reading disagrees with the expected state, confirm the terminal numbers, check that both probes contact the intended terminals and verify that the rocker is in the requested ordinary, rest or one-touch position. For a rest test, make sure nothing is holding the rocker off center.

Repeat the same check and record whether the mismatch persists. If the indication changes while you hold the same position and maintain sound probe contact, record that variation too. Parts guessing is a remarkably expensive substitute for two steady probes.

steps.title: Choose replacement or further diagnosis
steps.body:
Compare the complete set of results with the [contact test](#/document/wiring-149-005). A repeatable mismatch means the switch does not meet the required contact behavior; use the passenger-switch replacement branch in the next step.

If every state passes, retain the switch and proceed to reassembly. If the window complaint remains afterward, continue through [window-system diagnosis](#/document/G1958066). Passing these contact checks does not establish that the motor is faulty.

steps.title: If replacing the passenger switch, release its retaining tab
steps.body:
Skip this step if you are reinstalling the tested switch.

With the assembly disconnected and out of the door, turn it over to reach the passenger switch beneath the bezel. Release the retaining tab identified in the passenger-side illustration, then withdraw the switch downward out of the bezel as shown. The passenger branch uses this tab; do not apply the driver-side three-retainer operation.

Install the matching replacement in the reverse direction and engage its retaining tab so the switch is held in the bezel. These are the relevant passenger replacement actions from [front door window switch removal and installation](#/document/G1695936).

steps.title: Reconnect the switch and seat the bezel
steps.body:
Remove all test leads. Support the switch and bezel above the armrest opening, reconnect the electrical connector and make sure its retaining feature engages.

Position the wiring clear of the bezel’s seating surfaces. Align the bezel and its four retaining clips with the door opening, then press the assembly back into place until the clips engage. Check that the bezel sits evenly and that the rocker can move and return freely.

steps.title: Check the assembled window function
steps.body:
With the assembly installed and the vehicle in its normal window-operating condition, check ordinary Up and Down, then one-touch Up and Down. Keep hands and objects clear of the moving glass. Recheck the function that prompted the work.

This is the completion check after reconnecting the switch. If the original problem remains, use the recorded contact results to guide the next diagnosis instead of treating a new switch—or a passing old one—as the end of the story.

diagnostics.finding: Terminals 1 and 2 remain open in ordinary Up.
diagnostics.meaning: The switch is not making the required ordinary-up contact.
diagnostics.next: Confirm terminals, probe contact and the ordinary Up position. If the result repeats, replace the passenger switch using the retaining-tab branch.

diagnostics.finding: Terminals 1 and 3 remain open in ordinary Down.
diagnostics.meaning: The switch is not making the required ordinary-down contact.
diagnostics.next: Confirm terminals, probe contact and the ordinary Down position. If the result repeats, replace the passenger switch.

diagnostics.finding: Any of the pairs 1–2, 1–3 or 2–3 is closed at rest.
diagnostics.meaning: The switch does not match the required released contact state.
diagnostics.next: Ensure the rocker is fully released and the probes are not bridging terminals. Repeat the affected pair; a persistent closed result supports switch replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Ordinary Up and Down pass, but one-touch does not connect terminals 1, 2 and 3.
diagnostics.meaning: The ordinary contacts pass while the required one-touch contact combination fails.
diagnostics.next: Confirm that you are holding the appropriate one-touch position and repeat all three pair checks in that direction. Replace the switch if the mismatch persists.

diagnostics.finding: A reading varies while the same switch position is held.
diagnostics.meaning: Probe contact or switch contact behavior is inconsistent.
diagnostics.next: Establish steady probe contact and repeat the check. If variation persists with the probes secure, record the affected position and treat the switch as failing that contact check.

diagnostics.finding: All required contact states pass, but the installed window complaint remains.
diagnostics.meaning: The switch passed the isolated checks; the remaining complaint needs investigation elsewhere in the window system.
diagnostics.next: Continue with [window-system diagnosis](#/document/G1958066), carrying forward the recorded switch results. Do not condemn the motor from this test alone.

diagnostics.finding: The fitted connector or switch positions do not match C624 and the illustrated arrangement.
diagnostics.meaning: These terminal expectations cannot be applied confidently to that component.
diagnostics.next: Resolve the component identification using the [C624 reference](#/document/connector-C624) before making a replacement decision.

verification.title: Keep a complete contact record
verification.body: Record the ordinary Up result for 1–2, ordinary Down for 1–3, all three rest pairs and all three pairs in each one-touch direction. Note any repeated mismatch or unstable result.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly
verification.body: Confirm that the electrical connector is retained, the bezel sits evenly with its clips engaged and the rocker moves and returns without interference. If replaced, confirm that the passenger switch is retained in its bezel.

verification.title: Confirm the original complaint after installation
verification.body: Check ordinary and one-touch operation with the assembly connected and installed. A remaining complaint calls for further window-system diagnosis, even when every isolated switch contact check passes.

watchFor.title: A reversed connector view changes the terminal identification
watchFor.body: The test drawing shows the switch’s male terminal face. Check its outline and orientation before counting terminals; the mating harness face must not be read as though it were the same view.

watchFor.title: Ordinary movement and one-touch movement are separate checks
watchFor.body: Hold the requested switch position for each reading. Moving into one-touch during an ordinary-direction test changes the contact combination and can confuse the result.

watchFor.title: Keep the probes electrically separate
watchFor.body: A probe touching an adjacent terminal, or two probes touching each other, can create a false closed-circuit indication. Reposition the leads before interpreting an unexpected result.

watchFor.title: Support the assembly during access
watchFor.body: Once the bezel clips release, support the assembly while disconnecting the connector. Do not let it hang from the wiring.

notes: For an unresolved connector-identification question, use the [C624 connector reference](#/document/connector-C624) before continuing.
The [general component-testing reference](#/document/wiring-149-001) is a next destination for additional testing guidance; the actionable switch checks here are those in diagram 5.

stepGroups.title: Access and identify the switch
stepGroups.summary: Release the bezel, unplug the switch and identify the component-side terminals.

stepGroups.title: Check every contact state
stepGroups.summary: Test ordinary movement, rest and both one-touch positions, then repeat any mismatch.

stepGroups.title: Choose the next action
stepGroups.summary: Interpret the results and replace the passenger switch only when warranted.

stepGroups.title: Reassemble and check operation
stepGroups.summary: Reconnect the switch, engage the bezel clips and revisit the original complaint.

guides.title: Test Micro, Ultra Micro and Power ISO relays
guides.summary: Check a relay’s coil, isolated contacts and powered changeover using the correct test for its relay family.
guides.introduction: A relay uses a small electrical coil to move a separate set of contacts. That lets a control circuit switch another electrical path. A click tells you the mechanism moved; the electrical checks establish whether the coil and contacts actually meet the required conditions.
guides.why: Relay families are not interchangeable test subjects. Their coil-resistance ranges differ, and the Micro ISO powered test uses different coil polarity from the Ultra Micro and Power ISO tests. Identifying the relay first prevents a plausible-looking test from answering the wrong question.

applicability.equipment: Only the matching Micro ISO, Ultra Micro ISO or Power ISO relay shown in the linked component tests; test the removed relay.

procedures.purpose: Use the matching component test and terminal identifiers.
Use the matching component test and terminal identifiers.
Use the matching component test and terminal identifiers.
Identify terminals, isolate the component and read the test correctly.

authoring.method: Codex diagram review and original explanation

when.summary: When circuit diagnosis calls for checking one of these relay types.

prepare.title: Identify the relay and test setup
prepare.detail: Remove the relay from the vehicle circuit and match its terminal layout to the exact relay-family diagram. Have an ohmmeter, voltmeter, suitable test leads and a controlled 12 V DC test supply. Do not bridge vehicle relay-socket terminals as a substitute for this bench test.

prepare.title: Keep resistance and powered tests separate
prepare.detail: Disconnect the ohmmeter before applying voltage. Set up the powered circuit with the supply off and follow the polarity for the identified relay family.

steps.title: Match the relay family and terminal face
steps.body: Open the [Micro ISO](#/document/wiring-149-009), [Ultra Micro ISO](#/document/wiring-149-010) or [Power ISO](#/document/wiring-149-011) test. Match the physical terminal orientation before using the numbers below; do not assign familiar generic relay numbers to this diagram.

steps.title: Measure the unpowered coil and contacts
steps.body:
With no external voltage applied, check every applicable row for that family. The coil should be within its stated resistance range, and the coil must remain electrically isolated from the listed contact terminals.

| Relay family | Coil pair | Coil resistance | Contact check | Coil-to-contact check |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Micro ISO | 1–2 | 66–106 ohms | 3–4 closed; 3–5 open | 1–3, 1–4 and 1–5 open |
| Ultra Micro ISO | 1–2 | 87–216 ohms | 3–5 open | 2–3 and 2–5 open |
| Power ISO | 1–2 | 51–125 ohms | 3–5 open | 2–3 and 2–5 open |

steps.title: Prepare for the powered check
steps.body: Remove the ohmmeter completely. Use voltage measurement for the next stage. Confirm the terminal identity again before connecting the test supply; the Micro coil’s ground terminal differs from the other two families.

steps.title: Run the Micro ISO changeover test
steps.body: For Micro ISO only, connect terminals 2 and 3 to 12 V DC and terminal 1 to ground. Measure between 5 and 1: the required result is 12 V. Then remove power from terminal 2 while keeping terminal 3 supplied. Measure between 4 and 1: the required result is again 12 V. Both stages are needed to check the changeover.

steps.title: Run the Ultra Micro or Power ISO test
steps.body: For Ultra Micro ISO or Power ISO only, connect terminals 3 and 1 to 12 V DC and terminal 2 to ground. Measure between 5 and 2: the required result is 12 V. Do not reuse the Micro ISO polarity for these relays.

steps.title: Decide from the electrical result
steps.body: A failed specified check calls for relay replacement after confirming the test setup. If the relay passes but the vehicle fault remains, continue diagnosis of its supply, control and load circuits. Remove the external supply and leads before refitting or replacing the relay.

diagnostics.finding: The relay clicks, but the required output voltage is absent.
diagnostics.meaning: Mechanical movement alone has not established a working contact path.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the exact family, supply and probe connections; repeat its powered test.

diagnostics.finding: The coil resistance is outside the range for that family.
diagnostics.meaning: The coil does not meet that relay’s specified check.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the relay identity and meter connection, then replace a confirmed failed relay.

diagnostics.finding: The relay passes every specified stage.
diagnostics.meaning: Its tested bench behavior is correct.
diagnostics.next: Continue the vehicle circuit diagnosis instead of assuming the entire system is healthy.

verification.title: Keep results by relay family
verification.body: Record the relay identity, coil resistance, unpowered contact states and powered voltage results. For Micro ISO, retain both changeover-stage results.

verification.title: Finish with the vehicle function
verification.body: Remove the test leads, reconnect the component securely and check the original complaint. If it remains, continue the relevant system diagnosis instead of treating the component check as proof that the entire circuit is healthy.

notes: These terminal assignments are specific to the illustrated relays. A similar housing or a familiar clicking sound does not establish an identical internal circuit.

guides.title: Test door-lock and memory buttons by their contact states
guides.summary: Check left, right and memory-equipped door switches without confusing their different common terminals.
guides.introduction: A door-lock switch makes a small electrical request when you press lock or unlock. A memory-equipped left switch adds separate seat-memory requests. The test checks those button contacts inside the disconnected switch; it does not drive a door latch or prove that a memory seat can move.
guides.why: Left, right and memory-equipped switches use different connector and terminal assignments. Keeping each variant separate prevents a good switch from failing a test that belongs to another door. Checking the released position also reveals a contact that remains closed after the button is let go.

applicability.equipment: C505 left door switch without memory, C541 left door switch with memory, or C605 right door switch, as fitted.

procedures.purpose: Use the matching component test and terminal identifiers.
Use the matching component test and terminal identifiers.
Use the matching component test and terminal identifiers.
Identify terminals, isolate the component and read the test correctly.

when.summary: When lock or memory-button diagnosis calls for an isolated switch check.

prepare.title: Isolate the part
prepare.detail: Disconnect the component from the vehicle harness before resistance or continuity testing. Probe the component terminals, not a live harness. Use appropriate leads that contact the terminals without spreading or damaging them.

prepare.title: Understand the meter reading
prepare.detail: A closed circuit means the selected contacts provide an electrical path. An open circuit means they do not. Follow the expected state for the selected position; neither result is automatically a fault.

prepare.title: Choose the correct variant
prepare.detail: Identify the door side and whether memory buttons are fitted. Match C505, C541 or C605 before selecting a terminal pair.

steps.title: Identify the switch and disconnect it
steps.body: Use the [left switch without memory](#/document/wiring-149-006), [left switch with memory](#/document/wiring-149-007) or [right switch](#/document/wiring-149-008) test. Disconnect the component from the harness before using the meter.

steps.title: Test lock and unlock separately
steps.body:
For each listed pair, check all three button states. “Rest” means no button is pressed.

| Switch | Pair | Rest | Lock | Unlock |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C505 left, no memory | 3 and 2 | Open | Open | Closed |
| C505 left, no memory | 4 and 3 | Open | Closed | Open |
| C541 left, memory | 1 and 3 | Open | Open | Closed |
| C541 left, memory | 2 and 3 | Open | Closed | Open |
| C605 right | 3 and 2 | Open | Open | Closed |
| C605 right | 1 and 2 | Open | Closed | Open |

steps.title: Check memory buttons only where fitted
steps.body: On C541, test 5 and 3 for Set 1, 6 and 3 for Set 2, and 7 and 3 for Set 3. Each pair must be open with its button released and closed while that corresponding Set button is pressed. These checks evaluate the buttons, not stored seat positions or the seat module.

steps.title: Repeat a questionable contact result
steps.body: Confirm the correct switch, terminal orientation and probe contact. Press and release the same button again and compare with the required states. Do not judge all of the switch’s functions from one successful button.

steps.title: Return to the system complaint
steps.body: Reconnect securely after testing. If the contacts pass but locking still fails, continue [locks and entry-system diagnosis](#/document/G1695898). A working request switch does not rule out a latch, supply, wiring or control problem.

diagnostics.finding: Lock works but unlock fails the contact check.
diagnostics.meaning: The two requests use distinct contact paths.
diagnostics.next: Verify the unlock pair for that exact switch and repeat the test.

diagnostics.finding: A memory button closes correctly, but the seat does not respond.
diagnostics.meaning: The button-contact test has passed; the seat system has not been tested.
diagnostics.next: Continue diagnosis of the fitted memory-seat system.

diagnostics.finding: A pair remains closed with the button released.
diagnostics.meaning: Its resting state is incorrect for this test.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the control has returned to rest and repeat with sound test connections.

verification.title: Record the complete result
verification.body: Write down the exact component, connector, terminal pair, control position and result. A single successful contact test does not establish that every function works.

verification.title: Finish with the vehicle function
verification.body: Remove the test leads, reconnect the component securely and check the original complaint. If it remains, continue the relevant system diagnosis instead of treating the component check as proof that the entire circuit is healthy.

notes: No external power is applied during these contact checks.

guides.title: Test the headlamp switch’s lighting requests
guides.summary: Remove the headlamp switch, check its lighting-request contacts at C205, and refit the switch and dash trim.
guides.introduction: The headlamp knob looks innocent enough for something that can send you shopping for perfectly good bulbs. I’ll walk you through checking what it actually asks the car to do, one contact at a time, before the parts cannon gets ideas. This guide applies to 2015 Mustangs with the 2.3L, 3.7L, 5.0L or 5.2L engine and the matching C205 headlamp switch; check the rear-fog control only when fitted.
guides.why: The switch tells the lighting system which mode you want by connecting particular terminals inside its housing. These connections are requests, so an open parking-lamp contact in the On position does not mean the parking lamps should be dark. I’ll compare each connection with its correct control position, keeping the switch’s behavior separate from what the rest of the car does with that request.

applicability.equipment: Headlamp switch C205 with the matching listed functions; test rear-fog controls only if fitted.

procedures.purpose: Primary procedure for the C205 male terminal orientation and all listed open/closed contact states.
Access and reassembly: remove the narrow trim, remove the finish-panel screw, position the panel aside, disconnect C205, release four switch tabs, and reverse those actions for installation.
Reference-only follow-up destination for general component-testing guidance; its internal procedure is not taught here.
Reference-only follow-up destination for resolving connector identification or continuing circuit diagnosis.

authoring.method: Codex diagram review and original explanation

when.summary: Use this procedure when lighting diagnosis calls for checking the headlamp switch’s internal request contacts.
notes: Check every listed knob position for each terminal pair, even if only one lighting mode prompted the investigation.
Use the rear-fog test only on a switch equipped with that control.

prepare.title: Gather the testing and access tools
prepare.detail: Have a non-marring trim tool, a suitable tool for the dash finish-panel screw, and either an ohmmeter or a self-powered test light. Use test leads that contact the switch terminals without spreading or damaging them.

prepare.title: Keep the measurement on the disconnected switch
prepare.detail: Disconnect C205 from the vehicle harness before using the ohmmeter or self-powered test light. Make these measurements across the switch’s own terminals, never across a powered harness connector. Support the dash finish panel while it is aside so its wiring does not carry its weight.

prepare.title: Understand the result and the test boundary
prepare.detail: A closed circuit provides an electrical path between the selected terminals; an open circuit does not. An ohmmeter distinguishes those states, while a self-powered test light illuminates through a closed path. The acceptance criteria here are open or closed, without a numerical resistance limit. This procedure covers the listed request contacts only; front-fog operation, headlamp leveling, illumination electronics, Hill Out and the rest of the lighting system need their own checks.

steps.title: Remove the narrow outboard dash trim
steps.body:
At the driver’s door opening, find the narrow trim panel along the outboard side of the lower dash, below the round side vent and beside the larger lower panel. Use the non-marring trim tool to release and remove this narrow panel. Keep the tool against the trim being released so the adjacent finished surfaces do not become collateral damage.

This is the first access operation in [Headlamp Switch](#/document/G1694120).

steps.title: Remove the finish-panel screw and move the panel aside
steps.body:
With the narrow trim removed, locate the screw at the lower outboard mounting tab of the left-hand dash finish panel. This is the panel surrounding the headlamp switch beneath the rectangular dash vent.

Remove that screw and retain it for refitting. Move the finish panel aside far enough to reach the back of the switch, supporting the panel as you work.

steps.title: Disconnect C205, release four tabs and remove the switch
steps.body:
Disconnect the electrical connector from the back of the headlamp switch, handling the connector housing rather than pulling its wires.

Release the four retaining tabs around the switch body. With the tabs disengaged, slide the switch out through the front of the finish panel. The removal illustration identifies the order as connector first, four tabs second, switch removal third.

steps.title: Orient the switch terminals before counting
steps.body:
Use the male terminal-face drawing in the [component test](#/document/wiring-149-012). With the drawing’s raised locating shape at the top, the upper row runs from terminal 1 at the left to terminal 8 at the right; the lower row runs from 9 at the left to 16 at the right.

Terminal 4 is therefore the fourth position from the left in the upper row. Keep this switch-side view consistent throughout the checks; looking into the disconnected harness connector can reverse your interpretation. If the connector does not match this layout, stop and resolve its identity using the [C205 reference](#/document/connector-C205) before probing.

steps.title: Connect the tester to the first pair
steps.body:
Set the ohmmeter to resistance or continuity, or use the self-powered test light. Connect one lead to switch terminal 4 and the other to terminal 12 for the first check. Contact only the intended terminals and keep the probes from bridging adjacent terminals.

For the remaining checks, terminal 4 stays common: move the other lead to the terminal named in each row. I’ll keep calling the results open and closed so the same instructions work with either testing tool.

steps.title: Check the four lighting-mode request contacts
steps.body:
For each terminal pair below, move the knob through Off, Park, On and Auto, recording the result at every position. Reposition the test lead only after identifying the next terminal.

| Request contact | Switch terminals | Off | Park | On | Auto |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Headlamp | 4 and 12 | Open | Open | Closed | Open |
| Autolamp | 4 and 13 | Open | Open | Open | Closed |
| Parking lamps | 4 and 11 | Open | Closed | Open | Open |
| Off | 4 and 10 | Closed | Open | Open | Open |

These are individual request contacts. In particular, the parking-lamp contact must be open in On, and the headlamp contact must be open in Auto. Those readings are deliberate; don’t let the labels talk you into condemning a good switch.

steps.title: Check the Dim + contact
steps.body:
Connect the tester between terminals 4 and 6. With the Dim + control off, expect an open circuit. Operate Dim + and expect a closed circuit.

Record both states. A successful operated-state reading alone does not establish that the contact opens correctly when the control is off.

steps.title: Check the Dim − contact
steps.body:
Move the tester to terminals 4 and 3. With the Dim − control off, expect an open circuit. Operate Dim − and expect a closed circuit.

Record the off and operated results separately from the Dim + results.

steps.title: Check the rear-fog contact if fitted
steps.body:
If the switch has a rear-fog control, connect the tester between terminals 4 and 2. Expect an open circuit with that control off and a closed circuit with rear fog selected.

If the control is not fitted, mark this check not applicable and continue.

steps.title: Confirm any mismatch before deciding what to repair
steps.body:
For an unexpected reading, check the terminal numbering, the exact knob or button position, and whether both probes are actually contacting their terminals. Repeat the same pair in every state specified for that function.

Record the pair, position, expected state and actual state. A poor probe connection can impersonate an open contact with irritating conviction. Use the diagnostic branches below to decide whether the switch has failed a listed check or whether diagnosis needs to continue elsewhere.

steps.title: Refit the switch and reconnect C205
steps.body:
Remove all test leads. Insert the tested switch, or a matching replacement if the confirmed fault calls for one, into the finish-panel opening. Seat it until all four retaining tabs engage and the switch is retained in the panel.

Reconnect C205 to the back of the switch and confirm that the connector is fully engaged. This starts the reverse installation sequence in [Headlamp Switch](#/document/G1694120).

steps.title: Return the finish panel and reinstall its screw
steps.body: Bring the left-hand dash finish panel back into position, making sure the switch wiring is clear of the panel’s seating surfaces. Seat the panel and reinstall the screw in its lower outboard mounting tab.

steps.title: Refit the narrow trim panel
steps.body: Return the narrow outboard trim panel to its original position beside the lower dash. Align its attachments and press it into place. Check that the edges sit correctly against the neighboring trim and that the finish panel and switch are secure.

steps.title: Check the original lighting concern
steps.body:
With the switch connected and the trim secured, operate the controls involved in the original concern and confirm their behavior. This is a completion check after reassembly, separate from the disconnected contact measurements.

If every listed contact passed but the lighting concern remains, continue the relevant lighting-system diagnosis. The switch has answered its part of the question; throwing another one at the dash is an expensive way to ask it again.

diagnostics.finding: A contact remains open where the table requires closed.
diagnostics.meaning: The required electrical path has not been demonstrated. Incorrect terminal selection or poor probe contact can produce the same reading.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the male terminal-face orientation, terminal pair and control position, then repeat the check with secure probe contact. If it remains open in the required closed state, the switch fails that contact test; arrange repair or replacement of the matching switch.

diagnostics.finding: A contact remains closed where the table requires open.
diagnostics.meaning: The measured path does not match the required switch state.
diagnostics.next: Check that the probes are not bridging terminals, confirm the selected pair and repeat the specified positions. A persistent mismatch means the switch fails that contact test.

diagnostics.finding: The parking-lamp contact is open in On, or the headlamp contact is open in Auto.
diagnostics.meaning: Both are expected readings for those particular contacts.
diagnostics.next: Continue through the complete matrix. Do not use the exterior lamps’ current behavior to override the contact table.

diagnostics.finding: Dim +, Dim − or the fitted rear-fog control does not change from open to closed when operated.
diagnostics.meaning: That control’s listed contact path has not passed its two-state check.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the pair: 4 and 6 for Dim +, 4 and 3 for Dim −, or 4 and 2 for rear fog. Repeat off and operated states with secure probe contact. Treat a confirmed mismatch as a failed switch contact.

diagnostics.finding: The Auto contact passes, but automatic lighting still behaves incorrectly.
diagnostics.meaning: The switch provides the tested Auto request between terminals 4 and 13.
diagnostics.next: Continue diagnosis of the automatic-lighting system and its other inputs. Repeating this successful contact check will not establish why the vehicle is responding incorrectly.

diagnostics.finding: Every applicable contact passes, but the original lighting concern remains.
diagnostics.meaning: The switch matches the listed contact states. The remaining fault has not been located by this component test.
diagnostics.next: Continue the appropriate lighting-circuit diagnosis. Use the [C205 connector reference](#/document/connector-C205) or [general component-testing reference](#/document/wiring-149-001) as follow-up destinations when needed.

diagnostics.finding: The switch face or fitted controls do not match the test layout.
diagnostics.meaning: The terminal assignments or function list cannot safely be assumed to apply to that switch.
diagnostics.next: Stop these measurements and resolve the switch configuration and connector identification using the [C205 reference](#/document/connector-C205) before continuing.

verification.title: Confirm the measurement record is complete
verification.body: Record all four knob positions for terminal pairs 4–12, 4–13, 4–11 and 4–10; record off and operated states for 4–6 and 4–3, plus 4–2 when rear fog is fitted. Identify any confirmed mismatch explicitly.

verification.title: Confirm reassembly
verification.body: Check that the test leads are removed, all four switch retaining tabs engage, C205 is connected, the finish-panel screw is installed, and both trim panels sit securely.

verification.title: Record the vehicle-level outcome
verification.body: Confirm whether the original lighting concern is resolved after reassembly. Keep that observation separate from the contact-test result so a passing switch is not mistaken for proof that the whole lighting system is healthy.

watchFor.title: A mirrored connector view
watchFor.body: Count terminals using the male switch-terminal face. Do not transfer left and right directly from a view into the harness connector.

watchFor.title: Probe damage or accidental bridging
watchFor.body: Use leads that fit the terminals without forcing them. Keep each lead on its selected terminal and clear of neighboring terminals.

watchFor.title: Expected open contacts
watchFor.body: Judge each reading against its exact row and control position. A lamp-related contact does not have to remain closed whenever exterior lamps are operating.

watchFor.title: A panel hanging from its wiring
watchFor.body: Support the finish panel while reaching the switch connector and retaining tabs. Disconnect the connector by its housing, not by pulling the wire bundle.

notes: The common terminal for every listed test is C205 terminal 4.
Keep a complete record of the tested contacts; passing one function does not establish that the other contacts work.

stepGroups.title: Reach and remove the switch
stepGroups.summary: Remove the access trim, move the finish panel aside and disconnect the switch before releasing its four tabs.

stepGroups.title: Measure the request contacts
stepGroups.summary: Orient C205, check every applicable control state and confirm any unexpected reading.

stepGroups.title: Reassemble and check operation
stepGroups.summary: Secure the switch, reconnect C205, refit the panels and check the original lighting concern.

guides.title: Test power-seat switch contacts for the failed direction
guides.summary: Check the electrical paths for seat travel, height, tilt and the applicable left-seat lumbar control.
guides.introduction: The seat switch selects an electrical path for each direction of movement. Forward and rearward, for example, use different contact combinations. Testing the disconnected switch can identify a contact problem without assuming that an unresponsive seat must have a failed motor.
guides.why: Two connections are checked for each seat movement. Passing one of them is not enough. Left and right switches also use different terminal assignments, and the left eight-way switch adds a lumbar-control branch that does not belong to a six-way-only test.

applicability.equipment: Matching left six-way or eight-way power-seat switch C352, or right six-way power-seat switch C3190. Excludes manual-seat controls.

procedures.purpose: Use the matching component test and terminal identifiers.
Use the matching component test and terminal identifiers.

Identify terminals, isolate the component and read the test correctly.

when.summary: When seat-system diagnosis calls for testing the direction switch itself.

prepare.title: Isolate the part
prepare.detail: Disconnect the component from the vehicle harness before resistance or continuity testing. Probe the component terminals, not a live harness. Use appropriate leads that contact the terminals without spreading or damaging them.

prepare.title: Understand the meter reading
prepare.detail: A closed circuit means the selected contacts provide an electrical path. An open circuit means they do not. Follow the expected state for the selected position; neither result is automatically a fault.

prepare.title: Establish terminal identity before probing
prepare.detail: Use the fitted switch’s reliable terminal identifiers and matching connector information. The required test terminals include 9 and 10. Do not infer their locations from an eight-cavity picture or count positions on a different switch. If terminal identity cannot be established, obtain the correct component identification before testing.

prepare.title: Use controlled switch access
prepare.detail: Follow the front-seat switch access procedure for the recline handle, side shield, knob and switch retainers. Keep the test confined to the seat control switch; do not probe nearby restraint connectors.

steps.title: Choose the exact seat-control branch
steps.body: Identify left C352 or right C3190 and the fitted functions. Open the [left six-way](#/document/wiring-149-002), [left eight-way](#/document/wiring-149-003) or [right six-way](#/document/wiring-149-004) test. The table below gives terminal identities, not physical probe locations.

steps.title: Access the isolated switch
steps.body: Follow [seat-switch access](#/document/G1695513), disconnecting the switch electrical connector. Check the component’s terminal identity before attaching an ohmmeter or the specified self-powered tester. The [C352](#/document/connector-C352) and [C3190](#/document/connector-C3190) assignments help identify the electrical functions; connector shape and orientation still must match the fitted part.

steps.title: Check both paths for each movement
steps.body:
Hold the selected movement while testing each listed pair separately. Every pair shown must read closed in that operating position.

| Movement | Left C352 pairs | Right C3190 pairs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Forward | 9–5 and 7–6 | 8–2 and 10–1 |
| Rearward | 9–6 and 7–5 | 8–1 and 10–2 |
| Height up | 9–8 and 7–10 | 8–9 and 10–7 |
| Height down | 9–10 and 7–8 | 8–7 and 10–9 |
| Tilt up | 9–1 and 7–2 | 8–6 and 10–5 |
| Tilt down | 9–2 and 7–1 | 8–5 and 10–6 |

steps.title: Add the left eight-way lumbar checks
steps.body: For the applicable left eight-way switch only, the position labeled Inflate requires closed paths at 9–4 and 7–3. The position labeled Deflate requires closed paths at 9–3 and 7–4. Treat these as switch-position labels; this contact test does not establish the health of the complete lumbar mechanism.

steps.title: Interpret the failed direction
steps.body: If a movement fails, repeat both of its contact checks with sound probe connections and confirmed terminal identity. A pass establishes those switch contacts only. It does not test motor load, seat-track movement, the vehicle power feed or the seat’s other controls.

steps.title: Restore the switch and check operation
steps.body: Remove the leads and reinstall the switch, knob, side shield and handle using the access procedure. Reconnect securely and verify the original movement complaint. Continue the seat-system diagnosis if a correctly functioning switch does not resolve the symptom.

diagnostics.finding: One of a movement’s two pairs remains open.
diagnostics.meaning: That movement has not passed its complete switch-contact check.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the pair and switch position, then repeat both paths.

diagnostics.finding: The required terminals cannot be identified reliably.
diagnostics.meaning: The component identity or connector geometry is unresolved.
diagnostics.next: Stop probing and establish the correct fitted-switch terminal identification.

diagnostics.finding: All tested contacts pass but the seat remains stationary.
diagnostics.meaning: The switch test has not found the cause in those contacts.
diagnostics.next: Continue diagnosis of the fitted seat system, its supply, wiring and driven mechanism.

verification.title: Record the complete result
verification.body: Write down the exact component, connector, terminal pair, control position and result. A single successful contact test does not establish that every function works.

verification.title: Finish with the vehicle function
verification.body: Remove the test leads, reconnect the component securely and check the original complaint. If it remains, continue the relevant system diagnosis instead of treating the component check as proof that the entire circuit is healthy.

notes: A left-switch diagram is not a right-switch pin-placement template. Keep vehicle wiring disconnected throughout the contact tests.

guides.title: Replace the accessory-drive idler pulley on the 2.3L EcoBoost
guides.summary: Replace the 2.3L accessory-drive idler, following the separate belt-removal sequence and checking both belts after refitting.
guides.introduction: The idler is the freely rotating pulley that guides and supports the accessory belt along its route. It is separate from the tensioner, which is the component moved to release belt tension. On the 2.3L EcoBoost, reaching the idler means dealing with two belts in the correct sequence: the A/C compressor belt comes off before the main accessory belt.
guides.why: Taking the belt load off first makes the pulley attachment accessible. The central bolt holds the idler in position while the pulley rotates around its bearing. Correct fastening and final belt seating matter together: a securely mounted pulley cannot guide a belt correctly if that belt is sitting outside its intended grooves.

when.summary: When inspection or diagnosis establishes that the 2.3L accessory-drive idler needs replacement.
notes: A belt-drive noise does not by itself identify the idler as the faulty component. Confirm which pulley or belt needs attention before replacing parts.

prepare.title: Plan the two-belt access sequence
prepare.detail: Have the full A/C belt and accessory-belt procedures available. The A/C belt uses its own removal and installation method, including the specified installation aid; it is not released by the main belt tensioner.

prepare.title: Prepare the fastening tools
prepare.detail: Use suitable access tools and a torque wrench capable of 10.5 Nm. Identify the idler’s central bolt in its component illustration before removing it.

steps.title: Remove the separate A/C compressor belt
steps.body: Follow the [2.3L A/C compressor-belt procedure](#/document/G1688221), including its access steps and stretchy-belt-tool method. Keep the separate belt installation instructions with the job so their hand-rotation and seating checks are not missed later.

steps.title: Release the main accessory belt
steps.body: Use the [accessory-drive belt procedure](#/document/G1688219). Rotate its tensioner counter clockwise and remove the belt. The tensioner releases belt tension; the idler is the different pulley being replaced.

steps.title: Remove and refit the idler
steps.body: Remove the central retaining bolt and the idler pulley identified in the [idler illustration](#/document/G2086104). Refit the pulley and its central bolt, tightening the bolt to 93 lb.in (10.5 Nm). This value belongs to the idler attachment, not to the tensioner mounting.

steps.title: Restore the belts and verify their seating
steps.body: Complete the linked belt installation sequence. The A/C belt instructions temporarily position the main belt away from the crankshaft pulley, then reinstall it after the A/C belt is fitted. Perform the specified hand-rotation checks, remove the installation aid and confirm that each belt is correctly seated on all of its pulleys.

watchFor.title: Confusing the idler with the tensioner
watchFor.body: The idler’s central fastening value is different from the mounting requirements of the tensioner assembly. Use the component picture to keep their jobs separate.

watchFor.title: A belt sitting outside its grooves
watchFor.body: Inspect the belt path after installation. The required seating checks include both the A/C belt and the main accessory belt.

verification.title: Confirm the idler attachment
verification.body: Confirm the idler’s central bolt has been tightened to its specified value and the pulley is installed in its illustrated position.

verification.title: Complete both belt procedures
verification.body: Confirm the installation aid has been removed, the prescribed hand-rotation checks are complete and both belts are correctly seated.

procedures.purpose: Idler-pulley attachment illustration, removal/reverse installation and central-bolt tightening.
2.3L accessory-belt removal and installation, including the A/C belt prerequisite, tensioner direction and final seating check.
Separate 2.3L A/C belt access, stretchy-belt removal, installation aid and hand-rotation seating checks.

authoring.method: Codex editorial review of original diagrams and local corroborating procedures

guides.title: Replace the output shaft seal on the 5.2L 3160 manual transmission
guides.summary: Service the transmission's rear output seal with dedicated installers and inspect the speed-sensor tone wheel before restoring the output flange.
guides.introduction: The output shaft carries transmission torque toward the rear driveshaft through its flange. A seal at the rear housing keeps transmission oil inside around this rotating connection. Replacing that seal requires removing the flange, discarding the old seal and inspecting the nearby speed-sensor tone wheel. This job applies to the 3160 six-speed manual transmission used with the 5.2L engine.
guides.why: The seal and tone wheel have different replacement rules: always renew the removed seal, while replacing the tone wheel only if it is damaged. Fit the tone wheel before installing the seal. The specified installer combination supports and aligns the new seal while it is fitted into the rear housing.

when.summary: When an output-shaft seal repair is required or the seal has been removed during related work.
notes: Confirm the transmission before selecting parts and procedures; its identification tag is on the top right-hand side.

prepare.title: Specified installers and replacement parts
prepare.detail: Have installer 205-199 (T83T-3132-A1), output shaft seal installer 308-959 and a new seal. A replacement tone wheel is needed if inspection finds damage.

prepare.title: Flange-service capability
prepare.detail: Be equipped to complete the exact output-flange removal and installation procedure, including its specified renewed parts and tightening requirements. Keep the seal-installer arrangement and the same-transmission assembly sequence available while reassembling.

steps.title: Remove the output shaft flange
steps.body: Follow the [Transmission Output Shaft Flange procedure](#/document/G1805399) to gain access to the seal. Keep that procedure available for the later flange installation.

steps.title: Remove and discard the seal
steps.body: Remove the output shaft seal and discard it. The replacement requirement applies even if the removed seal appears intact.

steps.title: Inspect the speed-sensor tone wheel
steps.body: Remove the speed-sensor tone wheel and inspect it for damage. Use a new tone wheel if damage is found; otherwise retain the serviceable wheel. Refit the tone wheel before fitting the output seal, as shown in the [same-transmission assembly sequence](#/document/G1849280).

steps.title: Install the new seal with its dedicated tools
steps.body: Place the new seal on the specified combination of 205-199 and 308-959, using the arrangement pictured in the [seal procedure](#/document/G1794237). Use that tool combination to install the seal into the rear housing. Keep the tool aligned with the opening.

steps.title: Restore the output flange
steps.body: With the tone wheel and new seal installed, complete the [output-flange installation](#/document/G1805399). Follow that procedure’s parts-renewal and tightening requirements rather than treating the flange as an ordinary bolt-on cover.

watchFor.title: Reusing the removed seal
watchFor.body: A removed output seal is discarded even if it appears intact. Have the replacement ready before reassembly.

watchFor.title: Omitting the tone wheel
watchFor.body: The tone wheel belongs ahead of the seal in this installation sequence. Record its inspection result and refit the serviceable or replacement wheel before installing the seal.

diagnostics.finding: Damage is found on the removed speed-sensor tone wheel.
diagnostics.meaning: The tone wheel meets the stated replacement condition.
diagnostics.next: Install a new tone wheel as part of the completed reassembly.

verification.title: Record the tone-wheel decision
verification.body: Record whether inspection found damage and whether a replacement was required.

verification.title: Confirm completion of the installation sequence
verification.body: Confirm the tone wheel is refitted, a new seal is installed with the specified tools and the complete output-flange installation has been finished.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L 3160 output shaft seal removal, mandatory seal replacement, tone-wheel inspection and specified installation tooling.
5.2L 3160 output shaft flange removal for seal access and flange installation after seal work.
Same TR3160 assembly sequence corroborating tone-wheel refitting before output-seal installation and output-flange restoration.

authoring.method: Codex editorial review of original diagrams and local corroborating procedures

guides.title: Rebuild the 5.2L 3160 manual transmission extension housing
guides.summary: Strip the extension-housing subassembly, inspect its shift-shaft bearings and rebuild the specified bearing, reverse-gear and sensor components.
guides.introduction: The aluminum extension housing forms the rear section of the 3160 six-speed manual transmission. It carries shaft-support bearings, shift-shaft bearings, seals and sensor components, along with the reverse idler gear and its pin. The idler participates in reversing output-shaft rotation. This is specialist bench work on an already accessible subassembly, rather than a complete transmission removal and installation job.
guides.why: The inspection distinguishes the shift-shaft bearings from the separately removed output-shaft and countershaft bearings. Damage to a shift-shaft bearing requires a new extension housing. Keeping those parts distinct prevents a rebuild from retaining a housing that the inspection has already ruled out.

when.summary: When transmission repair requires extension-housing disassembly or its shift-shaft bearings need inspection.
notes: This procedure begins at the subassembly stage; transmission removal and housing separation require their own procedures.
The transmission fluid temperature sensor is handled only if fitted.

prepare.title: Provide transmission bench-work capability
prepare.detail: Arrange a clean work area and the capability to handle seals, bearings and retaining rings without damaging the housing. Use the [extension-housing procedure](#/document/G1849275) for the illustrated component locations.

prepare.title: Keep components identifiable
prepare.detail: Distinguish the output-shaft bearing and ring from the countershaft bearing and ring. Have suitable torque equipment for the reverse gear pin bolt and sensor fasteners.

steps.title: Remove the fitted sensors
steps.body: If equipped, remove the transmission fluid temperature (TFT) sensor. Then remove the speed-sensor bolt and speed sensor. The temperature-sensor branch is conditional; the speed sensor is part of the main sequence.

steps.title: Remove the seals and tone wheel
steps.body: Remove the output shaft seal, then the tone wheel, followed by the manual shaft seal. Discard the removed output seal. Inspect the tone wheel and replace it if damaged, following the [matching output-seal procedure](#/document/G1794237). The tone wheel belongs to the speed-sensing arrangement; keep it identifiable for the later transmission assembly stage.

steps.title: Remove the reverse idler components
steps.body: Remove the bolt, reverse gear pin and reverse idler gear. Keep these components together so the pin and its fastening can be identified during assembly.

steps.title: Remove the shaft-support bearings
steps.body: Remove the retaining ring and output-shaft bearing first. Then remove the retaining ring and countershaft bearing. These are separate from the shift-shaft bearings inspected inside the housing.

steps.title: Clean and inspect the shift-shaft bearings
steps.body: Clean the shift-shaft bearings and inspect them for damage, using the highlighted locations in the illustration. If damage is found, install a new extension housing; the specified repair decision is housing replacement.

steps.title: Install the bearings and reverse gear
steps.body: Install the countershaft bearing and retaining ring, followed by the output-shaft bearing and retaining ring. Install the reverse idler gear, reverse gear pin and bolt. Tighten that bolt to 106 lb.in (12 Nm).

steps.title: Fit the manual shaft seal and sensors
steps.body: Install the manual shaft seal. Install the speed sensor and tighten its bolt to 71 lb.in (8 Nm). If fitted, install the TFT sensor and tighten it to 97 lb.in (11 Nm).

steps.title: Continue through the complete transmission assembly sequence
steps.body: The completed housing is a subassembly. Follow [3160 transmission assembly](#/document/G1849280) to install the housing and its remaining transmission components in order. That sequence fits the tone wheel after the housing is installed, then installs a new output seal with tools 205-199 and 308-959, followed by the output flange, washer and new nut. Keep those later operations in that sequence rather than fitting the seal prematurely on the loose housing.

watchFor.title: Shift-shaft bearing damage
watchFor.body: Do not confuse this finding with damage limited to a removable shaft-support bearing. The specified response to damaged shift-shaft bearings is a new housing.

watchFor.title: Different fastener torques
watchFor.body: The reverse gear pin bolt, speed-sensor bolt and optional TFT sensor have different tightening values.

notes: The output seal and tone wheel are fitted during the later transmission assembly stage. Completing the housing’s bench work is the handoff to that sequence.

diagnostics.finding: Damage found while cleaning and inspecting a shift-shaft bearing.
diagnostics.meaning: The extension housing requires replacement under this procedure.
diagnostics.next: Install a new extension housing before continuing the subassembly build.

verification.title: Check the specified assembly work
verification.body: Confirm that both shaft-support bearings and retaining rings, the reverse idler components, manual shaft seal and applicable sensors have been installed.

verification.title: Record the housing decision
verification.body: Record the shift-shaft bearing inspection result and whether the housing was retained or replaced. Before the complete transmission is finished, confirm that the later assembly sequence has restored the tone wheel, new output seal and output flange.

procedures.purpose: Extension-housing bench disassembly and assembly for the 5.2L 3160 six-speed manual transmission.
Complete 3160 transmission assembly, including housing installation followed by tone wheel, new output seal and flange restoration.
Matching output-seal renewal requirement, tone-wheel inspection and the dedicated seal-installer arrangement.
