guides.title: Adjust the parking brake cable
guides.summary: Set parking brake cable tension by measuring rear caliper lever clearance, cycling the mechanism and making the final adjustment.
guides.introduction: The parking brake cable transfers movement from the parking brake control to mechanical levers on the rear calipers. The adjustment nut changes cable tension, which changes where those levers sit relative to their stops. This job establishes that setting through measured clearances; it does not, by itself, diagnose the cause of poor parking brake operation.
guides.why: The procedure uses an initial setting followed by repeated application and release before the final adjustment. Moving the mechanism through its working travel makes that sequence important. Lever clearance is the adjustment reference, so tightening the nut by feel cannot establish the specified result.

when.summary: When the parking brake cable setting requires adjustment.
notes: Use the measured lever clearances to establish the setting rather than judging cable tension alone.

prepare.title: Arrange safe underside access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist and the specified lifting points, identified by stamped triangles. Position adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering components. Never work underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare to measure the levers
prepare.detail: Have a feeler gauge and suitable access to the adjustment nut and both caliper lever stops. The illustrated adjustment nut and lever gap identify the two places involved in the setting.

steps.title: Position the vehicle
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a hoist using the linked lifting procedure. Establish secure access before working at the cable adjustment mechanism.

steps.title: Establish the initial clearance
steps.body: Tighten the parking brake cable adjustment nut until one or both caliper levers are 2.0 mm away from their stops. Use the feeler gauge to measure the gap.

steps.title: Cycle the parking brake
steps.body: Fully apply and release the parking brake 5 times. Complete each application and release before beginning the next, retaining this stage between the initial and final settings.

steps.title: Make the final adjustment
steps.body: After the cycling stage, tighten the adjustment nut until one or both caliper levers are 1.0 mm away from their stops. Measure again with the feeler gauge; the initial clearance is not the finished setting.

watchFor.title: Unnecessary tightening to match both sides
watchFor.body: The specified condition is one or both levers at the stated clearance. Do not continue tightening solely to make the opposite lever match.

notes: The vehicle's emergency jack is intended for changing a deflated tire, not for providing access for this adjustment.

verification.title: Confirm and record the final setting
verification.body: Confirm that one or both lever gaps measure 1.0 mm after the prescribed cycling and adjustment sequence. Record the measured result and completion of the 5 full applications and releases.

procedures.purpose: Complete parking brake cable adjustment sequence, including initial clearance, cycling and final clearance.
Correct lifting points, hoist positioning and vehicle-support precautions.

applicability.equipment: Rear calipers with parking-brake operating levers; excludes the separate SVT parking-brake shoe arrangement

guides.title: Remove and install the side curtain airbag
guides.summary: Depower the restraint system, remove the roof-mounted curtain assembly and reinstall it with correct attachment, connector locking and repowering.
guides.introduction: The side curtain airbag is a roof-mounted part of the supplemental restraint system (SRS). The restraints control module (RCM) monitors sensor inputs and commands the appropriate restraint components when it determines that deployment is needed. This repair removes the curtain assembly from behind the headliner, then restores its mounting and electrical connection. Its installed position matters because the curtain must deploy correctly along the roofline.
guides.why: This work controls two serious risks: accidental deployment during repair and incorrect deployment during a crash. Depowering protects the repair operation, while sound roof structure, correct curtain orientation and the specified fastening sequence protect its installed function. Connector locking also matters electrically; a connector can make contact while its assurance tab remains incompletely seated.

when.summary: When side curtain airbag removal or replacement is required and SRS service capability is available.
notes: An illuminated airbag warning indicator alone does not establish that the curtain assembly needs replacement.

prepare.title: Arrange restraint-system capability
prepare.detail: The person doing the work must be able to follow the complete SRS depowering and repowering procedures and handle deployable-component connectors correctly.

prepare.title: Prepare access and fastening information
prepare.detail: Have the headliner procedure, suitable screw and retainer tools, and torque equipment. Use the numbered installation diagram to identify the screw positions and tightening sequence.

prepare.title: Allow for mounting repairs
prepare.detail: Installation requires inspection of the roofline. Damaged sheet metal must be restored to its original condition and structural integrity, damaged fasteners renewed and foreign material removed.

steps.title: Depower the SRS
steps.body: Complete [SRS Depowering](#/document/G1696297) before disturbing the curtain connection. Follow the full procedure precisely; its requirements govern safe disconnection and later reconnection.

steps.title: Remove the headliner
steps.body: Follow [Headliner](#/document/G1692615) to expose the curtain and its attachments. This provides access to the connector, screw groups and retainers without pulling against concealed fixings.

steps.title: Disconnect and release the screw groups
steps.body: In the order shown in [Side Curtain Airbag](#/document/G1696310), disconnect the electrical connector and remove the screws, then remove the next screw group. Note the unique installation instructions for these locations before proceeding.

steps.title: Release the retainers and T-tab
steps.body: Remove the A-pillar pin-type retainers, disengage the retainer and move the curtain away from the A-pillar. Disengage the remaining pin-type retainers, remove the final pin-type retainer, then slide the assembly forward and out to disengage its T-tab from the sheet metal.

steps.title: Prepare the roofline for installation
steps.body: Inspect the mounting area and resolve roofline damage before fitting the curtain. Remove foreign material and replace damaged fasteners. Check the curtain orientation so it is not twisted 360° between attachment points.

steps.title: Refit and tighten in sequence
steps.body: Reverse removal, following the installation diagram for attachment and screw positions. Keep the SRS depowered before reconnecting the component. Tighten screws 1 and 2 to 106 lb.in (12 Nm), then screws 3 through 7 to 80 lb.in (9 Nm), in the illustrated sequence.

steps.title: Restore trim and repower
steps.body: Complete headliner reinstallation and then follow [SRS Repowering](#/document/G1696298). Repowering is the final required phase of the curtain installation.

watchFor.title: Roofline damage or a twisted curtain
watchFor.body: Either can interfere with correct deployment. Resolve structural damage and curtain orientation before closing the headliner.

watchFor.title: Reconnection while powered
watchFor.body: The restraint system must be depowered before the component is reconnected; incorrect handling can cause accidental deployment.

notes: The numbered installation diagram is essential for identifying the two screw groups; do not infer their positions from the removal view.

diagnostics.finding: The deployable-component connector is attached, but its Connector Position Assurance (CPA) tab is not fully seated.
diagnostics.meaning: The connector pins can make contact while the component's shorting bars remain applied. The RCM can detect resistance below threshold and illuminate the airbag warning indicator.
diagnostics.next: Treat connector seating as a diagnostic consideration rather than proof of a failed curtain. Follow SRS depowering before correcting the connection, then complete the prescribed repowering process.

verification.title: Check installation before covering it
verification.body: Confirm roofline condition, curtain orientation, retainer and T-tab engagement, connector locking and completion of the numbered screw-tightening sequence.

verification.title: Record the repowering result
verification.body: Record completion of the repowering procedure and whether the airbag warning indicator reports a fault afterward. A remaining warning requires diagnosis rather than assuming the replacement curtain is defective.

procedures.purpose: Side curtain airbag removal and installation, roofline inspection, attachment orientation and numbered screw-tightening sequence.
Required SRS depowering before curtain disconnection or reconnection.
Headliner removal for curtain access and installation after the curtain is secured.
Required SRS repowering after installation is complete.

authoring.method: Codex source review against exact component application and completion procedures

guides.title: Set the correct torque when using an adapter
guides.summary: Match the tool arrangement, measure the right lengths and use the appropriate calculator before tightening a fastener with an offset adapter.
guides.introduction: A torque wrench measures the turning effort applied through its drive. An adapter can move the fastener away from that drive, changing the leverage between your hand and the bolt or nut. That means the number you set on the wrench can differ from the torque the fastener needs. A socket extension and an in-line crowfoot may both help you reach a cramped spot, but their geometry is different.
guides.why: Getting this setup right preserves the intended tightening load while allowing access around nearby parts. The useful question is where the adapter puts the fastener relative to the wrench handle. An adapter extending that reach calls for a different calculation from one pointing back toward the handle; certain right-angle arrangements use the original fastener specification within their stated limits.

when.summary: Before tightening a specified fastener with one of the illustrated adapter or extension arrangements.
notes: This is a tool-setup guide. Take the actual fastener torque, tightening sequence, replacement-fastener requirements and any additional angle stages from the exact repair article.

prepare.title: The fastener specification
prepare.detail: Open the repair article for the component and vehicle configuration you are working on. Keep its torque unit visible; lb-ft, lb-in and Nm are different scales.

prepare.title: A matching tool arrangement
prepare.detail: Compare the direction of the adapter and the position of the socket extension with the linked illustration. Left- and right-hand half-moon setups have separate calculators.

prepare.title: Actual tool dimensions
prepare.detail: Measure wrench length A from the center of the handle to the center of its drive. Measure adapter length B between its drive and fastener centers. Enter the correct length units in the calculator rather than using the tool’s overall end-to-end length.

steps.title: Choose the calculator that matches the geometry
steps.body: For an adapter pointing away from the handle, choose the [straight adapter](#/document/reference-6534a6eae93c), [straight adapter with extension](#/document/reference-72305394e0aa) or [in-line crowfoot](#/document/reference-d7780e6a592b) calculator as appropriate. If the adapter points back toward the handle, use the [reversed adapter with extension](#/document/reference-6943fbf4e2a0) calculator. Similar-looking tools do not guarantee the same leverage.

steps.title: Enter the fastener torque and measured lengths
steps.body: For the straight and crowfoot calculators, enter the specified fastener torque with its unit, then A and B with their length units. Read A from the handle center to the drive center; do not include B in A. The reversed arrangement requires the adapter to be shorter than the wrench because it subtracts from the effective reach.

steps.title: Use the limited half-moon selections when applicable
steps.body: Choose the [left half-moon](#/document/reference-bc8de71f1828) or [right half-moon](#/document/reference-a6c44300b9d8) setup. These calculators cover the listed torque specifications, wrench lengths and adapter combinations. Match the actual tool to those selections and the displayed adapter dimensions. If your combination is absent, choosing the nearest option does not establish a valid setting.

steps.title: Check whether your arrangement needs no correction
steps.body: The illustrated [crowfoot at 90 degrees](#/document/reference-b9ec8cea2317) and [socket extension](#/document/reference-c5d168787f95) arrangements use the original fastener torque. The [straight adapter at 90 degrees](#/document/reference-62fe207918f9) also uses that torque, provided the adapter is no longer than 50.8 mm (2.0 inches). For the [wobble extension](#/document/reference-d7d152a19bd1), keep the angle at or below 15 degrees. Do not extend those allowances to another geometry.

steps.title: Set the wrench using the matching result unit
steps.body: Calculate the required setting where a correction applies. Select the result in the unit marked on your wrench. The displayed unit values are rounded separately, so use the matching displayed value rather than converting a rounded result again.

steps.title: Keep the setup consistent while tightening
steps.body: Use the same adapter direction, length and angle that you checked. Follow the component’s complete tightening sequence and any later angle stage. Recalculate or recheck the arrangement if you change tools or reposition the adapter.

diagnostics.finding: The adapter points away from the wrench handle.
diagnostics.meaning: The fastener is farther from your hand than the wrench drive is, changing the effective leverage.
diagnostics.next: Use the corresponding in-line calculator with the measured wrench and adapter lengths.

diagnostics.finding: The adapter points back toward the wrench handle.
diagnostics.meaning: The effective reach is shorter than the wrench length.
diagnostics.next: Use the reversed-arrangement calculator and confirm that adapter length is less than wrench length.

diagnostics.finding: A right-angle or wobble setup looks close to a listed arrangement.
diagnostics.meaning: Its no-correction guidance applies only when the actual geometry and any stated angle or length limits match.
diagnostics.next: Check the exact linked diagram, including the straight-adapter length limit or wobble-angle limit where applicable.

diagnostics.finding: Your half-moon adapter or wrench length is not selectable.
diagnostics.meaning: The available calculator does not establish a setting for that combination.
diagnostics.next: Use a supported setup that suits the job instead of substituting a nearby selection.

verification.title: Recheck the entries against the tools
verification.body: Confirm the target fastener torque, torque unit, handle-to-drive measurement, adapter measurement and chosen arrangement before using the displayed setting.

verification.title: Complete the component’s tightening instructions
verification.body: The corrected wrench setting addresses adapter leverage. Finish the specified tightening stages and component checks in the linked repair article for the job you are performing.

watchFor.title: Length measured from the wrong endpoints
watchFor.body: A is the distance from handle center to drive center. B is the distance between adapter centers. Including the adapter in A as well as B changes the calculation.

watchFor.title: Right-angle limits lost during repositioning
watchFor.body: A setup that begins at the illustrated angle may change when space gets tight. Repositioning the adapter changes the arrangement you checked.

procedures.purpose: Calculate the setting for a straight adapter extending the wrench.
Calculate the setting for a straight adapter used with a socket extension.
Calculate the setting when the adapter points back toward the handle.
Calculate the setting for an in-line crowfoot.
Check the right-angle crowfoot arrangement that uses the fastener specification.
Check the socket-extension arrangement that uses the fastener specification.
Check the right-angle straight adapter and its 50.8 mm length limit.
Check the wobble-extension arrangement and its 15-degree angle limit.
Use the supported left-hand half-moon tool combinations.
Use the supported right-hand half-moon tool combinations.

authoring.method: Codex source and original calculator review

guides.title: Replace the convertible tonneau-cover sensor assembly
guides.summary: Replace the affected D-tower cover and its integrated sensor, then check roof operation with the tonneau covers removed.
guides.introduction: Each optional tonneau cover contains a magnet that activates a Hall-effect sensor, an electronic switch responsive to a magnetic field. The roof control modules use these signals to prevent the convertible top from being raised with the covers installed. The sensor being serviced is part of the D-tower cover, so replacement means changing that assembly rather than removing a separate sensor.
guides.why: Cover detection is an operating interlock. A refusal to raise the roof may be correct behavior when a cover is fitted. Confirming the actual cover condition and other roof operating requirements helps avoid replacing a working assembly.

when.summary: When the integrated tonneau-cover sensor or its D-tower cover assembly has been identified as requiring replacement.
notes: Left and right sides use similar operations; replace the affected assembly.

prepare.title: Assembly and trim access
prepare.detail: Obtain the appropriate D-tower cover assembly. Have tools suitable for trim clips and pin-type retainers, and the convertible loadspace-trim procedure available.

prepare.title: Establish the complaint
prepare.detail: Note whether the tonneau covers are physically installed and which message appears. A cover-removal message with covers fitted is expected.

steps.title: Expose the affected side
steps.body: Remove the loadspace trim only as necessary using [Loadspace Trim Panel — Convertible](#/document/G1692610). Establish access to the connector and D-tower cover on the side being repaired.

steps.title: Disconnect the harness
steps.body: Disconnect the sensor harness connector before releasing the cover assembly. The connector operation is similar on both sides.

steps.title: Remove the D-tower cover
steps.body: Remove the bumper stop and the two pin-type retainers, then release the remaining clip and remove the cover. Follow [Tonneau Cover Sensor](#/document/G1723917) for the attachment locations.

steps.title: Install the complete replacement
steps.body: Reverse removal: engage the cover clip, restore the retainers and bumper stop, reconnect the harness and reinstall the disturbed loadspace trim. The sensor stays part of the replacement cover assembly.

watchFor.title: Confusing the two covers
watchFor.body: The removable tonneau cover carries the magnet; the D-tower cover contains the sensor being replaced.

notes: The roof switch must be held in the requested direction during roof movement.

diagnostics.finding: TOP DISABLED — REMOVE COVERS appears with a tonneau cover installed.
diagnostics.meaning: The roof is reporting an expected closing interlock.
diagnostics.next: Remove the tonneau covers before requesting roof raising.

diagnostics.finding: The same message appears with both covers removed.
diagnostics.meaning: The reported cover condition needs investigation; the message alone does not prove which sensor or circuit is responsible.
diagnostics.next: Establish the affected side and cause before replacing an assembly.

diagnostics.finding: The roof remains inoperative without a cover warning.
diagnostics.meaning: Roof operation also depends on accessory-delay status, vehicle speed and confirmation that both rear quarter windows are fully lowered.
diagnostics.next: Continue roof-system diagnosis rather than assuming the new sensor is defective.

verification.title: Check closing under valid conditions
verification.body: With the vehicle stationary, accessory delay active and tonneau covers removed, hold the UP switch. Confirm the windows lower and the roof raises.

verification.title: Record the result
verification.body: Record roof response and whether a cover-removal message remains despite both covers being physically removed.

procedures.purpose: Tonneau sensor and D-tower cover assembly removal and installation.
Convertible loadspace-trim removal and installation for access.
Cover-sensor operation, roof interlocks and message interpretation.

authoring.method: Codex review: verified factory convertible applicability narrowed; original instructions retained

guides.title: Replace the 3160 Manual Transmission Vehicle Speed Sensor
guides.summary: Replace the vehicle speed sensor on the 5.2L engine's 3160 manual transmission and secure its bolt and electrical connection.
guides.introduction: The vehicle speed sensor (VSS) works with a tone wheel in the transmission to turn rotational movement into an electrical speed signal. The 3160 transmission carries engine torque toward the rear differential, while this sensor provides information about rotation. The repair removes the externally accessible sensor through its electrical connector and retaining bolt.
guides.why: Safe underside access is the main preparation requirement. Once the sensor is reached, the specified bolt torque secures it in its mounting, and reconnecting the electrical connector restores the signal path. Replacing the sensor is a repair action; it does not by itself establish the cause of a speed-signal concern.

when.summary: When diagnosis or other transmission service requires removal or replacement of the VSS.
notes: Confirm the 3160 transmission application before following this procedure.

prepare.title: Arrange lifting access
prepare.detail: Use a hoist positioned at the designated lifting points marked by stamped triangles. Check adapter clearance around suspension, steering, exhaust and underbody components. Never work beneath a vehicle supported only by a jack.

prepare.title: Prepare the fastener tools
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the sensor bolt and a torque wrench capable of 71 lb.in (8 Nm). Be able to access and disconnect the sensor's electrical connector.

steps.title: Position the vehicle
steps.body: With the transmission in NEUTRAL, position the vehicle on a hoist. Follow [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631) for lifting-point and clearance requirements.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the sensor
steps.body: Locate the VSS using the [3160 sensor procedure](#/document/G1794239). Disconnect its electrical connector, then remove the retaining bolt and the sensor.

steps.title: Install the sensor
steps.body: Install the VSS and its retaining bolt. Tighten the bolt to 71 lb.in (8 Nm), using a torque wrench suited to this small-fastener specification.

steps.title: Restore the electrical connection
steps.body: Connect the VSS electrical connector after securing the sensor. Confirm the connection is complete before finishing the underside work.

watchFor.title: Wrong transmission application
watchFor.body: Use this sensor procedure for the 3160 transmission. Its identification tag is on the upper right side of the transmission.

watchFor.title: Torque-unit confusion
watchFor.body: Use the inch-pound scale for the specified bolt value. Choosing a foot-pound scale instead changes the applied torque.

notes: The sensor and its retaining bolt are separate service items from the internal speed-sensor tone wheel.

verification.title: Confirm installation
verification.body: Confirm the sensor is installed and its electrical connector is reconnected.

verification.title: Record the fastener result
verification.body: Record tightening of the VSS bolt to 71 lb.in (8 Nm).

procedures.purpose: VSS removal and installation for the 5.2L application with the 3160 manual transmission.
Vehicle lifting points, support precautions and hoist positioning.
3160 transmission identification and identification-tag location.

authoring.method: Codex review preserving the source torque unit

guides.title: Replace a Two-Piston Front Brake Caliper
guides.summary: Disconnect and replace the two-piston front caliper, renew the brake-hose sealing washers and pressure bleed the brake system.
guides.introduction: The front brake caliper uses hydraulic pressure to press the brake pads against the disc. This procedure covers the two-piston caliper fitted to the listed 2.3L and 3.7L applications. Replacement involves opening the brake-hose connection and removing the guide-pin bolts, followed by reassembly and pressure bleeding.
guides.why: Opening the hose connection creates a route for fluid loss, contamination and air entry. The openings must remain sealed while disconnected, and the removed sealing washers must be discarded. Installing the replacement caliper restores the hardware; pressure bleeding completes the hydraulic part of the repair.
searchTerms: two piston front brake caliper replacement

when.summary: When a two-piston front brake caliper has been identified as requiring removal or replacement.
notes: Confirm the fitted caliper type before using this procedure.

prepare.title: Arrange wheel access and hydraulic equipment
prepare.detail: Have the capability to remove and reinstall the wheel safely, suitable means to seal hydraulic openings, new hose-connection washers and equipment for the referenced pressure-bleeding procedure.

prepare.title: Prepare for controlled tightening
prepare.detail: Have suitable tools for the flow bolt and guide-pin bolts, including a torque wrench. Follow the wheel procedure for its separate installation requirements.

steps.title: Remove the wheel and tire
steps.body: Follow [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507) to expose the front caliper. Use the [two-piston caliper procedure](#/document/G1693776) to identify the hose connection and guide-pin fasteners.

steps.title: Disconnect and remove the caliper
steps.body: Remove the brake-caliper flow bolt and disconnect the hose. Discard the washers and seal all openings. Then remove the two guide-pin bolts and the caliper, preserving the specified order of hydraulic disconnection before caliper removal.

steps.title: Install the replacement caliper
steps.body: Reverse removal. Tighten the guide-pin bolts to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm). Reconnect the hose using new washers and tighten the flow bolt to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm). Restore the wheel and tire according to their procedure.

steps.title: Pressure bleed the brake system
steps.body: Complete the referenced Brake System Pressure Bleeding procedure after installation. Tightening the connections does not remove air introduced while the hydraulic circuit was open.

watchFor.title: Unsealed hydraulic openings
watchFor.body: Keep all openings sealed while the hose and caliper are disconnected.

watchFor.title: Fluid on paintwork
watchFor.body: Immediately wash affected paintwork with cold water if brake fluid is spilled.

notes: The discarded parts specified here are the hose-connection washers.
Use the full pressure-bleeding procedure for its equipment, fluid and completion requirements.

verification.title: Confirm the installation details
verification.body: Verify new sealing washers were fitted and the flow bolt and guide-pin bolts were tightened to their respective specifications.

verification.title: Record hydraulic completion
verification.body: Record completion of the required pressure-bleeding procedure after caliper installation.

procedures.purpose: Remove and install the two-piston front brake caliper on the listed 2.3L and 3.7L applications, then pressure bleed.
Remove the wheel and tire assembly from the vehicle and reinstall it after caliper service.

guides.title: Replace a front brake disc with 2-, 4- or 6-piston calipers
guides.summary: Remove and replace a front brake disc on a 2015 Mustang 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L, supporting the caliper assembly, renewing its mounting bolts and correctly refitting the wheel.
guides.introduction: The brake disc spends its working life being squeezed between two pads. Fair enough if it eventually wants out. I’ll walk you through getting the front caliper assembly safely out of its way, fitting the disc and putting everything back with the right bolts and torque. The important trick is identifying which fasteners release the whole assembly—loosening every bolt in sight just gives the garage floor more opportunities.
guides.why: The disc, also called the rotor, turns with the wheel. The caliper presses brake pads against its two friction faces, converting the car’s motion into heat and slowing it down. During replacement, the disc must sit against clean mounting surfaces, the caliper must remain independently supported and the wheel must be tightened correctly. Those details matter as much as the shiny replacement part.

when.summary: Use this procedure after a front brake disc has been identified for replacement, or when it must be removed for related service.
notes: Applies to 2015 Mustangs with 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engines and the listed front brake configurations. Select the branch by the fitted caliper, rather than assuming the engine identifies it.
This is a removal and installation procedure. It does not establish disc thickness limits, permissible runout or a diagnosis for vibration.

prepare.title: Keep the job to disc replacement
prepare.detail: The steps below move the caliper and pads aside together, leaving the hydraulic hose connected. Separate pad replacement is additional work. The separate two-piston pad and anchor-plate instructions apply only to 2.3L and 3.7L cars; matching separate-pad instructions for a 5.0L are not established here. New-pad work also requires the correct brake-fluid specification before any necessary reservoir top-up; that specification is not included in this article.

prepare.title: Parts, cleaner and lubricant
prepare.detail: Have the replacement disc and two new anchor/caliper mounting bolts appropriate to the fitted brake package. All three disc-service branches require bolt renewal. Obtain Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner – VOC Compliant / Motorcraft Metal Brake Parts Cleaner, PM-4-A or PM-4-B, and Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant, XL-2.

prepare.title: Lifting, support and fastening equipment
prepare.detail: Use a hoist rated for the vehicle’s actual weight, including cargo and modifications, or a suitable workshop jack with floor stands. Have wheel chocks, suitable hand tools, a wire brush, a torque wrench capable of the required values and a hook or other independent support for the caliper. The emergency tire-changing jack is unsuitable for this repair.

prepare.title: Personal and chemical protection
prepare.detail: Wear eye and ear protection, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts. Read the cleaners’ and lubricant’s safety information before use. Keep solvents away from ignition sources.

steps.title: Prevent starting and restrain the car
steps.body:
Position the car on a hard, level surface. Apply the parking brake and chock every wheel that will remain on the ground.
Disable remote start, if fitted, through the central display under Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before working around the vehicle. With the stationary car restrained, select Neutral for the wheel-removal and hoist setup. Switch the ignition off and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent someone starting it during service.
These precautions come before lifting or reaching into the wheel area. See [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189).

steps.title: Locate the lifting points and raise the vehicle
steps.body:
Find the triangles stamped into the body structure along the underside of the sills. The lifting illustration shows four locations, just behind the front wheels and just ahead of the rear wheels. Use those marked lifting points; do not substitute a convenient-looking suspension part or either bumper.
Position the hoist adapters carefully so they clear the suspension, steering linkage, exhaust and nearby brackets. With a two-column hoist, also check clearance around the stabilizer brackets, axle and rear cover. If using a drive-on lift, check underbody clearance before driving onto it.
Raise the vehicle using equipment of adequate capacity. If using a workshop jack, support the vehicle on floor stands before beginning the repair. Never get underneath a car supported only by a jack. See [Jacking and Lifting](#/document/G1663631).

steps.title: Remove the front wheel
steps.body:
With the vehicle safely supported, remove the five wheel nuts and lift the wheel off the studs. Put it aside where it cannot fall into the work area.
Do not use heat to free a seized wheel nut: it can damage the wheel and wheel bearing. A nut that cannot be removed without heat needs a separate resolution before continuing. See [Wheel and Tire](#/document/G1686507).

steps.title: Identify the caliper mounting bolts before loosening anything
steps.body:
Look behind the caliper toward the steering knuckle—the suspension casting that carries the wheel hub. Identify the upper and lower attachments that secure the brake assembly to it.
On a two-piston setup, release the anchor bracket from the knuckle so the caliper, bracket and pads can move aside together. The anchor bracket is the support that holds the pads around the disc. Its mounting bolts are different from the two smaller guide-pin bolts that attach the sliding caliper to that bracket.
On four- and six-piston setups, use the upper and lower caliper-to-knuckle mounting bolts. The [Brake Disc procedure](#/document/G1693784) covers all three arrangements. I like to settle this distinction before a ratchet gets a vote.

steps.title: Move the matching brake assembly aside and discard both mounting bolts
steps.body:
Arrange independent support for the assembly before releasing it.
Two-piston caliper: remove the two anchor-to-knuckle mounting bolts, discard both and move the anchor bracket, caliper and pads aside together.
Four-piston caliper: remove and discard the two caliper mounting bolts, then move the caliper and pads aside together.
Six-piston caliper: remove and discard the two caliper mounting bolts, then move the caliper and pads aside together.
Support the assembly with a hook or suitable support so its weight is carried independently of the brake hose. Keep the hydraulic connection intact and make sure the hose is not pulled tight. Never let the caliper hang from its hose.

steps.title: Remove the disc from the hub
steps.body:
With the supported brake assembly clear, slide the disc outward off the five wheel studs. The disc illustration shows it coming away from the hub as a separate component.
Watch the caliper support as you handle the disc; moving a heavy part nearby must not pull the caliper off its support. If the disc will not come free, stop rather than inventing a hammering, heating or puller method.

steps.title: Clean the disc mounting interfaces
steps.body:
Use a wire brush and Motorcraft brake cleaner PM-4-A or PM-4-B to clean the brake-disc mating surfaces, including the faces where the disc and hub meet. These are the contact surfaces that locate the disc against the hub, rather than the broad friction faces swept by the pads.
Look for corrosion, dirt or other material trapped on those contact faces. Remove it before assembly so the disc can sit directly against its mounting face. Keep the supported caliper clear while cleaning.

steps.title: Fit the replacement disc
steps.body:
Place the replacement disc over the wheel studs and seat it against the cleaned hub face. Check that nothing is trapped between the mating surfaces and that the disc is sitting against the hub before bringing the brake assembly back into position.
This is an assembly check, not a measurement of disc runout.

steps.title: Refit the brake assembly with new bolts
steps.body:
Bring the supported assembly back over the disc with its pads in position. Align its mounting holes with the knuckle without pulling on the hose.
For a two-piston assembly, install two new anchor-to-knuckle bolts. For a four- or six-piston assembly, install two new caliper mounting bolts.
Tighten both mounting bolts to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm) for the selected branch. Remove the temporary caliper support only after the assembly is secured.
The 115 Nm value belongs to these disc-service mounting bolts. It does not belong to the separate two-piston caliper guide-pin bolts.

steps.title: Check the brake assembly and operate the pedal
steps.body:
Confirm that both new mounting bolts have been tightened, the pads remain correctly positioned and the caliper hose is free of tension from the assembly or its former support.
With the brake fully reassembled, apply the brake pedal several times to verify correct brake-system operation. If operation is not correct, stop and resolve it before driving. Pedal applications are the completion check here; they do not establish the cause of an existing brake complaint.

steps.title: Clean the wheel mounting face and central pilot bore
steps.body:
Clean corrosion, dirt and foreign material from the wheel’s flat mounting face and the corresponding hub/disc wheel-contact face. Also clean the wheel’s central pilot bore—the large center hole that fits around the raised locating lip on the hub. The wheel illustration calls for cleaning this bore as well as lubricating its locating interface.
Check that any rotor-to-hub attachment present is secured and does not stand between the wheel and its mounting face. The wheel must seat directly against the mounting surface; trapped material can allow the nuts to loosen.

steps.title: Apply anti-seize only at the wheel’s locating interface
steps.body:
Apply a thin film of Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant XL-2 only where the wheel’s central pilot bore meets the hub pilot.
Keep it off the flat wheel-to-disc mounting faces, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and disc friction faces. Leave the wheel-stud and wheel-nut threads clean and dry. The center locating interface gets the film; the rest does not need a damn thing added to it.

steps.title: Install the wheel and finger-tighten its five nuts
steps.body:
Position the wheel over the studs and against its clean mounting face. Install all five wheel nuts finger-tight at this stage.
Check that the wheel is seated and the nuts have started correctly. Reserve final torque for when the vehicle is resting on its tires.

steps.title: Restore restraints before and during lowering
steps.body:
Before lowering, confirm that the parking brake is applied; restore it now if it was released during positioning. Keep chocks at every wheel already on the ground.
Clear tools and supports as required for controlled lowering. As the raised wheels reach the ground, restore their ground-wheel chocks immediately. Do not wait until the car is fully lowered to restore those restraints. Finish lowering with the vehicle restrained and resting on its tires.

steps.title: Torque the wheel nuts in a star pattern and arrange the recheck
steps.body:
With the vehicle resting on its tires and the wheel-stud and nut threads clean and dry, tighten the five nuts to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm) in a star/cross pattern.
Following the illustrated layout, start at the top nut, move to the lower-left nut, then the upper-right, upper-left and lower-right nuts. This crosses the wheel rather than walking around its edge. Incorrect tightening order can introduce disc runout—sideways variation as the disc rotates—and contribute to brake roughness, shudder and vibration.
Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after wheel installation. Include that recheck in the job record before putting the tools away.

watchFor.title: A caliper hanging from its hose
watchFor.body: The hose is a hydraulic connection, not a lifting strap. If the assembly slips or its weight begins pulling on the hose, stop and restore independent support before continuing.

watchFor.title: Confusing anchor bolts with guide-pin bolts
watchFor.body: All two-, four- and six-piston disc-service mounting bolts are renewed and tightened to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). On the 2.3L/3.7L two-piston setup, the separate caliper guide-pin bolts use 24 lb.ft (32 Nm). Those guide-pin bolts remain installed for the whole-assembly route described here.

watchFor.title: Contamination under the disc or wheel
watchFor.body: Corrosion and debris at the mating faces prevent direct contact. Clean them before assembly. The wheel’s central pilot bore also needs cleaning; wiping only the flat face misses part of the job.

watchFor.title: Lubricant straying beyond the pilot
watchFor.body: The XL-2 film belongs only between the wheel pilot bore and hub pilot. Keep mounting faces, studs, nuts, pads and friction faces free of it. The wheel-nut torque assumes clean, dry threads.

notes: The two-piston anchor-plate procedure independently confirms that both anchor mounting bolts are discarded and replaced. See [Brake Caliper Anchor Plate](#/document/G1693782).

If separate two-piston pad work is undertaken on a 2.3L or 3.7L, its sequence is different: support and remove the caliper after removing its two guide-pin bolts, note the pad positions, remove the pads, then remove the upper and lower pad clips. Only then remove the anchor plate and discard its two mounting bolts. Reassembly restores the anchor with new bolts at 85 lb.ft (115 Nm), the clips, pads and caliper; guide-pin bolts tighten to 24 lb.ft (32 Nm). The clip with a tab belongs at the top of the anchor plate. See [Two-Piston Brake Pads](#/document/G1693786).

For that separate two-piston new-pad job, use all new hardware and lubricant supplied with the pad kit and follow the kit’s lubricant directions. The piston-retraction method uses a C-clamp bearing through a worn pad to push the pistons into their bores. After assembly, depress the brake pedal, check the reservoir level and top up only as necessary with the correctly specified brake fluid.

Before any underhood reservoir work, keep the ignition off and the key removed. Inspect the cooling fans for damage, cracks or separation; a damaged fan must be replaced before underhood work. Fans can operate with the ignition off, so disable them before working nearby.

diagnostics.finding: The fitted brake package has two, four or six pistons.
diagnostics.meaning: This selects the mounting arrangement to release for disc access.
diagnostics.next: For two pistons, release the anchor bracket from the knuckle with the caliper and pads attached. For four or six pistons, release the caliper at its two knuckle mounting bolts. Renew both removed bolts in every branch and use 85 lb.ft (115 Nm).

diagnostics.finding: Corrosion, dirt or foreign material remains between mating faces.
diagnostics.meaning: The disc or wheel cannot seat directly against its intended mounting surface.
diagnostics.next: Remove the contamination before refitting. Clean the disc mating surfaces with a wire brush and PM-4-A or PM-4-B, and clean the wheel mounting face and central pilot bore before wheel installation.

diagnostics.finding: A wheel nut is seized, or the disc will not slide free after the caliper assembly is moved aside.
diagnostics.meaning: The routine removal sequence cannot continue.
diagnostics.next: Stop and obtain a suitable component-specific removal method. Do not heat a seized wheel nut; that can damage the wheel and wheel bearing.

diagnostics.finding: The brake does not operate correctly after several pedal applications.
diagnostics.meaning: The required completion check has not passed.
diagnostics.next: Keep the vehicle out of service and resolve the brake operation before driving. This article does not provide a hydraulic fault-isolation test.

diagnostics.finding: The job expands into separate pad replacement.
diagnostics.meaning: Additional configuration-specific instructions and, if topping up is necessary, the correct brake-fluid specification are required.
diagnostics.next: On a 2.3L/3.7L two-piston car, use the separate pad sequence and kit requirements described in the notes. Do not extend those instructions to a 5.0L or to four- or six-piston pad service.

verification.title: Disc and brake assembly secured
verification.body: Confirm that the disc is seated against cleaned mating surfaces, the caliper and pads are restored, both disc-service mounting bolts are new and both have been tightened to 85 lb.ft (115 Nm). Check that the temporary support is removed and the hose carries no assembly weight.

verification.title: Brake-pedal completion check passed
verification.body: Apply the brake pedal several times after brake reassembly and verify correct operation before driving. An unresolved result prevents completion.

verification.title: Wheel installation completed on the ground
verification.body: Confirm clean mounting faces, a cleaned pilot bore, XL-2 confined to the pilot interface and clean, dry wheel-fastener threads. With the car resting on its tires, verify all five nuts were tightened in the star sequence to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm).

verification.title: Restraints and follow-up accounted for
verification.body: Confirm that the parking brake was applied before lowering and ground-wheel chocks were restored as the wheels reached the ground. Record the wheel-nut retightening requirement within 160 km (100 mi).

procedures.purpose: Primary front brake-disc removal and installation for two-, four- and six-piston calipers, including mounting-bolt torque, surface cleaning and brake-pedal completion check.
Wheel removal, mounting-face and pilot-bore preparation, restricted XL-2 application, ground-level wheel-nut torque, star sequence and retightening requirement.
Confirm two-piston anchor mounting-bolt renewal and 115 Nm torque; provide the separate anchor-service sequence for 2.3L and 3.7L cars.
Identify stamped-triangle lifting points and explain hoist positioning, floor-stand support and lifting restrictions.
Distinguish 32 Nm guide-pin fasteners from anchor bolts and explain the separate two-piston pad sequence, clip orientation and conditional new-pad requirements for 2.3L and 3.7L cars.
Task-relevant startup prevention, parking brake, chocking, lifting capacity, personal protection, solvent precautions and conditional underhood fan precautions.

stepGroups.title: Restrain, lift and expose the brake
stepGroups.summary: Prevent starting, use the marked lifting points and remove the wheel.

stepGroups.title: Support the caliper and remove the disc
stepGroups.summary: Choose the fitted mounting arrangement, discard its bolts and slide the disc off.

stepGroups.title: Clean, fit and secure the brake
stepGroups.summary: Prepare the mating surfaces, install the disc and restore the assembly with new bolts.

stepGroups.title: Prepare and reinstall the wheel
stepGroups.summary: Clean the wheel interfaces, lubricate only the pilot and install the nuts finger-tight.

stepGroups.title: Lower safely and finish tightening
stepGroups.summary: Restore restraints during lowering, torque the wheel in a star and arrange its recheck.

guides.title: Replace and configure the electric power steering gear
guides.summary: Remove the electric steering gear, rebuild its tie-rod and boot connections, and complete configuration and front-toe adjustment.
guides.introduction: The electric power-assisted steering (EPAS) gear converts steering input into sideways rack movement, while an electric motor reduces the driver's effort. Its power steering control module (PSCM), motor and torque sensor are serviced together as an assembly. Replacement combines mechanical steering work with electronic configuration; the separately serviceable tie rods and bellows boots also require careful assembly.
guides.why: An incorrectly centered gear can damage the steering gear or clockspring when the column is connected. Reused column bolts can allow shaft detachment, and poorly sealed bellows can draw water into the gear during steering movement. Correct configuration makes the replacement module match the vehicle, while front-toe adjustment addresses the wheel alignment disturbed by tie-rod work.

when.summary: When diagnosis establishes that the steering gear assembly requires removal or replacement.
notes: Heavy steering or a warning message does not, by itself, prove that the gear has failed.
Follow the engine, transmission, convertible-bracket and underbody-equipment branches that match the vehicle.

prepare.title: Arrange mechanical and electronic capability
prepare.detail: Provide safe underside access, a steering-wheel holding device, rack holding tool 204-816, a suitable crowfoot or open-end wrench, torque equipment and boot-clamp pliers. A replacement gear requires a configuration-capable scan tool; front-toe measurement and adjustment are also needed.

prepare.title: Have the replacement hardware ready
prepare.detail: Renew the removed inner tie rods, steering stops, bellows boots and clamps, both main gear bolts and the column shaft bolt. Renew the coupler bolt if removed for a new gear. Replacement gears have a separate kit containing inner rods, boots, clamps and jam nuts for installation after the gear is mounted.

prepare.title: Prepare branch-specific materials
prepare.detail: The 2.3L operation requires oil-drain equipment, a new oil filter and the specified engine oil. Boot mating surfaces require Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-E1 meeting ESA-M1C75-B.

prepare.title: Plan battery isolation after saving configuration
prepare.detail: Retrieve the required PSCM configuration before disconnection. Then follow Battery Disconnect and Connect before steering-linkage work; battery-ground isolation is required by the tie-rod-end procedure and must already be complete before the 3.7L starter-cable work.

steps.title: Save configuration and release the dash seal
steps.body: Before removing a gear being replaced, connect the scan tool and retrieve PSCM configuration. Follow the [complete steering gear procedure](#/document/G1686680). Remove the dash-seal nuts, loosen the seal, and hand-start the nuts again. Preserve its foam and brackets. After saving configuration, disconnect the battery ground cable through [Battery Disconnect and Connect](#/document/G1692356). Hold the steering wheel straight ahead, remove both tie-rod ends, and remove applicable shields, support brackets and V-brace.

steps.title: Disconnect the column and strip the inner rods
steps.body: Discard the column shaft bolt, separate the shaft from the lower coupler without hammering or prying, and secure the shaft to the frame rail. Disconnect EPAS wiring and release its retainers. Remove and discard both boots' clamps; move the boots and stops aside. Move the rack fully left and use tool 204-816 on the left side to hold it while removing both inner rods. Reverse the tool for the right-hand rod. Discard the rods and stops.

steps.title: Clear the applicable engine equipment
steps.body: On the 2.3L, remove and discard the oil filter and, with automatic transmission, move the cooler tubes aside through their bracket fasteners. On the 3.7L, follow the starter-solenoid battery-cable, solenoid-wire and engine-ground disconnections. Follow the transmission-specific bracket branch for the wiring and cooler tubes. On the 5.0L and 5.2L, release the specified oil-pan wiring retainers; the 5.2L also requires moving the oxygen-sensor harness.

steps.title: Remove the gear through the available clearance
steps.body: Remove and discard the left- and right-hand gear bolts and remove the convertible support bracket if fitted. Set the rack end flush with the right-hand side of the case. Slide the gear left, then rotate it and lower its right-hand side to extract it. When fitting a new gear, remove the coupler from the old assembly and discard its bolt.

steps.title: Mount the replacement assembly
steps.body: Install the transferred coupler with a new bolt when applicable. Raise the gear's left side and slide it left, then raise the right side and slide the assembly into position. Finger-tighten the convertible bracket bolt if fitted and both new main gear bolts. Tighten the bracket, right-hand gear bolt and left-hand gear bolt as directed.

steps.title: Restore engine-specific connections
steps.body: Refit the disturbed wiring retainers and transmission brackets. On the 3.7L, restore the engine ground, solenoid wire and battery cable, then close the cable cover. On the 2.3L automatic, restore the cooler-tube brackets; install a new oil filter using its specified tightening stages. Keep these oil and starter operations within their own engine branches.

steps.title: Install the inner rods and airtight bellows
steps.body: Position new stops and move the rack fully left. Hold the rack with tool 204-816 while tightening the new inner rods, reversing the tool for the right side. Seat each stop by hand until it clicks and cannot be pulled off by hand. Apply the specified grease to the boot mating surfaces. Fit new boots over the housing beads and rod grooves, install new inner and outer clamps, and thread on the jam nuts.

steps.title: Center the gear before joining the column
steps.body: Reconnect and secure the EPAS harness. Turn the gear input fully right, then fully left, and return it to center before connecting the held steering column. Fit a new column shaft bolt without forcing the joint. Carry out the Steering Column Collapsed Check before completing reassembly.

steps.title: Restore the surrounding structure
steps.body: Reinstall the applicable V-brace, shields and support brackets, then both tie-rod ends. Position the dash seal and tighten its nuts. Turn the steering wheel lock-to-lock to ensure the steering stops are fully seated.

steps.title: Complete oil restoration, configuration and alignment
steps.body: Complete the linked reassembly and battery-connection procedure once the mechanical and electrical connections are restored. For the 2.3L, fill with clean engine oil using its engine specifications. Configure a new gear using the previously retrieved information or vehicle As-Built data, following scan-tool instructions. Finally, check and, if needed, adjust front toe through Front Toe Adjustment (204-00).

watchFor.title: Column force or seal damage
watchFor.body: The dash seal must be loosened before lower-coupler work. Forcing the shaft can damage steering components; damaged seal foam or separated brackets can admit noise, fumes, air or water.

watchFor.title: Water entering the bellows
watchFor.body: Use new boots and proper clamps. Zip ties cannot provide the required airtight seal, and water contamination can damage the inner-joint grease.

watchFor.title: Rack position serving different purposes
watchFor.body: Full-left rack travel provides tie-rod tool clearance; a rack end flush with the right-hand case provides extraction clearance. Centering is required later, before column connection.

notes: The 2.3L oil specification in this operation is SAE 5W-30 synthetic blend, WSS-M2C946-B1. Do not apply this branch's oil instructions to the other engines.
If module programming occurs during installation, follow scan-tool key-cycling instructions and clear communication faults caused by programming.

diagnostics.finding: Steering assistance is reduced and steering feels heavier.
diagnostics.meaning: The PSCM can reduce assistance for low voltage, high voltage or over-temperature conditions.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose the recorded condition before deciding that the gear assembly requires replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Electrical assistance is absent.
diagnostics.meaning: A critical detected concern can place EPAS in manual steering mode, leaving mechanical steering with heavy effort.
diagnostics.next: Use the stored diagnostic trouble codes and system diagnosis to establish the cause.

diagnostics.finding: The identified defect is confined to a tie rod or bellows boot.
diagnostics.meaning: These parts are separately serviceable, whereas the PSCM, motor and torque sensor form the serviced gear assembly.
diagnostics.next: Select the repair scope that matches the established fault.

verification.title: Confirm the mechanical checks
verification.body: Complete the lower-shaft collapsed check, verify each stop's hand-retention check, and perform the final lock-to-lock seating operation.

verification.title: Confirm electronic completion
verification.body: For a new gear, record successful scan-tool configuration using saved configuration or As-Built data.

verification.title: Record alignment and fluid completion
verification.body: Record the front-toe check and any adjustment. On the 2.3L, confirm completion of the specified oil refill.

procedures.purpose: Complete steering gear removal and installation, including engine and equipment branches, rack positioning, new hardware and final checks.
Retrieve and restore PSCM configuration through programmable module installation and As-Built data when directed.
Remove and reinstall the outer tie-rod ends on both sides.
Inspect the steering column lower shaft after gear reconnection.
Apply the 2.3L engine specifications during the required oil refill.
Disconnect battery ground before steering-linkage and starter-cable work, then reconnect through the specified completion procedure.

authoring.method: Codex independent original-image and linked-prerequisite review

guides.title: Replace a coupe rear quarter panel
guides.summary: Restore body dimensions, section and weld in the replacement outer quarter panel, then restore sealing, paint and corrosion protection.
guides.introduction: The coupe quarter panel forms the outer rear body side around the wheel opening and sail-panel area. This mild-steel outer panel is joined to the surrounding body through welded and bonded areas. Replacement is a specialist collision repair involving body measurement, controlled cutting, several joining methods and full finishing work.
guides.why: Cutting only the outer panel protects the underlying structure, which contains different steel grades. Adhesive, expanding foam and seam sealer serve separate purposes: bonding, noise and vibration treatment, and joint sealing. Each must be restored in its designated locations.
searchTerms: quarter panel rocker and sail panel sectioning

when.summary: When quarter-panel damage requires outer-panel replacement, with body dimensions restored first if necessary.
notes: Establish the required dimensional correction before using the replacement panel to close the repair.

prepare.title: Arrange body-repair equipment and capability
prepare.detail: This work requires resistance spotwelding and metal inert gas/metal active gas (MIG/MAG) welding equipment, locking pliers, a spherical cutter, air body saw, spot-weld drill bit, 8 mm drill bit and hot air gun.

prepare.title: Prepare joining and finishing materials
prepare.detail: Select the listed metal bonding adhesive, flexible foam repair material and seam sealer. Arrange a Ford-approved paint system and corrosion-protection work. Establish the prescribed cut, adhesive, foam and weld locations before starting.

prepare.title: Provide a new left-side filler-door assembly
prepare.detail: When left-side access requires removing the fuel filler door assembly, obtain a new assembly before reassembly. Its removal releases clips by damaging the housing, so the removed assembly cannot be returned to service.

steps.title: Restore the body dimensions
steps.body: If required, restore the vehicle to its pre-accident dimensions using [Body and Frame](#/document/G1687516). Use the applicable coupe and shared body measurements; convertible-specific dimensions do not define this repair.

steps.title: Remove surrounding components
steps.body: Remove the front door, luggage-compartment lid, rocker moulding, fixed glass, coupe loadspace trim, rear quarter trim, rear bumper and rear lamp assembly. On the left side, remove the fuel filler door assembly and applicable filler pipe, treating the door assembly as a required replacement. Remove the affected door striker and position the carpet and wiring harness aside.

steps.title: Separate the damaged outer panel
steps.body: Follow the illustrated rocker and sail-panel cuts in the [quarter-panel procedure](#/document/G1687585), cutting through the outer panel only. Complete both spot-weld drilling stages, then remove the panel. A hot air gun may soften adhesive and noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) foam, but applied heat must not exceed 170°C.

steps.title: Prepare the replacement panel
steps.body: Cut the service panel to fit using the specified spherical cutter and air body saw. Drill the prescribed plug-weld holes with an 8 mm drill bit. Follow the installation locations rather than devising a general hole pattern.

steps.title: Apply materials and establish the panel position
steps.body: Apply NVH expanding foam and metal bonding adhesive to the indicated areas. Install and clamp the quarter panel in position, then perform the specified seam welding with MIG/MAG equipment.

steps.title: Complete the remaining weld stages
steps.body: Perform the resistance spotwelding stage, followed by the separate MIG welding stages in the installation sequence. Use locking pliers where directed. Each joining operation must follow its designated locations in the panel procedure.

steps.title: Finish, seal and protect
steps.body: Metal-finish the repaired areas, seal all areas to production level and refinish with a Ford-approved paint system. Restore corrosion protection through the dedicated [corrosion-prevention procedure](#/document/G1687508).

steps.title: Reassemble the body
steps.body: Reposition the carpet and wiring harness and install the door striker. Reinstall the removed closures, glass, trim, bumper and lighting through their individual procedures. For left-side work, install a new fuel filler door assembly and restore the applicable filler pipe; do not reuse the assembly damaged during removal.

watchFor.title: Cutting into underlying structure
watchFor.body: The sectioning instruction applies only to the outer panel. Keep the rocker and sail-panel cuts within that layer.

watchFor.title: Incomplete finishing
watchFor.body: Complete production-level sealing and corrosion protection as well as the visible paint finish.

diagnostics.finding: Body measurements show accident-related dimensional displacement.
diagnostics.meaning: The surrounding body needs restoration before panel replacement proceeds.
diagnostics.next: Restore pre-accident dimensions using the applicable body measurements before fitting the new quarter panel.

verification.title: Record body fit
verification.body: Record the applicable body-side and rear-panel margins and flushness against Body and Frame specifications, including the adjacent door, luggage-compartment lid, lamp and fuel door where relevant.

verification.title: Confirm repair completion
verification.body: Confirm completion of the specified joining stages, production-level sealing, refinishing, corrosion protection and reinstallation of all removed components.

Luggage-compartment lid removal and installation.

Applicable left-side 3.7L fuel filler pipe removal and installation.
Applicable left-side 5.0L fuel filler pipe removal and installation.

Rear bumper removal and installation.
