guides.title: Replace the fuel filler door and housing assembly
guides.summary: Replace the filler-door assembly through engine-specific filler-pipe removal, boot release and destructive access to its retaining clips.
guides.introduction: The fuel filler door covers the refuelling opening, while its housing attaches the assembly to the body. A boot connects the assembly around the opening behind it. Removing this unit involves work inside the wheel opening and removal of the fuel tank filler pipe before the housing can come free.
guides.why: Removal damages the existing assembly because access holes must be punched to reach its retaining clips. Clearance is limited, so releasing every clip before rotating the housing is central to the sequence. Have the replacement available before starting.

when.summary: When the filler-door assembly needs replacement or must be removed for access.
notes: Any removed assembly requires replacement because the removal process damages it.

prepare.title: Arrange parts, tools and access
prepare.detail: Obtain a new fuel filler door assembly and a screwdriver. Plan access inside the wheel opening to release the boot.

prepare.title: Prepare for filler-pipe work
prepare.detail: Use the filler-pipe procedure matching the engine for its access, precautions and installation requirements. This prerequisite makes the job more involved than an exterior door replacement alone.

steps.title: Open the door and remove the filler pipe
steps.body: Open the fuel filler door, then remove the fuel tank filler pipe through the matching [2.3L](#/document/G1671581), [3.7L](#/document/G1671603), [5.0L](#/document/G1671615) or [5.2L](#/document/G1794943) procedure. Complete its fuel-lowering, electrical-isolation and wheel-opening access requirements before releasing the housing.

steps.title: Unseat the boot
steps.body: Work from inside the wheel opening to unseat the fuel filler door assembly boot. This releases the flexible connection before the housing is pulled away from the body.

steps.title: Release the housing clips
steps.body: Follow the indicated locations in the [assembly procedure](#/document/G1693225). Use a screwdriver to punch four access holes, then release the clips through those holes while pulling the housing away. Once all four clips have released, rotate the housing out through the limited clearance.

steps.title: Install the new assembly
steps.body: Reverse the removal sequence using the new assembly: position and retain the housing, reseat the boot, then complete the engine-specific filler-pipe installation. The damaged old assembly is not suitable for refitting.

watchFor.title: A clip still holding the housing
watchFor.body: Rotation follows release of all four clips. Limited clearance does not change that order.

verification.title: Check reverse-sequence completion
verification.body: Confirm the new housing is retained by its clips, the boot is reseated and the filler pipe has been installed according to the matching engine procedure.

procedures.purpose: Filler-door assembly removal, illustrated clip access and reverse-order installation.
Required 2.3L filler-pipe removal and installation.
Required 3.7L filler-pipe removal and installation.
Required 5.0L filler-pipe removal and installation.
Required 5.2L filler-pipe removal and installation, with its fuel-lowering, electrical-isolation and access sequence.

guides.title: Check the collapsible lower steering shaft
guides.summary: Measure both specified lower-shaft spans with the steering fully assembled and replace the shaft if either dimension is outside its applicable range.
guides.introduction: The steering column links the steering wheel to the steering gear through upper and lower shafts and a coupling. The lower shaft is collapsible, so its assembled length needs checking whenever it has been disconnected from the upper shaft or coupling. This inspection establishes whether its dimensions remain acceptable.
guides.why: Two separate measurements assess the exposed shaft sections. Left-hand-drive and right-hand-drive arrangements have different limits, and both measurements must pass. Measuring the wrong endpoints can produce a misleading result.
searchTerms: left hand drive steering shaft measurement
right hand drive steering shaft measurement

when.summary: Whenever the lower steering shaft has been disconnected from the upper shaft or the coupling.
notes: Perform the dimensional check with the steering system fully assembled.

prepare.title: Provide clear measuring access
prepare.detail: Keep the steering system fully assembled and arrange access that lets you identify the illustrated reference points.

prepare.title: Use the matching diagram
prepare.detail: Have a millimetre measuring tool and the left-hand-drive or right-hand-drive diagram in the linked procedure. Accurate endpoint identification matters more than estimating the overall shaft length.

steps.title: Identify the steering arrangement
steps.body: Confirm whether the vehicle is left-hand drive or right-hand drive. Select that branch of the collapsed-check procedure before comparing any dimensions.

steps.title: Measure the longer exposed span
steps.body: Use the exact endpoints marked for the long dimension. The left-hand-drive range is 118–132 mm; the right-hand-drive range is 89–103 mm. Record the actual reading.

steps.title: Measure the shorter exposed portion
steps.body: Use the separate reference marks for the short dimension. The left-hand-drive range is 52–61 mm; the right-hand-drive range is 37–47 mm. Record this independently because an acceptable long span cannot establish that both dimensions pass.

steps.title: Make the replacement decision
steps.body: Compare both readings with their matching ranges. If either is outside its range, discard the lower shaft and install a new one; do not attempt to repair it. Shaft replacement requires its own installation procedure, followed by the assembled dimensional check.

watchFor.title: Mixing the drive-layout limits
watchFor.body: Right-hand-drive dimensions are separate requirements, not alternative limits for a left-hand-drive shaft.

watchFor.title: An incomplete assembly
watchFor.body: A measurement taken with the shaft disconnected does not satisfy this check.

notes: The illustrated dimensions describe two exposed spans, not a general end-to-end shaft measurement.

diagnostics.finding: Both measurements are within the applicable ranges
diagnostics.meaning: The lower shaft passes this dimensional inspection.
diagnostics.next: Record the results with the steering arrangement.

diagnostics.finding: Either measurement is outside its applicable range
diagnostics.meaning: The lower shaft fails the dimensional inspection.
diagnostics.next: Discard and replace the shaft without attempting repair.

verification.title: Retain an unambiguous measurement record
verification.body: Record the drive layout, both actual readings and the corresponding limits. Confirm that the system was fully assembled and both spans passed before closing this check.

procedures.purpose: Assembled lower-shaft inspection with distinct left-hand-drive and right-hand-drive measurement diagrams.

guides.title: Replace the brake pedal and bracket with the 6R80 automatic transmission
guides.summary: Remove and install the brake pedal assembly while preserving push-rod alignment, stoplamp-switch adjustment and the specified bracket tightening sequence.
guides.introduction: The brake pedal transfers your foot's effort to the brake booster through its push rod. The bracket supports the pedal and holds that connection in position. This job replaces the pedal and bracket assembly, then restores the push-rod connection, wiring retention and stoplamp switch.
guides.why: The stoplamp switch depends on the pedal's resting position for correct installation. Incorrect handling can damage or misadjust it. Push-rod alignment and controlled bracket tightening also matter: incorrect fastener tightening can damage the booster.
searchTerms: brake booster push rod clevis pin

when.summary: When repair requires removal or replacement of the brake pedal and bracket assembly.
notes: This procedure applies to the 6R80 automatic-transmission pedal assembly.

prepare.title: Obtain the replacement hardware
prepare.detail: Have four new bracket nuts and a new booster push-rod clevis-locking pin. Both are discarded during removal; the locking pin must be renewed whenever removed.

prepare.title: Prepare hand tools and switch instructions
prepare.detail: Use hand tools and a torque wrench for bracket installation. Keep the stoplamp-switch procedure available and establish access to the pedal, push rod and wiring retainers.

steps.title: Remove the stoplamp switch before pedal work
steps.body: Follow the linked switch procedure with the pedal at rest. The switch plunger must be compressed so the switch can rotate in its bracket. Attempting removal while the pedal is applied leaves the plunger extended and can damage the switch.

steps.title: Free the wiring and booster connection
steps.body: Detach the five wiring-harness retainers. Remove and discard the booster push-rod clevis-locking pin, then position the push rod aside. This releases the connections that would otherwise remain attached to the assembly.

steps.title: Remove the pedal and bracket
steps.body: Remove the two bolts and four nuts, discard the nuts, and remove the assembly. Retain the bolts for installation; they are not designated as discard parts.

steps.title: Position and tighten the replacement assembly
steps.body: Align the booster push-rod clevis with the pedal attachment point before installing retainers. Start all bracket fasteners by hand. Using the illustration's orientation, tighten in order: upper-left nut, lower-right nut, upper-right nut, lower-left nut, upper-right bolt, then upper-left bolt. Torque all six to 17 lb.ft (23 Nm), using a torque wrench rather than a power tool.

steps.title: Restore the push rod and wiring
steps.body: Continue reversing removal: ensure the push rod is aligned with the clevis and secure the connection with the new clevis-locking pin. Reattach all five harness retainers.

steps.title: Install the switch with the pedal undisturbed
steps.body: With the booster push rod attached and pedal at rest, install the stoplamp switch using its complete procedure. Do not press, pull or otherwise move the pedal during installation; its position determines correct switch adjustment.

watchFor.title: Misalignment before fastening
watchFor.body: Confirm clevis alignment before fitting retainers, rather than discovering an incorrect connection after fastening the assembly.

watchFor.title: Fluid on paintwork
watchFor.body: If brake fluid spills on paint, immediately wash the affected area with cold water.

notes: Fastener positions are relative to the drawing, not vehicle left and right.

verification.title: Confirm assembly completion
verification.body: Check that the aligned push rod has its new locking pin, all harness retainers are restored, and the switch was installed with the connected pedal at rest.

verification.title: Record hardware and tightening
verification.body: Record replacement of the four nuts and locking pin, and completion of the illustrated six-fastener sequence at the specified torque.

procedures.purpose: Complete 6R80 brake pedal and bracket removal, installation and illustrated tightening sequence.
Stoplamp-switch removal before pedal work and installation after restoring the push-rod connection.

guides.title: Trace low and high voltage faults in the instrument modules
guides.summary: Separate battery, charging-system and connection faults from module faults when U3003:16 or U3003:17 is recorded.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) presents gauges, indicators and message-center warnings, and controls warning chimes. These functions depend on dependable electrical power. Tests CC, CD and CE investigate voltage faults associated with the information center module (ICM) or IPC, identifying when battery or circuit work is needed before considering a module.
guides.why: A stored voltage code can describe a past event rather than a present failure. Charging or jump-starting can leave a high-voltage record, while resistance in an ICM connection can reduce its supply despite a charged battery. The reporting module and repeat-test result determine the next action.

when.summary: Use when U3003:16 or U3003:17 is recorded in the instrument-module diagnostic path.
notes: Record which module reports the code; Tests CD and CE have different final decisions.

prepare.title: Provide scan and voltage testing
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of module self-tests and continuous-memory code retrieval, a voltmeter, battery-testing capability and correct terminal adapters.

prepare.title: Establish the starting condition
prepare.detail: Record codes and battery voltage before clearing anything. Review battery charging, jump-starting and recent repairs, and inspect accessible wiring and connectors.

steps.title: Test CC: recheck the low-voltage code
steps.body: CC1 specifies ignition on, clearing diagnostic trouble codes, waiting 10 seconds and performing an ICM self-test. If U3003:16 does not return, clear it; the branch ends with a possible previous low-battery event. A returning code leads to CC2.

steps.title: Check charging faults and battery condition
steps.body: Run the body control module (BCM) self-test. Charging-system codes direct BCM diagnosis. Otherwise check battery condition and confirm it is fully charged. Diagnose the cause of discharge before continuing to the ICM circuit measurements.

steps.title: Measure the ICM supply and ground
steps.body: Switch ignition off and disconnect C2114, then switch ignition on. Measure pin 1 to ground: it must be within 0.2 volt of recorded battery voltage. Then measure pin 1 to pin 4: the result must exceed 11 volts. A failed check directs repair for high circuit resistance.

steps.title: Complete the low-voltage connection branch
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect the ICM connector. Repair corrosion, replace damaged or displaced terminals, and reconnect until seated and latched. Retest operation. If the concern remains, check applicable Technical Service Bulletins; without an applicable bulletin, CC6 directs ICM replacement. If operation recovers, address the connection's root cause.

steps.title: Tests CD and CE: screen for actual overcharging
steps.body: For U3003:17, self-test all modules and retrieve continuous-memory codes. Overcharging codes in multiple modules direct charging-system diagnosis. Otherwise turn off lights and accessories, run at approximately 2,000 rpm for 3 minutes and monitor battery voltage. A reading reaching 15.5 volts or higher also directs overcharging diagnosis.

steps.title: Recheck the correct high-voltage module
steps.body: If voltage remains below that threshold, cycle ignition off and on, clear continuous-memory codes and self-test the relevant module. Under CD, returning IPC U3003:17 requires the vehicle-identification-number-dependent guided routine. Under CE, returning ICM U3003:17 directs a new ICM. A code that does not return may reflect previous charging or jump-starting.

watchFor.title: Different thresholds serve different purposes
watchFor.body: The high-voltage code's trigger and the running-voltage test limit are different. Use each at its specified stage.

watchFor.title: Connector damage can imitate module trouble
watchFor.body: Use suitable terminal probes and repair pin fit or corrosion before treating a persistent complaint as an internal module fault.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3003:16 returns during Test CC.
diagnostics.meaning: The low-voltage concern requires further investigation rather than dismissal as a historical event.
diagnostics.next: Check BCM charging codes, battery condition, ICM supply, ground and connector condition in order.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3003:17 is recorded in the IPC or ICM.
diagnostics.meaning: The reporting module detected supply voltage above 16 volts for 5 seconds or longer.
diagnostics.next: Use CD for the IPC or CE for the ICM; establish whether overcharging is current before following the module-specific endpoint.

verification.title: Confirm the repeat-test outcome
verification.body: Complete the relevant module self-test and operating check after repair. A cleared historical code alone does not demonstrate a module failure.

verification.title: Record measurements and module identity
verification.body: Record the reporting module, battery and connector voltages, charging-test result and whether the code returned.

procedures.purpose: Tests CC, CD and CE for low-voltage investigation and separate IPC/ICM high-voltage decisions.
Electrical diagnostic methods and connector-testing precautions.
BCM diagnosis when CC2 retrieves charging-system codes.
ICM removal and installation when the completed diagnostic branch directs replacement.

guides.title: Diagnose audio and SYNC faults with the non-touchscreen system
guides.summary: Use the symptom and module-specific trouble-code charts to distinguish media, connection, configuration and hardware faults.
guides.introduction: The Audio Front Control Module (ACM) supplies radio and CD functions, while the Accessory Protocol Interface Module (APIM) supports SYNC voice and connected-device functions. Separate modules handle controls, the display and positioning information. Diagnosis starts by identifying the failed function, then follows the appropriate electrical or software branch.
guides.why: A diagnostic trouble code identifies a condition, not necessarily a failed module. The reporting module, fitted equipment and observable symptom determine the next action.

when.summary: When audio, SYNC, display or steering-wheel audio functions malfunction, or associated trouble codes are recorded.

prepare.title: Identify the complaint
prepare.detail: Establish body style, engine, affected speaker or input, and whether the fault affects one function or the whole system.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Have a suitable scan tool, applicable wiring information, a known-good CD when relevant, and access to programming and vehicle identification number (VIN)-dependent guided routines.

steps.title: Start with the SYNC symptom chart
steps.body: Consult it before connecting the scan tool. Follow its APIM reset referral, then the appropriate whole-system, stereo-output, mono-output, microphone, input-jack, front/rear USB or Bluetooth test if the concern remains. For individual Bluetooth features, check compatibility and device firmware. AppLink diagnosis also depends on application compatibility and the actual Bluetooth/USB connection.

steps.title: Separate reception, media and sound faults
steps.body: Poor reception or continuous seeking uses Test A for a coupe and B for a convertible. Coupe possibilities include an unavailable selected radio category, antenna grid, cable, amplifier, mounting corrosion and electrical interference. Test a faulty CD function with a known-good disc. Distortion affecting some speakers uses F; silence from all speakers uses G; ignition popping uses D; speed-compensated volume uses C.

steps.title: Locate control and speaker faults
steps.body: Choose individual speaker tests by physical location and body style. Right lower and upper steering-wheel controls use X and Y respectively. Front control interface module operation uses Z, and front control/display interface module operation uses AA. Illumination complaints follow the separate illumination diagnosis. For the right-rear speaker, Test L matches the convertible quarter-panel speaker at C396; Test M matches the coupe parcel-shelf speaker at C485. Choose the branch by the fitted location and connector.

steps.title: Read codes in their module context
steps.body: Use the reporting module's chart, retaining each code suffix. Voltage faults lead to AQ or AR; lost communication follows the named network test. For invalid received data, diagnose codes in the sending module first; if none exist, diagnose the observable symptom. A nonresponding module requires network diagnosis, including its supply and connections.

steps.title: Follow cross-system and engine branches
steps.body: Seat-heater, climate-control, rear-defogger, restraint-indicator and camera findings have their own referrals. Match the fitted equipment. Digital Audio Control Module C (DACMC) diagnosis applies only to 2.3L and 5.2L vehicles: microphone faults use AB–AD, and low-frequency noise uses E. The DACMC is integrated into the ACM.

steps.title: Correct configuration before condemning hardware
steps.body: Configuration codes call for the named module's programming procedure, generally using VIN-specific as-built data; APIM faults use APIM programming/provisioning. Capture configuration before removing a module. Reinstalling identical software does not repair hardware, and strategy updates require the applicable technical service bulletin direction.

steps.title: Follow the exact retest outcome
steps.body: Where directed, clear codes, wait at least 10 seconds and repeat the self-test. Recurring listed internal faults lead to ACM, display or positioning-module replacement, APIM Hardware Test, or a VIN-dependent front-control guided routine. Address other front-control codes first for U1000:00 and U3000:49. DACMC checksum or memory faults can require ACM replacement.

watchFor.title: Right-rear speaker identification
watchFor.body: The convertible quarter-panel speaker and coupe parcel-shelf speaker use different access procedures. Match the body style, speaker location and connector before opening trim or measuring the circuit.

watchFor.title: Protected control outputs
watchFor.body: U1000:00 indicates an output disabled by excessive current; clearing codes cannot correct the underlying short.

notes: Active noise control applies to the 2.3L; electronic sound enhancement applies to the 2.3L and 5.2L.
DACMC U3000:94 is disregarded without an observable symptom; with a symptom, follow Test E.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A56:21 appears after bezel testing.
diagnostics.meaning: The plant-oriented reception test depends on local broadcast conditions.
diagnostics.next: Disregard this code in that specific circumstance.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1D19:4B is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The ACM has overheated, potentially during extended use.
diagnostics.next: Allow it to cool and clear the code; audio can then resume.

diagnostics.finding: The APIM reports U3000:88.
diagnostics.meaning: Network communication was interrupted previously; communication is presently sufficient to report the code.
diagnostics.next: Inspect APIM wiring for damage or corrosion, clear the code, wait at least 10 seconds and repeat the network test.

diagnostics.finding: The global positioning system module reports U3000:09 again after the first clear-and-retest.
diagnostics.meaning: Its branch requires an additional power reset before replacement.
diagnostics.next: Disconnect the battery for 1 minute, reconnect, clear codes, wait at least 10 seconds and retest. Replace the module only if the code returns.

verification.title: Repeat the relevant check
verification.body: Confirm the original function and complete the prescribed self-test or network retest.

verification.title: Record the outcome
verification.body: Record the reporting module, exact codes, observed symptom and whether each returned after the directed action.

procedures.purpose: Primary SYNC symptom charts, module-specific code decisions and diagnostic routing across the listed engines.
APIM reset referral named by the symptom chart; this procedure is titled for SYNC 2/SYNC 3.
Configuration capture, programmable module installation and as-built data principles.
APIM programming for incorrect or incomplete provisioning.
ACM removal and installation when the diagnostic branch requires replacement.
Front control/display interface module removal and installation after a qualifying repeat fault.
Global positioning system module removal and installation after the required retests.
Diagnosis when a module does not respond to the scan tool.
Convertible rear quarter-panel speaker access and replacement after its diagnostic branch confirms the fault.
Coupe parcel-shelf speaker access and replacement after its diagnostic branch confirms the fault.

applicability.equipment: SYNC with six speakers and a non-touchscreen display

guides.title: Diagnose coolant-temperature and ICM oil-gauge faults
guides.summary: Use module self-tests, commanded gauge movement and engine-data checks to distinguish display faults from cooling, oil-pressure indication and communication concerns.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) displays coolant temperature using information from the powertrain control module (PCM). Vehicles with an information center module (ICM) gauge pack also display oil information. These tests separate a gauge’s ability to move from the information controlling its position, helping you follow the correct repair branch.
guides.why: A moving pointer does not establish that its incoming information is correct. Conversely, a cold or zero reading can be a communication fallback. Checking actual cooling-system operation and module faults first prevents misleading conclusions.
searchTerms: oil pressure gauge stuck at zero
SVT oil temperature gauge stays cold

when.summary: When the coolant-temperature gauge reads incorrectly or an applicable oil gauge is inoperative.
notes: The complaint must be present before following a branch that directs component replacement.

prepare.title: Provide scan-tool capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool supporting module self-tests, live parameter identifications (PIDs) and gauge commands. Have the vehicle identification number (VIN) available for guided IPC routines.

prepare.title: Establish reliable starting conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge above 70%. Inspect relevant wiring, connections, coolant and oil condition. Pressure-switch testing requires engine-running observations and access to the correct engine-specific connector.

steps.title: Choose the matching complaint
steps.body: Use Test I for an inoperative coolant gauge, J for an incorrect indication, K for an inoperative ICM oil-pressure gauge, or L for the SVT oil-temperature gauge. These are alternative diagnostic paths, not a sequence of tests every vehicle needs.

steps.title: Test I: diagnose an inoperative coolant gauge
steps.body: With ignition ON, perform the PCM self-test, then the IPC self-test, then check Gateway Module A (GWM) continuous-memory codes. Resolve findings through the engine diagnostics, IPC code chart or communications diagnostics respectively. If all pass, set ENGCOOLNT to zero/full cold and command cold–hot–cold movement. A failed sweep requires the VIN-specific IPC routine. A successful sweep directs GWM replacement, code clearing and a repeated self-test; only if the gauge remains inoperative does this branch direct PCM replacement using the appropriate engine procedure.

steps.title: Test J: investigate an incorrect coolant indication
steps.body: First verify cooling-system and thermostat operation; correct a cooling concern through engine diagnostics. Otherwise, perform PCM and IPC self-tests and follow their code routes before proceeding. Start ENGCOOLNT at full cold, then check commanded positions: 0% full cold, 15% beginning of normal, 45% center, 85% end of normal and 95% hot. These percentages command pointer positions; they are not instructions to heat the coolant to a target temperature. Incorrect movement leads to the guided IPC routine. If movement passes, start the engine and compare the rising PCM engine coolant temperature (ECT) PID with the gauge. Agreement establishes correct operation at that time; disagreement leads to the guided routine.

steps.title: Test K: command the oil-pressure gauge
steps.body: Run the ICM self-test with ignition ON; address recorded codes through its code chart. With no codes, command OIL_PRESS and watch for a 0–100–0 PSI sweep. Failure directs ICM replacement. A successful sweep leads to the pressure-switch comparison.

steps.title: Test K: compare the low-pressure warning
steps.body: Start the engine and observe the IPC low-oil-pressure warning. Switch ignition OFF before disconnecting the pressure switch: C103 for 2.3L and non-Performance Package 5.0L, C1642 for 3.7L, C1657 for Performance Package 5.0L, or C1652 for 5.2L. Restart and observe. If the warning is off connected and on disconnected, replace the ICM. Otherwise, follow Test AO for 2.3L, 3.7L and non-Performance Package 5.0L, or AP for Performance Package 5.0L and 5.2L.

steps.title: Test L: command the SVT oil-temperature gauge
steps.body: Run the ICM self-test and address codes first. Otherwise, command EOT_GAUGE_PP: the metric gauge should sweep 50–175–50°C; the English gauge should sweep 100–350–100°F. A failed sweep directs ICM replacement. A successful sweep directs diagnosis of any PCM codes through the appropriate engine procedure.

watchFor.title: A pointer can retain an old reading
watchFor.body: Missing coolant-temperature or overheat messages, or invalid temperature data, can leave the coolant gauge at its previous setting for 5 seconds or less.

notes: Use the complete applicable pinpoint test for connector details and any subsequent repair procedure.

diagnostics.finding: ICM diagnostic trouble code U0100:00 is recorded with a default gauge reading.
diagnostics.meaning: A relevant PCM message has been absent for at least 5 seconds. Oil pressure defaults to 0 PSI, SVT oil temperature to full cold, and the non-SVT vacuum-boost gauge to zero. Shorter interruptions retain the previous display.
diagnostics.next: Follow the ICM code chart. These fallback readings alone do not prove a failed gauge, PCM or actual oil-pressure condition.

verification.title: Confirm the branch result
verification.body: Check the specified sweep, warm-up comparison or warning response for the selected test. After the Test I GWM replacement branch, clear codes and repeat the self-test before deciding on the PCM.

verification.title: Record the evidence
verification.body: Record module codes, commanded versus observed movement, and the ECT comparison or connected/disconnected warning response where applicable.

procedures.purpose: Complete Tests I–L: coolant-gauge diagnosis, ICM oil-pressure testing with engine-specific branches, and SVT oil-temperature testing.
Preliminary electrical checks and correct use of module data and output commands.
Communications diagnosis when Test I finds GWM codes.
GWM removal and installation when directed by the completed Test I branch.
ICM removal and installation when directed by Test K or SVT Test L.

applicability.equipment: ICM gauge pack for oil-pressure testing; SVT with ICM gauge pack for oil-temperature testing

authoring.reviewNotes: J4 source Celsius823/English180 annotation is internally inconsistent. Root/API review agree the actual percentage-to-pointer command procedure is explicit and independently complete. This guide preserves all commanded pointer positions and does not invent a Celsius correction or physical coolant calibration threshold. J5 remains a separate PCM ECT comparison.

guides.title: Trace rear parking-aid communication faults
guides.summary: Follow Tests L–O to distinguish missing module messages, network faults and connection problems affecting rear parking aid.
guides.introduction: Rear parking aid uses ultrasonic sensors and rear-speaker tones to warn about nearby objects in reverse. Its parking assist control module (PAM) is integral to the body control module (BCM), but communicates as a separate network node. Lost messages from steering-column or information-and-entertainment modules can therefore disable parking assistance even when the bumper sensors are not the cause.
guides.why: These tests establish whether a fault is current, whether the network can reach the relevant modules and whether other modules report the same missing communication. That distinction determines whether to investigate the transmitting module or the BCM containing the PAM.

when.summary: When a rear parking-aid complaint accompanies U0212:00, U0253:00, U0256:00 or U0257:00.
notes: Use the audio/display branch matching the vehicle's fitted equipment.

prepare.title: Provide network diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of network tests, module self-tests and reading/clearing continuous-memory codes across all modules. Have Wiring Diagrams Cell 14 and the relevant connector-access procedures available.

prepare.title: Establish sound test conditions
prepare.detail: Verify battery state of charge above 70%, review previous repairs and inspect obvious wiring or connection damage. BCM replacement requires programmable module installation (PMI) capability.

steps.title: Confirm an observable concern
steps.body: Switch the ignition on and verify the complaint. Each test stops if no symptom is present: clear the code, since high network traffic or an intermittent condition may have stored it. A historical code alone does not justify replacement.

steps.title: Test the relevant network participants
steps.body: Run the network test for the module identified below and the gateway module (GWM). If either fails, follow communications-network diagnosis before continuing with the parking-aid test.

steps.title: Check module faults in order
steps.body: Perform the SCCM, APIM or FCIM self-test for L3, M3 or N3 respectively. At O3, perform the FCDIM self-test. Route module faults to steering-column or matching infotainment diagnosis. If none are recorded, check GWM continuous-memory codes; gateway faults return to network diagnosis.

steps.title: Determine whether the PAM code returns
steps.body: Clear codes, operate the system and read PAM continuous-memory codes again. If the relevant code does not return and operation is normal, the test ends. If it returns, continue to the all-module comparison.

steps.title: Compare reports across modules
steps.body: Clear all codes, turn the ignition off and on, wait 10 seconds, then retrieve continuous-memory codes from every module. The same U-code in another module directs inspection of the SCCM, APIM, FCIM or FCDIM. If only the PAM reports it, inspect the BCM connections.

steps.title: Repair the selected connections
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect that module's connectors and related in-line connections. Replace corroded or damaged terminals/connectors as directed, clean module pins and correct pushed-out pins. Reconnect and latch everything, then retest. After reconnecting the APIM, wait at least 2 minutes for re-initialization.

steps.title: Follow the supported replacement branch
steps.body: If the concern persists, check applicable technical service bulletins and follow any matching instructions. Without an applicable bulletin, the selected branch directs module replacement. The APIM branch requires its Hardware Test first. A BCM replacement also requires PMI; the PAM is not a separate replacement module.

watchFor.title: A fault disappears after reconnecting
watchFor.body: Correct the underlying terminal or connector defect rather than treating temporary recovery as proof that the connection is sound.

watchFor.title: Parking-aid menu is unavailable
watchFor.body: A MyKey restricted key prevents deactivation through the menu. That behavior alone is not a communication fault.

notes: Network paths vary: APIM and FCDIM communication uses high-speed controller area network (CAN) channels through the gateway; FCIM communication also uses the medium-speed CAN.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0212:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test L investigates communication involving the steering column control module (SCCM) and gateway.
diagnostics.next: Check their network results, SCCM self-test and gateway codes, then use the all-module comparison to select SCCM or BCM inspection.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0253:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PAM has missed accessory protocol interface module (APIM) messages for 5 seconds or more.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test M, including APIM re-initialization and the Hardware Test if its replacement branch is reached.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0256:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PAM has missed front controls interface module (FCIM) messages for 5 seconds or more.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test N to distinguish FCIM, gateway/network and BCM-side concerns.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0257:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PAM has missed front control/display interface module (FCDIM) messages for 5 seconds or more.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test O, beginning with the FCDIM network and self-test checks before the all-module comparison selects the FCDIM or BCM connection branch.

verification.title: Confirm operation and code status
verification.body: Operate parking aid under its specified reverse-gear conditions, confirm expected rear-speaker warnings and recheck the relevant PAM continuous-memory code.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Retain network results, module self-test findings and the all-module code comparison, together with whether the original symptom returned.

procedures.purpose: Rear parking-aid communication Tests L, M, N and O.
Network diagnosis when a module fails communication testing or gateway codes are present.
Investigate SCCM self-test faults encountered in Test L.
Infotainment diagnosis for the applicable SYNC 2/SYNC 3 module branch.
SCCM removal and installation only after Test L reaches replacement.
SYNC FCDIM removal and installation when Test O directs replacement.
Module configuration requirements, including the BCM replacement path.
Parking-aid operating conditions, network roles and BCM/PAM relationship.
SYNC non-touchscreen FCDIM trouble-code diagnosis for the fitted display system.

authoring.reviewNotes: Only O3 copied FCIM noun corrected to FCDIM, independently established by same-component G1960951 A7 and its original native HTML as well as own O2/O3/O7 module identity. Thresholds and replacement gates preserved.

guides.title: Diagnose a roof module, gateway or HS-CAN1 network that will not communicate
guides.summary: Check roof-module and gateway communication, then trace HS-CAN1 faults through verified measurements and supported isolation branches.
guides.introduction: Vehicle modules share commands and status over twisted pairs of communication wires. The gateway module (GWM) connects these networks. High-speed controller area networks HS-CAN1 and HS-CAN2 connect directly to the diagnostic data link connector (DLC); HS-CAN3 and the medium-speed network (MS-CAN) reach the scan tool through the gateway. These tests distinguish an isolated module communication problem from a fault affecting an entire network.
guides.why: A missing response does not prove a module has failed. Lost power, poor terminal contact or a shorted communication circuit can produce similar results. Even a poorly grounded scan tool can disrupt otherwise functioning modules.
searchTerms: roof control module not responding to scan tool
modules stop working when scan tool connected

when.summary: Use when the roof module, gateway or all HS-CAN1 modules currently fail scan-tool communication.
notes: Select optional-module branches only after confirming the vehicle has that equipment.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Record available diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), inspect previous repairs and check relevant service information.

prepare.title: Have electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool with IDS capability, a digital multimeter, approved Rotunda flex probes and Wiring Diagrams Cell 14. Access the DLC under the instrument panel and the connectors specified by the chosen test. Follow each ignition, battery-disconnection and connector-side instruction.

steps.title: Choose the test that matches the missing responses
steps.body: Use test AB for moveable roof control module B (MRCMB), AC for the gateway, or AD when all HS-CAN1 modules are unresponsive. Before AC, verify body control module (BCM) fuses 13 and 15. Keep the original complaint present during diagnosis.

steps.title: Follow AB through the roof module's electrical support
steps.body: Check supply voltage, both grounds and both MS-CAN circuits between the roof module and gateway. AB requires supply above 11 volts and the specified ground and continuity readings below 3 ohms. If supply fails, check battery junction box (BJB) fuse 15: repair the circuit if the fuse is sound, or investigate a short if it is blown. Finish with AB4 connector inspection and an operating check.

steps.title: Follow AC through the gateway's network connections
steps.body: With the negative battery cable and scan-tool cable disconnected, begin the termination tests. HS-CAN1 and HS-CAN2 checks at the DLC expect 54–66 ohms; abnormal readings lead to their respective continuity checks. The component-side MS-CAN and HS-CAN3 checks expect 108–132 ohms. Continue through the prescribed supply, ground and AC9 connector branches; retain the exact component-side versus harness-side distinctions.

steps.title: Begin AD with the diagnostic connection
steps.body: Inspect DLC terminals 4, 5, 6, 14 and 16 using the specified violet Rotunda probe 300-08039. Damage follows AD1's service-article check and, if no applicable article exists, gateway replacement route. With sound DLC terminals, inspect and repair gateway connector C2431, reconnect it securely and retest before proceeding.

steps.title: Classify the HS-CAN1 circuit fault
steps.body: Follow AD3–AD10 to distinguish termination problems, opens, shorts between the paired wires, shorts to ground and unwanted voltage. The termination branch disconnects the powertrain control module (PCM) before deciding between PCM wiring checks and gateway evaluation. If AD10 identifies an irregular intermediate resistance, wait 5 minutes and repeat the pinpoint test before its repair decision.

steps.title: Isolate a measured short
steps.body: In AD11 or AD12, disconnect modules individually in the stated sequence and watch the resistance. Include the accessory protocol interface module (APIM) and information center module (ICM) only if fitted. A qualifying change directs you to that module's connector and operation checks. If no disconnection changes the result, repair the circuit and reconnect all modules.

steps.title: Isolate communication disruption by disabling modules
steps.body: For AD13–AD18, establish the IDS session before disabling the PCM; use manual vehicle identification if necessary. Follow the specified fuse-removal sequence, restoring removed fuses at each decision. Recovery directs PCM diagnosis to test A, gateway diagnosis to AC, BCM diagnosis to I, APIM diagnosis to O, or ICM diagnosis to H. If AD16 finds neither optional module, or AD17/AD18 still fails to restore communication, stop at that unresolved branch. Restore the test configuration; these outcomes do not prove the network healthy or authorize module replacement.

steps.title: Resolve the final connector or module decision
steps.body: At the applicable endpoint, repair corrosion, damaged terminals and pushed-out pins, then seat and latch connectors and operate the system. If the concern persists, check applicable technical service bulletins before replacement. Roof module, gateway, PCM and ICM endpoints can authorize replacement; BCM and APIM endpoints require a vehicle-identification-number-based guided routine. Continue any replacement through its separate installation procedure.

watchFor.title: Symptoms appear only with the scan tool connected
watchFor.body: Spread DLC ground terminals can corrupt network traffic. Check terminal fit before treating the resulting module failures as separate faults.

watchFor.title: A repeated network test displays old results
watchFor.body: Close the network-test application before rerunning it, or IDS can display the previous results.

notes: PCM connections differ: C1551B for 2.3L, C1381B for 3.7L and C175B for 5.0L or 5.2L. Use the matching pin table and replacement procedure.
HS-CAN2 also connects directly to the DLC, but has a separate diagnostic route involving its braking, steering, restraint and other fitted modules.
An unloaded supply-voltage check detects an open circuit but does not establish that the circuit can carry its operating load.

diagnostics.finding: AD3 measures 54–66 ohms across HS-CAN1.
diagnostics.meaning: The termination reading permits the ground-short checks.
diagnostics.next: Follow AD4: readings above 1,000 ohms proceed to AD5; lower readings enter AD12. In AD5, voltage above 6 volts on either circuit requires circuit repair.

diagnostics.finding: The 108–132-ohm reading remains after disconnecting the PCM in AD7.
diagnostics.meaning: The branch requires checking the PCM-to-DLC wiring.
diagnostics.next: Follow AD8. If the reading does not remain within that range, follow AD19's gateway checks.

diagnostics.finding: Resistance between the HS-CAN1 wires is below 3 ohms, or above 10,000 ohms in the applicable branch.
diagnostics.meaning: The low reading enters short-together isolation; the high reading enters the open-circuit repair decision.
diagnostics.next: Use AD11 for the low reading or AD10's DLC/circuit repair route for the high reading.

verification.title: Confirm communication and operation
verification.body: Restore disconnected modules and removed fuses, rerun the applicable network test and operate the affected system. Address the cause of any connector fault even if reseating restored operation.

verification.title: Record the final result
verification.body: Record which modules now respond and whether the original concern remains. Clear DTCs from all modules after diagnosis because the isolation tests can generate network codes.

procedures.purpose: Exact AB roof-module, AC gateway and AD HS-CAN1 diagnostic branches, including engine-specific PCM connections.
Electrical diagnostic prerequisites, terminal probing and valid circuit measurements.
Gateway removal and installation when the completed diagnostic branch directs replacement.
2.3L PCM removal and installation following a confirmed replacement decision.
3.7L PCM removal and installation following a confirmed replacement decision.
ICM removal and installation when fitted and directed by diagnosis.

guides.title: Check 6R80 shift behavior during a controlled road test
guides.summary: Check warm, light-throttle automatic shifts in Drive on a 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine and 6R80 transmission, then use the observations to choose the next diagnostic step.
guides.introduction: The 6R80 has six forward gears and plenty of ways to make an awkward shift sound like an expensive opinion. I’ll help you put numbers to that opinion: warm the transmission, let it shift automatically in Drive, and record what actually happens. There’s no dismantling involved—the useful work starts behind the wheel.
guides.why: The transmission changes gears by directing pressurized fluid to internal clutches. Electrical valves called solenoids control that fluid under instructions from the powertrain control module, or PCM. Temperature and throttle position matter when comparing shift speeds. Many transmission performance diagnostic trouble codes, or DTCs, also need repeated fault detection before they are stored, so one uneventful drive cannot rule out an intermittent problem.

when.summary: Use this check to document an upshift, downshift or shift-timing complaint during normal driving.
notes: The result is a record of transmission behavior and a diagnostic direction, rather than identification of a failed part.
These instructions apply to the 2015 Mustang with the 2.3L, 3.7L or 5.0L engine and the 6R80 automatic transmission.

prepare.title: Choose a route that permits gentle, lawful acceleration
prepare.detail: Use roads and traffic conditions that allow normal driving without hurried acceleration or braking. Observe only the shifts that conditions safely permit. Speed limits, visibility and traffic take priority over completing every row of the chart.

prepare.title: Arrange a useful record without distracting the driver
prepare.detail: Have the shift ranges below ready for review while parked. A passenger can record observations; if driving alone, write them down only after stopping safely. Record the selector position, whether the engine and transmission were warm, throttle condition, shift involved and observed speed. No replacement parts, unplugging, lifting or underbody access are needed.

prepare.title: Understand the comparison limits before setting off
prepare.detail: This check covers warm, minimum-throttle operation in D and symptom follow-up. Both the engine and transmission must reach normal operating temperature; no fixed warm-up time or numeric temperature threshold is established for this check. The light-throttle chart is tied to a throttle-position sensor reading of 1.25 volts, but measuring that voltage requires a separate procedure. Without a confirmed reading, treat the speed comparison as indicative. The selector-2/1 test has no verified equivalent for this Mustang’s P/R/N/D/S selector: do not recreate it with the paddles. Internal testing, programming and repairs require the appropriate separate workshop procedure.

steps.title: Select normal automatic Drive
steps.body:
Begin stationary in P with the brake pedal pressed. With the engine running and the ignition in RUN, move the selector to D. Pressing the brake pedal allows the interlock to release the selector from Park.
Release the parking brake when ready to move and proceed only when the way is clear. Keep the selector in D throughout the observation run and leave the SelectShift paddles alone. D provides automatic shifts through gears 1–6. S adds manual-selection and engine-braking behavior that would change the comparison. See [Mustang selector operation](#/document/G1694284).

steps.title: Warm both the engine and transmission
steps.body: Drive normally until both reach normal operating temperature before collecting comparison readings. Keep any behavior noticed during warm-up separate from the warm test record. If transmission temperature cannot be confirmed, record that uncertainty instead of presenting the run as a confirmed warm test.

steps.title: Observe the warm upshifts with minimum throttle
steps.body:
With D still selected, apply minimum throttle and observe the vehicle speed when each automatic upshift occurs. Record the 1–2, 2–3, 3–4, 4–5 and 5–6 changes only as lawful speeds and traffic allow.
Let the transmission make the changes itself. If you cannot confidently identify a particular shift, mark it uncertain rather than assigning it a speed. Note a missing shift or unusual shift behavior and the conditions in which it occurred. The transmission doesn’t get to turn a vague impression into a parts order. See [Road Testing Vehicle](#/document/G1686459).

steps.title: End the observation run and park safely
steps.body:
Finish the run when the useful observations are collected or conditions stop permitting the check. If the vehicle’s behavior makes continued driving unsafe, stop at a safe location instead of trying to finish the chart.
Come to a complete stop, hold the foot brake, select P and apply the parking brake before releasing the foot brake. Review or write down the results while parked.

steps.title: Compare each observed upshift with the matching light-throttle range
steps.body:
The light-throttle rows in [Road Testing Vehicle](#/document/G1686459) use a throttle-position sensor voltage of 1.25 volts:
1–2: 13–21 km/h (8–13 mph).
2–3: 26–34 km/h (16–21 mph).
3–4: 35–43 km/h (22–27 mph).
4–5: 56–64 km/h (35–40 mph).
5–6: 71–79 km/h (44–49 mph).
Place your observed speed alongside the corresponding change. Keep an unobserved shift marked unobserved. If throttle voltage was not established, retain that qualification with any apparent discrepancy. A gentle right foot is useful, but it isn’t a voltmeter.

steps.title: Use the result to choose the next diagnostic step
steps.body:
If the transmission failed to upshift or downshift, take the record to [Diagnosis By Symptom](#/document/G1686447). Include any downshift failure already encountered during normal driving, identifying the affected change when known. That procedure is the next diagnostic destination; the road test alone does not establish the cause.
Many performance-related DTCs require repeated detections, sometimes consecutively and up to five times, before being stored. This explains why a fault may exist without a stored code after one run. It is not a requirement to repeat a malfunction five times or to continue driving until a code appears.

watchFor.title: Traffic and vehicle behavior decide when the test ends
watchFor.body: Do not chase a missing chart entry through traffic, exceed a speed limit or repeat unsafe behavior to obtain a code. Record the limitation and carry it into the diagnostic handoff.

watchFor.title: Closed-throttle speeds are a separate reference
watchFor.body:
The closed-throttle rows in [Road Testing Vehicle](#/document/G1686459) list these downshift ranges:
6–5: 56–64 km/h (35–40 mph).
5–4: 40–48 km/h (25–30 mph).
4–3: 13–21 km/h (8–13 mph).
3–2: 3–11 km/h (2–7 mph).
2–1: 2–6 km/h (1–4 mph).
Keep these separate from the light-throttle upshift comparison. They are reference data, not an additional maneuver sequence for this check.

watchFor.title: Wide-open-throttle speeds are workshop reference data
watchFor.body:
The wide-open-throttle rows in [Road Testing Vehicle](#/document/G1686459) list:
1–2: 45–53 km/h (28–33 mph).
2–3: 87–95 km/h (54–59 mph).
3–4: 140–148 km/h (87–92 mph).
These values are not instructions to reproduce those speeds on public roads and are not part of this normal-D, light-throttle test.

notes: In P, a mechanical parking pawl locks the transmission output shaft. In N, that shaft is free to turn. This road test requires D while driving and does not require selecting Neutral.

The 6R80 can retain 3rd or 5th gear hydraulically after a total loss of electronic control or electrical power, depending on the gear selected when the failure occurred. This is useful context for a single-gear complaint, but the road observation cannot confirm that failure mode. See [Transmission Description](#/document/G1686444).

diagnostics.finding: The transmission fails to upshift or downshift.
diagnostics.meaning: A shifting failure has been observed, but its mechanical, hydraulic or electrical cause remains undetermined.
diagnostics.next: Record the affected shift, selector position, temperature condition, throttle condition and speed. Continue with [Diagnosis By Symptom](#/document/G1686447). Stop the road check if continued driving is unsafe.

diagnostics.finding: An upshift appears outside its light-throttle speed range.
diagnostics.meaning: The observation differs from the chart, but the comparison depends on the warm operating condition and 1.25-volt throttle-position condition.
diagnostics.next: Retain the actual reading and any uncertainty about temperature or throttle voltage. Use the documented complaint for symptom-based follow-up; do not select replacement parts from shift speed alone.

diagnostics.finding: All confidently observed warm upshifts fall within the listed ranges.
diagnostics.meaning: Those shifts agree with the reference under the recorded conditions. This does not settle an intermittent complaint or cover shifts that were not observed.
diagnostics.next: Keep the record, identify any remaining complaint and pursue symptom-based diagnosis if the concern persists.

diagnostics.finding: No performance DTC is reported after one drive.
diagnostics.meaning: The fault-detection requirements may not have been met; some faults need multiple, sometimes consecutive, detections.
diagnostics.next: Preserve the symptom record. Do not declare the transmission fault-free from the absence of a code or keep reproducing unsafe behavior to obtain one.

diagnostics.finding: Traffic, speed limits or uncertainty prevent observation of a shift.
diagnostics.meaning: That shift has not been assessed.
diagnostics.next: Mark it unobserved or uncertain. Do not fill the gap with an assumed result.

diagnostics.finding: The transmission appears to remain in one gear.
diagnostics.meaning: A retained gear can occur during a control-system failure, but this observation does not establish either the gear or the cause.
diagnostics.next: Record what happened, end the run if driving is unsafe, and use [Diagnosis By Symptom](#/document/G1686447) for the next investigation.

verification.title: Confirm the test conditions are recorded
verification.body: The record should identify D-range operation, warm-up status, minimum-throttle operation and whether the chart’s 1.25-volt throttle condition was confirmed.

verification.title: Separate observations from conclusions
verification.body: List the observed shift speeds, missing or uncertain observations, and any failure to upshift or downshift. A comparison with the chart is complete only for the shifts and conditions actually observed. These are checks of the observation record, not additional transmission tests.

verification.title: Leave the car parked and the next action clear
verification.body: Finish stationary with P selected and the parking brake applied. A confirmed shifting failure proceeds to symptom-based diagnosis; a normal observation remains a record of that run rather than proof that every transmission function is healthy.

Mustang-specific selector positions, brake shift interlock operation, automatic Drive operation and the distinction between D and SelectShift operation in S.
Explanation of hydraulic and electronic gear control and retained-gear behavior during loss of control or electrical power.

authoring.reviewNotes: Matched all light-throttle shift-speed values to the exact original structured Km/h and MPH table columns. No source values or conversions changed; the incompatible manual2/1 selector operation remains excluded.

guides.title: Diagnose driver power-seat and memory faults
guides.summary: Separate driver-seat switch, motor, wiring, voltage and communication faults, and perform preliminary checks for inoperative climate-controlled seats.
guides.introduction: A driver seat without memory reverses its adjustment motors directly through the control switch. A memory seat instead uses the driver front seat module (DSM) to power the motors and track their positions. These tests distinguish faults in those arrangements; the heating and cooling checks address a separate seat system.
guides.why: A disabled seat does not automatically need a motor or module. Supply faults can inhibit memory operation, while disturbed seat wiring also brings Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) precautions into the job.
searchTerms: driver power seat will not move
seat moves forward but will not raise

when.summary: When driver-seat adjustment or memory fails, relevant codes are recorded, or fitted seat heating/cooling is inoperative.
notes: Select the test for the fitted equipment and current complaint before considering replacement.

prepare.title: Electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool supporting module self-tests and network tests, a digital multimeter, required Rotunda Flex Probes and the correct wiring diagrams. Check battery and charging operation; initial battery state of charge must exceed 70%.

prepare.title: Safe seat-connector access
prepare.detail: This work requires controlled live measurements and exact SRS depowering and repowering procedures. Follow the specified ignition and connector states, and isolate power for resistance measurements using Diagnostic Methods.

steps.title: Establish the complaint and test branch
steps.body: Record affected movements and module diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Inspect wiring, connectors and previous repairs. Use Test F for a driver seat without memory, G/H for DSM voltage codes, and I for lost body-module communication. Do not replace components for an absent concern.

steps.title: Test F: separate common supply faults from individual motor faults
steps.body: Follow SRS depowering, disconnect driver airbag in-line connector C3206, then test all directions. If every direction fails, check switch supply, battery junction box (BJB) fuse 12 (30A), and ground. The tests require greater than 11 volts and less than 3 ohms respectively. If these pass, replace the switch. For one failed axis, check motor voltage in both directions; polarity reverses. Correct voltage directs horizontal-motor replacement, but either height-motor fault requires a seat track. Otherwise test both motor wires: good continuity directs switch replacement; failed continuity requires circuit repair.

steps.title: Test G: investigate B1317 before condemning the DSM
steps.body: Check all modules for B1317, B1676 or P0563. Codes in multiple modules direct charging-system diagnosis. Otherwise switch accessories off and monitor battery voltage with the engine at approximately 2,000 rpm for 3 minutes. Reaching 15 volts also directs charging diagnosis. If it does not, cycle ignition, clear continuous-memory codes and run the DSM self-test. Replace the DSM only if B1317 returns.

steps.title: Test H: trace persistent B1318 through power, ground and connections
steps.body: Clear codes and repeat the DSM self-test. If B1318 returns, check powertrain control module charging codes, then battery condition and full charge. Record battery voltage before the specified SRS depowering and connector disconnections. Check both DSM feeds for greater than 11 volts. With ignition off and battery negative disconnected, check both grounds for less than 3 ohms. Repair failed circuits. After reconnecting the battery, inspect and repair DSM terminals, latch connectors and retest, leaving C3206 disconnected. Persistent trouble requires an applicable technical service bulletin check through OASIS before DSM replacement.

steps.title: Test I: establish whether U0140 is a current network problem
steps.body: With an observable symptom, run the network test; DSM nonresponse directs Communications Network diagnosis. If it responds, address B1317/B1318 first, then clear codes and repeat the DSM self-test. Consider incomplete programmable module installation (PMI) after previous module replacement. If U0140 persists, clear codes, cycle ignition, wait 10 seconds and retrieve all-module codes. U0140/U0140:00 elsewhere directs the vehicle-identification-number-dependent body control module (BCM) guided routine; a DSM-only recurrence directs DSM replacement.

steps.title: Begin the separate climate-seat checks
steps.body: For one or both climate-controlled seats inoperative, verify BJB fuse 14 (30A). Normal operation requires the engine running; scan-tool commands can operate the system with ignition on in 15-second intervals. The front seat climate control module (SCME) has constant power and internally joined feeds, so one open feed may not stop both seats. A seat-specific DTC disables only that seat. Continue climate-seat diagnosis of wiring, control requests and the module after these preliminary checks.

watchFor.title: Use the driver-seat connector
watchFor.body: C352 is the driver front-seat control switch. For the rear-height continuity check, match C352 pin 8 to C363 pin 3 and C352 pin 10 to C363 pin 1. Keep the specified airbag isolation and electrical test conditions in place.

watchFor.title: Unsafe SRS handling
watchFor.body: Incorrect repair actions can deploy an airbag. Follow the complete depowering instructions before disconnecting or restoring C3206.

notes: A new DSM requires PMI. Memory-seat hard/soft stops must also be set or reset after replacement of the DSM, driver track or horizontal motor.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1317 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: DSM input exceeded 15 volts, disabling memory outputs; earlier charging or jump starting can leave this code stored.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test G and distinguish a recurring fault from historical storage.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1318 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: DSM input fell below 10 volts, disabling memory outputs; a previously discharged battery can explain a nonrecurring code.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test H through the battery, supply, ground and connector decisions.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0140 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The DSM lost BCM communication for at least 15 seconds while DSM input remained between 10 and 15 volts.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test I; without an observable symptom or recurring code, intermittent network conditions remain possible.

verification.title: Restore and prove out the SRS
verification.body: After the applicable F/H work, depower as directed, reconnect C3206 and all disconnected connectors, then repower. An unsuccessful SRS prove-out requires SRS diagnosis.

verification.title: Confirm and record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Recheck affected operation and the applicable self-test. Retain the recorded battery voltage, circuit results and returning codes so the repair decision follows the measured fault.

guides.title: Diagnose missing turn-signal chimes and dashboard communication faults
guides.summary: Trace a missing turn-signal chime or lost engine and cruise-control messages through the correct dashboard and network tests.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) coordinates warning sounds and displays using information from other modules. It produces the turn-signal tick-tock itself, while most other chimes normally use audio speakers. These tests distinguish a chime complaint from missing network information and keep IPC faults separate from faults recorded by an information center module (ICM), where fitted.
guides.why: A communication code identifies information that did not arrive, not necessarily a failed receiving module. Comparing reports from several modules helps distinguish a shared communication problem from a local connection fault.
searchTerms: turn signal left on warning silent

when.summary: The turn-signal warning sound is missing, or the IPC or fitted ICM records a relevant communication fault.
notes: Use Test BO only with an ICM fitted. Cruise-module testing requires confirmed matching equipment.

prepare.title: Prepare for module diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of network tests and individual-module self-tests, good lighting and connector-repair capability. Have the vehicle identification number available for the IPC guided routine.

prepare.title: Check the electrical baseline
prepare.detail: Verify battery state of charge exceeds 70%, check charging operation and review recent repairs. Record the complaint and initial codes before clearing them.

steps.title: Test BM: establish which chime function is missing
steps.body: Perform the OFF-to-RUN check with the driver's belt unbuckled: the belt warning should sound for approximately 6 seconds. If it does not, use the vehicle-specific IPC guided routine. If it does, check both turn indicators; incorrect operation leads to Test S. With indicators working, run the body control module (BCM) self-test. Diagnose recorded BCM codes; otherwise diagnose gateway module (GWM) codes.

steps.title: Begin BN or BO with the correct receiving module
steps.body: For U0100:00, first establish a scan-tool vehicle session. Failure leads to communications-network diagnosis. With ignition on, use BN for the IPC or BO for the ICM: run its self-test, clear codes, wait 10 seconds and repeat. If U0100:00 does not return, the fault is not currently reproduced.

steps.title: Test BN: trace missing engine messages to the IPC
steps.body: If the code returns, test the powertrain control module (PCM) and diagnose its codes using the engine-specific procedure. Next address IPC codes U3003:16 or U3003:17 through the IPC chart, then GWM codes. Clear all codes, cycle ignition off/on, wait 10 seconds and retrieve all-module continuous-memory results. U0100:00 in the anti-lock brake system (ABS) module or U0100:87 in the BCM selects PCM connector checks; otherwise inspect the IPC connection.

steps.title: Test BO: trace missing engine messages to the ICM
steps.body: For returning ICM U0100:00, diagnose PCM self-test codes, then ICM U3003:16 or U3003:17 through the ICM chart. Clear all codes, cycle ignition off/on, wait 10 seconds and retrieve all-module results. U0100:00 in the IPC or ABS module, or U0100:87 in the BCM, selects PCM connector checks. Otherwise inspect the ICM connection.

steps.title: Test BP: establish the cruise communication fault
steps.body: Test BP applies only to a vehicle fitted with adaptive cruise and its cruise control module (CCM). For IPC U0104:00, first confirm an observable symptom. Without one, clear the code and stop. Otherwise network-test the CCM; nonresponse leads to network diagnosis. Diagnose CCM self-test codes through adaptive-cruise diagnosis, then GWM codes and IPC U3003:16 or U3003:17. A base-cruise complaint uses the separate base-cruise diagnostic article; do not test or replace a CCM that the car does not have.

steps.title: Locate a returning cruise-message fault
steps.body: On the adaptive-cruise branch, clear the IPC codes, wait 10 seconds and repeat its self-test. If U0104:00 returns, clear all codes, cycle ignition off/on, wait 10 seconds and retrieve all-module results. The same code in the ABS module selects CCM connector checks; otherwise inspect the IPC connection. For faults following module replacement, investigate incorrect or omitted programmable module installation and configuration.

steps.title: Complete the selected connector and module decision
steps.body: Switch ignition off before disconnecting the selected module. Repair corrosion, damaged or bent pins and pushed-out terminals; reconnect securely and operate the system. If the concern persists, check applicable technical service bulletins through OASIS first. Without an applicable bulletin, follow the selected PCM, ICM or adaptive-cruise CCM replacement procedure, or the vehicle-specific IPC guided routine. If reconnection restores operation, correct the underlying connection fault.

watchFor.title: Chime priority can affect what you hear
watchFor.body: A higher-priority warning can replace or delay another chime. Note other warnings sounding when the complaint occurs.

watchFor.title: Historical codes are not replacement instructions
watchFor.body: Do not replace a module when the required concern is absent during testing.

notes: Base cruise uses its own PCM/SCCM diagnostic path. CCM connector work, replacement and radar alignment apply only to fitted adaptive-cruise hardware. PCM work requires the procedure for the selected engine.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0100:00 is recorded in the IPC or ICM.
diagnostics.meaning: PCM messages have been missing for 5 seconds or longer. The IPC receives those messages through the GWM.
diagnostics.next: Choose BN or BO by the module recording the code, then establish whether it returns.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0104:00 is recorded in the IPC.
diagnostics.meaning: CCM messages received through the GWM have been missing for 5 seconds or longer.
diagnostics.next: On a vehicle fitted with adaptive cruise, begin BP with symptom verification and the CCM network test. For a base-cruise complaint, use its separate diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0121:00 is recorded in the IPC.
diagnostics.meaning: ABS module messages received through the GWM have been missing for 5 seconds or longer.
diagnostics.next: Continue the corresponding communication diagnosis; this finding alone does not justify ABS module replacement.

verification.title: Recheck the complaint
verification.body: After connector repair, confirm secure latching and operate the affected system to determine whether the original symptom remains.

verification.title: Keep the repeated results
verification.body: Record which module reported each code and whether it returned after the prescribed clearing, waiting and ignition sequence. A nonreturning code may reflect intermittent communication or high network traffic.
