applicability.equipment: ICM for its receiving-module tests; adaptive cruise control for the CCM communication branch

authoring.reviewNotes: BP1–BP9 is a CCM communication path for fitted adaptive-cruise hardware. The base-cruise referral under BP3 incorrectly points to the adaptive section. Base cruise has separate PCM/SCCM operation and diagnosis, while the adaptive system explicitly includes CCM. Explicitly limit BP/CCM self-test, connector and replacement guidance to a car fitted with adaptive-cruise hardware. Route base cruise complaints to G1693138; never run CCM tests or replace a nonexistent CCM on base cruise. Preserve all supported BP code/voltage/connector decision conditions, and include G1693160 replacement with required alignment/configuration only when that path establishes it. Do not guess an IPC guided routine action. Other BO/BN/BM tasks in the mixed guide retain their own scope.

guides.title: Diagnose a brake warning that stays on or lighting indicators that disagree with the lamps
guides.summary: Trace brake and lighting indicator complaints through switch inputs, module messages and commanded cluster operation.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) turns vehicle information into visible warnings. For example, the body control module (BCM) sends a low-brake-fluid warning through the gateway module (GWM). These checks distinguish an input or communication problem from an indicator that cannot respond correctly.
guides.why: A working exterior lamp and its dashboard indicator depend on different parts of the system. Checking actual lamp operation, stored faults and commanded outputs helps locate the failure before choosing a repair.
searchTerms: low beam malfunction indicator always on

when.summary: When the brake warning stays on, or a lighting indicator remains on or off regardless of actual lamp operation.
notes: Reproduce the concern before following a component-replacement decision.
Use the low-beam malfunction and front fog-lamp branches only where the corresponding equipment is fitted.

prepare.title: Prepare for module and circuit testing
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool with module self-tests, live data and IPC output commands, a digital multimeter, fused jumper and the specified Rotunda Flex Probes. This work requires connector identification and terminal-repair skills.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge greater than 70%. Inspect previous repairs, wiring and connectors. Disconnect the battery and isolate circuits for resistance measurements; restore power for the specified powered checks.

steps.title: Q: establish the brake-warning fault path
steps.body: With ignition on, run the IPC self-test and follow its code chart for recorded faults. Otherwise test the BCM and use the code branches below. If clear, check GWM continuous-memory codes, then run the anti-lock brake system (ABS) self-test. Refer faults to network or ABS diagnosis respectively. If all are clear, continue with the vehicle identification number (VIN)-specific IPC guided routine.

steps.title: Q5–Q7: separate the parking-brake switch from its wiring
steps.body: Compare the BCM PARK_BRK_SW parameter identification (PID) with the released parking brake. Agreement leads to Q12. Otherwise switch ignition off, disconnect C306, then switch on and reread it. A released indication now directs switch replacement. If still incorrect, follow Q7 with ignition off and BCM C2280E disconnected: its input-circuit resistance check selects wiring repair or Q12.

steps.title: Q8–Q11: investigate the brake-fluid input
steps.body: For Q8, switch ignition off, disconnect C124 and fit the specified fused jumper between pins 1 and 2. Switch on and observe the warning. Illumination directs reservoir or master-cylinder replacement as required. Remove the jumper in either outcome. If the warning remains off, switch ignition off for Q9: C124 pin 2 to ground must measure less than 3 ohms. For Q10, disconnect BCM C2280F; C124 pin 1 to C2280F pin 28 must also measure less than 3 ohms. Repair an open identified by either check. If both pass, keep both connectors disconnected and ignition off. Check the isolated input conductor, C124 pin 1, to ground: greater than 10,000 ohms leads to Q12; otherwise repair the circuit. Pin 2 is the permanent chassis return and is not the input conductor tested for an unwanted ground.

steps.title: Q12: inspect BCM connections and reassess
steps.body: With ignition off, inspect all BCM connectors. Correct corrosion, damaged or bent terminals and pushed-out pins; reconnect and latch securely. Operate the system again. If the concern persists, follow any applicable technical service bulletin; otherwise continue to the VIN-specific BCM guided routine.

steps.title: R: test the low-beam malfunction indicator
steps.body: Check actual low beams first; faulty lamps require headlamp diagnosis. With lamps working, check GWM codes, then the IPC self-test, following their diagnostic referrals when codes appear. If clear, command the light-emitting diode (LED) low-beam malfunction indicator on and off using A_F_LIGHT_F.

steps.title: S: test turn, fog or high-beam indication
steps.body: Check the corresponding exterior lamps first and follow their lighting diagnosis if faulty. Otherwise check GWM codes, then IPC self-test results. With no codes, command the appropriate indicator: F_FOG_IND, HIGH_BEAM, LH_TURN_L for left-hand turn or RH_TURN_L for right-hand turn.

steps.title: T: test the lights-on indicator
steps.body: Select PARKLAMP, switch ignition on and observe the parking lamps. A lamp fault leads to parking, rear and license-plate lamp diagnosis. Otherwise perform the IPC self-test, then check GWM codes. With no codes, command SIDELIGHT_LMP on and off.

watchFor.title: Unprotected jumper connections
watchFor.body: Use the fused jumper only at Q8's specified terminals. Unrequested power or ground connections can damage module circuits.

watchFor.title: A concern that disappears after reconnection
watchFor.body: Find and correct the connector defect's root cause; reseating alone may leave an intermittent fault.

notes: For R–T, missing status messages hold the last indication for less than 5 seconds, then default the indicator off.

The malfunction indicator lamp (MIL) holds its last state for a missing or invalid request shorter than 5 seconds, but defaults on after a request is missing for 5 seconds or longer. Communication, GWM, powertrain control module and IPC concerns require separate MIL diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: The BCM records diagnostic trouble code B1048:01.
diagnostics.meaning: The brake-fluid switch branch requires testing.
diagnostics.next: Follow Q8.

diagnostics.finding: The BCM records diagnostic trouble code B1048:7B.
diagnostics.meaning: This branch directs brake-fluid reservoir or master-cylinder replacement.
diagnostics.next: Install the new component as required using the linked brake procedure.

diagnostics.finding: The BCM records diagnostic trouble code C1D00:11.
diagnostics.meaning: The parking-brake input requires evaluation.
diagnostics.next: Begin Q5.

diagnostics.finding: An R, S or T indicator follows both scan-tool commands.
diagnostics.meaning: The cluster output responds.
diagnostics.next: Diagnose all BCM codes. If either command fails, use the VIN-specific IPC guided routine.

verification.title: Check operation
verification.body: Reoperate the affected system after connector repairs and observe whether the original concern remains.

verification.title: Record the decision
verification.body: Retain module codes, PID observations and command responses. Record the measured ground, input continuity and input-isolation results before following the applicable module checks.

BCM fault diagnosis at the directed branches.

Front fog-lamp diagnosis.

authoring.reviewNotes: Q11 repeats the ground terminal from Q9 even though it is checking the isolated input conductor. C124 pin2 is a permanent GD120 connection to G104; removing BCM C2280F does not isolate that chassis return. Q10 explicitly identifies C124pin1 to C2280Fpin28 as the brake-fluid input. Native060-002 and both terminal tables independently bind that exact CMC19 GY/VT input conductor, with no other connected branch, while pin2 remains hard-grounded.

guides.title: Diagnose instrument-cluster and information-center communication faults
guides.summary: Trace missing ABS, body-control and gateway messages to the appropriate network, connector or module diagnostic branch.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) uses information from other modules to operate gauges, warning displays and chime requests. Its message center makes those warnings more informative. The gateway module (GWM) carries messages between networks. These tests investigate where information stops arriving, with a separate branch for the information center module (ICM) where fitted.
guides.why: A lost-communication code identifies missing messages, not necessarily a failed sender. Battery voltage, module configuration and connector faults can produce similar results. Comparing reports from several modules helps distinguish a shared communication problem from one affecting a single receiver.

when.summary: Use when an observable instrumentation concern accompanies U0121:00, U0140:00 or U0146:00.
notes: Identify which module recorded the code: U0140:00 has different IPC and ICM routes.

prepare.title: Scan capability and vehicle history
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting network tests, individual module self-tests and all-module continuous-memory codes. Review previous module replacement and programming, and arrange access to vehicle-identification-number guided routines if needed.

prepare.title: Electrical baseline
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge above 70%. Inspect relevant wiring and connectors; use suitable terminal probes if electrical measurements become necessary.

steps.title: Establish whether the concern is present
steps.body: With ignition on, verify an observable symptom. Each of [Tests BQ–BT](#/document/G1693940) stops if none is present: clear the code and record that the system currently operates normally. High network traffic or an intermittent condition may explain the stored result.

steps.title: Check the message source before the display
steps.body: BQ tests communication with the anti-lock brake system (ABS) module, then runs its self-test; ABS codes divert to ABS and stability-control diagnosis. BR and BS network-test and self-test the body control module (BCM), diverting BCM codes to its diagnosis. BT checks gateway communication. A module failing the network test requires network diagnosis first. BQ, BR and BT also divert recorded gateway memory codes to network diagnosis.

steps.title: Resolve voltage and configuration concerns before retesting
steps.body: Check the receiving module for U3003:16 or U3003:17 and follow its code chart first. Review Programmable Module Installation (PMI) if modules were recently replaced. BQ, BR and BT then clear codes, wait 10 seconds and repeat the IPC self-test. For BS, clear the ICM codes, wait 10 seconds and repeat the ICM self-test. If U0140:00 returns, continue to BS6; if it does not, record that the ICM communication concern is not present at this time.

steps.title: Compare reports after a controlled reset
steps.body: When the applicable communication code persists, BQ, BR and BS clear all codes, switch ignition off and on, wait 10 seconds, then retrieve all-module continuous-memory results. Use the distinctions below to choose the sender or receiver connector check. Keep the originating module attached to every recorded code.

steps.title: Repair connections at the selected endpoint
steps.body: Switch ignition off before disconnecting the specified module. Inspect for corrosion, bent or damaged terminals and pushed-out pins. Replace affected connectors or terminals and clean module pins as directed. Reconnect securely, then operate the system. If the concern disappears, address the underlying connector fault rather than ending with a temporary reseat.

steps.title: Escalate only after the endpoint checks
steps.body: For a persistent concern, check applicable Technical Service Bulletins before proceeding. IPC and BCM endpoints require their guided routines. BQ permits ABS replacement at its ABS endpoint; BS permits ICM replacement at its ICM endpoint once that branch is established.

steps.title: Preserve Test BT’s gateway-first sequence
steps.body: BT checks gateway connectors before considering the IPC. If its persistent-fault branch directs gateway replacement, clear codes and repeat the IPC self-test afterward. Continue to BT7’s IPC connector check only if U0146:00 remains.

watchFor.title: Incorrect or omitted programming
watchFor.body: A communication code appearing after module replacement may reflect incorrect configuration or incomplete PMI.

watchFor.title: Identical codes in different receivers
watchFor.body: An IPC result and an ICM result are not interchangeable; retain their separate diagnostic records.

notes: Use the ICM branch only where that module is fitted.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0121:00 remains in the IPC after the BQ retest.
diagnostics.meaning: The ABS-related communication concern remains despite the preceding network, source-module and voltage checks.
diagnostics.next: BQ7 selects the ABS connector endpoint if the BCM also records U0121:87 after the reset; otherwise it selects the IPC endpoint.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0140:00 is recorded in the IPC.
diagnostics.meaning: BCM messages arriving through the gateway have been missing for 5 seconds or longer.
diagnostics.next: Follow BR. After its reset, the same code in the ABS, accessory protocol interface module (APIM) or restraints control module (RCM) selects the BCM endpoint; otherwise select IPC.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0140:00 is recorded in the ICM.
diagnostics.meaning: The ICM has missed BCM messages for 5 seconds or longer.
diagnostics.next: Follow BS using the ICM as the receiving module. Its later comparison selects BCM if IPC, ABS, APIM or RCM also records U0140:00; otherwise it selects ICM.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0146:00 is recorded in the IPC.
diagnostics.meaning: Gateway messages have been missing for 5 seconds or longer.
diagnostics.next: Follow BT through gateway network and memory-code checks, then its gateway-before-IPC endpoint sequence.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0151:00 is recorded in the IPC.
diagnostics.meaning: RCM messages arriving through the gateway have been missing for 5 seconds or longer; network, voltage, gateway, RCM or IPC concerns remain possible.
diagnostics.next: Continue with the dedicated U0151:00 diagnostic route; this code description does not establish a replacement decision.

verification.title: Confirm the symptom and code outcome
verification.body: Operate the system after connector repairs and perform the branch-specific repeat self-test. A code that does not return supports normal operation at that time.

verification.title: Record the decision evidence
verification.body: Save the original symptom, originating module, network results and post-reset codes, including any corroborating code in another module.

The same source independently writes the ICM clear/wait/repeat sequence in BV6. That evidence establishes the module identity only; no BV code or routing is borrowed.

guides.title: Diagnose instrument-cluster communication and low-voltage faults
guides.summary: Trace steering-column, blind-spot, power-steering and cluster supply faults through network tests, module self-tests and targeted electrical checks.
guides.introduction: The instrument panel cluster (IPC) presents gauges and warning messages and coordinates warning chimes using information from other modules. A communication code can therefore describe missing information from elsewhere in the vehicle. These tests separate message-source faults, network problems, poor connections and inadequate voltage before directing further module work.
guides.why: A stored code alone does not establish a failed module. Checking the active symptom, message sender and power supply first prevents an intermittent connection or battery problem from being mistaken for cluster failure.

when.summary: When the cluster records one of these communication, steering-data or low-voltage codes.
notes: Use the blind-spot branch only where the corresponding side obstacle detection modules are fitted.

prepare.title: Diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting network tests, module self-tests, continuous-memory diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) and live data. Have the vehicle identification number (VIN) and access to applicable technical service bulletins and guided routines.

prepare.title: Electrical preparation
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation; initial battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Live measurements require a digital multimeter, Rotunda Flex Probes, Wiring Diagrams Cell 60 and competence in terminal-safe voltage testing.

steps.title: Confirm the communication complaint
steps.body: For BY, BZ and CA, turn the ignition ON and confirm an observable symptom. If none is present, clear the code and stop that branch: network traffic or an intermittent condition may have caused it. CB starts with its own code recheck below.

steps.title: Check the message path before the cluster
steps.body: Network-test the module identified by the applicable test, then run its self-test. A failed network test leads to Communications Network diagnosis; sender-module codes lead to steering-column, blind-spot or power-steering diagnosis respectively. In BY and BZ, also check gateway module (GWM) continuous-memory codes. Next run the IPC self-test: U3003:16 or U3003:17 takes priority through the IPC code chart. Otherwise clear codes, wait 10 seconds and repeat the IPC self-test. A code that does not return ends this branch.

steps.title: BY: separate steering-column and cluster concerns
steps.body: If U0212:00 returns, clear all codes, switch ignition OFF then ON, wait 10 seconds and retrieve continuous-memory results from all modules. U0212:87 in the body control module (BCM) selects steering column control module (SCCM) connector checks; its absence selects IPC connector checks. Apply the connector process below before either module decision.

steps.title: BZ: follow the affected blind-spot side
steps.body: For returning U0232:00 or U0233:00, inspect the corresponding left or right side obstacle detection control module (SODL or SODR) connections. If the concern survives connector repairs and no applicable bulletin changes the repair, replace that module using its removal-and-installation procedure. Clear codes and repeat the IPC self-test; a remaining code leads to BZ8 IPC connector checks.

steps.title: CA: investigate the steering-data sender
steps.body: For returning U0420:82, inspect power steering control module (PSCM) connections. If the concern persists, check applicable bulletins, then follow the power-steering symptom chart and VIN-specific guided routine. Clear codes and repeat the IPC self-test. If the same U0420:82 returns, continue to CA7 IPC connector checks. Retain the existing symptom-chart, bulletin and VIN-guided steering diagnosis before this retest.

steps.title: CB: establish battery condition and compare voltages
steps.body: With ignition ON, clear codes, wait 10 seconds and repeat the IPC self-test. If U3003:16 disappears, a previous low-battery condition may explain it. If it remains, run the BCM self-test and diagnose charging-system codes first. With no such codes, verify a healthy, fully charged battery; diagnose any discharge. Record battery voltage and compare it with the IPC MODULE_VOLT parameter identification (PID). A difference within 0.2 volt leads to CB7 connector inspection; otherwise continue to CB5.

steps.title: CB: distinguish supply and ground resistance
steps.body: Turn ignition OFF, disconnect IPC connector C220, then turn ignition ON. CB5 measures C220 pin 8 to ground and requires greater than 11 volts; otherwise repair high circuit resistance. If it passes, CB6 measures pin 8 to pin 3 and also requires greater than 11 volts. A failed result directs circuit repair; a pass leads to CB7.

steps.title: Repair connections before escalation
steps.body: Switch ignition OFF before disconnecting the selected module. Replace corroded connectors or terminals and clean module pins; replace damaged, bent or pushed-out pins as required. Reconnect and latch securely, then operate the system. If restored, address the underlying connector damage. Persistent concerns require bulletin review before replacement or guided diagnosis. BY8 permits SCCM replacement when no bulletin applies; IPC endpoints require the VIN-specific routine.

watchFor.title: Recent module replacement
watchFor.body: Missing or incorrect Programmable Module Installation (PMI) configuration can cause returning communication codes.

watchFor.title: Repairing a message sender does not finish the receiver check
watchFor.body: After the power-steering concern is addressed, repeat the IPC self-test and check specifically for U0420:82 before following the cluster connector branch.

notes: The information center module (ICM) also records U3003:16 for supply voltage below 9 volts for 5 seconds or longer. CB's C220 measurements apply to the IPC, not the ICM.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0212:00 is recorded in the IPC.
diagnostics.meaning: Test BY investigates the steering-column communication path.
diagnostics.next: Confirm the symptom, test SCCM communication and use the BCM U0212:87 decision to select the connector branch.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0232:00 or U0233:00 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Left or right obstacle-module messages through the gateway have been missing for 5 seconds or longer.
diagnostics.next: Use Test BZ for the indicated side; the code alone does not justify replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0420:82 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The steering-data alive/sequence counter is incorrect or not updated; the trigger describes missing steering data for 5 seconds or longer.
diagnostics.next: Follow CA through PSCM checks and guided steering diagnosis, then clear codes and repeat the IPC self-test. Returning U0420:82 leads to CA7.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U3003:16 is recorded in the IPC.
diagnostics.meaning: The cluster detected supply voltage below 9 volts for 5 seconds or longer.
diagnostics.next: Use CB to distinguish a previous discharge, charging concern, circuit resistance or unresolved IPC concern.

verification.title: Reproduce operation and retest
verification.body: Operate the affected system after connector repairs and repeat the prescribed self-tests. A temporary disappearance establishes current operation, not a proven permanent repair.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Retain returning codes, the selected branch, battery and MODULE_VOLT readings, and any C220 measurements so the next repair decision is traceable.

guides.title: Diagnose BCM communication and crash-event signal faults
guides.summary: Trace missing module messages and a grounded crash-event output through symptom checks, network tests, circuit isolation and connector inspection.
guides.introduction: The body control module (BCM) coordinates functions such as lighting, locks and ignition-state messaging. It also sends crash information to the powertrain control module (PCM), which initiates fuel cut-off when that signal indicates a crash. These tests separate communication faults involving other modules from a fault in that dedicated crash-event circuit.
guides.why: A missing message does not identify a failed module: network conditions, battery voltage, configuration and connections can interrupt communication. Checking whether other modules report the same loss helps determine which end of the communication path needs attention.

when.summary: When the BCM records these communication codes or B143A:11 and the corresponding concern needs diagnosis.
notes: Match the entertainment-system branch to the installed SYNC equipment.

prepare.title: Establish reliable electrical conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%. Review previous repairs and record relevant diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) across all modules.

prepare.title: Arrange diagnostic access
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool capable of network tests and module self-tests, a digital multimeter, and the specified Rotunda Flex Probes. Have Wiring Diagrams Cells 13 and 14, connector information and the vehicle identification number (VIN) available.

steps.title: Confirm the concern before pursuing communication codes
steps.body: For Tests M, O and P, switch the ignition on and verify an observable symptom. Without one, clear the code; the system is operating normally at that time. High network traffic or an intermittent condition may explain the stored event. Recent module replacement also makes incomplete or incorrect programmable module installation (PMI) relevant to Test M.

steps.title: Follow the network and self-test sequence
steps.body: Use the matching branch in the [BCM diagnostic procedure](#/document/G1692965). Test M network-tests the driver front seat module (DSM), then uses its self-test after the BCM voltage-code checks. Test O checks steering column control module (SCCM) communication; Test P checks the accessory protocol interface module (APIM). A failed network test requires communication diagnosis. After a pass, clear BCM codes, wait 10 seconds and reread continuous memory. Route U3006:16, U3007:16, U3013:16 or U3014:16 to Test K; U3006:17, U3007:17, U3013:17 or U3014:17 to Test L. Otherwise, perform the branch’s module self-test and pursue any returned codes.

steps.title: Compare the communication loss across modules
steps.body: After a clean self-test, clear BCM codes, wait 10 seconds and recheck. If the target code returns, clear again, cycle ignition off and on, wait 10 seconds and retrieve all continuous-memory codes. U0208, U0212 or U0253 in another module directs inspection toward the DSM, SCCM or APIM respectively; a BCM-only report directs inspection toward the BCM. A code that does not return may have been intermittent.

steps.title: Confirm and isolate B143A:11
steps.body: For N1, ignition on, clear codes, wait 10 seconds and run the BCM self-test. If B143A:11 persists, switch ignition off and disconnect PCM C1551B for 2.3L, C1381B for 3.7L, or C175B for 5.0L/5.2L. Switch ignition on and repeat the clear, wait and self-test sequence. A code that disappears directs PCM connector inspection; one that remains requires circuit isolation.

steps.title: Measure the isolated crash-event circuit
steps.body: With ignition off and the PCM still disconnected, disconnect BCM C2280F. Measure resistance from C2280F pin 29 to ground. Resistance greater than 10,000 ohms leads to BCM connector inspection; any other result directs circuit repair. Follow the specified isolation conditions so connected electronics do not distort the measurement.

steps.title: Repair connections and operate the affected system
steps.body: Inspect the connectors selected by the branch. Replace corroded connectors or terminals and clean module pins; replace damaged, bent or pushed-out terminals/pins as necessary. Reconnect securely, ensuring the latches engage, then operate the system. If operation returns, address the underlying connector damage rather than stopping at reseating.

steps.title: Use the correct final decision
steps.body: If the concern remains, check applicable technical service bulletins through OASIS and follow any matching bulletin. Otherwise, the remote-module branches can direct DSM, SCCM or APIM replacement, and N4 can direct PCM replacement. BCM endpoints require the VIN-based guided routine. Use the applicable replacement procedure; BCM replacement requires PMI.

watchFor.title: A historical code without a present fault
watchFor.body: Do not use an inactive concern as justification for the module-replacement endpoints.

watchFor.title: Damaged test connections
watchFor.body: Forced probes can spread terminals and create another intermittent fault. Use the specified adapters.

notes: For APIM replacement, distinguish vehicles without a touchscreen from those with a touchscreen; follow the matching SYNC procedure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0208:87 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: Test M addresses driver front seat module (DSM) communication and possible configuration problems after replacement.
diagnostics.next: Use the DSM for the M2 network test and M4 self-test; DSM self-test faults lead to Front Seats diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B143A:11 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detects its crash-event output to the PCM shorted to ground.
diagnostics.next: Use Test N. If N1 does not reproduce it, a momentary self-test interruption may explain the code.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0212:87 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: SCCM messages received through the gateway module (GWM) are missing.
diagnostics.next: Use Test O; SCCM self-test faults lead to steering-column electrical diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0253:87 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: APIM messages received through the GWM are missing.
diagnostics.next: Use Test P; APIM self-test faults lead to diagnosis for the installed SYNC system.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0256:87 is recorded
diagnostics.meaning: Its code definition identifies missing front controls interface module (FCIM) A messages.
diagnostics.next: Continue with the applicable FCIM communication diagnosis; Tests M–P do not complete that fault path.

verification.title: Confirm actual operation
verification.body: Operate the affected system after connector repairs and verify whether the original concern remains.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic outcome
verification.body: Record returning codes, which modules reported them, relevant measurements and the resulting repair or guided-routine handoff. Distinguish a non-reproduced fault from a confirmed repair.

guides.title: Diagnose memory exterior mirrors that will not move correctly
guides.summary: Trace missing mirror movement through switch inputs, door-module communication, motor circuits, position sensors and the mirror’s internal harness.
guides.introduction: Each exterior mirror has separate horizontal and vertical motors, with integral sensors that report glass position for memory recall. The driver door module (DDM) controls the left mirror and sends right-mirror requests to the passenger door module (PDM). These tests distinguish a command problem from faulty wiring, a motor or a module.
guides.why: A stationary mirror does not prove its motor has failed. Checking switch data, loaded outputs and sensor feedback in order prevents a poor connection or missing command from being mistaken for a defective assembly.
searchTerms: left mirror only moves in one direction

when.summary: Use when a memory exterior mirror currently fails to move correctly in one or more directions.
notes: Do not replace a component through these tests when the reported concern cannot be reproduced.

prepare.title: Prepare for electrical diagnosis
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool with door-module self-tests and live data, a digital multimeter, a test lamp and fused jumpers. These tests require competent live-circuit testing and access to mirror and door-module connectors.

prepare.title: Protect terminals and establish conditions
prepare.detail: Use Rotunda Flex Probes NUD105-R025D; never insert a test-lamp probe directly into a connector. Verify battery state of charge exceeds 70%, inspect previous repairs and obtain Wiring Diagrams Cell 124.

steps.title: Choose the correct side’s entry test
steps.body: For the left-hand mirror, begin Test C with the DDM self-test. For the right-hand mirror, inspect body control module fuse 26 (30A), then begin Test D with a network test of both door modules. A network failure requires communication diagnosis before continuing. Follow the recorded codes into their specified branches.

steps.title: Check whether the switch request arrives
steps.body: With no relevant codes, monitor the DDM parameter identifications (PIDs), meaning its live data values. MIR_SEL must follow both selection buttons; MIR_SW_DN, MIR_SW_UP, MIR_SW_L and MIR_SW_R must follow directional inputs. A mismatch directs replacement of the front door window control switch, which incorporates the mirror controls.

steps.title: Follow the motor-output branch
steps.body: The common motor-circuit lamp check responds to left and down commands; horizontal and vertical checks respond to right and up commands. For the right memory mirror, horizontal motor testing uses C626 pin 4 (CPM33) and PDM C652B pin 8; vertical motor testing uses C626 pin 1 (CPM34) and PDM C652B pin 7. The test lamp connects the selected motor-output pin to ground. Illumination without a command leads to short-to-voltage testing; absent illumination leads to the specified isolated ground-short and continuity checks. Keep the original ignition and connector states: switch ignition off before disconnecting, restore ignition only for powered checks, and switch it off with both ends disconnected for resistance checks. C626 pins 10 and 8 are position-feedback signals, not motor outputs; do not load those sensor circuits.

steps.title: Separate sensor wiring faults from module response
steps.body: C8 or D9 checks sensor circuits for unwanted voltage, ground shorts and opens before checking the approximately 5-volt reference. Next, clear codes and self-test with the mirror disconnected. The prescribed horizontal and vertical feedback jumpers should produce the specified ground-short codes. Remove each jumper after its test; unexpected responses lead to module checks.

steps.title: Inspect the module connections before replacement
steps.body: At C23 or D24, inspect every relevant module connector. Replace damaged terminals or connectors, clean module pins as directed, and correct pushed-out pins. Reconnect and latch all disconnected connectors, then operate the system. If the concern persists, check applicable Technical Service Bulletins through OASIS before following the module-replacement decision.

steps.title: Inspect the mirror’s jumper harness
steps.body: A successful output or sensor-response branch leads to C24 or D25. Inspect the internal harness for opens, shorts, corrosion and damaged or displaced pins. Repair it where possible. An unrepairable harness requires the exterior mirror assembly; a sound harness leads to motor replacement through the separate exterior-mirror procedure.

steps.title: Keep heater complaints on their own diagnostic path
steps.body: Heated glass operates with rear-window defrost, with each door module controlling its own side. Cold glass or heat that remains on requires heater-circuit diagnosis. Successful movement tests alone do not establish that the heating element or its control circuit works.

watchFor.title: Incorrect test connections
watchFor.body: Make only the instructed jumper connections. Isolate circuits and follow ignition states for resistance measurements; powered circuits can give misleading readings.

watchFor.title: A fault disappears after reconnection
watchFor.body: Find and correct the terminal problem rather than treating restored operation as proof that the connection is permanently sound.

notes: These are memory-mirror tests. Mirrors without memory use a different control arrangement.
Other door-module codes are routed to Locks, Latches and Entry Systems diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: The DDM records B1C09:11 or B1C09:15, or B1C10:11 or B1C10:15.
diagnostics.meaning: The codes select the left mirror’s horizontal or vertical motor-circuit branch.
diagnostics.next: Follow C15 for the B1C09 pair or C19 for the B1C10 pair; do not condemn the motor from the code alone.

diagnostics.finding: The PDM records B1C11:11 or B1C11:15, or B1C12:11 or B1C12:15.
diagnostics.meaning: These concern horizontal or vertical drive. The :11 codes indicate excessive current; :15 indicates insufficient current and a possible open or short to battery.
diagnostics.next: Use D16 for horizontal drive or D20 for vertical drive with the motor-output terminals identified above. Retain the original response and wiring-test decisions.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1163:11, B1163:15, B1164:11 or B1164:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: B1163 concerns left heater output; B1164 concerns right heater output. The :11 and :15 variants indicate excessive and insufficient current respectively.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the appropriate heater wiring, glass and door module; verify the rear-defrost operating condition.

verification.title: Restore and operate
verification.body: Remove test jumpers, seat and latch disconnected connectors, then operate the affected mirror to determine whether the original concern remains.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record switch-data agreement, circuit-test outcomes and restored or remaining movement faults. Distinguish deliberately induced sensor-test codes from the original codes.

guides.title: Diagnose passive trunk-release failure and keyless-entry communication faults
guides.summary: Separate rear-antenna faults from wiring, voltage and network problems affecting passive trunk release and related door features.
guides.introduction: Passive entry uses an antenna to activate the programmed key, a radio transceiver module (RTM) to receive its response, and the body control module (BCM) to control entry functions. A trunk that will not release passively may still respond to its button or remote, providing useful evidence about which command path needs testing.
guides.why: Communication codes report missing messages, not necessarily a defective receiving module. Proving the complaint, checking voltage and comparing codes across modules prevents a local connection problem from becoming an unnecessary module replacement.
searchTerms: trunk opens with remote but not passive entry

when.summary: Use for failed passive trunk release or relevant communication codes accompanied by entry, door or mirror symptoms.
notes: Tests U and W stop when no observable symptom is present; a stored code alone does not justify replacement.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Verify battery state of charge exceeds 70% and charging operation is correct. Review previous repairs and applicable technical service bulletins (TSBs); diagnose circuit codes before system or performance codes.

prepare.title: Arrange tools and capability
prepare.detail: Use a valid programmed key, a diagnostic scan tool, a digital multimeter and Rotunda Flex Probes. Electrical testing requires exact connector information; BCM escalation requires access to the vehicle-identification-number-specific guided routine.

steps.title: Test the two ordinary trunk-release paths
steps.body: In Test T, close the lid, switch ignition on, unlock using the door control and press the luggage-compartment release button. Failure redirects to Test N. If it works, switch ignition off, close the lid and press the programmed key's release button twice. Failure here redirects to Test O; success leads to rear-antenna testing.

steps.title: Separate antenna and wiring faults
steps.body: With ignition off, disconnect rear antenna C4378 and measure between its component-side pins: resistance outside 1–3 ohms directs antenna replacement. For the wiring checks, leave the antenna disconnected and disconnect BCM C2280D. T4 then switches ignition on to check both conductors for unwanted voltage. T5 switches ignition off and requires each conductor-to-ground resistance to exceed 10,000 ohms. At T6, with both ends still disconnected, measure C4378 pin 1 to C2280D pin 16 and C4378 pin 2 to C2280D pin 15. Each must be less than 3 ohms; repair a failed circuit, or continue to T7 when both pass. The rear antenna uses connector D, not connector E.

steps.title: Follow Test U for gateway-message loss
steps.body: For U0146:00, establish an observable symptom, then network-test the gateway module (GWM). A failed network test redirects to communications diagnosis. If it passes, investigate battery-voltage or charging codes first. Otherwise clear codes and repeat the RTM self-test. A returning code leads to the all-module comparison below.

steps.title: Follow Test V for transceiver communication
steps.body: For U0258:87 or U1A00:00, both RTM and BCM must pass the network test before circuit diagnosis. Follow V2–V4's connector and ignition sequence to test their local interconnect network (LIN) circuit for voltage shorts, ground shorts and continuity. If wiring passes, inspect and retest the RTM connection before considering replacement.

steps.title: Follow Test W for BCM-message loss
steps.body: For U0140:00 in a driver or passenger door module, verify the symptom and network-test the BCM. Network failure redirects to communications diagnosis; voltage codes from its self-test redirect to BCM diagnosis. Otherwise clear codes and repeat the affected door module's self-test before comparing other modules.

steps.title: Compare persistent communication codes
steps.body: At U5 or W5, clear all codes, switch ignition off and on, wait 30 seconds and retrieve continuous-memory codes from every module. U0146 in other modules directs GWM replacement; otherwise RTM replacement. U0140 in other modules directs the BCM guided routine; otherwise replace the affected door module.

steps.title: Complete connector and module decisions
steps.body: At T7, V5 or V6, repair corrosion, damaged or pushed-out terminals, latch connectors and retest. Persistent faults require the TSB check before escalation. Without an applicable bulletin, T7/V6 use the BCM guided routine; V5 directs RTM replacement, followed by V6 only if the complaint remains.

watchFor.title: Invalid resistance measurements
watchFor.body: Isolate the circuit and verify the prescribed ignition state. Voltage or a connected module can invalidate resistance readings.

watchFor.title: Terminal damage
watchFor.body: Do not force probes into connectors or apply power or ground to module-controlled circuits unless the procedure directs it.

notes: Recent module replacement can leave incorrect or missing programmable module installation (PMI), producing communication faults.
If BCM replacement is ultimately directed, PMI, programming at least 2 keys and the passive anti-theft parameter reset are required.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0146:00 is recorded by the RTM.
diagnostics.meaning: Gateway messages are missing over the controller area network (CAN).
diagnostics.next: Use Test U's symptom, network, charging and repeat-code checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0258:87 is recorded by the BCM.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detects missing RTM communication over LIN.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test V; a missing message does not identify the failed component.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U1A00:00 is recorded by the RTM.
diagnostics.meaning: The RTM detects a fault in its LIN connection to the BCM.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test V's network and circuit checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0140:00 is recorded by a door module.
diagnostics.meaning: The driver or passenger door module is missing BCM messages; associated lighting features may fail.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test W before selecting a module.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code U0208:00 accompanies a memory-mirror complaint.
diagnostics.meaning: A door module is missing driver seat module messages.
diagnostics.next: Continue the dedicated communication diagnosis; this description alone provides no replacement decision.

verification.title: Repeat the affected functions
verification.body: Recheck passive trunk release, button and remote operation, or the affected door feature. After RTM replacement in Test V, continue to V6 if the concern remains.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record symptoms, measurements, reporting modules and repeat self-test results. Distinguish a resolved complaint from an intermittent fault that is currently absent.

guides.title: Diagnose driver seat overtemperature codes B2729 and B2730
guides.summary: Separate airflow restrictions, temperature-sensor faults, wiring problems and module faults before replacing climate controlled seat components.
guides.introduction: Each climate controlled seat has cushion and backrest blower assemblies that heat or cool cabin air and distribute it through the foam. Each assembly contains a thermoelectric device and a thermistor, a temperature-sensitive resistor. The front seat climate control module (SCME) controls their operation. Pinpoint Test AF investigates driver cushion code B2729; Test AG investigates driver backrest code B2730. A separate performance test measures cooling from operational blowers on either front seat.
guides.why: Restricted airflow can cause genuine overheating, while faulty temperature feedback can report an apparent temperature rise. Comparing airflow, temperature readings and electrical measurements separates these causes. Seat wiring also includes airbag connections, making the specified Supplemental Restraint System (SRS) precautions essential.

when.summary: When B2729 or B2730 is recorded, or an operational climate controlled seat needs its cooling performance checked.
notes: A stored code alone does not justify replacing a blower or module.

prepare.title: Diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use an SCME-capable scan tool, digital multimeter, specified Rotunda Flex Probes, inductive current probe and thermocouple thermometer.

prepare.title: Electrical and seat access capability
prepare.detail: This work requires SRS depowering and repowering, controlled live electrical testing, and potentially seat and trim removal. Obtain the linked procedures before disconnecting seat wiring.

prepare.title: Preliminary checks
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, confirm battery state of charge exceeds 70%, inspect previous repairs and wiring, and address related circuit codes before performance faults.

steps.title: Confirm the appropriate fault
steps.body: Start the engine, select driver HIGH heat and run the SCME self-test. An on-demand B2729 leads to AF2; B2730 leads to AG2. If absent, follow AF5 or AG5: switch the driver seat OFF for AF, or passenger seat OFF for AG, clear codes, then monitor driver cushion CSHTEMP and backrest BKTMP temperature data. Occupy the driver seat on HIGH heat for at least 15 minutes.

steps.title: Use the temperature trend to choose the branch
steps.body: Smooth readings remaining within 15° C indicate the fault is not currently present. A gradual rise separating the affected reading from the other by more than 15° C leads to airflow checks. A sudden jump leads to AF16 or AG16 thermistor checks. Past faults, repeated heat/cool switching or excessive cabin temperature can explain a non-reproduced concern.

steps.title: Separate the thermistor from its wiring
steps.body: For an on-demand fault, follow AF2–4 or AG2–4, beginning with SRS depowering and the specified connector disconnections. Check for shorts to ground, then compare combined thermistor-and-wiring resistance with the ambient-temperature table. AF16 and AF17, or AG16 and AG17, use the same temperature comparison for jumping readings. A correct component reading with an incorrect harness reading identifies wiring resistance; an incorrect component reading directs blower replacement.

steps.title: Compare airflow unloaded and occupied
steps.body: Run both seats on HIGH cool and compare corresponding cushion or backrest exhaust airflow. Wiggle the relevant harness; changing blower operation directs wiring repair. If airflow becomes unequal only when occupied, the affected driver foam pad requires replacement. Otherwise switch ignition off and inspect for an obstruction or restricted filter. Remove an obstruction. If the integral filter is restricted in AG8, replace the driver backrest blower using the linked backrest procedure; the cushion blower is a different assembly.

steps.title: Check blower circuits and physical installation
steps.body: AF9–14 or AG9–14 test speed-control continuity, unwanted voltage, shorts to ground, supply-circuit continuity and blower resistance. Follow each ignition state and the specified meter polarity; reversed leads can falsely condemn a blower. If electrical checks pass, AF15 or AG15 requires seat and corresponding cover removal to inspect blower installation and crushed foam. Correct the installation or replace damaged foam; refit sound components before continuing.

steps.title: Check heating current and module connections
steps.body: At AF18 or AG18, reconnect the specified circuits and measure the designated cushion or backrest conductor with an inductive probe during HIGH heat. A draw of 11 amps or more directs blower replacement. Otherwise compare combined-circuit and component-only resistance to distinguish wiring from blower faults. Protect any opened harness conduit and close it afterward.

steps.title: Resolve the remaining module branch
steps.body: At AF21 or AG21, repair corrosion, damaged terminals and pushed-out pins, then latch SCME connectors securely. Keep both airbag in-line connectors disconnected during this operational check. If the concern persists, check applicable Technical Service Bulletins through OASIS before replacing the SCME. A replacement requires programmable module installation. If operation returns, address the connector fault’s root cause.

steps.title: Restore SRS operation and measure cooling
steps.body: Complete AF22 or AG22 before returning the vehicle. For an operational blower’s cooling test, use a stable shaded environment, an occupied seat and the engine running on HIGH cool. Measure inlet air beside each filter and the corresponding scan-tool temperature. Use CSHTEMP/BKTMP for the driver or PCSHTMP/PBKTMP for the passenger, with DCCSMOD/PCCSMOD monitoring seat mode. Close the backrest trim cover before recording its inlet temperature.

watchFor.title: Invalid cooling-test starting readings
watchFor.body: An initial temperature reading above 205° C or below 2° C indicates hardware failure. Stop and use the symptom or SCME code chart.

watchFor.title: Recovery during the cooling test
watchFor.body: A mode change to Blower Only means the seat has failed this test. Stop and return to diagnosis.

notes: The blower filter is integral and is not serviced separately.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B2729 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The driver cushion has an overtemperature-related fault; the code does not identify the failed component.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test AF to distinguish airflow, thermistor, wiring, blower and SCME causes.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B2730 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The driver backrest overtemperature threshold triggered seat shutdown.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test AG, including occupied airflow checks and electrical isolation before component replacement.

verification.title: Prove out the restraint system
verification.body: Follow SRS depowering, reconnect driver C3206, passenger C219 and all other disconnected connectors, then follow SRS repowering. Successful prove-out is required for completion; failure leads to SRS diagnosis.

verification.title: Record cooling results
verification.body: For each tested cushion and backrest, record inlet temperature, matching blower temperature and inlet-minus-blower difference. Each difference should be 6–8° C. If outside specification, inspect ducts, filters, blockages, disconnections and assembly. If those are correct, run the SCME self-test and follow its code chart.

guides.title: Diagnose door locks that will not operate or work in only one direction
guides.summary: Separate latch binding, switch faults, wiring problems and module concerns by matching the lock complaint to Tests H–K.
guides.introduction: Electric actuators in the door latches move the locks in response to switch requests. The body control module (BCM) controls their outputs; memory-seat equipment introduces driver and passenger door modules (DDM and PDM) into switch diagnosis. Comparing both switches and both directions helps identify where the request or movement stops.
guides.why: A binding latch, missing electrical output and lost switch request can produce similar symptoms. Testing them separately prevents unnecessary latch or module replacement.
searchTerms: doors lock but will not unlock
door locks work from only one switch

when.summary: When door locks fail from an interior switch, operate in only one direction, or a lock indicator is inoperative.
notes: The complaint must be present during testing; an unreproduced fault does not justify component replacement.

prepare.title: Establish reliable test conditions
prepare.detail: Check battery and charging operation, with battery state of charge greater than 70%. Inspect previous repairs, harnesses, fuses and connectors; diagnose related circuit codes first.

prepare.title: Prepare electrical test equipment
prepare.detail: Use a module-capable scan tool, digital multimeter, correct probe adapters, Rotunda Flex Probes and fused jumpers. Test I requires a Rotunda Test Lamp (SGT27000) or 250–300mA incandescent test lamp. Consult Wiring Diagrams Cell 117; indicator diagnosis also references Cell 89.

steps.title: Test H: classify a complete lock failure
steps.body: With ignition on, run BCM, DDM and PDM self-tests and route any codes through their charts. With no codes, try lock and unlock from both switches. Failure of both directions from one switch leads to K; directional failure leads to J. If neither switch operates any lock, follow H4–H5 for BCM lock-ground and all-lock circuit continuity. Resistance must be less than 3 ohms; otherwise repair the circuit.

steps.title: Test I: separate a stuck latch from missing drive
steps.body: Operate the affected lock manually above the latch opening. Binding directs latch replacement. If it moves, check BCM fuse 24 (30A); investigate a short if faulty. At the disconnected latch, perform the prescribed loaded lock-output test, then unlock-output test. Missing lock output directs circuit repair. Both outputs present direct latch replacement. Missing unlock output requires its continuity test, then circuit repair or BCM checks.

steps.title: Test J: isolate a switch-input short
steps.body: First route any door dead in both directions to I. Without memory seats, self-test the BCM; with memory seats, self-test DDM and PDM. For the relevant switch code, disconnect switches in the specified sequence, clear codes and repeat the self-test. A code that disappears directs switch replacement. A persistent code requires input-to-ground resistance checks: greater than 10,000 ohms leads to module checks; otherwise repair the circuit.

steps.title: Test J: trace a missing directional request
steps.body: With neither switch code present, check BCM fuse 3 (20A), investigating a short if faulty. J7–J12 use fused-jumper request simulations and continuity checks with ignition off and the specified switch disconnected. For the passenger unlock request in J10, momentarily connect C605 pin 3 to pin 2 with the fused jumper. Pin 1 to pin 2 is the lock request, not unlock. Keep pin 2 as the stated return; do not substitute chassis ground on memory-equipped vehicles. Successful lock and unlock requests direct switch replacement; a failed request leads to the appropriate memory-seat or non-memory input-circuit test. J11's non-memory BCM connector is C2280E; retain its listed pin endpoints and isolated resistance checks. Memory-equipped vehicles use the separate door-module branch.

steps.title: Test K: investigate one completely ineffective switch
steps.body: Inspect the switch for damage. With memory seats, first confirm DDM and PDM communication using a network test; communication failure requires network diagnosis. Without memory seats, proceed directly to the switch-ground test. Ground resistance below 3 ohms directs replacement of the affected switch; otherwise repair its ground circuit.

steps.title: Finish the applicable module branch
steps.body: At H6, I5 or J13–J15, inspect module connectors for corrosion, bent or pushed-out terminals, repair defects and reconnect securely. Retest before condemning a module. Persistent faults require an applicable Technical Service Bulletin check through OASIS. Follow any bulletin; otherwise J13/J14 direct PDM/DDM replacement, while BCM branches require the vehicle identification number for the guided routine.

watchFor.title: Brief outputs and damaged terminals
watchFor.body: Watch the test lamp while pressing the switch: latch power is momentary. Never insert the lamp probe directly into a connector. Follow ignition-off and isolation instructions for resistance measurements.

notes: If BCM replacement becomes necessary, its prerequisites include programmable module installation, programming at least 2 keys and a parameter reset.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B126A:01 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detected a door-lock switch input short to ground during self-test.
diagnostics.next: Follow J's non-memory switch-isolation branch; the code alone does not prove switch failure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B108F:23 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The DDM or PDM detected a switch input stuck low through a short to ground.
diagnostics.next: Isolate the switch associated with the reporting door module.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1490:11 accompanies an inoperative lock indicator.
diagnostics.meaning: The BCM detected a short to ground in the indicator supply circuit.
diagnostics.next: Pursue indicator-circuit diagnosis rather than assuming the latch actuator has failed.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1490:15 accompanies an inoperative lock indicator.
diagnostics.meaning: Its description includes short to battery or open; the stated trigger is an open indicator supply circuit.
diagnostics.next: Continue indicator diagnosis; this definition does not establish a replacement decision.

verification.title: Repeat and record the complaint checks
verification.body: Operate lock and unlock from both switches after repairs or connector reseating. Record each door's response and any repeated self-test results. If reseating restores operation, correct the underlying terminal or connector defect.

guides.title: Diagnose 5.2L charging faults and generator-related radio interference
guides.summary: Separate radio interference, generator-current sensing faults and generator control or feedback faults through the dedicated charging-system tests.
guides.introduction: The belt-driven generator produces electricity and uses an internal regulator to control charging voltage. The powertrain control module (PCM) commands output through the generator command circuit and receives load and error information through the generator monitor circuit. A separate Hall-effect sensor measures current in the generator's positive battery cable, helping the PCM manage engine load.
guides.why: A generator can produce voltage while its control or feedback circuit is faulty. Loaded measurements expose poor connections that an unloaded check can miss, while sensor and communication tests distinguish wiring faults from generator or PCM failure.

when.summary: Use for charging-related radio interference, generator-current codes, or generator control and monitor circuit codes.

prepare.title: Provide the required electrical testing capability
prepare.detail: Use a PCM-capable scan tool with active commands, digital multimeter, Flex Probe adapters and fused jumper. The sense-circuit load test requires a 250–350 mA incandescent 12-volt test lamp; an LED lamp is unsuitable. Live tests and generator-cable handling require experienced electrical diagnosis.

prepare.title: Prepare the battery and circuit information
prepare.detail: Verify battery condition and state of charge above 70%. Tests E and F require voltage above 12.2 volts before and throughout testing, with no battery charger attached. Use Wiring Diagrams Cells 12 and 13 and follow each ignition-off disconnection instruction.

steps.title: Retrieve codes and inspect shared connections
steps.body: Use the [5.2L charging diagnostic procedure](#/document/G1807237). Inspect battery, generator, junction-box, C1046 and engine-ground connections for looseness or corrosion. Check for abnormal ignition-off drain where appropriate. In Test E, P0562 takes priority and routes to Test B. For F and G, a failed battery condition test requires charging or replacement before continuing.

steps.title: Test D: isolate radio interference
steps.body: At idle, tune to a station exhibiting interference. Switch the ignition off before disconnecting the regulator connector C102B and the main B+ connection C102C, then restart and compare at idle. Interference that remains routes to the SYNC information and entertainment diagnosis for the fitted touchscreen configuration. If it disappears, Test D directs generator replacement.

steps.title: Test E: follow the current-sensor code
steps.body: For P0A5A, inspect sensor damage, corrosion, connection, cable routing through the sensor and trapped debris. For P0A5B, begin with reference voltage and signal return; the specified range is 4.8–5.2 volts. P0A5C enters the feedback-circuit checks. Follow the required connector isolation, then test feedback for voltage shorts, ground shorts, shorts to reference or return, and an open.

steps.title: Retest the current sensor before escalating
steps.body: At E9, repair damaged or corroded terminals, seat the sensor connector, clear all module codes and repeat the PCM self-test. A returning code directs repair or sensor replacement. Clear and retest again; only a persistent fault advances to the PCM checks. A passing retest still requires correction of any identified connector problem.

steps.title: Test F: prove supply and command paths
steps.body: At F2, compare C102C pin 1 to ground with the recorded battery voltage. This is the 5.2L main B+ connection; C102B pin 1 carries regulator feedback. The supply must be within 0.5 volt of battery voltage. For F3, use the same-engine B4 loaded check: positive meter lead at C102C pin 1 and negative meter lead at battery POSITIVE. Idle with headlamps on and blower high; wiggle the wiring and require a drop below 0.5 volt. Repair a failed supply or cable connection before continuing to the A-sense load test and command-wire short/open checks. At F8, use only the specified fused loopback: generator monitor (GENMON) and generator command (GENCMD) readings within 5% direct generator replacement; disagreement advances to PCM checks. Remove the jumper in either case.

steps.title: Test G: distinguish monitor-circuit faults
steps.body: Test G uses the same C102C pin 1 B+ supply check and the loaded cable-drop measurement to battery positive. After those pass, P0625 requires the sense-circuit load test; P0626 proceeds to monitor-circuit testing. Check for voltage shorts, ground shorts and opens, then perform the generator and regulator internal-resistance tests. Failed internal checks direct generator replacement. If they pass, G10 uses the specified fused loopback and commands GENVDSD to 14 volts. Compare GENMON with GENCMD: agreement within 5% directs generator replacement; disagreement advances to PCM checks. Remove the jumper.

steps.title: Complete the PCM decision only after upstream checks
steps.body: For E10, F9 or G11, inspect PCM connectors, replace damaged terminals or connectors, clean module pins as directed and ensure connectors latch. Operate the system again. If the fault remains, check applicable technical service bulletins and follow any matching instructions. PCM replacement is the final branch when no bulletin addresses the persistent concern; clear all module codes afterward.

watchFor.title: Keep the two positive-cable tests distinct
watchFor.body: The supply check measures the main C102C terminal to ground. The loaded cable-drop check measures that terminal to battery positive. The second test measures loss along the cable, not the total charging voltage.

watchFor.title: Apparent charging does not prove control is healthy
watchFor.body: Certain command or monitor faults allow fallback generator output while the charging warning remains active. Continue the relevant circuit test.

watchFor.title: Protect terminals during load testing
watchFor.body: Connect the specified incandescent lamp through Flex Probe adapters. Do not push its probe directly into a connector or improvise powered jumper tests.

notes: An engine-off battery-saving message can be normal during ignition-on or accessory use: low charge or elapsed time can switch off audio/navigation. Messages with the engine running, or confined to the audio display, require the audio-system fault path.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0A5A is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detects no generator current without a current-sensor circuit code.
diagnostics.next: Start with Test E's physical sensor and cable-routing inspection.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0A5B or P0A5C is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Feedback is low, suggesting an open or ground short, or high, suggesting a voltage short, respectively.
diagnostics.next: Use the corresponding Test E entry point; neither code alone proves sensor failure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0620 or P065B is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P0620 concerns command, sense or positive-supply circuit faults; P065B reports an internal regulator failure.
diagnostics.next: Complete Test F's battery, supply and command checks before the replacement decision.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0625 or P0626 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The monitor signal is low or high respectively. Supply faults can also set P0625; generator or PCM faults remain possible.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test G, retaining its different entry branches and internal-resistance checks.

verification.title: Recheck the original concern
verification.body: Repeat the relevant operating or PCM self-test after repair. For intermittent connections, confirm seating and address the cause of terminal damage or corrosion.

verification.title: Keep a measurement record
verification.body: Record battery voltage alongside the supply comparison, the loaded cable-drop result, loopback PID readings and returning codes. Note the electrical load used so the result can be repeated.

procedures.purpose: 5.2L charging diagnosis: radio interference, current sensing, command and monitor Tests D–G, plus load-shed interpretation.
Electrical diagnostic prerequisites, loaded measurements and safe connector testing.
5.2L generator removal and installation when the diagnostic branch directs replacement.
Generator-current-sensor removal and installation following Test E.
SYNC information and entertainment diagnosis when interference persists with the generator disconnected.
Battery removal and installation if battery condition testing requires replacement.

authoring.reviewNotes:
Exact 5.2L connector identification: native charging diagram 012-002 explicitly groups 5.0L/5.2L main generator B+ at C102C pin 1 on SBF01 RD. It separately identifies C102D pin 1 for 3.7L, C102A pin 1 for 2.3L, and regulator C102B pin 1 as CDC15 VT GENLI/GENMON. Connector C102C is a one-pin SBF01 terminal, while C102B is the separate three-pin regulator connector. Therefore the 5.2L B+ supply role is C102C1; do not tell the reader to measure the monitor terminal C102B1 as battery feed.
The 5.2L chapter incorrectly reuses C102D1 in B3/B4/F3/G2/G3 and C102B1 in F2. These are role-identification errors corroborated by the exact engine-labeled native drawing and connector records. Use C102C1 only for the explicitly named main B+ cable checks. Do not alter monitor/control tests on C102B or invent a new diagnostic branch.
The SAME 5.2L B4 contains a battery-POSITIVE pictogram in its negative meter-lead cell, with engine idling, headlamps on, blower high and less-than-0.5V drop. Original F3/G3 negative cells are genuinely empty: no text or image. Their named B+ drop check can explicitly use the complete same-engine B4 endpoint and loading conditions, with the independently corrected 5.2L C102C1 B+ identification. Do not claim an image was recovered from F3/G3 themselves.
Verbatim same-engine B4 (its negative endpoint is supplied by the inspected pictogram):

Start the engine.
With the engine running at idle, headlamps on and blower on high, measure:
Positive Lead

Perform a wiggle test of the generator wiring and connections while measuring voltage drop.
Is the voltage drop less than 0.5 volt?
Yes

INSPECT and REPAIR any corrosion in the generator B+ circuit or positive battery cable connections.

Native engine-labeled diagram: generator B+ SBF01 RD is C102C pin 1 for 5.0L and 5.2L; C102D pin 1 for 3.7L; C102A pin 1 for 2.3L. Separate C102B pin 1 CDC15 VT is GENLI/GENMON, not B+. For 5.0/5.2 its monitor goes to PCM C175B26.

guides.title: Diagnose high or low charging voltage and generator noise on the 5.0L
guides.summary: Use measured voltage, commanded charging data and mechanical checks to distinguish generator faults from wiring, battery drain and accessory-drive problems.
guides.introduction: The belt-driven generator converts mechanical power into electrical power for the running vehicle and battery. Its internal regulator follows a voltage target from the powertrain control module (PCM). Diagnosis therefore compares actual battery voltage with the requested value while checking whether cables, grounds and the belt drive allow the generator to work correctly.
guides.why: Corroded connections can appear satisfactory without a load but lose voltage when current flows. A discharged battery, electrical noise or an unusual sound also has several possible causes, so none alone justifies generator replacement.

when.summary: Use for excessive charging voltage, low voltage, a discharged battery or suspected generator noise.
notes: The concern must be present for component-replacement decisions.
Recent charging, jump starting and extended accessory use matter when interpreting the results.

prepare.title: Establish valid battery conditions
prepare.detail: Verify battery state of charge exceeds 70%. Tests A and B require battery voltage above 12.2 volts before and throughout testing, with no battery charger attached.

prepare.title: Arrange the required capability
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting PCM self-tests, live data and active commands; a digital multimeter; flex probes; fused jumpers; and a stethoscope or equivalent. Engine-running measurements and controlled acceleration require a technician competent in these procedures.

prepare.title: Use the specified circuit loads
prepare.detail: The generator sense-circuit test requires a 250–350 mA incandescent 12-volt lamp; an LED lamp is unsuitable. PCM circuit tests use an appropriate load such as a headlamp bulb. Obtain Wiring Diagrams Cell 12 and confirmed measurement connections.

steps.title: Select the complaint and check codes
steps.body: Use Test A for high voltage, B for low voltage or discharge, and C for noise. During A or B, PCM diagnostic trouble code P0620 redirects to Test F; P0625 or P0626 redirects to Test G. Complete those circuit investigations before continuing the voltage branch.

steps.title: Inspect the physical supply path
steps.body: Correct obvious damage first. Inspect the battery, generator connections and high-current battery junction box (BJB). For discharge, also inspect for ignition-off drain and front-end accessory drive (FEAD) faults. In B3, inadequate generator B+ voltage leads to the terminal nut, high-current fuse and cable circuit.

steps.title: Follow the high-voltage comparisons
steps.body: A3 compares battery voltage with generator voltage desired (GENVDSD). A mismatch leads to unloaded and loaded checks of the generator’s A-sense circuit and its BJB fuse. Continue through the prescribed loaded wiring wiggle test and ground voltage-drop test. At A8, measure battery positive to ground with the engine running and use its greater-than-15.2-volts question to choose the next branch. This is an output-voltage check, not a measurement at an unspecified generator terminal.

steps.title: Follow the low-voltage output branch
steps.body: After checking connectors, B4 measures loaded positive-cable loss from C102C pin 1 to battery positive, and B5 measures the generator case to battery negative. B6 commands 14 volts and expects battery voltage within ±0.5 volt. Failure directs automatic-transmission vehicles to generator replacement; manual-transmission vehicles first require the Test J clutch check. Use its confirmed abnormal clutch findings; normal one-way clutch behavior alone is not a reason to replace the generator.

steps.title: Check what the PCM sees
steps.body: Continue the applicable branch’s supply-voltage (VPWR) comparison and loaded PCM power and ground checks. For A9, switch ignition off, disconnect generator C102B and connect the specified fused jumper between pins 1 and 2. Start the engine, command GENVDSD to 14 volts, and compare GENMON with GENCMD—the monitored and commanded percentages. Agreement within 5% leads to A10; disagreement leads to A13. Follow those branches’ jumper-removal instructions. In Test B, B10 uses the specified momentary wide-open-throttle checks with accessory loads off. Correct tracking and sound connectors lead to a battery-drain check; failed tracking leads to PCM connection checks.

steps.title: Locate a mechanical noise
steps.body: Test C first checks the belt, tensioner, generator mounting and alignment. Then use the listening device to locate the running noise. Noise elsewhere requires engine diagnosis. If the generator is the source, follow the clutch-test branch before selecting the clutch or generator. Matching the normal reference sound is acceptable only without other abnormal symptoms or codes.

steps.title: Handle radio interference as a separate complaint
steps.body: Proceed to Test D for interference. Its prerequisites include factory audio equipment and inspection of added accessory wiring for connections to, or routing near, generator circuits. During prescribed generator-disconnected testing, keep engine speed below 2,000 RPM; exceeding that speed can self-excite the generator and requires ignition OFF and restarting the test.

steps.title: Finish the module decision carefully
steps.body: At A13 or B12, repair corroded, bent or displaced PCM terminals, reconnect and latch the connectors, then reproduce the concern. Check applicable service bulletins and service actions before replacing the PCM. If the replacement branch is reached, follow its separate procedure and clear diagnostic trouble codes in all modules as directed.

watchFor.title: Misleading unloaded readings
watchFor.body: A normal unloaded voltage does not establish that a cable or sense circuit can carry its required load. Do not skip the specified loaded checks.

watchFor.title: Terminal damage during testing
watchFor.body: Connect lamps and jumpers through flex probes. Never push the lamp’s own probe into a connector or improvise module power connections.

notes: A charging warning indicator that is always or never illuminated follows charging codes first; without charging codes, use instrumentation diagnosis.
Load-shed and Battery Saver – System Off messages route to Test H; Tests A–C do not complete that diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0563 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detected charging voltage above 15.9 volts with vehicle speed above 8 km/h (5 mph); recent jump starting or charging can also account for this code.
diagnostics.next: Establish the current condition and follow Test A rather than replacing the generator from the stored code.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0562 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Voltage remained at least 1.5 volts below the PCM’s desired generator voltage for 30 seconds.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test B through connections, loaded voltage losses and commanded output.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P1397 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: System voltage was outside the self-test range; recent jump starting or a discharged battery may contribute.
diagnostics.next: Use present voltage and the actual complaint to choose the appropriate diagnostic branch.

verification.title: Repeat the relevant operating check
verification.body: After correcting the identified fault, operate the system under the branch’s specified conditions and establish whether the original voltage or noise concern remains.

verification.title: Record measured and commanded results
verification.body: Record battery voltage alongside the relevant GENVDSD or VPWR reading, loaded circuit results and any remaining codes. Preserve the measurement conditions so a later comparison is meaningful.

procedures.purpose: 5.0L charging symptom routing and Tests A, B and C, including the radio-interference prerequisites.
