guides.title: Diagnose radio interference and generator control faults on the 2.3L EcoBoost
guides.summary: Trace radio interference and charging-control faults through generator isolation, loaded supply checks and circuit tests, with current-sensor diagnosis limited to initial inspection.
guides.introduction: The generator supplies electrical current while the engine runs. The powertrain control module (PCM) requests output through the generator command circuit (GENCOM) and reads regulator feedback through the generator monitor circuit (GENMON). A separate Hall-effect current sensor surrounds the generator’s main positive output cable, called B+. It receives a 5 volt reference and ground from the PCM, which interprets its feedback voltage as current flow.
guides.why: A fault code identifies a detected condition, not necessarily a failed generator. Loose connections can carry voltage without carrying current properly, so loaded voltage-drop checks matter. Lost control or feedback can also leave the generator producing a default output while the charging warning remains on.
searchTerms: system off to save battery message

when.summary: When radio interference, charging warnings, generator-related codes or battery-saving messages require diagnosis.
notes: Radio diagnosis follows the applicable SYNC audio-system route, with or without touchscreen controls.

prepare.title: Electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a diagnostic scan tool capable of PCM self-tests, live parameter identifications (PIDs) and active commands, a suitable meter, and a fused jumper. Running-engine measurements and safe handling of the high-current B+ connection require appropriate competence.

prepare.title: Battery and test conditions
prepare.detail: Tests E and F require battery voltage greater than 12.2 volts before and during testing, with no battery charger attached. Establish battery condition before F or G; charge or replace a failed battery as indicated before continuing.

prepare.title: Correct circuit-loading equipment
prepare.detail: The A-sense load test requires the specified 250–350 mA incandescent 12-volt test lamp and Flex Probe Kit. An LED lamp will not load the circuit correctly. Never insert the test-lamp probe directly into connector terminals.

steps.title: Establish the complaint and inspect the supply connections
steps.body: Record the warning, message or radio symptom and any diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Inspect the battery junction box (BJB), battery, generator, C1046 and battery/engine grounds for loose or corroded connections. For Test G, also investigate abnormal ignition-off current drain. Use the code-specific branches below rather than assuming every battery-saving message indicates generator failure.

steps.title: Test D: isolate engine-running radio interference
steps.body: Idle the engine and tune to a station where interference is present. Switch the ignition off, disconnect generator C102B, then C102A, and restart at idle. If interference remains, continue with the applicable Information and Entertainment System diagnosis. If it disappears with the generator disconnected, Test D directs installation of a new generator through its removal and installation procedure.

steps.title: Test E: record codes and inspect current-sensor routing
steps.body: With ignition on, perform the PCM self-test. If P0562 is present, route first to charging Test B. For P0A5A, switch ignition off and inspect the current sensor for damage, corrosion, a disconnected connector, debris between sensor and cable, and correct routing of the B+ cable through the sensor. Record and address visible connection or routing issues as appropriate. This branch ends after E1/E2: P0A5B, P0A5C or unexplained P0A5A requires further current-sensor diagnosis before terminal testing or sensor/PCM replacement decisions.

steps.title: Tests F and G: establish generator B+ supply
steps.body: After the battery passes, switch ignition off and inspect all generator connectors for corrosion, bent or damaged terminals and pushed-out pins. Repair the applicable terminals or connectors, clean module pins where specified, then seat and latch the connectors. Record battery voltage and measure C102A pin 1 to ground; it must be within 0.5 volt of battery voltage. If it fails, address the B+ nut and verify the 275A MEGA fuse. Repair the circuit if the fuse is sound; investigate the short’s cause if it is not.

steps.title: Measure the loaded positive-cable voltage drop
steps.body: For F3/G3, use the same-engine B4 measurement: positive meter lead at C102A pin 1 and negative meter lead at battery POSITIVE. Idle the engine with headlamps on and blower on high, and wiggle the wiring and connections while measuring. The drop must be less than 0.5 volt. Repair corrosion or poor connections in the generator B+ circuit or positive battery cable if it fails. A passing F result advances to F4; in G, P0625 advances to G4 and P0626 to G5.

steps.title: Load-test A-sense where the branch requires it
steps.body: At F4 or G4, switch ignition off and disconnect C102B. With ignition on, use the specified lamp and probe adapters between C102B pin 3 and ground. Measure that circuit while wiggling the harness; voltage must remain within ±0.5 volt of recorded battery voltage. If it fails, check BJB fuse 36 (10A), repair the circuit if the fuse is sound, or investigate the short if it has failed. This loaded check exposes resistance that an unloaded reading can miss.

steps.title: Separate command-circuit faults from monitor-circuit faults
steps.body: F5–F7 test GENCOM at C102B pin 2; G5–G7 test GENMON at C102B pin 1. Follow each test’s connector isolation and ignition states: check for unwanted voltage with ignition on, then switch ignition off for resistance tests. Any voltage indicates a short to voltage; resistance to ground must exceed 10,000 ohms, and end-to-end resistance must be less than 3 ohms. At F7, leave generator C102B and PCM C1551B disconnected with ignition off, and measure C1551B pin 59 to C102B pin 2 while wiggling the wiring. Less than 3 ohms continues to F8; otherwise repair the circuit. GENMON continuity uses the separate PCM C1551B pin 26 and remains unchanged.

steps.title: Test G: check generator internal resistance
steps.body: After the external monitor circuit passes, G8 disconnects C102B and C102A and measures generator B+ terminal to generator case. Resistance must exceed 25K ohms. G9 then checks each of the three regulator component-side pins to the case; every reading must exceed 10,000 ohms. A failed internal-resistance check directs a new generator; passing results advance to G10.

steps.title: Compare commanded and monitored signals
steps.body: After all preceding checks pass, follow the branch-specific connector setup for F8 or G10. Reconnect PCM C1551B and fit the fused jumper between C102B pins 1 and 2. Start the engine, watch GENMON and GENCMD on the scan tool, and wiggle the wiring. G10 additionally requires commanding GENVDSD to 14 volts. Readings within 5% of each other direct generator replacement; otherwise continue to PCM connection checks. Remove the fused jumper for either result.

steps.title: Complete the PCM decision only after circuit testing
steps.body: At F9 or G11, switch ignition off, inspect and repair PCM connector corrosion, damaged terminals or pushed-out pins, then reconnect securely and operate the system. If the concern disappears, address the underlying connection problem. If it persists, check applicable service articles and campaigns and follow any relevant instructions. Only when none addresses the concern does the branch direct PCM replacement and clearing DTCs in all modules.

watchFor.title: Confusing two different B+ measurements
watchFor.body: The supply check measures C102A pin 1 to ground. The loaded cable-drop check measures it to battery positive; these tests establish different things.

watchFor.title: Intermittent connector faults
watchFor.body: A reading that changes during a wiggle test points toward a connection or wiring problem that must be addressed before component decisions.

notes: C1645 identifies the generator current-sensor connector. C1046 is a separate harness connection, not the sensor connector.
On the 2.3L, C102A pin 1 is the main B+ connection. C102B pin 1 carries regulator feedback, pin 2 carries command, and pin 3 receives the fused A-sense supply.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0A5A is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detects no generator current while no current-sensor circuit DTC is set. Possible causes include the sensor, generator clutch, wiring or PCM.
diagnostics.next: Perform E1/E2 and record physical findings. A normal inspection requires further diagnosis, not automatic sensor replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0A5B is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Current-sensor feedback voltage is lower than expected, indicating an open circuit or short to ground.
diagnostics.next: Resolve any P0562 priority first, then obtain the remaining current-sensor electrical diagnosis beyond this inspection branch.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0A5C is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Current-sensor feedback voltage is higher than expected, indicating a short to voltage.
diagnostics.next: Continue through the applicable current-sensor electrical diagnosis; the code alone does not authorize replacement.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0620 or P065B is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P0620 identifies an open or ground fault involving GENCOM, A-sense or B+. P065B means the generator reports an internal regulator failure.
diagnostics.next: Use Test F, beginning with battery, connections and supply checks. Complete command-circuit testing before its generator or PCM decision.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0625 or P0626 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P0625 concerns low GENMON feedback and can also arise from an open A-sense or B+ circuit. P0626 concerns an open GENMON circuit or short to voltage. Generator or PCM faults can also set either code.
diagnostics.next: Use Test G. After the B+ drop check, P0625 includes the A-sense load test; P0626 advances to monitor-circuit testing.

diagnostics.finding: A System Off to Save Battery or Battery Saver message appears.
diagnostics.meaning: With the engine off and ignition on or in accessory mode, the body control module can shut down audio/navigation when battery charge falls below 50% or 45 minutes elapse. This can be normal battery protection.
diagnostics.next: Distinguish normal engine-off operation from messages occurring with the engine running or confined to the audio display, which require audio-system diagnosis. Do not condemn the generator from the message alone.

verification.title: Repeat the relevant operating check
verification.body: After the indicated repair and proper reconnection, operate the system under the conditions that produced the concern. Confirm that temporary jumpers are removed and connectors latch securely. Complete the branch’s required DTC clearing after PCM replacement.

verification.title: Record results and unfinished decisions
verification.body: Record battery voltage, B+ supply and loaded drop, applicable A-sense and circuit readings, PID comparison and the radio-isolation result. For Test E, record codes and physical findings without claiming electrical diagnosis is complete.

procedures.purpose: 2.3L charging diagnosis: Test D, bounded E1/E2 inspection, Tests F/G, and same-engine B3/B4 supply and cable-drop checks.
Identify the 2.3L generator supply, command and feedback conductors and their exact connectors.
Identify the 2.3L generator main B+ connection.
Identify regulator feedback, command and A-sense connector cavities.
SYNC audio diagnosis when radio interference remains with the generator disconnected.
Investigate abnormal ignition-off battery drain identified during prechecks.
Battery removal and installation if condition testing requires replacement.
Charging-system operation and interpretation of battery-protection behavior.

authoring.reviewNotes: Native012-002 explicitly labels the 2.3L variant column C1551B59 on CDC10 BU/OG, the direct GENRC/GENCOM conductor through inline C1046pin2 to generator C102Bpin2/RC. Native023-016 independently repeats C1551B59 GENRC/CDC10 for the 2.3L PCM. Exact connector-C1551B table identifies pin59 as generator regulator control and pin21 as unused; connector-C102B identifies pin2 as that same control circuit. GENLI/GENMON is the separate CDC15 conductor on C1551B26/C102B1 and is unchanged.

guides.title: Diagnose DATC compressor performance and climate-control signals
guides.summary: Check evaporator sensing, shared sensor supply, variable-compressor response and the air-conditioning request path on DATC-equipped vehicles.
guides.introduction: Dual automatic temperature control (DATC) maintains selected cabin temperatures, with separate driver and passenger settings. Its externally controlled variable-displacement compressor changes pumping capacity through a pulsed ground command from the powertrain control module (PCM). Poor cooling can therefore originate in temperature sensing, electrical supply, compressor response or the messages requesting air conditioning (A/C).
guides.why: Correct refrigerant charge and suitable ambient temperature make compressor-response tests meaningful. A shared sensor-supply fault or missing request can disrupt cooling even when the compressor itself can change displacement.

when.summary: When cooling is poor or evaporator-sensor, sensor-supply, compressor-control or clutch-request codes are recorded.
notes: Electronic manual temperature control (EMTC) is a separate equipment variant; these paths apply to DATC.

prepare.title: Confirm the fault and electrical condition
prepare.detail: Verify the current symptom, inspect PCM and compressor connections, and record diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs). Check battery and charging operation; battery state of charge must exceed 70%.

prepare.title: Obtain the required diagnostic equipment
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool for module/network tests and parameter identification (PID) data, a digital multimeter and correct probe adapters. Compressor-performance testing requires the EVDC100 tester or access to PCM EVACC data. If neither is available, obtain the specified equipment before continuing.

prepare.title: Establish valid compressor-test conditions
prepare.detail: Verify correct refrigerant charge and ambient temperature above 21.1°C (70°F). Pressure testing and refrigerant work require suitable refrigeration capability and the engine-specific procedures. Follow each electrical test's ignition and circuit-isolation instructions.

steps.title: Check evaporator temperature sensing — P
steps.body: With ignition OFF, disconnect sensor C296 and compare component resistance with the temperature/resistance table in Test P. An out-of-range result directs sensor replacement. If resistance is correct, P2–P5 check the input for a short to voltage, short to ground, open circuit and a short between signal and return. Repair a failed circuit; passing checks lead to the front controls interface module (FCIM) connector assessment at P6.

steps.title: Determine which sensor-supply fault is present — Q
steps.body: Run the FCIM self-test with ignition ON. C1B14:11 takes the ignition-OFF ground-isolation check at Q2, followed by the reference-to-return resistance check at Q3. Resistance above 200 ohms proceeds to Q6; otherwise continue to component isolation. If C1B14:11 is absent, Q5 checks the disconnected reference circuit for voltage: any voltage requires circuit repair; none leads to Q6.

steps.title: Identify a component pulling down the shared supply — Q4
steps.body: Monitor reference-to-return resistance while disconnecting, in order: the in-vehicle temperature/humidity sensor, driver temperature-door actuator, air-distribution actuator, passenger temperature-door actuator and air-inlet actuator. Stop when resistance exceeds 200 ohms and replace the last component disconnected. If it never rises, repair the circuit. Connect a replacement actuator before connecting the FCIM so calibration can occur.

steps.title: Assess displacement with the EVDC100 — R1
steps.body: Follow the tester's instructions. A decrease in suction pressure or increase in high-side pressure establishes that displacement can change: do not replace the compressor. With P06A0 present, proceed to R4; without it, check charge amount. No pressure response directs compressor replacement through the applicable procedure, clearing all DTCs and testing normal operation. If P06A0 is present afterward, proceed to R4.

steps.title: Use the EVACC scan-data route when the tester is unavailable — R2
steps.body: Start the engine and monitor EVACC. Close windows and doors; select floor mode, full warm, lowest blower and A/C off for 5 minutes. Then select PANEL, full cold, highest blower, recirculation on and A/C on. An initial PID rise followed by a fall confirms displacement response: do not replace the compressor; check charge. Failure to show that response leads to R4.

steps.title: Follow the verified control-circuit entry — R4–R7
steps.body: Use this sequence only after the preceding tester/PID decision directs it. The solenoid wiring assignments here are for 2.3L. With ignition OFF, connect battery junction box fuse 42 (15A), disconnect C1110, then switch ignition ON: pin 2 must exceed 11 volts. Otherwise check the fuse and repair the supply or investigate the short. With the specified isolation and ignition changes, test pin 1 for a short to ground, short to voltage and an open to PCM C1551B pin 41. Failed checks require wiring repair. Passing R7 directs compressor replacement, clearing the DTC and repeating the self-test; a returning code leads to R8.

steps.title: Trace a missing clutch request — S
steps.body: For P193E, first confirm an observable symptom. Without one, the system is operating correctly at this time; traffic or an intermittent fault may explain the code. Otherwise network-test the body control module (BCM), PCM and FCIM, diagnosing any communication failure. With the engine running, PANEL selected and A/C indicated on, PCM AC_REQ showing YES leads to S7. If not, monitor FCIM CC_SW_AC while operating the button: Active with the indicator on leads to BCM check S6; failure leads to FCIM check S5.

steps.title: Resolve connections before the module endpoint
steps.body: At P6, Q6, R8 or S5–S7, inspect the specified module connectors with ignition OFF. Replace corroded connectors/terminals, clean module pins and renew bent, damaged or pushed-out pins. Reconnect securely and retest. If the concern persists, follow any applicable technical service bulletin. Without one, FCIM/BCM branches require a vehicle identification number-specific Guided Routine; only the completed R8/S7 branches direct PCM replacement through its full procedure.

watchFor.title: Clutch engagement alone is insufficient
watchFor.body: Judge variable-compressor performance by the specified pressure response or EVACC pattern, not simply by whether the clutch engages.

watchFor.title: Keep engine-specific wiring separate
watchFor.body: Do not transfer the 2.3L solenoid connector assignments or compressor-replacement path to another engine.

notes: Use the complete Test P temperature/resistance table and the exact Q/R measurement thresholds. General continuity expectations do not replace the limits for these circuits.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1B71:11 or B1B71:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: Test P investigates evaporator temperature sensing and its wiring; the code alone does not establish a failed sensor.
diagnostics.next: Compare sensor resistance with temperature, then follow the circuit checks if it passes.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code C1B14:11 or C1B14:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: C1B14:11 indicates sensor-reference voltage below 5 volts; C1B14:12 indicates voltage above 5 volts.
diagnostics.next: Use Q to distinguish a ground fault or component loading from a short to voltage before assessing the FCIM.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P06A0 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM sees higher-than-expected feedback voltage, consistent with a short to voltage or an open circuit or sensor.
diagnostics.next: Follow the supported compressor-response route and its explicit decision before entering R4.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P193E is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM has not received the A/C enable request from the BCM; this does not identify a failed module.
diagnostics.next: Use S to confirm the symptom, communication and request data.

verification.body: After compressor replacement, clear codes and perform the prescribed normal-operation test or self-test. After connector repairs, operate the system again and resolve the connection's underlying cause.

verification.title: Record the observed result
verification.body: Record ambient conditions, charge verification, pressure response or EVACC trace, request-PID results and post-repair codes. Distinguish demonstrated compressor response from unresolved cooling or control faults.

guides.title: Check EMTC air-conditioning compressor performance and control
guides.summary: Separate compressor performance problems from evaporator-sensor, shared sensor-supply and compressor-request faults on vehicles with electronic manual temperature control.
guides.introduction: Electronic Manual Temperature Control (EMTC) uses the control-panel selections to set outlet temperature, airflow and cooling. Air conditioning also removes moisture from cabin air. Where an externally controlled variable-displacement compressor is fitted, the powertrain control module (PCM) changes its pumping capacity by switching the control-solenoid ground. These checks establish whether the problem lies in that response, its electrical control or the information requesting cooling.
guides.why: A compressor that can change displacement should not be condemned for poor cooling alone. Incorrect refrigerant charge, misleading temperature information and missing network requests can all lead the investigation elsewhere.

when.summary: Use when poor A/C performance or relevant climate-control codes are present on an EMTC-equipped vehicle.
notes: These are EMTC tests. Dual Automatic Temperature Control (DATC), with independently selectable driver and passenger temperatures, has a separate diagnostic guide.
Use the compressor tests only for the applicable variable-displacement compressor; the solenoid wiring branch described here is specifically for 2.3L.

prepare.title: Establish sound electrical test conditions
prepare.detail: Confirm the complaint, check battery and charging operation, and ensure battery state of charge exceeds 70%. Retrieve relevant module codes. Use a diagnostic scan tool, digital multimeter and correct connector probe adapters; these tests require automotive electrical diagnostic skills.

prepare.title: Prepare the compressor test equipment
prepare.detail: Both performance routes require correct refrigerant charge and ambient temperature above 21.1°C (70°F). Use the EVDC100 tester with its instructions, or a scan tool displaying the PCM EVACC parameter identification (PID). If neither route is available, obtain the specified equipment before continuing. Refrigerant servicing requires the appropriate recovery, evacuation and charging capability.

steps.title: Test evaporator temperature feedback when B1B71:11 or B1B71:15 is recorded
steps.body: Follow Test L. With ignition off, disconnect the evaporator sensor and compare its resistance against the temperature table; resistance must be judged at the corresponding temperature. Replace an out-of-range sensor. If it passes, follow L2–L5 in order for an input short to voltage, short to ground, open circuit and signal-to-return short. Repair a failed circuit; passing results lead to the front controls interface module (FCIM) connection checks.

steps.title: Isolate a shared sensor-supply fault
steps.body: Test M starts with an FCIM self-test. For C1B14:11, check for a ground short, then reference-to-return continuity. When M4 is reached, disconnect the cabin temperature/humidity sensor, distribution-door actuator, driver temperature-door actuator and inlet-door actuator in that order. Stop when resistance rises above 200 ohms: the last disconnected component is the replacement branch. No rise directs wiring repair. The C1B14:12 branch checks for unwanted voltage. Connect a replacement actuator before reconnecting the FCIM so calibration can occur.

steps.title: Use the EVDC100 performance route
steps.body: At N1, operate the tester according to its instructions. A decrease in suction pressure or increase in high-side pressure proves the compressor can change displacement: do not replace it. With P06A0 present, continue to N4; without it, check charge quantity. No pressure response directs compressor replacement through the applicable procedure, clearing codes and testing operation. If P06A0 remains, continue to N4.

steps.title: Alternatively, observe the EVACC response
steps.body: At N2, start the engine and monitor EVACC. Select floor airflow, full warm, lowest blower and A/C off; close the doors and windows and run for 5 minutes. Then select panel airflow, full cold, highest blower, recirculation and A/C on. An initial PID increase followed by a decrease confirms displacement response: retain the compressor and check charge. If that pattern is absent, continue to N4.

steps.title: Follow the directed 2.3L solenoid-circuit branch
steps.body: Enter N4 only when the preceding tester or scan-data decision directs it. Check solenoid power and the specified battery junction box fuse, then follow N5–N7 for pulse-width-modulated control-wire shorts to ground, shorts to voltage and an open. Preserve each ignition state and connector-disconnection instruction. Repair failed wiring. Only the all-pass branch directs compressor replacement, clearing the code and repeating the self-test; a returning code leads to N8.

steps.title: Trace a missing compressor request with Test O
steps.body: P193E means the PCM did not receive the enable request from the body control module (BCM). Without an observable symptom, replacement is not justified. Otherwise, run the Network Test and resolve noncommunicating modules first. With panel mode and A/C selected, AC_REQ displaying YES leads to the PCM branch. If it does not, check FCIM CC_SW_AC: Active leads to the BCM branch; an incorrect switch response leads to the FCIM branch.

steps.title: Complete the appropriate module-connection branch
steps.body: At L6, M6, N8 or O5–O7, inspect the designated module connectors. Correct corrosion, replace damaged or displaced terminals, and reconnect securely before operating the system again. Persistent concerns require checking applicable technical service bulletins. FCIM and BCM branches then require their vehicle-specific guided routines; PCM replacement is directed only at the relevant completed PCM branch when no bulletin applies.

watchFor.title: Connector damage introduced during testing
watchFor.body: Incorrect probes can spread terminals and create a new intermittent fault. Follow the specified measurement and isolation method.

watchFor.title: Chafed cabin-sensor wiring
watchFor.body: Inspect the temperature/humidity sensor harness before attributing its codes to the sensor or FCIM.

notes: Cabin-sensor codes below identify further circuit investigation; they do not independently justify replacing a sensor or module.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code C1B14:11 or C1B14:12 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: C1B14:11 indicates a sensor reference below 5 volts; C1B14:12 indicates a reference above 5 volts.
diagnostics.next: Use Test M to distinguish wiring, a connected component and FCIM concerns.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P06A0 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detects higher-than-expected feedback voltage, consistent with a voltage short or an open circuit or sensor.
diagnostics.next: Use the supported N1/N2 performance route and its result-directed electrical checks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B105A:12 or B105A:14 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: B105A:12 reports high cabin-sensor fan-circuit voltage with the fan inactive. B105A:14 reports no voltage, indicating an open or ground short, with the fan active.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the fan supply, fuse, wiring and connections before deciding on a component.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A61:11 or B1A61:15 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: B1A61:11 indicates low cabin-temperature feedback voltage. B1A61:15 indicates high voltage from a voltage short or an open circuit or sensor.
diagnostics.next: Continue cabin-temperature sensor circuit diagnosis after checking harness condition.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1A69:12 or B1A69:14 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: B1A69:12 indicates high humidity-input voltage. B1A69:14 indicates no voltage from a ground short or an open circuit or sensor.
diagnostics.next: Investigate the humidity-input circuit and connections; the code alone does not establish sensor failure.

verification.title: Confirm operation after the directed correction
verification.body: Operate the climate system again. After compressor replacement, clear codes and repeat the required operation check or self-test; follow the returning-code branch when necessary.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record test temperature, charge assessment, pressure response or EVACC pattern, relevant codes and the resulting branch decision.

guides.title: Check charging, cruise, blind-spot and ajar message-center warnings
guides.summary: Separate message-center and network faults from charging, cruise, lighting and luggage-latch concerns using the appropriate diagnostic branch.
guides.introduction: The message center is part of the instrument panel cluster (IPC). It combines wired inputs and network messages to display warnings and reconfigurable telltales (RTTs). A warning that stays on—or never appears—can therefore reflect a display problem, missing information or a fault in the monitored system. These checks cover the Blind Spot Information System (BLIS) OFF indicator, charging and cruise indicators, and door or luggage-compartment ajar indications.
guides.why: Check the information reaching the display before replacing parts. Network interruptions can change warning behavior, while a luggage-latch switch or damaged wire can report the wrong lid position even when the cluster works correctly.

when.summary: When a charging, cruise, BLIS OFF or ajar indication remains on, never appears or disagrees with vehicle operation.
notes: Use the BLIS and adaptive-cruise branches only where that equipment is fitted.
The concern must be present before a diagnostic replacement decision is justified.

prepare.title: Arrange electrical diagnostic capability
prepare.detail: Use a module-capable scan tool, digital multimeter, Rotunda Flex Probes and a fused jumper. Have Wiring Diagrams Cell 89 and access to vehicle identification number (VIN)-guided routines. Check battery and charging condition; Diagnostic Methods requires battery state of charge above 70%.

prepare.title: Keep each test in its intended state
prepare.detail: Perform operation and scan checks with normal connections. For resistance measurements, switch ignition off, follow Diagnostic Methods' battery-isolation guidance and disconnect the connectors specified below. Never use an ohmmeter on a powered circuit.

steps.title: Establish message-center operation for AG and AI
steps.body: For a BLIS OFF or cruise-indicator complaint, turn ignition on and close the doors, hood and luggage lid. Acknowledge each warning with OK. Observe the door-ajar telltale, open the driver door and dismiss its popup. The telltale must be off closed and on open. Failure leads to the VIN-guided IPC routine; stop this branch there.

steps.title: Follow Test AG for the BLIS OFF indicator
steps.body: If the display check passes, perform the IPC self-test and follow its diagnostic trouble code (DTC) chart for recorded faults. With no IPC codes, self-test the left and right side obstacle detection modules, SODL and SODR. Their codes lead to BLIS diagnosis. Otherwise check Gateway Module A (GWM) continuous-memory codes: codes lead to network diagnosis; none lead to BLIS diagnosis.

steps.title: Check the charging indicator through AH2–AH4
steps.body: Perform the IPC self-test, then check GWM continuous-memory codes if the IPC has none. Follow the respective code chart or network diagnosis when faults appear. Otherwise check charging-system operation. An operating charging system with a never-on warning is functioning correctly at this time; an always-on warning requires diagnosis of all Body Control Module (BCM) codes. Failed charging operation needs the applicable charging-system procedure.

steps.title: Follow Test AI for a cruise indicator that never lights
steps.body: After the message-center check, perform the IPC self-test, then check GWM continuous-memory codes if no IPC codes are present. Resolve codes through the IPC chart or network diagnosis. With neither module reporting codes, continue with [base cruise diagnosis](#/document/G1693138) or [adaptive cruise diagnosis](#/document/G1693153), according to fitted equipment.

steps.title: Separate lighting and module concerns in AJ2–AJ5
steps.body: Open and close each door while watching the interior lamps; incorrect operation leads to interior-lighting diagnosis. Otherwise self-test the IPC, check GWM continuous-memory codes, then self-test the BCM, following faults at each stage. B1178:01 leads to AJ6; other BCM codes need BCM diagnosis. Without BCM codes, a door complaint requires the VIN-guided BCM routine, a luggage-lid complaint proceeds to AJ6, and a never-on hood indication leads to perimeter-alarm diagnosis.

steps.title: Check the luggage-latch closed circuit in AJ6–AJ9
steps.body: With ignition off, BCM C2280E disconnected and the lid fully closed, measure C2280E pin 34 to ground. Below 3 ohms leads to AJ10. Otherwise disconnect latch C4339, bridge pins 1 and 4 with a fused jumper and repeat. Below 3 ohms now directs latch replacement. Remove the jumper in either case. If resistance remains high, keep both connectors disconnected and check C4339 pin 4 to ground, then C2280E pin 34 to C4339 pin 1. Each must be below 3 ohms; repair the failing circuit. Passing both leads to AJ12.

steps.title: Check whether the open lid releases the ground path
steps.body: For AJ10, keep ignition off and C2280E disconnected, with the latch connected, and open the lid. Resistance from C2280E pin 34 to ground above 10,000 ohms leads to AJ12. Otherwise disconnect C4339 and repeat for AJ11. Above 10,000 ohms now directs latch replacement; a lower result directs repair of the grounded input circuit.

steps.title: Inspect BCM connections and reach the proper endpoint
steps.body: At AJ12, switch ignition off and inspect all BCM connectors. Renew corroded connectors or terminals, clean module pins and replace damaged, bent or pushed-out pins as required. Reconnect securely and operate the system. If the concern persists, check OASIS service information for applicable technical service bulletins and follow one if present. Otherwise stop at the VIN-guided BCM routine.

watchFor.title: Network defaults can resemble component faults
watchFor.body: For interruptions shorter than 5 seconds, the charging, cruise, ajar and drive-mode displays retain their previous states. At 5 seconds or longer, missing charging data turns its telltale on; missing ajar data turns ajar displays off. Missing or invalid cruise or drive-mode data turns those indicators off.

watchFor.title: Use the correct latch procedure
watchFor.body: The ajar switch is part of the luggage latch. A replacement decision requires the coupe procedure for a coupe or the convertible procedure for a convertible.

notes: Adaptive cruise also relies on override and set-speed display messages.
A drive-mode indication concern can involve communications, the GWM, powertrain control module input or IPC; its fallback behavior alone does not identify the fault.
These checks end at a supported repair decision, a system-specific diagnostic or a VIN-guided routine.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code B1178:01 is recorded by the BCM.
diagnostics.meaning: This on-demand code reports an open detected on the luggage-compartment ajar input; it does not by itself prove latch failure.
diagnostics.next: Follow AJ6 onward to distinguish the latch, ground circuit and input wiring.

verification.title: Confirm operation after connection work
verification.body: With connectors seated and latched, operate the system as AJ12 directs. If the concern disappears, address the underlying connector or terminal defect.

verification.title: Record the diagnostic result
verification.body: Record warning behavior, module codes, circuit readings and the resulting repair or referral. For AG and AI, retain the closed-door/off and open-door/on observations.

guides.title: Diagnose 5.0L generator interference and charging-control faults
guides.summary: Trace radio interference, inspect the generator current sensor and separate charging-supply faults from generator command and monitor problems.
guides.introduction: The generator supplies electrical power and replenishes the battery. The powertrain control module (PCM) requests output through the generator command circuit (GENCOM) and watches feedback through the generator monitor circuit (GENMON). A separate Hall-effect current sensor surrounds the generator battery-positive cable and reports current flow. These are distinct functions, so radio noise, current-sensor codes and control-circuit codes require different tests.
guides.why: Poor battery condition or resistance in a heavy cable can imitate generator trouble. Loading a circuit exposes weak connections that an unloaded voltage reading may miss, while command and monitor checks distinguish wiring faults from regulator problems.

when.summary: Use for radio interference, generator-current-sensor codes or generator command/monitor faults on the 5.0L.
notes: Current-sensor work here ends after code retrieval and physical inspection.

prepare.title: Prepare for electrical and engine-running tests
prepare.detail: Use a scan tool supporting PCM self-tests, data monitoring and active commands, plus a digital multimeter, Flex Probe Kit and fused jumper. The sense-circuit test requires a 250–350 mA incandescent 12-volt lamp; an LED lamp is unsuitable. Safe handling of battery-positive connections and engine-running measurements requires automotive electrical competence.

prepare.title: Establish battery condition
prepare.detail: Tests E/F require battery voltage above 12.2 volts before and during testing, without a charger attached. F/G begin with battery condition and state-of-charge testing; charge or replace a failing battery before continuing. Inspect junction-box connections and, for monitor faults, abnormal ignition-off drain.

steps.title: Use Test D to identify generator-related radio noise
steps.body: At idle, tune to a station exhibiting interference. Switch ignition off, disconnect generator C102B and C102C, then restart and listen at idle. Noise that remains directs diagnosis to the appropriate audio system. Noise that disappears directs generator replacement through the 5.0L removal and installation procedure.

steps.title: Complete the current-sensor code and physical checks
steps.body: Run the PCM self-test with ignition on. P0562 directs Test B before continuing the current-sensor branch. For P0A5A, switch ignition off and inspect the sensor for damage, corrosion, disconnection, correct routing of the B+ cable through it and trapped debris. Correct physical defects or replace a physically faulty sensor as appropriate. If inspection finds nothing, stop this branch for further electrical diagnosis; these checks do not authorize PCM replacement.

steps.title: Check the main supply using the G2 sequence for both F and G
steps.body: Use the complete G2/G3 supply-and-cable sequence at F2/F3 as well. With ignition off, inspect and repair generator connectors, then reconnect securely. Record battery voltage and measure C102C pin 1—the main B+ output—to ground. It must be within 0.5 volt of battery voltage. A failed result directs attention to the B+ nut, the 275A MEGA fuse and supply wiring; investigate the cause of a blown fuse.

steps.title: Measure cable loss under load
steps.body: Run at idle with headlamps on and blower high. Place the positive voltmeter lead on C102C pin 1 and the negative lead on the battery positive post. Wiggle the wiring and connections while observing the reading. Voltage drop must be less than 0.5 volt. Excessive drop directs repair of corrosion or poor connections in the generator B+ circuit or positive battery cable.

steps.title: Load-test the A-sense supply when directed
steps.body: Use F4 for the command-code branch and G4 for P0625; P0626 proceeds from G3 to G5. Switch ignition off, disconnect C102B, then switch ignition on. Connect the specified lamp from C102B pin 3 to ground through Flex Probes. During a wiring wiggle test, loaded voltage must remain within ±0.5 volt of recorded battery voltage. A failed result directs checks of fuse 36 and its circuit.

steps.title: Isolate command or monitor wiring faults
steps.body: F5–F7 investigate GENCOM; G5–G7 investigate GENMON. Follow the specified connector isolation and ignition changes for voltage-short, ground-short and open-circuit checks. With ignition off and the generator regulator and PCM connectors disconnected, F7 measures C175B pin 13 to C102B pin 2 while wiggling the wiring. Resistance below 3 ohms continues to F8; otherwise repair the circuit. G7 measures the separate monitor conductor from C175B pin 26 to C102B pin 1: below 3 ohms continues to G8; otherwise repair the circuit. Keep each subsequent test in its own command or monitor branch.

steps.title: Follow the monitor branch into internal generator checks
steps.body: After valid G5–G7 results, G8/G9 require both generator connectors disconnected. Resistance from the generator B+ terminal to its case must exceed 25K ohms; resistance from each regulator terminal to the case must exceed 10,000 ohms. A failed check directs generator replacement. Passing checks lead to G10.

steps.title: Compare command and monitor data only after preceding checks pass
steps.body: At F8 or G10, reconnect the PCM and install the specified fused jumper between C102B pins 1 and 2. Start the engine and compare GENMON with generator-command data, GENCMD, while wiggling the harness. G10 additionally commands GENVDSD to 14 volts. Agreement within 5% directs generator replacement; disagreement directs PCM connection checks. Remove the jumper in either case.

steps.title: Complete the final connection and bulletin checks
steps.body: At F9/G11, switch ignition off and inspect PCM connectors. Correct corrosion, damaged terminals and displaced pins, then reconnect securely and check operation. A continuing concern requires checking applicable service bulletins before the final PCM replacement branch. That decision requires all preceding tests to be valid. Clear all module codes as directed after repair.

watchFor.title: Confusing the output cable with a signal terminal
watchFor.body: C102C pin 1 is the main B+ connection. C102B pin 1 carries the monitor signal and is not the battery-feed test point.

watchFor.title: Apparently steady charging voltage
watchFor.body: The generator can default to steady output during a control or monitor fault. Voltage alone does not establish normal PCM control.

notes: For identification only, current-sensor C1645 pins 1, 2 and 3 correspond to PCM C175B reference pin 52, return pin 51 and feedback pin 53. This topology does not authorize additional current-sensor measurements or replacement decisions.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0A5A is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: The PCM detects no generator current without an accompanying current-sensor circuit code.
diagnostics.next: Perform E2 physical checks; a clear inspection does not prove sensor failure.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0A5B or P0A5C is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P0A5B indicates low current-sensor feedback voltage from an open or ground short; P0A5C indicates high voltage consistent with a voltage short.
diagnostics.next: Arrange further circuit diagnosis beyond this guide's current-sensor prechecks.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0620 or P065B is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P0620 identifies a possible GENCOM, A-sense or B+ open/ground short. P065B means the generator reports an internal regulator failure.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test F, starting with battery and supply checks; neither code alone completes the diagnosis.

diagnostics.finding: Diagnostic trouble code P0625 or P0626 is recorded.
diagnostics.meaning: P0625 indicates low monitor feedback and can also involve missing sense or B+ supply. P0626 indicates an open or powered-short monitor circuit. Generator or PCM faults are also possible.
diagnostics.next: Follow Test G and preserve its code-dependent sense-circuit branch.

diagnostics.finding: A battery-saving message switches off the audio system.
diagnostics.meaning: With the engine off, low battery charge or elapsed accessory time can trigger normal load shedding.
diagnostics.next: Messages with the engine running, or only on the specified audio display, direct attention to audio diagnosis. Inspect battery, generator, junction-box, C1046 and ground connections.

verification.title: Recheck the original concern
verification.body: Confirm whether interference or the charging concern remains after the directed correction. A concern resolved by connector work still requires addressing the cause of that connection fault.

verification.title: Record measurements and remaining current-sensor work
verification.body: Record battery voltage, B+ supply voltage, loaded cable drop, command and monitor circuit measurements, relevant codes and completed branch results. Current-sensor diagnosis still ends at the stated physical-inspection boundary; do not record a sensor or PCM verdict from that incomplete electrical branch.

authoring.reviewNotes:
The engine-labeled native012-002 5.0L/5.2L C175B column identifies GENRC at pin13, carried on CDC10 BU/OG through inlineC1046pin2 to generatorC102Bpin2/RC; it identifies GENLI at pin26 on CDC15 VT through inlineC1046pin3 to generatorC102Bpin1/LI.
The independently inspected exact 5.0L native024-015 repeats C175B13 GENRC/CDC10 and C175B26 GENLI/CDC15 with continuations to12-2. It labels C175B15 ACCR/CH302, a different A/C control conductor.
Connector-C175B confirms pin13 GENRC, pin26 GENLI, pin50 unused and a pin15 ACCR variant. Connector-C102B independently identifies pin2 GENRC/CDC10 and pin1 GENLI/CDC15.
GENCOM is the workshop name for this regulator-command/GENRC conductor; GENMON is the workshop name for the regulator-monitor/GENLI conductor. No monitor/control swap is being inferred from mere adjacent labels; both complete paths were visually traced.
